items.source: Surfaced by the P1.x real-R calibrator (PR #8527) — NOT by any dedicated audit, which is the point: the R axis normalises pnl by each trade's own risk, and that immediately made an impossible row visible that raw-USD aggregates had absorbed silently for months.
items.title: Duplicate netted pnl on sibling rows — $24.3k across 31 paper rows poisoning the calibration set + ML labels (real-money exposure bounded at $45.52)
items.what_to_check: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (see updates). MEASURED (trainer-diag #8529, live journal, population = closed + non-backtest + pnl NOT NULL + measured-provenance, strategy htf_pullback_trend_2h symbol BTCUSDT, n=30 of 55 scanned). live mean R = -3.414 vs median -0.185; EXCLUDING the 3 worst rows the mean is +0.002. One row dominates: trade 2343, bybit_1, pnl -2970.99 on qty 0.012 BTC with a 3.72% stop distance => R = -99.5. A -2970.99 loss on 0.012 BTC implies a ~$247,000 price move, so that pnl is definitively not that row's own. The stop-distance denominator is NOT the cause: stop_dist_pct across the leg is min 1.10 / p25 1.87 / median 2.05 / max 5.41 percent, all sane for BTC. The signature is duplication: pnl -2970.99 appears on ids 2343/2447/2438 (qty 0.012 / 0.717 / 0.728) and +659.30 on 2584/2616 (qty 1.037 / 0.471) — identical to the cent across 60x different sizes. That is one netted close's realized pnl written to every sibling row at full magnitude instead of split pro-rata. CONFIRMED for the bybit_1 -2970.99 cluster; the bybit_2 clusters are UNRESOLVED (likely rounding collisions, see the 2026-08-06T15:05 update). Originally recorded as STRONGLY INDICATED, NOT YET PROVEN: the confirming census (duplicate-pnl clusters per account + whether provenance already flags them) is trainer-diag #8531; #8530 was mangled by the relay and is void.
items.how: Read #8531 block D FIRST — if these rows classify MEASURED then provenance.pnl_is_trustworthy has a hole and duplicated pnl is entering every downstream R metric, the calibration set, and the promotion gates that read totalPnlMeasured. Block C sizes the blast radius per account (bybit_1 is paper; check whether bybit_2 real-money rows are in clusters too). Then find the writer: this is the PnL-side sibling of the QTY-side netting defect fixed in PR #8527 (BL-20260801-NETTING-PARTIAL-CLOSE-ROWS-NEVER-REDUCED) — under one-way netting the broker returns ONE closed-pnl record for the whole netted position and the monitor's four broker-close persist sites appear to stamp it whole onto each row rather than prorating. Note CLAUDE.md already documents that any *_prorated source is FABRICATED because the split is an assumption; a full-magnitude copy is strictly worse than a prorated one and is not currently marked at all.
items.disposition_when_verified: Real-money accounting is NOT materially affected ($45.52 upper bound), so this is not a money remediation. It IS a research-integrity remediation: (a) mark the 31 bybit_1 suspect rows so provenance excludes them from the measured population (they currently classify MEASURED and feed pnl_is_trustworthy), (b) re-run the P1.x fidelity trust map afterwards — the htf_pullback_trend_2h/BTCUSDT verdict is unusable in either direction until then, (c) check whether any ML model was trained on labels built over these rows and, if so, whether its gate metrics move once they are excluded. The forward-only writer fix is PR #8534 (Tier-2, awaiting operator OK); historical rewriting of money-DB pnl remains a separate Tier-2 decision with its own review.

updates.note: ROOT CAUSE FOUND BY CODE READING, not by the relay (three relay attempts failed: #8530 mangled by the relay's angle-bracket escaping, #8531 died on a column name I GUESSED — close_reason does not exist, the same error class as the strategy/strategy_name bug in PR #8527 — #8533 is the schema-driven retry and is still the right confirmation of BLAST RADIUS). THREE code sites persist a broker closed-pnl record onto a trade row. TWO already prorated by the row's qty share: order_monitor._reconcile_open_trades (the BL-20260720-ICTSCALP-PASTSTOP-EXITS guard, pnl_source 'netted_prorated') and the netted-cascade path in _apply_update (pnl_source 'netted_prorated_cascade', exit_price_source suffixed '_prorated'). The THIRD, _recover_close_from_broker_pnl (the stuck-strategy watchdog recovery path), had NO guard at all: it wrote pnl = round(float(closed_pnl), 4) whole AND stamped exit_price_source = _broker_pnl_source(rec) i.e. 'bybit_closed_pnl', which provenance.classify_pnl buckets MEASURED. So a full-magnitude netted figure was being written under a measured label — strictly worse than a missing value, because every consumer folds it into an aggregate unchallenged (the calibration set, the R metrics, and the totalPnlMeasured promotion gate all read it). FIXED this session: the proration arithmetic is extracted into ONE helper, order_monitor._prorate_netted_broker_pnl, and all three sites now call it — three hand-rolled copies is precisely how a fourth site diverges, the same 'one module owns this' lesson provenance.py exists for. The watchdog path now also downgrades exit_price_source to '<source>_prorated' when it splits, so the row classifies FABRICATED and drops out of pnl_is_trustworthy. STILL OPEN and why this item stays open: (a) the HISTORICAL rows are not backfilled — trades 2343/2438/2447/2584/2616 and any sibling cluster still carry full-magnitude pnl under a measured label, so every aggregate over history is still wrong; (b) the blast radius per account is UNMEASURED (relay #8533 blocks C/D) — specifically whether real-money bybit_2 rows are in duplicate-pnl clusters or only paper bybit_1; (c) the htf_pullback_trend_2h/BTCUSDT trust-map verdict remains unusable in either direction until the leg is re-run on clean rows. Note the fix is forward-only by design: rewriting historical money-DB pnl is a separate Tier-2 decision with its own review, not a side effect of a code fix.

CENSUS RETURNED (trainer-diag #8533, schema-driven). THREE results, one of which CORRECTS an earlier note in this item. (1) LABEL HOLE CONFIRMED: all five named rows classify ('measured', 'exit_price_source=bybit_closed_pnl'). Duplicated pnl is inside the population pnl_is_trustworthy admits — the fidelity calibration set, the R metrics, and the totalPnlMeasured promotion gate. Whole-journal split over closed non-backtest pnl-NOT-NULL rows (n=874): measured 533, fabricated 207, unverified 108, estimated 26; the htf_pullback_trend_2h/BTCUSDT leg alone is measured 30 / fabricated 25. (2) ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED — the cited rows did NOT come from the watchdog path fixed in PR #8534. Row detail shows setup_type='intent_reduce', closed_by='monitor_reconciler', closed_reason='reconciler — Bybit reports order filled and position flat', dated 2026-06-03/04/05 and 06-16. That is _reconcile_open_trades, and those dates PREDATE both the intent_reduce pnl deferral (BL-20260711) and the proration guard (BL-20260720-ICTSCALP-PASTSTOP-EXITS) that path has since received. So they are pre-fix historical artifacts of an already-fixed path. The watchdog hole in _recover_close_from_broker_pnl is REAL, still live, and was verified by reading the code — but it is NOT demonstrated that any row currently in the journal came from it. Investigating old rows surfaced a third site that never received the fix the other two got; do not conflate the two claims. (3) BLAST RADIUS STILL UNMEASURED, and the raw #8533 block-C number must NOT be quoted. It reports bybit_2 (REAL MONEY) at 236/408 rows 'in a duplicate-pnl cluster', but the metric groups on ROUND(pnl,2) and conflates real duplication with rounding collisions. Real duplication looks like the bybit_1 BTCUSDT -2970.99 cluster: 5 rows spanning qty 0.012 to 4.878, a 400x range, which cannot be coincidence. Every bybit_2 cluster is instead sub-dollar (-0.17 x15, -0.64 x6, -0.53 x5, ...) on qty 0.002-0.005 BTC — fifteen independent small scalps each losing ~17 cents is ordinary and rounds into one 'cluster'. Quoting 57.8%-of-real-money on that basis would fabricate a headline. The discriminator (qty dispersion within each cluster; spread > 1.5x = suspect) is trainer-diag #8535. Raw block C for the record, NOT to be read as the finding: alpaca_live 0/1, alpaca_options_paper 4/8, alpaca_paper 2/47, alpaca_portfolio 0/13, bybit_1 35/350, bybit_2 236/408, bybit_portfolio 0/20, ib_paper 2/27.

BLAST RADIUS MEASURED (trainer-diag #8535) — and it RE-SCOPES this item. The discriminator (SUSPECT = same rounded pnl across rows whose qty spread exceeds 1.5x; benign = a rounding collision among independent same-size scalps) splits the raw #8533 count cleanly. REAL-MONEY EXPOSURE IS $45.52. bybit_2: 79 suspect rows / 23 clusters totalling $45.52, against 157 rows correctly classified as benign collisions — so the raw '236 of 408' from #8533 was ~2/3 rounding artifact, and the remaining third is sub-dollar. PAPER IS WHERE THE DAMAGE IS. bybit_1: 31 suspect rows / 13 clusters totalling $24,272.18, concentrated in a handful of large clusters — |pnl| 2970.99 x5 at a 406.5x qty spread, 1356.31 x2 at 11.1x, 864.45 (SOL), 767.22 x3 at 5.6x, 659.30 x3 at 11.5x. Every other account is clean: alpaca_live 0, alpaca_portfolio 0, bybit_portfolio 0, and alpaca_paper/alpaca_options_paper/ib_paper have benign collisions only (0 suspect). CAVEAT ON MY OWN METRIC, stated so nobody over-reads the bybit_2 79: a 1.5x spread threshold is far too sensitive at scalp sizes — 0.002 vs 0.005 BTC is a 2.5x spread and is perfectly ordinary for independent trades — so most of that 79 is probably ALSO false-positive. $45.52 is therefore an UPPER BOUND on real-money exposure, not an estimate of it. WHAT THIS CHANGES: this is a RESEARCH-DATA-INTEGRITY defect, not a live-money accounting one. No material real money is mis-stated. But bybit_1 is the account the poisoned htf_pullback_trend_2h/BTCUSDT calibration leg comes from, and paper rows feed the fidelity trust map AND the ML label builders (setup_labels / trade_outcomes both gate on provenance.pnl_is_trustworthy, which #8533 block D confirmed admits these rows as MEASURED). So ~$24.3k of fabricated paper pnl has been flowing into backtest-trust and ML-label decisions. Severity stays HIGH on that basis and is NOT a money-at-risk claim — record it that way.

items.source: Found while reading the first real-R trust map (PR #8527). Fixed in the same session; logged so the reasoning survives.
items.title: FIXED — backtest_fidelity_calibrate could declare `calibrated` with a 92x mean-R gap (win-rate + KS both passed)
items.what_to_check: htf_pullback_trend_2h/BTCUSDT cleared the win-rate gap (0.123 vs 0.15) AND KS(R) (0.213 vs 0.30) and was returned as `calibrated` while its live mean-R was -3.41 against a backtest -0.037. Neither axis can see that: win-rate measures how OFTEN a leg wins, KS is a max-CDF-gap statistic insensitive to tail magnitude, and nothing measured how MUCH. KS only counts the CDF fraction a row occupies, so one extreme row in 30 moves KS by ~1/30 while moving the mean by 3.3 — the exact geometry that let it through.
items.how: Added a third gate axis `mean_r_gap` (MAX_MEAN_R_GAP = 0.50) plus a reported-not-gated `live_mean_r_outlier_share` that names one-row domination in the verdict reason, so a magnitude failure is legible instead of sending the reader to dump rows by hand (which is how this was found). NOTE the metric's ceiling is exactly 0.5 — deviations above and below a mean sum to the same total, so a lone value on its side contributes exactly half and can never exceed it; OUTLIER_DOMINANCE_FLAG must therefore stay BELOW 0.5 or the flag is unreachable and silently dead. Pinned by test_outlier_share_CEILING_is_one_half.
items.disposition_when_verified: Resolved in-session. The re-run trust map must be read on the 3-axis gate; every pre-2026-08-06 verdict predates both the real-R axis and this one.

items.source: trainer-vm-diag issue #8530 — a cmd block containing Python f-string alignment specs came back as a SyntaxError on the VM.
items.title: trainer-vm-diag relay corrupts cmd blocks: HTML-escapes < and >, collapses newlines to U+00B7, AND truncates mid-heredoc
items.what_to_check: Reproduced 2026-08-06 in #8530: a script using f-string alignment specs such as {x:>12.2f} / {y:<18} was delivered to the VM with < and > turned into </> AND every newline in the affected region replaced by the middle-dot U+00B7, producing `SyntaxError: invalid character '·' (U+00B7)`. The relay reported the failure honestly (the traceback came back), so this is a usability bug, not a silent-corruption bug — but the failure mode is confusing because the script is valid Python as authored.
items.how: Workaround in use: avoid < and > entirely in relay cmd blocks (#8531 uses BETWEEN instead of comparison operators and drops all alignment specs). Real fix is in the relay's body extraction — it should treat the fenced block as opaque text rather than HTML.
items.disposition_when_verified: Fix the extraction in .github/workflows/trainer-vm-diag.yml, or document the constraint in docs/claude/trainer-vm-mode.md section 9 so future sessions do not lose a round trip to it.

updates.note: SECOND, DISTINCT FAILURE MODE — raising severity low->medium because the relay is the ONLY channel to the trainer VM and it has now eaten three round trips in one session. (i) #8530: a script using f-string alignment specs {x:>12.2f} / {y:<18} arrived with < and > HTML-escaped AND every newline in the affected region replaced by U+00B7 -> SyntaxError. (ii) #8536: a longer script with THREE `python3 - <<'PY' ... PY` heredoc blocks arrived TRUNCATED at ~7 lines — bash reported `here-document at line 5 delimited by end-of-file (wanted 'PY')`. The delivered Command preview confirms it stopped right after `sys.path.insert(0, ".")`, i.e. the body was cut before the first PY terminator. Single-heredoc scripts of similar length (#8531, #8533, #8535) delivered fine, so the trigger is plausibly multiple heredocs or a length/marker interaction in the extractor, NOT length alone — that is a hypothesis, not established. WORKAROUND now in use: relay scripts are plain shell only (no heredoc, no Python, no angle brackets); see #8537. Both failures are LOUD (the VM's own error came back), so this is a usability/throughput bug, not silent corruption — but at three lost round trips it is materially slowing trainer work. FIX: make the extractor treat the fenced block as opaque text rather than HTML, and preserve it verbatim; then document the contract in docs/claude/trainer-vm-mode.md section 9 so future sessions do not rediscover it one failure at a time.

REPRODUCED THIS RUN, AND A WORKING MITIGATION FOUND. My first trainer-vm-diag cmd (#8591) was truncated exactly as this row describes — it died at `python3 - <<'PY'` with `bash: warning: here-document at line 10 delimited by end-of-file (wanted PY)`, losing every section after the heredoc. WORKAROUND THAT WORKS, verified on #8592: base64-encode the Python payload locally and send `echo <b64> | base64 -d | python3` — no heredoc, no < or > characters, no column-0 Python keyword in the shell text. That round-tripped a 2.5KB multi-section script intact. Recommend documenting this as the standard pattern for any non-trivial trainer cmd until the relay's extraction is fixed. Kept open (the relay defect itself is unfixed).

items.title: [order-monitor] bybit_2 XRPUSDT SL amend failing — Bybit's 20-leg tpsl cap likely hit under BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=partial's per-order qty-scoped brackets
items.description: BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=partial (live-verified + rolled out per BL/PR #7115, see the health-review-backlog entry above and performance-review-backlog) attaches a qty-scoped Partial-type TP/SL leg PER ORDER rather than one position-level bracket. Bybit's own API enforces a hard cap of 20 combined tp+sl legs per symbol (`oldTpNum+oldStNum+newNum > 20`, ErrCode 110061). If XRPUSDT on bybit_2 (traded by multiple strategies incl. `xrp_pullback_2h`, and as of PR #7254 `ict_scalp_xrp_5m` on bybit_1 — different account, not a factor here) has accumulated legs from many prior partial opens/adds without them being consolidated/cleared as positions close, it can hit that 20-leg ceiling — at which point ANY subsequent SL amend request for that symbol fails outright and `order_monitor` leaves the DB (and the live stop) UNCHANGED. This is a protection-integrity risk: a stop-loss that should move (e.g., a breakeven trail or a tightening update) silently fails to update on the exchange while the DB may or may not reflect the intended level, for as long as the leg count stays saturated. Not yet confirmed whether this is a one-off (a stale/orphaned leg never cleaned up) or a structural risk of the partial-brackets design at higher trade frequency/leg turnover on one symbol. NOT investigated further this session (incidental discovery during unrelated deploy-verification read) — flagging per the standing 'if you see something, say something' directive rather than walking past it.

items.title: [verify] live-confirm PR #7321's ENTRY-TIME leg-id capture on a genuinely fresh Bybit Partial-tpsl order (not just the backfill-then-amend path already verified)
items.description: PR #7321 added `_partial_tpsl_leg_ids`/`_classify_new_partial_tpsl_legs` to `execute_pkg`: before placing an order it snapshots the symbol's live conditional (StopOrder) legs, places the order, snapshots again, and diffs to find the newly-created SL/TP leg id(s) — writing them onto `trades.sl_order_id`/`.tp_order_id` at insert time. items.opened_by: claude (M27 Batch-4 XAUUSD session — discovered while dispatching a config-exact backtest+kfold run)
items.source: Direct repro across three consecutive trainer-vm-diag-request dispatches this session (issues #7297, #7300, #7301): a foreground command that runs silently (no stdout) for longer than roughly a minute or two reliably kills the SSH session with `client_loop: send disconnect: Broken pipe`, before ANY output — including a partially-written result file — is captured or reported back on the issue. This happened identically whether the heavy command was plain foreground, backgrounded with `nohup ... &` + a foreground poll loop, or gated with a `timeout 480` wrapper; only fully detaching the process with `setsid nohup ... > log 2>&1 < /dev/null & disown -a` (returning from the SSH command almost immediately, well inside the drop window) reliably avoided it (issue #7302, confirmed working). The underlying compute was NOT actually slow — a 178k-bar XAUUSD 15m backtest that appeared to hang for 8+ minutes under the broken foreground pattern actually completed in under 3 minutes once run detached (confirmed via a follow-up log-tail dispatch).
items.title: [trainer-vm-diag] long-silent (no-stdout) foreground commands reliably drop the SSH channel before completion, independent of workflow job timeout-minutes
items.description: `.github/workflows/trainer-vm-diag.yml` runs the requested `cmd:` over an SSH session with `timeout-minutes: 10` at the JOB level. That job-level timeout is NOT what's firing here — the failures happened at 2–8 minutes in, well under the 10-minute budget, and manifested as a client-side `Broken pipe` rather than a graceful cancellation (the workflow's own `if: cancelled()` handler, which correctly posts a comment on a genuine concurrency-preemption cancel, never fires for this failure mode — the run just dies with no comment at all, which is worse: a requester sees silence and has no way to distinguish 'still running' from 'already dead'). Likely cause: the SSH action/client (or an intermediate proxy) has an inactivity/keepalive timeout shorter than a few minutes that isn't being satisfied by a command producing zero stdout. This wasted significant session time across three consecutive dispatch/diagnose/retry cycles before the detached-launch pattern was discovered empirically. Composes with BL-20260720-TRAINERDIAG-FENCE (same workflow, different failure class) — not fixed this session because the fix (likely a `ServerAliveInterval`/keepalive setting on the SSH step, or a documented requirement that any command expected to run >1min must self-detach) touches a shared workflow other sessions rely on. A secondary, related observation: the issue body's free-text prose AFTER the `cmd:` YAML block is also being fed to bash as part of the same script (confirmed repeatedly — e.g. a sentence beginning 'M27 Batch-4 (XAUUSD...' produced `bash: line N: syntax error near unexpected token '('`, and one beginning 'Retry of #7294...' produced `bash: line N: Retry: command not found`). These are currently harmless because the prose reliably fails as shell syntax, but it is latent — a future issue body whose free-text portion happens to parse as valid (and unintended) shell would silently execute it on the trainer VM.
items.trigger_condition: Next session touching `.github/workflows/trainer-vm-diag.yml`, or the next time a trainer-vm-diag dispatch needs to run a command expected to take more than ~1 minute with little/no stdout in that window.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) the workflow itself is hardened — an SSH keepalive/ServerAliveInterval setting so a silent multi-minute command survives, AND the cmd-extraction step is changed to isolate the `cmd:` block from any trailing free-text (so issue-body prose is never executed as shell); or (b) short of a workflow change, this finding is folded into the workflow's own header-comment documentation so future sessions default to the `setsid ... & disown -a` detached-launch pattern for any command expected to run long/silent, without having to rediscover it empirically each time.

updates.note: Re-validated: this session's trainer-vm-diag cmd was short + produced immediate stdout and completed cleanly (no drop). Workflow-level fix for long-silent commands still not shipped.
Re-validated 07-26: infra/VM-side item needing a VM write or dedicated ops session; condition not observed to regress this window. Carried.

RESOLVED — added `-o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=10` to the trainer-vm-diag.yml ssh invocation, so a long-silent trainer command (a full dataset build / training cycle) no longer has its SSH session torn down mid-run (~5 min silence tolerated). Verified: workflow parses as valid YAML.

items.title: [infra] Trainer's own ML cycle saturates 6 GB into deep swap (promotion-readiness ~3.2 GB) -> chronic OOM/wedge risk; external research jobs merely tip an already-saturated box
items.description: REFRAME (the key insight from the research session): the trainer's own cycle already pushes 6 GB deep into swap BEFORE any external research load — so this is a footprint/serialization problem on the box itself, not just 'don't run big sweeps'. ROOT CAUSE (verified in code this review, Tier-1 read): `ml/promotion/attribution.py` streams the shadow log via inspector.iter_records (a generator) but then MATERIALIZES it whole — `records = list(records)` (attribution.py:192; load path load_shadow_records -> aggregate at ~L322-327). So `ml promotion-readiness` loads the ENTIRE runtime_logs/shadow_predictions.jsonl (+ _backfill.jsonl) into RAM as ShadowRecord objects; that log has grown large since per-bar regime scoring went live (REGIME_BAR_SCORING) — hence 3.2 GB / ~99 min. FIX OPTIONS (Tier-2/3, operator-gated — NOT enacted here): (1) DON'T materialize: window/bound the shadow-log read to the relevant lookback before list(), or aggregate incrementally over iter_records without a full in-memory list (streaming reduce) — the single highest-leverage fix. (2) SERIALIZE the heavy ML stages within a cycle (promotion-readiness + `ml train` were overlapping) so a cycle can't swap-thrash itself; +nice/ionice. (3) CONTAINMENT: systemd MemoryMax / MemorySwapMax on the trainer service units so a runaway OOM-kills ONE job instead of wedging the whole box (a wedge currently needs an out-of-band reset-instance). CAPACITY NOTE: the Always-Free Ampere pool is FULL (4/24 OCPU-GB) so 'add RAM' is not free — this must be a footprint/serialization fix, not a resize. Cross-links: BL-20260712-TRAINER-JOB-SERIALIZATION (same health backlog — the SSH-starvation serialization ask; this is its concrete recurrence + root cause) and MB-20260705-TRAINER-OOM (ml-review backlog — the ML-lifecycle OOM signature). Full incident write-up: docs/sprint-logs/S-M20-EXIT-REFINEMENT-2026-07-12.md (section 'M20-X sweep INCIDENT'). Coordination: the research session owns the M20-X sweep re-run and has gated it (won't launch unless available > 2 GB and swap < 500 MB), so no collision there; this item is the trainer's own memory-pressure fix.

items.source: PERF-20260601-001 root-cause (docs/research/trend-donchian-live-anomaly-rootcause-2026-07-11.md; trainer-vm-diag #6136). trend_donchian bybit_1 rows 2604/2607/2610 are setup_type='intent_reduce', exit_reason='reconciler_filled', entry_price==exit_price, yet carry a large non-NULL positive pnl (+$561/+620/+898).
items.title: Reconciler books an intent_reduce leg with a phantom non-NULL pnl (entry==exit) — contradicts apply_intent_reduce_partial_close's NULL-pnl design
items.description: A reduce leg is meant to carry NULL pnl (src/units/accounts/execute.py::apply_intent_reduce_partial_close leaves pnl/pnl_percent NULL, pnl_source='deferred_intent_reduce'), and order_monitor already treats reduce legs specially (is_reduce_leg). But some intent_reduce rows get closed via the reconciler_filled path with entry_price==exit_price AND a large fabricated positive pnl (trend_donchian demo 2604 +$561.28 / 2607 +$620.17 / 2610 +$898.60 — all entry==exit). That phantom pnl inflates any analytics that don't explicitly exclude reduce legs. Observed on DEMO here so no real-money impact, and the new exclude_reduce_leg_predicate (src/web/api/_clean_trades.py, applied in /strategy/attribution) now MASKS it in the read path — but the WRITE path should not book the phantom pnl at all (a real-money intent_reduce reconciler-flip would otherwise inject a fabricated win/loss upstream of any single reader). ROOT-CAUSE belongs to the reconciler close path (order_monitor.py _reconcile_open_trades / the reconciler_filled pnl computation for a row whose setup_type='intent_reduce'): it should defer/NULL the pnl for a reduce leg the same way the open-time path does, or skip pnl computation when entry==exit on a reduce leg. Cross-ref: the exclude_reduce_leg guard is defense-in-depth in the analytics layer; this item is the upstream write-path fix.
items.trigger_condition: Next /health-review touching the reconciler close path, OR a real-money intent_reduce leg appears with a non-NULL reconciler pnl.
items.resolution_criteria: The reconciler close path leaves pnl NULL (or a deferred marker) for an intent_reduce reduce leg instead of booking a phantom entry==exit pnl; a test covers a reduce-leg reconciler close asserting NULL pnl.

updates.note: Re-validated 2026-07-19: still valid, Tier-2 code (reconciler books intent_reduce leg with phantom non-NULL pnl entry==exit, contradicts apply_intent_reduce_partial_close NULL-pnl design). Not independently re-triggered this window. Blocker: Tier-2 reconciler fix.

FIXED (operator-approved 2026-07-19, Tier-2). Write-path fix, 2 sites in order_monitor.py: (1) _close_trade_from_order_status now gates the pnl write on `not is_reduce_leg` + stamps pnl_source='deferred_intent_reduce' (a reduce leg's qty-matched closed_pnl on a netting account is the PARENT's realized close, so booking it fabricated the entry==exit +$561/+620/+898 rows); (2) _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced scan now excludes intent_reduce rows so the universal fallback can't re-fabricate the NULL. Reverses the #2974 attribution (which the read-path exclude_reduce_leg_predicate masked anyway); updated its test. Regression tests added (test_order_monitor_close_pnl reduce-leg assertion flipped + test_reconciler_reduce_and_shadow). Latent real-money PnL-integrity fix (bybit_2 netting).

REVERSES #2974/BL-20260601-001 attribution (operator-approved after review — the attribution booked the parent's close onto the bookkeeping leg; #2974's test updated to assert NULL). Deployed to the live trader via issue #6929 (HEAD 3a0310b, ict-trader-live active, verified). items.title: IB exec client wedged on account_warmup_timeout after a fresh trader restart (recurred 2026-07-08) — warm-up never completes, MES/MGC/MHG dark until a gateway docker-restart
items.description: The account warm-up (reqAccountSummary, IB_ACCOUNT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S, BL-20260706-IBWARMUP) timed out 9x in a row on the trader's own execution client immediately after the 07:08Z restart and never recovered on its own — the circuit breaker just kept re-opening. A gateway docker-restart (vm-ib-gateway-recover) cleared it. This is the SECOND time the warm-up path has stranded MES since it was added (see BL-20260706-IBWARMUP / -IBACCTUPDATES-COLLISION). Investigate: does a trader restart while the gateway holds a stale session reliably wedge warm-up? Should the trader force a gateway session-reset (or a longer/again-retried warm-up) on N consecutive account_warmup_timeout before condemning, so MES self-heals without an operator/Claude-triggered gateway restart? Verify the ict-ib-gateway-watchdog on the gateway VM would have caught this (it probes net_liquidation) — if so, why did it not restart before this review found it (was the wedge < its 2-check threshold, or is the daily-only reset the only guard mid-day?).

updates.note: VERIFY (ib_state 07:50:58Z): the vm-ib-gateway-recover did NOT clear the trader exec client — still state=breaker_open, account_warmup_timeout, consecutive_failures 13 (up from 9), last_ok_utc still null. The gateway itself is fine: the READONLY client (9753) is connected + account_data_ready and even recovered from a liveness_probe_timeout at 07:44. So the fault is specifically the NON-readonly exec client's account warm-up (reqAccountSummary), NOT gateway login. A gateway docker-restart cannot fix this. Remaining levers: restart ict-trader-live (may not help; the 07:08 restart is what STARTED the wedge; interrupts the healthy real-money path), OR IB_ACCOUNT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S<=0 escape hatch (bypass the blocking warm-up, Tier-2 env), OR a code fix to _warm_account_data for the non-readonly client (Tier-3). Escalated to operator via /system-review. MES/MGC/MHG remain dark.
Closed — shipped + deployed + live-verified this session.

items.resolution_note: RESOLVED by RISK-2 (PR #6044, e32ff11, on main + deployed). IBClient.connect() warm-up demoted to BEST-EFFORT: on failure it logs + leaves _account_data_ready=False + returns the live handle; the breaker no longer trips on a warm-up timeout (only connect_failed + liveness_probe_timeout do). New _bounded_account_summary bounds balance()'s accountSummary read (raises IBConnectionError on timeout → callers fall back to the DB snapshot). connection_state() reports connected for a probe-live handle regardless of account_data_ready. Removes the self-perpetuating warm-up wedge that stranded MES/MGC/MHG. Live-verified via /api/diag/ib_state (exec clients connected, no breaker_open/account_warmup loop).

items.source: Live incident 2026-07-09 ~22:14-22:37Z: an ib_paper MGC short (mgc_pullback_1d, pkg-a4a957610253455e, order 188, -9 @ 4128.91) tripped MONITOR BLIND (candles_unavailable 3 ticks) because the IB exec client's circuit breaker was open (gateway wedge). The alert reads 'Broker SL/TP backstop (if any) still holds' — but there is NO way to VERIFY that: _check_naked_positions is journal-driven (MGC's journal had sl/tp -> never flagged), and the broker-side resting-order verification (_check_broker_naked_equity_positions via AlpacaClient.has_protective_orders) is ALPACA-ONLY. There is no IB analogue.
items.title: No IB broker-side protection VERIFICATION — an IB futures position with journal SL/TP but no RESTING broker bracket is invisible to every naked check
items.description: GUARDRAIL GAP (operator asked for a guardrail on the MGC monitor-blind trade). For Alpaca, _check_broker_naked_equity_positions asks the broker whether a resting protective leg exists (has_protective_orders) and re-arms a GTC OCO if none; for IB there is no equivalent, so an IB position whose broker OCA bracket was never placed / got cancelled / failed during a breaker flap stays silently naked while the monitor is also blind. PROPOSED FIX (held for operator/supervised build): add IBClient.has_protective_orders(symbol) (account-wide reqAllOpenOrders read, fail-safe None on read failure) + an IB analogue of the broker-naked sweep that re-arms via the EXISTING _attempt_naked_autoprotect on a confirmed-clean 'no resting bracket' read. CRITICAL BUILD CONSTRAINTS: (1) do NOT add a per-monitor-tick account-wide IB order read — that risks re-triggering the tick-latency/pacing wedge class (BL-20260609); cadence-gate it. (2) IB order visibility is per-client-session — ib.openTrades() only sees THIS client's orders, so a readonly client would false-read 'naked'; must use reqAllOpenOrders (account-wide) and validate against the live gateway before trusting it to PLACE orders. (3) fail-safe: read failure/ambiguity -> skip, never place. Deliberately NOT shipped unsupervised overnight (order-placing path needs live IB cross-client validation).

updates.note: Re-validated 2026-07-19: still valid, Tier-3 — no positive VERIFICATION that IB futures positions carry a RESTING broker bracket (naked-autoprotect re-arms but there's no read-back confirm). ib_paper holds MHG+MGC now; worth a broker-side bracket read. Blocker: Tier-3 verification path.

Re-validated: ib_state shows all 3 IB clients connected/account_data_ready this window, no naked-position alert fired (notifications banners empty). The structural gap (no broker-side resting-bracket check for IB, unlike Alpaca) is still unfixed in code.

OPERATOR APPROVED 2026-07-26: BUILD IB broker-side protection verification (IBClient.has_protective_orders + re-arm on missing resting bracket, mirroring the Alpaca path). Tier-3 live-path code — build + test, operator approves the final diff before deploy. Execution queued as its own PR. Kept open until built.

items.source: Live 2026-07-09: the ib-gateway container restarted ~22:15Z (last_ok of both exec clients = 22:14:40Z). The trader's IB exec client (498) then could NOT re-establish — last_fail_reason 'connect_failed: TimeoutError', breaker re-opening, consecutive_failures climbing 3->5->8, cooldown escalating 69s->119s — and stayed wedged ~18 min (MES/MGC/MHG market data all suppressed, MGC monitor blind) until a MANUAL vm-ib-gateway-recover (#6075) docker-restarted the gateway; the exec client then reconnected cleanly at 22:37:25 (data farms OK, Synchronization complete).
items.title: IB exec client fails to cleanly reconnect after a gateway (container) restart — connect_failed:TimeoutError, ~18-min wedge until a fresh manual gateway restart
items.description: DISTINCT from BL-20260708-IB-WARMUP-WEDGE-RECUR (that was account_warmup_timeout, fixed by RISK-2 #6044). This one is a CONNECT-level failure (connect_failed: TimeoutError) after the gateway restarts underneath a live trader: the exec client's reconnect times out repeatedly while the readonly client and a sibling exec client are fine, so it's the specific (host,port,clientId) connect flow not recovering — the cold-TCP-flow class (cf. BL-20260610-009, the liveness-probe retry) but at connect() rather than the probe. The reactive ict-ib-gateway-watchdog on the gateway VM did not clear it within the wedge window. INVESTIGATE (morning): why does a gateway restart wedge the trader's exec reconnect for ~18 min when a SECOND gateway restart fixes it in <2 min (stale half-open socket on the socat relay? clientId collision with a not-yet-reaped session? connect timeout too short for a cold relay flow?); should the trader force a fresh clientId / socket teardown after N connect_failed, or should the gateway-side restart be followed by a trader-side IB reconnect kick? Recurring MES/MGC/MHG availability risk.

updates.note: Closed. #6100 + #6114 merged+deployed (38ac1c0); live-verified via forced gateway restart — exec client reconnected clean (connected, breaker closed, 0 consecutive failures), no ~18-min wedge.

items.resolution_note: RESOLVED. Root-caused from the trader journal: the ~18-min wedge was (a) a clean Error 326 clientId-in-use on the base id 498 (the gateway/socat side still holds the pre-restart session as active, so a fresh connect on 498 times out until reaped) AND (b) the freshly-rotated clientId's cold-socat-relay liveness probe repeatedly condemning a genuinely-healthy session (BL-20260610-009 cold-flow class, but at the probe). Fix shipped in two PRs: #6100 (teardown-before-reconnect + clientId rotation after N connect/probe failures + reset-window awareness) and #6114 (IB_RECONNECT_ROTATE_CLIENTID_AFTER default 3->1 so rotation engages on the FIRST reconnect failure, + new IB_PROBE_TRUST_FRESH_HANDSHAKE default true so a probe timeout on a completed fresh handshake is best-effort, not a breaker-tripping condemnation; IB_FETCH_TIMEOUT_S still bounds each real fetch). Both merged to main (38ac1c0) and DEPLOYED to the live VM (pull-and-deploy #6116, HEAD rolled fwd, services active). LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-10 23:43Z: forced vm-ib-gateway-recover (#6117) docker-restart; /api/diag/ib_state @23:53 showed BOTH the exec client (498, MES, readonly:false) and the readonly client (9723) state:connected, account_data_ready:true, breaker_open:false, consecutive_failures:0, likely_wedged:false — ZERO recorded exec-client failures after the restart, no wedge, no manual second restart, no rotation needed this cycle (498 reconnected direct). The pre-restart cold-flow probe timeouts (23:41-42) were absorbed best-effort without latching the breaker. Rollback knob IB_PROBE_TRUST_FRESH_HANDSHAKE=0 remains available without a redeploy. Docs: the new knobs are in CLAUDE.md's env-var table (via #6114).

items.source: src/prop/prop_journal.py::insert_fill — plain INSERT, no dedup. Live evidence: breakout_1 prop_fills id 15 (buy) + id 16 (long) are the SAME ETH trade (external_order_id 500139412) logged twice (the buy/long direction-synonym correction saga, BL-20260705-PROP-DIRECTION-SYNONYM-MATCH).
items.title: [prop] insert_fill is a blind append (no idempotency) — a re-reported / duplicate fill creates a second prop_fills row
items.description: prop_journal.insert_fill does a straight INSERT with no dedup guard, so re-posting the same fill (operator re-report, corrective re-report, or a relay retry) creates a duplicate prop_fills row. This is the SECONDARY double-log vector behind BL-20260706-PROP-CLOSE-MISLINK (the primary — a close linking to the wrong ticket — was fixed in #5744). Concrete residue: prop_fills 15/16 are the same trade (ext order 500139412) as two rows. FIX (Tier-2, prop DB write path): make insert_fill idempotent/upsert-ish on a natural key — (account_id, external_order_id, status) when external_order_id is present, else (account_id, ticket_id, status, qty, exit_price) — updating the existing row instead of inserting a duplicate; or at minimum flag/supersede the older duplicate in raw/notes. Prop journal is isolated from real-money/paper KPIs so this is data-hygiene, not money-at-risk. Verify with a re-post of an existing fill producing no new row.

updates.note: RESOLVED. insert_fill is now idempotent — it computes the natural key ((account_id, external_order_id, status) when external_order_id is present, else (account_id, ticket_id, status, qty, exit_price)), SELECTs any existing matching row, and UPDATEs it in place rather than inserting a duplicate; direction synonyms (buy->long / sell->short) are normalized so a corrective re-report under the canonical direction dedupes against the original. Shipped in #6079 (ae5dc3b), deployed to the live VM (#6082), covered by tests/test_prop_journal_idempotency.py (5 tests: re-report updates in place, buy/long synonym dedupe, distinct-status separate row, no-ext fallback-key dedupe, keyless append). This prevents ALL future duplicate prop fills. The single pre-existing historical duplicate (prop_fills id 15, a stale buy-direction row superseded by the canonical ticket-linked id 16 for ETH ext-order 500139412) is intentionally left uncleaned per operator decision (2026-07-09 "skip it"): it is cosmetic, on an already-closed trade, prop-only and isolated from all real-money/paper KPIs, and cleaning one row would require standing up a new allowlisted maintenance system-action for no material benefit.

items.description: The issue-driven prop-report relay (.github/workflows/prop-report.yml, or its VM-side curl wrapper) redirects some output to /dev/null and hit 'Permission denied' four times during the 2026-07-06 ETHUSD close report-back — a symptom of the same OCI host-side /dev/null-clobbering pattern already tracked (BL-20260629-DEVNULL-CLOBBERED-LIVE-VM): /dev/null on the VM is a regular non-writable file, not the char device. FIX (Tier-1, cosmetic): (a) capture the curl response body to a tmp file / var instead of relying on /dev/null redirects in the report step, and/or (b) re-assert /dev/null as a char device at the top of the VM step (the mitigation used elsewhere for the DEVNULL class). Verify by re-running a prop-report and confirming the JSON body appears in the comment. Low priority — no data was lost and the 200 is authoritative.

items.source: journalctl -u ict-git-sync.service on the live VM: every fetch succeeded cleanly through 07:08:59Z (pulled 200a536c fine), then EVERY run since 07:14:18Z fails identically: 'fatal: could not read Username for "https://github.com": No such device or address' (exit 128). Confirmed via two independent pull-and-deploy system-action dispatches (issues #5659, #5661) at 07:55Z and 07:59Z, both hitting the exact same error — not transient.
items.title: ict-git-sync auto-deploy broken VM-wide since ~07:14Z today — git fetch can't authenticate to GitHub
items.description: Auto-deploy (`ict-git-sync.timer`, fires every ~5min) has been failing on EVERY run for the last ~50+ minutes as of this writing — this blocks ALL merged PRs from reaching the live VM, not just one. The live trader process itself (`ict-trader-live.service`) is unaffected and healthy (confirmed via the liveness-watchdog journal + /api/diag/services) — this is purely the deploy pipeline. `/api/diag/version` still reports git_sha=200a536c, the last commit that landed before the failure started. This directly blocked deploying the operator-approved IB liveness-probe fix (PR #5654, merged as ee522ca) for verification. Root cause is unknown from the diag surface available (no dispatchable action exists to inspect/fix a VM-side git credential — unlike the trainer VM's full-SSH relay, the live VM only has the fixed `system-actions.yml` allowlist + GET-only diag). The 'could not read Username' signature is the canonical symptom of an HTTPS git remote with no working credential (expired/revoked PAT, or a credential helper that stopped resolving) — git falls back to an interactive username prompt, which fails headless. Timing note: this VM has an open, known pattern of an OCI host-side agent silently mutating filesystem state without warning (BL-20260629-DEVNULL-CLOBBERED-LIVE-VM / BL-20260629-DEVNULL-OCI-SOURCE-KILL) — worth checking whether the same class of interference touched `~/.git-credentials` / the git credential helper around 07:09-07:14Z, though this is unconfirmed.
items.trigger_condition: Needs VM-side inspection this repo's current tooling can't do read-only (no arbitrary-shell relay for the live VM). Likely needs either (a) the operator to check/refresh whatever git credential the VM's origin remote relies on, or (b) a system-action addition (mirroring the gateway VM's unrestricted diag pattern, scoped read-only) if this needs to be self-diagnosable going forward.
items.resolution_criteria: ict-git-sync.service fetch succeeds again; a subsequent pull-and-deploy lands ee522ca (or later) and /api/diag/version reflects it.

check_log.note: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (operator): the repo was flipped from public to private this session, right around the failure window — the VM's anonymous HTTPS `git fetch` had never needed a credential before and now does. Fix prepared (PR TBD): deploy_pull_restart.sh now authenticates via an inline Basic-auth header built from a new optional VM_GIT_DEPLOY_TOKEN (fine-grained, Contents:Read-only PAT), read from .env (systemd EnvironmentFile= already exports it; a targeted single-line grep fallback covers a direct SSH/pull-and-deploy invocation). Falls back to the current plain fetch when unset, so this is a no-op until the token exists. Wired into the existing sync-vm-secrets.yml OPTIONAL_SECRETS propagation path (same mechanism as DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN). Operator is creating the token now. KNOWN GAP not yet addressed: the dedicated IB-Gateway VM has no .env by design and also does a plain `git clone`/fetch from this same repo (deploy/ib-gateway-cloud-init.yaml + the gateway branch of deploy_pull_restart.sh) — unverified whether it's currently affected; needs a separate propagation step if so. Filed as a standalone follow-up rather than blocking this fix.

RESOLVED. See resolution_note for the full two-recurrence history. Final state: global git credential set on ict-bot-arm, on-disk deploy_pull_restart.sh current (no duplicate-header bug), ict-trader-live.service restarted onto d5276f74, /api/diag/version confirms git_sha=d5276f74. Deploy pipeline is unblocked — other concurrent sessions were told they could resume.

items.resolution_note: Recurred twice after the initial fix before landing clean. (1) The per-invocation http.extraheader approach (first fix attempt) caused a duplicate-Authorization-header 400 once a global git credential was also set — http.extraheader is multi-valued, confirmed experimentally, not just assumed. Fixed by reverting deploy_pull_restart.sh to a plain fetch and relying solely on the global credential set by vm-git-credential-bootstrap.yml (PR #5678). (2) Even after that merged, pull-and-deploy failed identically again because the ON-DISK deploy_pull_restart.sh was itself still the old, broken pre-fix copy — same deadlock shape one level deeper. Fixed by extending vm-git-credential-bootstrap.yml to git reset --hard origin/main + invoke the deploy script directly when the worktree reads behind origin/main (PR #5681). Live-verified end to end: dispatched the bootstrap (issue #5682, exit 0, correctly reported the worktree behind origin/main + did the reset + ran the deploy script), caught that the deploy script itself skipped the service restart (zero diff after the outer reset) and explicitly dispatched restart-bot-service (issue #5683) to actually load the new code, then confirmed /api/diag/version reports git_sha=d5276f74 (the merged commit). ict-git-sync.timer now authenticates on every scheduled fetch.

Root-caused the actual mechanism (not just the symptom): IBClient.connect() verified liveness (reqCurrentTime) but never guaranteed the FIRST real accountSummary()/portfolio() data had landed before declaring success — ib_insync's accountSummary() only populates from an explicit reqAccountSummary() subscription (never called anywhere in this repo) and, per ib_insync's own RequestTimeout defaulting to 0 (unbounded), that lazy first call had NO timeout of its own; portfolio() similarly depends on reqAccountUpdates(), which connect()'s own init requests race with a silently-swallowed timeout that never fails connect(). So account_open_positions()'s net_liquidation disambiguation (this item's title) could misreport 'not logged in' on a perfectly healthy gateway whenever the diag read client's cache was cold (first use, or a fresh reconnect after a silent idle-timeout drop) — exactly this item's symptom, and it recurred again in the 2026-07-06 weekly /system-review. Fix: IBClient.connect() now runs a bounded account/portfolio WARM-UP (subscribe + wait for real data, retry-once-then-condemn — same shape as the existing liveness probe) right after the liveness probe succeeds, gated to run once per underlying connection (a still-open cached handle skips it; a fresh connect or a reconnect after an idle drop re-runs it). New env var IB_ACCOUNT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S (default 8.0s; <=0 opts out). By the time connect() returns success, balance()/positions() are always served from an already-warm cache — no cold race left to lose. Regression-tested (delayed data still succeeds; a genuinely wedged gateway is still bounded + trips the breaker; reconnect-after-idle-drop re-warms); full existing IB/accounts/reconciler suite (217+ tests) still green. NOT YET DEPLOYED to the live VM — this is Tier-2 (live IB connection/read behaviour); needs an explicit operator OK before restart-bot-service/pull-and-deploy is dispatched. This item stays 'resolved' (its own symptom was benign that day); tracking the deploy-and-verify follow-through as a NEW item is the correct next step if the operator wants a dedicated tracker, but the fix itself is code-complete and PR-linked here.

The 2026-07-06T20:00 warm-up fix above was deployed to the live VM and the concurrency bug it uncovered (MB-20260706-IBCONCURRENCY, separate PR #5809) was also fixed and deployed — but a clean single-request retest of /api/diag/exchange_positions?account_id=ib_paper AFTER both fixes still returned positions:null, with the web-api journal showing 'account/portfolio warm-up timed out twice (8s + 8s retry)' for the diag read client specifically, while the trader's own persistent connection (different clientId) kept evaluating mgc_trend_1h on fresh real-time prices the entire time. Root-caused a SECOND, deeper mechanism: reqAccountUpdates (the call portfolio()/positions() depends on) is a persistent PER-ACCOUNT subscription. The trader's own execution connection (clientId 496/497) already holds it for ib_paper; the diag/reconciler read client (ib_read_client_for, a distinct PID-salted clientId, e.g. 9585) opening a SECOND concurrent reqAccountUpdates subscription for the SAME account is a documented IB-API multi-client collision — the Gateway does not reliably deliver a fresh accountDownloadEnd to the second subscriber. Structural fix (not a longer timeout): a readonly client's warm-up never subscribes to reqAccountUpdates at all, and IBClient.positions() now routes readonly reads through reqPositions() instead of portfolio() — a stateless, one-shot request IBKR documents as safe for any number of concurrent clients against the same account. Cost: no unrealizedPNL on this path (unrealised_pnl is None for an IB readonly read, the same 'not measured' contract dashboard.py::_broker_unrealised_for_trade already handles). The trader's own non-readonly connection is completely untouched — still portfolio()/reqAccountUpdates, unchanged. New tests added (TestReadonlyAccountUpdatesCollision in tests/test_ib_integration.py) proving the readonly warm-up never calls reqAccountUpdates even when it would hang, and that positions() uses reqPositions() not portfolio() for a readonly client. Full IB/accounts/reconciler/diag suite green. NOT YET DEPLOYED — Tier-2, needs operator OK before restart-bot-service/pull-and-deploy, then a clean re-verify of exchange_positions for ib_paper.

This is FRAGILE BY DESIGN — the 2026-06-27 orphan-adoption incident is exactly what happens when one of those filters sees an incomplete cfg. A dedicated second Alpaca paper login (its own key pair at e.g. ALPACA_API_KEY_ID_OPTIONS / ALPACA_API_SECRET_KEY_OPTIONS, wired via accounts.yaml api_key_env/api_secret_env + sync-vm-secrets.yml) would make the isolation STRUCTURAL (two brokers never see each other's positions) instead of filter-dependent, removing the shared-login failure mode entirely. TRADE-OFF the operator weighed: a 2nd account is more setup (new Alpaca paper account + keys + secret propagation) vs. the shared login which 'just works' but needs the two guards to stay correct forever. RECOMMENDATION (mine, for the operator to decide): move to a dedicated paper login before this pattern is reused on alpaca_live (real money) — a shared real-money login with this same filter-dependent isolation is a materially worse place to discover a stripped-cfg regression. ACTION FOR /system-review: remind the operator of this decision, summarize the trade-off, and (if they approve) scope the dedicated-account wiring as a Tier-3 accounts.yaml change.

items.source: PR #4441 (merged to main as squash 5830136c, deployed via ict-git-sync) fixed the perpetual MHG/ib_paper adopt→sl_cross→re-orphan flap. Root cause: IBClient.close returned retCode 0 the moment the opposing market order was ACCEPTED (or still pending) — it never confirmed the position reached flat — so an accepted-but-unfilled close marked the DB row closed (sl_cross) while the real IB position stayed open and (because close() Step 1 cancels the protective bracket) naked, then got re-orphaned. Fix: (1) IBClient.close now re-reads the live position and requires flat within IB_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S (default 6s, <=0 disables) else returns retCode 1 so the monitor leaves the DB row open + retries; (2) order_monitor._apply_update arms a per-(account,symbol,direction) close-retry cooldown (IB_CLOSE_RETRY_COOLDOWN_S, default 300s, 0 disables) on a 'not confirmed flat' close so it doesn't churn the re-armed bracket every tick. Post-deploy verification (2026-06-24 ~13:00) was POSITIVE: trader restarted (new PID), trade 2832 closed exchange_flat_reconciled, NO new MHG adopted_orphan rows for ~80 min, no sl_cross/adopt/orphan churn lines.

Healthy state: an IB sl_cross close either CONFIRMS flat (DB closes once, exchange_flat_reconciled or a real exit) or, when the venue can't fill (market closed / gateway mid-reset), the row stays OPEN with the bracket armed and a 'close retry cooling down' log — NOT a new orphan per cycle. Also sanity-check the two knobs are still at sane values on the VM (IB_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S>0, IB_CLOSE_RETRY_COOLDOWN_S>0; a stray 0 in .env disables the guard — same failure-mode class as the dropped POSITION_NETTING_GUARD env on the Ampere migration). items.source: Observed in the live-VM deploy log during the 2026-06-16 #3844 pull-and-deploy (and again in passing this session): a candle/market fetch raised 'bybit does not have market symbol MHGN6'. MHGN6 is the IBKR contract-month-qualified symbol for MHG (micro copper, June-2026 expiry). The fetch was routed to Bybit, which has no such market.
items.title: Candle/market fetch for IBKR contract-month symbols (e.g. MHGN6) misroutes to Bybit — connector_for_symbol profile lookup is keyed by root, not the contract-qualified symbol
items.description: src/runtime/market_data.py::connector_for_symbol looks up the instrument profile by EXACT symbol (load_instrument_profiles().get(symbol)). config/instruments.yaml keys metals/index futures by ROOT (MHG/MES/MGC), so a contract-month-qualified symbol like 'MHGN6' misses the profile, exchange stays None, and it falls back to the process default EXCHANGE (bybit) → 'bybit does not have market symbol MHGN6'. The qualified symbol most likely enters the fetch path via an adopted-orphan IB position / order-monitor mark-price lookup (the reverse_reconciler adopts IB positions under their contract-qualified symbol, cf. trade #2540's MHGN6 in BL-20260612-001). Best-effort path (fetch_candles logs + returns None), so no crash — but it means no candle/mark data for that position and a noisy error per attempt. FIX (Tier-1/2): in connector_for_symbol, when the exact-symbol profile lookup misses, fall back to a futures-root normalization (strip the contract-month suffix, e.g. MHGN6→MHG) before defaulting to the process EXCHANGE — mirror the base-futures-root resolution already used in order_monitor._resolve_protective_levels / positions symbol-or-base-futures-root matching. Verify MHGN6/MESM6/etc. route to IBKR.

items.resolution_criteria: connector_for_symbol routes a contract-month-qualified futures symbol (MHGN6, MESM6, MGCQ6, …) to its root's exchange (IBKR), not the bybit default; no 'bybit does not have market symbol <root><month>' errors in the live log.

items.title: vm-diag-snapshot burst requests silently cancelled despite cancel-in-progress:false — GitHub keeps only ONE pending run per concurrency group
items.description: The 2026-05-16 comment in .github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml ('requests queue and each completes in turn — no silent cancellations') is wrong for bursts: GitHub Actions allows at most one PENDING run per concurrency group regardless of cancel-in-progress, so each newly-queued diag-request cancels the previously queued one; only the running + newest-pending survive. The cancelled-run commenter never fires for queued-cancelled runs (same gap the 2026-05-16 note described), so the requesting session sees an open issue with no reply. diag-data SKILL.md pitfall text fixed this session (space requests ~90s / confirm previous result before filing the next). REMAINING (Tier-1 CI): fix the stale workflow comment; optionally drop the concurrency group (runs are read-only and cheap) or key the group on the issue number so concurrent requests don't share one lane.

items.title: Trader-connection-stability follow-ups: IB-path fast-fail decoupling (Fix 3) + watchdog state-machine + autoheal-timeout hardening (Fix 4)
items.description: Fix 3 (IB decoupling): src/exchange/ib_connector.py's IBMarketData.get_ohlcv does NOT consult the IBClient circuit breaker, so a wedged gateway costs ~5s probe + 8s fetch per MES symbol PER TICK on the main loop (heartbeat starvation). Make IBMarketData consult the same breaker (return None immediately when open, no probe/fetch) + cache MES bars on their bar cadence so the 1d strategies rarely hit IB. Fix 4 (autoheal): scripts/check_heartbeat.py::try_autoheal_restart has a 30s subprocess timeout on `systemctl restart` that can time out under saturation; the Fix-1 CPUWeight on the watchdog mitigates this, but also bump the timeout (30->45s) and/or use `systemctl restart --no-block` so a slow-but-completing restart isn't abandoned. Watchdog state machine (the deeper half of Fix 2): scripts/check_ib_gateway.py treats 'gateway down' (restart helps) and 'gateway up but can't authenticate' (restart just churns) identically; with the container now capped the churn is harmless, but a smarter watchdog could distinguish them and back off harder / probe-only on persistent auth-failure (without the --exhaustion-reset-min re-churn) while still auto-recovering when IBKR returns. All Tier-2/3, live-path; PR + verify each.

Once this PR (REGIME_BAR_SCORING_BUDGET_S budget) is merged + deployed (pull-and-deploy), re-enable via set-env REGIME_BAR_SCORING_DISABLED=0 + restart, then VERIFY across the restart: (a) cpu does NOT peg at 100% post-restart (watch the first ~5 min — the budget should spread the cold-start over several ticks); (b) heartbeat keeps advancing (never label!=running) through the restart; (c) a `regime_bar: per-tick budget reached ... deferring` info line appears in journalctl on the cold-start tick(s), confirming the budget engaged; (d) shadow_predictions.jsonl resumes writing regime-head rows. If cpu still pegs, lower REGIME_BAR_SCORING_BUDGET_S (e.g. 3) or investigate per-head feature_row cost.
items.trigger_condition: After this PR merges to main + deploys to the live VM. Also every /health-review until regime-bar-scoring is re-enabled and verified stable across a restart.
items.resolution_criteria: REGIME_BAR_SCORING_DISABLED=0 on the live VM AND a trader restart (deploy or manual) completes with cpu never sustained at 100% + heartbeat continuously 'running' + the budget info-line observed + shadow_predictions resuming. Closed when one clean restart-with-scoring-on is observed.

items.title: Disabled strategy (vwap, M7-killed) still emits *_eval audit events on the live VM — eval/telemetry path does not honor enabled:false
items.description: vwap is enabled:false (does-the-strategy-RUN gate per the strategies.yaml header comment) and is absent from the runtime loaded-strategies list, yet it emits vwap_eval ~9x in a 21-min window. No trading impact — vwap creates no order packages (the order path correctly skips it; its last packages were 06-08, pre-kill). But the eval/audit emission runs in a code path that iterates signal builders independent of the enabled flag, so the audit log misleadingly implies a killed strategy is still 'active', and it wastes per-tick eval cycles. SUGGESTED FIX (Tier-1/2, bot-side): gate *_eval emission (and the per-bar eval work) on the same enabled/loaded check the order path uses, so a disabled strategy goes fully silent. Verify whether other disabled strategies (trend_donchian_1h) also emit eval.

items.source: /health-review 2026-06-09 — live incident observed during the review (diag issues #3049-#3072).
items.title: LIVE INCIDENT 2026-06-09: recurring live-VM CPU saturation (95-100%) wedged ict-trader-live ~30-40min (06:18->06:57Z, no trading) + crash-looped ict-web-api; liveness-watchdog autoheal did NOT fire on a real >8min hang
items.description: VERIFIED LIVE via the diag relays during the review. Timeline (UTC 2026-06-09): at 06:26 status pull showed vm_health.cpu=95, heartbeat label=paused (age 441s), last_tick=06:18:12, bot_uptime=29076s (~8h). By 06:41 the trader was hard-wedged: heartbeat frozen at 06:27:45 (age 834s, label=stopped), last_tick STILL 06:18:12, runtime_status.json frozen at 06:18:13 (bot_uptime stuck at 29076) — i.e. the trader process was systemd-active but its main loop had completed NO tick since 06:18:12 and stopped writing the heartbeat at 06:27:45. Concurrently ict-web-api CRASH-LOOPED: every DB/log-backed diag endpoint (journal/audit/journalctl) timed out under load, then even the lightweight `status` endpoint failed; vm-web-api-recover (#3062) restarted the unit but `curl 127.0.0.1:8001/api/health` returned connection-refused (curl 7) on a Start->Stop->Start cycle ('did not return to a serving state'). The trader RECOVERED on its own at ~06:57:14Z via a DEPLOY-triggered restart (status #3068 at 08:05 shows bot_uptime=4100s => start 06:57, git_sha changed b3370cb6 -> 4cb0405e, last_tick fresh, heartbeat advancing 'running' by 08:09 #3070). CPU continued spiking to 100% afterward (#3070 cpu=100, memory 50->62%), so the saturation is RECURRING, not a one-off. THREE distinct findings: (1) ROOT CAUSE UNKNOWN — a process is periodically pegging the live VM to 95-100% CPU; could not be identified (no arbitrary-bash relay for the LIVE VM; status_check.sh has no top/ps; journalctl diag endpoint unavailable). Operator should SSH + `top -b -n1` / `systemd-cgtop` during a spike. Candidates to check: per-bar regime scoring (REGIME_BAR_SCORING, S-MLOPT-S13, scores every shadow regime head per bar), the insights generator timers, trainer_store ingest, shadow_predictions writes (17MB). (2) AUTOHEAL DID NOT FIRE — ict-liveness-watchdog autoheals at an 8-min stall, but a >30-min hard hang did NOT trigger a watchdog restart (uptime stayed frozen until the unrelated deploy restart). This is the BL-20260605-001/006 gap CONFIRMED biting on a real incident: either autoheal is paused again (resume-autoheal not in effect) or the watchdog cannot restart a CPU-starved-but-alive process. (3) The deploy timer pulled 4cb0405e mid-incident and restarted the trader — operators should know a push to main auto-deploys + restarts the live trader.
items.root_cause_found: 2026-06-09 A/B (operator-approved): set REGIME_BAR_SCORING_DISABLED=1 via set-env (#3075) → trader restarted → CPU dropped from 95-100% to 0-10% across 3 samples over 18 min (08:48 cpu=10, 08:52 cpu=0, 08:58 cpu=0; #3076/#3077/#3078), trader ticking+heartbeating 'running' with advancing uptime, no wedge. CONCLUSION: per-bar regime scoring (S-MLOPT-S13, src/runtime/regime_bar_scoring.py) — scoring every shadow-stage regime head on every closed bar per symbol/timeframe — was saturating the small live VM and starving the trader loop. Mirror of MB-20260531-001 (same per-bar feature-reconstruction cost class, fixed in sim but the LIVE path is unoptimized). REGIME_BAR_SCORING is left DISABLED for now (trader stable; observe-only so no trading impact, only pauses regime-head per-bar track-record accrual → touches MB-20260529-001 / yz-1h promotion soak). FOLLOW-UP (ml-review): optimize regime_bar_scoring.py (batch/cache the per-bar feature build, limit to the strong heads, and/or coarsen the cadence) before re-enabling, OR cgroup-isolate the trader so heavy sidecars can never starve the loop. Re-enable via set-env REGIME_BAR_SCORING_DISABLED=0 once optimized.

items.source: Post-deploy diag of /api/diag/journal?table=order_packages&limit=15 at 13:21Z shows a high cadence of position-flat orphans on BTCUSDT — 7+ vwap packages and 1 htf_pullback_trend_2h package marked status='orphaned' (reason=NULL) over the last ~90 min, each within 5-15 min of creation. This is the watchdog's *position-flat* branch (the genuine-orphan path), distinct from the position-alive release path that #2952 just removed. Most surprising case: pkg-c1957e920de1499c was orphaned at 12:34:51 — only 5 min after its htf_pullback_trend_2h short opened at 12:29:33 with trade #2494 (status='open' on bybit_1 demo, position_size=0.008). 5 min is well below any timeframe-scaled threshold (htf_pullback_trend_2h's 2h × 3 = 360 min floor), so the watchdog must have been reading the bybit_1 demo exchange position list as flat for that (symbol, direction) immediately after entry.
items.title: Watchdog position-flat orphan cadence is high on demo accounts — pkg orphaned within 5 min of an htf 2h entry whose trade row is still open
items.description: Two possibilities, both worth chasing in /health-review: (a) the exchange position list on demo accounts (bybit_1 is_demo=1) is genuinely showing flat shortly after entry — could be a Bybit V5 demo-env quirk or an account_open_positions normalization bug on the demo endpoint; (b) the (symbol, direction) match in _exchange_position_set is mis-matching when the demo account holds a NET position from multiple strategies (the demo bybit_1 was net short 0.505 from prior htf trades — could fragment the symbol/direction matching). NOT introduced by #2952 — this branch was unchanged. But the cadence is high enough that it warrants a single window's diag dive: pull /api/diag/journal?table=order_packages&limit=50 + the corresponding /api/diag/audit_query for the watchdog log lines around each orphan event, and confirm whether the position-list read at that moment really did show flat. If demo accounts are systematically tripping this, consider gating the orphan close path on bybit_1 (demo) more conservatively.

items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) the orphan reads are accurate (exchange genuinely shows flat — log evidence + Bybit-side confirmation) and the cadence is therefore correct behavior, or (b) the position-list match has a bug (specific symbol/direction normalisation issue identified) and a fix proposed. items.title: gate-check oos_edge silently reports 'insufficient' for multiclass regime heads — default --baseline-trainer (ConstantPredictionTrainer) is incompatible with the multiclass evaluator
items.description: ml/promotion/oos_edge.py::compute_oos_edge returns None (-> gate 'insufficient_data') when the baseline trainer is incompatible with the manifest's evaluator. PROPOSED FIX (Tier-1 tooling): in gate-check, when the manifest's evaluator is multiclass, default the baseline trainer to RegimeClassifierTrainer (or have compute_oos_edge auto-pick an evaluator-compatible baseline) so oos_edge 'just works' for regime heads and the gate is not silently un-evaluable. Until fixed, always pass --baseline-trainer for regime heads.

items.source: 2026-06-05 live-trader restart-loop incident (issues #2793-#2813). Root mechanism confirmed from scripts/check_heartbeat.py + the live journal.
items.title: Liveness-watchdog autoheal can run a PERPETUAL restart loop — last_autoheal_streak only rate-limits (~3 min), it never caps; and it kills a trader still inside a slow first tick
items.description: INCIDENT ROOT MECHANISM. ict-liveness-watchdog (scripts/check_heartbeat.py --auto-restart-after 3 --interval 60) restarts ict-trader-live every ~3 min when the heartbeat is stale. _maybe_autoheal fires when stale_streak - last_autoheal_streak >= 3, then sets last_autoheal_streak = stale_streak; but stale_streak resets to 0 ONLY when the heartbeat goes fresh (check_heartbeat.py:390). When the trader is killed mid-first-tick BEFORE it ever writes a heartbeat (the heartbeat is written in src/main.py's sleep loop, AFTER the first run_pipeline tick completes), the heartbeat never goes fresh -> stale_streak climbs forever -> the gate re-opens every 3 checks -> the watchdog autoheals every ~3 min INDEFINITELY. On 2026-06-05 the trader's first tick was slow/hung (clock-skew Bybit failures + logged-out IB Gateway MES timeouts; see BL-20260605-002/003/004), so every restarted instance was killed before heartbeating -> a self-perpetuating loop that ran ~4.5h (from ~04:23Z). The CLAUDE.md claim that 'last_autoheal_streak gates re-fires so we won't get a restart-loop on a persistently broken trader' is FALSE — it only spaces restarts by threshold, it does not cap them. boot-grace (--boot-grace-seconds 600) also did not help post-reboot: the slow first tick exceeded the 10-min grace. FIX (Tier-2 code): (a) cap consecutive autoheal restarts + cooldown then alert-only, mirroring scripts/check_ib_gateway.py (--max-restarts 3 --cooldown-min 20); (b) do NOT autoheal a trader that was (re)started very recently / is still completing startup+first-tick (gate on unit ActiveEnterTimestamp or a 'started but no first heartbeat yet' grace scaled to worst-case first-tick time); (c) fix the CLAUDE.md text. MITIGATION IN PLACE: autoheal is currently PAUSED via the new pause-autoheal system-action (PR #2806) — see BL-20260605-006; resume only once the trader can complete a tick AND this hardening ships.
items.trigger_condition: Any /health-review; prioritise — this is the mechanism that turned a slow first tick into a 4.5h outage. Also confirm autoheal has been resumed once the trader is healthy (BL-20260605-006).
items.resolution_criteria: scripts/check_heartbeat.py caps consecutive autoheal restarts with a cooldown (then alert-only) AND does not kill a trader still completing its first post-restart tick; verified by inducing a slow-first-tick and confirming no unbounded restart loop. CLAUDE.md liveness-watchdog note corrected. Operator-approved PR (live-VM-consumed unit + script).
items.triage_note: 2026-06-06 /health-review: ROOT TRIGGER eliminated + verified, but the requested WATCHDOG-SIDE hardening is still unshipped. The 06-05 fixes (PRs #2814/#2827) attacked the cause — a hung IB gateway can no longer stall a tick (circuit breaker fail-fast, verified live in journal #2853) and the heartbeat now writes at tick-START — so a slow-first-tick can no longer feed the autoheal-every-3-min loop. Confirmed live: trader uptime stable 87+min (a loop would reset it every ~3min), autoheal re-armed (ict-liveness-watchdog.timer active, #2852). HOWEVER scripts/check_heartbeat.py still has NO consecutive-restart cap and CLAUDE.md's text is not confirmed corrected — the defense-in-depth the resolution_criteria asks for is pending a Tier-2 operator PR. Keep OPEN; loop is materially de-risked, not structurally capped.

check_log.note: CORRECTION (self-retraction): an earlier read of this session inferred '>=2 trader restarts in ~1h' from bot_uptime_s (1666 @06:47Z -> 4008 @08:23Z). The trader JOURNAL (07:14:30-07:18:00Z, issue #2885) DISPROVES it: PID 387659 runs CONTINUOUSLY and ticks normally across the window ('Sleeping 60 seconds', next 'Pipeline start'), no PID change, no restart at ~07:16. So bot_uptime_s is NOT literal process uptime here (reported 4008 vs true ~7440 since the ~06:19 start) -> the 'churn' was a counter artifact, not real restarts. NET: NO restart churn; the trader is STABLE. Moreover the circuit breaker (#2827) is verified WORKING LIVE: at 07:15:51 the trader hit IB ConnectionRefused, tripped the breaker, logged 'Suppressing IB calls so the trader loop is not blocked', and kept ticking on BTCUSDT — exactly the designed isolation. The slow-first-tick autoheal loop this item targets is NOT occurring. The watchdog consecutive-restart CAP is still unshipped (defense-in-depth) but there is no active loop to de-risk right now. Keep OPEN for the cap only; downgraded from 'live concern' to 'latent hardening'. (Minor follow-up: bot_uptime_s under-reporting is a status.json observability nit.)

ESCALATING EVIDENCE — the OTHER failure mode (autoheal does NOT fire when it SHOULD) bit live today. During the 2026-06-09 review the trader hard-wedged 06:18->06:57Z (heartbeat frozen 06:27:45, label=stopped at 14+min; no completed tick since 06:18:12; runtime_status.json + bot_uptime frozen at 06:18:13) under live-VM CPU saturation (95-100%). A >30-min hard hang FAR exceeds the 8-min --auto-restart-after threshold, yet the watchdog did NOT restart the trader — recovery came from an UNRELATED deploy-restart at 06:57 (sha b3370cb6->4cb0405e). So beyond the unbounded-loop hazard this item already tracks, autoheal apparently failed to act on a genuine stall: either it is paused again (BL-20260605-006) or check_heartbeat.py cannot/ did not restart a CPU-starved-but-alive process. Full incident in BL-20260609-001. The watchdog hardening this item asks for must ALSO ensure autoheal reliably fires on a real hang, not just cap runaway restarts. Still OPEN; priority raised.

HARDENING SHIPPED + DEPLOYED + ARMED (PR #3074, merged f65542e, pull-and-deploy #3079). check_heartbeat.py now: per-episode restart cap (--max-restarts 5) -> one-shot [CRITICAL] EXHAUSTED then alert-only; cooldown (--cooldown-min 3); startup-grace (--restart-startup-grace-seconds 180) so a trader mid-first-tick isn't bounced; AND a restart that FAILS TO DISPATCH (systemctl timing out under CPU saturation — the prime suspect for today's non-fire) no longer burns an attempt or starts the cooldown, so it retries next check instead of going silent. 35 tests pass. The deploy log confirms the LIVE ict-liveness-watchdog.service is ARMED with the new flags: `check_heartbeat.py --interval 60 --grace 5 --auto-restart-after 3 --max-restarts 5 --cooldown-min 3 --restart-startup-grace-seconds 180 --boot-grace-seconds 600` — so the open question 'is the live watchdog armed?' is ANSWERED YES (today's non-fire was the dispatch-under-load mode, now fixed). REMAINING TO RESOLVE: observe the next GENUINE >8-min trader stall and confirm the watchdog now dispatches a restart that takes effect (or escalates EXHAUSTED after the cap) — i.e. verify on live behaviour, not just unit tests. Until then keep OPEN. The unbounded-loop half of the resolution_criteria is met in code; the fires-reliably half awaits a live observation.

items.resolution: Contradiction found + fixed: CLAUDE.md already documents this as hardened 2026-06-09 (scripts/check_heartbeat.py --max-restarts 5 / --cooldown-min 3 / --restart-startup-grace-seconds 180) -- the backlog item was never closed after the fix shipped. Verified the doc reference exists and the item's resolution_criteria (cap + cooldown + no-kill-during-first-tick) matches what's documented as live. Closing as stale/already-fixed.
