items.source: 2026-06-05 incident — trader journal for pid 1254/29483/43093 shows the first run_pipeline tick blocking on market-data fetches.
items.title: Per-tick market-data fetches (IBKR/MES + Bybit) block the BTCUSDT pipeline + heartbeat — a down PAPER gateway / a clock-skewed Bybit auth can stall the LIVE-money loop and the liveness signal
items.description: INCIDENT CONTRIBUTOR. The first run_pipeline tick synchronously fetches market data for every tick symbol. With the IB Gateway logged out, each MES/IBKR fetch times out ~10s x 3 timeframes (ib_insync: Connected -> Disconnected -> 'API connection failed: TimeoutError'); and with the VM clock skewed (BL-20260605-003) the Bybit signed market-data fetch fails (ErrCode 10002) and intermittently HARD-HANGS (pid 29483 sat at 'Pipeline start' 29 min consuming ~1 min CPU = blocked on a network call, no enforced timeout). Because the heartbeat is only written AFTER a tick completes, a stalled fetch starves the heartbeat -> the liveness watchdog autoheals (BL-20260605-001) -> restart loop. NET: a secondary/paper data source (IBKR) being down, or a transient Bybit auth failure, can take down the live-money trader. FIX (Tier-2 code): make per-tick market-data fetches non-fatal to the loop + heartbeat — short, enforced timeouts on every connector fetch so none can block indefinitely; skip/short-circuit a symbol whose feed is down rather than blocking the whole tick; and/or write the heartbeat from a path that cannot be starved by a hung fetch (separate liveness thread, or write heartbeat at tick-START as well as tick-end). The dashboard /api/bot/candles already fails best-effort; the trader signal-builder fetch path needs the same discipline.
items.trigger_condition: Any /health-review; or whenever a market-data source (IBKR gateway / Bybit) outage coincides with trader heartbeat staleness.
items.resolution_criteria: A down IBKR gateway and/or a transient Bybit fetch failure no longer prevents the trader from completing a tick + writing a heartbeat within the watchdog window — verified by inducing an IBKR-down condition and confirming BTCUSDT keeps ticking + heartbeating. Tier-2 code (src/runtime market-data path + src/main heartbeat) — operator-approved PR.
items.resolution: FIXED + VERIFIED LIVE. PR #2814 (IB_FETCH_TIMEOUT_S default 8s) bounds every IB market-data fetch; PR #2827 added a post-connect liveness probe (IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S) + circuit breaker (IB_BREAKER_COOLDOWN_S) in IBClient.connect() AND moved the heartbeat write to tick-START as well as tick-end. Verified in this review's trader journal (issue #2853, 2026-06-06 06:08-06:12Z): with the IB gateway down (127.0.0.1:4002 ConnectionRefused) every IB connect fails FAST and trips 'circuit breaker OPEN ... Suppressing IB calls so the trader loop is not blocked'; meanwhile the BTCUSDT loop keeps ticking every ~60-75s and the heartbeat advances every 60s (status #2852: heartbeat age 8s, uptime stable 87min, last_tick current). A down gateway no longer stalls the tick or starves the heartbeat — resolution criteria met. The watchdog-side autoheal cap (defense-in-depth) is tracked separately under BL-20260605-001.

items.source: 2026-06-05 incident — pybit ErrCode 10002 on the live trader: req_timestamp[1780648878986] vs server_timestamp[1780648885508] = ~6522 ms skew, persisting AFTER a full VM reboot.
items.title: OPERATOR/INFRA: live VM clock skewed ~6.5s (exceeds Bybit recv_window 5000ms) — NTP not correcting it even post-reboot; breaks Bybit signed requests + contributes to the first-tick hang
items.description: OPERATOR/INFRA ACTION LIKELY NEEDED — Claude has no allowlisted lever for the VM clock. The live trader logs pybit ErrCode 10002 'invalid request, please check your server timestamp or recv_window' with req_timestamp ~6.5s BEHIND Bybit server_timestamp. 6.5s > the 5000ms recv_window, so every Bybit signed request (market data, balances, orders) fails until pybit widens recv_window + retries. This persisted AFTER the 2026-06-05 reboot, so systemd-timesyncd/chrony is NOT keeping the clock disciplined (NTP egress blocked? service not running? OCI clocksource issue?). Beyond the restart-loop contribution, a 6.5s skew is independently TRADING-IMPACTING (Bybit can reject signed ORDER requests on timestamp). INVESTIGATE: is chrony/systemd-timesyncd active + reaching NTP from the OCI VM; consider widening the bot pybit recv_window as a stopgap, but the real fix is clock discipline. Needs operator (or a new sanctioned time-sync system-action) — no current allowlisted action runs timedatectl/chronyc on the live VM.

items.resolution_criteria: Live VM clock disciplined to <1s of true time (NTP working), pybit ErrCode 10002 lines gone, Bybit signed requests succeed first-try. Operator fixes NTP/chrony, or a sanctioned time-sync path is added.
items.resolution: RESOLVED on current evidence (re-open if ErrCode 10002 recurs). PR #2814 added a sanctioned `sync-clock` system-action — the previously-missing Claude-dispatchable time-sync lever called for in the resolution_criteria. This review's live trader journal (issue #2853, 150-line tail through 2026-06-06 06:12Z) shows NO pybit ErrCode 10002 lines and Bybit 'market data environment: mainnet' signed requests succeeding on every tick — the ~6.5s skew that broke Bybit signed requests on 2026-06-05 is gone. Criteria 'ErrCode 10002 lines gone + Bybit signed requests succeed' met. Caveat: durable NTP/chrony discipline across multiple days was not separately confirmed this run — if 10002 reappears, re-open and dispatch sync-clock / escalate the underlying NTP egress.

items.triage_note: 2026-06-06 /health-review: STILL UNRESOLVED — IB Gateway intentionally STOPPED since the 06-05 incident (#2839 stopped the up-but-unauthenticated container after IBC login wouldn't complete: exit-1112 loop / 'did not confirm login within 150s'). Live journal #2853 confirms 127.0.0.1:4002 ConnectionRefused on every tick → MES + MGC + MHG dark (strategies raise 'no candle data' and skip). NO trading-loop impact (PR #2827 circuit breaker isolates it cleanly — verified). MES/metals stay dark until the IBKR-login root cause is fixed and the gateway is re-provisioned. check_log.note: RE-CONFIRMED still down + still cleanly isolated. (1) ib-gateway-watchdog journal (#2884): every 5-min probe 08:18->09:21Z reports healthy=False reason='connect failed ... ConnectionRefusedError [Errno 111] 127.0.0.1:4002' with action=none — i.e. the watchdog does NOT auto-restart a connect-REFUSED (fully-stopped) gateway; its restart path is built for the wedged/logged-out state (connected=true, net_liq=None), not a stopped container. That is consistent with #2839 having INTENTIONALLY stopped it (auto-restart would just re-enter the IBC login loop), but means the watchdog can't bring metals back on its own once the login fix lands — re-provision must be manual/operator-driven. (2) Trader journal (#2885, 07:15:51Z) independently shows the breaker tripping on the same ConnectionRefused and 'Suppressing IB calls so the trader loop is not blocked' — BTCUSDT keeps trading. MES/MGC/MHG remain dark by this known cause. No change to status; carry forward until the IBKR-login root cause is fixed + gateway re-provisioned.

RECURRED (operator-reported ~21:44Z) + diagnosed + watchdog gap fixed. State this time differs from 06-05/06-06: the container was UP (Up 12h, last restart ~09:53Z) and the gateway LOGS IN CLEANLY — ib_insync 'Connected'/'Logged on server version 176', all 3 data farms (usfarm/ushmds/secdefnj) report OK — but the trader's 5s reqCurrentTime liveness probe times out (PR #2827) and the read-path client's 'account updates request timed out' independently confirms a GENUINE upstream IBKR session wedge (not a too-tight probe). So this is the wedged-but-up signature (connected=true, net_liq=None), NOT the stopped-container case. RECOVERY: fired vm-ib-gateway-recover TWICE (#3145 21:53Z; #3157 22:11Z). Both did a clean docker restart + clean IBC paper login (exit 0, no 2FA, ReadOnlyApi=false, farms OK; ushmds even went 2107 inactive->2106 OK). gateway-logs (#3156) showed clean login + no 2103/2105 farm-broken errors, just repeated 'remove Client 498/497/9548' (trader connect->probe-fail->disconnect). YET MES/MGC/MHG stayed dark through 22:17Z — two clean restarts, one post-CME-reopen (17:00 CT), did NOT make the IBKR session service requests. => Residual cause is IBKR-SIDE (degraded paper session for DUQ325724 that a container restart can't clear). Per operator: WAIT for IBKR self-heal (these usually clear within hours / by IBKR's next reset; the watchdog auto-recovers once a probe reads healthy) — do NOT keep hammering restarts. WHY THE WATCHDOG DIDN'T SELF-HEAL: journals (#3150 16:00->17:31Z, #3142-window 20:33->21:28Z) show EVERY 5-min probe healthy=False net_liq=None but action=none for 5.5h+ — it spent its 3-restart budget EARLY (in/near the reset window, when re-login can't re-establish the session) and then went permanent alert-only for the whole episode. FIX SHIPPED (draft PR, branch claude/ib-gateway-recovery-ooh9xq): add --exhaustion-reset-min (default 120) to scripts/check_ib_gateway.py + the deploy unit — re-arms the spent budget after 2h of no restart so a multi-hour wedge is retried once IBKR recovers; loop-proof (re-arm only after a long quiet gap); 0 reverts to old behaviour. ACTION FOR NEXT /health-review: (a) re-check whether the IBKR session self-healed — ibkr_mes_pull status:ok + mes/mgc/mhg_pullback evals reappearing + watchdog probe healthy=True; (b) confirm the --exhaustion-reset-min PR merged+deployed and, on the next real multi-hour wedge, that the re-arm path fires (action=restart after the reset window) — cf. BL-20260528-001.

items.source: /health-review — operator-flagged squeeze_breakout_4h Telegram sequence (2026-05-31 16:00-16:15 UTC)
items.title: Misleading 'TRADE OPENED — SHORT' ping on an intent_reduce leg (carries parent LONG's entry/SL/TP)
items.description: VERIFIED ON LIVE DATA, NOT A REAL TRADING BUG — notification-only. When the multi-strategy intent layer emits an intent_reduce/close leg, coordinator._delta_to_legs does dataclasses.replace(pkg, direction=delta.side) to flip the leg's direction to the opposite (reduce-only) side, but KEEPS the parent package's entry/sl/tp. execute_pkg then fires enqueue_trade_open(side=pkg.direction) (execute.py:881) for the reduce leg, so the operator sees '🟢 TRADE OPENED — BTCUSDT SHORT' with Entry 73693.8 / SL 72385.78 (BELOW) / TP 80989.49 (ABOVE) — SL/TP levels that are correct for a LONG, not a short. Ground truth (trade 1949, bybit_1): setup_type=intent_reduce, a 0.007 reduce-only SHORT leg trimming the open LONG position (pkg-838fe5ef, dir=long, the squeeze 4h winner), NOT a new short entry. The position was never short. Two sub-issues: (a) a reduce/close leg should not fire the 'TRADE OPENED' lifecycle ping at all (it's a partial close, not an open) — or should be labelled 'POSITION REDUCED'; (b) if it does ping, it must not show the parent's open-side SL/TP on the opposite-side leg. Fix is in the notification path only (execution_diagnostics.enqueue_trade_open call site in execute.py + the reduce-leg branch in coordinator), Tier-2 (touches execute.py / coordinator.py which the live VM consumes) — propose via PR, do not self-merge.

items.resolution: Fixed by PR #2476 (merged Tier-2, 2026-05-31, per S-PROFIT-GAPS-2026-05-31 sprint log): 'reduce-only legs no longer fire the TRADE OPENED — SHORT ping with the parent long's SL/TP' (11 new tests). Fix is live on the running sha f91aa32 (post-#2476). Live re-verification against a fresh reduce leg is opportunistic — no reduce leg fired in this review's quiet window — but the notification-path code fix is shipped + tested. Closing on the fix; re-open only if a misleading reduce-leg ping recurs.

items.title: '🚨 ALL accounts failed to dispatch' fires on an expected flip_suppressed_hold_policy no-op (false alarm)
items.description: VERIFIED ON LIVE DATA, NOT A REAL TRADING BUG — alerting false-positive. coordinator.multi_account_execute emits the high-priority 'ALL accounts failed to dispatch' roll-up whenever NO account placed a trade in a round (line 1617: `not any(r.trade_id)`). But under FLIP_POLICY=hold (the live default since PR #2451), an opposite-side signal against an open position is INTENTIONALLY suppressed to a noop (intent_noop:flip_suppressed_hold_policy) — zero trades placed is the CORRECT, designed outcome, not a dispatch failure. On 2026-05-31 16:15 the squeeze short signal (id 1951 bybit_1 / 1952 bybit_2) was correctly held (open long present), yet the operator got a 🚨 ALL-accounts-failed alert. The roll-up should treat a round where every account result is an intent_noop (at_target / flip_suppressed_hold_policy / hold) as a benign no-op, NOT a failure — only genuine errors (RiskBreach, exchange_rejected, missing creds) should trip the 🚨 alarm. Fix in coordinator.py:1617 guard (exclude intent_noop reasons) + possibly execution_diagnostics.enqueue_all_accounts_failed_dispatch. Tier-2 (live-path file) — propose via PR.

items.title: ib_paper account has no ib_port — MES order client cannot reach IB Gateway
items.description: The live trader logs `ib_client_for(ib_paper): no ib_port set (config or IB_PORT env) — cannot reach IB Gateway.` on every tick that routes to ib_paper. IB *market data* works (the gateway is up after the 2026-05-25 restart and MES candle fetches succeed via IBMarketData on 127.0.0.1:4002), so MES ticks complete fast and the heartbeat is stable. But the ib_paper account's ORDER client (src/units/accounts/clients.py::ib_client_for) has no ib_port configured, so it cannot place orders on MES — the account effectively collects signals/data but can't execute. If MES is intended to trade (paper), config/accounts.yaml::ib_paper needs `ib_port: 4002` (or the IB_PORT env on the trader unit). Pre-existing (predates this session); surfaced during post-deploy verification. Operator was informed in chat 2026-05-25 and chose to log it rather than fix immediately.

items.resolution: PR #2167 (squashed as 288d9bf) forwarded ib_host/ib_port/ib_account/ib_client_id through _load_account_cfgs_for_reconcile in src/runtime/order_monitor.py. The original diagnosis attributed the warning to the ORDER client (coordinator.py::multi_account_execute calling ib_client_for(account_cfg)), but that path's account_cfg already carries ib_port via getattr(account, 'ib_port', None) at coordinator.py:1045 — confirmed by reading the code. The actual emitter was the MONITOR RECONCILER path: _load_account_cfgs_for_reconcile() built an account_cfg dict that only forwarded a subset of fields and dropped the IB connection keys, so account_open_positions(cfg) → ib_read_client_for(account) → ib_client_for(...) → account.get('ib_port') = None → warning + return None. Fired from 4 call sites in order_monitor.py (1523, 1877, 2491, 3463), each on a 60s monitor tick — hence the per-tick spam. Post-deploy verification on diag-request #2169 confirmed: 'ib_client_for warning count: 0' across 300 lines / ~5 ticks; reconciler successfully opened the IB read socket (clientId 9731 visible at 17:57:38). MES order dispatch was never actually blocked — the data-collection-only framing in the original description was incorrect.

items.description: src/runtime/intent_multiplexer.py::_collect_intents (the live path; pipeline uses multiplexed_intents) catches a builder exception with only `logger.warning('strategy X raised ... skipping this tick')` and continues. items.source: operator flagged a live BTCUSDT trade whose TP (~143,210) sat ~2x the BTC price / above the all-time high
items.title: EXPECTED, NOT A BUG: trend_donchian (+ fade/squeeze) place a far ~50R 'unreachable sentinel' TP — don't re-flag it as a broken take-profit
items.description: A live trend_donchian BTCUSDT long showed TP=143,210.10 with SL=76,355.40 (entry ~77,666; current ~77,300). This is the DESIGNED 50R sentinel, not a malfunction. trend_donchian/fade_breakout_4h/squeeze_breakout_4h have NO fixed profit target (matches their backtests, which have no TP) — the Chandelier ATR trailing stop is the sole profit exit. But the pipeline's dispatch gate requires every order to carry BOTH an SL and a TP, so the TP is parked tp_r*risk away (tp_r=50.0 in config/strategies.yaml:153/216/259) where it can't realistically fill (max single-trade excursion in 3yr backtest ~11R). Signature to recognize it: reward:risk ~= 50:1. Math check on this trade: TP = entry + 50*(entry - SL) => 77,666.27 + 50*1,310.87 = 143,209.8 ~= 143,210.10. Formula lives at src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py:190/195 (order_package) and the trade is protected by the live ratcheting trail in monitor() at trend_donchian.py:285 (moves SL up only, never loosens). The TP-cross close at trend_donchian.py:342 exists only for completeness. A far TP carries no margin/liquidation risk; if BTC ever printed 143k the trade would simply close at +50R. The only live strategy that emits this is trend_donchian (turtle_soup uses tp1_at_r 1.0 / tp2_at_r 3.0, ict_scalp tp_at_r 1.5, vwap a VWAP-anchored TP) — fade/squeeze share the 50R sentinel and (as of 2026-05-25) also run execution: live, so their 50R TPs now appear on real bybit_2 order packages too — still the intended sentinel (see BL-20260525-008).
items.trigger_condition: Any /health-review run that scores a trend_donchian / fade_breakout_4h / squeeze_breakout_4h order package and sees a TP far from price (~50R / ~2x BTC). Recognize it as the intended sentinel — do NOT score it as a TP defect.
items.resolution_criteria: Informational standing note; nothing to fix. Close only if the 50R-sentinel mechanism is itself removed (e.g. the pipeline stops requiring a TP for trail-only strategies, or tp_r is changed in an operator-approved Tier-3 PR).

items.source: Investigating the trend_donchian stuck-watchdog alert (trade 1722 / pkg-ac6bb4b3b33f4339); fixed the alert symptom in PR #2002
items.title: Zero-sized same-direction reinforcement signals persist as open order_packages (clutter + watchdog churn)
items.description: trend_donchian (and any breakout strategy) re-fires a same-direction signal on each new bar while the breakout persists. The intent multiplexer correctly refuses to pyramid onto an already-open position — it sizes the reinforcement to target_qty=0.0 (aggregation_reason 'same_direction_reinforcement: ... max target_qty=0.0', sized_qty_by_account={}) — but the zero-qty package is STILL persisted as status='open' with linked_trade_id set, even though no exchange order was placed. These ghost packages never close on their own; their updated_at goes stale and they accumulate in order_packages, and they are what trips the stuck-strategy watchdog (the live snapshot for trade 1722 showed pkg-ac6bb4b3b33f4339 and earlier ones already watchdog_released_alive). PR #2002 made the watchdog timeframe-aware so it no longer false-alerts on these, but the underlying clutter remains. Root fix: a reinforcement that sizes to 0 (no order to monitor) should NOT create a lingering open order_packages row — either skip persisting it, persist it with a terminal status (e.g. status='skipped'/'no_order' + close_reason), or auto-close it so it's never gated/monitored/watchdog'd. Verify the strategy_monocle gate (pipeline.py::_has_open_package_for_strategy) and the per-strategy gates still behave correctly afterward.
items.trigger_condition: Any /health-review run; or whenever order_packages shows multiple open same-direction zero-qty packages for one live position. Investigate the intent_multiplexer / order-package persistence path.
items.resolution_criteria: A same-direction reinforcement that aggregates to target_qty=0 no longer leaves a lingering status='open' order_packages row (it is skipped or persisted terminal), so ghost packages stop accumulating and the stuck-watchdog has nothing benign to flag. Order-path change (Tier-2): open a draft PR + operator review.

items.source: /health-review 2026-05-27 — three of six diag-relay issues opened back-to-back never returned a comment
items.title: vm-diag-snapshot relay: subset of issues opened in quick succession never comment+close (stuck OPEN; 38 stale opens accumulated since 2026-05-17)
items.description: This review opened six diag issues at 2026-05-27T07:19:28..54Z. Three returned comments within 30s and auto-closed normally (#2125 status, #2128 order_packages, #2130 trainer-vm). Three never returned a comment in 16+ min and stayed OPEN (#2126 services, #2127 audit, #2129 trades). Cross-check: there are now 38 open vm-diag-request issues going back to #1327 (2026-05-17) — a chronic accumulation. Hypothesis: when issues open within seconds of each other, the concurrency-group serializer (`group: vm-diag-snapshot, cancel-in-progress: false`) starts them but a subset of runs fail/timeout SSH or curl in a way that the post-step `if: cancelled()` / `if: failure()` comment-back step doesn't fire — so the issue is left open with no comment. The 2026-05-16 commentary in vm-diag-snapshot.yml already flagged this exact failure mode (#1278/#1281/#1284). Effect: /health-review can't reliably pull a full state set in one fire; chronic open-issue clutter on the repo. Code-level fix needed in .github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml: add an always() post-step that drops a 'workflow ran but produced no output / failed at step X' comment so the issue stops looking 'in flight'.
items.trigger_condition: Any /health-review run; or any session that opens >2 diag issues in quick succession and notices subsequent ones never return.
items.resolution_criteria: vm-diag-snapshot.yml carries an `if: always()` (or `if: cancelled()` + `if: failure()`) closing-comment step that ALWAYS posts a result-or-error comment + closes the issue, so no diag issue can be left silently OPEN. Then sweep the 38 stale open issues — close as 'workflow run silently failed; re-open if you need the data'. Code change (Tier-1 observability); not editable from /health-review.
items.resolution: ROOT-CAUSE refined 2026-05-27: vm-diag-snapshot.yml ALREADY carries `if: cancelled()` + `if: failure()` + an implicit-success handler that together cover every terminal job state. The remaining gap is when GitHub's webhook layer batches rapidly-filed `issues.opened` events and silently drops some — the workflow never starts, so none of the handlers fire. There's no in-workflow fix for that. Instead, a SEPARATE sweeper workflow `.github/workflows/diag-relay-sweep.yml` was shipped (PR #2144, merged 2026-05-27 ~09:50Z): daily cron at 06:00 UTC + on-demand workflow_dispatch; finds open `vm-diag-request` / `trainer-vm-diag-request` issues >30 min old with no `github-actions[bot]` reply, comments + closes them. VERIFIED 2026-05-28: the first 06:00 UTC cron ran and cleared the entire stale backlog — `list_issues(label=vm-diag-request, state=OPEN)` returned 0 (the ~38 issues going back to #1327 are all closed). The webhook-drop wedge still recurs (this review's #2173/#2174/#2175 never returned and were closed manually), but that is now an accepted condition: the sweeper cleans up any silently-dropped issue within ≤24h, so no diag-request stays OPEN indefinitely. Mitigation confirmed working end-to-end.
items.triage_note: 2026-05-28 /health-review: sweeper verified — 0 open vm-diag-request issues remain after the 06:00 cron. Re-wedge of 3 rapid-fired pulls observed but auto-cleanup confirmed. Marked resolved. | 2026-06-01 /health-review: webhook batch-drop RECURRED at high rate — opened 6 issues at 16:57:01Z (#2585-2590); only #2585 (status, first of the burst) and #2590 (trainer, separate workflow) returned + closed; #2586/2587/2588/2589 (services/audit/order_packages/trades) were silently dropped (stayed OPEN, no run). Confirms the accepted-condition framing: prevention isn't fixed, but spaced single fires work and the diag-relay-sweep cron will close the 4 stale opens within ≤24h. items.title: setup-quality-lgbm-v2 underperforms v0 baseline on n=76 closed trades — too little data for LightGBM
items.description: setup-quality-lgbm-v2 trained cleanly (PR #2053's LightGBM stack works end-to-end) but loses to setup-quality-baseline-v0 on the eval split: MAE 0.0710 vs 0.0478, MSE 0.0114 vs 0.0092 (n_eval=76). Promoting this model would mean shipping noise instead of signal. The model is auto-wired into the shadow factory by the 2026-05-19 default-flip rule, so it's currently logging shadow predictions on every live signal — that's fine and produces useful data, but the model itself shouldn't be considered for promotion past shadow until either it beats baseline at higher n, or the manifest is explicitly demoted/deprecated. items.source: Today's IB Gateway wedge — Up 21h, upstream IB session dead.
items.title: IBC nightly auto-restart doesn't reliably recover the upstream IB session
items.description: IBC's `Auto restart time` is configured to 11:59 PM on the ib-gateway container (verified in the IBC log on issue #2165 post-recovery: `Auto restart time already set to 11:59 PM`). Yet today the container was 'Up 21 hours' with its upstream IB session entirely dead (Warning 2103 usfarm / 2105 ushmds / 2157 secdefnj all 'broken'; every API call timed out at 10s; 200/200 log lines were `remove Client <id>` with no upstream activity). Either IBC's nightly restart didn't fire, or it fired and didn't successfully re-authenticate to IB's data farms. The autonomous `vm-ib-gateway-recover` workflow is the current mitigation (Claude can dispatch it whenever the symptom recurs), but the root cause needs investigating. Candidates: 2FA timing on the nightly relogin, stale Java/Gateway state on Auto-restart that needs a hard container restart, or IB-side throttling on rapid reconnects. Probable scope: inspect IBC config (jts.ini, ibc.ini) + the docker entrypoint + gateway startup logs around the 11:59 PM window over multiple days to see if the restart fires at all.
items.trigger_condition: Any /health-review run; investigate via gateway-logs + provision_ib_gateway.sh on the next 12-24h MES outage.
items.resolution_criteria: Either IBC's nightly auto-restart reliably re-establishes the upstream IB session (verifiable by 7 consecutive days with no `Up >20h with broken farm connections` state), or a sanctioned scheduled job replaces it (e.g. systemd timer triggering vm-ib-gateway-recover at 11:55 PM UTC, before IB's reset window).
items.resolution: ROOT CAUSE REFINED 2026-05-28 (corrects the original 2FA/nightly-restart hypotheses). gateway-logs (issue #2184) showed the container 'Up 13h' but logged OUT of IBKR since `2026-05-28 04:30:50 IBC: detected dialog entitled: Unrecognized Username or Password` — i.e. during IBKR's overnight server-reset window the Gateway's in-place re-login hit a TRANSIENT bad-credential dialog and IBC parked on it, never retrying. NOT 2FA (the paper account DUQ325724 logs in with no 2FA — confirmed by the #2185 recover log: 'Click button: Paper Log In' → 'Login has completed', no Mobile prompt). NOT a real bad password (a full container restart re-logins cleanly — that's why vm-ib-gateway-recover works). NOT `restart: unless-stopped` (the process hangs on the dialog, it never dies, so Docker never restarts it). The gap: nothing auto-recovers a stuck login-failure dialog (`TWOFA_TIMEOUT_ACTION=restart` only covers 2FA timeouts, which never fire for paper). FIX (operator-approved 2026-05-28, branch claude/health-check-CjAWV, draft PR #2183): a symptom-driven auto-heal watchdog — scripts/check_ib_gateway.py + deploy/ict-ib-gateway-watchdog.{service,timer}, firing every 5 min: probes ib_paper via ib_connect_check (healthy ⇔ connected AND net_liquidation populated — a logged-out gateway reports connected=true but net_liquidation=None), and after 2 consecutive wedged checks runs scripts/ops/restart_ib_gateway.sh, with max-restarts=3 + 20-min cooldown so a genuine bad-cred/lockout can never become a restart loop (then it alert-only escalates). The fixed daily scheduled-restart option was considered and DROPPED as non-structural per operator — the watchdog self-heals any wedge within ~5-10 min, fine for delayed paper data. REMAINING: operator merge + pull-and-deploy, then verify the watchdog auto-heals across a few overnight IBKR resets (target: no manual vm-ib-gateway-recover needed).
items.triage_note: 2026-05-28 working session: RECURRED + diagnosed + fix built. gateway-logs caught the 04:30:50Z 'Unrecognized Username or Password' dialog (logged-out 2h+); restored live via vm-ib-gateway-recover #2185 (clean paper login, no 2FA). Auto-heal watchdog shipped to draft PR #2183. 2026-05-28 (S-MES-AUTOHEAL): MERGED (#2183 -> main 6972a9f) + DEPLOYED (4d4d0c3 via pull-and-deploy #2196); watchdog confirmed LIVE — timer active + healthy probe (probe: healthy=True net_liquidation=1000600.6 action=none) in the #2196 post-restart systemd dump. The HEALTHY path is proven; the RESTART path on a real wedge is not yet observed in prod — tracked for next-health-review verification as BL-20260528-001.

items.source: Post-deploy journal during PR #2167 ship — first signal emitted after deploy triggered FCM push attempts that all 404'd.
items.title: FCM mobile-push notifier hits Firebase with stale / unregistered device tokens (404 NOT_FOUND)
items.description: When the trader emitted a fresh BTCUSDT VWAP signal at 2026-05-27T17:57:30Z, the M12 mobile-push notifier (src/runtime/mobile_push/notifier.py) fired FCM push attempts that came back `status=404 body={"error":{"code":404, "message":"Requested entity was not found.","status":"NOT_FOUND","details":[...FcmEr...]}}` — Google saying the device registration tokens FCM is targeting don't exist. Visible in the post-deploy journalctl on issue #2168. Means notifications aren't reaching the Android app. Either the dashboard/Android app never registered tokens after FCM init, or the tokens stored in the bot's token store are stale (device uninstall / FCM revocation / token rotation). Notifier should be marking these tokens as dead on 404 and stop retrying them; investigate whether notifier.py implements the FCM `UNREGISTERED` cleanup (remove-on-404) or silently retries. Pre-existing (the FCM key leak earlier today is unrelated — that was about the credential shape in .env, not the device tokens).
items.trigger_condition: Any /health-review run; tractable as a code-only investigation (no live-trading risk).
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) confirm + ship a token-cleanup-on-404 path in notifier.py so dead tokens are pruned automatically, or (b) confirm the cleanup already exists and the token store has been drained, and document the operator path to re-register the Android app's FCM token. The 404 cluster should stop appearing in the journal after a fresh signal emission.
items.triage_note: 2026-05-28 /health-review: CONFIRMED STILL OCCURRING. journalctl shows a flood of 'FCM publish non-2xx: status=404 ... NOT_FOUND' on every signal emission — ~12+ per emit at 04:55:36-38 (post-boot fade signal) and again at 06:00:35-36 (vwap signal_emitted). Dead/unregistered device tokens are not being pruned on 404; the notifier keeps targeting them each emit. No token-cleanup-on-404 path is taking effect. Tier-1 code investigation in src/runtime/mobile_push/notifier.py — not editable from /health-review.

check_log.note: 2026-05-30 (/health-review, operator-confirmed): push DELIVERY IS WORKING - operator confirms notifications are landing on the phone. So the FCM 404 NOT_FOUND lines (still seen in ict-trader-live journalctl, e.g. ~23:50Z 2026-05-30) are LOG-NOISE from a stale/secondary unregistered token, NOT a delivery outage. Severity downgraded: remaining work is just pruning 404'd tokens from the registry so the notifier stops logging WARN+error bodies on every cycle. Not a user-facing problem.

items.source: Today's FCM-credential bleed incident (issue #2157).
items.title: Operator-only follow-ups from the FCM private-key bleed
items.description:
The 2026-05-27 systemd-EnvironmentFile bleed dumped the FCM service-account PEM private key into the journalctl tail on TWO pull-and-deploy issue comments. PR #2158 shipped the scrub-env-noncompliant system-action and it ran successfully (12 lines stripped, journal warning is now gone — verified on issue #2161). What's left is operator-only because the MCP tools I have can neither delete issue comments (no delete_issue_comment) nor vacuum the journal (no journalctl vacuum system-action) nor rotate the FCM key (that's Google Cloud Console). Three steps:
  1. Delete the comments containing the leaked key (one-click `...` → Delete on each):
     - https://github.com/benbaichmankass/ict-trading-bot/issues/2157#issuecomment-4555473441
     - https://github.com/benbaichmankass/ict-trading-bot/issues/2159#issuecomment-4555811974
  2. Rotate the FCM service-account key at Google Cloud Console (only step that actually neutralizes the exposure — the journal copies on the VM, webhook archives, and any third-party GitHub mirror still hold the old key). After rotation, re-dispatch `set-mobile-push-secrets` with the new JSON in the FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON secret to update the on-disk file at ${DATA_DIR}/fcm_service_account.json.
  3. Optional: `sudo journalctl --rotate && sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=1s` on the live VM to wipe historical journal copies containing the key. Reduces forensic surface; the scrub already stops future bleeds at source.
items.trigger_condition: Operator-only — no autonomous action possible. Surface every /health-review run until resolved.
items.resolution_criteria: Both leaked issue comments deleted (404 on the comment URLs); FCM service-account key rotated at Google Cloud Console; ${DATA_DIR}/fcm_service_account.json updated to the new credential and a fresh push test succeeds (kicks the notifier and confirms no 404 NOT_FOUND).

items.title: vm-diag-snapshot relay rejects multi-param diag paths (the & query separator)
items.description: Issue-driven diag requests whose title carries a & failed this session (#2251 `journal?table=order_packages&limit=40`, #2252 `journal?table=trades&limit=40`) while single-param paths (`journal?table=order_packages`, `db_info`) and the broad `snapshot?limit=200` succeeded. Suspected cause: GitHub stores the title's & as the HTML entity &; the workflow decodes it (${raw//&/&}) but the path-validation regex ^[A-Za-z0-9/?&=_.:%-]+$ in .github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml rejects the ; if any entity slips through un-decoded, so the run exits 1 with 'Rejected diag_path'. Workaround in use: single-param paths or the broad snapshot. Low priority — the relay works for the common cases.

items.title: git-sync deploy restarts the LIVE TRADER for docs-only commits (brief trading + read-surface interruption); web-api has no VM-side self-heal and the GitHub recover dispatch is webhook-flaky
items.description: OBSERVED this review: between status #2286 (09:44:05Z, uptime 36577s, git_sha b149b15) and status #2302 (09:52:15Z, uptime 405s, git_sha 22e2cf0) the live trader RESTARTED and HEAD advanced b149b15 -> 22e2cf0. The only commit in that range is 22e2cf0 (#2284, a DOCS-ONLY 'docs(health-review): recurring carry-forward item' change). So the ict-git-sync timer pulled the new commit and ran the full deploy_pull_restart path, which restarts ALL ict-* units (trader + web-api) regardless of whether the diff touches any runtime code. Two consequences: (1) the live money-path trader was bounced (~7 min, 09:45-09:52Z) for a pure documentation change — an unnecessary trading interruption; (2) during that window ict-web-api was down so the diag/dashboard READ surface was blinded (diag pulls #2293-#2296,#2298 failed 09:45:44-09:48:03Z). I misread (2) as a crash and fired three vm-web-api-recover dispatches (#2297/#2299/#2300) — ALL webhook-dropped (issue OPEN, updated_at==created_at, no run), same GitHub issues.opened batching as the resolved BL-20260527-001. They turned out UNNECESSARY (the deploy completed and both services self-recovered by 09:52Z). Net: no real outage, but two genuine gaps surfaced. PRIMARY GAP: deploy_pull_restart restarts the live trader for non-runtime (docs/comms) commits — consider gating the trader restart on whether the diff touches runtime paths (src/, config/, deploy/, requirements). SECONDARY GAP: ict-web-api has no VM-side self-heal and the only autonomous recover lever (GitHub-dispatched vm-web-api-recover) is webhook-flaky exactly when needed.
items.trigger_condition: Any /health-review run; or whenever a deploy of a docs/comms-only commit is observed to bounce the live trader, or a vm-web-api-recover dispatch is webhook-dropped.
items.resolution_criteria: PRIMARY: deploy_pull_restart.sh (or the git-sync path) skips the ict-trader-live restart when the pulled diff touches no runtime path (docs/comms-only) — verify a docs-only commit deploys without a trader uptime reset. SECONDARY: ict-web-api gets a VM-side auto-restart-on-unhealthy guard (systemd watchdog/timer probing local :8001 /api/health) so the read surface self-heals without a webhook-dependent dispatch. Both are Tier-2 deploy/runtime changes; not editable from /health-review — surface to the operator.
items.triage_note: 2026-05-29T19:40Z /health-review: RECURRED AGAIN this review, both gaps. (1) A docs/comms-only commit (d4e4a0c, HEAD at 19:28:42Z) was pulled by ict-git-sync and ran the full deploy_pull_restart — status #2375 shows the live trader bounced to bot_uptime_s=31 at 19:35:46Z (git_sha d4e4a0c) and web-api was down 19:29-19:35Z. The first 7 diag pulls of this review (#2367-2371) failed during that window and 4 rapid re-fires (#2378-2381) webhook-dropped (BL-20260527-001 batching). (2) vm-web-api-recover #2373 FAILED (wrapper exit 1) — it ran mid-bounce: restart_web_api.sh saw ict-web-api stop-sigterm time out (SIGKILL at 19:32:57) then a slow uvicorn boot, so its /api/health probe got curl-7 connection-refused for ~60s and gave up; the service self-recovered by 19:35. Net: ~6 min read-surface blind + 1 unnecessary failed recover, no real trading outage, all self-healed. This is now the 2nd consecutive review (cf. the in-description 09:45Z event) where a non-runtime commit bounced the money-path trader — the PRIMARY gap (gate trader restart on whether the diff touches runtime paths) is worth prioritising with the operator. | 2026-06-01 /health-review: REPRODUCED A 3RD TIME. status pull (issue #2585, captured 16:57:17Z) shows bot_uptime_s=341 (~5.7 min → restart ~16:51:36Z) on git_sha=f91aa32, which is the 2026-06-01 'night session-end' DOCS-ONLY commit (#2584). So a documentation-only commit again ran the full deploy_pull_restart and bounced the live trader. The trader recovered healthy (heartbeat 'running' age 107s, last_tick 16:56:58Z, all 9 strategies loaded, no crashloop). Persistent low-grade trading/read-surface interruption on every docs commit; PRIMARY gap (gate the restart on runtime-path diffs) still the priority Tier-2 fix for the operator.
items.resolution_note: FIXED + DEPLOYED — the item was stale-open. PR #2595 (commit 4a8594d, 2026-06-01 21:21Z, a later same-day /health-review session) added the runtime-path gate to scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh (lines ~142-181): it diffs PRE_SYNC_HEAD..POST_SYNC_HEAD and, when every changed path matches the safe set ^(docs/|tests/|\.claude/|[^/]+\.md$), SKIPS dependency-install + unit-refresh + service restart (exit 0) — so a docs/backlog/sprint-log commit no longer bounces the live trader. Fail-safe: empty/uncomputable diff OR any other path (src/ ml/ config/ deploy/ scripts/ comms/ requirements*/pyproject) falls through to the normal restart; DEPLOY_FORCE_RESTART=1 overrides. Confirmed in deployed HEAD e97991f (git merge-base --is-ancestor 4a8594d e97991f = true). The 2026-06-01 'reproduced 3rd time' triage note (16:57Z) predates the 21:21Z fix. This review's 04:39Z trader restart had git_sha UNCHANGED (not a deploy) — consistent with the gate. The PRIMARY gap is closed. SECONDARY gap (web-api has no VM-side self-heal; the GitHub vm-web-api-recover dispatch is webhook-flaky) is NOT addressed by #2595 — re-logging it as BL-20260604-003 so it isn't lost.

The goal is NOT just to confirm the discrepancy but to ROOT-CAUSE it in the template analyst (src/runtime/insights/template_analyst.py + generator.py): likely two different closed-trade definitions feeding the same card — e.g. the prose 'closed' counts rows with a terminal close timestamp while row_counts 'trades_closed' counts a different status, OR a shadow-vs-live filter applied to one path but not the other (vwap is execution:shadow, 89 trades / mostly unfilled), OR a window/symbol-join mismatch. items.title: High order_package ORPHAN rates across strategies — positions go DB-open / exchange-flat without a clean fill record
items.description: While auditing whether strategies exit properly, found high orphan rates in order_packages: trend_donchian 22/38 (58%), vwap 917/1460 (63%), squeeze 24/83 (29%), ict_scalp 4/13 (31%). 'Orphaned' = the reconciler found the DB-open package flat on the exchange but could not record a clean fill/PnL (vs reconciler_filled where it could). This loses PnL attribution and inflates the 'rejected'/'orphaned' noise in the journal, which can skew per-strategy performance stats and therefore the research/demotion evidence. Likely contributors: (a) the re-entry storm (fixed separately by the bar-close debounce) creating packages that never stabilise into real positions; (b) entry orders that fill-then-immediately-exchange-SL vs orders that never fill (the 341 exchange_rejected + intent_noop rejections suggest a mix); (c) the reconciler/orphan-handler not querying Bybit get_closed_pnl to attribute the realised PnL on a derivatives SL/TP fire (see order_monitor._classify_orphan_close — derivatives orphans are left 'unknown'). NOTE the exit machinery itself works (fade + ict_scalp win normally through reconciler_filled; the Chandelier trail ratchets) — this is a reconciliation/attribution + order-stabilisation issue, not a broken-exit issue.

NEW ROOT CAUSE FOUND + FIX PREPARED (draft PR, Tier-2, operator-gated) for a DISTINCT, currently-ACTIVE orphan-rate driver — the FALSE-ORPHAN / split-attribution class, separate from the closed-pnl-attribution class. Live re-measure via /api/diag/journal (issue #7657, git_sha 08154e3a): the two most-recent orphaned order_packages — pkg-07d51e1d986447b3 + pkg-da56584ddd114439 (both ict_scalp_avax_5m, bybit_1 demo) — carry status='orphaned' + meta.orphaned_reason='BUG-049 — no linked_trade_id after 5 min; package was never executed', YET each HAS a real trade back-referencing it via trades.order_package_id: pkg-07d51e1d986447b3 ← trade #4022 (setup_type=intent_reduce, status=closed), pkg-da56584ddd114439 ← trade #4021 (status=OPEN, a live position). So these packages DID execute; they were falsely stamped 'orphaned — never executed'. ROOT CAUSE: order_packages.linked_trade_id is a ONE-SLOT 'primary entry trade' pointer (database._migrate_add_order_package_id docstring) — when a decision fans out into several trade rows (real entry + demo mirror + intent_reduce leg + multi-account), only the LAST update_order_package(linked_trade_id=...) survives, so the slot is often left NULL even though the package filled. order_monitor._sweep_unlinked_packages keys the BUG-049 orphan stamp SOLELY on linked_trade_id IS NULL and only consults the newer trades.order_package_id back-reference for REJECTION rows (stage 1) and shadow strategies (stage 1.5) — there was NO stage recognizing a package whose linked trade actually EXECUTED (open/closed). This both (a) pollutes per-strategy orphan-rate stats with executed packages (the resolution_criteria) and (b) when the linked trade is still OPEN, wrongly terminalises a package whose position is LIVE, clearing the strategy-monocle open gate on a live position. items.title: vm-diag-snapshot relay returns fetch_failed for ALL /api/bot/* + db/table/* paths while /api/diag/* works (blocks review pulls of decision-level + filtered-count endpoints)
items.description: Isolated across 3 relay runs: issue #7654 (batch of /api/bot + db/table, all fetch_failed), issue #7656 (version → OK with git_sha 08154e3a; stats + all /api/bot/db/table → fetch_failed in the same run), issue #7657 (/api/diag db_info + status + services + journal all OK). The web-api is UP and serving (db_info: error_per_table {}, order_packages=3290, trades=4022 rows; recovery-log journal shows the dashboard getting /api/bot/stats 200s), and the DB is healthy — so this is NOT a web-api/DB outage. It is a relay-side handling issue specific to the /api/bot/ upstream_prefix in the batched issues path (.github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml resolve_one/curl loop), OR the /api/bot GETs 5xx specifically to the localhost curl (note the relay sends 'Authorization: Bearer DIAG_READ_TOKEN' to /api/bot Tier-1 GETs, which are unauthenticated — a stray bearer + curl --fail could interact; and /api/bot/stats returns HTTP 503 on structural DB failure per S-067, but db_info shows the DB is fine, so that path is not it). Impact: future health/system reviews cannot pull the /api/bot decision-level view (/order-packages) OR the filtered-count endpoints (/db/table/<t>?filter_col=status&...&limit=1 → total) through the relay — the cleanest way to MEASURE the orphan rate (per resolution_criteria of BL-20260601-001). This session worked around it with /api/diag/journal + db_info. NOTE (honesty): on the first all-fetch_failed batch (#7654, before /api/diag/version was tested) this session fired a vm-web-api-recover (#7655) diagnosing a web-api outage; the recovery log showed the service was already active and serving — the restart was a harmless ~2s no-op (health 200 after), and the true cause is this relay/endpoint /api/bot handling, not a down service.

Repro: open a vm-diag-request issue with any /api/bot path (e.g. 'stats' or 'db/table/order_packages?limit=1') and observe fetch_failed while a sibling /api/diag path (e.g. 'version') returns 200.
items.resolution_criteria: The relay returns real JSON for allowlisted /api/bot/* + db/table/* GETs (verify 'stats' and 'db/table/order_packages?filter_col=status&filter_op=eq&filter_val=orphaned&limit=1' both return a body, not fetch_failed). Root-cause whether it is the curl --fail/Bearer handling for the /api/bot prefix in the batched loop, or a genuine localhost 5xx on those endpoints.
items.resolution_note: NOT A BUG — misdiagnosis, corrected honestly. The relay's default upstream_prefix is /api/diag/ and a /api/bot route MUST be namespaced as 'api/bot/<path>' by the caller (resolve_one in vm-diag-snapshot.yml only rewrites the prefix to /api/bot/ when the path starts with 'api/bot/'). I passed the bare basenames ('stats', 'db/table/...', 'order-packages', 'notifications') without the 'api/bot/' prefix, so the relay resolved them under /api/diag/ → 404 → the curl --fail fallback wrote {"error":"fetch_failed"}. Proven via issue #7659: the ict-web-api journal shows 'GET /api/diag/stats 404', 'GET /api/diag/notifications 404', 'GET /api/diag/db/table/... 404' at 12:03:55Z — the relay had prefixed them /api/diag/. Re-fired with the correct 'api/bot/' prefix (issue #7660) and the same endpoints return real JSON. The /api/diag/* paths I passed bare (version/db_info/status/journal) worked because they ARE diag paths. Lesson for future sessions: diag paths are bare (e.g. 'snapshot?limit=200'); /api/bot paths MUST be prefixed 'api/bot/' (e.g. 'api/bot/db/table/order_packages?filter_col=status&filter_op=eq&filter_val=orphaned&limit=1'). No workflow change needed; the calling convention is by design (diag is the default surface, /api/bot is explicitly namespaced). Also for the record: the vm-web-api-recover (#7655) fired on the first all-fetch_failed batch was an unnecessary (harmless) no-op driven by the same misread — the service was up the whole time.
items.notes: Optional low-value follow-up for a future session: add a one-line 'api/bot/ paths must be prefixed; diag paths are bare' reminder to docs/claude/diag-relay.md so the next PM-side session doesn't repeat this. Not blocking.

items.source: Noticed while investigating the MES (mes_trend_long_1d) IBKR-paper pipeline (PR #2626): order_packages + signal-audit pulls show htf_pullback_trend_2h producing MES order packages even though its config declares symbols:[BTCUSDT] and it routes only to bybit_1.
items.title: Per-strategy `symbols:` does not gate EVALUATION — the multi-symbol tick loop runs every enabled builder on the union of all account symbols, producing cross-product packages no account routes (ORPHANED)
items.description: The tick loop (src/main.py::_resolve_tick_symbols) unions every configured account's symbols ({BTCUSDT, MES}) and evaluates each enabled strategy's signal builder on every symbol in the union, regardless of the strategy's own `symbols:` field in config/strategies.yaml. Observed 2026-06-02: htf_pullback_trend_2h (symbols:[BTCUSDT], routed to bybit_1 only) emitted MES order packages (status 'orphaned'); conversely mes_trend_long_1d (symbols:[MES]) is evaluated on BTCUSDT (the signal audit shows symbol=BTCUSDT eval rows for it, reason 'short_suppressed_long_only'). These cross-product packages are dropped/orphaned because no account routes that (strategy x symbol) combo — the symbol->exchange dispatch gate (coordinator._eligible_for_dispatch) + the account.strategies filter correctly prevent execution, so this is HARMLESS to trading (no wrong-symbol order can fire). But it is wasted per-tick evaluation + journal noise: the orphaned cross-product rows pollute per-strategy orphan-rate stats (cf. BL-20260601-001, whose triage_note already saw these htf_pullback_trend_2h-on-MES orphans). Fix: gate EVALUATION by the strategy's own declared `symbols:` (intersected with its routed accounts' symbols) so a BTCUSDT-only strategy is never run on MES and vice-versa.
items.trigger_condition: Next /health-review or any session touching src/main.py::_resolve_tick_symbols or the per-tick strategy-evaluation loop. Re-pull order_packages and confirm orphaned cross-product packages (htf_pullback_trend_2h on MES, mes_trend_long_1d on BTCUSDT) still appear.
items.resolution_criteria: Strategy signal builders are evaluated only on the symbols the strategy declares in config/strategies.yaml (intersected with account routing), so no cross-product (strategy x non-declared-symbol) order packages are produced. Verify htf_pullback_trend_2h no longer emits MES packages and mes_trend_long_1d no longer emits BTCUSDT packages, with no loss of legitimate signals.
items.resolution_note: Fixed by the per-strategy symbol-scope gate (PR #2643, merged + deployed 2026-06-02, HEAD 3d35e24). intent_multiplexer._collect_intents now skips a strategy whose declared config/strategies.yaml symbols: do not include the current tick symbol (permissive on no-symbols/unknown/config-error), so a strategy is evaluated/emits ONLY on its declared instrument(s) — no cross-product (strategy x non-declared-symbol) packages are produced. Gated at intent EMISSION (not dispatch) so a higher-priority off-symbol strategy can't win a symbol's per-symbol aggregation and starve the legitimate owner. Verified live post-deploy via audit_query: mgc_pullback_1d evaluates MGC-only (zero MES/MHG/BTCUSDT rows) where pre-deploy it ran on all four. Crypto strategies (symbols:[BTCUSDT]) no longer evaluate on MES. Tests: tests/test_intent_symbol_scope.py (4) + 324 intent/coordinator/pipeline regression green. NOTE: the gate lives in the production intent-multiplexer path (STRATEGY=multiplexed_intents); the legacy first-wins pipeline path is not gated but is not the production path.

items.title: ict-web-api has no VM-side self-heal; the only autonomous recover lever (GitHub vm-web-api-recover) is webhook-flaky exactly when needed
items.description: BL-20260529-002's PRIMARY gap (docs-commit trader bounce) was fixed by PR #2595. Its SECONDARY gap remains: ict-web-api.service has no on-VM auto-restart-on-unhealthy guard, and the only autonomous recovery path (the GitHub-dispatched vm-web-api-recover workflow) is subject to the issues.opened webhook batch-drop (BL-20260527-001) precisely during a deploy bounce when the read surface is down — observed 2026-05-29 (#2297/#2299/#2300 all dropped) and the #2373 recover that ran mid-bounce failed. With the PRIMARY gap closed the read-surface blind windows are now rarer (docs commits no longer bounce anything), but a genuine web-api crash still has no VM-side self-heal. Fix: add a systemd watchdog/timer (mirror ict-liveness-watchdog / ict-ib-gateway-watchdog) that probes local 127.0.0.1:8001/api/health every ~2 min and restarts ict-web-api.service on N consecutive failures, with restart-cap + cooldown so a genuine crashloop alert-escalates rather than loops. Removes the webhook dependency for read-surface recovery.

items.title: check_accounts_api fails in the standalone health-snapshot writer context (account_balance() returns None without the trader's live exchange clients) — card shows a perpetual accounts_api 'watch'
items.description: src/runtime/health.py::check_accounts_api reuses src.bot.data_loaders.account_balance() per account and WARNs on any None. In the trader PROCESS this works (it holds the live exchange/IB clients). But ict-health-snapshot.service runs write_health_snapshot.py as a SEPARATE oneshot that has no such clients (e.g. the local smoke logged 'account_balance(ib_paper): ib_insync is not installed' and Bybit balance needs a live socket), so account_balance() returns None -> accounts_api WARN -> the M13 health card sits at 6/7 'watch' with accounts_api failing even though the live trader's accounts are fine. This is a CONTEXT artifact of running the check outside the trader, not a real outage (verified: the trader dispatched real trade 2428 + is healthy). Net effect: the card never shows fully-green when it should. Fix options: (a) point check_accounts_api at the CONNECTION-FREE balance snapshot (runtime_logs/balance_snapshots.json — the same source /api/bot/accounts/balances uses, 'never opens an exchange socket'), so it reflects the last recorded balance instead of trying to connect; or (b) have the standalone writer skip/soften the accounts_api check (env flag) when not in-process; or (c) accept the warn as a known standalone limitation and document it. (a) is the cleanest — it makes the check connection-free + context-independent. Tier-1 code (observability); not a money-path change.

items.source: /health-review 2026-06-06: /api/diag/journalctl relay calls for ict-trader-live.service (lines=90) AND ict-liveness-watchdog.service (lines=70) both failed (run failed / curl --fail/--max-time), while journalctl?unit=ict-web-api.service (lines=120), status, config, journal, and log_file all succeeded.
items.title: Observability gap: /api/diag/journalctl fails for high-volume units (ict-trader-live) under the relay's curl --max-time, blocking restart-cause root-cause exactly when needed
items.description: When investigating the 2026-06-06 trader restart churn (BL-20260605-001), the diag journalctl pulls for ict-trader-live.service and ict-liveness-watchdog.service both returned 'run failed' via the vm-diag relay, while the lighter ict-web-api.service journalctl (and status/config/journal/log_file) succeeded. The trader logs a large volume per tick, so a journalctl tail of 70-120 lines likely exceeds the relay's `curl -sS --fail --max-time 40` budget (slow/large response -> curl exit 28/timeout -> workflow reports failure), OR the response byte size trips the same ~414KB cap noted elsewhere. Net effect: the single most useful pull for diagnosing a restart loop (the trader + watchdog journals) is the one that fails, so the autoheal-vs-crash-vs-IB-wedge trigger could not be captured this session. Candidate fixes (Tier-1/2): (a) raise the journalctl curl --max-time in vm-diag-snapshot.yml for journalctl paths; (b) add `since=`/`until=` narrowing support guidance so callers pull a small time-window instead of N lines; (c) add a dedicated lightweight 'restart-cause' diag (e.g. systemctl show --property=NRestarts,ActiveEnterTimestamp + the last N ExecStart lines) that returns small output; (d) gzip/cap journalctl output server-side. Until fixed, restart-cause investigation must use systemctl show timestamps + smaller line counts.

items.source: Session 2026-06-07: built the cancel-queued-runs workflow (#2935/#2938) to clear 23 stale 'queued' Actions runs dated 2026-05-15. The runner (with actions:write) found all 23 but cancelled 0 — both `gh run cancel` and the force-cancel endpoint return HTTP 500 for every one.
items.title: 23 zombie 'queued' Actions runs (2026-05-15) are un-cancellable — GitHub returns HTTP 500 on both cancel and force-cancel
items.description: 23 workflow runs have been stuck in 'queued' since 2026-05-15 (ids 25906694928..25907269254). They never got a runner and consume no compute, but clutter the Actions list. The cancel-queued-runs workflow added this session (runner-path, since the PM-side MCP token lacks actions:write) lists them correctly and attempts normal cancel then force-cancel (POST repos/.../actions/runs/{id}/force-cancel) — both return `HTTP 500` for all 23, so the workflow cancels 0. A 500 (not 403/422) means it is a GitHub server-side failure on these specific orphaned runs; nothing a runner or the Actions UI (same endpoints) can do. The cancel-queued-runs workflow itself is sound and reusable for any FUTURE cancellable queued backlog — these particular runs are the exception. Resolution is GitHub-side: GitHub may garbage-collect them eventually, or GitHub Support can purge zombie runs. No code change in this repo will clear them. Note runs can't be DELETED either (the delete-run endpoint only accepts completed runs, not queued). Tracked here only so a future health-review doesn't re-investigate the same inert clutter.
items.trigger_condition: A future health-review or session notices the 23 stale queued runs and considers re-attempting cancellation, or wonders whether cancel-queued-runs is broken.
items.resolution_criteria: The 23 stale 2026-05-15 queued runs no longer appear in the Actions list (GitHub-side GC or Support purge). No repo change is expected to satisfy this; close when the runs are gone or the operator decides to leave them.

updates.note: Confirmed STILL PRESENT 2026-07-11 via actions_list(status=queued): exactly 23 runs, ALL dated 2026-05-15 (Health Snapshot / vm-web-api-recover / vwap-backtest / vm-cloud-fix etc.), stuck ~2 months. Not autonomously closable: the available GitHub MCP toolset exposes no workflow-run cancel/delete method, and GitHub historically 500s on cancelling these. BENIGN — they are queued (never scheduled), so they consume ZERO Actions minutes and don't block the runner. Downgrading urgency: leave open as a known cosmetic nuisance; a real fix needs `gh run delete`/API DELETE from a non-MCP context (desktop CLI or a one-shot workflow), not worth prioritising.

Attempted a real clear via the runner-path cancel-queued-runs workflow (#6131) — which has actions:write AND a force-cancel fallback (repos/.../actions/runs/<id>/force-cancel), i.e. more power than the MCP token. Result: cancelled 0 of 23 — BOTH `gh run cancel` and the force-cancel endpoint failed on every one of the 23 stuck 2026-05-15 runs. So these are genuinely un-cancellable at GitHub's side (a terminal stuck-queued state GitHub's own API refuses to clear), not just an MCP-permission limitation. Confirmed benign (queued → 0 minutes) and NOT fixable from here — stop retrying the canceller. Only a GitHub-support action or natural GC would clear them; not worth pursuing. Downgraded/parked.

items.title: backfill-monitor-closed-pnl (and likely sibling backfill/inspect closed-pnl actions) can't reach Bybit creds in the system-action subprocess
items.description: The backfill-monitor-closed-pnl system-action skipped 100% of candidates (16/16, incl. demo bybit_1 rows #2482/#2484/#2490/#2492/#2494 and live rows) with 'account_closed_pnl_for_trade returned None'. The script's own heuristic warns the cause is 'exchange CREDENTIALS NOT REACHABLE from this process's env — silent auth failure'. _lib.sh::load_runtime_secrets sources REPO_DIR/.env; the live ict-trader-live.service reaches Bybit fine (actively trading), so the gap is specific to the system-action subprocess env (likely .env at REPO_DIR missing/incomplete vs the trader's systemd EnvironmentFile, and/or bybit_1 demo creds not present). This blocks any closed-pnl backfill/inspect action regardless of the BL-20260601-001 fix. Pre-existing; surfaced while remediating BL-20260601-001.
items.trigger_condition: Next time a closed-pnl backfill/inspect action is needed, or proactively to unblock BL-20260601-001 demo-row remediation.
items.resolution_criteria: backfill-monitor-closed-pnl (and inspect-closed-pnl) reach Bybit with valid creds from the system-action subprocess and recover/inspect at least the demo rows; root-cause the env mismatch between the wrapper's load_runtime_secrets and the trader's systemd env.
items.triage_note: 2026-06-08: opened from BL-20260601-001 deploy session. Needs VM diagnosis of REPO_DIR/.env contents + how ict-trader-live/ict-web-api load creds (systemd EnvironmentFile vs .env) + whether bybit_1 demo keys are configured.
items.resolution_note: MISDIAGNOSIS — NOT a credential gap. inspect-closed-pnl (Tier-1, read-only) on demo rows #2482 and #2490 (issues #2992, #2994) proved: bybit_client_for(cfg) built the demo client (demo=True → api-demo.bybit.com), get_closed_pnl executed WITHOUT error, and Bybit returned 0 records for each (within the 7-day window). So bybit_1 demo keys ARE configured and reachable from the system-action subprocess (load_runtime_secrets sources the same /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/.env that ict-trader-live uses). True cause of the backfill 0/16: Bybit DEMO doesn't populate /v5/position/closed-pnl. The 'credentials not reachable' WARNING is a misleading 100%-skip heuristic. Follow-up tracked in BL-20260608-DEMOPNL.

items.source: BL-20260608-CRED diagnosis: Bybit demo /v5/position/closed-pnl returns 0 records (verified #2482/#2490).
items.title: Bybit DEMO realised PnL is unrecoverable from closed-pnl; build a demo-PnL source + fix the misleading backfill warning
items.description: bybit_1 (demo) closed trades carry pnl=NULL because Bybit demo trading does not populate /v5/position/closed-pnl — verified via inspect-closed-pnl on #2482 and #2490 (0 records, creds OK). (1) backfill_monitor_closed_pnl.py prints 'credentials not reachable' on any 100%-skip — soften to distinguish client-None/auth-exception from a successful empty response. (2) OPERATOR REQUESTED building a real demo-PnL source: recon shipped (inspect-closed-pnl now also dumps /v5/execution/list + /v5/order/history) to determine which endpoint the demo venue populates; then implement a demo fallback in account_closed_pnl_for_trade (reconstruct exit avg-price + realised PnL from closing executions) + backfill. If demo populates NEITHER endpoint, fall back to computing PnL from entry/exit fills captured at close time.
items.trigger_condition: In progress (operator-requested 2026-06-08). Next: run the enhanced inspect-closed-pnl on a demo trade post-deploy to see execution-list/order-history output.
items.resolution_criteria: Demo closed trades carry non-NULL realised pnl from a working source; AND the backfill warning distinguishes empty-result from auth-failure.
items.triage_note: 2026-06-08: opened from BL-20260608-CRED diagnosis; recon tooling shipped same session. | 2026-06-08 RECON + DEFERRED: enhanced inspect-closed-pnl run on demo #2490 (issue #2997) — /v5/position/closed-pnl=0 rows, BUT /v5/execution/list=6 rows and /v5/order/history=3 rows ARE populated on demo. Key finding: the demo account NETS every strategy fill into a single position (each htf 'trade' is an incremental Sell with closedSize=0; the whole ~0.505 short was flattened by ONE Buy @63483.4), so there is NO per-trade close to attribute — a real demo-PnL source needs a position-accounting/allocation layer (FIFO/avg across constituent opens), not just a different endpoint. Sub-findings: demo opens carry no SL/TP (reduceOnly=False, empty stopOrderType) so positions accumulate vs live bybit_2 which closes per-trade; and the reconciler marked these closed while the net position was still open. OPERATOR DECISION 2026-06-08: DEFER — added to ROADMAP.md 'Items Under Consideration'. Recon tooling (inspect-closed-pnl execution/order dump) is shipped (PR #2996). The backfill false-'creds' warning softening (sub-item 1) also remains open. | 2026-06-08 SL/TP ROOT-CAUSE INVESTIGATED (operator-requested): root cause confirmed = one-way-mode position-level SL/TP OVERWRITE on same-direction re-entry + reconciler closing on NET-flat (not per-trade) + monocle release → accumulation cycle. SL/TP ARE attached on demo entries (execute.py:659-660) — CORRECTION to the earlier 'demo opens carry no SL/TP' note, which was an over-read (attached position-level SL/TP don't show as separate stop ORDERS in order/history). Evidence: audit_query #3002 (33 sell+28 short htf signals in 9h, only 3 bar_debounce_blocked), inspect #2997 (incremental Sell opens → one Buy 0.505 close), code (no positionIdx/hedge anywhere = one-way; order_monitor.py:2017-2029 net-flat close). Money-relevant on live bybit_2 too (currently masked). Full analysis + Tier-3 remediation proposal (recommend Option A: suppress same-dir re-entry while position open + harden reconciler against transient net-flat; behind a kill-switch + walk-forward) in docs/audits/position-netting-sltp-2026-06-08.md. Awaiting operator decision on the proposal before any Tier-3 code. | 2026-06-08 Option A SHIPPED + LIVE (PRs #3023 guard + #3031 account-scope, deployed f81cf9b): the position-netting / per-trade SL/TP guard is now active on both Bybit accounts (POSITION_NETTING_GUARD_ENABLED=true, POSITION_NETTING_GUARD_ACCOUNTS=bybit_1,bybit_2) after a demo-only soak on bybit_1. Monocle suppresses same-direction netted adds; reconciler requires an extra grace tick before closing on a net-flat snapshot. This restores per-trade=per-position, the prerequisite for closed-pnl to repopulate as positions close discretely. Validated: 36 unit tests + net-vs-suppress walk-forward (real BTCUSDT 5m, 4 windows, no trade-count/win-rate regression + lower max-DD). Kept OPEN because the bybit_1 DEMO venue still does not populate /v5/position/closed-pnl, so demo realised-PnL recovery for already-netted historical rows remains limited — forward demo trades should now close per-trade and attribute. Rollback = unset POSITION_NETTING_GUARD_ENABLED (or narrow POSITION_NETTING_GUARD_ACCOUNTS) + restart, no redeploy.

updates.note: TIER-2 PREP → PROPOSED (awaiting operator OK before ship). Root cause: Bybit's closed-pnl endpoint doesn't return reliable per-trade records for the DEMO account (bybit_1 testnet); _bybit_closed_pnl_lookup returns shared/mismatched records (the sibling BL-20260620-CLOSEDPNL-LOOKUP-MISMATCH-DEMO: two SOL paper trades booked an identical -864.45). PROPOSED FIX (Tier-2, paper-only, real-money untouched): for is_demo Bybit trades, route realised-PnL resolution through the LOCAL compute path (src/runtime/local_pnl.py, multiplier-aware via config/instruments.yaml contract_value_usd) instead of the Bybit closed-pnl lookup — mirroring the local_compute path already used for IBKR/Alpaca/OANDA realised PnL (order_monitor._sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced). Net: demo realised PnL becomes entry/exit/qty-derived (deterministic, no shared-record bleed); the misleading backfill that pulls a wrong Bybit record for demo is bypassed. Scope: the demo branch of _bybit_closed_pnl_lookup + the backfill. Needs operator OK (touches the close/PnL resolution path, paper accounts).

RESOLVED (operator-approved build) — account_closed_pnl_for_trade now returns None EARLY for demo accounts, the single chokepoint both demo-PnL writers funnel through (the monitor close path + _sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit). Demo's unreliable Bybit closed-pnl lookup (shared/mismatched testnet records — the BL-20260620 -864.45 double-book) is skipped; realised PnL now resolves via the universal local-compute sweep (_sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced: entry×exit×qty×contract_value_usd, multiplier-aware, or mark-to-market exit) — the same path IBKR/Alpaca/OANDA use. Removed the now-dead demo wide-fallback wiring at the call site. Real-money Bybit untouched (strict broker-truth contract). 3 new tests (demo→None + client-not-called; truthy variants; live→reaches client) pass; py_compile clean. On bot PR #4503; ships on merge+deploy. Sibling BL-20260620-CLOSEDPNL-LOOKUP-MISMATCH-DEMO is subsumed by this (demo no longer queries the lookup at all).

items.source: Session-end observation: PR #3007 (branch claude/vibrant-babbage-9Wbls, head SHA e286c4ea) shows total_count=0 on get_status for 7+ hours after push. No check runs fired at all.
items.title: PR #3007 CI never triggered after push (0 check runs in 7+ h on SHA e286c4ea)
items.description: After opening PR #3007 against main from claude/vibrant-babbage-9Wbls, mcp__github__pull_request_read method=get_status returned state='pending', total_count=0 across 4+ polls over a 7-hour window. No workflow runs reference the head SHA in the Actions list for the period. Either (a) a path/branch filter excluded this PR's changes, (b) the push event was accepted but didn't fan out to workflow triggers, or (c) the runners were idle/wedged. Worth investigating because the same trigger anomaly would silently let other PRs from claude/* branches merge without CI. First step next session: check Actions for any run referencing e286c4ea; if absent, inspect the workflow trigger filters in .github/workflows/*.yml against the changed paths in #3007. An empty commit on the branch would kick the trigger as a workaround if the configs are correct but state is stale.
items.resolution_note: Not a CI bug. All 11 checks ran green on commit 1 (e286c4ea); commit 2 (61c64816) had 0 runs because the PR was dirty — the backlog-JSON appends conflicted with main, which blocks GitHub from building the merge ref, so the synchronize push triggered nothing. get_status/get_check_runs report only the head SHA, hence total_count=0. The path/branch-filter hypothesis is ruled out (no CI workflow has a path filter). Fixed by resolving the conflict and pushing 61c6481..2be6549; 11 checks re-fired green; #3007 merged. See docs/audits/s9-yz-shadow-promotion-2026-06-09.md §1.

2026-06-10 07:07Z LIVE INCIDENT (recurrence, COLD-START variant): a trader restart (07:02:50, enabling the netting guard) re-wedged the VM — cpu 72%->100%, heartbeat froze at 07:03:49, no tick since 07:01:56. Root cause IDENTIFIED + distinct from MB-20260609-001: the regime_bar_scoring fetch-gate + dedup caches are PER-PROCESS and EMPTY on a fresh restart, so the first post-restart tick fetched every (symbol,timeframe) group (incl. blocking IB/MES fetches) AND scored all ~20 shadow heads in ONE synchronous mega-tick on the main loop -> heartbeat (written between ticks) froze. MB-20260609-001 bounded steady-state per-tick cost but NOT the cold-start burst. Operator-approved remediation: set-env REGIME_BAR_SCORING_DISABLED=1 + restart (#3211, 07:10:56Z) -> cpu 100->52% + heartbeat resumed advancing (07:12:52, label running) = recovered. FIX shipped this PR: REGIME_BAR_SCORING_BUDGET_S (default 6s) caps per-call wall time, deferring remaining whole groups to the next tick. Regime-bar-scoring is DISABLED on the VM pending the fix deploy + re-enable (see BL-20260610-002).

items.source: Self-inflicted incident: vm-web-api-recover run 27150313822 (issue #3026) restarted a healthy ict-web-api.service, then the wrapper's 15-second post-restart health probe failed because cold-start exceeded 15 s, leaving the unit in unknown state and emitting a misleading 'unit did not return to a serving state' error.
items.title: vm-web-api-recover wrapper's 15 s post-restart health probe is too tight for cold-start of ict-web-api.service
items.description: scripts/ops/restart_web_api.sh probes /api/health for ~15 s after the systemctl restart returns. Observed timeline 16:02:23–16:03:01 UTC: systemd stopped uvicorn cleanly (16:02:23–16:02:41), check_data_dir.sh ran (16:02:43–16:02:44), systemd reported 'Started ICT Trading Bot — dashboard API' at 16:02:44, but uvicorn didn't bind port 8001 within the wrapper's 15 s probe window (curl exit 7 at 16:03:01). At 16:13:49 /api/diag/status returned 200 OK — so uvicorn DID come up, just slowly. The 15 s probe ceiling needs widening (suggest 60 s) or the wrapper should poll until ExecStartPost completes systemd-side. Secondary issue: the wrapper's failure message implies the unit is wedged, which led this session to escalate to the operator unnecessarily. Both behaviours wasted operator attention. Lower priority than BL-20260609-001's CI trigger bug but worth a small PR.

items.title: regime_bar_scoring budget can starve later predictor groups (no per-tick rotation)
items.description: emit_regime_bar_predictions (src/runtime/regime_bar_scoring.py:~348-359) iterates groups in fixed insertion order and breaks when the per-tick wall-clock budget (REGIME_BAR_SCORING_BUDGET_S) is hit; the budget check runs before the fetch-gate skip, so the same groups are always considered first each tick. Pathological case: one group whose single fetch always consumes the whole budget could indefinitely defer the groups after it (low practical risk - an already-fetched group is a cheap continue on most ticks). Fix: rotate the group start index per tick, or order by most-overdue-for-a-fetch. Observe-only path, Tier-1.
items.resolution_note: RESOLVED 2026-07-26 (backlog-drain-tier1). Added per-tick group rotation to emit_regime_bar_predictions (src/runtime/regime_bar_scoring.py): a module-level _REGIME_GROUP_ROTATION offset (injectable `rotation` param for tests) advances each call and rotates the scan start, so a group whose fetch always eats the whole REGIME_BAR_SCORING_BUDGET_S can no longer indefinitely starve the groups behind it — over successive ticks every group takes a turn at the front of the budget-bounded scan. Observe-only path, unchanged when budget=0/unset. VERIFIED: 2 new tests (a starved group gets scored when rotated to the front; the counter advances each real call) + the existing budget test pinned to rotation=0 for determinism; tests/runtime/test_regime_bar_scoring.py 35 passed.

updates.note: Re-validated 2026-07-19: still valid — regime_bar_scoring budget can starve later predictor groups (no per-tick rotation). REGIME_BAR_SCORING_BUDGET_S bounds it. Blocker: Tier-1 code (rotation).

items.title: _capture_account_context_snapshots opens a fresh read-only SQLite connection per signal
items.description: src/core/coordinator.py:~2376 opens a new mode=ro connection on every order-package decision, then loops daily_state_for + open_trades_count_for per account (an N-account fan-out per signal). Best-effort + shares one connection across the account loop, but the connection is re-established each decision. Fix: cache a ro connection across decisions, or fold the per-account reads into one grouped query. Observe-only writer, Tier-1, minor.
items.resolution_note: RESOLVED 2026-07-26 (backlog-drain-tier1). _capture_account_context_snapshots (src/core/coordinator.py) no longer does a 2-per-account query fan-out per signal: added daily_state_for_accounts() + open_trades_count_for_accounts() to src/units/accounts/context_snapshot.py (each ONE grouped `... IN (?)` query over the whole account set), and the coordinator now issues exactly two grouped reads per decision instead of 2N. Chose the grouped-query fix over a long-lived cached RO connection deliberately — a persistent ro fd on the live trader could read a stale inode after a DB swap/migration, whereas the per-decision open (microseconds) plus 2 grouped queries removes the real N-fan-out cost with no stale-fd risk. Absent/error entries fall back to (None,None)/None, preserving the exact NULL-storing semantics. VERIFIED: 4 new batch-helper tests (match the scalar helpers, empty/missing-table → {}) + the coordinator hook test (tests/test_account_context_snapshot*.py 17 passed).
