items.source: MES restore on the isolated-gateway topology (2026-06-10). Connectivity fixed via the OCI SL rule (#3313); the post-connect liveness probe then false-tripped the breaker. Shipped an opt-out (PR #3318) and disabled the probe via env to restore MES; this is the follow-up to do it properly.
items.title: Re-enable the IB liveness probe: retry-tolerant fix shipped, live env flip (IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S=5) still pending
items.description: The IB post-connect liveness probe (IBClient._probe_liveness, src/units/accounts/ib_client.py) runs loop.run_until_complete(asyncio.wait_for(ib.reqCurrentTimeAsync(), IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S)) on the persistent loop. Over the isolated gateway (10.0.0.251, socat-relayed cross-host) this never resolves even though the connection is fully healthy (connect + 'Logged on server v176' + 'Market data farm connection is OK' + 'Synchronization complete', and the read-path client which skips the probe works) - verified timing out at BOTH 5s and 15s while sync completes in <1s. As a workaround MES is currently running with the probe DISABLED via IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S=0 on the live VM (the <=0 skip added in PR #3318); IB_FETCH_TIMEOUT_S=8 is the backstop. Proper fix: make the probe resolve over this path - likely use ib_insync's sync wrapper ib.reqCurrentTime() (which drives the loop the way connectAsync does) instead of the manual run_until_complete(reqCurrentTimeAsync()), or otherwise pump the reader during the probe; add a regression test mirroring tests/test_ib_integration.py TestEventLoopResilience. Then set-env IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S back to 5 (restores the cheap dead-session catch on top of the per-fetch timeout). Related: BL-20260610-004 Fix 3 (IBMarketData.get_ohlcv should also consult the breaker). Tier-3 (live IB connection path); PR + verify on the live gateway.
items.resolution_note: IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S set back to 5 on the live VM via the set-env system-action (issue #5685) and live-verified against a real forced cold reconnect (vm-ib-gateway-recover, issue #5686: gateway container restarted 09:14:25, IBC login completed 09:14:48). In the minutes after, the retry-tolerant probe hit four separate cold-TCP-flow misses (MES, MGC x2, MHG) between 09:17:42-09:18:10, each logging "attempt 1/2 timed out ... retrying once after 1.5s" and recovering cleanly on the retry with real candle data fetched right after — zero circuit-breaker trips, zero IBConnectionError/ConnectionError in that window (confirmed via journalctl pulls, issues #5688 + #5689). One genuine breaker trip DID fire at 09:14:26, the moment the gateway container was actually down mid-restart (ConnectionError: Socket disconnect) — correct behavior, not a false trip, since it was not a first-attempt asyncio.TimeoutError.

check_log.by: claude (IB pipeline stability review follow-up, 2026-07-06, operator-requested)
check_log.note: Shipped a code fix (PR TBD): IBClient._probe_liveness now retries the reqCurrentTime round-trip ONCE after IB_PROBE_RETRY_GAP_S (default 1.5s) before condemning the connection, instead of failing on a single timeout. Rationale: the probe fires as the FIRST message on a freshly-established connection, right after connect() — a cold TCP flow over the cross-host socat relay can miss that one round-trip even on a genuinely healthy session (every OTHER call — reqHistoricalData, accountSummary — is proven reliable over this exact relay per today's live selftest + diag pulls). A real wedge still never answers either attempt, so detection is unaffected; only a one-off cold-start miss on a healthy session is absorbed. Added 2 regression tests (tests/test_ib_integration.py: cold-miss-then-recovers stays connected + breaker closed; still-hung-after-retry trips the breaker, bounded). This does NOT yet restore protection on the live VM — IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S is still 0 (disabled) in the live .env. Re-enabling it (set to 5, restart ict-trader-live.service) is a deliberate follow-up step that should be verified against a real cold connect over the relay first, not flipped blind alongside the code merge.

RESOLVED + live-flipped. IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S=5 is enabled on ict-bot-arm; the retry-tolerant probe (ee522ca) has been proven against a real cold gateway restart with zero false breaker trips. See resolution_note for the full verification trail.

evidence_log: 2026-06-13 (operator-directed root-cause): ROOT CAUSE = DATA_DIR drop-in coverage gap. ict-hourly-snapshot.service (scripts/send_hourly_now.py -> hourly_report.account_snapshots() -> _save_balance_snapshots -> runtime_logs/balance_snapshots.json) is NOT in install_systemd_units.sh's data-dir.conf auto-install list (which covers trader-live/web-api/telegram-bot/health-snapshot/claude-bridge/insights) and sets no Environment=DATA_DIR in its unit. fix_data_dir.sh STRIPS DATA_DIR from .env, so the hourly writer resolves runtime_logs_dir() to the REPO-relative path (paths._resolve_root unset->repo fallback) and writes the fresh balance file to <repo>/runtime_logs, while ict-web-api (has the drop-in) READS /data/bot-data/runtime_logs -> frozen at the data-dir migration (~5/25). Cap the widget chip row — a window of ~6 symbols centred on the selected one (always including it), or wrap into two Rows with an overflow chip. VERIFIED still broken AND WORSE this session: CandleChartWidget.kt:95 renders availableSymbols.forEach in a single non-wrapping Glance Row, the worker writes the full uncapped union, and the state store applies no cap on read — now ~20 instruments vs the 8-chip threshold.

FIXED (ict-trader-android#117). Verified still broken AND WORSE than filed before touching it: CandleChartWidget.kt:95 rendered `availableSymbols.forEach` into a single non-wrapping Glance Row, the refresh worker wrote the full uncapped union, and the state store applied no cap on read — ~20 instruments across 51 strategies against the 8-chip threshold this row names.

Fix is `visibleSymbolWindow()`: a window of 6 CENTRED on the selection and clamped at both ends, plus a `+N` chip stating the remainder. The centring is the actual fix — a naive take(6) would drop the SELECTED chip once it moved past index 6, leaving the widget charting a symbol with no visible way back, which is worse than clipping. The `+N` chip exists so the row cannot read as 'the roster IS this short' (an unasserted denominator in UI form).

Algorithm verified out-of-band across all seven cases (short roster, exactly-max, selection first / mid / near-end / last, and a stale selection absent from the roster): the selected symbol is visible in every case and the row is always full. NOT verified by a Kotlin unit test — the app module has no test source set (only core/data does), which is filed separately as BL-20260813-ANDROID-APP-MODULE-NO-TEST-SOURCE-SET.

items.source: Operator pasted live ict-trading-bot ERROR logs: bybit_get_positions_failed / bybit_get_order_status_failed -> 'Unmatched IP, please check your API key's bound IP addresses (ErrCode: 10010)' on account=bybit_2, starting ~18:37 UTC (after the 2026-06-14 live->Ampere cutover).
items.title: Bybit API-key bound-IP allowlist not updated for the new Ampere live VM -> ErrCode 10010 on bybit_2 (real-money money-path outage)
items.description: ROOT CAUSE: the live->Ampere cutover (2026-06-14) moved the trader's egress IP from the micro 158.178.210.252 to the Ampere VM ict-bot-arm 141.145.193.91, but the Bybit API key BYBIT_API_KEY_2 (real money, mainnet api.bybit.com) still has its bound-IP allowlist set to the OLD micro IP. Bybit rejects every authed request from the new IP with ErrCode 10010 'Unmatched IP'. Effect: bybit_2 get_positions + get_order_status (and almost certainly order placement) fail every tick -> the real-money account is blind (cannot reconcile / monitor / open new trades). Native exchange-side SL/TP brackets still protect open positions (they fire on Bybit, not via the client). The cutover checklist in docs/runbooks/live-vm-migration-ampere.md NEVER included 'update the Bybit API-key IP allowlist' -- documented now as follow-up item 6. FIX (operator-only, broker-side, no workflow can do it): on Bybit -> API Management, add 141.145.193.91 to the bound-IP list for BYBIT_API_KEY_2 (keep 158.178.210.252 during the rollback soak; drop it at micro decommission). Also check/repeat for BYBIT_API_KEY_1 (demo, api-demo.bybit.com). NOTE the new VM's egress IP is its OCI public IP (1:1 NAT) = 141.145.193.91; if Bybit still rejects after binding, confirm the exact egress empirically before re-editing. Tier: operator broker-side action + Tier-1 doc fix (this entry + runbook item 6).
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-06-15. The operator bound 141.145.193.91 on the Bybit key, but binding the IP is necessary-not-sufficient: the running ict-trader-live + ict-web-api processes hold BYBIT_API_KEY_2 in os.environ from their last start and never re-read creds at runtime, so they kept failing 10010 until RESTARTED (restart-bot-service + vm-web-api-recover reloaded the corrected .env; new-VM processes then authenticate retCode 0 OK, verified by reproducing the exact call inside the trader's /proc/<pid>/environ). LESSON added to runbook item 6: after rebinding the IP on Bybit, RESTART the trader + web-api. NOTE: a SEPARATE, longer-lived source of the same 10010 spam was the zombie bot fleet left running on the retired micro (158.178.210.252) calling Bybit from its now-unbound IP -- tracked + resolved as BL-20260615-MICRO-ZOMBIE.

items.opened_by: claude (operator-driven live IBKR login validation session)
items.source: Operator wanted to validate the real-money IBKR live login + 2FA works (ib_live, U25907316). Built vm-ib-gateway-live-login-test (throwaway read-only live container on the gateway VM, paper untouched). Four runs (#3631/#3633/#3635/#3640) all reached IBC 'Authenticating...' and timed out with NO push. Operator's IBKR-Mobile screenshot showed the IB Key 'Generate Response' (challenge/response) screen.
items.title: Live IBKR login blocked: bot user's IB Key 2FA is challenge/response (Seamless Authentication OFF) -> headless gateway can't complete a live login
items.description: Paper logins are 2FA-exempt so ib_paper is unaffected and healthy. LIVE logins require 2FA; the bot user's IB Key is in CHALLENGE/RESPONSE mode (Seamless OFF), so IBKR issues no push and the headless gateway (Xvfb) can neither read the on-screen challenge nor type the response -> hangs at 'Authenticating...' and times out. Pinning IBC SecondFactorDevice='IB Key Security via IBKR Mobile' changed nothing (no device-selection dialog ever appeared), confirming the block is upstream of device selection (no push challenge issued). FIX (operator-only, broker-side): enable SEAMLESS (push) authentication for the bot user in IBKR (account-specific; confirm exact steps with IBKR client services -- it is NOT the IBKR-Mobile Security page; involves Client Portal Secure Login + the bot user being registered for IBKR-Mobile push). Seamless push is REQUIRED for live anyway because the gateway re-logs in unattended daily after IBKR's reset; challenge/response cannot be automated. Then re-run via the vm-ib-gateway-live-login-test label and tap the push. NOT URGENT: ib_live is mode:dry_run (not trading); this is a pre-flight for a future capability. Tooling is built + verified. Full runbook: docs/runbooks/ib-live-login-2fa.md. Tier: operator broker-side action + Tier-1 doc (this entry + runbook).

items.title: Retired x86 micro (158.178.210.252) left running a ZOMBIE bot fleet post-cutover -> spammed bybit_2 ErrCode 10010 from its unbound IP + served stale data to the Android app
items.description: ROOT CAUSE: the 2026-06-14 live->Ampere cutover never actually shut the bot down on the retired micro. ict-trader-live + ict-web-api + a full fleet of TIMERS (ict-hourly-snapshot, ict-insights-generator(-strategies), ict-heartbeat, ict-health-snapshot, ict-web-api-watchdog, ict-git-sync, ict-liveness-watchdog, ...) kept running on the micro with the real bybit_2 key (its .env was unchanged). The micro egresses from 158.178.210.252, which was dropped from the Bybit API-key allowlist at cutover (only 141.145.193.91 is bound), so every authed bybit_2 call (get_positions via the timers' account_snapshots, get_wallet_balance) returned ErrCode 10010 and the micro's outcomes.report fanned it to the SHARED Telegram channel -- indistinguishable from a new-VM failure. The micro's web-api also still answered :8001, so the Android app (default BOT_API_URL = the micro) read live status+MES off it while BTCUSDT came back no_data (micro Bybit-frozen) -- the 'app shows data from the micro' symptom. WHY IT WAS HARD: api_call failures route to outcomes.jsonl + Telegram, NOT stdout, so journalctl was blind; and the new VM always reproduced OK, so the source had to be a different machine. RESOLUTION (operator-approved 'stop services, keep VM for rollback'): built .github/workflows/stop-micro-zombie.yml (issue label stop-micro-zombie) -- SSHes the micro and stop+disables ALL ict-*.timer + ict-*.service units (two passes; the web-api-watchdog + git-sync.timer resurrected the trader through the first two narrow passes -- they MUST be disabled first). Verified fully dark + zero residual python bot processes at 14:45 and again at 14:53 (stable). Micro VM left UP as the rollback target. PROCESS GAP: the cutover/decommission runbook (live-vm-migration-ampere.md Phase 3/4) must STOP+DISABLE the entire ict-* unit fleet on the old VM (or power it off) at cutover -- not just leave it 'stopped'. Rollback = re-enable the micro units + re-add 158.178.210.252 to the Bybit allowlist. Tier: ops action DONE + Tier-1 doc (this entry + runbook Phase 3/4 update).

items.source: Part-2 audit (dashboard code review). In ict-trader-dashboard streamlit_app.py, _lc_candle_data/_lc_ema_data/_lc_volume_data call int(ts.timestamp()) on tz-NAIVE timestamps (host-local epoch), while _lc_markers uses tz-aware UTC. On a UTC host (Streamlit Cloud prod) they agree; on any non-UTC host candles/EMA/volume shift vs signal/trade markers by the UTC offset.
items.title: Dashboard chart timezone divergence (candle/EMA/volume tz-naive vs UTC markers)
items.description: ACTION FOR CLAUDE: localize candle/EMA/volume timestamps to UTC before .timestamp() (pd.to_datetime(..., utc=True) + tz_localize('UTC')) so all series share one epoch basis. This is a UI-rendering change → must go through the dashboard preview-app verification workflow (claude/web-app-preview), NOT straight to main. Low urgency (production runs UTC, masked).
items.trigger_condition: Next dashboard chart work, or next time the preview app is in use.
items.resolution_criteria: Fix verified on the preview app and merged to dashboard main.
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-07-26 (backlog-drain-tier1) — fix pushed in ict-trader-dashboard PR #202 (draft, pending CI+merge; UI-render change → verify live on prod app after merge per the repo's single-app workflow). _lc_candle_data/_lc_ema_data/_lc_volume_data called int(ts.timestamp()) on the tz-NAIVE candle timestamp column (host-local epoch), diverging from the tz-aware UTC markers on any non-UTC host. Added _lc_epoch() which localizes a naive Timestamp to UTC (a relabel, not a shift) before .timestamp() so all series share one epoch basis on any host. VERIFIED: recovers the exact epoch (1700000000) from a naive UTC-wallclock ts; aware ts pass through. Masked in prod (Streamlit Cloud runs UTC), so live behaviour there is unchanged.

items.title: Reverse reconciler re-adopts ONE orphan exchange position as N trades (19x MGC -$23,773 + 3x MHG; episodic on IB-gateway flap)
items.description: One mgc_trend_1h MGC position (order_package pkg-81602a3b78e14f) appears as 18 CLOSED trade rows, ALL with identical entry_price 4318.872 + position_size 8, ALL notes.adopted_by=reverse_reconciler, adopted_at spanning 06-17 18:48->19:20 UTC, each booking a phantom sl_cross loss (sum -$20,127.68) on ib_paper. ROOT CAUSE: _reconcile_orphan_exchange_positions (src/runtime/order_monitor.py) creates a NEW orphan_adopt trade each time it sees the position unmatched, instead of recognising the prior adoption's open row as already covering it — so a flapping IB-gateway portfolio (empty->present->empty during the 06-17 evening IBKR reset window) spawns a fresh adopted trade per blip. ADOPT-side sibling of BL-20260614-ORPHANBLIP (which fixed the CLOSE-side re-orphan via the 2-observation close-confirm). Pollutes mgc_trend_1h stats; risks N-way realised-PnL double-count if it hits real-money bybit_2.
items.suggested_fix: Before creating an orphan_adopt row, check for an EXISTING open trade on the same (account,symbol,side,~entry/size) and re-attach/skip rather than adopt-again; or key adoption idempotency on the exchange position id. Add a regression test replaying empty->present->empty gateway snapshots. Consider a 2-observation confirm on the ADOPT side too.

Authoritative live count via the ict-db-integrity checker (INV-2, /api/diag/journalctl): 102 closed pnl-IS-NULL rows, recent=0 (none in the last 48h — the live multiplier-aware sweep keeps current closes clean). PR #4017 hardened scripts/ops/backfill_pnl_nulls.py to delegate to the canonical src.runtime.local_pnl helpers (contract_value_usd multiplier) — it previously undercounted IBKR futures (MGC 10x / MES 5x / MHG 2500x) via a raw (exit-entry)*size formula; real-money bybit_2 (crypto, cvu=1) was unaffected. The residual 102 rows all LACK an exit_price (so local compute is impossible and marking to today's price would be wrong) and are old (recent=0); they are correctly NULL and already excluded from /performance + /stats aggregates, so headline totalPnL / expectancy / equity are correct. items.source: Live VM diag (issue #4203 journalctl ict-liveness-watchdog.service): the liveness watchdog (Type=oneshot, fires every ~60s) intermittently fails at the systemd STDIN-setup step with `Failed to set up standard input: No such file or directory` / `status=208/STDIN` (~8% of runs; observed 16:08:08 and 16:12:29 UTC), BEFORE check_heartbeat.py runs. Each failure self-heals on the next minute's run, so the unit's `failed` state is transient (the snapshot at 16:12:32 happened to land 3s after a failed run). The repo canonical unit (deploy/ict-liveness-watchdog.service) sets NO StandardInput (default null -> /dev/null, which cannot ENOENT), so the deployed unit/drop-in has drifted OR a git-sync `git reset --hard` race transiently breaks the spawn.
items.title: VERIFY the liveness-watchdog 208/STDIN intermittent exec failure is gone after the StandardInput=null pin reinstall
items.description: The dead-man switch must spawn reliably on every tick; an ~8% per-run exec failure erodes the 3-strike (~8 min) autoheal margin and a sticky `failed` state masks a genuinely-dead watchdog. Remediation: PR pins `StandardInput=null` explicitly in deploy/ict-liveness-watchdog.service (BL-20260622-WATCHDOG-STDIN), which on the next runtime git-sync forces install_systemd_units.sh to recopy the (now-differing) unit, reconverging any drift. FOLLOW UP: after the reinstall is confirmed (deployed unit == repo), pull `journalctl?unit=ict-liveness-watchdog.service&lines=200` and confirm ZERO `208/STDIN` occurrences across a >=30-min window. If 208/STDIN PERSISTS after a confirmed reinstall of the explicit-StandardInput unit, the cause is a drop-in (/etc/systemd/system/ict-liveness-watchdog.service.d/*.conf) or a git-sync `git reset --hard` spawn race (NOT main-unit drift) — escalate to a targeted system-action that `systemctl cat`s the deployed unit + drop-ins and purges any rogue drop-in. Note: the `/etc/ict-vm-role: No such file or directory` log line in deploy_pull_restart.sh line 91 is cosmetic/expected on the trader (empty role = not gateway); NOT a drift to fix.
items.resolution: PR #4206 pinned StandardInput=null on deploy/ict-liveness-watchdog.service; merged 2026-06-22T16:36:59Z (main baeec23e) and deployed via ict-git-sync (full path: install_systemd_units.sh recopied the now-differing unit + one trader bounce; VM confirmed on git_sha baeec23e, trader healthy post-restart). SOAK VERIFIED: watchdog journal 16:41:01-17:17:04 UTC (~36 min, ~36 consecutive per-minute runs, diag issue #4210) shows EVERY run clean (Starting -> Deactivated successfully -> Finished); ZERO 208/STDIN / "Failed to set up standard input" after the reinstall, vs ~8% failure rate before. Root cause confirmed as MAIN-UNIT DRIFT (reconverged by the idempotent reinstall) — NOT a drop-in or git-sync reset --hard race, so no escalation/purge action needed. The /etc/ict-vm-role "No such file" deploy-log line was confirmed cosmetic/expected on the trader.

items.description: A closed real-money row must carry a realised pnl (broker-truth or local_compute sweep). The reconciler close path that produced #2783 set status='closed' without resolving pnl, and the 6h order_monitor._sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced grace then elapsed with it still NULL. Investigate the instant-close path (closedAt<=openedAt, null exit) in order_monitor — likely a netting/flat reconcile that booked a close without an exit fill. check_log.note: Fix landed (order_monitor close/sweep path, Tier-2): the gap was the local-compute sweep deferring broker-reader (Bybit) rows the full 7-day _BROKER_PNL_RECOVERY_MS window while the Bybit closed-pnl sweep could never fill them (no realised closed-pnl record exists for a same-instant net-flat). Between the 6h INV-2 grace and day 7 nothing touched the row -> closed/NULL -> INV-2. Fix: new _LOCAL_PNL_BROKER_DEFER_MS (6h = DEFAULT_PNL_GRACE_HOURS) shortens the local-sweep defer so a broker row the reader still can't price converges to local_compute (pnl~=0 truthful for a same-instant flat) right after the grace. Broker truth still wins within the grace. +3 tests in tests/test_local_pnl.py. The larger 'should it be booked closed at all' question logged for follow-up if instant-flat reconciles recur.

No recurrence of the 06:00Z wedge observed since the retime. Leaving open one more full week before closing outright to be sure — full findings in docs/research/ib-pipeline-stability-review-2026-07-06.md.

RECURRENCE 2026-07-07 ~07:55:14Z: ict-web-api.service journal (diag #5829) shows 'IBClient: account/portfolio warm-up timed out twice (8s+8s retry) for 10.0.0.251:4002 (account=...5724) -- gateway likely logged out' + 'circuit breaker tripped ... consecutive failures=16'; concurrent exchange_positions?account_id=ib_paper (diag #5831) reads positions=null (could-not-read). Raised as the mandatory broker-reachability flag for this review (see anomalies/flags). Recommend vm-ib-gateway-recover if not already auto-fired by the reachability-alert latch.

ROOT-CAUSE FINDING: system-actions.yml's gateway-logs action has been silently pointed at the wrong host since the 2026-06-10 gateway-isolation redesign -- it SSHes to VM_SSH_HOST (141.145.193.91, the live trader) and runs 'docker ps/logs ib-gateway' there, but the ib-gateway container has lived on the dedicated gateway VM (10.0.0.251) since that redesign. Confirmed live (issue #5834): 'docker ps -a' returned empty and 'docker logs ib-gateway' returned "No such container: ib-gateway" -- there's no gateway container on the trader VM to inspect. This means every attempt since 2026-06-10 to use gateway-logs for root-causing a wedge (including the open BL-20260527-003 investigation) silently got no real data. FIXED this session (system-actions.yml): gateway-logs now routes via ProxyJump through the trader to GATEWAY_HOST (10.0.0.251), mirroring the pattern already used by vm-ib-gateway-recover.yml/vm-ib-gateway-selftest.yml. Also confirmed the current wedge self-recovered on its own between 07:56Z and 08:39Z (exchange_positions?account_id=ib_paper went from positions:null to positions:[],error:null) without an operator/Claude-triggered recover -- so the reactive watchdog or a passive retry cleared it, timeline TBD once gateway-logs is re-run post-fix.

OPERATOR DECISION: explored two mitigation paths for the recurring IB-gateway instability -- (1) IBKR's own Client Portal Web API (CPAPI) as a same-account transport swap to escape the Xvfb/IBC GUI-automation layer, and (2) migrating futures to a broker with a cleaner native API (Tradovate, Ironbeam direct API, Rithmic via AMP/Ironbeam). CPAPI is closed off: it requires an IBKR Pro account (confirmed via IBKR's own docs -- Lite is unsupported for API access, no SSO-only carve-out), and the operator does not have Pro and cannot get it in a relevant timeframe. On reviewing the broker-migration options (Tradovate/Ironbeam/Rithmic), the operator decided none of them are worth pursuing right now. DECISION: drop both lines of investigation for now -- stay on the current TWS-socket/ib_insync/Xvfb/IBC integration. The gateway-logs system-action routing fix (this session, see the linked PR) remains valuable regardless -- it unblocks root-causing future wedges on the CURRENT integration, which is now the only path being pursued for IB reliability. Revisit CPAPI/broker-migration only if the account tier changes or the wedge frequency/impact gets materially worse.

items.title: [risk] crypto/fx sub-min-lot refusal uses account-default min_qty, not the per-instrument platform lot (ETH 0.01 gap)
items.description: PR #4969 (merged) made a sub-min-lot risk-based size a per-trade REFUSAL on the crypto/fx (non-whole-unit) path instead of bumping it up to min_qty (the over-risk #3910 flagged). It was scoped MINIMALLY: the refusal threshold is the ACCOUNT-configured min_qty (RiskManager.min_qty, default 0.001), NOT the per-instrument platform lot from config/instruments.yaml. For BTCUSDT that's correct (real lot == 0.001), but ETHUSDT's real Bybit lot is 0.01 (instruments.yaml min_qty/qty_step 0.01) — so a risk-based ETH size in [0.001, 0.0099) currently passes the refusal (>= account 0.001) yet the exchange would reject it as sub-lot. Pre-existing (the old bump was equally wrong there) and NOT worsened by #4969 — bybit_2's live ETH position (0.01) sizes legitimately today. FOLLOW-UP (the part of #3910 deliberately left out of #4969 to keep the real-money PR surgical): add an instrument-aware floor — instrument_min_qty_step_for(symbol) reading (min_qty, qty_precision from qty_step) from config/instruments.yaml — and resolve eff_min_qty/eff_precision from it on the non-whole path, falling back to the account min_qty when a symbol has no profile. The reference implementation is in the closed #3910 diff (src/units/accounts/risk.py). Tier-3 (sizing on the live order path) + needs the test reworks for profiled-symbol precision (IWM-on-bybit synthetic tests in test_alpaca_whole_share_sizing.py).
items.source: PR #4969 (merged 744ac178) § 'Why minimal (vs full #3910)'; src/units/accounts/risk.py::position_size non-whole-unit refusal branch; config/instruments.yaml ETHUSDT min_qty/qty_step 0.01 vs RiskManager default min_qty 0.001.

updates.note: THIRD sibling of this defect found + fixed on branch claude/order-qty-rounding-issue-wj1d1v (Tier-3, draft PR pending operator approval). The intent-mode netting-DELTA guard in coordinator.py::multi_account_execute (~line 1900) also compared delta.qty_delta against account.risk_manager.min_qty (0.001), NOT the venue lot. A live ETHUSDT/bybit_2 top-up (sized 0.111, held ~0.102 -> delta 0.009) slipped the guard and hit the _submit_order pre-flight ('below the exchange lot minimum after step-alignment') -> bybit_place_order_failed error ping on every top-up/trim signal. Fix folds venue_min_qty_for into the delta guard (max(account_min, venue_min); None -> account_min unchanged), converting the noisy ping into a clean intent_sub_min_qty_delta noop. Regression tests in tests/test_intent_delta_dispatch.py::TestIntentModeVenueMinDelta. The risk.py::position_size path this item primarily tracks is STILL OPEN (separate location).

items.resolution: RESOLVED by the sizing/qty-legalization consolidation (docs/sizing-legalization-DESIGN.md, operator-approved). The recurring root cause — four divergent copies of 'the venue minimum' — was collapsed onto ONE seam, src/units/accounts/qty_legalize.py::legalize_qty, resolving (qty_step, min_qty) from the per-instrument InstrumentProfile (config/instruments.yaml) first, live Bybit lot rule second, passthrough third. Phase 2 wired the seam into the two coordinator guards (sized-qty ~1503, intent-delta ~1900) + the execute._submit_order Bybit pre-flight (#5720). Phase 3 (#5732, merged 581b45e, Tier-3 operator-approved) closed the risk.py::position_size half this item primarily tracked: the non-whole path now resolves eff_min_qty/eff_precision from qty_legalize.instrument_lot(symbol) when 0 < step < 1 (ETHUSDT 0.01, SOLUSDT 0.1), so a risk-based ETH size in [0.001, 0.0099) is now REFUSED per-trade at the sizing layer instead of passing risk.py's own 0.001 account-min. Whole-share sizing stays exchange-gated by whole_units (BL-20260622), never inferred from the instrument; BTC (step 0.001 == account default) unchanged. Tests: tests/test_instrument_min_sizing.py (11), tests/test_qty_legalize.py, tests/test_intent_delta_dispatch.py. Phase 4 (a qty-legalization CI guard forbidding raw-min comparisons outside the seam) is the remaining Tier-1 follow-up to prevent a fifth copy re-appearing.

items.title: [order-path] Alpaca positions can sit NAKED (no SL/TP) — naked-autoprotect + reconciler-adopt are IB-only; no re-arm for non-IB
items.description: Operator observed alpaca_paper showing 6 open ETF positions (TLT/SPY/SLV/QQQ/IWM/GLD) but only 2 working orders -> ~4 positions are naked (no resting SL/TP bracket leg). Alpaca entries DO attach an atomic bracket at entry (alpaca_client.place order_class=bracket, alpaca_client.py:121-129), so these lost their protective legs afterward (suspected: reverse-reconciler adopt/reattach of an orphan, or a bracket child-leg cancel/reject) and nothing re-armed them: order_monitor naked-position auto-protect (_check_naked_positions/_attempt_naked_autoprotect/_rearm_broker_protection_after_recovery) is IB-ONLY (order_monitor.py ~5159-5190); non-IB accounts only get a one-shot alert. AlpacaClient ALREADY has modify_protective + open_orders, so the building blocks for a non-IB re-arm exist. FIX (Tier-2/3, order-protection path, operator-gated): extend the naked-position sweep to re-arm an Alpaca bracket via AlpacaClient (place a fresh protective OTO/bracket or modify_protective) when an open Alpaca position has no resting SL/TP leg; cover the reconciler adopt/reattach path too. Verify on alpaca_paper first. Applies to real-money alpaca_live as well (currently flat).

items.title: [alerting] A broker account being DOWN/unreachable warrants its own loud Telegram warning + a remediation trigger (gap: IB-dark went unflagged across reviews)
items.description: OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-06-29: the IB gateway was DOWN (ib_paper/ib_live positions=null, MES/MGC/MHG dark) across one or more /system-review runs and it was NOT surfaced loudly — it landed in the report body, not as a can't-miss alert, and the gateway watchdog only Telegrams after EXHAUSTING its restart budget (a terse restart ping easy to skim past). There is no dedicated 'account X unreachable' warning and no remediation trigger. REQUIREMENT: when a SUPPOSED-TO-BE-LIVE broker account reads unreachable (diag exchange_positions positions=null / accounts/balances api_ok=false / IB net_liquidation=None) for >= N consecutive checks, fire its OWN high-priority Telegram [ALERT] (latched: one on cross-into-down, one [OK] on recovery — mirror the daily-cap latch, no per-tick spam), and recommend the fix (vm-ib-gateway-recover / open a /health-review session). DESIGN PROPOSAL: (a) a small latched per-account 'broker reachable' check on an existing periodic path (hourly-report or a dedicated ~5-15min watcher), scoped to accounts declared live — EXCLUDE intentionally-shelved accounts (oanda_practice, ib_live-2FA-blocked) via an allowlist/skip flag so they don't spam; (b) make the health-review + system-review skills treat any down live account as a MANDATORY flags_raised item that fires a standalone high-priority ping (not buried in the report). Optional stretch: the alert auto-opens a remediation issue/session. Tier-1/2 (observability + a live-VM check/alert); operator wants it built — confirm scope (IB-only vs all live accounts; include auto-open-session vs alert-only) before shipping.

items.title: [infra] live trader VM /dev/null clobbered into a regular file — blocks all operator-action wrappers (pull-and-deploy / restart / reboot) and every '>/dev/null' redirect
items.description: DISCOVERED 2026-06-29 while deploying #5061: the pull-and-deploy system-action FAILED with 'ERROR: /dev/null is not writable on this host — it has been clobbered into a regular file, so every ">/dev/null" redirect (and most operator-action wrappers) fail.' On the LIVE trader VM (ict-bot-arm, 141.145.193.91), /dev/null is a regular file instead of the char-special device (1,3). IMPACT: (a) every operator-action wrapper that preflight-checks or redirects to /dev/null aborts — pull-and-deploy, restart-bot-service, reboot-vm are all blocked (so the relay can't even self-repair this), (b) any process doing '>/dev/null' fails, (c) a future systemd restart of ict-trader-live whose ExecStart/redirects touch /dev/null could fail to come up. NOT currently fatal: ict-git-sync still auto-deployed #5061 (trader confirmed on git_sha d661a0ec, uptime ~104s, heartbeat running, ticks healthy) and the trader is alive — but this is a latent live-VM hazard. ROOT FIX (needs root ON the VM; no autonomous path — the action wrappers that would run it are themselves blocked by the same /dev/null breakage, so this is a genuine operator hand-off): `sudo rm -f /dev/null && sudo mknod -m 666 /dev/null c 1 3`. After repair, re-dispatch pull-and-deploy to confirm the operator-action path works again. FOLLOW-UP: find what clobbered /dev/null (a stray '>' to the literal path /dev/null from a process that ran with /dev not mounted, or a script bug writing to '/dev/null' as a file) so it doesn't recur; consider a cheap health-check assertion that /dev/null is char-special (1,3).

items.title: [infra root-source] stop the OCI host agent clobbering /dev/null on the live VM (the recurring source behind the guard + self-heals)
items.description: The live trader VM's /dev/null is repeatedly clobbered by an OS-level OCI host agent (suspected oracle-cloud-agent oci-wlp / Cloud Guard Workload-Protection FIM 'remediating' world-writable files, incorrectly including /dev/null) — see docs/runbooks/devnull-guard.md. As of 2026-06-29 we now have THREE self-heal layers (ict-devnull-guard.timer 60s, deploy_pull_restart.sh, and _lib.sh::require_systemctl — the last two added this session) plus the guard %-specifier bugfix, so consumers no longer break on a transient clobber. REMAINING: kill it at the source so /dev/null isn't being rm'd/chmod'd at all. AUTONOMOUS path to try first (SSH+sudo via a runner, NOT operator-manual): `sudo auditctl -w /dev/null -p wa -k devnull` then after it next flips `sudo ausearch -k devnull` to positively identify the writing process/agent; if it's a local oracle-cloud-agent plugin, disable that plugin's /dev remediation via its on-VM config. OPERATOR/OCI-CONSOLE path (only if the rule is tenancy-level): exclude /dev from the OCI Cloud Guard / Workload-Protection FIM profile attached to the instance — needs OCI console/tenancy access (a legitimate category-1 operator/external action). OPTIONAL mitigation regardless: tighten ict-devnull-guard.timer OnUnitActiveSec 60s -> ~20-30s to shrink the exposure window for any non-self-healing consumer (e.g. the trader's own >/dev/null subprocess plumbing). | 2026-07-14 ROUND-5/6 FINDINGS (session_01SDLWbfLGV4WYHgC2ugzedf): (1) The strip is a chmod to 644 (NOT 444) — guard journal 'was 644' heals at 14:20:44/14:58:51/15:12:01/15:27:13Z, recurring ~15-40min, NOT restart-correlated. (2) The denied opens ARE captured (key=devnull success=no exit=-13 EACCES; victims bash/git/ld/python/gawk, uid=1001, subj=unconfined) — NOT AppArmor; no shadow mount (findmnt clean); no DELETE/CREATE. (3) DECISIVE: the -w /dev/null -p wa watch does NOT capture chmod on this aarch64 kernel — the guard's own chmod-0666 heals at exact known timestamps produced ZERO attr records, so the culprit's chmod-644 was equally invisible (rounds 3-5 'no mutation events' inferences were artifacts of a blind watch). (4) Round-6 armed: explicit syscall rules -S fchmod,fchmodat (+setxattr family) -F path=/dev/null -k devnullmode via vm-devnull-diagnose arm-audit; with strips recurring ~15-40min the next read-audit should name the culprit exe=/ppid= directly. ausearch remains broken (use journald _TRANSPORT=audit or raw /var/log/audit grep, ~7.5h retention). | 2026-07-14 ROUND-7 CONCLUSION (session_01SDLWbfLGV4WYHgC2ugzedf): a denial window hit at 19:26Z, FOUR MINUTES after the fchmodat2 (#452) rule armed (19:22Z re-arm confirmed in CONFIG_CHANGE rows) — and the devnullmode key STILL captured zero events. Every plausible arch=b64 userspace mutation path is now EXCLUDED by direct observation: fchmod/fchmodat/fchmodat2/setxattr-family (armed syscall rules, silent), node DELETE/CREATE + mounts (clean), AppArmor (subj=unconfined victims, no AVC). Residual hypotheses, in rough likelihood order: (a) kernel-internal attribute change on the devtmpfs inode (no syscall record by construction) — e.g. a snapd/OCI-agent device-cgroup or devtmpfs refresh path; (b) arch=b32 compat process (untested — b32 audit rules may not even load on this Ampere kernel without CONFIG_COMPAT); (c) an eBPF/LSM inode modification. ACTIVE HUNTING PAUSED after 7 rounds: the operational impact is fully mitigated (ict-devnull-guard 60s heal + restart_bot.sh mid-run heal_devnull + ERR_SINK, all live-verified), strips are brief (~15-60s before heal) and harm nothing, and the devnull/devnullmode traps STAY ARMED — if a future capture names the culprit, resume at the source-kill step (Tier-2, operator OK). Empirical facts bank: chmod to 644 (not 444); windows recur in bursts roughly aligned with the ~15-min timer/tick cadence; victims are all uid-1001 + snap_daemon (oracle-cloud-agent unifiedmonitoring appears as a VICTIM, weakening the original oci-wlp-as-culprit theory).

updates.note: Diagnostic tooling BUILT (Tier-1); the mutating step is HELD for one operator OK. The prior hand-off ('sudo auditctl ... then ausearch') is now an owner-gated workflow: .github/workflows/vm-devnull-source-diagnose.yml (label vm-devnull-diagnose, added to bootstrap-labels.yml). Modes: inspect (READ-ONLY — dumps oracle-cloud-agent/oci-wlp units+plugins+config and greps its logs for dev/null|remediat|world-writable + current /dev/null state + any existing auditd rule/events; may name the agent with zero mutation), arm-audit (Tier-2 — installs auditd if absent + persistent /etc/audit/rules.d/devnull.rules '-w /dev/null -p wa -k devnull', survives reboot), read-audit (READ-ONLY — ausearch -k devnull -i; CULPRIT = the SYSCALL setting mode 0444/stripping the write bit; the guard's own 0666 restores are expected noise). Run inspect first; only arm-audit needs the operator ack. Once the writer is identified: reconfigure the on-VM agent plugin's /dev remediation (autonomous via runner+sudo) OR exclude /dev from the tenancy Cloud Guard/Workload-Protection FIM profile (OCI-console operator action if tenancy-level).

Diagnostic pass (vm-devnull-diagnose #6130 read-audit + #6132 inspect). Findings: (1) the auditd watch IS loaded/active — `auditctl -l` → `-w /dev/null -p wa -k devnull`; auditd running. (2) ausearch -k devnull is EMPTY — no /dev/null attr event captured since arming. (3) /dev/null healthy: 666 char(1,3), mtime unmoved ~20h; ict-devnull-guard runs every ~60s but every cycle 'Finished' as a no-op (it only mknod/chmods on a detected problem) — i.e. NO clobber has occurred in ~20h. The clobber is far rarer than the 'recurring' framing (or currently dormant); the guard fully contains the symptom. (4) NO direct attribution in the oracle-cloud-agent logs — the apparent '0444' grep hits are MICROSECOND-TIMESTAMP false positives (e.g. '18:34:10.000444'), not mode-0444 remediation lines; no 'remediated /dev/null' log exists. Prime suspect remains oci-wlp (OCI Workload Protection / FIM plugin — snap.oracle-cloud-agent running; oci-falcon NOT installed) but UNCONFIRMED. FORWARD PATH: leave the watch armed; the NEXT clobber will be captured by `-w -p wa` (attribute-change) with the acting exe/pid → attribution. IF the next confirmed flip ALSO yields an empty ausearch, THEN the -w watch has a blind spot and we add a syscall rule (`-a always,exit -F path=/dev/null -F perm=a -k devnull`). No source-kill is proposable without attribution, and the guard makes this LOW-urgency. No operator action needed now.

Re-validated 2026-07-19: root-source (OCI host agent clobbering /dev/null) NOT eliminated — the recurring source behind the whole devnull cluster. Currently /dev/null is healthy (this session's actions succeeded). Blocker: Tier-2 infra (stop the host agent / durable guard).

ESCALATION (system-review-partial-2026-07-21): confirmed STILL ACTIVE and now observed breaking a THIRD operational surface this session -- (1) health snapshot git_drift check ('fatal: could not open /dev/null for reading and writing: Permission denied'), (2) the grade-closed-trades system-action wrapper (scripts/ops/_lib.sh:205 and grade_closed_trades_action.sh:82 both hit the same Permission denied), and per the existing backlog items, pull-and-deploy tooling. This has been open since 2026-06-29 (>3 weeks) across 5 backlog items without a landed fix. Per the operator's 2026-07-19 'if you see something, say something' directive, a recurring-and-unfixed condition spanning multiple sessions without resolution is itself the P1 (alarm-fatigue) pattern that directive names -- recommend the next VM-ops session prioritize actually fixing the OCI host-agent /dev/null clobbering at its root cause (BL-20260629-DEVNULL-OCI-SOURCE-KILL) rather than continuing to note the symptom each review.

NEW CLUE (read-audit re-run, issue #7298, 2026-07-21T07:52Z): the armed audit rules are STILL capturing zero chmod/fchmod/fchmodat/fchmodat2/setxattr/mount events on /dev/null (the mode-strip mechanism remains syscall-invisible to this rule set, as in Rounds 5-7) -- but this pass's DENIED-open sweep (success=no, key=devnull) caught one denial from Oracle's OWN agent, not just our tooling: comm="unifiedmonitori" exe="/snap/oracle-cloud-agent/118/plugins/unifiedmonitoring/unifiedmonitoring" subj=snap.oracle-cloud-agent.oracle-cloud-agent, EACCES on openat, in the same ~07:35Z window as ~30 denied opens from our own unconfined bash/git/python. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this is the unifiedmonitoring plugin being DENIED /dev/null too (a victim, like our tooling), NOT proof it's the one stripping the mode -- no process was ever caught performing the actual strip. That both a snap-confined OCI process AND unconfined trader processes hit the same denial in the same narrow window, with zero captured mutation syscalls, points away from 'some process ran chmod' and toward the mode genuinely being wrong on the device node for a brief window via a path the current audit rules don't cover -- most likely candidate not yet tried: a udev coldplug/hotplug re-trigger recreating /dev/null with a udev-rule default mode (would show as a kernel uevent, not a userspace chmod syscall). NEXT STEP for whoever picks this up: `udevadm monitor --udev --kernel` left running (or `journalctl -k -f | grep -i null`) across a captured strip window, correlated against the guard's restore timestamps, to check for an add/change uevent on the null device node.

items.title: ml-review staleness check should track a model's CURRENT registry stage, not the stage it was at when first observed
items.description: Root cause of the false alarm: both models were demoted advisory→shadow around 2026-06-23 / 2026-06-25 (MB-20260623-001 / MB-20260625-001, degenerate live-score reasons — the yz vol_bucket-edge calibration gap documented in src/runtime/regime_bar_scoring.py's own module docstring). ShadowPredictor logs whatever `stage` value it was instantiated with, so predictions before the demotion carry stage="advisory" and predictions after carry stage="shadow" for the SAME model_id. The staleness check that fed the system-review evidently kept querying (or reasoning about) the OLD stage label instead of re-resolving the model's current registry stage before judging it stale — so a clean, expected demotion looked identical to a silent failure. No code fix needed for the models themselves (they are healthy); the fix is in the review methodology: any future staleness/liveness check for a shadow model should look up its CURRENT target_deployment_stage from the registry first, then query shadow_stats for that stage specifically — never assume the stage recorded at first-flagged-stale time is still current.

items.resolution_criteria: The staleness-check step in the ml-review / system-review skill (wherever it lives) re-resolves each candidate model's current registry stage before querying shadow_stats, rather than reusing a stage captured earlier in the session or assumed from a prior finding.
items.resolution: Diagnosed as a false alarm, not a bug in the models or the shadow-logging pipeline (Track C of the 2026-07-02 system-review follow-up plan). Both btc-regime-1h-lgbm-yz-v1 and btc-regime-5m-lgbm-yz-v1 confirmed actively producing shadow-stage predictions in real time. items.source: gpu-burst-train.yml run 28772601594 (arm-B burst issue #5642) was CANCELLED while queued: the workflow triggers on EVERY issues.opened (non-labeled ones conclude 'skipped'), and its single `concurrency: group: gpu-burst-train` means each new issue's run displaces the previously PENDING run in the group - so an unrelated trainer-diag/diag-request issue opened while one burst runs silently cancels the next queued burst.
items.title: gpu-burst-train concurrency group lets ANY new issue cancel a queued burst
items.description: Queued (pending) gpu-burst runs are silently cancelled by any subsequent issue in the repo because all issues.opened events share the one concurrency group. A cancelled burst looks like 'never ran' unless someone inspects the Actions history. Observed 2026-07-06 (arm B #5642 cancelled by the #5643 trainer-diag issue's skip-run); worked around by firing bursts one at a time.
items.suggested_fix: Gate the concurrency group on the label match (e.g. move the label check to a first job whose output gates the burst job, and key concurrency as gpu-burst-${{ github.event.issue.number }} on the burst job only, or set the group at job level only for labeled issues). Keep spend-gate serialization by having the burst job itself take a repo-level lock (the ledger commit step already serializes on push).
items.trigger_condition: Next health-review / CI-touching session.
items.resolution: Fixed: the concurrency group is now conditional — only gpu-burst-train-labelled runs share the serializing 'gpu-burst-train' group (so two real bursts still can't run at once), while every other issues.opened event (diag-relay, system-action, trainer-diag skip-runs) gets a unique 'gpu-burst-skip-<run_id>' group and can never cancel a queued burst. Root cause was that concurrency is evaluated at the workflow level before the job's label `if`, so all issues entered the one group.

items.source: diag relay issues #5827/#5829/#5831 (2026-07-07): GET /api/bot/health/latest and /api/bot/health/services both returned non-2xx (curl --fail -> 'fetch_failed') on TWO independent pulls this session, and /api/bot/accounts/balances failed the same way once, while every sibling /api/bot/* route in the SAME ssh batch (stats, positions, order-packages, trades/closed, strategies/*/review, candles, config, etc.) succeeded. Code review: src/web/api/routers/accounts.py::get_account_balances is `async def` but calls `_from_db()` -> `Database().get_latest_balance_snapshots()` synchronously (a blocking sqlite3 read against a 433MB trade_journal.db under constant live-trader write load), not wrapped in run_in_threadpool/asyncio.to_thread.
items.title: GET /api/bot/health/{latest,services} and /api/bot/accounts/balances intermittently return non-2xx -- likely a blocking DB call stalling uvicorn's single event loop under load
items.description: Reproduced twice this session (diag #5827 first batch, #5829 targeted retry) for health/latest + health/services; accounts/balances failed once (#5831), succeeded in other pulls. Hypothesis: `accounts.py::_from_db()` runs a synchronous sqlite3 read directly inside an `async def` route with no thread-pool offload -- if that read blocks (WAL lock contention / long fsync under the live trader's constant write volume), it freezes uvicorn's whole single-worker event loop, starving every other in-flight request (which is why health/latest and health/services, both otherwise-trivial file/subprocess reads, failed in the same window). This co-occurred with a live IB-gateway circuit-breaker trip (BL-20260623-002 recurrence) and a burst of ~80 near-simultaneous dashboard/Android requests in the same ~90s window (ict-web-api journalctl, diag #5829) -- consistent with event-loop contention, though not proven without a direct trace. A similar class of bug was just fixed for IB account/position reads in commit 1f286ee (BL-20260706-IBCONCURRENCY, 'offload IB account/position reads off uvicorn's event loop') -- this may be the same pattern in a different router. FIX (Tier-1, API code, no live-trade-path risk): wrap `Database().get_latest_balance_snapshots()` in `asyncio.to_thread(...)` (or equivalent) inside `accounts.py::get_account_balances`; audit `health_snapshots.py::get_services`'s `subprocess.run` similarly (it already has timeout=3 but is still a blocking call inside an async route). Verify by re-pulling health/latest + health/services + accounts/balances via the diag relay several times back-to-back and confirming no repeat 'fetch_failed', ideally during/after a deliberately-induced DB-busy window.
items.resolution_note: RESOLVED (RISK-3 Task 1) by PR #6029 (9c3987d, 'web-api: eliminate event-loop-blocking in async routes'), verified on main 2026-07-09. Every blocking read route across 23 routers is now either a plain `def` (FastAPI threadpools sync routes) or an `async def` that offloads via `asyncio.to_thread` (`get_account_balances` is now plain `def`; `prop.post_report` offloads `ingest_report`). `PRAGMA busy_timeout=3000` added to both connect paths (`prop_journal._connect` + `units/db/database.py`). A permanent class-eliminator AST guard `scripts/ci/check_async_route_blocking.py` is wired as the `async-route-blocking-guard` CI merge gate (green) + `tests/test_async_route_blocking_guard.py`.

items.title: IB account/portfolio-warmup timeout recurred on ib_paper the day after BL-20260706-IBWARMUP / BL-20260706-IBACCTUPDATES-COLLISION landed — confirm the fix is actually deployed + effective
items.description: This is the exact failure signature (`IB_ACCOUNT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S` probe-then-condemn path in `IBClient.connect()`/`_warm_account_data`) that BL-20260706-IBWARMUP and its BL-20260706-IBACCTUPDATES-COLLISION follow-up were supposed to fix on 2026-07-06. Seeing it trip again on 2026-07-07T02:15Z blocked a legitimate mgc_pullback_1d short (confidence 0.55, trending regime ADX 37.9 — a decent setup that never got a chance to fill; see performance-review scoring for pkg-8d2b5d6cffbc4552). Two possibilities: (a) the fix reduces but does not eliminate cold-TCP-flow misses (the retry-then-condemn design accepts SOME residual failures by construction, per IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S's own docs — in which case this is expected background noise, not a regression); or (b) the fix hasn't actually rolled to the live VM (check `/api/diag/version` git_sha against the PR merge commit) or isn't retrying as designed. FIX: pull `/api/diag/version` + `/api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live.service` around 2026-07-07T02:14-02:16Z to see whether `_warm_account_data` actually attempted its documented retry before condemning the connection; if the retry never fired, the deploy or the retry logic itself needs a second look. If it did retry and still failed, this is within the documented residual-failure envelope and just needs a frequency count over a longer window before deciding whether IB_ACCOUNT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S/IB_PROBE_RETRY_GAP_S need raising.
items.trigger_condition: Next health-review or VM investigation session; also re-check if this recurs multiple times in a short window (would argue for (b) over (a)).
items.resolution_criteria: Either confirmed as expected residual noise within the documented retry-tolerant design (close as won't-fix, cite the retry evidence), or confirmed as a deploy/logic gap and fixed with a follow-up PR.
items.resolution: NOT A REGRESSION — outcome (a): the retry-tolerant warm-up worked exactly as designed and correctly condemned a GENUINELY-WEDGED gateway. Definitive evidence from the narrow journalctl window (diag relay #5847, 2026-07-07T02:13-02:16Z on ict-trader-live.service): the gateway (10.0.0.251:4002, clientId 497) failed the LIVENESS PROBE repeatedly 02:13:05-02:14:47 ('liveness probe attempt 1/2 timed out after 5s ... retrying once'), then on the mgc_pullback_1d dispatch at 02:14:52 the probe passed but the WARM-UP 'timed out TWICE (8s + 8s retry)' at 02:15:10 -> 'gateway likely logged out' -> breaker tripped (consecutive failures=1) -> order rejected. So the documented retry (BL-20260706-IBWARMUP / BL-20260610-009) DID fire on both the probe and the warm-up; the gateway genuinely wasn't answering either attempt. Deploy confirmed current at the time (/api/diag/version git_sha=3690317e, well after the 2026-07-06 fix commits). This was an UNSCHEDULED gateway wedge (02:15Z is before IBKR's ~03:45-05:45 reset window), and the gateway recovered on its own (a live exchange_positions read on ib_paper succeeded at 10:05Z). CONCLUSION: raising IB_ACCOUNT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S / adding retries would be the WRONG fix — the gateway was DOWN, not slow, and a longer timeout would only block the trader loop longer. The warm-up/breaker path is correct: it isolated the dead gateway from the loop, which is its job. The two GENUINE gaps this exposed are NOT in the warmup code: (1) gateway-wedge RECOVERY LATENCY (reactive gateway-VM watchdog ~10-15min + daily 06:05 reset), and (2) DROPPED DAILY SIGNALS — a 1d strategy fires once, so a wedge at the exact fire moment loses the signal entirely with no retry. (2) is the real hardening opportunity (retry a breaker-open-rejected order across the next few ticks) and is surfaced to the operator as a Tier-2/3 design option; if pursued it gets its own item, not this one. Observability for all of this now ships via /api/diag/ib_state (PR #5845, merged e08fe3a).

items.source: journal?table=trades (diag relay #5836), trade ids 3226/3227 (mgc_trend_1h short MGC, ib_paper, 2026-07-07 05:25/06:00Z): `entry_reason` reads 'REJECTED: dry_run_no_order_placed | mgc_trend_1h signal' and `notes.reason` is 'dry_run_no_order_placed' with `notes.is_dry: false` — but the linked order_package's `meta.rejected_reason` says 'risk-refused (no fill placed); reconciled from the journalled rejection row' and `meta.rejected_by: monitor_reconciler`.
items.title: mgc_trend_1h rejections carry a stale/mismatched 'dry_run_no_order_placed' entry_reason text while the order-package meta records the real cause as risk-refused (reconciled)
items.description: Two data points disagree about WHY the same rejected trade happened: the `trades.entry_reason`/`notes.reason` literally say 'dry_run_no_order_placed' (which would imply `is_dry: true`), yet the same row's `notes.is_dry` is `false` and the linked order_package's `meta` says the real cause was a risk-manager refusal later reconciled by `monitor_reconciler`. This is confusing for anyone (human or /performance-review) reading `trades.entry_reason` at face value — it doesn't match the account's actual dry-run state or the order package's own recorded rejection cause. Likely a stale/leftover reason string written at an earlier point in the rejection path that never got updated when the reconciler backfilled the real cause into `meta`. FIX (Tier-1, observability/data-integrity, no live-trade-path change): trace where `entry_reason='dry_run_no_order_placed'` gets written for a `mgc_trend_1h`/ib_paper rejection (likely `src/runtime/orders.py` or the risk-refusal path in `RiskManager`) and confirm it reflects the account's actual `is_dry` state, or have the reconciler backfill the same corrected text into `trades.entry_reason` (not just `order_packages.meta`) so the two never disagree again.
items.trigger_condition: Next health-review or a session touching the risk-refusal/reconciler rejection-reason write path.
items.resolution_criteria: Either the root cause is found and the reason text is corrected (both fields agree), or the discrepancy is explained as intentional (e.g. two independent 'reason' fields with legitimately different meanings) and documented so it stops looking like a bug.

updates.note: ROOT FRAME CLARIFIED (narrows the fix, item stays open): the 'dry_run_no_order_placed' entry_reason is NOT a stale/wrong string — mgc_trend_1h is config execution:shadow (config/strategies.yaml L785), so the STRATEGY-level shadow gate folds into effective_dry in Coordinator.multi_account_execute even though the ACCOUNT (ib_paper) is mode:live and notes.is_dry (the account-level flag) is correctly false. So 'dry_run_no_order_placed' is the CORRECT disposition for a shadow-suppressed package; there is no is_dry contradiction. The ONE genuine inconsistency left is cosmetic: the reconciler backfills order_packages.meta.rejected_reason='risk-refused (no fill placed); reconciled from the journalled rejection row' for these shadow-suppressed packages, which is misleading — they were shadow-suppressed, not risk-refused. FIX (Tier-1, cosmetic): have the reconciler label a shadow/dry-suppressed no-fill as such (e.g. 'shadow_suppressed_no_order' / 'dry_run_no_order_placed') rather than the generic 'risk-refused' when the underlying journal row's reason is dry_run/shadow. Downgraded in practical severity — nothing is mis-executing; a reader just needs to know shadow==effective_dry.

items.resolution: Root cause found + fixed (Tier-1 observability — label-only, no order-path behaviour change). TWO independent bugs made trades.entry_reason disagree with notes.is_dry: (1) log_rejection_to_journal HARDCODED is_dry=False for every rejection row, so even a genuine dry/shadow skip (mgc_trend_1h is execution: shadow — demoted live->shadow 2026-06-18) wrote reason='dry_run_no_order_placed' with notes.is_dry=false, a direct contradiction; and (2) execute_pkg forces is_dry=True when exchange_client is None (a LIVE account with the IB gateway wedged) and journaled it with the SAME 'dry_run_no_order_placed' reason — mislabeling a gateway-down infra skip as an intentional dry-run. Fix: log_rejection_to_journal now takes is_dry (writes notes.is_dry; default False, back-compat) and the dry-branch caller passes the honest value + a cause-specific reason: genuine dry/shadow -> 'dry_run_no_order_placed' + is_dry=True; client-unavailable -> new 'exchange_client_unavailable_no_order_placed' + is_dry=False. Both fields now always AGREE. Verified is_dry writes ONLY notes.is_dry — the is_demo/account_class paper-vs-real column is derived separately from account_cfg and is unaffected (new test asserts this). paper_record_classifier _REFUSAL_MARKERS gained 'exchange_client_unavailable' so the new reason still buckets as a refusal. 2 new tests + full execute/coordinator/classifier sweep (451 passed). Shipped on PR #6302 branch.

items.title: Config-only PRs can merge with a RED full test suite — the filtered pytest-run skips the config-assertion tests
items.description: Twice this session, config/docs-heavy PRs (#5850 turtle_soup demote + ib_paper prune; #5851 pull-ibkr-history system-action) merged GREEN via a fast/filtered pytest-run that did NOT execute the full suite, leaving main's full-suite CI RED: test_strategy_execution_gate (turtle_soup now shadow), test_ib_integration x2 (ib_paper strategy list), test_intent_delta_dispatch (turtle_soup-as-live premise), test_system_actions_workflow + test_notify_run (pull-ibkr-history allowlist/priority). The failures were only exposed when the NEXT PR (#5853) touched real code and triggered the full 7192-test run. A config-only change that breaks a config-assertion test should NOT be able to merge green. Likely the pytest-run job path-filters to changed files/affected tests and a config/yaml/workflow change resolves to 'no affected tests'. FIX OPTIONS: (a) always run the full suite on changes to config/**, .github/workflows/**, docs that back tests; or (b) map config/strategies.yaml + config/accounts.yaml + the workflow allowlist to their assertion tests in the affected-test selector; or (c) a nightly full-suite run on main that alarms on red. All 5+ tests were fixed in #5853, so main is green now — this backlog item is about the PROCESS gap that let it go red.
items.trigger_condition: Next CI/tooling pass, or when a config PR merges green but a later PR's full suite goes red.
items.resolution_criteria: A config-only PR that breaks a config-assertion test is caught before merge (full-suite-on-config-paths, an affected-test mapping, or a main nightly full run).

updates.note: Re-validated 2026-07-19: still valid — config-only PRs can merge with a red full suite (filtered pytest skips config-assertion tests). Blocker: Tier-1 CI fix.

Not re-checked this window; no config-only PR in this window's audit set was observed merging on a red full suite (the 46 PRs audited this window all show green-CI test-plan checkboxes in their bodies, though full-suite state itself wasn't independently queried).
Re-validated 07-26: infra/VM-side item needing a VM write or dedicated ops session; condition not observed to regress this window. Carried.

RESOLVED — extended the pytest-run 'relevant changed files' matcher to include `^config/` and `^\.github/workflows/`, so a config-only or workflow-only PR now RUNS the full suite instead of short-circuiting past it and merging green while main's full CI is red. The incident PRs (#5850 config demote breaking test_strategy_execution_gate; #5851 system-action breaking test_system_actions_workflow) would now be caught pre-merge. Verified: pytest-run.yml valid YAML. (CI-minutes cost: config/workflow-only PRs now pay one full suite run — correctness over minutes for test-asserted paths.)

items.title: ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (bot-caused, not broker-side): a mass reconciler false-close on 2026-07-07T14:15:56Z hid ~$218k of still-open, uncapped concurrent notional exposure on alpaca_paper — see BL-20260707-RECONCILER-MASS-FALSE-CLOSE for the mechanism
items.description: Investigated a 'ALL accounts failed to dispatch' alert (spy_pullback_1h/SPY, alpaca_paper + alpaca_live). alpaca_live's risk_refused was plain underfunding — not a bug. alpaca_paper's zero_balance (shared Alpaca paper login with alpaca_options_paper, both ~-$67,946) took several rounds to trace because the trades journal's own pnl was actively misleading (see below). FINAL MECHANISM, confirmed via a fresh diag pull at 2026-07-07T16:19-16:28Z, minutes after it happened: at 2026-07-07T14:15:56.749880Z, `position_snapshot_reconciler` closed MULTIPLE alpaca_paper positions across DIFFERENT symbols simultaneously (same closed_at timestamp on trades 3131 SPY 125sh, 3077 SPY 142sh — wait, distinct order_package_ids but same closed_at batch also covers 3060 SLV 1360sh, 2868 GLD 33.6sh, 2774 TLT 231sh, and more), each stamped `pnl_source: local_compute` / `exit_price_source: local_markprice` (a FABRICATED mark-to-market, not a real fill) — almost certainly because the reconciler's exchange-positions read came back empty/misread at that moment and it concluded every open position was flat (the same failure class as the historical 'AlpacaClient.positions() returning [] instead of None on a read failure' bug this repo has hardened against elsewhere, e.g. RECONCILER_SNAPSHOT_MIN_FILL_AGE_S). The individual fabricated PnLs looked small/benign (+$805, -$441, +$1706, -$434, -$176, etc.) — which is why an earlier pass through this backlog entry incorrectly concluded the journal 'didn't show a loss anywhere near -$67,946' and pointed the operator at Alpaca's own activity screen instead. ~2 hours later, at 2026-07-07T16:19:38-45Z, the REVERSE reconciler discovered the SAME positions were STILL genuinely open on the broker (they never actually closed) and re-adopted all of them fresh as `adopted_orphan` rows: SPY 125sh (~$92.6k), SLV 1360sh (~$73.5k), TLT 10sh, QQQ 16sh (~$11.9k), IWM 9sh (~$2.7k), IEF 8sh (~$753) — all simultaneously open on the SAME $100k paper account, ~$180k+ of concurrent notional exposure stacked across independently-sized strategies (spy_pullback_1h, slv_trend_1h, qqq_pullback_1h, iwm_trend_long_1d, ief_pullback_1d, tlt_pullback_1d/1h), each individually risk-bounded at trade-open time but with NO portfolio-level aggregate cap across strategies on one account. THIS is genuinely bot-caused: (1) the reconciler bug corrupted the journal's view of reality (false closes with fabricated PnL), which is why searching the journal for 'the loss' kept coming up empty; (2) the real financial exposure was always sitting on the broker the whole time, continuously, as an uncapped multi-strategy stack — exactly the mechanism BL-20260707-ALPACA-PULLBACK-NOTIONAL-SIZING flagged for a single trade, but worse in aggregate across concurrently-open positions. The operator's report that 'the old account reset itself to $100k' does NOT match this diag pull (accounts/balances as_of 2026-07-07T16:01Z still reads -$67,945.12 for both alpaca_paper and alpaca_options_paper) — worth the operator double-checking which account/view showed the reset (possibly the NEW dedicated alpaca_options_paper account, which would legitimately start at $100k when first created).
items.trigger_condition: Next /health-review or /system-review; also whenever alpaca_paper/alpaca_options_paper dispatch is checked.
items.resolution_criteria: Fix BL-20260707-RECONCILER-MASS-FALSE-CLOSE (the reconciler defect) and BL-20260707-ALPACA-PULLBACK-NOTIONAL-SIZING (the per-trade + portfolio-level sizing gap) so this class of incident can't recur; separately the shared Alpaca paper login's equity needs an operator-side reset via the Alpaca paper dashboard (Claude has no Alpaca dashboard access) once the currently-open positions are accounted for. The dedicated alpaca_options_paper login (PR #5879 part B, placeholder secrets ALPACA_API_KEY_ID_OPTIONS / ALPACA_API_SECRET_KEY_OPTIONS) fixes the SHARED-BLOCKING symptom but not this root cause.

items.resolution_note: RESOLVED by RISK-1 (full-system-audit 2026-07-09). The reconciler false-close CLASS is fixed structurally: positive per-symbol confirmation (AlpacaClient.position_present 404=flat/2xx=open/err=None + clients.account_position_present/supports_position_presence, alpaca-only capability gate) so a partial/stale snapshot can no longer false-close a still-open position, plus alert-first reset (a wholesale vanish is never mass-closed on inference — one latched alert, rows left OPEN). PR #6056 (squash c6694e8) operator-approved + merged + deployed (#6061, /api/diag/version git_sha c6694e8d); live-verified: trader ticks clean, zero spurious closes. 19 in-file + 169 cross-suite tests.

items.title: position_snapshot_reconciler mass-closed multiple alpaca_paper positions simultaneously with fabricated local-mark PnL, then the reverse reconciler re-adopted them ~2h later still genuinely open on the broker — the positions never actually closed
items.description: At 2026-07-07T14:15:56.749880Z, `position_snapshot_reconciler` closed several alpaca_paper trades across different symbols in the same batch (confirmed same `closed_at` timestamp on at least SPY id 3131 (125sh, pnl local-computed +$805.63), SLV id 3060 (1360sh, +$1706.80), GLD id 2868 (33.6sh, -$434.53), TLT id 2774 (231sh, -$176.77) — likely more not yet enumerated), each with `notes.pnl_source: local_compute` + `exit_price_source: local_markprice` (the '(symbol, side) confirmed absent from the exchange open-positions snapshot across two observations' closed_reason). At 2026-07-07T16:19:38-45Z (~2h5m later), the REVERSE reconciler (`_reconcile_orphan_exchange_positions`) found the exchange reporting the SAME symbols still open with matching or near-matching entry prices/sizes and re-adopted them fresh as `adopted_orphan` rows (SPY 125sh @740.67, SLV 1360sh @54.043, TLT 10sh @85.54, QQQ 16sh @720.63, IWM 9sh @298.53, IEF 8sh @94.14) — i.e. the positions were open continuously the whole time; the 14:15:56 batch-close was WRONG. Hypothesis (not yet confirmed against logs — needs journalctl/audit around 14:15:56Z): the exchange-positions read that fed the close-confirm at that tick returned an empty/degraded snapshot (Alpaca API blip, rate limit, or a client.positions() read failure that returned [] instead of None — the exact failure class RECONCILER_SNAPSHOT_MIN_FILL_AGE_S and the AlpacaClient/OandaClient None-on-failure hardening were built to prevent, but evidently a gap remains for `position_snapshot_reconciler`'s specific close-confirm path, distinct from the reverse reconciler's orphan-adopt path those fixes covered). CONSEQUENCE: the fabricated small per-trade PnLs from the false-close made the trades journal actively misleading during the -$67,946 root-cause investigation (BL-20260707-ALPACA-PAPER-NEGATIVE-EQUITY) — every individual number looked benign while the REAL uncapped multi-position notional exposure sat unaccounted-for on the broker the whole time. FIX (Tier-2, order_monitor.py / position_snapshot_reconciler close-confirm path — needs investigation before a specific patch is proposed): (1) find and harden whatever exchange-positions call feeds this reconciler's close-confirm for Alpaca (does it correctly distinguish 'read failed' from 'genuinely flat', matching the pattern already fixed for AlpacaClient.positions()/account_open_positions elsewhere?); (2) consider whether the 2-observation confirm this path already claims to require was actually satisfied, or whether a single degraded read slipped through; (3) audit `runtime_logs/signal_audit.jsonl` / journalctl around 2026-07-07T14:10-14:20Z for the actual read that triggered this to confirm the failure mode before patching blind.
items.trigger_condition: Next /health-review or /system-review; investigate before any real-money account routes through the same close-confirm path (alpaca_live currently has only 1 tiny position, low exposure, but this is a correctness bug that would apply there too).
items.resolution_criteria: Root cause of the 14:15:56Z false-close batch is confirmed from logs (not just inferred from journal state) and a fix lands so the close-confirm path can't mass-close genuinely-open positions on a degraded/empty exchange read. Regression test: a simulated empty/failed positions() read during the close-confirm path must NOT close an open trade.

updates.note: Root cause found by static analysis of src/units/accounts/clients.py::account_open_positions (the single function position_snapshot_reconciler calls for its exchange-truth read), not from logs — journalctl around 14:15:56Z was repeatedly requested via the diag relay but the issue-comment reply is capped at ~55KB and the trader logs too verbosely per tick to fit a usable window; log-level confirmation was not achieved despite 3+ attempts with progressively narrower windows. The code-level bug is nonetheless conclusive: the Alpaca branch's empty-snapshot verification used `if not bal:` to decide whether client.balance() proved the account genuinely reachable before trusting an empty positions() read as flat. A negative float is TRUTHY in Python, so alpaca_paper's ~-$67,946 balance sailed straight through as 'verified live' and the empty read was trusted as [] (flat) — exactly the mechanism this entry hypothesized. FIX LANDED (not yet pushed/deployed): commit bf0c0fe on branch claude/spy-dispatch-failures-ir2ktj changes the guard to `bal is None` (correctly means 'read failed') plus a new explicit `bal < 0` check (anomalous account state — don't trust the empty read even though it's a successful call) — both now return None (skip, no false-close) instead of falling through to return [] (flat). `bal == 0.0` now correctly returns [] where it previously also incorrectly returned None under the old truthiness bug — an intentional, low-risk behavior change (a genuinely-zero-balance account is separately blocked from new orders by the zero_balance gate). Regression tests added in tests/test_accounts_clients_open_positions.py: test_alpaca_empty_balance_negative_returns_none, test_alpaca_empty_balance_zero_returns_flat. Full suite green (20/20 in that file; 218 passed across the broader reconciler test set). Status stays 'open' until this is pushed, PR'd, merged, deployed to the live VM, and verified live.

Deployed and live-verified. PR #5901 merged (squash sha 0297fff) with operator OK in chat. `ict-git-sync` auto-deploy confirmed via `/api/diag/version`: live VM git_sha advanced from b7fcc87f (pre-merge) to 3a41031b (post-merge, includes 0297fff in ancestry, both trader + web-api services active) within ~10 minutes of merge. Closing resolved — the code-level defect is fixed and running; genuinely-open Alpaca positions can no longer be mass-closed on a negative-or-unreadable-balance empty-snapshot read. Note: while investigating a follow-on alert (QQQ close failing with 'insufficient qty available'), confirmed via a fresh /api/diag/exchange_positions pull that alpaca_paper's positions (QQQ, SPY, IWM, IEF, TLT, USO) were never actually flat/reset — they're still genuinely open on the broker, consistent with this fix's diagnosis. A separate, unrelated bug was found in the active-close path (AlpacaClient.close() doesn't cancel resting bracket legs before flattening) — tracked as a new task, not this backlog item.

items.title: spy_pullback_1h / qqq_pullback_1h (etc.) on Alpaca can size a single trade's NOTIONAL to ~100% of account equity because a thin stop-distance-to-price ratio is divided into the risk budget with no independent leverage/notional cap
items.description: While investigating BL-20260707-ALPACA-PAPER-NEGATIVE-EQUITY, found alpaca_paper trades id 3077 (142 shares SPY, ~$105,700 notional) and id 3131 (125 shares SPY, ~$92,600 notional) — both from spy_pullback_1h, both DOLLAR-RISK-BOUNDED to ~1.5% of equity at the stop (RiskManager.position_size correctly computed qty = risk_budget / (entry-stop)), but because the 1h pullback stop sits only ~0.6-0.8% away from entry on an expensive instrument (SPY ~$740-750/share), the resulting SHARE COUNT and therefore NOTIONAL is enormous relative to equity (~90-105% of the ~$100k paper account on ONE trade). position_size's only ceiling on this is the margin/buying-power cap (`available_usd * effective_leverage * _MARGIN_SAFETY_BUFFER`), which is large enough on a healthy account to permit it. Dollar-risk-at-the-tracked-stop is correctly bounded, but real-world execution risk (slippage on a 100+ share market order, a fast move that gaps through the stop, or the stop-loss leg not actually resting on the broker as assumed) scales with NOTIONAL, not with the intended risk budget — so a nominally-1.5%-risk trade can realize a loss far larger than 1.5% if the stop doesn't execute cleanly. This is a plausible contributing mechanism to how the shared alpaca_paper/alpaca_options_paper login could have gone deeply negative, though it was NOT confirmed as the literal explanation for the -$67,946 figure (see BL-20260707-ALPACA-PAPER-NEGATIVE-EQUITY — the specific trades checked netted near-breakeven; the real loss is earlier in Alpaca's history). PROPOSED FIX (Tier-3, src/units/accounts/risk.py::position_size — order-sizing path, needs operator approval before any change): add an independent max-notional-as-fraction-of-equity clamp (e.g. a `max_position_notional_pct` risk-config knob, applied after the existing risk-budget and margin-cap sizing, floor-rounded like the existing whole-unit clamp) so a thin-stop instrument can never commit near-100% of equity to one position regardless of how the risk-budget/stop-distance division works out. Applies to any account/strategy combination with a tight stop on an expensive instrument, not just alpaca_paper/spy_pullback_1h — worth an account_compat_matrix-style check across the other *_pullback_1h cells (qqq/gld/slv/tlt) once a fix direction is agreed.

Size is bounded only by the risk budget, the daily-loss budget, the margin/buying-power ceiling, and the exchange's lot size.' items.title: AlpacaClient.close() rejected with "insufficient qty available for order" because it never cancels the position's resting bracket SL/TP leg before flattening
items.description: Discovered while investigating a live '🛑 Position CLOSE failing' alert for QQQ/alpaca_paper (12 consecutive close failures, error 'insufficient qty available for order (requested: 16, available: 0)'). A fresh broker-truth pull (`/api/diag/exchange_positions`) confirmed QQQ (and SPY/IWM/IEF/TLT/USO) are genuinely open on the broker — this is NOT another instance of BL-20260707-RECONCILER-MASS-FALSE-CLOSE, it's a different bug in the ACTIVE-CLOSE path. Alpaca's exact error phrasing (`available: 0` while `existing_qty` matches the full position) is the documented signature of shares already `held_for_orders` by another resting order. Every Alpaca position here was opened as a bracket order (entry + SL + TP legs placed atomically, per AlpacaClient.place()'s docstring), so the original protective stop leg is still resting on the broker holding the full qty. `AlpacaClient.close()` (src/units/accounts/alpaca_client.py) just issued `DELETE /v2/positions/{symbol}` with no cancel-first step, unlike `IBClient.close()` (which explicitly cancels resting protective legs before the opposing order) and `AlpacaClient.place_protective()` (which already calls the same `_cancel_open_orders_for_symbol()` helper before re-arming, to avoid OCO stacking). Since nothing ever cancelled the stale leg, the close retried the identical failing DELETE every monitor tick indefinitely, leaving the DB row permanently open. FIX: `close()` now calls `self._cancel_open_orders_for_symbol(symbol)` before the flatten DELETE, mirroring the IB contract and reusing the helper `place_protective` already relies on. Regression tests added in tests/test_alpaca_wiring.py (`test_client_close_cancels_resting_orders_first`, `test_client_close_no_resting_orders_is_single_call`) pin that cancels happen, target the right order ids, and happen BEFORE the flatten call; existing `test_client_close_idempotent_on_404` still passes unchanged. This is a real-money order-path fix — `close_open_position` → `AlpacaClient.close()` is shared by alpaca_paper AND alpaca_live.
