items.title: AlpacaClient.close() treated Alpaca's HTTP-accept as a confirmed flatten — a close accepted right after market close never actually filled, fabricating a phantom-closed row with a made-up PnL, then re-adopted 7 minutes later as a fresh orphan; the re-adopt guard had zero protection for this because it only matched setup_type='adopted_orphan'
items.description: Live incident: `_close_unattributable_orphan` (exit_coverage_resolver) closed an orphaned SLV short (1360sh @ $53.94) at 2026-07-07T20:33:45Z (4:33pm ET, just after the US equity close). `AlpacaClient.close()`'s DELETE /v2/positions/SLV returned HTTP 200 (accepted); the code treated that as confirmed-flat, fabricated a local mark-to-market PnL (-$693.60, pnl_source=local_compute), and marked the trade row closed. The position never actually flattened on the broker. 7 minutes later the reverse reconciler found SLV still fully open (same 1360sh, same $53.94 entry) and bare-adopted it as a brand-new orphan trade row — TWO DB rows now exist for the SAME broker position, the phantom-closed one carrying a fabricated realized PnL that is never corrected. Root cause: `close_open_position`'s Alpaca branch (src/units/accounts/execute.py) and AlpacaClient.close() had no fill-confirmation step, unlike IBClient.close()'s IB_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S contract (poll the live position, require it to actually reach flat within a bounded window before declaring success). Compounding factor: the just-shipped resting-order-cancel fix (BL-20260707-ALPACA-CLOSE-RESTING-ORDER-BLOCK, PR #5918) cancels the protective bracket BEFORE the flatten attempt, so a phantom-closed position is genuinely NAKED on the broker for the entire gap — and invisible to `_check_naked_positions` (which only scans status='open' rows), so there was zero monitoring or alerting on the exposure window either. Separately, the re-adopt flap guard (RECONCILER_READOPT_GUARD_SECONDS, BL-20260618-RECONCILE-DUP) only matched rows with setup_type='adopted_orphan' — a phantom-closed STRATEGY-ATTRIBUTED row (still carrying its original strategy's setup_type) fell through with ZERO flap protection, not even the 300s SLV incidentally got via its own setup_type. Full investigation ordered by the operator ('do a full audit of the entire Alpaca pipeline... I don't want to keep fixing one bug just to create another') — four parallel read-only audit agents covered order placement/sizing, position/balance reads, close/flatten paths, and reconciler/re-adopt-guard logic; this entry captures the three findings judged tightly coupled enough to fix together. FIX (all three parts landed in one PR): (1) AlpacaClient.close() now polls positions() after the DELETE, bounded by new ALPACA_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S (default 6.0s, <=0 restores legacy accept-is-success), mirroring IB_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S exactly — and deliberately reuses the exact 'not confirmed flat' retMsg substring order_monitor.py's existing IB-built cooldown/retry/consecutive-failure-alert machinery already keys on generically (by account/symbol/direction, not by exchange), so no other file needed to change for that half. (2) _recently_closed_adopted_orphan (src/runtime/order_monitor.py) widened to also match a row closed via exit_reason IN ('exchange_flat_reconciled', 'exit_coverage_no_strategy') regardless of setup_type — deliberately NOT widened to every close reason (a genuine broker-confirmed close like Bybit's reconciler_filled or a normal sl_cross/tp_cross strategy exit must never suppress a legitimate new position). (3) AlpacaClient.balance()/buying_power() truthiness bugs fixed in the same PR (see BL-20260707-ALPACA-BALANCE-TRUTHINESS below) since they surfaced in the same audit pass and are the same bug shape as the original BL-20260707-RECONCILER-MASS-FALSE-CLOSE fix.

items.title: AlpacaClient.balance()/buying_power() treated a genuine $0 reading the same as 'could not read' — same truthiness bug shape as the already-fixed account_open_positions bug, one layer up
items.description: balance(): `float(acct.get('equity') or acct.get('cash'))` — a real equity=0.0 is falsy, so the code silently substitutes cash instead, even though equity is the more authoritative figure. buying_power(): `if bp > 0: return bp` inside a fallback loop over (regt_buying_power, buying_power, cash) — a genuine regt_buying_power=0.0 (fully invested / no free margin, a real and common account state) is treated identically to an unparseable value and falls through to a LESS authoritative key; if all three read non-positive, the function returns None. Coordinator.multi_account_execute reads a None buying_power() as 'could not determine' and falls back to a MORE PERMISSIVE sizing basis (total_account_usd/balance_usd x leverage) — exactly backwards: the account has genuinely zero free margin and the sizer should be MOST conservative, not fall back to a laxer basis. Verified safe to fix: Coordinator's caller already does `if _bp is not None: available_usd = _bp`, and RiskManager.position_size's margin cap correctly computes max_qty_by_margin=0 when available_usd=0.0, safely refusing the trade rather than erroring.

items.title: Order ENTRY has the same accept-vs-fill confirmation gap as the close side (BL-20260707-ALPACA-CLOSE-NOT-CONFIRMED-FLAT) — a bracket order journals status='open' the instant it's HTTP-accepted, with a fabricated entry price, no fill confirmation
items.description: `_submit_order`'s Alpaca branch (src/units/accounts/execute.py ~line 780) treats any retCode==0 (HTTP 2xx accept) from AlpacaClient.place() as success; execute_pkg then calls `_log_trade_to_journal` synchronously right after, writing status='open' with entry_price=the strategy's DECISION-TIME signal price, not a broker-confirmed fill price — no polling for an actual fill. Lower urgency than the close-side bug fixed today: Alpaca bracket orders are time_in_force:day MARKET orders, which fill almost instantly during RTH, and RECONCILER_SNAPSHOT_MIN_FILL_AGE_S (BL-20260622-ALPACA-SNAPSHOT-FALSECLOSE) already exists specifically as a grace period for a just-placed order that hasn't propagated to the positions() snapshot yet — i.e. the team already knew entries can sit apparently-unfilled for minutes. NOT yet confirmed whether a genuinely NEVER-filled entry (rejected post-accept, or placed outside RTH) converges to a correct state or fabricates a phantom trade with fake entry+exit+PnL for a position that never existed on the broker — this needs tracing before a fix is designed. Deliberately deferred out of today's close-side fix: the entry path is more sensitive (delaying/blocking a live entry has different risk than delaying a close) and deserves its own careful design, not a bolt-on.
items.trigger_condition: Next full-pipeline review, or if a phantom-entry (journaled open, never actually filled) is observed live.
items.resolution_criteria: Trace whether a never-filled Alpaca entry self-heals cleanly today; if not, design + ship an entry-side fill-confirmation step analogous to the close-side fix, sized to the entry path's different risk profile (do not just copy-paste the close-side poll loop without considering it delays a live entry, not a close).

updates.note: Operator directive: 'finish the fix for the entry side as well - I want full pipeline stability.' Fixed the REJECTION half only, deliberately NOT the fill-price half (scoped down from the original description after tracing the actual call path). AlpacaClient.place() (src/units/accounts/alpaca_client.py) now polls the order by id after a successful POST, bounded by new ALPACA_PLACE_CONFIRM_S (default 3.0s, matching IB_PLACE_CONFIRM_S; <=0 restores legacy behaviour): a terminal rejected/canceled/expired status within the window is surfaced as retCode!=0 so _submit_order raises and _log_trade_to_journal never writes a phantom open trade row for an order the broker never actually executed. Still-pending or filled at the deadline is reported as success unchanged. Deliberately did NOT attempt to capture/backfill the broker's real filled_avg_price into the journal: _submit_order's return contract is a bare str (order_id) shared byte-for-byte across bybit/IB/alpaca/oanda; threading a richer fill-price payload through it would be a materially larger, cross-exchange refactor and a separate design decision, not a bug fix — the decision-time entry price is already the documented, accepted convention for every exchange here (IB's own IB_PLACE_CONFIRM_S only checks non-rejection too, never fill price), and RECONCILER_SNAPSHOT_MIN_FILL_AGE_S remains the existing downstream grace period for a genuinely-slow-but-good fill. Tests: test_client_place_confirms_no_rejection_when_filled, test_client_place_detects_post_accept_rejection, test_client_place_still_pending_at_deadline_is_success, test_client_place_confirm_disabled_restores_legacy_behavior (tests/test_alpaca_wiring.py) — 34/34 in that file, 323 across the broader order-management/reconciler surface.

items.title: Minor / lower-priority findings from the full Alpaca-pipeline audit — logged, not blocking
items.description: Bundle of smaller findings from the four-way parallel audit (order placement/sizing, position/balance reads, close/flatten paths, reconciler/re-adopt-guards), none individually urgent enough to block the main close-confirm fix: (1) OandaClient.close() (src/units/accounts/oanda_client.py) has the IDENTICAL accept-is-success defect as the pre-fix Alpaca close — not live-impactful today since oanda_practice is dry-run-only, but will need the same confirm-flat treatment before any OANDA account goes live. (2) No client_order_id / idempotency key on AlpacaClient.place()/place_protective() — a lost HTTP response to a timeout could leave a real accepted broker order un-journaled; low probability today since there's no retry loop in execute.py/coordinator.py to trigger a double-submit, but worth hardening. (3) The naked-position re-arm paths (_rearm_broker_protection_after_recovery, _check_broker_naked_equity_positions in order_monitor.py) size the re-armed OCO from trades.position_size (the journal column) rather than a fresh broker-side qty read — suspected staleness risk, not confirmed as a live bug, needs a follow-up trace of whether position_size reliably stays broker-truth-synced across partial fills/closes. (4) AlpacaClient.place_protective() duplicates whole_unit_qty's rounding logic inline instead of calling the shared helper place() already uses — cosmetic DRY violation, functionally identical today but a latent drift risk if the rounding rule ever changes. (5) _PENDING_ORPHAN_NOSTRAT_CLOSE (order_monitor.py) is never popped on the 'absent' (closed via disappear-confirm) branch, only the 'recoverable' branch — an unbounded but harmless in-process dict leak (trade ids are never reused). (6) _recover_orphan_order_package searches order packages of ANY status (not just open) for a symbol/direction/entry-price(+-2%) match — theoretical risk of resurrecting an already-closed, unrelated order package on a coincidental price match; not observed live, worth a defensive exclusion (e.g. skip packages whose linked trade closed via exit_coverage_no_strategy/exchange_flat_reconciled within the readopt-guard window) as a follow-up.

items.title: Alpaca close() still races share-release on a re-arming OCO (QQQ #3269) — needs qty_available-gated flatten, not blind retry
items.description: MECHANISM: the position's protective OCO stop-sell leg (stop 708.38, price hovering ~708.7) reserves all 16 shares as held_for_orders. close() cancels the leg + retries the DELETE within a 6s window, but Alpaca's cancel->qty_available release appears to take longer than 6s AND/OR the naked-autoprotect sweep re-arms a fresh OCO on an intervening monitor tick, so every close attempt re-hits available:0. This is a real close-path bug that could also strand a REAL alpaca_live position on a slow cancel, not just this paper orphan. CORRECT FIX (deterministic, not another blind retry): after the cancel pre-pass, POLL the position's qty_available (raw /v2/positions/{sym} field, add to AlpacaClient.positions() or a helper) until it == qty before issuing the DELETE, with a longer bound; and/or make the close a persistent 'closing' latch that suppresses the naked re-arm for that (account,symbol) until confirmed flat (not just the same-tick guard). NEEDS order/qty-level broker visibility — consider adding /api/diag/exchange_orders?account_id (read-only, mirrors exchange_positions) to SEE what holds the shares before the next attempt. LOW URGENCY: QQQ is alpaca_paper (is_demo, no real capital) — the live cost is the 'won't flatten' banner/Telegram noise, bounded to every-Nth-failure. Deprioritized behind real-money work per operator.

items.source: pairs SOLUSDT/BNBUSDT garbage-order investigation. A live BNBUSDT pairs leg was placed with SL=2x entry / TP=0.5x entry (an exploded/collapsed bracket the venue would reject). Root cause traced to risk_spread ~= 5.4 in LOG-spread units (implausibly large) fed into leg_protective_levels.
items.title: Pairs sleeve: unstable rolling OLS beta on a 15-bar lookback blows up risk_spread -> exploded SL/TP (clamp #6549 band-aids the symptom, not the beta)
items.description: The pairs executor sizes each leg off risk_spread = stop_z * std(log-spread), where the log-spread = log(price_a) - beta*log(price_b) and beta is a rolling OLS hedge ratio. On a SHORT (15-bar) lookback the OLS beta is numerically unstable (a few outlier bars swing it far from 1.0), which inflates the spread std and drives risk_spread to implausible values (~5.4 in log units => a leg backstop of e^5.4 ~ 220x). SYMPTOM FIXED (#6549, src/units/strategies/pairs_sizing.py::leg_protective_levels): the log-move is now clamped to [log(1.02), log(2.0)] so a degenerate risk_spread can never emit an exploded/collapsed bracket the venue rejects — the garbage BNBUSDT order can't recur. The clamp is defensive-in-depth and correct, but it masks rather than fixes the BETA estimation: a clamped-but-wrong risk_spread still mis-sizes the notionals (pair_notionals divides risk_budget by risk_spread), so the sleeve's risk-per-trade is still off when beta is unstable. Pairs is currently execution: shadow on bybit_1 (demoted #6552 after the live-placement break), so this is NOT live-money-at-risk today. REAL FIX (Tier-3, backtest-gated, NOT enacted here): stabilize the hedge-ratio/spread estimation before it reaches sizing — e.g. a longer/robust beta lookback, ridge/Kalman beta, winsorized spread std, or an explicit sanity guard that rejects a pair-tick when |beta| or risk_spread falls outside a plausible band (the honest 'skip this tick' rather than size on garbage). Validate on the pairs backtest harness before re-flipping any pair to live. Cross-ref: pairs SL/TP clamp #6549, pairs shadow demotion #6552, /api/bot/pairs/soak (M22 D2 soak surface).

items.title: /dev/null unwritable on live VM breaks pull_and_deploy git-fetch (deploy-tooling hygiene)
items.description: Root cause to confirm: /dev/null on ict-bot-arm likely got replaced by a regular file or chmod'd off 0666 (crw-rw-rw-). Fix is a privileged one-liner `sudo chmod 666 /dev/null` (or recreate: `sudo rm -f /dev/null && sudo mknod /dev/null c 1 3 && sudo chmod 666 /dev/null`), or a VM reboot (devtmpfs recreates /dev). There is no autonomous arbitrary-command wire to the LIVE VM (system-actions is a fixed allowlist; trainer-vm-diag is trainer-only), so this needs either an operator chmod, a new one-shot labelled workflow that SSHes the chmod (Tier-2), or a reboot-vm system-action (Tier-2). Not urgent while git-sync keeps the code current + the trader is healthy, but it must be fixed before a code deploy that requires a restart-with-fetch and to remove the latent risk to /dev/null-redirecting processes (incl. the liveness watchdog's restart path).

items.title: Alpaca EXIT path had no market-hours awareness — fired doomed market flattens into a closed equity market every tick
items.description: Operator (rightly) pushed back on the endless QQQ 'Position CLOSE failing — won't flatten' alerts. Root cause: is_market_open('us_equity') was wired into ~20 ENTRY signal-builders (they refuse to open when the market is closed) but into NONE of the exit path (order_monitor.py / execute.py / alpaca_client.py had zero market-hours awareness), and every Alpaca order is type:market. US equities cannot fill a market order outside 13:30-20:00 UTC (9:30-16:00 ET), so after the close the monitor kept firing market flattens that can't fill + re-alerting every tick for a position that simply can't be exited until the session (re)opens. FIX (this PR): (1) market_hours.us_equity_session() → 'rth'|'extended'|'closed'; (2) AlpacaClient.close is session-aware — CLOSED: defer (retCode 2, leave the GTC bracket armed, place nothing); EXTENDED: marketable LIMIT + extended_hours=true (ALPACA_EXT_LIMIT_BUFFER_BPS); RTH: the normal market flatten (incl. the cancel_orders=true escalation); (3) order_monitor treats the retCode-2 defer as a quiet no-change (no consecutive-close-failure streak, no 'won't flatten' alarm). Operator (2026-07-17) approved core+extended scope. Tier-2 order-path; also affects alpaca_live when it leaves dry_run.

items.title: btc-regime-5m-lgbm-flow-v1 OOM-thrashes into D-state and wedges the WHOLE trainer ~24h, evading the per-manifest timeout + OOM-kill
items.detail: On 2026-07-19 the trainer was found with run_training_cycle.sh stuck ~24.8h on ml/configs/btc-regime-5m-lgbm-flow-v1.yaml: the training python (working set ~4.2-4.8GB RSS) sat in State D (uninterruptible disk-sleep), 0% CPU, wchan=mem_cgroup_handle_over_high. No manifest trained since Jul 18 01:24 (journal) -> ALL trainer work (other manifests, drift-retrain, any gate-check I tried to run) was blocked for a day; every fc-pcv gate-check 'hang' that night was this process starving the 6GB box. ROOT CAUSE: the flow head's ~4.8GB working set sits in the GAP between the unit's MemoryHigh=3G (soft -> kernel keeps reclaiming, pushing pages to the MemorySwapMax=512M swap and faulting them back = perpetual swap-thrash, D-state) and MemoryMax=5G (hard -> never reached at 4.8G RSS, so the kernel OOM-killer never fires). The existing per-manifest `timeout --kill-after=30s 1800s` in run_training_cycle.sh CANNOT reap it because SIGTERM/SIGKILL do not land on a process in uninterruptible D-state until it leaves the mem-cgroup-over-high reclaim path -> the cycle stays blocked at that manifest and the OOM-quarantine (trainer_manifest_health, BL-20260717) never records a timeout so it never quarantines. Cleared manually via pkill -9 (freed 4.4GB); it re-wedged on the same manifest the next cycle -> recurs every cycle.
items.fix: Operator-domain memory tuning (these caps were deliberately iterated - MemoryHigh 4G->3G, MemorySwapMax 512M - so pick values with care). Options, not-yet-applied: (a) MemorySwapMax=0 on ict-trainer.service + ict-trainer-catchup.service (deny cgroup swap) so an over-MemoryHigh manifest can't swap-thrash in D-state - it runs in RAM (throttled) or hits MemoryMax and OOM-kills cleanly (OOMPolicy=continue + run_training_cycle.sh already handle a killed subprocess); risk: a legit manifest relying on the 512M cushion would OOM-kill instead. (b) Lower MemoryMax below the flow head's ~4.8G peak (e.g. 4G) so it OOM-kills; risk: kills other 4-5G-peak manifests too. (c) Memory-bound the 5m flow head specifically (streaming/subsample its market_features load; the unit comment already flags a 'market_features streaming refactor' as the real peak-RSS fix) or exclude it from the cycle until bounded. (d) Add an external D-state-watchdog: a trainer process in State D at 0% CPU for >N min = wedged -> the watchdog lowers memory pressure (e.g. `systemctl set-property ... MemorySwapMax=0`) or pkills it so the cycle's timeout can then proceed. Recommend (a)+(c). NOT applied autonomously - memory-policy change on the running trainer, operator to choose values.

Once fixed, re-run whatever training/gate-checks were starved (incl. the fc-pcv oos_edge, already done in a manually-cleared window: oos_edge PASS +0.282).

items.title: FALSE ALARM (corrected same day): 'GitHub Actions outage' was actually an unmergeable (dirty) PR — pull_request workflows silently never run when the merge ref cannot be built
items.detail: ORIGINAL (WRONG) diagnosis: pushes/PR events after ~07:30Z produced zero check runs, so a GitHub-side push/pull_request webhook outage was presumed. REAL root cause (operator pushed back — 'no way it's been down 5h' — forcing proper investigation): the PR branch had a MERGE CONFLICT with main (squash-merge of #7042 vs the branch's original commits diverged in ml/promotion/live_parity.py + tests/ml/test_live_parity.py), so mergeable_state was 'dirty'. GitHub builds pull_request-event workflow runs against the MERGE REF; when the merge ref cannot be built, the workflows are silently skipped — zero check runs, indistinguishable at a glance from an Actions outage. Push-event workflows also only trigger on main in this repo, so branch pushes never fire CI regardless. Fixed by merging origin/main into the branch (conflicts resolved); CI fired instantly on the push, all 26 checks green. LESSON (the durable part): before suspecting an Actions outage, check the PR's mergeable_state — 'dirty' means no merge ref, means no pull_request CI; another session's PRs running CI at the same time is the fastest disproof of an outage.

items.title: Netted-position bracket fires close ONLY the newest journal row — older rows go phantom-open, then get mis-resolved with other trades' closed-pnl records / stale mark prices (root-caused; exchange behaved correctly)
items.detail: ROOT-CAUSED 2026-07-20 (forensics: trainer relay #7122 full-notes dump + 1h candles #7118/#7117). SUPERSEDES the earlier 'no effective bracket / stop-enforcement failure' framing — the exchange behaved CORRECTLY throughout. Mechanism: on Bybit one-way mode the netted (multi-strategy) position carries ONE position-level tpsl — each new same-symbol open REPLACES it (execute.py attaches stopLoss/takeProfit on every non-reduce Market order). When that bracket fires (Full mode) the ENTIRE position flattens, but the journal/reconciler closes only the NEWEST trade row; older rows stay phantom-'open'. Jun 21-23 bybit_2 BTCUSDT timeline (all verified): TP fire 06-22 11:37 @64729 (journal closed only 2768; 2765's 0.001 share actually exited HERE at a PROFIT), SL fire 06-22 21:23 @64250 (closed only 2797/2769; 2783's real exit, ~-0.9R), SL fire 06-23 06:21 @62724 (closed only 2798/2799). The phantom rows were later mis-resolved: (a) closed-pnl matcher stamped OTHER trades' broker records byte-identically — 2765<-2799 (-1.63903789/62724.0, REAL MONEY), 2764<-2769 (-3350.54/64255.9), 2796<-2798 (-828.847/62725.0); (b) reconcile_orphan_history (Jun 25 06:14) stamped 2757/2762/2770 with local_markprice 62402.2 (Jun-23+ price). The catastrophic per-trade R reads (-7..-14R) that drove the ict_scalp 'lets losses run' narrative are 100% measurement artifact; real losses were bracket-bounded. TWO REAL DEFECTS: (1) [attribution, Tier-1/2] the reconciler's 'position flat' close must cascade to ALL open journal rows on (account,symbol,direction) at that fire, qty-prorating the closed-pnl record, instead of closing only the row it was checking — and the closed-pnl matcher must refuse/flag a record whose close flattened a position that had >1 open journal row (netted_ambiguous), never stamp it verbatim onto one row. (2) [protection semantics, Tier-3] under Full-mode tpsl the NEWEST trade's bracket governs every strategy's share — older trades ride geometry they never chose. Candidate fix: tpslMode=Partial with qty-scoped brackets per order (needs Bybit API validation), or accept position-level semantics and make the journal model it honestly. Also explains part of BL-20260713-BYBIT2-PNL-UNDERRECORD and generalizes BL-20260720-PAPER-PNL-CROSSWRITE (NOT paper-only: 2765 is real money). Analytics impact: per-trade R for netted bybit windows is unreliable until (1) lands + a historical repair pass re-attributes the Jun 21-23 rows. FIX BUILT + VALIDATED 2026-07-20 (operator-approved Tier-2, PR #7115): (1) order_monitor._cascade_close_netted_siblings closes ALL open same-direction rows at the position-flat verdict with qty-prorated pnl; primary-row proration guard added; 7 new tests + 130 adjacent green. (2) repair-netted-rows system-action (dry-run default, apply-gated) validated on the trainer copy (dry 8/8 #7124, apply-on-copy 8/8 idempotent #7125). RESOLVED 2026-07-20: PR #7115 merged (squash 6937849) + live-deploy verified via /api/diag/version (git_sha 69378490, trader restarted, ict_scalp_5m loaded). repair-netted-rows dispatched on the LIVE DB: dry-run #7139 matched all 8 signatures, apply #7141 repaired 8/8 (honest-null pnl/exit, provenance under notes.netted_repair). Fix 2 venue validation PASSED on demo (#7159, after 4 iterations: #7142 wrapper creds -> #7143; #7145 BTCUSDT contamination -> #7147 isolated flat LTCUSDT; #7152 5-USDT min order value -> #7154; #7156 proved position tpslMode is a display-level field that reads Full even with set_tp_sl_mode OK and all legs Partial-type -> #7157 asserts the functional leg-type invariant): both bracket pairs coexist as qty-scoped Partial-type legs, zero Full legs, qty-scoped amend preserves the sibling. ONLY REMAINING: the Tier-3 set-env BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=partial flip on the live VM — operator decision, presented with the PASS evidence + the honest caveat that an actual partial-leg FIRE has not been observed on-venue (deterministic immediate triggers are not constructible; the M20 first-decision health check watches the first live fire).

items.title: Merge-serialization protocol lapsed under load: 3 claim-less merges raced 'behind' 3x in one day while claimed merges raced 0x — the protocol needs per-merge framing + a mechanical nudge
items.detail: 2026-07-20 (operator flagged it: 'are we using the merge queue and message board correctly? we added those specifically to prevent this'). Self-audit of board #6927: on 07-19 every merge by this session carried MERGE SLOT CLAIM/RELEASE comments and zero races occurred. On 07-20 the same session merged/attempted #7082, #7155, #7167 WITHOUT claiming first and hit mergeable_state 'behind' THREE times (each costing a branch refresh + a full ~10-min CI rerun + a squash-vs-original conflict in one case); the two merges where a claim WAS posted (reactively) merged cleanly first try. Root causes: (1) the claim step lives in session memory, and under time pressure (racing an approved promotion chain) it was skipped exactly when the repo was busiest; (2) the session also did not READ the board before merging, so even a counterpart's claim would have been missed; (3) docs/claude/session-board.json (the merge-queue file) went untouched all day — the two mechanisms (file queue + live board) have drifted, with the 07-19 note declaring the live board 'the real-time signal', leaving the file's role unclear. PROPOSED FIXES for a review session: (a) reword session-coordination SKILL.md + the SessionStart clause-0 text to frame the claim as a PER-MERGE precondition ('before every merge_pull_request call: read board tail, post CLAIM, merge, post RELEASE'), not a session-start ritual; (b) clarify or retire session-board.json's merge_slot in favor of the board comments (one source of truth); (c) optional mechanical nudge: a tiny helper script sessions are told to run (checks the newest CLAIM/RELEASE comment pair and refuses to proceed on someone else's open claim) — cheap, no branch-protection change. Evidence: board comments 5026296972 (reactive claim #7167), 5025958114 (reactive claim #7155), merge failures at 16:11Z/18:52Z/19:11Z-19:19Z in the session log.

updates.note: Proposed fixes (skill-doc reword, session-board.json clarification, mechanical-nudge helper) not shipped this window. No merges were performed by this review session (health-review makes no code changes needing a merge), so no fresh evidence either way on protocol adherence.
Re-validated 07-26: infra/VM-side item needing a VM write or dedicated ops session; condition not observed to regress this window. Carried.

Shipped proposed fixes (a)+(b): reworded session-coordination/SKILL.md § 2 to frame the merge claim as a PER-MERGE precondition on the merge_pull_request call ('read board tail -> post 🔒 MERGE SLOT CLAIM comment -> sync -> merge on green -> 🔓 RELEASE'), not a session-start ritual, and made the LIVE BOARD COMMENT (#6927) the authoritative claim with session-board.json::merge_slot demoted to a durable mirror (one source of truth) — updated the two-surfaces preamble, § 2 steps, the session-board.json _doc + merge_slot schema, and coordination-board.md's 'complements not replaces' bullet to match. Fix (c) (a mechanical nudge helper script) intentionally deferred as optional — the reframe + one-source-of-truth addresses root causes (1)+(2)+(3) without new tooling; re-log if the lapse recurs after the reword.

items.title: trainer-vm-diag cmd extractor executes markdown-fenced bodies via backtick command substitution
items.detail: A trainer-vm-diag-request issue whose cmd: block is wrapped in markdown ``` fences is passed to bash WITH the backticks intact — triple-backtick acts as nested command substitution, so the request half-executes and stray output is itself executed as a command (issues #7208/#7209: pgrep's PID line ran as a command, '275311: command not found'). The documented `cmd: |` YAML-block form works (#7211). Fix: in .github/workflows/trainer-vm-diag.yml's extractor, strip leading/trailing ``` fence lines from cmd_raw (the vm-diag-snapshot relay may share the pattern — check both), or reject fenced bodies with a loud comment instead of executing them mangled. Repro: any fenced cmd body.

updates.note: Fix (strip/reject markdown fences in the cmd extractor) not shipped this window; this session's own trainer-vm-diag dispatch used a clean `cmd: |` block (no fences), so it did not hit the bug, but the extractor is unchanged.
Re-validated 07-26: infra/VM-side item needing a VM write or dedicated ops session; condition not observed to regress this window. Carried.

RESOLVED — the trainer-vm-diag.yml cmd extractor now strips markdown code-fence lines (```/```lang) from the cmd body via a `found && /^[[:space:]]*```/{ next }` awk rule, so a fenced cmd body no longer leaks the fence into bash (an un-stripped ```bash line ran as command ``` + backticks got command-substituted). Verified: valid YAML.

items.title: RESOLVED: pytest-run CI test_skip_when_dataset_and_manifest_predate_last_run — real glob-order bug in dataset_unchanged_check.py, not test flakiness
items.detail: CI run https://github.com/benbaichmankass/ict-trading-bot/actions/runs/29948446729/job/89019758539 (PR #7381, a docs/backlog/report-only /system-review PR) failed this ONE test out of 7976 passed/8 skipped: assert duc.decide(...) == 'SKIP' got 'TRAIN'. The test sets a manifest+dataset mtime to 1 day old (_set_old default 86400s) and a registry run_at 0.5 days old (12h) -- a 12h margin that should not be flaky by itself. Confirmed NOT caused by this PR: scripts/ops/dataset_unchanged_check.py and tests/ops/test_dataset_unchanged_check.py are both unchanged since PR #7082 (well before this branch's merge-base 2a21ed5), and running just this test file in isolation (pytest tests/ops/test_dataset_unchanged_check.py -k test_skip_when_dataset_and_manifest_predate_last_run) PASSES cleanly. This strongly suggests an order-dependent interaction with another test earlier in the ~8000-test full-suite run (e.g. a time.time()/os.utime patch or monkeypatch that leaks past its own test's teardown) -- the same class of issue the pytest-run workflow's own comments cite as the 2026-05-28 time-bomb-test incident. Needs a full local repro of the full test suite (matching CI exactly, ~6-7 min) with a bisection pass to find the offending earlier test, then either fix its teardown or make this test's time reference injectable/mockable so it can't be perturbed by global state. ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED same session: scripts/ops/dataset_unchanged_check.py::decide() called d.get("model_id") on every glob-matched registry JSON file OUTSIDE the try/except that only guarded json.load() -- the test fixture's own "not-an-entry.json" sibling artifact (a JSON list, not a dict) crashes that .get() call with AttributeError when glob.glob() happens to enumerate it before the real dict entry (glob order is filesystem-dependent, not sorted). The AttributeError propagated to the function-level fail-open (except Exception: return "TRAIN"), silently flipping the expected SKIP to TRAIN. Confirmed by forcing both glob orderings locally with a monkeypatch -- reproduces 100% of the time when the non-dict sibling glob-sorts first, regardless of environment. Fixed with a one-line isinstance(d, dict) guard (commit pending on PR #7381) + a new regression test (test_skip_regardless_of_glob_order_with_non_dict_sibling) that forces both orderings explicitly so it can never again depend on ambient filesystem behavior. Not a flake, not order-dependent test pollution from another test -- a real latent bug in production code that happened to only manifest under GitHub Actions runner's particular directory-entry order. (Cross-reference: an independent concurrent session, ml-strategies-workplan-nm3xnx, also hit this exact bug on PR #7379 and logged it as BL-20260722-DATASET-UNCHANGED-CHECK-FLAKE, now marked resolved pointing back here.)
items.source: PR #7381 CI failure, investigated inline by the /system-review master session
items.recommended_action: Done -- fixed + regression-tested in the same PR that surfaced it.

items.title: CI flake: test_skip_when_dataset_and_manifest_predate_last_run fail-opens to TRAIN
items.detail: tests/ops/test_dataset_unchanged_check.py::TestDecide::test_skip_when_dataset_and_manifest_predate_last_run intermittently fails 'assert TRAIN == SKIP' in CI (seen on PR #7379 run 29948106302, HeadSHA c0235198). The setup is deterministic (dataset/manifest mtime 24h old vs registry run_at 12h old, a 12h margin) and reproduces as SKIP locally, so the TRAIN can only come from decide()'s bare-except fail-open (scripts/ops/dataset_unchanged_check.py:77) — i.e. TrainingManifest.from_yaml/path_under raised in CI. The fail-open MASKS the real intermittent exception. Diagnose: replace the bare-except with logging of the exception type, or harden the test to assert no fail-open occurred (distinguish real SKIP from fail-open TRAIN). Not dangerous in prod (fail-open TRAIN = one unnecessary retrain) but it flakes CI and hides an intermittent manifest-load error. Introduced with MB-20260720-FCPCV-RETRAIN-NOOP.
items.source: observed by ml-strategies-workplan session while landing an unrelated WS-B PR (#7379); re-triggered CI to unblock

Fixed with an isinstance(d, dict) guard + a regression test that forces both glob orderings explicitly (PR #7381, commit 682efda). See BL-20260722-PYTESTRUN-DATASETCHECK-FLAKE for the full writeup.

items.opened_by: claude (session continuing /system-review 2026-07-22, investigating operator-reported XRPUSDT trade 3577 SL-notification-spam + stale-dashboard report)
items.source: Root-cause investigation of the operator XRP report: diag pull of order_packages showed pkg-395c72c733074358 (linked trade 3577, xrp_pullback_2h, bybit_2 real money) had sl=1.1116 vs trades.stop_loss=1.0655 (the original entry-time stop), with order_packages.updated_at essentially continuous (stamped within the same minute as the diag query, 5 days after entry). Traced the mechanism: htf_pullback_trend_2h.py::monitor() (and trend_donchian.py::monitor, which claims an identical contract) computes current_price = candles_df['close'].iloc[-1] and ext = window['high'].max() off whatever candles_df the ohlcv_fetcher returns; src/runtime/market_data.py::fetch_candles never drops the exchange-returned forming/incomplete final candle. On Bybit, fetch_ohlcv's last row is the live, continuously-updating current-period candle, so current_price/ext (and therefore the ATR trail candidate = ext - trail_mult*atr) update on every tick a live price makes even a fractional new high, not just on bar close. Each such tick that clears 'candidate > sl' triggers order_monitor.py's modify branch: an exchange amend call + (pre-fix) an unconditional Telegram ping, producing the observed near-continuous stream of SL moves the operator correctly perceived as noise (the SL LOOKED static because none of these micro-moves were individually meaningful).
items.title: [order-monitor][strategy] Pullback-family trail (htf_pullback_trend_2h / trend_donchian monitor()) reacts to the live/forming candle instead of closed-bar-only, causing far more exchange SL amends than intended — proposed Tier-2 fix, needs operator sign-off
items.description: Mitigated (shipped, Tier-1/2, no order-path behavior change) this session: order_monitor.py's modify branch now drops any sl/tp key whose new value is not >0.05% different from the package's current value BEFORE any exchange call, DB write, or notification (_MEANINGFUL_MODIFY_REL_TOL gate) — this kills the notification spam and the pure float-noise exchange amends. trades.stop_loss/take_profit_1 are now also synced on every successful modify so the dashboard/API no longer goes stale after the first trail move (both landed together, tests added: test_modify_skips_immaterial_change_no_exchange_call_no_db_write, test_modify_still_fires_on_meaningful_change, test_modify_syncs_trades_stop_loss_after_success in tests/test_s030_pr4_exchange_modify_close.py). Also fixed in the same pass: _fire_trade_opened_event / _fire_trade_updated_event in database.py SELECTed qty/sl/tp — none of which exist on trades (real columns: position_size/stop_loss/take_profit_1) — so TRADE_OPENED push notifications have silently never fired (swallowed by insert_trade's bare except); fixed to use the real column names. NOT fixed (deeper root cause, proposed only): the trail computation itself should arguably use only CLOSED bars (drop candles_df's last row when it is the forming candle) so the trail advances once per bar close like the strategy's own trail_decay_arm_r/trail_decay_tight_mult meta fields imply it was designed to, rather than continuously intrabar. This changes real order-routing cadence (fewer, larger, discrete SL amends instead of many tiny ones) for every strategy sharing this monitor() shape, not just xrp_pullback_2h — meaningful blast radius (any donchian/pullback-family leg). Proposed exact change: in fetch_candles or the ohlcv_fetcher closure in src/main.py::_build_monitor_ohlcv_fetcher, drop the last row when its timestamp indicates the bar has not yet closed (bar_start + timeframe_seconds > now), mirroring the 'closed bars only' principle already codified for ML scorers this session (docs/research/RESEARCH-RIGOR-STANDARD.md). Also worth checking whether _send_modify_to_exchange rate-limits/dedupes on its own — if Bybit's API is still being hit at a materially reduced but still-elevated cadence post-gate, that's worth knowing before deciding whether the closed-bar fix is urgent or can wait. NOT YET INVESTIGATED this session: the operator's separately-reported 'partial close' bookkeeping question on trade 3577 (does a partial close correctly reduce position_size in place, or should it produce a second row?) — flagged for a follow-up, not fabricated an answer to here.

items.source: While standing up the M0a import-linter layer guard I initially reported to the operator (Telegram ping #7456 + chat) that src/units/strategies/vwap.py and src/units/strategies/_base.py 'import execution (strategy-purity violations)'. On verification BOTH direct-import claims were FALSE POSITIVES from a naive grep: vwap.py:976 is a docstring comment that merely NAMES order_monitor.py (not an import), and _base.py:48 is `from src.core.order_contract import OrderPackage` inside an `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block (a type-only import of the CONTRACT type, erased at runtime, and order_contract is the contract seam not Execution). Corrected with the operator. However an authoritative import-linter check (temp forbidden contract on src.units.strategies.vwap vs {units.accounts.risk, units.accounts.execute, exchange}) surfaced a REAL TRANSITIVE coupling: src.units.strategies.vwap -> src.units.db.database (vwap.py:679) -> src.runtime.local_pnl (database.py:841) -> {src.units.accounts.risk (local_pnl.py:151) -> src.core.coordinator -> src.units.accounts.execute; and src.runtime.market_data -> src.exchange.ib_connector/oanda_connector}. The load-bearing seam is database.py:841 importing runtime.local_pnl — that single edge is what drags the entire persistence layer (and therefore every strategy that persists) up into Execution.
items.title: [architecture][M0b] units.db.database imports runtime.local_pnl (database.py:841), transitively coupling the DB/persistence layer — and every strategy that touches it (e.g. vwap) — up into Execution (risk/coordinator/execute + exchange connectors). Correction of an earlier false-positive 'vwap/_base import execution' report: the direct imports were a comment + a TYPE_CHECKING contract import; the real issue is this transitive DB-layer edge.
items.description: Genuine layer-boundary finding for the M0b incremental-drain migration (ROADMAP_MACRO.md §1). ROOT EDGE: src/units/db/database.py line ~841 does `from src.runtime.local_pnl import ...` (a PnL compute helper). runtime.local_pnl in turn imports units.accounts.risk (→ core.coordinator → units.accounts.execute) and runtime.market_data (→ exchange.*_connector). So the persistence layer, which strategies legitimately need for reads, is not itself layer-clean — it reaches into Execution. CONSEQUENCE: no strategy module that imports units.db.database can be added to the import-linter forbidden-vs-Execution contracts yet (vwap, and any strategy sharing that persistence access, would fail transitively even though its own code is pure). This is exactly the kind of edge the M0b drain exists to cut, one seam at a time, without touching live behavior. PROPOSED FIX (non-behavioral refactor, Tier-1/2, NOT done here): move the local_pnl compute helper that database.py needs behind an inversion — either (a) database.py should not import a runtime/Execution PnL helper at all (invert the dependency so local_pnl imports the DB read fn, or pass the computed value in), or (b) extract the pure part of local_pnl that database.py uses into a Signals/Platform-level helper with no risk/exchange imports. Then database.py's only upward reach disappears and vwap (+ siblings) can be locked into the layer guard. VERIFY with `lint-imports` before/after (the temp contract above is the repro). Blast radius must be measured: database.py is load-bearing on the live path, so the refactor ships behind the normal test suite + a green layer-guard, and the equivalence of the moved helper is asserted. This is tracked as an M0b drain candidate, not an urgent bug — nothing is broken at runtime; it is an architecture-debt seam that blocks widening the enforced contract.

items.resolution_criteria: database.py no longer imports runtime.local_pnl (or any Execution/risk/exchange module, directly or transitively); `lint-imports` with a forbidden contract on src.units.strategies.vwap vs {units.accounts.risk, units.accounts.execute, exchange} passes; the vwap purity contract is added to .importlinter and stays green; the change is behavior-preserving (test suite green, no order-path diff).

items.source: The platform-layering plan flagged a 'violation #2': the live intent/coordination layer (src/runtime/intents.py, src/runtime/intent_multiplexer.py) 'hardcodes the strategy roster' — proposed fix: decouple it. Investigated before implementing (operator granted option (a): merge behavior-preserving live-path refactors autonomously; operator also asked for disagreement where warranted).
items.title: [architecture][assessment] 'violation #2' (decouple hardcoded roster from live intents.py / intent_multiplexer.py) is largely a MISDIAGNOSIS — DECLINED, with the one safe sub-fix shipped
items.description:
Assessment (disagreeing with the 'decouple the roster' framing, evidence below):
(1) intents.DEFAULT_PRIORITIES is NOT an architecture violation. It is a legitimate CENTRAL conflict-arbitration policy table (which strategy wins when two want the same symbol) — a Platform/coordination concern that is correctly centralized (a strategy self-declaring its own priority would be worse: every strategy claims top priority). Its values are Tier-3 order-routing decisions wrapped in load-bearing safety comments (e.g. '0 = untested-roster floor so a wiring slip can't override the established roster'; 'tune upward only with operator approval after a backtest'). Moving it to config would relocate Tier-3 data and strip that safety context for no behavioral gain.
(2) The two builder rosters are NOT a dup-that-drifted. pipeline._STRATEGY_BUILDERS (16 keys) is a strict SUBSET of intent_multiplexer._default_intent_builders (54 keys, the authoritative live intent-layer roster, MULTI_STRATEGY_INTENT_LAYER default on). pipeline.monitor_unit_for already looks up the legacy dict first then FALLS BACK to the superset (_resolve_builders) for the sleeves the legacy dict omits — a fallback added to fix a naked-orphan money-loss bug (BL-20260615-MGCNAKED). Deduping/refactoring them is a Tier-3-adjacent order-path change with real risk (that fallback exists for a money-loss reason) and ~zero architectural benefit. Under the default config the 54-superset drives everything, so there is no latent gap.
SHIPPED (the one genuinely-safe, valuable fix from this review): corrected the stale/misleading 'Mirrors pipeline._STRATEGY_BUILDERS to keep the rosters in sync' docstring on _default_intent_builders to accurately describe the legacy-subset / authoritative-superset + fallback relationship (PR #7460) — that comment would otherwise lead a future session to wrongly trim the superset and reintroduce the naked-orphan bug (field beats comment).
NOT DONE (declined): the broad 'decouple the hardcoded roster' refactor. Recommend leaving both the priority table and the two builder registries as-is. If the operator still wants the roster made config-driven for the layering story, the correct precedent is how SUPPORTED_SYMBOLS was already made config-driven (supported_symbols() unions accounts.yaml) — but that would move Tier-3 priority VALUES + their safety documentation into YAML, so it is a Tier-3 change needing explicit operator approval + a backtest that the arbitration outcomes are unchanged, not an autonomous refactor.
items.trigger_condition: Operator revisits the 'decouple the roster' idea, OR a future session proposes deduping the two builder rosters / moving DEFAULT_PRIORITIES to config — read this assessment first.
items.resolution_criteria: Operator either (a) accepts the disagreement (leave the roster/priority centralization as-is; this item closes as 'assessed, declined, comment fixed'), or (b) explicitly directs the config-driven priority migration as a Tier-3 change with a backtest gate.
items.resolution: CLOSED per explicit operator decision (2026-07-23, in chat: 'ok, i'll take your rec on violation 2'). The operator ACCEPTED the recommendation: the 'decouple the hardcoded roster' change is a misdiagnosis and is NOT being pursued. DEFAULT_PRIORITIES stays as the central Tier-3 conflict-arbitration policy table; the two builder rosters stay as legacy-subset + authoritative-superset with the existing fallback. The one safe sub-fix (the stale 'keep the rosters in sync' comment) shipped in PR #7460. No config-driven priority migration will be done; if that is ever revisited it is a Tier-3 change requiring a backtest gate that arbitration outcomes are unchanged.

items.source: The M28 valuation-snapshot producer workflow (macro-valuation-snapshot.yml) tried to direct-push its appended comms/macro/valuation_snapshots.jsonl to main and was declined with GH006 'Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/main - 9 of 9 required status checks are expected' (run 30017310010). Confirmed general: every commit on main is a squash-merged PR, there are ZERO bot direct-pushes on main. This is the SAME wall as BL-20260706-GPU-BURST-LEDGER-PUSH-RACE (gpu-burst spend-ledger). So it is a GENERAL gap: no GitHub-hosted workflow in this repo can autonomously land committed data on protected main.
items.title: No autonomous workflow path to commit data to protected main (blocks valuation-snapshot producer AND gpu-burst spend ledger)
items.description: main is branch-protected with 9 required status checks and no Actions-bot push-allowance, so a workflow's `git push HEAD:main` is rejected outright (GH006). A GITHUB_TOKEN-opened PR does NOT trigger the on:pull_request required checks (recursive-trigger suppression), so an auto-merge PR from the default token stalls forever. Net: two workflows are affected today - (1) gpu-burst-train's spend-ledger append (BL-20260706, the $10 budget-gate input silently under-counts), and (2) the M28 valuation-snapshot producer. INTERIM WORKAROUND SHIPPED for the valuation producer (this session): it now accrues its append-only log on the UNPROTECTED data branch `automation/valuation-snapshots` (restore-then-append-then-force-push), which the off-VM M28 P4 gate reads via `git show origin/automation/valuation-snapshots:comms/macro/valuation_snapshots.jsonl`. That unblocks the P4 research consumer with zero operator dependency; the live macro-thesis sleeve is observe-only (no order path) so deferring the main path strands no live capability. DURABLE FIX (operator/admin-gated, resolves BOTH workflows): choose one of - (a) add a branch-protection push-allowance / bypass scoped to the github-actions[bot] for commits touching only comms/** data files (repo Settings -> branch protection -> allow specified actors to bypass required checks, or a ruleset bypass), so a data-only workflow can direct-push; or (b) provision a write-scoped PAT secret (contents+pull-requests write, on the bypass list) so a workflow can open an auto-merging PR whose required checks actually trigger. (a) is the least-moving-parts option and needs no daily PR/CI. Once (a) or (b) is in place, repoint macro-valuation-snapshot.yml back at main (the reader-fallback in valuation_store.py already prefers comms/macro on main, so the live sleeve lights up automatically) and fix gpu-burst-train.yml the same way.
items.tier: Tier 1 (CI workflow + one operator/admin action: branch-protection setting OR a PAT secret value).
items.trigger_condition: Next CI/infra-touching session, OR when the live macro-thesis sleeve is about to go order-affecting (then the snapshots MUST be on main), OR the next /health-review. Pairs with BL-20260706-GPU-BURST-LEDGER-PUSH-RACE - fix both together.
items.resolution_criteria: A workflow can land committed data on main autonomously (verified by a green gpu-burst ledger append on main AND the valuation producer repointed at main landing a snapshot commit), OR the operator explicitly accepts the data-branch pattern as permanent for these data feeds.

items.source: ruff 0.16.0 was released 2026-07-23 and the REQUIRED ruff-lint check installs ruff from the unpinned floor `ruff>=0.15.0` in requirements-dev.txt, so CI pulled 0.16.0. Its expanded DEFAULT rule set now flags C4 (flake8-comprehensions, e.g. C408 'unnecessary dict()') + I001 (import-order) among others, surfacing 8228 pre-existing hits across the repo (visualize_all.py, visualize_swings.py, and many more) and turning ruff-lint red on every .py-touching PR (first observed on PR #7500, run 30039827262). Earlier same-day green runs (#7488-#7490 at ~17:45-18:08) used ruff 0.15.x; the repo's ruff.toml sets NO `select` (intended: ruff's default rule set as-of-S-045) so the 0.16 default expansion silently changed the gate. Reproduced locally: `ruff check .` passes on 0.15.22, `Found 8228 errors` on 0.16.0.
items.title: ruff 0.16.0 default-ruleset expansion turned the required ruff-lint check red repo-wide (8228 pre-existing hits); pinned <0.16 as the interim hold
items.description: INTERIM FIX SHIPPED (PR #7500, this session): requirements-dev.txt pinned `ruff>=0.15.0,<0.16` so CI reproduces the S-045-intended 0.15.x default-ruleset behaviour and ruff-lint goes green again on every PR (self-healing: the pin lands in the same tree the workflow installs from). This holds the line but does NOT adopt the newer, stricter rules. DURABLE FOLLOW-UP (deliberate, separate PR): decide whether to adopt ruff 0.16's expanded default set. If yes: bump the pin, then clear the 8228 residuals by fix-or-suppress. Most are mechanical autofixes (`ruff check --fix` handles 6558) but they span operator-hold paths (src/runtime/*, src/units/accounts/*, src/main.py, config/*, deploy/*) which S-045/ruff.toml deliberately keep out of scope for mechanical lint edits without an operator ping-PR - so a blanket --fix is NOT safe; the operator-hold residuals need routing through a ping-PR or a ruff.toml per-file-ignores entry with the tracking comment block. If no: keep the <0.16 pin and periodically re-evaluate as ruff moves. Either way, when ruff eventually drops 0.15.x support the decision is forced.
items.tier: Tier 1 (CI/tooling: a dev-dependency pin already shipped; the adopt-or-hold follow-up is docs/tooling + possibly operator-ping-PRs for operator-hold-path lint fixes).

items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) the operator/team explicitly accepts staying on the <0.16 pin as the standing policy, OR (b) ruff 0.16+ is adopted with all 8228 residuals fixed-or-suppressed (operator-hold paths routed correctly) and the pin bumped, with ruff-lint green on both paths.

On the trainer DATA_DIR is unset, so trade_journal_db_path() returns the STALE repo-root trade_journal.db (empty) while sync_trainer_data.sh writes the fresh live DB to $REPO_ROOT/data/trade_journal.db. relay #7772's ad-hoc `ml build-dataset` passed neither db_path= nor DATA_DIR, so source_mode=union scanned the empty file -> 0 live rows. 2026-07-27 A/B RESULT (NEGATIVE): union = ~400 live + 1525 backtest rows. Live-holdout A/B (time_aware_holdout on created_at -> most-recent = live rows): conviction-meta-v1-bt (augmented) accuracy 0.5247 / macro-F1 0.509 on n=385; conviction-meta-v1 (live-only baseline) accuracy 0.5250 / macro-F1 0.514 on n=80. Augmentation gave the stacker a testable fit but no lift. conviction-meta-v1-bt stays at candidate (zero influence) -> NO Tier-3 promotion. OBSERVED: a real-money bybit_2 XRPUSDT position with no TP/SL bracket. ROOT-CAUSE CLUSTER (all code-verified):

(1) No Bybit broker-side naked-verification sweep. order_monitor.py has _check_broker_naked_equity_positions (Alpaca, ~6112) and _check_broker_naked_ib_positions (IB, ~6234) that ask the broker 'does a resting protective leg actually exist?' and re-arm if not. There is NO Bybit equivalent. A Bybit position broker-naked-but-journal-protected is invisible to every check in the file.

(2) _attempt_naked_autoprotect (order_monitor.py:6084-6085) hard-returns False for Bybit ('not a re-armable broker (bybit/oanda atomic at entry)'). So even the DB-driven _check_naked_positions, if it flags a Bybit row, can only alert — never re-arm.

(3) _check_naked_positions selects on the JOURNAL row's stop_loss/take_profit_1 being NULL/<=0. Those fields are written from the INTENDED order['sl']/order['tp'] at open (execute._log_trade_to_journal), NOT from a confirmed broker leg — so a broker-naked Bybit position whose journal shows valid SL/TP is never flagged. (The observed XRP rows carry populated journal SL/TP.)

(4) The false assumption threading through all three (comments at order_monitor.py:6049-6050 and execute.py:1053-1056; CLAUDE.md 'Bybit/OANDA/Alpaca attach SL/TP atomically at entry, so a naked orphan can't occur there') is FALSE under two live conditions: (a) BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=partial (live on bybit_2, PRs #7161/#7162) makes SL/TP separate qty-scoped conditional legs whose lifecycle desyncs from the NETTED one-way exchange position — intent_reduce legs (NULL SL/TP by design) trim net qty without adding legs, and close_open_position cancels a closing trade's own legs (execute.py:2160-2185), so the SUM of resting legs can fall below (or to zero for) the net open qty; (b) the 20-combined-leg-per-symbol cap (BL-20260721) can silently block a leg amend/creation.

(5) Entry does not verify the SL/TP LEG was created. execute._submit_order bybit branch (execute.py:1116-1117) returns the parent orderId without confirming the qty-scoped Partial SL/TP legs exist; _classify_new_partial_tpsl_legs returns (None,None) when zero new legs appear, and that NULL is treated as 'untracked, use legacy path' rather than 'bracket failed — position is naked'. No rejection journal row, no re-arm.

SCOPE/RISK: bybit_2 is real_money (account_class real_money, yaml_mode live), symbols BTC/ETH/XRP/ADA. At audit time (08:01Z) bybit_2 held only ETHUSDT 0.06 (journal-protected; broker-leg existence UNVERIFIABLE by the bot — which is the point). No CURRENT naked real-money position, so not an active fire, but the class is live and recurs on XRP under partial-mode netting churn.

SECONDARY (separate, lower-severity) cracks found in the same audit: (a) order_packages.linked_trade_id frequently not written at execution ('multi-writer fan-out'); reconciler repairs it (live-observed on pairs pkgs 73775/4e4f) — self-heals but the monitor keys on order_packages status='open', so the package<->trade link is a fragile dependency. (b) monitor() is only invoked for strategies with an order_packages row at status='open'; a bare orphan_adopt row (or a package not status='open') is never handed to monitor(). (c) reverse-reconciler ORPHAN_POSITION_POLICY=close is an unimplemented stub that degrades to detect_only. (d) _MONITOR_BLINDNESS streak is in-process — resets on restart.
items.tier: 3 (order-path: the primary fix PLACES protective orders on a live real-money Bybit account — operator-gated, validate on bybit_1 demo first)
items.trigger_condition: A Bybit open position (esp. bybit_2 real-money) with no resting SL/TP conditional leg at the broker, regardless of journal SL/TP.
items.resolution_criteria: PRIMARY: add _check_broker_naked_bybit_positions(db) mirroring the Alpaca sweep (order_monitor.py:6112) — for each open, past-grace Bybit trade, read resting StopOrders via the existing primitive execute._partial_tpsl_leg_ids(client, category, symbol) (get_open_orders orderFilter=StopOrder); if the net position has no covering SL leg, re-arm via a new Bybit branch in _attempt_naked_autoprotect using set_trading_stop (qty-scoped in partial mode) with journal/resolved levels. Broker order-state is the idempotency (skip if a leg exists); fail-safe on read failure; skip a symbol in _TICK_ACTIVE_CLOSE_SYMBOLS. Wire into run_monitor_tick beside the Alpaca/IB sweeps. SECONDARY: in execute.py, when Partial-mode entry yields zero new SL (or TP) legs from _classify_new_partial_tpsl_legs, treat it as a bracket-placement FAILURE — attempt an immediate qty-scoped set_trading_stop re-arm and, if still absent, journal a rejection/alert instead of silently NULL-ing the id. Validate the re-arm path on bybit_1 (demo) via a dry-run/validation action before enabling on bybit_2. Also run cancel-stale-tpsl-legs (dry-run) on bybit_2 XRPUSDT to clear any stranded pre-fix legs.

updates.note: PRIMARY fix (Bybit broker-naked sweep + re-arm + entry-side verification) MERGED as PR #7874, demo-validated on bybit_1 (#7881), deployed live (git_sha dfd0172, trader restarted). SECONDARY cracks dispositioned: (1) linked_trade_id fan-out — FIXED: paper-only packages now stamp linked_trade_id immediately at execution (NULL-conditional first-writer-wins via Database.update_order_package_linked_trade_if_unset; real-money leg's unconditional write still wins in a mixed fanout), eliminating the 5-min reconciler-backfill NULL window (execute.py + database.py + tests, follow-up PR). (2) bare orphan_adopt not run through monitor() — VERIFIED-COVERED, no code change: _check_naked_positions selects ALL open non-backtest rows with no strategy filter, so a bare adopted orphan (NULL SL/TP) IS naked-swept + re-armed (now incl. Bybit); the reverse reconciler reattaches or closes-on-disappear. monitor() not firing on a strategy-less orphan is by-design. (3) ORPHAN_POSITION_POLICY=close stub — INTENTIONAL deferral, left as-is: default is 'adopt' (not close); the close branch logs + alerts + safely degrades to detect_only (never silent), and implementing reconciler-driven active flatten needs the integration test the code comment specifies (reduceOnly size/side + alert-before-close ordering) — a separate Tier-3, not requested. (4) monitor-blindness streak resets on restart — INTENTIONAL cold-start grace (a persisted streak would false-alert on the first post-restart tick before candles are fetched; the broker SL/TP backstop protects throughout). cancel-stale-tpsl-legs dry-run on bybit_2 XRPUSDT returned abort_flat (symbol currently flat — no stranded legs on an open position; re-run --apply if it re-accumulates).

items.source: RESEARCH-PROGRAM-2026-07-30 §3. Two producer failure classes exist and only ONE is guarded. Class A STALENESS (producer stops firing, ledger freezes) is covered by check_producer_liveness.py + macro-producer-liveness.yml (daily, Telegram + issue) — but scoped to ONE ledger (valuation_snapshots.jsonl). Class B VACUITY (producer fires, ledger grows, artifact is FRESH, but the measurement inside is empty and a verdict is published anyway) is guarded by NOTHING. The M1 econ event study was a textbook case: snapshots grew daily, the scorecard regenerated weekly, and the verdict came from price_bars:0 — every liveness signal green, the artifact perfectly fresh and completely vacuous (BL-20260730-M1-PRICE-JOIN-DEAD). silent-empty-guard cannot catch it either: it is a diff-scoped Python-`except` scanner over three src/ paths, so it sees neither scripts/macro|research/, nor the shell `|| echo` that actually hid this, nor the output-side contract of a verdict computed from an empty input set. An S-067 audit of this same bug CLASS exists from 2026-05-10 and it recurred anyway — a guard covering three paths against one language's syntax is not a guard against a bug class.
items.title: [tooling] Extend producer liveness from FRESHNESS to VALIDITY — nothing guards the 'green but vacuous' failure class
items.description: Fix has five parts, in leverage order: (1) DECLARED-INPUT ASSERTIONS — every research artifact already reports its input counts (price_bars, releases, n, total_scanned, records, max_n); the monitor reads them and reports VACUOUS when a load-bearing input is 0 or below the artifact's own declared floor, reusing the Telegram + GitHub-issue alerting already wired. (2) REGISTER EVERY SCHEDULED PRODUCER, not one ledger. (3) PRODUCERS FAIL LOUD — a load-bearing fetch may not degrade to a warning (done for econ-event-study in this session; generalize). (4) STANDING VACUITY SWEEP over comms/** scorecards + the soak logs, scheduled. (5) EXTEND silent-empty-guard's path scope to scripts/macro|research/ + add a shell rule for `|| echo` / `|| true` on a load-bearing fetch step.
items.trigger_condition: Any research/producer artifact can publish a verdict computed from zero inputs while its workflow exits 0.
items.resolution_criteria: check_producer_liveness (or a sibling) asserts non-zero declared inputs for every registered producer artifact and alerts VACUOUS; silent-empty-guard covers scripts/macro + scripts/research and flags `|| echo` on load-bearing fetch steps; a scheduled sweep reports any comms/** artifact whose inputs are zero.

updates.note: RESOLVED by weekly /system-review evidence pass: check_artifact_validity.py shipped covering the 4 motivating instances; artifact-validity-guard is a REQUIRED context (branch-protection-sync.yml:116).

The KNOWN_VACUOUS grandfather entry this row owned EXPIRED on 2026-08-15 and turned artifact-validity-guard red repo-wide — blocking every open PR, not just the one that surfaced it. THE EXPIRY MECHANISM WORKED AS DESIGNED: it forced the decision instead of letting the debt go permanent, which is what the `until` field exists for. Dispositioned by doing BOTH halves of the entry's own contract, because either alone leaves the class open: (a) PRUNED comms/macro/econ_calendar_captures/US-20260729T073711Z.fmp.json after verifying `rows == []`, so zero rows left the PIT ledger (econ_calendar_produce globs every capture in that dir, incl. .fmp.json, so a non-empty file could not have been removed silently); (b) econ_calendar_fmp.write_capture now REFUSES to write a zero-row capture and reports it (`wrote: False` + reason; CLI exits 1), so provisioning FMP_API_KEY later cannot re-seed the same vacuous artifact. It was the only .fmp.json ever written (one-off from the #7888 free-tier NO-BUILD probe); the daily econ-calendar-produce cron runs FXStreet, not FMP, so nothing regressed. Two plant-proven tests added (the refusal, plus a positive control that the normal write path still works). NOTE ON THIS ROW'S OWN STATE, since my first draft of this note got it wrong and the error is the interesting part: the row is NOT open — it was marked `resolved` on 2026-08-01 (the guard shipped + became a required context), i.e. FIFTEEN DAYS BEFORE the entry naming it as owner expired. So the entry's attribution requirement was satisfied by a row nobody was watching any more. Filed separately as BL-20260816-KNOWN-VACUOUS-OWNER-MAY-BE-A-CLOSED-ROW. This row stays resolved; only the one grandfathered artifact cleared here.

The one KNOWN_VACUOUS entry this item owned has CLEARED, by pruning rather than by fixing a producer. comms/macro/econ_calendar_captures/US-20260729T073711Z.fmp.json (rows: []) expired on 2026-08-15 and was hard-failing artifact-validity-guard on every PR repo-wide. Checked before deciding: it was the ONLY *.fmp.json in that directory and nothing newer had been written since 2026-07-29, so the producer is not still emitting empties - FMP was abandoned after the free-tier NO-BUILD finding (#7888) and this was its last residue. Its only repo-wide reference was the registry entry itself. Artifact and entry deleted together; the guard now reports 8 registered artifacts, 0 tracked vacuous. Deliberately NOT resolved by pushing the `until` date forward - that is the survival path the expiry mechanism exists to close.

items.source: Found while auditing for the Class-B vacuity pattern (BL-20260730-PRODUCER-VACUITY-GUARD). The M20 exit-refinement research memo records the exit-ladder soak at '135 rows / 0 differing' and calls it structural (only shadow turtle_soup declares a ladder, so P4-as-scoped is unanswerable). That is the SAME shape as the M1 price-join bug: an artifact that is fresh and growing while measuring nothing, whose verdict reads like a thin result rather than a broken one. ONE confirmed instance of a bug class means the class is unswept — this is the second candidate, not necessarily a second bug.
items.title: [soak] Exit-ladder soak reads '135 rows / 0 differing' — confirm it is structurally empty, not silently broken
items.description: Verify whether the 0-differing reading is genuinely structural (no strategy declares a materially different ladder, so there is nothing to differ) or whether the comparison itself is not running / always short-circuits. If structural: say so explicitly IN the artifact (a `differing_pct: 0` with a declared reason), so a future reader cannot mistake it for a measurement. If broken: fix and re-soak. Either way it should carry a declared-input assertion once BL-20260730-PRODUCER-VACUITY-GUARD lands. Then sweep the remaining soaks (fc-geometry, allocator, pairs, exit-lever) for the same pattern.
items.trigger_condition: A soak artifact reports rows>0 with a differing/positive count of exactly 0 and no declared structural reason.
items.resolution_criteria: The exit-ladder soak's 0-differing reading is confirmed structural (and states so in the artifact) or fixed; the other four soak logs are swept for the same shape.
items.resolution_note: RESOLVED 2026-08-02 (T5, session metis-insights-research-backlog-0tq6uz). CONFIRMED STRUCTURAL by code proof, not just the memo: in src/runtime/exit_ladder_soak.py the soak ALWAYS derives its ladder via build_exit_plan_from_legacy(cfg=None), so differs_from_single_target reduces to `n_rungs>0` (the legacy builder never emits a trailing final, so the `or final_trailing` arm is dead), and a rung is produced ONLY from a distinct `meta.tp2` price. The ONLY writer of meta['tp2'] in the whole tree is src/units/strategies/turtle_soup.py:316, and turtle_soup is execution:shadow (config/strategies.yaml:52 — net-negative money-loser, operator-demoted 2026-07-07), so it emits no live/api orders. Therefore every live-order row materializes to a single-rung plan and 0-differing is a MEASURED zero, not a broken comparison. FIX: read_soak_records() now returns a self-describing summary (differ_basis + laddered_rows + single_rung_rows + a declared differing_reason that reads 'structural zero: all N rows single-rung ... MEASURED zero, not an unrun comparison' when differing==0) — data-driven so it can never go stale: the day a live strategy emits a multi-rung exit, laddered_rows/differing rise on their own. SWEEP of the other four soaks (per the resolution criteria): fc_geometry_soak already carries an honest coverage denominator (fc_coverage_pct over fc_present) — no ambiguous zero; pairs_soak is self-describing via its by_event distribution; allocator_soak carries total_scanned as the denominator and its `disagree` is a direct two-pick comparison (low silent-no-op risk); exit_lever_soak is a write-only annotate log with NO aggregate metric to mislabel (tailed raw via /api/diag/log_file). So exit-ladder was the only soak with the genuinely ambiguous headline, and it is now fixed. VM corroboration (diag relay #8357, /api/diag/log_file?name=exit_ladder_soak): the 75 most-recent records (api 70 / prop 6, across ~20 LIVE strategies — eth_pullback_2h, pairs_sol_eth_*, trend_donchian, ict_scalp_*, tlt/spy/gld/qqq/slv/uso, htf_pullback_trend_2h, …) ALL carry n_rungs=0 and differs_from_single_target=false, and turtle_soup (the only meta.tp2 emitter) is ABSENT — exactly as the code proof predicts (it's shadow). Full soak file is 226 KB (grown past the original 135 rows); the differ semantics are unchanged. So the '0 differing' is a MEASURED structural zero, confirmed against live VM data. Follow-up note: the soak is a VM-side runtime_logs file (not comms/**), so check_artifact_validity.py (which scans comms/**) cannot reach it — the in-artifact self-describing summary IS the declared-input assertion the item asked for.

updates.note: Confirmed structural via code proof (only meta.tp2 writer is turtle_soup, which is shadow), made the summary self-describing (differ_basis/differing_reason/laddered_rows), and swept the other four soaks (fc-geometry/pairs/allocator/exit-lever — none has the same ambiguous zero). 19 exit-ladder tests pass, soak-doctrine-guard + ruff clean.

items.description: (1) STOOQ FUTURES TICKER FORM (T2, fetch_macro_candles.stooq_symbol): `NG=F` -> `ng.f` is asserted from Stooq's documented conventions, not observed. If the form is wrong the econ-event-study run now FAILS VISIBLY (the new >=100-closes-per-symbol assertion + the study's exit-2 on an empty panel), so the failure mode is loud rather than silent — but it is UNCONFIRMED until a green run reports non-zero price_bars. (2) FRED SERIES IDS (config/macro_econ_series.yaml: WNGSTUS, WCESTUS1, ICSA, CCSA, CPIAUCSL) are declared from FRED's published catalogue, not fetched. The backfill hard-fails per series with the offending id named and writes NO output, so a wrong id cannot produce a partial-looking success — but each id is unconfirmed until the first runner run. ACTION: dispatch econ-event-study (label econ-event-study-now) and run the backfill on a runner; confirm price_bars>0 and per-kind row counts; correct any id in config (an edit, not a code change). items.source: Found running macro-program M5 (docs/research/M5-vix-term-corrected-cost-reexamination-2026-08-02.md). scripts/macro/vix_term_backtest.py's SP500/DJIA legs read FRED's `SP500`/`DJIA` daily series, which are ROLLING ~10-year windows (both n=2514, span 2016-08-01->2026-07-31); NASDAQ100 has fixed deep history (1986->). So the SP500/DJIA size read grades a DIFFERENT decade on different run dates at ~identical n — the 21d FULL Sharpe swung 0.18->0.64 (SP500) / 0.05->0.62 (DJIA) at identical n=118 vs the #7577 record, purely from the window slide; NDX byte-identical (the control).
items.title: [research][reproducibility] vix_term_backtest SP500/DJIA Sharpe is a function of run-date because FRED's series are rolling 10y windows
items.description: The A-S5 timing backtest's SP500/DJIA magnitudes (Sharpe/CAGR/maxDD) are not reproducible across dates because the underlying FRED convenience series drop their oldest data as time advances. This does NOT change the VERDICT — NDX's fixed-window null already settles 'validated lead, not deployable standalone', and a Sharpe that triples from a few-month slide at constant n is itself proof of window-fragility — but it makes the SP500/DJIA numbers non-comparable across runs. Mitigation SHIPPED this session: vix_term_backtest.py now emits each leg's `data_span` (start/end/n_aligned) in JSON + a text line, so a reader sees the window instead of it being silent. Full fix (LOW priority, not required to trust the verdict): pin an explicit start date or swap SP500/DJIA to a non-rolling S&P/Dow source (e.g. ^GSPC via Stooq/yfinance) so magnitudes are comparable across dates.
items.trigger_condition: Any comparison of vix_term_backtest SP500/DJIA Sharpe/CAGR across two run dates, or any deployment decision resting on those absolute magnitudes.
items.resolution_criteria: vix_term_backtest.py's SP500/DJIA legs read a non-rolling source or a pinned window, so the size read is reproducible across dates; OR the item is closed as won't-fix because the span disclosure is deemed sufficient and no consumer depends on the absolute magnitudes.

items.source: Found by the corrected-cost re-run itself (issue #7955, run 30519435812 on f67df73). Both re-grade tools iterate config/regime_coverage_exemptions.yaml::coverage_debt — and authoring a Tier-3 cell PAYS THE STRATEGY DOWN OUT of coverage_debt. So the moment a cell is authored, the strategy becomes unmeasurable by the tooling that authored it: regime_cell_walkforward.run_cell returned the literal error 'not in coverage_debt roster'. The tools could grade CANDIDATES but never RE-AUDIT a DECISION.
items.title: [regime][governance] Authoring a cell removed the strategy from the debt roster, making the authored cell permanently un-re-auditable by its own tooling
items.description: This bit immediately and exactly where it mattered most: the 2026-07-30 corrected-cost re-run (the whole point of which was to re-check evidence graded under a ~25x fee over-charge) silently DID NOT re-measure `gld_pullback_1h` — the one live Tier-3 cell the fee fix most called into question — because authoring that cell in #7923 had removed it from coverage_debt. The run reported 34 rows and zero errors, so nothing looked wrong: a blind spot precisely at the live gate, presented as a complete re-grade. Same shape as the 'green but vacuous' class (BL-20260730-PRODUCER-VACUITY-GUARD) one level up: the artifact was complete WITH RESPECT TO ITS ROSTER, and the roster was the wrong set. FIXED in this session: regime_debt_matrix.resolve_strategy(name) resolves ANY strategy declared in config/strategies.yaml, and both --only and regime_cell_walkforward.run_cell fall back to it, so an explicitly-named already-celled strategy stays auditable. The DEFAULT roster is unchanged (still the debt list). FOLLOW-UP still open: (a) re-measure gld_pullback_1h + walk-forward it on corrected costs and record the verdict; (b) consider whether every AUTHORED cell should be on a standing re-audit list, so a cell's evidence is periodically re-checked rather than frozen at authoring time — a cell authored on a bug is otherwise permanent.

items.resolution_criteria: gld_pullback_1h re-measured + walk-forwarded on corrected costs with the verdict recorded; and a decision taken on whether authored cells get a standing re-audit list.

items.source: The corrected-cost regime re-grade (issue #7955) cannot cleanly attribute its deltas: the matrix window is a ROLLING 730 days and the baseline run was ~a day earlier, so every delta mixes the fee correction with a window slide. Proof the confound is real: slv_trend_1h chop short moved -0.56R the WRONG way at n=10, which a fee REDUCTION cannot cause.
items.title: [research][method] Run the fixed-window fee A/B — the corrected-cost deltas are inferred, not attributed
items.description: One matrix pass, same candle window, two --fee-bps-roundtrip arms (0 for commission-free vs the flat 7.5), diffed per cell. That isolates the fee effect from window drift and turns 'consistent with the predicted 0.04-0.12 R/trade band' into a measured number. Cheap (a second arm in the same run). Until it exists, no per-cell delta in docs/research/regime-debt-matrix-corrected-cost-2026-07-30.md should be quoted as a fee amount, and the asset-class re-read (whether marginal-negative equity/ETF legs flip positive) stays deferred — the legs that would flip are small-n, which is exactly where drift dominates.
items.trigger_condition: Anyone quoting a corrected-cost delta as a measured fee effect, or re-reading the equity/ETF sleeve off the uncontrolled comparison.
items.resolution_criteria: A fixed-window two-arm fee A/B is run and its per-cell deltas recorded; the findings doc's §1 caveat is replaced with measured attribution.
items.resolution: Fixed-window fee A/B run 2026-08-02 (regime_debt_matrix --fee-ab 0,7.5, issue #8329, tooling PR #8327). Grades the SAME 730d candle window at both fee arms so the per-cell delta isolates the fee effect from the rolling-window slide. RESULT: all 20 gradeable cells show a NEGATIVE net-R delta (a fee can only reduce R — the confounded two-run comparison could not guarantee this and had one wrong-signed cell). The commission-free equity/ETF sleeve (gld/slv) lands 0.044-0.090 R/trade, squarely in the predicted 0.04-0.12 band; BTC cells run lower (~0.03-0.06, ATR scaling). The 2026-07-30 doc's wrong-signed slv_trend_1h chop-short row is confirmed WINDOW DRIFT (clean -1.28R over the identical window). Findings: docs/research/regime-debt-matrix-fee-ab-2026-08-02.md; the corrected-cost doc's §1 caveat is replaced with the measured attribution. No cell authored/revoked (Tier-3).
