items.source: Found while scoping the operator-directed re-audit of authored regime cells (#7962, #7963). regime_debt_matrix measures the 1-D TREND axis only — it has no vol-split — so the six 2-D `trend_vol` cells cannot be re-measured by ANY existing tool. This is a second, independent instance of BL-20260730-REGIME-CELL-UNAUDITABLE: cells that gate live routing with no mechanism to re-check them.
items.title: [regime] the offline harness has NO vol axis — and the obvious fix (the frozen vol_detector) would reproduce the very population-mismatch this row exists to flag
items.description: The 2-D cells and why they matter: trend_donchian (trending/volatile, transitional/calm, chop/calm), squeeze_breakout_4h (trending/calm), ict_scalp_5m (trending/volatile, chop/volatile). All six affect LIVE BTC routing — BTC has an advisory regime head and REGIME_ML_VERDICT_MODE=use enforce is live, so these cells drop real intents. Yet regime_debt_matrix has no vol axis, so a matrix re-run cannot see them. ict_scalp_5m is the worst case: it carries NO 1-D cells at all, so its entire live gating rests on two 2-D cells that NOTHING can currently re-measure. After #7962 + #7963 land, 6 of 16 live-affecting cells remain un-re-audited. NEEDED: a vol-split re-run — tag emitted trades with the vol label the router would resolve (ml_vol_regime_for_symbol when an advisory head exists, else the frozen vol_detector edges) and break the matrix down per (trend, vol, direction). The 2026-06-27 Design-A vol-split (docs/research/A-vol-gating-OFFcell-design-2026-06-27.md) did this once by hand; the gap is that it was never turned into repeatable tooling. Until it is, do NOT describe the authored cells as re-checked. || ESCALATED 2026-07-30 (severity medium -> high) after this nearly caused a bad Tier-3 proposal. The scope is worse than 'the 2-D cells cannot be audited': because regime_cell_walkforward / regime_debt_matrix / regime_tag_emitted contain NO vol axis at all (verified by grep: zero hits for trend_vol|vol_regime|calm|volatile), a 1-D cell re-audit POOLS every vol state -- including the vol states a 2-D cell already gates live. The measured trade population therefore differs from the live-traded population, so the verdict is not decision-grade. Same fidelity class as the side_filter bug fixed this morning (BL-20260730 side_filter forwarding): the harness measured legs the strategy never takes. CONCRETE NEAR-MISS: I was about to propose squeeze_breakout_4h trending short -> off on walk-forward #7990 (short_stable_drag TRUE, 3/4 folds, pooled -3.40R n=26, sign holds ex-fold-3). But config/regime_policy.yaml already gates trending/calm squeeze short via a 2-D cell, so an unknown fraction of those 26 shorts are calm trades LIVE ALREADY REFUSES. If the drag sits in the calm shorts, live is already protected and the 1-D change only adds a block on volatile shorts that may be fine; if it sits in the volatile shorts the change is justified -- and the harness cannot tell these apart. Proposal WITHHELD. EXACT CONTAMINATED SET (both 1-D and 2-D cells): squeeze_breakout_4h (trending/calm) and trend_donchian (trending/volatile, transitional/calm, chop/calm). VERIFIED CLEAN, so prior conclusions on them STAND: htf_pullback_trend_2h has NO 2-D cell (the operator-approved long->off merged in #7979 is unaffected -- checked, not assumed) and gld_pullback_1h has none (its SURVIVES verdict is unaffected). FIX: add the vol axis to the harness so a cell is graded on the (trend, vol) population live actually trades; until then NO 1-D cell change may be proposed for a contaminated strategy. || SCOPED 2026-07-30 -- and the fix is NOT 'add a vol indicator to the harness', which is what this row would previously have led a session to build. Verified in intents.py's own docstring: 'BTC has the 15m advisory head, so every BTC cell resolves the ML label regardless of the strategy's timeframe (the live trend_vol cells gate BTC trend_donchian (1h) + squeeze_breakout_4h (4h) and they DO resolve ML, not frozen)'. BOTH contaminated strategies are BTCUSDT, so their LIVE vol label comes from the ADVISORY ML HEAD btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1 thresholded at ML_VOL_VERDICT_THRESHOLD (0.5) -- NOT from the frozen vol_detector. Splitting the harness on the frozen detector would therefore NOT reproduce live; it would be a SECOND, different mismatch that looks like a fix. TWO PATHS, and they answer different questions: (A) BACKTEST-BASED CELL GRADING requires replaying the ML vol head offline per bar. The manifest IS in-repo (ml/configs/btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1.yaml) but the trained ARTIFACT is not -- it lives in the trainer registry, pullable via the trainer-vm-diag relay (autonomous territory). Steps: pull the artifact; score it on historical BTC 15m bars using the manifest's feature list via the offline pure fns so live==train; threshold at 0.5 -> calm/volatile per bar; map each emitted trade's entry time to the containing 15m bar's label; then add a --vol-split to regime_tag_emitted / regime_debt_matrix / regime_cell_walkforward so a cell is graded on the (trend, vol) population. This is the real unlock and it is a MULTI-STEP BUILD, not a one-commit change -- do not scope it as one. Same replay class as analyze_exit_head (see BL-20260730-EXITHEAD-REPLAY-SINGLE-THRESHOLD); it is feasible, just not cheap. (B) CHEAPER, COMPLEMENTARY, DIFFERENT QUESTION: for LIVE trades the vol label is ALREADY RECORDED -- the hard gate writes a regime_hard_gate audit row carrying the resolved `cell`, queryable via /api/diag/audit_query?event=regime_hard_gate. That measures what live is actually gating and can be done now with no ML replay, but it CANNOT grade a backtest cell (historical backtest trades have no audit rows) so it does not substitute for (A). UNTIL (A) LANDS: no 1-D cell change may be proposed for squeeze_breakout_4h or trend_donchian. || DESIGN SCOPED 2026-07-30 (operator-directed 'start on the vol axis'). Two facts, both verified in CODE not inferred from docs, that together kill the obvious approach. (1) ALL SIX live 2-D cells are BTCUSDT: trend_donchian 1h (trending/volatile long, transitional/calm long, chop/calm long), ict_scalp_5m 5m (trending/volatile and chop/volatile, both legs), squeeze_breakout_4h 4h (trending/calm short). (2) NONE of those three strategies declares a `vol_spec` in config/strategies.yaml (only ict_scalp_xrp_5m does, and it has no 2-D cell) -- because live does NOT use the frozen detector for them at all. src/runtime/intents.py::_decision_vol_regime resolves the DECISION vol label from the BTC 15m ADVISORY HEAD's ML P(volatile), keyed PER SYMBOL (deliberately not per (symbol,timeframe), so the single 15m head's label drives the 1h and 4h cells too), thresholded at ML_VOL_VERDICT_THRESHOLD. THE KILLER DETAIL, quoted from that function's own docstring: the trend_vol cells 'were authored under the ML label and LOSE money under the frozen label' (docs/research/A-vol-gating-OFFcell-design-2026-06-27.md). So an offline vol axis built on vol_detector would not merely be an approximation -- it would measure a population live does not gate on, whose documented behaviour is OPPOSITE. (1) fc-pcv-v1 over v520 SUCCEEDED: 175,272 bars labelled, calm 159,324 / volatile 15,948 = 9.1% volatile, P(volatile) over 109,751 distinct values, 15s / 423MB RSS, feature audit ok with vol_bucket parity 5,008 compared / 0 mismatches. Operator answered the standing question ('should every authored cell be re-audited?') with yes. #7958 made authored cells MEASURABLE again; nothing yet re-measures them on a cadence, so a cell authored on a bug stays authored indefinitely — which is exactly how the gld_pullback_1h cell survived a ~25x fee over-charge unnoticed.
items.title: [regime][governance] Stand up an authored-cell RE-AUDIT REGISTER — a decision is not permanent evidence
items.description: Eight strategies carry authored cells (5 live: gld_pullback_1h, htf_pullback_trend_2h, ict_scalp_5m, squeeze_breakout_4h, trend_donchian; 3 shadow: fade_breakout_4h, fvg_range_15m, vwap). Most 1-D cells trace to regime-roster-matrix-2026-06-01 and had NEVER been re-measured before 2026-07-30. Build the register: for each authored cell record (a) the evidence run + date it was authored from, (b) its fidelity flag at authoring time, (c) a re-audit due-date, and (d) the last re-audit verdict. Then re-measure on that cadence — the natural home is the /system-review roll-up, which already has a promotion/demotion readiness mandate and a coverage guard that fails when a required assessment is skipped. Two design points learned the hard way: the register must key off config/regime_policy.yaml (the CELLS), never off coverage_debt (a work queue that ERASES an item when it is acted on); and it must record fidelity, because an approximate row cannot sustain a cell. Composes with the binding 'Green is not evidence' rule's corollary — a decision is not permanent evidence.

items.source: The multiline-aware `|| echo` guard found FOUR producer workflows whose candle fetch swallows its own failure and lets the downstream gate report 'the honest n=0': cot-positioning-backfill.yml, m28-value-grade.yml, macro-valuation-backfill.yml, sysdyn-gas-calibrate.yml. All four were INVISIBLE to the first (line-based) version of the guard because the `||` sits on a shell line-continuation.
items.title: [research] Four macro gates degrade a failed candle fetch into an 'honest n=0' verdict — annotated allow-degraded, not resolved
items.description: Each workflow comments that a degraded fetch means the gate 'will report the honest n=0 / insufficient_data'. That framing is exactly the class BL-20260730-PRODUCER-VACUITY-GUARD exists to kill: a gate publishing a verdict computed from zero inputs, on a green run. 'Honest n=0' is honest about the COUNT but not about the CAUSE — a reader cannot tell 'no data exists' from 'the fetch broke'. Annotated with `# allow-degraded: <this id>` so the guard passes and the debt is attributed rather than silent; NOT fixed, because changing four producers' failure semantics is a real behaviour change that deserves its own reviewed pass. THE FIX for each: let the fetch fail (set -e), or keep it tolerant but have the DOWNSTREAM gate distinguish 'no candles fetched' from 'candles fetched, no signal' and refuse to emit a verdict in the former case (register those artifacts in check_artifact_validity.CHECKS). NOTE the annotation has no expiry mechanism — unlike KNOWN_VACUOUS, which fails once its date passes; consider giving allow-degraded the same treatment so these cannot become permanent.
items.trigger_condition: A macro gate reports n=0 / insufficient_data and nobody checks whether its inputs were fetched at all.
items.resolution_criteria: Each of the four either fails on a degraded fetch, or its downstream gate distinguishes unfetched from no-signal and is registered in check_artifact_validity; the allow-degraded annotations are then removed.

updates.note: RESOLVED via the FIRST arm of the resolution criteria ('each of the four fails on a degraded fetch'). ROOT: fetch_macro_candles.py::main already returns exit 1 ONLY on TOTAL failure (0 symbols with >=30 closes) and exit 0 on partial/full — the four workflows just SWALLOWED that signal (continue-on-error + `|| echo`/`|| true`), so a totally-failed fetch proceeded to a grader that emitted a false n=0. FIX: removed continue-on-error + the `|| echo` swallow on the three backfill fetch steps (macro-valuation-backfill / cot-positioning-backfill / sysdyn-gas-calibrate), so a total fetch failure now FAILS the step instead of grading an empty candle dir; m28-value-grade's mid-block `|| true` (its run block has no set -e) replaced with an explicit `if ! fetch; then error + exit 1; fi` guard. Partial coverage (>=1 usable symbol, fetcher exit 0) still proceeds — the acceptable 'honest n=0 for the uncovered symbols' case. All four allow-degraded annotations removed. This distinguishes 'no candles fetched' (now a hard failure) from 'candles fetched, no signal' (a genuine n=0), which was the defect; no grader / check_artifact_validity.CHECKS edits needed (the second arm) since the first arm suffices. RESIDUAL not covered: per-symbol partial-fetch attribution (one symbol's fetch broken reading n=0 while its siblings grade) — the total-failure case, the one that produced a fully-false clean grade, is fixed.

items.source: Self-review. KNOWN_VACUOUS in check_artifact_validity.py requires a backlog owner AND an `until` date, and the guard FAILS once the date passes — so tracked debt cannot become permanent. The sibling override for swallowed fetches, the inline `# allow-degraded: <reason>` comment, has NEITHER requirement enforced: any string satisfies it, forever. I shipped the weaker override in the same PR as the stronger one.
items.title: [tooling] `# allow-degraded:` has no owner/expiry enforcement — the weaker sibling of KNOWN_VACUOUS
items.description: Make the guard parse the annotation and require (a) a backlog id matching a real row in one of the three review backlogs, and (b) an `until:` date, failing once it passes — mirroring known_vacuous_problems(). Otherwise allow-degraded is exactly the silence list KNOWN_VACUOUS was deliberately designed not to be, and the four annotations added in this PR (BL-20260730-CANDLE-FETCH-DEGRADES-TO-N0) will sit forever. Small change; worth doing before the annotation spreads.
items.trigger_condition: An `# allow-degraded:` annotation exists with no backlog row or no expiry.
items.resolution_criteria: The guard validates every allow-degraded annotation for a resolvable backlog id + an unexpired `until:`, and fails otherwise.

updates.note: RESOLVED. New guard `scripts/ops/check_allow_degraded.py` (stdlib, reuses check_backlog_refs.filed_ids) scans .github/scripts/src/config for the COMMENT-form `# allow-degraded: <payload>` and fails unless the payload carries (a) a backlog id resolving to a filed review-backlog row AND (b) an `until:YYYY-MM-DD`, failing once that date passes — mirroring known_vacuous_problems() exactly. Wired into CI as step 2b of artifact-validity-guard.yml (beside the producer-swallow check that ALLOWS the override). The four existing annotations (all BL-20260730-CANDLE-FETCH-DEGRADES-TO-N0, in macro-valuation-backfill / cot-positioning-backfill / sysdyn-gas-calibrate / m28-value-grade) were given `until:2026-11-01` (a ~90-day re-review horizon for that still-open medium item — the candle-fetch degradation is a standing acceptable-degradation, not near-term debt, so a longer window than KNOWN_VACUOUS's ~2wk). Detection is precise not presence-only (the new-table-wiring-guard lesson): a payload containing `<` is a syntax placeholder (skipped), and the guard's own definition file is the one self-exclusion — no file allow-list, so it can't be cheaply lied to. 10 tests (well-formed / missing-id / unresolvable-id / missing-until / expired / boundary / placeholder-skip / non-comment-form-ignored); `check_allow_degraded.py` green on the live repo (4 valid); the artifact-validity-guard doc-text updated to the `<BL-id> until:<date>` contract.

items.source: scripts/research/regime_debt_matrix.py::_SQZ_TP_R_NONBINDING. Wiring backtest_squeeze.py into classify() exposed one infidelity: the harness has no --tp-r flag (it models the Chandelier trail as the sole profit-exit). The live config's tp_r: 50.0 cannot bind before a 3.5-ATR trail fires, so the omission is harmless there — but that is currently asserted via a THRESHOLD CONSTANT (20R), not measured.
items.title: [regime] squeeze tp_r non-binding bound is a threshold constant, not an empirical check
items.description: The honest version of this check is empirical: after the harness run, verify no emitted trade's MFE ever reached tp_r on the sample; only then is ignoring tp_r provably non-binding FOR THAT SAMPLE. The threshold form can be wrong in principle (a tighter trail or a calmer regime could let a 20R+ target bind, and a future strategy could sit just above the line). Implementing it needs a post-run fidelity adjustment in BOTH callers (regime_debt_matrix.run_one and regime_cell_walkforward.run_cell), which return fidelity before the subprocess runs — a real refactor, not a one-liner, which is why it is filed rather than inlined. Severity is low because the current bound fails CLOSED (below 20R the row degrades to `approximate`, blocking cell authoring) and the live value is 50R. Note this is self-filed: the guard I wrote is weaker than the guard I would want reviewing someone else's.

Discovered because `git log -S'exit_head_model' -- config/strategies.yaml` dead-ended at a single 2026-07-28 whole-file commit, which looked like a real answer. `git fetch --deepen=2000` recovered history to 2026-03-22 (2718 commits) and immediately changed a research conclusion (see docs/research/regime-debt-matrix-corrected-cost-2026-07-30.md A6).
items.title: [tooling] shallow session clone silently defeats the mandated `git log -p` history check
items.description: CLAUDE.md § 'Every session' requires, for Tier-2/3 files, 'also read its recent history (git log -p <file>) so you don't undo a load-bearing, operator-approved decision.' On a shallow clone that check returns a PLAUSIBLE BUT WRONG answer with no error: the file reads as having one commit, three days old. This is the session's own bug class turned on its own tooling -- green relative to a wrong scope -- and it is the highest-leverage item here because it silently degrades EVERY session's compliance with a rule meant to prevent undoing operator-approved decisions. Concrete harm already observed: without the deepen, trend_donchian's regime cells appeared to have no authoring history, so the fact that all 6 predate the 2026-07-12 exit-head go-live (#6211) was invisible. Fix options: (a) have the session bootstrap/CLAUDE.md instruct `git fetch --deepen` (or --unshallow) before any history-dependent check; (b) better, make the check fail LOUD -- a tiny helper that refuses to answer a history question on a shallow clone rather than answering it wrongly. (b) is preferred and is the same fail-closed shape as the artifact-validity guard.

items.title: [regime] trend_donchian's 6 live cells rest on evidence SUPERSEDED by the exit head — re-audit via the M20 exit-panel path
items.description: CORRECTED 2026-07-30 by the operator. This row previously claimed the cells could NEVER be re-measured because an ML exit head cannot be replayed offline. THAT WAS FALSE and the row is rewritten so the false premise is not carried forward. The M20 toolchain replays exactly this: scripts/research/build_intrabar_exit_panel.py builds the per-bar in-trade panel and scripts/research/analyze_exit_head.py SIMULATES the head's exit decisions per trade (first bar the head says exit, the trade realizes its mark-to-market R there, net of an exit fee) under grouped-by-trade_id, purged, embargoed, uniqueness-weighted walk-forward, scored against the baseline fixed SL/TP exit. That is more rigorous than the harness I had treated as the only option. ROOT CAUSE OF THE ERROR: regime_debt_matrix.py::_UNREPLAYABLE carried the comment 'an ML exit head can never be replayed offline'; its real meaning is narrow (backtest_trend.py does not model this lever). A local scope limitation was read as a global impossibility and promoted to a research conclusion. Same bug class as the rest of this session, one level up -- a tool reporting IMPOSSIBILITY out of a wrong scope deserves at least as much suspicion as one reporting success, because it closes off work rather than merely mis-reporting it. The stale comment is fixed in place. WHAT STANDS: the dates. Cells authored 2026-06-01 (#2583) and 2026-06-28 (#4868); exit-head-donchian-1h-v1 began driving real exits 2026-07-12 (#6211). All 6 live cells predate it by 2-6 weeks, so the evidence IS superseded. ACTUAL NEXT STEP (no operator decision needed): (1) build the intrabar exit panel for trend_donchian over the regime-tagged window; (2) replay exit-head-donchian-1h-v1 at its LIVE threshold 0.10 / action close so simulated exits match the live exit policy; (3) split per-trade R by regime via regime_tag_emitted.py and apply the SAME short_stable_drag/long_stable_drag gate used for every other cell (#7915), so all six are graded on one consistent bar.

items.title: [regime] side_filter was not forwarded to the harnesses — short-only strategies measured on BOTH legs
items.description: FIXED in this PR (side_filter added to both lever maps, with tests anchored on the real config so a roster change surfaces). Filed anyway as the record, because the shape recurs: a parallel session adds a live capability + its harness flag correctly, but does not know the regime debt-matrix lever maps exist, so the research tool silently keeps measuring the OLD behaviour. Impact if unfixed: any regime cell authored or re-audited for those two strategies rests partly on long trades the strategy never takes live. Note it did NOT fail closed on its own -- an unknown key degrades the row to `approximate` (which blocks cell AUTHORING, good), but the measurement itself would still have been wrong and readable. The durable fix is a coupling check: a CI guard asserting every behavioural key in config/strategies.yaml is either in a harness lever map or explicitly declared unmodelled. Without that, the next capability added lands the same way.

items.source: Generalization of BL-20260730-SIDE-FILTER-NOT-FORWARDED. There is no mechanical link between config/strategies.yaml's behavioural keys and the lever maps in scripts/research/regime_debt_matrix.py (_TREND_PLAIN/_TREND_LEVER_FLAG/_PB_*/_SQZ_*). A new live lever can be added, wired into the live builder AND its harness, and the research matrix keeps silently measuring the old behaviour.
items.title: [research-tooling] no guard couples live strategy keys to the harness lever maps
items.description: Proposed: a CI guard that collects every key appearing on any enabled strategy in config/strategies.yaml and asserts each is classified in exactly one of (a) a PLAIN set (non-behavioural / modelled by default), (b) a LEVER_FLAG map (forwarded), (c) _UNREPLAYABLE, or (d) an explicit UNMODELLED declaration with a reason. An unclassified key fails the build with the strategy and key named, which converts a silent measurement error into a build error at the moment the capability is added. This is the same fail-closed shape as artifact-validity-guard and the shallow-clone guard. Worth doing because the failure is invisible by construction: the matrix still produces a plausible row, and only the fidelity label (approximate) hints that something was dropped -- and `approximate` is common enough to be background noise.

updates.note: SHIPPED (#8404): scripts/check_harness_lever_coupling.py + harness-lever-coupling-guard.yml. Fail-closed like env-gate-guard — every key on an ENABLED, harness-classified strategy MUST be in exactly one of PLAIN | LEVER_FLAG | _UNREPLAYABLE | UNMODELLED. The PLAIN/LEVER_FLAG/_UNREPLAYABLE maps are imported from regime_debt_matrix (one source of truth, module untouched); the guard adds the explicit per-family UNMODELLED registry (the previously-implicit omitted-lever branch). Whole-state check on every PR + a self-test proving detection still fails on an injected gap. Live config passes (42 enabled classified strategies). An unclassified key now fails the build naming the strategy+key. Sibling BL-20260730-CAPABILITY-INDEX-NEEDS-FIDELITY-LIMITS can reuse this UNMODELLED registry for its per-tool 'cannot model' column.

items.title: [research-tooling] capability index routes tools but does not declare their fidelity limits
items.description: This is where the 2026-07-30 error actually lived, so it is the highest-value follow-up to the index itself. Knowing analyze_exit_head.py exists is necessary but not sufficient: a session also needs to know that backtest_trend.py cannot model exit_head_*, that backtest_squeeze.py has no --side-filter and no --tp-r, and that backtest_ict_scalp.py has NO fee model at all (gross only, BL-20260610-M15-1). Today those facts live scattered in lever maps and code comments -- and a code comment is exactly what produced the false impossibility conclusion. Proposal: a per-tool 'cannot model' column in the index, generated from the lever maps rather than hand-written (hand-written would drift, which is the failure mode being fixed). Composes with BL-20260730-HARNESS-LEVER-MAP-COUPLING-GUARD: the same extraction feeds both.

items.source: Found while auditing the exit-head path. research-exit-head-build.yml swallowed BOTH the panel build and the analyzer with `|| true`, so an empty panel still rendered a VERDICT.md; it also had no roster/clock_tf input, so a backtest_system run silently used the DEFAULT roster instead of the requested strategy. research-panel-build.yml swallowed five steps. The artifact-validity guard's PRODUCER pattern matched only fetch_*/_produce/_backfill/_snapshot and missed the entire research family (build_*_panel.py, analyze_*.py).
items.title: [research-tooling] both research workflows swallowed producer failures; the guard's pattern missed the whole family
items.description: FIXED in this PR; filed as the record and because the guard-coverage lesson generalizes. Fixes: exit-head workflow gained validated roster/clock_tf inputs, lost both `|| true`s, and now asserts a non-empty panel BEFORE the analyzer runs. research-panel-build got three DIFFERENT treatments rather than one blanket rule -- the panel build is load-bearing (must fail), the multi-outcome sweep tolerates one outcome failing but now fails if EVERY outcome failed and warns on partial, and the explicitly-requested per-cell step must fail. The guard's PRODUCER regex was widened to build_*/analyze_*/_resolve and is now clean repo-wide. LESSON: a guard that names a bug class but matches only one naming convention is scoped-wrong in exactly the way the class describes -- worth re-checking the other guards' patterns against the families they claim to cover.

items.title: [macro/M1] econ event study joined ZERO price bars for its entire life — the flagship 'green is not evidence' instance
items.description: FILED LATE, and that is itself the finding. This id is cited from docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md (as the canonical example of the binding 'Green is not evidence' rule), scripts/ops/check_artifact_validity.py, scripts/macro/{econ_event_study,fetch_macro_candles,econ_calendar_snapshot_backfill}.py, and FOUR workflows -- but it existed only as other rows' `refs` and was never filed as a row of its own. So the flagship instance of the rule was 'tracked by' an id that resolved to nothing, which reads as tracked while being tracked by nobody. Exactly the crack the operator's 2026-07-30 directive names. THREE causes, all fixed but NOT ALL VERIFIED: (1) the Stooq URL/symbol mapping was wrong so the candle fetch returned nothing -- fixed (_STOOQ_URL + _STOOQ_FUTURES map + stooq_symbol()); (2) econ_event_study.py treated an empty panel as a soft zero and exited 0 -- fixed, now exits 2 unless --allow-empty-panel is passed explicitly; (3) the workflow swallowed the fetch with `|| echo` so a dead fetch stayed green -- fixed, plus a >=100-closes-per-symbol assertion. STILL UNVERIFIED ON A RUNNER: the econ-event-study workflow has not re-run since. Until it does, the fix is code-complete and evidence-free -- the same state that produced the bug. Verify then close. || RESOLVED + LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-07-30 (econ-event-study run on issue #7991): **price_bars: 899** for NG=F, against `price_bars: 0` for the producer's entire life. items.source: The LIVE exit-head firing rule (src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py::_exit_head_verdict) is CONDITIONAL and shape-dependent: for below_half_r it fires on `score < tau AND open_r < below_r`; for peak shapes the comparison INVERTS (`score > tau`, plus `open_r >= below_r` for peak_winner). scripts/research/analyze_exit_head.py applies a SINGLE --exit-threshold and models neither the second condition nor the shape inversion.
items.title: [research] analyze_exit_head's policy sim is a single threshold — it does not reproduce the live CONDITIONAL exit-head rule
items.description: So a run at --exit-threshold 0.10 reproduces tau ONLY and will fire on trades the live head leaves open, OVERSTATING the head's activity. It is an APPROXIMATION of the live policy, not a replay of it -- and the difference decides whether a regime cell can be graded against the strategy that actually trades. Noted explicitly in the dispatch (issue #7976) so the result cannot be misread as 'the live head replayed'. CONTEXT: this was found while correcting a WORSE error in the opposite direction -- I had claimed an ML exit head can never be replayed offline at all, which is false (the M20 toolchain does exactly that). The correct position is the narrow one: replay IS possible, and the current analyzer's policy sim is not yet faithful to the live conditional rule. FIX: the live-matching predicate already exists as src/runtime/.../exit_head_shadow.py::would_exit (the docstring of _exit_head_verdict says it mirrors it) -- reuse that in the policy sim rather than re-deriving a threshold rule, so live==replay by construction. Until then, no trend_donchian cell may be authored or retired off analyze_exit_head output.

items.title: [macro/M1] the two ENERGY event kinds use EIA series codes in a FRED-series config — 404, and they are the M1 targets
items.description: CATEGORY ERROR, not a typo. WCESTUS1 and WNGSTUS are EIA's own dnav series codes (eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?s=WCESTUS1), not FRED series ids, so fredgraph.csv correctly 404s them. I authored them into config/macro_econ_series.yaml from EIA's catalogue while the fetcher is a FRED fetcher. THE FIX IS A SOURCE DECISION, NOT AN ID GUESS -- two possibilities needing different work: (1) FRED republishes these EIA series under different ids => a config edit; (2) FRED does not carry them keyless at all => needs EIA's own feed (ir.eia.gov weekly text/CSV is keyless; EIA API v2 needs a KEY, which is an operator hand-off). I CANNOT DETERMINE WHICH FROM THE SANDBOX: fred.stlouisfed.org is firewalled here (confirmed twice -- WebFetch 403, direct fetch fails) while the same call works on a GitHub runner. Guessing candidate ids into config would reproduce precisely the bug being fixed (an unverified id that looks authoritative), so it is deliberately NOT done. PROPOSED NEXT STEP: add a `--probe-ids` DIAGNOSTIC mode to econ_calendar_snapshot_backfill.py that tests candidate ids on the runner and REPORTS which resolve, writing no output ever -- so the runner does the verification instead of the sandbox guessing. It must stay a diagnostic: a try-candidates-until-one-resolves FALLBACK inside the producer would silently backfill from whatever id happened to work, which is the same class as the original bug. IMPACT: these two kinds ARE the ROADMAP_MACRO M1/M2 energy-event targets, so M1 stays blocked on this even though the machinery now works -- the 3 verified kinds (jobless claims x2, CPI) unblock the study END-TO-END but are not the energy sleeve. Do not report M1 as unblocked on the strength of the 3 working kinds. || PROBE BUILT 2026-07-30 (`--probe-ids`): reports which configured ids resolve, writes nothing, and DISTINGUISHES the two cases that need different config actions -- HTTP 404 (wrong id / wrong source) vs HTTP 200 with empty history (right id, data question). The shared adapter logs-and-returns-empty on an HTTP error, collapsing both into one message, so the probe reads the status itself; the production path still goes through the adapter untouched. Deliberately NOT a fallback -- it never tries candidate ids and adopts whichever resolves, which would backfill from whatever happened to work (same defect class one level down); a test guards that by inspecting the code with the docstring stripped AND behaviourally. Run it on a runner to decide FRED-republished vs EIA keyless feed vs keyed API. || UPDATE 2026-07-30: the --probe-ids diagnostic proposed above was built and RUN, and it settled the first half: the ids as configured are dead (HTTP 404, measured on a runner that can reach FRED, not inferred). The second half needs candidate ids TESTED, which --probe-ids could not do because it probes only what is already configured -- meaning the sole way to test a candidate was to COMMIT it, i.e. the bug itself. So --probe-extra <csv> now probes CANDIDATE ids alongside the configured ones under a `candidate:` prefix, reports them separately, never auto-adopts one, and deliberately does NOT let a failing candidate fail the run nor a resolving candidate mask a broken configured id. NEXT STEP is now cheap: dispatch econ-calendar-backfill with `mode: probe` + `probe_extra: <candidates>` and read which resolve; a resolving id STILL has to be checked for units/frequency/vintage before it is committed. SCOPE CORRECTION: this is a COVERAGE gap on the two ENERGY kinds, not the M1 gate blocker it was called when the probe was dispatched -- the full-scale event study and the M3 verdict both ran on the three resolving kinds.

items.source: Attempting to build the M3 overlap validator found ZERO joinable rows between the forward consensus file and the FRED backfill, for all 3 kinds (initial_jobless_claims fwd=8 dates / bf=3031 dates / intersect=0; continuing 8/3030/0; cpi_yoy 1/917/0). Cause: scheduled_for means DIFFERENT THINGS in the two files. Forward (bigdata:fxstreet) = the RELEASE date (cpi_yoy 2026-07-14). Backfill (keyless FRED) = the OBSERVATION / REFERENCE PERIOD (cpi_yoy 2026-04-01, 2026-05-01, 2026-06-01).
items.title: [macro/M1] backfill `scheduled_for` is the FRED reference period, not the release date — zero join with the forward file, and the event study joins prices at the wrong date
items.description: TWO consequences, the second worse than the first. (1) M3 CANNOT RUN AT ALL -- the overlap validation the operator-approved M1 gate names as its satisfiability condition for option (b) has an empty join. I previously told the operator M3 was 'runnable right now on the labour kinds (n=13/8)'; that was WRONG and is corrected -- those counts were rows with a survey consensus, not rows joinable to a model expectation. (2) THE EVENT STUDY ITSELF JOINS AT THE WRONG DATE when fed backfilled rows. CPI for reference period 2026-06-01 is released ~2026-07-15; joining forward returns at 06-01 measures a window that mostly PRECEDES the release, i.e. the wrong window entirely. That does not create lookahead (the window is too EARLY, not too late) but it does guarantee a measured null that a reader would misinterpret as 'no edge in economic surprise'. Any M1/M2 verdict computed off backfilled rows before this is fixed is meaningless. ROOT CAUSE IS A DATA LIMITATION, NOT JUST A BUG: keyless FRED (fredgraph.csv) serves OBSERVATION dates only; true release timestamps live in ALFRED / the FRED releases API. So there is no exact release date available on the keyless path. PROPOSED FIX (declared approximation, never presented as truth): add a per-kind `release_lag_days` to config/macro_econ_series.yaml (weekly claims: week-ending Saturday -> Thursday release, ~+5d; CPI: ~+15d), emit BOTH `reference_period` and a computed `scheduled_for`/release date, and stamp `release_date_basis: modeled_lag` alongside the existing `pit_basis` so a modeled release date can never be mistaken for an observed one. Join on that. Then re-verify the overlap is non-empty BEFORE trusting any M3 result. || FIX LANDED 2026-07-30, NOT YET RE-RUN. Per-kind release_lag_days added to config (claims +5d week-ending Sat -> Thu; continuing +12d; CPI +45d reference-month -> mid next month; natgas +6d; crude +5d). rows_for_kind now emits scheduled_for = MODELED RELEASE date, keeps FRED's own date as `reference_period`, sets observed_at to the release instant, and stamps release_date_basis: modeled_lag + release_lag_days. The misleading comment that claimed the reference date WAS the observation instant 'because the expectation used only strictly-prior data' is replaced -- it conflated the EXPECTATION being leakage-safe (true) with the reference date being the RELEASE date (false). STILL UNVERIFIED: the backfill has not been re-run, so the overlap with the forward feed is not yet confirmed non-empty. Do not close until a re-run shows a NON-ZERO join. || VERIFIED END-TO-END 2026-07-30 via the regenerated backfill (issue #8004 -> PR #8005, 6966 rows) + the M3 validator run. Row-level proof: initial_jobless_claims actual=189.0 (THOUSANDS, not 189000), reference_period=1968-06-22 -> scheduled_for=1968-06-27 (+5d, a Thursday), release_date_basis=modeled_lag, units_transform=scale:0.001. cpi_yoy dropped to 905 rows from 917 -- exactly the 12 months yoy_pct_from_level discards for having no prior year, which is the predicted behaviour rather than a loss. M3 NUMBERS, before vs after the two fixes (same model, same survey data, ONLY units + date basis changed): Spearman -0.5982 -> +0.7364; Pearson -0.4629 -> +0.9465; sign agreement 0.455 -> 0.909; OLS slope -49205 -> 1.1288; match offset -5..+2 -> 0/0/0 on every row. The slope near 1 is the load-bearing one: it shows the model's surprises are on the SAME SCALE as the survey's, which correlation alone cannot establish. The old -0.5982 was ENTIRELY artifact and would have read as the M1 gate's kill condition -- i.e. these two defects came within one reading of killing the expectation-model path. M3's verdict remains insufficient_overlap (n=11 < min_honest_n 12) and that stands: the numbers look like a pass but one row short of the pre-registered floor is not a pass, and lowering the floor to reach a verdict is the exact move being eliminated. One more weekly claims release closes it.

items.title: [macro/M1] backfill emits raw FRED units while the survey feed uses the release convention — and `cpi_yoy` is actually the CPI LEVEL
items.description: Blocks M3 independently of the date-key bug: even once the join works, comparing survey-surprise to model-surprise across mismatched units is meaningless. Two DIFFERENT severities here. (a) The claims series differ by a pure SCALE factor (x1000 / x1e6) -- a normalization, mechanical to fix, and note that a scale factor cancels in a CORRELATION but NOT in a slope/magnitude check or in surprise_pct, so it cannot simply be ignored. (b) cpi_yoy is not a scale problem, it is THE WRONG QUANTITY: the backfill emits the CPI index level (332.568) under a kind named `cpi_yoy` while the survey feed emits year-over-year percent (3.5). config/macro_econ_series.yaml even says 'level; YoY derived downstream' -- and nothing downstream derives it. So the backfilled cpi_yoy series is MISLABELED; it is cpi_level. Its 917 rows are not usable as cpi_yoy by anything, and its model expectation is an expectation of the wrong series. FIX: declare a per-kind `units` + `transform` in config (identity / x1e-3 / yoy_pct_from_level) applied in the backfill so emitted rows match the release convention the survey feed uses, and rename or derive cpi_yoy properly. A unit/transform mismatch that silently produces plausible numbers is the same class as the fee over-charge (BL-20260730-RESEARCH-VENUE-FEE) -- wrong scale, right-looking output. || FIX LANDED 2026-07-30, NOT YET RE-RUN. Per-kind `transform` added and applied BEFORE the expectation is fitted -- ordering is load-bearing: fitting on a level and converting afterwards would forecast the wrong series. claims scale:0.001 (persons -> thousands), continuing scale:0.000001 (-> millions), cpi_yoy yoy_pct_from_level (the mislabeled-series fix: it was emitting the CPI INDEX LEVEL under a kind named cpi_yoy). An UNKNOWN transform now RAISES rather than passing raw units through, because a silent pass-through emits plausible numbers in the wrong units -- the bug itself. yoy drops the first `period` observations rather than fabricating a value. Every row records units_transform. 40 tests. STILL UNVERIFIED on a runner. || VERIFIED END-TO-END 2026-07-30 via the regenerated backfill (issue #8004 -> PR #8005, 6966 rows) + the M3 validator run. Row-level proof: initial_jobless_claims actual=189.0 (THOUSANDS, not 189000), reference_period=1968-06-22 -> scheduled_for=1968-06-27 (+5d, a Thursday), release_date_basis=modeled_lag, units_transform=scale:0.001. cpi_yoy dropped to 905 rows from 917 -- exactly the 12 months yoy_pct_from_level discards for having no prior year, which is the predicted behaviour rather than a loss. M3 NUMBERS, before vs after the two fixes (same model, same survey data, ONLY units + date basis changed): Spearman -0.5982 -> +0.7364; Pearson -0.4629 -> +0.9465; sign agreement 0.455 -> 0.909; OLS slope -49205 -> 1.1288; match offset -5..+2 -> 0/0/0 on every row. The slope near 1 is the load-bearing one: it shows the model's surprises are on the SAME SCALE as the survey's, which correlation alone cannot establish. The old -0.5982 was ENTIRELY artifact and would have read as the M1 gate's kill condition -- i.e. these two defects came within one reading of killing the expectation-model path. M3's verdict remains insufficient_overlap (n=11 < min_honest_n 12) and that stands: the numbers look like a pass but one row short of the pre-registered floor is not a pass, and lowering the floor to reach a verdict is the exact move being eliminated. One more weekly claims release closes it.

items.title: [macro/M1] a FIXED release lag cannot join a MONTHLY series — BLS/CPI release day drifts, so the join needs a tolerance window
items.description: Weekly series are safe: DoL/EIA publish on a fixed weekday, so reference + constant lag lands exactly every week (verified -- claims now join). MONTHLY is different: the BLS CPI release falls roughly the 10th-15th of the following month and MOVES, so no single constant hits every month. A fixed lag will join some months and silently miss others, and a partial join looks like a small sample rather than a systematic miss -- the same read-it-wrong failure mode as the rest of this class. FIX: the consumer should join on NEAREST RELEASE WITHIN A TOLERANCE WINDOW (e.g. +/- 5 trading days) instead of exact-date equality, and REPORT the matched offset distribution so a systematic bias is visible rather than absorbed. That belongs in the M3 validator + the event study, not in the backfill (the backfill's job is to emit an honest modeled date; the consumer's job is to match tolerantly). Until then cpi_yoy's contribution to any overlap is unreliable even though 43d happens to hit the one captured month -- do NOT read a cpi_yoy join count as complete. The clean long-term answer is the same one already documented for vintages: ALFRED / the FRED releases API give TRUE release dates and remove the need to model this at all.

items.title: [research] exit-capture-deepdive-2026-07-30 asserts BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=full/'not deployed' — it was ALREADY partial, so its root cause for the scalp exit leak is unproven and the real cause is still unknown
items.source: Deploy-verification session 2026-07-30. docs/research/exit-capture-deepdive-2026-07-30.md states 'BYBIT_TPSL_MODE is at its default full on the live VM' and 'It is not deployed (default full)', and builds its root-cause attribution for the scalp exit leak on that. The new bybit-bracket-audit action (PR #7993) read the live value three ways on 2026-07-30 (issue #7999): .env:81 = partial, the unit's EnvironmentFiles points at that .env, and /proc/<MainPID>/environ = partial (the authoritative source — a set-env writes the FILE while the running process keeps what it started with). _bybit_tpsl_mode() resolves 'partial'. Independently, trades.sl_order_id (written ONLY on the _bybit_tpsl_mode()=='partial' branch of execute_pkg) is non-null on 75 of 211 bybit opens between 07-21 and the 05:37Z flip, across bybit_1, bybit_2 and bybit_portfolio — a non-null PROVES the partial path ran, and the one-off backfill-tpsl-leg-ids (07-21, single trade) cannot explain 75 rows over 9 days. Earliest entry-time capture: #3789 2026-07-21 14:45:59, the day PR #7321 deployed. This matches ROADMAP.md L19 ('FLIPPED live' 2026-07-20) and S-XRP-TPSL-LEGCAP-2026-07-21 ('already partial ... per the earlier PR #7115 rollout').
items.description: TWO problems, the second is the expensive one. (1) DOC DRIFT: the memo's premise is false and it is the document a future session will read to understand the exit leak, so it must be corrected in place (not deleted — it is the record of a real measurement; the MFE/giveback/round-tripper numbers stand, only the CAUSE attribution is wrong). (2) THE REAL CAUSE IS STILL UNKNOWN: because the memo blamed BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=full, today's 05:37Z set-env flip was dispatched as the fix (issues #7945 gate + #7946 flip) — but it was a no-op re-assertion of an already-active value, so NOTHING was actually changed and the leak is unaddressed. The leak is real and measured: in the 7 days BEFORE the flip, bybit scalp closes were 37 trades / -$6,358.37 with only 2 of 37 (5%) exiting via a clean broker bracket — exit_reason was reconciler_filled on 28 of them carrying essentially the whole loss (-$6,360.46), vs tp n=1 (+$5.35) and sl n=1 (-$3.26). And it persisted straight THROUGH the days when partial-mode leg capture was demonstrably running, which is what rules the mode out as the cause. The single best evidence is trade #4218 (ict_scalp_avax_5m, bybit_1) opened 05:44:22Z — 7 min AFTER the flip, WITH both legs captured at entry (sl 58e24253, tp 610837ec) — which still held 1h56m (a 5-MINUTE scalp) and exited reconciler_filled. ACTION: correct the memo, then re-derive the cause from the reconciler_filled exit path itself (why is the broker bracket not producing a clean tp/sl journal exit, and is reconciler_filled even the expected recording for a broker-side Bybit SL fire?) rather than from the bracket-scope env var.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) docs/research/exit-capture-deepdive-2026-07-30.md corrected: the BYBIT_TPSL_MODE claim fixed and the root-cause section reopened as unresolved, with a pointer to the audit receipts (issue #7999); (b) a re-derived, evidence-backed cause for the reconciler_filled-dominated scalp exits, or an explicit finding that reconciler_filled IS the normal recording for a broker-side Bybit bracket fire (in which case the real defect is the hold time, not the exit reason); (c) ROADMAP/L19 vs the memo reconciled so the next session cannot re-derive the wrong premise.

items.title: [db] trades.created_at and trades.closed_at use DIFFERENT timestamp formats in the same table — string comparisons across them silently return wrong rows
items.source: Deploy-verification session 2026-07-30, found by being bitten by it. Live rows on trade #4218: created_at = '2026-07-30 05:44:22' (space-separated, no offset) while closed_at = '2026-07-30T07:40:36.498032+00:00' (ISO 'T' + microseconds + offset). Because ' ' (0x20) sorts BELOW 'T' (0x54), any SQL string comparison of a space-separated column against a 'T'-separated literal silently excludes every row: `created_at >= '2026-07-30T05:37'` matched ZERO of today's rows and made a read report '0 opens since the flip' when there were 5. Same class of error is the likely cause of scripts/research/m20_exit_analysis.py reporting journal_latest_close = 2026-07-30T00:57:54 while #4218 demonstrably closed at 07:40:36 — a verified 0 of 67 closed rows since 07-25 have a NULL closed_at, so the under-report is a parse/compare artifact, not missing data.
items.description: This is a silent-wrong-answer generator, not a crash: every consumer that windows or sorts on these columns can quietly drop rows, and the result looks like a small sample rather than a systematic miss. The repo already has scar tissue from exactly this shape — src/web/api/_closed_at.py exists because the reconciler-filled close path writes closed_at as a raw epoch-ms string that an unguarded datetime() drops from the window (the '0 closed trades in 24h while lifetime is non-zero' bug). So there are now at least THREE closed_at encodings in the wild (space-separated, ISO T+offset, raw epoch-ms) and the normalisation lives in one API helper rather than at the writer. INVESTIGATE: enumerate the distinct formats actually present per column (a cheap GROUP BY on shape), identify which writers emit which, then decide between normalising AT THE WRITER (one canonical encoding, plus a migration for existing rows — note migrate-closed-at-iso already exists as a system-action) or making the _closed_at.py normaliser the mandatory read path for every consumer and guarding new raw comparisons in CI. Do NOT hand-fix rows without first establishing which writers produce which format, or it will drift back. || CROSS-CHECK 2026-07-30 (research session, code-level — NOT a live reproduction): the CORE finding is CONFIRMED and reproduced — as strings, '2026-07-30 05:44:22' >= '2026-07-30T05:37:00' evaluates FALSE, so a raw SQL comparison of a space-separated column against a 'T' literal does silently exclude rows exactly as described. BUT the sub-hypothesis that this explains m20_exit_analysis.py's under-reported journal_latest_close is REFUTED: (a) that script's `_epoch` was tested against all four encodings actually in the wild -- space-separated CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, ISO T+micros+offset, ISO+Z, and raw epoch-ms -- and parses ALL FOUR correctly, ordering them correctly once parsed (verified with the exact #4218 values from this row); and (b) `journal_latest_close` is a Python max() over already-parsed floats, so there is no SQL string comparison anywhere in that path. The LIVE hypothesis for that specific under-report is therefore the sibling row BL-20260730-TRAINER-JOURNAL-PULL-STALE: m20_exit_analysis defaults --db to `data/trade_journal.db`, i.e. the TRAINER's synced copy, measured ~15-16h stale the same day. A stale mirror does not mis-parse recent rows -- it does not CONTAIN them, which also fits the observation that 0 of 67 closed rows since 07-25 have a NULL closed_at. WHY THIS MATTERS: the two hypotheses imply DIFFERENT fixes (normalise at the writer + guard raw comparisons in CI, vs. never point a recent-window read at the trainer mirror), so attributing the symptom to the wrong one would leave the real cause live -- the same shape as this session's own BL-20260730-EXITCAPTURE-DEEPDIVE-WRONG-TPSL-PREMISE, where a plausible nearby cause was fixed and the actual leak went unaddressed. TO SETTLE IT with one command: re-run m20_exit_analysis with --db pointed at a FRESH journal copy and compare journal_latest_close; if it then matches live, staleness was the cause. The freshness field is now self-judging (journal_age_hours / journal_stale / a loud ::warning::, --max-journal-age-hours default 6) so a stale mirror can no longer present as 'nothing closed recently'. The writer-side normalisation question this row raises is UNAFFECTED by the above and still stands on its own merits.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) the distinct timestamp encodings present in trades.created_at / closed_at enumerated with counts, and each mapped to its writing code path; (b) a decision recorded (writer-side canonicalisation + migration, or mandatory read-side normalisation) and implemented; (c) m20_exit_analysis.py's journal_latest_close verified to agree with the newest closed_at in the DB; (d) if read-side normalisation is chosen, a CI guard against new raw string comparisons on these columns.

updates.note: A+B SHIPPED — PR #8397 (merged 2026-08-02). A: scripts/check_timestamp_comparisons.py CI guard (whole-tree, fails-closed) + fixed 8 raw comparisons (2 FROM-trades sites in insights/data_sources.py were the live bug dropping every trades row). B: insert_trade now stamps ISO created_at (stops new space-sep rows); migrate_closed_at_to_iso gained an opt-in --include-created-at pass. Live census (trainer-diag #8398): created_at 4319/4319 space-separated, closed_at ISO except 1 epoch-ms straggler, is_backtest=0 on all rows. Consider closing once the migration runs.

items.title: [pnl] a reconciler_filled Bybit close can land with exit_price = NULL AND pnl = NULL — the trade is closed and we do not know at what price or for how much money
items.source: Deploy-verification session 2026-07-30. Trade #4218 (bybit_1, AVAXUSDT, ict_scalp_avax_5m, qty 21971.2, entry 6.463) closed at 2026-07-30T07:40:36 with exit_reason='reconciler_filled', and BOTH exit_price and pnl are NULL. notes records closed_by='monitor_reconciler', closed_reason='reconciler — Bybit reports order filled and position flat', and — the tell — exit_price_source='entry_order_avg_price_unreliable'. So the close path knew it could not trust the price it had and recorded nothing rather than something wrong (honest, and better than a fabricated number) — but it then left the money unmeasured with no follow-up.
items.description: Being honest about an unknown is right; leaving it permanently unknown is not. A closed trade with NULL pnl is invisible to every dollar aggregate (the P&L scoreboard is DOLLARS per the 2026-07-30 doctrine), so this silently shrinks the denominator of exactly the exit-capture measurement the exits work depends on. There IS already a backfill path for this class — order_monitor._sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced fills non-Bybit realised PnL via local compute — but Bybit is the venue that HAS broker truth (clients.BROKER_PNL_READER_EXCHANGES = {bybit}), so the right resolution is probably to read the actual fill back from Bybit (get_closed_pnl / the exchange-fills store, which scripts/pull_exchange_fills.py already populates and /api/bot/pnl/exchange already serves) rather than to local-compute it. INVESTIGATE: how many closed rows carry NULL pnl and/or NULL exit_price, per account and per exit_reason (is #4218 one instance or a standing population?); whether the reconciler_filled path can always resolve a fill price from the exchange-fills store after the fact; and whether a closed row with NULL pnl should raise an operator signal instead of settling silently.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) a count of closed non-backtest rows with NULL pnl and/or NULL exit_price, broken out by account and exit_reason, so the size of the population is known rather than assumed; (b) #4218's dollars recovered from exchange truth (or a stated, evidenced reason they cannot be); (c) a decision on whether the reconciler_filled close path should resolve price from the exchange-fills store before recording NULL; (d) a signal (not silence) when a close settles with unmeasured money.

updates.note: RESOLVED by weekly /system-review evidence pass: #8069 exit-anchor three-way contract (anchored/deferred/no_anchor): NULL rows are retried or explicitly UNMEASURED, never silently permanent (src/runtime/exit_anchor.py::bar_close_at).

items.title: [bybit] bybit_1 XRPUSDT resting SL legs are DIVERGING from the position, not merely stale — 444.7% -> 830% over-coverage in 41 minutes, with the remediation still unbuilt
items.source: Live receipts, same day. bybit-bracket-audit at 2026-07-30T11:48Z: bybit_1 XRPUSDT position 32557.2, resting SL legs 58686.8 + 86102.5 = 144789.3 (444.7%). The #8000 monitor sweep at 12:29:55Z on live HEAD dd07b45f: 'LEG OVER-ACCUMULATION bybit_1/XRPUSDT — position size=17438.9 but resting SL legs total 144789.3 (830%) across 2 leg(s)'. The leg total is byte-identical across both reads; the POSITION halved. So the legs are not tracking the position at all.
items.description: This is the leg-accumulation failure mode of BL-20260721-BYBIT2-XRP-TPSL-LEGCAP observed mid-drift rather than as a static snapshot, and it is getting worse on its own. Because Bybit Partial-mode set_trading_stop is ADD-only, a leg that outlives the qty it was sized for is never reduced when the position shrinks — so any partial close widens the gap. At 830%, the first leg to trip would close roughly 3.4x the live position: it over-closes, flips the sign of the exposure, and strands the remaining legs against a position that no longer exists. PR #8000 detects this (that is where these numbers come from) but deliberately does NOT remediate — detection was in scope, de-accumulation was not. The detector now proves the condition is live, escalating, and unattended. Scope is bybit_1 (paper), so no real money is at risk today; bybit_2 (real money) audited clean at 11:48Z. That is the only reason this is not a P1.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) the one-off cancel-stale-tpsl-legs system-action is run against bybit_1 XRPUSDT and a follow-up bybit-bracket-audit shows coverage back within the 0.5% epsilon of position size, AND a structural fix keeps it there (close/reduce cancels or amends the leg it sized, so coverage tracks the position); or (b) an explicit, recorded decision that add-only leg drift is acceptable on paper accounts, with the real-money guard named. Detection alone does not close this item.

updates.note: ACUTE STATE CLEARED, item kept open on the structural half. cancel-stale-tpsl-legs dry-run (#8269) aborted: bybit_1 XRPUSDT is now FLAT (size=0), so the action is out of scope (it collapses legs on a LIVE position) and the position-scoped over_covered detector no longer fires. Read-only bybit-bracket-audit (#8270) confirms XRPUSDT FLAT with ZERO stranded resting conditional legs and a clean roll-up (0 naked, 0 over-covered) — the over-accumulated legs were cancelled by Bybit when the position flattened. So resolution_criteria (a) 'coverage back within epsilon' is met NOW, but the STRUCTURAL half ('a fix keeps it there for untracked/pre-#7321 rows on the next live position') is not verified, and add-only drift can recur on the next bybit_1 XRP position from an untracked row. No apply was needed. Left open for the review skills to decide (a)-with-structural-fix vs (b) record add-only paper-account drift as acceptable with the real-money guard named (bybit_2 audited clean; the structural leg-id fix #7321 covers post-fix trades).

Re-validated: bybit_1 (demo/paper) still shows large journal/exchange divergence (exchange ADA 258303, BNB/SOL/ETH/BTC positions). Over-accum/divergence class persists; detect-only signals in place, remediation Tier-2. No real-money exposure (bybit_1 is demo). Keep open.

Operator-approved dry-run of cancel-stale-tpsl-legs on bybit_1/XRPUSDT (#8518) returned action:abort_flat — 'live XRPUSDT position on bybit_1 is flat (size=0) - out of scope for this script; nothing to protect', and /api/diag/exchange_positions (#8517) confirms bybit_1 now holds ADA/BTC/ETH/BNB/SOL and NO XRP. items.title: [audit] bybit_bracket_audit.py prints 'every audited symbol is fully SL-covered at the broker' directly beneath a 444.7% over-coverage — an all-clear over a live anomaly
items.source: scripts/ops/bybit_bracket_audit.py (added in PR #7993), run 2026-07-30T11:48Z via the bybit-bracket-audit system-action (issue #8009). The body reported 'bybit_1 XRPUSDT ... SL coverage: 144789.3 / 32557.2 qty (444.7%) ... uncovered=0.0' and the ROLL-UP then printed 'every audited symbol is fully SL-covered at the broker.'
items.description: The roll-up is derived solely from uncovered qty, so over-coverage satisfies it: 444.7% covered is not under-covered, therefore 'fully covered', therefore all-clear. Both statements are individually true and the composite reads as 'nothing to see here' on the one account that had the worst anomaly of the run. This is the normalization failure mode the see-something-say-something directive names as a bug in its own right: a reader who trusts the summary line — which is the point of a summary line — walks straight past a live 830%-and-climbing leg pile-up (see BL-20260730-BYBIT1-XRP-LEG-OVERACCUM-WORSENING). Note this is NOT fixed by PR #8000: #8000 added over_covered/journal_qty_divergent to the order_monitor SWEEP, a different code path. The standalone audit script — the thing an operator actually runs and reads — still summarises as all-clear.
items.resolution_criteria: The roll-up distinguishes 'covered' from 'correctly covered': a symbol whose SL legs exceed the position beyond the over-cover factor, or whose open journal qty exceeds the broker position beyond the divergence fraction, must break the all-clear line and be named in the roll-up. Reuse the thresholds already in order_monitor (_BYBIT_OVERCOVER_FACTOR, _BYBIT_QTY_DIVERGENCE_FRAC) rather than introducing a second set. A regression test should assert the roll-up does NOT read all-clear for the 144789.3-vs-32557.2 case.

updates.note: RESOLVED by weekly /system-review evidence pass: Roll-up buckets over-coverage separately; all-clear requires coverage within [100%, cap] with 0 naked + 0 over-covered (scripts/ops/bybit_bracket_audit.py:264-277,454-457).

items.title: [diag-relay] vm-diag-snapshot parses the issue BODY line-by-line as paths, so any prose in the body hard-fails the run with a misleading 'illegal characters in resolved path'
items.source: Three failed runs in one session, 2026-07-30. Issue #8010 (body = a JSON array plus explanatory prose) failed with 'Rejected diag path ["/api/diag/journalctl?...", "..."]: illegal characters in resolved path'. Issue #8012 (body = a single explanatory paragraph, path correctly in the title) failed with the same error naming the PARAGRAPH as the rejected path. #8013 succeeded only once the body was reduced to bare path lines and the context moved to a comment.
items.description: The documented pattern is a '[diag-request] <path>' TITLE, which invites the reasonable assumption that the body is free text for context. It is not: the body is parsed as the path list, and the title is consulted only when the body is empty or unparsable. So adding a sentence of context — or the mandatory Claude Code attribution footer — silently converts a valid request into a failed run. The error message compounds it by reporting 'illegal characters in resolved path', which reads as a malformed PATH and sends the next session hunting the query string (it cost this session one wrong diagnosis: the array literal was blamed before #8012 proved it was prose in general). Two cheap fixes: state the rule where people look, and make the error say what is actually wrong.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) docs/claude/diag-relay.md states explicitly that for a multi-path request the body must contain ONLY paths, one per line — no JSON, no prose, no attribution footer — and that context belongs in a follow-up comment; (b) the workflow's rejection message distinguishes 'this line does not look like a diag path (did you put prose in the body? context goes in a comment)' from a genuinely malformed path. Either half alone is a partial fix.

updates.note: RESOLVED by weekly /system-review evidence pass: vm-diag-snapshot accepts prose/bulleted/JSON bodies with title fallback; prose hard-fail gone (vm-diag-snapshot.yml:27-29,410-427). Live-verified by this session's batched requests.

items.title: [deploy] install_systemd_units.sh:407 redirects to /dev/null, so an OCI-agent 0444 window makes 'systemctl enable --now' a no-op that reports nothing
items.source: pull-and-deploy 2026-07-30T11:42Z (issue #8008) logged 'install_systemd_units.sh: line 407: /dev/null: Permission denied' six times while enabling timers. ict-devnull-guard.service is healthy — running and finishing cleanly every ~60s (#8013) — and its own unit description names the cause: 'OCI agent resets it to 0444, breaking >/dev/null for the trader + auto-deploy'.
items.description: In bash a failed redirection aborts the command before it executes, so each of those six 'systemctl enable --now <timer> >/dev/null' calls did not merely lose its output — it did not run. IMPORTANT, so nobody re-chases this as an outage: it caused NO harm on this deploy. /api/diag/services (#8015) confirms ict-db-integrity.timer, ict-exchange-fills-pull.timer, ict-exchange-funding-pull.timer, ict-health-snapshot.timer and ict-devnull-guard.timer are all active — they were already enabled, so the skipped call was a no-op regardless. (ict-ib-gateway-watchdog.timer reads inactive, which is correct: gateway-only, and the trader's role is unset.) The latent bug is the case that has not happened yet: a genuine FIRST-time enable of a new timer landing inside a 0444 window would be skipped silently, the deploy would report success, and the new scheduled job would simply never run — discoverable only by noticing its absence.
items.resolution_criteria: install_systemd_units.sh no longer makes command execution contingent on a writable /dev/null for these enables — e.g. drop the redirect, or guard it so a redirect failure cannot swallow the command — and a failed enable is surfaced rather than silent. Bonus: have the deploy assert /dev/null is a 0666 char device up front and re-assert (the guard's own logic) instead of racing it.
items.resolved_by: claude (backlog-cont session 170lwv) — re-resolved after the 2026-08-01 partial fix recurred; see the updates trail

updates.note: RESOLVED by weekly /system-review evidence pass: Enable loop captures 2>&1 + WARNs (install_systemd_units.sh:407-414); /dev/null clobber class separately belted (heal_devnull + ict-devnull-guard.timer, active on the VM per #8236 services read).

REOPENED — recurred on the 2026-08-02 pull-and-deploy (#8330). The 2026-08-01 resolution was PARTIAL: it de-/dev/null'd the `enable --now` OUTPUT (install_systemd_units.sh, now :435) but LEFT the is-enabled/is-active IDEMPOTENCY CHECK (now :430) redirecting to /dev/null — which spammed `line 430: /dev/null: Permission denied` ~15x — and never touched the three sibling scripts (deploy_pull_restart.sh :334/:388/:403/:468/:492/:535, pull_and_deploy.sh :88/:95, run_research_results_gate.sh :21/:25/:32). REAL damage this time, not cosmetic: the deploy marker deployed_sha.txt went unwritten (its own `2>/dev/null` EACCESed → 'could not write deploy marker' → redeploy drift, BL-20260714), Post-deploy HEAD read 'unknown', unit enumeration degraded to the 3-unit canonical fallback, and ict-research-results-gate.service latched `failed` (its `>/dev/null` reporter died on the clobber; journal #8336). Root: the strip lands MID-RUN (healthy at entry → the entry-only [ -w ] repair no-op'd) and the 60s ict-devnull-guard belt can't heal inside a ~12s deploy. Lesson: the 2026-08-01 'evidence pass' resolved on the enable-line grep without checking the is-enabled line or the sibling scripts — a premature resolution. FIX (this session's deploy /dev/null-hardening PR): a re-callable two-variant heal_devnull() invoked before EACH load-bearing redirect across all four scripts (chmod fixes mode-strip, rm+mknod fixes regular-file clobber; cheap when healthy). Tier-2 (live-VM deploy path) — operator-gated. Do NOT re-close until a real pull-and-deploy shows ZERO `/dev/null: Permission denied`, a written marker, non-'unknown' Post-deploy HEAD, full unit enumeration, and a green ict-research-results-gate.service.

RESOLVED + LIVE-VERIFIED. Fix merged in PR #8338 (Tier-2, operator-approved) and deployed via pull-and-deploy #8339. The clobber DID recur mid-deploy — the log shows exactly one `install_systemd_units: /dev/null not writable (host-agent clobber) — self-healing` line — and heal_devnull healed it, after which EVERY previously-failing site succeeded: ZERO `/dev/null: Permission denied`, `Recorded deploy marker: ab481db`, `Post-deploy HEAD: ab481db9…` (non-unknown), full `enumeration: 20 ict-* unit(s)` (not the 3-unit fallback), and `restarted ict-research-results-gate.service` → status `inactive` (clean oneshot exit, not failed). Live diag #8343 confirms ict-research-results-gate.service `inactive` (latch cleared) + NO service `failed`. Every one of the reopen's re-close criteria met. Fix = a re-callable two-variant heal_devnull() before each load-bearing redirect in deploy_pull_restart.sh (entry + unit-refresh + enumeration + status + version-assertion loop + both marker writes), install_systemd_units.sh (entry + per enable-loop iteration + claude-bridge), pull_and_deploy.sh (post-deploy verify + poll), run_research_results_gate.sh (sources _lib.sh; before its own >/dev/null). Residual (separate, deeper): the OCI oci-wlp FIM /dev/null clobber at the SOURCE — BL-20260629-DEVNULL-OCI-SOURCE-KILL.

items.title: [macro/M1] the event study REPORTED a stale natgas scorecard while its own n=1349 results were discarded
items.description: TWO leftovers from the two-energy-kind era that my kind-parameterization did not follow through on. Both fixed; filed because the failure SHAPE is the day's recurring one and I nearly mis-reported it. (1) The summary step hardcoded `json.load('comms/macro/econ_event_study_scorecard.json')` and labelled it `natgas`. That file was NOT regenerated by a run over other kinds, so the comment published a PREVIOUS run's n=6 natgas verdict as though it were this run's result -- a plausible, decision-shaped, completely wrong report over a correct run. Now summarizes the kinds EES_KINDS actually names, resolving each kind's own scorecard path. (2) commit-to-main's `paths:` were hardcoded to the two energy scorecards, so the three per-kind scorecards this run wrote were never committed -- the action logged 'nothing to commit -- no PR opened' and the real results survived only in the run log. Now globbed. LESSON: I diagnosed 'the parameterization was ignored' from the comment and was WRONG -- the log showed the run had been correct all along. Verify a run from its LOG, not from the artifact it chose to report; a reporting step is as capable of being scoped-wrong as a producer. HONEST RESULT of that run, now recoverable: all three kinds `no_edge_at_tested_horizons` -- claims |t| <= 1.57 across every horizon at n=1349, cpi_yoy strongest +0.1064 IC at H=1 with t=1.876 (below the t=2 flag) at n=309. A clean measured null at real n, which is a stronger result than the same null at n=6.

items.source: M3 first real verdict at n=1263 after the FXStreet survey backfill (#8024/#8025). Pooled: Spearman 0.5885 / sign agreement 0.720 / slope 0.9335 -> model_tracks_survey (bars 0.50 / 0.70). PER KIND: initial_jobless_claims 0.6312/0.791 slope 0.936 TRACKS (n=586); cpi_yoy 0.5176/0.753 slope 1.364 TRACKS (n=127); continuing_jobless_claims 0.4239/0.640 slope 0.5234 DOES NOT TRACK (n=550).
items.title: [macro/M3] the pooled M3 pass is carried by 2 of 3 kinds — the model expectation does NOT track survey consensus for continuing_jobless_claims
items.description: The M1 gate's option-(b) satisfiability condition PASSES pooled, but the pass is not uniform and the failing kind is 550 of 1263 pairs. continuing_jobless_claims misses BOTH pre-registered bars individually (Spearman 0.4239 < 0.50, sign agreement 0.640 < 0.70) CORRECTION (same day, before this row was acted on): the OLS slope of 0.5234 was first written up here as 'the model surprise is roughly HALF the survey surprise in magnitude -- a scale error'. THAT IS WRONG and it pointed at the wrong fix. slope = pearson x sd(model)/sd(survey), so it conflates correlation with scale. Measured: sd(model)=0.4258 vs sd(survey)=0.3126, i.e. the model surprises are MORE dispersed (ratio 1.362), and the sub-unit slope is WEAK CORRELATION (pearson ~0.384), not compression. The validator now reports dispersion_ratio (scale only) and rmse_model/rmse_survey (accuracy) so the slope cannot be misread this way again. CONSEQUENCE: any M1/M2 consumer that uses the MODEL expectation as a stand-in for survey consensus on continuing claims is measuring a systematically undersized surprise. Do not read the pooled `model_tracks_survey` as licence for that kind; the validator now names it in `kinds_not_tracking` and in the rendered note. WHAT THIS IS NOT: it is not a reason to lower a bar or to re-pool. The bars were pre-registered before the first run and the pooled rule was deliberately left unchanged when the per-kind split was added, so the goalposts have not moved. NEXT: (a) investigate the 0.52 slope — continuing claims is a LEVEL series with strong autocorrelation, so the seasonal-AR expectation may be over-smoothing (a period/harmonics question in econ_expectation, testable offline against the 550 pairs already committed); (b) until it tracks, prefer the real survey consensus for this kind and treat model-expectation rows for it as unusable. A NOTE ON READING THE SCORECARD: mean_abs_gap CANNOT rank kinds (it is in each kind's own units) — that column made initial_jobless_claims look like the weak kind (gap 26.6) when it is the STRONGEST tracker, while continuing claims has the SMALLEST gap (0.11) and the worst tracking. Use the scale-free columns. || THE BIGGER FINDING, which the pooled pass concealed and which the correlation bars never test: the MODEL EXPECTATION IS A WORSE PREDICTOR THAN THE SURVEY ON ALL THREE KINDS. Since surprise = actual - expectation, the RMSE of a surprise series is that expectation's own error against what happened: initial_jobless_claims model 227.62 vs survey 174.62 (1.304x), continuing_jobless_claims 0.4261 vs 0.3137 (1.358x), cpi_yoy 0.3526 vs 0.1354 (2.603x). So option (b) is not merely 'noisier on one kind' -- it is a strictly worse expectation than the survey everywhere both exist, worst by far on CPI. This does NOT overturn the gate as written (the gate asks whether model-surprise TRACKS survey-surprise, and pooled it does), but it bounds what a downstream M1/M2 result may claim: an edge measured against model surprises is measured against a noisier yardstick than the market's own, so a null is weaker evidence of no-edge than it looks. It also kills the tempting alternative reading of continuing claims -- 'the model beats the survey on a smooth autocorrelated series, so M3 is just measuring survey noise'. It does not beat it anywhere. PROPOSED NEXT (offline, no runner): the CPI 2.6x gap is the biggest and CPI is the kind with the fewest pairs and a real release-date drift, so start there -- check whether yoy_pct_from_level plus the modeled_lag join is degrading the CPI expectation before touching the seasonal-AR parameterization for claims.

items.title: [macro/M3] the M3 validator read ONE of its two survey sources — a join proven in a runner was never wired into the tool that reads out the verdict
items.description: RECORDED AS A PATTERN, not just a fix. The runner and the tool disagreed about what the survey side IS, and the tool is the one that publishes the verdict — so the published verdict was insufficient_overlap at n=11 while 1,263 joinable rows sat committed in the repo. Nothing errored: read_rows is FileNotFound-tolerant and the missing file simply was not named, so the tool measured a fraction of the available data and graded it. Same family as BL-20260730-M1-PRICE-JOIN-DEAD (a verdict published over an input that was not there), one layer up. FIXED IN THIS CHANGE: DEFAULT_SURVEY is now a LIST of both sources; --survey takes nargs=+; the report records survey_paths / survey_rows_by_path / survey_paths_missing, and an absent declared path emits a warning so 'the file is not there' can never present as 'the overlap is thin'; the artifact is registered with check_artifact_validity (report.n_overlap >= 1); and the survey-backfill workflow now RE-READS M3 in the same run that changes n, so the verdict cannot sit at a stale n behind a comment telling a human to re-run it. GENERAL LESSON worth carrying: when a runner has to hand-assemble inputs to demonstrate a result, that assembly is missing from the tool.

items.title: [macro/M1][gate] the operator-approved M1 gate tests whether the model TRACKS the survey, not whether it is USEFUL — and the best-tracking kind is worse than a random walk
items.description: OPERATOR DECISION NEEDED — this is about the gate's wording, which the operator approved, so it is not mine to change. THE FINDING: M3's pre-registered bars ask whether model-surprise tracks survey-surprise. `initial_jobless_claims` PASSES them most convincingly of all three kinds (Spearman 0.6312, sign agreement 0.791) and is SIMULTANEOUSLY the one kind whose model expectation is FURTHER from the outcome than 'assume no change since last release' (1.101x worse RMSE). The other two clear the naive floor only narrowly (0.906x, 0.952x). So the gate as written can be satisfied by an expectation model that adds no information at all, and on one kind demonstrably does not. WHY BOTH CAN BE TRUE: tracking is about the CORRELATION of two error series; the naive floor is about the MAGNITUDE of one of them. A model that errs in the same direction as the survey, but by more, tracks well and predicts badly. Nothing in the gate's bars separates those. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT INVALIDATE: it does NOT invalidate the M3 measurement (the verdict is honest about what it measured) and it does NOT retroactively break the gate change. It DOES bound every downstream M1/M2 claim: a surprise computed against the model is computed against a yardstick that is noisier than the survey everywhere and worse than no-model on initial claims, so a NULL result (which is what the full-scale event study returned: no_edge_at_tested_horizons at n=1349) is much weaker evidence of no-edge than it appears. MITIGATED IN TOOLING (not in the gate): the validator now computes rmse_naive / rmse_ratio_model_over_naive / model_beats_naive per kind, lists kinds_worse_than_naive next to the verdict, and renders a loud block, so a tracking pass can never again be read as usefulness. PROPOSED (operator call): add a floor condition to the gate — a kind may only use the MODEL surprise where the model beats the naive random walk on that kind — which would today exclude initial_jobless_claims. THE BETTER ALTERNATIVE, now cheap: 12,076 survey rows exist, so for the overlap period the study can use REAL survey consensus and skip the stand-in entirely; the model is then only needed OUTSIDE the survey window. That converts the weakest part of the macro line into its strongest.
