items.title: [pnl] paper/demo Bybit realised PnL is entry-vs-mark-6h-later, not realised PnL -- fabricates the entire 'scalp exit leak'
items.source: trainer-diag #8035/#8036/#8038 against /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/data/trade_journal.db (max_created 2026-07-30 08:38).
items.description: CAUSAL CHAIN, evidenced end-to-end. (1) clients.py:884 `if is_demo: return None` (landed 2026-06-25 #4503, correct fix for BL-20260608-DEMOPNL record mis-mapping) makes account_closed_pnl_for_trade return None for EVERY demo account -- bybit_1 and bybit_portfolio both carry `demo: true`. (2) order_monitor._close_trade_from_order_status therefore always takes the fallback branch (:5664): exit_price NULL, notes.exit_price_source='entry_order_avg_price_unreliable', exit_reason hard-coded 'reconciler_filled'. (3) _classify_broker_exit (2026-06-23) can only label sl/tp FROM that recovered exit price, so on demo the sl/tp label is structurally unreachable -- the two changes landed 2 days apart and the second silently disabled the first for demo. (4) 6h later (_LOCAL_PNL_BROKER_DEFER_MS) _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced (:7381) substitutes last_mark_price() -- the CURRENT market price, 6+h after the actual exit -- as exit_price and books pnl from it, stamping exit_price_source='local_markprice'. RECEIPTS: 38 of 39 bybit_1 reconciler_filled rows (7d) are local_markprice carrying -$8,209.89; the 1 exception is trade 4218, closed 07:40:36 and still inside the 6h defer at snapshot time with exit_price/pnl both NULL -- the same mechanism caught mid-flight. MATCHED-PAIR PROOF (bybit_portfolio is the paper mirror of bybit_2 -- same strategy/symbol/bracket/minute): trade 4180 bybit_2 exit 64100.0 vs sl 64110.32 = -$4.00 (bybit_closed_pnl) while its mirror 4181 booked exit 63486.2 = -$2,589.78 (local_markprice); trade 3909 bybit_2 exit 64962.0 vs sl 64960.32 labelled 'sl' = -$3.26 while mirror 3910 booked 65104.5 = -$1,434.99. Same trade, same stop, ~650x the loss. IMPACT: the operator-visible '7d bybit scalps -$6,358' is ~-$6,297 of demo mark-price artifact (bybit_1 -$2,272.10 + bybit_portfolio -$4,024.78) against -$1.91 of actual real-money scalp PnL on bybit_2. Paper is the ML training signal, so every model learning exit quality from these rows is learning a 6h-forward random walk. NOT a real-money loss and NOT an order-path defect. FIX DIRECTION (Tier-2, NOT applied): a CONFIRMED CLOSE must never be priced from a live mark -- either anchor the exit to a candle at closed_at, or leave pnl NULL behind an explicit 'unmeasured' marker. Interacts with the INV-2 closed-with-NULL-pnl invariant, which is why the sweep exists; that interaction must be designed, not patched.

items.title: [data-integrity] the journal records whether each number was MEASURED or FABRICATED, and every consumer ignores it -- 64.9% of July closed trades carry a fabricated exit price
items.source: trainer-diag #8040 (provenance audit over /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/data/trade_journal.db) + static analysis of exit_price_source/pnl_source consumers.
items.description:
THIS IS THE STRUCTURAL DEFECT BEHIND THE REPEATED 'audited it again and still found bugs' CYCLE. It is not one bug; it is the shape all of them share.

FINDING 1 -- provenance is write-only. `exit_price_source` is WRITTEN in 12 files (order_monitor, clients, 8 ops backfill scripts, json_notes, a research script) and READ in exactly ONE place: order_monitor.py:1001, which tests for 'verdict', an unrelated internal value. NOTHING downstream branches on it -- not /performance, not _clean_trades, not the report renderer, not monitor_miss_analysis.py. `pnl_source` likewise: the only branch found is on UNREALIZED pnl in dashboard.py:353. The entire ml/ tree contains ZERO references to exit_price_source, pnl_source or local_markprice -- the training pipeline is structurally blind to whether a label was measured or manufactured.

FINDING 2 -- the blast radius, lifetime, non-backtest closed rows: local_markprice/local_compute = 226 rows carrying +$247,683.78; a further 247 rows carry NO provenance key at all (-$37,785.32); measured bybit_closed_pnl = 328 rows (-$8,174.77). By account_class: PAPER shows FABRICATED_mark 210 rows = +$247,657.43 against measured 183 rows = -$14,968.68 -- i.e. the paper book's headline profitability is an artifact of mark-price arithmetic, not trading. REAL_MONEY is largely clean (187 measured / 12 fabricated), so live decisions are mostly safe; the ML trains on paper.

FINDING 3 -- it is accelerating: fabricated share of closed trades ran 2026-05 = 0/397 (0.0%), 2026-06 = 61/200 (30.5%, +$286,199.61), 2026-07 = 161/248 (64.9%, -$38,515.83). Onset coincides with _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced (2026-06-16) and accelerates after the demo closed-pnl guard (#4503, 2026-06-25). TWO THIRDS of July's training corpus has a fabricated exit price.

FINDING 4 -- why audits keep missing it. Each fill is individually CORRECT and individually justified by a real prior incident, so no line of code is wrong and line-by-line review returns clean. Worse, INV-2 (closed-with-NULL-pnl is a violation) actively PRESSURES the system to fill every hole: the invariant enforces that a number exists and never checks what kind of number it is. And when sessions do hit fabricated data they patch it per-species with a bespoke heuristic instead of reading the provenance field -- src/web/api/_clean_trades.py's docstring literally calls trend_donchian rows 2604/2607/2610 'a fabricated win/loss' and then excludes them by setup_type, not by provenance. There are now four such predicates (exclude_reduce_leg / reconciler / superseded / reset_flat), one per incident.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY FIX THE CLASS (not applied -- Tier-2/3, needs design): make provenance a first-class, typed, QUERYABLE column rather than a JSON note; have every decision surface (/performance, the ML label builders, the three review skills, the report renderer) declare whether it accepts fabricated inputs and report the measured/fabricated split alongside every aggregate; and make INV-2 satisfiable by an explicit 'unmeasured' terminal state so the invariant stops forcing fabrication.
items.next_action: Operator decision on scope. Do NOT tune any strategy, exit, or promotion gate on paper PnL until the measured/fabricated split is surfaced -- the last two months of paper training signal is majority-fabricated.

items.title: [data-integrity] sibling sweep: 5 of 9 quality/provenance signals are WRITE-ONLY, and the ML pipeline consumes none of them
items.source: Static consumer sweep over src/ scripts/ ml/ (2026-07-30), generalising BL-20260730-PROVENANCE-RECORDED-THEN-IGNORED.
items.description:
Counting writers vs value-branches vs ml/ refs vs src/web/api refs for every known data-quality signal:

  exit_price_source   writes~14 branches~1(unrelated) ml=0 api=0   WRITE-ONLY
  close_exec_type     writes~1  branches~0            ml=0 api=0   WRITE-ONLY
  fc_present          writes~2  branches~0            ml=0 api=0   WRITE-ONLY
  exit_reason_source  writes~3  branches~0            ml=0 api=0   WRITE-ONLY
  pnl_source          writes~12 branches~1            ml=0 api=6    near-write-only
  reconcile_status    writes~6  branches~24           ml=0 api=5    healthy
  cost_source         writes~5  branches~9            ml=0 api=0    healthy
  backfill_kind       writes~4  branches~4            ml=16 api=6   healthy

TWO of the write-only fields matter independently of the PnL-provenance bug:

* `close_exec_type` (order_monitor.py:~7162, written from Bybit /v5/execution/list) distinguishes 'BustTrade' = LIQUIDATION / demo margin call, 'AdlTrade' = auto-deleveraging, 'Trade' = a normal fill. A liquidated position is a categorically different event from a bracket exit, and would present as an enormous adverse exit price. Nothing reads this field, so no analysis, review skill, or ML label has EVER distinguished a liquidation from a stop. This is a live candidate explanation for part of the bybit_1 loss tail and for the unexplained long holds (BL-20260730-SCALP-LONG-HOLDS-UNEXPLAINED) -- CHECK IT before theorising further about exit geometry.

* `fc_present` is the M19 fc-geometry soak's HONEST COVERAGE DENOMINATOR -- the field whose entire purpose is to record 'no forecast was served here'. It is written and never consumed, which is precisely the failure the canonical 'green is not evidence' rule (§ obligation 1, assert the inputs) exists to prevent. The rule is stated; nothing enforces it.

Note ml=0 for EVERY provenance signal except backfill_kind: the training pipeline cannot express 'this label is untrustworthy' about anything.

GENERAL FIX (the class, not the instances): a signal that is written and never read is indistinguishable from one that does not exist, so recording it creates false assurance -- reviewers see the field and assume something acts on it. Proposal: a CI guard that fails when a declared quality/provenance key gains a writer but no consumer (the same shape as the existing canonical-db-resolver / env-gate-guard guards), plus a consumer contract requiring each decision surface to declare which provenance values it accepts.
items.next_action: (1) Query close_exec_type distribution over the bybit_1 loss tail -- cheap, may reclassify a chunk of the 'exit leak' as liquidations. (2) Propose the write-only-signal CI guard.

items.title: ML label builders derive `won` from trades.pnl with NO provenance filter
items.detail: ml/datasets/families/trade_outcomes.py (label_version 'won-from-pnl-v1') sets `payload['won'] = bool(payload['pnl'] > 0)` straight off trades.pnl. A mark-price-fabricated pnl flips that label arbitrarily, so any model trained on this family has been learning from up to 64.9% manufactured outcomes on the affected books (the +$247,683.78 local_markprice population, concentrated on ib_paper). Other families reading pnl should be checked the same way (execution_quality, backtest_results, setup_labels). Recommended shape, mirroring what /performance now does: emit a `pnl_provenance` metadata column (leakage-safe — excluded from features exactly like `pnl` already is), report measured-coverage in the dataset metadata, and make any row filtering an EXPLICIT training decision rather than a silent drop. Do NOT silently change the training population without measuring first. Live exposure measurement was requested via trainer-diag issues #8068/#8071; #8068 failed (no sqlite3 CLI on the trainer) and its journal copy was dated Jul 20 (see the sibling staleness item).

items.source: Observed while driving PR #8069 to green. Verified against three independent PRs and the Actions run list.
items.title: PR CI attachment: the 'does not run on ANY PR' premise is REFUTED as of 2026-08-10 (PR #8733 attached 4 pull_request check runs); residual question is whether the original observation used the commit-status API, which reports 0 for Actions checks
items.detail:
EVIDENCE (all read via the GitHub MCP, 2026-07-30):
1. PR #8069 (this session's): total_count=0 checks across FIVE separate real pushes (826cfe89, f6e2b100, c77344c7, 6f80d2e5, 1d9a7886).
2. PR #8039: mergeable_state 'blocked', total_count=0.
3. PR #8053 — **already MERGED to main today** — also total_count=0. So recent merges went in with NO checks run at all.
4. actions_list filtered to event=pull_request repo-wide returns only 'claude-run-failure-alert' runs (all on main). No ruff-lint / pytest-run / pytest-collect / secret-scan / dry-run-guard / env-gate-guard / silent-empty-guard / canonical-config-loaders / canonical-db-resolver run for any PR.

WHAT STILL WORKS (so Actions itself is NOT disabled):
- push-triggered workflows DO run (json-extract-guard.yml fired on two pushes to a claude/** branch).
- issues-triggered workflows DO run (the trainer-vm-diag relay served four requests this session: #8068, #8071, #8072, #8073).
So the fault is specific to the `pull_request` event, not to Actions or to runners.

WHY THIS IS P1: 'zero checks' renders identically to 'all green' in the PR UI and in the MCP status payload. Branch protection lists nine REQUIRED contexts (branch-protection-sync.yml) — if those are genuinely required and never report, PRs should be unmergeable; #8053 merged anyway, which means either protection is not actually enforcing or the contexts are not matching. Either way the repo currently has NO pre-merge verification, on a live-money system.

NOT DIAGNOSED (needs operator/console access this session does not have): repository Actions permission settings, branch-protection enforcement state, or an org policy. Ruled OUT: a `paths:` filter (the required guards deliberately carry none), workflow syntax (unchanged files that used to run), and runner availability (push + issue workflows run fine).

IMMEDIATE CONSEQUENCE for PR #8069: the promotion of provenance-consumer-guard to a REQUIRED context in that PR cannot be verified by a green run, because no PR run happens. The guard passes locally (`python3 scripts/check_provenance_consumers.py` -> OK) and its workflow is a copy of the canonical-db-resolver template validated with a duplicate-key-rejecting YAML loader, but 'CI green' is NOT available as evidence for it or for anything else merged right now.

RESOLVED 2026-08-14 by a controlled sequence on PR #9240 — the residual question ('did the original observation use the commit-status API?') is answered YES, and the real mechanism is now identified.

TWO SEPARATE THINGS WERE CONFLATED:
  (a) READ-SURFACE ERROR. pull_request_read method=get_status reads the COMBINED COMMIT-STATUS API, which does NOT include GitHub Actions check runs. It returned {state: pending, total_count: 0} on #9240 the whole time, including while 4 checks were running. Use method=get_check_runs. This is exactly the trap CLAUDE.md already warns about for curl pollers, one layer up: a surface that answers a DIFFERENT question and reads as a clean negative.
  (b) A GENUINE NON-ATTACHMENT, with a cause. Measured sequence on #9240:
        12:07Z  draft PR opened                          -> 0 check runs
        12:42Z  marked ready_for_review                  -> STILL 0 check runs (verified 12:43Z)
        12:46Z  merged origin/main + pushed              -> 4 check runs within ~30s
      Draft status is REFUTED as the cause: ready_for_review is in every workflow's trigger types and firing it changed nothing. The PR read mergeable_state='dirty' (a real conflict in docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json against a base that had moved 32f0393 -> 2091d57f). GitHub evaluates `pull_request` workflows against the MERGE REF, which cannot be computed for a conflicted PR — so no merge ref, no run. Resolving the conflict restored CI immediately.
  What was read to establish this (checked: .github/workflows/pytest-run.yml and checked: .github/workflows/guards.yml — the on: trigger blocks and the job-level if: conditions, which confirmed types include opened/synchronize/ready_for_review and NO draft gating exists; plus the PR's own mergeable_state via the GitHub MCP).
  Denominator check that makes this non-vacuous: pytest-run fired normally on OTHER branches throughout the same window (claude/m20-exit-coverage-matrix-8d3he7 at 12:40Z, claude/roadmap-work-plan-review-m2aw6p at 12:09Z), so the workflows were healthy and the gap was specific to this PR's state.

RECURRENCE CONFIRMED 2026-08-17 (PR #9884) — the merge-ref diagnosis above HELD, with clean attribution this time. PR opened 15:51Z sat at total_count 0 check runs for ~9 minutes; `mergeable_state` read **dirty** (base had moved 279edec -> ee268e2b while the branch was being built, and both sides touched this very file). Resolving the conflict and pushing the merge produced check runs 50s later.

ATTRIBUTION IS NOT INFERRED FROM TIMING: run 32044027788 carries `event: pull_request` and `head_sha: e97fc6f` (the merge commit). This matters because the same session ALSO hand-dispatched guards/pytest-collect/pytest-run at ~15:57Z on the pre-merge sha 3b335cc, which would have confounded a timing-only read — those dispatched runs never attached to the PR at all, because the head had moved past the sha they ran against.

TWO PROCESS LESSONS worth more than the recurrence itself:
(1) The workflow_dispatch escape hatch these three workflows carry does NOT rescue this failure mode. It is the documented remedy for a DROPPED DELIVERY, and it is useless for a CONFLICTED PR: the run lands on the branch sha, not on the PR's merge ref, so the PR still shows zero checks. A future session reaching for dispatch first will conclude the remedy is broken. **Check `mergeable_state` BEFORE dispatching** — this row already had the answer and the session dispatched first anyway, having pattern-matched the symptom to the wrong cause.
(2) The window is dangerous precisely because it is silent. This repo's own workflow comments say a check that did not run 'renders identically to green', and here the cause is not even a CI fault — it is an ordinary merge conflict on a busy `main`. With several concurrent sessions all appending to shared files (docs/claude/*-backlog.json, CLAUDE.md), a PR going dirty between push and PR-open is now a ROUTINE event, not an edge case. SIGHTING 2026-08-20 (PR #10029, branch claude/e2-exit-mechanism-info-n67zzs): total_count = 0 check runs, re-read twice ~100s apart after the PR was opened. RULED OUT before recording: the PR was opened as a DRAFT, which is the obvious innocent explanation, and it does not hold -- guards.yml and pytest-run.yml carry NO draft condition (0 greps for 'draft' in either) and both declare types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review], and GitHub delivers 'opened' for draft PRs. So the delivery was dropped, not skipped by design. Recovered via the sanctioned path -- workflow_dispatch of guards.yml / pytest-run.yml / pytest-collect.yml / repo-inventory.yml on the branch ref, all four returning 204. That dispatch affordance exists BECAUSE of this row (pytest-run.yml's own comment says so), so the recovery is the documented one rather than an improvisation. Note for whoever closes this: the intermittency is now dated on both sides -- REFUTED-as-universal 2026-08-10 (#8733 attached 4 runs), recurring 2026-08-20 -- so the open question is the DELIVERY rate, and closing it needs a denominator (how many PRs in a window attached checks), not another single-PR observation. REFINEMENT, same PR #10029, ~10 min later: a PUSH to the same branch DID auto-attach checks -- 4 check runs appeared from the pull_request 'synchronize' event alongside the 4 I had dispatched (8 total on head 8806e0e5). So on ONE pull request, in one ~10-minute window, with one workflow set and one branch: the 'opened' delivery was dropped and the 'synchronize' delivery arrived. That narrows the failure from 'PR CI sometimes does not attach' to a per-EVENT delivery drop, and it rules out the standing explanations that would have been reached for otherwise -- it is not the branch, not the workflow files, not repo settings, and not the draft state (a draft PR stays draft across a synchronize). It is consistent with the 2026-08-10 refutation of the 'never attaches' premise. The denominator this row still needs is therefore per-EVENT-TYPE, not per-PR: of N 'opened' events in a window how many attached, and separately for 'synchronize'. A per-PR rate would average the two and hide it.
items.observation_2026_07_30_evening:
NOT resolved — INTERMITTENT, which is worse than consistently broken because it reads as fixed. Checks attached for exactly three consecutive SHAs (8377f29c, 31d61f69, 09c7a11a; 25 runs each, 18:37-18:43Z) and then stopped again: f10d2b54, 19a5d883 and bf29519b produced ZERO runs. Correlation with the merge commit that brought #8039 down from main is therefore coincidence, not cause.

Ruled out this pass: no `draft` guard exists in any workflow (checked), so draft status is not the gate; `paths:` filters are not it either (pytest-run has none and still did not fire); and Actions is plainly not disabled, since push- and issue-triggered workflows have run reliably all session.

Note for whoever picks this up: `pytest-run.yml` CANNOT be dispatched as a workaround — its `push` trigger is `branches: [main]` only and it has no `workflow_dispatch`, so on a feature branch `pull_request` is the ONLY event that can run it. While that event is dropping, a feature branch has no way to run the test suite in CI at all.
items.why_critical: Zero checks renders identically to green in every UI and in `get_status`. This PR shipped 11 test failures, a false-positive guard trip and a deploy-safety gap that were ALL invisible until the event happened to fire — on a repo where main receives live-trading code.
items.evidence_2026_07_30_2000z:
SHARPENED, and one of my own earlier claims corrected. Correlating every branch SHA against actual workflow runs (ruff-lint, one run per SHA expected):
  8377f29c pull_request OK | 31d61f69 OK | 09c7a11a OK
  f10d2b54 NO RUN | 19a5d883 NO RUN
  bf29519b OK | 6c5273a1 OK | e02b0ada OK

So the gap is TWO SHAs, not three as I first wrote, and the two are not equally damning. f10d2b54 and 19a5d883 were pushed ~25s apart; a `synchronize` for a head that has already moved on is plausibly normal coalescing, so f10d2b54 alone would not evidence a defect. **19a5d883 is the real case**: it was the PR head for ~6 minutes with no event at all, then bf29519b (pushed later) fired normally. Concurrency cancellation is ruled out — neither ruff-lint nor pytest-run declares a `concurrency:` group.

TOOLING TRAP I fell into, worth recording: `pull_request_read get_status` returns `total_count: 0` on this repo ALWAYS, because it reads the legacy commit-status API while every check here is a Check Run. Some of my earlier 'zero checks' readings came from that call and were not evidence of anything. **Use `get_check_runs`, or correlate `actions_list` workflow runs by head_sha** — that is what the table above is built from. A watcher polling `get_status` would report a permanently-red repo.
items.severity_note: Lowered critical -> high on the sharper evidence: 1 confirmed dropped delivery out of 8 pushes, not the near-total outage the first reading suggested (part of which was the get_status artifact above). Still high, not medium: a check that runs SOMETIMES is not a check, and zero checks renders identically to green.

updates.note:
SCOPE CORRECTION + detail, so a review session doesn't start from a false premise. This row's TITLE says CI 'does not run on ANY PR' and its description is EMPTY. The 'any PR' claim is too broad, measured:
  #8085 15 checks all green | #8091 19 | #8097 15 | #8099 15 | #8102 15 | #8109 15 — six PRs merged by this session on 2026-07-30, every one fully checked. #8099 was a SINGLE-FILE docs-only change and still drew all 15.
Meanwhile #8069 read total_count:0 at 19:1x and 25/25 by 21:xx — i.e. INTERMITTENT, and PR/SHA-specific, not a repo-wide Actions outage.

Ruled out (checked directly, not inferred): no workflow carries a `draft == false` condition, so draft status is not the filter; and required checks deliberately carry NO `paths:` filter — env-gate-guard.yml documents exactly why ('trigger can never carry paths: — would leave the check permanently pending').

WHY IT STILL MATTERS AT THIS SEVERITY: zero checks renders identically to green in the UI and in get_status, so an unchecked merge is indistinguishable from a verified one. Keep it open. But the investigation should start from 'intermittent per-SHA' rather than 'Actions is down', which is a much cheaper problem.

Cross-referenced from a concurrent session's PR #8069, which independently reached the same intermittent conclusion.
RESOLVED by weekly /system-review evidence pass: Scope-corrected same day (subsequent PRs ran 15-19 green checks); W2 #8198 fixed merge_group across 15 workflows + fail-red branch-protection sync.

updates.note:
MEASURED AGAINST A REAL PR THIS RUN — the stated premise ('pull_request-triggered CI does not run on ANY PR') is FALSE as of 2026-08-10. PR #8733 (head bc2876e) attached FOUR pull_request-event check runs within ~90s of creation: repo-inventory (success), pytest-collect (success), pytest-run (in_progress), Guards (in_progress). Confirmed twice, from both directions: mcp get_check_runs returned total_count 4, and actions_list filtered to the branch shows 4 runs whose `event` is literally `pull_request`. So merges are NOT landing unchecked.

LIKELY SOURCE OF THE FALSE PREMISE, worth checking before anyone re-reopens this: the legacy COMMIT-STATUS api and the CHECK-RUNS api disagree, and this run hit that disagreement directly. `pull_request_read method=get_status` on the very same PR/SHA returned `total_count: 0, state: pending` at the same moment `get_check_runs` returned 4. GitHub Actions publishes CHECK RUNS, not commit statuses, so a poller built on get_status sees zero checks forever and concludes CI never attached. That is the same shape as BL-20260730-DIAGNOSTIC-PROVENANCE-CLASS sub-class C (an unasserted denominator read as a clean negative) and the documented `curl … || echo '{}'` CI-watcher failure in CLAUDE.md.

NOT CLOSING on n=1: one PR proves the mechanism works, it does not prove no PR is ever missed (a dropped webhook is intermittent by nature). Downgrading from 'P1: merges landing unchecked' to 'verify the detection method, then re-scope'.
updates.next_check: Re-audit the ORIGINAL observation with get_check_runs rather than get_status. If the original was a get_status read, close this as a measurement defect and file the poller fix instead. If it was a genuine get_check_runs zero, re-scope to 'intermittent webhook drop' and quantify the rate over the last N PRs.

updates.note:
RECURRED on PR #8744, hours after the same PR had attached checks normally — which settles the residual question this item was left on. It is NOT purely a stale-observation artifact: delivery is genuinely intermittent, on the SAME PR.

Measured. Head ed2caa73 attached all four checks at 17:13:51Z and all four went green (repo-inventory, Guards, pytest-collect, pytest-run). The next three pushes (594467be, 395be524, 958aad98) attached NOTHING: `pull_request_read get_check_runs` returned total_count 0, and `actions_list list_workflow_runs` filtered to the branch showed no run newer than the 17:13:51Z set — two independent reads agreeing, and the branch ref on GitHub confirmed at the pushed sha, so this is not a push that failed to land.

Note the reporting shape, which is the dangerous part and is exactly what the pytest-run.yml header warns about: a check that SILENTLY DID NOT RUN renders identically to a check that passed. `total_count: 0` must never be read as 'no checks required' — it is an unasserted denominator (sub-class C). The recovery is the `workflow_dispatch` escape hatch that same header added: I dispatched pytest-run / guards / pytest-collect / repo-inventory on the branch ref by hand. repo-inventory was only dispatchable at all because this session had added `workflow_dispatch` to it earlier today (BL-20260807-REQUIRED-CHECKS-LACK-WORKFLOW-DISPATCH) — without that, one required check would have had no recovery path.

A merge-queue-independent consequence worth stating: because required contexts are matched by name, a PR in this state sits un-mergeable with no red anywhere to explain why, and the natural (wrong) reading is 'CI hasn't started yet, wait'.

MEASURED REFINEMENT of the residual question this row was left on. The premise 'does not run on ANY PR' is refuted (already noted); what I measured today is the SHAPE of what remains, and it is not 'flaky'.

On PR #9244: CI attached on PR OPEN and ran four workflows on the first commit `047d0d1` — repo-inventory, pytest-collect, Guards, pytest-run, **all four `success`**. Then FOUR further commits were pushed to the same branch (`e7f1b95`, `496b47e`, `b90b9af`, `937f4cd`) and `actions_list` filtered to the branch returns **still only 4 runs, all on `047d0d1`**. So the pattern is: **attaches on open, does not re-run on subsequent pushes to the branch.**

That is materially more dangerous than not attaching at all, and in the same direction this row already flags. A PR that shows four green checks reads as verified, while the four commits that followed — carrying the actual substance — are covered by nothing. 'Green' and 'green for a commit five commits ago' are indistinguishable on both the PR UI and the MCP status payload. Note also that `pull_request_read` `get_check_runs` returned `total_count: 0` for this PR throughout, even while `actions_list` showed four successful runs — so the two surfaces disagree, and the one a session naturally reaches first is the one that says nothing ran.

PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE for any session in this state: your own `scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main` run over a VERIFIED-NON-EMPTY /tmp/pr.diff is the only coverage the later commits have. Say which sha CI actually verified rather than calling the PR green — I did on #9244.

[sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The RECOVERY half of the criteria is fully met: all three contexts in branch-protection-sync.yml:137 carry workflow_dispatch — pytest-collect.yml:52, pytest-run.yml:59, guards.yml:46 — so any recurrence is dispatchable. A MECHANICAL CAUSE FOR AN APPARENT NON-ATTACHMENT, OBSERVED TODAY — and it is NOT the residual question this row is holding open, so read it as a confound to rule out rather than an answer.

On PR #9693 I read `get_check_runs` -> `total_count: 0` at ~2 min after a push, again at ~5 min, and again after a SECOND push. Three zero reads across two SHAs is the pattern that reads as 'CI is not attaching'. It was not. The PR was `mergeable_state: "dirty"` — a MERGE CONFLICT with `main` — and no checks ran until I merged `origin/main` and pushed the resolution. Checks then attached within ~3 minutes: 4 runs on the merge commit (guards, repo-inventory, pytest-collect, pytest-run).

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THIS ROW SPECIFICALLY: `get_check_runs` alone cannot distinguish 'workflows are not attaching' from 'this PR is unmergeable so nothing was scheduled'. Both present as `total_count: 0` on a current head SHA. Any future measurement against this row should read `mergeable_state` from the PR object in the same breath, or it risks re-opening a refuted premise on a confound.

CARRIES MY 2026-08-16 CORRECTION, restated so it is not lost: an earlier claim of mine in this session that pushes were 'clearing checks' and needed a manual re-dispatch was WRONG. My own evidence refuted it — a `total_count: 0` read taken immediately after a push, a manual dispatch, and then the push-triggered set appearing, leaving EIGHT check runs on one SHA. The zero read was a race, and the manual dispatch was the thing that made it look otherwise. Today's episode is the same error class caught earlier: I did not re-dispatch this time, and checking the PR object instead of re-triggering is what surfaced the real cause.

STILL NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a non-conflicted PR ever fails to attach. Nothing here speaks to that; the residual question stands.

A SECOND, DETERMINISTIC MECHANISM FOR THE RELAY-OPENED SUBSET -- offered as COMPLEMENTARY, not as a refutation of the intermittent-delivery finding above. That update says delivery intermittency was proven on one PR both ways, and nothing here contradicts it. What follows explains a DIFFERENT population: PRs opened by a relay.

THE MECHANISM: a pull request OPENED by a workflow using the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN does not fire `pull_request: opened`. It is the same recursion rule this repo already documents for PUSHES ('GitHub does not trigger workflows for pushes made with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN'), applied to PR CREATION. The four required checks trigger only on `pull_request: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]`, so a relay-opened PR is born with NONE of them and never acquires any on its own. They attach when a session-credentialed push later fires `synchronize`.

POPULATION -- every relay-opened PR observed 2026-08-21, 4 of 4:
  #10083 (pr-opener): 0 required checks -> one ordinary commit -> 4 attached -> merged 932f0a54.
  #10086 (pr-opener): 0 required checks -> one ordinary commit -> 4 attached -> merged a67b112.
  #10090 (claude-pr-automerge): `open`/`post`/`open-and-automerge` only, stable across reads minutes apart.
  #10082 (claude-pr-automerge): stuck at 1 of 5 since 04:44Z, auto-merge armed and unable to fire.

IT CORRECTS THE REASONING THAT EXCLUDED THE RECURSION RULE FOR #10082. That analysis checked WHO PUSHED THE HEAD (daace9af, session credentials) and concluded the rule 'does not apply'. The actor that matters is WHO OPENED THE PR. A push landing BEFORE the PR exists fires no `pull_request` event either -- there is no PR yet -- so both halves are silent and the PR sits permanently at zero required checks. The head's author is a red herring.

IF IT HOLDS, #10082 NEEDS NO DISPATCH AND NO ADOPTION: one ordinary commit on its branch attaches all four checks. That is much cheaper than the workflow_dispatch route previously proposed, and it explains why every relay-opened PR in this repo has needed 'arming'.

STATED AS A HYPOTHESIS WITH A NAMED POSITIVE CONTROL, deliberately: this note ships in an ordinary session-credentialed commit pushed to #10090's branch. If the four required checks attach to #10090 on that commit with nothing else changed, the mechanism is confirmed; if they do not, it is wrong and only the delivery framing survives. DO NOT QUOTE THIS AS SETTLED WITHOUT CHECKING THAT OUTCOME -- an unfalsifiable framing is what kept this row open since 07-30, and replacing it with a second unchecked one would be no improvement.

CONTROL RESULT: **CONFIRMED**. The preceding update is no longer a hypothesis. Landing this separately because the PR carrying the hypothesis (#10090) merged BEFORE this result existed, which left the claim dangling on main for a few minutes -- exactly the state that update told readers not to quote.

PR #10090 (opened by claude-pr-automerge, i.e. by GITHUB_TOKEN) sat at `open` / `post` / `open-and-automerge` and ZERO of the four required checks, stable across repeated reads several minutes apart. One ordinary session-credentialed commit (7920084) was pushed to its branch, changing NOTHING but one backlog row. All four required checks attached within ~30 s -- pytest-collect, pytest-run, repo-inventory, guards, all starting 07:32:08-07:32:09.

Nothing else differed between the two observations: same PR, same base, same workflows, same branch protection. The only variable was a push under session credentials. So for a relay-opened PR the required checks are not LATE and not DROPPED -- they were never requested, because `pull_request: opened` does not fire for a PR created with GITHUB_TOKEN.

THEREFORE #10082 NEEDS NO DISPATCH AND NO ADOPTION: one ordinary commit on `claude/session-wrap-0820` attaches all four checks, and its already-armed auto-merge fires on green. It is another session's PR, so this session recorded the remedy rather than applying it.

ONE TRAP INSIDE THE CONTROL, so nobody reuses it wrongly: `pytest-run` concluded success in NINE SECONDS on the control commit, against 11.5 minutes on an earlier commit of the same branch. That is `pytest-run.yml`'s own relevance short-circuit (MB-20260706-CI-MINUTES), which diffs `origin/main...HEAD` -- the WHOLE branch, not the last commit -- against a regex of code/config/workflow paths. Before #10086 merged, the branch diff carried workflows, scripts and tests, so the suite ran; afterwards the diff is one backlog JSON file, outside the regex, so it skipped install+tests and reported success. Correct behaviour, and the reason it is written down: **a green `pytest-run` on a docs-only branch is evidence the check ATTACHED, and is NOT evidence that any test executed.**

THE CONVERSE ARM, RUN IMMEDIATELY AFTER, WHICH MAKES THIS AN A/B RATHER THAN A ONE-SIDED OBSERVATION: PR #10091 was opened **directly through the GitHub MCP under session credentials** instead of through a relay. All four required checks attached **ON OPEN**, at 07:36:01, with no arming commit -- pytest-collect, pytest-run, repo-inventory, guards.

So both arms agree, on the same repo, the same branch protection and the same workflow files, with the ONLY variable being who opened the PR:
  relay-opened (GITHUB_TOKEN): #10083, #10086, #10090, #10082 -> 0 of 4 required checks on open, 4 of 4 cases.
  session-opened (OAuth):      #10091                          -> 4 of 4 required checks on open, no arming needed.

That is a sufficient basis to stop treating the relay-opened subset as flaky delivery and to fix it structurally: either open the PR with a credential that is not GITHUB_TOKEN (a PAT / app token), or have the relay push one trivial arming commit immediately after opening, so a relay-opened PR is not born un-runnable. Until one of those ships, EVERY relay-opened PR costs the session that opens it a wasted CI cycle plus the time to rediscover why.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER FIXES IT: the session MCP's PR-write capability VARIES BY SESSION. `claude-pr-automerge.yml`'s placeholder PR body asserts 'the session's GitHub MCP integration is read-only for PRs -- 403', and that was true of the 2026-08-20 session; it is NOT true of this one, where `create_pull_request` and `update_pull_request` both succeeded (the create returned a VALIDATION error for an existing PR, never a 403). So 'open it from the session instead' is not universally available and the relay cannot simply be deleted.

RESOLVED by direct observation this session. My own PR #10414 attached and RAN the full PR check set: `guards` (PASS 41 / FAIL 1 / SKIP 16) and `pytest-run` both executed on head 811f0a0 and again on beb84a2, and both reported check_run.completed back. The row's own residual question was whether CI attaches to PRs at all; it demonstrably does, twice, on a fresh PR from a fresh branch.

REOPENED 40 MINUTES AFTER I RESOLVED IT, by the condition itself. My resolution above is WITHDRAWN — it was true of the heads it named and I generalised it one step too far. MEASURED on this same PR #10414: pushes of d19c2c4 (17:10:23Z) and 90bfd35 (17:23Z) produced ZERO workflow runs, verified 35+ minutes after the first — actions_list filtered to this branch returns total_count 12 with NO run at either sha, and pull_request_read get_check_runs returns total_count 0. The DENOMINATOR is asserted, which is the whole point: the same query DOES return the four runs at 3083f34 (16:39:48Z), so the probe can find a positive and the silence is real rather than a broken read. Neither commit is empty and neither is a no-op; both changed tracked files. So the last successfully-attached push on this branch is 3083f34 and everything after it has been silent. WHAT MY RESOLUTION GOT WRONG: I observed attachment on two heads and concluded the mechanism works, when what those two heads show is that it works SOMETIMES. Intermittent attachment and reliable attachment are different claims and only the weaker one was evidenced — a negative needs a denominator, and I never established one across pushes. WORKAROUND USED, so it is on the record rather than hidden in a green check: all three required workflows (guards.yml, pytest-run.yml, pytest-collect.yml) were fired by hand via actions_run_trigger workflow_dispatch, each returning 204. That is exactly why those three carry a workflow_dispatch trigger (BL-20260807-REQUIRED-CHECKS-LACK-WORKFLOW-DISPATCH) and it is the reason this PR can go green at all. A required check that depends on a webhook which silently does not fire is a merge-blocking condition dressed as a pending one — 'CI failed' and 'CI never ran' are indistinguishable to a reader, which this repo already names as the worse failure.

A CLEAN, FULLY-ATTRIBUTED INSTANCE OF THE ZERO-CHECKS STATE — cause identified, and it is NEITHER of the two this row and its siblings enumerate. Backlog-drain session #1, PR #10707, 2026-09-02T00:0xZ.

OBSERVED: `get_check_runs` on PR #10707 returned **total_count: 0** with **mergeable_state: `blocked`**.

CAUSE: the head commit `d8792651` was authored by **github-actions[bot]** — the `board-post` relay's own results commit, landed when I posted a coordination-board comment on this PR's branch. GitHub does not trigger workflows for `GITHUB_TOKEN` pushes, so nothing fired.

WHY THIS IS WORTH RECORDING HERE. This row's criteria are about measuring an ATTACHMENT RATE, and this instance shows the denominator is contaminated by a cause that is not a delivery failure at all: a push that was never eligible to trigger CI. Any rate computed over 'pushes to claude/** branches' without excluding bot-authored heads will score these as misses and overstate the failure rate. The three method requirements already on this row (score from the run list's `event` field, wait 5 minutes, do not dispatch on a scored sha) do not cover it — **a fourth is needed: exclude heads whose author is `github-actions[bot]`, or score the latest HUMAN-authored head.**

THE DIAGNOSTIC THAT SEPARATES THE THREE CAUSES, in the order that costs least:
  * `mergeable_state: dirty`  -> MERGE CONFLICT, no merge ref, no runs (BL-20260812-PR-CHECKS-NOT-ATTACHING-WAS-A-MERGE-CONFLICT). Fix is the merge.
  * `mergeable_state: blocked` + head authored by github-actions[bot] -> THIS: the push was never eligible. Fix is one ordinary human-authored commit; an EMPTY one is forbidden.
  * `mergeable_state: blocked` + head authored by a human -> the genuine delivery question this row is about.
Reading `total_count: 0` alone cannot tell them apart, which is the whole shape of this row.

BOTH of this session's zero-checks encounters on #10707 were the first two causes and neither was a delivery drop: `dirty` at 23:23Z (a sibling merged mid-branch; resolved by union merge -> 6 checks fired within seconds), and this one at 00:01Z. CLAUDE.md documents the relay-results-commit trap under the `pr-opener` bullet, but as an incidental warning rather than as a NAMED cause of `total_count: 0` beside the merge-conflict one — which is why it is recorded on this row, where a session measuring the rate will actually read it.

NOT CLOSING ANYTHING: this row wants a RATE over a stated denominator, and two anecdotes are explicitly named as insufficient. This is a method correction plus a third cause, not the measurement.

items.correction_2026_07_30_2205Z:
I WAS WRONG about the 'second confirmed drop'. Retracting it rather than leaving a false data point in a row whose whole value is its evidence.

The two pushes I recorded as dropped deliveries (7b814d64, bc70ef48) were NOT drops. PR #8111 was in `mergeable_state: dirty` — a merge conflict against main. `pull_request`-triggered workflows run against the MERGE REF (refs/pull/N/merge), and a conflicted PR cannot produce one, so no check CAN attach. The absence was correct behaviour, not a delivery failure. Proof it was never an outage: other branches got runs throughout the same window (21:53, 21:56, 21:59).

Two lessons, both about my own method:
1. I diagnosed 'CI is not delivering' from the ABSENCE of runs without first checking the PR's own mergeable_state — the same shape as the get_status artifact that inflated my original P1: reading a zero and concluding a cause instead of asking what else produces a zero.
2. Checking whether the symptom was repo-wide is what unstuck it. A branch-specific symptom with a healthy repo means look at the branch, not the platform.

So the standing evidence remains ONE unexplained drop (19a5d883), not two. Severity lowered back to medium. The workflow_dispatch mitigation is still worth having — a feature branch genuinely had no way to run the suite when pull_request did not fire — but it is now a defence against a single observed event, and the honest headline is 'one drop in ~10 pushes', not 'CI is unreliable'.
items.recurrence_2026_08_07:
RECURRED. MEASURED: PR #8608 sat at total_count=0 check runs across FOUR distinct pull_request event types on TWO shas — opened, synchronize (force-push ecea6665), ready_for_review, and reopened (close+reopen on 4febab0f). Repo-wide, the last pull_request-triggered run of any required workflow (pytest-collect/pytest-run/guards) was 2026-08-07T18:14:27Z; at 18:51Z nothing further had fired, i.e. ~37 minutes of dropped deliveries. 

NEW AND USEFUL, which the 2026-07-30 session could not establish because run_workflow was 403 for the MCP at the time: workflow_dispatch on the BRANCH REF is a working recovery — guards.yml and pytest-run.yml were dispatched and their check runs ATTACHED to the PR head sha correctly (ids 92966429842 / 92966451853). So a stranded PR is recoverable for any required workflow that carries workflow_dispatch. 

THE GAP THAT REMAINS: pytest-collect.yml did NOT carry workflow_dispatch, so it was the one required context with no recovery route — and workflow_dispatch is only honoured for a workflow already carrying it on the DEFAULT branch, so adding it on a feature branch does not unblock that same branch. PR #8608 adds it, which helps the NEXT stranded PR, not itself. 

ONE DIFFERENCE FROM 2026-07-30 worth recording: branch protection IS enforcing now — PR #8600 read mergeable_state 'blocked' until its checks went green and merged only after. The original report's #8053 'merged with zero checks' symptom did NOT reproduce today, so the protection-not-enforcing half appears genuinely fixed; the delivery half is not.
items.action: Short term: dispatch the required workflows on the branch ref when a PR shows total_count=0 — do NOT interpret zero checks as green, and do not merge on it. Medium term: (a) ensure EVERY required context carries workflow_dispatch on main (pytest-collect was the gap; fixed in #8608), (b) consider a scheduled watchdog that flags an open PR sitting at zero checks past N minutes, since zero renders identically to green in both the UI and the MCP payload. Root cause is GitHub-side delivery and is not fixable from this repo; the repo-side fix is making the condition detectable and recoverable.
items.resolution_criteria: Establish the RATE of PR check attachment over a named window of pushes to claude/** branches, with the denominator stated. THREE method requirements, each from a specific error already made on this row: (a) score from the workflow-run list's `event` field, NOT from get_check_runs — that surface cannot distinguish a webhook-triggered run from a manually dispatched one, which is how a 2026-08-29 measurement scored an attaching push as a miss; (b) wait at least 5 minutes before scoring a miss — observed push-to-run-creation latency is ~2.5 minutes and every false miss came from checking inside it; (c) do NOT workflow_dispatch on any sha you intend to score, since the dispatch occupies the concurrency group and confounds the observation. Explicitly NOT sufficient: observing attachment on one or two heads (the existence proof that wrongly closed this row twice), or a rate computed without the `event` field.
items.next_action: Escalated medium -> high on the same-day recurrence. The premise question is now closed (delivery IS intermittent, proven on one PR both ways), so the work is detection, not diagnosis: nothing today distinguishes 'checks pending' from 'checks will never arrive', and they look identical. Add a positive-denominator assertion wherever CI state is polled — treat total_count==0 on a PR older than a few minutes as ABSENT (actionable) rather than pending — and keep workflow_dispatch on every required check as the standing recovery path (now true for all four).

history.note:
RECURRENCE, MEASURED — and it is currently blocking a Tier-3 real-money PR from being mergeable.

PR #9257, branch claude/m20-exit-coverage-matrix-8d3he7. guards.yml has a completed run for EVERY commit through 7e364578 (created 17:29:58Z) and NONE for the three that followed: f39ad850, ce5ca23b, 8395b531. Enumerated from the workflow-run list filtered to the branch (30 runs returned, newest 7e364578); the three SHAs are absent from it. The PR's own check-run list returns total_count 0 — NO WORKFLOW ATTACHED, which is a different state from attached-and-pending and must not be read as 'still running'.

SPAN: ~2 hours, 3 pushes, zero runs.

RULED OUT BY READING THE WORKFLOW, not assumed: guards.yml carries NO `paths:` filter (deliberately — the comment says a required check must never hang pending on a non-matching PR), and `synchronize` IS in its pull_request types, so an ordinary push to the PR branch should fire it. Draft status is not the cause either: every earlier run on this same draft PR fired normally.

NOT RULED OUT: the concurrency group (guards-pull_request-9257, cancel-in-progress true). A cancelled run would still APPEAR in the run list, and none do, so cancellation does not fit the evidence — but I have not proven the negative and say so.

MITIGATION ATTEMPTED: an empty commit (ce5ca23b) to force a synchronize event — no run appeared. Then a manual workflow_dispatch on the branch, which GitHub accepted (204, run queued). A dispatch run verifies the CODE but does NOT satisfy the PR's required `guards` context, because it is a different event.

WHY THIS IS THE DANGEROUS SHAPE RATHER THAN AN INCONVENIENCE: the PR carries a Tier-3 real-money config change awaiting operator merge. A reader who remembers 'all four checks green' is remembering 7e364578, three commits back. Branch protection should FAIL CLOSED here (a required context absent on HEAD blocks the merge), which is the safe direction — but it means the PR cannot be merged at all until this clears, and that is a morning blocker the operator needs to know about rather than discover at the merge button.

FAULT ISOLATED — with a positive control, which is what the earlier entry lacked.

pull_request events: ZERO guards.yml runs across FOUR consecutive pushes (f39ad850, ce5ca23b, 8395b531, 48d820e2), ~2.5 hours. PR check-run list total_count 0.

workflow_dispatch of the SAME workflow on the SAME branch: RAN AND PASSED, 2026-08-14T19:24:45Z on 8395b531 (enumerated from the run list filtered to event=workflow_dispatch; 29 such runs exist, and sibling branch claude/roadmap-work-plan-review-m2aw6p has five more the same day).

SO THE FAULT IS LOCATED, not merely observed. Healthy and therefore excluded: the runner pool, the workflow file, the branch, repo-wide Actions availability, and the guard code itself (it passes). What is dead is specifically the pull_request / synchronize event path for this PR.

This is the check the previous entry could not make: 'no runs' alone is consistent with an Actions outage, a paths filter, a draft skip, or an event-delivery failure, and those have different remedies. A dispatch that succeeds on the same ref discriminates between them in one call.

WHAT IT DOES NOT FIX: a workflow_dispatch run does not satisfy the PR's required `guards` context, because the context is keyed to the event. So the code is verified while the PR stays unmergeable. Branch protection failing closed is the correct direction here — the risk is not a bad merge, it is a reader trusting a green from 7e364578, five commits back.

STILL NOT ESTABLISHED, and I am not guessing at it: WHY pull_request delivery stopped. Candidates not discriminated — a GitHub-side webhook/event-delivery incident, something about this PR's state specifically (it has 40+ commits and has been open ~8h), or the concurrency group. Cancellation still does not fit, since a cancelled run appears in the list and none do.

progress.note: RECURRED TODAY, on a real-money Tier-3 PR, and the row's own 'refuted' framing is what let me nearly wait it out. PR #10206 was opened 21:03Z and pushed twice (4d04ef93, ee8adaad). At 21:31Z — 28 minutes and three pull_request-triggering events later — `get_check_runs` returned **total_count: 0**. NOT DRAFT GATING, checked rather than assumed: `guards.yml` / `pytest-run.yml` / `pytest-collect.yml` / `repo-inventory.yml` all declare `types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]` and NONE of the four contains the string 'draft' anywhere, so there is no job-level draft exclusion to explain it. STATE THE POPULATION — this is intermittent, not universal: TWO OTHER PRs from this same session, on this same branch, got their check runs within seconds today (#10204 at 18:42Z, #10205 at 20:03Z). So 1 of 3 PRs today attached nothing. The one that failed is the only one that STAYED draft, which is a correlation worth recording but not a mechanism — I did not establish causation, and #10204's own draft-era runs (three 'cancelled' entries at 18:42:00-18:42:01) suggest drafts CAN trigger here, which cuts against the draft hypothesis. REMEDY USED — the one this repo already built for exactly this: `workflow_dispatch` on the feature branch. `pytest-run.yml`'s own comment names it ('Manually dispatchable so a FEATURE BRANCH can always run the suite ... the one confirmed dropped pull_request delivery (BL-20260730-PR-CI-NOT-ATTACHING) left a branch with...'). All four dispatched at 21:35Z via the MCP `run_workflow`, each returning 204 queued. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE PR: total_count 0 is indistinguishable from 'CI has not started yet', and my own scheduled check-in said 'CI not started yet -> re-arm silently'. Followed literally that instruction would have re-armed forever on a PR whose CI was never going to attach — a silent wait that looks exactly like patience. That is the sub-class-C shape (an empty result read as a clean negative) applied to CI attachment, and the row's status of 'the premise is REFUTED' actively encourages reading a 0 as 'just slow'.

items.source: Self-reported after THREE near-misses in ONE session (2026-07-30, session_01HSz1HjdRBCF63MhT5iXfvJ). Each destroyed or would have destroyed committed work; in every case the ONLY thing that surfaced it was git's own rejection on a LATER push, not any guard, check, or rule. (1) `git checkout -B <branch> origin/main` discarded PR #8003's already-pushed commits; caught by the non-fast-forward rejection, recovered from origin/<branch> + cherry-pick. (2) `git reset --soft HEAD~1` on a MERGE commit during #8027's conflict resolution: --soft moves HEAD to the FIRST parent, silently dropping the second, so the union CONTENT landed while the merge LINK did not -- GitHub correctly kept reporting mergeable_state 'dirty' and I misdiagnosed it as a stale async computation, burning a diagnostic cycle before re-doing the merge properly. (3) `git reset --hard origin/main` at the start of the session-end doc sweep discarded commit 26333205 (vol-axis scoping), which was already PUSHED and open as PR #8051; caught by the non-fast-forward rejection, recovered by cherry-pick onto the remote tip.
items.title: [process/tooling] destructive git sync (`reset --hard` / `checkout -B` / `reset --soft` on a merge) has NO pre-flight guard — 3 near-miss data losses in one session, all caught by luck
items.description: ROOT CAUSE, stated as a behaviour not an accident: `git reset --hard <remote-ref>` and `git checkout -B <branch> <remote-ref>` are used as a 'sync to main' idiom WITHOUT first asking whether the branch carries commits that are not in the target. That question is one cheap command (`git log --oneline <target>..HEAD` must be empty, or `git diff <target> HEAD` must be empty when the content is expected to be equivalent). It was not asked in any of the three incidents. WHY THE CURRENT SAFETY NET IS NOT ONE: recovery depended on git's non-fast-forward / stale-info rejection on the NEXT push. That only fires IF a push happens, only AFTER the local work is already gone, and is easy to misread -- my push-retry loop treats every push failure as a transient network error and retried 4x with exponential backoff on a 'stale info' rejection, which is deterministic and will never succeed on retry. If a session resets, does not push, and the container is later reclaimed, the work is simply gone with no signal at all. THE MERGE-COMMIT SUB-CASE IS THE NASTIEST and deserves calling out separately: `git reset --soft HEAD~1` reads as 'undo one commit', but on a merge commit it moves to the FIRST parent and discards the merge relationship. The tree looks correct afterwards (content intact), so nothing local reveals the loss -- only the REMOTE disagrees, by continuing to report a conflict that the operator can see and the session cannot explain. BLAST RADIUS: bounded so far -- Tier-1 research/docs branches, all recoverable from the remote, zero production or live-VM impact. Severity is medium rather than high for that reason, NOT because the behaviour is acceptable; the same idiom on a branch whose commits were never pushed loses the work outright. PROPOSED FIXES (pick one or more; a later session decides): (a) a `scripts/ops/git_safe_sync.sh` helper that REFUSES to reset/checkout -B onto a ref when `<target>..HEAD` is non-empty unless an explicit --force-discard flag is passed, and which stashes-to-a-branch rather than discarding by default; (b) a binding line in `.claude/skills/git-actions/SKILL.md` requiring the emptiness check before any destructive sync, plus an explicit 'never `reset --soft` a merge commit' note; (c) make the push-retry loop classify failures -- non-fast-forward / stale info / rejected are DETERMINISTIC and must short-circuit to diagnosis, never burn 4 backoff retries (this half is cheap and independently useful); (d) consider a SessionStart or pre-tool hook, analogous to the existing `git_history_check` hook that refuses a history question on a shallow clone -- same spirit: refuse the unsafe operation rather than answer/perform it. NOTE ON SCOPE: this is NOT the same as the stop-hook's unverified-commit check, which watches commit ATTRIBUTION. Nothing currently watches DESTRUCTIVENESS. Three times today the hook's own suggested remedy (`git rebase --exec ... --reset-author`) would itself have rewritten published main history for GitHub-authored squash commits, which is a related instance of 'the suggested git operation is more destructive than the problem'.

updates.note: PARTIAL — shipped scripts/ops/git_sync_preflight.sh: run it before 'git reset --hard <ref>' / 'git checkout -B <branch> <ref>'; it refuses (exit 2) when HEAD carries commits absent from <ref>, listing exactly what a hard reset would discard, with a --allow-discard escape for the intentional read-only-mirror syncs (deploy_pull_restart.sh, trainer_git_sync.sh). This is a WRAPPER, not a CI check — CI cannot intercept a local reset — so it is opt-in by construction; enforcing its use is a discipline/doc matter, tracked as the residual of this item. Verified against a live case (a branch carrying 2 unmerged commits correctly refused).

Re-validated by /health-review 2026-08-03. No live-health regression tied to this item this window (trader healthy, 7/7 checks ok, all 7 live broker accounts reachable, notifications banner clean, DB 717MB/no errors). Condition unchanged; remains blocked on its declared tier/owner — no in-session Tier-1 fix available. Kept open.

Re-checked: scripts/ops/git_sync_preflight.sh exists (the partial fix from 08-02) but is still advisory — nothing enforces it. Relevant this window: the concurrent session reported getting a branch-restart wrong once and self-correcting, which is another near-miss in the same family. Kept open.

Triaged in the system-review 2026-08-10 (RPT since-last, window from 2026-08-07T14:55Z) full-backlog pass. This run produced NO new evidence bearing on this item — the state I pulled (live diag: services/heartbeat/tick_cost/db_info/positions/balances/exchange_positions/notifications; performance 24h+7d; exchange-truth PnL; the pairs/allocator/exit-ladder/fc-geometry/netting/exposure soaks; ML lifecycle via /api/bot/ml/status; m20_exit_analysis on the trainer) does not touch it. items.title: [trainer][infra] trainer VM root filesystem at 95% — 2.4G free against a workload that writes ~480MB per dataset build
items.description: Not urgent-broken, but on a clear trajectory and cheap to fix now. The trainer's root fs is 43G/45G used with 2.4 GB free. That box's normal work is writing market_features builds of ~480 MB each (BTCUSDT/15m/v520 alone is 480,607,056 bytes), and `datasets-out/market_features/BTCUSDT/15m/` currently holds SIXTEEN versions (v001-v006, v104, v106, v107, v513-v515, v520, v903, v905, vfmac003), most of them 175,272-row siblings differing only in which optional side-stream was joined. Several are plainly superseded (v003/v004/v104/v106/v107 have NO fc_ columns at all; v513/v514/v515 are same-day predecessors of v520). WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND HOUSEKEEPING: a build that runs out of disk mid-write is exactly the failure mode that produces a TRUNCATED-BUT-PRESENT artifact — the 'green but vacuous' class the binding 'Green is not evidence' rule exists for. A half-written data.jsonl looks like a dataset until something asserts its row count. Two things worth doing: (a) prune superseded market_features versions on the trainer (keep the one each live/advisory head actually trained on — v520 for btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1 — plus the newest), and (b) consider whether the dataset-build path should pre-check free space and fail loudly rather than write a partial file. NOTE the pruning is NOT purely mechanical: the registry pins heads to specific dataset versions, so a version must be confirmed unreferenced before deletion.
items.trigger_condition: Trainer root fs above ~90%, or any dataset build failing/short-writing.
items.resolution_criteria: Trainer root fs back under ~80% via a verified-unreferenced prune, and a decision recorded on whether build writes pre-check free space.

updates.note: RESOLVED. Measured first (trainer-diag #8087): root was at 96% (43G used / 2.3G free of 45G), worse than the 95% filed. Pruned CACHES AND LOGS ONLY (#8089): ~/.cache/pip 3.1G + journalctl --vacuum-size=200M freeing 1.5G of archived journals. Result 96% -> 85%, free 2.2G -> 6.8G. Deliberately did NOT touch datasets-out/ (15G) despite ~14 redundant market_features/BTCUSDT/15m versions: manifests PIN dataset versions (btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1 pins v520), so pruning there could strand a head's training provenance — that is a reviewed decision, not a disk-pressure reflex. Verified v520/data.jsonl intact at 480,607,056 bytes after the prune.

items.source: Verifying that #8048's five econ event-study scorecards actually landed on main (#8053, dc6b0a0). Four are comms/macro/econ_event_study_<kind>_scorecard.json; eia_natgas_storage is comms/macro/econ_event_study_scorecard.json — the UNSUFFIXED default name.
items.title: [macro][naming] eia_natgas_storage's scorecard uses the unsuffixed default filename — a `econ_event_study_*_scorecard.json` glob enumerates 4 of 5 kinds and looks complete
items.description: Low-severity but exactly the recurring wrong-roster shape, so it is filed rather than shrugged at. `scripts/macro/econ_event_study.py` writes to a per-kind suffixed path when given one and to the bare default otherwise; the #8053 run left natgas on the default. Consequence: any future consumer, audit, or re-grade that enumerates the family with a `econ_event_study_*_scorecard.json` glob gets FOUR kinds, no error, and no way to tell one is missing — and the missing one is natgas, the kind carrying the strongest (wrong-signed vs the pre-registered hypothesis) IC. Same failure class as BL-20260730-REGIME-CELL-UNAUDITABLE (complete with respect to its roster; roster is the wrong set) and the 'Green is not evidence' § instance table. NOT urgent: all five scorecards exist, all carry non-zero releases + price_bars, and the M1 null verdict is unaffected and already recorded. FIX (either is fine, pick one): (a) rename to econ_event_study_eia_natgas_storage_scorecard.json and have the producer ALWAYS suffix, so the default bare name never exists; or (b) if the bare name is deliberately 'the primary kind', document that in the producer + wherever the family is consumed, so a glob author knows to add it. Prefer (a) — an implicit primary is how the trap re-forms. Whichever is chosen, add the family to the artifact-validity registry so its COUNT is asserted, not its existence.
items.trigger_condition: Any consumer or audit that enumerates the econ event-study scorecard family by glob.
items.resolution_criteria: Either every kind's scorecard is suffix-named (no bare default written), or the bare name's meaning is documented at the producer and every consumer; and the family's expected kind-count is asserted rather than assumed.

updates.note: RESOLVED — both halves of resolution_criteria met. (a, at the source) `econ_event_study.py`'s `--json` default is now per-kind suffixed via `default_scorecard_path(kind)` -> a default invocation can NEVER write the ambiguous bare `econ_event_study_scorecard.json` again (the implicit-primary that re-forms the trap). The workflow still writes the bare natgas name via an explicit --json for landed-artifact/registry back-compat, and that name is now DOCUMENTED as the eia_natgas_storage kind at the producer + in the registry note. (count) The artifact-validity registry (`scripts/ops/check_artifact_validity.py::CHECKS`) now registers ALL FIVE kinds by path (natgas-bare + crude-alias + initial_jobless_claims + continuing_jobless_claims + cpi_yoy) — so the ROSTER is asserted: a dropped kind is a MISSING finding, not a silently-shorter glob. Pinned by `test_check_artifact_validity.py::test_the_full_econ_event_study_family_is_registered` + `test_m1_econ_event_study.py::test_default_scorecard_path_is_always_kind_suffixed`. BONUS hygiene (see-something-say-something): the two `KNOWN_VACUOUS` grandfather entries for the natgas + crude scorecards were REMOVED — the price join was fixed 2026-07-30 and both now read price_bars>0 (natgas 5428/789, crude 5427/2211, verified against committed artifacts), so per each entry's own contract ('fix landed -> remove the entry') they were dead debt. `check_artifact_validity --no-heuristic` clean (8 registered, 0 vacuous).

items.source: First real `verify` run of scripts/research/ml_vol_label_replay.py (trainer-diag #8079) comparing replayed btc-regime-15m-lgbm-v2 labels against the 34 live regime_ml_vol_shadow rows the gate itself recorded for BTCUSDT over 2026-06-28..06-30. Bar-alignment ruled out by a targeted +/-2-bar probe (#8080).
items.title: [regime][parity] the OFFLINE replay does not reproduce the LIVE P(volatile): 88.2% label agreement but median |dP| 0.043, p90 0.209, max 0.412 — and the agreeing rows do not match numerically either
items.description: WHAT WAS MEASURED. verify over the only window where live ML labels and offline-replayable bars both exist: comparable=34, agree=30 => 88.24% label agreement. The probability delta, which is the stronger check: median 0.042715, p90 0.208866, max 0.411516. WHY THE LABEL NUMBER IS MISLEADING ON ITS OWN. A label is a coarse threshold at 0.5, and most bars sit far below it, so two materially different probabilities usually threshold the same way. The 88% is therefore substantially COINCIDENCE, not agreement. BAR ALIGNMENT IS NOT THE EXPLANATION — checked, not assumed. The natural hypothesis was an off-by-one bar (live scores CLOSED bars; a 15m bar opening 13:00 closes 13:15, so a row logged 13:02 might legitimately carry the 12:45 score). #8080 printed the replayed p_volatile for every bar +/-2 around each of the 4 disagreements plus one AGREEING control. The live value matches NO adjacent replayed bar in any case: e.g. live 13:02:08 and 13:09:12 both read 0.21057753 while replayed 12:30/12:45/13:00/13:15/13:30 = 0.1935/0.2859/0.5512/0.4579/0.0730. THE CONTROL IS THE DECISIVE PART: an AGREEING row (live 09:03:33, p=0.07394825) also matches nothing — replayed 08:30/08:45/09:00/09:15 = 0.0376/0.0099/0.0511/0.0564. So even where the labels agree, the underlying probabilities differ. This is a genuine offline-vs-serve feature-row difference, not a join bug. WHAT IT DOES AND DOES NOT MEAN. It does NOT invalidate the vol axis: grading a 2-D cell on the offline label is still far better than the 1-D pooling it replaces, which measured a population live never trades at all. It DOES bound the claim — any cell verdict produced from these labels must carry the ~88% live-label-agreement fidelity, and a cell whose verdict flips on a handful of near-threshold bars is NOT decision-grade. LIKELY CAUSES, none yet confirmed, ordered by suspicion: (a) the live row is built by feature_row_for_predictor from LIVE-FETCHED candles over a trailing window, while the offline row comes from the market_features builder — rolling_log_return_vol over a 20-bar window is the most sensitive shared input; (b) the live candle window may include a partially-formed current bar; (c) hour_of_day/dayofweek derived from the latest live bar vs the frame's ts. Note -v2 has NO fc_ features, so the Chronos side-stream is NOT a candidate here — which usefully narrows it to the 7 base columns. THIS IS THE GAP S-MLOPT-S17 EXISTED TO CLOSE. That sprint added build_parity_feature_row and asserted live==builder bit-for-bit in a unit test using MarketFeaturesBuilder as oracle. This measurement says the property does not hold in PRODUCTION over real bars. The unit test passing while live disagrees is itself the finding: the test's oracle and the live fetch path are not the same input. NEXT STEP TO ISOLATE: dump the live feature ROW (not just the score) for a handful of bars and diff it column-by-column against the builder's row for the same ts. shadow_predictions.jsonl already captures feature_row per prediction (added 2026-05-19), so this may be answerable from existing data with no new instrumentation.
items.trigger_condition: Any use of offline-replayed vol labels to grade, author, or retire a regime cell; and any claim that train/serve parity for the regime heads is closed.
items.resolution_criteria: The per-column source of the offline-vs-serve difference is identified from a real feature-row diff, and either fixed or documented as an irreducible bound with the agreement rate that every downstream cell verdict must carry.

updates.note: STALENESS RULED OUT — the finding is STRONGER, not weaker. Before letting the parity claim stand I tested the most likely benign explanation: _p_volatile_from_cache explicitly serves a STALE-but-present per-bar score ('the staleness is at most one bar duration'), and REGIME_BAR_SCORING_BUDGET_S can defer whole (symbol,timeframe) groups to a later tick, so the live value could simply be an older bar's score rather than a different computation. TEST (trainer-diag #8084): search the ENTIRE 175,272-bar replayed label file for each live p_volatile value, not just nearby bars. RESULT: 0 of 32 live values appear ANYWHERE in the replay. CONTROL that makes the test meaningful: the replay holds 171,381 DISTINCT p_volatile values across 175,272 rows, so values are essentially unique and a match would have been real signal rather than coincidence. Combined with the earlier +/-2-bar probe (#8080) and its AGREEING control row, three independent explanations are now excluded: bar misalignment, cache staleness, and join error. What remains is a genuine difference in the FEATURE ROW the head is scored on. ALSO CONFIRMED, and it removes a candidate cause: the live feature_row for btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1 DOES carry all six fc_* columns (shadow_predictions tail, 2026-07-30T15:04:22Z), so forecast_live is populating them and a missing-fc_ hypothesis is dead. The live row also carries the full parity superset (parkinson/garman_klass/rogers_satchell/yang_zhang vols) beyond the head's own 13 features, as build_parity_feature_row intends. COLUMN ISOLATION IS BLOCKED ON A DATA WINDOW, and this is the concrete next step rather than a vague one: a column-by-column diff needs a MATCHED pair — one live feature_row and the builder's row for the SAME bar. shadow_predictions.jsonl is 85 MB and the diag log_file tail is capped at 1000 lines, which covers roughly EIGHT MINUTES of live scoring (400 lines spanned 15:03:58->15:11:22), while the newest market_features build (v002) ends 2026-07-29T22:30 — so the tail and the dataset do not currently overlap. Two ways to close it, neither started: (a) rebuild market_features BTCUSDT/15m through today and diff against a fresh live row — note BL-20260730-TRAINER-DISK-95PCT, the trainer root fs is at 95%/2.3GB so a ~480MB build needs the prune first; or (b) add a diag path that serves shadow_predictions filtered by model_id + since, so a historical live row can be pulled without a 200k-line tail. (b) is cheap and reusable and is probably the right one.

HYPOTHESIS worth testing, explicitly NOT a finding — but it connects two items tracked separately and would be easy to lose. FRAMING CORRECTION FIRST: I have been calling this 'the offline replay does not reproduce live', which quietly assumes LIVE is the reference and offline is the deviation. That assumption is not obviously right. The OFFLINE row comes from the canonical MarketFeaturesBuilder — literally the rows the head TRAINED on. The LIVE row is assembled by feature_row_for_predictor from live-fetched candles. If the two differ, it is at least as likely that the LIVE row is the deviant one, i.e. the head is being served feature rows unlike its training distribution. That is train/serve SKEW, and it is a live model-quality issue rather than an offline-tooling caveat. THE CONNECTION: M25's promotion work found the shadow regime fleet blocking FLEET-WIDE on `live_regime_discrimination` (the RG4 gate) — the same wall the vol-gate operating-curve study MB-20260701-001 hit, and the reason the 2026-07-19 gate reframe demoted RG4 to advisory so promotions could proceed on offline oos_edge instead. A head scored live on rows that differ from its training rows is EXACTLY what would produce good offline metrics and poor live discrimination. So 'the fleet cannot discriminate live' and 'the live feature row differs from the builder row' may be the same bug seen from two ends, and the fleet-wide-ness is itself suggestive — a per-head modelling failure would not hit every head equally, whereas a shared serve-path defect would. WHAT WOULD TEST IT: the same matched-pair column diff already needed for column isolation. If a specific column (rolling_log_return_vol over its 20-bar window is the prime suspect, being shared by every regime head) is systematically offset live-vs-builder, that single defect would explain both symptoms. If the columns match and only the score differs, this hypothesis is dead and the gap is elsewhere. DO NOT act on this as established. It is recorded so the column-diff, when it happens, is read against BOTH questions rather than only the narrow tooling one — and so nobody re-derives the connection from scratch. Refs MB-20260701-001 and the M25 RG4 reframe.

CORRECTION + SCOPE. While isolating the column difference I ran scripts/ml/_feature_parity_probe.py against the BTC ADVISORY head (#8088) and read its 'PREDICTED score(volatile)' line as mean 0.967 / min 0.504 over 2336 live rows — i.e. the live gate pinned to volatile on real money. THAT READING WAS WRONG and I did not escalate it. The shadow log's `score` is ShadowPredictor.predict -> MulticlassPredictor.predict = max(proba.values()) (ml/predictors/multiclass.py:38), the PREDICTED CLASS's confidence, hence >= 0.5 by construction for a 2-class head. Fleet sweep (#8090) confirms: frac(score<0.5)==0.0000 for ALL ~30 regime heads, while non-multiclass heads in the SAME log (exit-head-donchian-1h-v1 0.036-0.452, setup-quality-lgbm-v2 -0.755-0.278, execution-quality-baseline-v0 constant -0.20) sit below 0.5 freely — a clean natural control. The live gate is NOT affected: regime_bar_scoring._maybe_publish_p_volatile reads predict_proba['volatile'] explicitly, and RG4 (replay_pregate_live.py:249) does the same, so neither the gate nor the fleet-wide RG4 block is an artifact of this. THE ORIGINAL FINDING IS UNAFFECTED — it was measured on p_volatile from the gate's own audit rows vs the replay, not on this `score` field. Still open; still ungraded cells.

LIVE-SIDE MEASUREMENT (fixed probe, trainer-diag #8092 + live audit rows #8094). The BTC advisory head btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1 gates VOLATILE only 10/979 = 1.02% of advisory-stage rows (shadow stage 6/1357 = 0.44%); mean P(volatile) 0.0366. Training base rate on the MANIFEST-PINNED v520 is 4.6% (the buggy probe was reading vfmac003 at 16.04% — a 3.5x different base rate). My offline replay is 9.1%. Independently corroborated on the LIVE gate's own audit rows: 40/40 sampled regime_hard_gate rows for BTCUSDT carry vol_regime='calm' with vol_label_source='ml' and vol_regime_frozen='unknown' — so the ML label is the ONLY thing supplying the vol axis, and it reads calm essentially always. CAVEAT, stated because it bounds the claim: the live rows span 2026-07-07..2026-07-30, a calm ~3-week window, against 5 years of training — so part of the offline-vs-live gap is market conditions, not necessarily skew. The column-level residual: xa_breadth_up is present in TRAIN at 100% but CONSTANT 0.0, and entirely ABSENT from live rows (pres=0.0%) — the BL-20260628-XA-TRAINING-ZERO dead-feature class; a constant-0 column carries no information so the impact is probably nil, but that should be confirmed, not assumed.

SELF-CORRECTION — THE HEADLINE COMPARISON WAS EPOCH-MISMATCHED. items.source: Found while using scripts/ml/_feature_parity_probe.py to isolate the offline-vs-serve feature gap (BL-20260730-OFFLINE-VS-SERVE-PVOLATILE-GAP). The probe is a PROMOTION-DECISION diagnostic, so a misleading line in it propagates into stage decisions.
items.title: [ml][tooling] feature-parity probe reported max(proba) as 'P(volatile)' and compared against the wrong dataset version — nearly produced a false P1 on the live money gate
items.description:
TWO defects, both fixed in the same PR that files this item.

(1) MISLABEL. The probe printed the shadow log's `score` under the label 'PREDICTED score(volatile)'. That field is max(proba.values()) — the predicted class's confidence — not P(volatile), so it is >= 0.5 by construction for a 2-class regime head. Every regime head therefore rendered as saturated-volatile (BTC advisory read mean 0.967 / min 0.504). A head that is 97% sure the regime is CALM prints 0.97 under a label that says volatile: the meaning is INVERTED, not merely imprecise. I came within one step of escalating a false P1 against the live real-money BTC vol gate on the strength of this line.

(2) WRONG TRAINING DATASET. _training_rows took sorted(glob(...))[-1] — the alphabetically LAST version dir — not the manifest's pinned dataset. datasets-out/market_features/BTCUSDT/15m holds ~14 versions, so it silently selected vfmac003 while btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1 actually pins v520. Every 'TRAINING dataset' distribution line was therefore potentially against data the head never saw — which is the probe's entire output.

FIX: the probe now (a) prints the logged value as 'LOGGED score = max(proba), NOT P(vol)' AND separately re-runs predict_proba to report the real P(volatile) the gate thresholds plus the would-gate-VOLATILE share, degrading honestly when the predictor can't be resolved; and (b) resolves ml/configs/<id>.yaml::dataset.version, warning LOUDLY on any fallback instead of silently substituting. Regression guard: tests/ml/test_feature_parity_probe_score_semantics.py pins max(proba) semantics (including the inverted 0.03 case) and forbids the old print label.

items.resolution_criteria: Probe reports P(volatile) distinctly from the logged max-proba, resolves the manifest-pinned dataset, and warns on fallback; regression test present and green.
