items.title: [infra][tooling] vm-diag-snapshot's failure comment blames the VM for what is actually a malformed request
items.description:
When the diag path fails VALIDATION, the workflow posts: 'Common causes: VM_SSH_KEY/DIAG_READ_TOKEN secret unset, malformed key, VM web-api down, token mismatch.' All four are infrastructure causes; none is what happened. No VM contact is even attempted on that path. I read that comment and recorded 'VM web-api down' — a false infra diagnosis — and later re-derived the same wrong conclusion, then posted it to the coordination board before checking the run log.

Root cause of the malformed request itself: the workflow reads the path from the issue BODY; a prose body ('path is in the title') is parsed AS a path and rejected.

FIX (this PR): the failure comment now branches on steps.resolve/resolve_multi.outcome and, for a validation rejection, leads with 'MALFORMED REQUEST, not a VM outage', states that the BODY is what is parsed, and shows a correct example body. The infra text is kept for genuine infra failures.

items.source: Tripped on PR #8069 against a DOCSTRING sentence, not a table declaration.
items.title: [ci][tooling] new-table-wiring-guard matches CREATE TABLE inside prose, producing false trips
items.description:
scripts/check_new_table_wiring.py scans a raw diff for CREATE TABLE and does not distinguish code from prose. On PR #8069 it failed on src/runtime/exchange_fills_ib.py for a docstring line that merely SAID the exchange_fills schema is created with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS. That module declares no table at all — it maps into the existing store.

Why this matters more than one false positive: the only ways to clear a false trip are to reword the prose (what PR #8069 did) or to add a `# data-wiring:` annotation for a table that does not exist. The second is FALSIFYING the wiring declaration the guard exists to protect, and it is the path of least resistance — so a prose-blind guard actively teaches contributors to lie to it. Combined with routine false trips, that is the alarm-fatigue failure mode CLAUDE.md names as itself a P1.

Third instance of this exact class in one session: my own json-extract guard first flagged 3 docstring-prose lines, and a structural test matched the explanatory comment NAMING the thing it forbade. Prose-vs-code is a systematic blind spot in this repo's diff-scanning guards, not a one-off.
items.resolution_criteria: The guard ignores CREATE TABLE occurrences inside string literals and comments. scripts/ci/check_json_extract_guarded.py::_prose_lines already solves this with ast+tokenize and is the reference implementation — but it parses FILES, while this guard parses a DIFF (hunks are not valid Python), so the fix likely means resolving each touched file at HEAD and mapping added line numbers onto it rather than porting _prose_lines directly. Add a test asserting a prose mention does NOT trip while a real CREATE TABLE does.

updates.note: RESOLVED by weekly /system-review evidence pass: Guard excludes comment/docstring prose from CREATE TABLE matching and requires the marker to name a real table (check_new_table_wiring.py:55-70,123-127) — verified this session.

  transitional/calm     +32.6577    57  +0.5729  −$356 / 43t         *** CONTRADICTED (sign flips) ***
  transitional/volatile  -1.4852    17  -0.0874  (not gated)         mildly negative, ungated
  chop/calm             -11.5476   124  -0.0931  −$218 / 11t         GATE SUPPORTED (sign agrees)
  chop/volatile          -0.2376     8  -0.0297  (not gated)         near zero, thin, ungated

Arithmetic closes exactly against the harness total: the nine cells (incl. the three */unknown rows +8.5701/-1.6812/+0.9571) sum to 79.2802 = the reported net_r, and the per-regime subtotals reproduce 60.617 / 29.4913 / -10.8281. So this is not a bookkeeping artifact.

TWO of the three authored cells are directionally supported. The third is not: transitional/calm is the SECOND-most-profitable cell in the entire strategy by this measurement, and the live router drops it.

A SECOND, SEPARATE ANOMALY worth its own attention: the per-cell POPULATION SHAPE disagrees with the authoring comments, not just the sign. Authoring n = 136 / 43 / 11 across trending-volatile / transitional-calm / chop-calm; mine = 21 / 57 / 124. The totals are comparable (190 vs 202) but the mass has moved from trending/volatile to chop/calm. Two measurements of the 'same' cells that disagree this much on WHICH BARS FALL WHERE are probably not using the same labelling basis (candidate explanations: a different vol label — note the frozen vol_detector is documented to behave OPPOSITELY to the ML label — and/or a different trend classifier, period, or a live-journal dollar basis rather than a backtest R basis). I did NOT resolve which, and the sign contradiction cannot be adjudicated until someone does.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: I am NOT proposing that this cell be un-gated. My own pre-registered gate (BL-20260730-SQZ-CELLS-N-TOO-THIN) requires regime_cell_walkforward's #7915 *_stable_drag test before any cell-level proposal, precisely because pooled net-R is what produced the htf_pullback_trend_2h fold-3 artifact (+7.89R pooled that was −3.70R ex-fold-3). A +32.66R pooled reading is that exact shape and gets that exact suspicion. The gate is UNMET and cannot currently be met — see BL-20260730-WALKFORWARD-NO-VOL-AXIS: the walk-forward driver is 1-D and cannot fold a 2-D cell at all. A 1-D `transitional` proxy was dispatched (#8117) and is explicitly NOT the same test.

FIDELITY LIMITS, stated rather than graded past: (1) trend_donchian runs exit_head_model exit-head-donchian-1h-v1 (threshold 0.1, action close) LIVE; this harness simulates only the mechanical trail/stop, so live per-cell PnL can differ and an ML exit head that cuts early would plausibly hit the long-runner cells hardest. (2) 89.6% vol coverage — 37 trades sit in */unknown and are NOT folded into calm/volatile. (3) R vs dollars is a different basis from the authoring comment; the SIGN comparison is meaningful, the magnitude comparison is not.

DIRECTION OF THE RISK: this is opportunity cost, not loss. A wrongly-gated profitable cell blocks trades it should have taken; it cannot itself lose money. That is why this is filed high rather than as a P1 — but at expR +0.573 over ~10 trades/yr on a real-money book it is not small either.

updates.note:
SELF-REFUTATION, SAME DAY, BEFORE ANYONE ACTED ON IT. Read this update BEFORE the description above; the description's +32.66R table is NOT safe to act on.

The walk-forward proxy (trainer-diag #8117) was dispatched as a REFUTATION instrument and it refuted. On the SAME 1-D population, with the SAME harness (regime_debt_matrix resolves harness 'trend' to scripts/backtest_trend.py — verified by md5, it is the same file I drove, NOT the scripts/research/ sibling):
    transitional : my grade (#8115) +29.4913R n=86   |   walk-forward (#8117) -1.25R  n=94   <-- OPPOSITE SIGN
    chop         : my grade (#8115) -10.8281R n=141  |   walk-forward (#8117) -4.3089R n=134  <-- same sign, 2.5x magnitude
My +32.66R transitional/calm cell lives INSIDE the transitional population that the second instrument scores negative. So the sign contradiction I reported against the authoring comment is not established — I have two of my own measurements that disagree with EACH OTHER, and I cannot say which is right.

KNOWN DIFFERENCES between the two runs, none yet shown to be the cause: (a) DATA FEED — mine data/btc_1h_multiyear.csv (2021-01-01..2026-06-01), walk-forward Binance-vision 48,000 rows (2021-02-06..2026-07-29); (b) the walk-forward self-reports fidelity 'approximate' with omitted_levers [exit_head_action, exit_head_model, exit_head_threshold, trail_decay_arm_r, trail_decay_tight_mult] — my invocation omitted the same trail_decay_* levers, so that is NOT obviously the difference; (c) param forwarding is done by the driver in one case and by me in the other. A ~30R swing on ~8 differing trades is a big ask, so 'just the extra span' is a hypothesis, not an explanation.

THE OPEN QUESTION IS NOW THE DISCREPANCY ITSELF, not the cell. Until the two instruments are reconciled on a SINGLE feed with IDENTICAL forwarded params, no per-cell number from either run should be quoted. That includes the numbers in the description above and the ones in merged PR #8118.

FOLD-COUNT FRAGILITY, worth its own note: the walk-forward's own verdict flips on fold count at an IDENTICAL pooled value. 4 folds -> [-2.7163, +1.0116, +2.5854, -2.1307], 2/4 negative, stable_drag FALSE. 3 folds -> [+2.7118, -3.4177, -0.5441], 2/3 negative, stable_drag TRUE. Same pooled -1.25R, opposite verdict. A gate whose PASS/FAIL depends on an unstated fold count is not a gate yet; whoever fixes BL-20260730-WALKFORWARD-NO-VOL-AXIS should pin or report fold-count sensitivity too.

WHAT SURVIVES: (1) the vol axis joins and grades cleanly (96.4% / 89.6% coverage) — the tagger is not in question; (2) the arithmetic within each run closes exactly, so neither run is internally inconsistent — which is precisely why this is a seam defect, the class docs/sprint-logs/S-PROVENANCE-EXITLEAK-ROOTCAUSE-2026-07-30 was written about: every component individually correct, the defect between them; (3) NOTHING was proposed and config/regime_policy.yaml was never touched, so no live behaviour depended on the wrong number.

PROCESS NOTE FOR THE NEXT SESSION: the pre-registered walk-forward bar is the only reason this was caught before it became a proposal. It was dispatched expecting it could only refute, never establish — and it refuted. Do not weaken that bar.

CAUSE IDENTIFIED, finding withdrawn. Isolation run trainer-diag #8137.

Params and fees were eliminated FIRST by code inspection, no run needed: regime_debt_matrix.build_harness_cmd forwards exactly the flags I passed; _TREND_LEVER_FLAG = {stale_exit_bars, stale_exit_below_r, side_filter} and trend_donchian carries NONE of them; no adx_min/adx_max; fee 7.5 on both sides (backtest_trend.FEE_BPS_ROUNDTRIP = 7.5, and roundtrip_fee_bps_for('BTCUSDT') -> None -> DEFAULT_FEE_BPS_ROUNDTRIP = 7.5). Byte-identical parameterisation.

That left the FEED, which the 2x2 then split into trade GENERATION vs regime LABELLING:
  A_on_A  (feed A trades, feed A ADX)  transitional +29.4913  n=86   <- reproduces #8115 exactly
  A_on_B  (feed A trades, feed B ADX)  transitional  +4.5742  n=90   <- SAME 357 trades, total net_r 79.28 both
  B_on_B  (feed B trades, feed B ADX)  transitional  -1.6799  n=93   <- reproduces the walk-forward
Attribution: LABELLING 29.4913 - 4.5742 = 24.9171R (79.9% of the swing); GENERATION 4.5742 - (-1.6799) = 6.2541R (20.1%). Total 31.1712R.

Corroboration that the feeds do NOT meaningfully disagree about outcomes: of 357 trades each, 331 entry times (92.7%) are shared, and on those shared trades the two feeds total A=67.8283 vs B=68.8762 -- a 1.05R difference. Aggregate regime base rates are near-identical too (chop 30.0 vs 29.7, transitional 18.8 vs 18.8, trending 51.1 vs 51.5). The ~25R MIGRATED BETWEEN BUCKETS: out of transitional, into trending (+12.98) and chop (+12.30).

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW: the +32.66R transitional/calm cell is not a finding. Its 1-D parent collapses +29.49 -> +4.57 from an ADX-source swap alone, so the cell number was never separable from label noise. The authoring comment (-$356/43t) is NOT contradicted -- and equally is NOT confirmed; this instrument cannot adjudicate it at this resolution. NOTHING was proposed and config/regime_policy.yaml was never touched.

NEITHER RUN WAS WRONG. Both are correct computations of a quantity that is fragile to its input feed. scripts/research/regime_tag_emitted.py gained a --vol-labels axis (PR #8056) so 2-D cells could be graded. That axis was NOT propagated to scripts/research/regime_cell_walkforward.py, whose CLI is --strategy/--regime/--folds/--days/--workdir/--json: it folds on the 1-D trend regime only.

items.title: [research][tooling] regime_cell_walkforward's *_stable_drag verdict FLIPS on fold count at an identical pooled net-R — 4 folds says FALSE, 3 folds says TRUE
items.description:
Same strategy, same regime, same 2000-day window, same pooled result (-1.25R over n=94). Only --folds changed:
  --folds 4 -> [-2.7163, +1.0116, +2.5854, -2.1307]  2/4 negative  long_stable_drag = FALSE
  --folds 3 -> [+2.7118, -3.4177, -0.5441]           2/3 negative  long_stable_drag = TRUE

The verdict is a 'strict majority of folds negative' test, so with an even fold count 2/4 is not a majority while with an odd count 2/3 is. That makes PASS/FAIL a function of an argument the caller picks, at identical underlying evidence. --folds defaults to 4 and no caller is required to state it.

WHY IT MATTERS: this driver IS the repo's gate for promoting a cell observation into a Tier-3 draft (#7915). A gate that can be flipped by an unstated, defaulted knob is not yet a gate — and the failure is silent, since both runs exit 0 and emit a confident verdict field. Same class as BL-20260730-WALKFORWARD-NO-VOL-AXIS: confident output, unstated population/parameterisation.

SUGGESTED SHAPE (not applied — scripts/research/ is ceded to a concurrent session this session): either require an odd fold count, or report the verdict across a fold sweep and demand agreement, or state the fold count in the verdict field so a reader cannot quote it context-free.

items.title: [data][broker] Every broker's fills are pulled on a timer and never read back into trades.pnl
items.description:
96% of fabricated closed rows (198 of 206) sit on accounts whose fills are ALREADY being collected on a schedule. The store is read only by the /api/bot/pnl/exchange display endpoint and two offline scripts. Until PR #8069's IB path, nothing read it into trades.pnl. Same defect class as the provenance keys themselves — written and never read — one level up.

Root cause per account:
* bybit_1 (152/323 fabricated) and bybit_portfolio (11/12) are `demo: true`, and account_closed_pnl_for_trade returns None unconditionally for demo. The lookup is never ATTEMPTED. bybit_2 — same exchange, same code path, NOT demo — is 2.0% fabricated, which is the control proving the venue's data is fine.
* That demo exclusion (BL-20260608-DEMOPNL) is a CORRECT fix for the closed-pnl endpoint, silently over-generalised into 'there is no broker truth for demo'. False: live_bybit_fill_accounts explicitly pulls both demo accounts via fetch_my_trades (a different endpoint) and its own docstring calls them 'real exchange-side fills'.
* alpaca_paper (26/44) and alpaca_options_paper (6/8) — alpaca is not in BROKER_PNL_READER_EXCHANGES at all, although pull_alpaca_fills.py runs daily.
items.resolution_criteria:
STEP 0 FIRST, do not build before it: verify exchange_fills.sqlite on the live VM actually holds rows for bybit_1 / bybit_portfolio (counts per account_id + exec_time span). BL-20260713-EXCHANGE-FILLS-STORE-EMPTY is precedent that a scheduled puller can accrue nothing unnoticed. If empty, the fix is upstream and cheaper.
Then: generalise exchange_fills_ib.closed_pnl_from_fills into a venue-neutral resolver (local SQLite read, never a broker call on the monitor tick) and give Bybit-demo and Alpaca branches. Keep its refusal semantics exactly. Narrow the demo `if` so demo skips the closed-pnl ENDPOINT and falls through to the fills-derived resolver. Bybit fills need FIFO matching (_fifo_match, already written) since they carry no realizedPNL; Alpaca options realised PnL comes from /v2/account/activities cash, not the equity formula.
Move pnlCoverage as the metric; re-run scripts/ops/provenance_exposure_audit.py before and after. Target is not 100% — it is that every remaining fabricated row has a stated reason it could not be measured.
items.step0_measured_2026_07_30:
MEASURED via diag #8114 (/api/bot/pnl/exchange?days=90). The store is NOT empty: 305 fills across 12 symbols over 90 days, spanning 2026-07-06 to 2026-07-30. So the pullers are working and the data was there all along — the gap was purely that nothing read it. Proceeded to the resolver on that basis.

THE MEASUREMENT ALSO CAUGHT A BUG THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THE FIX INERT: the Bybit puller stores ccxt symbols (BTC/USDT:USDT, ADA/USDT:USDT, XRP/USDT:USDT) while the journal carries plain form (BTCUSDT). An equality match on `symbol` would have returned ZERO rows for every Bybit trade — the resolver would have run clean, logged nothing, and changed nothing. Equities (GLD/SLV/TLT/SPY/USO/GDX/IEF) and MGC are stored plain, so a test written against a hand-made fixture would never have surfaced it. Fixed by folding both forms through the canonical broker_cost_attribution.normalize_symbol, with three tests pinning it (including that the fold does not collapse DIFFERENT instruments).
items.shipped_2026_07_30: src/runtime/fills_pnl.py — venue-neutral resolver, two modes (require_realized for IB's own realizedPNL; measured exit PRICE for Bybit/Alpaca which serve none). clients.py: the demo branch narrowed to skip the closed-pnl ENDPOINT only and fall through to fills; alpaca added to BROKER_PNL_READER_EXCHANGES; exchange_fills_ib delegates so there is one implementation. Alpaca OPTIONS deliberately excluded (their realised PnL is /v2/account/activities cash, owned by the options-lifecycle reconciler). Also fixed a real ordering bug the tests caught: the linear/inverse gate ran BEFORE the demo branch, but that constraint belongs to the closed-pnl endpoint, not the fills store — a spot demo account was dead-ended for a reason that did not apply to its path.
items.remaining: (1) DEPLOY + re-measure: the change is inert until the live VM runs it. Re-run scripts/ops/provenance_exposure_audit.py after deploy and confirm pnlCoverage moves off 504/829. (2) The store holds 90d; the journal's fabricated rows run back to June, so forward rows resolve but older ones stay unmeasured — historical relabel remains RELABEL ONLY per the 2026-07-30 operator decision unless re-derivation is explicitly approved. (3) Bybit fills carry no realised PnL, so fees are not yet folded into the local compute on that path — the exit PRICE is measured, the fee treatment is unchanged. Worth a follow-up measurement, not an assumption.

updates.note: RESOLVED by weekly /system-review evidence pass: Store has live readers: #8111 fills_pnl (fees netted) in close pricing, #8069 IB fills reader, backfill-fabricated-exits Tier-2 action registered for the historical tail.

items.title: [tooling][meta] UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT is a defect CLASS — guard shipped (diagnostic-provenance-guard); residual sites grandfathered
items.description:
THE CLASS. A human-facing diagnostic asserts a labelled claim without emitting the derivation that would let a reader falsify it. The number is real; the label is confident; the substitution is invisible. Because every component is individually correct, line-by-line review keeps returning clean — the defect lives at the seams, exactly like the provenance/exit-leak incident the same day.

THREE SUB-CLASSES (mechanically distinguishable, different fixes):
  A SEMANTIC SUBSTITUTION — the printed label names quantity Q; the code called accessor f(); f() != Q.
    A1 inverted (max(proba) vs P(volatile) — meaning destroyed, low bucket empty by construction);
    A2 narrowed/widened ("every audited symbol is fully SL-covered" is TRUE at 444.7% coverage but asserts far more than the verdict measured);
    A3 untested causal claim (a failure comment names a cause no code path tested — the diag-relay 'VM down' for a pre-contact request rejection). A3 is really its own thing: the fix is to branch on the actual failure stage, not to rename a label.
  B IMPLICIT INPUT SELECTION — newest/alphabetically-last/default substituted for the declared or pinned input.
    B1 input artifact (sorted(glob(...))[-1] instead of the manifest's dataset.version);
    B2 input PARAMETER (a function default that differs from what the canonical caller passes — see the vol_threshold item below). Same class, and the one most likely to recur, because nothing in the output distinguishes the two label definitions.
  C UNASSERTED DENOMINATOR — an empty/zero/truncated result reads as a clean negative (a curl||echo '{}' poller turning HTTP 403 into '0 checks'; 'limit: 500' mistaken for a row count).

NOTE the division of labour with silent-empty-guard: that guard catches the PRODUCER (a broad except returning []). C is the CONSUMER (reading [] as a clean, labelled answer). Neither covers the other.

SYSTEMIC FIX SHIPPED (this PR, Tier-1): scripts/check_diagnostic_provenance.py + .github/workflows/diagnostic-provenance-guard.yml + tests/test_diagnostic_provenance_guard.py — same family as canonical-db-resolver / env-gate-guard / silent-empty-guard / provenance-consumer-guard. Diff-scoped in CI (pre-existing sites grandfathered, same contract as silent-empty-guard); `--all` is the standing audit mode. Its override is VERIFIED, not presence-only: `# provenance: <accessor> — <meaning>` must name an identifier that actually appears in the file, and the annotation is excluded from its own evidence pool. This is the direct lesson from new-table-wiring-guard, whose presence-only marker made the cheapest way to silence it naming a table that does not exist.

VALIDATION that the guard generalises rather than memorises: run against the tree it independently re-found bybit_bracket_audit.py:411 (the PR #8069 roll-up finding) and scripts/research/m20_ml_exit_probe.py:64 (a NEW instance nobody had reported), and it passes PR #8091's fixed parity probe.

RESIDUAL (grandfathered, discoverable via --all; ~20 sites, mostly B on market_raw candle dirs where a wrong version is far less dangerous than a wrong LABELLED feature dir): scripts/ml/_labeling_gap_probe.py, scripts/ml/fc_sltp_geometry_backtest.py, scripts/ml/gpu_burst/_remote.py, scripts/research/m20_exit_analysis.py, scripts/research/ws_a_s{2,3,3b}_*.py, ml/cli.py:579 (the promotion gate-check's candle pick — highest blast radius of the B residue), scripts/ml/m23_ev_gate.py:110 and scripts/research/build_research_panel.py:228 (A, latent: predictor is binary today, nothing enforces it).

LIVE VERIFICATION (trainer VM, issues #8122/#8123/#8124, 2026-07-30, over 101,503 rows of runtime_logs/shadow_predictions.jsonl):
  A. All 30 regime heads: frac(score < 0.5) == 0.0000, minima clustered at 0.5001-0.5068 — the exact signature of max(proba) on a 2-class head. CONTROL: 6 of 7 non-regime heads in the SAME log DO range below 0.5 (down to -0.7549), so the log is not merely saturated and the contrast is decisive.
  B. score vs predict_proba[volatile] on the SAME rows: they agree on 0 of 400 rows for EVERY resolvable head. btc-regime-15m-baseline-v1 400/400 INVERTED (e.g. score=0.9696 while p_volatile=0.0287 — a row printed as 'P(volatile)=0.97' was a head 97% sure the regime was CALM); btc-regime-5m-baseline-v1 400/400 (0.9743 vs 0.0253); mes-regime-5m-baseline-v1 383/400; mes-regime-15m-baseline-v1 327/400. 1,510 inverted rows in a 400-per-model sample. The inversion is MEASURED, not inferred.
  The 26 heads whose predictors do not resolve on the trainer are REPORTED as unresolved and their rows DROPPED — never substituted.
items.resolution_criteria: Guard is a required check; the --all residue is driven to zero or each remaining site carries a verified `# provenance:` annotation.

items.title: [research][tooling] m20_ml_exit_probe bucketed max(proba) as 'P(volatile)' — its 'lo' bucket was empty by construction and 'hi' mixed calm with volatile
items.description:
Same defect as BL-20260730-PARITY-PROBE-MISLABELS-MAXPROBA, in a second probe, undetected.

scripts/research/m20_ml_exit_probe.py read the shadow log's `score` (line 64) and bucketed it at `score>=0.6`/`score<=0.4` (line 135), printing the result under the header '=== future_dR by P(volatile) bucket ==='. `score` is ShadowPredictor.predict -> wrapped.predict(row), and every regime head is a MulticlassPredictor whose predict is max(proba.values()). Therefore:
  * score >= 0.5 by construction for a 2-class head, so the `lo` bucket (score<=0.4) was EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION and `mid` only spanned (0.5,0.6];
  * a row reading 0.97 may mean '97% sure the regime is CALM', so the `hi` bucket labelled high-P(volatile) was a MIXTURE of confidently-volatile and confidently-calm bars.

The probe's stated question — does a high regime-head P(volatile) predict a worse REMAINING hold? — was therefore unanswerable from what it computed, while the printed output (bucket means + an 'Interpretation:' paragraph telling the reader how to conclude) looked exactly like an answer.

BLAST RADIUS: this probe's output is the evidence for whether to build an ML exit trigger (M20). That decision is Tier-3 downstream (an exit-geometry change on live legs). No live-money decision was changed. Blast radius is LOWER than first filed, for a reason found only by running it: the probe could not even IMPORT via its own documented invocation (`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'scripts'`, verified on the trainer) — it was runnable only under `PYTHONPATH=.`, which nothing documented. So the defective output was harder to produce than the finding implied. It remains the same severity CLASS as the parity probe.

FIX (this PR): buckets the real predict_proba(row)['volatile'] — the quantity regime_bar_scoring._maybe_publish_p_volatile hands the live gate — via a new SHARED accessor, scripts/ml/_regime_score_semantics.py, which is now the one module that owns what `score` means. Rows whose predictor cannot be resolved are DROPPED and COUNTED (an honest coverage denominator, the rCoverage pattern), never bucketed on the substituted value; if nothing resolves the probe ABORTS rather than emitting a plausible wrong answer. Header now states the accessor and the gate cut.

VERIFIED AFTER FIX (trainer, issue #8124): the probe now runs and reports `P(volatile) coverage: 14440/71661 records re-scored` with the 26 unresolved heads named and their rows DROPPED. All buckets land at n=0, and it now says NO CONCLUSION AVAILABLE instead of printing interpretation guidance over empty buckets — a residual sub-class C defect the live run exposed in this very file, now fixed. Before the fix it would have bucketed ~71k rows of max(proba) under a 'P(volatile)' header and produced a confident, meaningless answer; it now produces an honest absent measurement.
items.resolution_criteria: Probe buckets predict_proba[volatile], reports coverage, and aborts rather than substituting. Regression-pinned.

items.title: [infra][tooling] trainer-vm-diag's failure comment blamed 'SSH timeout (VM down?)' for a pre-SSH request-parse rejection
items.description:
The sibling relay had the identical defect and PR #8097 did not reach it.

.github/workflows/trainer-vm-diag.yml 'Parse command from issue body' (step at L138) exits 1 at L185 when the body carries no `cmd:` line. That step runs BEFORE 'Set up SSH key' (L198), so on a parse rejection the SSH key is never installed and NO trainer-VM contact is attempted. The failure comment nonetheless posted: 'Common causes: VM_SSH_KEY unset, SSH timeout (VM down?), malformed cmd: block' — lumping the one true cause in with two that are impossible on that path, with nothing telling the reader which applied.

This is exactly the reading that produced a false 'VM web-api down' diagnosis twice in one session on the sibling relay, and reached the coordination board before anyone opened the run log. It matters more here: a false 'trainer VM down' is a conclusion the ml-review / system-review skills treat as a mandatory standalone flag.

FIX (this PR): the comment branches on steps.parse.outputs.cmd_present. A parse rejection now leads with 'MALFORMED REQUEST, not a VM outage', states that the BODY is what is parsed (the title is display-only — the recurring operator trap), shows a correct example body, and points at the parse step's log. The infra text is kept, unchanged, for genuine post-parse failures.

STILL OPEN (lower severity, same shape, NOT fixed here): system-actions.yml — 'Validate action and tier policy' (L511) holds ~40 exit-1 paths, all ~250 lines BEFORE 'Set up SSH key' (L764), while the failure comment leads 'Common causes: VM_SSH_KEY secret unset/corrupted; SSH host unreachable'. It is milder (it does print `exitCode || '(set up failed before exec)'`, which a careful reader can use) but the cause list is still untested. health-snapshot.yml and set-diag-token.yml carry the same untested cause lists.

items.title: [ml][TIER-3 PROPOSAL] market_features vol_threshold default 0.003 silently disagrees with the canonical builder's 0.005 — two different regime_label definitions, no marker in the output
items.description:
VERIFIED: ml/datasets/families/market_features.py L504 defaults vol_threshold=0.003 (docstring L22 agrees). scripts/ops/build_trainer_datasets.sh — the CANONICAL builder — passes 0.005 for the Bybit legs (L275, L738) and a DATA-DRIVEN median for MES (L519-525, deliberately: a fixed threshold collapses MES intraday to all-range, MB-20260527-002).

So a hand-rolled `python -m ml build-dataset ...` that omits the argument produces a dataset whose `regime_label` means something DIFFERENT from every dataset the fleet trained on — measured on disk, 0.003 dirs read 16.04% volatile vs 4.6% at 0.005 — and NOTHING in the resulting dataset dir, the manifest, or any downstream metric says which definition it carries. This is sub-class B2 (implicit input PARAMETER selection) and it is the residue most likely to recur, because it needs no code change to bite: just a rebuild that forgets an argument.

It has already caused real confusion: the parity-probe incident (BL-20260730-PARITY-PROBE-MISLABELS-MAXPROBA) compared a head pinned to v520 (4.6% volatile) against vfmac003 (16.04%) — datasets built at DIFFERENT thresholds — and ml/cli.py:585 carries a comment recording an earlier burn by the same class ('the legacy hardcoded 0.003 that mis-scores the fleet', MB-20260628-RG4-THRESH).

NOT FIXED HERE — TIER-3. Changing the default changes the LABEL DEFINITION of every dataset built without an explicit argument, which changes what models learn. Three options for the operator, in preference order:
  1 (recommended) Make it REQUIRED, no default. A caller must state the threshold; the canonical builder already does. Nothing can drift because nothing is implicit. Cost: any ad-hoc caller must be updated (grep shows the canonical builder + the MES path already pass it explicitly).
  2 Stamp the resolved vol_threshold into the dataset dir's metadata AND require every consumer that compares distributions to read it. This is the provenance-consumer-guard shape and is strictly better than (3), but it is more code.
  3 Change the default 0.003 -> 0.005. Cheapest, but it silently reinterprets any historical rebuild and leaves the same class of trap for the MES data-driven path.
Recommendation: (1) + (2). (3) alone re-arms the trap.

RESOLVED — operator approved 'make it required' 2026-07-30.
A BETTER argument than the original 'stamp it' proposal emerged while implementing: `DatasetBuilder.build` records `effective_build_params` from the kwargs it was PASSED, so a DEFAULTED value never reaches iter_rows_kwargs and never lands in metadata.json. Proven locally before changing anything (omit the param -> build_params records ONLY market_raw_path). Requiring the kwargs means the resolved value is ALWAYS recorded — the metadata hole closes for free.
MEASURED ON THE TRAINER (issue #8122): 25 of 38 on-disk market_features dirs have NO recorded vol_threshold — INCLUDING BTCUSDT/15m/v520, the dataset the live advisory BTC head pins. 5 distinct values are in use across recorded dirs ({None:25, 0.005:10, 0.0005687:1, 0.0062791:1, 0.0003346:1}). The hole was real and sitting under the live real-money vol gate, not hypothetical.
SCOPE: 43 python call sites updated to pass 0.005 (the PRODUCTION value, deliberately not the orphaned 0.003); every shell/YAML site already passed it. Requiring it does NOT retro-fix the 25 existing dirs — that is a separate follow-up (BL-20260730-DATASET-DIRS-MISSING-VOL-THRESHOLD).
items.resolution_criteria: Operator picks an option; vol_threshold can no longer be implicit, or the resolved value is stamped and read by every distribution consumer.

items.title: [ml][tooling] `python -m ml <heavy-cmd> --help` acquires the trainer heavy-job lock before arg parsing — printing help queues behind a training run
items.description:
VERIFIED: ml/cli.py::main resolves `cmd = argv[0]` and, at L1100, `if cmd in _HEAVY_COMMANDS: _heavy_lock = _acquire_heavy_lock(...)` — BEFORE the `build-dataset`/`validate-dataset` dispatch (L1102-1105) and before `_build_parser().parse_args()` (L1108-1109). `--help` is just another argv element at that point.

So `python -m ml build-dataset --help` takes the shared flock on a 1-core trainer VM with a FIFO queue: it blocks behind any running training cycle, and while held it blocks the next real job. The lock is bound for the whole process lifetime by design (correct for a real run), so a help invocation holds it until argparse exits. On a clean-timeout it raises SystemExit(75) — a documentation lookup failing with a queue-timeout exit code.

This is adjacent to the diagnostic-provenance class rather than an instance of it (nothing is mislabelled), but it shares the root: the tool's OBSERVABLE behaviour disagrees with what the invocation says it is doing. It is filed here because it was surfaced by the same sweep and would otherwise be lost.

FIX (Tier-1, trainer-autonomous, NOT applied here to keep this PR to one class): hoist a pure-help/version short-circuit above the lock — if any of {-h, --help, --version} appears in argv, dispatch to the parser and return without ever calling _acquire_heavy_lock. Guard it with a test asserting `main(['build-dataset','--help'])` never touches the lock. Deliberately left unmerged here because ml/cli.py is the trainer's real entry point and it deserves its own change + test rather than riding a tooling-guard PR.

items.title: [tooling] new-table-wiring-guard matched PROSE and accepted a presence-only marker — the cheapest way to silence it was to name a table that does not exist
items.description:
Two defects that made the guard's own output untrustworthy. A guard is a diagnostic; 'clean' is a claim a human acts on.

  1 PROSE MATCHING. `_CREATE_TABLE_RE = CREATE\s+TABLE` fired on any added line containing the words — a docstring sentence or a comment describing the rule. A guard that flags prose trains reviewers to wave its findings through, which is the alarm-fatigue failure this repo already classes as its own P1 bug (MB-20260719-DATASET-AUDIT-NOISE).
  2 PRESENCE-ONLY MARKER. Any `# data-wiring:` line anywhere in the file's added lines cleared every finding in that file, content unchecked. The path of least resistance to silencing a real finding was therefore to add a marker naming a table that does not exist — the guard actively taught contributors to lie to it.

FIX (this PR): (1) the pattern now requires an actual table NAME after CREATE TABLE and skips comment/docstring lines; (2) the marker must name either the table itself or an identifier that appears in the change's added lines, and — the subtle half — the annotation line is EXCLUDED from its own evidence pool, otherwise its own prose validates it. A marker that names nothing real now produces a distinct, explanatory finding rather than silence. (3) The all-clear now prints its denominator ('N changed file(s) scanned, 0 unannotated CREATE TABLE') so 'clean' is distinguishable from 'scanned nothing'.

The same verified-annotation rule is what the new diagnostic-provenance-guard uses for its `# provenance:` override, so the lesson is encoded in both. All 33 pre-existing new-table-wiring tests still pass.
items.resolution_criteria: Prose no longer matches; an annotation naming nothing real no longer clears a finding; the all-clear carries a denominator.

items.title: [ops][tooling] bybit_bracket_audit's roll-up printed 'every audited symbol is fully SL-covered' over a 444.7% over-coverage
items.description:
VERIFIED in code: the verdict ladder (L216-222) has no OVER_COVERED bucket — `covered + eps >= size` resolves to PROTECTED regardless of how far above `size` the summed SL legs run — and the roll-up (L397-411) buckets only PARTIALLY_NAKED / NAKED / *_UNRELIABLE, so an over-covered symbol fell into the `else` and printed the all-clear.

'Fully SL-covered' is LITERALLY TRUE at 444.7% coverage. That is what makes it sub-class A2 rather than a simple mislabel: the summary asserts a clean bill of health far stronger than the verdict measured, and a reader who stops at the roll-up walks past live leg over-accumulation — the very condition the runtime's own _check_broker_naked_bybit_positions flags as `over_covered` (BL-20260730-BYBIT1-XRP-LEG-OVERACCUM-WORSENING, live-verified firing the same day). The audit and the runtime disagreed about the same position, and only the audit was being read.

BLAST RADIUS: this audit is the operator-facing check for whether real-money positions are protected. It did not mis-state NAKED (under-coverage was always bucketed correctly), so no position was reported protected while actually naked — the failure is a missed anomaly, not a false safety claim about stop coverage.

FIX (this PR): over-coverage gets its own roll-up bucket with its own explanatory line ('not a naked risk but not clean either'), FLAT symbols are excluded from the denominator, the all-clear now carries the count it ranges over, and the JSON summary gains a `rollup` block so a machine consumer sees the same three numbers.
items.resolution_criteria: Over-coverage is bucketed and named; the all-clear carries its denominator.

  bucket        feed-A ADX            feed-B ADX            delta

  transitional  +29.4913  n= 86        +4.5742  n= 90       -24.92

THE POINT IS NOT THAT THE FEEDS DISAGREE -- THEY BARELY DO. 331/357 entry times (92.7%) are shared and on those the two feeds total 67.8283 vs 68.8762 (1.05R apart). Aggregate regime base rates differ by under 0.5pp (chop 30.0 vs 29.7, transitional 18.8 vs 18.8, trending 51.1 vs 51.5). Two near-identical inputs, and a single bucket still moves by a quarter of the strategy's lifetime net-R.

MECHANISM: the regime axis is a HARD CUTOFF (chop <20, transitional 20-25, trending >=25) applied to a noisy rolling indicator, and the per-trade R distribution is heavy-tailed (avg_win_r 2.57, max_mfe_r 18.9). A handful of large winners sitting near ADX 20 or 25 flip buckets on sub-1% input differences and carry tens of R with them. This is structural fragility of the instrument, NOT a bug in either run and NOT a data-quality problem -- every component is individually correct, which is the seam-defect signature docs/sprint-logs/S-PROVENANCE-EXITLEAK-ROOTCAUSE-2026-07-30.md documents.

WHY THIS IS CRITICAL RATHER THAN INTERESTING: per-regime net-R IS the evidence base for Tier-3 regime cells. The rec #5 programme graded ~35 strategy-regime rows on single-feed net-R, and one of those verdicts SHIPPED a live cell (gld_pullback_1h trending-short, operator-approved #7923). Nothing in that pipeline reports feed-sensitivity, so a verdict that would flip under a different-but-equally-valid feed is indistinguishable from one that would not. NOTE the scope limit honestly: this was measured on BTCUSDT 1h with two crypto feeds; gld is a Yahoo-sourced equity on a different path, so it is NOT shown to be wrong -- it is shown to be UNVALIDATED against a defect class its pipeline cannot currently detect.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT (design, not applied -- scripts/research/ is ceded this session): report per-cell feed-sensitivity as a first-class output. Minimum viable version: re-tag the same emitted trades against a second independent feed and publish the per-bucket delta beside the number, the way vol_coverage and rCoverage already publish their own honesty metric. A cell whose sign flips across feeds is not gradeable and must not reach a Tier-3 proposal. A boundary-distance histogram (how much net-R sits within +/-1 ADX of 20 and 25) would quantify exposure per strategy cheaply.

IMMEDIATE CONSEQUENCE: no per-regime net-R number anywhere in this repo should be quoted as decision-grade until it carries a feed-sensitivity figure. That includes the numbers in merged PR #8118 (already marked UNSAFE) and the rec #5 matrix results.

updates.note:
DETECTION SHIPPED (operator-directed, same session). scripts/research/regime_tag_emitted.py now emits two honesty metrics in the same shape as vol_coverage / rCoverage:
  (1) BOUNDARY EXPOSURE - always computed, no second feed needed, so there is no run for which it is unavailable. Share of sum|net_R| sitting within +/-band ADX of the 20/25 cutoffs, per bucket, plus the largest single near-boundary |R| (one trade able to move a bucket alone). ABSOLUTE value deliberately: a +8R and a -8R at a cutoff are BOTH one relabel from moving, and netting them first would report 0% for a maximally-fragile grade.
  (2) FEED SENSITIVITY - optional --sensitivity-data: re-tags the SAME trades against a second feed's ADX and reports per-bucket delta + any SIGN FLIP. Holding the trade set fixed is the point: every delta is attributable to LABELLING, never to generation. A sign-flipped bucket cannot source a Tier-3 proposal in EITHER direction, at any n.
Both are DECLARED on every run (feed_sensitivity_checked: bool + a 'NOT CHECKED' console line), the same contract as vol_axis: present|absent - a grade with no second feed must never read as one that was cross-checked.

A TAUTOLOGY WAS CAUGHT AND FIXED DURING THE BUILD, worth recording because it is the exact class the repo now guards: the first working version reported `transitional` at 100% exposure on EVERY run. Shipping that would have manufactured a permanent false alarm from a real number. Fixed with _structural_floor_pct: every bucket now reports the floor its own WIDTH implies plus the excess over it, and `trending` returns None rather than an invented floor because it is unbounded above.

items.title: [ml][data] killzone/bias are 100% NaN in trade_outcomes — quarantined the only learning trade-outcome model
items.description:
dataset_audit flagged `trade-outcome-lgbm-v1` with nan_fraction 1.0000 on BOTH `killzone` and `bias`, setting quarantine=true. The trainer then logged manifest_audit_skipped_enforced every cycle, so the ONLY feature-learning trade-outcome model (the rest are constant baselines) has not trained at all. The label itself is healthy — `won` 251 True / 581 False, 2 classes, unflagged — so this was a DEAD FEATURE quarantine, not a degenerate label.

The signal builders DO emit these: strategy_signal_builders.py:331, advisory_sizing.py:78 and vwap.py:872 all set `killzone` in the signal meta. So the values exist at signal time and are lost somewhere between meta and the trades column. That is the INVERSE of the defect this session root-caused: instead of written-and-never-read, this is read-and-never-written — a feature consumed by a model that nothing populates.

Immediate unblock: both columns removed from the manifest's feature_columns and categorical_columns. They carried zero information, so the model loses nothing and can finally train. That is a WORKAROUND, not the fix.
items.resolution_criteria: Trace meta['killzone']/['bias'] from the signal builder to the trades row and find where it is dropped (likely the INSERT in execute._log_trade_to_journal not carrying the meta keys). Fix the writer. Then re-add both to the manifest ONLY after dataset_audit shows a non-degenerate nan_fraction — re-adding them while still dead just re-quarantines the manifest. Historical rows stay NaN either way; the feature only becomes useful going forward.

updates.note: RESOLVED by weekly /system-review evidence pass: Quarantine consequence fixed: killzone/bias dropped from the manifest as 100%-NaN dead features (documented in-file); trade-outcome-lgbm-v1 unquarantined and training daily (verified in 08-01 cycle this review).

items.source: Found while building the vol_threshold backfill — I had to establish which parameters actually determine a label before I could claim to recover one. That check caught a mislabel in my OWN merged comment from PR #8116 the same day.
items.title: [ml] market_features `trend_threshold` is INERT — it affects no emitted column, yet it is a required kwarg and I documented it as label-defining
items.description:
`_label_regime` accepts `trend_threshold` and then ignores it: its own docstring says "kept in the signature for backward compatibility but is no longer used", because the 3-class -> 2-class collapse (S-ML-REGIME-CLASSIFIER-FIX, 2026-05-20) removed the 'trend' class. The trend-axis label that DOES exist (`trend_regime_label`) keys off `trend_chop_max`/`trend_trend_min` via the Kaufman efficiency ratio, not this parameter. So `trend_threshold` determines nothing.

TWO CONSEQUENCES.
(a) DOC DEFECT, already fixed in the PR that files this: PR #8116's comment said 'these two DEFINE regime_label' of BOTH thresholds. True of vol_threshold, false of trend_threshold — a mislabel introduced in the PR about mislabels, which is the sharpest possible argument for 'verify, don't assert'. Both the module docstring and the inline comment now state the inertness plainly.
(b) OPEN QUESTION for the operator: should an inert parameter stay REQUIRED? It is currently required, and I kept it that way deliberately — every production caller already passes it, and a required kwarg always lands in metadata.json::build_params, so the dir records what the caller believed it was building with. The counter-argument is real though: requiring a parameter that does nothing invites exactly the wrong inference (a reader diffing two dirs will read a trend_threshold difference as a label difference when it cannot be). Options: (1) leave required + documented inert (status quo); (2) drop it from the signature — callers passing it are absorbed by **_ and it still reaches build_params, so no caller breaks; (3) remove it from every caller too, losing the record of intent. I lean (2): it stops the wrong inference at the source while keeping the recorded value. NOT doing it unasked — it touches the dataset builder's public signature.
items.trigger_condition: n/a
items.resolution_criteria: Operator picks an option; no reader can infer a label difference from a trend_threshold difference.

updates.note: RESOLVED by weekly /system-review evidence pass: market_features.py documents trend_threshold as INERT with the real label-driving params named; keeping it required is a recorded provenance decision (b9234ba).

items.title: [data-integrity] bybit_1 journal reports ~50x the exchange position on SOLUSDT (2836.1 vs 55.4) — phantom open rows with DEAD protective legs
items.description:
MEASURED, both sides of the comparison, same minute:
  exchange (/api/diag/exchange_positions, bybit_1): SOLUSDT Buy 55.4 · BTCUSDT Buy 0.01 · BNBUSDT Sell 9.72 · ADAUSDT Buy 130562.0 · ETHUSDT Sell 109.92
  journal open rows (bybit_bracket_audit #8132):
    SOLUSDT qty_sum=2836.1 across #4213 pairs_sol_eth_a 55.4 (leg ALIVE), #4220 ict_scalp_sol_15m 1844.6 (leg DEAD), #4243 ict_scalp_sol_5m 936.1 (leg DEAD)
    BTCUSDT qty_sum=1.553 across #4112 pairs_bnb_btc_b 0.01 (ALIVE) and #4179 ict_scalp_5m 1.543 (leg DEAD)
    BNBUSDT qty_sum=13.43 across 5 rows vs position 9.72, three with NO tracked leg

Under one-way netting the exchange position should equal the sum of same-direction open rows. It does not: ~2780 SOL and ~1.54 BTC of journal-open quantity has no exchange backing, and in every divergent case the row's tracked SL leg is DEAD. The shape is consistent with rows that never filled, or that closed at the broker without the journal being updated — this item does NOT assert which, because nothing measured so far distinguishes them.

SCOPE: bybit_1 is account_class=paper, so there is no real-money exposure. bybit_2 (real_money) was clean in the same audit — 100.0% coverage, both legs ALIVE, journal matching the exchange exactly. That contrast is the reason to treat this as a data bug rather than a venue problem.

WHY IT MATTERS ANYWAY: a phantom open row is invisible to the naked-position sweeps (the exchange position IS covered, so coverage reads fine), it inflates open-exposure analytics, and if such a row is ever closed by a reconciler it books a fabricated PnL — which lands in the ML labels, the exact exposure BL-20260730-ML-LABELS-IGNORE-PNL-PROVENANCE tracks. This is the `journal_qty_divergent` signal that order_monitor._check_broker_naked_bybit_positions already emits DETECT-ONLY; this item records concrete instances against it.

NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately. Reconciling a phantom row means deciding whether to close it and with what exit price — a money-DB writeback (Tier-2) whose wrong answer manufactures exactly the fabricated PnL described above. The right next step is to establish WHY the rows diverged (never-filled vs closed-unrecorded) before choosing a remediation, not to null them out.

  state=connected · connected=true · account_data_ready=true · breaker_open=FALSE · breaker_seconds_remaining=0.0 · consecutive_failures=0 · likely_wedged=FALSE

items.title: [ci][ops] registry-keyed guards cannot police an action MISSING from the registry — a half-registered system-action passes CI (fixed + guarded)
items.description:
CORRECTION to my own first draft of this item, which claimed 'nothing cross-checks the three lists against each other'. That was WRONG and I had not read the tests before writing it. `tests/ops/test_system_actions_workflow.py` cross-checks thoroughly — choice options, SCRIPT dispatch, tier alternation, notify_run.sh, the docs table and wrapper existence.

THE REAL DEFECT is narrower and more interesting: every one of those guards iterates `EXPECTED_ACTIONS`. An action added to the WORKFLOW but never added to that dict is absent from every loop, so the entire suite passes on a broken registration. A registry-keyed guard cannot police an entry missing from the registry.

PR #8149 added `backfill-fabricated-exits` to the SCRIPT-name case only. CI was green; the dispatch then died with `Permission denied (publickey)` because the Validate step hit `*) exit 2` before the SSH-key step.

THE STING: `test_validate_step_classifies_every_action_into_a_tier` was written for this precise incident (`backfill-account-class`, 2026-06-15) and its docstring even describes the confusing `Permission denied (publickey)` symptom — and it could not catch the recurrence, because it too loops over `EXPECTED_ACTIONS`.

FIXED in #8152: the action is registered in all six places, and a REVERSE-direction guard now asserts every `<action>) SCRIPT="…"` mapping in the workflow appears in `EXPECTED_ACTIONS`. Verified by reproduction — removing the entry makes the new guard fail with exactly the #8149 shape, and restoring it goes green (324 tests).

STILL OPEN, filed separately below as the diagnostic half: the failure comment posted back to the issue lists 'Common causes: VM_SSH_KEY secret unset/corrupted; SSH host unreachable; wrapper script returned nonzero' — none of which was tested or true. The real cause reaches the run log via ::error:: but never the comment, so the operator-facing message points AWAY from the fault. A `pull-and-deploy` had succeeded minutes earlier on the same secret, which is what disproved the suggested causes.
items.resolution: Fixed + guarded in #8152 (reverse-direction check, reproduction-verified). The unprovenanced failure comment remains open as BL-20260731-SYSTEM-ACTION-FAILURE-COMMENT-UNPROVENANCED.

items.title: [ml][data] backtest augmentation is fully built and has NEVER been fed — zero is_backtest=1 rows in trades
items.description:
Measured on the live journal 2026-07-31 (trainer-diag #8155): of 833 closed rows with non-null pnl, `is_backtest=0` for 833 and there are ZERO `is_backtest=1` rows — none, in any month.

The augmentation path is fully built and unused: `trade_outcomes` takes `include_backtest`, emits a `source` ('live'|'backtest') column for exactly this purpose, and `ml/experiments/splitters.py::split_live_holdout` exists to train on simulated rows while holding out real ones. The family docstring states the intent — 'manufactures more labeled training data than the ~80 real trades collapse the decision models against (gap G4)'. Nothing ever writes the rows: the backtest harness records to the `backtest_results` TABLE, not to `trades.is_backtest=1`.

CONSEQUENCE: the decision-model corpus is capped at live trades only (833, and 506 after the provenance filter), and every 'not enough data to train' conclusion in this repo has been reached WITHOUT the augmentation that was built to solve it. Operator raised this directly 2026-07-31: 'there is lots of infrastructure to backtest and backfill rows of data so that we can train things not on live data only.' They are right; the infrastructure exists and is not connected.

NOTE the trap for whoever picks this up: switching a manifest to `split_live_holdout` BEFORE the rows exist RAISES ('no synthetic (train) rows') rather than degrading — it would convert a quarantine-skip into a hard failure. Write the rows first, then switch the split.

Same defect class as the two other findings this session: infrastructure READ but never WRITTEN (cf. BL-20260731-KILLZONE-BIAS-NEVER-PERSISTED), the mirror of provenance WRITTEN but never READ.

[RESOLVED-VERIFIED 2026-08-04] The augmentation was FED for the first time: trades.is_backtest=1 went 0 -> 1473 (standing datasets-out/backtest_trades.db), and the pooled head trained on 5,094 backtest + 324 real + 217 paper rows (~19x the ~78-row wall). MEASURED on a real live holdout WITH the paper-book population (trainer #8460): the augmented meta-label learns a REAL edge (26%->57% win-rate on its selected slice, net-R positive) but BELOW the usable-volume floor (4-6% coverage) -> not a deployable filter yet. Binding constraint proven = the TRUSTED EVAL BOOK (324 real trades; honest-provenance guard correctly excludes fabricated paper pnl), which backtests cannot grow. The breach ('never fed') is CLOSED and made un-repeatable by the new training-population-guard (config/training_population.yaml). Full record: docs/research/S-P0-LABEL-AUGMENT-2026-08-04.md.

updates.note: SHARPENED, still open. The MES augmentation run (#8318, 2026-08-01/02) exercised the full chain end-to-end (config-exact 10y ES_F backtest to 26 rows to include_backtest builds to 2 shadow baselines), but per docs/sprint-logs/S-WEEKLY-REVIEW-EXEC-2026-08-01.md the rows were written to a schema-bootstrapped standing sidecar db (backtest_trades_mes.db, merged at nightly build time via #8326), NOT to trades.is_backtest=1 in the live journal. So this item's core observation — zero is_backtest=1 rows in the live `trades` table, pooled/crypto decision models unfed — is LIKELY still true, but needs a fresh live is_backtest count to confirm (not asserting it without the read). The generic pipeline is proven; the gap is that only MES has been pointed at it and via a sidecar, not the pooled models. Cross-ref ml MB-20260530-001 (verified-state update 2026-08-02) + docs/research/WORK-PLAN-2026-08-02.md W1.2/W2.1. Kept open.

CONFIRMED with a hard count — trainer-diag census #8398 (2026-08-02): is_backtest=0 on ALL 4319 live journal rows (0 rows with is_backtest=1). So the MES backtest augmentation rows (#8318, 26 trades) went to the standing sidecar backtest_trades_mes.db, NOT trades.is_backtest=1 in the live journal, exactly as this item observed. The A1 pooled/crypto extension (W1.2/W2.1) remains the open work.

Re-validated by /health-review 2026-08-03. No live-health regression tied to this item this window (trader healthy, 7/7 checks ok, all 7 live broker accounts reachable, notifications banner clean, DB 717MB/no errors). Condition unchanged; remains blocked on its declared tier/owner — no in-session Tier-1 fix available. Kept open.

RESOLVED. system-actions.yml's 'Reply to issue with outcome' step no longer prints the static 'Common causes: VM_SSH_KEY unset; SSH unreachable; wrapper nonzero' list on every failure. It now branches on the actual failure STAGE via `exitCode === ''` (the `exec` step publishes exit_code ONLY when it ran): a PRE-EXEC abort (validation/allowlist/missing-input) states 'FAILED BEFORE the VM action ran — NOT an SSH/VM/credential problem; the failing step + its ::error:: are on the run page', while a wrapper failure (exit set) states 'the wrapper RAN and returned exit N' and only THEN scopes in the VM-side causes. Exactly the diagnostic-provenance sub-class A fix CLAUDE.md prescribes (branch on the stage, don't reword the label). Verified: YAML parses + the embedded github-script JS passes `node --check`. The 2026-07-31 allowlist-miss case (which printed all 3 false causes minutes after a successful deploy) now reports the honest pre-exec stage.

items.title: [ops][diagnostics] system-action failure comment names causes no code path tested
items.description:
Split out of BL-20260731-SYSTEM-ACTION-HALF-REGISTERED (whose code half is fixed).

On any failure, system-actions.yml posts a STATIC cause list: 'VM_SSH_KEY secret unset/corrupted; SSH host unreachable; wrapper script returned nonzero'. It is printed regardless of which step failed, and nothing in the comment reveals that it is a guess.

Observed 2026-07-31: an allowlist miss (Validate step, `*) exit 2`) produced that comment verbatim. All three suggested causes were false — a `pull-and-deploy` had succeeded minutes earlier on the same secret. The true cause was printed via ::error:: in the run log but never surfaced to the reader.

This is diagnostic-provenance sub-class A (a failure message naming a cause no code path tested), and CLAUDE.md's prescribed fix applies directly: branch on the actual failure STAGE rather than rewording the label. The workflow already knows the stage — EXIT_CODE is empty for a pre-flight abort vs set for a wrapper failure — so the comment can state which stage failed instead of listing causes it never checked.

items.source: Observed live in trainer-vm-diag issue #8157, whose own relay output ended with `Expected: command not found` after the real work completed.
items.title: [fixed] trainer-vm-diag executed the issue body's PROSE — the cmd extractor stripped fence lines but never stopped at the CLOSING fence
items.description:
The `cmd:` extractor in .github/workflows/trainer-vm-diag.yml terminated on two conditions only: the next unindented `word:` key (BL-20260607-002), or end of body. A fenced `cmd:` block therefore did not end at its closing ```; every line after it — explanatory paragraphs, the `---` rule, the attribution footer — was appended to the script handed to bash.

Live instance: issue #8157 (the vol_threshold apply). Its trailing paragraph ran as commands, producing `Expected: command not found`, `vol_threshold: command not found`, and a failed `cd` — after the real work, so that run's RESULT is unaffected and its output is trustworthy.

It was harmless there and is not harmless in general. Prose routinely contains backticks (command substitution — a markdown-quoted `rm -rf /tmp/x` would have been SUBSTITUTED, not printed), parentheses (the standard `_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_` footer is a bash syntax error), and redirect characters. A body that reads as documentation must never execute as code.

Same family as BL-20260720-TRAINERDIAG-FENCE, which added the fence-line STRIP but not the fence-based TERMINATION — the strip made the leak quieter (no stray ``` command) without closing it.
items.resolution_criteria: Extractor tracks fence state across the whole body and exits on the closing fence while inside the cmd block; covered by tests/test_trainer_diag_cmd_extraction.py, which runs the REAL awk program extracted from the workflow YAML (not a copy, which would drift) and was verified to FAIL against the pre-fix extractor.

items.title: [meta][STRUCTURAL] every CI guard in this repo checks CODE SHAPE — nothing checks the CLAIMS that Tier-3 decisions are actually made from. 5 claim-defects in one session, each filed as a harmless one-off
items.description:
THE OPERATOR'S POINT, restated so it is not softened: filing each of these as its own row is what lets the pattern survive. Individually every one reads as 'caught and fixed, no harm done'. Collectively they are a single recurring defect with no preventer, and the next session repeats it from a clean context. This row exists so the CLASS is the tracked object.

WHAT HAPPENED (one session, 2026-07-30/31, all self-caught, none by a repo mechanism):
  1. Epoch-mismatched comparison stated as a finding — 9.1% offline vs 1% live over DISJOINT windows (withdrawn #8102).
  2. Same error again, different dressing — 'the ML vol axis reads calm ~99% of the time' generalised from ~979 live rows; the full 175,272-row replay says 8.92%, ranging 0.44%-30.42% monthly (corrected #8118).
  3. A decision-grade finding published off an unvalidated instrument — trend_donchian transitional/calm at +32.66R against an ACTIVE REAL-MONEY gate cell (#8118), destroyed by my own follow-up 15 minutes later (#8119) and root-caused as an ADX labelling artifact (#8144).
  4. A diagnostic printing max(proba) under the label P(volatile) — INVERTED, so a 97%-CALM head read as saturated volatile; nearly escalated as a false P1 against the live BTC vol gate (#8091).
  5. A public failure diagnosis naming a cause no code path had tested — a diag relay blaming 'VM down' for a request that never reached the VM (#8097).
  (+ a 6th caught pre-merge during #8147: a boundary metric that would have reported `transitional` 100% fragile on EVERY run — a tautology of the band's 5-ADX width, i.e. a permanent false alarm.)

THE STRUCTURAL OBSERVATION — this is the actionable part.
This repo has an unusually strong guard family: canonical-db-resolver, env-gate-guard, silent-empty-guard, provenance-consumer-guard, diagnostic-provenance-guard, new-table-wiring-guard, writer-conformance-guard, strategy-coverage-guard, qty-legalization-guard, layer-guard. EVERY ONE OF THEM CHECKS CODE SHAPE.
A wrong NUMBER in a backlog row, a PR body, a ROADMAP cell, or a research doc passes all of them. And those numbers are precisely what Tier-3 cell/promotion/risk decisions get made from. **The code surface is heavily guarded; the evidence surface is unguarded.** Every defect above lived on the evidence surface, which is why zero of them were caught by CI and all of them were caught by a bar the session happened to set for itself. A bar that depends on the session setting it is not a control.

A DOC-PLACEMENT DEFECT MADE IT WORSE, and it is cheap to fix. CLAUDE.md ALREADY carries the exact rule that would have stopped defects 1 and 2: 'ALWAYS STATE THE POPULATION ... A headline whose sign flips on a filter choice is exactly the kind of number this module exists to stop trusting — including when it is ours.' It is well written and it was violated twice in one session by a session that had read it — because it lives UNDER the 'Number provenance' heading, scoped to PnL rows in the journal, so it does not read as governing research claims. The rule is right; its scope is wrong.

PROPOSED PREVENTERS (a review session should pick, refine, and land — none applied here):
  P1 (Tier-1, cheap, highest value): PROMOTE 'always state the population' out of the provenance section into a top-level canonical rule covering EVERY quantitative claim in any artifact — chat, PR body, backlog row, ROADMAP cell, research doc. Required basis: population + window + instrument + n. Mirrors the existing instruction-hierarchy mirroring already enforced by canonical-doc-coherence.
  P2 (Tier-1, mechanical): a `claim-basis-guard` in the existing guard family — a backlog row or research doc asserting a % or R figure must carry an explicit basis block. Same shape as check_backlog_refs. NOTE the lesson from new-table-wiring-guard recorded in CLAUDE.md: a presence-only marker is cheaper to LIE to than to satisfy, so the basis must be verified (n parses as an integer, window parses as a date range), not merely present.
  P3 (Tier-1, process): INSTRUMENT-BEFORE-FINDING — a new measurement instrument may not produce a decision-grade number until it emits its own honesty metric, shipped in the SAME PR. Precedent already exists and works: rCoverage, vol_coverage, and now boundary_exposure/feed_sensitivity (#8147). Defect 3 is exactly what happens without it.
  P4 (Tier-1, process): FULL-SPAN DEFAULT — a rate claimed as a standing property must be computed over the full available span or carry an explicit scope. Direct preventer for defects 1 and 2, which are the same error twice.

WHAT NOT TO DO WITH THIS ROW: do not close it by fixing the five instances — they are already fixed and closing on that basis is the exact failure mode the operator called out. It closes when a PREVENTER exists.
items.trigger_condition: n/a — a standing gap in the control surface, not an incident
items.resolution_criteria: At least P1 (rule promotion) AND one mechanical or process preventer are landed and in force. Explicitly NOT resolvable by fixing the individual instances.

updates.note: RESOLVED per its own criteria (P1 + one mechanical preventer landed): P1 — 'Always state the population' promoted to a TOP-LEVEL binding rule in docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md (new section after Honesty; CLAUDE.md provenance paragraph now points at it), covering every quantitative claim in every artifact, with the full-span and instrument-before-finding corollaries. P2 — claim-basis-guard (scripts/check_claim_basis.py + workflow): a NEW backlog row asserting %/R/$ evidence must carry a parseable denominator (n of M / n=N / count-noun / date-window); diff-scoped, failure path self-tested, first run caught a real basis-less row (BL-20260731-TRAINERDIAG-DOUBLE-EXECUTION, fixed). Guard is ADVISORY pending a ~0-false-positive soak, then promote via branch-protection-sync (the audit row tracks that tail). P3/P4 (instrument-before-finding as process, full-span default) are folded into the rule text as binding corollaries.

resolution_criteria AUTHORED. Re-validated: an umbrella row holding a P0-P3 plan, not a single defect. Keep as the index it is; its children are tracked separately.

items.resolution_criteria: THIS IS A CONTAINER ROW. It closes when each of the 12 enumerated NEW findings carries its own disposition recorded against its number here - fixed, filed as its own backlog row (with the id), or closed with a reason - and not before. It does NOT close on 'the P0-P3 plan was worked': a container that retires while any of the 12 is undisposed silently loses that finding, which is the specific way a consolidated audit row fails.

items.description: build_trainer_datasets.sh::build_family recovered row_count via a bash-expanded glob '<family>/*/*/*/metadata.json' passed to a python that read sys.argv[1] — the FIRST expanded match, alphabetical, i.e. the empty 2026-05-22 MES/all/v001 dir for trade_outcomes/execution_quality/setup_labels, and v001 (not the just-written v002) for review_journal. The all/all/v002 datasets the nightly build actually wrote were never read. Consequence: the 2026-07-31 full-system-audit item (7) concluded the outcome families were dead-but-green since May 22 — the FAMILIES were alive; the LOG was lying (sub-class B implicit input selection, the exact class diagnostic-provenance-guard exists for — this site predated the guard and was grandfathered as diff-scoped). Fixed: build_family parses the build's own 'wrote dataset under <dir>' stdout line (DatasetPaths.root) and reads THAT dir's metadata, emitting dataset_dir alongside row_count and an explicit 'count UNKNOWN (not zero)' note when unparseable. The genuinely-empty datasets (MES-scoped variants, review_journal, the rc-78 manifests) now surface per-cycle via manifest_training_staleness.py instead of hiding in a green stream.

items.title: [infra] trainer-vm-diag relay executed a cmd block twice (retry) — harmless for the idempotent GC, a hazard for any non-idempotent relay cmd
items.description: Evidence is one observed instance (issue #8188); the mechanism is unconfirmed — likely a workflow/step retry re-running the SSH command after the first execution's result failed to post. Follow-up for a review session: (1) check the run's job/attempt history (actions run 30643599945) to confirm the retry mechanism; (2) if confirmed, either make the relay execution at-most-once (e.g. a per-issue nonce/marker file on the VM checked before executing) or document the at-least-once semantics prominently in docs/claude/diag-relay.md + the trainer-vm-diag workflow header so future sessions write idempotent cmd blocks (the GC survived precisely because it re-scans before deleting). Do NOT treat 'output shows nothing changed' as 'nothing changed' on this relay until this is settled — verify end-state (df/ls), not the run's narration.
items.resolution_criteria: Retry mechanism confirmed from the Actions run history AND either at-most-once execution shipped or the at-least-once contract documented in docs/claude/diag-relay.md + the workflow file.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: .github/workflows/trainer-vm-diag.yml:113-136 has a dedup step, but it guards the wrong case: it bails only when a github-actions[bot] comment ALREADY EXISTS on the issue ('skipping the duplicate labeled-fire'). A retry that fires before any comment lands — which is exactly the observed case, since the posted output was the SECOND pass — sees no comment and re-executes. And docs/claude/diag-relay.md carries no at-least-once contract: grep for retry/at-least-once/at-most-once/idempot hits only :461 ('retry the original diag request'), which is advice to the caller, not a contract. — Cheap to close on the documentation branch of its own criteria.

Re-validated: a relay that can execute a cmd block twice is a hazard for any non-idempotent command. Same relay as BL-20260807-TRAINER-DIAG-RELAY-SILENT-CMD-TRUNCATION and BL-20260807-TRAINERDIAG-COLUMN0-PYTHON-KEYWORD-TRUNCATES-CMD — three independent defects in ONE relay's command handling. That is a class: the trainer relay's cmd extraction needs one owner, not three patches.

items.description:
MEASURED per-account map (journal total_size vs exchange size):

CLEAN / MATCHING:
  * bybit_2 (REAL MONEY): ETHUSDT short 0.06 = 0.06; XRPUSDT short 149.5 = 149.5. One residual: journal BTCUSDT short 0.004 (opened 07-31T01:51) absent from the 20:20Z exchange snapshot — likely closed broker-side inside the 11h skew; needs the same-moment check below before any action.
  * bybit_portfolio: ETH short 21.05 = 21.05; XRP short 48625.8 = 48625.8. BTC short journal 1.442 vs exchange 2.544 (journal UNDER by 1.102 — a post-09:35 add or a missing row; same-moment check).
  * ib_paper MHG short 25 = 25. alpaca books: 11 of 15 open groups match exactly (GDX/GLD/IAUM/IEF/QQQ/TLT both books); SLV/SPY/USO deltas are plausibly intraday churn (SLV longs opened 07-30T19:19; USO absent from the 09:35 journal) — same-moment check, not findings.

STRUCTURAL DIVERGENCE (cannot be skew):
  * bybit_1 (demo/paper): BTCUSDT journal 2 rows / 1.553 vs exchange 0.01 (155x); SOLUSDT 3 rows / 2836.1 vs 55.4 (51x — the audit's 'SOL 50x' CONFIRMED); ETHUSDT 3 rows / 109.92 vs 3.16 (35x); BNBUSDT 5 rows / 13.43 vs 9.72 (1.4x). ADAUSDT matches exactly (130562 = 130562), so the writer is not uniformly broken — the inflation pattern fits the one-way-netting partial-close class (rows never reduced when the netted exchange position shrank; the journal_qty_divergent detect-only signal fired live on 07-30 on exactly this).
  * ib_paper MGC: journal LONG 99 contracts (opened 07-30T08:24) with NO exchange position + 3 orphaned MGC rows totaling 244 contracts — the audit lead's 99-lot observation confirmed as journal-only.
  * Orphan backlog (status='orphaned', excluded from analytics): bybit_2 BTCUSDT 119 rows / 0.532 total (the known BL-20260713 orphan set); bybit_1 8 rows across 6 symbols incl. ADA 108761 + XRP 16839.5; ib_paper MHG 3.643 (the fractional-reject row).

TIER-2 REMEDIATION PROPOSALS (operator decision; NO journal writes made):
  1. Same-moment recheck first: one live-VM pass reading account_open_positions + journal in the same process (no sync skew) to finalize the small/ambiguous deltas (bybit_2 BTC 0.004, bybit_portfolio BTC, alpaca SLV/SPY/USO) before touching anything.
  2. bybit_1 + ib_paper phantom-open cleanup: close/mark the inflated journal rows 'superseded' with reconcile_status set and pnl left UNMEASURED (never priced from a mark — the provenance rule), reconciled against the broker snapshot. Paper-only accounts, but this data feeds ML datasets and paper analytics, so the cleanup is worth a reviewed batch.
  3. Root-cause (separate session, order-monitor logic): why partial closes on one-way-netted bybit_1 do not reduce the constituent journal rows — the same class the 07-30 journal_qty_divergent detector now flags per tick; wire its firings to this row.
  4. bybit_2's 119-row orphan set stays as-is pending its own investigation row (already excluded from analytics).
