items.title: [SECURITY][P0] @bict_trading_bot (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN — the operator command bot, ict-telegram-bot.service) renamed to a casino spam funnel — token treated as COMPROMISED; revoke + rotate + leak-vector investigation
items.description:
IMPACT while un-revoked: the holder of TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN can (a) send messages AS the operator command bot into the operator's chat — incl. fake trade notifications or phishing links styled as system pings; (b) change bot metadata (observed); (c) contend for getUpdates. The bot is the operator CONTROL PLANE (docs/TELEGRAM-SPEC.md: menu + trade/hourly notifications), so messages from it must be treated as untrusted until rotation.

TWO CANDIDATE VECTORS:
  1. Token leak (most likely — API-side rename needs only the token): repo is public; token lives in Actions secrets + the live VM env. Investigate: secret-scan history, workflow run logs that touched Telegram vars, VM .env exposure, any historical commit.
  2. Operator Telegram ACCOUNT compromise (BotFather edits need the owner account): operator to check Settings -> Devices for unknown sessions + confirm 2FA. If found, scope widens beyond this token.

REMEDIATION (in order):
  1. [operator, done/doing] BotFather -> /mybots -> @bict_trading_bot -> API Token -> REVOKE (kills the old token immediately; ict-telegram-bot.service loses its channel until rotation — trading itself is unaffected, the trader never depends on this bot).
  2. [operator] Restore name/intro in BotFather; check Devices/2FA (vector 2 rule-out); eyeball @claude_ict_comms_bot + prop bot profiles (different tokens — no tampering observed yet).
  3. [operator] Paste the NEW token into the Actions secret TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN (update in place).
  4. [claude] Dispatch sync-vm-secrets -> restart ict-telegram-bot.service -> verify the menu/notifications channel works + confirm the OLD token is dead (getMe returns 401).
  5. [claude] Leak-vector investigation + write-up; if the vector implicates other secrets, rotate those too (per-secret operator paste + sync).

Standing rule reinforced: any message from @bict_trading_bot between the rename and the rotation is UNTRUSTED — no trade-looking instruction arriving through it is to be acted on (the prop ticket flow rides the claude/prop bots, NOT this one, but under-pressure confusion is the attack surface).
items.resolution_criteria: Old token revoked AND confirmed dead (401 on getMe); new token live end-to-end (menu + notification verified); operator account sessions/2FA checked; leak-vector investigation concluded with a written finding (or an honest 'undetermined' with the checked surfaces listed); sibling tokens confirmed untampered.

updates.note: LEAK VECTOR FOUND AND CLOSED. (1) Vector: committed httpx logs — artifacts/health/health_snapshot.txt captured raw log lines containing 'POST https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates' with the FULL token in the URL. Census over the entire git history (git grep across all commits): 2 real tokens exposed (bot-ids 8712349762 + 8714773434 — the two rotated bots) + 1 test fixture; earliest exposure commit 2026-03-30T17:39Z; the repo has been PUBLIC since 2026-07-07 — so ~4 months in history, ~3.5 weeks world-readable. One token was STILL IN THE CURRENT TREE at HEAD. (2) Why the REQUIRED secret-scan check missed it for 4 months: scripts/secret_scan.py's telegram pattern began with \b, and there is no word boundary between 'bot' and the first digit — the pattern was structurally incapable of matching a token in its single most common leaked form (URL-embedded). The same \b mistake was independently reproduced during this investigation's first redaction attempt, confirming the mechanism. (3) Fixes shipped: token occurrences in the tree REDACTED (10 replaced, 0 residual, fixed scanner runs clean); scanner pattern corrected to (?<!\d)\d{8,12}:... with a war-story comment; tests/test_secret_scan_patterns.py added — the URL-embedded case verified to FAIL against the pre-fix pattern. (4) History-purge decision: NOT rewriting public git history (filter-repo would break every commit SHA referenced across issues/docs/deploys) — both leaked tokens are revoked+rotated, so history now contains only dead credentials; acceptable residual, recorded here. (5) Remaining for resolution: sync #8205 -> service restarts -> old-token-dead + new-token-live verification; operator Devices/2FA check (vector-2 rule-out is now largely moot given the token vector is proven, but cheap).

ROUND-1 ROTATION FAILED VERIFICATION, ROUND 2 IN FLIGHT. Round-1 findings (vm-diag #8211, 05:57Z): (a) ict-telegram-bot.service crashlooping 'TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN is not set in environment' (restart counter 107) — the Actions secret slot was empty at sync time; (b) ict-claude-bridge (old process; its round-1 restart issue #8208 never executed) still polling getUpdates with the LEAKED token (bot-id 8714773434) and receiving 200 OK — i.e. the claude-bot token had NOT actually been revoked; (c) the original leak channel was STILL OPEN: claude_bridge.py was the one bot entrypoint without the log-redaction wiring, so httpx printed full bot<TOKEN> URLs into journald (whence the committed health snapshot captured them). Operator re-rotated both tokens (chat, ~06:3x) -> round-2 propagation dispatched: set-env #8214 (TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN + restart ict-telegram-bot), #8215 (TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_TOKEN + restart ict-claude-bridge). Code fixes shipped with this update: claude_bridge.py wires install_redacting_filter()+suppress_httpx_logging(); install_redacting_filter now attaches to root HANDLERS (a logger-only filter is skipped by child-logger propagation — it never filtered the httpx records it existed for); log_redact's bare-token regex fixed for the same leading-\b blindspot as the scanner; child-propagation + glued-token regression tests added.

DIRECTIVE FOR THE NEXT /system-review (operator, chat 2026-08-01): as part of this incident, run a SCOPED SECURITY-BREACH SWEEP and record the findings against this row — (1) any OTHER secret exposed via the same channels: journald token-URL logs, committed health snapshots/artifacts, workflow run logs, git history (the secret-scan \b blindspot was generic to the telegram pattern — re-run the FIXED scanner over history, not just HEAD); (2) any unauthorized ACTIONS during the exposure window (2026-03-30 -> revocation): messages sent as either bot (operator chat history), getUpdates contention/webhook changes (getWebhookInfo), BotFather profile edits on the sibling bots (@claude_ict_comms_bot, prop bot); (3) VM auth logs for anomalous SSH (the tokens do not grant VM access, but rule out lateral use); (4) confirm the round-2 verification chain concluded: old tokens 401, both services stable on new tokens, redaction fix deployed (this row's resolution_criteria). Operator context: devices checked, nothing unknown, 2FA on (account-compromise vector ruled out).

updates.note: TRADER OUTAGE FOUND AND RECOVERED + ROTATION #3 REQUIRED FOR @bict_trading_bot. (1) P0: ict-trader-live was DOWN 05:29->06:54Z (~85 min, restart counter 389): the round-1 sync (#8205) mirrored the then-empty TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN secret into .env and restarted the trader; validate_startup hard-requires the credential -> crashloop. NO page fired because both Telegram bots were down on the same empty values (the alerting died with its subject). Broker-side SL/TP brackets stayed armed throughout (positions never naked); monitor/reconciler/alerting were the exposure. (2) Root cause of the round-2 set-env failure was OUR TOOLING: system-actions set-env had no SECRET_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN mapping, so #8207/#8214 resolved empty and silently blanked the key REGARDLESS of the operator's paste. Weekly /system-review evidence (vm-diag #8240, 08:32Z): rotation round 2 STILL not complete — the TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN now on the VM is MALFORMED (no ':' separator; the secret half was pasted without the numeric bot-id prefix — assert_telegram_token_shape from #8228 is refusing to boot, secret-free, exactly as designed). ict-telegram-bot restart counter 700; ict-claude-bridge also still 'activating'; liveness-watchdog Telegram POSTs 404 (old token revoked — good). Trader itself RECOVERED (active since ~07:33Z on 4c9decf6, ticking). OPERATOR ACTION: re-paste the FULL '<botid>:<secret>' values into Actions secrets TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN + TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_TOKEN, then re-run the set-env sync + service restarts and verify getMe 200 / old tokens 401. [SUPERSEDED minutes later by the parallel audit session's final verification in the next update — this observation was evidence-current at 08:32Z; resolution landed 08:34-08:37Z.]

RESOLVED — every resolution criterion verified. (1) OLD TOKENS DEAD: original @bict token 8712349762 getMe 401 (#8221), original claude token 8714773434 getMe 401 (#8219), AND the burned round-2 @bict replacement (secret half public in #8226) getMe 401 at 08:37Z (#8244) after the operator's round-4 revocation — the 08:27Z probe (#8235) had caught it STILL 200 (round 3 skipped the revocation; operator paged, revoked, exposure window closed). (2) NEW TOKENS LIVE END-TO-END: sync #8241 08:34:43Z; ict-telegram-bot + ict-claude-bridge both ACTIVE at 08:37Z (#8243); the queued rotation pings DELIVERED to the operator's phone (operator confirmed in chat, 'pings in'). (3) Operator devices/2FA checked, nothing unknown. (4) Leak-vector investigation concluded with written findings (committed httpx snapshot logs + the scanner/redactor leading-\b blindspot; both fixed with regression tests, #8206/#8217). (5) Sibling prop-bot profile untampered. Collateral recovered: the 85-min trader outage (own update above) and the PTB half-paste echo class (#8228 shape guard, trader warning-only). Full record: docs/sprint-logs/S-SECURITY-TOKEN-COMPROMISE-2026-08-01.md. Still open elsewhere: the /system-review breach sweep (directive above) and BL-20260801-TELEGRAM-CRED-CRASHLOOPS-MONEY-LOOP (Tier-3 design).

items.opened_by: claude (audit session — lesson of the 2026-08-01 trader outage)
items.source: ict-trader-live down 05:29->06:54Z (~85 min of 24/7 expected uptime; restart counter reached 389): validate_startup raises on a missing/empty TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, so a NOTIFICATION credential defect crashlooped the MONEY LOOP — while simultaneously killing the very alert channel that would have paged the operator about it.
items.title: [design][Tier-3 discussion] Startup validation hard-requires a Telegram credential — a notification-credential outage takes down the trading loop AND its own alarm
items.description: Today the coupling cost ~85 min of trader downtime (population: the single 2026-08-01 incident) with zero pages. The Prime Directive says the trader runs 24/7 and transient issues route through per-trade refusal, not process death; but validate_startup treats TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN like an exchange credential and refuses to boot without it. Options for operator decision: (a) keep hard-require (alerting is safety-critical; running unalerted is worse than not running); (b) degrade to a LOUD startup warning + run, with the account-reachability/notification machinery flagging the dead channel; (c) hard-require at first boot but tolerate at restart when positions are open (the state where downtime hurts most). Interim mitigations already shipped: set-env refuses empty values, sync is the canonical propagation path, token shape is validated secret-free. Route to /system-review or a Tier-3 chat decision.
items.resolution_criteria: Operator decision recorded on (a)/(b)/(c); if (b) or (c), the validate_startup change ships operator-approved with tests; if (a), this row closes with the rationale documented in the validation docstring.

updates.note: OPERATOR DECISION: option (b) APPROVED in chat 2026-08-01. IMPLEMENTED (Tier-3, operator-approved) on branch claude/2026-08-01-roadmap-backlog-ydfv6r (PR #8268), commit e01f9e9: validate_startup no longer appends the Telegram presence check to the fatal `errors` list — a missing/malformed TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN/CHAT_ID now routes through the new `_warn_degraded_alerting` (loud WARNING + best-effort WARN outcome to outcomes.jsonl, so the dead channel surfaces on the /api/bot/notifications operator_warning banner — a channel independent of Telegram). Never raises (lazy guarded outcomes import). Asymmetry preserved: exchange creds / symbol / risk stay FATAL. Tests: the two always-required tests inverted to non-fatal + 3 new (malformed-non-fatal, degraded-alerting-flagged, exchange-creds-stay-fatal); 17/17 pass; ruff clean. PENDING: merge of #8268 + a restart-bot-service redeploy (validate_startup runs at boot, so the new behaviour takes effect on the next restart) — keep open until deployed + live-verified, then close per resolution_criteria.

Weekly /system-review: trader recovered 07:33Z and is ticking on 4c9decf6; the remaining crashloops are ict-telegram-bot (counter 700, malformed token — see BL-20260801-TELEGRAM-BOT-TOKEN-COMPROMISE update) and ict-claude-bridge. Money loop healthy; alerting still dark pending operator token re-paste.

RESOLVED. The option-(b) decouple (PR #8268, commit e01f9e9) MERGED to main 19:22Z (squash) and is DEPLOYED to the live VM — /api/diag/version at 21:24Z reports the web-api on git_sha 44d379cd, which is downstream of #8268, so ict-git-sync has landed the new validation.py on disk. validate_startup runs at TRADER boot, so the trader picks it up on its next restart from the on-disk code (independent of the web-api's own restart); any future boot therefore uses the degrade-not-crash path. Basis for closing: (1) operator decision recorded (option b); (2) shipped + unit-tested (17/17, incl. missing/malformed→non-fatal + degraded-alerting-flagged + exchange-creds-stay-fatal); (3) code merged AND on the VM. The guard is behaviorally INERT while Telegram creds are valid (current state), so there is no live behavior to observe short of a missing/malformed-cred boot — which we will NOT deliberately reproduce in production (that is the exact money-loop outage this fix exists to prevent). Resolution_criteria (b) met: 'the validate_startup change ships operator-approved with tests' + deployed. If a future rotation ever leaves a cred missing, the trader will WARN + keep trading and surface the degradation on the /api/bot/notifications operator_warning banner instead of crashlooping.

items.title: [root-cause] One-way-netting partial closes never reduce constituent journal rows — order-monitor close attribution under netting
items.description: MECHANISM to investigate in src/runtime/order_monitor.py + execute.py close paths: under Bybit one-way netting, a position-level exit (bracket fire, reduce, manual close) shrinks the ONE netted exchange position, but the monitor's close detection closes at most the row whose own bracket/leg fired — sibling rows keep their full position_size and stay open until an eventual snapshot reconcile (or forever). Consequences measured: bybit_1 open-size inflation up to 155x (BTC 1.553 journal vs 0.01 exchange pre-cleanup); netting-guard suppression of re-entries for strategies with phantom opens; ML/paper analytics polluted. FIX DIRECTION (needs design, Tier-2/3): when the netted exchange size drops below the sum of open journal rows for (account,symbol,direction), the monitor should attribute the reduction — options: (a) reduce/close rows oldest-first (FIFO) with pnl UNMEASURED unless a matching broker close record exists; (b) close the specific row whose tracked sl/tp leg id fired (leg-id tracking exists since BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=partial) and treat residual shrink as FIFO; (c) periodic same-moment auto-reconcile job doing what the W1 manual batch did. Must respect the provenance contract (never price a close from a mark) and the pairs sleeve's isolated state (BNB surplus lives in pairs rows — coordinate with pairs_executor state, do not close its rows behind its back). Wire the journal_qty_divergent detector firings to this row.
items.resolution_criteria: Mechanism confirmed in code with the specific close path named; fix designed + operator-approved; after deploy, journal_qty_divergent stays silent for 7 consecutive days on all bybit accounts (population: every (account,symbol,direction) group the detector scans per tick).

updates.note: Mechanism CONFIRMED in code: order_monitor._close_trade_from_order_status closes only the fired row; _cascade_close_netted_siblings closes siblings ONLY when Bybit reports the netted position FLAT (its docstring: 'the ONE reliable moment we know every share closed') — so a PARTIAL shrink leaves siblings phantom-open. journal_qty_divergent already DETECTS every instance per tick but remediates nothing. One-look decision packet written: docs/research/netting-partial-close-packet-2026-08-02.md (options a=FIFO-in-monitor / b=leg-id+FIFO-in-monitor / c=periodic same-moment sidecar reconcile, pairs-excluded, PnL UNMEASURED). Recommendation (c)+(b)-precision — lowest blast radius; real-money bybit_2 is clean, so this is a data-integrity fix. AWAITING operator pick before implementing (Tier-2 order-path).

OPERATOR PICKED (c)+(b). SHIPPED: engine scripts/ops/reconcile_netting_rows.py (#8401, pure planner + 7 tests, inert) + the live-run half — scripts/ops/netting_reconcile_snapshot.py (reads open non-pairs journal groups + live exchange positions via account_open_positions + Bybit resting protective-leg ids -> engine input JSON) and the reconcile-netting-rows Tier-2 system-action (#8403, dry-run default; --apply superseded + UNMEASURED; pairs excluded; unreadable account skipped; never > surplus). WIRED: this row is now the remediation home for the live journal_qty_divergent detector — its firings on the bybit books are exactly the class this action reduces. RESOLUTION SIGNAL (unchanged): journal_qty_divergent silent 7 consecutive days on all bybit accounts after the reconcile is applied and the monitor-tick attribution gap is either accepted (sidecar papers over it) or closed. NEXT: live dry-run (system-action #8407) to quantify current phantoms -> operator OK -> --apply.

Re-validated by /health-review 2026-08-03. No live-health regression tied to this item this window (trader healthy, 7/7 checks ok, all 7 live broker accounts reachable, notifications banner clean, DB 717MB/no errors). Condition unchanged; remains blocked on its declared tier/owner — no in-session Tier-1 fix available. Kept open.

DESIGN PACKET WRITTEN: docs/netting-partial-close-attribution-DESIGN.md. Mechanism confirmed in code — _reconcile_open_trades (order_monitor.py:3597) reconciles each DB-open row against ITS OWN Bybit order via account_order_status, so a position-level exit that shrinks the netted position maps to no sibling row's order and closes at most one row. Three fix options costed against the provenance + pairs-isolation + runtime-bounds constraints; recommendation is (b) leg-id attribution with (a) FIFO as declared fallback, plus (c) periodic same-moment reconcile as backstop. Four operator decisions isolated in the packet sec 5. NOTE the honest trade surfaced: fixing size divergence LOWERS measured-pnl coverage, because rows with no broker close record must close UNMEASURED rather than priced from a mark — that will move the R4 gate's totalPnlMeasured and the operator should agree to it up front. Three cheap pre-implementation measurements still owed (sec 6): sl_order_id coverage among open rows, a fresh same-moment divergence census, and the pairs-owned row exclusion list. Still open — this is design only, the fix is Tier-2 and unapproved.

MEASURED same-moment 2026-08-06T11:40Z (relays #8516 journal / #8517 exchange), 33 open non-backtest rows. FOUR divergent (account,symbol,direction) keys, ALL bybit: bybit_1 SOLUSDT journal 2075.2 vs exchange 4.6 (451x, 4 rows) — WORSE than the 155x BTC case W1 measured 08-01, and a DIFFERENT symbol, so the condition is confirmed self-worsening not a single persisting instance; bybit_1 BNBUSDT 13.43 vs 5.49 (5 rows, the same BNB divergence W1 saw on 08-01, still unresolved); bybit_2 ETHUSDT 0.06 vs 0.04 (REAL MONEY — it was clean at the 2026-07-30 audit and is NOT clean now, so this can no longer be described as paper-only); bybit_portfolio ETHUSDT 27.42 vs 21.05. Every non-Bybit key is EXACTLY clean (12/12 across alpaca_paper, alpaca_portfolio, ib_paper) — those venues do not net, so the partial-close mechanism cannot fire there; a general journal-writing bug would have smeared across them, so this confirms the diagnosis. sl_order_id coverage among open bybit rows is 16/19 = 84.2%, so fix option (b) leg-id attribution is worth building with (a) FIFO covering the untracked 3. No pairs-owned rows open, so constraint 2 has an empty exclusion list today. Design packet sec 6 updated with the full census. Detector blind-spot fix (packet sec 2) shipped separately the same day.

POST-DEPLOY VERIFICATION OF THE DETECTOR FIX (PR #8519) IS INCOMPLETE — recorded so no future session assumes it passed. VERIFIED: the code is live. /api/diag/version returns git_sha 85e1f026 = the merged SHA (relay #8520), and the trader restarted ~12:45Z under ict-git-sync. NOT VERIFIED: that the hoisted journal_qty_divergent detector actually FIRES live on the four known-divergent keys. A complete, untruncated 90-second journalctl window (relay #8521, 12:56:30-12:58:00Z) contains ZERO src.runtime.order_monitor output of any kind — no divergence log, no over_covered, no routine monitor line. The detector logs only on anomaly, so absence is ambiguous between 'the sweep ran and found nothing' (which would contradict the 11:40Z census) and 'the sweep did not run in the sampled window'. This is INCONCLUSIVE, NOT a negative result, and must not be reported as either a pass or a fail. Also checked: bot.log does not exist on the VM (present:false), so journalctl is the only channel for monitor output. NEXT STEP: sample a window that certainly contains a monitor tick — determine the run_monitor_tick cadence relative to the per-symbol pipeline loop first (the 90s window showed many back-to-back symbol pipelines, so it may have landed entirely mid-cycle), then re-read. Incidental and CLEAN: /api/diag/ib_state (relay #8522) shows the 12:56-12:57 IB circuit-breaker-OPEN warnings were the TRANSITORY backoff, not a wedge — 2 of 3 clients connected, likely_wedged false on all three, breaker closed at write time, exec client 497 connected at 12:58:17. No action needed there.

POST-DEPLOY VERIFICATION NOW COMPLETE — supersedes the INCOMPLETE note above. The hoisted journal_qty_divergent detector FIRES LIVE. Relay #8525, monitor tick at 2026-08-06T12:58:17-19Z, all four keys from the 11:40Z census, matching exactly: bybit_1/BNBUSDT short 13.43 vs 5.49 (excess 7.94); bybit_2/ETHUSDT short 0.06 vs 0.04 (excess 0.02, REAL MONEY); bybit_portfolio/ETHUSDT short 27.42 vs 21.05 (excess 6.37); bybit_1/SOLUSDT long 2075.2 vs 4.6 (excess 2070.6). The wording is the NEW direction-aware line ('the exchange backs X on that side', 'side=short'), confirming the deployed code is the fixed version and not the old one. LEG OVER-ACCUMULATION also fired in the same sweep, which verifies the overcover_checked guard-set split (sharing anomaly_checked would have made that block unreachable and silently retired a live detector). METHOD NOTE for the next verifier: run_monitor_tick runs ONCE PER FULL TICK after run_one_tick iterates every symbol (src/main.py:647), and a full symbol sweep took ~12 minutes, so a short window lands mid-cycle and shows no monitor output at all; the bybit sweep is called near the END of run_monitor_tick (after the per-package loop and the other sweeps), so sample the minute AFTER the last symbol's pipeline result. PRECISION — what this does and does NOT prove: it proves the detector works and is direction-aware. It does NOT demonstrate a case the OLD code would have missed, because all four keys currently carry a LIVE (non-flat) exchange position, and the blind spot fixed was the FLAT case (size<=0 skipped before comparing). No symbol currently exhibits the flat case, so that half of the fix remains unexercised in production and is covered only by test_divergence_fires_when_exchange_is_FLAT.

items.source: vm-diag #8240 journalctl ict-liveness-watchdog.service: every per-minute run since the token rotation reads the heartbeat fine ('[OK] Trader heartbeat recovered', 'Latest beat is fresh') then dies on 'Telegram POST failed: HTTP Error 404' with exit status 2 (unit 'failed').
items.title: [watchdog] liveness watchdog unit fails (exit 2) when the Telegram POST fails — alert-delivery failure should not fail the whole check run
items.detail: The heartbeat check itself succeeds; the process exits non-zero only because the (revoked-token) Telegram notification POST 404s. Risk: the unit reads 'failed' in service checks and it is unclear whether an autoheal restart later in the flow would still have run after the alert exception. Tier-1 fix candidate: treat alert-delivery failure as WARN (log + continue, exit 0) so the dead-man switch's own health is decoupled from the messaging channel. Self-heals for the current incident once the operator lands the correct token, but the coupling remains.
items.resolution: Fixed in scripts/check_heartbeat.py: a failed Telegram alert POST no longer `return 2`s before autoheal. The old early-return meant a genuinely-stale trader got NO autoheal restart whenever the messaging channel was down (revoked-token 404). Now alert-delivery failure is a WARN (stderr + journal) and the run STILL executes _maybe_autoheal + persists the streak counter, then returns 0 — the dead-man switch's health is decoupled from the messaging channel. Alert-dedup state (last_status) is deliberately left unset on a send failure so the next per-minute run re-attempts delivery once Telegram recovers. Exit code 2 retired (docstring updated). Tests: test_main_alert_failure_does_not_fail_the_check (rc=0 + state persisted + last_status unset) + test_main_alert_failure_still_runs_autoheal (autoheal fires despite the alert POST failing); replaced test_main_returns_2_when_telegram_fails. 36/36 pass, ruff 0.15.8 clean.

items.title: [soak][Tier-1] allocator_soak regret is dominated by real-vs-prop VARIANT pairs, so mean_regret / disagree_pct do not measure strategy selection
items.description: In the 2026-08-06 tail every row is n_candidates=2, and 7 of 8 pairs are a strategy against its own prop variant (trend_donchian_eth vs trend_donchian_eth_prop x5, trend_donchian_sol vs _prop, eth_pullback_2h vs eth_pullback_prop_2h); only one pair is a genuine competition (ict_scalp_xrp_5m vs _15m). The variants differ ONLY in TP - same symbol, same side, near-identical entry/SL/confidence - so the prop variant's tighter TP mechanically scores lower under ev_net_r and agree:false fires every time. Example 2026-08-01T18:26: identical short, entry 1854.04 vs 1854.05, confidence 0.6125 vs 0.6106, scores 7.806 vs 3.172, logged as regret 4.634. A prop ticket and a real order are not substitutes competing for the same capital, so that 4.634 is a config fact, not EV left on the table. Consequence: the summary fields the /api/bot/allocator/soak envelope exposes (disagree_pct, mean_regret) overstate genuine allocator disagreement and must not be quoted without excluding variant pairs. NOTE this does NOT reverse the M18 backtest conclusion in docs/research/M18-allocator-backtest-findings-2026-06-29.md (EV selection does not beat dumb priority, ranker OOS AUC ~0.51) - it makes the soak's apparent disagreement look better than the real one, so it strengthens the case for keeping P2/P3 parked. Decision needed, not just a filter: should variant pairs be logged at all, or excluded at write time in allocator_soak.py? Also observed: head_p_win is null on every candidate, confirming the parked P_win input.

updates.note: CONFIRMED THIS RUN with direct evidence. /api/bot/allocator/soak summary: total_scanned 165, disagree 85, disagree_pct 51.5, mean_regret 0.485. items.source: Measured live during the 2026-08-06 Actions incident via mcp__github__actions_list. Sibling finding to BL-20260806-CI-FANOUT-AMPLIFIES-ACTIONS-OUTAGES (the PR-side fan-out, fixed in PR #8539).
items.title: [ci][Tier-1] 85 of 100 workflows carry an `issues:` trigger, so ONE issue creates up to 85 workflow runs — 275,328 runs (77% of all Actions runs this repo has ever produced) are issue-triggered, and ~29 of every 30 are immediately skipped
items.description:
ALWAYS STATE THE POPULATION. Measured 2026-08-06 18:45Z against the live Actions API:
  * `event=issues` runs, all time: 275,328 of ~357,254 total completed runs = 77.1%.
  * Issue #8538 (one trainer-vm-diag relay request, opened 18:14:59Z) created 30 runs on the first API page ALONE, all within the same minute: 29 `skipped` + 1 real. 85 workflow files carry an `issues:` trigger, so the true per-issue figure is up to 85.

MECHANISM. GitHub cannot filter an `issues` trigger by LABEL — the label test has to happen in a job-level `if:`. So the repo's entire issue-driven control plane (every diag relay, every system-action, every recover/provision workflow) creates a run for EVERY issue and then skips all but the one whose label matched. The pattern is correct; its cost is that the run count is multiplied by the number of relays, and that number has grown to 85.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT EXPLAIN. A `skipped` run consumes no runner, so this is NOT demonstrated to be the cause of the 2026-08-06 queue stall — the proximate cause of that was GitHub's own incident (status page 15:22Z onward; `POST /actions/runs/{id}/cancel` returning 502; runner allocation degraded but not dead — the 16:26Z batch took up to 70 min to complete and the last success landed 17:40:02Z). Billing was RULED OUT as a cause: the repo is public, so hosted minutes are free and unlimited. What this finding IS: the dominant source of this repo's Actions volume, a standing throttling-exposure risk, and noise that makes the run list unreadable during exactly the incident you most need to read it.

PROPOSED FIX (needs design + operator review — deliberately NOT attempted during the outage, because a change to the entire ops control plane cannot be verified while CI is down): one `issue-router.yml` on `issues.opened` that reads the label and dispatches the matching relay via `workflow_dispatch`, with each relay's `issues:` trigger removed and its issue number passed as an input (relays comment back on the originating issue, so that context must be threaded). Collapses up to 85 runs per issue to 2. Same shape as the guards consolidation in PR #8539. Risk to weigh: it puts every relay behind one router, so the router becomes a single point of failure for the whole control plane — it needs its own failure-path self-test, and a documented manual `workflow_dispatch` fallback per relay.

No change landed this window beyond the 30-guards-into-one-`guards`-job consolidation already merged 2026-08-06 (#8539). Kept open.

That is the same 85-of-100 shape the row filed, slightly worse in absolute terms. No consolidation of the issue-triggered relays has landed. — Not soaking — genuinely unactioned. Ending condition: either one dispatcher workflow that reads the issue label and fans out internally, or a repo-level change so a labelled issue does not start 88 no-op runs. The billing/latency cost is real but bounded; it competes with higher-severity work.

LIVE CORROBORATION FROM MY OWN ACTIVITY: I opened 3 labelled issues today (#10415, #10417, #10418) plus 1 PR. If 85 of 100 workflows carry an `issues:` trigger, those three issues alone could have fanned out to ~255 workflow runs. The repo being public makes minutes free, which is exactly why this has been tolerated — but it also buries real runs. Unchanged.

RE-MEASURED 2026-09-02 AT 943a7192 AND IT HAS NOT IMPROVED — it is marginally WORSE in absolute terms, and the denominator moved, so quote both numbers or neither.

  filed 2026-08-06:  85 of 100 workflows carry an `issues:` trigger
  measured 2026-09-02: 87 of 127

So the issue-triggered set GREW by 2 while 27 new workflows landed. The share fell 85% -> 68.5%, and reading that fall as improvement would be the error this measurement exists to prevent: the blast radius of ONE issue is the ABSOLUTE count (every issue-triggered workflow starts a run), not the share. On that quantity nothing has been fixed.

METHOD, so it is re-runnable and so its limits are visible: a workflow counts when a line matching `^\s{2,4}issues:\s*$` appears in its file — a bare `issues:` key, which is the `on:` trigger form. POSITIVE CONTROL: the four workflows CLAUDE.md documents as issue-driven — vm-diag-snapshot, system-actions, trainer-vm-diag, prop-report — are all four DETECTED. NEGATIVE CONTROL: guards.yml, board-post.yml and pr-opener.yml are all three correctly NOT counted; the latter two are `on: push` relays and carry `issues: write` under `permissions:`, which the trailing-anchor in the pattern excludes. So the probe discriminates in both directions rather than merely returning a number. CAVEAT: it would miss an inline `on: {issues: ...}` mapping, so 87 is a LOWER BOUND.

AN EXIT CONDITION IS AUTHORED BELOW from this measurement — the row previously stated none.

items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when the count of workflows carrying a bare `issues:` ON-trigger falls materially below the 87 measured 2026-09-02 (baseline 85 at filing on 2026-08-06) — the mechanism being a shared dispatcher that fans out to handlers rather than 87 workflows each waking on every issue — AND a run-count read over a window that CONTAINS at least one labelled issue shows the per-issue run fan-out reduced. STATE THE ABSOLUTE COUNT, NEVER THE SHARE: the share fell 85% -> 68.5% between those two dates purely because 27 unrelated workflows were added, while the blast radius of one issue GREW. Re-run: count files matching `^\s{2,4}issues:\s*$` under .github/workflows/, with vm-diag-snapshot/system-actions/trainer-vm-diag/prop-report as the positive control and guards/board-post/pr-opener as the negative one.

items.title: [ml][observability][Tier-1] The trainer's `runtime_logs/signal_audit.jsonl` is BACKTEST-HARNESS output at the same path the live trader uses, with nothing marking it as such — a live-parity check run there silently measures the wrong population
items.description:
ALWAYS STATE THE POPULATION. Measured 2026-08-07 00:31Z over all 13,461 `regime_hard_gate` rows in the trainer's runtime_logs/signal_audit.jsonl:
  * median inter-row gap 0.066s; 12,317 of 13,460 gaps (91.5%) are under ONE SECOND. The live trader emits one tick per TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS and cannot produce that.
  * max gap 1,061,066s (~12.3 days) = the idle stretch between separate research runs.
  * symbols SOLUSDT 4,850 / ETHUSDT 4,743 / BTCUSDT 3,868; strategies include `trend_donchian_eth`, `trend_donchian_sol`, `eth_pullback_2h`, `trend_donchian_eth_4h` -- research variants, not the live roster.
  * span 2026-06-27 -> 2026-08-02T04:50:22, which is exactly the file's mtime (stale 4+ days).
CONTRAST, same window: 81 complete live `regime_hard_gate` rows via /api/diag/audit_query (#8550) are 100% BTCUSDT, dominated by `htf_pullback_trend_2h`.

WHY IT IS A HAZARD, not just a stale file. `scripts/research/ml_vol_label_replay.py verify` exists specifically to stop a vol-label replay being graded against the wrong population, and its documented input is 'JSONL of regime_ml_vol_shadow / regime_hard_gate rows'. On the trainer the nearest such file IS this one, and nothing in it, its path, or its rows says 'harness'. A session that points verify at it gets a confident agreement percentage computed against replay output.

This was NOT hypothetical: verify was returning `no_overlap_nothing_verified` only because of an unrelated reader bug (it never read `logged_at_utc`, fixed in PR #8551). Landing that fix ALONE would have made verify start comparing -- turning a loud, honest failure into a plausible wrong answer. Two independent defects were masking each other.
items.recommendation:
Make the population self-describing rather than relying on a reader to infer it:
  1. Have the backtest harness write its audit rows to a DISTINCT path (e.g. runtime_logs/backtest/signal_audit.jsonl) or stamp every harness-emitted row with an explicit `source: backtest` / run-id field. A row that cannot say where it came from is the same class as an un-provenanced pnl.
  2. Have `verify` REFUSE (or loudly warn) when the audit corpus looks non-live -- a sub-second median inter-row gap is a cheap, decisive tell -- rather than comparing whatever it is handed.
  3. Point live-parity checks at the `signals` dual-write table (the source /api/diag/audit_query reads), which is unambiguously live, instead of at a JSONL whose provenance depends on which box it sits on.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED: the replay ran the -v2 head over -v1's frozen v520. 'Labels end 2026-06-30' was a POINTER artifact, not staleness. Both files are exactly 175,272 rows — a fixed-width rolling window — so v520 did not stop growing; it is a snapshot, and reading its end date as a data ceiling is the trap.

- CLAUDE.md 'Diagnostic provenance' sub-class B (implicit input selection): the declared input was substituted and nothing in the output marked it.
- CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL 'Green is not evidence' obligation 5: before waiting on accrual, establish what BOUNDS it. The bound here was a filesystem path, not a data limit — the same shape as the FRED/FXStreet backfill pair whose supposed ceiling was 115x off.

items.source: Surfaced by the 2026-08-06 GitHub Actions webhook-throttle incident, which left PRs unmergeable for ~6h with no recovery path.
items.title: [ci][Tier-1] Every required-check workflow should carry a workflow_dispatch trigger so a webhook outage is recoverable
items.description:
During the 2026-08-06 Actions incident, push webhooks were throttled to ~15% and several pushes to claude/** produced ZERO workflow runs. There was no way to satisfy the required-check set manually:
  * guards.yml was new in the PR and not yet on the default branch, so run_workflow returns 404 for any ref (a workflow must be on the default branch to be dispatchable);
  * pytest-collect has no workflow_dispatch trigger at all.

So a green-able PR sat unmergeable with no operator-free recovery. Adding `workflow_dispatch:` to each required-check workflow costs nothing and converts a hard block into a manual re-trigger.

Note this composes with the now-verified `run_workflow` MCP capability (re-verified 2026-08-06, HTTP 204) -- the tool exists, the triggers do not.

items.title: [infra][Tier-2] The trainer's trade_journal.db pull rsyncs a HOT WAL-mode SQLite DB -> torn copy; 2026-08-07 05:00 produced a malformed mirror, and no integrity check exists to catch it
items.description:
POPULATION: the trainer VM's read-only mirror data/trade_journal.db (750,125,056 bytes, 16 tables, signals=1,401,444 rows), pulled 2026-08-07 05:00:13->05:00:41Z. The LIVE money DB (/data/bot-data/trade_journal.db on ict-bot-arm) is the rsync SOURCE and is only read, not implicated.

SYMPTOM: `PRAGMA quick_check` -> `database disk image is malformed`. Corruption is LOCALIZED, which is why it went unnoticed: sqlite_master lists all 16 tables, COUNT(*) succeeds on signals (1,401,444), trades (4,491) and order_packages (3,578) — but `SELECT MAX(logged_at_utc) FROM signals` fails. COUNT(*) succeeding while MAX(indexed_col) fails is the signature of a corrupt INDEX, not lost table data.

HYPOTHESIS REFUTED FIRST (recorded so it is not re-tried): stale -wal/-shm sidecars. A body-only copy with no sidecars present is EQUALLY malformed, so sidecar replay is not the cause.

ROOT CAUSE: scripts/ops/sync_trainer_data.sh:106 does `rsync -az --checksum ubuntu@141.145.193.91:/data/bot-data/trade_journal.db` — a plain rsync of a WAL-mode SQLite database the live trader is actively writing to. No .backup, no VACUUM INTO, no snapshot. The transfer took 28s on a 750 MB file with a live writer. A torn copy is the expected outcome of that race.

WHY THIS IS BIGGER THAN ONE BAD PULL: the mechanism is unchanged since the script was written, so every prior pull was a coin-flip that happened to win. Nothing runs an integrity check after the pull, and the success line is `{"status":"ok","artifact":"trade_journal.db","size_bytes":750125056}` — a SIZE match, which is not integrity. Earlier cycles may have trained on subtly-torn mirrors undetected. This is CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL 'Green is not evidence' obligation 1 (assert the inputs, not the exit code).

PROPOSED FIX (Tier-2, NOT applied): snapshot live-side (`sqlite3 <db> ".backup /tmp/tj.snap"` or `VACUUM INTO`), rsync the SNAPSHOT, then `PRAGMA quick_check` on arrival and FAIL LOUDLY rather than proceeding. Re-pulling without changing the mechanism only re-rolls the dice.

IMPACT WHILE OPEN: any trainer work reading the journal mirror fails or silently mis-reads. datasets-out/ is unaffected (market_features BTCUSDT 15m v002 is healthy, current to 2026-08-06 22:30Z).

updates.note: VERIFIED REPAIRED AT REST this run (trainer-diag #8592, 14:40Z): PRAGMA quick_check = ok; trades 4504, order_packages 3590, signals 1,406,974; MAX(logged_at_utc) = 2026-08-07T13:40:06Z (the indexed-column read that previously failed now works). Trainer HEAD is cf101726, so the cf10172 fix is deployed. NOT closing: the concurrent session (metis-ml2-cell-audit-cont-6ewta2) found the shipped fix had two defects of its own — the VACUUM INTO snapshot path was inert (no sqlite3 CLI on the live VM, silently degrading to direct rsync) and the verify step leaked -wal/-shm sidecars — both carried in PR #8584, which is still open. Kept open until #8584 lands AND a subsequent pull records method=snapshot with integrity_verified:true.

RESOLVED — the snapshot path is now PROVEN FIRING, not merely deployed. trainer-diag #8598, trainer HEAD 796aaf16 (PR #8584). A real sync_trainer_data.sh run logged: status=ok, artifact=trade_journal.db, size_bytes=753938432, method=python_backup_snapshot, integrity_verified=true. That is the exact field whose absence hid the original defect: the first implementation probed `command -v sqlite3` before VACUUM INTO, the live VM has no sqlite3 CLI, so it fell back to direct_rsync_fallback on every run while reporting success. The whole chain — python3 Connection.backup(pages=-1) over a mode=ro source, quick_check + a real consumer query, promote-on-verify — is now end-to-end verified against production. `method` in the log is what made this checkable; a pull that did not state its method could not have been caught.

items.resolution_note: FIXED + merged cf10172 (#8576), hardened in #8584. Promote-on-verify (a bad pull can no longer overwrite a good mirror), python3 online-backup snapshot, bounded retry, loud failure. Mirror VERIFIED repaired at rest 2026-08-07: quick_check ok, full integrity_check ok, trades 4504 / signals 1406974 / 3903 regime_hard_gate. STILL MONITORING, not resolved: the snapshot path shipped INERT in the first cut (live VM has no sqlite3 CLI, so it silently used direct_rsync_fallback); the python-backup replacement is NOT yet confirmed firing on the trainer. Close only after a live pull reports method:python_backup_snapshot. CONCURRENT CONFIRMATION: an independent /system-review session (#8594) measured the same state the same day — see updates[]. Its `status: open` and this row's `fix_landed_monitoring` are the same claim, not a disagreement: the fix is deployed and NOT yet proven on a real merge/pull. Both were written without sight of the other; merged here without dropping either.

The two are plausibly one incident but have NOT been shown to be — they are filed separately so that fixing the rsync is not mistaken for fixing this.

items.source: trainer-vm-diag #8575 (silent truncation) vs #8573/#8577 (worked). .github/workflows/trainer-vm-diag.yml awk extractor.
items.title: [infra][Tier-1] trainer-vm-diag: a column-0 Python `try:` inside a heredoc silently TRUNCATES the command (third extraction trap in this family)
items.description:
REPRO: a `cmd: |` block containing a python heredoc whose body has `try:` at column 0. Observed trainer-diag #8575; the identical structure with `try:` INDENTED ran fine (#8577).

CAUSE: the extractor's stop rule is `found && /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/ { exit }` — 'stop at the next unindented top-level YAML-ish key'. Python's `try:` / `else:` / `finally:` at column 0 match that regex exactly, so awk exits mid-heredoc. The truncated script is then fed to bash, which reports only `warning: here-document delimited by end-of-file (wanted PYEOF)` — the error names the heredoc, not the extractor, so it reads as a quoting mistake in the body rather than a parser collision.

This is the THIRD trap in this extractor's family (BL-20260720-TRAINERDIAG-FENCE fenced blocks; BL-20260731-TRAINERDIAG-TRAILING-PROSE executing prose). Note the extractor preserves indentation VERBATIM, so the naive fix — indenting the cmd block for readability — breaks heredocs a different way (an indented `PYEOF` delimiter is not recognised; observed #8571/#8572). Both failure modes cost this session four round trips.

ASKS (either): (a) require the stop-key to be a KNOWN body key rather than any `word:`; or (b) document the two rules together in docs/claude/diag-relay.md — 'cmd block must be flush-left AND must contain no column-0 `word:` line' — since satisfying one naively breaks the other.

updates.note: REPRODUCED THIS RUN (#8591) — same family, same session. Confirms this is not a one-off: a heredoc-delivered Python block truncated at the heredoc opener. See the sibling row BL-20260806-TRAINER-RELAY-MANGLES-ANGLE-BRACKETS for the base64 mitigation verified on #8592, which sidesteps ALL THREE known extraction traps at once (angle brackets, newline collapse, column-0 keyword) because the payload never appears as shell-parsed text. Kept open.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: .github/workflows/trainer-vm-diag.yml:177 still terminates extraction on `found && /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/{ exit }`, which a column-0 Python `try:` matches, and :214 additionally exits on any non-indented non-empty line inside a block scalar. Neither rule can distinguish a sibling YAML key from Python source. The base64 mitigation is documented (docs/claude/diag-relay.md:176-209) but the extractor is unfixed. — Actionable but low value while the documented base64 pattern sidesteps all three traps. Ending condition: either the extractor stops parsing the block as YAML-ish text, or the doc requirement is enforced (e.g. the workflow refuses a cmd block that is not a single base64 pipeline).

Re-validated: third of three independent cmd-extraction defects in the trainer relay (with BL-20260731-TRAINERDIAG-DOUBLE-EXECUTION and BL-20260807-TRAINER-DIAG-RELAY-SILENT-CMD-TRUNCATION). Work as one class.

FIXED. Root cause characterised and repaired in .github/workflows/trainer-vm-diag.yml. The extractor's terminator `found && /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+:/{exit}` — 'stop at the next top-level YAML key' — was applied INSIDE a fenced block, where the content is CODE, not YAML. A great many code lines legitimately begin `word:` at column 0: `try:` / `else:` / `except:` / `finally:` in an embedded python heredoc, a shell `case` label, a heredoc-written YAML key. The rule now carries `!fence`; a fenced block already has an unambiguous terminator (its closing fence), so the YAML-key rule is not needed there. Unfenced blocks are unaffected and still stop at a top-level key (BL-20260607-002). REPRODUCED INDEPENDENTLY THIS SESSION on trainer-diag #10452, whose embedded `try:` cut the script so bash reported `here-document at line 15 delimited by end-of-file`. EVIDENCE THE FIX IS REAL, NOT ASSUMED: tests/test_trainer_diag_cmd_extraction.py extracts the awk program from the workflow itself (no copy to drift), and two new tests were verified NON-VACUOUS by reverting the one-token change and observing both fail, then pass with it restored (12 passed / 2 failed-when-reverted). Three pre-existing regression cases the parser was built for — BL-20260607-002 (unfenced ends at top-level key), #8157 (fenced ends at closing fence), #9400 (unfenced ends at prose) — all still pass and still exclude their bad lines. NOTE ON A VACUOUS TEST CAUGHT IN PASSING: the first draft of the second test used a shell `case` block, which contains NO column-0 `word:` and therefore passed against the broken parser too; it was rewritten to a heredoc-written YAML key. NOT YET EXERCISED LIVE: GitHub runs the workflow from the default branch for `issues` events, so live proof requires the merge, then one trainer-diag whose cmd contains a column-0 `try:` returning the FULL script.

items.title: [positions][provenance] ib_paper unrealized PnL on /api/bot/positions contradicts exchange truth by ~3 orders of magnitude (MGC +$110,040 vs +$37.80)
items.detail:
Two ib_paper rows report an unrealizedPnl that no other endpoint supports, both with unrealizedPnlSource='markprice_local' (the server-side mark-to-market fallback, since IBKR is not in BROKER_PNL_READER_EXCHANGES for the unrealized path).

  MGC  105 contracts long : /positions uPnL = +$110,040.00 | /pnl/exchange unrealized_pnl = +$37.80 (open_qty 105, last 4276.5) | exchange avg entry 4276.236 => true uPnL ~ +$28. Ratio ~2,900x.
  MES   15 contracts long : /positions uPnL = +$10,481.25  | /pnl/exchange unrealized_pnl =  $0.00 (open_qty 15, last 7630.75) | exchange avg entry 7630.872 => true uPnL ~ -$9.

PROBABLE MECHANISM (stated as hypothesis, not verified): markprice_local prices the NETTED position size against the single journal row's entry price. ib_paper MGC accumulated 105 contracts over 94 fills; any one journal row's entry is meaningless against that netted size, so qty(netted) x (mark - entry(one row)) x multiplier(10) produces a number with no referent. This is the unrealized-side sibling of BL-20260801-NETTING-PARTIAL-CLOSE-ROWS-NEVER-REDUCED, on IB rather than Bybit.

WHY IT MATTERS: this number is rendered as a headline uPnL on the dashboard Overview and the Android app and the Glance widget. It inflates paper open-PnL by ~$120k. It is paper-only today (ib_paper), so no money is at risk — but the same markprice_local path serves every non-Bybit account, and it is the exact 'a metric that cannot be right' shape.

CROSS-CHECK THAT ARGUES THE POSITION IS FINE AND ONLY THE NUMBER IS WRONG: ib_paper balance delta_1h reads -$16,923.86 over the same hour the position supposedly gained $110k. Those cannot both be true. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'measured_hypothesis_falsified' was collapsed to 'resolved' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.

updates.note:
**THE HEADLINE COMPARISON IN THIS ROW IS INVALID, AND THE uPnL APPEARS CORRECT.** I came here to fix a fabricated number and measured my way out of it. Recording the arithmetic in full so nobody re-derives it.

MEASURED 2026-08-14T12:18-12:19Z:
  * BROKER truth (/api/diag/exchange_positions, ib_paper): MGC size **105.0**, entry **4276.236**. The qty is REAL - it matches the journal exactly - and the entry differs from the journal's 4272.4 by **$3.84**, which over 105 contracts x10 is $4,032. That cannot produce a $119,490 gap, so the entry-price hypothesis in this row's PROBABLE MECHANISM is ruled out by size.
  * LIVE MARK (/api/bot/candles?symbol=MGC&interval=1h): last three 1h closes **4372.8 / 4392.9 / 4396.8**.
  * The reported uPnL of $119,490 implies a mark of **4386.2** (119490/(105*10) + 4272.4), which sits INSIDE that range. At the latest close 4396.8 the figure would be $130,620; against the broker's own entry, $126,592.

So $119,490 is what a genuine 105-contract MGC long at the standard 10 oz multiplier IS worth at the live mark. It is arithmetically correct, not manufactured.

WHY THE ORIGINAL COMPARISON MISLEADS - and this is the reusable lesson: `/api/bot/pnl/exchange` computes `unrealized_pnl` by marking open lots against the **last FILL price**, per its own contract. That is near-zero BY CONSTRUCTION for any position not currently being traded. Comparing it to a mark-to-market is comparing two different quantities, and the '~2,900x ratio' is an artifact of that, not evidence of fabrication. Worse: in the 7d window that endpoint returns **10 symbols and MGC/MES are not among them** - every row is Bybit or Alpaca - so for IBKR it had no coverage to contradict anything with. The '$37.80' was never IBKR broker truth.

The `delta_1h -$16,923.86` cross-check this row also cites cannot be re-tested: ib_paper's `delta_1h` reads **null** in today's snapshot.

STATUS -> `measured_hypothesis_falsified`, NOT `resolved`: the number is exonerated, but two real questions this row surfaced are untouched and should not be lost with it. **(1)** Is a 105-contract MGC position (~$4.6M notional against $1.29M paper equity, ~3.6x) intended? It accumulated over ~94 fills and is now HELD - trades 4643/4644/4647 are all `mgc_trend_1h` shorts rejected `intent_noop:flip_suppressed_hold_policy: desired short opposes current long (qty=105.0)`, so FLIP_POLICY=hold is pinning it. That is a position-accumulation question, not a PnL-provenance one, and it deserves its own row if someone judges the size wrong. **(2)** `markprice_local` genuinely does price the netted size against one journal row's entry; here the two entries happen to agree closely so it does not bite, but the structural concern stands for a symbol where they diverge - the broker path already scales by `share = qty/size` and the local path does not.

Nothing was changed in code on the strength of this row. Had I 'fixed' it I would have replaced a correct number with a wrong one.

items.source: /system-review 2026-08-07: /api/bot/news/recent?limit=8 top_items inspection + code read of src/news/news_client_rss.py::fetch_news_rss and src/news/news_feeds.py::feeds_for_tags against config/news_feeds.yaml, config/accounts.yaml, config/strategies.yaml.
items.title: [news] symbol->feed map covers 5 of 24 traded bases — 19 symbols read macro-only feeds while the news VETO is armed
items.detail:
config/news_feeds.yaml::symbol_groups maps 7 bases (BTC, ETH, MCL, MES, MGC, MHG, MNQ). The bot trades 24 bases. Intersection is 5 (BTC, ETH, MES, MGC, MHG) — MCL and MNQ are mapped but not traded. The 19 unmapped bases fall through feeds_for_tags to the `global` group only: ADA, AVAX, GDX, GLD, IAUM, IEF, IWM, QLD, QQQ, SCHA, SLV, SOL, SPLG, SPY, TLT, TQQQ, USO, XAU, XRP. Coverage 5/24 = 20.8%.

CONSEQUENCES:
  - XRP/ADA/SOL/AVAX are crypto but never fetch the `crypto` group (CoinDesk/Cointelegraph/Decrypt). They cannot see a symbol-specific crypto story at all.
  - uso_trend_1h trades oil and never fetches the `energy` group (oilprice.com), which exists and is unused by any traded symbol.
  - SLV/GLD/GDX/IAUM never fetch `metals`; SPY/QQQ/IWM/TLT never fetch `equities`.

OBSERVED IN THE LIVE LOG (2026-08-07T14:0x): the identical MarketWatch headline 'How S&P 500 options action may help explain the rising volatility in memory stocks' is the #1 scored item for ADAUSDT (0.0240), XRPUSDT (0.0277), TLT (0.0292) and MGC (0.0293), and XRP's #2/#3 items are two Social Security stories at score 0.0.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO AN EASY MISREAD, so the next session does not overstate this: the macro fallback is BY DESIGN. news_normalizer._relevance_breakdown deliberately gives a macro article a partial relevance weight for a symbol whose own keywords do not match, so that Fed/inflation stories register. The defect is NOT that macro articles score — it is that 19 symbols have NOTHING ELSE in their feed set, so macro is all they ever see. Also note the audit row records a per-symbol `query` string (e.g. 'XRP OR Ripple') that under NEWS_SOURCE=rss selects nothing: fetch_news_rss takes symbol_tags and resolves FEEDS, never a query. That is a provenance defect in the log independent of the coverage gap.

BLAST RADIUS: NEWS_VETO_ENABLED defaults true and is armed whenever the source is active (it is: rss). A veto blocks the signal for EVERY account including real money at sentiment < -0.6 AND impact > 0.7. Nothing is vetoing today (observed adjustments 0.004-0.008, decisions all `neutral`), so this is a latent mis-targeting rather than an active loss — but the gate is live and its input is wrong for 79% of traded symbols.
items.recommendation: Tier-1 YAML: extend symbol_groups to the 19 uncovered bases (crypto: ADA/AVAX/SOL/XRP; metals: GLD/GDX/IAUM/SLV/XAU; equities: SPY/QQQ/IWM/TQQQ/QLD/SPLG/SCHA/TLT/IEF; energy: USO). Separately, stop recording a `query` on rss-sourced audit rows, or record the resolved feed set instead. PROPOSED ONLY — not enacted by this review, because it changes what a live trade-blocking gate sees.
items.resolution_criteria: symbol_groups covers every traded base, and an rss-sourced news_decisions row names the feeds actually read rather than an unused query.

items.detail:
At capture time /api/diag/status reported heartbeat.age_seconds 226.18 and heartbeat.label 'paused', and /api/bot/stats reported status 'paused' — while status.last_tick_utc was 2026-08-07T14:35:45Z, five seconds before the 14:35:50Z capture. The trader was demonstrably running (bot_uptime_s 3247, ict-trader-live.service active, a trade opened within the prior 30m per /api/bot/notifications).

MECHANISM (hypothesis, consistent with the documented design): CLAUDE.md states the heartbeat is refreshed every HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 60) from inside src/main.py's SLEEP loop, so it fires between ticks. It therefore does NOT fire DURING a tick. A 226s heartbeat age with a fresh last_tick implies a single tick ran ~226s — nearly 4 minutes — against a 60s heartbeat cadence and the <180s 'running' threshold. With 52 loaded strategies that is plausible.

TWO DISTINCT PROBLEMS, worth separating:
  (1) FALSE ALARM SURFACE. Every consumer that reads `status` (dashboard, Android, Glance widget, and the operator's own eye) is told the trader is paused when it is not. A liveness signal that cries wolf during normal operation is the alarm-fatigue failure mode CLAUDE.md names as itself a P1.
  (2) POSSIBLE REAL SIGNAL. A ~4-minute tick may be a genuine slow-tick regression worth measuring on its own, and the current design cannot distinguish 'slow tick' from 'dead trader' — which is precisely what the liveness watchdog exists to decide (it autoheals after 8 minutes of stall).

NOT ASSERTED: I did not measure tick duration directly, so (2) is inferred from the heartbeat gap, not observed. The external ict-liveness-watchdog.timer is active and did not fire, consistent with the trader being alive.
items.what_to_check: Measure real tick duration from runtime_logs (successive last_tick_utc deltas) over a few hours. If ticks routinely exceed HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECONDS, either refresh the heartbeat from inside the tick as well as the sleep, or derive the label from max(heartbeat_age, tick_age) so a fresh tick counts as liveness.
items.resolution_criteria: A running trader never reports 'paused'.

With HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECONDS=60 the 'running' bound is 180s, so any tick exceeding 180s still labels 'paused'. — needs live data: current tick max_ms from /api/diag/tick_cost. The M20 exit-loop decouple cut the tick to ~69s mean / ~97s max per CLAUDE.md, which would keep it under the 180s bound most of the time — but a 187.2s tick was measured pre-decouple, so the mislabel is still reachable.   3491 IAUM alpaca_paper      opened 2026-07-15T15:13 closed 08-05T13:36:20

All are alpaca accounts; all closed in a tight cluster; all have pnlProvenance null (which is the honest UNVERIFIED outcome, so the provenance layer is behaving correctly here — it is not fabricating a number).

WHY IT MATTERS: these rows leave the open-position set but contribute nothing measurable. In a 37-row window they are 8 rows (22%) of trades with no outcome, which silently shrinks every denominator the performance aggregates rest on — /performance 7d paper reports pnlCoverage 0.357, and rows like these are part of why. A position held 21 days and closed with no exit price is either a real close whose price was lost, or a bookkeeping close of something that was never open.

NOT ASSERTED: I have not determined which reconciler path did this. Candidates are the P3b position-snapshot reconciler (RECONCILER_SNAPSHOT_MIN_FILL_AGE_S guards the fresh-fill case, not the stale case) and a manual/cleanup sweep.

items.title: [tooling][diagnostic-provenance] m20_exit_analysis reports hold_h exactly 24.0 with mfe exactly 0.0 for trades whose real hold was 21-23h — a truncated candle window rendered as a measurement
items.detail:
Four of the 15 per-trade rows returned by the S3 compact dump read hold_h exactly 24.0 AND mfe exactly 0.0 AND mae in the -1.2..-1.4 range:
  4430 slv_trend_1h    opened 2026-08-05T14:11 -> real close 2026-08-06T13:13 = 23.0h (reported 24.0)
  4431 slv_trend_1h    opened 2026-08-05T14:11 -> real close 2026-08-06T15:34 = 25.4h (reported 24.0)
  4450 qqq_pullback_1h opened 2026-08-05T18:04 -> real close 2026-08-06T13:03 = 19.0h (reported 24.0)
  4451 qqq_pullback_1h opened 2026-08-05T18:04 -> real close 2026-08-06T13:40 = 19.6h (reported 24.0)
A fifth, 4442 ict_scalp_mgc_15m, reports 24.0 against a real 21.6h.

An exact-24.0 hold on five rows with three different true durations is a CLAMP, and mfe exactly 0.0 on four long positions is the signature of an empty/short candle slice rather than a genuine absence of favourable excursion. Neither is marked in the output.

This is CLAUDE.md's UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class C (unasserted denominator): a truncated result reads as a clean measurement. It matters more than usual because m20_exit_analysis is the instrument /system-review's mandatory execution_capture block depends on — a capped hold_h systematically UNDER-states exactly the hold-time overrun the block exists to detect.

HONEST SCOPE: the ict_scalp rows this review actually escalated (0.8-15.8h, and trade 4413 at 15.8h/-8.41R) are all BELOW the clamp, so this defect does not undermine that finding. It does mean the four clamped rows must not be quoted, and it caps what the tool can see at 24h.

items.resolution_criteria: No row reports a clamped hold or a window-limited MFE without a flag marking it as such.

items.source: /system-review 2026-08-07: /api/bot/prop/status (#8588), 14:36Z.
items.title: [prop][diagnostic-provenance] rule_distance renders a live-looking cushion from an 18-day-old account snapshot with no staleness marker
items.detail:
/api/bot/prop/status returns a fully-populated rule_distance block — distance_to_daily_loss_usd 144.77, distance_to_dd_floor_usd 125.61, day_pnl 0.0 — computed from a prop_account_status snapshot whose reported_at is 2026-07-20T08:28:32Z, eighteen days before the read. The block does carry as_of, but the dashboard Prop panel's loud st.error/st.warning cushion alarms are driven by these numbers, and a $125.61 distance-to-floor presented without a staleness treatment reads as current risk.

Mitigating facts, so this is rated low rather than high: there are no open prop positions right now (prop/reconcile unacted_count 0), the recent prop order-packages are all status 'shadow' / close_reason 'prop_shadow_no_emit' so the sleeve is emitting nothing, and PROP_STATUS_REQUEST_MAX_AGE_HOURS (default 24) only requests a refresh WHILE a prop position is open — so the staleness is expected behaviour, not a broken nag.

The defect is presentational: a derived risk figure should carry its input's age, or decline to compute. Sub-class B (implicit input selection) of the diagnostic-provenance class.
items.resolution_criteria: rule_distance either carries an explicit staleness flag consumers render, or returns null when its snapshot is older than the freshness threshold.

updates.note: WORSENED. /api/bot/prop/status 2026-08-10 returns rule_distance with distance_to_daily_loss_usd 144.77 and distance_to_dd_floor_usd 125.61 computed from a prop_account_status snapshot whose reported_at is 2026-07-20T08:28Z — now 21 DAYS stale (was 18 when filed). The envelope carries as_of but the cushion figures render with no staleness marker, so a 21-day-old balance presents as a live rule cushion on an account whose killer limit is a $145 daily loss. Same diagnostic-provenance class as the relay message fixed this run.
updates.next_check: surface age_seconds beside rule_distance and refuse to render a cushion past a freshness bound

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: src/prop/prop_reconcile.py:188-213 adds `_status_freshness` returning a four-state ok/stale/absent/unchecked verdict (stale also covers an undateable snapshot), and compute_rule_distance now returns `status_age_hours`, `status_freshness` and `status_max_age_hours` INSIDE the rule_distance dict (:296-298) so a consumer reading only the panel cannot miss the caveat. src/web/api/routers/prop.py:151-152 mirrors both onto the envelope, with `status_freshness: "error"` at :160 when the read itself failed.

items.title: [risk][alpaca] alpaca_paper has $85.9k balance but $0.00 available_usd — every new signal is risk_refused with sized_qty=0
items.detail:
Live banner at 2026-08-07T14:02:29Z: 'Strategy: tlt_pullback_1h | Symbol: TLT | Side: sell - Accounts attempted: 3 | Trades placed: 0 - alpaca_paper: risk_refused: sized_qty=0 with balance=85949.19 available_usd=0.00 total_account_usd=n/a direction=short market_type=spo...'

The account reports balance $85,908.90 and api_ok true, but available_usd 0.00, so RiskManager.position_size returns 0 and the refusal is correct behaviour given the input. The question is why available is zero: alpaca_paper holds 7 open positions including large shorts (TLT short 938, SLV short 376, IEF short 141) alongside longs (IWM 124, QQQ 18, SPY 11, GLD 7). Buying power looks exhausted by the short book.

WHY THIS IS A FINDING RATHER THAN NORMAL: the refusal is a per-trade rejection with a logged cause, which is the Prime-Directive-correct shape — the account is NOT demoted and nothing auto-flipped. But if available_usd stays pinned at zero, alpaca_paper is silently non-participating in every new signal while still reading 'live', and the soak data it exists to generate stops accruing. That is a capability stranded by state rather than by a flag, and it will not show up as an outage anywhere.

NOT ASSERTED: I have not confirmed how long available_usd has been zero, nor whether alpaca_portfolio (balance $98,739.90, 6 open positions) is in the same state — the banner names only alpaca_paper of the 3 accounts attempted.
items.what_to_check: /api/diag/broker_account_status?account_id=alpaca_paper for the trade-enabled flags, and track available_usd over a few hourly balance snapshots to see whether it recovers as positions close.
items.resolution_criteria: Either alpaca_paper regains non-zero buying power and places trades again, or the persistent-zero condition raises its own operator alert instead of only appearing as per-signal refusals.

updates.note:
STILL OCCURRING, and the id OVERSTATES it — 'REFUSES-ALL' is not true.

Fresh rows from trades @ account_id=alpaca_paper (diag #8986) confirm the condition is live: uso_trend_1h and tlt_pullback_1h both rejected 2026-08-07 with `risk_refused: sized_qty=0 with balance=85,949-86,382 available_usd=0.00 total_account_usd=n/a ... market_type=spot`. BUT the same page contains slv_trend_1h id 4549 (2026-08-10T18:36Z) FILLED at position_size 310.0 on the same account — so the account does NOT refuse everything, and a reader who trusts the id would conclude alpaca_paper is fully stranded when it is not. That matters for triage: a total refusal is a dead account, an intermittent one is a condition that comes and goes and needs its TRIGGER identified (buying-power recomputation timing, market_type=spot vs the SLV path, or a settlement window).

Keeping the id (it is referenced elsewhere and renaming breaks the tracking-ref guard), but the resolution must explain the INTERMITTENCY, not just the zero. Population honesty: the page was truncated to the newest rows, so this is 'both states occur', NOT a rate.

items.source: /system-review 2026-08-07: /api/diag/db_info row_counts, 14:36Z.
items.title: [m13][data] insights_history 92,364 rows and insights_usage 92,470 rows — far above what the generator cadence can produce
items.detail:
db_info reports insights_history 92,364 and insights_usage 92,470 rows, against trades 4,509 and order_packages 3,593.

BACK-OF-ENVELOPE (stated as an estimate, and the reason this is filed as low rather than high — I have not read the writer): the M13 generators run at 15-minute (fast tier, 3 endpoints) and 60-minute (slow tier, per-strategy) cadence. Since the dashboard consumer was adopted 2026-05-12 (~87 days) that is roughly 8,350 fast-tier and 2,090 slow-tier invocations. Even at one row per endpoint per invocation the expected order of magnitude is ~10k-35k, not ~92k. The two tables also track each other to within 106 rows, which suggests a shared writer rather than two independent ones.

Possible benign explanations I have NOT ruled out: a longer history than I assumed, more endpoints per invocation than I counted, or a retry that legitimately writes per attempt. Possible defect: a duplicate write per invocation, or no retention policy on an append-only observability table that will keep growing inside the money DB.

WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW AT ALL: these two tables are ~96% of all rows in trade_journal.db by count and live in the SAME file as the money data, which the trainer pulls in full over the network every cycle (750 MB, and the pull mechanism was just found to be a torn hot-DB copy). Unbounded observability growth in the money DB is a cost even if every row is legitimate.
items.what_to_check: SELECT COUNT(*), MIN(ts), MAX(ts), endpoint FROM insights_usage GROUP BY endpoint — confirm rows-per-invocation and whether any retention exists.
items.resolution_criteria: Row count is explained against cadence, and a retention or archival policy exists if the tables are unbounded.

updates.note: WORSENING, measured. 2026-08-07: insights_history 92,364 / insights_usage 92,470. 2026-08-10 (/api/diag/db_info): 95,345 / 95,451. That is +2,981 / +2,981 in ~3 days = ~1,000 rows/day/table, against a generator cadence of 15min (fast) + 60min (slow) = ~120 writes/day expected. So the observed rate is ~8x the cadence ceiling and the two tables track each other exactly. Severity raised low -> medium: this is now a measured contradiction with a known denominator, not a suspicion.
updates.next_check: re-derive the writer's per-invocation row count; the 1:1 history/usage lockstep suggests one write per row rather than one per run

The row's own measurement shows +2,981 rows per table in ~3 days against a ~120 writes/day cadence ceiling, i.e. ~8x — a measured contradiction, not a suspicion. — needs live data: SELECT endpoint, COUNT(*), MIN(ts), MAX(ts) FROM insights_usage GROUP BY endpoint via /api/bot/db/table (assert filter_state=='applied'), to establish rows-per-invocation. Ending condition: rows-per-invocation is explained (a per-row-not-per-call writer) or a retention policy lands.

items.title: artifact-validity-guard cannot distinguish a FORWARD 'tracked by BL-X' claim from a BACKWARD citation of a CLOSED incident
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-07 while adding src/runtime/monitor_verdict.py. check_backlog_refs.py resolves an id ONLY against open rows in docs/claude/*backlog*.json. When a row is resolved its id is deleted, so every historical citation of it becomes un-resolvable. The repo cites closed incidents this way extensively — the XRP SL-spam id alone appears in src/runtime/order_monitor.py, src/units/db/database.py and 2 test files, all of them documenting WHY a piece of code exists. Those are grandfathered only because the guard is diff-scoped. CONSEQUENCE: a new file documenting the same scar is blocked from naming it, so the cheapest way to pass is to DELETE the provenance link — the guard pushes authors in the opposite direction from the rule it serves. That is what happened here: the citation in monitor_verdict.py was reduced to prose + a pointer to order_monitor.py. POPULATION: 1 blocked change observed; the count of already-committed src/ citations to resolved ids has NOT been measured (the diff scope hides it) — measuring it is step 1. Candidate fixes: (a) a resolved-ids ledger the guard also reads, so closing a row records the id instead of erasing it; (b) distinguish the assertion by phrasing (a bare id is a citation; 'tracked by <id>'/'see <id>' is a tracking claim) — note (b) alone is weak, a typo'd id would read as a citation and pass. Do NOT fix by accepting any id that appears in 2+ files: that makes a propagated typo self-validating, the presence-only lie new-table-wiring-guard was defeated by.
items.close_condition: A new file can cite a resolved incident id without the guard failing, AND a genuinely dangling forward reference still fails. Both directions covered by a guard selftest.

items.title: trainer-vm-diag SILENTLY TRUNCATES a long `cmd:` block — the run reports success over a command that was cut
items.detail: OBSERVED on trainer-diag #8598. The issue body's cmd: block had 12 lines; the relay executed only the first ~8. The echoed Command in the result comment ends mid-token (`echo "==== methods seen on the last 5 journal rows ==`) and the output stops at the sync's own last line — the two verification sections AFTER the sync (`db_pulls tail AFTER` and the per-row method summary) never ran and never appeared. THE RUN STILL REPORTED SUCCESS. WHY THIS MATTERS: this is the unasserted-denominator / diagnostic-provenance class applied to the relay itself. A truncated command whose surviving prefix happens to succeed is indistinguishable from a command that ran in full — the reader sees plausible output and a green run. I only noticed because I knew which two sections were missing; a session that did not author the command would have read the output as complete. Any past relay result may have been truncated the same way without anyone knowing. POPULATION: 1 confirmed instance. The truncation POINT has not been characterised — I do not know whether the cause is a byte/line cap in the issue-body parser, the `==` token, or the embedded multi-line `python -c` string, and I have not measured it. Step 1 is to find the boundary with a deliberate ladder of increasing cmd: lengths. CANDIDATE FIX: make the relay echo a checksum/line-count of the cmd: block it PARSED next to the block it RECEIVED, and fail loudly on a mismatch — the same shape as `method` in db_pulls.jsonl, which is what made the sibling defect above catchable at all. A relay that cannot state what it ran is a diagnostic that does not say what it computed.
items.close_condition: The relay either refuses or loudly flags a cmd: block it could not parse in full, verified by a deliberately over-long test dispatch that FAILS rather than silently running a prefix.

updates.note: REPRODUCED LIVE this run, which upgrades this from 'observed once' to 'deterministic'. trainer-diag issue #8728 echoed the command back cut mid-token at `python3 -c "import jso` and the run still reported SUCCESS; the three tails after the cut point returned empty and the registry line printed 0. A reviewer reading only the output would have concluded the trainer mirror was empty. The ML lifecycle had to be sourced from the live VM's /api/bot/ml/status instead (which was fine: 2 cycles/24h, 68 manifests trained, 0 failed).
updates.next_check: the relay must fail loudly on a truncated cmd — compare the received byte length against the issue body and abort rather than executing a prefix

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: .github/workflows/trainer-vm-diag.yml:308 echoes the command as `cmd.slice(0, 500)` with NO ellipsis or marker — that is the confirmed source of an 'echoed Command ends mid-token' with a green run. Note the asymmetry two lines down: the OUTPUT truncation at :314 DOES append '... (truncated)'. The parse step writes the full cmd_raw to /tmp/trainer_diag_cmd.sh (:222) and SSH streams that whole file (:269), so the display half is proven and the EXECUTION half is not established by the code. — The reported 'later sections never ran' half still needs a deliberate length-ladder repro against the relay, which needs live dispatch.

Re-validated: silent truncation reporting success over a cut command. One of the three trainer-relay cmd-extraction defects; and see BL-20260816-TRUNCATION-STRIPS-THE-FIELDS-THAT-CERTIFY-A-RESPONSE — I hit the same CLASS today on the system-action comment cap (last 50,000 of 66,841 bytes kept, oldest 22 rows silently dropped, while the retained tail carried `truncated: false`).

PRIMARY EVIDENCE REFUTED, AND THE PROPOSED NEXT STEP WITH IT. This row's headline evidence is that 'the echoed Command in the result comment ends mid-token', read as proof the EXECUTION was cut. It is not: the comment renderer did `cmd.slice(0, 500)` with NO ellipsis and NO marker, so the `**Command:**` field showed a silent 500-char display prefix of a command that had been executed IN FULL. A MID-TOKEN cut is the signature of a character slice; the genuine execution-truncation bug (the sibling row, column-0 `word:`) cuts at LINE boundaries, so the two are distinguishable and were being conflated. MEASURED 2026-08-30 on trainer-diag #10452: the echo ended at exactly 499 chars, byte-for-byte where a 500-char slice lands. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW'S PLAN: the stated Step 1 — 'find the boundary with a deliberate ladder of increasing cmd: lengths' — would have searched for a length cap that does not exist on the execution path, and any 'boundary' it found would have been the 500-char DISPLAY cap misread as an execution limit. Do not run it. FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE: the echo now appends '(echo truncated for display — showing first 500 of N chars; the FULL command was executed)', matching the marker the OUTPUT field below it already carried. That asymmetry — output marked, command unmarked — is why the one field a reader uses to check WHAT RAN was the one field that lied. WHAT REMAINS OPEN, and why this is not resolved: whether #8598's and #8728's executions were ALSO genuinely truncated is still unsettled. Their surviving evidence is that sections after the cut produced no output, which is consistent with execution truncation but also with those sections running and finding nothing. POPULATION: 2 historical instances, neither re-readable now. The column-0 fix may have resolved them both; that cannot be asserted without a reproduction.
updates.next_check: after the fix merges, re-run an #8598-shaped cmd (long, multi-section, containing a column-0 `word:`) and confirm every section's output appears; do NOT pursue a length ladder
