items.title: [test-infra] pytest.approx is unreliable suite-wide when numpy is absent — a truthy sys.modules stub makes it RAISE instead of compare
items.detail:
`pytest.approx.__eq__` branches on `np := sys.modules.get('numpy')` and then touches `np.bool_`. numpy is NOT installed in the lean test env, but something in the suite leaves a truthy stub at `sys.modules['numpy']` (tests/conftest.py::_stub_optional inserts MagicMock() for missing optional deps and the pattern propagates). `approx` then raises inside `is_bool` instead of comparing.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A LINT NIT: it is a HEISENBUG. An assertion passes when its file runs alone and fails in a full run, with the CORRECT value in the traceback (observed: `val = 8000.0` on an `== approx(8_000.0)` assertion). I initially read my own 5 new failures as a real regression in the code under test; they were not. Any future session doing the same before/after diff will hit the same false signal, and the reverse is worse — a genuinely broken assertion can be dismissed as 'just the numpy thing'.

BLAST RADIUS: 144 `is_bool` frames in a single selective run, so a large share of the ~81 baseline failures in that selection are this artifact rather than real defects. That means the local baseline is not a trustworthy regression reference until this is fixed.

WORKAROUND USED: tests/test_risk_gross_exposure.py uses an explicit `close_to()` tolerance helper instead of approx.

NOT ASSERTED: I did not confirm which module inserts the numpy stub — `grep numpy tests/conftest.py` finds nothing, so it arrives transitively. That is the first thing to establish.
items.what_to_check: Run any approx-using test file alone (passes) then in a full run (raises in is_bool). Find who sets sys.modules['numpy'] — likely a transitive _stub_optional call. Fix by not stubbing numpy with a MagicMock, or by installing numpy in the test env.
items.resolution_criteria: An approx-based assertion behaves identically alone and in a full run.

items.title: [observability] a strategy that CANNOT evaluate is indistinguishable from one that evaluated and declined — no alert exists for permanent data starvation
items.detail:
THE GENERALIZABLE DEFECT BEHIND THE SPLG CASE, and the reason it sat unnoticed.

8 strategy modules (trend_donchian, fvg_range_15m, fade_breakout_4h, turtle_soup, htf_pullback_trend_2h, ict_scalp, squeeze_breakout_4h, vwap) emit a 'need at least N candles ... got M' no-trade signal. NOTHING aggregates or alerts on it.

To every monitoring surface both states look identical — `side: none`:
  CANNOT evaluate : "need at least 46 candles ...; got 35"   (permanent, structural)
  evaluated, declined: "no breakout on the latest bar (close=773.075 within channel [716.58, 776.81])"  (normal, healthy)
Only the free-text `reason` distinguishes them, and nothing reads it.

The stuck-strategy detector (STUCK_STRATEGY_THRESHOLD_MINUTES) keys on TIME SINCE LAST SIGNAL. A data-starved strategy emits a signal every single tick, so it reads as perfectly healthy. That is why SPLG could shout its exact blocker every 5 minutes for days with nobody seeing it — and why the /system-review that DID look reached for KILL instead of the audit log.

PROPOSED (not built): treat 'cannot evaluate' as its own state. Any strategy whose evaluations are 100% insufficient-data over a rolling window is data-starved, not quiet — alert on it the way a down broker account alerts. This is the same shape as the news-coverage guard: detect a whole CLASS of silent capability loss rather than the one instance that happened to be noticed.
items.recommendation: A startup + periodic check that every configured strategy/symbol can actually obtain the data its parameters require (lookback vs available bars), alerting when it cannot. Proposed to the operator 2026-08-07 as a shared mechanism with the news-coverage guard.
items.resolution_criteria: A strategy that cannot evaluate for lack of data raises its own alert rather than looking identical to one finding no setup.

items.title: Puller counted ATTEMPTS as successes — a 100%-failing account was indistinguishable from an empty book, for weeks, with systemd green
items.what_to_check: Two halves compose into the outage. PRODUCER: exchange_fills_puller.fetch_fills_window caught every per-target exception and returned [] (the silent-empty shape). CONSUMER: pull_exchange_fills.main incremented `ran` for any account with credentials, regardless of outcome, and returned `0 if ran > 0 else 2` — the unasserted-denominator shape (docs sub-class C). Neither guard covers the other, exactly as CLAUDE.md notes for silent-empty-guard vs diagnostic-provenance-guard. items.title: The exit-anchor estimator's 'median 1.33 bps' was measured on rows it is never applied to — the two populations are disjoint by construction
items.what_to_check: Rows the validator can score have a broker fill, so closed_at came from the broker record (the true close time). Rows the sweep prices have NO broker fill, so closed_at is detection time — the anchor is the bar at whenever the reconciler happened to notice. Worked example: AVAXUSDT trades 4361 (trend_donchian_avax_4h) and 4413 (ict_scalp_avax_5m) on bybit_1 closed 1.34s apart (2026-08-06T10:17:15.670 and 10:17:17.008) carrying the IDENTICAL exit_price 6.416 despite different entries (6.788 / 6.692) and different stops (6.46475 / 6.6592). One bar close stamped on two rows. 4413 opened 2026-08-05T08:03 — the anchor sits at the far end of a >=26h window — and the resulting -8.41R (pnl -$4,254.24) is the distance from 4413's own stop to 4361's exit, not a measured fill. Note this does NOT make the estimator wrong where it was validated; it makes the quoted accuracy inapplicable where it is used. Sub-class B (implicit input selection) raised one level, at the validation rather than the diagnostic.
items.action: Do not re-price history (the 2026-07-30 relabel-only operator decision stands). Options to weigh: (a) record whether closed_at is broker-sourced or detection-sourced and expose it, so a consumer can tell a close-time anchor from a detection-time one; (b) re-run the validator restricted to rows whose closed_at is detection-time to get an honest error distribution for the applied population; (c) treat a detection-time anchor as a distinct, weaker provenance than a close-time anchor rather than both being ESTIMATED. Blocked on BL-20260807-BYBIT-DEMO-FILLS-NEVER-PULLED for bybit_1 — without exchange fills there is no ground truth on that account to validate against.
items.resolution_criteria: An anchored row's provenance distinguishes close-time from detection-time anchoring, and the accuracy figure quoted for the estimator is computed on the population it is applied to.
items.measured_2026_08_07:
FIRST MEASUREMENT ON THE APPLIED POPULATION, now possible because bybit_1 exchange truth exists. POPULATION (stated explicitly): the 3 AVAXUSDT/bybit_1 trades whose fills fall in the 7-day window — 4314 (trend_donchian_avax_4h, closed 08-02), 4361 (trend_donchian_avax_4h, closed 08-06), 4413 (ict_scalp_avax_5m, closed 08-06). The window contains EXACTLY 6 AVAX fills (3 entries + 3 exits) and first_exec_time 2026-08-01T18:33:23.795Z matches trade 4314's created_at 18:33:24 to the second, so the 6 fills are those 3 trades and nothing else; open_qty_signed is 0 (flat). 

JOURNAL sum of the 3 rows: -2840.5578 + -2574.612 + -4254.2364 = -$9,669.41. EXCHANGE realized over the same 6 fills (FIFO-matched, net of $233.91 fees): -$5,403.09. The journal OVERSTATES the loss by $4,266.32 — 79% more than broker truth. 

MECHANISM CONFIRMED IN THE TIMESTAMPS: the last real AVAX fill is 2026-08-06T10:00:58.915Z, but the journal closed 4361 at 10:17:15.670 and 4413 at 10:17:17.008 — ~16 minutes AFTER the position was already flat — and stamped BOTH with the same bar close of 6.416 despite different entries (6.788 / 6.692) and different stops (6.46475 / 6.6592). So the detection lag here is ~16 MINUTES, not the >=26h the trade's open-to-close span suggested; the anchor is far closer than feared and STILL produced a $4,266 error, because a bar the market has already moved through is not a fill. 

CONSEQUENCE for BL-20260720-ICTSCALP-PASTSTOP-EXITS / the ict_scalp review: trade 4413's -8.41R is substantially an EXIT-PRICE RECONSTRUCTION ARTIFACT, not evidence that a 0.49% stop let price run 8x past it. NOT YET ESTABLISHED: the per-trade split of the $4,266 — /api/bot/pnl/exchange serves by_symbol aggregates only, and although the store implements fifo_pnl_by_strategy, NO HTTP route exposes it (filters are days + account_id, and all three trades are bybit_1). So no corrected R is asserted for 4413 specifically.

items.source: Hit on 2026-08-07 while trying to attribute a measured journal-vs-exchange discrepancy across three trades. POPULATION: the 3 AVAXUSDT trades on account bybit_1 whose fills fall in the /api/bot/pnl/exchange?days=7 window (4314, 4361, 4413) — exactly 6 exchange fills, 3 entries + 3 exits, open_qty_signed 0. Journal sum of those 3 rows -$9,669.41 vs exchange FIFO realized (net of $233.91 fees) -$5,403.09, a $4,266.32 gap (79%). Two of the three trades are trend_donchian_avax_4h and one is ict_scalp_avax_5m, so the per-symbol aggregate cannot say which strategy the gap belongs to.
items.title: Broker-truth PnL can be attributed per STRATEGY in the store, but no endpoint serves it — so a journal-vs-exchange discrepancy cannot be split per trade
items.what_to_check: src/runtime/exchange_fills_store.py implements fifo_pnl_by_strategy (tested in tests/test_exchange_fills_store.py), but its only consumer is scripts/strategy_gate.py. GET /api/bot/pnl/exchange exposes by_symbol aggregates with filters days + account_id only. When several strategies trade the same symbol on the same account — the normal case on bybit_1 — the symbol aggregate cannot separate them, so exchange truth cannot be compared against a per-strategy or per-trade journal figure from the read surface.
items.action:
PARTIALLY ADDRESSED 2026-08-08: added GET /api/bot/pnl/exchange/fills (src.runtime.exchange_fills_store::list_fills) — the raw fill ROWS, filtered by days/account/symbol, with `truncated` declaring a capped page. That is what makes a small population (the 6 AVAX fills) exactly attributable by hand. 

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the per-STRATEGY aggregate. fifo_pnl_by_strategy wants an `order_id -> strategy` map, and src/runtime/broker_cost_attribution.py:13 records why that cannot work alone — a broker SL/TP exit fills under an order id the bot never sees, so the map covers ENTRIES only and every exit would bucket to `unattributed`, leaving FIFO with buys and no sells. strategy_gate.py:32-35 already documents the same gap ('until the P3b resolver lands the caller passes {} and these gates read insufficient_data'). The correct attributor attributes FILLS to TRADES via entry-exact + exit-FIFO (the shape attribute_roundtrip_fees already implements for fees) and then groups trades by strategy — NOT an order_id map. Build it against the new rows so it can be checked, rather than shipping a plausible split.
items.resolution_criteria: A journal-vs-exchange discrepancy on a symbol traded by multiple strategies can be attributed per strategy without adding new code.

items.source: MEASURED across four backfill-fabricated-exits DRY RUNs on 2026-08-08 (issues #8619/#8620/#8622/#8623/#8625/#8627). POPULATION for every run: 889 closed non-backtest rows with pnl NOT NULL, whole journal; 543 already measured/estimated, so 346 candidates. Resolvable-from-own-fills went 3 (08:45Z, 7-day store) -> 39 (13:18Z, after the range-walk fix 036f065c + 315 historical fills from a 180-day pull), and REPRODUCED at 39 across three subsequent runs. Final split of the 307 unresolved, by ACTUAL refusal stage (7830a53a): no_fill_in_window 273 | fills_present_but_qty_unreconciled 28 | account_has_no_fills_stored 6. items.title: Fabricated-exit backlog: 39 of 346 repairable from broker truth; 273 have NO stored close-side fill despite 180-day coverage — demo-account retention is the open question
items.what_to_check:
TWO OF MY OWN HYPOTHESES WERE FALSIFIED HERE; both are recorded because each would have sent the next session the wrong way.

(1) 'Bybit retention is short, so the backlog is unrepairable' — WRONG. Bybit V5 caps the QUERY RANGE at 7 days while retaining 2 years; a --days 90 pull returned the slice [now-90d, now-83d] and reported candidates=0 on all three accounts. Caught by monotonicity: a 90-day window cannot hold fewer fills than the 7 days nested inside it (63/3/13 at 7 days vs 0/0/0 at 90).

(2) 'The residual is mostly the netting qty-refusal, so it is unrepairable BY DESIGN' — ALSO WRONG, and I stated it in advance in #8627 so it could fail honestly. The netting refusal is only 28 rows. 273 rows genuinely have NO close-side fill in their window, on accounts that DO have fill coverage.

THE OPEN LEAD, explicitly a hypothesis and NOT established: the 180-day walk returned only 332 candidate fills for bybit_1, but bybit_1 carries ~323 closed journal trades, which need roughly twice that many fills (entry + exit). No PAGE-CAPPED warning fired, so no chunk hit the 200-row ceiling — the venue simply did not serve that depth. bybit_1 and bybit_portfolio are DEMO accounts (api-demo.bybit.com); the documented '2 years' retention is for the mainnet endpoint, and demo execution history may be purged far sooner. bybit_2 is real money and shows the same shape (85 unresolved), so account type alone may not explain it.
items.action:
NEXT TEST, cheap and decisive: establish the OLDEST stored fill per account and compare it against the age distribution of the unresolved rows. If the oldest fill is far younger than 180 days, the venue is not serving the depth and the 273 are permanently unrepairable from broker truth — they keep their honest FABRICATED/UNVERIFIED provenance, which is the CORRECT outcome, not a failure. GET /api/bot/pnl/exchange/fills?days=180&account_id=bybit_1&limit=1000 answers it in one read (newest-first, so the last row is the oldest; check `truncated`), but NOTE that route is under /api/bot/ and the diag relay only reaches /api/diag/*, so it needs either direct DIAG_BASE_URL egress or a per-chunk count added to the puller's log.

SEPARATELY AND ALREADY ACTIONABLE: the 39 own-fills rows are MEASURED-tier and ready to apply. That is a Tier-2 money-DB write needing one operator OK; it is NOT requested by this row. The 28 qty-unreconciled rows belong to netting attribution (NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_MODE), not to this backfill — guessing a split there is the proration error exit_from_fills refuses on purpose. The 6 alpaca_options_paper rows need a puller for that venue or stay unverified permanently.
items.resolution_criteria: The oldest-stored-fill measurement is recorded per account, closing the question of whether the 273 are recoverable at all; and the operator has either approved or declined applying the 39 MEASURED-tier repairs.
items.resolution_note: PHANTOM-NETTING-ROW HYPOTHESIS FALSIFIED — measured 2026-08-09, system-action issue #8668 (dry run on 0bb9432f). A NEGATIVE result, recorded so no future session re-attempts the repair on this theory. POPULATION: 894 rows scanned, 587 already measured/estimated, 307 unresolved, of which 273 are `no_fill_in_window`. The top-15 (account, symbol) buckets cover 262 of those 273 (96.0%). THE TEST: if the residual were phantom netting rows, it would cluster on the symbols with a known journal-vs-exchange qty divergence. It does not. Known-divergent pairs hold 49/273 = 17.9%. BTCUSDT — NOT a divergent symbol — holds 131/273 = 48.0% (bybit_2 81 + bybit_1 50). bybit_1/BNBUSDT, the symbol carrying the LIVE 2.45x divergence, holds **4 rows = 1.5%**, the smallest bucket shown. The tail runs to 23 distinct pairs across 6 accounts and 4 venue types, including NON-netting venues (alpaca_paper SLV/SPY/QQQ/TLT/GLD, ib_paper MGC/MHG) which cannot have netting artifacts at all. READ: the residual tracks TRADING VOLUME, not divergence — the biggest bucket is the most-traded symbol on the two busiest accounts. So the fabricated-exit backlog and the netting divergence are TWO problems, not one, and these are real trades whose fills are genuinely absent from the store rather than rows that never had a fill. POST-STATE CONFIRMED as a side effect: resolvable went 39 -> 0 and already-measured 547 -> 587 (+40 = the 39 written 2026-08-08 plus one new row), so the Tier-2 apply landed and is not silently re-offering work. NEXT QUESTION (do not guess it): why does the store lack fills for the MOST-traded symbol? The store holds ~540 fills across the three Bybit accounts against 894 journal trades, which is thin. Two candidates, NOT distinguished by anything measured so far: (a) PAGE_LIMIT=200 per 7-day chunk with NO intra-chunk pagination — a busy BTCUSDT week would be page-capped, and fetch_fills_window logs a FULL-page warning when that happens, so the puller run log ALREADY answers this; (b) the walk simply does not reach far enough back for the oldest trades. Read the ict-exchange-fills-pull log for the FULL-page warning before assuming either. || PAGE-CAPPING FALSIFIED + REACH CAUSE FOUND — measured 2026-08-09, diag #8670 (ict-exchange-fills-pull journal, 4 nightly runs 08-06..08-09). (a) ZERO FULL-page warnings; per-run candidates max 61 against PAGE_LIMIT=200 (bybit_1 61/60, bybit_2 3/2, bybit_portfolio 13/11). Page-capping is NOT why the store is thin — that hypothesis is dead. (b) THE ACTUAL CAUSE: every nightly run is `days=7`. The range-walk shipped in #8621 makes a deep window POSSIBLE but nothing exercises it on a schedule — history enters the store only via a one-off MANUAL deep pull. Consequence worth acting on: if the fills store is ever lost or rebuilt, it silently comes back 7 DAYS deep and `/api/bot/pnl/exchange` + the broker-truth cost sweep would serve that as normal. Nothing detects a store that is shallower than the journal it is read against. NOT fixed here (Tier-2, changes a live timer's behaviour): the options are a one-off deep pull re-run after any store rebuild, or a periodic deep-walk on a slower cadence than nightly. Deep-pull cost is ceil(days/7) requests per account, so days=180 is 26 chunks x 3 accounts = 78 requests.

items.source: Found while measuring the two backtest_trend.py engines for BL-20260808-TREND-HARNESS-FORK-SPLITS-FIDELITY-FROM-EVIDENCE. Measured on main @bf72205.
items.title: A LIVE armed Tier-3 trail lever (trend_donchian trail_decay_arm_r 6.49) was tuned on the harness whose trail uses a ROLLING ATR, while the live monitor trails off the FROZEN entry ATR
items.what_to_check:
config/strategies.yaml::trend_donchian declares trail_decay_arm_r: 6.49 and trail_decay_tight_mult: 2.5 TODAY (execution: live, BTCUSDT 1h) - an armed, order-affecting exit lever. src/runtime/trail_decay.py and src/runtime/trail_vol.py both name scripts/research/backtest_trend.py as their 'Harness reference'.

But that harness is NOT the live-faithful one. Measured 2026-08-08 (scripts/research/trend_harness_divergence.py; population BTCUSDT 2022-07-23->27, 1001 5m bars, n=21-35/config, levers OFF): the research engine multiplies the CURRENT bar's rolling ATR on every managed bar, while trend_donchian.order_package freezes the entry ATR into meta['atr'] and monitor() trails off that frozen value. Isolating that axis alone moves gross R by -34.0% / -23.0% / +41.2% across three configs.

WHY IT MATTERS: trail_decay's whole job is to TIGHTEN trail_mult once peak open profit reaches arm_r. Both the R path that reaches 6.49 and the stop path the tightened mult then produces depend on the baseline trail's distance - which is the thing that differs. So the arm threshold and tight mult were fitted against a trail that behaves differently from the one running on real money. This is NOT an assertion that 6.49 is wrong; it is that its evidence base does not reproduce the live trail, and nothing has measured the gap.

NOT a live incident: the lever is reductive (tightens a stop, never loosens it - trail_decay re-loosens the MULT on a new peak but the caller's price ratchet never loosens the STOP), so the failure mode is a suboptimal exit, not an unprotected position.
items.proposed_fix: Sequenced behind BL-20260808-TREND-HARNESS-FORK-SPLITS-FIDELITY-FROM-EVIDENCE step (a): once the research levers are ported onto the live-faithful engine, RE-RUN the M20 trail-decay sweep for trend_donchian on that engine over real BTC 1h history and compare the chosen (arm_r, tight_mult) cell against 6.49/2.5. Report the delta per fold, not a single pooled number. If the optimum moves materially, the config change is Tier-3 -> operator-approved PR; if it does not, record that and correct the two module docstrings to cite the live-faithful harness. Either way the docstring citations in src/runtime/trail_decay.py + trail_vol.py should stop pointing at an engine the fidelity pipeline never runs. Cheap partial mitigation available immediately: run scripts/research/trend_harness_divergence.py --data <real BTC 1h history> to size the axis honestly on the leg's own instrument/timeframe.
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-08-09 as HOLD-AT-2.5 (operator approved the retune conditional on testing it; the test withdrew it). Re-sweep on the converged engine confirmed the live cell arm6.49/tight2.5 fails the exit gate on IS maxDD (+0.4220R, 14.7968 -> 15.2188) -- reproduced on BOTH the date-restricted and full-tape-split bases (bases_agree: true), so the tuning-basis defect is real. But per-trade attribution (scripts/research/m20_trail_attribution.py; trainer-diag #8672/#8676/#8677) shows the proposed tight_mult 2.0 is NOT the fix: POPULATION 250 trades, only 17 (6.8%) arm the lever and just 3 of 75 OOS. On those 17, 2.0 is WORSE by 1.8395R -- it gains exactly +0.2R on 14 trades (the mechanical (2.5-2.0)*ATR / (2.5*ATR) when both arms stop on the same bar) and loses 4.6395R on 3 where the tighter stop fired earlier. Its apparent +0.2960R aggregate edge is a SEQUENCING artifact: the residual +2.1355R comes from 3 trades present in only one book (2 unique to live, 1 to proposed) after one shifted exit moved next_idx over a week in June 2023. Negative at every arm with a usable sample (3.0/4.0/5.0/6.49); only arm 8.0 is positive and it is TOO_THIN (n=7). Config UNCHANGED. Two bounds: the lever vs OFF is +9.53R at identical full-tape maxDD (27.3002 across all three arms), so the lever earns its place and option B (remove) is also unsupported; and nothing can fire below 6.49R peak, which 2026 has not reached (max 4.593 over 35 trades). Memo: docs/research/M20-trail-decay-resweep-2026-08-09.md (superseding section).

items.title: exchange_funding_puller has the SAME single-call/no-chunking shape that made the fills puller silently return a wrong window — and it is invoked with days=30
items.source: READ FROM SOURCE 2026-08-08, NOT measured — stated as an unverified structural exposure, not a confirmed defect. src/runtime/exchange_funding_puller.py::fetch_funding_window issues ONE fetch_funding_history(sym, since_ms, 200, {}) per target with no pagination and no range chunking, and scripts/pull_exchange_funding.py / the pull-exchange-funding action invoke it with days=30. That is byte-for-byte the shape fetch_fills_window had before 036f065c.
items.what_to_check:
The fills sibling was NOT hypothetical: Bybit caps /v5/execution/list's query RANGE at 7 days while retaining 2 years, so a --days 90 call returned the slice [now-90d, now-83d] and reported candidates=0 on all three accounts while looking successful (exit 0, ok=3 failed=0). If Bybit's funding/transaction-log endpoint carries ANY range cap below 30 days, the nightly funding pull has been returning a wrong window the whole time, and the same two properties that hid the fills bug hide this one: an out-of-range read returns [] rather than raising (so FundingWindowUnavailable never fires), and the 200-row limit has no cap declaration.

I have NOT established Bybit's funding range cap. Do not record one until measured.

WHY IT MATTERS: funding is a real cost component. backfill-broker-truth-costs attributes funding_paid_usd onto closed trades from this store, so a silently-short funding window under-reports cost and biases every net-R figure computed on top of it in the favourable direction.
items.action:
CHEAP DECISIVE TEST, the same monotonicity check that caught the fills bug and needs no new code: dispatch pull-exchange-funding twice, once narrow and once wide, and compare candidate counts per account. A WIDER window returning FEWER rows is proof the range was silently rewritten. If it reproduces, port the MAX_RANGE_DAYS walk from exchange_fills_puller (chunk oldest-first, pass endTime explicitly, dedupe on funding_id, declare a full page) — the fix is already written and tested next door, so this is a port, not a design.

If it does NOT reproduce, record the measured window depth in this row and close it: 'checked and clean' is the useful result, and leaving the question open invites a future session to re-derive it.
items.resolution_criteria: Bybit's funding-history range behaviour is MEASURED for these accounts and recorded here, and either the walk is ported or the puller is documented as correct at days=30.
items.resolution_note: STILL UNVERIFIED — but no longer UNVERIFIABLE, which was the actual blocker. Two things shipped 2026-08-09 (PR pending): (1) `pull-exchange-funding` now takes a `days:` selector (it hardcoded 30 with no override, so the monotonicity test that caught the fills bug — a wider window returning FEWER rows than a narrower one nested inside it — could not be run at all). The workflow's per-action ACTION_DAYS plumbing became a list rather than one `if` per action, since funding needing exactly that missing line is what caused this. (2) fetch_funding_window now logs the span it was actually SERVED beside the one it requested, and WARNs when the newest row falls far short of the window end — the signature of a moved-not-widened window. So the next ORDINARY nightly run is itself the evidence; a probe may not be needed. The warning is deliberately cause-neutral: from inside the puller a stale tail is genuinely ambiguous between 'no position was open across a funding settlement' and 'the recent period was never queried', and only the journal knows which. Naming one would be the sub-class-A defect. SHARPER THAN THE FILLS CASE IF TRUE: fills defaulted to 7 days, INSIDE the cap, so only deep probes were affected. Funding requests 30. If the cap applies, production has been serving [now-30d, now-23d] nightly and missing the most RECENT three weeks of funding while printing a healthy row count — which would under-attribute funding_paid_usd in the broker-truth cost sweep. NEXT: read the next nightly ict-exchange-funding-pull run log for the SERVED span line; or dispatch days:7 vs days:30 and compare counts.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: src/runtime/exchange_funding_puller.py::fetch_funding_window:154-161 still issues ONE `fetch_funding_history(sym, since_ms, 200, {})` per target with no chunking and no pagination — the shape the row flagged. What DID land is the detector: `_log_returned_span` (called at :171) declares the span actually returned vs the span requested, with the fills-sibling incident cited at :143-150, and a `FundingWindowUnavailable` raise when every target fails (:174-177). So the exposure is now observable but not eliminated. — needs live data: one nightly pull-exchange-funding run's `_log_returned_span` line for a days=30 request, to establish whether Bybit's funding endpoint carries a range cap. Do NOT record a cap until measured — the row is explicit that none has been established. Ending condition: either the span line shows the full 30 days (exposure refuted) or it shows a short window and the chunking loop is added, mirroring exchange_fills_puller's MAX_RANGE_DAYS walk.

Re-validated: the funding puller carries the same single-call/no-chunking shape that already caused a silent wrong window in the fills puller. A known-bad shape reproduced in a sibling is exactly the recurrence class this review was asked to look for.

items.source: Deferred OUT of PR #8633 after CI (pytest-collect + pytest-run) caught an attempt to retire the engine in that PR. Measured on the #8633 branch @2fb2081a.
items.title: scripts/research/backtest_trend.py cannot be retired yet: 8 importers, 5 of them test files whose assertions ARE the only executable record of that engine's semantics
items.what_to_check: PR #8633 converged the FLAGS (all 15 research-only levers ported into scripts/backtest_trend.py, byte-identical at default; research-only flag count 15 -> 0) but deliberately did NOT retire the losing engine. POPULATION for the consumer sweep: the whole repo, `grep -rn 'from backtest_trend import'` (NOT a path grep - see the trap below). EIGHT importers, measured: scripts/research/regime_adx_cutpoint_sweep.py (_load, _resample) | scripts/research/regime_tag_emitted.py (_load, _resample) | scripts/research/regime_matrix.py (_load, _resample, backtest) | tests/test_skip_hours_lever.py (backtest) | tests/test_confirm_bars_live_twin.py (backtest) | tests/test_confirm_bars_lever.py (backtest) | tests/test_vol_conditional_trail_lever.py (backtest as trend_backtest) | tests/test_vol_at_entry_lever.py (backtest as trend_backtest). The five TEST files are the blocker, not the three scripts: their assertions encode the research engine's OWN semantics (rolling current-bar ATR trail, opposite-signal flip exit, post-exit cooldown, its fee basis and win-rate denominator). They are currently the only executable record of what that engine does, i.e. the evidence a future session would need to re-confirm the convergence direction. Deleting the engine without migrating them destroys that record silently. THE TRAP THAT CAUSED THIS (reusable, worth more than the row): the original sweep grepped for the PATH 'scripts/research/backtest_trend' and returned CLEAN. Every real importer uses the BARE MODULE NAME resolved through sys.path, so the path grep under-reported over a population it structurally could not see - an unasserted-denominator read (CLAUDE.md 'Diagnostic provenance' sub-class C) applied to a code sweep rather than a diagnostic. When sweeping for consumers of a Python module in this repo, grep the MODULE NAME, never the path.
items.proposed_fix: Sequenced, in its own PR (Tier-1 throughout - research tooling + tests only, no config/, no order path, no DB write): (1) Decide per test file whether the behaviour it pins is (a) research-engine-specific - then port the assertion onto scripts/backtest_trend.py's semantics and re-derive the expected numbers, stating the new population, or (b) genuinely engine-independent - then just repoint the import. Do NOT blanket-repoint: several of these assert the rolling-ATR trail and the flip exit, which the live-faithful engine does NOT have, so a blind repoint turns a real test into a green one that checks nothing. (2) Repoint the three scripts/research/* callers - regime_matrix.py needs `backtest` (a real engine swap, re-verify its output), while regime_adx_cutpoint_sweep.py and regime_tag_emitted.py only need `_load`/`_resample` (pure IO helpers; consider lifting those two into a shared module so the retirement stops being blocked on them at all). (3) Only then retire scripts/research/backtest_trend.py - prefer a hard-fail shim over a deletion so a missed caller gets an explanation rather than a FileNotFoundError, and a third copy cannot quietly reappear. (4) Convert scripts/research/trend_harness_divergence.py from a comparison instrument into a convergence GUARD that fails if a flag ever exists only in a non-live-faithful copy again; it must detect the shim by the absence of its engine entry point, not by parsing prose. Gate: the guard in (4) is what makes the retirement durable - landing (3) without it just re-opens the fork later.
items.resolution: RETIRED. Sequence landed in one PR: (1) all 5 coupled test files migrated onto the live-faithful scripts/backtest_trend.py via tests/trend_harness_engine.py — 4 were engine-INDEPENDENT (entry-side assertions; both engines agreed on the entry bar, so no number moved) and 1, tests/test_vol_conditional_trail_lever.py, was genuinely engine-SPECIFIC and was PORTED with re-derived numbers (its tape's trade SET differs: research 1 trade/base vs live-faithful 2, and the gated long moves from exit 07:00 r+0.6786 to exit 08:00 r+1.6786 — population in that file's docstring). 30 tests before, 30 after. (2) _load/_resample lifted VERBATIM to scripts/candle_io.py (proved identical: 5000 rows DataFrame.equals True, 4 resample rules identical) and the two IO-only scripts repointed; regime_matrix.py took the real engine swap. (3) The engine became a hard-fail shim (module-level __getattr__ raising RetiredEngineError) rather than a deletion — importable so the guard can confirm it exposes no entry point, but any attribute access fails with the migration map. (4) trend_harness_divergence.py became the trend-engine-convergence-guard, wired into scripts/ci/run_guards.py with when:None. RE-VERIFIED regime_matrix across the swap (the operator's explicit ask): on the committed smoke corpus (BTCUSDT 1h, 84 bars, 2022-07-23 22:00Z->2022-07-27 09:00Z, dc20/atr14/stop2.5/trail5.0) it moves from 1 trade +1.5727 net R in the TRENDING bucket to 1 trade -0.2246 in TRANSITIONAL — sign flip and bucket change, 100% attributable to the engine (cooldown 0/1/3 and timeout 200/10000 all give -0.2246 on this corpus). n=1, so DIRECTION only. Consequence recorded in the module docstring: any regime-matrix number from before 2026-08-09 was produced on the engine the live strategy does not match.

items.source: Self-caught in PR #8633 by parametrizing a test over BOTH branches of a predicate it had only ever exercised one side of. Measured on the #8633 branch @b7547005.
items.title: An `exit_head_replayable()` gate shipped INERT — byte-identical output on both branches — and the PR description claimed a measured behaviour change it did not produce
items.what_to_check: FIXED in #8633; filed for the CLASS, which is not covered by any existing guard. The defect: `regime_debt_matrix.build_harness_cmd` computes `omitted` as 'every cfg key not in _TREND_PLAIN and not in _TREND_LEVER_FLAG' (line ~343), so exit_head_model/threshold/action land there unconditionally and `faithful = not omitted` is already False. The change made a SECOND, caller-level `_UNREPLAYABLE` fold conditional on `exit_head_replayable()` - but that fold only ever did `omitted | unreplayable`, a UNION. A union can add, never remove. So with the probe forced True the output was IDENTICAL: faithful=False, omitted=['exit_head_action','exit_head_model','exit_head_threshold']. VERIFIED by monkeypatching the probe both ways. The PR body meanwhile stated 'the remaining exit_head_* clear wherever the artifact is present' - a claim no code path produced. WHY THE TESTS MISSED IT: the fidelity test asserted a flat `faithful is False`, which is the value BOTH branches return, so it passed while proving nothing about the branch. On a GitHub runner only the no-head branch is reachable, so the trainer branch was never executed anywhere. This is the D/inert-parameter sub-class of `diagnostic-provenance-guard` (a declared knob that changes nothing) crossed with the 'written and never read' shape `provenance-consumer-guard` catches - but neither guard fires here, because the inert thing is a CONTROL-FLOW predicate, not a printed label or a stored key.
items.proposed_fix: The instance is fixed: the inert fold is deleted, replaced by `annotate_exit_head_replayability()` which records `exit_head_replayable` + `exit_head_deferred_to_replay` as EXPLICIT row fields; `fidelity` deliberately stays harness-scoped (upgrading it on a loadable head would claim the row's numbers account for an exit head that never touched them - the row's numbers come from the harness, the replay is a separate pass). The trainer workflow now reads the same predicate instead of re-deriving it from an `ls`, so the field is load-bearing rather than write-only. Tests parametrize over both branches. THE CLASS is what needs a decision: is a guard worth it for 'a new conditional whose branches produce identical output'? A cheap approximation is a review-time rule rather than a script - when a diff makes an existing unconditional path conditional, the PR must show the measured output of BOTH branches, not just assert the intent. Consider adding that to the review skill's checklist; a static guard would likely be high-false-positive (many conditionals legitimately no-op on the common path). Do NOT add a presence-only marker guard - see the new-table-wiring-guard lesson in CLAUDE.md (a guard cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than none).

updates.note: Triaged in the system-review 2026-08-10 (RPT since-last, window from 2026-08-07T14:55Z) full-backlog pass. This run produced NO new evidence bearing on this item — the state I pulled (live diag: services/heartbeat/tick_cost/db_info/positions/balances/exchange_positions/notifications; performance 24h+7d; exchange-truth PnL; the pairs/allocator/exit-ladder/fc-geometry/netting/exposure soaks; ML lifecycle via /api/bot/ml/status; m20_exit_analysis on the trainer) does not touch it. Carried forward unchanged rather than restated as re-validated — recording a re-check I did not perform would be the exact dishonesty the review rules forbid.

What is open is the CLASS decision, and it closes on a recorded choice: either the review-skill checklist gains the rule - a diff that makes an existing unconditional path conditional must show the MEASURED output of both branches, not assert the intent - or that rule is declined with a reason. items.source: Found while qualifying the FIRST measured exit-head replay result (issue #8653, trainer-diag #8656). Measured on the trainer @247f025c.
items.title: Exit-head artifacts DON'T RECORD their training window (train_start/train_end), so a replay's in-sample fraction can't be read off the artifact — though the exporter already holds the rows needed to write it
items.what_to_check: MEASURED on the trainer (#8656): exit-head-donchian-1h-v1.json carries trained_at=2026-07-12T14:44:43Z, train_rows=34338, train_trades=1662, symbols=[BTCUSDT,ETHUSDT,SOLUSDT], tf=1h, shape={policy:below_half_r,tau:0.1,below_r:0.5}, 14 features, evidence='docs/research/M20-exit-refinement-2026-07-12.md 9'. No train_start / train_end / dataset id. CORRECTED CLAIM — checked: scripts/ml/export_exit_head.py + scripts/ml/build_exit_head_dataset.py. An earlier draft of this row said the window 'cannot be computed'. That is FALSE and impossibility-claim-guard caught it, correctly: export_exit_head.py:70-82 builds the artifact dict while `rows` is in scope, and those rows come from harness emit JSONLs (build_exit_head_dataset.py --trades) which carry per-trade timestamps. So the window IS derivable AT EXPORT TIME (min/max over rows) — it is simply never written. What is genuinely true is narrower: the window is not recoverable FROM THE ARTIFACT ALONE by a downstream consumer, and `trained_at` is the wall-clock moment of fitting, not the data bound, so the two must not be used interchangeably. WHY IT MATTERS: the first measured exit-head replay (#8653) scored 2026-02-09 -> 2026-08-07 and reported delta_gross_r +10.804 on n=31 trades (30 scored, 24 re-resolved), baseline -11.826R -> replayed -1.022R. Assessing how much of that is in-sample required INFERRING from trained_at that the data ends ~2026-07-12, implying ~5 of 6 replayed months sit at-or-before fitting time and only ~26 days are forward. POPULATION: train_trades=1662 across three symbols vs 31 BTC-only trades replayed (~54x), a second reason the delta is not an edge. This is the diagnostic-provenance class one level upstream: the replay's output cannot state its own derivation (in-sample vs forward) because the artifact it consumes drops a fact its producer had in hand.
items.proposed_fix: (1) scripts/ml/export_exit_head.py — write train_start / train_end (min/max of the row timestamps already in `rows` at line ~70) plus the dataset/emit paths, alongside the existing trained_at. Additive; no consumer breaks. (2) scripts/ml/exit_head_replay.py — once (1) lands, emit in_sample_bars / forward_bars / forward_trades beside the delta so the split is a FIELD, not a caveat a reader has to remember. Same shape /performance already uses with rCoverage rather than silently blending measured and manufactured rows. (3) Until (1) lands, any exit-head replay result MUST be quoted with trained_at AND the scoring window together, and must not be presented as an edge. Do NOT widen the replay window to 'get more data' — a longer window makes the in-sample fraction LARGER. The fix for evidence quality is a forward-only window (start > train_end), which belongs with the M20 re-sweep (BL-20260808-TRAIL-LEVER-TUNED-ON-NON-LIVE-FAITHFUL-TRAIL).
items.resolution: BOTH halves shipped. (1) scripts/ml/export_exit_head.py now writes train_start / train_end / train_window_coverage / train_dataset beside the existing trained_at, derived by the new pure helper training_window(rows) from each row's `bar_t` (epoch seconds of the in-trade bar, written by build_exit_head_dataset.py) — the data the exporter already held. HONEST-NULL: a row set with no usable bar_t yields None rather than a manufactured date, and train_window_coverage reports the fraction of rows that actually carried one, so a partially-stamped dataset cannot pass as a fully-measured window. (2) scripts/ml/exit_head_replay.py now emits an `in_sample_split` block via the pure helper split_in_sample(): in_sample_bars / forward_bars / in_sample_trades / forward_trades plus a FORWARD-ONLY baseline/replayed/delta gross R — and prints them next to the headline delta, not only into --json, because the delta alone is the number that gets quoted. `trained_at` is never substituted for `train_end` (a pre-fix artifact reports train_window_present:false and nulls throughout, and an unparseable train_end degrades to UNKNOWN rather than to epoch 0, which would have manufactured a fully-out-of-sample claim). A boundary row counts as IN-sample — the conservative direction, since the alternative inflates the forward population. 12 tests in tests/test_exit_head_training_window.py pin the arithmetic (not just the source text): on a fixture mirroring the #8653 shape the headline delta is +9.25 while the forward-only delta is +2.25. NOT DONE, deliberately: the replay window was not widened - a longer window makes the in-sample fraction LARGER, and the fix for evidence quality is a forward-only window (start > train_end), which belongs with the M20 re-sweep.

items.title: pairs-sleeve journal/exchange divergence has NO owner — the netting reconciler refuses it by design and pairs_executor never reconciles its own legs
items.source: MEASURED live 2026-08-08. bybit_1/BNBUSDT short: open journal rows sum to 13.43, the exchange backs 5.49 (2.45x, excess 7.94). _check_broker_naked_bybit_positions logged it at ERROR every ~5 minutes continuously. BNBUSDT is a pairs-sleeve leg (config/pairs.yaml: symbol_a BNBUSDT / symbol_b BTCUSDT, execution live on paper).
items.what_to_check:
THE ASYMMETRY: _reconcile_netting_partial_closes deliberately SKIPS pairs rows (summary['skipped_pairs']) because pairs_executor is an isolated 2-leg path holding its own state and closing its rows behind its back would desync it (design packet §4 constraint 2). The divergence sweep had NO pairs handling and printed the generic 'At least one open row is a phantom' ERROR anyway. So the alarm named a remediation that was never coming — a permanent ERROR no operator could action.

That is the alarm-fatigue P1 in CLAUDE.md § 'If you see something, say something': an alarm that fires constantly and is routinely walked past trains everyone to walk past the ones that matter. PARTIALLY FIXED in this session — the sweep now branches on ownership, emits a WARNING naming pairs_executor and stating that no attribution pass will reduce it, and both call sites share ONE _is_pairs_sleeve_row predicate so they cannot drift apart about who owns a row.

WHAT IS NOT FIXED, and is why this row is open: the DIVERGENCE ITSELF. 13.43 journal vs 5.49 exchange on a live-trading sleeve means analytics and risk sizing both read a journal that overstates the position by 2.45x. Relabelling the alarm did not reduce a single row.
items.action:
Teach pairs_executor to reconcile its own legs — it is the only component allowed to touch those rows, so it is the only place the fix can live. Mirror the netting reconciler's contract rather than inventing a second one: 2-observation confirm before acting, leg-id-then-FIFO selection, and the anchored/no_anchor/deferred provenance ladder (an anchorless estimate is FABRICATED). Tier-2 — it writes the money DB.

DO NOT 'fix' this by removing the pairs skip from _reconcile_netting_partial_closes. The skip is load-bearing: closing a pairs leg behind the executor's back desyncs the sleeve, which is a worse failure than an overstated journal.
items.resolution_criteria: bybit_1/BNBUSDT journal qty matches the exchange within tolerance, and a pairs-sleeve divergence is reduced by a reconciler that owns those rows rather than being relabelled.
items.resolution_note: ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-09 (PR pending). It is a collapsed-state bug, the same shape as the other two this session: `_close_pair` is best-effort PER LEG and deliberately leaves a leg that failed to flatten open ('the monitor/backstop retries'), but `run_pairs_tick` asked only `_pair_is_open` = are BOTH legs open. So leg-A-closed / leg-B-stranded answered False — INDISTINGUISHABLE from a pair that was never opened. The tick then built open_state=None, the decision saw no position, and the executor was free to emit a fresh `open` and place BOTH legs again, stacking a second journal row on the stranded leg's symbol while the venue holds ONE netted position. That is the divergence, and the 'monitor/backstop retries' the comment relied on does not exist for these rows: the netting-attribution reconciler skips pairs rows BY DESIGN (_is_pairs_sleeve_row -> skipped_pairs), on the correct premise that this executor owns its own legs. It did not. FIX: `_pair_leg_state` returns open / flat / half_open. A half-open pair flattens the stranded leg (live only; shadow has no order authority), alerts `pairs_half_open` (CRITICAL while the leg stands, WARN once flattened — a lone leg is un-hedged directional exposure in a market-neutral sleeve, the same exposure `_legs_below_min_qty` refuses to CREATE at open time), logs a `half_open` soak row with stranded_legs + cleanup_confirmed, and places NOTHING that bar. `_pair_is_open` keeps its meaning for the concurrency helpers but no longer decides. Two of the new tests were verified to FAIL against the restored two-state read. STILL OPEN: the fix stops NEW divergence; it does not retire the EXISTING bybit_1/BNBUSDT ~2.45x journal excess. Those rows are pre-existing and need a separate one-off reconciliation, which must come from this executor (or an explicitly pairs-aware tool) rather than the netting reconciler whose pairs skip is deliberate and must NOT be deleted.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The ownership/labelling half shipped: src/units/strategies/pairs_executor.py:204-272 implements the three-state open/flat/half_open predicate, `_alert_half_open_pair` (CRITICAL while a leg stands, WARN once flattened) and the stranded-leg flatten at :819-828, with the divergence shape documented at :217-219. But the row's stated open half — reducing the EXISTING divergence — has no owner still: grepping pairs_executor for a reconciliation of its own legs finds only the half-open cleanup, and order_monitor's netting reconciler still skips pairs rows by design. — needs live data: /api/bot/pairs/soak and the open BNBUSDT journal-vs-exchange sums on bybit_1, to see whether the 2026-08-10 max-hold flush cleared the 13.43-vs-5.49 backlog. Tier-2 either way (a DB writeback). Ending condition: a pairs-scoped attribution pass (or a one-off reconciliation) reduces the stale rows, or they are supersede-flagged so analytics stop reading them.

LIVE AND ACTIVE: 35 `pairs_half_open cleaned` WARN events in 9 days (30 SOL/ETH, 5 BNB/BTC), and 17 of the 42 pairs closes in this window exited via pairs_half_open_cleanup. The netting reconciler still refuses pairs rows by design and pairs_executor still does not reconcile, so the divergence remains unowned while occurring several times a day.

items.title: Gross-exposure governance is phase 1 of 2 — the ceiling VALUES were explicitly deferred, and the observability gap is why phase 2 stalled
items.source:
READ FROM SOURCE + config 2026-08-08. src/units/accounts/risk.py: the cap is fully wired — evaluate() refuses GROSS_EXPOSURE_CAP at the boundary, position_size() clamps into exposure_headroom_usd() below it, report() surfaces it. config/accounts.yaml declares max_gross_exposure_pct on NONE of the 11 accounts, so gross_exposure() short-circuits to None and every path is inert — including real-money bybit_2. Shipped 2026-08-07, never enabled anywhere.

CORRECTION 2026-08-08 (same session, later): my original framing of 'shipped 2026-08-07, never enabled' implied an oversight. It was not. bb5203ae's commit message closes with: 'No config/accounts.yaml change: declaring max_gross_exposure_pct on a live account is Tier-3 and is proposed separately, not shipped here.' The feature was DELIBERATELY shipped unset as phase 1. Phase 2 never happened — that is the actual gap, and the observability chicken-and-egg below is the plausible reason why.
items.what_to_check:
THE CHICKEN-AND-EGG: gross_exposure() returns None unless a ceiling is configured, and report()['exposure'] is gated the same way. So the exposure MULTIPLE has never been visible on any account, and an operator cannot pick an informed cap — they would have to declare an arbitrary one first to find out what they actually run at.

I ATTEMPTED the obvious fix (measure always, enforce only when declared) and REVERTED it. Recording both traps, because each is a fleet-wide trading halt and neither is visible from the diff:

  TRAP 1 — evaluate(): `state[2] >= self.max_gross_exposure_pct` with the default 0.0 is true for ANY exposure INCLUDING 0.0. Ungating the measurement without guarding enforcement refuses every trade on every live account, even a flat one.

  TRAP 2 — position_size(): exposure_headroom_usd() computes `max(0, pct*equity - notional)`, which at pct=0 is max(0, -notional) = 0.0. Headroom zero clamps EVERY position to nothing. I guarded trap 1 and missed this one entirely; the pre-existing tests/test_risk_gross_exposure.py caught it.

  ALSO: test_unset_ceiling_is_a_noop asserts `gross_exposure() is None` when unset — 'no declared ceiling => no exposure state, no gate, no clamp' is a DELIBERATE, tested contract, not an oversight. Any change here is a design change and must argue with that test, not just edit around it.

FULL DESIGN INVESTIGATION: docs/design/gross-exposure-governance-DESIGN.md (2026-08-08). It establishes what the goal actually is — the originating incident was an AVAILABILITY failure (alpaca_paper at 2.03x vs a 2.00x Reg-T limit, available_usd 0.00, REFUSING EVERY SIGNAL), not a loss failure — confirms the gap is real (every other control is per-trade or post-hoc; nothing bounds accumulated concurrent capacity), and proposes separating observation / policy / verdict so both halt vectors become unreachable by construction rather than by guard.
items.action:
SEE docs/design/gross-exposure-governance-DESIGN.md. Two PRs, in order:

1. STRUCTURAL (safe, unblocks everything): split gross_exposure() into observe_exposure() / exposure_policy() / exposure_verdict(). Policy-is-None short-circuits to ALLOW before any arithmetic, so 0.0 can never be compared against nor become a headroom. Observation gains no path to a refusal, so the multiple can be surfaced safely. Preserves test_unset_ceiling_is_a_noop rather than arguing with it: still no gate, still no clamp — only the measurement becomes available. Same remedy exit_anchor.py already applies.

2. VALUES (Tier-3, operator): after soaking (1), a conservative fleet default with per-account overrides (design §5 option C). Option B — deriving from the venue limit — is REJECTED in the doc: Reg-T 2x is a PORTFOLIO limit while Bybit's leverage 3 is PER-POSITION, so deriving one from the other compares different quantities (the semantic-substitution defect class).

BINDING CONSTRAINT on any value (§6): a ceiling that binds in NORMAL operation is worse than none — it silently clamps correctly-risk-sized trades, the exact reasoning that removed POSITION_SIZE_CAP. First value should be deliberately LOOSE: too loose still prevents the 2.03x incident, too tight causes the silent throttling this system keeps getting bitten by.
items.resolution_criteria: Per-account exposure multiples are observable without a declared ceiling, and the operator has either set caps from observed data or explicitly decided the fleet runs uncapped.
items.resolution_note: PHASE 4 (the structural fix) SHIPPED 2026-08-09 — src/units/accounts/exposure.py splits observe / policy / verdict, and both halt vectors recorded above are now unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by guard: exposure_verdict() short-circuits to ALLOW on an absent-or-non-positive policy BEFORE any comparison or arithmetic, so 0.0 can neither be compared against (trap 1) nor become a headroom (trap 2). Asserted directly against the pure verdict function, not only through RiskManager. ENFORCEMENT IS BYTE-FOR-BYTE UNCHANGED — the original test_unset_ceiling_is_a_noop contract (no gate, no clamp with no ceiling declared) is preserved and was strengthened with the position_size() assertion the reverted attempt lacked. WHAT CHANGED: report()['exposure'] is now emitted ALWAYS, so the exposure multiple is visible without declaring a ceiling — which is the input the operator needs and whose absence is the documented reason phase 2 stalled. STILL OPEN, still Tier-3: choosing the VALUES (design § 5, recommendation Option C — one conservative fleet default plus evidence-driven per-account overrides). Per § 6 the first value must be deliberately LOOSE: a too-loose ceiling still prevents the 2.03x incident, a too-tight one causes the silent throttling this system has repeatedly been bitten by. Read the observed multiples off report() first — that is now possible.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The observability half — which the row itself names as why phase 2 stalled — is now CLOSED: /api/diag/exposure and /api/bot/exposure/soak both exist and serve report()['exposure'] verbatim with the three uncollapsed states. But `max_gross_exposure_pct` is still declared on NO account (grep of config/accounts.yaml returns nothing; only src/units/accounts/risk.py:359 reads it, defaulting to 0.0), so evaluate()/position_size()/report() remain inert on every account including real-money bybit_2. — Tier-3 awaiting operator: the ceiling VALUES are the deferred half and gross-exposure-governance-DESIGN.md § 7 forbids shipping one with no observation soak behind it. Ending condition: the soak accumulates a weekday RTH distribution (tracked by BL-20260809-EXPOSURE-SOAK-NOT-YET-TAKEN), the operator picks per-account values above normal operation and below the venue limit, and they are declared in config/accounts.yaml (Tier-3 merge). Note both TRAPs recorded in this row still apply to any implementation: default 0.0 refuses every trade in evaluate(), and exposure_headroom_usd at pct=0 clamps every position to zero.

HALF RESOLVED, AND THE REMAINING HALF IS NOW UNBLOCKED. LIVE EXPOSURE SOAK READ 2026-08-29 — the soak is no longer thin. /api/bot/exposure/soak reports total_scanned 20,328 rows, 1,848 rows PER ACCOUNT, essentially all measured (bybit_1 1848/1848, bybit_2 1848/1848, bybit_portfolio 1848/1848, ib_paper 1818/1848). max_multiple: bybit_portfolio 2.8930, bybit_2 2.7703 (REAL MONEY), bybit_1 1.7705, ib_paper 0.4497. venue_sessions across the soak: closed 10,021 / extended 6,259 / rth 4,048 — so it spans real trading sessions, not just a held weekend book. And policy_declared is FALSE on every account, i.e. no ceiling is declared anywhere. So the observability gap this row names as the reason phase 2 stalled is CLOSED — the distribution exists. What stays open is phase 2 itself: policy_declared is False on every account, i.e. no ceiling is declared, so the cap is still inert. Choosing the values is Tier-3 and is now an operator decision with real numbers behind it rather than a blocked measurement.

items.title: Gross-exposure ceiling values: the measurement is finally readable, but ONE weekend snapshot is not the observation soak the design requires
items.what_to_check:
THE VALUES CANNOT BE CHOSEN FROM THIS READ, and the design already says so: gross-exposure-governance-DESIGN.md section 7 explicitly lists 'any value shipped without section 4's observation soak behind it' as NOT proposed. What exists today is one sample, not a distribution.

WHY THE SNAPSHOT IS PARTICULARLY WEAK: it was taken on a SUNDAY. US equities and CME futures were closed, so the Alpaca and IB numbers are a held-over Friday book with no intraday variation in them. bybit (crypto, 24/7) is the only leg whose reading reflects an active market.

A NEAR-MISS WORTH RECORDING, because the next session will be tempted the same way: alpaca_paper/portfolio/live show no new opens since Friday 15:32Z and ib_paper none since Friday 14:02Z, while bybit_1 traded Sunday 01:14Z. That pattern looks exactly like the originating incident (BL-20260807-ALPACA-PAPER-ZERO-BUYING-POWER-REFUSES-ALL: 'walked to 2.03x ungoverned and then refused every signal with sized_qty=0'). It is NOT. It is the weekend. Venue-closed silence and refusal silence are indistinguishable in the trades table; only the calendar separates them.

SECOND NEAR-MISS: /api/diag/broker_account_status came back fully clean (ACTIVE, trading_blocked false) for both Alpaca accounts. That does NOT clear the brick — it reports AUTHORIZATION (permitted to trade), while the incident is CAPACITY (available_usd 0.00, no room to trade). Do not read one as the other.
items.action:
TAKE THE SOAK, then propose. Sample /api/diag/exposure across a full TRADING week (Mon-Fri, several reads per session incl. US open and close) and record the distribution per account — max, not just mean, since the ceiling has to clear the peak of normal operation. The route is connection-free and token-gated, so sampling costs nothing on the money box.

THE ONE ANALYTIC RESULT THAT DOES NOT NEED THE SOAK, and it is the interesting one: section 6 requires the ceiling to sit BELOW the venue limit AND ABOVE normal operation. For Alpaca those two constraints are INVERTED in this read — measured 2.0238x against a 2.00x Reg-T limit. If a weekday soak reproduces >2.00x as normal operation, then NO ceiling value satisfies section 6 for those accounts, and a ceiling is the wrong instrument: it would mask a sizing problem rather than govern one. Establish whether >2.00x is genuinely normal BEFORE proposing any Alpaca value.

bybit_2 is the only funded real-money account (equity $278.17, multiple 0.9939) and is the one that most warrants a considered ceiling; its per-account value should not be inherited from a fleet default derived mostly from paper books.
items.resolution_criteria: A weekday exposure distribution exists per account; the question 'is >2.00x normal for Alpaca' is answered from measurement; and the operator has either approved a proposed fleet default + per-account overrides or explicitly declined.

updates.note: MATERIALLY ADVANCED — the soak is now accruing on weekdays (exposure_soak.jsonl 148,739 bytes, multi-day). First readings pulled 2026-08-10: bybit_2 (REAL MONEY) exposure_multiple 0.9888 on $279.61 equity / $276.47 gross notional; bybit_portfolio 1.0513 (ABOVE 1x); bybit_1 0.5516; ib_paper 0.4442; alpaca_live / oanda_practice 0.0; breakout_1 and ib_live measured:false with unmeasured_reason equity_unavailable (correctly NOT reported as flat). Every account reads policy_declared:false — no ceiling is declared anywhere. Note real money sitting at ~1.0x gross with no declared ceiling. Still open because the load-bearing statistic is max_multiple over a full observation window and I could not read summary.by_account: `exposure/soak` was missing from the relay allowlist (fixed this run, commit c80a318) so I had to read the raw log tail instead, which gives no denominator.

updates.note:
NOW READABLE via /api/bot/exposure/soak (the relay allowlist fix landed and works). 638 rows, 58 per account across 11 accounts. max_multiple by account: alpaca_paper 2.0258, alpaca_portfolio 2.0156, bybit_1 1.6225, bybit_portfolio 1.0607, bybit_2 (REAL MONEY) 0.9966, ib_paper 0.4477; alpaca_live / oanda_practice / alpaca_options_paper 0.0. ib_live and breakout_1 are measured_n 0 / unmeasured_n 58 — correctly NULL rather than a fabricated 0.0.

BUT THE CEILING STILL CANNOT BE SET, and the envelope says why: venue_sessions is {closed: 561, extended: 77} and **rth: ZERO**. Not one row has been logged during a regular US equity session. The design's own rule (gross-exposure-governance-DESIGN.md) is that a soak which is mostly closed has not observed normal operation — so the two accounts carrying the HIGHEST multiples (both Alpaca, both >2.0x) have been observed only while their venue was shut or thin. Setting a ceiling on this population is precisely the error the design warns against.

items.what_to_check:
The diag surface offers `bot_log` in its documented name allowlist, but the resolved path is absent on the live VM, so the target always returns empty. items.title: exit_head_replay emitted fee-only `net_r` under a full-cost label (the in-process harness default is DELIBERATE, not a bug)
items.detail: The real, narrower defect: scripts/ml/exit_head_replay.py imports the harness and calls run_backtest() directly, so it inherited the fee-only basis while writing a field named `net_r` under a comment promising 'TOTAL round-trip cost (fee+slippage+funding)'. Every CLI harness fills that same emit-trades JSONL schema with net-of-FULL-cost, and scripts/ml/record_harness_trades.py ingests `net_r` while scripts/ml/fit_confidence_calibrators.py labels `won = net_r > 0` -- so a leg on a cheaper basis flips the won/lost label on any trade whose true net is marginally negative. The module's own docstring calls this emit a 'faithful' leg. A SECOND affected output was found late: the JSON payload's `baseline_summary_net_total_r` reads baseline.get('net_total_r'), which an earlier grep for `baseline[` missed -- a grep returning nothing read as proof of absence, the same unasserted-denominator shape this repo tracks elsewhere. MEASURED severity: LATENT, not active. build_calibration_corpus.py builds from a FIXED list of six CLI harnesses (all shelling out, all venue-resolved); exit_head_replay is not among them, so nothing ingests the mislabelled file today. It is still worth fixing because the schema is shared and portfolio_combine --trades accepts a DIRECTORY (globs *.jsonl), so a stray file joins the pool silently. Magnitude on a 4-trade fixture: venue cost 0.118072 R/trade vs fee-only 0.045412 -- 2.6x, moving net_r by -0.0727 R per trade. Zero labels flipped on that fixture (no trade sat in the band); the flip risk is real but was not exercised there.
items.correction: THIS ROW'S ORIGINAL FRAMING WAS WRONG and is corrected here rather than quietly edited. It called the in-process fee-only default a silent trap. items.source: Found while retiring scripts/research/backtest_trend.py for BL-20260808-RESEARCH-TREND-ENGINE-RETIREMENT-BLOCKED-BY-TEST-COUPLING. Measured on main @1099001.
items.title: The repo has TWO OHLCV readers and they disagree on input FORMAT, not just style: scripts/backtest_trend.py::_load_candles silently cannot read the JSONL the IBKR pull writes
items.what_to_check: MEASURED 2026-08-09 on data/backtest_candles.csv (5000 rows) plus a synthetic 5-row JSONL in the IBKR pull's shape ({ts,open,high,low,close,volume}). scripts/candle_io.py::load_candles (lifted verbatim from the retired research trend engine's _load) reads CSV + Parquet + JSONL, accepts `ts` as the timestamp column, and coerces OHLC to numeric. scripts/backtest_trend.py::_load_candles reads CSV + Parquet ONLY, requires the column to be literally `timestamp`, and does not coerce OHLC. On the SAME CSV both produce identical frames (5000 rows, DataFrame.equals True; and identical resamples at 5m/5min/1h/4h). On the JSONL, candle_io returns 5 usable rows while _load_candles raises KeyError: 'timestamp'. WHY IT MATTERS: this is why the three research scripts (regime_matrix, regime_tag_emitted, regime_adx_cutpoint_sweep) were repointed at the lifted candle_io rather than at the engine's own private reader — the naive repoint would have silently dropped JSONL support that regime_matrix and regime_tag_emitted both document reading, converting a working input into a KeyError. NOT a live-path issue: neither reader is on the order path, and no current caller feeds JSONL to _load_candles. It is a latent trap for the next person who assumes 'the engine's loader' is the general one.
items.proposed_fix: Decide ONE reader and make the other delegate. Preferred: scripts/backtest_trend.py::_load_candles becomes a thin call to candle_io.load_candles, which is a strict superset for every input the engine accepts today. That change is deliberately NOT bundled into the retirement PR: _load_candles feeds the fidelity pipeline (regime_debt_matrix, the calibration corpus, the M20 sweeps), and widening its NaN-drop from 'timestamp only' to 'timestamp + OHLC' could move a number on a CSV containing an unparseable price cell — a behaviour change that needs its own before/after over the real corpora, not a footnote in a retirement. Verify by running the debt matrix + one M20 sweep before/after and asserting byte-identical output.
items.resolution: RESOLVED IN THE SAME PR, and the severity was understated when filed. I opened this as a LATENT trap ('no current caller feeds JSONL to _load_candles'). The session-end doc-freshness pass found a REAL one: scripts/research/build_continuous_contract.py writes the canonical market_raw shape as JSONL and its own docstring instructs backtesting that file with a trend harness - and the retired engine was the ONLY trend engine that could read JSONL. So the retirement BROKE a documented end-to-end workflow (roll-adjusted continuous futures -> trend backtest), which is not something to leave filed. FIX: scripts/backtest_trend.py::_load_candles now delegates to candle_io.load_candles, so there is ONE reader. VERIFIED BEFORE THE CHANGE, not assumed: 18 full-summary backtest comparisons (2 committed corpora x 5min/15min/1h x 3 configs incl. the config-exact trend_donchian block) were IDENTICAL, and the loaded frames compared equal via DataFrame.equals; then confirmed end-to-end that a JSONL file now runs through the engine (exit 0, trades=1). The shared reader is a strict superset of what the engine accepted before - it adds JSONL + the IBKR `ts` column and coerces OHLC to numeric. Two stale citations in src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py (comment-only) and the build_continuous_contract example were repointed in the same pass.

items.title: exit-refinement coverage matrix: MULTI-LEG rows carry ONE status, so a row can be 'shipped' while most of its legs failed
items.detail: docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json is M20's done-condition roll-up: one row per 'strategy leg', one status per lever column. But several rows are not one leg -- they bundle a whole family under a single status field, and the status then describes only the leg that PASSED while the ref text carries the rest. Found by a screen for fail-words appearing under a non-negative status: 11 hits, and 10 are this shape (the 11th, trend_donchian BTC trail_decay, was a genuine stale status and is fixed as `shipped_gate_failed`). Concrete examples, all currently `shipped`: (a) row 'sol_pullback_2h / xrp_pullback_2h / ...' trail_decay -- ref says sol PASS wf 5/6 while 'xrp 3/6, ada 3/6, avax 2/6, eth_prop 2/6 all fail', so 4 of 5 legs are honest negatives counted under a shipped cell; (b) row 'MES/MGC/MHG' trail_geometry -- 'MES trail3 4/6 + MHG trail3 5/6 PASS ... MGC fails'; (c) row 'equities 1h fleet' trail_geometry -- 'TLT-1h trail3 PASS; gld/spy/qqq/slv fail'. WHY IT MATTERS: the roll-up is the milestone's done-condition and is quoted as a completion percentage (currently 141/184 cells resolved). A bundled row inflates 'shipped' and hides per-leg negatives, so the number overstates coverage by an amount nobody can compute without re-reading every ref string. It is the same class as the defect just fixed -- a status field that does not describe what the evidence says -- one level up: here the field cannot be correct for all its legs, whatever value it holds. NOT fixed in this PR because it is a schema/normalisation change (explode bundled rows to one row per leg, or add a per-leg sub-status), touches many rows, and the ref text preserves the underlying evidence so nothing is LOST today -- only mis-aggregated.
items.suggested_fix: Explode every bundled row into one row per (strategy, symbol, tf) so the status field has exactly one leg to describe, then re-derive the roll-up. Cheap validation: a guard asserting each row's `strategy` field names exactly one strategy (no '/' and no 'fleet'), which is a one-line structural check that cannot be satisfied by editing prose.
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-08-09. 6 of the 7 multi-leg rows exploded to one row per leg (23 -> 50 rows, 184 -> 400 cells); each exploded row carries `exploded_from`. Per-leg statuses assigned ONLY from each ref's explicit wording; a ref silent on a leg, or naming a run that ERRORED / TIMED OUT, becomes `pending` -- an un-run cell is not a negative however plausible its neighbours (trend_donchian_ada_4h / _avax_4h trail_decay were recorded as negatives 'consistent with the family's fails', which is an inference; both are now pending). The `shadow fleet` row is deliberately NOT exploded: its label does not enumerate its legs and it is execution:shadow, outside the live-leg done-condition. MEASURED CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN CLAIM: it said the roll-up 'overstates coverage'. That is true of `shipped` (9.2% -> 6.0% of cells) but FALSE of resolved overall, which went UP (76.6% -> 79.5%) because most bundled cells were legitimately honest_negative for every leg. The honest live-leg figure is 304/376 = 80.9% over 47 live legs. Also fixed: a DUPLICATE leg -- xauusd_trend_1h existed as both a standalone row (execution:live, trail_geometry:blocked 'candle coverage task #27') and inside the xauusd/mgc bundle (disabled/shadow, trail_geometry:shipped). Settled from config, not by preferring a row: enabled:false => disabled, and trail_mult:4.0 IS declared with the M20 sweep cited inline => shipped. Merged per-cell, keeping the standalone's vol_trail (#6507) and exit_head_ml `blocked` verdicts which the bundle lacked.

items.title: The collapsed-states defect class has no canonical home despite 5+ instances in 2 days across 2 sessions
items.detail: Recurring class: TWO distinct states share one value, and the missing state is the dangerous one. Verified 2026-08-09 that it is described in a sprint log and two design docs but appears NOWHERE in docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md or CLAUDE.md (grepped). Instances, two concurrent sessions, two days: (1) gross-exposure ceiling -- 'no policy' = 'no data' (#8665); (2) netting allowlist -- 'not staged' = 'not observed' (#8666); (3) pairs executor -- 'half_open' = 'flat' (#8667); (4) harness cost basis -- None ('unresolved') = 0.0 ('explicitly fee-only') (#8685); (5) exit-refinement coverage -- 'shipped' conflated live-ness with validated-ness, needing a new `shipped_gate_failed` status (#8687). The counter-example already in the codebase is src/runtime/exit_anchor.py, whose anchored/deferred/no_anchor contract states outright that collapsing any two reintroduces a defect -- the pattern is known and correctly applied in ONE place while being rediscovered incident-by-incident everywhere else. That is the same shape that motivated RULE ONE (four scoped verify rules, no general one): a class with no canonical name gets re-derived instead of checked for.
items.suggested_fix: A short canonical section naming the class, cross-referencing the instances rather than restating them (the RULE ONE shape), with the design test: for any field encoding a condition, ask whether 'we did not look' and 'we looked and found nothing' are distinguishable -- if not, that is the bug. NOT actioned in-session: this session had already restructured the canonical docs once at operator direction, and deciding the doc's shape twice on its own judgment is a step past its remit. Operator call.

updates.note: RESOLVED — operator approved promotion WITH a CI guard. docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md now carries § 'Collapsed states — can this field say "we did not look"?', naming the class, cross-referencing the five instances rather than restating them (the RULE ONE shape), and citing src/runtime/exit_anchor.py as the worked example. Mirrored in CLAUDE.md beside the number-provenance and diagnostic-provenance sections (the same guard family). Enforced by the NEW collapsed-state-guard (scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py, registered in scripts/ci/run_guards.py): per declared contract the producer must emit every state, every state must be branched on by a real consumer, and no consumer may see only one; the override is verified rather than presence-only. Three contracts registered (exit_anchor.bar_close_at, pairs_executor.leg_state, netting_attribution.anchor_status) — clean, and negative-control tested (an injected undeclared state makes it fail). NOT folded in: the sibling BL-20260809-THIRD-CASE-AND-UNTESTED-BRANCH-RULES also proposes 'a green suite over an untested branch is not evidence' — that is a testing rule, still open, still the operator's call; the new section says so explicitly rather than absorbing it silently.

items.source: DERIVED from six instances measured and fixed in one session (2026-08-09): PRs #8665, #8666, #8667 (defects in code), #8678, #8683 (the same defect in this session's own REVIEW), plus #8688. Each is a merged PR with the failing-test evidence recorded in its body and in docs/sprint-logs/S-COLLAPSED-STATES-2026-08-09.md.
items.title: Promote two rules to canonical: the THIRD-CASE rule, and 'a green suite over an untested branch is not evidence'
items.what_to_check:
RULE 1 — THE THIRD CASE. When adding a boolean or a scoping flag to a DECISION path, check whether it can express the third state. Six instances in one day, and in the worst of them the boolean was INDIVIDUALLY CORRECT:

  * `_pair_is_open()` genuinely answers 'is this pair on'. It simply could not carry 'exactly one leg open', so a half-closed pair read as FLAT and the executor opened a second pair on top of a stranded leg (#8667).
  * `gross_exposure()` returned None for BOTH 'no ceiling declared' and 'no data', so the ceiling's own measurement was gated on the ceiling already existing — unpickable for a year (#8665).
  * `NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_ACCOUNTS` intersected the account set at the top of the pass, collapsing 'not staged for writes' into 'not observed', which made real-money bybit_2 invisible to the soak whose whole purpose was to justify including it (#8666).

The recurring shape: a control or predicate that quietly switches OFF the observation that would justify using it. The repo already had the remedy written down — `src/runtime/exit_anchor.py`'s three-way `anchored`/`deferred`/`no_anchor`, whose docstring states outright that collapsing any two reintroduces a defect — but it was never generalised past that one module.

RULE 2 — AN UNTESTED BRANCH IS NOT COVERED BY A GREEN SUITE. #8666's intersection survived its original review because there was NO allowlist test at all; the suite was green over a branch nobody had ever asserted. Every behavioural test written this session was therefore verified to FAIL against the restored old behaviour before being accepted, which caught two real bugs mid-development (an empty-dict payload rendering a confident 'not measured (unknown)', and a truthiness guard admitting partial dicts).

BOTH RULES ALSO APPLY TO THE REVIEWER, which is the part most worth writing down: I verified that no consumer would BREAK on #8665's new key and never that any consumer would DISPLAY it (#8678), and I read a weekend of venue-closed silence as a live brick because quiet-because-shut and quiet-because-refusing are indistinguishable in the trades table (#8683).
items.action: PROPOSE to docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md, alongside the existing 'Always state the population' and 'Green is not evidence' entries — those are the same family and these two extend it from QUANTITIES to STATE MACHINES and to TEST COVERAGE. Operator approves the promotion; do not self-promote a canonical rule.\n\nA guard is NOT proposed for rule 1: 'can this boolean express the third case' is a design judgement, and a presence-only marker would be cheaper to lie to than to satisfy (the new-table-wiring-guard lesson). Rule 2 is partially mechanisable — a coverage delta on changed branches — but that is a separate, evidenced proposal, not a bolt-on here.
items.resolution_criteria: Both rules are either merged into docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md with the incident citations, or explicitly declined with a reason recorded here.

RULE 2 is explicitly NOT: the block quote at :450-455 says 'Still open, deliberately not folded in here … it remains the operator's call; it is not silently absorbed by this section.' — Proposed change, for the operator's yes/no: add to docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md § 'Green is not evidence' — 'A green suite over a branch no test asserts is not evidence about that branch. Any behavioural test written for a new predicate or scoping flag must be verified to FAIL against the restored old behaviour before it is accepted.' The rule is a testing-discipline addition, not a state-modelling one, which is why the collapsed-states section declined to absorb it.
