items.title: docs/api-tier-policy.md calls itself the single source of truth for route tiers and is 60% incomplete, with no CI guard behind it
items.what_to_check:
The file's own header says 'single source of truth for which routes are Tier 1 / 2 / 2.5 / 3', and CLAUDE.md points at it for 'the complete tier inventory'. On the completeness axis that is false: 54 of 90 live routes have no row.

The cause is structural, not neglect. Every sibling inventory that STAYS correct has a CI check behind it — canonical-doc-coherence, provenance-consumer-guard, new-table-wiring-guard, canonical-db-resolver. This one never did, so every route added since S-063 (2026-05-09) could land without a row and none announced itself.

Also corrected in the same pass: the Tier-1 preamble described the VERCEL REWRITE proxying /api/* with CORS as the gate. That stack was retired 2026-05-12 and purged from the repo; today's consumers are Streamlit (server-side), the Svelte SPA (browser-direct), and Android. The TIER was right; the transport rationale was two-and-a-half months stale and read as current.

WORTH NOTING FOR WHOEVER BACKFILLS: the completeness figure was miscounted twice while writing the warning banner (77% -> 69% once the family row was credited -> 60% after this PR's own backfill). A hand-counted completeness claim is stale the moment anyone edits the file, INCLUDING the person writing the claim. That is the argument for the guard rather than for a periodic manual audit.
items.action: Ship a DIFF-SCOPED guard: a new or changed route under src/web/api/routers/ must carry a row in docs/api-tier-policy.md; the existing 54 are grandfathered. Same shape as diagnostic-provenance-guard, so the backlog shrinks instead of growing and no PR is blocked on a pre-existing gap.\n\nThen backfill the 54 as a scoped cleanup. Do NOT bulk-generate the rows: each is a TIER JUDGEMENT about a live surface, and a confidently-wrong tier is worse than a missing one. Until then the banner at the top of the file tells readers to treat it as a partial sample.

items.resolution_note: RESOLVED. Guard shipped FIRST, then the backfill, per the item's own action. (1) GUARD: scripts/check_api_tier_policy.py, registered as `api-tier-policy-guard` in scripts/ci/run_guards.py, with a failure-path self-test in scripts/ci/guard_selftests.py and 24 unit tests in tests/test_check_api_tier_policy.py. Coverage is now 92/92 (100%), computed by `--list`, and a test asserts the number stated in the doc equals a freshly computed one — the previous banner's figure was hand-miscounted twice (77% -> 69% -> 60%). items.title: backtest_ict_scalp._load_yaml_params() ALWAYS loads the ict_scalp_5m block — safe today only because the 8 legs happen to be identical
items.source: scripts/backtest_ict_scalp.py::_load_yaml_params hardcodes load_strategy_config().get('ict_scalp_5m'). Every sweep of every ict_scalp leg (m27 sweep, m20_fleet_exit_sweep scalp branch, M27 run_symbol_p0) therefore runs BTC's detection params regardless of --symbol/--timeframe.
items.what_to_check:
VERIFIED SAFE AS OF 2026-08-09 — I diffed all eight leg blocks in config/strategies.yaml rather than trusting the 'every ict_scalp leg is a config-exact copy' comment: detection geometry is byte-identical across all eight, and exactly four keys differ (off_cells + vol_spec on xrp_5m; stale_exit_bars + stale_exit_below_r on eth_15m), none of which _load_yaml_params feeds. So today the substitution is a no-op.

The RISK is that this safety is a coincidence of config, not a property of the code, and nothing detects the day it stops holding. If any leg's detection params are ever tuned independently, every sweep of that leg silently measures BTC's strategy under that leg's name and reports a confident, wrong verdict into the coverage matrix — with no error and no diagnostic naming the substitution. That is textbook UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class B (implicit input selection), which diagnostic-provenance-guard exists to catch.
items.action: Either (a) resolve params from the leg actually being swept (the harness already takes --symbol/--timeframe, and the m27 sweep now takes --leg, so the leg name is available), or (b) keep the shared load but ASSERT at startup that the requested leg's detection params equal ict_scalp_5m's and fail loudly with the diff when they do not. (b) is cheaper and turns a silent wrong answer into a stop.

items.source: MEASURED INSTANCE (PR #8693, mine): the M20 exit-refinement coverage roll-up published "304/376 = 80.9% across 47 live legs". POPULATION: docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json, 50 rows x 8 lever columns = 400 cells counted. Only 398 existed -- squeeze_breakout_4h and fvg_range_15m were missing the `vol_trail` column outright, not `pending`, ABSENT. The roll-up did r.get(col) per row x column and bucketed the None from a MISSING KEY as if it were a status. Corrected by a concurrent session to 308/376 = 81.9% on a complete denominator; both gaps then filled by AST-checking the harness CLIs (squeeze has --trail-mult but no --trail-vol-above-pctl -> blocked:no_harness_levers; fvg has no --trail-mult at all -> n/a).
items.title: No guard catches a roll-up published over a denominator containing cells that do not exist
items.what_to_check:
WHY THE EXISTING GUARDS DID NOT REACH IT. collapsed-state-guard (scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py, added the same day) polices DECLARED THREE-STATE CONTRACTS IN CODE -- producer emits every state, every state has a real consumer, no consumer sees only one. This defect is in a DATA ARTIFACT: a record missing a declared field, and an aggregate that buckets the absence. Same class ('missing' indistinguishable from 'needs no verdict'), different substrate, so the guard's scope does not reach it. diagnostic-provenance-guard sub-class C is the nearest relative (an empty/zero result read as a clean labelled answer) but it scans scripts/, not tracked JSON artifacts.

WHY PROSE DID NOT CATCH IT. RULE ONE #2 ('a negative result needs a denominator') was canonical and merged HOURS before this shipped, written by the same session that then shipped it. The roll-up's own output printed `None 3` then `None 2` -- the missing cells, on screen, in the author's own status table -- and was read past. A rule its own author breaks the same day is evidence about ENFORCEABILITY, not about the author: the enforcement ledger for this class stands at CI guards 3, in-script assertions 3, another session 1, tooling 1, PROSE 0.

SCOPE QUESTION TO ANSWER FIRST, before building anything: how many tracked JSON artifacts actually declare their own field set? exit-refinement-coverage.json declares `lever_columns`. If it is the only one, a guard is over-engineering and an in-script assertion in the producing tool is the right size. If there are several, the guard is warranted. Count them -- do not assume either way.
items.action:
Validate the ARTIFACT, not the producing script -- so any bad transform is caught regardless of which script or session wrote it. Validating the script would be presence-only and gameable (the new-table-wiring-guard lesson: a guard cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than no guard).

SHAPE: for each tracked JSON artifact that declares its own field set, assert every record carries every declared field. Cheap to satisfy HONESTLY -- you must write a status, and `pending` is the correct default for an un-adjudicated cell -- and expensive to satisfy dishonestly, since there is no way to fill it without stating a verdict. Ship with a self-test that plants a missing field and asserts the guard fails closed, per the scripts/ci/guard_selftests.py pattern, and wire it into run_guards.py.

SECOND, CHEAPER HALF worth doing either way: any roll-up that prints a per-status tally should assert its buckets sum to a denominator it computed independently (rows x declared columns), and should FAIL rather than print when a bucket key is None. That is the specific line that would have stopped this one.
items.resolution_criteria: The count of tracked JSON artifacts declaring their own field set is MEASURED and stated. Then either (a) a guard validating record-completeness against that declaration is wired into run_guards.py with a fails-closed self-test, or (b) the count is 1 and an in-script assertion in the producing tool is shipped instead, with that scoping decision recorded here. In both cases: re-running the M20 coverage roll-up over a deliberately field-stripped copy of exit-refinement-coverage.json exits non-zero.

items.source: Observed while registering `api-tier-policy-guard`, then VERIFIED by running `python3 scripts/ci/run_guards.py --only api-tier-policy-guard --all`, which printed `(skipped: step not relevant to this diff)` for the `when`-gated step while the ungated step ran. Mechanism, in scripts/ci/run_guards.py::main: `changed = [] if args.all else changed_files(...)`. `--all` sets force_all, which bypasses relevance for the GUARD, but the per-STEP check in run_guard() calls `is_relevant(step['when'], changed)` against that same EMPTY `changed` list — so a per-step `when` with globs can never match under `--all`.
items.title: Per-step `when` clauses are silently SKIPPED on push/workflow_dispatch, so guards.yml's 'on push, run EVERYTHING' is nominal rather than real for step-gated guards
items.what_to_check: guards.yml says in a comment that push/workflow_dispatch runs `--all` because there is no PR diff to scope by, and that this is 'stricter than the retired per-workflow push behaviour, never weaker'. For guards whose SCAN lives in a `when`-gated step that is exactly inverted: the guard is selected, its ungated steps run, and its scan is skipped. AFFECTED (grep for a step dict carrying 'when'): `diagnostic-provenance-guard` — its scan step is `{'argv': [...check_diagnostic_provenance.py, '{pr_diff}'], 'when': {'regex': '^scripts/.*\\.py$'}}`, so on a push to main only its self-test runs and the scan does not. Others should be enumerated rather than assumed — I only confirmed the mechanism and the one instance I was sitting next to. NOT a live-trading issue and NOT urgent: the diff-scoped PR path is the one that actually gates merges, and it works. The cost is that the push-time 'run everything' is weaker than the comment claims, which is the sort of thing that reads as coverage when it is not — the same green-that-checked-nothing shape the repo already tracks.
items.proposed_fix: Pick one, deliberately: (a) under force_all, treat a per-step `when` as satisfied rather than evaluating it against an empty list — one line in run_guard(), and it makes the comment true; (b) leave the behaviour and fix the comment in guards.yml so nobody reads push as a full sweep; or (c) leave both and require any guard that wants a real push-time audit to carry an ungated step, which is what `api-tier-policy-guard` does deliberately (see its registry comment). (a) is the smallest change but flips behaviour for every step-gated guard at once, so it wants its own PR and a look at what newly starts running on push — do not fold it into an unrelated change.
items.resolution_note: RESOLVED — but NOT by the fix this item proposed, and the correction is the point. The item offered (a) 'under force_all, treat a per-step `when` as satisfied — one line, and it makes the comment true'. MEASURED before implementing: BOTH step-gated commands in the registry (the only two — `api-tier-policy-guard` and `diagnostic-provenance-guard`) consume `{pr_diff}`, and on push that file is EMPTY. Forcing them to run makes `check_diagnostic_provenance.py` print 'OK - every scanned diagnostic states what it computed' and exit 0 having scanned NOTHING. Option (a) would have made the comment true and the CHECK false — manufacturing exactly the green-that-checked-nothing this repo treats as worse than a red. Substituting the whole-tree equivalent is not a drop-in either: `check_diagnostic_provenance.py --all` exits 1 on 52 pre-existing grandfathered sites (that is WHY it is diff-scoped), so wiring it to push would redden `main` on every merge. SO THE SKIP IS CORRECT AND STAYS. What was actually wrong was that it was INDISTINGUISHABLE from an ordinary not-relevant skip — the reader could not tell 'we asked about this diff and it did not apply' from 'there was no diff to ask about'. SHIPPED: (1) `run_guard()` takes `no_diff_scope`/`unscoped` and names the real reason on the skip line; (2) the run summary prints a 'NOT SCANNED on this event (N)' block listing those steps and stating that a guard needing real push coverage must carry an UNGATED whole-tree step; (3) `guards.yml`'s 'stricter ... never weaker' comment — the actual defect, since it was the claim that made the gap invisible — is corrected in place; (4) `tests/test_run_guards_step_scoping.py` pins the distinction, AND asserts the premise the decision rests on (every step-gated command consumes `{pr_diff}`; the population is exactly those two guards) so a future step that scans the whole tree fails the test rather than silently inheriting reasoning that no longer applies to it. NOTE the affected population was 2, not the 'several' this item guessed at — the guess is corrected here rather than left standing.

items.source: MEASURED on PR #8698. `.github/workflows/guards.yml` declares `concurrency: group: guards-... cancel-in-progress: true`. `pytest-run.yml`, `pytest-collect.yml` and `repo-inventory.yml` declare NO `concurrency:` block at all (verified by grep over each file). Consequence observed directly: marking #8698 ready-for-review re-queued the required checks, and because pytest-run has no group the second run did NOT supersede the first — BOTH ran a full suite to completion on the SAME head 6ded70b: job 93325586744 (00:41:59 -> 00:50:50, 8m51s, success) and job 93325625028 (00:42:19 -> ~00:51:35, ~9m16s, success). guards.yml's own run on that head was correctly CANCELLED by its group (job 93325586606), which is the control showing the fix works.
items.title: pytest-run / pytest-collect / repo-inventory declare no `concurrency:` group, so a re-queue stacks a second full ~9-minute suite instead of superseding the first
items.what_to_check:
This is the same stacking mode BL-20260806-CI-FANOUT-AMPLIFIES-ACTIONS-OUTAGES identified ('because almost none of those workflows declared a concurrency: group, every re-run STACKED instead of superseding the last -- 75 queued runs from ~3 attempts at the same PR'). That PR added the group to guards.yml, which was the workflow it consolidated; the three OTHER required/always-on workflows were not touched and still have no group. So the root cause is only partly fixed, and the part that is fixed is the CHEAP job (guards, ~45s) while the three unfixed ones include the EXPENSIVE one (pytest-run, ~9 min).

TWO COSTS. (1) Runner minutes: every re-queue on a busy PR burns a duplicate ~9-minute suite. (2) Legibility: two runs share one required-check NAME, so 'is pytest-run green?' has two answers at once and branch protection's view is not obvious from the check list.

NOT urgent and NOT a correctness risk -- both duplicate runs passed, and branch protection still gates on the required context. This is waste plus ambiguity, not a hole.
items.proposed_fix:
Add the same group guards.yml already uses to pytest-run.yml, pytest-collect.yml and repo-inventory.yml:
  concurrency:
    group: <name>-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
    cancel-in-progress: true
Keep the event_name in the key for the reason guards.yml documents: grouping push/merge_group by ref alone would cancel a main-branch run and lose the post-merge signal.

CAUTION worth stating: cancel-in-progress on a REQUIRED check means a cancelled run leaves that context non-successful until the superseding run finishes. That is correct (only the newest head's verdict is meaningful) and is already how guards.yml behaves, but verify on one PR before assuming it composes with 'require branches up to date'.

items.title: RETRACTED PREMISE (measured false 2026-08-10): banking CAN pass the M20 gate. Residual open question is narrow — should the PROP sleeve be gated on survival-weighted EV instead of net_R?
items.source:
FILED 2026-08-10 on an a-priori argument: that banking necessarily lowers net_R and lowers maxDD, so no banking cell could ever satisfy beats() (net_R AND maxDD must improve) — 'P(pass) = 0 a priori'.

REFUTED THE SAME DAY by the ict_scalp exit_ladder round (GH Actions run 31344328313, 7 legs x 4 cells = 28 cells, memo section 10.5/10.6):
  * net_R ROSE in 6/28 IS and 8/28 OOS cells. On a fixed 1.5R bracket with a 1.0R rung, banking turns a loser that first printed +1R from -1R into 0.25*(+1)+0.75*(-1) = -0.5R. The argument followed only the WINNER side of the distribution.
  * maxDD ROSE (got WORSE) in 14/28 OOS cells — 12 of the 16 5m cells. Drawdown is a property of the equity PATH; capping the biggest winners removes the recoveries that used to END drawdowns.
  * 2/28 cells (ict_scalp_sol_15m bank0.25@1R, bank0.5@1R) passed the gate outright AND survived the yearly walk-forward 3/4. Counterexample.

This row is kept, not deleted: the wrong claim was written into the memo and into scripts/research/m20_banking_risk_adjusted.py and acted on, so the correction needs a findable home. Both artifacts are now corrected (memo section 11.1 carries a retraction banner; the section 6.2 MEASUREMENTS were never in doubt and stand).
items.what_to_check:
The generalisable lesson, which is NOT about banking: an a-priori argument that a measurement 'must' come out a certain way is a hypothesis, and this one was written into a canonical memo as a structural fact hours before the run that refuted it. RULE ONE covers this explicitly ('verify your own output too, hardest when it confirms what you expected') — the failure was that the claim FELT like a derivation, so it was never queued for measurement.

What survives and is still open: under a PROP ruleset a daily-loss or static-DD breach is TERMINAL, so drawdown there is a survival constraint net_R genuinely does not price. That is a real gate question and is independent of the retracted argument.
items.action:
(a) DONE 2026-08-10: memo section 11.1 retracted in place with the measurement (section 10.6); m20_banking_risk_adjusted.py docstring corrected; coverage matrix records the 7 measured legs.
(b) OPERATOR QUESTION, still open and now the ONLY one: should the prop sleeve be gated on survival-weighted EV rather than net_R? Execute PB-20260712-PROP-BANKING-EV (src/prop/montecarlo.py::run_ev_montecarlo + config/prop_rulesets/breakout.yaml already exist; unused for a month).
(c) SEPARATE Tier-3 decision, do not conflate with (b): the two ict_scalp_sol_15m walk-forward survivors are a PROPOSAL awaiting explicit operator approval. Nothing has been merged into config/strategies.yaml.
items.resolution_criteria: Closed when the operator has ruled on (b) — either the prop sleeve gains a survival-weighted arm, or the memo records that a net_R-first gate is deliberate there too, decided on the prop EV run's evidence. (a) is done; (c) is tracked as its own Tier-3 proposal, not as this row.

items.title: Exit-lever verdicts in the coverage matrix do not state WHICH dataset produced them — and two different datasets are in active use
items.source: MEASURED 2026-08-09/10 on the trainer. /home/ubuntu/m27_data/ETHUSDT_15m.csv = 124,497 rows from 2023-01-01. /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/data/ETHUSDT_15m.csv = 184,443 rows from 2021-03-15. Different md5. Both are 'the ETH 15m data'. ict-scalp-exit-sweep.yml scp's from m27_data; a hand-run on the trainer defaults to data/.
items.what_to_check:
I nearly wrote ladder verdicts measured on data/ into the SAME matrix rows whose stale_stop/giveback_stop cells were measured on m27_data. The rows would have silently mixed two populations, and the coverage matrix is the artifact M20's done-condition is read from.

It also changes the GATE: the yearly walk-forward folds run 2021-2026, so on m27_data (starts 2023) folds 2021/2022 are unusable -> usable=4, need=ceil(2*4/3)=3. On data/ all six are usable -> need=4. The same cell can pass on one and fail on the other with identical trade logic.

This is 'always state the population' applied to a research artifact: a verdict without its dataset is not comparable to the cell beside it.
items.action: Add the dataset identity (path + row count + first/last timestamp, ideally md5) to what a sweep writes into verdicts.json AND to the matrix cell ref, so a cell carries its own population. The sweep already records `data`; the matrix ref does not. Backfill the existing M27 cells with 'measured on m27_data (2023+)'.
items.resolution_criteria: Every exit-lever cell in exit-refinement-coverage.json names the dataset its verdict was measured on, and a reader can tell whether two cells in one row are comparable.

items.title: ict_scalp_avax_5m places NOTHING on bybit_1 — every order is EXCHANGE_REJECTED for exceeding Bybit's AVAXUSDT max_qty
items.source: MEASURED via /api/diag/journal?table=trades 2026-08-10T00:39Z. Trades 4532, 4526, 4524, 4522, 4521 (and the row after) are all status='exchange_rejected', strategy ict_scalp_avax_5m, account bybit_1, identical cause: 'The number of contracts exceeds maximum limit allowed: too large, order_qty:2655280000000 > max_qty:2200000000000 (ErrCode: 10001)'. Sizes 26,552-33,220 AVAX.
items.what_to_check:
POPULATION, stated honestly: 5 rejections were visible in the newest ~12 journal rows the diag response returned BEFORE it truncated (the response hit its comment budget at ~18KB of 577KB). I have NOT counted the full rate or the denominator. What IS established: they span 2026-08-09T01:04Z -> 2026-08-10T00:11Z, i.e. AT LEAST ~23 hours, and every AVAX row I saw in that window is a rejection — I saw no successful ict_scalp_avax_5m open on bybit_1 at all.

This is the STRANDED-CAPABILITY shape the Prime Directive exists for, reached by a different route than an env gate: the strategy is enabled: true / execution: live in config/strategies.yaml and reads as healthy on every status surface, while placing nothing. It is not refusing per-trade for a risk reason (which would be correct and logged as such) — the order reaches Bybit and is bounced.

The sizing is producing a qty above the VENUE's per-order maximum for AVAXUSDT. RiskManager already legalises qty against min_qty / qty_step / whole-unit rules (see BL-20260628-CRYPTO-INSTRUMENT-MIN-FLOOR and the qty-legalization-guard seam) — a per-instrument MAX appears to have no equivalent, so nothing clamps or splits the order before submission.
items.action: (1) Confirm the rate + denominator over the full journal (this session only saw a truncated head). (2) Decide the correct behaviour and put it in the ONE legalisation seam rather than a second bespoke check: clamp to the venue max, split across orders, or refuse with an honest journalled cause. A silent repeat-reject is the worst of the three because it looks like a live strategy. (3) Check whether other high-notional alt legs (XRP at 208k units, SOL) sit near their own venue caps — AVAX may be first, not alone.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. Clamp position_size's returned qty to a per-instrument max_qty resolved from the SAME instrument source that already provides qty_step / min_qty, so the clamp cannot drift from the step resolution.
2. When the clamp BINDS, journal it as an explicit sized-down reason rather than silently shrinking - a silently-clamped order and a correctly-sized one must not be indistinguishable (the collapsed-state rule).
3. When even min_qty exceeds max_qty, refuse the trade with a distinct cause instead of submitting a doomed order; today every one of these costs a live venue round-trip and a journal row.
4. Regression test: an account whose margin-implied qty exceeds a symbol's venue max must size to the venue max, not the margin cap. Confirm it FAILS against current risk.py.
5. Re-measure the rejection rate on ict_scalp_avax_5m/bybit_1 after the fix; the honest success criterion is 0 EXCHANGE_REJECTED for this cause, not 'some orders fill'.

Single-path read of trades @ strategy_name=ict_scalp_avax_5m, limit=40, newest-first (diag #8987; page truncated, `total` fell past the cut). 26 complete rows parsed, ALL on bybit_1, spanning 2026-07-31T11:03Z -> 2026-08-13T01:27Z (13 days, not the ~23 hours originally established):
    exchange_rejected  18
    closed              4   <-- REAL FILLS
    rejected            4   (intent_noop:flip_suppressed_hold_policy — a correct, different cause)

** 'places NOTHING' / 'every order is EXCHANGE_REJECTED' IS DISPROVEN. ** Four orders filled and closed in this very window at 368.4 / 3,217.2 / 3,347.4 / 15,413.9 AVAX. This is NOT the stranded-capability shape the row was filed as; it is a SIZE-DEPENDENT partial failure. That distinction is the whole triage: a dead leg needs re-enabling, an intermittent one needs its threshold found — and the threshold is now known exactly.

THE CAP, DERIVED FROM THE VENUE'S OWN ERROR TEXT (not assumed):
    order_qty:3452630000000 / position_size 34526.3 = scale 1e8
    max_qty:2200000000000 / 1e8 = **22,000 AVAX**

IT SEPARATES THE OUTCOMES PERFECTLY — 22 of 22 sized orders, zero exceptions:
    largest FILLED    15,413.9  <  22,000
    smallest REJECTED 23,090.0  >  22,000
No overlap. Every fill is under the cap and every exchange rejection is over it, so the cap alone explains the entire observed outcome set. Rejected share of SIZED orders: 18/22 = 81.8%.

ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED where the row guessed it. src/units/accounts/risk.py carries a per-account `min_qty` FLOOR and two ECONOMIC ceilings (`max_qty_by_margin`, `max_qty_by_exposure`) — and NO per-instrument VENUE maximum anywhere in config/ or the legalisation seam. The economic ceilings cannot substitute: they scale with equity and were satisfied here (margin_cap was ~65k AVAX on the comparable avax_pullback_2h rows), so a structurally-illegal order passes every existing check.

POPULATION, STATED: the page was truncated and `total` was not returned, so 26 is the NEWEST rows, not the full history. The 81.8% is the rate WITHIN that page — a real rate over a real window, not a lifetime rate. The 22,000 cap and the perfect separation do not depend on the denominator.
updates.next_check: Action (2) only — the diagnosis is complete. Tier-2/3 (order path), so NOT enacted here. Put a per-instrument venue max in the ONE legalisation seam beside min_qty/qty_step (never a second bespoke check), sourced from the venue instrument-info rather than hardcoded — 22,000 is today's AVAXUSDT value, not a constant. Then choose ONE of clamp / split / refuse-with-journalled-cause; the current silent repeat-reject is the worst of the three because the leg reads healthy on every status surface while dropping 4 of 5 orders. Check XRP (~208k units) and SOL against their own caps: AVAX may be first, not alone.

updates.note:
ACTION (2) SHIPPED and ACTION (3) ANSWERED. Operator approved implementing the fix conditional on verifying the XRP/SOL impact; this is that verification.

XRP AND SOL ARE NOT AFFECTED. Enumerating exchange rejections by STATUS rather than by strategy (diag #8990) — the cut that could actually find a second affected leg, which every prior AVAX-scoped read could not — the newest 25 rejections spanning 2026-07-30 -> 08-13 contain exactly two symbols: AVAXUSDT (18, venue max) and BTCUSDT (7, a balance error, filed separately as BL-20260813-ICTSCALP-BTC-BYBIT2-BALANCE-REJECTS). ZERO XRP. ZERO SOL. So the row's suspicion that 'AVAX may be first, not alone' is correct in spirit — there IS a second stranded leg — but it is BTC on real money, and it is a different cause the clamp does not address. Population: page truncated, so this is the newest 25, not all history; XRP/SOL are absent from a ~2-week window, which is not the same as never.

THE CLAMP CANNOT AFFECT THEM REGARDLESS, and this is structural rather than empirical: it is entered only when qty > maxOrderQty, and any such order is bounced by the venue today. Every currently-succeeding order is already below the cap, so the blast radius is exactly the set of currently-FAILING orders. The AVAX evidence bears this out — the four sizes that really filled (368.4 / 3,217.2 / 3,347.4 / 15,413.9) are all under 22,000 and are pinned untouched by test_currently_legal_sizes_are_untouched.

SHIPPED: maxOrderQty was already arriving in the same lotSizeFilter payload precision.py fetches for qtyStep/minOrderQty and was being discarded — the fix is a wider read of an existing response, no new round-trip. Clamp lives in the qty_legalize seam beside the floor. Chose clamp over refuse (restores the capability, matches risk.py's existing ceilings, strictly risk-reducing) and over split (under netting the legs merge anyway, so it only adds a multi-order failure mode at the last gate). 17 tests.
updates.next_check: Confirm on the live VM after deploy: an ict_scalp_avax_5m order above 22,000 should now appear in the journal at 22,000 with the clamp warning in the log, instead of exchange_rejected. That is the observable that closes this row.

items.detail:
RE-VALIDATED 2026-08-14 — the filed headline is REFUTED but the defect is real, and the ROOT CAUSE is now identified (it was not in the original filing).

MEASURED, 8 most-recent ict_scalp_avax_5m rows on bybit_1:
  4640 08-14 REJECTED qty 33997.9 | 4609 08-13 REJECTED 34526.3 | 4608 08-13 REJECTED 34497.3
  4606 08-12 REJECTED 34502.7 | 4570 08-11 **CLOSED, FILLED** qty 368.4, pnl -15.47, BOTH sl_order_id and
  tp_order_id populated | 4534 08-10 REJECTED 32799.6 | 4533 08-10 REJECTED 24357.8 | 4532 08-10 REJECTED 26552.8
So 7 of 8 rejected, 1 filled — 'places NOTHING' is false. The correct statement is an ~87.5% venue-rejection rate on this leg, which is still severe.

ROOT CAUSE — THE MARGIN PRE-FLIGHT CAP IS NOT CLAMPED TO THE VENUE'S max_qty:
  Trade 4640's notes carry the sizing basis verbatim:
    margin_basis = {kind: venue_available, basis_usd: 81229.86, leverage: 3, buffer: 0.9,
                    max_qty_by_margin: 33997.92498997939}
  and the order was submitted at EXACTLY that figure, 33997.9. Bybit refused:
    order_qty:3399790000000 > max_qty:2200000000000 (ErrCode 10001)
  Bybit scales these by 1e8 (3399790000000 / 33997.9 = 1.0e8 exactly), so the venue ceiling for AVAXUSDT is
  22,000 AVAX and the sizer asked for 33,997.9 — 1.55x over.
  src/units/accounts/risk.py::position_size resolves a per-instrument qty_step and min_qty (lines ~995-1018) and caps by margin (max_qty_by_margin, ~911-932), but there is NO max_qty clamp anywhere in the file. The margin cap is therefore free to exceed the venue's maximum order size, and nothing catches it before submit.
  This also explains why exactly one order filled: 4570 was RISK-sized (tighter stop -> qty 368.4), so it never reached the margin cap and landed well under the venue ceiling. The rejections are precisely the orders where the margin cap BOUND.

SCOPE — NOT AVAX-SPECIFIC AND NOT PAPER-SPECIFIC. bybit_1 is paper, but position_size is the single sanctioned sizing path for every account including real money. Any symbol whose venue max_qty is below available x leverage x buffer / price will hit this; AVAX surfaces it first only because its unit price (~$6.45) makes the margin-implied qty large. A high-equity real-money account on a low-priced instrument is the same shape.

items.title: 24 of 25 live positions have NO time/stall exit lever: nothing in the system can decide a trade has peaked or stopped being worth holding
items.source:
OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-08-10: 'we have a 12 day eth trade that's going nowhere and no mechanism that knows how to decide when the trade has peaked, or that it's clearly not worth holding anymore ... we could be missing winning trades on other strategies because we're just sitting on a trade that goes nowhere.'

MEASURED live 2026-08-10 01:40Z (relay #8713), population = ALL 32 open positions across every account; 25 have a timeframe resolvable from config/strategies.yaml (the other 7 are pairs-sleeve legs, see the sibling row). Hold time normalised to each strategy's OWN bars, which is the honest unit: 12 days on a 1d strategy is 12 bars, on a 2h strategy it is 149.

  * eth_pullback_2h / bybit_2 (REAL MONEY): 12.4 days = 149 bars on a 2h strategy, -0.33R. Its paper mirror bybit_portfolio: -$327.80 (-0.24R). This is the operator's example, confirmed.
  * 5 of 25 positions are held past 100 of their own bars, and ALL 5 have NO time/stall lever declared.
  * ict_scalp_mgc_15m / ib_paper: 289 bars on a 15m SCALP (3.0 days).
  * Exactly ONE of the 25 (uso_trend_1h) declares any time/stall lever (giveback_r + giveback_min_mfe_r). 24 of 25 declare NONE — their only exit machinery is a chandelier trail frozen at the entry bar's ATR, plus the 50R sentinel TP. Neither can end a trade for being OLD or STALLED.

This is the SAME defect the M20 memo section 2 already quantified over 90d (mean MFE +1.92R vs realised -0.16R; giveback 2.08R; 26% of real-money trades touched >= +1R and still closed negative) and named 'the chop-hold problem'. What is new is that it is measurable in the LIVE book right now, and that the CONFIG shows why: the lever does not exist on 24 of 25 legs.
items.what_to_check:
THE NAIVE FIX IS WRONG AND THE DATA SAYS SO. xrp_pullback_2h is 139 bars old on the same timeframe as the ETH trade and is +3.94R (+$2,523 on the portfolio mirror). A flat bar-count timeout would have killed it. tlt_pullback_1d is 11.5 days / 12 bars at +12.00R. So the lever MUST be conditional — old AND not working — never a flat max age. That is exactly the shape the M20 harnesses already implement as stale_exit_bars + stale_exit_below_r (exit at N bars only if open R is below a floor) and giveback_r/giveback_min_mfe_r (exit after MFE >= X gives back Y).

THE MEASUREMENT AXIS ALREADY EXISTS AND NO GATE READS IT. scripts/backtest_ict_scalp.py::_summarize now emits net_r_per_position_day and net_r_per_capital_day (added 2026-08-10, the exit-refinement skill's declared-but-never-implemented tiebreak). The shipping gate is still net_R + maxDD only, so a trade that eventually reaches TP after 149 bars scores identically to one that reached it in 10. The operator's point is precisely that these are not the same trade: the capital was unavailable to every other strategy for 12 days. Opportunity cost is not priced anywhere in the gate.

NOT A NEW LEVER — a DEPLOYMENT gap. stale_exit_bars/giveback are implemented in every research harness and shipped live on exactly TWO legs (ict_scalp_eth_15m stale_exit_bars 12; uso_trend_1h giveback). mgc_pullback_1d/mhg_pullback_1d carry timeout_bars 200. The M20 memo section 4 swept stale-stop fleet-wide and passed it only on trend_donchian_sol + trend_donchian_eth; the pullback family FAILED that gate — but it failed a net_R-first gate, which is the criterion the operator is now questioning.
items.action:
OPERATOR APPROVED 2026-08-10: capital efficiency is now a SHIPPING criterion, not a tiebreak. Landed in .claude/skills/exit-refinement/SKILL.md P2 as a SECOND QUALIFYING PATH (Path B: net_r_per_capital_day improves in both IS and OOS AND maxDD does not worsen AND net_R falls no more than a declared floor), which must still pass the SAME yearly walk-forward. Path A (net_R AND maxDD) is unchanged. A second door, never a lower bar.

STILL OPEN, and deliberately NOT invented:
  (a) Path B's two thresholds ('improves materially', the net_R floor) are UNSET. No sweep has reported the net_r_per_capital_day distribution yet, and a threshold with no distribution behind it is the exposure-ceiling mistake. Until the operator sets them from data, Path B SURFACES candidates for review rather than shipping them.
  (b) RUN THE SWEEP: the pullback family across stale_exit_bars / stale_exit_below_r / giveback_r cells, config-exact, IS/OOS split 2025-07-01 + yearly walk-forward, with net_r_per_capital_day reported beside net_R and maxDD. The harness is READY — backtest_pullback.py already had every lever and now emits the capital block via scripts/capital_efficiency.py. Route to free GH runners (the ict-scalp-exit-sweep.yml pattern), not the 1-core trainer.
  (c) Any resulting per-leg value is a Tier-3 config change and should ride the exit_lever_soak ANNOTATE trail first.
items.resolution_criteria: Closed when either (i) the pullback family has per-leg stale/giveback values shipped on operator-approved evidence that reads capital efficiency, or (ii) the memo records, on a capital-efficiency-aware sweep, that holding through chop is genuinely the better policy for these legs. 'It failed the net_R gate' is NOT sufficient to close this row - that is the criterion under question.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: This is a DEPLOYMENT gap, not a missing lever: stale_exit_bars / stale_exit_below_r and giveback_r / giveback_min_mfe_r are implemented in the harnesses (scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py's lever cells) and shipped on only two legs. The coverage matrix confirms the fleet position — stale_stop is honest_negative on 43 of 47 live legs and shipped on 3; giveback_stop is honest_negative on 44 and shipped on 1. Those honest_negatives were measured against a net_R-and-maxDD gate, which is exactly the criterion the operator is questioning. — Proposed operator decision, in two parts. (1) GATE: adopt net_r_per_capital_day (already computed, already read by the Path B branch at m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:1403, thresholds unset) as a shipping criterion alongside net_R + maxDD, so a trade that reaches TP after 149 bars stops scoring identically to one that reaches it in 10. (2) LEVERS: with that gate, re-sweep stale_stop / giveback_stop fleet-wide and ship where they pass. Do NOT ship a flat max-hold — the row's own data refutes it (xrp_pullback_2h at 139 bars is +3.94R; tlt_pullback_1d at 12 bars/11.5 days is +12.00R), so the lever must be conditional on old AND not working. Tier-3 (strategy params); the sweep itself is Tier-1 and can run first as evidence.

CORROBORATED LIVE THIS REVIEW and it is the same finding as BL-20260821-SCALPS-HELD-10-TO-100X-THEIR-DESIGN-HORIZON: window holds include tlt_pullback_1d 721.2 h, iwm_trend_long_1d 554.0 h, qqq_pullback_1h 193.7 h, and ict_scalp_mgc_15m 47.8 h on a 15-MINUTE leg. 15 positions are open now. Only 8.3% of the window's closes came from a declared bracket. The absent time/stall lever is the single highest-leverage exit gap in this backlog.

items.title: pairs sleeve has opened 29 pairs and CLOSED ZERO: 38.8% of every decision is skip_state_unreadable, so max_hold_bars 20 has never once been evaluated on an open pair
items.source:
MEASURED live 2026-08-10 01:40Z (relay #8713) against config/pairs.yaml read the same session.

config/pairs.yaml::pairs_bnb_btc declares timeframe 1h, max_hold_bars: 20 (= 20 hours), execution: live, account bybit_1.

Live open BNBUSDT legs on bybit_1, all strategy pairs_bnb_btc_a, all sell, all at -0.06R:
  24.8 days = ~595 bars  -$33.38
  23.8 days = ~571 bars  -$89.24
  20.3 days = ~487 bars  -$97.50
  17.7 days = ~425 bars  -$61.48
  12.5 days = ~300 bars  -$162.28
plus one pairs_bnb_btc_b BTCUSDT leg at 5.4 days (-$20.44).

That is 15x to 30x over the pair's OWN declared limit, and -$443.88 of unrealised loss sitting in a sleeve whose entire thesis is mean reversion within 20 bars.

TWO things are wrong and they may share a cause. (1) The time exit is not firing. (2) There are FIVE journal rows on one netted BNBUSDT position for a pair that should hold ONE.

NOT YET CONFIRMED - the mechanism is a hypothesis, relay #8714 was opened to check it against runtime_logs/pairs_soak.jsonl and is not back yet. The hypothesis: _reconstruct_open_state() returns None when the durable order_packages.meta bookkeeping cannot be read, and the caller then SKIPS the pair for that tick (soak event skip_state_unreadable). A skip is correct for a transient read failure and is NOT correct 595 bars later - nothing escalates, so max_hold_bars is never evaluated at all. That is the collapsed-state class this repo made canonical on 2026-08-09: 'we could not read the state' is being handled as 'do nothing', indefinitely and silently.

MECHANISM CONFIRMED 2026-08-10 (relay #8714, /api/bot/pairs/soak). Population: ALL 2,471 soak rows ever written. by_event sums to exactly 2471, so the breakdown is EXHAUSTIVE, not a truncated tail — checked by arithmetic before drawing the conclusion:
    skip_flat              1237
    skip_state_unreadable   958   (38.8% of every decision)
    skip_concurrency         228
    open                     29
    open_failed              10
    shadow_open               9
                          -----
                           2471

**29 opens. ZERO closes.** `close`, `hold`, `half_open`, `shadow_close` and `skip_size` have NEVER been emitted, not once in 2,471 decisions. The executor has never reached its own close branch, which is why legs sit at 300-595 bars against a declared 20-bar limit: whenever a pair IS open, _reconstruct_open_state() fails, the tick skips, and max_hold_bars is never evaluated at all. The limit is not being violated — it is never being READ.

This is the collapsed-state class made canonical 2026-08-09, in its purest form: 'we could not read the state' is handled as 'do nothing', indefinitely, with no ceiling and no escalation. It is ALSO the alarm-fatigue P1 from CLAUDE.md — the signal fired 958 times into a soak log and nothing ever acted on it, which is exactly the failure mode that rule exists to kill. The half_open cleanup shipped 2026-08-09 cannot be helping here: half_open has never been emitted either.
items.what_to_check:
Read runtime_logs/pairs_soak.jsonl (relay #8714 or /api/bot/pairs/soak?pair=BNBUSDT/BTCUSDT) and count events by kind. A long run of skip_state_unreadable confirms the hypothesis; a run of hold means the state IS readable and the max-hold predicate itself is wrong. The two need different fixes, so do not conflate them.

The 5-rows-on-one-netted-position half is the documented pairs divergence shape (BL-20260808-PAIRS-DIVERGENCE-UNOWNED, half_open cleanup added 2026-08-09) plus netting row divergence (BL-20260801-NETTING-PARTIAL-CLOSE-ROWS-NEVER-REDUCED). Check whether the half_open fix is actually running on this pair before assuming it covers this.

Blast radius today is bounded: bybit_1 is the demo/paper account, so no real money. It is filed HIGH anyway because the same executor is what a real-money pairs sleeve would run, and because a declared limit that silently does not apply is worse than no limit - it reads as governed.
items.action:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED IN CODE 2026-08-10 (PR #8712). Proven, not inferred: building the table from the REAL DDL in src/units/db/database.py and running _open_pkg_meta's exact query raises 'OperationalError: no such column: account_id'. `order_packages` has NEITHER `account_id` NOR `id` (PK is the TEXT order_package_id, which is not a rowid alias), so the query named TWO nonexistent columns and could never have returned a row.

Fix, three parts:
  1. The query drops the impossible predicates and orders by created_at/rowid. account_id is deliberately NOT re-added as SQL — the sleeve is single-account by config and leg strategy names are unique per pair, and the docstring says so, so nobody restores it on the assumption the column exists.
  2. The read is now THREE-STATE (found/absent/error) and registered with collapsed-state-guard as pairs_executor.open_state_read. Collapsing 'we could not look' into 'nothing there' is what hid this.
  3. A persistent unreadable state ALERTS (pairs_state_unreadable, CRITICAL) instead of skipping silently, rate-limited once per hour per (pair, reason) — the condition fires every tick and a per-tick alarm is itself the desensitized-alarm P1.

WHY IT SURVIVED TESTING: the existing tests declared their OWN order_packages as (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, strategy_name, account_id, meta) — a schema production does not have — so they were green against a fictional table. They now lift the DDL from the module that owns it, plus a test pinning that account_id/id do NOT exist. Negative-controlled: reverting the query makes 4 tests fail with the production error.

REMAINING (not done here):
  (a) DEPLOY + verify on the live VM: the proof this is fixed is a NON-ZERO `close` count in /api/bot/pairs/soak. Until then it is fixed in code only.
  (b) The 6 stranded legs (-$443.88 unrealised, bybit_1/paper) still need flattening — Tier-2, operator OK, and only AFTER (a) or they re-accumulate.
items.resolution_criteria: Closed when the LIVE pairs soak shows a non-zero `close` count and skip_state_unreadable is no longer dominant. Code-fixed + tests green is NOT closure — that is exactly the 'green is not evidence' shape this bug already exhibited once.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The root cause is fixed in code with positive evidence: src/units/strategies/pairs_executor.py:358-413 `_open_pkg_meta` now returns a THREE-STATE (found/absent/error) tuple, its docstring names this row and states the exact defect (a SELECT on `account_id` and `id`, two columns order_packages does not have, raising OperationalError into a broad DEBUG-level except so every open pair read unreadable), the query no longer uses account_id as a SQL predicate, and `_reconstruct_open_state` (:416-428) propagates the three states with an ALERT on a persistent `error`. CLAUDE.md's /api/bot/pairs/soak row records the same fix plus the test correction (the old tests declared a fictional `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account_id TEXT` schema and now lift the DDL from src/units/db/database.py). — HONEST CAVEAT: I verified the code fix, not the live outcome. Confirming enforcement needs /api/bot/pairs/soak summary.by_event showing close > 0 and skip_state_unreadable collapsed — I did not perform that read this session.

items.source: Third recurrence of the same behaviour, observed first-hand this session. docs/claude/session-board.json's schema says of merge_slot: 'At most ONE session holds this at a time. Mirror the claim here before merge, clear after.' I held the authoritative live slot on PR #8698 from 00:47Z to 01:17Z and never wrote the mirror; it read held_by:null the entire time. On the NEXT merge (#8711) I did not write it either — that time deliberately, and the reason is the finding.
items.title: The merge_slot durable mirror is structurally unwritable for a claim on the PR that carries it, so 'remember to mirror it' cannot be the fix
items.what_to_check:
merge_slot lives in a COMMITTED file. For the common case — a session claiming the slot in order to merge a PR — writing the mirror means committing to that PR's branch, which (a) restarts the full CI cycle (~9 min here) and (b) still reaches no other session until the PR merges, at which point the claim is already over. So at the exact moment the mirror would be useful it cannot be written usefully.

That is why BL-20260720-MERGE-PROTOCOL-LAPSE ('sessions treated this JSON as the claim, it went untouched under load') and BL-20260726-MERGE-PROTOCOL-LAPSE-RECURRENCE both closed as resolved and the behaviour recurred anyway. Both remedies were exhortations. The schema itself already concedes the live board comment on #6927 is authoritative and the JSON is a 'best-effort DURABLE MIRROR' — but the mirror's ONE job (surviving a session that dies mid-merge, where the comment stays up and nobody knows the holder is gone) is exactly the case the current placement cannot serve.

NOT urgent: the authoritative live claim works when sessions read it, and branch protection is the real safety net. This is about the durable half being unreachable, not about merges being unsafe.
items.proposed_fix:
Pick one deliberately; do NOT re-file an exhortation:
(a) Move the durable slot OFF the merge-gated path — e.g. a dedicated pinned GitHub issue whose body is the slot state, or a label on the PR. Both are writable instantly by any session and readable by all, which is the property the JSON lacks.
(b) Accept the board comment as the ONLY claim and DELETE merge_slot from the schema, so nothing implies a durable record exists. A field everyone is told to write and nobody can usefully write is worse than no field.
(c) Keep it, but scope it explicitly to non-PR claims (VM lane, live-VM actions) where the writer is not the thing being merged.
Whichever is chosen, close the two prior lapse items by pointing at it rather than leaving them 'resolved' against a behaviour that keeps happening.

updates.note: Triaged in the system-review 2026-08-10 (RPT since-last, window from 2026-08-07T14:55Z) full-backlog pass.
