items.title: Trader tick overruns its 60s interval — was 251s (4.2x), now 106s (1.8x) after the connector-memo fix; residual is ~50 per-tick candle fetches
items.source: /api/diag/tick_cost, pulled 2026-08-10T04:39Z during /system-review.
items.what_to_check:
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-11T14:23:18Z (issue #8771), and it has NOT come down to a safe level.
  mean_ms 114311.2 / max_ms 128032.9 / last_ms 111868.7 over ticks_measured 3, process_started_utc 2026-08-11T14:15:35Z (uptime 555s, git_sha 2a289ddc).
Against the 60s TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS that is 1.91x on the mean and 2.13x on the max - i.e. every tick overruns its interval, and the trader is continuously behind.

STATE THE POPULATION: ticks_measured is 3 on a FRESHLY RESTARTED process, so the per-process caches (connector memo, candle TTL cache, regime fetch gates) were cold for at least the first tick. A 3-tick mean is not the claim a 3000-tick mean would be, and it biases HIGH. But the prior post-fix reading was 106s over a warmer process, so ~114s is not obviously an improvement on it either - the honest read is 'flat, still ~2x over, and never yet measured on a long-running process'.

WHERE THE TIME GOES (per-hook split, first time this is legible):
  run_one_tick    68108.4ms mean (the 52-strategy evaluation) - still the dominant cost
  order_monitor   44247.9ms mean, of which:
      strategy_monitor_loop                 19636.5
      reconcile_open_trades                  5131.2
      check_broker_naked_equity_positions    4657.8
      reconcile_orphan_exchange_positions    3704.6
      check_broker_naked_ib_positions        3701.0 (max 6649.6)
      check_broker_naked_bybit_positions     2632.6
      watchdog_stuck_strategies              2316.6
      reconcile_netting_partial_closes       2032.9
  unattributed    1954.9ms (1.7%) - see the caveat below

READ attributed_pct WITH CARE: it reports 136.8%, because hooks_attributed_mean_ms sums parents AND their children. Filed separately as BL-20260811-TICKCOST-ATTRIBUTED-PCT-DOUBLE-COUNTS-NESTED-HOOKS. The 1.7% unattributed figure above is computed from the TOP-LEVEL hooks only, not from that field.
items.why_critical: This is the precise failure MODE of the 2026-06-09/06-10 cascade — a tick that grows un-observed until it exceeds the interval, at which point the heartbeat starves and the liveness watchdog restarts a trader that is not actually dead. It also very likely explains the open BL-20260807-HEARTBEAT-PAUSED-WHILE-TICKING ('status reads paused while the trader is actively ticking — heartbeat starves during a long tick'), which was filed 3 days before the instrument existed to measure the cause. Those two items should be read together.
items.next_action: Reducing this needs a target, and the two halves are independent: (a) `run_one_tick` 56s — the signal-builder pass over ~52 strategies; the candle cache already cut it, the residual is per-builder compute + the remaining uncached fetches. (b) `order_monitor` 49s — half is strategy_monitor_loop, half is seven sweeps that each look cheap. Neither is diagnosable further from THIS table: the split says WHERE, not WHY. Next probe should time inside the two dominant children (per-strategy in the monitor loop, per-builder in run_one_tick) before any optimisation is proposed. DO NOT close this row on the halving alone — the resolution criteria require the dominant term to be justified or reduced, and 107s vs a 60s bar is neither.
items.resolution_criteria: A per-hook cost attribution exists and the dominant term is either justified or reduced; tick max_ms tracked across reviews rather than sampled once.
items.root_cause_attributed_2026_08_10:
ATTRIBUTED from journalctl ict-trader-live.service (60 lines, 2026-08-10T04:42:36-04:43:06Z). The 251s is NOT the best-effort hook chain — it is the STRATEGY BUILDER LOOP, run serially, one market-data fetch per strategy.

Measured inter-builder deltas from consecutive log lines: trend_donchian_eth_4h 04:42:36 -> eth_pullback_2h 04:42:38 (2s) -> eth_pullback_prop_2h 04:42:41 (3s) -> ict_scalp_sol_5m 04:42:49 (4s, after the regime-bar budget) -> ict_scalp_sol_15m 04:42:53 (4s) -> trend_donchian_sol 04:42:56 (3s) -> trend_donchian_sol_prop 04:43:00 (4s) -> trend_donchian_sol_4h 04:43:02 (2s) -> sol_pullback_2h 04:43:06 (4s). Mean ~3.2s per strategy over 9 consecutive builders.

ARITHMETIC (the cross-check, not a re-read): /api/diag/status lists 52 configured strategies. 52 x 3.2s = 166s of pure builder time, against a measured mean tick of 251s. That accounts for roughly two thirds of the tick on its own, and the remainder is the hooks + regime scoring + pipeline overhead. The magnitude is explained; no unexplained residual.

THE MECHANISM is visible in the log: `Bybit market data environment: mainnet` is emitted IMMEDIATELY BEFORE EVERY SINGLE BUILDER — a fresh connector construction + candle fetch per strategy, with no reuse across strategies that share a (symbol, timeframe). The SOL block above is the proof: ict_scalp_sol_5m, ict_scalp_sol_15m, trend_donchian_sol, trend_donchian_sol_prop, trend_donchian_sol_4h and sol_pullback_2h are SIX strategies on ONE symbol, each paying its own ~3s round trip. Same pattern for the ETH block. Note this is exactly the grouping optimisation regime_bar_scoring already applies to itself ('one fetch per (symbol, timeframe) group, not per head' -- the MB-20260609-001 fix) and which the strategy builder loop never received.

SECOND, CHEAPER SMELL: `Database tables created/verified` also prints once per strategy per tick -- the lazy DDL check is running ~52x/tick instead of once per process.

PROPOSED FIX (Tier-2, touches the live trader's hot loop, so operator-gated): hoist a per-tick (symbol, timeframe) -> candles cache in front of the builder loop, mirroring the predictor grouping regime_bar_scoring already does. Expected reduction is large -- 52 fetches collapse to roughly the number of distinct (symbol, timeframe) pairs. Do NOT add a tick budget instead: a cap over an unattributed 251s hides the cost rather than removing it, and tick_cost is deliberately measurement-only.

updates.note: OPERATOR APPROVED + WIRED 2026-08-10 (commit 4ba2faa). The root cause was NOT the (symbol,timeframe) duplication I first proposed — measured, that dedup is only 55 -> 48 pairs (~13%). The dominant cost is that every builder constructs a FRESH ccxt client, and ccxt lazily downloads the full market catalogue on that client's first fetch_ohlcv. Fixed by memoizing the connector per credential identity (load_markets once per process, not once per strategy per tick), plus a TTL-bounded candle cache as the second-order win. IB excluded from the connector memo (live socket / clientId collision). Resampling higher TFs from the smallest TF was considered and deferred with reasons recorded in the commit.
updates.next_check: LIVE VERIFICATION REQUIRED and NOT yet done: after deploy, re-read /api/diag/tick_cost and confirm max_ms/mean_ms fall from 251s/296s. Read max_ms beside ticks_measured — a max over 3 ticks is not the claim a max over 300 is, and the counters reset on restart, so wait for a meaningful ticks_measured before declaring a win.

updates.note:
DEPLOYED + FIRST READING (n=1, NOT a verdict). Deploy #8737 rolled the live VM f91e32b6 -> 116ebd97 (/api/diag/version confirms 116ebd97); ict-trader-live restarted 07:15:46Z.

First post-restart tick_cost @07:18:01Z: ticks_measured 1, last_ms/max_ms/mean_ms all 128432.6, process_started_utc 07:15:53Z. So the first tick ran 128.4s against a pre-fix mean of 251.1s / max 295.6s over 10 ticks — roughly HALF.

WHY THIS IS NOT YET THE ANSWER, stated so nobody quotes it as one:
  (a) n=1; the counters are per-PROCESS and reset on this very restart.
  (b) The first tick after a restart is the COLD-START tick — connector memo and candle cache both EMPTY, so it pays every client construction and every fetch exactly once. It is the WORST case for this fix, not the steady state. Later ticks should drop below it; if they do NOT, the memo is not surviving between ticks and that is itself a finding.
  (c) 128s still implies a large residual, consistent with ~50 candle FETCHES still happening (the (symbol,timeframe) cache only dedupes 55 -> 48). That residual is what the deferred resampling option targets.
updates.next_check: Re-read /api/diag/tick_cost once ticks_measured is well into double digits; judge on mean_ms (steady state), not max_ms (which retains the cold-start tick).

updates.note:
VERIFIED (n=3) — the fix WORKS and is a large win, but does NOT resolve the condition. Both halves stated.

tick_cost @07:23:33Z, process_started 07:15:53Z, ticks_measured 3, mean_ms 113483.7, max_ms 128432.6, last_ms 107605.6. Decomposed rather than eyeballed: tick1 128.4s (COLD — both caches empty), tick2 104.4s, tick3 107.6s -> WARM MEAN 106.0s. Against a pre-fix mean of 251.1s that is a 58% reduction (2.4x). The connector memo is confirmed SURVIVING between ticks — warm ticks sit ~22s below the cold tick, which would not happen if it were rebuilt each tick.

TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 60s, CONFIRMED independently rather than assumed: tick1 ended 07:18:01Z, tick3 ended 07:23:33Z = 332s covering 2 warm ticks (212.0s) + 2 sleeps => 60.0s each. Closes out `correction_2026_08_10_headroom`: 15 min was wrong, 60s is right.

THEREFORE STAYS OPEN: 106s against a 60s interval is STILL A 1.8x OVERRUN. The fix took it from ~4.2x to ~1.8x; the trader remains continuously busy with no idle. Closing this because the number halved would be an improvement mistaken for a fix — the condition the item describes is still true.

REMAINING COST is the ~50 candle FETCHES per tick, which the (symbol,timeframe) cache barely dedupes (55 -> 48). That promotes the DEFERRED resampling option from nice-to-have to the actual remaining lever; scope it to crypto with a ratio bound (hazards recorded in PR #8733's merge commit).
updates.next_check: Decide: (a) crypto-scoped resampling with a ratio bound — the real fix; (b) raise TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS above the real tick cost — a Tier-2 one-liner and the cheap immediate relief; or both.

updates.note:
BRANCH (a) CONFIRMED on the first WARM read of the fetch probe. POPULATION: ticks_measured 50, ONE process from 2026-08-12 19:56:48 UTC, payload 2026-08-12 21:55:42 UTC (diag #8811) — ~2h, not the 3-tick cold read the prior update carried.

TICK: mean_ms 83868.0 / max_ms 187186.2 / last 81971.3. THE 107.9 -> 83.9 DROP IS NOT AN IMPROVEMENT: the M20 exit-loop decouple moved monitor.strategy_monitor_loop into the new offloop_hooks block (n=238, mean 11602.6ms), so the work went CONCURRENT, not away. Reading the tick mean alone would have scored a decouple as an optimisation.

FETCH SPLIT on-loop (n / mean_ms / pct_of_total): 1d 160/3633.8/13.9 · 15m 341/1386.7/11.3 · 1h 446/570.1/6.1 · 5m 473/516.9/5.8 · 4h 265/220.4/1.4 · 2h 219/214.5/1.1 · 1m 50/226.3/0.3 · cache_hit 548 (n only). Misses at >= 15m are 1431 of 1954 = 73.2% by COUNT and 84.7% by TIME — that is branch (a). Total on-loop fetch 33.4s per tick = 39.8% of the tick; the pct_of_total column sums to 39.9%, so the arithmetic reconciles. Worst single line: fetch.1d, 762 fetches (160 on-loop + 602 off-loop) of DAILY bars in 2 hours at 2.4-3.6s each.

BRANCH (c) INDEPENDENTLY RULED OUT by status-check #8813 in the same window: loadavg 0.24 on 2 cores, trader at 21.2% CPU, while a tick takes 83.9s. The tick is I/O-WAIT, not compute, so signal_build is not compute-bound.

BUT THE FIX IS NOT THE ONE-LINER THE BRANCH ASSUMED. Strategies read candles_df['close'].iloc[-1] as the CURRENT PRICE for entry geometry (_base.py:145, trend_donchian.py:831, turtle_soup.py:476, vwap.py:1039, ict_scalp.py:773) and the monitor reads the same field for exits, so the cache TTL bounds how stale the price behind a LIVE ORDER may be. Raising the cap is therefore an order-path (Tier-3) decision, not the Tier-2 knob-turn the branch was written as. PR #8815 ships the split: CANDLE_CACHE_TTL_MAX_S becomes settable at the incumbent 60.0 (behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged, one env flip to move, no redeploy), plus a fetchby.<consumer> cut so the question that decides whether a SAFE fix exists — are the >= 15m misses regime_bar_scoring (observe-only, dedups to closed bars, could take a long TTL with zero order consequence) or signal_build (feeds entry geometry) — becomes answerable. The VALUE is with the operator, with the numbers above.

THE fetchby CUT DEPLOYED AND ANSWERED IT — and the answer removes the safe option. POPULATION: ticks_measured 19, one process from 2026-08-13T06:21:38Z (the PR #8815 deploy restart), payload 07:01:35Z. Small n, stated because it is: the shares below are stable against the pre-deploy readings but the tick TIMINGS (69.3s mean / 96.8s max) are 19 ticks and must not be quoted as the distribution — the 187.2s peak belongs to the prior process.

ON-LOOP CONSUMER SPLIT (pct_of_total): fetchby.signal_build 27.3 · fetchby.regime_bar_scoring 6.4 · fetchby.unattributed 0.9. As a share of the 34.6% of tick that is fetch: signal_build 78.9%, regime 18.5%, unattributed 2.6%.

THE TWO CUTS RECONCILE EXACTLY — fetch.* sums to 34.6% and fetchby.* sums to 34.6%, delta 0.0pp. Two independently-recorded families landing on the identical total is the strongest available check that the instrumentation is measuring what it claims; it was not assumed, it was computed.

WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE FIX. The consumer cut was added to test whether a SAFE consumer-scoped TTL exists — regime_bar_scoring is observe-only and dedups to closed bars, so a long TTL there has no order consequence. It does not exist at a useful size. The families cannot be crossed (they are two cuts of the same seconds, not a joint distribution — do NOT multiply them), but they can be BOUNDED: by inclusion-exclusion, at least 78.9 + 84.4 - 100 = 63.3% of on-loop fetch time is BOTH signal_build AND >= 15m, and since regime is at most 18.5% of all fetch it can explain AT MOST 21.9% of the >= 15m cost. So roughly three quarters of the frames worth caching are asked for by the path that feeds `close.iloc[-1]` into entry geometry.

CONSEQUENCE: raising the cap trades cache hits directly against the price freshness behind live orders, with no side door. That is a genuine Tier-3 trade-off, which is why it was not taken overnight. The prize if the operator accepts it: 1d+1h+4h+2h are 19.8% of the tick.

ALSO NOTE the off-loop table: fetchby.strategy_monitor_loop n=1120 — the decoupled exit loop is now the single largest fetch consumer by COUNT anywhere, and its fetches feed EXIT decisions off the same field. Any TTL change reaches the exit path too, not only entries.

A REMAINING MEASUREMENT GAP, stated rather than glossed: nothing here says WHICH TIMEFRAMES signal_build asks for. That needs a fetchby.<consumer>.<tf> cross, which costs names against _MAX_HOOK_NAMES (now 64, live chain measured 27 pre-cut). The bound above is what is available without it.

[sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Materially improved but the condition (tick overruns its 60s interval) still holds. The connector memo and the TTL-bounded candle cache shipped (src/runtime/market_data.py, CANDLE_CACHE_TTL_FRACTION / CANDLE_CACHE_TTL_MAX_S), the cap was raised to 300 on 2026-08-13, and the exit-loop decouple moved strategy_monitor_loop off the tick thread into offloop_hooks. CLAUDE.md records the post-change readings at 69.3 s mean / 96.8 s max and then 64.1 s mean — still 1.07x-1.6x over TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS=60. — needs live data: a warm /api/diag/tick_cost read at large n for the current process, reported as mean AND max beside ticks_measured. Severity drops because the harm that made it matter (exit cadence) was decoupled; what remains is signal freshness and Actions/VM cost. Ending condition: either the tick fits its interval, or the interval is deliberately widened with the staleness consequence stated (the TTL is a Tier-3 value because strategies read close.iloc[-1] as the current price).

RESOLVED. This row tracks the tick overrunning its 60 s interval — 251 s (4.2x) originally, 106 s (1.8x) after the connector-memo fix. Re-measured live 2026-08-29 on two independent trader processes: n=31 mean 45,467 ms / max 61,467 ms, and n=19 mean 47,986 ms / max 59,627 ms. The tick now runs at ~0.8x its 60 s interval — UNDER, not over. Per-hook split on the second process: run_one_tick 28,896 ms mean (60.2%), order_monitor 17,961 ms (37.4%), attributed_pct 97.6. The residual '~50 per-tick candle fetches' concern is also not visible: fetch.1d does not appear among the top hooks. ⚠️ Both reads are per-PROCESS with small n, so the MAX is under-observed — that limitation is BL-20260816-TICK-COST-MAX-RESETS-EVERY-DEPLOY, which stays open.

items.correction_2026_08_10_headroom:
CORRECTION to this item's original 'why it is not currently a wedge' paragraph, which claimed TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS is 15 min and there was therefore ~3.0x headroom. THAT WAS WRONG, and wrong in the REASSURING direction.

Derived from this item's own pre-fix numbers: process_started 03:44:37Z, sampled 04:35:29Z = 3052s over ticks_measured 10 = 305s per CYCLE against a 251s mean TICK, leaving ~54s of sleep. That implies TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS is approximately 60, not 900.

So the tick was OVERRUNNING its interval by ~4x rather than consuming a third of it: the trader had almost no idle and was effectively saturated, ticking every ~5 min instead of every ~1 min. This STRENGTHENS the link to BL-20260807-HEARTBEAT-PAUSED-WHILE-TICKING. The arithmetic was available in the original reading and I asserted the 15-min interval without checking it — the same failure to state/verify a population this review flagged elsewhere. Confirm TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS directly rather than trusting either figure.
items.warm_measurement_2026_08_11: WARM-PROCESS READ (the denominator this row was missing) — diag #8791, 2026-08-11 22:35Z. POPULATION: 51 ticks, ONE process, started 20:14:15Z (the set-env restart), ~2.35h of steady state. Every prior read was 3 cold ticks and could not support a distribution claim. MEAN 107.2s / MAX 122.2s (max at 20:16:18Z, i.e. the 2nd tick — cold-start, and the steady-state spread is narrow: mean 107.2 vs last 107.5). Against the pre-fix 251s mean / 296s max (over 10 ticks — a DIFFERENT and much smaller denominator, so treat the delta as directional): the connector-memo fix roughly HALVED the tick. THE 1.8x OVERRUN IS REAL AND STEADY-STATE, NOT A COLD-START ARTIFACT — so this row stays OPEN. 107s mean still fails the operator's '>60s without evaluation' bar by ~1.8x, and a position is re-evaluated only once per tick. PER-HOOK SPLIT (now trustworthy: attributed_pct 98.4, nested_hooks 14, hook_names_refused 0; the two top-level hooks sum 52.4 + 46.0 = 98.4 EXACTLY, so the 2026-08-11 nesting fix that had reported 136.8% is confirmed correct on live data). Two roughly equal halves: `run_one_tick` mean 56.2s (52.4%) and `order_monitor` mean 49.3s (46.0%). Inside order_monitor: `strategy_monitor_loop` 24.5s (22.8%) is half of it; the REST is ~20s spread across seven 2-5s reconcilers/sweeps (reconcile_open_trades 5.3s, check_broker_naked_equity 4.7s, reconcile_orphan_exchange_positions 3.4s, check_broker_naked_ib 3.3s, check_broker_naked_bybit 2.8s, reconcile_netting_partial_closes 2.8s, watchdog_stuck_strategies 2.2s). That is precisely the 'each individually cheap, nobody watched the sum' shape this row exists to catch — no single sweep is the culprit and none is obviously wrong. NOT CLAIMED, worth a look rather than an assertion: `check_broker_naked_ib_positions` is documented as cadence-gated at IB_BROKER_NAKED_CHECK_SECONDS=300 yet shows mean 3.3s over n=51. That is ARITHMETICALLY CONSISTENT with correct gating (~18 real executions across 5457s of wall clock, ~9s each, averaging to 3.3s, and max 6.7s fits), so it is NOT evidence of a broken gate — it is simply the one hook whose cost cannot be read off this table alone.

items.title: ict_scalp_mgc_15m raises 'no candle data for MGC 15m' every evaluation — the strategy cannot evaluate and it is surfacing only as a generic operator_warning banner
items.source: /api/bot/notifications, pulled 2026-08-10T04:39Z.
items.what_to_check: Live banner at severity 'alert', kind operator_warning, since 2026-08-10T03:56:28Z: 'RuntimeError: ict_scalp_mgc_15m: no candle data for symbol=MGC timeframe=15m.' detail 'strategy_builder * exception'. MGC is an IBKR-fed symbol and IB was healthy at the same moment (/api/diag/ib_state: all four clients state=connected, account_data_ready=true, breaker_open=false, consecutive_failures=0), so this is NOT a gateway wedge — the 15m bar request specifically returns nothing while the account connection is fine. ib_paper holds a live MGC position (105 contracts, entry 4276.236) at the same time, so the symbol is tradeable but not evaluable at 15m.
items.why_critical: This is a direct instance of the open BL-20260807-CANNOT-EVALUATE-IS-INVISIBLE class: a strategy that CANNOT evaluate is indistinguishable from one that evaluated and declined. Here it happens to raise, so it surfaces — but as an untyped operator_warning that reads like any other exception, with no 'this strategy has been unable to evaluate for N hours' aggregate anywhere. ict_scalp_mgc_15m also carries SHIPPED M27 verdicts whose dataset is already known missing (BL-20260809-XAU-PROXY-DATASET-GONE-VERDICTS-UNREPRODUCIBLE), so this leg is now both unevaluable live and unreproducible offline.
items.next_action: Determine whether MGC 15m is a contract/bar-size request the IB feed will not serve (vs a transient). If it is structural, the leg is dead and should be declared so rather than raising every tick — a per-tick RuntimeError is also a contributor to the tick-cost item above.
items.resolution_criteria: MGC 15m either serves candles or the leg is explicitly declared unevaluable; either way the condition is visible as a state, not an exception string.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: src/runtime/strategy_signal_builders.py:776 and :1727 still raise the bare `f"{name}: no candle data for symbol={symbol} timeframe={timeframe}."` RuntimeError, which is what surfaces as the generic operator_warning banner. Separately, the coverage matrix's ict_scalp_mgc_15m exit_head_ml cell was re-graded 2026-08-14 to `blocked:native-history-thin` on a measured basis (IBKR serves ~1yr of MGC 15m and the series is flat-bar contaminated), which is consistent with a real upstream data problem rather than a transient. — needs live data: /api/bot/candles?symbol=MGC&interval=15m and /api/diag/ib_state at the same moment, to confirm the 15m request specifically still returns nothing while the account connection is healthy. Ending condition: MGC 15m returns bars, or the leg is retired/re-timeframed — a strategy that cannot evaluate should not read as healthy (BL-20260807-CANNOT-EVALUATE-IS-INVISIBLE is the observability half).

RE-CONFIRMED AND RE-QUANTIFIED. The condition persists: ict_scalp_mgc_15m logs 38 transient_market_data_unavailable WARN rows over 08-25..08-29, INCLUDING the trading days 08-27 (8) and 08-28 (11). What CHANGED on 2026-08-26 is the classification, not the condition — the rows moved ERROR -> WARN when the transient classifier was fixed to match the variant families. That was correct (they ARE transient) but it made a live capability outage quieter. ⚠️ Do NOT read the ERROR feed going to zero as this row being fixed.

items.title: Two Tier-1 read surfaces (exposure/soak, pnl/exchange/fills) shipped unreachable by the relay — and the relay's rejection message invented a cause
items.source: Hit directly while pulling state for /system-review 2026-08-10; both fixed in commit c80a318.
items.what_to_check:
(1) ALLOWLIST GAP: /api/bot/exposure/soak and /api/bot/pnl/exchange/fills are documented Tier-1 GETs but were absent from BOTH allowlists in .github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml. A relay-only (Trusted-network) session — which is the ONLY session type that runs these reviews — therefore could not read them at all. exposure/soak was blocking BL-20260809-EXPOSURE-SOAK-NOT-YET-TAKEN, whose entire ask is the observation window that endpoint serves. Aggravating: one bad path fails the WHOLE batch, so the miss took out a 15-path request.
(2) INVENTED CAUSE: resolve_one raises three distinct rejections (allowlist miss / illegal characters / empty path) and prints the real one to the run log, but the issue comment DISCARDED it and asserted one unrelated cause — 'the path is read from the issue BODY, the title is display-only' — sending the caller to fix a body that was already correct. UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A.
items.resolution: c80a318. Both paths added to the shell case and BOT_ALLOWLIST_EXACT, with a comment stating that adding a /api/bot/* read surface without adding it here ships it unreachable. The rejection reason is now carried to the issue comment via $GITHUB_ENV and read through process.env (not ${{ }} interpolation, so caller-supplied text cannot break out of the script literal); the comment names all three causes and states that an allowlist miss is a gap in the relay rather than a mistake in the request.

items.title: /api/bot/shadow/stats first_seen is the LOG-ROTATION boundary, not the model's soak start — so soak duration, the shadow->advisory promotion denominator, is unreadable from the promotion surface
items.source: Found while trying to answer 'does any shadow model meet its promotion gate' during /system-review 2026-08-10.
items.what_to_check:
MEASURED. /api/bot/shadow/stats returns 19 model records. EVERY ONE has first_seen inside a TWO-MINUTE band: 2026-08-05T23:35 to 2026-08-05T23:37 — models promoted to shadow on wildly different dates (the fc-pcv-v1/v2 pair alone spans 2026-07-20 to 2026-08-04 per CLAUDE.md) all report the same soak start. 19 independent soaks do not begin in the same two minutes.

ARITHMETIC CROSS-CHECK — this is what turns suspicion into a finding; a careful re-read would not have caught it. If first_seen were a rotation boundary, each model's count should equal its OWN bar cadence times ONE COMMON window. Against 2026-08-05T23:36 -> 2026-08-10T05:15 (~4.24 days):
  5m heads (btc/sol/eth-regime-5m-*): count 1149-1160; predicted 4.24 x 288 = 1221 (ratio ~0.95).
  15m heads (btc-regime-15m-*, eth-15m): count 410-411; predicted 4.24 x 96 = 407 (ratio ~1.01).
  MES 5m heads: 588 — lower, consistent with a futures session calendar vs 24/7 crypto.
  per-signal heads (conviction-meta, setup-quality-*, execution-quality-*): all EXACTLY 436, one shared signal population.
Counts track BAR CADENCE x A SHARED WINDOW almost exactly. That is rotation, not 19 coincident promotions.

MECHANISM: ict-shadow-log-rotate.timer is active on the live VM (confirmed in /api/diag/services). ml.shadow.inspector.aggregate derives first_seen as the min timestamp of SURVIVING rows in runtime_logs/shadow_predictions.jsonl, so rotation silently resets it for every model at once.
items.why_critical:
This is the denominator of the promotion gate. shadow->advisory is THE operator-approved live-trading switch, and 'days in shadow' + 'prediction volume' are how a review decides a soak has accrued enough. Read off this endpoint EVERY model looks like it started 4 days ago with ~1,000 predictions — a model soaking since July is indistinguishable from one wired up last Wednesday. The failure runs in the DANGEROUS direction: long soaks look short, so a promotion that is DUE reads as not-yet-ready and is deferred indefinitely — the 'gate met but unactioned' condition /system-review is explicitly required to surface. And if rotation ran mid-review, a brand-new model's window would look complete.

Textbook UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class B (implicit input selection): the field is LABELLED as the model's first sighting and is actually 'the oldest row surviving the last rotation', with nothing in the envelope disclosing the substitution.
items.next_action: RESOLVED — live-verified 2026-08-12 on the running fleet (diag #8804, git_sha 1a5126a1), against BOTH halves of the criteria. (a) True soak duration is readable: every row now carries soak_start_basis ('registry' / 'registry_registration'), soak_started_at from the durable registry stage-transition, and soak_days with soak_days_is_lower_bound=false. btc-regime-5m-baseline-v1 reads 82.18d and sol-regime-5m-lgbm-v1 45.24d, where the log floor (2026-08-05T23:35, a rotation boundary shared by all 30 models) would have said ~6.7d — a 12x understatement, on the promotion gate's own denominator. (b) The endpoint states its retention window: the envelope carries log_coverage plus registry_soak_source. Fixed by #8774; the relay-reachable mirror was still serving the undisclosed first_seen until #8796 made /api/diag/shadow_stats delegate, so a relay-bound session could not have confirmed this before today — which is why it stayed open with the fix already shipped.
items.resolution_criteria: A reviewer can read a model's true shadow-soak duration without silent truncation by log rotation, and the endpoint states its retention window.

items.title: IB account warm-up subscribed reqAccountUpdates on the READONLY diag/reconciler client too — a documented IB multi-client subscription collision
items.source: BACKFILLED 2026-08-10 from CLAUDE.md's account (see the IB_ACCOUNT_WARMUP_TIMEOUT_S env-var row, which documents this incident and its fix in full). Filed retroactively from that DOCUMENTATION, not from a fresh investigation this session — the provenance matters and is stated here rather than implied.
items.what_to_check:
The BL-20260706-IBWARMUP fix made IBClient.connect() explicitly (re-)subscribe to reqAccountSummary AND reqAccountUpdates so balance()/positions() had real data before connect() declared success. reqAccountUpdates is a persistent PER-ACCOUNT subscription: the trader's own execution connection already holds it for every account it trades, so a SECOND concurrent client subscribing to the same account is a documented IB-API multi-client collision — the Gateway does not reliably deliver a fresh accountDownloadEnd to the second subscriber.

Live-verified 2026-07-06: the readonly diag read client's warm-up timed out twice (8s + 8s retry) while the trader's own connection stayed healthy throughout (still evaluating mgc_trend_1h on fresh prices).
items.resolution: A readonly client's warm-up never subscribes to reqAccountUpdates at all, and IBClient.positions() routes readonly reads through reqPositions() — a stateless one-shot request IBKR documents as safe for any number of concurrent clients against the same account. Cost: no unrealizedPNL on that path, so unrealised_pnl is None — the honest 'not measured' value the rest of the stack already handles. The trader's own non-readonly connection is untouched (still portfolio()/reqAccountUpdates, unchanged behaviour).
items.why_filed_now: The incident was real, closed, and documented, but had NO backlog row — so every citation of it resolved to nothing. artifact-validity-guard correctly flagged a reference to it from src/runtime/market_data.py (the connector-cache comment explaining WHY IB is excluded from that cache). Two already-resolved rows (BL-20260705-IBPAPER-POSITIONS-NULL-WEEKEND, BL-20260707-IBWARMUP-RECURRENCE) also cite it in prose and were likewise dangling. Filing the row fixes all three at once. Deliberately NOT suppressed: the guard has no suppression mechanism by design ('suppress it, which is worse than not having it') and its own error message names filing the row as the fix.

items.title: CLAUDE.md's CONVICTION_SIZING_MODE row is STALE — it says off/annotate while ROADMAP.md records the operator-approved 2026-08-05 apply/reductive/bybit_1 flip. Config is correct; the doc is not.
items.source: Found in the routine soak audit at the end of /system-review 2026-08-10 (diag issue #8743, log_file conviction_sizing).
items.what_to_check:
MEASURED, from the live conviction_sizing log at 2026-08-10T04:04:47Z:
  {"kind": "apply", "mode": "apply", "direction": "reductive", "applied": true, "strategy": "htf_pullback_trend_2h", "symbol": "BTCUSDT", "account": "bybit_1", "conviction": 0.3488, "risk_based_qty": 3.684, "final_qty": 1.151}

So conviction sizing is not annotating — it is APPLYING, and it reduced that order from 3.684 to 1.151, a ~69% size cut, with applied:true. The adjacent rows are the flagless would_be_size annotator (action='would_be_size'), which is the expected observe-only shape; the row above is a different `kind` entirely.

THE CONTRADICTION: CLAUDE.md's env table for CONVICTION_SIZING_MODE states, verbatim, 'The backtest A/B FAILED the gate for symmetric c_strat-only sizing (4.5x worse maxDD) -> stays at off/annotate. Tier-3; apply is operator-gated + backtest-gated.' The FIELD says apply; the DOC says off/annotate.

WHAT I AM **NOT** CLAIMING: that this is unauthorised. The documented A/B failure was specifically for SYMMETRIC c_strat-only sizing, and the live row is direction='reductive' — a different configuration that may well have been approved separately, with CLAUDE.md simply never updated. I could not determine which from a read-only session, and guessing either way would be worse than saying so.
items.why_critical:
This is a Tier-3 order-path setting (it changes the quantity actually sent to a venue) where the canonical doc and the running system disagree. Under 'field beats comment' the field wins and the DOC gets fixed — but that rule assumes the field's state was intended. A Tier-3 size multiplier is exactly the case where 'it was already like that' is not an acceptable disposition, because the same reasoning would have silently accepted the MULTI_SYMBOL_ENABLED and netting-guard regressions.

Scope matters and is unresolved: the sampled row is bybit_1 (paper), but CONVICTION_SIZING_ACCOUNTS is an allowlist whose live value I did not read, so I cannot say whether real-money bybit_2 is in scope.
items.next_action: (1) DONE — authorisation confirmed via ROADMAP.md M16; CLAUDE.md corrected. (2) READ SURFACE DONE — `get-env` Tier-1 action shipped. (3) REMAINING — once this merges to main and the VM syncs, dispatch `action: get-env / env_key: CONVICTION_SIZING_ACCOUNTS` and record the measured value. Treat the bybit_1 scope as DOCUMENTED until that run returns; if it comes back `set_empty` or `unset`, the multiplier is scoped to ALL accounts including real-money bybit_2 and that is a Tier-3 finding to raise immediately, not a doc fix.
items.resolution_criteria: CLAUDE.md and the live env agree, with the approval (or the rollback) recorded.

updates.note:
RESOLVED THE QUESTION, and my original framing was half wrong — worth recording which half.

ROADMAP.md (instruction-hierarchy priority 3) M16 states verbatim: the reductive apply path is LIVE ON THE DEMO ACCOUNT, `CONVICTION_SIZING_MODE=apply` / `DIRECTION=reductive` / `ACCOUNTS=bybit_1`, **operator-approved 2026-08-05**, with symmetric staying off because it failed the A/B. So the live config is AUTHORISED and correctly scoped, and the observed bybit_1 row is exactly the intended behaviour.

CLAUDE.md (priority 6) still says it 'stays at off/annotate'. Higher doc wins: CLAUDE.md is stale and gets fixed. Severity high -> low, tier 3 -> 1. What I got right was that a contradiction existed on a Tier-3 order-path setting; what I got wrong was implying the FIELD might be the unauthorised side. I hedged rather than asserted, which is the only reason this did not become a false alarm.

ROADMAP also records the gate for widening: the C1 A/B was PARTIAL (reductive cuts maxDD on BTC by $1,810 but WORSENS SOL by $1,786, over a net-negative population), so demo-only is a deliberate stance, not an oversight.
updates.next_check: Update the CLAUDE.md env row to match ROADMAP. SEPARATELY worth verifying the live CONVICTION_SIZING_ACCOUNTS really is `bybit_1` and has not drifted to empty (empty = ALL accounts, incl. real-money bybit_2) — the sampled rows were all bybit_1 but n=3 is not proof.

updates.note:
FIXED the doc half. CLAUDE.md's CONVICTION_SIZING_MODE row now records the live state per ROADMAP.md M16 (apply / reductive / bybit_1, operator-approved 2026-08-05, DEMO-ONLY), states that the failed A/B applied to the SYMMETRIC variant only, carries the C1-PARTIAL evidence, and notes that an EMPTY CONVICTION_SIZING_ACCOUNTS means ALL accounts including real money — an empty allowlist is the widest setting, not a safe default.

STILL OPEN, and stated plainly rather than assumed: I did NOT read the live CONVICTION_SIZING_ACCOUNTS value this session. ROADMAP records bybit_1 and the sampled soak rows are bybit_1, but a sample of rows cannot establish an allowlist (bybit_2 having no qualifying signal in the window is indistinguishable from bybit_2 being excluded — an unasserted denominator). So the scope question is documented, not verified.

WHY it is unverified is itself the finding: there is NO env-READ surface. The system-actions allowlist has `set-env` (write) and no get/show/print-env; no /api/diag/* route exposes process env; SSH is unavailable from a web session. A Tier-3 order-path multiplier whose scope can be WRITTEN from a session but never READ back is the write-without-a-reader asymmetry provenance-consumer-guard exists to catch, one level up at the ops surface. A bounded read-only `get-env` over a fixed key allowlist (the same shape as set-env's, values redacted for anything secret-like) would close it and is the natural next_action.

Operator directed building the read surface now rather than backlogging it, so the verification can actually be closed. Shipped `get-env` as a Tier-1 read-only system-action (scripts/ops/get_env.py + get_env_action.sh, wired into system-actions.yml + docs/claude/system-actions.md).

It reports BOTH /proc/<MainPID>/environ (authoritative — what the running process holds) and the unit's systemd-declared EnvironmentFiles (what the next restart picks up), flagging a mismatch as `pending_restart`. Four states per source, never collapsed: set / set_empty / unset / unreadable — `set_empty` vs `unset` being the load-bearing pair for THIS item, since an empty CONVICTION_SIZING_ACCOUNTS means ALL accounts including real money. Agreement is asserted only when both sides were readable (`undetermined` otherwise), so a failed measurement cannot manufacture a finding. Fixed key allowlist, no freeform input; secret-NAMED keys are fingerprinted and never printed because the action's stdout is commented onto a PUBLIC issue.

Verified the self-test catches a positive: planting the exact defect it exists to catch (collapsing set_empty into unset) makes it FAIL, exit 1. Also confirmed the mechanism is reachable — scripts/ops/status_check.sh already reads /proc/<TRADER_PID>/environ successfully over the same relay, it just greps four hardcoded path vars and so could never answer this key.

STILL NOT VERIFIED: the live CONVICTION_SIZING_ACCOUNTS value. The system-actions workflow dispatches from the DEFAULT BRANCH and the wrapper runs from the VM's checkout, so `get-env` is only usable once this lands on main and ict-git-sync pulls it. That is a sequencing constraint, not a new blocker.

items.resolution:
RESOLVED — VERIFIED, not inferred. get-env run #8755 read the live trader and returned CONVICTION_SIZING_ACCOUNTS = 'bybit_1' on BOTH sides (process /proc/<MainPID>/environ AND the unit's declared env, agreement='agree', so not a pending-restart artifact), alongside CONVICTION_SIZING_MODE='apply' and CONVICTION_SIZING_DIRECTION='reductive'.

That matches ROADMAP.md M16 exactly: the reductive apply path is live and DEMO-ONLY. Real-money bybit_2 is NOT in scope, and the empty-allowlist hazard (empty = ALL accounts) is not present. The doc half was fixed earlier in the session; this closes the scope half that had been DOCUMENTED but never MEASURED.

Path to the answer, for the record: the read surface did not exist, so it was built (get-env, #8744), its first dispatch failed because ENV_KEY never crossed the SSH boundary (#8753, fixed in #8754), and the retry (#8755) returned the value. Three PRs to read one string — which is the measure of how unreachable it was.

items.title: StrategyIntent.target_qty is ALWAYS 0.0 in production — which makes the documented 'max target_qty wins' reinforcement rule INERT, and makes the conviction-arbitration soak's sizing half structurally unmeasurable where it sits
items.checked: checked: src/runtime/intents.py (aggregate_intents winner key + line ~1368 max(i.target_qty ...) + the StrategyIntent validator documenting 0.0-on-directional as the sentinel) and src/runtime/intent_multiplexer.py (line 794, target_qty_hint=0.0 hardcoded at the sole production entry point) and src/runtime/conviction_arbitration.py (the reader that wrote the sentinel out as a literal 0.0). Scope of the 'unmeasurable' claim: it is about THESE files / this layer, not about the quantity. The real per-account qty exists downstream of RiskManager.position_size and IS measured by the sibling conviction_sizing soak.
items.source: Root-caused while investigating BL-20260806-ARBITRATION-SOAK-QTY-ALL-ZERO during /system-review 2026-08-10.
items.what_to_check:
TRACED IN CODE, not inferred from the log. The single production entry point `intent_multiplexer.build_multiplexed_signal` calls `_collect_intents(..., target_qty_hint=0.0)` — the value is HARDCODED 0.0 (intent_multiplexer.py:794) under a comment that says so explicitly: 'target_qty=0 — ... the actual per-account qty is settled by RiskManager.position_size. The intent layer never decides qty.' `intent_from_signal` then stores `target_qty=float(target_qty or 0.0)`, and StrategyIntent's own validator documents 0.0 on a directional side as the deliberate sentinel for 'the per-account RiskManager decides the qty — THIS IS THE PRODUCTION PATH'.

So target_qty is 0.0 for every directional intent in production, by design. Two consequences follow, and they are very different in severity.

CONSEQUENCE 1 (the reason the soak is empty, benign): `conviction_arbitration` logs `getattr(i, 'target_qty', 0.0)` from these intents, so every qty field it writes is 0.0. This is NOT a value being lost at the writer, which is what BL-20260806 assumed and what I repeated this morning — the soak is simply reading a field that is a SENTINEL at that point in the pipeline. No amount of fixing the writer helps.

CONSEQUENCE 2 (the real finding): `aggregate_intents` resolves same-direction reinforcement with
  winner = max(same_side, key=lambda i: (i.target_qty, i.effective_priority(), -i.timestamp, <name>))
Its docstring says '**Same-direction reinforcement: max target_qty wins.**' Because the first sort key is a CONSTANT 0.0 across every candidate, it contributes nothing and the winner is decided ENTIRELY by the tiebreakers — priority, then timestamp, then name. Likewise `target_qty = max(i.target_qty for i in winning_side_intents)` (line 1368) is always 0.0.

The documented selection rule has therefore never fired. That is the INERT-CONDITIONAL class (BL-20260808-INERT-CONDITIONAL-SHIPPED-AS-A-BEHAVIOUR-CHANGE): a branch whose output is identical on both sides, described in prose as if it discriminates.
items.why_critical:
The routing behaviour may well be FINE — priority-then-timestamp-then-name is deterministic and defensible. The defect is that anyone reasoning about 'which strategy wins when two agree' from the docstring, the design doc, or the audit trail will reach a confidently wrong answer, and any future work that tries to tune reinforcement by influencing target_qty will have no effect and no error.

It also invalidates the premise of BL-20260806-ARBITRATION-SOAK-QTY-ALL-ZERO, which is filed as 'the sizing half of the soak has produced no usable data' — true, but the stated cause (a writer bug) is wrong, and chasing the writer would have burned a session finding nothing.
items.next_action:
TWO SEPARATE DECISIONS, deliberately not bundled:
(A) TIER-1, safe now: fix the prose. The `aggregate_intents` docstring and any design doc claiming 'max target_qty wins' must say what actually decides — effective_priority, then timestamp, then name — and note that target_qty is a sentinel at this layer.
(B) TIER-3, operator-gated, DO NOT enact: decide whether reinforcement SHOULD size-discriminate. Either (i) accept priority-ordering as the real rule and delete the dead sort key, or (ii) move the arbitration measurement DOWNSTREAM of RiskManager.position_size where a real per-account qty exists, which is also the only place the conviction soak's sizing half can ever be measured. (ii) changes what the soak measures, not what the router does, so it is the cheaper path to usable data.
items.resolution_criteria: The documented reinforcement rule matches what the code actually discriminates on, and the conviction-arbitration soak either measures a real qty or stops claiming to.
items.progress: 2026-08-10 PARTIAL. (A) DONE (Tier-1): aggregate_intents' docstring, the inline comment at the winner key, and the emitted `same_direction_reinforcement` reason string now state that target_qty is a sentinel at this layer and that effective_priority -> timestamp -> name is what actually decides; the reason string no longer prints 'max target_qty=0.0' as if it were a measured max. (B)(ii) DONE (Tier-1, measurement only): conviction_arbitration now reports qty as NULL with `qty_measured:false` + `qty_unmeasured_reason` instead of a fabricated 0.0; ordering still coerces to 0.0 via `_sort_qty` so the would-be conviction winner is byte-for-byte unchanged. (B)(i) NOT ENACTED and still owed: deleting the dead target_qty sort key changes selection behaviour and stays Tier-3, operator-gated. Moving the arbitration measurement downstream of position_size (the other half of (ii)) is also still open.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The Tier-1 halves are DONE and I verified both. src/runtime/intents.py:1217-1233 now states in the aggregator's own docstring that the first sort key is inert in production, that the winner is decided entirely by effective_priority -> timestamp -> name, names this backlog id, and declares that changing or removing the key is a Tier-3 routing decision. :1355-1362 fixes the diagnostic label so a 0.0 sentinel no longer prints as 'max target_qty=0.0' but as 'target_qty unsized at this layer (RiskManager sizes per account); winner by priority/timestamp/name'. The FIELD is unchanged: src/runtime/intent_multiplexer.py:794 still passes `target_qty_hint=0.0` unconditionally. — Proposed operator decision (Tier-3, order routing): either (a) DELETE target_qty from the reinforcement sort key and from DesiredPosition, so the documented rule matches the code and nothing reads a permanent sentinel — the cheapest honest option, since the per-account RiskManager already owns sizing; or (b) have build_multiplexed_signal pass a real pre-sizing hint so 'max target_qty wins' actually fires. Do not do nothing quietly: today a documented selection rule has never once executed in production. Consequence 1 (the conviction-arbitration soak's all-zero qty column) is benign and explained by the same sentinel — it needs no writer fix.

Re-validated: a documented reinforcement rule that is INERT in production, plus a soak whose sizing half is meaningless. Written-and-never-read class (A) — the highest-value class this review identified.

items.opened_by: claude (system-review 2026-08-10, hit it twice while working)
items.title: impossibility-claim-guard reports a FALSE failure when there are uncommitted edits above a claim — it takes line numbers from a commit diff but resolves its annotation window against the working tree
items.checked: checked: scripts/check_impossibility_claims.py (_added_lines yields new-file line numbers from `git diff base...HEAD`, a COMMIT diff; main() passes body_lines=full worktree text; check_lines._window slices body_lines by that lineno)
items.source: Hit twice in one session while working docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json, both times self-inflicted-looking and both times cleared by committing.
items.what_to_check:
REPRODUCED, twice, with the same signature. `_added_lines()` runs `git diff --unified=0 <base>...HEAD` — a COMMIT-to-COMMIT diff, so its line numbers describe HEAD. `main()` then calls `check_lines(lines, path, context=body, body_lines=body.splitlines())` where `body` is the WORKING TREE file. `_window(lineno)` slices the worktree text using the committed line number.

So any uncommitted insertion ABOVE a claim shifts that claim in the worktree while its diff lineno stays put, and the +/-6-line window (ANNOTATION_WINDOW, tight by design for row-structured JSON) slides off the `checked:` annotation that is in fact sitting directly beside the claim.

Observed sequence, both times identical:
  1. `checked:` inserted on the line immediately after the title -> guard PASSES.
  2. ~7 further lines appended to an EARLIER item, still uncommitted -> guard FAILS with 'appears in a REFUTING block but still names nothing' / 'no checked: annotation', naming the same title.
  3. `git commit` (no content change to the claim or its annotation) -> guard PASSES again.
Measured on the second occurrence: title at worktree line 12375, guard reported line 12368 — a 7-line offset exactly equal to the uncommitted insertion above it.
items.why_critical:
Low severity because it is transient and clears on commit, but it has a genuinely bad failure mode for the NEXT session rather than for CI. CI only ever sees committed trees, so this never fires there — it fires locally, mid-edit, which is precisely when a session is deciding how to satisfy it.

The obvious way to 'fix' a guard that says an annotation is missing when the annotation is visibly right there is to add a SECOND one somewhere the window will catch, or to reword the claim until the pattern stops matching. Both are the 'a guard that is cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than no guard' failure the guard's own docstring warns about (the new-table-wiring-guard lesson). A guard that cries wolf teaches sessions to route around it, which is the desensitized-alarm P1 shape.
items.next_action: Make the two sides agree on which tree they describe. Cheapest correct fix: in `main()`, when `--base` is given, read the body from the SAME revision the diff describes (`git show HEAD:<path>`) instead of the worktree, so linenos and body_lines are consistent by construction. Alternative: have `_added_lines` return the added TEXT with enough surrounding context to satisfy the window without needing absolute line numbers at all. Do NOT fix by widening ANNOTATION_WINDOW — the window is deliberately tight for row-structured JSON (its own comment records that a wide window previously harvested unrelated `checked:`-shaped strings from elsewhere in the file, an unasserted-denominator defect in the guard written to catch unasserted claims), and widening would trade a false positive for a false negative.
items.resolution_criteria: Editing a backlog file with uncommitted changes above an annotated claim no longer produces a failure that disappears on commit. Add a self-test that plants exactly that offset.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The mismatch is unchanged. scripts/check_impossibility_claims.py:202-204 `_added_lines` runs `git diff --unified=0 {base}...HEAD` (commit-to-commit line numbers describing HEAD), while main() at :231-244 reads `body = full.read_text()` from the WORKING TREE and passes `body_lines=body.splitlines()` alongside those line numbers into check_lines. `_window(lineno)` therefore slices worktree text with committed line numbers, and ANNOTATION_WINDOW is 6 (:127) — tight enough that any uncommitted insertion above a claim slides the window off its annotation.
Re-validated: a guard that reports a FALSE failure on uncommitted edits. Same family as BL-20260813-GUARDS-THAT-TEST-FOR-THE-ABSENCE-OF-A-WRONG-ANSWER — guards whose own correctness is unverified.

items.title: docs/claude/diag-relay.md told every session the diag path is the TITLE and the body is ignored; the workflow parses the BODY first and the title is only an empty-body fallback
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-10 02:23Z. Issue #8716 was opened exactly as the doc's 'Common mistakes' section #1 prescribes -- path in the title, prose in the body -- and was REJECTED before any VM contact.

Authority is .github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml step 'Resolve and validate diag path(s)' (resolve_multi): it reads ISSUE_BODY first (JSON array, fenced JSON array, or one path per line), and only `if not candidates` does it fall back to title_path. A prose body therefore becomes the candidate list and fails PATH_RE, and one bad path sys.exit(1)s the WHOLE batch.

The doc has been wrong since the multi-path batching change, and the section it is wrong in is the one headed 'read before first use'.
items.what_to_check: Whether any other doc or skill still teaches the title-carries-the-path form (grep '[diag-request]' across docs/ and .claude/skills/).
items.action: FIXED in this PR: 'Common mistakes' #1 rewritten to the measured contract (body = path list, one per line, no prose; title = display-only fallback; MAX_PATHS 15; one bad path fails the batch; the /api/bot/ read-only allowlist named). The retraction is kept inline rather than silently overwritten, since sessions acted on the old text.
items.resolution_criteria: Doc matches resolve_multi's actual precedence, verified by reading the workflow rather than by one successful request.

items.title: M20's gate optimises net_R and maxDD only -- the TWO metrics that measure the operator's actual complaint (MFE capture ratio, capital efficiency) are both computed in-repo and read by ZERO gates
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-10. Coverage matrix census: 400 cells (50 legs x 8 levers) -> 266 honest_negative (66.5%), 63 pending, 24 shipped (6.0%), 5 passed_unshipped.

Operator 2026-08-10: 'the amount of times that a trade has gotten within literally several cents of its take profit and then it drops and turns into a loss ... we're working on this so hard and we're getting absolutely nowhere.'

The standard metric for that phenomenon is MFE CAPTURE RATIO (exit profit / maximum favorable excursion). It is already computed here -- src/research/excursions.py, build_backtest_panel.py, build_exit_panel.py, analyze_research_panel.py -- and grep finds NO gate, sweep verdict, or matrix cell that reads it. It is not one of the 8 lever_columns. Same for net_r_per_capital_day (BL-20260810 sibling): declared as the gate's tiebreak in the exit-refinement skill since inception, first computed 2026-08-10.

So every one of the 266 honest_negative verdicts was rendered by an objective function that is INDIFFERENT to both 'how much of the move did we keep' and 'how long did the capital sit'. A lever that improves either while costing a little net_R is not merely unreported -- Path A's `beats()` requires net_R >= base, so it short-circuits to is_oos_fail BEFORE the walk-forward runs.

This is the THIRD instance of the written-but-never-read class in this repo, after exit_price_source (12 writers / 1 unrelated reader -> the phantom -$6,358 leak) and net_r_per_capital_day. The pattern is the finding.
items.what_to_check: Quantify the prize before designing a lever: over the fleet's backtest panel, the share of LOSING trades whose mfe_r reached >= 80/90/95% of the leg's tp_r, and the fleet capture_ratio distribution against the external <30% 'severe edge leakage' / >75% 'excellent' reference points. That number sizes the opportunity and says which legs to work first. Do NOT design from the anecdote alone.
items.action: Add capture_ratio to the reported axes beside net_r_per_capital_day (same report-not-grade discipline, thresholds operator-set). Then re-evaluate the 266 honest_negatives -- they are not wrong, they are answers to a different question.
items.resolution_criteria: A gate or verdict surface reads capture_ratio, and the fleet re-evaluation under the widened objective is recorded in the coverage matrix.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Half fixed. CAPITAL EFFICIENCY is now read by a gate: scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:1403 `is_path_b_candidate` branches on `_up(cap_oos.get("d_net_r_per_capital_day"))`, the metric is recorded per cell (:1979, :2447-2449) and its derived tolerance is reported per window and per leg (:2170+). MFE CAPTURE RATIO is still read by nothing — grepping the sweep for `capture_ratio` returns zero hits. And the file's own comment at :1488 confirms 'Path B's two thresholds … remain unset', so the capital metric informs a candidate branch but promotes nothing. — The remaining work splits cleanly: (a) compute and record a per-cell MFE capture ratio in the sweep so the operator's actual complaint has a number; (b) the Path B thresholds are a Tier-3 operator decision (see BL-20260810-NO-STALL-EXIT-CAPITAL-SITS-IN-DEAD-TRADES, which proposes exactly that). (a) is Tier-1 but not a minimal edit — it needs the harness to emit per-trade mfe_r, which only some harnesses do.

Re-validated and it is the ROOT of this review's exit findings: a gate optimising net_R and maxDD only cannot see MFE capture or capital efficiency, which is why 8.3% declared-bracket exits and 191x holds pass every gate the program runs. Pair with BL-20260810-NO-STALL-EXIT-CAPITAL-SITS-IN-DEAD-TRADES.

items.title: the coverage matrix's 8 lever columns are not the lever space: 21 exit-relevant harness flags exist, 3 have no column at all, and the operator's near-TP-reversal case has NO lever anywhere
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-10 by enumerating add_argument() across the 6 backtest harnesses: 21 exit-relevant flags vs 8 matrix lever_columns.

Flags with NO matrix column:
  --timeout-bars   present in ALL SIX harnesses. A hard max-hold, distinct from stale_stop (which is conditional on R). This is the crudest form of the exact 'capital sits in dead trades' complaint and it has never been swept.
  --sim-breakeven  ict_scalp only. A breakeven stop is the most direct protection against the give-it-all-back case, and it is neither a column nor ported to the other five harnesses.
  --tp-r / --exit-style / --atr-stop-buffer / --pierce-min  fade + fvg_range only.

MISSING ENTIRELY -- no harness has it: a lever parameterized on PROXIMITY TO TARGET. Every giveback lever is in absolute R (--giveback-r, --giveback-min-mfe-r), so on a 1.5R bracket a trade that reaches 1.45R and reverses only triggers after surrendering the configured absolute R. 'Arm breakeven / tighten at X% of the distance to TP' cannot currently be expressed, let alone tested. That is precisely the operator's case.
items.what_to_check: Whether --timeout-bars and --sim-breakeven were deliberately excluded from the matrix or simply never added. check_harness_lever_coupling.py's UNMODELLED sets list timeout_bars as unmodelled-by-family, which is about REPLAY parity, not about the matrix's column set -- the two gaps are being conflated.
items.action: Enumerate the lever space exhaustively BEFORE the next sweep (operator directive 2026-08-10: 'deep research all the levers and then actually test them, not just one or two'). Add the missing columns; port --sim-breakeven and a new proximity-to-target lever across harnesses; then sweep the full grid rather than one lever at a time.
items.resolution_criteria: Every exit-relevant harness flag maps to a matrix column or a recorded n/a with a reason, and the proximity-to-target lever exists and has been swept.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json still declares exactly 8 lever_columns (trail_geometry, stale_stop, giveback_stop, exit_ladder, exit_head_ml, trail_decay, regime_flip_exit, vol_trail) — unchanged from filing. `--timeout-bars` is threaded through the sweep as a config passthrough (scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:445, :461) but has no matrix column and is never varied as a lever; `--sim-breakeven` is appended unconditionally at :471 rather than swept. — Ending condition: a recorded decision per unenumerated flag — either it gets a matrix column and is swept, or the matrix legend states why it is excluded (the row's own question: deliberate exclusion vs never added). Note the row correctly warns that check_harness_lever_coupling.py's UNMODELLED sets are about REPLAY parity, not the matrix column set — do not conflate the two gaps when closing this.
Re-validated: the operator's near-TP-reversal case still has no lever anywhere, which is exactly the shape the 8.3% declared-bracket exit rate produces.

⚠️ THE ROW'S HEADLINE PREMISE IS REFUTED, MEASURED 2026-09-02 -- correcting it here because a wrong premise in a backlog row propagates, and this one has been re-validated unchanged as recently as 2026-08-29 ('the operator's near-TP-reversal case still has no lever anywhere').

THE PROXIMITY-TO-TARGET LEVER EXISTS AND HAS BEEN SWEPT. It is `--rr-floor` (M31 P5), declared in scripts/backtest_trend.py:1059 and scripts/backtest_pullback.py, and its own help text is the operator's case verbatim: 'close at bar CLOSE once rr_from_here = r_to_target / r_to_stop falls below this -- the remaining upside to the capped TP no longer justifies the give-back to the current stop'. It was swept on the fleet's own machinery: docs/research/e35-rr-floor-walkforward-2026-08-20.md, artifacts runtime_logs/m20_rrfloor/2026-08-20/, POPULATION 19 legs x 3 cells = 57 (leg x cell) rows, `--tp-cap-pct 0.099`, split-mode oos-trades, walk-forward folds 2021-2026, net of fees. Tally: 43 is_oos_fail, 4 wf_fail, 3 path_b_wf_fail, 2 Path-A PASS, 2 path_b_wf_pass, 3 rows that were not errors (squeeze_breakout_4h, whose harness declares no --rr-floor). Only `rrfloor0.5` ever passes. So the second half of this row's criterion -- 'the proximity-to-target lever exists and has been swept' -- is SATISFIED, with a locator.

WHAT ACTUALLY REMAINS IS THE FIRST HALF, and it is now narrow and named. Enumerating the exit-relevant flags across both harnesses (population: every `add_argument` string in backtest_trend.py and backtest_pullback.py, classified by whether the flag changes HOW OR WHEN A TRADE EXITS), the mapping to the matrix's 9 `lever_columns` is: --trail-mult -> trail_geometry; --atr-stop-mult/--tp-r/--tp-cap-pct -> bracket_geometry; --stale-exit-bars/--stale-exit-below-r -> stale_stop; --giveback-r/--giveback-min-mfe-r -> giveback_stop; --trail-decay-{arm-r,stall-bars,tight-mult} -> trail_decay; --trail-vol-{above-pctl,below-pctl,tight-mult} -> vol_trail; --bank-at-r/--bank-frac -> exit_ladder; --flip-exit-bars -> regime_flip_exit. THREE HAVE NO COLUMN AND NO RECORDED n/a, which reproduces the row's own count of 3:
  * `--rr-floor` -- GRADED by the sweep (cells rrfloor0.5/0.75/1, confirmed by `scripts/ci/check_lever_wiring.py`) and swept as above, yet it has no matrix column, so its 57 measured rows are invisible to anyone reading the matrix. It is also backtest-only (BL-20260818-RR-FLOOR-IS-BACKTEST-ONLY-AND-CANNOT-BE-DECLARED), so a column would need to say so.
  * `--timeout-bars` -- a real time-exit, no column; this is the same gap BL-20260810-NO-STALL-EXIT-CAPITAL-SITS-IN-DEAD-TRADES describes from the live side.
  * `--exit-grain` -- arguably a legitimate n/a (it is a measurement-fidelity knob choosing the bar grain levers are evaluated on, not a lever), but that n/a is nowhere RECORDED, which is exactly what the criterion asks for.

NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: adding three columns to docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json is a schema change to a 765 KB artifact behind four guards (exit-coverage-matrix, matrix-corpus-agreement, matrix-config-agreement, matrix-bracket-values) and other sessions are working that file; a single-purpose PR should do it. STATUS STAYS OPEN on the first clause only.

items.title: 10 of 52 live harness-classified legs have NO matrix row that joins by name: 8 equities legs are named *_trend_1d in the matrix vs *_trend_long_1d in config, and 3 more are still inside an un-exploded bundled row
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-10 by set-differencing config/strategies.yaml (legs whose m20_fleet_exit_sweep.classify() resolves a family) against docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json row ids.

config harness-classified: 52. matrix rows: 50. The counts nearly agree, which is what hid this -- the SETS do not.

IN CONFIG, NOT IN MATRIX (10): iwm_trend_long_1d, qld_trend_long_1d, qqq_trend_long_1d, scha_trend_long_1d, splg_trend_long_1d, spy_trend_long_1d, tqqq_trend_long_1d, trend_donchian_1h, trend_donchian_eth_prop, trend_donchian_sol_prop.

IN MATRIX, NOT IN CONFIG (8 + 1 bundle): iwm_trend_1d, qld_trend_1d, qqq_trend_1d, scha_trend_1d, splg_trend_1d, spy_trend_1d, tqqq_trend_1d, and the literal row 'shadow fleet (turtle_soup, fade_breakout_4h, vwap, ict_scalp_5m, trend_donchian_1h, mgc_trend_1h, *_prop)'.

TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS.
(1) NAME DRIFT: the 7 equities legs are the same strategies under a matrix id missing the `_long` infix. A human reading the matrix sees them covered; any automated join on strategy name sees ZERO rows and would report them uncovered -- or, worse, a writer could append a SECOND row under the config name and the matrix would then carry two rows for one leg with independent statuses.
(2) A SURVIVING BUNDLED ROW: trend_donchian_1h + both *_prop legs are inside one multi-leg row. That is exactly the shape BL-20260809-COVERAGE-MATRIX-MULTILEG-ROW-ONE-STATUS exploded on 2026-08-09 -- the explosion was INCOMPLETE, and this row is the residue. One status across seven named legs cannot be read per-leg.
items.what_to_check: Which name is canonical for the equities legs -- config is the field and the matrix is the claim, so config wins (`field beats comment`) unless the verdicts were measured under the other id. Check the referenced sweep outputs before renaming, so a rename does not silently re-point a verdict to a leg it was not measured on.
items.action: Rename the 7+1 matrix ids to their config ids and explode the surviving bundled row per BL-20260809's rule (per-leg status from the ref's explicit wording only; silent or un-run -> `pending`, never an inherited verdict). Then add a CI guard asserting the matrix id set equals the config harness-classified set -- the matrix calls itself M20's done-condition, and a done-condition that does not join to the thing it measures cannot be checked.
items.resolution_criteria: Set-difference between config harness-classified legs and matrix row ids is empty in both directions, enforced by a guard rather than by inspection.

updates.note:
RESOLVED, and the three halves closed differently — stated separately so the close is auditable.

(1) NAME DRIFT: GONE, measured not assumed. Re-ran the item's own set-difference this session (config/strategies.yaml legs whose m20_fleet_exit_sweep.classify() resolves a family, vs exit-refinement-coverage.json row ids): config harness-classified 52, matrix rows 50. IN CONFIG NOT IN MATRIX = {trend_donchian_1h, trend_donchian_eth_prop, trend_donchian_sol_prop} (all three execution:shadow, correctly outside the live denominator). IN MATRIX NOT IN CONFIG = the one bundled row. The 7 `*_trend_1d` vs `*_trend_long_1d` equities ids this item was opened on no longer drift — the matrix now carries the config ids. Restricted to the population that actually matters, the LIVE one: 45 live harness-classified legs in config, 45 live rows in the matrix, set-difference EMPTY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.

(2) THE SURVIVING BUNDLED ROW: kept, deliberately, NOT a defect left open. It is excluded from the done-condition denominator (execution != live) and carries a written `_bundled_row_note` explaining that per-leg evidence does not exist and inventing one would be worse than the bundle. That is the documented-keep disposition, not an orphan.

(3) THE GUARD — the actual remaining work, now SHIPPED. resolution_criteria asked for the set-difference to be empty 'in BOTH directions, enforced by a guard rather than by inspection', and only ONE direction was ever enforced: m20_coverage_rollup.validate() walked matrix->config (a row naming a leg that does not exist -> denominator too BIG) and had nothing for config->matrix (a live leg with no row at all -> denominator too SMALL). The second is the more expensive error and it was live-relevant this week: M20's headline hit 360/360 = 100.0% on 2026-08-13, and a 100% over an under-counted denominator reads as finished. Added to the SAME validate() rather than a new guard file (single-homing: a second definition of the join would be free to drift): config->matrix for live legs, execution-agreement in both directions, duplicate-row detection, and BOTH unreadable-input paths (no yaml / no classify import) reported as 'NOT checked' rather than clean.

TWO DEFECTS IN MY OWN GUARD, both caught before merge and both by evidence rather than review:
  a. The self-test (tests/test_m20_coverage_join.py, 8 cases) planted a leg declared `shadow` in config but `live` in the matrix and the guard did NOT fire — an early-`continue` skipped non-live legs BEFORE comparing execution, exempting exactly the denominator-INFLATING direction. Fixed by ordering the agreement check ahead of the liveness filter.
  b. On real data the guard then reported `xauusd_trend_1h: matrix says disabled but config declares live`. The MATRIX WAS RIGHT and the guard was wrong: that leg is `enabled: false` WITH `execution: live`, and the live trader's loaded-strategy list (52 legs, diag read 2026-08-13T08:14Z) does not contain it. Two config keys collapse into the matrix's one `execution` column and `enabled: false` outranks `execution:`. Single-homed as `_effective_execution()`. Had I 'fixed' the matrix row to match my guard I would have corrupted a correct row on a false positive.

VERIFICATION: 8/8 join self-tests pass; `--check` clean on real data; 106 pre-existing m20 tests still pass; headline population unchanged (45 live legs x 8 levers = 360). Also corrected this module's own docstring, which stated `47 x 8 = 376` and quoted `319/376` as 'the one to keep quoting' in the present tense — both stale, and stale in the direction that matters now that headline and done-condition have separated (360/360 vs 37 open).

items.title: the trail families place a REAL ~1.3-5R take-profit live and the harness models it at 50R -- 30 legs' exit verdicts were measured against an exit geometry production does not run
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-10 by reading the live signal builders against the harnesses.

LIVE: trend_donchian.py, htf_pullback_trend_2h.py and fade_breakout_4h.py each
define _TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT = 0.099 and place
    tp = min(entry * 1.099, entry + tp_r * risk)
The 50R 'sentinel' is CLAMPED to 9.9% from entry because Bybit rejects a TP
further than ~10% (ErrCode 10001, hit on every trend_donchian short at BTC ~75k
on 2026-05-27, PR #2141). So the live order carries a real, resting,
exchange-side take-profit.

BACKTEST: neither scripts/backtest_trend.py nor scripts/backtest_pullback.py
contains the cap, tp_r, or any tp assignment. backtest_pullback.py line 10 states
the premise outright: 'the tp_r (~50R) sentinel is parked far from price'. The
harness therefore simulates a trade whose ONLY profit-exit is the Chandelier
trail.

HOW REACHABLE THE LIVE TP ACTUALLY IS. TP distance in R = 0.099 /
(atr_stop_mult * ATR%). At atr_stop_mult 2.5 (every 2h crypto pullback leg):
  ATR% 0.5% -> 7.9R   1% -> 4.0R   2% -> 2.0R   3% -> 1.3R
A 2h crypto leg running 2-3% ATR has its live take-profit at 1.3-2.0R. That is
an ordinary, frequently-touched target -- not a sentinel.

CONSEQUENCE 1 (operator-reported, now explained): the operator reports live
trades repeatedly running to within a hair of take-profit and then reversing into
a loss. On these legs that is mechanically expected, and the 2026-08-10 capture
census could not see it -- the census measured the harness, where the TP is at
50R and never binds, so it reported near-miss as inapplicable on 40 of 43 legs.
The census is not evidence against the observation; it is blind to it.

CONSEQUENCE 2 (the larger one): every exit-lever verdict for these 30 legs --
trail_geometry, stale_stop, giveback_stop, trail_decay, vol_trail -- was measured
on a book with no take-profit, against a live book that has one at ~1.3-5R. A
trail lever tuned where the trail is the sole exit is not the same lever where a
hard TP truncates the right tail first. This is a live/backtest PARITY break in
the exit geometry itself, and it sits underneath M20's 266 honest_negatives.
items.what_to_check:
The ATR% figures above are illustrative ranges, NOT measured -- compute the
real per-leg distribution of 0.099/(atr_stop_mult*ATR%) from each leg's own
frame before quoting an R number for that leg. Also confirm per venue: the
9.9% clamp is a Bybit constraint, so an Alpaca/IBKR leg may place the
uncapped 50R TP and genuinely never bind -- in which case the parity break
is crypto-only and the equities legs are fine. Do not assume it is uniform.
items.action:
Teach the harnesses the live TP: add the same cap to backtest_trend.py /
backtest_pullback.py / backtest_fade.py behind an explicit flag so the A/B
(capped vs uncapped) is itself measurable, then RE-RUN the census and re-open the
affected exit-lever cells. Until that lands, treat trail-family exit verdicts as
measured-on-the-wrong-geometry rather than as settled negatives.
items.resolution_criteria:
The harness reproduces the live TP placement for every leg that has one,
demonstrated by a parity check on real closed trades, and the affected
coverage-matrix cells are re-measured or explicitly re-opened.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The instrument gap is closed and live parity is the DEFAULT where it matters. scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:532-536 appends `--tp-cap-pct` (plus the leg's own `--tp-r`) only for families in LIVE_TP_CAPPED_FAMILIES — deliberately per-family, since applying it elsewhere would manufacture a parity break; .github/workflows/m20-exit-lever-sweep.yml:15 and :264/:339 make tp_cap_pct 0.099 the workflow default with 'Pass tp_cap_pct=0 only to reproduce a historical verdict'; and scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py:183 defaults --tp-cap-pct to 0.099 with a WARNING at :811 when it is 0. The four-state tp_geometry_for helper (:103, :113-121) stops a run-level flag from mislabelling a leg. — The residual — re-measuring verdicts taken before the 2026-08-10 cutover — is owned by BL-20260813-SEVENTEEN-SHIPPED-LEVERS-REST-ON-PRE-TP-PARITY-EVIDENCE and is now machine-readable via `m20_coverage_rollup.py --stale-decisions`, which I ran: 3 of 66 stale cells remain as decisions, all routing=paper.

items.title: winner_mfe_p80 read mfe_r top-level only, so the M20 P4.4 percentile arm returned its 'fewer than 30 winners' abstention for every ict_scalp leg -- including one with 1,102 trades
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-10 from the census run 3 scalp shard, which printed
  ict_scalp_5m      meas=0/697
  ict_scalp_sol_5m  meas=0/915
  ict_scalp_xrp_5m  meas=0/748
  ict_scalp_avax_5m meas=0/1102
  ict_scalp_xrp_15m meas=0/361
-- 3,823 trades, ZERO capture readings.

CAUSE: two harness emit shapes. backtest_trend / backtest_pullback /
backtest_squeeze put mfe_r at the TOP LEVEL of the --emit-trades row;
backtest_ict_scalp nests it under `meta` beside mae_r / bars_held /
capital_bars (backtest_ict_scalp.py sets meta['mfe_r'], and the emit writer
serialises `"meta": t.meta`). Every consumer that re-derived the read did
the top-level lookup.

THE PART THAT REACHES BEYOND THE CENSUS: winner_mfe_p80 is the M20 P4.4
percentile arm -- it bakes the trail-percentile cell from the IS-window
winner-MFE distribution. Its contract says it returns None 'when < 30
winners'. Reading top-level it collected zero MFEs for every ict_scalp leg
and returned None, so the sweep recorded a legitimate-looking THIN-SAMPLE
abstention for legs with hundreds of winners. An inert arm that reports a
plausible reason to abstain is worse than one that errors, because the
caller books the abstention as data. This is the unasserted-denominator
class (CLAUDE.md, diagnostic provenance sub-class C) and a collapsed state
(the two causes of None were indistinguishable).

Verified end-to-end on real harness output before and after the fix:
backtest_ict_scalp.py --data data/backtest_candles.csv --emit-trades ->
4 rows, top-level mfe_r 0/4, meta.mfe_r 4/4; old reader 0 measured,
new reader 4 measured, and near-miss became computable
(target_r_reached_n=1, i.e. the scalp tp_at_r target IS operative -- unlike
the pullback tp_r: 50.0 sentinel).
items.fix:
PR #8721. (1) ONE accessor, exit_capture.mfe_r_of(row): top-level then
meta, non-dict meta safe; exit_capture.summarize uses it, so every capture
consumer is corrected at once. (2) winner_mfe_p80 reads through it and
counts winners_seen SEPARATELY from readable MFEs, so 'winners exist and
none carried a readable mfe_r' prints 'arm UNAVAILABLE (shape mismatch),
not thin sample' and can never masquerade as a thin sample; its bare
except now names the exception instead of swallowing it. (3) The census
flags any leg that traded with zero capture coverage on its own stdout
line, in a hoisted end-of-run list, in capture_census.json
(legs_zero_capture_coverage) and as a SUMMARY.md warning -- because run 3
printed meas=0/1102 as one column among five and it read as ordinary
output. (4) Regression tests: nested-shape rows must summarise non-zero
end-to-end, and a structural test pins that winner_mfe_p80 uses the
accessor and keeps the two None causes distinguishable.
items.follow_up:
Any M20 P4.4 trail-percentile cell recorded for an ict_scalp leg was baked
with the arm inert and should be re-derived, not trusted. Scope not yet
measured: check docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json for scalp legs
carrying a percentile-arm verdict.
