items.title: the trader tick takes 253s mean / 296s max, so every open live trade is evaluated once per ~5 MINUTES, not per TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS=60
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-10 05:53Z, the FIRST real reading of /api/diag/tick_cost (added 2026-08-09, one day earlier, explicitly because 'each hook is
individually bounded and documented as cheap; nothing measured the SUM').

  ticks_measured      13
  mean_ms        253583.9   (4.2 min of WORK per tick)
  max_ms         295641.5   (4.9 min)
  process_started 2026-08-10T03:44:37Z -> generated 04:51:34Z

Arithmetic reconciles: 4016.6s / 13 ticks = 308.9s per cycle, and
253.6s work + 60s sleep = 313.6s. Cross-checked against /api/diag/status:
last_tick_utc 04:50:02Z vs captured_at 04:53:03Z = 181s since the last
tick, consistent with a ~5-min cycle.

CONSEQUENCE: run_monitor_tick is called once per tick and is NOT gated by
strategy timeframe, so it is the tick cadence that bounds how often an
open live trade is re-evaluated. That is ~5 minutes, not 60s. Every
discretionary exit -- the break-even ratchet (monitor_breakeven_sl),
trail updates, the M20 stale/giveback levers -- inherits that latency.
The broker-side SL/TP bracket is unaffected (it rests at the exchange and
fires in real time), so this bounds DISCRETIONARY exits only.

NOTE THE TRAP: TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS is already 60 and lowering it changes
NOTHING -- the sleep is the small term. The cadence is dominated by the
tick's own work.

Small denominator stated honestly: 13 ticks, one process, counters reset on
restart. The wall-clock cross-check agrees, but a longer sample should
confirm before any capacity conclusion.
items.why_it_matters:
This is the shape of BOTH June 2026 wedges (MB-20260609-001 steady-state,
BL-20260609-001 cold-start): components individually cheap, the total never
watched, growing un-observed. tick_cost was built to catch exactly this and
its first reading is 253s. Nothing alerts on it -- the endpoint is
MEASUREMENT ONLY by design (a cap with no distribution behind it is the
exposure-ceiling mistake), so a human has to look, and until now nobody had.
items.next_step:
1. Get the PER-HOOK split. tick_cost measures the SUM only, so the 253s
   cannot currently be attributed -- designing a fix against a guess is the
   thing to avoid. Instrument per-hook timing before proposing anything.
2. Then decide between making the tick cheaper vs DECOUPLING position
   monitoring from the signal tick (a cheap loop touching only open
   positions: one journal read + one price read per open symbol). The
   operator asked 2026-08-10 for <=60s evaluation of every live trade;
   decoupling is the only route that gets there, since the 253s is
   signal-generation work across 52 strategies plus IB-paced fetches.
3. SEPARATELY and independently: the monitor already HAS intrabar data and
   discards it. monitor_breakeven_sl reads candles_df['close'].iloc[-1],
   but the fetched frame's last row is the FORMING bar (CCXT fetch_ohlcv,
   no trimming in fetch_candles or bybit_connector.get_ohlcv), so its
   high/low already carry the running intrabar extreme. Reading the extreme
   instead of the close arms the ratchet on a TOUCH and needs no cadence
   change at all. Tier-3 (order-path behaviour); backtest first.
items.next_action: NUMBER SUPERSEDED, CONCERN STILL LIVE — do not quote 253s. Re-measured 2026-08-12 over 96 ticks on one process: mean 107.9s / max 127.7s (was 253s/296s over 10 ticks, a much smaller denominator). The candle-cache + connector-memo work roughly halved it. The row's ACTUAL concern is unchanged and is the operator's bar: an open live trade is still evaluated once per ~108s, not per TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS=60. CONSOLIDATED: BL-20260810-TICK-CHAIN-260S-PER-TICK is the live row and carries the current measurement, the per-hook split (pipeline.signal_build 43.3%, monitor.strategy_monitor_loop 21.9%) and the open probe. This row is kept OPEN only for its framing — the cadence bar, which the other row states in seconds rather than in monitor-evaluations — but its NUMBER must not be cited. Two rows describing one condition with contradictory figures is the drift that makes a backlog stop being believed.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The specific harm — a live trade evaluated once per ~5 minutes because exit evaluation rode the 253s tick — is fixed by the M20 exit-loop decouple: src/main.py:327 `_exit_loop` runs exit evaluation on its own daemon thread, :321 sets EXIT_LOOP_INTERVAL_SECONDS default 30, :736-742 gates it on EXIT_LOOP_DECOUPLE_DISABLED as the one-env-flip rollback, and src/runtime/exit_loop_health.py:81 adds EXIT_EVAL_MAX_INTERVAL_SECONDS as a graded 60s requirement with a four-state requirement_state. — Successor risk, already tracked separately: CLAUDE.md records the worst observed inter-evaluation interval at 58.9 s against the 60 s requirement (n=694), i.e. 1.1 s of margin — BL-20260816-EXIT-EVAL-INTERVAL-AT-60S-REQUIREMENT and BL-20260816-IB-QUEUE-TIMEOUT-EXCEEDS-EXIT-BUDGET own that. Do not re-close those under this row.

items.title: scripts/backtest_ict_scalp.py had no --start/--end, so no ict_scalp verdict was ever IS/OOS split
items.detail: The fleet sweep passes --start/--end to every cell because the IS/OOS split is the gate's first stage; this harness rejected both with an argparse usage error, failing all seven scalp legs of the 2026-08-10 dispatch in under three minutes. Implication beyond the dispatch: every ict_scalp verdict on record is full-history, with no window split and therefore no walk-forward (the walk-forward only runs on cells that already cleared both windows). The capture census had passed on the same legs minutes earlier because a census windows nothing. RESOLVED: _date_filter added (tz-robust; a missing timestamp column with a window requested RAISES rather than returning full history under an IS/OOS label; a zero-bar window exits non-zero), main()'s parser extracted to build_parser(), and a test now checks the sweep's own scalp argv against that parser in-process.
items.evidence: PR #8721; run 31359385806 (7/7 harness_error); verified partition on data/backtest_candles.csv: full 4 trades/-0.6535R = IS 1/-0.1210 + OOS 3/-0.5325

items.title: A push-fired sweep sentinel described a scalp run and dispatched the donchian default
items.detail: A push carries no workflow_dispatch inputs, so inputs.legs was empty and the plan job fell through to the ten-leg census DEFAULT while the sentinel file's prose described a scalp-family run in four paragraphs. Nothing in the pipeline compares a sentinel's stated intent to the matrix it produces, so it was caught by cancelling the run, not by the run complaining; the cancelled jobs posted 'no SUMMARY' comments under leg names the sentinel never mentioned. Unprovenanced diagnostic output, sub-class B (implicit input selection). RESOLVED: the sentinel's `legs:` line is read by the plan job and is authoritative for the run it fires; precedence (dispatch input > sentinel > census default) is logged, not inferred.

items.title: A naive intrabar exit-evaluation arm would peek at the future and manufacture an improvement
items.detail: scripts/backtest_trend.py::run_backtest advances ext/mfe/trail from the WHOLE leg bar's extreme and THEN evaluates the giveback/stale levers at that bar's close. Sound while the lever is evaluated once per bar. The moment a lever is evaluated at a SUB-BAR close inside that bar, the comparison is against a peak that may be set later in the same bar - the rule appears to exit at the top with uncanny timing, the arm beats baseline, and the result is an artifact. Contract for the build: ext/mfe/trail advance on the SUB-BAR clock; bar-counted params (stale_exit_bars, trail_decay_stall_bars, peak_j) stay on the LEG-BAR clock or every threshold is silently redefined; and run THREE arms (baseline / levers-fine-with-SL-first-at-leg-grain / everything-fine) because a finer grain also converts some SL-first bars into target-first, which would credit the lever for the convention. Applies to the operator's 2026-08-10 intrabar-monitor directive.
items.evidence: docs/live-exit-monitor-cadence-DESIGN.md sec 4.1; scripts/backtest_trend.py:480-560

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: scripts/backtest_trend.py:505-526 confirms the filed mechanic: ext/mfe/trail advance from the WHOLE leg bar's high/low (`if bh > ext: ... ext = max(ext, bh)`, `trail = max(trail, ext - _effective_trail_mult(...))`) and the levers are evaluated at that bar's close. No sub-bar/intrabar arm exists anywhere in the file (grep intrabar: only the :15 convention comment). — Nothing to fix — this is a standing design contract for work that has not started (the operator's 2026-08-10 intrabar-monitor directive). Ends when an intrabar arm is built and honours the three-arm contract, or the directive is dropped.
Re-validated: a documented trap to avoid, not a defect to fix. Keep as a design constraint on any intrabar arm.

items.summary: m20_fleet_exit_sweep's `config-exact` base omitted the trail-VOL lever. `base_args::declared_levers()` threaded stale/giveback/trail-DECAY but not `trail_vol_{above,below}_pctl`/`trail_vol_tight_mult`, while both harnesses carried the flags. Exactly two census legs declare an ARMED vol-trail lever - trend_donchian_eth (below 0.1/tight 2.5) and qqq_pullback_1h (above 0.8/tight 2.5) - so their sweep deltas were measured against a baseline missing a lever that is armed in live. Both A/B arms omitted it, so each delta is internally consistent; what is unverified is its transport to the live book, since exit levers interact. Consequence: 2 of the 3 live-leg Path A winners in the 2026-08-10 promotion packet are HELD pending a re-run on the corrected base.
items.evidence: Found while reading config/strategies.yaml to write the Tier-3 packet - the same read also corrected two FALSE 'inert lever' findings I had published (trend_donchian_eth's vol-trail and avax_pullback_2h's decay lever are both armed). Easy to miss because `vol_pctl_window` WAS threaded - it belongs to the entry vol-skip gate, not the trail.
items.fix: declared_levers() now threads the three trail_vol_* keys. tests/test_m20_fleet_capital_report.py asserts per-leg completeness against config/strategies.yaml, plus a companion test that fails on any new lever-shaped YAML key with no harness-flag mapping. Positive control run: reverting the fix reproduces exactly the two legs and four keys.
items.outcome_measured: RE-RUN COMPLETE (GH run 31414856214, both legs). The defect was OUTCOME-CHANGING, not cosmetic. On trend_donchian_eth BOTH Path A winners died: decay_stall10_t2.5 went PASS (dNetR IS +7.49, dMaxDD -7.77) -> is_oos_fail (dNetR IS -1.00, dMaxDD +5.96) - the IS SIGN FLIPPED; stale12_lt0R went PASS -> wf_fail (still clears both windows, now fails the yearly folds). The Tier-3 promotion packet drops from 3 live-leg winners to 1. Self-verifying: the two cells that merely RE-DECLARE each leg's existing lever (trend_donchian_eth vt_cold10_t2.5, qqq_pullback_1h vt_hot80_t2.5) now correctly read tie_no_improvement with 0.0 on every axis - under the broken base they read as improvements. Two independent legs, same signature.

items.summary: scripts/ml/ is a REGULAR package and shadows the repo's top-level ml/ whenever scripts/ precedes the repo root on sys.path - which is the default, since Python puts a script's own directory at sys.path[0]. backtest_ict_scalp.py / backtest_pullback.py used insert-if-absent, so under PYTHONPATH=<repo root> (how pytest-run.yml runs the suite) the insert was skipped and the harness died on `No module named 'ml.predictors'` before argparse ran.
items.evidence: Reddened pytest-run on PR #8721. Matters beyond CI: the fleet sweep reports a harness that cannot start as `harness_error` on every cell, which in a summary table is indistinguishable from 'the harness ran and found nothing'.
items.fix: Both harnesses now REPOSITION the repo root ahead of scripts/ rather than inserting if absent. tests/test_ict_scalp_exit_levers.py starts each harness under PYTHONPATH=<repo root>. Measured after the fix: 0 of 333 scripts under scripts/ fail with the shadowing signature; probe validated against a positive (restoring the old ordering makes it fire).

items.summary: m20_fleet_exit_sweep::base_args read cfg keys `trend_len` and `pullback_len` that NO strategy has ever declared - the YAML says `trend_lookback` / `pullback_lookback`. `opt()` passes nothing when the key is absent, so the flags were dropped and backtest_pullback substituted its OWN defaults (40 / 10 / 0.5). Unlike the trail-vol gap this is ENTRY geometry: it changes which trades exist at all, not just how they exit.
items.evidence: Measured across all 19 pullback legs in config/strategies.yaml: 11 legs diverge from the harness defaults, 23 individual key divergences. spy/qqq/tlt/gld `_1h` declare trend_lookback 60 + pullback_lookback 12; the `_1d` metals declare pullback_lookback 15; several declare pullback_frac 0.618; ief_pullback_1d declares trend_lookback 30. Those legs' sweep results were produced on entry geometry the live leg does not use. Legs that MATCH the defaults are unaffected - incl. eth_pullback_2h and avax_pullback_2h (both 40/10/0.5), the two pullback legs in the 2026-08-10 promotion, so that promotion is NOT affected.
items.fix: Key names corrected. New general test test_every_cfg_key_base_args_reads_is_declared_by_some_strategy asserts every cfg key base_args reads is declared by at least one strategy - a key no leg declares is dead, and a dead read fails SILENTLY rather than raising. It cannot catch a key threaded to the wrong flag, but it catches every key that is not real. Positive control: restoring `trend_len` reproduces the failure naming that key.
items.followup: Any pullback-leg sweep verdict recorded BEFORE 2026-08-10 for one of the 11 diverging legs should be re-measured before it is cited; the affected 2026-08-10 packet entries are spy_pullback_1h and qqq_pullback_1h, both of which were REJECTIONS, so nothing was promoted on them.

items.title: FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=0.15 and FLIP_MIN_POSITION_AGE_HOURS=4.0 are LIVE on the trader — a Tier-3 order-routing override that CLAUDE.md documents as default-off and 'requires operator approval before deploying', with no authorization record I can find
items.checked: checked: issue #8755 (get-env ALL against ict-trader-live.service, reading /proc/<MainPID>/environ AND the unit's declared env) plus CLAUDE.md's env table, docs/research/M26-regime-transition-conflict-DESIGN.md, and comms/reports/daily/20260717T055600Z/report.md
items.source: Surfaced by the first successful run of the new get-env read surface — the exact class of finding it was built to make visible.
items.what_to_check:
MEASURED on the live trader, both sides agreeing (so this is not a pending-restart artifact):
  FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD  process '0.15'  declared '0.15'
  FLIP_MIN_POSITION_AGE_HOURS process '4.0'  declared '4.0'
  FLIP_POLICY                 process <unset> declared <unset>  -> defaults to 'hold'

WHAT THE DOCS SAY. CLAUDE.md's env table, verbatim, for FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD: "Default `0.0` — **disabled, hold-policy behaviour is unchanged**" and "**Requires operator approval (Tier-3 order-routing change) before deploying.**" For FLIP_MIN_POSITION_AGE_HOURS: "Default `0.0`".

docs/research/M26-regime-transition-conflict-DESIGN.md line 45 lists BOTH as "Dormant flip-override knobs ... built, default-off, Tier-3" and "already implemented, NEVER VALIDATED".

The 2026-07-17 system report (comms/reports/daily/20260717T055600Z/report.md:19,31) states the threshold "is 0.0 = disabled" and RECOMMENDS backtesting a small positive value. So as of 2026-07-17 it was off; it is on now.

WHAT THIS DOES. With FLIP_POLICY at its 'hold' default, an opposing signal is normally refused and the position rides to its stop. These two knobs re-open that path: a new signal whose confidence exceeds the held position's entry confidence by >= 0.15, on a position older than 4h, OVERRIDES the hold and flips (close + reopen opposite). Both conditions must hold, so it is narrow — but it is a live order-routing behaviour on EVERY account including real money, not a demo-scoped one like CONVICTION_SIZING_ACCOUNTS.
items.why_critical:
This is a Tier-3 order-path setting whose own documentation says it must not be deployed without operator approval, running with a non-default value. Under 'field beats comment' the field is the truth and the doc gets fixed — but that rule presumes the field's state was INTENDED. A Tier-3 order-routing override is exactly where 'it was already like that' is not an acceptable disposition, because the same reasoning would have accepted the MULTI_SYMBOL_ENABLED and netting-guard regressions.

Note the asymmetry with the sibling finding from the same run: CONVICTION_SIZING_ACCOUNTS came back 'bybit_1', matching ROADMAP.md M16 exactly — authorized, demo-scoped, correct. This one has no such record. That contrast is the argument for the read surface existing at all: one run distinguished a correctly-scoped Tier-3 setting from an unrecorded one, and neither was checkable before tonight.
items.limits_of_this_check: STATED PLAINLY so the next reader does not over-trust it. I searched ROADMAP.md, docs/sprint-logs/*.md and docs/claude/*.md for either variable name and found NOTHING. I did NOT and cannot check: the .env's own edit history (it is not in git), the operator's Telegram/chat history, or any approval given in a session whose log I have not read. So the honest claim is 'no authorization record exists in the repo', NOT 'this was unauthorized'. It may well have been an approved experiment that was never written down — which is itself worth fixing, because an undocumented Tier-3 flip is indistinguishable from an unauthorized one.
items.next_action:
OPERATOR DECISION, deliberately not enacted (Tier-3, and the operator is asleep):
(1) Was this deliberate? If YES -> record it: CLAUDE.md's env table still says default-off/'requires approval before deploying', ROADMAP.md has no entry, and the M26 design doc still calls both knobs dormant and never-validated. All three need correcting, with the approval date and the evidence that cleared the gate.
(2) If NO -> this is an unauthorized live order-routing change; the rollback is FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=0.0 via set-env + restart (Tier-2), which restores pure hold-policy behaviour.
(3) Either way, ask what the M26 design doc asks: has a walk-forward ever validated a positive threshold? The doc says never. A live Tier-3 order-routing knob with no validation behind it is the shape regime-selectivity's 'walk-forward-before-Tier-3' rule exists to prevent.
items.resolution_criteria: The live value and the canonical docs agree, and the authorization (or the rollback) is recorded.
items.resolution:
RESOLVED — disposition (1): the operator confirmed 2026-08-11 that the flip-override values are deliberate. No rollback. The finding was 'no authorization record in the repo', which was accurate; the record now exists.

Docs corrected to match reality, all three that contradicted it:
  * CLAUDE.md — both env rows now state the LIVE values (0.15 / 4.0), the operator confirmation + date, and the combined effect; the stale 'default 0.0 = disabled' framing is explicitly flagged as not describing live routing.
  * docs/research/M26-regime-transition-conflict-DESIGN.md:45 — the knobs were listed as 'Dormant ... built, default-off'; they are LIVE, and P3's job changes from 'propose enabling' to 'measure the arm already running'.
  * ROADMAP.md M26 — the row asserted 'No live change before P3 beats the incumbent hold policy out-of-sample'. A live change WAS made before that gate. Corrected in place rather than quietly dropped, because a roadmap that overstates its own gate-keeping is worse than one that admits an exception.

WHAT IS NOT RESOLVED, and is deliberately split out rather than closed with this item: approval is not validation. No walk-forward has ever tested a positive threshold. Tracked as BL-20260811-FLIP-OVERRIDE-NEVER-WALKFORWARDED.

items.title: The live flip-override (FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=0.15 / FLIP_MIN_POSITION_AGE_HOURS=4.0) has now been walk-forwarded and LOSES: -$1,280 over 34 fires (79% of net), never improves drawdown in any cell -- Tier-3 recommendation to disarm is with the operator
items.checked: checked THIS SESSION: both fold-job logs of run 31523739722 read end-to-end (the numbers above are transcribed from them, not from a summary); scripts/backtest_system.py's `hold` branch read in full -- it was a bare `pass`, so the backlog row's original premise ('the harness exists, this is a run not a build') was WRONG and the arm had to be built before it could be run; the built arm calls the LIVE src/runtime/intents._evaluate_confidence_override rather than mirroring its logic; 13 hermetic tests, verified against a planted defect (the first plant PASSED all 13 and the atomicity assertion was added because of it). NOT checked: any symbol other than BTCUSDT, any roster other than 4mem, and the tf_class split (captured in the artifacts, not surfaced -- see next_action).
items.source: Split from BL-20260810-FLIP-CONFIDENCE-OVERRIDE-LIVE-WITHOUT-RECORD when the operator confirmed the values were deliberate. Approval closed the authorization question; it does not close the evidence question.
items.what_to_check:
RESOLVED-ON-EVIDENCE 2026-08-11. Full write-up: docs/research/flip-override-walkforward-2026-08-11.md. Runner .github/workflows/flip-override-walkforward.yml, run 31523739722, both fold jobs success.

POPULATION (state it before the number): BTCUSDT 5m, 2020-06-01 -> 2026-02-28, Binance-vision, 604,512 rows; roster `4mem`; the May walk-forward's own folds (A train 2020-06..2023-12 / oos 2024-01..2026-02; B train 2022-01..2024-06 / oos 2024-07..2026-02); account $10k, risk 0.3%/trade. THE ARM FIRED 34 TIMES (13/6/11/4) -- this is a measured result, not an untested arm; a `fired: 0` row would have been the incumbent under another name.

  cell      hold net   confgap net   d net    hold maxDD%   cf maxDD%   d maxDD   fired
  A/train      $672          $113    -$559           8.20       11.04     +2.84      13
  A/oos        $242          $180     -$62           9.23        9.23      0.00       6
  B/train     $1157          $445    -$712           5.55        7.60     +2.05      11
  B/oos       -$449         -$396     +$53           8.67        8.67      0.00       4
  TOTAL      $1,622          $342  -$1,280                                            34

Worse on net in 3/4 cells. Worse on maxDD in 2/4, identical in 2/4, BETTER in 0/4 -- there is no 'worse PnL but safer' trade-off to weigh. Both TRAIN halves (the largest samples, 13 and 11 fires) are worse on BOTH axes simultaneously. The single positive cell is B/oos +$53 on 4 fires with maxDD identical and the book losing money either way (-$449 vs -$396): that is what a null effect looks like, not OOS support.

This CONFIRMS the repo's existing prior rather than contradicting it -- docs/research/M26-P1-conflict-taxonomy-2026-07-22.md:203 already lists this exact arm as `A_confgap_flip`, 'Demoted by P0 (same-clock flip lost -$7.1k)'. The design doc demoted it on theory; this measures it and agrees.
items.why_critical:
Raised medium -> high on the measurement. The evidence question the row was opened to answer is now answered, and it answered against the live arm: an unvalidated override is displacing a walk-forward-validated incumbent AND costing money on the only population it has ever been tested on. It remains live on every account including real money.

Severity is high but the row is not an alarm: the operator approved these values knowingly, the gate is narrow (>=0.15 confidence gap AND >4h age), and the absolute cost is small on a $10k model account. What makes it high is that nothing now argues FOR the arm.
items.next_action:
TIER-3, PROPOSED NOT ENACTED -- the operator's call. Recommendation: disarm by setting FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=0.0 on the live VM (one env flip + restart, no redeploy; FLIP_MIN_POSITION_AGE_HOURS becomes inert automatically since it only gates a positive threshold). Routing returns to the walk-forward-validated `hold`.

TWO THINGS THIS RUN DID NOT ANSWER, both cheap now the harness exists:
(1) THE M26 tf_ratio SPLIT IS CAPTURED BUT NOT REPORTED. The conflict ledger records `tf_class` (cross_clock / same_clock / unknown) per conflict and `by_tf_class` per run, but the workflow summary does not print it and the MCP cannot download run artifacts -- so 'does it lose on same-clock specifically?', the question M26 P0 says is decisive, is open. If the loss turns out confined to same_clock and the arm is positive on cross_clock, the right move is a TF-AWARE gate (M26's A_coexist_crossclock), not the current TF-blind one. BUILT 2026-08-11 (follow-up PR): the summary now prints a per-cell TF-class table, AND the split is no longer only a report -- two counterfactual ARMS (`hold_confgap_crossclock` / `hold_confgap_sameclock`) run the same live predicate restricted to one class, so the question gets an A/B on the same cells rather than a post-hoc PnL attribution that could not be checked. Each conflict now records `would_fire_tf_blind` beside `override_fired`, so the live fires a TF-aware gate would REMOVE are countable. Awaiting the run.
(2) ONE SYMBOL, ONE ROSTER. BTCUSDT + 4mem only; the live override applies to every symbol and account. A per-symbol run could still show the arm winning on legs this did not cover.

ALSO FIX (workflow defect found in this run): the driver prints 'Verdict: ... Overall: FAIL' in each fold job, which is an ARTIFACT -- _evaluate_pass_criteria spans both folds while the matrix runs one fold per job, so the other fold's cells are always missing_cell => automatic FAIL; the criteria also test hold-vs-reverse (the May question), not the override. FIXED 2026-08-11 (same PR): the verdict is scoped to the folds/rosters/arms actually in the run and is now THREE-state -- pass / fail / NOT TESTED (`pass: null` + `applicable: false`), with `overall_pass: null` when nothing was applicable and an exit code that does not report untested as failed. It was the repo's own collapsed-state class inside a research tool. New test module tests/test_walkforward_flip_verdict.py (there was none, which is why it shipped); all three fixes plant-verified.
items.resolution_criteria: The walk-forward exists (DONE 2026-08-11). Row closes when the operator has decided on the Tier-3 recommendation -- disarm, keep, or make TF-aware -- and the decision plus its rationale is recorded against the FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD row in CLAUDE.md.
items.description: Walk-forwarded 2026-08-11. The arm fired 34 times across 4 cells and cost -$1,280 (79% of net), worse on net in 3/4 cells, worse on maxDD in 2/4 and better in 0/4. Confirms M26 P1's prior demotion of the same arm. Tier-3 recommendation to disarm (FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=0.0) is with the operator; the row stays open until they decide. Two follow-ups: surface the captured tf_class split, and fix the fold-matrix verdict artifact.
items.evidence: docs/research/flip-override-walkforward-2026-08-11.md
items.resolution:
OPERATOR DECIDED: DISARM. Tier-3 approval granted in-conversation 2026-08-11; enacted the same day and VERIFIED on the running process, not just the file.

WHAT WAS DONE: set-env FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD=0.0 on ict-bot-arm + ict-trader-live restart (issue #8785, run 31531849716, 20:14:09Z). FLIP_MIN_POSITION_AGE_HOURS deliberately LEFT at 4.0 -- it is inert while the threshold is 0 (_evaluate_confidence_override returns at `threshold <= 0` before the age check), and clearing both would make a future re-arm ambiguous about which value was the tested one.

items.title: [exits] the M20 Path A gate has no minimum trade count: 9 of 21 fleet PASSes sit on an OOS base under 20 trades
items.summary: m20_fleet_exit_sweep::beats plus the walk-forward decide which exit-lever cells get PROPOSED for promotion, and neither requires a minimum number of trades. Measured over the 43-leg fleet corpus, 9 of the 21 Path A PASSes rest on an out-of-sample base of fewer than 20 trades, and spy_trend_long_1d has FOUR PASSes on a three-trade window.
items.evidence: checked: docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl (575 cells / 43 legs, run 2026-08-10) and scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py. PASSes by OOS base n: spy_trend_long_1d n=3 (4 PASSes), qqq_trend_long_1d n=4 (2), scha_trend_long_1d n=5 (3), uso_trend_1h n=27 (1), gld_pullback_1h n=31 (1), trend_donchian_xrp_4h n=32 (2), trend_donchian_avax_4h n=34 (6), mgc_trend_1h n=97 (1), trend_donchian_1h n=168 (1). items.title: Does the flip-override lose on BOTH M26 TF classes, or only same-clock? The counterfactual arms are running; the answer decides whether a TF-AWARE re-arm is worth proposing
items.source: Split out of BL-20260811-FLIP-OVERRIDE-NEVER-WALKFORWARDED when that row resolved (operator disarmed the override 2026-08-11). The disarm is settled and this does not reopen it -- the override is OFF and the question is only whether a NARROWER version earns a future re-arm proposal.
items.what_to_check: GitHub Actions run 31529876774 (workflow flip-override-walkforward.yml), folds A+B in parallel, four arms: hold / hold_confgap / hold_confgap_crossclock / hold_confgap_sameclock, BTCUSDT 4mem. Job 93907088540 = fold A, 93907088507 = fold B. Read BOTH job logs end-to-end (get_job_logs, return_content) -- do not read a summary and call it measured. Pull: per-cell net/maxDD/fired for all four arms; the 'Conflicts by M26 TF class' table, especially suppressed_by_tf_filter (on a restricted arm that is the count of LIVE fires a TF-aware gate would remove -- it IS the measurement). Reconciliation: cross-only fires + same-only fires need NOT equal the blind arm's, and the shortfall should be the `unknown` bucket; divergence for any OTHER reason is a defect, not a finding.
items.why_critical: Not critical -- it is a re-arm question on a knob that is now OFF, which is why this is severity low and not high like its parent row. Logged because the run outlives the session that dispatched it, and an unread result is how a measured answer rots into 'nobody ever checked'.
items.next_action:
DECISION RULE, FIXED IN ADVANCE so it cannot be fitted to the result: propose a TF-aware re-arm (M26 A_coexist_crossclock) ONLY if cross-clock-only beats PLAIN `hold` on net AND does not worsen maxDD. Beating the blind arm is NOT sufficient -- the blind arm loses, so clearing it proves nothing. If the loss shows up in both classes, the disarm stands and gets stronger, and this row closes as 'no re-arm warranted'. State the population and the per-class fire counts before any conclusion: a class with 2 fires is not a finding. PROPOSE, DO NOT ENACT -- any re-arm is Tier-3 and needs the operator.

MEASUREMENT LIMIT that survives whatever this run says: BTCUSDT + 4mem only, while the override applied to every symbol and account. A per-symbol run could still show the arm winning on legs neither run covered.
items.resolution_criteria: Both fold logs read end-to-end, the per-class fire counts and net/maxDD stated with their population, and either (a) a Tier-3 TF-aware re-arm proposal put to the operator against the rule above, or (b) this row closed as 'no re-arm warranted -- the loss is present in both TF classes'. Recorded in docs/research/flip-override-walkforward-2026-08-11.md either way.
items.resolution: NO RE-ARM WARRANTED — the loss is present in BOTH TF classes. Run 31529876774 completed (success); both fold job logs read end-to-end (93907088540 fold A, 93907088507 fold B). POPULATION: BTCUSDT 5m, 604,512 bars, 2020-06-01 -> 2026-02-28 (binance-vision), roster 4mem, arm at the LIVE gap 0.15 / age 4.0h. AGAINST THE FIXED RULE: cross-clock-only does NOT beat plain `hold` — it loses in 3 of 4 cells (A train $446 vs $672; A oos $186 vs $242; B train $789 vs $1,157; B oos -$390 vs -$449), aggregate $1,031 vs $1,622 = -$591, AND it worsens maxDD in both train halves (10.12% vs 8.20%; 6.49% vs 5.55%). Its single winning cell is B/OOS on ONE fire inside a losing book — not a finding at n=1. Same-clock-only loses in all four cells ($683 aggregate). PER-CLASS FIRE COUNTS (the denominators): cross-only 9/3/7/1 = 20 fires, same-only 7/3/6/3 = 19. suppressed_by_tf_filter (live fires a TF-aware gate would remove): cross-only 20, same-only 38. M26 P0's prediction that cross-TF is the LESS BAD class is confirmed — cross-only beats the TF-blind arm by +$689 ($1,031 vs $342) — and that is precisely the comparison the pre-fixed rule refuses: the blind arm loses, so losing less clears nothing. RECONCILIATION: `unknown` is 0 in every cell (verified by arithmetic — each arm's conflicts equal cross+same exactly), so no unknown bucket can absorb a difference. Both OOS halves reconcile exactly (3+3=6, 1+3=4); both TRAIN halves show an EXCESS not a shortfall (16 vs 13, 13 vs 11). NOT a defect: the cross-only arm's fires equal the blind arm's cross-class fires in ALL FOUR cells (9/9, 3/3, 7/7, 1/1), so the filter under test is exact; all divergence is in the same-only arm on the train halves, where it suppresses the majority of the blind arm's fires (9 of 13, 7 of 11) and perturbs the position path hardest — its own conflict population moves with it (A/train same-clock 45 vs 37). That is the already-documented post-first-fire path divergence, now measured: the identity holds where paths stay close (the shorter OOS halves) and opens where they diverge. The disarm therefore stands and gets stronger. Nothing was enacted (Tier-3); no proposal is put to the operator because the rule's precondition failed. LIMIT THAT SURVIVES: BTCUSDT + 4mem only — a per-symbol run could still show a winning leg neither run covered; a re-arm would need that AND a cross-clock arm clearing plain `hold` on net and maxDD. Recorded in docs/research/flip-override-walkforward-2026-08-11.md § 'The M26 TF-class split — ANSWERED'.

items.title: status-check prints a 2-month-old heartbeat mtime under 'runtime_logs canonical files' and skips its env dump saying 'trader pid not found' -- while the trader is demonstrably running in the same output
items.source:
Observed in system-action status-check #8788 (run 31532187508, 2026-08-11T20:18Z), dispatched to confirm the trader was healthy after the FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD restart. Two defects in ONE output, both of the repo's own UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT class (CLAUDE.md section 'Diagnostic provenance'):

(1) SUB-CLASS C, unasserted denominator. The section '--- runtime-data path diagnostic ---' printed '(trader pid not found or /proc unreadable -- env dump skipped)' and again '(trader pid not found or /proc/<pid>/cwd unreadable)'. The SAME report's ps output lists the trader at PID 402857 with 231s elapsed, and systemctl reports ict-trader-live active. So the process was there and the lookup failed -- but the message collapses 'we could not look' and 'it is not there' into one string, which is exactly the distinction the collapsed-states rule exists for.

(2) SUB-CLASS A/B, semantic substitution. Directly above it, '--- runtime_logs canonical files (repo path) ---' printed heartbeat.txt with mtime 2026-06-14 -- TWO MONTHS STALE -- because the live heartbeat is at /data/bot-data/runtime_logs/ (DATA_DIR) and the repo-path copy has been dead since the Ampere cutover. The label does say 'repo path', but a reader skimming a health check for a stale heartbeat can read that line as the answer. The report's own '===== heartbeat =====' section correctly showed the /data/bot-data file at age 42s. One output, two heartbeat mtimes, 2 months apart, no line saying which one governs.
items.what_to_check: scripts/ops/status_check.sh -- the pid-resolution for the runtime-data path diagnostic (why it fails while ps and systemctl both see the process; likely a pgrep pattern that does not match the venv ExecStart '/home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/.venv/bin/python -u -B -m src.main' installed by the venv.conf drop-in), and the repo-path file listing.

The pid lookup also silently drops the DATA_DIR env dump, which is the part that would diagnose a path-bifurcation incident -- the very failure class status-check grew that section for.

items.title: m20-exit-lever-sweep's corpus job pushes straight to main and branch protection rejects it -- every sweep's durable corpus row is lost
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-12, run 31647462929 (9 legs, live-parity re-sweep). All 9 sweep jobs succeeded and the corpus job's 'Merge this run into the corpus' step succeeded -- only 'Commit the corpus' failed, on all 4 retry attempts:
    remote: error: GH006: Protected branch update failed for refs/heads/main.
    remote: - 3 of 3 required status checks are expected.
    ! [remote rejected] HEAD -> main (protected branch hook declined)
The job does `git push` to main directly. Branch protection on main requires 3 status checks, and a direct push presents none, so the push can NEVER succeed -- this is not a race that a retry can win, which is why all 4 attempts failed identically.

CONSEQUENCE: docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl -- the durable, queryable record of every swept cell, and the population the Path B threshold work is supposed to be set from -- receives NOTHING from any sweep run. The per-leg results survive only as artifacts (90-day retention) and as comments posted onto whatever PR happens to be associated with the dispatch SHA. For run 31647462929 that was PR #8814, an ALREADY-MERGED doc PR, purely because it was the PR attached to main's HEAD commit.

WHY IT IS NOT SILENT (the one good part): the job fails loudly and the workflow author had already hardened the neighbouring failure mode -- an earlier version exited 0 when the corpus file was untracked, reporting 'nothing to commit' over a run that had produced everything. That fix is intact; this is a different, later failure.
items.why_critical: The corpus is the evidence base for a decision that has not been made yet: Path B's two thresholds are deliberately UNSET pending a measured net_r_per_capital_day distribution, and that distribution is supposed to accumulate IN THIS FILE. Sweeps that cannot write to it look successful, report per-leg verdicts, and leave the corpus exactly as it was -- so the distribution never accrues and the thresholds stay unsettable, with nothing anywhere connecting the two facts.
items.what_to_check: gh run view <sweep run id> --job corpus, or read docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl's git log: confirm whether any row has landed since branch protection began requiring checks. Cross-check the corpus row count against the number of legs swept across all runs -- if the corpus is short by whole runs, this is the reason.
items.next_action: Route the corpus commit through the repo's existing sanctioned path instead of a direct push: .github/workflows/claude-pr-automerge.yml already exists for exactly this (push to a claude/** branch touching .github/pr-automerge-request -> PR -> required checks -> auto-merge). That keeps branch protection intact rather than working around it. A weaker alternative is to have the corpus job open a PR of its own. Do NOT 'fix' this by exempting the bot from branch protection -- the checks are the reason main is trustworthy.
items.resolution_criteria:
SATISFIED 2026-08-13. The criterion was written as 'rows reach main through a PR opened by claude-pr-automerge.yml' -- and that second clause is IMPOSSIBLE, not merely unmet: a GITHUB_TOKEN push starts no workflows (BL-20260813-CORPUS-RETARGET-CANNOT-OPEN-ITS-OWN-PR). Leaving it would have made this row uncloseable by construction, which is a worse failure than the bug.

The criterion this row is actually ABOUT -- rows are no longer discarded at the push step -- IS met and measured: default-branch dispatch run 31657293634 retargeted onto claude/m20-sweep-corpus and preserved 72 rows (736 -> 808), where the four pre-fix runs (31647462929, 31648068353, 31648088122, 31648666524) each discarded every row. Merged to main as PR #8865.

The remaining manual PR-open step is tracked separately in the new row rather than held against this one -- they are different defects with different fixes.
items.resolution:
FIXED 2026-08-12 in .github/workflows/m20-exit-lever-sweep.yml (corpus job, 'Commit the corpus'). Three separate defects, because the retry loop was hiding the other two:
  (1) TARGET. A dispatch whose ref is the default branch is now RETARGETED onto 'claude/m20-sweep-corpus' and writes .github/pr-automerge-request, so claude-pr-automerge.yml opens the PR and merges it on green. The corpus reaches main through CI rather than by weakening the protection that refused it.
  (2) CLASSIFICATION. A GH006/protected-branch decline is structural, not a race, so it now fails IMMEDIATELY and names the fix instead of burning 4 backoff attempts. Retrying it is what made four separate runs read as flaky pushes rather than as one reproducible cause.
  (3) APPEND-MERGE. A rebase conflict on the append-only corpus now re-derives the UNION by re-running the extractor over the still-present sweep_out/ on top of the other side's copy, instead of aborting and dropping this run's rows -- which would have discarded evidence for the same reason the push did.
Scope was wider than this item recorded: FOUR runs were lost, not one -- 31647462929, 31648068353, 31648088122, 31648666524, each 11/12 jobs green with all ten wave-2 vol_trail legs swept and every artifact uploaded.
VERIFIED BY SIMULATION ONLY so far (git stubbed, 4 cases: retarget-and-push; still-declined fails in 0s not 30s; a claude/** dispatch does NOT retarget and does NOT create the request file; rebase-conflict re-derives the union WITH the automerge opt-in surviving the hard reset). That last case caught a real bug in the fix as written -- `git reset --hard` deletes a staged-but-new file, so the branch would have been pushed with no PR ever opened, which looks like success. NOT yet exercised against a real protected-branch dispatch; closing this item requires that.

items.title: A cell too thin for the single-split OOS gate is refused the walk-forward, whose folds span the full history it CAN support -- so low-frequency legs are ungradeable by construction
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-12/13, PR #8849, two sweeps over the same 8 daily legs (runs 31655236776 @ split 2025-07-01, 31655318804 @ split 2023-01-01).

m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:1442-1451 orders the gates:
    if _thin:            -> verdict=insufficient_base   (walk-forward SKIPPED)
    elif candidate:      -> walkforward(...)
    elif is_path_b_...:  -> walkforward(...)
The skip is deliberate and its comment gives the reason: 'it would be measuring the same too-thin book, and it is the expensive step.'

THAT REASON DOES NOT HOLD, and the divergence is measurable. `_thin` is computed from the POST-SPLIT OOS window only. The walk-forward does not use that window -- its folds span the whole history. The one cell in these runs that reached it (uso_trend_1h/vt_cold10_t2) ran SIX folds, 2021 through 2026, 4/6 ok. So for a high-frequency leg the two denominators roughly agree, and for a low-frequency leg they diverge by an order of magnitude:

  leg                  OOS n @2025-07  OOS n @2023-01  lifetime trades
  iwm_trend_long_1d           5              16              73
  mes_trend_long_1d           4              12              33
  qld_trend_long_1d           6              21              57
  qqq_trend_long_1d           4              15              79
  scha_trend_long_1d          5              15              68
  splg_trend_long_1d          4              16              77
  spy_trend_long_1d           3              13              60
  tqqq_trend_long_1d          8              27              74   <- only one that clears

A 60-79-trade leg is refused a 6-fold all-history test on the grounds that its 3-8-trade post-split window is too thin. The floor is right about the single-split comparison and is then used to terminate the cell entirely.

MOVING THE SPLIT IS NOT THE FIX -- that was tested, not assumed. At 2023-01-01 seven of the eight are STILL under the floor (12-21) while IS shrinks (mes drops to IS=20). Only tqqq crosses, at 27, and it returns is_oos_fail there too.
items.impact: 8 vol_trail cells recorded `blocked` rather than closed, and the shape generalises: any 1d leg in the matrix meets the same wall on any lever. This is a live share of the M20 done-condition, not a rounding error -- blocked cells went 6 -> 13 on this finding alone.
items.suggested_fix:
Run the walk-forward when the OOS window is thin but the leg's LIFETIME trade count supports N usable folds, and record the verdict as fold-based, kept DISTINCT from a single-split verdict (never silently merged -- they answer different questions over different populations). Gate the fold-based verdict on its own minimum usable-fold count rather than reusing MIN_OOS_TRADES, which is a statistic about a window.

NOT actioned here on purpose: this changes the evidentiary standard by which a live exit lever is judged, which is the operator's call, not a research-tooling edit. Queued for the 2026-08-13 morning review alongside the two Tier-3 lever proposals.
items.resolution_criteria: A sweep row exists in docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl for a leg whose base_trades_OOS is under MIN_OOS_TRADES and whose `wf_ran` is true, carrying a fold-based verdict in a field DISTINCT from the single-split `verdict` — and the 7 cells this row blocked (iwm/mes/qld/qqq/scha/splg/spy _trend_long_1d vol_trail in docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json) have moved off `blocked` to a status citing that fold-based verdict. If the operator instead decides low-frequency legs are not gradeable, closing requires that decision recorded in the matrix legend or the exit-refinement skill, so the 7 cells stop reading as work someone can pick up.
items.tested_remedy:
AN EARLIER SPLIT WAS TRIED AND DOES NOT WORK. Measured 2026-08-13T02:26Z, the same four 1d legs re-run through the lever-OFF arm at split 2024-01-01 instead of 2025-07-01 (run 31660836102, tp_cap_pct=0.099):

  leg                OOS n  2025-07-01 -> 2024-01-01   what moved
  gld_pullback_1d      4 -> 10   d_max_dd OOS -0.9994 -> +0.5526   SIGN FLIP (now worse)
  mhg_pullback_1d      7 -> 18   d_net_r  IS  +0.1479 -> -0.1305   SIGN FLIP
  slv_pullback_1d      6 -> 19   d_net_r  OOS  0.0    -> -0.3761   and d_max_dd 0.0 -> +1.1343
  iaum_pullback_1d     4 -> 10   d_max_dd OOS -0.9994 -> +0.5313   SIGN FLIP (now worse)

NOT ONE REACHES THE 25 FLOOR, so every one is still `insufficient_base` -- the remedy buys 4-13 extra OOS trades and clears nothing.

THE SECOND FINDING IS THE MORE USEFUL ONE. FOUR OF FOUR legs CHANGE SIGN on at least one axis when only the split moves. That is a stronger statement than 'the OOS window is thin': a verdict that inverts under a split change is not a verdict that a longer window would merely sharpen. `slv_pullback_1d` is the clearest -- its 0.0 at the standard split meant the lever NEVER FIRED in that window (read as 'not armed', not 'neutral'); given a window where it does fire, it is negative on both axes.

SO THE REMEDY IS NOT A SPLIT CHOICE. What these legs need is more OOS TRADES, which for a daily leg means more calendar -- and `iaum_pullback_1d` cannot get there at all on arithmetic: 30 trades total, so no split yields both a 25-trade OOS and a usable IS. That prediction was then MEASURED rather than left as arithmetic -- at 2024-01-01 it returned IS=19 / OOS=10, i.e. 29 trades split two ways with neither window adequate, exactly as the count implied. Do not close this row by re-running at a third split.

items.confirmation:
CONFIRMED ON THE COMPLETED ROUND 2026-08-13T02:10Z (trainer relay #8872), so this is not an in-progress artifact. The 15m round finished at 00:45:57Z and all three e1_reports read `live_trades: 0` -- eth (harness 379), sol (415), xrp (353). 3 of 3 legs, zero live rows each.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: scripts/ml/build_exit_head_dataset.py:634-642 still counts `skipped["no_candles"]` and `skipped["unresolvable"]` at the candle-resolution stage, and the comment at :656 records the corrected reading of the 2026-08-13 numbers. BOTH DEFECTS ARE NOW FIXED IN CODE; THE ROW STAYS OPEN BECAUSE ITS CRITERION DEMANDS A REAL TRAINER ROUND AND THIS SESSION CANNOT DISPATCH ONE.

DEFECT 1 (the live arm is selected by INSTRUMENT, not by LEG) -- FIXED this session, and it was still live until now. `scripts/ml/build_exit_head_dataset.py --db` loaded EVERY strategy-attributed closed trade in the journal with no leg filter, and `family_of()` (build_exit_head_dataset.py:151) buckets on the strategy NAME, so a scalp round asking for ict_scalp_xrp_15m also inhaled xrp_pullback_2h and manufactured `donchian` / `pullback` families it never named -- exactly the build_report.json this row quotes. The builder now takes `--legs` (CSV of strategy_name), and `scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py` passes it on the same line it passes `--db`, so the two cannot drift apart. The filter is REPORTED, never silent: `legs_filter_state` is three values and they are not collapsed -- `not_requested` / `applied` / `applied_no_match` -- because 'we did not scope' and 'we scoped and the journal holds nothing for these legs' are opposite statements, and reading the second as the first is how an empty live arm gets blamed on data accrual again (which is what happened on 2026-08-12). `legs_dropped` names the excluded strategies and their row counts, so the pull stays VISIBLE rather than merely prevented, and `rows_matching_filters` keeps its pre-existing meaning so a reader comparing it across rounds is not handed a different population under the same key. items.title: The two remaining pending exit_ladder cells cannot be swept: the ladder harness is ict_scalp-only and the fleet sweep has no exit_ladder lever

items.title: 17 SHIPPED exit levers on live legs are justified by evidence measured before the 2026-08-10 TP-parity cutover -- and the one case that was actually re-swept did NOT reproduce
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 over docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json, live legs only, vintage taken from the newest date in each cell's own ref.

  closed live cells, TP-parity-affected families (donchian/pullback/squeeze):
      post-cutover   56
      pre-cutover   198
      undated        15
  => 213 of 269 (79.2%) rest on evidence measured against a geometry production does not run.

The coverage roll-up already PRINTS this caveat. What it does not separate, and what matters, is that 19 of those cells are NOT negatives -- they are decisions with a live consequence:
  shipped              17
  passed_unshipped      2   (mhg_pullback_1d stale_stop; qqq_pullback_1h vol_trail)
  shipped_gate_failed   1   (trend_donchian trail_decay)

A pre-cutover NEGATIVE costs knowledge -- the lever might have passed and we would not know. A pre-cutover SHIPPED costs money: the lever is running on a real-money leg right now, and the backtest that justified it modelled NO take-profit while the live unit clamps TP at 9.9% from entry (BL-20260810-BACKTEST-DOES-NOT-MODEL-THE-LIVE-CAPPED-TP, _TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT).

THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. The single cell where the re-sweep was actually run -- trend_donchian trail_decay -- did NOT reproduce: the live arm6.49/tight2.5 worsened IS maxDD, the 'improves both axes' claim failed on the live-faithful engine, and the cell now carries the `shipped_gate_failed` status invented for exactly that outcome (BL-20260808-TRAIL-LEVER-TUNED-ON-NON-LIVE-FAITHFUL-TRAIL, decided HOLD 2026-08-09). One for one, the re-sweep overturned the shipped justification.

The 17 shipped, by lever: trail_decay 7 (gld/iaum/mhg/slv/sol_pullback/tlt_pullback + donchian), trail_geometry 4 (mes_trend_long_1d, htf_pullback_trend_2h, mhg_pullback_1d, tlt_pullback_1h), stale_stop 4 (trend_donchian_eth/_sol/_xrp_4h + eth), exit_head_ml 3 (trend_donchian/_eth/_sol -- NOT sweepable, these are heads), giveback_stop 1 (uso_trend_1h), vol_trail 1 (trend_donchian_eth).
items.impact: Every one of these levers is changing real exit behaviour today on the strength of a number that has not been reproduced under the geometry the bot actually places. The precedent says roughly how often that matters: 1 of 1 tested so far failed to reproduce. This ranks ABOVE closing the remaining pending cells -- a pending cell costs knowledge, a wrongly-shipped lever costs money.
items.resolution_criteria:
A lever-OFF arm exists in the sweep, and each stale shipped cell has a corpus row comparing base-with-lever against base-without-lever at tp_cap_pct=0.099 on a window clearing MIN_OOS_TRADES. Enumerate the outstanding set with `python3 scripts/research/m20_coverage_rollup.py --stale-decisions`.

EXPLICITLY NOT SUFFICIENT: a run of the CURRENT sweep over those legs. That measures alternatives on top of the shipped lever and returns delta 0.0 for the shipped cell itself -- it looks like a clean re-test and answers a different question. This clause exists because I ran exactly that and had to correct the conclusion.
suggested_fix:
SUPERSEDED -- the re-sweep instruction below cannot validate a shipped cell (see correction_2). Validating one needs an arm the sweep does not currently build: the config-exact base with the declared lever REMOVED, compared against the base with it on. Concretely, a `--drop-declared-levers` (or per-lever `--without <lever>`) input that makes declared_levers() emit nothing for the named lever, so the A/B is lever-OFF vs lever-ON rather than alternative-vs-shipped.

Until that exists, a shipped cell's pre-TP-parity evidence cannot be reproduced by any tool in the repo, and the honest status of those cells is 'justification not reproducible', not 'verified'. Original text, kept as the record of what was tried: 'Re-sweep the 14 sweepable cells at live-parity geometry, highest-consequence first.'
correction_2:
THE FIX THIS ROW ORIGINALLY PRESCRIBED CANNOT WORK, and I found that out by running it.

It said: 're-sweep the sweepable shipped cells at live-parity geometry'. I dispatched exactly that (8 legs x trail_decay+trail_geometry, run on 2026-08-13). The fleet sweep STRUCTURALLY CANNOT re-validate a shipped cell.

m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py::base_args -> declared_levers() puts every DECLARED exit lever into the BASELINE, and says so: 'a shipped stale/giveback cell is part of the leg's baseline, so a new lever cell is measured ON TOP of it'. So the sweep measures ALTERNATIVES against a base that already contains the shipped lever. A swept cell equal to the leg's declared config returns delta 0.0 on every axis because it IS the base.

I nearly recorded those zeros as 'the shipped lever is INERT' -- every one of the 8 legs showed exactly one all-zero decay cell, and in every case it was the cell matching that leg's own YAML (tlt decay_stall6_t1.5 with stall_bars 6 / tight_mult 1.5; sol decay_stall10_t2.5 with stall_bars 10 / tight_mult 2.5; and so on). A clean, repeating, entirely spurious pattern. Caught by reading base_args instead of trusting the shape.

WHAT THE RUN DID ESTABLISH, on the 3 legs with a gradeable OOS window: every ALTERNATIVE around the shipped value fails at live-parity geometry, so the shipped value stands as best-of-tested. That is WEAKER than re-validation and must not be written up as it -- it does not show the lever beats having no lever.
items.progress:
13 OF THE 21 ARE NOW ANSWERED (2026-08-13T02:13Z, PR #8868). The lever-OFF arm this row's suggested_fix specified was built AND run at live parity. Result: not one of the 13 is inert, 2 PASS, 5 are net-negative out-of-sample (Tier-3 queued as BL-20260813-FIVE-SHIPPED-LEVERS-MEASURED-OOS-NEGATIVE), 4 are ungradeable on a thin OOS and an earlier split was tested and does not rescue them.

THE ROW STAYS OPEN FOR THE REMAINING 8, and they need a DIFFERENT instrument, not more of this one: 4 `trail_geometry` (trail_mult is a continuous parameter with no OFF state, so there is no lever to remove -- grading it means sweeping alternative multipliers, which the normal arm already does), 3 `exit_head_ml` (no leg declares a head in YAML; those are gated on the E1->E2 live arm, BL-20260813-EXIT-HEAD-LIVE-ARM-DROPPED-ON-NO-CANDLES), and 1 `mhg_pullback_1d stale_stop` which is correctly `passed_unshipped` -- there is nothing shipped to validate.

High-priority precisely because they are shipped — same posture as BL-20260813-SHIPPED-DONCHIAN-1H-HEAD-RESTS-ON-BESTARM and BL-20260813-FIVE-SHIPPED-LEVERS-MEASURED-OOS-NEGATIVE. items.title: The sweep's corpus retarget preserves the rows but cannot open the PR -- a GITHUB_TOKEN push starts no workflows, so no automatic variant of this can work without a PAT
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 on the FIRST real default-branch dispatch of the #8849 retarget (run 31657293634, 18 pullback legs x 2 levers).

WHAT WORKED: branch protection declined the push to main, the job retargeted onto `claude/m20-sweep-corpus`, wrote `.github/pr-automerge-request`, and pushed. 72 rows preserved (736 -> 808) that four earlier runs had discarded. That half is verified.

WHAT DID NOT: no PR was opened. `claude-pr-automerge.yml` has 3 lifetime runs, newest 2026-08-04. Checked the branch's full run list rather than inferring from the missing PR:
    total runs on claude/m20-sweep-corpus: 4
    ALL FOUR event=pull_request, created 2026-08-13T01:25:37Z
    runs triggered by PUSH: 0
The four appeared the instant a SESSION opened the PR by hand (#8865). The GITHUB_TOKEN push triggered NOTHING -- not the automerge, and not CI either.

THAT SECOND HALF IS WHAT RULES OUT EVERY VARIANT. Having the corpus job call the PR API itself does not help: a PR opened with GITHUB_TOKEN gets no checks either, so it sits permanently un-mergeable behind required checks. It would look MORE automatic and be no more automatic -- strictly worse, because a PR that can never merge reads as progress.

This is the failure mode the retarget's own comment named -- 'a corpus branch nobody opens a PR for, which looks like success' -- reached by a route I did not guard. I protected the opt-in file from being deleted by the rebase path; I never checked that writing it would be READ.
items.impact: Every default-branch sweep dispatch now needs one manual step. The rows are never lost (that was the original bug and it is fixed), but a run can complete green with the corpus still off main. Mitigated in the same change: the retarget path now emits a ::warning:: plus a GitHub step-summary block stating the rows' location and that a human step remains, and the misleading comment claiming automerge finishes the job is corrected.
items.resolution_criteria: A default-branch sweep dispatch results in the corpus reaching main with NO session intervention -- verifiable as a merged PR from claude/m20-sweep-corpus whose checks ran, with no session-authored PR-create call in that window. That requires a credential other than GITHUB_TOKEN. Alternatively, closing as WONTFIX is legitimate if the operator prefers the manual step to a stored PAT -- in which case the warning + step summary IS the resolution, and this row should say so rather than stay open forever.
items.suggested_fix: Operator-gated: create a fine-grained PAT with Contents+PullRequests write, store it as an Actions secret, and have the corpus job push and open the PR with it. Originating that secret VALUE is the operator's category (CLAUDE.md 'Access & autonomy'); the wiring is mine once it exists. The existing VM_GIT_DEPLOY_TOKEN is Contents:Read-only and cannot serve. Until then the loud hand-off is the correct behaviour, not a stopgap to hide.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: .github/workflows/m20-exit-lever-sweep.yml:540-575 now documents the mechanism accurately and correctly: GitHub does not start workflows from events produced with a workflow's own GITHUB_TOKEN, so the pr-automerge opt-in file is written and never read, and a PR opened by the job would get no checks either and be permanently un-mergeable behind required checks. The path ends in a LOUD hand-off (::notice:: at :565) plus a marker file whose own text says it is NOT read on this path, rather than a false claim that something downstream finishes the job. The row's finding is therefore fully recorded; only the credential is missing. — Proposed operator action: originate a fine-grained PAT with Contents:write + Pull requests:write on this repo, store it as an Actions secret (e.g. CLAUDE_PR_PAT), and have the corpus-retarget step push with it instead of GITHUB_TOKEN so the push starts CI and claude-pr-automerge.yml. This is credential origination — the one category CLAUDE.md reserves for the operator. If the operator declines, the correct disposition is to close this row recording that the hand-off IS the final state and a session must open the corpus PR by hand; that is already what the workflow says.
Re-validated: a GITHUB_TOKEN push starts no workflows. I hit the sibling constraint today — my own pushes DID start workflows because they came from a session token, not the in-workflow token.

items.title: 31 corpus rows measured a SHIPPED lever against a base that already contains it -- all-zero deltas labelled `is_oos_fail` / `insufficient_base`, verdict names for a comparison that never happened
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 over docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl, population stated:
    corpus cell rows                                     860
    all-zero delta (d_net_r + d_max_dd = 0 in BOTH windows) 37   (4.3%)
    of those, on a leg whose YAML DECLARES that lever      31
    verdict labels those 31 wear: is_oos_fail 27 - insufficient_base 4
    gate_reason on them: tie_no_improvement; net_r_retained_frac 1.0
20 distinct (leg, lever) pairs, incl. 9 of the 13 gradeable stale decisions.

THE MECHANISM, which is structural and not a bug in any one run: base_args -> declared_levers() puts every YAML-declared exit lever INTO the config-exact base (correctly -- a shipped lever is part of the leg's baseline). A swept cell that reproduces the leg's own declared values is therefore the base compared against itself. The sweep cannot grade a SHIPPED lever at all: every cell asks 'does this alternative beat the shipped one?' and none asks 'is the shipped one worth anything?'.

WHY IT IS A FINDING AND NOT JUST A TIE: the row does not say 'not compared'. It says `is_oos_fail`. Worked example -- qqq_pullback_1h `vt_hot80_t2.5` is the exact cell the coverage matrix calls a 'LONE PASS', its YAML carries trail_vol_above_pctl: 0.80 / trail_vol_tight_mult: 2.5 (armed 2026-08-09, #8683), and its corpus row reads verdict=is_oos_fail, d_net_r_IS/OOS 0.0, wf_ran=false. A reader taking that at face value concludes the live cell failed out-of-sample. Nothing did. This is diagnostic-provenance sub-class A (a label naming a quantity the code did not compute) sitting inside the corpus rather than in a probe.

I nearly recorded the inverse of this earlier in the same session -- all 8 legs in a trail_decay re-sweep showed one all-zero cell and I nearly wrote 'the shipped lever is INERT'. It is the same artifact read the other way round.
items.suggested_fix:
SHIPPED 2026-08-13 in the same commit as this row: the LEVER-OFF ARM. `--without-declared-lever <lever>` (repeatable) removes a declared lever from every leg's config-exact base and emits ONE `shipped_<lever>_<values>` cell that puts it back at the leg's own live values, so the delta the sweep already computes becomes a direct verdict on the SHIPPED cell. Invariant asserted over all 22 real declaring legs: base-OFF + shipped cell == base-ON exactly, so the verdict is attributable to the lever and nothing else.

WHAT REMAINS (this row stays open until the runs land): the arm exists but has not been RUN. Reach is 13 of the 21 stale live decisions -- trail_geometry (4) is excluded by design (trail_mult is a continuous parameter with no OFF state) and exit_head_ml (3) plus mhg_pullback_1d stale_stop (1, correctly passed_unshipped) are not YAML-declared, so there is nothing in the base to remove. Those 8 need a different instrument, not this one.
items.resolution_criteria:
CLOSE only when ALL of:
  1. A lever-OFF run has landed corpus rows carrying non-null `declared_levers_dropped` for at least the 13 gradeable stale decisions, at tp_cap_pct=0.099 (live parity -- a lever-OFF run at the legacy geometry reproduces the vintage problem it exists to answer).
  2. Each of those 13 coverage-matrix cells carries a status derived from that run, with the ref naming the run id.
  3. A re-measurement of the all-zero-delta population reports how many REMAIN, with the denominator stated. A drop to zero is NOT expected -- a normal-arm run still produces these rows by construction; the claim to check is that no CLOSED matrix cell any longer rests on one.
REFUSED as evidence: any run of the sweep WITHOUT --without-declared-lever. That run structurally cannot grade a shipped cell, which is the whole finding.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The lever-OFF arm shipped and is the documented remedy: .github/workflows/m20-exit-lever-sweep.yml:71-72 declares `without_declared_levers` naming this backlog id verbatim ('the shipped lever IS the base, so a normal cell reproducing it measures the base against itself — 31 of 860 corpus rows are exactly that'), and scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:1693 threads it into base_args so the leg's declared levers are removed from the base and each shipped cell restores exactly one. Two supporting states also landed: `declared_levers_dropped` with a loud MULTI-LEVER BASE warning (:1700-1715) so a two-lever drop is not read as a live-config answer, and `inert_cells` (:1673, :1719, :2216 cells_withheld_inert) so a structurally inert cell is recorded as skipped-and-why rather than labelled `is_oos_fail`.

items.source:

items.resolution_criteria:
OPERATOR DECISION, one per lever -- this row is a QUEUE, not a recommendation to bulk-remove. For each: either (a) remove the declared keys from config/strategies.yaml with the measured numbers in the commit message, or (b) keep it with a stated reason (e.g. the IS gain is judged to reflect a regime the OOS window under-samples), recorded on the matrix cell so the next session does not re-raise it.
DO NOT close this row on a walk-forward alone: the walk-forward was already run and these are its IS/OOS verdicts. What would legitimately change the answer is a LONGER OOS window or a per-year fold split, neither of which exists yet for these legs.
REFUSED as evidence: any re-measurement made WITHOUT --without-declared-lever.
