items.title: The exit head's harness arm passed 3/3 folds and LOST to doing nothing on the live book -- measured on the ONE leg where both arms exist, so no `candidate` verdict in the program currently means what it reads as
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13, E1 5m scalp round on the trainer (completed 03:16:17Z, relays #8878/#8879, merged main 7f0955e9, per-leg cut, MIN_OOS_TRADES floor 25).

`ict_scalp_5m` is the FIRST leg in the entire E1 program whose live arm is populated (live_trades 24, 2009 rows). Every other graded leg -- three at 15m, three more at 5m -- reads `live_trades: 0` / `live_validation: null`.

HARNESS ARM, 3/3 FOLDS, oos_trades 533, mean_auc 0.5929:
    2024  auc 0.5546  best tau_0.15  net_r +19.49  vs actual -12.58   beats_hard true
    2025  auc 0.6358  best tau_0.10  net_r  +8.03  vs actual -19.98   beats_hard true
    2026  auc 0.5884  best tau_0.20  net_r +11.71  vs actual  -0.09   beats_hard true
It also cut drawdown hard (fold-2024 model max_dd 3.95 vs the actual book's 23.80). By the harness this is an unambiguous win and the verdict is `candidate`.

LIVE ARM, SAME LEG, SAME MODEL:
    actual        net_r +14.58   max_dd 2.02   mean_hold 83.7 bars
    stale_8_0     net_r  +5.22   (hard rule)
    giveback_1_1  net_r +11.78   (hard rule)
    tau_0.10 +1.32 · tau_0.15 +0.78 · tau_0.20 +0.33 · tau_0.25 -0.60
    tau_0.30 -0.59 · tau_0.40 -1.46 · tau_0.50 -0.43
EVERY TAU IS WORSE THAN DOING NOTHING. The best one keeps 9% of the live book's PnL. Both hard rules also beat every tau.

RANKING TRANSFERS; POLICY DOES NOT. Live AUC is 0.6333 -- HIGHER than the harness mean of 0.5929 -- so the model orders live bars fine. It is the THRESHOLD POLICY that destroys value, and that distinction is the useful part: an AUC gate alone would have waved this through.

THE MECHANISM IS VISIBLE IN THE OUTPUT, NOT INFERRED. Live `mean_hold_bars` for the actual book is 83.7 against ~18.7 on the harness -- the live book earns by holding ~4.5x longer, and the model exits at 11.5 bars, cutting exactly the winners the live edge comes from. The reliability tables show the same shift from the other side: harness folds run frac_pos ~0.21-0.32 across bins while the live set runs ~0.56. A model fitted to a 1-in-4 base rate is being applied to a better-than-even one.
items.impact:
SEVEN legs currently carry `verdict: candidate` off a harness arm alone (ict_scalp_5m, _sol_5m, _xrp_5m, _avax_5m, and the three 15m legs). On the ONE leg where the live arm could be evaluated, that same harness pass did not survive contact with the live book. So a 3/3 fold record is not currently evidence a leg would promote, and any reading of `candidate` as 'nearly ready' is unsupported. All seven matrix cells are `blocked`, which is the correct state, but the REASON now has evidence behind it rather than only the absent-live-arm argument.

This is also the concrete justification for the E1->E2 gate's live-agreement leg, which until tonight had never once been exercised.
items.resolution_criteria:
This row is CLOSED by evidence about the transfer gap, not by a passing leg.
  1. The live arm reaches n >= MIN_OOS_TRADES (25) on at least one leg -- `ict_scalp_5m` sits at 24, ONE short, so its own direction is recorded but cannot yet carry a verdict.
  2. A stated diagnosis of the base-rate/hold-length shift: either the training population is changed to include live rows (see the augmentation debt the training-population guard already tracks), or the tau policy is recalibrated ON live rows, or the gap is shown to be an artifact of n=24.
  3. A re-run showing whether the harness->live inversion reproduces on a SECOND leg. One leg is one leg; the sibling legs cannot test it until their live arms are non-empty (BL-20260813-EXIT-HEAD-LIVE-ARM-DROPPED-ON-NO-CANDLES).
REFUSED as evidence: a harness-only round, however many folds it passes. That is the exact artifact this row exists to record.
items.suggested_fix:
Do NOT respond by loosening the gate. The gate worked -- it is the only thing that caught this. Two directions worth testing, in order of cheapness:
  (a) Recalibrate the tau threshold on live rows rather than harness rows. Ranking already transfers (live AUC 0.6333), so the head may be salvageable with a live-fitted threshold while the same head at harness-fitted taus is not.
  (b) Train on a population that includes live rows. The training-population guard already tracks 1 decision family in `augmentation_debt` for exactly this class of problem.
Also worth measuring before either: whether the 83.7-vs-18.7 hold-length gap is a property of the live book or an artifact of which 24 trades happened to be in the window.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: No gate change landed. scripts/ml/train_exit_head.py:829-830 records `live_trades` and `live_validation` in the output but nothing consumes them as a promotion condition — greps for a live-arm requirement in train_exit_head.py and m20_exit_head_round.py return nothing. So a `candidate` verdict is still produced from the harness arm alone, on legs where the live arm is `live_trades: 0` / `live_validation: null`. — This is a research finding whose remedy is a gate change, and it is the same Tier-3 decision as BL-20260813-E1E2-LIVE-ARM-NO-MINIMUM-N — close them together. Ending condition: `candidate` cannot be emitted without a populated live arm above a stated floor, or the verdict name changes to something that does not read as promotable (the row's point is that no `candidate` in the program currently means what it reads as). The mechanism the row identified is worth preserving in whatever ships: live mean_hold_bars 83.7 vs ~18.7 on the harness, and harness frac_pos 0.21-0.32 vs live 0.56 — ranking transferred (live AUC was HIGHER), policy did not.
Re-validated: a harness-vs-live divergence measured on the one leg where both arms exist. Blocks any exit_head_ml candidate verdict; correctly open.

STILL OPEN, AND CORRECTLY -- but the SHAPE of the blocker has changed and that is worth recording so the next session does not re-derive it. Clause 3 ('a re-run showing whether the harness->live inversion reproduces on a SECOND leg') was blocked on BL-20260813-EXIT-HEAD-LIVE-ARM-DROPPED-ON-NO-CANDLES, i.e. on the sibling legs' live arms being empty. As of 2026-09-02 the leg-selection half of that is FIXED IN CODE (`--legs` now scopes the E0 live arm; see that row), so the blocker has moved from 'the harness structurally cannot produce the data' to 'a trainer round has not been run' -- a different and much cheaper state. It is not yet OBSERVED: no round has been dispatched, and the `no_candles` drop stage is untouched by the fix and may still empty the arm. Clauses 1 (live arm reaches n >= 25 on at least one leg; ict_scalp_5m sat at 24, ONE short) and 2 (a stated diagnosis of the base-rate/hold-length shift) are both untouched by this session. THIS SESSION HAS NO ISSUE-WRITE and cannot dispatch the trainer relay. The row's own REFUSED-AS-EVIDENCE clause still binds: a harness-only round, however many folds it passes, does not close this.

items.title: 3 of 5 backtest harnesses emit rows the E0 builder REFUSES -- missing `exit_time`/`entry`/`sl` (and, until #8889, `symbol`) -- so no trend/squeeze/fvg leg has EVER produced an E0 exit-head dataset row
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 on the first-ever exit-head rounds over the trend/pullback 1d + 1h fleets (trainer, relays #8885/#8887/#8888; rounds completed 05:20:27Z and 05:21:00Z).

`scripts/ml/build_exit_head_dataset.py` resolves each trade's candles with `resampled.get(tr["symbol"])` and counts a miss as `no_candles`. A row without that key is DROPPED -- into a counter, not an error.

  round   trend trades emitted                          landed in the build
  1d      371  (spy 48, qqq 60, tqqq 32, qld 31,
                iwm 65, splg 72, scha 63)               0
  1h      510  (slv_trend_1h 292, uso_trend_1h 218)     0

Both build_reports list ONLY `pullback`. `eh_1d/` contains no `donchian` directory at all. The 1d report reads `trades_in: 1332`, `skipped: {no_candles: 697, unresolvable: 63}` -- and 1332 - 760 = 572, which is the pullback count alone.

  backtest_trend.py       symbol key MISSING
  backtest_squeeze.py     symbol key MISSING
  backtest_fvg_range.py   symbol key MISSING
  backtest_pullback.py    present
  backtest_ict_scalp.py   present

The two harnesses that DO emit it are the two whose legs have ever built a dataset. That is the whole pattern, and it means no trend-family leg has ever produced a single E0 row -- which read as 'the family has no data' for as long as the harness has existed.

NOT a regression from the same-night `--strategy-name` change (PR #8868); checked before concluding. That change alters the `strategy` field. This is `symbol`, which `backtest_trend.py` has never written on any revision.
items.impact: Every `exit_head_ml` matrix cell on a trend/squeeze/fvg leg was unreachable for a reason that presented as an empty family rather than as an error. It is the `no_candles` counter doing exactly its job -- the counter was added precisely so a total drop would not read as an empty input -- and nobody had read it against the emitted count until tonight.
items.resolution_criteria: CLOSE when a round over at least one trend leg produces a build_report family with NON-ZERO `trades.harness`, and that family's e1_report carries a per-leg verdict. The fix landing in code is NOT sufficient -- the whole finding is that the rows silently never arrived, so the evidence has to be their arrival.
items.suggested_fix:
SHIPPED in PR #8889: `"symbol": symbol` added to the emit dict in all three harnesses.

SEPARATE DECISION, recorded so it is not discovered later as a surprise: `family_of` returns `pullback` for `gld_pullback_1d` (substring match) but `spy_trend_long_1d` for a trend leg (nothing matches, so it falls through to the leg name). So pullback legs POOL for training while trend legs each train ALONE on 48-72 trades. Pooling to train and cutting per-leg to grade is the documented intent (the round's own `per_leg_note`), but the two families now get different treatment by accident of string matching rather than by choice. Decide this before reading any trend-leg verdict.

updates.note:
CORRECTION -- the original diagnosis was INCOMPLETE and the first fix did not work. #8889 added `symbol` alone; the re-run at the merged sha produced BYTE-IDENTICAL numbers (trades_in 1332, skipped {no_candles:697, unresolvable:63}, only a `pullback` family). The builder refuses a row missing ANY of FOUR keys (build_exit_head_dataset.py:193): entry_time, exit_time, entry, sl. Those three harnesses emitted only entry_time.

MEASURED per emit file, 1d round: 7 trend legs 371 rows / 0 usable (exit_time+entry+sl missing on all 371); 6 pullback legs 578 rows / 578 usable. And trades_in 1332 == 578 harness-usable + 754 live-usable, which PROVES the 371 never entered the population -- so the original claim that they 'landed in no_candles' is FALSE. no_candles is a later stage they never reached; that claim came from a subtraction that happened to reconcile (1332-697-63=572=the pullback count) and was shipped as a comment into three source files. Corrected in PR #8901.

METHOD NOTE, since this is the reusable part: reasoning from the NAME of the counter the survivors landed in produced a confident wrong cause twice. What found it in one step was diffing the emitted key set against the family that WORKS (`in PULLBACK but NOT in TREND: [entry, exit_reason, exit_time, sl]`). tests/test_harness_emit_schema.py makes that permanent, importing the requirement from the builder's own guard rather than restating it, and is verified to FAIL on exactly the three broken harnesses at the pre-fix sha.

HALF DEMONSTRATED, STAYS OPEN. #8901 merged (ec3073b7); the watcher re-ran both rounds at that sha (relay #8910).

THE ROWS NOW ARRIVE -- the finding's actual subject, measured:
  1d  rows_seen/loaded at load  949/949   (was 578/949)
  1h  rows_seen/loaded at load 1992/1992  (was 1482/1992)
  1d  trades_in 1332 -> 1703  (+371, exactly the trend count)
  1h  trades_in 2236 -> 2746  (+510, exactly)
and for the first time a donchian-side family EXISTS: eh_1d has spy/qqq/tqqq/qld/iwm/splg/scha_trend_long_1d (48/60/32/31/65/72/63 harness trades), eh_1h has slv_trend_1h 289 + uso_trend_1h 215.

NOT CLOSING, because this row's criteria require rows AND a per-leg verdict, and every one of those families returned `folds=0, per_leg_entries=0`. Loosening the criteria to match what shipped would be fitting the contract to the outcome, which is the thing the criteria exist to stop.

The remaining half is owned by two OTHER rows, and the round output now proves both rather than predicting them:
  * each trend leg trained ALONE (its own dir), and the new skip message names the bound -- `slv_trend_1h fold 2019: skipped — test 35 < 50 (--min-fold-trades)`, folds 33-38; `uso_trend_1h` folds 12-27, one showing BOTH conditions (`test 20 < 50; train 395 rows < 500`). Measured earlier: these two clear 0 folds alone and 8 of 9 POOLED. -> BL-20260813-FAMILY-RESOLVER-DRIFT-SCALP-NEVER-POOLED
  * the 1d legs cannot clear the gate even pooled -> BL-20260813-E1-PER-YEAR-FOLD-UNSATISFIABLE-ON-DAILY-BARS

So the emit-schema defect is FIXED and demonstrated; this row closes when one of those two decisions lands and a trend leg finally carries a verdict.

[sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The permanent guard shipped and is verified-failing by construction: tests/test_harness_emit_schema.py imports the requirement from the builder's OWN guard rather than restating it (`assert req == {"entry_time", "exit_time", "entry", "sl"}` at :98) and ships a negative control at :126 so a scan that silently stops matching cannot read as a clean pass. The row's own last update measured the rows arriving after #8901 (1d trades_in 1332 -> 1703, exactly +371 the trend count; 1h 2236 -> 2746, exactly +510) and a donchian-side family existing for the first time. The remaining half it was held open for — folds=0 / per_leg_entries=0 — is now closed by scripts/ml/train_exit_head.py:688 defaulting --fold-mode to `trades` (BL-20260813-E1-PER-YEAR-FOLD-UNSATISFIABLE-ON-DAILY-BARS), and per-leg exit_head_ml verdicts now exist in the matrix (26 honest_negative + 1 shipped + 2 shipped_gate_failed).

items.title: Two independent definitions of "which family is this leg" disagree on 24 of 55 legs -- and the measured consequence is that the 8 ict_scalp legs have NEVER trained as the pooled family the design says they should, while the 12 equity/commodity trend legs are absent from `donchian` entirely
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13, two ways.

(1) STATIC, over all 55 legs in config/strategies.yaml. `m20_fleet_exit_sweep.classify()` (what the round driver uses to pick the HARNESS) and `build_exit_head_dataset.family_of()` (what the builder uses to pick the DATASET DIR) are separate string-matchers asking the same question. They agree on 31 and DISAGREE on 24 (43.6%):

    equity/commodity *_trend_*  12 legs   classify=donchian  family_of=<own leg name>
    ict_scalp_*                  8 legs   classify=scalp     family_of=<own leg name>
    fvg_range_15m                1 leg    classify=fvg       family_of=<own leg name>
    fade_breakout_4h/turtle_soup/vwap  3  classify=None      family_of=fade / <own name>

(2) DYNAMIC, over the 11 exit-head round dirs actually on the trainer (relay #8895). This is the part that matters, because it is the state of every verdict produced so far:

  * There is NO `scalp` dir anywhere, in any round. All 8 ict_scalp legs got their OWN dir every time (scalp_5m/ict_scalp_5m 14787 rows, ict_scalp_avax_5m 19417, ict_scalp_sol_5m 16026, ict_scalp_xrp_5m 13576; scalp_15m/ict_scalp_eth_15m 5173, ict_scalp_sol_15m 7627, ict_scalp_xrp_15m 6702). So EVERY scalp exit-head verdict in the matrix -- including BL-20260813-EXIT-HEAD-HARNESS-PASS-DOES-NOT-SURVIVE-THE-LIVE-BOOK, which was read off ict_scalp_5m -- came from a model trained on ONE leg, not the pooled family.
  * The `donchian` dirs that exist pool only the legs whose name literally contains "donchian" (scalp_5m/donchian = trend_donchian 7920 + trend_donchian_xrp_4h 5258 + trend_donchian_avax_4h 452 + trend_donchian_sol_4h 451, 4 legs). The 12 equity/commodity `*_trend_*` legs appear in no donchian dir at all.
  * Cross-TIMEFRAME leakage exists in the pooled dirs, small but real: eh_1d/pullback carries gld_pullback_1h (7) + spy_pullback_1h (7) = 14 of 15093 rows (0.09%); eh_1h/pullback carries gld_pullback_1d 17 of 34890 (0.05%). The features are tf-relative (age_bars, stagnation_run), so a tf-impure pool is a real if currently tiny contamination.

WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT A PREFERENCE. train_exit_head.py's own module docstring states the design: "one E0 dir pools every symbol in the family ... That is the right unit for TRAINING (it is what breaks the n-wall the program doc describes) but it is the wrong unit for a VERDICT." `per_leg_summary` already cuts verdicts per leg INSIDE a pooled family (verified -- it keys on the trade's `strategy`, and it produced the four per-leg pullback_1h verdicts on 2026-08-13). So pooling costs no attribution. The 24 legs that do not pool are getting neither half of the intended design by accident of string matching. This is the same shape CLAUDE.md records for the shadow-log `score` question -- "import the module; do not re-derive the answer per probe (two probes re-derived it independently and both got it wrong on the same day)".

WHAT THIS BLOCKS. The 1d trend legs carry 31-72 emitted trades each (spy 48, qqq 60, tqqq 32, qld 31, iwm 65, splg 72, scha 63). Alone, every one of them falls under MIN_OOS_TRADES=25 after an IS/OOS split, so each is permanently `insufficient_base`; pooled as `donchian` they are 371 and gradeable. The 1h trend legs (slv 292, uso 218) would clear the floor either way -- so the pooling need is per-round, not per-family, which is itself an argument against a static table.
items.why_it_matters: Every exit_head_ml verdict currently in the coverage matrix was produced under this drift, so the pooling unit behind each one is not what a reader of the design doc would assume. The scalp verdicts in particular are per-leg models being read as family results.
items.proposed_fix:
SINGLE-HOME the resolver and make the pooling unit a DECLARED choice rather than an accident of two regexes. Follow the precedent already in this file pair: train_exit_head.py imports MIN_OOS_TRADES from m20_fleet_exit_sweep rather than mirroring it, with an import failure yielding None ('cannot grade') and never a local default.

CRITICAL -- THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG, and the dynamic measurement is what caught it. `family_of` serves TWO populations, not one: harness-emitted rows (where classify() governs, because it picked the harness) AND live-DB rows from the --db arm (where classify() was never consulted). classify() returns None for vwap, fade_breakout_4h and the pairs legs -- all of which HAVE live rows and their own dirs today (scalp_5m/vwap 2244, scalp_5m/fade 1823, scalp_5m/pairs_sol_eth_a 4206, scalp_5m/pairs_bnb_btc_b 1398). Delegating family_of to classify and refusing on None would silently DROP all of those. Any fix must keep a defined, visible bucket for a leg that has no harness family.

Also decide explicitly whether a pooled dir may mix timeframes, since the round is invoked per-tf but the live arm is not.
items.notes: NOT fixed in-session deliberately. Changing the pooling unit changes what every future exit-head model trains on and therefore every exit_head_ml verdict in the matrix -- a research-design decision, not a mechanical repair, and my first-instinct fix was measurably wrong (see proposed_fix). Filed with the measurement so the decision is made once, deliberately, rather than at 05:45 with a CI run still pending.
items.resolution_criteria: ONE resolver governs family membership for both the harness and live arms, with a defined non-silent bucket for harness-less legs; the pooling unit and the mixed-tf question are each a recorded decision rather than a fallthrough; and a re-run shows the previously-unpooled legs landing in their intended dir. Re-grading the affected exit_head_ml cells is part of the close, since existing scalp verdicts were produced per-leg.

items.title: The E0 builder's load-stage drop counters are reported ONLY on total failure, so a 100%-drop of one family beside a healthy one is invisible -- the instrumentation added after the last incident covers the failure that already happened, not the one that had not
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 (relay #8900). `build_exit_head_dataset.py` drops rows at TWO stages: LOAD (rejected on shape -- `missing:exit_time` etc., counted into `harness_report`) and CANDLE (`no_candles`/`unresolvable`, counted into `skipped`). Only the CANDLE counters reached `build_report.json`; the LOAD counters were printed only inside the `if not trades:` total-failure branch (line 566).

So on the 1d round -- 371 trend rows dropped at LOAD (100% of that family) beside 578 pullback rows loaded fine -- `build_report.json` read exactly:
    {"no_candles": 697, "unresolvable": 63}
with no trace of the 371, and `'missing:' present in report -> False` for both the 1d and 1h rounds. Reading that report, the trend family simply did not exist. `trades_in: 1332` counted only the survivors, so even the denominator gave nothing away -- an unasserted denominator in the sense of CLAUDE.md § 'Diagnostic provenance' sub-class C, one level up from the row it hid.

THE SHAPE WORTH REMEMBERING: the counters exist BECAUSE of the 2026-08-12 ict_scalp incident, where 1170 rows dropped 100% and the message was 'no trades loaded'. That fix instrumented the TOTAL-drop path -- the failure that had already happened -- and a PARTIAL drop, which is the case the counters are most needed for, still reported nothing.
items.why_it_matters: A partial drop is the common case once more than one family is in a round, and it is the case a reader is least likely to catch by eye, because the report looks healthy: a family is present, rows are non-zero, nothing is obviously wrong. It cost two misdiagnoses tonight before a key-set diff found the cause.
items.proposed_fix:
SHIPPED in PR #8901: `skipped_at_load` + `rows_seen_at_load` + `rows_loaded_at_load` are written into `build_report.json` unconditionally and echoed to stderr so the round driver's log carries them. Kept as a SEPARATE key from the candle-stage `skipped` deliberately -- 'rejected on shape' and 'had no candles' are different failures with different fixes, and merging them would re-create the ambiguity being corrected.

STILL OPEN: nothing yet ALERTS on a family whose load-usable count is 0 while a sibling family in the same round is healthy. Surfacing the number is necessary and not sufficient -- the number was computable all along.
items.resolution_criteria: CLOSE when a build_report from a real round carries a non-empty `skipped_at_load` block that names the missing key, AND a round in which one family drops 100% at load while another loads fine produces a LOUD signal (non-zero exit, or an explicit per-family 'loaded 0 of N' line) rather than a quiet field a reader must know to look for.
refs: relay #8899 (the key-set diff that found the real cause)

updates.note:
SURFACING VERIFIED LIVE (relay #8910). Both re-run reports now carry the load-stage block: `rows_seen_at_load: 949` / `rows_loaded_at_load: 949` (1d) and 1992/1992 (1h), with `skipped_at_load: {}`.

READ THE EMPTY DICT CORRECTLY: `{}` here means 'nothing was rejected on shape', and it is trustworthy ONLY because the seen/loaded pair is published beside it and they are equal. An empty `skipped_at_load` with no denominator would be exactly the unasserted-negative this row is about -- which is why the counts ship with it rather than the skip dict alone.

Row STAYS OPEN on its stated criteria: nothing yet ALERTS when one family loads 0 of N while a sibling is healthy. Surfacing the number was necessary and is not sufficient; the number was computable all along.

BOTH criteria now met. The surfacing half shipped in #8901; the ALERT half — 'a round in which one family drops 100% at load while another loads fine produces a LOUD signal' — is this change.

THE MISSING PIECE WAS ATTRIBUTION, NOT VOLUME. `skipped_at_load` said HOW MANY rows were rejected and WHY, but not WHOSE, so 'trend dropped 100% while pullback loaded fine' was not computable from the report at all. `load_harness_trades` now buckets seen/loaded PER FAMILY — `family_of` reads only `strategy`, which survives every rejection reason, so a row is attributable even when the keys that disqualified it are missing. The report gains `per_family_load` + `families_starved`, and stderr prints `loaded N of M` for EVERY family unconditionally, so a 0 is visible by CONTRAST rather than by a reader knowing to look; an asymmetric starvation additionally prints an unmissable banner naming the starved family, the healthy siblings, and that every verdict this round produces EXCLUDES the starved family.

NOT a non-zero exit, deliberately: a round can legitimately be invoked on inputs where one family has no emitted rows, and failing the build would make the round driver's error path the thing needing explanation. The criteria offered either; the explicit per-family line plus a machine-readable field is the one that does not create a second failure mode.

VERIFIED against the real incident, not a toy: a synthetic 1d round at the actual counts (371 trend rows missing exit_time + 578 complete pullback rows) yields rows_seen 949 / loaded 578, per_family_load {donchian: 0 of 371, pullback: 578 of 578}, families_starved ['donchian']. Negative control (all-healthy) reports no starvation; the 2026-08-12 total-drop case still reports starvation; a row with no `strategy` and an unparseable line each keep their own bucket rather than hiding in a real family or shrinking the denominator. 10 tests.

SIDE FINDING, worth more than this row: writing the tests INDEPENDENTLY REPRODUCED BL-20260813-FAMILY-RESOLVER-DRIFT-SCALP-NEVER-POOLED. I asserted family_of('ict_scalp_5m') == 'scalp' from the design intent and it returned 'ict_scalp_5m' — `family_of` has branches for donchian/pullback/squeeze/fade and NONE for scalp. The test now pins the ACTUAL behaviour with a docstring explaining why, so the drift is asserted in exactly one place and that test's failure is the signal when the pooling decision lands.

items.title: The E1 walk-forward folds by CALENDAR YEAR at --min-fold-trades 50, which a daily-bar strategy cannot satisfy -- so the 16 `1d` exit_head_ml cells (over half the open block) cannot produce a verdict at the default, no matter how much upstream plumbing is fixed
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 from the 1d round's own log (trainer, relay #8898). The round loaded 568 healthy pullback harness trades and produced ZERO verdicts: `per-leg: no fold produced a leg block (no usable folds)`.

`train_exit_head.py:471` skips a fold when `len(test) < a.min_fold_trades or len(train_rows) < 500`. `--min-fold-trades` defaults to **50**. The 19 test folds ran 12-42 trades:
    2008:17 2009:18 2010:23 2011:25 2012:33 2013:25 2014:25 2015:29 2016:27
    2017:35 2018:33 2019:28 2020:29 2021:37 2022:39 2023:42 2024:42 2025:29
    2026:12
max 42, threshold 50, folds clearing it: ZERO. (Arithmetic check: the folds sum to 548, +20 in the first year which is never a test fold, = the 568 reported.)

POOLING DOES NOT RESCUE IT, so this is independent of BL-20260813-FAMILY-RESOLVER-DRIFT-SCALP-NEVER-POOLED:
    donchian 1d alone   371 trades / ~16y = ~23.2 per year
    pullback 1d alone   568 trades / ~20y = ~28.4 per year
    ALL 1d legs pooled  949 trades / ~20y = ~47.5 per year  <- still under 50
Contrast 1h: 1450 trades / ~10y = ~145 per year, which clears comfortably -- and the 1h round DID produce the four per-leg pullback verdicts on 2026-08-13. The fold scheme is fine for intraday families and cannot work for daily ones.

SCOPE: 16 of the 31 open `exit_head_ml` cells across all 50 matrix rows are `1d` (gdx/gld/iaum/ief/mgc/mhg/slv/tlt pullback_1d; iwm/mes/qld/qqq/scha/splg/spy/tqqq trend_long_1d). Over half the largest open block on M20's done-condition.

NOT a structural impossibility -- `--min-fold-trades` is a CLI argument, so this is a THRESHOLD CHOICE nobody has made for daily bars, not a wall.
items.why_it_matters: The 1d cells have been sitting `pending` and reading as 'not run yet'. They have effectively been un-runnable at the default, so upstream fixes (the emit schema in #8901, the family-resolver pooling) are necessary and still not sufficient to close a single one of them. Anyone planning M20's remaining work off the matrix would mis-estimate this block badly.
items.proposed_fix:
A RESEARCH-DESIGN choice, deliberately not made in-session at 06:10 with the operator asleep -- it changes the OOS reliability of every verdict the harness produces, and picking a fold threshold ad hoc to make cells go green is the anti-pattern this repo files as cosmetic. Two options, both needing a stated basis:
  (a) Lower `--min-fold-trades` for 1d rounds toward the repo's established       MIN_OOS_TRADES=25 floor. Attraction: one floor governs the matrix       instead of two. Cost: folds of 25-42 are thin, and the per-leg cut       inside them is thinner still.
  (b) Fold by MULTI-YEAR blocks for daily families (e.g. 3y test windows),       keeping the trade count per fold comparable to the intraday rounds       rather than keeping the calendar unit. Costs fold COUNT (19 -> ~6).
Whichever is chosen, the 1d verdicts it produces are not comparable to the intraday ones unless the choice is recorded on the cell.

SEPARATELY AND CHEAPLY: `train_exit_head.py:472` prints one message for TWO skip conditions and states neither threshold, so `fold 2024: skipped (test=42 trades, train=12402 rows)` cannot tell a reader that 42 was compared against 50. Naming the failing condition and its bound is a one-line fix and would have made this visible on the first read.
items.resolution_criteria: CLOSE when a 1d exit-head round produces at least one usable fold with a recorded per-leg verdict, AND the fold-geometry choice behind it (threshold or windowing) is stated on the matrix cells it graded, so a reader can see those verdicts rest on a different OOS structure than the intraday ones. Lowering the threshold without recording it does NOT close this.
refs: relay #8898 (the 1d round log with the 19 skipped folds)

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: scripts/ml/train_exit_head.py:688 now declares `--fold-mode` with choices ['trades','years'] and default **'trades'**, and fold_blocks (:433) blocks by trade index instead of calendar year. Its docstring's 'WHY `trades` IS THE DEFAULT' section (:463+) records exactly this row's measurement: 'The original cut was one test fold per CALENDAR YEAR, which silently makes a strategy's TRADE FREQUENCY the thing that decides whether it can be graded at all. A daily-bar leg trades ~20x/year, so every year-fold lands 12-42 trades against a 50-trade floor and is skipped — while the pool holds 371 trades across 19 years. Measured 2026-08-13: BOTH 1d family pools returned ZERO usable folds, and the conclusion drawn from that was "the 1d fleet cannot be graded", which was wrong.'

items.title: A bundled coverage-matrix row survived the 2026-08-09 per-leg explosion -- one row carrying 8 lever statuses for 4 named legs plus a `*_prop` WILDCARD -- and it CONTRADICTED two legs' own rows on 8/8 and 6/8 cells; the leg-name validator cannot see it because it skips non-live rows
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 against docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json.

Row `shadow fleet (turtle_soup, fade_breakout_4h, vwap, ict_scalp_5m, trend_donchian_1h, mgc_trend_1h, *_prop)` carries ONE set of 8 lever statuses for six named legs and a wildcard. That is exactly BL-20260809-COVERAGE-MATRIX-MULTILEG-ROW-ONE-STATUS, which the per-leg explosion was performed to eliminate -- the bundle survived it.

TWO of the six ALSO have their own rows, and the two representations DISAGREE:
  ict_scalp_5m  8 of 8 cells differ (e.g. stale_stop own=honest_negative vs bundled=passed_unshipped; trail_geometry own=n/a vs bundled=pending)
  mgc_trend_1h  6 of 8 cells differ
So the matrix asserted two different things about the same leg, and which answer a reader got depended on which row they happened to read.

WHY NO GUARD CAUGHT IT: `m20_coverage_rollup.py:306` scopes the leg-name-resolves-in-strategies.yaml check to `execution == 'live'` rows. The bundled row is `execution: shadow`, so the one validator that would flag an unresolvable row identity skips exactly the row that is most unresolvable. The live-only scope is defensible for the DENOMINATOR (a non-live leg cannot be swept and is not counted), but it means a non-live row may carry any string as its identity indefinitely.

NOT A HEADLINE DEFECT: the row is excluded from the 47-leg done-condition denominator, so 354/376 and the 42 open cells are unaffected -- verified by re-running the roll-up after the edit below (42 before, 42 after). The cost is to a READER, not to the count.
items.why_it_matters: The matrix's declared unit is the LEG -- that is the whole reason for the 2026-08-09 explosion, and train_exit_head.py's own docstring repeats it ('the family is the wrong unit for a VERDICT'). A surviving bundle reintroduces the retired failure inside the artifact that was supposed to have retired it, and a contradiction between two rows is worse than a gap: a gap reads as unknown, a contradiction reads as known.
items.proposed_fix:
DONE 2026-08-13 (safe half): removed `ict_scalp_5m` and `mgc_trend_1h` from the bundle's label, since both have dedicated rows carrying per-leg evidence. That removes the contradiction WITHOUT inventing any status. A `_bundled_row_note` on the row records what it still is.

NOT DONE, deliberately: exploding the remaining four legs + the wildcard. Their 8 statuses are fleet-level (e.g. stale_stop `passed_unshipped` cites a sweep whose ref names specific OTHER legs); assigning them per-leg would be fabricating a verdict per cell, which is worse than the bundle it replaces. Explode when a per-leg sweep actually covers these legs.

GUARD GAP, proposed not shipped: add an invariant that EVERY row's `strategy` names exactly one leg -- applied to ALL rows, not just live ones -- with this bundled row as a single DECLARED, dated exception so it stays visible and countable rather than silently exempt. Not added tonight: a new check that fails on a known-unfixable row would put a red guard on main, and the exception list has to be right the first time.
items.resolution_criteria: CLOSE when no matrix row's `strategy` names more than one leg (the `*_prop` wildcard included -- a wildcard row has no countable denominator), AND a guard enforces that over ALL rows rather than live-only, so the next bundle cannot be added silently. Removing the contradiction alone does NOT close this -- the bundle is still there.
refs: BL-20260809-COVERAGE-MATRIX-MULTILEG-ROW-ONE-STATUS (the defect this is an instance of)

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The bundled row still exists in docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json: 'shadow fleet (turtle_soup, fade_breakout_4h, vwap, trend_donchian_1h, *_prop)' carries one set of 8 lever statuses for five named legs plus a `*_prop` wildcard — and the wildcard now overlaps real per-leg rows, since trend_donchian_sol_prop and trend_donchian_eth_prop entered the matrix as LIVE legs on 2026-08-13 with their own exit_ladder cells. The named-leg set has shifted since filing (ict_scalp_5m and mgc_trend_1h are no longer in it) but the shape the 2026-08-09 explosion was performed to eliminate survives. The validator still cannot see it: m20_coverage_rollup.py's config->matrix leg check at :880-905 is scoped to `_is_live(body)` rows.
Re-validated: one row carrying 8 lever statuses for 4 named legs plus a wildcard, contradicting the per-leg rows. A matrix that contradicts itself cannot gate anything.

items.title: M20's remaining done-condition is not 42 independent tasks -- 25 of the 42 open cells (59.5%) are the 1d fleet, and all three lever families block there for ONE reason: daily bars do not produce enough trades for the OOS standards in use
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 over docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json (live legs only -- the done-condition population, 42 open cells).

By timeframe: 1d=25, 15m=8, 5m=4, 4h=3, 1h=2.

The 25 are spread across three levers and every one of them is the same underlying fact:
  exit_head_ml   16  E1 folds by CALENDAR YEAR, skipped under
                     --min-fold-trades 50; the 1d folds run 12-42, so ZERO
                     clear. Pooling every 1d leg reaches ~47.5/yr, still
                     short. (BL-20260813-E1-PER-YEAR-FOLD-UNSATISFIABLE-ON-DAILY-BARS)
  vol_trail       7  'insufficient OOS base' at the corpus-standard split,
                     with the ref recording OOS n=3,4,4,4,5,5,6 against
                     MIN_OOS_TRADES=25
  giveback_stop   2  blocked:insufficient_base (mes_trend_long_1d,
                     mhg_pullback_1d)

Three different levers, three different code paths, one cause: a daily-bar strategy over ~16-20 years produces 31-72 trades TOTAL, and every evidence standard in the programme is calibrated on intraday volume (1h pullback is ~145 trades/yr and grades without difficulty).

WHY THIS IS WORTH ITS OWN ROW: the individual cells are filed accurately and each reads as its own small blocker, so the matrix presents 42 items of roughly equal weight. It is one item of weight 25 and seventeen others. A reader planning the milestone off the cell list -- which is what the matrix is FOR -- would mis-estimate the remaining work badly, and would expect plumbing fixes to move it. Tonight's two plumbing fixes (#8889, #8901) move none of these 25.
items.why_it_matters: M20's done-condition is 'no pending AND no blocked on live legs'. As things stand it cannot be reached without an explicit decision about daily bars, because no amount of correct work closes a cell whose evidence standard its population cannot satisfy. That decision is the milestone's critical path and it is currently invisible, distributed across 25 individually-reasonable cell notes.
items.proposed_fix:
OPERATOR / RESEARCH-DESIGN DECISION, not a bug fix. The options are not equivalent and the choice should be made once for the whole 1d fleet rather than per lever:
  (a) A DIFFERENT EVIDENCE STANDARD for daily bars -- multi-year folds, a       lower OOS floor, or pooled-across-legs OOS. Cost: 1d verdicts are then       not comparable to intraday ones, so the standard must be recorded on       every cell it grades.
  (b) ACCEPT 'not gradeable at this standard' as a terminal disposition for       the 1d fleet, and say so in the matrix legend. The done-condition then       becomes reachable honestly, at the cost of admitting 25 cells will       never carry a verdict.
  (c) Leave them open indefinitely -- the status quo, which quietly makes       M20 unreachable while reading as 'in progress'.
(c) is the current default and is the one option nobody has chosen deliberately. Flagging that is the point of this row.
items.resolution_criteria: CLOSE when the 1d fleet has ONE recorded disposition covering all three lever families -- either a stated alternative evidence standard (with the standard named on the cells it grades) or an explicit terminal 'not gradeable at this standard' status in the matrix legend. Closing the individual cells one at a time under the CURRENT standard does not resolve this, because it cannot happen.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Recomputed over docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json (updated_at 2026-08-15): 25 open cells on live legs, 17 of them tf=1d (exit_head_ml 12, vol_trail 6, giveback_stop 2, exit_ladder 4, regime_flip_exit 1). The legend block holds only the 7 status values (shipped/passed_unshipped/honest_negative/pending/blocked/n-a/shipped_gate_failed) — no terminal 'not gradeable at this standard' entry, and the string '1d fleet' appears only inside `exploded_from`. So no single disposition covering the 1d fleet has been recorded; option (c) is still the default. — Proposed: the operator picks (a) a stated alternative evidence standard for daily bars, recorded on every cell it grades, or (b) an explicit terminal legend status ('not gradeable at this standard') for the 1d fleet, so M20's done-condition becomes reachable honestly. Closing individual cells under the current standard cannot resolve it — the derivation in docs/research/M20-E1-block-size-derivation-2026-08-13.md shows no block size makes those legs gradeable.
Re-validated and worth acting on precisely BECAUSE it collapses 42 tasks into one fact. Live corroboration: the 1d legs are the longest holds in this window (tlt 721 h, iwm 554 h).

items.title: The coverage matrix's `execution` field -- which alone decides M20's done-condition denominator -- disagreed with config/strategies.yaml on 3 of 50 rows, and it conflates the strategy gate with whether the leg is routed to any account at all
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13, matrix `execution` vs config/strategies.yaml (49 rows resolvable; the bundled row is not a leg):
    avax_pullback_2h   matrix=live      config=shadow   -> inflated the denominator
    fvg_range_15m      matrix=live      config=shadow   -> inflated the denominator
    xauusd_trend_1h    matrix=disabled  config=live     -> excluded a declared-live leg

The first two are unambiguous and are FIXED here. The strategy-level gate is one of the two canonical execution gates (CLAUDE.md § 'The two execution gates'): `execution: shadow` logs order packages and NEVER sends a live order, whatever the account's `mode:`. `fvg_range_15m` is routed to real-money `bybit_2` and the shadow gate is precisely what stops it. The matrix's own `_doc` puts shadow rows outside the live-leg done-condition, so counting them was applying the matrix's rule to the wrong field.

HEADLINE IMPACT -- and it is a PRECISION defect, not a large error. Measured three ways over the same file:
    matrix `execution` (what was quoted)     47 legs  354/376 = 94.1%  22 pending
    config strategy-gate                     46 legs  348/368 = 94.6%  20 pending
    config gate AND routed to an account     45 legs  340/360 = 94.4%  20 pending
The percentage is stable at 94.1-94.6% under every definition, so no conclusion drawn from it was wrong. What WAS wrong is that two legs the milestone's own definition excludes were inside its done-condition. After the fix: 340/360 = 94.4%, done-condition 39 open (20 pending + 19 blocked), down from 42.

THE UNRESOLVED HALF -- `xauusd_trend_1h` is the interesting one. Config says `execution: live`, so a mechanical matrix<-config sync would ADD it to the done-condition. But it is routed to NO ACCOUNT (checked every entry in config/accounts.yaml, including the all-strategies wildcard), so nothing dispatches it and it cannot trade. The matrix's `disabled` is therefore MORE accurate than the config field alone -- while not being a value the two-gate vocabulary has. A blind sync would make this row worse, which is why this row is filed rather than the whole thing automated.
items.why_it_matters: This single field decides which legs the milestone must close, so an error in it is an error in the milestone's definition of done -- not in a metric derived from it. And the failure mode is silent: every downstream tool reads the matrix's own field, so nothing cross-checks it against the config that actually governs execution.
items.proposed_fix:
DONE: `avax_pullback_2h` and `fvg_range_15m` set to `shadow` with a `_execution_note` recording why (field beats comment).

OPEN: decide what `execution` in the matrix MEANS when a leg is declared live but routed nowhere, then enforce it. Tradeability is the conjunction of THREE facts -- account `mode`, strategy `execution`, and whether any account routes the leg -- and the matrix records one. Recommended: define the field as actual tradeability (gate AND routed), which yields 45 legs / 360 cells, and add a validator that recomputes it from config on every run rather than trusting the stored value. Note that a validator asserting matrix==config naively would FAIL on xauusd_trend_1h and be wrong to.
items.resolution_criteria: CLOSE when the matrix's `execution` is DERIVED from config (strategy gate + routing) rather than stored independently, or a guard recomputes and compares it on every run with the unrouted-leg case explicitly handled. Correcting the two rows by hand -- which this row does -- does not close it: the next config change re-opens the same gap silently.
refs: config/strategies.yaml (execution: shadow on both) + config/accounts.yaml (xauusd routed nowhere)

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: scripts/research/m20_coverage_rollup.py:883-901 now RECOMPUTES each leg's execution from config via `_effective_execution` (which folds `enabled: false` -> 'disabled', the case that made xauusd_trend_1h look like a disagreement — config/strategies.yaml:1543 `enabled: false` beside `execution: live`) and reports a problem on any mismatch; it also reads config/accounts.yaml routing via `_funding_by_leg`. The check is registered as `exit-coverage-matrix-guard` in scripts/ci/run_guards.py:237 and `python3 scripts/research/m20_coverage_rollup.py --check` returns OK on the tree. The two corrected rows carry `_execution_note` (avax_pullback_2h, fvg_range_15m both now `shadow`).

items.title: `train_exit_head.py` dies on an unhandled sklearn ValueError when a family has 0 harness trades, and the `--db` live arm CREATES such families because it is not scoped to the round's `--legs`
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 (relay #8917). A round invoked with `--legs squeeze_breakout_4h` alone produced FOUR family dirs, because the `--db` live arm buckets live trades by `family_of` regardless of which legs the round was asked for. Three of the four had ZERO harness trades:
    pullback  0 harness (0 rows), 20 live (128 rows)   -> CRASH
    vwap      0 harness (0 rows),  3 live (6 rows)     -> CRASH
    squeeze  98 harness (2197 rows), 2 live            -> ran, no usable folds
Each crash is the same unhandled exception out of sklearn:
    ValueError: Expected 2D array, got 1D array instead: array=[]
raised from `check_X_y` -> `check_array`, i.e. the walk-forward built an empty training matrix (the folds iterate over harness years, and there are none) and handed it to the model.

NOT FATAL to the round — each family trains in its own subprocess, so the round completed and the one family that mattered produced its report. The cost is diagnostic: a reader gets a 20-line sklearn traceback where a one-line statement of the condition belongs, and a traceback in the log reads like a broken run rather than an empty input.
items.why_it_matters: This is the same class as the two defects fixed earlier tonight, one level down: the code KNOWS the condition (`0 harness trades` is printed on the line immediately above the traceback) and still fails as if it were unexpected. A round log that contains tracebacks trains the reader to skim past them, which is exactly how the 100%-drop went unnoticed for as long as it did.
items.proposed_fix:
Two independent halves, both small:
  (a) `train_exit_head.py` — refuse early with a stated reason when the       harness set is empty ('0 harness trades: the walk-forward folds over       harness years, so there is nothing to train on; live rows alone       cannot form a fold'), exit non-zero, no traceback. NOTE the live-only       case is not nonsense in principle — it is the shape an E1 live-arm       evaluation would want — so the message should say which arm is       missing rather than implying the dir is invalid.
  (b) `m20_exit_head_round.py` / `build_exit_head_dataset.py` — decide       whether the live arm should be SCOPED to the round's `--legs`.       Today a one-leg round silently acquires unrelated families. That may       be deliberate (the live arm is a cross-check, not a subject), but       nothing states it, and the surprise is what produced this crash.
items.resolution_criteria: CLOSE when a family dir with 0 harness trades produces a one-line stated refusal and a non-zero exit instead of a sklearn traceback, AND the live arm's scoping relative to `--legs` is either enforced or documented as deliberate. Suppressing the traceback without answering the scoping question only hides how those dirs appear.
refs: relay #8917 (the round log with all three tracebacks)
scripts/ml/train_exit_head.py (the fold loop over harness years)

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: scripts/ml/train_exit_head.py:717-723 still computes `harness`/`h_trades` and prints the counts, then line 806-807 calls `train_model(harness)` whenever `l_trades` is non-empty; `train_model` (line 129-137) goes straight to `matrix(rows)` + `clf.fit(X, y)` with no empty-input guard, so a 0-harness family still raises the sklearn ValueError. No early refusal exists anywhere in main(), and nothing in m20_exit_head_round.py scopes the --db live arm to --legs. — Tier-1 research tooling; low severity (per-family subprocess, round still completes). Ends when a 0-harness family prints a one-line stated refusal + non-zero exit and the live-arm scoping is either enforced or documented.
Re-validated: an unhandled sklearn ValueError on a 0-harness-trade family, where the --db live arm CREATES such families. Crash-on-a-state-you-generate.

items.title: E1->E2 gate's live arm has no minimum-n: counted as confirmation at n=15, discounted at n=24
items.source: docs/research/m20-what-remains-2026-08-13.md
items.what_to_check: On ict_scalp_5m the E1->E2 live arm became evaluable for the FIRST time in the whole E1 program and CONTRADICTED the harness arm: harness verdict=candidate (beats_actual 3/3, beats_hard 3/3, 533 OOS trades, AUC 0.5929) vs a live arm where EVERY tau is worse than doing nothing (best tau +1.32 vs actual +14.58; both hard rules also beat every tau). Ranking transfers -- live AUC 0.6333 is HIGHER -- policy does not. Mechanism is visible, not inferred: live mean_hold_bars 83.7 vs ~18.7 on the harness, so the model exits at 11.5 bars and cuts exactly the long holds the live edge comes from; harness frac_pos 0.21-0.32 vs live 0.56, i.e. a model fitted to a 1-in-4 base rate applied to a better-than-even one. THE GAP: that leg is blocked at n=24 against the MIN_OOS_TRADES floor of 25, while the three LIVE SHIPPED donchian-1h heads were promoted on evidence including 'the n=15 live set agrees in sign' (PR #6211, 2026-07-12, operator-approved). Both are sub-floor. The live arm has no minimum-n, the same gap beats() has, so sub-floor live evidence counts as confirmation when it agrees and is (rightly) discounted when it disagrees. NOT a claim that the promotions were improper: their primary evidence was a purged walk-forward winning 5/5 folds on net_R + maxDD + net_R/pos-day, and the gate as written asks only for sign agreement, which n=15 satisfied.
items.next_action: RE-EVALUATE the live arm for the three shipped donchian heads (trend_donchian, _eth, _sol) at their ACCRUED n -- live since 2026-07-12, ~1 month, so materially more than the n=15 they were promoted on. PR #6211 committed to two follow-ups that I did NOT verify ever happened: a mandatory health-review mechanics check on the first head-driven exit, and the realized future_r_delta record accruing for /ml-review. Check both. Then decide whether the E1->E2 live arm should carry an explicit minimum-n (and whether 'agrees in sign' is the right test at any n).
items.resolution_criteria: CLOSE when (a) the live arm for the three shipped donchian heads has been re-evaluated at accrued n and the result recorded, AND (b) the E1->E2 gate either declares a minimum-n for its live arm or records an explicit decision not to. If (a) shows the sign no longer agrees, this escalates to Tier-3 (three live heads trimming winners on real money) and must NOT be closed on the re-measurement alone.
items.limits_of_this_check: The contradiction is measured on EXACTLY ONE leg (ict_scalp_5m, 5m scalp). Donchian 1h is a different family with a different hold-time distribution; the mechanism is plausibly general but must not be read across without measuring. Equally, 'the scalp leg is special' must not be assumed either -- that is the assumption this item exists to test.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Confirmed unchanged in code: scripts/ml/train_exit_head.py:829-830 emits `"live_trades": len(l_trades)` and `"live_validation": live_eval` with no floor anywhere — greps for MIN_LIVE / a live-arm minimum return nothing in train_exit_head.py or m20_exit_head_round.py. So sub-floor live evidence still counts as confirmation when it agrees (n=15 on the donchian-1h promotions) and is discounted when it disagrees (n=24 on ict_scalp_5m), which is the asymmetry the row names. — Proposed operator decision (Tier-3 — it changes a promotion gate): give the E1->E2 live arm an explicit minimum-n, and state it. The natural value is the same MIN_OOS_TRADES=25 the harness arm already uses (m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:548, operator decision 2026-08-11), so the two arms share one floor rather than one being floored and the other not. Below the floor the live arm should report `live_validation: insufficient_n` — a third state, not a pass and not a fail — so 'we could not look' never reads as agreement. This is NOT a claim the three donchian-1h promotions were improper: their primary evidence was a purged walk-forward winning 5/5 folds, and the gate as written asked only for sign agreement.
Re-validated: a gate with no minimum n counted n=15 as confirmation and discounted n=24. Cheap to fix (declare the floor); still undone.

items.title: A passwordless-root sudoers grant for the REMOVED claude-vm-runner subsystem is still installed on the live money VM
items.source: MEASURED 2026-08-13, three probes. (A) CALL SITES: `grep -rn 'claude-vm-dispatch|claude_vm|CLAUDE_VM_PROMPT' src/` returns EMPTY -- nothing starts an instance. The only starter was the Telegram `/vm` + `/vm_write` command surface. (B) PROVENANCE: build-arc + retire-arc, NO delete-arc. docs/claude/vm-operator-mode.md:3-5 states the surface 'was removed (PR #1933, 2026-05-25) ... the VM-runner that no longer exists'. (C) STILL INSTALLED: scripts/vm_bootstrap.sh:129-141 copies deploy/claude-vm-runner.sudoers to /etc/sudoers.d/claude-vm-runner and deploy/claude-vm-dispatch to /usr/local/bin/claude-vm-dispatch. The grant reads `ubuntu ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/local/bin/claude-vm-dispatch`.
items.why_it_matters: A passwordless-root path on the money VM whose only caller was deleted ~3 months ago. Nothing exercises it, so nothing would notice if the wrapper were replaced. This is the zombie class at its most expensive: a clean consistency pass sees an installed unit + an installer + defensive 'is one active?' guards and reads it as alive.
items.careful: DO NOT blanket-delete the sudoers file. It carries a SECOND grant -- `ubuntu ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/sbin/ufw` -- with a documented justification in the file itself (VM-local firewall has historically blocked TCP/8001 across reboots, refs #537/#542/#545; auto-recovery needs it). The ufw grant may still be wanted. Split the file, do not drop it.
items.action: (1) TIER-1, repo side: delete deploy/claude-vm-runner@.service, deploy/claude-vm-dispatch, deploy/claude-permissions.{read,write}.json; drop the dispatch+sudoers install block from scripts/vm_bootstrap.sh (keeping a ufw-only sudoers file if the ufw grant is retained); remove the 8 dead 'is a vm-runner active?' guards in scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh:358, scripts/ops/pull_and_deploy.sh:63, enable_m5_consumer.sh:55, disable_m5_consumer.sh:42, disable_closed_flat_invariant.sh:45, disable_signal_dual_write.sh:37, fix_data_dir.sh:94; drop the check_diag_unit_allowlist.py:44 exemption in the SAME PR or the guard goes stale-green. (2) TIER-2, VM side and the part that actually matters: remove /etc/sudoers.d/claude-vm-runner (or replace with a ufw-only file) and /usr/local/bin/claude-vm-dispatch from the live VM. OPERATOR-GATED.
items.resolution_criteria: No passwordless-root grant remains on the live VM for a dispatcher with no caller, and the repo no longer installs one.

updates.note:
REPO SIDE DONE, VM SIDE PENDING A DISPATCH. Operator approved the split in chat 2026-08-13.

Shipped: deploy/ict-ufw.sudoers (the surviving ufw grant, on its own with its own justification); scripts/ops/purge_vm_runner.sh; the `purge-vm-runner` system-action registered in all three places in system-actions.yml + documented; the 5 dead deploy artifacts deleted; vm_bootstrap.sh repointed so a FRESH VM is never bootstrapped back into this state; the claude-vm-runner@.service exemption dropped from check_diag_unit_allowlist.py.

STILL OWED — the actual grant is still on the live VM. The purge script runs from the VM's clone of `main`, so the ORDER IS: merge the PR -> ict-git-sync lands it on the VM -> dispatch `purge-vm-runner` -> read its post-state block (it asserts all three artifacts absent, the new file present, and `sudo -n -l /usr/sbin/ufw` still resolving). Dispatching before the sync would fail on a missing script, which is safe but wastes a run.

DO NOT close this row on the merge — the grant is removed when the action has RUN and its post-state check passed, not when the code that removes it lands.

RESOLVED ON A ROOT-VERIFIED POST-STATE (action #9003, exit 0). Every line checked as root:
    [ok] absent  (verified as root): /etc/sudoers.d/claude-vm-runner
    [ok] absent  (verified as root): /usr/local/bin/claude-vm-dispatch
    [ok] absent  (verified as root): /etc/systemd/system/claude-vm-runner@.service
    [ok] present (verified as root): /etc/sudoers.d/ict-ufw
    [ok] ufw grant resolves — the #537/#542/#545 recovery path is intact

THE ANSWER TO THE OPEN QUESTION: the dead sudoers grant was GENUINELY ABSENT. It had already been removed (or was never installed on this box) before any of the three runs. So the split is complete and the ufw grant is preserved and confirmed working.

WORTH RECORDING PRECISELY, because it is the uncomfortable part: run #8993's '[ok] absent' reached the RIGHT ANSWER BY AN INVALID METHOD. It could not read /etc/sudoers.d at all, so it would have printed exactly the same line had the grant been present. Being accidentally correct is not the same as being verified, and treating that run as evidence would have been wrong even though its conclusion happened to match. The row stayed open across two failed attempts for that reason, and that was the right call.

THREE ATTEMPTS, AND BOTH FAILURES WERE IN THE VERIFICATION RATHER THAN THE WORK — the install-first, verify-ufw, remove-last ordering meant nothing was ever removed on a failed run and the recovery path was never at risk:
  #8993 unprivileged [ -f ] on a root-only dir -> false 'absent' for an unreadable path
  #8997 `priv_exists "$p"; v=$?` aborted under set -e on the first non-zero (= genuinely-absent) return, before any post-state printed
  #9003 root-privileged three-state check, set -e-exempt call form -> clean pass

Hardening that outlives this row: tests/ops/test_purge_vm_runner_reaches_post_state.py stubs sudo to force each of the three states and asserts the script reaches a TRUTHFUL post-state in every one, including that an UNDETERMINED path is never reported as a verified absence; and the exact set -e-aborting call form is pinned so it cannot be quietly restored.
updates.next_check: None — verified as root on the live VM, exit 0.

items.title: replay-pregate-nightly has failed 3/3 consecutive scheduled runs and NOTHING alerts -- and 6 of 10 cron'd workflows share the defect
items.source: MEASURED 2026-08-13 via the GH Actions API. Runs 31460751157 (08-11), 31567167485 (08-12), 31671108501 (08-13) -- ALL `failure`, zero successes in the window. Log tail: fleet scoring dies at head 9/22 with 'Timeout, server 158.178.209.121 not responding' -> 'no JSON object in driver output' -> exit 1 (the trainer-VM SSH drops mid-run). WHY IT IS SILENT, verified in the workflow file: both notification steps are gated `if: github.event_name == 'issues'` (.github/workflows/replay-pregate-nightly.yml:203 and :222), while the schedule trigger is at :37 (`cron: 0 4 * * *`) and the job's own `if` at :62 explicitly admits `github.event_name == 'schedule'`. So the nightly path runs and emits nothing on success OR failure. It is also absent from claude-run-failure-alert.yml's watch list (:35-44) and from macro-producer-liveness.yml's registry (:6-9).
items.why_it_matters: This is the 'silently-skipped scheduled job' the 'if you see something, say something' rule names by name. The pre-gate has been dead for at least 3 days and the only reason anyone knows is that an audit read the API. CLASS BREADTH, stated with its denominator: of 10 cron'd workflows, 6 have NO notification on the schedule path -- diag-relay-sweep, doc-audit-weekly, econ-event-study, purge-artifacts, research-backtest-augment, replay-pregate-nightly. Only health-snapshot.yml Telegrams itself; two more are indirectly covered by the macro ledger-freshness check.
items.action: (1) Un-gate the failure notification so it fires on the schedule path too, and add replay-pregate-nightly to claude-run-failure-alert.yml's watch list. (2) Do the same sweep for the other 5 -- a per-workflow fix repeated 6 times is the wrong shape; prefer registering the cron'd set in the existing failure-alert workflow once. (3) SEPARATELY investigate the trainer-VM SSH timeout under the 22-head scoring load (Tier-1 investigation, possibly Tier-2 fix); it is a distinct defect from the silence and must not be closed by fixing the alerting alone.
items.resolution_criteria: A failing scheduled run of any cron'd workflow produces an operator-visible signal, and the pre-gate nightly either passes or its failure is being actively worked.

updates.note:
HALF ONE SHIPPED (the silence). All 9 unwatched cron'd workflows added to claude-run-failure-alert.yml's workflow_run listener, which already existed for exactly this class ('stop waiting, it's dead'). Chose the ONE registration over patching 6-9 workflows' own notify gates: the per-workflow gate is what drifted in the first place, and a listener on the default branch cannot be forgotten by the next workflow author... though note it CAN be, which is why a guard asserting 'every cron'd workflow is watched' is the honest follow-up and is NOT yet built.

MY OWN FIRST COUNT WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. I probed for a literal 'api.telegram.org' in each workflow and concluded 10 of 10 were silent. `Health Snapshot` notifies through scripts/notify_session.py, which that probe cannot see — the sub-class-C unasserted-negative this repo names. The honest population: 10 cron'd; 1 (Health Snapshot) self-notifies and is DELIBERATELY excluded to avoid a double-ping; 9 added.

macro-valuation-snapshot + econ-calendar-produce are included even though macro-producer-liveness watches them: that check asserts their OUTPUT is fresh, which cannot distinguish 'the run errored' from 'the producer is late'. Output-freshness is not run-status coverage. macro-producer-liveness itself is listed too — a silent watchdog is worse than none.

VERIFIED: all 17 watched names resolve to a real workflow `name:` (workflow_run matches on name, not filename — a typo here would fail silently, which is the failure mode of an alerting fix); no duplicates; the only cron'd workflow absent from the listener is the documented Health Snapshot.

HALF TWO STILL OPEN, and it is the one that costs: replay-pregate-nightly is STILL FAILING every night on a trainer-VM SSH timeout at head 9/22 ('Timeout, server 158.178.209.121 not responding'). This change means the next failure is LOUD; it does not make the pre-gate run. That is a separate Tier-1 investigation (trainer SSH under the 22-head scoring load) and this row stays open for it — closing on the alerting alone would be fixing the smoke detector and calling the fire out.

[sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The alerting half is shipped and currently complete: .github/workflows/claude-run-failure-alert.yml:80-89 lists all 9 cron'd workflows (diag-relay-sweep, doc-audit-weekly, econ-calendar-produce, econ-event-study, macro-producer-liveness, macro-valuation-snapshot, purge-artifacts, replay-pregate-nightly, research-backtest-augment) and I enumerated the schedule-carrying workflows independently — exactly those 9 plus health-snapshot.yml, which self-notifies. But nothing asserts that a NEWLY cron'd workflow gets watched (no such guard among the 39 in run_guards.py), and the pre-gate nightly's own trainer-VM SSH failure cannot be checked from here. — needs live data: current run status of replay-pregate-nightly (GH Actions API) to know whether its failure is fixed or being worked. The recurrence half is fixable now.

HIGH-VALUE AND UNCHANGED: 3/3 consecutive silent scheduled failures with nothing alerting, and 6 of 10 cron'd workflows share the defect. This is the same 'the mechanism stopped firing is indistinguishable from it firing quietly' class as the alert-latch read-surface family — and unlike those, nobody would find out.

items.title: Caddy / ict-bot.duckdns.org is a load-bearing production HTTPS transport, appears in ZERO canonical docs, and no diag surface can see it
items.source: MEASURED 2026-08-13. WIRED AND DEFAULT: the Svelte SPA hardcodes it -- ict-trader-dashboard/webapp/src/lib/config.ts:18 `const DEFAULT_BOT_API_URL = "https://ict-bot.duckdns.org"`. Server side: deploy/caddy/Caddyfile:24-27 (`ict-bot.duckdns.org { reverse_proxy localhost:8001 }`), scripts/ops/install_caddy.sh, .github/workflows/vm-caddy-deploy.yml, docs/runbooks/webapp-https-caddy.md. Bot CORS is already wired for it (src/web/api/main.py:65-66). /ws/market streams WSS through it. UNDOCUMENTED: `rg -i 'duckdns|caddy' CLAUDE.md docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md ROADMAP.md` -> ZERO hits, while CLAUDE.md:171-172 still frames the transport story as 'no Vercel rewrite, no Cloudflare tunnel, no cf-worker' and the dashboard repo claims the failure set 'collapses to: Streamlit Cloud, the VM's FastAPI, this script's code' -- now wrong for the SPA, which adds three failure modes (Caddy process, the DuckDNS record, LE cert renewal).

Second-order and worse: `caddy.service` is not an `ict-*` unit, has no deploy/ file, is absent from diag's _CANONICAL_UNITS, and therefore sits OUTSIDE check_diag_unit_allowlist.py's glob entirely (DEPLOY_GLOBS = ('deploy/*.timer','deploy/*.service'), :31). A Caddy outage takes the SPA down and NO diag surface can see it; ict-web-api-watchdog does not cover it. That is the recurring invisible-unit class in a form the guard was not built to catch.
items.action: (1) Document the transport in CLAUDE.md + ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL (the SPA reaches the bot over Caddy/HTTPS; Streamlit still goes direct) and correct the 'no tunnel' framing, which is true of Streamlit and false of the SPA. (2) Add caddy.service to diag _CANONICAL_UNITS so the outage is visible. (3) Decide whether the LE cert-expiry / DuckDNS record is worth its own liveness check -- currently nothing watches either.
items.resolution_criteria: The canonical docs describe the live transport for both frontends, and a Caddy outage is visible on a diag surface.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Both resolution criteria are met on the tree: CLAUDE.md § 'Dashboard consumer' now describes the two transports explicitly (Streamlit plain-HTTP server-side vs the SPA through Caddy/ict-bot.duckdns.org, incl. the LE/DuckDNS failure modes) and docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md also matches `caddy|duckdns`; src/web/api/routers/diag.py:88-102 adds `"caddy.service"` to _CANONICAL_UNITS with a comment recording that check_diag_unit_allowlist.py's deploy/*.service glob cannot see it.

items.title: src/runtime/orders.py's halt check is SKIPPED entirely when HALT_FLAG_PATH is absent from its settings dict -- a third, quieter halt semantics
items.source: Found while single-homing the halt flag (this session's halt-flag fix covered the three READERS; this is the remaining ORDER-PATH site and was deliberately left alone). orders.py:129-132: `halt_flag_path = _get_value(settings, 'HALT_FLAG_PATH', None)` then `if halt_flag_path and os.path.exists(...)`. So when the key is absent from `settings`, the guard short-circuits to False and the halt check does not run at all -- distinct from both the pipeline's env-based check and from the readers' path.
items.what_to_check: NOT YET ESTABLISHED and the reason this is filed rather than fixed: whether `settings` as constructed in production actually carries HALT_FLAG_PATH. If it does, this is latent. If it does not, the orders-layer halt check is inert in production and the pipeline's pre-dispatch check is the ONLY thing enforcing the kill switch. Determine which before proposing a change -- the answer decides whether this is cosmetic or a real second line of defence that is down.
items.action: Establish the production value first. Then, if inert, propose the fix as TIER-3 (it changes when an order can be refused): route orders.py through runtime_flags.halt_flag_path() so the order layer and the pipeline agree, with the fail-direction stated explicitly. Do NOT change the order path on inference.
items.resolution_criteria: The orders-layer halt check either demonstrably runs in production or is deliberately and documentedly not a gate.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The open question is now ANSWERED against the field: src/runtime/validation.py::build_settings_from_env (lines 202-215) — the only production settings constructor, called at src/main.py:632 — returns exchange/symbol/timeframe/risk_per_trade/log_level/tick_interval/loop/MAX_DAILY_LOSS_USD/MAX_OPEN_POSITIONS and NO 'HALT_FLAG_PATH' key. src/runtime/orders.py:129-132 reads that key with default None and short-circuits, so the orders-layer halt check does not run in production; src/runtime/pipeline.py:41,501 is the only live halt enforcement. — Tier-3 (it changes when an order can be refused). Proposed change: route src/runtime/orders.py's halt check through src/runtime/runtime_flags.py::halt_flag_path() so the order layer and the pipeline read one flag, with the fail-direction stated in the code; OR, if the pipeline gate is deliberately the only one, delete the dead check in orders.py and say so. Do not change on inference — operator picks.

Re-validated: a HALT check skipped entirely when HALT_FLAG_PATH is absent from the settings dict. A safety gate that silently no-ops on a missing key is the highest-severity shape in this backlog's structure, even at medium severity.
