items.title: After the TTL cap went 60 -> 300 every capped frame's fetch rate fell except 1d, which ROSE 6.5% — the frame with the largest expected win
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 comparing two tick_cost reads: pre-flip n=19 ticks (process 06:21:38Z) vs post-flip n=4 ticks (process 08:04:17Z, diag #8954). Denominators stated because every figure below is a per-tick RATE over those two samples, not a raw count. Per-tick fetch counts:

  1h   8.84 -> 5.25  (-40.6%)
  2h   4.32 -> 2.00  (-53.7%)
  4h   5.26 -> 2.50  (-52.5%)
  1d   3.05 -> 3.25  (+6.5%)   <-- the outlier
  control 15m+5m+1m 19.00 -> 16.25 (-14.5%)

Headline cache hit rate 21.5% -> 41.5%, so the cap IS working overall; this row is about the one frame that did not follow.

STATE THE POPULATION: post-flip n=4 ticks, over which 1d was fetched 13 times (13 of 117 total post-flip misses). That is small enough that +6.5% on 1d could be noise on its own — but it is the only capped frame that failed to move in the same direction as its three siblings, all of which fell 40-54%, and 1d is the frame where the cap should bite HARDEST (8640s wanted vs 60s granted before, now 300s).
items.why_it_matters: 1d was the single largest line in the original finding — 762 fetches in 2h at 2.4-3.6s each, 13.9% of tick on-loop. It is the frame the whole cap argument was strongest for, so a non-response is exactly the result worth chasing rather than averaging into a favourable headline. Plausible causes NOT yet distinguished: the off-loop exit loop dominates 1d (its offloop n=22 vs on-loop 13, and the exit loop runs on its own cadence so its inter-fetch gap may exceed 300s); more distinct 1d symbols than other frames, so each (symbol,tf,limit) key is hit less often; or a `since=` parameter on some 1d reads, which is never cached by design.
items.resolution_criteria: A tick_cost read at ticks_measured >= 30 on a single post-flip process either (a) shows fetch.1d per-tick falling in line with its siblings, closing this as small-sample noise, or (b) confirms it stays flat/up, in which case the cause is identified among the three candidates above — distinguished by comparing on-loop vs off-loop 1d counts and checking whether the 1d callers pass `since=`. Either way the outcome is recorded on the CANDLE_CACHE_TTL row in CLAUDE.md so the headline hit-rate is never read as covering 1d.
items.next_action: One warm tick_cost read once the current process has 30+ ticks (~1h). Tier-1, read-only.

updates.note:
RESOLVED — DIAGNOSED at n=40, and the answer is that the 1d frame is behaving CORRECTLY. There is no cache bug; the cap simply sits below 1d's reuse period.

THE MATURE SAMPLE, finally obtained (diag #9170): process_started_utc 2026-08-14T05:17:25Z, ticks_measured 40, ~87.2 min uptime, so the tick INTERVAL is 87.2*60/40 = 131s (note this is the interval, not the 72.3s mean tick DURATION — they are different numbers and the TTL competes with the interval). On-loop per-tick fetch rates against the row's pre-flip / post-flip baselines:
    1h   3.73   (pre 8.84, post 5.25)   -57.9% vs pre
    2h   1.52   (pre 4.32, post 2.00)   -64.7%
    4h   1.82   (pre 5.26, post 2.50)   -65.3%
    1d   3.02   (pre 3.05, post 3.25)    -0.8%   <-- the outlier, confirmed
    ctl 16.05   (pre 19.00, post 16.25) -15.5%   (15m+5m+1m, uncapped)
So at 4x the largest previous sample the anomaly is real and not noise: every capped sibling fell 58-65% while 1d did not move.

THE CAUSE — arithmetic, not a defect. config/strategies.yaml has SIXTEEN enabled 1d strategies, each pinned to its own symbol (MES MGC MHG SPY QQQ TQQQ QLD IWM GLD TLT IEF SLV GDX SPLG IAUM SCHA). 121 fetches / 16 symbols = 7.6 fetches per symbol over 40 ticks, i.e. each 1d symbol is re-requested about once every 40/7.6*131 = **692 SECONDS**. The TTL is 300s. 692 > 300, so every 1d entry has ALREADY EXPIRED on its own TTL before the next request for that symbol arrives. The cache cannot hit, and raising 60 -> 300 could not have helped, because 300 was still less than half the revisit interval. 1h/2h/4h improved precisely because their revisit intervals fall INSIDE 300s.

TWO OF THE THREE CANDIDATE CAUSES ARE REFUTED, not merely unselected:
  * `since=` reads never cached — REFUTED. Zero callers pass since= on the signal path (grep over src/ for fetch_candles(... since ...)     returns 0); the only since= mention in market_data.py is its own error string. `limit` is 200 at 22 of 26 call sites, so key     fragmentation by limit is not material either.
  * off-loop exit-loop dominance — REFUTED AS THE CAUSE. Off-loop fetch.1d is n=242 vs on-loop 121, exactly 2.00x, holding the ratio     seen at every earlier sample. But the ON-LOOP rate is fully explained by the revisit interval alone, so the exit loop does not need     to be invoked to account for it. (It remains true that the exit loop is the larger 1d consumer in absolute terms.)
  * more distinct 1d symbols — CONFIRMED, in the precise form above: 16 symbols spreading the per-symbol revisit interval past the TTL.

NOTED WHILE READING, NOT THE CAUSE HERE: market_data.py::_candle_cache_put bounds the map by CLEARING IT ENTIRELY at >512 entries rather than evicting LRU. That is not what is happening to 1d (the TTL expiry alone accounts for it), but a wholesale flush disproportionately harms exactly the long-revisit frames, so it is worth knowing if the cap is ever raised.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY FIX 1d, IF THE OPERATOR WANTS IT (Tier-3, NOT actioned): a cap above ~700s would bring 1d's revisit interval inside the TTL. That is well within 1d's OWN declared tolerance — the CANDLE_CACHE_TTL_FRACTION contract is 10% of the bar, which for a daily bar is 8640s, so even 900s would be 1.0% of the bar. But the VALUE is Tier-3 (strategies read close.iloc[-1] as the current price for entry geometry, and the monitor reads it for exits), so this is a proposal, not a change. The measured upside is bounded: 1d is 15.5% of on-loop tick time here, and eliminating its misses is worth at most that.

items.title: Four live env vars had no read surface — a new var can ship without being added to get_env.py's ALLOWED_KEYS, and nothing catches it
items.source:
FOUND BY HITTING IT. The Tier-3 write of CANDLE_CACHE_TTL_MAX_S (60 -> 300, #8949) was followed by the standard post-state verification via get-env (#8950), which FAILED: "key 'CANDLE_CACHE_TTL_MAX_S' is not allowlisted". The key had shipped in PR #8815 the same night without being added to ALLOWED_KEYS, so its first live write could not be read back.

A sweep of the same class found 4 of 4 checked vars missing (measured against src/, not inferred):
  CANDLE_CACHE_TTL_MAX_S       src/runtime/market_data.py   (mine, #8815)
  EXIT_LOOP_DECOUPLE_DISABLED  src/main.py                  (M20 decouple, #8778)
  EXIT_LOOP_INTERVAL_SECONDS   src/main.py                  (same)
  EXIT_LOOP_STALE_SECONDS      src/runtime/exit_loop_health.py (same)

So this is not a one-off slip by one author — two separate PRs on two different nights each added live env vars and neither added the reader.
items.why_it_matters:
get-env exists precisely to close write-without-a-reader on order-path settings (BL-20260810-CONVICTION-SIZING-APPLY-LIVE-VS-DOC). The gap reopens silently every time a new var ships, and the failure only surfaces when someone tries to verify a write — i.e. AFTER the write is already live.

EXIT_LOOP_DECOUPLE_DISABLED is the sharpest instance. It is a kill-switch whose set state makes exit_loop_health report `never_ran`, which that contract calls "emphatically NOT healthy" — and the decoupled exit loop is the one condition the liveness watchdog explicitly no longer covers. A set switch would have produced an unhealthy grade with no way to read back the cause.

CANDLE_CACHE_TTL_MAX_S bounds how stale the price behind a live order may be, so it belongs in the "reason this exists" tier, not the cadence tier.
items.resolution_criteria: All four keys present in ALLOWED_KEYS and returned by `get_env.py --list-keys`, with `--self-test` still PASS. Verified: 43 keys listed, all four confirmed present, self-test PASS (5 states incl. pending_restart and the two undetermined paths).
items.resolution: RESOLVED same session. All four added with comments naming why each belongs. NOT resolved by this row and left open deliberately: nothing PREVENTS the next var from shipping without a reader — a guard would need to diff env-var reads in src/ against ALLOWED_KEYS, which is the provenance-consumer-guard shape applied to the ops read surface. Filed as its own item rather than folded in here, because 'we fixed the four we found' is not the same claim as 'this cannot recur'.
items.next_action: See BL-20260813-NO-GUARD-FOR-ENV-READ-SURFACE for the recurrence half.

items.title: Nothing prevents the next env var shipping without a get-env read surface — the recurrence half of the four found on 2026-08-13
items.source:
Split from BL-20260813-ENV-VARS-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE, which fixed the four instances found (CANDLE_CACHE_TTL_MAX_S, EXIT_LOOP_DECOUPLE_DISABLED, EXIT_LOOP_INTERVAL_SECONDS, EXIT_LOOP_STALE_SECONDS). Those came from TWO separate PRs on two different nights (#8815 and #8778), which is the evidence that it is a recurring class and not one author's slip.

The detection today was accidental: it surfaced only because a Tier-3 write happened to be followed by a post-state verification. A var that is never written from a session would sit unreadable indefinitely and nothing would say so.
items.why_it_matters: This is provenance-consumer-guard's own shape applied one level up at the ops surface: a setting that can be WRITTEN but not READ is exactly the asymmetry that guard exists to catch in code, and the ops read surface has no equivalent. The cost is not hypothetical — CONVICTION_SIZING_ACCOUNTS is the recorded case where an EMPTY value meant EVERY account including real money and no surface could establish the live value (BL-20260810).
items.resolution_criteria: A CI guard fails when a file under src/ reads an env var (os.environ.get / os.getenv) that is absent from get_env.py's ALLOWED_KEYS, with a declared exemption list for vars genuinely not worth a read surface (each exemption carrying a one-line reason, verified-not-presence-only in the style of collapsed-state-guard). The guard must ship with a self-test proving it FAILS on a planted unlisted var, and must state its denominator (vars scanned / listed / exempted) so a clean run is a measured clean rather than an empty scan.
items.next_action: Model it on scripts/check_provenance_consumers.py, which already does writer-vs-consumer matching. Tier-1.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Enumerated the 39 registered guards in scripts/ci/run_guards.py (`"name":` keys) — none scans env-var reads against scripts/ops/get_env.py::ALLOWED_KEYS; scripts/ci/ holds no such check, and `grep -l ALLOWED_KEYS scripts/` returns only get_env.py itself. So the recurrence half is still unguarded. — Tier-1 CI. Ends when a guard fails on a src/ env read absent from ALLOWED_KEYS, with a declared exemption list carrying reasons and a self-test proving it fails on a planted unlisted var.

Re-validated and it GENERALISES to this review's own top finding. The row asks for a guard so an env var cannot ship without a get-env read surface; the identical gap let prop_risk_gate ship a *_MODE knob with NO soak writer and NO diag allowlist entry (BL-20260829-PROP-RISK-GATE-PROMISED-A-SOAK-ROW-AND-WROTE-NOTHING, filed and fixed today). Recommend widening this row's fix to: any *_MODE gate must have a soak writer AND a diag read surface, checked in CI. That one guard retires the largest class in this backlog.

items.title: backtest_trend.py --symbol is a display LABEL while --data silently defaults to a BTC fixture; account_compat_matrix.py has the same shape
items.source: trainer relays #8969 (the void run) and #8975 (the corrected re-run)
items.what_to_check: scripts/backtest_trend.py:885 `--data` defaults to data/backtest_candles.csv -- 5,001 rows of BTC 1-MINUTE candles spanning 2022-07-23..27 -- while `--symbol` (:887) only labels the output. Passing --symbol SOLUSDT without --data therefore grades BTC-1m-over-one-long-weekend and prints it under a 'SOLUSDT 1h' heading. MEASURED 2026-08-13 (#8969): a breakout_1 prop EV/survival gate returned a confident skip at ev_net_usd -$69,945 (SOL) / -$138,467 (ETH), computed entirely from that fixture and extrapolated from 3.5 days to a '(12-mo)' horizon. The corrected run (#8975) on the real per-symbol data returned ROUTE at +$483 / +$883 -- the verdict INVERTED. scripts/prop/account_compat_matrix.py:258 has the identical shape, defaulting --data to /home/user/ict-trader-data/btc_5m.parquet: two harnesses in one call chain, two silent BTC fallbacks. Diagnostic-provenance sub-class B (implicit input selection) feeding sub-class A (the label names a quantity the code never read). THE TELL that caught it, worth keeping: two DIFFERENT symbols returned byte-identical data spans, and 74 trades in 84 hourly bars is arithmetically impossible. Neither is visible unless the span is printed and read. scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py::resolve_data is the only caller that avoids this, because it carries its own resolver. FIX: make --data required, or default it to resolve_data(symbol, tf), or emit a loud warning when the fixture path is used with a --symbol that is not BTC. A run whose declared symbol and loaded data disagree should refuse, not print.
items.why_it_matters: This sits directly under the prop-account routing gate, i.e. a Tier-3 live-wiring decision. The void run produced a plausible, confidently-formatted verdict with the WRONG SIGN. Nothing in the output said which file it read.
items.resolution_criteria: Run `scripts/backtest_trend.py --symbol SOLUSDT --timeframe 1h` with NO --data. Closable when it either exits non-zero naming the missing input, or loads the SOLUSDT file -- confirmed by the printed `  data <start> -> <end>` line NOT reading `2022-07-23 21:24:00+00:00 -> 2022-07-27 08:43:00+00:00` (the BTC fixture span). Repeat for `scripts/prop/account_compat_matrix.py --symbol SOLUSDT` with no --data against its own btc_5m.parquet default. BOTH harnesses must pass; fixing one leaves the call chain broken. A run that still silently loads the fixture keeps this row open however good the surrounding docs are.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Both defaults are unchanged. scripts/backtest_trend.py:885 still has `p.add_argument("--data", default=os.environ.get("BACKTEST_DATA_PATH", "data/backtest_candles.csv"))` beside `--symbol` defaulting to BTCUSDT at :887, and scripts/prop/account_compat_matrix.py:258 still has `p.add_argument("--data", default="/home/user/ict-trader-data/btc_5m.parquet")`. Greps for a symbol/data mismatch refusal or a resolve_data call in either file return nothing. backtest_trend.py does print data_start/data_end (:731, :820) — the tell that caught it — but nothing refuses.
Re-validated: a --symbol that is a display label over a silently-defaulted BTC fixture is the diagnostic-provenance sub-class B shape (implicit input selection). Two tools share it.

items.title: A guard that greps for the bad value reads a CRASH as a pass; pair it with a stale artifact and it certifies the previous run
items.source: trainer relay #8973
items.what_to_check: After BL-20260813-HARNESS-SYMBOL-IS-A-LABEL-DATA-DEFAULTS-TO-BTC, the follow-up probe guarded the input with `grep -qF "<fixture span>" out.txt` -- i.e. it tested for the ABSENCE of the wrong answer. The harness then died at import (ModuleNotFoundError: pandas, bare python3 instead of the venv), printed no span at all, and the guard read that silence as innocence. Compounding it, the emit path was reused from the prior run and never truncated, so `wc -l` reported the PREVIOUS void run's ledger: the probe printed '-- emitted 74 trades' / '129 trades', byte-identical to #8969, for a run that computed nothing. Had numpy been importable, it would have produced a confident SOL/ETH prop verdict off BTC 1-minute data, now laundered through a guard that certified the input. An unrelated missing dependency is the only reason it did not. PATTERN TO ENFORCE (already applied in #8975): assert the evidence is PRESENT and correct, never that the wrong value is absent; truncate an artifact before writing it; check the exit code; and give each refusal its own named state (env_unavailable / harness_error / unverified_input / no_trades / insufficient_sample) so 'we could not look' never reads as a verdict. This is the consumer-side half of sub-class C and the same shape silent-empty-guard catches on the producer side -- consider whether diagnostic-provenance-guard can flag `grep -q <literal>` used as an input-provenance check in scripts/{ml,research,ops}/.
items.why_it_matters: The guard was written specifically to prevent the defect it then let through. A guard that is cheaper to satisfy than to actually pass is worse than no guard (the new-table-wiring-guard lesson).
items.resolution_criteria: Closable when a check flags `grep -q <literal>` (and equivalents) used as an INPUT-PROVENANCE test in scripts/{ml,research,ops}/, demonstrated the way the other guards self-test: plant a probe that greps for a bad value, see it flagged; plant one that asserts a positive match plus a non-zero exit code, see it pass. Absent a new check, closable when diagnostic-provenance-guard's --all run over those directories reports zero absence-tests AND that count is shown to be a real denominator (a planted positive is detected), so a clean result is not just an empty scan.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The row's own suggested enforcement — 'consider whether diagnostic-provenance-guard can flag `grep -q <literal>` used as an input-provenance check in scripts/{ml,research,ops}/' — has not shipped: scripts/check_diagnostic_provenance.py has no pattern for grep-as-assertion (its only 'literal' mention is a prose comment at :175 about unquantified universal claims). The pattern was applied by hand in #8975 but nothing enforces it. — The class is real and recurring (a guard that greps for the bad value reads a CRASH as a pass; paired with a stale artifact it certifies the previous run). Ending condition: either the guard gains the check with a planted positive control, or the four-part discipline (assert evidence present not absent; truncate before writing; check the exit code; name each refusal state) is written into docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md § Generation Discipline so relay probes inherit it.

Re-validated: a guard that greps for the bad value reads a CRASH as a pass. The repo's better guards already self-test (11 registered self-tests, all wired, verified in this session's CI run) — the fix is to extend that discipline to the rest.

items.title: pull-and-deploy silently skips the post-deploy version assertion when DIAG_READ_TOKEN is unset, and still reports success
items.source: system-action run 31684933837 (issue #8974), deploying af9be48
items.what_to_check: scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh emitted '>>> Skipping post-deploy version assertion (DIAG_READ_TOKEN unset and /etc/ict-trading-bot/diag_token not readable).' and then '>>> Recorded deploy marker: af9be48' + wrapper exit 0. So the one step that confirms the RUNNING process actually rolled forward did not run, and the deploy reported success anyway. On this particular run the roll-forward is independently evidenced (post-sync HEAD printed, systemd restart visible in the journal tail), but that is luck of the log format, not the assertion. The check exists precisely for the BL-20260706 class, where the on-disk script was itself stale and its own fetch could not pull the fix that would repair it. Skipping it silently reproduces the condition it guards. FIX: make the skip a loud WARN in the workflow comment (not just a log line), or read the token the same way the prop-report workflow does (sourced from /etc/ict-trader/web-api.env on the VM), or fall back to asserting `git rev-parse HEAD` against the systemd MainPID's cwd. Also seen in the same run and probably benign but unexamined: 'scripts/install_systemd_units.sh: line 392: /etc/ict-vm-role: No such file or directory' on the live trader, which is why both gateway timers log 'skip enable (gateway-only; host role=unset)'. Correct outcome, but it reaches it via a file-not-found error rather than a declared role.
items.why_it_matters: A deploy that cannot verify what is running is a green that checked nothing, on the money box.
items.resolution_criteria: Closable when a real `pull-and-deploy` system-action issue comment either (a) shows the post-deploy version assertion RUNNING and matching the deployed SHA, or (b) surfaces the skip as an explicit WARN in the COMMENT BODY -- not only in the log tail -- so an operator reading the comment cannot mistake the run for verified. Verify by reading the comment on the next deploy, not by reading the script.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The silent skip is unchanged: scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh:518-522 still echoes '>>> Skipping post-deploy version assertion (…)' for three conditions including DIAG_READ_TOKEN unset AND /etc/ict-trading-bot/diag_token unreadable, and the script continues to the deploy marker and exit 0 with nothing surfaced in the workflow comment (greps of .github/workflows/system-actions.yml for the skip string return nothing). — IMPORTANT — the obvious fix would make things worse, and this changed since filing. Commit a0f559b (2026-08-16) filed BL-20260816-DEPLOY-VERSION-ASSERTION-CANNOT-FAIL: the assertion this row wants un-skipped compares /api/diag/version to POST_SYNC_HEAD, and /api/diag/version re-reads ON-DISK HEAD, which IS POST_SYNC_HEAD at that point — so an un-restarted web-api returns the new sha and PASSES. Making a vacuous assertion louder is not a fix. Ending condition: close this row against that one's criterion 3 (compare against the runtime_logs/deployed_sha.txt marker or a genuine in-process value, or delete the assertion), and only then surface the skip.

Re-validated and it COMPOUNDS a live observation: at 16:06Z today /api/diag/version read git_sha eb061699 against git_sha_on_disk fccd9a16 with restart_pending true — code pulled, process not restarted. It resolved by 16:22Z. A deploy that skips its own version assertion when DIAG_READ_TOKEN is unset and still reports success is exactly how that state goes unnoticed.

RE-OBSERVED LIVE, 18 days after filing — the condition still holds and the row is correctly still open. Deploying PR #10544 (per-account arbitration, merged 12e4a9e) via pull-and-deploy issue #10553, the run printed ">>> Skipping post-deploy version assertion (DIAG_READ_TOKEN unset and /etc/ict-trading-bot/diag_token not readable)." and then reported "wrapper exit code: 0" / completed. So a deploy of a Tier-3 order-path change reported success while its own verification step no-opped. === THE CODE WAS IN FACT FINE, WHICH IS THE POINT. An independent /api/diag/version read (direct path, served by ict-bot.duckdns.org) returned git_sha 12e4a9eb == git_sha_on_disk, restart_pending false, and /api/diag/status showed uptime 254s with a 38s heartbeat — so the restart genuinely rolled the code forward. The defect is not that the deploy was wrong; it is that the deploy's OWN output could not distinguish that from a stale-code deploy, and a session that trusted it would have had no way to tell. Establishing it took a separate manual read this session. === NOTE THE INTERACTION with BL-20260823-DIAG-VERSION-REPORTS-DISK-SHA-NOT-RUNNING-CODE (resolved): now that /api/diag/version reports the RUNNING sha rather than the disk sha, this assertion would finally be meaningful if it ran — which raises the value of fixing the skip, because the check it skips is no longer vacuous.

items.title: bybit_2 (REAL MONEY): the margin pre-flight cap sizes from TOTAL EQUITY, not available margin — 9 venue refusals across 3 strategies and 2 symbols, 30% of the account's orders
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 (diag #8990), filtering trades on status=exchange_rejected across ALL strategies rather than one leg — which is how this was found at all: every prior read was AVAX-scoped and structurally could not have seen it.

Of the newest 25 exchange rejections (2026-07-30T22:11Z -> 2026-08-13T01:27Z) there are exactly TWO causes and TWO symbols:
  AVAXUSDT  18  venue max exceeded   ict_scalp_avax_5m  bybit_1 (demo)
  BTCUSDT    7  ErrCode 110007       ict_scalp_5m       bybit_2 (REAL MONEY)

This row is the second one. Full venue text: 'ab not enough for new order (ErrCode: 110007)' — Bybit's available-balance refusal, NOT a structural lot limit. The request is well-formed:
  qty 0.011 BTCUSDT Buy Market, tpslMode Partial, tpSize/slSize 0.011

ALL SEVEN ARE THE IDENTICAL SIZE, 0.011 BTC — ids 4252, 4302, 4325, 4328, 4339, 4359, 4366, account_class real_money, is_demo 0. A repeated identical size against a repeated balance refusal means the sizer is not adapting to the account's actual available balance: it recomputes the same number and the venue refuses it again.

NOT COVERED BY THE VENUE-MAX CLAMP shipped today for BL-20260810 — that clamp engages on qty > maxOrderQty and this order is nowhere near a lot ceiling. Recording that explicitly so the two are never conflated: a fix for one does nothing for the other.

updates.note:
ROOT-CAUSED, and the mechanism is NOT what the opening note guessed. Four measurements, each one falsifiable, and one hypothesis I raised and then REFUTED.

1. THE CAP BOUND — this is not an unbounded sizer. All seven orders are exactly 0.011 BTC while confidence varies 0.6982..0.9466 and stop distance varies 119.05..334.95. Risk-based sizing (1.5% of ~$275 equity / stop distance) would have produced 0.0121..0.0340 — a 2.8x spread that cannot floor to a constant. So risk.py::position_size's margin pre-flight cap (available x leverage x _MARGIN_SAFETY_BUFFER / entry) is what produced 0.011 on all seven.

2. REFUTED: 'the venue leverage is not the configured 3x'. That was my first hypothesis and it is WRONG. journalctl at the 2026-08-13T08:04Z boot (diag #9008) shows 'set_leverage pre-flight: account=bybit_2 symbol=BTCUSDT x3 already set (retCode=110043, idempotent)' — the venue confirms 3x. Recording the refutation so no future session re-runs it.

3. THE CAP'S INPUT WAS NOT THE VENUE'S AVAILABLE MARGIN — proved by contradiction from measured quantities only. Inverting qty==0.011 across the seven entry prices at 3x/0.9 pins the cap's input basis to a NON-EMPTY intersection of $264.71..$278.69. Meanwhile the smallest of the seven orders needed initial margin $229.92 and Bybit refused it for insufficient available balance, so the venue's available was BELOW $229.92. Input >= $264.71 while available < $229.92: the cap was fed something other than broker truth.

4. WHAT IT WAS FED IS TOTAL EQUITY. balance_snapshots for bybit_2 across 2026-08-02T01:00Z..2026-08-05T14:01Z (diag #9010) is 92 hourly rows: equity min $271.64 / max $278.97 / mean $274.91, and open_positions == 2 at EVERY row. The implied input band straddles EQUITY, not equity minus the initial margin those two positions had already committed. That is coordinator.py's buffer-fallback path: when _fetch_linear_available_balance returns None the sizer falls back to total_account_usd (total equity) and multiplies it by leverage as though NONE of it were already pledged.

WHY IT WENT UNATTRIBUTABLE: coordinator.py:1379 logs available_usd vs total_account_usd at DEBUG, so in production the one line that distinguishes 'we read broker truth' from 'we could not, here is equity instead' does not exist. The journal row records the sized qty and Bybit's refusal text but NOT the basis we sized from. This is the repo's own collapsed-states rule: available_usd=None ('we did not look') and available_usd=<figure> ('we looked') produce a cap the record cannot tell apart. Reaching the conclusion above required four separate diag pulls and an argument by contradiction; the next occurrence would cost the same.

AND WHY _fetch_linear_available_balance RETURNS None IS ITSELF UNOBSERVED. It reads account['totalAvailableBalance'], treats ''/'null' as absent, falls through to the per-coin availableToWithdraw that Bybit DEPRECATED for UTA on 2025-01-09, then returns None — and logs nothing on either the deprecated branch or the None. That is the silent-empty producer shape. Note the second-order risk: if it took the DEPRECATED branch rather than returning None, the figure it returned would be wallet-balance-like, which is the exact defect BL-20260701-BYBIT-AVAILABLE-FIELD claimed to close. I cannot distinguish those two from here — there is no diag surface for a Bybit raw wallet response (/api/diag/broker_account_status is Alpaca-only) — and BOTH are the same class: a substitute silently wearing the label of broker truth. The fix is the same either way.

SCOPE IS ACCOUNT-WIDE; THE SYMPTOM IS BALANCE-GATED. bybit_1 ($156,365) and bybit_portfolio ($89,914) run the identical code path and would have the identical over-permissive ceiling — they simply never bind it, because the cap only matters when it is below the risk-based size. Reading 'only bybit_2 rejects' as 'only bybit_2 is affected' would be wrong.

CONDITION IS LATENT, NOT CLEARED. ict_scalp_5m is alive and evaluating BTCUSDT every ~2 minutes (diag #9007: 25 consecutive ict_scalp_eval rows through 2026-08-13T12:09:43Z, all side=none for legitimate setup reasons — 'no liquidity sweep in last 12 bars' / 'no displacement bar' / 'no qualifying FVG'). It has produced no actionable BTC setup since 2026-08-04, which is why the rejections stopped; it is not a silent strategy and nothing was fixed. bybit_2 equity today is $280.75 against $274.91 mean in the window, so the next actionable BTC signal re-runs the same arithmetic to the same refusal.

DENOMINATOR (the opening note correctly refused to state a rate; here it is). Newest 30 ict_scalp_5m rows of ANY status, 2026-07-27T14:24Z..2026-08-04T07:35Z, evenly split 10/10/10 across bybit_1 / bybit_2 / bybit_portfolio: bybit_2 is 7 exchange_rejected + 3 closed — so SEVEN OF TEN real-money attempts in the window were refused by the venue. The bybit_1 'rejected size=0.0' rows are a DIFFERENT and correct behaviour (flip_suppressed_hold_policy / reentry_suppressed_netting_guard) and must not be pooled with these.

TIER RAISED 2 -> 3 and severity medium -> high: the fix changes real-money position sizing.

POINTER NOTE (corrected same session): BL-20260701-BYBIT-AVAILABLE-FIELD had NO row when I first wrote this — it existed only as an id in src/units/accounts/{execute,risk}.py docstrings and two tests, so all five citations pointed at nothing. artifact-validity-guard refused the commit that referenced it, which is the guard working: I filed the row rather than rewording around the check. That the earlier fix left its evidence in comments instead of a tracked item is part of why this seam could regress unobserved.

SCOPE CORRECTED — IT IS NOT ONE STRATEGY OR ONE SYMBOL, and my own two previous notes on this row said it was. Reading bybit_2's trades by ACCOUNT rather than by strategy (diag #9015, newest 30 rows 2026-07-21..2026-08-11) finds NINE exchange_rejected rows, and every one is ErrCode 110007:

    trend_donchian   BTCUSDT   x1   (4013) 0.011
    xrp_pullback_2h  XRPUSDT   x1   (4047) 270.062

The earlier '7 BTC rejections by ict_scalp_5m' framing was an artifact of having filtered by STRATEGY — the same class of scoping error that hid this whole family from the AVAX-scoped reads before it. The defect belongs to the ACCOUNT's sizing path; the strategy that trips it is whichever one signals while pledged margin is high.

THE NATURAL EXPERIMENT — the journal proves the mechanism without any arithmetic from me. The SAME 0.011 BTC size, the SAME account:
    3909  2026-07-23T19:44  ict_scalp_5m    0.011  -> FILLED (closed)   pledged margin $0.00, no open legs
    4013  2026-07-25T18:52  trend_donchian  0.011  -> 110007 REFUSED    pledged margin $101.34 (XRP $133.66 + ETH $170.36 open)
Same size, same venue, same account, opposite outcomes — separated by whether other positions were holding margin. That is the mechanism stated as an observation rather than a derivation.

INDEPENDENT CROSS-CHECK OF THE AVAILABLE FIGURE. Two estimates derived from different evidence agree: (a) the contradiction proof off Bybit's own refusal put available BELOW $229.92; (b) reconstructing pledged margin from the journal's open legs (XRPUSDT 4163 at $161.55 held continuously from 2026-07-29 to today, plus ETHUSDT 4134 at $76.61) gives IM $79.39 at 3x and so available ~$195.52. (b) sits inside (a). The two open legs also reconcile exactly with the independently-measured open_positions == 2 in every one of the 92 hourly balance_snapshots.

PART A VALIDATED RETROACTIVELY — the proposal is no longer just a proposal. Replaying the corrected basis (equity - SUM(open_notional/leverage)) against all nine rejections, with the SAME 0.9 buffer, every one becomes an order the account's available margin covers:
    4366/4359/4339/4302/4252  0.011 -> 0.008 BTC   (IM ~$170 vs available ~$196)
    4328/4325                 0.011 -> 0.007 BTC   (IM ~$147 vs available ~$183)
    4013                      0.011 -> 0.007 BTC   (IM ~$150 vs available ~$174)
    4047                    270.062 -> 142 XRP     (IM ~$52  vs available ~$58)
It also lands in the range the account ACTUALLY fills at: the ict_scalp_5m orders that succeeded in the same period were 0.004, 0.005 and 0.007 (4258, 4076, 4180). So the corrected cap does not strangle the leg — it reproduces the sizes that were already working.

LIMITS OF THE ABOVE, STATED. Equity is held at the MEASURED $274.91 window mean for all nine rows, but hourly snapshots only cover 2026-08-02..08-05 — the 07-25 and 07-27 rows use it as an APPROXIMATION, not a reading. The pledged-margin model (notional/leverage) ignores unrealised PnL and fee reserves and assumes every leg sits at 3x cross, so it is an ESTIMATE — which is exactly what Part A proposes to use and why Part A must stamp it ESTIMATED rather than pass it off as measured. The validation is therefore directional-with-margin, not exact; it clears in every case by $25-$45, not by cents.

MEASURED DIRECTLY — and it CORRECTS my own scope claim from the 12:20 update, which said the defect was account-wide and merely balance-gated. That was WRONG. Read via the new Bybit arm on /api/diag/broker_account_status (deploy confirmed, git_sha 965eefba == the merge commit, so this is not a stale process answering):
    bybit_1          paper        venue_available   $79,988.85
    bybit_2          REAL MONEY   unavailable       null
    bybit_portfolio  paper        venue_available   $60,077.54
BOTH PAPER BOOKS GET BROKER TRUTH. THE ONE REAL-MONEY BOOK DOES NOT. It is not that bybit_1 and bybit_portfolio share the defect and never bind the ceiling — they are not on the fallback at all. The figures they return are sane and position-aware (bybit_1 $79,989 available against $156,366 equity with 5 positions open; bybit_portfolio $60,078 against $89,914 with 2), which also confirms the field works correctly wherever it is present.

This also upgrades the diagnosis from INFERRED to MEASURED. The 12:20 conclusion that the cap runs on the equity fallback for bybit_2 was reached by contradiction across four diag pulls; it is now a direct reading of the branch taken. And it is STRUCTURAL, not intermittent — available_usd is None on every dispatch for this account, so the cap has never once had broker truth to work from.

WHY bybit_2 SPECIFICALLY IS NOT YET ESTABLISHED — do not let the next session assume. What is known: bybit_1/bybit_portfolio are Bybit DEMO-endpoint books while bybit_2 is mainnet real money, and bybit_2 is the account the broker-truth ledger records as having mixed spot+perp and SWITCHED SUB-ACCOUNTS on 2026-05-10 (sub_accounts MAIN + SUB). A key scoped to a sub-account, or an account that is not UTA/UNIFIED, would make get_wallet_balance(accountType='UNIFIED') return no account object. That is a HYPOTHESIS; the first read could not test it because the detail string collapsed three different causes into one line (see below).

THE FIRST READ EXPOSED A RESIDUAL COLLAPSE INSIDE MY OWN CONTRACT. `unavailable` was correct — we could not look — but its detail ('neither totalAvailableBalance nor per-coin availableToWithdraw present') could not distinguish (a) the venue REFUSED the read with a retCode, (b) the read succeeded and carried NO account object, (c) an account object was present but LACKED both fields, (d) the call RAISED. Those are four different bugs with four different fixes. Registering a three-state contract does not make the states internally honest — the state was right and the detail was not, which is the same shape as a failure message naming a cause no code path tested. Now staged, so the NEXT read of this route names which one.

THE FIX PRIORITY CHANGES AS A RESULT. Making the equity fallback subtract pledged margin (Part A) is now DEFENCE IN DEPTH, not the primary fix. The primary fix is that bybit_2's wallet read should SUCCEED — every other Bybit book's does. If it is an accountType/sub-account mismatch then the sizer gets broker truth and the fallback never runs for this account at all, which is strictly better than a smarter fallback. Part A remains worth doing because a read CAN fail transiently on any account, and when it does the basis must not count pledged margin as free — but it should no longer be presented as the whole answer.

THE DERIVATION IS REFUTED, AND I MADE THE EXACT ERROR I HAD JUST DIAGNOSED. One read earlier I wrote that 'totalEquity AND totalInitialMargin both sit in that response with values' and proposed deriving available margin as totalEquity - totalInitialMargin. I inferred that from the KEY LIST — the key was present — and assumed presence implied a value. That is precisely the present-vs-populated confusion I had corrected in the code one level up, in the same hour, and I then committed it in prose. Reading the VALUES (diag #9029, git_sha 0a95d0b8):
    accountType            'UNIFIED'
    totalEquity            '280.07421681'   <- populated
    totalWalletBalance     '269.27775375'   <- populated
    totalMarginBalance     ''
    totalAvailableBalance  ''
    totalInitialMargin     ''               <- EMPTY. The derivation is NOT COMPUTABLE.
    totalMaintenanceMargin ''
    accountIMRate/MMRate/LTV  ''
EVERY account-level margin aggregate is empty. Only totalEquity and totalWalletBalance carry values, and their difference ($10.80) is unrealised PnL — consistent with the open XRP short's +$11.47 measured independently, and emphatically NOT available margin. Anything that presses that $10.80 into service as an available figure is fabricating.

THIS IS WHY THE PREVIOUS STEP DELIBERATELY COMPUTED NOTHING. Had the derivation been built when it looked obvious, it would have shipped against a field that does not exist and failed in a way that reads as an arithmetic bug rather than a missing input. The check cost one diag read; skipping it would have cost a real-money sizing change built on a false premise.

WHAT THE EMPTINESS MEANS. Bybit reports accountType UNIFIED while returning no unified USD margin aggregates at all. The reading this most supports is that the account computes margin PER-POSITION rather than at account level — i.e. isolated margin — in which case there is no account-level 'available' for Bybit to report and none of the four fields will ever populate. THAT IS A READING, NOT A FINDING: it is consistent with the evidence and it is not established. It also matters beyond this row, because the sizer's whole cap models margin as notional/leverage from a shared pool, which is the CROSS-margin model. If the account is isolated, the cap's shape is wrong for it independently of which number feeds it.

WHAT IS STILL UNREAD: the per-coin USDT block. Under UTA that block carries walletBalance, equity, totalPositionIM, totalOrderIM and availableToBorrow. If totalPositionIM/totalOrderIM are populated there, pledged margin IS available from broker truth after all, just not at the account level. The diag now reports that block VERBATIM and un-cherry-picked — selecting fields would reproduce the same error one level down. /v5/position/list positionIM is the second candidate if the coin block is also empty.

PART A REVERTS TO THE JOURNAL RECONSTRUCTION as the leading proposal, since the broker may simply not expose the number for this account. Its $195.52 estimate still stands on its own two independent supports (open-leg reconstruction, and the < $229.92 contradiction bound) — neither of which depended on the refuted derivation.

PLEDGED MARGIN IS BROKER TRUTH AFTER ALL — it lives at COIN level, not account level. The USDT coin block (diag #9031, git_sha 48a5b2e6) carries what every account-level aggregate on this account leaves empty:
    equity            '280.61928992'
    walletBalance     '269.58618992'
    unrealisedPnl     '11.0331'
    totalPositionIM   '53.93341186'   <- PLEDGED MARGIN, POPULATED
    totalOrderIM      '0'
    totalPositionMM   '0.87045386'
    availableToWithdraw ''            (the deprecated field, empty — so that branch was never going
                                       to fire here either)
The block is internally consistent to the cent: walletBalance + unrealisedPnl = equity exactly (280.61928992, zero residual).

SO AVAILABLE MARGIN IS COMPUTABLE FROM THREE BROKER-REPORTED NUMBERS, using Bybit's own definition:
    available = equity - totalPositionIM - totalOrderIM = 280.62 - 53.93 - 0 = $226.69
This is MEASURED-grade, not ESTIMATED — no model of ours enters it.

AND IT VALIDATES THE JOURNAL ESTIMATOR TO 0.05%. Today's book is a single XRP short (149.5 @ 1.0799, 3x). The journal reconstruction gives 280.62 - 53.82 = $226.80 against broker truth $226.69 — a $0.12 gap. The venue's own totalPositionIM (53.93) sits 0.22% from my modelled notional/leverage (53.82), so the leverage model underlying Part A is correct. Two methods, built from disjoint evidence, agree to a rounding error.

ALL THREE METHODS NOW RECONCILE ON THE REJECTION WINDOW. With XRP $161.55 + ETH $76.61 open, derived available = 274.91 - 79.39 = $195.52, which sits inside the independently-derived contradiction bound of < $229.92. Feeding $195.52 to the existing cap at the same 0.9 buffer yields 0.008 BTC (IM $169.88 against $195.52 available) where 0.011 was emitted and refused. The fix reproduces sizes the account was ALREADY filling at (0.004 / 0.005 / 0.007).

THE FIX IS THEREFORE NO LONGER AN ESTIMATE. Part A should read the coin block, not reconstruct from the journal — same arithmetic, broker-supplied inputs. The journal reconstruction remains valuable as the CROSS-CHECK that validated it, and as the last-resort path if the coin block is empty on some other account; it should not be the primary.

PROVENANCE: this deserves its own read_state rather than being folded into venue_available. It is NOT the field Bybit labels 'available' — it is our arithmetic over three fields Bybit does publish. That distinction is the entire subject of this investigation and collapsing it here would be the same mistake one more time.

CAVEAT, UNRESOLVED: coin_count is 2. A second coin exists on this account and I have not read it. For a USDT-margined linear account the USDT block governs, but a second collateral coin (both collateralSwitch and marginCollateral are true for USDT) could contribute to the real ceiling. The derivation above is therefore a LOWER bound on available margin if that coin carries collateral value — which is the safe direction to be wrong in, but it should be read before the fix ships.

READ 2 (diag #9053) — NOT in the prescribed procedure; added to separate two states #9051 structurally cannot distinguish: 'Part B's stamp is broken' vs 'bybit_2 is merely quiet'. Query: trades ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 8 (ALL accounts). Post-deploy rows DO exist — ids 4624-4631, newest 2026-08-13T17:01:13Z, comfortably after the 17:00Z deploy. NONE carries notes.margin_basis.

THAT ABSENCE IS NOT A FALSIFICATION, AND THE REASON MATTERS — I checked the paths rather than reading the empty key as an answer. Of the 8 rows: 4 are intent-layer noops (flip_suppressed_hold_policy x2 on bybit_1, hold_to_bracket_reduce_non_derivative x2) which reject BEFORE sizing runs; 2 are alpaca 'balance() returned None' (sizing aborts before a basis exists); 2 are alpaca_live 'dry_run_sizing_skip: risk_refused: sized_qty=0'. Verified by reading the code, not inferring: coordinator.py:1732 DOES pass margin_basis=margin_basis or None at the dry_run_sizing_skip site, so the stamp IS wired there — but risk.py has SIX `return 0.0` early exits (lines 952, 1053, 1055, 1067, 1082, 1090) that ALL precede the margin_basis_out write at 1223-1226, so a sized_qty=0 refusal leaves the dict empty and `or None` stamps nothing.

NET: Part B is confirmed WIRED at the call site by code reading; it is NOT confirmed FIRING by any live row, because no post-deploy row has yet taken a path that computes a basis. The A1 coin_derived rung for bybit_2 remains entirely unobserved. Next session: re-run READ 1 only. Do not re-run READ 2 (its answer is now recorded) and do not substitute a journalctl tail — 400 lines is ~43 seconds on a ~9 line/sec log and the INFO line fires only on a dispatch.

SPUN OUT: the fact that I could not tell 'no basis computed' from 'stamp broken' by reading the field is itself the repo's named collapsed-states bug -> filed BL-20260813-MARGIN-BASIS-ABSENCE-IS-A-COLLAPSED-STATE.

READ PATH CONFIRMED LIVE ON THE REAL-MONEY ACCOUNT. /api/diag/broker_account_status at 2026-08-13T17:58:56Z, production code, live bybit_2:
    read_state       'coin_derived'
    available_usd     226.57733733
    is_coin_derived   true
    detail            'totalAvailableBalance empty; derived from the USDT coin block (equity - totalPositionIM - totalOrderIM)'
$226.58 against the $226.90 predicted from the 14:19Z snapshot — the delta is unrealised-PnL drift on the open XRP short, which is the expected direction and magnitude. Controls hold: bybit_1 and bybit_portfolio both 'venue_available' (81311.70 / 60235.38), and the new is_coin_derived boolean partitions correctly across all three.

BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THIS PROVES. The READER is confirmed working against the live account — the exact function the coordinator calls, on the exact account, returning the derived figure instead of None. What is NOT yet proven end-to-end is the SIZER CONSUMING it: no bybit_2 dispatch has occurred since 2026-08-11 (verified again — newest row is still id 4572), so no journal row carries a margin_basis stamp. The gap between the two is the coordinator wiring, which is unit-tested but not live-observed.

So: available_usd is no longer None for this account, which is the single fact the whole defect rested on. The equity fallback CANNOT now be reached on bybit_2 while the coin block stays readable. Status moves from 'not observed at all' to 'input confirmed, consumption inferred'.

WHAT WOULD STILL FALSIFY: a post-deploy bybit_2 row whose notes.margin_basis.kind is NOT coin_derived. That would mean the coordinator is not passing what the reader returns. One read, unchanged from the previous update.

items.title: pytest-run short-circuited past scripts/deploy/comms, and a hardcoded fixture date detonated a 14-day time bomb that reddened main mid-session
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13. PR #8998 (a .sh change + one new test file) turned pytest-run RED with 7 failures, all in tests/test_sweep_no_mark_fabrication.py:
  test_no_anchor_declares_unmeasured_instead_of_pricing   KeyError: 'pnl_source'
  test_declaring_is_idempotent                            assert 0 == 1
  test_deferred_neither_prices_nor_declares               assert 0 == 1
  test_anchored_prices_and_stamps_estimated               assert 0 == 1
  test_a_recorded_fill_is_still_preferred                 'bybit_closed_pnl' != 'recorded_exit_price'
  test_anchoring_a_previously_declared_row_clears_marker  KeyError: 'pnl_source'
  test_sweep_never_raises_on_a_broken_anchor              assert 0 >= 1

NOT CAUSED BY THAT PR. Its diff is exactly two files — scripts/ops/purge_vm_runner.sh and a new tests/ops/ file — neither of which the failing tests import. Verified by bisect: the same 7 fail on PLAIN origin/main with the branch's changes fully removed, at SIX shas (b3ef9df, 87af13f, f1e815a, 3271941, fdce380, a318303).

THE CI GAP THAT LET IT LAND. pytest-run 'succeeded' on #8994 in 9 SECONDS (10:47:43->10:47:54) and on #8995 in 9 SECONDS (10:54:25->10:54:34). A real run of this suite takes 7-9 MINUTES (443-543s, ~10,600 tests). Those two were path-filtered short-circuits because neither PR touched Python. Both MERGED TO MAIN on a green tick that executed no tests. So the last genuine full-suite verification of main was ead678f, and main's true health has been unverified since.

That is the load-bearing defect and it is worth more than the 7 failures: a required check that reports SUCCESS without running is the 'green is not evidence' shape — indistinguishable, at the merge button, from a real pass.
items.what_to_check:
HONEST LIMIT ON THIS REPORT: I could NOT reproduce CI's green locally — the 7 fail on every sha I tried, including ones whose CI was green, so my local environment cannot arbitrate and I did not establish WHEN they started failing in CI. Two hypotheses remain untested and they differ in severity:
  (a) the failures are long-standing on main and were simply never run because recent merges short-circuited — then the subject code may be genuinely wrong;
  (b) they are order-dependent and adding a test file perturbed collection order — then the TESTS are fragile rather than the code. (No pytest-randomly / random-order / xdist is installed locally, which weakens but does not eliminate (b).)
Do not act on either until one is established. The distinguishing experiment is cheap: force a real full-suite run on a branch that does NOT contain the new tests/ops file.

WHY THE SUBJECT MATTERS. tests/test_sweep_no_mark_fabrication.py guards _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced against pricing a CONFIRMED CLOSE from a live mark — the exact fabrication behind the phantom -$6,358 leak and the matched pair 4180 (-$4.00) vs 4181 (-$2,589.78). If (a) holds, the money-path provenance guarantee is unprotected right now.
items.action: (1) Make pytest-run's short-circuit VISIBLE and non-equivalent to a pass — a skipped run must not present the same green tick as an executed one, or report as a distinct neutral state. A 9-second 'success' on a required check is the thing to fix first; it is what allowed two unverified merges. (2) Force one real full-suite run on current main to establish which hypothesis holds. (3) Fix whichever it turns out to be — the sweep code, or the tests' order-dependence.
items.resolution_criteria: pytest-run cannot report a green tick without having executed the suite (or reports a visibly distinct state when it skips), AND tests/test_sweep_no_mark_fabrication.py passes on a real full-suite run of main, AND the reason for the 7 failures is stated — code defect or test order-dependence — rather than having quietly stopped reproducing.

updates.note:
ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED. My earlier note offered two hypotheses and said neither was established; hypothesis (a) — 'the code may be genuinely wrong' — was WRONG, and the real cause is neither of the two I listed. Correcting that rather than leaving it.

IT WAS A TIME BOMB, and the boundary is exact. tests/test_sweep_no_mark_fabrication.py hardcoded its fixture row at created_at='2026-07-30T11:00:00Z'. The sweep's scan query bounds itself with `AND datetime(created_at) >= datetime('now', '-14 days')`, so the row aged OUT of the window at precisely 2026-08-13T11:00:00Z. The CI runs bracket that minute:
    last GREEN full suite finished 10:38:48Z  (row inside the window)
    first RED  full suite finished 11:09:03Z  (row outside)
Nothing in either diff was related. `summary['scanned']` was 0 — the row was never fetched — so all 7 failures surfaced as `assert 0 == 1` and `KeyError: 'pnl_source'`, which read as defects in the exit-anchor/provenance code that had not changed. That mis-presentation is why a bisect across six shas came back 'red everywhere' and looked like a broken main.

THE MONEY-PATH GUARANTEE WAS NEVER UNPROTECTED. The subject code is correct; only the fixture's clock had drifted. Recording that explicitly because my earlier note raised the opposite possibility.

SECOND TIME BOMB IN SIX DAYS — #8778 fixed one in tests/test_exchange_fills_list_rows.py by injecting a fixed clock into the function under test. That pattern was unavailable here: the window is applied by SQLite INSIDE the query as datetime('now', ...), so there is no clock to inject without changing production SQL for a test's convenience. The fixture dates are now RELATIVE (row always 2 days old — inside the 14-day scan window, older than the 6h broker-reader defer), which makes the test time-invariant by construction.

PLUS the regression that names it: test_fixture_row_is_inside_the_sweep_scan_window asserts `scanned == 1` directly. Next time the fixture and the window disagree, the failure says so instead of being found by elimination.

THE SHORT-CIRCUIT WAS REAL AND IS ALSO FIXED — it is what let the bomb land unobserved. pytest-run's relevance filter enumerates the trees the suite READS and had missed scripts/ (201 test references; tests/ops/test_system_actions_workflow.py asserts every scripts/ops/*.sh wrapper uses `set -euo pipefail` and sources _lib.sh), deploy/ (the S-012 service-set test) and comms/ (schema templates). PROVEN: PR #8994 changed only scripts/ops/purge_vm_runner.sh, short-circuited to a NINE-SECOND green, and merged having executed no tests. This is the THIRD recurrence of that class after config/ and .github/workflows/ (BL-20260707-FASTCI-CONFIG-DRIFT). All three trees are now in the filter, and tests/test_pytest_run_filter.py pins BOTH the inclusions and the deliberate exclusions (docs/, data/ — owned by the non-short-circuiting `guards` job) so the CI-minutes trade-off stays a decision rather than drifting. It carries a negative control: if the filter is ever widened to everything, the saving is gone and that test fails too.
updates.next_check: None — verified: 12/12 in the sweep file, 487 across the touched suites, and the guard demonstrably fails against the pre-fix filter.
