items.title: Bybit available-margin read: the deprecated per-coin fallback is still live and the None return is silent — the residue the 2026-07-01 fix left behind
items.source:
FILED RETROACTIVELY 2026-08-13. This id predates this row: it was minted in code on/around 2026-07-01 and cited in src/units/accounts/risk.py (x2), src/units/accounts/execute.py, tests/test_fetch_linear_total_equity.py and tests/test_risk_manager_margin_cap.py — but a row was never filed, so every one of those five citations pointed at nothing. The opened_at above is TODAY, not the original date, because the original filing date is not something I can verify; do not read it as the date the defect appeared. It is filed now because artifact-validity-guard correctly refused a change that referenced the id, and because the residue below is a live candidate explanation for BL-20260813-ICTSCALP-BTC-BYBIT2-BALANCE-REJECTS.

WHAT THE 2026-07-01 CHANGE DID (from the code + tests, which are the whole record): (a) _fetch_linear_available_balance switched from the per-coin USDT availableToWithdraw to the account-level totalAvailableBalance — availableToWithdraw is a WITHDRAWAL-eligibility figure governed by different rules than new-order margin, and Bybit DEPRECATED it for UNIFIED accounts on 2025-01-09; (b) the live path in risk.py::position_size gained _MARGIN_SAFETY_BUFFER, which it previously lacked — it had been sizing to 100% of the exchange figure with no headroom for taker fees or IM rounding, and so tripped 110007 at submit.

WHAT IT LEFT BEHIND — three things, all still live as of 2026-08-13:
  1. The deprecated per-coin availableToWithdraw is STILL the fallback. If totalAvailableBalance comes back '' / 'null' / absent for an account, the code silently re-enters the exact figure the fix was about, and its own docstring warns that on the demo endpoint that figure reports approximately the full wallet balance.
  2. Both the deprecated-fallback branch and the final `return None` are SILENT — no log on either, and the None also comes out of a broad `except`. Call-failed, field-absent and field-present are three different states collapsed into one return value.
  3. The change was never verifiable against a live account, and still is not: there is no read surface for a Bybit raw wallet response. /api/diag/broker_account_status is Alpaca-only.

Both surviving branches share one shape: a substitute silently wearing the label of broker truth.
items.what_to_check:
I have NOT established that either branch actually fires on any live account — that is precisely what cannot be read today, and stating otherwise would be the thing this row is about. What IS measured (2026-08-13, diag #9005/#9008/#9010) is that on bybit_2 the margin pre-flight cap ran on a basis of $264.71-$278.69 while the venue's available margin was below $229.92, i.e. the cap was NOT fed the venue's figure. Two branches can produce that: available_usd came back None (coordinator falls back to total equity), or it came back from the deprecated per-coin field with a wallet-balance-like value. They are indistinguishable from outside, which is item 2 above.

Do not assume this is bybit_2-only. bybit_1 and bybit_portfolio call the same function; their balances are large enough that a wrong ceiling never binds, so the same defect would be invisible there.
items.action: (1) Make _fetch_linear_available_balance report WHICH branch it took — field present / field absent so deprecated fallback used / call failed — instead of a bare None from a silent except. Three states, never collapsed. Tier 1. (2) Add a Bybit arm to /api/diag/broker_account_status (or an equivalent read-only wallet route) so the raw UNIFIED wallet response is reachable at all; without it neither this row nor the sizing row can be closed on evidence. Tier 1. (3) Once (1) and (2) land, read the live value for every Bybit account and decide whether the deprecated fallback should be REMOVED outright rather than kept as a silent second-best.
items.resolution_criteria: The three states are distinguishable in the record without a contradiction proof, a live Bybit wallet response is readable from a diag surface, and the branch actually taken by each Bybit account is recorded. The row does NOT close on 'the preferred field is read first' — that was already true before this row was filed and did not prevent the 2026-08 rejections.

updates.note:
FIRST LIVE READ, hours after filing. The read surface this row asked for now exists and answers: bybit_1 venue_available $79,988.85 · bybit_2 unavailable · bybit_portfolio venue_available $60,077.54. So the DEPRECATED per-coin branch is NOT firing anywhere — the second-order risk this row raised (a wallet-balance-like figure silently standing in for new-order margin) is NOT what is happening today on any of the three books. That branch remains live and still deserves removal, but it is not the active defect and this row should not be worked as though it were.

What the read DID find is a residual collapse inside `unavailable` itself: one detail string covering a venue retCode refusal, an empty result.list, an account object lacking both fields, and a raised call. Staged now, so the next read discriminates. Action item (1) on this row is therefore partly delivered and partly re-opened at one level deeper.

Action item (1) — the three-state read — is DONE and now four-state (`coin_derived` added by Part A). Item (2), the Bybit read surface, is DONE (/api/diag/broker_account_status bybit arm + margin_fields + coin block). ITEM (3) REMAINS OPEN: the deprecated per-coin availableToWithdraw is still in the ladder as the third rung. Measured 2026-08-13, it fires on NONE of the three Bybit books — bybit_1 and bybit_portfolio are venue_available, bybit_2 is now coin_derived — so it is currently dead code wearing a trap. Removing it outright is the right end state but is an order-path change on a rung nothing currently takes, so it is left for a session that can justify the Tier-2/3 on its own rather than smuggling it in behind Part A. Row stays open on that one item.

[sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: All three resolution clauses are met on the tree. Four named, uncollapsed states exist at src/units/accounts/execute.py:820-824 (AVAILABLE_STATE_VENUE / COIN_DERIVED / DEPRECATED / UNAVAILABLE) with the read returning `(value, read_state, detail)` and the docstring at :977-1016 documenting each; the contract is registered as `bybit_available.read_state` in scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py CONTRACTS (one of 8) and `collapsed-state-guard` is registered in scripts/ci/run_guards.py; the Bybit arm of /api/diag/broker_account_status is documented in CLAUDE.md with the live per-account branches recorded (bybit_1 venue_available, bybit_2 unavailable→coin_derived, bybit_portfolio venue_available).

items.title: A test fixture stamped with a LITERAL date, exercised against a ROLLING window, expires and takes the whole repo red
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13T11:07Z. tests/test_sweep_no_mark_fabrication.py inserted its fixture trade at created_at='2026-07-30T11:00:00Z'. _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced scans "created_at >= datetime('now','-14 days')". At 2026-08-13T11:00:00Z - 14 days later TO THE MINUTE - the row aged out, the scan returned zero rows, and 7 of 11 cases failed on EVERY branch, blocking every open PR. Nothing had regressed; the clock moved.

STATE THE POPULATION: the failure was measured on clean origin/main with local changes stashed (7 failed / 4 passed), and reproduced identically at four separate commits including 80820f4e - the commit that INTRODUCED the file - which is what ruled out a code regression. I had initially attributed it to a concurrently-merged PR (#8964) on adjacency alone; #8964 does not touch that module, that source file, or that test. The bisect is the only reason a false blame report was not posted to the coordination board.

THE DANGEROUS HALF IS NOT THE OUTAGE, IT IS THE SHAPE. An aged-out row makes the sweep scan zero rows and report still_pending=0, declared_unmeasured=0, filled=0 - byte-identical to a correctly-behaving sweep over a clean book. Three of the cases assert only that something did NOT happen (pnl is None; pnl_source != UNMEASURED_MARKER) and pass VACUOUSLY on an empty scan. They went red only because sibling cases happened to assert '== 1'. That is diagnostic-provenance sub-class C (an unasserted denominator reading as a clean negative). Had the file contained only absence-assertions it would have gone quietly green-while-testing-nothing on 2026-08-13 and stayed that way.

MERGE NOTE 2026-08-13: two sessions diagnosed this independently within the hour. That is itself evidence about the class - the failure is discoverable but not attributable without a bisect, and BOTH of us initially looked at recently-merged PRs before finding the clock.
items.evidence:
sqlite3: datetime('2026-07-30T11:00:00Z') >= datetime('now','-14 days') -> False (cutoff 2026-07-30 11:07:32 at time of measurement).
Source predicate: src/runtime/order_monitor.py::_sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced (~line 8175).
Bisect: 87af13f5 / f1e815aa / af9be482 / 80820f4e all -> 7 failed, 4 passed.
items.fixed_instance:
CORRECTED ON MERGE 2026-08-13: the instance was fixed by a CONCURRENT session in PR #8998 ('Defuse the 14-day time bomb reddening main'), which landed on main first. I had independently diagnosed and fixed the same fixture on my branch; on rebase I took THEIR version wholesale rather than mine. Do not read this row as crediting my fix.

Their fix is relative fixture timestamps (_ROW_AGE_DAYS=2 / _HOLD_SECONDS, preserving the original 1h0m30s hold) plus test_fixture_row_is_inside_the_sweep_scan_window pinning scanned==1. They also found something I did not, filed separately as BL-20260813-PYTEST-RUN-SHORTCIRCUITS-SO-MAIN-MERGES-UNVERIFIED, and recorded a PRIOR instance of this same class I was unaware of: #8778 in tests/test_exchange_fills_list_rows.py, where list_fills measured its cutoff from datetime.now(). That makes this the SECOND time bomb to redden main in six days, which strengthens the case for the class-level guard below.

The one thing I carried over is a CAN-FAIL companion they did not have: test_the_scan_window_check_can_fail ages the row out on purpose, so the denominator test cannot pass while inert (hardcoded scanned, a dropped date filter, or a future 'simplification' back to a literal that happens to be inside the window that day). It also reproduces the outage on demand and pins why it was expensive: an aged-out row is SILENT, not loud.
items.remaining_work:
The CLASS is not swept. ~70 test files carry literal 2026-xx ISO timestamps on created_at/closed_at rows. Only the two SQL rolling-window predicates in source (order_monitor.py: -7 days and -14 days) were checked this session; the -7 day sweep's four test modules (test_s030_pr4_exchange_modify_close, test_local_pnl, test_s030_pr3_monitor_loop, test_broker_pnl_source_stamp) are GREEN as of 2026-08-13 (85 passed). NOT checked: Python-side rolling windows (timedelta(days=N) / now() - delta), which are far more numerous than the SQL ones and have exactly the same failure mode.

Proposed remedy, in order of value: (1) a CI guard that flags a test file combining a literal ISO timestamp with a call into a function carrying a rolling-window predicate; (2) a repo convention that fixture timestamps are relative helpers, never literals; (3) treat 'assert a counter is zero / assert something did not happen' as REQUIRING a companion population assertion, per the sub-class C rule already in CLAUDE.md.
items.resolution_criteria: A CI guard exists that FAILS on a test file combining a literal ISO timestamp on a created_at/closed_at fixture row with a call into a function carrying a rolling-window predicate, AND that guard is demonstrated to have teeth by reverting tests/test_sweep_no_mark_fabrication.py's fixture to the literal '2026-07-30T11:00:00Z' and observing the guard fail on it (the guard must catch the known instance before it is trusted on unknown ones). Until then this row stays open even though the single known instance is fixed - a fixed instance is not a swept class.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The single instance is fixed (tests/test_sweep_no_mark_fabrication.py:86-93 uses `_ROW_AGE_DAYS = 2` with `datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(...)`, plus test_the_scan_window_check_can_fail at :297). The CLASS guard is absent: scripts/check_timestamp_comparisons.py is a different check (raw SQL string comparison of created_at/closed_at, per its own docstring), and no guard among the 39 in run_guards.py flags a literal ISO fixture timestamp fed into a rolling-window predicate. — The row's own resolution_criteria keeps it open until a guard exists AND is shown to fail on the reverted literal fixture. Tier-1 CI.
Re-validated: pairs with BL-20260812-WALLCLOCK-TIMEBOMB-TESTS-NO-SOUND-DETECTOR — a time-bomb fixture and no detector for it. Two rows, one fix.

items.title: The venue-max qty clamp trades a LOUD failure for a SILENT success - the under-sized position reaches no operator surface
items.source:
PR #8964 added a per-order venue ceiling to qty_legalize.legalize_qty: an order above maxOrderQty is now CLAMPED to the cap instead of being bounced by the venue. The logic is correct and this row is not a defect report - the clamp is risk-reducing, matches risk.py's existing clamp idiom for max_qty_by_margin/max_qty_by_exposure, and its blast radius is structurally confined to orders that fail today.

The CONSEQUENCE is the finding. Before the change an oversized order was REJECTED by the venue, leaving an exchange_rejected row - which is how BL-20260810-ICTSCALP-AVAX-QTY-EXCEEDS-VENUE-MAX was discovered at all. After the change the order SUCCEEDS at a smaller size than the risk model asked for, and the only trace is a logger.warning at src/units/accounts/execute.py:1097.

TRACED: runtime_logs/outcomes.jsonl is populated ONLY by explicit outcomes.report() calls (_PERSIST_LEVELS, src/runtime/outcomes.py:158); it is not wired to the logging framework, and execute.py never imports outcomes. So a clamp reaches journalctl and NOTHING else - not outcomes.jsonl, not the operator_warning banner on /api/bot/notifications, not Telegram, not the dashboard, not Android. CLAUDE.md's banner contract exists for exactly this case ('a live operational condition ... surfaces on the banner, not only in Telegram').

Why it matters beyond tidiness: a clamp means the position TAKEN is smaller than the sized risk. A leg that clamps routinely is systematically under-sizing with no signal anywhere, and the R-metrics would be computed over a risk the bot did not actually take.
items.evidence:
src/units/accounts/qty_legalize.py - clamp sets LegalizedQty.clamped=True.
src/units/accounts/execute.py:1097 - the ONLY consumer of .clamped; emits logger.warning and writes back order['qty'] (the journal does record the sent qty - that part is fine).
grep: no outcomes import in execute.py; no counter, no soak row, no other .clamped reader.
items.not_measured: HOW OFTEN THE CLAMP ACTUALLY FIRES IN PRODUCTION IS UNKNOWN - not pulled this session. It may be rare enough not to matter. But the reason that question is hard to answer IS the gap: there is no counter and no soak row, so frequency cannot be read off any surface. Do not close this row on an assumption of rarity; measure it.
items.resolution_criteria: A venue-max clamp on a live order is observable WITHOUT reading journalctl: the clamp branch routes through outcomes.report(..., Level.WARNING) so it persists to outcomes.jsonl and appears as an operator_warning banner on /api/bot/notifications - verified by forcing one clamp (a test or a staged qty above a known cap) and observing the banner, not by inspecting the code. Additionally, the clamp RATE is readable over a window from some surface (a counter or soak row), so 'is this leg systematically under-sizing?' has an answer with a stated denominator.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Half one IS shipped: src/units/accounts/execute.py:1379-1434 now wraps the clamp branch in `from src.runtime.outcomes import Level, report` / `report('submit_order','venue_max_qty_clamped', level=Level.WARN, …)` with requested_qty/placed_qty/venue_max, so a clamp persists to outcomes.jsonl and can reach the operator_warning banner. Half two is not: there is no counter, soak row or windowed rate surface for clamps, and the row explicitly forbids closing on an assumption of rarity. — Remaining: (a) live verification that a forced clamp actually renders on /api/bot/notifications (needs live data), and (b) a clamp RATE readable over a window with a stated denominator. Note outcomes.report is per-fingerprint rate-limited, so counting outcomes.jsonl rows is not a rate.

Re-validated: a LOUD failure traded for a SILENT success, with the undersized position reaching no operator surface. Pairs with BL-20260814-VENUE-MAX-NONE-CANNOT-SAY-WE-COULD-NOT-LOOK — same clamp, two defects.

items.title: Two CLOSED M20 verdicts rest on an input file that no longer exists, and neither cell said so
items.source:
ict_scalp_mgc_15m carries honest_negative on BOTH stale_stop and giveback_stop, each citing the M27 config-exact sweep of 2026-07-28 over data/XAUUSD_15m_deep.csv (Dukascopy XAU 15m proxy, 178,953 bars, split 2025-07-01).

That file is GONE. The leg's OWN exit_ladder cell records a trainer probe (issue #8696, 2026-08-09) finding no MGC_* or XAUUSD_* file remaining - only GC_F_1d/GC_F_1h - and states outright that 'this leg's existing stale_stop/giveback_stop verdicts are also not currently reproducible'. So the fact was MEASURED and WRITTEN DOWN four days ago, in a DIFFERENT CELL of the same row, and neither affected cell carried any hint of it. A reader of the stale_stop cell had no path to the caveat.

WHY IT MATTERS TO THE MILESTONE: honest_negative counts as CLOSED in BOTH the headline and the done-condition. M20 was therefore counting this leg as resolved on evidence nobody can reproduce, and would never revisit it - closed cells are not re-examined.

NOT COVERED BY THE EXISTING EVIDENCE-VINTAGE WARNING. That warning concerns the un-modelled capped TP and explicitly EXCLUDES these legs ('the other 8 legs (scalp, fvg) place a real target their harness models'). It is also about STALE evidence; this is ABSENT evidence, a strictly stronger condition - a stale number can at least be re-derived.
items.action_taken: Both cells annotated in place with the reproducibility caveat and a pointer to the probe. VERDICTS DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED: the sweep genuinely ran, on real data, and its numbers are recorded in full. Downgrading to pending because the input was later deleted would destroy real work AND would be a fabrication in the opposite direction - 'we never looked' is false. The honest state is a verdict that stands with its caveat attached.
items.not_measured: WHETHER THE VERDICTS WOULD REPRODUCE is unknown - the sweep was not re-run this session. The caveat records irreproducibility, NOT that the numbers are wrong. Do not read it as doubt about the result.
items.remaining_work:
CLASS NOT SWEPT. Only this leg was checked, because its sibling cell happened to name the deletion. NOTHING systematically verifies that a closed M20 verdict's cited input still EXISTS, so other cells may rest on deleted files with no cell anywhere recording it. A matrix-wide audit (parse cited data/ paths out of every closed cell's ref, probe the trainer for each) is the actual fix and was not attempted.

Restoring THIS one is cheap: the input is regenerable on a FREE GitHub runner via research-symbol-p0-build.yml (Dukascopy XAU) - no GPU, no Tier-3. Re-running the M27 sweep against a regenerated file either reproduces the numbers (drop the caveat) or does not (a finding in itself).
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) data/XAUUSD_15m_deep.csv is regenerated and the M27 sweep re-run for both levers, with the outcome recorded on each cell - reproduced (caveat removed) or not (verdict revised) - verified by the run artifact, not by asserting the file exists; OR (b) the matrix-wide audit above is run, its results recorded, and a guard added so a closed cell citing a data path that cannot be located is FLAGGED rather than counted silently as closed. (b) is the one that closes the class; (a) alone closes one instance and this row should then be narrowed to the class rather than closed.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The in-place annotation is done — ict_scalp_mgc_15m's stale_stop and giveback_stop refs both now carry the '⚠️ EVIDENCE NOT CURRENTLY REPRODUCIBLE' segment naming the deleted data/XAUUSD_15m_deep.csv and issue #8696. Neither resolution branch is done: `ls data/` holds 5 entries and no XAUUSD_*/MGC_* file, the M27 sweep has not been re-run, and no guard flags a closed cell citing a data path that cannot be located (nothing in scripts/ci/ or the rollup parses cited data/ paths). — needs trainer/runner work: regenerate the Dukascopy XAU 15m series via research-symbol-p0-build.yml and re-run the M27 sweep (branch a), or build the matrix-wide cited-input audit + guard (branch b, the one that closes the class). The cited inputs mostly live on the trainer, so a repo-local guard alone cannot verify existence.
Re-validated: two CLOSED verdicts resting on a file that no longer exists, and neither cell said so. Third member of the unreproducible-evidence class.

items.title: 140 M20 corpus rows were measured WITH the 0.099 TP cap and record `tp_cap_pct: null` - diagnosed from the run head SHAs; relabel script ready, corpus write not yet made
items.source:
RESOLVED. This row was rewritten three times as the evidence moved; the terminal answer and the two wrong turns are both recorded, because the wrong turns are the reusable part.

THE ANSWER. Two `m20-exit-lever-sweep` runs bracket the affected window, both on `claude/m20-exit-refinement-continue-g1qv46`, both `event: push`:
  run 31438120910  created 2026-08-10T22:23:54Z  head d76643b9  -> legs finished 22:26:28-22:28:42Z
  run 31438683081  created 2026-08-10T22:31:57Z  head e6e519d1  -> legs finished 22:34:13-22:42:40Z
On a push event the `inputs` context is EMPTY, so the workflow's `TP_CAP_PCT: ${{ inputs.tp_cap_pct || '0.099' }}` resolves to 0.099 and the sweep runs `--tp-cap-pct 0.099`. BOTH runs were capped. They differ only in whether their sweep script wrote the provenance field: `git show d76643b9:scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py | grep -c '"tp_cap_pct": a.tp_cap_pct'` returns 0, the same on e6e519d1 returns 1. So the 140 `null` rows are the first run's output: measured at 0.099, recorded as nothing.

WRONG TURN 1 - 'the flag is inert'. Refuted by a direct positive control: backtest_trend.py on a 4,000-bar synthetic series, identical args but for the cap, gave 57 trades / net_R 466.37 / tp_r_effective_n 0 versus 127 / 347.55 / 127 at median reach 4.41R.

WRONG TURN 2 - and this is the one worth remembering. I proposed 'null just predates the field', then REFUTED MY OWN CORRECT HYPOTHESIS by dating the field from its merge to `main` (2a289ddc, 2026-08-11 14:10:55Z) and finding 464 rows carrying 0.099 with earlier timestamps. That apparent contradiction dissolves completely once you date the field by THE REF THAT RAN: on the feature branch the two commits sit about eight minutes apart on 08-10. **Date a run's code by its head SHA, never by when the change reached main** - a feature branch runs its own code for hours or days before merge, and `sweep_generated_at` alone cannot date a row's provenance.

AND THE FRAMING WAS ALSO WRONG. The previous version of this row called the defect 'duplicate measurements of one geometry under two identities'. Measured over the 35 (leg,lever,cell,split) pairs carrying both labels: they differ on THREE identity fields, not one - tp_cap_pct 35/35, regime_router None->'off' 35/35, min_oos_trades_floor None->25 35/35, declared_levers_dropped None->[] 8/35. So relabelling the cap collapses NOTHING (measured: 0 duplicate keys after relabel), and that is correct - the 25-trade floor is an operator decision dated 08-11, so those rows really were graded under no floor, and two rows for one cell at two floors is the corpus working as designed. The defect is narrower than claimed: ONE axis, mislabelled, on rows a reader is likely to trust.
items.action_taken:
1. Plumbed `live_tp_reach_r_{n,median,min,max}_{IS,OOS}` onto every corpus row (scripts/research/m20_corpus_extract.py, PR #9037) so a future row states whether the cap BOUND rather than only which value was requested. `n: 0` stays distinct from `n: None`. Three tests, can-fail verified.
2. Shipped scripts/research/m20_corpus_relabel_tp_cap.py - dry-run by default, carries the run-SHA evidence in its docstring, asserts its preconditions and REFUSES rather than guessing if the corpus does not match them (verified: it exits 1 on an already-relabelled file). Dry run on the corpus branch's 925 rows reports 140 rows / 10 legs to relabel, 0 collapses. It fills ONLY the cap - min_oos_trades_floor is deliberately left null because null is the TRUTH for a pre-floor run.
3. APPLIED 2026-08-13 (operator-authorised the corpus-branch write). Ran the script with --apply on claude/m20-sweep-corpus (commit dea29fec). Verified before/after rather than trusting the script's own report: rows 925 -> 925 (no collapse, as predicted); cap distribution {0.099: 785, null: 140} -> {0.099: 925}; exactly 140 rows changed, every one null -> 0.099; 0 changed rows outside the evidenced window; and the non-cap content of every row is BYTE-IDENTICAL (symmetric diff 0 rows over a dict-compare excluding tp_cap_pct) - so the write touched one field and nothing else. 10 legs: avax_pullback_2h, eth_pullback_2h, htf_pullback_trend_2h, qqq_pullback_1h, spy_pullback_1h, trend_donchian, trend_donchian_1h, trend_donchian_eth, trend_donchian_eth_prop, trend_donchian_sol.
items.not_measured:
Whether null-cap rows exist OUTSIDE the evidenced window: the script reports and refuses to touch them; on this 925-row corpus there were none, but that is a property of this snapshot rather than a guarantee, and a future re-extraction of an old artifact could reintroduce them.

The three OTHER identity fields those rows are missing (regime_router null on 35/35 compared pairs, min_oos_trades_floor null on 35/35, declared_levers_dropped null on 8/35) are deliberately still null. min_oos_trades_floor MUST stay null - the floor is an 2026-08-11 operator decision and those runs predate it. regime_router could be backfilled to 'off' on the same run evidence but was not: the evidence in this row was gathered to establish the CAP, and widening a correction past its basis is the habit this row exists to discourage.
items.remaining_work:
NONE for this row - both the diagnosis and the write are complete and verified. Two spin-offs, each standing on its own:
1. Guard for the CLASS: a provenance field added to a producer AFTER the behaviour it describes went live leaves a window of rows silently MISLABELLED rather than merely unlabelled. `live_tp_reach_r`, added in PR #9037, has exactly that window open right now - every row written between the flag and the field will read null and mean 'unrecorded'.
2. Separable legibility gap: a corpus row records `cells_tried` but not the lever set the run REQUESTED, so a 7-cell and a 14-cell run of the same leg cannot be told apart from the corpus alone.
items.resolution_criteria: The relabel is applied on the corpus branch. The diagnosis is complete and evidenced (run head SHAs + push-event input resolution), and the downstream audit is DONE and clean (0 of 72 cells affected) - so what remains is one --apply run, not further investigation.

items.title: alpaca_paper + alpaca_portfolio: balance() returns None and every signal is refused, while /v2/account reads ACTIVE on the same client
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13. Found incidentally while verifying an unrelated fix — which is the only reason it was found at all; nothing alerted.

Two accounts are refusing every signal:
  trades 4630 (alpaca_portfolio) + 4629 (alpaca_paper), both 2026-08-13T17:01:13Z, package pkg-31ffb00aaed54c18:
    'sizing_failed: RuntimeError: balance() returned None for <acct> (exchange=alpaca): API error or credentials missing - account unreachable'
and /api/bot/accounts/balances confirms both at balance:null, api_ok:false as of 2026-08-13T17:00:53Z.

THE ERROR MESSAGE IS WRONG, AND THAT IS THE INTERESTING PART. It blames 'credentials missing / account unreachable'. Measured on the SAME accounts at 17:58:56Z via /api/diag/broker_account_status, which opens its own read-only client with the SAME resolved creds and calls GET /v2/account:
    alpaca_paper      status ACTIVE, trading_blocked false, account_blocked false
    alpaca_portfolio  status ACTIVE, trading_blocked false, account_blocked false
Both returned a FULL flag set. So the credentials resolve, the host is reachable, and the account object parses — while balance() on the same client returns None. The failure is inside the balance path specifically, NOT in auth or reachability, and the message names a cause no code path tested (sub-class A of the diagnostic-provenance rule).

SCOPE IS PARTIAL, WHICH RULES OUT AN ALPACA-WIDE OUTAGE: **2 of 4** Alpaca accounts are affected (n=4 declared alpaca accounts: alpaca_paper FAIL, alpaca_portfolio FAIL, alpaca_options_paper OK, alpaca_live OK). POPULATION FOR EVERY DOLLAR FIGURE IN THIS ROW: a single `/api/bot/accounts/balances` snapshot per timestamp — n=1 snapshot each, not an average over a window. The healthy pair read $100,000.00 (alpaca_options_paper) and $0.10 (alpaca_live) in the 2026-08-13T17:00:53Z snapshot.

REGRESSION WINDOW: 2026-08-13T12:00:56Z → 2026-08-13T17:00:53Z (two snapshots, n=1 each, ~5.0h apart). At the first, both were healthy — alpaca_paper $86,272.60 with 7 open positions and alpaca_portfolio $100,070.28 with 8 open positions, api_ok:true on both. At the second, both null / api_ok:false. Those are the only two observations I have, so the break is bounded to that window and NOT located within it — 2 samples cannot say when inside 5 hours it happened, and the hourly balance_snapshots table can narrow it if that matters.
items.what_to_check:
NOT real money — both are paper (alpaca_paper is the soak book, alpaca_portfolio the live-portfolio mirror). Severity is high on DATA LOSS, not capital: the portfolio mirror exists to evaluate the real book unconstrained, and a mirror that refuses every signal silently stops mirroring while still looking configured.

I have NOT established the mechanism. Candidates, none confirmed: an Alpaca API shape change on the balance endpoint that the parse does not tolerate; a numeric field arriving null for these two accounts specifically; or a per-account rate limit. The discriminator is cheap — AlpacaClient.balance() and account_status() use the same client, so diff exactly which call each makes and what the balance path does with the response.

Do NOT read 'api_ok:false' as 'the account has no money'. The 8 open positions on alpaca_portfolio at 12:00Z have not been verified closed; the balance is UNREADABLE, which is a different statement.
items.action: (1) Diff AlpacaClient.balance() against AlpacaClient.account_status() — same client, same creds, one works. Whatever balance() does that account_status() does not is the bug. (2) Fix the error message: 'credentials missing - account unreachable' is refuted by /v2/account succeeding on the same client, and it will send the next investigator to check creds first. Stage it so it names the branch that actually failed. (3) Establish whether the open positions on both books are still open and monitored, since a sizing refusal does not close anything. (4) Consider whether an account whose balance is unreadable for N consecutive ticks should raise the existing account-down latched alert — it did not fire here, which is why this needed to be found by accident.
items.resolution_criteria: balance() returns a figure for both accounts, OR the refusal names the branch that actually failed rather than blaming credentials. The row does NOT close on the accounts happening to recover: an intermittent failure that recurs unalerted is the same defect. Closing also requires stating why account_reachability_alert did not fire.

updates.note:
THE TITLE IS NOW TOO NARROW — a THIRD account outside Alpaca shows the identical symptom, which changes the diagnosis. Adding the observation rather than renaming the row; the owner of the fix should decide the final scope.

GET /api/bot/notifications, live, 2026-08-13T22:04:27Z (diag #9082) carries an all_accounts_failed banner from 22:00:33Z:
  Strategy mgc_trend_1h | Symbol MGC | Side sell | Accounts attempted 1 | Trades placed 0
  ib_paper: sizing_failed: RuntimeError: balance() returned None for ib_paper (exchange=interactive_brokers): API error or credentia[...]

That is the SAME failure shape this row documents for alpaca_paper and alpaca_portfolio — balance() returning None, surfaced through a message blaming credentials — but on INTERACTIVE_BROKERS, a different client, different transport, different credential path. So the defect is very likely NOT inside AlpacaClient.balance(): either the shared coordinator balance path (coordinator.py::_default_balance_fetcher) is converting a per-client failure into a None, or the 'credentials missing - account unreachable' string is a generic wrapper applied regardless of the real cause. Action item (1) on this row — 'diff AlpacaClient.balance() against AlpacaClient.account_status()' — is still worth doing, but on this evidence it will not be the whole answer, and a fix scoped to the Alpaca client would leave the IB case live.

RELATED, SAME READ: a monitor_blindness banner for ict_scalp_mgc_15m (pkg-dbcc140fd43c4a79) cites 'candles_unavailable for 3 consecutive ticks', and three operator_warning rows report transient_market_data_unavailable on MGC/MHG. All of it is IBKR-side and concurrent, so the balance() None on ib_paper may be one symptom of a broader IBKR data/connection problem in this window rather than an independent bug. Worth establishing which before attributing it — I did not, and am not asserting it.

NOT INVESTIGATED FURTHER HERE: I own neither this row nor the IBKR window; recording the observation so the owner is not misled by the Alpaca-only framing. Separately noted against myself: rows 4629/4630 carrying this same balance()-None appeared in my own earlier read of this backlog and I classified them as off-path and moved on, which is how the wider pattern was nearly missed twice.

TWO CHANGES, and the first one matters for whoever picks this up next: **BOTH ACCOUNTS HAVE RECOVERED.** Measured 2026-08-14T11:00:38Z via /api/bot/accounts/balances (n=1 snapshot, the same basis this row's original figures use): alpaca_paper balance $86,157.74 / api_ok true / 6 open positions; alpaca_portfolio $99,983.92 / api_ok true / 7 open positions. So the outage self-resolved somewhere in the ~18h between the 2026-08-13T17:00:53Z null reading and this one. TWO SNAPSHOTS CANNOT LOCATE THE RECOVERY INSIDE THAT WINDOW, exactly as the original regression window is bounded but not located; the hourly balance_snapshots table can narrow both if it matters. Do NOT re-open this as a live outage without re-measuring first.

That makes the durable defect the MESSAGE, not the accounts — and that half is now FIXED (PR on branch claude/roadmap-work-plan-review-m2aw6p): the non-prop refusal in coordinator.py no longer asserts 'API error or credentials missing - account unreachable'. It is now a module-level `balance_none_refusal_message()` (symmetric with the prop branch's existing `prop_balance.refusal_message`) that states only what the branch knows — the fetch was attempted and returned no value — explicitly disclaims the two causes that were measured healthy while it fired, and points at /api/diag/broker_account_status, the surface that actually discriminates. 6 tests, verified to fail pre-fix.

It was made a FUNCTION rather than a better inline f-string for a reason worth recording: the first draft of the test grepped coordinator.py for the new prose and FAILED — because the string wraps across source lines and so is not contiguous in the file. Had the wrapping fallen differently the grep would have passed while asserting nothing. An inline refusal is only testable by grepping, and a grep for wrapped prose is a test that can silently check nothing.

STILL OPEN on this row: the root cause of the balance() None itself is NOT diagnosed — the message fix makes the NEXT occurrence legible, it does not prevent it. Also see the new sibling row BL-20260814-REACHABILITY-PROBES-POSITIONS-NOT-BALANCE for why nothing alerted.

updates.by: claude (dead-leg audit over the trainer's synced journal, trainer-diag #9262)
updates.note:
**SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THIS ROW'S TITLE, AND THE CONDITION IS NOT OVER.** Correcting my own update from earlier today, which said the two Alpaca accounts had recovered and implied the item was winding down. Both halves of that were too narrow.

Measured over the trainer's synced journal (mtime 2026-08-14T05:00:05Z), 14-day window, via `scripts/ops/dead_leg_audit.py`:

  * **`ib_paper` / `mgc_trend_1h`: 43 rejections, ALL of them** `sizing_failed: RuntimeError: balance() returned None for ib_paper (exchange=interactive_brokers)`. **So this is NOT an Alpaca-specific condition** - it hits INTERACTIVE_BROKERS too, and it is the single largest refusal cluster in the whole fleet. This row's title should be read as naming an instance, not the class.
  * `alpaca_paper` / `tlt_pullback_1h`: **21** rejections, same balance()-None message.
  * `alpaca_portfolio` / `tlt_pullback_1h`: **21**, same.
  * `alpaca_paper` / `spy_pullback_1h`: 5. Plus gdx/gld/iaum 1d legs at 2 each.

The original row rested on **2 trades**; the real 14d population is **90+ refusals across at least 8 legs and 3 accounts on 2 different exchanges**. The 'both accounts recovered' observation stands for the balance SNAPSHOT at 11:00Z - but recovery of the snapshot did not mean the refusals had stopped, and I should not have let a point-in-time reading stand in for a window.

NOTE the message in the live data is still the OLD one ('API error or credentials missing - account unreachable'), which is expected: the corrected `balance_none_refusal_message` is on branch `claude/roadmap-work-plan-review-m2aw6p` and not yet merged/deployed. That the old string appears 90+ times in 14 days is the strongest argument for the message fix - every one of those rows sent a reader after credentials that were measured ACTIVE.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE None ITSELF REMAINS UNDIAGNOSED. That is now the whole of this row.

**CORRECTION OF MY OWN PREVIOUS UPDATE — I read a SAMPLE as a POPULATION.** Two hours ago I wrote that `ib_paper`/`mgc_trend_1h` showed '43 rejections, ALL of them balance() returned None' and that the class totalled '~90+ refusals across 8 legs / 3 accounts / 2 exchanges'. **Both figures are wrong.**

The dead-leg audit reported 43 `rejected` rows for that leg and, separately, a `MAX(entry_reason)` **sample** string. I generalised the one sampled reason to all 43 rows. Counting the actual predicate (`entry_reason LIKE '%balance() returned None%'`) over ALL history gives:

| account | n | first | last |
|---|--:|---|---|
| `alpaca_live` | 20 | 2026-06-26 13:32 | 2026-06-26 19:10 |
| `breakout_1` | 18 | 2026-06-26 06:43 | 2026-06-29 03:11 |
| `ib_paper` | **5** | 2026-07-01 14:00 | 2026-08-13 22:00 |
| `alpaca_paper` | 4 | 2026-07-15 13:31 | 2026-08-13 17:01 |
| `alpaca_portfolio` | 1 | 2026-08-13 17:01 | 2026-08-13 17:01 |

**Total 48 over ~7 WEEKS, not 90+ over 14 days. `ib_paper` is 5, not 43.** The other ~38 of that leg's 43 rejections are a DIFFERENT cause — almost certainly `intent_noop:flip_suppressed_hold_policy` (the journal shows exactly that string for `mgc_trend_1h`, 'desired short opposes current long (qty=105.0)'), which is the hold policy working CORRECTLY on the 105-contract MGC position, not a defect at all.

WHAT SURVIVES the correction, and it is still the substantive part: the class is **not Alpaca-specific** — `ib_paper` (interactive_brokers) and `breakout_1` (prop) both carry it, so the row's title still under-scopes. And it is **recurrent rather than a single incident**: 5 distinct onsets spread over 7 weeks, most recently 2026-08-13T22:00Z. Nothing in the last ~14h.

WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE: any claim about the magnitude. 48 refusals over 7 weeks is a much smaller problem than I stated, and the severity should be judged on that number.

[sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The message half shipped: src/core/coordinator.py:47-77 adds `balance_none_refusal_message`, whose docstring records that the old 'API error or credentials missing - account unreachable' text was refuted by /v2/account succeeding on the same client, and the raise at :999-1003 now uses it. The alerting gap also has an answer now — src/runtime/silent_refusal_alert.py + src/runtime/dead_leg.py exist (the reachability probe reads positions(), not balance()). What is NOT established anywhere in the tree is why balance() returns None intermittently on alpaca_paper / alpaca_portfolio / ib_paper. — needs live data: a fresh /api/bot/accounts/balances + a diff of AlpacaClient.balance() vs account_status() against the live accounts to identify the failing branch. Both books are paper, and the refusal now states what it knows rather than blaming credentials, so the acute half is mitigated.

items.title: notes.margin_basis absent collapses THREE states — 'sizing never computed a basis', 'account is off the margin path', and 'the stamp is broken' — so the field cannot verify the fix it was added to verify
items.why_it_matters:
This is docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md § 'Collapsed states' in its canonical form: 'we did not look' and 'we looked and found nothing' are opposite statements sharing one representation. It is the sixth instance of the class and the first committed BY a fix written to close a different instance of it. The remedy already exists correctly in exactly one module — src/runtime/exit_anchor.py's anchored/deferred/no_anchor — and the fix's own A1 rung got this RIGHT (four named read_states, registered with collapsed-state-guard); the B half then shipped a bare presence/absence field beside it.

Concretely it blocks the parent row: with bybit_2 quiet since 2026-08-11, the only available evidence is other accounts' rows, and those cannot speak because absence there is unreadable. A stamped 'not_applicable: pre-sizing rejection' would have answered the whole question in one read.
items.action:
Give the basis an explicit not-computed state rather than leaving the key off, mirroring exit_anchor's three-way contract:
  kind=not_sized      — rejected before position_size ran (intent noop / risk gate)

Then register margin_basis.kind in scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py::CONTRACTS so producer-emits-every-state and consumer-branches-on-it are ENFORCED, not asserted — the guard's override is verified, not presence-only.

items.title: The operator_warning banner filtered on a level string the producer never writes — every Level.WARN outcome was persisted to outcomes.jsonl and then silently dropped, for ~5 weeks
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 by executing the real producer enum against the real consumer set, while implementing BL-20260813-VENUE-MAX-CLAMP-IS-INVISIBLE-TO-EVERY-OPERATOR-SURFACE.

PRODUCER — src/runtime/outcomes.py: `class Level(str, Enum)` has exactly FOUR members, info/warn/error/critical. There is no WARNING member. `_Reporter.emit` writes `record['level'] = level.value`, so a Level.WARN row lands in outcomes.jsonl as level='warn'. _PERSIST_LEVELS = {WARN, ERROR, CRITICAL}, so WARN rows ARE written.

CONSUMER — src/web/api/routers/notifications.py:_recent_warning_banners: `lvl = str(r.get('level') or '').upper()` then `if lvl not in _WARN_LEVELS: continue`, with _WARN_LEVELS = {'WARNING','ERROR','CRITICAL'}.

'warn'.upper() == 'WARN', which was NOT in that set. Executed proof:
  warn      old_match=False  new_match=True
  error     old_match=True   new_match=True
  critical  old_match=True   new_match=True
  info      old_match=False  new_match=False   (correctly still excluded)

20 Level.WARN call sites exist under src/. All of them were invisible to the banner. The single grep hit for level='warning' is coordinator.py:2665 push_alert, which feeds the in-memory alerts queue, NOT outcomes.jsonl — so nothing anywhere produced the string the filter required.
items.why_it_matters:
The WARN tier is the entire middle of the alerting contract: ERROR/CRITICAL also go to Telegram, so WARN is precisely the band whose ONLY operator surface is this banner. Losing it is silent by construction — ERROR/CRITICAL banners kept rendering, so the feature looked alive on every inspection.

It is also a textbook instance of two rules this repo already canonicalised, committed inside the alerting path itself: 'field beats comment' (CLAUDE.md's banner row ALSO said WARNING, so doc and code agreed with each other and both disagreed with the enum — agreement between two claims is not verification), and the unasserted-negative class (no test asserted a WARN row produces a banner; a test that fed 'WARNING' would have passed against a string production never emits).

Directly consequential: the venue-max-clamp fix filed as BL-20260813-VENUE-MAX-CLAMP-IS-INVISIBLE-TO-EVERY-OPERATOR-SURFACE specifies routing the clamp through outcomes.report(Level.WARN) so it reaches the banner. Shipped against the old filter that fix would have persisted correctly, rendered nothing, and closed on a code inspection.
items.action_taken: _WARN_LEVELS = {'WARN', 'WARNING', 'ERROR', 'CRITICAL'} — 'WARNING' deliberately KEPT rather than swapped: it costs nothing, and a set that accepts only one producer's spelling is the failure mode itself. Comment records that the matched value must come from the producer, not from the docs. CLAUDE.md's /api/bot/notifications row corrected in the same commit (it asserted the wrong string). Tier-1: read-only API router, no order path, no schema change.
items.not_measured: HOW MANY WARN ROWS WERE LOST IS UNKNOWN — not pulled. outcomes.jsonl retains a bounded tail and the banner window is only NOTIF_WARNING_WINDOW_MIN (default 60m), so the historical count is not recoverable from the live file. Do not state a number. The blast radius is 'every Level.WARN outcome since the banner shipped 2026-07-08', which is a duration, not a count.
items.resolution_criteria: A real Level.WARN outcome appears as an operator_warning banner on GET /api/bot/notifications on the live VM — observed on the endpoint, NOT inferred from the set literal. Until that read is taken this stays resolved_pending_live_verification, for the same reason the bybit_2 row does: nothing here has been seen working live.
refs: src/core/coordinator.py:2665 (the only level='warning' — push_alert, a different sink)
CLAUDE.md § Dashboard REST API, GET /api/bot/notifications row

updates.note:
LIVE-VERIFIED — status moves resolved_pending_live_verification -> resolved. This is an OBSERVATION on the live endpoint, not a code inspection, which is what the resolution_criteria demanded.

GET /api/bot/notifications on the live VM at 2026-08-13T22:04:27Z (diag #9082), deployed git_sha da0d0728 (the merge of PR #9060), returned THREE banners with kind='operator_warning' and severity='warning':
  transient_market_data_unavailable: mhg_pullback_1d  (21:07:53Z)
  transient_market_data_unavailable: mgc_trend_1h     (21:04:36Z)
  transient_market_data_unavailable: mgc_pullback_1d  (21:04:36Z)
each with detail 'strategy_builder - exception'.

WHY severity='warning' IS THE PROOF, and not merely consistent with it: _recent_warning_banners sets sev = 'alert' if lvl in (ERROR, CRITICAL) else 'warning'. So a row can only reach severity='warning' if its level passed the _WARN_LEVELS filter WITHOUT being ERROR or CRITICAL. Under the OLD set {'WARNING','ERROR','CRITICAL'} the only level that could do that was the literal 'WARNING' — a string the Level enum cannot produce. Therefore these three banners were UNREACHABLE before this fix. has_alerts:false confirms none of them is ERROR/CRITICAL.

PRODUCER CONFIRMED AT THE CALL SITE: src/runtime/intent_multiplexer.py:507-514 emits exactly these rows with level=Level.WARN, and its own comment says they will be 'visible on the diag surface (outcomes.jsonl) + the operator_warning banner feed, just not an ERROR page'. That comment described an intent the code did not deliver for roughly five weeks. It does now.

SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY: this verifies the CONSUMER (a WARN outcome now renders as a banner). It does NOT measure how many WARN rows were lost while the filter was wrong, and that number is not recoverable — checked: src/web/api/routers/notifications.py, whose _recent_warning_banners reads only a bounded 65536-byte tail of the log and then filters to the last NOTIF_WARNING_WINDOW_MIN minutes (default 60), so the endpoint structurally cannot see beyond a rolling window; and checked: src/runtime/outcomes.py, whose _Reporter.emit appends to outcomes.jsonl without retaining a level-keyed index to count against. So the blast radius is a DURATION ('every Level.WARN outcome since the banner shipped 2026-07-08'), never a count, and no number should be quoted for it.

items.title: exit_head_ml: the E1 block size is now DERIVED (keep 50) — and the derivation says no block size makes the 7 daily legs gradeable
items.source:
REFRAMED THE SAME DAY IT WAS FILED, after the operator challenged the premise: "why aren't we using backtesting? nothing is ever supposed to need live soaking for anything other than seeing that the mechanics work correctly and performance matches the backtesting expectations." That is correct and my original framing was wrong.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I measured each blocked leg's trades-per-year and reported that the missing trades 'arrive in about 6.3 to 14.5 YEARS', concluding the M20 done-condition was unreachable and needed an operator decision. That silently assumed the trades arrive through FORWARD LIVE ACCRUAL. They do not: `lifetime harness trades` are produced by a BACKTEST over the built dataset, so the count is a function of how much history we BUILT, not of elapsed time. The arithmetic was fine; the interpretation was the error, and it pointed at a milestone-governance decision when the real finding is a config default.

THE ACTUAL CONSTRAINT. scripts/ops/build_trainer_datasets.sh:925 sets EQ_1D_START="${EQ_1D_START:-2015-01-01}", and line 942 builds every equity 1d dataset (SPY QQQ GLD TLT IWM SLV IEF TQQQ QLD SPLG IAUM) from that date through the yfinance adapter. That is a ~11.6-year window BY CHOICE. yfinance serves SPY from 1993, QQQ from 1999, IWM from 2000, SPLG from 2005, SCHA/TQQQ/QLD from 2009-2010 - roughly 2.5-3x the history for the majors. At the measured ~4 trades/yr, a full-inception window would put SPY/QQQ/IWM near 130-190 lifetime trades against the 100 needed, i.e. comfortably gradeable, with NO waiting and NO live soak.

SECOND FINDING, INDEPENDENT: E1's fold minimum is an UNDEFENDED DEFAULT. scripts/ml/train_exit_head.py:492 is a bare `ap.add_argument("--min-fold-trades", type=int, default=50)` with no stated basis, and the help text does not defend the value either. Contrast _MIN_FOLD_TRAIN_ROWS = 500 forty lines above, which carries an explicit comment saying exactly what it floors and why ('a floor on fitting a model at all, not a research choice about OOS width'). So one of the two numbers gating every E1 verdict is derived and the other is asserted. This does NOT mean lower it - block size must be settled on what makes a walk-forward meaningful, never on which legs it unblocks (block 50 unblocks 0 of these legs, 40 unblocks 1, 30 unblocks 5, 25 unblocks 6, 16 unblocks all 8, so it is a very large lever on coverage and correspondingly easy to abuse).
items.action_taken:
Retracted the wrong horizon note in place on all 8 cells rather than deleting it - the retraction names the error, keeps the arithmetic (still valid as a trades-per-year-of-DATA rate), and states the real constraint. No status changed. Filed the block-size finding here rather than acting on it.

The done-condition question this row originally posed is WITHDRAWN: these cells are not structurally unreachable, so they need no `n/a`, no new status, and no redefinition of M20 done.

DERIVATION DONE 2026-08-13 (operator chose 'derive it from a stated statistical target' over keeping/lowering/renaming): docs/research/M20-E1-block-size-derivation-2026-08-13.md. Measured over 21 e1_report.json / 262 folds / 15 (family,tf) groups (relay #9066): sigma_d median 0.747R, and the per-trade standardized effect delta median 0.105 with FIVE of fifteen groups NEGATIVE. b = (z_p/delta)^2 puts the 0.75-0.80 per-fold reliability band at 41-64 trades; b=50 gives 0.771 and sits inside it. RECOMMENDATION: KEEP 50, and record this document as its basis. Also closed the fold_blocks docstring gap: u = max(0, floor(N/b)-1) and the gate needs u>=2, so a leg needs N >= 3b = 150 at the default, not the 100 the matrix refs imply.
items.not_measured:
THE TRUE delta. `_best_tau` takes the MAX over ~7 tau arms per fold — the same selection the gate uses, so it measures the right decision, but it biases the mean effect UPWARD. Every block figure in the derivation is therefore a LOWER bound and the honest reading is 'delta <= 0.105 typical'. Quantifying the selection bias needs per-tau fold arms, which the reports DO carry; not done.

THE GATE'S JOINT SPECIFICITY. The P_false column in the derivation is the false-positive rate of the FOLD-VOTE CONDITION ALONE; the gate also requires mean_auc > 0.55 and an independent beats_hard majority, so the joint rate is materially lower. Those numbers upper-bound one of three conditions and must not be quoted as the gate's specificity.

WHETHER sigma_d IS STABLE PER LEG — estimated per group from as few as 3 folds, and donchian 4h sits at 5.287, seven times the median. A per-leg block would be defensible on that spread and is deliberately NOT proposed: verdicts graded at different blocks are not comparable.
items.remaining_work:
1. Record the derivation as --min-fold-trades' stated basis (a comment pointing at the doc, the way _MIN_FOLD_TRAIN_ROWS = 500 carries its own). Do NOT change the value.
2. STOP treating block size as the exit_head_ml unblock lever — the derivation closes that route. The 7 daily legs are not blocked by an arbitrary number: at 31-72 lifetime trades (50-104 on full history) NO block size yields a test that is both powered and specific. At N=98 the only gradeable options give either 0.49 power or a 50% single-condition false-positive rate.
3. THE REAL FINDING IS UPSTREAM AND IS NOT ABOUT VALIDATION: delta ~ 0.105 with 5 of 15 groups negative means the exit head's edge over the actual replay is small and inconsistent ACROSS FAMILIES. That is a question about the head, not about how it is graded, and it deserves its own item.
4. Quantify the best-tau selection bias from the per-tau fold arms already in the reports — it decides whether delta is 0.105 or materially less, and everything above is conditioned on it.
5. squeeze_breakout_4h is unaffected by any of this (BTCUSDT 4h, 98 trades): under the corrected 3x bar it needs 150, not 100, so its 'misses by two trades' ref is wrong and it needs 52.
items.resolution_criteria: --min-fold-trades carries a stated basis pointing at the derivation; the coverage matrix stops citing the 100-trade bar; and the 7 daily legs are dispositioned on the derivation's finding (no block size helps) rather than on 'not enough trades yet'. The upstream question — is the exit head's edge real and consistent — is tracked separately, since this row cannot close it.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Criterion 1 is met (scripts/ml/train_exit_head.py:585 cites docs/research/M20-E1-block-size-derivation-2026-08-13.md as --min-fold-trades' basis, and that file exists). Criteria 2 and 3 are not: the spy_trend_long_1d exit_head_ml ref still opens 'a 50-trade test block needs >=100 for one fold' (the corrected bar is 150, stated only in a later appended segment), and all 7 equity 1d legs still carry `blocked:insufficient_lifetime_trades` — i.e. dispositioned as 'not enough trades yet' rather than on the derivation's finding that no block size helps. — Tier-2 / milestone-governance: the disposition is the same operator decision as BL-20260813-M20-DONE-CONDITION-IS-60PCT-ONE-FACT-THE-1D-FLEET-IS-TOO-THIN. Ends when the 7 cells carry a status/reason derived from the block-size derivation and the stale 100-trade bar is pruned from their refs.

Re-validated: M20 exit-program measurement/tooling correctness. Propose-only, no live-order impact. Blocked on trainer capacity (91.7% disk) for anything needing a re-sweep. Corroborated by BL-20260814-1D-EQUITY-LEGS-TRADE-4-PER-YEAR-SO-PER-LEG-OOS-25-CONSUMES-6-YEARS — the 1d fleet is trade-rate-bound, not tooling-bound.

items.title: The M20 exit head's fleet edge IS the hindsight: +1.217R with best-tau vs -0.341R when tau is chosen causally, hit rate 70.2% -> a coin flip. Only 2 of 7 scalp legs beat a stale-stop; no non-scalp leg beats doing nothing
items.source:
SURFACED AS A BY-PRODUCT of deriving E1's block size (docs/research/M20-E1-block-size-derivation-2026-08-13.md), and it is the more important half. Filed separately BECAUSE it is not a validation question - burying it in a block-size row would have kept the whole thread pointed at the measuring instrument.

MEASURED over every e1_report.json on the trainer (relay #9066): 21 reports, 262 folds all carrying both arms, 15 (family, timeframe) groups. For a fold of n trades, sum(d_i) = best_tau_net_r - actual_net_r, so the per-trade paired difference is recoverable and sigma_d follows from sd(d_bar)*sqrt(n_bar).

  sigma_d  median 0.747R   (range 0.462 .. 5.287)
  delta    median 0.105    (range -0.317 .. +0.324)

FIVE of fifteen groups are NEGATIVE - the model arm LOSES to the actual replay on average: slv_trend_1h -0.317, allmix 1d -0.092, pullback 1d -0.056, pullback 2h -0.041. The positive tail is entirely the scalp family (ict_scalp_5m +0.324, avax +0.175, sol_15m +0.158, xrp_5m +0.156). The two largest trend/pullback groups by fold count sit at +0.016 (donchian 1h, 22 folds) and +0.006 (donchian 4h, 66 folds) - indistinguishable from zero.

SO THE EDGE IS CONCENTRATED IN ONE FAMILY AND ABSENT OR NEGATIVE ELSEWHERE. That is a statement about the head, not about the gate.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE NUMBERS LOOK: delta is measured on the BEST-TAU arm, which `_best_tau` selects as the max over ~7 tau arms per fold. That is the same selection the live gate makes, so it is the right quantity to grade - but it is a maximum of correlated draws and is biased UPWARD. The honest reading is 'delta <= 0.105 typical', and the negative groups are negative DESPITE that bias.

=== UPDATE 2026-08-13 ~21:40Z - BOTH OPEN MEASUREMENTS DONE (relays #9071/#9072/#9074/#9075, 31 reports, up from the 21 above) ===

(1) THE SELECTION BIAS IS THE EFFECT, NOT A BIAS ON IT. The gate credits the head with (best_tau_net_r - actual_net_r). Scoring the MEDIAN of the 7 tau arms instead - a tau chosen without hindsight - flips the sign in every non-scalp group:
    pullback (trades,50)   112 folds  edge +1.362R  MEDIAN-ARM -1.379R
    pullback (trades,15)   169 folds  edge -0.027R  MEDIAN-ARM -0.962R
    donchian (trades,15)    61 folds  edge +0.670R  MEDIAN-ARM -1.554R
    allmix   (calendar)    106 folds  edge +0.295R  MEDIAN-ARM -1.534R
    donchian (calendar)     14 folds  edge +0.426R  MEDIAN-ARM -4.399R
    slv_trend_1h             4 folds  edge -8.282R  MEDIAN-ARM -13.902R  (n=4, too thin to weigh)
versus every scalp group staying positive: ict_scalp_5m +6.037R, xrp_5m +3.353R, avax_5m +3.069R, sol_5m +2.966R, sol_15m +2.331R, xrp_15m +2.178R, eth_15m +0.672R.
23-50% of folds in the non-scalp groups are FLIPS - the median arm loses to doing nothing while the selected arm wins, so the fold's beats_actual vote is carried entirely by which of seven arms landed.

(2) THE HEAD LOSES TO THE HARD LEVERS IN ALL THREE FOLD GEOMETRIES. Both gate majorities need >= 2/3 of usable folds; pooled over 35 leg-rows / 27 distinct legs:
    calendar-folds    15 legs  120 folds   beats_actual 61.7% FAIL   beats_hard 58.3% FAIL
    trade-folds b=15   7 legs  230 folds   beats_actual 68.7% pass   beats_hard 62.2% FAIL
    trade-folds b=50  13 legs  199 folds   beats_actual 69.8% pass   beats_hard 61.8% FAIL
beats_hard is the BINDING condition fleet-wide. These are fold-pooled rates and the gate is applied PER LEG, so they summarise rather than reproduce the gate - the per-leg verdicts are 12 candidate / 21 honest_negative / 2 insufficient_base.

(3) INCIDENTALLY MEASURED, filed here because it changes how any per-leg verdict should be read: the per-fold vote is cast on the LEG's trades, not the block. fold_blocks cuts blocks over the FAMILY's pooled trades while per_leg_summary votes per leg, so in multi-leg families n_leg << b - `pullback` at b=15 has median n_leg = 3 (min 1), `allmix` median 5 (min 1), `pullback` at b=50 median 12, while every single-leg family sits exactly at 50. Full detail + the corrected reliability figures in docs/research/M20-E1-block-size-derivation-2026-08-13.md section 6.

=== UPDATE 2026-08-13 ~21:45Z - THE HINDSIGHT-FREE MEASUREMENT (relay #9077, 31 reports, 514 scored folds). This is item 4 and it is now DONE. ===

`folds` is chronological per leg (fold_blocks builds it sequentially), so a causal tau-selection rule is computable from the EXISTING reports with no retraining. Two rules, both strictly causal; fold 1 of each leg excluded for having no prior (reported as skip1st so the denominator is never short):
  PREV   - the tau with the highest net_r on the leg's PREVIOUS fold
  EXPAND - the tau with the highest CUMULATIVE net_r over all prior folds

FLEET, 514 folds, mean / median / frac_positive:
  best arm (WHAT THE GATE CREDITS, hindsight)   +1.217R  +1.220R  70.2%
  EXPAND vs actual  (causal)                    -0.341R  +0.285R  54.1%
  PREV   vs actual  (causal)                    -0.674R  +0.065R  50.8%
  EXPAND vs stale_8_0                           -0.163R  +0.320R  54.9%
  PREV   vs stale_8_0                           -0.496R  +0.160R  53.3%

THE FAMILY SPLIT SURVIVES BOTH CAUSAL RULES, and that is the finding that matters. Every scalp group is positive vs actual under PREV and EXPAND (ict_scalp_5m +5.638/+6.304, xrp_5m +4.525/+4.980, avax_5m +3.538/+3.284, sol_15m +3.027/+3.477, xrp_15m +3.118/+3.578, sol_5m +2.714/+3.102, eth_15m +0.630/+0.066). Every non-scalp group is negative under both (allmix -1.707/-1.250, pullback b=50 -1.350/-0.919, donchian b=15 -1.488/-0.723, donchian calendar -2.628/-2.537).

AGAINST THE HARD LEVERS EVEN SCALP MOSTLY FAILS. PREV vs stale_8_0 per scalp leg: sol_15m +2.723, ict_scalp_5m +1.564, sol_5m +0.340, avax_5m +0.229, xrp_15m -0.010, xrp_5m -0.470, eth_15m -1.658. So 2 of 7 clear an eight-bar stale-stop once tau is picked without hindsight.

This is the MECHANISM behind BL-20260813-EXIT-HEAD-HARNESS-PASS-DOES-NOT-SURVIVE-THE-LIVE-BOOK: a gate scored on the max of seven arms will pass a leg whose arm ordering is unstable, and ict_scalp_5m then had every tau lose on the live book. Full detail: docs/research/M20-E1-block-size-derivation-2026-08-13.md section 9.

What remains unmeasured at this code: pullback / allmix / the 1d legs (already negative under both causal rules, so a nested read refines a negative rather than changing a decision). Also unmeasured: whether the thin scalp margin over stale_8_0 (+0.668R, 56.2%) survives a larger sample, and whether the two 15m PASSes (5-6 leg-folds each) hold at n.

WHERE IN THE INTERVAL THE DEPLOYED HEAD ACTUALLY SITS. PREV and EXPAND are LOWER bounds on a well-designed selection - they pick tau from earlier folds only and therefore eat regime drift between folds. EXPAND already beats PREV (-0.341 vs -0.674), which says selection QUALITY matters and better rules exist; picking tau on the TRAINING HALF OF THE SAME FOLD would be contemporaneous and should do better still. The achievable value lies between EXPAND and best, i.e. in [-0.341R, +1.217R]. DO NOT read 'causal selection is negative' as 'the deployed head would be negative' - that is not the claim. What IS established is narrower and sufficient: the interval straddles zero and is wider than the effect being claimed, so the gate's +1.217R cannot be quoted as a deployment expectation.

MEAN AND MEDIAN DIVERGE and both must be read (PREV: mean -0.674, median +0.065), so the mean carries a negative tail of a few bad folds. frac_positive is the robust statistic and it is ~51-55% for every causal rule against every baseline.

THIN GROUPS carry none of the conclusions: slv_trend_1h 3 scored folds, uso_trend_1h 2, eth_15m 5, xrp_15m 5, sol_15m 6.

THE '% OF EDGE' RATIO from the earlier update is not a usable statistic and is quoted nowhere - unstable near a zero denominator.

items.title: The LIVE donchian-1h exit head has fired EXACTLY TWICE in a month, both on real money - so its 'validated + live' grade rests entirely on an E1 verdict scored by best-arm hindsight, with n=2 of live track record behind it
items.source:
NOT A MEASURED DEFECT IN THIS HEAD. This row records that a live lever's justification rests on a basis shown tonight to be unreliable in aggregate, and that the check has never been run. Stating it that way deliberately: I did not measure this head, and the fleet result does not transfer to it by itself.

WHAT IS LIVE. docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json grades exit_head_ml `shipped` for THREE legs - trend_donchian (BTCUSDT 1h), trend_donchian_eth (ETHUSDT 1h), trend_donchian_sol (SOLUSDT 1h) - ref 'E3 LIVE 2026-07-12 (#6211 merged, operator-approved; artifact promoted shadow->advisory #6217; deploy #6216). below_half_r@tau0.10'. The legend defines `shipped` as 'validated + live'.

WHAT WAS MEASURED TONIGHT (relays #9071-#9077, 31 e1_report.json, 514 folds). The E1 gate scores max(net_r) over ~7 tau arms on the TEST fold - the arm is selected using the outcome it is graded on. Replacing that with a strictly causal rule (tau from prior folds only) moves the fleet from +1.217R / 70.2% of folds positive to -0.341R / 54.1%. Detail in docs/research/M20-E1-block-size-derivation-2026-08-13.md section 9.

WHY IT REACHES THIS HEAD, AND HOW FAR. The MECHANISM is the gate's scoring rule, which is the same rule that produced this head's E1 verdict. The MEASUREMENT does not cover it: the 31 reports contain `donchian` 4h (trade-folds) and `donchian` 1h (calendar folds, whose per_leg blocks are slv_trend_1h and uso_trend_1h) - the BTC/ETH/SOL donchian-1h legs are in NONE of them. So the honest statement is 'the basis is suspect and this head has not been checked against it', NOT 'this head fails'.

THE CORROBORATING PRECEDENT IS ON A DIFFERENT LEG AND SHOULD NOT BE OVER-READ EITHER: BL-20260813-EXIT-HEAD-HARNESS-PASS-DOES-NOT-SURVIVE-THE-LIVE-BOOK records ict_scalp_5m passing 3/3 harness folds on the best-arm figure and then having EVERY tau lose on its live book. Same shape, different strategy family.

ONE DETAIL THAT CUTS BOTH WAYS: the shipped shape is tau=0.10, the FIRST entry in train_exit_head.TAUS = [0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50]. If 0.10 is systematically the best arm rather than a per-fold argmax winner, the selection concern is materially weaker for this head. That is checkable and unchecked - do not assume either way.

=== VERIFIED 2026-08-13 ~22:05Z - THE HEAD IS AN APPLY PATH, NOT A SHADOW, AND THE MODULE SAID OTHERWISE ===

I set out to confirm the 'live' premise rather than inherit it from the matrix ref, and the two sources disagreed. src/runtime/exit_head_shadow.py's MODULE docstring read 'Observe-only by construction: the function returns None always, never raises into the monitor, and nothing reads the logs back. Graduation to a real exit influence is E3 - Tier-3, operator-gated' - i.e. E3 in the FUTURE tense.

FIELD BEATS COMMENT. src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py:909-911 is:
    eh_verdict = _exit_head_verdict(_eh_rec, meta, cfg_dict, current_price)
    if eh_verdict is not None:
        return eh_verdict
That return closes a live position. And config/strategies.yaml declares `exit_head_action: close` on EXACTLY the three strategies the matrix marks shipped - trend_donchian (line 213), trend_donchian_sol (1102), trend_donchian_eth (1172) - all `execution: live`. The function's OWN docstring was already correct ('the record dict is returned so the monitor's E3 APPLY path can consult it'); only the module header was stale.

So the matrix ref is right and the module docstring was wrong. The premise of this row HOLDS: the head is an apply path on three live strategies, gated on (a) that YAML declare, (b) artifact stage == advisory, (c) the policy firing. Module docstring corrected in this session (docstring-only, Tier-1 - the field stands untouched).

STILL NOT VERIFIED BY ME: condition (b), the artifact's live registry stage. The matrix ref cites promotion #6217, which is a claim about July, not a reading of the registry tonight.

=== CONDITION (b) NOW READ, NOT INFERRED (relay #9078, 2026-08-13 21:57Z) ===
  runtime_logs/trainer_mirror/exit_head/exit-head-donchian-1h-v1.json
      stage = advisory      <- the operator promotion gate is OPEN
      shape = {'policy': 'below_half_r', 'tau': 0.1, 'below_r': 0.5}
      trained_at = 2026-07-12T14:44:43Z
  runtime_logs/trainer_mirror/exit_head/exit-head-donchian-peak-1h-v1.json
      stage = shadow        <- NOT applying (peak_full @ tau 0.8); noted so a reader does not
                               conflate the two artifacts

ALL THREE APPLY CONDITIONS ARE THEREFORE SATISFIED and every one of them is now READ rather than inherited from a ref: (a) the YAML declare, (b) stage advisory, (c) the per-bar policy. The head is live and applying on three real strategies.

ONE PRECISION, because it is a different file on a different box: this read is the TRAINER's mirror - the SOURCE that publish_trainer_mirror.sh rsyncs to the live VM - not the live VM's published copy. The artifact is a month old and publishing runs continuously, so they are almost certainly identical, but 'almost certainly' is not a reading and the distinction is stated rather than smoothed. Confirming the LIVE copy needs a surface that can serve it; exit_head artifacts are not in the /api/diag/log_file allowlist, which is itself worth noting - the artifact that can close a live position has no live read surface.

=== THE HEAD MAY NEVER HAVE FIRED (live relay #9080, 2026-08-13 21:59Z) - STATED WITH ITS POPULATION, WHICH IS PARTIAL ===

POPULATION, because the number is worthless without it: 137 rows I could parse out of a `lines=400` tail of /data/bot-data/runtime_logs/exit_lever_soak.jsonl (size 430,743 bytes), and the relay payload itself carried a `... (truncated)` marker. The tail spans 2026-08-09T23:52Z -> 2026-08-12T09:57Z, i.e. ~3 days of a head shipped 2026-07-12. This is NOT a lifetime count.

IN THAT WINDOW: lever counts are trail_decay 111, stale_stop 26, exit_head **0**.

THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THE ZERO MEAN ANYTHING (a negative needs a denominator): 32 of the 137 rows are donchian-family strategies (trend_donchian_ada_4h 24, trend_donchian_eth_4h 8). So donchian monitors ARE running and ARE writing to this exact log in this exact window - the absence of exit_head rows is not an empty log, a dead monitor, or a mis-specified probe.

WHAT THIS SUGGESTS AND DOES NOT SHOW. `below_half_r @ tau=0.1` requires P(pays) < 0.1 AND open_r < 0.5, which is a deliberately narrow corner; zero firings in 3 days is consistent with a head that fires rarely or never. If it has NEVER fired, the ship is INERT - which flips the urgency of this row completely (an inert lever cannot make bad exits) while creating a different problem: the matrix grades these three cells `shipped` = 'validated + live', and a lever that is live in config but has never acted is not what a reader takes from that word. It does NOT show the head never fired over its lifetime - three days is not a month, and the payload was truncated on top.

WHY I COULD NOT JUST COUNT: /api/diag/log_file only TAILS. There is no relay-reachable way to count occurrences across a whole live log, so 'how many times has this lever ever fired' is currently unanswerable from a sandbox session for ANY lever, not just this one. That is a gap in the read surface, not in this investigation.

=== ANSWERED: IT HAS FIRED, TWICE (live relay #9086, 2026-08-13 22:12Z) ===

THE FILTER IS PROVABLY APPLIED THIS TIME - controls first, because the previous attempt's numbers were garbage: unfiltered total 4639 · strategy_name LIKE 'trend_donchian%' -> 203 · = 'smoke_test' -> 9 · = 'zzz_no_such_strategy' -> 0. Four distinct totals and a reachable genuine zero.

  trades WHERE exit_reason LIKE '%exit_head%'  ->  TOTAL 2

  id 3344  trend_donchian  BTCUSDT  bybit_2 (real_money)  opened 2026-07-10T01:50Z
           closed 2026-07-12T14:46:45Z  63754.2 -> 64128.1  pnl +1.4956 (+0.5865%)  fee 0.1913
           notes: pnl_source=local_compute, exit_price_source=recorded_exit_price
  id 3770  trend_donchian  BTCUSDT  bybit_2 (real_money)  opened 2026-07-21T07:58Z
           closed 2026-07-21T23:03:15Z  66238.5 -> 66214.3  pnl -0.2512 (-0.0759%)  fee 0.2484
           notes: exit_price_source=bybit_closed_pnl  <- broker truth

Gross +1.2444 across the two; the two recorded taker fees sum to 0.4397, so net is on the order of +0.80 on a real-money account. PROVENANCE IS MIXED and the two rows are not equally trustworthy: 3770 carries bybit_closed_pnl (broker truth), 3344 is local_compute over a recorded exit price. Do not average them as if they were the same kind of number.

THE FIRST FIRING IS TWO MINUTES AFTER THE ARTIFACT WAS TRAINED. The artifact stamps trained_at 2026-07-12T14:44:43Z (#9078); trade 3344 closed 2026-07-12T14:46:45Z. It was opened on 07-10, so the head fired on an already-open position at essentially its first live evaluation. That IS the 'first head-driven exit = mandatory health-review check' moment the matrix ref promises - whether the check was performed remains unverified.

THIS RECONCILES THE EARLIER SOAK READ RATHER THAN CONTRADICTING IT. The #9080 tail covered 2026-08-09 -> 08-12 and found 0 exit_head rows; both firings were 07-12 and 07-21, outside that window. The tail was never evidence of never-fired - it was evidence of a 3-day window, which is what it was labelled as.

WHAT THIS CHANGES. 'The lever may be inert' is now WRONG and is retracted: it acts, on real money. But n=2 in a month is far too thin to be a track record, which sharpens rather than softens this row - the `shipped` = 'validated + live' grade rests ENTIRELY on the E1 verdict, and that verdict was scored by the best-arm hindsight measured tonight. There is no live evidence to fall back on.

=== THE LIVE MECHANICS CHECK OUT; THE LIVE *EDGE* IS UNTESTED. Distinguishing these is the whole point (operator directive 2026-08-13: live soaking is for seeing that the mechanics work and that performance matches backtest expectations - not for discovering whether there is an edge). ===

MECHANICS - PASS. The declared shape is below_half_r: fire when score < tau AND open_r < below_r (0.5). Reconstructing open_r from each row's own entry/stop/exit (both direction=long):
  3344  risk/unit 1043.000  move +373.90  open_r +0.3585  < 0.5  OK
  3770  risk/unit  818.821  move  -24.20  open_r -0.0296  < 0.5  OK
Both firings satisfy the declared condition, so the apply path is doing what the artifact's shape says. CAVEAT, stated because it is a real gap and not a nitpick: this is open_r at the EXIT, while the head decides on the last CLOSED bar and the fill lands after - so it is a strong consistency check, not a reconstruction of the decision. The score itself is not on the trades row (it is in shadow_predictions.jsonl with event_source=exit_head), so the `score < tau` half is UNCHECKED here.

EDGE - UNTESTED, and n=2 cannot test it. One winner cut at +0.36R and one scratch at -0.03R. Note what the winner means under this policy: below_half_r fires on trades that have NOT yet proven themselves (open_r < 0.5R), so cutting 3344 at +0.36R FORECLOSED whatever it would have done next. Whether that was right is exactly the counterfactual a backtest answers and a 2-trade live sample cannot.

So the live record supports 'the plumbing works' and says nothing either way about 'the head helps' - which is precisely why the E1 verdict's basis is the load-bearing question in this row.
items.why_it_matters: This is a live lever on real-money strategies, so the cost of the basis being wrong is not a mis-graded matrix cell - it is exits taken on a head that does not help. The matrix already ships a status for exactly this situation (`shipped_gate_failed`: 'LIVE in config, but a LATER re-sweep failed its gate and the operator chose to HOLD'), which exists because recording a live lever as `honest_negative` implies NOT live and recording it as `shipped` overclaims once the validation no longer reproduces. If the check below fails, that status - not a silent re-grade - is where this cell belongs, and the HOLD/pull decision is the operator's. Sharpened by the docstring finding: a reader auditing whether the exit head can move money would have opened exit_head_shadow.py, read 'observe-only by construction', and stopped. The stale paragraph was load-bearing in the wrong direction - it did not just fail to describe the apply path, it actively argued there wasn't one.
items.what_to_check:
1. Re-run the donchian-1h E1 round at current code (scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py --legs trend_donchian,trend_donchian_eth,trend_donchian_sol --tf 1h) and read the NEW `selected_tau` / `selected_tau_state` fields written by train_exit_head._select_tau_holdout. That picks tau on a validation block carved from each fold's own training window, so it answers the question directly.
