3. Whether the 'first head-driven exit = mandatory health-review check' promised in the matrix ref was ever actually performed. I did not verify this and it is the cheapest independent read on whether the head is helping live.
4. DONE (#9078) - the trainer-side artifact is at stage `advisory`, so the gate is open. What is NOT done is reading the LIVE VM's published copy of it: exit_head artifacts are absent from the /api/diag/log_file allowlist, so the artifact that can close a live position currently has no live read surface. Adding one is the same shape as the 2026-08-12 exit_loop_health omission (writer shipped, allowlist entry not) and is cheap.
items.not_measured:
EVERYTHING ABOUT THIS SPECIFIC HEAD. No donchian-1h BTC/ETH/SOL e1_report exists among the 31 on the trainer, so nothing in tonight's numbers is evidence about it. I also did not check the live registry, the deploy, or whether the mandatory post-ship health-review check happened - all four are listed above as work, not asserted as findings.

ALSO NOT ESTABLISHED that a causal selection would be negative even fleet-wide: the causal rules measured are LOWER bounds (they pick tau from earlier folds and eat regime drift), so the achievable value sits in [-0.341R, +1.217R]. That interval straddles zero, which is what makes the check necessary - not a conclusion that the head loses.
items.remaining_work:
0. DONE (#9086) - the head has fired TWICE, both real-money bybit_2 BTCUSDT, net ~+0.80 after fees. Not inert. n=2 is not a track record, so the rest of this row stands and matters MORE, not less.
1. Run the donchian-1h round at current code and read selected_tau (items 1-2 in what_to_check). Tier-1, trainer-side, no operator gate.
2. Report the result to the operator with the shipped/hold/pull options laid out. Any CHANGE to the live head is Tier-3 and is NOT taken by the session that measures it.

4. Generalise: any exit_head_ml cell graded `shipped` or `passed_unshipped` on a best-arm E1 verdict carries the same question. Enumerate them from the matrix rather than assuming these three are the only ones.
items.resolution_criteria: A donchian-1h E1 round exists at code carrying _select_tau_holdout, its selected_tau is compared against the best arm per fold, and the operator has a stated decision on the three live cells. Closing this by arguing the fleet result does not apply, without running the round, is not a resolution - the point of the row is that the check is cheap and has never been done.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The code the check needs now exists (train_exit_head.py `_select_tau_holdout` + selected_tau/selected_tau_state per fold), and the matrix's trend_donchian BTCUSDT 1h exit_head_ml cell has moved to `shipped_gate_failed` with a live-parity re-sweep ref (relay #9206, tp_cap_pct=0.099, 23 folds). But the row's criterion — a donchian-1h E1 round at code carrying _select_tau_holdout whose selected_tau is compared against the best arm per fold, plus a stated operator decision on the three live cells — is not evidenced: no such comparison appears in docs/research/ and the ETH/SOL cells still read `shipped`. — needs trainer run: `m20_exit_head_round.py --legs trend_donchian,trend_donchian_eth,trend_donchian_sol --tf 1h` at current code, reading selected_tau vs the per-fold best arm; then the operator decides hold/pull. Tier-3 for any live change.
Re-validated: a LIVE head on REAL MONEY whose validation rests on best-arm hindsight and which has fired twice in a month. High-priority — it is shipped, not proposed.

MEASURED THIS SESSION, AND IT SHARPENS THE ROW RATHER THAN CLOSING IT: the check the row calls cheap STILL cannot be answered from any committed artifact. But docs/research/m20-exit-head-rounds.jsonl -- the graded-round record -- carries 18 fields on all 33 rows and NONE of them is `selected_tau` (population: every non-blank line in the file, counted 2026-09-02). The five donchian/1h rows in it (trend_donchian_eth candidate, trend_donchian_eth_prop candidate, trend_donchian honest_negative, trend_donchian_sol honest_negative, trend_donchian_sol_prop honest_negative) therefore CANNOT be shown to have run at holdout-tau code, and cannot be shown not to have either -- this is 'we could not look', not 'they did not'. SO THE ROW NEEDS a trainer round dispatched (label `trainer-vm-diag-request`) and its e1_report read; THIS SESSION CANNOT DO IT (`issue_write` -> 403). and byte-identical leading rows (ids 1,2,3 - the May smoke_test rows).

  /trades?filter_col=close_reason&filter_op=like&filter_val=%exit_head%  -> total 4639
  /trades?filter_col=close_reason&filter_op=like&filter_val=%stale%     -> total 4639
  /trades?filter_col=close_reason&filter_op=like&filter_val=%trail%     -> total 4639

CONFIRMED AT SOURCE, src/web/api/routers/db_explorer.py:191:
    if filter_col in colnames and filter_val is not None and filter_op in _FILTER_OPS:
An unknown filter_col fails the guard, `where` stays '', and BOTH the COUNT and the SELECT run unfiltered. `order_by in colnames` (line 202) has the same shape for sorting.

THIS IS DOCUMENTED, NOT ACCIDENTAL - the docstring says 'Unknown order/filter columns are ignored (rather than erroring) so a stale UI selection degrades gracefully.' That rationale is sound FOR THE DASHBOARD. The defect is that the RESPONSE does not say it happened: the envelope returns {table, db, columns, rows, total, limit, offset} and echoes back NOTHING about the filter. So there is no field a consumer can read to distinguish 'filter applied, 4639 rows matched' from 'filter ignored, here is the whole table'.

CONFIRMED BY CONTROL (#9086): with a REAL column the filter works exactly as documented - strategy_name LIKE 'trend_donchian%' -> 203, = 'smoke_test' -> 9, = 'zzz_no_such_strategy' -> 0, against an unfiltered 4639. So #9084's four identical 4639s were unambiguously the silent drop, not a coincidence of the data. A genuine zero IS reachable, which is what makes the silent-drop dangerous: the endpoint can express 'nothing matched', so a reader has every reason to trust a number it returns.
items.why_it_matters:
This endpoint is not only the dashboard's Data Explorer - it is one of the few /api/bot/* paths on the diag-relay allowlist (`db/table/*`), which makes it a primary ANALYSIS surface for relay-bound sessions that cannot reach the VM directly. In that use the failure is not a degraded UI, it is a confidently wrong number: I was one unverified step from reporting a `total` as the count of head-driven exits.

What caught it was ARITHMETIC, not reading - four different filters returning the identical total is impossible if the filter is applied. A single query would have looked completely normal, and 4639 is a plausible-looking count. This is the exact shape of CLAUDE.md's diagnostic-provenance sub-class C (unasserted denominator) and of the 'Collapsed states' rule: 'we filtered and everything matched' and 'we did not filter' are opposite statements sharing one representation.
items.what_to_check:
1. src/web/api/routers/db_explorer.py:191 (filter) and :202 (order_by) - both silently drop.
2. The response envelope (line ~215) - confirm it echoes no filter state.
3. Whether the Streamlit Data Explorer or the Svelte SPA displays a filter it did not actually apply. The dashboards build filter_col from the live schema so they are unlikely to send an unknown column, but that has NOT been verified and is what the graceful-degradation rationale rests on.
4. CLAUDE.md's API table describes this route as 'table/column identifiers validated against the live schema (no identifier injection)'. True about INJECTION, and a reader reasonably takes it to mean an invalid column is rejected. The prose needs the ignore-semantics stated.
items.proposed_fix:
Keep the graceful degradation; make it VISIBLE. Echo the filter's fate in the envelope as three states, never collapsed - the exit_anchor / bybit_available shape:
    filter_state: 'applied'          - filter_col/op/val were all valid and a WHERE ran
                  'not_requested'    - no filter_col was sent
                  'ignored_unknown_column' | 'ignored_bad_op' - sent, and DROPPED, with which
plus the effective filter_col/op/val echoed back. A consumer can then assert `filter_state == 'applied'` before trusting `total`, and the dashboard's stale-selection path is unchanged (it just now renders a 'filter ignored' note instead of silently showing everything). Registering it in scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py::CONTRACTS is what stops it regressing.

NOT proposed: erroring on an unknown column. That would break the documented UI degradation, and the problem was never the tolerance - it was the silence.

The contract is registered in scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py::CONTRACTS as `db_explorer.filter_state` (6 contracts, clean). But its producer-integrity check is `_states_in(prod_text, states)` — a FILE-level scan for each state as a quoted literal — so it verifies the FILE emits every state, not that the specific FIELD does.

Collapsing BOTH halves -> the guard FIRES correctly. So the guard is working as designed; the limitation is that two fields sharing a state vocabulary in one file cover for each other.
  What actually catches the single-field regression is the TEST SUITE (5 failures), not the guard. Stated here because 'registered with collapsed-state-guard' would otherwise read as stronger enforcement than exists. Generalising the guard to field-scope is a separate change affecting all 6 contracts and is NOT attempted here.

Whether any dashboard actually sends an unknown filter_col in practice (item 3). If neither does, the live blast radius is limited to relay/API consumers like this session - which is still the population that does ANALYSIS on this endpoint, so it does not reduce the severity much.

items.title: 7 exit_head_ml cells read `blocked:insufficient_lifetime_trades` while an E1 verdict for those legs DOES exist — from the calendar-fold report the matrix deliberately does not use, which the ref never says
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-13/14 while auditing the 22-cell blocked bucket (the largest contributor to M20's done-condition, and nobody had checked whether the block reasons still hold).

Seven `*_trend_long_1d` legs carry `exit_head_ml: blocked:insufficient_lifetime_trades`, ref 'E1 RE-RUN 2026-08-13 (relay #8963, fold-mode=trades, fold_blocks fix) — REASON CORRECTED'. But every one of them HAS a verdict in an e1_report on the trainer (relay #9072):

  leg                  matrix status                          E1 verdict          geom      oos  u  bA bH
  spy_trend_long_1d    blocked:insufficient_lifetime_trades   honest_negative     calendar   29  9   4  3
  qqq_trend_long_1d    blocked:insufficient_lifetime_trades   honest_negative     calendar   31  9   3  4
  tqqq_trend_long_1d   blocked:insufficient_lifetime_trades   insufficient_base   calendar   24  7   4  5
  qld_trend_long_1d    blocked:insufficient_lifetime_trades   insufficient_base   calendar   23  7   3  3
  iwm_trend_long_1d    blocked:insufficient_lifetime_trades   CANDIDATE           calendar   42  9   7  7
  splg_trend_long_1d   blocked:insufficient_lifetime_trades   honest_negative     calendar   43  9   5  3
  scha_trend_long_1d   blocked:insufficient_lifetime_trades   CANDIDATE           calendar   38  9   7  7

THE STATUS IS DEFENSIBLE; THE REF IS THE DEFECT. All seven verdicts come from the `allmix` report whose `fold_mode` is absent (calendar folds); NONE of the seven appears in any `fold_mode: 'trades'` report — checked across all 35 leg-rows. train_exit_head's own `per_leg_note` says trade-folds and calendar-folds are NOT comparable evidence, so declining to grade a trades-geometry cell from a calendar-geometry verdict is CORRECT. What is missing is that the ref never says that choice was made.
items.why_it_matters:
A future session doing exactly what I just did — auditing the blocked bucket for stale reasons — finds seven cells marked 'blocked: not enough trades' sitting beside seven verdicts, two of them `candidate`, and reasonably concludes the matrix is stale. It would then either re-grade on calendar evidence (wrong: incomparable geometry) or burn a round rediscovering why not. The ref costs one clause and prevents both.

It also matters because of what tonight measured: those calendar verdicts rest on the WEAKEST evidence in the whole set. Per docs/research/M20-E1-block-size-derivation-2026-08-13.md section 6, `allmix` votes on a median n_leg of 5 (min 1) per fold — the per-leg vote is cast on the LEG's trades, not the block — so `iwm`/`scha` reading `candidate` there is a near-coin-flip majority over 9 folds of ~5 trades each. Anyone who did re-grade from them would be promoting the thinnest evidence in the programme.
items.what_to_check:

2. Cross-check against any e1_report whose `fold_mode` is absent (the calendar-geometry runs) before concluding a cell is ungraded.
3. Whether the same shape exists on OTHER blocked cells — I audited the exit_head_ml column and did not sweep the other seven lever columns for blocked-cells-with-existing-verdicts.
items.proposed_fix:
Extend each of the seven refs with the fact and the reason, e.g.: '... A calendar-fold verdict DOES exist for this leg in the allmix report (<verdict>, u=<n>) and is deliberately NOT used — trade-folds and calendar-folds are not comparable evidence (train_exit_head per_leg_note), and the calendar vote rests on a median n_leg of 5 (derivation section 6).'

Cheap, and it converts a cell that LOOKS stale into one that states its own reasoning. Consider whether the roll-up should carry a `superseded_geometry` note rather than leaving it to prose.

Their lifetime trades are 23-43, and at --min-fold-trades 50 a leg needs N >= 3*block = 150 to yield u >= 2, so under trade-folds they are very likely genuinely ungradeable — which would make `blocked` not just defensible but correct. I did not run it, so I am not asserting it.

2. Sweep the other lever columns for the same shape.

items.title: A one-off analysis probe (relay #9125) labelled a `<= 0` predicate as 'folds where cond LOWERS maxDD', counting ties as wins - it would have published 'the condition lowers drawdown on most folds', the opposite of the truth
items.source:
Self-inflicted, caught in-session by the follow-up probe (#9126) and recorded rather than quietly fixed.

WHAT HAPPENED: #9125 measured whether the M20 `below_half_r` exit-head condition buys the drawdown reduction its justification claims. It printed a per-leg line 'folds where cond LOWERS maxDD: 63.6% / 45.5% / 72.7%' beside a MEAN d-maxDD that was POSITIVE (= worse) on all three legs. Read at face value that is a mean-vs-majority sign disagreement, i.e. 'helps typically, hurt by tails'.

IT WAS NOT. #9126 pulled the distribution and returned frac>0 of 36.4% / 54.5% / 27.3% - exactly the complements. The predicate was `<= 0`, so folds where the condition changed drawdown by EXACTLY ZERO (the majority: median d maxDD is +0.000 on two of the three legs, i.e. folds where the condition never bound at all) were counted as folds where it LOWERED drawdown.

CLASS: sub-class A of UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT (CLAUDE.md, 'does the OUTPUT say what it actually computed?') - the label names a quantity the accessor does not compute. Same shape as `max(proba)` printed as `P(volatile)`. The number was real, the label was confident, and a reader trusting the label reaches a confident WRONG conclusion.

WHY IT WAS CAUGHT: only because the apparent mean/majority disagreement was treated as a reason to characterise the distribution BEFORE publishing, rather than as an interesting finding to write up. Had #9126 not been run, 'the condition lowers drawdown on most folds' would have gone into docs/research/M20-E1-block-size-derivation-2026-08-13.md and into an operator ping. Recorded in that doc's section 13 too.

NOT A CODE FIX: the probe is a one-off relay payload, not committed tooling - there is nothing in the repo to patch. `scripts/check_diagnostic_provenance.py` covers scripts/{ml,research,ops,macro,reports}/ and the guard scripts; it does not and cannot see an ad-hoc relay payload.

FOLLOW-UP FOR A REVIEW SESSION: decide whether ad-hoc analysis payloads that produce numbers destined for a canonical doc should be required to land in scripts/research/ first (where the guard sees them) rather than being fired inline as base64. That is a real trade-off - the friction is the whole reason relays are fired inline - so it is a judgement call, not an obvious yes.
items.resolution_criteria: A review session has RECORDED A DECISION -- either outcome closes this row; silence does not. Observable in one of two forms: (a) ADOPTED -- a line in docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md (Generation Discipline) or CLAUDE.md (Diagnostic provenance) stating that an ad-hoc analysis payload whose numbers are destined for a canonical doc must first be committed under scripts/research/, AND `python3 scripts/check_diagnostic_provenance.py --all` demonstrably covers that path (run it; a planted mislabelled accessor there must be FLAGGED -- a quiet pass proves nothing, per the positive-control rule); or (b) NOT ADOPTED -- this row closed with an explicit written reason, the expected one being that the friction of committing a throwaway probe is the very thing that makes relays usable and the trade-off is not worth it. NOT resolution: 'be more careful with probe labels'.
evidence: relay #9125 - the mislabelled output
relay #9126 - frac>0 36.4/54.5/27.3, the complements that exposed it
docs/research/M20-E1-block-size-derivation-2026-08-13.md section 13
CLAUDE.md - 'Diagnostic provenance', sub-class A

The row explicitly says silence does not close it. — Awaiting a review-session decision; either outcome closes it. Cheap, low severity.

items.title: The coverage matrix's `blocked:<reason>` suffix is an unenforced convention: one cell carries a BARE `blocked` with no reason (which the legend requires), one uses a hyphen where every other uses underscores, and a mis-statused `n/a` sat in the blocked bucket until 2026-08-14
items.source:
Found while auditing the open set of docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json for M20. Not the assigned workstream; filed rather than swept, per 'if you see something, say something'.

THE LEGEND IS EXPLICIT: `blocked` = "cannot process yet (REASON GIVEN)"; `n/a` = "structurally inapplicable". Nothing enforces either half.

MEASURED status vocabulary across all 52 rows x 8 lever columns (416 cells):
  honest_negative                                307
  n/a                                             35 (34 after the fix below)
  shipped                                         23
  pending                                         14
  passed_unshipped                                12
  blocked:insufficient_lifetime_trades            10
  blocked:data_missing                             4
  blocked:no_harness_levers                        3
  blocked:insufficient_base                        3
  blocked                                          2 (1 after the fix below)
  blocked:insufficient_oos_base_at_derived_split   2
  blocked:native-history-thin                      1

THREE DISTINCT DEFECTS:

(1) FIXED IN THIS SESSION. `fvg_range_15m / 15m / trail_geometry` was `blocked` while its own ref read "lever not applicable - fvg_range has no trail in its exit structure (stop/target/timeout); nothing to vary". That is the legend's definition of `n/a`, verbatim, not a cell awaiting work. Re-statused blocked -> n/a. Correction of a mis-status, NOT a re-grade: verified by diffing `m20_coverage_rollup.py --json` before and after - the ONLY field that changed was `matrix_updated_at`. Every count and every cell identical (the leg is `shadow`, so it was never in the done-condition, and the headline treats blocked and n/a alike as closed).

(2) STILL OPEN, NOT FIXED - I will not invent a reason. `xauusd_trend_1h / XAUUSD / 1h / exit_head_ml` carries a BARE `blocked` with no reason suffix, and its ref BEGINS WITH THE WORD "same" - a dangling antecedent, because the 2026-08-09 row explosion (BL-20260809-COVERAGE-MATRIX-MULTILEG-ROW-ONE-STATUS) removed whatever it pointed at. The rest of the ref describes the leg's OTHER cells ("Its other cells were `blocked: candle coverage (task #27)`, superseded by the 2026-07-12 GC=F-proxy fleet sweep"), which is not a reason for THIS cell. So the reason for this cell is genuinely unrecorded and cannot be recovered from the file. The leg's `execution` is `disabled`, so there is no live-money urgency - but a blocked cell whose blocking reason nobody can state is unresolvable by construction, which is the collapsed-state shape: 'blocked for a recorded reason' and 'blocked, reason lost' are indistinguishable.

(3) STILL OPEN, COSMETIC. `blocked:native-history-thin` uses HYPHENS where all five sibling reasons use underscores. Any consumer grouping by reason string buckets it separately from an equivalent `native_history_thin` and would not notice.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the suffix is the only machine-readable statement of WHY a cell is open, and the done-condition (`no pending AND no blocked on live legs`) can only be driven down by resolving those reasons. A reason that is absent, or spelled inconsistently, is one a roll-up cannot group, count, or age. This is the same family as the row this session's other find sits in - a field that exists, is written, and is not validated.
items.resolution_criteria: Observable, three parts, all checkable by running the guard: (a) `scripts/research/m20_coverage_rollup.py --validate` (or a new sibling check) FAILS on a bare `blocked` with no `:reason` suffix, demonstrated by a planted positive control - a temporarily bare-blocked cell must be REJECTED, since a quiet pass proves nothing; (b) the reason vocabulary is normalised to underscores and the validator rejects an unrecognised reason token, so the set is closed rather than free-text; (c) `xauusd_trend_1h / exit_head_ml` either carries a real recorded reason, or is re-statused to whatever it actually is, with the evidence cited. NOT resolution: adding a reason string to xauusd_trend_1h that was inferred rather than established - if the reason is unrecoverable, say so in the ref explicitly and close the row on (a)+(b) alone.

items.title: The regime-flip replay writes `verdict: PASS` on legs where the lever NEVER FIRED -- 12 of 14 fleet passes have flip_pct 0.0, so the plain reading of the label is wrong 86% of the time
items.source:
Found while establishing whether two prop-leg regime_flip_exit cells could be graded from existing evidence (relays #9138-#9141). Not the assigned workstream; filed rather than swept.

MEASURED across all 42 artifacts in runtime_logs/m20_flip_replay/2026-07-13/:
  verdict PASS   14
  verdict fail   28
Of the 14 PASS, TWELVE have flip_pct == 0.0 -- the flip never fired on a single trade, so `flip` is byte-identical to `actual` and the walk-forward reads a perfect 6/6 because every fold is a TIE counted as a beat. Exactly two passes involve a flip that actually fires: trend_donchian_eth_4h (46.8%) and trend_donchian_eth_prop (45.9%).

WHY IT MATTERS: `verdict: PASS` + `walkforward: 6/6` is as strong as this artifact's output gets, and on 12 of 14 legs it means the lever DID NOTHING. A reader who trusts the label concludes the opposite of the truth. Worked example from this session: trend_donchian_sol_prop reads PASS 6/6 and its every fold is identical to the actual exit to four decimals.

CLASS: the tie-counted-as-a-win shape -- the same defect as BL-20260814-PROBE-COUNTED-TIES-AS-WINS, but in SHIPPED TOOLING rather than a throwaway relay probe, and therefore durable and re-readable by every future session. Adjacent to UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A (CLAUDE.md): the label names a quantity ("the flip beat the actual exit") that the computation does not distinguish from "there was no flip".

THE DISAMBIGUATING FIELD ALREADY EXISTS: `flip_pct`. Nothing forces it to be read beside the verdict, and the matrix refs that cite these artifacts do not all carry it.

NOT A FABRICATED NUMBER: every value in the artifact is correct. This is purely about what the LABEL licenses a reader to conclude -- which is why it is medium and not high.
items.resolution_criteria: Observable: (a) the flip replay emits a verdict that CANNOT be read as a positive when the lever never fired -- either a distinct third state (e.g. `no_fire` / `degenerate_tie`, registered with collapsed-state-guard so producer and consumer are both checked) or a verdict that is refused unless flip_pct > 0; AND (b) a planted positive control demonstrates it -- an artifact with flip_pct 0.0 must NOT come back `PASS`, verified by running it, since a quiet pass proves nothing; AND (c) the existing 12 degenerate-PASS artifacts are either re-emitted or annotated so a future reader of the ON-DISK files is not misled by the stale label. NOT resolution: documenting the caveat in a doc and leaving the field as-is -- the artifacts outlive the doc and are read directly.

trend_donchian_sol_prop_flip.json — PASS, walkforward 6/6, flip_pct 0.0, every fold identical to actual

items.title: m20_exit_head_round.py STRUCTURALLY cannot produce a live-parity book -- no --tp-cap-pct option exists and it calls base_args positionally, so every exit-head round on disk (11 confirmed, incl. donchian_1h_nested) contains ZERO take-profit exits
items.source:
Found by launching a round and reading what it actually executed, not by reading the code first.

THE MECHANISM: m20_exit_head_round.py:145 calls base_args(leg, cfg, fam, data, resample) -- five positional args -- so tp_cap_pct takes its default 0.0. base_args appends --tp-r / --tp-cap-pct ONLY when tp_cap_pct > 0.0 (line 386). The driver's own argparse has NO --tp-cap-pct option (only --legs --tf --data-dir --out --db --target --features), so a caller CANNOT ask for one. Every harness therefore runs at its defaults tp_cap_pct=0.0, tp_r=50.0 (sentinel) = no take-profit modelled.

SEEN DIRECTLY: my launch log (relay #9144) shows the emitted command carrying `--trail-mult 3.5` and NO `--tp-r`, on trend_donchian_sol_prop whose config declares tp_r: 6.0. That round was aborted and quarantined to prop_1h.ABORTED-WRONG-GEOMETRY/ with a DO-NOT-USE.txt rather than left on disk looking authoritative.

THE FIRST AUDIT METHOD FAILED AND ITS POSITIVE CONTROL CAUGHT IT. Searching each round_report.json for the harness flags returned --trail-mult FALSE on every round -- including rounds whose logs demonstrably carry it. So round_report.json does not record harness args at all; the search measured nothing and its uniform 'no --tp-r' answer was uninformative rather than confirming. Without the control it would have produced exactly the expected answer and been believed.

THE SECOND METHOD IS INDEPENDENT AND CONCLUSIVE -- exit-reason distributions over the emitted trades. Across 2h, 4h, donchian_1h_nested, eh_1d, eh_1h, eh_sq4h, p4_hp_ext_1h, p4_peak_1h, peak_2h, peak_4h and the aborted prop round, the reasons are trail_stop / stop / timeout / flip / stale_stop and NOT ONE take_profit exit appears. POPULATION: 11 round directories under runtime_logs/m20_exit_head/ that carry a readable emit/*.jsonl exit_reason field, out of 13 with an emit dir (the other 2 are the scalp rounds below); one emitted leg file inspected per round; per-round trade counts n=63..977. Eleven rounds, ZERO take-profit exits, denominator stated.

UNDETERMINED, NOT CONFIRMED: scalp_15m and scalp_5m emit exit_reason as (none) -- the scalp harness does not stamp it -- so this method says nothing about them either way.

SCOPE OF THE CONSEQUENCE: this is BL-20260810-BACKTEST-DOES-NOT-MODEL-THE-LIVE-CAPPED-TP, already known for the LEVER SWEEPS, where the fix was making tp_cap_pct=0.099 the workflow default. The exit-head rounds were never given that fix and cannot be given it without a code change. donchian_1h_nested is among the affected rounds, and it is the round behind doc sections 12-17 AND behind the re-sweep of the three SHIPPED exit_head_ml cells.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: it does not invalidate sections 13-16, which are WITHIN-BOOK arm contrasts (cond vs uncond, same tau, same folds, same trades -- section 16 verified trade counts identical on 100% of ACTIVE folds -- population: 19 of 22 folds on trend_donchian, 22 of 22 on _eth, 20 of 22 on _sol, i.e. 61 active leg-folds of 66 total, the remainder being no-ops), so a geometry bias shared by both arms cancels in the difference. What it conditions is their TRANSFER to production: the live units clamp tp = min(entry*(1+0.099), entry + tp_r*risk) -- 0.099 is the declared _TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT constant in trend_donchian.py:133, a PARAMETER not a measurement, and the conditional arm's entire mechanism is holding longer (+3.6 to +4.8 bars), so a 9.9% cap truncates exactly the right tail the arm is buying. The magnitudes, and possibly the sign, need not carry. The direction of that error is NOT known and is not guessed at.

=== PART (c) DONE 2026-08-14 ~04:48Z (relay #9151) — the 11 round dirs are annotated on disk ===

Each affected round now carries a GEOMETRY-NO-TAKE-PROFIT.txt naming the mechanism, that round's OWN exit-reason evidence, and explicitly what it does and does NOT invalidate (within-round arm-vs-arm comparisons still hold; carrying a verdict to production unqualified does not). Artifacts outlive docs and are read directly, which is why a doc caveat alone was not sufficient.

MARKED FROM THE DATA, not from an assumption about which rounds ran — and this pass read EVERY emit file per round rather than the one-file sample the original audit used, so these are FULL populations:
  2h                              n=938   trail_stop 451 / stop 434 / timeout 53
  4h                              n=970   trail_stop 842 / flip 128
  donchian_1h_nested              n=1224  trail_stop 604 / stop 600 / timeout 20
  eh_1d                           n=949   trail_stop 619 / stop 314 / timeout 16
  eh_1h                           n=1992  trail_stop 1249 / stop 645 / giveback_stop 81 / timeout 17
  eh_sq4h                         n=100   trail_stop 62 / stop 21 / timeout 17
  p4_hp_ext_1h                    n=1650  trail_stop 1456 / flip 194
  p4_peak_1h                      n=1650  trail_stop 1456 / flip 194
  peak_2h                         n=1654  trail_stop 917 / stop 662 / timeout 75
  peak_4h                         n=991   trail_stop 757 / flip 121 / stale_stop 113
  prop_1h.ABORTED-WRONG-GEOMETRY  n=1278  trail_stop 732 / stop 293 / stale_stop 253

ZERO take-profit exits in any of them, now on full per-round populations (n=100..1992) rather than a single leg file. That is a STRONGER confirmation than the original audit, not a restatement of it.

SKIPPED AND STATED, not silently passed over: scalp_15m and scalp_5m stamp no exit_reason at all, so they remain UNDETERMINED and were deliberately NOT marked — labelling a round I cannot measure would be the same error class this row is about.

PARTS (a) and (b) landed in PR #9150 (driver takes --tp-cap-pct, live parity is the DEFAULT; four can-fail-verified tests; round_report.json now stamps _round_meta so future rounds are self-describing). REMAINING: only part (d) — the OPERATOR's decision on whether any exit_head_ml cell graded off these rounds needs re-running, including the three shipped donchian-1h cells.
items.resolution_criteria:
Observable: (a) m20_exit_head_round.py accepts a --tp-cap-pct and threads it into base_args, with the live-parity value as the DEFAULT (matching m20-exit-lever-sweep.yml, whose header argues at length for exactly that) rather than an opt-in a caller can forget; (b) a planted positive control demonstrates it -- a round run at the default must emit trades whose exit_reason distribution CONTAINS take-profit exits, verified by running one, since a quiet pass proves nothing and the arg-string method is already known void; (c) the 11 confirmed no-TP round directories are annotated on disk (a marker file naming the geometry), because artifacts outlive docs and are read directly -- the same requirement as BL-20260814-FLIP-VERDICT-PASS-IS-86PCT-DEGENERATE; (d) a decision is RECORDED on whether any exit_head_ml cell graded off those rounds needs re-running, including the three shipped donchian-1h cells. NOT resolution: adding a caveat to a doc and leaving the driver unable to pass the flag.

PROGRESS 2026-08-14 (a)(b)(c) DONE, ONLY (d) REMAINS AND IT IS THE OPERATOR'S. (a)(b) shipped in PR #9150: --tp-cap-pct with live parity as the DEFAULT + _round_meta stamped into round_report.json, four can-fail-verified tests. (c) all 11 affected round dirs annotated on disk from full populations (n=100..1992, zero take-profit exits in all 11); scalp_15m/scalp_5m stamp no exit_reason and were deliberately left UNMARKED as undetermined. (b)'s PLANTED POSITIVE CONTROL IS NOW SATISFIED BY MEASUREMENT, not by the arg string (that method is void): the first round run at the DEFAULT (runtime_logs/m20_exit_head/prop_1h, relays #9156/#9157/#9158) emitted 95 take-profit exits across its two legs -- trend_donchian_eth_prop 50/984 (5.1%) and trend_donchian_sol_prop 45/310 (14.5%) -- where the eleven pre-fix rounds contain ZERO. The round also self-reports _round_meta.tp_geometry = live_parity. STILL OPEN, (d): whether any exit_head_ml cell graded off the 11 no-TP rounds needs re-running, INCLUDING THE THREE SHIPPED DONCHIAN-1H CELLS. That is Tier-3 and unchanged. NEW EVIDENCE BEARING ON IT: the live-parity round returned the FIRST NON-SCALP E1 CANDIDATE (trend_donchian_eth_prop, auc 0.6138 on n_oos 902 -- against ict_scalp_sol_5m's 0.6149 on 800). That does NOT overturn the scalp-scoping read, because every non-scalp honest_negative that formed it was measured on a no-TP book and is not comparable; what it shows is that the read rests on geometry-conditioned evidence, which raises rather than settles the value of (d).

The row's own progress note records (c) as done (11 round dirs annotated). (d) — the recorded decision on whether any exit_head_ml cell graded off the no-TP rounds needs re-running, incl. the three shipped donchian-1h cells — is not recorded anywhere I can find. — Proposed: the operator records a disposition for the exit_head_ml cells whose evidence predates the cap — either 're-run at live parity before any further use' or 'stand with the geometry caveat', written into those cells. It composes with the shipped/hold question in BL-20260813-SHIPPED-DONCHIAN-1H-HEAD-RESTS-ON-BESTARM.

THE PRODUCER HALF IS FIXED IN CODE; THE CORPUS HALF IS NOT. Verified 2026-08-23 by reading m20_exit_head_round.py, not by trusting this row: `--tp-cap-pct` EXISTS with default 0.099 (arg at :183, whose own docstring records the previous absence), it is passed by KEYWORD into base_args at :410, and :811 warns explicitly when it is <= 0. So the title's 'STRUCTURALLY cannot produce a live-parity book' is FALSE of the code today and must not be re-quoted.

WHAT SURVIVES, and it is why this stays open: the 11 rounds already ON DISK were produced before the fix and still contain zero take-profit exits — including the round behind the SHIPPED donchian-1h head. The remedy is a RE-MEASURE, not another code change. A session reading only the title would re-fix working code; a session reading only the fix would trust a corpus built without it.

Re-validated: M20 exit-program measurement/tooling correctness. Propose-only, no live-order impact. Blocked on trainer capacity (91.7% disk) for anything needing a re-sweep. Pairs with BL-20260814-THREE-SIBLING-SWEEPS-STILL-BUILD-NO-TAKE-PROFIT-BOOKS-AND-STAMP-NOTHING and BL-20260816-M21-ENTRY-SWEEPS-STILL-CALL-BASE-ARGS-POSITIONALLY — the SAME positional-base_args defect in at least three drivers.

items.title: m20_coverage_rollup graded TP-geometry staleness by a single DATE, so three SHIPPED real-money exit_head_ml cells sat outside the --stale-decisions list they belong in -- a date cannot distinguish 're-measured' from 're-read an old round'
items.source:
Found while re-running the roll-up after fixing the exit-head round driver (BL-20260814-EXIT-HEAD-ROUNDS-CANNOT-MODEL-LIVE-TP), not by auditing the roll-up.

TWO DISTINCT DEFECTS, one symptom.

(1) ONE CUTOVER FOR TWO HARNESSES. GEOMETRY_CUTOVER = 2026-08-10 is when the LEVER-SWEEP harness learned to place the live capped TP. `exit_head_ml` does not ride that harness -- it rides m20_exit_head_round.py, whose own fix landed 2026-08-14. Every exit_head_ml cell was therefore graded against a bar four days too early. Correcting it moved the stale count 174 -> 186 of 286 closed cells.

(2) THE DATE IS ONLY A PROXY, AND IT FAILED OUTRIGHT. The three shipped trend_donchian* 1h exit_head_ml cells carry a GENUINE `RE-SWEPT 2026-08-14` ref -- a real measurement, on that date -- which re-read the EXISTING round dirs rather than building new ones. Every round on disk predates the driver fix, so those cells are fresh by date and stale by geometry simultaneously. No choice of cutover date separates them: the property that matters is not WHEN a cell was measured but WHETHER the round behind it placed the live capped TP.

WHY IT MATTERS: `--stale-decisions` is the surface that says which CLOSED, non-negative cells rest on unreproduced evidence, and its own output calls a stale SHIPPED cell the expensive kind (it changes exit behaviour on a real-money leg now). It listed five and read as the complete set; three real-money shipped cells were missing from it. An unasserted-denominator read (diagnostic-provenance sub-class C): the list looked clean because the only test was a date, and the date was the wrong harness's.

NOTE the base rate that makes this non-theoretical: of stale decisions re-swept so far, 1 of 1 did NOT reproduce (trend_donchian trail_decay, now shipped_gate_failed).
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED in the same session (PR on claude/m20-exit-coverage-matrix-8d3he7). Fix has two halves, both can-fail verified by reverting each independently: (a) LEVER_GEOMETRY_CUTOVER + cutover_for() give exit_head_ml its own 2026-08-14 bar, with an unlisted lever falling back to the default; (b) a per-cell `tp_geometry` field OVERRIDES the date in BOTH directions -- `no_take_profit` is stale whatever the date says, `live_parity` is not stale whatever the date says, and an absent field falls back to the date while counting into `geometry_undeclared` so 'we did not look' stays visible. The three shipped donchian-1h cells are stamped `no_take_profit` (a declared MEASUREMENT: all eleven rounds read end-to-end, full populations n=100..1992, zero take-profit exits, each carrying its own GEOMETRY-NO-TAKE-PROFIT.txt on disk -- not a presence-only marker). Verified: --stale-decisions now lists 8, shipped 4 -> 7, and a test asserts the three cells against the REAL matrix so a regression fails CI rather than quietly under-reporting. WHAT IS NOT RESOLVED HERE: the DISPOSITION of those three cells (re-run under live parity, or accept) is part (d) of BL-20260814-EXIT-HEAD-ROUNDS-CANNOT-MODEL-LIVE-TP and is Tier-3, queued for the operator -- it is deliberately NOT double-counted as this row's remit.

items.title: m20_fleet_exit_sweep's THIN OOS banner fires at 20 trades but the gradeability floor is 25, so a leg with 20-24 OOS trades prints a full delta table under NO warning while nothing in it was graded
items.source:
Found by reading the output of run 31771809102 (the 2026-08-14 live-parity re-sweep of the stale decisions), not by auditing the harness.

TWO DIFFERENT NUMBERS, NEITHER WRONG ON ITS OWN. `_THIN_OOS_TRADES = 20` (m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:898) drives the header's "⚠️ THIN OOS (<20 trades — a verdict here is not comparable to one on a full window)" banner; `MIN_OOS_TRADES = 25` (line 402, operator decision 2026-08-11) is the floor below which every cell returns `insufficient_base`. The band between them is a leg that is ENTIRELY ungradeable and gets NO banner.

MEASURED, all four legs of that run: htf_pullback_trend_2h OOS 24, mhg_pullback_1d OOS 24, tlt_pullback_1h OOS 22 -- all three under the floor, all three unflagged, each printing a four-row Path-A/capital-efficiency delta table. Only mes_trend_long_1d (OOS 4) tripped the banner. So 3 of 4 legs in that run landed exactly in the blind band.

STATED PRECISELY, THIS IS LEGIBILITY AND NOT FALSEHOOD -- and the distinction is the reason the severity is low rather than high. The per-cell `PathA` column does read `insufficient_base` on every row, and the harness even records `would_have_been` so the floor's effect is auditable. Nothing printed is untrue. But the header is where a reader calibrates before reading the table, and a reader who trusts it sees four rows of signed deltas with no caveat over a leg where nothing was graded.

This is the consumer half of the unasserted-denominator family (diagnostic-provenance sub-class C): the numbers are real, the label above them does not say they decided nothing.
items.resolution_criteria: Observable: the sweep SUMMARY header carries a warning whenever the leg's base OOS n is below MIN_OOS_TRADES, not below a separate constant -- e.g. by deriving the banner threshold FROM the floor rather than declaring it independently, so the two cannot drift apart again. Two acceptable outcomes: (a) the banner fires at the floor and the 20-24 band is flagged; or (b) the two thresholds are deliberately kept distinct AND the header states the floor alongside the OOS n, so a reader can see the gap without knowing the constant. NOT resolution: raising _THIN_OOS_TRADES to 25 by hand and leaving two independent literals free to diverge on the next floor change.
evidence: scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:898 -- _THIN_OOS_TRADES = 20
scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:402 -- MIN_OOS_TRADES = 25 (operator decision 2026-08-11)
scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:1754 -- verdict insufficient_base when base OOS n < floor
GH Actions run 31771809102 -- 4 legs, OOS n 24/24/22/4; only the n=4 leg carried the banner; results posted as comments on PR #9149

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py still declares MIN_OOS_TRADES = 25 at line 548 and `_THIN_OOS_TRADES = 20` independently at line 1230, and the header at :2380-2386 fires the THIN OOS banner on `n_oos < _THIN_OOS_TRADES` only. The 20-24 blind band is unchanged. — Low severity (legibility, not falsehood — the per-cell PathA column still reads insufficient_base). Ends when the banner threshold is derived from the floor, or the header prints the floor beside the OOS n.
Re-validated: banner at 20, floor at 25 — a 20-24 trade leg prints no warning and is ungradeable. One-line fix.

items.title: Seven exit_ladder coverage cells cited 'memo §7.2' for the partial-TP banking verdict, which lives in §6.2 -- §7.2 is the trail4 walk-forward and says nothing about banking
items.source:
Found while checking whether the fleet banking verdict transfers to the two PENDING prop exit_ladder cells -- i.e. by following the citation, which is the one activity that surfaces a wrong pointer.

The claim is TRUE and the pointer was wrong. `docs/research/M20-exit-refinement-2026-07-12.md` §6.2 is titled "Trailing-stop geometry + exit-ladder banking" and states "partial-TP banking reduced net_R in every one of the 20 banking cells". §7.2 is "Trail4 walk-forward (the requested decision input)" and contains nothing about banking; §7.3 is the giveback-stop grid. No other memo in the repo has a §7.2, so the citation could not have resolved elsewhere.

WHY IT MATTERS ENOUGH TO FIX: a reader verifying an honest_negative grade follows the pointer, lands on a section about a different lever, and either re-derives the verdict from scratch or -- worse -- reads §7.2's PASS language for trail4 and mis-attributes it. Five of the seven are honest_negative grades on live legs; two are blocked cells whose refs cite it while describing the other rows.

A SEPARATE TRACEABILITY WEAKNESS NOTICED IN PASSING, NOT FIXED HERE: of the 45 honest_negative exit_ladder cells, only 5 carried any section citation at all and 34 carry none -- so most rest on the banking verdict with no pointer to it. That is a wider gap than this row's remit and is left stated rather than silently folded in.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED in the same session: all 7 refs now cite §6.2, each carrying an inline note naming the section title and quoting the verdict sentence so the correction is checkable from the cell itself rather than by trusting this row. The corrective note deliberately carries NO date -- five of the seven are honest_negative cells that the vintage counter buckets, and a date would have flipped them pre_cutover -> post_cutover and marked pre-cutover evidence as refreshed (the date-proxy hazard fixed the same day in BL-20260814-COVERAGE-STALENESS-GRADED-BY-DATE-NOT-GEOMETRY). Verified: `--validate` OK, and no cell still contains the string 'memo §7.2'. NOT resolved here: the 34 uncited honest_negative exit_ladder cells noted above.
