items.title: mgc_pullback_1d and mhg_pullback_1d exit_head_ml cells are blocked:data_missing on native IBKR history that NO scheduled job produces -- the pull-ibkr-history action was added 2026-07-07 expressly to unblock them and appears never to have been run for either symbol
items.source:
Found by asking what would actually unblock the 22 blocked M20 cells, then following the data dependency rather than accepting the status label.

THREE exit_head_ml cells read `blocked:data_missing` with the ref 'needs native IBKR history for E0 (proxy OK for levers, not for head training)': mes_trend_long_1d, mgc_pullback_1d, mhg_pullback_1d. `data_missing` reads as 'the data will arrive'. For two of the three, nothing is bringing it.

THE PRODUCER IS MES-ONLY. The only IBKR deep-history puller in the repo is scripts/ops/pull_mes_ibkr_history.sh. It IS symbol-parameterised (MES_SYMBOL, default MES), but the scheduled unit deploy/ict-mes-ibkr-pull.service invokes it with NO override, so the daily 23:30 UTC timer only ever pulls MES. MGC and MHG accrue nothing on a schedule.

THE ON-DEMAND PATH EXISTS AND WAS BUILT FOR EXACTLY THESE CELLS. `pull-ibkr-history` (Tier-2, docs/claude/system-actions.md:89) is the symbol-parameterised sibling, allowlisted to MES/MGC/MHG, and its own entry says it was 'Added 2026-07-07 to backtest the metals sleeve (mgc_trend_1h / mgc_pullback_1d / mhg_pullback_1d) on native IBKR history before any shadow->live.' Those cells are still blocked five weeks later.

MEASURED, WITH ITS DENOMINATOR STATED. runtime_logs/ibkr_mes_pull.jsonl via diag #9162/#9163: in the window the relay returned (2026-07-30 -> 2026-08-05, 337 stamped lines, 44 pull_start runs) EVERY run is symbol=MES -- 44/44, zero MGC, zero MHG. I could NOT see 2026-07-07 -> 07-30 (the relay truncates a 400-line request of a 132,659-byte log), so an unseen run in that window is not excluded by the log alone; what makes it unlikely is that both cells still read 'needs native IBKR history'.

A FALSE ALARM I ALMOST FILED, recorded because the next reader will hit the same trap: the truncated 400-line payload's newest visible stamp was 2026-08-05, nine days stale on a DAILY timer, which reads exactly like a recurrence of BL-20260626-MES-BASE-STALE. It is not. A small complete read (lines=12) shows the pull ran 2026-08-13T23:33 -> 23:45 with both timeframes ok (47,190 and 15,751 rows). The truncation had handed me the OLDER part of the 400, not the newest. A large truncated read is worse than a small complete one when the question is 'what happened most recently'.
items.resolution_criteria: Observable: `pull-ibkr-history` has been dispatched for MGC and for MHG and the pull log shows a `pull_end` with `any_ok:1` for each symbol, OR the two cells are re-stated with a status that does not imply pending arrival. TIMING IS PART OF THE FIX, not incidental: the pull shares the LIVE trading gateway on clientId 450 and takes ~27 min, so it must not be launched inside IBKR's own ~03:45-05:45 UTC reset window nor across the 06:05 UTC gateway reset -- both would burn pacing budget on a session being restarted. Run the two SEQUENTIALLY (the wrapper takes a single-instance lock, so a concurrent second invocation exits cleanly and would look like a silent no-op). Then the exit_head_ml cells for mgc_pullback_1d / mhg_pullback_1d become runnable via an E1 round at live parity, the same path that closed the two prop cells on 2026-08-14. NOT resolution: re-labelling the cells without either pulling the data or establishing that IBKR cannot serve it.
evidence: docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json -- 3 exit_head_ml cells blocked:data_missing, ref 'needs native IBKR history for E0'
deploy/ict-mes-ibkr-pull.service -- ExecStart passes no MES_SYMBOL, so the daily timer is MES-only
scripts/ops/pull_mes_ibkr_history.sh:105 -- MES_SYMBOL="${MES_SYMBOL:-MES}" (parameterised but defaulted)
docs/claude/system-actions.md:89 -- pull-ibkr-history, Tier 2, allowlisted MES/MGC/MHG, 'Added 2026-07-07 to backtest the metals sleeve'
diag #9162 -- 44/44 pull_start runs are MES over 2026-07-30..08-05; window does not cover 07-07..07-30
diag #9163 -- lines=12 complete read: last run 2026-08-13T23:33->23:45, both timeframes ok; the daily pull is HEALTHY

updates.note:
CORRECTION -- THIS ROW'S ID IS WRONG AND SO WAS ITS CONCLUSION. MGC and MHG WERE pulled, on 2026-07-07, the same day `pull-ibkr-history` was added. Direct evidence on the trainer (relay #9183): data/ibkr_datasets/market_raw/MGC/1d/v003 = 940 rows 2022-09-30..2026-07-06, mtime 2026-07-07 13:33:20, and .../MHG/1d/v003 = 1043 rows 2022-05-03..2026-07-06, mtime 2026-07-07 14:18:02.

Why I got it wrong: I measured `pull_start` rows over the window the relay returned (07-30..08-05, 44/44 MES) and stated that denominator honestly -- but then drew an UNBOUNDED conclusion ('nothing is bringing it', 'never run for either') from a BOUNDED observation. The 2026-07-07 pulls predate the window entirely. A negative needs a denominator, and mine was correct; the sentence I wrote around it was not.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE: the scheduled daily timer IS MES-only (it invokes the wrapper with no symbol override), so there is no RECURRING MGC/MHG pull. That is the real, surviving finding.

WHAT IS NOW SUPERSEDED: the premise that these cells were blocked on ABSENT data. They were not. Deep native 1d history is present on the trainer and is refreshed daily -- datasets-out/market_raw/{MGC,MHG,MES}/1d/v002 at 2,919 / 2,920 / 2,921 rows spanning 2015-01-02..2026-08-13, mtimes 2026-08-14 05:30-05:34, i.e. hours before my pulls. The real blockers were (a) BL-20260814-PROXY-MAP-SHADOWS-NATIVE-DATA and (b) the conversion gap in the new row below.

Also superseded: my 07:28Z ping said the pulls would make both cells runnable. They would not have.

Re-validated and it COMPOUNDS a live condition: MGC/MHG are among the 5 IB legs logging transient_market_data_unavailable (mgc_trend_1h 154, mgc_pullback_1d 143, mhg_pullback_1d 129 WARN rows over 9 days). Native history is never pulled AND the live feed is intermittent.

items.title: roadmap.py::_parse_last_updated returns the ENTIRE prior-entry chain as the 'summary', so /api/bot/roadmap's lastUpdated summary is ~1000-1400 chars of history rather than the current entry
items.source:
Noticed while updating ROADMAP.md's header for the M20 coverage move, and CHECKED against the pre-edit file rather than assumed -- the run-on is PRE-EXISTING, not introduced by that edit.

MEASURED both ways with the real parser: BEFORE the edit `_parse_last_updated` returned date=2026-08-13 with a summary of 998 characters; AFTER, date=2026-08-14 with 1374. The DATE is correct in both cases; it is only the summary that runs on. The header line is a chain of the form `**Last Updated:** <date> (**<summary>**) - prior: <date> (**<summary>**) - prior: ...`, and the terminator does not stop at the first entry, so every historical entry is concatenated into the field.

WHY IT IS ONLY LOW: nothing is wrong or fabricated -- the text returned is real and the date is right. The cost is legibility on the surface that consumes it: `/api/bot/roadmap`'s `lastUpdated` feeds the dashboard + Android Roadmap views, where a 'summary' is presumably meant to be a line, not the full changelog. It also grows monotonically as entries accumulate, so it degrades over time rather than staying constant.

I did not fix it in the same change deliberately: the fix is a parser-regex change on a live read surface two front-ends consume, and bundling it into a ROADMAP content edit would have mixed a doc update with a behaviour change to an endpoint.
items.resolution_criteria: Observable: `_parse_last_updated` returns ONLY the first entry's summary -- i.e. its length stops growing as `- prior:` entries accumulate. A regression test that appends a second synthetic `- prior:` entry and asserts the returned summary is unchanged would pin it, since the defect is precisely that the field grows with history. Either fix is acceptable: terminate the summary at the first `) - prior:` boundary, or return a structured list of entries and let the consumer pick the first. NOT resolution: truncating the string to N characters, which would still be the whole chain, just clipped.
evidence: src/web/api/routers/roadmap.py::_parse_last_updated
measured 2026-08-14: summary_len 998 (pre-edit HEAD:ROADMAP.md) and 1374 (post-edit), date correct in both
ROADMAP.md:9 -- the '- prior:' chain the parser runs through

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Reproduced with the parser's own regexes against the current ROADMAP.md: the `**Last Updated:**` raw line is 2339 chars and `re.search(r'\(\*\*(.+?)\*\*\)')` — the non-greedy match src/web/api/routers/roadmap.py:242 uses — returns 1839 chars, whose tail still contains '— prior: 2026-08-10 (**…**) — prior: 2026-07-28 (…'. The non-greedy `.+?` cannot stop at the first entry because the entry text itself contains `**bold**` runs, so the first literal `**)` lands far down the chain. — Low severity, read-path legibility on /api/bot/roadmap's lastUpdatedHeadline (both front-ends render it).
Re-validated: tooling/guard correctness. Cheap to fix, unblocked, still undone.

items.title: m20_fleet_exit_sweep.resolve_data applied PROXY_DATA unconditionally, so m20_exit_head_round -- which REFUSES proxied data -- could never see native IBKR history, making the three mes/mgc/mhg exit_head_ml cells unreachable no matter how much data was pulled
items.source:
Found while checking whether the MGC/MHG IBKR history pull I ran tonight (per BL-20260814-MGC-MHG-IBKR-HISTORY-NEVER-PULLED) could actually close the cells it was run for. It could not, and the reason was NOT the data.

THE CHAIN, read from source rather than inferred:
1. docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json grades mes_trend_long_1d / mgc_pullback_1d / mhg_pullback_1d `exit_head_ml` as `blocked:data_missing`, noted 'needs native IBKR history for E0 (proxy OK for levers, not for head training)'.
2. scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py:154 enforces exactly that -- `if proxy: SKIP ... native history required for head training`.
3. scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:147 opened with `sym = PROXY_DATA.get(symbol, symbol)`, applying the proxy UNCONDITIONALLY. PROXY_DATA maps MGC->GC_F, MHG->HG_F, MES->ES_F, XAUUSD->GC_F.
4. So resolve_data('MGC','1d',...) looked for GC_F_1d.csv and NEVER for MGC_1d.csv -- including the glob fallback, whose prefixes were built from the proxied spelling ({'gc_f'}).

Therefore proxy was True for those symbols on every call, the head round skipped them every time, and the cells could not close. The Tier-2 `pull-ibkr-history` action was added 2026-07-07 for exactly these cells and was inert against this resolver -- a successful pull would have landed data the round could not reach.

The function's own docstring said the map is 'for futures without their own file', a condition the code never checked. Field beats comment, and here the field was the wrong one.
items.resolution_criteria:
RESOLVED in this PR. resolve_data gained a `prefer_native: bool = False` parameter; m20_exit_head_round passes prefer_native=True. Verified by 7 tests in tests/test_exit_head_per_leg.py with a can-fail control (removing the prefer_native branch fails test_prefer_native_reaches_a_native_file_the_default_cannot_see with `assert True is False`, and ONLY that test -- the fallback and no-proxy cases correctly still pass because proxy-first gives the same answer there).

THE DEFAULT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT PROXY-FIRST, and that is the load-bearing half. Native-first unconditionally would have been a REGRESSION for the lever sweeps: GC_F is the deep COMEX series reaching the full 2021..2026 fold structure, while native IBKR intraday history is ~1y, so silently preferring a shallow native file would collapse a 6-fold walk-forward to ~1 fold and quietly invalidate recorded verdicts. Depth (levers) and fidelity (head training) are genuinely different needs, so it is a caller decision. For the same reason the default did NOT gain a native fallback either -- a missing proxy file must keep reading `data_missing` rather than resolving shallow native data into a 1-fold run.

FOLLOW-UP, NOT CLOSED BY THIS: the three cells are now REACHABLE but not yet graded, and reaching them is not the same as clearing them. Two conditions remain unverified -- (a) the native shard must reach the TRAINER (the pull writes market_raw on the LIVE VM; sync_trainer_data.sh carries it on the trainer's ~00:50 UTC daily cycle, then scripts/research/market_raw_to_csv.py must convert it to data/<SYM>_<tf>.csv), and (b) the pull I ran was 5m/15m over a 365-day window (the script's default, MES_HIST_START='365 days ago'), which is roughly one year -- against a 6-fold 2021..2026 structure and MIN_OOS_TRADES=25. A 1d deep pull (the pull-mes-ibkr-history-daily precedent uses MES_HIST_START=2019-05-06 with MES_MAX_CONTRACTS=28) is the right-shaped attempt for these 1d legs, since IBKR daily-bar retention is far deeper than intraday. Whether that clears the OOS floor is a MEASUREMENT still to take, not a prediction.

updates.note:
CORRECTION to this row's own rationale. It argued the default must stay proxy-first because 'the proxy is the deep series ... native IBKR history is ~1y'. That is TRUE of native IBKR *intraday* shards but FALSE at the 1d frame -- the frame all three blocked cells use. Measured (relay #9183): native MGC 1d = 2,919 rows 2015-01-02..2026-08-13 vs proxy GC_F_1d.csv = 2,512 data rows 2016-07-12..2026-07-10. The native series is deeper AND a month fresher. MHG/MES the same shape.

The DECISION stands, the REASON changes: the default stays proxy-first so that flipping the basis a recorded verdict was measured against is its own measured decision rather than a side effect of a reachability fix. Code docstring, inline comment, and the test name/docstrings corrected in the same PR rather than left to read as justified by a false premise.

TWO CORRECTIONS, one to this row's rationale (again) and one to its claimed consequence.

1. THE DEPTH CLAIM: my 07:55 update said 'at the 1d frame the native series is DEEPER and fresher than its proxy'. FALSE — I measured that on data/MGC_1d.csv, a file I had created MYSELF from yfinance GC=F, so I was comparing the proxy against itself. Genuine native (IBKR contract) is 940 rows vs the proxy's 2,512. The proxy is ~2.7x deeper and THE ROW'S ORIGINAL RATIONALE WAS CORRECT. I corrected a true statement into a false one by measuring a file whose name asserted a provenance its content lacked — diagnostic-provenance sub-class B (implicit input selection) committed against my own artifact. Code docstring, inline comment, one test name and two test docstrings re-corrected.

2. THE CONSEQUENCE: this row says the fix means the three exit_head_ml cells 'could never close no matter how much data was pulled'. The DEFECT is real and the fix stands — a consumer that refuses proxies genuinely could not see native data. But the fix does NOT unblock those cells, and the binding constraint is not data at all: `build_trainer_datasets.sh:375` records that mes_trend_long_1d fires ~2.6x/yr — 26 trades over a 10-YEAR config-exact backtest — against MIN_OOS_TRADES=25 for the OOS half ALONE. No quantity of history reaches that. These are volume-blocked, the same 'wait, not to-do' shape as the other 10 insufficient_lifetime_trades cells, and their matrix note ('needs native IBKR history for E0') describes a prerequisite rather than the binding gate.

items.title: scripts/research/market_raw_to_csv.py has no scheduled or committed caller, so deep native 1d market_raw shards for MGC/MHG/MES have never become the data/<SYM>_1d.csv the sweeps read -- the second half of why three exit_head_ml cells are blocked
items.source:
Measured on the trainer 2026-08-14 (relay #9182, #9183) while checking whether tonight's IBKR pulls could close the cells they were run for.

THE DATA IS ALREADY THERE, AND IT IS DEEP:
  datasets-out/market_raw/MGC/1d/v002  2,919 rows  2015-01-02 -> 2026-08-13  (mtime 2026-08-14 05:34)
  datasets-out/market_raw/MHG/1d/v002  2,920 rows  2015-01-02 -> 2026-08-13  (mtime 2026-08-14 05:34)
  datasets-out/market_raw/MES/1d/v002  2,921 rows  2015-01-02 -> 2026-08-13  (mtime 2026-08-14 05:30)
  datasets-out/market_raw/MES/1d/v001  6,484 rows  2000-09-18 -> 2026-05-22  (deeper but stale since May)

BUT data/ contains ONLY the proxies -- GC_F_1d.csv (2,513 lines, 2016-07-12..2026-07-10), HG_F_1d.csv (2,514), ES_F_1d.csv (2,515), GC_F_1h.csv. The probe printed '(NO native MGC/MHG/MES csv in data/)'.

So the native 1d series is DEEPER (2,919 vs 2,512 data rows) and a MONTH FRESHER than the proxy the sweeps actually read -- and no code path converts it. A repo-wide grep for `market_raw_to_csv` returns its own usage string, two sprint-log mentions and one capability-index row: NO scheduled unit, NO workflow, NO script calls it. It is a hand-run tool, and for these three symbols it was never hand-run.

This is the second half of the blocker. BL-20260814-PROXY-MAP-SHADOWS-NATIVE-DATA meant the resolver could not SEE native data; this means there was no native CSV to see. Either alone keeps the cells shut, which is why five weeks of 'still blocked' survived a Tier-2 tool built to fix it.
items.resolution_criteria:
Two observable conditions, in order. (1) `data/MGC_1d.csv`, `data/MHG_1d.csv` and `data/MES_1d.csv` exist on the trainer with row counts matching their shards (~2,919 / ~2,920 / ~2,921), produced by `market_raw_to_csv.py <SYM> datasets-out data/<SYM>_1d.csv 1d` -- the script prints 'wrote N rows', so the count is measured, not assumed. (2) A durable caller exists so this cannot silently rot again: either the trainer's daily cycle converts every market_raw shard that a configured leg's symbol needs, or a guard fails when a strategy symbol has a market_raw shard but no corresponding data/ CSV. Until (2) lands, (1) is a one-off that the next fresh trainer loses.

NOTE for whoever does (1): market_raw_to_csv takes `cands[-1]`, the highest-sorted version dir, so MES/1d resolves v002 (2,921 rows from 2015) and NOT the deeper-but-stale v001 (6,484 rows from 2000, last updated 2026-05-22). If the longer MES history is wanted that is an explicit choice to make, not a default to inherit.

updates.note:
SUPERSEDED — MY PREMISE WAS WRONG, AND WRONG IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION. I claimed 'the deep native 1d data is ALREADY there' on the strength of datasets-out/market_raw/{MGC,MHG,MES}/1d/v002 at 2,919/2,920/2,921 rows. That data is NOT native. `build_trainer_datasets.sh:943-944` builds it as `build_equity_daily MGC "GC=F"` / `MHG "HG=F"` -- yfinance on the FULL-SIZE contract, which is the same series the GC_F/HG_F proxies already are.

MEASURED, not inferred (relay #9191): data/MGC_1d.csv vs data/GC_F_1d.csv = 2,512 overlapping dates, 2,511 IDENTICAL closes (100.0%), the single difference being the proxy's stale final bar (2026-07-10, ratio 0.99767). MHG 2,512/2,513 identical. MES 2,514/2,514 identical, zero differing. 407 native-only dates, 0 proxy-only -- i.e. the same series with a longer head and tail.

SO THE CONVERSION I RAN PRODUCED A PROVENANCE LIE: a file whose NAME asserts native provenance and whose CONTENT is the proxy. With the prefer_native fix in the same PR, resolve_data would have returned proxy=False, m20_exit_head_round's 'native history required for head training' refusal would have PASSED, and three exit_head_ml cells would have been graded native-trained on the exact series that check exists to exclude. I removed all three files the same hour (relay #9192, verified absent; the GC_F/HG_F/ES_F proxies confirmed intact).

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: genuine native = the IBKR CONTRACT shards under data/ibkr_datasets/market_raw/ -- MGC 940 rows (2022-09-30..2026-07-06), MHG 1,043, MES 677. So the PROXY IS ~2.7x DEEPER, and the original rationale I 'corrected' an hour earlier was right all along.

WHAT SURVIVES AS A REAL ITEM: market_raw_to_csv.py genuinely has no caller. But it is NOT the blocker I filed it as, and building a durable caller over datasets-out would MASS-PRODUCE this same mislabelling for every futures symbol. Any future caller must convert from the IBKR root, or name the output for the series it actually contains. Re-filed at that framing as BL-20260814-EQUITY-DAILY-LABELS-PROXY-DATA-AS-THE-NATIVE-SYMBOL.
Re-validated: written-and-never-run (class A). Directly blocks BL-20260814-MGC-MHG-IBKR-HISTORY-NEVER-PULLED. Also on the standing unwired-artifacts list I ran this review.

items.title: build_trainer_datasets.sh writes yfinance FULL-SIZE-contract bars into market_raw/<MICRO_SYMBOL>/, so market_raw/MGC/1d is GC=F wearing the MGC name -- any consumer that treats the shard name as provenance is misled
items.source:
`scripts/ops/build_trainer_datasets.sh:943-944` runs `build_equity_daily MGC "GC=F"` and `build_equity_daily MHG "HG=F"`, writing to `market_raw/MGC/1d/` and `market_raw/MHG/1d/`. The SHARD IS KEYED BY THE MICRO SYMBOL; the CONTENT is the full-size continuous contract from yfinance.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 (relay #9191), converting both to CSV and comparing: MGC vs GC_F 2,512 overlapping dates with 2,511 IDENTICAL closes (100.0%); MHG vs HG_F 2,512/2,513; MES vs ES_F 2,514/2,514 with ZERO differences. They are the same series.

For the LEVER sweeps this is harmless and arguably intended -- a proxy is explicitly sanctioned there, and `PROXY_DATA` already maps MGC->GC_F, so both paths reach the same bars. The hazard is any consumer that reads the SYMBOL DIRECTORY as evidence of provenance. `m20_exit_head_round` refuses proxied data ('native history required for head training'); combined with the new `prefer_native` resolution it would have accepted `data/MGC_1d.csv` built from this shard, reported `proxy=False`, and trained on the refused series. I did exactly that this session and reverted it within the hour (relay #9192).

This is the number-provenance rule one level out: not 'is this value measured or manufactured' but 'does this shard's KEY describe its CONTENT'.
items.resolution_criteria:
Any ONE of these, verifiable by reading the shard: (a) `build_equity_daily` records the fetched ticker INTO the shard -- a `ticker`/`source_symbol` field in the manifest or each row -- so a consumer can ask what it actually holds instead of inferring from the path, and `market_raw_to_csv.py` refuses (or renames) when the shard's recorded ticker does not match the symbol requested; or (b) the yfinance full-size series is written under its OWN key (`market_raw/GC_F/1d`) with `market_raw/MGC/1d` reserved for genuine MGC bars; or (c) a guard asserts that no `market_raw/<SYM>` shard is byte-identical to a declared `PROXY_DATA[<SYM>]` series without being labelled as that proxy.

NOT resolved by adding a market_raw->CSV caller: over `datasets-out` that would mass-produce this mislabelling for every futures symbol at once. Explicitly supersedes BL-20260814-MARKET-RAW-TO-CSV-HAS-NO-CALLER, which mistook this shard for native data.

updates.note:
PARTIAL: criterion (c) SHIPPED. `market_raw_to_csv.py` now refuses to write a native-named CSV that IS the proxy. Before writing it loads `data/<PROXY><suffix>.csv`, compares overlapping-date closes at 1e-6, and exits 2 with the measurement when >= 95% are identical. `--allow-proxy-alias` overrides for deliberately materialising a proxy under its own name.

WHY A CONSUMER-SIDE CHECK FIRST: it needs no producer change and no new shard field, so it protects every shard ALREADY on disk. Criteria (a) (record the fetched ticker IN the shard) and (b) (write GC=F under its own key) remain the better long answers and stay OPEN -- they belong in `build_trainer_datasets.sh`, which feeds the trainer's nightly ML builds, and that is not a change to make unattended at 08:40 on a night whose lesson was 'measure before you act'.

THRESHOLD RATIONALE, since 0.95 looks arbitrary: the discriminator is BIMODAL, not a similarity score. At 1e-6 two different instruments share ~0% exactly-identical closes (the low digits differ on essentially every bar) while two copies of one series share ~100%; nothing real lands between, so any cut in 0.5..0.99 picks the same answer on real data. 0.95 rather than 0.99 because the shortfall does not scale with n -- the proxy's final bar is often a stale print (measured MGC: 2,511 of 2,512), and on a SHORT overlap that one bar is 5%, which a 0.99 cut would wave through. My first draft used 0.99 and a 20-bar test caught it.

FAIL-OPEN BY CONSTRUCTION, verified by test: no declared proxy, no proxy CSV on disk, no overlapping dates, or a genuine difference all proceed normally. The check can block only on positive evidence the two series are the SAME. 9 tests incl. a can-fail control -- disabling the check fails exactly the two refusal tests and leaves the seven fail-open/override tests passing.

[sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The consumer-side half is shipped: scripts/research/market_raw_to_csv.py:7-8,51,91,158-176 refuses to write a native-named CSV when the shard's closes match the declared proxy (`_PROXY_OF = {MGC: GC_F, XAUUSD: GC_F, MES: ES_F, MHG: HG_F}`), with `--allow-proxy-alias` as the deliberate override. Neither producer-side criterion is met: scripts/ops/build_trainer_datasets.sh's `build_equity_daily` still writes the yfinance ticker's bars under the micro symbol with no `ticker`/`source_symbol` recorded in the shard, so a consumer reading the shard directly is still misled. — The remaining half changes the trainer's nightly dataset builds and cannot be verified from this checkout. Ends when the shard records its fetched ticker (a) or the full-size series gets its own key (b).

Re-validated: yfinance FULL-SIZE contract bars written into market_raw/<MICRO_SYMBOL>/ — proxy data wearing the native symbol's label. Diagnostic-provenance sub-class B, and it silently corrupts every MGC/MHG measurement built on it.

items.title: m20_fleet_exit_sweep derives the IS/OOS split to target EXACTLY MIN_OOS_TRADES, so ordinary boundary loss lands under the floor and the cell is refused -- and re-running never helps, because the split is re-derived to the same target every time
items.source:
Found while checking whether the 5 non-exit-head stale live DECISIONS can be re-validated. VERIFIED IN SOURCE, not inferred:

  scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:1270  --split-mode  default='oos-trades'
  scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:1277  --split-target-oos  default=MIN_OOS_TRADES  (=25)
      help: "Defaults to the floor a cell is judged against, so the boundary
             aims at exactly what the verdict requires."

and `resolve_split`'s own docstring already warns why aiming at exactly the floor is fragile: "THE TARGET IS NOT THE ACHIEVED COUNT ... The harness windows CANDLES, not trades, so an OOS run starting at the derived date needs warmup and may produce slightly different trades near the boundary."

So the loop is: derive a split leaving ~25 -> warmup shaves it to 24 -> `_base_oos_n (24) < MIN_OOS_TRADES (25)` -> verdict `insufficient_base`. Re-running CANNOT fix it, because the split is re-derived to target 25 again regardless of how many trades exist.

THE CASE THAT EXPOSES IT. `htf_pullback_trend_2h` / `trail_geometry` is a SHIPPED real-money cell. Its own ref records a re-sweep run TODAY at live parity (m20-exit-lever-sweep run 31771809102) returning `insufficient_base` on EVERY cell because "base OOS n (24) is below MIN_OOS_TRADES=25", and concludes "THIS CELL IS NOT A TO-DO, IT IS A WAIT -- re-running the sweep before this leg accumulates OOS trades returns exactly this again."

The CONCLUSION is right and the REASON is wrong. Measured today (trainer relay #9209, config-exact, tp_cap_pct=0.099): the leg emits **407 lifetime trades and 97 OOS at the corpus-standard 2025-07-01**, span 2021-07-21..2026-07-10. `tlt_pullback_1h` likewise: **527 lifetime, 60 OOS**. Neither is trade-starved; the derivation chose a window containing 24 out of 97 available and then refused it for being one short.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE CELL: 'wait for trades' is a disposition that makes a cell invisible for months. Two SHIPPED real-money cells currently carry it on a premise that is false for them, at a moment when the stale-decision re-sweep base rate is 3-of-4 NOT reproducing (see BL-20260814 sprint items 56-57) -- i.e. exactly when re-validating a shipped lever matters most.

NOT ALL FIVE BLOCKED CELLS ARE THIS SHAPE, and the distinction is the point: `mes_trend_long_1d` (5 OOS) and `mhg_pullback_1d` (10 OOS) ARE genuinely thin -- measured relay #9195 -- so for them the split-targeting is doing exactly the job it was built for. The defect bites the legs that have PLENTY of trades.
items.resolution_criteria:
Falsifiable and cheap, in this order:

(1) ESTABLISH THE MECHANISM ON THE REAL CELL. Re-run `htf_pullback_trend_2h` / `trail_geometry` with `--split-mode date --split 2025-07-01` (or `--split-target-oos 50`) and record `base_trades_oos`. If it comes back ~97 (vs the recorded 24) and the cell produces a real verdict instead of `insufficient_base`, the mechanism is confirmed and the cell was never a 'wait'. If it still returns ~24, the cause is something else and THIS ITEM IS WRONG -- say so and close it; I did NOT verify which split mode run 31771809102 actually used, because the cell ref does not record it (see (3)).

(2) FIX THE DEFAULT so a target cannot land under its own floor -- e.g. target `MIN_OOS_TRADES * k` (k>1) or accept `>= target - boundary_slack`. Whatever is chosen must be justified against a measured boundary-loss distribution, not picked; the current value was picked precisely because it looked principled ('aims at exactly what the verdict requires').

(3) MAKE THE VERDICT STATE ITS OWN DERIVATION. `resolve_split` already returns meta with mode AND target, and its docstring says this is 'so a verdict states its own derivation' -- but the coverage-matrix ref for this cell records neither. That is diagnostic-provenance sub-class B (implicit input selection) one level up: a reader cannot tell which split produced the number they are being asked to trust. A cell refused for thin OOS must carry the split mode, target, and achieved count.

DO NOT record a verdict obtained at a non-standard split into the matrix as if it were the standard one. Choosing a split that clears a floor is a decision that must be visible, not a side effect of debugging this item.

updates.note:
CRITERION (1) COMPLETE -- THE ITEM IS CONFIRMED, NOT FALSIFIED. Ran base_oos under BOTH split modes on the two legs (trainer relay #9211, config-exact, tp_cap_pct=0.099, MIN_OOS_TRADES=25):

  htf_pullback_trend_2h (BTCUSDT 2h)
    --split-mode oos-trades -> split=2026-04-03  base_oos_n=24  -> insufficient_base
    --split-mode date       -> split=2025-07-01  base_oos_n=95  -> GRADEABLE

  tlt_pullback_1h (TLT 1h)
    --split-mode oos-trades -> split=2026-02-05  base_oos_n=22  -> insufficient_base
    --split-mode date       -> split=2025-07-01  base_oos_n=56  -> GRADEABLE

Both SHIPPED real-money cells are GRADEABLE at the corpus-standard split and are refused only under the derived one. The derivation places htf's boundary at 2026-04-03 -- roughly three months before the data ends (2026-07-10) -- leaving 24 trades, then refuses for 24 < 25.

These also cross-check the independent full-history measurement in relay #9209 (97 and 60 there vs 95 and 56 here); the small gap is the warmup/boundary effect resolve_split's own docstring predicts, which is itself further confirmation of the mechanism rather than a discrepancy.

THE FIX NOW HAS A ONE-SENTENCE FORM, which it did not when this row was filed: THE DERIVATION SHOULD ONLY EVER *ENLARGE* A THIN OOS WINDOW, NEVER *SHRINK* A RICH ONE. `oos-trades` exists to rescue legs that land at OOS 3-6 on a fixed date (resolve_split's docstring says exactly that); it has no business reducing 95 to 24. Concretely: take max(derived_split_window, fixed_corpus_split_window) rather than the derived one unconditionally -- which also makes criterion (2)'s 'measured boundary-loss distribution' unnecessary for the common case, since a leg that clears the floor at the standard split never needs the derivation at all.

STILL NOT DONE and still deliberately not taken here: criterion (2) (the actual default change -- fleet-wide verdict impact) and criterion (3) (make the verdict record its split mode/target/achieved count; the cell ref that started this records none of them). And NO cell was re-graded: these are `shipped` real-money cells and their disposition is queued operator decision (d).

CRITERION (3) SHIPPED -- a thin-OOS refusal now states WHICH WINDOW produced the count. This is the half of the finding that needed no fleet-wide verdict decision, so it did not have to wait on the operator.

What was wrong: `insufficient_base_why` read `OOS base 24 trades < floor 25` -- a COUNT over a window it did not name. That one sentence covered two OPPOSITE conditions with opposite remedies: a trade-starved leg (wait, or stop grading it) and a badly-placed boundary (move the split and re-grade TODAY). Both printed identically, which is why establishing that htf_pullback_trend_2h was the second kind cost a fresh trainer-relay run instead of a read. Diagnostic-provenance sub-class B. `resolve_split`'s own docstring already promised the cure -- 'Returned meta records target AND mode so a verdict states its own derivation' -- and NO verdict read the meta, so the docstring described a property that did not exist (field beats comment, in the direction where the comment was the aspiration).

Shipped: (a) a new pure `insufficient_base_reason(base_oos_n, floor, split, split_meta)` in scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py -- extracted rather than inlined BECAUSE the verdict block lives inside main() and was not reachable from a test; (b) the message now names the split date, the split_mode, the target (omitted under `date`, where nothing was targeted), the leg LIFETIME, and any fallback; (c) every cell entry -- not only refused ones -- records split / split_mode / split_target_oos / split_lifetime_trades / split_fallback, the assignments placed ABOVE the `if _thin:` branch so a PASS carries the same audit trail as a refusal; (d) tests/test_m20_split_provenance.py, 7 tests.

THE LIFETIME IS THE LOAD-BEARING FIELD, not the split date: it is what separates 407-lifetime/24-window (htf, boundary problem) from 33-lifetime/5-window (mes_trend_long_1d, genuinely starved). The test that matters asserts the two strings DIFFER and still differ when both legs share a boundary date, so the discrimination cannot be an accident of the dates.

Two ways a provenance string lies, both pinned: an absent input is OMITTED, never fabricated (under `--split-mode date` no emit runs, so the lifetime is unknown -- printing 0 would turn 'we did not count' into 'the leg has no trades', which makes a refusal look deserved); and a fallback is never silent. CAN-FAIL VERIFIED: reverting the function body to the old one-liner fails 5 of the 7 tests including the discriminator; the 2 that survive are the structural wiring tests, which that mutation does not touch.

PURELY ADDITIVE -- no verdict branch reads any of these keys, so no grade can move and no cell was re-graded. STILL OPEN: criterion (2), the actual default change, which DOES move verdicts fleet-wide and stays queued behind operator decision (d).

CAVEAT ON MY OWN PROPOSED FIX -- `max(derived_split_window, fixed_corpus_split_window)` is validated for the RICH-leg case ONLY, and I should not have written it as though it covered the row.

Under the derived split, run 31771809102 recorded base OOS n for four legs: htf_pullback_trend_2h 24, mhg_pullback_1d 24, tlt_pullback_1h 22, mes_trend_long_1d 4. THREE OF THE FOUR CLUSTER JUST UNDER THE FLOOR OF 25 ON LEGS WITH VERY DIFFERENT LIFETIMES, which is itself the clearest signature of the defect: a derivation aiming at exactly 25 lands at 22-24 after the warmup loss its own docstring predicts, whatever the leg. It also explains why the same '(24)' appears on two different legs -- that is the mechanism, not a copy-pasted ref.

But I measured the STANDARD-SPLIT counterfactual for only TWO of them (htf 95, tlt 56, relay #9211). For mhg_pullback_1d and mes_trend_long_1d I did NOT, so I do not know whether the derivation SHRANK their window or ENLARGED it. mes at 4 is far below the target, which is what the documented `leg_too_thin` fallback to the fixed date looks like -- i.e. probably genuinely trade-starved, not mis-split.

WHY THAT BREAKS THE PROPOSED FIX AS STATED: `max(derived, fixed)` helps a leg whose rich window was shrunk. It does NOTHING for a leg whose derivation ENLARGED a thin window and still landed at 24 -- that leg fails under both branches of the max. If mhg is that case, the fix leaves it refused. The complete fix has to give the target MARGIN OVER THE FLOOR rather than equality with it (target = floor + expected boundary loss, or derive-then-check-achieved-and-retry), which is a different change from the max.

DO NOT compare these fleet-sweep base_oos figures to the OOS 5/7/10 recorded on the exit_head_ml cells for MES/MGC/MHG -- those come from the exit-HEAD harness with its own fold structure, not from this sweep, and reading them as the same quantity would manufacture a shrink that was never measured.

CONTROLLED CONFIRMATION FROM THE COMMITTED CORPUS -- stronger than the relay A/B, because it is the corpus's own history rather than a comparison I set up.

docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl, leg=htf_pullback_trend_2h cell=trail3 lever=trail_geometry, run 2026-08-13T01:36:21Z:
    tp_cap_pct 0.099 | split 2025-07-01 | min_oos_trades_floor 25
    base_trades_OOS 95 | verdict is_oos_fail   <- GRADEABLE
The same cell in run 31771809102 on 2026-08-14 under the derived split: base OOS 24 -> insufficient_base.

THE FLOOR WAS 25 ON BOTH DAYS, so 'the floor is new' is refuted as an explanation -- it is recorded in the 08-13 row itself. Same leg, same lever, same live-parity TP, same floor; the only variable that moved is the split, and the window went 95 -> 24.

Corroborating: tlt_pullback_1h/trail4 carries base_trades_OOS 56 / 55 / 56 across the 08-10, 08-12 and 08-13 runs at the fixed split -- stable, and matching relay #9211's independent 56 exactly.

METHOD NOTE, because it nearly went the other way: a first pass read `base_oos=None` on every corpus row and I briefly took that for 'these rows predate the floor', which would have made the comparison uncontrolled and the claim unsupportable. It was my own key-name error -- I queried `base_trades_oos`, the field is `base_trades_OOS`. Checking the field that would have INVALIDATED the claim is what turned it from suggestive into controlled.

COMPLETE: 4 OF 4 AFFECTED LEGS NOW MEASURED BOTH WAYS (trainer relay #9218, config-exact, tp_cap 0.099, MIN_OOS_TRADES=25). The derivation does THREE different things, and only one of them is the harm this row was opened for:

  leg                     derived (oos-trades)     fixed (date)        direction
  htf_pullback_trend_2h   2026-04-03 -> 24         2025-07-01 -> 95    SHRANK a rich window
  tlt_pullback_1h         2026-02-05 -> 22         2025-07-01 -> 56    SHRANK a rich window
  mhg_pullback_1d         2023-02-07 -> 24         2025-07-01 ->  7    ENLARGED 7 -> 24
  mes_trend_long_1d       fell back  ->  4         2025-07-01 ->  4    leg_too_thin, lifetime 33

MHG IS THE CASE I WARNED ABOUT TWO UPDATES AGO, AND IT LANDED. The derivation ENLARGED its window from 7 to 24 -- doing precisely the job `oos-trades` exists for -- AND IT STILL FAILS, SHORT BY ONE TRADE. That is the whole defect in a single row: the derivation aimed at exactly 25, executed correctly, and missed by 1.

SO `max(derived, fixed)` IS REFUTED AS A COMPLETE FIX, not merely caveated. On mhg it picks 24 (the larger of 24 and 7) and refuses anyway. Had I shipped it as 'the' fix -- which is how I first wrote it -- htf and tlt would have been rescued and mhg would have stayed silently refused, with the row closed.

THE FIX THE EVIDENCE ACTUALLY SUPPORTS: `max(derive(target = floor + margin), fixed_window)`. Both terms are needed and each covers what the other cannot -- the MARGIN rescues the enlarge case (mhg), the MAX rescues the shrink case (htf/tlt). Worked against these four: htf max(~24, 95) = 95 GRADEABLE; tlt max(~22, 56) = 56 GRADEABLE; mhg derive at target 30 clears 25 with room, and 30 is supportable on its lifetime; mes lifetime 33 cannot give 30 to OOS, so it falls back and stays correctly refused at 4. All four end up right, and mes stays refused -- which is the control that the fix is not simply making everything gradeable.

The margin VALUE still needs the boundary-loss distribution criterion (2) asks for; 30 is an illustration on n=4, not a proposal. mes also confirms the documented `leg_too_thin` fallback path fires correctly (lifetime 33, cannot support 25 in OOS), so that branch is working as designed.

[sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Criterion (1) is confirmed in the row's own update and (3) is shipped (resolve_split returns split meta and `summary_split_line`/insufficient_base_reason print mode+target+clamp, m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:1095-1147). Criterion (2) is NOT: scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:1543-1547 still declares `--split-target-oos` with `default=MIN_OOS_TRADES` and the help text still says it 'aims at exactly what the verdict requires' — so an ordinary 1-4 trade boundary loss (the measured distribution in docs/research/m20-split-boundary-loss-2026-08-14.md: 0,1,1,1,1,1,2,2,4,4,4) still lands under the floor. — The boundary-loss distribution is now measured, so the value can be justified rather than picked — that was the blocker on (2).

history.note:
CRITERION (2) IS CLOSED — the boundary-loss distribution is measured. Memo: docs/research/m20-split-boundary-loss-2026-08-14.md (checked: docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl, a pure read of the committed corpus — no harness run).

POPULATION: 922 corpus rows, 18 carry split_target_oos, which are 14 distinct (leg, split, target) boundary EVENTS — not 14 rows; several lever cells share one derivation and counting rows would inflate n exactly as double-counting _prop legs did on decision (a) earlier today. 3 are leg_too_thin fallbacks (no derivation happened) -> 11 derived events across 7 distinct legs. Three of those legs (iwm/scha/splg _trend_long_1d) are near-identical and behave identically, so the effective independence is nearer FIVE than eleven. Stated because it is the binding caveat on the answer.

DISTRIBUTION: 0,1,1,1,1,1,2,2,4,4,4 — min 0, median 1, mean 1.91, MAX 4. Ten of eleven are losses; ZERO are gains. The never-negative half is a refuted hypothesis, not an unexamined one: `[:10]` truncates the boundary to a DATE, so windowing from midnight could plausibly sweep in same-day trades sitting BEFORE the boundary trade and push realized above target. It never does — warmup dominates and the effect is strictly one-directional.

IT TRACKS target/lifetime, NOT target. The same three legs lose 4 at ratio ~0.55 and 1 at ~0.44; target alone spans 1..4 at a fixed 35. A boundary pushed deep into a short history lands in sparser data. The three worst come from a regime the clamp (added today) now PREVENTS — it caps target at lifetime//2, so ratio cannot exceed 0.50, and every observation at ratio <= 0.5 lost <= 2.

ANSWER: margin 5 -> target 30. Covers the observed max (4) with one spare, including the pre-clamp ratio-0.55 regime that can no longer arise; post-clamp headroom is better than 2x.

THIS CONFIRMS THE ILLUSTRATIVE VALUE, IT DOES NOT REPLACE IT — and the near-miss is the part worth keeping. Mid-analysis I had a tidy story that the illustrative 30 came from mis-counting the three leg_too_thin rows, whose apparent 'loss' is 30/31, a striking numeric match. Wrong: 30 was always the TARGET (floor 25 + margin 5), never a margin, and those rows are the fixed-date cliff the clamp already fixes. Reading the sprint-log line instead of trusting the match is what caught it. A confirmation is a duller result than a correction, which is exactly when the pull toward the correction should be distrusted.

STILL OPEN: the DEFAULT is unchanged. Flipping --split-target-oos moves recorded verdicts fleet-wide (htf 95->24, tlt 56->22, mhg 7->24 measured both ways), so it is the operator's call; this memo is its basis. Also unmeasured: any leg at ratio > 0.5, which the clamp forbids — if the clamp is relaxed the margin needs re-measuring.

FRESH EVIDENCE FOR THE QUEUED DEFAULT FLIP, from a run that was not looking for it. Dispatched a scoped fleet re-sweep of the 32 stale cells the coverage roll-up labels re-runnable (19 legs, defaults, tp_cap 0.099) and it refused EVERYTHING it reached before I stopped it: 28 of 28 cells graded `insufficient_base` across three legs (trainer relay #9542, progress read #9544).

THE n IS THREE, NOT 28 — a leg's cells share ONE split derivation, so those 28 cells are three independent boundary events. Stating it because this item's own criterion-(2) memo insisted on exactly that distinction ('18 rows ... are 14 distinct boundary EVENTS — not 14 rows; counting rows would inflate n'), and 28/28 reads far stronger than it is. Three of three is still decisive enough to stop a run.

It reproduces on the filing leg: htf_pullback_trend_2h, 375 lifetime trades, boundary derived to 2026-03-30 targeting 25, refused — the same leg that graded at base_oos 95 under the corpus-standard split in criterion (1). The other two are trend_donchian (343 lifetime, split 2026-02-25) and squeeze_breakout_4h.

WHAT THIS ADDS beyond criterion (1): that run tested TWO legs chosen BECAUSE they had failed. This one drew 19 legs by a criterion unrelated to the defect (stale + re-runnable) and the first three all failed, which is evidence about the RATE rather than about two known cases. It does not establish the rate over all 19 — I stopped at three.

NOT ACTED ON: the default is unchanged. Re-dispatched that one research run with an explicit --split-target-oos 50 (relay #9545), justified against this item's measured max loss of 4 rather than picked, and the value criterion (1) itself used. The DEFAULT flip is still the operator's call and stays queued.

items.resolution_note: RESOLVED 2026-08-16 by the operator's Tier-3 default flip (in-conversation). `--tp-cap-pct` now defaults to LIVE_TP_CAP_PCT=0.099 and `--split-target-oos` to DEFAULT_SPLIT_TARGET_OOS=50, separated from the MIN_OOS_TRADES=25 floor it used to equal. Passing `--tp-cap-pct 0` is now the explicit opt-out and is REQUIRED to reproduce any verdict recorded before 2026-08-10. Raising the TARGET strands no thin leg: resolve_split already clamps to len(stamps)//2 and RECORDS split_target_clamped_from/to, refusing only below the 25 floor — the clamp is why target and floor can differ at all.

items.title: pytest-run short-circuits on docs/ changes, but 39 test files read docs/ -- the exclusion's stated justification is per-file and was never checked per-file
items.detail:
MEASURED, WITH THE INCIDENT: PR #9208 changed ONLY docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json. pytest-run's relevance filter excludes docs/, so the check went green in TEN SECONDS (08:51:24 -> 08:51:34; a real run is 7-9 min over ~10,677 tests), the PR merged, and it left `main` RED -- tests/test_exit_head_per_leg.py reads that matrix AS THE REAL FILE and its stale_decisions assertion inverted. Caught only because an unrelated PR ran the suite locally.

THIS IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE of the class tests/test_pytest_run_filter.py's own header enumerates (config/, .github/workflows/, then scripts/ via PR #8994's NINE-second green on 2026-08-13). Each previous instance was fixed by adding the one proven tree; the class keeps recurring because the filter is a hand-enumerated allowlist and nothing measures what it misses.

THE ROOT IS A PREMISE THAT WAS NEVER CHECKED PER-FILE. The exclusion is justified in the workflow comment as 'the suite's assertions over them are owned by the separate `guards` job, which does not short-circuit'. That is TRUE for docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json (every test touching it writes a tmp_path fixture) and FALSE for the coverage matrix (read as-committed). The premise is per-file; it was applied per-TREE. `guards` does run exit-coverage-matrix-guard, but that validates statuses + refs only -- it does not and cannot run the pytest assertion that broke.

THE UNMEASURED DENOMINATOR: 39 test files under tests/ reference docs/ paths. I verified TWO of them (the matrix -- real file, now covered; the backlog -- fixture, correctly excluded). THE OTHER 37 ARE UNCHECKED, so I cannot say whether more real-file reads sit behind the same short-circuit. Shipped in this PR is the narrow proven fix (that one JSON path added to the grep + to test_pytest_run_filter.py::COVERED), NOT the general case -- and a narrow fix that reads as complete is exactly how instance 5 happens.

WHY NOT JUST WIDEN TO docs/: the cost rationale is real and documented (MB-20260706-CI-MINUTES) -- docs/ changes on nearly every PR and a full suite is 7-9 min. Widening wholesale trades one silent-failure class for a cost regression the short-circuit exists to prevent.

ENUMERATION DONE -- criterion (1) is COMPLETE, and it CORRECTS THIS ROW'S OWN FIRST NUMBER. I originally wrote '39 test files reference docs/ paths'. That counted files MENTIONING docs/ anywhere, including docstrings, which is the wrong denominator for this question. Scanning tests/ mechanically for a docs/ path joined onto the repo root: 19 test files carry a docs/ path LITERAL, and exactly FOUR read a COMMITTED docs/ file (the rest write fixtures under tmp_path):
  docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json -> test_exit_head_per_leg (the incident)
  docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl        -> test_m20_regime_book_provenance
  docs/claude/system-actions.md               -> tests/ops/test_system_actions_workflow
  docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md              -> test_audit_verification_checklist
All four are now in the filter, so the scope was three more paths, not a project.

THE ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL ONE IS THE WORST OF THE THREE AND WAS NEARLY MISSED: `test_live_repo_checklist_clean` asserts the LIVE doc has no drift, and the only other check of that property is the WEEKLY doc-audit-weekly.yml. `arch-doc-guard` DOES list that doc in its globs, which is exactly why it looked covered -- but it runs scripts/arch_doc_guard.py, a different script that does not check the checklist. Covering it costs a full suite on many docs-only PRs; included anyway, because a check a docs PR can silently skip is not a check.

THE CLASS WAS PREVIOUSLY MARKED RESOLVED ON A CRITERION THAT WAS NOT MET. BL-20260813-PYTEST-RUN-SHORTCIRCUITS-SO-MAIN-MERGES-UNVERIFIED (severity high, status resolved) required 'pytest-run cannot report a green tick without having executed the suite (or reports a visibly distinct state when it skips)'. That was never achieved -- it was closed by adding the three trees then known (scripts/deploy/comms), leaving the green-tick ambiguity that IS the hazard fully intact. Instance 4 arrived four weeks later through the one tree nobody had added. Closing a class-level row on an instance-level fix is itself the recurrence mechanism, and it is worth more than the path list above.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) DONE -- enumerated mechanically; 4 committed readers, all now covered. (2) DONE -- tests/test_pytest_run_filter.py::test_docs_committed_readers_are_all_covered re-derives the set FROM THE TESTS on every run and fails when a new committed docs/ reader is not covered, so instance 5 cannot merge quietly. It ships with a negative control (test_the_scan_finds_the_reader_we_already_know_about) so a scan that silently stops matching cannot read as a clean pass. (3) OPEN, and it is the one that matters: pytest-run still reports an IDENTICAL green tick whether it ran 10,677 tests or zero. Every fix so far, including this one, has widened the allowlist rather than removed that ambiguity. Done = a skipped run is visibly distinct at the merge button (a neutral/skipped conclusion, or a required check that reports what it executed). Until then the class can recur through any tree the allowlist does not name. (4) OPEN, cheaper alternative worth pricing first: move the four committed-doc assertions into the `guards` job, which never short-circuits -- that removes the CI-minutes cost this PR just accepted on ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md.

items.title: 4 of the 5 remaining stale live DECISIONS are trail_geometry cells that no re-sweep can ever clear -- the list asks for a remedy that does not exist for them
items.detail:
`evidence_vintage`'s `stale_decisions` flags live cells whose evidence predates the TP-parity cutover, and the implied remedy is 're-sweep it at live parity'. For `trail_geometry` cells that remedy DOES NOT EXIST, for two compounding reasons the sweep already documents in its own help text:

  1. THE SHIPPED LEVER IS THE BASE. A normal cell measures the base against itself -- BL-20260813-SWEEP-GRADES-SHIPPED-LEVERS-AGAINST-THEMSELVES records 31 of 860 corpus rows as exactly that, all-zero deltas wearing an `is_oos_fail`/`insufficient_base` label.
  2. THE LEVER-OFF ARM, which exists precisely to grade a shipped lever, EXCLUDES trail_geometry: `--without-declared-lever` offers stale_stop/giveback_stop/trail_decay/vol_trail, and the workflow states plainly that `trail_geometry is not offerable: trail_mult has no OFF state`.

So the shipped trail value cannot be re-graded either by a normal cell or by the OFF arm. Measured against the current matrix, 4 of the 5 remaining stale live decisions are trail_geometry (htf_pullback_trend_2h, mes_trend_long_1d, mhg_pullback_1d, tlt_pullback_1h); the 5th is mhg_pullback_1d/stale_stop, which IS offerable.

WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A CURIOSITY: it is the desensitized-alarm shape. A flag that cannot be cleared by the action it implies gets walked past, and it will sit in every future review's output looking like outstanding work. I nearly spent a trainer run on it tonight -- I had the invocation written before reading the workflow's own help text, and it would have produced confident base-vs-base numbers that LOOK like verdicts. That is the failure this row exists to stop for the next session.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE ACTUALLY SUPPORTS, so the flag is not simply deleted: the corpus DOES carry live-parity (tp_cap 0.099) rows for these legs' NEIGHBOUR cells, dated 2026-08-13. For htf_pullback_trend_2h (ships trail4) both neighbours trail3/trail5 come back `is_oos_fail` at live parity, which is consistent with the shipped value still being the local best -- weaker than a re-grade, but not nothing. For tlt_pullback_1h (ships trail3) the neighbour trail4 comes back `path_b_wf_pass`, filed separately as PB-20260814-TLT-PULLBACK-1H-SHIPS-TRAIL3-WHILE-TRAIL4-PASSES-AT-LIVE-PARITY. So the honest state is 'the shipped decision is not re-gradeable, but its neighbourhood has been measured at live parity' -- and NOTHING in the matrix says that today.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) `stale_decisions` distinguishes a cell that CAN be re-swept from one that cannot -- e.g. a `remedy` field per row (`resweep` / `neighbourhood_only` / `not_regradeable`), so a reviewer is never handed an alarm whose implied action is impossible. Three states, not a boolean: 'not yet re-swept', 're-swept', and 'cannot be re-swept' are different, and collapsing the third into the first is what produces the walk-past. (2) The neighbourhood evidence that DOES exist is reachable from the cell -- the trail_geometry cells for htf_pullback_trend_2h and tlt_pullback_1h reference their 2026-08-13 live-parity neighbour rows, so a reader is not left believing nothing has been measured. (3) Either a way to grade a shipped trail_mult is built (the natural one: compare the shipped value against its neighbours as the cell grid already does, and say so explicitly) or the matrix records that trail_geometry decisions are permanently ungradeable post-hoc and the stale flag is scoped accordingly.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The rollup did grow a three-state corpus classification (m20_coverage_rollup.py:653-700: CORPUS_NO_ROW 'a re-run IS the remedy', CORPUS_HARNESS_UNFIXED and CORPUS_NO_PRODUCER 'a re-run is NOT the remedy'), but it does not cover this row's case: `trail_geometry` is listed IN `COLUMNS_WITH_A_SWEEP_PRODUCER` (line 690-693), so a shipped trail cell still reads as re-sweepable even though the shipped value is the base and `--without-declared-lever` cannot offer trail_geometry (the map deliberately omits it, per the comment at :331-333). — Ends when stale_decisions distinguishes 'not yet re-swept' / 're-swept' / 'cannot be re-swept' for a shipped trail_geometry cell, or the matrix records that trail decisions are permanently ungradeable post-hoc and scopes the flag.
Re-validated: M20 exit-program measurement/tooling correctness. Propose-only, no live-order impact. Blocked on trainer capacity (91.7% disk) for anything needing a re-sweep.

items.title: 100 of the 186 stale cells already have a LIVE-PARITY corpus row, and 9 of those rows PASS on a floor-clearing window while the matrix records a negative — the remedy is a JOIN, not a re-run
items.detail:
MEASURED against the committed artifacts (docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json + docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl), 2026-08-14:

  stale_cells (evidence_vintage)                                   186
  ...that ALREADY have a live-parity (tp_cap_pct 0.099) corpus row  100  (53.8%)
  ...of which at least one such row is a PASS or path_b_wf_pass      11

The eleven, matrix status vs the live-parity corpus verdict:
  ada_pullback_2h        vol_trail        honest_negative   path_b_wf_pass
  eth_pullback_prop_2h   trail_decay      honest_negative   path_b_wf_pass
  gld_pullback_1h        vol_trail        honest_negative   PASS
  mhg_pullback_1d        stale_stop       passed_unshipped  path_b_wf_pass
  slv_pullback_1d        stale_stop       honest_negative   path_b_wf_pass
  tlt_pullback_1h        trail_geometry   shipped           path_b_wf_pass   (already filed as PB-20260814-TLT-...)
  trend_donchian_avax_4h stale_stop       honest_negative   PASS
  trend_donchian_avax_4h vol_trail        honest_negative   PASS
  trend_donchian_sol_4h  trail_geometry   honest_negative   path_b_wf_pass
  trend_donchian_sol_4h  vol_trail        honest_negative   path_b_wf_pass
  trend_donchian_xrp_4h  trail_decay      honest_negative   PASS

WHY IT MATTERS: `evidence_vintage`'s own comment says a stale NEGATIVE 'costs knowledge -- the lever might have passed and we would not know'. For these it is not hypothetical: the lever DID pass at live parity, the run happened, the row is committed, and the matrix still carries the pre-cutover negative. Worked example -- trend_donchian_xrp_4h/trail_decay reads honest_negative on a ref dated 2026-07-12/13 ('eth/sol/xrp 4h all cells is_oos_fail'), while the corpus holds two live-parity PASSes from 2026-08-10: decay_arm2R_t2.5 (wf 5/6, d_net_r_OOS +1.0043, base_OOS 32) and decay_arm1.5R_stall6_t2.5 (wf 4/6, +0.9204).

So the 186-cell backlog is not 186 re-runs. Over half is a JOIN the roll-up does not perform, and the expensive part (the sweep) is already paid for.

CAVEATS THAT BOUND THIS, stated because the list above will read as a to-flip list otherwise:
  1. A passing CELL is not automatically a passing LEVER disposition. Precedent cuts toward it      (tlt_pullback_1h shipped on exactly one passing cell), but each of the 11 needs adjudication.
  2. EIGHT of the 11 are `path_b_wf_pass` -- the weaker route, whose history includes candidates      that reached it with zero generalisation evidence. Only 4 are a full PASS.
  3. I did NOT re-run anything; this is a read of two committed files.
  4. Any resulting status change on a `live` leg is Tier-3 and belongs to the operator.

MY OWN ERROR, RECORDED BECAUSE IT NEARLY BECAME THE HEADLINE: my first pass reported these cells as NOT flagged by evidence_vintage -- i.e. 'invisible'. That was wrong. I unpacked the stale_cells tuple as (leg, lever, ...) when it is (leg, symbol, timeframe, lever, ref_date, cutover), so I was comparing levers against SYMBOLS and every lookup missed. All 11 ARE flagged. The staleness machinery is working; what is missing is the join to the evidence that resolves it. Checking the tuple shape instead of trusting my unpacking is the only reason this row says something true.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) The roll-up (or a sibling tool) reports, per stale cell, whether a live-parity corpus row EXISTS for that (leg, lever) and what it says -- so a reviewer sees 'stale, and here is the newer evidence' rather than 'stale'. Three states, not two: no live-parity row / live-parity row agrees / live-parity row DISAGREES with the recorded status. (2) The 11 disagreements above are each adjudicated and the matrix cell updated or the disagreement explained in the ref (e.g. 'one cell passes but the lever disposition stands because X'). (3) A guard or check fails when a matrix cell's status contradicts the newest live-parity corpus row for the same (leg, lever) without the ref acknowledging it -- otherwise this recurs on the next sweep.

updates.note:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN HEADLINE, DOWNWARD: the count is NINE, not eleven. Caught while collecting the per-cell evidence to write into the refs -- i.e. by doing the next step, not by re-reading.

Two of the eleven pass on windows TODAY'S FLOOR WOULD REFUSE, and the corpus has ALREADY retracted them:
  mhg_pullback_1d/stale_stop  cell stale8_lt0R  base_OOS=7
      2026-08-10  min_oos_trades_floor=None -> path_b_wf_pass
      2026-08-13  min_oos_trades_floor=25   -> insufficient_base
  slv_pullback_1d/stale_stop  cell stale8_lt0R  base_OOS=6
      2026-08-10  min_oos_trades_floor=None -> path_b_wf_pass
      2026-08-13  min_oos_trades_floor=25   -> insufficient_base

Both passed on 6- and 7-trade OOS windows BEFORE the floor existed, and the same cells were re-run after it landed and correctly refused. They are not live contradictions with the matrix -- the corpus superseded them on its own. That is the floor doing exactly its job, and it is evidence FOR the floor, not against it.

MY ERROR WAS THE AGGREGATION, NOT THE READ: I counted 'any live-parity row whose verdict is a PASS' rather than 'the NEWEST live-parity row', so a superseded pass and a standing one carried equal weight. The newest-row logic I used elsewhere in the same analysis was right; this particular tally was not.

CORRECTED FIGURES: 186 stale cells | 100 with a live-parity row | 9 whose newest floor-clearing live-parity evidence PASSES against a recorded negative. Of those 9, four are a full PASS (gld_pullback_1h/vol_trail 31 OOS, trend_donchian_avax_4h/stale_stop 34, trend_donchian_avax_4h/vol_trail 34, trend_donchian_xrp_4h/trail_decay 32) and five are path_b_wf_pass; base_OOS on the nine runs 29-67. The tlt_pullback_1h row (56 OOS) is one of the nine and is separately filed as PB-20260814-TLT-...

This also sharpens resolution criterion (1): the per-cell report must compare against the NEWEST live-parity row, and must not treat a pre-floor pass as standing evidence. A join that ignores supersession manufactures contradictions -- which is what mine did twice over before this check.

TWO MORE FOUND BY THE GUARD, AND ONE OF THE ELEVEN IS ON REAL MONEY -- the prioritisation the list was missing.

(a) The guard written for criterion (3) (matrix-corpus-agreement) failed on its FIRST run against a tree I had just audited by hand, with two cells I had never seen:
  uso_trend_1h/vol_trail        honest_negative  vs vt_cold10_t2  path_b_wf_pass 2026-08-13 wf 4/6 base_OOS 27
  ict_scalp_sol_5m/stale_stop   honest_negative  vs be_touch_arm  path_b_wf_pass 2026-08-11 wf 3/4 base_OOS 286
NEITHER IS IN `stale_cells`: their refs carry post-cutover dates, so the staleness date-proxy reads them as CURRENT while the STATUS rests on an older negative. My item-65 audit scanned the stale list, so it could not have reached them however carefully I looked. That is the difference between an audit and an invariant. Both are now annotated.

(b) ACCOUNT ROUTING, read from config/accounts.yaml + config/strategies.yaml:
  trend_donchian_xrp_4h  -> bybit_1(paper/live), **bybit_2(real_money/LIVE)**, bybit_portfolio(paper/live)
  uso_trend_1h / gld_pullback_1h / tlt_pullback_1h -> alpaca_paper(paper/live), alpaca_portfolio(paper/live), alpaca_live(real_money/**dry_run**)
  ict_scalp_sol_5m / trend_donchian_avax_4h / trend_donchian_sol_4h / ada_pullback_2h -> bybit_1(paper/live)
  eth_pullback_prop_2h -> bybit_1(paper/live), breakout_1(prop/live)

SO EXACTLY ONE OF THE DISAGREEMENTS IS ON A REAL-MONEY ACCOUNT THAT IS ACTUALLY LIVE: trend_donchian_xrp_4h/trail_decay on bybit_2 -- and it is one of the four FULL PASSes, not a path_b. That is the one worth the operator's attention first. The three alpaca legs touch a real_money account whose ACCOUNT-LEVEL gate is `dry_run`, so they place no live orders; calling them 'real money' without that qualifier would overstate them, which is the same state-your-population discipline the rest of this row is built on. Everything else is paper or prop.

A BUG IN MY OWN GUARD, CAUGHT BEFORE MERGE BY BUILDING THE ROLL-UP REPORT ON TOP OF IT -- and it was hiding real findings.

The first version of matrix-corpus-agreement reduced a (leg, lever) group by max(run_id) ACROSS CELLS. But a lever is swept as MANY CELLS in one run -- trail4 and trail6, vt_hot90 and vt_cold10 -- which are ALTERNATIVE parameterizations, not successive measurements. Only the same CELL re-run later supersedes. Taking the max across cells returned whichever cell fell last in list order within a single 2026-08-10 run, so a failing SIBLING masked a standing pass.

IT FAILED IN THE SAFE-LOOKING DIRECTION -- fewer contradictions reported -- which is the kind nobody re-checks. Five of the nine read as 'superseded' when nothing had superseded them; e.g. gld_pullback_1h/vol_trail's passing vt_hot90_t2 was masked by a failing vt_cold10_t2 from the SAME run.

FIXED: reduce to the newest row PER CELL first (that is supersession), then ask whether any surviving cell passes. The self-test now pins the sibling case explicitly, since the broken behaviour was invisible from the output.

TWO MORE DISAGREEMENTS SURFACED BY THE FIX, both previously masked:
  gld_pullback_1h/trail_decay   honest_negative vs decay_arm1.5R_stall6_t2 path_b_wf_pass base_OOS 31
  slv_trend_1h/trail_decay      honest_negative vs decay_stall10_t2        path_b_wf_pass base_OOS 40
Both annotated. RUNNING TOTAL OF DISTINCT DISAGREEMENTS FOUND: 13 -- 9 from the stale-cell audit, 2 the guard found that were not stale at all (uso_trend_1h/vol_trail, ict_scalp_sol_5m/stale_stop), and these 2 that the guard's own bug had masked. All 13 are annotated; no status changed.

AND A SECOND SELF-INFLICTED DEFECT FROM THE SAME SESSION, also caught pre-merge: annotating a cell stamps today's date into its `ref`, and evidence_vintage's date-proxy read that as the evidence being renewed -- 8 cells with `tp_geometry: null` DROPPED OUT of stale_cells purely because I wrote a note on them (186 -> 178). The cells that survived did so only because they carry an explicit `tp_geometry: no_take_profit` overriding the proxy. The matrix's own refs already state the rule in prose -- 'a note about the evidence is not the evidence being renewed' -- so it was written down and unenforced. Fixed with `evidence_dates()`, which excludes annotation segments before extracting dates; stale_cells back to 186.

[sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: (1) the rollup reports per-stale-cell corpus state in three uncollapsed buckets (m20_coverage_rollup.py:1393-1440: CORPUS_NO_ROW / CORPUS_AGREES / CORPUS_DISAGREES, plus the 'NOT COMPUTED' third state when the corpus cannot be read). (3) the guard exists and is registered: scripts/ci/check_matrix_corpus_agreement.py is `matrix-corpus-agreement` in run_guards.py. (2) running it now returns 'OK — 235 live cell(s) checked against 1264 corpus row(s); no unacknowledged disagreement', i.e. every remaining disagreement is acknowledged in the cell ref — the criterion's second branch.

items.tier: 1 (research measurement; any resulting disposition change is Tier-3)
items.title: 6 SHIPPED levers have no lever-OFF row — never graded against their own absence (was filed as 9; 2 were never gradeable and 1 was a stale matrix cell)
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 against docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl + exit-refinement-coverage.json + config/accounts.yaml.

THE SWEEP CANNOT GRADE A SHIPPED LEVER IN A NORMAL RUN -- the shipped lever IS the base, so a normal cell measures alternatives against it (BL-20260813-SWEEP-GRADES-SHIPPED-LEVERS-AGAINST-THEMSELVES). The `--without-declared-lever` arm exists precisely for this: it DROPS the declared lever from the base and re-adds it as a `shipped_*` cell, so d_net_r = (with lever) - (without lever). A negative delta means the shipped lever is WORSE than not having it.

That arm has run: 22 corpus rows carry `without_declared_levers`, all dated 2026-08-13. It works, and its results are already correctly reflected -- e.g. trend_donchian_eth/stale_stop measures d_net_r_OOS -10.55 over 117 OOS trades and the matrix cell is `honest_negative`; trend_donchian/trail_decay measures +2.03 and PASSES. I checked the money-losing direction specifically (positive status + failing live-parity evidence) and found NO unrecorded case: the four positive-status cells whose alternatives all fail are the EXPECTED shape, because alternatives failing means the shipped value is locally best.

THE GAP IS COVERAGE, NOT CORRECTNESS. Nine live cells hold a `shipped`/`passed_unshipped` status on a lever the OFF arm CAN remove (stale_stop / giveback_stop / trail_decay / vol_trail) and have no OFF-arm row at all -- so their shipped lever has never been compared to its own absence:
  ict_scalp_eth_15m       stale_stop   shipped           bybit_1 (paper/live)
  iwm_trend_long_1d       trail_decay  shipped           ib_paper, alpaca_paper, alpaca_portfolio, alpaca_live(dry_run)
  mhg_pullback_1d         stale_stop   passed_unshipped  ib_paper (paper/live)
  qqq_trend_long_1d       vol_trail    passed_unshipped  ib_paper, alpaca_* 
  scha_trend_long_1d      trail_decay  shipped           alpaca_paper (paper/live)
  splg_trend_long_1d      trail_decay  shipped           alpaca_paper, alpaca_live(dry_run)
  trend_donchian_avax_4h  trail_decay  passed_unshipped  bybit_1 (paper/live)
  trend_donchian_eth_prop stale_stop   shipped           breakout_1 (PROP/live)
  trend_donchian_eth_prop trail_decay  shipped           breakout_1 (PROP/live)

SCOPED HONESTLY: NONE of the nine is on a real-money account that is actually live. Six are paper, two are the prop bridge (breakout_1 -- real capital, different risk class, manual placement), and the alpaca_live appearances are on an account whose account-level gate is `dry_run` so it places no orders. So this is a KNOWLEDGE gap, not money at risk -- which is why it is medium and not high, and why it should not be reported as 'nine shipped levers may be losing money'.

`trail_geometry` is deliberately excluded from the nine: trail_mult has no OFF state, so its shipped cells are permanently ungradeable by this route (BL-20260814-STALE-DECISION-LIST-HOLDS-CELLS-NO-RESWEEP-CAN-CLEAR).

POPULATION, STATED: the scan (positive status AND offerable lever AND no OFF-arm corpus row) returns ELEVEN matrix cells, not nine. Two of the eleven are the single aggregate roll-up row `shadow fleet (turtle_soup, fade_breakout_4h, vwap, trend_donchian_1h, *_prop)` / symbol `various` / tf `various` (stale_stop + trail_decay, both passed_unshipped, execution `shadow`). That row is not a leg and cannot be swept as one -- it would have to be expanded into its constituent shadow legs first -- so it is excluded from the nine rather than silently dropped. Quote nine as LEGS and eleven as CELLS; neither number is wrong, and reporting one without the other is what makes them look inconsistent.

CORRECTED 2026-08-14 BY THE SWEEP ITSELF (the nine is SIX). The OFF arm was dispatched over these nine pairs and reported `NO-OP <leg>: no_declared_lever_to_drop:<lever>` for two of them, which is the correct answer and not a failure:
  - mhg_pullback_1d / stale_stop  -- config arms no stale_exit_* key
  - qqq_trend_long_1d / vol_trail -- config arms no trail_vol_* key
Both cells read `passed_unshipped`, and for these two that status is EXACTLY RIGHT: the lever was never declared. A lever that is not shipped cannot be graded against its own absence, because its absence IS the base -- the ORDINARY arm already measures the comparison the OFF arm would manufacture. So these two were never a coverage gap; including them was my error, from inferring config state out of a cell status rather than reading config.

The THIRD passed_unshipped pair went the other way and is a separate, worse finding: trend_donchian_avax_4h / trail_decay DOES declare the lever (stall_bars 6 / tight_mult 2.5), the OFF arm measured it as `shipped_trail_decay_6_2.5`, and it PASSED. Its matrix cell is simply stale -- filed as BL-20260814-MATRIX-STATUS-CONTRADICTS-LIVE-CONFIG-ON-SIX-LEVER-CELLS.

So the OFF-arm coverage gap is SIX (leg, lever) pairs, all `shipped`: ict_scalp_eth_15m/stale_stop, trend_donchian_eth_prop/stale_stop, iwm_trend_long_1d/trail_decay, scha_trend_long_1d/trail_decay, splg_trend_long_1d/trail_decay, trend_donchian_eth_prop/trail_decay. The scoping conclusion is unchanged: none is on a real-money account that is actually live.

FIRST RESULTS (2026-08-14, runs 31793061293 / 31793067690 / 31793072500, tp_cap_pct 0.099, split_mode oos-trades): five of the six measured, and **every one returned `insufficient_base`** at base OOS 23/24/24/24/23 against MIN_OOS_TRADES=25. The only leg in the whole dispatch to clear the floor was trend_donchian_avax_4h at OOS 25 -- and it PASSED. The cause is the split-targeting defect: `--split-target-oos` defaults to the floor itself, so the derived boundary aims at exactly what the verdict requires and a shortfall of one trade returns no verdict. The workflow could not even ask for a margin -- it never declared the input (fixed 2026-08-14, with a test asserting exposed-set == used-set). Re-dispatched at --split-target-oos 35.

Read the five `insufficient_base` rows as the THIRD STATE this row's criterion (4) reserves -- *we could not grade it* -- and NOT as evidence about the levers. Their directional deltas are recorded but are not verdicts: iwm +4.37 R OOS, splg +2.01, eth_prop/trail_decay +1.92, scha +1.60 OOS but -3.50 IS, eth_prop/stale_stop **-2.24 OOS** with +3.17 IS (the overfit shape). The last of those is the one to look at first once it is gradeable.

FINAL RESULTS 2026-08-14 — ALL SIX MEASURED, criterion (1) SATISFIED. Round 1 (default target) left five ungradeable; round 2 (target 35) fixed the high-frequency legs and broke the 1d ones (the cliff, BL-20260814-SPLIT-DERIVATION-FALLBACK-IS-A-CLIFF-SO-ASKING-FOR-MORE-OOS-RETURNS-FAR-FEWER); round 3 after the clamp shipped returned OOS 31 on all three 1d legs from the SAME target-35 dispatch that had returned OOS 4/5/4.

  leg / lever                          verdict        d_net_r IS   d_net_r OOS   base_OOS
  splg_trend_long_1d / trail_decay     is_oos_fail       +7.584        -0.439        31
  iwm_trend_long_1d / trail_decay      is_oos_fail       -1.373        +6.452        31
  scha_trend_long_1d / trail_decay     is_oos_fail       -4.298        +2.399        31
  trend_donchian_eth_prop / stale_stop is_oos_fail       +3.630        -2.678        33
  trend_donchian_eth_prop / trail_decay wf_fail          +1.015        +1.924        34
  ict_scalp_eth_15m / stale_stop        wf_fail          +7.305        +3.845        34

SIX OF SIX FAIL PATH A — and the split inside that is the actual finding, because the count alone misleads. FOUR are `is_oos_fail`: three sign-flip between windows (noise at n~31) and ONE is a clean negative (eth_prop/stale_stop, -2.678 R OOS). TWO are `wf_fail` and POSITIVE ON BOTH WINDOWS, failing only the walk-forward — ict_scalp_eth_15m/stale_stop is the strongest cell in the set (+7.305 IS, +3.845 OOS, drawdown improved on BOTH, base IS=350). Reporting that as 'fails' without saying how would turn evidence that the lever HELPS but does not generalise across folds into evidence against it.

Two comparability caveats, stated rather than smoothed: the three 1d rows come from a CLAMPED target (35 -> 32) while the others used 35 outright, so each row is its own one-leg measurement on its own boundary; and ict_scalp_eth_15m ran UNCAPPED because the scalp unit carries no _TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT — that IS live parity for that leg, but its figures are not comparable to the five capped rows on the cap axis.

Criterion (3) — the disposition — is queued for the operator as Tier-3 decision (i) in docs/sprint-logs/S-M20-TPCAP-PROVENANCE-AND-BLOCK-SIZE-2026-08-13.md. NO status was changed and NO config was touched. Criterion (2) (each cell's ref recording the OFF-arm result) is NOT yet done and is what remains before this row can close.

CRITERION (2) DONE 2026-08-14: all six cells' `ref` now carries the OFF-arm verdict, both windows' d_net_r AND d_max_dd, base_OOS, the split target actually used (including where the clamp reduced it), and the APPLIED geometry. Each annotation also states how its verdict must be read -- a `wf_fail` is positive on both windows, an `is_oos_fail` with flipped signs at n~31 is noise -- because the verdict STRING alone invites the wrong conclusion in both directions. Statuses verified unchanged by histogram before and after (309 honest_negative / 23 shipped / 13 passed_unshipped; live cells 373/376).

WHAT REMAINS: criteria (3) and (4). (3) is the operator's Tier-3 disposition (queued as decision (i)) -- this row does NOT close by me re-grading a live cell. (4) is satisfied structurally: no cell in this set returned `insufficient_base` in the final measurement, but the round-1 rows that did are recorded above as 'we could not grade it', not as a lever verdict.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) A lever-OFF sweep runs over these nine (leg, lever) pairs at live parity (--tp-cap-pct 0.099, --without-declared-lever <lever>) and the rows land in the corpus. (2) Each of the nine cells' `ref` records the OFF-arm result -- the d_net_r_OOS, the verdict, and base_trades_OOS -- so a reader can see whether the shipped lever earns its place, the same way the 22 already-swept pairs do. (3) Any cell whose OFF arm shows the shipped lever is WORSE than its absence is raised to the operator as a Tier-3 disposition question; the row is NOT closed by silently re-grading a live cell. (4) A cell whose OFF arm returns `insufficient_base` is recorded as such -- 'we could not grade it' is a third state and must not read as 'the lever is fine'.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The mechanism the row depends on exists (`--without-declared-lever` and LEVER_DECLARED_KEYS in scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py, with trail_geometry deliberately absent), but the row's criteria are all run-dependent: OFF-arm rows landing in docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl for the six (leg, lever) pairs, and each cell's ref recording d_net_r_OOS / verdict / base_trades_OOS.
