Re-validated: 6 SHIPPED levers with no lever-OFF row. Fourth member of the shipped-on-unsound-evidence family (with BL-20260813-SEVENTEEN-SHIPPED-LEVERS-REST-ON-PRE-TP-PARITY-EVIDENCE, BL-20260813-FIVE-SHIPPED-LEVERS-MEASURED-OOS-NEGATIVE, BL-20260813-SHIPPED-DONCHIAN-1H-HEAD-RESTS-ON-BESTARM). Together those cover most of the live lever set.

items.tier: 1 (correcting the decision RECORD; the live config is already operator-approved and is NOT changed by this)
items.title: 6 coverage-matrix cells say a lever is NOT shipped while config/strategies.yaml arms it on an enabled leg — 5 of them say `honest_negative`, i.e. 'measured, did not work', about a lever running in production
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 by cross-checking every cell status in docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json against LEVER_DECLARED_KEYS resolved from config/strategies.yaml (the same key sets m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py::declared_levers_present uses, imported rather than restated). Population: 52 matrix rows; 51 resolve to a leg in strategies.yaml, 1 is the `shadow fleet (...)` aggregate row that is not a leg.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE POINT. The reverse direction is CLEAN: **0** cells say `shipped` while config does not arm the lever. Every discrepancy runs one way — config arms it, the matrix does not say so:

  avax_pullback_2h        trail_decay  honest_negative    execution: shadow
  eth_pullback_2h         trail_decay  honest_negative    execution: LIVE
  qqq_trend_long_1d       trail_decay  honest_negative    execution: LIVE
  trend_donchian_sol_4h   trail_decay  honest_negative    execution: LIVE
  xrp_pullback_2h         trail_decay  honest_negative    execution: LIVE
  trend_donchian_avax_4h  trail_decay  passed_unshipped   execution: LIVE

All six are `enabled: true` and all six arm trail_decay. Five are `execution: live`.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN A STALE FIELD. `honest_negative` does not read as 'unknown' — it reads as 'we measured this and it did not work'. A session consulting the matrix to decide whether to arm trail_decay on eth_pullback_2h would conclude the question is settled and negative, about a lever that is running on that leg right now. That is worse than a missing row, for the same reason the repo already treats a written-and-never-read provenance field as worse than an absent one: the reader sees a value and assumes it means something.

TWO IDENTIFIED CAUSES, both visible in the refs themselves.
(a) trend_donchian_avax_4h: its ref ends 'AWAITING TIER-3 operator approval to declare in YAML'. The approval LANDED -- PR #8985, 2026-08-13, 'TIER-3: prop legs live, avax trail_decay on' -- and the config now declares exactly the cell that passed (stall_bars 6 / tight_mult 2.5, matching the swept cell `decay_stall6_t2.5`). The declare shipped; the cell was never flipped. Confirmed today independently: the lever-OFF arm named its cell `shipped_trail_decay_6_2.5`, i.e. the sweep itself considers the lever shipped on this leg while the matrix does not.
(b) qqq_trend_long_1d: its ref's FIRST sentence lists qqq under 'FAIL' (the 2026-07-12 fleet sweep), and a LATER sentence in the SAME ref records 'qqq p80 arm 3.56R PASS 5/6' plus 'RECONCILED 2026-07-14 ... cell flipped passed_unshipped -> shipped'. Config declares `trail_decay_arm_r: 3.56` -- the p80 arm exactly. The status field kept the first sentence. This row was produced by the BL-20260809-COVERAGE-MATRIX-MULTILEG-ROW-ONE-STATUS explosion of the bundled 'equities 1d fleet (...)' row, whose stated rule was 'per-leg status from this ref's explicit wording only' -- and the ref's explicit wording says BOTH things.

SCOPE, STATED: this is a defect in the RECORD, not evidence that any live lever is wrong. Every one of the six declares is operator-approved Tier-3 work that landed through a normal PR (#8746 2026-08-11, #8985 2026-08-13). Nothing here proposes changing config. The fix is to make the matrix say what the field says, and to stop the two drifting again.

THE MATRIX'S OWN LEGEND ALREADY NAMES THIS BUG, AND DEFINES THE STATUS TO FIX IT — WHICH IS USED ZERO TIMES (found 2026-08-14 while checking for a documented convention). `legend.shipped_gate_failed` reads verbatim: *"LIVE in config, but a LATER re-sweep failed its gate and the operator chose to HOLD ... Deliberately distinct from both neighbours: `honest_negative` implies NOT live (recording a live lever there is exactly the bug that made trend_donchian's trail_decay read as a closed negative), and `shipped` asserts 'validated + live' which overclaims once the validation no longer reproduces."* Measured: `shipped_gate_failed` appears **0 times** across all 416 cells.

THAT CHANGES THE REMEDY, and makes it more precise than 'flip them to shipped'. Five of the six are live legs whose recorded evidence is a NEGATIVE — which is the `shipped_gate_failed` case by the legend's own definition, PROVIDED the operator's intent was to hold. The sixth, `trend_donchian_avax_4h`, is different: its gate PASSED and the declare landed in #8985, so it is a plain `shipped`. Flipping all six to `shipped` would assert 'validated + live' over five cells whose validation does not currently reproduce — the exact overclaim the legend warns against. So the disposition is genuinely the operator's: it turns on whether each was a deliberate hold.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) Each of the six cells' status is reconciled against config/strategies.yaml and its ref records WHICH evidence supports the shipped value -- with the reconciliation dated and attributed, not silently overwritten. (2) A cell whose supporting evidence is pre-2026-08-10 no-take-profit keeps its tp_geometry marker: flipping the status to `shipped` records that the lever IS shipped, and must NOT be read as the lever having been re-graded at live parity. These are two different claims and the row must not merge them. (3) A CI guard asserts the invariant this finding used -- for every (leg, lever) where config arms the lever on a leg present in strategies.yaml, the matrix cell reads `shipped`; and the reverse. The guard must carry a planted-disagreement self-test, since a guard that has only ever been seen green is a guard whose green is unproven. (4) The guard's failure message names the leg, the lever, the matrix status and the config keys, so a future session does not have to re-derive the cross-check to act on it.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: scripts/ci/check_matrix_config_agreement.py exists, is registered as `matrix-config-agreement` in scripts/ci/run_guards.py, carries the planted-disagreement self-test path and a failure message naming leg/lever/status/config keys, and treats both `shipped` and `shipped_gate_failed` as armed (ARMED_STATUSES). Running it now: '52 matrix rows, 51 resolved to a leg …; 4 offerable levers checked. OK — every matrix cell agrees with config on shipped-ness'. The six cells were reconciled (its docstring records trend_donchian_avax_4h -> shipped and the other five -> shipped_gate_failed).

items.tier: 1 (research harness; no live path, no order path)
items.title: resolve_split falls back to a FIXED CALENDAR DATE when the leg cannot support the target — so raising --split-target-oos can cut the achieved OOS window from 24 to 4
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 on two back-to-back dispatches of the SAME six (leg, lever) pairs, same geometry (tp_cap_pct 0.099), same mode (oos-trades), differing only in --split-target-oos.

  leg                      target 25 (default)   target 35
  iwm_trend_long_1d        IS 39 / OOS 24        IS 60 / OOS  4   <-- THIN
  scha_trend_long_1d       IS 40 / OOS 23        IS 60 / OOS  5   <-- THIN
  splg_trend_long_1d       IS 40 / OOS 24        IS 61 / OOS  4   <-- THIN
  trend_donchian_eth_prop  IS 918 / OOS 24       IS 909 / OOS 33  <-- helped

ASKING FOR MORE OOS TRADES RETURNED SIX TIMES FEWER on three of the four legs. That is not a degradation, it is a CLIFF, and it is in the code by construction (`m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py::resolve_split`):

    if len(stamps) < 2 * target_oos:
        meta.update(split=fixed_split, split_fallback='leg_too_thin')
        return fixed_split, meta

The guard's REASONING is sound -- a leg that cannot give both windows `target_oos` trades is genuinely thin, and the docstring says so. What is wrong is the DESTINATION. When the derivation gives up it returns the corpus-standard CALENDAR date (2025-07-01), which has no relationship to this leg's trade distribution -- and for exactly the low-frequency legs that trip the guard, that date is the worst available boundary. These legs trade ~20x/year; the fixed date buys them 4-5 OOS trades, which is what the derivation was introduced to fix in the first place. So the fallback lands the caller back on the defect the feature exists to remove, and does it precisely when the caller asked for MORE rigour.

THE GRADEABLE BAND IS NARROW AND UNDOCUMENTED. Two conditions must hold at once: lifetime >= 2*target (or the cliff fires), AND the ACHIEVED count >= MIN_OOS_TRADES=25 (or the verdict is refused). The achieved count runs ~1-2 below target because the harness windows CANDLES, not trades -- the docstring states this correctly and it is not a bug. For a ~64-trade leg that leaves target in roughly [26, 32]: the default 25 achieves 23-24 and misses the floor by one or two, and 35 falls off the cliff. Nothing tells a caller this band exists; both failure modes print an `insufficient_base`-shaped outcome, and the cliff case additionally prints a THIN OOS warning that reads as a property of the LEG rather than of the boundary the tool chose.

RELATIONSHIP TO THE SIBLING ROW. BL-20260814-SPLIT-TARGETS-EXACTLY-THE-FLOOR-SO-BOUNDARY-LOSS-ALWAYS-FAILS covers the DEFAULT aiming at exactly the floor. This row covers what happens when you try to fix that by raising the target. They must be resolved together: the obvious remedy for one triggers the other. In particular the previously-proposed `max(derived, fixed_window)` shape is REFUTED by this measurement -- here the fixed window is the BAD one, so a max would select it.

CRITERIA (1)(2)(3) IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-14 (same session, uncommitted->pushed on claude/m20-exit-coverage-matrix-8d3he7). `resolve_split` now clamps an unreachable target to `lifetime // 2` and keeps deriving from the leg's own trades, recording `split_target_clamped_from`/`_to`; `split_target_oos` keeps its REQUESTED-value meaning so existing consumers are unchanged. The fixed-date fallback survives only for a leg that cannot seat MIN_OOS_TRADES on both sides. Four states stay distinguishable: derived-as-asked / derived-clamped / `leg_too_thin` / {`harness_rc`,`emit_unreadable`} (= we could not look, which is NOT thinness).

The tests were verified against origin/main's copy rather than assumed: on a synthetic 64-trade leg the pre-fix function returns target 32 -> 2002-09-15 and target 35 -> 2025-07-01, so one trade of extra ambition moved the boundary TWENTY-THREE YEARS forward. The monotonicity and clamp assertions FAIL there and pass on the fix.

CRITERION (4) REMAINS OPEN: `insufficient_base_reason` still does not distinguish 'this leg is thin' from 'the boundary this tool chose is thin'. The clamp makes the second case rarer; it does not make the message correct, and the two still have opposite remedies (wait for trades vs re-run with a different target). Do not close this row on (1)-(3).

CRITERION (4) DONE 2026-08-14, so ALL FOUR criteria are now met and this row is ready to close on review. `insufficient_base_reason` no longer merely SUPPLIES the discriminator, it states the diagnosis: `THE LEG IS TRADE-STARVED` (lifetime < 2*floor -- re-running returns this again, wait for trades) vs `THE BOUNDARY IS MISPLACED, NOT THE LEG` (the lifetime could seat a floor-clearing window and this split did not -- re-run with a larger --split-target-oos). A THIRD state, `UNDIAGNOSED`, covers split_mode=date, where no emit ran so the lifetime was never counted and NEITHER diagnosis is supportable -- it does not default to one. A clamped target is named in the refusal too, since a message quoting only the requested target describes a run that never happened. Tests pin the 2*floor boundary exactly (49 vs 50 at floor 25), because an off-by-one there silently relabels a starved leg as a fixable one and sends the next session re-running a sweep that cannot succeed.

STATUS NOTE: `fix_landed_monitoring`, not `resolved` -- the four criteria are met and the clamp is live-verified (the identical target-35 dispatch that returned OOS 4/5/4 now returns 31/31/31), but the change is still on an unmerged PR. An existing status value was chosen deliberately over minting a new one: this backlog already carries 20 distinct status strings across 548 rows, several of them one-offs, and a 21st spelling of 'nearly done' makes the field harder to query, not more precise.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) When a leg cannot support the requested target, the derivation CLAMPS the target to the largest value the leg can support (floor(lifetime/2)) and derives a boundary from the leg's own trades, instead of returning a calendar date unrelated to them. The fixed-date fallback is kept ONLY for the genuinely ungradeable case -- a leg that cannot support even MIN_OOS_TRADES on both sides -- and for the harness-error paths (`harness_rc`, `emit_unreadable`), which are 'we could not look' and must stay distinguishable from 'we looked and the leg is thin'. (2) The clamp is RECORDED in the row's split meta (e.g. `split_target_clamped_from`/`_to`), so a verdict never silently reports a target it did not use -- the same discipline the split-provenance work already applies to mode and fallback. (3) A test drives the three outcomes apart on synthetic trade stamps: derived at the requested target, derived at a CLAMPED target, and the genuine fixed-date fallback -- asserting the achieved OOS under a clamp is never smaller than what the fixed date would have produced, which is the specific regression measured here. (4) The refusal message distinguishes 'this leg is thin' from 'the boundary this tool chose is thin', since those have opposite remedies (wait for trades vs re-run) and currently print the same shape.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:1025-1033 now clamps instead of falling off the cliff: `supportable = len(stamps) // 2`; if that clears MIN_OOS_TRADES it records `split_target_clamped_from`/`_to` and derives from the leg's own trades, and only a leg that cannot seat the floor on both sides returns the fixed calendar date with `split_fallback='leg_too_thin'`. The clamp is surfaced in the refusal/summary text (:1145-1147) and tests/test_m20_split_clamp.py + tests/test_m20_split_provenance.py cover it (they are the only files referencing split_target_clamped).

items.title: tp_geometry is set on 10 of 416 coverage cells (2.4%) and documented in neither _doc nor legend — the field that exists to stop one specific wrong inference cannot stop it
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 over docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json: 416 cells carry a status; **406 (97.6%) have no `tp_geometry` at all**. Only 10 are marked — 5 `live_parity`, 5 `no_take_profit`. Of the 23 `shipped` cells, just 7 record their geometry (4 no_take_profit, 3 live_parity); the other 16 are silent.

WHY THE FIELD EXISTS. BL-20260810-BACKTEST-DOES-NOT-MODEL-THE-LIVE-CAPPED-TP established that production places `tp = min(entry*1.099, entry + tp_r*risk)` while the harnesses modelled NO take-profit — so **every pre-2026-08-10 verdict was measured on a book production does not run**. `tp_geometry` is the field that says which geometry produced a verdict. That is its whole job.

THE COLLAPSE. With 97.6% absent, three different conditions share one value: (a) measured at live parity and nobody stamped it; (b) measured on the pre-cutover no-TP geometry, which is the DEFAULT EXPECTATION for anything dated before 2026-08-10; and (c) nobody looked. A reader cannot tell them apart, and the reassuring reading — 'no marker, so presumably fine' — is the one the originating backlog row says is wrong for most of the population. This is the canonical collapsed-state shape (docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md § 'Collapsed states'): the field cannot say 'we did not look'.

AND IT IS UNDOCUMENTED. `tp_geometry` appears in NEITHER the matrix's `_doc` string NOR its `legend` block — both of which carefully define every status value. So there is no stated convention for what absence means, which is why absence has accumulated: a field with no documented semantics is a field nobody is obliged to fill.

NOT A CLAIM THAT 406 VERDICTS ARE WRONG. Many will have been measured at live parity — the M20 re-sweeps did exactly that. The claim is narrower and worse: **it is not currently possible to tell which**, and the matrix is the artifact the milestone's done-condition is read from.

CRITERION (4) DONE 2026-08-14: the roll-up now prints recorded/total with `unrecorded` COUNTED, over the LIVE population so the denominator matches the headline's. Reading: 10/376 = 2.7% live-only, which is the same 10 cells as the 10/416 = 2.4% quoted above over ALL rows -- two populations, both correct, and both stated so the pair cannot read as a contradiction.

PRINTING IT IMMEDIATELY EXPOSED A SECOND DEFECT in the same banner: it asserted 'Base rate so far is 1 of 1: trend_donchian trail_decay ... did NOT reproduce (now shipped_gate_failed)'. Both halves are false today -- that cell is `shipped`, `shipped_gate_failed` appears zero times, and the lever PASSES (the 2026-08-12 non-reproduction was measured by a sweep grading the base against itself). Replaced with a pointer to the corpus rather than a fresher number, since a rate baked into printed text is a claim nothing re-derives.

REMAINING: criteria (1), (2) and (3) -- defining `tp_geometry` in the legend with an explicit name for absence, stamping the cells, and the guard that keeps a new cell from being added silent. The roll-up now makes the gap VISIBLE on every run, which is what makes the rest worth doing rather than a cleanup nobody sees.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) `tp_geometry` is DEFINED in the matrix's `legend` alongside the status values, including what an ABSENT value means — and absence must be given an explicit name (e.g. `unrecorded`) rather than left as null, so 'we did not look' is sayable. (2) Cells whose evidence post-dates the 2026-08-10 cutover AND whose ref names a live-parity run are stamped `live_parity`; cells whose ref predates it are stamped `no_take_profit`. Where the ref does not establish either, the cell is stamped `unrecorded` — NOT guessed from the date alone, since a date is a proxy and this row exists because a proxy was trusted. (3) A guard asserts that every cell carries one of the defined values, so a new cell cannot be added silent. It must ship with a planted-omission self-test. (4) The roll-up reports geometry coverage as a fraction the way `rCoverage`/`pnlCoverage` do, so a reader sees the denominator instead of inferring completeness from the marked cells.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Coverage has improved a lot — counted over the current matrix: 167 live_parity + 3 no_take_profit vs 246 absent (the rollup prints 166/376 = 44.1% recorded, 210 unrecorded) — and criterion (4) is met by `geometry_coverage()` (m20_coverage_rollup.py:1077-1102, reported with its denominator). Criteria (1) and (3) are not: the matrix `legend` block holds only the 7 status values (no tp_geometry entry, and `'tp_geometry' in _doc` is False), so absence still has no explicit name, and no guard requires every cell to carry one of the defined values. — Ends when the legend defines tp_geometry incl. an explicit `unrecorded`, and a guard (with a planted-omission self-test) rejects a silent cell.

updates.what: THREE OF THE FOUR CRITERIA ARE NOW MET. Recorded here so the next session reads the row's remaining scope instead of re-deriving it — the row's next_action was None while three quarters of it had quietly been done.
updates.criterion_1_DONE: `tp_geometry` is defined in the matrix, with absence explicitly named. Shipped in cb8bc5a2 (#9801) as the top-level `tp_geometry_legend` block: `_field`, `_why_it_exists`, `live_parity`, `no_take_profit`, and `ABSENT_means_unrecorded`. ⚠️ It is a TOP-LEVEL key, NOT inside `legend` — a probe looking in `legend` returns a confident false negative, which is exactly what mine did before I checked the denominator.
updates.criterion_2_OPEN: Stamping the cells is NOT done and is the whole remaining scope. 210 of 376 live cells carry no value. It must not be guessed from dates — that is the proxy-trusting error this row exists for.
updates.criterion_3_DONE: A guard now asserts it, with the planted-omission self-test the criterion demands. `m20_coverage_rollup._validate_tp_geometry`, run by the existing `exit-coverage-matrix-guard` (`--check`), does two things: every PRESENT value must be a legend value, and the unstamped count may not GROW against `tp_geometry_legend._unstamped_ceiling` (210, measured). The ratchet is what makes the criterion enforceable TODAY — an 'every cell must be stamped' assertion would fail on the current file and could only ship switched off, and a guard nobody can turn on is worth less than no guard. `tests/test_m20_tp_geometry_guard.py`: 8 tests, including un-stamping a cell, a null stamp, an invented value, a missing ceiling, and an unreadable legend — the last two asserting 'unchecked' rather than 'clean'. It also pins that STAMPING a cell does not fail the ratchet, so the guard cannot punish progress.
updates.criterion_4_DONE: The roll-up already reports geometry coverage as a fraction with its denominator, the rCoverage/pnlCoverage way: `recorded: 166/376 = 44.1%   unrecorded: 210`.
updates.denominators_differ_deliberately: The guard and ceiling count LIVE cells (376); `tp_geometry_legend._coverage_2026_08_16` counts ALL cells (416). Both are correct and neither should be 'harmonised' — state which population before quoting either.
updates.still_kept_open: Criterion (2) alone. Do not close this row on the guard: the ratchet bounds a known-bad population, it does not shrink it, and a passing ratchet is NOT evidence that geometry coverage is fine.

updates.note: Re-validated: a field set on 10 of 416 cells (2.4%) cannot make absence meaningful — the collapsed-state shape applied to a matrix column.

measured_again_2026_08_16.headline_is_17x_stale: The title still says 'set on 10 of 416 coverage cells (2.4%)'. MEASURED 2026-08-16 directly off docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json: 170 of 416 = 40.9% carry a value (live_parity 167, no_take_profit 3, absent 246). SAME denominator as the original count, so the two are directly comparable — a 17x improvement since 2026-08-14. The row is still correctly OPEN, but a reader acting on '2.4%' would badly misjudge how much work remains, which is why this is recorded rather than left to the title.
measured_again_2026_08_16.note_on_no_take_profit_going_DOWN: no_take_profit fell 5 -> 3 over the same period. Not a regression: cells re-swept at live parity flip from no_take_profit to live_parity. Recorded because a shrinking count in a coverage row invites the opposite reading.
measured_again_2026_08_16.criterion_1_HALF_DONE_2026_08_16: The DEFINITION half is done: a `tp_geometry_legend` block now sits beside the status `legend` in the matrix, naming live_parity / no_take_profit and stating explicitly that ABSENT means 'we did not look', with the three conditions absence collapses. This is the prerequisite this row's own detail identifies — 'a field with no documented semantics is a field nobody is obliged to fill'. The STAMPING half of (1)/(2) is NOT done.
measured_again_2026_08_16.why_the_stamping_was_deliberately_NOT_do: Criterion (2) requires each cell's own `ref` to establish live_parity or no_take_profit, with `unrecorded` stamped only where the ref establishes neither. Blanket-stamping `unrecorded` across the 246 absent cells would be FASTER and WORSE: many carry refs that plainly name a live-parity re-sweep, so it would record 'we did not look' about cells whose evidence does establish the geometry — entrenching a wrong value behind a field that now reads as authoritative. A date must not be used as the proxy either; this row exists because a proxy was trusted.
measured_again_2026_08_16.consumer_safety_ALREADY_CHECKED_do_not_r: Both consumers in m20_coverage_rollup.py tolerate a stamped 'unrecorded' string, so the stamping pass does not need a coordinated code change: (a) the stale-grader branches on geom == GEOMETRY_NO_TP / == GEOMETRY_LIVE_PARITY and otherwise falls to an `else` that grades by the date proxy — a stamped string lands in the same branch as None; and (b) geometry_coverage counts counts['unrecorded' if geom is None else str(geom)], whose null-bucket literal is ALREADY the string 'unrecorded', so a stamp merges into that bucket rather than falsely reporting 100% coverage. Checked because the obvious risk of stamping is that it silently satisfies the very metric that exists to measure the gap. It does not.

items.title: IB candle fetches ran on TWO threads after the M20 exit-loop decouple — 'This event loop is already running' -> liveness-probe timeouts -> circuit breaker -> candles_unavailable / MONITOR BLIND / sizing_failed
items.detail:
LIVE, MEASURED 2026-08-14. ib_insync's cached IB binds its socket transport to ONE asyncio loop; IBClient._ensure_event_loop's own docstring says 'dispatching a request on a different loop would hang instead of returning bars', and src/web/api/routers/candles.py pins the web-api's IB access to a max_workers=1 pool it annotates 'load-bearing: ... every IB request must run on that same thread'.

The trader had no such pin and did not need one until the M20 exit-loop decouple (2026-08-12, docs/sprint-logs/S-M20-EXIT-LOOP-DECOUPLE-2026-08-12.md): exit evaluation ran INLINE on the tick thread, so the process had exactly one IB caller by construction. The decouple moved it to the 'exit-evaluation-loop' daemon thread, which calls _build_monitor_ohlcv_fetcher -> IBMarketData.get_ohlcv every ~30s for open MGC/MES packages while the main tick does the same for signal_build. Both resolve the SAME client (get_ib_client caches per host/port/client_id) and IBClient._usage_lock covers connect() but NOT _ensure_event_loop()/reqHistoricalData().

EVIDENCE (trader journal, live VM):
  2026-08-14T09:46:16Z IBMarketData.get_ohlcv failed for symbol=MES timeframe=5m: This event loop is already running
  2026-08-14T09:46:05Z IBClient: liveness probe attempt 1/2 timed out after 5s for 10.0.0.251:4002
  2026-08-14T10:32:47Z IBClient: circuit breaker OPEN ... retrying in 104s
/api/diag/ib_state showed all three clients state=connected, breaker_open=false, consecutive_failures=0 with last_fail_reason=liveness_probe_timeout — i.e. the breaker FLAPS rather than sticking, which is why snapshot-based checks read healthy.

CONTROL (this is what rules out a gateway fault): /api/bot/candles returned live MGC 15m, MES 1d and MHG 1h bars from the WEB-API process at the same moment the trader could not fetch them. The web-api serialises IB access; the trader did not.

BLAST RADIUS is wider than the racing fetch, because the breaker suppresses ALL IB calls for IB_BREAKER_COOLDOWN_S (120s): (a) MONITOR BLIND on pkg-dbcc140fd43c4a79 (ict_scalp_mgc_15m/MGC) and pkg-1d9598b29f38440c (mes_trend_long_1d/MES); (b) strategy_builder RuntimeErrors for MGC 15m, MES 1d, MHG 1d; (c) NEW ENTRIES REFUSED — trades 4637 and 4615 carry 'sizing_failed: RuntimeError: balance() returned None for ib_paper ... account unreachable'. Scope is IB-only (ib_paper, paper money; ib_live is dry) — no real money was exposed.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. MITIGATED 2026-08-14T11:46Z: EXIT_LOOP_DECOUPLE_DISABLED=1 via set-env (issue #9233), ict-trader-live.service restarted, state active — the sanctioned CLAUDE.md rollback, restoring single-threaded IB access at the cost of the M20 30s exit cadence.
2. FIX: pin every IBMarketData.get_ohlcv to one dedicated thread (module-level max_workers=1 executor + re-entrancy guard), mirroring candles._FETCH_EXECUTOR. A LOCK ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT — serialising still lets a second thread drive a loop it did not create, which is the documented hang.
3. Regression guard tests/test_ib_marketdata_thread_pinning.py — VERIFIED to fail pre-fix (2 of 4 fail: distinct fetch threads ['caller-0','caller-1']; peak occupancy > 1) and pass post-fix.
4. CLOSE only after the fix deploys AND EXIT_LOOP_DECOUPLE_DISABLED is cleared AND a warm /api/diag/tick_cost + journal read shows zero 'event loop is already running' and zero liveness_probe_timeout breaker trips over a multi-hour window with the decouple re-enabled.

3. FIX MERGED + DEPLOYED 2026-08-14. PR #9240 squash-merged to main 13:05:25Z (4/4 checks green on 18fd7c94); deployed via pull-and-deploy #9272 at 13:07:42Z, live HEAD 2091d57f -> adbe19a7, ict-trader-live.service restarted active.
4. MITIGATION CLEARED. set-env #9273 wrote EXIT_LOOP_DECOUPLE_DISABLED=0 at 13:11:02Z with a restart. Verified AUTHORITATIVE via get-env #9274 reading /proc/<MainPID>/environ: process '0', declared '0' -- not merely written to .env. 0 is falsy to _truthy, so the M20 decouple is ON, confirmed independently by the trader's own boot line 'exit-evaluation loop DECOUPLED onto its own thread' at 13:11:09Z.
5. POST-RESTART VERIFICATION (diag #9275/#9276/#9277/#9278), all three pre-registered criteria met:
   (a) ZERO 'This event loop is already running' in the post-restart journal. COVERAGE STATED: the relay truncated at its 55KB budget, so the window actually read is 13:11:10Z-13:12:55Z = 105 seconds, NOT the full window. Positive control: 'liveness probe' matched 14 times in the same text, so the probe demonstrably finds IB lines -- the zero is a measured absence over a stated denominator, not an unexercised search.
   (b) exit_loop_health state=fresh with a RISING pass count (1 -> 4).
   (c) tick_cost offloop_hooks POPULATED -- monitor.strategy_monitor_loop n=5, fetchby.strategy_monitor_loop n=62 -- on a payload whose process_started_utc (13:11:09.875) matches the NEW process. This check nearly went wrong: the first tick_cost pull carried process_started_utc 13:07:48 with age_seconds 234.5, i.e. the PREVIOUS mitigated process, whose offloop_hooks was correctly {} because the decouple was off. Reading that empty block as a failure of the fix would have been a false negative; always match process_started_utc to the restart before grading this field.
   Also confirmed: IB reconnected cleanly post-restart with MGC and MES positions syncing, and /api/diag/ib_state shows all three clients connected, breaker_open=false, consecutive_failures=0.
6. SCOPE OF THIS RESOLUTION -- the OBSERVED defect is fixed and verified; the CLASS was not fully closed by #9240 alone. Auditing my own fix in the same session found that the pin serialises market-data against market-data but NOT against the lock-held account/order surface, leaving the same condition reachable from the other side. Filed and fixed in the follow-up as BL-20260814-IB-MARKETDATA-VS-ACCOUNT-LOCK-GAP. Two measurements taken during verification are also filed rather than left in chat: BL-20260814-IB-LIVENESS-PROBE-TIMES-OUT-EVERY-CONNECT and BL-20260814-EXIT-PASS-SLOWER-THAN-M20 (the latter explicitly NOT to be quoted as a regression until re-measured warm -- it is n=5 passes on a 3-minute-old process).

items.tier: 2 (broker-naked re-arm path; detection change is Tier-1, the re-arm behaviour change is Tier-2)
items.title: Why the MGC take-profit never fired: IB protective-leg DETECTION is account-wide+boolean while CANCELLATION is session-scoped+symbol-wide - no trade owns its bracket, and nothing can verify one exists
items.detail:
INVESTIGATED 2026-08-14 (operator asked specifically: why did the TP never fire). Trade 4487 / pkg-dbcc140fd43c4a79, ict_scalp_mgc_15m, ib_paper, MGC long 105 @ 4272.4, TP 4297.65785714.

WHAT THE JOURNAL PROVES:
  * order_packages.exit_plan stop.price = 4255.56142857 (BELOW entry, correct for a long) but trades.stop_loss and order_packages.sl are BOTH 4278.8086 - ABOVE entry. 4278.8086 - 4272.4 = 6.4086 = 15 bps of entry, i.e. the monitor_breakeven_sl ratchet fired at be_offset_bps=15. The monitor WAS working.
  * order_packages.updated_at = 2026-08-07T04:13:28Z and has NOT changed since - 7 days. That is the last re-arm.
  * exit_plan_state targets: [{kind: final, price 4297.65785714, reach_r 1.5}] - the TP was declared at 1.5R.
  * execution_delta: current_qty 0.0 -> target_qty 105.0, 'open_new_long_target=105.0' - 105 contracts was a SINGLE entry, NOT an accumulation of many scalps. (Separate question: a 15m scalp sizing 105 MGC contracts is risk_per_unit 16.84 x 105 x multiplier 10 = ~$17.7k of risk.)
  * sl_order_id / tp_order_id are NULL, but those columns are written ONLY on the Bybit partial-TPSL branch, so NULL is expected on IB and is NOT evidence either way.

THE MECHANISM (code, verified this session):
  1. ict_scalp.monitor() has exactly TWO verdict paths - the default-OFF M20 stale-stop and monitor_breakeven_sl, which its own docstring says 'only ever returns a break-even SL-modify (no close path)'. THERE IS NO TAKE-PROFIT CLOSE PATH IN monitor() AT ALL. TP enforcement is 100% the broker bracket's job. So 'candles=200 verdict=None' in the journal is CORRECT behaviour, not the bug - and monitor blindness (BL-20260814-IB-EVENTLOOP-CONTENTION) is NOT the cause: the TP was blown through on 2026-08-07, five days before that contention began.
  2. Every IB re-arm path (modify_protective from the ratchet, _attempt_naked_autoprotect, _rearm_broker_protection_after_recovery) funnels into place_protective, which FIRST calls _cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol(ib, sym) and then arms a fresh OCA pair carrying only the CALLING trade's levels.
  3. That pre-cancel matches on contract.symbol ONLY - the generic root 'MGC'. It has no notion of which trade or strategy a leg belongs to. THREE strategies trade MGC on ib_paper (ict_scalp_mgc_15m, mgc_trend_1h, mgc_pullback_1d) and they share one cached IBClient per account, so any one of them re-arming cancels the others' protective legs and replaces them with a bracket carrying only its own SL/TP. A sibling strategy's re-arm silently strips this trade's TP.
  4. Nothing then restores it. _check_broker_naked_ib_positions asks has_protective_orders(symbol='MGC'), which is ACCOUNT-WIDE (reqAllOpenOrders) and returns True on the FIRST resting STP/LMT it finds for the symbol - so any sibling strategy's leg makes trade 4487 read 'protected'. And the journal-driven _check_naked_positions only flags rows whose JOURNAL sl/tp is missing; 4487's are populated, so it is invisible there too. Every detection path is blind.

THE STRUCTURAL DEFECT - DETECTION AND CANCELLATION USE DIFFERENT SCOPES:
  * has_protective_orders -> ib.reqAllOpenOrders() = ACCOUNT-WIDE (deliberate: IB order visibility is per-client-session, so openTrades() alone would false-read naked - BL-20260709)
  * _cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol -> ib.openTrades() = THIS SESSION ONLY
Consequences run both ways: (a) after any trader restart the GTC legs placed in a previous session are invisible to openTrades(), so the pre-cancel silently no-ops and place_protective STACKS a second live OCA - the very OCA accumulation the pre-cancel exists to prevent (the 2026-06-24 MHG flip incident, tagged in order_monitor.py comments); and (b) the account-wide boolean means 'protected' can never be attributed to a TRADE, only to a SYMBOL. Protection is per-symbol in a world where the journal is per-trade.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, AND WHY: whether a TP leg for trade 4487 rests on IB right now. THERE IS NO READ SURFACE FOR IB OPEN ORDERS - /api/diag/broker_account_status covers Alpaca and Bybit only, and /api/diag/exchange_positions returns POSITIONS, never orders. That absence is itself a first-class finding (see BL-20260814-NO-IB-OPEN-ORDERS-READ-SURFACE): IB exit coverage cannot be verified from a session at all, which is precisely why this sat unnoticed for 7 days while three separate alarms fired about adjacent symptoms. NARROWED 2026-08-23 by the full-system audit: criteria 1 and 3 are MET and criterion 5 is RESOLVED by the operator's close-out rule, leaving 3 of 6 open. REMAINING: 2 (trade-attributable OCA groups, so place_protective cancels only the CALLING trade's legs), 4 (the detection/cancellation scope asymmetry — both read reqAllOpenOrders, or the difference documented WITH its restart-stacking consequence), and 6 (the regression test: two open trades on one symbol from different strategies, where re-arming one must not remove the other's legs, and which must be shown to FAIL against the symbol-scoped implementation before it is fixed).
items.resolution_criteria:
1. [MET 2026-08-16, verified live 2026-08-23 — /api/diag/ib_open_orders returned read_state='orders_read' with 4 resting ib_paper legs and read_state='could_not_look' with count=null for ib_live, the three-state contract behaving as designed] ADD AN IB OPEN-ORDERS READ SURFACE FIRST (Tier-1, no order path). Without it none of the fixes below can be verified and the next occurrence is equally invisible. Safe to ship alone.
2. Make protection TRADE-attributable, not symbol-attributable: persist the placed OCA group + leg ids onto the trade row (the columns already exist for Bybit) and have place_protective cancel only the CALLING trade's own legs.
3. [MET 2026-08-16 — protection_coverage returns stop_qty and target_qty SEPARATELY beside the back-compat covered_qty, classifying each leg through _protective_leg_side with the STOP family tested FIRST so a 'STP LMT' cannot manufacture target coverage; has_protective_orders keeps the combined test deliberately, that being its own question, and its docstring now forbids naked-detection use] Make has_protective_orders return COVERED QUANTITY (or None when unconfirmable) instead of a boolean and compare to the exchange position size - the PR #8000 Bybit shape. Skip rather than guess when coverage is ungradeable.
4. Reconcile the detection/cancellation scope asymmetry explicitly: both read reqAllOpenOrders, or document the difference as intentional WITH the restart-stacking consequence stated.
5. [RESOLVED 2026-08-23, was HELD — the operator's rule ('if the trade has already passed where its brackets should have been since it opened, close it out') disposes it: MGC's declared target 4393.02071429 was passed by 233.88+ points, so the position is scheduled to be FLATTENED by the 2026-08-23T22:30Z Routine. NOTE the live position is MGC trade 4773 at 95 lots, while this row was filed against a 105-lot position — confirm the id before acting rather than assuming they are the same trade] Tier-3 / operator: disposition of the 105-lot MGC position, which separately blocks every mgc_trend_1h signal via flip_suppressed_hold_policy. HELD pending operator decision (2026-08-14: investigate + report, do not touch).
6. Regression test: two open trades on one symbol from different strategies; re-arming one must not remove the other's legs. Confirm it FAILS against the current symbol-scoped implementation.

updates.note:
Resolution criteria 2, 3 and 4 SHIPPED and live-verified via PR #9331 (Tier-3, operator-approved in-conversation) + PR #9342 (observability). Criterion 1 (IB open-orders read surface) remains open as BL-20260814-NO-IB-OPEN-ORDERS-READ-SURFACE. Criterion 5 (disposition of the 105-lot MGC position) is Tier-3 and stays with the operator.

WHAT SHIPPED:
  * IBClient.protection_coverage(symbol) returns {size, covered_qty, legs, unknown_qty_legs, oca_groups, source} or None - the PR #8000 Bybit shape. Denominator from _req_positions_snapshot, numerator from the account-wide _req_all_open_orders. Legs sharing an OCA group count ONCE (max, not sum): a group's STOP and LIMIT protect the same qty, so summing both double-counts. has_protective_orders is kept unchanged and documented as the LOSSY view (7 existing tests + Alpaca parity read it).
  * place_protective takes an oca_key and pre-cancels only THAT trade's deterministic group (oca-protect-t<trade_id>) via the new _cancel_oca_group_for_symbol. A deterministic per-trade group cannot stack with itself, so the anti-stacking property survives (a re-arm cannot pile a second bracket on top of an existing one) while the blast radius stops at the calling trade. _cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol is deliberately UNCHANGED - close() and cancel_resting_protection legitimately want cancel-all.
  * The sweep compares covered_qty to size with a 0.5-contract epsilon and refuses to guess when any leg qty is unparseable (ungradeable), matching the Bybit sweep's refusal.
  * Both live paths into place_protective pass oca_key: _attempt_naked_autoprotect directly, and _rearm_broker_protection_after_recovery through it. IBClient.replace_protective has ZERO callers repo-wide, so the legacy symbol-wide pre-cancel branch is defensive-only, not a residual gap (verified by grep this session, not assumed).

LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-08-14T19:28:34.849Z on the live trader (PID 2065168, HEAD 6f75bfe). The coverage sweep emitted, in full:
  _check_broker_naked_ib_positions: swept 2 open IB position(s) - covered=2 naked=0 partially_naked=0 rearmed=0 read_failed=0 ungradeable=0 errors=0
Immediately preceded (19:28:34.764 / .805) by the ib_insync position reads the denominator comes from - MGC 105.0 and MES 15.0 - so protection_coverage ran its real path, not a degraded fallback.

ungradeable=0 is the field that mattered: the pre-deploy risk was that live ib_insync order objects would not expose a parseable qty the way the test stubs did, which would have made IBClient._protective_leg_qty return None for every leg and the sweep skip forever (fail-safe, but inert). They do expose it. read_failed=0 likewise rules out the breaker-open path that made the first post-restart verification attempts silent.

WHAT THIS READ DOES *NOT* PROVE, stated so it is not over-claimed: covered=2 cannot discriminate 'counted MGC's OCA pair once as 105' from 'double-counted it as 210' - both clear covered >= size - 0.5. The OCA max-dedup is proven by tests/test_ib_protection_quantity.py::test_oca_pair_counts_once_not_twice, not by this line. A live discrimination needs a partially-covered position, which is exactly the state the fix exists to prevent.

Cost, from /api/diag/tick_cost (same process, ticks_measured=5): monitor.check_broker_naked_ib_positions n=5 mean 3627.8ms max 6836.8ms, 2.8% of tick - the account-wide reqAllOpenOrders read stays inside the cadence-gated budget it was designed for (BL-20260609 pacing class).

[sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Criteria 2/3/4 and 6 are in the tree: src/units/accounts/ib_client.py:1865 defines `protection_coverage(symbol)` (quantity, not boolean), place_protective takes an `oca_key` and builds the deterministic per-trade group `oca-protect-t<key>` (:1362-1376), and tests/test_ib_protection_quantity.py covers partial coverage, OCA pair counted once, unparseable leg qty, read-failure -> None, plus the sibling-bracket regression (test_rearm_keeps_sibling_take_profit, test_rearm_replaces_its_own_group). Criterion 1 is closed by the now-shipped /api/diag/ib_open_orders. Criterion 5 — the disposition of the 105-lot MGC position — is explicitly Tier-3 and still with the operator. — Proposed: operator decides the disposition of the 105-lot MGC/ib_paper position on trade 4487 (flatten via the flatten-ib-position action, or hold with a stated reason); it separately blocks mgc_trend_1h signals through flip_suppressed_hold_policy. The detection/cancellation defect itself is fixed.

PARTIALLY FIXED AND VERIFIED: protection_coverage now returns stop_qty and target_qty SEPARATELY and the two-sided grading is live — proven by 108 ib_target_naked pages in the ERROR feed (which a boolean check could not have produced) and by today's clean MES read (STP 15 + LMT 15 in one OCA group against a 15-lot position). The CANCELLATION half — session-scoped and symbol-wide — is unchanged, and that is what keeps this open (see BL-20260816-NO-PER-ORDER-IB-CANCEL).

items.title: No read surface for IB open orders - IB exit coverage cannot be verified from any session, which is why a stripped take-profit sat undetected for 7 days
items.detail:
Established while root-causing why trade 4487's MGC take-profit never fired. To answer 'does a protective leg currently rest on IB for this trade?' there is no available route:
  * /api/diag/exchange_positions returns POSITIONS, never orders.
  * /api/diag/broker_account_status is populated for Alpaca (status flags) and Bybit (available_margin) only; for interactive_brokers it returns supported:false with no order data.
  * /api/bot/positions carries the JOURNAL's stopLoss/takeProfit - which is exactly the thing under suspicion: it is what the bot INTENDED, not what the broker holds.
The only consumer of IB order state is IBClient.has_protective_orders, which collapses the answer to one boolean and exposes it nowhere. So the system can ACT on IB protection but no operator or review session can OBSERVE it. Bybit got exactly this treatment in PR #8000 (covered_qty summed vs size, plus over_covered / journal_qty_divergent detect-only signals); IB never did.
This is why the MGC defect went 7 days unnoticed while THREE alarms fired nearby (MONITOR BLIND, stuck-strategy watchdog, operator_warning): each described a symptom, and the one question that would have identified the cause was unanswerable from any surface.
items.resolution_criteria: Ship a token-gated read-only /api/diag/ib_open_orders (or an interactive_brokers arm on broker_account_status) returning per account+symbol: orderId, orderType, action, totalQuantity, auxPrice/lmtPrice, ocaGroup, tif, status. Account-wide read (reqAllOpenOrders), never openTrades(). Add it to the vm-diag-snapshot relay allowlist in the SAME PR - a /api/diag/* surface shipped without an allowlist entry is unreachable by the only session type that reviews it (the exit_loop_health lesson). Three states, never collapsed: read_ok with rows / read_ok empty (genuinely no resting orders) / could_not_read (breaker open or gateway wedged - NOT 'no orders').

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: src/web/api/routers/diag.py:1320 defines `GET /api/diag/ib_open_orders`, whose docstring names this backlog id and documents the three uncollapsed per-account states (null = could not look / [] = confirmed clean read / rows), returning symbol, order_id/perm_id, order_type, action, total_quantity, aux_price/lmt_price, oca_group, tif, parent_id, status via `account_ib_open_orders`. tests/test_diag_ib_open_orders.py exists. Relay reachability holds by construction: .github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml allowlists /api/bot/* paths explicitly and defaults every other path to the /api/diag/ prefix, so no per-route entry is required.

items.title: The /system-review SKILL documents review_coverage blocks as STRINGS; render_system_report.py --strict requires DICTS and dies on AttributeError
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) make the renderer accept the string form the skill documents (coerce str -> {'summary': s}), or (b) fix the skill prose to state the dict/list shapes and point at the template. EITHER WAY, --strict must fail with a NAMED key and expected type instead of an AttributeError - a validator whose failure mode is a stack trace teaches nothing. Add a fixture test that renders the exact payload shape the skill's prose describes.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Both halves still hold. .claude/skills/system-review/SKILL.md:162 still documents relay-blocked data as 'an explicit "unavailable: <reason>" string', and scripts/reports/render_system_report.py:393-420 still does `sp = rc.get('strategy_promotion') or {}` then `sp.get('ready_to_promote')` — a non-empty string survives the `or {}` and raises AttributeError. No str-coercion and no named-key/expected-type validation exists on that path. — Tier-1 tooling/docs; bites every /system-review render.

CONFIRMED LIVE BY THIS REVIEW, repeatedly. Building RPT-20260829-163000 I hit three shape contradictions the SKILL does not document: unexercised_fixes must be a LIST (the validator wraps a dict as ONE row and then reports verdict ''), since_last_build_verification items need a `name` key for the UNWIRED escalation check to match, and health.findings must be a DICT for _section_health while the skill's prose implies a list. Each cost a render cycle. The skill and the renderer disagree and the renderer wins.

items.title: --strict passes a report whose backlog_drive.count_untriaged is 201/39/26, even though the skill calls 100% triage a HARD COMPLETION GATE
items.detail:
MEASURED this run. The /system-review skill states the backlog drive is 'a HARD COMPLETION GATE, every open item, not a sample', that 'each domain's count_untriaged MUST be 0', and that a run must STOP if it is not. It also names render_system_report.py --strict as 'the mechanical coverage backstop' so 'a skipped assessment can't quietly ship'.
But --strict only validates that required review_coverage KEYS are present/non-empty and that an execution_capture anomaly with reviews_open>=2 is escalated. It never reads backlog_drive.count_untriaged. This report rendered GREEN under --strict while declaring count_untriaged of 201 (health), 39 (performance) and 26 (ml) - i.e. the single gate the skill describes as hardest to fake is the one the backstop does not check.
The honest disclosure survived here only because the payload was written honestly; a run that quietly omitted the counts, or set them to 0, would have rendered identically. That is the 'green is not evidence' shape applied to the review process itself.
items.resolution_criteria: Extend _validate_review_coverage to fail when any domain's backlog_drive.count_untriaged > 0 or when triaged != open_at_start, with the domain named in the message. If a partial run should still be publishable, make that an EXPLICIT opt-out flag (e.g. --allow-partial-triage) that stamps a visible 'PARTIAL REVIEW' banner into the rendered HTML - so an incomplete review is publishable but never mistakable for a complete one.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: `grep -n count_untriaged scripts/reports/render_system_report.py` returns NOTHING, while the required-key list at :700 covers only strategy_promotion / ml_training_health / soak_status (etc). So --strict still validates key presence and the execution_capture escalation, and never reads backlog_drive.count_untriaged — exactly as filed. — Tier-1 review tooling. High value: this is the gate the skill calls hardest to fake and the backstop does not check it.

⚠️ CONFIRMED LIVE BY THIS VERY REVIEW, which is the strongest possible evidence for this row. I rendered RPT-20260829-163000-since-last with --strict and it PASSED while backlog_drive.count_untriaged read 456 / 40 / 19. The guard checks that `deferred` entries carry a reason and that SOMETHING was disposed; it does not check count_untriaged == 0, even though the skill calls 100% triage a HARD COMPLETION GATE. I then went and did the triage by hand — which is exactly the outcome a guard should not have to depend on. The fix is a one-line check in _validate_review_coverage; deliberately NOT bundled into this review's PR because it would have let this same run pass itself.

items.tier: 2 (trader runtime; lock scope around a loop-driving path)
items.title: PR #9240's thread pin closed market-data-vs-market-data but NOT market-data-vs-account/order — the 'event loop is already running' class stayed structurally reachable
items.detail:
FOUND BY AUDITING MY OWN FIX, same session, before declaring the incident closed. PR #9240 pinned every IBMarketData.get_ohlcv onto one 'ib-marketdata' thread, which is correct and necessary: it serialises market-data against market-data and keeps the cached IB's transport on the loop it is bound to. But it is only HALF the class.

IBClient._ensure_event_loop keeps ONE persistent loop per client (self._loop) and re-asserts it as current on whatever thread calls it. The failure string 'This event loop is already running' is raised when a second thread enters loop.run_until_complete while the loop is already running — i.e. it is a CONCURRENCY condition on one loop object, not a distinct-loop condition.

Two families of caller drive that loop:
  (a) IBMarketData.get_ohlcv -> _ensure_event_loop + reqHistoricalData, which ran OUTSIDE _usage_lock entirely. This is the one that failed live and the one #9240 pinned.
  (b) The account/order surface -- verified by reading the file, _usage_lock is taken at 14 sites: connect, disconnect, place, place_protective, modify_protective, close, cancel_resting_protection, has_protective_orders, cancel, status, balance, positions, executions, self_test.

Within (b) the RLock makes those mutually exclusive. Within (a) the pin does the same. NOTHING excluded (a) against (b). After the M20 decouple the exit thread runs (b) (close/positions/has_protective_orders on open packages) while the tick thread triggers (a) via signal_build -- so the pinned fetch thread and a lock-holding thread could still drive the one loop concurrently. The pin closed the half that was firing, not the class.

WHY THE FIRST TEST DID NOT CATCH IT (recorded because the near-miss is the lesson): the first version of the regression test started the account op FIRST and asserted no overlap -- and it PASSED against the unfixed code. connect() takes _usage_lock and RELEASES it before reqHistoricalData, so the fetch merely blocked inside connect() and the op had finished before the real hazard window opened. The test passed on timing, identically with and without the fix. Reproducing the actual hazard requires the op to arrive while the fetch is ALREADY inside reqHistoricalData. Once reordered, the test fails without the lock and passes with it -- confirmed both directions by reverting only the lock acquisition and keeping the pin.
items.resolution_criteria:
FIXED in the follow-up PR to #9240: _get_ohlcv_pinned now holds the client's _usage_lock across connect + _ensure_event_loop + reqHistoricalData, so EVERY loop-driving operation in the process is mutually exclusive. _usage_lock is an RLock and connect() re-takes it, so the nesting is safe on the pinned thread.
The wait is BOUNDED (IB_USAGE_LOCK_WAIT_S, default IB_FETCH_TIMEOUT_S*3 = 24s): an unbounded wait would back the single-worker queue up behind a slow connect() (~20s worst case: probe + retry + account warm-up + retry) and every later fetch would miss its caller's _IB_FETCH_QUEUE_TIMEOUT_S while the worker sat blocked.
A lock that cannot be acquired is NOT collapsed into 'no data': it returns None like any unavailable fetch, but logs its own distinct cause naming the lock and stating that no request was sent to the venue -- 'we could not look' and 'the venue has nothing' are opposite statements. Covered by tests/test_ib_marketdata_thread_pinning.py::{test_fetch_excludes_the_account_order_surface,test_unacquirable_lock_is_not_reported_as_no_data,test_lock_wait_is_bounded_and_outlasts_a_worst_case_connect}, all three verified to fail on the unfixed code.

items.title: IBClient liveness probe attempt 1/2 times out on essentially EVERY connect -- 14 times in 89s -- burning ~5s of dead wait per IB call; the retry saves it, so nothing alarms
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 on the post-restart trader (PID 1924521, journal 13:11:24Z through 13:12:53Z): 'IBClient: liveness probe attempt 1/2 timed out after 5s for 10.0.0.251:4002' appears 14 times in 89 seconds -- roughly one every 7s, i.e. on essentially every connect().

WHY IT IS INVISIBLE, which is the actual finding: it is logged at INFO, not WARNING; the single bounded retry (IB_PROBE_RETRY_GAP_S, the BL-20260610-009 fix) then SUCCEEDS; so no circuit breaker trips ('circuit breaker' appears 0 times in that window) and /api/diag/ib_state reports all three clients state=connected, consecutive_failures=0, likely_wedged=false. Every health surface reads clean while every IB call pays a 5s tax. This is the desensitised-signal shape: the retry that made the condition survivable also made it unobservable.

NOT CAUSED BY the 2026-08-14 thread pin -- the same string appears in the ORIGINAL incident evidence at 09:46:05Z, before any fix. It is a chronic condition of the cross-host socat-relayed gateway (the cold-TCP-flow miss documented under IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S / IB_PROBE_TRUST_FRESH_HANDSHAKE), but its CADENCE has never been measured or bounded.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: ~5s of dead wait per connect is a plausible contributor to the exit-loop pass measuring 40.7-41.5s against the M20-documented 22.4s mean (see BL-20260814-EXIT-PASS-SLOWER-THAN-M20). Every exit evaluation that touches IB pays it.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. Measure the probe-timeout rate over a WARM window of at least 30 minutes (n>1 process, not a single post-restart burst) -- the honest denominator is timeouts per connect(), not timeouts per minute.
2. Establish whether attempt 1 EVER succeeds on this relay; if it effectively never does, the 5s first attempt is pure latency and IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S should be retuned (Tier-2 env flip) or the first attempt shortened, rather than left as a tax paid on every call.
3. Decide the log level deliberately: a condition firing on every connect is either normal (and should not be logged per-occurrence at all) or abnormal (and must not sit at INFO). It is currently logged as if it were rare, which is what let it run unnoticed.
4. Do NOT 'fix' this by widening the retry -- that is what hid it.

updates.note:
SECOND INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION, on a different process. Measured over a contiguous 92s union of three journal windows (19:28:28 -> 19:30:00, PID 2065168, started 19:13:51Z): 10 'liveness probe attempt 1/2 timed out after 5s' lines - 19:28:33.209, 19:28:33.261, 19:28:39.715, 19:28:55.870, 19:29:03.104, 19:29:09.611, 19:29:25.870, 19:29:33.066, 19:29:39.573, 19:29:56.209. The invisibility claim is now directly corroborated rather than inferred: /api/diag/ib_state captured at 19:28:39 in the SAME window reports all three clients state=connected, connected=true, account_data_ready=true, breaker_open=false, consecutive_failures=0, likely_wedged=false. Every health surface reads clean while ~10 connects per 92s each pay a 5s dead wait plus a 1.5s retry gap. Severity left at medium (the retry rescues every one; nothing is stranded), but the resolution criteria's 'measure the rate' step is now satisfied twice.

[sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Criterion 1 (measure the rate over a warm window, >1 process) is satisfied twice per the row's own update (0.157/s on PID 1924521, 0.109/s on PID 2065168). Criteria 2-4 remain: the probe/retry structure and its INFO log level are unchanged in the tree (IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S / IB_PROBE_RETRY_GAP_S semantics as documented in CLAUDE.md), and no decision is recorded on whether attempt 1 ever succeeds on this relay. — needs live data + Tier-2: establishing whether attempt 1 ever succeeds requires a live journal read, and retuning IB_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S on the VM is a Tier-2 env flip. items.title: Exit-loop pass measured 40.7-41.5s post-fix against the M20-documented 22.4s mean -- needs a WARM re-measure before anyone reads it as a regression OR as fine
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-14, ~3 minutes after the trader restarted with the IB thread pin deployed and EXIT_LOOP_DECOUPLE_DISABLED cleared.
  exit_loop_health: passes 4, last_pass_ms 40654.0, max_pass_ms 40710.7
  tick_cost offloop_hooks: monitor.strategy_monitor_loop n=5, mean 36654.7ms, max 41527.0ms
The M20 sprint log documents a 22.4s mean pass with one 55-pass distribution behind it. So this is ~1.8x slower.

STATE THE DENOMINATOR: n=5 passes from a single process that had been up ~3 minutes, with cold caches (tick_cost ticks_measured=1, fetch.1d mean 17942.8ms on-loop). The M20 figure is n=55. These are not comparable samples and the 1.8x MUST NOT be quoted as a regression until re-measured warm.

TWO CANDIDATE CAUSES, neither established:
  (a) EXPECTED AND ACCEPTED. The pin routes all market-data through one thread, so the exit loop's fetches now QUEUE behind the tick's. That is the deliberate cost of correctness over latency -- but it was never quantified when the pin was proposed, and it should be.
  (b) The ~5s-per-connect liveness-probe tax (BL-20260814-IB-LIVENESS-PROBE-TIMES-OUT-EVERY-CONNECT).
The follow-up lock (BL-20260814-IB-MARKETDATA-VS-ACCOUNT-LOCK-GAP) will add further serialisation and can only increase this, so the warm baseline should be taken AFTER that lands, not before.

CONTEXT FOR JUDGING IT: the operator's stated ask is that no live trade goes >60s without evaluation. At 41.5s the interval-targeting loop (slack = interval - elapsed, so effective interval = max(30, pass)) still clears that -- but the margin is now 31% rather than the 2x the M20 decouple bought. It is not a breach; it is a thinner cushion than the sprint log implies, and the sprint log's 22.4s is the number a future session would otherwise trust.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. Re-measure exit_loop_health + tick_cost offloop_hooks on a WARM process (>=30 min uptime, ticks_measured>=10, passes>=30) after the _usage_lock follow-up is deployed.
2. Report mean AND max pass_ms beside the pass count -- a max over 5 passes is not the claim a max over 55 is.
3. If the warm pass still exceeds ~40s, attribute it: instrument whether the time is fetch-queue wait (pin cost) or probe wait (BL-...PROBE-TIMES-OUT), because the remedies are opposite.
4. Whatever the answer, update docs/sprint-logs/S-M20-EXIT-LOOP-DECOUPLE-2026-08-12.md's 22.4s figure with the post-pin number, so the sprint log stops being a stale claim about current behaviour.

WARM RE-MEASURE 2026-08-14T14:34Z — RESOLVED, and the cold reading was indeed misleading.
Read on the post-#9280 process (tick_cost process_started_utc 13:45:23.410Z, exit_loop_health process_started_utc 13:45:48.167Z), both gates cleared BEFORE grading: passes 88 (>=30) and ticks_measured 13 (>=10). offloop_hooks POPULATED (monitor.strategy_monitor_loop n=78, fetchby.strategy_monitor_loop n=1016), and process_started_utc asserted against the 13:45:16Z restart so a stale pre-restart payload could not be graded as a live one.

  exit pass, warm : mean 27.6s / max 47.6s  (n=88 passes; offloop monitor.strategy_monitor_loop mean 27602.5ms / max 47617.1ms, n=78)
  M20 sprint log  : mean 22.4s              (n=55)
  cold, this day  : 40.7-41.5s              (n=5, 3-minute-old process)

So +23% on M20, NOT the +82% the n=5 cold read implied. This item existed precisely to stop that cold number being quoted as a regression, and it worked. The 47.6s max landed at 13:47:58Z — 2m10s after process start, during cache warm-up, not steady state. Last pass 28.0s, under the 30s interval floor, so the effective cadence is ~30s and the operator's 60s ask retains ~2x margin at the mean.

ATTRIBUTION (criterion 3), stated to the limit of what the data supports:
  ESTABLISHED — the pass is 97.2% FETCH WAIT: 26.8s of the 27.6s mean. Reconciled two independent ways: (a) the per-timeframe sum over off-loop real fetches (15m 79x10569.6 + 1d 123x9872.8 + 4h 9x601.0 + 1h 27x1273.7 + 2h 18x227.3 = 2,093,242ms / 78 passes = 26,836ms), and (b) the fetchby.strategy_monitor_loop aggregate (n=1016 = 256 real + 760 cache hits, matching exactly). Two routes agreeing is the check that the instrumentation measures what it claims.
  NOT ESTABLISHED — that the PIN's queueing is what inflates that wait. Off-loop vs on-loop means for the same timeframe: 15m 4.40x, 4h 2.95x, 1d 1.56x, 2h 1.14x, but 1h 0.34x — FASTER off-loop. The two consumers fetch different symbol mixes (and different venues: only IB market data is pinned, Bybit is not), so the per-timeframe comparison is confounded. Quoting only the four ratios that fit the queueing story would be cherry-picking; the honest statement is that the pass is fetch-dominated and the cause of the fetch cost is not isolated by this read.
  The probe tax (BL-20260814-IB-LIVENESS-PROBE-TIMES-OUT-EVERY-CONNECT, ~5s per connect) is INSIDE those fetch times but cannot account for 26.8s on its own.

Criterion 4 (update the sprint log) done in the same commit: docs/sprint-logs/S-M20-EXIT-LOOP-DECOUPLE-2026-08-12.md now carries a SUPERSEDED block on the 22.4s figure so it stops reading as current behaviour.

items.title: The tick is 2.15x the M20 baseline after the IB single-thread pin — 148.7s mean / 200.0s max warm (n=13) vs 69.3s/96.8s — and the pin's cost to the TICK was never measured before it shipped
items.detail:
FOUND WHILE MEASURING SOMETHING ELSE (the warm exit-pass re-measure, BL-20260814-EXIT-PASS-SLOWER-THAN-M20). Not the thing that read was for, filed rather than dropped.

MEASURED 2026-08-14T14:29:37Z, tick_cost on the post-#9280 process (process_started_utc 13:45:23.410Z), ticks_measured 13, ~44 minutes of uptime:
  tick mean 148741.2ms (148.7s) / max 200008.0ms (200.0s)
  run_one_tick mean 122304.7ms, pct_of_total 82.2
  pipeline.signal_build mean 4237.7ms x n=299, pct_of_total 65.5
  order_monitor mean 24590.3ms, pct_of_total 16.5
  attributed_pct 98.8, nested_hooks 27, hook_names_refused 0

THE SEQUENCE, so nobody re-derives it:
  M20 post-decouple baseline (sprint log, pre-pin)  mean  69.3s / max  96.8s  n=55
  mitigated, EXIT_LOOP_DECOUPLE_DISABLED=1          mean  98.5s / max 118.0s
  after #9240 (pin only), COLD                      mean 195.4s              n=1
  after #9280 (pin + _usage_lock), WARM             mean 148.7s / max 200.0s n=13
Warm vs the M20 baseline: 2.15x mean, 2.07x max.

WHY THIS IS NOT AN ARGUMENT TO REVERT THE PIN: the pin fixed a LIVE defect (BL-20260814-IB-EVENTLOOP-CONTENTION) in which two threads drove one ib_insync event loop, tripping the circuit breaker and taking MGC/MES candles away entirely — MONITOR BLIND on open packages and refused entries. Correctness over latency was the right call. The failure here is that the pin's cost to the TICK was never quantified before it shipped, by me, in either PR. A cost you did not measure is not a cost you accepted.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY DELAYS: the EXIT half is unaffected — it is decoupled and still hits its ~30s cadence (see the sibling item). The TICK half generates SIGNALS, so a 148.7s tick delays new entries and regime scoring. TICK_INTERVAL_SECONDS is 60 but the observed inter-tick spacing is ~204s (13 ticks over 2654s), because the loop targets a period and a pass that overruns starts the next immediately.

CONFOUND, stated rather than assumed away: this warm read is a DIFFERENT process, a different market session (US equities closed for much of the window — many strategies short-circuit on 'US market closed'), and a different cache state from the M20 n=55 baseline. 2.15x is real against the recorded baseline but is NOT a controlled comparison, and BL-20260810-TICK-CHAIN-260S-PER-TICK was already open with the tick at 96.5s before any of this.

CONFIRMED AT n=37 2026-08-14T17:05Z — and one confound I stated above is WRONG; correcting it here because a false confound is a wrong reason to dismiss a real regression.

Larger sample, a DIFFERENT process (process_started_utc 15:02:59Z, git_sha 84ba67e0 — a later restart by another session, so this is an independent observation rather than a longer read of the same one):
  tick      n=37 : mean 140.1s / max 191.5s   vs M20 69.3s / 96.8s  ->  2.02x mean, 1.98x max
  tick      n=13 : mean 148.7s / max 200.0s   (the original read)
So the 2x is NOT a small-sample artifact. It reproduces across two processes on two different commits, and the mean is drifting DOWN slightly rather than being a one-off spike.

** CORRECTION to the confound list above. ** The original entry named "US cash mostly closed" as a confound. That is FALSE. US equity RTH is 09:30-16:00 ET = 13:30-20:00 UTC in August (EDT = UTC-4). The n=13 window was 13:45-14:29Z = 09:45-10:29 ET, and the n=37 window was 15:03-17:05Z = 11:03-13:05 ET. BOTH sit entirely inside RTH. I inferred "market closed" from 'US market closed - side=none' lines I read in a 13:20Z journal slice — 13:20Z IS pre-open (09:20 ET), but that slice was from BEFORE the measurement window, not inside it. Reading a property off the wrong time range and carrying it forward as a caveat is the same shape as the stale-figure defect this session kept finding elsewhere.
The remaining confounds stand: different cache state, and BL-20260810-TICK-CHAIN-260S-PER-TICK already had the tick at 96.5s pre-pin, so the pin is not the whole 2x.

Sibling reading, same pull, for context — the EXIT half continues to be fine and is NOT the problem: exit pass n=219 mean 26.6s / max 51.2s (vs 27.6s at n=88 and M20's 22.4s at n=55) = +18.9%, with last_pass 21.4s, BELOW the M20 figure. The pass is 96.9% fetch wait at this sample (25.8s of 26.6s), matching the 97.2% measured at n=78. So the cost lands on the TICK, not the exit loop.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. Re-measure the tick on a comparable session (US cash open, so the equity strategies actually run) at ticks_measured>=20, and report mean AND max beside the count.
2. SPLIT the pin cost from everything else. Only IB market data is pinned (src/exchange/ib_connector.py::_IB_FETCH_EXECUTOR); Bybit is not. So the pin can only inflate IB-symbol fetches (MES/MGC/MHG) — quantify how much of pipeline.signal_build's 65.5% is IB-bound before attributing the 2.15x to the pin. The fetch.* timeframe buckets aggregate ACROSS venues and cannot answer this; a per-venue cut can.
3. If the pin is a material contributor, the remedy is NOT to remove it. Options worth evaluating in order: raise CANDLE_CACHE_TTL_MAX_S so IB frames survive a tick gap (already Tier-3, see CLAUDE.md); give IB market data its own executor per client_id rather than one process-wide (the collision is per-loop, i.e. per-client, so a process-wide single thread is stricter than the invariant requires); or cut the number of IB fetches per tick.
4. Do NOT close this by pointing at BL-20260810-TICK-CHAIN-260S-PER-TICK. That item predates the pin and is about signal_build's own cost; this one is about a regression ON TOP of it.

updates.note:
CONFIRMED AT n=116, NOT n=5. The earlier readings behind this row were small-sample; /api/diag/tick_cost at 2026-08-16T05:39:18Z covers 116 ticks from one process (started 2026-08-15T23:06:29Z, 6.6h) and the degradation is real and slightly worse: mean 143.7s, max 195.6s.

WHERE IT GOES, at that sample: pipeline.signal_build 65.3% (max 60.4s) and fetch.1d 31.0% at a mean of 14825.4ms per fetch over n=348. A 14.8s MEAN on daily bars is the single largest line and is not explained by the cache TTL discussion alone.

A shared ~29s ceiling across different timeframes and both loops looks like a client/venue timeout being hit, not organic latency. If so, the tail is a TIMEOUT population and averaging it with healthy fetches understates how often a fetch fails outright. Establish which before tuning any TTL.

Do not close it against BL-20260810-TICK-CHAIN-260S-PER-TICK (different question).

RESOLVED. LIVE RE-MEASUREMENT 2026-08-29, two independent trader processes: process 15:11:25Z n=31 mean 45,467 ms / max 61,467 ms; process 16:10:51Z n=19 mean 47,986 ms / max 59,627 ms. So the tick is ~46-48 s mean / ~60 s max. That is not merely better than the regression this row records — it is BETTER THAN THE M20 BASELINE (69.3 s mean / 96.8 s max) the row measures against.
