The MEAN is what this row is about and it has recovered.

items.title: account_reachability_alert probes positions(), but the sizer depends on balance() - so an account that refuses EVERY signal reads UP and nothing alerts
items.detail:
POPULATION MISMATCH between the alert and the thing it is meant to protect. `account_reachability_alert.run_account_reachability_check` grades an account with `reachable = positions is not None`, where the prober is `clients.account_open_positions` (src/runtime/account_reachability_alert.py, the `prober(cfg)` call). But the per-signal sizing path refuses on `balance()` returning None (coordinator.py, `_default_balance_fetcher` -> `balance_none_refusal_message`).

Those are DIFFERENT broker capabilities on the same account. An account whose positions() answers while balance() returns None is therefore graded REACHABLE and never alerts, while refusing every single signal it is routed. The latched DOWN/OK alert - which exists precisely so a dark account cannot go unflagged across reviews - is structurally blind to this failure mode.

THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. It is the measured explanation for why BL-20260813-ALPACA-BALANCE-NONE-WHILE-ACCOUNT-READS-ACTIVE went unnoticed: that row records the condition was 'found incidentally while verifying an unrelated fix - which is the only reason it was found at all; nothing alerted', across TWO accounts (alpaca_paper carrying 19 routed strategies, alpaca_portfolio carrying 14) for a window bounded at ~5h and in fact lasting into the next day.

SCOPE: every exchange in the reachability prober's set (bybit/interactive_brokers/alpaca/oanda), not an Alpaca-specific gap - the mismatch is in the alert's choice of probe, not in any one integration.

NOT FIXED IN THE SAME PR AS THE MESSAGE, DELIBERATELY. Adding a balance() dimension to the latched alert changes what pings the operator, and this repo treats a desensitised alarm as its own P1. The alert fires one Telegram + one WARNING FCM push per cross-into-down, so the correct sequence is to OBSERVE the balance-vs-positions disagreement rate first and only then decide whether it earns a latched alert - the same 'distribution before you set the threshold' discipline the gross-exposure ceiling design imposes. Shipping the alert on zero observations would be the exposure-ceiling mistake in a new place.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) a soak has measured how often balance() and positions() disagree per account over a window with a stated denominator, and on that evidence the reachability check gained a balance dimension (with the two states kept distinguishable - 'positions down' and 'balance down' are different operator actions and must not collapse into one DOWN); OR (b) the balance-refusal path itself gained a latched alert, so a signal refused for an unreadable balance is loud at the point of refusal rather than at the reachability probe. Either way the done-condition is that a repeat of BL-20260813 ALERTS rather than being found incidentally.

updates.by: claude (roadmap review session, design follow-up before anyone implements this)
updates.note:
DO NOT FIX THIS BY ADDING A BALANCE PROBE. That is the obvious reading of this row and it is the wrong implementation — recording the better one now, because the naive fix breaks a deliberate invariant and the row as originally written invites it.

account_reachability_alert.py's own docstring states the constraint: the check reuses the value the reverse reconciler ALREADY calls every tick (account_open_positions) and adds 'No new exchange round-trip.' Bolting a balance() call onto it would add a broker round-trip per live account per cadence window to the live trader's tick — the exact cost class behind both June 2026 wedges, where every added component was individually cheap.

THE EVIDENCE IS ALREADY IN THE JOURNAL, so no broker call is needed. When balance() returns None the coordinator raises through balance_none_refusal_message (coordinator.py:47/1000) and the refusal is persisted to trades.entry_reason as 'sizing_failed: ... balance() returned None for <acct> (exchange=<x>)'. That column is queryable and is precisely what this session's measurements read (48 occurrences over ~7 weeks all-history; 6 in the last 30d, 4 of them clustered on 2026-08-13 across THREE accounts). A journal-backed detector is strictly better than a probe on three counts:
  * zero broker load, so the no-round-trip invariant survives;
  * it cannot false-positive on a transient network blip, because it keys on refusals that ACTUALLY HAPPENED and cost real signals, not on a probe that might merely have timed out;
  * it measures the thing that matters — signals refused — rather than a proxy for it.

Note the asymmetry that makes this a genuine gap rather than a duplicate of the existing alert: account_open_positions returning a list proves the account is READABLE, which is a weaker claim than TRADEABLE. An account can answer positions() all day while refusing every signal it is routed. That is the state this row exists for.

TIER: shipping a new latched alert is Tier-2 (it fires operator Telegram + FCM), so this stays a proposal. The rate-limiting must be designed in from the start — this condition can recur every tick for a routed strategy, and a per-tick alarm IS the desensitized-alarm P1 this repo already has a rule about. Latch per (account, cause) the way the existing DOWN/OK alert does, not per occurrence.

items.resolution: RESOLVED (detection) 2026-08-14 by PR #9334, merged e97d8390, via a NEW sibling rather than a change to the prober. `src/runtime/silent_refusal_alert.py` latches on an account that produced refusal rows and ZERO placed rows in the window, hooked into the `src/main.py` tick beside `run_account_reachability_check`. ⚠️ THE PROBER WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE. The obvious fix -- have `account_reachability_alert` also call `balance()` -- would break its documented 'No new exchange round-trip pattern' invariant by adding a per-account broker round-trip to a live tick, which is the shape of both June 2026 wedges. The new detector reads the journal the trader has already written (one read-only SQLite connection, no socket), so `positions()` remains the reachability primitive and this covers the population it cannot see. Per ACCOUNT not per leg (alpaca_live routes 16 strategies; 16 pings for one cause is the desensitized-alarm P1); latched per (account, cause) so a second, different cause is not swallowed. Verdicts come from the shared `src/runtime/dead_leg.py`, the same module `scripts/ops/dead_leg_audit.py` grades with. ⚠️ BL-20260813-ALPACA-BALANCE-NONE-WHILE-ACCOUNT-READS-ACTIVE STAYS OPEN: this makes that condition DETECTABLE, it does not fix it. `balance()` still returns None on those accounts while /v2/account reads ACTIVE, and every signal routed to them is still refused.

items.title: legalize_qty's venue_max=None collapses 'the venue published no maximum' with 'we could not resolve one' - so the BL-20260810 clamp silently no-ops and the oversized order is still sent
items.detail:
THE CLAMP EXISTS, WAS DEPLOYED, AND DID NOT ENGAGE. Established by proof of inclusion rather than by inference:

  * The venue-max clamp landed in #9032 (9301947, 2026-08-13T14:02:13Z) - `qty_legalize.legalize_qty` clamps to `maxOrderQty`, and `execute._submit_order` logs 'EXCEEDS venue maxOrderQty ... clamped'.
  * Journal trade **4640** (`ict_scalp_avax_5m`, `bybit_1`, **2026-08-14T00:31:39Z** - 10.5h LATER) is still `exchange_rejected`: `order_qty:3399790000000 > max_qty:2200000000000 (ErrCode: 10001)` i.e. 33,997.9 AVAX sent against a 22,000 cap.
  * That same row carries a `notes.margin_basis` block, and `margin_basis` only exists in code from #9039 (5bbb341, 2026-08-13T16:46:59Z). `git merge-base --is-ancestor` confirms #9032 is an ANCESTOR of #9039. So the running code necessarily CONTAINED the clamp. 'Not deployed yet' is ruled out, not merely unselected.

THEREFORE `venue_max` resolved to None and no clamp was applied. And that is a COLLAPSED STATE of exactly the class this repo names: qty_legalize.py's own comment says '``venue_max=None`` means the venue published no maximum', so 'the venue has no maximum' and 'we could not look up the maximum' are the SAME value. The first is a reason to send the order; the second is a reason to refuse it. They are opposite statements wearing one representation.

WHY IT RESOLVES None HERE, and why this is not a rare edge: **the offline profile cannot supply a maximum at all.** `grep -rn 'max_qty|max_order_qty' config/instruments.yaml src/units/accounts/instrument_profile*.py` returns ZERO hits - `config/instruments.yaml`'s AVAXUSDT block carries exchange/category/base_asset/asset_class/quote/settlement and no ceiling. `_submit_order` calls `legalize_qty(..., prefer_live=True)`, so the ceiling depends ENTIRELY on the live lot-rule lookup; any failure of that lookup - a blip, a breaker, a rate limit - degrades silently to 'no maximum' and the raw qty goes on the wire.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE: the sizer computed 33,997.9 from the margin cap (`margin_basis.max_qty_by_margin: 33997.925`, `basis_usd: 81229.857`, `leverage: 3`, `buffer: 0.9`; 81229.857*3*0.9/6.451 = 34,001, which reconciles). The leg is `ict_scalp_avax_5m`, promoted to `execution: live` on `bybit_1` by M27 Batch-1 - so a leg the roadmap records as a PASS has been contributing zero fills whenever the lookup degrades. Paper account, so no money at risk; it corrupts the soak/ML population, which is what that promotion was for.

NOT A DUPLICATE of BL-20260810-ICTSCALP-AVAX-QTY-EXCEEDS-VENUE-MAX: that row is the symptom and its fix (the clamp) SHIPPED. This is the reason the shipped fix does not hold - one level down.

--- RECURRENCE 2026-08-22 (s4-pairs-control): STILL FIRING, eight days on. ---
Trade at 2026-08-22T10:30:58Z, ict_scalp_avax_5m / bybit_1: qty 33,265.4 AVAX sent, bounced ErrCode 10001 'order_qty:3326540000000 > max_qty:2200000000000'. The clamp's own WARNING in execute._submit_order ('EXCEEDS venue maxOrderQty ... clamped to ...') is ABSENT from the journal window 10:29:30-10:32:30Z, so the clamp branch was not entered -> venue_max was None. Same conclusion as the trade-4640 instance, reached the same way, nine days after 87af13f5 landed the clamp.

THE THREE SILENT PATHS, narrowed. venue_max can reach None by exactly three routes and NONE of them is observable at INFO:
  (a) precision._live_lot_rule returns None on an empty instruments-info response -- logs NOTHING at all;
  (b) qty_legalize._from_live raises (import, _bybit_category, or the lookup) -- logs at DEBUG only;
  (c) _from_live returns None and _from_profile answers instead, which returns venue_max=None BY CONSTRUCTION (its own comment: 'asserts NO ceiling ... only that this source cannot speak to it') -- logs nothing.
No 'lot_rule live lookup failed' WARNING appears in the window, which excludes only the sub-case of (a)/(b) that logs. So WHICH path was taken is UNDETERMINABLE FROM OUTSIDE -- and that unobservability, not the clamp logic, is what makes this row unfixable-and-unverifiable today. legalize_qty already returns `source` on its LegalizedQty result; nothing logs or exposes it on the success path.
items.resolution_criteria: `legalize_qty` distinguishes at least three states for the ceiling and no consumer sees only one: (a) a resolved maximum, (b) the venue genuinely publishes none, (c) **we could not look** (lookup raised / timed out / returned nothing). On (c) the order path must REFUSE rather than send unclamped - the same fail-safe posture the reconcilers take on an unreadable broker read ('never attribute on an unconfirmed read'). Registering the contract with `collapsed-state-guard` is how it stops regressing. A cheap complement, not a substitute: give `config/instruments.yaml` a maxOrderQty so the offline profile can answer at all - today it structurally cannot, which is why (c) is the common case and not the rare one. Done-condition: a forced lookup failure produces a refusal with a typed reason, and NOT an exchange_rejected row.

updates.note: n is much larger than the single row this was filed on. Over 14 days `bybit_1`/`ict_scalp_avax_5m` shows **18 `exchange_rejected` against 4 placed** (verdict `partially_refused`, refusal rate 0.85), with the same shape: `order_qty:3452630000000 > max_qty:2200000000000`. So the clamp fails to engage **most of the time, not occasionally** - consistent with the ceiling depending on a live lookup that frequently does not resolve, and inconsistent with a rare blip. The 4 that DID place are what rule out 'the leg is simply misconfigured'.

**CONFIRMED BY PERFECT SEPARATION AT THE CAP.** Every `ict_scalp_avax_5m` order over 14 days, by qty against Bybit's 22,000 AVAXUSDT ceiling:

  * **exchange_rejected: n=18, range 24,357.8 - 34,526.3 — ALL ABOVE the cap.**
  * **placed/closed: n=4, range 368.4 - 15,413.9 — ALL BELOW the cap.**
  * Zero overlap. The cap is a clean discriminator with no exceptions in either direction.

(A further 4 rows are `rejected` at `qty=0.0` — a different refusal, sizing produced nothing, correctly excluded from the above.)

This rules out the competing explanations that a boundary case would leave open: it is not intermittent venue behaviour (nothing above the cap ever succeeded), not a misconfigured leg (orders below the cap place fine), and not a sizing bug per se (the sizer's number is defensible from margin - it is simply never clamped to the venue ceiling). The clamp is absent from the decision, not wrong in it.

[sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: src/units/accounts/qty_legalize.py still collapses the ceiling: the LegalizedQty docstring at lines 68-77 says verbatim '``venue_max=None`` means the venue published no maximum', there is no third state / read-state field, the clamp at :291-329 simply skips when venue_max is None, and scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py CONTRACTS (8 entries) has no venue-max contract. config/instruments.yaml carries no maxOrderQty key either. — Tier-2 (it changes when an order is refused) and it lives in the live order path, so it is outside what I may edit here. Ends when a lookup failure produces a typed refusal instead of an unclamped send, registered with collapsed-state-guard.

Re-validated: a textbook collapsed-state (venue_max=None conflating 'no maximum published' with 'we could not resolve one'), and it silently no-ops a clamp. NOT registered with collapsed-state-guard — the guard listed 19 contracts this review and this is not among them. Registering it is the structural fix.

items.next_action: || 2026-08-22: OBSERVABILITY IS NOW THE BLOCKING STEP AND IS TIER-1. Record, on the submit path or a diag read, which source resolved the lot rule (legalize_qty already returns `source`) and whether a ceiling was found. Without it, a fix cannot be distinguished from the current silent no-op, and 'no rejections' cannot be distinguished from 'the sizer stayed under the cap by luck'.

items.title: bybit_2 (REAL MONEY) / ict_scalp_5m: 6 of 6 orders exchange_rejected in 14d - the leg placed nothing
items.detail:
Surfaced by `scripts/ops/dead_leg_audit.py --days 14` over the trainer's synced journal (mtime 2026-08-14T05:00:05Z), trainer-diag #9262. Verdict `signalled_never_placed`: `bybit_2` / `ict_scalp_5m` shows **placed=0, refused=6, total=6**, all `exchange_rejected`.

WHY THIS ONE IS PROMOTED ABOVE THE OTHER 31: **`bybit_2` is the ONLY live real-money account in the system** (workplan 2026-08-14 s0.1), and `ict_scalp_5m` is one of its 7 routed strategies. It is also the leg carrying the best 30d expectancy on the real book (+35.4R over 4 trades - small-n, but the only positive one). A leg that is both the best-performing and unable to place is the worst combination available.

POPULATION: 6 rows is a small denominator and is stated as such - this is 14 days of one leg, not a rate over a long window. What makes it worth a row anyway is that the conversion is ZERO, not low.

NOT YET ATTRIBUTED to a cause: the per-leg refusal-reason pull in #9262 was truncated before reaching this leg's sample text (the top-10 cut). The obvious candidate is the same venue-max / margin class as `BL-20260814-VENUE-MAX-NONE-CANNOT-SAY-WE-COULD-NOT-LOOK`, but **that is a hypothesis, not a finding** - do not act on it without pulling this leg's `entry_reason` directly.
items.resolution_criteria: Pull `entry_reason` for `bybit_2`/`ict_scalp_5m` rows with `status='exchange_rejected'` over the window, attribute the rejection to a named cause, and either fix it or record why the refusal is correct. Done when the leg's 14d verdict is no longer `signalled_never_placed`, or a row explains why zero conversion is the right outcome.

updates.note:
**CAUSE IDENTIFIED, AND ALL SIX ROWS PREDATE THE FIX FOR IT.** I filed this without guessing a cause; the pull names one and it changes the disposition.

Every rejection is Bybit **`ErrCode 110007` — 'ab not enough for new order'** (available BALANCE, not venue max — so my noted venue-max hypothesis was WRONG for this leg). BTCUSDT qty 0.011 at ~$63.5k is ~$700 notional against `bybit_2`'s $280.92 equity.

That is exactly `BL-20260813-ICTSCALP-BTC-BYBIT2-BALANCE-REJECTS`, whose Part A fix (sizing from the `coin_derived` margin rung instead of falling back to total equity) shipped **2026-08-13**. The six rows are dated **2026-07-25, 07-31, 08-02 x2, 08-03 x2, 08-04** — every one of them BEFORE that fix. The leg has produced no rejection in the 10 days since.

STATUS -> `likely_already_fixed_unverified`, NOT `resolved`, because the fix is **untested on this leg**: the dead-leg audit shows `placed=0` over 14d, so the leg has neither rejected NOR placed since. Absence of rejections here is absence of ATTEMPTS, not evidence the fix works. Do not close this until `bybit_2`/`ict_scalp_5m` actually places an order.

MY FRAMING WAS ALSO WRONG in a way worth recording: I presented this as a live real-money defect on the strength of a 14-day window that happened to still contain pre-fix rows. A window that straddles a fix will always make a fixed bug look current — the dead-leg audit should be read with the fix dates in hand, and I have added that caveat to the workplan.

[sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The cause is attributed in the row's own update (all six rejections are Bybit ErrCode 110007, available-balance, all predating the 2026-08-13 Part A coin_derived sizing fix, which IS in the tree — src/units/accounts/execute.py:822 AVAILABLE_STATE_COIN_DERIVED). The row's close condition is that bybit_2/ict_scalp_5m actually PLACES an order; absence of rejections is absence of attempts. — needs live data: a journal/dead-leg read over a window after 2026-08-13 showing bybit_2/ict_scalp_5m placed (not merely stopped rejecting). Real money, so keep the row until a placement is observed.

Re-validated: same family as BL-20260813-ICTSCALP-BTC-BYBIT2-BALANCE-REJECTS on the same REAL-MONEY account. Live 30d shows ict_scalp_5m DID place on real money (14 trades, +$4.00), so the leg is not placing nothing now — but the 14d window this row measured is not the 30d window I read, so this is context, not closure.

items.title: On the TRAINER VM the canonical journal resolver points at an EMPTY stray database — trade_journal_db_path() -> <repo>/trade_journal.db (0 rows, stale since 2026-08-02) while the db-puller writes the real 4649-row journal to <repo>/data/. Any trainer-side tool using the resolver gets a clean, confident, WRONG 'zero rows'.
items.detail:
MEASURED on the trainer 2026-08-14 (trainer-diag #9291), by enumerating every trade_journal*.db on the box and grading each by row count rather than trusting the first path that exists:

  /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/data/trade_journal.db   837,308,416 B  mtime 2026-08-14 05:00
      trades=4649  nonbacktest=4649  accounts=12  newest=2026-08-14T03:03:19Z
  /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/trade_journal.db          8,495,104 B  mtime 2026-08-02 04:50
      trades=0     nonbacktest=0     accounts=0   newest=None

and, decisively:
      resolver -> /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/trade_journal.db | exists: True

i.e. src.utils.paths.trade_journal_db_path() on the trainer resolves to the EMPTY file. The db-puller's own log agrees about where the real data goes: db_pulls.jsonl records {"status":"sync_done","data_dir":"/home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/data"}.

WHY THIS IS HIGH AND NOT COSMETIC. The failure is silent and it inverts conclusions. A trainer-side consumer that resolves canonically opens a schema-valid database with zero rows, every SELECT returns empty, and the output renders as a clean negative. This is exactly the stray-duplicate-journal class canonical-db-resolver was written to prevent — the guard forbids the CWD-relative fallback in SOURCE, but nothing checks that the resolved path on a given BOX actually holds data.

HOW IT WAS FOUND — and how close it came to producing a false finding. A diag query in this session asked five questions about zero_balance refusals against the repo-root path. All five returned '(zero rows)'. The ONLY reason that was not read as 'no such refusals exist' is that the query carried a sanity/denominator probe first, which returned COUNT(*)=0 and invalidated everything under it. Without that probe the session would have reported a confident negative about live sizing behaviour derived from a database containing nothing.

KNOWN EXPOSED CONSUMER: scripts/ops/dead_leg_audit.py resolves ONLY via the canonical resolver by design. Run on the trainer without --db it would have printed 'legs graded: 0 / No signalled-never-placed legs in this window' — an all-clear from the wrong file. Hardened in the same PR to refuse a zero-row journal outright and to publish nonbacktest_rows_in_db as the denominator; that hardening is a mitigation for ONE consumer, not a fix for the resolver.
items.what_to_check:
1. Enumerate every trainer-side consumer of trade_journal_db_path() and determine which have been reading the empty file — dataset builds and any offline analysis are the ones that matter, since an empty read there is a silently-degraded training input, not a visible error.
2. Decide the correct resolution on the trainer: either point DATA_DIR/TRADE_JOURNAL_DB at <repo>/data so the resolver agrees with the puller, or move the puller's target. ONE of them, not both — two conventions is how this happened.
3. DELETE or rename the 8.5 MB empty repo-root journal once (2) lands. While it exists, any resolver regression silently re-acquires it; a missing file at least raises.
4. Consider extending canonical-db-resolver (or a trainer boot check) from 'the SOURCE resolves canonically' to 'the RESOLVED path on this box is non-empty' — the guard currently cannot see this failure at all.
items.resolution_criteria: The trainer's canonical resolver and its db-puller agree on one path; that path holds the populated journal; the empty stray is gone; and a consumer resolving canonically on the trainer reads the same non-zero row count the puller wrote.
items.source: roadmap + work-plan review 2026-08-14 (Lane 0)

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: This is a TRAINER-VM filesystem condition (resolver -> /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/trade_journal.db with 0 rows vs the puller's /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/data/ 4649-row file). Nothing in the repo can prove it fixed: src/utils/paths.py's resolver is env-driven (TRADE_JOURNAL_DB -> $DATA_DIR -> repo root) and the fix is a box-side env/path decision plus deleting the stray file. I did not reach the trainer this session. — needs live data: a trainer-diag read enumerating trade_journal*.db by row count and printing `trade_journal_db_path()`, then the DATA_DIR/TRADE_JOURNAL_DB decision + deletion of the empty stray. items.title: LATENT: coordinator._default_balance_fetcher branch 3 sizes off $0.00 on a WHOLE-fetch exception, and the logger.warning on that exact path promises a 'cached/explicit fallback' that cannot exist in production — both of its documented fallbacks are assigned only in test files.
items.detail:
TWO CLAIMS, DIFFERENT CONFIDENCE. Stated separately on purpose.

(A) THE LOG LINE IS WRONG TODAY — verified, no measurement needed.
When src.units.ui.processor.get_account_balances() raises, coordinator.py logs:
    'live balance fetch failed (%s) - per-account sizers will use the cached/explicit fallback instead'
In production there IS no such fallback. Both named mechanisms are test-only:
  * pkg.meta['account_balances_usd'] - grep over src/ finds exactly TWO mentions, both in coordinator.py (one comment, one read). ZERO writers in src/. It is assigned only in tests/ (test_s026_g3_dynamic_sizing, test_prop_risk_manager, test_exchange_rejection_circuit_breaker, test_all_accounts_failed_ping, test_s026_g2_position_size). The comment at coordinator.py:904 nonetheless says "the bot's per-tick balance refresh use this" - that is false.
  * acc.cached_balance_usd - TradingAccount has no such attribute at all. Asked the class directly rather than grepping the source: not a dataclass field, not a class attribute, not in __init__'s signature (positive control: 'name' IS in the signature). Assigned only in one test file's _FakeAccount. coordinator.py:910 is honest about this ('so synthetic test fixtures ... still work'); the LOG line is not.
So on that path the sizers use neither - they take branch 3 and return 0.0. A log that names a recovery no code path can take, printed during the incident it fires on, is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A.

(B) THE 0.0 RETURN IS LATENT - NO EVIDENCE IT HAS FIRED. Say this plainly rather than implying an active bug.
Branch 2 (a per-account total_usdt of None) was fixed to RAISE rather than return 0.0, precisely because the silent 0.0 produced a misleading 'zero_balance: gate_balance=0.00' that read as 'the account is empty' when the fetch had failed. Branch 3 - the whole-fetch exception, or an account simply absent from the map - still returns 0.0. Same defect, other door.
It is untested at the production shape: the existing whole-fetch-exception test (test_live_fetch_exception..., test_s026_g3_dynamic_sizing.py:255) supplies a pkg.meta override so sizing still succeeds - it states so in its own body - and production never sets that key. So the bare branch-3 path has no coverage.

MEASURED, AND IT DID NOT SUPPORT THE HYPOTHESIS (trainer-diag #9293, against the CORRECT journal - data/trade_journal.db, 4649 non-backtest rows, newest 2026-08-14T03:03Z). I expected the 120 zero_balance refusals to be branch 3. They are not:
  * zero_balance refusals, 30d: alpaca_live 120 (2026-07-16 -> 2026-07-31), bybit_portfolio 7. None since 2026-07-31.
  * The discriminator (does it BURST across accounts within an hour, as a service outage must, or TRICKLE on one account, as an unfunded account does?) answers trickle: 3-5 per hour, on alpaca_live ALONE, across 16 separate days; exactly ONE hour in the window touched two accounts.
  * alpaca_live's recorded balance is $0.10.
So those 120 are a genuinely unfunded real-money account refusing correctly. The workplan's original reading ('correct - a $0.10 dry_run account') was RIGHT and the doubt raised against it was wrong; recorded here so the next session does not re-open it.

WHAT THE SAME PULL DID SURFACE, separately: 'balance() returned None' refusals are LOW volume - 6 in 30d - but 4 of the 6 fall on 2026-08-13 across THREE different accounts (ib_paper x2, alpaca_paper, alpaca_portfolio). That IS the burst signature, and it is the cross-client shape BL-20260813-ALPACA-BALANCE-NONE-WHILE-ACCOUNT-READS-ACTIVE already tracks. It is branch 2, which refuses correctly - so it is loud, not silent, and that row owns it.
items.what_to_check:
1. Fix the log line first - it is free, it is wrong today, and it actively misleads an operator reading the journal during a balance outage. Say what branch 3 will actually do (size off 0.0), not what it cannot do.
2. Decide branch 3's contract. It cannot distinguish 'fetch never attempted' (test fixture) from 'whole fetch raised' (production outage) - the account is simply absent from live_balances in both. That is a collapsed state, and it is why one branch has to serve two opposite situations. Separating them (e.g. an explicit fetch_attempted flag) is the precondition for making the production half raise like branch 2 without breaking the fixtures branch 3 exists for.
3. Add the missing coverage: a whole-fetch exception with NO pkg.meta override - the production shape - asserting whatever contract (2) settles on.
4. Do NOT wire cached_balance_usd as a live fallback without a staleness bound. Sizing off an hour-old equity is a money decision; the current code's refusal to size off a guess is deliberate and correct.
5. SEPARATE, FOUND WHILE FILING THIS: the June 2026 branch-2 fix is cited by tracking id in coordinator.py's comment (~line 963) and again in tests/test_s026_g3_dynamic_sizing.py, but that id was NEVER FILED in any docs/claude/*-backlog.json. artifact-validity-guard rejected this row when it cited the same id, which is the guard working — but the guard only scans ADDED lines, so the two pre-existing references in src/ and tests/ are grandfathered and still resolve to nothing. Code saying 'see BL-X' where BL-X does not exist reads as tracked while being tracked by nobody. Either file the row retroactively from the fix's own commit, or correct the citations to point at something real.
items.resolution_criteria: The whole-fetch-exception path either raises with a true cause or sizes off a bounded, explicitly-stated basis; the log line describes what that path actually does; and a test exercises it WITHOUT a pkg.meta override.
items.source: roadmap + work-plan review 2026-08-14 (Lane 0.3)

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Claim (A) still holds verbatim: src/core/coordinator.py:926-930 still logs 'live balance fetch failed (%s) — per-account sizers will use the cached/explicit fallback instead', while branch 3 at :1004-1007 returns `float(cached) if cached is not None else 0.0` and `cached_balance_usd` is set only in test fixtures. No fetch_attempted flag distinguishes 'never attempted' from 'whole fetch raised'. — The log line is a one-line change but sits in src/core/coordinator.py, the live sizing/order path (Tier-2 per the row), so it is outside what I may edit here. Ends when the whole-fetch-exception path either raises with a true cause or sizes off a bounded stated basis, the log describes what it does, and a test exercises it without a pkg.meta override.
Re-validated: LATENT, and the more dangerous half is the log that lies about it. Sizing off $0.00 on a whole-fetch exception is fail-DANGEROUS in the quiet direction.

items.title: ROADMAP.md cells carry STALE forward-looking 'queued/remaining' lists beside later 'Shipped'/'corrected' statements about the SAME items, in the SAME cell — so a planner reading top-down generates work that is already done. It did: 2 of 5 lanes in the 2026-08-14 work plan were already shipped.
items.detail:
TWO CONFIRMED INSTANCES, both found by planning real work off them and then checking the field.

(1) M30. The cell lists: 'Queued loose-ends ... P1 C2 --features selector (unblocks pooled multivariate discovery - DO FIRST)'. Further down THE SAME CELL: 'PIVOT 2026-07-27 ... Shipped: P1 --features (f4cbc3b) - P2 sweep driver (#7730) - P4 wider capture (#7723) - P5 excursion toolchain (#7737/#7741)'. The field agrees with the second: commit f4cbc3ba is titled 'M30 P1: C2 --features common-core selector (unblocks pooled multivariate discovery) (#7718)', the implementation sits at scripts/research/analyze_research_panel.py:913 with its argparse at :1120, and TWO other callers already consume it (sweep_research_panels.py, m20_exit_head_round.py). The queued list was simply never pruned when the pivot shipped its items.

(2) M29. The cell says 'P1b remaining = calibrate on real point-in-time EIA/weather/NG-price history'. Elsewhere it says the dual calibration ran on eia_v2 with 864 real storage obs at OOS storage R^2 ~0.58, and that the operator ask is 'stale - no operator hand-off is outstanding here'. The artifact agrees with the second: comms/macro/sysdyn_gas_dual_scorecard.json carries target_source 'eia_v2 + fred + open-meteo', n_obs 418, generated 2026-07-25.

WHY IT IS COSTLY RATHER THAN MERELY UNTIDY. A stale descriptive claim misinforms; a stale FORWARD-LOOKING claim GENERATES WORK. 'Remaining' and 'do first' are instructions, and a planner reading a 900-line roadmap top-down hits them before the correction buried later in the same cell. This is field-beats-comment at document scale: the queued list is a CLAIM ABOUT the work; the commit, the argparse and the committed scorecard are the FIELD.

MEASURED IMPACT: 2 of the 5 lanes in docs/research/WORKPLAN-2026-08-14.md were derived from these stale lists and were already complete. That plan was itself the product of an operator-requested full roadmap review whose stated purpose was working out what is actually left - which is the strongest possible evidence that the current structure does not answer that question reliably.
items.what_to_check:
1. Sweep every ROADMAP.md cell for a 'Queued'/'Remaining'/'Next'/'do first' list and reconcile each named item against the field (a commit, a symbol in the tree, or a committed artifact) rather than against later prose in the same cell. Prune what shipped.
2. Consider a structural fix rather than a one-off sweep, since this WILL recur: the forward-looking list and the shipped-log are two different kinds of statement sharing one cell, and nothing forces them to agree. Either (a) keep queued items in ONE place per milestone with shipped items struck through in-line, or (b) drop the per-cell queued lists entirely in favour of the backlogs, which are already the tracked, guard-enforced surface.
3. A cheap CI-adjacent probe worth considering: flag any ROADMAP cell that names the same P-number in both a 'queued/remaining' context and a 'Shipped' context. That is a purely textual check and it would have caught BOTH instances here.
4. Re-derive what actually remains of M30 (P2/P3/P5/P6) and M29 (P2-P4) by field check. This row does NOT claim those are done - only that the roadmap cannot be trusted to say.

updates.by: claude (roadmap review session) — two self-inflicted instances, so the class is wider than the title says
updates.note:
THIS ROW'S TITLE SAYS 'ROADMAP.md cells'. THE CLASS IS WIDER: it is ANY forward-looking artifact written before the facts moved. Evidence — my own scheduled self check-ins reproduced it TWICE within 40 minutes today, from a completely different producer than a roadmap cell.

Instance 1 (fired ~15:20Z). Instructed: check CI on head 477bf042, undraft, merge #9244; then file the CI-duration observation; then build M30 P6. By then #9244 was MERGED, the CI-duration claim had been RETRACTED as built on a fabricated clock, and P6 had been shown to be 'a low-priority interpretation nicety' with P3 blocked.
Instance 2 (fired ~15:42Z). Instructed: verify #9313 merged, restart the branch, then build M30 P6 or drain a Lane-0 item. #9313 had merged as 142d634b, the branch was already restarted, and the P6 question was settled and merged as #9316.

In BOTH cases every substantive action item was finished or refuted, and in both cases the instruction was reasonable WHEN WRITTEN. That is precisely the roadmap defect's shape: a forward-looking claim ages into an instruction to redo or to build something worthless, and unlike a stale descriptive claim it GENERATES work rather than merely misinforming.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE FOR CHECK-INS THAN FOR THE ROADMAP: a roadmap cell is read by a human with context, occasionally. A scheduled check-in is delivered as an ordinary user turn to a session that may have compacted its context, and it reads with the authority of an instruction. The failure mode is a session dutifully re-doing merged work or building a de-prioritised item because its own past self said to.

CHEAP REMEDY, for whoever owns the check-in/handoff templates: a scheduled self-message should (a) stamp its assumptions AS OF a timestamp, (b) open with a verify-first clause ('confirm each item below is still open before acting'), and (c) carry explicit DO-NOTs for anything already refuted. The 16:02Z check-in I armed after noticing instance 1 did exactly this — scoped verify-then-HOLD with a do-not list — and it is the one that will not misfire. So the fix is known to work; it just is not the default shape.

items.title: breakout_1's breach guard has been computing off a 25-day-stale equity because the balance REQUEST is gated on 'a position is open', while the STATIC-DD floor it feeds is an account-level constraint that applies when flat. Last reading sits $125.61 above the hard breach floor.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 (trainer-diag #9311, journal path pinned to data/trade_journal.db).

  latest prop_account_status : 2026-07-20T08:28:32Z  balance = equity = $4,825.61
  age                        : 25.27 days
  total snapshots EVER       : 6 (2026-07-04 -> 2026-07-20), then reporting stops dead

Against config/prop_rulesets/breakout.yaml (account_size_usd 5000, max_drawdown_pct 0.06, drawdown_type STATIC off the starting balance, daily_loss_pct 0.03):
  static-DD floor  = $4,700   -> distance from the last known equity = **$125.61** (2.60%)
  daily-loss limit = $150
So /api/bot/prop/status has been reporting a $125.61 cushion derived from a reading that predates 25 days of activity.

THE ACCOUNT DID NOT GO QUIET - ONLY THE BALANCE HALF DID. This is the part that makes it a defect rather than an abandoned account. The manual bridge is demonstrably alive: prop_fills carries 11 'closed' rows with the newest at 2026-08-13T22:14:53Z and 7 'filled' with the newest at 2026-08-13T16:59:26Z, and prop_tickets shows 11 'closed' newest 2026-08-13T16:43Z. The operator has been reporting FILLS as recently as the day before this measurement. What stopped is the `bal <balance> <equity>` half.

ROOT CAUSE, read from the code not inferred: src/prop/prop_status_request.py's module docstring states the account set is 'pruned to accounts that currently hold open positions' and it reuses prop_monitor_pulse.find_open_prop_positions for that. So the bot asks for a balance ONLY while it believes a position is open. Query 4 of the pull returned ZERO tickets in 'filled' or 'placed' - so the bot believes the account is flat, therefore never asks, therefore the snapshot ages without bound.

That gate is wrong for the quantity it feeds. A daily-loss limit is arguably position-scoped, but a STATIC drawdown floor is an ACCOUNT-level constraint measured off the starting balance - it does not stop applying because the book is flat, and the equity that determines the distance to it moves with every closed trade. The guard's input is therefore conditioned on something unrelated to whether the input matters.

SEPARATE OBSERVATION FROM THE SAME PULL - 10 tickets stuck in 'emitted', ages 22.1 to 53.7 days, all ETHUSDT. PROP_EXPIRY_PROMPT_MAX_AGE_HOURS (default 12) bounds how stale a ticket may be before the bot stops asking, so these aged out of the prompt window and can now never reach 'expired' or 'awaiting_report'. They are almost certainly never-placed, but 'emitted' at 54 days does not SAY that - it says we asked and never got an answer, which is a different claim from 'not placed'. They will also sit in find_unacted_tickets / the reconcile drift count forever.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING: that a live prop position is currently open. Zero tickets read 'filled'/'placed'. prop_fills does carry 6 rows at status 'open' (newest 2026-07-16) which may or may not be superseded by the 11 later 'closed' rows - that is not decidable from these counts alone and I did not chase it. The finding stands without it: the guard's input is stale whether or not anything is open.
items.what_to_check:
1. THE FIX IS TIER-2 (it changes a live notification path): request a balance on a cadence for any account with a DECLARED prop ruleset, not only one holding an open position. The existing PROP_STATUS_REQUEST_MAX_AGE_HOURS/COOLDOWN knobs already bound the nagging; only the open-position prune has to go.
2. Decide what /api/bot/prop/status should REPORT when its snapshot is older than the threshold. Today it returns a rule_distance computed from stale data with no staleness on the face of it - which is the collapsed-state shape: 'the cushion is $125.61' and 'the cushion was $125.61 twenty-five days ago' are different statements and the consumer cannot tell them apart. It should carry the snapshot age and refuse to present a distance as current beyond a bound.
3. Ask the operator for a fresh `bal` for breakout_1 NOW, independently of the fix - the current true distance to the $4,700 floor is unknown and the last known value was $125.61.
4. Decide the disposition of the 10 aged 'emitted' tickets (bulk-expire them, or widen PROP_EXPIRY_PROMPT_MAX_AGE_HOURS so the prompt still fires). Leaving them is the option that keeps the reconcile drift count permanently wrong.
items.resolution_criteria: prop_account_status for breakout_1 refreshes on a cadence regardless of open-position state, and /api/bot/prop/status cannot present a rule_distance as current when the underlying snapshot is stale.
items.source: roadmap + work-plan review 2026-08-14 (Lane 0.6)
items.resolution: RESOLVED (mechanism) 2026-08-14 by PR #9334, merged e97d8390. `run_prop_status_request` no longer early-exits on a flat book: the ask is driven by `prop_identity.declared_prop_account_ids(live_only=True)` unioned with any account holding an open prop position, and the cadence state is pruned to that set rather than to position-holders. An open position is now context in the message, not the trigger. Also shipped: `/api/bot/prop/status` + `compute_rule_distance` now carry `status_age_hours` + a four-state `status_freshness` (ok/stale/absent/unchecked, plus `error` on the envelope), so a 25-day-old cushion can no longer render identically to a live one -- `present` only ever meant a row EXISTS. ⚠️ WHAT IS *NOT* FIXED: the measured reading itself. As of this row's measurement the latest snapshot is still 2026-07-20 (25.27d), and the $125.61 cushion to the $4,700 static-DD floor is derived from it. The code change makes the bot ASK (next tick, then every 12h while stale); it cannot manufacture the number -- only the operator's `bal <balance> <equity>` closes that half. Operator was asked on 2026-08-14 and chose 'ship the fix, don't chase the number'.

items.title: The 1d equity legs produce ~4 backtest entries/year over 16.5 years of data — the OOS window is capped by the STRATEGY'S TRADE RATE, not by data depth or live accrual
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 (trainer relays #9245, #9247, #9251) after an operator challenge that was correct and that I had answered wrongly twice.

WHAT I GOT WRONG FIRST. I reported that deepening these windows needed 'more price history on disk, or elapsed time (these legs trade ~20x/year)'. Both halves were wrong: `split_lifetime_trades` is a BACKTEST count (`resolve_split` runs the harness over full history with `--emit-trades`), not a live-trade count, so waiting on live accrual was never the constraint; and the ~20x/year rate was invented, never measured.

THE DATA IS DEEP. `IWM_1d.csv` = 4,151 rows, 2010-01-04 -> 2026-07-07 (16.5y). SCHA identical; SPLG 4,148; QQQ and TLT 4,896 back to 2007. The harness uses ALL of it -- the emit run reports data_start 2010-01-04 / data_end 2026-07-07 with first entry 2010-03-10 and last 2026-04-13. No truncation in the sweep (it passes no global --start) and none in backtest_trend.py's loader.

SO WHY ONLY ~65 TRADES? MEASURED, not inferred:
  IWM  65 trades  mean hold 26.95 bars (39.2 cal days, median 28, max 172)  TIME IN MARKET 2546/6028 = 42.2%  exits: trail_stop 51, stop 13, timeout 1
  SPLG 72 trades  mean hold 27.40 bars (39.8 cal days, median 30, max 179)  TIME IN MARKET 2863/6023 = 47.5%  exits: trail_stop 56, stop 16

The arithmetic is internally consistent and closes the question: the leg alternates ~39 days IN and ~54 days OUT, a ~93-day cycle = 3.9 entries/year, which is exactly the measured 3.94. For a Donchian-30 entry (needs a fresh 30-day high) with a 4.0-ATR trail, that cadence is the DESIGN working, not entries being suppressed. 65 trades over 16.5 years is correct.

THE ACTUAL CONSTRAINT, restated correctly: at ~4 entries/year a per-leg OOS window of 25 trades consumes ~6.3 years of history, and `lifetime // 2` caps the derived OOS at ~32. These legs are gradeable (32 > 25) but sit permanently near the floor, and NO amount of additional backtesting or waiting changes it -- the binding term is the strategy's trade rate against the evidence standard. Pooling was measured and ruled out on 2026-08-13 (both same-family 1d pools give ZERO usable folds).

ALSO SURFACED: `SCHA` is NOT in build_trainer_datasets.sh's equity symbol list (`SPY QQQ GLD TLT IWM SLV IEF TQQQ QLD SPLG IAUM`), yet `SCHA_1d.csv` exists with 4,151 rows and a live leg trades it. Where that frame is produced and whether it is refreshed by the normal cycle is unaccounted for.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) The measured trade rate (IWM 65 trades / 6,028 calendar days = 3.94 entries/year; SPLG 72 / 6,023 = 4.37) and the measured time in market (IWM 2,546 of 6,028 calendar days = 42.2%; SPLG 2,863 of 6,023 = 47.5%) are recorded where a future session meets the constraint -- beside the legs' matrix cells or in the M20 memo -- so nobody re-derives 'the window is thin' as a data or accrual problem a third time. (2) An explicit decision is recorded on what evidence standard applies to a ~4-trade/year leg, given per-leg OOS >= 25 leaves ~32 as the ceiling and pooling is already ruled out: either the standard is met as-is and these legs are simply always near the floor, or the fleet is declared ungradeable to that standard and the reason is written down. It must NOT stay implicit. (3) The SCHA frame's provenance is established -- which builder writes it, on what cadence -- or SCHA is added to the builder list. A live leg trading a frame no documented job refreshes is a staleness risk independent of M20. (4) Any future claim about a leg's trade count states whether it is a BACKTEST or LIVE count; conflating them is what produced the wrong answer here.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Criterion (1) is unmet: the measured figures do not appear where a future session meets the constraint — searching the matrix JSON for '3.94', '4.37', 'entries/year' and 'time in market' finds no such record on any iwm/splg cell (the two '3.94'/'4.37' hits are unrelated numbers in other refs), and grep over docs/research/*.md finds no '65 trades … 6,028 days' record either. Criteria (2)-(4) (an explicit evidence-standard decision, SCHA frame provenance) are likewise unrecorded. — Cheap docs work, but it partly overlaps the operator decision in BL-20260813-M20-DONE-CONDITION-IS-60PCT-ONE-FACT-THE-1D-FLEET-IS-TOO-THIN (criterion 2 is an evidence-standard call).

Re-validated and it is the STRUCTURAL reason the 1d fleet blocks — corroborated by BL-20260813-M20-DONE-CONDITION-IS-60PCT-ONE-FACT-THE-1D-FLEET-IS-TOO-THIN. The OOS window is capped by the strategy's trade rate, so no amount of tooling fixes it. This should be treated as a design constraint, not a backlog item to grind.

items.title: matrix-corpus-agreement reported 376 live cells as 'checked' when 141 of 376 (37.5%) sat in lever columns holding ZERO corpus rows
items.detail:
THE DEFECT. `find_disagreements` looks up each cell's corpus evidence and, on `hit is None`, continues. That branch cannot distinguish 'corpus rows exist for this lever and none contradicts' from 'this lever has NO corpus rows at all', and the summary counted both as checked.

MEASURED on the committed pair (2026-08-14): 3 of the 8 lever columns hold ZERO of the 922 corpus rows -- `exit_ladder` 0, `exit_head_ml` 0, `regime_flip_exit` 0. Positive control, so the zero is a reading and not a broken accessor: trail_decay 278, vol_trail 191, stale_stop 190, giveback_stop 150, trail_geometry 112; a raw `grep -c exit_head` on the corpus returns 0 against 288 for trail_decay. So the reassuring line '376 live cell(s) checked against 922 corpus row(s)' actually covered 235. The other 141 of 376 (37.5%) were unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION, and 115 of them carry an explicit `honest_negative` -- a stated negative outcome resting on evidence the guard implied it had verified.

THE CLASS. Sub-class C, an unasserted denominator (CLAUDE.md, 'Diagnostic provenance'). The file already argued this exact principle at its INPUT-MISSING branch -- 'an empty denominator reading as OK is the failure this whole family exists for' -- so a missing FILE was guarded while a missing COLUMN, one level down, was not. Found by USING the guard while scoping operator decision (a), the same way its own per-cell supersession bug was found.

WHY THE THREE ARE EMPTY, and it is structural in each case: `exit_head_ml` is measured by `scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py`, whose `--out` is a REQUIRED ephemeral directory (round_report.json / emit/*.jsonl) run on the trainer VM via `research-exit-head-replay-trainer.yml`, and nothing is committed back -- there is no `round_report.json` or `e1_report.json` anywhere in the repo. `exit_ladder` is an observe-only shadow soak, not a fleet sweep. `regime_flip_exit` has no runtime implementation at all to sweep (building it is operator decision (c)).

CONSEQUENCE BEYOND THE GUARD. Operator decision (d) -- 'establish the re-sweep base rate from the corpus, per gate, without pooling incomparable measurements' -- is NOT EXECUTABLE for `exit_head_ml`, because that lever has no corpus. And decision (a) (the ETH hypothesis) can be answered from the MATRIX alone only by pooling cells whose geometries are unknown: ETH 3/6 pass vs non-ETH 6/30 = 50% vs 20%, Fisher one-sided p=0.15, NOT significant -- but `tp_geometry` is recorded on 10 of 376 cells (2.7%), so comparability cannot be established, and pooling across geometries is precisely the trap (d) exists to avoid. That number is therefore a bound on what the record can currently say, not a settlement of (a). | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'resolved (guard); follow-up OPEN, see resolution_criteria (3)' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) DONE -- the guard reports `checked` and `NOT CHECKED` as SEPARATE counts and never sums them (the sum is the number that misled); real-tree output is now '235 live cell(s) checked ... NOT CHECKED ...: 141 of 376 live cell(s) across 3 of 8 column(s)'. items.title: exit_head_ml: NEITHER symbol NOR book size explains the E1 verdict — both refuted on held-out strata; ETH 2/3 vs non-ETH 4/11 (p=0.38) across 3 live-parity families
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 via `scripts/research/m20_exit_head_denominator.py` (reproducible; reads the committed matrix), executing operator decision (a) -- 'test the ETH hypothesis with a denominator'.

POPULATION: 20 of the 36 resolved exit_head_ml cells -- those whose ref states an `n_oos`. 16 are excluded for stating none. Geometries are MIXED across the 20 (only 5 confirmed live-parity), which is why the pooled figures below are a BOUND on what the record can say rather than a result.

THE HYPOTHESIS INVERTS. Two ETH legs passing had attracted a symbol explanation. Head to head on the same 20 cells: `is ETH` classifies the verdict at 80.0% accuracy (ETH 3 of 3 pass, non-ETH 4 of 17); a single threshold `n_oos >= 350` classifies it at 90.0% (big-book 6 of 7 pass, small-book 1 of 13). Holding book size fixed, the symbol adds essentially nothing: in the large-book stratum ETH is 2 of 2 and NON-ETH IS 4 OF 5. Everything left of the 'ETH effect' is ONE cell -- ict_scalp_eth_15m, the only pass among 13 small books (Fisher one-sided p=0.0769, n=13). Medians: PASS 600 (range 300-902, n=7) vs FAIL 168 (range 29-1000, n=13).

WHY THIS IS ABOUT THE GATE, NOT ABOUT ETH. The E1 gate is a FOLD-COUNT (train_exit_head.py): candidate requires mean_auc>0.55 AND beats_actual*3>=u*2 AND beats_hard*3>=u*2 -- at least two-thirds of folds on the right side. Per-fold noise falls as trades-per-fold rises, so a thin book has fewer chances to land two-thirds of its folds correctly WHETHER OR NOT THE HEAD HELPS IT. A gate whose outcome is 90% predicted by book size is substantially a POWER TEST, and a small-book `honest_negative` is then nearer to 'underpowered' than to 'the head does not work here' -- a distinction the status vocabulary cannot currently express, which is the same collapsed-state shape this repo keeps finding. Note the correlation is partly DEFINITIONAL (n_oos feeds the fold counts), which strengthens the power-test reading and weakens any causal claim about book size as such.

THE ONE INTERNALLY-CLEAN STRATUM still points at ETH, and is underpowered by construction: trend_donchian 1h at live parity (relays #9206 main / #9156-58 prop; one geometry, one strategy, one calendar window) is ETH 2 of 2, non-ETH 0 of 3, Fisher one-sided p=0.10, n=5. But WITHIN it the highest AUC belongs to a FAILING leg -- trend_donchian_sol 0.6161 vs trend_donchian_eth 0.6079 and trend_donchian_eth_prop 0.6138 -- so whatever separates them is NOT the head's discrimination; it is fold consistency, which is the book-size axis again. And the n_oos ordering separates the stratum perfectly (passes 902/566, fails 311/298/273), so at n=5 these two explanations are not distinguishable.

TWO EXCEPTIONS THAT BOUND THE CLAIM: ict_scalp_avax_5m FAILS on the LARGEST book in the set (n_oos=1000), so size is necessary and not sufficient; ict_scalp_eth_15m PASSES on 300, the only sub-threshold pass. The 350 threshold is the best single split ON THIS SAME SAMPLE, so 90.0% is an upper bound on out-of-sample separation, not an estimate of it.

=== UPDATE 2026-08-14, SAME DAY: the 2h live-parity round settles both explanations, and the answer is neither ===

A matched round was dispatched and completed on the trainer (relays #9271 launch / #9282 report; round `eth_denom_2h_20260814T130657Z`, `_round_meta.tp_geometry: live_parity`, `tp_cap_pct: 0.099`, `--tp-cap-pct` passed EXPLICITLY rather than defaulted): the whole 2h pullback family at ONE geometry, 2 ETH legs vs 5 non-ETH controls. It is genuine held-out data for the `n_oos >= 350` split, which was fitted on the earlier 20 mixed-geometry cells.

**BOOK SIZE IS REFUTED.** On the 2h stratum the split scores **1 of 7 = 14.3%**, against 90.0% in-sample — worse than a coin. The two LARGEST books both FAIL (htf_pullback_trend_2h n_oos 400, avax_pullback_2h 357) and the SMALLEST pass (ada_pullback_2h 231) sits below the largest failure. The 90.0% was an in-sample artifact, which is exactly what the row above warned it might be — the threshold was chosen on the same sample it was scored on. This is the rare case where the stated caveat was not decoration.

**THE ETH EFFECT SURVIVES BUT DOES NOT REACH SIGNIFICANCE.** Pooled over both live-parity strata (n=12): ETH **4 of 4**, non-ETH **2 of 8**, Fisher one-sided **p=0.0303**. But two of those four ETH rows are `_prop` siblings of the other two — same symbol, same strategy family, overlapping book — so counting them doubles a single observation. Dropping every prop sibling (n=9): ETH **2 of 2**, non-ETH **2 of 7**, **p=0.1667**. The significance turns ENTIRELY on that choice, so it is reported both ways rather than picked. Honest reading: no non-ETH leg in either family matches ETH's record, and the sample cannot establish that as more than chance.

**WHAT IS ACTUALLY BINDING.** All three 2h negatives fail on `beats_hard` (22/43, 26/42, 25/41 against a 2/3 bar), while two of them PASS `beats_actual`. `sol_pullback_2h` carries the stratum's second-highest auc (0.6330) and still fails. So the separating axis is fold consistency against the CHEAP LEVER, not the head's discrimination and not book size — and what drives it is now explicitly unexplained rather than wrongly attributed.

**A committed artifact now exists** — `docs/research/m20-exit-head-rounds.jsonl`, 12 rows, each carrying its own `tp_geometry` stamp and provenance, every verdict re-derived from the gate rather than copied. This is the first exit-head evidence file in the repo and it is the start of the fix for item (3) below.

=== UPDATE 2 — 2026-08-14, the 4h stratum settles it: the answer is NEITHER ===

A third matched round (relays #9288 launch / #9294 report; `eth_denom_4h_20260814T134036Z`, `tp_geometry: live_parity`, `tp_cap_pct: 0.099` passed EXPLICITLY) ran the whole 4h trend_donchian family. This family has NO `_prop` siblings, so all five rows are independent observations — which is precisely the weakness in the earlier pooled figure.

**ETH FAILED.** `trend_donchian_eth_4h` n_oos=161, auc=0.6285, beats_actual 12/16, beats_hard **9/16** against an 11-of-16 bar → honest_negative. Meanwhile `trend_donchian_ada_4h` (13/16 & 13/16) and `trend_donchian_xrp_4h` (13/16 & 11/16) both → candidate. ETH 0 of 1, non-ETH 2 of 4 in this stratum. Every verdict was re-derived from the gate before being recorded.

**THE P-VALUE MOVED AWAY FROM THE CLAIM, WHICH IS THE POINT:**
  n=12, prop siblings counted -> ETH 4/4 vs 2/8   p=0.0303  (the earlier, arguably-significant read)
  n=17, all three strata      -> ETH 4/5 vs 4/12  p=0.1109
  n=14, prop siblings dropped -> ETH 2/3 vs 4/11  p=0.3846  (the honest figure)
The single arguably-significant reading was an artifact of a small sample plus double-counted prop legs, and it did not survive a third family.

**BOOK SIZE IS REFUTED A SECOND TIME, INDEPENDENTLY:** in the 4h stratum the SMALLEST book passes (n_oos 123, XRP) while the LARGEST fails (188, AVAX). That is a separate refutation from the 2h one, where the fitted `n_oos >= 350` split scored 1 of 7 = 14.3% against 90.0% in-sample.

**WHAT REMAINS, and it is deliberately named as unexplained rather than given a third wrong cause:** the separating axis is fold consistency against the CHEAP LEVER (`beats_hard`). Across 2h and 4h, negatives fail there while passing or nearly passing `beats_actual`, and legs carrying a stratum's HIGHEST auc still fail (`sol_pullback_2h` 0.6330; `trend_donchian_avax_4h` fails at 0.6226 while XRP passes at 0.6554 on a smaller book). Neither discrimination nor sample size orders these.

**Running totals:** 15 of the 29 negative cells have now been re-measured at live parity; **6 did not survive** (eth/xrp/ada/eth_prop pullback_2h, xrp/ada donchian_4h). **14 negatives have still NEVER been measured at the geometry production places** (1h 6, 1d 6, 5m 1, 15m 1). The 6/15 flip rate ships beside its denominator and scope (2 families, 3 timeframes) and is NOT projected onto the 14. Evidence file is now 17 rows.

=== UPDATE 3 — 2026-08-14, the 15m scalp round: a recorded POSITIVE did not survive ===

Round `scalp_15m_20260814T135244Z` (relays #9297 / #9307). Every re-measurement before this one was of a NEGATIVE, so the only observed risk was 'a negative might really be a pass'. This round was set up to test the other direction, because the scalp family holds 5 of the 6 `passed_unshipped` cells in the column and had never been measured at a comparable geometry.

**`ict_scalp_eth_15m`, recorded `passed_unshipped`, came back `honest_negative`** — n_oos=550, auc=0.6083, beats_actual 9/11, **beats_hard 4/11** against an 8-of-11 bar. `ict_scalp_sol_15m` reproduced (candidate) and `ict_scalp_xrp_15m` flipped negative→candidate. So a recorded positive CAN fail a re-measurement, and that is the more expensive direction: a `passed_unshipped` cell is what would justify shipping a lever onto a live leg. Running totals now split by direction — positives 4 of 7 re-measured, **1 did not survive**, 3 never re-measured; negatives 16 re-measured, 7 did not survive.

**AND IT ENDS THE ETH STORY COMPLETELY.** `ict_scalp_eth_15m` was the single cell the 'only small-book pass was ETH' observation rested on. It is gone. ETH is now 0/1 in the 15m stratum (non-ETH 2/2), 0/1 in the 4h (non-ETH 2/4), and the honest pooled capped figure remains ETH 2/3 vs non-ETH 4/11, p=0.3846.

**GEOMETRY — recorded by hand, NOT from the stamp.** That round ran the pre-fix driver, whose `_round_meta` claimed `live_parity` from the run flag. The correct label is **`live_parity_uncapped`**: `grep -c -- --tp-cap-pct` over the round log = 0, and the live `ict_scalp` unit carries no clamp, so an uncapped book IS parity for that unit. It is NOT the same geometry as the capped donchian/pullback rounds. The analysis script now STRATIFIES by geometry rather than pooling — and its pre-existing single-geometry assert FIRED when these rows landed, which is the behaviour wanted: it refused to average two things rather than quietly doing it.

⚠️ **A power caveat that cuts against reading too much into this round:** its fold counts are 9–11, against 41–43 in the 2h round and 16 in the 4h. The gate is clearing two-thirds of a much smaller denominator, so single-fold noise moves a verdict far more easily here. Noted and not corrected for.

That is the finding's actionable half and it is a vocabulary/reporting change, not a gate change. (2) DONE for 2h (see the UPDATE: refutes book size, leaves ETH unproven). DONE for 4h too (ETH fails; book size refuted again). DONE for 15m (a positive failed; ETH story ended). Remaining: the 5m scalp stratum — re-run (2h pullback, 4h donchian, 15m/5m scalp) at LIVE PARITY so ETH-vs-control can be compared at one geometry beyond the single trend_donchian 1h family; the eth_prop ref already identifies this as the test that would settle the scalp-scoping question, and it is the same run that would settle (a). items.title: scripts/ci/run_guards.py consumed /tmp/pr.diff but never wrote it, so every local run scanned a STALE diff and reported 'All relevant guards passed'
items.detail:
THE DEFECT. 8 of the 38 registered guards take `{pr_diff}` and scan ONLY that file (api-tier-policy, diagnostic-provenance, dry-run, env-gate, new-table-wiring, silent-empty, strategy-risk-field, writer-conformance). CI builds it in a SEPARATE `guards.yml` step (`git diff origin/<base>...HEAD > /tmp/pr.diff`, line 93) and exports GUARDS_PR_DIFF. `run_guards.py` never wrote it -- it only read `--pr-diff`, defaulting to the fixed path `/tmp/pr.diff`. So a LOCAL run scanned whatever a previous run had left there. A file absent from that stale diff is never scanned at all, and the harness prints 'All relevant guards passed'.

MEASURED 2026-08-14. Three consecutive local runs reported `diagnostic-provenance-guard PASS (0.2s)` on a tree where CI failed that exact guard on the same commit -- identical command, identical path, different file contents. The CI finding was real (2 sub-class-C universal claims with no denominator in `m20_exit_head_denominator.py`). Rewriting /tmp/pr.diff by hand with `git diff origin/main...HEAD` and re-running reproduced the failure immediately.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE ONE FINDING. This session had already logged the recurring 'guards passed locally, failed on CI' pattern ELEVEN times and attributed it to running diff-scoped guards on uncommitted work. That diagnosis was incomplete: the harness itself could not see the change on ANY local run, committed or not. A stale diff is strictly worse than a missing one -- an absent file errors, a stale file PASSES -- which is why the failure always presented as a false green rather than a crash. It is also sub-class C in the harness that enforces sub-class C.

NOT A CI DEFECT: CI was always correct, because the workflow builds the diff itself. The gap was local-only, which is exactly the surface a session uses to decide whether to push.
items.resolution_criteria: DONE. `run_guards.py` now generates `{pr_diff}` from `origin/<base_ref>...HEAD` whenever no caller supplied one (GUARDS_PR_DIFF unset AND no `--pr-diff` argument), prints the path and line count so the scanned range is visible, and returns 2 rather than continuing if the diff cannot be produced -- refusing to scan a stale file instead of reporting a green that checked nothing. CI is untouched: it exports GUARDS_PR_DIFF, which suppresses generation, so the workflow's own range still wins. Verified by planting an EMPTY /tmp/pr.diff (regenerated to 1,070 lines), by confirming an explicit GUARDS_PR_DIFF is never overwritten, and by planting the real violation behind a stale diff and watching the run go rc=1 where it previously passed. Pinned by 2 tests in tests/test_run_guards_step_scoping.py, both proven load-bearing by removing the fix (1 failed).
refs: .github/workflows/guards.yml:93 (the step that builds the diff in CI)
scripts/check_diagnostic_provenance.py (the guard whose false green exposed this)
PR #9257 check_run 94775601819 (the CI failure that contradicted three local passes)

items.title: m20_exit_head_round stamped tp_geometry from the RUN-LEVEL flag, so a scalp round self-reported live_parity for a cap its harness never received
items.detail:
THE DEFECT. `_round_meta` computed `tp_geometry = 'live_parity' if a.tp_cap_pct > 0.0 else 'NO_TAKE_PROFIT'` -- a pure function of the CLI argument, applied to every leg in the round regardless of family. But `base_args` (m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:452) appends `--tp-cap-pct` ONLY when `fam in LIVE_TP_CAPPED_FAMILIES` = {donchian, pullback, fade, squeeze}. So a round over the `scalp` family emits harness commands with NO cap and then stamps the report `live_parity`.

CAUGHT BY READING THE RELAY OUTPUT, not the code: the 15m scalp launch (#9297) showed `backtest_ict_scalp.py --data ... --sim-breakeven --htf-rule 1h ... --emit-trades ...` with no `--tp-cap-pct` and no `--tp-r`, where the 2h/4h rounds visibly carried `--tp-cap-pct 0.099 --tp-r 50.0`.

⚠️ THE WITHHOLDING IS CORRECT; ONLY THE LABEL WAS WRONG. Verified rather than assumed: `grep -c _TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT src/units/strategies/ict_scalp.py` -> **0**, against **4** for `trend_donchian.py` (positive control, so the zero is a reading and not a broken probe). The live scalp unit does not clamp, so a scalp book WITHOUT a cap IS live parity for that unit. Passing the cap would have been the bug; stamping it as the same geometry as a capped donchian round is the bug that shipped.

THE CLASS, and it is a repeat. `diagnostic-provenance-guard` sub-class A (semantic substitution): the label names 'the geometry the book was built with'; the code reported 'the value of the CLI arg'. **`m20_fleet_exit_sweep` was already fixed for exactly this on 2026-08-10** -- its comment reads 'THE GEOMETRY THIS LEG ACTUALLY RAN, not the one the run requested', after its PR banner printed 'LIVE-PARITY (capped TP 0.099)' over 8 ict_scalp legs and fvg_range_15m. The fix landed in one sibling and never propagated to the other, which is the more general lesson: a per-file fix for a class leaves every sibling that shares the class.

WHY IT MATTERED HERE. The stamp is what `docs/research/m20-exit-head-rounds.jsonl` records, and that file's ENTIRE value is that its geometry stamps can be trusted across strata -- it exists because this lever had no committed evidence at all. The 15m scalp round was running when this was found; recording its output would have put a false `live_parity` row beside 17 true ones and silently made every cross-stratum comparison unsound. The 17 existing rows are UNAFFECTED: 2h is `pullback` and 4h is `donchian`, both in LIVE_TP_CAPPED_FAMILIES, and their emit commands visibly carried the flag.
items.resolution_criteria: DONE. The stamp is now derived from `fams_seen` -- the families that ACTUALLY EMITTED trades, recorded after the harness returns rows so a skipped or failed leg cannot colour the label -- crossed with `LIVE_TP_CAPPED_FAMILIES`. Four states, never collapsed: `live_parity_capped` (cap applied, unit clamps) / `live_parity_uncapped` (no cap AND the unit does not clamp -- parity for that unit) / `NO_TAKE_PROFIT` (no cap on a family that DOES clamp live -- a book production does not run) / `MIXED_capped_and_uncapped_families` (a round spanning both says so rather than picking one). The two uncapped states are deliberately distinct: they mean the same mechanics for OPPOSITE reasons. `_round_meta` additionally ships `families`, `cap_applied_to_families` and `cap_withheld_from_families`, so a reader can CHECK the label rather than trust it. Pinned by 4 tests in tests/test_exit_head_round_geometry_stamp.py, including a positive-control assertion that the `_TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT` probe finds a non-zero in trend_donchian before believing the zero in ict_scalp; proven load-bearing by restoring the old one-line stamp (1 failed).
refs: scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:452 (base_args cap gate) + :100 (LIVE_TP_CAPPED_FAMILIES) + :2169 (the 2026-08-10 fix this never inherited)
trainer relay #9297 (the 15m scalp launch whose command exposed it)

items.title: 42 of 43 regime_flip_exit negatives were graded on NO-TAKE-PROFIT books: three sibling drivers still call base_args positionally, and none of them stamps a geometry
items.detail:
FOUND BY APPLYING THE LESSON FROM THE SAME DAY'S FIX, not by a new symptom. `BL-20260814-EXIT-HEAD-ROUND-STAMPS-LIVE-PARITY-ON-FAMILIES-THAT-NEVER-GOT-THE-CAP` ended with 'a per-file fix for a class leaves every sibling that shares the class'. Auditing the other `base_args` callers found three that still carry the ORIGINAL defect (`BL-20260814-EXIT-HEAD-ROUNDS-CANNOT-MODEL-LIVE-TP`), which the exit-head driver was fixed for earlier today:

  scripts/research/m20_flip_replay_sweep.py:65   base_args(name, cfg, fam, data, resample)
  scripts/research/m21_entry_head_round.py:125   base_args(name, cfg, fam, data, resample)
  scripts/research/m21_entry_sweep.py:133        base_args(name, cfg, fam, data, resample)

`tp_cap_pct` is the 6th positional parameter and defaults to `0.0`, and `base_args` gates on `if tp_cap_pct > 0.0 and fam in LIVE_TP_CAPPED_FAMILIES`. DEMONSTRATED rather than reasoned, on a real leg (`trend_donchian_eth_4h`, family `donchian`): the sibling call shape yields `--tp-cap-pct present: False | --tp-r present: False`, the exit-head call shape yields `True | True`. So the sibling books have **no take-profit target at all** — not merely an uncapped one — for every donchian/pullback/fade/squeeze leg.

**IMPACT, and it is larger by cell count than the exit-head instance.** `m20_flip_replay_sweep` is what produced the `regime_flip_exit` column. Measured against the committed matrix: the column holds 43 `honest_negative`, 8 `n/a`, 1 `pending`, and **42 of the 43 negatives are capped-family legs** (donchian 22, pullback 19, squeeze 1). So essentially the entire regime_flip_exit negative column was graded on a book production does not run, on legs whose live unit clamps TP at 9.9%.

**AND IT IS INVISIBLE.** Unlike the exit-head driver — which at least stamped a geometry, even a wrong one — these three write NO geometry field at all (`grep -c 'tp_cap|geometry'` returns 0 for both m21 drivers). There is no field in their output a reader could check, which is why 42 cells accumulated without anyone noticing. That is sub-class C, an unasserted denominator, in the strongest form: not a mislabelled value but an absent one.

**WHY THIS IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY 'RE-RUN EVERYTHING'.** A regime-flip exit fires on an ADX regime flip, and a take-profit that closes the trade EARLIER mechanically removes opportunities for a later flip to fire — so a no-TP book plausibly OVERSTATES the flip lever's opportunity, meaning the negatives may hold or even strengthen at live parity. That is a hypothesis about the direction, not a result; the point is that nobody has measured it and the column reads as though someone had.

**Scope note:** `m20_flip_replay_sweep` is M20 (mine). The two `m21_entry_*` drivers belong to the entry-head workstream, so their books are conditioned the same way but the call is not mine to make unilaterally.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) Decide, per driver, whether its book SHOULD be live-parity. For `m20_flip_replay_sweep` the answer is almost certainly yes — its verdicts feed a matrix column that is read as evidence about live legs — in which case pass `tp_cap_pct` through and re-run, treating the existing 42 negatives as provisional until they reproduce. (2) Whatever is decided, every one of these drivers must STAMP the geometry it ran, using the same four-state derivation now in `m20_exit_head_round.py` (`live_parity_capped` / `live_parity_uncapped` / `NO_TAKE_PROFIT` / `MIXED_capped_and_uncapped_families`), so the next reader can check rather than trust. An unstamped research output is the condition that let 42 cells accumulate silently. (3) Consider a guard asserting that any caller of `base_args` either passes `tp_cap_pct` explicitly or records why it does not — the positional default is what makes this failure silent and repeatable, and it has now recurred in four drivers.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Criteria (1) and (2) are done for all three drivers: m20_flip_replay_sweep.py:84, m21_entry_head_round.py:130 and m21_entry_sweep.py:142 now pass `a.tp_cap_pct` as the 6th positional to base_args, and each stamps geometry through the shared `tp_geometry_for` (m20_flip_replay_sweep.py:119,144,157; m21_entry_sweep.py:144; m21_entry_head_round.py:131). Criterion (3) is not: no guard asserts that a base_args caller passes tp_cap_pct (grep over scripts/ci/ and scripts/check_*.py finds no base_args reference), and the 42 regime_flip_exit negatives have not been re-run — matrix-corpus-agreement still reports regime_flip_exit among '141 live cell(s) NOT CHECKED'. — needs a re-run of the flip replays at live parity to retire the 42 provisional negatives; the positional-default guard is the durable half.

Re-validated: 42 of 43 negatives graded on NO-TAKE-PROFIT books. This is the single largest evidence-invalidation in the M20 program and it shares one root with BL-20260814-EXIT-HEAD-ROUNDS-CANNOT-MODEL-LIVE-TP and BL-20260816-M21-ENTRY-SWEEPS-STILL-CALL-BASE-ARGS-POSITIONALLY: base_args called POSITIONALLY in every sibling driver. One fix, three rows, ~70 invalidated verdicts.

MEASURED 2026-08-14 while resolving the NEXT conflict in the same file (merge a38123cd on claude/m20-exit-coverage-matrix-8d3he7).

WHAT HAPPENED. This backlog is append-only in intent, so a conflict here looks purely additive and invites the fast resolution: keep my new items, keep theirs, move on. It is not purely additive. Sessions also EDIT existing items — adding history, flipping status, stamping resolved_at. My earlier merge (c601d82e) resolved the conflict by taking my side of the overlapping region, which silently discarded main's edits to six items that I had never touched:

  BL-20260814-IB-EVENTLOOP-CONTENTION                       status resolved -> mitigated_fix_in_pr, resolved_at cleared
  BL-20260814-IB-MARKETDATA-VS-ACCOUNT-LOCK-GAP
  BL-20260814-EXIT-PASS-SLOWER-THAN-M20
  BL-20260814-REACHABILITY-PROBES-POSITIONS-NOT-BALANCE      (main-side, survived)
  BL-20260813-ALPACA-BALANCE-NONE-WHILE-ACCOUNT-READS-ACTIVE
  BL-20260730-PR-CI-NOT-ATTACHING
  BL-20260807-IBPAPER-UPNL-CONTRADICTS-EXCHANGE-TRUTH

The IB-EVENTLOOP one is the sharp end: another session closed that item, and my merge REOPENED it. A reopened item is not a loud failure — it looks exactly like an item that was never closed, so the next reader re-investigates work already done, and the session that closed it has no way to notice.

HOW IT WAS CAUGHT, AND WHY THAT IS THE ACTUAL FINDING. Not by review and not by CI — by my doing the three-way classification on the NEXT conflict instead of resolving it by hand again. Comparing both sides against the merge base separates 'they changed it' from 'I changed it' from 'both changed it'; that immediately showed 8 shared items differing, 0 changed by both, and 6 whose divergence I could not account for. Walking all 11 of my own non-merge commits that touch the file confirmed NONE of them had edited those six. The reversion was invisible to every other check available: the file parses, the item count only grows, and no guard reads item status transitions.

WHY A GUARD IS THE RIGHT ANSWER RATHER THAN 'BE MORE CAREFUL'. The failure mode is a merge that LOSES information while every surface-level invariant (valid JSON, monotonic item count, no duplicate ids) still holds. Those invariants are exactly what a careful person spot-checks. A status going resolved -> open across a merge is mechanically detectable and semantically almost never intended.
items.resolution_criteria: A CI guard (diff-scoped, the canonical-db-resolver / silent-empty-guard family) fails when a commit moves any backlog item from a terminal status (resolved / fixed / measured_no_action / invalid) to a non-terminal one, or clears a populated resolved_at, unless the same commit records why. Item COUNT is not a sufficient invariant and must not be what the guard checks.
items.what_to_check:
1. Whether any EARLIER merge on any branch did the same thing and has not been undone — this one was caught only because a second conflict followed. A sweep of `git log -p` on this file for terminal->non-terminal status transitions would establish the denominator; I did not run it, so the count of past instances is UNKNOWN, not zero.
2. Whether performance-review-backlog.json and ml-review-backlog.json (same shape, same multi-session write pattern) have the same exposure. Almost certainly yes; unverified.
3. Whether the coordination board protocol should say anything about this file specifically — it is the one artifact nearly every session writes to, which is what makes it the most likely to be concurrently edited.
