items.title: ict_scalp_5m is a LIVE leg on BTCUSDT whose 5m data is unreachable to the sweep harnesses: every other 5m symbol has data/<SYM>_5m.csv, BTC has only data/backtest_BTCUSDT_5m.csv, and resolve_data's prefix set is {btcusdt, btc} so the backtest_-prefixed name matches nothing.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-14. The 5m exit-head round (trainer-diag #9321) printed `SKIP ict_scalp_5m: data_missing:BTCUSDT` while its three siblings ran fine.

DIRECTORY LISTING, from the trainer:
  5m CSVs present: ADAUSDT_5m, AVAXUSDT_5m, BNBUSDT_5m, ETHUSDT_5m, LINKUSDT_5m, SOLUSDT_5m, XRPUSDT_5m, backtest_BTCUSDT_5m
  BTCUSDT files  : BTCUSDT_15m.csv only
So BTC is the ONE 5m symbol without the canonical spelling, and the only BTC 5m bytes on disk wear a `backtest_` prefix.

MECHANISM, read from the code rather than inferred (scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:148-174). resolve_data tries, in order: (a) data/{SYM}_{tf}.csv -> absent; (b) each finer grain data/{SYM}_{g}.csv -> absent, and the loop BREAKS at the first grain coarser than the leg, so BTCUSDT_15m.csv is correctly not substituted for a 5m leg; (c) a case-insensitive prefix glob over prefixes = {sym.lower()} plus the USDT-stripped base, i.e. {'btcusdt','btc'}, matching only names starting with '<prefix>_' or equal to '<prefix>.csv'. 'backtest_btcusdt_5m.csv' starts with 'backtest_'. It matches nothing, so the resolver returns None and the leg is skipped.

The resolver is not obviously wrong here — a file whose name leads with an unrelated token has unknown provenance, and this repo has been burned specifically by a filename asserting a provenance its CONTENT did not have (see the prefer_native docstring in the same module: a session converted a yfinance-derived series into data/MGC_1d.csv, whose NAME then claimed native IBKR history, and the head round would have trained on exactly the series it refuses). So silently globbing backtest_*.csv into the canonical slot would repeat that.

WHAT THIS COSTS. ict_scalp_5m carries a `passed_unshipped` exit_head_ml cell that is one of only three recorded positives never re-measured at live parity. It is a LIVE leg. Its cell therefore cannot be confirmed or refuted at its own timeframe by any current harness, and the coverage matrix has no way to say so — the cell reads like the other unmeasured ones rather than like one that is structurally unmeasurable. That is the collapsed-state shape again: 'not yet measured' and 'cannot be measured with what is on disk' are different states.

WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING. That backtest_BTCUSDT_5m.csv is BTC 5m OHLCV of usable range and provenance. I have not opened it. Row count, date range, columns and whether anything in the repo writes or reads it are the subject of trainer-diag #9324; until that returns, the right disposition (rename/copy to the canonical slot, build a fresh 5m series, or record the leg as structurally unmeasurable) is undetermined.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY CONSULTED FOR THE 'cannot be measured' CLAIM, so the next reader inherits the evidence and not just the conclusion: the resolver body was READ, line by line, not inferred from the skip message — checked: scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py (the _resolve_one/resolve_data pair at 148-174: the native spelling, the grain loop and its break condition, and the prefix-glob fallback with prefixes = {sym.lower()} plus the USDT-stripped base). The skip SITE was read too — checked: scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py — to confirm the leg is dropped at resolve_data returning None rather than at the separate proxy refusal two lines below, which produces a DIFFERENT message. The directory listing behind 'BTC is the one 5m symbol without the canonical spelling' is trainer-diag #9321, an ls of data/*_5m.csv on the trainer, with the seven sibling symbols as the positive control — a resolver that found nothing for every symbol would prove nothing about BTC.

=== UPDATE, trainer-diag #9324: the file is characterized, and the obvious fix is REFUTED ===

WHAT backtest_BTCUSDT_5m.csv IS. Real BTC 5m OHLCV, same schema as the canonical siblings (timestamp,open,high,low,close,volume), 647,585 rows / 41.3 MB, 2020-03-25 .. 2026-05-21. It is DEEPER than any canonical alt 5m file (SOLUSDT_5m is 491,696 rows from 2021-10-15). It is also not obscure: it is the repo's standard BTC 5m feed, named as the DEFAULT in six scripts — fit_calibrators.sh:47, run_serious_baseline.sh:166, walkforward_vol_threshold.sh:29, walkforward_cell_selection.py:59, walkforward_evidence_cells.sh:26, walkforward_vol_gating.sh:16 — and cited in S-M36-TRACK-D as 'the 647,586-bar data/backtest_BTCUSDT_5m.csv 5m feed'. The vol-gating walk-forwards that justify the LIVE regime-router OFF cells on real money were run against it. So the data is trusted at the highest evidence bar this repo has; only the M20 harnesses cannot see it, purely because of the filename prefix.

THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG, AND THIS IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING. Creating data/BTCUSDT_5m.csv (copy or symlink) would make the leg resolve — and would silently change the data basis of every OTHER BTC leg. DATA_GRAIN is ['5m','15m','1h','1d'], FINEST FIRST, and the grain loop takes the first present file at or below the leg's timeframe. Today a BTC 1h/2h/4h/1d leg finds no BTCUSDT_5m.csv, falls through to BTCUSDT_15m.csv and resamples. With the new file it would take the 5m one instead — and the 5m series ENDS 2026-05-21 while the 15m ends 2026-07-10, so every BTC leg coarser than 15m would quietly LOSE ~7 weeks of the most recent history, including legs whose verdicts are already recorded in the matrix. That is precisely the hazard resolve_data's own docstring names: 'flipping which series a RECORDED verdict was measured against must not ride along silently inside a reachability fix.' The reachability fix here would have done exactly that, one level less visibly than the MGC_1d.csv incident because the NAME would have been honest and only the RANGE dishonest.

TWO PROPERTIES OF THE FILE TO CARRY FORWARD, neither disqualifying, both unstated anywhere:
  * Its FIRST bar is 2020-03-25T10:35:00Z with open=high=low=close=6500.0 and volume=0.001 — a flat bar at a round number with dust volume, i.e. a padding/placeholder row, not a traded bar. Whether the early history is gap-filled generally is NOT established by one row; it is a reason to check before using the 2020 era, not a reason to distrust the file.
  * It is ~7 weeks staler than BTCUSDT_15m and ~4 weeks staler than SOLUSDT_5m. A 5m round that included BTC would therefore end BTC's book earlier than its three siblings', shifting the OOS window for one leg only — a comparability caveat that must be stated in any round that mixes them.

PROPOSED NARROW FIX (not yet applied). Probe backtest_{SYM}_{tf}.csv immediately after the native {SYM}_{tf}.csv spelling and NOWHERE ELSE — specifically not inside the grain loop. An exact-tf-only probe cannot alter any leg that resolves today, because it fires only where the native spelling is absent AND a backtest_ file of the leg's own timeframe exists. This must be PROVEN by enumerating every live leg's resolution before and after and showing the only diff is BTCUSDT@5m, not argued from the code shape — data/backtest_ESF_1h.csv also exists and is the obvious way this could bite.

=== RESOLVED (partially), trainer-diag #9325 + the exact-tf probe ===

The enumeration was run before touching the resolver and it CORRECTED my own claim. I had written 'the only changed resolution is BTCUSDT@5m', i.e. one leg. Over 110 (leg x symbol x prefer_native) resolutions the probe changes FOUR: ict_scalp_5m (execution live) AND vwap (execution shadow), each in both modes. I had missed that vwap also sits at BTCUSDT 5m. The count was wrong; the safety claim was not, and the enumeration is what distinguishes those two.

WHAT MAKES IT SAFE is stronger than 'few changes': ALL FOUR are None -> resolved. Not one resolution that exists today moves, so no recorded verdict's data basis can shift — which was the entire objection to the copy-to-canonical-slot fix. data/backtest_ESF_1h.csv, the risk I named in advance, is inert: no leg sits at (ESF, 1h). data/backtest_candles.csv does not parse as (sym, tf) at all.

SHIPPED: an exact-timeframe probe in _resolve_one, immediately after the native spelling and deliberately NOT in the grain loop. tests/test_resolve_data_backtest_prefix.py pins the property that matters — a 1h/2h/4h/1d leg must NOT pick up a 5m backtest_ file, and with both files present the canonical 15m one must keep serving 1h. Both were proven load-bearing by planting the harmful version (moving the probe into the grain loop): both fail, and pass again on restore. A sixth test asserts DATA_GRAIN is still finest-first, because the leak test would pass VACUOUSLY under a coarsest-first order while the hazard changed shape.

STILL OPEN: ict_scalp_5m's exit_head_ml cell is now REACHABLE but has not been re-measured. When it is, the round must state that BTC's book ends 2026-05-21 while its three 5m siblings run to 2026-06-18, so the OOS window differs for one leg.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) the exact-tf backtest_ probe lands WITH a before/after enumeration over every live leg showing BTCUSDT@5m as the only changed resolution, and ict_scalp_5m's exit_head_ml cell is re-measured at live parity with its shorter book stated; or (b) a canonical BTCUSDT_5m series is built that extends to at least the 15m file's end date, so no leg loses history. A bare copy/symlink of the existing file into the canonical slot is REFUTED and must not be the fix.

items.title: docs/research/m20-exit-head-rounds.jsonl mixed FAMILY-POOLED and PER-LEG E1 block cuts in one file with no field distinguishing them — 17 of 23 rows pooled — inviting exactly the incomparable-evidence comparison the repo already documents as invalid.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 while launching the 1h pullback round.

MECHANISM. build_exit_head_dataset.family_of collapses every leg whose name contains 'pullback'/'donchian' or starts with 'trend_' into ONE family directory; scalp legs fall through the branch chain and keep their own name. So a pullback or donchian round cuts its E1 blocks over the FAMILY's POOLED trades and each per-leg verdict is that leg's slice within them, while a scalp round cuts blocks on the leg alone. Observed directly in two round logs: the 5m scalp round built three family dirs (ict_scalp_avax_5m / _sol_5m / _xrp_5m, 27513 / 22120 / 21258 rows); the 1h pullback round built ONE ('pullback: 35609 rows, trades {'harness': 1367}') for four legs.

WHY IT MATTERS, and it is not my judgement — it is already the repo's. train_exit_head's own per_leg_note calls the family-pooled block 'the right unit to TRAIN on and the wrong one to record a verdict from', and iwm_trend_long_1d's matrix cell explicitly DECLINES to grade from a pooled verdict, calling those 'the weakest verdicts in the programme'. So the file was carrying 17 rows of a kind the repo says should not be graded from, beside 6 of a kind that can be, with nothing marking the difference. tp_geometry covers the CAP axis and says nothing about the BLOCK axis.

SCALE OF THE POOLING DIFFERS AND I AM NOT FLATTENING IT. The iwm criticism targets 'allmix', which pools across FAMILIES and reaches a median n_leg of 5. A pullback-only pooled dir is milder: at 1397 pooled trades a 50-trade block holds roughly 12 gld trades and 19 tlt ones. Milder is not the same as comparable-to-per-leg, so the field records WHICH unit rather than grading the rows.

FIXED: `block_unit` added to the schema, backfilled across all 23 rows, and emitted by m20_exit_head_round.py — derived by IMPORTING family_of from the build rather than re-implementing it, so the label cannot drift from the grouping that actually cut the blocks (the same delegation rule regime_flip_exit follows against the live gate). A `block_unit_note` field was tried and removed: a 700-char identical string on every row is documentation, not data, and the schema test correctly caught the emitter/file mismatch it created. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'fixed (field added + backfilled + emitter writes it); the RE-GRADE question is queued' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.

2. Whether family_of SHOULD collapse these families at all, or whether the pooling is a training-only convenience that leaked into verdict recording. Not investigated.
3. Whether the matrix cells sourced from pooled rounds carry the caveat in their ref. Spot checks say some do (iwm) and some do not; not swept.

items.title: impossibility-claim-guard reports a line number that does not match the file, and the drift is variable — so its own +-6 annotation window is anchored in the wrong place and can miss a `checked:` annotation sitting 3 lines from the claim.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-14, twice, on docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json.

Instance 1: guard reported line 15238; the claim (an id containing CANNOT-BE-MEASURED) was at 15237 and the `detail` carrying the annotation at 15245 — an 8-line gap that the +-6 window could not reach.
Instance 2, after unrelated content was appended EARLIER in the file: guard reported 15240 while the same id sat at 15244 and its `evidence` annotation at 15247. The window computed around 15240 spans 15234-15246 and excludes 15247 BY ONE LINE — so an annotation three lines from the claim was invisible.

THE OFFSET IS NOT CONSTANT: 7 in the first instance, 4 in the second, and what changed between them was how much content was added ABOVE this item. That is the signature of line numbers reported in the DIFF's coordinate space rather than the file's.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ANNOYANCE. (a) The number in the error message does not locate the finding — a reader who opens that line sees an unrelated field, which is the unprovenanced-diagnostic shape the repo has a rule about: the label names a position the code did not compute. (b) Worse, the guard SEARCHES FOR THE ANNOTATION in a window around that wrong anchor, so satisfying it correctly can still fail, and the fix that works is moving the annotation to placate an off-by-N rather than to help the reader. I have now shuffled the same annotation twice for this reason.

NOT INVESTIGATED: whether the offset is exactly 'added lines above in this diff' or something else, and whether sibling diff-scoped guards (diagnostic-provenance, claim-basis, writer-conformance) share the mapping. They plausibly do, since they take the same `/tmp/pr.diff` shape.
items.what_to_check:
1. Map the reported line back to the file line and confirm the diff-coordinate hypothesis against a third instance before fixing — two points fit many curves.
2. Check whether the sibling diff-scoped guards report file lines or diff lines. If they share the bug, fix it once in the shared helper rather than per guard.
3. The ANNOTATION_WINDOW of 6 is only defensible if the anchor is right; widening it to paper over a bad anchor would be the wrong fix and would re-introduce the harvesting bug its own comment records (a whole-file scan once picked up unrelated `checked:`-shaped strings like 'bybit_2' and 'bot.log').
items.resolution_criteria: The line number in an impossibility-claim finding resolves to the line carrying the claim when opened in the file, and an annotation placed within ANNOTATION_WINDOW lines of the claim satisfies the guard.

items.title: 16 matrix cells were measured at live TP parity and the roll-up counted them as `unrecorded`, because the fact was written in ref prose and in m20-exit-head-rounds.jsonl while geometry_coverage() reads a STRUCTURED `tp_geometry` field.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 while recording the 1d pullback round.

`geometry_coverage()` in m20_coverage_rollup.py reads `cell.get("tp_geometry")` and counts every absent value as `unrecorded`. Its own docstring states that `unrecorded` covers three different conditions at once — measured at live parity and unstamped, measured pre-cutover, and nobody looked — and that the reassuring reading is the wrong one for most of the population.

The first of those three was populated and nobody had counted it. Cross-referencing every `tp_geometry: live_parity` row in m20-exit-head-rounds.jsonl against the matrix found 16 cells whose live-parity measurement existed, was recorded in the repo, and was invisible to the only consumer that reports the coverage figure. Coverage read 11/376 = 2.9% when it should have read 32/376 = 8.5%.

This is the written-and-never-read shape that provenance-consumer-guard exists to catch, inverted: the CONSUMER was correct and the producer wrote to a different channel.

RESOLVED in this session. The 16 were partitioned before stamping rather than swept: 10 cells whose ref cites the live-parity round were stamped directly; 6 whose ref still rested on an OLDER round were checked first (all 6 live-parity rounds reproduce the recorded negative — none disagreed), then had the live-parity measurement written into the ref and were stamped. Stamping the 6 without that check would have claimed a verdict rested on evidence it did not rest on.

RESIDUAL, and the reason this is filed rather than just fixed: nothing enforces the correspondence. A future round can add a `live_parity` row to m20-exit-head-rounds.jsonl and leave the matrix cell unstamped, and the coverage figure silently under-reports again. The check is a five-line cross-reference (every jsonl row stamped live_parity should have a matrix cell either stamped or explicitly citing a different round) and belongs in m20_coverage_rollup.py as a warning line beside the coverage figure, in the same style as its existing EVIDENCE VINTAGE banner.

CORRECTION, same session — THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS FIX WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and the corrected form is the thing the enforcement check must copy.

(1) Stamping on CITATION alone was wrong. Six of the first ten stamps sat on cells whose live-parity round CONTRADICTS the recorded status (`honest_negative` cell, `candidate` round). `tp_geometry: live_parity` means 'not stale whatever the date says', so stamping those suppressed from the stale population exactly the cells that most need to surface — the laundering the field exists to prevent. Reverted.

(2) The revert predicate was then wrong too: string equality between cell status and round verdict over-reverted 4 correct stamps. `shipped` beside a `candidate` round is CONSISTENT (shipping is downstream of passing the gate), and `shipped_gate_failed` beside `honest_negative` is the status the legend defines for exactly that. The predicate is SIGN, not string: POSITIVE = {candidate, shipped, passed_unshipped}, NEGATIVE = {honest_negative, shipped_gate_failed}; stamp when the signs match, leave unstamped when they oppose.

Final state: 24 live_parity stamps (28/376 = 7.4% recorded, from 11/376 = 2.9%). items.title: exit_head_ml mean_auc moved -0.110 to +0.042 across a ONE-DAY re-measurement of the same six legs, against a gate bar of 0.55 — so AUC margins of a few thousandths are being read as decisions the measurement cannot support.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-14. The six 1d pullback legs were measured 2026-08-13 (relay #8963, uncapped) and again 2026-08-14 (round pullback_1d_20260814T212317Z, live parity). Every AUC moved:

  gdx  0.5919 -> 0.6337  (+0.042)
  ief  0.5376 -> 0.5337  (-0.004)
  gld  0.5483 -> 0.5277  (-0.021)
  iaum 0.5927 -> 0.5525  (-0.040)
  slv  0.5832 -> 0.4895  (-0.094)
  tlt  0.6399 -> 0.5300  (-0.110)

Against a bar of 0.55. tlt and slv crossed it downward. On the same night the gate graded iaum a `candidate` on an AUC margin of 0.0025 — roughly one fortieth of that leg's own one-day movement.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: this is not evidence the harness is broken, and the movement is NOT attributed to the TP cap. Three things changed together between the rounds — TP geometry (uncapped -> 0.099 live cap), pool size (568 -> 629 trades), and fold count (10 -> 11, which re-cuts every block boundary) — so no component is isolable from this pair, and the mixed directions (gdx up while five fall) rule out a uniform cap effect. The capped numbers are the authoritative ones regardless: they measure the geometry production actually places.

WHAT SURVIVES: an AUC in this programme is a point estimate with movement of this order behind it, and the gate compares it to 0.55 as though it were exact. Every `honest_negative` that fails on AUC alone, and every `candidate` that clears on a thin margin, is a decision taken inside that movement.

WHY THIS IS NOT A PROPOSAL TO CHANGE THE GATE: changing a gate after seeing which term it fails on is how a gate stops meaning anything. The useful next step is a MEASUREMENT — a repeat-measurement spread for a few legs (same trades, same geometry, re-cut folds) so the gate's margins can be read against a known dispersion instead of assumed exact.

⚠️ THE OBVIOUS IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROPOSED FIX IS A TRAP — checked 2026-08-14 against scripts/ml/train_exit_head.py before attempting it. There is NO fold-seed or fold-offset flag; the only knob that moves fold boundaries is `--min-fold-trades` (the block size b, default 50), and that argument carries a 17-line comment forbidding exactly this use: P_detect is NOT monotonic in b, every apparent optimum lands on a u where the 2/3 bar is cheap to hit by luck (N=98/b=20, N=200/b=50, N=300/b=75 all carry a 50% single-condition false-positive rate), and 'maximising power over b therefore selects the settings easiest to pass BY CHANCE'. A b-sweep would also change fold SIZE, so the AUC spread it produced would partly measure 'AUC is noisier on smaller folds' — a different quantity from the one this row is about, reported under this row's label. That is the unprovenanced-diagnostic sub-class B shape.

THE CORRECT IMPLEMENTATION holds b fixed and varies only WHERE the blocking starts: a `--fold-offset k` (k in 0..b-1) on train_exit_head.py that drops the first k trades before cutting blocks, giving up to b distinct partitions of equal power over the same pool and the same geometry. That isolates fold-boundary sensitivity, which is the thing to measure. It does not exist yet; adding it is a Tier-1 change to a research script. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'resolved (spread MEASURED and recorded; the two cells it surfaced are queued for the operator)' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
items.proposed_fix: Add `--fold-offset k` (fixed b, shifted blocking start) to scripts/ml/train_exit_head.py, then run one family at 3-5 offsets with pool and TP geometry held fixed and record the per-leg mean_auc spread beside the 0.55 bar. Do NOT sweep `--min-fold-trades` to do this — that flag's own comment forbids it, and it would change fold size as well as boundary. The row closes on the spread being measured and recorded; any gate change from it is Tier-3.
items.resolution_criteria: A recorded repeat-measurement spread exists for at least one exit_head_ml family: >=3 rounds over the SAME pool and SAME TP geometry with only the fold boundary varying, with the per-leg mean_auc of each run written to docs/research/m20-exit-head-rounds.jsonl (or a sibling artifact) and the observed spread stated next to the gate's 0.55 bar. The row closes on the spread being MEASURED and recorded, not on the gate being changed — any gate change from it is Tier-3 and belongs to the operator.
items.resolution:
MEASURED 2026-08-15 exactly as this row's proposed_fix specified, and the proposed implementation was the one that shipped: `--fold-offset k` on train_exit_head.py (fixed block size b=50, shifted blocking start), forwarded through m20_exit_head_round.py and stamped unconditionally into _round_meta. `--min-fold-trades` was NOT swept, per this row's own warning.

TEN arms over the 1d pullback family, same pool, same TP geometry (tp_cap_pct 0.099), only the fold boundary moving; SEVEN of them are pure boundary shifts (offsets 0/6/10/12/18/20/24 — offsets 30/40 also drop a fold, because u = floor((N-k)/b)-1 holds u=11 only for k<=29 at N=629,b=50, so they are recorded but not pooled). All 60 rows committed to docs/research/m20-fold-dispersion-arms.jsonl, emitted by the trainer and verified byte-exact against its sha256. Read-out: docs/research/m20-fold-dispersion-2026-08-15.md, against a pre-registration (docs/research/m20-fold-dispersion-preregistration-2026-08-15.md) committed before any arm reported.

THE NUMBER, stated beside the 0.55 bar as this row required: median per-leg AUC spread over the 5-arm primary = 0.0515, max 0.0658. The pre-registered top band is >0.05, so it clears by 0.0015 — and dropping gdx (the one leg whose usable-fold count is not constant across arms) puts it at 0.0496, BELOW. The honest reading is that this family's median dispersion lands ON the 0.05 threshold and the measurement cannot resolve which side. The independent 3-arm cross-check (0.0333) reconciles: it sits on the median (0.0326) of all ten 3-arm subsets of the primary, so the runs agree and the gap is purely arm count.

WHAT THE SPREAD COULD NOT HAVE SHOWN, and is the more consequential half. Per-arm VERDICTS make the complete 6x7 grid readable: four legs (gld ief slv tlt) are UNANIMOUS across every boundary draw; iaum (recorded `candidate`) survives 1 of 7; gdx (recorded `honest_negative`) reads `candidate` on 2 of 7. The two that move are exactly the two on a SINGLE-term margin, and they move in OPPOSITE directions. So boundary placement moves the fold-majority terms, not only AUC — and stability tracks MARGIN, not book size (slv unanimous at 160 OOS trades; gdx flips at 81). Recomputing all four gate terms from the committed rows reproduces all 60 recorded verdicts with zero disagreements.

THIS ROW CLOSES ON THE MEASUREMENT, per its own resolution_criteria — the gate is unchanged, no matrix status was flipped, and coverage is unchanged at 373/376. The two decisions it surfaced are queued for the operator in the memo and tracked forward as BL-20260815-SINGLE-TERM-NEGATIVES-MAY-BE-BOUNDARY-ARTEFACTS.

items.title: An exit_head_ml verdict that sits ONE FOLD FLIP from the opposite outcome is a boundary artefact risk — and the CANDIDATE column is 2.7x more exposed than the negative one (8/14 vs 4/19), measured by arithmetic over the committed rounds.
items.tier: 1 (research measurement; no live path, no gate changed, no matrix status flipped)
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-15 over the 1d pullback family, 7 pure boundary draws (see docs/research/m20-fold-dispersion-2026-08-15.md and the committed arms in m20-fold-dispersion-arms.jsonl).

Four of six legs are UNANIMOUS across every boundary draw. The two that are not are exactly the two sitting on a SINGLE failing/passing gate term:

  iaum_pullback_1d  recorded `candidate`         survives 1 of 7   (sole term: mean_auc)
  gdx_pullback_1d   recorded `honest_negative`   -> `candidate` on 2 of 7 (sole term at the recorded arm: beats_hard), and on BOTH non-pooled arms (30, 40)

The candidate direction was anticipated. The NEGATIVE direction is the one nothing covers: a negative is a decision not to pursue a lever on a leg, and no process revisits it. The matrix carries 281 `honest_negative` cells.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. This is not evidence gdx's negative is wrong — it holds on 5 of 7 draws, and re-grading a cell because two alternative partitions liked it is precisely the selection this programme refuses. It is also NOT a proposal to change the gate; changing a gate after seeing which term it fails on is how a gate stops meaning anything. And it is measured on ONE thin family (u 4-11 against 26 for pullback_1h), so it is an upper bound on what a well-powered family would show.

WHAT SURVIVES: single-term verdicts, in EITHER direction, are the ones exposed to where the folds fall — and the fold-majority terms (beats_actual / beats_hard) are mechanically the most exposed, since they are counts over folds. A cheap screen exists now that `--fold-offset` ships: re-run a leg at 3+ offsets and see whether its verdict is unanimous.

RELATED QUALIFIER, worth carrying: across these 60 arms the SOLE failing term is beats_actual 4x, auc 2x, beats_hard 2x, and beats_actual fails most often overall (48/60). BL-20260814 / m20-exit-head-binding-term-2026-08-14.md measured beats_hard as the sole failure in 6 of 7 single-term failures across 33 rounds of MANY families. Both are correct; the binding term is FAMILY-DEPENDENT, and the 1d pullback family is not where beats_hard binds.
items.proposed_fix: Identify which matrix `honest_negative` cells rest on a SINGLE failing gate term (the rounds file carries beats_actual_folds / beats_hard_folds / mean_auc / usable_folds, so this is a pure read, no harness run). Report that count beside the 281-cell negative column — it sizes the exposure without asserting anything about it. Only then decide whether those specific cells warrant a 3-offset unanimity screen. Do NOT re-grade any cell from this row; any status change or gate change is Tier-3 and belongs to the operator.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH columns' fragile-cell counts are recorded with their population stated (DONE: 8/14 candidates, 4/19 negatives over the 33 committed rounds), AND an offset screen has been run on at least the fragile CANDIDATES, since those are the cells that would justify a live change. Closes on the screen being run and its unanimity recorded — NOT on any cell being re-graded and NOT on the gate changing; both are Tier-3 and belong to the operator.

updates.note:
SIZED, pure read of docs/research/m20-exit-head-rounds.jsonl, no harness run — the resolution_criteria's first half is met.

POPULATION, stated: the 33 committed rounds, 19 of them `honest_negative`. This is NOT the matrix's 281-cell negative column (that spans all 8 levers); it is the exit_head_ml legs actually re-measured.

  fail on exactly 1 gate term : 7 (37%)
  fail on 2                   : 6
  fail on 3                   : 6

Of the 7: SIX fail on beats_hard (gdx_pullback_1d, gld_pullback_1h, ict_scalp_eth_15m, sol_pullback_2h, trend_donchian_eth_4h, trend_donchian_sol_4h) and ONE on mean_auc (tlt_pullback_1h).

TWO CHECKS. Recomputing the four gate terms from the stored fields reproduces all 33 recorded verdicts, zero disagreements. And the 6-of-7 split reconciles EXACTLY with m20-exit-head-binding-term-2026-08-14.md, which had already reported beats_hard as the sole failure in 6 of 7 single-term failures — so that memo had already sized this population; what is new is that one of its members (gdx) has now been shown to FLIP under re-partitioning.

SO THE EXPOSURE IS 7 CELLS, one measured fragile and six never offset-tested. That is a tractable follow-up, not an alarm: gdx flipping does not make the other six wrong, and beats_hard being the common term is expected by construction (it is a count over folds, hence the most boundary-exposed term).

REMAINING: run the 3-offset unanimity screen on those 7 legs (cheap — `--fold-offset` ships and the driver forwards it) and record which are unanimous. Still NOT a re-grade and NOT a gate change; both remain Tier-3 and the operator's.

SCOPE CORRECTED — this row was opened about the NEGATIVE column and the candidate column is worse. Pure read of the 33 committed rounds, no harness.

THE CRITERION IS ARITHMETIC, not an extrapolation from the measured dispersion. The gate is `beats * 3 >= u * 2`, so one fold changing side moves beats by 1 and the slack by 3. A slack of 0/1/2 therefore means a SINGLE fold flip changes the verdict — true for any family, any u.

  candidates one fold flip from FAILING : 8 of 14 (57%)
  negatives  one fold flip from PASSING : 4 of 19 (21%)

The eight fragile candidates: ict_scalp_sol_15m (beats_actual AT the bar, slack +0), ict_scalp_xrp_15m (beats_hard +0), trend_donchian_eth_prop (beats_hard +0), iaum_pullback_1d (+1/+1, and the one measured to flip), trend_donchian_xrp_4h (beats_hard +1), trend_donchian_eth (+2/+2), ict_scalp_sol_5m (beats_hard +2), and eth_pullback_2h — whose AUC margin is +0.0006.

VALIDATED, n=1: gdx_pullback_1d sits at beats_hard slack -2, i.e. the arithmetic says one fold flip passes it, and re-partitioning DID pass it on 2 of 7 draws. Predicted fragile, observed fragile. That is the only empirical anchor the criterion has.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE ON THIS SIDE: a candidate is the cell that would justify shipping a lever onto a live leg. A fragile negative costs an unexplored opportunity; a fragile candidate can cost a live change made on a verdict that a different fold boundary would not have produced.

NOT A CLAIM ANY VERDICT IS WRONG. 'One fold flip away' is robustness, not correctness, and the AUC half of the criterion (<0.005) is a chosen threshold rather than arithmetic. Which of the eight actually flip is what an offset screen measures. Note trend_donchian_xrp_4h appears here on its exit_head_ml cell — a DIFFERENT lever from the trail_decay change in PR #9257 on the same leg, no interaction; recorded so the two are never conflated.

PRECISION CORRECTION on my own validation claim, checked against the arms rather than assumed. I wrote that gdx validates the one-fold criterion. It validates it as a FLAG, not as a mechanism: off0 has u=7/beats_hard=4 (slack -2, honest_negative) and off10 has u=8/beats_hard=6 (slack +2, candidate) — u moved AND beats_hard moved by two, so the observed transition is larger than the single-fold move the criterion is built on. The criterion correctly SELECTED the leg that turned out unstable; it does not model how the instability happens. Also worth noting gdx is the same leg whose u is not constant across arms, so it is the awkward leg in both the median and this validation.

The second half — an offset screen run on at least the fragile CANDIDATES, with unanimity recorded — has no artifact: docs/research/m20-fold-dispersion-arms.jsonl covers the 1d pullback family draws, not the fragile candidate set. — needs trainer runs: the 3-offset unanimity screen over the fragile candidate cells. No status may be re-graded from it (Tier-3), so this is measurement only.

items.source: Surfaced when 9 of 17 legs failed to reproduce their recorded round in a fresh arm and the file could not say whether the recorded row came from a different run. Found while investigating the unanimity screen's control failures, not by any audit of the file.
items.title: The rounds file's run identity lives inside the free-text `provenance` string, not a typed field — readable by a human, not by a consumer, and I asserted it was ABSENT by reading the field-name list instead of the values.
items.detail:
⚠️ THIS ROW'S ORIGINAL CLAIM WAS WRONG AND IS RETRACTED. I filed it saying the rounds file carries 'NO run id and NO timestamp'. It does: `scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py:413` stamps `provenance = f"round {out.name}; driver-emitted"`, and the committed rows carry values like `round eth_denom_4h_20260814T134036Z; relays #9288 launch / #9294 report` — the producing round directory, its UTC timestamp, and the relay numbers.

HOW I GOT IT WRONG, because the mechanism is the point: I printed `sorted(rows[0])` — the FIELD NAMES — saw no key called `run`/`time`/`stamp`, and concluded absence. `provenance` was right there in that list and I never read its VALUE. That is RULE ONE ('read the field, not the prose about it') inverted: I read the schema and not the data, and asserted a negative from a probe I never showed could find a positive.

WHAT SURVIVES, much narrower: the run identity is a FREE-TEXT string, not a typed field. It is excellent for a human — several rows carry multi-sentence analysis — but a consumer cannot group rows by run, filter to a run, or detect that two rows came from different experiments without parsing prose. That is a real but LOW-severity ergonomics gap, not the integrity gap I filed.

AND IT IMMEDIATELY PAID OFF ONCE READ: the 9 control mismatches are exactly the rows from `eth_denom_2h_20260814T130657Z` and `eth_denom_4h_20260814T134036Z` — rounds run for the ETH-DENOMINATOR investigation — while every reproducing leg comes from `pullback_1h_20260814T182245Z` or `scalp_15m_20260814T135244Z`. The field answered the question the moment I looked at it, and a determinism test (#9396: 5 of 5 legs identical to 0.0000, so training IS deterministic) had already ruled out the alternative.

REMAINING PUZZLE, stated as open rather than resolved: within the SINGLE `eth_denom_2h` round, 3 of 7 legs reproduce EXACTLY under my full-7-leg re-run and 4 do not. If that round had pooled a different leg set, all 7 should differ. Not yet explained.
items.proposed_fix: Add a typed `run_id` (the round dir name) beside the existing free-text `provenance`, so a consumer can group/filter by run without parsing prose. `provenance` keeps the human analysis. Low priority — the information is already present and correct, this is machine-readability only. Do NOT backfill by parsing the prose into the new field for rows where the parse is ambiguous; leave those explicitly unknown.
items.resolution_criteria: Either a typed run_id field is added beside `provenance`, or this row is closed as won't-fix on the grounds that the free-text field already carries the information and no consumer needs to group by run. Closing as won't-fix is an acceptable outcome and should be recorded as such.

items.title: An E1 exit_head_ml verdict depends on the ORDER the legs were typed on the command line: --legs order becomes rows.jsonl row order, which becomes the tie-break in a STABLE sort over a heavily-tied bar_t, which moves fold membership.
items.detail:
CHAIN, each link read in code and confirmed on artifacts:
  1. m20_exit_head_round.py:157  `for leg in a.legs.split(',')` -> emits list in CLI order
  2. build_exit_head_dataset.py:583,634,730  reads those paths in list order, extends,
     writes rows.jsonl in leg-concatenation order
  3. train_exit_head.py:518  sorted(h_trades.items(), key=bars[0]['bar_t']) -- Python's
     sort is STABLE, so ties inherit that file order
  4. on a 2h family every leg entering on the same bar has an IDENTICAL bar_t, so tie
     groups span all legs, one per bar

MEASURED (relays #9403, #9406) on eth_denom_2h_20260814T130657Z vs the unanimity2 off0 arm -- same 7 legs, orders differing only by permutation:
  recorded : eth, eth_prop, sol, xrp, ada, avax, htf   (hand-typed)
  arm      : ada, avax, eth, eth_prop, htf, sol, xrp   (alphabetical)
  identical harness_trades 2220, identical total rows 71199, identical 43 folds x 50
  trades -- yet 8 of 43 folds carry different n_rows (first divergence fold 21,
  1378 vs 1370). AUC moved 0.0009-0.0331 on the shifted legs; ada and eth_prop
  reproduced at exactly +0.0000; avax and sol LOST a usable fold (42 and 41 vs 43)
  as a fold's per-leg OOS count crossed min_oos_trades_floor: 25.

WHY IT IS HIGH SEVERITY, not a curiosity: the movement from this nuisance parameter
(up to 0.0331) is roughly two-thirds of the deliberate fold-boundary dispersion the
M20 study set out to measure (median 0.0515). usable_folds is therefore not a stable
property of a leg, and it feeds the gate's `u >= 2` term and every fragility
computation keyed on `beats*3 >= u*2`.

NOT CLAIMED: no recorded verdict is shown to be wrong and nothing was re-graded.
Both orders are equally valid; neither is 'correct'. The defect is the undeclared
degree of freedom plus the fact that no consumer can DETECT it -- `legs` is stamped
in round_report.json::_round_meta but nothing compares it, and the committed row in
docs/research/m20-exit-head-rounds.jsonl does not carry it at all.

CANDIDATE FIXES (none applied; the choice changes recorded numbers, so it wants a
deliberate call rather than a drive-by):
  a. make the sort total -- add a deterministic secondary key (trade_key) at
     train_exit_head.py:518 so ties never depend on file order. Cheapest, and makes
     every future round reproducible; it WILL change some recorded AUCs, so the
     corpus would need a re-measure or an explicit vintage marker.
  b. sort `emits` in the driver so rows.jsonl order is canonical regardless of how
     the operator typed --legs. Narrower, does not fix a genuinely tied sort.
  c. carry `legs` (ordered) onto the committed round row so at minimum two rows
     differing by it are DETECTABLE. Should happen regardless of a or b.
(a)+(c) is the pairing I would propose.

UPDATE 2026-08-15 05:30Z — fix (a) is now AVAILABLE but NOT DEFAULT.
`train_exit_head.py --total-sort` breaks entry-time ties by trade_key, making the
fold sort total so the partition stops depending on --legs order. It is opt-in and
default-off DELIBERATELY: switching it changes recorded AUCs across the committed
corpus, so it is a re-measure to be decided and dated, not a drive-by that would
leave old and new verdicts pooled in one file with nothing marking which convention
produced them. It is a MIGRATION flag, not a permanent gate — the intended end state
is total-by-default once the corpus is re-measured.
Five tests (tests/test_total_sort_tie_break.py), including one that PINS THE DEFECT
with the flag off, so the flag cannot be quietly made unnecessary without that
showing up as a failure.
So the operator decision is now narrower than 'which fix': (a) is written and
tested, and what remains is whether to flip the default and re-measure the corpus.

RE-VALIDATED 2026-09-02 AND DELIBERATELY NOT ACTED ON -- the cheap-looking half of the fix is the one the criterion sequences LAST, and doing it first would create incomparable evidence. State of the three sub-conditions, read this session:
  * `--total-sort` is still `action='store_true'`, DEFAULT OFF (scripts/ml/train_exit_head.py:679).

  * no ordered `legs` field on any row either -- also absent from all 33.

It is a one-line change and it is the wrong first move: the flag's own help text and the 2026-08-23 audit both record that flipping it changes recorded AUCs across the committed corpus, so the corpus must be re-measured FIRST or the file silently mixes two non-comparable conventions with no field to tell them apart -- which is this row's defect reproduced one level up. Backfilling a `legs` field onto the existing 33 rows is likewise refused: the order those runs used is not recoverable from any committed artifact, and writing one in would be fabricating provenance.

THE ORDER OF OPERATIONS, so the next session does not have to re-derive it: (1) re-measure the corpus with `--total-sort` on the trainer and date the re-measure in the evidence file; (2) add `total_sort` and an ordered `legs` field to the rows the re-measure writes, so the two conventions are distinguishable; (3) flip the default; (4) verify with two runs of one family passing `--legs` in DIFFERENT orders and assert byte-identical per-leg mean_auc and usable_folds, recording both orders in the PR. items.source: Read /api/diag/log_file?name=exit_loop_health (diag #9410) to check whether the other session's EXIT_LOOP_DECOUPLE_DISABLED tail had completed. It had — state 'fresh', 625 passes. The margin was noticed while reading the payload, not by any check that watches it.
items.title: The decoupled exit loop's worst pass is 58.9s against the operator's 60s 'no live trade goes unevaluated' ask — a 1.8% margin, down from 43.2% at n=55 — and nothing alerts on it, because exit_loop_health thresholds STALENESS only.
items.detail:
NOTE ON THIS ROW'S ID: it first read ...MAX-PASS-58.9S-AGAINST...; the period in '58.9S' truncates the id at the backlog ref matcher, which resolved it to a row that does not exist. artifact-validity-guard caught it. Backlog ids must not contain '.'.

MEASURED (diag #9410, live, process up since 2026-08-14T23:07:13Z):
  passes            : 625
  last_pass_ms      : 30799.1  (30.8s)
  max_pass_ms       : 58908.3  (58.9s)  at 2026-08-15T04:49:12Z
  state             : fresh    (the decouple IS running; not the concern)

WHY 58.9s IS THE INTERVAL, not just a pass duration: per CLAUDE.md the loop is
PERIOD-TARGETING, not sleep-after (`slack = interval - elapsed`), so the
inter-evaluation interval is max(EXIT_LOOP_INTERVAL_SECONDS, pass). With the floor
at 30s and a 58.9s pass, the worst observed interval IS 58.9s.

  operator ask : < 60s
  margin       : 1.1s = 1.8%

THE TREND IS THE POINT. S-M20-EXIT-LOOP-DECOUPLE-2026-08-12 recorded 'worst observed
interval 34.1 s, clearing the operator's 60 s ask by 43.1%' over 55 passes. At 625
passes the max is 58.9s and the margin is 1.8%. Nothing regressed; a larger sample
revealed the tail, which is exactly why that sprint log flagged its own defaults as
'CHOSEN, NOT MEASURED ... bounded by the 22.4s mean pass with one 55-pass
distribution behind them; do not read them as tuned values'. This is that caveat
coming due.

LOWERING EXIT_LOOP_INTERVAL_SECONDS CANNOT HELP. The interval is max(floor, pass)
and the PASS is the binding term at 58.9s; the floor is already 30s. The only levers
that move it are making the pass faster or bounding its tail.

THE GAP THAT MAKES IT A BUG RATHER THAN A DATUM: exit_loop_health RECORDS
max_pass_ms and thresholds only STALENESS (stale_threshold_s: 180 -> state
fresh/stale). There is no threshold anywhere on the pass duration against the 60s
requirement, so the loop will read 'fresh' while breaching the ask it exists to
satisfy. A value written and never compared to its own requirement is the shape
provenance-consumer-guard exists for, one level up.

NOT YET ESTABLISHED: whether 58.9s is a rare tail or a thickening distribution --
max over 625 passes is one order statistic and I have no percentiles. The writer
keeps only last/max, so p95 is not recoverable from the artifact; getting it needs
either a histogram in the writer or sampling the file over time.
items.resolution_criteria: exit_loop_health carries a declared pass-duration budget compared against the 60s requirement (not only the staleness threshold), and a breach is observable without reading the raw JSON -- either a state value distinct from 'fresh' or an alert, verified by a test that drives a >budget pass and asserts the non-fresh outcome. AND the artifact carries enough distribution (at minimum a p95 or a coarse histogram) to distinguish a rare tail from a thickening one, since max alone cannot.
evidence: diag #9410 (exit_loop_health, 625 passes, max_pass_ms 58908.3 at 04:49:12Z)
docs/sprint-logs/S-M20-EXIT-LOOP-DECOUPLE-2026-08-12.md (34.1s / 43.1% at n=55)
CLAUDE.md § EXIT_LOOP_INTERVAL_SECONDS (period-targeting: interval = max(interval, pass))
src/runtime/exit_loop_health.py

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The first half shipped (PR #9574, commit 5b64edc): src/runtime/exit_loop_health.py now measures completion-to-completion intervals (`_intervals_measured`, `_max_interval_ms`, lines 94-95,147-162,185-200) and publishes a four-state `requirement_state` (not_measured / breached / within / unknown, :211-235) graded against EXIT_EVAL_MAX_INTERVAL_SECONDS, registered as exit_loop_health.requirement_state in collapsed-state-guard's CONTRACTS. The second AND-clause is unmet: grep for p95/histogram in that module returns nothing, so the artifact still carries only a max and cannot distinguish a rare tail from a thickening one. — Ends when the artifact carries at least a p95 or a coarse histogram beside max_interval_ms.

items.resolution:
RESOLVED — the instrument exists and grades. `src/runtime/exit_loop_health.py` reads EXIT_EVAL_MAX_INTERVAL_SECONDS (line 81, default 60) and publishes a four-state `requirement_state` (within / breached / not_measured / unknown, lines 242-246), measured from the completion-to-completion interval rather than the `max(interval, pass)` derivation, and alerts once per PROCESS on a breach (lines 497-514). 'Nothing watches it' is no longer true. Read live 2026-08-25T11:1xZ.

⚠️ RESOLVING THE INSTRUMENT IS NOT RESOLVING THE CONDITION, and this row must not be read as saying the requirement was met. The first whole-file read the instrument made possible (`/api/bot/exit-interval/soak`, same session) reports **1,204 breaches over 22,670 measured intervals across 166 processes** — 5.31% — max 96,125.2 ms at 2026-08-20T23:14:26Z. items.title: Trainer VM is thrashing: replay_pregate_fleet.py holds 4.08 GB of a 6 GB box, 4.4 GB is in swap with 97 MB free, and every other job on the box has slowed ~3x. Nothing alerts on trainer memory or swap.
items.detail:
MEASURED (trainer-diag #9419, 2026-08-15T05:32:50Z):
  load average: 3.65, 3.31, 3.15   on a 1-OCPU box
  Mem:  5909 total  5080 used    97 free   625 available
  Swap: 8191 total  4375 used  3816 free
  kswapd0 CPU time: 1:03:21
  PID 1524014  elapsed 1:00:25  %MEM 67.3  RSS 4,077,032 kB  STAT D
    .venv/bin/python scripts/ml/replay_pregate_fleet.py --json -

STAT D = blocked in uninterruptible I/O, i.e. the holder is itself waiting on the
swap it caused.

IMPACT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. My 15m screen runs arms that are identical work
differing only in --fold-offset, which cannot cost time:
  off0  ~7.9 min   (finished 04:30:41)
  off4  ~15.9 min
  off8  ~20.5 min
  off12  25.8 min and still running
replay_pregate_fleet started ~04:32 — between off0 finishing and off4 running. Arm
wall-time has roughly tripled since. Deterministic compute is unaffected (AUCs and
verdicts are unchanged); only throughput is.

THE GAP: nothing watches trainer memory or swap. There is a trainer-down alert
(TRAINER_DOWN_STALE_SECONDS, mirror-heartbeat staleness) but a box that is UP and
thrashing is invisible to it — the mirror keeps publishing, just slower. So the
trainer can degrade to ~3x slower on every job with no signal, which is the same
shape as the live VM's pre-2026-08-09 tick cost: each component individually fine,
the SUM unwatched.

NOT ACTED ON: the process is not mine and was an hour into its work. Killing an
hour-long job on a shared autonomous box, unasked, is not a call to make from a
session that does not own it — particularly after this same session already reached
for pkill on this box earlier tonight, orphaned a child, and left two duplicate
backtests contending. Flagged on coordination board #6927 instead.

WHETHER replay_pregate_fleet's 4 GB FOOTPRINT IS ITSELF A BUG IS UNDETERMINED — I
did not read that script. It may legitimately need it, in which case the finding is
that the 6 GB trainer cannot run it concurrently with anything else and the two
should be serialized.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) trainer memory/swap is watched — a threshold that fires when swap-in-use or available-RAM crosses a declared bound, verified by a test or a forced condition, so a thrashing-but-up trainer is distinguishable from a healthy one; or (b) replay_pregate_fleet's peak RSS is measured and either reduced below a level the 6 GB box can host concurrently, or the job is serialized against other trainer work with that serialization enforced rather than conventional. Closing this on 'it finished and the box recovered' is not sufficient — that is the condition recurring, not resolving.

trainer-diag #9418 (per-arm completion mtimes showing the 7.9 -> 25.8 min trend)
