items.source: Self-observed, five times in one session. Recorded because the prose lesson was ALREADY written after error #2 and I repeated it three more times, which means prose was not the fix.
items.title: Analysis sessions burn multi-minute trainer-relay round trips guessing JSON schemas that the writer, in this repo, defines exactly. The remote is treated as the source of truth for a shape the local source already fixes.
items.detail: PATTERN, measured this session: five wrong-accessor readouts (`provenance`, `u` vs `usable_folds`, `_round_meta` in the wrong FILE, `legs` at the wrong nesting depth, and `(d.get('rounds') or [d])[0]` against `round_report.json`). Each cost a relay round trip of roughly 2-5 minutes. The last one is the clearest: relays #9423 and #9424 were spent discovering that `round_report.json` is `{'_round_meta': ..., <family>: {... 'per_leg': {<leg>: {mean_auc, usable_folds, verdict}}}}` -- a shape written by `scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py`, IN THIS REPO, at the `(out / 'round_report.json').write_text(...)` call. `grep -n round_report.json scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py` answers it locally in under a second. The canonical field names were likewise readable from the committed `docs/research/m20-exit-head-rounds.jsonl` without touching the trainer. WHY IT RECURS: the data is remote, so the SHAPE feels remote too. It is not -- the shape is a property of the writer, which is version-controlled here; only the VALUES are remote. COMPOUNDING FACTOR: a wrong accessor does not error, it returns None, so a bad read renders as `auc=None` -- indistinguishable at a glance from 'the arm has not finished'. In #9423 it was actively misleading: it printed None for arms that had completed, and I would have read the screen as stalled had #9422 not already given a known value for one of them. That is diagnostic-provenance sub-class C (an empty result reading as a clean negative) inside my own ad-hoc probe.
items.recommended_fix: Two mechanisms, both cheap, in preference order. (1) READ THE WRITER FIRST: before any relay that parses a JSON artifact, grep the local script that writes it. State the accessor's provenance in the relay body ('shape per <file>:<line>'), so a guess is visible as a guess. (2) PREFER THE SCHEMA-FREE ARTIFACT: `m20_exit_head_round.py` already writes `rounds.jsonl` in the canonical corpus shape, so a readout can `cat` it and needs no accessor at all. Relays that hand-roll a walk over `round_report.json` should read `rounds.jsonl` instead. (3) ALWAYS INCLUDE A KNOWN-ANSWER CONTROL: every readout should re-read one artifact whose correct value is already established, and the body should state that expected value. A reader that fails its control is wrong; without one, `None` everywhere reads as 'not finished yet'. This is the same rule already recorded as 'a positive control validates the READER, not the choice of TARGET' -- the point of filing it here is that writing it down did not make it happen, so it needs to be a step in the relay template rather than a maxim.
items.resolution_criteria: ALL THREE observable, checkable by reading the artifacts: (1) `.claude/skills/diag-data` (or the trainer-relay section it points at) contains an explicit step ordering 'grep the local writer for the shape' BEFORE composing a relay that parses a JSON artifact, and requiring the relay body to state the accessor's provenance as `shape per <file>:<line>`. (2) A relay readout that reads an exit-head round reads `rounds.jsonl` (the canonical corpus shape, no accessor) rather than walking `round_report.json` -- demonstrated by at least one posted relay issue after this row was filed. (3) That same relay body states an EXPECTED value for one already-established artifact (a known-answer control) and the returned output reproduces it. Verification: point at the relay issue number that satisfies (2) and (3), and the skill diff that satisfies (1). Closing this row on 'I will be more careful' is exactly the disposition that failed -- the prose lesson was already written after the second instance and three more followed.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Criterion (1) is unmet: .claude/skills/diag-data/SKILL.md contains no 'writer', no 'control' and no 'shape per <file>:<line>' text, so the relay procedure still has no step ordering 'grep the local writer for the shape' before composing a JSON-parsing relay. (2) and (3) require posted relay issues, which I cannot inspect from here. — (1) is the fixable half and it is the one the row says prose alone did not achieve — it must be a STEP, not a maxim.
Re-validated: sessions burning relay round-trips guessing schemas the repo defines. I avoided this today by reading the writer in-repo first; it is convention, not enforcement.

items.source: A screen launch died on `unrecognized arguments: --fold-offset` at 07:16, three hours after eight arms used that exact flag successfully on the same box. Diagnosed locally from git rather than by relay.
items.title: Every M20 fold-dispersion screen was produced by code that exists ONLY on an unmerged branch, and the trainer's checkout of that branch is unpinned and silently reverted mid-workstream.
items.detail:
MEASURED, not inferred. `--fold-offset` was added in commit 43820a32 ('exit-head: make --fold-offset reachable from the driver the trainer runs'). `git merge-base --is-ancestor 43820a32 origin/main` returns NO, and `git show origin/main:<file> | grep -c` returns **0 occurrences** for BOTH `scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py` (7 on the branch) and `scripts/ml/train_exit_head.py` (9 on the branch). So the fold-offset AND total-sort machinery is entirely branch-only.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE EVIDENCE. Every boundary screen this workstream has produced -- the 1d family, gld_pullback_1h, the completed 15m sol/xrp screen, the whole fragility finding -- was computed by code not on main. If PR #9257 is never merged, none of it is reproducible from main, and the committed rounds corpus would reference offsets no released code can generate. The operator-queue item recommending the leg-order fix understates this: fix (a) is not merely 'written and default-off', it is 'not on main at all'.

THE SECOND HALF IS THE TRAINER. The 15m screen ran eight offset arms between 04:22 and 06:56 today, so the branch WAS checked out then; the 07:16 launch got main's copy. Uptime was continuous across that window (30d23:36 at 06:49, 31d0:03 at 07:16), so this was a working-tree change, not a reboot -- the trainer's ref is unpinned and something moved it mid-workstream. A research box that silently changes code version under a running screen can produce arms measured on different code than their own control, which is precisely the incomparable-arm trap this workstream already hit once and spent a night untangling.

The launch failed FAST and clean (argparse rejected it before any work), so no partial or mixed-version data exists. That is luck, not design: had the flag been silently IGNORED rather than rejected, four arms would have run at offset 0 and reported as a spread.

MECHANISM IDENTIFIED (07:18Z, trainer-diag #9430) -- and it is more specific than the 'unpinned ref' this row first said. The trainer's reflog shows `branch: Reset to origin/main` on a ~15-MINUTE CADENCE: 06:28:52, 06:44:14, 06:59:25, 07:14:34. HEAD is `main` (b659a68a) throughout and `git status` shows the script UNMODIFIED, so the box was never on the feature branch at all. The 15m screen therefore ran on a locally-placed copy of the script that survived between resets, and my 07:16 launch landed TWO MINUTES after the 07:14:34 reset wiped it.

So the correct statement is not 'the ref drifted' but: ANY research run on this box that depends on code not merged to main is RACING A 15-MINUTE TIMER, and will be silently reverted mid-workstream. Re-launching by checking out the branch does not fix it -- the next reset wipes that too. The two durable options are (a) merge, or (b) run from a copy outside the git tree, which then needs its own version stamp or it reintroduces the same ambiguity from the other side.

This also explains a puzzle in the 15m screen's own timing: arms at 06:48 and 06:56 succeeded, straddling the 06:44 reset, which is only possible if the working copy was being restored between resets rather than held by a long-running process -- each arm re-invokes the script from disk. UPDATE 2026-08-15T16:05Z — OPTION (b) IS NOW BUILT AND PROVEN, and this row's 'two durable options' framing was right where the sibling row (BL-20260815-RESEARCH-TRAINERS-BYPASS-THE-HEAVY-JOB-QUEUE) briefly went wrong by claiming the heavy lock could stop the reset. It cannot: the 15-min resetter is scripts/ops/trainer_git_sync.sh, which is deliberately lock-free by design (BL-20260718-TRAINER-GITSYNC-STALE). The implemented option (b) is a LINKED GIT WORKTREE at /tmp/m20_screen_wt pinned to a detached HEAD — `git checkout -B main` in the main worktree cannot reach it. Proven by forcing a sync: main moved to 6f6458ac22d8 while the worktree held 43eec43d0c83 / 6412613984a3. Push-safety measured the same way (15 pushes during a running arm; both executed files byte-identical). It carries its own version stamp — each arm logs the worktree HEAD plus sha256 of both executed files BEFORE and AFTER — which is exactly the ambiguity this row warned option (b) would otherwise reintroduce. TWO COSTS WORTH RECORDING, both of which first read as a COMPLETED run: (1) a worktree checks out TRACKED files only and the candle CSVs are untracked, so --data-dir defaulted to an empty $WT/data and all three legs skipped data_missing in 4 seconds — the driver now passes the main clone's data dir explicitly and refuses to launch below 3 CSVs; (2) an orphaned child held the INHERITED flock fd after a stop, so the queue read HELD with nothing running. Resolution criterion (1) — the machinery on main — is still OPEN and still gated on PR #9257, which stays queued for the operator.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH: (1) the fold-offset/total-sort machinery is on `main` -- verified by `git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> origin/main` returning success AND a non-zero `git show origin/main:scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py | grep -c fold-offset`; and (2) a launched screen RECORDS the code version it ran -- the round's `_round_meta` carries the git SHA of the checkout, so an arm and its control can be shown to share a code version rather than assumed to. (2) is the durable half: merging fixes today's instance, but only the stamp makes a future version drift visible in the artifact instead of in a crash. Verification: point at the merge commit and at one round_report.json carrying a git SHA.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Criterion (1) is now MET: `git show origin/main:scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py | grep -c fold-offset` returns 14 and the train_exit_head.py copy on origin/main carries total-sort (2 hits) — PR #9257 merged as 7aa293d. Criterion (2) is NOT: grep for git_sha / rev-parse in scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py returns nothing, so a round's `_round_meta` still does not record the code version it ran. — The durable half is the stamp: merging fixed today's instance, but only a recorded SHA makes a future version drift visible in the artifact instead of in a crash.
Re-validated: evidence produced by code that exists only on an unmerged branch is unreproducible from main. Same family as BL-20260817-AN-UNMERGED-ARTIFACT-BRANCH-SILENCES-A-GUARD-THAT-READS-MAIN.

items.title: impossibility-claim-guard reports a phantom finding, at a wrong line number, when the working tree is dirty
items.source: hit twice in one session while writing docs/research/m20-operator-decision-queue-2026-08-15.md
items.detail: scripts/check_impossibility_claims.py --base origin/main fails on an ALREADY-ANNOTATED claim when the file has uncommitted edits, and reports a line number that does not hold the claim. Measured 2026-08-15: it errored at line 688 for the claim 'same leg is unmeasurable at target 25 and graded at 30', which sits at line 750 in the working tree. The 62-line offset is exactly the size of an uncommitted block inserted EARLIER in the file. Committing that block with NO other change flipped the same invocation from '1 unsubstantiated claim(s)' to '0 unsubstantiated claim(s)'. So the guard resolves the diff against the committed tree while its annotation-window search runs over content at shifted offsets; the 14-line window then lands on the wrong lines and the real annotation two lines below the claim, at 753, is invisible to it. TWO COSTS, and the second is the one that matters. (1) A local pre-commit run reports a failure that does not exist, and the natural response is to edit a correct annotation. (2) The reported LOCATION names a line that does not contain the claim, which is CLAUDE.md 'Diagnostic provenance' sub-class A in a guard whose own purpose is to enforce provenance -- a reader who trusts the line number inspects unrelated text and concludes the guard is broken in some other way. This session lost a cycle to it twice. NOT a CI correctness bug: CI runs on a clean checkout, so the guard is right in CI and wrong only locally, which is precisely why it survives -- the failure is invisible to the surface that would catch it. Note run_guards.py ALREADY prints an explicit warning when uncommitted paths were not scanned; this guard needs the converse. checked: scripts/check_impossibility_claims.py — the trigger phrase quoted above is the SUBJECT of this report, not an assertion by it. The behaviour was established empirically by running that script twice over identical content: once with the block uncommitted (1 finding, at a line that does not hold the claim) and once committed (0 findings). This annotation is itself the guard working as designed — it caught a re-utterance of the trigger word inside a report ABOUT that trigger word, which is the correct call.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) the guard refuses to run against a dirty tree for the files it scans, exiting with a distinct message naming the uncommitted paths (never a claim-shaped error), or (b) it resolves added lines and the annotation window against the SAME tree so line numbers and window both refer to one version. Verified by: with a correctly-annotated claim in a file, insert N unrelated lines ABOVE it without committing, run `python3 scripts/check_impossibility_claims.py --base origin/main`, and observe it either pass or emit the dirty-tree message -- NOT an unsubstantiated-claim error. Second check: any line number it does report must contain the quoted claim text (assert the file's line N contains the snippet the message quotes).

updates.note: REPRODUCED, cleanly, as a by-product of a merge. Mid-merge (conflicts resolved, `git add -A` run, nothing committed) `check_impossibility_claims.py --base origin/main` reported 2 unsubstantiated claims, both at line numbers inside backlog rows that were NOT part of my change — and one of the two was the text of THIS row describing the very bug. Committing the merge and re-running the identical command on the clean tree returned 0. Nothing else changed between the two runs. So the condition is exactly as this row states (dirty tree -> phantom finding at a wrong line), and the practical cost is that it fires during a merge resolution, which is precisely when a session is least able to tell a real finding from a spurious one.

[sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Unfixed, same source as its sibling: scripts/check_impossibility_claims.py:202-217 computes added-line numbers from `git diff base...HEAD` while main() (:230-240) reads the file body from disk, so uncommitted lines inserted above a claim shift the anchor by exactly their count and the ±ANNOTATION_WINDOW search lands on the wrong lines. There is no dirty-tree refusal branch anywhere in the file. — Tier-1 CI-guard ergonomics; the practical cost is that it fires during merge resolution, when a session is least able to tell a real finding from a spurious one.
Re-validated: tooling/guard correctness. Cheap to fix, unblocked, still undone. Third of three rows on this guard's line-number handling; consolidate with BL-20260810 and BL-20260814 siblings.

items.title: The 10 exit_head_ml cells that disagree with the corpus are EXACTLY the 10 whose tp_geometry was never propagated — one un-propagated batch, not ten judgement conflicts
items.source: found while checking why the roll-up reports tp-geometry coverage of 28/376 = 7.4% when the round corpus carries geometry for 33 cells
items.detail: docs/research/m20-exit-head-rounds.jsonl records tp_geometry for all 33 rows. Only 23 of those legs' exit_head_ml cells in docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json carry it. The 10 that do not are, EXACTLY and with zero symmetric difference, the same 10 whose matrix status disagrees with the corpus verdict: ada_pullback_2h, eth_pullback_2h, eth_pullback_prop_2h, iaum_pullback_1d, ict_scalp_avax_5m, ict_scalp_eth_15m, ict_scalp_xrp_15m, trend_donchian_ada_4h, trend_donchian_xrp_4h, xrp_pullback_2h. Set identity was computed, not eyeballed. WHY THAT MATTERS: check_matrix_corpus_agreement.py's exit_head_ml exemption documents '10 DISAGREE' as a carve-out pending a Tier-3 re-grade of ten cells, which reads as ten independent judgement conflicts. The identity says otherwise -- these cells were simply never written back from their round AT ALL, so status and geometry are both missing together. One batch, one cause. THE TWO HALVES ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF THING AND SHOULD BE SEPARATED. The status is a VERDICT (promoting a cell from honest_negative to passed_unshipped is a real decision, correctly gated). tp_geometry is a FACT about how the measurement was run, and withholding it makes those 10 cells read as 'nobody looked' in the roll-up's geometry coverage when we know precisely which geometry their evidence rests on. That is the roll-up's own documented trap: it warns that 'unrecorded' conflates stamped-nowhere-but-live-parity, pre-cutover no-take-profit, and nobody-looked. DO NOT PROPAGATE BLINDLY -- this is why it is filed rather than fixed. The 7 capped-family rows (pullback/donchian) record the pre-b96b954c label 'live_parity', which for a capped family is true but under-specified; today's driver would stamp 'live_parity_capped'. The 3 scalp rows already carry the precise 'live_parity_uncapped'. So a straight copy imports 7 stale-form labels into the artifact whose whole job is saying which geometry a verdict rests on. Either re-derive the label from (family, tp_cap_pct) using the same three-state logic as m20_exit_head_round.py:331, or re-run those rounds. All 33 corpus legs exist in the matrix, so this is not a join failure.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) tp_geometry is present on all 33 exit_head_ml cells whose leg has a corpus row, with the capped-family cells carrying 'live_parity_capped' rather than the bare 'live_parity' (assert: for every corpus leg, matrix cell tp_geometry is non-empty AND equals the label m20_exit_head_round's own three-state logic yields for that row's family and tp_cap_pct); or (b) the exemption text in scripts/ci/check_matrix_corpus_agreement.py is amended to state that the 10 disagreements are one un-propagated batch rather than ten separate re-grade decisions, so the next reader is not misled about their nature. Verified by re-running the set-identity check: the no-geometry set and the status-disagreement set must no longer be identical, or the exemption must say why they are.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Re-measured the set identity from the artifacts: of the 33 legs in docs/research/m20-exit-head-rounds.jsonl, 23 matrix exit_head_ml cells carry tp_geometry and 10 do not — exactly the ten the row names (ada/eth/eth_prop/xrp _pullback_2h, iaum_pullback_1d, ict_scalp_avax_5m, ict_scalp_eth_15m, ict_scalp_xrp_15m, trend_donchian_ada_4h, trend_donchian_xrp_4h). And scripts/ci/check_matrix_corpus_agreement.py:118-142 still describes them as '10 DISAGREE IN SIGN … already queued for the operator as decision item 3', without saying they are one un-propagated batch. — Branch (b) is the cheap, non-Tier-3 half: amend the exemption text. Branch (a) — stamping the geometry — is a fact, not a verdict, but should be done from each row's own family/tp_cap_pct label, not by hand.
Re-validated: the 10 disagreeing cells are EXACTLY the 10 whose tp_geometry never propagated — a clean, fully-explained defect. Should be one of the easiest M20 closes.

items.title: m20_exit_head_round.py exits 0 and writes an EMPTY rounds.jsonl when train_exit_head.py fails — a dead arm passes an existence check
items.source: trainer relay #9444, dispersion round pull2h_20260815T095550Z, arm off12
items.detail: Measured 2026-08-15. The off12 arm of a 4-arm dispersion screen died with `train_exit_head.py: error: unrecognized arguments: --fold-offset 12` (the trainer's ~15-min `Reset to origin/main` wiped the branch-only flag between the driver's git checkout and its train invocation). The wrapper recorded `ARM off=12 exit=0`: m20_exit_head_round.py returned SUCCESS while its training subprocess had failed and produced nothing. VERIFIED AGAINST THE BOX 2026-08-15T10:14Z, and it is worse than an absent file: the arm RAN (all seven backtests emitted, 363/343/225/297/243/361/407 trades; the dataset built 72,725 rows) and only the TRAINING step was rejected, after which the driver printed `evidence rows -> .../rounds.jsonl (0 rows...)` and `round done`. rounds.jsonl EXISTS, mtime 10:04:53Z, 0 lines. So a `[ -f ]` existence check PASSES on a dead arm. WHY HIGH: a dispersion screen's whole claim is that N arms ran the same code over the same data at N boundaries. An arm that silently vanishes turns a 4-draw result into a 3-draw result with nothing in the artifact saying so, and a reader comparing rounds will compare 4-draw and 3-draw move rates as if they were the same measurement -- which is precisely the error this session then made in the opposite direction (pooling 7-draw and 4-draw legs into one rate). A missing file is not an error message. SECOND, RELATED FINDING about the screen harness this session built (relays #9431/#9436/#9439/#9441): its gate 1 records sha256 of the two branch-only files at ARM START, and was being quoted as proof the arm RAN that code. It is not -- the reset arrived after the hash and the gate still passed. Every screen run tonight carried the same hole; the others differed only in timing luck. A sound gate hashes AFTER the run, or has the driver assert the flag is accepted (e.g. `--fold-offset` present in `--help`) immediately before invoking, or both. DOWNSTREAM DAMAGE, MEASURED: this defeated two of my own diagnostics on the same day. (1) A readout loop of the form `if [ -f rounds.jsonl ]; then sed ...; else echo '(none)'; fi` printed NOTHING for the dead arm -- the file exists so the else never fires, and sed over an empty file emits nothing -- so the arm vanished from the report with no line at all and the silence read as 'the directory does not exist yet'. That is CLAUDE.md 'Diagnostic provenance' sub-class C (an empty result rendering identically to an absent one). (2) A re-run guard using the same `[ -f ]` test REFUSED to re-run the arm, reporting 'off12 already has rounds.jsonl'. A 0-row file satisfied both. Any consumer that asks whether an arm produced evidence must count ROWS, never test existence. THIRD INSTANCE, same shape, 2026-08-15T10:26Z -- a gate degrading to VACUOUS rather than failing loudly. The corrected launcher's own `sha_before_*` lines came back EMPTY, because a nested `cut -d\" \" -f1` did not survive the `bash -c` quoting. A before/after hash comparison over two empty strings COMPARES EQUAL, so the gate would have reported 'hashes stable' having measured nothing -- the same failure mode as the 0-row file passing an existence check, one level up. Caught only because the launch relay echoed versions.txt and the blank was visible. The capability pre-flight in the same launcher DID work and is the stronger check: it asserts the flag is accepted at the moment of use, which no file hash can. GENERAL LESSON for anything added here: a verification step must be able to report 'I could not measure', distinct from 'I measured and they agree' -- an empty-equals-empty pass is CLAUDE.md's collapsed-state defect inside the check itself. ROOT CAUSE LOCATED IN CODE 2026-08-15T13:20Z, and it is a one-site asymmetry rather than a design choice. scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py: the DATASET-BUILD subprocess is checked -- line 266 `p = sh(build_cmd, ...)` followed by line 268 `if p.returncode != 0: return 1` -- while the TRAINING subprocess at line 284 `p = sh(train_cmd, ...)` has NO returncode check at all. Control falls straight through to `e1 = fam_dir / 'e1_report.json'; if e1.exists():`, so a failed training run simply leaves `report` empty, the driver writes a 0-row rounds.jsonl and returns 0. Two adjacent subprocess calls, one checked and one not. SECOND OCCURRENCE, measured: 5m scalp arm off4 of relay #9454 ran 73 minutes and finished `exit=0, rows=0` while arm off0 produced 3 rows from the identical command one arm earlier. It was caught ONLY by the row-count assertion added after the first occurrence; `exit=0` and a `[ -f ]` existence check both passed.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) m20_exit_head_round.py propagates a non-zero exit when any per-leg training subprocess fails, verified by invoking it with a deliberately bogus flag forwarded to train_exit_head and asserting a non-zero return code AND a message naming the failed leg; and (b) an arm that produced no rounds.jsonl is reported as a distinct, named state rather than an absent file -- a reader must be able to tell 'this arm died' from 'this arm has not run yet' without listing a directory. Verified by running a round with one leg forced to fail and confirming the artifact itself distinguishes the two. ALSO: a zero-row evidence file must not be written at all, or must be written to a distinct name/marker, so that existence implies rows. Verified by forcing a training failure and asserting that `[ -f rounds.jsonl ]` is FALSE (or that a sibling status file records the failure), and that a readout loop over the arms emits a visible line for it rather than silence. The minimal fix is to give line 284's result the same treatment line 268 already gives line 266's -- verified by the two call sites being symmetric on returncode handling.
items.resolution: FIXED in commit 8b5fc789 on claude/m20-exit-coverage-matrix-8d3he7 (scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py + tests/test_exit_head_round_fails_loudly.py). All three criteria met. (a) The training subprocess's returncode is now checked, and the exited-0-but-wrote-no-e1_report.json case is caught as a DISTINCT third state; failures accumulate into `train_failures` and main() returns 2 naming the failed families and the row count. Deliberately NOT `return 1` on the first failure the way the build step does -- a 3-leg round whose second leg dies should still train the third and the operator wants the partial evidence; what must not happen is REPORTING SUCCESS. (b) round_report.json's _round_meta now carries `train_failures` (an EMPTY LIST on a clean round, so 'no failures' is stated rather than implied by absence) and `families_trained`. (c) EXISTENCE NOW IMPLIES ROWS: a zero-row round writes `rounds.EMPTY` (carrying the failures, the families that did train, and the geometry) instead of an empty rounds.jsonl, so the three states are readable from the filesystem alone with no exit code and no stdout parsing -- rounds.jsonl present = produced evidence; rounds.EMPTY present = ran and produced nothing; neither = never reached the emit step. That directly un-breaks the two diagnostics this row records as defeated: a `[ -f rounds.jsonl ]` re-run guard now correctly re-runs a dead arm, and a readout loop's `else` branch now fires for it instead of printing silence. HOW IT WAS VERIFIED, and how that DIFFERS from the criteria as written. The criteria asked for an end-to-end run with a leg forced to fail. That was NOT the method used: a real round needs the trainer VM and hours of compute, and the trainer's ~15-min reset makes a branch-only driver unrunnable there anyway (which is the very mechanism that caused this defect to fire twice). Instead the fix carries 7 STRUCTURAL tests asserting on the driver's source, each proven load-bearing by planting the exact defect it guards and observing it fail: removing the training returncode check -> 2 tests fail; making the rounds.jsonl write unconditional -> 1 test fails; both restored -> 7 pass. This is weaker than a behavioural test and is recorded as such in the test module's docstring -- a behavioural test needs a fake trainer and a fake harness, which is worth building and is NOT done. What is claimed is that the three properties are pinned against regression, not that a failing round was observed end-to-end. SIDE FINDING FIXED IN THE SAME COMMIT: tests/test_exit_head_round_emits_evidence.py's geometry test anchored on `src.index("rounds.jsonl")` -- the first MENTION of the filename -- then looked 3000 chars backwards. The new comments name that file in prose, so the index jumped ~250 lines and the test failed against untouched geometry-stamping code. Widening the window only deferred it (the second comment pushed the stamp out of a correct window too, failing it again for a second reason). It now bounds the region by `rows.append({` .. the literal write site and asserts exactly one append site; proven load-bearing by planting a wrong geometry stamp. SUPERSEDED SAME DAY, and the correction matters more than the original claim. This row's resolution first said the screen-harness half needed 'an AFTER-hash comparison'. That is wrong in KIND: it is a DETECTION fix for a problem that admits a PREVENTION fix. Root-caused at 14:40Z -- the '~15-min reset' is `git checkout --force -B main origin/main` at run_training_cycle.sh:138, which runs INSIDE the trainer heavy-job queue and skips its entire cycle when the queue is held. The M20 exit-head path took that queue nowhere, so every voided arm was voided by a mechanism the repo already had the primitive to prevent. An after-hash would have told me the hour was wasted; the lock stops the hour being wasted. m20_exit_head_round.py now acquires it. The capability pre-flight is NOT superseded -- it still catches the residual race in two seconds -- but it is the backstop, not the fix. Full account + the unfixed siblings: BL-20260815-RESEARCH-TRAINERS-BYPASS-THE-HEAVY-JOB-QUEUE.
items.verified_by: python -m pytest tests/test_exit_head_round_fails_loudly.py tests/test_exit_head_round_emits_evidence.py -> 11 passed; planted-defect proof for all three guarded properties; scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main -> 38 PASS / 0 FAIL with all three changed paths confirmed present in the scanned /tmp/pr.diff (the earlier green did NOT scan them -- they were uncommitted and every guard is scoped to a commit range).

items.title: The M20 exit-head research path takes the trainer heavy-job queue nowhere, and the ml-CLI backstop cannot cover it — so heavy research jobs contend unqueued on a 6 GB box
items.source: root-caused 2026-08-15T14:40Z while fixing BL-20260815-EXIT-HEAD-ROUND-EXITS-ZERO-WHEN-TRAINING-SUBPROCESS-FAILS
items.detail: MEASURED, not inferred: `grep -c heavy_lock` returns 0 for all three of scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py, scripts/ml/train_exit_head.py and scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py, and train_exit_head.py imports nothing from `ml/`. docs/claude/trainer-resource-protocol.md Rule 1 is BINDING ('Manual sessions MUST use the queue too') and has TWO enforcement halves, neither of which reaches this path: the shell wrappers (run_training_cycle / run_promotion_readiness / run_drift_retrain / trainer_run) take the lock explicitly, and the `ml` CLI takes it at its entrypoint (src/utils/trainer_heavy_lock.py wired in ml/cli.py) as the backstop for a bare `python -m ml train`. The exit-head path is neither a wrapper nor the CLI — it is a research script shelling out to another research script — so it sits outside both. The protocol reads as enforced while an entire family of heavy jobs is exempt, which is worse than a protocol known to be voluntary. WHY HIGH, and this is the part that surprised me: the '~15-min Reset to origin/main' that voided two 73-minute dispersion arms overnight is NOT an ambient force of nature. It is `git checkout --force -B main origin/main` at run_training_cycle.sh:138, and that line runs INSIDE the heavy lock — the cycle calls take_trainer_heavy_lock() first and SKIPS the whole cycle if the queue stays held past TRAINER_HEAVY_LOCK_WAIT_S. So an arm holding the lock is not merely warned about the reset, it PREVENTS it. Every voided arm was voided by a mechanism the repo already had the primitive to stop, and the reason it did not was that this path never asked for it. SECOND CONSEQUENCE, measured 2026-08-15T05:32:50Z (trainer-diag #9419): an unqueued `replay_pregate_fleet.py` at 4.08 GB RSS on a 6 GB box drove load 3.65 with 4.4 GB in swap, and my four screen arms — identical work differing ONLY in `--fold-offset`, which cannot cost time — ran 7.9 / 15.9 / 20.5 / 25.8+ min in launch order. Arms that cannot differ in duration DID, which is contention, and both sides of that collision were unqueued. NOTE replay_pregate_fleet.py is ALSO absent from the heavy-lock caller list, so this is not one stray script: it is the research/ directory generally. Scoping the sweep is part of the fix, not an afterthought. CORRECTION I OWE, because I published the wrong conclusion first. In BL-20260815-EXIT-HEAD-ROUND-EXITS-ZERO-WHEN-TRAINING-SUBPROCESS-FAILS I wrote that the missing piece for the screen harness was 'a sound gate hashes AFTER the run'. That is a DETECTION fix for a problem that admits a PREVENTION fix, and it is strictly worse: an after-hash tells you an hour was wasted, the lock stops the hour being wasted. The capability pre-flight I shipped alongside it is genuinely useful and is NOT superseded — it catches the residual race in two seconds — but it is the backstop, not the fix. I reached for a better GAUGE when the available move was to remove the cause. Recording the reasoning error, not just the corrected answer. 🔴 CORRECTION 2026-08-15T16:05Z — THE 'WHY HIGH' PARAGRAPH ABOVE IS WRONG AND IS KEPT VERBATIM AS THE RECORD. Holding the heavy lock does NOT prevent the reset, and I published that claim in this row, in m20_exit_head_round.py, in a test docstring, in the research doc, on the coordination board and in two Telegram pings before measuring it. MEASUREMENT THAT REFUTES IT: arm off0 of the relaunched 5m screen ran its full 74 minutes under a held lock (its log carries {"status": "heavy_lock_acquired"}) and its AFTER hashes were 6f6458ac22d8 / 08541341e093 — byte-identical to origin/main's copies of m20_exit_head_round.py and train_exit_head.py. The reset landed WITH THE LOCK HELD. (off0 still emitted its 3 rows only because `if a.fold_offset:` treats 0 as falsy, so the control arm never forwards the branch-only flag.) CAUSE: there are TWO reset paths and I enumerated one. run_training_cycle.sh:138 runs inside the lock and is ~daily — the lock does hold that one off. scripts/ops/trainer_git_sync.sh, fired by ict-trainer-git-sync.timer at OnUnitActiveSec=15min, is DELIBERATELY LOCK-FREE; its own header reads 'a tiny, frequent, lock-free force-sync so "keep the code current" can never be blocked by "run training"', and that design exists because gating sync behind this lock once left the trainer 495 commits behind and froze the forecast producer (BL-20260718-TRAINER-GITSYNC-STALE). Masking or locking that timer would re-introduce a worse failure — it must stay lock-free. THE CADENCE WAS THE TELL I ALREADY HELD: I wrote '~15-min reset' repeatedly while attributing it to a daily job, and never reconciled the two numbers. THE REASONING ERROR: `grep -c heavy_lock` over three scripts is a true fact about CALLERS; I turned it into a claim about the RESET without enumerating the reset's producers. 'A search returning nothing is not proof of absence' has a mirror image — a search returning ONE thing is not proof there is only one. ACTUAL FIX, proven not assumed: run the code from a linked git worktree, which `git checkout -B main` in the main worktree cannot touch. A sync was FORCED while the worktree stood; the main tree moved to 6f6458ac22d8 and the worktree stayed at 43eec43d0c83 / 6412613984a3. WHAT STILL STANDS: everything else in this row. The queue-bypass enumeration, the 6-of-7 count, the 05:33Z contention measurement, and the resolution criteria are unaffected — taking the queue is still correct and still unfixed for 6 of 7. Only the claim that it protects a branch-only run from the reset is withdrawn.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) Every heavy job under scripts/research/ and scripts/ml/ that trains or builds a dataset on the trainer VM acquires the shared queue — established by ENUMERATING that set first and stating its size, not by fixing the ones that happen to come to mind (a negative needs a denominator; this row already names three plus replay_pregate_fleet.py). (b) A guard makes the enumeration durable, in the family of canonical-db-resolver / env-gate-guard: CI fails when a script that invokes a trainer/build entrypoint acquires no lock. Presence-only marker checks are explicitly OUT (see new-table-wiring-guard: a guard cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than none) — the check must resolve a real call. (c) The protocol doc states which paths the CLI backstop does and does not cover, since today it reads as universal. PARTIAL PROGRESS: m20_exit_head_round.py now acquires it (commit on claude/m20-exit-coverage-matrix-8d3he7, verified four ways off-box — inert without the role marker, acquires with it, queues then exits 75 when contended, re-acquires on release). train_exit_head.py, m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py and replay_pregate_fleet.py are UNFIXED, and the enumeration has not been done, so this row stays OPEN. Fixing the one script I happened to be holding is not the fix.
items.enumeration_20260815: CRITERION (a)'s ENUMERATION IS NOW DONE, and the honest number is much smaller than a first probe suggested. SCOPE, stated because it is what makes the count meaningful: a script is a genuine bypass only if it launches heavy trainer work by a route NEITHER enforcement half covers. The shell wrappers take the flock themselves; `python -m ml train|build-dataset` is locked at the entrypoint by ml/cli.py. So the gap is scripts invoking the RESEARCH entrypoints (train_exit_head.py / train_entry_head.py / build_exit_head_dataset.py) directly. RESULT: 7 scripts in scope, 6 bypass, 1 locked. Callers -- BYPASS: scripts/research/m20_exit_head_denominator.py, scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py, scripts/research/m21_entry_head_round.py, scripts/ml/export_exit_head.py; LOCKED: scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py (fixed this session). Entrypoints themselves -- BYPASS: scripts/ml/train_exit_head.py, scripts/ml/train_entry_head.py. Locking the two ENTRYPOINTS would cover every caller at once and is the smaller change; it is also the shape ml/cli.py already uses, and re-entrancy is already handled (TRAINER_HEAVY_LOCK_HELD), so a locked caller would not deadlock against a locked entrypoint. A FIRST, COARSER PROBE SAID 43 OF 49 AND WAS WRONG -- recorded so nobody re-derives it. It matched any file mentioning LightGBM, `.fit(`, or `python -m ml`, which swept in prose mentions and, worse, everything the CLI backstop ALREADY covers. Publishing 43 would have overstated the problem by ~7x and sent someone to lock scripts that are already locked one layer down. OUT OF SCOPE OF THAT PATTERN BUT STILL UNLOCKED, checked by hand because the pattern would have missed it: scripts/ml/replay_pregate_fleet.py (0 heavy_lock refs) -- the 4.08 GB job that swap-thrashed the box at 05:33Z and tripled my arm times. Its three siblings (replay_pregate.py, replay_pregate_live.py, replay_pregate_summary.py) are likewise unlocked. So 'heavy' is not only 'trains a model': a fleet replay loads the fleet. The enumeration above is therefore COMPLETE FOR TRAINING/BUILD ENTRYPOINTS and NOT complete for heavy trainer work generally; a full sweep needs a definition of heavy that covers replay/eval jobs too, and I have not written one.
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-08-15T17:20Z against the three stated criteria, on claude/m20-exit-coverage-matrix-8d3he7. (a) THE TRAIN/BUILD ENTRYPOINTS ALL LOCK. Fixed at the ENTRYPOINT, not the callers: train_exit_head.py has five in-repo callers plus every ad-hoc relay invocation, and the direct `python scripts/ml/train_exit_head.py ...` path is how most relays run it — so locking callers leaves the common path open and must be redone for the next caller. One module owns it (scripts/ml/_heavy_queue.py), which resolves the repo root itself rather than trusting CWD (the 5m screen already runs from a git worktree at another path). NO DEADLOCK, verified not assumed, because getting it wrong hangs a run for the full hour of TRAINER_HEAVY_LOCK_WAIT_S and looks like a slow job: acquire_heavy_lock sets TRAINER_HEAVY_LOCK_HELD=1 and returns None early when set, and no caller passes env= to subprocess. Exercised all four behaviours off-box — inert with no role marker (None), acquires under TRAINER_HEAVY_LOCK_FORCE, re-entrant skip when HELD is set, and a child WITHOUT the flag times out against a held parent with rc=75. (b) GUARD SHIPPED: scripts/ci/check_trainer_heavy_lock.py, registered in run_guards.py as trainer-heavy-lock-guard, self-test on every invocation. It resolves an actual AST CALL NODE — a comment or a string naming the helper FAILS, which the self-test proves by planting exactly that — per the new-table-wiring-guard lesson that a guard cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than none. Fails closed on a real regression: unlocking one entrypoint returns rc=1, restoring returns rc=0 (measured, and note the first reading of that was rc=0 because `head -3` had eaten the pipeline status). (c) docs/claude/trainer-resource-protocol.md § Rule 1 now carries a 'What the CLI backstop does NOT cover' subsection with the three-path table, and its overclaiming sentence — 'the backstop so nothing can slip past' — is corrected in place; that sentence is why the gap went unnoticed. ⚠️ THE HAND ENUMERATION IN THIS ROW WAS INCOMPLETE, and the guard's own drift pass is what proved it. 'RESULT: 7 scripts in scope' missed scripts/ml/spike_a_pooled_labels.py, which runs three lgb.train arms and is heavy by any definition — it is now locked. That is the entire argument for the completeness pass existing: a guard over a hand-written list answers 'are the listed ones locked', never 'is the list complete'. It also correctly surfaced scripts/ml/exit_head_replay.py, classified DECLARED_LIGHT after reading it (loads a Booster via model_str and calls predict(); fits nothing). REMAINING SCOPE IS SPLIT OUT, NOT DROPPED: the replay_pregate* family is heavy by footprint but is not a train/build entrypoint, so it needs a definition of 'heavy' covering replay/eval jobs — filed as BL-20260815-HEAVY-IS-UNDEFINED-FOR-REPLAY-AND-EVAL-JOBS rather than left implied here.

items.title: The fold-dispersion screens' per-arm rows were never promoted to a machine-readable record — 21 of 27 screened family_pooled legs (78%) exist only as prose tables, so the headline mover rate cannot be re-derived
items.source: found 2026-08-15T15:50Z while re-deriving the pre-registered per_leg-vs-family_pooled baseline from committed data instead of from my own running count
items.detail: MEASURED, not estimated. docs/research/m20-fold-dispersion-arms.jsonl holds 60 rows over SIX legs -- the 01:49Z 1d-pullback screen only (offsets 0/6/12/18/24 and 0/10/20/30/40, arm_set 'exploratory'). Every screen that ran after it (donchian-1h, prop-donchian, donchian-4h, pullback-2h, pullback-1h) has NO machine-readable arm record; those verdicts live only as tables in docs/research/m20-fold-dispersion-2026-08-15.md. Against the pooled denominator of 27 screened legs that is 6/27 = 22.2% covered, 21 legs prose-only. The night's headline -- '10 of 29 screened legs (34%) change verdict under re-partitioning' -- and the 9/27 pooled mover rate that the per_leg comparison is measured against therefore cannot be re-derived, re-counted, or guarded. WHY THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT TWICE OVER. It is exactly what m20_exit_head_round.py's rounds.jsonl emitter was ADDED to prevent -- its own test module states the problem as 'every verdict reached the repo only as PROSE hand-copied into a matrix ref'. And it is the same shape as the ten trend_donchian corpus rows whose hand-transcribed `family` field silently disagreed with classify() until tests/test_rounds_family_matches_classify.py was written: a transcription slip in the 21 prose-only legs would be invisible today, and I made exactly that class of slip twice tonight in ANALYSIS of these same numbers (the p=0.66 pooling of legs at different draw counts, and 'zero false negatives in 17'). NOT A CLAIM THAT THE PROSE IS WRONG. The tables are detailed and each screen was reported with its gates. What is absent is auditability: nothing can re-derive the rate, no guard can check it, and a future session inherits a headline it cannot verify. ALSO NOTE the arms file's block_unit is unset on all 60 rows, so even the covered 22.2% cannot answer the per_leg-vs-family_pooled question it would most be wanted for -- the very comparison this session pre-registered. ONE THING CHECKED AND FOUND SOUND, recorded so nobody re-opens it: the denominator 27 is correct. All 27 family_pooled corpus legs were screened, so it is a screened count and not a corpus-wide count standing in for one. I checked expecting to find that error.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) The per-arm rows for every dispersion screen are committed in one machine-readable file with a stated schema, carrying at minimum leg, fold_offset, block_unit, mean_auc, usable_folds, beats_actual_folds, beats_hard_folds, verdict and provenance -- block_unit specifically, since without it the file cannot answer the question it exists for. Rows already emitted by m20_exit_head_round.py as rounds.jsonl need only be appended; the prose-only legs need transcription, and that transcription is itself the risk this row is about, so it must be done from the arm logs where they survive rather than from the document. Where an arm log is gone, the row is recorded as prose-sourced and SAID to be, never silently mixed in. (b) The headline mover rate is computed BY A SCRIPT from that file rather than maintained by hand, so it cannot go stale confidently -- the same reasoning that removed the hardcoded re-sweep base rate from m20_coverage_rollup.py. (c) A test pins the rate the script computes against the rate any document quotes, in the family of tests/test_rounds_family_matches_classify.py.
items.basis: population: the 27 family_pooled legs screened across all fold-offset screens of 2026-08-15 (denominator verified: all 27 family_pooled rows in docs/research/m20-exit-head-rounds.jsonl were screened, so it is a screened count not a corpus count). Machine-readable coverage measured by set-intersecting the leg names in docs/research/m20-fold-dispersion-arms.jsonl (60 rows, 6 distinct legs) with those 27: 6 covered, 21 not = 22.2% covered / 77.8% prose-only. Window: screens run 2026-08-15 00:55Z-13:20Z.
items.update_20260815_1615z: GOOD NEWS, and a correction to how I nearly scoped this row's remedy. I ran an inventory (trainer relay #9476) that searched /tmp, found ZERO surviving rounds.jsonl, and was about to record 'the arm logs do not survive, so the 21 prose-only legs can only be recovered by re-running the screens'. That would have been wrong. A deeper search WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL (#9477 -- first assert the probe can find the arm that is currently running, then trust its negatives) found every screen's output alive under /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/runtime_logs/m20_exit_head/: donch1h, propdonch1h, donch4h, pull2h, pb1h, cand15m, dispersion, dispersion_clean, determinism and the VOID scalp5m, each with per-arm rounds.jsonl AND round_report.json. The first probe was scoped to the wrong directory, and a search returning nothing is not proof of absence -- the positive control is what separated the two readings. SO THE PROMOTION IS MECHANICAL, NOT LOSSY. No transcription from the document is required and none should be done; criterion (a)'s 'prose-sourced where the log is gone' clause should not be needed. ONE COMPLICATION, from the sibling row BL-20260815-EVIDENCE-ROWS-DO-NOT-RECORD-FOLD-OFFSET: the rows themselves carry no fold_offset, so it must be taken from each arm's round_report.json `_round_meta.fold_offset`. Consolidation therefore records `offset_source` (round_meta / unavailable) and keeps the directory-name offset as a SEPARATE `dir_offset` field to cross-check against, rather than letting one silently stand in for the other; an arm whose meta cannot be read gets a null offset, never a defaulted 0. Consolidation running as trainer relay #9478.
items.resolution: RESOLVED for criterion (a). docs/research/m20-fold-dispersion-arms-consolidated.jsonl is committed: 234 rows / 61 arm files / 60 screens / 33 legs, assembled from every surviving rounds.jsonl under runtime_logs/m20_exit_head/ -- against the 60 rows / 6 legs the old arms file held, a 3.9x increase. No prose transcription was needed or done. fold_offset came from each arm's round_report.json _round_meta (61 of 61 recovered, meta_missing 0), cross-checked against the directory-name offset kept as a SEPARATE dir_offset field: 0 mismatches. Every row carries offset_source='round_meta'; none is a defaulted 0. Transfer sha256-verified end-to-end (92,606 bytes) after a first plain-text emit was silently truncated by GitHub's comment limit at 137 of 234 rows -- caught only because the relay printed its own row count first, which is the same unasserted-denominator shape one layer down in the transport. WHAT THE DATA SAID ABOUT THE PROSE: the headline survives re-derivation. family_pooled 9/27 = 33.3% matches the document exactly; the all-leg figure is 10/30 = 33.3% against a prose 10/29 = 34%. The per_leg count does NOT survive: 3 legs, not 2 (ict_scalp_eth_15m was screened in unanimity2 and uncounted), which invalidated this session's own pre-registered power calculation -- corrected in the research doc before the 5m rows land. A SECOND-ORDER FINDING only the consolidation could surface: 22 legs were measured by more than one screen and on 2 of them the MOVER VERDICT ITSELF disagrees (gdx_pullback_1d, trend_donchian_sol_4h). So 'does this leg move' is itself unstable at ~9%, and every mover rate in the document is one draw of a statistic with its own dispersion. That was unobservable while the two measurements of each leg lived in separate prose tables. STILL OPEN, and tracked here rather than closed silently: criteria (b) and (c) -- the rate is computed by an ad-hoc script in this session, not by a committed one, and no test pins the computed rate against the rate the documents quote. Filed as a follow-up row rather than left implied by this resolution.

items.title: m20_exit_head_round.py stamps total_sort and block_unit on every evidence row but NOT fold_offset — 0 of 33 corpus rows carry the key, so N arms at N offsets are indistinguishable in the one file that gets promoted
items.source: found 2026-08-15T16:15Z while checking whether the running 5m screen's rows would satisfy BL-20260815-DISPERSION-SCREEN-ARMS-NOT-PROMOTED-TO-A-MACHINE-READABLE-RECORD's schema
items.basis: population: all 33 rows of docs/research/m20-exit-head-rounds.jsonl (the committed evidence corpus). Measured by testing for KEY PRESENCE ('fold_offset' in row), not by reading its value: 0 of 33 carry the key. Source-checked against the row literal in m20_exit_head_round.py's rows.append({...}) block, which lists 18 fields and does not include fold_offset, while the _round_meta block in the same function does.
items.detail: The driver emits 18 fields per evidence row -- leg, symbol, tf, lever, n_oos, mean_auc, beats_actual, beats_hard, usable_folds, verdict, tp_cap_pct, tp_geometry, family, prop_sibling, block_unit, pooled_legs_ordered, total_sort, provenance -- and NOT fold_offset. `_round_meta` in the same function does record it, so the round REPORT knows the offset while the row file that gets promoted does not. THE DRIVER ALREADY ARGUES THIS EXACT CASE AGAINST ITSELF. Its comment on `total_sort` reads: 'Legacy rows predate the flag and carry False; a row from a re-measured corpus carries True. WITHOUT IT THE TWO CONVENTIONS POOL INVISIBLY IN ONE EVIDENCE FILE.' That is word-for-word the situation fold_offset is in, and it is the more consequential of the two because the offset is the independent variable of the whole dispersion study. `--fold-offset`'s own help text says it is 'Recorded in _round_meta, because N rounds at N offsets that do not say which offset they used are not a dispersion measurement' -- true of the meta, false of the rows, and the rows are what a corpus is built from. LIVE IMPACT, right now: the 5m screen running since 14:47Z has four arms (off0/4/8/12). Their rounds.jsonl rows will be byte-comparable except for the numbers, with nothing saying which arm produced which -- and indistinguishable from a baseline row too. MY OWN MISREADING, recorded because it is the same defect one level up. Earlier this session I printed the corpus with r.get('fold_offset') and read the resulting 'off=None' on all 33 rows as 'these are all baseline rows'. It is not a recorded null -- the key is ABSENT, and .get() collapsed 'we never wrote this' into 'we wrote nothing'. That is exactly the collapsed-state class CLAUDE.md names, committed while auditing someone else's record for the same thing, and it changed my reading of what the corpus contains.
items.action_taken: NOT fixed mid-screen, deliberately. The trainer re-checks out the branch per arm, so pushing now would give arms off4/8/12 a different driver from off0 -- a code change between arms of a running screen, which my own gate would correctly flag and which would weaken the result to fix its labelling. The field is additive and could not change a verdict, but 'could not' is an argument, not a measurement. ATTRIBUTION FOR THE RUNNING SCREEN IS RECOVERABLE WITHOUT THE FIX: each arm's offset is in its own round_report.json `_round_meta.fold_offset` (which survives the driver's cleanup -- only emit/ and the per-family dataset rows.jsonl are deleted) and redundantly in the arm directory name (off0/off4/off8/off12). So this screen's rows can be stamped at promotion time. Fix the driver once the screen finishes. ⚠️ THE 'NOT FIXED MID-SCREEN' REASONING ABOVE IS NOW OBSOLETE AND WAS BUILT ON THE ROOT CAUSE I LATER MEASURED FALSE. It says 'the trainer re-checks out the branch per arm, so pushing now would give arms off4/8/12 a different driver from off0'. Since 16:13Z the screen runs its CODE from a linked git worktree pinned at a detached HEAD, which the 15-min lock-free `trainer_git_sync.sh` cannot reach and which the driver no longer re-checks-out per arm. Push-safety was MEASURED, not assumed: 15 pushes to the branch during a running arm left both executed files byte-identical. So the fix landed mid-screen safely, and the running screen's rows will still lack the field (they run the pinned pre-fix driver) — recoverable exactly as this row already describes, from each arm's `_round_meta.fold_offset` and its `off<N>` directory name.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) The evidence row carries fold_offset, stamped from the same `a.fold_offset` that _round_meta reads, so the two cannot disagree. (b) A test pins it, in the family of tests/test_exit_head_round_emits_evidence.py -- and it must assert the row literal, since the failure mode is a field that is never written rather than one written wrongly. (c) The 33 existing corpus rows are backfilled with an explicit fold_offset of 0 ONLY where that is established from the round report or the provenance string; any row whose offset cannot be established records it as unknown rather than defaulting to 0, because 'we did not record it' and 'it was the control arm' are different facts and defaulting collapses them -- the same error my .get() made.
items.resolution: All three criteria met on claude/m20-exit-coverage-matrix-8d3he7. (a) The evidence row stamps `fold_offset` from the same `a.fold_offset` `_round_meta` reads, so the two cannot disagree — plus a companion `fold_offset_basis` (`argv` / `predates_flag_<commit>` / `unavailable`), because a backfilled 0 and a measured 0 are not the same claim and the whole point of this row was that collapsing them changed my reading of the corpus. Same shape as the consolidator's `offset_source`. (b) `tests/test_exit_head_round_emits_evidence.py::test_the_row_records_WHICH_FOLD_PARTITION_produced_it`, asserted against the `rows.append({` … write-site region rather than the whole file, and PROVEN LOAD-BEARING by planting both failure modes: field removed (fires) and field present but hardcoded to 0 (fires). Worth recording that my FIRST plant of the second case passed — `.replace(..., 1)` hit the identical string in `_round_meta` rather than in the row, so the plant was wrong, not the test. A plant that does not land is indistinguishable from a guard that does not work unless you check WHICH occurrence you edited. (c) All 33 corpus rows backfilled by the committed, idempotent `scripts/research/m20_backfill_corpus_fold_offset.py` — committed rather than pasted for the same reason the consolidator is: a producer that is a throwaway makes its artifact unreproducible. ESTABLISHMENT, not a default: `--fold-offset` was added in 43820a32 @ 2026-08-14T23:49:18Z, and every row predates it, so each was produced by a driver whose argparse would have REJECTED the flag — the unshifted partition is therefore derived, not assumed. Dating: 28 rows from the `_YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ` round-dir stamp (13:06:57Z..21:23:17Z on 08-14); the 5 rows naming only a relay were dated by READING THE GITHUB API this session, not by inferring from issue numbering — #9156 @ 05:20:00Z, #9206 @ 08:44:23Z, and #9206's own command opens with `git reset --hard origin/main`, independently establishing it ran main where the flag has never existed. A row that could not be dated, or one dated AFTER the flag, records `null` + `unavailable`; zero rows needed it. VERIFIED PURELY ADDITIVE: the corpus round-trips byte-identically through json before the edit, all 33 changed lines are a pure suffix append of the two new keys, and every pre-existing field compares equal across all rows. The corpus path was already in pytest-run's relevance grep, so the guard is actually enforceable (checked — that exact gap bit a different guard earlier today). 21 tests green.

items.title: The fold-dispersion mover rate is still hand-computed — no committed script derives it from the consolidated arms file and no test pins it against the rate the documents quote
items.source: carved out of BL-20260815-DISPERSION-SCREEN-ARMS-NOT-PROMOTED-TO-A-MACHINE-READABLE-RECORD when its criterion (a) was resolved
items.basis: population: docs/research/m20-fold-dispersion-arms-consolidated.jsonl, 234 rows / 60 screens / 33 legs, of which 30 legs have >=2 arms and can therefore move. Rates computed ad hoc this session: all legs 10/30 = 33.3%; family_pooled 9/27 = 33.3%; per_leg 1/3. Dedup rule used: a leg is a mover if it moved in ANY screen; the stricter every-screen rule gives family_pooled 7/27 = 25.9%.
items.detail: The data half is done (the consolidated file exists and is verified); the DERIVATION half is not. The 33.3% figure now quoted in docs/research/m20-fold-dispersion-2026-08-15.md was produced by a script typed into a shell during one session and not kept, so the number is re-derivable in principle and not in practice -- which is a weaker version of the defect the parent row was about. It matters more than usual here because the rate depends on a DEDUP RULE that is a real choice, not a detail: counting a leg as a mover if it moved in ANY screen gives family_pooled 9/27 = 33.3%, while requiring it to move in EVERY screen that measured it gives 7/27 = 25.9%. A rate whose definition lives only in a paragraph will be re-derived under the other rule eventually, and the two differ by 7.4 points. This is the same reasoning that removed the hardcoded re-sweep base rate from m20_coverage_rollup.py: a rate baked into printed text is a claim nothing re-derives.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) A committed script reads the consolidated arms file and prints the mover rates, with the dedup rule NAMED in its output rather than only in its code -- and it must print BOTH the any-screen and every-screen rates, since reporting one silently picks a side of a 7.4-point choice. (b) It states its denominator explicitly, including how many legs were excluded for having <2 arms (14 at present) -- a leg that cannot move must not dilute a rate. (c) A test asserts the rate the script computes equals the rate the research doc quotes, in the family of tests/test_rounds_family_matches_classify.py, so the two cannot drift.
items.resolution: RESOLVED. scripts/research/m20_dispersion_rate.py reads the consolidated arms record and prints the rates; tests/test_dispersion_rate_matches_the_doc.py (6 tests) pins them against the research doc so the two cannot drift. (a) BOTH dedup rules are printed and NAMED in the output -- any-screen (family_pooled 9/27 = 33.3%) and every-screen (7/27 = 25.9%) -- because printing one silently picks a side of a 7.4-point choice. (b) The denominator is stated, including the 14 single-arm screen-leg pairs EXCLUDED: a leg measured at one offset cannot move and would deflate the rate. (c) The disagreeing legs are printed with the caveat attached rather than as a footnote. EVERY TEST PROVEN LOAD-BEARING by planting the defect it guards, and one of them FAILED that proof and was rewritten: test_the_disagreeing_legs_are_NAMED_in_the_doc originally searched the whole document, and since those leg names appear in a dozen other tables it passed with the disagreement section gutted. Scoped to the section around the 'mover verdict itself' anchor; re-planted, and it now fails. A guard that cannot fail is not a guard, and this test file makes that argument about the rules it pins -- it should not have exempted itself. Also pinned: a positive control asserting the two dedup rules actually DIFFER, since a change making them identical would silently make half the module vacuous.

items.title: The trainer queue's definition of 'heavy' is train/build-only, so the replay_pregate* family (4.08 GB measured) is legitimately outside it
items.source: split out of BL-20260815-RESEARCH-TRAINERS-BYPASS-THE-HEAVY-JOB-QUEUE on its resolution, which closed the train/build half and explicitly flagged this as the part it did not cover
items.basis: population: scripts/ml/replay_pregate_fleet.py + replay_pregate.py + replay_pregate_live.py + replay_pregate_summary.py. Measured 2026-08-15T05:32:50Z (trainer-diag #9419): replay_pregate_fleet.py at 4.08 GB RSS on a 6 GB box, load 3.65, 4.4 GB in swap. Its collision with a concurrent exit-head screen made four arms of IDENTICAL work — differing only in --fold-offset, which cannot cost time — run 7.9 / 15.9 / 20.5 / 25.8+ min in launch order. `grep -c heavy_lock` returns 0 for all four.
items.detail: The queue's enforced scope is now three paths (shell wrappers, the `ml` CLI, and the research train/build entrypoints via scripts/ml/_heavy_queue.py), and `trainer-heavy-lock-guard` keeps that set honest. But every one of those covers a job that FITS A MODEL or BUILDS A DATASET. A fleet REPLAY does neither: it loads the fleet and scores, which is why the guard's DECLARED_LIGHT line ('does it fit?') correctly lets a scoring script through — and replay_pregate_fleet.py is the counter-example proving that line is drawn in the wrong place for MEMORY. 4.08 GB is heavier than most of the jobs the queue does protect. THE FIX IS A DEFINITION, NOT A PATCH. Adding these four files to HEAVY_ENTRYPOINTS would make today's scan pass while leaving the next 4 GB eval job equally invisible, and would also make the guard's own stated criterion ('does it fit') disagree with its contents — a guard whose registry contradicts its rule is one nobody can extend correctly. What is needed is a criterion for heavy that is about FOOTPRINT rather than about verb, and it has to be checkable statically or it cannot be guarded.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) A written definition of 'heavy' that covers replay/eval jobs as well as train/build, stated in docs/claude/trainer-resource-protocol.md § Rule 1 beside the three-path table. It must be decidable from the source (the guard cannot measure RSS), e.g. 'loads the fleet / iterates every strategy / reads a full dataset into memory' expressed as a resolvable code property — NOT a hand-maintained list, which is what this row exists to avoid repeating. (b) trainer-heavy-lock-guard's classifier extended to that definition, with its DECLARED_LIGHT rationale updated so the registry and the stated rule agree. (c) The replay_pregate* family either locked or declared light under the new definition, with the reason recorded. Verification: point at the definition, at a guard run whose drift pass classifies all four files, and at a planted-regression run proving the extended classifier still fails closed.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: docs/claude/trainer-resource-protocol.md:86-89 still records the gap in its own words ('Still outside the queue: scripts/ml/replay_pregate_fleet.py and its three replay_pregate* siblings … closing them needs a definition of "heavy"'), and scripts/ci/check_trainer_heavy_lock.py still classifies by HEAVY_ENTRYPOINTS / DECLARED_LIGHT on a 'does it fit?' rule, with no footprint-based criterion. — The fix is a decidable-from-source definition of heavy plus a classifier extension — a design decision, not a mechanical edit, and it must not degenerate into adding four filenames to a list (which the row explicitly forbids).

Re-validated and it is the direct cause of the thrash above: replay_pregate* at 4.08 GB is legitimately outside the queue's train/build-only definition of 'heavy', so it serialises against nothing. Pairs with BL-20260815-WORKTREE-RUN-TAKES-A-PRIVATE-HEAVY-LOCK — two independent ways the trainer's mutual exclusion fails.

items.title: The trainer heavy-job lock path is CHECKOUT-RELATIVE, so a job run from a git worktree takes a PRIVATE mutex, logs heavy_lock_acquired, and serializes against nothing
items.source: found by reading _lock_file() while trying to close a 'lock unexercised on the trainer' gap; CONFIRMED on the box in trainer-vm-diag #9497 with the 5m screen mid-arm
items.basis: population: the two lock implementations and the one running worktree job. MEASURED 2026-08-15T16:42Z (#9497), not inferred: (1) `/tmp/m20_screen_wt/runtime_logs/trainer/.heavy.lock` read **HELD**; (2) `/home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/runtime_logs/trainer/.heavy.lock` read **FREE**; (3) the decisive test — `acquire_heavy_lock('probe_from_main_clone')` launched from the canonical clone while the screen ran **ACQUIRED IMMEDIATELY, rc=0**. Both implementations were asked what they resolve rather than inferred: python-from-main -> the canonical path, python-from-worktree -> the worktree path, shell wrapper -> the canonical path.
items.detail: `src/utils/trainer_heavy_lock.py::_lock_file()` returns `_repo_root()/runtime_logs/trainer/.heavy.lock`, and `_repo_root()` is `parents[2]` of the RUNNING module; `scripts/ops/_trainer_heavy_lock.sh` mirrors it as `$REPO_ROOT/runtime_logs/trainer/.heavy.lock`. That is correct for the canonical clone and a TRAP for any other checkout: the mutex silently becomes per-checkout. A machine-level resource lock whose path depends on which copy of the code you launched cannot do its job. WHY IT SURVIVED REVIEW: every log line said the right thing. The job prints {"status": "heavy_lock_acquired"}, which is TRUE — it did acquire A lock — and there is no output anywhere that distinguishes 'joined the shared queue' from 'created a private one'. The lock message is not evidence the queue was joined; the only check that separates them is whether a second process resolving its repo root differently is actually blocked. This is the diagnostic-provenance A-class one level down: the label describes a quantity adjacent to what was computed. HOW IT GOT HERE, worth recording because both changes were individually right: the worktree was introduced HOURS EARLIER THE SAME SESSION to fix a different problem — the lock-free 15-min `trainer_git_sync.sh` resetting code mid-arm (BL-20260815-RESEARCH-TRAINERS-BYPASS-THE-HEAVY-JOB-QUEUE's correction). Moving the code out of the synced clone was the correct fix for THAT, and it silently opted the job out of the queue. Two correct fixes; their INTERACTION was the defect, which is the seam-defect shape CLAUDE.md's provenance section already names. ALSO NOTED, both minor: my own relay probes in #9492/#9493/#9496 tested `runtime_logs/.trainer_heavy.lock` — a path NEITHER implementation uses — so those 'flock FREE' readings were meaningless, and worse, `flock -n <path> -c true` CREATED that file, so there is now a stray zero-byte lock file on the trainer that a future reader could mistake for real state (it should be removed). And `heavy_lock_holder.json` at the canonical clone still names `drift_retrain` pid 1550937 from 16:05:07Z while the lock reads FREE — that is the documented stale-holder behaviour working as designed (read_holder() treats a dead pid as stale), not a bug, but the file is never cleaned on release so every reader must go through read_holder() rather than cat it.
items.action_taken: PARTIAL, and deliberately the additive half only. scripts/ml/_heavy_queue.py::canonical_lock_file() now points a NON-canonical checkout at the canonical clone's lock via TRAINER_HEAVY_LOCK_FILE (no-op when already canonical, no-op when the canonical clone is absent i.e. CI/dev/sandbox, and an explicit caller override always wins). scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py was importing acquire_heavy_lock DIRECTLY, bypassing that helper entirely, and is now routed through it — it is the one job we KNOW runs from a worktree. Covered by tests/test_heavy_queue_shared_across_checkouts.py, which asserts the property with REAL processes and a REAL flock (a path-string comparison would have passed against the broken version too, since it resolved a perfectly valid path — just not a shared one) and is proven load-bearing by planting the pre-fix return. I did NOT change the default lock path in trainer_heavy_lock.py or the shell wrapper: they agree with each other today, and changing where the mutex lives has a transition window in which an in-flight job holding the OLD path does not serialize against a new job on the NEW one. That is a live-behaviour change to the trainer's scheduled-job serialization and belongs to an operator-awake decision, not an overnight one. THE RUNNING SCREEN IS NOT RETROFITTED and is accepted as-is: its arms are already in flight, each arm is a fresh process but the driver's env is fixed, and a restart costs ~35 min of arm off0 to buy protection against a risk that is bounded — contention costs TIME and carries an OOM risk, but not verdict correctness (an E1 verdict does not depend on wall-clock). Box headroom at the time of the decision: 5,242 MB available. Stated rather than silently accepted.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) The heavy lock resolves to ONE machine-level path independent of which checkout is running, in BOTH implementations (python + shell) so they cannot diverge, with the transition sequenced so no window exists in which two live jobs take different files. (b) The acquisition message distinguishes joining the shared queue from creating a private one — e.g. `heavy_lock_acquired` carries the resolved path, so the log line alone is falsifiable; today it is not. (c) A guard or test asserts the property across checkouts rather than asserting a path string. (a) is the operator-gated half; (b) and (c) are Tier-1. Verification: point at a run from a worktree that BLOCKS on a lock held from the canonical clone, and at the log line naming the path it took.

items.title: Three exit_head_ml cells state their block using the LEVER sweep's date-split arithmetic, and name an 'earlier split' escape route the exit-head fold code forecloses
items.source: found while checking whether the mes/mgc/mhg exit_head_ml cells were reachable — a gap an earlier turn of this session had recorded as 'deeper futures series existence NOT measured' and which relay #9195 had in fact already closed
items.basis: population: the 12 blocked exit_head_ml cells in docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json. 3 of 12 (mes_trend_long_1d, mgc_pullback_1d, mhg_pullback_1d) reason from MIN_OOS_TRADES=25 + the 'corpus-standard split 2025-07-01'; the other 7 equity 1d cells + squeeze_breakout_4h reason from lifetime trades and the >=100-for-one-fold bound. Fold arithmetic COMPUTED against the real code (scripts/ml/train_exit_head.py::fold_blocks, `range(block_n, len(ordered)-block_n+1, block_n)`), not from prose: u=len(range(50,N-49,50)) gives u=0 for N in {33,74,80,99}, u=1 at N=100, u=2 at N=150.
items.detail: `MIN_OOS_TRADES=25` and the date-based IS/OOS split live in `m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py` and govern the LEVER sweep. `exit_head_ml` is graded by `train_exit_head.fold_blocks`, which has NO date split: it sorts harness trades and cuts fixed blocks of `--min-fold-trades` (50) starting one block in, so the usable-fold count u depends on LIFETIME trades alone. u>=2 needs N>=150; even one fold needs N>=100. The three futures legs have 33/74/80 lifetime trades, so u=0 at ANY split and the E1 gate cannot be evaluated at all. The refs nonetheless carried: 'NOTE for MGC/MHG the lifetime total means an EARLIER split could arithmetically reach 25 OOS, but only by trading away in-sample — a judgement flagged here, not silently made'. The flagging is careful and the judgement is real under the lever-sweep protocol; it just is not this lever's protocol. WHY IT MATTERS: the same ref exists partly to stop a session burning time on a dead route — it records that a 2026-08-14 session spent an hour pulling IBKR history on a premise that was not the binding gate — and then named a second dead route of its own. A future session reading 'an earlier split could reach 25 OOS' has an actionable-looking lead that cannot work. THE MATRIX ALREADY CONTAINED THE RIGHT ARITHMETIC ONE COLUMN OVER, which is what makes this a drift rather than an unknown: the seven equity 1d cells in the SAME lever say '48 lifetime harness trades; a 50-trade test block needs >=100 for one fold, so BOTH fold modes' — correct, and inconsistent with its three neighbours. NOT A STATUS ERROR: all three cells are correctly `blocked:insufficient_lifetime_trades`, and the headline is unchanged at 373/376 = 99.2%.
items.action_taken: The three refs carry an appended correction stating the fold arithmetic, the computed u=0, and that the block is arithmetic rather than data availability ('do not re-split'). Statuses deliberately untouched — verified programmatically that zero cell statuses changed across the edit. coverage-matrix validation, matrix-corpus-agreement and matrix-config-agreement all re-run green; headline unchanged.
items.resolution_criteria: Met: (a) the three refs no longer name a route the code forecloses, and state the arithmetic that actually binds; (b) no status moved (asserted by diffing every cell's status old-vs-new, not by eye); (c) the matrix guards pass and the headline is unchanged. THE CLASS-LEVEL HALF IS NOW DONE TOO, and NOT the way this row first proposed it. The proposal was a blocked-reason VOCABULARY check; that would not have caught this instance, because both arithmetics wrote the same status string (`blocked:insufficient_lifetime_trades`) and the divergence was in ref PROSE. A keyword guard over prose would also be brittle and cheap to lie to, which this repo already rules out (new-table-wiring-guard). What was actually wrong is that the lifetime-trade counts lived ONLY in prose, so nothing could recompute the bound. Fixed by promoting them to a `lifetime_trades` FIELD on all 11 blocked cells and having `m20_coverage_rollup.py` DERIVE u from it — mirroring `train_exit_head.fold_blocks`'s own `range(b, N-b+1, b)` rather than a closed form, so a change to the fold construction surfaces as a diff instead of a stale formula. The roll-up now prints, per cell, N / u / how many trades short of u>=2, and states that 11 of 11 cannot form a SINGLE fold — so 'the block is arithmetic, not data availability' is computed rather than asserted. A cell missing the field is REPORTED as ungraded, never skipped. Covered by tests/test_fold_reachability_is_derived.py, proven load-bearing by planting both classes: stripping the field from one cell fires 2 tests, and drifting the derivation to a closed form that disagrees with fold_blocks fires the arithmetic test. Statuses untouched; headline unchanged.

items.title: exit_ladder is sweepable on the donchian/pullback harnesses but NO driver emits the column, so the 2 open cells cannot be closed by re-running anything
items.source: found while checking whether the 3 remaining PENDING cells on live legs are genuine work or mislabels; two of the three are exit_ladder on the prop donchian legs that graduated shadow->live 2026-08-13
items.basis: POPULATION: the 52 rows of docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json, exit_ladder column. 45 honest_negative / 3 pending / 2 blocked:no_harness_levers / 1 blocked:native-history-thin / 1 passed_unshipped. MEASURED, not inferred: (a) bank-flag hits per harness -- backtest_ict_scalp.py 32, backtest_trend.py 16, backtest_pullback.py 17, backtest_squeeze.py 0, backtest_fvg_range.py 0; (b) `exit_ladder` has ZERO non-comment occurrences in scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py, and its --levers is constrained to choices=sorted(LEVER_DECLARED_KEYS) = {stale_stop, giveback_stop, trail_decay, vol_trail}; (c) the ONLY driver that constructs exit_ladder cells is scripts/research/m27/ict_scalp_exit_sweep.py::ladder_cells(), whose _HARNESS is HARDCODED to scripts/backtest_ict_scalp.py. COHERENCE CHECK that this read is right: the two cells already carrying blocked:no_harness_levers are squeeze_breakout_4h and fvg_range_15m -- exactly the two harnesses measuring 0 bank flags. The vocabulary is being applied correctly; the gap is elsewhere.
items.detail: The harness CAPABILITY exists for donchian/pullback (--bank-frac/--bank-at-r are implemented in backtest_trend.py and backtest_pullback.py). What is missing is a DRIVER wired to it: the fleet sweep -- which is what .github/workflows/m20-exit-lever-sweep.yml invokes on free runners -- cannot emit the exit_ladder column at all, and the driver that can (m27 ladder_cells) is pinned to the scalp harness. So the 45 honest_negative donchian/pullback verdicts rest on the 2026-07-12 memo-era pass (refs cite `memo M20-exit-refinement-2026-07-12 section 6.2` and `fleet sweep 2026-07-12 (runtime_logs/m20_fleet)`), and NO currently-runnable tool reproduces that column for a leg added since. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE 2 CELLS: this is the capability-present/driver-absent shape, which reads from the matrix exactly like ordinary un-run work.
