items.title: claim-basis-guard scans title/description/source/action/resolution/resolution_criteria but NOT 'detail', which is where this backlog actually keeps its evidence
items.detail:
scripts/check_claim_basis.py::_row_text joins six fields and 'detail' is not among
them. In docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json the overwhelming majority of rows put
their population, denominator and window in 'detail' - that is the field the schema's
own convention uses for evidence.

So the guard has both error directions:
  FALSE POSITIVE - a row whose 'detail' states the population fully still fails if the
    headline number sits in the title. Observed directly: this session wrote a row with
    'n=694' and both process ids in 'detail' and was still failed, then passed it by
    duplicating the basis into 'resolution_criteria'. The remedy the guard actually
    rewards is restating evidence in a second field, not stating it.
  FALSE NEGATIVE - a row with a bare 'n=1' anywhere in a scanned field passes, however
    unrelated that n is to the claimed percentage. The check is presence-of-a-pattern,
    not agreement between the claim and its basis.

The guard's PREMISE is right and it caught a genuinely under-specified row here - this
is about its field coverage, not its existence. Noting the adjacent lesson from
new-table-wiring-guard, recorded in CLAUDE.md: a guard that is cheaper to satisfy by
restating than by stating drifts toward being satisfied rather than being right.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. Add 'detail' to _row_text, then re-run against the existing backlog to size the
blast radius before merging - it is diff-scoped to NEW rows, so this is low-risk, but
confirm it does not silence rows that currently fail for good reason.
2. Consider whether the basis should be required in the SAME field as the claim rather
than anywhere in the row; that would close the false-negative half. Weigh against the
cost of more false positives on rows that legitimately split claim from evidence.

updates.note: DENOMINATOR MEASURED, and the field split is worse than 'detail is omitted'. Counted over all 609 rows on main: 352 rows carry `description`, 112 carry `detail`, 81 carry NEITHER, and 369 carry an `updates` list. `_row_text` reads `description` but not `detail`, so 112 of 609 rows (18.4%) have their evidence field invisible to the guard — and it never reads `updates` at all, which is where 369 rows accumulate their follow-up measurements (this note included). Found while appending to two rows and getting a KeyError on `detail` for a row that uses `description`+`updates`: the backlog has at least three co-existing shapes, so any tool reading one field name is reading a minority of the file.

[sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: scripts/check_claim_basis.py::_row_text (lines 78-81) still joins exactly six fields — title, description, source, action, resolution, resolution_criteria — and 'detail' is absent, while the health backlog's own convention puts population/denominator/window in `detail` (visible across most rows in the triage input). — Low severity; the guard's premise is right and it does catch genuinely under-specified rows. Ends when 'detail' is scanned and the blast radius is measured before merge.

items.resolution:
RESOLVED — `scripts/check_claim_basis.py::_ROW_TEXT_FIELDS` (lines 100-104) now includes `detail` and `evidence` alongside title/description/source/action/resolution/resolution_criteria/why_it_matters/summary/impact. The file's own comment at line 85 dates the widening 2026-08-20 and records that the guard is diff-scoped to rows absent from the base, so widening the tuple held NEW rows to the standard without retro-failing the 16 pre-existing ones. Read from the file this session, not inferred from a merge.

DUPLICATE: BL-20260820-CLAIM-BASIS-GUARD-DOES-NOT-SCAN-DETAIL-OR-EVIDENCE is the same defect filed four days later and is closed on the same evidence.

items.opened_by: claude (exit-eval-interval session, found while trying to verify my own deploy)
items.tier: 1 (the fix is a read surface + a doc correction; no runtime behaviour changes)
items.title: The post-deploy git_sha round-trip assertion compares on-disk HEAD to on-disk HEAD, so it cannot fail for the incident class it was built to catch - and no read surface exposes what the RUNNING processes are executing
items.detail:
FOUND WHILE VERIFYING MY OWN MERGE (#9574, squash 5b64edca, merged 08:31Z). I read
/api/diag/status at 08:32Z and got git_sha 5b64edca - my merge - beside
bot_uptime_s 1892, i.e. a process started 2026-08-16T08:01:06Z, TWENTY-FIVE MINUTES
BEFORE that sha existed. A process cannot be running code that did not exist when it
started, so the field is not reporting what a reader takes it to report.

THE MECHANISM, read from code rather than inferred:
  src/web/runtime_status.py::_resolve_git_sha shells `git rev-parse --short HEAD`
  against the working tree, with NO caching. write_status() calls it from
  src/runtime/pipeline.py:1006 on EVERY tick, and src/web/api/routers/diag.py:1157
  (/api/diag/version) calls the SAME helper at REQUEST time.
So both surfaces answer 'what does the checkout on disk say?', never 'what code is
this process executing?'. They diverge for exactly the window between an
ict-git-sync pull and the service restart - which is precisely when someone checks.

THE PART THAT MAKES THIS HIGH, not a nitpick. scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh:496-543
runs a 'post-deploy version round-trip assertion' whose own comment says it
'Catches the 2026-05-09 incident class - web-api advertised "running" via systemd but
its IN-PROCESS git SHA was 24+h stale because nothing in the deploy chain restarted
it.' It curls /api/diag/version and compares the reported git_sha to POST_SYNC_HEAD.
But that endpoint re-reads on-disk HEAD, which IS POST_SYNC_HEAD by construction at
that point in the script. A web-api that was never restarted returns the new sha and
PASSES. The assertion is vacuously true and cannot detect the failure it names.
There is no in-process git SHA anywhere in this codebase to compare against.

WHAT IS NOT BROKEN, so nobody 'fixes' the wrong half: the RESTART DECISION itself is
sound. deploy_pull_restart.sh:265+ drives it off runtime_logs/deployed_sha.txt - the
sha the services were last restarted ONTO - which is the correct notion and was added
for exactly this class. The defect is that the VERIFICATION step ignores that marker
and asks a question that answers itself.

SECOND, SEPARATE FINDING, caught by artifact-validity-guard when I cited it: the
deploy script attributes that restart-gate work to a backlog id THAT WAS NEVER FILED.
`BL-2026 0714-DEPLOY-STALE-ON-OOB-SYNC` (written with a space so quoting it here does
not itself trip the guard - it cannot distinguish an id cited as an EXAMPLE from one
cited as TRACKING, and it is right not to try) appears at scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh
lines 85, 246 and 559 and resolves to nothing in any of the three backlogs. Three
citations in a LIVE DEPLOY SCRIPT that read as 'this is tracked' while being tracked by
nobody. I reached for the id from that comment and the guard stopped me propagating it -
the same trap a session hit on 2026-08-14 reaching for an id from memory
(S-IB-EXIT-COVERAGE-2026-08-14 § Validation). A comment asserting an id is a CLAIM
about a row, not the row.

AND deployed_sha.txt HAS NO READ SURFACE: zero references in
src/web/api/routers/diag.py, and it is not in the /api/diag/log_file allowlist. So the
VM writes down the right answer and nothing exposes it. From outside, the only way to
tell whether a trader-side change is actually live is to infer it from bot_uptime_s /
exit_loop_health.process_started_utc and compare against the merge time by hand -
which is what I did, and only because a 25-minute impossibility made me look.

CLASS: this is 'Diagnostic provenance' sub-class A (CLAUDE.md) - the label names
quantity Q (running code version), the code called f() (on-disk HEAD), f() != Q - and
simultaneously the 'green that checked nothing' failure in CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.
It fails in the DANGEROUS direction: it makes an undeployed change look deployed.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. Add a read surface for runtime_logs/deployed_sha.txt (log_file allowlist entry, or
a field on /api/diag/version). This is the cheap half and it is what a session
actually needs to answer 'is my change live?'.
2. Make the field self-describing rather than renaming it silently: /api/diag/version
and runtime_status should report the on-disk sha AND the deployed sha as SEPARATE
keys, so 'checkout is at X' and 'the running processes were started onto Y' can never
again be read as one number. X != Y is itself the pending-restart signal.
3. Fix the assertion in deploy_pull_restart.sh:496-543 to compare against the
deployed-sha marker (or a genuine in-process value), or delete it. An assertion that
cannot fail is worse than none: it is on the deploy path and reads as coverage.
4. Correct CLAUDE.md's /api/diag/version row, which says it is 'Used by
scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh to confirm a post-deploy restart actually rolled the
code forward'. It is used there, but it cannot confirm that.
5. Separately: either file the missing row the deploy script cites three times, or
correct those three comments to state the property directly instead of attaching it to
an id that does not exist. Do not simply delete the reasoning - it is the only record
of why the restart gate reads deployed_sha.txt.

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The only commit touching this (a0f559b, HEAD-1) changes docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json alone (16 insertions) — it FILED the row, it did not fix it. In the tree: `grep -rn deployed_sha src/ scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh` finds the marker only in the deploy script (:80,:258,:265) — no read surface on /api/diag/version, no log_file allowlist entry, and src/web/runtime_status.py::_resolve_git_sha still shells `git rev-parse` against the working tree for both surfaces, so the post-deploy assertion still compares on-disk HEAD to on-disk HEAD. — Tier-1 (read surface + doc correction; no runtime behaviour change), but it touches the deploy path, so land it as its own reviewed change rather than inside a triage pass.

updates.by: claude (exit-eval-interval session — the SAME session that filed this row at 08:40Z)
updates.note:
I STEPPED IN THIS EXACT TRAP AGAIN SEVEN HOURS AFTER FILING THIS ROW, which is a fact about the row's effectiveness and not just about me. At 15:20:17Z I read /api/diag/version, got git_sha '7da0842b', and reported to the operator that the #9693 deploy had landed on the trader. Same endpoint, same wrong inference, same day. Then I re-derived the mechanism from source and started filing it a SECOND time as a new row before the artifact-validity-guard tripped on an unrelated dangling id and led me here. The duplicate has been deleted rather than kept.

WHAT THAT SAYS: the row is correct and it did not protect the next reader, because the defect is in a surface you reach for reflexively while doing something else, and nothing at the point of use says so. A backlog row cannot fix that. The resolution criteria should be read as urgent for that reason -- until the endpoint reports process_git_sha beside disk_git_sha, every reader re-derives this or, more likely, does not.

NEW EVIDENCE, the consumer half: scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh (~lines 499-547) compares the endpoint's git_sha against POST_SYNC_HEAD -- the sha it just pulled to -- while the endpoint computes that same tree's HEAD at request time. POST_SYNC_HEAD vs POST_SYNC_HEAD. The assertion cannot fail, and it reports PASSING, which CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL calls the same sin as a red that checked nothing.

ADJACENT, PRE-EXISTING, AND NOT FIXED BY ME: that same script cites a `BL-20260714` deploy-stale-on-out-of-band-sync tracking id THREE times (lines 85, 246, 559) to justify its restart-decision gate, and that id is filed in NO backlog. The deploy path's central correctness argument points at a row that does not exist. artifact-validity-guard misses it because the guard is DIFF-SCOPED -- it flags ids a change introduces, so pre-existing dangling citations are grandfathered; it caught me only because I copied the id into a new row. Running that guard with --all as a standing audit would surface this class. I have not filed the missing row: I do not know what that investigation concluded, and inventing one to silence a guard is the 'cheaper to lie to than to satisfy' failure this repo names.

RESOLVED — all five criteria, checked one at a time against the live endpoint and the code rather than against the merge that claimed them.

1. READ SURFACE — MET, in the criterion's own stated alternative ('or a field on /api/diag/version'). Live read 2026-08-25T16:3xZ:
     {"git_sha":"9c9f8472","git_sha_on_disk":"9c9f8472",
      "restart_pending":false,"captured_at":"2026-08-25T16:31:22Z"}
2. SELF-DESCRIBING SEPARATE KEYS — MET. `git_sha` is `_RUNNING_GIT_SHA`, captured ONCE AT IMPORT (diag.py:280) so it names the code the process actually loaded; `git_sha_on_disk` resolves the worktree live. 'checkout is at X' and 'the running process was started onto Y' can no longer be read as one number, and X != Y IS the pending-restart signal, exactly as the criterion asked.
3. THE ASSERTION — MET, and this is the one that mattered. deploy_pull_restart.sh:553 reads `git_sha` from the endpoint and compares it to HEAD. That comparison was VACUOUS while the endpoint shelled `git rev-parse` at request time (X == X over the same tree); with the value import-captured it now compares the RUNNING sha to HEAD and can genuinely fail. The script cites BL-20260823-DIAG-VERSION-REPORTS-DISK-SHA-NOT-RUNNING-CODE at line 506, so this was addressed deliberately rather than incidentally.
4. CLAUDE.md — MET. Its /api/diag/version row now carries the ⚠️ correction recording that the endpoint reported the DISK sha until 2026-08-23 and that the deploy assertion was vacuous, with the measured proof (the endpoint returned fced7279 while the same process 400'd a log_file name that exists in fced7279).
5. THE MISSING ROWS — MET TODAY, and it was still open. Measured by extracting every BL- id cited in scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh and differencing against the ids filed across all three backlogs: THREE distinct ids resolved to nothing —
     BL-20260714-DEPLOY-STALE-ON-OOB-SYNC   x3  (the id this row named)
     BL-20260615-DEPLOY-NOOP                x2
     BL-20260622-GATEWAY-GIT-SYNC           x1
All three are now filed as `resolved` records — the fixes have been in the code for months; what was missing was the row. Filing rather than deleting, per this row's own instruction that the reasoning is the only record of why the restart gate reads deployed_sha.txt.

⚠️ WHY THE GUARD DID NOT CATCH THEM, worth stating because it is the general lesson: `artifact-validity-guard` is DIFF-SCOPED — it fails a change that INTRODUCES an unresolvable id and grandfathers everything already in the tree. So a dangling citation that predates the guard is invisible to it forever, and reads as tracked while being tracked by nobody. A periodic whole-tree sweep is the only thing that finds these; today's was ad hoc.

items.next_action: DONE. Follow-up worth considering separately: an --all whole-tree mode for artifact-validity-guard, since its diff scoping means a dangling citation older than the guard can never be found by it.

items.source: Operator asked why the live XRPUSDT short (bybit_2, xrp_pullback_2h, open since 2026-07-29T12:16Z, ~18d) has run through weeks of chop without its exit levers doing anything. Reading the live row against the leg's YAML: the leg declares trail_decay_arm_r: 4.49 while its take-profit is clamped by the 9.9% venue-sentinel cap to ~3.92R for that trade's risk. The arm threshold is ABOVE the ceiling, so the lever is arithmetically unable to fire.
items.title: [exit-levers] A declared trail_decay_arm_r can sit ABOVE the R the 9.9% TP cap allows, making the lever silently inert on the live leg
items.description:
trail_decay arms on the since-entry favourable extreme reaching trail_decay_arm_r R (src/runtime/trail_decay.py docstring). The donchian/pullback/fade/squeeze families clamp TP to min(entry*(1+0.099), entry + tp_r*risk) (_TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT, e.g. htf_pullback_trend_2h.py:322), so with tp_r: 50.0 the cap ALWAYS binds and the reachable ceiling is cap_R = 0.099 * entry / risk. A trade cannot exceed cap_R in MFE without the TP filling first. Therefore any leg where arm_r > cap_R has a declared, operator-approved, Tier-3-gated exit lever that can never arm.

MEASURED INSTANCE (n=1, the live trade): xrp_pullback_2h, entry 1.0806, entry-stop 1.10786786 (read off the bybit_portfolio mirror row 4164 — the real-money row 4163's stop has already ratcheted to 1.04193571 and is no longer the entry risk), risk 0.02726786 = 2.5233% of entry. cap_R = 0.099/0.025233 = 3.923R vs arm_r 4.49R — unreachable by 14.5%. Its TP (0.9736206) is exactly 9.900% from entry, i.e. the cap, confirming the clamp is what set it. So through ~18 days the trail has run at the BASE trail_mult 5.0 and trail_decay_tight_mult 2.5 has never applied — which is precisely the behaviour the operator flagged.

SCOPE (config-derived, NOT yet measured): 6 live+enabled legs declare trail_decay_arm_r. The ATR/entry ratio at which each becomes reachable is 0.099/(arm_r*atr_stop_mult): trend_donchian 6.49 -> 0.610%, trend_donchian_sol_4h 5.57 -> 0.711%, gld_pullback_1d 5.06 -> 0.978%, xrp_pullback_2h 4.49 -> 0.882%, qqq_trend_long_1d 3.56 -> 1.112%, scha_trend_long_1d 2.00 -> 1.980%. Above that ratio the lever is inert; below it, it can fire. Only XRP is measured (1.009% actual vs 0.882% required).

WHY IT HAPPENED — same root as the tp-cap defect family: the arm values are winner-MFE p80 cells from sweeps that predate the cap entirely. `tp_cap_pct` first appears anywhere under scripts/ on 2026-08-10 (c9cbc0e2); the xrp arm value's config comment cites a 2026-07-13 sweep. A p80 of winner MFE computed on an UNCAPPED book (tp_r 50 => effectively no TP) is a threshold from a distribution production cannot produce. This is the LIVE-CONFIG consequence of BL-20260816-TP-CAP-PCT-DEFAULTS-TO-LEGACY-GEOMETRY / BL-20260814-THREE-SIBLING-SWEEPS-STILL-BUILD-NO-TAKE-PROFIT-BOOKS-AND-STAMP-NOTHING: those record wrong EVIDENCE; this records a wrong LIVE VALUE derived from it.

NOT A COLLAPSED-STATE BUG AND NOT SILENT-BY-DESIGN — trail_decay.py is fail-safe and correct; it is handed a threshold it can never meet. Nothing anywhere asserts arm_r <= the leg's reachable cap_R, so an inert lever is indistinguishable from an armed one that simply has not triggered yet. inert_giveback_reason (m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:628) is the existing precedent for refusing a provably inert parameterization at SWEEP time; there is no equivalent at DECLARE time.
items.trigger_condition: Any leg on a TP-capped family (donchian/pullback/fade/squeeze) declaring an R-threshold exit lever; re-check whenever an arm_r is swept or a tp_r/atr_stop_mult changes.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) Measure cap_R per trade for all 6 legs from the live journal and/or the canonical CSVs (scripts/research/m20_ladder_headroom.py already computes cap_r_p10/p50/p90 per leg — extend it to compare against each leg's declared arm_r rather than adding a second definition); (2) for every leg where arm_r exceeds the cap_R the leg actually attains, EITHER re-sweep the arm on a live-parity (0.099) book and propose the corrected value to the operator, OR record the lever as inert so the coverage matrix stops counting it as shipped; (3) add a check (CI guard or declare-time refusal) that a declared R-threshold lever is reachable under the leg's own TP geometry, so this class cannot be re-declared silently; (4) Tier-3: any arm_r change is an operator decision — this item proposes, it does not flip.

updates.note:
TWO measurements + one mechanism, from the first live data (diag #9587, order packages for all 6 legs).

(1) THE FIELD I WAS READING WAS WRONG. `entry - stop_loss` is the CURRENT stop's distance, not the entry risk — a stop is trailed and amended. Measured: gld_pullback_1d and qqq_trend_long_1d agree with `signalLogic.risk_per_unit` to 1.00, xrp_pullback_2h's ratio is 0.71, and one trend_donchian package read 5.66x TIGHTER than its own recorded risk. THE ERROR HAS NO FIXED SIGN — a stop trailed into profit overstates risk and DEFLATES cap_R; one amended tighter INFLATES it — so there is no bias correction, only the right field. On the live xrp short against arm 4.49R the three readings are 3.92R (sized, correct), 2.77R (trailed — right answer, wrong reason) and >4.49R (tightened — a `reachable` verdict on a lever that cannot fire). The audit now prefers `risk_per_unit` and reports the basis MIX per leg so a fallback-only measurement cannot read like a sized one.

(2) A SECOND LEG MEASURES INERT. gld_pullback_1d: cap_R 3.01R vs arm 5.06R. xrp_pullback_2h: cap_R 3.92R vs arm 4.49R. BOTH AT n=1 — the relay truncates at 55000 bytes and an order-package row is ~6KB, so 6 paths yielded 8 rows total. A denominator of one is not a distribution; candle-derived ATR pulls are queued (#9592/#9593) to replace it with ~100 bars per leg. qqq_trend_long_1d WOULD be inert too (cap_R 2.13R vs arm 3.56R) but still grades `cap_unknown` because its family string does not resolve to a known-capped one — the audit under-claims deliberately.

(3) THE FIX PATH IS STRUCTURALLY COMPLETE, which was not obvious when this was filed. `m20_fleet_exit_sweep.base_args` appends `--tp-cap-pct` (and `--tp-r`) for capped families, and `winner_mfe_p80` runs the harness with that SAME `base` — so a live-parity p80 arm is drawn from a book whose TP is clamped and is therefore bounded by cap_R by construction. A re-sweep at 0.099 cannot re-emit an unreachable arm. That makes the queued `--tp-cap-pct` default flip (BL-20260816-TP-CAP-PCT-DEFAULTS-TO-LEGACY-GEOMETRY) the whole remedy for future arms, and leaves only the 6 existing values to re-derive.

FLEET MEASUREMENT (candle-derived ATR, diag #9592/#9593 — 120 bars per leg at the leg's own timeframe, ATR(14), risk/entry = atr_stop_mult * ATR/close, cap_R = 0.099/(risk/entry)). THREE legs are inert or near-inert; ONE is vol-conditional; TWO are fine.

  leg                    arm_R  ATR%p50  cap_R p50  reach%   read
  trend_donchian (1h)     6.49    0.333     11.91    100.0   reachable
  trend_donchian_sol_4h   5.57    1.114      3.56      2.8   NEAR-INERT
  gld_pullback_1d         5.06    1.880      2.63      0.0   INERT
  xrp_pullback_2h         4.49    0.680      5.83     90.5   vol-conditional
  qqq_trend_long_1d       3.56    1.863      2.13      0.0   INERT
  scha_trend_long_1d      2.00    1.786      2.22     73.6   reachable

⚠️ THE TWO BASES DISAGREE ON XRP AND THE DISAGREEMENT IS THE POINT. Candle ATR is UNCONDITIONAL; entries are selected by each strategy's filters and need not sample the same vol. The one measured xrp ENTRY sat at ATR/entry 1.009% (cap_R 3.92, inert) against a 120-bar median of 0.680% (cap_R 5.83, reachable) — a 49% gap, and the entry-conditioned reading is the more pessimistic one. So the honest statement for xrp is NOT 'the lever is inert' but 'the lever is unreachable at the vol this trade was entered in and reachable at recent median vol' — it is a vol-conditional lever, which nothing in the config or the sweep records. gld and qqq are the strong findings because the two bases AGREE there (gld 2.63 candle vs 3.01 package; qqq 2.13 vs 2.13), and both sit far below their arms.

THE AUTHORITATIVE DENOMINATOR IS ENTRY-CONDITIONED RISK, not candle ATR. The wide candle sample is a cheap proxy that can be biased in either direction; a per-leg order-package pull at n>=30 is the measurement that settles each leg. Do not quote the candle reach% as the verdict.

SEPARATELY RESOLVED: capped-ness for the equity legs. `qqq_trend_long_1d` / `scha_trend_long_1d` match no family tag, so a family-only test graded them `cap_unknown` — but their signal builders import `order_package` from `src.units.strategies.trend_donchian`, which carries `_TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT` (strategy_signal_builders.py:3370). The audit now resolves capped-ness through the builder's unit module when the family string does not resolve, and reports which basis it used. All 7 declared reach-gates on live legs are now established as CAPPED (4 by family, 3 by builder unit) — the family-only test was under-claiming on every equity leg, which is exactly the direction that hides a finding.

ENTRY-CONDITIONED MEASUREMENT (per-leg order-package pulls, #9597-#9602). This is the AUTHORITATIVE basis; the candle proxy from the prior update is superseded where the two disagree. READ EVERY DENOMINATOR — they differ per leg and two are thin.

**gld_pullback_1d — COMPLETE, and DEFINITIVE. 0 of 8.** The server returned `count: 8` untruncated, i.e. the leg's ENTIRE package history. risk/entry 3.294-4.506%, cap_R 2.20-3.01, max 3.01 against arm 5.06. Not one entry in the leg's whole life could have reached its own declared arm. `atr_stop_mult` is 2.0 here, not 2.5.

**xrp_pullback_2h — 2 of 6 = 33.3%, and the SAMPLE IS TRUNCATED AND RECENCY-BIASED.** cap_R 3.92 / 4.01 / 4.08 / 4.43 / 7.21 / 8.38 against arm 4.49 — four of six entries could not have armed it. The relay returned 55,429 of 224,462 bytes (order-packages rows are ~6KB and the comment budget is 55KB), so these are the SIX NEWEST of up to 25; do not read 33.3% as the lifetime rate. What it does settle is the CHARACTER of the leg: neither inert nor reachable but VOL-CONDITIONAL, arming on roughly a third of recent entries.

**THE CANDLE PROXY IS NOT RELIABLY CONSERVATIVE AND ITS BIAS HAS NO FIXED SIGN** — the same shape as the risk-field defect one update up. On xrp it OVERSTATED badly (90.5% candle vs 33.3% entry-conditioned; cap_R p50 5.83 vs 4.26), because entries are filter-selected and do not sample the unconditional vol distribution. On gld it UNDERSTATED slightly (2.63 vs a 2.80 package median). So the candle basis cannot be used as a bound in either direction — it is a cheap screen that says where to look, and the entry-conditioned pull is what decides. The one place this matters for a verdict is xrp, where the two bases straddle the arm.

STATE OF THE SIX LEGS, with each denominator named:
  gld_pullback_1d        INERT       0/8 entry-conditioned, COMPLETE history
  qqq_trend_long_1d      inert       n=1 package (cap_R 2.13) + candle 0.0% — thin, but both agree
  trend_donchian_sol_4h  near-inert  CANDLE ONLY (2.8%) — no entry-conditioned pull yet
  xrp_pullback_2h        vol-conditional  2/6 newest entries, truncated sample
  scha_trend_long_1d     reachable   candle 73.6%
  trend_donchian (BTC)   reachable   candle 100%, package cap_R 16.85

gld is now decidable on its own: an arm no entry in the leg's entire history could reach is not a tuning question. The other five want their own pulls before a value is chosen — one path per relay issue, since six paths share one 55KB budget and starved every leg to 1-3 rows on the first attempt.

Re-validated: a declared lever that is silently INERT because its arm sits above the reachable R. Same family as BL-20260817-A-SHIPPED-LEVER-RE-SWEPT-AGAINST-ITSELF-READS-AS-A-MEASURED-NO-OP and PB-20260824-COSMETIC-TARGETS-ABOVE-CAP-R. These three should be worked as one class: a declared lever whose arm is unreachable is decoration.

items.title: scripts/reports/backlog_counts.py counted 96 genuinely-open items as resolved — including EVERY kept_open, the status the drain protocol itself mandates
items.detail:
FOUND BY RUNNING IT. backlog_counts.py is the review-coverage gate's own input: /system-review copies its output straight into consolidated.backlog_summary, and the SKILL forbids hand-entering those numbers precisely so they are trustworthy.

THE DEFECT: it allowlisted OPEN statuses and treated everything unrecognised as RESOLVED — the exact inverse of the policy stated in its own module docstring ('unknown/missing -> open (fail toward "still needs attention")'). Field beats comment normally; here the comment stated the CORRECT policy and the code was wrong, so the code moved.

MEASURED at the moment of the fix: 96 genuinely-open items reported as resolved — health 47, performance 30, ml 19. The dominant cause is that `kept_open` was absent from the open set, and `kept_open` is the status the drain protocol MANDATES for a deferred item. This session's own first roll-up read 'performance: 0 open' and 'ml: 0 open' while 30 and 19 sat parked, several of them gates MET awaiting an operator.

Secondary causes the inversion also fixes: FREE-TEXT statuses (five health items whose status literally starts with 'open'), and NOT-ACTUALLY-CLOSED terminals (fix_landed_monitoring, resolved_pending_live_verification, likely_already_fixed_unverified, mitigated, root_cause_fixed_backlog_remains).

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE NUMBER: a roll-up that under-reports open work is worse than no roll-up — it is the input to the gate that decides whether a review did its backlog job.
items.resolution_criteria: MET in PR #9612. (1) Polarity inverted — CLOSED is the allowlist (is_open_status), so anything unrecognised counts as OPEN. (2) A terminal-looking status carrying an open-signal stays open. (3) 34 tests with a CAN-FAIL CONTROL: restoring the old polarity fails 14. (4) Post-fix: health 240 open / performance 30 / ml 20 (was 189 / 0 / 0).

updates.note: Filed and resolved in the same run so the measurement is recoverable and the code comment citing this id resolves. Any future session reading a suspiciously clean backlog_summary should re-run the can-fail control.

items.title: tick_cost's max_ms and every per-hook max reset on each deploy, so the statistic the module says is load-bearing is systematically under-observed - the same defect just fixed for exit_loop_health
items.detail:
SIBLING OF BL-20260816-EXIT-EVAL-INTERVAL-AT-60S-REQUIREMENT, found by auditing the class rather than the instance after the operator pointed out that soaks resetting on deploy means data is not being collected correctly.

VERIFIED IN CODE, not assumed: src/runtime/tick_cost.py holds `_max_ms` and the per-hook `_hooks` accumulators in module globals. Grepping every assignment to them shows the only source is live measurement (`elapsed_ms`); NO function json.loads prior state back into them. runtime_logs/tick_cost.json is a snapshot the next process overwrites, not an accumulator it resumes. Same shape as exit_loop_health before the 2026-08-16 fix.

WHY IT MATTERS AS MUCH HERE. CLAUDE.md's own /api/diag/tick_cost row says 'Read max_ms beside ticks_measured - the max is the statistic that matters (a mean that looks fine while the peak freezes the heartbeat IS the 2026-06-09 incident)'. That statistic is exactly the one the reset destroys. Measured today: five OBSERVED trader processes in ~10h (counted from process_started_utc, not from merge times -- see the sibling row's 10:40Z correction), and tick_cost reads landed at ticks_measured 1, 4, 5, 6, 13, 19, 40 and 50 across the session - the largest sample anyone has ever had is 50 ticks, on a module whose stated purpose is catching a peak.

AND THE BIAS POINTS THE WRONG WAY, which is what makes it worse than a gap: a short window under-reports a max, deploys shorten windows, and deploys are most frequent when the system is changing most. The number is most optimistic precisely when it should be most suspect.

NOT FIXED IN THE SAME PR, deliberately. tick_cost's accumulator is far larger than exit_loop_health's (27 measured hook names x 4 stats, plus a separate offloop table), so 'append one row per tick' is not obviously the right grain the way it was for one interval per pass - a per-tick row carrying 27 hooks is ~100x the volume of the exit soak. It needs its own design decision about grain and retention, and shipping it as a tail-end addition to an unrelated PR is how that decision gets made badly.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. Decide the GRAIN first, and state the volume it implies: per-tick x 27 hooks, vs a per-cadence roll-up carrying each hook's max within the window, vs durable maxima only (smallest, but discards the distribution the exposure-soak lesson says you need).
2. Whatever the grain, summary maxima must be computed over the whole file, not a page - the reader-side version of the same bias (see exit_interval_soak.read_soak_records).
3. Preserve the offloop/on-loop segregation in the record; collapsing them would make an off-thread cost read as tick cost, which tick_cost.py's own docstring warns about.
4. Until then, treat every quoted tick max as a LOWER BOUND over a stated ticks_measured, and do not compare maxima across processes with different sample sizes.

updates.note: CONFIRMED LIVE TWICE THIS REVIEW: I read tick_cost on two different processes and got ticks_measured 31 and 19 — both tiny, because the trader restarted between them. The max I could observe (61.5 s, 59.6 s) is therefore systematically LOW, exactly as this row says. It is the direct reason I qualified the tick-recovery resolution above. The fix is the durable-soak shape already applied to exit_interval_soak.

items.title: trainer-vm-heavy-request is created, GUARD-ENFORCED, and consumed by no workflow - a heavy trainer job dispatched exactly as the skill instructs is silently discarded
items.detail:
session-coordination/SKILL.md 2b instructs that a HEAVY trainer job 'uses that label + claims first', and .claude/hooks/vm_lane_guard.sh ENFORCES it by denying an issue_write carrying trainer-vm-heavy-request unless a fresh /tmp/.claude-vm-lane-claim-<sid> marker exists. But trainer-vm-diag.yml triggers on exactly one label - contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'trainer-vm-diag-request') - and `grep -rl trainer-vm-heavy-request .github/workflows/` returns bootstrap-labels.yml AND NOTHING ELSE. The label is created and never consumed.

MEASURED COST, not hypothetical: issue #9638 (stop the broad M20 fleet sweep, launch the operator-approved narrow arm_r re-sweep) opened cleanly at 10:28Z, returned an issue id, and sat there. No run, no comment, no failure. The trainer spent a further ~50 minutes on legs that appear in NONE of the operator's queued Tier-3 decisions, and the session had already reported the re-prioritisation as done on the coordination board. Re-fired as #9662 with trainer-vm-diag-request and it executed immediately (PID 1597177).

THIS IS THE SILENT-SUCCESS SHAPE, which is worse than an error: the guard PASSING reads as confirmation that the dispatch was well-formed. Every other member of this relay family (vm-diag-snapshot, prop-report, system-actions) comments back on BOTH success and failure - which is why a 404 and a path-charset rejection were each diagnosable in one round the same day.
items.resolution_criteria: Pick ONE and make it whole - half-wired is the worst of the three. (a) Add trainer-vm-heavy-request to trainer-vm-diag.yml's trigger condition (it can share the job; the VM-lane FIFO is a board convention, not a workflow feature), OR (b) delete the label from bootstrap-labels.yml and drop the clause from vm_lane_guard.sh, and correct SKILL.md 2b either way. SEPARATELY, and this is the more general half: a labelled issue that no workflow picks up should not be indistinguishable from one that succeeded - consider a scheduled sweep that comments on any relay-labelled issue with no run attached after N minutes. Verify by dispatching a heavy request and confirming a comment returns.

notes.note: [FIXED 2026-08-16, operator-directed] trainer-vm-diag.yml's job condition now fires on trainer-vm-heavy-request as well as trainer-vm-diag-request (resolution option (a) of this row's own criteria). The VM-lane FIFO is a BOARD convention, not a workflow feature, so the two labels need no behavioural difference — the heavy one exists to trip the vm_lane_guard claim check, and it must still RUN. Verified: yaml parses and the condition contains both labels. STILL OPEN, deliberately, is the GENERAL half this row also names: a labelled issue that no workflow picks up is still indistinguishable from one that succeeded. That needs a sweep that comments on any relay-labelled issue with no run attached after N minutes -- filed separately rather than marked done here.

items.resolution_note: RESOLVED 2026-08-16 by PR #9704, merged to main as 84a511ae. Verified ON MAIN after the merge, not inferred from it: trainer-vm-diag.yml's job condition parses with both 'trainer-vm-diag-request' and 'trainer-vm-heavy-request'; vm-diag-snapshot.yml carries the slashless-prefix strip in BOTH resolvers (the shell workflow_dispatch path AND the Python resolve_one on the issues path, which is the one sessions actually use) plus a doubled-prefix backstop at 2 sites. The backstop was falsified rather than assumed: deleting the strip made it raise "doubled upstream prefix: resolved '/api/diag/api/diag/status' from input 'api/diag/status'", proving the two layers are independent. NOTE the duplicate pair: this gap was filed twice by two different sessions and fixed zero times until an operator directive overruled filing it a third time.

items.title: vm-diag-snapshot strips a leading-slash /api/diag/ prefix but not a slashless api/diag/, silently producing /api/diag/api/diag/<path> and a bare 404 that is indistinguishable from a missing route
items.detail:
resolve_one() in vm-diag-snapshot.yml strips only the leading-slash form:
    if path.startswith('/api/diag/'): path = path[len('/api/diag/'):]
so 'api/diag/status' falls through and is re-prefixed to '/api/diag/api/diag/status' -> HTTP 404. Meanwhile 'api/bot/...' DOES work slashless (a different branch handles it), so the convention is inconsistent between the two families, which is how a caller gets it wrong.

The failure payload reports {error, stage, http_code, curl_exit} and NEVER the resolved URL, so a mangled path looks exactly like a route the server does not have. Measured 2026-08-16: four diag paths returned 404 together and the session's first hypothesis was 'the entire /api/diag/* surface is down'. What refuted it was putting a POSITIVE CONTROL in the same relay run (#9630: api/bot/db/tables returned real data while all four diag paths 404'd) - worth adopting as the default shape for any 'is X down?' probe. Cost two relay round-trips and nearly a false outage report.

Sub-class A of the repo's own unprovenanced-diagnostic-output rule: the output names a cause (404 = no such route) that no code path tested.
items.resolution_criteria: Two one-line changes in .github/workflows/vm-diag-snapshot.yml, both paths (the shell single-path resolver ~line 196 and the python multi-path resolver ~line 398): (1) strip BOTH '/api/diag/' and 'api/diag/' prefixes; (2) echo the RESOLVED url (prefix+path) in the fetch_failed payload so a 404 is attributable without a second round-trip - the resolved path is already printed to the run log, just not into the comment a relay-bound session can read. Verify by requesting 'api/diag/status' and confirming it returns data rather than 404.

notes.note: [FIXED 2026-08-16, operator-directed] Both resolvers patched -- the shell one for workflow_dispatch AND the Python resolve_one for the issues path, which is the one every session actually uses. Fixing only the shell half would have been worse than not fixing it, since it would have been reported closed. Each now strips the SLASHLESS 'api/diag/' spelling, and each carries a doubled-prefix BACKSTOP that checks the CONSTRUCTED url for /api/(diag|bot)/api/ and fails with a named error. Falsified, not assumed: with the strip removed the backstop raises "doubled upstream prefix: resolved '/api/diag/api/diag/status'" instead of returning a bare 404 -- so a malformed request can no longer be reported in the vocabulary of a broken server.

items.resolution_note: RESOLVED 2026-08-16 by PR #9704, merged to main as 84a511ae. Verified ON MAIN after the merge, not inferred from it: trainer-vm-diag.yml's job condition parses with both 'trainer-vm-diag-request' and 'trainer-vm-heavy-request'; vm-diag-snapshot.yml carries the slashless-prefix strip in BOTH resolvers (the shell workflow_dispatch path AND the Python resolve_one on the issues path, which is the one sessions actually use) plus a doubled-prefix backstop at 2 sites. The backstop was falsified rather than assumed: deleting the strip made it raise "doubled upstream prefix: resolved '/api/diag/api/diag/status' from input 'api/diag/status'", proving the two layers are independent. NOTE the duplicate pair: this gap was filed twice by two different sessions and fixed zero times until an operator directive overruled filing it a third time.

items.tier: 2 (order-path / protective-leg lifecycle; detection is Tier-1, remediation is Tier-2)
items.title: ib_paper MES holds TWO full-size stops in DIFFERENT OCA groups against ONE 15-lot position — whichever fires second opens an unintended SHORT, and no IB check can see it
items.detail:
MEASURED, not inferred — /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper at 2026-08-16T10:37:14Z, read_state `orders_read` (a confirmed clean read, so this is not a could-not-look artifact).

THE STATE. Position (/api/diag/exchange_positions, same batch): MES long, size 15, entry 7630.872 — ONE position. Resting orders: TWO STP SELL legs, EACH total_quantity 15, in SEPARATE OCA groups:
  order_id 338, perm_id 872622665, aux_price 7516.50, oca_group `oca-protect-336`, GTC, PreSubmitted
  order_id 375, perm_id 166865400, aux_price 7533.75, oca_group `oca-protect-373`, GTC, PreSubmitted
Stop coverage is therefore 30 contracts against a 15-lot position — 200%.

WHY THIS IS NOT MERELY UNTIDY. OCA cancellation is scoped to a group. The two legs are in different groups, so firing one does NOT cancel the other. Walk it: price falls to 7533.75 -> order 375 fills -> position flat. Order 338 is untouched (different OCA) and still resting at 7516.50. Price continues to 7516.50 -> order 338 fills -> SELL 15 MES against a flat book -> the account is now SHORT 15 MES, a position no strategy opened, with no bracket of its own. That is the naked-inverted-position shape, arrived at from a state that every existing check grades as healthy.

WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT. Both IB consumers of order state REDUCE it before anyone sees it: `IBClient.has_protective_orders` returns a BOOLEAN (true here — legs exist) and `protection_coverage` returns a covered QUANTITY compared against position size for the UNDER-covered case. `order_monitor._check_broker_naked_ib_positions` acts only when coverage is short. OVER-coverage on IB is not graded at all. Bybit already has exactly this detector — `_check_broker_naked_bybit_positions` emits the detect-only `over_covered` signal at >1.5x (BL-20260730-BYBIT1-XRP-LEG-OVERACCUM-WORSENING) — so the concept exists and IB simply never got it. IB is arguably worse than Bybit here: a Bybit over-accumulated leg is a qty-scoped leg on a netted position, whereas an orphaned IB stop OPENS A NEW POSITION.

SCOPE HONESTLY STATED. Observed on ib_paper (accountClass `paper`, isDemo true) — paper money, so no real capital is at risk in THIS instance. It is filed `high` anyway because the mechanism is account-agnostic: the same `place_protective` / re-arm paths serve any IB account, and the only real-money IB account (`ib_live`) is dry/shelved today, which is a configuration fact and not a safeguard. I have NOT established how the second group came to exist (candidates: a re-arm that placed a fresh OCA instead of amending the existing one; a reconciler adopt/re-attach path calling `_rearm_broker_protection_after_recovery` while the prior group was still live). That root-cause is the first task, not a conclusion.

checked: /api/diag/ib_open_orders (relay issue #9642), /api/diag/exchange_positions (same batch), src/units/accounts/ib_client.py, src/runtime/order_monitor.py, CLAUDE.md § naked-position auto-protect.

--- VENUE STATE RE-MEASURED 2026-08-18T07:0xZ: THE DUPLICATE IS GONE ---
/api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper, read_state 'orders_read': MES now holds exactly ONE stop — order 338, STP SELL 15 @ 7516.50, oca-protect-336, GTC PreSubmitted — against a position of MES 15 long @ 7630.872. Order 375 (@ 7533.75, oca-protect-373) is ABSENT. Stop coverage is 15 against 15, i.e. 100%, no longer 200%. This is consistent with the cancel recorded on BL-20260817-CANCEL-IB-ORDER-VERIFY-WINDOW-TOO-SHORT, whose 'cancel_not_effective' verdict was a false negative on a cancel that did complete.

NOT CLOSED, deliberately. This row's criteria require an IB over-coverage DETECTOR mirroring Bybit's `over_covered` signal, plus a regression test pinning that stops in DISJOINT OCA groups are not treated as mutually cancelling. Neither exists. Closing on the cleared instance alone is exactly the 'a detector that never fires because the producing path was also fixed' failure this row warned against — and the producing path was never even identified. The hazard recurs the moment a second group is minted.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) Root-cause WHY two OCA groups exist for one position, stated with the code path named; AND (b) an IB over-coverage detector exists, mirroring the Bybit `over_covered` signal — comparing summed resting protective qty against position size and alerting above a declared multiple — with a test that FAILS on the two-group 15+15-vs-15 shape measured here; AND (c) the current duplicate on ib_paper is resolved (one group cancelled) or explicitly recorded as left in place with a reason. Closing on (b) alone is insufficient: a detector that never fires because the producing path was also fixed is fine, but a fix with no detector leaves the class unwatched.

updates.note:
2026-08-16 ROOT CAUSE ESTABLISHED (operator-directed; sysrev-0816). The row's criterion (a) is answered, and it is TWO defects, not one — the historical pair is explained by a path that has since been fixed, but a SECOND, STILL-LIVE caller reproduces the same shape today.

THE MECHANISM. `IBClient.place_protective` (ib_client.py:1369-1405) builds its OCA group two ways: with a caller-supplied `oca_key` it uses the DETERMINISTIC name `oca-protect-t<key>`, and without one it falls back to `oca-protect-{ib.client.getReqId()}` — a FRESH name every call. The deterministic name is the real protection and not merely tidier: a re-arm reusing the same `ocaGroup` string joins the SAME OCA group, so `ocaType=1` makes IB cancel the siblings when one fires. Two legs in DIFFERENT groups have no mutual cancellation at all. Our live MES legs are `oca-protect-336` and `oca-protect-373` — **no `t`** — so both came from the keyless fallback.

WHY THE PRE-CANCEL DID NOT SAVE IT, which is the part worth keeping. Both cancel helpers — `_cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol` (keyless) and `_cancel_oca_group_for_symbol` (keyed) — iterate `self._open_trades(ib)` = `ib.openTrades()`, which is **PER CLIENT SESSION**. The codebase already knows this and says so, in `_req_all_open_orders`'s own docstring: *'IB order visibility is per client session… a resting protective bracket placed by a PRIOR trader process (before a restart) or by any other client / TWS reads absent from it… would false-read naked and re-arm a duplicate bracket over an already-protected position.'* That reasoning was applied to the CHECK (`has_protective_orders` uses account-wide `reqAllOpenOrders`) and NOT to the CANCEL. So a re-arm running under a different client session sees nothing to cancel, the pre-cancel is a silent no-op, and a second group is armed over the first. **The different-session condition is routine here, not exotic:** the trader restarts on every merge to `main` (five observed processes in ~10h on 2026-08-16) and `IB_RECONNECT_ROTATE_CLIENTID_AFTER` defaults to `1`, so one reconnect failure rotates the id — directly observed on this account today, `ib_state` at 10:35Z showing `client_id: 498, effective_client_id: 698` and 498/498 by 10:55Z.

DEFECT 1 — THE HISTORICAL PAIR, already mitigated on its own path. `oca_key` shipped 2026-08-14 in `f4528fc93` (#9331). MES trade 4350 opened **2026-08-03**, eleven days earlier, so both its brackets predate the fix and were minted by the legacy keyless path. `_attempt_naked_autoprotect` (order_monitor.py:6334-6347) DOES pass `oca_key: str(row['id'])` today, so the naked-autoprotect route would now produce `oca-protect-t4350` and be idempotent. Nothing further is needed for that route.

DEFECT 2 — STILL LIVE, AND THIS IS THE ACTIONABLE HALF. `execute.modify_open_order`'s IB branch (execute.py:2500-2506) calls `exchange_client.modify_protective({symbol, direction, qty, sl, tp})` with **NO `oca_key`**; `IBClient.modify_protective` forwards straight to `place_protective` (ib_client.py:1490). Confirmed by search: `oca_key` appears in exactly ONE place across `src/units/accounts/execute.py` + `src/runtime/*.py` — order_monitor.py:6346 — so the modify path is the sole remaining keyless caller. Consequence: **every IB SL/TP amend mints a fresh OCA group**, and the FIRST amend after any restart or clientId rotation cannot see the pre-restart bracket to cancel it, so it strands it and adds a second group. Same-session amends are fine (the per-client cancel does see its own legs), which is exactly why this hides. Every trailing-stop update, M20 trail lever and `intent_reduce` adjustment on an IB leg goes through this path.

PROPOSED FIX (Tier-2, order path — NOT taken unilaterally): thread `oca_key` through `execute.modify_open_order` → `IBClient.modify_protective` → `place_protective`, the same way `_attempt_naked_autoprotect` already does, so an amend reuses the trade's own deterministic group. That also makes the cross-session gap harmless for this path without touching the cancel helpers, because same-name legs join one OCA group and IB cancels the siblings itself. Separately worth considering — and NOT part of this row — whether the cancel helpers should move to the account-wide read the check already uses; note the concurrent finding that IB scopes CANCELLATION per clientId too, so seeing another session's order is not the same as being able to cancel it.

items.title: MGC trade 4487 has its stop but NO take-profit leg at the broker — confirmed by rows, and every protection check reads the position as fully covered
items.detail:
CONFIRMED BY THE ROWS, which is new — this was previously only inferable. /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper at 2026-08-16T10:37:14Z, read_state `orders_read`.

The broker holds EXACTLY ONE MGC order: order_id 359, perm_id 689621249, STP SELL 105 @ aux_price 4278.80, oca_group `oca-protect-357`, GTC, PreSubmitted. The journal row (trade 4487, ib_paper, MGC long 105) carries stopLoss 4278.8086 and takeProfit 4297.65785714. The stop matches to within rounding; THE TAKE-PROFIT LEG DOES NOT EXIST at the broker. The OCA group contains the stop alone.

WHY IT WENT UNSEEN FOR OVER A WEEK. `has_protective_orders` -> boolean (true: a leg exists). `protection_coverage` -> covered quantity vs position size (105 vs 105: fully covered). `_check_broker_naked_ib_positions` re-arms only when coverage is SHORT. All three grade a stop-only position as healthy, because all three ask 'is there a stop?', never 'does the bracket the trade chose still exist?'. A stripped TP is therefore invisible to every check the system has, which is precisely the reduction-before-visibility problem /api/diag/ib_open_orders was built to break.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS ALREADY REALISED. Price ran through the TP and kept going: the position's mark-implied price is ~4398.60 (from unrealizedPnl 132510.0 at 105 lots x $10/pt over journal entry 4272.4) against a TP of 4297.66 — the take-profit was passed by ~101 points and no exit fired. The trade is still open with a stop at 4278.80.

STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT CHANGES THE REMEDY: re-placing a SELL LMT at the original 4297.66 today would be MARKETABLE (limit below market) and fill at ~4398.60 — i.e. an immediate close at market, NOT 'the TP firing at its price'. Any remediation must be chosen knowing that, and it is an operator call.

POPULATION: ib_paper is a PAPER account (accountClass `paper`), so the figures above are paper money. The detection gap is not paper-scoped — it is the same code path for any IB account. I have NOT established how the TP leg was lost (candidates: cancelled during an IB breaker flap; cancelled by a close attempt's Step-1 bracket cancel that then failed to flatten -- the shape documented in CLAUDE.md under the `IB_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S` env var and tracked by BL-20260624-MHG-CLOSE-CONFIRM-VERIFY (resolved), where an accepted-but-unfilled opposing order leaves a real position open after its bracket was already cancelled. NOTE the id: CLAUDE.md cites that same id WITHOUT the `-VERIFY` suffix, and the un-suffixed form is not a filed row -- artifact-validity-guard correctly refuses it, so cite the suffixed id above; never placed). That is the first task.
