items.title: 5 of the 6 `passed_unshipped` exit_head_ml cells are ict_scalp legs, and ict_scalp has NO exit-head code — the lever cannot run there, and lever-reachability-guard does not cover it
items.detail:
FOUND WHILE PREPARING THE SHIP, not by audit. The operator approved shipping the exit_head_ml lever on the cells the coverage matrix marks `passed_unshipped`. Six qualify. Five of them -- ict_scalp_sol_5m, ict_scalp_xrp_5m, ict_scalp_5m, ict_scalp_sol_15m, ict_scalp_eth_15m -- run on the **ict_scalp** unit, which contains no exit-head implementation at all.

THE DENOMINATOR, because an absence needs one: the identical probe over the two unit files returns 17 matches in src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py and 0 in src/units/strategies/ict_scalp.py. The probe demonstrably finds positives, so the zero is real and not a broken search. Widening to the whole tree, exactly six files mention exit_head and the ONLY strategy unit among them is trend_donchian.py (the others are src/runtime/{exit_head_shadow,order_monitor,entry_head_pwin,execution_costs}.py and src/analysis/paper_record_classifier.py).

SO A DECLARE WOULD BE INERT. The lever is expressed in config as `exit_head_model` / `exit_head_threshold` / `exit_head_action`, and the only reader is trend_donchian.py:555 (`meta.get('exit_head_model') or cfg_dict.get('exit_head_model')`). Adding those three keys to an ict_scalp leg would parse, commit, pass review and change NOTHING at runtime -- the shape of a declared capability with no consumer. Today they carry no such keys (verified: exit_head_model is None on ict_scalp_xrp_5m and ict_scalp_sol_15m; the only three legs carrying it are trend_donchian, trend_donchian_sol and trend_donchian_eth, all donchian 1h).

THE GUARD DOES NOT COVER IT. scripts/ci/check_lever_reachability.py contains ZERO occurrences of `exit_head`; it currently checks reach-gates (trail_decay_arm_r, giveback_min_mfe_r) on capped live legs. That guard shipped in #9614 THIS MORNING under the title 'a guard that stops an unreachable lever landing again' -- so the class is known and actively defended, and this instance sits just outside its coverage. That is the more valuable half of this row: one inert declare is cheap to avoid once seen, a blind spot in the guard that exists to see it is not.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE EVIDENCE, stated carefully: the E1 rounds for those five legs are not wrong, they measured a counterfactual exit policy on each leg's book. What is wrong is reading a `passed_unshipped` cell as 'ready to ship' when the shipping mechanism does not exist for that unit. `passed_unshipped` is defined as 'validated, awaiting implementation/approval' -- for these five the missing word is IMPLEMENTATION, and nothing in the cell says so.

THE SIXTH CELL IS DIFFERENT AND MAY BE GENUINELY SHIPPABLE: trend_donchian_eth_prop is a donchian 1h leg (signal_prefixes ['trend_donchian_eth_prop','donchian_eth_prop'], timeframe 1h, execution live), so the consumer exists and its siblings already carry the keys. ONE THING IS STILL UNVERIFIED and must be settled before it ships: which head artifact its E1 verdict corresponds to. src/runtime/exit_head_shadow.py hardcodes a single MODEL_ID = 'exit-head-donchian-1h-v1' with ARTIFACT_SUBPATH trainer_mirror/exit_head/<MODEL_ID>.json, and trend_donchian.py:541 requires that an `exit_head_model` pin MATCH the artifact's model_id -- while the prop leg's round was run under runtime_logs/m20_exit_head/prop_1h. If that round trained its own head, declaring the donchian-1h id would ship a DIFFERENT model than the one measured. Establish this before any declare.

checked: src/units/strategies/ict_scalp.py, src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py, src/runtime/exit_head_shadow.py, scripts/ci/check_lever_reachability.py, config/strategies.yaml, docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) lever-reachability-guard (or a sibling) FAILS on an exit_head_* declare placed on a unit whose code cannot read it, with a test that fails on an ict_scalp leg carrying the three keys; AND (b) the five ict_scalp exit_head_ml cells carry an explicit note that shipping is blocked on IMPLEMENTATION in the ict_scalp unit, not on approval, so no future session reads them as ready; AND (c) a recorded decision on whether the ict_scalp unit SHOULD gain an exit-head consumer at all -- the measured edge is real and currently unreachable, so 'implement it' is a legitimate answer and this row must not be closed by merely relabelling the cells.

updates.note:
2026-08-16, SAME DAY, CONVERGENT CONFIRMATION FROM AN INDEPENDENT IMPLEMENTATION. A concurrent session shipped scripts/ops/exit_mechanism_coverage.py (#9633, 'Does a leg's own module implement the exit lever it declares?') while this row was being written. It covers exit_head explicitly (LEVERS maps 'exit_head' -> ('exit_head','exit_head_threshold')) and carries the five states this row's finding needs, including not_implemented ('module has no such lever') and orphaned ('declared, module cannot read it -- the defect'). Running it reproduces the finding independently: EVERY ict_scalp leg reads not_implemented for exit_head, and fleet-wide exit_head is {not_implemented: 26, undeclared: 17, LIVE: 1, DECL: 2, unresolved: 1}. Two sessions found the same gap from opposite directions on the same day -- I from a specific blocked ship, they from auditing the class.

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT REASON ict_scalp_5m CANNOT SHIP: their tool reports it UNRESOLVED (unit 'no_builder_found') -- the only unresolved leg of 47. So that cell is blocked both by the missing ict_scalp exit-head implementation AND by its own unit not resolving, on top of already being unmeasurable at live parity (data_missing:BTCUSDT). Three separate blockers on one 'ready to ship' cell.

WHAT THIS CHANGES IN THIS ROW'S ASK. Criterion (a) is now MOSTLY satisfied by their script, so do not re-implement it. What remains is narrower and should not be lost in the hand-off: their script lives in scripts/ops/ and REPORTS -- its own commit says 'Reports; decides nothing'. So an orphaned or not_implemented declare is visible to a manual run but is NOT blocked in CI. The remaining ask is the ENFORCEMENT half: wire this (or an equivalent assertion) into the guards job so an exit_head declare on a unit that cannot read it FAILS a PR rather than merely appearing in a report nobody runs. Criteria (b) and (c) are untouched by #9633 and still stand. checked: scripts/ops/exit_mechanism_coverage.py (line 57 LEVERS table, lines 64-68 state constants), its run output over 47 live legs, commit 41f9f0467.

2026-08-16: THE SIXTH CELL IS ALSO BLOCKED, so the gate is now zero-for-six. This row's detail left trend_donchian_eth_prop as 'may be genuinely shippable' pending which artifact its verdict corresponds to. Settled via trainer relay #9670: NONE. The prop_1h round tree contains zero 'model_id' occurrences and its _round_meta carries target:null / features:null; the only loadable exit-head artifacts are exit-head-donchian-1h-v1.json and exit-head-donchian-peak-1h-v1.json, both dated Jul 12 — a month BEFORE the Aug 14 round. Since trend_donchian.py:541 requires the config pin to match the loaded artifact's model_id, declaring the donchian-1h id would ship the July artifact under an August verdict it did not produce. Unblocking needs either publishing the head that round trained, or re-measuring the leg against the existing artifact — work, not a config edit.

ACTED ON (operator decision 2026-08-23). The five ict_scalp exit_head_ml cells are re-graded passed_unshipped -> `blocked:no_lever_consumer_in_unit` in docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json, and the QUEUED Tier-3 ship of ict_scalp_sol_5m is CANCELLED. The E1 verdicts are NOT withdrawn — they stay in each ref — what is withdrawn is the reading that these cells are ready to ship. Re-verified the absence with a positive control before acting: `grep -c exit_head` returns 0 in ict_scalp.py against 17 in trend_donchian.py, and the only three legs declaring exit_head_model are trend_donchian / _sol / _eth. sol_5m carries a second reason: its pass flips to honest_negative when folds are cut 12 trades later, with the SMALLEST AUC spread of the three legs (0.0034), so the AUC gave no warning.

Re-validated: 5 of 6 passed_unshipped cells are legs where the lever CANNOT run, and lever-reachability-guard does not cover it. A pass on a leg with no consumer is the written-and-never-read class again.

CLAUSES (a) AND (b) ARE NOW OBSERVED; (c) IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT REMAINS AND IS NOT A SESSION'S TO CLOSE. Taking them in order.

(a) DONE, and the fix is larger than the clause asked for. The clause reads 'lever-reachability-guard (or a sibling) FAILS on an exit_head_* declare placed on a unit whose code cannot read it'. Measured 2026-09-02 by PLANTING declares on ict_scalp_sol_5m (a leg whose unit has zero exit-head code: `grep -c exit_head src/units/strategies/ict_scalp.py` -> 0, against 17 in trend_donchian.py as the positive control) and running `scripts/ops/exit_mechanism_coverage.py --orphans-only`:
    exit_head_threshold + exit_head_action  -> orphan reported, exit 1
    exit_head_model     + exit_head_action  -> SILENT,          exit 0
So a sibling guard (exit-mechanism-coverage-guard, NOT lever-reachability-guard, which the row is right that it does not cover this) already caught one shape and was blind to the other -- and the blind one is the shape that ships. `trend_donchian._exit_head_verdict` (src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py:554) returns None unless `exit_head_action == 'close'` and falls back to the artifact's own tau when no `exit_head_threshold` is given, so **exit_head_action is the key that ARMS the head and exit_head_threshold is an OPTIONAL MODIFIER** -- the detector was keyed on the modifier and blind to the arm. The tuple's other entry, `"exit_head"`, is a key no leg declares and no module reads.

NOT CONFINED TO exit_head, which is why the remedy is a derivation and not four hand-added strings. A scan of every `meta|cfg|cfg_dict.get("<prefix>...")` read across src/units/strategies/*.py + src/runtime/*.py found the same incompleteness in 3 of 4 mechanisms: `stale_exit_below_r` (read by exit_levers.py and ict_scalp.py) and `trail_decay_stall_bars` (read by runtime/trail_decay.py) were missing too; only giveback_stop was complete. AND THE TABLE WAS DUPLICATED -- `scripts/ops/exit_path_coverage.py::_KEYED_MECHANISMS` carried its own copy with the identical staleness.

FIX (this session): `DECLARE_KEYS` (the full config surface, used for `declared`) is now separate from `MECHANISMS` (the narrow probe for whether a module IMPLEMENTS the lever, unchanged), `declared_surface_gaps()` derives the surface from the implementations, and the guard's `--self-test` FAILS on any read-but-undeclared key -- so it cannot silently regrow the next time a lever gains a knob. exit_path_coverage now imports both tables instead of restating them. Carries a positive control (removing exit_head_action from the table IS detected as a gap), because an empty gap list from a probe that cannot fail is the answer this whole file exists to stop anyone acting on. Verified: live config still reports ZERO orphans (no false positive), and the previously-silent plant now exits 1. Tests: tests/test_exit_mechanism_coverage.py::TestTheDeclaredSurfaceIsComplete.

(b) ALREADY SATISFIED BEFORE THIS SESSION -- observed in the artifact, not inferred. Measured over docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json (52 rows): exactly FIVE cells carry status `blocked:no_lever_consumer_in_unit`, and they are exactly the five ict_scalp legs the row names (ict_scalp_5m, ict_scalp_sol_5m, ict_scalp_xrp_5m, ict_scalp_sol_15m, ict_scalp_eth_15m). The sol cell's ref carries the words the clause asks for verbatim: 'SHIPPING IS BLOCKED ON IMPLEMENTATION, NOT APPROVAL'. Note the counts have MOVED since filing -- the row says '5 of the 6 passed_unshipped exit_head_ml cells are ict_scalp legs'; today there is exactly ONE passed_unshipped exit_head_ml cell in the whole matrix and it is trend_donchian_eth_prop, because the five were re-graded to `blocked` by operator decision 2026-08-23. Do not re-derive the old 5-of-6 figure from this row's title.

(c) REMAINS, AND IT IS AN OPERATOR DECISION: should the ict_scalp unit gain an exit-head consumer at all? The row is explicit that 'implement it' is a legitimate answer and that closing by relabelling is not allowed. Nothing a session can measure settles it -- the measured edge on those five legs is recorded and currently unreachable, and building the consumer is Tier-3 work on the live monitor path. ROUTE IT TO THE OPERATOR rather than re-validating it in another review; two review passes have now re-validated this row without moving it, which is the cost the clause imposes. STATUS STAYS OPEN on (c) alone.

THE CONSUMER NOW EXISTS — and this row STAYS OPEN, because its own criteria say so. MI-150 shipped src/units/strategies/ict_scalp.py::_exit_head_verdict, calling the SAME exit_head_shadow.maybe_score_exit_head and the SAME shared decision (src/runtime/exit_head_apply.exit_head_verdict) that trend_donchian now delegates to. `grep -c exit_head src/units/strategies/ict_scalp.py` goes 0 -> non-zero; the lever can run there.

AGAINST THE THREE CRITERIA, SEPARATELY, because collapsing them is what this row warns about:
  (a) NOT SATISFIED. There is still no guard that FAILS an exit_head_* declare placed on a unit whose code cannot read it. ict_scalp is no longer such a unit, but htf_pullback_trend_2h, squeeze_breakout_4h and fvg_range_15m still are, and 17 exit_head_ml cells still carry blocked:no_lever_consumer_in_unit for exactly that reason. Fixing one unit does not build the detector. ⚠️ Note also that MI-150 EXTRACTED the lever to a shared module, which is precisely the shape BL-20260818-CAPABILITY-AUDITS-GREP-ONE-FILE-AND-MISS-SHARED-LEVERS says a one-file grep misreads as losing a capability — so any such guard must resolve through the leg's unit AND the modules it imports, not by grepping the unit file.
  (b) SATISFIED. All five cells (plus the two downgraded siblings) are re-statused off blocked:no_lever_consumer_in_unit and their refs now record the real remaining blocker.
  (c) SATISFIED. The operator decided: 'Yes on MI 146' (2026-09-06), approving MI-146 recommendation #2 — build the consumer. It is built.

⚠️ AND THE BLOCKER MOVED RATHER THAN CLEARING: measured 2026-09-06, the live mirror publishes only 1h exit_head artifacts while every ict_scalp leg is 5m/15m, so the in-distribution tf guard refuses all 8 and the new consumer records decision_state: not_scored. Tracked as OI-20260906-ICT-SCALP-EXIT-HEAD-CONSUMER-SHIPPED-AND-CANNOT-SCORE-UNTIL-A-SCALP-HEAD-IS-PUBLISHED. Closing this row on 'the consumer exists' would assert a reachability nobody has observed.

items.opened_by: claude (exit-eval-interval session, operator-directed after the ib_paper/MGC flatten failed)
items.title: IBClient.close ABANDONS the market order it just placed when the flatten is not confirmed flat -- so a failed close leaves MORE resting sell orders than it started with, and every retry adds one
items.detail:
OPERATOR-DIRECTED. Found by reading /api/diag/ib_open_orders 48s after system-action #9648 (flatten-ib-position, ib_paper/MGC) returned exit 1.

WHAT close() DOES. `_locked_close`'s not-confirmed-flat branch returns retCode 1 -- correct, it must not claim a close it cannot confirm -- and then WALKS AWAY FROM ITS OWN LIVE ORDER. tif is DAY, nothing cancels it, and the order id exists only inside the retMsg string, so no caller can act on it.

THE METHOD ARGUES AGAINST ITSELF. Its Step-1 docstring says to cancel resting protective orders first because 'a later fill of one leg would re-open a position in the opposite direction', and that cancelling first is what makes the close 'idempotent and naked-order-free'. That argument applies exactly to its own abandoned order and was never applied to it -- on the failure path, the only path where it matters.

MEASURED STATE (2026-08-16T10:57:23Z, relay #9650, 48s after the failed flatten). ib_paper/MGC, one 105-contract long, held TWO resting sells:
  order 359  STP SELL 105 @ 4278.80  oca_group 'oca-protect-357'  GTC
  order   6  MKT SELL 105            oca_group null               DAY
210 contracts of sell against a 105 long, in two orders with NO linkage, so neither can cancel the other. If the market order fills, the position goes flat and the GTC stop remains resting on a flat book.

CONSEQUENCES, in order: (1) the abandoned order can still fill later, flattening a position nobody expects flat; (2) retries CAN stack -- IB_CLOSE_RETRY_COOLDOWN_S (300s) bounds the RATE, never the total. STATED PRECISELY, because the obvious phrasing overstates it: stacking is a property of the MONITOR's close path (order_monitor._apply_update), which is what retries. THIS incident was a one-shot ops action against a strategy whose monitor has no close path at all (ict_scalp.monitor()'s only verdict is the break-even ratchet), so exactly ONE order was abandoned and NO stacking occurred -- a re-read at T+23min (relay #9664) showed the same four orders, unchanged. The hazard is real for a strategy whose monitor DOES close against a non-filling venue; it is not what was measured here, and this row must not be cited as if it were; (3) one filling while another rests flips the account to a short.

NOT ASSERTED: whether IB would in fact fill the survivor into a reverse position. Two independent GTC/DAY sells against one long is VERIFIED from broker truth; the fill path is not, and is not claimed here.

SIBLING (same PR, see resolution): `_cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol` reads `ib.openTrades()`, which is per-clientId. `scripts/ops/flatten_ib_position.py` builds a PID-salted ops client (`9900 + os.getpid() % 90`), so the flatten could not SEE the trader's legs (clientId 496/497) and Step 1 cancelled ZERO -- reporting exactly like success. That is why the stop survived, which is the only reason the position was never naked. Two defects partially cancelling out is not a safety property. The repo already records the same clientId scoping for reqExecutions ('a separate pull process sees zero of the trader's fills, unless it is the gateway master client').

NOTE ON A DANGLING ID, found by artifact-validity-guard while filing this row: the filed row is BL-20260624-MHG-CLOSE-CONFIRM-VERIFY, but ~8 sites cite it WITHOUT the -VERIFY suffix -- CLAUDE.md's IB_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S and IB_CLOSE_RETRY_COOLDOWN_S rows, order_monitor.py (x3), ib_client.py, reconcile_orphan_history.py, and two test modules. That truncated form resolves to nothing, so those comments read as tracked while being tracked by nobody. Pre-existing and grandfathered by the diff-scoped guard, so it is recorded here rather than swept; correct the suffix next time any of those files is edited for another reason.

(Stated without quoting the truncated id verbatim, because the guard matches the token itself and cannot tell 'citing this id as a tracking reference' from 'reporting that this id is broken' -- so writing it out would trip the guard on a row whose whole point is that it dangles. Worth knowing before anyone tries to document a dangling id again.) | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'fix_landed_pending_live_verification' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. SHIPPED: close() cancels its own order on the not-confirmed path and declares the outcome three ways -- cancelled / already_filled (a fill raced the cancel; nothing rests and the position may now be FLAT) / cancel_failed (an order STILL RESTS). Never collapsed to a boolean.
2. SHIPPED: the symbol-wide cancel returns {seen, cancelled, failed, account_wide_seen} and WARNs when the account holds more legs than this session can see. account_wide_seen is None when that read failed -- not zero.
3. NOT DONE, deliberately: the symbol-wide READ is not widened to reqAllOpenOrders. Cancelling is symbol-wide and one IB symbol's legs span several trades, so widening the read before the cancel is TRADE-scoped would let one partial close strip every sibling's protection -- a bigger blast radius than this bug. That is criterion 2/4 of BL-20260814-IB-PROTECTION-BOOLEAN-NOT-QUANTITY.
4. OPEN: no wire exists to cancel ONE IB order. The allowlist has cancel-stale-tpsl-legs (Bybit only). Needed for the existing stranded order 6, and blocked on an unverified question -- IB documents cancellation as own-client-only unless the client holds the gateway MASTER client id, and the placing ops session has exited with a PID-derived id. reqGlobalCancel would work but cancels everything including the stop.
5. LIVE VERIFICATION: after deploy, a failed close must leave ZERO abandoned orders on /api/diag/ib_open_orders. Until that read exists this is untested against a real gateway.

updates.note:
OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-16, in-conversation: 'let it expire'. Option 3 of the three put to them. The stranded MGC order 6 (MKT SELL 105, tif DAY, placed by system-action #9648's ops client and abandoned when the flatten failed its confirm window) is left to expire at the COMEX session close (~21:00 UTC). NOTHING IS BEING DISPATCHED — this is a decision to take no action, recorded so it is not re-litigated by the next session that reads the order list and treats it as an unhandled anomaly.

WHY IT COULD NOT BE CANCELLED (the reason the other two options existed): IB scopes order cancellation per clientId; flatten_ib_position.py builds its ops client as `9900 + os.getpid() % 90`, a PID-derived id whose session has exited. No `cancel-ib-order` system-action exists (the allowlist has cancel-stale-tpsl-legs, Bybit-only), and reqGlobalCancel would also cancel the stop the operator wanted kept plus both MES stops. The two options not taken were: (1) a gateway Master API client id + a narrow cancel-ib-order action; (2) reqGlobalCancel followed by an immediate re-arm.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DECISION DOES NOT RESOLVE, stated so it is not mistaken for closure. Expiry removes the DOUBLED-SELL hazard (210 contracts of resting sell against a 105 long in two unlinked orders). It returns MGC 4487 to its PRE-FLATTEN state: 105 long, one stop at 4278.80, and NO take-profit at the broker. ict_scalp.monitor() has no close path, so the position still has no profit exit of any kind — it can only stop out or run. That is BL-20260816-IB-PROTECTION-CHECKS-GRADE-STOPS-ONLY-A-STRIPPED-TP-IS-INVISIBLE (sysrev-0816's row, landed in main via PR #9643 at 2026-08-16 ~12:10Z). It remains OPEN and is unaddressed by this decision. Note for the record: when this update was first written the row was still unmerged, so the id resolved to nothing and artifact-validity-guard correctly rejected it; it was cited by PR number until #9643 landed, then restored to the id. Citing another session's in-flight row by PR until it merges is the general rule.

RESIDUAL RISK DURING THE WINDOW (~9h, paper account, no capital at risk): if order 6 transmits and fills before expiry, the position goes flat and stop 359 remains resting on a flat book. Whether IB would then fill it into a short is NOT verified and is not asserted. Criterion 4 (no wire to cancel one IB order) stays OPEN — this decision routes around it once; it does not close it, and the next stranded order will hit the same wall.

OPERATOR REVERSED THE 11:50Z DECISION, in-conversation 2026-08-16: 'cancel order 6'. The earlier 'let it expire' disposition is superseded. Recording it here rather than editing that update, so the sequence stays legible.

IT COULD NOT BE CARRIED OUT, and the reason is the one the 11:50Z update already named as criterion 4 -- there is no wire to cancel one IB order. Re-verified in code this session rather than taken from the prior note: `IBClient.cancel(order_id)` (src/units/accounts/ib_client.py::_locked_cancel) resolves the target by iterating `self._open_trades(ib)` = `ib.openTrades()`, which is SESSION-SCOPED to the calling clientId. Order 6 was placed by flatten_ib_position.py's PID-salted ops client (`9900 + os.getpid() % 90`), whose process has exited, so any new ops client returns 'order 6 not found among open trades'. The same scoping is documented in this file's own `_cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol` docstring, which records the MEASURED 2026-08-16 case: a flatten ran, its Step-1 cancel reported nothing wrong, and the trader's stop was still resting afterwards -- zero legs cancelled.

THE TWO CANDIDATE PATHS, BOTH REFUSED ON EVIDENCE, NOT PREFERENCE. (a) `flatten-ib-position --apply` would run on an ops clientId that cannot see order 6, AND would place a THIRD market sell for 105 -- it is a flatten, not a cancel. (b) `reqGlobalCancel` would cancel order 6 but also the MGC stop and both MES protective legs, leaving 105 MGC + 15 MES naked until naked-autoprotect re-arms.

AND THE BROKER WAS UNREACHABLE AT THE TIME OF ASKING. `/api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper` at 2026-08-16T12:37:33Z (relay #9695) returned `read_state: "could_not_look"`, `orders: null`, `count: null` -- the IB circuit breaker was open ('retrying in 73s' on the MES 1d fetch in the same window). So at that moment nothing could read or write IB order state at all. Noting explicitly that `count: null` is the three-state contract working, NOT an empty order book.

STATE LEFT: order 6 still resting, tif DAY, expiring at the COMEX session close (~21:00Z). Order 378 (the post-restart attempt) was in PendingCancel at 12:33:32Z, which is #9663 working. NOTHING WAS DISPATCHED. Criterion 4 is now BLOCKING an operator instruction rather than merely open, which is the argument for building the narrow order-id-scoped `cancel-ib-order` action: unlike the symbol-wide cancel this row's sibling docstring declines to widen, an order-id-scoped cancel has no sibling-stripping blast radius. Whether a non-placing client can cancel another clientId's order at all (the IB Master API client id question) is the crux and is NOT yet verified -- it must be, before that action is built.

CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN VERIFICATION CLAIM. The fix was recorded as live-verified because the apply run emitted `(own close order: cancelled)`. A confirmed broker read at 14:13:09Z (relay #9718) shows order 378 **still resting in PendingCancel, remaining 105**, ~1h43m after the cancel was requested. The LOG LINE was verified; the OUTCOME it asserts was not, and is now refuted. Filed as BL-20260816-IB-CANCEL-REPORTS-CANCELLED-ON-ACCEPTANCE.

The original finding stands -- the close DID abandon its own order, and cancelling it is the right move. What is wrong is the reporting: acceptance of a cancel request was read as completion, which is the same 'accepted != done' class this whole line of work is about.
Re-validated: a failed close leaving MORE resting sell orders than it started with is an order-path defect on a live venue. Related to the over-cover family. Tier-2.

items.title: /api/diag/tick_cost counters are per-PROCESS with no durable sibling, so on a day with frequent merges every read is small-n and the tick regression cannot be measured at a useful sample size
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-16. Asked to re-read tick_cost 'at larger n' and could not, for a structural reason rather than a transient one: the counters reset on every trader restart, the trader redeploys on every merge to main, and this session merged five PRs. FIVE processes were observed in ~80 minutes (11:11:15, 11:49:06, 12:05:46, 12:10:21, 12:27:03). Every tick_cost read available today is ticks_measured: 5 or fewer.

Two reads I took, both n=5, different processes: mean 121.4s / max 203.5s (proc 11:49:06) and mean 129.8s / max 199.3s (proc 12:10:21). The mean moved +8.5s while the max moved -4.2s -- OPPOSITE directions -- so no direction is supportable, and the largest-n reading on record (138.8s at n=20) is also the HIGHEST. A reader taking any single small-n read as the current state gets a number that is systematically unrepresentative, and which way it is biased is not predictable.

THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT exit_interval_soak WAS BUILT TO FIX, one surface over. That fix is recorded in CLAUDE.md: 'every field in exit_loop_health lives in a module global that starts empty and is never reloaded, so max_interval_ms is scoped to ONE process ... a max over a short window is systematically LOW, so the in-memory grade reads most reassuring exactly when the system is busiest.' tick_cost has no such durable half. The remedy already exists in-repo as a worked pattern -- append one row per tick to a JSONL, compute the summary over the file rather than the returned page, and stamp process_started_utc so a restart gap is never read as a real interval.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: the tick regression (83.9s -> ~120-140s) is an OPEN investigation whose cause is not established, and the instrument used to investigate it is blinded by exactly the activity that investigating it requires. Note the asymmetry with the exit loop: a busy day biases the exit-interval max LOW (reassuring), and biases tick_cost in no predictable direction (misleading either way).

checked: src/runtime/tick_cost.py (no JSONL/append path -- it writes ONE fixed-size state object, as CLAUDE.md documents); checked: src/web/api/routers/diag.py (the log_file allowlist carries exit_interval_soak at L373 but no tick_cost sibling, and /tick_cost L1704 reads tick_cost.read_state, the single object); checked: docs/research/RESEARCH-CAPABILITY-INDEX.md (names /api/diag/tick_cost as the tool, i.e. the same single-state surface). So the gap is the ABSENCE of a durable writer, verified against the three places one would be registered -- not an inference from a quiet grep.
evidence: relay #9673 -> tick_cost proc 11:49:06Z, ticks_measured 5, mean_ms 121384.7, max_ms 203529.2
relay #9684 -> tick_cost proc 12:10:21Z, ticks_measured 5, mean_ms 129848.8, max_ms 199288.7
same payloads: attributed_pct 98.8 / 99.0, so the cost is not hiding in an uninstrumented hook
CLAUDE.md ss EXIT_LOOP_* + /api/diag/log_file exit_interval_soak -- the precedent fix for the identical per-process bias
items.proposed_remedy: Add a durable tick_cost sibling on the exit_interval_soak pattern (one row per tick, summary over the file, process_started_utc stamped). Tier-1. Until then, any tick_cost figure MUST be quoted with its ticks_measured, and a single small-n read must not be reported as a trend -- which is what this session did.
items.resolution_criteria: /api/diag/log_file?name=tick_cost_soak (or an equivalent durable surface) returns rows spanning at least TWO distinct process_started_utc values, and its summary max/mean are computed over the whole file rather than the returned page -- verified by a live read taken AFTER a trader restart, with the summary's tick count exceeding the in-memory ticks_measured of the then-current process. Until that read exists the row stays open; a merged writer is not sufficient, for the same reason #9614 shipped an account_id column that no code path could populate and passed its tests.

updates.note: CONFIRMED LIVE TWICE TODAY and it directly limited this review: my two tick_cost reads returned ticks_measured 31 and 19 because the trader restarted between them, so the MAX I could observe is systematically low. I qualified two resolutions on exactly this basis. Duplicate condition of BL-20260816-TICK-COST-MAX-RESETS-EVERY-DEPLOY; consolidate. The fix pattern already exists — exit_interval_soak's durable per-pass append.

items.title: m20_fleet_exit_sweep's --tp-cap-pct and --split-target-oos defaults are both Tier-3 proposals recorded ONLY in a dated operator memo, which no review cadence drains
items.detail:
Two defaults in scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py were queued for operator decision on 2026-08-16 and written up in docs/claude/m20-m31-operator-decisions-2026-08-16.md section 4. That memo is DATED and belongs to one session; the three review skills drain BACKLOGS, not memos. So without this row the two decisions survive only as long as someone remembers the memo exists.

(a) --tp-cap-pct: the harness default is not live parity. A sweep run without --tp-cap-pct 0.099 measures a book production does not run. Every measurement in the 2026-08-16 memo passes it explicitly.

(b) --split-target-oos: DEFAULTS TO MIN_OOS_TRADES (25) -- the target IS the floor, so any boundary loss puts the OOS window under it and the cell refuses with insufficient_base. Already filed as BL-20260814-SPLIT-TARGETS-EXACTLY-THE-FLOOR-SO-BOUNDARY-LOSS-ALWAYS-FAILS; THIS row is not a duplicate of it -- that row is the DEFECT, this row is the un-drained TIER-3 DECISION about the default value.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE 2026-08-16: at the default, the pullback-family re-sweep refused EVERY cell on EVERY leg. At --split-target-oos 50 the same run returned 2 PASS + 3 path_b_wf_pass + 67 is_oos_fail + 4 insufficient_base over 76 cells. What caught it was not a check but htf_pullback_trend_2h reporting insufficient at 407 lifetime trades -- implausible on its face. A leg with a genuinely thin history would have produced the same output and been believed, and a table of insufficient_base reads as 'no lever helps this family'.

WHY IT IS TIER-3 AND NOT A FIX I SHOULD HAVE MADE: changing either default changes what every future sweep measures AND what already-recorded numbers mean. My recommendation, labelled as one: raise --split-target-oos above the floor. I did not, because past sweep results were produced under it and re-interpreting them is the operator's call.
evidence: scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py: MIN_OOS_TRADES = 25 (L548); --split-target-oos default=MIN_OOS_TRADES (L1543)
insufficient_base_reason docstring: htf_pullback_trend_2h refused at n=24 derived vs graded at n=95 corpus-standard, same config same day
trainer relays #9681 (default -> all cells refuse) and #9683 (target 50 -> real verdicts)
docs/claude/m20-m31-operator-decisions-2026-08-16.md section 4 (4a and 4b)

items.title: exit_interval_soak's summary -- the cross-process max the module exists to produce -- was computed on every read and reachable by NOBODY; #9627 shipped the writer with no HTTP route
items.detail:
SELF-INFLICTED, found while live-verifying #9627 and recorded because the shape is the one this repo has a guard family for.

WHAT SHIPPED: #9627 added src/runtime/exit_interval_soak.py (writer + read_soak_records with a `summary` computed over the WHOLE file) and registered the log on /api/diag/log_file?name=exit_interval_soak. That surface returns a raw TAIL of lines. It cannot return `summary`. Every sibling soak has a router -- exposure.py, pairs.py, allocator.py, exit_ladder.py, fc_geometry.py -- and this one had none. So `summary.max_interval_ms`, the cross-process maximum that is the entire reason the module exists, was computed on every call and consumed by nothing outside tests.

THE REPO ALREADY SAYS NOT TO DO THIS, in the docstring of the router I copied the shape from: exposure.py says 'This route is shipped in the same PR as the writer, deliberately... a signal written and never read is worse than a missing one, because reviewers see the field and assume something acts on it. A soak log with no read surface repeats that exactly.' I read that file while writing the fix and shipped the defect anyway.

HOW IT SURFACED, which is the part worth keeping: #9627's OWN stated verification criterion was 'summary.max_interval_ms spanning more than one process_started_utc' -- a read that could not be performed. Verifying it meant paging the entire 37KB file out through the diag tail and re-implementing the aggregation client-side, which is precisely the reader-side windowing bias read_soak_records computes over the whole file to avoid. A PR whose acceptance test is unrunnable should have been caught at review, not at verification.

THE VERIFICATION STILL SUCCEEDED, by hand (relay #9686, whole file): 5 processes, 140 rows, 135 intervals, cross-process max 50044.3ms = 83.4% of the 60s requirement, ZERO breaches. The max came from the process that ended at 11:49:41Z, so every read after that restart lost it -- the newest process alone (n=3) shows 40648.6ms = 67.7%. The per-process reset would UNDERSTATE the max by 15.7 percentage points at this moment. That is the bias #9627 was built to remove, now demonstrated on live data rather than argued from first principles. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'fix_landed_pending_ci' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. SHIPPED: src/web/api/routers/exit_interval.py -> GET /api/bot/exit-interval/soak, a thin wrapper over read_soak_records mirroring the five sibling routers, mounted in main.py.
2. SHIPPED: a mount test that FAILS when the router is written but not wired in (falsified by deleting the include_router line). Deliberately NOT written against the FastAPI app object -- that import needs email-validator, absent here, so such a test would SKIP rather than fail, and a skipped mount test is how a missing route stays invisible.
3. OPEN, and the reason this row is worth more than the fix: NO sibling soak route has a mount test either. The class question is whether a guard should assert 'every src/runtime/*_soak.py with a read_soak_records has a router that is mounted' -- the same shape as provenance-consumer-guard, which exists because a written-and-never-read signal is worse than a missing one. Five existing routes are correct today by inspection, not by enforcement.
4. LIVE VERIFY after deploy: GET /api/bot/exit-interval/soak returns summary.processes_seen > 1 without paging the whole file by hand.
refs: src/web/api/routers/exposure.py (the docstring that states the rule)
issue #9686 (the by-hand verification this made necessary)
items.resolution:
RESOLVED — `/api/bot/exit-interval/soak` exists (`src/web/api/routers/exit_interval.py`, thin wrapper over `src.runtime.exit_interval_soak.read_soak_records`) and serves the CROSS-PROCESS summary computed over the whole file, which is exactly what the 1000-line `/api/diag/log_file?name=exit_interval_soak` page cannot give. Verified live 2026-08-25T11:1xZ: `{rows: 22836, intervals_measured: 22670, processes_seen: 166, breaches: 1204, max_interval_ms: 96125.2, mean_interval_ms: 33888.6, max_interval_at_utc: 2026-08-20T23:14:26Z, last_breach_utc: 2026-08-22T15:01:14Z}`.
