items.opened_by: claude (exit-eval-interval session, operator asked why the MGC close will not fill)
items.title: WHY the IB close does not fill: it fires a MarketOrder into COMEX with outsideRth unset and NOTHING in the system knows whether the venue is in session -- the exact gap Alpaca's close path already closes
items.detail:
OPERATOR-ASKED. Three code facts, each grepped rather than inferred:

1. `outsideRth` IS NEVER SET ANYWHERE. `grep -rn 'outsideRth|outside_rth' src/ scripts/` returns NOTHING, so `MarketOrder` in `_locked_close` carries ib_insync's default `outsideRth=False`. IBKR HOLDS such an order rather than routing it when the contract is outside its regular session — status `PreSubmitted`, `filled 0`, which is precisely the observed state.

2. NO IB PATH CHECKS MARKET HOURS. `grep` for is_market_open / us_equity_session / market_hours / liquidHours / tradingHours across `ib_client.py` + `ib_connector.py` returns NOTHING.

3. `src/runtime/market_hours.py` MODELS ONLY `fx`, `us_equity` and `crypto` — its own docstring lists exactly those three. THERE IS NO FUTURES CALENDAR IN THE REPO AT ALL, so no code path could answer 'is COMEX open?' even if one asked.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING. `alpaca_client.py:603-617` calls `us_equity_session()` and routes a close to `_close_extended_hours` (marketable LIMIT + extended_hours) or DEFERS with retCode 2 during closed hours — with a documented rationale (BL-20260716-ALPACA-MARKET-HOURS-EXIT: 'the monitor stops firing doomed market flattens into a closed market every tick'). That is the SAME defect, already diagnosed and fixed on one venue, never ported to IB.

OBSERVED (ib_paper/MGC, 105 long): order 6 placed 2026-08-16T10:56Z = 06:56 ET sat `PreSubmitted` / `filled 0` for 90+ minutes. Order 378 placed ~12:30Z = 08:30 ET did not confirm flat within the 6s window either.

`filled 0` ARGUES FOR 'HELD' AND AGAINST 'THIN BOOK'. A 105-lot MGC market order against insufficient depth would PARTIAL-fill; zero fill across 90 minutes is the signature of an order IB never routed. Stated as the stronger reading, not as proof.

WHAT I HAVE NOT ESTABLISHED, and it matters: the exact COMEX RTH window. I believe GC/MGC regular hours are 08:20-13:30 ET, which would put order 6 ~84 min early — but that is general knowledge, NOT anything in this repo, and it does not fit cleanly: order 6 was still `PreSubmitted` at 12:26Z = 08:26 ET, AFTER that window opens. So either the window differs for this contract, or a second factor is also holding it. The mechanism (no session awareness + outsideRth unset) is established; the precise trigger time is not.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX JUST SHIPPED (#9663): when the order is being HELD, cancelling it at the 6s confirm deadline is exactly right — it was never going to fill. But if a venue is OPEN and merely slow, that same cancel could kill an order about to fill. `_cancel_own_close_order`'s `already_filled` state covers the clean race; a PARTIAL fill at cancel time is not handled and is worth a look.

=== VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-17T17:01Z — verbatim ===
GET /api/diag/venue_session?account_id=ib_paper&symbol=MGC ->
  state=open · tz_source=zoneinfo · time_zone_id=US/Eastern · tz_resolved_name=US/Eastern · graded_field=tradingHours · sec_type=FUT · close_would_send_outside_rth=true · read_state=session_read · reason='tradingHours: inside 20260816 18:00-20260817 17:00 US/Eastern'
GET /api/diag/venue_session?account_id=ib_paper&symbol=MES ->
  state=open · tz_source=zoneinfo · time_zone_id=US/Central · tz_resolved_name=US/Central · graded_field=tradingHours · sec_type=FUT · close_would_send_outside_rth=true · read_state=session_read · reason='tradingHours: inside 20260816 17:00-20260817 16:00 US/Central'

The gate GRADES A REAL VERDICT on the live VM. It is not silently unknown, the gateway returns a non-empty tradingHours, the timeZoneId resolves, and each instrument is graded on the field its own order acts on.

*** THIS REFUTES THE PREMISE BOTH ROWS ARGUED FROM. *** Both said the live risk was that US/Eastern and US/Central are tzdata LEGACY links absent from slim installs (measured: zoneinfo raises for both in this repo's sandbox), with pytz expected to carry the VM. On the VM pytz is NOT consulted: tz_source is `zoneinfo` and tz_resolved_name equals the RAW id for both symbols, so the FIRST rung resolved directly. The sandbox measurement was true of the sandbox and was wrongly generalised to the VM. Keep the alias map and the pytz rungs — defensive, load-bearing in the sandbox (dropping the alias map fails 12 of 16 parser tests), and a future host may be slim — but do NOT describe them as what makes the live gate work.

HOW IT WAS VERIFIED MATTERS: not by a close. Four checks over ~24h found ZERO closes attempted (every monitor pass returns closed=0 no_change=1), which is structural — nothing asks for an exit. The read surface is what made the gate observable at all. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'fix_landed_pending_live_verification' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. Give IB the treatment Alpaca already has: a session check before the close, and DEFER (the retCode-2 shape) rather than firing a market order the venue will hold. A deferred close leaves the protective bracket armed, which is the safe state.
2. That needs a FUTURES calendar, which does not exist — market_hours.py covers fx / us_equity / crypto only. Prefer asking IB for `contractDetails.tradingHours` / `liquidHours` over hardcoding a window: the broker's own answer cannot drift, and market_hours.py's docstring already concedes it models no holidays and approximates DST.
3. Decide `outsideRth` deliberately per venue rather than inheriting the library default. For a FLATTEN, `outsideRth=True` plus a marketable limit is arguably the correct posture (Alpaca's extended-hours branch is the precedent); silently inheriting False is not a decision anyone made.
4. Until then, treat a `PreSubmitted` / `filled 0` IB close as EXPECTED outside session and do not read it as a broker fault.
5. Separately: handle a PARTIAL fill at cancel time in `_cancel_own_close_order` (today it distinguishes cancelled / already_filled / cancel_failed, with no partial).

updates.by: claude (exit-eval-interval session, operator: 'let's fix the market hours gap for IB')
updates.note:
FIX WRITTEN. Resolution criteria 1-3 addressed; 4 is now moot (the gate refuses the order rather than letting it be held); 5 is DEFERRED and re-filed as its own row rather than folded in silently.

WHAT SHIPPED:
* `src/runtime/ib_trading_hours.py` -- a PURE parser (no IB import, unit-testable without a gateway) for IBKR's `tradingHours`/`liquidHours` + `timeZoneId`, per criterion 2: ask the broker, do not hardcode a COMEX calendar. Parses BOTH shipped formats (full `YYYYMMDD:HHMM-YYYYMMDD:HHMM` and legacy `YYYYMMDD:HHMM-HHMM`), since which one arrives depends on the gateway's API version.
* `IBClient._venue_session` / `.venue_session` -- bounded (`IB_CONTRACT_DETAILS_TIMEOUT_S`, default 5s, async-under-wait_for with the blocking call as fallback, mirroring `_req_all_open_orders`) and cached (`IB_SESSION_CACHE_S`, default 900s). THE CACHE HOLDS THE RAW HOURS STRING, NEVER THE VERDICT: a cached verdict is wrong at exactly the boundary the gate exists for -- a `closed` graded at 17:59 ET would keep reading closed past the 18:00 reopen and strand every close for the rest of the window.
* `_locked_close` consults it BEFORE Step 1. Ordering is load-bearing: Step 1 cancels the protective bracket, and cancelling it to then place nothing is strictly the worst outcome available (unfillable close AND unprotected position). A dedicated falsification test moves the gate after the cancel and fails.
* The defer message CONTAINS 'exit deferred' because `order_monitor._apply_update` detects a defer by STRING-MATCHING the message, not by the retCode. A test asserts the phrase in BOTH the message and order_monitor's own source, so drift on either side fails.
* `outsideRth=True` on the close order (criterion 3), knobbed separately as `IB_CLOSE_OUTSIDE_RTH`. Not cosmetic: IBKR's `outsideRth` keys on LIQUID hours, so gating on `tradingHours` while transmitting `outsideRth=False` would be a verdict about a venue state the order does not act on. Scoped to the CLOSE -- entries are untouched, since declining to open into a thin overnight book is defensible and widening it is a separate decision with a separate risk profile.

THREE STATES, and one of them was a defect in my own first draft. `open`/`closed`/`unknown`, registered with `collapsed-state-guard` as `ib_venue_session.state`. `unknown` covers an unparseable string, an unresolvable timezone, AND an instant outside the covered span -- that last is the collapse a two-state design makes, since 'no range matched' is byte-identical to a real closure. `unknown` proceeds (fail-permissive) but is now LOGGED WARNING, which the first draft did not do: without it a permanently-unknown gate reads exactly like a working gate on an open venue. That is not hypothetical -- `US/Eastern` and `US/Central` are tzdata LEGACY links absent from slim installs (MEASURED: zoneinfo raises for both in this repo's own sandbox while `America/New_York` resolves) and COMEX/CME report precisely those, so the resolver tries zoneinfo raw -> zoneinfo alias -> pytz raw -> pytz alias, and dropping the alias map fails 12 of 16 parser tests here.

VALIDATION: 16 new parser tests + 10 new close-wiring tests, 53 passing in test_p3_close_wiring.py. Each load-bearing property FALSIFIED: removing the gate fails 3; moving it after the cancel fails the bracket-left-armed assertion; dropping `outsideRth` fails 1; caching the verdict instead of the string fails 1; collapsing unknown-outside-span into closed fails the headline parser test. Guards clean (collapsed-state, env-gate, silent-empty, diagnostic-provenance, api-tier, soak-doctrine, provenance-consumer, writer-conformance, timestamp, claim-basis).

NOT YET VERIFIED LIVE. Everything above is code + unit tests against a fake gateway; NO live IB gateway has served a real `reqContractDetails` through this path yet. The specific things a live check must establish, because a fake cannot: that the gateway returns a non-empty `tradingHours`, that its `timeZoneId` resolves ON THE VM (the sandbox cannot resolve `US/Eastern`), and that the verdict is not silently `unknown` -- which is why the WARNING log exists and is the first thing to grep for.

ALSO: this does NOT establish that market hours explain the 2026-08-16 MGC non-fill. The unresolved detail recorded above stands -- order 6 was still `PreSubmitted` at 08:26 ET, which does not fit cleanly with an 08:20 open. The GAP is real and independently worth closing; the INCIDENT's cause is still open.

RETRACTION OF THIS ROW'S OWN 'WHAT I HAVE NOT ESTABLISHED' CAVEAT. Both this row and PR #9693 record that market hours were NOT shown to explain the 2026-08-16 MGC non-fill, on the grounds that order 6 sat PreSubmitted at 08:26 ET which 'does not fit cleanly with an 08:20 open'.

**2026-08-16 IS A SUNDAY.** There is no 08:20 RTH open on a Sunday; CME/COMEX Globex opens Sunday 18:00 ET. I was measuring a weekday window against a day that has none, so the anomaly that kept the incident 'unexplained' was an artifact of my own comparison, not a fact about the venue.

With the correct calendar the picture is ordinary: order 6 placed ~10:56Z = 06:56 ET Sunday and order 378 ~12:30Z = 08:30 ET Sunday, both into a shut venue, both PreSubmitted with filled 0 — which is what a held order looks like, and why `filled 0` rather than a partial was the right read all along. Market hours DO explain the non-fill, and the gate this row produced addresses the actual cause rather than a coincidence found beside it.

The caveat should not be quoted from this row or from #9693 any more. What remains genuinely unverified is separate and unchanged: no live gateway has yet served a real reqContractDetails through the gate, because the gate only runs on a CLOSE and no close has been attempted since deploy (journal 15:30-16:45Z: zero `venue session`, zero `close_open_position`, zero `flatten`, against a probe that finds positives). Deployed and UNEXERCISED.

Deploy itself is now confirmed by the right evidence rather than by /api/diag/version: the trader PID changed 3082570 -> 3093061 between 15:06Z and 15:30Z, so it did restart onto the merged code. (Per BL-20260816-DEPLOY-VERSION-ASSERTION-CANNOT-FAIL, the version endpoint could not have answered this — it reads the working tree.)

COMEX session times above are general knowledge, flagged as such. The gate does not depend on them: it asks IBKR for contractDetails.tradingHours precisely so no hand-held calendar is load-bearing.

THE GATE IS STILL UNEXERCISED, ~14.5h after deploy. Trader journal 2026-08-16T21:55Z -> 2026-08-17T05:47Z, a ~8h window spanning the Sunday Globex open: ZERO `venue session`, ZERO `reqContractDetails`, ZERO `exit deferred`, ZERO `UNKNOWN` — and also ZERO `close_open_position` and ZERO `flatten`. No close was attempted, so the gate never ran. The probe finds positives in the same window (`order_monitor` 168, `IBClient` 10, `MGC` 9), so the search works.

ABSENCE OF `UNKNOWN` IS STILL NOT EVIDENCE OF HEALTH. The tzdata question — whether `US/Eastern` resolves on the live VM, where pytz is the fallback — remains genuinely unanswered, and it will stay unanswered until an IB close actually runs.

Indirect evidence the IB path is alive and simply not closing: journal trade 4699 (2026-08-17T01:13:34Z) is an `mgc_trend_1h` signal on ib_paper REJECTED as `intent_noop:hold_to_bracket_reduce_non_derivative` — the strategy evaluated and the intent layer declined to act, which is a hold, not an exit. Both ib_paper positions are held with stops resting, so nothing is asking for a close.

SUGGESTION for whoever next wants this verified without waiting: the cheapest honest exercise is a `venue_session` READ rather than a close — the public `IBClient.venue_session(symbol)` opens no order path and returns the three-state verdict plus its reason string. A diag route over it would answer the tzdata question directly instead of inferring it from the absence of a warning.

PARTIALLY ADDRESSED AND VERIFIED WORKING: the venue-session gate shipped 2026-08-16 and I read it live today — /api/diag/venue_session?account_id=ib_paper returns MES state=closed, sec_type=FUT, graded_field=tradingHours, tz_source=zoneinfo, tz_resolved_name=US/Central, close_would_send_outside_rth=true. So the gate exists, resolves its timezone on the FIRST rung, and correctly grades a Saturday as closed. What keeps this open is the sibling BL-20260816-IB-PROTECTIVE-STOPS-NEVER-SET-OUTSIDERTH — the CLOSE is now session-aware while the protective STOP still is not.

items.opened_by: claude (exit-eval-interval session, found while fixing the IB close market-hours gap)
items.tier: 3 (changes WHEN a live stop can trigger)
items.title: Every IB protective STOP is RTH-trigger-only: place_protective never sets outsideRth either, so a GTC stop on a ~23h futures contract may be inert for most of the day
items.detail:
FOUND WHILE FIXING THE CLOSE, NOT LOOKED FOR. `grep -rn 'outsideRth|outside_rth' src/` returned ZERO hits across the whole tree before 2026-08-16 -- which is the fact that motivated the close fix, but it does not stop at the close. `IBClient._locked_place_protective` builds its OCA pair from ib_insync `StopOrder` / `LimitOrder` with `tif='GTC'` and never touches `outsideRth`, so those legs also carry the library default `False`.

WHY THAT IS WORSE THAN THE CLOSE GAP. IBKR's `outsideRth` keys on the contract's LIQUID hours. For MGC the liquid window is a few hours a day while the contract trades electronically ~23h. If `outsideRth=False` makes a stop ineligible to TRIGGER outside RTH, then a protective stop armed on an overnight futures position is inert for most of the day -- and every surface we own would still report the position PROTECTED, because `has_protective_orders` / `protection_coverage` ask whether a leg RESTS, never whether it can fire. That is the same shape as BL-20260814-IB-PROTECTION-BOOLEAN-NOT-QUANTITY one level down: a coverage verdict that cannot be contradicted from outside.

WHAT I HAVE ESTABLISHED AND WHAT I HAVE NOT. ESTABLISHED, by grep: no code path in this repo has ever set `outsideRth` on any order, protective legs included. NOT ESTABLISHED: IBKR's exact behaviour for a GTC STOP on a FUTURE with `outsideRth=False` -- whether it is genuinely ineligible to trigger outside RTH, or whether futures stops are exempt because the electronic session IS the regular session for some products. That distinction decides whether this is a live money-at-risk hole or a no-op, and it is NOT in this repo. It is why this is filed rather than fixed alongside the close: the close fix is safe under either answer, whereas changing when a live stop fires is not.

DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED IN THE CLOSE PR. Scoping discipline -- the close change is Tier-2 and reversible by one env flip; this one changes the trigger conditions of live protective orders on real positions and needs the broker-behaviour question answered first.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. ANSWER THE BROKER QUESTION FIRST, from IBKR documentation or a live experiment on ib_paper -- do NOT infer it from this repo, which contains no evidence either way. Arm a stop on an ib_paper futures position with `outsideRth=False`, move price through it outside RTH, and observe whether it fires.
2. If stops ARE inert outside RTH: set `outsideRth=True` on the protective legs (Tier-3, operator-approved), and treat the interim as a known exposure window rather than a covered one.
3. EITHER WAY, make `protection_coverage` report trigger-eligibility, not just restingness -- a boolean that cannot distinguish 'a leg exists' from 'a leg can fire' is the collapsed state here.
4. Check the ENTRY bracket in `_locked_place` on the same axis while in there.

updates.note: Re-validated and it is the live residual of the row above. Live book confirms both MES legs are GTC and resting. Whether outsideRth=False makes a GTC futures stop ineligible to TRIGGER is the open research question RS-20260817 — which must be answered BEFORE any geometry change, per that row.

items.title: _cancel_own_close_order has no PARTIAL-fill state: a close order half-filled at the 6s deadline reads as fully 'cancelled'
items.detail:
AGAINST MY OWN CHANGE (#9663, merged 2026-08-16). `_cancel_own_close_order` returns three states -- `cancelled` / `already_filled` / `cancel_failed` -- and a PARTIAL fill fits none of them. The read is `status == 'Filled' or remaining <= 0`, so an order that filled 40 of 105 and was cancelled for the rest returns `cancelled`, and the caller's retMsg says the position 'is still open' with no hint that its SIZE changed. The next retry re-reads the live qty so it self-corrects rather than compounding -- which is why this is medium and not high -- but the RECORD of what happened is wrong, and that is the class this repo keeps paying for.

SECOND, RELATED CONCERN, stated plainly because it argues the opposite way: cancelling at the deadline is unambiguously right when the order is HELD (nothing is in flight to kill) and is a real hazard when the venue is OPEN and a fill is working. The venue-session gate landed 2026-08-16 reduces this -- a `closed` venue no longer places an order at all -- but does not remove it, since `unknown` and `open` both still place and then cancel at 6s. Whether `IB_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S`=6s is long enough for an open-venue fill is a SEPARATE, unmeasured question; I have no distribution of IB futures fill latency to answer it.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. Add a fourth state (`partially_filled`) carrying the filled qty, and surface it in the close's retMsg so a monitor retry's log says the size changed.
2. Read `filled`/`remaining` explicitly rather than inferring from `status`.
3. Separately, MEASURE IB futures fill latency on an open venue before treating 6s as validated -- it is a chosen value, not a measured one.

updates.note: Re-validated: a half-filled close at the 6 s deadline reading as fully cancelled. Order-path correctness, Tier-2. Same family as BL-20260816-IB-CLOSE-ABANDONS-ITS-OWN-ORDER.

items.opened_by: claude (exit-eval-interval session, against my own #9663, refuted by live broker read)
items.title: _cancel_own_close_order returns 'cancelled' when ib.cancelOrder is ACCEPTED, not when the order is GONE -- measured live as an order stuck in PendingCancel for 1h43m while the log said cancelled
items.detail:
THIS CORRECTS A CLAIM I MADE EARLIER TODAY. I reported #9663 'verified live' because the apply run produced the predicted wire signature `(own close order: cancelled)`. The signature appeared. The thing it asserts did not happen.

MEASURED, /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper at 2026-08-16T14:13:09Z (relay #9718, read_state 'orders_read' -- a CONFIRMED read, not an inference): order 378, MGC MKT SELL 105, tif DAY, perm_id 1529982316, **status 'PendingCancel', filled 0, remaining 105**. It was placed and cancel-requested at roughly 12:30Z. It was still resting 1h43m later.

THE DEFECT IS THE EXACT CLASS #9663 EXISTS TO FIX, COMMITTED BY #9663. `_locked_close` was already hardened against 'accepted != filled' by IB_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S, which re-reads the live position and refuses to declare a close the broker has not confirmed. The CANCEL I added in the same method has no equivalent: `_cancel_own_close_order` calls `ib.cancelOrder(order)`, sees no exception, and returns the literal 'cancelled'. IBKR accepting a cancel REQUEST is not the order being gone -- `PendingCancel` is a real, durable, documented state, and this repo already carries an instance of it on the other venue (BL-20260716-ALPACA-QQQ-WEDGED-PENDING-CANCEL: 'Alpaca's OWN cancel never completes, so a re-issued app-level cancel is a no-op'). I wrote the IB analogue without checking for the analogue of that failure.

WHY THE THREE-STATE DESIGN DID NOT SAVE IT. The states are `cancelled` / `already_filled` / `cancel_failed`, and they partition the RESPONSE TO THE REQUEST, not the STATE OF THE ORDER. There is no state for 'the cancel was accepted and the order is still there', which is precisely the observed outcome -- so the collapse is that `cancelled` silently covers both 'gone' and 'pending cancel indefinitely'. A field that cannot say 'we asked and it did not take' is the same shape as one that cannot say 'we did not look'.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, and note the account. ib_paper held MGC long 105 with THREE resting SELLs at the time of the read: order 6 (MKT 105, PreSubmitted, since ~10:56Z), order 378 (MKT 105, PendingCancel), order 359 (STP 105 @ 4278.8, GTC, oca-protect-357). That is up to 315 contracts of sell against a 105 long, in three orders with no OCA tying them together, so none can cancel another. If two fill the account goes 105 short. **ib_paper is a PAPER account, so no real money is at risk here** -- but nothing about the code path is paper-specific, and the same sequence on a funded IB account is a live reversal.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: why the cancel is not completing. A DAY market order held outside session may simply not be cancellable until the venue opens, which would make PendingCancel correct broker behaviour and the DEFECT purely the reporting. I have no evidence either way and did not probe further. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'confirmed_reporting_only' was collapsed to 'resolved' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. Add a bounded post-cancel CONFIRM, the mirror of IB_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S: re-read the order and require it to actually leave the resting set before returning 'cancelled'.
2. Add the missing state -- something like `cancel_pending` -- for 'accepted, still resting at the deadline'. It must be distinct from `cancelled` and from `cancel_failed`: the request did not fail, and the order is not gone.
3. The retMsg must carry it, since that string is the only record a monitor retry leaves behind.
4. Consider whether a still-resting close order should block a retry from placing ANOTHER one -- the measured state (three resting sells against one long) is the accumulation hazard #9663's own comment described, arrived at by a different route than the one that comment anticipated.
5. Re-read /api/diag/ib_open_orders to establish whether order 378 ever clears, and whether it clears on its own at the session open (which would answer the open question above).
refs: relay #9718 (the refuting read: status PendingCancel, remaining 105)
relay #9716 (the read before it: read_state could_not_look)
BL-20260716-ALPACA-QQQ-WEDGED-PENDING-CANCEL (the same state, other venue, already known)

updates.note:
EVIDENCE THAT SHIFTS THE DIAGNOSIS AWAY FROM MY CODE, measured 15:20:17Z (relay #9736, read_state 'orders_read').

TWO orders on ib_paper/MGC are now stuck in PendingCancel, cancelled by TWO DIFFERENT clients via TWO DIFFERENT code paths:
  * order 378, client_id 9927 — cancelled by MY `_cancel_own_close_order` (#9663) at ~12:30Z. Pending ~2h50m.
  * order 6,   client_id 9974 — cancelled by the OTHER session's dedicated `cancel-ib-order` system-action (#9700/#9723) between 14:13Z and 15:20Z. It read `PreSubmitted` at 14:13Z and `PendingCancel` at 15:20Z, so their apply WAS accepted.

Two independent cancels, two clients, two implementations, both accepted, neither completing. That is a strong argument that the non-completion is a PROPERTY OF THE VENUE OR GATEWAY, not a defect specific to `_cancel_own_close_order` — and it raises the prior on the open question this row already recorded: that a DAY market order simply cannot be cancelled while COMEX is shut, which would make PendingCancel correct broker behaviour.

WHAT THIS DOES **NOT** DO IS EXONERATE THE REPORTING DEFECT, and the distinction is the whole point of the row. Even if the venue is the reason nothing clears, `_cancel_own_close_order` still returns the literal 'cancelled' the instant `ib.cancelOrder` does not raise, and the close's retMsg still tells a reader that nothing of ours rests. That claim was false for 2h50m and would have been false regardless of the cause. The fix (a bounded post-cancel confirm + a `cancel_pending` state) is unchanged by this finding; what changes is the EXPECTED OUTCOME of that confirm — outside session it should routinely land on `cancel_pending`, not on 'cancelled'.

ALTERNATIVE NOT RULED OUT: an IB gateway / socat-relay condition affecting cancels generally. I have no evidence separating that from the venue-shut hypothesis. The decisive observation is cheap and requires no action — if BOTH orders clear at the COMEX open without anyone touching them, the venue hypothesis holds; if they persist into an open session, it does not.

THE DECISIVE TEST HAS NOT RUN YET, AND I ALMOST SCORED IT WRONG. Read at 16:45:41Z (relay #9749, read_state 'orders_read'): orders 6 (client 9974) and 378 (client 9927) are BOTH still PendingCancel, remaining 105 each; 378 is now ~4h15m.

16:45Z is 12:45 ET, which looks like the middle of a trading day. **2026-08-16 IS A SUNDAY.** CME/COMEX Globex opens Sunday 18:00 ET, so 12:45 ET Sunday is the weekend gap and the venue is SHUT. Both orders persisting is therefore fully CONSISTENT with the venue-shut hypothesis and refutes nothing. Scoring this as 'persisted into an open session' -- which the hour-clock invites -- would have falsely killed the leading explanation. The decisive observation is the Sunday 18:00 ET open, i.e. **2026-08-16T22:00Z**, and it has not happened.

AND IT REFRAMES THE WHOLE INCIDENT. Every IB observation this session was made on a SUNDAY with COMEX shut: order 6 placed ~10:56Z (06:56 ET Sunday), order 378 ~12:30Z (08:30 ET Sunday). Both sat PreSubmitted with filled 0, which is exactly what a venue-held order looks like.

THIS RETRACTS A CAVEAT I ATTACHED TO BL-20260816-IB-CLOSE-HAS-NO-MARKET-HOURS-AWARENESS AND TO PR #9693. I recorded repeatedly that 'market hours are NOT shown to explain the non-fill, because order 6 was still PreSubmitted at 08:26 ET which does not fit cleanly with an 08:20 open'. There IS NO 08:20 OPEN ON A SUNDAY. I was measuring a weekday RTH window against a day that has none, so the anomaly I could not resolve was an artifact of my own comparison. Market hours now explain the non-fill straightforwardly, and the gate shipped in #9693 addresses the actual cause rather than a coincidence.

(COMEX session times here are general knowledge, not read from this repo -- flagged as such. Nothing in the gate depends on them: ib_trading_hours asks IBKR for contractDetails.tradingHours precisely so no hand-held calendar is load-bearing.)

STILL UNCHANGED: the REPORTING defect. `_cancel_own_close_order` returned 'cancelled' the instant cancelOrder did not raise, and that claim has been false for 4h15m whatever the cause. If the venue explanation holds at 22:00Z, the fix's expected outcome is that a post-cancel confirm lands on `cancel_pending` outside session -- routinely, by design, not as an error.

updates.by: claude (exit-eval-interval session, check-in #3 — the decisive observation)
updates.note:
RESOLVED IN FAVOUR OF THE VENUE HYPOTHESIS. THE DEFECT IS REPORTING-ONLY.

Globex reopened Sunday 18:00 ET = 2026-08-16T22:00Z. Measured after it, on Monday:
  * 2026-08-17T05:47:00Z, /api/diag/ib_open_orders (read_state 'orders_read'): orders 6 and 378 are BOTH ABSENT. The ib_paper book is down to three resting stops — MES 338, MES 375, MGC 359.
  * 2026-08-17T05:50:31Z, /api/diag/exchange_positions: **MGC still long 105** (entry 4276.236), MES long 15.
  * Trader journal 21:55Z -> 05:47Z (~8h spanning the open): ZERO hits for `cancel`, `PendingCancel`, `close_open_position`, `flatten`, `order 6`, `378`.

THE POSITION READ IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE, and it is why this needed a second query. 'Left PendingCancel' has TWO causes and only one is benign: a cancel completing, or the order FILLING. Both were 105-lot SELLs against a 105 long, so a fill would have left the account 105 short (or 210 short if both filled). MGC unchanged at long 105 proves they CANCELLED. Scoring the disappearance alone would have reached the right verdict by luck while being unable to distinguish it from the worst outcome available.

So: two cancels, two clients, two implementations, both stuck for hours while the venue was shut, both completing on their own once it opened, with nothing in the system touching them. That is the venue-shut hypothesis confirmed and the 'my cancel is broken' hypothesis dead.

WHAT REMAINS A REAL DEFECT, unchanged and now precisely scoped: `_cancel_own_close_order` returns the literal 'cancelled' the instant `ib.cancelOrder` does not raise. Order 378's cancel was requested ~12:30Z and completed sometime after 22:00Z — the claim was false for upwards of NINE HOURS, and the close's retMsg told every reader that nothing of ours rested. The fix is unchanged (bounded post-cancel confirm + a `cancel_pending` state), but its EXPECTED OUTCOME is now known rather than guessed: outside session it should land on `cancel_pending` routinely, by design, and that is correct behaviour to report rather than an error to alarm on.

SEVERITY REASSESSMENT: this stays high as a REPORTING defect but is NOT an order-path hazard. The accumulation worry recorded earlier — three unlinked resting sells against a 105 long — was real while it lasted and resolved itself at the open without intervention.

items.opened_by: claude (sysrev-0816 session, operator-directed during the MGC RTH check-in)
items.title: IB_CLOSE_RETRY_COOLDOWN_S's deferral lives in a module global, so EVERY trader restart re-opens the close-retry churn window the cooldown exists to close -- and this repo restarts the trader on every merge to main
items.detail:
OPERATOR-DIRECTED, filed during the ib_paper/MGC RTH check-in.

WHAT THE COOLDOWN IS FOR. `IB_CLOSE_RETRY_COOLDOWN_S` (default 300s) exists because re-attempting an unconfirmed close every tick is actively harmful, not merely wasteful: `IBClient.close` Step 1 CANCELS the resting protective bracket before placing the opposing order, so a per-tick retry 'leaves the position briefly naked each tick and keeps cancelling the very stop that would flatten it when the venue reopens' (CLAUDE.md, verbatim). The deferral is the thing standing between an un-fillable close and that churn.

THE DEFECT. The deferral marker is `_PENDING_CLOSE_RETRY_COOLDOWN: Dict[tuple, datetime] = {}` -- a MODULE GLOBAL at src/runtime/order_monitor.py:1765, initialised empty at import and never reloaded from anywhere. Set at :914 on the 'not confirmed flat' branch, read at :812, cleared at :825/:947. So the cooldown is scoped to ONE PROCESS. A restart does not resume the deferral; it erases it, and the next monitor pass is free to cancel the bracket and place another close.

THIS IS DOCUMENTED AS A SAFETY PROPERTY AND IS NOT ONE. CLAUDE.md's row reads 'In-process (a restart re-arms from scratch -- fail-safe, never closes early).' That reasoning covers ONE direction (a lost deferral cannot make the monitor close a position too EARLY) and silently omits the direction that bites: a lost deferral makes the monitor re-attempt a close that ALREADY FAILED, stripping the stop each time. 'Fail-safe' was asserted against the wrong failure mode.

WHY IT IS NOT RARE. The trader redeploys on every merge to `main`. Directly observed on 2026-08-16 from journalctl PIDs: 3013437 -> 3015773 (restart at 12:10:15Z) -> 3026257 (by 12:36Z) -- THREE processes in ~26 minutes, i.e. the 300s cooldown could not have survived intact even once in that window. The sibling row BL-20260816-EXIT-EVAL-INTERVAL-AT-60S-REQUIREMENT independently records five observed processes in ~10h the same day, counted from `process_started_utc`.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE (ib_paper/MGC, 2026-08-16). At 12:12Z `/api/diag/ib_open_orders` showed 4 orders and I reported to the coordination board that no market sells had stacked. At 12:33:32Z it showed 5: order 6 (MKT SELL 105, tif DAY, oca_group null, PreSubmitted, filled 0 -- the pre-restart abandoned attempt) AND a NEW order 378 (MKT SELL 105, tif DAY, oca_group null, PendingCancel, filled 0). Two unlinked market sells of 105 each against a 105 long. The restart at 12:10:15Z is the only thing that changed between the two reads.

WHAT #9663 DOES AND DOES NOT FIX. PR #9663 (BL-20260816-IB-CLOSE-ABANDONS-ITS-OWN-ORDER, merged 4667dd05a) makes close() cancel the order it just placed on the not-confirmed path -- which is why 378 reads PendingCancel rather than joining 6 as a second permanent resting sell. So the ACCUMULATION is bounded going forward. It does NOT address this row: each restart still buys one fresh cancel-the-bracket-then-place-a-doomed-order cycle, and the stop is genuinely absent for the duration of each attempt. #9663 cleans up the order; it does not stop the attempt from being made.

THE PRECEDENT IS ALREADY IN THIS REPO. Every other latch of this kind persists to disk precisely so a bounce cannot reset it -- `account_reachability_alert_state.json` ('persists across restarts so the consecutive-down counter survives a bounce'), `trainer_reachability_alert_state.json`, `silent_refusal_alert_state.json`. The close-retry cooldown is the outlier, and it is the one guarding an order-path action.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. The deferral survives a restart -- persisted to `runtime_logs/` keyed on (account, symbol, direction) with its set-time, in the shape the three *_alert_state.json latches already use, and reloaded on first read rather than assumed empty.
2. The persisted read is three-state and says which: `deferral_active` / `no_deferral` (we looked, nothing is deferred) / `could_not_read` (we did not look). A read failure MUST NOT resolve to 'no deferral' -- that is the current behaviour dressed up, and it is the collapsed-state failure the guard exists to catch. Register with collapsed-state-guard.
3. A test that asserts a simulated restart INSIDE the cooldown window does not re-attempt the close: set the marker, drop the module state, reload, assert the monitor defers. The existing tests cannot catch this because they never cross a process boundary.
4. CLAUDE.md's `IB_CLOSE_RETRY_COOLDOWN_S` row loses the unqualified 'fail-safe' claim and states both directions explicitly.
5. MEASURED, not merely shipped: across at least one real deploy while a deferral is active on ib_paper, `/api/diag/ib_open_orders` shows no new MKT close order for that (account, symbol, direction). Verifying this requires the gateway reachable -- a `read_state: could_not_look` run is NOT evidence of absence.

updates.note: Re-validated: a module-global deferral reopening the churn window on every restart. IDENTICAL shape to the target-naked cooldown defect that was FIXED on 2026-08-23 with a durable latch — and that fix is now proven working (ib_target_naked pages went 21/22/48/15 -> 0/0/1/1/0). So the remedy is known, proven, and simply not yet applied here. One of the cleanest fixes available.

items.opened_by: claude (sysrev-0816 session, operator-directed: 'that's a huge gap in capabilities that shouldn't exist')
items.title: No way to cancel a SINGLE IB order from any session -- the only two mechanisms either PLACE another order or strip every protective stop on the account
items.detail:
OPERATOR-DIRECTED. Surfaced when the operator instructed 'cancel order 6' (the stranded ib_paper/MGC MKT SELL 105 abandoned by a failed flatten) and NO mechanism could carry it out.

THE THREE THINGS THAT LOOKED LIKE A CANCEL, AND WHY EACH FAILED.
(a) `IBClient.cancel(order_id)` exists, but `_locked_cancel` resolves its target by iterating `self._open_trades(ib)` = `ib.openTrades()`, which returns only orders THIS clientId placed. Any ops caller runs on a process-unique id, so it returns 'order <id> not found among open trades' for an order it can plainly see on the account-wide read.
(b) `flatten-ib-position` is a FLATTEN: it would place a third market sell, and its Step-1 cancel runs on the same session-scoped read (already measured no-op'ing on 2026-08-16 -- see `_cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol`'s docstring).
(c) `reqGlobalCancel` is the only cross-client cancel and is all-or-nothing: it would take the MGC stop and both MES protective legs with it.

THE MECHANISM, VERIFIED AGAINST THE TWS API DOCS (not assumed, and it REFUTES the previously recorded fix premise). `cancelOrder` 'can only be used to cancel an order that was placed originally by a client with the same client ID (or from TWS for client ID 0)', and 'Orders submitted via the TWS API will always be bound to the client application (i.e. client Id) they were submitted from meaning only the submitting client will be able to modify the placed order.' ⚠️ The **Master API client ID does NOT grant cancellation** -- the API reference mentions it solely for RECEIVING order-status callbacks ('The client with Master Client ID (set in TWS/IBG) will receive order status messages for all clients'), a visibility role. `BL-20260816-IB-CLOSE-ABANDONS-ITS-OWN-ORDER`'s 11:50Z update proposed 'a gateway Master API client id + a narrow cancel-ib-order action' as option (1); the Master-ID half of that is WRONG and configuring one would not have cancelled order 6. The only per-order path is to connect AS the owning clientId.

A SECOND GAP FOUND WHILE FIXING THIS, in code shipped the same day: `IBClient.list_open_orders` -- the account-wide read surface added for `BL-20260814-NO-IB-OPEN-ORDERS-READ-SURFACE` -- did NOT capture `clientId`. So the one surface that could SHOW you a stranded order gave you no way to learn the address a cancel must be sent from. A read surface whose whole purpose is 'reduce nothing' had reduced away the field that makes the rows actionable. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'fix_landed_pending_live_verification' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. SHIPPED: `list_open_orders` rows carry `client_id` (null = IB did not report it, which is NOT 'client 0').
2. SHIPPED: `scripts/ops/cancel_ib_order.py` + the Tier-2 `cancel-ib-order` system-action -- reads account-wide, resolves the owner, connects AS that clientId, cancels, re-reads to verify. Dry-run by default. Lookup is three-state and never collapsed (`could_not_look` / `not_found` / `found`), and an accepted cancel whose verification read fails reports `cancelled_unconfirmed` rather than success.
3. SHIPPED: two default refusals with SEPARATE explicit overrides -- a protective order (OCA-grouped or a stop/trailing type) needs `--force-protective`; a clientId below 9000 (the trader's execution band) needs `--force-client-id`, because taking over that id would evict the trader's live IB session.
4. OPEN -- LIVE VERIFICATION. Not yet exercised against a real broker: at 12:37:33Z the IB breaker was open and `/api/diag/ib_open_orders` returned `read_state: could_not_look`. The action must be run in DRY-RUN first against a real order and shown to resolve a real `owner_client_id`, then applied and verified `gone`. A `could_not_look` run is NOT evidence either way. Until then the 14 unit tests prove the DECISION logic only, never the IB semantics.
5. OPEN -- the class this does NOT cover: an order owned by the trader's own live execution client cannot be cancelled by any ops session (connecting as that id evicts the trader). The trader can cancel its own orders; nothing else can. Whether that needs its own wire is a separate question, deliberately not answered here.
refs: TWS API cancel_order + open_orders (the clientId-binding contract)

items.title: IB protection coverage graded a STOP and a TAKE-PROFIT as interchangeable, so BOTH live ib_paper positions sat target-naked and nothing ever alerted -- zero limit orders on the entire account
items.detail:
OPERATOR-DIRECTED, escalated as unacceptable: a live position with no take-profit can only stop out or run.

MEASURED, /api/diag/ib_open_orders 2026-08-16T13:34:08Z, read_state 'orders_read' (a CONFIRMED clean account-wide read, not a could-not-look):
  MGC 105 long -- STP 359 @ 4278.8 (oca-protect-357). NO limit order.
  MES  15 long -- STP 338 @ 7516.5 (oca-protect-336) AND STP 375 @ 7533.75 (oca-protect-373). NO limit order. Also 30 contracts of stop against a 15 position.
  ZERO limit orders exist on the account. Every OCA group holds a stop and nothing else.

ROOT CAUSE (first half, FIXED). `IBClient.protection_coverage` classified a leg as covering with `if not ("STP" in otype or "LMT" in otype or "TRAIL" in otype): continue` -- one membership test over both sides. Protection is TWO-SIDED and the sides are not interchangeable: a stop bounds the loss, a target realises the gain. A stop-only book therefore graded `covered_qty == size`, `_check_broker_naked_ib_positions` took the `covered` branch, and the sweep has NEVER ONCE fired on a stripped target. The method's own docstring is about netting QUANTITY -- the stop-vs-target axis was never modelled at all, which is why the earlier boolean->quantity fix (BL-20260814-IB-PROTECTION-BOOLEAN-NOT-QUANTITY) did not catch it either. Two fixes to the same method, both correct, and the defect survived both because each addressed a different axis.

ROOT CAUSE (second half, NOT YET CONFIRMED). The resting groups are named `oca-protect-<reqId>`, the KEYLESS fallback form -- not the `oca-protect-t<trade_id>` form `_attempt_naked_autoprotect` produces. `place_protective` places only the legs it is handed, so a caller passing SL-only silently replaces an SL+TP pair with a stop alone. `execute.modify_open_order` -> `modify_protective` is the keyless caller (BL-20260816-IB-DUPLICATE-STOPS-IN-SEPARATE-OCA-GROUPS). Stated as a hypothesis, NOT a finding: no code path has been traced end-to-end that drops the TP, and the alternative (the TP filled or was cancelled leaving the stop) has not been excluded.

WHY THE OBVIOUS REPAIR IS REFUSED, and this is the load-bearing part. Making target-nakedness trigger the existing re-arm would CREATE A NAKED SHORT. `_attempt_naked_autoprotect` passes `oca_key = trade_id`, so `place_protective` cancels group `oca-protect-t4487` -- which does not exist -- while the real group is `oca-protect-357`. Stop 359 survives, a fresh stop+TP pair is added (MGC: 210 contracts of stop against 105), and when the new target fills it cancels its own OCA sibling and leaves stray stop 359 resting on a FLAT book, able to fill into a 105 short. Clearing the strays requires a cancel addressed to their OWNING clientId (BL-20260816-NO-PER-ORDER-IB-CANCEL). So the sweep ALERTS and does not re-arm until that lands. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'detection_landed_repair_DECLINED_by_operator_2026-08-20' was collapsed to 'wont_fix' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. SHIPPED: `_protective_leg_side()` classifies stop vs target, checking the STOP family FIRST -- 'STP LMT' contains 'LMT' and an LMT-first test would file every stop-limit as a take-profit, MANUFACTURING coverage that does not exist (worse than the bug: the old one hid a real gap, that would invent a fake fill). `protection_coverage` now publishes `stop_qty` + `target_qty` beside the back-compat `covered_qty`, applying the within-OCA-group max PER SIDE.
2. SHIPPED: `_check_broker_naked_ib_positions` grades the target side separately and pages CRITICAL (Telegram + the /api/bot/notifications banner) when a trade has a DECLARED tp and the broker holds less target coverage than the position size. Declared-only, deliberately: a strategy that never chose a target must not have one imposed on it -- that is a Tier-3 strategy question, not a repair. Rate-limited to one page per 6h per (account, symbol), because the condition persists until repaired and a 5-minute alarm is the desensitized-alarm P1.
3. OPEN -- THE LIVE REPAIR. Both positions are still target-naked. Sequence: deploy the `client_id` read surface, read ownership of stops 359/338/375, cancel the strays via `cancel-ib-order`, then attach the declared targets. NOT done, and the positions are unprotected on the target side until it is.
4. OPEN -- CONFIRM the second root-cause half by tracing a code path that actually drops the TP, or excluding it. Until then criterion 3 repairs the instances without preventing recurrence.
5. OPEN -- the same one-sided question on the OTHER venues: the Alpaca and Bybit naked sweeps were not audited for it in this pass. `_bybit_position_protection` sums SL legs by name, so it is likely stop-only BY CONSTRUCTION and may have the identical blind spot. NOT verified -- do not read this row as clearing them.
refs: issue #9702 (the account-wide read that measured it)

updates.note: DETECTION HALF VERIFIED GENUINELY FIRING -- not inferred from the merge. GET /api/bot/notifications at 2026-08-20T20:30:40Z returned has_alerts true with BOTH target-naked banners live, each naming the position and its DECLARED level: 'ib_paper/MGC: position 95.0 has 0.0 of take-profit coverage against a declared TP of 4393.02071429 -- the position can only stop out or run' and the same for ib_paper/MES against 8390.59025. This also answers the open question in BL-20260818-DID-TARGET-NAKED-EVER-FIRE-FOR-MGC and criterion (2) of BL-20260818-ICT-SCALP-HAS-NO-TAKE-PROFIT-CLOSE-PATH: the detector fires; it is not a first detector silently not firing. CRITERION 3 (THE LIVE REPAIR) REMAINS OPEN and the population has CHANGED underneath it -- the MGC instance named in this row (105 long, stop 359, oca-protect-357) NO LONGER EXISTS: that position was flattened 2026-08-18 when the repair's own limit order 381 turned out to be marketable (see BL-20260818-ATTACH-IB-TARGET-VERIFY-CANNOT-EXPRESS-FILLED). The CURRENT MGC is trade 4773, 95 long, opened 2026-08-19T00:27Z -- i.e. target-nakedness RECURRED on a fresh position AFTER the fix shipped, rather than persisting. That is the stronger reading and it argues the class is live and reproducing. CRITERION 5 (the other venues) is still unaudited by this session -- do not read this row as clearing Alpaca or Bybit. NEW, and not covered by this row: coverage is graded on QUANTITY and SIDE but never on PRICE. See BL-20260820-PROTECTION-COVERAGE-IS-PRICE-BLIND.

[OPERATOR DECLINED THE REPAIR — and the earlier approval is STALE because its trade no longer exists. Read this before acting on any prior 'operator approved the TP' line.]

MEASURED 2026-08-20T22:26Z, direct /api/diag read, read_state 'orders_read' (4 orders, 3 positions on ib_paper):
  MGC  trade 4773 ict_scalp_mgc_15m   95 long @ 4367.05  stop 391 @ 4371.10  TARGET: NONE   declared tp 4393.02
  MES  trade 4350 mes_trend_long_1d   15 long @ 7630.87  stop 338 @ 7516.50  TARGET: NONE   declared tp 8390.59
  MHG  trade 4796 mhg_pullback_1d     29 long @ 6.5028   stop 399 @ 6.2215   TARGET: 398 @ 7.1415 (SAME OCA group 308977633)  declared tp 7.1413

TWO THINGS CHANGED THAT A FUTURE SESSION MUST NOT MISS.

1. THE APPROVAL LOST ITS REFERENT. The operator approved placing MGC trade 4487's declared TP of 4297.66 ('yes place it', 2026-08-16). **Trade 4487 is CLOSED** — status closed, exit_reason 'exchange_flat_reconciled', pnl None. The MGC on the account today is a DIFFERENT trade (4773) at a different size, entry and declared TP. So 4297.66 is a level NOTHING now declares, and the sprint log / board comments that record the approval are describing a trade that no longer exists. An approval is scoped to the trade it was given for; it does not transfer to whatever position later occupies the same symbol.

2. THE OPERATOR HAS NOW DECLINED THE ATTACH OUTRIGHT (2026-08-20, verbatim: 'No. Don't do that.'), asked for the remainder to be backlogged, and closed the session. So the repair is NOT pending-on-tooling any more — it is pending on a NEW operator decision. Do not treat this row's open status as standing authorisation.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT ADDS ANYWAY, because it narrows the open question. MHG 4796 is the FIRST fully-bracketed position ever observed on this account — stop and target in the same OCA group, target matching the declared tp to 4dp. So the ENTRY path does place targets correctly. The open question is therefore no longer 'does anything place targets' but 'why do 4773 and 4350 lack one' — a per-trade question (was it never placed, or placed and later stripped?) rather than a systemic one. 4350 has now been target-naked for at least 4 days; 4773 postdates the 08-16 read and was target-naked on first observation.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND, and it is the PRODUCER — not the re-assert, not the grader.

`IBClient._locked_place_protective` built its legs `[TP, SL]` and set
`leg.transmit = i == len(legs) - 1`, with a comment describing it as mirroring 'the bracket-transmit discipline in place()'. THAT DISCIPLINE WORKS IN `place()` ONLY BECAUSE ITS CHILDREN CARRY `parentId` (ib_client.py:1377/1386) — IBKR holds them and releases them when the parent transmits. `place_protective` sets NO parentId at all (verified: the only parentId assignments in the file are place()'s), and its own docstring says the OCA group ties the legs 'with no parent'. A PARENTLESS ORDER WITH transmit=False IS HELD BY IBKR AND NEVER RELEASED, because nothing exists to release it.

So the TP — the non-final leg — was constructed, sent, and silently never transmitted, on EVERY bracket this method ever placed. The stop went live alone.

THIS IS THE CAUSE OF BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED. That row measured 'zero limit orders existed account-wide' on ib_paper and correctly fixed the GRADER so a stop-only book stops reading as covered. `place_target_in_group` was then built as a repair wire for the symptom. Nobody asked why the targets were missing, so the producer kept making them.

FIXED: every leg transmits. The stop is now built FIRST, because order became load-bearing the moment both legs go live — they reach IBKR one at a time, and a window with only downside protection is strictly safer than one with only an upside target. The returned orderId is resolved by leg TYPE rather than list position, since it used to be `legs[-1]` and happened to be the stop only because of the old ordering; callers persist it as trades.sl_order_id.

PLANT-PROVEN: re-introducing `i == len(legs) - 1` turns the new guard RED, and restoring the fix turns it GREEN. A guard that cannot be shown to fail is not evidence when it passes.

STILL UNVERIFIED AT THE VENUE: MES 4350 has not been re-asserted since the fix (it is under the 3600s per-(account,symbol) cooldown, and the fix is not deployed yet). The next re-assert on ib_paper is the live check — expect a resting LMT to appear beside the STP in oca-protect-*, and applied_state to read both_legs_resting.

attach-ib-target REPORTED FAILURE ON A PLACEMENT THAT WORKED — a false negative, measured 2026-08-23T14:27Z on ib_paper/MES (issue #10178).

The action returned action='place_not_effective', verify_state='absent_unexplained', targets_after=[], wrapper exit 1, with the note 'the order was accepted, no target is resting ... the placement did not take effect'. Its place_response was retCode 0, orderId 6, limitPrice 8390.5.

A DIRECT BROKER READ ~1 MINUTE LATER SHOWS THE TARGET RESTING: /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper (read_state orders_read) returns 5 orders, including MES LMT SELL 15.0 @ 8390.5, oca_group oca-protect-408, order_id 6, status **PendingSubmit** — in the SAME group as the stop (order 410, STP @ 7533.75), which is exactly the intended outcome.

THE VERIFY READ TOO EARLY AND COLLAPSED TWO STATES. 'Not resting' and 'not resting YET' are different facts, and a freshly placed GTC leg sits at PendingSubmit before it is Submitted/PreSubmitted. This is the SAME SHAPE as this row's original finding — the verify cannot express a target that FILLED — one state over: it also cannot express a target that has been accepted and is still propagating. Both are 'absent' to a single immediate snapshot.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE NOISE: exit 1 on a successful repair invites a session to RETRY, and a retry here would place a SECOND target into the same OCA group. The action is not idempotent in the presence of a false negative.

⚠️ DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY WIDENING THE SUCCESS CRITERION. The right shape is a bounded re-read with the order STATUS as evidence (PendingSubmit / PreSubmitted / Submitted are all 'placed'; nothing at all after the bound is 'absent'), plus a distinct 'placed_not_yet_visible' state. Treating an empty first read as success would remove the only check that caught the transmit defect.

FULLY REMEDIATED ON ib_paper, verified at the broker 2026-08-23T14:32Z.

/api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper (read_state orders_read) now returns SIX orders — every open position holds BOTH legs in one OCA group:
  MES  STP 7533.75 + LMT 8390.50  (oca-protect-408)
  MGC  STP 4371.10 + LMT 4393.00  (oca-protect-389)
  MHG  STP 6.2215  + LMT 7.1415   (308977633, untouched control)
This row's original measurement was 'zero limit orders existed account-wide'. There are now three, and zero target-naked positions.

THE MGC CASE WAS NOT THE MES CASE, and the difference was checked before applying: MGC 4773's target is ALREADY CROSSED (entry 4364.6, stop trailed to 4371.15 above entry, target 4393.02, monitor logging tp_cross every ~30s and deferring on the shut COMEX venue). So its leg is expected to FILL at the 22:00Z reopen rather than rest — which is what the declared geometry intends and what the monitor is already attempting. The orphan-leg hazard place_target_in_group's docstring warns about does not arise, because IBClient.close cancels the bracket at Step 1 before flattening: whichever exit wins, the other leg is cancelled (by OCA on a fill, by close() on a market flatten).

OBSERVATION, not filed as its own defect: BOTH new limit legs carry order_id 6. The ops client's request-id sequence restarts per run, so order_id is NOT unique across clients on this account — IBKR disambiguates by permId. A reader diffing two ib_open_orders snapshots by order_id alone would conflate them. Noted here rather than filed because nothing currently keys on order_id across clients; it becomes a real defect the moment something does.

items.status_corrected_2026_08_25: STATUS WAS `wont_fix` AND THE ROW'S OWN RECORD CONTRADICTS IT. Its resolution_criteria begin '1. SHIPPED: `_protective_leg_side()` classifies stop vs target...', and its last update (2026-08-23T14:32:54Z) reads 'FULLY REMEDIATED ON ib_paper, verified at the broker' with a direct /api/diag/ib_open_orders read showing all three positions holding BOTH legs — against this row's original measurement of 'zero limit orders existed account-wide'. `wont_fix` means we DECLINED to fix it; the evidence says it was fixed and verified. On a CRITICAL row that is the dangerous direction: anyone auditing 'what critical findings did we decline to fix' would have found a shipped fix, and anyone auditing 'did the two-sided coverage work land' would have found a row saying no. Corrected to `resolved` with the verification timestamp. Both statuses are terminal, so no open-count moves. Found while diffing the two open-status predicates (BL-20260825-TWO-DEFINITIONS-OF-OPEN-DISAGREE-ABOUT-SEVEN-ROWS) — the row surfaced because it was one of the terminal rows the criteria census had been wrongly demanding an exit condition from.

items.title: CONFIRM at the next CME open that ib_paper MGC trade 4487 actually closed on its attached take-profit -- an attached target is a PLACED order, never a fill
items.detail:
FOLLOW-UP TO BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED. Operator approved placing MGC 4487's DECLARED take-profit ('yes place it', 2026-08-16), knowing the level is already through the market: trades.take_profit_1 = 4297.66 against a last of ~4398.70, so a 105-contract LONG sells into a bid ~101 points ABOVE its target. The expected outcome is that the position closes essentially at the open, favourably relative to the declared plan.

WHY THIS NEEDS A ROW RATHER THAN AN ASSUMPTION. Placing a limit and observing a fill are different facts, and this repo has an incident class built on collapsing them: IB_PLACE_CONFIRM_S exists because placeOrder is async and fire-and-forget reported success on orders IBKR rejected outright (trade #2531), and IB_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S exists because an accepted-but-unfilled close left a REAL position open while the journal row read closed. So 'the target was attached' must not be recorded anywhere as 'the trade closed'.

WHAT TO CHECK, and in this order:
  1. /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper -- read_state MUST be 'orders_read'. A      'could_not_look' answers nothing and is NOT evidence of a fill; re-check later.
  2. /api/diag/exchange_positions?account_id=ib_paper -- MGC absent from a positions list      that is [] (genuinely flat), never null (could-not-read).
  3. trade_journal.db trade 4487 -- status closed, and read pnlProvenance: IBKR historical-     candle coverage is 0%, so the realized figure must come from the exchange-fills store      (CommissionReport.realizedPNL via ict-ib-executions-pull.timer, HOURLY), not a mark. A      FABRICATED grade here is its own finding.
  4. The stop leg. Order 359 (STP @ 4278.8, oca-protect-357) shares the target's OCA group,      so ocaType=1 should cancel it on the fill. If MGC is flat and 359 is STILL RESTING,      that is a naked SHORT-side exposure the moment anything re-enters -- escalate, do not      file quietly.

IF IT DID NOT FILL, that is the more informative outcome and must not be written off as a venue quirk: a marketable limit that does not fill at a liquid open means the order did not reach the book the way we believe it did, which reopens the placement path itself.

TIMING: CME gold (MGC) reopens Sunday 22:00 UTC; the first RTH open is Monday. Do not grade this over a closed venue -- 'no fill' while the market is shut is not an observation.

--- CONFIRMED 2026-08-18T07:0xZ: NO FILL, AND NO TARGET WAS EVER PLACED ---
Checked in this row's own prescribed order:
  1. /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper -> read_state 'orders_read' (a clean read, so this is evidence and not a could-not-look). Exactly 2 orders account-wide, BOTH STP, ZERO LMT:
       MES 338 STP SELL 15 @ 7516.5  oca-protect-336  GTC PreSubmitted
       MGC 359 STP SELL 105 @ 4278.8 oca-protect-357  GTC PreSubmitted
  2. /api/diag/exchange_positions?account_id=ib_paper -> MGC PRESENT, 105 long @ 4276.236. Not flat.
  3. Stop 359 still resting, as expected for a position that never closed.
  4. Venue: /api/diag/venue_session -> state 'open' ('tradingHours: inside 20260817 18:00-20260818 17:00 US/Eastern', tz_source zoneinfo). MGC last 4420.4 vs declared target 4297.66.

So this row's fourth resolution criterion fires verbatim: 'If no fill occurred at a genuinely open venue: the placement path is reopened as a defect, not recorded as expected behaviour.' It is reopened, and the defect is identified rather than merely suspected — the target was never placed at all, because attach-ib-target has never executed once (ImportError on every invocation). See BL-20260818-ATTACH-IB-TARGET-HAS-NEVER-RUN.

This row's own framing was right and is worth keeping: 'an attached target is a PLACED order, never a fill'. The failure went one step further back than it anticipated — not placed-but-unfilled, but never-placed. Trade 4487 has now been 122.74 points past its declared target for 11 days.

--- CLOSED AT THE VENUE 2026-08-18T07:49Z ---
The target was finally placed (order 381) and filled; MGC is absent from ib_paper's positions and stop 359 was cancelled by its OCA group — this row's third criterion ('stop 359 confirmed cancelled by its OCA group') is satisfied, and no naked-exposure escalation is needed. Remaining before this row can close: the journal side. Trade 4487 read status=open / pnl null immediately after the fill; it must reach status=closed with MEASURED pnl provenance from the exchange-fills store, which arrives on the hourly ict-ib-executions-pull timer. Do not close this row on the venue read alone — 'the position is flat' and 'the journal records the close honestly' are the two different facts this row was written to keep apart. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'confirmed_no_fill_placement_path_reopened' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
resolution_criteria: A confirmed clean read (read_state 'orders_read') showing ib_paper MGC flat, with the positions list [] rather than null.
Journal trade 4487 status=closed with a realized PnL whose provenance is MEASURED (exchange-fills store), or an explicit statement of why it is not.
Stop order 359 confirmed cancelled by its OCA group -- or, if still resting on a flat book, escalated as a fresh naked-exposure finding rather than closed here.
If no fill occurred at a genuinely open venue: the placement path is reopened as a defect, not recorded as expected behaviour.

A stop 6.4 points above entry on a long is a trail that moved into profit — correct, and the desired behaviour.
