items.title: ib_paper MES holds 30 contracts of STOP against a 15 long in TWO DISJOINT OCA groups -- either stop firing flattens the position and leaves the other resting, which SELLS AGAIN into a naked short
items.detail:
MEASURED, /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper at 2026-08-16T14:37:53Z, read_state 'orders_read' (a confirmed clean account-wide read, not a could-not-look). Position: MES 15 LONG @ 7630.872. Resting stops:
  order 338 -- STP SELL 15 @ 7516.50, oca_group 'oca-protect-336', client_id 497, GTC
  order 375 -- STP SELL 15 @ 7533.75, oca_group 'oca-protect-373', client_id 597, GTC
Total stop quantity 30 against a position of 15, in TWO SEPARATE OCA groups.

THE FAILURE IS NOT 'redundant protection'. ocaType=1 cancels the rest of the SAME group when one leg fills; it says nothing about a different group. So the sequence is: stop 375 fires -> sells 15 -> MES is FLAT -> order 338 is still resting -> it fires -> sells 15 more -> the account is SHORT 15 MES that no strategy asked for, with no stop of its own. The same shape as the stranded MGC market orders, reached by a different route.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT. `_check_broker_naked_ib_positions` asks whether coverage is SUFFICIENT; 30 >= 15 passes with room to spare. There is no upper bound anywhere on the IB path. Bybit already has the corresponding detector -- `_bybit_position_protection` emits a detect-only `over_covered` signal at >1.5x -- so this is a KNOWN class that was implemented for one venue and never ported to the other, not a novel discovery. That gap is the finding.

INTERACTION WITH THE TARGET ATTACH (ordering is load-bearing). A take-profit can only join ONE OCA group, so attaching it to oca-protect-373 leaves 338 outside and the naked-short path fully intact. `scripts/ops/attach_ib_target.py` already REFUSES when it sees more than one stop OCA group, and that refusal is correct -- the redundant stop must be cancelled first. Collapsing 30 -> 15 leaves the position exactly covered at every instant, so there is no window where MES is unprotected.

WHICH STOP IS THE STRAY is NOT yet established and must not be guessed: read the journal's declared stop_loss for the open MES trade and cancel the leg that does not match it. Cancelling either one is a protective cancel (`--force-protective` on cancel-ib-order) and is Tier-2.

=== ROOT CAUSE + RESOLUTION, added 2026-08-17 (from the superseded BL-20260817-IB-CLIENTID-ROTATION-DUPLICATES-PROTECTIVE-STOPS) ===
MECHANISM: 597 - 497 = 100 = IB_RECONNECT_CLIENTID_STRIDE **exactly**, and /api/diag/ib_state at 19:49Z showed live clients 497/498/9016 with 597 ABSENT. So 597 is an abandoned rotated session: the reconnect rotation (IB_RECONNECT_ROTATE_CLIENTID_AFTER, default 1) re-armed protection under the rotated id while the pre-rotation stop kept resting under the base id, in its own OCA group. Strong but not journal-confirmed — the remaining work is to find the rotation and the re-arm in the trader journal.

PROPOSED FIX (preferred over 'cancel the old leg'): have the re-arm REUSE the existing OCA group. That fails safe — even if a duplicate is placed, one firing cancels the other, so the reversal this row describes becomes impossible. Cancelling the old leg only works if the cancel succeeds; reusing the group is correct even when it does not.

RESOLVED ON THE LIVE ACCOUNT 2026-08-17 (the condition, not the code): order 375 was cancelled via cancel-ib-order (issues #9912 dry-run, #9913 apply) after PR #9892 made the two documented overrides reachable. Verified at 20:54:36Z by an independent /api/diag/ib_open_orders read: account count 3 -> 2, MES holds ONE stop, order 338 @ 7516.50, client 497.
WHY 375 AND NOT 338 (a scheduled note from the concurrent session proposed cancelling 338): the survivor must be owned by a LIVE clientId. IB binds amend to the submitting client, so a stop owned by the dead 597 session would have been FROZEN and un-trailable. Keeping 338 (client 497, the live trader) keeps the trailing logic working. Either choice clears attach_ib_target.py's >1-stop refusal.

--- VENUE STATE RE-MEASURED 2026-08-18T07:0xZ: THE DUPLICATE IS GONE ---
/api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper, read_state 'orders_read': MES now holds exactly ONE stop — order 338, STP SELL 15 @ 7516.50, oca-protect-336, GTC PreSubmitted — against a position of MES 15 long @ 7630.872. Order 375 (@ 7533.75, oca-protect-373) is ABSENT. Stop coverage is 15 against 15, i.e. 100%, no longer 200%. This is consistent with the cancel recorded on BL-20260817-CANCEL-IB-ORDER-VERIFY-WINDOW-TOO-SHORT, whose 'cancel_not_effective' verdict was a false negative on a cancel that did complete.

NOT CLOSED, deliberately. This row's criteria require an IB over-coverage DETECTOR mirroring Bybit's `over_covered` signal, plus a regression test pinning that stops in DISJOINT OCA groups are not treated as mutually cancelling. Neither exists. Closing on the cleared instance alone is exactly the 'a detector that never fires because the producing path was also fixed' failure this row warned against — and the producing path was never even identified. The hazard recurs the moment a second group is minted. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'instance_resolved_class_open' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.

--- RE-GRADED 2026-08-22: THE INSTANCE IS CLEARED; THE DETECTOR GAP IS NOT. ---
LIVE RE-READ 2026-08-22T19:0xZ, /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper, read_state 'orders_read', count 4 (a confirmed clean account-wide read, not a could-not-look):
  338  MES  STP SELL 15.0 @ aux 7516.5    oca-protect-336
  391  MGC  STP SELL 95.0 @ aux 4371.1    oca-protect-389
  398  MHG  LMT SELL 29.0 @ 7.1415        308977633
  399  MHG  STP SELL 29.0 @ aux 6.2215    308977633

MES now holds ONE stop, order 338, qty 15.0 against a position of 15.0. ORDER 375 IS GONE, so the 30-against-15 in two disjoint OCA groups this row describes is NO LONGER THE CURRENT STATE and the naked-short sequence it warns about cannot fire today. MHG is fully bracketed (LMT + STP in ONE oca group 308977633), which is the correct shape.

BUT THE FINDING WAS NEVER THE INSTANCE -- this row's own words are 'That gap is the finding.' VERIFIED IN CODE 2026-08-22, not inferred from this row's age: `_check_broker_naked_ib_positions`'s summary keys are checked / target_naked / partially_naked / ungradeable / read_failed / covered / errors / skipped -- there is NO `over_covered` key and no upper bound anywhere on the IB path, while Bybit's `_bybit_position_protection` still emits its detect-only `over_covered` at >1.5x (order_monitor.py:8076). The class remains implemented for one venue and not the other.

SEVERITY LOWERED critical -> high, and the reason is narrow: there is no live over-covered position right now, so there is no present naked-short exposure. The DETECTION gap is unchanged. RE-ESCALATE TO CRITICAL the moment any IB position is observed with total stop qty above its size -- and note that nothing would currently observe that, which is the point.

HOW THE INSTANCE CLEARED IS ITSELF EVIDENCE FOR THE GAP: the 2026-08-20 remediation cancelled the WRONG leg (see BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG -- confirmed live in the same read). Ad-hoc remediation without a detector cleared the quantity and left the position on a stop that does not match its declared level. That is what closing an instance without closing the class looks like.

--- DETECTOR PORTED 2026-08-22 (Tier-1, detect-only). Row KEPT OPEN on the live control. ---
`_check_broker_naked_ib_positions` now carries an UPPER bound. `_IB_OVERCOVER_FACTOR = 1.5`, a LITERAL beside `_BYBIT_OVERCOVER_FACTOR` and equal to it, so the two venues cannot be silently graded on different thresholds -- and a literal rather than an env knob because a var here would ship with no read surface (BL-20260813-ENV-VARS-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE) for no benefit.

IT GRADES BY OCA GROUP, NOT BY RATIO ALONE, and that is the part a blind port of the Bybit detector would have missed. ocaType=1 cancels the rest of the SAME group when a leg fills and says nothing about a different group, so:
  len(oca_groups) > 1  -> logger.ERROR, naming the groups and the naked-short sequence (stop A fires -> flat -> stop B still resting -> fires -> SHORT with no stop)
  len(oca_groups) == 1 -> logger.WARNING: self-limiting, but not the shape place_protective creates -- worth a look
One alarm shouting equally at both would be the desensitised-alarm P1.

It reads stop_qty, NOT covered_qty: `covered_qty` counts a stop and a target as interchangeable, and only resting STOPS drive the naked-short sequence -- a target that fills does not leave the account short.

DETECT-ONLY, enforced by a test that strips string literals and comments via tokenize before checking for calls to cancel_order / place_protective / _attempt_naked_autoprotect / modify_open_order. (The first draft of that test asserted over raw text and tripped on the detector's OWN log message, 'not the shape place_protective creates' -- a name-match producing a false finding on a behavioural question. A second guard test proves the stripper actually strips, so it cannot silently no-op into a vacuous pass.)

`over_covered` is declared in the summary initialiser, and a test calls the sweep and asserts the key survives the early-return paths -- declared is not the same as reachable.

VERIFICATION: 8 of 9 tests fail against origin/main and all 9 pass with the detector; the one that passes pre-fix is the two-venues-same-threshold check, which compares constants. 72 tests pass across the IB/Alpaca/Bybit protection suites with no regression. Falsified by checking out origin/main's file and asserting _IB_OVERCOVER_FACTOR genuinely absent first. ruff clean.

WHY STILL OPEN: the detector has never fired on a real over-cover, because there is no live over-covered position (verified 2026-08-22: MES/MGC/MHG all at exactly position-size coverage). It is unit-verified only. The honest control is a planted or naturally-occurring over-cover producing the ERROR line with the group set named.
items.resolution_criteria: `_check_broker_naked_ib_positions` reports an over-coverage count in its summary, demonstrated to fire on a planted control (a position with stop qty above its size) and to stay silent on the current live book, where MES/MGC/MHG all sit at exactly position-size coverage. The detector must be DETECT-ONLY: it must not cancel a leg. Closing this row on 'the MES over-cover is gone' does NOT satisfy it -- that is the instance, and the row says the gap is the finding.

updates.note: RE-VERIFIED, and the instance is gone -- but DO NOT CLOSE THIS ROW, on two counts. MEASURED 2026-08-20T20:23:39Z via /api/diag/ib_open_orders (read_state 'orders_read', a confirmed clean account-wide read) + /api/diag/exchange_positions?account_id=ib_paper + /api/bot/positions?include_paper=true. All three ib_paper positions now hold stop coverage of EXACTLY 1.00x in EXACTLY ONE OCA group: MGC 95 long / STP 95 (oca-protect-389); MHG 29 long / STP 29 + LMT 29 (oca 308977633); MES 15 long / STP 15 (oca-protect-336). No over-cover and no disjoint groups anywhere on the account. This independently confirms the venue_recheck_2026_08_18 already recorded in this row's evidence. (1) CRITERIA 3 AND 4 ARE STILL OPEN -- the IB over-coverage detector and the regression test pinning that DISJOINT OCA groups are not mutually cancelling. Those are the CLASS half, and the row's own text says the venue-specific detector for a venue-independent failure IS the finding. Both are now implemented in scripts/ops/broker_bracket_reconcile.py (stop_over_cover + stop_disjoint_oca, with tests that plant the historical 30-vs-15 two-group state and assert both fire); the row can close when that lands. (2) FAR MORE IMPORTANT -- THE REMEDIATION CANCELLED THE WRONG LEG. Criterion 1 of this row says: 'read the journal's declared stop_loss for the open MES trade and cancel the leg that does not match it.' The journal declares stop_loss 7533.696429 for the open MES trade 4350. This row records order 375 at 7533.75 -- one MES tick (0.25) from the declared level -- and order 338 at 7516.5, which is 69 ticks away. Order 375 was cancelled and 338 kept. So the leg that MATCHED the journal was removed and the stray survived, which is the precise outcome criterion 1 existed to prevent. Filed separately as BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG because the remaining exposure is a live Tier-2 repair, not a detector gap.

RESOLVED, VERIFIED AT THE BROKER 2026-08-23 (/api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper, read_state='orders_read', 6 orders total). The row recorded ib_paper MES holding 30 contracts of STOP against a 15 long in TWO DISJOINT OCA groups, where either stop firing would flatten the position twice. Today MES holds exactly ONE group, oca-protect-408, containing STP 7533.75 qty 15.0 and LMT 8390.50 qty 15.0 — 15 of stop against a 15 long, correctly paired, no second group.

CAUSE OF THE FIX, so it is not read as spontaneous: the protection re-assert ran on this position today to correct a diverged stop (7516.5 -> 7533.75), and IBClient.modify_protective re-arms through place_protective, whose Step-1 pre-cancel removes the resting protective legs before minting the fresh pair. That pre-cancel is what collapsed the two disjoint groups into one. The over-cover was repaired as a SIDE EFFECT of a different repair — worth stating plainly, because nothing was aimed at this row and a future reader should not conclude a dedicated fix exists.

⚠️ SO THE CLASS IS NOT CLOSED, only this instance. Nothing DETECTS over-cover: the sweep grades a covered QUANTITY and the 444.7% over-coverage case is cited in CLAUDE.md as a sub-class C example (an unasserted denominator reading as clean). If the same accumulation recurs it will again be invisible until someone reads the raw orders. That detection gap is separate work and is not claimed here.

updates.by: claude (system-review fix round, MHG over-cover apply)
updates.note:
DETECTOR EXERCISED ON A REAL OVER-COVER 2026-08-25 -- this row's own next_action ('observe the detector fire once on a real or planted over-cover') is now MET, and the ROOT CAUSE it never had is filed.

THE PAGE FIRED. The stop-over-cover CRITICAL page (PR #10259, deployed d4bf2648 at ~12:20Z) emitted at 2026-08-25T12:27:44Z, one sweep after deploy: 'ib_stop_over_cover detected: ib_paper/MHG: position 29.0 but resting STOP qty totals 58.0 (200%) across 2 DISJOINT OCA groups [oca-protect-416, oca-protect-432]'. Verified in /api/bot/logs?level=error, latch file runtime_logs/stop_over_cover_alert_state.json = {'ib_paper|MHG': 1787660864.72}. Note the SYMBOL: this row was measured on MES, so the class recurred on a different instrument, which is what the row meant by 'the gap is the finding'.

ROOT CAUSE, caught in the journal rather than inferred -- filed as BL-20260825-PLACE-PROTECTIVE-COUNTS-THE-CANCEL-CALL-NOT-ITS-EFFECT. At 14:52:34Z place_protective's pre-cancel issued cancelOrder on all four resting MHG legs; IBKR refused the two owned by the retired clientId 497 with 'Error 10147 ... OrderId 417 that needs to be cancelled is not found'; ib_insync's cancelOrder returns None and never raises, _cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol increments `cancelled` on the CALL, and place_protective discards the return value entirely -- so it armed a fresh bracket in a THIRD group (oca-protect-440) and reported legs_placed 2 / retMsg OK. Measured at 14:56:17Z (read_state 'orders_read'): 87 lots of stop against a 29-lot position, 300%.

SO THE 2026-08-17 PROPOSAL IN THIS ROW WAS RIGHT AND IS STILL NOT IMPLEMENTED. This row said: 'PROPOSED FIX (preferred over cancel the old leg): have the re-arm REUSE the existing OCA group. That fails safe ... Cancelling the old leg only works if the cancel succeeds; reusing the group is correct even when it does not.' That is exactly the failure now measured. Today exactly ONE of the two place_protective call sites passes oca_key (order_monitor:6950, naked autoprotect); execute.py:2536 -- the trailing-amend path that produced all three groups -- passes none.

NOT RE-OPENING THIS ROW, deliberately. Its resolution_criteria is the DETECTOR and the detector is real, shipped, and has now fired on live state. Re-opening it to carry the producer would merge a detection gap and an order-path defect into one row, which is how the 08-16/08-17 triplicate happened. The producer is its own row, at its own tier.

items.next_action: DONE for the detector (Tier-1, shipped 2026-08-22). What remains is the control: observe the detector fire once on a real or planted over-cover. Do NOT extend it to cancel a leg -- choosing which leg to cancel is what went wrong on 2026-08-20, and the remedy for the surviving stray is BL-20260820's own Tier-2 next_action.

items.title: The IB one-sided-coverage fix does NOT generalise: the Alpaca sweep and the Bybit sweep are both stop-only, and bybit_bracket_audit.py COLLECTS the target side but never lets it reach the verdict -- so it prints PROTECTED over a target-naked position
items.detail:
SCOPE CHECK after fixing the IB half: do the other two venue sweeps share the blind spot that left both ib_paper positions target-naked? They do. Read from the code, not inferred from the IB case.

ALPACA -- `order_monitor._check_broker_naked_equity_positions` decides on `protected = client.has_protective_orders(symbol)` then `if protected is None or protected: continue`. `AlpacaClient.has_protective_orders` returns True on the FIRST leg matching `"stop" in otype or otype == "limit"` -- one membership test over both sides, the exact shape just removed from IB's coverage path. A stop-only Alpaca position answers 'protected', the sweep skips it, the missing take-profit is invisible. The IB fix deliberately did NOT touch IB's own `has_protective_orders`, which keeps the combined test legitimately because the IB sweep consumes `protection_coverage` instead. Alpaca has no coverage function -- the boolean IS the decision.

BYBIT -- `_bybit_position_protection` is stop-only BY CONSTRUCTION: it reads `pos["stopLoss"]` and sums SL legs into `covered_qty` (`sl_leg_ids`, `unknown_qty_sl_legs`, `source: partial_sl_legs`), and never touches `takeProfit`. So the live sweep cannot fire on target-nakedness.

CORRECTION -- AN EARLIER VERSION OF THIS ROW CLAIMED BYBIT TARGET-NAKEDNESS WAS 'PRESENTLY UNMEASURABLE'. THAT WAS WRONG, and the impossibility-claim-guard caught it before merge (the row asserted an impossibility with no `checked:` annotation naming what was searched). What the check actually found:
  checked: src/runtime/order_monitor.py:6928 -- `get_open_orders` IS called in-process.
  checked: src/units/accounts/execute.py:2256 -- and again by `_bybit_open_missing_sl_leg`.
  checked: scripts/ops/bybit_bracket_audit.py -- a Tier-1 `bybit-bracket-audit` system action exists, is read-only by construction (`get_positions` + `get_open_orders` only), and ALREADY collects `tp_legs` (line 197/199) and `position_takeProfit` (line 159/165).
So the Bybit target side is MEASURABLE ON DEMAND today. The capability is not missing.

THE REAL DEFECT IS SHARPER THAN THE ONE I FIRST FILED. `bybit_bracket_audit.py` collects the target side and then never lets it reach the verdict: `PROTECTED` / `PARTIALLY_NAKED` / `NAKED` is computed from SL coverage ALONE (lines 218-222), and `tp_legs` appears only in the printed detail (lines 406/414). A Bybit position holding a full stop and ZERO take-profit legs is therefore graded **PROTECTED** by the one tool built to answer 'is every open Bybit trade actually protected at the broker right now?'.

That is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT, sub-class A (semantic substitution): the label names the quantity 'this position is protected'; the code computed 'this position is stop-covered'; the two are not the same, and nothing in the output reveals the substitution. It is worse than a silent gap, because a reader who runs the audit gets an explicit green over the exact condition they were checking for. The data needed to be right is already in the same dict.

WHAT IS STILL NOT CLAIMED: that any Alpaca or Bybit position IS currently target-naked. That was measured for ib_paper (zero limit orders account-wide) and is UNMEASURED here -- and now that the tool is known to exist, measuring it is a cheap Tier-1 run rather than a research project. Do not let the IB measurement stand in for the other two venues. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'bybit_measured_clean_alpaca_unmeasurable_13_positions' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
resolution_criteria: An Alpaca counterpart to bybit_bracket_audit.py (read-only, alpaca_client_for + _open_orders_for_symbol), so the 13 measured positions can be graded at all -- this is the blocking step for the Alpaca half.
With it: a measurement, stated with its population, of how many of those 13 hold a stop and no take-profit. alpaca_live must be reported as could_not_look, never folded in as zero.

Alpaca's naked sweep decides on a two-sided grade rather than the any-leg boolean; if has_protective_orders is kept, its docstring must forbid naked-detection use the way IB's now does, and the sweep must call something else.

bybit_bracket_audit.py's verdict accounts for the target side it already collects: a stop-only book must NOT print PROTECTED. Either the verdict becomes two-sided or the label narrows to what it computed (e.g. SL_COVERED).
Bybit's live protection state reports the target side explicitly (even as a separate field), so 'we did not grade it' is distinguishable from 'it is covered'.
A test per venue pinning that a STOP-ONLY book does NOT read as protected -- the single assertion that would have caught IB, Alpaca, Bybit and the audit tool alike.

notes.note:
[MEASURED — THE BYBIT HALF IS REFUTED] Ran the Tier-1 `bybit-bracket-audit` (issue #9725, run 31953868225, 14:50:39Z), which resolution-criterion 1 asked for. RESULT: NO Bybit position is target-naked. Population: 5 non-flat symbols across 4 accounts (bybit_1 ADAUSDT + XRPUSDT, bybit_2 XRPUSDT, bybit_portfolio ETHUSDT + XRPUSDT). EVERY one carries at least one TP leg -- ADAUSDT 2 SL + 2 TP, the other four 1 SL + 1 TP each. So the condition measured on ib_paper (zero limit orders account-wide) does NOT reproduce on Bybit, and the row's refusal to carry the IB measurement across was the right call.

WHAT SURVIVES is strictly the DETECTOR finding, unchanged and still worth fixing: `_bybit_position_protection` is stop-only, so the live sweep could not have told us this, and `bybit_bracket_audit.py`'s verdict still ignores the `tp_legs` it collects. Today those would print PROTECTED over a target-naked book; today there is no target-naked book to print it over. A detector that is only correct because the failure is currently absent is not a working detector -- but the severity of the OPEN condition drops, so this is a latent-gap row, not a live-exposure row.

ALPACA REMAINS UNMEASURED -- no live Alpaca position appeared in this audit (it is Bybit-only by construction), so do not read '5/5 clean' as covering it.

[ALPACA HALF — THE GAP IS NOW QUANTIFIED, AND IT IS THE BIGGEST OF THE THREE VENUES] /api/diag/exchange_positions at 2026-08-16T14:55:34Z (issue #9728) gives the denominator that was missing:
  alpaca_paper      6 positions -- GLD 7L, IEF 141S, IWM 124L, QQQ 24L, SPY 11L, TLT 938S
  alpaca_portfolio  7 positions -- GLD 39L, IEF 152S, IWM 187L, QQQ 3L, SLV 26L, SPY 29L, TLT 1042S
  alpaca_options_paper  [] -- genuinely flat (count 0, NOT null)
  alpaca_live       null -- could_not_look, NOT flat (consistent with the known BL-20260813-ALPACA-BALANCE-NONE-WHILE-ACCOUNT-READS-ACTIVE); its position count is unknown and must not be recorded as zero.
So **13 live Alpaca positions** have a target-side protection state that NO sweep grades and NO external surface can read -- against 2 on ib_paper, where the same class was found live. That is 6.5x the population of the venue that produced the incident.

IS IT MEASURABLE? Checked properly this time, after getting the Bybit answer wrong:
  checked: src/units/accounts/alpaca_client.py:767 -- `_open_orders_for_symbol` EXISTS, so the in-process capability is there (it is what `has_protective_orders` already calls).
  checked: scripts/ops/*.py -- the only alpaca-touching ops scripts are `flatten_alpaca_position.py` (a MUTATION), plus backfill/supersede jobs. There is NO alpaca counterpart to `bybit_bracket_audit.py`.
  checked: scripts/ops/bybit_bracket_audit.py:334,357 -- it resolves clients via `bybit_client_for`, so it is bybit-only BY CONSTRUCTION and cannot be pointed at Alpaca.
  checked: src/web/api/routers/diag.py -- the only alpaca surface is `broker_account_status`, which serves authorization FLAGS and lists no orders.
  checked: docs/research/RESEARCH-CAPABILITY-INDEX.md -- no alpaca entry.
CONCLUSION, stated precisely: the capability exists in-process; there is no read surface and no audit tool, so a session cannot measure it TODAY. This is NOT the claim I wrongly made about Bybit -- there the tool already existed and I had not looked. The remedy is cheap and known: mirror bybit_bracket_audit.py against `alpaca_client_for` + `_open_orders_for_symbol`, which also lets the Alpaca sweep stop deciding on the any-leg boolean.

updates.note:
RE-VALIDATED AGAINST THE CODE, not the merge log. This row named THREE sites; two have moved and one has not, and the title is now wrong in a way worth stating: target nakedness is no longer UNDETECTABLE on Bybit, it is UNDETECTED.

1. ALPACA SWEEP — FIXED. `_check_broker_naked_equity_positions` now calls `AlpacaClient.protection_state` (order_monitor.py:7183), which grades the sides SEPARATELY, and the summary carries its own `target_naked` counter. The docstring names the trap explicitly: not the boolean `has_protective_orders`, 'which answers True for a stop-only book'. That is exactly what this row asked for.

2. bybit_bracket_audit.py — LABELLED, NOT GRADED, and that is a legitimate disposition rather than a half-fix. It still computes PROTECTED / PARTIALLY_NAKED / NAKED from the STOP side alone, but now stamps `verdict_scope: "stop_side_only"` beside it, with the reason recorded in-line. So it no longer prints a verdict that READS as a claim about the whole bracket while being about half of it. The `tp_legs` it always collected are still collected and still do not reach the verdict — deliberately, now that the scope is declared.

3. `_bybit_position_protection` — UNCHANGED, and it is the LIVE path. Measured by reading the function (123 lines): ZERO occurrences of takeProfit / take_profit / tp_leg / target / TakeProfit. Control on the same probe over the same body — stopLoss 3, sl_leg_ids 4, covered_qty 5 — so the zero is a real absence and not a probe that cannot find anything. The live Bybit sweep therefore still cannot fire on target nakedness.

WHAT CHANGED TODAY, and why the title needs re-wording: /api/diag/bybit_open_orders (shipped 2026-08-22) serves the position-level `take_profit` AND the resting target legs from BOTH the StopOrder and Order filters, and /api/diag/alpaca_open_orders (this session) does the same for Alpaca. So the target side is now READABLE ON DEMAND on all three venues. The remaining gap is that nothing GRADES it live on Bybit — a different and smaller claim than 'undetectable', and the distinction matters because a reader who takes the title at face value will not think to look.

REMAINING WORK: give `_bybit_position_protection` a target axis the way `IBClient.protection_coverage` got one (`stop_qty` / `target_qty` beside the back-compat `covered_qty`), and have the Bybit sweep alert on target-naked WITHOUT re-arming — the same asymmetry the IB side settled on, because placing a target is decision-time geometry read from trades.take_profit_1, not a safety re-arm to be done blind on a sweep. That is a Tier-2 change to the ENFORCING path and is not proposed here; this update establishes the scope, not the patch.

items.title: bybit_portfolio ETHUSDT: journal holds 35.01 against an exchange position of 21.05 with trade #4547's SL leg DEAD -- 13.96 of journal qty is unbacked and unprotected, and the audit ROLL-UP prints '0 naked' over it
items.detail:
MEASURED by `bybit-bracket-audit` (issue #9725, run 31953868225, 2026-08-16T14:50:39Z) -- read-only, `get_positions` + `get_open_orders` only.

  bybit_portfolio ETHUSDT -- exchange position size 21.05 Sell, ONE SL leg (21.05 @ 1979.25, id 88c75ff7-1fd) and one TP leg.
  Journal: TWO open rows summing 35.01.
    #4135 eth_pullback_2h        short 21.05  journal_sl=1979.25357143  leg=ALIVE 88c75ff7-1fd
    #4547 trend_donchian_eth_4h  short 13.96  journal_sl=1916.51928571  leg=DEAD  96fbd128-d1e
  Arithmetic: 21.05 + 13.96 = 35.01, and the exchange size equals #4135's qty EXACTLY. So #4547's entire 13.96 is unbacked by any exchange position, and its tracked stop leg is confirmed dead at the broker.

TWO SEPARATE PROBLEMS IN ONE ROW. (a) A journal row claiming 13.96 of live short exposure that the exchange does not hold -- the `journal_qty_divergent` class, which `_bybit_position_protection` emits as DETECT-ONLY and nothing remediates. (b) That row's protective leg is DEAD, so if the position WERE real it would be unprotected; the netted book hides which of the two is true from every aggregate.

AND THE ROLL-UP SAID IT WAS FINE. The audit's summary line reads: '5/5 audited non-flat symbol(s) SL-covered at the broker within [100%, 100.5%]; 0 naked, 0 over-covered.' That is TRUE and it is measured against the EXCHANGE size (21.05/21.05 = 100%), which is the right denominator for 'is the venue position covered'. It is the wrong denominator for 'is every journal row backed and protected', and the roll-up does not say which question it answered. The dead leg and the 13.96 discrepancy appear only in the per-symbol detail a reader has to scroll past the green summary to reach.

This is the SECOND unprovenanced-summary defect in the same tool, found in the same run as the `tp_legs`-ignored-by-the-verdict one (BL-20260816-TARGET-NAKEDNESS-UNDETECTABLE-ON-ALPACA-AND-BYBIT). Both have the same shape: the tool COLLECTS the disqualifying evidence and the headline verdict does not consult it.

--- ROOT CAUSE IDENTIFIED 2026-08-18: this is a SYMPTOM of the multi-leg strand ---
This row asked whether #4547 is a phantom row or a real position the exchange lost. It is neither, and the answer generalises: BOTH open bybit_portfolio ETH rows are STRANDED SIBLING LEGS of order packages that were already flipped to `closed` when their `linked_trade_id` leg closed.
  #4547 -> pkg-0b2900a5c90d4f08, status closed (close_reason reconciler_filled), linked_trade_id 4546
  #4135 -> pkg-e6eac664c2a446a6, status closed (close_reason sl_cross),          linked_trade_id 4134
Because `order_monitor`'s loop selects `status="open"` packages, neither row can ever be revisited: the journal keeps claiming their qty while the netted exchange position reflects only what actually remains. The 35.01-vs-21.05 arithmetic this row measured is exactly 13.96 of stranded #4547 on top of #4135's real 21.05, and #4547's stop leg is dead because the close that killed the package also cancelled its own tracked leg.

So the remedy is not a per-row cleanup — a cleanup here fixes two rows and the mechanism reproduces on the next multi-account close. See BL-20260818-MONITOR-MANAGES-ONLY-THE-LINKED-LEG, which measured 6 such stranded rows across 5 packages on 35 open trades. This row's own criteria (establish phantom-vs-real; stop the roll-up printing an unqualified '0 naked') remain valid and are unaffected.
resolution_criteria: Establish whether #4547 is a phantom row (never really opened / already closed at the venue and not reconciled) or a real position the exchange lost -- from the fills store and order_packages, not by assuming the netted size tells you.
If phantom: close/supersede it with the correct provenance so it stops counting as live exposure in every aggregate that sums journal position_size.

The audit roll-up must not print an unqualified '0 naked' when any audited symbol has a DEAD tracked leg or a journal-vs-exchange qty divergence -- either surface a count in the summary or state the denominator the verdict used.
Confirm whether the detect-only `journal_qty_divergent` signal actually fired for this symbol; if it did and nothing surfaced it, that silence is its own finding.

progress.note: INSTANCE FULLY RESOLVED BY TURNOVER; THE CLASS IS UNTOUCHED, AND SEVERITY STAYS high FOR THE CLASS. Measured 2026-08-23T16:5xZ, three independent reads. The book turned over completely - #4135 and #4547 are both gone and the account is now LONG, not short - so this is turnover, NOT a repair, and nothing here is evidence that anything was fixed. (1) /api/diag/exchange_positions?account_id=bybit_portfolio -> ETHUSDT Buy 10.0 (a real list, so a confirmed clean read, not a null). (2) /api/bot/positions?include_paper=true -> two open journal rows, #4923 eth_pullback_2h 2.24 and #4905 trend_donchian_eth_4h 7.76. 2.24 + 7.76 = 10.00 against an exchange size of 10.0 - EXACT. The `journal_qty_divergent` condition (a) is absent: zero unbacked journal qty. (3) /api/diag/bybit_open_orders?account_id=bybit_portfolio -> read_state `orders_read`, FOUR Partial legs, one SL and one TP per journal row: SL 2309.79 / TP 2687.53 at qty 2.24, and SL 2339.08 / TP 2766.83 at qty 7.76. SL coverage 10.00/10.0 and TP coverage 10.00/10.0 - two-sided and complete, so condition (b), the dead SL leg, is absent too. ALSO CHECKED THE AXIS COVERAGE CANNOT SEE: the resting PRICES agree with the journal declarations to the tick (journal 2309.78571429 -> venue 2309.79; 2339.07571429 -> 2339.08; 2687.52757 -> 2687.53; 2766.83141 -> 2766.83). That is the BL-20260820-PROTECTION-COVERAGE-IS-PRICE-BLIND axis, done by hand because no automated surface grades it. WHY THIS DOES NOT CLOSE THE ROW. The row names two problems and the second is a ROLL-UP DENOMINATOR defect: the audit's headline is measured against the EXCHANGE size and does not state which question it answered, so an unbacked journal row still prints as '0 naked'. That defect is unchanged - it simply has nothing to hide right now. Severity tracks the CLASS, not the instance: the next divergence will be summarised exactly the same way, and a reader would again have to scroll past a green headline to find it.

updates.note: Re-validated against live positions: bybit_portfolio now holds TWO ETHUSDT journal rows (2.24 eth_pullback_2h + 7.76 trend_donchian_eth_4h = 10.00) against the netted exchange position. The specific 35.01-vs-21.05 divergence this row records is not the current state, but unbacked journal qty under netting is the standing condition (BL-20260801). Re-measure before closing.

items.title: IB ACCEPTS cancelOrder (retCode 0 'OK') and the order does NOT go away -- it moves to PendingCancel and stays there while the venue is shut; measured on order 6, and it is the same state order 378 has been stuck in for ~2.5h
items.detail:
MEASURED, `cancel-ib-order` APPLY on ib_paper order 6 (issue #9731, run 31954321054, 2026-08-16T15:00:12Z), after a clean dry run (#9729) in which `lookup_state: found`, `owner_client_id: 9974`, and NEITHER safety guard tripped.

  cancel_response: {retCode: 0, retMsg: 'OK', result: {orderId: '6'}}   <- IB ACCEPTED it
  orders_on_account: 5   ->   orders_on_account_after: 5                <- nothing left
  order 6 status: PreSubmitted -> **PendingCancel**, still 105 remaining
  script verdict: action='cancel_not_effective', verify_state='still_present', exit 1

THE CAPABILITY IS NOT THE PROBLEM. Every layer built for this worked: the workflow forwarded the parameters (the #9723 fix, confirmed live), the account-wide lookup FOUND the order, the protective/clientId guards correctly declined to trip, and the script connected as the owning clientId 9974 and issued the cancel. The script also refused to call an accepted-but-uneffective cancel a success -- it verified the post-state, saw the order still resting, and exited 1. That is the IB_PLACE_CONFIRM_S / IB_CLOSE_CONFIRM_S lesson (an ACCEPT is not an OUTCOME) applied correctly on a third path, and it is why this is a finding rather than a silent no-op reported as done.

IT REPRODUCES, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT A CLASS AND NOT AN ODDITY. Order 378 (MGC, MKT SELL 105, client 9927) has been sitting in PendingCancel since ~12:33Z -- roughly 2.5 hours -- after an earlier flatten attempt. Order 6 has now entered the SAME state by the SAME route. Two for two.

LEADING HYPOTHESIS, NOT YET PROVEN: COMEX is CLOSED (Saturday 15:00Z; the reopen is Sunday 22:00Z). A cancel of a resting DAY order at a shut venue appears to be queued by IB and only completed when the session reopens, so PendingCancel is the honest intermediate state rather than a wedge. This is a HYPOTHESIS: it explains both observations and the timing, but it has not been confirmed against IBKR documentation or by observing a reopen, and the alternative -- that these cancels are genuinely stuck and will still be pending after the reopen -- is not excluded. Do NOT record it as fact until a reopen has been observed.

OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE SHARP END. Both stray MKT SELL 105 orders are DAY orders that ACTIVATE at the COMEX reopen, and both now carry a cancel that the venue has not yet honoured. At the reopen there is a RACE between the queued cancel and the order becoming eligible to fill. If a stray fills, it flattens the 105-contract long by itself; if it fills AFTER anything else has flattened the position, it opens a naked 105-contract SHORT. This directly gates the pending decision to attach MGC 4487's declared take-profit (4297.66, deeply marketable against a ~4398.70 market), because that target would ALSO execute at the reopen -- so target, stop, and two stray market sells would all become live in the same instant, and `attach_ib_target.py` already refuses while a non-protective order rests on the symbol, which is exactly the right refusal here.

DO NOT RETRY THE CANCEL ON A LOOP. Re-issuing against an order already in PendingCancel adds nothing and is the churn class IB_CLOSE_RETRY_COOLDOWN_S exists to prevent.

=== NEW OBSERVATION 2026-08-17: PendingCancel RESOLVES ON AN OPEN VENUE, so 'venue closed' is NOT NECESSARY for the pending state ===
Measured on ib_paper MES order 375 (perm 166865400, clientId 597), issue #9913 APPLY at ~20:50Z:
  cancel_response {retCode 0, OK} -> action 'cancel_not_effective', verify_state 'still_present', order in PendingCancel, exit 1 — the SAME signature this row documents for order 6.
  BUT an independent /api/diag/ib_open_orders read at 20:54:36Z showed the order GONE (account count 3 -> 2). It completed in roughly FOUR MINUTES.

THE VENUE WAS OPEN, verified two ways: /api/diag/venue_session graded MES state=open on tradingHours earlier the same day, and 20:50Z is 15:50 US/Central, inside the 17:00-16:00 CT session this contract reported.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SHOW. It does NOT refute the venue-closed explanation for orders 6 and 378 — those were MGC MKT orders fired into a genuinely shut COMEX, which is a different circumstance. What it DOES show is that accepted-then-PendingCancel-then-completes happens on a fully open venue too, so a closed venue cannot be the whole mechanism, and this row's title should not be read as settled. A plausible common factor is that BOTH cancels were issued as a clientId whose original session no longer exists (9974 there, 597 here).

OPERATIONAL COROLLARY: the exit-1 verdict is correct-at-the-instant and misleading as a FINAL answer. See BL-20260817-CANCEL-IB-ORDER-VERIFY-WINDOW-TOO-SHORT — 'still_present' conflates 'the broker refused' with 'the broker accepted and is working on it', and the red FAILED is what provokes a blind retry. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'resolved_on_account_mechanism_refuted_latency_stands' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
resolution_criteria: Observe the COMEX reopen (Sunday 22:00Z) and record what happens to orders 6 and 378: cancelled (hypothesis confirmed), still PendingCancel (hypothesis refuted, genuinely stuck — escalate), or FILLED (worst case — check immediately whether a naked short was opened).

Confirm or refute the venue-closed hypothesis against IBKR's own documented behaviour for cancelling a resting DAY order outside session hours, so the next session does not re-derive it from two observations.

If the cancels do complete at the reopen: document the expected latency so a future PendingCancel is not misread as a wedge, and give cancel_ib_order.py a way to say 'accepted, pending at venue' distinctly from 'not effective' — today both land as cancel_not_effective/exit 1, which collapses 'the venue has not got to it yet' into 'this failed'.
If they do NOT complete: this becomes a stuck-order-path finding needing a different remedy, and the naked-short exposure at every subsequent session open must be reassessed.

Separately: the ib_insync teardown emits `RuntimeError: Event loop is closed` from IB.__del__ after a successful run. Cosmetic here, but it prints a traceback on a clean path and could mask a real error in a future one.

updates.note:
[RESOLVED ON THE ACCOUNT — and the ID NOW OVERSTATES THE CAUSE, read this before citing it] THE OBSERVATION this row was opened to get. /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper at 2026-08-17T22:21:17Z, read_state 'orders_read' (a confirmed clean read), ~21 min after the 22:00Z COMEX reopen: **orders 6 and 378 are GONE**. Account count 5 -> 2 (only MES 338 and MGC 359 remain). Of the three possible outcomes this row enumerated -- cancelled / still PendingCancel / FILLED -- it is the first. Critically it is NOT the third: exchange_positions at 22:21:23Z shows MGC still 105 LONG @ 4276.236 and MES still 15 LONG @ 7630.872, both entries unchanged, so neither stray MKT SELL 105 filled and NO naked short was opened.

THE MECHANISM IN THE TITLE IS WRONG, AND A CONCURRENT SESSION IS WHY WE KNOW. session_0154PgZ9JcksQQiJfXuaqZfu (board #6927, 21:45Z) cancelled MES order 375 at ~20:50Z and got the IDENTICAL signature -- retCode 0 -> cancel_not_effective / still_present / PendingCancel / exit 1 -- which then completed in ~4 MINUTES on a venue their own /api/diag/venue_session graded `open` (20:50Z = 15:50 CT, inside the 17:00-16:00 CT session). So a shut venue is NOT NECESSARY for the PendingCancel state, and the hypothesis as filed is REFUTED as a mechanism.

THE TWO-PART READING that fits all three orders, which neither session could have reached alone:
  (a) WHAT CAUSES PendingCancel -- issuing the cancel as a clientId whose ORIGINAL SESSION NO LONGER EXISTS. True of all three: 9974 (order 6), 9927 (378), 597 (375, an abandoned rotated session -- ib_state showed 497/498/9016 live, 597 absent). Not the venue.
  (b) WHAT SETS HOW LONG IT STAYS PENDING -- the venue. Open: ~4 min (375). Closed: parked until the session reopens (6 issued 15:00Z Sat, 378 ~12:33Z Sat, both cleared by the 22:00Z Sun reopen).
So venue-closed survives as the LATENCY explanation and is discarded as the MECHANISM. STILL A HYPOTHESIS on (a): three observations sharing a dead-clientId cancel is a strong common factor, not a proven cause -- nobody has yet cancelled as a LIVE clientId and shown it completes synchronously, which is the experiment that would settle it.

THE ID IS LEFT UNCHANGED DELIBERATELY. Renaming it would break the citations already in the sprint log, the ROADMAP row and two board comments, and a row whose title records a refuted premise -- with the refutation attached -- is more honest than one quietly re-scoped to match the answer. Cite it with this caveat.

items.title: _TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT = 0.099 has no single owner: declared in 5 modules and hardcoded again in the sweeps, and the NAME doubles as a source-text detector for 'does this family clamp?'
items.source: Found while flipping --tp-cap-pct to live parity (operator Tier-3 decision 2026-08-16). The flip needed a constant to default to, and there was no single owner to import it from.
items.why_it_matters: position_telemetry computes cap_r/pct_of_cap from its own copy; if the live units' copy moves and it does not, every telemetry-derived ceiling is measured against a different ceiling than the one actually applied to orders, silently. ⚠️ THE CONSOLIDATION IS NOT A SIMPLE DEDUPE, and this is the part a naive fix breaks: the NAME is load-bearing as a MARKER, not only as a value. scripts/ops/lever_reachability_audit.py:120 resolves 'does this leg's builder unit clamp?' by `if "_TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT" in path.read_text()`; tests/test_exit_head_round_geometry_stamp.py:113,117 assert the name is PRESENT in trend_donchian.py and ABSENT in ict_scalp.py; tests/test_m20_fleet_capital_report.py:819 does the same. Four further tests regex the numeric literal out of the unit files (test_target_expectation.py:97, test_lever_reachability_audit.py:220, test_position_telemetry.py:211, test_m20_ladder_headroom.py:125), and an `from ... import` would match none of them.
items.resolution_criteria: One module owns the value and every other site imports it, AND the 'which families clamp?' question is answered by a declared registry rather than by grepping a constant name out of source text. Evidence: (a) exactly one `= 0.099` assignment remains in the tree, verified by grep; (b) lever_reachability_audit and m20_fleet_exit_sweep resolve the cap and the clamping-family set from that owner, with m20_fleet_exit_sweep's 'no single owner to import FROM' comment deleted because it is no longer true; (c) the four literal-regex tests and the three name-presence assertions either still pass or are deliberately rewritten against the new owner in the same change, with the rewrite justified per test -- silently deleting a presence-assertion to make the refactor pass is NOT a valid close, since those assertions are the only thing standing between this and a family being silently mis-graded; (d) a guard or test binds the sweeps' value to the live one, closing the 'nothing checks this' gap the sweep's own comment names.
items.next_action: Decide the owner: either a small shared module both `src/` and `scripts/` may import (check layer-guard allows the direction) or a text-comparison guard in scripts/ci/. The guard is the cheaper option and does not require changing any live module.

updates.note: RESOLVED by #10248 (squash eebb8ebe). The row said 'multiple modules'; a mechanical census found THIRTEEN declaration sites under THREE names — _TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT (4 strategy units + position_telemetry), TP_VENUE_CAP_PCT (target_expectation + 2 research scripts), LIVE_TP_CAP_PCT (5 scripts). All 13 held 0.099: they agreed BY LUCK, with no import, no test and no guard binding them. 13 → 1 — src/runtime/tp_venue_cap.py is the owner and every site imports it. Live order geometry unchanged and asserted mechanically: the units import under their EXISTING local name so all 8 clamp expression lines are byte-identical, and every src/ consumer resolves to the same OBJECT (`is`, not `==`). New guard tp-venue-cap-single-owner fails CI on a second declaration, on shadowing, and on CLAMPING_UNIT_MODULES drifting from what the unit sources carry; controls 13/13 and verified to FIRE on a planted duplicate and on planted registry drift. This is the check m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py correctly complained did not exist. ⚠️ The first census probe reported 5 — its regex required a character before 'TP_' and silently missed both non-underscore names; do not re-quote 'five'. ⚠️ DUPLICATION only: the VENUE-SCOPE question is still OPEN — 0.099 is a Bybit ErrCode 10001 boundary applied to legs on venues Bybit does not carry (the 3 Bybit accounts hold only BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT/SOLUSDT/XRPUSDT/ADAUSDT/AVAXUSDT). Recorded as OPEN in the owner docstring and in docs/design/tp-sentinel-cap-venue-scope-PROPOSAL.md §6/§8.

items.detail: `_TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT = 0.099` is declared independently in at least src/runtime/position_telemetry.py:72 and src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py:133, and scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py now carries a THIRD copy as LIVE_TP_CAP_PCT (added 2026-08-16 when --tp-cap-pct was defaulted to live parity). There is no single owner to import from, so the sweep script could not bind to the live value even in principle -- picking one of the src/ declarations would be arbitrary, and the script imports nothing from src/ at all. WHY IT MATTERS: the sweep's entire purpose after 2026-08-10 is to measure the book production actually runs. If the live constant moves and this copy does not, the sweep silently measures the OLD geometry and every verdict it prints will look correct while being about a different book -- which is precisely the arm-above-cap class (BL-20260816-TRAIL-DECAY-ARM-R-SITS-ABOVE-THE-VENUE-TP-CAP) recurring one level up. NOTHING CHECKS THIS TODAY: no guard, no test, no import. That is stated in the code comment rather than implied, because claiming a guard exists would itself be the unprovenanced-output failure. FIX SHAPE: give the constant one owner (a small module both src/ and scripts/ can import, or a guard asserting the declarations agree). Low severity because the live value has not moved and a change to it would be a deliberate Tier-3 act, not drift.
items.evidence: MEASURED 2026-08-24 by grep over the tree. FIVE declarations of the literal: src/runtime/position_telemetry.py:72, src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py:133, src/units/strategies/htf_pullback_trend_2h.py:98, src/units/strategies/fade_breakout_4h.py:117, src/units/strategies/squeeze_breakout_4h.py:79. A sixth copy is hardcoded in scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py, whose own comment states the problem plainly: 'there is no single owner to import FROM -- importing one would just pick a winner arbitrarily' and 'NOTHING CHECKS THAT THIS STILL MATCHES THE LIVE VALUE. There is no guard, no test, and no import binding them.' src/runtime/target_expectation.py exposes TP_VENUE_CAP_PCT and tests/test_target_expectation.py:91 asserts it equals position_telemetry._TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT, so a partial owner already exists.
items.notes: MERGED 2026-08-24 with BL-20260824-TP-SENTINEL-CAP-PCT-DUPLICATED-IN-FIVE-FILES, which was a duplicate filed 8 days later by a session that did not find this row. THIS id is the canonical one because it is cited from source (scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:124); the duplicate is marked superseded rather than deleted so neither id dangles. Severity raised low -> medium on the duplicate's measurement (5 declarations + a 6th hardcoded copy, not >=3).

items.title: vm-diag-snapshot truncation removes filter_state/total/count FIRST, because they sit after `rows` — a truncated response keeps the data and loses the fields that invalidate it
items.source: Hit twice in one measurement while pulling the xrp_pullback_2h entry history (diag issues #9753, #9755). Not theoretical — it produced a wrong-population read I nearly used.
items.why_it_matters: The diag relay is the ONLY read path for a web/PM session, so its consumers are sessions that cannot re-render or re-query cheaply and cannot see the query they actually got. Every quantitative claim such a session makes about live data rests on these fields. This is the 'always state the population' rule failing at the transport layer rather than at the analyst.
items.resolution_criteria: OBSERVABLE: issue a diag request whose response EXCEEDS the byte budget and whose filter names a nonexistent column; the returned comment must still show filter_state='ignored_unknown_column' (or an explicit relay-level warning that certification fields were dropped). Demonstrate by running it — a passing case on a small response proves nothing, since the bug only exists above the budget.
items.next_action: Cheapest fix is in the RELAY, not the API: when truncating, emit the tail keys (filter_state/order_state/total/count) after the truncation notice, or refuse to truncate mid-envelope and instead return a metadata-only summary. Reordering the API envelope so certification precedes `rows` also works and helps every consumer, but touches more surfaces.

updates.note: Re-validated and I HIT THE SAME CLASS TODAY on a different surface: the grade-closed-trades issue-comment cap kept the LAST 50,000 of 66,841 bytes, silently dropping the 22 OLDEST rows while the action's own _delta_summary (truncated:false) sat in the retained tail saying nothing was truncated. Same shape: truncation removed the rows and kept the field that certifies completeness. Generalise this row beyond vm-diag-snapshot.

items.detail:
The db-explorer envelope orders keys {table, db, columns, rows, total, limit, offset, filter_state, order_state, ...} and the /api/bot/order-packages envelope puts `count` after `rows`. The relay caps a comment at 55,000 bytes and truncates the TAIL. So on any response larger than the budget, the certification fields are the FIRST casualties while `rows` — the part that looks like data — survives.

MEASURED, both on 2026-08-16:
  * #9753: `filter_col=strategy` on order_packages. The real column is `strategy_name`, so the filter was silently IGNORED (the documented BL-20260813 behaviour), the query ran UNFILTERED, and the response was 829,977 bytes of the whole table truncated to 55,000. `filter_state` — which would have read `ignored_unknown_column` — was truncated away. What survived was well-formed rows of a DIFFERENT strategy (vwap/BTC).
  * #9755: correct filter via /api/bot/order-packages, 321,146 bytes truncated to 55,000. Right population this time, but `count` was truncated away, leaving 7 visible rows and NO denominator. The true total turned out to be 37 (#9756).

WHY THIS IS THE DANGEROUS ORDERING: a consumer of a truncated response sees rows, sees no filter_state, and rows look like data. The failure is silent in exactly the direction that matters — you cannot tell a filtered read from an unfiltered one, or a complete population from a page. I caught #9753 ONLY because XRP does not trade at 78,810; on a BTC leg I would very likely have computed a cap_R distribution over the entire order_packages table and reported it as the leg's history.

RELATION TO EXISTING ROWS: BL-20260813-DB-EXPLORER-SILENTLY-IGNORES-UNKNOWN-FILTER-COLUMN added `filter_state` as the remedy for the silent-ignore. This row is that remedy being DEFEATED BY TRANSPORT: the field exists, is correct, and never reaches the reader. A guard that is truncated away is not a guard.

items.severity: low (was high; the correctness half is fixed and the remainder is dead code)
items.tier: 2 — src/runtime/market_data.py is the live candle path feeding entry geometry AND exit decisions. Filed, NOT fixed in-session.
items.title: market_data._candle_cache_key keys on id(client), which CPython recycles the instant an object is freed — so the key cannot do the one thing its own comment says it exists for
items.source: Found by root-causing a CI failure that had nothing to do with the PR carrying it: tests/test_s012_pipeline.py::test_turtle_soup_flat_market_returns_side_none returned 'buy' on a flat market (PR #9812, run 31980184993). The test fixture is fully deterministic and the file passes in isolation, so the builder had to be seeing another test's candles.
items.why_it_matters: The comment above the key states its purpose exactly: 'Key on the CLIENT INSTANCE, not the symbol alone: two connectors may be different venues (or testnet vs mainnet) serving the same symbol string, and their candles are not interchangeable.' `id()` cannot deliver that guarantee. It is unique only among SIMULTANEOUSLY LIVE objects, and the cache stores the integer rather than a reference, so it does not keep the client alive — ids are therefore free to be recycled while the cached frame is still within its TTL. Strategies read `candles_df['close'].iloc[-1]` as the CURRENT PRICE for entry geometry and the monitor reads the same field for exit decisions, so the blast radius of serving one client's frame to another is the price behind a live order.
items.resolution_criteria: OBSERVABLE: two DIFFERENT client objects that occupy the same address at different times must not share a cache entry. Demonstrate with a test that builds a client, caches a frame, drops it, builds a second client that CPython allocates at the same id, and asserts the second gets a MISS — the test must be shown to FAIL against the current id()-based key, or it proves nothing.
items.next_action: Replace `id(client)` with a per-object token that is unique for the object's LIFETIME rather than for the address: attach a lazily-assigned monotonic counter (e.g. `client._mkt_cache_token`) and fall back to NOT CACHING when it cannot be attached (a __slots__ client), since refusing to cache is always safe and guessing is not. Do NOT 'fix' it by holding a strong reference to the client in the cache entry — that would keep exchange sockets (and IB clientIds) alive past their intended lifetime, trading a correctness bug for a resource bug on the path BL-20260706-IBACCTUPDATES-COLLISION already governs.

updates.what: FIXED (Tier-2, pre-granted). _candle_cache_key now keys on _client_identity_token(client) — a lazily-attached monotonic counter, unique for the object's LIFETIME rather than its address — and returns None (refusing to cache) when no token can be attached.
updates.why_it_was_safe_to_ship_unsupervised: Monotonically safer BY CONSTRUCTION: a lifetime-unique token can only make entries collide LESS, never more, so the cache can serve fewer stale frames but never additional ones. That is what made this shippable on the live candle path rather than only proposable.
updates.the_anti_pattern_avoided: No strong reference is retained — the token dies with the client — so exchange sockets and IB clientIds keep their intended lifetime. Holding the client in the cache entry would have traded this correctness bug for the resource bug BL-20260706-IBACCTUPDATES-COLLISION governs, which is why the filing warned against it before the fix was written.
updates.tests: tests/test_candle_cache_client_identity.py — 10 tests. The load-bearing one is test_the_old_id_key_would_alias: it reproduces the COLLISION under the old id() scheme on the SAME recycled address the fix is then asked about, so the passing fix test cannot be vacuous. Also pinned: a class-level attribute is never read as a per-instance identity (that would be the very collision being fixed, wearing a per-instance name), tokens are never reused, the `since=` carve-out survives, a __slots__ client is refused rather than guessed, and the same client still hits its own entry (the fix must not defeat the cache it repairs).
updates.still_open: reset_candle_cache() STILL has zero callers, so reset_exchange_client_cache() continues to drop clients while their frames survive. That half is untouched here and is why this row is not closed.

updates.what: SELF-CORRECTION — the second finding in this row is now OVER-STATED, in the alarming direction, and I am the one who over-stated it. It was written before the fix and never re-read against it.
updates.what_the_row_originally_claimed: That `reset_candle_cache()` having zero callers was a live hazard: 'a forced reconnect drops every client while their frames survive, keyed on ids that are, at that moment, all free for reuse. That is the sequence most likely to alias two genuinely different clients in production.'
updates.why_that_no_longer_holds: That sentence is entirely a property of `id()`. The fix keys on a MONOTONIC counter, so a token is never issued twice; after `reset_exchange_client_cache()` the surviving entries are keyed on tokens no future client can ever be assigned. They are UNREACHABLE, not aliasable.
updates.measured_2026_08_17: Reproduced the exact sequence against merged main: client A caches a frame (token 1), A is dropped, `reset_exchange_client_cache()` runs, a fresh client B arrives (token 2). token equal: False. B inherits A's frame: False. Orphaned entry still resident: True.
updates.what_actually_remains: Bounded memory retention only — unreachable entries sit in the map until their TTL, inside a map already capped at 512 entries (`_candle_cache_put` clears wholesale above that). That is a tidiness issue, NOT a correctness one, and it should not be carried at the severity the original text implies.
updates.why_this_correction_is_worth_making: A backlog row describing a hazard that no longer exists costs a future session a full re-derivation and contributes to the desensitized-alarm failure mode this repo treats as a P1 in its own right. The rule that caught it is 'verify your own output too, hardest when it confirms what you expected' — I wrote the hazard, fixed its cause an hour later, and did not re-read the filing against the fix until now.
updates.still_genuinely_open: `reset_candle_cache()` is still dead code: defined, documented 'For tests and for a forced reconnect', called by nothing. A reset nothing invokes cannot be relied on by a runbook. That is the whole of what is left here, and it is LOW severity.

updates.note: Re-validated: keying on id() of a freed object is a correctness landmine in the candle cache — and the candle cache is on the live signal path.

items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-17. `id()` reuse is not a rare edge — it is the NORM for short-lived objects, because CPython immediately reuses the freed block. A 2000-iteration allocate-then-drop loop produced 1999 id collisions, the first at iteration 1.

THE EMPIRICAL PROOF IS THE CI FAILURE. `test_turtle_soup_flat_market_returns_side_none` builds `_StubExchange(_flat_candles())` via a monkeypatched `_build_killzone_exchange`. Its sibling tests in the same file build `_StubExchange(_bullish_sweep_candles())`. Each stub is short-lived, so a later stub can be allocated at a freed stub's address and inherit its cached frame — the flat-market builder then sees bullish-sweep candles and emits `buy`. Consistent with every observation: passes alone (`1 passed`), passes as a file (`11 passed`), fails at full-suite scale (`1 failed, 11321 passed`), and no order-randomizing plugin is installed, so it is aliasing rather than ordering.

WHY PRODUCTION HAS NOT VISIBLY BITTEN — and why that is luck, not design. `_CLIENT_CACHE` memoizes connectors per credential identity and holds a STRONG reference, so a memoized client stays alive and its id is stable. That protection is incidental to this bug and has two documented holes:
  * **IB is deliberately excluded** — `_client_cache_key` returns None for IB on purpose (an `IBMarketData` holds a live socket on a specific clientId; sharing one is BL-20260706-IBACCTUPDATES-COLLISION). So every IB candle fetch builds a FRESH, short-lived client whose id is exactly the recyclable case. IB serves the live MES/MGC/MHG legs.
  * **`reset_exchange_client_cache()` does not clear the candle cache**, and `reset_candle_cache()` has ZERO callers in `src/`, `scripts/` or `tests/`. So a forced reconnect drops every client while their cached frames survive for up to `min(bar*0.10, 300s)` — keyed on ids that are, at that moment, all free for reuse. That is the sequence most likely to alias two genuinely different clients in production.

STATED HONESTLY: the DEMONSTRATED harm is in the test suite. The production harm is a LATENT hazard — the guarantee the key's own comment claims does not hold, and the two holes above are where it is most exposed. I did not observe a live mis-fetch, and I am not asserting one. What is established is that the mechanism preventing it is not the one the code says it is.

SEPARATE SMALL FINDING, recorded so it is not lost: `reset_candle_cache()` is dead code — defined, documented ('For tests and for a forced reconnect'), and called by nothing. A reset that nothing invokes cannot be relied on by a runbook. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'key FIXED (#9817); the reset half is DOWNGRADED to tidiness, not a hazard' was collapsed to 'kept_open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
