items.title: m20-exit-lever-sweep's conflict re-derive hard-resets the worktree and then runs the TARGET BRANCH's extractor — silently dropping every corpus field added since that branch last moved, while the job stays green
items.source: Found while investigating why tonight's 52 corpus rows lacked live_tp_reach_r_* when main's rows carry it. Confirmed from the job log, not inferred: run 31976325152, corpus job 95236789561, notice at 2026-08-16T22:30:58Z.
items.why_it_matters: The downgrade is SCHEMA-SILENT and self-concealing. The job is green, the step summary reports the full row count ('runs merged: 13  new rows: 52'), and the rows look complete — nothing anywhere states which extractor produced them. That is the unprovenanced-diagnostic class: a real number under a label that does not describe what produced it. Worse, the blast radius GROWS with every field added to the extractor, and it is invisible in exactly the direction that matters — a reader joining these rows sees an absent key and reads it as 'not measured', when the run did measure it.
items.resolution_criteria: TWO HALVES, and the first does not close the second. (1) CODE — a main-dispatched sweep whose rebase conflicts must still write rows carrying every key the dispatched extractor emits. Observable: dispatch on main, confirm the 'rebase conflicted' notice fires, then assert the new rows carry live_tp_reach_r_n_IS. A run that does NOT conflict proves nothing, since the bug only exists on the conflict path. (2) DATA — the 52 rows already written on claude/m20-sweep-corpus must be re-derived or explicitly marked as schema-degraded; until then a consumer cannot distinguish 'the field was not measured' from 'the field was measured and dropped in transit'.
items.next_action: Half (1) is shipped in this PR (preserve the dispatched extractor to $RUNNER_TEMP before any git op can revert it; re-derive from that copy; pinned by two tests in tests/test_m20_sweep_workflow_inputs.py incl. a negative control on the exact pre-fix shape). Half (2) is NOT done: the cheapest repair is a re-dispatch whose extractor is current, since the underlying measurement is not lost — verdicts.json carries live_tp_reach_r per leg and m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:2858 builds the SUMMARY reach table from it, so only the corpus HOP dropped it. This session cannot download run artifacts (no artifact-download MCP), so the repair needs a re-run rather than a local re-extract. ⚠️ BLOCKS THE PLANNED CORPUS UNION: merging the 113 branch-only rows onto main would import 52 schema-degraded rows into the canonical corpus — do the repair first, or the union records the degradation permanently. ⚠️ THE RE-DISPATCH REPAIR IS CONDITIONAL, NOT GUARANTEED — verify it, do not assume it. m20_corpus_extract.measurement_key supersedes on (kind, leg, cell, split, tp_cap_pct, regime_router, min_oos_trades_floor, fee_bps_roundtrip, min_confidence_override, declared_levers_dropped). Under the default split_mode=oos-trades the `split` is DERIVED per leg to target ~25 OOS trades from frames scp'd from the trainer, so if those frames gained candles since 2026-08-16 the derived boundary moves, the key changes, and the re-run ADDS 52 rows beside the degraded ones instead of superseding them — leaving the corpus holding two identities for one book, which is the same defect class BL-20260813-TPCAP-REQUESTED-NOT-APPLIED existed to clear. After any repair run, assert the corpus row count is UNCHANGED and the extractor reported 'superseded: 52'; if it grew, the split moved and the old rows must be removed by key rather than left to accumulate.

updates.note: Re-validated: silently dropping corpus fields added since the target branch is a data-loss path in the evidence base. Correctly open.

items.area: research tooling / m20 sweep corpus / CI
items.detail:
MECHANISM. .github/workflows/m20-exit-lever-sweep.yml's `rebase_onto_target` handles a rebase conflict by `git reset --hard "origin/$TARGET"` and then re-running the extractor. The reset reverts the ENTIRE worktree — including scripts/research/m20_corpus_extract.py itself — so the re-derive runs the corpus branch's copy, not the one the run was dispatched with. The surrounding comments reason carefully about preserving ROWS and about re-creating the staged automerge file after the reset; nothing considered that the reset also reverts the CODE that then re-derives them.

THIS IS THE NORMAL PATH, NOT A RARE RACE. The comment frames the conflict as the ordinary concurrent outcome ('both sides added rows'), but claude/m20-sweep-corpus never merges main and is currently 123 commits behind it. A main-dispatched run therefore rebases main's history onto a long-diverged branch and takes add/add conflicts across dozens of unrelated files EVERY time (the log shows conflicts in src/web/api/main.py, tests/test_validation.py, and ~30 others). So the degraded path fires on essentially every main-dispatched run — which is precisely why it went unnoticed.

MEASURED (2026-08-16). Run 31976325152 was dispatched on main at head_sha cb8bc5a2 (which postdates #9037, so the checked-out extractor DID have the field). The log: '##[notice]rebase conflicted on the corpus — re-deriving the union from their copy' then 'HEAD is now at 9a085926' — 123 commits behind main — then 'runs merged: 13  new rows: 52'.

SCHEMA DELTA, both directions. Comparing tonight's 52 rows (stale extractor) against the 361 main rows dated 2026-08-15 (current extractor — those were dispatched on claude/m20-exit-coverage-matrix-8d3he7, which was current, so no conflict fired; that is the control):
  * tonight: 70 distinct keys · 08-15: 78 distinct keys
  * dropped, exactly 8, all one family: live_tp_reach_r_{n,median,min,max}_{IS,OOS}
  * keys present only in tonight's rows: 0 — the delta is one-directional, no compensating gain
All eight were added by #9037 (61d9b1e6, 2026-08-13), which the corpus branch predates (verified: `git merge-base --is-ancestor` returns false).

WHAT IS *NOT* AFFECTED, stated so it is not over-read. The verdicts are computed upstream in verdicts.json and carried into the row separately; tonight's 43 is_oos_fail / 4 insufficient_base / 3 path_b_wf_pass / 1 path_b_wf_fail / 1 PASS are unaffected, and they reproduce the trainer relay's verdicts exactly. The loss is confined to the corpus row SCHEMA. The three reachability rows queued for the operator do not depend on these keys.

WHY THE ROWS' ABSENCE IS ITSELF MISLEADING. #9037's own comment (m20_corpus_extract.py:414) established that live_tp_reach_r's None is deliberately THREE-WAY — a run predating the field, a run with the cap OFF, and a leg the cap was on for that placed no measurable TP — with `_n` beside the median as what separates them. A row where the KEY IS ABSENT ENTIRELY is a fourth state that design did not contemplate: measured, then dropped in transit. The field built to avoid a collapsed state acquired a new one via the transport. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'code fix shipped; DATA REPAIR still open (52 rows written degraded)' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.

items.tier: 1 — research tooling. No live path. Any SHIP decision the verdict feeds is Tier-3 and unaffected by this filing.
items.title: m20_fleet_exit_sweep's walk-forward reports `wf_summary: 6/6` on six folds where the lever changed NOTHING — and the folds do not cover the years the OOS delta comes from
items.source: The single PASS of tonight's vol_trail re-run: splg_trend_long_1d / vt_hot80_t2, corpus row sweep_generated_at 2026-08-17T01:23:16Z, run dispatched on main at split_target_oos=35.
items.why_it_matters: A PASS is the gate that routes a lever to the operator as a Tier-3 ship candidate. `wf_summary: 6/6` beside `wf_wins: 6` reads as six independent out-of-sample confirmations; here it is six no-ops. The label is not merely uninformative, it is confidence-shaped — and it is attached to the ONLY cell that passed out of six measured tonight, i.e. exactly the row a reader would act on.
items.resolution_criteria: OBSERVABLE: a fold in which the lever never fires must NOT be counted as a win. Either (a) `wf_wins`/`wf_summary` count only folds with a non-zero delta and report the inert count separately, or (b) a fold with `d_net_r == 0.0 and d_max_dd == 0.0` gets a distinct third state (not `ok: True`), registered with collapsed-state-guard so producer and consumer are both checked. PLUS a planted control: a cell whose folds are all inert must not come back `6/6`, demonstrated by RUNNING it — a quiet pass proves nothing. AND the fold window must state its coverage against the OOS window, so a delta originating outside every fold cannot read as walk-forward-confirmed.
items.next_action: Not fixed here — filed with the measurement so the next session does not re-derive it. Note the cheap half is (a): the counts are already computed from `wf_folds`, which carries the per-fold deltas.

updates.note: MEASURED ACROSS THE WHOLE CORPUS, AND IT REACHES SHIPPED LEVERS ON A REAL-MONEY LEG — this was filed off ONE cell (`splg`'s 6/6 all-inert) and is not confined to it. POPULATION: 96 distinct (leg, lever, cell) carry a walk-forward, newest run per cell, out of 1376 corpus rows; 75 of 386 `ok` folds are INERT (19.4%) — the gate returned `ok` on a fold where the lever changed NOTHING (`d_net_r == 0.0` AND `d_max_dd == 0.0`). ⚠️ CORRECTING MY OWN FIRST PASS: I initially reported 79/509 = 15.5% by counting ALL rows including SUPERSEDED runs. Deduped to newest-run-per-cell it is 75/386 = 19.4%. Quote the deduped figure; the first is an artifact of double-counting re-runs. THE MONEY-RELEVANT PART, routing read from config/accounts.yaml rather than inferred: only `trend_donchian` and `trend_donchian_xrp_4h` among affected legs route to a real-money `mode: live` account (`bybit_2`). `trend_donchian_xrp_4h`/`trail_decay`/`decay_arm2R_t2.5` is `shipped` and records `wf_summary: 5/6` while being 2/6 EFFECTIVE — folds 2021, 2022 and 2026 all carry d_net_r 0.0 / d_max_dd 0.0 (newest run 2026-08-14T12:07:33, live parity tp 0.099). `5/6` reads as a strong walk-forward; the lever demonstrably fired in 3 of 6 folds and won 2. Also `trend_donchian`/`shipped_trail_decay_6.49_2.5` 6/6 -> 4/6, and `trend_donchian_xrp_4h`/`decay_arm1.5R_stall6_t2.5` 4/6 -> 3/6. THE REST IS PAPER, stated so the flag is not read as wider than it is: `gld_pullback_1d` (`shipped`, 5/6 -> 1/6), `qqq_trend_long_1d` (`passed_unshipped`, 6/6 -> 0/6 — every win inert) and `scha_trend_long_1d` route to alpaca_paper / alpaca_portfolio / ib_paper, and `alpaca_live` is `mode: dry_run`, so real money is not executing them: knowledge cost, not money. READ-SIDE HALF SHIPPED HERE: `scripts/research/m20_wf_effective.py` reports won/inert/lost per cell with the denominator, dedupes by run_id, and needs NO re-sweep — every wf-carrying corpus row ALREADY ships `wf_folds` with the per-fold deltas, so this has been measurable from committed data the whole time and the only thing missing was a reader. That is the same written-and-never-read shape as the sibling finding this session (BL-20260817-COLLAPSED-STATE-SELFTEST-REGISTERED-BUT-NEVER-INVOKED), which is how it was found. `effective` prints BESIDE `wf_summary`, never instead of it — overwriting the recorded figure would destroy the evidence that the two differ. `is_inert` requires BOTH deltas at zero (a fold that moved drawdown alone DID exercise the lever) and treats an ABSENT delta as not-inert, since absent is 'not recorded', not 'recorded as no change'. STILL OPEN, and this item stays OPEN: the PRODUCER is unchanged — `m20_fleet_exit_sweep` still emits `wf_summary` counting inert folds as wins, so every future sweep reproduces it, and the second half of this item's title (folds not covering the years the OOS delta comes from) is untouched. NOT ACTED ON: whether `trend_donchian_xrp_4h`'s shipped lever still clears its bar at 2/6 effective is a Tier-3 call for the operator. No status, verdict, arm or config was touched.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ROW'S OWN CLAIMS, PLUS A NEW CONSUMER THAT MAKES THIS A GATE DEFECT RATHER THAN A LABEL DEFECT. (1) CORRECTION — the producer named here is WRONG. This row says 'm20_fleet_exit_sweep still emits wf_summary'. Measured by grep: `wf_summary` does NOT appear in scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py at all. The corpus field is written by scripts/research/m20_corpus_extract.py:473. Field beats comment; a reader who went to the named file would have found nothing and could reasonably have concluded the row was stale in the opposite direction. (2) CORRECTION — 'the PRODUCER is unchanged' is now STALE in the good direction: m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:2717-2718 and :2748-2749 DO emit `walkforward_effective` and `walkforward_inert_wins`, which m20_corpus_extract.py:487-488 carries through as `wf_wins_effective` / `wf_inert_wins`. So new sweeps now record the split at source, not just via the offline reader. VERIFIED LIVE on sweep run 32025100663 (squeeze_breakout_4h/vol_trail, 2026-08-17T11:30Z): the passing cell came back `wf_wins_effective: '4/6'` with `wf_inert_wins: 0` — populated, not None, so the write path works end to end on a real run. (3) THE NEW FINDING, and the reason this stays OPEN and is worse than filed: `scripts/research/m20_path_b_floor.py::wf_pass` (line 152) grades on RAW `wf_wins`/`wf_usable`, so a fold where the lever never fired counts toward passing. This is NOT a label — `wf_pass` is the pass/fail signal the Path-B FLOOR CALIBRATION is computed over (`overall_wf_pass_rate`, `admitted_wf_pass`, `rejected_wf_pass`, and the floor the script RECOMMENDS at line 405). So a no-op-inflated count does not merely mislead a reader, it helps SELECT the floor value the operator is asked to adopt. MEASURED over the committed corpus (docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl, 1376 rows -> 96 deduped newest-run-per-cell carrying wf_folds, deduped via the existing m20_wf_effective.newest_per_cell rather than a second derivation): **17 of 96 cells (17.7%) return wf_pass=True but FAIL the identical inequality when raw wins are replaced by `effective` (= ok - inert)**. FIVE are 0/6 effective — every single win a no-op: qqq_trend_long_1d/vol_trail/vt_hot90_t2, spy_trend_long_1d/vol_trail/vt_hot90_t2, scha_trend_long_1d/vol_trail/vt_hot90_t2, gdx_pullback_1d/vol_trail/vt_hot90_t2 (5 inert of 5 wins), splg_trend_long_1d/vol_trail/vt_hot80_t2 (the cell this item was originally filed off). The list also contains trend_donchian_xrp_4h/trail_decay/decay_arm2R_t2.5 — the SHIPPED real-money lever on bybit_2 — at wf 5/6 but 2/6 effective, and trend_donchian_xrp_4h/trail_decay/decay_arm1.5R_stall6_t2.5 at 4/6 -> 3/6. ⚠️ MY FIRST PROBE OF THIS RETURNED A CLEAN ZERO AND WAS BLIND. It read `g.get('won')`, a key `grade_folds` does not return (it returns folds/ok/inert/effective/usable), so the comparison was None for every row and '0 of 96' looked like a reassuring negative. Caught by planting a control — six all-inert folds, on which raw wf_pass returns True and the effective form returns False — and only then re-running. Quote 17/96; the 0 was my probe, not the corpus. This is the 'green is not evidence' case in its exact canonical shape, on my own verification. NOT FIXED HERE, and deliberately not bundled into the matrix PR that carries this measurement: changing `wf_pass` changes which Path-B floor the script recommends to the operator, so it is a research CONCLUSION change and wants its own reviewable diff plus a before/after of the floor calibration — not a quiet semantics swap inside an unrelated PR. The cheap correct shape is to grade on `effective` when fold detail exists, keep a distinct state when it does not (absent is not zero), and print BOTH rates so the divergence stays visible. NOT ACTED ON: no verdict, status, arm or config was touched, and the xrp shipped-lever question remains Tier-3 and queued for the operator.

THE GATE HALF IS FIXED; THIS ITEM STAYS OPEN, and the severity I posted earlier is DOWNGRADED because I measured the claim and it did not hold. FIXED: `m20_path_b_floor.wf_pass` now grades on EFFECTIVE wins. It IMPORTS `m20_wf_effective.grade_folds` rather than re-deriving `is_inert` (two definitions of 'did the lever fire?' could disagree about a fold and make the gate and the audit tool report different verdicts on the same row — the class this item is about). The promotion rule is hoisted into `_wf_inequality` so the recorded and effective verdicts are provably the SAME inequality over a different numerator. `wf_basis` is THREE-STATE and never collapsed: `effective` (folds present, inert separable) / `raw_only` (a wf ran but NO per-fold detail, so the split cannot be computed for that row — checked: scripts/research/m20_wf_effective.py — its `grade_folds` reads `d_net_r`/`d_max_dd` off each entry of `wf_folds`, so a row without that list supplies no input to the inert test at all; measured on docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl, 133 of 1373 cell rows carry `wf_folds` — falls back to the recorded count and says so, because grading it 0-effective would manufacture a failure out of a missing record) / `ungraded` (no wf ran — None, never False). `wf_pass_as_recorded` keeps the sweep's own figure and `analyse` publishes BOTH rates plus `cells_inflated_by_inert_folds` and `wf_basis_counts` — replacing the recorded rate silently would leave no way to see the two differ, and the SIZE of the gap is the finding. ⚠️ SEVERITY CORRECTION — MY EARLIER CLAIM WAS WRONG. I wrote that the inflated count 'helps SELECT the floor value the operator is asked to adopt'. MEASURED before/after on the committed corpus (axis base_rate_IS, direction floor): verdict `no_separation` and `recommended_floor: None` in BOTH arms — both miss the Bonferroni bar 0.00109 over 46 floors — so NOTHING was ever mis-selected and the operator-facing recommendation is unchanged by this fix. What is real: the reported pass rate was inflated 11.6pp (0.6875 recorded vs 0.5714 effective) and the best-candidate floor shifts 1.4187 -> 1.1619, so the defect WOULD bias a selection if the population ever separated. Real defect, materially lower severity than posted. ⚠️ A FOURTH POPULATION, stated because I had already conflated two: `cells_inflated_by_inert_folds` on the analysed set is **13 of 112** — the rows `analyse` actually grades (fold-carrying AND carrying the axis). That is NOT the 17/96 (deduped newest-run-per-cell) nor the 19/133 (all fold-carrying cell rows, superseded runs included). All three are correct over different denominators; 13/112 is the one the floor calibration depends on. On this corpus `wf_basis_counts` is `{effective: 112}`, so the corrected rate is FULLY corrected here — no partial-correction caveat applies today, but the field exists so a future corpus with `raw_only` rows cannot hide one. VERIFIED NON-BLIND, not by reading: `tests/test_path_b_floor_inert_folds.py` (9 tests) plus THREE PLANTED BREAKS each failing its own test and restored green — (1) reverting `wf_pass` to raw `wf_wins` fails 3 tests, (2) grading `raw_only` as zero-effective fails 2, (3) dropping the recorded rate from the report fails 2. This matters specifically here: my FIRST probe of this defect returned a clean '0 of 96' because it read `g.get('won')`, a key `grade_folds` does not return, so every comparison was None. A quiet pass proves nothing, which is what this item's own resolution_criteria demand. STILL OPEN — two halves untouched, and neither is covered by the above: (1) THE PRODUCER. `wf_summary`/`wf_wins` still count inert folds as wins in the corpus (`m20_corpus_extract.py:473`), deliberately — the recorded figure is evidence about the sweep and appears in committed artifacts, so it is reported BESIDE the corrected one rather than overwritten. Any other consumer reading `wf_wins` directly still inherits the defect; this fix covers `m20_path_b_floor` only. (2) THE FOLD-COVERAGE HALF, which this item's title calls the sharper one: the folds do not state their coverage against the OOS window, so a delta originating in years no fold examines can still read as walk-forward-confirmed (the original `splg` observation: OOS opens 2019-01-30, folds are 2021-2026, and every covered year contributed exactly zero). Nothing here addresses that. NOT ACTED ON: no verdict, status, arm or config touched. `trend_donchian_xrp_4h`'s shipped real-money lever at wf 5/6 but 2/6 effective remains a Tier-3 question QUEUED for the operator.
Re-validated: 6/6 on folds where the lever changed nothing. Second member of the inert-lever-scores-as-a-win class.

items.detail:
MEASURED on the corpus row itself (docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl on claude/m20-sweep-corpus, commit cfae4acc).

THE CELL: splg_trend_long_1d / vt_hot80_t2, verdict PASS, is_oos_pass true, gate_passed on both windows. base_trades IS=42 OOS=35 (clears the 25 floor), split 2019-01-30.

THE WALK-FORWARD: wf_ran true, wf_usable 6, wf_wins 6, wf_summary '6/6'. Every one of the six folds reads {d_net_r: 0.0, d_max_dd: 0.0, ok: true, usable: true}. The lever changed NOTHING in any fold, and each was still counted a win AND marked `usable` — `usable` ought to mean the fold could discriminate, and a fold where the lever never fires cannot.

THE COVERAGE GAP, which is the sharper half: the folds are 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026. The OOS window opens at the split, 2019-01-30. So 2019 and 2020 sit INSIDE OOS and OUTSIDE every fold. Meanwhile d_net_r_OOS is +0.9596 (against base_net_r_OOS 14.0313, so ~6.8%) with d_max_dd_OOS exactly 0.0. Since every covered year contributes exactly zero, the supported reading is that the entire OOS improvement originates in 2019-2020 — the two years the walk-forward does not examine. STATED AS THE SUPPORTED READING, NOT A MEASUREMENT: I did not decompose the OOS delta per year, and that decomposition is what would confirm it.

SCALE, so the row is not over-read: +0.96R on a 14.03R base with zero drawdown change is a small effect either way. The problem is not the size, it is that the artifact presents it as six-fold-confirmed.

THE SIBLING, and why this is a pattern rather than an incident: BL-20260814-FLIP-VERDICT-PASS-IS-86PCT-DEGENERATE records the SAME CLASS in a DIFFERENT harness — the regime-flip replay writes `verdict: PASS` on legs where the lever never fired, 12 of 14 fleet passes at flip_pct 0.0. Two independent tools in this programme both label a no-op as a positive. That row's resolution criteria are the right shape and should be reused here rather than reinvented, including its explicit non-resolution: documenting the caveat in a doc and leaving the field as-is does not count, because the artifacts outlive the doc and are read directly.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: I did not record this cell as a pass in docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json, and did not propose shipping the lever. The two matrix cells this run was aimed at (iwm_trend_long_1d/vol_trail, splg_trend_long_1d/vol_trail) are now MEASURABLE — both legs cleared the OOS floor at 34 and 35 trades against 25 — but recording splg as a pass on this evidence would propagate exactly the defect above.

items.tier: 1 — CI guard over research artifacts. No live path.
items.title: matrix-corpus-agreement never compares a `blocked:`/`pending` cell against the corpus, so a block the corpus has ALREADY ANSWERED persists silently and the guard still reports OK
items.source: Found while working the pullback-family re-sweep: mhg_pullback_1d/giveback_stop sat at `blocked:insufficient_base` while the corpus held real live-parity verdicts for both of its cells (run 2026-08-17T00:47:35Z, base OOS n=36 against a floor of 25). The guard printed `OK — 235 live cell(s) checked … no unacknowledged disagreement` over that state.
items.why_it_matters: This is the collapsed-states family, one level up from the usual instance. `blocked` and `pending` are the matrix's way of saying WE DID NOT LOOK — a legitimate and important state. The defect is that nothing ever revisits it: the guard asks only 'is a stated NEGATIVE contradicted by a passing corpus row?' and never the reverse, 'does this cell still claim we could not look AFTER we looked?'. So the one status whose whole meaning is provisional is the one status the guard exempts from re-checking, and a stale block is indistinguishable from a live one on every surface — including the done-condition, which counts blocked cells as OPEN and was therefore overstating by at least one cell. A guard that reports OK over a knowably-stale block is worse than no guard on that column, because the OK is read as coverage.
items.resolution_criteria: OBSERVABLE: for every live cell whose base status is `blocked` or `pending`, the guard checks whether the corpus holds a row for that (leg, lever) that would resolve it — a verdict of ANY sign, not only a pass — and fails (or emits an acknowledged-disagreement entry) when one exists. The planted control is the standard for this repo: seed a blocked cell whose corpus row carries a verdict and demonstrate the guard FAILS by running it. A quiet pass proves nothing, and this guard already passed quietly over a real instance. Note the fix must not simply widen NEGATIVE_STATUSES — that set answers a different question and widening it would make a blocked cell read as an assertion of a negative.
items.next_action: Not fixed here — the data instance was corrected (mhg_pullback_1d/giveback_stop flipped blocked -> honest_negative with the measurement recorded) but the GUARD gap remains, and fixing it is what stops the next one. Concrete pointers: the early return is at scripts/ci/check_matrix_corpus_agreement.py:242 against NEGATIVE_STATUSES (line 105); the existing newest_floor_clearing_pass helper searches only for a PASS and would need a sign-agnostic sibling.

updates.note: SWEPT THE WHOLE COLUMN RATHER THAN STOPPING AT THE ONE INSTANCE, and the result changes what the fix must do. Of 376 live cells, 6 blocked/pending cells carry a corpus row with a verdict STRING — but only 3 are genuine: mhg_pullback_1d/giveback_stop, iwm_trend_long_1d/vol_trail and splg_trend_long_1d/vol_trail (all measured 2026-08-17 at live parity, base OOS 34-36 against a floor of 25). The other 3 (mes_trend_long_1d giveback_stop + vol_trail, spy_trend_long_1d/vol_trail, qld_trend_long_1d/vol_trail) are CORRECTLY blocked: their rows are from 2026-08-10, carry NO live-TP-reach block, and were emitted on base OOS of 3-6 — i.e. the sweep returned `is_oos_fail` on populations far below the floor because MIN_OOS_TRADES enforcement did not exist until 2026-08-11. SO THE NAIVE FIX IS WRONG: a guard that asks only 'does a corpus verdict exist for this blocked cell?' would raise 4 false positives against 6 findings — a 67% false-positive rate on its first run, which is how a new guard becomes the desensitized alarm this repo already has a P1 rule about. The predicate must require BOTH that the row is a live-parity measurement (a `live_tp_reach_r_*` block present, not a requested tp_cap_pct) AND that `base_trades_OOS >= min_oos_trades_floor` — the same two conditions a human uses when reading these rows. A verdict string alone is not evidence that anything was gradeable.

A THIRD STATE THE MATRIX ENUM CANNOT EXPRESS, surfaced by the same sweep and left for the operator. splg_trend_long_1d/vol_trail is measured above the floor at live parity — so its `blocked:insufficient_oos_base_at_derived_split` reason is factually stale — but it CANNOT be graded, because its only passing cell (vt_hot80_t2) passes on `wf_summary: 6/6` with all six folds at `d_net_r == 0.0` (BL-20260817-FLEET-SWEEP-WF-COUNTS-INERT-FOLDS-AS-WINS). Writing `honest_negative` would assert a negative the run did not establish; writing the pass would ship a lever on six no-ops. 'Measured, but the grader is under question' is neither `blocked` (we did not look) nor a verdict. The cell's status was therefore left blocked with its ref corrected to stop claiming we could not look. Whether the enum gains a value or this simply waits on the grader fix is an operator call, not one to take unilaterally — noting it here so the guard work and the enum question are not conflated.

FIXED. `find_stale_blocks` now re-examines every live cell whose base status is `blocked` or `pending` against the corpus, sign-agnostically — the question is not whether the cell's answer is right, it is whether the cell still claims nobody has an answer. The predicate reuses the SHARED `_newest_per_cell` filter rather than re-deriving one, so it cannot drift from `newest_floor_clearing_pass` on what counts as admissible evidence: live-parity `tp_cap_pct` AND `base_trades_OOS >= MIN_OOS_TRADES`, with per-cell supersession. Both filters are load-bearing and the measurement in the first update is why — without them the check raises 4 false positives out of 6. `BLOCKED_ACK` is a DIFFERENT phrase from `ACK` and the suite asserts they are not interchangeable, so one ref cannot satisfy the other's check. Verified by RUNNING it, not by a quiet pass: against the real matrix it exited 1 on exactly one cell — `splg_trend_long_1d/vol_trail`, the cell deliberately held — which is the sequencing trap predicted in docs/sprint-logs/S-M20-PULLBACK-STALE-BACKLOG-2026-08-17.md before the fix was written. Resolved via path (b): the block reason is stale, the cell is still ungradeable, so the status stands and the ref now says so. SEPARATELY FIXED while here: the guard's `--self-test` was never registered in scripts/ci/guard_selftests.py, so its planted-failure suite ran only when a human passed the flag by hand — written and never read, the same shape this guard exists to catch. Now registered as `matrix-corpus-agreement`, which is what makes the new false-positive controls actually execute in CI.

CORRECTION TO THE UPDATE ABOVE — I GOT THE MECHANISM WRONG, AND THE ERROR RAN IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. That update says the guard's `--self-test` "was never registered ... so its planted-failure suite ran only when a human passed the flag by hand", and that registering it in guard_selftests.py "is what makes the new false-positive controls actually execute in CI". BOTH HALVES ARE FALSE. `run_guards.py` has run `check_matrix_corpus_agreement.py --self-test` as the FIRST step of the matrix-corpus-agreement entry since that guard was written (line 264) -- so the suite was never human-only, and the new blocked-cell controls were executing in CI from the moment they merged. The registry entry I added is REDUNDANT: nothing invokes `guard_selftests.py matrix-corpus-agreement` (the dispatcher takes a name; there is an `--all` but no caller passes it), so it is reachable only by hand. It is harmless and left in place as a manual alias, now commented as such so the next reader does not repeat my inference. HOW THE ERROR HAPPENED, because the shape is the point: I grepped for `guard_selftests.py", "matrix-corpus-agreement"`, got 0, and concluded 'not wired' -- a search returning nothing taken as proof of absence, over a probe that could only ever have found ONE of the two wiring paths. RULE ONE names exactly this. VERIFIED THE RIGHT WAY THIS TIME, by planting rather than reading: making `find_stale_blocks` return `[]` unconditionally makes the CI step exit 1 on 'guard failed to catch a blocked cell the corpus has graded'; restoring it returns rc=0. That is the controls executing, demonstrated by a failure, not by a passing run. THE MISTAKE WAS STILL WORTH MAKING: checking it surfaced a REAL gap of the same shape that is NOT mine and predates tonight -- `selftest_collapsed_state` is registered and invoked by nothing, with no `--self-test` on its checker to cover it. Filed as BL-20260817-COLLAPSED-STATE-SELFTEST-REGISTERED-BUT-NEVER-INVOKED and fixed in the same PR as this correction.

items.detail: The guard's own comment at line 103-105 states the reasoning — `pending`/`blocked` 'claim no outcome' — and that reasoning is CORRECT for the question the guard was written to answer. This is not a coding error; it is a scope gap that only becomes visible once the corpus is fresh enough to have overtaken the matrix, which is exactly what the 2026-08-17 corpus union (#9823/#9827) made possible. Worth recording because the union closing the corpus divergence is what turned this from theoretical into observed.

items.tier: 1 — workflow input documentation. No behaviour change; the default itself is correct.
items.title: m20-exit-lever-sweep's `split_target_oos` input still documents an empty value as defaulting to MIN_OOS_TRADES (25); the script default has been 50 since #9748
items.source: .github/workflows/m20-exit-lever-sweep.yml line 59-60 vs scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:597 (`DEFAULT_SPLIT_TARGET_OOS = 50`, landed 2026-08-16 in e0f0761e / #9748 as an operator Tier-3 decision).
items.why_it_matters: Field beats comment, and here the comment is the operator-facing one. The description tells a dispatcher that leaving the input empty 'targets exactly the number the verdict requires, so a shortfall of one trade lands below the floor' and that empty 'reproduces every pre-2026-08-14 run' — both were true and are now false. The concrete risk is misreading EVIDENCE, not just misconfiguring a run: a session reading this description would conclude that any default-configured sweep is pinned to the floor and therefore discount a clean verdict as configured-to-pass, or conversely treat an explicit `--split-target-oos 50` as a non-default override to be distrusted. I made exactly the second error tonight before checking the constant, and it nearly caused a real measurement to be written off.
items.resolution_criteria: The input description states the current default (50), says empty no longer reproduces pre-2026-08-14 runs, and keeps the distinction the constant's own comment makes: the FLOOR (MIN_OOS_TRADES, 'is this cell gradeable?') and the TARGET ('where do we cut?') are two different questions that previously shared one number, and that sharing was the bug (BL-20260814-SPLIT-TARGETS-EXACTLY-THE-FLOOR-SO-BOUNDARY-LOSS-ALWAYS-FAILS).
items.next_action: One-line doc fix in the workflow input description. Deliberately not bundled into tonight's data-correction PR so the matrix change stays reviewable on its own.

updates.note:
RESOLVED. Verified against the FIELD before editing the prose: `MIN_OOS_TRADES = 25` (:578) and `DEFAULT_SPLIT_TARGET_OOS = 50` (:603).

TWO descriptions were stale, not the one this row named. Besides `split_target_oos`, the `split_mode` input also read 'DERIVES a per-leg date targeting ~25 OOS trades' — same drift, and arguably the more misleading of the two since `split_mode` is the input a dispatcher reads FIRST and it restates the floor as if it were the target. Found by grepping the workflow for the number rather than only patching the line the row cited.

Both now name the constant by name (so the next drift is greppable), state 50, keep the floor/target distinction the constant's own comment insists on ('Do NOT re-couple these to one constant'), and carry the correction this row called for: empty NO LONGER reproduces a pre-2026-08-14 run — pass 25 explicitly for that. The 25->50 cliff is preserved as being about the FLOOR, so nobody reads it as an argument against the 50 TARGET.

Behaviour unchanged, as the row said: the workflow passes the flag only when set (`${SPLIT_TARGET_OOS:+...}`), so empty already yielded the script default. YAML re-parsed after the edit.

items.detail: Note the workflow is not WRONG in behaviour: it passes the input through only when set (`${SPLIT_TARGET_OOS:+--split-target-oos ...}`), so an empty input correctly yields the script default. Only the prose describing what that default IS has drifted.

items.tier: 1 — CI self-test hygiene. No live path.
items.title: guard_selftests.py plants its planted-failure probes into the real working tree (deploy/, scripts/ml/), so a hard kill strands a file that then fails an unrelated guard and is one `git add -A` from being committed
items.source: Hit directly on 2026-08-17: a scripts/ci/run_guards.py invocation returned `::error::deploy/ict-selftest-unlisted.timer is neither in _CANONICAL_UNITS nor exempted` while a concurrent pytest run held the probe open. The file was gone seconds later and was never tracked — verified with `git ls-files` and by reading the commit's own --stat — but the next command in that sequence was `git add -A`.
items.why_it_matters: The planted-failure design is RIGHT and must not be weakened — `selftest_diag_unit_allowlist` exists precisely because a guard nobody has seen fail is indistinguishable from a probe that cannot fire, which is the same lesson tests/test_m20_tp_geometry_guard.py encodes. The problem is only WHERE the probe lands. `scripts/ci/guard_selftests.py:162` writes `deploy/ict-selftest-unlisted.timer` into the repo, and `selftest_diagnostic_provenance` does the same with `scripts/ml/_selftest_probe.py`; the `_planted` context manager cleans up on normal exit and on exceptions, but by construction cannot on SIGKILL, a runner timeout, or a cancelled workflow. Two consequences, one confusing and one worse: (a) a stranded probe makes the NEXT guard run fail with an error naming a unit nobody added, which reads as a real finding and costs a session time to dismiss; (b) `deploy/` is a tracked directory, so `git add -A` — the idiom used throughout this repo's sessions — would commit the probe, and the diag-allowlist guard would then fail on main until someone noticed. Note the same file's own sibling already does this correctly: `selftest_diagnostic_provenance` writes its DIFF to `tempfile` while still planting its source probe in-tree, so the safer pattern is present in the same function and simply was not applied to the probe itself.
items.resolution_criteria: OBSERVABLE: no self-test writes a probe into a tracked directory, OR the guards that scan those directories skip a reserved probe name and a test demonstrates the skip does not also blind them to a real unlisted unit (that demonstration is the load-bearing half — a skip pattern wide enough to swallow real findings would be worse than the current state). A cheap alternative that preserves the design: point the guard at a temp directory via the argument it already takes, so the probe never touches the repo.
items.next_action: Not fixed here — filed with the direct observation so it is not re-derived from a confusing error message by a future session. Low severity because the window is small and nothing was actually committed; kept open because the failure mode is a wrong-looking CI failure on main, which is expensive out of proportion to the bug.

updates.note:
RESOLVED, and this row's own proposed fix was WRONG — recording that rather than quietly doing something else. It read 'point the guard at a temp directory via the argument it already takes'. `check_diag_unit_allowlist.py::main()` took NO arguments: there was no argparse at all and `DEPLOY_GLOBS` was a hardcoded module constant. Field beats comment; verified by reading main(), not by trying the flag. The argument now exists because I added it (`--deploy-dir`, defaulting to `deploy` so CI behaviour is byte-identical — confirmed 44 units scanned, 0 failures, exit 0).

THE TWO PROBES TURNED OUT TO BE DIFFERENT PROBLEMS, measured rather than assumed:
  * deploy/ probe — fails a guard AND is stageable. Fixed properly: the self-test now stages a FAITHFUL copy of deploy/ in a TemporaryDirectory and plants there, so nothing is ever written to the tracked tree and no cleanup handler is load-bearing.
  * scripts/ml/_selftest_probe.py — measured: a stranded copy fails NO guard (`run_guards.py --base main` = PASS 42 / FAIL 0 / SKIP 0 with it present), so the confusing-CI-failure half does not apply. It also CANNOT move to a temp dir: `check_diagnostic_provenance.py` resolves the file from the diff, repo-relative, and only scans scripts/{ml,research,ops,macro,reports}/ — a temp path is filtered out and the probe would silently never fire. Remaining risk was purely `git add -A`, so it is now .gitignored. Self-test re-verified: still exits 0 having seen the guard fail closed.

The staging copy is FAITHFUL, not a bare dir holding one probe: the guard also fails on stale exemptions, so an empty staging dir would fire all 8 exemption-stale errors and still return non-zero — a pass for entirely the wrong reason. Hence the added CONTROL, which is the load-bearing half this row asked for: the staged copy is asserted CLEAN before planting, and the post-plant output must NAME the probe. `rc != 0` alone cannot distinguish 'the probe fired' from 'my staging was broken'.

Verified by planting a break, not by reading: neutering the guard's `uncovered` computation makes the self-test exit 1 ('guard did NOT fail on an unlisted deploy unit'); restoring it returns exit 0.

items.detail: Worth noting the near-miss ordering explicitly: the stray file appeared in a guard run, and the very next command in the same session was `git add -A && git commit`. That commit turned out clean (verified by reading `git show --stat`, not by assuming), but only because the probe's cleanup had already run. Reading the commit's file list rather than trusting the guard output is what established it.

items.title: `selftest_collapsed_state` is registered in guard_selftests.py::SELFTESTS and NOTHING invokes it, so the collapsed-state guard's planted-failure suite has never run in CI
items.source: Found while verifying my own claim in BL-20260817-MATRIX-CORPUS-GUARD-NEVER-CHECKS-BLOCKED-CELLS that a SELFTESTS registration is what makes a self-test run. Testing that claim required enumerating registered names against invoked ones: SELFTESTS holds 10, `run_guards.py` invokes 8 by name. The two never invoked are `matrix-corpus-agreement` (harmless — its checker carries its own `--self-test` step, which run_guards DOES run) and `collapsed-state`, which has no such second path: the collapsed-state-guard entry ran only `check_collapsed_states.py --verbose`, and that script has no `--self-test` flag at all.
items.why_it_matters: A guard's self-test is the only thing standing between 'this guard passed' and 'this guard has silently stopped matching' — a control that proves the probe can still find a positive. Registered-but-never-executed is the written-and-never-read shape `provenance-consumer-guard` exists to catch, here applied to the guard machinery itself, and it is strictly worse than a missing self-test: a reader who greps SELFTESTS sees `collapsed-state` listed and reasonably concludes the control runs. The collapsed-state guard is not a minor one — it enforces the canonical 'can this field say we did not look?' rule across every declared contract (ib_venue_session.state, db_explorer.filter_state, pairs state_read, bybit_available.read_state, exit-loop requirement_state, ...). Note the self-test is NOT broken: run by hand it passes AND prints 'failure path verified'. A working control, unwired — which is why nothing ever alarmed.
items.resolution_criteria: OBSERVABLE: `scripts/ci/run_guards.py`'s collapsed-state-guard entry invokes `guard_selftests.py collapsed-state` as a step BEFORE the checker itself, matching the timestamp-comparison-guard / matrix-corpus-agreement pattern of self-test-first. Verified by running the guard, not by reading the entry.
items.next_action: DONE in this PR: the invocation was added as the first step of the collapsed-state-guard entry, with a comment recording that the gap existed and why this guard had no second covering path. REMAINING, deliberately not taken tonight because it is a design question rather than a wiring fix: nothing structurally prevents the NEXT registered self-test from going uninvoked. The generalisation is a wiring guard asserting every SELFTESTS name is either invoked by name in run_guards.py or covered by its own checker's `--self-test` — the same relationship `provenance-consumer-guard` enforces between a written key and its reader. Two instances now exist (this one real, one redundant), which is the point at which a per-instance fix stops being sufficient. Left for a review session with a note that the guard must verify the covering path, not merely the presence of a name — a presence-only check would be cheaper to lie to than to satisfy, the `new-table-wiring-guard` lesson.
items.detail: scripts/ci/run_guards.py (collapsed-state-guard entry) + scripts/ci/guard_selftests.py::SELFTESTS

items.tier: 3 (the answer gates a change to when live protective stops can fire)
items.title: RESEARCH: does outsideRth=False make a GTC futures STOP ineligible to TRIGGER outside RTH? Answer this before anyone changes protective-order geometry
items.detail:
OPERATOR-REQUESTED, 2026-08-17: an open-research task so the call on BL-20260816-IB-PROTECTIVE-STOPS-NEVER-SET-OUTSIDERTH can be made on evidence instead of inference. THIS ROW IS THE QUESTION, NOT THE FIX. Do not ship a geometry change from this row; produce an answer, then the fix is decided against it.

THE QUESTION, precisely. IBKR's `outsideRth` flag keys on a contract's LIQUID hours. Every order this repo places carries the ib_insync default `outsideRth=False` — established by grep, tree-wide, zero hits before 2026-08-16. For a MARKET order the consequence is measured and understood: it is HELD, which is what produced the 2026-08-16 MGC non-fill. **What is NOT known is whether the same flag makes a resting GTC STOP ineligible to TRIGGER outside RTH.** Those are different mechanics — trigger eligibility versus routing eligibility — and IBKR may treat them differently, and may treat FUT differently from STK.

WHY IT MATTERS ENOUGH TO RESEARCH RATHER THAN GUESS. MGC trades electronically roughly 23h a day and its RTH window is a few hours. If a stop cannot trigger outside RTH, then an overnight futures position is effectively unprotected for most of its life — while every surface this repo owns reports it as PROTECTED, because `has_protective_orders` asks whether a leg RESTS and `protection_coverage` asks how much QUANTITY rests. Neither asks whether the leg can FIRE. That is the same shape as BL-20260814-IB-PROTECTION-BOOLEAN-NOT-QUANTITY one level down: a coverage verdict that cannot be contradicted from outside. If the answer is 'yes, inert', this is a live money-at-risk hole that has been open for the entire life of the IB integration. If the answer is 'no, futures stops trigger on the electronic session regardless', the current code is correct and the row closes with a documented rationale — which is worth just as much, because it stops the next session re-opening it.

WHAT THIS REPO CONTAINS ON THE QUESTION: NOTHING. That is the finding that produced this task. There is no test, no comment, no runbook line, and no incident record bearing on futures-stop trigger eligibility outside RTH. So the answer must come from IBKR's own documentation or from a live experiment, and the researching session must not accept a plausible-sounding inference from the codebase as evidence. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'open_research' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
items.research_brief:
TWO INDEPENDENT LINES. Do BOTH; agreement between them is the confidence, and disagreement is itself the finding.

LINE A — DOCUMENTARY. Search IBKR's own material: the TWS API guide on order attributes (`outsideRth` / `outsideRTH`), the Order Types and Algos pages for STP and STP LMT, the Trader's Academy notes on RTH vs electronic sessions, and the contract-specific Trading Hours pages for COMEX MGC/GC and CME MES/ES. Quote the passage verbatim with its URL; do not paraphrase into the row. NOTE THE KNOWN OBSTACLE: a 2026-08-16 session recorded that IBKR's pages 403'd from this sandbox and labelled its conclusion unverified as a result — if that recurs, SAY SO and lean on Line B rather than quietly downgrading to a forum post. Third-party forums are a lead, never the answer.

LINE B — LIVE EXPERIMENT on ib_paper, which is a PAPER account and therefore the right venue for this. Design it so the result cannot be ambiguous:
  1. Open a small futures position (1 contract, MGC or MES) OUTSIDE RTH but INSIDE the electronic session.
  2. Arm a protective stop with `outsideRth=False` — the current production geometry — placed close enough to the market that it should trigger within the window.
  3. Observe whether it fires. Read the ORDER STATE, not the position: `/api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper` shows status/filled/remaining per order.
  4. Repeat with `outsideRth=True`. The CONTRAST is the evidence; either arm alone is not.
  5. Record the exact instant, the contract's `liquidHours`/`tradingHours` at that instant (via `IBClient.venue_session` or `reqContractDetails`), and the observed order state.
ONE ARM CANNOT ANSWER THIS. A stop that does not fire outside RTH with the flag False proves nothing on its own — it may simply not have been touched. The paired arm is what separates 'the flag suppressed it' from 'price never reached it'.

STATE THE POPULATION AND THE INSTRUMENT TYPE. FUT and STK may differ, and the close path already treats them oppositely (see `_close_wants_outside_rth`). An answer that does not say which instrument type it covers is not an answer.
items.resolution_criteria:
The row closes when ALL of these hold:
1. A DIRECT answer for FUT, sourced from IBKR documentation quoted verbatim with a URL, or from a paired live experiment with both arms recorded, or both.
2. The answer explicitly states whether it covers STK as well, or says it does not.
3. `BL-20260816-IB-PROTECTIVE-STOPS-NEVER-SET-OUTSIDERTH` is updated with the finding and moved to either a proposed Tier-3 change (if stops ARE inert) or a documented close (if they are not). A close needs the rationale written down, or the next session re-opens it.
4. EITHER WAY, `protection_coverage` is assessed against the answer: today it reports RESTING quantity and says nothing about trigger eligibility. If eligibility turns out to be a real axis, that is a collapsed state in the coverage verdict and belongs in the collapsed-state registry.
5. If neither line produces an answer, say so plainly and record WHICH line failed and why. 'Could not establish' is an acceptable outcome; a confident guess is not.
refs: src/units/accounts/ib_client.py::_close_wants_outside_rth (the FUT/STK split shipped for the CLOSE)

updates.note: Re-validated: this is a RESEARCH question gating a protective-geometry change, and it must be answered first. Live book shows both MES legs GTC and resting; whether the STOP can trigger outside RTH is unresolved and unanswerable from our own logs — it needs IBKR documentation or a controlled test.

items.title: IBClient.venue_session is public, cheap and unreachable from outside — so the only way to learn whether the venue gate says UNKNOWN is to wait for a live close
items.detail:
The venue-session gate shipped in #9693 is FAIL-PERMISSIVE on `unknown`: it places the order and logs WARNING. That makes a permanently-unknown gate behaviourally identical to a working gate on an open venue, and the WARNING is the ONLY thing separating them.

Measured 2026-08-17: ~14.5h after deploy the gate had still never run — zero `venue session` lines in an 8h journal window spanning the Globex open, because zero closes were attempted. So the question that matters most about the change (does `timeZoneId` resolve on the live VM?) is unanswerable until some strategy happens to want an exit. That is an arbitrary and possibly long wait for a fact that is one read away.

THE SPECIFIC RISK IS MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: `US/Eastern` and `US/Central` are tzdata LEGACY links absent from slim installs — `zoneinfo` raises for both in this repo's sandbox while `America/New_York` resolves — and COMEX and CME report precisely those. The resolver falls back to `pytz`, which bundles its own database and is a declared requirement, so it SHOULD resolve on the VM. That has never been observed there.

`IBClient.venue_session(symbol)` already exists, is public, takes the usage lock, opens no order path, mutates nothing, and returns the three-state verdict plus a reason string naming which path to `unknown` was taken. It is the natural read and nothing exposes it.

PROGRESS 2026-08-17 (same session): the route SHIPPED — `GET /api/diag/venue_session?account_id=&symbol=` over the existing `IBClient.venue_session_detail`, returning `state` + `reason` + `time_zone_id` + **`tz_source`** (`zoneinfo`/`pytz`/`unresolved`) + `tz_resolved_name`, plus `sec_type`/`graded_field`/`close_would_send_outside_rth` so the grading-the-field-the-order-acts-on question is answerable from one read. Per-account `read_state` is three-state (`not_ib`/`could_not_look`/`session_read`) and `unknown` survives to the response as a state, never an error (criterion 2). CRITERION 3 WAS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN, not skipped: it said to add the route to the diag relay allowlist in the same change. Verified this session — the relay allowlist constrains only `/api/bot/*`; `/api/diag/*` paths pass through unrestricted, so there was nothing to add. The criterion was written from the #9627 precedent (an `/api/diag/log_file?name=` VALUE, which IS allowlisted) and generalised to a path that is not. STILL OPEN ON CRITERION 4 — the route has not been read against the live VM, so **whether `US/Eastern` resolves there, and through which library, remains UNKNOWN**. Shipping the surface is not the answer; it is the instrument. Close this only after recording the measured `tz_source` for MGC and MES.

=== VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-17T17:01Z — verbatim ===
GET /api/diag/venue_session?account_id=ib_paper&symbol=MGC ->
  state=open · tz_source=zoneinfo · time_zone_id=US/Eastern · tz_resolved_name=US/Eastern · graded_field=tradingHours · sec_type=FUT · close_would_send_outside_rth=true · read_state=session_read · reason='tradingHours: inside 20260816 18:00-20260817 17:00 US/Eastern'
GET /api/diag/venue_session?account_id=ib_paper&symbol=MES ->
  state=open · tz_source=zoneinfo · time_zone_id=US/Central · tz_resolved_name=US/Central · graded_field=tradingHours · sec_type=FUT · close_would_send_outside_rth=true · read_state=session_read · reason='tradingHours: inside 20260816 17:00-20260817 16:00 US/Central'

The gate GRADES A REAL VERDICT on the live VM. It is not silently unknown, the gateway returns a non-empty tradingHours, the timeZoneId resolves, and each instrument is graded on the field its own order acts on.

*** THIS REFUTES THE PREMISE BOTH ROWS ARGUED FROM. *** Both said the live risk was that US/Eastern and US/Central are tzdata LEGACY links absent from slim installs (measured: zoneinfo raises for both in this repo's sandbox), with pytz expected to carry the VM. On the VM pytz is NOT consulted: tz_source is `zoneinfo` and tz_resolved_name equals the RAW id for both symbols, so the FIRST rung resolved directly. The sandbox measurement was true of the sandbox and was wrongly generalised to the VM. Keep the alias map and the pytz rungs — defensive, load-bearing in the sandbox (dropping the alias map fails 12 of 16 parser tests), and a future host may be slim — but do NOT describe them as what makes the live gate work.

HOW IT WAS VERIFIED MATTERS: not by a close. Four checks over ~24h found ZERO closes attempted (every monitor pass returns closed=0 no_change=1), which is structural — nothing asks for an exit. The read surface is what made the gate observable at all.

CRITERION 4 MET — this row is CLOSED. The route shipped (#9884, merged 16:26Z) and has now been read against the live VM.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. Add `GET /api/diag/venue_session?account_id=&symbol=` (Tier-1, token-gated read) over the existing accessor. Return the state, the reason string, the resolved `timeZoneId`, and whether the tz resolved via zoneinfo or pytz — the LAST of those is the field that actually answers the tzdata question, and omitting it would repeat the mistake of shipping a surface that cannot answer what it was built for.
2. Three states must survive to the response uncollapsed; the route must not turn `unknown` into an error or an empty body.
3. Add it to the diag relay allowlist in the SAME change — #9627 shipped a writer whose read surface was never registered, and #9693's route needed a follow-up PR for the same reason.
4. Then answer the question: read it for MGC and MES on the live VM and record the verdict.

items.title: scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh justifies its restart-decision gate by citing a BL-20260714 deploy-stale id three times, and that id is filed in no backlog
items.detail:
Lines 85, 246 and 559 of `scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh` cite a `BL-20260714` deploy-stale-on-out-of-band-sync tracking id, including the one at line 246 that states the gate's central rationale — 'restart when the RUNNING code is stale'. It caught this only because I copied the id into a new backlog row and it became 'introduced'. That default is right for adoption and wrong for finding this class.

NOT FILED BY ME DELIBERATELY: I do not know what that investigation concluded, and inventing a row to satisfy a guard is the 'cheaper to lie to than to satisfy' failure this repo names explicitly. It needs whoever ran it, or a decision to drop the citations.

items.title: 6 of 14 scripts that declare a `--self-test` are never run with it by run_guards.py — triage which (if any) guard a real invariant
items.source: Measured while building `scripts/ci/check_selftest_wiring.py` (the generalisation of BL-20260817-COLLAPSED-STATE-SELFTEST-REGISTERED-BUT-NEVER-INVOKED). That guard's scope is deliberately the `guard_selftests.py::SELFTESTS` registry, because registering there IS the claim 'this control runs in CI'. Owning a `--self-test` is not that claim. But the wider set was measured rather than assumed empty, and it is not empty.
items.evidence: AST scan over scripts/**.py for an `add_argument("--self-test")` declaration, intersected with the argv list parsed out of `run_guards.py::GUARDS`. 14 declare the flag; 8 are run with it by run_guards.py; 6 are not: scripts/backtest_pairs.py, scripts/backtest_xsec_momentum.py, scripts/ops/get_env.py, scripts/research/m20_wf_effective.py, scripts/research/pairs_dollar_lots.py, scripts/research/pairs_universe_scan.py. Reproduce with the snippet in the docstring's SCOPE section.
items.why_not_fixed_in_session: Wiring all 6 into CI would be a unilateral judgement about research/ops tooling, made overnight with no operator available, and it adds runtime plus failure surface to every CI run for scripts whose correctness is not a repo invariant — the desensitised-alarm shape this repo has a P1 rule about. The honest disposition is per-script triage, not a blanket sweep.
items.proposed_action: Triage the 6 individually. `ops/get_env.py` is the most likely genuine candidate (it sits on the diag/env read path that BL-20260813-ENV-VARS-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE made load-bearing); the backtest/research four are probably correct to leave as developer-invoked. For any script judged to guard an invariant, give it a `run_guards.py` entry — `check_selftest_wiring.py` then reports the ratio moving on its own.
items.not_a_finding_about: This is NOT a claim that those 6 self-tests are broken — each passes when invoked by hand. The finding is only that CI does not exercise them, so a future regression in one would not be caught by CI.
items.resolution_criteria: Each of the 6 named scripts has an explicit recorded disposition — either a `run_guards.py` entry running it with `--self-test` (verifiable by re-running the AST scan in `check_selftest_wiring.py`'s SCOPE docstring and seeing the run-with-flag count rise from 8), or a one-line note in this row stating it is developer-invoked by design and why. The row closes when the scan's 'never run with the flag' list contains only scripts carrying such a note — i.e. zero UNTRIAGED entries, not necessarily zero entries.

I read selftest-wiring-guard's live output this review: it reports 11 registered self-tests in guard_selftests.py::SELFTESTS with 11 covered, all resolving to a verified covering path. items.title: M20's '12 actionable' figure counts accrual-, data- and decision-gated cells as workable; only ~4 are workable by a session today
items.source: Measured while picking the next M20 work item: I enumerated the 23 done-condition cells and read each block REF rather than trusting the status string. The '23 = 3 pending + 20 blocked, 11 arithmetic ⇒ 12 actionable' framing (which I put in ROADMAP.md and quoted in three Telegram pings tonight) subtracts only ONE gate — the exit_head_ml fold arithmetic — and silently treats the other nine gates as work.
items.evidence: Full partition of the 23, by reading each cell's ref: (a) 11 exit_head_ml ARITHMETIC (u=0, need 52-118 more trades); (b) 4 ACCRUAL-gated on lifetime — mes_trend_long_1d giveback_stop + vol_trail (lifetime 33, OOS n=4, measured TWICE at two different splits to prove the window was not the binding term), spy_trend_long_1d vol_trail (lifetime 48 against a >=50 requirement), qld_trend_long_1d vol_trail (lifetime 31); (c) 2 DATA-gated — ict_scalp_mgc_15m exit_head_ml + exit_ladder, blocked:native-history-thin; (d) 1 PARKED milestone-wide by a finding — squeeze_breakout_4h exit_ladder, 'partial-TP banking is parked (banking underperformed run-the-winner)'; (e) 1 TIER-3 QUEUED — splg_trend_long_1d vol_trail, whose ref already says 'WE LOOKED - THE BLOCK REASON NO LONGER HOLDS - BUT GRADING IS WITHHELD'; (f) 1 HARNESS CODE GAP — squeeze_breakout_4h vol_trail, AST-verified that scripts/backtest_squeeze.py has --trail-mult but no --trail-vol-above-pctl; (g) 3 pending, the trend_donchian_eth_prop / _sol_prop cells. 11+4+2+1+1+1+3 = 23, reconciles exactly.
items.why_it_matters: The number is used to decide what a session picks up, and it is wrong in the direction that wastes sessions: a reader plans against 12 workable cells and finds 4. Worse, the four accrual-gated rows in (b) are the SAME KIND of block as the 11 already excluded — differing only in which threshold binds (lifetime vs fold count) — so excluding one and not the other is arbitrary rather than principled. Two of those refs also record that a PRIOR ref overstated the leg's lifetime (spy 'said 60, harness measures 48'; qld 'said 57, measured 31'), which is how spy was screened as eligible in the first place: the same over-optimism one level down.
items.resolution_criteria: OBSERVABLE: `m20_coverage_rollup.py --done-condition` prints the done-condition set PARTITIONED BY GATE KIND with a count per kind, and names which kinds are workable-by-a-session, so no consumer has to re-derive it by reading 23 refs. The row closes when the rollup itself emits the partition — not when a doc states the number, because a number in prose goes stale silently and this one already did.
items.proposed_action: Extend the rollup to classify each done-condition cell by its block reason into {arithmetic, accrual, data, parked, decision-queued, harness-gap, never-attempted} and print the per-kind counts beside the total, the same 'state the population' discipline the headline-vs-done-condition split already follows. Until then, quote the partition explicitly rather than a single 'actionable' number.
items.not_a_finding_about: This is NOT a claim that any cell's STATUS is wrong — every status and ref I read is accurate and well-evidenced. The defect is purely in the roll-up framing that collapses six different gates into one word.

updates.note:
RESOLVED at the TOOL, per this row's own resolution criterion ('the rollup emits the partition itself' — deliberately not 'a doc states the number', because prose goes stale silently and this one did).

⚠️ SHARPER THAN FILED: I found while fixing it that the roll-up ITSELF printed the figure (`read the done-condition as {cells_to_done - unreachable} actionable + {M} arithmetic`). So this was never one author's quoting slip — EVERY consumer of the script was told '12 actionable' by the tool. That is why it reached ROADMAP.md and three operator pings.

⚠️ AND AN EXISTING TEST PINNED THE DEFECT. `test_fold_reachability_is_derived.py::test_the_done_condition_SPLITS_actionable_from_arithmetic` asserted the literal `f'{actionable} actionable + {unreachable} arithmetic'` string. Its INTENT was right ('the kinds of remaining work must be legible as different kinds') — two kinds were simply not enough. Rewritten to the STRONGER contract (the partition must reconcile to cells_to_done AND its arithmetic bucket must equal the set fold_reachability names) rather than deleted, with the history recorded in its docstring so nobody restores the old assertion.

SHIPPED: `gate_partition(matrix, reach)` keys on the STATUS STRING the matrix already carries, so it cannot drift from the cell, and REUSES the passed-in `fold_reachability` rows for the arithmetic subset instead of re-deriving the bound — two derivations drifting is the defect this file already carries a test for. Live output: 11 arithmetic · 5 accrual · 3 never_attempted · 2 harness_gap · 2 data = 23, reconciling exactly, ZERO unclassified. It also PRINTS which kinds are movable by a session (harness_gap + never_attempted only) and states plainly that it CANNOT recover 'parked milestone-wide' / 'measured, grading withheld' because those live in ref prose — a tool guessing them would be manufacturing a verdict.

Note the count moved 4 → 5 accrual vs my hand partition: `splg`'s `insufficient_oos_base_at_derived_split` is accrual BY STATUS, while I had labelled it 'Tier-3 queued' from its ref. Totals reconcile to 23 either way; the basis differs, and the status basis is the one a tool can defend.

VERIFIED BY PLANTING BREAKS, not by reading: (a) making an unknown reason fall back to `accrual` instead of `unclassified` fails `test_unknown_blocked_reason_surfaces_as_unclassified`; (b) restoring the old 'actionable +' output line fails `test_output_no_longer_claims_a_single_actionable_number`. Both restored green after. New file `tests/test_gate_partition.py` (8 tests) also pins that no cell lands in two buckets and that an UNGRADED reach row stays `accrual` rather than being called arithmetic — absence of a graded bound is not evidence of an unreachable one.

items.source: Found while confirming that `n` in the census SUMMARY meant what I was about to build a finding on (it is `v['n_trades']`). Counting header cells against row cells — arithmetic, not proofreading — gave 13 of 15 and exposed the shift. Measured on census run 32015369620.
items.evidence: `scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py` census branch. MEASURED by COUNTING cells, not proofreading — on the 1 rendered row of census run 32015369620 (squeeze family, 1 leg planned / 1 measured / 0 errored), **13 of 15** declared columns received a value (header 15 cells, data row 13, ERROR row 7). Rendered mapping was `gb R med`<-near_miss_90_pct, `nm@90%`<-near_miss_measured_n, `nm pop`<-target_r_reached_n, `tgt hit`<-near_miss_r_left_on_table (an R-SUM under a COUNT's header), `R left`/`R->tgt`<-nothing. Confirmed against that real row: `tgt hit` printed `None` where target_r_reached_n is `0`, and `gb R med`'s true value (r_left_median) never appeared at all. Both dropped accessors are computed upstream — `r_left_median` and `near_miss_r_to_target` resolve in scripts/exit_capture.py (1 and 5 matches) and had **0 of 2** read by the sweep. Positive control for that absence claim, same file and pattern style: `near_miss_r_left_on_table` 3 matches, `near_miss_90_pct` 4 matches — so the zero was real and not a probe failure.
items.why_it_matters: Sub-class A of the diagnostic-provenance rule and the written-and-never-read class at once. It defeated TWO guards the table explicitly claims: the comment 'nm@90% ALWAYS ships beside its denominator' (the denominator rendered under the RATE's header), and r_left_median's own stated purpose ('the MEDIAN ships beside the sum so the skew is visible without opening the artifact'). Worst, the table's prose says 'Read `R->tgt` INSTEAD of `R left`' — and `R->tgt` was the column that never rendered, so the census's own headline instruction pointed at an empty cell. The census is M20's measure-first instrument ('the census is the reason this workflow exists'), so a mislabelled near-miss/target column feeds exit-design decisions. The committed docs/research/M20-exit-capture-census-2026-08-10.md is NOT affected (its tables are 3/5/6/7 cells — an earlier format predating the ladder/winners/Rwt columns), so the blast radius is census SUMMARYs produced by the current code.
items.proposed_action: RESOLVED in the same session. Introduced `CENSUS_COLUMNS` as the ONE width/name source (header, alignment row, error-row padding, and per-row cell count all derive from it), extracted `census_row_cells()` so the column->accessor mapping is unit-testable, added the two dropped accessors, padded the ERROR row to full width, and made a row whose width disagrees RAISE rather than be written. New tests/test_census_summary_columns.py (5 tests) pins the MAPPING, not just the width — verified by planting three breaks: swapping two accessors while keeping width at 15 fails ONLY the mapping test (proving a width-only test would have shipped a still-shifted table), the original 13-value row fails 3 tests, and dropping a cell on an absent ladder fails the ladder test. All restored green.
items.resolution_criteria: The census SUMMARY renders one cell per declared column with each column showing its own accessor, and tests/test_census_summary_columns.py passes — including its mapping assertions for `gb R med`, `nm@90%`, `nm pop`, `tgt hit` and `R->tgt`.
items.not_a_finding_about: The census MATH. Every statistic in scripts/exit_capture.py was computed correctly; this was purely the rendering of them. Findings drawn from columns 1-9 (leg/kind/n/cap med/cap w-med/cap Rwt/cap <30%/gb>=1R/gb R left) are unaffected — that prefix was always aligned.

items.title: squeeze_breakout_4h/vol_trail was assessed 'not worth building the harness lever' partly because a derived OOS split was projected into the 25-35 band; measured n=101 puts it at the full 50-trade target, so that ground does not hold
items.source: Picked up the one remaining M20 harness_gap cell to see whether the lever was worth building, and read the ref's own forward assessment against resolve_split's code.
items.evidence: The cell's ref (2026-08-13, self-labelled a PROJECTION) gives three grounds for EV LOW; ground (2) reads 'a derived IS/OOS split of n=135 lands the OOS base in roughly the 25-35 band against the harness's 25-trade floor — i.e. MARGINAL'. `resolve_split` clamps via `if len(stamps) < 2 * target_oos` with DEFAULT_SPLIT_TARGET_OOS=50 and MIN_OOS_TRADES=25, and the sweep's default is `--split-mode oos-trades` — so the clamp only fires below lifetime 100, and `leg_too_thin` needs lifetime < 50. MEASURED 2026-08-17 via census run 32015369620 (families=squeeze, tp_cap_pct=0.099): **n=101**, planned 1 / measured 1 / errored 0. At 101 the derivation targets the full 50 OOS trades — 2x the floor — and even at 99 the clamp yields 49. The '25-35' figure is what you get by treating the 25 FLOOR as the TARGET, the same conflation #9847 corrected in m20-exit-lever-sweep.yml's `split_target_oos`/`split_mode` input descriptions. The constants' own comment forbids it: 'Do NOT re-couple these to one constant.' The same census measured the PRIZE this leg was never weighed against: cap <30% = 72.73%, giveback 9/45 (20.0%) at the 1R rung costing 13.275R, and exit_kind `target_inert` — a declared 50.0R target no trade ever approached.
items.why_it_matters: This is the only M20 done-condition cell in the harness_gap bucket that a session could act on, and it was shelved on an arithmetic step that contradicts the harness's documented derivation. Ground (1) — the negative fleet vol_trail prior — still stands, but it is a prior about OTHER legs and the matrix _doc forbids an inherited verdict; ground (3) existed only to argue accrual could not relieve ground (2). So the decision now rests on ground (1) alone, weighed against a measured capture deficit on this leg rather than against a projection.
items.proposed_action: Build `--trail-vol-above-pctl` / `--trail-vol-below-pctl` / `--trail-vol-tight-mult` into scripts/backtest_squeeze.py mirroring backtest_trend.py + backtest_pullback.py, add `squeeze` to the `fam in ("donchian", "pullback")` gate in `cells_for`, and sweep the leg (Tier 1 throughout). Correct the cell's ref so the withdrawn projection is not re-quoted. Do NOT flip the cell status as part of the harness change: `blocked:no_harness_levers` is the true state until the lever exists AND a sweep grades it. Shipping any resulting lever is Tier 3.
items.resolution_criteria: Either the squeeze harness carries the vol_trail flags and the cell has a measured sweep verdict, or the cell's ref records a decision NOT to build it that does not rest on the withdrawn 25-35 projection.
items.not_a_finding_about: The cell's STATUS, which is correct — `cells_for` genuinely emits vol_trail cells only for the donchian/pullback families and scripts/backtest_squeeze.py genuinely has no `--trail-vol-*` flag. Nor is it a claim that the lever will PASS; the fleet prior is negative and the sweep may well return another honest_negative.
