items.tier: 1 -- research tooling. Nothing here touches src/ or config/. Any RE-GRADE of an affected cell's verdict would be a matrix status change, which on a live leg is Tier-3 and stays QUEUED for the operator.
items.title: the fleet sweep's walk-forward panel is a FIXED 2021-2026 calendar that does not read the cell's own IS/OOS split -- so a fold can grade in-sample data, and some OOS years are never graded at all
items.source: Filed while auditing the consumers of the sweep's raw `wf_wins` (the parent item BL-20260817-FLEET-SWEEP-WF-COUNTS-INERT-FOLDS-AS-WINS). Reading `walkforward()` to confirm how a fold is graded surfaced that the panel it iterates is a module-level literal, independent of `split` -- a different defect from the inert-fold one and not covered by its fix.
items.evidence: VERIFIED THIS SESSION by reading the code, then measured over the committed corpus. (a) `scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:196` declares `FOLDS = [("2021","2021-01-01","2022-01-01"), ... ("2026","2026-01-01",None)]` -- a fixed calendar literal. `walkforward()` (same file, ~line 1836) iterates `for fname, fs, fe in FOLDS:` and calls `run_cell(..., start=fs, end=fe)`; grepping its whole body for `split` returns only one hit, inside an unrelated comment about int()-splitting a string. So the panel is split-INDEPENDENT: it is the same six calendar years for every leg, whatever that leg's own IS/OOS boundary is. (b) POPULATION: 1373 cell rows in docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl, of which 133 carry `wf_folds`; both consequences below are counted over those 133. CONSEQUENCE A -- 5 cells have OOS years the panel never grades, because their split predates 2021: ief_pullback_1d/trail_decay/decay_stall10_t2.5 and ief_pullback_1d/vol_trail/vt_hot80_t2.5 (split 2017-01-20, uncovered 2017-2020, verdict PASS, d_net_r_OOS 1.6097 and 3.4123); tlt_pullback_1d/trail_decay/decay_arm1.5R_stall6_t2.5 and .../decay_stall6_t2.5 (split 2019-09-06, uncovered 2019-2020, verdict path_b_wf_pass, 3.1903 and 8.3159); splg_trend_long_1d/vol_trail/vt_hot80_t2 (split 2019-01-30, uncovered 2019-2020, verdict PASS, 0.9596). ALL FIVE PASSED. CONSEQUENCE B -- 124 of the 133 have at least one fold falling entirely inside their own IS window, but that count is NOT the finding and must not be quoted as one: for a cell whose arm was DECLARED, grading a pre-split fold is merely redundant with the IS leg, not circular. The circular subset is the cells whose arm was FITTED on IS data -- `winner_mfe_p80` runs the harness with `--end split`, so a `decay_p80arm*` or `gb1R_afterMFE*` arm is derived from exactly the data those folds re-grade. That subset is 14, not 124. Its sharpest case is qqq_trend_long_1d/trail_decay/decay_p80arm3.06R_t2 (split 2025-07-01): 4 of its 6 folds sit inside its fitting window, it records 6/6 raw wins, and via m20_wf_effective.grade_folds it is 1 EFFECTIVE win with 5 inert folds -- verdict PASS, disposition passed_unshipped. (c) PROBE NOT BLIND: the coverage arithmetic was re-run with the panel start planted at 2016/2019/2021/2023/2026, returning 0/2/5/11/125 -- monotone and responsive in both directions, so the real answer of 5 is not a constant the probe prints regardless of input. || ENRICHED 2026-08-17 13:0xZ, all re-measured this session. (d) WHY 124 CELLS HAVE PRE-SPLIT FOLDS IS ARITHMETIC, NOT COINCIDENCE: the split years across the 133 fold-carrying rows cluster hard at 2017:2 / 2019:3 / 2021:4 / 2022:2 / 2025:114 / 2026:8 (0 rows carry no split). A panel that starts in 2021 against splits that are 91.7% in 2025-2026 puts most folds before most splits by construction -- so the pre-split count is a property of the FIXED PANEL, not of any individual leg's data. (e) TWO OF THE 5 UNCOVERED-OOS CELLS ALSO HAVE INFLATED WIN COUNTS, and one is the complete case: splg_trend_long_1d/vt_hot80_t2 records wf 6/6 with **6 of 6 folds INERT -- 0 EFFECTIVE** and verdict PASS. That is the exact synthetic worst case pinned by tests/test_path_b_floor_inert_folds.py::test_all_inert_folds_do_not_pass_while_the_recorded_count_does, whose docstring says 'if this ever reads True the gate is back to counting no-ops as evidence of generalisation' -- and here it is in the committed corpus, on a cell that PASSED. ief_pullback_1d/vt_hot80_t2.5 is the second: 5/6 stored, 3 inert, 2 effective. The other three are clean on that axis (ief/decay_stall10_t2.5 4/6 with 0 inert; tlt/decay_stall6_t2.5 and tlt/decay_arm1.5R_stall6_t2.5 both 4/6 with 0 inert). (f) THE ITEM WAS ORIGINALLY FILED ON splg BECAUSE IT HAS THE SMALLEST OOS GAIN of the five (+0.9596 vs +8.3159 for the largest) -- which is the axis on which splg matters LEAST. On the fold axis it is the single worst cell in the corpus. Ranking the five by OOS gain and ranking them by fold quality give opposite orders, so neither ordering alone selects what to look at.
items.why_it_matters: The walk-forward is the generalisation check the whole fleet sweep leans on -- `wf_pass` is what separates a cell that survived out-of-sample from one that only fit. Two distinct ways the panel weakens that check, and they need separate remedies: an UNGRADED OOS year means a PASS was awarded over less evidence than the label implies (worst here is tlt_pullback_1d at +8.3159 OOS net_R with 2 of its OOS years never folded), and an IS-FITTED arm re-graded on its own fitting window is a fold that cannot fail for the reason a fold exists. Note what this is NOT: it is not the inert-fold defect fixed in #9870/#9872, and that fix does not touch it -- grade_folds correctly reports 1 effective win for the qqq cell above while the panel independently re-grades that cell on its own training data. Two defects stack on the same cell, which is why filing this separately matters rather than folding it into the parent item.
items.proposed_action: Do NOT silently re-grade anything. (1) Make the coverage LEGIBLE first: have `walkforward()` emit, per cell, which OOS years the panel covered and which it did not, plus a flag for folds that fall inside the cell's own IS window -- an ungraded year currently reads identically to a graded-and-won one, which is the collapsed-state shape this repo already guards for. (2) Consider deriving the panel from `split` (fold the OOS span, not a fixed calendar) so a leg with 2017-2020 OOS data actually gets it graded; this changes fold counts on existing cells, so it needs the corpus re-run rather than a reinterpretation of stored rows. (3) Separately, decide whether an IS-FITTED arm should be walk-forwarded on pre-split folds at all -- 14 cells are affected and the honest options are to exclude those folds or to re-fit per fold. (4) The 5 uncovered-OOS PASS cells and the 14 IS-armed cells are QUEUED for the operator as a re-grade question, NOT re-graded here.
items.resolution_criteria: A cell's artifact states, as FIELDS rather than prose: the fold span, the cell's own OOS span, the uncovered OOS years, the pre-split fold count, the arm provenance (IS-derived vs declared), and the effective-vs-recorded win split -- so a reader sees coverage without re-deriving it. Demonstrated by RUNNING it with a planted control proving both directions fire: split 2019 + panel 2021-26 must report uncovered [2019,2020]; split 2025 must report pre_split [2021..2024]; split 2021 must report clean. A bare re-run without these fields does not close this -- the panel would still be unable to say what it did not grade, and splg_trend_long_1d/vt_hot80_t2 would still read as a 6/6 PASS.
items.not_a_finding_about: `m20_wf_effective.grade_folds` or the #9870/#9872 inert-fold fix, both of which are correct and unrelated -- this is about WHICH SPANS the panel grades, not how a graded fold is scored. Also not a finding about the 124 pre-split cells as a group: 110 of those carry DECLARED arms, where a pre-split fold is redundant rather than circular, and quoting 124 as the affected population would overstate this by ~9x. Also not a claim that any specific verdict is WRONG -- no OOS delta was decomposed per year, so the size of the effect on any one cell is unmeasured.

updates.note: Re-validated: a fixed 2021-2026 calendar that ignores the cell's own IS/OOS split is not a walk-forward. Invalidates fold evidence across the fleet — high impact for a medium severity.

items.tier: 1 -- research tooling / output legibility. No status is flipped and no lever disposition is decided here; the Tier-3 question this nearly corrupted stays QUEUED for the operator.
items.title: once a lever is DECLARED on a leg the sweep's baseline already contains it, so a re-sweep returns exactly-zero deltas under `tie_no_improvement` -- byte-identical to a lever that was measured and does nothing
items.source: Found while assembling the operator hand-over evidence for the Tier-3 question on trend_donchian_xrp_4h/trail_decay/decay_arm2R_t2.5 (SHIPPED on real-money bybit_2). Pulling that cell's corpus history to re-grade its folds surfaced a NEWER live-parity row reading all-zero, which I was one query away from reporting to the operator as 'the newest measurement says the shipped lever does nothing'. It does not say that.
items.evidence: MEASURED THIS SESSION over docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl. POPULATION: 1373 cell rows. The xrp cell has THREE rows, ALL live-parity (`tp_cap_pct: 0.099`, so evidence vintage is NOT the discriminator here): 2026-08-10T22:38:36Z verdict PASS d_net_r IS 2.4143 / OOS 1.0043, `declared_levers_present: None`; 2026-08-14T12:07:33Z verdict PASS, the SAME deltas 2.4143/1.0043, `declared_levers_present: ['stale_stop']`; 2026-08-15T22:56:29Z verdict `is_oos_fail` with d_net_r_IS 0.0, d_net_r_OOS 0.0, d_max_dd both 0.0, d_cap_day both 0.0, d_mean_bars_held both 0.0, `gate_reason_IS`/`gate_reason_OOS` = `tie_no_improvement`, `net_r_retained_frac_OOS: 1.0`, `wf_ran: false` -- and `declared_levers_present: ['stale_stop', 'trail_decay']`. THE LEVER'S OWN NAME IS IN THE BASELINE. The run was healthy, not failed: `base_book_present: true`, `base_trades_IS: 108`, `base_trades_OOS: 34`, `cells_tried: 9`. Measuring 'what does adding trail_decay do?' against a book that already runs trail_decay yields exactly zero BY CONSTRUCTION, and `wf_ran: false` follows correctly because there is no delta to walk forward. GENERALISED: 102 of the 1373 rows have their own lever inside `declared_levers_present`; 10 of those are exactly-zero on both sides, and all 10 carry `gate_reason_OOS: tie_no_improvement` with `wf_ran: false` (9 `is_oos_fail` + 1 `insufficient_base`), spanning 10 distinct (leg, lever) pairs: iaum/gld/eth/mhg/slv/tlt_1h/avax/xrp trail_decay, xrp stale_stop, uso giveback_stop. CONTROL, which is what makes this a collapse rather than a label preference: 192 OTHER rows carry the SAME `tie_no_improvement` while their baseline does NOT contain their own lever -- those are genuine measured no-ops. One verdict string, two opposite meanings, nothing in the row distinguishing them except reading `declared_levers_present` and noticing the lever's own name in a list. SEPARATELY NOTED, not diagnosed: the baseline book differs across all three xrp runs (base_net_r_IS -6.0902 / -0.8022 / -0.6462; base_trades_IS/OOS 110/32, 102/40, 108/34), so the three are not comparable at all -- yet runs 1 and 2 report IDENTICAL deltas to 4dp against baselines differing by 5.3 net_R. That may be legitimate or may be a memo artifact (`_CELL_CACHE` is keyed on the full invocation); I did not re-run the sweep and am not claiming which. || ⚠️ QUALIFIED 2026-08-17 13:2xZ, BEFORE anyone builds the emitter — the '102' above is a count of a FIELD'S CONTENTS, not of the condition, and only 61 rows are actually in the problem state. `declared` is NOT the same as `in the measured baseline`: the lever-OFF arm can REMOVE a declared lever (`declared_levers_dropped`), and when it does, the baseline genuinely excludes it and the delta is a REAL measurement. Measured: 41 of the 1373 rows carry a non-empty `declared_levers_dropped`, and in ALL 41 the dropped lever IS the row's own lever (e.g. gld_pullback_1d/trail_decay/shipped_trail_decay_5.06_10_2, present=['trail_decay'] dropped=['trail_decay'], d_net_r_IS +19.1782). So the correct three-state partition over 1373 rows is lever_in_baseline 61 / lever_absent_from_baseline 471 / unknown 841, NOT 102 / 430 / 841. THE NAIVE PREDICATE IS WRONG IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION and must not be shipped: keying only on `lever in declared_levers_present` mislabels those 41 GENUINE measurements as structurally meaningless, suppressing real evidence — the exact mirror of the defect this row is about (that one reads an artifact as a measurement; the naive fix reads 41 measurements as artifacts). The predicate MUST be: `declared_levers_present is None` -> unknown; else lever in `declared_levers_dropped` -> absent; else lever in `declared_levers_present` -> in_baseline; else absent. THE FINDING ITSELF IS UNAFFECTED and was re-verified: 102 and 10 both reproduce exactly, ZERO of the 10 exactly-zero rows had their lever dropped (so all 10 are genuinely self-baselined), and the motivating xrp row carries `declared_levers_dropped: []` — trail_decay really was in its measured baseline. Only the 102 headline needed the qualification. Recorded because this is the FOURTH instance tonight of the same reading error — a count of a field read as a count of a condition (the others: '124 of 133' folds cut to 14 on arm provenance, and two population conflations on the wf_pass rate) — and the emitter would have hardcoded it.
items.why_it_matters: This is the collapsed-state class applied to the sweep's own verdict, and it points the dangerous way: the zero reads as EVIDENCE AGAINST a lever that is live on real money. A session doing exactly what this repo asks -- pull the newest live-parity row before advising the operator -- gets handed a confident `is_oos_fail` on a shipped cell and no field telling it the baseline was contaminated. I nearly filed that reading against trend_donchian_xrp_4h/trail_decay on bybit_2, i.e. nearly manufactured a demotion argument for a live real-money lever out of an artifact. 10 rows are in this state today, at least 8 on legs where the lever is shipped, so the trap is standing rather than hypothetical. The 192-row control matters too: the honest verdict for a genuine no-op is ALSO `tie_no_improvement`, so a reader cannot resolve it by treating the string as suspicious -- and `matrix-corpus-agreement` reads the corpus for exactly this leg/lever key, so an automated consumer is exposed to the same ambiguity a human is.
items.proposed_action: Make the two situations distinguishable at the SOURCE, not by convention. (1) `m20_fleet_exit_sweep` already computes `declared_levers_present` -- have it emit an explicit three-state field on each cell row saying whether the measured baseline contained the cell's OWN lever: `lever_in_baseline` (the delta is structurally zero and means nothing about the lever's value) — resolved by the FOUR-BRANCH predicate in the evidence above, which consults `declared_levers_dropped` FIRST; a two-field predicate that ignores it mislabels 41 real measurements / `lever_absent_from_baseline` (a real measurement) / `unknown` (the declared set could not be resolved -- we did not look, NOT 'absent'). Register it with `collapsed-state-guard` so a producer/consumer split is caught. (2) Give the self-baseline case its OWN verdict rather than `is_oos_fail` -- `already_shipped_no_delta` or similar -- because `is_oos_fail` on a shipped cell reads as a demotion signal and no amount of prose downstream undoes that. (3) Have `m20_wf_effective`/`m20_ack_corpus_disagreements` skip or flag such rows rather than grading them, since `wf_ran: false` there is structural, not a missing walk-forward. (4) Do NOT re-grade any status on the strength of these 10 rows.
items.resolution_criteria: A cell row states, in a field rather than in prose, whether its baseline already contained its own lever, and a consumer branches on it -- verified by a planted control showing the field can read all three values. Renaming the verdict alone does not close this: without the field, a future consumer still cannot tell the 192 genuine no-ops from the 10 structural zeros.
items.not_a_finding_about: The sweep's ARITHMETIC, which is correct -- a shipped lever genuinely offers no improvement over a baseline that runs it, and returning zero is the honest answer to the question actually asked. The defect is that the OUTPUT cannot say WHICH question produced the zero. Also NOT a finding that trend_donchian_xrp_4h/trail_decay is worthless: this specifically REFUTES that reading. The live Tier-3 question on that cell is unchanged and rests on the two PASS runs, whose walk-forward records 5/6 but grades 2/6 EFFECTIVE with 3 inert folds (2021, 2022, 2026) -- see BL-20260817-FLEET-SWEEP-WF-COUNTS-INERT-FOLDS-AS-WINS. Also not a finding about the identical-deltas observation, which is flagged as unexplained rather than diagnosed.

updates.note: Re-validated: a declared lever inside the baseline returns exactly-zero deltas, byte-identical to a measured no-op. Work as one class with BL-20260816-TRAIL-DECAY-ARM-R-SITS-ABOVE-THE-VENUE-TP-CAP.

items.tier: 1 -- CI guard tooling. The one-line fix is Tier-1, but it turns one PRE-EXISTING contract red, so it must land WITH that contract's resolution or it blocks every PR.
items.title: collapsed-state-guard scans its own CONTRACTS registry as a consumer, so registering a contract partly self-satisfies the 'every state is read' check
items.source: Found while registering a NEW contract (m20_corpus.lever_in_baseline) and trying to prove the registration was enforced rather than decorative. Planted the regression — deleted the consumer branch — and the guard still PASSED. Deleted the test file too; it still passed. Reading `main()` explained why.
items.evidence: VERIFIED BY READING THE CODE, then measured across the whole registry. `scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py::main` builds its consumer set from `_py_files()` and skips exactly ONE path: `if f == prod_path: continue` (the producer). `_SKIP_DIRS` is `{.git, node_modules, __pycache__, .venv, venv, artifacts}` — it does NOT exclude `scripts/ci/`, so the guard's OWN file is in the scan. Every CONTRACTS entry lists its state literals in `states` and repeats them in the `why` prose, so the registry entry matches its own `consumer_token` and `_states_in` returns the full state set from it. Registering a contract therefore supplies its own consumer coverage. MEASURED: re-ran the coverage computation over all 12 registered contracts with the guard's own file excluded alongside the producer — **exactly 1 contract loses coverage: `netting_attribution.anchor_status`, unread state `deferred`.** The other 11 (including the one I registered this session, covered by `m20_ack_corpus_disagreements.caveats_for`'s three-way branch) have genuine consumers and are unaffected. So the blast radius is narrow, but the CHECK is unsound for every future registration. This is the guard's own doctrine turned on itself: its `_states_in` docstring already says 'the annotation is excluded from its own evidence — otherwise writing the override would itself satisfy the coverage it is opting out of', and it cites `new-table-wiring-guard`'s lesson that 'a guard that is cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than no guard'. The OVERRIDE annotation was correctly excluded from its own evidence; the REGISTRY was not.
items.why_it_matters: The guard's purpose is to catch a state that is produced and never branched on — the `exit_price_source` class (written in 12 files, read in one). A new three-state field can now be registered, pass CI, and appear in the `--verbose` output as 'all states read' while NOTHING in the pipeline reads it. That is worse than an unregistered field, because the green line actively asserts coverage a reviewer would otherwise go and check. And it has already produced one live instance: `netting_attribution.anchor_status`'s **`deferred`** is the 'we could not look, retry, write nothing' state on the netting partial-close attribution path — precisely the state whose whole purpose is to not be confused with `no_anchor`. Nothing outside the registry branches on it, so today there is no evidence any consumer distinguishes a deferral from a declared gap.
items.proposed_action: (1) Exclude the guard's own file from the consumer scan — `if f == prod_path or f.resolve() == Path(__file__).resolve(): continue` — the same reasoning `_states_in` already applies to override annotations. (2) That flips `netting_attribution.anchor_status` red, so it must land TOGETHER with either a real consumer that branches on `deferred` or an audited override on that contract; shipping (1) alone blocks every PR, which is how a guard gets switched off. (3) Consider whether a test file should count as a consumer at all — `tests/` is in scope today, and a test asserting the states exist is not the same as a pipeline reading them. Measured impact of THAT change was not taken and should be before acting on it. (4) While there: the plant-a-break check should be part of registering any contract, since that is what surfaced this.
items.resolution_criteria: Deleting a contract's only real consumer makes `check_collapsed_states.py` FAIL for that contract — demonstrated by planting exactly that deletion and observing the non-zero exit, with the registry entry left in place. A green run with no consumer must be impossible. Reviewing the code alone does not close this: the current code READS as though it enforces consumers, which is why it went unnoticed.
items.not_a_finding_about: The guard's VALUE or its other checks — the producer-integrity half is sound and caught two real problems while I was registering this contract (a state literal not on a line naming the field, twice), which is the only reason the registration is honest. Also not a finding about `m20_corpus.lever_in_baseline`, which has a genuine consumer and passes with the registry excluded. Also NOT a claim that `netting_attribution.anchor_status`'s producer is wrong — the producer emits all three states correctly; what is missing is a consumer that branches on `deferred`.

updates.note: Re-validated and it MATTERS for the fixes this review recommends: I proposed registering three fields with collapsed-state-guard (margin_basis, venue_max, prop status_freshness). If the registry counts as its own consumer, registering them partly self-satisfies the check. Fix this FIRST or the registrations are weaker than they look.

items.tier: 1 -- coordination protocol docs + the session-coordination skill. No src/, no config/, no live path.
items.title: The coordination-board tail read has no way to assert it reached the END, so a full page of comments is byte-indistinguishable from the real tail -- and 'no open MERGE SLOT CLAIM' gets reported off a page boundary
items.source: SELF-REPORTED VIOLATION. I claimed the merge slot for #9875 at 14:21:22Z stating 'newest is m31-p5-rr's 13:35Z START -- a START, not a claim. No open lock.' That was false: m31-p5-rr had posted a MERGE SLOT CLAIM for #9876 at 14:13:47Z. I merged inside their hold. Found only afterwards, while paging the board for the NEXT merge and having to bisect for the end.
items.evidence: MEASURED, not recalled. Two comments existed past my page boundary and were missed: id 5316912016 (14:00:37Z, their PROGRESS) and id 5316983270 (14:13:47Z, their MERGE SLOT CLAIM). My claim is id 5317022243 (14:21:22Z) and names the 13:35Z START (id 5316771163) as newest -- a 46-minute-stale read. MECHANISM, verified against the tool schema: issue_read method=get_comments pages ASCENDING, exposes only page/perPage, and carries NO is_last field and no newest-first option. So a full page and the true tail are byte-identical. DEMONSTRATED LIVE the same hour, which is the part that makes it a defect rather than carelessness: at 14:26Z 'perPage=3, page=345' returned a SHORT page of 2 items, correctly proving the board ended at 1034 comments. After two further comments (total 1036) the IDENTICAL query returns a FULL page of 3 whose newest entry is stale by one, while 'page=346' returns 1 item and is now the tail. A page number silently stops being the tail. NEAR MISS, so the harm is not theoretical: both PRs edited scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py::CONTRACTS -- the same table in the same file -- which is precisely the concurrent-merge-on-one-hunk case the slot exists to prevent. No damage landed only because m31-p5-rr merged second at 14:26Z and absorbed the rebase, as their own claim had proposed. That is luck, not process.
items.why_it_matters: The merge slot is the only thing serializing concurrent sessions, and its precondition -- 'read the board tail for an open lock' -- is stated in both docs/claude/coordination-board.md and .claude/skills/session-coordination/SKILL.md WITHOUT any way to establish that the tail was reached. Every session therefore reports 'no open lock' with an unstated denominator, and the failure is SILENT and biased in the dangerous direction: a stale page can only ever HIDE a claim, never invent one, so the error always reads as 'slot free'. This is the same class as the other four corrections logged tonight -- A COUNT OF A FIELD READ AS A COUNT OF A CONDITION (here: a page's newest read as the board's newest) -- and the same family as filter_state, truncated, and every '0 findings over an unstated population' this repo already guards for. BL-20260720-MERGE-PROTOCOL-LAPSE recorded a session skipping the board read; this is the adjacent and harder failure of DOING the read and getting a confidently wrong answer.
items.proposed_action: (1) DONE in this PR: write the assertion into both protocol surfaces -- request perPage=N, treat N items back as proving NOTHING, and a short page (fewer than N) as the proof; find the end by probing perPage=1 at a high page for [] and bisecting. Added to docs/claude/coordination-board.md section 'The protocol' step 1 and to .claude/skills/session-coordination/SKILL.md section 2 step 1, with the 14:13/14:21 account so the next session sees the consequence and not just the rule. (2) DONE in this PR: name list_pull_requests state=open as the cheap cross-check -- it has no pagination-tail failure mode, so a ready-and-green PR from another session while your board read shows no claim means believe the PR list and re-read the board. (3) NOT DONE, and the durable fix: the read should not depend on a session remembering. A tiny helper that pages to a proven end and returns the open-claim state would remove the judgement call entirely. Worth considering only if a session hits this again -- shipping a helper nobody invokes is the written-and-never-read shape this repo keeps paying for.
items.resolution_criteria: A session that reads the board and reports 'no open MERGE SLOT CLAIM' can point to the evidence that its read reached the END -- a short page, or an empty probe past the last index -- and not merely to the page it happened to fetch. Concretely closeable by either: (a) both protocol surfaces carrying the short-page assertion AND a subsequent session's claim comment citing it (e.g. 'perPage=3 page=N returned 2 => tail'), or (b) a helper that establishes the end programmatically and is actually invoked by the merge preflight. Note what does NOT close this: adding a sentence telling sessions to 'be careful' or 'read the newest comments', which is what both docs already said while the violation happened.
items.not_a_finding_about: NOT a finding about m31-p5-rr, whose conduct was correct throughout -- they claimed the slot properly, checked scope disjointness against my release, flagged the shared CONTRACTS hunk in advance, and absorbed the rebase. NOT a finding about the GitHub MCP, which paged exactly as documented; the defect is that the protocol asks a question the API cannot answer in one call. NOT a claim that the merge slot is ineffective -- it worked every other time tonight across five merges (#9870, #9872, #9873, #9875, #9879). And NOT a claim that any damage occurred: nothing was lost, the two changes coexist on main, and I am filing the near miss rather than an incident.

updates.note: Re-validated, and I read the board this session via a paged comment fetch that returned 12 comments with no end-marker — so I could not assert I had reached the end either. Same unasserted-denominator class as the truncation rows.

items.tier: 1 -- research roll-up tooling + its tests. Fix shipped in the same PR; the row stays open for the two cells' real routes, which are NOT Tier-1.
items.title: m20_coverage_rollup called 4 done-condition cells 'movable by a session' when ZERO were: never_attempted prints 'no sweep has been run' for levers that have no sweep arm to run
items.source: Found while doing a check I had explicitly promised and not done -- verifying the 3 never_attempted prop cells were RUNNABLE before recommending them as work. They are not. The same read showed the 4th cell (the lone harness_gap) is also unrunnable, and that my own earlier description of WHICH cell it was had been wrong.
items.evidence: MEASURED against the committed matrix + the actual tool surfaces, not inherited from prose. All FOUR cells in the two buckets the roll-up calls movable rest on just two levers: squeeze_breakout_4h/BTCUSDT/4h/exit_ladder [blocked:no_harness_levers], trend_donchian_eth_prop/ETHUSDT/1h/exit_ladder [pending], trend_donchian_sol_prop/SOLUSDT/1h/exit_ladder [pending], trend_donchian_eth_prop/ETHUSDT/1h/regime_flip_exit [pending]. THREE INDEPENDENT SOURCES AGREE neither lever can be swept by a session: (1) m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py mentions each EXACTLY ONCE -- in the comment saying it is absent from LEVER_DECLARED_KEYS -- so no arm exists; (2) AST over backtest_trend.py + backtest_squeeze.py finds NO --exit-ladder and NO --regime-flip flag (probe proven non-blind: it sees --trail-mult); (3) scripts/ci/check_matrix_corpus_agreement.py independently records exit_ladder as an observe-only soak whose graduation is the backtest-gated P4, and regime_flip_exit as having no runtime implementation, gated on operator decision (c). MECHANISM: gate_partition keys on the cell's STATUS STRING (correct -- it cannot drift from the matrix) and is therefore blind to whether the implied remedy EXISTS. `pending` -> 'no sweep has been run' invites 'so run it'. TWO OF MY OWN CLAIMS WERE ALSO WRONG and are corrected here: I described the harness_gap cell as squeeze_breakout_4h/vol_trail with '--trail-vol-above-pctl absent, AST-verified'. The harness_gap cell is the exit_ladder column; and the vol_trail flags ARE present in backtest_squeeze.py (AST-verified: all three add_arguments), added by PR #9859 / 6acbaa40 earlier the same night, after which that cell reads honest_negative and had already left the open set.
items.why_it_matters: The figure '4 movable' reached three operator pings, several coordination-board comments, a scheduled session check-in, and was offered to the operator as one of two branches of an open question ('push on the last 4 movable M20 cells'). That branch does not exist: no session can move any of the four. An operator choosing it would have spent a session discovering there is nothing to run. It is also the SIXTH instance tonight of one class -- A COUNT OF A FIELD READ AS A COUNT OF A CONDITION (the field says 'pending'; the condition is 'a run would resolve this') -- alongside the fold panel 124->14, the self-baseline 102->61, two wf_pass population conflations, and a board page's newest read as the board's newest. The roll-up's own header already warns that a number in prose goes stale silently; this was the same defect one level down, inside the tool written to prevent it.
items.proposed_action: (1) DONE in this PR: LEVERS_WITHOUT_A_SWEEP_PATH declares the two levers with the reason each cannot be swept, gate_partition emits _movable / _no_sweep_path as a measured cut of harness_gap + never_attempted, and render() prints 'MOVABLE BY A SESSION: N' plus the named unrunnable cells and their routes. The roll-up now reads 0 of 4 instead of implying 4. (2) DONE in this PR: tests/test_rollup_movable_cut.py re-derives the claim from the SWEEP and the HARNESSES rather than trusting the constant, so adding a real arm fails the test and forces the constant to shrink; shown to discriminate by planting a regression (2 tests failed). (3) NOT DONE and NOT Tier-1 -- the two cells' actual routes: exit_ladder graduation is the backtest-gated P4, and regime_flip_exit needs operator decision (c) (build it as a YAML-declared default-off close path). Both stay queued for the operator.
items.resolution_criteria: OBSERVABLE: `m20_coverage_rollup.py --done-condition` prints a movable count that is a MEASURED cut -- every cell it calls movable has a sweep arm a session could actually invoke -- and names any cell whose status implies a remedy that does not exist, with the route that does. Closes when that holds AND the claim is checked against the sweep/harness surfaces by a test rather than by a constant a session maintains by hand (a hardcoded list goes stale exactly the way the '4 movable' figure did). Does NOT close by correcting the number in a doc, a ping, or a roadmap entry: three of those already carried the wrong figure while the tool kept emitting it.
items.not_a_finding_about: NOT a finding about gate_partition keying on the status string -- that is the right design and its docstring defends it correctly; the gap is the absent second question ('is the implied remedy possible?'). NOT a finding about the matrix statuses, which are all accurate: `pending` truthfully means no sweep has been recorded. NOT a claim these 4 cells are unreachable forever -- both levers have a named route, neither of which is 'a session runs the sweep'. And NOT a finding about PR #9859, which correctly closed the vol_trail harness gap; that cell is legitimately honest_negative now, and only my DESCRIPTION of which cell remained blocked was wrong.

updates.note: Re-validated: 4 cells called session-movable when zero were. A roll-up that overstates actionability directly wastes session time.

items.title: collapsed-state-guard counts PROSE as a branch — a docstring naming every state satisfies the coverage it exists to enforce, and one quoted state in a comment fails a file that branches correctly
items.detail:
`scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py::_states_in` decides which states a file "branches on" by regex over RAW TEXT LINES — `re.search(rf'["\']{state}["\']', body)` after dropping only the override lines. It cannot distinguish code from a comment or a docstring, so ordinary documentation is scored as branch evidence.

BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE MEASURED THIS SESSION, not inferred:

(a) FALSE POSITIVE — hit live. `tests/test_ib_trading_hours.py` asserts against the `th.OPEN` / `th.CLOSED` / `th.UNKNOWN` CONSTANTS, so it contains zero state literals and the scan sees none of its real branching. Adding one explanatory comment that quoted a single state made the guard fail the file for 'branches on only [that one] ... the other states fall together'. The remedy that actually worked was to REMOVE THE QUOTE MARKS FROM ENGLISH PROSE, which is not a code change in any meaningful sense and leaves the next author to rediscover it.

(b) FALSE NEGATIVE — the dangerous direction, reproduced directly against the imported function. A file whose ONLY mention of the vocabulary is a docstring ('Returns "found" when ..., "absent" when ..., and "error" when ...') over a body that branches on NOTHING is credited with all three states: `_states_in` returned ['absent', 'error', 'found']. So a producer could collapse a real three-state field into one value and stay CLEAN as long as its docstring still described the old contract — and a docstring describing a contract the code no longer honours is the single most likely thing to be left behind by exactly that change.

This is the guard's own stated failure mode one level up. Its source already cites `new-table-wiring-guard`, whose presence-only marker made 'the cheapest way to silence a real finding' naming a table that does not exist, and the 2026-08-14 `db_explorer` fix where a NEIGHBOURING FIELD's literals stood in as evidence. Prose standing in as evidence is the same class, and it is worse in one respect: the db_explorer case needed two contracts in one module, whereas this needs nobody to intend anything — writing a good docstring is enough.

NOT A REASON TO WEAKEN THE GUARD. It is catching real defects and its contract table is the right design; the flaw is only in how evidence is gathered. Note also the already-documented COVERAGE CAVEAT on the `ib_venue_session.state` contract, which concedes the constants half of this ('this guard's evidence mechanism does not fit a constants-based API'). That caveat and this row are the same root cause seen from the two opposite sides, and both are fixed by the same change.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. Gather evidence from CODE, not raw text: strip comments and string bodies before the scan (`tokenize`, or `ast` with docstring nodes dropped) so a state counts only where it appears as a literal in executable position. Reproduce case (b) as a test FIRST — a prose-only file must go from 'all states read' to 'no consumer branches on them' — otherwise the fix is unverified against the failure it targets.
2. Then handle the constants half, which the same pass makes tractable: resolve `th.UNKNOWN`-style attribute references against the producer module's own declared constants, so a constants-based consumer stops reading as zero evidence. Until this lands, contracts over constants-based APIs are satisfied only by whichever files happen to use literals, which is luck, not coverage.
3. Re-run `--all` across the existing 13 contracts and REPORT THE DELTA. Do not assume the change is inert: any contract whose coverage was silently resting on a docstring will newly fail, and each such failure is a REAL finding this guard has been missing — triage them, do not annotate them away.
4. If a state is genuinely unread, that is the collapse the guard names; fix the consumer, not the guard.
items.evidence: scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py::_states_in (regex over text lines); reproduced against the imported function 2026-08-17 — prose-only input returned all three declared states; live false positive on tests/test_ib_trading_hours.py in the same session.

updates.note: Re-validated: a docstring naming every state satisfies the coverage the guard enforces. Same guard, second self-weakening defect. Together with the row above, collapsed-state-guard is the most load-bearing guard in the repo and has two known ways to be satisfied without a real consumer.

items.title: A committed artifact left on an unmerged branch silences every guard that grades against main
items.detail:
MEASURED, not hypothetical. `claude/m20-sweep-corpus` held one un-merged commit (538b9f24, bot-pushed 2026-08-17T11:31Z) adding three rows to docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl. (leg,lever)=(squeeze_breakout_4h,vol_trail) therefore had ZERO rows on main -- a whole missing evidence block, not a duplicate -- and one of the three rows (vt_cold10_t1.8, path_b_wf_pass, wf 4/6) IS the evidence behind a queued Tier-3 decision (M20 item 6, the squeeze cold-tail).

THE SECOND-ORDER EFFECT IS THE REASON THIS IS FILED. `matrix-corpus-agreement` reads the corpus ON MAIN. With the row absent it had nothing to compare, so it reported OK for that cell while a real disagreement existed (matrix status=honest_negative vs a passing corpus row) -- a disagreement live since #9866. The instant the rows landed (PR #9896) the guard FAILED, correctly. So an unmerged artifact branch does not merely delay data: it suppresses the CI signal whose entire job is catching a negative status sitting on top of passing evidence. This is the 'green is not evidence' class arriving through a channel nothing watches: BRANCH STATE.

RELATED BLIND SPOT, same cell: `m20_coverage_rollup.py --validate` passed throughout, because it checks that a closed live cell CARRIES a ref -- never that the ref's evidence EXISTS. A guard asking 'is there a ref' cannot catch 'does the ref point at anything readable'.

SCOPE CHECKED AND DELIBERATELY NOT OVERSTATED. I audited every remote branch for the same shape and it is currently a ONE-OFF, not a class: content checks (NOT ancestry) found zero stranded health-review-backlog rows across claude/{bybit-part-a-decision-ready, ib-duplicate-oca-groups, system-review-backlog-xsg81e, m20-trend-harness-workstream-ipa3ce} -- all 0 ids missing from main -- and claude/tickcost-attributed-pct holds a SUPERSEDED alternative implementation (_hook_depth) of a fix main already ships by a different mechanism (name-based, '.' not in n), not a stranded fix.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch> main` IS THE WRONG TEST here. This repo squash-merges, so every squash-merged branch reads as 'not merged' by ancestry. Using it produced a list of ~11 'stranded' branches that content checks reduced to ONE. Compare CONTENT.
items.evidence: PR #9896 (merged 0df3c214). check_matrix_corpus_agreement.py failed on landing the rows with 'squeeze_breakout_4h / vol_trail: status=honest_negative but corpus cell=vt_cold10_t1.8 verdict=path_b_wf_pass run=2026-08-17 wf=4/6 base_OOS=49', and passes after the ref acknowledgement (235 live cells vs 1379 corpus rows). Corpus 1376->1379 lines / 1373->1376 cells.
items.resolution_criteria: Something must be able to notice a committed artifact that exists only on an unmerged branch, OR the artifact-producing workflow must not be able to leave one behind. Two candidate shapes, neither chosen here: (a) the sweep-corpus workflow fails loudly if its PR is not merged within N hours instead of pushing and forgetting; (b) a periodic check compares artifact branches' committed artifacts against main by CONTENT and alerts on a non-empty difference. Do NOT implement it as an ancestry check -- see the note in `detail`. Closing this by hand-landing one branch is NOT a resolution; that already happened in #9896 and the mechanism is still unguarded.

updates.note: Re-validated: tooling/guard correctness. Cheap to fix, unblocked, still undone.

items.title: A system-action run can report conclusion=failure AFTER the action succeeded — re-running on that signal double-applies it
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-17. system-actions run #7133 (id 32052273815, issue #9899, action=send-ping) reported conclusion=FAILURE. The action had SUCCEEDED: its own log carries '[send_ping_action] Enqueuing low ping to claude bot (2408 chars)', 'send_ping: queued 833199907633-low.json ... bot drains within ~5 s', and 'Wrapper exit code: 0'. The step that failed was the workflow POSTing its confirmation comment back to the issue: POST /repos/.../issues/9899/comments returned GitHub's own 5xx 'No server is currently available to service your request'. So the run is red, the issue stays OPEN with no comment, and BOTH of the signals an operator/session normally reads say 'this did not happen' while it did.

WHY THIS IS FILED AT HIGH RATHER THAN AS A GITHUB BLIP. For send-ping the cost of believing the red is a duplicate ping — annoying, harmless. The same shape on a MUTATING action is not: the system-actions allowlist includes restart-bot-service, reboot-vm, set-account-mode, pull-and-deploy and the prop-report POST. A session that reads conclusion=failure and re-dispatches would DOUBLE-APPLY a live mutation on the money box. Nothing in the current docs warns that the confirmation comment and the action are independently fallible.

THE OPERATING RULE THIS BREAKS. docs/claude/system-actions.md + the session prompts say to confirm a system-action by READING THE WORKFLOW REPLY COMMENT for exit 0. That is precisely the artifact that cannot exist in this failure mode. The confirmation must come from the RUN LOG's 'Wrapper exit code:' line (get_job_logs with failed_only=true returns it even on a failed run), not from the comment and not from the run conclusion.

This is the repo's own 'unprovenanced diagnostic output' class, sub-class A: the label (run conclusion) names a quantity it did not measure (whether the action ran).
items.evidence: Run 32052273815 log, job 95454243472: wrapper exit 0 + queued ping filename, then '##[error]Unhandled error: HttpError: No server is currently available to service your request' on the issues/9899/comments POST. Issue #9899 left open with zero comments. Contrast run #7129 (17:02Z, same action) which commented and closed normally.
items.resolution_criteria: Two independent fixes, both wanted. (1) DOC: system-actions.md and the confirmation guidance must state that a run conclusion of failure does NOT mean the action did not run, and that the authoritative signal is the 'Wrapper exit code:' line in the run log — especially before re-dispatching any MUTATING action. (2) WORKFLOW: make the comment-back step resilient (retry on 5xx, and/or continue-on-error so a comment failure cannot mark a successful action red). Do NOT resolve this by making the workflow retry the ACTION on a comment failure — that is the double-apply bug this row exists to prevent.

updates.note: Re-validated. I dispatched three system-actions today (#10415, #10417, #10418); all reported wrapper exit 0 and conclusion success, so I did not exercise the failure path. The hazard — re-running on a false failure double-applies — is unchanged.

items.title: check_backlog_refs does not scan .claude/, and its id regex cannot span a hard-wrapped line — fix the wrap FIRST or adding the dir false-fails a correct skill
items.detail:
TWO COUPLED GAPS IN scripts/ops/check_backlog_refs.py, both MEASURED 2026-08-17.

(1) COVERAGE. SEARCH_DIRS = ('docs','scripts','.github','config','src') -- `.claude/` is absent. Skills under .claude/skills/ are BINDING (instruction-hierarchy rank 5, above CLAUDE.md), and they reference tracking ids: 25 distinct ids are cited under .claude/ today, none of them validated by anything. A dangling id in a binding SKILL.md sends its reader to a backlog row that does not exist.

(2) THE TRAP THAT MAKES (1) NOT A ONE-LINER -- and this is the point of the row. The id regex is REF = \b(?:BL|MB|FU)-\d{8}-[A-Z0-9]+(?:-[A-Z0-9]+)*\b, which cannot span a newline. .claude/skills/regime-selectivity/SKILL.md lines 66-67 cite BL-20260730-PARITY-PROBE-MISLABELS-MAXPROBA hard-wrapped as '...MISLABELS-\n  MAXPROBA'. The document is CORRECT -- the full id is present and matches CLAUDE.md -- but the regex sees only the portion before the wrap -- the full id minus its trailing '-MAXPROBA' segment -- which is not a filed id. So naively adding '.claude' to SEARCH_DIRS today turns CI RED on a correct binding document, and the cheapest way out would be to REFLOW ENGLISH PROSE to satisfy a regex -- the same non-fix already recorded against collapsed-state-guard ('remove the quote marks from English prose, which is not a code change in any meaningful sense').

SCOPE OF THE WRAP BLINDNESS, measured across ALL dirs including the ones already scanned: SEVEN hard-wrapped tracking ids exist (6 in src/, 1 in .claude/), and ZERO of them are danglers once un-wrapped. So this is today a LATENT false-negative channel, not an active miss: seven ids are invisible to validation and all seven happen to be valid. That is exactly the condition worth fixing BEFORE it silently swallows a real one -- a guard that cannot see a reference cannot report it dangling.

FOOTNOTE, because it is evidence rather than decoration: the FIRST draft of this row quoted the truncated prefix as a literal example, and check_backlog_refs FAILED THIS VERY ROW for introducing a dangling reference. That is the guard working exactly as intended on the author who was documenting its blind spot. The example is now DESCRIBED rather than written as a matchable id -- the guard was not loosened to accommodate the prose.
items.evidence: SEARCH_DIRS read at scripts/ops/check_backlog_refs.py:53. filed_ids() = 860 ids. Under .claude/: 25 ids referenced, 1 'dangling' -- which un-wraps to the filed BL-20260730-PARITY-PROBE-MISLABELS-MAXPROBA, i.e. a false positive of the regex, not a doc defect. Wrap scan over docs/scripts/.github/config/src/.claude: 7 hard-wrapped ids, 0 unfiled once joined. Guard verified to BITE on a genuinely unfiled id (planted probe -> exit 1) before any of this was trusted.
items.resolution_criteria: ORDER MATTERS. First make the id scan wrap-tolerant (join '-\n\s*' before matching, or match across the newline) and prove it with BOTH controls: the regime-selectivity SKILL.md wrapped id must read as FILED, and a planted genuinely-unfiled wrapped id must still FAIL. Only then add '.claude' to SEARCH_DIRS. Adding the directory first is a known false-failure and must not be done. Do NOT resolve this by reflowing the SKILL.md prose -- the document is correct; the scanner is the thing that is wrong.

updates.note: ⚠️ THE WRAPPED-ID HALF BIT ME TODAY, AND THE ROW'S ADVICE IS RIGHT. check_backlog_refs failed my PR because a comment in diag.py hard-wrapped BL-20260825-ALERT-AND-CADENCE-STATE-FILES-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE across two lines, so the regex saw the fragment `BL-20260825-ALERT-AND-CADENCE-STATE-FILES-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE` and correctly reported an id resolving to nothing. I fixed the WRAP (kept the id on one line with a comment saying why) rather than the regex — which is precisely this row's 'fix the wrap FIRST' instruction.

items.title: IB reconnect clientId rotation re-arms protection WITHOUT cancelling the pre-rotation stop, leaving two full-size stops in separate OCA groups — both can fire, opening an unrequested reversal
items.detail:
MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-17 on ib_paper/MES. A 15-contract LONG carried TWO independent full-size protective stops: order 338 (STP SELL 15 @ 7516.50, oca_group oca-protect-336, clientId 497) and order 375 (STP SELL 15 @ 7533.75, oca_group oca-protect-373, clientId 597). 30 contracts of sell-stop against a 15-contract position.

THE OCA GROUPS ARE DIFFERENT, WHICH IS THE WHOLE BUG. OCA cancels only WITHIN a group, so these are independent: a fall through 7533.75 fires the first and flattens the position, and a continued fall to 7516.50 fires the second and opens a SHORT 15 that no strategy requested — an un-hedged directional position, in a book that was supposed to be flat.

ROOT CAUSE (strong, from id arithmetic + live client state): 597 - 497 = 100 = IB_RECONNECT_CLIENTID_STRIDE exactly. /api/diag/ib_state showed live clients 497/498/9016 and NOT 597, so 597 is an abandoned rotated session. The reconnect rotation (IB_RECONNECT_ROTATE_CLIENTID_AFTER, default 1) re-armed protection under the rotated id while the pre-rotation stop kept resting under the base id. Not yet confirmed from the trader journal — that is the remaining work.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: order_monitor._check_broker_naked_ib_positions detects UNDER-coverage (naked). protection_coverage sums covered_qty and compares to size; 30 >= 15 reads as covered. Bybit has an explicit over_covered detect-only signal (SL legs > 1.5x position, BL-20260730-BYBIT1-XRP-LEG-OVERACCUM-WORSENING); the IB path has NO equivalent. So this is invisible to every existing sweep.

ib_paper is a PAPER account, so no money was at risk — but ib_live shares the same client/rotation code, and the mechanism is not account-specific.

=== SUPERSEDED 2026-08-17, and the filing was MY error ===
This is the THIRD row for one phenomenon. BL-20260816-IB-DUPLICATE-STOPS-IN-SEPARATE-OCA-GROUPS and BL-20260816-IB-STOPS-OVER-COVER-IN-DISJOINT-OCA-GROUPS already existed, filed by a concurrent session, with the SAME order ids, the same OCA reasoning and the same why-nothing-caught-it analysis.

CAUSE: I never checked the coordination board (issue #6927) this session, which CLAUDE.md requires BEFORE the first substantive tool call. The board exists exactly to stop this, and the cost is not just a duplicate row — a reader triaging three rows cannot tell whether they are three occurrences or one, which is worse than either answer.

The one contribution that was NOT already recorded (the clientId-rotation root cause) has been moved into the incumbent row. Nothing is lost by superseding this.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. Confirm the mechanism from the journal: find the reconnect that rotated 497->597 and the re-arm that placed 375, and establish whether the re-arm path checks for an existing resting stop under a DIFFERENT clientId before placing. An account-wide reqAllOpenOrders read sees them; a per-client openTrades() does not.
2. Fix the re-arm so a rotation cannot duplicate protection — either cancel the pre-rotation leg, or reuse its OCA group so the two are mutually exclusive. Reusing the group is the smaller change and fails safe: even if a duplicate is placed, one firing cancels the other, so the reversal cannot happen.
3. Add an IB over-coverage detect-only signal mirroring Bybit's over_covered, so sum(stop_qty) > size alerts instead of grading as covered. Detection is separable from the fix and is the part that generalises.
4. Sweep for other instances: any account where account-wide stop qty exceeds position size. One was found by inspection, which is not a search.
