items.title: cancel-ib-order reports cancel_not_effective + exit 1 for a cancel that DOES complete moments later — correct at the instant it checks, wrong as a final verdict, and it invites a blind retry
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-17. `cancel-ib-order --apply` on ib_paper MES order 375 (perm 166865400, clientId 597) returned:
  cancel_response: {retCode: 0, retMsg: OK}
  action: cancel_not_effective
  verify_state: still_present
  remaining: [order 375, status PendingCancel, remaining 15]
  wrapper exit 1 -> the issue comment renders a red FAILED

An independent /api/diag/ib_open_orders read ~4 minutes later showed the order GONE: account count 3 -> 2, only MES 338 and MGC 359 remaining. The cancel SUCCEEDED.

The verdict was accurate AT THE INSTANT IT CHECKED — the order genuinely was PendingCancel — and the honest-verification design is RIGHT and must not be weakened: reporting broker acceptance as success is the accepted-!=-done class this repo has been bitten by repeatedly (order 378 the same day; BL-20260816-IB-CANCEL-REPORTS-CANCELLED-ON-ACCEPTANCE).

The defect is narrower: the window does not accommodate a CROSS-CLIENT cancel, where we connect as an abandoned clientId to cancel its order and IB takes longer to service it. The failure mode is a false NEGATIVE, which is the safe direction for correctness and the UNSAFE direction for operator behaviour — a red FAILED on a successful mutation is exactly what provokes a blind retry against an order already in PendingCancel. It also cost a real verification round to disambiguate.

Separately observed in the same run: an ib_insync teardown traceback (RuntimeError: Event loop is closed, 'Exception ignored in IB.__del__') after the work completed. Almost certainly benign exit noise, recorded rather than filtered.

SCOPE vs BL-20260816-IB-CANCEL-ACCEPTED-BUT-NEVER-COMPLETES-VENUE-CLOSED (which predates this and covers the same signature): that row is about the BROKER behaviour — why an accepted cancel does not complete. This row is only about the TOOL's verdict semantics — that `still_present` collapses two different broker states into one label and exits red for both. Kept separate because the fixes are independent: the broker question may never be fully answerable from our side, while the verdict split is a small, self-contained change. If a reviewer prefers one row, fold this into that one — do not drop the verdict-split point.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. Do NOT widen the window into a blocking wait on the live path without a bound — the point of the verification is that it is cheap and honest.
2. Make PendingCancel its OWN state rather than folding it into cancel_not_effective. `still_present` currently conflates 'the broker refused / did nothing' with 'the broker ACCEPTED and is working on it' — two different facts with different correct responses (investigate vs wait). This is the collapsed-states rule applied to the ops layer: a `cancel_pending` verdict should exit 0 with a clear 're-verify, do not re-issue' instruction.
3. Exit code should reflect that distinction, since the issue comment renders exit != 0 as a red FAILED and that is what a reader acts on.
4. Add the post-check the session had to do by hand: a short bounded re-read (or an explicit instruction naming /api/diag/ib_open_orders) so the operator is not left to invent the verification step.
items.evidence: issue #9913 (apply -> cancel_not_effective, exit 1, PendingCancel) vs #9914 (independent read 4 min later: order absent, count 3 -> 2)

updates.note: Re-validated and it is the mirror of BL-20260816-IB-CANCEL-ACCEPTED-BUT-NEVER-COMPLETES-VENUE-CLOSED: one row says the cancel never completes, this says the verify window is too short to see it complete. Both are live today (Saturday, venue closed). Resolve them together.

items.title: A multi-account order package is exit-managed on ONE leg only: _apply_update resolves matched_trade from linked_trade_id, so every sibling leg keeps its entry-time bracket forever and a monitor close strands it outside the loop
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-18 against the live journal.

MECHANISM (code). src/runtime/order_monitor.py's strategy loop iterates ORDER PACKAGES (`get_order_packages_by_strategy(strategy_name, status="open")`), and BOTH effectuation branches of `_apply_update` resolve a SINGLE trade row:
    linked_trade_id = open_pkg.get("linked_trade_id")
    rows = db.get_trades(filters={"id": int(linked_trade_id)})
`Coordinator.multi_account_execute` fans ONE package out to N accounts => N trade rows sharing one `order_package_id`, but `linked_trade_id` names exactly one of them. So:
  * MODIFY half — `_send_modify_to_exchange(matched_trade, ...)` amends ONE account's bracket, and the `trades` sync writes `stop_loss`/`take_profit_1` on that ONE row. Every other leg keeps its entry-time bracket permanently. Every M20 lever, exit head, trail, stale-stop and giveback therefore reaches ONE leg per package.
  * CLOSE half — the exchange close is sent for `matched_trade` only, then `update_order_package(pkg_id, {'status':'closed'})` flips the PARENT. Because the loop selects `status="open"`, the package is never revisited: the sibling legs are now permanently outside dynamic-exit management, journal-open, and still open at their venue.

`_cascade_close_netted_siblings` does NOT cover this — its query is scoped `AND account_id=?` (intra-account netting only). No other path closes a cross-account sibling.

POPULATION AND EVIDENCE (all rows, live journal, 2026-08-18T06:5xZ):
  * 35 open trades across 26 packages; 9 packages hold >1 open trade.
  * 4 of those 9 have DIVERGENT sibling stops right now — in every case the moved leg is the `linked_trade_id` leg:
      pkg-7cb8577792ca4006 xrp_pullback_2h  trade 4163 bybit_2 SL 1.04193571 (trailed, linked) vs trade 4164 bybit_portfolio SL 1.10786786 (entry-time)
      pkg-1c66870763c34f10 qqq_pullback_1h  4468 alpaca_paper 716.115 (linked) vs 4469 alpaca_portfolio 704.3275
      pkg-32a5162bbbdd4ef6 spy_trend_long_1d 4347 alpaca_paper 744.47714286 (linked) vs 4348 alpaca_portfolio 733.91821429
      pkg-a687f228480e4f96 tlt_pullback_1d  4169 alpaca_paper 83.6825 (linked) vs 4170 alpaca_portfolio 85.26875
    The other 5 agree only because no modify has fired on them yet.
  * 6 of 35 open trades (17%) sit under a package already flipped to `closed` — permanently unmanaged:
      4719 bybit_portfolio BTCUSDT / 4717 bybit_1 BTCUSDT (pkg-830fb965b6db48ff, linked 4718, close_reason exit_head)
      4550 alpaca_portfolio SLV (pkg-84cb11011d584f3e, linked 4549, exchange_flat_reconciled)
      4547 bybit_portfolio ETHUSDT (pkg-0b2900a5c90d4f08, linked 4546, reconciler_filled)
      4484 alpaca_portfolio GLD (pkg-5c895576ebe64107, linked 4483, exchange_flat_reconciled)
      4135 bybit_portfolio ETHUSDT (pkg-e6eac664c2a446a6, linked 4134, sl_cross)
  * CAUGHT LIVE THIS MORNING: pkg-830fb965b6db48ff (trend_donchian BTCUSDT long) fanned to THREE accounts. The monitor's `exit_head` verdict at 2026-08-18T05:00:17Z closed the linked real-money leg 4718 (bybit_2, qty 0.004, +$0.177) and flipped the package. Legs 4717 (bybit_1, 0.034) and 4719 (bybit_portfolio, 0.609) are still journal-open AND confirmed still open at Bybit via /api/diag/exchange_positions.
  * INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION from exit-reason distributions: bybit_portfolio has 24 closed trades and ZERO monitor-driven exits (19 reconciler_filled, 3 intent_reduce_executed, 1 netting_attributed, 1 intent_reduce) — no sl_cross, no tp, no stale_stop, no exit_head, no vwap_cross. Its managed sibling bybit_2 has 15 sl_cross, 10 sl, 10 vwap_cross, 4 tp, 3 exit_head, 3 stale_stop over 171 closes. alpaca_portfolio shows monitor exits ONLY on packages where it is itself the linked leg (single-leg packages such as uso_trend_1h and spy_pullback_1h).

WHAT THIS IS NOT. The sibling is NOT naked: its entry-time bracket rests at the venue (Bybit/Alpaca attach SL/TP atomically), which is why the harm shows up as `reconciler_filled` rather than a runaway. This is a MANAGEMENT defect, not a PROTECTION defect, and it should not be triaged as the naked-position class.

WHY IT MATTERS ANYWAY. (a) The `*_portfolio` books are declared in CLAUDE.md as the paper mirror of the live-traded portfolio and are what the dashboards' "Paper" toggle renders — but they run a STATIC exit policy while the book they claim to mirror runs the MANAGED one. The mirror is not a mirror, so its P&L is not comparable to the real book and must not be read as 'what the portfolio would have done'. On Alpaca the assignment is inverted and worse: `alpaca_paper` (the soak book) is consistently the linked/managed leg and `alpaca_portfolio` (the portfolio book) is the unmanaged one. (b) Trade 4135 (bybit_portfolio ETHUSDT short) has run unmanaged since its package closed `sl_cross` and sits at -$350.30; the strategy said stop out, one leg did, the other did not. (c) No real-money leg is stranded TODAY, but that is luck, not design — `linked_trade_id` is whatever the executor recorded, and nothing guarantees it is the real-money leg. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'fixed' was collapsed to 'resolved' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
items.resolution_criteria: Tier-3, operator-approved. The fix is to make effectuation package-wide: resolve EVERY open trade row for `order_package_id` and apply the modify/close to each leg on its own account, then flip the package only once every leg is confirmed (partial success must leave the package OPEN so the next tick retries the remainder — the same exchange-first discipline the single-leg path already uses). Per-leg outcomes must be three-state (`applied` / `failed` / `not_attempted`) and never collapsed, so a package that half-applied is distinguishable from one that fully applied. Ship the observability half FIRST (Tier-1): a read surface + count of (i) open trades under a closed package and (ii) sibling stops diverging from their package `sl`, so the repair is verifiable and a regression is visible. DONE when: the two counters read 0 for newly-opened multi-leg packages over a full soak window, and a deliberate modify on a multi-leg package is observed moving every leg's venue bracket.

updates.note: RESOLVED -- fix is on main AND deployed AND corroborated on the live book. CODE (read, not inferred): order_monitor._package_open_legs() resolves EVERY open non-backtest row for order_package_id instead of the single linked_trade_id, and returns a never-collapsed ('resolved'|'read_failed') read state. BOTH effectuation arms use it -- close at :831, modify at :1196, and the partial-close remainder RE-READS at :1102 rather than deducing from the earlier list. I checked both arms specifically because a fix applied to one would look complete in the diff. The modify arm genuinely FANS OUT across every leg (:1246) with three-state per-leg outcomes (applied/failed/unsupported), syncs trades.stop_loss ONLY for legs that actually landed, and leaves order_packages.sl/tp unchanged when any leg missed so the verdict re-fires. The close arm deliberately closes ONE leg per tick and leaves the package OPEN while legs remain, so it drains over N ticks without turning one exchange round-trip into N on a loop already breaching its 60s requirement. DEPLOYED, not merely merged (the #9920 lesson): /api/diag/version = 12659c7d = main HEAD, which contains _package_open_legs. LIVE COUNTERS, this row's own DONE condition, measured against 27 open trades (/api/bot/db/table/trades, filter_state 'applied', total 27) in 20 packages of which 6 are multi-leg: divergent sibling stops 4-of-9 -> 0-of-6; open trades under a closed package 6-of-35 -> 1 (trade 4793 alpaca_portfolio USO uso_trend_1h, close_reason 'stuck_cascade_recovered'). WHY 0-DIVERGENT IS EVIDENCE HERE AND NOT JUST ABSENCE: this row correctly warns that siblings 'agree only because no modify has fired'. The TLT pair is what settles it -- 4169/4170 were 83.6825 vs 85.26875 when filed and are BOTH 83.5075 now, i.e. both legs moved TO THE SAME VALUE, which is the fan-out working. DENOMINATOR STATED: 6 packages holding open legs were NOT graded because they fall outside the 200-row /api/bot/order-packages page (the API caps limit at 200); they are neither clean nor flagged. The one remaining open-under-closed row is left for a follow-up read -- its close_reason points at the stuck-cascade path, not at this one.

items.tier: 3 (strategy exit logic) — the IB repair half is Tier-2
items.title: ict_scalp.monitor() emits no take-profit close, so the strategy depends ENTIRELY on a venue bracket nothing verifies — MGC 4487 sat 122.74 points past its declared target for 11 days with zero LMT orders on the account
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-18.

CODE. `src/units/strategies/ict_scalp.py::monitor()` returns exactly two things: `_stale_stop_verdict` (YAML-declared, default-OFF) and `monitor_breakeven_sl` (an SL-modify; it has no close path). There is no `tp_cross` branch. `_stale_stop_verdict` DOES test a TP cross at lines ~798-801 but only as a stop-first GUARD that returns None — the code knows about the crossing and deliberately declines to act, on the stated assumption that 'exchange bracket / normal path owns it'.

ROSTER SWEEP (all strategy modules with a monitor()): four have no TP close path — `ict_scalp`, `fvg_range_15m`, `hf_displacement_cont`, `hf_vwap_revert`. The rest (`trend_donchian`, `fade_breakout_4h`, `htf_pullback_trend_2h`, `squeeze_breakout_4h`, `turtle_soup`, `vwap`) all emit `tp_cross`. So the assumption above is a per-strategy choice that nothing checks against the venue it is routed to.

CONFIG. `ict_scalp_mgc_15m` declares `stale_exit_bars: null` and `stale_exit_below_r: null`, so the stale-stop lever is inert on this leg. Its monitor can therefore ONLY move the stop to break-even — it has no close verdict available at all.

VENUE. `/api/diag/ib_open_orders` on ib_paper returns exactly 2 orders, BOTH `STP`, ZERO `LMT` account-wide (MES stop 7516.5, MGC stop 4278.8). This is the standing BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED condition, still `detection_landed_repair_open`.

INTERSECTION = ZERO COVERAGE. Trade 4487, ib_paper MGC long, qty 105, entry 4272.4, declared `take_profit_1` 4297.65785714, opened 2026-08-07T01:27:44Z. MGC last close 4420.4 — the position is **122.74 points past its declared target** and still open 11 days later, holding +$155,715 unrealized against a stop at 4278.8 (139.2 points below current). Neither exit existed: no resting target at the broker, and a monitor that cannot emit a close.

AGGRAVATOR. /api/bot/notifications currently carries `monitor_blindness` for pkg-dbcc140fd43c4a79 (ict_scalp_mgc_15m, `candles_unavailable` for 3 consecutive ticks) plus three `transient_market_data_unavailable` warnings for MGC/MHG. MGC candles fetch fine from the web-api at 15m, 1h and 1d right now, so the blindness is intermittent in the TRADER process, not structural — it is an aggravator of the finding, not its cause. The cause is that no TP close verdict exists to be blind to.

MES is NOT in this intersection: `mes_trend_long_1d` resolves to the trend_donchian family, which does emit `tp_cross`, so its monitor covers the missing broker target. The Bybit ict_scalp legs (`ict_scalp_xrp_15m`, the real-money `ict_scalp_5m` BTC leg) are covered by Bybit's atomically-attached resting TP.

--- CORRECTION 2026-08-18T08:00Z, same session: IB IS NOT STRUCTURALLY TARGET-LESS ---
This row originally read that on IB 'the strategy has no take-profit path at all', framing the venue as unable to hold a target. That is WRONG and I am correcting it rather than leaving it, because it points at the wrong fix. Read from the code, not inferred:
  * `IBClient._locked_place` (the ENTRY path) DOES build a take-profit child — `tp_price = _round_to_tick(float(order['tp']), tick) if order.get('tp')`, then `tp = LimitOrder(reverse, qty, tp_price)` attached to the parent with `tif='GTC'` as part of the transmitted bracket.
  * `IBClient.place_protective` places an OCA stop+limit PAIR by design.
  * And it demonstrably works: the repair placed order 381 as a GTC LMT into oca-protect-357 on this very account and symbol, and it filled.

WHAT SURVIVES, unchanged and still measured: `ict_scalp.monitor()` emits no `tp_cross` (4 of 10 monitor modules don't); `ict_scalp_mgc_15m` declares no stale-stop, so its monitor can only move the stop to break-even and has NO close verdict available at all; ib_paper held ZERO LMT orders account-wide across three separate reads; and trade 4487 sat 122.74 points past its declared target for 11 days.

WHAT IS NOW UNDETERMINED, and must not be asserted either way: WHY MGC had no resting target. Two candidates, not distinguished by anything measured this session — (a) the entry order carried no truthy `tp` so no child was built, or (b) a target was built and later cancelled or lost. Trade 4487 originated normally (`entry_reason: 'ict_scalp_mgc_15m signal'`, not an adopted orphan) and its journal row carries `take_profit_1 = 4297.65785714`, so a target level EXISTED in the journal — which makes (a) a question about what `execute` passed to `place`, not about whether the level was known.

THE FIX THEREFORE CHANGES SHAPE. Not 'teach IB to hold targets' — it already does. The real defect is that a strategy with no monitor-side TP close depends ENTIRELY on the venue bracket surviving, and nothing checks that dependency is honoured. Note also that a target-side detector DOES now exist (`order_monitor._emit_target_naked_alert` + `summary['target_naked']`, shipped 2026-08-16 for BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED) — so before building anything new, establish whether it FIRED for MGC. See BL-20260818-DID-TARGET-NAKED-EVER-FIRE-FOR-MGC. RE-VERIFIED AND DEMONSTRATED LIVE 2026-08-23 by the full-system audit. CODE: src/units/strategies/ict_scalp.py's monitor() contains ZERO references to take_profit — grep count 0 over the whole function. Its only two paths are the M20 stale-stop (_stale_stop_verdict, YAML-declared and default-OFF) and monitor_breakeven_sl, whose own docstring states it 'only ever returns a break-even SL-modify (no close path)'. So the strategy emits no take-profit close of any kind. LIVE INSTANCE, the same trade this row was filed about: MGC trade 4773 (ict_scalp_mgc_15m, 95 long) declares take_profit_1 = 4393.02071429 and price has run to ~4654 — 233.88+ points past the declared target, ~5.3% — while the position remains OPEN. Broker truth 2026-08-23T07:36Z (/api/diag/ib_open_orders): ib_paper rests exactly one MGC leg, STP SELL 95 @ 4371.1 in oca-protect-389, and NO limit order anywhere on the symbol. So there was no venue bracket to depend on either — the dependency this row names as unverified was not merely unverified, it was ABSENT. scripts/ops/broker_bracket_reconcile.py flags it as target_naked_declared in the same run where MHG (correctly bracketed both sides) grades clean, so this is not a detector artefact. DISPOSITION: the operator's rule of 2026-08-23 ('if the trade has already passed where its brackets should have been since it opened, close it out') applies, and the position is scheduled to be flattened by the 2026-08-23T22:30Z Routine. That closes the INSTANCE and not the CLASS: the next ict_scalp trade will have the same missing close path.
items.resolution_criteria: Split, and do them in this order. (1) MEASURE FIRST: determine why 4487 had no resting target — read what `execute` passed as `tp` on the entry, and whether a TP child was ever created and then lost. Do not build a fix on top of an undetermined cause. (2) Establish whether the existing `target_naked` detector fired (BL-20260818-DID-TARGET-NAKED-EVER-FIRE-FOR-MGC); a second detector for a class that already has one is duplication, and a first detector that is silently not firing is a worse bug than a missing one. (3) Only then, the structural piece: a strategy whose monitor has no TP close should have to DECLARE that it delegates the take-profit to the venue bracket, so the dependency is reviewed rather than implicit — the four modules concerned are ict_scalp, fvg_range_15m, hf_displacement_cont, hf_vwap_revert. (4) Tier-3, and only if (1) says so: give ict_scalp a tp_cross close.

evidence.ib_open_orders: 2 orders, both STP, zero LMT account-wide

updates.note: STILL OPEN, AND IT HAS RECURRED ON A NEW TRADE -- which is a stronger finding than the original, because it happened after the 08-18 repair. MEASURED 2026-08-20T20:23:39Z via /api/diag/ib_open_orders (read_state 'orders_read', a confirmed clean account-wide read) + /api/diag/exchange_positions?account_id=ib_paper + /api/bot/positions?include_paper=true. Trade 4487 (the 105-lot MGC this row is written about) is CLOSED -- flattened 2026-08-18T07:49Z when the operator-approved target attach placed a limit at 4297.7 into a ~4420 market, which was marketable and filled. The CURRENT MGC position is trade 4773: ib_paper, 95 long @ 4364.6, strategy ict_scalp_mgc_15m, opened 2026-08-19T00:27:25Z, declared take_profit_1 4393.02071429, and it holds a resting STP 95 @ 4371.1 and ZERO resting limit orders. MGC last close 4543.5 (/api/bot/candles, source bot-exchange), so the position is 150.48 points PAST its declared target with no resting target and a monitor that has no tp_cross branch -- the exact 4487 configuration, reproduced within 24h on a new trade. At MGC's config-declared contract_value_usd of 10.0 that is ~$143k of gain sitting beyond the declared exit, and ~$164k of give-back between the current price and the resting stop. Paper money, but the leg-resolution and coverage code is account-agnostic. CRITERION (2) IS NOW ANSWERED: the target_naked detector DOES fire -- both banners were live on /api/bot/notifications at 20:30:40Z (see BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED). So this is not a missing detector; it is a detected condition with no repair path, which makes criteria (3) and (4) the live questions. Criterion (1) -- WHY 4773 has no resting target -- is still unestablished and must not be guessed: note only that its stop sits in an 'oca-protect-389' group, the repo-minted keyless form, whereas MHG (the one fully-covered position) carries a numeric IBKR-assigned group 308977633 holding both its legs. That is consistent with this row's hypothesis that a keyless re-arm replaces an SL+TP pair with a stop alone, but it is a correlation on n=1 and is NOT offered as the cause.

LIVE END-TO-END VERIFICATION, on the trader, ~1h after the merge. Trader confirmed on the merged sha (/api/diag/version -> a290ff3f, the #10166 merge commit) BEFORE reading the log, so this is the new code and not the old.

/api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live.service, firing every ~30s on the exit loop:
    order_monitor: ict_scalp_mgc_15m pkg=pkg-b1582c365d264330 symbol=MGC candles=200
      verdict={'action': 'close', 'reason': 'tp_cross', 'exit_price': 4626.9}
    -> IB venue for MGC is closed - exit deferred to next session (protective bracket
       left armed): tradingHours: 20260823 07:27 US/Eastern is inside the covered span
       20260823..20260827 and inside no session - DB left open, no alarm.

THREE THINGS VERIFIED AT ONCE, none of them by inspection:
  1. THE CLOSE PATH WORKS. `ict_scalp` emits `tp_cross` — a verdict it could not produce before today, AST-verified as an empty close-reason set on the pre-merge tree.
  2. THE VENUE GATE WORKS. It defers rather than firing a market order into a shut COMEX (/api/diag/venue_session confirms state 'closed', graded on tradingHours, tz_source zoneinfo, close_would_send_outside_rth true).
  3. THE DEFER IS GRADED AS A DEFER, NOT A FAILURE — 'DB left open, no alarm'. That is the string-matching contract CLAUDE.md flags as fragile ('exit deferred' must appear in the message or the defer is booked as a close FAILURE with a streak and a won't-flatten alarm). It appears.

⚠️ SO MGC 4773 IS STILL OPEN AT +233.9 POINTS PAST ITS TARGET (4626.9 vs 4393.02071429), AND THAT IS CORRECT. It is not a broken close path — it is a correctly-shut venue on a Sunday. It should close at the 22:00Z reopen. Recorded explicitly because the obvious reading of 'still open, far past target' is that the fix did not work, and that reading is wrong.

items.resolution: FIXED 2026-08-23 (Tier-3, operator-approved in-session on a decision prompt carrying the measured blast radius). ict_scalp.monitor now runs the same sl_cross / tp_cross belt-and-braces check both sibling families (trend_donchian, htf_pullback_trend_2h) have run all along; an AST scan confirmed ict_scalp emitted ZERO close reasons before this while both siblings emitted ['sl_cross','tp_cross']. It fires ONLY when price has already passed a level the strategy itself declared at entry, so it introduces no new opinion about where a trade ends - it closes where the declared geometry asked to, which is the operator's own stated rule ('if the trade has already passed where its brackets should have been since it opened, close it out'). Checked BEFORE the stale-stop, the stop-first ordering that lever's own docstring already assumes, pinned by a test that spies on _stale_stop_verdict. BLAST RADIUS MEASURED AGAINST LIVE PRICES BEFORE SHIPPING (state the population: 30 open positions, 2 of them ict_scalp): ETHUSDT 4962 on bybit_1 sits inside its brackets and does NOT close; MGC 4773 on ib_paper (PAPER, no real money) is 233.88 points past its declared target and closes tp_cross - the same incident class this row was filed for (MGC 4487, 122.74 points past target for 11 days with zero LMT orders resting on the account). 12 tests, including controls that it closes nothing inside the brackets, nothing on a package with a null sl or tp, and nothing on an unparseable direction, plus an AST control asserting all three families now emit the same close reasons so they cannot drift apart again.

items.title: The prop rule-distance guard derives the cushion from the account_status snapshot ALONE and ignores the 2 prop_fills reported since it, so on 2026-08-18 a stale panel overstated the distance to the account-killer floor by $78.61 (167%)
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-18, breakout_1.

Before today's snapshot, `/api/bot/prop/status` reported `distance_to_dd_floor_usd: 125.61` off the 2026-07-20T08:28:32Z snapshot (balance 4825.61), correctly graded `status_freshness: "stale"` at 694.2h.

But the system already held STRICTLY BETTER information it did not use: two closed prop fills reported AFTER that snapshot — 2026-07-28 (-18.06) and 2026-08-13 (-50.55), total -68.61. Snapshot + fills reconstructs 4757.00 against an operator terminal truth of 4747.00 (residual -10.00, fees/swap). So:
    panel cushion    +125.61
    reconstructable   +57.00
    ACTUAL            +47.00
The panel overstated the remaining cushion to an account-killer floor by $78.61 — 167% too generous — while a two-row query against a table in the same DB would have got within $10.

`status_freshness` (added 2026-08-14) correctly says the snapshot is old, and that work was right. But 'stale' communicates LOW CONFIDENCE in a number that is still rendered, when the fix available here is not more caveat — it is a BETTER NUMBER. Grading a value you could have improved is the weaker half of the job.

OPERATOR-FACING CONSEQUENCE, and why this is filed high rather than medium: with the true balance now ingested (id 7, 4747.00), the cushion to the static DD floor is **$47.00** while the daily-loss limit is $142.41 — the binding constraint has crossed over to the DD floor and the daily-loss guard can no longer bind first. Every one of the last five reported prop closes (-18.49, -85.90, -96.94, -18.06, -50.55) is LARGER than the remaining cushion; the mean is ~$54. The next average losing trade breaches the account.
items.resolution_criteria: Measured 2026-08-18 against the 2026-07-20 snapshot plus the 2 fills reported since it. `prop_status`'s rule-distance should compute from the snapshot AND every `prop_fills` row reported after `reported_at`, and must expose the basis rather than silently improving the number — a `balance_basis` field that is never collapsed: `snapshot` (no later fills) / `snapshot_plus_fills` (reconstructed, with `fills_applied` count and their sum) / `unavailable`. The reconstructed figure is ESTIMATED provenance, not measured, and must be labelled as such per src/runtime/provenance.py — it is an improvement on the stale snapshot, not a substitute for a fresh one, so the status-request nudge must still fire on snapshot age. DONE when /api/bot/prop/status returns the reconstructed cushion with its basis and the dashboard Prop panel renders both the basis and the snapshot age.

evidence.closed_by: account_status id 7 ingested 2026-08-18T06:53:45Z via prop-report issue #9926

updates.note: RESOLVED on a live read 2026-08-29. /api/bot/prop/status now returns `fills_applied_since_snapshot: 0` and `fills_pnl_since_snapshot_usd: 0.0` alongside `balance_basis: snapshot` and `equity_provenance: measured` — i.e. the rule-distance computation DOES consult the fills stream since the snapshot and reports how many it applied. The exact gap this row names (cushion derived from the snapshot ALONE, ignoring fills reported since) is closed, and the field that proves it is published rather than implied. Today's read happens to be 0 fills since a 0.9 h-old snapshot, so the count is honest rather than merely absent.

items.title: attach-ib-target has four refusals but none for a declared target already THROUGH the market — on such a position it is a market exit wearing the label of a protective repair
items.detail:
OBSERVED 2026-08-18 while triaging the target-naked ib_paper book.

`attach-ib-target` reads the target from the journal (`trades.take_profit_1`) so a repair cannot fat-finger a level — good — and refuses on four real hazards (stray non-protective order, target already resting, >1 stop OCA group, stop qty != journal position_size). None of them tests the target against the CURRENT PRICE.

On trade 4487 (ib_paper MGC long 105) the declared target is 4297.66 and MGC last traded 4420.4. Placing that target is a SELL LMT 122.74 points BELOW the market: it is marketable and fills immediately at ~4420. The operation is therefore an immediate flatten at market, realising ~+$155.7k, while the run comment, the action name and the docs all describe attaching protection. The outcome is not wrong in price — it fills better than the limit — it is wrong in KIND, and the caller cannot tell from the interface which one they are about to get.

This is the diagnostic-provenance class already canonical in this repo (§ 'Diagnostic provenance — does the OUTPUT say what it actually computed?'), sub-class A: the label names a quantity the code did not compute. Here the label names an ACTION the code will not perform.

CORRECTION TO THIS ROW, same session: the operator ALREADY ruled on 4487 specifically — 'yes place it' on 2026-08-16, explicitly knowing the level was through the market (recorded on BL-20260816-MGC-4487-CONFIRM-CLOSE-AT-OPEN). So 4487 is not an open decision, and a HARD refusal would strand an approved instruction. The finding stands for the general case — the interface still cannot tell a caller which of the two operations they are about to get — which is why the criterion below is refuse-by-default plus an explicit opt-in whose NAME says flatten. Note the approval is also now price-stale: it was given against a last of ~4398.70 and MGC is 4420.4.
items.resolution_criteria: Add a fifth refusal: read the current price and refuse when the declared target is already through the market for the position's direction (long: target <= last; short: target >= last), reporting the gap and naming the consequence ('this would fill immediately at market'). Refuse by default and require an explicit separate opt-in flag whose NAME says flatten, not attach — or route the caller to `flatten-ib-position`, which already exists and is honestly named. The price read must be three-state: a price we could not read is `could_not_look` and must also refuse, never fall through to placing. DONE when a dry-run against trade 4487 reports the through-market refusal instead of a clean plan.

updates.note: Re-validated: a missing refusal for a declared target already THROUGH the market, which turns a protective repair into a market exit. Directly relevant given MGC 4773's history. Cheap to add as a fifth refusal.

items.title: DIAG_BASE_URL in the cloud-session environment still points at the x86 micro terminated 2026-06-16, so the documented 'try direct first' path is dead and fails as a timeout rather than as a config error
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-18 at session start. `DIAG_BASE_URL=http://158.178.210.252:8001` — the AMD micro `ict-bot` decommissioned via `terminate-instance` on 2026-06-16 after the 2026-06-14 Ampere cutover. `DIAG_READ_TOKEN` is set and valid.

`scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh` against that base returns nothing and the raw curl hangs to timeout; the live VM's plain-HTTP `http://141.145.193.91:8001` is also unreachable from a web session (Trusted-level egress firewalls arbitrary IPs, as documented). The transport that DOES work is the Caddy HTTPS hostname `https://ict-bot.duckdns.org`, which served every read in this session including `/api/diag/*` with the same bearer (verified: `/api/diag/version` -> git_sha 08dc9987, matching local HEAD).

The failure mode is the problem, not the staleness: a stale IP presents as a 45s hang, which reads as 'the VM is down' or 'the token is wrong' rather than 'this address no longer exists'. docs/claude/diag-relay.md's direct/relay contract tells the next session to try direct first and fall back on exit 3, so every session pays the timeout before falling back.

DEDUPED 2026-08-20. BL-20260818-DIAG-BASE-URL-POINTS-AT-TERMINATED-HOST was an independent same-day filing of this finding by the concurrent S-LLM-BURST-WORKER session (08:45Z vs this row's 07:00Z). That sprint's log records the pair as 'Deduped at wrap; evidence merged into the earlier row' -- IT WAS NOT: both rows were still present and open two days later. A claim of having deduped is not a dedup, which is the same class as a green test that asserted nothing. Merged in from the dropped row, because it carries provenance this one did not: the stale value is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the one in the issue #1615 comment, so the env was pasted from that comment on or after 2026-05-21 -- i.e. this was never correct for the Ampere topology rather than having drifted. It also framed the impact more sharply: CLAUDE.md documents the direct diag path as the durable fallback for when the hosted GitHub MCP drops, so the fallback has been dead for ~2 months and a session reaching for it mid-outage gets an empty body rather than an error. Its next_action, preserved: bundle the diag_fetch.sh three-state fix and the CLAUDE.md web-reachability correction into one Tier-1 PR, and pair the env-var change with the DIAG_READ_TOKEN rotation so the operator does both in one sitting.  RE-CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-08-20T09:05Z (session llm-burst-2): the cloud environment still ships DIAG_BASE_URL=http://158.178.210.252:8001 — the x86 micro terminated 2026-06-16 — two days after this row was filed. Measured in the same session, so the remedy is now concrete rather than theoretical: the WORKING direct path is https://ict-bot.duckdns.org (Caddy), which returned 200 on /api/health AND 200 on a bearer'd /api/diag/version from a DEFAULT-Trusted web session with no Full/Custom network change. The raw IP returned 000 in the same session, so the stale value fails twice over: dead host AND a scheme the proxy drops. CLAUDE.md's 'egress to the VM is firewalled and the issue relay is the only channel' was corrected in the same PR — it was the reason sessions kept reaching for the relay instead of noticing the var was simply pointing at the wrong host.
items.resolution_criteria: Point `DIAG_BASE_URL` at `https://ict-bot.duckdns.org` in the cloud-environment config (env changes take effect on a NEW session), and make `diag_fetch.sh` fail FAST and LOUD on an unresolvable/unreachable base — distinguishing `dns/connect failed` (a config error, exit 3 with the base echoed) from `HTTP error` (the VM answered). Update docs/claude/diag-relay.md to name the Caddy hostname as the direct base, since that is the one that works from a Trusted-level session. DONE when a fresh session's first `diag_fetch.sh` succeeds without a manual base override. Also closes what BL-20260818-DIAG-BASE-URL-POINTS-AT-TERMINATED-HOST asked for; do not re-file a third row for this finding -- check for an existing DIAG-BASE-URL row before opening one, there have now been five across four dates.  RESOLVED IN THE REPO 2026-08-20 (session llm-burst-2), and the previous resolution text was WRONG in a way worth recording. It read: 'an OPERATOR action - it is an environment variable, not a repo file, so no session can fix it.' That is false. The var is only ever consumed by scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh, which IS a repo file, so the repo can decide what to do with a bad value - and it already tried to: a self-heal block (added for BL-20260705-ENV-DIAG-BASE-URL-STALE) rewrote the retired micro 158.178.210.252 to the raw live IP 141.145.193.91. THAT REWRITE PRODUCED AN UNREACHABLE HOST, because the sandbox proxy allowlists by SCHEME+HOSTNAME and drops plain-http to a raw IP at the default Trusted level. Run live this session against the real stale env: the self-heal fired, curl returned 28 (timeout after 10s), exit 3. So the 'fix' had been silently sending every session down the 30-60s issue relay while reporting that it had healed the setting - a green that checked nothing. Fixed by replacing the single rewrite with an ORDERED CANDIDATE LIST that puts the canonical HTTPS base https://ict-bot.duckdns.org FIRST whenever the configured value is plain-http or names a known VM IP, keeps a deliberately-set https base first, de-dups, and names on stderr WHICH base served. The gate was also relaxed to require only DIAG_READ_TOKEN (a session holding a good bearer but no base URL was stranded on the relay for no reason). VERIFIED LIVE IN THE SAME SESSION, same process, with the SAME stale env still set: `scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh version` -> exit 0, real JSON, 'diag_fetch: served by https://ict-bot.duckdns.org'. Covered by tests/test_diag_fetch_sh.py (11 tests; curl is shimmed on PATH so candidate ORDER is asserted without network, and the parametrized retired/raw-IP/plain-http case is the regression test for exactly this defect). The env var itself is STILL stale and correcting it remains a genuine (now cosmetic) operator nicety - but it is no longer load-bearing, and no session should describe this class as unfixable-from-the-repo again.

evidence.merged_provenance: stale base byte-identical to the issue #1615 comment (pasted on/after 2026-05-21)
evidence.repo_fix: scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh - ordered candidate list, canonical HTTPS first
evidence.verified_live_same_session: exit 0, 'served by https://ict-bot.duckdns.org', with DIAG_BASE_URL still http://158.178.210.252:8001

items.title: prop-report strips ``` fence LINES but then jq-parses the WHOLE body, so a fenced JSON block with any surrounding prose fails validation before SSH — the fence support reads as 'fenced block is extracted' and is not
items.detail:
OBSERVED 2026-08-18, issue #9925 (failed) -> #9926 (succeeded, HTTP 200).

The workflow does `grep -vE '^[[:space:]]*```'` to drop fence lines and then `jq -e 'type=="object"' report.json` over everything that remains. A body that is a ```json block PLUS any explanatory sentence therefore fails, because the prose survives the fence strip and lands in the JSON. The docs do say 'whose body is a single JSON object', so this is behaving as written — but the parenthetical 'optionally inside a ```json fence — stripped' invites exactly the shape that breaks, and the error ('failure happened before/at validation') does not say which line was not JSON.

Cost here was one wasted round trip on a report closing a 694h-stale prop cushion. The same shape will bite an operator pasting a terminal screenshot's numbers with a note above them.
items.resolution_criteria: When a ```-fenced block is present, EXTRACT that block and parse only it; fall back to whole-body parse when there is no fence. On failure, echo the first non-JSON line so the author can see what broke. DONE when an issue body with a sentence above a ```json block ingests successfully.

updates.note: Re-validated: fence LINES stripped but the WHOLE body jq-parsed, so prose around a fenced block fails. Relevant — the prop bridge is the account $55 from death, and a rejected report-back is a missed fill.

items.title: claim-basis-guard's _row_text reads title/description/source/action/resolution/resolution_criteria but NOT `detail` — the field recent backlog rows actually put their evidence in, so it fails well-evidenced rows and passes bare claims
items.detail:
OBSERVED 2026-08-18 on this session's own PR (#9927), 1 of 7 new rows failing.

`scripts/check_claim_basis.py::_row_text` joins exactly six keys: title, description, source, action, resolution, resolution_criteria. `detail` is not among them. But `detail` is where essentially every row written since ~2026-07 puts its measurement — populations, denominators, dates, the row counts the guard is looking for.

This fails in BOTH directions, which is why it is filed rather than worked around:
  * FALSE POSITIVE — a row whose `detail` states '2 fills since the 2026-07-20 snapshot' and whose title carries the resulting percentage is rejected as basis-less. That teaches authors to pad the title, not to measure better.
  * FALSE NEGATIVE, the worse one — a bare claim living only in `detail` is never scanned at all, because `_CLAIM_RE` also runs over the same six keys. A row asserting '3x worse' in `detail` and nothing in its title passes silently. The guard's own docstring says a number without its basis is not a finding; a number the guard cannot see is not even a claim to it.

Same family as BL-20260817-COLLAPSED-STATE-GUARD-READS-PROSE and BL-20260817-BACKLOG-REF-GUARD-SKIPS-DOT-CLAUDE-AND-CANNOT-SEE-A-WRAPPED-ID: a guard whose SCAN SURFACE does not match where the content actually lives.
items.resolution_criteria: Add `detail` (and any other free-text key the schema admits) to `_row_text`, then re-run `--base origin/main` over a window of recent merges to size the fallout before enforcing — some existing rows will newly trip, and that population should be counted and triaged, not discovered one PR at a time. Add a self-test pinning both directions: a row with its basis ONLY in `detail` must PASS, and a row with a bare claim ONLY in `detail` must FAIL. DONE when both self-test cases hold.

updates.note: Re-validated: tooling/guard correctness. Cheap to fix, unblocked, still undone. A guard reading five fields but not the one that carries the claim.

items.title: attach-ib-target has NEVER executed once — both invocations died before touching IB (exit 127, then ImportError on a symbol src.units.db.database has never exported), so the operator-approved MGC repair silently never happened and nothing noticed for ~8h
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-18T07:0xZ.

TIMELINE.
  2026-08-16  operator approves placing MGC 4487's declared target ('yes place it'), knowing the level is through the market — recorded on BL-20260816-MGC-4487-CONFIRM-CLOSE-AT-OPEN.
  2026-08-17T22:31:49Z  #9717 merges the action + wrapper.
  2026-08-17T22:32:46Z  issue #9920, DRY RUN -> exit 127 'No such file or directory'. Correctly diagnosed as ict-git-sync timer lag (VM at a745f752, which predates #9717), not a deploy failure.
  2026-08-17T22:38:31Z  issue #9922, DRY RUN retry ~6.5 min later -> wrapper exit 1:
        File "/home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/scripts/ops/attach_ib_target.py", line 102, in _open_trade
          from src.units.db.database import get_connection
        ImportError: cannot import name 'get_connection' from 'src.units.db.database'
  ...and nothing since. No `apply: true` run was ever dispatched.

VERIFIED AGAINST THE MODULE, not inferred from the traceback: `src/units/db/database.py` exports `Database` (with an instance method `.connect()`) and `get_db()`. `get_connection` appears nowhere in it — `hasattr(module,'get_connection')` is False. So the action could never have run, in dry-run OR apply mode, on any symbol or account. It is not a flake and a blind retry would have failed identically.

A SECOND LATENT DEFECT ON THE SAME THREE LINES: the call site was `with get_connection() as conn:`. sqlite3's connection context manager commits or rolls back a TRANSACTION; it does NOT close the connection. Had the symbol existed, this would have leaked a handle on every invocation — and it opened a read/write connection to the money DB for a pure SELECT.

CONSEQUENCE, and why this is critical rather than medium. The tool exists solely to repair BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED, whose whole lesson was that a reduced verdict ('covered') hid a real gap. The repair for it was then reported as SHIPPED on the strength of a merge, and its only two executions both failed loudly in an issue comment that nobody re-read. Measured now: ib_paper still holds exactly 2 orders, BOTH STP, ZERO LMT account-wide (read_state `orders_read`); MGC is still 105 LONG @ 4276.236; MGC's venue is `open` ('tradingHours: inside 20260817 18:00-20260818 17:00 US/Eastern'); and MGC last traded 4420.4 against a declared target of 4297.66. Green-is-not-evidence, one level up: a MERGED repair is not a RUN repair, and a run that failed is not a repair at all.

FIX LANDED in this PR: `_open_trade` now opens a READ-ONLY connection resolved through `src.utils.paths.trade_journal_db_path()` (the canonical resolver the CI guard requires) with an explicit try/finally close. Verified locally: the resolver imports and resolves, `get_connection` is confirmed absent, ruff clean.

--- RESOLVED 2026-08-18T07:46Z: IT RAN. ---
The import fix merged (#9927, cf3f0c1) and was CONFIRMED DEPLOYED before dispatch (/api/diag/version -> cf3f0c12 == main tip, so this was not another git-sync-lag retry — the #9920 lesson applied). Issue #9928, the first successful execution in the action's life, returned wrapper exit 0 and state `ready`: orders_on_symbol 1, oca_group oca-protect-357, declared_tp 4297.65785714 read from trades.take_profit_1 (NOT supplied by the caller, as designed), qty 105.0, trade_id 4487. All four refusals passed.

The APPLY (#9929, operator-re-approved) then placed order 381 and the position flattened: MGC absent from exchange_positions, orders 381 and 359 both gone, no orphan stop on a flat book.

This row's three DONE conditions are met (deploy confirmed, dry run completed, operator re-confirmed against the current price). A FOLLOW-UP is filed rather than folded in here, because it is a different defect in a different function: the apply's post-place verification reported `place_not_effective` on that successful fill — BL-20260818-ATTACH-IB-TARGET-VERIFY-CANNOT-EXPRESS-FILLED. Note this row's own criterion asking for a regression test that IMPORTS the module and exercises _open_trade remains outstanding and is carried into that row. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'resolved_ran_successfully_followup_filed' was collapsed to 'resolved' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
items.resolution_criteria: NOT closed by the import fix. DONE requires, in order: (1) the fix merged and confirmed deployed on the live VM by `/api/diag/version` showing a SHA at or past it — the #9920 lesson is that a merge is not a deploy; (2) a DRY RUN that actually completes and reports a plan (expected: target 4297.66 read from `trades.take_profit_1`, joining `oca-protect-357`, not minting a group); (3) an operator RE-confirmation before any apply, because the 2026-08-16 approval was given against a last of ~4398.70 and MGC is now 4420.4 — an approval to sell at market is price-sensitive and two days stale. A regression test that IMPORTS the module and exercises `_open_trade` against a temp DB is required, since a smoke test that never reaches line 102 would have passed this whole time.

items.title: attach-ib-target verifies by asking whether a target is RESTING, so a marketable target that FILLS reports `place_not_effective` / `still_absent` + exit 1 — a red on a successful flatten, and a retry on that signal opens a naked reverse position
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-18T07:49Z, issue #9929 (run 32113224835), on the operator-re-approved MGC repair.

WHAT THE ACTION REPORTED:
    place_response: {retCode: 0, result: {orderId: 381, ocaGroup: oca-protect-357,
                     limitPrice: 4297.7, qty: 105.0}, retMsg: OK}
    targets_after: []
    action: place_not_effective
    verify_state: still_absent
  -> wrapper exit 1 -> the issue comment renders a red ❌ FAILED.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED, verified by three independent reads minutes later:
  * /api/diag/exchange_positions?account_id=ib_paper -> MGC ABSENT; only MES 15 long remains. The list is a real list, not null, so this is a confirmed clean read.
  * /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper -> read_state 'orders_read', count 1: only MES 338. BOTH MGC order 381 and MGC stop 359 are gone.
  * journal trade 4487 still status=open / pnl null at the time of the read — the reconciler and the hourly ict-ib-executions-pull had not caught up yet.
Order 381 was a SELL LMT 105 @ 4297.66 into a ~4420 market: marketable, filled essentially instantly, and ocaType=1 then cancelled sibling stop 359. The mechanism worked exactly as designed, including the part that matters most — NO orphan stop was left resting on a flat book.

THE DEFECT IS THE PREDICATE, NOT THE WINDOW. `verify_state: still_absent` is carrying two OPPOSITE outcomes — 'the order never got placed' and 'the order placed and has already filled' — because the check asks only whether a target is RESTING. A filled order is not resting. Lengthening the verify window (the fix for the sibling row BL-20260817-CANCEL-IB-ORDER-VERIFY-WINDOW-TOO-SHORT) would not help at all here: nothing is pending, the work is done.

WHY CRITICAL RATHER THAN MEDIUM — it is strictly more dangerous than its sibling. There, a red on a completed cancel invited a harmless duplicate cancel. Here, a red on a FILLED sell invites a retry that places a SECOND SELL 105 MGC against a now-flat book, opening a naked SHORT 105 with no bracket of its own. That is the same end state BL-20260816-IB-STOPS-OVER-COVER-IN-DISJOINT-OCA-GROUPS describes, reached by a different route — and this one is reached by a session doing the obviously-reasonable thing after a red. The honest-verification design is RIGHT and must not be weakened; reporting broker acceptance as success is the accepted-!=-done class this repo has repeatedly been bitten by. The gap is that 'done' has more than one shape and only one of them is represented.

--- FIXED 2026-08-22 (Tier-1). Row KEPT OPEN on the live control, which arrives on its own. ---
The predicate is now THREE-STATE plus an explicit could-not-look, and the position is read as a SECOND, INDEPENDENT signal -- the order book alone cannot separate the two outcomes, because a filled order is not an OPEN order and both read as absent.
  target_resting     -> action 'placed', exit 0        (a target is on the book: the protective case)
  target_filled      -> action 'placed_and_filled', exit 0  (position FLAT or REDUCED below the placed qty: the marketable case, a SUCCESS)
  absent_unexplained -> action 'place_not_effective', exit 1 (no resting target AND a confirmed clean position read AND the position still stands at full size: the ONLY genuine failure)
  could_not_look     -> action 'placed_unconfirmed', exit 3  (the POSITION read failed -- we did not look, so no verdict is earned)
Every non-resting verdict now publishes `position_after` {state, size}, so the evidence behind the verdict is checkable rather than asserted. The old output showed only `targets_after: []`, which is consistent with BOTH outcomes -- that is why the verdict could not be contradicted from outside.

items.title: [verify] establish whether the target_naked detector ever fired for ib_paper MGC — it shipped 2026-08-16 and the position stayed target-naked for two more days with nothing visible on /api/bot/notifications
items.detail:
OPEN QUESTION, deliberately filed as a measurement rather than answered by inference.

`order_monitor._emit_target_naked_alert` and `summary['target_naked']` exist in code, shipped 2026-08-16 for BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED, and are documented in CLAUDE.md as alerting on the target side without re-arming. The IB broker-naked sweep that drives them is cadence-gated by `IB_BROKER_NAKED_CHECK_SECONDS` (default 300s).

Yet ib_paper MGC remained target-naked from at least 2026-08-16 until the repair on 2026-08-18T07:49Z, and `/api/bot/notifications` read at 2026-08-18T07:0xZ carried four banners — one `monitor_blindness` for ict_scalp_mgc_15m and three `transient_market_data_unavailable` — and NO target-naked banner.

That is not proof of silence. Three benign explanations must be ruled out before concluding anything: the alert may be latched and have fired once on 08-16 before the window this session looked at; `/api/bot/notifications` may simply not surface this alert KIND (its banner list is a fixed set — trainer_down / account_down / operator_warning / orphan_unreconciled / trade_open — and a target_naked alert routed only to Telegram would not appear there at all, which would make its absence expected and meaningless); or the sweep may be skipping on a `None` read. A search that returns nothing is not proof of absence — show the probe can find a positive first.

This matters beyond MGC: if a detector shipped for a critical finding is not firing, the finding is still live AND now wears a green badge, which is worse than having no detector. If it IS firing and the operator never saw it, the delivery channel is the defect.
items.resolution_criteria: Grep the trader journal (`/api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live.service`) and `outcomes.jsonl` across 2026-08-16 → 2026-08-18 for the target-naked alert string, and read `_check_broker_naked_ib_positions`'s summary counters for the same window. State which of the three explanations holds. If the alert fired: confirm which channel carried it and whether `/api/bot/notifications` should surface this kind (it currently cannot — that would be its own finding). If it did not fire: root-cause why, with the code path named. DONE when the question is answered with evidence, not when MGC is closed — MGC is already closed and the detector's behaviour is the open question.
items.resolution: ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT, and the answer is explanation #1: THE ALERT FIRED, repeatedly. Read /api/bot/logs?limit=1000&level=error&since=2026-08-16 (the ERROR+/CRITICAL feed, which merges outcomes.jsonl; ib_target_naked is Level.CRITICAL so it persists there and reaches Telegram). POPULATION: 376 rows returned against a cap of 1000, so NOT truncated; oldest row 2026-08-17T08:03:56Z, so 08-16 is UNMEASURED here rather than shown empty. ib_target_naked rows by day/symbol: 08-17 MES 16 / MGC 16; 08-18 MES 11 / MGC 1; 08-19 6/5; 08-20 31/31; 08-21 11/11; 08-22 24/24; 08-23 9/6. MGC alerted 16 times on 08-17 alone. So the detector was never silent and the delivery channel worked. The /api/bot/notifications absence observed at 08-18T07:0xZ needs no detector defect to explain: MGC produced exactly ONE row on 08-18 (the 07:49Z repair ended the condition), and the operator_warning banner is capped at 3 newest-first - measured again 2026-08-23, 3 of the 4 live banners were transient_market_data_unavailable, so this alert routinely loses its slot. Explanations #2 (the banner cannot carry this kind) and #3 (the sweep skipping on a None read) are both REFUTED by the positive rows. THE MEASUREMENT SURFACED A LARGER DEFECT, fixed in the same PR: those 202 rows are 53.7% of the entire ERROR+/CRITICAL feed over 6.5 days, for two paper positions in an already-filed state - see BL-20260823-TARGET-NAKED-COOLDOWN-RESETS-ON-EVERY-RESTART.

items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-18. Chain, each link verified rather than inferred:
  1. Repo visibility is PUBLIC (GitHub API: private=false, visibility=public).
  2. Issue #1615 comment 4507810670 (posted 2026-05-21T11:36:56Z by github-actions[bot], from get-diag-token.yml) contains the DIAG_READ_TOKEN value in plaintext inside a fenced block, plus DIAG_BASE_URL=http://158.178.210.252:8001. The issue is CLOSED but NOT deleted; closing does not remove comments, and public issue comments are mirrored by third-party archives.
  3. The exposed value is still the value in use: SHA-256 fingerprint of the comment's token == fingerprint of this session's DIAG_READ_TOKEN env var (first 12 hex: 9a4b80473d32). Compared by hash so neither value was printed.
  4. It still authorizes against the LIVE VM over the public Caddy route: GET https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/diag/status with that bearer -> HTTP 200, returning live heartbeat + git_sha.
  5. Rotation attempt: operator updated 'the secret' and set-diag-token.yml was dispatched (run 32117038449, 08:34:05Z, conclusion=success). It genuinely restarted ict-web-api (journal shows PID 4032174 -> 4040432 at 08:34:14-15Z) and printed 'RESULT: ok — authorized with the new token'. The leaked token STILL returned 200 afterwards.
  6. Discriminating probe AFTER the restart: leaked token -> 200; obvious garbage token -> 401; no token -> 401. Auth IS enforcing. Therefore the repo Actions secret DIAG_READ_TOKEN still holds the OLD value and the rotation changed nothing.
items.why_it_matters:
/api/diag/* is read-only (no order path, cannot mutate) which is why the operator triaged it as non-urgent on 2026-08-18 — that call is recorded here, not disputed. But the surface it exposes is the whole business: trade journal + order_packages, signal audit, journalctl, DB schema and contents, exchange positions, per-account exposure/balances, IB open orders. Anyone who reads one public issue comment gets the full trading history and live positions of a money-at-risk system, for as long as the value stands. Discovery risk is currently low (0 stars/forks/watchers) but 'nobody has looked' is not a control, and the exposure window is already ~3 months.

The compounding hazard is that the rotation LOOKED done: a green workflow run reported success over an unchanged value, so without the A/B/C probe this would have been closed as fixed. See the sibling item BL-20260818-SET-DIAG-TOKEN-REPORTS-NEW-ON-UNCHANGED-VALUE.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) Set a genuinely NEW value on the REPOSITORY Actions secret named DIAG_READ_TOKEN (Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions), e.g. `openssl rand -hex 32`. Confirm it is the repo-level Actions secret — the 2026-08-18 attempt failed because the new value went somewhere else (a Claude env var, an environment-scoped secret, or an unsaved edit). (2) Dispatch set-diag-token.yml to propagate + restart. (3) VERIFY with the three-way probe, which is the pass condition: leaked token -> 401, garbage -> 401, no token -> 401, and the NEW token -> 200. A green workflow run is NOT evidence on its own (see step 5 above). (4) Delete issue #1615 (delete, not close). Rotation is what closes the hole; deletion is hygiene only, since mirrors may retain the comment.
items.next_action: Operator originates the new secret value (step 1) — Claude cannot write repo secrets. Steps 2-4 are then autonomous. Operator deprioritized on 2026-08-18 as read-only; re-surface this item on the next /system-review or /health-review until the step-3 probe passes.

THE BLOCKER IS CLEARED; THE ROTATION IS STILL THE OPERATOR'S. PR #10251 gated get-diag-token.yml on repository.private, fail-closed. That ordering was forced and had not been stated anywhere until board comment 5406416710: rotating THROUGH the ungated emitter would have re-leaked the new value on the way out, burning the rotation. It cannot now.

The operator's 2026-08-18 deprioritisation is NOT being re-litigated -- that call stands and is recorded in this row. What changed is only that acting on it is no longer self-defeating.

The same PR also fixed the sibling that made the 2026-08-18 attempt LOOK done (BL-20260818-SET-DIAG-TOKEN-REPORTS-NEW-ON-UNCHANGED-VALUE): set-diag-token now reports a measured `rotation_state`, so a rotation that changes nothing reports `unchanged` instead of 'authorized with the new token'. Steps 1 and 4 are unchanged and still need a human: originate a new value on the REPOSITORY Actions secret named DIAG_READ_TOKEN (confirm repo-scoped, not environment-scoped, and that the edit saved -- the 2026-08-18 attempt failed because the value went somewhere else), and delete issue #1615 (delete, not close). Claude cannot write repo secrets.

NOT RE-MEASURED THIS SESSION: whether the leaked token still authorizes. The 2026-08-18 measurement is what this row records, and it is not being restated as current.

⚠️ RE-CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-08-29 AND ESCALATED TO THE OPERATOR IN THIS REVIEW'S REPORT. The token STILL AUTHORIZES: this session made roughly fifteen authenticated /api/diag/* calls against https://ict-bot.duckdns.org (version, status, services, snapshot, tick_cost, exposure, ib_state, ib_open_orders, venue_session, journal, journalctl, log_file x4) and every one returned 200. So a bearer that has been readable in a WORLD-READABLE issue comment since 2026-05-21 — 100 days — is still a working credential for the live trading VM's read surface. It is read-only (Tier-1 GETs), which bounds the blast radius to disclosure rather than control, but that disclosure includes the journal, service state and open orders. ROTATION IS OPERATOR-ONLY on a public repo: per CLAUDE.md the get-diag-token workflow now REFUSES on a public repo (BL-20260818-GET-DIAG-TOKEN-EMITS-SECRET-TO-PUBLIC-SURFACE), so the operator must originate a new value, put it in the Actions secret and the consuming env, then push it to the VM with set-diag-token. Nothing a session can do closes this.

OPERATOR DECISION — CLOSED AS ACCEPTED RISK. DO NOT RE-RAISE THIS ROW. The operator directed, verbatim in substance: freeze the diag-token question, "I'm not rotating that again", mark it, and stop sessions asking about it. This is a DECISION, not a fix, which is why the status is wont_fix and not resolved — the condition below is unchanged and true.

RE-MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY 2026-08-30T05:09:21Z, which is why this closes on evidence rather than on fatigue: GET https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/diag/version with the token value held in a live session's environment returned HTTP 200 ({"git_sha":"35211baf","restart_pending":false}). So the row's central claim — that the exposed value STILL authorizes and that the 2026-08-18 rotation was a no-op — is confirmed against the live VM, not merely restated. Two rotation attempts have now failed to take (2026-08-18, and one the operator made 2026-08-30 before this measurement), which is the practical case for stopping: the mechanism itself is broken, tracked separately as BL-20260713-SET-DIAG-TOKEN-RESTORE-BROKEN, and THAT row stays open. Rotating cannot succeed until it is fixed, so re-proposing a rotation here is proposing an action that does not work.

WHAT THE ACCEPTED EXPOSURE ACTUALLY IS, stated plainly so the decision is not remembered as smaller than it is: any reader of the public issue comment from 2026-05-21 holds a working bearer for /api/diag/*. That surface is READ-ONLY and token-gated — it serves diagnostics, journal SELECTs, service state, journalctl and log tails. It is NOT an order path, it cannot place, modify or cancel a trade, and it carries no exchange credentials. So the realistic harm is disclosure of trading-system internals and operational state, not loss of funds. That is a real, bounded exposure the operator has weighed and accepted.

FOR FUTURE SESSIONS: do not file a successor row for this, do not add it to OPEN-ITEMS.json, and do not raise it in a review's flags_raised[] or operator_priorities. It is decided. The ONLY thing that reopens it is the operator saying so, or a material change in what the diag surface can do — specifically, if /api/diag/* ever gains a WRITE route or begins returning secrets, the risk calculus that justified this decision no longer holds and the decision must be re-put to the operator rather than assumed to carry over.

items.title: get-diag-token.yml writes a live secret into an issue comment / run artifact, justified by a 'two principals' threat model that only holds on a PRIVATE repo — the repo is public, so the guard and the visibility have silently drifted apart
items.source: READ 2026-08-18 from .github/workflows/get-diag-token.yml. Its header states: 'This repo has exactly two principals (owner + Claude), so the artifact / comment audience is the owner only.' Delivery paths: workflow_dispatch -> upload-artifact 'diag-env'; issues-labelled -> posted as an issue comment, then the issue is closed. Repo visibility measured the same day: private=false. On a public repo, issue comments are world-readable and run artifacts are downloadable unauthenticated. The repo's interaction limit ('Limit to repository collaborators') restricts who may COMMENT, not who may READ — so it does not mitigate this. A narrowed scan of all 66 workflows found this is the ONLY deliberate secret-emitter (the broad first-pass screen was false-positive heavy: workflows that legitimately USE secrets while also commenting).
items.why_it_matters: This is the mechanism that produced BL-20260818-DIAG-READ-TOKEN-PUBLIC-EXPOSURE-UNREMEDIATED. Until it is gated, any future run re-leaks — including a run triggered to deliver the ROTATED token, which would immediately re-expose the fix. The repo has flipped visibility before (public -> private 2026-07-06 -> public 2026-07-07), so a comment asserting privacy is exactly the kind of claim that goes stale silently: 'field beats comment', and here the field is repository.private.
items.resolution_criteria: get-diag-token.yml gates its delivery steps on `github.event.repository.private == true` and FAILS CLOSED (explicit error naming the reason) when the repo is public, rather than falling back to a quieter delivery. The stale 'two principals' rationale in the header is replaced with the actual rule. Verified by a dispatch on the public repo that refuses to emit.
items.next_action: Tier-1 workflow fix; ship alongside the set-diag-token sibling fix in one PR.
items.resolution:
RESOLVED 2026-08-25 by PR #10251. get-diag-token.yml now reads repository visibility at run time and FAILS CLOSED. Repo visibility MEASURED the same session (GitHub API): private=false, visibility=public -- so the gate refuses on this repo today, which is the criterion's own pass condition.

THREE STATES, NEVER COLLAPSED: `private` delivers - `public` refuses, naming the reason - `unknown` (WE COULD NOT READ THE VISIBILITY) refuses too. The third is the load-bearing one: collapsing it into the permissive branch would recreate this exact defect one API hiccup at a time. Both sources must independently agree (the event payload AND a live repos.get), so a visibility flip mid-run refuses rather than picking a winner -- and a mid-run flip is precisely the condition this row is about.

TWO SMALLER DEFECTS FOUND IN THE SAME FILE while fixing this, both load-bearing and neither in the original filing:
  (a) The artifact-upload step carried `always()`, which runs a step even after an earlier failure. A delivery step that opts out of failure propagation must carry its own gate or the gate is one reordering away from being bypassed -- both delivery steps now re-state the condition in their own `if:`.
  (b) The failure comment named ONE cause ('secret unset, or SSH unreachable') for every failure. For a visibility refusal that is a cause no code path tested -- the unprovenanced-diagnostic class, sub-class A -- and misleading in the costly direction, since it reads as a transient VM problem worth re-running. It now branches on the actual failure STAGE.

VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED: tests/test_diag_token_workflows.py (24 cases) EXECUTES the shipped shell extracted from the workflow YAML at test time -- never a pasted copy, which is how a guard and the thing it guards drift apart. All 9 gate verdicts are exercised by running the real `run:` block, including `True` and `yes` failing closed. The defect was PLANTED (collapse `unknown` into the permissive branch) and 5 of 9 cases failed; restored, 24/24 green. A test that also passes on the broken code proves nothing.

DOCS CORRECTED IN THE SAME PR, because three surfaces instructed sessions to use the path this gates: CLAUDE.md ('deliver it for a cloud env var via the get-diag-token workflow, not by hand-copying'), docs/claude/diag-relay.md's token-management section, and the workflow catalog.

NOTED WHILE READING (fixed in passing): get-diag-token.yml had NO ROW in the docs/github-actions-workflows.md catalog table. It passed check_workflow_catalog because Direction A matches a bare filename ANYWHERE in the doc, and the only mention was an incidental artifact-retention line -- so a SECRET-EMITTING workflow sat uncatalogued while the guard read green. Row added; the guard looseness is filed as its own row rather than changed here.

LIVE-VERIFIED ON THE PUBLIC REPO 2026-08-25T06:52Z -- the criterion asked for exactly this ('Verified by a dispatch on the public repo that refuses to emit'), and a green test run would not have satisfied it. Run 32818860134 (workflow_dispatch on the PR branch, job 97712610121):
  - `Read repository visibility (live)` -> success. The live repos.get resolves under the workflow's existing `contents: read` permission -- checked, not assumed, since a gate whose live read always failed would grade every run `unknown` and refuse forever.
  - env showed PAYLOAD_PRIVATE=false AND LIVE_PRIVATE=false; the step printed `visibility_state: public` and emitted the ::error:: naming PUBLIC as the cause.
  - Step 4 `Resolve token + write env block` -> SKIPPED. This is the load-bearing observation: the token was never RESOLVED, so it did not reach the runner's disk at all, let alone a delivery surface. Steps 5 (artifact) and 6 (issue comment) -- both delivery paths -- also SKIPPED.
  - Job conclusion `failure`, which is the correct outcome: a refusal to emit a secret is a failed run, not a quiet no-op.
