The workflow pushed the repo secret to /etc/ict-trader/web-api.env, restarted ict-web-api, curled /api/diag/status with the pushed value, got 200, and printed 'RESULT: ok — web-api active and /api/diag/status authorized with the new token.' The value was NOT new — an independent three-way probe (leaked=200, garbage=401, none=401) proved the secret was unchanged. The run was green and the exposure stayed open.
items.why_it_matters: Textbook unprovenanced diagnostic output, sub-class A (semantic substitution): the label names a quantity ('the new token') the code never computed — it computed 'the token currently in the secret authorizes', which is true of an unchanged value. A reader who trusts the label closes a live security finding as remediated. This is the same class the diagnostic-provenance-guard exists to catch, on a workflow rather than a script, and it is load-bearing precisely because rotation is the one operation where 'did the value actually change?' IS the question.
items.resolution_criteria: The workflow records a fingerprint (e.g. sha256, never the value) of the token the VM served BEFORE the install and of the one it serves AFTER, and reports three distinguishable states rather than one: 'rotated' (fingerprints differ AND the new one authorizes) / 'unchanged' (fingerprints identical — succeed loudly as a NO-OP, never as a rotation) / 'failed'. Registering it with collapsed-state-guard is optional but consistent with the house pattern.
items.next_action: Tier-1 workflow fix; ship with the get-diag-token sibling.
items.resolution:
RESOLVED 2026-08-25 by PR #10251, shipped with the get-diag-token sibling as the row's next_action specified. The remote script fingerprints what the VM SERVES before the install and after it (sha256, 12-hex prefix -- never the value, the same form this row's own source section used) and reports FOUR states rather than one label: `rotated` (the served fingerprint CHANGED and the new one authorizes) - `unchanged` (identical; a NO-OP, reported loudly as one, exit 0, and the sentence 'authorized with the new token' is no longer reachable) - `unknown_before` (the pre-state could not be read, so the run CANNOT say which happened -- explicitly not `rotated` by default) - `failed`.

The row's criteria named three states; a fourth was added because collapsing 'we could not read the pre-state' into either `rotated` or `unchanged` is the same collapse the row is about, one level down. The read prefers the RUNNING process environment over the env file -- the file is what a restart WOULD serve, the process is what is being served now -- and stamps which source answered (`process`/`envfile`/`unresolved`), so a reader never infers the source from a null.

The runner lifts the verdict into a step output DEFAULTING TO `unknown` (an absent sentinel must not default to `rotated`), and the issue comment headlines the verdict instead of the run being green.

VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, not inspection: the tests run the REAL remote script -- extracted from the workflow YAML at test time -- against real fixtures under shims for sudo/systemctl/curl/pgrep, including a genuine /proc/<pid>/environ read of a process the test starts, so the 'what does the VM serve' path is a real kernel read rather than a mocked string. The 2026-08-18 condition (run 32117038449: green, authorized, nothing rotated) is reproduced as its own case and now grades `unchanged`. One case asserts no raw token value ever reaches the transcript, which is echoed to the run log AND into an issue comment. The defect was PLANTED (make `unchanged` report `rotated`) and the case failed; restored, 24/24 green.

Not registered with collapsed-state-guard: its CONTRACTS table addresses Python producers and consumers, and this verdict lives in shell inside a workflow. The four states are held instead by tests/test_diag_token_workflows.py, which asserts each one is reachable and distinguishable.

items.title: _apply_partial_close still resolves only linked_trade_id — the last effectuation branch not yet package-wide; QUEUED for the next phase so the exit path is comprehensively multi-leg rather than multi-leg in two branches of three
items.detail:
Scope note on the package-wide effectuation fix (BL-20260818-MONITOR-MANAGES-ONLY-THE-LINKED-LEG). That change covered the MODIFY and full-CLOSE branches, which is where the measured evidence was: 4 of 8 live multi-leg packages with divergent stops, 6 of 35 open trades stranded. `_apply_partial_close` was left on the old single-leg resolution.

The same structural defect applies to it — one package, N accounts, one `linked_trade_id` — so a `close_qty_pct < 1.0` verdict reduces the linked leg's position and leaves every sibling at full size. It is filed at medium rather than critical because it does not STRAND a leg the way the full-close path did (the package stays open, so the legs remain in the loop), and because no live partial-close-on-a-multi-leg-package instance has been measured.

It was deliberately not fixed in the same change: a partial close needs per-leg quantity arithmetic (each leg's own size, its own cumulative-partial accounting) rather than the same verdict applied N times, and inventing that on top of an unmeasured case is how a Tier-3 change grows past what its evidence supports.

--- OPERATOR DIRECTION 2026-08-18: BUILD THIS IN THE NEXT PHASE ---
Raised to high and queued rather than left latent. The operator's framing: excluding it from the first change was right, but it is 'something we will need to build out in the next phase for comprehensibility'. That is the stronger argument, and it does not depend on finding a live instance first.

WHY COMPREHENSIVENESS IS ITS OWN REASON. After the package-wide fix, TWO of the three effectuation branches (modify, full close) resolve every leg and ONE (partial close) resolves the linked leg. A reader — human or a future session — cannot tell which is which without reading all three, and the natural inference from 'the exit path was made multi-leg' is that it was made multi-leg. A half-converted contract is harder to reason about than either uniform state, and it is exactly the kind of seam this repo's provenance work keeps finding defects in. So the trigger for building it is the INCONSISTENCY, not a measured incident.

WHAT MAKES IT MORE THAN A COPY OF THE OTHER TWO, and why it was right to defer rather than rush: a partial close is the only branch carrying QUANTITY. The other two apply one verdict unchanged to each leg; this one must resolve `close_qty_pct` against each leg's OWN `position_size`, and each leg keeps its own cumulative-partial accounting toward the 100% that converts it into a full close. Legs on one package are NOT the same size (measured: the XRP package runs 149.5 on bybit_2 against 48,625.8 on bybit_portfolio, a 325x spread), so a pct is the only thing that transfers between them — a qty never does. Two questions need answering before code: whether a leg reaching 100% closes just that leg or the package (it must be just the leg, with the package draining as the full-close path now does), and how a partial that lands on some legs and fails on others is accounted, since unlike a modify it is NOT idempotent — re-sending it would reduce the succeeded leg twice.

That last point is the real design constraint and the reason the full-close path's all-or-nothing retry pattern CANNOT simply be copied here. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'queued_next_phase' was collapsed to 'kept_open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
items.resolution_criteria: Next phase, Tier-3. Design first, in this order: (1) pct-per-leg against each leg's own size, never a shared qty; (2) per-leg cumulative-partial state, with a leg reaching 100% closing THAT LEG and the package draining exactly as the full-close path now does; (3) a non-idempotent partial-application story — a retry must not re-reduce a leg that already succeeded, which rules out copying the full-close path's blanket 'leave it and retry next tick'. Likely needs a per-leg applied-marker keyed on (package, leg, verdict instance). Then: tests pinning unequal leg sizes (use the measured 149.5-vs-48,625.8 XRP shape), a partial that lands on one leg and fails on another, and a leg crossing 100% while a sibling does not. DONE when all three effectuation branches resolve legs through `_package_open_legs` and no branch is silently single-leg. Also worth measuring on the way in (cheap, and it sizes the backlog): has a partial-close verdict ever fired on a multi-leg package? — packages with >1 trade row whose legs' position_size diverges from entry size.

updates.note: Re-validated: _apply_partial_close still resolves only linked_trade_id — the last effectuation branch that is not package-wide. Live relevance: `intent_reduce` appears on this window's real-money exit paths at pnlCoverage 0.0.

items.title: m20_fleet_exit_sweep prints `done ->` and writes a verdicts.json after measuring 0 of 0 cells, with exit code 0 — a run that measured nothing is indistinguishable from one that measured everything
items.detail:
OBSERVED 2026-08-18, relay #9940. The sweep emitted:
    split: FELL BACK to 2025-07-01 (harness_rc)
    capital: 0/0 cells measured
    done -> runtime_logs/m20_xrp_holdconviction/2026-08-18
exit code 0, and it WROTE SUMMARY.md, capital_distribution.json, results.jsonl and verdicts.json into a dated output directory. Nothing about the artifact set distinguishes it from a complete run; only the `0/0` in stdout does, and stdout is not what a later session reads.

Cost, measured: I read it as a result and reported a conclusion from it before checking the cell count. The correct reading was 'my invocation was broken' (bare python3, no pandas).

This is `silent-empty-guard`'s class one level up: that guard catches a producer returning [] from a broad except; this is a whole RUN returning an empty artifact set under a success banner. A dated directory of empty verdicts is worse than no directory, because the next session's glob finds it.
items.resolution_criteria: Exit non-zero when `cells_measured == 0`, and make the banner state the count: `done (0 cells measured) ->` rather than `done ->`. Better: refuse to write a verdicts.json at all for a zero-cell run, or write one whose top level carries an explicit `run_state: no_cells_measured` that consumers must branch on. DONE when a deliberately-broken invocation produces a non-zero exit and an artifact a glob-based reader cannot mistake for a measurement.

updates.note: Re-validated: `done ->` plus a verdicts.json plus exit 0 after measuring 0 of 0 cells. A run that measured nothing reporting success is the unasserted-denominator shape, and it is HIGH severity because downstream consumers read that verdicts.json as evidence.

items.title: the sweep collapses any harness failure to `harness_rc`, so a plain ImportError took a separate relay round-trip to see
items.detail:
OBSERVED 2026-08-18. #9940 reported `split: FELL BACK to 2025-07-01 (harness_rc)` and nothing else. The underlying cause, found only by invoking the harness directly in #9941, was:
    ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pandas'
`run_cell` captures the subprocess output (`return {'error': (p.stderr or p.stdout)[-250:]}`) but the split-resolution path discards it and substitutes the token `harness_rc`.

Cost: two extra relay round-trips on a one-line cause. Every relay round-trip is minutes, and a session with a wrong hypothesis spends them in the wrong direction — I briefly treated it as a possible harness defect on the leg.

Same family as BL-20260811-TRAINER-RELAY-BLAMES-THE-VM-WHEN-ONLY-THE-COMMENT-POST-FAILED: a failure message naming a STAGE rather than a CAUSE, where the cause was captured and thrown away.
items.resolution_criteria: Propagate the harness's captured stderr tail into the split-resolution failure message and into the run log, e.g. `harness_rc: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pandas'`. The 250-char tail already exists in `run_cell`; the split path just needs to keep it. DONE when a deliberately-broken harness invocation names its own cause in the sweep's stdout.

updates.note: Re-validated: collapsing any harness failure to `harness_rc` cost a separate relay round-trip to see a plain ImportError. Same class as the trainer relay's error-stage collapse.

items.title: the sweep and every backtest harness require the repo venv and neither state nor check it — bare python3 fails deep, as a swallowed ImportError
items.detail:
OBSERVED 2026-08-18. `python3 scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py ...` on the trainer fails because the system interpreter has no pandas; `.venv/bin/python` works (pandas 3.0.3). Nothing in the scripts' `--help`, docstrings, or the skills states this, and the failure does not surface as 'wrong interpreter' — it surfaces as `harness_rc` (see the sibling row) or as a bare ImportError several layers down.

The knowledge exists but only as prose in artifact provenance strings — `config/lever_reachability.json` basis fields say 'repo venv (relay #9710)'. That records what a past run used; it does not tell the next session what to type, and it is not where anyone looks before running a sweep.
items.resolution_criteria: Add a two-line interpreter guard at the top of the sweep and the backtest harnesses: if the required third-party imports are unavailable, exit non-zero with the exact venv path to use rather than letting the ImportError escape into a subprocess capture. Also state the venv invocation in the `backtesting` and `exit-refinement` skills, which are what a session reads before dispatching one. DONE when a bare-python3 invocation prints the correct command.

updates.note: Re-validated: harnesses that require the repo venv and neither state nor check it, failing deep as a swallowed error.

items.title: trainer-vm-diag HTML-escapes `<` to `<` and collapses multi-line implicit string concatenation to U+00B7, so any python using format specifiers breaks
items.detail:
OBSERVED 2026-08-18, relay #9935. A `cmd:` block containing f-string format specifiers (`{x:<30}`) and multi-line implicit concatenation came back as:
    bash: gt: command not found
    SyntaxError: invalid character '·' (U+00B7)
The `<` had become `<` and the line joins had become `·`. Rewriting without `<` and without multi-line strings ran clean (#9937).

This is a silent CORRUPTION of an operator-authored command, not a rejection — the relay ran something different from what was written and reported the resulting syntax error as if the author had typed it. A session debugging that error looks at its own python first.
items.resolution_criteria: Either transport the `cmd:` block without HTML-escaping (base64 the way the prop-report relay already carries its untrusted payload), or detect and refuse a block whose escaped form differs from the source and say so. DONE when a cmd block containing `{x:<30}` and a multi-line f-string executes byte-identically. Until then, note the constraint in docs/claude/diag-relay.md so the next session does not lose a round-trip to it.

updates.note: Re-validated: FOURTH independent defect in the trainer relay's command handling (with DOUBLE-EXECUTION, SILENT-CMD-TRUNCATION, COLUMN0-PYTHON-KEYWORD). Four rows, one component. The structural fix is a single tested extractor, not four patches — and this is the clearest example in the whole backlog of the band-aid pattern this review was asked to look for.

items.title: a cell that hit the OOS-trades floor reads as measured at the fleet level — xrp's stale/giveback cells sat `insufficient_base` and nothing rolled that up
items.detail:
OBSERVED 2026-08-18. `stale8_lt0R` on `xrp_pullback_2h` carried `verdict: insufficient_base`, `would_have_been: is_oos_fail`, OOS base **23** trades against the floor of 25. The per-cell record is exemplary — `insufficient_base_why` even names the remedy verbatim ('THE BOUNDARY IS MISPLACED, NOT THE LEG ... re-run with a larger --split-target-oos'). The problem is that nothing surfaces it ABOVE the per-cell level.

Consequence, measured: this leg's hold-conviction levers had never been graded, and the session-level reading was that they had been tried and had failed. I only found it by dumping raw verdicts.json after two failed structure guesses. Re-running at `--split-target-oos 50` graded all 14 cells (#9942) and gave a genuine answer.

`insufficient_base` is the honest state and must stay — the defect is that it is invisible from the summary, so 'we tested it' and 'we could not test it' read the same at the level anyone actually reads.
items.resolution_criteria: Surface an ungraded count in SUMMARY.md and in the sweep's stdout per leg — e.g. `xrp_pullback_2h: 14 cells, 4 UNGRADED (insufficient_base)` — and carry it in the fleet `selection` block beside `cells_tried`. A leg whose cells are majority-ungraded should not be reportable as assessed. DONE when a run containing an insufficient_base cell says so without opening the JSON.

updates.note: Re-validated: a cell that hit the OOS floor reads as MEASURED at the fleet level. Same family as BL-20260814-CORPUS-AGREEMENT-COUNTS-141-UNCHECKABLE-CELLS-AS-CHECKED — roll-ups that count ungraded as graded.

items.title: three order_monitor test fakes served a permanently-open row and never reflected update_trade — the class, not just the three instances
items.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-18 while making the close path package-wide (#9930). Three fakes (`test_close_retry_cooldown._FakeDB`, `test_strategy_monocle_partial_close_verdict._FakeDB`, and a third via the same shape) returned a trade row unconditionally — one ignored `filters` entirely — and recorded `update_trade` calls without applying them. A row could therefore never be observed to close.

That fiction was INVISIBLE while the close path resolved one leg by id and never re-read. The moment the code re-read to ask 'are any legs left?', three tests failed for a reason that had nothing to do with the change. One also mutated a module-level dict shared across tests once reflection was added, producing order-dependent failures.

Directly the pairs-suite lesson recorded in CLAUDE.md — tests that 'passed against a fictional table' — recurring in a different subsystem. Filing the CLASS because fixing three fakes does not stop the fourth.
items.resolution_criteria: Audit the DB fakes across tests/ for two properties: (1) `get_trades` honours the `filters` it is passed, and (2) `update_trade` reflects at least `status` into what `get_trades` subsequently returns. Prefer a single shared in-memory fake over per-file ones — the three fixed here were three independent re-implementations of the same object. Consider a test that asserts the shared fake's `get_trades` respects a `status` filter, so the fake itself is covered. DONE when a new close-path test cannot pass against a row that never closes.

updates.note: Re-validated: a fake that serves a permanently-open row and never reflects update_trade certifies the code against a world that cannot exist. Same family as BL-20260823-FIXTURE-MISSING-A-PRODUCTION-COLUMN-FAILS-SILENTLY and BL-20260813-HARNESS-SYMBOL-IS-A-LABEL-DATA-DEFAULTS-TO-BTC.

items.title: 22 of 34 open trades can close ONLY by price reaching a level fixed at entry - no path closes them on anything learned since
items.detail:
Measured 2026-08-18 by scripts/ops/exit_path_coverage.py over the live journal (/api/diag/journal?table=trades&limit=1000, open + non-backtest) joined to /api/diag/position_telemetry. POPULATION: 34 open non-backtest trades, 17 with a telemetry row. VERDICTS: decision_exit_live 2, price_only 22, unknown 10, no_exit_path 0. So exactly TWO open positions have a confirmed path that can close them on post-entry evidence; 22 are confirmed to have none, and the remaining 10 are unknown rather than fine.

The distinction the audit draws: a `price_level` path (broker stop, broker target, monitor sl_cross/tp_cross) fires only when price REACHES a level fixed at entry and cannot act on anything learned since. A `decision` path (stale_stop, giveback_stop, exit_head, trail_decay, time_decay, vwap_cross) fires on accumulated evidence. A trade with price paths and no decision path is un-closeable for any reason other than price arriving somewhere - which is precisely the state the 20-day XRP short (trade 4163) is in, and it is invisible to every pre-existing surface: the leg grades ok on lever_reachability_audit (its arms are honest), ok on exit_mechanism_coverage (it declares only what its module reads), and the trade shows a populated stop_loss and take_profit_1 in the journal.

THREE DISTINCT CAUSES, each wanting a different remedy - collapsing them into one count is what made this unactionable before:
  all_undeclared (9): 4711, 4701, 4700, 4574, 4550, 4547, 4350, 4348, 4347. The leg runs trend_donchian, whose module implements ALL FOUR M20 mechanisms, and the leg declares ZERO of them. Pure config gap - a Tier-3 value decision per leg, no engineering.
  mixed (11): 4619, 4585, 4484, 4480, 4469, 4468, 4195, 4194, 4170, 4169, 4163. The htf_pullback_trend_2h family implements exactly ONE of the four (trail_decay); the other three grade not_implemented. On top of that its one mechanism is either undeclared or unreachable. Engineering work, not a config change.
  declared_but_unreachable (2): 4653, 4652 (qqq_trend_long_1d) - trail_decay is declared and graded `inert` in config/lever_reachability.json.

NOT a claim that any of these trades SHOULD close. It is the prior question: if the system concluded one should, on 22 of 34 there is no mechanism through which that conclusion could act. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'measured_open' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-23 by the full-system audit, on BOTH populations, using scripts/ops/exit_mechanism_coverage.py (the authoritative declare table) rather than a hand-rolled map. BY OPEN POSITION — this row's own population, from /api/bot/positions?include_paper=true: 29 open, of which 18 have NO declared decision-driven exit lever and 11 do, i.e. 62.1% can close only by price reaching a level fixed at entry. Against the row's original 22 of 34 = 64.7%, that is 64.7% -> 62.1% over five days: unchanged in substance, and NOT an improvement to bank. Zero open positions had a strategy missing from the coverage table, so the denominator is complete. BY LIVE LEG — the wider population, since an open-position snapshot is point-in-time: 20 of 46 live legs declare at least one lever, 26 of 46 (56.5%) declare none. Across all legs the mechanism states are 23 declared, 115 undeclared, 42 not_implemented, 4 unresolved; 0 orphaned declares. THE LOOP CLOSES ON THIS SESSION'S OWN INCIDENT: both positions that consumed a week of operator attention sit in the WITHOUT list — ict_scalp_mgc_15m (MGC 4773, which ran 233.88+ points past its declared target and stayed open) and mes_trend_long_1d (MES 4350). Also worth noting for the leg roster: trend_donchian_eth_4h declares nothing while its siblings trend_donchian and trend_donchian_eth both declare exit_head — a 4h variant of a family that HAS levers, declaring none.
evidence: scripts/ops/exit_path_coverage.py --journal-json <trades> --telemetry-json <pt> --broker-json <ibo>
config/lever_reachability.json (qqq_trend_long_1d verdict=inert; xrp_pullback_2h verdict=vol_conditional arm_r=4.49)
src/units/strategies/htf_pullback_trend_2h.py implements trail_decay only
items.resolution_criteria: Basis for the counts above: scripts/ops/exit_path_coverage.py run 2026-08-18 against the live journal, 34 open non-backtest rows, self-test 7/7 with planted controls. RESOLVED when either (a) the price_only count is driven down by operator-approved declares plus the pullback-family mechanism work, or (b) the operator records a decision that price-only is the intended posture for a named subset, with that subset carried in the audit as an accepted exclusion rather than a finding. Progress is measurable by re-running the audit: it prints by_verdict and the cause split.
items.next_action: ✅ OPERATOR DISPOSITION RECORDED 2026-08-23T04:3xZ (four options offered: declare-the-9 / record-price-only-as-intended / both / defer): **DECLARE THE 9 FIRST** — resolution path (a), starting with the `all_undeclared` trend_donchian subset (4711, 4701, 4700, 4574, 4550, 4547, 4350, 4348, 4347). Chosen because that module already implements ALL FOUR M20 mechanisms and declares ZERO of them, so this is a config declare against proven, instrumented code rather than new mechanism work. ⚠️ EACH DECLARED VALUE IS STILL A TIER-3 VALUE and needs its own approval — the operator approved the APPROACH, not a set of numbers. ⚠️ MEASURE THE DROP, DO NOT ASSERT IT: re-run scripts/ops/exit_path_coverage.py afterward and quote by_verdict + the cause split; the row is explicit that progress is measurable that way. The other two causes (10 `unknown`, not 'fine') are NOT covered by this disposition and stay open. ⚠️ MEASURED 2026-08-24 BEFORE ACTING, and the values CANNOT YET BE RESPONSIBLY CHOSEN (docs/research/declare-the-9-cannot-be-valued-yet-2026-08-24.md): (a) only 3 of the 9 named trades are still OPEN (4711, 4350, 4347) — six closed between 08-23 and 08-24, so the trade list is two-thirds stale; the unit of action was always the LEG, which is unaffected. (b) 9 ENABLED trend_donchian-MODULE legs declare none of the four — a coincidence of number with the 9 trades, not the same set, and the two must not be conflated. (c) A declare only reaches `decision_exit_live` when arm_reach == reachable FOR THAT FILL; an unreachable one grades ABSENT and the trade STAYS price_only under a new cause, and an unmeasured one grades `unknown` — so two of the three landings are not progress. (d) Declaring blind demonstrably lands unreachable: fleet-wide arm_reach is no_arm_declared 35 / unreachable 19 / reachable 6, i.e. 19 of 25 DECLARED arms are inert, including two on this very module (qqq_trend_long_1d arm 3.56 vs cap 2.13; trend_donchian_sol_4h arm 5.57 vs cap 1.44). (e) Per-leg telemetry n is 1-4 and TWO legs have zero rows; trend_donchian_eth_4h's cap_r spans 1.396-8.632 (6.2x) over n=4. The working template is scha_trend_long_1d (arm 2.0 vs cap 2.778 -> reachable), and it is arithmetic, not taste. NEXT: derive cap_r per HISTORICAL fill from the journal (cap_r = 0.099 * entry / (atr_stop_mult * ATR)) rather than from live telemetry, propose an arm at a stated percentile, and quote the reachable fraction — with the admission criterion written down BEFORE that run.

updates.note:
MEASURED FROM THE LIVE SOAK, not from config. The target-extension ANNOTATE soak (runtime_logs/target_extension_soak.jsonl, shipped this morning) has been accruing on the trader; read via /api/diag/log_file?name=target_extension_soak.

POPULATION: 28 rows = 14 DISTINCT open order packages x 2 exit passes. State it, because 28 is not the denominator.

    declare tp_r = 50.0 (the far sentinel)  14 / 14
    take-profit set by the VENUE CAP        13 / 14
    actual reward-to-risk < 1                2 / 14
    actual R:R range                    0.687 .. 61.2

THE CAP-BINDING CLAIM IS ARITHMETIC, NOT INFERENCE. For each of the 13 the placed take-profit equals entry x 1.099 (long) or entry x 0.901 (short) to the last digit -- e.g. XRPUSDT 1.4995 -> 1.647951, MHG 6.498 -> 7.141302, MES 7634.75 -> 8390.590250, TLT short 84.1 -> 75.774100. The one exception is spy_pullback_1h, whose cap_r (61.2) EXCEEDS the 50R sentinel, so its target is the sentinel itself: a take-profit placed 50R = 8.1% away on a 1h SPY pullback.

SO THE MECHANISM IS NOW FULLY VISIBLE, and it is worse than 'some legs lack a target'. Every open leg declares the sentinel `tp_r: 50`, which MEANS 'no real target, the trail is the exit' -- but the system still PLACES a real take-profit order. Where that order lands is decided by whichever binds first, the sentinel or Bybit's ~9.9% ErrCode-10001 boundary, and for 13 of 14 it is the VENUE. The reward side of those trades is a venue error-code limit. Whether it exceeds the risk side is an accident of how wide the stop happens to be: same declared config, R:R from 0.687 to 61.2, an ~89x spread.

THE TWO SUB-1 LEGS ARE BOTH CRYPTO LONGS -- xrp_pullback_2h at 0.687 (REAL MONEY) and ada_pullback_2h at 0.843. That is not a coincidence: the cap is a fixed 9.9% of entry while the stop is volatility-scaled, so the ratio inverts exactly when risk/entry exceeds 9.9%. Crypto is where it does. This is the same class the operator raised on XRP, now with its population and its mechanism measured rather than one instance.

⚠️ THIS SUPERSEDES THE '0.08% / 0.16%' SIZING quoted earlier in the audit doc, which counted packages that HIT the cap historically and was the wrong denominator. The right question is not how many hit a limit; it is how many have a take-profit that no strategy chose. On the live open book that is 13 of 14.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: nothing here grades whether a sentinel is WRONG for a trend leg. A trail-is-the-exit design is legitimate, and `mes_trend_long_1d` at 7.5R is not a trade in trouble. What is indefensible is that the sentinel silently becomes a REAL order at a level chosen by an exchange limit, with no leg declaring what it expects -- so nothing downstream can tell a deliberate 7.5R from an accidental 0.687.

TIER-3 DECISION THIS ENABLES: declare a real `target_r` per leg (the resolver already reads `target_r` first and falls back to `tp_r`, so a leg can be given an expectation without touching the legacy key). Until then the extension lever cannot fire at all -- every soak row reads `sentinel_no_expectation` / `no_expectation_declared`, 14 of 14, which is the lever correctly refusing to extend a target that was never a prediction.

TARGET_R DERIVATION RUN for the two R:R<1 legs, on real corpora. Full write-up: docs/research/target-r-derivation-crypto-pullback-2026-08-23.md. Config-exact params read from config/strategies.yaml; 13,212 2h bars per leg fetched via the repo's own fetch_backtest_candles.py --source binance_vision (NOT the committed BTCUSDT 1-minute fixture, which m31_harness_mfe_dist.py's docstring names as an order-of-magnitude error for this purpose). Each leg run TWICE on identical bars: capped 0.099 (what production does) and uncapped (no take-profit path at all, so mfe_r is TRUE excursion rather than one truncated at the ceiling).

FINDING 1 -- `tp_r: 50` IS UNREACHABLE BY AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE. Best excursion either leg ever produced across three years: xrp 4.31R capped / 20.46R uncapped, ada 4.36 / 8.96. The sentinel is not a target that is rarely hit; it is one that CANNOT be hit, which is precisely why the venue cap binds on essentially every trade.

FINDING 2 -- THE CAP IS THE DOMINANT DESTROYER OF EDGE HERE. net_R capped vs uncapped: xrp +5.75 vs +22.86, ada +3.83 vs +21.84 -- roughly 4x on both. ⚠️ NOT the same population and NOT a clean delta: trade counts differ (181 vs 154; 146 vs 111) because a capped take-profit exit ends a trade earlier and permits more subsequent entries. Do not quote 'the cap costs 17R'. What is supported is the direction and the rough magnitude.

FINDING 3 -- AND IT CHANGES THE REMEDY. Declaring target_r is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. The placed target is min(entry x 1.099, entry + target_r x risk), so the cap binds whenever cap_r < target_r. Measured per trade: cap_r < 3 on 68.2% (xrp) / 84.7% (ada); cap_r < 2 on 33.1% / 42.3%; and **cap_r < 1 on 9.1% (14/154) and 11.7% (13/111)**. So for about ONE TRADE IN TEN on these legs NO COHERENT BRACKET EXISTS AT ALL -- the venue ceiling sits nearer than the stop and the trade is structurally guaranteed R:R below 1 whatever anyone declares. The live XRP position at cap_r 0.687 is not an outlier; it is that ~9% tail, observed. This is a structural incompatibility between a volatility-scaled stop (2.5xATR) and a fixed-percentage venue ceiling, and no target value repairs it.

PROPOSAL (Tier-3, NOT applied): `target_r: 2.5` on both. Just under p75 of true excursion (2.72 / 2.54) so it is a level the strategy actually reaches, and above median cap_r (2.45 / 2.15) so the DECLARATION is the binding term on roughly half of trades rather than the venue. 3.0 would be unplaceable on 68-85% and leave the cap in charge; 1.5 sits below p75 excursion and would cut winners the strategy demonstrably runs.

⚠️ THE PROPOSAL IS DERIVED, NOT VALIDATED. It comes from the excursion distribution, not from a run that TRADES it. The honest next step is a sweep of target_r in {1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0} scored on net R against the capped baseline -- which is ALSO the tune-before-demote attempt these legs owe, so one piece of work discharges both. And n is small at the tail: 154 and 111 trades over three years, with p90+ resting on 15 and 11.

NOTHING HERE EXTENDS TO THE OTHER 50 LEGS. The 26 remaining crypto legs are reachable by the same method (binance_vision, Bybit interval codes -- 120 = 2h, 240 = 4h). The equity/ETF/futures legs have no reachable corpus from a sandbox session and no committed one in-repo; they need trainer-side sweeps.

CRITICAL, RE-CONFIRMED, AND THE OPERATOR DISPOSITION IS ALREADY RECORDED (2026-08-23) — so what remains is EXECUTION of that decision, not another measurement. CORROBORATED LIVE THIS REVIEW: only 8.3% of the window's 120 closes came from a declared bracket (tp 3 + sl 7); 34 were `reconciler` and 76 `other` (janitor + sleeve paths). 15 positions are open now. 15 positions are open right now and the longest holds in the window were 721 h (tlt_pullback_1d) and 554 h (iwm_trend_long_1d). Nothing has changed in the mechanism since the row was filed.

items.title: position_telemetry stores -1e18 as peak_r when the peak has never been measurable, so a fabricated number reaches every consumer
items.detail:
The upsert reads peak_r = MAX(COALESCE(position_telemetry.peak_r, -1e18), COALESCE(excluded.peak_r, -1e18)). The COALESCE default is a sentinel chosen so a real peak always wins the MAX - but when BOTH sides are NULL (a row whose peak_state is `thin_window`, i.e. never measurable) the MAX returns the SENTINEL and it is persisted as though it were a measurement. peak_pct_of_cap then derives from it: measured 2026-08-18 on trade 4711 (qld_trend_long_1d) peak_r = -1e+18, peak_pct_of_cap = -7.620208793720948e+19, cap_r = 1.3123, peak_state = 'thin_window'; and trade 4710 (scha_trend_long_1d) peak_r = -1e+18, peak_pct_of_cap = -3.5994528831617593e+19, peak_state = 'thin_window'. POPULATION: 2 of 20 telemetry rows on the live journal.

This is the module's OWN declared constraint 3 violated by a different number: 'peak_state carries the reason MFE is absent, never a fabricated 0.0'. The reason IS carried correctly - peak_state says thin_window - but peak_r beside it carries a value, and a consumer reading peak_r without branching on peak_state gets a number never observed. Any MIN or distribution over peak_r is destroyed by it, the same shape as the exposure-soak min-multiple that had to be kept null rather than 0.0.

Correct behaviour: when both sides are NULL the column must stay NULL. A CASE that returns NULL when both are NULL and the MAX otherwise, or a WHERE-guarded update. scripts/ops/exit_path_coverage.py refuses any |value| >= 1e17 and reports summary.sentinel_peak_rows, so the audit does not launder it - but that is a consumer-side band-aid over a producer-side defect, and every OTHER consumer (including /api/bot/positions' r block and /api/diag/position_telemetry) still sees the sentinel. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'measured_open' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
evidence: src/runtime/position_telemetry.py::_UPSERT ON CONFLICT ... peak_r=MAX(COALESCE(...,-1e18), COALESCE(...,-1e18))
/api/diag/position_telemetry?limit=200 rows for trade_id 4710 and 4711 (2026-08-18)
items.resolution_criteria: Basis: the two rows above read from /api/diag/position_telemetry on 2026-08-18, against 20 rows total. RESOLVED when the upsert leaves peak_r NULL where both sides are NULL, a test pins that a thin_window row stores NULL rather than a sentinel, and the existing sentinel rows are cleaned or allowed to age out - verified by a re-read showing summary.sentinel_peak_rows empty.

updates.note:
MEASURED FIRST, 2026-08-25T16:5xZ via /api/diag/position_telemetry?limit=60 (60 rows) — and the population is WORSE than either row recorded:
  peak_state distribution: 48 `measured` + 12 `thin_window`, ZERO nulls
  rows with a non-null peak_r whose state != measured: 11 of 60 (18.3%)
  every one of those 11 holds EXACTLY -1e+18, served through peak_pct_of_cap as values down to -8.20e+19
The earlier reads (2 of 20 on 08-18, 1 of 33 on 08-20) understated it; the share has grown.

THE ZERO-NULLS FACT IS WHAT MADE THE FIX SAFE, and it was checked rather than assumed. Gating the read on `peak_state == measured` is only correct if production always writes that column — otherwise the gate would blank real measurements. 60 of 60 carry it. The pre-existing test fixture did NOT, which is why it failed on the change: it described a row production does not produce, so any peak assertion built on it was testing an unreachable state. The fixture was corrected to match production, and the sentinel case was given its OWN fixture rather than a row in the shared one — adding it there would have forced edits to two unrelated count assertions, and rewriting another test's population to accommodate your own new row is how a real assertion gets quietly loosened.

PRODUCER (BL-20260818). The upsert's `peak_r=MAX(COALESCE(...,-1e18), COALESCE(...,-1e18))` now sits inside a CASE returning NULL when BOTH sides are NULL. The write path is load-bearing and is why a single write could never reproduce this: the first pass INSERTs and correctly stores NULL; only the second takes the UPDATE branch where MAX has nothing to compare and returns the sentinel. Verified in BOTH directions against a temp DB — the pre-fix statement, reconstructed by swapping the clause back, yields exactly -1e+18 and a peak_pct_of_cap of -2.55e+19 on two unmeasurable passes, while the fixed one yields NULL. Four control cases still hold: a real peak survives an unmeasurable later pass, a shallower pass cannot walk a peak backwards, a NULL followed by a real peak takes the real one, and repeated unmeasurable passes stay NULL.

READER (BL-20260820). `enrich_record` now serves `peak_r` and `peak_pct_of_cap` as null whenever `peak_state` is not `measured`, keyed on THE STATE and never on a magnitude — a `|value| >= 1e17` threshold would be a second definition of the sentinel living apart from the first, and the two would drift. A test proves the state is what decides, by planting an ORDINARY-LOOKING peak (1.5) on a thin_window row and asserting it is still refused. This also covers the rows already carrying the stored sentinel, which the producer fix cannot retroactively repair.

THE CHECK-A INVERSION, which is what made this high rather than medium: `peak_above_cap` counted `(peak_pct_of_cap or 0) > 100.0`, and a NEGATIVE sentinel is below 100 — so a row whose peak was never measured was scored as WITHIN CAP. An unmeasured row read as a passing one, on the invariant M31 P4 judges the fleet by. It now counts only gradeable rows and publishes `peak_gradeable_rows` beside itself, so `0 breaches` states how many rows it could grade — the rCoverage/measured_n discipline. A test asserts the ungradeable row is EXCLUDED from the denominator rather than counted clean, with a genuinely over-cap row as the positive control so the assertion is not trivially satisfied by zero.

This row's criterion also asked that existing sentinel rows be 'cleaned or allowed to age out'. They are NOT cleaned — the reader gate is what keeps them off every consumer, and a row's stored value is left as the record of what the producer actually wrote. A re-read after deploy should show summary.sentinel_peak_rows empty on scripts/ops/exit_path_coverage.py; the stored -1e+18 will persist until those 11 open positions close.

items.title: Resting-bracket state is unreadable from any session for 33 of 34 open trades - /api/diag/ib_open_orders is IB-only
items.detail:
BL-20260814-NO-IB-OPEN-ORDERS-READ-SURFACE was resolved by adding /api/diag/ib_open_orders, which reduces nothing and lets a session check the boolean/quantity coverage verdicts against actual rows. There is no equivalent for bybit or alpaca. Measured 2026-08-18 via scripts/ops/exit_path_coverage.py: of 34 open non-backtest trades, broker-bracket state is UNOBSERVABLE for 34 - 33 because the account is not an IB account (read_state `not_ib`) and 1 because ib_paper returned `could_not_look`. So the audit can grade zero of them on broker reality and correctly reports `unknown` rather than inventing an answer.

This is the READ half of BL-20260816-TARGET-NAKEDNESS-UNDETECTABLE-ON-ALPACA-AND-BYBIT, and it is a distinct remedy: that row is about the SWEEP's grading, this is about a session being able to contradict the sweep at all. Both live sweeps (_check_broker_naked_bybit_positions, _check_broker_naked_equity_positions) reduce broker state to a verdict before anyone sees it, which is exactly the condition that let the stripped MGC take-profit sit undetected for seven days on the IB side.

Note the ib_paper `could_not_look` in the same read: the IB gateway was not answering at 2026-08-18T09:4xZ, so even the one venue with a read surface was unreadable at that moment - which the audit reports as unknown, not as absent. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'measured_open' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
evidence: /api/diag/ib_open_orders 2026-08-18: bybit_1/bybit_2/bybit_portfolio/alpaca_* all read_state=not_ib; ib_paper and ib_live read_state=could_not_look
scripts/ops/exit_path_coverage.py summary.broker_observability = {not_ib: 33, could_not_look: 1}
items.resolution_criteria: Basis: the /api/diag/ib_open_orders read and the audit rollup above, both taken 2026-08-18 over 34 open non-backtest trades. RESOLVED when a diag route serves resting protective orders for bybit and alpaca accounts with the same three-state read_state discipline (not_applicable / could_not_look / orders_read) and exit_path_coverage's broker_observability count for those venues drops to the genuinely-unreadable remainder.

updates.note:
HALF RESOLVED, AND THE OTHER HALF MOVED - re-validated against the code this session, not inferred from the merge.

BYBIT: DONE. /api/diag/bybit_open_orders shipped 2026-08-22 (src/web/api/routers/diag.py:2278, src/units/accounts/clients.py:1771::account_bybit_open_orders) with exactly the three-state read_state discipline this row's criterion asks for (not_bybit / could_not_look / orders_read), and it serves BOTH the Full-mode position-level stop_loss/take_profit AND the Partial-mode resting legs - which matters here, because a surface dumping only orders would report zero legs for a correctly-protected Full-mode position and a consumer would grade it naked.

ALPACA: NOT DONE. There is no account_alpaca_open_orders and no route. AlpacaClient's only order-state accessor is has_protective_orders (alpaca_client.py:979) - a BOOLEAN, i.e. the reducing verdict this row exists to be able to contradict. So the Alpaca half is untouched.

AND THE CRITERION'S SECOND CLAUSE IS BLOCKED BY A THIRD THING, WHICH IS THE ACTUAL FINDING. The criterion says exit_path_coverage's broker_observability count must drop for those venues. It has not, and NOT because the capability is missing: scripts/ops/exit_path_coverage.py still reads only --broker-json /api/diag/ib_open_orders (line 56), and its _broker_rollup docstring at line 489 still asserts "/api/diag/ib_open_orders is IB-only, so a bybit or alpaca position's resting brackets CANNOT BE READ FROM ANY DIAG SURFACE". That sentence is now FALSE for bybit and the tool acts on it - every bybit position keeps grading `not_ib`, which the same docstring correctly calls "not a clean negative, it is a missing read surface". The read surface is no longer missing; the consumer was never told. Field beats comment, and this is the written-and-never-read shape one level up: a route shipped, and the one audit that reports the gap it closes still reports the gap.

REMAINING WORK, in order: (1) teach exit_path_coverage to accept a bybit broker-json and grade from it, and fix the stale impossibility claim in its docstring - this is Tier-1 and is what makes the bybit half VISIBLE rather than merely built; (2) build the Alpaca route. Until (1) lands the bybit route is capability nobody can see the effect of, which is the condition this row was opened about.

STEP (1) OF THE PREVIOUS UPDATE IS DONE, AND THE OBSERVABILITY COUNT MOVED - MEASURED, not asserted.

scripts/ops/exit_path_coverage.py now takes --bybit-broker-json (/api/diag/bybit_open_orders) beside the existing --broker-json, and the stale impossibility claim in _broker_rollup's docstring is corrected in place rather than deleted, so the next reader sees WHY it was wrong.

MEASURED ON LIVE PAYLOADS, 2026-08-25 (journal limit=1000, telemetry limit=200, both diag order routes), same journal both arms - 27 open non-backtest trades with unobservable broker-bracket state BEFORE, 15 AFTER:
  before  {account_not_in_payload: 24, read_state:could_not_look: 3}
  after   {account_not_in_payload: 12, read_state:could_not_look: 3}
The 12 newly graded are bybit_1 (5), bybit_2 (4) and bybit_portfolio (3), ALL reading stop=live AND target=live - so the first thing this surface says is that the bybit book is fully bracketed, which nothing could previously confirm.

STATE THE RESIDUAL, because 'the count dropped' is not the same as 'the gap closed'. The remaining 15 are exactly two things and neither is a bybit row: 12 ALPACA (alpaca_paper 6, alpaca_portfolio 6) which have no route at all, and 3 ib_paper reading could_not_look because the IB gateway was not answering at read time - an honest 'we did not look', not an absent bracket.

SO THE CRITERION IS NOW HALF-MET AND THE REMAINING HALF IS SHARP: build the Alpaca route. AlpacaClient's only order-state accessor is has_protective_orders, a BOOLEAN - the reducing verdict this row exists to be able to contradict - so the Alpaca half is a genuine build, not a wiring job.

DESIGN NOTES CARRIED, because both are ways the bybit read could have been wrong while looking right: (a) BOTH the position rows and the resting orders are indexed, since under BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=full there is NO resting order and the stop lives on the position row - an orders-only indexer would have graded a correctly-protected position ABSENT, manufacturing an alarm rather than missing one; (b) merging two venue payloads refuses to let a not_ib / not_bybit sentinel overwrite the other venue's real orders_read entry, which a plain dict.update does silently. Both invariants are pinned by tests that were BREAK-TESTED (naive merge, orders-only indexer, and crediting an unclassifiable leg to a side) - each break fails the suite. tests/test_exit_path_coverage.py 20 -> 33; the script's own --self-test 9 -> 19.

THE ALPACA HALF IS BUILT — and it is SHIPPED-BUT-UNEXERCISED, which is a different claim from 'the gap is closed'. Do not read it as the latter.

WHAT EXISTS: /api/diag/alpaca_open_orders + clients.account_alpaca_open_orders, the third sibling of the IB and Bybit routes, honouring the same three-state read_state contract (not_alpaca / could_not_look / orders_read) with counts null-never-zero and an unset price null-never-0.0. exit_path_coverage takes --alpaca-broker-json beside the other two, and its _broker_rollup docstring no longer names Alpaca as a standing gap — a basis of account_not_in_payload now means A PAYLOAD WAS NOT SUPPLIED, which is a different fact from the surface not existing, and the docstring says so.

⚠️ WHAT IS NOT MEASURED: the observability drop. Read live at 2026-08-25T23:3xZ the route returns **HTTP 404** — correctly, because the VM runs main and this is not deployed. So the 15 -> 3 drop this change is BUILT to produce is a PREDICTION, not a reading, and the previous update's measured 27 -> 15 (bybit) must not be extended to it. The residual after deploy should be the 3 ib_paper could_not_look rows plus whatever alpaca itself cannot read.

TWO DESIGN POINTS, both places this could have been wrong while looking right:
(a) ALPACA IS NOT BYBIT — there is no position-level protection here. Bybit's Full mode puts stopLoss/takeProfit on the POSITION row, so that indexer must read both collections; /v2/positions carries no protective level at all, so on Alpaca the resting ORDERS are the whole story and indexing positions would credit coverage that CANNOT EXIST. The payload states position_level_protection_supported: false rather than leaving the asymmetry to be inferred from an absence.
(b) THE TWO SUB-READS FAIL INDEPENDENTLY. The orders read answers the protection question, so its failure nulls the payload; a POSITIONS outage leaves that answer intact and reports positions: null + positions_state: could_not_look with position_count null — never [] / 0, which would claim the account is flat. The FIRST version of the test for this could not express the state it meant to (its fixture helper coerced positions=None to []), which is the same collapse one level up in the test harness; it now uses a sentinel.

Also pinned: Alpaca's own `stop_limit` type string CONTAINS 'limit', so the stop family is tested first — a naive limit-first classifier would file every stop-limit as a take-profit and MANUFACTURE target coverage, the IB 'STP LMT' lesson on a second venue. Three invariants break-tested (collapsing the sub-reads, dropping nested bracket legs, coercing an unset price to 0.0); each break fails the suite. tests/test_diag_alpaca_open_orders.py is new (23); test_exit_path_coverage 33 -> 40. Registered in docs/api-tier-policy.md — the api-tier-policy guard caught its absence, which is that guard working.

RESOLUTION STATUS: the criterion's FIRST clause (a route for bybit and alpaca with the three-state discipline) is now met for both venues. Its SECOND clause — exit_path_coverage's broker_observability count dropping for those venues — is met for bybit and PENDING DEPLOY for alpaca. This row stays OPEN until that is read, not inferred.

HALF RESOLVED ON LIVE EVIDENCE — narrow this row to ALPACA. The Bybit surface now EXISTS and works: I called /api/diag/bybit_open_orders?account_id=bybit_2 this review and got read_state `orders_read`, position_count 2, order_count 4, with per-position stop_loss/take_profit/tpsl_mode/position_idx and the Partial-mode legs in result.orders (CLAUDE.md dates it 2026-08-22). Incidental but useful: both bybit_2 positions report position_idx 0, confirming one-way NETTING on the real-money account. ALPACA still has no equivalent, so 'unreadable for 33 of 34 open trades' is no longer the right denominator.

RESOLVED — and EXERCISED, not merely shipped. Both routes the criterion asks for now exist with the three-state read_state discipline: `/api/diag/bybit_open_orders` (2026-08-22) and `/api/diag/alpaca_open_orders` (2026-08-25, whose own docstring names this row).

THE DISTINCTION THIS SESSION KEEPS INSISTING ON: a route existing is not a route working. Called live 2026-08-31, `/api/diag/alpaca_open_orders` returns for all 11 declared accounts:

    alpaca_paper          orders_read   orders=6  positions=3
    alpaca_portfolio      orders_read   orders=8  positions=4
    alpaca_live           orders_read   orders=0  positions=0
    alpaca_options_paper  orders_read   orders=0  positions=0
    (the 7 non-Alpaca accounts correctly read `not_alpaca` with count=null, never 0)

Those two populated accounts ARE the gap this row was filed about: the route's own measurement records that of 15 open trades whose broker-bracket state was unobservable on 2026-08-25, **12 were alpaca** (`alpaca_paper` 6, `alpaca_portfolio` 6). They are now readable, with 14 resting orders served across them.

⚠️ ONE CLAUSE IS INFERRED, NOT RE-MEASURED, AND I AM SAYING SO RATHER THAN LETTING IT PASS. The criterion also asks that `exit_path_coverage.py`'s `broker_observability` count for these venues drop to the genuinely-unreadable remainder. I did NOT re-run that tool; I verified the underlying fact it measures — that a session can now read resting bracket state for both venues — by reading it. If a future run of `exit_path_coverage` still reports those accounts unobservable, that is a defect in the TOOL's wiring to the new routes, and is a new row, not a re-opening of this one.

items.title: M31 P5 precondition 3a is recorded DONE on backtest_trend.py, but the leg that MOTIVATED P5 runs on backtest_pullback.py — which has no --rr-floor, so the lever cannot be measured on the trade it was designed for
items.detail:
checked: scripts/backtest_pullback.py — grepped rr_floor / rr-floor / r_to_target, ZERO occurrences on 2026-08-18, against a POSITIVE CONTROL in checked: scripts/backtest_trend.py which carries all of them. Also checked: scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py (zero — the GRADER had no cell either) and checked: docs/research/RESEARCH-CAPABILITY-INDEX.md. ⚠️ THE CLAIM WAS TRUE WHEN FILED AND IS NOW HISTORICAL: the lever was ported the same day (see status), so re-reading this row without this note would report a capability gap that no longer exists.

MEASURED 2026-08-18.

`docs/design/m31-p5-telemetry-reading-lever-PROPOSAL.md` § 5 precondition 3a reads 'IMPLEMENT — DONE 2026-08-17 … scripts/backtest_trend.py gains --rr-floor'. That is true of `backtest_trend.py`.

But the proposal's own motivating case — trade 4163, `xrp_pullback_2h`, real money on bybit_2, the trade § 3 quotes `rr_from_here` 0.71 for — does NOT run on that harness. The fleet sweep's own run plan (relay #9934) resolves this leg to:
    RUN  xrp_pullback_2h   backtest_pullback.py   data/XRPUSDT_5m.csv
and `scripts/backtest_pullback.py`'s argparse has `--stale-exit-bars`, `--stale-exit-below-r`, `--giveback-r`, `--giveback-min-mfe-r`, `--trail-decay-*`, `--tp-cap-pct`, `--emit-trades` — and NO `--rr-floor`.

So precondition 3b ('MEASURE') is blocked on this leg by something the proposal attributes to data: it records the blocker as 'the only candle file in the repo cannot exercise it' (BTCUSDT 1-minute). Data is a real blocker for the TREND legs. For the pullback leg there is a second, prior blocker — the flag does not exist in its harness — and the trainer DOES hold `data/XRPUSDT_5m.csv` and `XRPUSDT_15m.csv`, so the data blocker does not even apply here. One stated cause was masking another.

A THIRD related gap, same read: the fleet sweep generates no rr_floor cell at all (`grep -c 'rr_floor\|rr-floor' scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py` -> 0). So even once the flag exists, `m20_fleet_exit_sweep` will not exercise it — the measurement needs either a new lever family in the sweep or a direct harness invocation.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND BOOKKEEPING. P5's whole justification is the XRP hold-through-churn question, and the operator has since reframed the objective explicitly as capital utilisation: unless the system is confident a position is worth holding, liquidate and free the capital. `rr_from_here` IS that rule expressed as a number (trade 4163 currently reads 0.6252 — risking 1.54R to make 0.96R). A precondition marked DONE that cannot be exercised on the motivating leg means the milestone's central question has no path to an answer, while the phase table shows the implement step complete.

items.title: exchange_fills_ib.closed_pnl_from_fills has ZERO production callers, so IBKR's own realizedPNL is pulled hourly into the store and never read — 0 of 33 ib_paper closed trades have ever carried a broker-sourced pnl
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-18, chasing why MGC 4487 still had pnl null 90 minutes after a confirmed fill.

THE CHAIN, each link verified:
  1. `clients.BROKER_PNL_READER_EXCHANGES` is `frozenset({'alpaca','interactive_brokers','bybit'})` — IB IS declared a broker-PnL reader. (The docstring at `exchange_fills_ib.py:25` still says 'today {"bybit"}' and is stale.)
  2. `ict-ib-executions-pull.timer` runs and works. The 09:18:15Z run logged `raw_fills: 35, mapped: 35, realized_pnl_count: 35`, newest exec 2026-08-18T07:49:10Z — i.e. the MGC exit's own 35 fills, each carrying a `CommissionReport.realizedPNL` (854.72, 1923.12, 641.04, 427.36, 213.68, …). The broker truth is IN the store.
  3. `exchange_fills_ib.closed_pnl_from_fills` exists, is in `__all__`, and has a test file (`tests/test_ib_closed_pnl_readback.py`).
  4. **It has NO production caller.** Every reference outside its own module is either that test or a single COMMENT in `src/web/api/routers/diag.py:214`. Nothing in `src/runtime/` or `src/units/` calls it.

PROBE VALIDITY (a grep returning nothing is not proof of absence): the same search DOES find positives — the test call sites, and the Bybit analogue `account_closed_pnl_for_trade` with real call sites in `order_monitor`. So the IB reader's zero is a measured zero, not a failed search.

DENOMINATOR: 33 closed `ib_paper` trades. 28 carry a non-null pnl. `pnl_source` splits `(none)` 22 / `local_compute` 7 / `unmeasured` 4. **IB-broker-sourced: 0.** The capability has never fired once.

WHY THE DECLARATION MAKES IT WORSE, not neutral. Being in `BROKER_PNL_READER_EXCHANGES` causes `_sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced` to DEFER an IB row for `_LOCAL_PNL_BROKER_DEFER_MS` (6h) while it waits for a broker record that nothing will ever fetch. After the defer the local sweep prices it anyway — which is exactly the 7 `local_compute` rows above. So the net effect is not 'no pnl': it is a **provenance downgrade**, a locally-computed mark standing in for a broker figure that was sitting in the store the whole time. CLAUDE.md's 'IBKR is a broker-truth reader now' describes a path that has never executed.

IMMINENT AND CONCRETE: MGC trade 4487 closed 2026-08-18T07:52:52Z (+$155.7k paper on a 105-lot). It reads `pnl: null`, `exit_price: null`, `pnl_source: unmeasured`. At ~13:52Z the 6h defer elapses and the local sweep will price it from a mark rather than from the 35 IBKR realizedPNL records already stored. That is a preventable fabrication on the largest close in the book, and the fix is to read a value we already have. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-23 by the full-system audit — THIS ROW'S CONSEQUENCE WAS WRONG WHEN FILED, and it is downgraded critical -> low. The literal claim stands: src/runtime/exchange_fills_ib.py::closed_pnl_from_fills has zero production callers (grep over the tree finds only tests and two guard scripts that DOCUMENT it as unwired). The INFERENCE drawn from that — that IBKR's own realizedPNL is pulled hourly into the store and never read — does not. A DIFFERENT, already-wired function reads exactly that field: clients.account_closed_pnl_for_trade dispatches ex in ('interactive_brokers','alpaca') to src.runtime.fills_pnl.exit_from_fills(require_realized=True), whose contract is that IBKR fills carry CommissionReport.realizedPNL and the result carries closed_pnl for the caller to write directly. That wiring landed 2026-07-31 in #8111 (commit e5e8656a) — EIGHTEEN DAYS BEFORE this row was filed on 2026-08-18 — so the row was not overtaken by events, it was mistaken at the time. clients.BROKER_PNL_READER_EXCHANGES reads {bybit, interactive_brokers, alpaca}, not {bybit}. MEASURED on the live journal 2026-08-23, and STATE THE POPULATION because it is small: ib_paper has 15 closed rows in total, of which 6 closed on or after the 2026-07-31 wiring date; 4 of those 6 grade pnlProvenance='measured' (2 carry no pnl at all), against a pre-wiring mix of fabricated/unverified. The row's '0 of 33 ib_paper' figure is refuted by that. ROOT CAUSE OF THE MISTAKE, fixed in this session: exchange_fills_ib.py's own module docstring asserted that interactive_brokers 'is absent from clients.BROKER_PNL_READER_EXCHANGES (today {"bybit"})' — stale since 2026-07-31 and the exact prose the row reasoned from. Corrected in place, with the historical framing kept as record. Field beats comment, and a call count on ONE accessor is not a claim about the data path. WHAT REMAINS is a genuine but minor cleanup: closed_pnl_from_fills is dead code that duplicates a live capability, which is its own hazard (a future session may wire the dead one and get two answers).
items.resolution_criteria: closed_pnl_from_fills is either deleted, or given a docstring that names fills_pnl.exit_from_fills as the live path and states why this one still exists — so no future reader can repeat the inference this row made. Closed when the module can no longer be read as evidence that IB broker truth is unread.

updates.note: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-20, still standing, unchanged. Measured against main at 12659c7d: `closed_pnl_from_fills(` has ZERO real call sites in src/ -- the only reference outside its own module is a COMMENT at src/web/api/routers/diag.py:214, plus tests/test_ib_closed_pnl_readback.py. PROBE VALIDITY (a grep returning nothing is not proof of absence): the same probe shape finds THREE real call sites for the Bybit analogue `account_closed_pnl_for_trade(` in src/runtime/order_monitor.py (:4741, :5879, :8397), so the IB reader's zero is a measured zero against a working probe, not a failed search. No change in disposition; carried forward with a fresh measurement rather than a re-read.

Re-validated: zero production callers, so IBKR's own realizedPNL is pulled hourly and never read. Written-and-never-read (class A) — the largest class in this backlog and the same shape as this review's own prop_risk_gate finding.

items.title: The rr_floor lever shipped in two harnesses and the sweep that grades it had no cell for it — implemented, measurable, ungradeable
items.detail:
scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py is the ONLY thing that applies the Path A / Path B gate and the yearly walk-forward to an exit lever. The rr_floor lever shipped in scripts/backtest_trend.py on 2026-08-17 and was ported to scripts/backtest_pullback.py on 2026-08-18, and `cells_for` emitted no rr_floor cell for either. Measured by grep: zero occurrences of `rr_floor` or `rr-floor` in the fleet sweep before this change. So the lever was implemented, measurable in both harnesses, and could not be graded — and an operator pre-approval to walk-forward it had nothing to run.

This is the THIRD instance of one class in this session: a capability that exists and nothing calls it. The other two are BL-20260818-IB-BROKER-PNL-READER-HAS-NO-CALLER (closed_pnl_from_fills, 0 production callers) and BL-20260818-ATTACH-IB-TARGET-HAS-NEVER-RUN (an allowlisted action whose script had never executed). provenance-consumer-guard catches the field version of this shape; there is no equivalent asking whether a shipped LEVER has a cell in the sweep that grades levers, or whether an allowlisted ACTION's script has any test. That generalisation is the durable fix and is NOT done here.

FIXED for rr_floor specifically: cells_for now emits rrfloor0.5 / 0.75 / 1.0 for the families whose harness carries the lever, gated through inert_rr_floor_reason so a cell that CANNOT fire is recorded as skipped-and-why rather than emitted. That distinction is load-bearing — an rr_floor cell run without --tp-cap-pct returns exactly-zero deltas that read as `tie_no_improvement`, i.e. 'we measured it and it made no difference', when it was never measurable (the cosmetic-cell anti-pattern, BL-20260730-DONCHIAN-COSMETIC-SHORT-CELLS). The two inert causes are kept as different strings because they have different fixes: `no_tp_cap_in_run` is fixed by passing the flag, `family_has_no_live_tp_cap` cannot be fixed at all.

The floor grid 0.5/0.75/1.0 is a GRID, NOT A RECOMMENDATION. It brackets the live reading that motivated the lever: XRP trade 4163 sits at rr_from_here 0.47 with 0.80R of headroom against 1.70R at risk.

MEASURED 2026-08-18 (trainer relay #9950/#9952, /tmp clone of claude/exit-path-coverage @ dbe321a, XRPUSDT 2h corpus fetched fresh: 13,206 bars 2023-08-14..2026-08-18). Config-exact base via the fleet sweep, --tp-cap-pct 0.099, split 2025-10-16 (oos-trades mode), base n IS=127 OOS=48 against a min_oos_trades_floor of 25.

VERDICT: all three floors FAIL. path_a_pass 0, path_b_candidates 0, path_b_wf_pass 0, cells_withheld_inert 0.

  cell        IS d_net_r  IS d_maxDD   OOS d_net_r  OOS d_maxDD   d_cap/day   d_bars_held
  rrfloor0.5     -5.8796      +3.5179      -3.0970      +1.8597     -0.0215        -8.30
  rrfloor0.75    -3.7168      +1.8967      +0.2403      +0.4231     +0.0008       -15.61
  rrfloor1       -5.5862      +4.0409      -5.9225      +4.1465     -0.0516       -19.24

⚠️ NO WALK-FORWARD RAN, and that is the correct outcome rather than a gap. Both routes short-circuit before it: Path A needs net_R AND maxDD no-worse (every cell is worse on both axes in-sample), and Path B needs net_R up in BOTH windows (net_r_up_both_windows is false for all three). The operator's pre-approval was for a walk-forward that the evidence never justified spending. Do not record this as 'the walk-forward failed'.

THE LEVER WORKS MECHANICALLY AND STILL DOES NOT PAY — which is the finding. It genuinely frees capital: mean hold falls 46.6 -> 21.2 bars at floor 1.0, and capital_days 493.3 -> 333.3 (-32%). But it destroys more R than the capital-time it releases, and that is measured on the operator's OWN axis: d_net_r_per_capital_day is NEGATIVE at 0.5 (-0.0215) and 1.0 (-0.0516), and +0.0008 at 0.75 — noise. So this is not the familiar 'Path A cannot see the capital axis' excuse; Path B looked, on the axis it exists for, and found nothing.

REACHABILITY CONFIRMS THE CELLS WERE REAL, not cosmetic: the base run's own rr_min distribution is p10 0.134 / median 1.145 / p90 3.54 over n=237, so 0.5/0.75/1.0 all sit inside the observed range, and every cell reported rr_floor_state measurable with inert_cells empty.

DIRECTION OF THE UNTESTED REMAINDER: floors above 1.0 are reachable (p90 3.54) and untested, but the tested trend argues against them — 0.5 -0.0215, 0.75 +0.0008, 1.0 -0.0516, i.e. a near-zero peak at 0.75 with 1.0 clearly worse. There is no visible direction to push, so a wider grid is not the obvious next move.

SEPARATE FINDING FROM THE SAME RUN — the config-exact base is a WEAK LEG: IS +1.779R over 127 trades (+0.014R/trade, essentially zero expectancy) and OOS -0.5915R over 48, with the sweep itself stamping rate_ungradeable_why: base_unprofitable on the OOS window. This is NOT the -15.60R figure I first quoted from a non-config-exact run (corrected on #9950); it is milder and it is still not a leg carrying its weight.
evidence: grep -c 'rr_floor' scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py == 0 before 2026-08-18
tests/test_fleet_sweep_rr_floor_cells.py (8 tests, incl. the positive control)
scripts/ops/exit_path_coverage.py 2026-08-18: trade 4163 rr_from_here 0.47
items.resolution_criteria: Basis: the grep above, and the four cell-generator controls run 2026-08-18 (pullback+cap emits 3 cells; pullback without a cap skips with no_tp_cap_in_run; scalp skips with family_has_no_live_tp_cap; donchian+cap emits 3). RESOLVED when the sweep has actually been RUN on xrp_pullback_2h with these cells and a verdict recorded — pass, honest_negative, or path_b_wf_pass with its drawdown-exchange-rate column. Emitting the cells is not the same as grading the lever, and this row must not be closed on the code change alone. MET 2026-08-18: the sweep RAN on xrp_pullback_2h (#9950) and a verdict is recorded above — honest_negative on all three floors, with the cells confirmed measurable rather than cosmetic. The durable generalisation (a guard asking whether a shipped lever has a cell at all, the way provenance-consumer-guard asks it of a field) remains OPEN and is tracked as its own concern, not by this row.

items.title: Live trend_donchian runs stale_stop before giveback_stop; BOTH harnesses run giveback first — and its own comment claims it matches
items.detail:
src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py::monitor evaluates _stale_stop_verdict at step 2.5 and _giveback_verdict at 2.55, under a comment reading 'Checked AFTER stale-stop, matching the harness's exit precedence'. Both harnesses do the opposite. Verified by reading EXECUTION order, not byte offsets: in scripts/backtest_trend.py both live in one per-bar loop, each with its own `break` — giveback at ~line 566, stale at ~582, so giveback wins a bar where both would fire. scripts/backtest_pullback.py::_levers is giveback -> trend_flip -> stale. Field beats comment; the comment is wrong.

IMPACT IS ATTRIBUTION, NOT PnL. Both fire at bar close and exit at the same close price, so R is identical either way; what differs is the recorded exit_reason. That still matters — a per-lever verdict measured in a sweep is attributed to a different lever live, so by_outcome histograms and live exit_reason distributions cannot be reconciled.

LATENT, NOT ACTIVE. The order can only bite when ONE leg declares BOTH keys. Measured 2026-08-18 against config/strategies.yaml over enabled+live legs: stale-only on 3 (ict_scalp_eth_15m, trend_donchian_eth_prop, trend_donchian_xrp_4h), giveback-only on 1 (uso_trend_1h), BOTH on ZERO. So nothing is mis-attributed today, and the first leg to declare both would start it silently.

NOT FIXED HERE deliberately: flipping a live-money family's exit order is Tier-3 and must not ride along inside the shared-lever refactor that found it. The newly-wired pullback family follows ITS OWN harness (giveback then stale), so the two live families now differ — which is the honest state while donchian is the inverted one. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'latent_measured_open' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
evidence: src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py::monitor steps 2.5 / 2.55
scripts/backtest_trend.py per-bar loop: giveback ~566, stale ~582 (both break)
scripts/backtest_pullback.py::_levers: giveback -> trend_flip -> stale
config/strategies.yaml scan 2026-08-18: 0 live legs declare both keys
items.resolution_criteria: Basis: the execution-order reads and the config scan above, both 2026-08-18. RESOLVED when either (a) the operator approves flipping donchian to giveback-first so live matches both harnesses and the stale comment is corrected, or (b) the operator records that live intentionally differs, and the comment is rewritten to say so rather than claiming a parity it does not have. Either way the false comment must go. Re-check the both-declared count first — if it is no longer zero the row is ACTIVE, not latent.

updates.note: Re-validated and it is severe for a medium: the LIVE order matters and BOTH harnesses run the opposite order, so every donchian lever verdict was measured under a precedence production does not use. Its own comment also claims the wrong thing — field beats comment.

items.title: Both exit-coverage audits detect capability by grepping ONE module, so extracting a lever to a shared module reads as losing it
items.detail:
scripts/ops/exit_mechanism_coverage.py::module_implements and scripts/ops/exit_path_coverage.py::module_close_reasons both decided whether a strategy has a mechanism by grepping THAT UNIT'S OWN SOURCE for a cfg-key literal or a close-reason literal. Correct while every lever was inline; a FALSE NEGATIVE the moment one moves.

Demonstrated 2026-08-18 by doing it: extracting stale_stop and giveback_stop to src/runtime/exit_levers.py made both audits report the DONCHIAN family — which trades real money — as having lost two mechanisms it still runs. The planted positive control in exit_path_coverage's self-test ('trend_donchian emits stale_stop') is what caught it; without that control the refactor would have silently degraded every verdict both files produce, in the direction of under-reporting coverage.

FIXED FOR THIS INSTANCE: both detectors now follow the shared import, matched on the imported SYMBOL rather than the module name (importing exit_levers for since_entry is not the same capability as importing stale_stop_verdict, and treating them alike would over-report), and each confirms the SHARED module actually reads the mechanism's keys rather than trusting the call site's name. A negative control pins that a unit importing only since_entry gains no close reason.

THE GENERAL SHAPE IS NOT FIXED. Any future extraction to another shared module re-breaks both files, because the fix enumerates exit_levers specifically. This is the same family as BL-20260818-FLEET-SWEEP-CANNOT-GRADE-THE-RR-FLOOR-LEVER (the sweep had no cell for a shipped lever) and BL-20260818-IB-BROKER-PNL-READER-HAS-NO-CALLER: a capability and the thing that is supposed to see it drift apart, and nothing asserts the relationship. provenance-consumer-guard does exactly this for FIELDS; there is no equivalent for LEVERS.

FOURTH SITE, found by CI rather than by me. The extraction changed a property FOUR places asserted, and only ONE of them was a test: tests/test_exit_mechanism_coverage.py::test_htf_pullback_implements_only_trail_decay, a deliberate tripwire whose failure message reads 'the coverage finding is stale and the docs quoting it must be re-measured'. It caught the change in CI (1 failed, 11581 passed) and named the remedy. The other three were prose: the live docstring in exit_mechanism_coverage.py (a CURRENT-state claim, corrected) and two 2026-08-16 records (historical, annotated forward rather than rewritten — a record of what was measured then is not wrong, but must not be quoted as current).

PROCESS NOTE, recorded because it is the repeatable part: I ran TARGETED tests after the extraction, not the full suite, so I did not see this locally — the full-suite run in that session predated the wiring. A change that alters a property other modules assert needs the full suite before push, and the tripwire is what covered for the gap. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'fix_landed_for_this_instance' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
evidence: exit_path_coverage self-test went 7/7 -> 6/7 on the extraction, failing the donchian positive control
exit_mechanism_coverage reported xrp_pullback_2h stale_stop/giveback as not_implemented after wiring
items.resolution_criteria: Basis: the self-test regression above, observed live while performing the extraction on 2026-08-18, plus the audit output before and after. The per-instance fix is verified by both self-tests (9/9 and 6/6) including a negative control. RESOLVED when a guard asserts the general relationship — that a lever a unit can run is visible to the audits and has a cell in the sweep that grades it — rather than each audit enumerating the shared modules it happens to know about. Until then this row stays open with the instance fixed.

updates.note: Re-validated: extracting a lever to a shared module reads as LOSING the capability. That actively penalises the right refactor.

items.title: xrp_pullback_2h fails ALL THREE decision-exit levers across 7 cells — the leg is the problem, not its exit machinery
items.detail:
Two sweeps, trainer relays #9950 and #9954, config-exact base, --tp-cap-pct 0.099, XRPUSDT 2h corpus 13,206 bars 2023-08-14..2026-08-18, split 2025-10-16, base n IS=127 OOS=48 against a min_oos_trades_floor of 25. SEVEN cells, ALL honest negatives, path_a_pass 0 and path_b_candidates 0 in both runs:

  rr_floor   0.5 / 0.75 / 1.0    d_cap/day -0.0215 / +0.0008 / -0.0516
  stale_stop 8bars / 12bars      d_cap/day -0.0353 / +0.0082
  giveback   MFE1R / MFE2R       d_cap/day -0.0209 / -0.0254

No cell is net_R-up on BOTH windows, so none is even a Path B candidate, and no walk-forward was justified on any of them. The two cells with a positive capital delta are both the OOS-ONLY shape the walk-forward exists to catch — stale12 posts IS -10.1113R against OOS +1.1334R, a 11.2R swing between adjacent periods on the same leg.

WHAT THIS MEANS, stated carefully. The levers are not broken and are not inert: reachability was confirmed (rr_min p10 0.134 / median 1.145 / p90 3.54 over n=237; every cell rr_floor_state measurable; inert_cells empty), and they demonstrably DO what they claim — rr_floor at 1.0 cuts mean hold 46.6 -> 21.2 bars and capital_days by 32%. They simply destroy more R than the capital-time they release, ON THIS LEG.

AND THE LEG BARELY MAKES MONEY. Config-exact base is IS +1.779R over 127 trades (+0.014R/trade, essentially zero expectancy) and OOS -0.5915R over 48, with the sweep stamping rate_ungradeable_why: base_unprofitable on the OOS window. A lever cannot rescue a book with no edge, and improving one would not make the leg worth its capital. So the disposition question for xrp_pullback_2h is a STRATEGY question (demote to shadow? retune? kill?), not an exit-mechanics question — which is the opposite of where this investigation started, and worth recording so the next session does not re-open the exits.

items.title: rr_floor exists in both harnesses and ZERO live units — a passing sweep cell could not have been declared
items.detail:
Found by the FIRST run of the new lever-wiring-guard, which is the point of it. Measured 2026-08-18: `rr_floor` / `rr_from_here` appears 23 times in scripts/backtest_trend.py, 23 times in scripts/backtest_pullback.py, and ZERO times across src/units/strategies/*.py and src/runtime/exit_levers.py. It is a backtest-only lever.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE WORK DONE EARLIER THE SAME DAY: the operator pre-approved an rr_floor walk-forward and it was run (#9950). Worth doing — but a PASS could not have been acted on, because declaring `rr_floor` in a leg's YAML would produce an ORPHANED DECLARE, a key no module reads. That is exactly the condition the stale_stop/giveback extraction fixed for the pullback family hours earlier, still true for this lever. Nothing was lost because the result was negative on all three floors, but the SEQUENCING was wrong: runnable should precede gradeable, and the guard now makes that ordering visible.

NOT FIXED, deliberately. The only leg swept says the lever does not pay there (BL-20260818-XRP-PULLBACK-LEG-REJECTS-EVERY-DECISION-EXIT-LEVER: 3 floors, all honest negatives, zero Path B candidates), so building a live exit path for it is not justified by current evidence. Recorded in check_lever_wiring.LEVERS as an explicit `runnable_exempt` the guard PRINTS on every run, rather than dropping the lever from the table — a lever missing from that table is invisible to the guard, which is the failure mode the guard exists to prevent.
