items.title: EVERY hook in .claude/settings.json is inert on Claude Code on the web -- four SessionStart contract echoes, the board nudge, the merge-slot guard and the VM-lane guard all never run, so the repo's session-discipline enforcement layer does not exist where most sessions run
items.detail: Split out of BL-20260819-MERGE-SLOT-GUARD-DOES-NOT-FIRE, which is resolved for the merge guard specifically. The general finding is larger and has no fix inside this repo. Measured 2026-08-20: /tmp/claude-code.log carries 1,379 consecutive 'Hooks: Found 0 total hooks in registry' DEBUG lines spanning 2026-08-18T06:40:17Z to 2026-08-20T08:12:10Z with not one non-zero count, and /tmp holds no marker file written by any hook in .claude/settings.json across ~120 sessions. So the web runtime registers zero project hooks. WHAT THAT SILENTLY TURNS OFF: (a) the four SessionStart echoes -- the mandatory session-start contract, the Generation Discipline rules, the capability + coordination contract, and the shallow-clone history guard, each written on the stated assumption that 'Claude Code on the web injects stdout into the session-init context'; (b) the once-per-session board nudge; (c) the merge-slot guard; (d) the VM-lane guard on trainer-vm-heavy-request. Their CONTENT still reaches a web session only because CLAUDE.md and the canonical docs repeat most of it in prose -- which is why this went unnoticed for so long, and is not the same as the hook running. The shallow-clone guard is the sharpest loss: it exists precisely because a truncated clone returns a plausible-but-wrong history answer rather than failing loudly, and its whole design is fail-closed at session start. Inert, it fails open. WHY IT IS SEVERITY high DESPITE BEING UNFIXABLE HERE: three sessions across three days read their own successful merges as evidence the merge protocol had run. A control believed present and absent is worse than a known-absent one. Same class as 'Claude Code on the web does not honour project .mcp.json' (root CLAUDE.md, PM-side session capabilities), which is already documented -- the hooks half never was.
items.resolution_criteria: Not closeable by making hooks run; that is an Anthropic-side capability. Close when EITHER (a) a web session verifies a non-zero 'Found N total hooks in registry' line, i.e. the platform started honouring project hooks, and the four contracts are re-verified to actually fire; OR (b) each control that MATTERS has a mechanism that works in this runtime and the docs stop implying the hook provides it. For the merge slot the only shape that binds on the web is a required CI status check verifying a claim comment on issue #6927 for that PR -- operator-gated, since it changes the required-check set on every PR. For the shallow-clone guard, a cheap call to scripts/ops/git_history_check.py from the session-start doc read would restore it. Do NOT close this by noting that CLAUDE.md repeats the prose: prose that a session may skip is exactly what the hooks were added to backstop.
items.evidence: /tmp/claude-code.log 'Hooks: Found 0 total hooks in registry' x1379 (2026-08-18T06:40:17.452Z -> 2026-08-20T08:12:10.193Z, zero non-zero-count lines); ls /tmp -- no .claude-board-nudge-* and no .claude-merge-claim-* across ~120 session diag logs; .claude/settings.json hooks.SessionStart (4 entries) + hooks.PreToolUse (3 entries); tests/test_merge_slot_guard.py proves the guard's logic is sound, so absence of effect is absence of invocation; root CLAUDE.md 'No custom MCP servers' for the sibling platform limitation.

updates.note: RE-CONFIRMED BY THIS SESSION: I am a Claude Code on the web session and received NO SessionStart hook output — no contract echo, no board nudge. The mitigation works though: the SESSION BRIEF is inlined directly in CLAUDE.md, which I did read, and it is why I checked the coordination board and the open-items register. Keep open (the hooks are still inert) but note the inline-brief workaround is load-bearing and effective.

items.title: 62 of 79 label descriptions in bootstrap-labels.yml exceed the 100-char GitHub cap the file itself documents; harmless today only because the sync loop is get-then-skip, so deleting any one of them makes its recreation 422 and turns the bootstrap red
items.detail: Measured 2026-08-20 by parsing each {name,color,description} object individually. A first, naive attempt zipped names to descriptions positionally and was NOT trusted -- a misaligned zip produces exactly this kind of alarming list, so the per-entry parse is what settled it: 79 entries, 62 over. bootstrap-labels.yml warns TWICE that 'GitHub caps label descriptions at 100 chars (422 otherwise)' and then violates it in 62 entries; worst are trainer-vm-heavy-request (291), research-symbol-p0-request (261), trainer-offload-train-request (249), cutover-live (242). Nothing fails today because the loop is get-then-skip -- an existing label never reaches the create path where length is validated -- so all 62 were presumably created when shorter or by hand. THE LATENT FAULT IS THE ONE THIS FILE EXISTS TO PREVENT: lose any of those 62 and its re-bootstrap 422s, core.setFailed marks the run red, and that workflow's label-dispatch path is dead until someone shortens the string. Two entries near lines 140/145 were added for precisely that reason ('the workflow filtered on this label but it was never bootstrapped, so the label-dispatch path was dead'). Surfaced only because the new oci-inventory entry was length-checked before commit (94 chars).
items.resolution_criteria: Truncate the 62 over-cap descriptions to <=100 chars, moving the rationale into a YAML comment above each entry where length is unconstrained, and add an assertion inside the sync step that fails the run when any DECLARED description exceeds the cap -- so a violation surfaces at edit time rather than at some future recreation. Do NOT close by observing that the bootstrap currently passes: it passes because the labels already exist, which is the definition of a latent fault. Cheap positive control: create then delete a throwaway label with an over-cap description and confirm the run goes red before the fix and green after.

evidence.why_invisible: sync loop is get-then-skip; existing labels never reach the create path

updates.note: Re-validated: tooling/guard correctness. Unblocked and cheap; still undone. Harmless today; 62 of 79 over the documented cap.

items.title: analyze_exit_head._univariate_fdr scores features on the POOLED row set with no folds, purge, embargo or grouping — its q-values assume the row independence overlapping triple-barrier labels violate
items.detail: scripts/research/analyze_exit_head.py:270 calls _univariate_fdr(usable, feats, fdr_alpha) on the ENTIRE usable row set. That call sits BEFORE and OUTSIDE the fold loop: no folds, no purge, no embargo, no grouping by trade_id. The correct splitter _grouped_purged_folds lives in the SAME FILE at line 170 -- trades ordered by first decision_time, split into n_folds+1 contiguous blocks, train rows purged where label_t1 reaches within embargo_bars of the test block's min label_t0 -- and is used ONLY by the multivariate head immediately below. So the two halves of one analyzer disagree about whether the panel's rows are independent, and only the half with a printed q-value gets read as a per-feature verdict. WHY IT MATTERS: the panel is per-BAR with triple-barrier labels, so rows inside a trade overlap in time by construction and are strongly dependent; BH-FDR's analytic q-values are computed under an independence assumption that is false here, and they are anti-conservative in exactly the direction that manufactures 'informative' features. This is the function a reader naturally mistakes for E2 of the exit-mechanism process ('measure which inputs carry information') -- it is the leaky version of that test, and E2 was recorded as never-run while this sat in the codebase looking like it. checked: scripts/research/analyze_exit_head.py read directly at the call site, not inferred; _grouped_purged_folds confirmed present and correct in the same file. NOT a claim that the multivariate head is affected -- it correctly uses the splitter. NO live-order path touches this; it is a research analyzer.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) route _univariate_fdr through _grouped_purged_folds so its statistic is out-of-fold and purged, or (b) if the pooled form is deliberately kept as a cheap screen, rename it and stamp its output so a reader cannot mistake a pooled q-value for a validated per-feature verdict -- and have it emit the fact that it is pooled in the report it writes, not only in a docstring. Either way scripts/research/e2_feature_information.py (which imports the splitter and never calls this) is the reference for what the purged form looks like. Closable when analyze_exit_head's own report distinguishes the two, verified by reading the emitted JSON rather than the source comment.
items.evidence: scripts/research/analyze_exit_head.py:270 (call site, pooled) vs :170 (_grouped_purged_folds); docs/research/e2-feature-information-2026-08-20.md section 1.1; scripts/research/e2_feature_information.py self-tests no_leaky_univariate_called / no_leaky_univariate_imported / splitter_is_imported_not_copied.

updates.note: Re-validated: q-values from a pooled, unpurged, ungrouped scoring pass are not q-values. Invalidates feature-selection claims built on it.

items.title: 5 of 6 committed candle files are constant-price placeholders with 1 distinct close each, and nothing at the call site distinguishes them from a real series
items.detail: Measured 2026-08-20 over every committed candle file in the repo (n = 6, the full population, not a sample): data/ohlcv/btc_5m_2026.csv, eth_5m_2026.csv, qqq_15m_2026.csv, spy_15m_2026.csv and spy_5m_2026.csv each hold 300 rows with exactly 1 DISTINCT CLOSE (sd 0.000000); only data/backtest_candles.csv is real (5,000 rows, 4,873 distinct closes, BTC 1m, 2022-07-23 -> 2022-07-27). The five are deliberate -- 29014899 'feat(s006-m1): add ICT multi-symbol validate manifest and placeholder OHLCV data' -- so this is NOT a claim that they are wrong to exist. The finding is that the placeholder-ness is recorded only in a commit message from that sprint: the files carry no header marker, no sidecar, and scripts/candle_io.py::load_candles applies no check, so a harness pointed at one produces a confident, fully-green, entirely meaningless constant-price backtest with no signal that anything was off. WHY IT MATTERS: this is the same class as BL-20260813-HARNESS-SYMBOL-IS-A-LABEL-DATA-DEFAULTS-TO-BTC (kept_open), where --symbol is a display label while --data silently defaults to a fixture -- that row covers the wrong-file-by-default half; this covers the file-does-not-declare-itself half, and the two compose into a run that is mislabelled AND unfalsifiable from its own output. A zero-variance series also makes any correlation or rho undefined, so a peer feature built on one is not merely weak but ill-defined. checked: scripts/candle_io.py::load_candles read directly -- it has no variance or placeholder check; git log for data/ohlcv/ on a FULL clone (the session clone arrived shallow at 50 commits and was unshallowed to 3,469 first).
items.resolution_criteria: Make a placeholder declare itself where the consumer reads it, not where it was committed: either a marker the loader recognises (sidecar or header column) or a check in scripts/candle_io.py::load_candles that flags a zero-variance close column, whichever the owner prefers. The check must be shown to FIRE on one of the five files and to stay silent on data/backtest_candles.csv before this closes -- a guard demonstrated only on the negative case is not demonstrated.
items.evidence: measured over all 6 committed candle files 2026-08-20 (per-file row and distinct-close counts in docs/research/e2-feature-information-2026-08-20.md section 4); commit 29014899; scripts/candle_io.py::load_candles; related BL-20260813-HARNESS-SYMBOL-IS-A-LABEL-DATA-DEFAULTS-TO-BTC.

updates.note: Re-validated: 5 of 6 committed candle files are constant-price placeholders with nothing at the call site distinguishing them. A test that passes against a constant series proves nothing, and cannot be told from one that does.

items.title: ib_fill_to_row falls back to cumQty when shares is missing, which is the ORDER's running total, not this execution's size
items.detail: src/runtime/exchange_fills_ib.py::ib_fill_to_row does `qty = _f(execution.shares)` then `if qty is None: qty = _f(execution.cumQty)` (verified at lines 203-205). In the IBKR API `cumQty` is the cumulative quantity filled for the WHOLE ORDER up to and including this execution, not the quantity of this execution. So on a partially-filled order where `shares` is absent, the rows OVERSTATE and double-count: an order for 10 filling 4 then 6 stores 4 and 10, summing to 14. This store is the substrate for /api/bot/pnl/exchange and /api/bot/pnl/exchange/fills — the surfaces used precisely when the journal is not trusted — so an inflated qty corrupts FIFO lot pairing and the realized/unrealized split in the one place that is supposed to be exchange TRUTH. NOT YET OBSERVED IN LIVE DATA: whether ib_insync ever leaves `shares` None on a real execution is unmeasured, so this is a latent path, not a confirmed corruption. Establishing that is step one and it is cheap — the fills store can be queried for rows whose qty exceeds the order's own total. Surfaced by the llm-delegate burst worker (task bl5-ibfills-bugfind, issue #9944) pointed at a real backlog subsystem rather than its own source, and VERIFIED against the file by the grading session — the delegate's line citations were all wrong (a separate, now-fixed defect), so every location below was re-derived by grep.
items.resolution_criteria: First MEASURE: query runtime_state/exchange_fills.sqlite for IB rows sharing an order_id whose qty sums above any single row's qty, and state the count over its denominator — if zero, the path is latent and the row can be closed as such rather than silently. If non-zero, the fallback must be removed or replaced with a per-execution delta (cumQty minus the previous cumQty for that order_id), and a test must assert a two-partial-fill sequence stores 4 and 6, never 4 and 10.

updates.note: Re-validated: falling back to cumQty (the ORDER's running total) for THIS execution's size silently inflates fill quantities — and IB is now a broker-truth PnL reader, so this feeds measured PnL.

items.title: realizedPNL is guarded against IB's unset-double sentinel and commission on the very next line is not
items.detail: src/runtime/exchange_fills_ib.py guards `realized` with `if realized is not None and abs(realized) > 1e17: realized = None` (lines 217-218, carrying a comment that IB 'uses a sentinel for not applicable on realizedPNL in some builds'), and then reads `commission = _f(getattr(report, 'commission', None))` on line 219 with NO equivalent guard. Line 245 writes `fee: commission if commission is not None else 0.0`, so an unset-double commission (~1.798e308) lands in the typed `fee` column intact. The asymmetry is the finding: the same report object, the same sentinel risk, one field defended and its neighbour not. PREMISE NOT VERIFIABLE FROM THE REPO: whether IBKR actually emits the sentinel on `commission` is broker behaviour this repo holds no evidence on — the code's own comment establishes it does so for realizedPNL. Surfaced by the llm-delegate burst worker (task bl5-ibfills-bugfind, issue #9944) pointed at a real backlog subsystem rather than its own source, and VERIFIED against the file by the grading session — the delegate's line citations were all wrong (a separate, now-fixed defect), so every location below was re-derived by grep.
items.resolution_criteria: Either apply the same magnitude guard to `commission` (cheapest, and symmetric with the field beside it), or record explicitly why commission cannot carry the sentinel. A test should assert a report with commission=1.7976931348623157e+308 does not produce that value in `fee`. Also worth checking the fills store for any existing row with an absurd fee, which would settle the premise from data.

updates.note: Re-validated: realizedPNL guarded against IB's unset-double sentinel and commission on the very next line is not. One-line fix, same file.

items.title: order_id 0 is stored as NULL because the falsy-or chain cannot distinguish 0 from absent
items.detail: src/runtime/exchange_fills_ib.py lines 250-252: `str(getattr(execution, 'orderId', '') or '') or None`. Integer 0 is falsy, so `0 or ''` is `''` and the row stores `order_id: None`. Confirmed by direct evaluation, not inference: `str(0 or '') or None` returns None while `str(5 or '') or None` returns '5'. This is the collapsed-state shape on a smaller field — 'the execution had no order id' and 'the execution had order id 0' render identically. Low severity because order_id is metadata here (the docs already note a broker SL/TP exit fills under an order id the bot never sees, so attribution does not depend on it), but it is exactly the class that later reads as a missing denominator. Surfaced by the llm-delegate burst worker (task bl5-ibfills-bugfind, issue #9944) pointed at a real backlog subsystem rather than its own source, and VERIFIED against the file by the grading session — the delegate's line citations were all wrong (a separate, now-fixed defect), so every location below was re-derived by grep.
items.resolution_criteria: Use an is-None test rather than a falsy chain, so 0 stores as '0'. A test should assert orderId=0 round-trips to '0' and a genuinely absent orderId stores None — the two must stay distinguishable.

updates.note: Re-validated: a falsy-or chain that cannot distinguish 0 from absent. Textbook collapsed state, low blast radius.

items.title: An IB execution side outside BOT/SLD/BUY/SELL/B/S is dropped with no count, so a dropped fill is invisible
items.detail: src/runtime/exchange_fills_ib.py::ib_side_to_row_side (lines 92-105) maps only ('BOT','BUY','B') and ('SLD','SELL','S'); anything else returns None, and ib_fill_to_row line 208 then returns None for the whole row. The SKIP IS DELIBERATE and correct in intent — its docstring says a mis-signed fill would corrupt every downstream FIFO pairing, and guessing is worse. THE DEFECT IS THAT THE SKIP IS SILENT: nothing counts it, so a systematically-dropped side would present as a store that is simply smaller than reality, which is the unasserted-denominator class (an exchange-truth surface reading clean because rows never arrived). The delegate proposed 'SSHORT' as the concrete trigger; that is BROKER BEHAVIOUR THIS REPO CANNOT CONFIRM and it is recorded as the delegate's hypothesis, NOT as an established fact — IB documents BOT/SLD on Execution.side, and SSHORT appears on the ORDER side for equity short sales. The repo-side finding stands regardless of whether SSHORT is the trigger. Surfaced by the llm-delegate burst worker (task bl5-ibfills-bugfind, issue #9944) pointed at a real backlog subsystem rather than its own source, and VERIFIED against the file by the grading session — the delegate's line citations were all wrong (a separate, now-fixed defect), so every location below was re-derived by grep.
items.resolution_criteria: Count the skips rather than widening the mapping on a guess: have the caller tally rows dropped for an unrecognised side and surface the count (and the raw value) wherever the pull reports, so a non-zero count is a finding rather than an absence. Only then decide whether a specific side string needs mapping — and settle SSHORT from live data, not from the model's claim.

updates.note: Re-validated: a dropped fill with no count is invisible — silent-empty on the broker-truth ingest path.

items.title: The oci-inventory weekly cron was armed 2026-08-20 with its schedule path unexercised - RESOLVED the same day: the trigger fired for real, the job ran, and the verdict was clean
items.detail:
Shipped 2026-08-20 (M37): `.github/workflows/oci-inventory.yml` gained `schedule: - cron: "0 6 * * 1"` (Mondays 06:00 UTC), `github.event_name == 'schedule'` in the job gate, a bash-resolved `fail_on_drift` default that is ON for the schedule path only, `continue-on-error` on the run step so the verdict is classified rather than aborted, and a four-state classifier (`clean` / `drift` / `not_declared` / `could_not_check`) derived from the REPORT rather than the exit code.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY PROVEN before arming: `--fail-on-drift` is bidirectional against the real cloud - run 32351336623 went RED on an induced drift and run 32351503893 went GREEN when clean. That is the falsifier this milestone set itself, and it passed.

WHAT WAS NOT PROVEN: those were `workflow_dispatch` runs. The SCHEDULE path has never executed, so `github.event_name == 'schedule'` reaching the job, the fail_on_drift default resolving to true without an input, the Telegram step, the issue-alert step, and the auto-resolve-when-clean step are all untested in the shape they will actually run in. A cron that has never fired is not a check; it is an intention.

RESOLVED 2026-08-20T11:15Z. MEASURED, not inferred - run 32362843960, `event=schedule`, head 220a9d4:
  - the job `inventory` RAN (status in_progress -> completed), it was NOT `skipped`. So the disjunct `github.event_name == 'schedule'` in the job `if:` genuinely admits, and the weekly cron is not decorative.
  - Run inventory: success. Classify verdict: success.
  - Telegram alert: SKIPPED. Open/update drift issue: SKIPPED. Fail-the-run: SKIPPED.
  - Auto-resolve drift issue (only when clean): SUCCESS -> the verdict was `clean`.
That is the exact shape a healthy Monday run should have, and it is ALSO the first live exercise of the `EVENT_NAME = schedule` branch that defaults fail_on_drift ON - so the enforcing default is confirmed in production, not just in the extracted-block test.

HOW IT WAS EXERCISED: two one-off probe crons (`0 11 20 8 *` / `20 11 20 8 *`) merged in PR #10037 and removed the same day. Day-of-month + month scoped rather than day-of-week, so a delayed removal could at worst produce one stray run in August 2027, never a second weekly cron racing the real one. Two windows rather than one because GitHub does not guarantee a scheduled run fires promptly or at all - and that caution paid: the 11:00Z window fired at 11:14:30Z, **14.5 minutes late**. A single-window probe plus an impatient reader would have called that a dropped run and drawn the wrong conclusion.

⚠️ GITHUB SCHEDULING LAG IS NORMAL AND IS NOW ON RECORD (the reusable finding): a late scheduled run is not a missed one. Do not diagnose the Monday cron as broken because 06:00Z passed with no run - give it ~20 minutes before concluding anything, and read the run list filtered by `event=schedule` rather than eyeballing timestamps.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: one firing proves the trigger and the gate, not that the check will catch a real future drift - that half was proven separately and earlier (32351336623 RED on induced drift, 32351503893 GREEN when clean). The two together are what make the weekly cron a check rather than an intention.
items.why_it_matters: This workflow exists BECAUSE the inventory only told the truth when someone remembered to ask - the exact failure mode the schedule was added to fix. If the schedule path is silently broken (a gate that does not match, a default that resolves false, an alert step that never fires), the repo now believes it has a weekly topology check that in fact runs never, which is strictly worse than knowing it is manual: a green that cannot go red.
items.trigger_condition: On or after Monday 2026-08-24 06:00 UTC (the first scheduled firing), OR the next /health-review or /system-review run, whichever comes first.
items.what_to_check: 1) A run of `oci-inventory` exists with `event: schedule` - list runs and confirm the trigger, do not infer from the workflow file. 2) Its verdict step emitted a state, and that state is one of the four (a missing/empty `state` output means the classifier did not run). 3) If the cloud is genuinely unchanged the state must be `clean` and NOT `could_not_check` - `could_not_check` on a healthy cloud means the report was unreadable and the whole check is inert. 4) If the state was not `clean`, confirm the Telegram step and the issue-alert step actually produced their side effects, and that the run FAILED (the deliberate final-fail step). 5) If the state WAS clean, confirm the auto-resolve step closed any open alert issue rather than leaving a stale one. Record which of the five you verified and which you could not.
items.resolution_criteria: CLOSED. Required a REAL run with `event=schedule` whose job was not `skipped`; observed 2026-08-20T11:15Z (run 32362843960, verdict clean). The proof is recorded at the cron itself in .github/workflows/oci-inventory.yml so a future reader does not have to re-derive it or re-run the probe.
items.resolved_by: claude (llm-burst-2, 2026-08-20) - one-off probe crons, PR #10037 in / removal PR out

items.title: The LLM delegate's line-citation accuracy is 0/20 on the PRE-fix prompt and UNMEASURED after the fix - the numbering change is a hypothesis with a test behind it, not a measured improvement
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-20 over 20 findings the delegate produced on code this session did not write (`src/web/api/routers/strategies.py`, `src/runtime/exchange_fills_ib.py`): substantive findings 20/20 usable, line citations **0/20** correct. Every cited line number was fabricated.

ROOT CAUSE was OURS, not the model's: `scripts/llm/delegate.py::build_prompt` handed the file content with no line numbers at all, so the model had nothing to count from. Fixed by adding `number_lines()` and wrapping the content in it, with 6 tests including a positive control (`test_build_prompt_carries_the_true_number_for_a_deep_line`, a 220-line file) - removing the numbering fails 2 tests, verified by planting the defect back and restoring.

NOTE the pilot's prompt shape ('quote the exact expression') HID this defect: a grader checking the quoted expression finds it in the file and scores the finding correct without ever checking the number beside it.
items.why_it_matters: A confident fabricated line number is the expensive failure here - it sends the reader to the wrong place in a real file and, unlike a wrong claim, it looks like provenance. Shipping the fix without re-grading leaves the repo believing a number (0/20) that is now stale in the reassuring direction, which is the same class as quoting a stale go-live margin.
items.trigger_condition: The next session that runs the delegate on real code for any reason, OR 2026-08-27, whichever comes first. Do not schedule a run purely to close this row if a delegate run is already due.
items.what_to_check: Re-grade line citations on a fresh delegate run over code the grading session did NOT write, with the same denominator discipline as the first grading: report `correct / total cited`, keep it SEPARATE from the self-review numbers, and state the file set. Grade the NUMBER independently of the quoted expression - checking only the quote is what hid the defect the first time. Expectation to falsify: materially better than 0/20. If it is still near zero, the numbering was not the (only) cause and the finding is that the prompt shape, not the input format, is at fault.
items.resolution_criteria: Closed when a post-fix line-citation accuracy is recorded against a stated denominator and file set. A qualitative 'looks better' does not close it.

evidence.tests: tests/scripts/test_llm_delegate_scope.py (48 total, 6 added, incl. a positive control)

updates.note: Re-validated: 0/20 pre-fix and UNMEASURED after. The fix is unverified, which is this review's unexercised_fixes discipline applied to tooling.

items.title: The four src/runtime/exchange_fills_ib.py findings are CODE-verified only - none has been checked against the live exchange-fills store, so their real-world incidence is unknown
items.detail:
Filed 2026-08-20 from the delegate's first run on unfamiliar code. Each of the four was confirmed by READING the file - the code path exists and behaves as described. None was confirmed against DATA: nobody has asked the live `runtime_state/exchange_fills.sqlite` how many rows actually hit each path.

This is deliberately recorded as a limit rather than smoothed over: 'the code can do X' and 'the code does X on N of M live rows' are different claims, and only the second sizes the fix.

A finding with no incidence attached competes for attention on plausibility instead of on impact, which is how a real defect soaks inside a pile of theoretical ones (the dataset-audit alarm-fatigue failure mode).

Then re-rank: a finding at 0 of N observed rows is a latent-code note, not a bug to schedule. If a count cannot be obtained, say so explicitly rather than leaving the row implying it was checked.

items.title: The diag_fetch ordered-candidate fix is verified from exactly ONE session - the claim that matters ('a FRESH session's first diag_fetch succeeds with no override') has not been tested
items.detail:
Shipped + verified live 2026-08-20 (session llm-burst-2): with the stale `DIAG_BASE_URL=http://158.178.210.252:8001` still set, `scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh version` returned exit 0 with real JSON and 'served by https://ict-bot.duckdns.org'. That is one process, one network posture, one moment.

The resolution criterion the DIAG-BASE-URL rows actually asked for is a FRESH session succeeding without a manual override, and n=1 in the session that wrote the fix is the weakest possible position from which to declare it - it is verifying your own output, which is exactly where RULE ONE says the check is hardest.
items.why_it_matters: The defect this replaced was itself a self-heal that LOOKED fixed and was not, undetected for weeks because no session re-checked it from cold. Repeating the same one-session confidence on the replacement would repeat the mistake with better prose.
items.trigger_condition: The FIRST session after 2026-08-20 that needs live VM diag data for any reason. Do not open a session solely for this.
items.what_to_check: Run `scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh version` as the first diag action, with whatever DIAG_BASE_URL that session ships and NO manual override. Record: the exit code, the 'served by' line (which base actually answered), and whether the candidate list had to fall through. Also confirm the network posture is the default Trusted rather than Full/Custom - a success under a widened posture does not prove the Trusted-level claim, and the whole point is that no cloud-environment change is required.
items.resolution_criteria: Closed when a session OTHER than the one that wrote the fix records exit 0 plus the serving base, at the default network level, with no override. A second failure instead is the more valuable outcome and should reopen the parent row.

updates.note: RESOLVED-ADJACENT — I am the second session and it worked. diag_fetch.sh resolved the canonical HTTPS base on my FIRST call despite DIAG_BASE_URL still being set to the terminated micro (http://158.178.210.252:8001), printing `served by https://ict-bot.duckdns.org`, and every subsequent call succeeded. That is the 'a FRESH session's first call' claim this row says is unverified, now verified once more from an independent session. Keeping it open only because n=2 is still not a distribution.

items.title: The oci-inventory issue-label path has no way to request fail_on_drift - a session triggering it by label always gets a plain report, and nothing in the issue tells it so
items.detail:
Observed 2026-08-20 while arming the weekly cron. `.github/workflows/oci-inventory.yml` resolves the flag in bash: an explicit `inputs.fail_on_drift` wins, else `schedule` defaults it TRUE, else FALSE. `inputs` does not exist on the `issues` path, so a label-triggered run ALWAYS lands on the FALSE branch. The issue-label path was exercised for the first time this session (run 32351518408, event=issues, issue #10030) and that is what surfaced it.

The behaviour itself is defensible - the issue path is an on-demand READ ('tell me the current topology'), and the schedule is the enforcer. The gap is that the asymmetry is invisible from the trigger: nothing in the issue, the label, or the run output says 'this run could not have failed on drift'.
items.why_it_matters: A session that opens the issue expecting the drift check to bite gets a green run that was never able to go red - the exact 'a check that cannot fail' shape the whole M37 falsifier exists to prevent, one layer up. Low severity only because the schedule path DOES enforce weekly, so the blind window is bounded at 7 days rather than unbounded.
items.trigger_condition: The next session that edits `.github/workflows/oci-inventory.yml` for any reason, OR the next /health-review, OR 2026-09-01 - whichever comes first. Deliberately NOT fixed on 2026-08-20: the cron's first firing is 2026-08-24 and the highest-value property until then is that the schedule path is byte-identical to the one that was positive-controlled. Editing the same file first would trade a real guarantee for a convenience.
items.what_to_check: Two options, pick one and say which. (a) Parse a `fail_on_drift: true` line out of the issue BODY the way `system-actions.yml` parses `action:`/`reason:` (through env, never inline-interpolated), and fold it into the existing bash resolution so precedence stays in one place. (b) Leave the behaviour and make it VISIBLE instead - have the run's own issue comment state `fail_on_drift=false (issue path; this run could not fail on drift)`. Option (b) is cheaper and closes the actual harm; (a) is only worth it if a session genuinely wants an on-demand enforcing run, which no one has asked for yet. Whichever is chosen, the schedule path's default-ON behaviour must be re-confirmed by test after the edit.
items.resolution_criteria: Closed when a label-triggered run's own output states which flag it ran under, OR the issue body can set it. Not closed by documenting it in a comment nobody reads at trigger time.

updates.note: Re-validated: tooling/guard correctness. Unblocked and cheap; still undone.

items.title: FILED RETROACTIVELY 2026-08-20 — the prop pulse reported a closed ETHUSDT trade as still open because the open fill said 'buy' and the close said 'long'; the id was cited by 4 files and had never been filed
items.detail: This row is filed on 2026-08-20 for an id that has been CITED since 2026-07-08 and never existed. Measured on origin/main: BL-20260708-PROP-PULSE-DIRECTION-ALIAS appears in 4 files (including the src/prop/prop_monitor_pulse.py module docstring and _position_key's own docstring, which describe it as the reason the direction canonicalisation exists) and in 0 rows across docs/claude/*backlog*.json. THE UNDERLYING BUG IS GENUINELY FIXED: _DIRECTION_ALIASES collapses buy/b/bought -> long and sell/s/sold -> short in _position_key, so an open reported in broker vocabulary and a close reported in order-package vocabulary now share one key. The journal still carries the original evidence — prop_fills id 15 'ETHUSDT buy filled' beside id 16 'ETHUSDT long filled', 2026-07-05. WHY IT IS FILED ANYWAY, LATE: an unfiled id is worse than no id, because the code reads as tracked. This one is a measured instance of that cost, not a hypothetical: when the SAME class recurred on 2026-08-19 (an open fill admitted with direction NULL, keying apart from its own close — BL-20260820-PROP-FILL-DIRECTION-ADMISSION-GAP), there was no backlog row to find it under, so the recurrence was discovered by the operator noticing Telegram pulses for a trade they had closed rather than by a review reading the class. This is one of the ~109 pre-existing dangling refs (21% of all cited ids) that scripts/ops/check_backlog_refs.py measures and deliberately does not fail on, attributed to BL-20260730-CITED-BUT-UNFILED-BACKLOG-IDS; it is filed individually because the 2026-08-20 full-system audit cites it as the precedent for a live HIGH finding and a citation that resolves to nothing would carry that finding's history nowhere.
items.resolution_criteria: Already met for the alias half: _canonical_direction maps buy/sell to long/short and is covered by tests. Nothing further is asked of THIS row. The residual — that direction can be absent entirely, which the alias map does not address — is tracked separately in BL-20260820-PROP-FILL-DIRECTION-ADMISSION-GAP and must not be closed against this one.

items.title: prop_report.ingest_report admits a fill with no direction while _position_key requires one, so such a fill is permanently unclosable — a live SOLUSDT position has read open since 2026-08-19 and an undirected position can never fire an SL/TP alert
items.detail: Operator-reported 2026-08-20 ('long after I close a prop trade I'm still getting monitoring things on Telegram') and reproduced from the live journal over the FULL population of 32 prop_fills rows, not a sample. THE ROWS: id 30 breakout_1 SOLUSDT direction=NULL status=open qty 83.0 reported 2026-08-19T12:52:40, ticket prop-manual-5e30b930; ids 31 and 32 the same account/symbol/qty with direction='long' status='closed' at 2026-08-19T21:31:28 and 21:31:42. prop_monitor_pulse._position_key keys a position on (account_id, symbol, canonical_direction), so row 30 keys as 'akd:breakout_1|SOLUSDT|' (empty) while its own closes key as 'akd:breakout_1|SOLUSDT|long'. The newest fill under row 30's key is therefore still 'open' and find_open_prop_positions has reported a phantom-open 83-SOL position continuously since 2026-08-19. ROOT CAUSE — AN UNENFORCED CONTRACT BETWEEN TWO MODULES: src/prop/prop_report.py::ingest_report is the single chokepoint every report-back passes through, and it validates account_id (line 57) and symbol (line 86) while passing direction through unvalidated (line 106). _position_key requires all three. One module owns ADMISSION, another owns IDENTITY, and nothing asserts they cover the same fields. A fill admitted without a direction can never be closed, because any close carrying a direction keys elsewhere. THE SAFETY HALF, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN THE PING: find_open_prop_positions has four consumers and they read the malformed row three different ways. The pulse iterates all positions and pings hourly (the visible symptom). prop_sl_tp_alert.py:139 iterates them too and reaches _sl_crossed('') / _tp_crossed(''), whose direction dispatch falls through to 'return False' (lines 91-106) — so an undirected position CAN NEVER FIRE AN SL OR TP ALERT. On a phantom that is harmless; on a real position reported without a direction it is a silently dead stop-loss warning on an account whose static-DD floor is $4,700. breakout_executor._suppress_reason compares pos['direction'].lower() == d, so 'none' != 'long' and it does NOT suppress — the order path is unaffected (a hypothesis that the phantom was gating prop tickets was checked and REFUTED: the 2026-08-19T21:01 SOLUSDT suppressions are explained by ticket prop-manual-8eccec2028f3, emitted 20:57 with valid_until 21:57, via the outstanding_ticket:emitted branch). WHY THIS IS A CLASS AND NOT AN INCIDENT: the same shape has now occurred three times, each a different way operator-typed text can differ between the open and the close report — ticket_id mismatch (prop_fills 10 opens under prop-manual-SOLUSD-4, 11 closes under prop-manual-1014c5ab; worked around by dropping ticket_id from the key), direction alias (BL-20260708-PROP-PULSE-DIRECTION-ALIAS, fixed by normalising buy/sell), and now direction absent. Each was fixed per-instance. The class is that prop position state is INFERRED from the absence of a matching close row, so 'we have not been told it closed' and 'it is open' are the same state — the collapsed-state doctrine that CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md makes binding and collapsed-state-guard enforces on the live trader, never applied to the prop book. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'data_repaired_class_still_open' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
items.resolution_criteria: TWO HALVES. (1) DATA REPAIR — ✅ DONE 2026-08-20 via the `repair-prop-fill-direction` system-action (dry runs #10040/#10049 both failed writing NOTHING, dry run #10052 clean, apply #10053 `updated: 1`, backup /data/bot-data/trade_journal.db.bak-prop-fill-direction-1787227987). prop_fills id 30 now carries direction='long', corroborated two ways: the linked ticket prop-manual-5e30b93050b2 AND rows 31/32 (same account, symbol and qty) which both already read 'long'. VERIFIED against the DEPLOYED grouping logic, not by reasoning: importing prop_monitor_pulse._position_key and running it over the 32 live breakout_1 fills returns 3 keys / 0 OPEN, while a CONTROL that restores row 30's NULL direction returns 4 keys / 1 OPEN on the empty-direction key `akd:breakout_1|SOLUSDT|` — so the phantom reproduces on demand and the check is capable of failing. (2) THE CLASS — ⛔ STILL OPEN, and this is the half that matters. This is the FOURTH instance (see BL-20260708-PROP-PULSE-DIRECTION-ALIAS); each previous one got a per-instance fix. Closing it requires: (a) ONE module owning what identifies a prop position, read by BOTH prop_report.ingest_report (admission) and prop_monitor_pulse._position_key (identity), so a field cannot be required by one and optional to the other -- NOT a third hand-maintained list, which is how three lists come to disagree; (b) a guard or test that FAILS if admission and identity diverge, since the defect is invisible per-module and lives only at the seam; (c) an explicit reconciliation state so an unkeyable row is VISIBLE rather than silently phantom-open -- 'we admitted a row we cannot address' must be a state the system can report, not something an operator notices from a Telegram pulse. DEFERRED BY OPERATOR DIRECTION 2026-08-20 ('hold the main fix for after we finish the audit') -- deferred, not dropped.

items.title: scripts/ml/strategy_review_packet.py's execution_mode_mismatch override compared a point-in-time config field against a whole-window aggregate, so every correctly-demoted strategy was refused a grade by construction
items.detail: Found during the 2026-08-20 full-system audit (finding F-107 family). decide() opened with an early return: `if execution == "shadow" and headline.n_filled > 0: action='hold'; return decision` -- skipping the ENTIRE decision matrix. `execution` is read from config/strategies.yaml at render time (a point-in-time fact); `n_filled` is counted over the whole review window (an aggregate). A strategy demoted live->shadow mid-window therefore satisfies both terms as a matter of arithmetic, not as evidence of anything -- and that is exactly the population whose grade matters most, since a just-demoted leg is the one an operator is deciding whether to kill or restore. MEASURED over the 2026-06-30 packet set (runtime_logs/strategy_reviews/2026-06-30/), the full population of packets carrying the flag is TWO and they are opposite cases given the identical non-answer: vwap (322 closed, -$50.71, expectancy -0.157) and ict_scalp_5m (18 closed, 66.7% win, +$142.78, expectancy +7.93). Every metric was computed and then discarded by the early return. ict_scalp_5m's flag was a FALSE ALARM: config/strategy_changelog.json records live->shadow on 2026-06-29, the packet ran 06-30, and it returned to live on 2026-07-20 -- so a profitable leg was refused a grade because a completed demotion is indistinguishable, to an unscoped predicate, from a live pipeline anomaly. SECOND DEFECT, same site: the reason string asserted 'pipeline anomaly' unconditionally, including for fills that could not be dated at all -- a cause no code path had established (diagnostic-provenance sub-class A).
items.evidence: runtime_logs/strategy_reviews/2026-06-30/vwap.json and ict_scalp_5m.json (proposed_action='hold', reasons[0] the mismatch string, headline{} fully populated); config/strategy_changelog.json (ict_scalp_5m live->shadow 2026-06-29, shadow->live 2026-07-20); scripts/ml/strategy_review_packet.py::decide pre-fix early return. Control run at fix time: reverting only the script while keeping the new tests fails exactly the two behaviour-change tests (test_shadow_with_only_historical_fills_is_GRADED_not_refused, test_undatable_fills_hold_but_do_not_claim_an_anomaly) and passes 56.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED 2026-08-20 by classify_execution_mismatch(), which returns four never-collapsed states -- not_shadow / shadow_no_fills / shadow_filling_now (a fill inside MISMATCH_RECENCY_DAYS of the window end: the real anomaly, still holds) / shadow_fills_historical (a completed demotion: GRADED on the matrix, with a reason recording that the old override would have fired) / shadow_fill_recency_unknown (holds, but says 'we could not look' rather than asserting an anomaly). decide() takes window_end so recency is measured against the window the packet covers, never wall-clock at render time. Verified by 8 new tests in tests/test_strategy_review_gate.py including a control that reproduces the historical case. Re-opens if a future packet is observed refusing to grade a strategy whose newest fill predates its window end.

items.title: The doc-freshness SKILL's documented hand-greps return ~40 false positives where check_canonical_doc_coherence.py returns 0 - a session that runs them as instructed learns to ignore the output
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-20 while running the sweep as written. `.claude/skills/doc-freshness/SKILL.md` § 'Mechanical scans' offers two paths and calls them equivalent: run `python scripts/ci/check_canonical_doc_coherence.py`, 'or the raw greps it wraps, if you want to eyeball'. They are NOT equivalent.

Same working tree, same moment:
  - `check_canonical_doc_coherence.py` -> 5/5 PASS, zero findings.
  - The three documented `rg ... | rg -v -i '<filter>'` one-liners -> ~40 hits: historical sprint logs, audits, runbooks, the CI checker's OWN source line (`DEAD_IP = "158.178.210.252"`), and the doc-freshness SKILL quoting the gate names it is looking for.

Every one is a false positive. The cause is that the `rg -v` allow-list in the SKILL is a hand-written word list ('terminat|retir|histor|...') while the checker carries a real allowlist, so the greps cannot tell a historical mention from a live claim.
items.why_it_matters:
The SKILL says 'A non-empty result from any of these (after the allow-list filter) is drift to fix in this session, not to defer.' Followed literally that is ~40 items of nothing, every run. The predictable adaptation is to stop reading the output - which is the desensitized-alarm failure this repo names as its own P1 (`MB-20260719-DATASET-AUDIT-NOISE`: an audit degenerated to 62/86 alarming and a real dead-feature bug soaked for weeks inside the noise). A checker that cries wolf on every run trains the reader to walk past the one time it does not.

Note what this is NOT: the CI guard is fine and the sweep still works. The defect is in the DOCUMENTED MANUAL PROCEDURE, which is the half a session actually follows.
items.trigger_condition: The next session that runs /doc-freshness, OR the next /health-review, OR 2026-09-05 - whichever comes first. Zero urgency; it costs a few minutes of noise per sweep, not correctness.
items.what_to_check: Cheapest fix is to DELETE the raw greps from the SKILL and keep only `python scripts/ci/check_canonical_doc_coherence.py`, since the checker is the authority and the greps are a lossy paraphrase of it - two definitions of the same check are free to drift, and this one already has. If the eyeball path is worth keeping, give the checker a `--explain`/`--verbose` flag that PRINTS what it scanned and what it allow-listed, so a reader can audit the verdict without re-deriving it with a worse instrument. Do NOT just tighten the grep filters: that recreates the same drift one generation later.
items.resolution_criteria: Closed when running the sweep exactly as the SKILL documents produces no false positives - either because the greps are gone, or because the eyeball path is served by the checker itself.

self_referential_hits: the doc-freshness SKILL quoting the removed-gate names

updates.note: Re-validated: tooling/guard correctness. Unblocked and cheap; still undone. ~40 false positives vs 0 from the CI checker — a documented procedure worse than the tool beside it.

items.title: src/config/accounts_loader.load_accounts_dict returns {} for three different reasons and populates `errors` for only one, so 'we could not look' is indistinguishable from 'there are no accounts'
items.detail: Found 2026-08-20 while routing src/research/risk_basis.py through the canonical loader (the `canonical-config-loaders` guard correctly refused a hand-rolled parser). load_accounts_dict returns an empty dict in THREE distinct situations and only one of them is reported: (1) the file does not exist -> `return {}` at the `if not yaml_path.exists()` guard, with NOTHING appended to `errors`; (2) yaml parsing raises -> `{}` AND an entry appended to `errors` (the only observable case); (3) the top-level `accounts:` key is missing or is not a mapping -> `{}`, again with nothing appended. So a caller holding `({}, [])` cannot tell a MISSING config from a PRESENT-but-empty one, which is the collapsed-state defect CLAUDE.md § 'Collapsed states' names: *we did not look* and *we looked and found nothing* must be distinguishable. It matters most for the case the module docstring itself cites as its origin story — a consumer that silently saw zero accounts and produced zero recoveries against a real backlog (scripts/ops/backfill_orphan_pnl.py, 2026-05-16). The loader fixed the SHAPE bug that caused that and left the SILENCE. This is a real gap and NOT hypothetical for the new caller: risk_basis must report `unreadable` vs `account_absent` distinctly, so it works around the loader by checking `path.exists()` itself before calling in — a workaround that every future caller needing the distinction will have to re-invent, which is how a second parser gets born.
items.evidence: src/config/accounts_loader.py::load_accounts_dict — `if not yaml_path.exists(): return {}` (no errors append); `raw = data.get('accounts')` / `if not isinstance(raw, dict): return {}` (no errors append); only the `except Exception` branch appends. Verified by reading the function, not inferred: tests/test_risk_basis.py::test_an_unreadable_config_is_UNREADABLE_not_absent and ::test_a_garbled_config_is_UNREADABLE pin the distinction on the caller side and pass only because risk_basis adds its own existence check.
items.resolution_criteria: load_accounts_dict can express the three outcomes without the caller re-deriving them — e.g. it appends a typed entry to `errors` for the missing-file and non-mapping cases too (cheapest, fully back-compatible: every existing caller that passes no `errors` list is unaffected), or it grows a sibling returning an explicit state. Then risk_basis drops its `path.exists()` workaround and its two collapsed-state tests still pass. Closing this by making the states distinguishable ONLY inside risk_basis does not count — that is the second-parser outcome this row exists to prevent.

updates.note: Re-validated: {} for three different reasons with `errors` populated for only one. Collapsed state on the ACCOUNTS loader — the highest-consequence config path there is. Not in collapsed-state-guard's 19 contracts.

items.title: The trainer disk-low banner thresholds (2 GB alert / 5 GB warn) are CHOSEN, not calibrated -- one reading is not a distribution
items.detail: notifications.py::_trainer_disk_banner grades free space against _DISK_FREE_ALERT_GB=2.0 and _DISK_FREE_WARN_GB=5.0. Both are declared in the source as chosen rather than derived, because exactly ONE reading of this disk existed when they were written (2026-08-20: 45G/3.2G free/94%). Shipping a threshold with no distribution behind it is the exposure-ceiling mistake gross-exposure-governance-DESIGN.md sec 6 names: a bar set below normal operation silently alarms on correct work, and one set above the real failure point never fires. They are absolute GB rather than a percentage deliberately -- the operational question is whether the next dataset build can complete, which is a size, not a fraction of an arbitrary volume. CONSEQUENCE TO WATCH: at 3.2G free the warning fires from the first read and will keep firing until disk is freed. That is correct today (it is a true, unaddressed condition) but a banner that fires forever and is walked past becomes the desensitized alarm this repo calls a P1 in its own right -- so this item closes by EITHER calibrating the bar or resolving the disk pressure, never by muting it.
items.resolution_criteria: Accumulate the published free_gb series from /api/bot/ml/status across at least one full dataset-build cycle, then state (a) the observed minimum free space during a successful build and (b) the free space at which a build actually failed, if one does. Set warn ABOVE (a) and alert between (a) and (b). Quote the series length -- a threshold set from 3 samples is this same finding again. Alternatively close by recording that the disk pressure was resolved and re-deriving the bars against the new headroom.
items.evidence: src/web/api/routers/notifications.py (_DISK_FREE_ALERT_GB / _DISK_FREE_WARN_GB and their declaring comment); trainer-vm-diag #10057; docs/design/gross-exposure-governance-DESIGN.md sec 6-7

updates.note: Re-validated: 2 GB alert / 5 GB warn are CHOSEN, not calibrated, and today's 4.03 GB sits inside the warn band — so the banner is firing on an uncalibrated threshold. Same discipline gap as the gross-exposure ceiling, and unlike that one the soak has NOT been taken here.

items.title: scripts/ops/trainer_dataset_gc.py has NO CALLER anywhere -- but wiring it is NOT the disk fix, because it reclaims 0.09 GB against a 3.2 GB shortfall
items.detail: Confirmed on the trainer 2026-08-20 (#10057): no systemd timer invokes trainer_dataset_gc.py, it is not called from run_training_cycle.sh, and it appears 0 times across 7,442 training_cycle rows. It is a built-and-abandoned tool -- the exact class this audit exists to catch. BUT the measurement refutes the obvious remedy: a dry run scanned 115 version dirs, KEPT 111 (41 held by manifest pins, 76/76 manifests parsed), found 4 candidates, and would reclaim 0.09 GB. Against 3.2 GB free that is 2.8% of the shortfall. So wiring it on a nightly timer would produce a recurring '0.09 GB reclaimable' line while the disk keeps filling -- an alarm that reports motion while nothing moves, which is worse than no alarm. RECORD THIS EXPLICITLY so a future session does not re-derive 'the GC is unwired' and wire it as the fix. The real reclaimable mass is datasets-out/market_features at 9.9G, which is PINNED by manifests, so freeing it is a question about which pinned dataset versions are still needed -- a different decision, needing the manifest owner's input, not a GC schedule.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) wire the GC report-only and record in the same change that it is housekeeping and NOT the disk remedy, with the 0.09 GB figure stated so the next reader is not misled; OR (b) delete the script as dead, if the 4-candidate yield never justifies the surface. Separately and independently: decide what to do about the 41 manifest pins holding 111 version dirs -- that is where the 9.9G lives and it is a pinning-policy question, not a GC question.
items.evidence: trainer-vm-diag #10057 (gc dry-run summary: scanned 115, kept 111, candidates 4, reclaim_gb 0.09, manifest_pins 41, manifests_parsed 76/76; timer + cycle-log greps); scripts/ops/trainer_dataset_gc.py

items.title: claim-basis-guard scanned 6 fields that excluded `detail` and `evidence` -- the two richest prose fields these backlogs use -- so it reported a clean negative over 24.7% of claim-bearing rows it could not see
items.detail: Found 2026-08-20 when the guard FALSE-POSITIVED on a correct new row: the row stated 94% in `title` and its basis (ONE reading, n=1) in `detail`, and _row_text scanned ('title','description','source','action','resolution','resolution_criteria') -- no `detail`, no `evidence`. Measuring the exposure across all three backlogs (940 rows, the full population, not a sample): 198 rows carry a quantitative claim in a then-scanned field, and 65 MORE carry one ONLY in an unscanned field -- 65 of 263 claim-bearing rows = 24.7% the guard never examined at all. Of those 65, 16 have no parseable basis anywhere in that text either, i.e. they would have FAILED had the guard been able to read them; one of the 16 (BL-20260730-JSON-EXTRACT-GUARD-PROMOTE) cites $247,683.78, which is precisely the figure CLAUDE.md flags as an ALL-STATUS population number whose SIGN flips on the filter choice. Field usage in the health backlog: description 353 of 738 rows (47.8%, scanned), detail 226 (30.6%, NOT scanned), evidence 125 (16.9%, NOT scanned). BOTH error directions were live: false NEGATIVE where the claim hides in detail (guard sees no claim, passes silently -- the unasserted-denominator class, diagnostic-provenance sub-class C, on the guard itself), and false POSITIVE where the basis hides in detail (a correct row failed, which teaches sessions to duplicate prose into `description` to appease the guard -- worse than the gap). FIX: field list extracted to a single declared _ROW_TEXT_FIELDS tuple with detail/evidence/why_it_matters/summary/impact added. SAFE TO WIDEN because the guard is diff-scoped -- `if rid in base_ids: continue` -- so the 16 pre-existing rows are not retro-failed; only NEW rows are held to the standard. A test asserts that diff-scoping explicitly, because without it the widening would have turned every subsequent PR red on rows nobody in that PR wrote, and would have been reverted. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'fix_landed_needs_no_further_action' was collapsed to 'resolved' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.

Re-open only if a NEW prose field appears in these backlogs and repeats the pattern; the guard's own comment names the check (count rows using a field vs the tuple). items.title: the daily promotion-readiness sweep could not emit `promote` for ANY model, by construction — live_parity and labels_accruing starved on timer ordering, oos_edge is off because on it OOM-kills the trainer
items.detail: Measured live 2026-08-20 over 12 consecutive daily reports (the full retained set, 2026-08-09..2026-08-20, verified by ls). Every one reports `0 promote`, and every shadow-stage row in the hold list blocks on the SAME three required gates: oos_edge, live_parity, labels_accruing. `0 promote` was therefore not a verdict about 28 shadow models — it was a property of the sweep's own configuration, and the headline reads as the former. Unprovenanced diagnostic, sub-class C (an unasserted denominator: an empty result reading as a clean negative). BLOCKER 1 — TIMER ORDERING (fixed by this row's change). ml/promotion/gates.py:640-650 judges live_parity only over rows logged SINCE THE CURRENT ARTIFACT'S TRAINING RUN. The trainer's own clocks: the live->trainer pull of shadow_predictions.* completes 00:51; the training cycle ends 01:14 and re-trains every head, resetting artifact_at; this sweep grades at 04:22; the NEXT pull lands 05:04. So the sweep counted rows logged after 01:14 inside a log that ended at 00:51 — n_fresh_rows 0 by construction, daily, for reasons that are not about any model. labels_accruing starved on the same stale feedstock. THE KNOWLEDGE ALREADY EXISTED AND WAS APPLIED TO ONLY ONE OF TWO PATHS: scripts/ml/gate_check_candidates.sh (the HAND-RUN path) documents this exact trap in its own header, cites MB-20260721-FCPCV-V2-SOAK, and calls sync_trainer_data.sh before gating. run_promotion_readiness.sh (the SCHEDULED path) never got the same call, for 19 days. BLOCKER 2 — oos_edge, STILL OPEN. PROMOREADY_OOS_EDGE defaults off because on it OOM-kills the 6 GB trainer: ml/promotion/oos_edge.compute_oos_edge does rows = _load_jsonl(data_path), materializing a whole ~2.1e5-row market_features dataset as dicts for ONE head's k-fold CV, which alone exceeds MemoryMax=4500M. The 2026-07-26 subprocess-isolation fix was REVERTED 2026-07-27 (isolation bounds fleet accumulation, not one head's load); off is the known-good state. items.title: feat_bars_in_trade_frac is rank-identical to feat_bars_in_trade BY CONSTRUCTION, so every rank-based or tree-based analysis silently double-counts one feature
items.detail: src/research/intrabar_features.py:122 computes bars_in_trade_frac = n / expected_hold_bars, where expected_hold_bars is a CONSTANT for a given panel build (build_intrabar_exit_panel.py:214: expected = expected_hold_bars if expected_hold_bars else time_stop_bars). Division by a positive constant is rank-preserving, so under ANY rank-invariant method the two columns are the same feature. That covers Spearman (what scripts/research/e2_feature_information.py scores) AND gradient-boosted trees (split on order, not magnitude), i.e. essentially every method applied to this panel. MEASURED, n = 27 scored features on one real panel (XRPUSDT 15m, 973 rows from 48/48 trades, Binance 15m feed, time_stop_bars 12, expected_hold_bars 24): the two features returned statistic 0.1189399575806653 and p_empirical 0.054945054945054944 -- equal in full float repr, not merely to the 4 decimals a report renders. The E2 reference run (docs/research/e2-feature-information-2026-08-20.md) recorded them as 'identical to 16 s.f.' and treated that as an empirical coincidence to note; it is structural and holds at every horizon. COST, and it is not cosmetic: the FWER max-statistic threshold is calibrated over the family, so a duplicated column inflates the apparent number of independent tests and makes the family very slightly harder to clear, while a reader counting features overstates the panel's breadth by one. NOT a correctness bug in E2 -- the tool faithfully scores the columns it is handed.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) drop bars_in_trade_frac from the dense feature list and state in intrabar_features.py why the raw count is the one kept, or (b) redefine it against a per-trade-varying denominator (e.g. that trade's own realised hold, or a rolling expectation) so it is genuinely a different feature -- and, if (b), re-run E2 since the column then carries information the current one cannot. Whichever is chosen, add a test asserting the two columns are NOT rank-identical on a panel with >1 distinct bars_in_trade value, so the collapse cannot return silently.

items.title: E2's harness gate invalidates a run when the negative control clears the POINTWISE bar, which by construction misfires at alpha — 4 of 24 runs discarded in one sweep, ALL on one leg
items.detail: scripts/research/e2_feature_information.py sets neg_ok = not controls['negative']['informative_pointwise'], so a run is declared harness_invalid whenever the injected pure-noise control exceeds the POINTWISE threshold. That threshold is the alpha=0.05 quantile of the control's own null, so a correctly-behaving negative control clears it about 5% of the time BY DEFINITION -- the gate has a designed-in false-invalidation rate equal to alpha. MEASURED on the COMPLETED 2026-08-20 horizon sweep, n = 24 runs (2 symbols x 4 horizons x 3 targets, the full population, not a sample): 4 came back harness_invalid -- SOLUSDT h24 advantage_r, h48 advantage_r, h48 label_hold, h96 advantage_r -- every one with positive_control_fired=true and negative_control_stayed_silent=false. In the inspected case the negative control scored statistic 0.02171461183460063 at p_empirical 0.04095904095904096, just inside the pointwise bar, while far BELOW the FWER threshold 0.11265093781086809 that the run's actual DECISION uses. TWO THINGS MAKE THIS MORE THAN ALPHA NOISE, and an interim filing of this row at n=21 understated both -- it reported 3/21, P(X>=3)=0.075 and called that 'within range'. At the final count the rate is 4/24 = 16.7% against an expected 5%: P(X>=4 | binomial(24,0.05)) = 0.0298, i.e. BELOW the same alpha the gate itself uses. And ALL FOUR landed on SOLUSDT, none on XRPUSDT (P = 0.125 that four independent discards share a leg). Together those point at a SOL-panel-specific factor inflating the negative control's own statistic -- NOT at 5% bad luck. That factor is unidentified and is the first thing to look for. COST: the gate deletes runs at a rate uncorrelated with whether they were sound, and here it removed exactly the SOL h48 label_hold cell that the XRP leg's flip most needed replicated, leaving a hole at the decisive rung (the h96 rung did replicate, so the finding survived -- by luck, not by design). NOT a false result: no bad verdict was admitted and the FWER machinery was correct in all four.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED 2026-08-20, both questions answered separately as the row required, and the rule committed (d5251d1) BEFORE the re-run sweep was dispatched so the ordering is provable from history rather than asserted. (1) WHY IS IT SOL? -- NO DEFECT LARGE ENOUGH TO EXPLAIN IT, which is narrower than 'refuted' and is stated that way deliberately. THE MATCHED-HORIZON COMPARISON THE ROW ASKED FOR, both h48 panels, label_hold, 400 controls each: XRP clear-rate 0.0375 (mean p 0.5008, null sd 0.00687, cv_length 0.4256, binom p 0.901) vs SOL 0.0700 (mean p 0.4921, null sd 0.00655, cv_length 0.4503, binom p 0.048). SOL's control null IS ~5% narrower with a ~1.9x clear-rate, in the direction the block-length mechanism predicts -- but it is marginal (one cell, alpha 0.05, three targets examined, nowhere near the gate's 0.01) and the other two targets on the SAME SOL panel measure 0.0375 and 0.0475, so it is not a stable property of the leg and is far too small to produce four discards. New diagnostic scripts/research/e2_null_calibration.py pushes a BANK of independent noise columns through E2's IMPORTED fold/block/shuffle machinery (never a second copy). On panel_SOLUSDT_h48 (10,724 rows / 567 trades, reproducing the horizon arm's substrate exactly): pointwise clear-rate 0.040 against alpha 0.05, mean permutation p 0.517 and median 0.507 (a valid null gives 0.5), and a length-matched comparison null -- constructed to have no cycling or truncation to distort -- returns 0.045. The null on the SOL panel is calibrated under BOTH schemes. THE ACTUAL CAUSE: inject_controls seeds from the run seed and fills columns in panel row order, so the __ctrl_noise column is BYTE-IDENTICAL across all three targets of a panel (verified by direct comparison). The sweep had 8 independent control draws, not 24. Measured co-discard lift on a 400-column bank: 6.8x-14.0x, 1.59 cells per affected column. Re-doing the row's own arithmetic under that measured dependence: P(>=4 discards) = 0.086, NOT the 0.0298 quoted, and P(all on one leg | >=4) = 0.329, NOT 0.125. Both published numbers assumed an independence the runs do not have, and both flip the conclusion -- the pattern is unremarkable. (2) WHICH BAR? The gate now reads a RATE over a bank of K=64 noise columns: under a valid null the count is Binomial(K, alpha), and a run is refused only when the upper tail falls below gate_level=0.01. harness_state is four never-collapsed states -- valid / invalid_positive_control_dead / invalid_null_miscalibrated / unchecked (K=0: we did not look, and it deliberately does not fall back to a bank of one). legacy_pointwise_gate_would_invalidate is recorded per run so the re-run stays comparable without re-running the old code. MEASURED over 40 seeded sound null panels, as the row demanded the rate be a property of the tool: the legacy single-draw gate discards 2/40 = 5.0% (alpha, reproduced exactly); this gate discards 0/40; bank clear-rate 0.052 vs 0.05 expected. K=64 sized on a power curve (false-invalidation 0.0044; power 0.64 vs a 3x-inflated null, 0.92 vs 4x). THE FWER GATE THIS ROW PROPOSED WAS DESIGNED, MEASURED AND REJECTED: the null rate of an out-of-family column clearing the family-max bar is not a constant, so P(any of K clears) RISES with K and the rule gets more trigger-happy the more carefully you measure it -- 2/64 on the module's own 2-feature synthetic null panel against a clean 3/64 pointwise. Kept as the diagnostic n_cleared_fwer with no vote, and redundant anyway given a valid null. The FULL 24-cell sweep was re-run under the new rule rather than the four cells patched. Re-opens if a sweep is observed discarding cells at a rate the bank's own binomial tail does not explain. ⚠️ FORWARD NOTE, so this row is not read in isolation: the matched-horizon single-cell comparison quoted above (XRP 0.0375 vs SOL 0.0700 on label_hold h48) is REVERSED by the properly-powered per-leg pooling over the 24-cell re-run -- XRP 87/768 = 0.1133 (2.27x alpha, +8.0 sd) vs SOL 38/768 = 0.0495 (0.99x alpha). Any SINGLE-cell reading of this quantity is noise: the same panel and target swings 0.047-0.141 across six seeds. The per-leg figure is the one to quote, and the resulting defect is filed separately as BL-20260820-TRADE-BLOCK-NULL-IS-ANTICONSERVATIVE-ON-XRP.
