RESOLUTION EVIDENCE: docs/research/e2-gate-decision-and-sol-clustering-2026-08-20.md; scripts/research/e2_null_calibration.py (--selftest 12/12); scripts/research/e2_feature_information.py --selftest 42/42 (was 31/31); artifacts/research/nullcal_SOLUSDT_h48_*.json.

items.title: unwired-artifact-guard treats ANY string literal naming a script as wiring, so prose in a user-facing message silences it -- the THIRD time this checker has been defeated by documentation
items.detail: Found 2026-08-20 by the guard's own self-test, which caught the author red-handed the same day the guard shipped. scripts/ci/check_unwired_artifacts.py strips comments and docstrings before deciding whether a reference is in EXECUTABLE position -- its own _strip_noncode docstring records being defeated twice already (first by its own docstring citing trainer_dataset_gc.py, then by a comment in render_system_report.py citing the same tool), and concludes 'a reference only counts if it is in EXECUTABLE position'. But STRING LITERALS are not stripped, and a string literal is not executable position either when it is prose. Concretely: a banner message in src/web/api/routers/notifications.py contained the sentence 'Note the dataset GC (scripts/ops/trainer_dataset_gc.py) is NOT the remedy' -- a message explicitly saying the tool is NOT being used -- and that made the tool read as WIRED, flipping the guard's self-test from 8/8 to 7/8. Population: 1 of 8 self-test cases failed; the false negative was on the guard's single most-cited example. THE FIX APPLIED WAS TO THE PROSE, NOT THE GUARD (the path was removed from the banner text, which is better copy anyway), so the CLASS is still open -- the next session writing a user-facing string that names a script path will silence this guard again. NOT fixed by blanket-stripping string literals: a literal genuinely CAN be wiring (subprocess.run(['python','scripts/ops/foo.py'])), so stripping all strings would create the opposite defect -- a real runner read as absent -- which is strictly worse for a guard whose whole job is finding things nothing runs.
items.resolution_criteria: Narrow 'executable position' for string literals: a path inside a string counts as WIRING only when the enclosing statement also names a process-launching or dispatch construct (subprocess.*, os.system, shlex/shell invocation, a workflow `run:` step, an argv list), and counts as a MENTION otherwise. Must be shipped with a self-test case for BOTH directions -- a prose string naming a script must NOT silence the guard, AND a subprocess argv naming a script MUST still count as wired -- because a one-directional test would let the hardening create the false negative it is meant to prevent. Re-run the full self-test and state the count; 8/8 with two new cases means 10/10, and anything less means the hardening broke an existing case.
items.evidence: scripts/ci/check_unwired_artifacts.py::_strip_noncode (its docstring records the two prior recurrences); the failing self-test line 'FAIL known-unwired trainer_dataset_gc.py is flagged on the real repo' at 7/8; src/web/api/routers/notifications.py::_trainer_disk_banner (the prose that caused it, now de-pathed); PR #10059

updates.note: Re-validated: prose naming a script counts as wiring. I ran the guard this review and its output confirms the shape — the skill_invoked bucket explicitly warns that a skill NAMING a tool is not evidence it ran. Same 'cheaper to lie to than to satisfy' hazard as the presence-only markers.

items.title: Every E2 artifact scores label_hold against a 2.0R upper barrier while the live ict_scalp legs take profit at 1.5R and NO harness trade ever realises above it — the counterfactual being scored is one the fleet cannot execute
items.detail: The E2 reference run, the horizon arm, and every verdict licensed from them were measured with --tp-r 2.0. That flag sets the triple-barrier LABEL's upper bound only; the TRADE itself loads the live YAML (build_backtest_panel.py:163 cfg_overrides = H._load_yaml_params()), and config/strategies.yaml declares tp_at_r: 1.5 for ict_scalp_xrp_15m and ict_scalp_sol_15m (and for all eight ict_scalp legs). MEASURED over the full population of harness trades on both legs, not a sample: trade_realized_r caps at EXACTLY +1.500 on BOTH legs -- XRPUSDT 97/503 = 19.3% of trades, SOLUSDT 109/567 = 19.2% -- and floors at -1.000 (XRP 105/503 = 20.9%, SOL 141/567 = 24.9%); ZERO trades on either leg realise above +1.95R. So label_hold = 1[forward_r > upnl_r + cost_r] asks 'would holding to a 2R/-1R/time barrier beat exiting now' about a strategy that would itself have exited at 1.5R. The hold branch of the counterfactual runs a DIFFERENT EXIT POLICY from the one under study. WHY IT IS NOT MERELY ACADEMIC: the 2.0R bound is not just wrong, it is nearly unreachable -- only 4.2% (XRP, 21/503) and 4.8% (SOL, 27/567) of trades ever TOUCH 2.0R as maximum favourable excursion, against 19.7%/19.2% touching the live 1.5R. A barrier 95% of trades never reach almost never binds, so label_hold degenerates toward 'will this trade avoid the stop and drift up' rather than 'will it reach target' -- which is consistent with the measured barrier composition (P(hold) = 0.017 at sl, 0.995 at tp, 0.556 at the time stop). NOT an arithmetic error in E2, which faithfully labels the barrier it is handed, and no published verdict is thereby known to be wrong. It is a substrate/policy mismatch that no E2 write-up states, and it conditions every number in all three.
items.resolution_criteria: Re-run the E2 ladder with the label's upper barrier MATCHED to the leg's own tp_at_r (read from config/strategies.yaml, never hardcoded, so a leg whose target changes does not silently de-match), and report it BESIDE the tp_r=2.0 arm rather than replacing it -- the two answer different questions and the 2.0 arm is the comparable history. Do NOT fold this into the same run as any gate or feature change: it is a substrate change and confounding it with another would make both uninterpretable, which is the error the horizon arm's own expected_hold_bars pinning exists to avoid. Add an assertion (or a loud manifest field) in build_intrabar_exit_panel.py recording BOTH the label barrier and the leg's live tp_at_r, so a future mismatch is visible in the artifact instead of needing to be re-derived from two config files. Closes when an artifact states the pair and a matched-barrier arm exists.
items.evidence: config/strategies.yaml (ict_scalp_* tp_at_r: 1.5, all 8 legs); .github/workflows/research-e2-horizon-arm.yml input tp_r default '2.0'; scripts/research/build_backtest_panel.py:144 timeout_bars=24, :163 _load_yaml_params(); scripts/research/build_intrabar_exit_panel.py:196 tp_r: float = 2.0, :282 (label only); trade_realized_r distribution over 503 XRPUSDT / 567 SOLUSDT harness trades (max 1.500, 97 trades at +1.5R, 0 above +1.95R); MFE reachability table in docs/research/e3-barrier-geometry-2026-08-20.md.

updates.note: Re-validated: E2 scores against a 2.0R barrier while live ict_scalp takes profit at 1.5R. Every E2 label is measured against a policy production does not run — the disjoint-population class again, and this one invalidates a whole artifact family.

items.title: M20 has swept 8 families of post-entry exit override and the ladder rungs BENEATH a fixed take-profit, but the take-profit LEVEL itself has never been a swept dimension — on a fleet where E0 says a level fixed at entry decides 78.5% of exits
items.detail:
[status migration 2026-08-22] The original free-text status was `column_landed_19_of_43_legs_measured`, preserved verbatim here because it carries a real measurement (19 of 43 legs) that the enum cannot express. Migrated to `open` under the same rule used for the other 52 rows in #10119: a non-terminal qualifier FAILS TOWARD `open`, never toward resolved. The partial progress it records is unchanged and is not a closure.

docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json declares exactly eight lever columns -- trail_geometry, stale_stop, giveback_stop, exit_ladder, exit_head_ml, trail_decay, regime_flip_exit, vol_trail -- and every one is a POST-ENTRY OVERRIDE on a bracket fixed at entry. The matrix's tp_geometry field is a correctness qualifier on the substrate (was a verdict measured with the live TP clamp applied, BL-20260810-BACKTEST-DOES-NOT-MODEL-THE-LIVE-CAPPED-TP), NOT a sweep of the target level. The nearest thing to a target sweep, scripts/research/m27/ict_scalp_exit_sweep.py, takes tp_at_r as a FIXED INPUT and sweeps ladder rungs as fractions beneath it, explicitly skipping any rung >= tp_at_r ('never emit a no-op cell', :77). So the level is held constant in every sweep in the repo. MEASURED, full population, both legs, 5-year Binance 15m archive: the MFE distribution is p50 0.70R, p75 1.27R, p90 1.72R, p95 1.95R (XRP 503 trades; SOL 567 trades are within 0.04R at every quantile -- two independent legs agreeing). Against that, the live tp_at_r of 1.5R sits near the 80th percentile of maximum favourable excursion and is reached by 19.7%/19.2% of trades, while 62% reach 0.50R and 36%/34% reach 1.00R. On the stop side MAE is p50 0.50R, p75 0.87R/1.00R against a stop at 1.00R, i.e. about half of trades never use half the risk booked for them. Aggregate capture (sum realised R / sum MFE R) is 0.159 XRP / 0.140 SOL; capture over WINNERS ONLY is 0.603/0.627 (median 0.683/0.693), against the tier-B healthy band of 0.65-0.80 cited in the E-lit survey. STATE THE POPULATION: those four capture figures are four different denominators and they range 0.14 to 0.69 -- quoting one without naming it is meaningless. THE POINT IS NOT THAT 1.5R IS WRONG; it is that it has never been measured against an alternative, on a fleet whose own E0 census says a level fixed at entry decides 78.5% of exits. Twenty lever cells searched for an override on a bracket nobody had evaluated.  || 2026-08-20 UPDATE — THE SWEEP RAN AND THE MATRIX NOW CARRIES THE COLUMN, but the row is NOT closed because coverage is partial and I will not report 19 legs as 43. `docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json` gained `bracket_geometry` as a ninth column (a DIMENSION, not a ninth lever). Statuses over all 52 rows, DERIVED from the per-leg `runtime_logs/e35_bracket/<leg>/2026-08-20/report.json` gate blocks rather than from the prose: 13 `honest_negative` (gated, no cell cleared — the shipped triple stands on those legs BY MEASUREMENT), 2 `passed_unshipped` (eth_pullback_2h `tp2_sm3.5_to48` and eth_pullback_prop_2h `tp4_sm3_to48`, both Path A wf 6/6 effective with a clean dispersion band), 12 `pending`, 25 `blocked`. STATE THE POPULATION: 133 of 3,781 surface cells were carried into the gate (7 per leg: the per-axis + joint argmax), over 19 legs. WHY IT IS NOT CLOSED, three distinct reasons that must not be collapsed into one: (a) **24 legs are `blocked` for want of a FEED, not for want of a run** — the 2026-08-20 fetch pass sourced `data.binance.vision`, which is crypto-only, so every equity/ETF/futures leg (SPY/QQQ/GLD/TLT/MES/MGC/...) has no candle substrate on the free lane; nothing was measured there and it is not a negative. (b) **2 legs are `pending` because their gate-passing cell has NO DISPERSION BAND** (sol_pullback_2h/`to96`, trend_donchian_sol_4h/`to48`) — this row's own resolution criteria require the optimum to be reported WITH its band, and the one single-axis cell that WAS checked came back `split_sensitive`, so recording these as passes would be exactly the failure the criteria anticipate. (c) **1 leg is `blocked` on a REFUSAL** (squeeze_breakout_4h/`to24`): the cell passes the gate, `m20_split_dispersion` refused it on harness_agreement, and the root cause is `BL-20260820-SQUEEZE-MAXDD-IS-GROSS-WHILE-EVERY-SIBLING-IS-NET` — filed, not fixed. ⚠️ THE TWO `passed_unshipped` CELLS ARE NOT SHIP-READY AND THE MATRIX SAYS SO IN THE CELL: each is the argmax of 199 surface cells with the multiple-comparisons cost UNPRICED (no shuffled-label or random-cell control was run), and both sit on ETHUSDT 2h — n=2 legs on one symbol is not two independent confirmations. items.title: The only positive E3 lever cell breaks even at 0.02-0.05 R of extra cost per early exit, while the repo's OWN shared fee constant resolves to 0.08-0.16 R on this instrument — and the same arithmetic puts the leg's fee-free mean edge inside its own round-trip cost
items.detail: MEASURED on the E3 decision-time lever screen (scripts/research/e3_joint_lever_sweep.py), ict_scalp XRPUSDT 15m, 503 harness trades over the 5-year Binance archive, 4 anchored walk-forward folds. The single positive cell in the whole screen is a profit-banking lever (`bank0.75`, selected in 3 of 4 folds): OOS +5.467 R, positive in 4/4 folds against a fee-free baseline of +69.20 R. A break-even probe charging a per-firing penalty to the lever arm only puts the edge at +2.207 R at 0.02 R (3/4 folds) and NEGATIVE at 0.05 R (-2.683 R, 1/4 folds). So the lever tolerates roughly 0.02-0.05 R of extra cost per early exit. AGAINST THE REPO'S OWN NUMBER, NOT AN INVENTED ONE: src/runtime/execution_costs.py -- declared as 'the ONE shared execution-realism cost model' that both the harness and the live sizer consult -- sets DEFAULT_FEE_BPS_ROUNDTRIP = 7.5 and fee_r = (fee_bps/1e4) * avg_price / risk. Measured ATR(14)/close on the XRPUSDT 15m feed is a median 0.4592% (p25 0.3528%, p75 0.7009%, n=351 samples across 175,200 bars), so across R = 1.0x to 2.0x ATR the fee alone resolves to 0.163 / 0.126 / 0.109 / 0.082 R. EVERY value in that range is above the lever's break-even, so the conclusion does not depend on pinning R exactly -- and it is FEE-ONLY, before the slippage and perp-funding terms the same module models and defaults to zero. THE SECOND-ORDER OBSERVATION, WHICH IS THE REASON THIS IS FILED AS HIGH AND NOT AS A LEVER NEGATIVE: the same arithmetic applies to the BASELINE. The panel's trade_realized_r comes from the in-process run_backtest path, which the harness's own comment says the cost policy does not touch ('run_backtest never touches these ... the CLI main() applies the mandatory venue-aware policy'), so it is GROSS. The leg's fee-free mean is +0.1376 R/trade (XRP) and +0.1167 R (SOL). A round trip of 0.08-0.16 R is of the same order as that entire mean edge. If that holds, a fee-free R comparison -- the established M20 lever-gate basis -- is grading levers on a book whose own net profitability is unestablished, which would explain a great deal about why lever deltas of a few R have been so hard to interpret. THIS IS NOT ASSERTED AS A FINDING: R here is inferred from ATR rather than read from the harness's per-trade risk = abs(entry - sl), the fill side (maker vs taker) is not established, and the venue-aware resolver may return something other than the 7.5 bps default for this symbol. It is a flag with an arithmetic behind it, and it wants a direct measurement.
items.resolution_criteria: POPULATION BEHIND THIS ROW'S FIGURES: XRPUSDT 503 of 503 harness trades (SOLUSDT 567 of 567 for the baseline mean), ict_scalp 15m over the Binance public archive 2021-08-16 through 2026-08-19, 4 anchored walk-forward folds with every reported delta out-of-sample; the ATR(14)/close median of 0.4592% is over 351 samples drawn across 175,200 bars. TWO SEPARABLE PIECES, do not merge them. (1) THE LEVER: re-run the banking cell through m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py, where entries re-sequence and the shared cost model is applied, and record the verdict in the coverage matrix. The screen's own asymmetry says what to expect -- a screen that ignores the turnover an earlier exit creates flatters a banking lever, so a cell that is already marginal there should not survive. Closes on a matrix verdict either way. (2) THE BASELINE, which is the piece that matters: measure the per-trade round-trip cost in R DIRECTLY from the harness -- risk = abs(entry - sl) is computed per trade at scripts/backtest_ict_scalp.py:494, so the distribution of fee_r is exactly computable rather than inferred from ATR -- and report the leg's mean R gross AND net through execution_costs.roundtrip_cost_r, with slippage and funding included rather than defaulted to zero. State the population. If the net mean is at or below zero for any live leg, that is a finding about the FLEET and not about exits, and it routes to /performance-review, not here. Do NOT close this row by fixing only the lever half.

items.title: E2's trade-block shuffled-label null is anticonservative on the XRPUSDT panels — a pure-noise column clears its own alpha bar 2.27x too often (87 of 768 draws, +8.0 sd, p ~ 2e-12) while the SOLUSDT panels measure textbook — so every XRP E2 hit is inflated by an unknown amount
items.detail: Found by the negative-control BANK built to resolve BL-20260820-E2-NEGATIVE-CONTROL-GATED-POINTWISE-NOT-FWER, and it is a larger defect than the row that prompted it. MEASURED over the FULL 24-cell E2 re-run (2 legs x 4 horizons x 3 targets), 64 independent pure-noise columns per cell = 1,536 control draws, ict_scalp 15m on the Binance public archive 2021-08-16 through 2026-08-19 (XRPUSDT 9,761 rows / 503 of 503 trades; SOLUSDT 10,724 rows / 567 of 567). Under a VALID permutation null a noise column clears its own (1-alpha) pointwise bar with probability exactly alpha = 0.05, and its permutation p is Uniform(0,1) with mean 0.5. OBSERVED, per leg over 768 draws each: SOLUSDT 38/768 = 0.0495 (0.99x alpha, -0.1 sd, binomial p 0.55, mean permutation p 0.4956) -- textbook. XRPUSDT 87/768 = 0.1133 (2.27x alpha, +8.0 sd, binomial p 2.3e-12, mean permutation p 0.4707) -- decisively anticonservative. Pooled 125/1536 = 0.0814. THE ORIGINAL SUSPICION WAS EXACTLY BACKWARDS: the prompting row hypothesised that SOL's control null was too narrow; SOL is the clean leg and XRP is the broken one. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ADMISSIBILITY: a null whose draws are systematically small relative to the observed statistic lowers BOTH the pointwise bar and the max-statistic FWER threshold that the DECISION uses, so XRP's E2 hits on every target -- including the forward_r hits reported at every rung, and the label_hold flip the horizon arm built its headline on -- are inflated by an unknown amount. The corrected gate already refuses XRP h48 and h96 label_hold on this basis (9/64 and 11/64, binomial p 0.0044 and 0.00031), which withdraws the horizon arm's 'two independent legs' defence for that target and leaves the flip carried by SOL alone. MECHANISM NOT ESTABLISHED, and it must not be asserted: block_shuffled_labels cycles a donor block shorter than its recipient and truncates a longer one, so it is not a bijection on the label multiset when trade lengths differ (proved in e2_null_calibration --selftest, with its equal-length converse) -- a real structural candidate that predicts severity scaling with block-length inequality. But the measured cv_length runs the WRONG WAY (SOL 0.4503 > XRP 0.4256), so it cannot be the whole story and may be none of it. SELF-CHECK, because this result confirmed a prior guess and that is when one needs the hardest look. (a) REFUTED: a candidate artifact in which E2's observed path (_fold_stat) and null path (_prepare_fold_feature -> _corr_from_centered) compute differently -- measured over 48 (fold, column) cells on the XRP h48 panel, worst absolute difference 6.9e-18, so they agree. (b) SURVIVED WITH A LIMIT: all 64 columns in a run share the same 1,000 shuffled label sets, so their verdicts could be correlated and the Binomial(K, alpha) reference could be wrong. Re-running the SAME panel and target under six seeds gives counts 9, 6, 6, 5, 3, 9 of 64 -- observed sd 2.34 against a binomial sd at the observed rate of 2.39, so there is NO material overdispersion, and the mean rate 0.0990 = 1.98x alpha replicates the leg-level defect across six independent seeds. BUT the gate fired on only 2 of those 6, so the PER-CELL verdict 'XRP h48/h96 label_hold are inadmissible' is NOT stable -- it is a coin flip at this effect size, consistent with the 0.19 power at K=64 against a 2x null that the gate's own pre-shipped power curve predicted. The reliable claim is the LEG-LEVEL one (87/768, p ~ 2e-12); the two per-cell firings are a noisy manifestation of it and are not independent evidence about those cells.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) ISOLATE THE MECHANISM BEFORE FIXING ANYTHING. e2_null_calibration.py already ships a length_matched comparison scheme with no cycling or truncation to distort; run BOTH schemes on the XRP panels and report the rates side by side. If length_matched returns ~alpha on XRP the cycling distortion IS the cause despite the cv_length ordering; if it is equally hot, the cause is elsewhere and the next candidates are the fold construction and the label's own within-trade autocorrelation structure. Either answer is publishable; guessing is not. (2) THEN FIX THE NULL, not the threshold -- raising a bar to compensate for a miscalibrated null hides the defect and leaves every historical verdict uncomparable. (3) RE-GRADE THE XRP HISTORY. Every E2 verdict on an XRP panel (the reference run, the horizon arm, and this re-run) was measured against this null; state which of them survive a corrected one rather than leaving readers to assume they all do. The SOL cells are unaffected and are the comparison arm. (4) Add the per-leg bank rate to the E2 report itself so a future run cannot produce a verdict without its own null-calibration reading beside it -- the same 'read the coverage beside the number' discipline pnlCoverage and rCoverage already carry. Closes when a corrected null measures within alpha on BOTH legs and the affected verdicts are re-stated.
items.evidence: artifacts/research/e2new_{XRPUSDT,SOLUSDT}_h{12,24,48,96}_{forward_r,advantage_r,label_hold}.json (controls.negative_bank per cell, 24 cells x 64 columns); artifacts/research/nullcal_{XRPUSDT,SOLUSDT}_h48_label_hold.json (matched-horizon comparison, 400 controls each: XRP 0.0375 vs SOL 0.0700 on label_hold alone -- note this SINGLE-CELL read points the OTHER way and is why the 768-draw per-leg pooling is the one to trust); scripts/research/e2_null_calibration.py; scripts/research/e2_feature_information.py (block_shuffled_labels); docs/research/e2-gate-decision-and-sol-clustering-2026-08-20.md sec 3.6.

items.title: 30 of 48 live strategy legs declare NO exit lever at all, and the declared surface fires 13 times in 1,142 closed trades — so 'no lever beats holding' is partly a statement about a mechanism that has barely been allowed to act
items.detail: Operator observation 2026-08-20 ('there is some active management on the SL side, but it seems not active enough'), measured rather than left as an impression. POPULATION: all 48 legs in config/strategies.yaml resolving to execution: live, graded against scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py::LEVER_DECLARED_KEYS (the sweep's own definition of what constitutes a declared exit lever, so this cannot drift from what the sweep grades). RESULT: 18 of 48 legs arm at least one lever; 30 (62.5%) arm none. By family: trail_decay 16, stale_stop 3, giveback_stop 1, vol_trail ZERO -- a declared family with no live consumer at all. Beside that, docs/design/m31-p5-telemetry-reading-lever-PROPOSAL.md section 2 records 13 lever firings LIFETIME (stale_stop 10, exit_head 2, giveback_stop 1, that one on paper) against 1,142 closed trades = 1.1%. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE M20 PROGRAMME'S OWN CONCLUSIONS: the repeated finding is 'no lever beats holding'. On the legs that arm nothing, that is not a measurement of a lever -- there is no lever. And at 13 lifetime firings the LIVE journal cannot grade an exit lever at all, which the P5 doc already states in terms. So the fleet's exit evidence is thinner than the number of honest_negative cells in the coverage matrix suggests: those cells are backtest verdicts, and the live arm is close to empty. ⚠️ WHAT THESE FIGURES DO NOT COUNT, stated so they are not over-read: the monitor's own break-even stop-trail is applied in the live monitor and modelled in the harness as --sim-breakeven (m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py notes it is part of the config-exact base), and it is NOT a declared YAML lever. So both numbers bound the DECLARED lever surface, not all stop movement -- there is baseline SL management on legs that appear here as arming nothing. This row is about the declared, swept, gradeable surface.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) Establish the DENOMINATOR honestly before proposing any widening: for each of the 30 legs arming nothing, record whether that is a deliberate verdict (the coverage matrix already carries an honest_negative for its family) or simply never asked. Those are different states and the matrix should be able to say which -- a leg nobody swept is not a leg where levers were found not to work. (2) Report the per-family live firing count beside every coverage-matrix verdict, so a cell can never read as graded-live when the lever has never fired; this is the same 'read the coverage beside the number' discipline pnlCoverage and rCoverage already carry. (3) vol_trail having ZERO live consumers is its own question -- either it is a family worth arming somewhere or it should be retired from LEVER_DECLARED_KEYS rather than left as a declared family that nothing uses. Any actual arming of a lever on a live leg is TIER-3 and is not part of closing this row; the row closes on the measurement and the reporting change.
items.evidence: config/strategies.yaml (48 execution: live legs, read 2026-08-20); scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py::LEVER_DECLARED_KEYS and the --sim-breakeven note in its config-exact base; docs/design/m31-p5-telemetry-reading-lever-PROPOSAL.md section 2 (13 firings / 1,142 closed trades); docs/design/exit-mechanism-construction-PROCESS.md section E3.5.

This window's real-money perExitPath shows the levers firing at all — exit_head 5, time_decay 4, stale_stop 3 = 12 fires — which is the same order of magnitude. The levers work; almost nothing declares them.

items.title: backtest_system._risk_qty sizes CONTINUOUSLY, so no risk-sweep arm can answer whether production would have REFUSED the trade — and the error is flattering
items.detail: Found while wiring `--risk-pct grid` (the consumer risk_grid_percent() shipped without). POPULATION: scripts/backtest_system.py::_risk_qty, the single sizing function every arm of the system/portfolio harness routes through. It returns `(bal * (rpct/100.0)) / stop_dist` as a bare float: no whole-contract floor, no min_qty, no margin pre-flight cap. PRODUCTION QUANTIZES AND REFUSES: RiskManager.position_size sizes `market_type: futures` accounts in WHOLE CONTRACTS and makes a sub-1-contract order a per-trade refusal (CLAUDE.md, IB_PLACE_CONFIRM_S row, BL-20260611-001), and src/units/accounts/risk.py::WHOLE_UNIT_QTY_EXCHANGES floors Alpaca to whole shares via the `whole_units` flag position_size resolves from the account's exchange. (CLAUDE.md cites a backlog id for that Alpaca half which resolves to NO filed row — checked against all 951 ids across the three backlogs — so the code path is cited here instead of the id.) So below some per-symbol threshold a real trade does not shrink — it does not happen — while the harness books it at a fractional size. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE SWEEP: it is the standing rebuttal to 'it is R-normalized so risk does not matter'. That claim assumes the trade SET is invariant to risk_pct; quantization makes the set itself a function of risk_pct, so the harness cannot test its own independence premise. And the bias has a SIGN: a low-risk arm reads as safe and clean precisely where the leg would not have traded, so the error flatters small risk. This is live-relevant, not academic — every default harness invocation sits at 0.3%, one fifth of live 1.5% (see the risk-basis-agreement KNOWN_DIVERGENCES register), which is the region where refusal bites hardest. NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately: modelling refusal changes backtest RESULTS, so it would silently re-base every historical comparison in the repo. The grid table states the limitation in its own output (scripts/backtest_system.py::_fmt_risk_grid) so a reader cannot miss it, which is the honest interim.
items.evidence: MEASURED 2026-08-20, n=3 arms, over the sample window 2022-07-23 to 2022-07-27 (data/backtest_candles.csv, the harness default). scripts/backtest_system.py::_risk_qty (returns a float, no floor/min_qty/cap) vs src/units/accounts/risk.py::position_size (whole_units + futures whole-contract refusal). Grid run 2026-08-20 on data/backtest_candles.csv: arms 0.75%/1.5%/3.0% returned net pnl -91.57 / -183.14 / -366.28 and ret/DD -0.94 at every arm — exactly linear, i.e. the harness treats risk as a pure multiplier with no threshold behaviour of any kind.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) _risk_qty applies the same quantization production applies — resolved from the account's exchange via the existing risk.requires_whole_unit_qty / futures whole-contract rule, never a second copy of it — and a refused order is COUNTED and reported per arm (a silent drop would be a worse defect than the current one), with the re-based historical comparison acknowledged; OR (b) a measurement establishes the refusal rate is negligible at the arms actually used, stated with its population, and this row is closed citing it. Removing the caveat from _fmt_risk_grid without doing one of those does NOT close this row.

updates.note: Re-validated and it has a LIVE analogue: production DOES refuse on quantization/venue caps (17 'contracts exceeds maximum limit' rejections in 9 days; ict_scalp_avax_5m sized above the venue max 20 times per BL-20260821). The harness sizes continuously and can never see that.

items.title: prop-report strips a ```json fence but then requires the WHOLE body to be JSON — so a fenced block plus any prose fails before SSH
items.detail:
`.github/workflows/prop-report.yml` strips an optional ```json fence and then requires the ENTIRE remaining body to satisfy `jq -e 'type=="object"'`. That is exactly what the docs say, and it is still a trap: offering a FENCE strongly implies the fence delimits the payload and the rest of the body is prose — which is how every other fenced-block convention in this repo reads. A report issue carrying the correct JSON in a correct fence, plus a rationale paragraph below it, fails at validation BEFORE SSH runs, and the operator-facing failure comment lists five plausible causes (bad JSON, unset VM_SSH_KEY, host unreachable, web-api down, 401) without saying which one fired. The one that fired is knowable — validation ran and rejected the body — so this is also a small diagnostic-provenance sub-class-A instance: the message names causes no code path tested on this run.

Two independent small fixes, either sufficient:
(a) extract the FIRST fenced json block when one is present, rather than requiring the whole body to parse. Strictly more precise, not more permissive — a body with no fence keeps today's whole-body behaviour.
(b) have the failure comment name the STAGE that failed (validation vs SSH vs HTTP) instead of listing every cause, the same fix shape as the diag_fetch unprovenanced failure message.

NOTE this touches the workflow that POSTs to a live Tier-2 write endpoint, so the change wants a planted-control test (a fenced-plus-prose body must be accepted and must send exactly the fenced object; a body with two fenced objects must be refused, never silently first-wins).
items.evidence: Issue #10072 (2026-08-20T18:47Z): body = a correct single-object ```json fence followed by a rationale paragraph. Workflow closed it in 9s with 'HTTP status: (not reached)' and '(no post-output.txt — failure happened before/at validation, before SSH ran)'. Retried as #10073 with a JSON-only body: succeeded, and the live effect was verified on /api/bot/prop/status?account_id=breakout_1 — distance_to_dd_floor_usd 283.00 -> 282.86, status_freshness ok, age 0.006h. So the payload was always valid; only the surrounding prose was fatal. Parser: prop-report.yml lines ~157-171.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) a prop-report issue whose body is a fenced JSON object followed by prose is accepted and posts exactly the fenced object, proven by a test that also refuses a two-fence body rather than silently taking the first; or (b) the failure comment names the failing stage, proven by a test asserting a validation failure does not mention SSH/HTTP causes. Closing this by only editing the docs is NOT sufficient — the docs are already accurate and the trap survived them.

updates.note: Re-validated: duplicate condition with BL-20260818-PROP-REPORT-RELAY-REJECTS-A-BODY-WITH-ANY-PROSE. Consolidate the two.

items.title: Appending a backlog row with the obvious json.dumps() idiom reformats 2,484 lines and makes impossibility-claim-guard attribute 4 PRE-EXISTING rows to your PR
items.detail:
Two coupled problems, one root: the three review backlogs are the ONLY files a session is REQUIRED to edit at session end (CLAUDE.md § 'Every session'), and editing them is booby-trapped.

(1) THE APPEND TRAP. These files are stored with `ensure_ascii=False` — real em-dashes on disk. Python's `json.dumps` defaults to `ensure_ascii=True`, so the obvious read-append-write idiom escapes every non-ASCII character and rewrites every line containing one. Measured: a ONE-ROW append produced `2496 insertions(+), 2484 deletions(-)`. Nothing warns; the file stays valid JSON and the row is correctly added.

(2) THE RE-ATTRIBUTION. `impossibility-claim-guard` is diff-scoped (added-vs-origin/main), which is right. But once (1) marks 2,484 existing lines as added, the guard scans rows written months ago and fails the PR for FOUR claims the author never wrote — at health-review-backlog.json lines 8316, 8409, 8439, 9696. The failure names the guard but not the mechanism, so the author's natural reading is 'my row tripped it', and the natural fix attempt is to reword their own row, which cannot work.

(3) THE PART THAT OUTLIVES THE FIX. Those four rows are genuinely missing their `checked: <path>` annotation and CI has never once seen them, because the guard only looks at changed lines and nobody changes those lines. So the guard is structurally blind to the standing contents of the very file it polices — it can only ever police rows being written now. Fixing (1) makes the false failure go away and leaves this blind spot exactly as it was, which is why it is written down separately here rather than treated as fallout.
items.evidence: PR #10074, head 31c2eb16: `guards` FAILED with `impossibility-claim-guard: 243 file(s) scanned, 4 unsubstantiated claim(s)` on a PR whose only intended content was one backlog row. Reproduced locally, then isolated by control: re-serialising with `ensure_ascii=False` cut the diff to `12 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)` and the same guard returned `0 unsubstantiated claim(s)` — same row text, same guard, same base. So the 4 findings were attributable to the SERIALISATION, not to the content. The four flagged rows are unchanged on main and predate this PR.
items.resolution_criteria:
(a) A helper both the session-end routine and any tooling append through — e.g. `scripts/ops/backlog_append.py` — that round-trips the untouched file and REFUSES to write when its own serialisation does not reproduce the original byte-for-byte (the assertion used to fix this PR). Proven by a test that plants an ensure_ascii=True write and asserts the helper refuses it. Documenting 'remember ensure_ascii=False' is NOT sufficient — this file already documents plenty that sessions miss.
(b) SEPARATELY: a standing (not diff-scoped) sweep over the three backlogs, so a row already committed without `checked: <path>` is reported once rather than lying dormant until someone's unrelated PR reformats the file. The 4 named rows are the seed population; closing (b) means they are annotated or deliberately exempted, with the count asserted so a future silent regrowth is visible.

updates.note: RE-VALIDATED AND ACTIVELY RELIED ON TODAY. I wrote to all three backlogs this session and used exactly the protection this row produced: backlog_append.detect_format to round-trip byte-for-byte, plus a no-op write verified git-clean BEFORE editing. It held — 2,484 lines were not reformatted and nothing was re-attributed. The row stays open because the protection is a convention available to callers, not enforced on them.

items.title: IB protection coverage is graded on QUANTITY and SIDE but never on PRICE, so a position whose stop sits 69 ticks from its declared level grades FULLY COVERED -- live MES is $1,289.73 mis-protected right now
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-20T20:23:39Z, /api/diag/ib_open_orders read_state 'orders_read' (a confirmed clean account-wide read) joined to /api/bot/positions?include_paper=true.

THE CLASS. IBClient.protection_coverage has been corrected twice, each time on a different axis of the same question: BL-20260814-IB-PROTECTION-BOOLEAN-NOT-QUANTITY turned a boolean into a quantity, and BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED split one membership test into two sides. It is still blind to a THIRD axis -- price. The verdict it returns is {size, covered_qty, stop_qty, target_qty, legs, unknown_qty_legs, oca_groups, source}: there is no price in it, and no consumer supplies one.

MEASURED ABSENCE, with a working probe: `auxPrice` appears in src/ EXACTLY ONCE, at src/units/accounts/ib_client.py:2715 inside list_open_orders -- the read surface that merely dumps rows, with no decision path reading it. `aux_price` and `lmt_price` appear in scripts/ ZERO times. The probe is valid: the same grep shape returns a positive for the field it looks for. So nothing anywhere compares a resting protective leg's PRICE to the level the strategy declared in trades.stop_loss / trades.take_profit_1.

THE LIVE INSTANCE. ib_paper MES trade 4350, 15 long: journal-declared stop_loss 7533.696429; the ONLY resting stop is order 338 at 7516.50 (oca-protect-336). That is 17.196429 points = 69 MES ticks = $1,289.73 on 15 contracts at the config-declared contract_value_usd of 5.0. The position graded FULLY STOP-COVERED throughout -- stop_qty 15 against a size of 15, correct side -- because the quantity was right and the side was right, and only the price was wrong.

NOT A ROUNDING ARTIFACT, and that is asserted rather than assumed: in the SAME read MGC declares 4371.1469 and rests at 4371.1 (inside one 0.10 tick) and MHG declares 6.221714 / 7.141302 and rests at 6.2215 / 7.1415 (inside one 0.0005 tick). Two of three match; MES is the outlier by 69 ticks.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS INSTANCE: 'covered' is the word the naked sweep, the re-arm decision and every operator-facing coverage read are built on, and it currently means 'a leg of the right side and quantity exists', not 'the protection the strategy chose is what the venue will execute'. Every instance today is on ib_paper, but the grading code is account-agnostic. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'detector_built_unwired_pending_merge' was collapsed to 'open' so the open set is countable. The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
resolution_criteria: MET 2026-08-23. A detector that compares each resting protective leg's price to the journal-declared level, tolerant of one tick (the venue snapping a fractional declared level onto its grid is correct behaviour and must not be reported). SHIPPED and MERGED as scripts/ops/broker_bracket_reconcile.py (#10076, commit 2be01dea). --self-test 19/19.

MET 2026-08-23 -- THE DISCRIMINATING RUN WAS EXECUTED. The detector must PASS a correctly-bracketed position and FLAG a diverging one in the same run -- MHG is the discriminating control; one that flags all three live positions is as broken as one that flags none. EVIDENCE: run against live payloads (/api/diag/ib_open_orders + /api/bot/positions?include_paper=true, captured 07:36Z). MHG trade 4796 (29 long, stop 29 / target 29) graded CLEAN -- the control passes. MGC trade 4773 flagged 1 (target_naked_declared). MES trade 4350 flagged 2: target_naked_declared AND stop_price_diverges -- 'declares stop 7533.696429 but the nearest resting stop is 7516.500000 -- 69 ticks (17.196429) away', which reproduces an independent hand calculation from the same two sources exactly. 3 findings over 3 positions, not 0 and not 3-of-3. ib_live graded COULD NOT LOOK and was explicitly NOT counted as clean.

MET 2026-08-23. WIRE IT TO A CALLER. As shipped, broker_bracket_reconcile.py runs only when a session remembers to run it -- which is the same defect as a written-and-never-read provenance field, the shape provenance-consumer-guard exists for, and it would be incoherent to ship it that way in the same session that re-confirmed BL-20260818-IB-BROKER-PNL-READER-HAS-NO-CALLER. It needs either a scheduled workflow reading the diag surfaces with DIAG_READ_TOKEN (the diag-relay-sweep.yml pattern) or a standing obligation in the health-review skill. Until then its exit codes reach nobody and a recurrence is caught only by luck. NOT done in this PR -- flagged deliberately rather than left implied. CLOSED BY #10086 (commit a67b1125) -- .github/workflows/broker-bracket-reconcile.yml is the scheduled caller, with fingerprint-based change detection so it cannot become a desensitized alarm.

MET 2026-08-23. The ENFORCING path carries the price axis on ALL THREE venues, and every one grades through the SAME pure module (src/runtime/protection_price.py) so no venue gets its own definition of 'diverges'. (a) IB: protection_coverage now returns stop_prices/target_prices; _protective_leg_price reads auxPrice FIRST for a stop because a STP LMT carries both and its TRIGGER is aux. (b) BYBIT: _bybit_position_protection returns stop_prices on ALL THREE paths (flat / full_position_stop / partial_sl_legs) via the new _bybit_sl_leg_trigger, a sibling of _bybit_sl_leg_qty. (c) ALPACA: protection_state returns them via AlpacaClient._leg_price. In every case an unreadable price is ABSENT, never 0.0 - a zero would compare against a declared level as a catastrophic divergence when the truth is we could not look. _check_broker_naked_ib_positions grades the divergence and logs it at ERROR with the tick count, the DIRECTION (more_exposed vs exits_earlier - the same |diff| grading to opposite consequences) and the dollar figure; summary declares stop_price_diverges up front so 'we looked and found none' cannot read as 'we did not look'. DETECT-ONLY, asserted by a test that the block calls none of cancel / modify_open_order / place_protective / _attempt_naked_autoprotect - because choosing what to do about a divergence is exactly what went wrong on 2026-08-20 (BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG). The QUANTITY verdicts are byte-unchanged on every venue. Also added profile_loader.tick_size_for, the canonical resolver: it returns None rather than a default UNLIKE its contract_value_usd_for sibling, because a wrong contract value scales a P&L figure while a wrong tick flips a real divergence into 'agrees'. 35 tests.

MET 2026-08-23 for both venues this row left unchecked. ALPACA: the located fix was applied exactly as this row described it - _open_orders_for_symbol already returned dicts carrying stop_price and limit_price, so the data was present and simply unread. BYBIT: the Full-mode branch no longer grades protection on the STRING alone; note the blast radius here is LARGER than the instance this row was filed on, since the IB one is ib_paper while bybit_2 is MAINNET. Both keep their QUANTITY verdicts unchanged. ONE RESIDUAL, recorded rather than implied: only the IB SWEEP consumes the divergence today. The Alpaca and Bybit sweeps now EXPOSE prices but do not yet grade them, so this row's detection is IB-live and alpaca/bybit-ready - filed as BL-20260823-ALPACA-BYBIT-SWEEPS-EXPOSE-PRICES-BUT-DO-NOT-GRADE.

updates.note: CRITERION 5 IS ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER WIDENS THIS ROW FROM PAPER TO REAL MONEY. Criterion 5 read: 'Re-audit the Alpaca and Bybit coverage reads for the same price blindness. NOT checked by this session -- do not read this row as clearing them.' Checked now, by code read on 968bbea8. BOTH carry it. (a) Bybit -- order_monitor._bybit_position_protection grades qty+side; its Full-mode branch returns covered_qty == size on any pos['stopLoss'] that is merely non-empty and not '0', so the STRING is the whole test; the Partial branch sums _bybit_sl_leg_qty and never reads triggerPrice. (b) Alpaca -- AlpacaClient.protection_state returns {stop: bool, target: bool, legs: int}: booleans, not even a quantity, let alone a price. has_protective_orders is weaker still (it tests the type string only). BLAST RADIUS: this row's own instance is ib_paper. bybit_2 is MAINNET. Live read 2026-08-22T12:4xZ via /api/diag/exchange_positions: 9 open Bybit positions across bybit_1/bybit_2/bybit_portfolio -- 2 of them on real-money bybit_2 (XRPUSDT 21.3, ETHUSDT 0.03) -- plus 16 Alpaca. Every one grades 'protected' today on a test that cannot see where the stop sits. CRITERION 3 HAS LANDED since this row was written: broker_bracket_reconcile.py DOES now have its scheduled caller (.github/workflows/broker-bracket-reconcile.yml, cron 6h + dispatch, recording to #10089). Verified by reading the workflow, not inferred. WHAT I SHIPPED, AND ITS LIMIT: the Bybit price axis was not merely unread, it was UNREADABLE -- broker_bracket_reconcile.py consumes /api/diag/ib_open_orders and there was no Bybit equivalent anywhere (clients.py carried account_ib_open_orders alone; the diag router's 20 routes had no sibling). So on the one venue trading real money the question could not be asked from outside at all. Added GET /api/diag/bybit_open_orders + clients.account_bybit_open_orders: three-state (not_bybit / could_not_look / orders_read), counts null-never-zero, and an unset venue price reported None NEVER 0.0 (Bybit reports no-stop as '' or '0'; a zero would grade as a catastrophic divergence from the declared level when the truth is that no stop is set). It carries BOTH the position-level Full-mode stop AND the Partial-mode legs, because under BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=full there is no resting order at all and an orders-only surface would report a correctly protected position as NAKED -- the inverse error, and the worse one, since it would drive a re-arm. Also reads BOTH the StopOrder and Order filters (a resting limit take-profit is an 'Order', invisible to the StopOrder filter) and inherits the BL-20260713-BYBIT2-BTC-SETTLECOIN-BLIND per-symbol cross-check. Tests falsified against three planted defects, each with the edit ASSERTED applied rather than assumed: naive price coercion -> 3 price tests fail; single filter -> the filter test fails; cross-check dropped -> the cross-check test fails; restored -> 15/15. (My first run of the second break reported the WRONG failure signature from a stale file in my own script -- caught and re-run, because reporting a falsification that did not actually run is the same class as everything else on this row.) STILL OPEN, and explicitly NOT done by me: criterion 4 -- whether protection_coverage / _bybit_position_protection should themselves carry the price axis so the LIVE SWEEP can act on it. That is a Tier-2/3 change to the enforcing path (a price-divergent stop grading uncovered would trigger a re-arm, which is an order-path action) and it needs an operator decision plus a tolerance chosen on a measured distribution -- the same staging #10081's proposal argues for. I built the measurement, not the enforcement. Also still open: the ALPACA read surface, which has the same gap and no equivalent route.

LIVE RE-CONFIRMATION 2026-08-22T13:2xZ, and it supplies the DISCRIMINATING CONTROL criterion 2 asks for. Read /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper (read_state 'orders_read', a confirmed clean account-wide read, count 4) beside the declared levels on /api/bot/positions?include_paper=true.

  MHG  declared SL 6.22171429 -> resting STP 6.2215   (within a tick)  | declared TP 7.141302    -> resting LMT 7.1415  PRESENT
  MGC  declared SL 4371.14690 -> resting STP 4371.1   (within a tick)  | declared TP 4393.02071  -> NO resting limit    ABSENT
  MES  declared SL 7533.69643 -> resting STP 7516.5   *** 17.196 pts   | declared TP 8390.59025  -> NO resting limit    ABSENT

So the detector's criterion-2 requirement is satisfiable on today's book: MHG PASSES on both axes while MES FAILS on price -- a run that flagged all three would be as broken as one that flagged none. The MES stop divergence is UNCHANGED from the 2026-08-20 measurement this row was written on: 17.196 points on 15 MES = $1,289.73, still live, still unremediated, and still grading FULLY STOP-COVERED because the quantity and the side are right.

SEPARATE AND WORTH STATING: target coverage on this account is 1 of 3. MGC and MES hold a stop and NO resting limit at all. That is BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED's live instance and, for MGC (strategy ict_scalp_mgc_15m), it is also the live instance of BL-20260818-ICT-SCALP-HAS-NO-TAKE-PROFIT-CLOSE-PATH -- a leg whose monitor emits no tp_cross close, holding a position with no venue target either. I did NOT re-run the take-profit counterfactual: that was measured and REFUTED (net +$6,237 is the residue of 29 worse-exits against 23 better, and a naive max-hold exit could destroy value), and re-deriving a refuted result is the failure this programme keeps naming.

MES is scheduled for an operator-approved target attach at the Sunday 2026-08-23 22:30Z reopen (trig_014S3NAzMKy2Ac2AM2GgyRE5); MGC is scheduled to be FLATTENED instead, because its declared TP sits the wrong side of market. Neither was touched by me, and the MES stop divergence above is deliberately NOT folded into that attach -- it is #10081's subject.

CORRECTION TO CRITERION 4, SAME DAY, BY THE SESSION THAT WROTE IT. Criterion 4 claims the grader reports `exposure` (more_exposed vs exits_earlier) -- 'the same |diff| grading to opposite consequences'. It did, and for an UNREADABLE direction it got the answer confidently BACKWARDS.

grade_protection_price resolved direction as `is_long = str(direction or '').lower() in ('long','buy')` -- a TWO-state read of a THREE-state fact. An absent, empty or unrecognised direction fell through to False and was graded as a SHORT, so a long whose direction the caller failed to supply got `exits_earlier` printed over what is actually un-agreed risk. That is the diagnostic-provenance sub-class A shape this repo names: the accessor does not compute what the label says, and nothing in the output reveals the substitution.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, which is the part worth recording: NOT by reading the code. A self-test fixture in broker_bracket_reconcile.py omitted the `side` key, the mirrored-divergence check failed, and the fixture looked wrong before the grader did. 35 existing tests passed over it -- every one of them supplied a direction, so none exercised the branch.

FIXED: direction is now three-state. `direction_known` ships beside `exposure`, an unreadable direction earns NO exposure verdict (None, not a guess), and the GEOMETRY (`side_of_declared`, `ticks`, `diff`) is still published because it needs no direction -- suppressing the whole verdict would be the opposite error, since the divergence is real regardless of which way the trade faces. The live IB sweep's log line now says 'consequence UNKNOWN (direction unreadable)' rather than printing a bare None beside a confident geometry. 18 new tests (53 total).

LIVE IMPACT: none observed. The live sweep passes `row['direction']` from the journal, which is populated, and the reconciler reads `side` from /api/bot/positions, which is populated -- so no live verdict was wrong. The defect was latent, and is the reason the fixture that omitted the key is now the one that carries it.

items.tier: 2 (a protective cancel + re-attach on a live position)
items.title: The MES over-cover repair cancelled the stop that MATCHED the journal and kept the stray, so the position is now protected 69 ticks below its declared level -- the exact outcome the row's own criterion 1 was written to prevent
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-20T20:23:39Z (/api/diag/ib_open_orders, read_state 'orders_read') against the journal (/api/bot/positions?include_paper=true).

BL-20260816-IB-STOPS-OVER-COVER-IN-DISJOINT-OCA-GROUPS recorded two resting MES stops against a 15 long: order 338 STP @ 7516.50 (oca-protect-336, client_id 497) and order 375 STP @ 7533.75 (oca-protect-373, client_id 597). Its criterion 1 said, explicitly: 'Establish from the journal which of 338 / 375 matches the open MES trade's declared stop_loss -- documented, not inferred from order id ordering' and then cancel the one that does NOT match.

The open MES trade 4350 declares stop_loss 7533.696429. MES tick size is 0.25 (config/instruments.yaml), and 7533.696429 rounds to 7533.75 -- order 375, to within a single tick. Order 338 at 7516.50 is 69 ticks away and matches nothing in the journal.

ORDER 375 IS GONE AND 338 SURVIVES. So the leg that matched the journal was cancelled and the stray was kept. The over-cover hazard is genuinely resolved (coverage is now exactly 1.00x in one OCA group), but the position is left protected at a level no strategy chose, 17.196 points below its declared stop -- $1,289.73 of additional loss on 15 contracts at contract_value_usd 5.0 if it fires.

AN ALTERNATIVE READING IS NOT EXCLUDED and is recorded rather than dismissed: the journal's stop_loss could have been trailed to 7533.696 AFTER the cancel, in which case 338 is simply a stale venue leg that the modify path never amended. Either way the actionable fact is identical and independently verified -- the venue stop and the journal stop disagree by 69 ticks and nothing in the repo compares them (BL-20260820-PROTECTION-COVERAGE-IS-PRICE-BLIND). What would settle which: the run record of the cancel that removed 375, and the trades.stop_loss history for 4350.

NOTE ALSO: MGC's and MHG's resting legs are held by client_id 597, which is ABSENT from /api/diag/ib_state at 20:26:43Z (live clients 498, 9297 readonly, 497). BL-20260819 work on PR #9919 concluded that issuing a cancel as a clientId whose session is gone is what produces PendingCancel. So a future repair touching those two legs should expect that path, not a synchronous cancel.

--- CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-08-22T19:0xZ, and the figure re-derived from source rather than inherited. ---
LIVE RE-READ 2026-08-22T19:0xZ, /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper, read_state 'orders_read', count 4 (a confirmed clean account-wide read, not a could-not-look):
  338  MES  STP SELL 15.0 @ aux 7516.5    oca-protect-336
  391  MGC  STP SELL 95.0 @ aux 4371.1    oca-protect-389
  398  MHG  LMT SELL 29.0 @ 7.1415        308977633
  399  MHG  STP SELL 29.0 @ aux 6.2215    308977633

The surviving MES stop is order 338 at aux 7516.5 -- the STRAY. Journal trade 4350 (read the same minute, filter_state asserted 'applied'): account ib_paper, MES, long, status open, position_size 15.0, entry_price 7634.75, stop_loss 7533.69642857, take_profit_1 8390.59025.
  declared 7533.69642857 - resting 7516.5 = 17.196429 points
  x 15 contracts x MES multiplier 5 = $1,289.73
That reproduces #10081's figure EXACTLY, now derived from the venue read and the journal row rather than carried forward. The position is protected 17.196 points BELOW its declared stop, i.e. it will ride $1,289.73 further against the trade than the strategy declared before the stop fires.

This is the live consequence of the 2026-08-20 remediation, and it is unchanged two days on. The over-coverage it was fixing IS gone (see BL-20260816, re-graded the same day) -- the quantity is right and the level is wrong. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-23T07:36Z by the full-system audit — STILL LIVE AND UNREMEDIATED, three days on. Broker truth (/api/diag/ib_open_orders): ib_paper holds ONE resting MES leg, STP SELL 15 @ 7516.5 under oca-protect-336, and no limit order. Journal truth (trade 4350, mes_trend_long_1d, 15 long opened 2026-08-03, status=open): stop_loss=7533.69642857, take_profit_1=8390.59025. Delta = 17.196 points = 68.8 ticks at MES's 0.25 tick — the '69 ticks' this row was filed on, unchanged. For a LONG a stop BELOW the declared level fires LATER, so at 15 contracts x $5/point the position carries ~$1,289.70 of loss exposure beyond what it declared. It is ib_paper (is_demo=1), so this is paper money — but the code path is the one real-money accounts use, and mis-protection is M20's own subject. NOTE FOR THE SCHEDULED REMEDIATION: the 2026-08-23T22:30Z routine attaches the MES TARGET and does NOT touch the stop, so it will leave this exposure in place. The MGC leg cross-checks CLEAN on the stop (journal 4371.1469 vs resting 4371.1, a rounding delta) and is target-naked as documented; MHG is correctly bracketed on BOTH sides (LMT 7.1415 + STP 6.2215).
resolution_criteria: Establish from the run record which cancel removed order 375, and whether trades.stop_loss for 4350 was 7533.696429 BEFORE that cancel. Do not guess -- the two readings above have different remedies.

Bring the venue stop and the declared stop into agreement for MES 4350 -- either amend 338 to the declared level or cancel and re-arm. Tier-2, and it must READ trades.stop_loss rather than take a level from the operator or the caller.

Confirmed by a follow-up read_state 'orders_read' showing the resting MES stop within one tick of the journal-declared level, and by scripts/ops/broker_bracket_reconcile.py returning no stop_price_diverges finding for ib_paper.

updates.note:
CRITERION 1 IS ANSWERED. The row offered two readings with DIFFERENT remedies and told the next session not to guess. Reading 2 -- 'the journal's stop_loss could have been trailed to 7533.696 AFTER the cancel, in which case 338 is simply a stale venue leg' -- is EXCLUDED, on evidence.

THE DECIDING FACT: order_packages pkg-1d9598b29f38440c carries sl = 7533.69642857 (identical to trades 4350's stop_loss to 8 decimal places) with updated_at = 2026-08-13T14:34:49.782796Z. `order_packages.sl` is written ONLY by the modify path, and only when the amend LANDED on every leg (order_monitor.py:1300-1343 -- a partial landing deliberately leaves it unchanged). So the package has not been touched since 2026-08-13, a full WEEK before the 2026-08-20 remediation. The declared stop was already 7533.696429 when order 375 (resting at 7533.75, that level snapped to the 0.25 MES tick grid) was cancelled and stray 338 at 7516.50 was kept.

A THIRD READING SURVIVES AND IS WORTH RECORDING, because it fits every fact and the row did not consider it: 7516.50 may be the ENTRY-time stop and 7533.696 a trail that landed on 08-13, in which case the 08-13 modify PLACED a new leg (375, in its own OCA group oca-protect-373) instead of amending 338 in place -- which is precisely the disjoint-OCA over-coverage BL-20260816-IB-STOPS-OVER-COVER-IN-DISJOINT-OCA-GROUPS found. Under that reading the remediation cancelled the NEW correct leg and kept the STALE original.

⚠️ READINGS 1 AND 3 HAVE THE SAME REMEDY, so the criterion's warning is satisfied without choosing between them: the venue must be brought to the journal-declared 7533.696429 either way. Only reading 2 implied 'do nothing', and it is the one ruled out.

CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-08-23T10:5xZ (/api/diag/ib_open_orders, read_state 'orders_read', count 4): order 338 MES STP SELL 15.0 @ aux 7516.5, oca-protect-336, GTC, client_id 497 -- and 497 is CONNECTED per /api/diag/ib_state (0 consecutive failures, last_ok 28.8s). So the placing session is ALIVE. Note the contrast the row flagged: MGC 391 and MHG 398/399 are all held by client_id 597, which is absent from the live client list (498, 497, 9108) -- the dead-session case that produces PendingCancel. MES is NOT that case.

WHY IT HAS NEVER SELF-HEALED, which the row did not have and which is the more important find: the modify path's idempotence filter compares the strategy's intent against `order_packages.sl` -- THE JOURNAL -- and never against the venue (order_monitor.py:771 passes current_sl=open_pkg.get('sl')). The journal says 7533.696429, the strategy re-computes 7533.696429, the filter drops it as 'no_meaningful_change', and nothing is sent. The system is not failing to notice; it is correctly concluding that the change it wants is already made, from the only record it consults. Filed separately as BL-20260823-MODIFY-IDEMPOTENCE-COMPARES-INTENT-TO-JOURNAL-NEVER-TO-VENUE, because it is a general defect and this position is one instance of it.

CRITERION 2 IS NOT DONE, AND THE TOOL FOR IT DOES NOT EXIST. The ops allowlist has `cancel-ib-order`, `attach-ib-target` and `flatten-ib-position`; there is no `amend-ib-stop`, and an ops process could not amend 338 anyway -- IB requires the PLACING clientId to modify an order, and `attach_ib_target._ib_ops_client_id()` deliberately uses a fresh 9900+ id precisely so it cannot collide with the trader's 497 (BL-20260822-ATTACH-IB-TARGET-USES-TRADER-CLIENTID: using 497 produces 'Error 326, clientId already in use' and trips the breaker). So the two available shapes are: (a) cancel 338 with the existing action and let the baseline naked sweep re-arm at the declared level -- the re-arm is done by the TRADER itself, which owns 497 and reads trades.stop_loss, at the cost of a naked window bounded by IB_BROKER_NAKED_CHECK_SECONDS (300s) on a PAPER account; or (b) fix the structural row above so the re-assert happens without an ops action at all. (b) is the durable answer and (a) is available now. NOT executed in this update -- the last remediation on this exact position is what created the current state, so the ordering and the naked window are stated here first rather than discovered afterwards.

CRITERION 2 NOW HAS A ROUTE, AND IT IS NOT THE ONE THE PREVIOUS UPDATE OFFERED.

That update listed '(a) cancel 338 and let the baseline naked sweep re-arm ... at the cost of a naked window bounded by IB_BROKER_NAKED_CHECK_SECONDS (300s)'. **THAT COSTING WAS WRONG and the dry run proved it** (system-action issue #10169, cancel-ib-order, apply NOT set):
    action: refused
    owner_client_id: 497
    blockers: [PROTECTIVE (oca_group set) -- cancelling strips a live position's exit,
               owning clientId 497 is in the trader's execution band (<9000) ... pass
               --force-client-id only with the trader stopped]
`cancel_ib_order` connects AS the owning clientId -- that is its documented mechanism -- and 338's owner is the trader's own LIVE execution session. So route (a) is not a 300s naked window; it is: stop the trader, cancel, position naked, restart, and wait for the sweep that was itself stopped for part of it. The naked window spans a service restart, to repair a PAPER position's stop.

⚠️ A COSTING I HAD ALREADY WRITTEN INTO THIS ROW WAS WRONG BY A LARGE FACTOR, and it read plausible. Recorded rather than corrected silently, because the previous update also told the next session that route (a) was 'available now'. It is not.

THE ROUTE THAT WORKS: the trader ALREADY owns order 338 and can amend it in place via IBClient.modify_protective -- no cancel, no ops clientId, no downtime, no naked window. What was missing was only the trigger, which shipped today as order_monitor._reassert_from_divergence riding the cadence-gated naked sweep (BL-20260823-MODIFY-IDEMPOTENCE-COMPARES-INTENT-TO-JOURNAL-NEVER-TO-VENUE). It reads trades.stop_loss, sends BOTH declared legs, and is bounded per (account, symbol).

STATUS: shipped at `annotate`, so nothing is repaired yet. One env flip (PROTECTION_REASSERT_MODE=apply, PROTECTION_REASSERT_ACCOUNTS=ib_paper) repairs MES 4350 on the next sweep. Tier-2, operator-gated, deliberately not taken unilaterally on the position whose last remediation is the subject of this row.

CRITERION 3 IS UNCHANGED AND IS THE PROOF: a follow-up read_state 'orders_read' showing the resting MES stop within one tick of 7533.69642857, and scripts/ops/broker_bracket_reconcile.py returning no stop_price_diverges finding for ib_paper. Do not close this row on the apply flip alone -- close it on that read.

CRITERION 3 IS MET. RESOLVED — VERIFIED AT THE BROKER 2026-08-23T13:54Z.

Sequence: PROTECTION_REASSERT_ACCOUNTS=ib_paper written with service:none (#10175), then PROTECTION_REASSERT_MODE=apply with a trader restart (#10176, post-restart state active). The very next cadence-gated IB naked sweep acted: soak row 13:54:32Z reads mode=apply, apply_scope=allowlisted, acted=true (the 13:42 and 13:48 rows immediately before it read mode=annotate, apply_scope=not_allowlisted, acted=false — so the flip is what changed the behaviour, not a coincident sweep).

BROKER TRUTH, not our own log: /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper, read_state=orders_read, shows MES STP SELL 15.0 at aux_price 7533.75 under a NEW oca group oca-protect-408, order_id 410. It was 7516.5. |7533.75 - 7533.69642857| = 0.0536 = 0.21 MES ticks, inside the one-tick bar this criterion sets. The 68.79-tick / $1,289.73 divergence that had stood since 2026-08-20 on a healthy monitor and a connected session is closed.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: one position, one venue, one account (ib_paper). The re-assert remains scoped to ib_paper — bybit and alpaca are still not_allowlisted, and widening it is a separate Tier-2 decision that should rest on more than n=1.

items.title: A session whose GitHub MCP is read-only could not post the MANDATORY coordination-board START -- relays existed for the PR half of that 403 and none for the board half; board-post.yml closes it, demonstrated by a real post
items.detail:
MEASURED this session: mcp__github__add_issue_comment against issue #6927 returns 403 'Resource not accessible by integration' repeatedly, while every MCP READ (issue_read, pull_request_read) succeeds. This is the same 403 the header of .github/workflows/claude-pr-automerge.yml already documents, and that header names issue comments explicitly.

docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md, section 'Multi-session coordination', makes posting a START comment to #6927 MANDATORY before a session's first substantive tool call. Two relays already existed for the PR half of the same 403 -- pr-opener.yml (open a PR) and claude-pr-automerge.yml (merge one) -- and there was NO relay for the board comment, which is the one the rules call mandatory. So a read-only session was structurally unable to comply with a binding rule; its only available moves were to skip the board or to stop.

FIXED HERE by .github/workflows/board-post.yml: pushing a markdown file to automation/board-posts/ on a claude/** branch posts its contents as one comment on #6927 and writes the resulting URL back to automation/board-results/. Deliberately stricter than the pr-opener.yml it is modelled on, in two ways chosen for this artifact: an empty or whitespace-only body is REFUSED rather than posted (a blank comment reads as compliance while saying nothing), and a failed post FAILS THE RUN rather than recording 'FAILED:' and exiting 0 (pr-opener's behaviour is fine for a PR, whose absence is self-evident, but a session that believes it claimed the board and did not is invisible to every other session AND to itself).

Blast radius: comments on one hardcoded issue number. It cannot open, close, label or edit an issue, cannot touch a PR, and cannot reach src/, config/, a unit file, or either VM. The issue number is hardcoded rather than read from the request precisely so this does not become a general issue-commenting primitive.

SEPARATE OBSERVATION, recorded because it wastes time otherwise: `git push` from this session was ALSO refused for a period and then began working with no change in approach, whereas the MCP 403 has been stable throughout. A transient block and a permission boundary look identical on the first failure; retry before concluding a capability is absent, and do not conclude it is present until a write actually lands.

=== OUTCOME OF THE ATTEMPTED FIX, 2026-08-20 -- IT DOES NOT WORK ===
Reported honestly because this row's own criteria say a workflow that has never posted is not evidence it can, and the first version of this row read 'fix_built_pending_merge' before the workflow had ever run.

ATTEMPT 1 (push ae02aa1e + 913634b6): board-post.yml did not trigger AT ALL. No run, no result file, request unconsumed after 10 minutes of polling. The POSITIVE CONTROL is what makes that a measurement rather than an assumption: pr-opener.yml fired on the SAME push, opened PR #10076, consumed its request and committed its result back -- so push-triggered workflows demonstrably work for this session and the fault was in this workflow. The trigger block was structurally identical to claude-pr-automerge.yml's (branches: ['claude/**'] + a paths filter), so the difference was narrowed to the workflow-level `env:` block and the branches filter; both were removed and the issue number inlined.

ATTEMPT 2 (push c5aad31d, after that change): the workflow DID trigger -- it appears as check run `post` on PR #10076, started 2026-08-20T21:03:53Z, completed 21:04:04Z, conclusion FAILURE, 11 seconds. So the trigger is fixed and the POST is what fails.

WHAT IS NOT KNOWN, and I am not guessing at it: no board comment appeared, AND no result file was committed back -- which is itself informative, because the 'Commit results back' step carries `if: always()`, so a failure inside the post loop should still have committed a result file saying FAILED. That it did not means the run died BEFORE the result write, or the commit-back step itself failed. Distinguishing those needs the job log, and this session has no Actions log tooling (mcp actions_list / get_job_logs are absent from its tool surface; root CLAUDE.md says they work on some sessions -- read the session's own tool list, do not assume).
A plausible-but-UNVERIFIED candidate worth checking first: `gh issue comment` failing under the same restriction that 403s the MCP, in which case the relay approach itself is void and the gap needs a different answer entirely. Do not build on this workflow until that is settled.

STATE LEFT BEHIND: board-post.yml is merged-pending on the branch but the pending request file was REMOVED, so it no longer retriggers and no longer shows a red check. It has never successfully posted a comment. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS SESSION, stated plainly rather than buried: the MANDATORY coordination-board START for session_014myC5S5VacHNuzzBR8dGBC was NEVER POSTED. Other live sessions had no notice of this session's scope while it worked. That is a real compliance gap, not a formality, and it is recorded here rather than quietly dropped.

=== RESOLVED 2026-08-20T21:12Z -- AND THE ROOT CAUSE WAS THE COMMIT-BACK, NOT THE POST ===
SUPERSEDES the 'IT DOES NOT WORK' section above, which was written after two failed runs and before the third succeeded. Left in place rather than deleted, because the sequence is the useful part.

DEMONSTRATED: comment posted to issue #6927 -- https://github.com/benbaichmankass/Metis-Insights/issues/6927#issuecomment-5361707655 -- with automation/board-results/001-start-exit-integrity.txt committed back to the branch carrying that URL. That is the non-vacuous demonstration this row's own criteria demanded: a REAL post, not a green run over zero pending requests.

ROOT CAUSE. The commit-back step ran `git add -f automation/board-results automation/board-posts`. Consuming the last pending request `git rm`s it, which leaves automation/board-posts/ EMPTY -- and git does not track empty directories, so the path disappears from the worktree and naming it explicitly makes `git add` exit non-zero. Under that step's `set -e` the whole job failed. Fixed by staging the parent with `git add -A automation/`, which handles both the vanished subdirectory and the deletion.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, since no job log was available: by taking seriously that NO result file was committed even though the commit-back step carries `if: always()`. That combination excludes a failure inside the post loop (which writes a result before returning) and points at the commit step itself. It was confirmed by the second failure being IDENTICAL -- 11 seconds, same shape -- on a run with ZERO pending requests, which the post loop cannot fail on at all. Two hypotheses were live and BOTH WERE WRONG: that `gh issue comment` was refused by the same restriction that 403s the MCP (it is not -- the post succeeds), and that `actions/checkout` was failing. Recorded because the tempting hypothesis was the one that would have voided the whole approach.

THE EARLIER NON-TRIGGER (attempt 1) IS A SEPARATE, STILL-UNEXPLAINED FACT. Removing the workflow-level `env:` block and the `branches: ['claude/**']` filter made it start triggering, but which of the two mattered was NOT isolated -- both changed in one push. claude-pr-automerge.yml carries the same branches filter and is documented as working, which makes the `env:` block the likelier culprit, but that is an inference and not a measurement. Anyone adding a workflow here should know the ambiguity is unresolved.

=== FOLLOW-ON DEFECT FOUND 2026-08-20T21:3xZ: THE RESULTS COMMIT STRANDED THE PR'S CI, AND pr-opener.yml HAS THE SAME SHAPE ===
The relay posted correctly, and then its own results commit left PR #10076 with ZERO check runs that could never arrive.

MECHANISM. Consuming a request `git rm`'d it, so the results commit touched `automation/board-posts/**` -- this workflow's OWN trigger path. To avoid retriggering itself the commit carried `[skip ci]`, and `[skip ci]` suppresses EVERY workflow for that commit, not just this one. When the results commit is the last one pushed it becomes the PR HEAD, and required checks are evaluated against the head: `get_check_runs` on #10076 returned total_count 0 against head 57a25aa9 ('board-post: results [skip ci]'), while earlier heads on the same branch had run guards / pytest-collect / pytest-run / repo-inventory normally.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. The merge is BLOCKED, which is fail-safe, but the PR renders with no red -- and `pytest-collect.yml`'s own header already warns that 'a check that silently did not run renders identically to green'. So the failure mode is the one this repo has explicitly named.

I MISATTRIBUTED IT FIRST. I reported the 0 check runs to the operator as probably BL-20260730-PR-CI-NOT-ATTACHING, the repo's documented delivery-flakiness row. That was a guess wearing an attribution's clothes; one `git log` on the head disproved it. Recording the misattribution because blaming a known-flaky subsystem is the most comfortable available wrong answer and it would have survived unexamined.

FIXED HERE. Idempotency is now the RESULT FILE, not deletion of the request: a request whose `automation/board-results/<name>.txt` already exists is skipped. The commit therefore touches only `automation/board-results/**`, which is outside the trigger path -- no self-retrigger, so no `[skip ci]`, so the PR keeps its CI.

⚠️ `pr-opener.yml` HAS THE IDENTICAL SHAPE AND IS NOT FIXED HERE. It `git rm`s its request from `automation/pr-requests/**` (its own trigger path) and commits `pr-opener: results [skip ci]`. Whenever that commit is the last one on a branch, the PR it just opened starts life with zero checks. It was masked on #10076 only because later commits landed on top. Not touched here -- one PR, one concern, and it is a shared-infrastructure file other sessions depend on -- but it is the same bug and should be fixed the same way.

=== AND THEN THE FIX COMMIT REPRODUCED THE BUG, VIA ITS OWN MESSAGE ===
After the fix above, all three PRs STILL showed zero check runs. The remaining cause: GitHub scans the whole commit-message body for a CI-skip directive, ANYWHERE in it -- not just as a prefix or a trailer. The commit that fixed the workflow was titled 'board-post: results commit no longer strands the PR's CI ([skip ci] on the head)', and the two commits that were supposed to restore CI on the sibling PRs read 'ci: restore checks after the pr-opener [skip ci] head commit'. All three NAMED the token in order to explain it, and were therefore skipped by it. Fixed by pushing commits that describe the directive without containing it; checks attached within ~30s (guards / pytest-collect / repo-inventory on PR #10076).

THE GENERAL TRAP, which is the reusable part: a commit message, PR title or branch-name that MENTIONS a CI-skip directive triggers it. This bites the person documenting the class rather than the person causing it, so it will recur exactly when someone tries to write it down. Note that this backlog row itself assembles the token from fragments for the same reason -- writing it literally here would make any future commit that touches this file skip CI, which would be a very quiet way to disable the required checks on an unrelated PR.

It is also the same failure SHAPE as the rest of this row: the PR renders with no red, and the repo has already named that -- 'a check that silently did not run renders identically to green'. Three separate mechanisms produced that identical surface in one session (the relay's trigger-path deletion, pr-opener's inherited copy of it, and a commit message), which is the argument for detecting the SURFACE -- a PR head with zero required checks -- rather than any one of its causes.

=== RETRACTION 2026-08-20T21:35Z: 'ATTEMPT 1 DID NOT TRIGGER' IS FALSE, AND THE RETRIES SPAMMED THE BOARD ===
Everything above about WHICH attempts posted is wrong, and the error is the one this whole cluster is about: I graded a thing by a PROXY instead of by the thing itself.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED, read off issue #6927 directly:
  20:45:53Z  comment 5361466923  START posted   <- 'attempt 1', recorded above as 'did not trigger AT ALL'
  20:54:43Z  comment 5361552900  START posted   <- 'attempt 2', recorded above as failing
  21:04:02Z  comment 5361641801  START posted
  21:10:43Z  comment 5361707655  START posted   <- the only one I believed had worked
  21:13:48Z  comment 5361737407  DONE posted
THE RELAY POSTED EVERY SINGLE TIME. The `gh issue comment` call never failed. Only the commit-back step failed (the `git add` on a directory `git rm` had emptied), so no result file ever appeared -- and the job went red for that reason alone, which made the red look like a failed post.

THE ERROR. I polled for `automation/board-results/<name>.txt` and treated its absence as proof the comment had not posted. The result file is a PROXY. The board is the thing, it was one API call away, and I never checked it -- three times. Reading it once would have stopped this at 20:46. This is the same shape as everything else in this cluster: coverage graded by quantity instead of by the resting price; 'no result file' graded as 'no comment'. A negative needs the denominator you actually care about, not a correlate of it.

THE COST WAS NOT ZERO. Four near-duplicate START comments now sit on a SHARED coordination board that every live session reads, three of them redundant. That is noise on the one channel whose value is that sessions actually read it, and this repo treats a routinely-ignored alarm as a P1 in its own right. Recorded rather than quietly left, because a board that becomes skimmable is exactly how the next collision goes unnoticed.

WHAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: the relay should verify by READING BACK, not by writing a file. `gh issue comment` returns the comment URL on success -- and it did, every time. The failure was never in the post; my monitoring of it was pointed at the wrong artifact. | STATUS NORMALISED 2026-08-22 (workplan 0.1 Step 0): the free-text status 'fixed' was collapsed to 'resolved' so the open set is countable.
