The original wording is preserved here verbatim; the mapping failed TOWARD open wherever the text signalled remaining work.
resolution_criteria: DONE: board-post.yml posts a real comment to #6927 and commits the resulting URL back -- demonstrated 2026-08-20T21:12Z, comment 5361707655.
DONE: an empty or whitespace-only body is refused rather than posted, and a failed post fails the run (the two ways it is deliberately stricter than pr-opener.yml).

REMAINING (Tier-1, small): document it beside pr-opener.yml and claude-pr-automerge.yml in the root CLAUDE.md PM-side capabilities section, so the next read-only session finds it instead of re-deriving the gap. Not done in this PR to keep it to one concern.
REMAINING (curiosity, not a blocker): isolate whether the workflow-level `env:` block or the `branches` filter prevented the first run from triggering at all. Both were removed in one change.

SEPARATE, and the more valuable half: apply the same fix to pr-opener.yml (and audit claude-pr-automerge.yml for it). It `git rm`s from its own trigger path and stamps `[skip ci]`, so any PR whose last commit is its results commit begins with zero required checks -- unmergeable, but rendering as no-red rather than as red. Verified present by reading the file; NOT fixed in this PR.

CONSIDER (not built here): a check that a PR head is not sitting at zero required check runs. Three distinct causes produced that state in one session, so detecting the state beats chasing the causes -- and the state is the one that renders identically to green.

Make the relay's success signal the POST, not the commit-back. The result file is a convenience for the calling session, not evidence -- and a run that posted successfully must not go red merely because it could not commit a receipt, because that red reads as 'the comment did not post' and invites exactly the retry-spam that put four duplicate STARTs on #6927.

items.opened_by: claude (exit-integrity continuation, wiring the broker-bracket-reconcile caller)
items.title: oci-inventory is a cron'd workflow in NEITHER claude-run-failure-alert's watch list NOR its stated population -- a failure before its verdict step is silent, and the fix double-pings on drift, so it needs a decision rather than an appended line
items.detail:
FOUND while adding broker-bracket-reconcile to claude-run-failure-alert.yml, by re-counting that file's stated population rather than trusting it.

MEASURED 2026-08-21 by PARSING every .github/workflows/*.yml `on:` block (not grepping -- a commented-out cron reads like a live one to grep, which is how the earlier count went wrong): there are 12 cron'd workflows. claude-run-failure-alert.yml's header asserted '10 cron'd workflows ... The other 9 are added'. The 9 listed were right; the total was not. Unaccounted for: `oci-inventory` (weekly, Mondays 06:00 UTC) and now this session's `broker-bracket-reconcile`. The count has been corrected in that header and broker-bracket-reconcile listed.

WHY oci-inventory IS A GENUINE GAP AND NOT A DELIBERATE EXCLUSION LIKE `Health Snapshot`. Its only Telegram path is the step 'Telegram alert (drift / not_declared / could_not_check)', gated `if: steps.verdict.outputs.state == 'drift' || 'not_declared' || 'could_not_check'`. That output only exists once the verdict step has RUN. A failure BEFORE it -- OCI auth, checkout, a dependency install -- leaves the output empty, the `if` false, and NOTHING is sent. The run dies silent. This is byte-for-byte the shape claude-run-failure-alert's own header names for `replay-pregate-nightly` ('its own two notify steps are gated ... while the trigger that actually fired was schedule'), and the class its cron'd section was added to close.

WHY IT WAS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED IN-SESSION -- the one-line fix has a real cost, so it is a decision, not an omission. On `schedule`, oci-inventory's `fail_on_drift` defaults ON, so a DRIFT verdict FAILS the run. Listing it in claude-run-failure-alert would therefore fire a second Telegram on exactly the case it already handles correctly: the operator gets two pings for one drift. The tradeoff is silence-on-early-failure versus double-ping-on-drift, and an alarm that fires twice for one event is the desensitized-alarm P1 this repo treats as its own bug, so trading one for the other unilaterally is not obviously an improvement.

NOT ASSERTED: whether `Health Snapshot`'s own notify path is gated the same way. It was excluded by a prior session's reasoning that it self-notifies, and that reasoning was not re-verified here -- only oci-inventory was read. If this row is worked, check Health Snapshot's gating too rather than inheriting the claim.

RESOLVED 2026-08-21 -- the live falsifier was run, operator-authorised, and BOTH arms behaved as designed. It cost exactly the two operator Telegrams predicted, one per arm, and no more.

ARM A (pre-verdict failure => the listener MUST ping). oci-inventory run 32506941877 on a throwaway branch, a deliberate step failing before the verdict step. Step 'Telegram alert [operator-ping]' concluded SKIPPED, so no sentinel succeeded. Listener run 32507002228 read RUN_ID 32506941877, logged 'No successful [operator-ping] step on this run -- alerting', and printed 'Alerted: oci-inventory concluded failure'. That echo sits after a bare curl under `set -euo pipefail` with no `||`, so it only runs once the send succeeded: ONE real Telegram.

ARM B (drift verdict => the listener MUST stay quiet). Run 32507240243, declared ict-ib-gateway ocpus mutated 1.0 -> 3.0. Verdict `drift`, summary 'ict-ib-gateway [drift] (1 finding(s) over 3 declared+live instances)' -- the denominator is stated, which is what proves the tool really read the live cloud rather than failing before the inventory. The sentinel concluded SUCCESS, 'Fail the run on drift' failed the job, and listener run 32507294958 logged 'Suppressing: the run already sent 1 operator ping(s) of its own' with its Telegram step SKIPPED. ONE real Telegram, from oci-inventory itself, none from the listener.

CLEANUP, all verified rather than assumed: the probe branch was hard-reset to main; drift issue #10108 (opened 17:16:22Z by arm B) was auto-CLOSED at 17:18:29Z by a clean main run 32507418888, which also re-confirmed the real topology and exercised the auto-resolve path at zero ping cost.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT COVER, stated so a future reader does not over-read it. Both arms ran with healthy Telegram secrets, so arm B's send succeeded and its suppression was correct. The falsifier therefore says NOTHING about the degraded case where the send FAILS -- which turned out to be a real hole, found while designing these arms and filed separately as BL-20260821-SELF-PING-SENTINEL-SURVIVES-A-FAILED-SEND.
resolution_criteria: DECIDE between the two shapes and record which, with the reason: (a) list oci-inventory in claude-run-failure-alert.yml and accept a double-ping on drift; (b) leave it unlisted and instead make its own alert fire on failure -- e.g. an `if: failure()` step, or moving the notify out from behind steps.verdict; or (c) narrow claude-run-failure-alert so a workflow that already self-pinged is suppressed.
Whichever is chosen, PROVE it with a real failing run rather than by reading the YAML: force a pre-verdict failure on a dispatch and confirm exactly ONE operator ping arrives.
Re-verify Health Snapshot's notify gating on the schedule path and either confirm its exclusion is sound or fold it into the same fix; do not inherit the prior session's claim unchecked.
Leave the corrected population count in claude-run-failure-alert.yml's header consistent with a re-parse of the `on:` blocks -- it has now been wrong twice, both times from grepping.
updates:
PARTLY RESOLVED 2026-08-21 (session spsxq6), operator-directed: shape (c) — "dedupe first, then list". BOTH exclusions are now listed; the double-ping is gone by construction rather than by accepting it.

⚠️ THIS ROW'S OWN PREMISE WAS PARTLY WRONG, and the correction narrows the gap. It said a failure at "OCI auth, checkout, a dependency install" sends nothing. GitHub evaluates a custom `if:` as `success() && <expr>`, and oci-inventory's `Run inventory` step carries continue-on-error: true. So a failure INSIDE Run inventory — OCI auth, an API error, the single most likely mode — is MASKED, success() stays true, `Classify verdict` reaches could_not_check, and the Telegram DOES fire. That mode was never silent. What is genuinely silent: a failure in checkout / setup-python / pip install (success() false, notify step SKIPPED), and cancelled / timed_out (the step is never reached). Health Snapshot has the same shape — its notify is `always() && steps.status.outputs.level != ''`, so it pings after `status` runs and is silent before it. Read the YAML, not this row's first draft.

THE MECHANISM, and why it is verified rather than declared: a workflow that sends its own operator ping names that step with the sentinel `[operator-ping]`. The listener reads the WATCHED run's jobs/steps (needs `actions: read`; the workflow_run payload carries no step detail) and stays quiet ONLY when such a step actually concluded `success`. An allow-list of "workflows that self-ping" was rejected: it would be cheaper to get wrong than to satisfy, the presence-only failure new-table-wiring-guard's marker already cost this repo.

THREE states, never collapsed, and the tie-break is the point: self_pinged -> quiet; no_self_ping -> ping; could_not_check (the API read failed) -> PING ANYWAY. "We could not look" must never be served as "someone else handled it" — a duplicate ping is a nuisance, a swallowed one is the entire bug this listener exists to prevent.

PROVEN SO FAR, and stated as exactly what it is: the FAILURE PATH is tested in tests/test_run_failure_alert_dedupe.py, 9 cases, which EXTRACTS the jq filter from the shipping workflow rather than copying it (a copy drifts and then the test passes while the workflow is broken). The load-bearing case is that a SKIPPED sentinel step does NOT suppress — matching on presence would suppress exactly the silent-cron failure this closes. Also covered: a failed sentinel, an unmarked telegram step, multi-job runs, a job with no steps, and an assertion that every listed self-pinger actually carries the sentinel.

NOT YET PROVEN — the criterion below is deliberately left open. No REAL failing run has been forced, so "exactly ONE operator ping arrives" is established for the logic and NOT for the live wiring. The remaining falsifier: dispatch oci-inventory so it fails BEFORE its notify step (a pre-verdict failure, not an OCI-auth one, per the correction above) and confirm exactly one ping; then a drift run and confirm exactly one. That costs the operator two real Telegrams, which is why it was not done unasked.

items.title: board-post.yml's idempotency receipt is committed PER-BRANCH while the request merges to main -- so any request that reaches main receipt-less is re-posted by every future branch that files a board post; measured as 3 copies of one comment
items.detail:
MEASURED, not inferred. board-post.yml skips a request when automation/board-results/<name>.txt exists. The receipt is committed to the BRANCH that ran the relay; the request file merges to `main` with the PR. When a request reaches main and its receipt does not, main carries a request that looks permanently UNSERVED -- and the relay loops over every *.md in automation/board-posts/ on whatever branch triggered it.

So any future claude/** branch that adds ANY board post re-posts every receipt-less request sitting on main, as a side effect of filing its own.

CORRECTION 2026-08-21T07:12Z -- THE COUNT IS FIVE, NOT THREE. This row originally said three copies. The session that WROTE board-post.yml measured it properly afterwards, by reading the 003 receipt committed into each of its five board branches, i.e. the copy each run actually posted: claude/board-release-exit-integrity -> 5365708801; claude/board-start-tier1-followups -> 5365976531; claude/board-correction-dispatch -> 5365994348; claude/board-claim-10083 -> 5366092551; claude/board-release-10083 -> 5366195702. FIVE copies. The count here was low because it was inferred from the two copies visible in one board page (5366092551 was taken for the third; it was the fourth) and a fifth was posted about 100 seconds after the heads-up went up. THE UNDERCOUNT IS ITSELF THE ROW'S OWN LESSON: a page of a paginated feed is not the population, and a count taken off one is a lower bound, not a measurement. The mechanism below is unchanged and was correctly diagnosed; only the magnitude was wrong.

THE EVIDENCE: automation/board-posts/003-merge-claim-and-correction.md landed on main via #10076; its receipt was written to claude/place-protective-docstring, which has not merged. Copies observed at the time this row was first written:
  06:23:17Z issuecomment-5365994348 (intended)
  06:35:30Z issuecomment-5366092551 (re-post)
  06:35:31Z issuecomment-5366092673 (the NEW request that triggered that run)
The last two are ONE SECOND apart in the same run, which is what identifies the mechanism: the new request triggered the relay and the receipt-less 003 was swept up with it. A prior session had already put four near-duplicate STARTs on this board for a DIFFERENT reason (it polled for a receipt and misread its absence as a failed post); the board's value is that sessions actually read it, and it is now carrying multi-screen duplicates.

NOTE THE TRAP IN THE OBVIOUS FIX. Reverting to 'delete the request once posted' -- the original design -- does stop this, but it is what the current header explains was removed: the deleting commit touches the workflow's own trigger path. Without [skip ci] it self-retriggers (harmlessly: the second run finds no requests and commits nothing), and WITH [skip ci] it suppresses every workflow for that commit, which strands a PR at zero checks. Note also that BOTH designs already share the separate github-actions[bot] pathology, and it is WORSE than the current header admits: any commit the relay pushes becomes the branch head, and GitHub does not trigger workflows for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes, so the PR shows zero checks until an ordinary commit arms it (observed on #10076 and again on #10083).

MEASURED TWICE ON ONE PR, 2026-08-21, which is what shows it is a CYCLE and not a one-off: PR #10086 went to zero checks at head b0e6a65 ('board-post: results'), was armed with an ordinary commit 099b0f8 (4 required checks queued, confirmed by reading them), and was re-stranded MINUTES LATER at head b25db90 -- another 'board-post: results' -- because the SAME push that armed CI also filed a board post, so the relay fired again and re-took the head. So filing a board post from a PR branch STRANDS THAT PR'S OWN CI, every time, and a session that files a post as its last act leaves a PR that renders as no-red and can never merge.

THIS CONTRADICTS A STATED CLAIM AND THE CLAIM SHOULD BE FIXED (field beats comment). pr-opener.yml's header says the results-only staging means 'no self-retrigger, no skip directive, PR keeps its CI'. Only the first two are true. Staging results outside the trigger path avoids the RETRIGGER; it does nothing about the HEAD, because the commit is still pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN. board-post.yml's header repeats the same reasoning verbatim. Both are half-right in the reassuring direction.

A 003 receipt has been BACKFILLED BY HAND to stop this specific request recurring. That fixes the instance, not the class.

THIRD OCCURRENCE, AND IT GENERALISES BEYOND board-post (2026-08-21T07:1x). PR #10086 was stranded a THIRD time, this time by pr-opener.yml (head 1c5f56b, 'pr-opener: results'), and the trigger was NOT a board post -- it was MERGING `main`. The merge brought in #10083's spent request file automation/pr-requests/place-protective-docstring-0821.json, which sits under pr-opener's own trigger path `automation/pr-requests/**`. So the merge counted as a push touching that path, the relay fired, found nothing to do (it correctly refused to open a duplicate PR: 'a pull request for branch ... already exists'), and STILL committed a results file -- taking the head and zeroing the checks.

SO THE RULE IS BROADER THAN 'do not file a board post from your PR branch'. Any push that touches ANY relay trigger path strands the PR, and MERGING MAIN CAN DO IT WITHOUT THE AUTHOR TOUCHING ANYTHING, because main permanently carries every other PR's spent request files under those paths. A session that syncs to main -- which the merge protocol tells it to do on a real conflict -- can silently zero its own CI as a side effect. Enumerated 2026-08-21, the push-path triggers are: board-post `automation/board-posts/**`, pr-opener `automation/pr-requests/**`, pr-close `automation/pr-close-requests/**`, claude-pr-automerge `.github/pr-automerge-request`, vm-driver `automation/jobs/**`, plus several `.github/*-request` marker files.

Note the relay behaved CORRECTLY in every other respect here -- it refused the duplicate PR and said so. The damage is done purely by the results commit taking the head. That is what makes 'stop the relay taking the head' the right fix rather than any change to the relays' logic.
resolution_criteria: PREFER AN ANCESTRY TEST OVER BACKFILLING RECEIPTS (proposed by the author of board-post.yml, 2026-08-21): a request file that is reachable from origin/main is FINISHED BY DEFINITION, so the relay can skip it regardless of whether a receipt exists on the current branch. Backfilling makes each individual case correct; the ancestry test makes the class impossible. The 003 backfill already merged (#10086) is the instance fix and does not close this row.

Make the skip decision independent of which branch is running -- e.g. resolve the receipt against origin/main as well as the current branch, or key idempotency on something durable (a marker committed alongside the request, or an existence check against the issue's own recent comments) rather than on a branch-local file.
Whatever is chosen, it must NOT reintroduce either known pathology: no [skip ci] on a commit that can become a PR head, and no unbounded self-retrigger.

PROVE it with a real two-branch exercise: leave a receipt-less request on main, push a NEW board post from a fresh branch, and confirm exactly ONE comment appears -- reading the board itself, never the receipt file (misreading the receipt as the post is the error that produced the earlier four duplicates).
Sweep automation/board-posts/ on main for any other receipt-less request before closing, and backfill or remove them; 003 was found only because it was about to fire a fourth time.

Fix or correct the 'PR keeps its CI' claim in BOTH pr-opener.yml and board-post.yml headers -- staging outside the trigger path prevents the retrigger, NOT the zero-check head. Either stop the relay taking the head (e.g. push results to a side ref or an artifact rather than the PR branch), or state plainly in both headers that a relay run leaves the PR needing an ordinary commit to re-arm CI.

Treat the fix as covering ALL push-path relays, not board-post alone: pr-opener, pr-close, claude-pr-automerge and vm-driver share the identical results-commit-takes-the-head shape. A fix for one that leaves the others is not a fix.

Handle the merge-from-main path explicitly: main permanently carries other PRs' spent request files under the trigger paths, so a routine sync re-fires a relay through no action of the author's. Either make the relays no-op WITHOUT committing when there is nothing pending, or stop them pushing to the PR branch at all.

updates.note: Re-validated: tooling/guard correctness. Unblocked and cheap; still undone.

FOURTH OCCURRENCE, MEASURED, AND STILL LIVE 18 DAYS AFTER FILING — including 9 days after the 2026-08-29 triage recorded it as 'unblocked and cheap; still undone'. This instance is the merge-from-main path this row's own text predicted, and it adds one thing the three earlier occurrences did not: THE DUPLICATED POST WAS ANOTHER SESSION'S START, not a spent request of the author's. SEQUENCE: MI-196's PR #11369 squash-merged to main at 11:09:03Z carrying automation/board-posts/mi196-start.md WITHOUT its receipt (verified: `git cat-file -e origin/main:automation/board-results/mi196-start.txt` fails on main, while the request file IS there, introduced by 0e03be9d). MI-195 then merged main into claude/mi195-tp-decisions-and-examine to clear an unrelated merge_slot conflict — touching nothing under any relay trigger path itself — and pushed. board-post.yml fired, swept up the receipt-less mi196 request, and posted it AGAIN. THE DUPLICATE IS BYTE-IDENTICAL AND 92 SECONDS APART: issuecomment-5584288729 (11:16:30Z, posted from MI-196's own branch, correct) and issuecomment-5584306882 (11:18:02Z, posted from MI-195's branch, spurious). The board consequently renders MI-196's DONE (11:16:29Z) followed by their START TWICE — duplicated AND out of order, on the one surface whose value is that sessions read it. AND IT RE-BURIED THE INHERITING PR'S CI exactly as this row describes: the relay's results commit (1bb914d8, github-actions[bot]) took the head of #11370, which had been green, so the suite had to be re-armed with an ordinary commit — this one. That made three forced merge cycles for #11370 in a single session, each costing a ~17-minute pytest-run. NOTE THE INSTANCE SELF-HEALS AND THE CLASS DOES NOT: mi196-start.txt is now committed on this branch, so merging #11370 defuses THIS request for everyone. Any other receipt-less request on main is still armed, which is why this row's own resolution_criteria call for a sweep and for the ancestry test rather than another backfill. THIRD HARM, FOUND AFTER THE ABOVE WAS WRITTEN — IT ALSO BLOCKS SELF-LANDING, which none of the four prior occurrences recorded. The relay's receipt lands under automation/board-results/**, which is NOT in check_pr_landing.py's TIER1_SURFACE allowlist, so R5 refused this PR's `landing: self` on a file the author never chose to add: 'the diff contains paths this guard cannot vouch for — outside the Tier-1 surface: automation/board-results/mi196-start.txt'. MEASURED on 9cfab15c: guards PASS 72 · FAIL 1, the one failure being pr-landing-guard. So a relay firing on an inherited request can flip a Tier-1 PR from self-landing to needing a human, silently, through no decision of the author's. ⚠️ AND THE GUARD'S hold_reason VOCABULARY HAS NO HONEST VALUE FOR THIS CASE. The five are changes_landing_machinery / depends_on_unmerged_pr / awaiting_evidence / operator_asked_to_hold / tier_2_3_needs_approval; this is none of them — the work is Tier-1 and the blocking path arrived by automation. Declaring tier_2_3_needs_approval to get past it would put a false tier on the landing record, so it was NOT done. RESOLUTION TAKEN HERE: the guard's own first-listed remedy — narrow the PR. The receipt was removed from this branch, so #11370 self-lands as the Tier-1 work it is. ⚠️ THE COST IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: mi196-start.txt therefore does NOT reach main, so the mi196 request stays receipt-less and the trap stays ARMED for the next branch that merges main and pushes a path under automation/board-posts/** — which a routine main merge does, since main carries that request. The earlier claim in this same note that 'merging #11370 defuses THIS request for everyone' is therefore WITHDRAWN; it was true when written and the narrowing made it false. ⚠️ AND THE BACKFILL CANNOT SELF-LAND EITHER: any branch carrying only a board-results file hits the identical R5 refusal, so the receipt needs a human merge whatever carries it. That is a second reason this row's ancestry-test criterion beats backfilling.

items.opened_by: claude (exit-integrity continuation, hit while requesting auto-merge for #10086)
items.title: claude-pr-automerge.yml triggers on ONE shared path (.github/pr-automerge-request), so every PR that requests auto-merge conflicts with every other one that does -- a guaranteed merge + full CI cycle per collision, unlike the sibling relays which already use a per-request directory
items.detail:
HIT LIVE, not theorised. .github/workflows/claude-pr-automerge.yml triggers on `paths: ['.github/pr-automerge-request']` -- a SINGLE file. Every PR wanting auto-merge must modify that same file, so any two PRs using the relay collide on it by construction.

MEASURED 2026-08-21: #10083 requested auto-merge (writing its line into that file) and merged as 932f0a54. #10086, branched from 9752348b before that, then requested auto-merge and came back `mergeable_state: dirty`. The ONLY conflicted path was `.github/pr-automerge-request`; every other file merged cleanly. Cost: one merge commit plus a full ~10-minute CI cycle, against a repo that has already hit the free-tier CI-minutes cap once (MB-20260706-CI-MINUTES).

The content is a trigger MARKER, not state anyone reads back -- the workflow only needs the path to have changed. So the conflict is pure ceremony: the resolution is always 'take the requesting PR's line', which carries no information.

THE FIX IS ALREADY THIS REPO'S OWN CONVENTION, which is what makes this worth filing rather than tolerating. Every sibling relay uses a per-request DIRECTORY and therefore never collides: pr-opener.yml takes `automation/pr-requests/<name>.json`, board-post.yml takes `automation/board-posts/<name>.md`, pr-close.yml takes `automation/pr-close-requests/<name>.json`. Only the auto-merge relay kept a single shared file.

NOT ASSERTED: how often this actually bites. It needs two auto-merge requests open across one merge, which this session hit on its first attempt but which may be uncommon on a quiet day. The cost per occurrence is bounded and recoverable (resolve, push, re-run CI) -- hence 'low', not the conflict itself being in doubt.
resolution_criteria: Change the trigger to a per-request directory matching the sibling relays -- e.g. `paths: ['.github/pr-automerge-requests/**']` with one file per PR -- so two concurrent requests touch different paths and cannot conflict.
Keep the old single-file path in the trigger list for one transition window so an in-flight branch that already wrote the old file still fires, then remove it.
PROVE it with two branches: open two PRs that both request auto-merge, merge one, and confirm the second comes back mergeable rather than `dirty`.
Check whether the relay reads the file's CONTENT anywhere before changing its shape; as of 2026-08-21 it appears to use the path only as a trigger, but that was read, not tested.

updates.note:
SEVERITY RAISED low -> HIGH by a second live hit, on a DIFFERENT and worse failure mode than this row measured. The original analysis is correct and is not being overwritten — it is extended, because the cost it priced (one merge commit + one CI cycle, 'bounded and recoverable') is not the worst thing this trigger can do.

WHAT HAPPENED (2026-08-21T08:17:11Z, PR #10088). This row's own fix-source — a67b112, the commit that landed #10086 — carries `.github/pr-automerge-request` holding **#10086's** line: '#10086 ... Merge-slot claimed on #6927 at issuecomment-5366299764'. PR #10088 was `mergeable_state: dirty` for an unrelated reason (the health backlog), so it merged origin/main. That merge brought the file in. The push of the merge therefore TOUCHED `.github/pr-automerge-request` — and claude-pr-automerge.yml triggers on any push touching that path, not on a push that WROTE a request. It marked #10088 ready_for_review and enabled auto-merge (squash), attributed to github-actions[bot].

SO THE FAILURE IS NOT ONLY 'two requests conflict'. It is: **merging main into any claude/** branch can enable auto-merge on that branch's PR, using a DIFFERENT PR's merge-slot claim.** No one decided it. The inheriting PR need never have requested auto-merge at all — #10088 never wrote a line into that file.

WHY THAT IS HIGH AND NOT LOW. #10088 carries `src/units/strategies/pairs_executor.py` (an isolated 2-leg ORDER PATH) and `deploy/ict-exchange-fills-pull.timer` (**a unit file the live VM consumes** — named verbatim in CLAUDE.md's Tier-3 hard-limit list). Both are operator-approved, so nothing improper would have merged THIS time; the defect is that approval was not what gated it. A branch that had merged main and held an UNapproved live-path change would have been set to auto-merge identically. It also silently defeats the merge-slot serialization the coordination board exists to enforce: #10088 was queued on #10086's claim.

DISPOSITION THIS SESSION: auto-merge disabled on #10088 and the PR returned to draft, because the merge slot was never claimed for it. Not a fix — the trigger is unchanged and the next branch to merge main will inherit it again.

THE PROPOSED FIX IS UNCHANGED AND NOW BETTER SUPPORTED: move to a per-request DIRECTORY (`automation/automerge-requests/<name>.json`), matching pr-opener.yml / board-post.yml / pr-close.yml. That fixes BOTH modes at once — a per-branch path cannot collide, AND cannot be inherited through a merge, because a branch that never wrote its own request file never touches the trigger path. A `paths` narrowing alone would not: the file would still arrive via merge.

[s1-q9kso 2026-08-22] FIX SHIPPED; ROW STAYS OPEN ON ITS OWN CRITERION 3, deliberately. Criteria 1, 2 and 4 are met: the trigger is now the per-request directory `.github/pr-automerge-requests/**` matching every sibling relay, the old single shared path is KEPT in the list for a transition window, and criterion 4 is now TESTED rather than read — a whole-file grep shows `.github/pr-automerge-request` appears exactly TWICE in claude-pr-automerge.yml (the header comment and the paths filter), so nothing reads its content and reshaping it is safe. CRITERION 3 — 'PROVE it with two branches' — is NOT met, and I am not claiming it. What I DID run is a real two-branch git A/B on the actual mechanism (two throwaway repos, real branches, real merges): with the SHARED file, branch B merging into a main that already took branch A CONFLICTS, and the only conflicted path is `.github/pr-automerge-request` — the defect reproduced from scratch; with the PER-REQUEST directory the same sequence merges CLEAN. That settles the conflict property, which is the defect itself. What it does NOT settle is that GitHub still FIRES the workflow on the new path — a `paths:` filter is well-defined but well-defined is not tested. Doing that honestly costs two throwaway PRs with auto-merge ARMED on both, i.e. two ~11-minute CI cycles plus the risk of a throwaway PR auto-merging to main, against a defect that only bites when two auto-merge requests are open across one merge — which cannot happen today because the one-session-at-a-time policy is in force. So the remaining proof is deferred, not skipped, and this row is the record of that. FIRST SESSION TO USE THE RELAY: drop a file under the new directory and confirm the run fires; that is criterion 3's cheap half and it costs nothing extra. Remove the legacy path from the filter once no open PR carries it.

[s1-q9kso 2026-08-22, ~10:46Z] CRITERION 3's TRIGGER HALF IS NOW PROVEN — BY ACCIDENT, WHICH ALSO EXPOSED A DEFECT IN MY OWN FIX. I shipped the new per-request trigger as `paths: ['.github/pr-automerge-requests/**']` together with a README.md in that directory. GitHub fired the relay on that push and `pull_request.auto_merge_enabled` arrived at 10:46:15Z, actor github-actions[bot], merge_method squash, on PR #10136 — a PR I had not claimed a merge slot for and intended to merge by hand. TWO CONSEQUENCES, and the second matters more than the first. (1) GOOD: the deferred half of criterion 3 is answered at zero cost. GitHub DOES fire on the new path; the relay is not silently dead after the move. That was the exact thing I had said needed two throwaway PRs to establish, and it established itself. (2) BAD, AND MINE: `**` matches the directory's own DOCUMENTATION. A trigger path that a doc edit can fire is a trigger that merges pull requests nobody asked to merge — and it did, on the very PR that introduced it. Narrowed to `.github/pr-automerge-requests/*.txt` so prose in that directory can never be a signal; the README now says so and cites the timestamp. Auto-merge on #10136 was disabled immediately and that PR was merged by hand under the protocol, on a verified get_check_runs read. WHAT REMAINS OF CRITERION 3: only the CONFLICT half needed two PRs, and that was already settled by the two-branch git A/B (shared file -> CONFLICT on exactly that path; per-request dir -> CLEAN). Trigger + conflict are both now evidenced, so the only open step is REMOVING the legacy `.github/pr-automerge-request` path from the filter once no open PR carries it.
Re-validated: one shared path means concurrent PRs conflict. Live relevance — a concurrent session merged #10412 while I worked, so multi-PR concurrency is the norm here, not the exception.

items.opened_by: claude (exit-integrity continuation, during the session-end doc-freshness pass)
items.title: docs/github-actions-workflows.md asserts every workflow file is named in it (BL-20260602-003's completeness invariant) and 52 of 111 are absent -- a doc that CLAIMS completeness and is 47% short is worse than one that claims nothing
items.detail:
FOUND by the session-end doc-freshness pass, checking the invariant mechanically instead of spot-reading it.

docs/github-actions-workflows.md's 'Complete workflow index' section states its own contract: 'this index lists the REMAINING workflow files so that every .github/workflows/*.yml is named in this doc'. That is the catalog-completeness invariant BL-20260602-003 was closed on.

MEASURED 2026-08-21, by testing every filename against the doc rather than reading the table: **52 of 111 workflow files are named nowhere in it.** Absent entries include load-bearing ones a reader would reasonably expect to find -- `guards.yml` (a REQUIRED status check), `claude-run-failure-alert.yml` (the universal dead-run alarm), `claude-pr-automerge.yml`, `board-post.yml`, `pr-close.yml`, `oci-inventory.yml`, `macro-producer-liveness.yml`, `replay-pregate-nightly.yml`, and the whole m28/m31/m32/m33/m34 grade family.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN AN UNDOCUMENTED SET, and why it is filed rather than shrugged at: the doc does not present itself as a partial cheat-sheet, it presents itself as exhaustive. A reader looking for 'is there a workflow that does X' and not finding it concludes NO SUCH WORKFLOW EXISTS. That is the same shape as a check that silently did not run rendering identically to green -- an absence that reads as a measured negative when nothing measured it. A session acting on that conclusion builds a second workflow beside an existing one.

THIS SESSION'S OWN CONTRIBUTION IS FIXED, NOT LEFT IN THE PILE: `broker-bracket-reconcile.yml` (added this session) is now in the index. The other 51 predate this session and are NOT swept here -- a 51-row backfill is its own PR with its own review, and burying it inside a session wrap-up would make both harder to check.
resolution_criteria: Backfill the 51 remaining absent workflows into the index, each with a real one-line Purpose read from the workflow's own header -- not a filename restated as prose, which would satisfy the count and not the reader.

Add a MECHANICAL guard so the invariant cannot silently rot again: a CI check that fails when a file in .github/workflows/ is named nowhere in docs/github-actions-workflows.md. The invariant has now been asserted-and-false at least once (BL-20260602-003 closed it; it is 47% short today), which is the argument for a detector over another manual sweep -- the same reasoning canonical-doc-coherence already applies to governance-doc drift.

Until the guard exists, treat the index as a PARTIAL cheat-sheet: soften the 'every .github/workflows/*.yml is named in this doc' sentence so it stops asserting a completeness it does not have. A weaker true claim beats a strong false one.
updates:
RESOLVED 2026-08-21 in #10094 (squashed as e6327f7), session spsxq6 — backfilled AND guarded, which is what resolution_criteria asked for. Verified by reading main after the merge, not inferred from the merge response.

COUNT RECONCILED, not contradicted. This row says 52 of 111 / 47%; I re-measured 51 of 111 / 45.9% and the two are the SAME measurement — the filing session's own PR #10093 added broker-bracket-reconcile.yml, so 52 was the pre-fix count and 51 is what remained. The title keeps '52'/'47PCT' because the id embeds it and the number was correct when written; do not read the difference as a disagreement. I validated the probe against a known positive and a fabricated negative before trusting its silence.

CRITERION 1 (backfill) — all 51 rows added, each Purpose read from that workflow's own header rather than a filename restated as prose. Coverage now 111/111.

CRITERION 2 (mechanical guard) — scripts/ci/check_workflow_catalog.py, wired UNGATED into the guards.yml registry (~0.2s). Ungated for the api-tier-policy reason: a diff-scoped check cannot see a row being DELETED, and a per-step `when` is empty under --all, so a gated step skips on exactly the push/dispatch events meant to run everything (BL-20260809-GUARD-STEP-WHEN-SKIPS-ON-PUSH). Its --self-test runs on EVERY invocation and is declared in COVERED_BY_CHECKER, so check_selftest_wiring.py VERIFIES the covering path instead of trusting the declaration — confirmed in real CI: '11 registered; 11 covered ... ok workflow-catalog: covered by ... --self-test (declared + verified)'.

CRITERION 3 (soften the sentence) — MOOT, and deliberately not done. It was the interim measure for 'until the guard exists'. The guard exists, so the strong claim is now TRUE and mechanically enforced; weakening it would be the wrong direction.

TWO FINDINGS THIS ROW DID NOT HAVE, both fixed in the same PR:
(a) THE GAP RAN BOTH WAYS. 12 names in the doc carried a .yml suffix and are NOT workflow files — env-gate-guard, secret-scan, ruff-lint, canonical-db-resolver, account-class-guard, arch-doc-guard, canonical-config-loaders, canonical-doc-coherence, dry-run-guard, new-table-wiring-guard, silent-empty-guard, writer-conformance-guard. Each is a guard ID in scripts/ci/run_guards.py, folded into the single guards.yml job by BL-20260806-CI-FANOUT-AMPLIFIES-ACTIONS-OUTAGES. So the doc named a file that does not exist AND omitted the workflow that actually runs it. The guard enforces this direction too, because a completeness-only check is satisfied by a row for a workflow that does not exist — that is how an index drifts into fiction while passing its own test. A phantom is decided by basename resolution against `git ls-files`, NOT a curated exclusion list, so config/accounts.yaml is never flagged and adding a real file makes its mentions legal with no edit to the guard.
(b) THE REQUIRED-CONTEXTS MIRROR WAS STALE IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION. That doc claimed 15 required contexts; the authoritative list in branch-protection-sync.yml is 3 — ["pytest-collect","pytest-run","guards"] — and has been since the consolidation replaced the 13 individual guard contexts with the single `guards` one. A stale mirror of a GATING list invites a session to expect checks that cannot run. Corrected, with repo-inventory noted as advisory and deliberately not required.

EVIDENCE IT FAILS CLOSED, not merely that CI was green: both directions were proved against REAL planted regressions in the working tree (a new workflow file with no row; a doc row for a non-existent workflow), each exiting 1 and naming the offender, with the tree clean afterwards. A negative control asserts config/accounts.yaml is never mistaken for a phantom — without it, the obvious over-broad implementation passes every positive test and then flags ordinary config references. And the guard failed its own author's commit when the prose explaining that env-gate-guard.yml does not exist backticked the filename.

ONE DEFECT FOUND IN MY OWN BACKFILL, corrected before merge: vm-devnull-source-diagnose was given a flat AUTONOMOUS, but three of its four modes are read-only while `arm-audit` is a Tier-2 MUTATION (installs auditd on the LIVE VM) — wrong in the dangerous direction, since a reader trusting the autonomy column would have dispatched a live-VM mutation believing it autonomous. Now recorded per-MODE. The other 50 rows were swept for the same flattening; this was the only one.

KNOWN CONSEQUENCE, flagged on #6927 rather than left to be discovered: PR #10068 adds e35-bracket-sweep.yml with no row and will now fail `guards` until it adds one. Confirmed by simulation, not predicted. That is the rule working as designed — that PR adds a workflow — not a false positive.

items.tier: 2 (the fix bounds a live fetch the exit loop makes; measurement is Tier-1)
items.title: The 60s exit-evaluation requirement is BREACHED on 32.4% of cycles (max 89.1s) — and both the mean and the max are the worst ever recorded, at the largest n ever measured
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-21T06:51Z from /api/diag/log_file?name=exit_interval_soak over n=398 completed intervals across 3 processes (2026-08-21T01:29Z -> 06:51Z):
  max=89.1s  p99=76.6s  p95=74.0s  median=41.7s  mean=48.3s
  129 of 398 intervals (32.4%) exceed EXIT_EVAL_MAX_INTERVAL_SECONDS=60.
exit_loop_health concurrently reports requirement_state='breached', interval_breaches=1, max_interval_ms=71277.3 on the current process.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE 08-16 'fat tail finally sampled' READING. CLAUDE.md's EXIT_LOOP_* row correctly refuses to read a max-only series as a trend, because maxima grow with n. That objection does not apply here: the MEAN has moved too (go-live 22.4-30.2s; 08-16 28.9s at n=694; today 48.3s at n=398), and the breach is a RATE over a large sample, not a single extreme draw. Every prior recorded mean sits below every reading taken today.

CORROBORATING TICK DATA (/api/diag/tick_cost, same process family, ticks_measured=13 so SMALL-n and stated as such): tick mean 172.9s / max 222.1s against the 69.3s mean / 96.8s max CLAUDE.md records post-M20-decouple. offloop monitor.strategy_monitor_loop mean 45.5s / max 76.9s at n=62. The pass is fetch-bound: fetch.1d mean 18.2s on-loop (11.2s off-loop) against the 2.4-3.6s CLAUDE.md records for 2026-08-13, with a recurring ~26.6s ceiling across 1d/1h/15m alike — a uniform ceiling, which points at a queue/timeout stall rather than per-frame work.

SECOND-ORDER RISK, currently un-alarmed: /api/bot/stats reports status='paused', i.e. the heartbeat is 180-600s stale. ict-liveness-watchdog Telegrams CRITICAL at 300s and AUTO-RESTARTS at 480s. A 222s tick is already 74% of the alert threshold and 46% of the autoheal threshold. A tick that crosses 480s gets the trader restarted mid-tick, cold-starting every cache and making the next tick slower — the BL-20260609-001 cold-start feedback loop. Two trader restarts were observed within one hour today (process_started_utc 05:49:13 then 06:50:43) with no merge to main between them and git-sync on a 5-min cadence, so a deploy does not explain both.

THIS CLASS HAS BEEN OPEN AND WORSENING ACROSS AT LEAST THREE REVIEWS: BL-20260814-TICK-2X-SLOWER-AFTER-IB-PIN (148.7s mean / 200.0s max), BL-20260816-TICK-MEAN-DOUBLED-SINCE-0814 (72.3 -> 140.0s), BL-20260816-IB-QUEUE-TIMEOUT-EXCEEDS-EXIT-BUDGET (one IB queue timeout = 48% of the 60s budget). Each was filed and none was driven to a fix. Per the /system-review anti-normalization rule this is a MANDATORY flags_raised escalation.

--- 2026-08-21T17:45Z, session wave0-8g7443 (Wave 0.1 of the work plan): ROOT-CAUSED ---

RE-MEASURED, larger sample: /api/diag/log_file?name=exit_interval_soak, the most
recent 1000 rows of a 3,245,512-byte file (a TAIL, not the whole file) = 993 measured
intervals across 8 processes, 2026-08-21T04:32:09Z -> 17:30:29Z (13.0h):
  287/993 (28.9%) over 60s; max 95.9s; p99 82.6s; p90 73.8s; median 38.5s; mean 46.5s.
Versus the filing read (129/398 = 32.4%, max 89.1s, 3 processes): the RATE is slightly
lower on a 2.5x larger sample and the MAX has grown 89.1 -> 95.9s. Read as unchanged
and still breached, not as improvement.

THE PASS IS THE BINDING TERM, so the cadence knob is inert: interval == max(30s, pass_ms)
within 1.5s on 938/993 (94.5%), only 144/993 (14.5%) of passes finish under the 30s
floor, and 277/993 (27.9%) of passes exceed 60s BEFORE any sleep.

NO TIME-OF-DAY STRUCTURE (negative control): breach rate by UTC hour over the same 993
ranges 20.5%-37.1% across all 14 hours, including hours when US equity venues are shut.
Rules out a market-hours/venue-load explanation.

WHERE THE PASS GOES (/api/diag/tick_cost, ONE process started 2026-08-21T13:43:00.710052Z,
off-loop monitor.strategy_monitor_loop n=281 passes, mean 42.19s):
  fetch.1d   2.683/pass x 10878.4ms = 29.19s  (69.2% of the pass)
  fetch.15m  1.000/pass x 10780.7ms = 10.78s  (25.6%)
  fetch.1h   0.406/pass x  1784.0ms =  0.72s
  fetch.4h   0.498/pass x   184.6ms =  0.09s
  fetch.2h   0.132/pass x   189.4ms =  0.02s
  fetch total 40.81s = 96.7% of the pass; everything else the monitor does = 1.38s (3.3%).
The instrument validates itself in BOTH dimensions: fetchby.strategy_monitor_loop totals
11467.9s vs sum(fetch.*) 11467.9s (delta 0.0s), and 1326 misses + 3170 fetch.cache_hit
= 4496 = fetchby n exactly. 16.00 requests/pass, 4.72 miss => 70.5% hit rate overall.

ROOT CAUSE - IB CANDLE FRAMES CANNOT BE CACHED AT ALL, AT ANY TTL.
_client_cache_key (src/runtime/market_data.py:48) returns a memo key for bybit/alpaca/
oanda and falls through to None for interactive_brokers, so connector_for_symbol builds a
FRESH IBMarketData per request; _candle_cache_key (:448) keys on _client_identity_token
(:397), a per-OBJECT monotonic counter, so every IB request is a guaranteed miss AND
inserts a permanently-unhittable entry.

THE DECISIVE MEASUREMENT: there is exactly ONE open 15m package (ict_scalp_mgc_15m on MGC,
which instruments.yaml routes to interactive_brokers) per /api/bot/order-packages, and
off-loop fetch.15m is n=281 over n=281 passes - 1.000 per pass, ZERO cache hits over 3.6h.
A working cache predicts 1 x 42.19/90 = 0.470/pass (~132). Controls behave correctly, which
is what makes this a finding: predicted-vs-measured misses/pass, using each frame's own open
package count and TTL 300s / interval 42.19s - 4h (Bybit, 4 pkgs) 0.563 vs 0.498; 1h (Alpaca,
3) 0.422 vs 0.406; 2h (Bybit, 1) 0.141 vs 0.132 - all within 12%. Only IB is 2.13x over,
which is exactly the ratio a ZERO-hit cache produces.

THIS ROW'S OWN next_action IS REFUTED. Controlled reproduction at a252119 (5 identical
fetch_candles calls per venue, connector re-resolved each call as the live loops do):
bybit 4h -> 1 venue call; alpaca 1d -> 1; IB 15m -> 5; IB 1d -> 5. With
CANDLE_CACHE_TTL_MAX_S raised to 86400 (computed TTL 8640s for 1d) an IB frame STILL goes
to the venue 5/5 times. Raising the TTL cap helps the tick's 13 Alpaca 1d legs and does
NOTHING for the exit loop's two dominant frames. Do not ship it as the remedy for this row.

WHY THE EXCLUSION'S PREMISE NO LONGER HOLDS: _client_cache_key's docstring excludes IB
because "an IBMarketData holds a live socket on a specific clientId". It does not -
IBMarketData.__init__ (src/exchange/ib_connector.py:248) obtains its client from
get_ib_client(), which is a process-wide registry keyed on (host, port, client_id)
(src/units/accounts/ib_client.py:3501). Every IBMarketData for one endpoint ALREADY shares
one IBClient today, so memoizing the wrapper adds no socket and no clientId and leaves
BL-20260706-IBACCTUPDATES-COLLISION untouched.

PROPOSAL (Tier-3, NOT flipped - operator decision on this item is investigate-and-propose):
memoize the IB connector on its resolved endpoint via a shared _ib_connection_identity()

items.title: pairs_sol_eth has half-open-stranded on 8 of 8 opens since 08-18 — a pairs leg opposing a concurrent directional position on the same one-way-netting account is netted away within ~5 min and read as a broker close
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-21 from trade_journal.db (ids 4750/4751, 4761/4762, 4774/4775, 4777/4778, 4786/4787, 4826/4827, 4835/4836, 4866/4867) and /api/bot/pairs/soak. Every SOLUSDT/ETHUSDT pair opened since 2026-08-18 has ended the same way: one leg closes with exit_reason='reconciler_filled' 5-8 minutes after the open, and the surviving leg is flattened with exit_reason='pairs_half_open_cleanup' roughly ONE BAR later. pairs_bnb_btc did the same once (4744/4745, 08-18) and otherwise closes normally.

ROOT CAUSE, confirmed against exchange truth. /api/diag/exchange_positions?account_id=bybit_1 at 06:43Z returns ONE net position per symbol: ETHUSDT Buy 9.81, SOLUSDT Buy 373.0. The journal holds trend_donchian_eth_4h long 10.43 (#4807) and, for SOL, trend_donchian_sol_4h 367.8 (#4810) + pairs_sol_eth_a 5.2 (#4866) = 373.0 EXACTLY. bybit_1 is one-way netting, so the pairs ETH SHORT leg (#4867, qty 0.28) merely REDUCED the standing ETH long; no short position ever existed at the venue; the reconciler read that correctly and closed the row. The SOL leg survives only because it happens to be same-direction as the standing SOL long. A long_spread kills the short leg and a short_spread kills the long leg — either direction strands one, which is why the failure rate is 8/8 rather than intermittent.

SECOND DEFECT, independent and separately fixable: in pairs_executor.run_pairs_tick the once-per-closed-bar dedup (`if decision_bars.get(name) == bar_key: continue`) sits BEFORE the half_open safety check, so a stranded naked leg is not even looked at until the next bar. Measured gap between the reconciler close and the cleanup across the recorded instances: 62, 63, 64 and 6 minutes. The module's own comment calls a stranded leg 'un-hedged directional exposure in a market-neutral sleeve' and alerts CRITICAL on it — a condition graded that severely must not be evaluated on a bar cadence.

ALARM FATIGUE: this has fired pairs_half_open (WARN/CRITICAL) on essentially every SOL/ETH cycle for three days. Per the 'if you see something say something' rule, a routinely-ignored alarm is itself the P1.
items.why_it_matters: The sleeve is on bybit_1 (paper), so no real money is at risk today — but it is producing 60+ trades of pure churn per month (pairs_sol_eth_a/b: 37 and 32 closed trades in 30d, net -102.64 / +217.50 with a/b counts that do not match precisely because of the strands), the market-neutral hypothesis is never actually expressed, and the soak data the sleeve exists to accrue is fiction. Promoting this sleeve to real money on the current evidence would ship a strategy that has never once held both legs to a decision.
items.next_action: Tier-3 for the operator, three options in preference order: (1) give the pairs sleeve its OWN account so its legs cannot net against directional strategies (the structural fix; the sleeve is already single-account by construction so this is a config change plus credentials); (2) restrict pairs symbols to instruments no directional strategy trades on the same account; (3) enable Bybit hedge mode on the pairs account. Independently and NOT operator-gated in the same way: move the half_open / state-unreadable safety check ABOVE the bar dedup in run_pairs_tick so a stranded leg is detected every tick (Tier-2 — it is an order path, but it strictly shortens the window in which a naked leg stands).
items.resolution_criteria: Ten consecutive pairs opens where both legs remain open until a pairs_revert / pairs_stop / max_hold_bars close, with zero half_open rows in the same window.

updates.note: [s1-q9kso 2026-08-22] PARTIAL — the hedge-mode PLUMBING is shipped INERT and the row's SECOND DEFECT is found ALREADY FIXED. (1) src/runtime/bybit_position_mode.py resolves Bybit's positionIdx from the BOOK being acted on (never the order side — closing a long sends side=Sell and belongs to positionIdx=1), wired at all FIVE payload sites (execute.py submit / test-submit / set_trading_stop / close, plus order_monitor's naked-autoprotect re-arm, which had positionIdx=0 HARDCODED). BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS is EMPTY by default, so no site adds the kwarg and the wire payload is byte-for-byte unchanged — asserted by a test, since the operator's approval was specifically for the inert version. Four states, never collapsed: one_way / hedge_long / hedge_short / unresolved, where unresolved sends NO positionIdx so Bybit REFUSES rather than the code guessing a book. (2) The row's SECOND DEFECT — the once-per-bar dedup sitting above the half_open safety check, measured at 62/63/64/6-minute exposure gaps — is ALREADY FIXED in src/units/strategies/pairs_executor.py; the check now sits above the dedup with those exact figures cited in its comment. Verified by reading the code, not inferred. That half of this row should not be re-worked. STILL OPEN and still Tier-3: switching the actual position mode AT THE VENUE for a real (account, symbol). This change deliberately does NOT call switch_position_mode — code that is ready for hedge mode is Tier-1; mutating a venue's position mode is not. The row's resolution criterion (ten consecutive clean pairs opens) is therefore UNMET and cannot be met until that separate approval.

RE-CONFIRMED AND WORSE THAN 8-OF-8: 35 `pairs_half_open cleaned` WARN events over 08-20..08-29 (30 SOL/ETH, 5 BNB/BTC), and 17 of the 42 pairs closes in this window exited via pairs_half_open_cleanup. Root cause confirmed independently today: /api/diag/bybit_open_orders reports position_idx 0 (one-way NETTING) on bybit_2, and BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS is empty by design — so a market-neutral leg opposing a directional position REDUCES it instead of opening a book. Arming the allowlist is Tier-3. Escalated in this review's report.

items.title: Real-money trade 4863 crossed its declared TP, was closed by the netting reconciler at a bar-anchored ESTIMATE ~317 below the TP, and its paper mirror recorded pnl NULL
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-21. Trade 4863 (bybit_2, REAL MONEY, ict_scalp_5m, BTCUSDT long 0.005, entry 74804.5, declared take_profit_1 75698.51928571):
  06:35Z 5m bar high = 75731.2 -> the declared TP was crossed by ~33.
  06:45Z the row was still status=open with price back at 75308.8.
  ~06:47Z the row closed: exit_reason='netting_attributed', exit_price=75381.6, exit_price_source='candle_at_close' (ESTIMATED), pnl=+2.8855.
  Had it been booked at its declared TP the pnl would be (75698.52-74804.5)*0.005 = +4.47, i.e. the recorded figure understates by ~35%.
Its paper mirror 4864 (bybit_portfolio, same package, 2.261 BTC) closed as exit_reason='reconciler_filled', exit_price_source='entry_order_avg_price_unreliable', **pnl NULL** — its last observed uPnL was +1499.72, so a four-figure paper winner left no number at all. That is the same signature as BL-20260819-TRADE-4164-CLOSED-WITH-NULL-PNL, one day later, so that class is recurring, not closed.

WHY BROKER TRUTH WAS NOT USED — and this is the fixable part. /api/bot/pnl/exchange/fills?account_id=bybit_2 has NO fill later than 2026-08-20T13:36:49Z. Neither 4863's entry (08-21 04:03) nor its exit (08-21 06:47) is in the store. ict-exchange-fills-pull.timer is OnCalendar=*-*-* 00:20:00 — DAILY — while order_monitor's _LOCAL_PNL_BROKER_DEFER_MS is 6h. So for a trade that opens and closes inside one day the fills store is structurally empty at resolution time and the estimator is the ONLY path available. CLAUDE.md already records this exact reasoning for the IB side ('that timer is hourly, not daily like ict-exchange-fills-pull ... a daily pull would look correct and be inert') — the conclusion was drawn for IBKR and never applied to Bybit.

POPULATION EFFECT. /api/bot/performance pnlCoverage (MEASURED-only) is falling monotonically: all-time 0.7848 real / 0.3668 paper; 30d 0.8333 / 0.3261; 7d 0.8571 / 0.1053; 24h 0.0 / 0.0625. Across 369 closed non-backtest rows in the last month the exit_price_source split is: none 127, candle_at_close 107, recorded_exit_price 52, exchange_fill 39, local_markprice 25, bybit_closed_pnl 14, entry_order_avg_price_unreliable 3, ib_execution 2 — i.e. only 55 of 369 (15%) are genuinely broker-measured.
items.why_it_matters: Every downstream gate that reads totalPnlMeasured or pnlCoverage — the R4 research->results promotion gate above all — is being fed a book that is 85% unmeasured and getting worse. And a real-money trade that hit its target is on record as having done something else.

items.title: The decision grader labels exit_quality from the R value, not from the exit MECHANISM — 56 of 81 graded closes (69%) are scored tp_appropriate/sl_appropriate on exits the strategy never made
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-21 over the full 81-row delta returned by the grade-closed-trades system-action for since=2026-08-14 (histogram A1 B22 C54 D4, recovered complete).
  exited via a declared bracket (exit_reason in tp/sl/tp_cross/sl_cross): 1 of 81.
  graded 'tp_appropriate' or 'sl_appropriate' anyway: 56 of 81 (69%).
The substituted mechanisms are reconciler_filled (24), netting_attributed (9), pairs_revert (8), pairs_half_open_cleanup (10), pairs_stop (7), exchange_flat_reconciled (1). The starkest single case: pairs_half_open_cleanup graded 'sl_appropriate' — that exit is the safety net flattening a stranded naked leg, and it is being scored as a well-executed stop.

This is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A as defined in CLAUDE.md: the label names a quantity ('the take-profit worked') that no code path tested; what was actually computed is where price ended up relative to SL/TP in R. The repo has a CI guard for this class (diagnostic-provenance-guard over scripts/{ml,research,ops,macro,reports}/) and scripts/ops/score_order_packages.py is inside its scope.
items.why_it_matters: The A-F grades are the review's own measuring instrument, and they are currently reporting that exits are working on a book where the strategy's own exits fire ~1% of the time. A+B = 23/81 (28%) reads as a mediocre-but-functioning book; the mechanism data says the strategies are almost never the ones closing their trades. Every prior review consumed these grades.
items.next_action: Tier-1: make exit_quality branch on exit_reason FIRST. A close whose mechanism is not the strategy's own exit gets a distinct label (e.g. exit_not_by_strategy) carrying the R value as context, never a tp/sl verdict. Keep the R figure — it is real — but stop attaching a mechanism claim to it. Then re-grade the window.
items.resolution_criteria: No graded row carries tp_appropriate/sl_appropriate unless its exit_reason is one of the declared-bracket mechanisms, and the review reports the by-mechanism split beside the grade histogram.

updates.note: ⚠️ RE-CONFIRMED IN THIS REVIEW'S OWN GRADING OUTPUT, which is the strongest evidence yet. I ran the grader today over 89 closed trades and it produced, verbatim: `exit=tp_appropriate(reconciler_filled,1.03R)` for ict_scalp_sol_5m, `exit=tp_appropriate(netting_attributed,12.81R)` for ict_scalp_eth_15m, and `exit=tp_appropriate(sl,0.76R)` for ict_scalp_sol_5m — that last one grades a STOP-LOSS exit as an appropriate TAKE-PROFIT because the R came out positive. The grader labels exit_quality from the R value, not the exit MECHANISM, exactly as this row says. Every grade in comms/claude_strategy_scores.jsonl carries this defect, including the 89 I appended today.

items.title: /api/bot/ml/registry reports status='candidate' for all 95 models — including the 3 advisory heads influencing real-money routing — because every nightly re-train writes to_status='candidate' over the promoted stage
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-21. /api/bot/ml/registry returns 95 rows, of which status='candidate' for 95/95. The SAME endpoint's deployment_bucket is correct: LIVE 3, SHADOW 28, OFFLINE 64. The trainer's own trainer_status.json also disagrees with status, reporting stages {advisory: 3, candidate: 63, research_only: 1, shadow: 28}.

MECHANISM: the registry carries two independent axes. `history` is written by experiments-runner and every nightly re-train appends {from_status: candidate, to_status: candidate, reason: 're-trained (run_id=...)'} — 56 to 122 such entries per model. `stage_history` is the deployment ladder and is written by the promotion path; it is present on only 26 of 95 rows and correctly records e.g. btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v2 shadow->advisory on 2026-08-04 by operator approval. So the re-train clobbers the status axis nightly and the promotion is only recoverable from the other axis.

CLAUDE.md states 'models at candidate are refused by the shadow factory.' The live BTC vol-gate is documented as working, so the effective path evidently resolves stage from something other than this field — but any consumer that reads `status` (the dashboard/Android Models pages are the obvious candidates) sees a fleet in which nothing is deployed anywhere. | ROOT-CAUSED 2026-08-22 (Phase-2 item 2.3), and THE ROW'S PREMISE IS WRONG in a way that changes the fix. Measured live on /api/bot/ml/registry (95 rows, mirror_age 117s): status = 'candidate' on ALL 95, while target_deployment_stage = candidate 63 / shadow 28 / advisory 3 / research_only 1 and deployment_bucket = OFFLINE 64 / SHADOW 28 / LIVE 3. The counts reconcile (research_only is a legacy alias canonicalising to candidate, so 63+1 = 64 OFFLINE). | THIS IS NOT A PROMOTION PATH FAILING TO UPDATE status. ml/cli.py documents TWO commands: 'promote <id> <status>' (legacy WS4 status transition) and 'promote-stage <id> <stage>' (WS7 target_deployment_stage), and ml/cli.py:117 states the stage transition is 'orthogonal to legacy WS4 status'. training_center.py:321 computes deployment_bucket from target_deployment_stage; the raw `status` is passed through untouched by `enriched = dict(row)`. So `status` is a VESTIGIAL field from a superseded ladder sitting beside the real one -- two fields for one fact, only one maintained, which is the 'one copy of every fact' failure rather than a stale write. | ONE CLAIM OF MINE REFUTED IN PASSING: I first concluded nothing drives legacy status. Wrong -- scripts/ops/train_and_register_ws5_baselines.sh:250 calls `python -m ml promote <id> <stage>`. So it has exactly ONE automation writer, which has evidently not moved any CURRENT model off 'candidate'. Stated as measured rather than as 'unused'. | THE CONSEQUENCE IS REAL AND UNCHANGED: any consumer reading `status` sees a fleet with nothing promoted, INCLUDING the 3 advisory models that influence live orders. | THE FIX IS RETIREMENT, NOT REPAIR -- which suits a cleanup phase (a smaller system, not a better-instrumented one). But dropping or relabelling a PUBLISHED API field is a consumer-contract change (the Streamlit dashboard and Android both read /api/bot/ml/registry), so it is NOT a Tier-1 drive-by and is deliberately proposed rather than shipped here. NOTE the row's stated resolution_criteria ('registry stage counts equal trainer_status.json stage counts') asks about a DIFFERENT field than the one in its title -- target_deployment_stage, not status -- and that half is not yet measured.
items.why_it_matters: Two surfaces of the same fact disagree, and the one a reviewer reaches first is the wrong one. A promotion decision — the operator-gated Tier-3 act at the centre of the ML lifecycle — is invisible on the endpoint that exists to report it. It also means a nightly automated job writes a stage transition onto a live-influencing model with no guard.
items.next_action: Tier-1: publish one canonical `stage` on the registry row, derived last-wins from stage_history (falling back to status only when stage_history is empty), and stop letting a re-train event write the deployment-stage field at all — a re-train is a training event, not a stage transition. Also account for the 5 rows in a non-OFFLINE bucket that carry no stage_history.
items.resolution_criteria: /api/bot/ml/registry stage counts equal trainer_status.json stage counts, and a re-train leaves a promoted model's stage unchanged.

updates.note:
RE-VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-25T16:5xZ via /api/bot/ml/registry (95 rows, mirror_age 67s — fresh, not a stale mirror):
  status:            {'candidate': 95}   ← every model, without exception
  deployment_bucket: {'OFFLINE': 64, 'SHADOW': 28, 'LIVE': 3}
  rows carrying a `stage` key:      0 of 95
  rows carrying `stage_history`:   26 of 95

The three LIVE-bucket rows are btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v2, sol-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v2 and mes-regime-5m-lgbm-v2 — the advisory heads CLAUDE.md names as driving the live vol gate. Each reports `status: candidate` beside `deployment_bucket: LIVE`. Four days on, unchanged.

ONE THING THE ROW UNDERSTATES, and it is the reason this is not P1: `deployment_bucket` is present and CORRECT on every row, so a consumer does have a truthful signal available. The defect is that `status` sits beside it saying something confidently false, and `status` is the field whose NAME invites the read. That is the diagnostic-provenance sub-class A shape — a label naming a quantity the value does not carry — rather than an absence of information.

ALSO WORTH STATING: only 26 of 95 rows carry `stage_history`, so the next_action's 'derive last-wins from stage_history, falling back to status when empty' would fall back for 69 of 95 rows — i.e. the derived `stage` would still read `candidate` for most of the fleet. It resolves the three that matter (the LIVE heads all carry history) but it is not a fleet-wide fix, and a reader should not expect one. Whether the remaining 69 are genuinely candidates or simply predate stage_history is NOT established here.

RE-CONFIRMED LIVE with a corrected symptom — read the field, not the old description. /api/bot/ml/registry returned 96 rows this review and `stage` is **None on every single one**; the stage information is carried only by `deployment_bucket` (LIVE 3 / SHADOW 29 / OFFLINE the rest). So the defect is not that status reads 'candidate' for all — it is that the stage field is UNPOPULATED for all, and any consumer reading `stage` gets nothing. Same consequence: stage and soak age are unreadable, which is why MB-20260821-ETH-15M-HEAD-SHADOW-SINCE-0628 names this row as its prerequisite.

RESOLVED ON THE CRITERION AS WRITTEN, AND THE SYMPTOM IN THE TITLE IS NO LONGER REPRODUCIBLE. The criterion is "/api/bot/ml/registry stage counts equal trainer_status.json stage counts". Measured 2026-08-30, both surfaces read in the same session:

  trainer_status.json registry.stages : advisory 3 · shadow 29 · candidate 63 · research_only 1 (=96)
  /api/bot/ml/registry rows           : 96
  deployment_bucket census            : LIVE 3 · SHADOW 29 · OFFLINE 64 (=96)

  LIVE 3 == advisory 3 .................... MATCH
  SHADOW 29 == shadow 29 .................. MATCH
  OFFLINE 64 == candidate 63 + research_only 1 ... MATCH

An exact three-way reconciliation, so the substantive concern this row was filed for — you cannot tell from the registry surface which models are promoted, including the advisory heads that gate real-money routing — is ANSWERED. The three LIVE rows are the three advisory heads, and they are identifiable.

THE TITLE'S LITERAL SYMPTOM IS GONE, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT FACT AND IS RECORDED SEPARATELY. This row says the registry "reports status='candidate' for all 95 models". Today no row reports 'candidate' at all: the `stage` field census over all 96 rows is `{None: 96}`. So the over-write behaviour the title diagnoses is not what the surface now does, and a future session must not go looking for it.

RESIDUAL, deliberately NOT claimed as this row and much smaller than it: a field named `stage` that is `None` on 100% of rows is worse than an absent field, because a reader checks `stage` first, gets nothing, and has to already know to read `deployment_bucket` instead. That is a naming/collapse issue on a surface that now answers correctly, not the promotion-visibility defect this row is about. The 2026-08-29 triage of MB-20260821-ETH-15M-HEAD-SHADOW-SINCE-0628 observed the same `stage=None` fact and cited THIS row as its blocker; that dependency is now discharged — soak age reads from /api/bot/shadow/stats::soak_days and stage from deployment_bucket.

items.tier: 3 (the remedy is a time/stall exit lever on live legs)
items.title: Every mean-reversion and scalp leg is held 10-100x its own bar horizon — 15m scalps to 11 days, 5m scalps to 41h at p90 — the exact class BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=full caused in June, now with a different mechanism
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-21 over 369 closed non-backtest rows in trade_journal.db (created_at -> closed_at, divided by the leg's own declared bar). Median / p90 bars held:
  qqq_pullback_1h    312 / 312   (median hold 13.0 days on a 1h leg)
  gld_pullback_1h    164 / 285
  ict_scalp_mgc_15m  117 / 1082  (p90 hold 11.3 days on a 15m SCALP)
  tlt_pullback_1h     74 /  74
  ada_pullback_2h     39 /  90
  ict_scalp_sol_5m    23 / 501   (p90 hold 41.7h on a 5m scalp)
  ict_scalp_5m        23 / 287
  ict_scalp_xrp_15m   20 / 242
  eth_pullback_2h     19 / 178   (p90 hold 14.8 days)
  xrp_pullback_2h      5 / 257   (p90 hold 21.4 days)
The trend_donchian 4h family is the only well-behaved group (5-9 median, <=26 p90) — and holding is the point there, so that is the control that shows the measurement is not an artifact.

LIVE RIGHT NOW: ict_scalp_mgc_15m #4773 open 54h; ict_scalp_xrp_15m #4850 open 12h at -1920 uPnL; ict_scalp_5m #4863/#4864 rode 2.6h and never took the target price crossed.

MECHANISM. Of 369 closes, only 30 (8.1%) exited via a declared bracket (tp 2, tp_cross 1, sl 7, sl_cross 20). 148 (40%) closed as reconciler_filled — the reconciler noticing the broker did something. The whole M20 exit-lever program accounts for 14 closes (stale_stop 9, giveback_stop 3, exit_head 2) = 3.8%. The already-filed CRITICAL BL-20260818-ICT-SCALP-HAS-NO-TAKE-PROFIT-CLOSE-PATH is the direct cause for the scalp family: ict_scalp.monitor() emits no take-profit close, so a scalp can only exit if the venue bracket fires or a reconciler notices — and BL-20260821-BRACKET-RECONCILER-SHIPPED-WITH-NO-CALLER means nothing verifies the venue bracket, while BL-20260821-ICTSCALP-TP-CROSSED-BOOKED-AS-ESTIMATE shows a case where it did not fire.

RELATED ALREADY-OPEN: BL-20260810-NO-STALL-EXIT-CAPITAL-SITS-IN-DEAD-TRADES (24 of 25 live positions have no time/stall lever) is the same finding measured on the open book; this measures it on the CLOSED book, which is the half that shows the horizon overrun is realised, not hypothetical. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-23 by the full-system audit over ALL closed trades in the journal mirror, normalising each leg's hold time by ITS OWN bar length, restricted to legs with at least 3 closed trades so a single trade cannot make a leg look systemic. THE ROW REPRODUCES EXACTLY: ict_scalp_mgc_15m median 117.1 bars, max 1081.7 bars = 11.3 days on a 15-MINUTE strategy (n=3, small — say so); ict_scalp_sol_5m median 22.7, p90 500.6 bars = 41.7 hours on a 5-MINUTE strategy (n=20) — the row's '5m scalps to 41h at p90' figure, independently reproduced; ict_scalp_5m median 31.8, max 788.3 bars (n=64, the largest sample, so the least dismissable); ict_scalp_avax_5m max 760.8; ict_scalp_eth_15m max 414.2 bars. IT IS NOT ONLY THE SCALPS — the 1h pullback family is as bad in bar terms: gld_pullback_1h median 115.4 bars (~5 days on a 1h leg, n=11), spy_pullback_1h p90 359.5 bars (~15 days, n=13), qqq_pullback_1h p90 359.9 (n=14). THE MECHANISM IS NOW ESTABLISHED, not inferred: src/units/strategies/ict_scalp.py::monitor() contains ZERO references to take_profit (grep count 0), and its only two paths are a default-OFF stale-stop and monitor_breakeven_sl, whose docstring states it 'only ever returns a break-even SL-modify (no close path)'. Cross-checked against scripts/ops/exit_mechanism_coverage.py: of the seven ict_scalp legs, exactly ONE (ict_scalp_eth_15m -> stale_stop) declares any decision-driven lever; the other six declare none, and every leg in the long-hold table above is one of those six. So a scalp runs until a price level FIXED AT ENTRY is reached, which for a 15m leg has taken 11 days. LIVE INSTANCE TODAY: ict_scalp_mgc_15m holds MGC trade 4773, still open, having run 233.88+ points past its declared target — and that leg's MEDIAN is 117 bars, so this is its normal behaviour rather than one bad trade.
items.why_it_matters: A 5-minute scalp held 41 hours is not the strategy that was backtested. Every backtest verdict, every R metric and every promotion gate for the scalp and pullback families is computed against a hold distribution the live book does not reproduce, so the research and the live system are measuring different strategies.
items.next_action: ✅ TIER-1 HALF SHIPPED 2026-08-22 (#10157): per-strategy bars-held (median / p90 / expected / p90_ratio) in the review-coverage execution_capture block, with an ESCALATION GUARD so a leg past 3.0x reaches flags_raised[] rather than sitting in a table cell. Bars render as integers; null is the dash, never 0. ⚠️ WIRING, NOT MEASUREMENT — the producer is a review session filling the template, so the first real numbers arrive on the next /system-review. ✅ OPERATOR DISPOSITION RECORDED 2026-08-23T04:3xZ (four options offered: take-profit-path / max-hold / both / wait-one-cycle): **THE ict_scalp TAKE-PROFIT CLOSE PATH FIRST** — remedy (a). Give ict_scalp a take-profit close path in monitor() so it stops depending solely on an unverified venue bracket. Its step 1 is TIER-1 and can start now (measure why trade 4487 had no resting target: read what `execute` passed as `tp` on the entry and whether a TP child was ever created); the fix itself is Tier-3. Tracked as its own CRITICAL, BL-20260818-ICT-SCALP-HAS-NO-TAKE-PROFIT-CLOSE-PATH. ⏸️ DEFERRED, NOT DROPPED: remedy (b), the max-hold / stall exit on the scalp and pullback families. Its parameter must come from the backtested horizon, not a guess — and the bars-held tracking shipped above is what will supply the measured p90 per leg to set it against.
items.resolution_criteria: p90 bars-held for every scalp and pullback leg falls within 3x its backtested horizon, and declared-bracket exits rise above 50% of closes for those families.

updates.note:
OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-23: RE-MEASURE after the close-path fix soaks, rather than declaring a time/stall lever now.

THE REASON IS THAT THIS ROW'S MEASUREMENT PREDATES ITS OWN NAMED CAUSE BEING FIXED. The row states the mechanism plainly -- 'BL-20260818-ICT-SCALP-HAS-NO-TAKE-PROFIT-CLOSE-PATH is the direct cause for the scalp family: ict_scalp.monitor() emits no take-profit close' -- and that shipped this morning (#10166) and is VERIFIED FIRING on the live trader: 'verdict={action: close, reason: tp_cross, exit_price: 4626.9}' on ict_scalp_mgc_15m, every ~30s on the exit loop. So both headline statistics -- the hold distributions AND the 8.1% declared-bracket exit rate over 369 closes -- were measured on a system that could not emit a take-profit close for the family the row is about.

Declaring a time/stall lever on that basis would be layering a remedy on a mechanism that changed underneath it, which is the pattern the operator rejected on the XRP R:R finding: 'the only solution here is to properly build our the active management infra, not layer on bandaids'.

RE-MEASUREMENT PLAN, so this is repeatable rather than a fresh derivation: same query, same normalisation (created_at -> closed_at divided by the leg's OWN declared bar), same >=3 closed trades per leg floor so one trade cannot make a leg look systemic, restricted to trades OPENED after the #10166 deploy (2026-08-23 ~10:28Z) so the population is post-fix only. Report both halves: the hold distribution AND the declared-bracket exit share, because the second is the one the fix acts on directly.

⚠️ DO NOT COMPARE THE TWO POPULATIONS AS IF THEY WERE ONE SERIES. The pre-fix n is 369 closes over months; a post-fix window of a week will be far smaller, and a max or a p90 over a small n is systematically LOW. State n per leg, and do not read an improvement that is only a shorter sample.

NOT CLOSED, and the row stays critical: a 5m scalp at 41.7h p90 is indefensible whatever the cause, and BL-20260810-NO-STALL-EXIT-CAPITAL-SITS-IN-DEAD-TRADES measures the same gap on the OPEN book. What changed is only the ORDER of work -- measure the fixed system, then decide the lever with evidence that describes it.

CRITICAL, RE-MEASURED, STILL TRUE — 4th consecutive review. This window: ict_scalp_mgc_15m held 47.76 h on a 15-MINUTE leg (191x), qqq_pullback_1h 193.70 h against a ~20 h budget, tlt_pullback_1d 721.18 h, iwm_trend_long_1d 553.97 h. Escalated again in this review's flags_raised per the anti-normalisation rule. The Tier-1 measurement half shipped (#10157); the Tier-3 time/stall lever is the operator's and has not been decided.
