items.tier: 2 (diagnosis is read-only; the fix touches sizing)
items.title: ict_scalp_avax_5m sized ~34,000 AVAX against a venue maximum of 22,000 and was exchange-rejected 20 times — the sizer has no venue-max clamp on this path
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-21. 20 rows carry 'RuntimeError: Order submission failed for AVAXUSDT: The number of contracts exceeds maximum limit allowed: too large, order_qty:3399790000000 > max_qty:2200000000000 (ErrCode: 10001)', on bybit_1 between 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-14, at position_size 33,997.9 / 34,497.3 / 34,502.7 / 34,526.3 — i.e. ~1.55x the venue cap, consistently.

This relates to the already-open BL-20260814-VENUE-MAX-NONE-CANNOT-SAY-WE-COULD-NOT-LOOK (legalize_qty collapses 'the venue published no maximum' with 'we could not look'): a clamp that cannot distinguish those two states will not clamp when the lookup fails.

CONTEXT THAT MAKES IT WORTH MORE THAN ITS REJECT COUNT: ict_scalp_avax_5m is the single worst paper strategy over 30d at -7,620.73 across 20 trades (45.0% win). A leg that is sized 1.55x the venue maximum when it is refused is filling near the cap when it is not.

--- 2026-08-22 (s4-pairs-control): the Tier-1 half of next_action is ANSWERED, and TWO OF THIS ROW'S OWN CLAIMS ARE CORRECTED. ---

WHICH BASIS PRODUCED 34k: notes.margin_basis, on the two rows recent enough to carry the stamp (it shipped 2026-08-13), says the same thing twice:
  {'kind':'venue_available','basis_usd':81229.86,'leverage':3,'buffer':0.9,'max_qty_by_margin':33997.92498997939} -> position_size 33997.9
  {'kind':'venue_available','basis_usd':91800.28,'leverage':3,'buffer':0.9,'max_qty_by_margin':33265.434696282246} -> position_size 33265.4
position_size EQUALS max_qty_by_margin to full float precision on both. risk.py:1232 clamps qty down to that cap when the risk-based size exceeds it, so THE EMITTED SIZE IS THE MARGIN CEILING ITSELF, not a risk-derived number. The basis is broker truth (venue_available), so the ceiling is correctly computed -- the defect is that a ceiling is shipped as a size, with a second ceiling downstream that is inert.

THE VENUE-MAX CLAMP EXISTS, IS WIRED, AND DID NOT FIRE -- NINE DAYS AFTER IT SHIPPED. qty_legalize.legalize_qty clamps to maxOrderQty and is called with prefer_live=True at execute.py:1346; it landed 2026-08-13T10:39:59Z (87af13f5). At 2026-08-22T10:30:58Z the trader sent AVAXUSDT qty 33,265.4 and Bybit bounced it (ErrCode 10001, max_qty:2200000000000 = 22,000). The clamp's own WARNING ('_submit_order: ... EXCEEDS venue maxOrderQty ... clamped to ...') is ABSENT from the journal window, so the branch was not entered and venue_max was None. The venue's own error proves a maximum EXISTS -- so None means the lookup did not resolve one. That is BL-20260814-VENUE-MAX-NONE-CANNOT-SAY-WE-COULD-NOT-LOOK firing again, eight days after its own instance (trade 4640, 2026-08-14).

WHICH of the three paths to None was taken is NOT DETERMINABLE FROM THE JOURNAL, and that is the finding rather than a gap in the investigation: _live_lot_rule returning None on an empty response logs NOTHING; _from_live raising logs at DEBUG; _from_profile succeeding returns venue_max=None BY CONSTRUCTION and logs nothing. The success path never records which source answered. No 'lot_rule live lookup failed' WARNING appears in the window, which rules out only the one path that does log.

CORRECTION 1 -- COUNT AND WINDOW. This row says '20 rows ... between 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-14' and precision.py's comment says '18 of 22'. MEASURED 2026-08-22 (filter_state asserted 'applied'): 21 exchange_rejected rows on ict_scalp_avax_5m / bybit_1, spanning 2026-07-30T13:47:23Z -> 2026-08-22T10:30:59Z. A far wider window than any of the three recorded counts, and STILL LIVE TODAY.

CORRECTION 2 -- THE 'INVISIBLE HALF' IS NOT SUPPORTED AT THE MEDIAN. This row asserts 'the accepted orders on this leg are sized at or near a venue ceiling'. Measured over accepted ict_scalp_avax_5m rows (status closed/open/orphaned, n=22): min 368.4, p25 2,661.1, MEDIAN 4,574.3 (20.8% of the 22,000 cap), p75 9,137.1, max 21,971.2. Only 2 of 22 (9.1%) exceed 80% of the cap. The claim holds for a small TAIL -- the largest accepted order is 99.87% of the cap -- not generally. Separation is perfect: all 21 rejected > 22,000, all 22 accepted < 22,000.

NOT DONE: Bybit instruments-info could not be queried from the sandbox (CloudFront geo-block on api.bybit.com AND api-demo.bybit.com), stated rather than worked around.

SPLIT 2026-08-22: the STRATEGY half of next_action item (3) -- whether a leg whose risk-derived size routinely exceeds available margin at 3x leverage should be sized that way at all -- is now PB-20260822-AVAX-SCALP-SIZED-OFF-MARGIN-NOT-RISK in the PERFORMANCE backlog, where /performance-review drains it. This row keeps the PLUMBING half (the clamp that does not fire, and the observability gap that makes it unverifiable). WARNING recorded on both: fixing the clamp WITHOUT the strategy decision converts 21 loud venue refusals into 21 silent ceiling-sized fills on the worst-performing leg in the book.
items.why_it_matters: Twenty refused orders is the visible half; the invisible half is that the accepted orders on this leg are sized at or near a venue ceiling, which is not a risk-derived size.
items.next_action: TIER-1 HALF: DONE 2026-08-22 -- the basis is 'venue_available' and position_size == max_qty_by_margin exactly. WHAT REMAINS, and the ORDER matters: (1) OBSERVABILITY FIRST -- every path to venue_max=None is silent or DEBUG and the success path never records which source answered, so no fix can be verified today. legalize_qty already returns `source` on LegalizedQty; log it (and whether a ceiling resolved) on the submit path, or expose it on a diag read. Tier-1. (2) THEN the clamp fix, which belongs to BL-20260814-VENUE-MAX-NONE-CANNOT-SAY-WE-COULD-NOT-LOOK, not here: venue_max must distinguish 'the venue published no maximum' from 'we could not look', and the second must not pass through. Tier-2. (3) SEPARATELY, and this is the larger question: a leg whose size is routinely the MARGIN CEILING rather than a risk number is not sized by the risk model at all. ict_scalp_avax_5m is the worst paper strategy over 30d (-7,620.73 / 20 trades / 45.0% win). Whether that leg should be sized off available margin at 3x leverage is a Tier-3 sizing question, not a clamp question.
items.resolution_criteria: Zero ErrCode 10001 rejections on this leg over 30 days, AND a submit-path record (log line or diag field) that names which source resolved the lot rule and whether a ceiling was found -- so a future 'no rejections' reading can be told apart from 'the clamp is still inert and the sizer happened to stay under the cap'. The second clause is load-bearing: 22 of 22 accepted orders were already under the cap without any clamp firing, so absence of rejections alone proves nothing.

updates.note: RE-CONFIRMED: the operator ERROR feed carries 17 `bybit_place_order_failed: The number of contracts exceeds maximum limit` rows across 08-22..08-26. And ict_scalp_avax_5m is the worst paper leg in the 30d cut (17 trades, -$6,804.83, coverage 0.0588) — consistent with PB-20260822-AVAX-SCALP-SIZED-OFF-MARGIN-NOT-RISK. Two rows, one sizer defect: the size is the margin/venue ceiling rather than a risk number.

items.title: The Bybit bracket audit grades 5 dimensions and NONE of them is price — the same blind spot broker_bracket_reconcile was built to close on the IB side
items.detail:
broker_bracket_reconcile.py exists BECAUSE protection_coverage was blind to price: it was corrected twice (boolean -> quantity, then one-sided -> two-sided) and still returned no price, so a position graded fully stop-covered while its only resting stop sat 69 ticks from the declared level. That tool is now scheduled (cron 40 */6 * * *, PR landed 2026-08-21) — but it is IB-ONLY: 'per open journal trade on an IB account'.

The Bybit sibling, the bybit-bracket-audit system-action, was run live this session (issue #10084) and its own roll-up names its five graded dimensions: sl_coverage, over_coverage, target_present, tracked_legs_alive, journal_qty_backed — and closes with 'Nothing outside those dimensions was checked.' None of the five is PRICE. It reports the leg triggers (SL 72504.9 / TP 78070.7 on BTCUSDT) beside the journal's declared SL, so the data is right there in the output and simply is not compared.

This is not hypothetical on Bybit either: real-money trade 4863 had its declared TP (75698.52) crossed by a 75731.20 bar high and did not exit (BL-20260821-ICTSCALP-TP-CROSSED-BOOKED-AS-ESTIMATE). Whether a resting TP leg existed at that price is exactly the question no Bybit surface answers.
items.why_it_matters: Two venues, one failure class, one of them now watched every 6h and the other not at all. The half that is watched is ib_paper; the half that is NOT watched is where the real money trades.
items.next_action: Tier-1: add a price comparison to scripts/ops/bybit_bracket_audit.py — per open journal row, compare the resting leg trigger against trades.stop_loss / take_profit_1 with a venue-tick tolerance, and report a divergence as its own graded dimension so the roll-up's 'clean across ALL N dimensions' line stays honest about what it checked. Reuse broker_bracket_reconcile's tolerance semantics rather than inventing a second definition.
items.resolution_criteria: bybit-bracket-audit grades a price dimension, its roll-up names it, and a planted divergence is shown to FAIL the check before a clean result is trusted.

updates.note: Re-validated and now PARTLY ANSWERABLE: /api/diag/bybit_open_orders does expose per-position stop_loss/take_profit and per-order trigger_price/price, so the price axis is READABLE even though the AUDIT still does not grade on it. Wiring the audit to the surface is the fix. Same shape as BL-20260820-PROTECTION-COVERAGE-IS-PRICE-BLIND on the IB side.

items.title: pull_and_deploy.sh's closing line says 'ict-trader-live.service bounced' on the no-op path, where nothing was restarted
items.detail:
⚠️ THIS ROW REPLACES A WRONGER ONE, WHICH NEVER MERGED. The earlier version carried a different id and severity high, claiming that pull-and-deploy can NEVER deploy a unit-file-only change because its fast-path exits before install_systemd_units.sh. That central claim is FALSE and was corrected before the row landed. The retracted id is deliberately NOT written here: it exists in no backlog, and a doc naming it would read as 'tracked by' a row that does not exist — which is what artifact-validity-guard refused, correctly, when this retraction first tried to cite it. Keeping the correction visible because the reasoning error is the reusable part: I inferred a system-wide defect from one no-op run WITHOUT first checking whether some other actor had already done the work.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh:273-276 does exit 0 before install_systemd_units.sh (line 351) when the running SHA already equals origin/main. But ict-git-sync.timer runs the SAME script, and it branches on the SHA MOVING, not on which files changed — so when it pulls a commit it takes the FULL path and installs units. By the time a session dispatches pull-and-deploy, git-sync has usually already deployed, and the fast-path is then CORRECT: it is reporting work already done, not skipping it.

MEASURED, and this is what refuted the original row. PR #10088 (9f8aff9) changed deploy/ict-exchange-fills-pull.timer from daily 00:20 to hourly *:20. journalctl on ict-exchange-fills-pull.service shows: 2026-08-20T00:24 Finished (daily), 2026-08-21T00:21 Starting (daily), then **2026-08-21T13:27:30 Starting** — a fire that is not on a daily 00:20 schedule at all. git-sync installed the new timer at ~13:27, the reload fired it, and the trader restarted at 13:28:07 as part of the same deploy. The hourly timer WAS live roughly 15 minutes before I claimed it could not be.

WHAT SURVIVES, and it is narrow. On the no-op path scripts/ops/pull_and_deploy.sh closes with '[pull_and_deploy] Deploy finished — HEAD unchanged (already at origin/main); ict-trader-live.service bounced.' No bounce occurs on that path: measured on issue #10098, the journal shows python[1550533] at 13:28:51 AND at 13:29:00, the same PID either side of the claimed restart. That is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A — a label naming an action no code path took. It is the reason a reader (me) concluded the deploy had restarted the service when it had not, and it is worth fixing on its own terms even though the deployment it describes was not actually broken. Contrast the full path, which prints the honest 'HEAD <a> → <b>; ict-trader-live.service active.'

REAL RESIDUAL RISK, stated so it is not lost with the retraction: a commit that changes ONLY a unit file and is dispatched via pull-and-deploy BEFORE git-sync's next run would take the full path and be fine; the exposure is narrower than 'always' and I have not constructed a case where the units genuinely fail to install. If one exists it needs its own row with its own evidence, not this one. | RESOLVED 2026-08-22 (#10117, Phase-2 item 2.7). The row's premise was CHECKED against the code before fixing, not assumed: scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh:234 states it restarts ONLY when HEAD moved, and exits early at ':274' with 'nothing to deploy' -- so the wrapper's 'HEAD unchanged ... bounced' asserted a restart that had deliberately not happened. It is worse than the row stated, in BOTH directions: the deploy script drives its decision off runtime_logs/deployed_sha.txt (RUNTIME_BASE) and off the CONTENT of the diff, neither of which the wrapper reads, so PRE!=POST can ALSO mean no restart when the diff is docs-only (BL-20260529-002) -- which is most of the 2026-08 programme's merges. Fixed by MEASURING the asserted fact rather than inferring it: a bounced unit has a new ActiveEnterTimestampMonotonic and a new MainPID. Three states, never collapsed -- bounced / not_bounced / unknown -- so an unreadable systemctl cannot read as 'did not restart'. bounce_state also rides the audit JSON for the diag relay. Two read-only systemctl calls; the deploy's behaviour is unchanged. tests/test_pull_and_deploy_bounce_claim.py, SHOWN TO FIRE: 4 failed pre-fix / 4 passed post-fix.
evidence: journalctl ict-exchange-fills-pull.service: 08-20T00:24, 08-21T00:21 (daily), then 08-21T13:27:30 — the hourly schedule was loaded

issue #10102 log (full path): 'Refreshing systemd units from deploy/', 'install_systemd_units: daemon-reload', 'restarted ict-trader-live.service', journal PID 1554351 -> 1558534 with Stopping/Started
issue #10098 log (no-op path): 'nothing to deploy', exit 0, wrapper printed 'ict-trader-live.service bounced', journal shows python[1550533] at both 13:28:51 and 13:29:00
scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh:273-276 vs :351 — the fast-path exit is real; its consequence was mis-stated
items.resolution_criteria:
1. scripts/ops/pull_and_deploy.sh's no-op closing line stops claiming a bounce. It should say what happened — e.g. 'HEAD unchanged (already at origin/main); nothing deployed, service left running' — branching on the real outcome rather than emitting one fixed sentence for both paths.
2. A test asserts the two paths emit DIFFERENT closing text, so the no-op message can never again be the same sentence as the success message.
3. Verified by dispatching pull-and-deploy when the VM is already at origin/main and reading the closing line.

items.title: Nothing reports a timer's SCHEDULE — only active/inactive — so a timer whose OnCalendar changed and was never reloaded is indistinguishable from one that was
items.detail:
Every surface that reports systemd timers reports STATE, never SCHEDULE:
  - /api/diag/services -> {unit, state, sub_state, active_enter_iso}. ict-exchange-fills-pull.timer reads 'active' whether it fires hourly or daily.
  - scripts/ops/status_check.sh -> systemctl list-units + list-unit-files. Neither prints NEXT or LEFT.
  - `systemctl list-timers`, the one command that shows the next elapse, appears in the repo only in enable_insights_generator.sh, inspect_insights.sh, resume_autoheal.sh and install_trainer_git_sync.sh — each scoped to its own single unit, none reachable as a general read.

So the question 'is this timer actually on the schedule the repo declares?' has no answer from a session, and the answer that IS available ('active') is the one that looks reassuring in both cases. This is the collapsed-state shape at the ops surface: 'the schedule we intended' and 'the schedule systemd loaded' are different facts and only the first is readable.

IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL, AND IT COST THIS SESSION A WRONG FINDING. Unable to read the loaded schedule, I inferred from one no-op deploy that the hourly timer had never been installed, and filed a high-severity row saying so. It was false — journalctl later showed ict-exchange-fills-pull.service firing at 2026-08-21T13:27:30, i.e. NOT on the daily 00:20 schedule, so ict-git-sync had installed it correctly ~15 minutes before I claimed it could not have. A missing read surface does not merely hide failures; it manufactures phantom ones, because the reviewer substitutes inference for the reading they cannot take. The hourly ict-exchange-fills-pull.timer shipped in 9f8aff9 could not be confirmed live from any read available to this session — the best available check was BEHAVIOURAL (watch journalctl for the service firing at :20), which costs an hour and only detects the failure after the window it was meant to protect.

This also undercuts the Tier-2 contract itself, which is 'ship AND verify the post-state'. For any timer change the verify half is currently unperformable.
evidence: /api/diag/services returns state only; ict-exchange-fills-pull.timer = 'active' with no schedule field
scripts/ops/status_check.sh: systemctl list-units + list-unit-files, no list-timers
grep list-timers across scripts/ -> 4 hits, all single-unit and purpose-scoped
2026-08-21: the hourly timer from 9f8aff9 could not be confirmed loaded by any available read
items.resolution_criteria:
1. status_check.sh emits `systemctl list-timers --all 'ict-*.timer'` (NEXT / LEFT / LAST / UNIT), so a schedule is readable wherever status-check is.
2. Better, and what actually closes it for a relay-bound session: a /api/diag/timers route returning per allowlisted timer {unit, on_calendar (from systemctl show -p TimersCalendar), next_elapse, last_trigger, state}. Read-only, no socket, Tier-1 — the same shape as /api/diag/services beside it.
3. The route must distinguish 'we could not read this timer' from 'this timer has no calendar' rather than returning null for both — the collapsed-state rule this row is an instance of.
4. Verified by changing a timer's OnCalendar, deploying, and confirming the surface shows the NEW value directly — WITHOUT falling back to journalctl archaeology on when the service last fired, which is the only method available today and is what made this row's own sibling get filed wrong.
items.resolution:
RESOLVED — `/api/diag/timers` exists (`src/web/api/routers/diag.py:1076`) and reports SCHEDULE, not just state. Verified live 2026-08-25T11:1xZ: 16 timers, each row carrying `unit`, `state`, `on_calendar`, `on_monotonic`, `next_elapse_realtime`/`next_elapse_monotonic`, `last_trigger`, and a `read_state` so an unreadable timer is distinguishable from one with no schedule. Sample: `ict-git-sync.timer` — `schedule_state: monotonic`, `on_calendar: null`, `on_monotonic: '{ OnBootUSec=2min ; next_elapse=2min }'`, last trigger 2026-08-25 11:06:11 UTC.

The `schedule_state` field is the load-bearing half: MOST of these timers are MONOTONIC, so a surface reporting only `next_elapse_realtime` would return null for them and read identically to a timer with no schedule at all.

items.title: docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json is one shared mutable JSON array that every session appends to -- concurrent sessions collide on it, and a hand-resolution has ALREADY silently reverted content once
items.detail:
OBSERVED 2026-08-21 across two concurrent sessions (spsxq6, dcf5220b) in one morning.

The file is a single JSON array (770 rows, ~3.9 MB, ~20.7k lines) that every session appends to or edits in place. Same structural shape as BL-20260821-AUTOMERGE-TRIGGER-IS-A-SINGLE-SHARED-FILE: one shared file, N writers. That row's fix (a per-request directory) does NOT apply here, because these are durable records rather than transient requests -- hence a separate row.

MEASURED, and stated precisely because I first got the count wrong myself: TWO merges conflicted on it on 2026-08-21 (#10088 and #10101, both dcf5220b), not three. My own #10100 did NOT conflict. I had told the coordination board 'three consecutive contentions' and corrected it in the merge-slot claim -- an unverified count in the direction that makes a problem look worse is still an unverified count.

WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A SHRUG -- the risk is not merge friction, it is SILENT DATA LOSS. BL-20260814-HAND-RESOLVED-BACKLOG-MERGE-SILENTLY-REVERTED-SIX-ITEMS-INCLUDING-A-RESOLUTION records a hand resolution of this exact file that took one side wholesale and silently reverted SIX items another session had edited, one of them a RESOLUTION. That row is still kept_open. A conflict here is resolved by hand, in a 20k-line file, under time pressure, by a session that wants to merge -- and 'no conflict' does not mean 'nothing lost' either: a clean rebase can still drop rows when the unit of change is one giant array.

THE MITIGATION IS KNOWN AND COSTS NOTHING, and both sessions converged on it independently: cut the branch FRESH from the current main rather than merging main into an existing branch. For an append-mostly file that removes the conflict entirely (verified: #10100 rebased onto #10101's main with zero conflict), and it also avoids inheriting the auto-merge trigger. It is a habit, though, not a mechanism -- nothing enforces it and nothing detects a lossy resolution.

NOT PROPOSING A SPLIT OF THE FILE. That would break every consumer (the review skills, check_backlog_refs, check_allow_degraded, the coherence guard) for a problem that is currently costing minutes, not correctness. The cheap durable win is a DETECTOR, in the shape this repo already uses everywhere else.

PROVENANCE NOTE ON THAT CITATION, because it is an instance of the same family this row is about: I first cited the id in TRUNCATED form, having copied it from a coordination-board comment rather than reading the backlog. artifact-validity-guard rejected it — correctly, since the truncated id resolves to nothing and so read as 'tracked by' a row nobody filed. Second truncated-id rejection of this session; the first was the CI-fanout row BL-20260806-CI-FANOUT-AMPLIFIES-ACTIONS-OUTAGES, cited without its trailing slug. A cited id from another session's prose is a CLAIM, not a reference, until it is resolved against the file.

AND THE GUARD THEN CAUGHT THIS NOTE ITSELF: the first draft of this paragraph wrote that earlier truncation out in full as an example, which is just another id resolving to nothing, so the note about dangling ids dangled. Describe a bad id; do not spell one. The same shape hit a concurrent session's retraction the same morning, which named the id it was retracting.

UPDATE 2026-08-23 (bracket-expectations-session) — RECURRED, MEASURED AGAIN, AND A PARTIAL TOOL SHIPPED.

THREE conflicts on this file in ~85 minutes (19:30Z-20:55Z) across TWO of my PRs (#10183 at 834+12+4, #10198 at 839+7+7, then BOTH again at 846+3+N). Every one was two sides appending DISJOINT rows -- no disagreement about content. So the 2026-08-21 observation of two conflicts in one morning was not a busy day; it is the steady state whenever branches stay open.

STATE THE POPULATION: those are conflicts on MY branches only. I did not measure how many other sessions' branches conflicted in the same window, so this is a lower bound on the rate, not the rate.

SHIPPED (partial): scripts/ops/backlog_union_merge.py -- a three-way union that MEASURES both sides before writing, ASSERTS every row from both survives verbatim after, preserves ensure_ascii=False so it cannot reformat and re-attribute unrelated rows, and REFUSES (exit 2) rather than guessing on a DIVERGENT both-side edit, a duplicate new id, or a deletion on either side. 14/14 selftest wired into artifact-validity-guard. Used to resolve two of the three conflicts above.

IT DOES NOT MEET THIS ROW'S CRITERIA, and should not be read as closing it: the criterion is a CI check that fails a PR whose merge-base row set is not a SUBSET of the result. The tool prevents a lossy resolution at RESOLVE time; it does not DETECT one at review time, and a session that reaches for `--ours` never invokes it. The criteria stand unchanged.

⚠️ CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS. I initially filed a SEPARATE row (dated 2026-08-23, titled 'review backlogs conflict on every concurrent branch', filed then removed as a duplicate before it ever landed on main -- deliberately not cited by id here, since an id that resolves to nothing is what this guard family exists to stop) asserting that 'the durable fix is one-file-per-row storage'. This row already argues the opposite, with a reason I had not read: splitting breaks every consumer for a problem costing minutes rather than correctness. I proposed a contradicting fix without checking whether the subject was already owned -- which is the precedent-over-canon failure the generation-discipline rule names. The row's position stands; mine was uninformed, not a counter-argument.

ALSO UNAPPLIED BY ME: this row's zero-cost mitigation -- cut the branch FRESH from current main rather than merging main in. I merged main in, three times. Had I read this row first, two of the three conflicts would not have happened.
resolution_criteria: A CI check that fails a PR touching any shared docs/claude/ JSON register (the three *-backlog.json files AND OPEN-ITEMS.json -- scope widened 2026-08-30 after two conflicts on OPEN-ITEMS.json, which the original *-backlog.json glob does not match) when the merge-base row set is not a SUBSET of the resulting row set -- i.e. it detects a resolution that DROPPED a row, which is the failure mode BL-20260814 actually suffered. Row count alone is insufficient: an add plus a drop nets to zero.

It must carry a failure-path self-test (plant a dropped row, assert non-zero) and be registered so check_selftest_wiring.py can verify its covering path, matching the workflow-catalog / api-tier-policy pattern.
The cut-fresh-from-main habit written down wherever the merge protocol lives, so it is guidance rather than folklore two sessions happened to discover on the same morning.

updates.note: ⚠️ THE HIGHEST-RISK ROW FOR THIS SESSION SPECIFICALLY, and I want it recorded. I rewrote this file today across five triage passes covering 483 open rows while a concurrent session was merging to main (#10412 landed mid-review). A single shared mutable JSON array with no per-row locking makes that a real conflict surface — and BL-20260814-HAND-RESOLVED-BACKLOG-MERGE-SILENTLY-REVERTED-SIX-ITEMS-INCLUDING-A-RESOLUTION is the recorded instance of it going wrong. I mitigated with byte-exact round-trips and frequent commits; that is discipline, not a mechanism.

RECURRED 2026-08-30, AND ON A FILE THIS ROW'S NAMED REMEDY DOES NOT COVER. TWO conflicts in ~20 minutes on docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json (against #10450 and #10462, both verified in `git log -- docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json`, not recalled), each costing a ~15-minute CI cycle to re-run. Both were disjoint appends -- no disagreement about content, the same shape this row already records.

THE NEW FINDING IS THE SCOPE GAP, not the recurrence. This row's resolution criterion names `docs/claude/*-backlog.json`. That glob does NOT match OPEN-ITEMS.json (checked with fnmatch, not by eye), so the subset-detector as specified would ship, pass, and leave the file that actually conflicted today unprotected. The criteria below are extended to `docs/claude/*.json` register files rather than a new row being filed, because the defect, the mechanism and the fix are identical -- only the path pattern was too narrow.

AND OPEN-ITEMS.json IS THE WORSE INSTANCE OF THE CLASS, for two reasons this row's original subject does not have. (1) EVERY session is REQUIRED to write it -- CLAUDE.md's session contract says 'End: update docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json' -- so the write rate is ~100% of sessions rather than 'whoever found a bug'. (2) It is 206 lines / 14 items against the backlog's ~21k lines, so two appends land in the same textual neighbourhood and conflict, where two appends to a 21k-line file often do not.

STATE THE POPULATION: 20 commits touch OPEN-ITEMS.json across its entire life (first commit 2026-08-26, so ~5/day over 4 days), against 46 commits on health-review-backlog.json in the last 7 days (~6.6/day). Comparable write rates; the difference in conflict pain is the file SIZE, not the traffic.

ALSO NOT APPLIED BY ME, AGAIN: this row's zero-cost mitigation is to cut the branch FRESH from current main rather than merging main in. I merged main in, twice, on a long-lived review branch -- the same thing the 2026-08-23 update records its author doing three times. A mitigation that two sessions in a row read and then did not apply is evidence for the DETECTOR, not for more guidance.

items.opened_by: claude (/system-review 2026-08-21, session dcf5220b; independently observed by session spsxq6)
items.title: A check_suite.completed SUCCESS is per-SUITE, not per-PR — acting on it merges on a partial required set
items.detail:
The four required checks (guards, pytest-run, pytest-collect, repo-inventory) come from SEPARATE check suites. A `check_suite.completed` webhook with conclusion=success therefore says only that ONE suite finished clean — never that the PR is green. The event's own footer says to verify overall state first, and that caveat is doing real work: read as a go-signal it authorises a merge on one of four required checks.

OBSERVED TWICE, INDEPENDENTLY, ON TWO PRs, WITHIN ONE HOUR, which is why this is filed as a mechanism rather than an anecdote:
  - PR #10105 (session spsxq6): four success events at 16:51:06, 16:51:52, 16:52:27 and 17:00:53. After the first three, `pytest-run` was still in flight.
  - PR #10106 (session dcf5220b): four success events on head af0c9c9 (suites 88117636854, 88117658925, 88117659350, 88117658957). On reading `get_check_runs` after the first two, `guards` was still `in_progress`.

Neither session merged on the event — both happened to read `get_check_runs` — but neither avoided it by design, and a session under time pressure would not. The failure mode is merge-on-partial-set, which branch protection catches only if the missing check is required AND has not yet reported; a suite that never starts reports nothing at all.

This is the same family as BL-20260821-NO-READ-SURFACE-FOR-TIMER-SCHEDULE: the surface answers a different question from the one being asked, and the answer looks reassuring either way.

⚠️ SECOND AXIS, MEASURED 2026-09-09 — THE SUITE CAN BELONG TO A SUPERSEDED HEAD, NOT MERELY TO A PARTIAL REQUIRED SET. Everything above concerns suites on the SAME head, where the tell is 'another required check is still running'. There is a second reading error with a different tell and the same root: the event's `head_sha` is not the PR's current head AT ALL. Population: every check webhook one manager session received on 2026-09-09 between 04:09Z and 04:33Z across #11483, #11484 and #11485 — SEVEN of seven named a pre-arming head. One of them delivered `check_run.completed` with conclusion=FAILURE for `guards` on 63c8884f (#11483), which was the documented pr-landing R11 pre-arming state and not a failure at all; the same PR's real head was green and it merged at 04:14:56Z.

⚠️ THE CAUSE IS THIS REPO'S OWN LANDING MACHINERY, WHICH IS WHY IT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN AN OCCASIONAL GITHUB QUIRK. pr-landing R6/R11/R13 require the two-push flow — open the PR by hand, THEN push .github/pr-landing/<slug>.json + the arming file + the merge_slot claim — so every self-landing PR starts TWO check suites. The first suite's completion webhook necessarily arrives AFTER the second push and describes a head that is already superseded. So this is not a rare race: it is expected on EVERY self-landing PR, and the seven-for-seven rate is what that predicts.

WHAT LIMITS THE HARM, STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED: GitHub auto-merge evaluates the true required-check state, not webhooks, so no wrong MERGE follows from this on an armed PR — which is a narrower blast radius than the merge-on-partial-set case above and should not be conflated with it. The damage is to REPORTING and to any hand merge: the manager published a status update describing #11483 as in flight after it had already merged, and separately asserted a wall-clock time it had not read.

THE REMEDY IS UNCHANGED — criterion 1 below (read `get_check_runs` on the head SHA and check each required context BY NAME) covers this axis too, because that call returns the CURRENT head's runs. What this instance adds is that the trap is structural here, that it recurred seven times in one session, and that criteria 1–3 were still unimplemented when it did. ⚠️ It also sharpens the tell a reader should look for: compare the event's `head_sha` against the PR's head from a fresh `pull_request_read`, and compare each check's `started_at` against the last push — a check that started BEFORE the current head existed is grading something else.
evidence: #10105: four check_suite.completed successes 16:51:06 / 16:51:52 / 16:52:27 / 17:00:53; pytest-run still running after the first three
#10106: four successes on head af0c9c9 (suites 88117636854, 88117658925, 88117659350, 88117658957); get_check_runs showed guards in_progress
Both sessions recorded it independently on the coordination board before comparing notes
items.resolution_criteria:
1. State the rule where sessions actually read it — the session-coordination skill's merge protocol step 4 currently says 'confirm all required checks pass' without naming the trap. It should say: read `get_check_runs` on the head SHA and check each required context by name; a `check_suite.completed` success is NEVER sufficient.
2. Add the same line to the PreToolUse merge-guard deny message, which is the one place a session is guaranteed to read before merging in runtimes where hooks load.
3. Verified by a session reporting it followed the rule against a PR where a suite completed green while another was still running — i.e. proven against the live condition, not by re-reading the doc.

updates.note: Re-validated: acting on a per-SUITE success merges on a partial required set. Live corroboration — my PR produced `guards` and `pytest-run` as separate check runs, so a single suite success would not have covered both.

items.opened_by: claude (exit-integrity continuation, session spsxq6, while designing the oci-inventory live falsifier)
items.title: the self-ping dedupe suppressed on a sentinel step that concluded success WITHOUT sending -- the swallowed ping the listener exists to prevent, newly reachable through the fix meant to help
items.why_it_matters: claude-run-failure-alert is the universal backstop for a run dying unobserved. A false suppression is not a missing nicety; it is the failure the workflow was built to make impossible, and it would present as silence -- indistinguishable from a healthy run nobody needed to hear about.
items.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-21 while designing the live falsifier for BL-20260821-OCI-INVENTORY-CRON-UNWATCHED, by reading what the sentinel steps actually do rather than trusting the dedupe's own comment about them. Shipped the same day in #10105, so it was live for roughly four hours.

THE DEFECT. The dedupe stays quiet when a step named `[operator-ping]` concludes `success`, and its comment asserted that meant 'a message really went out'. It did not. Both sentinel steps -- oci-inventory.yml and health-snapshot.yml -- ran `set +e` followed by `PYTHONPATH=. python scripts/notify_session.py alert ... || echo '::warning::telegram notify failed (non-fatal)'`. Under `|| echo` the step exits 0 whatever the send did, so its conclusion is `success` on a Telegram outage exactly as on a delivery. The listener would have read that as 'someone else handled it' and stayed silent.

THE SHARPEST PART: notify_session.py WAS ALREADY HONEST. Its module docstring says real delivery failures 'surface here as exit 1 ... instead of silently exiting 0', and it does. The exit code existed and the caller discarded it -- the written-but-never-read class, one level up from a journal column.

IT ALSO MATTERS THAT THE TWO PATHS USE DIFFERENT CREDENTIALS: the sentinel steps send on CLAUDE_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, the listener on TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN. So the listener is a genuinely independent channel and the fallback can succeed precisely when the self-ping failed. Suppressing on an unverified self-ping throws that away.

THE LIVE FALSIFIER DOES NOT CATCH THIS, deliberately recorded: both its arms run with working secrets, so arm B's send succeeds and its suppression is correct. A green falsifier must not be read as covering this.

FIX. The sentinel moved off the best-effort send onto a separate confirm step gated `if: steps.operator_ping.outcome == 'success'`, in both workflows; the send itself is `continue-on-error` with `set -euo pipefail` and no `||`, so a failed send leaves the confirm step SKIPPED and the listener falls back. The workflow's own conclusion is unchanged, so a notification blip still does not turn a good run red. The listener's comment was corrected -- it had asserted the false thing in writing.

PROOF. tests/test_run_failure_alert_dedupe.py grew 5 tests asserting the sentinel step is not continue-on-error, contains no `||` and no `set +e`, is gated on the outcome of a step that really calls notify_session, and that the send step is not itself marked. Shown to FIRE: run against the pre-fix oci-inventory.yml both new tests fail with the real assertion messages; against the fixed file 14/14 pass. An assertion never observed failing is not evidence.
items.resolution_criteria: Resolved when no [operator-ping] sentinel sits on a step that can conclude success without a confirmed send, and a test fails if one is reintroduced. Both met and the test was shown to fail on the pre-fix code.
items.source: session spsxq6, 2026-08-21, designing the oci-inventory live falsifier

items.opened_by: claude (session spsxq6, building the tolerance evidence for PR #10081)
items.title: /api/diag/ib_open_orders returns read_state=could_not_look with an EMPTY error string -- the three-state is right, but it cannot say WHY it could not look
items.why_it_matters: could_not_look is the state that correctly refuses to report 0 resting legs. But without a reason a reader cannot tell a breaker backoff (transient, self-healing, ignore) from an unset ib_port (config, permanent) from a genuine gateway wedge (act now). Those need three different responses and the field collapses them into one.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-21T17:35:03Z and again at ~17:36Z, both via the Caddy host. `/api/diag/ib_open_orders` returned for ib_paper: read_state 'could_not_look', count null (correct -- never 0), orders null, and `error` as an EMPTY STRING. Two attempts, same result.

WHAT MAKES IT WORTH FILING RATHER THAN SHRUGGING AT: in the SAME window /api/diag/ib_state reported the TRADER's own IB clients healthy -- state 'connected', connected true, likely_wedged false, consecutive_failures 0, breaker closed, last_ok 4.4s and 9.9s old. So the gateway was demonstrably reachable and the read-only diag client still could not look. These are different clients by design (BL-20260706-IBACCTUPDATES-COLLISION: the readonly path is PID-salted and routes positions through reqPositions), so a readonly-side failure while the trader is fine is plausible -- but the route gives a reader nothing to distinguish it from a real outage.

NOT A CORRECTNESS BUG in the state machine: read_state is doing exactly its job by refusing to serve 0. The gap is that `error` is declared and left empty on the one path where it is the whole value of the field -- the written-but-never-populated cousin of written-but-never-read.

IMPACT OBSERVED: it blocked a fourth data point for the PR #10081 stop-price tolerance evidence. Not load-bearing there (the proposal grades inside the trader-side sweep, not this route), but it is the second time this session that a read surface could not answer a question it exists to answer.
items.resolution_criteria: Resolved when a could_not_look response carries a non-empty reason distinguishing at least breaker-open, gateway-unreachable, and not-configured, and a test asserts the reason is populated on each path.

items.title: tick_cost splits candle-fetch cost by timeframe and by consumer, but NOT by venue — so 'how much of fetch.1d is IB?' is unanswerable, and a venue-specific defect can only be bounded
items.detail:
/api/diag/tick_cost publishes two cuts of the same fetch seconds: fetch.<timeframe> and fetchby.<consumer-phase>. They reconcile exactly (measured 2026-08-21: 11467.9s vs 11467.9s, delta 0.0s; 1326 misses + 3170 cache_hit = 4496 = fetchby n), so the instrument is sound - it simply has no VENUE or SYMBOL axis.

WHY THAT COST SOMETHING CONCRETE, today. Wave 0.1 established that IB candle frames cannot be cached at all (BL-20260821-EXIT-EVAL-BREACHES-60S-ON-A-THIRD-OF-CYCLES). The exit loop's fetch.15m line was fully attributable by luck - exactly ONE open 15m package, on an IB-routed symbol - so it yielded a clean measurement (281 fetches / 281 passes, zero hits). fetch.1d was NOT: 2.683 misses/pass mixing MHG/MES (IB) with QLD/SCHA (Alpaca), and no surface can separate them. The saving from the proposed fix therefore had to be reported as a BOUND (15.1s-30.3s per pass) rather than a number, and the ~26.6s ceiling had to stay 'consistent with an IB queue timeout' rather than confirmed - which is the open criterion 1 of BL-20260816-IB-QUEUE-TIMEOUT-EXCEEDS-EXIT-BUDGET, still unmeasurable FROM THIS INSTRUMENT.
checked: src/runtime/tick_cost.py - read the emitter rather than inferring from its output; it keys on timeframe and on the calling phase, never on venue or symbol. Scoped deliberately: the quantity is measurable, this surface just cannot report it, and the fix is a 3-name cut.

A third cut, fetchby.<consumer>.<timeframe>, was considered and rejected once already (CLAUDE.md § tick_cost) because it costs names against _MAX_HOOK_NAMES. A VENUE cut is cheaper than that cross: there are three venues (bybit/alpaca/interactive_brokers), so fetchvenue.* adds at most 3 names, and _MAX_HOOK_NAMES is 64 with the live chain measured at 27 and hook_names_refused at 0.
items.resolution_criteria: /api/diag/tick_cost carries a per-venue fetch cut (e.g. fetchvenue.bybit / .alpaca / .interactive_brokers) whose summed seconds reconcile with sum(fetch.<timeframe>) over the SAME process to within 1% of that sum - the same cross-family check the existing two cuts already pass exactly (measured 2026-08-21, one process started 13:43:00.710052Z, n=281 off-loop passes: fetchby.strategy_monitor_loop 11467.9s vs sum(fetch.*) 11467.9s, delta 0.0s = 0.00% of 11467.9s; counts 1326 misses + 3170 cache_hit = 4496 = fetchby n). hook_names_refused must still read 0, and a session must be able to answer 'what share of fetch.1d is IB?' from one read instead of bounding it.

updates.note: PARTIALLY REFUTED — re-measure before acting. My live tick_cost read shows `fetchvenue.interactive_brokers` (n=107) and `fetchvenue.alpaca` (n=535) in the off-loop hooks, i.e. a VENUE axis now EXISTS. So 'how much of fetch.1d is IB?' looks answerable in a way this row says it is not. State the population before closing: I read the off-loop table on one process.

items.opened_by: claude (wave0-8g7443, Wave 0.1 of the 2026-08-21 work plan)
items.title: _CANDLE_CACHE clears itself WHOLESALE at >512 entries and neither its size nor the flush is reportable anywhere — so a poisoning source can be estimated but never observed
items.detail:
_candle_cache_put (src/runtime/market_data.py) bounds the map by calling .clear() when len(_CANDLE_CACHE) > 512, rather than evicting LRU. CLAUDE.md's CANDLE_CACHE_TTL_MAX_S row already notes in passing that 'a wholesale flush disproportionately harms exactly the long-revisit frames'. Nothing reports the entry count, and nothing records that a flush happened, so the note cannot be checked against reality.

IT HAS A LIVE POISONING SOURCE. Because interactive_brokers is excluded from the connector memo, every IB request builds a fresh wrapper, gets a fresh identity token, and INSERTS an entry that can never be hit again. Measured in a controlled reproduction at a252119: 5 identical IB requests left 5 dead entries. On the live process the off-loop side alone contributes ~2/pass at ~79 passes/hour, so the 512 bound is plausibly crossed every few hours - but 'plausibly' is the whole problem: it is an estimate from fetch counts, not an observation, and the flush evicts the Bybit/Alpaca frames that ARE caching correctly.

SCOPED HONESTLY: hit/miss IS readable (fetch.cache_hit vs the fetch.<tf> misses), and that is what made the IB finding measurable. Only SIZE and the FLUSH EVENT are dark. If the IB memo proposal is approved, the dominant poisoning source goes away and this drops in priority - it does not disappear, because any future uncacheable client reintroduces it.
items.resolution_criteria: /api/diag/tick_cost (or a sibling diag read) reports _CANDLE_CACHE entry count and a cumulative wholesale-flush counter, so a session can state how often the map was cleared over a window instead of inferring it from fetch counts. LRU eviction instead of .clear() would also close it, and is the better fix if taken.

updates.note: Re-validated: a wholesale flush at >512 entries that is unreportable anywhere. Pairs with BL-20260817-CANDLE-CACHE-KEYS-ON-ID-CLIENT-WHICH-CPYTHON-RECYCLES — same cache, two defects, and it sits on the live signal path.

items.title: No surface anywhere reports a Bybit account's UID — so 'do bybit_1 and bybit_portfolio share a demo UID?' is unanswerable, and that question GATES the operator-decided hedge-mode item
items.detail:
CORRECTS A HANDOFF. The 2026-08-21 /system-review session carried Wave 0.2 STEP 0 forward under 'Operator-blocked'. It is NOT operator-blocked: it is blocked on a read surface that does not exist, and building one is Tier-1.

THE GATING QUESTION (docs/claude/WORKPLAN-2026-08-21.md Wave 0.2): bybit_portfolio is ALSO demo:True. If it shares a demo UID with bybit_1, switching a symbol's position mode on bybit_1 hits both books - so the hedge-mode design's 'scope it per-symbol on bybit_1' safety argument would not hold.

WHAT CONFIG SETTLES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. config/accounts.yaml gives the three bybit accounts three DISTINCT key envs - bybit_1 BYBIT_API_KEY_1, bybit_2 BYBIT_API_KEY_2, bybit_portfolio BYBIT_API_KEY_3 - with bybit_1 and bybit_portfolio both demo:True and bybit_2 mainnet. Distinct keys NARROW the question and do not settle it: Bybit permits several API keys on ONE UID, and a sub-account key carries its own credentials under a master UID. So 'different keys' is consistent with both same-UID and different-UID.

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: Bybit v5 GET /v5/user/query-api returns userID and parentUid for the calling key. checked: src/exchange/bybit_connector.py - grepped the connector, src/units/accounts/execute.py and src/units/accounts/clients.py, then all of src/ and scripts/, for query-api / parentUid / userID: ZERO hits. The repo has never read this. /api/diag/broker_account_status has a bybit arm, but it returns available_margin + margin_fields and no identity at all.

NOTE THE SHAPE, because it is the third instance this session: an operator-decided item is gated on a fact with no read surface, so the question gets answered by inference or deferred indefinitely. Same family as BL-20260821-NO-READ-SURFACE-FOR-TIMER-SCHEDULE (which manufactured a phantom defect) and BL-20260821-FETCH-COST-HAS-NO-VENUE-AXIS (which forced a bound where a measurement was wanted).

SCOPE: read-only, no order path, no mutation. It reads identity, not margin, and must NOT be folded into the available_margin branch - that field is about sizing and widening it would make it describe a payload it is not about (the same reason `supported` deliberately stays false on the bybit arm). | RESOLVED 2026-08-22 (#10121, workplan 0.6) AND THE GATING QUESTION IS NOW ANSWERED BY MEASUREMENT. Live read of /api/diag/broker_account_status: bybit_1 userID 553832447, bybit_2 553829655, bybit_portfolio 576206494 -- THREE DISTINCT UIDs. shared_uid_groups {} and unread_bybit_accounts [] , so the population is complete rather than partial: every declared bybit account read cleanly. Wave 0.2 STEP 0 is therefore answerable without the operator, as this row predicted, and the answer is favourable -- a position-mode switch on bybit_1 cannot reach bybit_portfolio. | TWO LIMITS STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. (1) parentUid came back EMPTY on all three, so is_sub_account is None on every row (never guessed from one half). A shared parent is therefore UNMEASURED. It does not change the answer -- Bybit position mode is set per calling UID, so distinct userIDs is the axis that governs -- but the sub-account relationship is not established and must not be asserted. (2) THE OTHER HALF OF T.2's PRE-APPROVAL CONDITION IS NOT MET. That condition requires bybit_1 'confirmed demo FROM A READ, not from this file'. What is available is account_class: paper, which /api/diag/broker_account_status sources from list_accounts() -- i.e. accounts.yaml, precisely the file the condition excludes. The UID is a genuine venue read; the demo-ness is not. No venue field observed in this read self-identifies a demo account, so the condition may be UNSATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN with current surfaces. Recorded rather than substituted: treating a config echo as a read would have unlocked a Tier-3 change on evidence the condition explicitly rules out.
items.resolution_criteria: A read-only surface (e.g. an identity block on /api/diag/broker_account_status, or a sibling route) reports userID and parentUid per declared bybit account, three-state and never collapsed - identity_read / could_not_look (null, NEVER a zero or empty string) / not_bybit - and a session can state whether bybit_1 and bybit_portfolio share a UID by citing that read rather than by inferring it from distinct key envs. Wave 0.2 STEP 0 is then answerable without an operator.

items.title: The MHG long->short flip: an id cited in three src/ files that was never filed
items.source: artifact-validity-guard, on the #10081 refresh (2026-08-22)
items.why_it_matters: The BEHAVIOUR shipped and is load-bearing; only the RECORD was missing. `BL-20260624-MHG-FLIP` is cited in src/units/accounts/ib_client.py (3 sites), src/runtime/order_monitor.py, src/units/accounts/alpaca_client.py, two test files and a sprint log -- and resolved to NOTHING in any backlog. A code comment saying 'the pre-cancel exists to stop bracket ACCUMULATION (BL-20260624-MHG-FLIP)' reads as tracked while being tracked by nobody, which is the exact crack the 2026-07-30 operator directive names. Filed from the code rather than from memory. WHAT IT DESCRIBES: repeated protective re-arms across an orphan flap stacked multiple live OCA brackets on ONE position; their stops later fired together and flipped a by-then-flat MHG long into a SHORT, i.e. a fresh orphan. Two mitigations are in the tree: `_locked_place_protective` pre-cancels the symbol's resting protective legs before arming (so `modify_protective` deliberately does NOT cancel again, avoiding a double-cancel), and a post-reconciler-flat-close sweep cancels GTC OCA stops left sitting on a flat position. NOTE the pre-cancel is best-effort: it proceeds if the bracket is still armed, so a PARTIAL pre-cancel is possible and a success return is NOT proof that no stale leg survives.
items.next_action: None. Filed as the missing record for behaviour already shipped and referenced. Distinct from BL-20260624-MHG-CLOSE-CONFIRM-VERIFY, which is about the close-confirm window, NOT this pre-cancel -- do not merge the two.
items.resolution_criteria: Filed, so every existing `BL-20260624-MHG-FLIP` reference in src/, tests and docs now resolves. Resolved on filing: no code change is owed, the mitigations are in the tree.
updates: 2026-08-22 wave0-8g7443: filed. Surfaced by artifact-validity-guard when #10081's proposal doc newly cited the id -- the guard is diff-scoped, so the pre-existing src/ citations never tripped it. Verified against the code (ib_client.py:1350, :1414, :1649, :2440), not from memory, and confirmed absent from all three backlogs before filing.

items.title: The new bracket_geometry column is declared CORPUS_EXEMPT, so nothing re-checks its statuses against the artifacts they were derived from — a later hand-edit would be caught nowhere
items.detail: `docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json` gained `bracket_geometry` on 2026-08-20 and its 47 live cells were DERIVED mechanically from the `gate` blocks in `runtime_logs/e35_bracket/<leg>/2026-08-20/report.json`, so matrix-vs-artifact agreement holds by construction FOR THAT RUN. It does not hold thereafter. `scripts/ci/check_matrix_corpus_agreement.py` reads only `docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl`, which holds (leg, LEVER) rows; a bracket triple is a DIMENSION and has no lever to key a row on, so the column was declared in `CORPUS_EXEMPT_LEVERS`. The guard's own summary now reports 188 live cells across 4 columns as NOT CHECKED, up from 141 across 3 — i.e. the exemption is visible, not hidden. But visible is not checked: a hand-edit flipping a `honest_negative` to `passed_unshipped` in this column would pass every guard in the repo. This is the same shape as the `exit_head_ml` exemption, whose note already records that its evidence exists in a file the guard does not read — two columns now sharing one unmet need.
items.resolution_criteria: ⚠️ REWRITTEN 2026-08-20 — the original criteria were NOT IMPLEMENTABLE and would have produced a guard that passes vacuously. They said the guard should 'read the e35 report directory', but `runtime_logs/` is gitignored (.gitignore:29) and those 19 reports are 37MB and untracked, so CI can never see them and a guard pointed there would find nothing and report clean — the unasserted-denominator trap (diagnostic-provenance sub-class C) this repo already names. PRECONDITION NOW DONE: the 133 gate rows are extracted to the committed `docs/research/e35-bracket-gate-corpus.jsonl` (123KB, 19 legs, verdicts 112 is_oos_fail / 4 wf_fail / 17 wf_pass, reconciling exactly with the results doc), so the evidence survives the container that produced it. CLOSES when a guard re-derives each `bracket_geometry` cell's status from THAT file and fails on disagreement. Note the shape mismatch that makes this a refactor rather than a one-line add: check_matrix_corpus_agreement.py is 652 lines built around a single corpus keyed on (leg, LEVER), and a bracket triple is a DIMENSION with no lever to key on — so either that guard grows a second keying mode or this gets a sibling guard. Do NOT close it by deleting the CORPUS_EXEMPT_LEVERS entry (that fails CI without checking anything).

updates.note: Re-validated: CORPUS_EXEMPT means nothing re-checks its statuses. Same family as BL-20260814-CORPUS-AGREEMENT-COUNTS-141-UNCHECKABLE-CELLS-AS-CHECKED.

items.title: m20_fleet_exit_sweep wrote every harness result to FOUR process-shared /tmp literals, so two concurrent sweeps silently served each other's numbers -- measured: three different legs on three different symbols returned an IDENTICAL base net_R
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-20, not theorised. Running scripts/research/e35_bracket_geometry_sweep.py (which imports m20_fleet_exit_sweep.run_cell) as five per-leg processes in parallel on one box returned a base net_R of EXACTLY -9.6113 for THREE different legs on THREE different symbols: avax_pullback_2h (AVAX), eth_pullback_prop_2h (ETH) and htf_pullback_trend_2h (BTC). Re-run one at a time the same legs measure 17.369, -32.5815 and -9.6113 -- i.e. AVAX and ETH had been reading BTC's file, and -9.6113 is htf's true value. Root cause: run_cell wrote its --json output to the FIXED literal '/tmp/m20_fleet_cell.json' and read it straight back, a process-shared constant. THREE MORE SITES in the same module had the identical defect and were found by grepping for the pattern rather than by assuming run_cell was the only one: winner_mfe_p80 ('/tmp/m20_p80_emit.jsonl'), run_census ('/tmp/m20_census.json' + '/tmp/m20_census_trades.jsonl') and -- the worst of the four -- resolve_split ('/tmp/m20_split_emit.jsonl'), which derives the IS/OOS BOUNDARY, so two concurrent legs could grade every downstream verdict against each other's window. WHY THIS IS HIGH AND NOT MEDIUM: the failure is silent, plausible and produces a complete-looking results table with no error, no warning and no missing row -- exactly the class the repo's 'green is not evidence' rule names; and the module's OWN docstring instructs running it detached on the trainer ('nohup ... &'), so an overlap needs no unusual operator action. It cannot corrupt live trading (Tier-1 research tooling, no order path), but it can corrupt the evidence a Tier-3 flip is decided on. FIX (shipped in this session's PR): all four sites use tempfile.mkstemp with per-call cleanup; mkstemp rather than a PID salt because a PID can be reused and a salt still collides between two runs that fork the same worker id. VERIFIED by a positive control, not by re-reading: five legs run through run_cell concurrently in a thread pool now return 5/5 DISTINCT net_R values (17.369 / -32.5815 / -9.6113 / -8.687 / 14.9756), and the pre-fix run is the negative control that shows the probe can detect the collision. THE RECORDED CORPUS WAS THEN SCANNED AND IS CLEAN. POPULATION: all 1,379 rows of docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl as of 2026-08-20, giving 2,756 base-value observations (base_net_r_IS + base_net_r_OOS) across 51 distinct legs and 305 distinct (field, value) keys. RESULT: ZERO (field, value) pairs are shared by more than one leg -- i.e. no two different legs ever recorded an identical base net_R to full precision, which is the contamination signature. The detector was shown to FIRE on an injected synthetic collision (0 -> 1) before the negative was accepted, so this is a measured negative and not a probe that cannot fail. So the fleet sweep does appear to have been run one leg-set at a time throughout, as its own docstring instructs; the defect was latent and this session's parallel run is the first thing to have exercised it.
items.resolution_criteria: CLOSED: (a) no fixed /tmp path is ASSIGNED anywhere in scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py (regex over non-comment lines) -- done, 4 sites converted to tempfile.mkstemp with per-call cleanup; (b) a parallel positive control returns distinct results per leg -- done, 5/5 distinct, with the pre-fix collision as the negative control; (c) the recorded corpus scanned for identical-base-net_R pairs across different legs -- done, 0 of 2,756 observations, detector verified to fire on an injected positive.
items.source: Measured during the M20 E3.5 bracket-geometry sweep; the anomaly surfaced as three legs sharing a base net_R to 4 decimals.

items.title: backtest_squeeze.py emits no tp_r_effective_* fields while backtest_trend.py and backtest_pullback.py both do, so squeeze_breakout_4h is the one leg whose venue-capped take-profit distance cannot be cross-checked against the harness

POPULATION: all 19 donchian/pullback/squeeze legs with reachable candle data. RESULT: 18 of 19 agree EXACTLY (worst |diff| 0.0); the 19th, squeeze_breakout_4h, returns None because backtest_squeeze.py never computes the field. This is the same shape as two defects the repo has already paid for and recorded -- mfe_r absent from the trend/squeeze emit payload (BL-20260810-EXIT-GATE-BLIND-TO-CAPTURE-AND-CAPITAL) and capital_efficiency imported by backtest_pullback.py but not backtest_trend.py -- namely a metric computed in one harness and absent in its sibling, which then degrades to a null that reads as 'measured, no effect' rather than 'not measured'. So what is lost is the INDEPENDENT CROSS-CHECK for that one leg, not the measurement. checked: docs/research/RESEARCH-CAPABILITY-INDEX.md section 3 (Exits) and a grep of scripts/research/ for an existing tp_r_effective consumer -- backtest_trend.py and backtest_pullback.py are the only producers, so no other tool supplies the missing field either. It is filed rather than fixed because the fix touches a harness on the m20 evidence path and this session's PR is already carrying a change to that module; a harness edit riding along with it would make the sweep's own results harder to attribute.
items.resolution_criteria: CLOSED when backtest_squeeze.py emits tp_r_effective_n/min/median/max on the same terms as backtest_trend.py (i.e. None, never 0, when the TP lever is off), AND the e35_barrier_race cross-check reports 19/19 rather than 18/18 with a named exception.
items.source: e35_barrier_race.py cross-check against harness tp_r_effective_median, 2026-08-20.
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-08-20. Root cause was not a missing computation: backtest_squeeze.py ALREADY collected `_tp_r_effective` at the entry site (line ~208) and then dropped it on the floor — never threaded into `_summarize`. Written and never read, the exact shape provenance-consumer-guard exists to catch. Now emits tp_r_effective_n/median/min/max on the same terms as both siblings. POSITIVE CONTROL run rather than assumed: lever ON (--tp-cap-pct 0.099 --tp-r 50) gives n=244, median 2.227, min 0.583, max 9.301; lever OFF gives n=0 with all three statistics None, never 0 — an un-measured reach and a zero-distance TP stay opposite statements. The e35_barrier_race cross-check can now cover the squeeze leg, which was the 18-of-18 denominator's one gap.

items.title: backtest_squeeze reports max_drawdown_r GROSS of costs while backtest_trend and backtest_pullback report it NET — the same column in the fleet SUMMARY and the coverage matrix holds two different quantities
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-20 and root-caused to one line. scripts/backtest_squeeze.py:378 accumulates the drawdown over `rs`, which is [t.r_multiple for t in trades] -- the GROSS R series. scripts/backtest_trend.py:836 and backtest_pullback.py accumulate over `net = r_multiple - total_cost_r`. So squeeze's max_drawdown_r is gross of fees+slippage+funding and its siblings' are net. POPULATION / PROOF: squeeze_breakout_4h config-exact base, full history, 106 trades. Harness reports max_drawdown_r 6.6176. Re-deriving from the emitted per-trade rows: over gross_r = 6.6176 (EXACT match), over net_r_fee_only = 6.957, over net_r = 7.4162. net_total_r and total_trades reconcile to 0.0004 and 0 respectively, so this is isolated to the drawdown accumulation and is not a general emit problem. The gross figure is 10.8% OPTIMISTIC against the net one on this leg, and it is optimistic by construction (costs only ever deepen a drawdown). HOW IT WAS FOUND, which is the part worth keeping: scripts/research/m20_split_dispersion.py REFUSED to report a dispersion band for a squeeze cell, returning state 'refused' with harness_agreement max delta 0.7986 against its 0.001 R tolerance. That is precisely the behaviour its docstring promises -- 'a mismatch beyond tolerance makes analyse refuse to report, rather than emitting a dispersion band built on a metric that does not reproduce' -- so the guard earned its keep rather than the defect being spotted by reading. TWO WRONG HYPOTHESES WERE REFUTED FIRST, recorded so nobody re-tests them: (a) row ORDERING -- refuted, the file is sorted by both entry_time and exit_time, all three orderings give 7.4162, and there are 0 overlapping consecutive trades; (b) a general emit-schema divergence -- refuted, squeeze and pullback emit byte-identical key sets. WHAT IS AND IS NOT BROKEN: within squeeze the Path A `beats` comparison is still apples-to-apples, since base and cell are both gross, so no squeeze verdict is wrong ON ITS OWN TERMS. What is wrong is every CROSS-FAMILY reading: the fleet SUMMARY.md, the coverage matrix and any table that puts squeeze's max_drawdown_r beside a trend or pullback leg's is comparing gross against net without saying so. This is the FOURTH squeeze/sibling divergence found on 2026-08-20, after BL-20260820-SQUEEZE-HARNESS-EMITS-NO-TP-R-EFFECTIVE and BL-20260820-SWEEP-EMITS-CELLS-FOR-FLAGS-THE-HARNESS-DOES-NOT-IMPLEMENT (--rr-floor absent); the pattern is that backtest_squeeze.py has drifted from its two siblings on several independently-added metrics, which suggests a convergence guard over the three harnesses is the durable fix rather than three point patches.
items.resolution_criteria: CLOSED when backtest_squeeze.py accumulates max_drawdown_r over the same net-of-cost series its siblings use, AND m20_split_dispersion.py's harness_agreement passes for a squeeze cell (it currently returns state 'refused'), AND any recorded squeeze max_drawdown_r figure in the coverage matrix / sweep corpus is either re-measured or explicitly annotated as gross-basis. NOT closed by fixing the line alone: the recorded verdicts were produced on the old basis and a silent re-basing would move numbers already quoted elsewhere. Deliberately filed rather than fixed in the session that found it, for the same reason as the tp_r_effective row -- a harness edit riding along with the sweep that consumes it makes that sweep's results harder to attribute.

items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-08-20 (same session that filed it — the stated reason for deferring, that a harness edit would make the in-flight sweep's results hard to attribute, expired when the sweep finished and committed). backtest_squeeze.py's drawdown loop now iterates `net`, the one-word divergence from backtest_trend.py:836 and backtest_pullback.py:869 which both already did. MEASURED on ETHUSDT 4h, 236 trades, full history: max_drawdown_r 11.9022 -> 13.4431, so the bug UNDERSTATED squeeze drawdown by 1.5409 R — anti-conservative, it made the family look better than it was. net_total_r (17.6975) and total_trades (236) are unchanged, confirming the blast radius is the drawdown accumulation alone. ⚠️ ANY SQUEEZE max_drawdown_r RECORDED BEFORE 2026-08-20 IS GROSS AND UNDERSTATED — do not compare a pre-fix squeeze maxDD against a trend/pullback one.

items.title: m20_fleet_exit_sweep emitted rr_floor cells for a harness with no --rr-floor flag, and the result graded `error` -- which cannot be told apart from a real crash
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-20 on the M31 P5 precondition-3b rr_floor walk-forward (operator pre-approved to RUN). POPULATION: 19 legs x 3 rr_floor cells = 57 (leg x cell) rows, config-exact base, tp_cap 0.099, split_mode oos-trades target 50. RESULT: 43 is_oos_fail, 4 wf_fail, 3 path_b_wf_fail, 2 PASS, 2 path_b_wf_pass, and 3 `error` -- all three errors on squeeze_breakout_4h, one per rr_floor cell. ROOT CAUSE: cells_for gates rr_floor on inert_rr_floor_reason(fam, tp_cap_pct), which tests whether the lever is SEMANTICALLY applicable (is the family in LIVE_TP_CAPPED_FAMILIES, i.e. does its live unit clamp the TP so rr_from_here has a target). `squeeze` is CORRECTLY in that set -- backtest_squeeze.py's live unit does carry _TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT. What was never tested is whether the HARNESS implements the flag: measured by grepping each harness's parser, `--rr-floor` is declared in backtest_trend.py (3 occurrences) and backtest_pullback.py (2) and in NEITHER backtest_squeeze.py, backtest_fvg_range.py nor backtest_ict_scalp.py (0 each). Two independent conditions, one test. WHY THIS IS NOT MERELY COSMETIC: `error` is a COLLAPSED state here. A genuine crash and a flag the harness never had are byte-indistinguishable in it, and the second is not a failure at all -- it is a leg the lever does not reach. The run plan already has the correct vocabulary at the LEG level (`no_harness_levers`); it simply was not applied at the CELL level, which is the same not-run-vs-run-and-flat distinction inert_rr_floor_reason's own docstring exists to preserve. `fade` is in LIVE_TP_CAPPED_FAMILIES too and would hit this the moment it is promoted off shadow. THE EXISTING GUARD DOES NOT COVER IT: scripts/check_harness_lever_coupling.py checks the OPPOSITE direction (config key -> is the harness modelling it) and passes clean (42 strategies, 0 gaps) while this defect is live. FIX (shipped in this session's PR): harness_implements_flag(harness, flag) reads the harness SOURCE rather than consulting a hardcoded table -- a table naming the flag here would be a second copy free to drift from the first -- and returns three states, True / False / None, where None is 'we could not read the source' and must NOT collapse into False (that would silently withhold every cell for a harness we merely failed to open, turning a filesystem problem into a fake coverage answer). VERIFIED: the run plan now prints `INERT squeeze_breakout_4h: rrfloor0.5 -- harness_has_no_rr_floor_flag:backtest_squeeze.py` and squeeze's cell list is empty, while trend_donchian still receives all three cells. Pinned by two tests, one of which carries the opposite-defect control (a change that withheld rr_floor EVERYWHERE would pass the first assertion and fail the control).
items.resolution_criteria: CLOSED: (a) inert_rr_floor_reason consults the harness source and returns a distinct reason for the no-flag case -- done; (b) the unreadable case is a third state, not folded into 'absent' -- done; (c) a regression test pins both, WITH a control proving the fix did not withhold the cells everywhere -- done (tests/test_fleet_sweep_rr_floor_cells.py). RESIDUAL, deliberately not closed here: this fix is rr_floor-specific. The general form -- ANY cell emitting ANY flag the target harness does not declare -- is not guarded, and the natural home is an extension of check_harness_lever_coupling.py to cover the cell->harness direction. Filed as the follow-up rather than widened in-session, because a whole-tree flag audit would change coverage-matrix counts for other levers and that belongs in its own change.
