items.title: The tp_geometry unstamped-ceiling was raised to the roll-up's measured 239 while the accounting predicts 238 — one cell is unexplained and was deliberately not papered over
items.detail: Raising `_unstamped_ceiling` 208 -> 239 for the new `bracket_geometry` column: the column adds 47 live cells, 17 of which are stamped `live_parity` from a measurement, leaving 30 unstamped, and 208 + 30 = 238. `scripts/research/m20_coverage_rollup.py --check` independently counts 239. The ceiling was set to the roll-up's own measured figure rather than to the arithmetic, because a ceiling tuned to my count would hide the discrepancy instead of recording it — but that means the ratchet currently carries exactly one cell of slack, and one cell of slack is what lets a single new unstamped cell ship without breaching (the precise failure the ceiling note's own history describes, where two cells of slack made both planted-omission self-tests go quiet). Not diagnosed this session: the likely candidates are a live-cell denominator that counts a row I classed as non-live, or a pre-existing cell the roll-up counts differently from my enumeration. STATE THE POPULATION: 423 live cells after the column was added, 376 before; 239 unstamped by the roll-up's count.
items.resolution_criteria: Reconcile the two counts by enumerating, cell by cell, the live cells `m20_coverage_rollup.py` counts as unstamped against the same enumeration done independently, and name the differing cell. Then either stamp it (if a measurement exists) or ratchet the ceiling to the reconciled figure. Closes when the ceiling equals a number BOTH counts agree on and the note records the reconciliation. Do NOT close by simply lowering the ceiling to 238 and observing CI still passes — that would be tuning the ratchet to the arithmetic, which is the thing this row exists to avoid.
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-08-20 by enumerating cell by cell, as the criteria asked. THERE IS NO SLACK — the ceiling of 239 is exactly right and MY arithmetic was the error. Measured: the bracket_geometry column has 47 live cells of which 16 are stamped (not 17), leaving 31 unstamped, and 208 + 31 = 239 = what m20_coverage_rollup.py --check independently counts. The single measured-status cell carrying no tp_geometry is `squeeze_breakout_4h/BTCUSDT/4h` at `blocked:dispersion_refused`, and its being unstamped is CORRECT rather than a gap: m20_split_dispersion refused that cell on harness_agreement, so there is no trustworthy measurement to stamp. I had counted it as stamped. The ratchet therefore carries ZERO cells of slack and a single new unstamped cell WILL breach it — which is the property the ceiling note wanted and which the filed row wrongly reported as lost. FOLLOW-ON, not a defect: the refusal's root cause (the gross-vs-net maxDD divergence) was fixed in the same session, so re-running dispersion on that cell should now clear harness_agreement and make it stampable — at which point the ceiling drops to 238.

items.title: attach-ib-target's apply path connected on the TRADER's execution clientId (497), so the repair action could never place a target while the trader was running — and its dry run reported ready
items.detail: `scripts/ops/attach_ib_target.py::_attach` called `ib_client_for(cfg, readonly=False)`, which resolves the account's configured execution clientId (`ib_client_id: 497`). IBKR refuses a duplicate clientId rather than evicting the incumbent, so with the trader up — i.e. always — the connect failed with `Error 326, reqId -1: Unable to connect as the client id is already in use`, the short-lived ops process tripped its own 120s circuit breaker, and the run returned `{"action": "place_failed"}`. Observed live on ib_paper/MES via system-action issue #10139 on 2026-08-22. STATE THE POPULATION: one apply attempt, one account, one symbol; the defect is in the code path, not inferred from a rate. NO LIVE HARM — verified immediately after via /api/diag/ib_state (all three clients 498/9505/497 `connected`, `consecutive_failures: 0`) and /api/bot/strategies (`bot_running: true`, `tick_age_seconds: 1.2`): the refusal is what protected the trader, and the breaker trip was inside the ops process, which then exited. THE SHAPE IS WHY THIS IS HIGH AND NOT MEDIUM: the DRY RUN never builds a client, so it reports `state: ready` with every refusal passed, and only the apply can falsify. A repair action for a live-protection gap that reads as available right up to the moment it is needed is worse than one that is visibly broken — it was shipped 2026-08-16 for BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED and had therefore never once placed a target against a running trader. Its sibling `scripts/ops/flatten_ib_position.py` carried `_ib_ops_client_id() -> 9900 + (os.getpid() % 90)` from the start, with a docstring saying exactly why, and `tests/test_flatten_ib_position.py::test_ops_client_id_range` asserted its band; `attach_ib_target.py` simply never got the same treatment, and no test covered the apply path to notice. `scripts/ops/cancel_ib_order.py` is NOT affected — it connects AS the owning clientId deliberately (IBKR only lets the owner cancel) and carries an explicit `_TRADER_CLIENT_ID_CEILING = 9000` refusal for exactly this hazard.
items.resolution_criteria: attach_ib_target._attach passes an ops-band clientId (9900-9989, PID-salted, disjoint from the trader execution ids and the 9000-9899 read band) to ib_client_for, covered by a test that falsifies against the pre-fix code.
items.resolution: Fixed 2026-08-22: `_ib_ops_client_id()` added (lifted from flatten_ib_position, same band and same PID salt) and passed as `client_id=` at the single `ib_client_for` call site. `tests/test_attach_ib_target_client_id.py` asserts BOTH the band and the wiring — the band alone is worthless if `_attach` does not pass it. Falsified: 2 failed pre-fix (AttributeError on the missing helper; `ib_client_for called without an explicit client_id`), 2 passed post-fix. NOT yet re-run against the live trader — the MES apply is scheduled for the Sunday 2026-08-23 reopen, and that run is the live positive control this row's fix is still owed.

items.title: Two unrelated test files pass in isolation and FAIL in the full suite — cross-file sys.modules pollution leaves a bare-MagicMock leaf, the exact failure mode tests/conftest.py already documents for `telegram`
items.detail: STATE THE POPULATION FIRST, because the headline is easy to over-read: measured on ONE sandbox at commit 74aa9a39, a full `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` gave **12 failed / 12021 passed / 15 skipped** in 619 s, while **CI's `pytest-run` passed the full suite green on the same tree** (PR #10140, 11m27s, and again on #10141). So this is NOT a red CI and NOT a blocker — but it is also not simply 'a lean sandbox', which is what I assumed before checking. Three groups, separated by measurement: (1) `tests/test_vm_health_helper.py` + `tests/test_s067_silent_empty_fixes.py` (2 tests, psutil-raises paths) fail at the PRE-SESSION baseline `1b05353` too, so they are pre-existing and environmental. (2) `tests/test_send_ping.py` — **20/20 pass in isolation at HEAD**, 5 fail inside the full suite. (3) `tests/ml/calibration/test_calibration.py` — **17/17 pass in isolation**, fails inside the full suite with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sklearn.isotonic'; 'sklearn' is not a package` — while `import sklearn` standalone resolves cleanly to `/usr/local/lib/python3.11/dist-packages/sklearn/__init__.py`, a real package. THE MECHANISM IS NAMED IN THE REPO ALREADY: `tests/conftest.py` lines 62-64 document precisely this shape — "No module named 'telegram.error'; 'telegram' is not a package ... because Python treats the bare-MagicMock `telegram` entry as a leaf, not a package" — and `_stub_optional` guards against it by only stubbing when the real import raises. `sklearn` is NOT in that stub list and imports fine, so something ELSE is putting a bare leaf at `sys.modules['sklearn']` and not restoring it. I did not find the writer: `grep` for `sys.modules["sklearn"]` / `ModuleType("sklearn` / `monkeypatch.setitem(sys.modules` over tests/ scripts/ src/ ml/ returns nothing, so it is likely indirect (an autouse fixture, a MagicMock attribute access materialising a submodule, or a stub inserted under a different name that shadows on import). WHY IT MATTERS DESPITE GREEN CI: a suite whose result depends on which subset you run cannot be used to falsify anything locally — a developer running one file gets a different verdict from CI, in BOTH directions, and the direction that costs is a real failure masked by running the file alone. It also means the local full-suite run is not usable as a pre-push check, which is the check this repo's practices lean on before merging. I have NOT established why CI differs (different install set, ordering, or the polluter being skipped there); that is the first thing to measure, not to assume.
items.resolution_criteria: Identify the writer that leaves a bare MagicMock (or non-package leaf) at sys.modules['sklearn'] and restore it, so `tests/ml/calibration/test_calibration.py` and `tests/test_send_ping.py` give the SAME verdict in isolation and in the full suite. Establish and record why CI's full-suite run does not hit it — a fix that only works because CI already differs is not a fix.
items.evidence: Full suite at 74aa9a39: 12 failed / 12021 passed / 15 skipped in 619.21s. Isolation at the same commit: test_send_ping 20 passed in 0.24s; tests/ml/calibration/test_calibration.py 17 passed in 2.72s. Baseline 1b05353 (git worktree): test_vm_health_helper + test_s067_silent_empty_fixes already fail, test_send_ping passes. CI pytest-run green on #10140 and #10141. No pytest-randomly installed, so ordering is deterministic file order.

updates.note: Re-validated: two files that pass in isolation and FAIL in the full suite. Directly relevant — my 31-test run today was narrow and would not have surfaced it, and a bare MagicMock left in sys.modules is the same mechanism as BL-20260807-PYTEST-APPROX-NUMPY-STUB. Two rows, one root: unscoped sys.modules stubbing.

items.title: A Bybit settleCoin=USDT position page silently OMITTED a live real-money BTCUSDT position, so the reconciler read the account as flat and FALSE-CLOSED the journal row, leaving the position invisible and unprotected
items.detail:
FILED RETROSPECTIVELY 2026-08-22, and the reason it is being filed is itself the finding: this id is cited in SIX places across the codebase -- src/units/accounts/clients.py x3 (the docstring at :1216, the cross-check comment at :1391, and the new one at :1860), tests/test_accounts_clients_open_positions.py:120, tests/test_bybit_open_orders_accessor.py, and CLAUDE.md -- and it had NEVER been filed in any backlog. Every one of those references reads as 'tracked by BL-...' while being tracked by nobody, which is precisely the crack the 2026-07-30 operator directive names and what artifact-validity-guard exists to catch. It surfaced only because that guard is diff-scoped: adding a SEVENTH reference finally tripped it. A pre-existing dangling reference is invisible to a diff-scoped guard by construction, so the count above is a LOWER BOUND on this class -- other long-standing ids may be equally unfiled and equally quiet.

THE UNDERLYING DEFECT (already fixed in code 2026-07-13; this row is the missing record, not new work): `client.get_positions(category, settleCoin='USDT')` returns ONE page which can omit a configured symbol. A live 0.001 BTCUSDT position on real-money bybit_2 was absent from that page while a symbol-scoped `get_positions(symbol=...)` read -- and the Bybit terminal -- both saw it. `account_open_positions` therefore returned a list not containing BTCUSDT, the reverse reconciler read the account as flat for that symbol, and it FALSE-CLOSED the open journal row. The position then appeared in neither /api/bot/positions nor Trades, and carried no journal-driven protection. The fix cross-checks every CONFIGURED symbol the settleCoin page did not return, symbol-scoped.

WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A COMMENT: the failure mode is an empty-vs-unread collapse on a real-money venue -- 'the venue says flat' and 'this page did not include it' were indistinguishable to the caller -- which is the same class as the collapsed-state family CLAUDE.md documents, and it is why the same cross-check had to be re-implemented in account_bybit_open_orders (2026-08-22) rather than inherited.
items.why_it_matters: A position the reconciler cannot see is a position nothing protects, on the account that trades real money. The cross-check is load-bearing production behaviour that was carried only by code comments pointing at a row that did not exist -- so any session auditing it would have found the citation and no record behind it.
resolution_criteria: The symbol-scoped cross-check exists in account_open_positions -- SHIPPED 2026-07-13, verified present at src/units/accounts/clients.py:1391 on 968bbea8.

It is inherited by any NEW Bybit position read -- done for account_bybit_open_orders (2026-08-22), with a test that fires when the cross-check is removed (falsified: dropping it fails test_settlecoin_blind_symbol_is_cross_checked).
This row exists so the six in-code citations resolve. Closed on filing.
items.next_action: None — the code fix shipped 2026-07-13; this row is the record that was missing. The residual class (pre-existing dangling ids a diff-scoped guard cannot see) is noted in detail and is a candidate for a one-off full-corpus sweep, NOT scheduled here.

I did not invent the history: the defect, the account, the symbol and the remedy are all recorded verbatim in the surviving code comment at clients.py:1391, which is the primary source. What I could NOT recover is the original incident issue/PR number, and I am not manufacturing one.

items.title: The pairs sleeve does not close its own order_packages rows -- the stuck-cascade SECOND-LINE-OF-DEFENCE sweep does it for 69% of its closes (100% for pairs_bnb_btc_a), and that sweep firing routinely is itself the alarm nobody hears
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-22 from /api/bot/order-packages?include_paper=true&since=2026-07-23. STATE THE POPULATION: the route's limit MAXIMUM is 200 and it returned exactly 200 rows, so this is a TRUNCATED newest-first page spanning 2026-08-16..2026-08-22 -- one week, NOT the 30d window requested. 110 of the 200 are closed packages.

Close reasons on that page: reconciler_filled 52 (47.3%), stuck_cascade_recovered 50 (45.5%), and then FOUR single rows -- tp_cross 1, sl_cross 1, exit_head 1, giveback_stop 1 -- plus exchange_flat_reconciled 1 and 3 nulls.

stuck_cascade_recovered is NOT an exit. order_monitor.py:4414 force-closes an order_packages row whose linked TRADE already reached a terminal status while the package stayed open. Its own docstring calls it 'the second line of defence' against 'a bug elsewhere (e.g. partial close path forgetting to cascade)'. A second line of defence carrying 45.5% of package closes is a primary path that is not working.

IT IS CONCENTRATED, NOT UNIFORM, AND THAT IS WHAT RULES OUT THE INNOCENT EXPLANATION. The obvious alternative is a tick-ordering RACE -- the sweep runs every monitor tick and could simply beat the normal cascade, which would stamp stuck_cascade_recovered on perfectly healthy closes. A race is uniform across strategies. This is not: pairs_bnb_btc_a 13/13 = 100%, pairs_bnb_btc_b 10/13, pairs_sol_eth_b 11/18, pairs_sol_eth_a 8/17 (pairs overall 42/61 = 69%), ict_scalp 5m legs 7/15 -- against trend_donchian_* at 0 of 14 and ict_scalp_sol_15m / ict_scalp_5m at 0 of 4 each. A sweep that beats the cascade for one strategy family and never for another is not a race.

MECHANISM HYPOTHESIS, stated as a hypothesis: the pairs sleeve is an ISOLATED 2-leg order path (src.units.strategies.pairs_executor.run_pairs_tick, called once per tick from src/main.py, NOT via Coordinator.multi_account_execute -- CLAUDE.md documents this isolation explicitly). The package-close cascade lives on the path pairs does not use. That fits the concentration exactly, but I have NOT traced pairs_executor's close path line by line and am not asserting it as established.

=== TRACED AND FIXED 2026-08-22 by session s3-exitpath (PR #10145). The hypothesis above is now ESTABLISHED. ===
The mechanism is traced, not inferred. _close_pair (pairs_executor.py:707) writes status='closed' straight to the trade row and therefore never routes through order_monitor._close_trade_from_order_status, which is the ONLY place _cascade_close_linked_package runs. There are ZERO cascade calls anywhere in pairs_executor.py. So the answer to this row's last open question -- does pairs_executor cascade its package close AT ALL -- is NO, by construction.

THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES EXACTLY ON BOTH ARMS (newest 500 closed non-backtest rows, filter_state asserted 'applied', 2026-07-15..2026-08-22): pairs legs closed via the monitor 57 <-> packages carrying a real reason (reconciler_filled) 57; pairs legs closed via _close_pair/intent_reduce 120 <-> packages left for the sweep 120 (109 swept + 11 not yet). pairs_revert/pairs_stop/pairs_half_open_cleanup appear on 99 TRADE rows and ZERO package rows.

CORRECTION to criterion 2's EVIDENCE (the CONCLUSION is unaffected and I reached it independently). The gate's only caller in src/ is src/runtime/pipeline.py:611 (imported at :56), NOT intent_multiplexer.py. intent_multiplexer.py:52 does import from strategy_monocle, but a DIFFERENT symbol -- _same_bar_entry_for_strategy (see its own :560) -- and contains zero references to _has_open_package_for_strategy. Verified by an untruncated grep across src/. The conclusion still holds by a second route: the gate sits on the pipeline's SIGNAL-DISPATCH path, and pairs legs are not in the strategy roster (pipeline.py resolves any 'pairs_' strategy to the pairs_executor monitor unit), so run_pairs_tick never reaches that site. Field beats comment.

FIX: _cascade_close_pair_package, called from _close_pair, forwarding the leg's own f'pairs_{outcome}'. Bookkeeping ONLY -- it places, modifies and cancels nothing, and is the same write the sweep already performed, made timely and honestly-reasoned. Guarded at BOTH the helper and the call site so the isolation is structural: a package-write failure must never reach _close_pair's except, which sets closed_ok=False and would report a leg that IS flat at the broker as a failed flatten. THE SWEEP WAS NOT CHANGED, per this row's own instruction. Tests: tests/test_pairs_package_cascade.py, 7/7 FAIL against the pre-fix file and 7/7 pass after; the end-to-end isolation test caught a real weakness in the first version of the fix.

GENERALISED: pairs was the instance, not the class -- only 1 of 8 literal status='closed' call sites cascades. See BL-20260822-SEVEN-OF-EIGHT-TRADE-CLOSE-SITES-DO-NOT-CASCADE-THEIR-PACKAGE.

=== LIVE POSITIVE CONTROL: ATTEMPTED TWICE 2026-08-22, RESULT = NOT YET OBSERVABLE (which is NOT a pass). ===
DEPLOYMENT IS CONFIRMED, by ancestry rather than assumption: the trader serves 4dcf3caa and BOTH e9dbd7b0 (the fix) and 4dcf3caa are ancestors of it (git merge-base --is-ancestor). So the code is live.

THE CONTROL COULD NOT BE TAKEN because NO PAIRS PACKAGE HAS CLOSED SINCE THE DEPLOY. Read twice, 16:27Z and 16:34Z (/api/bot/db/table/order_packages, status=closed, ordered by updated_at desc, filter_state asserted 'applied'): 177 pairs packages on the page, distribution UNCHANGED at stuck_cascade_recovered 109 / reconciler_filled 57 / null 11, pairs-native close_reason rows = 0, and packages updated after the deploy window opened (15:36Z) = 0. The newest pairs package update of any kind is 2026-08-22T12:10:22Z -- roughly 4.4 hours before the read, and BEFORE the deploy. Every one of those 177 rows predates the fix, which is exactly why the distribution has not moved.

⚠️ READ THAT AS 'WE DID NOT LOOK YET', NOT AS A FAILURE. Zero native rows is the EXPECTED reading when zero pairs packages have closed under the new code; reporting it as a failed control would be wrong, and reporting the deploy as a passed control would be worse. The pairs sleeve closed 5 times earlier the same day (09:03, 11:03, 11:05, 12:08, 12:10Z) and then went quiet, so the next close should land within hours.

A self check-in had been scheduled for 17:33Z to re-take it; it was DELETED at session close rather than left to fire into a closed session. The control is therefore carried in the session handoff instead. THE FIX REMAINS VERIFIED BY UNIT TEST ONLY (7/7 fail pre-fix, 7/7 pass post-fix) and this row says so.

LIVE POSITIVE CONTROL: PASS (2026-08-22T17:12Z, session s4-pairs-control, third attempt). POPULATION: all 189 packages with strategy_name LIKE 'pairs_%', filter_state AND order_state both asserted 'applied'. Deploy boundary e9dbd7b0 = 2026-08-22T15:35:53Z. PRE-deploy n=187: stuck_cascade_recovered 109 / reconciler_filled 57 / null 21 -- ZERO pairs-native reasons. items.title: order_packages.close_reason mixes real exits with BOOKKEEPING REPAIRS, so any exit-mechanism share computed from it is measuring two different things at once -- and it is the field workplan item 1.1's headline is built on
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-22, two populations read side by side.

(a) order_packages.close_reason, newest 200 packages since 2026-07-23 (the route's MAXIMUM limit; the page therefore spans only 2026-08-16..08-22), 110 closed: reconciler_filled 47.3%, stuck_cascade_recovered 45.5%, everything else 7.2%.

(b) trades.exit_reason via /api/bot/db/table/trades, status='closed', newest 500 by id (filter_state ASSERTED 'applied' before reading -- an ignored filter silently returns the whole table), spanning 2026-07-15..2026-08-22 out of 1292 closed rows total: reconciler_filled 41.2%, intent_reduce_executed 9.6%, exchange_flat_reconciled 8.4%, pairs_revert 8.0%, pairs_stop 7.0%, intent_reduce 6.2%, pairs_half_open_cleanup 4.8%, sl_cross 4.0%, netting_attributed 3.4%, sl 2.2%, stale_stop 1.8%, netting_phantom_reconciled 0.8%, tp_cross 0.6%, giveback_stop 0.6%.

stuck_cascade_recovered does not appear in (b) AT ALL, because it is not an exit -- it is order_monitor.py:4414 force-closing a PACKAGE row whose TRADE had already terminated by some other means. So in population (a) nearly half the denominator describes a bookkeeping repair, and the trade's actual exit mechanism is recorded on a different table.

THE HONEST SPLIT, from (b), excluding the pairs sleeve because it is a separate order path with its own exit vocabulary and it FLATTERS the aggregate: main order path n=323 -- decision-driven exits 15.2%, reconciler_filled 46.1%, tp_cross 3 rows = 0.9%, sl_cross+sl 31 = 9.6%. THE STOP:TARGET RATIO IS 10.3 : 1. The pairs sleeve alone (n=177) is decision-driven 42.4% and has ZERO tp_cross and ZERO sl_cross -- it exits on pairs_revert/pairs_stop instead, so pooling the two makes the main path look twice as healthy as it is.

This CORROBORATES the workplan's own figures on an independent population and at a different level (its 'closes reconciler_filled 148 = 40%' vs 41.2% here), which is the useful part: the numbers are right, but the FIELD they came from mixes categories, and the pairs/non-pairs pooling hides that the main path is the worse half.
items.why_it_matters: Workplan item 1.1 ('8.1% of closes use a declared bracket') and gate G.2 ('the grader calls a reconciler close a take-profit') are both exit-mechanism claims. If they are computed over order_packages.close_reason then ~45% of the denominator in a recent week is a repair sweep, and the resulting share is not the quantity anyone means by 'how do our trades exit'. The fix is not to distrust the headline -- it reproduces -- but to pin the measurement to trades.exit_reason and to state the pairs/non-pairs split every time.
resolution_criteria: Every exit-mechanism claim in the workplan and in the review skills names WHICH field it read (trades.exit_reason vs order_packages.close_reason) and states the pairs/non-pairs split.
The 200-row cap on /api/bot/order-packages is stated wherever that route backs a share, or the claim is recomputed off the DB explorer where the population is controllable.
A single owner for 'how did this trade exit' -- one accessor both the reviews and the reports read -- rather than two fields that disagree by construction.
items.next_action: When item 1.1 is next worked, recompute its headline from trades.exit_reason with the pairs split stated. Do not re-derive it from order_packages.close_reason.

items.title: On broker-truth exit prices the declared bracket is reached ~3x more often than the exit_reason records -- workplan item 1.1 is substantially an ATTRIBUTION defect, not a mechanism one
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-22. POPULATION: /api/bot/db/table/trades status='closed', newest 500 by id, filter_state ASSERTED 'applied', window 2026-07-15..2026-08-22 of 1293 closed; backtest excluded; pairs excluded (isolated 2-leg path, flatters the aggregate). Main order path n=323, of which 78 (24.1%) carry a BROKER-TRUTH exit price (exit_price_source in exchange_fill/bybit_closed_pnl/ib_execution). The other 245 carry an estimated/fabricated price (candle_at_close alone is 30.7% of main-path closes) and are UNKNOWN -- excluded, not counted, because geometry against a reconstructed price is not evidence.

METHOD: order_monitor._classify_broker_exit's OWN conservative inequality (long: exit<=sl -> sl, exit>=tp -> tp; short inverted; else None). NOT a picked tolerance. WARNING: a first pass of this analysis used a symmetric +/-0.10-risk-unit band and reported 72.7% at a bracket; that number is WRONG and is retracted -- a symmetric band counts a fill that stopped SHORT of the stop as a stop hit. Do not re-quote it.

RESULT over the 78: crossed the declared stop 40 (51.3%); crossed the declared target 6 (7.7%); strictly between 32 (41.0%). Reached a declared level either side = 46 (59.0%). LABELLED with a decision-driven exit_reason = 15 (19.2%). UNDER-ATTRIBUTION GAP = 31 rows.

WHAT SURVIVES OF THE ORIGINAL FRAMING: the stop:target skew is real -- 40:6 = 6.7:1 among fills that reached a level (less extreme than the label-derived 10.3:1, still heavily stop-weighted); and 41.0% of measurable exits landed BETWEEN the brackets, a large genuine residue.

SELECTION, NAMED: a broker-truth price requires the fills store to hold a fill, which over-selects exits that were real venue orders. It does NOT select the fill's PRICE, so within this population the price is unbiased evidence. Conditional on a fill existing.

PARTIAL DIAGNOSIS on reconciler_filled + broker truth (n=44): 21 crossed a level and kept the generic label. REFUTED: wrong level source -- the classifier reads order_packages.sl/tp, 0 of 44 had a null package stop, and the two sources agree on 43 of 44 (identical 21-hit/23-none verdict). REFUTED: a different close path -- closed_by is monitor_reconciler on all 44 and closed_reason is the identical string on both groups. CANDIDATE, UNDERPOWERED: 18 of the 21 carry a backfill marker (run_id bf-20260808T151707Z, local_markprice -> exchange_fill), consistent with the classifier having run against a mark price and the 2026-08-08 repair correcting the PRICE without re-running the DERIVED reason -- but the 2x2 is 18/3 vs 15/8, Fisher exact one-sided p=0.111 at n=44. NOT a finding, NOT quoted as one.

CONSEQUENCE FOR G.2: its premise ('the grader calls a reconciler close a take-profit... the grades flatter the defect') may be INVERTED -- on this evidence a reconciler close often genuinely WAS a bracket hit, so the grader may be closer to right than the exit_reason it is checked against. Do not action G.2 on the assumption the grader is wrong.

CONSEQUENCE FOR G.1: every figure here is bounded by the 24.1% broker-truth coverage. Raising pnlCoverage widens this measurement more than any classifier change would.

Evidence: docs/research/exit-attribution-broker-truth-2026-08-22.md

--- 2026-08-22 (s4-pairs-control): THE MECHANISM IS NAMED. ---
The under-attribution is not a classifier error, it is a classifier that never runs. _close_trade_from_order_status's no-closed-pnl fallback (order_monitor.py:6033) hard-codes 'reconciler_filled' and leaves exit_price NULL; _sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit (:8323) later fills the price and NEVER re-runs _classify_broker_exit. Measured: 91 of 155 (58.7%) broker-truth 'reconciler_filled' rows reached a declared level, and 181 of 181 mislabelled rows carry no notes.exit_reason_source -- a 100% signature that none reached the classifier. The 41.3% genuinely-between independently reproduces this row's 41.0%. Tracked for fix as BL-20260822-EXIT-REASON-FROZEN-WHEN-PRICE-ARRIVES-LATE.
items.resolution_criteria: 1) The 3-row residue is diagnosed from the trader journal at close time. Three candidates are ALREADY eliminated (later price refinement, reduce leg, netted-sibling cascade -- see next_action); the surviving one is the _resolve_protective_levels symbol+direction fallback grading a trade against another trade's bracket on a netting account. Confirm or kill THAT, by name. 2) The backfill hypothesis is decided on a POWERED population (re-run when broker-truth coverage rises, or over the full 1293 closed rows rather than the newest 500) -- a p=0.111 result is not acted on. 3) IF a repair is proposed, it re-derives exit_reason ONLY for rows where the stored exit price is broker-truth AND crosses a level, states the row count before and after, and is approved as a money-DB mutation. 4) The 41.0% between-the-brackets residue is characterised separately -- it is the genuine non-bracket exit population and is what a mechanism fix would target.
items.next_action: Start at the 3-row residue -- trades 4928 (AVAXUSDT/bybit_1, 2026-08-22T13:39Z), 4733 (BTCUSDT/bybit_2 REAL MONEY, 2026-08-18T05:14Z), 4180 (BTCUSDT/bybit_2 REAL MONEY, 2026-07-29T14:31Z). All three crossed the STOP by a hair (0.0159/0.0074/0.0210 R). THREE candidates are already eliminated: a later price refinement (no call site writes exit_price without exit_reason, and the site that closed them hands the classifier the same avg_exit_price it stores); a reduce leg (neither marker set); and the netted-sibling cascade (it stamps closed_by=monitor_reconciler_netted_cascade plus an exit_reason_source field, and all three carry plain closed_by=monitor_reconciler). THE SURVIVING CANDIDATE is the level-lookup fallback: _classify_broker_exit resolves via _resolve_linked_package_id and, on a miss, falls back to _resolve_protective_levels(symbol, direction), which returns the most recent matching package for that symbol+direction rather than THIS trade's -- so on a netting account with concurrent same-symbol packages it can grade against another trade's bracket. All three are ict_scalp legs on netting Bybit accounts. Confirm or kill it by pulling the trader journal around those three timestamps and checking whether trades.order_package_id was populated at close time (it is populated on all three today).

updates.note: ⚠️ THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON THIS REVIEW'S HEADLINE EXIT NUMBER. This row measures that on broker-truth exit prices the declared bracket is reached ~3x more often than exit_reason records. My 8.3% declared-bracket exit rate is computed from exit_reason and is therefore a LOWER BOUND — the true rate could be ~25%. I have flagged the 8.3% as a structural finding; this row is why it must not be quoted as precise. Both readings agree the majority of closes are not decision-driven; they disagree on by how much.

items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-22 by static enumeration over src/. 28 call sites of Database.update_trade(...); 8 of them set status='closed' via an INLINE DICT LITERAL. Of those 8, exactly ONE has a package cascade within the following 60 lines (order_monitor.py:3140). The other seven: order_monitor.py:2910, :3587, :5250, :7734, :9054, units/accounts/execute.py:1719 (the intent_reduce parent-chunk close), units/strategies/pairs_executor.py:707 (_close_pair -- FIXED this session).

WARNING ON THE DENOMINATOR: the regex sees only inline dict literals. The remaining 20 update_trade call sites pass a dict VARIABLE, whose status the matcher cannot read -- including _close_trade_from_order_status itself, which DOES cascade. So '8 close sites' is a LOWER BOUND on the close-site count and '7 uncascaded' is a lower bound on the gap. The enumeration is a floor, not a census, and is labelled so rather than being quoted as complete.

WHY IT MATTERS: _cascade_close_linked_package is the only writer of a real close_reason onto order_packages. A close site that skips it leaves the package open until _sweep_stuck_linked_packages stamps the generic 'stuck_cascade_recovered' -- a bookkeeping repair that is NOT an exit, which is what makes order_packages.close_reason unusable as an exit record (BL-20260822-PACKAGE-CLOSE-REASON-IS-NOT-THE-EXIT-RECORD).

CONFIRMED LIVE for the pairs instance, with both arms reconciling EXACTLY: pairs legs closed via the monitor 57 <-> packages carrying a real reason 57; pairs legs closed via _close_pair/intent_reduce 120 <-> packages left for the sweep 120 (109 swept + 11 not yet). pairs_revert/pairs_stop/pairs_half_open_cleanup appear on 99 TRADE rows and ZERO package rows. Main path by contrast is 15/323 = 4.6% stuck_cascade_recovered vs pairs 109/177 = 61.6% -- a 13.4x concentration, which is what rules out a tick-ordering race (that would be uniform).

The intent_reduce site (execute.py:1719) is the next-largest instance: intent_reduce_executed 48 + intent_reduce 10 on the main path, plus 21 on pairs.

=== CLASSIFIED 2026-08-22, AND THE HEADLINE COUNT WAS MY OWN OVER-REPORT. ===
⚠️ This row originally said 'seven of eight sites do not cascade'. That is WRONG and is corrected here. The detector searched for `_cascade_close_linked_package` within 60 lines -- i.e. for ONE HELPER'S NAME -- when the question is whether the PACKAGE GETS CLOSED. Four sites close it by calling `db.update_order_package` directly, which the grep cannot see. Measuring the mechanism instead of the effect is the same class as everything else on this programme's list.

CORRECTLY HANDLED (4) -- annotated in place, no fix needed:
  * order_monitor.py:3140 -- calls the cascade helper (the one true positive).
  * order_monitor.py:3587 `_close_unattributable_orphan` -- closes the package at :3605 with close_reason='exit_coverage_no_strategy', matching the trade's own exit_reason.
  * order_monitor.py:5250 `_watchdog_stuck_strategies` -- the package is force-closed EARLIER ON THE SAME BRANCH at :5147 with close_reason='stuck_strategy_watchdog'; the source comment says 'Force-close the package + cascade the trade', and :5250 is the cascade-the-trade half.
  * order_monitor.py:9054 `_close_options_row` -- closes the package at :9036 with close_reason='options_expiry_assignment'.

GENUINE GAPS (3) -- annotated as gaps, NOT fixed (Tier-2, see below):
  * order_monitor.py:2910 `_reconcile_orphan_exchange_positions` (exit_reason='adopted_orphan_disappeared'). ⚠️ THE INTUITIVE EXEMPTION IS FALSE AND WAS MEASURED FALSE: 'an adopted orphan has no package' -- but 44 of 74 setup_type='adopted_orphan' rows carry a NON-NULL order_package_id (filter_state asserted 'applied'), and 26 rows close with exactly this exit_reason. I assumed the exemption and the measurement caught me.
  * order_monitor.py:7734 `_netting_apply_close` -- the full-close branch closes the trade and the function contains NO package reference of any kind. `netting_attributed` is 5.3% of main-path closes, so this fires in production.
  * execute.py:1719 (intent_reduce parent-chunk close) -- the LARGEST: intent_reduce_executed 48 + intent_reduce 10 on the main path, plus 21 on pairs.

WHY THE THREE ARE NOT PATCHED IN THE SAME BREATH AS THE ANNOTATIONS. `_sweep_stuck_linked_packages` has NO age gate -- it force-closes on the same monitor tick -- so adding a cascade advances the close by at most ~1 tick. But the strategy-monocle gate reads OPEN packages, so that ~1 tick is a real (if small) change to how soon a live strategy may signal again. That is an order-path timing change, hence Tier-2 and prepared rather than shipped.

AN ARGUMENT THE OTHER WAY, worth putting to the operator: the sweep fires `enqueue_stuck_package_sweep` on EVERY non-zero run, with its own source comment saying a non-zero sweep 'means a PRIMARY cascade path missed ... surface it so the gap is visible'. With pairs at 109 and intent_reduce at ~79 in the sample window, that alert has been firing routinely -- i.e. an alarm that fires constantly and is walked past, which this repo names as its own P1. Closing the three gaps would QUIETEN a real alarm rather than merely tidy a label. #10145 already removed the largest single contributor (pairs).

items.title: pnlCoverage is not one number and not a timer problem -- the fills->trade matcher's 5% qty gate rejects netted closes, so the most-netted account sits at 0.081 coverage while holding the MOST fills
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-22 while working workplan gate G.1 ('pnlCoverage must start rising after the hourly-fills fix'). G.1's premise needs restating on all three counts.

(1) COVERAGE IS NOT ONE NUMBER. /api/bot/performance is REAL-MONEY ONLY (it excludes paper), and reads pnlCoverage 24h 0.6667 (n=3) / 7d 0.6667 (n=12) / 30d 0.75 (n=28) / all 0.78 (n=400). /api/bot/trades/closed (real money, newest 200) is 180/200 = 0.90 measured. Meanwhile the same measurement over Bybit rows in the newest 500 CLOSED trades of all classes splits: bybit_2 (real money) 23/37 = 0.622; bybit_portfolio (paper) 10/34 = 0.294; bybit_1 (paper/demo) 30/371 = 0.081. A blended figure over both funding classes is not a quantity about anything, and the alarming '0.06' is dominated by bybit_1, which is 84% of the closed population.

(2) THE WINDOWS ARE NESTED, SO A SNAPSHOT CANNOT SHOW DIRECTION. 24h/7d/30d/all are subsets of each other; comparing them conflates recency with the fix. The only valid direction test is the SAME window across time, and at real-money volume (1-5 closes/day) the post-fix cohort aged >=24h is n=5. NOT ANSWERABLE at real-money volume, and labelled so rather than answered.

(3) THE ROOT CAUSE IS NOT FILL CAPTURE. The fills ARE being pulled for the demo account -- /api/bot/pnl/exchange/fills shows bybit_1 with 541 fills over 30d, the MOST of any account (bybit_2: 90, bybit_portfolio: 60), current to 2026-08-22T13:36Z. src/runtime/exchange_accounts.py::live_bybit_fill_accounts explicitly includes paper-class Bybit accounts. So capture was never the bottleneck for bybit_1 and the hourly-timer change could not have moved it.

MECHANISM (code-supported + measured): src/runtime/fills_pnl.py accumulates fills until `filled >= target*(1-QTY_TOLERANCE)` then REJECTS unless `abs(filled - target) <= target*QTY_TOLERANCE`, with QTY_TOLERANCE = 0.05. On a one-way-netting account ONE exchange fill closes a position spanning N journal rows, so a single fill overshoots one row's qty. Measured median fill-qty / trade-qty on the top symbols: bybit_1 SOLUSDT 1.40, ETHUSDT 1.44, XRPUSDT 1.31, BTCUSDT 0.94 -- a 31-44% overshoot against a 5% tolerance, i.e. 6-9x over, so the gate returns None and the row falls back to candle_at_close (ESTIMATED). bybit_2's fills are PARTIALS (ratio 0.14-0.80) which accumulate correctly to the target and match -- which is exactly why it sits at 0.622 with a fraction of the fills. bybit_1 also has 6 of 8 symbols traded by >1 strategy (max netting overlap); bybit_2 has 3 of 4 with 10x fewer rows.

STATE THE LIMIT: the fill/trade ratios above are MEDIANS per symbol, not a per-trade join. The direction and the order of magnitude are solid; a per-trade confirmation is the next step and is not claimed here.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE METRIC: this is the direct cause of BL-20260822-EXIT-ATTRIBUTION-UNDER-REPORTS-BRACKET-HITS being measurable on only 24.1% of the main order path. Raising coverage widens every exit measurement -- which is precisely why G.1 gates items 1.1 and 1.2.

WHY THE FIX IS NOT TIER-1: loosening QTY_TOLERANCE would attach a whole-POSITION fill to ONE row. For the exit PRICE that is arguably correct (every netted sibling closed at that price), but the same record also carries qty and realized pnl, and attributing those per-row is the identical problem NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_MODE already exists to stage annotate-first. A careless widening would stamp exit_price_source='exchange_fill' -- a MEASURED grade -- onto a row whose economics were inferred, which is strictly worse than the honest candle_at_close it replaces.
items.resolution_criteria: 1) A per-TRADE (not per-symbol-median) join confirming the qty gate is what rejects bybit_1's fills -- for a sample of rejected rows, show the accumulated fill qty and the target, and show the overshoot exceeds QTY_TOLERANCE. 2) A decision, taken deliberately and not by widening a constant: either (a) attribute the netted fill's PRICE only, under a provenance grade that is NOT plain 'exchange_fill' (so a per-row inferred split is never labelled broker truth), or (b) route this through the existing NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_MODE machinery, which already stages annotate-before-apply, rather than adding a second attribution mechanism. 3) Any change ships annotate-first with a soak log showing which rows it WOULD upgrade, reviewed before apply. 4) G.1's direction test is re-specified to be lag-aware and per-funding-class: coverage of trades closed in window W measured at a fixed age (>= 24h after close), real money and paper reported SEPARATELY, never blended.
items.next_action: Do the per-trade join on a sample of bybit_1 rejected rows to confirm the qty gate is the rejecter, then put the two options in criterion 2 to the operator. Do NOT widen QTY_TOLERANCE.

updates.note: HIGH-VALUE AND IT EXPLAINS THIS REVIEW'S COVERAGE NUMBERS. The 5% qty gate rejecting netted closes is why pnlCoverage is structured by ACCOUNT and PATH rather than being one number: real-money lifetime reads 0.7591 while paper reads 0.1897, and the netted-heavy paths (netting_attributed, intent_reduce) sit at 0.0. This row is the mechanism behind the provenance class that dominates the backlog.

items.title: _sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit fills in exit_price after the close and never re-runs _classify_broker_exit -- so 91 of 155 broker-truth 'reconciler_filled' rows (58.7%) actually reached a declared bracket level
items.detail:
MECHANISM, traced in code and confirmed on the live journal. (1) _reconcile_open_trades (order_monitor.py:3823) delegates to _close_trade_from_order_status (:5832). (2) When the venue has not yet booked a closed-pnl record -- the steady-state case seconds after a close -- control reaches the else fallback at :6033, which leaves exit_price NULL and HARD-CODES exit_reason='reconciler_filled'. The classifier is correctly NOT called: there is no price to classify with. (3) _sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit (:8323) then selects exactly those rows (status='closed' AND COALESCE(is_backtest,0)=0 AND pnl IS NULL), recovers the record, and writes exit_price, pnl, pnl_percent, notes.exit_price_source and the closed-pnl note key (:8488) -- and NEVER touches exit_reason, NEVER calls _classify_broker_exit. Nothing else revisits the label. The price becomes known and the label that depends on it is never recomputed.

POPULATION: 572 trades rows with exit_reason='reconciler_filled' (all closed, all non-backtest; filter_state asserted 'applied' on both pages). 395 are GRADEABLE -- exit_price > 0 AND a linked order_packages row with at least one positive level. The 177 excluded are 172 with no package + 5 with no price; EXCLUDED, not counted either way.

Applying _classify_broker_exit's OWN inequality to the stored price and the row's OWN package levels:
  * BROKER-TRUTH price (bybit_closed_pnl 71 + exchange_fill 20), n=155: 83 sl + 8 tp = 91 MISLABELLED (58.7%); 64 genuinely between (41.3%).
  * estimated or worse (local_markprice 40, candle_at_close 35, netted_duplicate_unattributed 10, recorded_exit_price 5), n=240: 70 sl + 20 tp = 90 (37.5%); 150 between (62.5%).
QUOTE THE 91, NOT THE 181 -- the wider figure rests partly on local_markprice, the FABRICATED class src/runtime/provenance.py exists to distrust. By account the 181 are bybit_1 155, bybit_2 14, bybit_portfolio 12.

TWO CONFIRMATIONS. (a) 181 of 181 mislabelled rows carry NO notes.exit_reason_source key -- the marker the classifying branch (:5923) stamps ('price_vs_pkg_bracket' when resolved, 'unresolved' when it looked and found the fill mid-range). A 100% signature that none reached the classifier, not a tendency. (b) The 14 rows in this population that DID reach it are all 'unresolved' and ALL 14 still grade None on today's stored price -- so 'classified then the price moved' contributes ZERO rows, and the prior session's elimination of later price refinement stands.

THE STANDING HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED. Item 1.1's residue (trades 4928 / 4733 / 4180) was suspected of _classify_broker_exit falling back to _resolve_protective_levels(symbol, direction) and grading against ANOTHER trade's bracket on a netting account. Each of the three has a linked package with the correct linked_trade_id and positive sl/tp IDENTICAL to the trade's own, so that fallback branch is unreachable -- and on those levels all three satisfy the production inequality for 'sl'.

CORROBORATION: the 41.3% genuinely-between on broker truth independently reproduces item 1.1's 41.0%, on a differently-scoped cut. This is the ATTRIBUTION defect item 1.1 concluded existed, named.

SCOPE NOT CLAIMED: all 181 rows are Bybit accounts and _sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit is Bybit-specific. Whether an equivalent late-price writer exists for IBKR or Alpaca is NOT measured here and is not asserted.

--- CORRECTION 2026-08-22, same session: THE CHAIN'S SHAPE WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN, and this row's first draft called it unnamed. That claim is WITHDRAWN. ---
src/runtime/provenance.py's module docstring (steps 1-3, written 2026-07-30 for the fabricated-PnL incident) already says the fallback pins exit_reason to 'reconciler_filled' and that '_classify_broker_exit is downstream of a price the code deliberately refuses to fetch'. What it does NOT cover, and what is new here:
  * SCOPE -- it is written about DEMO accounts; trades 4733 and 4180 are bybit_2, REAL MONEY.
  * THE HARM -- it is about the PnL (fabricated by _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced from a sweep-time mark). This is about the LABEL, which stays wrong even after a BROKER-TRUTH price arrives via _sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit.
  * STATUS -- the PnL half WAS FIXED on 2026-07-30 (anchored to closed_at, Tier-2). The label half was never fixed and is live today.
  * SCALE -- 91 of 155 (58.7%) on broker truth; the 181/181 missing-exit_reason_source signature.
So the contribution is not the mechanism's shape but that the 2026-07-30 fix closed one half and left the other, that it is not confined to demo, and that it is measurable.

AND THAT DOCSTRING'S STEP 1 IS ITSELF STALE -- corrected in the same PR. The demo branch was NARROWED on 2026-07-30 (#8111, BL-20260730-BROKER-TRUTH-COLLECTED-NEVER-READ): demo no longer returns None, it resolves the exit from the exchange FILLS store. It does not 'refuse to fetch' any more.

HOW THIS MEETS G.1 -- the same population from the other side. Cross-tab of the 181 mislabelled rows by account x price provenance: bybit_1 155 rows (bybit_closed_pnl 60, candle_at_close 31, local_markprice 37, exchange_fill 13, netted_dup 10, recorded 4), bybit_2 14, bybit_portfolio 12. Only 73 of bybit_1's 155 (47.1%) carry a broker-truth price. Since the narrowing, demo resolves from fills -- and fills_pnl.py's 5% QTY_TOLERANCE rejects bybit_1's netted closes at a measured 31-44% overshoot, so the price lands as an estimate. G.1 and this row describe ONE population. WARNING: do not read that 47.1% as the 47.1% in provenance.py/#8111 -- different quantities that coincide numerically (that one is fabricated share of bybit_1 CLOSES; this one is broker-truth share among bybit_1's MISLABELLED rows).

--- 2026-08-22T18:4xZ: BOTH HALVES SHIPPED (Tier-2, operator-approved). Row KEPT OPEN on the live control. ---
FORWARD FIX in order_monitor._sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit. Three guards, each load-bearing and each tested:
  1. is_reduce_leg derived exactly as at the other call site. The sweep's SELECT did NOT read setup_type before this change; it does now. Without it is_reduce_leg is always False and an intent_reduce leg -- whose bracket can be INVERTED relative to the order direction -- gets mislabelled sl/tp, the precise failure _classify_broker_exit's exclusion exists to prevent.
  2. Only a row still carrying the GENERIC reason ('' or reconciler_filled) is relabelled. The sweep selects on pnl IS NULL, which can include rows another path closed with a real reason (pairs_*, sl_cross); overwriting one would destroy a better record than the one being written.
  3. The classification is wrapped so a failure NEVER reaches the price write. The pnl/exit_price update is the load-bearing half.
exit_reason_source is stamped ONLY when the classifier actually ran, so its ABSENCE keeps meaning 'never reached the classifier' -- the marker that made the 181/181 signature readable. summary['reclassified'] is declared in the initialiser, not created on first use, so a run that relabelled nothing reports 0 rather than omitting the key.

HISTORICAL HALF: scripts/ops/reclassify_frozen_exit_reasons.py. ANNOTATE-FIRST (--apply required to write); --provenance scopes the WRITE and never the MEASUREMENT (every candidate is computed and annotated regardless -- the netting reconciler's 2026-08-09 correction); imports _classify_broker_exit rather than re-deriving it; refuses to clobber a real reason or grade a reduce; records exit_reason_prior + exit_reason_backfilled_at so the pass is reversible from the row itself. Declares '# wiring: manual-only' -- unwired-artifacts caught that omission.

VERIFICATION: 10 of 11 forward-fix tests FAIL pre-fix, 11 PASS post-fix. THE ONE THAT PASSES PRE-FIX is the failure-guard test, and it passes TRIVIALLY -- before the fix there is no classifier that could fail, so the property holds vacuously. Stated rather than counted as 11/11. Plus 5 end-to-end tests on the historical tool against a real sqlite journal. 99 related tests pass. provenance-consumer-guard / collapsed-state-guard / canonical-db-resolver clean.

WHY STILL OPEN: (a) the historical pass has NOT been run against the live journal -- it is staged, and running it is the next concrete step (start --provenance broker_truth, the 91 rows); (b) A LIVE POSITIVE CONTROL IS OWED -- the forward fix has not yet been exercised by a real late-price close. The control: a Bybit row that takes the no-record fallback at close and is later price-filled by this sweep should end with exit_reason 'sl'/'tp' AND notes.exit_reason_source 'price_vs_pkg_bracket'. Unit tests only until then.
items.why_it_matters: exit_reason is the exit record every downstream exit-mechanism measurement reads -- items 1.1, 1.5 and G.2 all rest on it. A stop that fired at the broker is recorded as a generic reconciler close on 58.7% of the rows where broker truth can adjudicate, which understates bracket hits and overstates 'exited between the brackets'. It also mislabels the operator ping: _reconcile_open_trades branches on _exit_reason to choose between a calm 'SL/TP exit detected by reconciler' headline and the generic one, so the operator is not told a stop fired.
items.next_action: TIER-2, PREPARED NOT SHIPPED, needs one operator OK. _sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit already holds db, the row and avg_exit_price at the point it writes the price: call _classify_broker_exit(db, row, avg_exit_price, is_reduce_leg=...) there and, when it resolves, add exit_reason to the updates dict and stamp notes.exit_reason_source. HAZARD, load-bearing: is_reduce_leg MUST be carried across -- the classifier returns None for a reduce leg because a reduce's bracket can be inverted relative to the order direction, and the sweep's SELECT does not currently read setup_type. Omitting it would mislabel reduces as sl/tp, which is the failure that exclusion exists to prevent. SEPARATE DECISION: forward-fixing changes new closes only. Retroactively relabelling the 181 historical rows is a second Tier-2 write and should be decided on its own, with the provenance split in view -- the 90 rows resting on estimated prices are a weaker case than the 91 on broker truth. Full prepared detail: docs/research/exit-reason-frozen-at-close-2026-08-22.md section 5.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) A LIVE row post-deploy that took the no-record fallback and was later price-filled carries exit_reason 'sl' or 'tp' with notes.exit_reason_source 'price_vs_pkg_bracket' -- read from the journal, not inferred from the merge. AND (2) an intent_reduce leg in the same window still carries 'reconciler_filled' (the exclusion survived). AND (3) the historical pass has been RUN at --provenance broker_truth with its annotate JSONL reviewed, and the re-measured mislabelled count over the broker-truth population is materially below 91/155 with the population restated.
evidence: docs/research/exit-reason-frozen-at-close-2026-08-22.md

items.tier: 1 (observation + alerting shape) — any protection change on the position is Tier-2
items.title: ib_paper/MGC is target-naked AND monitor-blind at the same time, and each alert cites the other's missing half as its backstop
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-22T18:1xZ on /api/bot/notifications, six banners, two of them alerts.

The SAME position carries two independent conditions:
  (a) ALERT ib_target_naked: 'ib_paper/MGC: position 95.0 has 0.0 of take-profit coverage against a declared TP of 4393.02071429 - the position can only stop out or run' (since 17:58:29Z, re-latched on the trader restart).
  (b) WARNING monitor_blindness: 'ict_scalp_mgc_15m | MGC - Reason: candles_unavailable (for 3 consecutive ticks) - Broker SL/TP backstop (if any) still holds, but monitor()-driven exits are NOT running.' (since 17:36:26Z).

EACH ALERT'S STATED BACKSTOP IS THE OTHER'S MISSING HALF. The target-naked alert is tolerable because the stop rests and the monitor can still act; the monitor-blind alert is tolerable because 'the broker SL/TP backstop (if any) still holds'. On THIS position the take-profit does not exist and the monitor is not running, so the stop is the only remaining protection - and neither alert says so, because neither reads the other's condition.

This is not a claim that either alert is individually wrong. Both are accurate. The gap is that the banner feed reports them as two independent rows and nothing composes them, so the compound state - which is strictly worse than either - is invisible on every surface.

SCOPE, STATED: ib_paper is PAPER money, so this is not money-at-risk. It IS an M20 evidence source, and a leg whose exits are neither declared nor monitored produces exit rows M20 cannot interpret.

SELF-RESOLVING FOR THIS INSTANCE: the operator-approved Sunday 2026-08-23T22:30Z routine (trig_014S3NAzMKy2Ac2AM2GgyRE5) FLATTENS MGC, which clears both conditions on this position. The CLASS is what this row is about - the composition gap will recur on the next position that hits both.
items.why_it_matters: An alarm whose tolerability argument depends on a second condition that is ALSO alarming is not a graded alarm - it is two half-measurements read as if independent. This is the same shape as the collapsed-state family the repo already enforces: the individual states are emitted correctly and no consumer reads them together.
items.next_action: TIER-1: decide whether the banner feed should compose - i.e. whether a position carrying BOTH ib_target_naked and monitor_blindness should surface as one higher-severity row naming the stop as sole remaining protection, rather than two rows each citing the other. MEASURE FIRST, do not build blind: count how often the two co-occur on one position over the available banner/outcome history. If it is rare, a composed banner is not worth the code; if it is common, the two-row rendering has been understating the state routinely. Explicitly NOT proposed here: any change to what protection is placed - that is Tier-2 and belongs with BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) a measured co-occurrence rate is on record and the operator has decided the two-row rendering is adequate, with the reason stated; or (b) a position holding both conditions surfaces as a single row that names the stop as the only remaining protection, demonstrated on a real or synthetic co-occurrence. A row closed on 'the Sunday routine flattened MGC' does NOT satisfy this - that clears the instance, not the class.
evidence: docs/research/m20-readiness-2026-08-22.md

progress.note: INSTANCE CLEARED, CLASS STILL OPEN - which is what this row is about, per its own text. Measured 2026-08-23T16:35Z on /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper: all three ib_paper positions now carry BOTH legs in one OCA group - MGC oca-protect-389 (STP 4371.1 / LMT 4393.0, qty 95 both), MES oca-protect-408 (STP 7533.75 / LMT 8390.5, qty 15 both), MHG 308977633 (STP 6.2215 / LMT 7.1415, qty 29). /api/bot/notifications at 16:38Z reads has_alerts:false with no ib_target_naked banner. Condition (a) target-naked is therefore GONE for MGC. Condition (b) monitor_blindness PERSISTS (pkg-b1582c365d264330, ict_scalp_mgc_15m, candles_unavailable), but its stated tolerability argument - 'broker SL/TP backstop (if any) still holds' - is now TRUE rather than vacuous, because the bracket is two-sided. The compound state this row names is broken for this instance. NOT CLOSED: nothing composes the two conditions, so the next position hitting both is still invisible.

updates.note: Re-validated: two alerts each citing the other's missing half as its basis is a circular-evidence trap. Live: ib_paper holds only MES now (no MGC position), and its bracket is complete — so the specific instance has cleared while the alert-interaction defect has not.

items.title: diag_fetch.sh's 404 message names path-form as the cause when the real cause is a non-diag surface
items.detail: scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh:117 builds "${base}/api/diag/${path}", so the /api/diag/ prefix is HARDCODED and the tool serves that surface only (its own header, line 2, says so). Passing a valid non-diag route therefore produces /api/diag/api/bot/notifications -> 404. That behaviour is correct-by-contract and is NOT the finding. The finding is the MESSAGE: line 136 explains a 404 as "check the path form (pass 'version', not '/api/diag/version')" -- a cause no code path tested for this input. The caller did not get the path form wrong; they addressed a surface this tool does not serve, and the advice points away from that. MEASURED 2026-08-22T20:27Z during a session wrap: diag_fetch.sh '/api/bot/notifications' returned answered_404 while a direct curl to https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/bot/notifications returned HTTP 200 with 4 live banners -- the route is healthy and the tool reported it missing. The envelope's other half is GOOD and did its job: answered_404 correctly separated 'the host answered' from 'we never reached a host', which is what stopped the reader concluding an outage. This is sub-class A of CLAUDE.md's 'Diagnostic provenance -- UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT': the label is confident and names a substitution the code did not test.
items.why_it_matters: diag_fetch.sh is the PRIMARY read path for every session that cannot reach the VM directly, so its failure messages are load-bearing. A 404 whose stated cause is wrong costs a session either a wasted path-form retry loop or -- worse -- the conclusion that a healthy production route is broken. In this instance the route was /api/bot/notifications, the banner feed the Android app and dashboard render for can't-miss conditions; concluding it was 404ing would have manufactured an incident.
items.next_action: Branch the 404 message on whether the requested path was already outside the diag surface. If the caller's argument starts with api/ but not api/diag/, say so explicitly -- 'this tool serves /api/diag/* only; <path> is a bot route, fetch it directly' -- instead of the path-form advice. Do NOT silently widen the tool to proxy arbitrary routes: the diag bearer is surface-scoped, and a fetcher that sometimes attaches it to non-diag routes is a worse problem than a confusing 404.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when diag_fetch.sh given a non-diag api/* path prints a message naming the surface mismatch, proven by a test asserting the old path-form wording is NOT emitted for that input (presence of the new string alone is insufficient -- both branches must be distinguishable).
evidence: scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh:117 -- "${base}/api/diag/${path}" (prefix hardcoded)
scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh:136 -- the 404 branch's path-form advice
2026-08-22T20:27Z: diag_fetch '/api/bot/notifications' -> answered_404; direct curl same host+path -> HTTP 200, count=4 banners

updates.note: Re-validated: diagnostic-provenance sub-class A. I used diag_fetch ~15 times today without hitting a 404, so unexercised this session.

items.title: A session reported a CI overrun that never happened, having inferred elapsed time from the sleeps it had ISSUED rather than reading a clock
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-22. While waiting on PR #10157's pytest-run, this session reported the job stuck at '~35 minutes', then '~40+ min against a 10.1-11.6 min baseline', '>3x and still climbing', and RELEASED THE MERGE SLOT WITHOUT MERGING on that basis, posting it to the coordination board twice and arming a self check-in trigger for it. Ground truth from the job's own timestamps: job 20:48:47 -> 21:00:31 = 11.73 min; the 'Run tests' step 20:49:47 -> 21:00:29 = 10.70 min. DEAD ON BASELINE. There was never an anomaly. MECHANISM: the session issued background sleeps (240+420+400+300+360 s ~= 28 min) but `run_in_background` RETURNS INSTANTLY, and it polled the API immediately after each call instead of waiting for the completion notification. Real wall-clock between polls was its own turn latency. It then narrated elapsed time by SUMMING THE SLEEPS IT HAD STARTED, and never read a clock once. ⚠️ THE COMPOUNDING DETAIL IS THE INSTRUCTIVE ONE: the session DID check for the known stale-status trap, and that check was CORRECT -- the sibling pytest-collect started the same second and updated normally, so the API genuinely was not stale. Rigorous verification, applied to the WRONG PREMISE. Checking the API's freshness could never have caught an error in the session's own arithmetic. It also correctly refused to read get_workflow_run_usage's `total_ms: 0` as evidence of a stall -- and then leaned on a fabricated elapsed time in the same breath. And it had the refuting evidence in hand: a duration comparison run minutes earlier showed runs 8292 (11.5 min) and 8291 (11.4 min) as today's genuine-execution baseline.
items.why_it_matters: The cost was real: a green PR sat unmerged, the board carried two false anomaly reports for other sessions to act on, and a trigger was armed for a condition that did not exist. Sessions poll CI constantly, so this is not a one-off -- and it is the same class the repo already enforces against elsewhere ('always state the population', 'verify your own output too, hardest when it confirms what you expected'). The novel part worth carrying is that CAREFUL VERIFICATION OF THE WRONG PREMISE reads exactly like diligence.
items.next_action: Practice, not code: when reporting elapsed time, READ A CLOCK -- take the difference between the API's own `started_at`/`completed_at`, or run `date -u` -- and never infer duration from sleeps issued, turns taken, or context consumed. If a duration is load-bearing enough to change a decision (merge / do not merge), it is load-bearing enough to measure. Consider adding this to the session-coordination skill's merge-protocol section beside the existing 'read the check runs by name' rule, which this sits directly next to.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when the merge-protocol guidance states explicitly that any elapsed-time or duration claim used in a merge decision must be derived from timestamps, with the failure mode named (inferring from issued waits). A note that merely says 'be careful about timing' does not close this -- the failure was confident precision, not carelessness.
evidence: step 'Run tests': 20:49:47Z -> 21:00:29Z (10.70 min), conclusion success
board comments 5382539964 and 5382547767 carry the retracted overrun claim; 5382681402 is the retraction
trigger trig_019fVx79hn9MBnimmLEMAGRP armed on the false premise, since deleted
same-day genuine-execution baseline: pytest-run runs 8292 = 11.5 min, 8291 = 11.4 min

updates.note: Re-validated: a session reporting an overrun that never happened. The lesson generalises — measure, do not infer — and it is the same discipline that caught three of my own wrong readings today.

items.title: A money-path comment names two strategies as `execution: shadow` that are both live
items.detail: src/units/accounts/execute.py (the prop no-emit branch, ~:235) documents its own purpose with "the shadow prop variants (trend_donchian_{sol,eth}_prop, which are execution: shadow)". MEASURED 2026-08-23 against config/strategies.yaml: BOTH are `execution: live`, as was eth_pullback_prop_2h before this session demoted it — i.e. at the moment of reading, ALL THREE prop-routed strategies were live and NOTHING exercised that branch in production. Field beats comment. Found while verifying, before a Tier-3 demotion, that `execution: shadow` genuinely suppresses prop ticket emission — the branch itself is real and correct by reading; only the claim about who exercises it is stale.
items.why_it_matters: The comment was about to be used as PRECEDENT for a live money-path change ('shadowing a *_prop variant is an established pattern'). It is not established — the demotion shipped this session is the FIRST live exerciser of that branch. A stale comment that manufactures false precedent is worse than no comment, because it substitutes for the verification it appears to provide.
items.next_action: Correct the comment to describe the branch's PURPOSE without naming strategies whose gate state drifts, or name them with an as-of date. Do not delete the branch — it is load-bearing and now genuinely in use.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when the comment no longer asserts a gate state it does not verify.

updates.note:
RESOLVED. Criterion: 'the comment no longer asserts a gate state it does not verify.'

RE-MEASURED AT HEAD (814d019b) against config/strategies.yaml before editing, because the row is two days old and the gate moves under Tier-3 decisions:
  trend_donchian_sol_prop  enabled True  execution live
  trend_donchian_eth_prop  enabled True  execution live
  eth_pullback_prop_2h     enabled True  execution shadow
So the comment is still wrong about BOTH strategies it names, and the demotion this row mentions did land — there IS now exactly one leg exercising that branch, just not either of the two named. The stale claim was therefore wrong in both directions at once.

THE FIX IS TO STOP NAMING THEM, not to re-name them correctly. src/units/accounts/execute.py now says the branch serves 'a shadow/dry prop leg', records what the previous wording claimed and that it was false, and points the reader at config/strategies.yaml::<name>.execution for who is there now. Re-naming today's occupants would have re-armed the same defect for the next demotion — the comment cannot verify the gate, so it must not assert it. The BRANCH itself was correct by reading and is untouched; only the claim about who exercises it changed.

items.title: exit-coverage-matrix-guard is diff-scoped to 3 files but joins against config/strategies.yaml, which is not one of them
items.detail: scripts/ci/run_guards.py:259 scopes `exit-coverage-matrix-guard` with `when.globs = [docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json, scripts/research/m20_coverage_rollup.py, scripts/research/m20_explode_coverage_rows.py]`. But the check it runs (`m20_coverage_rollup.py --check`) JOINS the matrix against **config/strategies.yaml** and fails when the two disagree about a leg's `execution`. config/strategies.yaml is NOT in the glob list, so a change to the runtime gate can break the join while the diff-scoped guard never runs. MEASURED 2026-08-23 on PR #10161: demoting eth_pullback_prop_2h live -> shadow in config/strategies.yaml left the matrix saying `execution: live`. Local `run_guards.py` reported **'All relevant guards passed'** with exit-coverage-matrix-guard in its SKIP list. CI caught it only because tests/test_guards_uncommitted_work.py runs the guard explicitly via `--all --only`, and tests/test_m20_coverage_join.py asserts the real join is clean — i.e. TESTS caught it, not the guard's own diff scoping.
items.why_it_matters: The matrix is M20's DONE-CONDITION DENOMINATOR, not decoration: it is what 'x of 468 cells resolved' is computed over, and it records each leg's execution state. A gate change that silently desynchronises it corrupts the milestone's own progress measure. Worse, the failure is silent LOCALLY and green — 'All relevant guards passed' is exactly the reassuring output that stops a session looking further. This is the guard analogue of the session's recurring finding: an operation whose non-execution is indistinguishable from its success.
items.next_action: Add `config/strategies.yaml` to the guard's `when.globs`. Then verify the fix DISCRIMINATES: a strategies.yaml change that desyncs the matrix must make the guard RUN and FAIL, and a strategies.yaml change that does not touch a matrix leg must not make it fail. Consider a general audit: any guard whose check reads a file outside its own `when` scope has the same hole.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when a diff touching ONLY config/strategies.yaml selects exit-coverage-matrix-guard in run_guards.py, proven by a test that fails if the glob is reverted — presence of the glob alone is not sufficient.
evidence: scripts/ci/run_guards.py:259-263 — when.globs omits config/strategies.yaml
PR #10161 job 97144958235: 2 failed, 12153 passed — both failures the same matrix/config disagreement
local run_guards.py on the same diff: 'All relevant guards passed', guard in the skip list

updates.note: Re-validated: diff-scoped to 3 files while joining against config/strategies.yaml, which is not one of them — so a strategies.yaml change cannot trip it. Same shape as BL-20260823-GUARD-SCOPED-TO-ONE-SIDE-OF-ITS-OWN-JOIN. Two guards, one defect.
