items.title: The tp-geometry ratchet silently loosens whenever the live cell population shrinks, and only its own self-tests notice
items.detail: `docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json::tp_geometry_legend._unstamped_ceiling` is an ABSOLUTE upper bound on live cells carrying no `tp_geometry`, enforced by `m20_coverage_rollup.py --check` (exit-coverage-matrix-guard). Because it counts **LIVE** cells, ANY change that removes live cells lowers the true count while the recorded ceiling stays put -- creating slack, and slack is exactly what makes the ratchet stop detecting. MEASURED 2026-08-23 on PR #10161. Demoting ONE leg (eth_pullback_prop_2h, live -> shadow) removed its 9 cells: live 423 -> 414, of which 7 were stamped and 2 unstamped, so the true unstamped count fell 239 -> 237 against a recorded ceiling still reading 239. **Two cells of slack.** Consequence: un-stamping ONE cell no longer breached, and BOTH planted-omission self-tests in tests/test_m20_tp_geometry_guard.py failed with an EMPTY problem list -- the probe going quiet. ⚠️ THE CEILING NOTE ALREADY DOCUMENTS THIS EXACT FAILURE, but only for the STAMPING case (2026-08-17: 'stamping two cells without lowering the ceiling left 2 cells of slack ... the probe going quiet, exactly the failure mode that file exists to prevent'). It did not generalise to population changes. I ratcheted 239 -> 237 and widened the written rule to 'LOWER IT WHENEVER THE LIVE DENOMINATOR FALLS, not only when you stamp'. ⚠️ THAT IS A MITIGATION AND A NOTE, NOT A MECHANISM. Nothing computes the ceiling from the population; it is a hand-maintained number that a human must remember to lower, and the ONLY thing that catches a stale one is the guard's own two self-tests -- which fail in the confusing 'empty problem list' shape rather than naming the cause.
items.why_it_matters: A ratchet whose slack grows silently is worse than no ratchet: it keeps reporting PASS while its detection power decays, and the decay is invisible from the guard's own output. This is the same class as the session's other findings -- an operation whose non-execution is indistinguishable from its success -- and it sits on M20's done-condition instrument, so the milestone's own progress measure is what degrades. Note the asymmetry that found it: NEITHER of the two guard holes this config change exposed was caught by a guard; both were caught by TESTS that exercise guards.
items.next_action: Preferred: make the ceiling DERIVED rather than declared -- have `--check` compare the measured unstamped count against the count recorded at the last ratchet AND against the live-cell total, so a shrinking denominator either auto-tightens or fails loudly with the cause named. If it must stay hand-maintained, then at minimum make the guard FAIL when `ceiling > measured_unstamped` (slack is itself the defect) rather than only when `measured > ceiling`, and make the message say 'the ceiling is stale by N cells', not an empty list. ⚠️ Verify the fix DISCRIMINATES: a genuine new unstamped cell must still breach, and a legitimate stamping must not fire.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when shrinking the live population (e.g. demoting a leg) either auto-tightens the ceiling or produces a NAMED failure, proven by a test that plants a population shrink and asserts the specific message. A test that merely re-checks the current number does not close this -- the 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-23 instances both passed that bar and still recurred.
evidence: PR #10161 job 97146128984: 2 failed / 12153 passed — both tests/test_m20_tp_geometry_guard.py planted-omission tests, AssertionError: []
live cells 423 -> 414; unstamped 239 -> 237; roll-up independently counts 237
tp_geometry_legend._unstamped_ceiling_note records the identical 2026-08-17 recurrence for the stamping case

updates.note:
RESOLVED — and BOTH rows are resolved by the SAME change, because they are one defect with two filings (this row 2026-08-23, BL-20260824-DEMOTING-A-LEG-SILENTLY-LOOSENS-THE-M20-RATCHET 2026-08-24). Recorded as a class, per the /system-review backlog_classes mandate: three recurrences, all found by hand, none by the guard —
  2026-08-17  two cells STAMPED without lowering the ceiling  -> 2 cells of slack
  2026-08-23  eth_pullback_prop_2h demoted (live 423 -> 414)  -> 2 cells of slack
  2026-08-24  slv_trend_1h demoted                            -> 5 cells of slack

THE MECHANISM, one line: the ratchet tested `unstamped > ceiling` and NOTHING ELSE, so every way the count could FALL — stamping, or the live denominator shrinking under a demote — accumulated slack in silence. The 2026-08-23 instance is the proof that this is not theoretical: with 2 cells of slack, BOTH planted-omission self-tests failed with an EMPTY problem list. Un-stamping a live cell no longer breached. The probe had gone quiet and the guard was green.

THE FIX — the ratchet is now TWO-SIDED. `unstamped < ceiling` is a NAMED failure that reports the slack, the live population, and the two remedies it could be (cells were stamped, or the population shrank), and it tells the author to lower `_unstamped_ceiling` to the exact number in this diff. Criterion met: a population shrink now produces a named failure.

WHY NOT AUTO-COMPUTE THE CEILING FROM THE POPULATION, which this row also offered as an acceptable resolution: a self-computing ceiling can never fail, and a ratchet that cannot fail is the same as not having one. The reviewer seeing the number move IS the mechanism — the file's own docstring already says the ceiling lives in the matrix 'so a PR that stamps cells lowers it deliberately'. Auto-computing would delete exactly that property.

⚠️ A TEST WAS INVERTED, DELIBERATELY, AND THIS IS THE PART TO READ. `test_stamping_a_cell_does_NOT_fail_the_ratchet` asserted that stamping must pass, reasoning that 'the ratchet must not punish progress'. The reasoning is right; the assertion was wrong, because under a one-sided ratchet stamping is precisely what CREATES the slack the 2026-08-17 note describes. It is now `test_stamping_a_cell_WITHOUT_lowering_the_ceiling_is_a_named_slack_failure`, with the original intent preserved as a SEPARATE test — stamping AND lowering passes. Progress is not punished; progress that is not RECORDED is.

NEW TEST FOR THE PATH NOTHING COVERED: `test_demoting_a_leg_shrinks_the_population_and_is_a_named_slack_failure` flips a live row to `shadow` — what a Tier-3 demote does — so its cells leave the live_only denominator. It asserts BOTH that a slack failure fires AND that the message names the population shrink, because a demote and a stamping run need different remedies and a message that only says 'a number moved' sends the author to the wrong one. It raises rather than passing if no live row carries an unstamped cell, so it cannot become a vacuous pass — which is the specific bar the 08-24 row set ('the existing tests catch it only because the ceiling happened to be exactly tight').

STATE: the tree is exactly tight right now — 229 unstamped over 396 live cells against a ceiling of 229, slack 0 — so the two-sided check passes on the current file rather than shipping red. tests/test_m20_tp_geometry_guard.py 10 passed (was 8).

items.title: The exit LABEL was re-derived on the Bybit-truth sweep only; its anchored-price sibling wrote the price and left exit_reason frozen at reconciler_filled
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-23 over the whole live journal (1,309 closed non-backtest rows). #10151 (item 1.8) taught _sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit to re-classify at the moment the price arrives. _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced — the sweep that prices every row Bybit broker truth never covers — was not changed, so it wrote exit_price_source (candle_at_close / local_markprice) and never touched exit_reason or called _classify_broker_exit. Verified by reading the function body, not inferred. POPULATION: 578 rows still carried the generic reason; 497 eligible once reduce legs are excluded (81 rows — a reduce's bracket can be INVERTED, so classifying one mislabels it). Of the 497: 156 resolve to a real bracket level off a MEASURED price (123 sl, 33 tp), 35 off an ESTIMATED price (21 sl, 14 tp), 183 are honest 'unresolved', and 105 sit on a FABRICATED price and MUST NOT be labelled at all. THE FABRICATED REFUSAL IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART: local_markprice is the market read at SWEEP time, hours after the exit, so comparing it to the package bracket does not recover a lost label — it manufactures an sl/tp verdict out of unrelated later price action. An earlier framing of this finding (294 of 560) applied neither guard and would have written 29 sl/tp labels out of noise. BLAST RADIUS, traced consumer by consumer rather than assumed: M20's lever VERDICTS are NOT affected — m20_exit_analysis reads exit_reason only as a display column and every verdict-bearing metric is price/candle derived; build_exit_head_dataset sets it to None on the live branch outright; strategy_review_packet (the M7 gate) selects it and never references it; e35_barrier_race / peak_banking_basis / exit_census read HARNESS rows, whose exit_reason vocabulary (take_profit/stop/trail_stop/timeout) the live reconciler never touches. What IS affected: the per-trade diagnostic dump a human reads to choose a lever, and tp_recovery_counterfactual's per-mechanism split.
items.resolution_criteria: Forward: _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced re-classifies, gated on the price basis, stamping price_vs_pkg_bracket (MEASURED) / price_vs_pkg_bracket_est_price (ESTIMATED) / refused_unmeasured_price (FABRICATED-UNVERIFIED). Historical: scripts/ops/backfill_exit_labels.py run via the backfill-exit-labels system-action until the generic+unstamped count reaches its floor.
items.detector: tests/test_exit_label_on_anchored_price_path.py — 23 controls. The load-bearing one is parametrised over every member of provenance.FABRICATED_SOURCES and asserts each is absent from order_monitor._EXIT_LABEL_SOURCE_BY_BASIS, so a fabricated price is structurally unable to produce a label rather than being stopped by a downstream check a future edit could forget. Companions assert the sweep calls the classifier, SELECTs exit_reason (without which the still-generic guard is unevaluable), keeps the reduce-leg exclusion in the query rather than a second drifting predicate, and that resolved / unresolved / refused / never-ran remain four distinguishable states. Plus backfill_exit_labels.py --self-test (12 planted controls), run as a PRECONDITION by the action wrapper before any write.

items.tier: 1 (read-path correctness; no order path, no money write)
items.title: find_unacted_tickets' (account,symbol,direction) fallback had NO time bound, so one historical fill masked every future un-acted ticket — 17 of 17 live tickets invisible and unpromptable
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-23 on the live prop journal (72 tickets, 32 fills). A ticket is matched to a fill two ways: an explicit ticket_id link, and a (account, symbol, direction) FALLBACK. The fallback was a flat set with no time bound, so ANY fill on that key — however old — masked the ticket forever. Consequence: all 17 `emitted` tickets, 32 h to 62 DAYS past their valid_until and none carrying a fill, were dropped from find_unacted_tickets, so /api/bot/prop/reconcile reported `unacted_count: 0` while 17 sat stuck. The drift alert built to catch exactly this reported clean over a population it had excluded — the INDEPENDENCE shape: a reduced verdict nothing outside the producer could contradict. NOT COSMETIC: breakout_executor suppresses a fresh ticket while an `outstanding_ticket:emitted` exists (7 of the 25 suppressions), and prop_expiry_prompt.find_tickets_to_prompt is BUILT ON this function — so an invisible ticket is also un-promptable, and silently blocks its own symbol+direction forever. CORRECTED FUNNEL, since the headline attrition figure is easy to misread: of 72 tickets, 25 `suppressed` are the one-ticket-per-trade rule working correctly (18 open_position, 7 outstanding_ticket) and are NOT a leak; 47 were actually presented; 12 closed, 17 reached a decision (6 expired, 6 invalidated_prompted, 5 skipped), and 17 were stuck in `emitted`. So closure over the presented population is 12/47 = 25.5%, not 12/72 = 16.7%, and the single genuine leak is the stuck-emitted set this row fixes.
items.resolution_criteria: The fallback match requires the fill NOT to predate the ticket, and /api/bot/prop/reconcile's unacted_count reflects genuinely un-acted tickets. Verified against the live shape: 5 of the 17 surface as unacted under the causality bound; the other 12 had a fill genuinely follow them on the same key.
items.detector: tests/test_prop_unacted_time_bound.py — 8 controls. The load-bearing one plants the exact live shape (an old fill, a newer ticket) and asserts the ticket SURFACES; a companion plants 17 stuck tickets behind one old fill and asserts all 17 surface, so a regression to the unbounded set fails loudly. Counter-controls assert the fallback still masks a fill that FOLLOWED the ticket (this is a bound, not a removal), that an explicit ticket_id link stays unbounded, that an undateable fill keeps the old masking (fail-safe: a parse failure must never manufacture a drift alert), and that cross-account and direction isolation survive.
items.checked: checked: src/prop/prop_reconcile.py — the bound is CAUSALITY, not a tuned window: a fill recorded before the ticket existed cannot be that ticket's fill, which needs no evidence to justify. A tighter window (fill inside the ticket's validity plus a reporting-lag grace) would discriminate better, but choosing the grace needs lag evidence this repo does not have — filed as the follow-up rather than invented.
items.follow_up: Tighten the fallback to the ticket's own validity window once the manual bridge's reporting-lag distribution has been measured. Separately: the 17 now-visible stuck tickets need an operator disposition, and prop_expiry_prompt's 12 h PROP_EXPIRY_PROMPT_MAX_AGE_HOURS means anything that slips past it is never asked about again — worth revisiting now that the masking is gone.

items.title: A test fixture MISSING a production column fails silently: sqlite's `no such column` is swallowed into a generic scan failure and every behavioural test in the file then misreports as an assertion failure
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-23. Adding `exit_reason` to _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced's SELECT broke 8 tests in tests/test_sweep_no_mark_fabrication.py, whose hand-rolled `trades` table lacked the column. The failure mode is the problem, not the omission: sqlite raises `no such column`, the sweep's broad except swallows it into `scan query failed` at WARNING, the scan returns nothing, and the tests report `assert 0 == 1` and `KeyError: 'pnl_source'` — pointing squarely at production code that had not changed in the way the message implies. This is the `order_packages.id` class (BL-20260810, a fixture declaring a schema production does NOT have) in its MIRROR IMAGE: a fixture MISSING a column production DOES have. The prior class was swept; this direction was not. Worse, the file's own bomb-defusal regression test — added precisely so this shape names itself rather than being found by elimination — reported the WRONG cause ('the fixture clock has drifted, the sweep is not broken'). A `scanned == 0` has two very different explanations and it named only one, sending the reader to inspect a clock that was fine. ⚠️ DENOMINATOR, stated because the tempting number is misleading: 90 test files hand-roll a `trades` table and all 90 are missing at least one column that some src/ path SELECTs — but that is NOT 90 latent failures, because a fixture only needs the columns the path IT exercises. Quoting 90/90 as a finding would be the unasserted-denominator defect this repo has a rule about. The real population is unknown and only materialises when a SELECT gains a column, which is exactly why the failure needs to be legible rather than enumerated.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) the scan failure is legible — the swallow logs the offending column/query at ERROR, or re-raises under pytest so the fixture is named directly; OR (b) fixtures build `trades` from the production DDL through one shared helper, so drift is impossible rather than merely detectable. (b) is the stronger fix and the same single-homing move already made for the DB-path resolver and provenance.py.
items.detector: tests/test_sweep_no_mark_fabrication.py::test_fixture_row_is_inside_the_sweep_scan_window now PRAGMA-checks the fixture's columns against the set the sweep SELECTs and names the missing ones BEFORE falling through to the window check — so this file's next drift reports its own cause. That is one file; the class-wide detector is resolution criterion (a) or (b) and does not exist yet.
items.checked: checked: tests/test_sweep_no_mark_fabrication.py — verified 2026-08-23 by causing the failure, reading the swallowed warning in the CI log, and confirming the bomb-defusal test named the wrong cause.

updates.note: Re-validated: sqlite's `no such column` swallowed into a generic scan failure. Same family as BL-20260818-TEST-FAKES-THAT-DO-NOT-REFLECT-WRITES and BL-20260810's fictional order_packages.id — a fixture that does not match production certifies nothing.

items.title: `shorting_enabled` is read on the diag surface and consumed by NOTHING on the order path — flipping alpaca_live to live would send 60.1% of its flow to a broker that cannot fill it
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-23 while assessing the operator's dry_run->live ask for alpaca_live. The account reads ACTIVE with `shorting_enabled: false` (/api/diag/broker_account_status). Over ALL 318 alpaca_live journal rows ever produced (2026-06-30..2026-08-23) the direction split is 191 SHORT / 127 LONG = 60.1% short, concentrated in the four highest-volume legs (spy_pullback_1h 58.1%, tlt_pullback_1h 71.9%, qqq_pullback_1h 69.1%, gld_pullback_1h 74.5%) and 100% short across gdx/gld/iaum/slv_pullback_1d (n=24). The string `shorting_enabled` appears in exactly THREE places in the repo: src/units/accounts/alpaca_client.py (the read + the field list) and src/web/api/routers/diag.py (a docstring). There is no short gate, no can_short predicate, nothing on the order path. This is the written-and-never-read shape provenance-consumer-guard exists to catch, on a capability flag rather than a provenance key. Note the 5 existing `exchange_rejected` rows say `unauthorized` and were all LONG (2026-06-30/07-01) — they are NOT evidence for this finding and must not be quoted as such. ALPACA_PLACE_CONFIRM_S would surface the resulting rejections rather than journaling phantoms, which is correct behaviour and does not make the trades execute.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) shorting is enabled broker-side on the Alpaca live account AND the short book earns a forward record (it is currently 0-for-7, -$4,254 on alpaca_portfolio), or (b) a short gate refuses the signal at the coordinator with a logged cause for any account whose broker reports shorting_enabled false — so the refusal is attributable from the journal rather than from a venue error. (b) is Tier-3 order-path work and is worth doing regardless of (a). Closed when a non-shorting account can be shown, from the journal, to refuse a short with a named cause before placement.

updates.note: Re-validated: written-and-never-read (class A) on a SAFETY field. Reads on the diag surface, consumed by nothing on the order path — and see BL-20260823-ALPACA-LIVE-CANNOT-SHORT-BUT-60PCT-OF-ITS-FLOW-IS-SHORT for what that costs. Part of the alpaca_live go-live cluster. Live state this review: alpaca_live reads balance $200.10, api_ok true, ZERO open positions, and zero gross notional across 1,848 exposure_soak samples. HEAD of main also carries 'Confirm the $200 alpaca_live sizing wall'. Tier-3 and the operator's; nothing a review can drain.

items.title: `alpaca_portfolio` does not mirror the `alpaca_live` roster — 2 of 16 live legs have no forward paper record at all
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-23 from config/accounts.yaml. alpaca_live declares 16 strategies; alpaca_portfolio (paper_role: portfolio, the account the UIs render as 'Paper' and the one a live-readiness decision reads) declares 14. splg_trend_long_1d and iaum_pullback_1d run on alpaca_live and on NEITHER paper account with a portfolio role. The mirror's whole purpose is to be the forward record of what the live account would do, so a leg absent from it is a leg whose live promotion has no evidence behind it. Compounding: the mirror's positive result is thin and concentrated — closed-with-pnl n=21, long n=14 +$6,392.80, short n=7 -$4,254.23, and uso_trend_1h alone is +$8,822.10 over 10 closed trades, i.e. one leg exceeds the entire positive result.
items.resolution_criteria: alpaca_portfolio's strategy list is a superset of alpaca_live's, verified by a check that compares the two rosters (so the drift cannot recur silently), and the two added legs have accrued a stated soak before any live-promotion decision cites the mirror.

updates.note:
THE EVIDENCE GAP IS 9 OF 16, NOT 2 - AND THE STATED resolution_criteria ONLY CLOSES 2 OF THEM.

This row measures the ROSTER (config/accounts.yaml: alpaca_portfolio declares 14, alpaca_live 16, so splg_trend_long_1d + iaum_pullback_1d are unmirrored). Measured against /api/bot/performance?window=all's paperPortfolio.perStrategy on 2026-08-25, only SEVEN of the 16 routed legs have a closed row on the mirror at all. The nine with none are: gdx_pullback_1d, gld_pullback_1d, iaum_pullback_1d, ief_pullback_1d, iwm_trend_long_1d, slv_pullback_1d, splg_trend_long_1d, spy_trend_long_1d, tlt_pullback_1d.

THOSE NINE ARE TWO DIFFERENT STATES AND MUST NOT BE COUNTED AS ONE. Two (iaum, splg) have no row because they are NOT ROUTED to the mirror - the roster gap this row names. The other SEVEN ARE declared on alpaca_portfolio and have simply never closed a trade there. A roster fix reaches the first pair and does nothing for the second seven: making the roster a superset adds two legs that will then also have no rows.

So the resolution_criteria as written is necessary and not sufficient. A leg present in the roster with zero closed rows has exactly as much forward evidence as a leg absent from it - none - and the criterion's own second clause ('the two added legs have accrued a stated soak') is the part that actually binds, and it binds on nine legs rather than two. Proposed amendment, not applied: state the criterion over the WHOLE routed set - every alpaca_live leg is declared on alpaca_portfolio AND has a stated non-zero closed-trade count there before any live-promotion decision cites the mirror.

Cross-ref BL-20260823-ALPACA-LIVE-STRATEGY-SET-IS-NET-NEGATIVE-EXCEPT-ONE-LEG, re-measured the same session: the seven legs that DO have rows are six negatives and uso_trend_1h.

Re-validated: 2 of 16 live legs have no forward paper record, so the mirror cannot be the honest predictor it exists to be. Live: alpaca_portfolio holds 4 positions (TLT, QQQ, SPY, IEF) against alpaca_live's 16-strategy roster.

items.title: The pattern-day-trader rule is modelled NOWHERE in code, while the Alpaca paper book runs 14.9% same-day round trips and a live account under $25k gets 3 day trades per 5 business days
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-23. A repo-wide search for PDT / day_trade / daytrading_buying_power across src/ and config/ returns ZERO logic — only prose in docs/research/market-alternatives-2026-06-10.md and one comment in alpaca_client.py:148 noting PDT as an async rejection reason. Meanwhile, over the closed Alpaca paper trades carrying both timestamps (n=94), 14 are same-calendar-day entry+exit = 14.9%; median hold is 73.7h, p25 21.5h. Over the observed window that is ~1.3 day trades per 5 business days against a limit of 3 — under it, but with no headroom modelled and no gate, so a volatile week breaches it and the live account gets flagged. The research doc's assumption that 'the equities account will be >$25k, so the PDT rule is not a concern' does not hold for the funding level actually under discussion. ALPACA_PLACE_CONFIRM_S catches the resulting rejection after the fact; nothing avoids it. === 2026-08-29: INERT — THE BRANCH THIS ROW DESCRIBES WAS NOT TAKEN. The operator settled the cash-vs-margin fork as CASH ('we already said cash a million times, that's not gonna change'). PDT is a MARGIN-account constraint (FINRA's 3-day-trades-per-5-days cap applies to a margin account under $25k); a cash account cannot day-trade on unsettled funds at all, so the binding constraint there is T+1 settlement, not PDT. This row is therefore NOT a go-live blocker and must not be counted as one. It is kept OPEN rather than closed because the decision is a configuration choice, not a law: if the account is ever converted to margin this row becomes live again immediately and unmodelled. Do NOT close it on the cash decision alone. Active sibling under cash: BL-20260823-ALPACA-CASH-ACCOUNT-SETTLEMENT-UNMODELLED.
items.resolution_criteria: Either the live equity account is funded above $25k (and that is recorded as the reason no gate exists), or a day-trade counter is available to the sizing path so an entry that would be the 4th day trade in a rolling 5-business-day window is refused with a named cause rather than rejected at the venue. Closed when the constraint is either provably inapplicable or enforced.

updates.note: Re-validated: PDT modelled nowhere while the paper book runs 14.9% same-day round trips. CLAUDE.md now surfaces pattern_day_trader + daytrade_count on the diag capacity block, so the INPUT exists and nothing consumes it — class A again.

items.title: `RegistryEntry.status` is a dead axis — all 95 rows read `candidate`, including the 3 advisory heads, and nothing ever moves it
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-23 against the live registry mirror (95 rows). Every row reads status='candidate' while target_deployment_stage splits 63 candidate / 28 shadow / 3 advisory / 1 research_only. All 5,015 history entries carry to_status='candidate' — explained by ModelRegistry.register, which on a retrain writes StatusEvent(from_status=existing.status, to_status=existing.status): it records the retrain, it does not reset. Nothing is broken: the live ladder runs on the orthogonal target_deployment_stage (ml/cli.py promote-stage) and deployment_bucket derives from that. The cost is legibility — a reader who checks `status` sees a fleet that looks permanently stuck at candidate, and that reading is what seeded the (refuted) 'daily training resets soak decisions' worry this audit was asked to investigate. `ModelRegistry.promote` and VALID_STATUSES/_ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS exist and are exercised only by tests.
items.resolution_criteria: Either the status axis is retired (removed, or documented in ml/registry/model_registry.py's module docstring as vestigial with target_deployment_stage named as the live ladder), or it is driven for real. Closed when a reader of a registry row cannot mistake `status` for the deployment ladder.

updates.note: RE-CONFIRMED with the corrected symptom: I read all 96 registry rows this review and `stage` is None on every one, with deployment_bucket carrying the real information. Duplicate condition with BL-20260821-REGISTRY-STATUS-SAYS-CANDIDATE-FOR-EVERY-MODEL; consolidate the two.

items.title: T+1 settlement is modelled nowhere, and on a $200 CASH account the whole balance recycles every trade — a good-faith violation is one unsettled buy away
items.detail: Operator confirmed 2026-08-23 that alpaca_live is a NON-MARGIN (cash) account holding ~$200. In a cash account, proceeds of a sale are unavailable until settled (T+1); buying with unsettled funds is a good-faith violation and selling something bought with unsettled funds is free-riding, which carries a 90-day restriction. A repo-wide search finds no settled/unsettled-cash logic — the sizing path reads a single balance figure. At $200 the entire balance recycles on every round trip, so the condition is not an edge case, it is the normal operating mode. NOTE this REPLACES rather than compounds the PDT concern filed the same day: the pattern-day-trader rule is a MARGIN rule and does not apply to a cash account, so BL-20260823-NO-PDT-MODELLING-ON-ALPACA should be re-scoped to 'applies if/when this account goes margin' rather than treated as a live blocker. Also note shorting is structurally impossible here (Reg-T shorting needs a margin account; FINRA minimum $2,000), so BL-20260823-ALPACA-SHORTING-FLAG-READ-NEVER-CONSUMED resolves to its option (b) — a short gate — with option (a) off the table at this account size. POPULATION AND BASIS, measured 2026-08-23 over ALL 318 alpaca_live order packages carrying entry/stop geometry (the account's complete history, 2026-06-30 through 2026-08-23): 127 of 318 are long, 66 of 318 are both long and affordable at one share against the ~$200 balance, so 66 of 318 (20.8%) is the flow this account could act on at all — and every one of those recycles the whole balance, which is what makes the settlement constraint the normal case rather than an edge case. The $2,000 figure is not a measurement: it is FINRA's regulatory minimum equity for a margin account (Rule 4210), quoted here only to establish that converting this account out of cash status is not available at its current size. === 2026-08-29: THIS IS NOW THE GO-LIVE BLOCKER, BY OPERATOR CHOICE. The cash-vs-margin fork is settled as CASH, so this row's premise is not merely measured-true but is the branch the account is actually on. Offered three handlings, the operator chose 'MODEL T+1 BEFORE ANY LEG GOES LIVE' — declining the cheaper 'restrict to 1d legs and defer the model' option I had recommended on the argument that settlement rarely binds at daily cadence. So no leg is added to alpaca_live's roster until this is built AND observed acting. Tracked as the blocker in OI-20260829-ALPACA-GOLIVE-BLOCKED-ON-T1-SETTLEMENT-MODEL (loud). ⚠️ Its clears_when is deliberately an OBSERVATION, not a test: a would-be order the account cannot settle must be seen refused with a logged cause on a real or replayed case. A passing unit test is not an observation of the live mechanism. === 2026-08-29, THE MECHANISM, read from code rather than inferred — this is filed HERE rather than as its own row because backlog_search put it at 0.67 overlap with this one and it is a CONSTRAINT ON THIS ROW'S FIX, not a separate defect. The sizing path already exists and already reads a broker figure: src/core/coordinator.py::multi_account_execute (~L1547) calls client.buying_power() and feeds it to position_size(available_usd=...) as the margin pre-flight basis. src/units/accounts/alpaca_client.py::buying_power (L256) resolves regt_buying_power -> buying_power -> cash. ⚠️ THE CHAIN TERMINATES AT `cash`. If Alpaca's buying_power EXCLUDES unsettled sale proceeds while `cash` INCLUDES them, then any condition that makes both preferred keys absent sizes the order against UNSETTLED money — which is this row's violation exactly, reached MORE PERMISSIVELY than the correct answer. That is the same permissive-fallback class the function's own docstring cites BL-20260707-ALPACA-BALANCE-TRUTHINESS for, one level up: there a genuine 0.0 fell through to a less authoritative key; here an absent key falls through to a WIDER one. ⚠️ ALPACA'S CASH-ACCOUNT SEMANTICS ARE NOT ESTABLISHED AND COULD NOT BE FROM THE CURRENT LIVE STATE: measured 2026-08-29, alpaca_live reads cash = buying_power = regt_buying_power = equity = 200.10, all four IDENTICAL, because the account holds nothing and has nothing unsettled — so the state that would distinguish the fields does not exist yet. Both paper mirrors (alpaca_paper, alpaca_portfolio) are MARGIN accounts and therefore cannot exhibit cash-account settlement behaviour either. Do NOT resolve this row by asserting what Alpaca does; that is unverified either way. DESIGN CONSEQUENCE: the fix must not REST on the broker field. Compute the unsettled amount from OUR OWN fill record (data we own and can verify) and subtract it from the venue's cash, then take the MINIMUM of that and the venue's own buying_power — so the result is correct whether or not Alpaca already nets it out, and a manual sale we did not make is still caught by the venue side.
items.resolution_criteria: The sizing path reads Alpaca's settled-cash fields and refuses an entry that would buy with unsettled proceeds, with its own named cause in the journal (distinct from risk_refused and zero_balance). Closed when a cash account can be shown, from the journal, to refuse an unsettled buy before placement — verified before alpaca_live is flipped to live.

updates.note: PARTIALLY ADDRESSED WHILE I WORKED — and by a concurrent session, so verify before acting. ALPACA_CASH_SETTLEMENT_MODE now exists at `annotate` with a cash_settlement_soak, and origin/main moved to 5d6c87d ('Repo-side Monday timer for the T+1 settlement soak') DURING this review. I deliberately did not assess it to avoid colliding with that session. The `apply` flip is Tier-2 and wants `would_have_reduced_usd` read from the soak first.

items.title: There is no `rearm-ib-bracket` action, so correcting a MISPRICED protective leg needs a bespoke multi-step workaround every time — and that is why one MES stop has bounced across sessions for a week
items.detail: Operator, 2026-08-23: "This kind of thing can't be so complicated that it requires several sessions to weigh in across a week of work, and we're definitely not ready for live money if we still can't figure this out." Correct, and this row is the structural cause. The system-actions allowlist can FLATTEN a position (flatten-ib-position), CANCEL one order (cancel-ib-order) and ATTACH a target (attach-ib-target) — but nothing can RE-ARM a bracket at the journal's declared levels, which is the operation a mispriced or half-missing leg actually needs. So each occurrence gets improvised. TWO compounding causes, both measured. (1) The capability exists and was MISREAD: IBClient.place_protective CANCELS resting legs then places (the pre-cancel is in _locked_place_protective) and is scoped to one trade when passed oca_key — its own docstring now records that an earlier version described only the placing half, that a session which stopped there concluded no safe in-place repair existed, and that this was 'the opposite of the truth', and that the wrong conclusion was escalated to the operator as a Tier-3 question on that basis. scripts/ops/attach_ib_target.py and scripts/ops/cancel_ib_order.py already import it, so the machinery is one wrapper away from being an action. (2) The live sweep cannot self-heal this class: order_monitor._check_broker_naked_ib_positions grades whether a stop RESTS, never at what PRICE, so a mispriced stop reads as covered — BL-20260820-PROTECTION-COVERAGE-IS-PRICE-BLIND criterion 4, still open. The two together mean a mispriced leg is invisible to the healer AND unreachable by any action. MEASURED INSTANCE: MES trade 4350 (mes_trend_long_1d, 15 long, opened 2026-08-03) has rested a stop at 7516.5 against a declared 7533.69642857 since at least 2026-08-20 — 17.196 points = 68.8 ticks, ~$1,290 of exposure beyond the declared risk at 15 contracts x $5/point — across at least three sessions, with the 2026-08-22 scheduled Routine explicitly instructed 'do not fold in the MES stop/declared divergence, a separate Tier-3 item'. The interim workaround now scheduled is cancel-the-stop-and-let-the-naked-sweep-re-arm, which works only because cancelling converts a mispriced leg into a MISSING one that the sweep does handle, and it opens a naked window of up to IB_BROKER_NAKED_CHECK_SECONDS (300s). That is a workaround, not a mechanism.
items.resolution_criteria: A `rearm-ib-bracket` system-action exists that takes account+symbol (or trade_id), reads the journal's stop_loss and take_profit_1, and calls place_protective with the trade's oca_key so the repair is scoped to that trade and cannot destroy a sibling's protection on a netted contract. Dry-run by default like its siblings; Tier-2 to apply. Closed when a mispriced or half-missing IB bracket can be corrected in ONE dispatched action with no naked window, verified by broker_bracket_reconcile.py grading the position clean afterwards while MHG (the control) stays clean.

updates.note: Re-validated: correcting a mispriced protective leg still needs a bespoke multi-step workaround. Pairs with BL-20260816-NO-PER-ORDER-IB-CANCEL — the two together are why the 2026-08-20 remediation cancelled the wrong leg.

items.title: The prop screenshot reader reported ONLY the fallback provider's failure, so a Gemini 404 masked whatever took out the primary — and a primary ScreenshotParseError skipped the fallback entirely
items.detail: OBSERVED LIVE 2026-08-23 on the prop bot. The operator sent a Breakout terminal screenshot and received: '⚠️ screenshot reading failed (gemini-2.5-flash HTTP 404) — type the report instead.' TWO defects in src/prop/screenshot_parse.py::_call_vision, both fixed in this session. (1) The fallback call was not wrapped, so when the fallback ALSO failed its exception propagated ALONE — the message named Gemini, the provider that was merely SECOND, while whatever took out the primary appeared only in a VM WARNING line the operator never sees. A reader trusting that message would go debug Gemini. That is a failure message naming a cause no code path tested: CLAUDE.md § 'Diagnostic provenance' sub-class A. Fixed: both causes now travel in one message, asserted by a test that fails if EITHER is missing. (2) `except ScreenshotParseError: raise` sat before the generic handler, so a provider-level ScreenshotParseError on the PRIMARY never reached the fallback — and every ScreenshotParseError the two callers raise is provider-level and retryable on the other provider (SDK absent, API key absent, HTTP non-200, unreadable response, empty completion); none says anything about the image. A missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY therefore took out the whole manual bridge while a working GEMINI_API_KEY sat unused on the same VM — the exact single-point-of-failure the fallback was built for after the 2026-08-20 billing incident. Fixed, reversing a prior deliberate decision whose stated premise ('a retry would turn one clear message into a confusing second failure') is retired by fix (1). The non-retryable checks (empty image, unsupported media type) live in parse_screenshot, above the call, and are untouched. 22 tests pass.
items.resolution_criteria: STILL OPEN because the 404 itself is unexplained: a 404 from generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent means that model id is not served for that key/API version, and this session could not call the API to distinguish a retired id from a key-scope problem. Closed when a real screenshot round-trips end to end on the prop bot, OR the fallback model id is corrected to one the live key actually serves — verified by an actual send, not by inspection. Do NOT guess a replacement id.

updates.note: Re-validated: a fallback masking the primary's failure. Matters for the prop bridge specifically — a screenshot that fails to read is an unrecorded fill on the $55-cushion account.

items.title: The prop rule-distance panel is computing a $282.86 cushion from a 61-hour-old snapshot while the operator's own terminal shows a cushion of about $171 — and the mechanism that would refresh it is the broken screenshot reader
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-23T07:5xZ against the live endpoint /api/bot/prop/status?account_id=breakout_1. The panel returns balance 4982.86 with reported_at 2026-08-20T18:57:28Z, status_age_hours 60.96, and status_freshness 'stale' — the freshness work added 2026-08-14 is doing its job and labelling it correctly. From that snapshot it computes distance_to_dd_floor_usd = 282.86 against the static floor of 4700.00 on a 5000.00 account. THE OPERATOR'S OWN SCREENSHOT, sent the same morning, shows the Breakout terminal reading Balance 4,871 / Equity 4,871 — about 111.86 BELOW the snapshot, which puts the real distance to the floor at roughly 171, i.e. the panel OVERSTATES the surviving cushion by about 65%. THE ARITHMETIC, so the percentage is checkable: panel cushion 4982.86 - 4700.00 = 282.86; screenshot cushion 4871 - 4700 = 171; the overstatement is 282.86 - 171 = 111.86 on a true cushion of 171, and 111.86 / 171 = 0.654. THE WINDOW: the snapshot dates to 2026-08-20 and the operator's screenshot to 2026-08-23, so the panel had gone 61 hours with no refresh against a declared threshold of 24. POPULATION: one account (breakout_1) and the single latest row of prop_account_status — this is not a distribution and must not be quoted as one. (Stated as read off an image, not as a measurement of the account; the authoritative correction is a fresh report-back.) THE CAUSAL CHAIN IS THE POINT: the screenshot reader IS the refresh mechanism for this snapshot, and it is broken (BL-20260823-SCREENSHOT-FALLBACK-REPORTS-ONLY-THE-SECOND-FAILURE) — so the safety cushion on a live prop account went stale BECAUSE the data-entry path failed, and the two rows are one incident. Also note the panel's daily-loss half is weaker than it looks: realized_today and day_start_balance are both null on the latest row, so distance_to_daily_loss_usd = 149.49 is computed from an ASSUMED day_pnl of 0.0, not a measured one. A stale cushion that is labelled stale is honest; a stale cushion nobody refreshes is a breach waiting to be discovered afterwards.
items.resolution_criteria: A fresh account_status lands for breakout_1 (typed if the screenshot path is still down) and status_freshness reads 'ok'; the rule-distance panel then reflects the true balance. Structurally: the operator should not be the only refresh mechanism for a safety number — either the request cadence escalates when the snapshot crosses PROP_STATUS_REQUEST_MAX_AGE_HOURS by a large multiple (60.96h against a 24h threshold produced no escalation), or the panel refuses to publish a distance computed from a snapshot older than some hard bound rather than publishing one that reads live. Closed when a 60-hour-stale cushion cannot present as a number without an unmissable caveat on every surface that renders it.
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-08-23, verified against the live endpoint rather than inferred from the merge. /api/bot/prop/status?account_id=breakout_1 now returns status_freshness 'ok' at status_age_hours 1.71 (was 58.7-61h), and distance_to_dd_floor_usd 171.0 - which matches the operator's own terminal reading of about $171 EXACTLY, against the $282.86 the stale snapshot was rendering. THREE things had to land and all three did: (1) the refresh mechanism was root-caused and fixed - the screenshot reader was 404-ing because BOTH model ids were wrong (_DEFAULT_MODEL 'claude-sonnet-5' is not an API id; the Gemini fallback 'gemini-2.5-flash' 404s on this key), and _call_vision now falls back on a primary ScreenshotParseError instead of short-circuiting, reporting BOTH causes when both providers fail; (2) the operator reported a fresh balance, which the fixed path ingested; (3) ict-trader-dashboard#207 merged, so the Streamlit rule-distance panel reads status_freshness and cannot render a stale cushion as a live one - matching what the Svelte SPA already did, so the two frontends no longer describe the same payload differently. NOTE the residual is a DIFFERENT row: the three days of terminal trades the broken reader cost are still missing from the journal (BL-20260823-PROP-JOURNAL-MISSING-THREE-DAYS-OF-TERMINAL-TRADES), and the detector for that class shipped as P1 (src/prop/prop_fills_staleness.py). A fresh cushion does not repair an incomplete fill record.

items.title: The live sweep cannot tell that a declared bracket ALREADY got passed while the position stayed open — operator-directed: it needs the price axis and a should-have-fired inference
items.detail: Operator direction 2026-08-23: 'it also looks like the live sweep needs to be able to check the price and infer if it should have fired.' Full design written up in docs/audits/full-system-audit-2026-08-23.md Part 10; this row is the tracking item. THE GAP, measured this session: no enforcing reader carries a price. IBClient.protection_coverage returns stop_qty/target_qty/covered_qty; AlpacaClient.protection_state returns {stop,target,legs} and inspects only the order TYPE string; order_monitor._bybit_position_protection's Full-mode branch returns covered_qty == size on any stopLoss string that is merely non-empty and not '0'. So a leg resting at the WRONG price grades fully covered, and a level price has ALREADY traded through is not a concept the sweep has. The semantics exist and are proven OFFLINE — scripts/ops/broker_bracket_reconcile.py graded MHG clean and MES 69 ticks diverged in the same 2026-08-23 run — the enforcing path just cannot see them. THE DESIGN, in brief: (a) price-aware coverage with a ONE-TICK tolerance, re-arming at the declared level via place_protective scoped by oca_key — a correction, not a close — and sharing the detector's comparator rather than reimplementing it, since two definitions of 'is this protected' are free to drift; (b) a should-have-fired inference over bar history, which is a HISTORY read on the live trader and so inherits exit_anchor's timeout/budget/caching discipline verbatim (an unbounded per-row fetch here is the 2026-06-09 cold-start wedge shape, and this file has two of those in its history); (c) four states never collapsed — within / diverged / breached / unknown, with unknown never folded into within. THE REAL DESIGN QUESTION IS THE ASYMMETRY: a STOP breach means we are carrying risk we never agreed to and the position should not exist (a safety action), while a TARGET breach means we missed an exit and closing books whatever is available (a profit-taking action) — MGC sits +234 points PAST its target, so closing happens to be better, which is luck rather than policy. Conflating them is how a safety sweep starts making discretionary trading decisions, so the two sides get separate switches. STAGING copies NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_MODE exactly: annotate (default) does all the work and writes a soak row touching no order; apply acts on a confirmed stop-side breach; the target side stays alert-only until the soak shows what applying would have done. ⚠️ THE ASYMMETRY IS RESOLVED — operator decision 2026-08-23, and it overrides the framing above: 'if we missed a tp, we can't rely on hitting it again as that trade geometry is already stale — since the trade was already lost to our own technical incompetence, we should drop that risk sooner rather than later.' BOTH SIDES CLOSE. The reasoning is not profit-taking (which is how the design draft framed the target side, wrongly) but THESIS VALIDITY: the entry declared a target, the target printed, the setup is over, and everything after is unmanaged drift on levels that no longer describe anything. So a breached stop and a breached target are the SAME class — a position whose declared geometry has already been invalidated by events, held only because of a technical failure. Two consequences: MGC sitting +234 points past its target is NOT a windfall to bank and not a reason to hesitate, it is the measure of how long that position has drifted unmanaged; and the soak's purpose narrows from 'should we act' (decided) to 'does the implementation fire correctly and how often', which must not be used to defer the decision a second time. One residual difference survives and is about URGENCY, not policy: a breached stop is actively bleeding past its risk limit while a breached target is giving back from a profit, so the stop side is sequenced first if anything has to be.
items.resolution_criteria: Staged, and each stage independently verifiable. (1) The price axis lands in all three venue coverage reads, sharing broker_bracket_reconcile's comparator and tick table — this also closes BL-20260820-PROTECTION-COVERAGE-IS-PRICE-BLIND criterion 4 and its criterion-5 Alpaca half. (2) Breach detection ships in annotate and soaks against the three live controls available TODAY: MGC 4773 must grade breached on the target side, MES 4350 diverged on the stop side, and MHG 4796 within on both — a build that flags all three is as broken as one that flags none, the same discriminating-run discipline that validated the offline detector. (3) The stop side flips to apply only after that soak is reviewed, with the 2-observation confirm reused so a single bad bar cannot close a position, alerts rate-limited per (account, symbol, state) since the condition can hold for days, and the close booking the MARKET while the soak records that the declared level was passed at time T — writing the declared level as the exit price would be the anchorless-estimate class again. (4) The target side needs NO separate decision — the operator settled it on 2026-08-23 (both sides close, on thesis-validity grounds); it ships behind the same apply flip, sequenced after the stop side only for urgency. Reviewing the soak means confirming the implementation fires correctly, NOT re-litigating whether to act.

updates.note:
CRITERION 1 IS MET. 'The price axis lands in all three venue coverage reads, sharing broker_bracket_reconcile's comparator and tick table.'

(a) ALL THREE READS EMIT PRICES: IBClient.protection_coverage -> stop_prices/target_prices (#10166); order_monitor._bybit_position_protection -> stop_prices on all three return paths via the new _bybit_sl_leg_trigger; AlpacaClient.protection_state -> stop_prices/target_prices via _leg_price (both #10167).

(b) THE COMPARATOR IS NOW GENUINELY SHARED, which it was not when this criterion was written. src/runtime/protection_price.py::grade_protection_price is the one definition, and scripts/ops/broker_bracket_reconcile.py -- which had its OWN nearest-leg / tolerance arithmetic -- now grades through it. Two definitions of 'diverges' are free to drift, and a detector that disagrees with the enforcing path about a live position is worse than either alone.

(c) THE TICK TABLE CONVERGED TOO, and this was the load-bearing part. The reconciler defaulted an unresolvable tick to 0.01. For MHG (true tick 0.0005) that is 20x too WIDE -- it hides a real divergence behind a tolerance nobody chose -- and for MES (0.25) it is 25x too tight. It now reports *_price_ungradeable, and the QUANTITY axis still grades: a missing tick blinds the price axis only.

DISCRIMINATING RUN, live payloads, ib_paper 2026-08-23T10:39:16Z. MHG 4796 CLEAN (the control -- a build that flags all three is as broken as one that flags none); MGC 4773 one finding; MES 4350 two, including 'stop_price_diverges: declares 7533.696429, nearest resting 7516.500000 -- 69 ticks (17.196429) away [more_exposed]'. The [more_exposed] annotation is new and is the thing |diff| cannot say.

NO SPURIOUS ALERT FROM THE SCHEDULED CALLER, asserted rather than assumed: the fingerprint over the same two live payloads is byte-identical under origin/main and under the change (c007536253fdc911), because the fingerprint keys on (account, trade_id, symbol, kind) and no kind moved.

DEFECT FOUND IN THE SHARED GRADER WHILE DOING THIS: direction was a two-state read of a three-state fact, so an unreadable direction graded as SHORT and published an exposure label that was exactly backwards. Fixed (direction_known + no verdict when unknown); recorded in full on BL-20260820-PROTECTION-COVERAGE-IS-PRICE-BLIND. No live verdict was affected -- both callers pass a populated direction.

STILL OPEN, and this row stays open for it: criteria 2, 3 and 4. Only the IB SWEEP consumes the divergence; Alpaca and Bybit expose prices and do not yet grade them (BL-20260823-ALPACA-BYBIT-SWEEPS-EXPOSE-PRICES-BUT-DO-NOT-GRADE). And NOTHING yet does the should-have-fired inference over bar history, which is the half the operator's direction was actually about.

SCOPE CORRECTION on criterion 2, from the live system rather than the design doc. This row's design was written around MGC 4773 sitting +234 points past its declared target, as the case a 'should-have-fired inference' would catch. MEASURED TODAY: the monitor IS catching it, every ~30 seconds.
    order_monitor: ict_scalp_mgc_15m ... verdict={'action':'close','reason':'tp_cross',
                                                  'exit_price': 4626.9}
    -> IB venue for MGC is closed - exit deferred to next session
The position is open because COMEX is shut on a Sunday, not because anything failed to infer a breach. (`ict_scalp` gained that close path only this morning, BL-20260818-ICT-SCALP-HAS-NO-TAKE-PROFIT-CLOSE-PATH — before it, this row's premise held.)

WHAT THAT CHANGES. The breach inference is NOT the primary mechanism for a leg whose monitor runs; the monitor's own `sl_cross`/`tp_cross` is, and all three strategy families now emit both (AST-pinned). The remaining gap is narrower and should be built for what it actually is: a SAFETY NET for legs the monitor does not reach — a monitor-blind position (MONITOR_BLINDNESS_ALERT_TICKS), a family whose close path is missing, or a venue that defers indefinitely. Building the general bar-history inference as the front-line mechanism would duplicate a path that already works and would add a history read on the live trader to do it, which the row itself flags as the 2026-06-09 cold-start wedge shape.

⚠️ DO NOT READ THIS AS 'THE ROW IS SOLVED'. The safety-net case is real and unbuilt, and a deferring venue is exactly where it bites: the defer loop above is correct but UNBOUNDED, so a position past its bracket over a long holiday closure is held on the strength of a bracket nobody has re-verified. What changed is the JUSTIFICATION and the SIZING of the build, not whether it is needed.

CRITERION 1 remains MET (the price axis + shared comparator landed). Criteria 3 and 4 are untouched, and the apply-side machinery they describe now partly exists as the re-assert path (BL-20260823-MODIFY-IDEMPOTENCE-COMPARES-INTENT-TO-JOURNAL-NEVER-TO-VENUE), which is the closest sibling to reuse rather than reimplement.

CRITICAL and operator-directed. Re-validated: the live sweep still cannot tell that a declared bracket was ALREADY passed while the position stayed open. This is the mechanism behind BL-20260823-TP-CROSS-CLOSE-RECORDS-A-STALE-MARK-AS-A-MEASURED-EXIT and the MGC 4773 case, and it needs the price axis the sweeps now PRODUCE but do not CONSUME (BL-20260823-ALPACA-BYBIT-SWEEPS-EXPOSE-PRICES-BUT-DO-NOT-GRADE).

items.title: The prop journal's newest fill is 2026-08-19 while the operator's terminal shows trades on 2026-08-22 — the broken screenshot reader has cost three days of unrecorded prop trading
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-23 against /api/bot/prop/fills (32 fills) and /api/bot/prop/tickets (72 tickets). The newest fill of any status is 2026-08-19T21:31:42Z. The operator's Breakout terminal screenshot, sent the same morning, shows trade-history rows dated 22/08/26 08:10 (SOLUSD Sell Closing 20.00 @ 95.00, commission -0.76) and 22/08/26 07:48 (SOLUSD Buy Opening 20.00 @ 100.51, commission -0.81) — a complete round trip that does NOT appear in the journal. So the prop book has traded for three days with no record reaching the money DB. THIS IS THE THIRD CONSEQUENCE OF ONE ROOT CAUSE: the manual bridge has no broker feed, the screenshot reader IS the data-entry path, and it has been failing (BL-20260823-SCREENSHOT-FALLBACK-REPORTS-ONLY-THE-SECOND-FAILURE — both model ids were wrong). The other two are the 61-hour-stale safety cushion (BL-20260823-PROP-CUSHION-COMPUTED-FROM-A-61-HOUR-OLD-BALANCE) and the operator being told to 'type the report instead' twice in twelve minutes. WHAT IS NOT WRONG, checked rather than assumed: (a) the two SOLUSDT fills 14 seconds apart on 2026-08-19T21:31 are NOT a double-report — the terminal shows two genuinely separate 83-lot positions that day (opened 15:50 @ 78.52 and closed 15:51 @ 78.51; a second closed 20:01 @ 81.50), so both journal rows are real, and one of them simply carries ticket_id=None; (b) completion integrity on what DID land is clean — all 13 closed fills carry a pnl AND an exit_price, and 12 of 13 link to a ticket; (c) the PnL basis reconciles to the venue: journal +242.02 vs terminal Closed P&L +247.34, and journal -6.05 vs terminal -0.83, a consistent -5.32 / -5.22 delta on two independent trades that matches round-trip commission (2.61 x 2 = 5.22), i.e. the journal is booking NET of fees while the terminal column is gross. That is correct behaviour and should not be 'fixed'. SEPARATELY, 17 tickets remain at status=emitted spanning 2026-06-21 to 2026-08-21 — the stuck population whose DETECTION was fixed this session (the unacted-ticket fallback had no time bound and hid all 17); the tickets themselves are still stuck and still suppress new tickets on their symbol.
items.resolution_criteria: The 2026-08-22 SOLUSD round trip (and anything since) is reported into the journal, so /api/bot/prop/fills has a fill newer than the operator's most recent terminal activity. Structurally: a prop book that has traded with NO fill reported for longer than some bound should raise its own alert rather than being discovered by reading a screenshot in a chat — the account-status request escalation exists for the BALANCE and there is no equivalent for FILLS. Closed when a multi-day gap between terminal activity and the newest journal fill is detectable without an operator noticing it.

updates.note:
THE STRUCTURAL HALF OF THE CRITERION IS MET AND LIVE-VERIFIED; THE DATA HALF IS NOT, AND ONLY THE OPERATOR CAN SUPPLY IT.

STRUCTURAL. The criterion asks for 'a multi-day gap between terminal activity and the newest journal fill detectable without an operator noticing it'. src/prop/prop_fills_staleness.py (P1, merged #10165) is that detector, and it is not merely shipped -- it was RUN against the live table today and returns the true positive:
    balance_state 'unreported' | delta -111.86 | prev_balance 4982.86 (id 10, 2026-08-20T18:57Z)
    -> latest_balance 4871.00 (id 11, 2026-08-23T08:11Z) | fills_in_window 0
Pulled from /api/bot/db/table/prop_account_status (11 rows, order_state 'applied') and graded by the SHIPPED pure function, not a reimplementation. The -111.86 also independently corroborates the round trip this row describes: Buy Opening 20 @ 100.51 -> Sell Closing 20 @ 95.00 is -110.20, and the two commissions (-0.81, -0.76) bring it to -111.77, within $0.09 of the measured balance move. Two independent sources agreeing on a number neither derived from the other.

DATA. Still missing. /api/bot/prop/fills newest row is UNCHANGED at 2026-08-19T21:31:42Z, so the 08-22 round trip has still not reached the journal. I deliberately did NOT post it myself. The prices and quantities I would use are a SECOND-HAND TRANSCRIPTION of a screenshot recorded in this row -- not a source I read -- and more importantly a repair covering only the one trade I happen to know about would leave the journal still wrong while making it LOOK repaired, which is worse than the current state where the gap is visible. Nobody but the operator can confirm what else, if anything, the book did between 08-20 and 08-23.

WHAT IS NEEDED TO CLOSE THIS: the operator's Breakout trade-history for 2026-08-20 onward (a screenshot to the prop bot is the normal path and now works again), after which /api/bot/prop/fills should carry a row newer than the newest terminal activity and the detector's next run should grade 'explained' rather than 'unreported'.

DEFECT FOUND IN THE DETECTOR WHILE VERIFYING IT, and fixed. assess_balance_move required `snapshots` newest-first and graded whatever it was handed. That coupled correctness to the caller's ORDER BY, and the two do not share a basis -- prop_journal.list_account_status orders by `id DESC` while every comparison in the grader is on `reported_at`. They agree today (measured: zero inversions across all 11 live rows) by coincidence of entry order, not by anything enforcing it. Handed a mis-ordered list it did not fail loudly: it graded a BACKWARDS window (start > end), and since the fill filter is `start < ts <= end` no fill can fall inside one, so every non-noise delta came back 'unreported' -- a confident FALSE FINDING on a LATCHED alert, which is worse than a silent pass. Demonstrated on the real table: the same 11 rows reversed graded 'unreported' on a July pair with a window running 07-06 -> 07-04. The function now establishes its own ordering (undateable rows sort last, where the existing balance_unreadable branch catches them), so the verdict is byte-identical under newest-first, reversed and shuffled input. 6 new tests, 39 total.

DATA HALF NOW DONE. The operator supplied the Breakout Trade History screenshot directly, so the round trip was read from a primary source rather than transcribed from this row.

POSTED via the prop-report relay (issue #10170) and INGESTED: HTTP 200, {ok:true, kind:'fill', id:33, status:'closed', ticket_id:'prop-manual-3265eed44039', notified:{push:true, telegram:true}}. Verified on /api/bot/prop/fills — newest row is now 2026-08-23T11:04:22Z SOLUSDT long closed entry 100.51 exit 95.0 qty 20.0 pnl -111.77, linked to a ticket rather than orphaned.

⚠️ pnl IS THE NET FIGURE (-111.77), NOT THE GROSS (-110.20), and the mapping was verified against the journal rather than assumed: the two 08-19 fills already stored carry 242.02 and -6.05, which equal the screenshot's *Net* Closed P&L column exactly while its *Closed P&L* column reads 247.34 and -0.83. So the journal books net of commission. This row's earlier analysis had already reasoned to the same conclusion from a -5.32/-5.22 delta; the screenshot confirms it directly.

COMPLETENESS, which is why posting was safe where it was not before: the screenshot's range is 'Last Week' and its newest row IS the 08-22 08:10 close, with nothing between the 08-19 20:01 close and the 08-22 07:48 open. One round trip was the whole gap. Posting a partial repair would have left the journal wrong while making it look repaired, which is why the previous update declined to act on a second-hand transcription.

FIRST ATTEMPT FAILED AND THE CAUSE WAS MINE (issue #10168): the prop-report workflow strips fence LINES and passes the entire remaining body to `jq -e 'type=="object"'`, so the explanatory prose I put under the JSON broke validation before SSH ever ran. docs/claude/system-actions.md states the requirement plainly ('whose body is a single JSON object'); I did not read it closely enough. Retried clean in #10170.

THE DETECTOR STILL GRADES `unreported` ON THAT PAIR, AND THAT IS CORRECT — not a residual defect. Re-run against live data after the ingest: delta -111.86 over the window (08-20T18:57, 08-23T08:11], fills_in_window 0. The new fill's `reported_at` is 11:04Z, AFTER the 08:11Z snapshot that closes the window, so it cannot retroactively explain it — and the honest reading of that window is still 'at the time of the 08:11 report, nothing had been reported'. It self-clears on the next operator balance report, exactly as this row's design intends (a balance_moved_unreported latch is pruned silently rather than cleared with a false [OK]). Worth stating so the next reader does not treat a persisting `unreported` as evidence the repair failed.

STRUCTURAL HALF was already MET and live-verified in the previous update. Both halves of the criterion are now satisfied; leaving the row open only until the next snapshot confirms the grade moves off `unreported` on its own.

RESOLVED — both halves of the criterion, verified against the live journal 2026-08-25T16:3xZ (/api/bot/prop/fills?limit=200, 35 fills, count 35 so NOT truncated).

THE INSTANCE. The row named one specific missing round trip: 22/08/26 07:48 SOLUSD Buy Opening 20.00 @ 100.51 commission -0.81, and 08:10 Sell Closing 20.00 @ 95.00 commission -0.76. It is now FILL ID 33, reported 2026-08-23T11:04:22Z, status closed, pnl -111.77, whose reason reads 'operator terminal trade-history screenshot 2026-08-23; round trip opened 2026-08-22 07:48 Buy Opening 20 @ 100.51 commission -0.81, closed 2026-08-22 08:10 Sell Closing 20 @ 95.00 commission -0.76' — every figure matching the screenshot this row was filed from. The gap was backfilled the same day the row was written.

THE STRUCTURAL HALF, which is what the criterion actually turns on ('closed when a multi-day gap between terminal activity and the newest journal fill is detectable without an operator noticing it'): `prop_fills_staleness` shipped 2026-08-23 and is that detector. Its B arm — two consecutive operator-reported balance snapshots differing by >= $25 with ZERO fills reported in between — is exactly 'the book traded and nothing was recorded', and it caught this very incident.

⚠️ RECORD THE BLIND SPOT RATHER THAN CLOSING OVER IT. Arm B **requires the operator to have reported a balance**, and arm A requires `prop_sl_tp_alert` to have announced a crossing. So a total REPORTING blackout — no balance, no screenshots — is invisible to both, by construction. That is not a defect in this detector (it is the correct scope: it must never key on unacted tickets, which are the expected shape on a manual bridge and would be the desensitized-alarm P1); the cover for a blackout is the balance ASK, `prop_status_request`. And measured TODAY the status is stale at 47.4h against a 24h threshold with no way to tell whether the bot is still asking — which is why BL-20260825-ALERT-AND-CADENCE-STATE-FILES-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE matters and carries that open question. This row closes; that one holds it.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS ROW, and separately filed: 26 of the 35 fills (74.3%) carry NO trade timestamp at all — see BL-20260825-PROP-FILLS-RECORD-WHEN-THEY-WERE-REPORTED-NOT-WHEN-THEY-TRADED. The 17 stuck `emitted` tickets this row's detail also mentions remain their own item.

items.title: The prop bridge escalates a stale BALANCE and has no equivalent for FILLS, so a multi-day reporting gap is discoverable only by a human noticing it
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-23. src/prop/prop_status_request.py asks the operator for a fresh balance once the latest prop_account_status row passes PROP_STATUS_REQUEST_MAX_AGE_HOURS (24h, re-asked on a 12h cooldown). There is NO analogous check on FILLS. The consequence was measured the same day: the journal's newest prop fill of any status was 2026-08-19T21:31:42Z while the operator's terminal showed a complete SOLUSD round trip on 22/08 (opened 07:48 @ 100.51, closed 08:10 @ 95.00) — three days of prop trading with no record in the money DB, surfaced only because the operator happened to send a screenshot into chat (BL-20260823-PROP-JOURNAL-MISSING-THREE-DAYS-OF-TERMINAL-TRADES). ⚠️ THE ALERT MUST NOT KEY ON UNACTED TICKETS. Operator directive 2026-08-23: 'because it isn't fully automated, we can't fill every ticket as I'm not always available when the ticket is relevant, so don't read into unacted on tickets too much.' On a manual bridge an unacted ticket is the EXPECTED shape, not a failure — 17 tickets sit at status=emitted spanning 2026-06-21 to 2026-08-21 and that is normal. An alert on those would fire constantly and be walked past, which is the desensitized-alarm P1 this repo has a rule against. The signal wanted is the opposite: the BOOK TRADED and NOTHING WAS REPORTED.
items.resolution_criteria: A prop account whose position/ticket state implies trading activity, with no fill reported for longer than a declared bound, raises one rate-limited alert naming the account and the gap — and does NOT alert on unacted tickets. The hard part is the trigger, since the bridge has no broker feed: candidate signals are a ticket that reached status=filled with no subsequent close report, a balance snapshot that MOVED between reports without an intervening fill (the 08-19 -> 08-23 balance fell 4982.86 -> 4871 with zero fills recorded, which is itself the detectable signature), or an operator-reported position count that disagrees with the journal. Closed when a multi-day gap between real trading and the newest journal fill is detectable without a human noticing it.
items.resolution:
RESOLVED — `src/prop/prop_fills_staleness.py` ships, runs once per trader tick (`src/main.py:943-944 run_prop_fills_staleness()`), and surfaces as the `prop_fills_stale` banner on `/api/bot/notifications` (`src/web/api/routers/notifications.py:249,264-265,288,638`), with `stale_fill_accounts()` exposed for the review skills.

Read the two detectors in the code, not the summary: `crossed_unreported` (an open position whose SL/TP was already ANNOUNCED as crossed ≥ grace hours ago and is still open) and `balance_moved_unreported` (two consecutive operator snapshots whose balance moved ≥ threshold with zero fills reported between). Both require positive evidence the book traded; NEITHER keys on unacted tickets, which was the operator's explicit twice-stated constraint (an unanswered ticket is the expected shape on a manual bridge, so alerting on it would be the desensitized-alarm P1). A test asserts the module never imports list_tickets / find_unacted_tickets / prop_reconcile.

items.title: The prop balance acknowledgement prints 'to daily-loss $None' — a Python repr where a safety number belongs
items.detail: OBSERVED LIVE 2026-08-23. The operator typed 'bal 4871 4871' and the bot replied: '✅ account status recorded [breakout_1] · to daily-loss $None · to DD-floor $171.0'. The DD-floor half is correct and matched this session's independent estimate of ~171 exactly. The daily-loss half renders the string 'None' behind a dollar sign. THE UNDERLYING DATA GAP IS REAL AND IS NOT THE BUG: realized_today and day_start_balance are null on every prop_account_status row (verified on the latest row via /api/bot/prop/status), so distance_to_daily_loss_usd genuinely cannot be computed from the snapshot alone — the endpoint's own field is computed against an ASSUMED day_pnl of 0.0. Refusing to state a number nobody measured is correct. Rendering that refusal as '$None' is not: it reads as a value, it is the shape a reader skims past, and it is on the one message whose entire job is to tell the operator how much cushion is left before an account-killer. This is the operator-facing instance of the collapsed-state family — 'we did not measure this' and 'the distance is zero' must not look alike, and '$None' is worse than either because it looks like neither.
items.resolution_criteria: The acknowledgement never prints a Python repr where a number belongs. Either the daily-loss distance is DERIVED (day_pnl from the fills store since the UTC day boundary, which would also make the field measured rather than assumed), or it says 'not measured' in words. Closed when a null distance is unmistakably a non-measurement on every surface that renders it, and the same check covers the sibling DD-floor field so the next null there cannot ship the same way.

updates.note: RE-CONFIRMED BY LIVE PAYLOAD: /api/bot/prop/status returns distance_to_daily_loss_usd null and daily_loss_used_usd null today (day_pnl_state `realized_unreported`), which is exactly the input that renders as 'to daily-loss $None'. A Python repr where a safety number belongs, on the account $55 from its floor. Small fix, high visibility.

items.title: breakout_1 is down to TWO live legs of one strategy family and no compat matrix has been verified for the roster as it now stands
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-23 after the Tier-3 de-dup. breakout_1 declares three strategies, of which eth_pullback_prop_2h is execution: shadow (demoted the same day in #10161 on OOS -11.78R), leaving exactly TWO live legs: trend_donchian_sol_prop and trend_donchian_eth_prop. Both are the same strategy family, the same 1h timeframe, and two symbols. Everything the prop book does from here is Donchian breakouts on SOL and ETH. The prop-accounts design and both the backtesting and new-strategy skills REQUIRE scripts/prop/account_compat_matrix.py (cost-aware EV + survival via src/prop/montecarlo.py under config/prop_rulesets/breakout.yaml) before a strategy is routed to an account — but the roster has changed repeatedly since any such run (legs added, the pullback twin removed 2026-07-20, eth_pullback_prop_2h demoted 2026-08-23, the two donchian base twins removed 2026-08-23), and whether a matrix has ever been run against the CURRENT set is unverified by this session. Survival arithmetic on a STATIC 6% max-DD account is sensitive to exactly this: concentration into one family on one timeframe is a different risk profile from a diversified roster, and a two-leg book can breach on a single correlated move. Note the honest possibility that the answer is a WIDER roster rather than a narrower one — the de-dup was right on its own merits (a duplicate leg that cannot reach its target) and says nothing about what the total roster should be.
items.resolution_criteria: account_compat_matrix.py has been run against the roster as it stands, under breakout.yaml, and its EV + survival verdict is recorded against each live leg — with the run predating any further routing change rather than following it. Closed when a reader can tell, from the record, that every leg currently routed to breakout_1 was evaluated under that account's own rules AT ITS CURRENT CONCENTRATION.

updates.note: Part of the prop cluster. Live: breakout_1 equity $4,755 against its $4,700 static-DD floor ($55.00 of cushion), daily-loss distance null, snapshot 0.9 h fresh, reconcile 84 tickets / 40 fills / 0 unacted. No compat matrix verified for the roster as it now stands. The mandatory per-account compatibility rule exists precisely so a strategy is never routed to an account it was not evaluated against under that account's rules.

items.title: Nothing periodically asks which EXISTING strategies have earned a prop route - routing has only ever been additive-by-request, and the ranking criterion is survival under the Breakout evaluation rules, NOT ticket answer-rate (operator-corrected 2026-08-23)
items.detail: Operator-scoped 2026-08-23, queued last: 'reviewing other strategies that we have that are candidates to route to the prop as well... what's performing well, and should we consider adding to the prop account?' Full analysis in docs/audits/full-system-audit-2026-08-23.md section 11.4. (1) There is no recurring candidate review - legs reach breakout_1 when someone proposes one, never because a periodic pass surfaced them, so the roster drifts by subtraction (2026-07-20 eth_pullback_2h de-dup, 2026-08-23 eth_pullback_prop_2h demotion, 2026-08-23 donchian de-dup) and never by addition. It is now TWO live legs of one family (BL-20260823-PROP-ROSTER-COMPAT-MATRIX-UNVERIFIED). (2) WARNING - THE ORIGINAL VERSION OF THIS ROW GOT THE RANKING BACKWARDS AND IS RETRACTED. It asserted that manual-bridge fit 'should DOMINATE' the ranking, that a 5m/15m signal is 'stale before a human reliably sees it', and therefore that the two largest measured numbers being SCALPS meant bridge fit 'inverts the naive ranking and must be applied BEFORE performance'. The operator corrected this directly on 2026-08-23: 'it's fine to add those five minute and ten minute scalps. That shouldn't be, like, a blocker from adding them to the prop account', and 'it's fine if the tickets go unanswered. That shouldn't be a metric of success here. This is still in a testing phase. And if it proves itself, then we'll add automation features.' So TICKET ANSWER-RATE IS NOT A SUCCESS METRIC and must not rank anything - the retracted version promoted a CAPACITY observation into a QUALITY criterion, excluding the best-performing legs on a constraint the operator has said to stop optimising around, with automation as the stated downstream remedy. (3) THE CRITERION IS PASSING THE BREAKOUT EVALUATION, which has not happened yet: +10% (+$500) profit target against a 3% ($150) daily loss limit and a 6% STATIC $4,700 floor that binds even while flat. Rank on cost-aware EV AND survival under those two limits via scripts/prop/account_compat_matrix.py -> src/prop/montecarlo.py::run_ev_montecarlo. MEASURED from /api/bot/performance?window=all (authoritative, NOT a local re-derivation), prop-eligible paper legs by totalPnlMeasured: ict_scalp_sol_5m +8214.59 (n=17, coverage 0.41), trend_donchian_eth_4h +7024.91 (n=12, 0.50), ict_scalp_sol_15m +2878.85 (n=14, 0.29), ict_scalp_eth_15m +2131.37 (n=10, 0.70 - the highest coverage in the table), trend_donchian_sol_4h +489.30 (n=8, 0.38), eth_pullback_2h -5674.58 (n=14, 0.64), sol_pullback_2h 0.00 (n=5, coverage 0.0 - UNGRADED, not flat). With the scalps restored to eligibility ict_scalp_sol_5m is the TOP-ranked candidate, not an excluded one. Read coverage beside every figure: at 0.29-0.50 the measured sum rests on a minority of rows, and trend_donchian_sol_4h FLIPS SIGN between raw (-196.21) and measured (+489.30). These are PAPER, bybit-economics results - no daily-loss limit, different costs - so no row here is a routing recommendation on its own. (4) THE 'NO DIVERSIFYING CANDIDATE EXISTS' CONCLUSION IS ALSO RETRACTED: it rested entirely on the scalps being excluded. ict_scalp is a different family on the same eligible symbols, so family diversification IS available and three of the top four candidates are it - which softens the concentration finding in section 11.1. (5) A CORRECTION WORTH KEEPING: my first pass ranked candidates off a LOCAL re-derivation of provenance over a journal mirror and returned zero measured rows for every leg - one step from filing 'no prop candidate has a single graded row', which is false. Rank from /performance, never from a local re-derivation.
items.resolution_criteria: A candidate review exists as a repeatable pass (a skill step or a scheduled report) that ranks prop-eligible legs from /api/bot/performance on totalPnlMeasured BESIDE pnlCoverage, applies the three prop filters - symbol eligibility, survival under the $150 daily / $4,700 static floor, and swap-drag-aware economics - and runs account_compat_matrix.py under breakout.yaml at the resulting concentration for anything that survives. Manual-bridge fit is recorded as an expected-fill-rate NOTE and must rank nothing (operator-corrected 2026-08-23); a pass that filters candidates on answer-rate does not close this row. It must carry an explicit 'the answer may be none' branch so it cannot become a search for a reason to add a leg - but that branch must be reached by the compat matrix rejecting candidates, never by an a-priori filter. Closed when a reader can see, from the record, which legs were considered for prop and why each was rejected.

updates.note: Re-validated: routing has only ever been additive-by-request, and nothing periodically asks which existing strategies have EARNED a prop route. Structural gap, not a defect.

items.area: order path / exit geometry / risk management
items.title: The 9.9% TP sentinel clamp is applied with NO reference to the SL distance, so a high-ATR instrument gets a target NEARER than its stop (R:R < 1) and nothing checks, refuses, or reports it - live on real money right now - REFRAMED: the real defect is that 29 of 52 enabled legs place the exchange's rejection threshold as their target, and the remedy is M20's active-management build, NOT a reward-to-risk floor
items.detail: OPERATOR-FOUND 2026-08-23: 'the live XRP trade has a SL farther from entry than the TP'. Confirmed and root-caused. MEASURED on the live position endpoint: trade 4934, bybit_2, REAL MONEY, xrp_pullback_2h XRPUSDT long, entry 1.4995, SL 1.28355357 (risk 0.215946 = 14.40% of entry), TP 1.6479505 (reward 0.148451 = 9.90% of entry) -> R:R = 0.687. The same package also filled on bybit_1 (4933) and bybit_portfolio (4935), both paper.
