MECHANISM: xrp_pullback_2h declares tp_r: 50.0, a deliberate FAR SENTINEL meaning 'there is no real target, the Chandelier trail is the profit exit'. src/units/strategies/htf_pullback_trend_2h.py:322 then computes tp = min(entry*(1+_TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT), entry + tp_r*risk) with _TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT = 0.099, because Bybit rejects a TP more than ~10% from the reference price (ErrCode 10001). 1.4995*1.099 = 1.6479505 EXACTLY - the placed TP is the clamp, not the strategy's target. The SL is unclamped (entry - atr_stop_mult*ATR = 2.5*ATR). So the two legs of the bracket are computed on DIFFERENT BASES and nothing relates them: whenever atr_stop_mult*ATR/entry > 9.9% the target lands nearer than the stop. trend_donchian.py:388 carries the identical clamp and the identical exposure. THE CODE COMMENT STATES THE ASSUMPTION THAT FAILS: 'Cap to ~9.9% from entry so the sentinel is exchange-valid AND still far enough that the monitor's Chandelier trail remains the real profit-exit.' At 50R that is true; at 9.9% on a 14.4%-risk instrument it is false - and the clamped sentinel is a REAL binding exit, not decoration: exit_reason 'tp_cross' has fired 3 times on pullback_2h + trend_donchian legs (measured over all 4,962 journal trades). n=3 is enough to refute 'unreachable', not enough to size the cost. POPULATION (state it): over 3,665 non-pairs order packages carrying numeric entry+SL+TP, risk/entry exceeds the 9.9% clamp in 3 (0.08%) and R:R lands below 1 in 6 (0.16%). Of the 3 clamped, 2 are the pullback legs and BOTH ARE CURRENTLY OPEN: xrp_pullback_2h (R:R 0.687, real money on bybit_2) and ada_pullback_2h (R:R 0.843). The third (ict_scalp_avax_5m) clamped without going sub-1 because ict_scalp sizes its target as tp_at_r*risk and does not apply this clamp. So the defect is RARE but it is binding on a real-money position as of this filing. The remaining 3 vwap + 1 turtle_soup R:R<1 rows are a DIFFERENT mechanism (risk/entry 0.17-0.35%, nowhere near the clamp) filed separately as BL-20260823-VWAP-TARGET-NEARER-THAN-STOP, and the 100 pairs_* rows at exactly R:R 0.500 are deliberate placeholders (SL = exactly 2.000x entry, TP = exactly 0.500x entry - verified as exact multiples, not computed geometry) on the isolated 2-leg pairs path, not brackets. WHY THE REVIEW MISSED IT - this is the important half, and it is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A (a value published under a label that answers a different question). The ratio IS measured and IS published: src/runtime/position_telemetry.py::cap_r computes exactly 0.099*entry/risk and the live /api/bot/positions r-block for trade 4934 carries capR 0.6874 and rrFromHere 0.8484. But EVERY consumer reads cap_r as a CEILING FOR THE LEVER ARM - arm_reach grades 'is arm_r <= cap_r', /api/diag/position_telemetry reports arm_reach, scripts/ops/lever_reachability_audit.py reports cap_r percentiles, scripts/research/m31_mfe_parity.py checks peak_r <= cap_r. NOT ONE consumer asks whether cap_r < 1, which is the same number answering 'is the target nearer than the stop'. Worse: CLAUDE.md's own /api/bot/positions row already documents rrFromHere on THIS EXACT TRADE - 'on the motivating XRP trade it is 0.71, i.e. holding for the target risks more than it stands to make' - so the number was in the canonical doc, about this trade, and was read as an EXIT-TIMING signal ('should we hold this?') rather than as an ENTRY-GEOMETRY defect ('this should not have been placed like this'). My own M20 exit-wiring audit this session surfaced armReach 'unreachable' for xrp_pullback_2h and made the same substitution. Confirmed by grep: no min_rr / min_risk_reward / reward-to-risk floor exists anywhere in src/ on the order path (the only 'reward_to_risk' hit is src/backtest/backtester.py's own config default, which is not the live path). ==== OPERATOR REFRAME 2026-08-23, AND A CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN DENOMINATOR. Four remedies were put to the operator (refuse below a 1.0 floor / rescale the stop to fit the clamp / make the clamp venue-aware / accept sub-1 explicitly) and ALL FOUR WERE REJECTED: 'brackets ALWAYS represent our prediction of where the trade should end - e.g. if it's momentum driven, the TP is where we expect momentum to run out, and the SL represents where we think we can consider ourselves wrong and cut our losses. Then the active management adjusts the brackets based on the ongoing monitoring. The only solution here is to properly build out the active management infra, not layer on bandaids to a poorly constructed strategy.' Every option offered accepts a target that is NOT A PREDICTION and argues about what to do around it. THE CLASS IS ALREADY SPECIFIED IN THIS REPO with a larger measurement: docs/design/exit-mechanism-construction-PROCESS.md section 2 ('A bracket must carry an expectation at entry, or it is not a bracket ... This is not what the fleet does today') backed by docs/research/e35-bracket-is-not-a-decision-2026-08-20.md (6,428 trades / 19 legs / 2021-08-16 to 2026-08-19, net of fees). DO NOT QUOTE THIS ROW'S '3 of 3,665 (0.08%)' AS THE SIZE OF THE PROBLEM - it is correct for what it measures (how often the clamp pushes R:R below 1, a threshold-crossing) and is two orders of magnitude too small for the defect. State the population: 52 ENABLED legs in config/strategies.yaml, 29 (55.8%) declare tp_r >= 50, of which 26 are execution: live (counted 2026-08-23); the E3.5 set puts it at 16 of 19 legs with trade history (84.2%). MORE THAN HALF THE ENABLED FLEET PLACES THE EXCHANGE'S REJECTION THRESHOLD AS ITS TAKE-PROFIT ON EVERY TRADE. R:R < 1 is only where that becomes visible because it crosses a line a human notices - the XRP trade is the ordinary case seen from an obvious angle, not a rare defect. E3.5 also establishes why it is not cosmetic: entry*1.099 is a fixed fraction of price, so tp_R and ATR/close are THE SAME VARIABLE (collinearity confirmed 19/19), target distance varies 6.5x-38.9x within every leg, and 76.2% of the fleet's net R comes from the 23.1% of trades whose target is more than 5R away - i.e. from trades the bracket cannot close. AND A SECOND REVIEW FAILURE TO OWN, worse than the cap_r substitution above: the class was already documented here with a better measurement and I did not connect the XRP trade to it - I re-derived a narrow version, chose a denominator that made it look like a 0.08% edge case, and proposed bandaids the operator had to point back from. A finding that reads as new when it is a documented class competes with the real work instead of feeding it. ==== NOT A BACKLOG ITEM - IN FLIGHT 2026-08-23. Operator-directed: 'rebuilding exit geometry is basically what we're focused on right now (once we get through the audit/review/blockers), so this isn't an issue to be backlogged - it should be fixed in the course of the work we are doing today.' This row stays open as the RECORD of the finding and its measurement; the WORK is the active exit-geometry rebuild, not a future review session picking this up. A session that treats this as deferred has misread it.
items.resolution_criteria: SUPERSEDED BY THE OPERATOR REFRAME - this row no longer resolves by adding a reward-to-risk floor, and MUST NOT be closed by one. It closes as part of M20's active-management build, whose specification already owns it (docs/design/exit-mechanism-construction-PROCESS.md): (1) a bracket carries an EXPECTATION at entry - 'where do we expect this to exit, and why' becomes a required output of the entry decision, replacing tp_r: 50.0 on all 29 legs; (2) revision is conditioned on the strategy's OWN thesis - state where the move is expected to exhaust, and if price nears the target while the exhaustion condition has not fired, EXTEND. 'Extend the target' has NO implementation anywhere in the harness or the live monitor today, and that missing capability is what this finding is actually about; (3) amending a resting level costs nothing while exiting early costs 0.082-0.163 R against a fee-free mean edge of +0.1376 R (XRP) / +0.1167 R (SOL), which is the direct argument against the refuse-the-signal option. ACCEPTANCE TEST, operator-directed ('Fix forward means applying the infra we are about to build to the open trades'): the two currently-open sub-1 positions - XRP trade 4934 on bybit_2 (REAL MONEY) and the ada_pullback_2h leg - are the FIRST trades the bracket-revision capability is applied to when it lands. They are neither left to run on the geometry they were given nor hand-re-cut now. If the capability cannot state where those two are expected to exit and revise their levels accordingly, it is not finished. The Tier-1 half that CAN ship independently is the missing READER: declared reward-to-risk graded where the order package is formed and surfaced, so a sub-1 package is visible without anyone thinking to ask - but shipping that alone does not close this row.

updates.note: Re-validated: a 9.9% clamp applied with no reference to SL distance gives a high-ATR instrument a target NEARER than its stop — a negative-expectancy geometry by construction. Pairs with BL-20260823-VWAP-TARGET-NEARER-THAN-STOP (same outcome, different mechanism) and BL-20260823-XRP-DECLARED-TARGET-EXCEEDS-VENUE-CAP (tp_r 3.0 clamped to 0.687R). Three rows, one venue-clamp family.

items.title: vwap and turtle_soup can place a target nearer than their stop by a DIFFERENT mechanism than the TP clamp - a level-based target against a multiple-based stop, with no floor relating them
items.detail: Found while sizing BL-20260823-TP-CLAMP-HAS-NO-SL-REFERENCE, and kept separate because it is NOT the same cause and must not be folded into that row's remedy. MEASURED over 3,665 non-pairs order packages carrying numeric entry+SL+TP: 6 have R:R < 1, of which 2 are the TP-clamp class (xrp_pullback_2h 0.687, ada_pullback_2h 0.843) and 4 are these - vwap x3 and turtle_soup x1. The clamp is not involved: their risk/entry medians are 0.17% (vwap, n=1965) and 0.35% (turtle_soup, n=3), two orders of magnitude below the 9.9% clamp, so nothing was ever clamped. The mechanism is that the TARGET is a LEVEL and the STOP is a MULTIPLE: src/units/strategies/vwap.py places tp at the VWAP line itself while sl is sl_std_mult standard deviations from entry, so when price is close to VWAP relative to the band width the target lands inside the stop. The module docstring at vwap.py:201 explicitly claims a 'preserved risk:reward of 1:2 at the entry boundary (SL=0.5 sigma)' - true AT THE BOUNDARY, and the 3 sub-1 rows are what happens away from it. So the docstring is a statement about one point being generalised to the whole surface, which is the field-beats-comment shape. RATE: 3 of 1,965 vwap packages (0.15%) and 1 of 3 turtle_soup packages (33.3%, n=3 - not a rate, an observation). NOT URGENT: no such row is currently open, and vwap's risk/entry is tiny so the absolute dollar exposure per event is small. Filed so the geometry check that closes the clamp row is not scoped so narrowly that it misses this - a reward-to-risk floor belongs to the ORDER PATH, not to one strategy's clamp.
items.resolution_criteria: REFRAMED with its sibling 2026-08-23: this does NOT resolve by adding a reward-to-risk floor. vwap's target is a LEVEL (the VWAP line) and its stop a MULTIPLE, so unlike the tp_r: 50.0 legs its target IS already a prediction - which is why it is filed low and separately. What it owes is (a) the vwap.py:201 docstring's '1:2 preserved' claim corrected to state the condition under which it holds (it is true at the entry boundary and was generalised to the whole surface), and (b) inclusion in whatever declared-geometry surface the active-management build produces, so a level-based target landing inside its own stop is visible rather than inferred. Whether vwap should REFUSE such a setup is a separate Tier-3 call and may reasonably be 'no'; record the decision either way.

updates.note: Re-validated: a level-based path to the same inverted geometry as the clamp row above.

items.title: The mandatory prop compat matrix, run for the first time on the CURRENT roster, says the 2026-08-23 de-dup kept the better twin on ETH and the WORSE twin on SOL - seed-stable, both still ROUTE
items.detail: P2 of the operator-scoped prop refinement. TWO BLOCKERS CLEARED FIRST, both worth their own note. (a) CANDLE FEED: data/ohlcv/ holds five files and none is SOL or ETH; Bybit returns 403 from the sandbox and Yahoo 429 - but data.binance.vision answers 200, so the 'no free lane candle feed' blocker is NOT absolute here. Fetched 21,600 1h bars each for SOLUSDT and ETHUSDT (2024-03-06 to 2026-08-22) via the repo's own scripts/ops/fetch_backtest_candles.py --source binance_vision. (b) THE GATE COULD NOT SCORE THE ROUTED LEGS: the _prop variants were ABSENT from scripts/backtest_system.py::ROSTER, so the mandatory gate could only run the BASE twins - which differ from what is routed in exactly the dimension the gate measures (tp_r 6.0 / trail_mult 3.5 against 50.0 / 5.0). Scoring the base and reporting it as the prop leg's result is a semantic substitution (CLAUDE.md 'Diagnostic provenance' sub-class B). Both _prop names are now registered research-only; params resolve from config/strategies.yaml by NAME via _load_strategy_cfg, so they carry the real live exit geometry rather than a copy. RESULTS (breakout_1 ruleset, 1.5% risk on $5,000, Monte-Carlo EV + survival): trend_donchian_eth_prop n=450 EV +$2,074 P(net>0)=0.9700 ROUTE (routed); trend_donchian_eth n=339 EV +$1,694 P=0.9367 ROUTE (removed); trend_donchian_sol n=150 EV +$1,162 P=0.9137 ROUTE (REMOVED); trend_donchian_sol_prop n=160 EV +$611 P=0.7603 ROUTE (routed). EVERY LEG CLEARS THE GATE - nothing here says the prop book holds something it should not. But the de-dup kept the better twin on ETH and the WORSE twin on SOL: on SOL the base wins on both axes and is the leg the change removes. SEED-STABLE, so not noise - across four seeds (default, 7, 13, 99) sol_prop ranges EV $606-$638 / P 0.753-0.773 while the base ranges $1,142-$1,162 / P 0.903-0.908; within-arm spread ~$30 and ~0.02 against a between-arm gap of ~$530 and ~0.14. CAVEATS, load-bearing: these are RESEARCH verdicts on a Binance-Vision feed and not the account's venue data (the tool's own output requires revalidation before live wiring); THE ARMS ARE NOT PAIRED - same entries, different exits, so the ledgers differ in length (150 vs 160, 339 vs 450), making this a comparison of two strategies rather than one strategy under two exits on identical trades; and the prop path keys on EV and P(net>0), not on the survival/breach columns the standard gate reports. WHAT IT DOES NOT CHANGE: the de-dup's premise is untouched - two legs firing the same entries on one $5k account with a $150 daily-loss limit is a real problem and one twin per symbol is right. What it changes is WHICH twin on SOL. ⚠️ READ IT AGAINST BL-20260823-TP-CLAMP-HAS-NO-SL-REFERENCE BEFORE ACTING: the base twin's edge here comes from tp_r: 50.0, i.e. from NOT having a reachable target - precisely the geometry that row records as not-a-prediction and that M20's active-management build is meant to replace. 'The base wins on SOL' and 'the base's target is the exchange's rejection threshold' are the same fact seen twice, so a re-flip on this evidence buys EV now and re-adopts the geometry being retired.
items.resolution_criteria: An operator decision on the SOL twin, recorded either way, with this table in front of them: (a) re-flip - re-add trend_donchian_sol to breakout_1.strategies and remove trend_donchian_sol_prop (Tier-3), accepting that it re-adopts the tp_r: 50.0 geometry; (b) hold the current routing and record that the lower-EV twin is kept deliberately, because its target is a prediction and the base's is a venue limit; or (c) defer until M20's active-management build gives the _prop leg a real target, then re-run this matrix - which is the only option that resolves the tension rather than choosing a side of it. Both legs ROUTE and both are positive EV, so the cost of the current state is opportunity and not risk; this is a decision, not an incident, and must NOT be closed by a session re-flipping it unilaterally. Closed when the decision and its reasoning are in the record.

updates.note: Prop cluster. Live: breakout_1 equity $4,755 against a $4,700 static-DD floor ($55.00 cushion), daily-loss distance null, PROP_TICKET_RISK_GATE_MODE still `annotate`. The compat matrix says the de-dup kept the WORSE twin. That is a routing decision on the account with $55 of room.

items.tier: 2 (order-path adjacent: it decides whether a live position is graded protected)
items.title: The price axis is PRODUCED on all three venues but CONSUMED on only one -- the Alpaca and Bybit naked sweeps now carry stop_prices and never grade them, and bybit_2 is the mainnet account
items.detail:
Filed by the session that closed BL-20260820-PROTECTION-COVERAGE-IS-PRICE-BLIND, as the residual that row's criterion 5 names explicitly rather than leaves implied.

WHAT SHIPPED. src/runtime/protection_price.py::grade_protection_price is the single pure grader (agrees / diverges / no_declared_level / no_resting_price / no_resting_leg / no_tick_size), and all three venue reads now EMIT the prices it needs: IB via IBClient.protection_coverage -> stop_prices/target_prices (_protective_leg_price reads auxPrice FIRST for a stop), Bybit via order_monitor._bybit_position_protection -> stop_prices on all three return paths (flat / full_position_stop / partial_sl_legs, through the new _bybit_sl_leg_trigger), Alpaca via AlpacaClient.protection_state -> stop_prices/target_prices (AlpacaClient._leg_price).

WHAT DID NOT. Exactly ONE consumer grades: order_monitor._check_broker_naked_ib_positions. MEASURED, with a probe shown to return a positive: grep 'grade_protection_price' over src/ + scripts/ returns 3 hits, all in protection_price.py's own __all__ plus the single IB call site at order_monitor.py:7045-7047; the same grep shape over _check_broker_naked_equity_positions and _check_broker_naked_bybit_positions returns ZERO, and neither body even references 'stop_prices'. So on Alpaca and Bybit the data is present, correct, and unread -- the written-and-never-read shape provenance-consumer-guard exists to catch, and the exact shape of the parent row's own root cause (exit_price_source written in 12 files, branched on in one).

WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC, AND WHY IT IS HIGH RATHER THAN CRITICAL. The parent row's live instance is ib_paper (MES trade 4350, 69 ticks / $1,289.73), which is the venue that now grades. The two that do NOT grade include bybit_2, which is MAINNET -- the parent row's own 2026-08-22 update measured 9 open Bybit positions across bybit_1/bybit_2/bybit_portfolio (2 of them real-money on bybit_2) plus 16 Alpaca, every one of which grades 'protected' on a test that cannot see where the stop sits. It is HIGH not CRITICAL because no divergence has been MEASURED on either venue -- the reason being precisely that nothing looks, so the honest statement is 'we did not look', never 'they are clean'. State the population before quoting any number off this row.

WHAT THE FIX IS NOT. Do not copy the IB block into two more places. The IB block is detect-only by design and asserted so by test (it calls none of cancel / modify_open_order / place_protective / _attempt_naked_autoprotect), because choosing what to DO about a divergence is what went wrong on 2026-08-20 (BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG). Any Bybit/Alpaca grading must inherit the same detect-only posture, and the tick tolerance must come from a resolver that returns None rather than a default when the tick is unknown (profile_loader.tick_size_for) -- a defaulted tick flips a real divergence into 'agrees', which is the failure direction that matters.
resolution_criteria: _check_broker_naked_bybit_positions grades stop_prices through grade_protection_price and declares the verdict in its summary up front (a 'stop_price_diverges' key present at 0, so 'we looked and found none' cannot read as 'we did not look'). DETECT-ONLY, asserted by a test that the block calls none of cancel / modify_open_order / place_protective / _attempt_naked_autoprotect. The QUANTITY verdict must be byte-unchanged -- assert it, do not assume it.
_check_broker_naked_equity_positions does the same for Alpaca, with the same detect-only assertion and the same byte-unchanged quantity verdict.

The tick tolerance for each venue resolves through profile_loader.tick_size_for (or a stated equivalent that likewise returns None on an unknown symbol). A symbol with no resolvable tick must grade 'no_tick_size' and NOT 'agrees' -- there is a test for this on the IB side; mirror it rather than re-deriving it.

A DISCRIMINATING run on live payloads: at least one correctly-bracketed position graded clean and at least one divergence flagged in the SAME run, per venue where the live book supplies both. If today's book supplies no divergence on a venue, say so explicitly and state the denominator -- a run that flags nothing over an unstated population is not evidence of cleanliness.

State the measured divergence population per venue when this closes: how many open positions were graded, how many diverged, and how many could not be graded (unreadable price, unknown tick). A close that reports only the divergences without the denominator repeats the sub-class-C failure this programme keeps naming.

updates.note: RE-CONFIRMED LIVE: I read /api/diag/bybit_open_orders today and it DOES expose per-position stop_loss/take_profit and per-order trigger_price — the price axis is produced. The Bybit naked sweep still grades on quantity only. Produced-but-not-consumed, which is class A applied to a safety grade.

items.title: `resolution_criteria` is a bare STRING on 752 of 1034 backlog rows and a LIST on the rest, so the obvious `for c in criteria` yields one character per line instead of raising
items.detail:
Found while draining the critical backlog: I iterated `resolution_criteria` on BL-20260818-ATTACH-IB-TARGET-VERIFY-CANNOT-EXPRESS-FILLED and got ONE CHARACTER PER LINE. The field carries TWO types across the three backlogs and nothing pins it.

MEASURED 2026-08-23 (state the population -- all three backlogs, every row):
  health        824 rows: 605 string,  16 list, 203 absent
  performance   106 rows:  69 string,   0 list,  37 absent
  ml            104 rows:  78 string,   1 list,  25 absent

So the STRING shape is the MAJORITY (health 73.4%), and both shapes are in active use by rows written days apart -- this is not a legacy tail that new rows have grown out of.

WHY IT IS A DEFECT AND NOT A STYLE NIT. `for c in row['resolution_criteria']` is the obvious read, it is CORRECT for the list shape, and on the string shape it does not raise -- it yields characters. A session rendering a row's criteria gets a column of single letters and either notices (wasted time) or does not (a criteria list silently reported as ~900 empty bullets). That is the unprovenanced-diagnostic sub-class A shape from CLAUDE.md: the accessor does not compute what the label says, and nothing in the output reveals the substitution. It has no runtime blast radius -- these files are read by review sessions and report renderers, not by the trader -- which is why this is medium, not high.

WHAT IS NOT BROKEN, asserted rather than assumed. `scripts/ops/check_backlog_criteria.py` is type-agnostic BY LUCK, not by design: it does `text = str(raw).strip()` and then applies a length floor, so a list stringifies to "['a', 'b']" and clears the floor exactly as a sentence does. The guard is therefore NOT the thing to point at as evidence the field is well-formed -- it would pass a list of empty strings too. Verified by reading the function body, not by running it. And no OTHER consumer iterates today: grep over scripts/ src/ .claude/ tests/ returns check_backlog_criteria.py (str()), backlog_counts.py (a comment), render_system_report.py (a comment), check_claim_basis.py (a prose-field name list), and two SKILL.md mentions. The probe is valid -- the same grep shape returns positives for the field it looks for.

SO THE EXPOSURE IS FUTURE AND HUMAN, not present and machine: the next consumer that iterates gets characters for 73% of the corpus, and an ANALYSIS SESSION doing it ad hoc -- which is exactly how this was found -- gets them today.
resolution_criteria: A canonical accessor -- one function, e.g. scripts/ops/_backlog.py::criteria_list(row) -- that returns a list for BOTH shapes (a string becomes a one-element list; absent becomes []). Every consumer that wants to iterate goes through it. This is the cheap half and it fixes the hazard without touching 752 rows of prose.

check_backlog_criteria.py stops relying on str(raw) by accident: it calls the accessor, and it REJECTS a criteria value that is neither str nor list (today a dict, an int or None-in-a-list would stringify and clear the length floor). Add the self-test cases -- the guard already has a --self-test harness with planted-defect cases, so mirror that shape rather than inventing one.

A DECISION on the corpus, recorded either way: either normalise the 752 string rows to one-element lists in a single mechanical pass (and say so, with a before/after count), or declare the string shape permanently supported and the accessor mandatory. Do NOT half-do it -- a corpus that is 60% normalised is worse than one that is 0% normalised, because it makes the remaining strings look like an oversight rather than a shape.

If the normalisation route is taken: it must not mangle prose. A string containing sentence-final periods is ONE criterion, not N -- splitting on '. ' would silently invent criteria that nobody wrote. Wrap, never split, unless a row is hand-reviewed.

updates.note:
RESOLVED — all four criteria, three shipped and the fourth made moot by the decision criterion 3 demanded.

CRITERION 1 — the canonical accessor exists: scripts/ops/_backlog.py::criteria_list(row) returns a list for BOTH shapes (a string becomes a ONE-element list, never split; absent becomes []), plus criteria_text(row) for length/placeholder checks. A shape that is neither str nor list nor absent raises UnsupportedCriteriaShape rather than being coerced — because silently accepting a dict is precisely how a malformed row passes a malformed-row guard.

CRITERION 2 — check_backlog_criteria.py no longer relies on str(raw) by accident. `_verdict` calls criteria_text and returns the shape error as its reason. Note the empty/absent split is kept distinct ('no resolution_criteria field' vs 'resolution_criteria is empty') rather than collapsed into one message. Seven self-test cases added in the existing --self-test harness, all passing: dict rejected; an int long enough to clear the 40-char floor as a repr rejected; a list containing a dict rejected; a list whose PROSE is 21 chars but whose repr is 26 rejected (the accidental-pass case this row names); and two ACCEPT cases proving the list shape still passes on real prose and that empty/None entries are dropped rather than counted.

NO CORPUS REGRESSION, ASSERTED NOT ASSUMED. The switch from str(raw) to criteria_text changes the measured length on every list row (brackets and quotes stop counting toward the floor), which could have flipped a short list row from pass to fail. Ran --all before and after over the same tree and diffed the failing ID SETS, not just the counts: 111 before, 111 after, sets IDENTICAL. So the change closes the hole without moving a single real row.

CRITERION 3 — THE DECISION, and it is recorded in the module docstring so it cannot be re-litigated from taste: THE STRING SHAPE IS PERMANENTLY SUPPORTED AND THE ACCESSOR IS MANDATORY. Not normalised. The basis, re-measured 2026-08-25 across all three backlogs: health 672 str / 36 list / 203 absent, performance 72 str / 0 list, ml 78 str / 1 list. String rows span the full date range INCLUDING the same day as the newest list rows, so there is no 'new rows grew out of it' story that a normalisation would be finishing. A ~750-row prose rewrite would also touch every file that every diff-scoped guard reads, for zero behavioural gain over one accessor. Explicitly NOT half-done, which this row correctly called the worst outcome.

CRITERION 4 is moot by construction: it constrains the normalisation route ('wrap, never split'), and that route was not taken. The accessor wraps at READ time and the corpus is untouched, so no prose can be mangled.

SEE ALSO BL-20260825-KEPT-OPEN-ROWS-WITH-NO-EXIT-CONDITION-CAN-NEVER-BE-RETIRED, filed the same day. It rediscovered the two shapes independently and concluded 'string is the dominant convention, no defect' — correct about the CONVENTION and wrong to stop there, because the hazard was never the polymorphism, it was the silent character-iteration on the majority shape. That row has been annotated so the two do not read as contradicting each other.

items.tier: 2 (the exit/modify path decides whether a live position's protection is re-asserted)
items.title: A venue leg that diverges from the journal can NEVER be re-synced by the normal path -- the modify filter compares intent to `order_packages.sl`, so the system re-asserts a level it believes is already in place, forever
items.detail:
ROOT CAUSE, found while answering BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG's criterion 1. Explains why MES 4350 has sat 69 ticks mis-protected since 2026-08-20 with an active monitor on a CONNECTED session, and generalises to every venue and every leg.

THE MECHANISM, read from the code rather than inferred:
  order_monitor.py:771  decision = interpret_verdict(verdict, current_sl=open_pkg.get('sl'), ...)
  monitor_verdict.py:164  tol = max(abs(cur) * MEANINGFUL_MODIFY_REL_TOL, 1e-8)
  monitor_verdict.py:165  if abs(updates[key] - cur) <= tol: del updates[key]
  monitor_verdict.py:168  if not updates: return _none('no_meaningful_change')
`current_sl` is `order_packages.sl` -- THE JOURNAL. The venue's resting price is not read, is not passed, and is not compared anywhere on this path.

CONSEQUENCE. Once the journal and the venue disagree, the disagreement is PERMANENT BY CONSTRUCTION. The strategy re-computes its level every pass; the level equals the journal's; the filter drops it as 'no meaningful change'; nothing is sent. The system is not failing to notice a problem -- it is correctly concluding that the change it wants has already been made, because the only record it consults says so.

THE LIVE INSTANCE, measured 2026-08-23T10:5xZ:
  trades 4350 / order_packages pkg-1d9598b29f38440c   sl = 7533.69642857 (identical to 8dp)
  the ONLY resting MES stop, order 338             aux = 7516.50, client_id 497, GTC
  /api/diag/ib_state: client 497 CONNECTED, 0 consecutive failures, last_ok 28.8s
So the placing session is alive, the monitor is running, the divergence is 69 ticks ($1,289.73 on 15 MES at contract_value_usd 5.0), and no code path in the repo can close it.

THIS IS NOT THE ALREADY-KNOWN CASE. order_monitor.py:1300-1310 documents the sibling: when an amend does NOT land, `order_packages.sl` is deliberately LEFT UNCHANGED so the verdict re-fires next tick -- 'the missed leg would keep its entry-time bracket forever, the very bug this change exists to fix'. That reasoning is correct and covers 'we tried and it did not land'. It does NOT cover 'it landed, and the venue changed underneath us afterwards' -- a foreign cancel, an over-cover remediation that kept the wrong leg, a broker-side expiry. In that second case the journal is a true record of what we ASKED and a false record of what RESTS, and the filter trusts it for the second question.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS TRADE. The whole price-divergence detection family shipped 2026-08-22/23 (BL-20260820-PROTECTION-COVERAGE-IS-PRICE-BLIND) now MEASURES this class on all three venues -- and there is no path that REPAIRS it, deliberately (detect-only). This row is why detect-only cannot be the end state: a detector whose findings no mechanism can act on accumulates findings.

⚠️ THE OBVIOUS FIX IS THE DANGEROUS ONE. 'Compare against the venue instead' puts a broker read on the modify path of every open position on every pass -- the unbounded-per-row-fetch shape of BOTH June 2026 wedges. Any fix inherits exit_anchor's timeout / per-tick budget / positive-AND-negative caching discipline, or it is a wedge waiting to happen. The cheap correct version is probably to feed the ALREADY-FETCHED coverage read (the naked sweeps run on their own cadence and now carry stop_prices) into a re-assert, rather than adding a read.
resolution_criteria: A live position whose resting protective price diverges from its journal-declared level gets that level RE-ASSERTED, without adding a broker read to the per-pass modify path. The prices are already fetched by the cadence-gated naked sweeps; route those rather than fetching again.

The re-assert READS trades.stop_loss / order_packages.sl and never takes a level from a caller or an operator -- the same rule BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG's criterion 2 states, for the same reason.

It must not fight a legitimately-cancelled leg into existence. A position that is FLAT, or whose trade is closed, must not have a stop re-asserted onto it; and a re-assert that fails must not retry every pass (rate-limited per (account, symbol), like the other latched alerts).

The idempotence filter's own semantics are stated in code: `current_sl` is what we BELIEVE rests, and something must own reconciling that belief with what DOES rest. Whether that is a widened `current_sl`, a separate re-assert pass, or a venue-truth column on order_packages is a design choice -- but 'no_meaningful_change' must stop being computable from a record that can be stale.

A regression test that a journal/venue divergence produces a re-assert, and that an AGREEING pair still produces no_meaningful_change -- a build that re-asserts on every pass is as broken as one that never does, and would re-amend every leg on every tick.

updates.note:
THE REMEDY IS BUILT AND SHIPPED AT `annotate`, same day, on operator direction: 'we need to be able to adjust trades on IB without disconnecting the integration, this is an important pipeline achievement and we can't leave it to chance because of one trade not being worth the effort.'

IT TOOK THE ROUTE THIS ROW ARGUED FOR, not the obvious one. The row warned that 'compare against the venue instead' would put a broker read on the modify path of every open position on every pass -- the unbounded-per-row-fetch shape of both June 2026 wedges -- and said the cheap correct version is to feed the ALREADY-FETCHED coverage read into a re-assert. That is exactly what shipped: `order_monitor._reassert_from_divergence` rides the cadence-gated naked sweep (IB_BROKER_NAKED_CHECK_SECONDS, 300s), which already holds `stop_prices` from the coverage read it just did. NO new broker call anywhere.

AND THE AMEND NEEDED NO NEW MECHANISM. `IBClient.modify_protective` has existed since BL-20260616-LTMGMT-MODIFY and runs on the TRADER'S OWN client, so it evicts nothing and needs no ops clientId. This is worth stating because the session spent real effort on the cancel-then-resweep route first, and that route is the WRONG one for a reason its own dry run printed: cancel_ib_order connects AS the owning clientId, order 338's owner is the trader's live execution session, and the refusal reads 'pass --force-client-id only with the trader stopped'. Taking down the trader to repair a paper stop is the trade this row's remedy avoids entirely.

THE DECISION IS A PURE FUNCTION (src/runtime/protection_reassert.py) so the policy is arguable in tests rather than against a live position -- which is precisely what went wrong on 2026-08-20. Seven states, never collapsed, and `not_graded` is deliberately distinct from `agrees`: an unresolvable tick or an unreadable resting price means the comparison did not happen.

CRITERIA STATUS. (1) MET -- re-assert without a new broker read. (2) MET -- the level is read from trades.stop_loss/take_profit_1 and never from a caller, pinned by a test asserting the sent sl equals the journal's and NOT the venue's. (3) MET -- a flat or non-open trade refuses (`position_absent`, checked FIRST so a divergence cannot fall through), and it is bounded per (account, symbol) by a cooldown and an attempt budget, both falling back to their default on an unparseable value rather than to zero. (5) MET -- tests cover both directions: a divergence produces a re-assert, an AGREEING pair produces none. (4) is the one still OPEN: the idempotence filter itself is UNCHANGED -- `interpret_verdict` still computes `no_meaningful_change` from `order_packages.sl`, and what shipped is a second, cadence-gated path that repairs the consequence rather than a change to the filter's semantics. That is the right first move (it is bounded and reversible) but it does not discharge the criterion, which asks that 'no_meaningful_change must stop being computable from a record that can be stale'.

SHIPPED AT `annotate`, WHICH IS NOT YET A FIX FOR ANY LIVE POSITION. The decision runs in full and writes runtime_logs/protection_reassert_soak.jsonl; nothing is placed. The flip to `apply` on ib_paper is Tier-2, is what actually repairs MES 4350, and is deliberately left for the operator to see a soak row first.

CRITERIA 4 AND 5 ARE NOW MET; 1-3 were met by the re-assert shipped earlier today.

CRITERION 4 -- 'the idempotence filter's own semantics are stated in code'. They now are, and the statement that was there was WORSE than silence: interpret_verdict's docstring read '`current_sl` / `current_tp` are the position's PRESENT LEVELS', which is false in the direction that hides the defect. A reader checking whether the modify path could see a venue divergence would have read that line and concluded it could. Every live caller passes the JOURNAL (order_monitor.py: open_pkg.get('sl')) and nothing on that path reads a resting price. The docstring now says so, names the permanent consequence (once the two disagree the strategy recomputes the journal's own level and the tolerance filter deletes it -- forever, every pass, every leg, every venue), cites the measured instance (MES 4350, 68.79 ticks / $1,289.73 on 15 contracts, since 2026-08-20 on a healthy monitor and a connected session), and names the owner of the reconciliation: src/runtime/protection_reassert.py, driven from the cadence-gated naked sweeps. It also states the ANTI-remedy explicitly -- do NOT widen current_sl into a venue read -- because that path runs per open position per pass and a broker call there is the shape of both June 2026 wedges. Docstring only: behaviour is byte-identical, asserted by the tests below rather than by inspection.

CRITERION 5 -- the two-sided regression test. The criterion is explicit that this is a PAIR ('a build that re-asserts on every pass is as broken as one that never does'), so the test pins the SEAM, not either side: an agreeing pair still returns no_meaningful_change; a diverging pair still returns a modify; the MES shape (strategy recomputes the journal's own level) is confirmed invisible to interpret_verdict AND decided `reassert` by decide_reassert; an agreeing venue grades `agrees` and does not re-assert. The verdicts are built through grade_protection_price, the shared comparator, rather than hand-rolled dicts -- a hand-built verdict can drift from what the producer actually emits, which is exactly how the pairs-sleeve tests passed for weeks against a table production did not have. tests/test_protection_reassert.py: 37 -> 41.

NOT CLOSING THE ROW. Criteria 1-5 are met in code, but the re-assert is still at PROTECTION_REASSERT_MODE=annotate -- it has DECIDED `reassert` on MES 4350 (live soak row 2026-08-23T12:27:10Z, acted:false, apply_scope:not_allowlisted) and has never moved an order. The row closes when a live row shows acted:true and a follow-up /api/diag/ib_open_orders read shows the resting stop within one tick of the declared level -- which is also BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG's criterion 3.

RESOLVED. All five criteria were met in code earlier today; the row was held open pending a LIVE row showing acted:true and a broker read confirming the move. Both landed at 13:54Z.

RESOLVED — VERIFIED AT THE BROKER 2026-08-23T13:54Z.

Sequence: PROTECTION_REASSERT_ACCOUNTS=ib_paper written with service:none (#10175), then PROTECTION_REASSERT_MODE=apply with a trader restart (#10176, post-restart state active). The very next cadence-gated IB naked sweep acted: soak row 13:54:32Z reads mode=apply, apply_scope=allowlisted, acted=true (the 13:42 and 13:48 rows immediately before it read mode=annotate, apply_scope=not_allowlisted, acted=false — so the flip is what changed the behaviour, not a coincident sweep).

BROKER TRUTH, not our own log: /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper, read_state=orders_read, shows MES STP SELL 15.0 at aux_price 7533.75 under a NEW oca group oca-protect-408, order_id 410. It was 7516.5. |7533.75 - 7533.69642857| = 0.0536 = 0.21 MES ticks, inside the one-tick bar this criterion sets. The 68.79-tick / $1,289.73 divergence that had stood since 2026-08-20 on a healthy monitor and a connected session is closed.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: one position, one venue, one account (ib_paper). The re-assert remains scoped to ib_paper — bybit and alpaca are still not_allowlisted, and widening it is a separate Tier-2 decision that should rest on more than n=1.

The defect this row named — a venue leg that diverges from the journal can NEVER be re-synced by the normal path — is now false: the re-assert owns that reconciliation off the cadence-gated sweep, adding no broker read to the per-pass modify path.

items.opened_by: full-system-audit-2026-08-23 (surfaced by check_backlog_refs while citing it)
items.title: 133 distinct tracking ids are cited across src/tests/scripts/docs/.github and resolve to NO backlog row -- 513 citations, 11.5% of everything cited, including ids CLAUDE.md itself leans on
items.detail:
STARTED as one stray and the sweep made it a class. Surfaced when check_backlog_refs.py failed my own change for citing an ALPACA-REDUCE-HOLD id (2026-06-22) from src/core/coordinator.py:1961.

MEASURED 2026-08-23 (state the population): every /\b(BL|MB|FU|PB|SRQ)-\d{8}-[A-Z0-9-]+\b/ occurrence across src/ tests/ scripts/ docs/ .github/, against the union of ids filed in docs/claude/{health,performance,ml}-review-backlog.json.
    filed ids                    1037
    distinct ids cited           1153
    DANGLING (cited, not filed)   133   = 11.5% of distinct cited
    dangling CITATIONS            513
Heaviest, by citation count (ids described rather than spelled -- see the guard note below): a 2026-07-17 regime-coverage-debt id (45), a 2026-06-15 MGC-naked id (34), two 2026-06-18 SRQ ids (17 each), a 2026-05-15 FU id (13), a 2026-06-22 Alpaca snapshot-falseclose id (13), a 2026-07-06 IB-warmup id (13).

⚠️ SEVERAL ARE CITED BY CLAUDE.md ITSELF, the file every session reads first -- the MGC-naked, orphan-blip, IB-warmup and Alpaca snapshot-falseclose ids all appear there as the provenance for LIVE RUNTIME BEHAVIOUR. A reader who tries to follow one to its record finds nothing. Regenerate the exact list with the grep in the criteria below; it is deliberately not pasted here.

TWO EXPLANATIONS, NOT DISTINGUISHED HERE and I did not check which: (a) the row was never filed, or (b) it was filed and later deleted. (b) is plausible because resolved rows ARE retained in these files with status='resolved' -- so a missing id is not simply 'closed'. Telling them apart needs git history on the three backlog files and is the first task below, because the remedies differ: (a) is a discipline gap, (b) is a deletion policy that destroys provenance.

⚠️ THE LITERAL IDS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT WRITTEN OUT IN FULL WHERE THEY WOULD TRIP THE GUARD, and that is the second finding. check_backlog_refs.py scans added lines and fails on an unresolvable id with no exemption for a row whose SUBJECT is one -- so a finding of this class can only be recorded by not naming it. Verified the hard way: filing this row with the id spelled out failed twice, and the second failure surfaced a THIRD dangling id I had asserted in prose 'DOES resolve' without checking. It does not. That assertion has been removed; it is exactly the RULE ONE failure this repo keeps naming, made while writing a row about traceability.

WHAT THE ORIGINATING ONE CLAIMS TO TRACK IS NOT TRIVIAL: coordinator.py:1960-1990 is the record for a LIVE ORDER-ROUTING decision -- a reduce/close/flip delta on a non-linear/inverse account resolves to HOLD-TO-BRACKET, so no reducing order is sent and the position rides its entry bracket. The comment says operator-approved 2026-06-22 and says it supersedes an earlier hard refusal whose id ALSO dangles. So two unresolvable ids stand in as the provenance for why every Alpaca and IB position stops being actively resized. The behaviour is well-tested (tests/test_intent_delta_dispatch.py:718/782/858); it is the RECORD that is missing.

This is the crack the 2026-07-30 operator directive names. The guard did not catch the 513 because it is DIFF-SCOPED -- it grades ids a change INTRODUCES. It caught mine instantly.

⚠️ DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY MINTING ROWS TO MATCH THE IDS. That manufactures records of decisions nobody witnessed; a fabricated provenance row is worse than a dangling one, which at least announces that it is missing.

MEDIUM, raised from LOW when the sweep landed: nothing is broken at runtime, but 11.5% of the repo's tracking references pointing at nothing makes 'tracked by X' unreliable as a class, and that is the property the directive depends on.
resolution_criteria: Determine which of the 133 were NEVER FILED versus FILED-THEN-DELETED, from git history on the three backlog files. The remedies differ and the split is the finding: never-filed is a discipline gap; filed-then-deleted is a deletion policy that destroys provenance, and resolved rows are otherwise retained, so deletion would be anomalous.

check_backlog_refs.py gains a way to record a finding ABOUT a dangling id. Today it cannot be done -- this row had to omit the ids it is about. Use a VERIFIED escape (the collapsed-state-guard discipline: an annotation naming something that must actually exist), not a presence-only marker, which is how new-table-wiring-guard taught contributors to lie to it.

An `--all` sweep mode reporting the standing population, so the number is watched rather than rediscovered. The guard already has refs_everywhere(); it runs diff-scoped. Reproduce today with: grep -rEoh '\b(BL|MB|FU|PB|SRQ)-[0-9]{8}-[A-Z0-9-]+' src tests scripts docs .github | sort | uniq -c, minus the filed ids.

Decide the policy ONCE and write it down: either dangling ids are a CI failure repo-wide (a migration, since 133 rows would have to be filed or 513 citations corrected first) or they are tolerated outside backlog files and the diff scope is the deliberate line. Today the answer is only inferable from the guard's behaviour.

The CLAUDE.md citations are triaged first regardless of the policy chosen -- it is the file every session reads before acting, so a dangling reference there misleads at the highest leverage point in the repo.

updates.note: ⚠️ RE-CONFIRMED AND I HIT IT TODAY: 133 distinct tracking ids cited across the repo resolve to no backlog row. check_backlog_refs caught the same class on MY diff (a hard-wrapped id reading as a nonexistent one). The 513 pre-existing citations are grandfathered, which is why the guard only fires on new ones.

items.opened_by: full-system-audit-2026-08-23 (found while running the first sweep under the new rule)
items.title: The tune-before-demote gate reads `runtime_logs/strategy_tunes/`, which is GITIGNORED — so a tuning attempt is only 'on record' on the host that ran it
items.detail:
Found the same day the rule shipped, by running the first sweep under it.

`CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md` § 'Tune before demote' makes a demote_shadow/kill verdict soften to `tune` until a tuning attempt is on record, and the evidence is the M8 artifact `runtime_logs/strategy_tunes/<UTC-date>/<strategy>__<param>.json`. **`runtime_logs/` is gitignored** (.gitignore:29). So the artifact is host-local: it does not commit, does not travel, and a sweep run in a sandbox session is invisible to a /performance-review running on the VM or in CI.

VERIFIED, not assumed: `git check-ignore -v` on the artifact returns `.gitignore:29 runtime_logs/`, and `tuning_attempt_on_record` returns True in the session that produced it.

THE FAILURE DIRECTION IS THE SAFE ONE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS MEDIUM AND NOT HIGH. On a host without the directory the reader returns `None` (we could not look), and the override deliberately leaves the matrix verdict STANDING on `None` rather than softening it. So a demotion is never blocked by an attempt the reviewing host cannot see, and nothing fails silently. What is lost is the opposite: a real attempt does not COUNT anywhere but where it ran, so the same sweep may be demanded repeatedly on different hosts.

⚠️ DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY MAKING `None` SOFTEN. That would restore the property the override was built to avoid -- a losing leg stranded live on missing evidence -- and it is the collapsed-state error this repo has a guard family for. The fix is to make the evidence durable, not to weaken the reader.

INTERIM MITIGATION ALREADY IN PLACE for the two legs swept today: the full grids are pasted into docs/research/target-r-derivation-crypto-pullback-2026-08-23.md, a committed document, so the evidence survives even though the artifact does not. That works for a hand-run sweep and does not scale to a fleet.
resolution_criteria: Tune results land somewhere TRACKED, so an attempt counts wherever the review runs. `comms/` is the existing precedent for exactly this shape — comms/gpu_spend_ledger.json and comms/broker_truth_ledger.json are both committed file-backed records read by an API route. A committed index (strategy, param, date, chosen value, beats_baseline, train_oos_consistent) would be small and would version with the config it advises on.

OR: the rule states explicitly that sweeps must be run on the live VM, and the reader's canonical path is the one /api/bot/strategies/{name}/tune serves. That is a documentation fix rather than a code one and is legitimate — but it must be WRITTEN, because today the requirement is only inferable from which host happens to have the file.
Either way, `None` must keep meaning 'we could not look' and must keep leaving the matrix verdict standing. A fix that softens on an unreadable directory is not a fix.
State the population when this closes: how many legs have an attempt on record on the VM, against the 52 enabled. A count of 2 (today, in a sandbox that does not count) is the honest starting number.

updates.note: Re-validated: the tune-before-demote gate reads a GITIGNORED directory, so a tuning attempt exists only on one host. Evidence that cannot be reproduced from the repo — same family as the deleted-dataset rows.

items.opened_by: full-system-audit-2026-08-23 (surfaced by the first fleet-scale tp_r sweep)
items.title: `strategy_tune_sweep` recommended a ready-to-paste Tier-3 config line on a leg that loses money at EVERY tested value -- `beats_baseline` is a relative test and never checked the sign
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-23 on eth_pullback_2h.tp_r. STATE THE POPULATION: ETHUSDT 2h, a 13,212-bar corpus spanning 2023-08-14 to 2026-08-18 fetched via binance_vision; single-split walk-forward with the OOS window 2026-01-01 to 2026-08-18; n = 40 OOS trades on the baseline row; metric is net-of-fee net_total in R at 7.5 bps round-trip, cap pinned 0.099. Over that window every one of the seven grid values was net-NEGATIVE — the full grid is 1.5:-9.40 2:-6.17 2.5:-5.81 3:-6.48 4:-9.90 6:-9.61 50:-9.61 — so the best value (-5.81 R at tp_r 2.5) and the baseline (-9.61 R at tp_r 50) are both losses, and the recommendation read:
    action: propose_value | proposed_value: 2.5 | beats_baseline: true
    yaml_line: config/strategies.yaml::eth_pullback_2h.tp_r : 2.5
A ready-to-paste Tier-3 config line on a leg that loses at every tested value. 'Less bad' rendered as a proposal.

THE PRE-EXISTING CAVEAT DOES NOT COVER IT. `train_oos_consistent` grades CONSISTENCY, not profitability -- a leg can be flagged consistent and still lose at every value, and here it was flagged INconsistent for an unrelated reason, which reads as a different (weaker) complaint than 'this never makes money'.

CLASS: unprovenanced diagnostic, sub-class A. The label names a COMPARISON, a reader maps it to 'is this good?', and nothing in the output reveals the substitution. The repo's sibling sweep already had the concept (`rate_ungradeable_why: base_unprofitable`); this tool did not -- grep for 'unprofitable' in it returned ZERO before the fix.

FIXED SAME SESSION. The recommendation now publishes `chosen_net_total`, `chosen_is_profitable` and `any_grid_value_profitable`, and when NO tested value is profitable the action becomes `no_profitable_value` with an explicit '⛔ NO TESTED VALUE IS PROFITABLE ... beats_baseline here means LESS BAD, not good' caveat. A mixed grid (profitable values exist but the PICK is negative) is a THIRD, distinct case so 'the pick is negative' is never confused with 'the leg is'. `beats_baseline` is deliberately UNCHANGED and still True -- it is not wrong, it is insufficient, so the sign ships beside it rather than instead of it.

VERIFIED by running both branches against the real corpora, not fixtures: XRP (profitable grid) still returns `propose_value` 3.0; ETH (all-negative grid) now returns `no_profitable_value`. Caught mid-build by ruff F821 when the first draft referenced `rows` in a function that never received it -- the same class as an earlier defect this session, which is why the parameter was threaded properly rather than worked around. 10 tests.
resolution_criteria: MET. The recommendation publishes the SIGN (`chosen_net_total`, `chosen_is_profitable`, `any_grid_value_profitable`), not only the relative comparison.
MET. An all-negative grid reports `action: no_profitable_value` rather than `propose_value`, so the output cannot be pasted as a config change without reading past an explicit refusal.
MET. A mixed grid is a distinct third case, so 'the PICK is negative' and 'the LEG is' stay apart.
MET. Both branches exercised against real corpora rather than fixtures, and a clean grid gains NO new caveat -- a warning on every packet is how a signal becomes background noise.

items.title: exit-mechanism-coverage-guard reads config/lever_reachability.json and is not triggered by it — measured COSMETIC today, but it becomes real the moment a step is added
items.detail:
Found by scripts/ci/check_guard_glob_coverage.py, written after CI caught the same shape in exit-coverage-matrix-guard (which joined the M20 matrix against config/strategies.yaml while being scoped only to the matrix, so demoting a leg reported SKIP locally and went red in CI).

THE READ IS REAL: scripts/ops/exit_mechanism_coverage.py:60 resolves config/lever_reachability.json and :152 reads it in _reachability(), which is reachable from main(). The guard's when.globs are config/strategies.yaml, src/units/strategies/*.py, src/runtime/strategy_signal_builders.py and the script itself -- the registry is absent.

BUT IT IS NOT VERDICT-BEARING TODAY, measured rather than assumed. Emptying the file's `levers` list (8 entries -> 0) and re-running BOTH steps the guard actually invokes -- --self-test and --orphans-only -- produced byte-identical output and the same exit code. audit() computes the reachability map and neither step surfaces it. So adding the glob would fire the guard on edits it cannot grade, which is the desensitized-alarm P1 this repo treats as its own failure mode. NOT fixed by adding a glob, deliberately.

NOTE THE FIRST PERTURBATION WAS INERT AND SAID 'UNCHANGED': it cleared `_comment` (a str, so neither the dict nor list branch fired) while the consumer reads data['levers']. A probe that could not have produced a positive returned a clean negative. The measurement above is the re-run against the key actually read.
resolution_criteria: If a step is ever added to exit-mechanism-coverage-guard that SURFACES the reachability verdict (a plain run, or --json), add config/lever_reachability.json to its when.globs in the same change -- at that point the read becomes verdict-bearing and the guard would be scoped to one side of its own join.

Re-run python3 scripts/ci/check_guard_glob_coverage.py after any edit to the guard table; it reuses run_guards.is_relevant rather than re-implementing the matcher, so it cannot drift from the runner's own definition of relevance.
Close by either (a) the glob being added alongside such a step, or (b) a recorded perturbation showing the current steps still do not move -- re-verified, not assumed from this row.

updates.note: Re-validated: measured cosmetic today, structural in kind. Consolidate with BL-20260823-EXIT-COVERAGE-GUARD-CANNOT-SEE-THE-FILE-IT-JOINS-AGAINST.

items.title: The prop screenshot reader sent broker account data (balance, equity, account number, open positions) to Anthropic and Google — and the local backend the operator expected it to use does not exist
items.detail:
OPERATOR, 2026-08-23: 'that flow is supposed to use the local LM that we created for bursts of localized LLM usage. It shouldn't be sent to any outside service, which means that there's some other type of wiring issue here.'

TWO FACTS, both verified rather than assumed, and they do not match that intent.

1. THE EGRESS IS REAL AND UNGUARDED. src/prop/screenshot_parse.py posted the image to Anthropic and, on any failure, to Google (_call_vision_anthropic / _call_vision_gemini). The measured screenshot carried account balance 4869, equity 4867, the broker account number, an open ETHUSD position with entry/TP/SL, and a seven-row trade history. That is LIVE TRADING DATA. The `llm-delegate` skill DOES carry a scope guard — 'public repo code + docs ONLY -- never live trading data, credentials, or account config' -- but it governs the delegate WORKFLOW and has never covered this module, so nothing on this path enforced it.

2. THERE IS NO LOCAL BACKEND TO ROUTE TO. Every mention of a local runner (gguf/llama.cpp/ollama/vllm) in the repo is DOCUMENTATION -- ROADMAP.md, two sprint logs, docs/design/llm-burst-worker-DESIGN.md, docs/architecture/model-inventory.md -- and zero .py files. The design lists it as 'Phase 3: local GGUF backend ... if a privacy driver appears'. The burst worker that DOES exist is itself external (Cerebras/Gemini on an Actions runner), and its own design rejected the Oracle VM as a worker on capacity + wedge-risk grounds. So the operator's expectation describes a system that was designed and not built.

THE PRIVACY DRIVER HAS NOW APPEARED — that is the exact trigger the design names for Phase 3.

SHIPPED NOW (not the full fix): PROP_SCREENSHOT_BACKEND, three states never collapsed -- `local` (DEFAULT; refuses and names the typed-report remedy) / `external` (explicit opt-in to today's behaviour) / `off`. An unparseable value fails CLOSED. `local` and `off` are deliberately distinct: one is 'should work, not built yet', the other 'we chose not to'. A test asserts no hosted provider is called under the default.

⚠️ THIS STOPS THE EGRESS; IT DOES NOT RESTORE THE FEATURE. Until Phase 3 exists the operator types the report, which already works (`bal 5040 5010`, `close ETHUSD 2950 +80 tp`). Flipping to `external` is a deliberate, logged choice.

NOTE ON MY OWN EARLIER ADVICE: I reported the Anthropic 400 as 'out of credit -- operator action, add credits'. That remedy was WRONG. Paying to keep broker screenshots flowing to a third party is the opposite of the correction needed. The billing error was a symptom of a path that should not have been live.
resolution_criteria: THE EGRESS IS CLOSED AND STAYS CLOSED - this half is DONE. PROP_SCREENSHOT_BACKEND defaults to `local`, which refuses; no image reaches a hosted provider from this path. Operator 2026-08-23 WITHDREW the local-backend driver ('perhaps it's not worth pursuing ... we'll not do the screenshots via Telegram. I'll just keep on handing them to you in a cloud chat'), so `local` now means DELIBERATELY NOT SERVED rather than NOT BUILT YET. Do not 'fix' the refusal by changing the default, and do not re-open a local-vision build against this row.

The replacement path is the operator handing the screenshot to a Claude session, which files through the SAME prop_report.ingest_report chokepoint via the prop-report relay - exercised 2026-08-23 as fill id 34. Nothing further is owed on the screenshot axis.

DONE 2026-08-23, measured with a stated denominator. THREE python call sites repo-wide can reach a hosted model: scripts/llm/delegate.py, src/prop/screenshot_parse.py, src/runtime/insights/generator.py. (1) screenshot_parse - WAS sending live account data; now refuses by default. (2) insights/generator - CAN send trade data but is MEASURED in template mode: model_id 'template:v1' on all three live caches read directly from the producer's own stamp, plus 28,808 calls month-to-date at 0 tokens / $0.00 across all four endpoints. Nothing leaves. (3) delegate.py - scope-guarded default-deny to public repo code + docs. Non-python: m20-exit-lever-sweep.yml was a FALSE POSITIVE (a 'Co-Authored-By: ...@anthropic.com' line in a commit message); sync-vm-secrets.yml mirrors secrets and sends no payload; run_insights_cycle.sh / vm_bootstrap.sh only source or write the key. CAVEAT: the usage figure is MONTH-TO-DATE (August); prior months are not measurable from this surface.

DONE 2026-08-23, with a stated denominator: 13 M37 claims were TESTED and 13 HELD. Existence (7): scope_guard.py, delegate.py, oci_inventory.py, the llm-delegate SKILL.md (the discoverability fix), llm-delegate.yml, oci-inventory.yml, comms/cloud/expected_topology.json. Behaviour (6), probed rather than read: the scope guard is genuinely DEFAULT-DENY - 9 hostile probes all refused (config/accounts.yaml, config/strategies.yaml, config/prop_rulesets/breakout.yaml, trade_journal.db, .env, comms/broker_truth_ledger.json, comms/gpu_spend_ledger.json, runtime_logs/outcomes.jsonl, and a ../../etc/passwd traversal); it PERMITS public code+docs (src/*.py, docs/*.md, README.md, scripts/llm/*.py); its size cap REFUSES rather than truncates (order_monitor.py at 497,089 bytes vs MAX_FILE_BYTES=262144 - found while probing, and it is the guard being right, not over-strict, since a truncated file yields confident answers about code the model never saw); the result envelope really is three-state (completed/failed/not_attempted, with not_attempted used for scope refusal, missing key AND missing instruction, so an empty answer cannot read as 'found nothing'); oci_inventory NEVER writes its own baseline (EXPECTED_PATH is only read_text/is_file; --emit-expected prints for a human to review and commit) - which is the claim that a checker rewriting its baseline on drift could never fail; and the burst worker is TEXT-ONLY (zero image/vision/inline_data/base64 across scripts/llm/*.py). ⚠️ WHAT WAS NOT TESTED, stated so this does not read as total: the four GitHub run-id claims (32131324874, 32351336623, 32351503893, 32362843960) were not re-fetched, and the delegate PRECISION figures (17/19 pilot, 20/20 substantive vs 0/20 citations) are historical gradings that cannot be re-derived without re-running the tasks. So: every claim about what EXISTS and how it BEHAVES held; the claims about what was MEASURED on specific past runs are unverified here.

NEW, arising from the audit above, and CORRECTED 2026-08-23 once the key became readable: INSIGHTS_MODEL_MODE is one env var away from sending trade data to a hosted model, and NOTHING WATCHES IT. ⚠️ I first wrote 'template mode is the CODE DEFAULT, not a control' — that overstated the fragility and is retracted. Measured on ict-claude-bridge via the now-allowlisted get-env: `INSIGHTS_MODEL_MODE process='template' declared='template' declared via: env_file`, i.e. it is EXPLICITLY PINNED in /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/.env, not merely falling through to a code default. That is a deliberate declaration and it survives restarts. What STANDS is the rest: a declaration is not a GUARD - nothing alerts if it is changed - so the remedy is unchanged, either alert on a non-template mode or state explicitly that the flip is a deliberate operator action with no guard behind it.

updates.note:
CLAIM HISTORY CHECKED, because the operator said 'several Claude sessions worked on that and told me that it was done'. THE RECORD DOES NOT SHOW THAT, and saying so is worth more than agreeing:

  docs/sprint-logs/S-LLM-BURST-WORKER-2026-08-18.md:132 — 'A local-GGUF backend (design Phase 3) — deferred indefinitely; no privacy driver exists'
  docs/sprint-logs/S-LLM-BURST-WORKER-SCHEDULING-2026-08-20.md:334 — 'Deferred indefinitely, unchanged: the local-GGUF delegate backend (design Phase 3)'
  ROADMAP.md M37 — 'Deferred indefinitely: a local-GGUF backend'

So no session claimed the local model was built. What they shipped and called done is the BURST WORKER, which is real, works, and is EXTERNAL.

BUT THE OPERATOR'S BELIEF HAS A CAUSE, AND IT IS OURS. The design doc's own Problem statement reads: 'We wanted a "local LLM on cloud" the session could start on demand, use, and stop.' That phrase describes ERGONOMICS (cheap, disposable) in words that state a LOCATION. A reader is entitled to conclude inference is local. It is the same sub-class A defect the repo's guards exist to catch — a label naming a property the implementation does not have — in our own design of record. Corrected in place rather than left to be re-read the same way.

AND THE OPERATOR IS RIGHT ABOUT THE DECISION. The deferral rationale was 'NO PRIVACY DRIVER EXISTS' — a claim about the OPERATOR'S REQUIREMENTS, asserted on our own authority, never asked. On that unasked premise the flow was pointed at two hosted providers. 'That was Claude deciding something on his own that he should not have' is an accurate description of what the artifacts show. ROADMAP M37 and the design's Phase 3 line now record the premise as FALSIFIED rather than quietly dropping it.

WHAT REMAINS UNCHECKED, stated so it is not read as clean: I verified the LOCAL-BACKEND claim history only. Whether other completion claims in M37 hold — the burst worker itself, the scope guard, oci-inventory — is NOT established by this note, and the operator's wider concern ('several sessions told me it was done') deserves its own pass over what M37 asserts versus what exists.

PLAN WRITTEN AND TRACKED (operator-directed: "we need to make sure that this is in our work plans ... it doesn't need to be this session, but it needs to be part of what we're working on"). docs/design/local-vision-backend-DESIGN.md + ROADMAP M38.

THE DECISIVE FINDING, and it kills the obvious plan: ROUTING THIS FLOW THROUGH THE EXISTING BURST WORKER IS NOT AVAILABLE AND WOULD BE WORSE THAN WHAT IT REPLACES. Verified 2026-08-23, not assumed: (1) the repo is PUBLIC (`"private": false`, read from the GitHub API), and llm-delegate.yml prints its result envelope TO THE RUN LOG and uploads large outputs as an artifact - both world-readable. So a broker screenshot would be PUBLISHED, not merely transmitted, which is strictly worse than the hosted-API path being fixed. (2) the burst worker is TEXT-ONLY - zero `image|vision|inline_data|base64` matches across scripts/llm/*.py - so there is no vision path to point at even if the transport were acceptable. (3) a self-hosted runner does not rescue it: GitHub's own guidance forbids them on public repos because a fork PR can execute arbitrary code. Therefore llm-burst-worker-DESIGN.md's Phase-3 line ('add a local GGUF backend') is SUPERSEDED for this flow - it is a separate service, on the trainer VM, and the delegate keeps its own scope and its own purpose.

THE CREDITS FRAMING IS RETRACTED EVERYWHERE IT APPEARED, not just here. The operator: "the Anthropic credits are not relevant here at all. We cancel that out." It was removed from PR #10174's body and from the scheduled check-in prompt, and ROADMAP M38 carries an explicit do-not-re-quote marker. Reporting the live `credit balance is too low` 400 as 'operator action, add credits' was wrong in kind, not degree: paying to keep broker screenshots flowing to a third party is not a fix for a path that should not have been live. Billing is not a blocker on this milestone.

WHAT IS STILL UNMEASURED, stated so the plan is not read as settled: trainer private-subnet reachability from the live VM; VLM throughput on 1 Ampere OCPU (NO token/s figure appears anywhere in the design ON PURPOSE - the M37 Cerebras lesson is that a widely-quoted outside number is not evidence about this system); the trainer's own duty cycle against a per-read spawn; and whether any small local VLM can read a dense DXtrade table at all, where the failure mode is a plausible WRONG DIGIT rather than a refusal. P2 explicitly permits the answer 'no local candidate clears the hosted control' - the honest outcome then is that the feature stays typed-report-only, and saying so is a result rather than a failure to try. Deterministic OCR (Tesseract) is kept as a live alternative measured on the same fixtures, not dismissed.

OPERATOR WITHDREW THE DRIVER, same day, after reading the constraint analysis: "perhaps it's not worth pursuing. We should still build it just not for the screenshots ... we'll not do the screenshots via Telegram. I'll just keep on handing them to you in a cloud chat."

SO THE SCREENSHOT USE CASE IS CLOSED, NOT DEFERRED, and the phases in docs/design/local-vision-backend-DESIGN.md are NOT scheduled. The design doc and ROADMAP M38 are re-scoped in place to say so rather than left reading as planned work — a plan nobody intends to execute, left looking active, is the same decay class this backlog exists to prevent.

WHAT THIS COST AND WHAT IT DID NOT: the egress this row was opened for is closed and STAYS closed, and no local model was ever needed to close it. The feasibility study returned 'not worth it' on a measured basis (a public repo whose Actions run logs are world-readable, a text-only worker, zero Ampere headroom, and an accuracy bar set by a $171 balance discrepancy against a $4,700 floor). Withdrawing on that evidence is the correct outcome of a feasibility study, not a failure of one.

WHAT SURVIVES: the operator kept the general intent ('we should still build it, just not for the screenshots'), so the reusable finding is the constraint analysis — above all that the PUBLIC-REPO burst worker cannot carry ANY sensitive payload, because its envelope is printed to a world-readable run log. That is a standing conclusion about llm-delegate, not a screenshot-specific one, and it should be re-read before anyone proposes routing sensitive data through it.

TWO CRITERIA REMAIN OPEN and are NOT touched by the withdrawal: the other hosted-LLM call sites (the M13 insights generator reads trade data), and the audit of M37's other completion claims. The operator's original concern was a PATTERN; only one instance has been established.

PATTERN CRITERION CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT, not by inspection. The operator's concern was that this was a PATTERN rather than one row, so the question was answered empirically and with a denominator.

THE M13 INSIGHTS GENERATOR - the site this row named as the other suspect, because its inputs are trade data - IS NOT SENDING ANYTHING. Confirmed two independent ways rather than one: (a) `model_id: 'template:v1'` on the summary, recent and health caches, which is the PRODUCER'S OWN STAMP of what generated them, and (b) /api/bot/insights/usage reporting 28,808 calls month-to-date at 0 tokens and $0.00 across all four endpoints. (a) is the stronger evidence: cost=0 alone would be an INFERENCE from the price table, whereas the stamp records what actually ran.

METHOD NOTE, because the first probe was wrong and would have produced a confident false negative: /api/bot/insights/usage returned 404 through scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh, which reads as 'the route does not exist'. Probing a KNOWN-GOOD route (api/health) through the same tool returned empty as well - so diag_fetch is scoped to /api/diag/* and the 404 said nothing whatever about this route. The real read went direct to the Caddy host. A negative needs a denominator, including when the negative is your own tooling.

THE RESIDUAL IS REAL AND IS FILED AS A NEW CRITERION: template mode is the CODE DEFAULT, not a guard. INSIGHTS_MODEL_MODE is a single env var away from shipping trade data to Anthropic or Gemini, and nothing alerts if it flips - the same safe-by-code, unwatched shape the screenshot path had, which took an operator complaint to find.

THE OPERATOR'S PATTERN CONCERN, ANSWERED WITH A DENOMINATOR. They said 'several Claude sessions worked on that and told me that it was done', and this row's earlier note established only that no session had claimed the LOCAL MODEL was built. That left the wider question open: do M37's OTHER completion claims hold?

13 CHECKED, 13 HELD. The interesting ones were probed, not read: the scope guard was attacked with 9 hostile paths (live config, the money DB, .env, the prop ruleset, two comms ledgers, a runtime log, and a directory traversal) and refused every one, while still permitting the public code and docs it is supposed to serve.

ONE PROBE 'FAILED' AND THE GUARD WAS RIGHT: src/runtime/order_monitor.py is denied at 497,089 bytes against MAX_FILE_BYTES=262144, 'refused rather than truncated'. My probe expected an allow; the guard's behaviour is better than my expectation, because a silently truncated file is exactly how a delegate produces confident claims about code it never saw. Worth recording that the file it most plausibly needs to review is the one it cannot.

WHAT I COULD NOT TEST is stated on the criterion rather than glossed: the four run-id claims were not re-fetched, and the delegate precision figures are historical gradings not re-derivable without re-running. So the honest summary is: M37's artifacts are real and behave as advertised on every axis testable from the repo; its claims about past MEASUREMENTS remain on trust.

READ SURFACE VERIFIED BY USING IT, which is the half that usually never happens. PR #10182 allowlisted PROP_SCREENSHOT_BACKEND and INSIGHTS_MODEL_MODE; issue #10189 then read them through get-env on ict-claude-bridge (the unit hosting src.bot.claude_bridge — the screenshot parser's actual home; the earlier read was ict-trader-live and would not have covered it). Both keys RESOLVE rather than being refused as un-allowlisted, so the mechanism works.

TWO VALUES, one of which corrects me:
  PROP_SCREENSHOT_BACKEND — process '' / declared '' (UNSET). So the code default applies and the gate is `local`, i.e. REFUSING. That is the intended state after the operator withdrew the driver, and it is now CHECKABLE rather than assumed.
  INSIGHTS_MODEL_MODE — process 'template' / declared 'template' / via env_file. EXPLICITLY PINNED, not a fall-through. My earlier criterion called it 'the CODE DEFAULT, not a control'; that was imprecise and is corrected on the criterion itself.

IT ALSO CROSS-CONFIRMS THE EARLIER FINDING BY A SECOND, INDEPENDENT METHOD. The M13 generator was cleared as template-mode from the consumer side (model_id 'template:v1' on three caches + 28,808 calls at 0 tokens / $0.00). This reads the PRODUCER'S CONFIGURATION and agrees. Two methods that could have disagreed and did not.

⚠️ SECURITY-ADJACENT AND STILL OPEN. Re-validated: the prop screenshot reader sends broker account data (balance, equity, account number, open positions) to hosted models. Pair with BL-20260818-DIAG-READ-TOKEN-PUBLIC-EXPOSURE-UNREMEDIATED (re-confirmed live this review) — two live data-exposure rows, and both need an operator decision rather than a code change.

items.opened_by: full-system-audit-2026-08-23 (found by checking my own freshly-armed code against the broker)
items.tier: 2 (the apply path of a live protective re-arm)
items.title: The re-assert reports applied_ok on a bracket where only the STOP rests — retCode 0 proves the call succeeded, not that both declared legs are at the venue
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-23, one hour after arming PROTECTION_REASSERT_MODE=apply on ib_paper.

The acted soak row (13:54:32Z, MES 4350) carries declared_sl 7533.69642857 AND declared_tp 8390.59025, a reason reading 're-assert BOTH declared levels', result {'retCode': 0, 'result': {'orderId': '410', 'ocaGroup': 'oca-protect-408'}} and applied_ok: true.

THE BROKER DISAGREES ABOUT THE TARGET. /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper (read_state orders_read, 4 orders account-wide) shows for MES exactly ONE leg: STP SELL 15.0 @ 7533.75, oca-protect-408, order 410. There is NO MES limit order anywhere on the account. MGC is the same shape (STP only). MHG is the control that proves the probe sees targets: LMT 7.1415 + STP 6.2215 in one oca group.

THE MECHANISM: place_protective documents that it places 'a stop at sl and a limit at tp, both GTC', and returns an envelope with a SINGLE orderId. So retCode 0 establishes THE CALL SUCCEEDED; it does not establish that both legs rest. The re-assert reads that envelope and stamps applied_ok. Nothing re-reads the venue.

⚠️ WHAT THIS IS NOT: the re-assert did NOT strip a target. BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED already measured both ib_paper positions as target-naked on 2026-08-16 with zero limit orders account-wide. The re-assert inherited that state. The defect is the FALSE COMPLETENESS SIGNAL, not a regression -- and the stop move it made IS real and correct (7516.5 -> 7533.75, 0.21 ticks off declared).

⚠️ IT IS ALSO THE SAME DEFECT ONE LEVEL OVER. BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED is about the DETECTION path grading a stop-only book as covered. This is the REPAIR path reporting a stop-only re-arm as complete. Same one-sidedness, opposite end of the loop, and it reappeared in code written AFTER that row was filed -- by me, today.

CORRECTION TO THE RECORD: I reported to the operator that 'MES 4350 is repaired'. Its STOP is repaired. Its declared take-profit of 8390.59025 does not exist at the venue, and the system said the repair fully succeeded.
resolution_criteria: applied_ok must be established by RE-READING the venue after the call -- both declared legs resting, at the declared prices -- not by retCode. The read already exists (IBClient.protection_coverage returns stop_qty and target_qty separately since 2026-08-16); the re-assert must consume it. Do NOT add a per-pass broker read to the modify path: this runs on the cadence-gated sweep, which already holds the prices.

A stop-only outcome must be its own state, not a success. It is not `agrees`, not a failure, and must never read as applied_ok -- the same three-way discipline the rest of this module uses. Register it with collapsed-state-guard.

Establish WHY the target did not rest before adding a retry: rejected by IB, never transmitted, or refused for distance. A retry loop against an unknown cause is churn on a live bracket. The MHG control shows targets CAN rest on this account.
Re-check the other ib_paper position (MGC) after any fix -- it shows the same stop-only shape, so a fix verified on MES alone is verified at n=1.

updates.note:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND, and it is the PRODUCER — not the re-assert, not the grader.

`IBClient._locked_place_protective` built its legs `[TP, SL]` and set
