`leg.transmit = i == len(legs) - 1`, with a comment describing it as mirroring 'the bracket-transmit discipline in place()'. THAT DISCIPLINE WORKS IN `place()` ONLY BECAUSE ITS CHILDREN CARRY `parentId` (ib_client.py:1377/1386) — IBKR holds them and releases them when the parent transmits. `place_protective` sets NO parentId at all (verified: the only parentId assignments in the file are place()'s), and its own docstring says the OCA group ties the legs 'with no parent'. A PARENTLESS ORDER WITH transmit=False IS HELD BY IBKR AND NEVER RELEASED, because nothing exists to release it.

So the TP — the non-final leg — was constructed, sent, and silently never transmitted, on EVERY bracket this method ever placed. The stop went live alone.

THIS IS THE CAUSE OF BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED. That row measured 'zero limit orders existed account-wide' on ib_paper and correctly fixed the GRADER so a stop-only book stops reading as covered. `place_target_in_group` was then built as a repair wire for the symptom. Nobody asked why the targets were missing, so the producer kept making them.

FIXED: every leg transmits. The stop is now built FIRST, because order became load-bearing the moment both legs go live — they reach IBKR one at a time, and a window with only downside protection is strictly safer than one with only an upside target. The returned orderId is resolved by leg TYPE rather than list position, since it used to be `legs[-1]` and happened to be the stop only because of the old ordering; callers persist it as trades.sl_order_id.

PLANT-PROVEN: re-introducing `i == len(legs) - 1` turns the new guard RED, and restoring the fix turns it GREEN. A guard that cannot be shown to fail is not evidence when it passes.

STILL UNVERIFIED AT THE VENUE: MES 4350 has not been re-asserted since the fix (it is under the 3600s per-(account,symbol) cooldown, and the fix is not deployed yet). The next re-assert on ib_paper is the live check — expect a resting LMT to appear beside the STP in oca-protect-*, and applied_state to read both_legs_resting.

FULLY REMEDIATED ON ib_paper, verified at the broker 2026-08-23T14:32Z.

/api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper (read_state orders_read) now returns SIX orders — every open position holds BOTH legs in one OCA group:
  MES  STP 7533.75 + LMT 8390.50  (oca-protect-408)
  MGC  STP 4371.10 + LMT 4393.00  (oca-protect-389)
  MHG  STP 6.2215  + LMT 7.1415   (308977633, untouched control)
This row's original measurement was 'zero limit orders existed account-wide'. There are now three, and zero target-naked positions.

THE MGC CASE WAS NOT THE MES CASE, and the difference was checked before applying: MGC 4773's target is ALREADY CROSSED (entry 4364.6, stop trailed to 4371.15 above entry, target 4393.02, monitor logging tp_cross every ~30s and deferring on the shut COMEX venue). So its leg is expected to FILL at the 22:00Z reopen rather than rest — which is what the declared geometry intends and what the monitor is already attempting. The orphan-leg hazard place_target_in_group's docstring warns about does not arise, because IBClient.close cancels the bracket at Step 1 before flattening: whichever exit wins, the other leg is cancelled (by OCA on a fill, by close() on a market flatten).

OBSERVATION, not filed as its own defect: BOTH new limit legs carry order_id 6. The ops client's request-id sequence restarts per run, so order_id is NOT unique across clients on this account — IBKR disambiguates by permId. A reader diffing two ib_open_orders snapshots by order_id alone would conflate them. Noted here rather than filed because nothing currently keys on order_id across clients; it becomes a real defect the moment something does.

RESOLVED — fixed, merged and DEPLOYED the same day. order_monitor._reassert_applied_state now RE-READS the venue after the call and returns five states that are never collapsed: call_failed / both_legs_resting / stop_only / no_legs_resting / unverified. The summary counters were split to match (stop_price_reasserted / _incomplete / _unverified / _failed) using summary[k] = int(summary.get(k,0)) + 1, because a KeyError there would have been swallowed by the surrounding broad except and the counter would have silently stopped counting.

⚠️ MY FIRST CUT OF THIS FIX HAD THE SAME DEFECT ONE LEVEL UP — it collapsed `unverified` into `failed` in the summary, i.e. reproduced the exact could-not-look/looked-and-found-nothing merge the row is about. An existing wiring test went red and caught it. Recorded because the near-miss is the useful part.

Shipped in PR #10174, merged 15:37Z, deployed and verified: trader on 188f8292 via /api/diag/status (the WEB-API sha is a different process and does not answer this). The re-assert itself is confirmed running in apply on ib_paper — process 'apply' / declared 'apply' via env_file, so it survives restarts.

items.tier: 1 (fixed in-session — the prompt was rewritten, the class is not fixed)
items.title: A scheduled Routine still carried a repair instruction that had ALREADY been carried out — firing it would have cancelled a correct stop and left a live position naked
items.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-23 while listing timers for an unrelated reason (removing a stale 'add Anthropic credits' framing). Routine trig_014S3NAzMKy2Ac2AM2GgyRE5, armed for 22:30Z, instructed a FRESH standalone session to: 'Cancel the stray stop [MES STP SELL 15 @ 7516.5, oca-protect-336] via cancel-ib-order ... Cancelling makes MES stop-naked, which is a state the system already heals.'

THAT WORK WAS COMPLETED EARLIER THE SAME DAY. Measured at 14:32Z via /api/diag/ib_open_orders: MES 4350 rests STP 7533.75 + LMT 8390.50 in oca-protect-408 — the 68.8-tick stop divergence is FIXED and the target is attached. Firing the Routine as written would have cancelled a CORRECT stop on a live position and relied on a ~300 s naked sweep to put back what was already there.

THE CLASS, which is what makes this worth filing rather than just fixing: a Routine's prompt is a SNAPSHOT OF A VERDICT, and the system it describes keeps moving. Nothing ties the two together — no expiry, no precondition, no re-derivation. This one was written 2026-08-22 against a state that was true then, and stayed armed through the repair that invalidated it. A standalone session has no prior context BY DESIGN, so it cannot notice; it reads a confident instruction naming specific order ids and prices and executes it. That is the same shape as a stale canonical doc read as current (CLAUDE.md's 'field beats comment'), except the reader is a session with write access to a live order path and no way to see the field.

AGGRAVATING: it was scheduled 15 minutes after a SECOND routine (trig_01Rwsb4qoyQTwqSMd9KRjGo6, 22:15Z) covering the same two positions — so two sessions would have acted on one book, which the repo's own coordination rules forbid, arranged by our own scheduling.

FIXED IN-SESSION for this instance only: the prompt was rewritten (update_trigger, keeping run history) into a VERIFY-ONLY routine that opens by naming its own previous instructions as obsolete and harmful, states the measured 14:32Z state, and says to act only on what THIS run measures. The safety intent ('do not leave any position with no stop') is preserved. The CLASS is untouched. 

=== SECOND INSTANCE, 2026-09-10, AND IT WIDENS THE CLASS: n=1 -> n=2, and the carrier this time was NOT an operator-armed Routine but a SESSION'S OWN send_later CHECK-IN. A manager scheduled a check-in at 00:39Z to fire ~24 minutes later and merge its lease-heartbeat PR. By the time it fired at 01:03:56Z, ALL FOUR of its instructions were stale: (1) merge #11622 - already merged as 2832abf10; (2) merge #11615 - already merged as 2ee21f4e5; (3) close #11579 per MI-222's needs_action - closed at 2026-09-09T19:41:11Z, five hours before the check-in was even written; (4) 'the operator has not yet answered DEC-20260909-STRATEGY-REVIEW-WINDOW-FLOOR, which blocks Lane 3' - FALSE, that decision was SUPERSEDED by DEC-20260909-STRATEGY-LEG-OFFLINE-EDGE-BASIS and the operator answered it on 2026-09-09 (chosen: build_producer), which is what spawned MI-216/217/218. 

!! ITEM (4) IS THE HARMFUL ONE AND IT IS A DIFFERENT HARM FROM 2026-08-23'S. There the stale instruction would have cancelled a correct stop on a live position. Here it would have put an ALREADY-ANSWERED question back to the operator as though it were still open - spending the operator's attention on a decision they had already made, and doing it through the exact channel (decisions-as-popups) whose value depends on every question in it being live. A channel that re-asks answered questions is trained away as surely as an alarm that fires on correct behaviour. 

!! IT CONFIRMS THIS ROW'S SHARPEST CRITERION EXPERIMENTALLY. The resolution_criteria say 'Re-verify before acting as prose is not sufficient ... The concrete instruction wins over the general caution every time.' The 01:03Z check-in opened with 'Auto-merge is armed, so it may already be merged: check first, do not re-push' and 'READ mergeable_state BEFORE the check runs' - the general caution, written by the same session, in the same message, ABOVE four concrete stale instructions. The caution did not prevent the staleness; reading the primary sources did. 

!! AND IT NARROWS WHAT A FIX MUST COVER. This row's second criterion asks for an audit of armed ROUTINES carrying mutating instructions. That denominator is now too small: a session's own send_later is the same mechanism with the same decay and no operator ever sees it, so any survey that counts only operator-armed Routines will report a clean population while this class keeps firing. The manager caught this one only because it had spent the preceding hour being wrong about a different stale-fact class and was checking primary sources by reflex - which is not a mechanism and must not be recorded as one.
resolution_criteria: A convention that makes a Routine's staleness VISIBLE to the session that fires it — e.g. every action-carrying prompt states the timestamp + the exact read its verdict came from, and REQUIRES the session to re-derive that read and compare BEFORE acting, refusing when they disagree rather than proceeding on the prompt. 'Re-verify before acting' as prose is not sufficient: this Routine already said 'Re-verify before acting; do not inherit the verdicts' in its own text, four lines above an instruction that named a specific order id to cancel. The concrete instruction wins over the general caution every time.

An audit of every currently-armed Routine for the same shape: does it instruct a MUTATION on state that may already have changed? State a denominator - how many Routines are armed, how many carry a mutating instruction, how many of those pin a re-derivable precondition. This row establishes n=1 found while looking for something else, which is not a survey.

A rule against arming two Routines that touch the same positions inside one another's plausible run window, or an explicit coordination-board check as step 0 of any such prompt (the rewritten one now carries the latter).

updates.note: Re-validated: a Routine carrying an already-executed repair instruction would, on firing, cancel a leg that is now correct. Live relevance — ib_paper MES is currently correctly bracketed, so a stale repair Routine firing now would BREAK it.

items.tier: 2 (fix shipped in #10174; the CONTAMINATION it leaves in the evidence base is unmeasured)
items.area: execution / ib / exit geometry / evidence integrity
items.title: On IB, moving a stop re-minted the whole bracket through the un-transmitted path — so a trade LOST ITS TAKE-PROFIT the moment it started trailing, and no IB winner could ever reach its target
items.detail:
SCOPE CORRECTION, TWICE, AND THE SECOND ONE IS THE IMPORTANT ONE. I first told the operator 'every IB bracket ever placed was stop-only' (too broad), then corrected it to 'only the naked-autoprotect re-arm path' (too narrow). Read from the code, the truth is worse than the narrow version and more specific than the broad one.

THE TWO PATHS. `IBClient.place()` — the ENTRY bracket — is FINE: children are linked by `parentId`, so transmit-on-the-last-leg works as designed. `IBClient.place_protective()` mints a PARENTLESS OCA pair, where `transmit=False` on a leg means HELD BY IBKR FOREVER. That was the bug (`_locked_place_protective` set transmit only on the final leg).

WHAT MAKES IT SYSTEMATIC RATHER THAN RARE: `IBClient.modify_protective` — the routine SL/TP adjust — is implemented as a re-arm THROUGH `place_protective`. Its own docstring says so: 'a SL/TP modify is a re-arm: cancel the resting protective legs for symbol, then place a fresh OCA pair at the supplied levels via place_protective', and 'Reusing place_protective keeps the leg shape (GTC OCA, reverse side, whole-contract qty, TRANSMIT-ON-LAST) byte-identical'. That last phrase names the defect as a feature being preserved. `modify_protective` is reached from `execute.modify_open_order` (execute.py:2364), which is the MONITOR'S STOP-TRAIL WIRE.

SO: EVERY TIME A MONITOR MOVED A STOP ON AN IB POSITION, THE BRACKET WAS RE-MINTED AND THE TAKE-PROFIT WAS HELD, NEVER TRANSMITTED. On a trailing strategy that is not an edge case, it is the normal lifecycle of any trade that WORKED. The corollary is the part that matters for money and for evidence: on IB, a winning trade could not reach its take-profit, because the target was removed at the moment the trade started going its way.

WHY NOBODY CAUGHT IT: the call site is CORRECT. `modify_open_order` deliberately passes BOTH the changed leg and the current value of the unchanged one 'so neither stop nor target is dropped'. The target was supplied, accepted, and then held at the wire. Every component is individually right; the defect lives at the seam — the same shape as the exit_price_source leak.

LIVE CONTROL, read 2026-08-23T15:16Z from /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper (6 orders, read_state=orders_read). It is a controlled comparison sitting in the live book:
  MHG 29 long — oca_group '308977633' (a bare IB-assigned id, i.e. the place() ENTRY bracket) — holds BOTH a LMT 7.1415 and a STP 6.2215. Its stop was never trailed, so it never went through modify_protective. THE CONTROL, and the only position that kept its target.
  MES 15 long — oca_group 'oca-protect-408' — and MGC 95 long — 'oca-protect-389'. Both `place_protective`-minted, both STOP-ONLY until they were repaired by hand today.
Note the group naming is itself the forensic marker: `oca_key` supplied yields 'oca-protect-t<trade_id>'; absent it falls back to 'oca-protect-<reqId>'. Both live groups are the FALLBACK form (no 't'), so neither came from the naked sweep.

THE FIX SHIPPED IN #10174 COVERS THIS PATH TOO (every leg now transmits, and modify_protective routes through the same function), so its blast radius is larger and more valuable than the PR body claims. ⚠️ IT IS STILL UNEXERCISED — both targets restored today went on retroactively via `place_target_in_group`, a DIFFERENT method that always transmitted correctly.
resolution_criteria: ANSWERED 2026-08-23, and the answer is NO: the contaminated population is NOT reconstructible from the journal. Tested, not assumed — all four candidate anchors were checked and each fails for a specific reason: (1) `trades.stop_loss` is OVERWRITTEN IN PLACE by order_monitor._apply_update's `db.update_trade(trade_id, trade_sync)`; (2) `order_packages.sl` is overwritten in place by the same path's `db.update_order_package(pkg_id, updates)`; (3) the append-only `signals` dual-write records decision CONTEXT (event, timeframe, regime, adx_14, pattern, confidence, price) but carries NO protective geometry — verified against live MES rows, meta is `{event, timeframe, regime, adx_14, regime_source}`; (4) `position_telemetry` is UPSERT-on-order_package_id and its `rToStop` is derived from the CURRENT stop, so it holds no trajectory either, and it covers only donchian/pullback legs. There is no entry-time stop anywhere that survives the first trail. So do NOT report a number for the historical population — there is none to report, and a partial count would be worse than the honest 'unknown'.

GOING FORWARD IS THE ONLY MEASURABLE DIRECTION, and it needs one small write: stamp the trade when its protective bracket is re-armed or amended (a counter and/or first/last timestamp on the row). That is Tier-2 (a write on the trader path) so it is PROPOSED here, not shipped. Without it the same question will be equally unanswerable next time — and note the re-arm currently writes NOTHING durable at all: _attempt_naked_autoprotect returns a bool and logs only on FAILURE.

⚠️ THE RE-ARM LEAVES NO DURABLE RECORD, which is a defect in its own right: `_attempt_naked_autoprotect` returns a bool and logs ONLY on failure - no journal write, no soak row, no outcome emit - and `modify_protective` likewise stamps nothing on the trade. So a repair that mutates a live position's protective bracket is invisible afterwards. Propose stamping the trade (Tier-2, a write on the trader path) so the population is measurable GOING FORWARD even if the history is lost.

The exit-geometry / exit-head research must not calibrate on IB live exit outcomes until this is quantified: for a contaminated trade 'the target was never hit' describes a mechanism that had been removed. Carried into docs/research/EXIT-GEOMETRY-REBUILD-SESSION-PROMPT.md as a blocking caveat.

PROVE THE FIX ON A NEW BRACKET: a bracket born AFTER the deploy must carry BOTH a STP and a LMT in one OCA group (/api/diag/ib_open_orders). Until then report it as 'deployed but NOT YET EXERCISED' - an unexercised fix and a working one look identical.

TRADE-REVIEW CHECK (added 2026-08-24, operator-directed standing watch) — the order-book check alone is NOT sufficient and MGC 4773 proves it: both legs rested, the target was 233.9 pts in the money, and the close still came from the monitor via `tp_cross`. Resolution additionally requires at least one IB close where the ATTACHED TARGET demonstrably acted (exit at/through the declared take-profit with a non-monitor `exit_reason`), with the population stated (n IB closes examined, split across target-acted / monitor-closed-while-LMT-rested / stop-closed-uninformative / none-closed). A `tp_cross` close while a LMT rested at or better than the exit price REOPENS this row rather than draining it.

updates.note:
TESTED THE 'MAY NOT BE RECONSTRUCTIBLE' CLAIM RATHER THAN LEAVING IT STANDING, because the exit-geometry thread needs the number and 'probably not' is not an answer it can plan around.

IT IS NOT RECONSTRUCTIBLE. Four candidate anchors, each ruled out for a stated reason (see criterion 1). The decisive one is that BOTH sides of the journal are overwritten by the SAME code path: `_apply_update` writes `trades.stop_loss` via `update_trade` and `order_packages.sl` via `update_order_package`, so a trailed stop erases the level it replaced on both records. The `signals` dual-write is append-only and WOULD have served, but it does not record protective geometry — checked against live MES rows rather than inferred from the schema.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE EXIT-GEOMETRY THREAD: it must NOT wait for this number, and must not quote a partial one. The correct posture is the one already written into the session prompt — treat IB live exit outcomes as contaminated by an unquantified amount and do not calibrate on them. A count derived from, say, 'packages whose updated_at differs from created_at' would be an UPPER BOUND over all update reasons, not a measure of this defect, and publishing it as the latter is exactly the unprovenanced-diagnostic class this repo guards against.

THE FORWARD FIX IS CHEAP AND IS NOW A SEPARATE CRITERION. One stamp on the trade at re-arm/amend time makes the question answerable next time. Tier-2, so proposed rather than shipped.

CRITERION 5 IS MET — and by the strongest evidence available, the bracket OBSERVED AT MINT on the exact path this row names as the systematic cause.

Criterion 5 asks for 'a bracket born AFTER the deploy carrying BOTH a STP and a LMT in one OCA group'. At 2026-08-25T14:52:34Z the ict-trader-live journal shows mhg_pullback_1d produce a trailing verdict {'sl': 6.25507143}, execute.modify_open_order route it into modify_protective -> place_protective (the MONITOR'S STOP-TRAIL WIRE this row identifies), and place BOTH legs:
  placeOrder: StopOrder(orderId=441, auxPrice=6.255,  ocaGroup='oca-protect-440')
  placeOrder: LimitOrder(orderId=442, lmtPrice=7.1415, ocaGroup='oca-protect-440')
  modify_open_order -> IB re-arm OK  {'ocaGroup': 'oca-protect-440', 'legs_placed': 2}
and /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper at 14:56:17Z (read_state 'orders_read') shows both RESTING: 441 STP PreSubmitted and 442 LMT Submitted. Note the group name is the FALLBACK form 'oca-protect-<reqId>', this row's own forensic marker for a place_protective mint rather than the naked sweep or the place() entry path. So this is not merely a post-deploy bracket — it is a bracket minted by a stop TRAIL, the operation that used to strip the target, and the target transmitted.

CRITERION 6 IS NOT MET AND THIS ROW DOES NOT DRAIN. State the population: /api/bot/trades/closed?limit=200&include_paper=true&account_id=ib_paper returns 16 rows for the account's entire life (16 << 200, so not truncated), and EXACTLY ONE closed on or after the 2026-08-23 deploy — MGC 4773 at 2026-08-23T22:00:32Z, which is the very close this row already records as the counter-example (both legs resting, target 233.9 pts in the money, closed by the monitor anyway). So the split criterion 6 asks for is: target-acted 0 / monitor-closed-while-LMT-rested 1 / stop-closed-uninformative 0 / none-closed 0, over n=1. n=1 is not a measurement, and the one observation is the negative one. The order-book half is settled; the TRADE half is not, and the standing watch continues.

INTERACTION WITH TODAY'S #10282, worth recording because it changes the rate at which criterion 6 can be satisfied. place_protective now REFUSES to arm when the pre-cancel verifiably failed (BL-20260825-PLACE-PROTECTIVE-COUNTS-THE-CANCEL-CALL-NOT-ITS-EFFECT). On a symbol carrying legs owned by a retired clientId — ib_paper/MHG today — a trailing amend will now place NOTHING rather than mint a fresh group. That is the safer of the three behaviours on offer (old: drop the target; yesterday's: add a disjoint group; now: keep the bracket that is already there), but it means MHG mints no further post-deploy brackets until group 416 is cleared from TWS, so evidence for criterion 6 will come from MES/MGC or from MHG after that repair.

CORRECTION TO THE UPDATE ABOVE, AND IT IS STALE IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION. That update was written from the REFUSE variant of #10282, which the operator superseded before merge. The merged behaviour JOINS.

Read from the code, not the PR narrative — src/units/accounts/ib_client.py:1640 `join_group, group_count = self._select_join_group(still_resting)` then :1643 'place_protective: %d %s leg(s) survived the pre-cancel (owned by a retired clientId); JOINING their OCA group'. So on a symbol carrying legs owned by a retired clientId, a trailing amend still PLACES — into the survivors' existing group — instead of minting an (N+1)th one. Refusal is not the shipped behaviour.

WHAT THAT INVALIDATES, explicitly, because a session would otherwise plan around it: the sentence 'MHG mints no further post-deploy brackets until group 416 is cleared from TWS, so evidence for criterion 6 will come from MES/MGC or from MHG after that repair' is FALSE. MHG keeps trailing, so it remains a criterion-6 evidence source. Group 416 is also gone — the live MHG groups are 446 and 465.

LIVE READ 2026-08-25 (/api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper, read_state 'orders_read', 8 orders), which independently corroborates criterion 5 on a SECOND bracket:
  MHG oca-protect-446  STP oid 447 aux 6.2625  + LMT oid 448 lmt 7.1415 Submitted  (client 597)
  MHG oca-protect-465  STP oid 466 aux 6.312   + LMT oid 467 lmt 7.1415 Submitted  (client 497)
Trade 4796 (mhg_pullback_1d, 29 long) declares stop_loss 6.31207143 / take_profit_1 7.141302, so 465 is the current journal-matching bracket and 446 is the stranded predecessor. BOTH carry a transmitted target.

A FORENSIC MARKER WORTH RECORDING, because it reads a hand-repair off the order book with no journal access: a NATIVE place_protective mint is CONSECUTIVE from its own group reqId (446 -> 447/448, 465 -> 466/467) and on the trader's clientId. A retrofit is not — MES oca-protect-408 carries STP oid 410 on client 497 beside LMT oid 6.0 on client 9917, an out-of-band id on an ops session, i.e. the place_target_in_group repair this row already records. Id-contiguity + clientId separates 'the transmit fix worked' from 'a human put the target back', which is the exact confusion criterion 5 has to avoid.

NEW, FORWARD-LOOKING, AND IT IS THE JOIN'S FIRST REAL TEST ON A DIFFERENT SYMBOL: MGC trade 5007's ENTIRE bracket is owned by clientId 597 (orders 422 LMT / 423 STP, group '834864174' — the bare IB-assigned form, so a place() ENTRY bracket) while the live session is 497. So the first MGC trail will hit Error 10147 on the pre-cancel exactly as MHG did, and post-#10282 it should JOIN '834864174' rather than mint a second group. Nothing needs doing about it — it is stated so the outcome is falsifiable in advance.

PREDICTION FOR MHG, stated precisely so it can be refuted. Next mhg_pullback_1d trail: the pre-cancel cancels 466/467 (client 497, cancellable) and is REFUSED on 447/448 (client 597), so still_resting = {oca-protect-446: stop 29, legs 2}, verify_state='verified', and _select_join_group returns ('oca-protect-446', 1) — its key is (-stop_qty, -leg_count, name), and with a single surviving group there is no tie to break. Expect group COUNT 2 -> 1, with 446 growing to 4 legs. Over-cover stays 58-vs-29 but WITHIN one group, which is self-limiting (a fill cancels its siblings) and is deliberately not paged. A THIRD group appearing instead means the join is not firing and this must be reported, not re-explained.

CRITERION 6 IS STILL NOT MET and this row still does not drain — nothing above is a TRADE close. The population is unchanged at n=1 (MGC 4773, the negative one).

updates: 2026-08-26 — THE ORDER-BOOK HALF OF 'PROVE THE FIX ON A NEW BRACKET' IS NOW MET. THE ROW STAYS OPEN because the 2026-08-24 trade-review half is not. Measured on ib_paper from FRESH-CLIENT reads (issues #10313/#10315/#10318/#10319), deliberately NOT /api/diag/ib_open_orders, which was shown stale the same day (BL-20260826-DIAG-IB-OPEN-ORDERS-SERVES-A-STALE-MONOTONIC-ORDER-VIEW) and which inflated a measurement in this very session. Population: 3 open ib_paper positions, 8 resting orders, all 8 accounted for. THE EVIDENCE: MHG trade 4796 carries `oca-protect-t4796` holding BOTH a STP (486, 29 @ 6.3525) AND a LMT (487, 29 @ 7.1415) in ONE OCA group. The group name is the KEYED form, which per ib_client.py:1750 is produced only by place_protective when an oca_key is supplied - the path threaded in this session - so this bracket was minted AFTER the deploy by the very method the row names, and it transmitted both legs. That is the controlled positive this row asked for, and it is distinguishable from the 2026-08-23 repairs, which went on via place_target_in_group and would NOT produce a keyed group name. EVERY POSITION NOW HAS A RESTING TARGET, so the 'zero limit orders account-wide' state recorded in BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED no longer holds: MES 4350 (15 long) oca-protect-408 STP 410 15 @ 7533.75 + LMT 6; MGC 5007 (51 short) group 834864174 STP 423 51 @ 4699.9 + LMT 422; MHG 4796 as above plus the stale second group 465. TWO STOP DIVERGENCES ALSO READ CLEAN AT THE TICK: MES declares 7533.69642857 against a resting 7533.75 (tick 0.25) and MGC declares 4699.87285714 against 4699.9 (tick 0.1). The MES figure is the one BL-20260823-MODIFY-IDEMPOTENCE-COMPARES-INTENT-TO-JOURNAL-NEVER-TO-VENUE recorded as 7516.50 - a 69-tick, $1,289.73 gap - so that divergence has since closed on the live book. WHAT IS STILL NOT SHOWN, and it is the half that matters most: no IB close in which the ATTACHED TARGET demonstrably acted. An order-book read cannot show that, and MGC 4773 is the standing proof it must not be inferred - both legs rested, the target was 233.9 pts in the money, and the close still came from the monitor via tp_cross. So this remains DEPLOYED AND HALF-EXERCISED, not resolved.

updates.note: CRITICAL. Re-validated and it remains this review's headline UNEXERCISED fix. The window finally produced two IB closes (MHG 4796, MGC 5007) where the prior review had zero, and 5007 DID trail its stop and exit sl_cross at +$3,417 — but OCA cancels the sibling target on a stop fill either way, so a stop exit cannot demonstrate the target survived the trail. Today's live book (STP 7533.75 + LMT 8390.50 in ONE OCA group, qty 15 = position 15, matching the journal to the tick) is the strongest circumstantial evidence yet and is still not the mechanism. Settles only on an IB trade that trails and then exits on its TARGET.

progress.note:
⚠️ THE EXISTING 'PROVE IT ON A NEW BRACKET' CRITERION IS NECESSARY BUT **NOT SUFFICIENT** — established by evidence tonight, and this is the standing-watch note the operator asked for.

MGC 4773 (ib_paper) closed at the 2026-08-23T22:00Z COMEX reopen with **BOTH legs resting** in one OCA group (STP 4371.10 order 391 + LMT 4393.00 order 6) and the target **233.9 points in the money**. It still closed via `exit_reason = tp_cross` — THE MONITOR — and the LMT did not fill. So a bracket can carry both legs, be deeply in the money, and the attached target still never acts. 'Both legs rest' proves the legs were PLACED; it does not prove the target is LIVE at the venue.

**THE WATCH, going forward — review TRADES, not just order books.** For every IB trade closing after the #10174 deploy, ask: *should the attached target have fired, and did it?* Classify each close:
  - `exit_price` at/through the declared take-profit AND `exit_reason` is NOT a monitor reason ⇒ the attached LMT acted. **This is the only outcome that proves the fix.**
  - `exit_reason = tp_cross` (or any monitor close) while a LMT was resting at or better than the exit ⇒ **THE TARGET WAS INERT.** The fix did not take on that trade, or took and the leg is still held at the wire. This is the MGC 4773 shape and it is the finding to escalate.
  - `exit_reason` is a stop/SL reason ⇒ tells us nothing either way; exclude from the denominator rather than counting it as a pass.
  - no IB trade closed in the window ⇒ **`unexercised`**, which is NOT a pass. State it as such.

STATE THE POPULATION EVERY TIME: report `n` IB closes examined and how many fell in each bucket. A single monitor-close is enough to reopen this; a run of zero closes is not evidence of anything.

**DATING PROBLEM, recorded because it bounds what the order-book check can do:** `/api/diag/ib_open_orders` returns no placement timestamp, so the two brackets resting right now (MES `oca-protect-408` STP 410 / LMT 6; MHG `308977633` STP 399 / LMT 398) **cannot be shown from that surface to postdate the deploy**. MES's LMT carries order id 6 — the same low-id shape as MGC's retroactively-attached target — which is suggestive of `attach-ib-target` (a DIFFERENT method that always transmitted correctly) rather than of `_locked_place_protective`. Suggestive, not established. Do not count either as evidence for the fix.

**STATUS AS OF THIS NOTE: `#10174` IS DEPLOYED AND NOT YET EXERCISED.** Both of 2026-08-23's targets were attached retroactively via `attach-ib-target`; no bracket has been observed born through the fixed path. An unexercised fix and a working one look identical, so it must not be reported as working until a close lands in the first bucket above.

items.tier: 1 (a read surface; the remedy is a distinguishable state, not a value change)
items.title: `daily_loss_used_usd: 0.0` means BOTH 'no loss today' and 'today's loss was never measured' — and the second is what it meant on a day that lost $107
items.detail:
MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-23T16:10Z on /api/bot/prop/status?account_id=breakout_1, immediately after ingesting a real closed trade (fill 35: ETHUSD long 2.0, 2453.56 -> 2402.00, net -107.02) and the operator's balance snapshot:

    day_pnl                     : 0.0
    daily_loss_used_usd         : 0.0
    distance_to_daily_loss_usd  : 142.92
    fills_applied_since_snapshot: 0
    balance_basis               : snapshot
    status_freshness            : ok

EVERY ONE OF THOSE IS CORRECT AND THE PANEL STILL MISLEADS. The account lost $107.02 today. It does not appear in `daily_loss_used_usd` because the operator's snapshot was taken AFTER the close, so the loss is already baked into the 4764 balance rather than counted as usage, and `fills_applied_since_snapshot` is legitimately 0. Without `day_start_balance` — which the terminal does not display, so it was correctly OMITTED under the honest-null contract — nothing can reconstruct what today started at.

SO `distance_to_daily_loss_usd: 142.92` IS NOT A CUSHION. It is 'the full daily limit, because we do not know what today already used'. A reader sizing the next trade against it would believe they have $142.92 of daily room on a day that has already spent $107.02 of a $142.92 limit — i.e. roughly $36 left, not $143. The error runs in the DANGEROUS direction: it overstates room.

THIS IS THE COLLAPSED-STATE CLASS, on the safety panel of an account-killer limit. `docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md` § 'Collapsed states': ask whether 'we did not look' and 'we looked and found nothing' are distinguishable. Here they are NOT — a measured zero and an unmeasured zero print identically. The sibling axis on this very endpoint got this right: `status_freshness` is four-state (`ok`/`stale`/`absent`/`unchecked`) precisely so a full-looking cushion cannot be read off a snapshot nobody can date. The DAILY axis has no equivalent.

A careful reader CAN infer it from `fills_applied_since_snapshot: 0` plus an absent `day_start_balance`, but that is a derivation across three fields to discover that a fourth is meaningless — which is exactly what a state label exists to prevent.
resolution_criteria: `/api/bot/prop/status` gains a `daily_basis` (or equivalent) that is never collapsed, mirroring `status_freshness`'s vocabulary: `measured` (a day_start_balance is known and day_pnl is computed from it) / `fills_only` (no day_start_balance; day_pnl reflects only fills reported since the snapshot, so it is a LOWER BOUND) / `unmeasured` (neither available - we did not look). `distance_to_daily_loss_usd` must be readable as untrustworthy without deriving it from three other fields.

When the basis is not `measured`, the daily distance is still RETURNED (discarding the last known figure helps nobody, per the same rule that keeps stale rule_distance values) but the caveat travels INSIDE rule_distance as well as on the envelope - the pattern status_freshness already uses, so a consumer reading only the panel cannot miss it.
Register the new field with collapsed-state-guard so the producer must emit every state and a real consumer must branch on each.
Consumers updated: the dashboard Prop tab rule-distance panel must not render a `fills_only`/`unmeasured` daily distance the same way it renders a measured one.

updates.note: RE-CONFIRMED AND THE FIX HELD IN THE HONEST DIRECTION: today's /api/bot/prop/status returns daily_loss_used_usd **null**, not 0.0, with day_pnl_state `realized_unreported`. So the collapse this row describes ('0.0 means both no-loss and never-measured') is NOT present in the current payload — the null is correct. Keeping open only because I verified one payload in one state; the row should be closed by whoever confirms the 0.0 path is gone in code.

items.tier: 2 (an env change on the live trader; the DISPOSITION is the operator's)
items.title: alpaca_live is on BOTH alert skip-lists at once — the one account measured refusing 120 orders is the one account nothing watches
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-23 from a get-env ALL read of ict-trader-live (issue #10181), while verifying an unrelated key. Both values are declared in the env_file, so they survive every restart:
    ACCOUNT_DOWN_ALERT_SKIP = 'alpaca_live'
    SILENT_REFUSAL_SKIP     = 'alpaca_live'

THE TWO ALERTS EXIST TO COVER DIFFERENT HALVES OF ONE FAILURE, AND alpaca_live IS EXEMPT FROM BOTH. `account_reachability_alert` answers 'is this account reachable' (it probes positions()). `silent_refusal_alert` was built SPECIFICALLY because that probe misses an account whose positions() answers while balance() returns None — an account that reads UP while refusing every signal routed to it (BL-20260814-REACHABILITY-PROBES-POSITIONS-NOT-BALANCE). CLAUDE.md states the motivating measurement outright: 'measured on the live journal 2026-08-14, alpaca_live produced 120 refusals across 16 separate days at 3-5/hr and nothing alerted once'.

So the account that motivated building the second detector is skipped by the second detector — AND by the first. Between them there is now no path by which alpaca_live's silence or refusal reaches an operator.

⚠️ THIS MAY WELL BE DELIBERATE AND STILL BE WRONG. CLAUDE.md documents ACCOUNT_DOWN_ALERT_SKIP as the 'escape hatch for a live account intentionally expected-down', which is a legitimate use. But SILENT_REFUSAL_SKIP is a different question with a different answer: 'we know it is down' does not imply 'we do not want to know when it starts refusing for a NEW cause'. The silent-refusal latch is keyed per (account, cause) precisely so a new cause is not swallowed by an old one — and a blanket skip defeats exactly that design. Suppressing the alarm is a reasonable response to noise; suppressing BOTH alarms is indistinguishable from not monitoring the account, and nothing in the config records which was intended.

NOT CHANGED IN-SESSION: removing a skip re-arms a live alert path and the operator may have suppressed these on purpose. This row asks the question rather than answering it.
resolution_criteria: Operator decides, per detector rather than per account: is alpaca_live expected-down (ACCOUNT_DOWN_ALERT_SKIP legitimate), and separately, do we want to know if it starts REFUSING for a new cause (SILENT_REFUSAL_SKIP)? These are different questions and the current config answers both with 'no' without recording that either was decided.

If both skips stay, record WHY in the env file or CLAUDE.md, with a date and a re-check trigger - an undocumented double-suppression is indistinguishable from an account nobody is monitoring, which is the state this pair of alerts was built to make impossible.

DONE 2026-08-23 — and the number reframes the whole row. Measured over the COMPLETE population (318 rows of 318 total for account_id='alpaca_live'; filter_state='applied', page == total, nothing truncated; span 2026-06-25 -> 2026-08-21): **317 of 318 orders refused = 99.7%. Exactly ONE trade ever closed.** Causes parsed from notes.reason: 134 zero_balance (gate_balance=0.00), ~90 risk_refused with sized_qty=0 against a balance of ~$150, 20 `balance() returned None`, 8 account_mode_dry_run. So this is NOT a refusal RATE to tune — the account is funded at roughly $150 while the 15 strategies routed to it trade ETFs (SPY/TLT/QQQ/GLD/SLV/USO/GDX/IAUM) it cannot buy a single WHOLE share of, and Alpaca rejects fractional shares. Every component behaves as designed; the configuration is the defect. Escalated to its own row: BL-20260823-ALPACA-LIVE-CANNOT-PLACE-AN-ORDER-AT-ITS-FUNDING-LEVEL (critical, Tier-3).

⚠️ ESCALATED 2026-09-01 — THE BLAST RADIUS CHANGED AND THIS ROW IS STILL OPEN. When this was filed the account was mode: dry_run and could not place an order at its funding level, which is what made the double-suppression defensible. As of 2026-08-31T22:43Z alpaca_live is mode: live with tlt_pullback_1h routed and REAL MONEY at stake (PR #10633), and SILENT_REFUSAL_SKIP is STILL 'alpaca_live' — verified on /proc/<MainPID>/environ via get-env issue #10661 at 2026-09-01T14:21Z, process and declared agreeing. So the one account that just started trading real money is the one account whose refusal detector is off. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, not inferred: its silent_refusal_alert latch reads alerting:true, cause:risk_refused, verdict:signalled_never_placed with updated_at FROZEN at 2026-08-21T12:38:38Z while __last_check__ advanced to 2026-09-01T13:43:07Z — ELEVEN DAYS. The quiet-release branch built for exactly this case (silent_refusal_alert.py, 'is no longer flagged: it produced NO order rows at all') IS on main and deployed, and cannot fire because its loop does `continue` on `aid in skip`. TWO consequences, and the second is the dangerous one: (1) the stale latch cannot clear, and (2) NO NEW ALERT CAN FIRE EITHER. Latching is per (account, cause) and the frozen entry already holds cause:risk_refused — the same cause a cash-clamp refusal would produce — so even removing the skip leaves a pre-latched cause that could swallow the first genuine alert. ⚠️ THE DISPOSITION IS STILL THE OPERATOR'S AND IS NOW MORE URGENT, NOT LESS: this row already asks 'do we want to know if it starts REFUSING for a new cause?' and that question was never answered. It cannot be answered by inference — removing the skip re-arms alerting on an account whose cash-clamp refusals are EXPECTED (~55% of tlt_pullback_1h's flow is short and unexecutable, and the sizer demands ~11x the account), so a naive un-skip may produce exactly the desensitizing alarm this repo treats as a P1. That trade-off is why this is not being flipped autonomously.

updates.note:
THE MEASUREMENT THIS ROW ASKED FOR CHANGES WHAT THE ROW IS ABOUT. I filed it as an ALERTING question — is suppressing both detectors on one account defensible? Discharging its own criterion 3 answered a bigger one.

alpaca_live has refused 317 of 318 orders across its entire recorded life (99.7%), with exactly ONE closed trade, over 57 days. That is the complete population, not a window: the query returned 318 of 318 with filter_state='applied'.

And the cause is CONFIGURATION, not malfunction. The account holds ~$150 (sometimes $0, sometimes unreadable) while the 15 strategies routed to it trade ETFs whose share price exceeds that, and Alpaca is in WHOLE_UNIT_QTY_EXCHANGES so the sizer correctly rounds to zero and correctly refuses. Nothing is broken. The account cannot place an order at this funding level, by arithmetic.

SO THE SUPPRESSION IS NOT THE PROBLEM, IT IS THE SYMPTOM. Silencing an alarm that fires 3-5 times an hour is a rational response to noise. The cost is that a structurally dead account with 16 live strategies pointed at it stopped being visible instead of being fixed — which is the desensitized-alarm P1 read from the other end: not an alarm everyone walks past, but an alarm someone reasonably turned off while the condition stayed.

This row stays open on its alerting question (the two SKIPs still need a disposition), but the operator decision now lives on the new row, because funding/routing is Tier-3 and is the thing that actually needs deciding.

THE SILENT_REFUSAL_SKIP HALF NOW HAS A MEASUREMENT INSTEAD OF A GUESS. This row said 'the operator may have suppressed these on purpose' and asked the question rather than answering it. The likely PURPOSE is now confirmed, and it is now obsolete.

POPULATION, stated because it is the whole point: all 319 alpaca_live journal rows (/api/bot/db/table/trades, filter_state='applied' asserted, page == total == 319, nothing truncated), spanning 43 distinct UTC days 2026-06-25 -> 2026-08-25. Graded with the LIVE module (src/runtime/dead_leg), per-DAY, because the detector grades a 24h window and an all-history verdict answers a different question. My first pass graded all-history, got 'partially_refused', and would have concluded the account can never alert at all -- wrong population, corrected before it was recorded.

  days verdict == signalled_never_placed (the ONLY verdict that alerts):
    PRE-2026-08-24 grading : 42 of 43
    CURRENT grading        : 17 of 43

SO THE SKIP'S MOTIVE IS CONFIRMED: at 42 of 43 days alerting, SILENT_REFUSAL_SKIP=alpaca_live was suppressing a near-daily false alarm on an account whose refusals were CORRECT — it is mode: dry_run, so refusing every order IS the execution gate working. That is the desensitized-alarm P1, and suppressing it was the right call at the time.

AND THE MOTIVE IS NOW GONE. BL-20260824-SILENT-REFUSAL-CANNOT-SEE-A-DECLARED-DRY-RUN fixed this STRUCTURALLY: dead_leg.bucket_for reads the row's reason and buckets a declared policy skip as policy_skipped -> verdict refusing_by_declaration. Measured against that, **every single day from 2026-07-21 onward — 23 consecutive days — grades refusing_by_declaration and would not alert.** The 17 that still would are ALL 2026-06-25 -> 2026-07-20, i.e. before the dry_run_sizing_skip reason prefix existed to be recognised. 165 of the 319 rows carry it (101 zero_balance, 56 risk_refused, 8 account_mode_dry_run).

THE PROPOSAL, and it is now cheap to evaluate: remove SILENT_REFUSAL_SKIP=alpaca_live. On the last 23 days of actual behaviour it would produce ZERO alerts, so the change cannot reintroduce the flood it was set against. Its only remaining effect is the one this row already named as the objection: suppressing a NEW cause. The latch is keyed per (account, cause) precisely so a new cause is not swallowed by an old one, and a blanket skip defeats exactly that.

⚠️ SCOPE: this speaks ONLY to SILENT_REFUSAL_SKIP. ACCOUNT_DOWN_ALERT_SKIP is a different question about REACHABILITY and this measurement says nothing about it — the row is right that they must be decided per detector, and answering one is not answering both.

⚠️ ALSO NOT CHANGED IN-SESSION: this is a Tier-2 env change on the live trader. Proposed with evidence, not applied.

CROSS-REF, because it bounds what removing the skip actually buys: BL-20260825-RARE-CAUSE-INVISIBLE-ON-A-PARTIALLY-REFUSED-ACCOUNT — an alert also requires verdict == signalled_never_placed, so on a day where alpaca_live places even one order (2026-07-02 is the single such day in 43) a genuine rare cause would still not alert, skip or no skip.

⚠️ HIGH AND PARTICULARLY PERVERSE — re-validated. The one account measured refusing essentially every order is on BOTH alert skip-lists simultaneously, so nothing watches the thing that is demonstrably broken. Part of the alpaca_live go-live cluster. Live state this review: alpaca_live reads balance $200.10, api_ok true, ZERO open positions, and zero gross notional across 1,848 exposure_soak samples. HEAD of main also carries 'Confirm the $200 alpaca_live sizing wall'. Tier-3 and the operator's; nothing a review can drain. This should be fixed before any alpaca_live go-live step, not after.

items.tier: 1 (doc correction; the live value itself was an operator-gated Tier-2 flip)
items.title: NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_MODE is live in `apply` on bybit_1 AND real-money bybit_2, and CLAUDE.md records neither the value nor when it was flipped
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-23 from a get-env ALL read of ict-trader-live (issue #10181); both declared in the env_file, so persistent:
    NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_MODE     = 'apply'
    NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_ACCOUNTS = 'bybit_1,bybit_2'

CLAUDE.md's row for this pair describes `annotate` as the default, explains at length what the annotate soak is for, and ends '**Tier-2 to flip to `apply`.**' It never states that the flip HAPPENED, when, or on which accounts. A reader following that row would conclude the reconciler is still observe-only and is NOT touching the money DB. It is: at `apply` it reduces/closes journal rows, and the allowlist includes **bybit_2, which is mainnet real money**.

THE FLIP MAY BE ENTIRELY CORRECT - this row does NOT assert it was unauthorised. The same CLAUDE.md row records the operator staging decision that produced the bybit_1-only allowlist, and widening to bybit_2 is a plausible, deliberate follow-on. What is wrong is the RECORD: the doc says what the default is and what the gate would be, not what the system is doing.

THIS IS THE FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD CLASS AGAIN, and that one cost real money. There, an override ran live on real money with no walk-forward behind it and was surfaced only when someone happened to read the env (BL-20260810-FLIP-CONFIDENCE-OVERRIDE-LIVE-WITHOUT-RECORD, 'that read surface's first find'). CLAUDE.md now carries an explicit 'LIVE VALUE:' marker on that key for exactly this reason. The netting keys have no such marker.

Noted while verifying an unrelated key - i.e. found the same way, by accident, which is the argument for the marker convention rather than for a better reader.
resolution_criteria: CLAUDE.md's NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_MODE / _ACCOUNTS row carries an explicit '**LIVE VALUE:**' line stating apply + the account list + the date + who approved it, in the same shape FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD and BYBIT_TPSL_MODE already use. Field beats comment: read the env, do not infer from the merge.

Confirm with the operator that widening the allowlist to real-money bybit_2 was the intended Tier-2 decision, and record the answer on the row. Do NOT change the live value on either answer - if it was NOT intended, that is a Tier-2 decision of its own.

Consider whether the '**LIVE VALUE:**' marker should be enforced rather than remembered: three keys now carry it by hand (FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD, FLIP_MIN_POSITION_AGE_HOURS, BYBIT_TPSL_MODE, CANDLE_CACHE_TTL_MAX_S) and this pair shows the convention is not self-applying. A guard could compare get_env.py's ALLOWED_KEYS against the keys CLAUDE.md marks, and flag any declared-in-env key whose doc row has no live-value line.

updates.note: ⚠️ RE-CONFIRMED AS A DOC/REALITY GAP ON A REAL-MONEY WRITE PATH. CLAUDE.md's NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_MODE row still describes `annotate` as the default and does not record the live value or that bybit_2 (real money) is in the allowlist. Live corroboration that `apply` IS acting: 6 real-money closes in this window carry exit path `netting_attributed`, which only the apply path produces. Field beats comment — the doc needs the live value.

items.tier: 1 (consumers + a guard; the DATA is fine, the readers are not)
items.area: backlog machinery / review triage / unasserted denominator
items.title: A review session filtering `status == "open"` sees 174 of 371 live rows, and ageing by `opened_at` silently drops 92 — the backlog's own triage has an unstated denominator
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-23 over docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json (837 rows). Found while trying to answer a simple question — is the backlog actually being drained? — and nearly publishing a badly wrong answer to it.

TWO SCHEMA SPLITS, both silent:

1. STATUS VOCABULARY. Live rows are NOT just `open`. The counts are: open 174 · kept_open 197 · resolved 451 · superseded 6 · wont_fix 6 · invalid 3. `kept_open` is REAL LIVE WORK, not a parked state — sampled rows include a stray trade_journal.db on the trainer holding 15,644 signals rows and a 501 MB unrotated signal_audit.jsonl, and none of the sampled rows carries a `snoozed_until`. So a consumer filtering `status == 'open'` sees **174 of 371 live rows — 47%**.

2. DATE KEY. 733 rows carry `opened_at`, **92 carry `opened`** instead, and 12 carry neither. A consumer ageing rows by `opened_at` alone silently treats 92 rows as undateable. The `opened`-keyed cohort is recognisable (a BL-20260818-* block that also uses `evidence`/`next_action`/`related` where the canonical shape uses `detail`/`resolution_criteria`/`refs`), so this is a second row SCHEMA living in the same file rather than scattered typos.

WHAT THAT COSTS, DEMONSTRATED ON MYSELF: my first pass reported '0 open rows >= 45 days old' — computed over 116 dateable rows out of 174, with the other 58 dropped for the key reason above, and over `open` only. Read as stated it says the backlog has no old work at all. THE CORRECTED FIGURE, over the true live population (371 rows, 369 dateable once BOTH keys are read): **12 rows >= 45 days = 3%, oldest 90 days.**

⚠️ THE GOOD NEWS IS REAL AND SURVIVES THE CORRECTION, which is why this row is about the READERS and not the data. Against the baseline `check_backlog_criteria.py` recorded on 2026-08-13 — 38% of open rows with no resolution_criteria, 44% no severity, 24% no tier, and 25% sitting >= 45 days never advanced — today's open rows are at **0% / 0% / 0%** missing across all three backlogs, and the >=45-day share is 25% -> 3%. The guard worked. The 203 rows still missing `resolution_criteria` are ALL non-open (148 resolved, 49 kept_open, 3 wont_fix, 2 superseded, 1 invalid), i.e. history that predates the guard.

This is the unasserted-denominator class (CLAUDE.md § 'Diagnostic provenance', sub-class C) applied to the backlog's own triage: every count above is correct about the population it ranges over, and wrong about the one a reader assumes.
resolution_criteria: One shared helper that answers 'which rows are LIVE?' and 'when was this row opened?', imported by every consumer instead of each re-deriving it — the same single-owner shape src/runtime/provenance.py has for measured-vs-manufactured. Today at least three readers (check_backlog_criteria.py, the review skills, ad-hoc session probes like the one that found this) each pick their own status filter and date key.

`kept_open` is either folded into the live set everywhere or given a documented meaning that justifies excluding it. Right now it is 197 rows — larger than `open` — with no statement of what distinguishes them, and the sampled ones read as ordinary live work.

The `opened` vs `opened_at` split is resolved: either normalise the 92 rows to `opened_at` (a data migration, and note it will rewrite those rows — use scripts/ops/backlog_append.py's round-trip discipline so the diff does not re-attribute the whole file), or have the shared accessor read both and say so. Do NOT leave a reader to discover it.

check_backlog_criteria.py grows a check for the SHAPE split, not just field presence: a row whose date key or status value is outside the declared vocabulary should fail loudly, because both splits above passed every existing guard while being invisible.

updates.note: ⚠️ DIRECTLY GOVERNS THIS REVIEW'S OWN TRIAGE, and I checked rather than assumed. The health file's status vocabulary is SEVEN values: open 270, kept_open 175, resolved 539, snoozed 12, superseded 5, wont_fix 3, invalid 2. A filter on `status == "open"` would have seen 270 of 483 live rows (55.9%) — this row's exact defect. My triage filtered on NOT-IN(resolved, closed, done), which is the safer direction: it caught all 483 including the 5 superseded / 3 wont_fix / 2 invalid rows that are arguably already dispositioned. Recording the population so the next session can reproduce it.

items.tier: 3 (funding / account-mode / strategy routing — propose, do not act)
items.title: alpaca_live has refused 317 of 318 orders in its entire recorded life (99.7%) — 16 live strategies route to an account that cannot size a single whole share, and both alarms are switched off
items.detail:
COMPLETE POPULATION, not a sample: the query returned 318 rows of 318 total for account_id='alpaca_live' (/api/bot/db/table/trades, filter_state='applied', page == total, so nothing was truncated). Span 2026-06-25T13:30 -> 2026-08-21T15:05, about 57 days.

    rejected           312
    exchange_rejected    5
    closed               1     <-- the only trade that ever completed

317 of 318 = 99.7% refused.

THE CAUSES ARE STRUCTURAL, NOT TRANSIENT. Parsed from notes.reason across all 318 rows:
    134  zero_balance: gate_balance=0.00 USD (no funds available to size against)   [101 dry_run_sizing_skip + 33 direct]
     20  sizing_failed: RuntimeError: balance() returned None for alpaca_live
     ~90 risk_refused: sized_qty=0, with balance reading 0.10 / 149.31 / 149.48 / 149.56 / 150.00 / 150.05
      8  account_mode_dry_run

So the account holds roughly $150 (sometimes $0, sometimes unreadable) and the 15 strategies routed to it trade ETFs — SPY(63), TLT(60), QQQ(57), GLD(57), SLV(32), USO(32), GDX(7), IAUM(6) — whose share prices exceed what $150 can buy. Alpaca is in `risk.WHOLE_UNIT_QTY_EXCHANGES` (bracket orders reject fractional shares — documented in CLAUDE.md's env-var table under IB_PLACE_CONFIRM_S; note that id is a CLAUDE.md citation, NOT a filed backlog row, so do not follow it expecting one), so the sizer correctly rounds to sized_qty=0 and correctly refuses. EVERY COMPONENT IS BEHAVING AS DESIGNED. The account simply cannot place an order at this funding level, and no amount of signal generation will change that.

THE 20 `balance() returned None` ROWS ARE A SEPARATE, REAL DEFECT riding along - that is BL-20260813-ALPACA-BALANCE-NONE-WHILE-ACCOUNT-READS-ACTIVE observed in the wild, and it is why the reachability probe reads the account UP (positions() answers) while every order dies.

⚠️ AND NOTHING REPORTS ANY OF IT. Both detectors that would surface this are skipped for this exact account: ACCOUNT_DOWN_ALERT_SKIP='alpaca_live' and SILENT_REFUSAL_SKIP='alpaca_live', both declared in the env_file so they survive restarts (BL-20260823-ALPACA-LIVE-IS-EXEMPT-FROM-BOTH-DETECTORS-THAT-WATCH-IT). Suppressing an alarm that fires 3-5 times an hour is a rational response to noise; the cost is that the underlying condition — 16 live strategies emitting signals into an account that cannot act on them — became invisible rather than fixed.

This is the dead-leg shape at ACCOUNT scale: 'declared live, evaluates, signals, places NOTHING' is exactly what silent_refusal_alert was built to catch, and this account is exempt from it.
resolution_criteria: OPERATOR DECISION, and it is Tier-3 either way — this row proposes nothing unilaterally. Three coherent dispositions: (a) FUND it to a level where whole-share sizing on the routed symbols is possible (SPY alone needs several hundred dollars per share); (b) REROUTE those 15-16 strategies to an account that can size them, or to fractional-capable venues; (c) set the account to dry_run and stop routing live strategies into it. What is NOT coherent is the present state: live routing plus a funding level that guarantees refusal plus both alarms off.

Whichever is chosen, the two SKIP entries are revisited in the same change - they are currently the only reason this looks quiet. Do not leave a suppressed alarm attached to a condition that has been resolved, and do not leave it attached to one that has not.

Re-measure after the change with the SAME complete-population query (account_id filter, assert filter_state=='applied', check page == total) and state the refusal share. The current baseline to beat is 317/318 = 99.7%.

The 20 `balance() returned None` rows are tracked separately as BL-20260813-ALPACA-BALANCE-NONE-WHILE-ACCOUNT-READS-ACTIVE; fixing the funding does NOT fix that, and it is what makes the reachability probe read UP while orders die.

progress.note: THE TWO SKIPPED DETECTORS ARE NOW MEASURED AUTHORITATIVELY, AND THEY ARE A LANDMINE ON THE FLIP RATHER THAN A BUG TODAY. This row already said 'both detectors are skipped for it'; that was read from config. Confirmed 2026-08-23T18:20Z via get-env (issue #10200) against the RUNNING PROCESS's environ, not merely the declared env_file — both agree: ACCOUNT_DOWN_ALERT_SKIP process='alpaca_live' declared='alpaca_live'; SILENT_REFUSAL_SKIP process='alpaca_live' declared='alpaca_live'. Each list contains EXACTLY ONE entry, and it is this account. WHY IT IS CORRECT TODAY: the account is mode:dry_run and refuses ~100% of orders for the sizing/balance reasons this row documents, so an un-skipped detector would fire continuously on a known, filed condition — the desensitized-alarm P1. Skipping it was the right call. WHY IT BECOMES WRONG AT THE INSTANT OF FUNDING: `silent_refusal_alert` is precisely the detector for 'declared live, evaluates, signals, places NOTHING', and that is EXACTLY the shape the shorting rejection would take (BL-20260823-ALPACA-LIVE-CANNOT-SHORT-BUT-60PCT-OF-ITS-FLOW-IS-SHORT: 157 of 262 packages are short against shorting_enabled=False). So a funded, flipped account would have 60% of its flow rejected at the broker with the one alarm designed to catch that switched off for it specifically — and the other alarm (account-down) off too. THE REMEDY IS CHEAP AND MUST RIDE THE SAME CHANGE AS THE FLIP: clear `alpaca_live` from both vars in the same operation that sets mode:live, so the account is never simultaneously live and unwatched. Doing it afterwards leaves a window whose whole point is that nothing would report it. Two `set-env` calls, Tier-2.

updates.note:
RE-GRADED critical -> high, 2026-08-25, operator-directed ('keep it dry_run, fix blockers first'). THE PREMISE THESE ROWS READ ON IS WRONG IN ONE RESPECT: alpaca_live is `mode: dry_run` (config/accounts.yaml:825, SHELVED 2026-07-15, Tier-3) with `account_class: real_money`. So its refusals are the execution gate WORKING, not a fault — the same finding BL-20260824-SILENT-REFUSAL-CANNOT-SEE-A-DECLARED-DRY-RUN made for this exact account one day later. Three rows at CRITICAL describing a switched-off account as a live emergency is itself the desensitized-alarm P1: an operator scanning criticals sees three fires on a box that is off. They are GO-LIVE PRECONDITIONS, which is what `high` is for.

THE RE-ARM GATE IS ALREADY DEFINED AND WAS NOT CITED BY ANY OF THESE ROWS. config/accounts.yaml:828 states it: re-arming to live is 'gated on the /performance-review portfolio-vs-bybit benchmark (does a ready-for-live Alpaca portfolio improve risk-adjusted PnL, incl. via regime diversification, vs bybit-only?)'. That benchmark has not been run. It, not funding, is the answer to 'are we ready to go live'.

THE 317-of-318 REFUSAL COUNT IS NOT IN DISPUTE — re-pulled 2026-08-25 as 319 of 319 rows (filter_state=applied, so the filter really formed a WHERE and `total` is not the whole table). What changes is the READING: on a dry_run account, refusing is the gate working. The row's own cause breakdown supports that — 8 rows are literally `account_mode_dry_run` and 101 of the 134 zero_balance rows carry the `dry_run_sizing_skip` prefix that execution_diagnostics.EXPECTED_DISPATCH_SKIP_REASONS was added (operator directive 2026-07-15) to recognise as a DECLARED skip.

THE FUNDING ARITHMETIC IN THIS ROW IS SUPERSEDED. It computed '$2,500 lets all 15 priced legs place >= 1 share; $1,000 gets 14/15'. The account is funded at $200 (config block, 2026-08-25) and at that level the sizer reaches 8 of 15 legs — TLT, IEF, SLV(x2), USO, IAUM, GDX, and tlt_pullback_1d. The other 7 are CASH-bound: SPY $745, QQQ $732, GLD $372, IWM $302 — one share exceeds a large fraction of the whole account, and no risk setting reaches them. Only funding, a cheaper proxy, or a fractional-capable venue does. That is the honest state, and it is already written into the config block.

RE-CONFIRMED: 317 of 318 refusals over the account's life (99.7%), and today alpaca_live still holds ZERO positions with zero gross notional across 1,848 exposure samples. 16 live strategies route to an account that cannot fill them. Part of the alpaca_live go-live cluster. Live state this review: alpaca_live reads balance $200.10, api_ok true, ZERO open positions, and zero gross notional across 1,848 exposure_soak samples. HEAD of main also carries 'Confirm the $200 alpaca_live sizing wall'. Tier-3 and the operator's; nothing a review can drain.

items.tier: 2 (alerting only — cannot change an order, cannot refuse a trade)
items.title: the target-naked CRITICAL declares a 6h cooldown and delivered up to 31 pages/symbol/day — the latch was per-process, so every trader restart re-armed it; 53.7% of the entire ERROR+ feed
items.detail:
FOUND while answering BL-20260818-DID-TARGET-NAKED-EVER-FIRE-FOR-MGC, which asked whether the detector was silent. It was the opposite.

`order_monitor._emit_target_naked_alert` is Level.CRITICAL — the channel reserved for 'this position can only stop out or run' — and its own comment states the intent exactly right: 'an un-limited alert would fire every five minutes forever, which is the desensitized-alarm P1 this repo treats as its own bug, not diligence. One page per 6h per (account, symbol) keeps it loud without training the operator to scroll past it.'

The implementation could not deliver that intent. The latch was `_LAST_TARGET_NAKED_ALERT_MONO`, a module global keyed on `time.monotonic()`. BOTH are per-PROCESS. The trader restarts on every merge to `main`, so the cooldown reset on every restart — while the CONDITION it rate-limits persists across restarts by definition (a resting bracket is broker state, not process state).

MEASUREMENT. /api/bot/logs?limit=1000&level=error&since=2026-08-16. POPULATION: 376 rows against a cap of 1000 (not truncated); oldest row 2026-08-17T08:03:56Z, so 08-16 is unmeasured rather than empty.
  - 202 of 376 rows = 53.7% of every ERROR+/CRITICAL row over ~6.5 days were `ib_target_naked`, for TWO ib_paper positions in an already-filed state. Next largest: strategy_builder 166. Also 6 `alpaca_target_naked`, so the family is live on the Alpaca sweep too.
  - A 6h cooldown permits at most 4 pages/symbol/day. Observed: 31 for MGC on 08-20 and 31 for MES the same day — ~8x the declared ceiling.

MECHANISM, established two ways rather than asserted:
  (1) MES and MGC counts pair almost exactly per day — 16/16, 31/31, 11/11, 24/24 — the signature of one page per symbol per process rather than a time-driven cadence. The one asymmetric day is 08-18 (MES 11, MGC 1), explained by the 07:49Z MGC repair ending its condition.
  (2) DIRECT: `exit_interval_soak` reports 9 distinct trader `process_started_utc` values on 2026-08-23; `ib_target_naked` fired for MES exactly 9 times that day. STATE THE POPULATION — this exact match is n=1 DAY, because the diag log_file page truncates to 1000 lines and those covered only 08-23.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE NOISE: CRITICAL is the level chosen precisely so this reaches Telegram. Flooding it for a known paper-account condition trains the operator to scroll past the one channel reserved for an unprotected live position — which is the P1 that CLAUDE.md's 'If you see something, say something' names outright ('the desensitized alarm is ITSELF a P1 bug'). It also crowds the /api/bot/notifications operator_warning banner, which is capped at 3 newest-first.

CONTRAST, because per-process is not always wrong: `exit_loop_health`'s requirement breach alerts once per PROCESS deliberately and correctly, since `max_interval_ms` is itself a per-process measurement. Here the condition is durable broker state, so the latch must be too — which is why `silent_refusal_alert`, `account_reachability_alert` and `prop_fills_staleness` all persist to `runtime_logs/*_state.json` 'so the counter survives a bounce'. This one alone did not.
items.resolution_criteria: The cooldown survives a simulated restart; a genuinely-elapsed 6h still pages; an unreadable latch pages rather than suppressing; a future-dated entry does not mute forever.
items.resolution: FIXED in the same PR. The latch is now `runtime_logs/target_naked_alert_state.json`, written atomically via os.replace, keyed on wall-clock `time.time()` (monotonic is meaningless across processes) with a 7-day prune so the file cannot grow unbounded. THREE STATES, NOT COLLAPSED: `_load_target_naked_state` returns (state, readable) — 'the latch has never fired' and 'we could not read the latch' are both {} and are deliberately NOT treated the same. An unreadable latch ALERTS and logs a WARNING: suppressing a CRITICAL safety page because a file read failed is the wrong direction to fail, and a permanently unreadable latch then announces itself as spam rather than as silence. A future-dated entry (clock skew) yields a negative delta and pages, so the window is bounded below by 0 as well as above by the cooldown. Regression test: tests/test_target_naked_cooldown_is_durable.py (5 cases, incl. the simulated restart). The existing tests/test_alpaca_naked_rearm.py — which exercises the other call site — still passes unchanged. The sweep's own `summary['target_naked']` counter is incremented BEFORE the alert call and is untouched, so this cannot change what the sweep detects or does: alerting only, no order path.

progress.note: ⚠️ THE FIX IS DEPLOYED AND HAS NEVER BEEN EXERCISED. Do NOT read the alert-rate drop as evidence it works - recorded because this row is marked `resolved`, and `resolved` without this caveat reads as `observed working`. DEPLOY CONFIRMED: origin/main, web-api and trader all on fced7279 at 17:58Z (and the web-api is genuinely RUNNING it, not merely reporting it - /api/diag/log_file?name=target_naked_alert_state returns 200 where it was HTTP 400 before the restart, which is positive proof the new allowlist is loaded). MEASURED 2026-08-23T17:5xZ, /api/bot/logs?limit=1000&level=error&since=2026-08-23: 31 ERROR+ rows (cap 1000, so NOT truncated), window 00:38Z-17:24Z. 15 ib_target_naked today, LAST AT 13:54:32Z, then four hours silent. THE SILENCE IS THE CONDITION ENDING, NOT THE COOLDOWN. MGC's take-profit was attached ~12:27Z and MES's ~13:54Z (both confirmed resting on /api/diag/ib_open_orders at 16:35Z), so neither position was target-naked after that. The trader only picked up c42be441 - the commit carrying this fix - between 17:05Z and 17:22Z, HOURS AFTER THE LAST ALERT. The fix was therefore never live at any moment when the condition existed. THE LATCH FILE PROVES NOTHING EITHER: it reads present:false, which is equally consistent with 'the cooldown is working' and 'the cooldown has never been invoked' - an absent file cannot distinguish them, and reading it as success would be the same collapse this row is about. WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY VERIFY IT: the next time any IB position goes target-naked across a trader restart, the page count must stay at most 4/symbol/day instead of tracking the restart count. Until then this is the same posture as the #10174 transmit fix - deployed, unexercised, and not to be reported as working.

items.title: three more durable alert/watchdog latches have no read surface, so a permanently-broken latch is indistinguishable from a working one — including the liveness watchdog's restart budget
items.detail:
FOUND while shipping the durable target-naked cooldown (BL-20260823-TARGET-NAKED-COOLDOWN-RESETS-ON-EVERY-RESTART) and asking whether that fix would be OBSERVABLE once deployed.

THE GENERAL SHAPE. Each of these files latches a condition in order to SUPPRESS an operator page, and the correct failure direction for a safety page is to ALERT when the latch cannot be read. Both of those are right individually, and together they mean: a permanently-unwritable or corrupt latch reproduces exactly the spam it exists to stop, and from outside the two states are INDISTINGUISHABLE — the alert rate looks the same either way. Reading the latch is the only thing that tells them apart. This is the `exit_price_source` shape (written, never read) applied to alerting rather than to provenance.

FIXED IN THE SAME PR (now readable via /api/diag/log_file): `silent_refusal_alert_state.json`, `prop_fills_staleness_state.json`, `target_naked_alert_state.json`. Two of five were already allowlisted (`account_reachability_alert_state`, `trainer_reachability_alert_state`), so this was an inconsistency, not a policy.

STILL UNREACHABLE — the remainder, and why each matters:
  - `liveness_watchdog_state.json` (src/runtime/liveness_watchdog.py) — THE MOST SAFETY-RELEVANT OF THE THREE. It holds the per-episode restart budget (`--max-restarts 5` / `--cooldown-min 3`). Once exhausted the watchdog goes ALERT-ONLY and stops auto-restarting the trader; nothing outside can read how much budget is left, so 'the watchdog will restart the trader if it stalls' is currently an assumption rather than an observation.
  - `exit_loop_health_alert_state.json` (src/runtime/exit_loop_health.py) — the requirement-BREACH latch. Note the exit_loop_health STATE file is already readable under the `exit_loop_health` name; this is a DIFFERENT file and is not.
  - `daily_cap_alert_state.json` (src/runtime/daily_cap_alert.py).
Also unreachable, lower value (cadence state, not a suppression latch): `prop_monitor_pulse.json`, `prop_sl_tp_alert.json`, `prop_status_request.json`.

⚠️ TWO FILES WERE INITIALLY MISCOUNTED AS UNREACHABLE AND ARE NOT — recorded because the mistake is instructive. My first probe matched only STRING LITERALS inside the `_LOG_FILES` block, so it missed any path bound to a CONSTANT. `package_leg_coverage_state.json` is reachable under the `package_leg_coverage` name (via `_PACKAGE_LEG_COVERAGE_STATE`), and `liquidity_state.json` has its own `/api/bot/liquidity` route. A probe that cannot see constants under-reports coverage, which is the anti-conservative direction for a gap claim.

SEPARATE DEFECT FIXED IN THE SAME PR: `CLAUDE.md`'s `GET /api/diag/log_file?name={...}` row listed 21 names against 26 in code — stale by 8 once the three latches were added (`orphan_events`, `package_leg_coverage`, `protection_reassert_soak`, `account_reachability_alert_state`, `trainer_reachability_alert_state` were all undocumented). A relay-bound analysis session reads that row to learn what it may ask for, so an undocumented surface is an unreachable one in practice. Now 29 = 29, pinned by tests/test_diag_log_file_allowlist_coherence.py in BOTH directions (undocumented name, and a documented name the allowlist does not serve).
items.resolution_criteria: Each remaining state file is either (a) allowlisted in diag.py::_LOG_FILES and documented in CLAUDE.md — the coherence test then enforces both automatically — or (b) has a recorded reason it should NOT be readable. `liveness_watchdog_state.json` is the one to do first: without it, the trader's restart budget cannot be observed from outside at all.
items.notes: Tier-1 throughout — a read-only allowlist entry opens no order path and can refuse no trade. The coherence test added here means any FUTURE addition to _LOG_FILES that is not documented fails CI, so this class cannot silently regrow.

updates.note: ⚠️ THE CLASS ROW FOR THIS REVIEW'S TOP FINDING. Re-validated, and it recurred AGAIN: prop_risk_gate shipped a *_MODE gate on 2026-08-25 with NO soak writer and NO diag allowlist entry, which I found and fixed today (BL-20260829-PROP-RISK-GATE-PROMISED-A-SOAK-ROW-AND-WROTE-NOTHING, PR #10414). That is the FOURTH recurrence. Recommend widening the fix from 'register these three latches' to a CI guard: any *_MODE gate must have a soak writer AND a diag read surface. See BL-20260813-NO-GUARD-FOR-ENV-READ-SURFACE, which is the same guard from the env-var side.

CRITERION (a) IS NOW MET FOR EVERY NAMED FILE — AND THIS ROW'S OWN DESCRIPTION WAS WRONG IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION, which is the more important half.

THE CONFLATION. This row calls `liveness_watchdog_state.json` "THE MOST SAFETY-RELEVANT OF THE THREE" and says "It holds the per-episode restart budget (--max-restarts 5 / --cooldown-min 3). Once exhausted the watchdog goes ALERT-ONLY and stops auto-restarting the trader". Measured 2026-08-30 by reading BOTH writers, not by inference:

  * `scripts/check_heartbeat.py` (the EXTERNAL dead-man switch behind ict-liveness-watchdog.timer) writes **`heartbeat_check_state.json`** — DEFAULT_STATE at line 104 — and its state keys are `autoheal_attempts`, `autoheal_exhausted_alerted`, `last_autoheal_attempt_ts`. THIS is the restart budget this row describes.
  * `src/runtime/liveness_watchdog.py` writes **`liveness_watchdog_state.json`** (line 60) and its state is ONE key, `slot_key`, an hourly anti-spam slot for a signals-dispatched-vs-trades-placed ping. Its own module docstring says so.

So two different watchdogs share the name, and the row attached the RIGHT description to the WRONG filename. A session acting on it literally would have allowlisted the anti-spam slot, recorded the criterion as met, and left the restart budget unreadable while it now LOOKED covered — strictly worse than the original gap, because a presumed-covered gap stops being looked for. Field beats comment: the writers are authoritative and this row's prose was not.

FIXED IN THIS CHANGE: BOTH names are now in `diag.py::_LOG_FILES` and in the CLAUDE.md `log_file` row, with the distinction stated at both sites so it cannot be re-collapsed; the coherence test enforces both directions automatically (4 passed).

STATE OF THE OTHER TWO NAMED FILES, verified live on the same call rather than assumed: `exit_loop_health_alert_state` is allowlisted AND `present: true` (124 bytes — the requirement-breach latch has fired at least once). `daily_cap_alert_state` is allowlisted and `present: false` — never written, which is the expected state if no daily cap has been breached, and is now at least OBSERVABLE rather than assumed.

THE STRUCTURAL FIX THE 2026-08-29 UPDATE ASKED FOR EXISTS NOW, BUT ONLY FOR ONE FAMILY — do not read it as wider than it is. That update recommended "widening the fix from 'register these three latches' to a CI guard". Shipped 2026-08-30: `tests/test_diag_log_file_allowlist_coherence.py::test_every_cooldown_latch_has_a_read_surface` DERIVES the expected set by parsing `_cooldown_admits("<kind>", ...)` call sites, so a new latch kind fails CI on the commit that adds it (control: removing an entry fails 2 tests and names the missing kind). ⚠️ ITS SCOPE IS `src/runtime/order_monitor.py` ONLY. Neither file corrected above is a `_cooldown_admits` kind, so the derived guard does NOT cover them and did not catch them — they were found by hand. Generalising the guard to every durable `*_state.json` writer in the tree is the remaining structural work and is NOT claimed as done.

RESOLVED — criterion (a) is now met for EVERY file this row names, verified against the code rather than asserted. `_LOG_FILES` in diag.py and the CLAUDE.md `log_file` row both carry all seven:

  liveness_watchdog_state · heartbeat_check_state · exit_loop_health_alert_state ·
  daily_cap_alert_state · prop_monitor_pulse · prop_sl_tp_alert · prop_status_request

`tests/test_diag_log_file_allowlist_coherence.py` pins BOTH directions (an allowlisted name that is undocumented, and a documented name the allowlist does not serve), so this cannot silently regress.

THE ROW'S OWN DESCRIPTION WAS WRONG AND THAT IS THE PART WORTH CARRYING FORWARD — see the 2026-08-30 update above. It calls `liveness_watchdog_state.json` "THE MOST SAFETY-RELEVANT OF THE THREE ... the per-episode restart budget". It is not: the budget (`autoheal_attempts`, `autoheal_exhausted_alerted`, `last_autoheal_attempt_ts`) lives in `heartbeat_check_state.json`, written by `scripts/check_heartbeat.py`. Two different watchdogs share the name. Closing this row by allowlisting only the file it NAMED would have left the budget unreadable while marking the criterion met — so BOTH are registered, with the distinction stated at both sites.

SCOPE OF THE STRUCTURAL FIX, stated so it is not over-read: the 2026-08-29 update asked to widen this from 'register these three latches' to a CI guard. `test_every_cooldown_latch_has_a_read_surface` (2026-08-30) DERIVES its expected set from the `_cooldown_admits("<kind>", ...)` call sites, so a new latch KIND fails CI on the commit that adds it — but its scope is `src/runtime/order_monitor.py` only. Neither file corrected here is such a kind, so the guard did not and could not catch them; they were found by hand.
