Generalising it to every durable `*_state.json` writer in the tree is REAL REMAINING WORK and is deliberately NOT claimed as done — it is the successor, tracked by BL-20260813-NO-GUARD-FOR-ENV-READ-SURFACE's sibling class rather than by keeping this row open, because this row's own criterion is satisfied.

items.tier: 1 (read path + deploy tooling; no order path)
items.title: /api/diag/version reported the DISK git sha, not the running process's — so the deploy assertion built to catch the 2026-05-09 stale-code incident was X == X and would have passed during that incident
items.detail:
FOUND by accident, which is the point: after #10194 merged I tried to READ one of the allowlist entries it added, and got HTTP 400 from a process whose /api/diag/version reported the very sha containing that entry.

THE DEFECT. `get_version` called `_resolve_git_sha()` per request, and that helper (src/web/runtime_status.py:50) shells `git rev-parse --short HEAD` against the working tree at CALL time. So the endpoint reported what was on DISK. A `git pull` advances that WITHOUT restarting anything — meaning the endpoint reported the NEW sha while the OLD code served, which IS the 2026-05-09 24h-stale-code state. Its own docstring says it exists to 'assert that a post-deploy restart actually rolled the running code forward (the 2026-05-09 incident shipped because nothing in the deploy chain confirmed the running web-api had rebooted)'. Reading disk is the one thing that cannot answer that.

AND THE DEPLOY-SIDE ASSERTION WAS STRUCTURALLY VACUOUS, which is the more serious half. scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh:525 sets `EXPECTED_SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)` and compares it to the endpoint's `git_sha` — the SAME command over the SAME working tree. X == X. It could not fail whether or not the service restarted, and it would have PASSED during the incident it cites. Its failure message even reads 'This usually means ict-web-api.service didn't actually restart' — the intent was exactly right and the implementation could not deliver it. This is 'green is not evidence' in its purest form: a check that verifies nothing while reporting success.

LIVE PROOF, not a code-reading argument — two independent endpoints on ONE process, 2026-08-23T17:2xZ:
  - /api/diag/version -> git_sha `fced7279`
  - /api/diag/log_file?name=target_naked_alert_state -> HTTP 400 (name absent from the RUNNING allowlist), though that name is present in _LOG_FILES as of `fced7279`
  - CONTROL: /api/diag/log_file?name=account_reachability_alert_state (allowlisted before today) -> HTTP 200 with real data, so the endpoint, the token and the transport are all fine
The disk had moved to `fced7279`; the process had not. Corroborating: the TRADER reported `c42be441` at the same moment, a DIFFERENT sha from the web-api's — the trader captures its sha at process start, so it correctly showed the older code it was actually running.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED FOR SO LONG: the two shas agree in the overwhelmingly common case (deploy pulls AND restarts), so the endpoint is right almost always and wrong in exactly the situation it was built for. That is the signature of this class — the diagnostic is accurate until the moment it matters.
items.resolution_criteria: `/api/diag/version` reports the sha the process was loaded from; disk and running are separately readable; a caller can tell 'we could not look' from 'they agree'; and the deploy script's comparison is no longer same-source-to-same-source.
items.resolution: FIXED in the same PR. `_RUNNING_GIT_SHA` is bound ONCE at module import in diag.py, so it names the code actually loaded, and costs one `git rev-parse` per process start instead of one per request. The endpoint now publishes three fields instead of one: `git_sha` (the RUNNING sha — what the field name and the docstring always claimed), `git_sha_on_disk` (resolved live), and `restart_pending`. ⚠️ `restart_pending` is `None`, never `False`, when either sha is `unknown` — 'we could not look' must not be reported as 'they agree', and False would assert the process matches the tree, which is the one claim we cannot make when a sha is unreadable. scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh needed NO logic change: its EXPECTED_SHA (disk, post-pull) now compares against a RUNNING sha, so it differs exactly when the restart did not happen. Its comment records why the old comparison was vacuous, because a later reader seeing two `git rev-parse` calls would otherwise 'tidy' one away and silently restore the bug. tests/test_diag_version_reports_running_sha.py pins all five properties (import-scope binding, the field serving the constant rather than a live resolve, both shas published, the None-on-unknown rule, and the deploy script's recorded history). CLAUDE.md's endpoint row is corrected with the measurement.
items.notes: Operational follow-on, filed as its own action rather than assumed: issue #10195 (vm-web-api-recover) restarts ict-web-api so #10194's allowlist entries actually load. The 400 above is what a stale process looks like from outside — and until this fix, nothing could tell you that.

items.tier: 2 (safety panel; read-only — nothing refuses a trade on this value)
items.title: the prop rule-distance panel published a FULL $142.92 daily-loss cushion on a day with -$218.79 of recorded closes, because a missing realized_today was summed as zero
items.detail:
FOUND while checking whether BL-20260823-PROP-JOURNAL-MISSING-THREE-DAYS-OF-TERMINAL-TRADES had been repaired. It had not (see that row), but reading /api/bot/prop/status alongside the fills surfaced a worse number.

WHAT THE PANEL SAID, measured 2026-08-23T17:5xZ on breakout_1:
  daily_loss_limit_usd: 142.92 · daily_loss_used_usd: 0.0 · distance_to_daily_loss_usd: 142.92 (a FULL cushion)
  status_freshness: ok (1.8h old) — so this is NOT the stale-snapshot caveat that row BL-20260814 already covers

WHAT THE SAME DATABASE HELD for the same day — 2 of 2 closed prop fills on that UTC date (/api/bot/prop/fills, 12 rows returned):
  2026-08-23T11:04:22 SOLUSDT closed pnl=-111.77
  2026-08-23T16:09:38 ETHUSDT closed pnl=-107.02
  TOTAL -218.79 = 1.53x the daily limit, on an account sitting $64 above its $4,700 static DD floor.

THE MECHANISM, read from prop_reconcile.compute_rule_distance (not inferred):
    if realized_today is not None or unrealized is not None:
        day_pnl = (realized_today or 0.0) + (unrealized or 0.0)
The guard is HALF right — it correctly refuses when BOTH terms are absent — but it passes when only ONE is, and then `(realized_today or 0.0)` converts 'we did not look' into 'nothing was realized today'.

THE LIVE SNAPSHOT IS EXACTLY THAT CASE (prop_account_status id 13): realized_today = None (never reported by anyone) while unrealized = 0.0 (correctly reported — the book WAS flat). One non-None term let the guard through, so day_pnl = 0.0, daily_loss_used = 0.0, and the panel published a full cushion.

⚠️ THE FAILURE DIRECTION IS THE DANGEROUS ONE: it reports MORE cushion than exists, on an account-killer limit, for the one account in the system with no broker feed to contradict it. And the function's OWN DOCSTRING already stated the correct contract — 'any value that can't be derived from the available status fields is None (never a fabricated 0)'. The doc was right and the implementation broke it.

NOT the same defect as BL-20260814 (stale snapshot): that row is about a CURRENT-ness caveat on a correctly-computed number. This is a number that was wrong at the moment it was computed, on a snapshot graded `ok`.
items.resolution_criteria: A missing realized_today (or unrealized) yields day_pnl None and no published cushion; a genuinely reported zero still publishes one; the static DD floor is unaffected; and the regression is proven to FAIL against the pre-fix code.
items.resolution: FIXED in the same PR. The sum of an unknown and a known is UNKNOWN, so both terms are now required. `day_pnl_state` ships beside `day_pnl` and is never collapsed into the null itself — `measured` / `realized_unreported` (the live case) / `unrealized_unreported` / `unreported` — because a consumer must be able to tell 'the operator reported no loss today' from 'the loss today was never reported'. Only the first is a cushion. SAFE BY INSPECTION, verified rather than assumed: nothing refuses a trade on this value (grepped every consumer — the API serves it as-is, telegram_report_handler renders it through `_cushion()`, whose docstring already calls None 'legitimate'), so the change removes a false reassurance and cannot block an order. Tests: tests/test_prop_daily_cushion_not_fabricated.py, 6 cases including the exact live snapshot shape, a genuinely-reported zero (so the honest-null does not swallow a real report), a breach going NEGATIVE rather than clamping at 0, and an assertion that the DD floor still resolves. FALSIFIED, not just passed: 4 of the 6 FAIL against the pre-fix code. The fixture also asserts the breakout ruleset actually loaded — an earlier draft passed the account as a dict, `_ruleset_for` raised `unhashable type: 'dict'`, every limit resolved to None and the None-assertions passed vacuously.
items.notes: BETTER FIX AVAILABLE, DELIBERATELY NOT TAKEN HERE: realized_today could be DERIVED from prop_fills rather than depending on a field the operator has never once populated (None in 13 of 13 snapshots — the complete prop_account_status table). Not done because the day boundary is genuinely unresolved — prop_fills.reported_at is REPORT time, not close time (the 2026-08-23 ETHUSD trade closed at 17:42 terminal time and was reported at 16:09:38Z), and Breakout's own daily reset boundary is not necessarily UTC midnight. Bucketing on the wrong axis would move the error rather than remove it. Filed as the follow-up rather than guessed at. SEPARATE, LOW-SEVERITY TOOLING NIT observed while landing this: claim-basis-guard's two-date basis pattern is `\b20\d\d-\d\d-\d\d\b`, which an ISO TIMESTAMP never satisfies — in `2026-08-23T11:04:22` there is no word boundary between the `3` and the `T`. So a row whose only stated basis is a timestamped window fails the guard even though it did state its population, and the author is pushed toward re-wording rather than toward adding evidence. 4 of 6 basis patterns were checked against this row's text and none matched despite the row carrying explicit windows. Worth widening the pattern to accept `T`-suffixed dates.

items.title: alpaca_live has shorting_enabled=False while 157 of 262 routed order packages (60%) are SHORT — 4 of 16 legs are 100% short and would be entirely dead
items.detail:
FOUND answering the operator's direct question: 'I'm going to fund alpaca in the next few days, are we ready to go live?'

MEASURED 2026-08-23T18:1xZ. /api/diag/broker_account_status?account_id=alpaca_live returns status_flags {status: ACTIVE, trading_blocked: false, account_blocked: false, trade_suspended_by_user: false, transfers_blocked: false, SHORTING_ENABLED: FALSE, crypto_status: INACTIVE, currency: USD}. So the account is reachable and trade-enabled — it simply cannot sell short.

items.title: 7 of 15 alpaca_live legs size to MORE notional than the whole account on a single trade — scale-invariant, so funding does not fix it, and no exposure cap is declared
items.detail:
FOUND answering the operator's pre-funding readiness question.

THE ARITHMETIC. RiskManager sizes qty = (balance x risk_pct) / per-share-risk, then floors to whole shares (alpaca is in WHOLE_UNIT_QTY_EXCHANGES; a sub-1-share size is REFUSED, never bumped). alpaca_live declares risk_pct 0.02. So notional = entry x floor(balance x 0.02 / per_share_risk), and notional/balance is a pure function of entry / per_share_risk — INDEPENDENT OF BALANCE. A tight stop therefore buys a huge share count.

MEASURED per-share risk as the median |entry - sl| over live order packages per leg (262 packages, 40-row cap per leg; 15 of 16 legs priced, splg_trend_long_1d had none). Notional as a share of the account, identical at $2,500 / $10,000 / $25,000:
  tlt_pullback_1h 414% · spy_pullback_1h 254% · ief_pullback_1d 218% · gld_pullback_1h 179-185% · qqq_pullback_1h 111-132% · spy_trend_long_1d 121-133% · tlt_pullback_1d 109-111%
  Under 100%: uso_trend_1h 88-90% · slv_trend_1h 77-79% · iaum_pullback_1d 58-59% · gld_pullback_1d 45-56% · iwm_trend_long_1d 48-57% · qqq_trend_long_1d 29-41% · slv_pullback_1d 30% · gdx_pullback_1d 27-28%
7 of 15 exceed 100% at EVERY level tested.

AND NOTHING IN CONFIG BOUNDS IT. alpaca_live's risk block is exactly {max_dd_pct: 0.05, daily_loss_pct: 0.05, daily_usd: 200, risk_pct: 0.02} — there is NO max_gross_exposure_pct, no max_position_pct, no notional cap. So the binding constraint would be Alpaca's own buying-power/margin engine, i.e. the position size a live account actually takes would be decided by the BROKER rather than by our risk model. The risk model's '2% per trade' is expressed correctly in RISK terms and not at all in EXPOSURE terms.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE SAME ROW as BL-20260823-ALPACA-LIVE-CANNOT-PLACE-AN-ORDER-AT-ITS-FUNDING-LEVEL: that row is about sizes rounding to ZERO at ~$150 (the 317/318 refusals). This is the opposite failure at the opposite end — once funded enough to place at all, several legs size far too LARGE. Funding moves the account from one failure into the other; $2,500 is where all 15 priced legs can place >= 1 share, and it is also where 7 of them exceed 100% notional.
items.resolution_criteria: alpaca_live declares an exposure/notional bound (e.g. max_gross_exposure_pct and/or a per-position notional cap) such that no routed leg can size past it, verified by recomputing the notional table above against the declared cap; OR the per-leg stop geometry is widened so 2% risk implies sane notional. Either is Tier-3.
items.notes: Tier-3, proposed with evidence and explicitly NOT applied — config/strategies.yaml and risk caps are operator-gated. The exposure-soak infrastructure (EXPOSURE_SOAK_SECONDS, /api/bot/exposure/soak) already exists to choose such a ceiling from a measured distribution rather than picking a number, per gross-exposure-governance-DESIGN.md section 6-7: the ceiling must sit ABOVE normal operation and BELOW the venue limit, and section 7 forbids shipping a value with no soak behind it. alpaca_live is in dry_run so its soak distribution is of a book that never traded — that is the honest gap to close before choosing the number.

progress.note: UPGRADED FROM A PROJECTION TO A LIVE OBSERVATION — the mirror is running this sizing model RIGHT NOW and the aggregate is worse than the per-leg table said. The row's original evidence was computed (entry / per_share_risk x risk_pct at hypothetical balances). This is the actual open book, measured 2026-08-23T18:2xZ from /api/bot/positions?include_paper=true (16 open alpaca positions, 8 per account): alpaca_portfolio holds $199,697 of notional and alpaca_paper $168,166, priced at entry x qty. Largest single position: alpaca_portfolio TLT SHORT 1,042 shares = $87,632. Then IWM long 187 = $56,667, SPY short 26 = $20,024, GLD long 39 = $15,175, IEF short 152 = $14,211. WHY THE AGGREGATE IS WORSE THAN THE PER-LEG NUMBER: the per-leg table showed single trades at 109-414% of account. Nothing caps GROSS exposure either — alpaca_live's risk block has no max_gross_exposure_pct — so the legs STACK. A real-money account funded at the $2,500-$25,000 range discussed and routed identically would be attempting to carry roughly 8x to 80x its own equity. This is the strongest form of the finding: not a model of what would happen, but a paper account demonstrating it at full size, which is exactly what the portfolio mirror exists to surface BEFORE real money rather than after.

⚠️ CORRECTION TO MY OWN FRAMING, AND IT CHANGES WHAT THE DEFECT IS. This row (and what I told the operator) implied the oversized order reaches the venue. IT DOES NOT. RiskManager.position_size applies a margin pre-flight cap AFTER the risk-based size: max_qty_by_margin = available_usd x effective_leverage x _MARGIN_SAFETY_BUFFER(0.9) / entry, and available_usd IS populated for Alpaca — coordinator.py:1495 calls AlpacaClient.buying_power(), which prefers regt_buying_power (the OVERNIGHT figure, correct for these swing legs). VERIFIED BY SIMULATION, not by reading: position_size at balance=available=$2,500, whole_units=True — a TLT-like leg with a 0.5% stop computes a risk-based 114.94 sh ($10,000 = 400% of account) and the sizer RETURNS 25 sh ($2,175 = 87.0%); SPY at a 1.0% stop 7.81 sh (200%) -> 3 sh (76.8%); GLD at 2.0% 8.06 sh (100%) -> 7 sh (86.8%). SO THE REAL DEFECT IS NOT REJECTION, IT IS TWO THINGS AT ONCE, IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. (a) CONCENTRATION: one leg is clamped to ~87% of buying power, so the first leg to fire consumes the account and the other 15 size to near zero — first-come-first-served, not a portfolio. (b) THE RISK MODEL SILENTLY STOPS GOVERNING: the clamped TLT trade risks 25 x $0.435 = $10.88 = 0.44% of a $2,500 account against a declared risk_pct of 2%. The account is simultaneously over-concentrated in notional and under-risked per trade, from the same clamp. WHAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED: the scale-invariance (notional = balance x risk_pct / stop_distance_pct, so more funding does not change the percentage), the absence of any max_gross_exposure_pct, and the live $199,697 / $168,166 observation on the paper mirrors — those accounts have the buying power, so nothing clamped them. Severity stays critical; the resolution criteria are unchanged (declare an exposure bound). The failure MODE in the title and detail is what was wrong, and a fix aimed at 'stop the venue rejecting orders' would have been aimed at a problem this account does not have.

items.evidence_measured_2026_08_24: INDEPENDENTLY RE-MEASURED in the /system-review session, because the row carried a claim with no numeric basis recorded. Method: for each alpaca_live-routed leg that currently holds a live position on a sibling alpaca book, take the ACTUAL declared entry and stopLoss from /api/bot/positions and compute notional/equity = risk_pct / stop_pct. alpaca_live's accounts.yaml risk block declares risk_per_trade_pct 0.02. Result (5 of the 6 measurable legs exceed whole-account notional): spy_pullback_1h stop 0.162% -> 12.37x; qqq_pullback_1h 0.324% -> 6.17x; tlt_pullback_1d 0.705% -> 2.84x; ief_pullback_1d 0.868% -> 2.30x; slv_trend_1h 1.614% -> 1.24x; iwm_trend_long_1d 3.491% -> 0.57x (the one that is fine). CONFIRMS the row's scale-invariance claim: the ratio has no equity term, so a deposit of ANY size leaves it unchanged - a $10,000 deposit would have spy_pullback_1h attempt a $123,700 position.
items.operator_decision_2026_08_24: Operator elected 'fund it and go live' in the /system-review session. This row is a BLOCKER on that: funding without a declared bound puts real money behind the sizing above. Sequence recorded in BL-20260824-ALPACA-LIVE-GOLIVE-SEQUENCE.

updates.note:
RE-GRADED critical -> high, 2026-08-25, operator-directed ('keep it dry_run, fix blockers first'). THE PREMISE THESE ROWS READ ON IS WRONG IN ONE RESPECT: alpaca_live is `mode: dry_run` (config/accounts.yaml:825, SHELVED 2026-07-15, Tier-3) with `account_class: real_money`. So its refusals are the execution gate WORKING, not a fault — the same finding BL-20260824-SILENT-REFUSAL-CANNOT-SEE-A-DECLARED-DRY-RUN made for this exact account one day later. Three rows at CRITICAL describing a switched-off account as a live emergency is itself the desensitized-alarm P1: an operator scanning criticals sees three fires on a box that is off. They are GO-LIVE PRECONDITIONS, which is what `high` is for.

THE RE-ARM GATE IS ALREADY DEFINED AND WAS NOT CITED BY ANY OF THESE ROWS. config/accounts.yaml:828 states it: re-arming to live is 'gated on the /performance-review portfolio-vs-bybit benchmark (does a ready-for-live Alpaca portfolio improve risk-adjusted PnL, incl. via regime diversification, vs bybit-only?)'. That benchmark has not been run. It, not funding, is the answer to 'are we ready to go live'.

⚠️ I FORMED A HYPOTHESIS HERE AND MEASUREMENT REFUTED IT. Recording both, because the hypothesis was alarming and would have been acted on.

THE HYPOTHESIS: this row's arithmetic assumes `risk_pct 0.02`; config/accounts.yaml declares **0.05** (raised 2026-08-25, Tier-3: 'because this account is still a small demonstration account, we can raise the risk threshold to 5% of account per trade'). Since the row shows notional/balance is balance-INDEPENDENT and linear in risk_pct, a 2.5x raise should multiply every percentage by 2.5 — tlt_pullback_1h from 414% to ~1115%, and '7 of 15 legs over 100%' to 13 of 15. I reproduced the row's own numbers at 0.02 over the COMPLETE population (319 of 319 rows, filter_state=applied, vs the row's 40-per-leg cap) and got 446% / 248% / 218% against its 414% / 254% / 218% — so the row's figures ARE 0.02-based and the ratio scaling is real.

THE REFUTATION: the ratio never MATERIALISES at this account's actual funding. The config block itself instructs 'the sizer is authoritative' over hand arithmetic, so I ran RiskManager.position_size(whole_units=True) at the recorded $200 equity, at both 0.02 and 0.05, on median journal entry/stop per leg:
  * MAX notional across all 15 legs is $171 on a $200 account — 86%. NOT ONE leg reaches even the cash balance, let alone Reg-T 2x ($400).
  * Reachable set is 8 legs at 0.02 and 8 legs at 0.05 — IDENTICAL, exactly as the config block claims.
  * Only two legs grow at all: iaum_pullback_1d 2 -> 4 shares, slv_pullback_1d 1 -> 2.
WHY: on a whole-unit venue a share of TLT is $83.44, so a $200 account buys 2 regardless of what the risk budget permits. WHOLE-SHARE GRANULARITY AND CASH BIND LONG BEFORE risk_pct DOES. My 2.5x alarm was arithmetic on a ratio the sizer never reaches.

SO THIS ROW IS RE-SCOPED, NOT RETIRED. 'Exceeds account notional at EVERY funding level' is true at the $2,500 / $10,000 / $25,000 the row modelled and FALSE at the $200 the account actually holds. It is a FUNDING-GATED blocker that starts biting at roughly the funding level the row itself identifies as the fix for the refusals ($2,500) — which is a sharper and more useful statement than the original, because it names the exact moment the two blockers cross.

AND THE REMEDY IS NOT WHAT IT LOOKS LIKE. A per-trade notional cap DOES NOT EXIST AND MUST NOT BE RE-PROPOSED: src/units/accounts/risk.py:24 records that `pos_size` / `POSITION_SIZE_CAP` were REMOVED by operator directive 2026-06-24 for capping 'a correctly risk-sized trade on a number unrelated to account capacity'. The sanctioned instrument is `max_gross_exposure_pct` (risk.py:359) — a MULTIPLE OF THE ACCOUNT'S OWN EQUITY, which risk.py:336-344 argues explicitly passes the test that directive set. It is default-0 (no ceiling) and NO account declares one today. ⚠️ Choosing a VALUE is gated: the gross-exposure governance design forbids shipping one with no soak behind it, and a dry_run account with 1 closed trade in 319 cannot produce a distribution. That chicken-and-egg is the real open question here, and it is stated rather than papered over.

ONE CORRECTION TO THE CONFIG BLOCK, offered as input-dependent rather than as a defect. It enumerates the raise's effect as '(b) sizes grow where the budget was the binding term — IAUM 2 -> 4 shares. Nothing else moves: TLT/IEF/SLV/USO are capped by whole-share granularity and cash, not by risk.' Measured, slv_pullback_1d moves 1 -> 2 (slv_trend_1h is indeed unchanged at 3), so 'SLV' holds for one SLV leg and not the other. CAVEAT: I used MEDIAN journal entry/stop and the block used yfinance prices + ATR14 stop proxies, so a marginal leg can legitimately differ between the two inputs. Worth a re-check on the block's own inputs before treating the enumeration as wrong.

RE-CONFIRMED WITH A LIVE INSTANCE: alpaca_portfolio holds SPY 207 shares at entry 771.50 — about $159,700 of notional against a $95,542.76 account, i.e. ~167% of equity in ONE position. That is the scale-invariance this row describes, observed rather than modelled. It is paper today; alpaca_live runs the same sizer.

items.title: the 16 strategies routed to alpaca_live are net-negative on paper except uso_trend_1h — and that one leg carries the entire positive result on n=10
items.detail:
FOUND answering the operator's pre-funding readiness question. This is the SHOULD-we half; the other two alpaca rows are the CAN-we half.

POPULATION 1 — paperPortfolio (the alpaca_portfolio mirror of alpaca_live), window=all: 51 trades, winRate 29.4%, totalPnl +1518.47, totalPnlMeasured +4298.07, pnlCoverage 0.549, profitFactor 1.0524, maxDrawdown -14995.42, expectancy 29.77. Restricted to the 16 routed legs: 21 trades, +2138.57 raw / +5548.89 measured — of which uso_trend_1h alone is +9204.34 on 5 trades. EVERY OTHER ROUTED LEG IN THAT BLOCK IS NEGATIVE (slv_trend_1h -3556.21, tlt_pullback_1h -2161.11, gld_pullback_1h -1092.78, spy_pullback_1h -221.14, qqq_trend_long_1d -17.44, qqq_pullback_1h -17.10). Net of uso_trend_1h the routed set is roughly -7065 on 16 trades.

POPULATION 2 — all paper (wider sample), window=all: 574 trades, winRate 37.8%, profitFactor 0.6674, maxDrawdown -115508.77. Restricted to the 16 routed legs: 76 trades, -6909.13 raw / -39.30 measured. 10 of the 11 legs with data are net negative; uso_trend_1h (+8822.10 on 10 trades, coverage 0.90) is the sole positive of size.

BOTH POPULATIONS AGREE ON THE SHAPE and are reported separately rather than pooled: one leg carries everything, the rest lose.

⚠️ READ THE COVERAGE BEFORE READING THE PNL. pnlCoverage is 0.549 (portfolio) and 0.3484 (all paper) — roughly a third to a half of the PnL is MEASURED, the rest is estimated/fabricated/unverified. Several routed legs report coverage 0.00 (gld_pullback_1h, qqq_trend_long_1d, iwm_trend_long_1d, ief_pullback_1d), so their measured contribution is 0 and we genuinely know nothing about them. Low coverage is a reason for LESS confidence in going live, never more.

SCALE CHECK: the portfolio mirror's maxDrawdown is -14995 and all-paper -115508, against a proposed real-money funding of roughly $2,500-$25,000. Even proportionally scaled, the declared daily_usd 200 and max_dd_pct 0.05 would be tripped routinely.
items.resolution_criteria: Either the routed set shows a positive measured record on the alpaca_portfolio mirror at a coverage floor worth trusting, or the routing is narrowed to the legs that do. 'It is only paper so it does not count' is NOT sufficient — the portfolio mirror exists precisely to be the pre-live evidence.
items.notes: Tier-3 (live promotion), proposed NOT applied. TUNE BEFORE DEMOTE is canonical and applies: no leg here has had a genuine multi-axis tuning attempt on this account, so nothing is proposed for demotion — the proposal is to withhold REAL MONEY, which is a different decision from killing a leg. A defensible narrow go-live exists if the operator wants a live-pipeline test sooner: fund and route ONLY uso_trend_1h (100% long in the 32-package sample so the shorting blocker does not bite, the sole profitable leg, the best-measured at coverage 0.90, and 88-90% account notional which is the sanest of the fifteen). Caveat stated plainly: n=10 is thin and one leg is not a portfolio.

updates.note:
RE-MEASURED TWO DAYS ON (/api/bot/performance?window=all, read direct over the Caddy host). THE SHAPE HELD AND THE EVIDENCE GOT WEAKER, NOT STRONGER.

POPULATION 1 - paperPortfolio, window=all: headline 58 trades, winRate 31.0, totalPnl -1517.45, totalPnlMeasured +1258.83, pnlCoverage 0.3621, profitFactor 0.9549, maxDrawdown -14995.42. Note the headline totalPnl has FLIPPED SIGN since 2026-08-23 (+1518.47 -> -1517.45) and profitFactor has crossed below 1 (1.0524 -> 0.9549) - the mirror as a whole is no longer positive. Restricted to the 16 routed legs: 23 trades, +2169.32 raw / +5576.32 measured, of which uso_trend_1h alone is +9207.67 on 6 trades. EX-USO the routed set is -7038.34 raw / -3628.02 measured on n=17.

POPULATION 2 - all paper, window=all: headline 612 trades, winRate 38.4, pnlCoverage 0.1928. Restricted to the routed legs: 79 trades, -6856.25 raw / +10.26 measured. Ten of the eleven legs with rows are net negative; uso_trend_1h (+8825.42 on 11, coverage 0.4545) is the sole positive of size. EX-USO: -15681.68 raw / -8768.20 measured on n=68.

SLV_TREND_1H IS NOW execution: shadow (the 2026-08-24 demotion held, verified in config/strategies.yaml), so the FORWARD routed set is 15 legs, not 16, and its rows above are historical. Excluding it changes nothing that matters: paperPortfolio ex-slv ex-uso is -3509.57 raw / -785.43 measured on n=9, and all-paper ex-slv ex-uso is -9574.67 raw / -4553.35 measured on n=45. Both still negative. One leg still carries the whole result.

WHAT CHANGED IN TWO DAYS IS ALMOST NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. The routed set gained 2 trades on the mirror and 3 on all-paper; uso gained one trade worth +3.33. A roster whose live-readiness case rests on n=6 for its only profitable leg accrued one trade in two days - at that rate the evidence the resolution_criteria asks for is months away, not days.

COVERAGE FELL ON BOTH POPULATIONS: paperPortfolio 0.549 -> 0.3621 and all-paper 0.3484 -> 0.1928. The population grew while the measured fraction shrank, so the pnl figures above are LESS trustworthy than the ones this row was opened with, not more. Read that in the direction the row already states: low coverage argues for less confidence in going live, never more.

VERDICT: resolution_criteria NOT met. The routed set does not show a positive measured record at any coverage worth trusting. The narrow-go-live option in `notes` (fund and route ONLY uso_trend_1h) is the only reading this measurement supports, and it is now thinner-looking than when it was written, not less.

Re-validated: 16 strategies net-negative on paper except uso_trend_1h, which carries the whole set. A go-live decision resting on one leg's paper performance is exactly the kind of thin evidence this review flagged elsewhere. Part of the alpaca_live go-live cluster. Live state this review: alpaca_live reads balance $200.10, api_ok true, ZERO open positions, and zero gross notional across 1,848 exposure_soak samples. HEAD of main also carries 'Confirm the $200 alpaca_live sizing wall'. Tier-3 and the operator's; nothing a review can drain.

items.opened_by: claude (implementing the operator's long-only disposition for alpaca_live)
items.tier: 3 (config/strategies.yaml is operator-gated; a per-account side gate is new order-path code)
items.title: side_filter is per-STRATEGY, so making alpaca_live long-only also suppresses shorts on the paper soak book, the portfolio mirror, and ib_paper — there is no per-account side gate
items.detail:
BLOCKS the operator's 2026-08-23 Tier-3 disposition ("for alpaca, only long trades with short proxies"). The mechanism to express long-only ALREADY EXISTS and needs no new code: config/strategies.yaml carries `side_filter: long|short|both` (legacy `long_only: true` -> `long`), resolved by strategy_signal_builders._resolve_side_filter and enforced with a journalled `short_suppressed_long_only` refusal. Five alpaca_live legs already use it.

THE PROBLEM IS SCOPE, NOT MECHANISM. side_filter is keyed on the STRATEGY, and a strategy is routed to MANY accounts. Measured against config/accounts.yaml + config/strategies.yaml on 2026-08-23, every one of the 11 'both' legs alpaca_live routes is ALSO routed elsewhere:
  - all 11 -> alpaca_paper (the ML soak book, which trades the full roster precisely to accrue data)
  - 9 of 11 -> alpaca_portfolio (the live-portfolio mirror)
  - tlt_pullback_1d -> ib_paper as well
  - slv_trend_1h / slv_pullback_1d / gdx_pullback_1d -> alpaca_options_paper as well

So `side_filter: long` on those 11 legs is NOT an alpaca_live change. It is a fleet change that: (a) correctly makes alpaca_portfolio long-only, which is right because that account exists to mirror alpaca_live; and (b) PERMANENTLY STOPS the paper soak book from accruing short-side data on 11 legs — which is exactly the evidence needed to decide whether the short proxies are worth building, and whether long-only is the right call at all. Turning off the measurement that would grade the decision is the wrong order of operations.

TWO WAYS FORWARD, and they are not equivalent:
  A. Accept the collateral — config-only, Tier-3, one edit, and the soak loses the short side on 11 legs.
  B. Add a per-account side gate — e.g. an account-level `side_filter` in accounts.yaml folded into the same resolution the strategy-level key already feeds, so a strategy can be long-only on one account and both-sides on another. New code on the signal path (Tier-2/3), but it keeps the soak intact AND generalises: the same gap will recur the next time any account needs a direction policy its strategies do not share.

RECOMMENDATION: B. The cost is one gate; the cost of A is the dataset that grades the decision.

⚠️ NOT A REASON TO FLIP THE ACCOUNT LIVE EITHER WAY — see the sibling rows: the account still has no gross-exposure bound (BL-20260823-ALPACA-RISK-SIZING-EXCEEDS-ACCOUNT-NOTIONAL-AT-EVERY-FUNDING-LEVEL, whose failure mode is corrected in its progress log), both silent-failure detectors skip it (BL-20260823-ALPACA-LIVE-IS-EXEMPT-FROM-BOTH-DETECTORS-THAT-WATCH-IT), and the proxies the disposition depends on do not exist (BL-20260823-NO-INVERSE-ETF-INSTRUMENTS-DECLARED).
items.resolution_criteria: Either (A) the operator accepts the fleet-wide collateral and the 11 legs are declared `side_filter: long` in one Tier-3 PR, with the soak-data loss recorded in the PR body and a note on each affected leg; or (B) a per-account side gate ships and alpaca_live/alpaca_portfolio declare `long` while alpaca_paper keeps `both`, verified by a test that the SAME strategy resolves different side_filters on two accounts and by a live `short_suppressed_long_only` refusal appearing for alpaca_live and NOT for alpaca_paper on the same signal.
items.notes: Population for the routing claim: config/accounts.yaml as of 40d5a787, all declared accounts, every strategy in alpaca_live's 16-leg list cross-referenced against every other account's `strategies` list. Not a sample.

items.opened_by: claude (found while verifying what alpaca sizing actually does before the funding decision)
items.title: A trade sized to its intended risk and a trade clamped to the margin ceiling are indistinguishable from the stored row — the collapsed state is 'which term bound the size'
items.detail:
The `margin_basis` stamp added 2026-08-13 (Part B) records the basis INPUTS — kind, basis_usd, leverage, buffer, max_qty_by_margin — and it is a real improvement. What it does not record is the VERDICT: whether the returned qty came from the risk model or from the margin clamp. The branch that decides is `if qty > max_qty_by_margin:` in risk.py, and nothing downstream of it says which way it went.

WHY THAT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING PEDANTIC. The two states have opposite meanings for every downstream reader:
  - risk-bound  -> the trade carries the declared risk_pct, and R is the unit the analytics assume.
  - margin-bound -> the declared risk_pct DID NOT GOVERN. Measured by simulation on 2026-08-23 at a $2,500 alpaca-like account: a TLT-like leg with a 0.5% stop clamps 114.94 sh -> 25 sh, so the realised risk is $10.88 = 0.44% of equity against a declared 2%. Every per-trade R, expectancy and risk-adjusted figure computed over that row silently assumes the 2%.

A consumer CAN in principle re-derive it by comparing the stored `max_qty_by_margin` to the filled qty — but that is a reconstruction, it is pre-flooring (the stored ceiling is not the whole-share value actually used), and it is absent entirely on the futures branch where the crypto cap is deliberately skipped. Re-derivation by every consumer is exactly the shape `provenance.py` exists to stop.

THIS IS THE ORDINARY CASE ON A SMALL ACCOUNT, NOT AN EDGE CASE. On the alpaca_live funding levels under discussion, 7 of 15 priced legs compute a risk-based notional above 100% of the account, so the clamp is the binding term on nearly half the roster — the majority state would be the unlabelled one.
items.resolution_criteria: position_size records a never-collapsed size basis alongside the existing margin_basis — at minimum `risk_bound` / `margin_bound` / `not_applicable` (the futures branch, where no cap is computed: we did not look, which is not 'risk governed') / `unknown` — persisted on the trade row, registered with collapsed-state-guard, and read by at least one consumer. A stamp with no reader reproduces the exact defect `provenance-consumer-guard` was built for. No change to the arithmetic: the label must never be able to move the number, the same discipline the margin_basis kind already follows.
items.notes: Verified by running position_size directly rather than by reading the branch: three (entry, stop) pairs at balance=available=$2,500, whole_units=True. Reported as 3 of 3 simulated cases clamped, which is a demonstration that the path is reachable and binding — not a distribution over live trades.

updates.note: Re-validated: a risk-sized trade and a margin-clamped trade are indistinguishable in the stored row. This is the measurement gap behind PB-20260822-AVAX-SCALP-SIZED-OFF-MARGIN-NOT-RISK — the claim can only be made by reconstructing, not by reading. CLAUDE.md records notes.margin_basis being stamped (Part B), so the field may now exist; whether it disambiguates is BL-20260813-MARGIN-BASIS-ABSENCE-IS-A-COLLAPSED-STATE.

items.opened_by: claude (scoping the operator's 'short proxies' disposition for alpaca)
items.tier: 3 (new instruments + new strategy legs + per-account compat matrix)
items.title: The 'short proxies' half of the alpaca disposition has no substrate — zero inverse ETFs are declared, and the four legs that most need one are in the metals complex where no clean 1x inverse exists
items.detail:
The operator's 2026-08-23 disposition is long-only WITH short proxies. The long-only half has a mechanism (side_filter, blocked on scope — see BL-20260823-ALPACA-LONG-ONLY-CANNOT-BE-SCOPED-TO-ONE-ACCOUNT). The proxy half has nothing yet.

MEASURED: config/instruments.yaml declares 25 instruments and NONE is inverse. The only leveraged products present (QLD, TQQQ) are leveraged LONG. So each proxy is a new instrument + a new strategy leg + intent-multiplexer registration + backtest evidence + a per-account account_compat_matrix run, per the `new-strategy` skill. This is multi-session work, not a config line.

⚠️ AND THE PROXY MAPPING IS NOT UNIFORM ACROSS THE BOOK — this is the part that should shape the plan. The eight symbols carrying short flow split into two groups:
  - Broad index / rates, where a 1x unlevered inverse ETF is a genuine substitute: SPY, QQQ, TLT, IEF.
  - The METALS complex — GLD, IAUM, SLV, GDX — where the commonly available inverse products are 2x daily-rebalanced funds or ETNs. Neither is the same trade: a daily-rebalanced 2x fund is path-dependent and decays against a multi-day hold (every one of these legs is 1d or 1h swing), and an ETN carries issuer credit risk rather than tracking the underlying. Substituting one for a short is a DIFFERENT position, not a proxy.

AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHERE THE SHORT FLOW IS CONCENTRATED. Of the four legs long-only makes completely inert, THREE are metals (gld_pullback_1d 8/8 short, gdx_pullback_1d 7/7, iaum_pullback_1d 6/6) plus slv_pullback_1d (5/5); gld_pullback_1h is the most short-skewed volume leg at 38 of 51 (75%). So the group with a clean proxy is not the group that needs one most.

⚠️ THE SPECIFIC TICKERS ARE NOT ASSERTED HERE. I have not verified listing, liquidity, borrow, expense ratio or tracking for any candidate against a data source in this session — stating them as facts would be exactly the unprovenanced-diagnostic pattern. The structural claim (zero inverse instruments declared; the metals complex lacks a clean 1x) is what is filed; ticker selection is the first step of the work, with evidence.
items.resolution_criteria: Either each short-carrying symbol has a declared, backtested proxy leg that clears its account_compat_matrix on alpaca_live — with the instrument's liquidity and tracking verified against a source, and the 1x-vs-leveraged distinction resolved explicitly per symbol — or the symbols with no acceptable proxy are recorded as long-only-with-reduced-flow and their legs' expected contribution restated on that basis. A leg left nominally enabled while structurally inert is the state to avoid: it reads as coverage and produces nothing.
items.notes: Flow figures are over 100% of the order_packages table (3,984 rows, 2026-05-02..2026-08-23), not a sample. Instrument count is config/instruments.yaml at 40d5a787.

USABLE -1x ETFs (broad index + rates): SPY->SH (ProShares Short S&P500, -1x, ER 0.89%, ~$1B AUM); QQQ->PSQ (Short QQQ, -1x, ER 0.95%, $759M as of 2026-07-31); TLT->TBF (Short 20+ Yr Treasury, -1x, ER 0.95%, $80M); IEF->TBX (Short 7-10 Yr Treasury, -1x, ER 0.95%, $14M -- THIN, flag before use).

updates.state: DESIGN CHOSEN + EVIDENCE GATE SET — build not started, by design
updates.note:
DESIGN: 'mirror legs on index data'. A proxy leg computes its signal on the PARENT index candles (SPY/QQQ) exactly as the parent does, and emits a LONG order on the proxy (SH/PSQ) where the parent would have gone SHORT. Chosen over (a) translating at routing -- rejected because it edits the order path the new-strategy skill explicitly fences off and makes one strategy behave differently per account, which is hard to backtest -- and over (b) cloning the pullback logic onto the ETF's OWN price series, rejected because that is a DIFFERENT signal: trend/pullback-trading a decaying inverse instrument is what docs/research/leveraged-etf-research-2026-06-30.md measured at -7R to -17R.
NOTE THE NEW PATTERN THIS INTRODUCES: signal symbol != order symbol. No existing leg does this. It is the part of the wiring most likely to be got wrong -- per-strategy `symbols:` scope, intent-layer symbol validation (supported_symbols()), and the monitor's candle fetch all key on symbol.
EVIDENCE GATE: run the backtest FIRST, build only if it clears. Per the new-strategy skill the edge is decided OFFLINE before any soak; a soak is a MECHANICS check, never the edge. The backtest must carry the 0.89-0.95% expense ratio AND the daily-rebalance drift INSIDE it, not as a footnote.
updates.measured_basis: The flow at stake, measured over all 4,029 order_packages (whole history): the four SPY/QQQ legs alpaca_live routes produced 136 packages, 79 of them SHORT (58.1%) -- qqq_pullback_1h 40 of 63 (63.5%), spy_pullback_1h 39 of 70 (55.7%). The two *_trend_long_1d legs produced 3 packages total, ZERO short, so they are irrelevant to this work despite carrying side_filter: both. So SH+PSQ would recover ~79 packages of historical flow, i.e. the whole build serves TWO legs, not four.

The previous update's `remaining` opened with 'NEXT CONCRETE STEP: obtain SH + PSQ daily/hourly history'. Done, and the step was SMALLER than the handoff said.

⚠️ FIRST, A CORRECTION INHERITED FROM #10247's commit message, which said 'there is NO equity/yfinance fetcher in this repo -- scripts/ops/fetch_backtest_candles.py is Bybit-only' and therefore that 'the first build item is the data path (a yfinance equity OHLCV fetcher on a GitHub runner), not the backtest itself'. The gap was TWO map entries.

SHIPPED (PR #10251, Tier-1): SH + PSQ added to the ticker map, 20 -> 22 entries, plus tests that make the research-only claim FALSIFIABLE rather than a comment -- `test_the_inverse_proxies_are_not_yet_tradeable` measures their absence from config/instruments.yaml and config/strategies.yaml and is written to go RED when the Tier-3 build declares them, which is the signal to update it in the wiring PR. Control planted (`SH:` added to instruments.yaml): the test went red, then clean on restore.

MEASURED ON A REAL NETWORK, both symbols, `yfinance-lane-proof` on the PR branch, runs 32819916112 (SH) and 32819923567 (PSQ), 07:05Z, --interval 60 --days 1000:
  SH  -> rows=3456, span=726 d, 2024-08-28 -> 2026-08-24
  PSQ -> rows=3456, span=726 d, 2024-08-28 -> 2026-08-24
Identical, which is the consistency check worth having (same exchange calendar, same cap). 3,456 RTH hourly bars is consistent with ~2y x ~252 sessions x 6.5h, so this is a real book, not a padded one.

⚠️ **THE 1h WINDOW IS 726 DAYS, NOT 'ABOUT TWO YEARS OF WHATEVER WE ASK FOR' -- AND THIS IS THE BACKTEST'S BINDING CONSTRAINT.** 1000 d were requested; 726 came back, and the lane ANNOUNCED the truncation ('treat this as a PARTIAL window') rather than returning a short book silently. Both legs at stake -- `qqq_pullback_1h` and `spy_pullback_1h` -- are 1h, so the whole evidence base for this decision is 726 days per symbol. State that span whenever the result is quoted; a walk-forward split over 726 d has materially less OOS than one over the 1d history, and `YF_MAX_HISTORY_DAYS['1d']` is None (uncapped) if the design ever moves to daily.

STILL NOT DONE, and deliberately: the backtest itself. Per this row's own evidence gate the edge is decided OFFLINE before anything is built, and the 0.89%/0.95% expense ratios AND the daily-rebalance drift must sit INSIDE it. Also not yet verified: that the SIGNAL series (SPY/QQQ 1h) and the ORDER series (SH/PSQ 1h) align bar-for-bar over this window.
