updates.state: MEASURED — THE SIGNAL AND ORDER SERIES ARE NOT BAR-ALIGNED. The previous update listed this as unverified; it is now verified, and it is NOT clean.
updates.note:
The previous update flagged, as an assumption not yet measured, that the SIGNAL series (SPY/QQQ 1h) and the ORDER series (SH/PSQ 1h) 'share a calendar so they should' align. Measured. THEY DO NOT, for one of the two pairs.

All four fetched identically parameterised (`--source yfinance --interval 60 --days 1000`), same runner image, within three minutes of each other:
  SPY -> rows=3456  span=726 d  2024-08-28 -> 2026-08-24  (run 32820090931)
  SH  -> rows=3456  span=726 d  2024-08-28 -> 2026-08-24  (run 32819916112)
  QQQ -> rows=3457  span=726 d  2024-08-28 -> 2026-08-24  (run 32820098141)
  PSQ -> rows=3456  span=726 d  2024-08-28 -> 2026-08-24  (run 32819923567)

**QQQ carries ONE MORE hourly bar than PSQ over a byte-identical date range.** One bar in 3,457 is a rounding error in size and decisive in kind: a difference in COUNT is positive proof the two frames are not the same index. Whatever that extra bar is -- a halt, a late-print, an auction bar Yahoo carries for the more heavily traded name -- the mirror-leg design reads the signal off one frame and fills on the other, so it must join them.

⚠️ **THE BINDING REQUIREMENT THIS CREATES: the backtest MUST join signal to order bars ON TIMESTAMP, never by row position and never by zipping two frames assumed parallel.** A positional join over these two frames silently shifts every bar after the extra one by an hour -- and the result would look completely normal: right number of trades, plausible PnL, no error. That is the failure this measurement exists to prevent, and it would have been invisible in the output.

⚠️ **AND DO NOT READ SPY/SH's MATCHING COUNT AS ALIGNMENT.** 3456 == 3456 is consistent with identical timestamps and equally consistent with two offsetting gaps. Equal counts cannot prove equal indices; unequal counts CAN disprove them, which is the only direction this measurement runs. SPY/SH alignment is therefore still UNVERIFIED, not clean -- and since the join must be on timestamp regardless, it does not need to be verified separately so much as never assumed.

One more consequence for how the result gets quoted: the two legs no longer share a denominator. `spy_pullback_1h` would be backtested over 3,456 bars and `qqq_pullback_1h` over 3,457 signal bars against 3,456 fillable ones. Trivial numerically; it means the per-leg n must be stated per leg rather than as one figure for the pair.

updates.state: THE DESIGN COLLIDES WITH A SYSTEM-WIDE INVARIANT — two blockers, one correctness break, one operator question. Full map: docs/research/alpaca-proxy-signal-vs-order-symbol-2026-08-25.md
updates.note:
The design update flagged 'signal symbol != order symbol ... the part of the wiring most likely to be got wrong'. Measured. IT IS STRONGER THAN THAT. The repo carries one unbroken invariant end to end -- tick == candle == signal == intent == order-package == monitor-fetch symbol -- and there is NO place in the live path where a signal symbol and an order symbol exist as two variables. The design does not extend the system; it introduces a distinction the system does not have. Every site below was READ and is cited to file:line in the doc.

BLOCKER 1 -- the intent aggregator DROPS a cross-symbol intent, and the emitter OVERWRITES the symbol. `intents.py:1265-1268` filters `if i.symbol == norm_symbol` (documented rule: 'the aggregator never mixes symbols'), so an SH intent on a SPY tick is silently dropped; and `intent_multiplexer.py:684,:718` stamps the TICK symbol onto the outgoing signal, discarding `winning_intent.symbol`, so even a surviving intent would order SPY. `aggregate_intents` runs for EVERY strategy on EVERY tick -- changing its symbol rule is a change to core routing for the whole fleet, not a new leg.

BLOCKER 2 -- `supported_symbols()` (`intents.py:127`) validates against **accounts.yaml, never strategies.yaml**, and `StrategyIntent.__post_init__` (`:542`) RAISES for an undeclared symbol. The raise lands inside `_collect_intents`'s per-strategy isolation, so the leg is SILENTLY SKIPPED rather than failing loudly. Tractable, but accounts.yaml is Tier-3.

⚠️ CORRECTNESS BREAK -- THE MONITOR WOULD RE-EVALUATE THE EXIT ON THE WRONG SERIES. `order_monitor.py:10001-10005` fetches candles for `normalised.get('symbol')` -- the ORDER PACKAGE's symbol, not the trade row's and not the strategy config's. So a SPY-signalled / SH-ordered leg would have its monitor() -- Donchian channel, ADX, ATR trail -- recomputed on SH candles, an INVERSELY CORRELATED series, while its entry geometry was computed on SPY. A channel breakout on SPY is a breakdown on SH; the trail would trail the wrong way. NOTHING WOULD ERROR. This is the one that runs, produces output, and is wrong.
  ⚠️ AND IT IS A HOLE IN THE DESIGN, NOT JUST THE WIRING: the design says where the signal comes from and where the order goes, and is SILENT on what the EXIT re-evaluates on. The backtest will assume an answer -- and the natural assumption (evaluate the exit on the SPY series that produced the entry) is the OPPOSITE of what the live monitor does. Decide it explicitly before writing the backtest or the backtest measures a system nobody would build.

OPERATOR QUESTION -- `side_filter: long` STOPS SEEING THE SHORT, and that is the design working, not a bug. `account_side_filter` is keyed on ACCOUNT ONLY and is applied to `pkg.direction` (`coordinator.py:1322-1328`); under the mirror design 'short SPY' has already become 'long SH' before it looks. So the gate PERMITS the inverse expression of exactly the flow it was added to suppress -- which is the point of a proxy. What changes is what the guarantee MEANS: today 'alpaca_live is long-only' bounds the instrument side AND the economic exposure; with proxies it bounds ONLY the instrument side, because a long SH IS short-SPY exposure. Two readers will not notice: `portfolio_conflicts.py:133,:152` groups by symbol, so a long SPY beside a long SH reads as two unrelated longs rather than an offsetting pair; and `risk.py:1166`/`:543` sum open notional `WHERE symbol = ?`, so SPY and SH are two independent exposure budgets for one directional bet. **Worth answering BEFORE the backtest: is long-only meant to bound the instrument side only, or the economic exposure? If the latter, the proxy programme needs a netting rule that sees SPY and SH as one book -- nothing currently does.**

COST IMPLICATION FOR THE DESIGN CHOICE: alternative (a) 'translate at routing' was rejected partly because it edits the order path the new-strategy skill fences off. Blockers 1-2 plus the monitor mean the CHOSEN design also requires changes to shared routing code, so that particular argument no longer separates them. Not a counter-proposal -- the operator's reasons stand -- just cost information the decision did not have.

NOT CHECKED, stated so it is not read as covered: not all 32 pattern-A builders were read in full (3 were; the identical symbol line was confirmed at the other 29 offsets); and the pairs sleeve was not traced.
Re-validated: the 'short proxies' half of the alpaca disposition has no substrate — zero inverse ETFs declared. So the proposed remedy for the shorting gap does not currently exist.

items.opened_by: claude (operator sent a Breakout terminal History screenshot; reconciled it against the prop journal)
items.tier: 1 (measurement + a detector; any writeback to prop_fills is Tier-2)
items.title: The prop PnL series MIXES gross and net-of-commission rows with nothing marking which — CONFIRMED to the cent against the venue's own commission field
items.detail:
The operator sent the Breakout terminal's own History view (window 23/07/26-23/08/26). Reconciled against /api/bot/prop/fills, paired on symbol+qty, which is UNIQUE for all six round trips in the window.

GOOD NEWS FIRST: all six are PRESENT in the journal. There is no missing-trade gap in this window — BL-20260823-PROP-JOURNAL-MISSING-THREE-DAYS-OF-TERMINAL-TRADES was about reporting latency, and the rows did land. Note also that neither source shows ANY trade between 08-20 and 08-22, so that 'three-day gap' had no trades in it to lose.

THE PROBLEM IS THE VALUES.
  trade            venue     journal    delta
  ETH 2.00  08-23  -103.12   -107.02    +3.90
  SOL 20.00 08-23  -110.20   -111.77    +1.57
  SOL 83.00 08-19  +247.34   +242.02    +5.32
  SOL 83.00 08-19    -0.83     -6.05    +5.22
  ETH 3.00  08-13   -50.55    -50.55    +0.00
  ETH 2.00  07-28   -18.06    -18.06    +0.00
  TOTAL            -35.42    -51.43    +16.01

TWO of six match TO THE CENT and they are the OLDEST two. FOUR disagree and they are the four most recent, with the journal MORE NEGATIVE in 4 of 4 — a consistent direction, not scatter. The journal under-records by $16.01 over six trades.

⚠️ AND THIS FALSIFIES A CLAIM IN CLAUDE.md. The PROP_FILLS_STALENESS row argues detector B must NOT require the fills to RECONCILE with the balance delta, citing: 'the 2026-08-19 pair moved +$245.00 against +$235.97 of reported fills ... both correct-and-explained, and a reconciliation test would have called both a finding.' That +235.97 is EXACTLY the journal's figure for the two 08-19 SOL closes (242.02 - 6.05). The venue's own figure is +246.51, which sits $1.51 from the +245.00 balance delta — plausibly fees. The journal sits $9.03 away. So the reconciliation gap that was dismissed as explained IS the under-recording, and it was visible in the existing data the whole time. The doc's REMEDY may still be right (a hard reconciliation test would be noisy, and an alert on operator answer-rate is the desensitized-alarm P1) — but its EVIDENCE is not: that example is a true positive, and it must stop being cited as a false one.

CAUSE NOT ESTABLISHED. Candidates, none verified: the journal's exit prices on the four disagreeing rows are suspiciously round (2402.0, 95.0, 81.5, 78.51) and may be the DECLARED bracket level rather than the actual fill; or fees are handled differently by the two sources; or the screenshot-parse path rounds. I did not test any of these. What is established is the direction, the magnitude, and that two rows match exactly — which rules out a uniform systematic offset.

POPULATION: 6 round trips, the complete set visible in one screenshot of a 1-month window. Screenshot rows carry no visible timestamps, so the pairing is by symbol+qty (unique here) and not by id. Small n, and the operator's own terminal is the reference.
items.resolution_criteria: Every prop fill row carries an explicit, never-collapsed pnl BASIS — at minimum `gross` / `net_of_commission` / `unknown` (we could not determine it — never silently folded into either) — and the value is derived, not assumed: `(exit - entry) x qty` reproduces gross from the row's own fields, so `stored_pnl - gross` IS the commission and the basis follows from whether that residual is ~0 or ~the venue's bps. Registered with collapsed-state-guard, and READ by at least one consumer (a stamp with no reader is the exact defect provenance-consumer-guard exists to catch). Any aggregate over prop rows must then state its basis or refuse to mix. NO writeback to the existing rows — they are not wrong, they are unlabelled. SEPARATELY: confirm with the operator when and why the reported basis changed around 2026-08-19, since that boundary is currently recorded nowhere and silently splits the series in two.
items.notes: Filed rather than fixed: correcting the four rows would be a Tier-2 writeback to prop_fills, and the cause is not established, so a writeback now would be guessing at values on a real-money book. The prop bridge has no broker feed, so the operator's terminal IS the only truth source — which is exactly why a divergence here is invisible unless someone looks.

progress.note:
⚠️ MY OWN DIAGNOSIS ABOVE IS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN. The row said the journal UNDER-RECORDS versus the venue. It does not. I went looking for the cause and the cause refutes the finding.

THE DECISIVE ARITHMETIC. Recompute gross PnL from the journal's OWN stored fields — (exit - entry) x qty for a long, (entry - exit) x qty for a short:
  ETH 08-23  2.0 @ 2453.56 -> 2402.0   = -103.12   (venue -103.12)
  SOL 08-23 20.0 @ 100.51  -> 95.0     = -110.20   (venue -110.20)
  SOL 08-19 83.0 @ 78.52   -> 81.5     = +247.34   (venue +247.34)
  SOL 08-19 83.0 @ 78.52   -> 78.51    =   -0.83   (venue   -0.83)
  ETH 08-13  3.0 @ 1874.34 -> 1891.19  =  -50.55   (venue  -50.55)
  ETH 07-28  2.0 @ 1884.03 -> 1875.0   =  -18.06   (venue  -18.06)
**The journal's stored PRICES reproduce the venue figure EXACTLY on all six.** The prices were never wrong; the screenshot and the journal agree completely about what happened.

SO THE DIVERGENCE IS ENTIRELY IN THE `pnl` FIELD, and it disagrees with the entry/exit prices sitting beside it IN THE SAME ROW. The deltas are not scatter — as a share of notional they are **-0.0795% / -0.0781% / -0.0816% / -0.0801%** on the four recent rows and **exactly 0.0000%** on the two older ones. A consistent ~8 bps round-trip deduction, i.e. a FEE, applied to rows from ~2026-08-19 onward and to none before.

WHERE IT COMES FROM: not from us. `src/prop/prop_report.py` has no fee arithmetic anywhere (grepped), so `pnl` is whatever the report supplied. The likeliest reading is that the terminal's collapsed History column shows GROSS while the value that reached the journal was NET — the operator's own screenshot is the gross view. That is a REPORTING-SOURCE change around 08-19, not a bug in the bot.

⚠️ AND MY CORRECTION OF CLAUDE.md IS WITHDRAWN TOO. I claimed the PROP_FILLS_STALENESS row's '+$245.00 balance vs +$235.97 fills, correct-and-explained' was a TRUE positive that the doc wrongly dismissed. That claim rested entirely on the under-recording premise, which is now refuted. On the fee reading the 08-19 pair is gross +246.51, fees -10.54, net +235.97 against a +245.00 balance delta — which reconciles to neither figure cleanly (1.51 off gross, 9.03 off net) and I CANNOT resolve it from here. So the honest position is: the doc's example is **not established as a false positive and not established as a true one**, and I should not have asserted the latter. `docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md` needs no edit on my account; the earlier PR body and the operator message that stated otherwise are corrected by this note.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS A BETTER FINDING THAN THE ONE I FILED: a prop row can carry a `pnl` that does not follow from its own `entry_price`/`exit_price`/`qty`, with NOTHING checking the two against each other. That inconsistency is INTERNAL — detectable with no screenshot, no venue call and no operator, by pure arithmetic over one row. Today it is benign (a fee). It would look identical if a reported pnl were simply wrong, and there is no surface on which the difference would show. It is also the prop analogue of what `src/runtime/provenance.py` exists to prevent on the money DB: a number whose derivation is unrecorded, sitting next to the inputs that contradict it.

PROCESS NOTE, because it is the point: the original finding LOOKED right — six trades, four disagreeing, all in one direction, a tidy $16.01. A consistent direction reads as a systematic bug. It was a systematic FEE. RULE ONE says verify your own output hardest when it confirms what you expected, and I expected an under-recording because a three-day reporting gap had already been filed against this bridge.

✅ FEE HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED TO THE CENT — no longer an inference. The operator sent the terminal's EXPANDED rows, which carry a separate `Commissions` field per fill, ID-matched:
  open  38033351:6237101  SOL Buy  83 @ 78.52  19/08 15:50  -2.61
  open  38033351:6237135  SOL Buy  83 @ 78.52  19/08 15:51  -2.61
  close 38033351:6237147  SOL Sell 83 @ 78.51  19/08 15:51  -2.61  (headline  -0.83)
  close 38033351:6265955  SOL Sell 83 @ 81.50  19/08 20:01  -2.71  (headline +247.34)

Pairing each round trip and comparing its total commission to the journal-vs-headline delta I measured earlier:
  78.52 -> 81.50 : commissions 2.61 + 2.71 = 5.32   my delta -5.32   **EXACT**
  78.52 -> 78.51 : commissions 2.61 + 2.61 = 5.22   my delta -5.22   **EXACT**
Rate: 2.61 / (78.52 x 83 = 6517.16) = 0.0400% per leg, 0.0801% round trip — inside the 0.0781-0.0816% band the four rows showed. So the terminal's HEADLINE column is GROSS (commissions are a separate field on the expanded row) and the journal's `pnl` on those rows is NET of the round trip.

⚠️ THE FINDING IS NOW SHARPER AND WORSE THAN 'THERE IS AN UNDOCUMENTED FEE'. The prop PnL series is **MIXED**: the four recent rows are NET of commission, the two older ones (2026-08-13, 2026-07-28) are GROSS — their deltas were exactly 0.0000%, and a 3-ETH and a 2-ETH round trip would have carried roughly $4.50 and $3.00 of commission had it been deducted. Nothing on a row says which basis it is on. So:
  - any SUM over prop rows is neither a gross nor a net figure, it is an unlabelled blend;
  - a per-trade comparison across the 08-19 boundary compares two different quantities;
  - and the difference is invisible, because both bases are plausible numbers of the right magnitude.
This is precisely the shape `src/runtime/provenance.py` exists to prevent on the money DB — a value whose derivation is unrecorded, sitting beside inputs that do not determine it — reproduced on the prop book, where there is no `provenance` module at all.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE: the four NET rows are not WRONG, and no writeback is warranted. Net-of-cost is arguably the better basis. The defect is the absence of a label, plus the silent change of basis around 2026-08-19.

AND THE MEASUREMENT NOW EXISTS WITHOUT A SCREENSHOT: `(exit - entry) x qty` from the row's own stored fields gives GROSS exactly; `stored_pnl - gross` gives the commission. Both are pure arithmetic over one row. The check in resolution_criteria is therefore implementable today against the existing table, with no venue call and no operator in the loop.

updates.note: Part of the prop cluster. Live: breakout_1 equity $4,755 against its $4,700 static-DD floor ($55.00 of cushion), daily-loss distance null, snapshot 0.9 h fresh, reconcile 84 tickets / 40 fills / 0 unacted. A PnL series mixing gross and net-of-commission rows with nothing marking which is a provenance defect on the one account that can be permanently killed — every cushion computation reads it.

items.opened_by: claude (nearly reported a false green on PR #10206 from a task-completion notification)
items.tier: 1 (session discipline + a note in the rules)
items.title: A background task's completion notification reports the PIPELINE's exit code, so `pytest … | tail` completes as 'exit code 0' while 12 tests are failing
items.detail:
CAUGHT AT THE MOMENT IT WOULD HAVE BECOME A FALSE CLAIM. I backgrounded `pytest tests/ -q 2>&1 | tail -6`. The completion notification read *"completed (exit code 0)"*. The captured output ended: **`12 failed, 12456 passed, 15 skipped in 472.88s`**.

Both are true. `tail` exited 0, so the PIPELINE exited 0; pytest exited 1 and that value was discarded by the pipe before anything could observe it. A reader who trusts the notification's rc — which is the natural thing to do, since it is presented as the command's result — concludes the suite passed.

THIS IS THE THIRD TIME IN ONE DAY that a pipe swallowed an exit code in this session, and the first two were already recorded as lessons (`... | tail -N && break` masking a guards failure, twice). The lesson did not generalise because it was learned as *"check the rc of run_guards.py"* rather than as *"a pipe replaces the exit code you care about with `tail`'s"*. The BACKGROUND case is the dangerous variant: with a foreground command the output is right there, whereas here the summary line was ALSO truncated away by the same `tail`, so the notification's green rc was the most authoritative-looking thing available.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT PROBLEM in the same incident: `| tail -6` meant the captured file was **529 bytes** and held only 5 of the 12 `FAILED` lines. So even after distrusting the rc, the evidence needed to triage was gone and the full 8-minute run had to be repeated. A background run's output should be captured WHOLE and read afterwards, never pre-filtered at capture time.

(For the record on this particular run, established by re-running rather than assumed: of the 5 visible failures, 4 `test_send_ping` cases PASS in isolation and fail only in the full-suite ordering — pre-existing test pollution — and `test_vm_health_helper` fails identically on `origin/main`, verified by stashing. None are attributable to the change under test.)
items.resolution_criteria: The rule is stated where a session will actually hit it — a line in `docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md` under the verification rules: a backgrounded or piped command's reported exit code is the LAST element of the pipeline, so redirect (`> file 2>&1`) and echo the real `$?` into the file rather than piping, and never pre-filter a long-running run's output at capture time. Resolution requires the rule to be written down, not merely remembered — this row exists because remembering it twice did not work.
items.notes: Filed rather than fixed in-session because the fix is a canonical-doc edit whose right wording belongs with the other RULE ONE verification clauses, and this session has already made four CLAUDE.md edits today; batching one more into an unrelated Tier-3 PR would bury it. No code change is implied — the shell behaviour is correct and documented; what is missing is the repo's own note that the harness surfaces it.

updates.note: Re-validated: `pytest … | tail` completing as exit 0 regardless of pytest's result. I avoided this today by reading pytest's own summary line rather than the pipeline rc — convention, not enforcement.

items.opened_by: claude (COMEX-reopen verification of MGC 4773, scheduled routine)
items.tier: 1 (provenance/measurement); a change to what the monitor records at close is Tier-2
items.title: The monitor's tp_cross close recorded an exit price that NEVER TRADED — a 49-hour-old candle close, graded `measured` and below the reopen candle's low
items.detail:
FOUND by a scheduled routine written specifically to distinguish OUTCOME from MECHANISM at the COMEX reopen. The position closing was NOT the question; which path closed it was.

MGC trade 4773, ib_paper (PAPER — no money impact), 95 long @ 4364.6, `ict_scalp_mgc_15m`. COMEX shut 2026-08-21T20:45Z, reopened 2026-08-23T22:00Z.

WHAT HAPPENED. Raw row: `exit_reason = tp_cross`, `exit_price = 4626.9`, `pnl = 249185.0`, `closed_at = 2026-08-23T22:00:32Z` (32s after reopen), `notes.exit_price_source = recorded_exit_price`, `notes.pnl_source = local_compute`, `sl_order_id`/`tp_order_id` both NULL. Broker confirms flat (`/api/diag/exchange_positions` shows only MHG + MES) and NO MGC leg rests (`/api/diag/ib_open_orders`) — so the close itself is sound and the OCA sibling was cleaned up. The DEFECT is the recorded price.

⚠️ 4626.9 NEVER TRADED AT THE REOPEN. From the bot's OWN candle feed (`/api/bot/candles?symbol=MGC&interval=15m`, source `bot-exchange` — the same feed the strategies read):
  2026-08-21T20:45  O 4630.9  H 4631.0  L 4625.5  C **4626.9**   <- the last bar before the shutdown
  2026-08-23T22:00  O 4635.6  H 4648.6  L **4631.0**  C 4634.3   <- the reopen bar
The recorded exit equals Friday's final close EXACTLY, and it sits **below the reopen bar's LOW (4631.0)** — so it cannot be a fill from the bar during which the trade closed. It is a 49-hour-old mark.

AND IT IS GRADED `measured`. `/api/bot/trades/closed` returns `pnlProvenance: "measured"` for this row, because `provenance.classify_pnl` treats `recorded_exit_price` as MEASURED ("a broker fill / RECORDED EXIT"). That vocabulary was written for a recorded exit that IS the fill. On the tp_cross path the recorded value can instead be the monitor's last-known close, which is a mark read at an arbitrary earlier time — the FABRICATED bucket's own definition. The repo already fixed the mirror-image of this in `order_monitor._sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced` ("a confirmed close is anchored to its `closed_at`, NEVER to a live mark") and built `src/runtime/exit_anchor.py` for it; the tp_cross close path appears not to use that machinery.

SIZE OF THE ERROR, stated as an estimate because the true fill is unread: against the reopen OPEN of 4635.6 the recorded PnL is understated by (4635.6 - 4626.9) x 95 x $10 = **~$8,265** on a $249,185 close (~3.3%). The sign is determinate even if the magnitude is not — the market gapped UP through the shut window, so a stale pre-shutdown mark understates a long's exit. `pnl_source: local_compute` on an account whose exchange IS in `BROKER_PNL_READER_EXCHANGES` also says IBKR's own realizedPNL was not read back for this row (the hourly `ict-ib-executions-pull` may simply not have run yet — not established).

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE PAPER TRADE: a gap through a closed venue is exactly when the stale mark and the fill diverge most, and it is invisible from the row — the number is plausible, the provenance says `measured`, and the position really is flat. Every downstream R, expectancy and exit-quality figure over a tp_cross close inherits it. The whole reason this was caught is that the routine demanded the MECHANISM and not just "is it flat".
items.resolution_criteria: The tp_cross / monitor close path records an exit price that is either the BROKER FILL or an explicitly anchored estimate via `src/runtime/exit_anchor.py` (whose `anchored` / `deferred` / `no_anchor` contract already exists), and `exit_price_source` distinguishes them — a stale last-known close must NOT resolve to a bucket that `classify_pnl` grades MEASURED. Verified by a test that a close occurring after a data gap does not record a price outside the closing bar's range. SEPARATELY: audit how many historical closed rows carry an `exit_price` outside the range of the bar containing their `closed_at` — that is a pure arithmetic check over existing data, needs no venue call, and bounds how far this has propagated.
items.notes: PAPER account, so no money was lost and no writeback is proposed. Population: ONE trade, examined because a routine targeted it. The historical audit in resolution_criteria is what would establish prevalence — I have not run it and make no claim about how many other rows are affected.

updates.note: ⚠️ HIGH AND THE WORST PROVENANCE SHAPE IN THE BACKLOG: a 49-hour-old candle close recorded as an exit price that NEVER TRADED, and graded `measured`. A fabricated number wearing the label of a measurement is strictly worse than a missing one. Live relevance: MGC 5007 closed this window via a trailed stop with pnlProvenance `estimated` — not the same path, but the same family.

items.opened_by: bracket-expectations-session (found while trying to reuse the e35 bracket-geometry evidence for a dispersion test)
items.title: The e35 bracket-geometry sweep's 3,781 measured cells exist only as GitHub Actions artifacts — no session can read them back, so every consumer must re-run a multi-hour sweep
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-23. docs/research/e35-bracket-geometry-sweep-2026-08-20.md reports 19 legs x 199 grid cells = 3,781 measured cells plus 133 gate rows. Wanting to run a per-leg dispersion test on the donchian STOP cells, I went looking for that evidence and it is not reachable:

- docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl holds 1,379 rows, 331 of them donchian, across 44 distinct cells -- and ZERO of those cells name a stop (`sm*`). Every corpus cell is an M20 LEVER cell (giveback/decay/stale/flip). Asserted by counting, not by eye.
- .github/workflows/e35-bracket-sweep.yml ends in two `actions/upload-artifact` steps and a GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY. There is no corpus-extract step and no commit.
- Root CLAUDE.md is explicit that a PM-side session has NO artifact download.

So the sweep's own evidence is write-only from any session's point of view.

THIS IS THE EXACT PROBLEM m20_corpus_extract.py WAS BUILT TO SOLVE, unfixed for the newer sweep. That tool's own index entry says it: 'Before this, every sweep's evidence went to an Actions artifact no session can download ... so each run restarted the population from zero and no threshold could be derived from more than one sweep.' The lever sweep got the fix; the bracket sweep reproduced the defect.

WHY THE EXISTING EXTRACTOR CANNOT JUST BE POINTED AT IT: the e35 sweep writes report.json + SUMMARY.md + results.jsonl (e35_bracket_geometry_sweep.py:688-690), NOT the verdicts.json m20_corpus_extract.py consumes -- and that extractor deliberately REFUSES a foreign schema loudly (its own docstring: 'TWO SWEEPS WRITE A FILE CALLED verdicts.json AND THE SCHEMAS ARE [different]'). So this needs an e35-shaped extractor, not a path argument.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is not theoretical: the 2026-08-20 sweep's headline reading -- 17 of 19 argmax cells move the STOP, and the two families select from disjoint halves of the stop grid -- is quotable from the committed markdown but CANNOT BE RE-INTERROGATED. Any follow-up (dispersion on a specific cell, a different gate, wins_effective beside wins) requires re-running the whole multi-hour sweep from candles. I am re-running it now for exactly that reason.
items.evidence: docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl (1,379 rows; 331 donchian; 0 cells matching sm*); .github/workflows/e35-bracket-sweep.yml lines 158 + 208 (upload-artifact) with no extract/commit; scripts/research/e35_bracket_geometry_sweep.py:688-690 (writes report.json/SUMMARY.md/results.jsonl); scripts/research/m20_corpus_extract.py docstring + its foreign-schema refusal
items.resolution_criteria: An e35 sweep run leaves per-cell rows in a COMMITTED artifact a later session can read without re-running it, and the workflow does that automatically rather than relying on someone remembering. Acceptable: an e35-shaped extractor writing into m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl (with a schema/lever tag so bracket cells and lever cells stay distinguishable and cannot silently merge), plus a commit step in e35-bracket-sweep.yml. NOT sufficient: uploading a nicer artifact, or documenting that the artifact exists -- the failure is that no session can READ it, so the test is that one can, from a committed file, without a re-run.
items.not_a_finding_about: NOT a criticism of the sweep's measurements, which are sound and whose markdown report is committed. The gap is retrievability of the per-cell rows behind them.
items.resolution: RESOLVED -- and it was already resolved before this row was re-read; the verification is what was missing. Measured 2026-08-27 on origin/main: docs/research/e35-bracket-corpus.jsonl holds 8,211 rows / 6,581 stop cells (sm*) / 41 legs, with 4,378 rows carrying sweep_generated_at 2026-08-26. e35-bracket-sweep.yml's corpus job extracts, commits and pushes them, and a session can read every cell from main without re-running the sweep -- which is exactly what the criteria asked for. ⚠️ ONE DEVIATION FROM THE LETTER OF THE CRITERIA, and it is an improvement: the criteria named m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl as an acceptable target ('with a schema/lever tag so bracket cells and lever cells stay distinguishable and cannot silently merge'); the implementer used a SEPARATE file instead, which achieves that separation structurally rather than by a tag. A 2026-08-27 session (this one) read the criteria's filename as a description of the implementation, probed the wrong store, and filed a false 'the rows never landed' finding off it -- see the correction in BL-20260827-COMPUTE-IS-SOLVED-LANDING-IS-NOT-THREE-INSTANCES.

items.opened_by: bracket-expectations-session (measuring what expectation a bracket carries at entry, per family)
items.tier: 1 to MEASURE and to fix the comment; 3 to change any leg's declared geometry
items.title: `_TP_SENTINEL_CAP_PCT`'s stated rationale is FALSE on 5 of 10 sentinel legs: the 9.9% venue clamp is not a far-away formality, it is the DOMINANT profit exit, so those legs run an undeclared ~1.5R target while grading as `sentinel_no_expectation`
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-23 over the e35 bracket sweep's base runs (11 donchian legs, full history 2021-08-19 -> 2026-08-22, cap 0.099 ON, net of fee+slippage+funding) plus a matching xrp_pullback_2h run. State the population: 10 sentinel legs (9 donchian at tp_r 50 + xrp_pullback_2h at its pre-#10171 tp_r 50); the two `*_prop` legs declare 6.0 and are counted separately.

THE COMMENT. `src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py:126-132` (mirrored verbatim at `htf_pullback_trend_2h.py:98`) justifies the clamp: 'Cap to ~9.9% from entry so the sentinel is exchange-valid AND still far enough that the monitor's Chandelier trail remains the real profit-exit.'

THE FIELD. Ratio of clamped-TP exits to trail exits, per leg:
  trend_donchian      BTCUSDT/1h   16 TP :  154 trail = 0.10
  trend_donchian_1h   BTCUSDT/1h   55 TP :  308 trail = 0.18
  trend_donchian_eth  ETHUSDT/1h   73 TP :  218 trail = 0.33
  trend_donchian_sol  SOLUSDT/1h   67 TP :   99 trail = 0.68
  trend_donchian_avax AVAXUSDT/4h  76 TP :   78 trail = 0.97
  trend_donchian_eth_4h ETHUSDT/4h 60 TP :   35 trail = 1.71
  xrp_pullback_2h     XRPUSDT/2h   89 TP :   32 trail = 2.78
  trend_donchian_xrp_4h XRPUSDT/4h 28 TP :    9 trail = 3.11
  trend_donchian_ada_4h ADAUSDT/4h 85 TP :   22 trail = 3.86
  trend_donchian_sol_4h SOLUSDT/4h 93 TP :   24 trail = 3.88

The claim holds on every 1h leg (0.10-0.68) and FAILS on every 4h leg plus the 2h pullback (1.71-3.88). It is not a wrong claim so much as a claim made on one instrument (BTC 1h, where it was written after the 2026-05-27 ErrCode 10001 incident) and silently inherited by legs where the arithmetic reverses. Field beats comment.

WHY IT REVERSES, and it is arithmetic not luck: cap_r = 0.099 * entry / (atr_stop_mult * ATR). A longer bar carries a larger ATR per bar, so the same 9.9% price distance is a SMALLER number of R. The sweep's own `tp_r_effective_median` (the PLACED target in R -- its measurement, not a re-derivation) is monotone in exactly that:
  sol_4h 1.44 | avax_4h 1.48 | ada_4h 1.57 | eth_4h 2.04 | xrp_4h 2.11 |
  sol_1h 3.22 | eth_1h 4.08 | trend_donchian_1h 5.38 | trend_donchian 5.98
Every one of these legs DECLARES 50R. The venue is placing a 1.44R-5.98R target on their behalf.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND A STALE COMMENT. `src/runtime/target_expectation.py` grades these legs `sentinel_no_expectation` -- 'a sentinel target is not an expectation; it is the absence of one'. That grade is right about the CONFIG and wrong about the VENUE: on 5 of 10 legs a hard target exists, is hit more often than the trail, and nobody chose its value. So the two conditions 'no target, the trail is the exit' and 'no DECLARED target, but the clamp is acting as one and dominating exits' are indistinguishable in the state vocabulary -- the collapsed-state shape this repo names in CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL. The honest reading of the sentinel population changes: those legs are not unmanaged, they are managed by a constant that was chosen to satisfy an exchange error code.

COHERENCE CHECK that this is the right frame: the best risk-adjusted cell in the entire 2,189-cell donchian corpus is `trend_donchian_sol_4h tp1.5_sm2_to96` (IS MAR 4.25->7.41, OOS 0.73->1.44). Its declared 1.5R sits right beside sol_4h's clamp-imposed effective target of 1.44R. The winning geometry is close to 'declare what the venue was already placing, and tighten the stop so it is genuinely reachable rather than truncated'.

(b) A reader can tell, per leg, whether a sentinel bracket is genuinely far (trail-dominant) or clamp-dominant, WITHOUT re-running a sweep: either `target_expectation` gains a state that separates them, or the clamp-dominance ratio is surfaced beside the `sentinel_no_expectation` grade. NOT a claim that any leg is mis-performing because of it; the 4h legs are among the better performers in the corpus. The finding is that a value nobody declared is doing the work of a declared expectation, invisibly.

items.title: xrp_pullback_2h: the joint (stop, target) tuning attempt is COMPLETE and returns NO profitable geometry -- 37 measured cells, 0 positive, and the LIVE geometry is the interior optimum
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-23. State the population: 37 distinct (atr_stop_mult, tp_r) cells, run on scripts/backtest_pullback.py over data/XRPUSDT_1h.csv resampled to 2h, full history 2021-08-19 -> 2026-08-23, at the leg's other declared params (trend_lookback 40, pullback_lookback 10, pullback_frac 0.5, trail_mult 6.0, adx_min 25, trail_decay_arm_r 4.49), cap 0.099 ON, net of fee+slippage+funding. n=296 trades at the live cell.

Grid 1: atr_stop_mult {1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5} x tp_r {1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0} = 25 cells. net_R ranged -114.19 to -13.02. ZERO positive.
The optimum sat at the corner (stop 2.5, tp_r 3.0) -- a BOUNDARY, not an optimum -- so the grid was extended in the improving direction: stop {2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0} x tp_r {3.0, 4.0, 6.0, 50} = 16 more cells. net_R -22.03 to -13.02. ZERO positive. The optimum is now INTERIOR: it is the live geometry, stop 2.5 / tp_r 3.0, at -13.02R (maxDD 33.42, MAR -0.39).

SO THE TUNING ATTEMPT REQUIRED BEFORE ANY DEMOTION PROPOSAL HAS BEEN MADE ON THIS AXIS, AND IT FAILS. There is no placeable bracket geometry that makes this leg profitable, and the direction that would make its declared 3.0R target reachable more often (a tighter stop) makes it dramatically WORSE: stop 1.0 costs a further 66R.

SECONDARY: tp_r 6.0 and tp_r 50 return byte-identical results at every stop tested, because past a certain declared value the venue clamp binds on every entry and the declared number becomes wholly inert. That is a clean confirmation of the clamp mechanism in BL-20260823-VENUE-CLAMP-IS-THE-UNDECLARED-TARGET-ON-HALF-THE-SENTINEL-LEGS.

WHAT IS STILL UNTESTED, and why this is NOT yet a demotion proposal: two axes remain untouched -- the ENTRY criterion (adx_min 25 / the trend-structure predicate) and the TRAIL (trail_mult 6.0 with trail_decay_arm_r 4.49, an arm the position-telemetry read already grades `unreachable` under this leg's own cap of 3.9233, so the decay never arms). A leg whose exit geometry cannot be rescued may still have an entry problem, and TUNE-BEFORE-DEMOTE is per-axis, not per-attempt.
items.evidence: /tmp/xrp/grid.jsonl (25 cells) + /tmp/xrp/grid2.jsonl (16 cells), reproduced by docs/research/xrp-pullback-joint-geometry-2026-08-23.md which carries both grids in full; config/strategies.yaml::xrp_pullback_2h declared params
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) a tuning attempt on the ENTRY axis and the TRAIL axis is run and recorded, at which point the leg has had the genuine multi-axis attempt the rule requires and a disposition (keep / tune / demote) can be PROPOSED to the operator with evidence on every axis; or (b) the operator decides on the leg without waiting for those axes. Closure requires the axes to be NAMED as tested or explicitly waived -- 'we tuned it and it did not work' without saying which axis is exactly the shape this row exists to prevent. NOT sufficient: shipping any geometry change on the strength of this grid, which found nothing to ship.
items.not_a_finding_about: NOT a demotion proposal, and NOT a claim the leg should be demoted -- two axes are untested. NOT a finding that PR #10171 (which set tp_r 3.0) was wrong: 3.0 is the best value in the whole tp_r column at every stop tested, so that change moved the leg in the right direction. Its effect is simply smaller than it looks, because the clamp binds on 77.7% of entries at the live stop.

updates.note: Re-validated: a COMPLETE tuning attempt returning no profitable geometry is a finished negative and strong input to the xrp_pullback_2h disposition (see BL-20260818-XRP-PULLBACK-LEG-REJECTS-EVERY-DECISION-EXIT-LEVER). The leg is live on real money.

items.opened_by: bracket-expectations-session (found while trying to argue a drawdown floor for the Path B population)
items.title: e35 bracket sweep: Path B was UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION — the gate passed a raw `run_cell` dict where `is_path_b_candidate` reads a key `run_cell` never emits, so the predicate answered False for every cell ever gated
items.detail:
MEASURED + PROVEN 2026-08-23, two independent ways.

THE DEFECT. `e35_bracket_geometry_sweep.py::gate` called `fleet.is_path_b_candidate(beats_detail(c_is,b_is), beats_detail(c_oos,b_oos), c_oos)` — passing the RAW `run_cell` output as the third argument. `is_path_b_candidate` reads `cap_oos.get('d_net_r_per_capital_day')`. The M20 fleet sweep passes `entry['capital']['OOS']`, a `capital_delta(...)` result, which HAS that key; `run_cell` output does not.

PROOF 1 (static, over the real artifacts): scanned 308 `run_cell` dicts across 11 legs from the 2026-08-23 run. `net_r_per_capital_day` present: TRUE. `d_net_r_per_capital_day` present: FALSE. The delta key never exists in a run_cell output.

PROOF 2 (dynamic, calling the real predicate on real numbers — trend_donchian `sm2`, d_net_r +15.0732 IS / +3.8773 OOS): passed a raw run_cell dict -> False; passed a capital_delta dict -> True; positive control (both net_R up + cap up) -> True. So the predicate is correct and CAN say True; the argument shape is the bug.

CONSEQUENCE. `_up(None)` is False, so `path_b` was False for EVERY cell in every e35 run regardless of its numbers, and every such cell short-circuited to `is_oos_fail` before any walk-forward ran. The '77/77 gated cells fail' headline is correct as a tally of VERDICT STRINGS and OVERSTATES the finding: 10 of those cells improve net_R in BOTH halves, which is precisely the Path B population, and none was ever assessed as one. The drawdown tolerance the operator was asked to set is argued from walk-forward folds that Path B RECORDS rather than gates ('measure the axis first, threshold it second') — and that population had never been generated.

THIS IS THE SAME GATE GAP THE FLEET SWEEP FOUND AND FIXED ON 2026-08-10, reproduced in the newer sweep. `m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:2891` carries the note verbatim: 'THE GATE GAP (found 2026-08-10): a Path B candidate short-circuited to is_oos_fail BEFORE any walk-forward ran, so every Path B candidate on record ... had ZERO generalisation evidence.' Second instance of the lever sweep receiving a fix the bracket sweep did not inherit; the first is BL-20260823-E35-SWEEP-EVIDENCE-HAS-NO-DURABLE-PATH (the write-only corpus), found the same day.

WHY NO UNIT TEST CAUGHT IT: the predicate was always correct in isolation. The defect is the SHAPE of the argument the caller builds, which is invisible to a test of the predicate. tests/test_e35_path_b_reachable.py therefore asserts the CALLER's contract — including an AST check that the third argument is bound to a `capital_delta(...)` result and not to `c_oos` — and carries a positive control, since a test that can only ever fail is not evidence the thing works.
items.evidence: scripts/research/e35_bracket_geometry_sweep.py::gate (the call site, fixed in this change); scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py:1964 (is_path_b_candidate), :2109 (capital_delta), :2891 (the fleet's own 2026-08-10 gate-gap note); 308 run_cell dicts in /tmp/w/e35/*/2026-08-23/results.jsonl; tests/test_e35_path_b_reachable.py (6 tests incl. a positive control)
items.resolution_criteria: (a) The gate passes a `capital_delta` result and a test pins it so it cannot silently regress — DONE in this change. (b) The gate is RE-RUN on at least the donchian legs and the resulting Path B verdicts are recorded, so the population a drawdown tolerance would be argued from actually exists; a fix with no re-run leaves the same evidence gap the defect created. (c) Any OTHER caller of a fleet predicate from a sibling sweep is checked for the same argument-shape mismatch — this is the second inherited-fix miss between these two sweeps, so a third is likely and looking once is cheaper than finding it later. NOT sufficient: fixing the line without re-running, which would leave '77/77 fail' standing as if it had been a real assessment.
items.not_a_finding_about: NOT a defect in `is_path_b_candidate`, which is correct and proven to return True on the right input. NOT a claim that any cell WOULD have passed Path B — that is what the re-run determines. NOT a criticism of the Path B thresholds, which are deliberately unset pending a measured distribution.

updates.note: Re-validated: M20 measurement correctness, propose-only. Re-sweeps blocked on trainer capacity (91.7% disk + the 4 GB memory thrash). Unreachable BY CONSTRUCTION — every Path B verdict from that gate is vacuous.

items.tier: 1 to MEASURE; 3 to change any leg's declared arm
items.title: 2 of 4 measured `trail_decay_arm_r` values can NEVER fire under the live venue cap — including on trend_donchian_sol_4h, one of the fleet's better performers
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-23. State the population: 4 enabled legs whose declared arm could be compared against a measured peak; 4 more declare an arm and were NOT in this run (avax_pullback_2h 4.86, gld_pullback_1d 5.06, qqq_trend_long_1d 3.56, scha_trend_long_1d 2.00) — that is 'we did not look', not 'reachable', and they are counted neither way.

Declared arm vs the LARGEST peak the leg has printed (max_mfe_r, full history, cap 0.099 ON = live conditions):
  trend_donchian_sol_4h  SOL/4h  arm 5.57  max MFE 3.85  n=197  INERT
  xrp_pullback_2h        XRP/2h  arm 4.49  max MFE 2.92  n=296  INERT
  trend_donchian         BTC/1h  arm 6.49  max MFE 9.84  n=340  reachable
  trend_donchian_xrp_4h  XRP/4h  arm 2.00  max MFE 2.81  n=137  reachable

CONFIRMED TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS on xrp_pullback_2h: (1) the MFE distribution — 0 of 296 trades ever reached 4.49R (p50 0.70, p90 2.07, max 2.92), so the arm sits at 1.54x the largest peak in five years; (2) an A/B — arm 4.49 returns BYTE-IDENTICAL net_R to arm 0.0 (disabled) at every trail_mult tested (3.0/4.0/6.0/8.0). A declared mechanism that provably does nothing.

WHY A SANE-LOOKING VALUE IS INERT: the harness was uncapped. Same leg, same params, cap OFF: max MFE 8.55 and 16/224 = 7.1% of trades reach 4.49R. Cap ON: 0/296 = 0.0%. A value fitted without --tp-cap-pct looks defensible and is inert once the venue truncates every winner at ~9.9%. This is the SAME declared-vs-placed gap as BL-20260823-VENUE-CLAMP-IS-THE-UNDECLARED-TARGET-ON-HALF-THE-SENTINEL-LEGS, one lever further down: the clamp does not only replace the target, it silently disarms every lever whose trigger was calibrated above the truncation point.

WHY sol_4h MATTERS MORE THAN THE XRP LEG: it is one of the better performers in the corpus, and the cell that beats it hardest (tp1.5_sm2_to96, the best risk-adjusted cell measured) is precisely one that stops relying on the trail. A leg performing well with a dead lever is performing well for other reasons, and nothing in the config or on any surface says so.

items.resolution_criteria: (a) Every enabled leg declaring a reach-gated lever (trail_decay_arm_r, giveback_min_mfe_r) has its arm compared against a MEASURED peak under the live cap, with the unmeasured ones named as unmeasured rather than assumed reachable. (b) An inert arm is either removed or re-declared at a reachable value, per leg, as a Tier-3 change with its own evidence — NOT swept. (c) The comparison is repeatable without a live journal (see the sibling row on lever_reachability_audit.py). NOT sufficient: recording the two inert arms and leaving the other four unmeasured, since 'we did not look' is exactly what this row is about.
items.not_a_finding_about: NOT a claim that removing an inert arm would improve anything — arm 4.49 and arm 0.0 are the same number, so removing it changes no outcome; it only stops the config asserting a mechanism that does not run. NOT a claim that a reachable arm would help: on xrp_pullback_2h every reachable value measured WORSE. NOT a claim about the four unmeasured legs.

updates.note: Re-validated: 2 of 4 measured arm values can NEVER fire under the live cap, including on trend_donchian_sol_4h. Duplicate condition with BL-20260816-TRAIL-DECAY-ARM-R-SITS-ABOVE-THE-VENUE-TP-CAP; consolidate. A declared lever that cannot fire is decoration.

items.title: `lever_reachability_audit.py` grades all 8 declared levers `unmeasured` because it needs live journal rows, while the backtest already carries the answer over hundreds of trades
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-23. `scripts/ops/lever_reachability_audit.py` was built for exactly the question 'can this leg's declared reach-gate ever fire under the 9.9% TP cap' and names xrp_pullback_2h's 4.49 in its own docstring. Run today it returns: '8 declared levers on live+enabled legs; 0 journal rows supplied' and grades every one `unmeasured`, with `inert: 0   ungraded: 8`.

The refusal is CORRECT — it will not grade without evidence, and its own note is right that 'unmeasured/cap_unknown are NOT reachable'. The problem is the input: it accepts only live journal rows, which for these legs is a handful, while `max_mfe_r` from a capped backtest answers the same question over 137-340 trades per leg and is already computed in every e35 base run. Measured that way, 2 of 4 comparable legs are INERT (BL-20260823-DECLARED-TRAIL-DECAY-ARMS-ARE-INERT-UNDER-THE-VENUE-CAP) — a finding the audit as shipped reports as `inert: 0`.

⚠️ `inert: 0` beside `ungraded: 8` is honest (the tool states its denominator, which is why this row is LOW and not HIGH) but is exactly the shape a reader skims as 'nothing inert found'. The tool's own reading guide says so; the risk is the summary line, not the grading.
items.evidence: scripts/ops/lever_reachability_audit.py run output 2026-08-23 (8 levers, 0 journal rows, inert: 0 / ungraded: 8); the measured-from-backtest comparison in docs/research/xrp-pullback-trail-axis-and-inert-levers-2026-08-23.md
items.resolution_criteria: The audit can grade a lever from a CAPPED backtest's max_mfe_r / MFE distribution when no journal rows are available, keeping the three states distinct (reachable / inert / unmeasured) and stating which basis produced each verdict — a backtest-derived verdict must never be presented as a live-journal one. NOT sufficient: supplying journal rows by hand once; the point is that the cheap, large-n basis exists and the tool cannot consume it.
items.not_a_finding_about: NOT a criticism of the tool's refusal to grade without evidence, which is the correct behaviour and the reason this is LOW severity. NOT a claim that a backtest basis is superior to a live one — it is larger-n and counterfactual, and the two should be distinguishable in the output.

updates.note: Re-validated: all 8 declared levers grade `unmeasured` for want of live journal rows — an honest state, and the reason PB-20260816-REACHABILITY-REGISTRY-IGNORES-THE-CORPUS is worth doing (the corpus already carries the measurement).

items.opened_by: bracket-expectations-session (first run of the tool on a Path B population, which only became possible the same day)
items.title: `m20_split_dispersion` grades on PATH A only, so on a Path B cell it returns `pass_fraction: 0.0` and `split_sensitive: false` — and filtering on that boolean reads the stability of a FAILURE as evidence of a pass
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-23, on the first Path B population that has ever existed for the e35 sweep (see BL-20260823-E35-PATH-B-UNREACHABLE-RAW-RUNCELL-DICT).

THE DEFECT. `m20_split_dispersion.py:214` computes `passed = bool(beats(cm_is, bm_is) and beats(cm_oos, bm_oos))` — Path A: net_R AND maxDD, both windows. `split_sensitive` is then `len({passed values}) > 1` and `pass_fraction` is the share of graded targets that passed.

A Path B cell trades drawdown for net_R BY DEFINITION, so it fails `beats` at every target. `m20_fleet_exit_sweep::walkforward`'s own docstring already states the principle for the fold axis: 'Applying that to a Path B candidate would reject it in every fold BY CONSTRUCTION -- trading drawdown for net_R is what makes it Path B -- so the walk-forward would answer a question the cell never claimed to pass, and the ~2/3 tally would be a fabricated negative.' The same is true one axis over, on the IS/OOS split, and the dispersion tool did not inherit the distinction.

MEASURED: all 7 path_b_wf_pass survivors returned `state: measured`, `graded: 5`, `pass_fraction: 0.0`, `split_sensitive: false`.

⚠️ THE DANGEROUS PART IS THE BOOLEAN, NOT THE FRACTION. A reviewer told to 'keep only split_sensitive:false' -- which is the natural reading of the field name and was the instruction this session received -- would have KEPT ALL SEVEN and read them as stable. They are stable: stably failing a test they never claimed to pass. `pass_fraction: 0.0` is right there beside it and is the only thing that gives it away, so this is a legibility defect rather than a wrong number.

WHAT THE RIGHT GRADE LOOKS LIKE, and it is cheap: the rows the tool ALREADY emits carry `d_net_r_is` and `d_net_r_oos` per target, so the Path B claim (net_R up in BOTH windows) is gradeable with no new measurement. Done by hand for this session: 4 of 7 hold at all 5 targets (3 distinct cells, since ada_4h `sm1.5` and `sm1.5_to400` are the same object), and 3 are split-DEPENDENT -- including `trend_donchian_sol_4h tp1.5_sm2_to96` at 3/5, which is the cell this session had been treating as its headline result.

So the tool's OUTPUT already contains the answer; only the verdict layer is Path-A-only.
items.evidence: scripts/research/m20_split_dispersion.py:214 (the Path A predicate) and :234-236 (split_sensitive / pass_fraction derived from it); scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py::walkforward docstring (the same distinction, made for the fold axis); /tmp/xrp/disp/results.json (7 cells x 5 targets, harness_agreement True on all 7); docs/research/donchian-stop-gate-is-drawdown-bound-2026-08-23.md § 3.95
items.resolution_criteria: The tool grades a cell against the claim it actually makes: a `--path {a,b}` selector (or a per-cell path carried in from the sweep) choosing between `beats(...)` and the Path B claim (net_R up in both windows, drawdown RECORDED not gated), with the path named in the output so a verdict states which test produced it. `split_sensitive` must then describe stability of THAT verdict. NOT sufficient: documenting the caveat -- the field name is what misleads, and a reader filtering on it will not have read the docstring.
items.not_a_finding_about: NOT a claim that the tool's numbers are wrong -- `harness_agreement` was True on all 7, and its refusal to grade at all without `--base-reported` is the tool working correctly. NOT a claim that any of the 7 cells is shippable or unshippable; the Path B grading above is a hand computation over the tool's own rows, not a tool verdict.

updates.note: Re-validated: M20 measurement correctness, propose-only. Re-sweeps blocked on trainer capacity (91.7% disk + the 4 GB memory thrash). Returns pass_fraction 0.0 on a Path B cell — a false negative dressed as a measurement.

items.opened_by: bracket-expectations-session (operator-directed: what expectation should a bracket carry at entry)
items.tier: 3 (config/strategies.yaml — target/stop geometry on a real-money leg)
items.title: xrp_pullback_2h declares tp_r 3.0 but the venue clamps it to 0.687 R — the leg moved sentinel -> CLAMPED, not sentinel -> declared, and it is on real money
items.detail:
PR #10171 (merged 2026-08-23T13:37Z) set xrp_pullback_2h tp_r 50.0 -> 3.0 and left atr_stop_mult UNCHANGED at 2.5 (only trail_mult moved 5.0 -> 6.0).

MEASURED on the open trade via /api/diag/log_file?name=target_extension_soak: cap_r = 0.687 on all 5 rows of that order package. cap_r = 0.099 * entry / (atr_stop_mult * ATR), so the declared 3.0 R BINDS on 5/5 and the level that actually RESTS is 0.687 R — a take-profit NEARER than the stop. Backing ATR out: ATR/entry = 5.76%. Making 3.0 R reachable would require the stop to tighten from 2.5 to 0.573 ATR (4.36x tighter), which is not a sane stop.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN ROW AND NOT THE KNOWN R:R FINDING. Root CLAUDE.md already records 'xrp_pullback_2h at R:R 0.687 (real money)' — that is independent confirmation of the same number, not a new discovery. What is new is that the FIX DID NOT RESOLVE IT: target_expectation.py separates `clamped` from `sentinel_no_expectation` precisely because 'a clamped leg had an expectation the venue refused to place; a sentinel leg never had one'. The bracket now STATES a prediction the venue will not honour, which is a different defect from having none.

ROUTING: bybit_2 (real_money), plus bybit_1 (paper) and bybit_portfolio (paper).

SAME SHAPE, NOT YET MEASURED LIVE: trend_donchian_eth_prop and trend_donchian_sol_prop both declare tp_r 6.0 against cap_r ~1.98 at a 2% reference ATR, and both route to breakout_1 (prop, terminal breach). All three non-ict_scalp real targets in the live fleet are clamped.

LIMITS OF THIS MEASUREMENT: cap_r is fixed at entry and varies with entry ATR, so n = 1 trade. A calmer entry clamps less. The DIRECTION is structural (cap_r is inversely proportional to atr_stop_mult); the exact 0.687 is one reading.
items.evidence: docs/research/bracket-expectation-construction-2026-08-23.md sections 4-5; scripts/research/bracket_expectation_census.py (11/11 selftest); /api/diag/log_file?name=target_extension_soak 2026-08-23T10:12Z-14:43Z
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) atr_stop_mult moves WITH the target so that tp_r <= cap_r at typical entry ATR for XRPUSDT 2h, verified by re-reading cap_r from the soak on a NEW order package (not the current one), or (b) tp_r is set to a value that actually fits under cap_r, or (c) the leg is explicitly declared trail-exited and the target key removed rather than left at an unplaceable value. A row that merely re-states the current number does NOT close this: the test is that a soak row for a fresh entry shows expectation_state='declared', never 'clamped'. items.title: target_expectation.STATE_NO_TARGET_KEY can never fire in production, so the sentinel's PROVENANCE (chosen vs inherited) is collapsed for 10 live legs
items.detail:
resolve_expectation() carefully separates `no_target_key` from `sentinel_no_expectation`, and its own docstring gives the reason: calling one the other 'would accuse 20 legs of a defect they may not have'. In production the state is unreachable.

MECHANISM: the monitor hands resolve_expectation the MERGED config (strategy-class defaults + YAML), so the class default has already been applied before the module sees it. htf_pullback_trend_2h.py:67, trend_donchian.py:81, squeeze_breakout_4h.py:65 and fade_breakout_4h.py:88 each declare tp_r = 50.0, so a leg whose YAML has no target key arrives carrying tp_r=50.0 and grades sentinel_no_expectation.

MEASURED: all 72 target_extension_soak rows (2026-08-23T10:12Z-14:43Z) are sentinel_no_expectation; ZERO are no_target_key. Five of the covered legs (mhg/tlt/ief_pullback_1d, spy/qqq_pullback_1h) declare no target key in config/strategies.yaml yet emit target_source_key='tp_r', target_r=50.0 — the class default, observed from the other side.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE POPULATION: counting tp_r>=50 in the YAML gives 24 of 45 enabled+live legs; the number that BEHAVE as sentinels is 34 of 45. The YAML count understates it by 42%. The 10 invisible legs are gdx/gld/iaum/ief/slv/tlt_pullback_1d, gld/qqq/spy/tlt_pullback_1h.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT WRONG: the GRADE is behaviourally correct — the effective tp_r really is 50, and the placed level really is the venue threshold. What is lost is PROVENANCE: whether the sentinel was chosen or inherited. Those have different remedies (edit the leg vs change a class default that silently governs 10 legs), which is the exact distinction the state was built to preserve.
items.evidence: docs/research/bracket-expectation-construction-2026-08-23.md sections 1-1.1; scripts/research/bracket_expectation_census.py (reports declared and effective SEPARATELY and refuses to sum them)
items.resolution_criteria: A consumer can distinguish an EXPLICIT sentinel from an INHERITED one on a live trade. Acceptable shapes: the soak row carries the origin (declared_in_yaml | inherited_class_default) alongside expectation_state, or resolve_expectation is passed the raw YAML block beside the merged one. NOT sufficient: documenting the class defaults, or a test asserting the current counts — the failure is that the distinction is unobservable at runtime, so the test must show a leg with no YAML target key grading differently from one that writes tp_r: 50.0 explicitly.

updates.note: Re-validated: a state that can never fire means the sentinel's provenance (chosen vs inherited) is unrecoverable. Collapsed-state family.

items.title: target_expectation.py docstring quotes 29 of 52 enabled / 26 live sentinel legs; measured today it is 28 / 24
items.detail:
The module docstring states '29 of 52 enabled legs are here (counted 2026-08-23), 26 of them execution: live'. Measured against config/strategies.yaml at 9544ced: 28 of 52 enabled, 24 of 45 live.

RECONCILED, so this is staleness and not disagreement: at 9544ced~1 the docstring was exactly right (29 enabled / 26 live). PR #10171 then changed xrp_pullback_2h tp_r 50.0 -> 3.0 (removing one sentinel from both populations) and demoted the htf leg (removing a live sentinel and taking live 46 -> 45).

WHY FILE IT AT ALL: the docstring is quoted as a population, and this repo's own rule is to state the population on every number. A count that drifts one commit at a time is how a quoted figure becomes wrong without anyone deciding it should be.
items.evidence: docs/research/bracket-expectation-construction-2026-08-23.md section 1.2; scripts/research/bracket_expectation_census.py reproduces 55/52/45 with sentinel 30/28/24 declared and 40/38/34 effective
items.resolution_criteria: Either the docstring cites the census script as the source of truth rather than embedding a snapshot, or the embedded numbers are refreshed AND carry the commit they were measured at, so the next drift is visible rather than silent.

updates.note:
RESOLVED via the criterion's FIRST branch (cite the census, do not embed a snapshot) — and the re-measurement found something worth more than the staleness.

IT HAD DRIFTED A THIRD TIME. Docstring 29 of 52 enabled / 26 live (2026-08-23); this row recorded 28 of 52 / 24 of 45 at 9544ced; measured at 814d019b it is 28 of 52 / **23 of 44**. Three different answers in two days, none of them from a decision about targets — legs were demoted by unrelated PRs.

⚠️ THE BIGGER FINDING: THE QUOTED NUMBER IS THE WRONG MEASURE, and it under-reports the very problem the module exists to name. scripts/research/bracket_expectation_census.py — which already existed and which this row did not consult — separates sent_DECL from sent_EFF, because 10 pullback legs declare NO target key and INHERIT tp_r = 50.0 from their strategy class. They behave exactly as sentinels and are invisible to a `grep tp_r`. At 814d019b: enabled 52 -> 28 declared / 38 effective; enabled+live 44 -> 23 declared / 33 effective. So the docstring's '29 of 52' was quoting a figure roughly a third below the behavioural population. My own first re-measurement made the SAME mistake (a tp_r scan, 28/23) and was corrected only by running the census — which is the argument for citing it rather than re-deriving it per reader.

WHAT SHIPPED: the docstring no longer carries a count as a claim. It names the census as the authority, states why an embedded snapshot drifts, explains the declared-vs-effective split and why the two are never summed (a leg that writes tp_r: 50.0 CHOSE it; a leg that writes nothing INHERITED it — same behaviour, different remedy, and conflating them accuses legs of a defect they may not have), and gives the current numbers stamped 'for orientation only, measured at 814d019b'.

SCOPE NOTE — one thing fixed beyond this row, deliberately. The CENSUS's own header carried the identical defect (24 of 45 / 34 of 45, now 23 of 44 / 33 of 44) — the source of truth was itself quoting a stale snapshot. Refreshed with its commit stamp, plus a note that the gap is still exactly 10 so the movement is leg demotions and not a change in the phenomenon. Its 'understates by 42%' also never stated its basis; it is gap/declared, now 43%, with gap/effective (30%) given beside it. --selftest 11/11 passes and the headline table is unchanged.

items.opened_by: bracket-expectations-session (found while implementing an operator-approved change; the approval rested on my own mischaracterisation, which is corrected here)
items.tier: 3 (config/strategies.yaml — declaring adx_min CHANGES ENTRY ADMISSION, it is not observability)
items.title: 12 pullback legs declare no adx_min, so they have NO ADX filter at entry — and 'declare adx_min to fix thesis_unknown' is an entry-behaviour change, not the cheap observability fix it was described as
items.detail:
THE CORRECTION MATTERS MORE THAN THE FINDING. docs/research/bracket-expectation-construction-2026-08-23.md section 7 item 1 proposed 'declare adx_min on the 10 inheriting pullback legs -- cheapest, highest leverage, unblocks 31% of open trades from thesis_unknown, and CHANGES NO GEOMETRY'. The operator approved it on that description. The description was wrong in three ways and the item is retracted in place rather than silently repaired.

(a) THE SET IS 12, NOT 10. 'Legs that inherit the target' and 'legs that lack adx_min' are different sets. Measured against config/strategies.yaml: 16 enabled+live pullback legs, 4 declare adx_min (ada 28, eth 25, sol 30, xrp 25 -- all 2h crypto), 12 do not. The 12 are the 10 target-inheriting legs PLUS mgc_pullback_1d and mhg_pullback_1d, which declare tp_r: 50.0 explicitly but no floor. Declaring on only 10 leaves 2 legs thesis_unknown while looking complete -- and mhg_pullback_1d is one of the FIVE legs actually observed in the target_extension_soak with reason 'no_adx_min_declared'.

(b) IT IS AN ENTRY-BEHAVIOUR CHANGE. src/units/strategies/htf_pullback_trend_2h.py:76 declares "adx_min": None as the class default, and the gate at line 297 runs only `if adx_min_p is not None or adx_max_p is not None`. So these 12 legs have NO ADX filter at entry today. Declaring one starts REFUSING setups that are currently admitted. 'Changes no geometry' was true of SL/TP and false of admission, which is the more consequential axis. It also means thesis_unknown on these legs is CORRECT REPORTING, not a defect: a leg with no declared entry regime condition genuinely has no thesis to re-evaluate, which is exactly what _pullback_thesis_intact's docstring already says ('a leg with no declared floor has no thesis to test, which is a different thing from a broken one').

(c) THERE IS NO VALUE TO DECLARE. No class default exists to fall back on. The only declared values in the family are 25/28/30, every one of them on a 2h CRYPTO leg; the 12 are 1d/1h equity, bond and metal. Porting a number across instrument class and timeframe is chosen-not-measured, and adding an ADX floor to make a thesis readable is literally 'reaching for a refusal', which the operator's standing directive forbids: 'Do not reach for a clamp, a floor, or a refusal when the honest answer is that the geometry was never constructed.'

BLAST RADIUS (measured): all 12 route to alpaca_live (account_class real_money but mode: dry_run, so nothing executes today), plus alpaca_paper / alpaca_portfolio / alpaca_options_paper, plus ib_paper for the mgc/mhg pair. ZERO live real-money exposure right now. But alpaca_live is the latent account root CLAUDE.md flags -- 'real-money on dry_run with 16 strategies all execution: live; flipping that one account takes 16 legs live at once' -- so whatever is declared now is what goes live the day that account flips.
items.evidence: config/strategies.yaml (16 enabled+live pullback legs; 4 with adx_min, 12 without); src/units/strategies/htf_pullback_trend_2h.py:76 (class default None) and :297 (gate runs only when declared) and :458-460 (thesis returns no_adx_min_declared); /api/diag/log_file?name=target_extension_soak 2026-08-23 (5 of 16 open trades reason=no_adx_min_declared); config/accounts.yaml routing
items.resolution_criteria: A floor is DERIVED, not chosen. Required first: the ADX-at-entry distribution per leg over history for all 12, so the proposed adx_min is stated together with the fraction of historical entries it would have REFUSED. A value whose refusal rate is unmeasured does NOT close this row, and neither does porting 25/28/30 from the crypto legs. If the measurement shows a candidate floor refuses a material share of entries, it needs its own walk-forward before any Tier-3 flip -- at which point it is a strategy change, not a fix to thesis_unknown. Closing this row by declaring nothing is also acceptable IF the finding is recorded as 'these legs deliberately have no entry regime condition', since thesis_unknown is then correct behaviour rather than a gap.
items.not_a_finding_about: NOT a claim that these legs are broken, and NOT a demotion proposal. thesis_unknown is the honest state for a leg with no declared floor.

updates.note: Re-validated: 12 legs with no adx_min, so no ADX filter at entry — and the row correctly notes that declaring adx_min purely to fix `thesis_unknown` would be backwards. Live: the pullback family closed 12+ trades this window and is OOS-unprofitable on all 6 crypto legs (BL-20260818, critical).

items.title: The protective-bracket repair stamp is written and QUERYABLE but nothing BRANCHES on it — the exit_price_source shape, filed by its own author at the moment of writing
items.source:
Shipped 2026-08-24 (Tier-2, operator-approved): trades gains protection_repairs / _first_at / _last_at / _last_kind / _last_verified, written by Database.stamp_protection_repair from the three repair paths in order_monitor (naked re-arm, Bybit qty-scoped top-up, divergence re-assert).

The read surface is GENERIC and real — the Data Explorer (/api/bot/db/table/trades) and /api/diag/journal?table=trades both serve the columns with no new endpoint, so 'which trades were repaired?' is answerable by a query today, which is the whole ask. But NO CONSUMER BRANCHES on the field.

That is precisely the exit_price_source shape this repo already paid for (written in 12 files, branched on in ONE, for an unrelated value; zero references in the whole ml/ tree) and it is what provenance-consumer-guard exists to catch. Filing it at the moment of writing rather than waiting to be found is the point: a signal that is written and never read is worse than a missing one, because reviewers see the field and assume something acts on it.

STATE THE POPULATION: zero rows carry the stamp today. The writer deployed 2026-08-24; every pre-existing trade is NULL, and NULL means 'no repair RECORDED', never 'no repair happened'. So there is nothing yet to measure a consumer against — which is itself the argument for deciding the consumer deliberately rather than bolting one on to satisfy a guard.

DO NOT close this by adding a decorative branch. This repo's own rule: a guard cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than no guard, and the same applies to a consumer that reads a field only to keep a checker quiet.
resolution_criteria: DECIDE the consumer explicitly, with a reason, from these candidates (not all of them): (a) /api/bot/trades/closed emits a repaired flag beside pnlProvenance, so the dashboard + Android can caveat a trade whose exit ran on a repaired bracket; (b) /performance excludes or separately reports repaired rows, the way pnlCoverage reports measured share; (c) the system-review reads it as a standing count; (d) nothing — the generic query IS the consumer, recorded as a deliberate decision rather than an omission.

If (a) or (b): the flag must not collapse — a repaired trade whose repair landed both_legs_resting is a different claim from one that landed stop_only or call_failed, and a boolean 'repaired' would lose exactly the distinction the _last_verified column was added to keep.
Whichever is chosen, state the population it was measured over. Re-check first that the stamp has ACCRUED any rows at all: a consumer designed against an empty column is untested by construction.
If the decision is (d), say so in CLAUDE.md's trades row and close this — an explicit 'the query is the consumer' is a valid answer; a silent one is not.

updates.note: Re-validated: written and queryable, nothing branches on it — class A, and CLAUDE.md documents it as such explicitly. Same shape as exit_price_source (written in 12 files, branched on in one).

items.title: Unit-A selective-flip was SHELVED on measured evidence — and that evidence lives only on a closed draft PR, nowhere in the repo
items.source:
Operator asked whether the abandoned selective-flip code died on EVIDENCE or on NEGLECT. INVESTIGATED, not assumed. It died on evidence, and the evidence is specific.

PR #5025 (`claude/unit-a-selective-flip-mamcnu`, draft, opened and closed the same day 2026-06-29): 1,944 additions over 10 files — `src/runtime/flip_ev.py`, `src/runtime/flip_reentry.py`, an `intents.py` `selective` branch, 47 tests. Two backtests were run and reported ON THE PR:

1. Default knobs, BTC roster, net-of-fee: selective was BYTE-IDENTICAL to hold (both -$5,110, maxDD 54.26%, 573 trades) — the EV/confidence gates never fired. A no-op, correctly flagged as inconclusive rather than as a pass.

2. Tuned knobs on a genuinely flip-heavy roster (trend_donchian + fade_breakout_4h on BTC, ict_scalp_5m excluded), multi-year 2023-01 -> 2026-02 plus a chop sub-window. Gates DID fire (4-6 flips), so this is a real result:
   - maxDD FAILS the 'no worse' bar: EVERY selective combo lands 18.08% against hold's 17.92%. The flips it takes raise drawdown ~0.16pp in every cell, window and knob setting — uniformly, not on average.
   - Net edge is NOT ROBUST: selective beats hold multi-year (-$757 vs -$975) and LOSES in chop 2023 (-$816.4 vs -$799.5).
   - At best it makes a LOSING roster less-losing; never net-positive.
   - thr 0.15 == thr 0.20 (confidence gaps rarely exceed ~0.15) and the age gate is nearly inert — so two of the three knobs are not doing work.

Explicit recommendation on the PR: SHELVE. Closed 8 minutes later, with 'the code stays on the branch if we ever revisit'. So the branch is deliberately retained, not forgotten — and the 2026-08-24 prune correctly excludes it.

THE GAP IS NOT THE DECISION, IT IS WHERE THE DECISION LIVES. Nothing in the REPO records any of this: no backlog row, no research doc, no ROADMAP line. A session reading only the repo sees `FLIP_POLICY` with three implemented options, a fourth designed in `docs/research/pnl-optimal-conflict-resolution-DESIGN.md`, and no reason it is missing — and could rebuild all 1,944 lines to re-derive a negative that was already measured. This composes with BL-20260811-FLIP-OVERRIDE-NEVER-WALKFORWARDED, whose own resolution disarmed FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD on the same grounds: the flip family has now lost twice, measured, and the repo states neither loss.

STATE THE POPULATION: two backtest runs, one roster family (BTC), n=4-6 flips in the run that mattered. That is a SMALL flip count — enough to fail a 'no worse maxDD' bar that it fails uniformly, not enough to characterise a distribution. Raw grids: trainer relays #5068 / #5090 / #5094.
resolution_criteria: Land the verdict where a repo-only reader will hit it: a short docs/research/ note (or a section in the existing pnl-optimal-conflict-resolution DESIGN doc) carrying the two tables, the uniform-maxDD finding, the chop-window reversal, and the trainer relay ids.
Cross-reference it from the FLIP_POLICY row in CLAUDE.md, which today documents hold/reverse/flat and says nothing about `selective` having been built and measured.
State the small-n caveat explicitly (4-6 flips) so the record cannot be read as a stronger negative than it is — and so a future re-test knows what would actually settle it.
Do NOT delete claude/unit-a-selective-flip-mamcnu while this is open: the PR comment deliberately kept the code, and the record should point at a branch that still exists.

updates.note: Re-validated: evidence living only on a closed draft PR. Same family as BL-20260815-FOLD-DISPERSION-EVIDENCE-RUNS-ON-AN-UNMERGED-BRANCH — decisions resting on artifacts not in main.

items.title: A Claude web session can CREATE remote branches but gets HTTP 403 deleting one — which is how the bot repo reached 282 branches
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-24, not inferred. `git push origin --delete claude/admiring-davinci-MufpA` from this session returns:
  error: RPC failed; HTTP 403 curl 22 The requested URL returned error: 403
  send-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet
  fatal: the remote end hung up unexpectedly
  Everything up-to-date
while ref CREATION works fine (this session pushed several branches). The hosted GitHub MCP has `create_branch` and NO delete-branch tool, so neither channel can remove a ref.

CONSEQUENCE: every session adds branches and none can remove them. The bot repo holds 282, of which 149 are provably landed; dashboard and android hold 75 each.

TWO TRAPS THIS EXPOSED, both worth keeping:
1. The failure prints 'Everything up-to-date' immediately after 'fatal:' — a reassuring string on a failed operation. A reader skimming the tail sees success.
2. Wrapping the push in `if git push ... | tail -2` made the shell test TAIL's exit code, so a batch loop reported 'deleted: 146' having deleted zero. Caught only by re-counting the remote afterwards. This is the FOURTH pipe-swallows-rc incident in one session — see BL-20260823-BACKGROUND-TASK-RC-IS-THE-PIPELINE-NOT-THE-COMMAND.
resolution_criteria: RESOLVED BY the prune-landed-branches workflow shipped 2026-08-24 (a runner's GITHUB_TOKEN has the contents:write the delete needs) — confirm it deletes for real on a non-dry run, since a workflow that reports success having deleted nothing is exactly the failure above one level up.
Verify by RE-COUNTING the remote after the run, never by reading the workflow's own summary.
If the 403 ever lifts for sessions, note it here — the workflow stays either way, because the manifest + SHA-pin is a better audit trail than an ad-hoc push.

updates.note: Re-validated and I hit the adjacent condition today: my branch's remote ref was STALE (deleted upstream, still in my local refs) and the push failed until `git remote prune origin`. The 403-on-delete is why branches accumulate.

items.summary: BL-20260730-PR-CI-NOT-ATTACHING recurred on PR #10215 (2026-08-24), the third recorded occurrence after the original and the 2026-08-07 PR #8608 re-confirmation. Measured: branch claude/bracket-expectations-exit-ctjaiq was pushed at ~09:55Z to head adebefe and PR #10215 was opened as a draft against main at ~09:55Z; 27 minutes later the PR had total_count 0 check runs, and listing workflow runs for that branch showed NO run of any kind against adebefe — the newest pull_request-event run was 08:48:57Z against the PRE-RESTART head 19bfd89. The three required workflows (guards/pytest-run/pytest-collect) all declare pull_request types [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review] branches [main], so drafts are not excluded and 'opened' should have fired. Dispatching all three via workflow_dispatch on the same ref produced runs immediately AND they attached as PR check runs (total_count 0 -> 3), confirming the workflows and the ref are fine and only the pull_request delivery was lost.
