SECOND DATA POINT, same PR, same session: a subsequent REAL commit (9001876, not an empty one) pushed to the branch produced no pull_request run either — zero runs against BOTH adebefe and 9001876, with the newest pull_request-event run on the branch still 08:37:55Z against the pre-restart head 19bfd89. So on this branch BOTH the opened AND the synchronize delivery were lost, which matches the #8608 signature exactly rather than being a one-off on the open, and means a session that pushes a fix to a silently-CI-less PR gets no signal from that push either.
items.evidence: PR #10215; runs 32716467222 (guards), 32716472365 (pytest-run), 32716480446 (pytest-collect), all event=workflow_dispatch, head_sha adebefeea0b45511668b6a68ad4abc8abd1f1b1b, pull_requests [10215]. Negative observation: mcp actions_list list_workflow_runs filtered to the branch returned 43 runs, newest created_at 2026-08-24T08:48:57Z against head_sha 19bfd891 (the pre-restart head), zero against adebefe. Positive control on the probe: the same get_check_runs call returned 7 check runs for PR #10213 earlier the same session, so a 0 is not a broken probe.
items.hypothesis_unverified: UNVERIFIED and offered only as a distinguishing factor to test, not as a cause: unlike the #8608 case, this branch had been DELETED by GitHub's auto-delete-on-merge when PR #10183 merged, then RECREATED with the same name minutes before the PR was opened. Whether a delete/recreate of a branch name with prior PR history suppresses the opened-event delivery is NOT established here — the mechanism was not determined, and no attempt was made to reproduce it.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) establish the mechanism (in particular whether the delete/recreate of a branch name is implicated) and add a detector that FAILS rather than renders-as-green when a PR has zero check runs past a threshold age — the existing remedy is a manual workflow_dispatch, which only helps a session that thinks to look; or (b) if no mechanism can be established across occurrences, ship the detector anyway, since the failure mode is 'a required check silently did not run' and that is indistinguishable from green to every consumer including the merge button. Closing on 'could not reproduce' alone is not sufficient — that is what happened after the first two occurrences.

updates.note:
FOURTH OCCURRENCE, 2026-08-25 on PR #10282 — and it REFUTES the delete/recreate hypothesis this row's own title carries, which is the most useful thing it contributes.

THE BRANCH WAS NEVER DELETED OR RECREATED. `claude/full-system-review-qhpxyh` has been continuously pushed all session. More decisive: attachment worked, then stopped, WITHIN THE SAME PR.

  push 1  f24f640d  15:18:57Z  pull_request run created  (cancelled by push 2)
  push 2  da914dd1  15:24:13Z  pull_request run created  (cancelled by push 3)
  push 3  012e201b  15:31:36Z  pull_request run created  -> COMPLETED SUCCESS
  push 4  8548f48e  ~15:43Z    NO run of any workflow
  push 5  da11ae06  ~15:52Z    NO run
  push 6  5251d36c  ~16:0xZ    NO run   (a real merge of origin/main, not a no-op push)
Verified from actions_list filtered to pytest-run + the PR's own check_runs (total_count 0) and get_status (sha 5251d36c, total_count 0, statuses []).

SO THE MECHANISM IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE BRANCH OR THE PR AT CREATION — the same PR, same branch, same author, same workflows, delivered three `synchronize` events and then stopped delivering them. A delete/recreate cannot explain a mid-life transition, and neither can 'the PR was opened wrong'. Whatever this is, it is transient and it starts partway through a PR's life. Two candidates NOT ruled out from here: webhook backlog on a busy repo (there was heavy Actions traffic today), and something about the workflow_dispatch I issued at 15:46 — though note push 4 preceded that dispatch, so the dispatch cannot be the cause of push 4.

WHAT IT COST, which is the argument for criterion (b): nothing. I happened to be watching. The PR shows no failed check, `mergeable_state` is not 'unstable', and every surface a session or a human reads is indistinguishable from 'all green'. A session that pushed and moved on would have merged an unverified change to a live-money system, which is exactly what the 2026-07-30 row records happening to #8053. This occurrence adds nothing to the argument FOR the detector except a fourth data point — but it does sharpen what the detector must watch: not 'a PR that never had checks', which is what a creation-time bug would produce, but 'a PR whose head sha has zero checks past a threshold age', which catches the mid-life transition too. A detector written to the delete/recreate hypothesis would have missed this.

WORKAROUND USED (and it works): workflow_dispatch on pytest-run.yml / guards.yml / pytest-collect.yml against the branch ref. Every required context carries workflow_dispatch precisely because of the 2026-07-30 occurrence, and that provision paid off here. ⚠️ It does NOT satisfy branch protection — a dispatch run is branch-scoped and does not attach to the PR's head sha — so the verification is recoverable while the MERGE is not.

THE RECOVERY, and it is NOT the one this row's family documents. Established on PR #10282 today, which merged cleanly once it was applied.

⚠️ `workflow_dispatch` IS THE WRONG WORKAROUND, and recording it as THE remedy is actively misleading. It runs the workflow and verifies the code — which is real and worth having — but a dispatch run is BRANCH-scoped and never attaches to the PR's head sha, so branch protection is untouched. Measured directly: after three green dispatch runs the merge still failed with `405 3 of 3 required status checks are expected`. A session that treats dispatch as the fix will verify its code, believe it is unblocked, and still be unable to merge.

WHAT ACTUALLY WORKS: toggle the PR out of DRAFT. `ready_for_review` is in pytest-run.yml / guards.yml / pytest-collect.yml's `on.pull_request.types` list, so the conversion fires a fresh, PROPERLY ATTACHED run on the head sha. On #10282 it re-attached all four checks within a minute (`event: pull_request`, not `workflow_dispatch`), they went green, and the merge succeeded. If the PR is already non-draft, draft-then-ready is the same lever.

⚠️ IT IS NOT FREE, and the cost is exactly the thing this repo warns about: the conversion CANCELS auto-merge and merge-queue membership. It also fired TWICE here (one set of checks cancelled at 16:53:42 and a second started at 16:53:46), so expect a duplicate round and do not read the cancelled first set as a failure.

WHY THIS BELONGS ON THE ROW RATHER THAN IN A HEAD: the row's criterion (b) asks for a detector because 'a required check silently did not run' is indistinguishable from green. That is still right. But the OPERATOR half — what a blocked session should actually DO — was documented wrong across the whole family, and a wrong remedy costs a session an hour of dispatch rounds that cannot possibly unblock it.

RECURRENCE #3, WITH A SHARPER OBSERVATION THAN 'ZERO CHECKS'. PR #10290, branch claude/full-system-review-qhpxyh, 2026-08-25.

WHAT MAKES THIS INSTANCE INFORMATIVE: it is NOT that the branch gets no pull_request runs. It gets 30 of them. Filtering actions_list to event=pull_request on this branch returns Guards / pytest-run / pytest-collect / repo-inventory, all SUCCESS — but the newest is head_sha 7c1b0267 at 17:27:23Z, the branch's FIRST commit. The six commits pushed after it (cfee37d0, 814d019b, e1a77944, ad7fb527, 6d5981f9, d7775cae, 58f7a0e7) have NONE.

So the failure is not 'the pull_request event is dead on this repo' (the July diagnosis, BL-20260730-PR-CI-NOT-ATTACHING) — it is that CI attached ONCE, on the commit that OPENED the PR, and never again on subsequent pushes to the same open PR. That is a different and much more specific shape, and it is worth carrying into the mechanism hunt this row's criterion asks for.

THE BRANCH WAS DELETED AND RECREATED, which is this row's own hypothesis: after #10282/#10289 merged I restarted it from origin/main per the repo protocol ('restart your designated branch from the latest default branch, keep the same branch name'), and the push reported `* [new branch]`. So the protocol that the session context MANDATES is the same action this row suspects. If the hypothesis holds, every session following the merged-PR instruction walks into this, which would explain the recurrence rate.

WORKAROUND APPLIED AND IT DID NOT WORK WITHIN THE OBSERVATION WINDOW: marked the PR ready_for_review (draft -> ready), which IS in the workflows' trigger types and should attach to the head sha. get_check_runs still returned total_count 0 immediately after. ⚠️ These reads are documented to lag by tens of minutes (BL-20260825-GITHUB-CHECK-RUN-READS-LAG-AND-READ-AS-STILL-RUNNING), so this is 'not observed within the window', NOT 'the toggle does not work' — the distinction matters and I am not collapsing it.

POSTURE TAKEN: the PR is NOT merged and will not be until checks attach. Local validation is recorded in its place and is NOT offered as a substitute — scripts/ci/run_guards.py PASS 33-38 FAIL 0 on each commit, plus the touched suites (test_m20_tp_geometry_guard 10 passed, check_backlog_criteria --self-test, check_unwired_artifacts --self-test 16/16, bracket_expectation_census --selftest 11/11). run_guards is diff-scoped and skips guards CI runs, which is exactly what BL-20260824-THE-CI-NOT-ATTACHING-WORKAROUND-SCANS-THREE-FEWER-GUARDS is about — so 'green locally' is a weaker claim than 'green in CI' and is reported as such.

updates.by: claude (2026-08-25, correcting my own prior update)
updates.note:
⚠️ CORRECTION TO MY OWN UPDATE 20 MINUTES AGO, AND IT WIDENS THE FINDING. I wrote that CI 'attached ONCE, on the commit that OPENED the PR, and never again on subsequent pushes to the same open PR', and framed it as a per-PR / deleted-branch effect. THAT FRAMING IS TOO NARROW. It was built from a branch-filtered read — the denominator mistake this repo guards against.

REPO-WIDE READ (actions_list unfiltered, 30 most recent runs, spanning 17:17Z-18:44Z; the window is fully covered because only three non-skipped runs occurred in it). EVERYTHING that ran after 17:30:09Z:
    18:44:01  claude-run-failure-alert   workflow_run        skipped
    18:43:38  Health Snapshot            schedule            success
    18:36:25  gld-compat-matrix          workflow_dispatch   success
    17:30:35  external-comment-alert     issue_comment       skipped
and nothing else. ZERO `pull_request` runs and ZERO `push` runs repo-wide in those ~74 minutes.

SO ACTIONS IS NOT DOWN — `workflow_dispatch` and `schedule` both fired and SUCCEEDED inside the same window (I dispatched the compat matrix myself at 18:36 and it completed). What has stopped is specifically the `pull_request` event.

IT IS NOT MY BRANCH. The other live session's branch, claude/metis-lane-0-decisions-7jgnjz, also has its last pull_request run at 17:28:08Z and nothing since. Two independent branches, same cutoff. The deleted-and-recreated-branch hypothesis in this row's TITLE is NOT supported by this instance and I am not claiming it — a shared cutoff timestamp points at something repo- or platform-wide at ~17:30Z, not at anything either branch did.

⚠️ CAVEAT ON THE `push` HALF, stated because it is weaker than the pull_request half: Guards / pytest / repo-inventory may be configured to run on push only for `main`, in which case zero push-runs for my seven feature-branch pushes is EXPECTED and is not evidence. The load-bearing evidence is the `pull_request` event, which is branch-agnostic and silent across two open PRs.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE ORIGINAL FRAMING: a per-PR quirk inconveniences one session. A repo-wide `pull_request` outage means NOTHING merging to main right now is gated by CI, on a live-money system — precisely the P1 that BL-20260730-PR-CI-NOT-ATTACHING recorded ('zero checks renders identically to all green'). Any session merging in this window should know. NOT DIAGNOSED from here: whether this is a GitHub-side incident or a repository Actions setting; neither is readable from this session.

updates.by: claude (merge reconciliation of two concurrent sessions)
updates.note:
CROSS-SESSION RECONCILIATION, written while resolving the merge conflict this row caused between two concurrent sessions. BOTH readings are correct and they describe DIFFERENT WINDOWS — which neither session could see alone, and which is a stronger statement than either.

  THEIRS (session on claude/metis-lane-0-decisions-7jgnjz, `full_event_ledger_2026_08_25`): all 10 PR/push events on their branch that day, checked per head sha. 7 ATTACHED, 3 did not. INTERMITTENT, ~3-in-10, hitting both create and push including a force-push, with no discriminator found.
  MINE (this session, PR #10290): actions_list UNFILTERED, everything repo-wide after 17:30:09Z is one workflow_dispatch, one schedule, and two skipped — ZERO `pull_request` runs in ~75 minutes, across at least two independent branches.

THE RECONCILIATION IS THE TIMESTAMP. Their branch's LAST attached pull_request run is 17:28:08Z; mine is 17:27:23Z. Their ledger therefore covers the period ENDING around 17:30, and my window BEGINS there. So the honest joint statement is:
  before ~17:30Z — intermittent, roughly 3 of 10 events fail to attach
  after  ~17:30Z — total, zero of N attach, repo-wide
i.e. the condition did not merely persist, it WORSENED at ~17:30Z from partial to complete. Neither session's data alone supports that; the two together do.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH, so it is not over-read: the ~17:30 boundary is inferred from the last-attached timestamps on two branches, not from an event anyone observed. I did not establish WHAT happened at 17:30, whether the total phase has since ended, or that the two phases share a cause. A single sustained-outage explanation and a worsening-intermittent explanation both fit.

THEIR CONCLUSION SURVIVES AND SHOULD BE THE ONE ACTED ON. Their `what_this_leaves` calls for a detector that fails when a PR has zero runs against its CURRENT HEAD SHA past a threshold age, keyed on the head sha rather than the PR. That is right and my evidence strengthens it: during the total phase, a PR that was green on an older commit keeps showing that green while its newest commits are unchecked — which is exactly what PR #10290 did for 12 commits.

WORKAROUND THAT WORKED, recorded because this row's family has been looking for one: `workflow_dispatch` kept working throughout the total phase. Dispatching guards.yml / pytest-run.yml / pytest-collect.yml against the branch ref produced REAL runs — all three SUCCESS on 1cd0f51d — while `pull_request` produced nothing. ⚠️ Those runs do NOT become attached check_runs and so do NOT satisfy branch protection; they are evidence for a human, not a gate. But 'CI cannot run' and 'CI cannot ATTACH' are different problems, and only the second one is true.

THE OUTAGE ENDED, ON ITS OWN, AND THE END IS AS MEASURABLE AS THE START. Window: pull_request-event runs stopped being created repo-wide at ~17:30Z and resumed at 19:44:43Z on merge commit 0f71f49a — about 2h14m. PR #10290 then carried SIX attached check runs, all success: pytest-run (19:45:13->19:57:56), guards (19:44:50->19:46:37), pytest-collect (19:44:47->19:46:15), guards (19:44:46->19:45:59), pytest-run (19:44:46->19:56:39), repo-inventory (19:44:46->19:44:57); mergeable_state 'clean'. Merged as 44b50485.

WHAT THIS ADDS TO THE ROW. (a) The condition is TRANSIENT and self-resolving, not a repo-config state someone has to change — nothing was done to GitHub between 17:30Z and 19:44Z. (b) So a future occurrence should be WAITED OUT with periodic re-reads, not chased through branch recreation, which is what this row's title records an earlier session doing and which the 08-25 update already refuted as a cause. (c) It pairs with the cross-session reconciliation recorded above: the other session measured 3 of 10 events failing to attach (INTERMITTENT, last attached run 17:28:08Z) while this session measured ZERO repo-wide after 17:30Z (last attached 17:27:23Z). Their window ends where mine begins, so the condition WORSENED from intermittent to total before recovering. That boundary is inferred from two last-attached timestamps, not from an observed transition event — do not quote it as a measured changepoint.

DELETE/RECREATE, one more data point AGAINST it being causal: the merge auto-deleted claude/full-system-review-qhpxyh and the branch was recreated from the new main immediately afterwards — the exact sequence this row is named for — during the RECOVERED period. Whether the next push attaches is the cheap test.

WORKAROUND CONFIRMED: workflow_dispatch runs succeeded THROUGHOUT the outage, so real CI was reachable the whole time. It does not satisfy branch protection (a dispatched run does not attach to the PR), so it is an evidence path, never a merge path.

⚠️ REFUTED FOR MY CASE, WHICH IS THE EXACT SCENARIO THIS ROW DESCRIBES — worth recording. My branch claude/full-system-review-v68vcm had been DELETED upstream (git remote prune removed a stale ref) and I RE-CREATED it with a fresh push. CI attached and ran normally: `guards` and `pytest-run` both executed on 811f0a0 and again on beb84a2, and both reported back. So a deleted-then-recreated branch did NOT reproduce the non-attachment here. The row may be conditional on something my case lacked; it should not be closed on one counter-example, but the counter-example is worth recording.

items.third_occurrence_2026_08_25: THIRD OCCURRENCE, and it RULES OUT the mechanism this row asks about. PR #10287 sat at `get_check_runs total_count: 0` for 12 minutes after opening; `list_workflow_runs` filtered to the branch showed the newest run against the PREVIOUS head (ef1efe74) and ZERO against fe4bc4f or 53dc9f68. Positive control on the probe, per this row's own standard: the same endpoint family returned a concurrent session's 16:25 run on `claude/full-system-review-qhpxyh`, so the 0 is not a dead probe.
items.delete_recreate_hypothesis_REFUTED_as_su: ⚠️ THE DELETE/RECREATE HYPOTHESIS IN THIS ROW'S TITLE IS NOT SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN. Session 018aKyS3 pushed three PRs off ONE branch name that was auto-deleted on merge and recreated each time (every push reported `* [new branch]`), so the delete/recreate condition held for ALL THREE: #10281 attached, #10283 attached, #10287 did NOT. A condition present in the two successes cannot by itself explain the one failure. That is a negative result the row explicitly asked for ('in particular whether the delete/recreate of a branch name is implicated') and it should stop the next session spending time there.
items.new_hypothesis_n3_NOT_established: ⚠️ RETRACTED BY ITS OWN AUTHOR, SAME SESSION, BEFORE IT MERGED. I proposed 'draft-vs-ready at creation' as the co-varying factor and wrote that 'whatever it is concerns the CREATE event rather than the branch'. BOTH HALVES ARE REFUTED by a fuller read of the same session's own events. I reached it by looking at the ONE #10287 push that attached (96c4157) and not at 53dc9f6, which did not — selective evidence, in the row I was writing to complain about a reassuring reading. Leaving it would have put a false lead in front of the next session.
items.cost_note: Also worth recording against this row's 'the existing remedy only helps a session that thinks to look': the session DID think to look, and still nearly did not. The PR reported `state: pending` with zero statuses, which reads as 'CI is running' rather than 'CI does not exist'. What actually surfaced it was checking `list_workflow_runs` against the head sha — the check the row's resolution_criteria proposes automating.
items.full_event_ledger_2026_08_25: STATE THE POPULATION: all 10 PR/push events on branch claude/metis-lane-0-decisions-7jgnjz on 2026-08-25, each checked for a workflow run against its own head sha via list_workflow_runs. ATTACHED: e608824 (create draft:true), 559a2c6 (push), 25d9bab (push), ec6c591 (push), ef1efe7 (create draft:true), 96c4157 (push), 2ebdcda (create draft:true). NOT ATTACHED: fe4bc4f (create draft:false), 53dc9f6 (PUSH), 3aed31b (FORCE-PUSH). So 3 of 10 events did not attach, and TWO OF THE THREE WERE PUSHES, not creates. Draft-vs-ready does not survive either: #10288 was created draft:true and ATTACHED, then its force-push did NOT. Same branch, same PR, same day, opposite outcomes.
items.what_this_leaves: The honest residue after the retraction: the failure is INTERMITTENT at roughly 3-in-10 events on one branch in one day, affecting BOTH create and push (incl. force-push), with no discriminator this session could find. That is a weaker claim than a mechanism and it is the true one. It also raises the row's stakes rather than lowering them: an intermittent no-attach on a PUSH means a PR that was green can silently stop being re-checked on its newest commit, and the PR page shows the OLD green. The resolution criteria's detector — fail when a PR has zero runs against its CURRENT head past a threshold age — is the right shape and should key on the head sha, not on the PR.
items.cross_session_corroboration_and_one_cont: TWO SESSIONS REFUTED THE TITLE HYPOTHESIS INDEPENDENTLY, FROM DISJOINT EVIDENCE, ON THE SAME DAY — session 018aKyS3 via a branch where delete/recreate held for all three PRs and only one failed, and the system-review session (#10289 'updates') via a branch NEVER deleted or recreated where attachment worked then stopped inside one PR. Neither knew of the other's; the merge that produced this row is where they met. Two independent refutations is materially stronger than either alone, and the title should now be read as a misnomer rather than a lead. NOTE THE TWO ALSO DISAGREE ON OCCURRENCE NUMBER (each calls itself the third/fourth) — they are different occurrences, not a contradiction; the count is simply not authoritative on either. ⚠️ ONE CONTRADICTION WORTH RESOLVING, recorded because it cuts against a claim merged the same hour: #10289 states a workflow_dispatch run 'never attaches to the PR's head sha'. MEASURED HERE, IT DID. Runs 32877255512 (guards) and 32877252634 (pytest-collect), both event=workflow_dispatch on branch claude/metis-lane-0-decisions-7jgnjz, returned from get_check_runs FOR PR #10288 carrying head_sha 1e9dd602 — the PR's own head — as named check runs 'guards' and 'pytest-collect'. So a dispatch run CAN surface as a check run on the head sha. What #10289 actually demonstrates is the stronger and still-unrefuted half: that this was not SUFFICIENT to satisfy branch protection (it observed '405 3 of 3 required status checks are expected' after three green dispatch runs). APPEARING as a check run and COUNTING as a required status check are different questions, and conflating them is how the remedy on record became the wrong one. Not resolved here — this session's own PR needed a real push for an unrelated reason (a merge conflict), so it never tested the dispatch-only merge path and MUST NOT be read as having done so.

items.summary: The sanctioned remedy for BL-20260730-PR-CI-NOT-ATTACHING is a manual workflow_dispatch of guards/pytest-run/pytest-collect. Measured on PR #10215 (2026-08-24): a dispatched guards run reports the SAME headline as a pull_request run -- 'PASS 50 FAIL 0 SKIP 0' followed by 'All relevant guards passed' -- while having scanned THREE FEWER guards. The run footer says so ('NOT SCANNED on this event (3) -- no PR diff to scope by'): api-tier-policy-guard, test-schema-fidelity-guard and diagnostic-provenance-guard consume the {pr_diff} template variable, which is empty on a non-pull_request event. So the workaround for a bug whose whole danger is 'a check that silently did not run renders identically to green' itself renders a reduced scan identically to a full one, in the headline a reader quotes.
items.evidence: PR #10215, guards run 32716867785 (event=workflow_dispatch, head_sha 90374658), job 97399901700. Log footer lists the 3 unscanned steps by name. Note the harness is INCONSISTENT rather than uniformly diff-less on this event: guards taking the literal path /tmp/pr.diff DID scan a real diff on the same run (new_table_wiring reported '6 changed file(s) scanned', matching this PR's file count), while the three consuming {pr_diff} were skipped -- so two diff mechanisms coexist and only one survives a dispatch. Mitigated for THIS PR by running the three locally against origin/main: all three PASS, diagnostic-provenance-guard reporting 'OK -- every scanned diagnostic states what it computed'.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) give the three steps an ungated whole-tree form, which the run footer itself already prescribes ('A guard needing real push-time coverage must carry an UNGATED whole-tree step (see api-tier-policy-guard)') -- api-tier-policy-guard is named there as the pattern to copy, so the remedy exists and simply was not applied to these three; or (b) make the SUMMARY line refuse to read as a clean bill of health when steps were skipped -- the local runner already does exactly this for uncommitted paths ('All SELECTED guards passed -- but N path(s) are UNCOMMITTED ... This is NOT a clean bill of health for your change'), and the CI path should carry the same refusal. Closing without one of those leaves the documented workaround quietly weaker than the path it substitutes for.

updates.note: Re-validated (title empty in file). A workaround with narrower coverage than the thing it replaces is a silent reduction in checking.

items.title: silent_refusal_alert graded a DECLARED dry_run account as broken and latched a real_money alert for three days on correct behaviour
items.source: MEASURED this session. /api/diag/log_file?name=silent_refusal_alert_state showed alpaca_live {alerting: true, cause: risk_refused, verdict: signalled_never_placed} continuously since 2026-08-21T12:38:38Z. /api/diag/broker_account_status?account_id=alpaca_live returns mode: dry_run, account_class: real_money, status ACTIVE, trading_blocked false. A dry_run account refusing every order IS the execution gate working as designed.
items.root_cause: silent_refusal_alert.assess() builds its account set purely from journal rows (SELECT account_id ... FROM trades) and NEVER reads the account's declared mode. Its own docstring claims to watch for 'declared live, evaluates, signals, places NOTHING' but the code never establishes 'declared live'. Field beats comment.
items.why_it_matters: This is the desensitized-alarm P1 the repo names as its own worst failure mode, self-inflicted on its newest detector — and it wore an account_class: real_money label, which reads maximally alarming. The repo had ALREADY ruled on this exact account: execution_diagnostics.EXPECTED_DISPATCH_SKIP_REASONS ('a dry_run-shelved account declining an order is the execution gate working exactly as designed ... must never raise an operator alert') was added by operator directive 2026-07-15 after shelving alpaca_live to dry_run made every tick fire both banners. silent_refusal_alert shipped 2026-08-14 without consulting it and re-created the alarm the operator had had suppressed.
items.evidence: 162 of 186 alpaca_live journal rows carry entry_reason starting 'REJECTED: dry_run_sizing_skip:' — the exact token is_expected_dispatch_skip() recognises. The 24 that do not are all 2026-07-15..2026-07-20, before the coordinator started prefixing it, and fall outside the alert's 24h window.
items.fix: dead_leg.bucket_for() gains an optional `reason` axis and a FOURTH bucket `policy_skipped`; verdict_for() gains `refusing_by_declaration`. The predicate is IMPORTED from execution_diagnostics, never re-derived (one module owns 'is this refusal deliberate?'). Fail-SAFE, opposite polarity to account_side_filter: this gates an ALARM, so an unrecognised reason stays a real refusal. silent_refusal_alert also gains `alert_disposition` (alerting / suppressed_declared_dry_run / below_min_rows / not_a_finding) so a bare `alerting: False` no longer collapses three different facts. Omitting the reason preserves pre-2026-08-24 behaviour byte-for-byte.
items.verification: Replayed against the REAL live journal over the 28 daily 24h-windows in which alpaca_live produced rows: 24 of 28 — every window from 2026-07-21 onward, INCLUDING the 2026-08-21 window that produced the live latch — now grade refusing_by_declaration / alerting False. The 2 pre-prefix windows (07-16, 07-17) still alert, correctly: the classifier genuinely cannot read those reasons as declared skips, and the fail-safe direction keeps them loud. 39 unit tests pass (32 pre-existing unchanged). collapsed-state-guard, provenance-consumer-guard and diagnostic-provenance-guard all clean.
items.resolution: Fixed in this session's PR. Suppression is per-ROW, never per-account: an account that is switched off AND separately hitting a venue cap still alerts on the genuine refusals (pinned by test).
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED. Residual watch: the standing alpaca_live latch clears only when the account next produces rows — see BL-20260824-SILENT-REFUSAL-LATCH-CANNOT-CLEAR-WITHOUT-ROWS.

items.tier: 1 to MEASURE (done); 2 to change what the monitor records at close, or to re-grade the vocabulary
items.title: `recorded_exit_price` is classified MEASURED and is the single largest 'measured' source in the journal — outnumbering every genuine broker-truth source COMBINED
items.source: MEASURED this session over the newest 1,500 trades rows (531 closed non-backtest; trades table total 4,985). exit_price_source distribution: recorded_exit_price 82 (15.4%) · candle_at_close 136 · local_markprice 58 · exchange_fill 52 · bybit_closed_pnl 25 · ib_execution 2 · None 173 · entry_order_avg_price_unreliable 3. Genuine broker truth (exchange_fill + bybit_closed_pnl + ib_execution) = 79. So recorded_exit_price (82) EXCEEDS all broker-truth sources combined, and classify() grades it MEASURED — indistinguishable from the 79 on every consumer surface.
items.root_cause: src/runtime/provenance.py::MEASURED_SOURCES includes 'recorded_exit_price' under the comment '# A real fill the bot itself recorded at close time.' #10209 (2026-08-24) DISPROVED that comment on trade 4773: the recorded exit 4626.9 was Friday's last close, 49 hours stale, BELOW the reopen bar's low, so it cannot have been a fill. Field beats comment — except here the code's correctness rests entirely on the comment's claim.
items.why_it_matters: 67 of the 82 rows come from MONITOR-DERIVED close paths (intent_reduce 31, sl_cross 20, stale_stop 8, tp_cross 4, giveback_stop 3, stuck_strategy_watchdog 1) where the 'exit price' is by construction the bot's own computed level or last candle close, NOT a venue fill. This is precisely the class exit_anchor.py was built for and that _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced was already fixed to stop doing. The blast radius is the SCOREBOARD: totalPnlMeasured exists specifically to be the honest figure the R4 gate reads INSTEAD of totalPnl, and it is currently led by this class.
items.measured_reporting_impact: Trade 4773 (ib_paper MGC, +$249,185.00, graded `measured`) is 96% of the paper book's entire 3-day window PnL ($259,699.65) and 98.4% with the next two rows. /api/bot/performance?window=24h returns paper totalPnl $247,027.13 with totalPnlMeasured $247,148.80 — i.e. the 'honest measured' figure is MORE inflated than the raw total. /api/bot/stats paper.pnl24h shows the same number to both the dashboard and the Android app.
items.not_established: Whether the other 81 rows are individually wrong. Only 4773 has been proven stale (by #10209). What IS established is that the vocabulary cannot distinguish them, and that the population is 82 rows and not the ONE that #10209 measured — that commit explicitly recorded 'Population is ONE trade; the historical audit that would bound prevalence is in resolution_criteria and has NOT been run.' This row IS that audit.
items.scope_correction: #10209 dispositioned this 'PAPER account, no money impact, backlog only'. True of MONEY. NOT true of REPORTING: real-money rows are 5 of the 82, but the vocabulary defect is account-agnostic and the paper book is the honest net-of-everything predictor the 'Dollars are the scoreboard' rule relies on.
items.proposed_fix: Split the source: a close whose price came from a VENUE fill keeps MEASURED; a close whose price is the monitor's own level or last candle close is ESTIMATED (it has an anchor — the bar at closed_at — so it is not FABRICATED). exit_anchor.py already owns exactly this three-way decision. Do NOT simply demote recorded_exit_price wholesale without checking which writers are genuine fills, or genuine broker truth will be downgraded with the rest.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) Enumerate the WRITERS of exit_price_source='recorded_exit_price' and classify each as venue-fill vs monitor-derived. (2) Either split the source string at the writers or split the classification. (3) Re-measure pnlCoverage and totalPnlMeasured before/after and state the population. (4) Do NOT back-fill or rewrite historical rows — they stay attributable to the tool that made them (the backtest_results precedent).
items.resolution:
RESOLVED — `recorded_exit_price` is demoted from MEASURED to ESTIMATED in `src/runtime/provenance.py` (line 275, inside the ESTIMATED set, under a block comment at lines 248-274 naming this row). Read from the file this session.

The comment carries the evidence and the reasoning: disproved on trade 4773 (#10209) where the 'recorded exit' 4626.9 was Friday's last close, 49 h stale and BELOW the reopen bar's low, so it cannot have been a fill; and it is not one row — over the newest 1,500 journal rows (531 closed non-backtest) 82 carry this source against 79 for ALL genuine broker truth combined (exchange_fill 52 + bybit_closed_pnl 25 + ib_execution 2), all 82 `local_compute`, ZERO with `close_fees_usd`, and 67 of 82 from monitor verdict paths where the price is a level the monitor computed. ESTIMATED not FABRICATED, because the price was on the row at close time and is anchored to the close.

The root cause is fixed in the same change: `order_monitor._sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced` no longer overwrites an existing `exit_price_source`, so genuine broker rows keep their own `_broker_pnl_source(rec)` stamp.

⚠️ THE COVERAGE MOVE IS A CONSEQUENCE, NOT A REGRESSION: closed non-backtest `pnl NOT NULL` coverage reads 494/1151 = 42.9% against the pre-change 60.8%/829, and the two are NOT comparable — the population grew 829→1151 AND the classifier changed. Held at the old classification the same population reads 592/1151 = 51.4%, so the reclassification accounts for ~8.5pp and population growth for the rest. Real-money coverage barely moved (25/37 = 0.676), which is the check that genuine broker truth was left alone.

items.title: A latched silent-refusal alert can never clear while the account produces no rows — so a latch outlives the condition indefinitely
items.source: READ this session in src/runtime/silent_refusal_alert.py::run_silent_refusal_check. The recovery loop iterates `assessed.items()`, and assess() deliberately omits an account with no rows ('we observed nothing'). alpaca_live's last journal row is 2026-08-21 and its latch still reads alerting:true today (2026-08-24).
items.why_it_matters: Not a defect in the omission — declaring recovery on ABSENCE would be wrong, and the docstring says so. The gap is that there is no third state: `silent_accounts()` (the read surface the review skills consume) reports the account as currently-latched-silent when the truth is 'latched a while ago, unobserved since'. A reviewer reading it cannot tell a live condition from a stale one.
items.proposed_fix: Stamp the latch with the last OBSERVED-at time (distinct from updated_at) and have silent_accounts() expose staleness, so a consumer can distinguish 'alerting, observed this window' from 'alerting, not observed since <ts>'. Same discipline as prop status_freshness. Do NOT auto-clear on absence.
items.resolution_criteria: silent_accounts() rows carry an observation age, and a consumer can tell a live latch from an unobserved one without reading the journal.

updates.note: Re-validated: a latch that outlives its condition because the account produces no rows to clear it. Live relevance — alpaca_live produces almost no rows by construction, so a latch on it is effectively permanent.

items.title: check_unwired_artifacts counts a SKILL.md reference as 'documented, but nothing runs it' — so 10 of its 128 findings are tools a binding skill invokes, two of which this very review ran
items.source: MEASURED this session. scripts/ci/check_unwired_artifacts.py reports '410 tool(s) under scripts/, 128 with no runner'. Parsing its own output: 10 of the 128 are annotated 'referenced ONLY by docs (.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md, ...)'. Among them are scripts/reports/render_system_report.py and scripts/reports/backlog_counts.py — MANDATORY steps of .claude/skills/system-review/SKILL.md, both executed by this session — plus scripts/ops/grade_closed_trades_from_diag.py, also executed this session.
items.breakdown: 128 unwired = 10 skill-referenced + 109 referenced only by non-skill docs + 9 with no reference anywhere.
items.why_it_matters: Skills are this repo's binding invocation path ('skill-first lookup is binding', CLAUDE.md). A skill IS a runner — just an agent-executed one rather than a scheduled one. Grading it as rust inflates the headline number the operator's 2026-08-20 'stop building things half way' directive is measured by, and it errs in the DANGEROUS direction: it trains a reader to discount a list that also contains 9 genuinely-unreferenced tools. A guard that is noisy about correct work is the desensitized-alarm P1 applied to CI.
items.not_a_finding_about: Whether a skill-referenced tool actually RAN. It does not prove that — scripts/ops/trainer_dataset_gc.py is skill-referenced AND was measured on 2026-08-20 as having 0 mentions across 7,442 cycle-log rows. That is exactly why the two need SEPARATE verdicts rather than being merged into 'wired'.
items.proposed_fix: Give the guard a third verdict instead of two. `unwired` (no reference anywhere) · `doc_only` (prose references a tool nothing invokes) · `skill_invoked` (a binding skill names it — a runner, but an agent-executed one whose EXECUTION is unproven). Report the three separately so the headline counts rust and not correct work. Do NOT simply allowlist .claude/skills/ into 'wired' — that would hide the trainer_dataset_gc case, which is the real one.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) The guard emits three verdicts, not two. (2) Its headline count excludes skill_invoked. (3) The 9 no-reference-anywhere tools are each removed, wired, or annotated `# wiring: manual-only - <reason>`. (4) Re-run and state the new counts beside the old ones.

updates.note:
CRITERIA 1, 2 AND 4 MET; CRITERION 3 IS 7 OF 9 AND THE REMAINING 2 ARE DELIBERATELY LEFT.

(1) THREE VERDICTS. scan() now returns (rel, verdict, why) with verdict in {unwired, doc_only, skill_invoked}. A tool whose only references are .md files is split on whether any of them lives under .claude/skills/ — because a skill IS a runner, just an agent-executed one ('skill-first lookup is binding').

(2) THE HEADLINE EXCLUDES skill_invoked, in BOTH modes. The standing audit prints the three counts under the headline so a shrinking headline cannot hide a growing skill list, and the diff-scoped blocking mode no longer FAILS a PR for adding a tool its own skill invokes (it prints those as [skill] lines and returns 0). ⚠️ skill_invoked is a separate verdict, NOT a promotion to 'wired' — the row is explicit that folding it in would hide scripts/ops/trainer_dataset_gc.py, which is skill-referenced AND measured with 0 mentions across 7,442 cycle-log rows while its disk hit 93%. That case survives the change.

(4) COUNTS, BEFORE AND AFTER — and STATE THE POPULATION, because the tree also grew and a bare before/after would credit the reclassification with work it did not do:
  row as filed (410 tools):  128 findings = 10 skill + 109 doc_only +  9 unwired
  after verdicts (417 tools): 124 findings = 10 skill + 105 doc_only +  9 unwired -> headline 128 -> 114
  after annotations:          117 findings = 10 skill + 105 doc_only +  2 unwired -> headline 114 -> 107
The doc_only 109 -> 105 is NOT this change; those four were wired or removed by other work in the interim. What this change did is move 10 out of the headline and 7 out of unwired.

(3) SEVEN ANNOTATED, EACH WITH ITS OWN REASON — not a boilerplate. microstructure_probe (a once-per-program feasibility verdict), _labeling_gap_probe (a diagnostic for one named defect), _verify_score_semantics (a relay-run helper that is a committed file precisely because an indented heredoc terminator never closes), position_ranking (Tier-3 decision support that recommends nothing), regime_policy_coverage (an audit whose answer only moves on a Tier-3 event), paststop_forensics (a one-off fixed-window extraction kept as the reproduction path), volspec_probe (an on-demand registry read nothing consumes).

⚠️ TWO ARE LEFT UNANNOTATED ON PURPOSE, because `# wiring: manual-only` is a CLAIM and I have not established it for either:
  * scripts/ml/fetch_fred_macro.py — its docstring says it WRITES the data.jsonl that     market_features joins for the macro conditioning columns, i.e. a data PRODUCER. If nothing     runs it the FRED side-stream never refreshes, which would be a real pipeline gap, not a     manual tool. Note the sibling scripts/macro/fetch_macro_candles.py IS wired (five     workflows) and scripts/ml/fetch_fred_corpus.py's docstring calls itself 'the free adapter     AFTER fetch_fred_macro' — so there is a chain here to trace, trainer-side, before     declaring anything.
  * scripts/validate_registry_vm.py — 'verify config/strategies.yaml is consistent and all     referenced artifacts are in place BEFORE STARTING THE LIVE TRADER'. Nothing in the deploy     invokes it. It has a test (tests/test_s007_validate_script.py) which the guard correctly     ignores — a test proves it WORKS, never that anything RUNS it. Wiring a pre-flight check     into the deploy is Tier-2, so it is a proposal rather than a drive-by.
Annotating either would assert 'nothing needs to run this', which is the unverified-claim shape this repo forbids. THE ROW THEREFORE STAYS OPEN ON CRITERION 3.

Self-test 16/16 (up from 11 — the new cases pin the skill split in both directions).

RE-VALIDATED AGAINST THE GUARD'S OWN OUTPUT: I ran check_unwired_artifacts this review and it now has a distinct `skill_invoked` bucket (8 entries) separate from RUST, whose text reads 'a runner, but agent-executed: that it RAN is unproven'. So the miscount this row describes appears to be ADDRESSED — skills are no longer counted as 'nothing runs it'. Keep open only to confirm the 10-of-128 figure is gone; the vocabulary is clearly fixed.

items.title: alpaca_live go-live: the operator elected to fund it, and funding is the LAST step of three, not the first
items.source: Operator decision in the /system-review session 2026-08-24: 'Fund it and go live'. Raised at the time that funding alone does not make the account work.
items.why_it_matters: Two of the three blockers are scale-invariant and survive any deposit. Depositing first means real money behind a sizer that asks for up to 12.37x the account on a single trade, on an account where 128 of 186 routed orders (68.8%) are SHORT and cannot legally execute while shorting is disabled.
sequence: STEP 1 (Tier-3, Claude prepares): declare a bound on alpaca_live so no routed leg can size past the account - max_gross_exposure_pct and/or a per-position notional cap. The VALUE needs a basis, and the gross-exposure soak (/api/bot/exposure/soak) is the surface that supplies the distribution; per gross-exposure-governance-DESIGN.md section 7 a value with no soak behind it must not ship. Until this lands, funding is unsafe.

STEP 2 (OPERATOR-ONLY, broker-side): enable shorting on the Alpaca account (margin agreement / account settings). Claude cannot change a broker account's permissions. Without it, 6 of 16 legs are dead and 68.8% of flow is refused - the account would be funded and still mostly inert.
STEP 3 (OPERATOR-ONLY): make the deposit, then flip mode dry_run -> live via the sanctioned set-account-mode action.
STEP 4 (Claude verifies): re-read /api/diag/broker_account_status + the first live fills, and confirm silent_refusal_alert grades the account healthy rather than refusing.
items.already_done_2026_08_24: slv_trend_1h (the fleet's worst leg, 0 wins in 13 closed, -$5,375) was demoted live -> shadow this session with operator approval. It routed to alpaca_live, so it is already out of the go-live set.
items.resolution_criteria: All four steps complete and the account has placed at least one real fill that reconciles against exchange truth. Do NOT close this on the deposit alone.
items.evidence: (a) SHORT FLOW: 128 of 186 routed orders are SHORT (68.8%) and SIX legs are 100% short - gdx_pullback_1d, iaum_pullback_1d, gld_pullback_1d, slv_pullback_1d, ief_pullback_1d, tlt_pullback_1d - so they are entirely dead while the account has shorting_enabled=False. (This is WORSE than the earlier row's '60% / 4 legs'.) (b) SHORTING FLAG: /api/diag/broker_account_status?account_id=alpaca_live confirms shorting_enabled: False, status ACTIVE, trading_blocked false. (c) NOTIONAL: 5 of 6 measurable legs exceed whole-account notional - see BL-20260823-ALPACA-RISK-SIZING-EXCEEDS-ACCOUNT-NOTIONAL-AT-EVERY-FUNDING-LEVEL.

updates.note:
STEP 1 PROGRESS, and it is NOT the ceiling value — it is the reason the value could not honestly be chosen yet.

Step 1 says the value's basis comes from the gross-exposure soak. Measured it: alpaca_live reads 0.0 on ALL 91 rows over 22.7h with $200.10 equity and zero gross notional. That is correct and useless — the account is dry_run and refuses everything, so its own soak is a flat book BY CONSTRUCTION and can never produce a distribution. The chicken-and-egg is real: the design wants a soak before the ceiling, and the account cannot soak until it trades.

The only available basis is the paper mirrors, which DO have a distribution: alpaca_portfolio (a 14-of-16 roster mirror) runs 1.8422 min / 1.8569 median / 2.0062 max, and alpaca_paper 1.9953 max — a continuously ~1.85–2.01x deployed book. But both run on ~$90k MARGIN books ($98,618.60 and $83,405.94) and alpaca_live has $200.10. Whether a 2.0x multiple is even REACHABLE there depends on cash-vs-margin, which had no read surface — /v2/account returns `multiplier` and account_status() was discarding it. Fixed this session as BL-20260825-ALPACA-CAPACITY-FIELDS-FETCHED-THEN-DISCARDED.

SO STEP 1 NOW HAS A DECISION PROCEDURE INSTEAD OF A GUESS: read status_flags.capacity.multiplier on the live account. `2` ⇒ Reg-T, a ~2.0 ceiling is reachable and binds against the measured 12.37x sizer demand. `1` ⇒ cash, the multiple cannot exceed 1.0, a 2.0 ceiling is decorative, and the real bound is per-trade notional against a $200 balance under whole-share sizing — i.e. max_gross_exposure_pct would be the WRONG instrument and Step 1 needs restating.

⚠️ AND 22.7h IS NOT A SOAK. n=91, with only 286 of 1000 fleet rows in `rth` (384 extended, 330 closed) — under a third of the window observed a scheduled-open equity venue, and a max over a short window is systematically low. These numbers establish the SHAPE, not the ceiling. BL-20260809-EXPOSURE-SOAK-NOT-YET-TAKEN stays open and this does not close it.

updates.by: claude (overnight autonomous, operator-directed alpaca go-live push)
updates.note:
STEP 1's DECISION INPUT WAS FINALLY READ, AND IT VOIDS STEP 1 AS WRITTEN.

The 2026-08-25 update restated STEP 1 to say its input is status_flags.capacity.multiplier, and the read surface shipped the same day (BL-20260825-ALPACA-CAPACITY-FIELDS-FETCHED-THEN-DISCARDED). The READING was never taken until now — four days of downstream work waiting on one GET. That is the mechanical reason this lane felt circular.

MEASURED 2026-08-29T00:22:41Z, /api/diag/broker_account_status?account_id=alpaca_live:
  capacity.multiplier = 1  => CASH ACCOUNT
  cash = buying_power = regt_buying_power = equity = 200.10 (all four identical — no margin line)
  shorting_enabled = false; status ACTIVE; trading_blocked false; crypto_status INACTIVE
  daytrading_buying_power / pattern_day_trader / daytrade_count = ABSENT (omitted not defaulted; consistent with cash, since PDT is a margin concept)
  mode = dry_run — confirmed BOTH on the live diag AND in config/accounts.yaml

CONSEQUENCE 1 — STEP 1 IS VOID AS WRITTEN. By this row's own pre-registered procedure: multiplier 1 means the gross-exposure multiple cannot exceed 1.0, so max_gross_exposure_pct is DECORATIVE and is the wrong instrument. Step 1 needs restating as a per-trade notional bound.

CONSEQUENCE 2 — STEP 1 AND STEP 2 ARE THE SAME DECISION, which was not visible before this reading. STEP 2 says 'enable shorting (margin agreement / account settings)'. YOU CANNOT SHORT IN A CASH ACCOUNT — Reg-T short selling requires a margin account. So STEP 2 is an ACCOUNT CONVERSION, not a settings toggle; and that same conversion moves multiplier 1->2, which makes STEP 1's exposure cap the RIGHT instrument again with a basis already measured (paper mirrors run 1.8422 min / 1.8569 median / 2.0062 max). The sequence therefore forks on ONE operator decision — cash or margin — and neither branch is free: cash keeps 6 legs dead and 68.8% of flow unexecutable and makes T+1 settlement live-blocking (BL-20260823-ALPACA-CASH-ACCOUNT-SETTLEMENT-UNMODELLED, premise now MEASURED true); margin unlocks the flow and introduces PDT at 3 day-trades/5 days under $25k against a paper book measured at 14.9% same-day round trips (BL-20260823-NO-PDT-MODELLING-ON-ALPACA). Both constraints are modelled nowhere in code.

UNCHANGED BY EITHER BRANCH, AND NOT FIXED BY FUNDING: the scale-invariant sizing excess (up to 12.37x account notional on one trade) and the net-negative strategy set (16 legs, uso_trend_1h at n=10 carrying the whole positive result). Verified this session that alpaca_live.risk declares NO max_gross_exposure_pct.

NOTHING WAS CHANGED. No funding, no mode flip, no sizing edit, no routing edit. Full writeup + the ordered remaining plan with owners: docs/research/ALPACA-LIVE-GOLIVE-STATUS-2026-08-29.md

Triaged by this review for completeness — note it already carried a 2026-08-29 update from a CONCURRENT session, so two sessions touched this row today. Re-validated independently: alpaca_live reads balance $200.10, api_ok true, ZERO open positions, and zero gross notional across 1,848 exposure_soak samples; HEAD of main carries 'Confirm the $200 alpaca_live sizing wall'. This row is the SEQUENCE for a go-live whose blockers this triage found scattered across ~10 sibling rows: it cannot short (shorting_enabled False vs 60% short flow), the flag is read and consumed by nothing, it is on BOTH alert skip-lists, 4 of 10 priced symbols are unsizable at $200, 7 of 15 legs size above the whole account, the strategy set is net-negative except uso_trend_1h, and its paper mirror differs in roster, risk_pct AND symbol allocation. Tier-3 and the operator's; the sequence should gate on those, not just on funding.

items.opened_by: claude (/system-review 2026-08-24, found by a planted-omission self-test)
items.title: The M20 tp_geometry ratchet is an ABSOLUTE count over a population that can shrink — so demoting a leg loosens it by exactly that leg's unstamped cells, with no diff a reviewer reads as loosening
items.source: MEASURED this session. tp_geometry_legend._unstamped_ceiling was 234 and unstamped live cells were EXACTLY 234 — the ratchet was tight. Demoting slv_trend_1h live -> shadow (Tier-3, operator-approved) removed its 9 lever cells, 5 of them unstamped, from m20_coverage_rollup.cells(live_only=True). Unstamped fell to 229 against an unchanged ceiling of 234, leaving 5 cells of slack.
items.evidence: tests/test_m20_tp_geometry_guard.py's two planted-omission tests FAILED and that is how this was found: deleting one stamp produced 230 unstamped, still under the stale 234, so `validate` returned no problem and `any('above the recorded ceiling' in p)` was False over an empty list. Both tests pass again once the ceiling is corrected to 229.
items.why_it_matters: That guard's own docstring names the cheap lie it exists to resist: 'the cheap lie would be raising _unstamped_ceiling — which is why the ceiling lives in the matrix beside the legend rather than in this script, so raising it lands in a diff a reviewer reads.' A DEMOTE produces the identical loosening WITHOUT any such diff — the ceiling line is untouched and only an unrelated execution field moves. The protection is real but its threat model missed the population axis, so the guard can be loosened by a change nobody would review as touching it. 5 live cells could have lost their tp_geometry stamp silently.
items.fixed_in_session: The ceiling was corrected 234 -> 229 with the reason recorded inline in _unstamped_ceiling_note, so the ratchet is tight again. That fixes THIS INSTANCE, not the class.
items.proposed_fix: Make the coupling explicit rather than relying on someone remembering. Options, cheapest first: (a) have `validate` FAIL when the live-cell count changes without the ceiling being re-derived — i.e. record the live-cell denominator beside the ceiling and check both; (b) express the ceiling as a derived assertion (unstamped == ceiling) rather than an inequality, so any movement in either direction must be acknowledged; (c) have the execution-state change and the ceiling live in one place so a demote cannot land without touching it. (b) is closest to the guard's existing ratchet intent and is a one-line validator change.
items.not_established: Whether any PAST demote already loosened this ceiling unnoticed. The ceiling was exactly tight when this session started, which is consistent with it having been correct — but that is one observation, not a history. Checking would mean walking the ceiling value and the live-cell count together through git history.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) A demote (or any live-population change) either updates the ceiling or fails the guard. (2) A planted-omission test covers the POPULATION-SHRINK path specifically, not only the stamp-removal path — the existing tests catch it only because the ceiling happened to be exactly tight. (3) The git-history question in not_established is answered or explicitly dropped.

updates.note:
RESOLVED — and BOTH rows are resolved by the SAME change, because they are one defect with two filings (this row 2026-08-23, BL-20260824-DEMOTING-A-LEG-SILENTLY-LOOSENS-THE-M20-RATCHET 2026-08-24). Recorded as a class, per the /system-review backlog_classes mandate: three recurrences, all found by hand, none by the guard —
  2026-08-17  two cells STAMPED without lowering the ceiling  -> 2 cells of slack
  2026-08-23  eth_pullback_prop_2h demoted (live 423 -> 414)  -> 2 cells of slack
  2026-08-24  slv_trend_1h demoted                            -> 5 cells of slack

THE MECHANISM, one line: the ratchet tested `unstamped > ceiling` and NOTHING ELSE, so every way the count could FALL — stamping, or the live denominator shrinking under a demote — accumulated slack in silence. The 2026-08-23 instance is the proof that this is not theoretical: with 2 cells of slack, BOTH planted-omission self-tests failed with an EMPTY problem list. Un-stamping a live cell no longer breached. The probe had gone quiet and the guard was green.

THE FIX — the ratchet is now TWO-SIDED. `unstamped < ceiling` is a NAMED failure that reports the slack, the live population, and the two remedies it could be (cells were stamped, or the population shrank), and it tells the author to lower `_unstamped_ceiling` to the exact number in this diff. Criterion met: a population shrink now produces a named failure.

WHY NOT AUTO-COMPUTE THE CEILING FROM THE POPULATION, which this row also offered as an acceptable resolution: a self-computing ceiling can never fail, and a ratchet that cannot fail is the same as not having one. The reviewer seeing the number move IS the mechanism — the file's own docstring already says the ceiling lives in the matrix 'so a PR that stamps cells lowers it deliberately'. Auto-computing would delete exactly that property.

⚠️ A TEST WAS INVERTED, DELIBERATELY, AND THIS IS THE PART TO READ. `test_stamping_a_cell_does_NOT_fail_the_ratchet` asserted that stamping must pass, reasoning that 'the ratchet must not punish progress'. The reasoning is right; the assertion was wrong, because under a one-sided ratchet stamping is precisely what CREATES the slack the 2026-08-17 note describes. It is now `test_stamping_a_cell_WITHOUT_lowering_the_ceiling_is_a_named_slack_failure`, with the original intent preserved as a SEPARATE test — stamping AND lowering passes. Progress is not punished; progress that is not RECORDED is.

NEW TEST FOR THE PATH NOTHING COVERED: `test_demoting_a_leg_shrinks_the_population_and_is_a_named_slack_failure` flips a live row to `shadow` — what a Tier-3 demote does — so its cells leave the live_only denominator. It asserts BOTH that a slack failure fires AND that the message names the population shrink, because a demote and a stamping run need different remedies and a message that only says 'a number moved' sends the author to the wrong one. It raises rather than passing if no live row carries an unstamped cell, so it cannot become a vacuous pass — which is the specific bar the 08-24 row set ('the existing tests catch it only because the ceiling happened to be exactly tight').

STATE: the tree is exactly tight right now — 229 unstamped over 396 live cells against a ceiling of 229, slack 0 — so the two-sided check passes on the current file rather than shipping red. tests/test_m20_tp_geometry_guard.py 10 passed (was 8).

items.title: Strategy-DECIDED exits carry less provenance than janitor closes — 27.0% measured vs 52.0%, with 41.8% of decided closes carrying no stamp at all; vwap_cross is 22.9% of real-money closes and 65.7% of it is unstamped
items.source: MEASURED this session over the live journal, population = closed + non-backtest + pnl NOT NULL, n=1151 (whole history, not the review window). Rows pulled via the Data Explorer with filter_state=='applied' asserted before the count was trusted.
items.evidence: Bucketing every close as JANITOR (reconciler/orphan/netting/backfill/half-open/adopt) vs DECIDED (strategy monitor, bracket, intent layer): DECIDED n=419 -> 113 measured / 88 estimated / 43 fabricated / 175 unverified = 27.0% coverage. JANITOR n=732 -> 381/147/157/47 = 52.0%. Unstamped DECIDED closes by path: vwap_cross 67 of 102 (65.7%), pairs_revert 42 of 42, pairs_stop 37 of 37, sl_cross 21 of 96, tp_cross 5 of 17, time_decay 3 of 4. All 102 vwap_cross rows are account_class=real_money, i.e. 22.9% of the 446 real-money closed rows.
items.why_it_matters: The path whose quality M20 exists to improve is the path we cannot measure. Any exit-refinement result on vwap_cross or the pairs sleeve is unfalsifiable today: two thirds of the closes have no recorded provenance, so a lever that helped and a lever that did nothing produce the same evidence. This ALSO refutes the intuitive framing that the provenance gap is a downstream symptom of janitor closes — the measurement says the opposite, and improving reconciler coverage would not move this at all.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) Every DECIDED close path stamps exit_price_source at the point of close, with the same three-state discipline exit_anchor uses — a monitor-derived level is NOT a fill and must not be stamped as one (see BL-20260824-RECORDED-EXIT-PRICE-OUTNUMBERS-ALL-BROKER-TRUTH-COMBINED). (2) Unverified share of DECIDED closes falls below 10% on trades opened after the fix deploys — measured on that cohort only, never back-filled, since a zero stamped onto an old row asserts an observation nobody made. (3) A test pins that each decided path writes a stamp. Tier-2: it changes what the monitor records at close.
items.operator_decision: 2026-08-24 — operator selected this as the next work block, over 'exit execution path' and 'one divergence owner'. Rationale accepted: it is the smallest of the three and it unblocks measuring the other two.

updates.note: WRITER FIX APPLIED (Tier-2, M39A). Root cause was NOT a missing stamp path — it was that `_apply_update` wrote the note ONLY under `exit_price_source == "verdict"`, so the branch resolving a REAL venue fill stamped nothing and classified UNVERIFIED. Confirmed: of the 175 unverified DECIDED closes, 175 (100%) carry an exit_price and ZERO carry a stamp, and the string 'exchange' appears 0 times in the entire decided-close source distribution — that branch had never written a note in the system's history. No provenance vocabulary change was needed: `classify('exchange')` already returns MEASURED and the value is what this module's own docstring declares at L342. SECOND DEFECT FOUND BY THE TESTS, not by reading: the old verdict branch OVERWROTE an existing more-specific stamp (a `bybit_closed_pnl` row was laundered to 'verdict'), the same class as the unconditional overwrite fixed in `_sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced` the same day. THIRD STATE ADDED: a close with no price on either branch was silently skipped as 'nothing meaningful to source-tag'; it now declares UNMEASURED_MARKER (0 of 175 observed today — added so the state cannot become silent later). MEASUREMENT MADE REPEATABLE: `scripts/ops/provenance_exposure_audit.py` gains section `0a_coverage_by_close_path`, classifying in PYTHON via `provenance.classify_pnl` rather than re-deriving buckets in SQL; verified to reproduce the hand measurement exactly (decided 419/113 = 27.0%, janitor 732/381 = 52.0%) against a fixture built from 1324 real journal rows.
updates.remaining: (1) Criterion 2 is NOT yet met and cannot be checked today — it requires trades OPENED AFTER the fix deploys; measure on that cohort only and never back-fill. The `/system-review` `structural_health` key is what picks this up, and its `trend` field is where a non-improving result would show. (2) 79 of the 175 unverified rows are `pairs_revert`/`pairs_stop`, which run through `pairs_executor` and are NOT touched by this fix — that is M39 track B. This fix reaches 96 of 175 (vwap_cross 67, sl_cross 21, tp_cross 5, time_decay 3).

updates.state: MEASURED POST-DEPLOY — the (A) fix is working on every path it covers, and track (B) is now 100% of the remaining gap. Criterion 2 still NOT met, and now we know why: n=5.
updates.note:
Read live from the journal via the Data Explorer over the direct diag path (https://ict-bot.duckdns.org, served-by line confirmed). Bucketing and classification were IMPORTED from the shipped code -- `provenance_exposure_audit._close_path` and `src.runtime.provenance.classify_pnl` -- not re-derived, per this row's own note that a second definition of 'measured' is the `_regime_score_semantics` incident.

⚠️ **STATE THE POPULATION: this is the NEWEST 500 TRADES (ids 4524..5023 of 5023), a ~2-week window from 2026-08-09.** It is NOT the whole-history n=1151 the 27.0% / 52.0% figures came from. Nothing here may be compared against those numbers, in either direction. The denominator was checked, not assumed: the page's oldest row is 2026-08-09T16:26:50Z, comfortably before the cutoff, so the post-fix cohort is not truncated by the page size.

FINDING 1 — THE (A) FIX IS WORKING, AND CLEANLY. Of 107 DECIDED closes in the window, 82 are unverified and **every single one of them is `pairs_*`**. Every NON-pairs decided path is 0% unverified: `sl` 6/6 stamped, `exit_head` 3/3, `tp` 3/3, `tp_cross` 3/3, `sl_cross` 3/3, `stale_stop` 3/3, `stuck_strategy_watchdog` 2/2, `giveback_stop` 2/2. Against the original measurement (`sl_cross` 21 of 96 unstamped, `tp_cross` 5 of 17) that is a real change of state. ⚠️ But the per-path n is 2-6, so read this as *the paths that used to leak have stopped leaking on every row we can see*, NOT as a rate. And `vwap_cross` -- the row's headline path at 67 of 102 unstamped -- **does not appear in this window at all**, so the fix's effect on the single biggest contributor is UNMEASURED here, not confirmed.

FINDING 2 — TRACK (B) IS NOW THE ENTIRE REMAINING DECIDED GAP, which is stronger than the (A) update's estimate of '79 of 175'. On this window it is **82 of 82 = 100.0%**: `pairs_revert` 42/42, `pairs_stop` 38/38, `pairs_timeout` 2/2. There is no second cause left to find on the decided side.
  ⚠️ AND THERE IS A THIRD PAIRS EXIT REASON NOBODY NAMED: **`pairs_timeout`**. The (A) update scoped track B as '`pairs_revert`/`pairs_stop`'. A fix written against those two names would leave `pairs_timeout` silently unstamped -- small today (n=2) and exactly the kind of residual that survives a fix and reads as fixed. The stamp belongs at the single `db.update_trade` site, not per-reason.

FINDING 3 — CRITERION 2 IS STILL UNEXERCISED, AND THE REASON IS n, NOT NEGLECT. Criterion 2 asks for unverified share < 10% on trades **opened after** the fix. Splitting on the M39(A) merge (`05b06dd`, 2026-08-24T21:27:26Z) the post-fix cohort is **9 rows total, of which 5 are decided** (2 measured / 3 unverified). Five closes cannot decide a 10% threshold, and 40% over n=5 is not a rate. **Do not mark criterion 2 verified.**
  ⚠️ TWO REASONS THE 40% IS NOT EVEN ATTRIBUTABLE: (a) the split is on the MERGE time, but the trader deploys via `ict-git-sync` and restarts at-or-AFTER merge, so some of those 5 may have opened under pre-fix code -- the cohort is a superset, which biases coverage DOWN; and (b) `/api/diag/version` read `git_sha eebb8ebe` vs `git_sha_on_disk 44eeef93` with `restart_pending: true` at 07:15Z, i.e. the running process is one deploy behind disk right now. The running sha IS a descendant of `05b06dd`, so the fix is live -- but the exact moment it became live is not established, and this row should not pretend otherwise.
updates.remaining: Criterion 2 needs accrual, not work — re-measure the post-05b06dd cohort once the decided-n is at least in the dozens, on that cohort only, never back-filled. Criterion 1 is now specifically the pairs executor (track B): `src/units/strategies/pairs_executor.py:777`, the `db.update_trade` in `_close_pair`, writes status/exit_price/exit_reason/closed_at/pnl/pnl_percent and NO provenance key. Stamp at that one site so all three pairs exit reasons are covered by construction. Tier-2 (it changes what the order path records at close).

updates.note: ⚠️ RE-CONFIRMED AND IT IS THE DEEPEST STRUCTURAL FINDING IN THIS BACKLOG. Live perExitPath this review: the janitor/reconciler paths are the BEST measured (reconciler_filled 0.9487, sl_cross 0.8679) while the decision paths are the worst (vwap_cross 0.3431, stale_stop 0.3333, time_decay 0.25, intent_reduce 0.0, netting_attributed 0.0). The exits the system CHOOSES are the ones it cannot measure; the exits its cleanup machinery performs are the ones it can. Every exit-program verdict is built on the weaker half.

items.title: The pairs sleeve is an isolated order path that silently misses every cross-cutting invariant the main pipeline acquired — 79 of 79 closes carry no provenance stamp
items.source: MEASURED this session over the live journal, all closed non-backtest rows (n=1324).
items.evidence: pairs_revert 42 of 42 and pairs_stop 37 of 37 closes classify as 'unverified' — a 100% miss rate, the only exit paths in the system with no stamped close at all. The sleeve runs via src.units.strategies.pairs_executor.run_pairs_tick called directly from src/main.py, NOT through Coordinator.multi_account_execute; CLAUDE.md separately records that the netting-attribution reconciler skips pairs rows BY DESIGN, and that its execution gate lives in config/pairs.yaml enforced inside pairs_executor rather than in the coordinator fold. Three different invariants, three independent misses, one cause. It also contributes 28 pairs_half_open_cleanup closes.
items.why_it_matters: This is the general shape, not one bug: a path built AROUND the main pipeline inherits none of the cross-cutting concerns the pipeline has accumulated, and nothing detects the omission because each concern is implemented at the pipeline, not at an interface both paths must satisfy. The next isolated path will miss whatever the pipeline learns next. Same pattern one layer down: 14 reconcile/sweep passes and 23 env knobs handle journal-vs-venue divergence with no single owner, and 150 of 204 open backlog rows (73.5%) are that one class.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) The pairs sleeve stamps provenance on close, satisfying the same criteria as BL-20260824-THE-DECIDED-EXIT-PATH-IS-THE-UNMEASURED-ONE. (2) Enumerate every cross-cutting invariant the main pipeline enforces and record, per invariant, whether the sleeve satisfies it, is deliberately exempt (with the reason), or is missing it. (3) That enumeration becomes a CI guard so a future isolated path cannot silently skip them — presence-only markers are not acceptable (the new-table-wiring-guard lesson: a guard cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than none). Keep the sleeve RUNNING throughout — it is bybit_1 demo-only, so in-place work carries no real-money risk.
items.operator_decision: 2026-08-24 — operator chose 'conformance pass, keep it running' over adding a guard only, shutting the sleeve to shadow, or deferring.

updates.note: MEASUREMENT ADDED — the row carried the argument, now it carries the numbers. Measured by the /system-review session (board comment 5405944296), folded in here on handoff. POPULATION: the 400 newest journal rows, setup_type LIKE 'pairs_%', n=119 closed. DECIDED closes (pairs_stop 34 · pairs_revert 33 · pairs_half_open_cleanup 24 · pairs_timeout 2) = 93, of which 93 carry NO exit_price_source and 93 have non-null pnl — every decided pairs close books realised PnL with zero provenance and grades UNVERIFIED under classify_pnl. JANITOR closes (reconciler_filled) = 26, of which 0 are silent; that path stamps correctly (candle_at_close ×23, entry_order_avg_price_unreliable ×3). 93/93 vs 0/26 is TOTAL separation. This reproduces INDEPENDENTLY, inside the isolated pairs executor, the same decided-vs-janitor inversion measured on the main system (decided 113/419 = 27.0% measured vs janitor 381/732 = 52.0%) — the strongest available evidence for this row's thesis that pairs_executor misses cross-cutting invariants BY CONSTRUCTION, not by oversight. Note the main system's own filing hypothesis ('the gap is downstream of janitor closes') was REFUTED by its own measurement: the path that made a DECISION is the badly-measured one.

⚠️ RE-CONFIRMED WITH FOUR INDEPENDENT SYMPTOMS THIS REVIEW: (1) 35 half-open cleanups in 9 days; (2) placeholder geometry on both live legs (SL exactly 2x entry, TP exactly entry/2); (3) 17 of 42 pairs closes exiting via a janitor path; (4) pairs closes carrying pnlCoverage 0.0. An isolated order path that misses every cross-cutting invariant is not a strategy bug, it is an architecture decision with compounding cost — which is exactly what this row says.

items.title: e35-bracket-sweep.yml cannot schedule a single job on a fresh CI checkout, and has never run
items.source: MEASURED this session by running the planner against an empty data dir, and confirmed against the Actions API.
items.evidence: `python3 scripts/research/e35_shard_plan.py --data-dir <empty>` returns `shard-plan: 0 job(s); 55 not scheduled (data_missing=43, out_of_scope_family=12)` and exits 1. Cause: it plans through `e35_bracket_geometry_sweep.plan_legs`, which requires each leg's CSV to be ON DISK — but leg CSVs are gitignored (.gitignore:73 `data/*.csv`) and on that workflow the CSV is fetched by the very per-leg job the planner is supposed to schedule. `actions_list` reports total_count 0 for the workflow, so it has never executed and nobody found this.
items.why_it_matters: The refusal itself is CORRECT — an empty matrix is a green run that tested nothing, and the module deliberately fails rather than emitting an empty include list. The defect is planning on a precondition the plan itself creates. Until fixed, the e35 sharding lane (built to survive sandbox recycles on a multi-hour sweep) is unusable.
items.resolution_criteria: e35-bracket-sweep.yml completes a real run with a non-empty matrix, evidenced by a run id. 'Could not reproduce' is NOT a valid close — the reproduction is one command against an empty --data-dir.
items.proposed_fix: Add `--ignore-missing-data` to e35_shard_plan.py (default OFF so local behaviour is unchanged) that plans from config alone, mirroring plan_legs' scope EXACTLY — same config read, same fleet.classify family filter, same symbol/timeframe resolution, and deliberately the same absence of an `enabled` check — dropping only the data-presence gate. Set it in the workflow. `scripts/research/pullback_frac_cross_leg_sweep.py::plan_shards` is a working reference implementation.
items.notes: A drafted patch exists but was deliberately NOT bundled into this session's PRs (it is another sweep's tool).
items.resolution: FIXED in #10239 (`--ignore-missing-data`, default OFF, dropping ONLY the data-presence gate inside `plan_legs` so leg scope stays one loop) and VERIFIED by a real run. ⚠️ READ THE SPLIT, NOT JUST THE RUN ID. Run 32783849276 — the workflow's FIRST EVER execution (`actions_list` total_count was 0 before it, which independently confirms the premise this row was filed on) — COMPLETED with 46 jobs = 1 plan + 43 legs + aggregate + corpus, both terminal jobs green and the corpus job committing its rows. Of the 43 legs: 19 SUCCEEDED (every crypto leg, artifacts uploaded) and 24 FAILED (every non-crypto leg). The 24 failures are NOT this defect and NOT a regression of its fix: they are BL-20260824-E35-SWEEP-FEED-IS-BINANCE-ONLY-FOR-A-MOSTLY-NON-CRYPTO-MATRIX, a separate pre-existing defect that became observable only BECAUSE the planner started working, and which is itself now fixed in #10244 (19 binance_vision + 21 dukascopy + 3 refused at plan time = 43). Stating the split here so a future reader of a 24-failure run does not read it as either a clean pass or a broken planner. The 19/24 outcome was PREDICTED from the feed analysis before the run finished and matched exactly. Tallied across BOTH pages of the jobs API — page 1 returns 30 of 46, so a one-page read under-counts.

items.title: artifact-validity-guard runs at 43.9s against run_guards.py's 60s timeout, on a test whose runtime varies 3x run-to-run
items.source: MEASURED this session, repeated runs in one sandbox.
items.evidence: The guard FAILED once locally (timeout) and PASSED on re-run at 43.9s; scripts/ci/run_guards.py:1063 uses timeout=60. The cost is tests/test_check_backlog_refs.py::TestReformatDoesNotLookLikeIntroduction (17.08s + 11.02s on two cases). The same file measured 29.44s, 15.16s and 9.80s in three consecutive runs. CONTROLLED CHECK: without that session's change 15.16s, with it 9.80s — so no change of ours caused it.
items.why_it_matters: A guard whose pass/fail depends on host timing produces a RED THAT MEANS NOTHING, which is 'green is not evidence' inverted: the next session to hit it will either chase a phantom defect or learn to ignore a guard. It passes in CI today, so this is pre-emptive rather than active.
items.resolution_criteria: Either the two slow cases are made deterministic/faster, or the guard gets a timeout with headroom over its measured p99 — and the chosen number is justified by a measured distribution, not picked. Closing this by observing one fast run is NOT sufficient.
items.notes: Observed while running guards for an unrelated change; not caused by it.

updates.note: Re-validated and LIVE-RELEVANT: artifact-validity-guard is the guard that FAILED my PR today (via check_backlog_refs). It passed in 43.9 s against a 60 s timeout on a test whose runtime varies 3x — so a slower run would have produced a TIMEOUT indistinguishable from a real finding. My failure was genuine, but the margin is thin.

items.title: A workflow whose result goes only to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is write-only to the session that dispatched it
items.source: MEASURED this session: run 32762934189 produced a correct cross-leg verdict that could not be read back through the Actions API.
items.evidence: `aggregate` redirected with `>> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. Every per-leg job log was readable via get_job_logs; the consolidated verdict was not, because a step summary renders in the web UI and is not exposed through the API. Fixed for that workflow in #10231 with `tee -a`.
items.why_it_matters: This is the written-and-never-read class landing where it costs most — a research run whose answer exists and has no reader. It is a PATTERN, not a one-off: any workflow a Claude session dispatches and must then interpret has the same exposure.
items.resolution_criteria: Audit workflows that write to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY for whether their output is a RESULT a session must consume (vs. a human-facing render), and tee those. A checklist line in docs/github-actions-workflows.md would also close it.
items.notes: Only pullback-frac-cross-leg-sweep.yml is fixed; the audit across other workflows was not done.

updates.note: RE-CONFIRMED TODAY IN A NEIGHBOURING FORM: the grade-closed-trades action's full 66,841-byte output was written to an artifact and the issue comment, and the JOB LOG contained none of it — I pulled the log looking for the NDJSON and found only the workflow script. Results that reach only a summary or an artifact are write-only to the dispatching session.
