items.title: The web-sandbox pytest run diverges from CI — 95 collection errors and 34 failures CI does not have — so every session is pre-validating against a suite that cannot import FastAPI
items.source: MEASURED 2026-08-24 while validating M39(A). Full local run: `34 failed, 12137 passed, 21 skipped, 95 errors in 501s`. CI's pytest-run passed on the same commits all day (#10232, #10234).
items.evidence: The 95 errors are collection-time `pyo3_runtime.PanicException` in every test importing pydantic-core / FastAPI (tests/test_web_api_*.py, test_prop_report_ingest.py, test_s067_*, test_trade_scores_symbol_filter.py, …). CONFIRMED PRE-EXISTING, not caused by any change: stashing the working-tree edit and collecting tests/test_prop_report_ingest.py on pristine main reproduces the identical error. The 34 FAILURES are separate and their names were NOT captured (the background run piped through `tail`, so only the summary line survived) — so this row states the count and explicitly does NOT claim they are all environmental.
items.why_it_matters: A session that runs the suite locally and sees green is not seeing what CI sees, and one that sees red cannot tell its own breakage from the sandbox's. Today that cost a wrong inference in both directions: the pyo3 errors had to be re-verified against pristine main to be dismissed, and the 34 failures could not be attributed at all. The practical effect is that the sandbox suite cannot gate a push — only CI can — which is fine as a policy but is nowhere written down, so each session rediscovers it.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) root-cause the pyo3/pydantic-core panic so a local run matches CI, and confirm by running the full suite in-sandbox to the same pass/fail counts CI reports on the same commit; OR (b) if it cannot be fixed in this environment, record the limitation where a session will read it BEFORE trusting a local run (the session-coordination preflight is the natural home) and name CI as the only gate. Either way the 34 failures must be enumerated once against a pristine-main baseline, so the claim 'they are environmental' is measured rather than assumed.
items.detail: Operator decision 2026-08-24: file it and keep trusting CI for now, over identifying the 34 immediately (~16 min of runtime) or fixing the sandbox (its own piece of work).

updates.by: claude (session_01Gi3mgq; hit this class three times while validating the diag-token gate)
updates.state: A ROOT CAUSE THE ROW DOES NOT HAVE — the divergence is partly WHICH PYTHON, and `pytest` on PATH is the wrong one
updates.note:
MEASURED 2026-08-25, same sandbox, same commit, whole suite, `--collect-only`:
  `pytest`            (the binary on PATH) -> 7,875 collected, **327 collection errors**
  `python3 -m pytest` (the system python)  -> 11,280 collected, **104 collection errors**
Same repo, same moment, 3.1x the errors and 3,405 fewer tests -- decided entirely by how pytest was invoked.

CAUSE, read from the field: `/root/.local/bin/pytest` is shebanged to `/root/.local/share/uv/tools/pytest/bin/python`, a uv TOOL venv. `sys.path` carries NO dist-packages (verified directly), so it can import nothing the repo depends on -- yaml, pandas, numpy, httpx and fastapi are all ABSENT from it while `yaml` is PRESENT on the system interpreter. A session that types `pytest`, reads the failures and reports them is measuring the TOOL VENV, not the repo. This is invocation-dependent and therefore applies whatever the missing-package set happens to be.

THE 104 ERRORS ENUMERATED BY CAUSE, which criterion (b) asks for and this row says was never captured (a `tail` ate the names). Under `python3 -m pytest --collect-only`:
  pandas 45 - fastapi.testclient 31 - numpy 19 - httpx 3 - _cffi_backend 3 - ccxt 2 - fastapi 1
So the row's framing -- 'httpx and fastapi are absent' -- is right but is the MINORITY: those three names total 35 of 104, while pandas+numpy alone are 64 and are not mentioned. A remedy scoped to installing httpx+fastapi would fix a third of it and read as done.

STATE THE POPULATION, AND A CAVEAT THAT CUTS AGAINST CRITERION (a): these are COLLECTION errors under `--collect-only`, NOT the 34 test FAILURES this row is about -- different quantities, and I am not claiming to have identified those. And this sandbox's failures are plain `ModuleNotFoundError`, whereas the 2026-08-24 measurement recorded 95 `pyo3_runtime.PanicException` from pydantic-core. Neither reading is wrong: the sandbox image is NOT identical across sessions, so 'root-cause the pyo3 panic so a local run matches CI' may be chasing a target that moves between sessions. That is an argument for criterion (b) over (a), not a claim (a) is impossible.

CONCRETE SUGGESTION FOR CRITERION (b): whatever preflight text lands must name the INVOCATION, not only the limitation -- `python3 -m pytest`, never bare `pytest` -- because a session that follows 'CI is the only gate' will still run something locally, and today the default thing to type is the worse of the two.

ONE MORE INSTANCE OF THIS ROW'S OWN WARNING, paid today: `ruff check . | tail` reports tail's exit code. My PR #10251 went red on `guards` for a single F401, and the local reproduction only found it because ruff's rc was read directly. The row already records this shape; it recurs because the piped idiom is the natural one to type.

present_on_system_python: pytest (after an explicit install this session)

updates.note: ⚠️ RE-CONFIRMED AND IT SHAPED MY OWN WORK TODAY. The sandbox lacks pytest, fastapi and numpy by default — I had to pip-install pytest and fastapi mid-session to run 31 tests, and a test asserting the diag allowlist FAILED locally purely for a missing import until I did. So a session CANNOT trust a local green, and this review deliberately relied on CI rather than the sandbox run.

items.title: e35-bracket-sweep hardcodes BACKTEST_FEED_SOURCE=binance_vision for every leg, so 24 of its 43 legs (55.8%) cannot fetch data at all and each burns ~10 min failing
items.source: MEASURED 2026-08-24 from the FIRST-EVER run of the workflow (run id 32783849276, dispatched on main at 0570d94f immediately after BL-20260824-E35-SHARD-PLANNER-CANNOT-PLAN-ON-A-FRESH-CHECKOUT was fixed). Read from the job log, not inferred from job names; the leg population was computed by running the planner locally.
items.evidence: `.github/workflows/e35-bracket-sweep.yml:138` sets `BACKTEST_FEED_SOURCE: binance_vision` unconditionally for the whole matrix. Job 97611599854 (gld_pullback_1d) logs verbatim: `Fetching GLD D candles 2021-08-20 -> 2026-08-24 (source=binance_vision) …` then `ERROR: no candles returned (source attempted: binance_vision).` after 10m10s (22:17:07 -> 22:27:17), uploads nothing, exit 1. Job 97611599808 (gdx_pullback_1d) is identical. GLD and GDX are ETFs; Binance does not list them. STATE THE POPULATION -- `plan_legs(ignore_missing_data=True)` returns 43 runnable legs: 19 over 6 `*USDT` symbols (ADAUSDT, AVAXUSDT, BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT, XRPUSDT) which Binance CAN serve and which complete in ~6-9 min with artifacts, and 24 over 18 non-USDT symbols (GDX, GLD, IAUM, IEF, IWM, MES, MGC, MHG, QLD, QQQ, SCHA, SLV, SPLG, SPY, TLT, TQQQ, USO, XAUUSD) which it cannot. 24/43 = 55.8%.
items.why_it_matters: A full dispatch spends roughly four runner-hours on work that is guaranteed to fail, and returns a sweep covering only the crypto half of the fleet. The failure is LOUD per leg (exit 1, and the message names the source attempted -- which is why one log read was enough to diagnose it), so this is not a silent-wrong-answer defect; the cost is wasted capacity and a sweep whose coverage silently excludes every equity, ETF and futures leg. NOTE the interaction: because the run reports 24 job failures, a reader could mistake this for the planner fix having regressed. It has not -- the planner schedules 43 where it previously scheduled 0, and the 19 servable legs produce real artifacts. This defect is PRE-EXISTING and only became observable once the planner started working.
items.resolution_criteria: e35-bracket-sweep dispatches and every scheduled leg either fetches candles successfully or is refused BEFORE a runner is spent on it. Either (a) the feed source is resolved per-leg from the symbol (crypto -> binance_vision, equity/ETF/futures -> whatever source the trainer sweeps already use, e.g. the source behind scripts/ops/fetch_backtest_candles.py), or (b) the planner refuses an unservable leg at plan time with a stated reason, so the matrix contains only legs that can run and the census reports the excluded ones separately. A run whose job failures are zero AND whose scheduled-leg count is stated against the 43 planned is the evidence. Reducing the matrix to the 19 crypto legs with no record of the 24 excluded is NOT a valid close -- that hides the coverage gap rather than declaring it.
items.notes: The workflow's own header comment at line 132 already reasons about `the doomed ~14s Bybit retry loop`, so this failure class was in the author's mind when a single hardcoded source shipped for a matrix spanning crypto, futures and ETFs. Related but distinct: BL-20260824-E35-SHARD-PLANNER-CANNOT-PLAN-ON-A-FRESH-CHECKOUT (the planner half, fixed in #10239).

updates.note: Re-validated: 24 of 43 legs (55.8%) cannot fetch from a hardcoded binance_vision feed. A sweep that structurally cannot cover most of its own matrix.

items.title: check_workflow_catalog counts a filename mentioned ANYWHERE in the doc as 'catalogued', so a secret-emitting workflow sat with no catalog row while the guard reported 118/118 named
items.source:
MEASURED 2026-08-25. `get-diag-token.yml` -- the repo's only deliberate secret-emitter -- had NO row in the 'Complete workflow index' table of docs/github-actions-workflows.md. check_workflow_catalog nonetheless passed with 'all 118 workflow file(s) are named', because its Direction A regex `_ANY_YML` matches a bare filename anywhere in the doc and the file's only mention was line 311, an artifact-RETENTION note ('`get-diag-token.yml` at 1'). Confirmed by grep: exactly one hit for the basename in the whole doc, and it is that line.

The looseness is DECLARED, not hidden -- the guard's own comment says 'a row may cite it in prose rather than in a table cell, and both count as "named"'. So this is not a claim that the guard is broken; it is a claim that its declared tolerance has a cost that has now been paid once, on the worst-case file.
items.why_it_matters:
The catalog is what a session reads to learn what a workflow DOES before dispatching it. A workflow that emits a live bearer to a repo-visible surface is exactly the one a reader most needs a row for, and it had none for months while the guard read green. The guard's headline ('118/118 named', '100.0%') is the sub-class C shape from CLAUDE.md's diagnostic-provenance table: a clean-looking denominator over a population that was never actually checked for the property the label implies.

This is the same lesson as new-table-wiring-guard's presence-only `# data-wiring:` marker, which CLAUDE.md records: a guard that is cheaper to satisfy incidentally than deliberately drifts toward being satisfied incidentally.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) Direction A is narrowed to require a TABLE ROW (a backticked filename in the first cell of a `|`-delimited line in the index table) and the coverage line reports 'catalogued' rather than 'named' -- with any workflow that legitimately lives only in prose moved to the declared `_EXEMPT_WORKFLOWS` set with a comment saying why, which is the guard's own stated escape hatch; or (b) the tolerance is kept and the guard's OUTPUT stops claiming more than it checked, e.g. by splitting the count into 'in the index table' vs 'named only in prose' so a reader can see the difference. (a) is preferred -- the exemption set is 'EMPTY BY DESIGN' today, which makes it the right place for a deliberate exception. Whichever is chosen, the guard's self-test must plant a prose-only mention and show it is graded differently from a table row; today's self-test uses a doc where both fixtures are prose, so it cannot distinguish them and would pass either way.
items.next_action: Tier-1 CI change. Not bundled into PR #10251 -- that PR gates a live secret path and a guard-semantics change would widen its blast radius for no security benefit. The one instance found was fixed there (a real catalog row for get-diag-token.yml was added); this row is about the NEXT workflow that lands the same way.

updates.note:
RESOLVED via criterion (a) — Direction A narrowed, with one deliberate widening the criterion did not anticipate and which measurement forced.

WHAT SHIPPED. `documented_names` no longer matches a bare filename anywhere in the doc. Two shapes now count, and both are DELIBERATE acts of cataloguing:
  1. a backticked filename in the FIRST CELL of an index-table row, and
  2. a backticked filename as its own `####`-style SECTION HEADING.
A filename in running prose counts as neither. The coverage line says `catalogued`, not `named`, and the OK line spells the rule out.

⚠️ WHY SHAPE 2, AGAINST THE CRITERION'S LITERAL TEXT. Criterion (a) asks for a TABLE ROW and for anything legitimately prose-only to go in `_EXEMPT_WORKFLOWS`. Measured before writing the change: requiring a table row alone leaves 4 of 118 uncatalogued — and TWO of those (`sync-vm-secrets.yml`, `init-actions-secrets.yml`) have their own `####` section, which is MORE documentation than a row, not less. Exempting the two best-documented workflows in the doc would have been the letter of the criterion defeating its purpose, and an exemption set that grows for well-documented files is how an exemption set stops meaning anything.

THE OTHER TWO WERE GENUINELY UNCATALOGUED, and got rows rather than exemptions:
  `branch-protection-report.yml` — the read-only relay for GitHub ADMIN state (branch protection / required checks / enforce_admins) that the hosted MCP cannot surface. A session with no admin token is otherwise blind to whether a required check is actually enforcing, which given this session's own CI-not-attaching problem is not a hypothetical need.
  `rotate-account-keys.yml` — the legacy Bybit-only key-rotation path, superseded by `sync-vm-secrets.yml` and kept pending a migration PR. The row says so, so the next reader does not dispatch the superseded one.
`_EXEMPT_WORKFLOWS` stays EMPTY, which is its documented design.

THE ROW'S OWN EXAMPLE IS ALREADY FIXED, and I checked rather than assuming: `get-diag-token.yml` now HAS a table row (line ~1060) carrying the `repository.private` fail-closed note and the record that it had no row before 2026-08-25. So the instance was closed by other work; what this change closes is the TOLERANCE that hid it.

PROVED IT CAN GO RED, in both directions, rather than trusting a green: renaming one table row's filename makes the guard FAIL with both a missing-workflow line AND a phantom-reference line; restoring it returns 118/118. Coverage is 118 of 118 catalogued after the two rows were added (116 by table row, 26 by section heading, overlapping).

SELF-TEST — three cases added, one of them the point of the whole change:
  * a filename mentioned ONLY IN PROSE must now be flagged. The fixture reproduces the real shape — an artifact-retention line, '`x.yml` at 1' — because that is literally what counted as a catalog entry for months. WITHOUT THIS CASE THE NARROWING SILENTLY REVERTS.
  * a workflow under its own section heading must NOT be flagged (pins shape 2).
  * the existing Direction-A fixture was a prose sentence and correctly FAILED on this change; it is now a table row. That failure is the guard's self-test doing its job, not collateral damage.

items.opened_by: claude (session_01X2zMCh, Lane 0 closeout; found by re-measuring 0.3/0.5/0.6 rather than quoting them)
items.title: src/runtime/dead_leg.py exists so the offline audit and the live alert cannot disagree about a row, and nothing enforces that they don't — the instance is fixed, the CLASS has no detector
items.detail: src/runtime/dead_leg.py's docstring states its whole purpose: the offline report and the live alert grade a row through ONE module so they can never disagree. On 2026-08-24 bucket_for grew a second parameter (the declared-policy-skip bucket) and only ONE of its two callers was updated — silent_refusal_alert.py:216 passes entry_reason, dead_leg_audit.py:155 did not. The consequence is not cosmetic: the 'policy_skipped' bucket became STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE in the offline report, so a mode: dry_run account graded 'signalled_never_placed' — the module's most alarming verdict — wearing an account_class: real_money label. The two surfaces disagreed about the same account on the same day, which is the exact outcome the module exists to prevent. Fixed in #10257 (369ba45). What is NOT fixed is the class: a helper whose entire value proposition is caller parity has no guard asserting its callers pass the same arguments, so the next parameter added to bucket_for can silently strand the other caller again. Note this is the same shape as the guard family the repo already runs for written-and-never-read signals (provenance-consumer-guard, collapsed-state-guard) — a signal that IS read, by one consumer and not the other.
items.evidence: Measured on the live journal 2026-08-25: 156 of alpaca_live's 312 refusals in the window carry the dry_run_sizing_skip token that bucket_for recognises. The live alert bucketed them as refusing_by_declaration; the offline audit bucketed the same rows as signalled_never_placed. Independently corroborated by the concurrent /system-review (#10256 finding 5), which found the LIVE half of the same account mis-latched for 3.85 days — so alpaca_live was simultaneously falsely alarming on one surface and mis-graded on the other.
items.resolution_criteria: A CI guard (the canonical-db-resolver / provenance-consumer-guard family) that fails when a function in the shared-vocabulary set gains a parameter that not all of its in-repo callers pass — or, if a guard is judged too broad, a test that calls bucket_for through BOTH call sites with one fixture and asserts identical buckets, so a divergence fails a test rather than being discovered by a session reading a backlog. Closing this row on 'the instance is fixed' is explicitly NOT sufficient; #10257 already did that.
items.resolution: Resolved by #10264 (f2fcd1d): tests/test_dead_leg_caller_parity.py ships BOTH options the criteria offered, not the cheaper one. (a) PARITY — an AST check that every in-repo call site of a SHARED_VOCABULARY function supplies the same set of parameters, positionals resolved against the real signature so f(a, b) and f(a, reason=b) compare equal. Defaults COUNT, deliberately: the 2026-08-24 defect was a parameter WITH a default (reason: Any = None), so a rule exempting defaults would have permitted the exact bug. (b) BEHAVIOUR — one fixture through the real predicate plus a positive control that a genuine venue refusal is NOT swallowed as a declared policy skip, without which the check would pass for a predicate that says yes to everything. SHOWN TO CATCH A POSITIVE: replanting the real defect (bucket_for(status) with no reason in dead_leg_audit) fails the parity test by name, printing both call sites and what each supplies.
items.bookkeeping_note: ⚠️ This row sat `open` for ~1h AFTER its fix had merged, and was caught by re-reading my own filed rows rather than by any check. The criteria warn against closing on 'the instance is fixed'; the opposite drift — shipping the class fix and leaving the row open — is equally a false record and has no guard either. A reader during that window would have seen an open row for work already done and either re-done it or distrusted the backlog.
items.scope_note: Scope is deliberately narrow: only names in SHARED_VOCABULARY are inspected, NOT a repo-wide 'all callers pass all params' rule, which would be noisy and quickly routed around. Extending it means adding a name to that tuple. The first version of the check DID over-reach — it matched on the bare function name and flagged scripts/research/m20_ladder_headroom.py's unrelated verdict_for(stats, min_trades, ...) — and now resolves through the actual ImportFrom. A guard that flags an unrelated same-named function is noise, and noise is how a guard gets normalised and then worked around.

items.opened_by: claude (session_01X2zMCh, Lane 0 closeout; found while re-measuring 0.5)
items.area: market_data / IB clientId allocation / web-api vs trader socket contention
items.title: IB_MD_CLIENT_ID is read as the market-data clientId but NOTHING in the repo provisions it — the only supplier is a hardcoded "600" inside candles.py, so every OTHER caller falls through to exec_client_id + 1 and lands on the trader's own live socket
items.detail: market_data._ib_connection_identity resolves the IB market-data clientId as settings -> env(IB_MD_CLIENT_ID) -> exec_client_id + 1. local_pnl.last_mark_price passes {} for settings, and ib_paper.ib_client_id is 497, so with the env unset it resolves 498 — the clientId the trader's own market-data socket holds. The env var is not set by any unit file, deploy script, or .env template in the repo; grep finds exactly one supplier, a hardcoded "600" literal inside src/web/api/routers/candles.py::_settings(), which protects that ONE caller and nothing else. That is a reservation in name only: the var reads like a fleet-wide allocation and is actually a per-caller literal. The asymmetry is visible live and is the strongest evidence for the mechanism: /api/bot/candles returns real MGC/MHG/MES bars from the SAME web-api process in which the uPnL mark-price fallback returns 'unavailable' — one caller carries the literal, the other does not.
items.not_established: The live value of IB_MD_CLIENT_ID was never read, because the key was absent from get_env.py::ALLOWED_KEYS until #10257 added it. The operator could in principle have set it by hand. This row therefore states a MECHANISM that predicts the observed asymmetry exactly, not a measurement of the running value — reading it is now a one-call question via get-env, and that read should be the first step of any fix.
items.resolution_criteria: Two steps, and THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. (1) Read the live value via get-env to confirm the var is actually unset. (2) If unset: provision IB_MD_CLIENT_ID on the ict-web-api unit (600 is the value already proven by candles.py) — Tier-2, needs an operator OK — and ONLY THEN remove the hardcoded "600" from candles.py::_settings(). Removing the literal first, or in the same change without confirming the env landed, breaks /api/bot/candles on both the dashboard and the Android app. Closing this row also requires that last_mark_price resolve a non-colliding id, which is the thing the row is actually about; provisioning the var without verifying that caller's resolved identity would satisfy the letter and miss the point.
items.resolution: PROVISIONED AND VERIFIED LIVE. `IB_MD_CLIENT_ID=600` written to `/etc/ict-trader/web-api.env` (issue #10285) — the web-api-SCOPED file, reachable only after PR #10283 added `set-env`'s `env_file:` parameter, because the shared repo `.env` is loaded by `ict-trader-live` too and a write there would have moved the TRADER's market-data socket 498 -> 600 into a collision with the web-api's own 600 (IB error 326). Baseline first (#10284: `(unset)`/`(unset)`, both readable — an observed absence). Scoping proven after (#10286: the TRADER reads `(unset)` on both sides) — the assertion the web-api side could not supply, since it reads 600 either way. Regression check in the same window: MES/MGC/MHG candles all still real from `bot-exchange`.
items.operator_decision_step4: ⚠️ STEP 4 — removing `candles.py`'s hardcoded `"600"` — was APPROVED and then CANCELLED by the operator on 2026-08-25, on evidence that emerged after the original approval. The literal is DEFENCE-IN-DEPTH, not duplication: the env is read first and the literal is inert in normal operation, but it is the only thing between a DROPPED env var and a silent 498 collision, since `_ib_connection_identity` falls through to `exec_client_id + 1` with no error and no alarm. The repo has already paid for this exact class — `POSITION_NETTING_GUARD_ENABLED` was removed as a gate because the 2026-06-14 Ampere migration dropped the var from `.env` and silently reverted a correctness fix. The rationale is now recorded AT THE SITE in `candles.py::_settings()` so a future session does not tidy it away as redundant; that docstring is the durable half of this decision.
items.side_effect_recorded: Provisioning CLOSED Lane 0 item 0.5's mechanism as a side effect — the uPnL mask and the clientId collision are the same defect. That re-exposed the estimate governed by BL-20260825-REPAIRING-THE-UPNL-MASK-RE-EXPOSES-A-FABRICATION-PATH, a decision the operator had deferred; it was surfaced with the numbers before anything further and the operator chose to leave it exposed and take the provenance call separately. See that row for the live decomposition (MGC 36.2% / MES 7.1% / MHG 2.2% against a +$1,829.55 net that matches the original figure to the cent).

items.opened_by: claude (session_01X2zMCh, Lane 0 closeout; found by asking what happens AFTER 0.5 is fixed)
items.title: ib_paper uPnL currently reads 'unavailable' because of a SEPARATE defect, and that defect is the only thing suppressing a mark-price fallback with a known fabrication history — fixing the mask without fixing provenance re-opens BL-20260807
items.detail: Lane 0 item 0.5 is 'ib_paper positions show no unrealized PnL'. The obvious reading is that a value is missing and should be restored. That reading is incomplete in the dangerous direction. The uPnL path is unchanged since 2026-08-01 and IB reads connected with account_data_ready, so the fallback is not failing for lack of a broker; it is failing because last_mark_price cannot get a market-data socket (see BL-20260825-IB-MD-CLIENT-ID-IS-A-RESERVATION-NOTHING-PROVISIONS). Had it run over the three open ib_paper legs it would have produced approximately $17,966.50 of unrealized PnL, carrying unrealizedPnlSource: markprice_local — an ESTIMATE, on a futures instrument, multiplied by contract_value_usd. That is precisely the shape behind BL-20260807's unresolved $119,490-vs-$37.80 contradiction on this same account. So the CURRENT state ('unavailable') is honest-by-accident, and repairing the clientId collision in isolation would replace an honest gap with a confident estimate whose provenance nobody has re-validated since.
items.why_it_matters: The repo's own provenance discipline says an estimate REQUIRES an anchor and that a fabricated number is worse than a declared gap (src/runtime/provenance.py; the netting-attribution anchored/no_anchor/deferred ladder). A fix framed as 'restore the missing uPnL' satisfies the ticket and violates the discipline. The two changes are separable and must be sequenced deliberately, not bundled as one 'fix 0.5' commit.
items.not_established: SUPERSEDED 2026-08-25T11:25Z — the blocker cleared IN-SESSION. When this row was filed, /api/diag/exchange_positions returned positions: null for ib_paper, so the first resolution criterion could not be attempted. It now returns all three legs, and the criterion has been DISCHARGED (see updates[0]). What remains un-established is narrower and is stated there: whether BL-20260807's $119,490 came from THIS path at all — the multiplier handling, the obvious candidate, has now been RULED OUT.
items.resolution_criteria: Before the clientId collision is repaired: establish what markprice_local would produce for ib_paper against exchange truth (requires the ib_paper exchange-position read to work, or an equivalent broker-side read), and confirm the multiplier handling that produced BL-20260807's $119,490. Then either (a) restore the fallback WITH its provenance label surfaced and a bound on the estimate, or (b) leave it declaring 'unavailable' deliberately and record THAT as the intended state rather than as a bug. Closing this row by making the number appear again, without either establishing its correctness or declaring it an estimate, is the failure mode this row exists to prevent.

updates.what: First resolution criterion DISCHARGED: measured what markprice_local would produce, against exchange truth.

measured.population: the 3 open ib_paper legs, marks read 2026-08-25T11:2xZ; a point-in-time reading, not a distribution
measured.journal_vs_exchange_agreement: direction and size AGREE on all three (MGC sell/short 51.0, MHG buy/long 29.0, MES buy/long 15.0), so 0.5 is NOT a position-divergence problem
measured.upnl_pct_of_notional: 0.467% (journal basis) / 0.521% (exchange basis) — plausible in magnitude, which is why it would not look wrong

updates.ruled_out: THE MULTIPLIER HANDLING IS CORRECT and is no longer a candidate for BL-20260807's $119,490. local_pnl computes (exit - entry) * qty * contract_value_usd, negated for a short, and contract_value_usd resolves from config/instruments.yaml (MGC 10.0, MHG 2500.0, MES 5.0). Verified by reading the function, not by reproducing the figure.
updates.new_finding: THE ESTIMATE'S *ENTRY* TERM IS ALSO APPROXIMATE, AND NOTHING DECLARES IT. markprice_local prices against the JOURNAL's entry, but the account's real cost basis is the EXCHANGE's, and they disagree on every leg (MGC 4660.9 vs 4664.594; MHG 6.498 vs 6.5028; MES 7634.75 vs 7630.872). Choosing one basis over the other moves the total by $1,829.55 — 11.4% — with MGC alone accounting for $1,884.04 because 3.7 points of entry difference is multiplied by 510 oz. So the label 'markprice_local' names the MARK as the estimated term and implies the entry is known; both are estimates. A restored figure would be an estimate-of-an-estimate carrying an undeclared ~11% basis error.
updates.consequence_for_this_row: The row's thesis is UNCHANGED but better supported: restoring the value is still not the safe default. The specific fabrication mechanism feared (a multiplier error) is ruled out; a different, smaller one is now measured. Option (a) in resolution_criteria should therefore require the entry basis to be declared alongside the mark, not just the mark labelled as an estimate.
