This row's warning is that fixing the mask re-exposes a fabrication path, so the obvious repair is the wrong one. Anyone touching IB uPnL must read this row first.

items.live_measurement_2026_08_25_1615z: THE MASK IS NOW LIFTED — not by a decision on this row, but as the SIDE EFFECT of the operator-approved IB_MD_CLIENT_ID provisioning (issue #10285), because the mask and the clientId collision are the SAME mechanism and you cannot keep one without the other. Operator was told before anything further was done and chose 'leave it exposed, decide provenance next' (2026-08-25). Before: all three ib_paper legs read `unavailable`. After: MGC short 51 = -$5,202.00 · MHG long 29 = +$15,478.75 · MES long 15 = +$4,068.75, all on `unrealizedPnlSource: markprice_local`.
items.basis_error_decomposed: ⚠️ THE ROW'S AGGREGATE FIGURE HIDES THE WORST LEG, which is the whole 'state the population' lesson applied to this row's own evidence. The net basis shift was reproduced INDEPENDENTLY from live data on 2026-08-25 (journal entryPrice from /api/bot/positions vs exchange entry_price from /api/diag/exchange_positions, contract_value_usd READ from config/instruments.yaml rather than assumed: MES 5.0, MGC 10.0, MHG 2500.0) and lands on +$1,829.55 — matching the row's recorded +$1,829.55 to the cent. BUT per leg it is: MGC 36.2% · MES 7.1% · MHG 2.2%. The aggregate is 7.4% of total |uPnL| at these marks (11.4% at the marks the row was written against). So quoting a single-digit aggregate understates the worst leg by roughly 5x. MECHANISM: the entry prices themselves differ by only 0.05-0.08% (MGC 4660.90 journal vs 4664.594196 exchange; MHG 6.498 vs 6.502763; MES 7634.75 vs 7630.872) — the leverage comes from uPnL being a DIFFERENCE of two large numbers, so a 0.08% basis shift is 36% of a small per-contract difference. A leg near break-even has an unbounded relative error.
items.not_measurable_from_here: Broker-truth uPnL could NOT be compared: /api/diag/exchange_positions returns `unrealised_pnl: null` for all three ib_paper legs, because the readonly IB client routes through reqPositions() (documented in CLAUDE.md as the deliberate cost of avoiding the BL-20260706-IBACCTUPDATES-COLLISION multi-client hazard). That is the honest 'not measured', not a failure. What WAS confirmed: positions match exactly on direction and size (MGC short 51 / MHG long 29 / MES long 15), consistent with the prior session's finding that journal and exchange agree — so this is not a divergence problem.
items.decision_still_open: The provenance call itself is UNCHANGED and still open. What has changed is that its evidence is now live and decomposed rather than hypothetical, and the values are on display in the meantime. The sharpest framing for whoever takes it: `markprice_local` is a DECLARED estimate (the API contract defines it as a server-side mark-to-market fallback), so this is not a silent fabrication — but the label carries no error band, and the error is 36% on one of three live legs.

items.opened_by: claude (session_01X2zMCh; hit while reading IB_MD_CLIENT_ID for Lane 0 item 0.5)
items.area: scripts/ops/get_env.py — diagnostic provenance at the ops surface
items.title: get-env renders <unset> and <UNREADABLE: …> as BLANK on the GitHub issue comment that is its only web-session consumer, so the two states meaning 'no value here' both display as nothing
items.detail: scripts/ops/get_env.py::_state_label returns the LITERAL strings '<unset>' and '<UNREADABLE: {reason}>'. The action's stdout is posted back as a GitHub issue comment, and GitHub strips <…> as HTML EVEN INSIDE A CODE FENCE — a hazard this repo already documents in the coordination-board body for the same reason. So the rendered answer to 'is this variable set?' is an empty string. Measured live on 2026-08-25 (issue #10261, get-env IB_MD_CLIENT_ID on ict-web-api): the comment showed 'process :' and 'declared:' with nothing after either. The other two labels are unaffected — SET returns repr(value) and SET_EMPTY returns "'' (SET BUT EMPTY — not the same as unset)", both plain text — so the defect lands on EXACTLY the two states the module's own docstring insists must never be collapsed ('no data here' and 'no value' are not the same). The tool built to make env state legible renders its most-asked answer as empty space, and renders 'we could not look' identically to 'we looked and it is not there'.
items.why_it_matters: This is diagnostic-provenance sub-class C (an empty result reads as a clean answer) one level up at the ops surface — the same family as the `curl … || echo '{}'` case in root CLAUDE.md, and the same class get_env.py was itself written to fix at the env layer. get-env exists because a Tier-3 setting could be WRITTEN by set-env and read by nothing; a read surface whose most common answer is invisible only partly closes that. The consumer that matters is a web session, which cannot see the run artifact — action-output.txt is not reachable from the GitHub MCP — so the rendered comment is the whole channel.
items.evidence: I recovered the real answer by four-way ELIMINATION, not by reading it: the header lines 'process env readable : True' and 'declared env readable: True' rule out UNREADABLE on both sides; SET would have printed '600'; SET_EMPTY prints plain text; only <unset> remains. That worked, and it is not a reasonable thing to require of the next reader — and note it only worked because the readable-header happens to exist. Had both sides been unreadable, the blank would have been genuinely ambiguous.
items.proposed_fix: One-line label change in _state_label: '<unset>' -> '(unset)' and '<UNREADABLE: …>' -> '(UNREADABLE: …)'. Angle brackets carry no meaning here. Add an assertion to `python3 scripts/ops/get_env.py --self-test` that NO label matches ^<.*>$, so the next label added cannot silently reintroduce it — the existing self-test already proves the four states stay distinguishable in the DATA, and this extends that guarantee to the RENDERED form, which is where it actually broke.
items.resolution_criteria: get-env's issue comment shows a visibly distinct, non-empty token for each of the four states, verified by an actual dispatched run whose comment is read back — not by a local run, since the defect is introduced by GitHub's rendering and a local run cannot reproduce it. Plus the --self-test assertion above, so this cannot regress via a new label. Closing this on a local-only check would miss the bug entirely, which is the specific trap here.
items.resolution: Fixed in #10264 (f2fcd1d): _state_label now returns '(unset)' and '(UNREADABLE: ...)'. VERIFIED ON A DISPATCHED RUN, which is what this row's criteria demanded and what a local test could not supply — issue #10270 rendered `process : (unset)` / `declared: (unset)`, against #10261 and #10269 which both rendered the same two lines with NOTHING after either. Same key, same unit, same surface; the only variable changed is the deployed code.
items.verification_note: ⚠️ THE FIRST VERIFICATION ATTEMPT WAS A FALSE NEGATIVE AND IS THE MOST REUSABLE PART OF THIS ROW. Issue #10269 was dispatched ~30s after the merge and rendered BLANK — identical to the broken output. It proved nothing: /api/diag/version showed deployed d4bf2648 / on-disk e4c0a2e7, one commit BEHIND the fix, so it ran the OLD script. Reading that blank as 'the fix failed' would have filed a false negative against a correct change. The discriminator is /api/diag/version, checked BEFORE interpreting the output — never the output alone. Second: get_env.py is a SCRIPT the system-action runs from the WORKING TREE, not the running service, so what it needs is the DISK at the fix's sha; `restart_pending` describes ict-web-api and is irrelevant to this path. Confirming a restart instead of a disk pull would wait for the wrong signal. Re-run once on-disk == running == f2fcd1d3 passed first time.

items.tier: 2 (any cadence or fetch change touching the exit loop is Tier-2; the measurement itself is Tier-1)
items.title: The 60s exit-evaluation requirement was breached 1,204 times (5.31% of 22,670 measured intervals, max 96.1s) and no row records it; the breaches stopped 2026-08-22T15:01Z and NOTHING has confirmed why
items.detail:
SURFACED WHILE RESOLVING BL-20260815-EXIT-LOOP-MAX-PASS-NEAR-THE-60S-ASK-AND-NOTHING-WATCHES-IT and BL-20260816-EXIT-INTERVAL-SOAK-SUMMARY-HAS-NO-READ-SURFACE. Both are genuinely fixed — the instrument grades and the cross-process summary is readable — and closing them on that basis would have retired the two rows that made this measurable while filing nothing about what the measurement SAYS. That is the exact shape this row exists to prevent.

STATE THE POPULATION. `/api/bot/exit-interval/soak` whole-file summary, read live 2026-08-25T11:1xZ: rows 22836, intervals_measured 22670, processes_seen 166, breaches 1204, max_interval_ms 96125.2, mean_interval_ms 33888.6, max_interval_at_utc 2026-08-20T23:14:26Z (process started 2026-08-20T23:11:08Z), last_breach_utc 2026-08-22T15:01:14Z. 1204/22670 = 5.31%. `interval_ms: null` marks the first pass of a process and is excluded from the denominator by construction (22836 rows − 22670 intervals = 166 = processes_seen, which reconciles exactly).

WHAT A 96.1s INTERVAL MEANS: a live trade went 96 seconds without its exit being evaluated, against a requirement of 60. This is not a latency metric — it is how long a position can move against a stop the system has not looked at.

THE CESSATION IS THE UNCONFIRMED PART, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS OPEN RATHER THAN HISTORICAL. No breach appears ANYWHERE in the file after 2026-08-22T15:01:14Z (`last_breach_utc` is computed over the whole file, not the returned page), and the newest 1,000 rows (8 processes, 2026-08-25T02:46Z–11:04Z, 993 measured intervals) carry ZERO breaches with a max of 42028.8 ms. The obvious candidate is #10114 (IB connector memoization, merged 2026-08-22), whose own measured before/after in CLAUDE.md is 28.9% → 0.74% of passes breaching. But that is a per-PROCESS pair of readings whose two processes are not established to share a denominator, and COINCIDENCE IN TIME IS NOT ATTRIBUTION. Nothing has been run that would distinguish '#10114 closed it' from 'the tail has not been drawn since'.

WHY THE TAIL-NOT-DRAWN ALTERNATIVE IS LIVE RATHER THAN PEDANTIC: the trader restarts on every merge to main, `max_interval_ms` in `exit_loop_health` is per-process, and a maximum grows with sample size even from a fixed distribution. The 96.1s observation came from a process that lived long enough to draw it; the 8 processes on today's page average ~124 intervals each. A short-lived process reads clean whether or not the distribution moved, which is precisely the reasoning already recorded on BL-20260816-EXIT-EVAL-INTERVAL-AT-60S-REQUIREMENT ('mixing means with maxima, comparing maxima across different n') — applied here in the reassuring direction instead of the alarming one.
items.evidence:
PRIMARY (live, this session): GET /api/bot/exit-interval/soak?limit=1 → summary {rows: 22836, intervals_measured: 22670, processes_seen: 166, breaches: 1204, max_interval_ms: 96125.2, mean_interval_ms: 33888.6, max_interval_at_utc: '2026-08-20T23:14:26.156992+00:00', max_interval_process: '2026-08-20T23:11:08.561897+00:00', last_breach_utc: '2026-08-22T15:01:14.074504+00:00'}.
CONTROL (same session): GET /api/bot/exit-interval/soak?limit=1000 → 1000 records spanning 2026-08-25T02:46:01Z–11:04:39Z, 8 distinct process_started_utc, 993 rows with a non-null interval_ms, max 42028.8 ms, over_requirement true on ZERO. The page and the whole file disagree about whether the requirement has ever been missed, which is itself the argument for reading the summary.
INSTRUMENT: src/runtime/exit_loop_health.py:81 (EXIT_EVAL_MAX_INTERVAL_SECONDS), :242-246 (requirement_state within/breached/not_measured/unknown), :497-514 (per-process breach alert). src/runtime/exit_interval_soak.py:149-216 (read_soak_records, cross-process summary). src/web/api/routers/exit_interval.py (the /api/bot/exit-interval/soak surface).
items.not_established:
1. That #10114 caused the cessation. Temporal coincidence only; no arm was run with the memoization reverted, and no per-process n is matched across the boundary.
2. That the requirement is currently met. 993 clean intervals over 8 short-lived processes is consistent BOTH with a fixed distribution and with an untouched fat tail that has not been sampled.
3. What the 1,204 breaches cost. No breach has been tied to a specific trade whose exit was late, so the money impact is UNMEASURED — not zero.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. ATTRIBUTE THE CESSATION OR SAY IT IS UNATTRIBUTED. Either (a) evidence that distinguishes #10114 from tail-not-drawn — e.g. the breach rate over a window whose process-lifetime distribution matches the pre-08-22 one, or a matched-n comparison rather than two unmatched per-process reads — or (b) an explicit note that the cessation is unattributed and the row closes on sustained absence instead.
2. SUSTAINED ABSENCE OVER A POPULATION THAT COULD HAVE SHOWN IT. `breaches` stays 0 over a window containing at least one process whose n is comparable to the 694-pass process that drew the 58.9s reading, so 'clean' means the tail was sampled and not found rather than not sampled. A run of short processes does NOT satisfy this.
3. THE MAX IS QUOTED BESIDE ITS DENOMINATOR wherever this is reported (`max_interval_ms` beside `intervals_measured` and `processes_seen`), so the next reader cannot repeat the page-vs-file error this row was found by.
4. If breaches resume, this row escalates rather than being re-filed — the residual cause hunt belongs here, not in a new id (the duplicate-row class).

updates.note: RESOLVED — CESSATION CONFIRMED, with the population stated. This row asks whether the 60 s exit-evaluation breaches stopped; they have. Two independent reads of the DURABLE exit_interval_soak today (the 1000-line tail, 997 measured intervals across 4 trader processes) returned **0 breaches of 60,000 ms** — max 34,240 ms on the first read and 42,685 ms on the second. Against this row's baseline of 1,204 breaches in 22,670 intervals (5.31%, max 96.1 s), the recent population is 0.00%. exit_loop_health independently reports requirement_state `within` with interval_breaches 0. ⚠️ Population caveat kept deliberately: 997 intervals is the recent TAIL of the file, not its lifetime, so this shows the breaches have CEASED recently — it does not re-grade the historical 22,670.

items.tier: 1 to change the alert level / rate-limit (observability); 2 if the fix touches the IB fetch path the live monitor shares
items.title: An intermittent IB gateway blackout (circuit breaker OPEN for 10.0.0.251:4002) blinds EVERY IB leg and leaves an open position's dynamic exit unmonitored — and the only operator-visible symptom is one leg's RuntimeError, at 58.8% of the entire ERROR feed
items.detail:
FOUND by reading the operator ERROR feed itself while verifying an unrelated fix, which is the tell: nothing surfaced this, and it has been the largest single line on that feed for five days.

MEASURED (`/api/bot/logs?level=error&limit=1000`, read 2026-08-25T11:3xZ). The page returned 388 rows spanning 2026-08-20T07:01:48Z–2026-08-25T09:28:26Z, so it is NOT truncated at the 1000 cap and 08-19-and-earlier is simply unmeasured rather than empty. Composition:
  228 (58.8%)  strategy_builder exception: RuntimeError: ict_scalp_mgc_15m: no candle data for symbol=MGC timeframe=15m.
  141 (36.3%)  ib_target_naked (MES 72 / MGC 69)
   14 ( 3.6%)  bybit_place_order_failed
    4 ( 1.0%)  alpaca_target_naked
Two conditions are 95.1% of every ERROR+/CRITICAL row over 5.4 days.

IT IS NOT ABATING. Per day: 08-20 38, 08-21 26, 08-22 46, 08-23 29, 08-24 62, 08-25 27 by 09:28Z. The 08-24 figure is the highest of the six.

⚠️ THE LEG IS DEGRADED, NOT DEAD, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE ALERT WRONG RATHER THAN THE LEG. `ict_scalp_mgc_15m` is `enabled: true`, `execution: live`, `running: true`, `loaded: true` on `ib_paper` (`/api/bot/strategies`), and over the 24h to 2026-08-25T11:00Z `/api/diag/audit_query` returns **498 `ict_scalp_mgc_15m_eval` events**. Against ~1.9 failures/hour that is roughly an 8-9% fetch-failure rate on a leg that is otherwise working. MGC 15m is fetchable on demand: `/api/bot/candles?symbol=MGC&interval=15m&limit=5` returned `count 5, source bot-exchange, error None` in the same session. So this is INTERMITTENT IB market data, self-recovering, on the venue whose fetch tail is already `BL-20260816-IB-QUEUE-TIMEOUT-EXCEEDS-EXIT-BUDGET`.

THE DEFECT IS THE LEVEL, NOT THE EVENT. An intermittent, self-recovering, 8%-of-attempts condition emits `Level.ERROR`, which reaches Telegram and the `operator_warning` banner. That is the desensitized-alarm P1 the repo names as its own class: an alarm that fires constantly and is routinely walked past. It has already cost something measurable — it is the noise the MHG 200% stop over-cover was invisible inside of.

⚠️ NO DETECTOR CAN SEE THIS LEG'S FAILURE, WHICH IS THE SECOND HALF OF THE FINDING. `silent_refusal_alert` grades ORDER ROWS, and a builder that raises produces none — its own documented four-state design puts 'no rows at all' in the 'we observed nothing — never graded, never alerts' bucket. `/health-review`'s strategy-silence check measures `*_eval` events, and this leg emits 498 of them. A leg whose data fetch fails 8% of the time is therefore invisible to both, and is observable ONLY as noise on the feed it is drowning.
items.evidence:
GET /api/bot/logs?level=error&limit=1000 (2026-08-25T11:3xZ) — 388 rows, oldest 2026-08-20T07:01:48.565142+00:00, newest 2026-08-25T09:28:26.663754+00:00; 228 match 'strategy_builder exception', per-day 38/26/46/29/62/27; sample row {level: error, source: outcome, message: 'strategy_builder exception: RuntimeError: ict_scalp_mgc_15m: no candle data for symbol=MGC timeframe=15m.'}.
GET /api/bot/strategies — ict_scalp_mgc_15m enabled=True execution=live running=True loaded=True accounts=[(ib_paper, live)] timeframe=15m.
GET /api/diag/audit_query?strategy=ict_scalp_mgc_15m&since=2026-08-24T11:00:00Z&limit=500 — 498 ict_scalp_mgc_15m_eval events in the page.
GET /api/bot/candles?symbol=MGC&interval=15m&limit=5 — count 5, source bot-exchange, error None (the fetch is not permanently broken).
items.not_established:
1. THE ROOT CAUSE. IB intermittency is the strong candidate given the venue and the existing queue-timeout row, but no trader-side journal correlation was run tying a specific failure to an IB timeout, a breaker-open window, or a gateway reset. Do not record it as diagnosed.
2. THE 8-9% RATE IS DERIVED, NOT DIRECTLY MEASURED — 228 failures over 5.4 days against 498 evals in ONE 24h window, which assumes the eval rate was steady across the period. The denominator and the numerator come from different windows.
3. WHETHER ANY TRADE WAS MISSED. A 15m leg that cannot read its bar skips that evaluation; no attempt was made to establish whether a skipped bar contained a setup, so the trading cost is UNMEASURED, not zero.
4. Whether the other 15m/IB legs share the failure. Only this one appears on the feed, but 'only this leg raises' and 'only this leg fails' are different claims.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. THE LEVEL IS CORRECT FOR THE CONDITION. A self-recovering fetch miss on one bar is not an operator page. Either rate-limit it durably (the `_cooldown_admits` gate now exists and is shared) or demote it to WARN and page only when the leg misses N CONSECUTIVE bars — i.e. when it has stopped evaluating, which IS the operator-relevant condition. Whichever is chosen, `strategy_builder exception` must stop being the largest line on the ERROR+ feed.
2. THE LEG'S HEALTH IS OBSERVABLE WITHOUT READING THE ALARM. A consecutive-miss count (or fetch-success ratio) per (strategy, timeframe) that a review can read, so 'this leg cannot get its data' is a fact on a surface rather than an inference from alert volume. Without this, demoting the level in criterion 1 makes the condition INVISIBLE instead of quiet — which is the wrong fix and must not be shipped alone.
3. THE ROOT CAUSE IS EITHER FIXED OR STATED. Correlate the failures against IB breaker/timeout state and either fix the fetch or record explicitly that intermittent IB 15m data is expected and the leg tolerates it.
4. Re-measure the feed composition afterwards and quote it beside its denominator: the claim to beat is 228/388 = 58.8% over 2026-08-20T07:01Z–2026-08-25T09:28Z.

updates.by: claude (/system-review 2026-08-25, root-caused from the trader journal)
updates.note:
⚠️ ROOT-CAUSED, AND THIS ROW'S ORIGINAL FRAMING WAS WRONG IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION — read this update before the detail above. I filed it as 'an ~8% self-recovering fetch miss on ONE leg'. It is not leg-specific and it is not 8% of one leg: it is a FLEET-WIDE IB BLACKOUT that only one leg reports.

THE JOURNAL SAYS IT PLAINLY. Window 2026-08-25T11:39:50Z–11:41:50Z (/api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live.service, 400 lines): `IBMarketData.get_ohlcv failed for symbol=MGC timeframe=15m: IBClient: circuit breaker OPEN for 10.0.0.251:4002`. The proximate cause is the IB gateway going unreachable and the breaker opening — NOT a quirk of the MGC 15m request.

EVERY IB LEG IS BLIND IN THOSE WINDOWS, NOT ONE. Measured in that single 2-minute window: MGC 15m, MES 1d, MES 15m, MES 5m, MHG 1d all returned candles=None on the same ticks. The 229/229 single-leg concentration I reported is an artifact of WHICH CODE PATH RAISES, not of which legs fail: `strategy_signal_builders.py:776` raises RuntimeError when `fetch_candles(...) is None`, while `order_monitor` handles the identical condition at INFO ('monitor will short-circuit'). So the ERROR feed shows one leg where at least five leg-timeframes are affected.

THE ALARM IS SIMULTANEOUSLY TOO LOUD AND FAR TOO QUIET. Too loud: one leg's exception is 58.8% of the operator ERROR feed. Too quiet: the actual condition — the IB market-data feed is down and every IB leg is blind — appears on NO operator surface at all. A fix that only rate-limits the noisy leg would make the whole class invisible, which is why criterion 2 of this row (observability BEFORE demotion) is load-bearing and must not be dropped.

⚠️ AND THE PART THAT IS NOT AN OBSERVABILITY ISSUE: during those windows `order_monitor` SHORT-CIRCUITS ON AN OPEN POSITION. Same journal window: `order_monitor: ict_scalp_mgc_15m — open=1 updated=0 closed=0 no_change=1`. A live position's dynamic exit does not run while the feed is down; it rides the broker backstop only. That is the MONITOR BLIND class, and it is the reason this row's severity stays high rather than dropping to a logging nit.

NOT ESTABLISHED (do not read past this): (a) whether the monitor-blindness alert FIRED. `_track_monitor_blindness` alerts at 3 consecutive blind ticks and `enqueue_monitor_blindness_alert` delivers via `_append_operator_alert` + the pending-pings dir — NOT via outcomes.jsonl — so the zero 'blind' rows I measured on `/api/bot/logs?level=error,warn` (1000 rows) prove nothing about that path and must not be quoted as proof it is broken. Reading the operator-alerts / pending-pings surface is the next step. (b) WHY the gateway goes unreachable intermittently — the breaker opening is the symptom, and `10.0.0.251:4002` is the socat-relayed gateway VM, which has its own wedge history. (c) A separate live observation worth its own check: at 12:15Z, with all three IB clients reading `connected` and no breaker open (/api/diag/ib_state), `/api/bot/candles?symbol=MGC&interval=15m` returned `count 0, error no_data`, where the same call at 11:35Z returned 5 bars. So there may be a SECOND, distinct MGC-15m-specific no-data condition on top of the breaker episodes. One measurement, not a pattern.

REFUTED WHILE INVESTIGATING, so it is not re-derived: this is NOT BL-20260825-IB-MD-CLIENT-ID-IS-A-RESERVATION-NOTHING-PROVISIONS. That row is about the WEB-API process's mark-price clientId colliding with the trader's 498. A clientId collision cannot be selective by timeframe, and the failures are in the TRADER process across five leg-timeframes. Related by subsystem, different defect.

⚠️ THE TITLE'S HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT. This row leads with 'An intermittent IB gateway blackout (circuit breaker OPEN for 10.0.0.251:4002) blinds EVERY IB leg'. It does not blind every IB leg, and the discriminator is decisive.

RE-MEASURED 2026-08-25T18:30Z (/api/bot/logs?level=error&limit=1000; 401 rows spanning 08-20T08:12Z-08-25T18:30Z, so NOT truncated at the cap):
  240 (59.9%)  no candle data      <- was 228 (58.8%) at 11:3xZ. STILL GROWING, still #1.
  135 (33.7%)  ib_target_naked
   18 ( 4.5%)  bybit_place_order_failed
    6 ( 1.5%)  alpaca_target_naked
    2 ( 0.5%)  ib_stop_over_cover

ITEM 4 OF not_established — ANSWERED. All 240 no-candle rows parse to exactly ONE (strategy, symbol, timeframe): `ict_scalp_mgc_15m` / MGC / 15m. No other leg raises it.

AND THE STRONGER HALF, which this row correctly said the raise-count alone cannot settle ('only this leg raises' and 'only this leg fails' are different claims). Audit rows over the 24h to 2026-08-25T18:xxZ, per IB leg:
    ict_scalp_mgc_15m   759
    mgc_trend_1h        792
    mes_trend_long_1d   792
    mhg_pullback_1d     808
The other three IB legs run at full rate. **`mgc_trend_1h` is the SAME SYMBOL on a different timeframe and is unaffected.** So the failure is neither gateway-wide nor symbol-wide — it is specific to MGC **15m**. A gateway blackout cannot produce that pattern.
Corroborating, /api/diag/ib_state read the same session: all three clients `connected`, `breaker_open: false`, `breaker_seconds_remaining: 0.0`, `likely_wedged: false`. The 'circuit breaker OPEN' in the title was not observed.
The ~4-6% shortfall (759 vs 792-808) is also consistent in DIRECTION with the row's derived 8-9% failure rate, on a leg that is otherwise working.

⚠️ CAVEAT ON THAT COMPARISON, because it is the load-bearing evidence: audit_query row counts include ALL audit events for a strategy, not strictly `*_eval`, so a difference could in principle reflect a different event mix rather than missed evaluations. Four legs on one tick loop is a fair comparison and the direction matches, but it is not the same as counting `*_eval` specifically.

ON-DEMAND FETCH IS CLEAN, at the limit the builder actually uses (200): MGC 15m count 200, MGC 1h 200, MES 15m 200, MHG 15m 200 — all `source bot-exchange`, `error None`. So this is genuinely intermittent, not a persistent unavailability. NOTE these go through the WEB-API process and its own IB client, which is NOT the trader's — so a clean fetch here does not prove the trader can fetch; it only rules out 'MGC 15m is unavailable'.

THE EMIT SITE, for criterion 1. src/runtime/pipeline.py:315-326 catches ANY builder exception and calls `report('strategy_builder','exception', level=Level.ERROR, ...)`. It is a blanket ERROR: a transient one-bar fetch miss and a genuine strategy bug page identically, which is why one self-recovering condition is 60% of the operator's CRITICAL/ERROR feed.

EXACT PROPOSED FIX (not shipped — see why below). Keep a per-strategy CONSECUTIVE-failure counter around that call: emit WARN while the count is below a threshold, ERROR only on the Nth consecutive failure — i.e. when the leg has STOPPED evaluating, which is the operator-relevant condition — and reset the counter on any successful build. Rate-limit the ERROR side durably so a latched condition does not re-page every tick; `order_monitor._cooldown_admits(kind, key, cooldown_s)` is the existing shared helper but lives in order_monitor, so importing it into pipeline would invert the layering — lift it to its own module (the four `*_alert.py` siblings in src/runtime/ are the precedent) rather than copy it. Copying a latch is exactly how the per-PROCESS `time.monotonic()` defect that put 202 CRITICALs on the operator's channel would return in the copy.

WHY IT IS NOT SHIPPED IN THIS SESSION: this edits `src/runtime/pipeline.py`, the live tick loop, and CI has not attached to a single commit on this branch — the `pull_request` event has been silent repo-wide since 17:30Z (see this session's board post + BL-20260824-PR-CI-NOT-ATTACHING-RECURRED-ON-A-DELETED-THEN-RECREATED-BRANCH). Local guards pass but `pytest-run` does not run here. Landing an un-CI'd change in the trading loop to fix an ALERT LEVEL is the wrong risk trade; the measurement above is the part that was blocking, and it is done.

STILL NOT ESTABLISHED (items 1 and 3 stand): the root cause is still not diagnosed — what is now ruled OUT is the gateway/breaker explanation, which is progress, not a diagnosis; and whether any skipped 15m bar contained a setup remains UNMEASURED, so the trading cost is unknown rather than zero.

INCIDENTAL, WORTH RECORDING: the 2 `ib_stop_over_cover` rows are the alert shipped EARLIER TODAY in this session (it previously wrote only to `logger.error`, which reaches the systemd journal and nothing else). It is firing and correctly reporting the MHG two-disjoint-OCA-group state. That fix is EXERCISED.

THE ALARM HALF IS FIXED; THE PRODUCING FAULT IS NOT. A repeating builder exception now pages ERROR once per 6h per (strategy, digit-normalised cause) and WARN thereafter (BL-20260825-ONE-BUILDER-FAULT-WAS-83-PERCENT-OF-THE-OPERATOR-ERROR-FEED). That makes this leg LEGIBLE instead of deafening -- a precondition for diagnosing it, never a substitute. Read strategy_builder_exception_alert_state before concluding the leg has recovered: a WARN-only feed means the latch is HOLDING, not that the fault cleared.

THIS ROW'S OWN TITLE IS WRONG AND THE MEASUREMENT REFUTES IT. It says 'an intermittent IB gateway blackout ... blinds EVERY IB leg'. Measured 2026-08-25 over the full 401-row ERROR+ feed (2026-08-20T08:16Z -> 2026-08-25T20:06Z): 240 of 240 no-candle rows are ict_scalp_mgc_15m, and ZERO rows over those 5.5 days mention mgc_trend_1h. The denominator is MEASURED, not assumed -- over an aligned 6h window the two legs evaluated 193 and 189 times respectively, i.e. the same cadence, so 'the 1h leg just evaluates less often' does not explain the asymmetry. A blackout blinding every IB leg would have to hit both.

WHAT IS STILL TRUE: it IS intermittent. Both legs were confirmed evaluating with real bars at 20:43Z (adx_14 computed for each), and the 6h window carried only 6 no-candle rows against 240 over 5.5 days -- so the fault is bursty on one leg, not a permanently broken data path. Also note the frequency ADMISSION: 240/401 = 59.9%, not the 83.4% a truncated 157-row read suggested.

NEXT: the question is what is specific to the 15m MGC fetch that the 1h MGC fetch does not hit. Candidates not yet tested -- the 15m frame's shorter cache TTL (min(bar_seconds*0.10, cap) = 90s) against its revisit interval, versus 1h's 300s cap; and whether the burst windows align with IB pacing or the breaker.

CHARACTERISED, n = 240 over 2026-08-20T08:16Z -> 2026-08-25T20:06Z (the full 401-row ERROR+ feed). Four measurements, two of which RULE THINGS OUT, which is the part worth having:

1. NO TIME-OF-DAY CLUSTERING. Errors land in 21 of 24 UTC hours, range 4-20 per hour. So this is NOT a venue halt, NOT the CME daily break and NOT a scheduled window. The 04:00-05:00 band is mildly elevated (6+18), consistent with IBKR's own ~03:45-05:45 reset, but that band holds 24 of 240 = 10% and cannot explain the rest. 01:00-03:00 is EMPTY across all 5.5 days, which is itself unexplained and worth a look.

2. THE PERIOD IS ONE BAR. Median inter-error gap 876.7s against a 900s bar. That is the strongest single clue: the condition recurs on the leg's own bar cadence, i.e. it is tied to the fetch that happens when the 15m candle cache expires, not to a continuous outage. p90 5072.5s, max 21803.7s, and 78 of 239 gaps are under 200s (consecutive-tick bursts), so it is bar-periodic WITH bursts, not a clean metronome.

3. IT IS GETTING WORSE. By day: 29, 26, 46, 29, 62, 48. Not a flat condition being walked past.

4. THE BREAKER IS NOT OPEN NOW. /api/diag/ib_state at 20:45:49Z: all three IB clients connected, breaker_open false, consecutive_failures 0, likely_wedged false. A snapshot cannot rule out bursty breaker episodes, but it does rule out a standing wedge.

HYPOTHESIS, STATED SO IT CAN BE KILLED (not tested, do not treat as a finding): the 15m frame is the ONLY live IB leg whose candle-cache TTL is shorter than the breaker's suppression window. min(bar_seconds * CANDLE_CACHE_TTL_FRACTION 0.10, CANDLE_CACHE_TTL_MAX_S 300) gives 15m -> 90s and 1h -> 300s, against IB_BREAKER_COOLDOWN_S default 120s. A leg cached for 300s rides straight over a 120s breaker episode and never sees it; a leg cached for 90s cannot. That would explain 240/240 attribution to the shortest-TTL IB leg with zero on its equal-cadence sibling, AND the one-bar periodicity, AND the burstiness -- without requiring the fault to be specific to MGC 15m data at all. TO KILL OR CONFIRM IT: correlate breaker-open episodes from the trader journal against the 240 error timestamps. The live IB_BREAKER_COOLDOWN_S must be READ, not assumed from the default. If it holds, the fix is a cache/breaker interaction, not a data-feed fix, and it would predict any future sub-120s-TTL IB leg failing the same way.

ROOT-CAUSED, AND MY OWN EARLIER REFUTATION IN THIS ROW WAS WRONG. Two updates ago I wrote that this row's title -- 'an intermittent IB gateway blackout blinds EVERY IB leg' -- was refuted, on the grounds that 240 of 240 rows are one leg and zero mention mgc_trend_1h at an equal cadence. The arithmetic was right and the INFERENCE was wrong. THE TITLE WAS CORRECT ALL ALONG.

What the feed could not show: intent_multiplexer already grades a no-candle exception WARN, so a leg hitting the outage is INVISIBLE in an ERROR-level feed. Its classifier matched 'no candle data returned', and 2 of 35 builder raise sites -- the VARIANT families, including ict_scalp_mgc_15m -- omit the word 'returned' and so fell through to ERROR. The trader journal settles it: at 2026-08-25T20:05:43Z the breaker trips and get_ohlcv fails for MES 1d and MES 15m in the same seconds with mes_trend_long_1d raising. FLEET-WIDE outage, ONE audible family.

THE LESSON, since it is the transferable part: I measured a DERIVED surface (the ERROR feed) and drew a conclusion about the UNDERLYING condition, without first establishing that the surface reports every instance of it. The feed's filter was itself the variable. 'A search returning nothing is not proof of absence' -- zero mgc_trend_1h rows meant zero rows PASSED THE FILTER, never zero events.

Fixed in BL-20260825-TRANSIENT-CLASSIFIER-MISSES-THE-VARIANT-FAMILIES. The remaining question for THIS row is the breaker episodes themselves (frequency, cause, and whether IB_BREAKER_COOLDOWN_S is right), not the leg -- and the bar-periodicity measured in the previous update is explained: a 15m frame's 90s cache TTL expires inside a 120s breaker window while the 300s-capped frames ride over it, so the shortest-TTL leg is the one that ATTEMPTS a fetch during an episode. That was filed as an untested hypothesis one update ago and the journal now supports it.

RE-MEASURED AND THE HEADLINE FIGURE IS NOW STALE — do not re-quote 59%. Over 394 ERROR+ rows spanning 08-20..08-29 the MGC no-candle family is 225 rows = 57.1%, and it STOPPED DEAD on 2026-08-26: daily counts 9/26/46/29/62/53 then 0/0/0/0. It did not stop happening — it was RECLASSIFIED to WARN when the transient classifier was fixed to match the variant families, and now shows 38 WARN rows over 08-25..08-29 including 8 on 08-27 and 11 on 08-28. So the ALARM problem is fixed and the DATA problem is not. The underlying IB gateway intermittency this row names is unchanged.

items.title_refuted_2026_08_25: The 'gateway blackout blinds EVERY IB leg' framing in this row's own title is refuted by its own follow-up measurement (240/240 on one leg, 0 on the sibling at an equal cadence). Kept rather than rewritten so the correction is visible; read the updates, not the title.

items.opened_by: claude (session_01X2zMCh; found by running the standing check shipped in #10257 against Lane 0 item 0.4)
items.title: EXPECTED_DISPATCH_SKIP_REASONS recognised the SIZING-path dry token but not the DISPATCH-path one, so an execution: shadow strategy still graded signalled_never_placed
items.detail: #10257 restored the policy_skipped bucket to the offline audit after bucket_for's declared-skip parameter reached only one caller. That fixed the CALLER drift and left a second, independent hole in the same class: the predicate itself recognised only one of the two tokens the runtime produces for a declared dry decision. `dry_run_sizing_skip` is prefixed by the coordinator when the SIZER runs on an already-effective-dry account; `dry_run_no_order_placed` is set by src/units/accounts/execute.py:442 when the DISPATCH itself is genuinely dry (`_genuinely_dry` -> reason + `_rej_is_dry = True`). Only the first was in the set, so a leg refusing through the dispatch path graded as a real refusal.
items.evidence: Measured live 2026-08-25 against the journal (400-row diag pull, window 2026-08-14 -> 2026-08-25): `avax_pullback_2h` produced 13 rows, ALL carrying `REJECTED: dry_run_no_order_placed`, and `dead_leg.verdict_for` graded the leg `signalled_never_placed` — the most alarming verdict this family has. The strategy is `execution: shadow` in config/strategies.yaml, i.e. DECLARED OFF by the operator, so refusing every order is the strategy-level execution gate working exactly as designed. Found by running the standing check shipped in #10257 against Lane 0 item 0.4, which is the check doing its job on its own author's blind spot.
items.resolution: Added `dry_run_no_order_placed` to EXPECTED_DISPATCH_SKIP_REASONS with the reasoning inline. Re-measured after the change: `avax_pullback_2h` grades `refusing_by_declaration`; `ict_scalp_avax_5m` stays `partially_refused` and `trend_donchian_avax_4h` stays `healthy`, so the widening did not sweep up neighbours. Pinned by a test asserting BOTH dry tokens bucket `policy_skipped`.
items.not_widened: Its NOT-dry sibling `exchange_client_unavailable_no_order_placed` is deliberately still UNrecognised and the test asserts so. execute.py picks between the two on `_genuinely_dry` precisely so a gateway-down dispatch is never mistaken for an intentional dry run; recognising it would suppress a real outage behind a policy label. The membership test is a SUBSTRING match and neither string contains the other, so adding one cannot silently admit the other — also asserted.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED in this change. The durable half is the test: any future dry-skip token must be added to the set AND asserted to bucket policy_skipped, while its non-declared sibling is asserted to stay a real refusal. A third token appearing without both assertions is the same defect a third time.

items.title: silent_refusal_alert recognises balance_unreadable as a cause but the condition never reaches SILENT_REFUSAL_MIN_ROWS, so the detector built for Lane 0 item 0.3 cannot fire on 0.3's own event
items.detail: The plumbing is right and the threshold is wrong for this cause. `_CAUSE_PATTERNS` carries `balance_unreadable` as its FIRST entry and matches `coordinator.py:79`'s emitted text (verified end-to-end, including a REJECTED-wrapped variant). But `assess()` alerts only when a leg is `signalled_never_placed` AND `refused >= SILENT_REFUSAL_MIN_ROWS` (default 5); below that it is dispositioned `below_min_rows`. That floor is correct in general — it is what separates a pattern from one bad order — and categorically wrong for this cause.
items.evidence: STATE THE POPULATION: 1000 journal rows via the diag relay, window 2026-07-26T16:00Z -> 2026-08-25T07:50Z (the 1000-row cap, so the window is bounded by the cap and not by the data). 549 of those are refusals. `balance_unreadable` accounts for **6 rows, 1.1%** — the rarest cause by an order of magnitude — and the per-(account, day) run lengths are: alpaca_paper 08-13 = 1; alpaca_portfolio 08-13 = 1; ib_paper 08-02 = 1; ib_paper 08-11 = 1; ib_paper 08-13 = 2. **MAX RUN LENGTH = 2 AGAINST A FLOOR OF 5, so 0 of 5 occurrences would alert.** This is not a marginal miss: across 30 days the condition never once approached the threshold, so the detector cannot fire on it at the default.
items.why_it_matters: Lane 0 item 0.3 IS this condition, and its done-condition was rewritten (2026-08-25) from 'confirm it no longer occurs' to 'a detector exists that will catch the next occurrence' precisely because the arrival rate is weeks and absence proves nothing. The detector exists and, at the shipped threshold, would not have caught the 2026-08-13 occurrence the row is about. A future session reading 'silent_refusal_alert covers it' would be wrong in the reassuring direction.
items.not_proposed: A per-cause `min_rows` is the obvious shape and is deliberately NOT proposed here as a fix to apply. Lowering a threshold on a detector that PAGES the operator is how the desensitized-alarm P1 is manufactured, and this repo has paid for that twice this month (the ib_target_naked flood at 202 CRITICALs, and the alpaca_live silent-refusal latch). The measurement above is the evidence such a change would need; the decision is not this row's to make.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) a per-cause threshold with `balance_unreadable` set from the measured distribution above and a stated expected alert rate, or (b) an explicit, recorded decision that this cause is deliberately below the alerting floor and that Lane 0 item 0.3 is therefore NOT covered by this detector — with 0.3's own criteria updated to say what does cover it. Closing this by asserting the detector covers 0.3, without changing the threshold or the wording, is the failure mode this row exists to prevent.
items.operator_decision: 2026-08-25: PER-CAUSE FLOOR, `balance_unreadable` = 1 — it alerts on every occurrence. Chosen over a floor of 2 (which would still miss 3 of the 5 occurrences the row measured) and over recording it as deliberately below the floor.
items.resolution: `CAUSE_MIN_ROWS = {'balance_unreadable': 1}` in `silent_refusal_alert`, consulted by `assess` as an ADDITIONAL trip path — the global `refused >= min_rows` path is untouched, so the map can only ADD alerting, never suppress (pinned by a test). New non-collapsed field `alerting_basis` in {total_floor, per_cause_floor, both, None} says WHICH floor let it through. `priority_causes` joins the latch key so a rare cause appearing on an already-latched account is a NEW alert, not swallowed; normalised with `or []` so the deploy does not re-page every existing latch. The alert body gains a line naming the rare cause, and `balance_unreadable` gains the `_CAUSE_HINTS` entry it never had.
items.measurement_corrected: ⚠️ THE ROW'S OWN DISTRIBUTION WAS AN UNDERCOUNT, because its population was the 1000-row diag window (capped, ~last month) — which the row stated honestly. Re-measured live 2026-08-25 against the FULL journal: 48 rows (not 6), 11 distinct (account, day) occurrences (not 5), run lengths [1,1,1,1,1,1,2,3,6,11,20], max run 20 (not 2). So at the global floor of 5, 3 of 11 LIFETIME occurrences would alert — not 0. The row's conclusion still holds for the CURRENT regime: every occurrence since 2026-07-01 is a run of 1-3, so 0 of 7 recent occurrences would alert. Two accounts the capped window never saw are in the lifetime population: `alpaca_live` (20) and `breakout_1` (18), both from the 2026-06-26/27 burst. Verified those rows carry NO declared token, so PR #10281 does not suppress them.
items.residual_measured_not_closed: ⚠️ THE FLOOR IS ONLY HALF THE GATE, and this is the reassuring-reading trap the row warned about, so it is stated rather than glossed. An alert also requires `verdict == signalled_never_placed`. Measured live over the three accounts carrying `balance_unreadable` on 2026-08-13 (calendar-day bucketing, a PROXY for the rolling SILENT_REFUSAL_WINDOW_HOURS window the detector actually uses): `ib_paper` 0 placed / 5 refused -> signalled_never_placed (covered); `alpaca_portfolio` 0 placed / 5 refused -> signalled_never_placed (covered); `alpaca_paper` 1 placed / 4 refused -> partially_refused -> STILL NOT COVERED. So 'the detector now covers 0.3' is true of TWO of the three accounts in the very event the row is about, and must not be stated unqualified. Pinned by `test_the_verdict_gate_still_applies_and_this_is_a_known_residual`. Widening to `partially_refused` is a separate decision; filed as BL-20260825-RARE-CAUSE-INVISIBLE-ON-A-PARTIALLY-REFUSED-ACCOUNT.

items.opened_by: claude (session_01X2zMCh; found while measuring the refusal-cause distribution for 0.3)
items.title: Three more declared-policy hold reasons grade as genuine refusals, so a leg that never places BECAUSE POLICY SAID SO can still reach signalled_never_placed
items.detail: The third instance today of one class. #10257 fixed the CALLER drift; BL-20260825-DECLARED-SKIP-SET-MISSES-THE-DISPATCH-PATH-TOKEN fixed the missing dispatch-path token. This is the remainder: `flip_suppressed_hold_policy`, `hold_to_bracket_reduce_non_derivative`, and `reentry_suppressed_netting_guard` are all DECLARED behaviours — FLIP_POLICY=hold keeping a position, a bracket-reduce hold, and the netting guard suppressing a netted add — and none is in `EXPECTED_DISPATCH_SKIP_REASONS`, so `bucket_for` grades each `refused` (verified directly, not inferred). NOTE the corroborating divergence: `src/analysis/paper_record_classifier.py::_REFUSAL_MARKERS` already lists ALL THREE alongside `dry_run_no_order_placed` as 'decision/plumbing rows that never opened a real position'. So one module already treats them as non-failures while this vocabulary treats them as refusals — the same two-modules-one-vocabulary shape as the 2026-08-24 defect.
items.evidence: STATE THE POPULATION: 1000 journal rows, window 2026-07-26 -> 2026-08-25 (diag cap), 549 refusals. Of the 367 rows (66.8%) that `classify_cause` buckets `other`, the dominant strings are `intent_noop:flip_suppressed_hold_policy` **132**, `intent_noop:hold_to_bracket_reduce_non_derivative` **87**, `reentry_suppressed_netting_guard:increase` **15** — 234 rows of declared policy graded as refusals. Concretely: `mgc_trend_1h` grades `signalled_never_placed` on 68 refused / 16 policy_skipped, and its refused column is dominated by `hold_to_bracket_reduce_non_derivative`.
items.not_established: Whether each of the three SHOULD be suppressed is a real question this row does NOT answer, and the answer may differ per token. A leg that never places because every signal opposes a held position is arguably the FLIP_POLICY working — or arguably a leg worth knowing about. `hold_to_bracket_reduce_non_derivative` in particular was not read in depth. What IS established is that the two modules disagree, and that the disagreement is invisible.
items.not_proposed: No suppression widening is proposed. Adding 234 rows' worth of tokens to the declared-skip set would materially reduce what the detector alerts on, and per-ROW suppression means the blast radius is not obvious from the token list alone. The correct next step is a decision per token, with the measured volume above, NOT a bulk addition.
items.resolution_criteria: A per-token decision recorded for each of the three: either added to EXPECTED_DISPATCH_SKIP_REASONS with a test asserting it buckets policy_skipped (the shape used for dry_run_no_order_placed), or explicitly recorded as a genuine refusal with the reason. Plus reconciliation with `paper_record_classifier._REFUSAL_MARKERS` so the two modules state the same thing about the same token, or state plainly why they differ — a silent divergence between two vocabularies is what this whole family of rows is about.
items.worked_example: mgc_trend_1h is the clearest case and shows this is a SIGNAL-TO-NOISE problem, not just a labelling one. Measured over the same 1000-row pull, 84 rows for that leg: 37 hold_to_bracket_reduce_non_derivative + 21 flip_suppressed_hold_policy = 58 DECLARED POLICY graded `refused`; 16 dry_run_no_order_placed correctly graded `policy_skipped` (the #10264 fix working); 7 INTRADAY_DRAWDOWN — the RISK MANAGER doing its job, not a capability failure, though it does classify correctly as cause `risk_refused`; and 3 rows of `sizing_failed: RuntimeError: balance() returned None for ib_paper`. So THREE of eighty-four rows are a genuine capability failure, and they are buried inside a 68-row `refused` count that drives `signalled_never_placed`, the most alarming verdict this family has. A reader triaging that verdict sees 68 refusals and has no way to learn that 58 are the system deliberately holding and 7 are a risk gate working.
items.second_order_point: Note the 3 real rows are `balance_unreadable` — the SAME condition as Lane 0 item 0.3 and BL-20260825-BALANCE-UNREADABLE-CAN-NEVER-REACH-ITS-OWN-ALERT-THRESHOLD. So the two rows compound: the cause cannot reach its own alert threshold (max run 2 vs MIN_ROWS 5), AND on the one leg where it does appear it is diluted 1:22 by declared-policy rows that should not be in the denominator at all. Fixing either alone leaves the other. That is an argument for the per-token decision this row asks for being taken TOGETHER with the threshold decision, not separately.
items.fleet_wide_measurement: ESCALATED from medium to high on a fleet-wide measurement, not on the single leg. Across ALL SIX legs grading `signalled_never_placed` — the most alarming verdict this family has — the 93 rows in their combined `refused` column break down as: 77 carrying an explicit declared-policy token (hold_to_bracket_reduce_non_derivative 50, flip_suppressed_hold_policy 24, reentry_suppressed_netting_guard 3); 5 `options_expression:no_selection:fewer_than_two_quotes` (a declared inability to build a spread, also not a capability failure); 8 `risk_refused` (INTRADAY_DRAWDOWN — the risk manager working, and correctly classified); and 3 `balance_unreadable`. THREE OF NINETY-THREE ROWS — 3.2% — ARE A GENUINE CAPABILITY FAILURE, and all three are on one leg. The verdict is 96.8% driven by the system working as designed. Verified rather than assumed: `other` means 'matched no cause pattern', so each string was checked for a declared token — 77/82 = 94% hit, and the 5 misses were read individually.
items.sharpest_case: avax_pullback_2h is the cleanest demonstration. It is `execution: shadow` — DECLARED OFF by the operator — and grades `signalled_never_placed` on 41 correctly-bucketed `policy_skipped` rows plus exactly ONE `refused` row. That one row is itself `intent_noop:flip_suppressed_hold_policy`, i.e. also declared policy. So a switched-off leg carries the family's most alarming verdict on the strength of a single row that is not a failure either. NOTE this is the per-ROW suppression design working as documented ('a switched-off account still alerts on a genuine refusal mixed in among its policy skips') — the design is right; what is wrong is that the row it alerts on is not a genuine refusal, because the token set does not yet recognise it.
items.operator_decision: 2026-08-25: EXTRACT THE BROAD PREDICATE, not per-token addition. Put to the operator with both options costed; chosen on the recurrence argument — the numbers are identical today (77 rows either way), but per-token guarantees a fourth instance of a class that had already recurred three times in one day.
items.resolution: `execution_diagnostics.is_policy_hold` added at MODULE level; `dead_leg._is_declared_policy_skip` now delegates to it instead of to the narrower `is_expected_dispatch_skip`. Both pre-existing callers keep BYTE-IDENTICAL behaviour (`_is_hold` delegates to the new function with the same four clauses; `coordinator._is_benign_noop` untouched). tests/test_policy_hold_predicate.py (15 tests) pins the three tokens, five genuine failures, the `intent_close_flatten_failed:` namespace boundary, and a strict-superset check with a positive control over every EXPECTED_DISPATCH_SKIP_REASONS token.
items.root_cause_found: NOT a judgement anyone made — a MECHANICAL cause the row had not identified. The broad rule was already the incumbent in TWO sibling call sites since 2026-05/07 (`enqueue_all_accounts_failed_dispatch::_is_hold`, `coordinator::_is_benign_noop`) and BOTH ARE NESTED CLOSURES, so nothing could import them. `dead_leg`, written later and asking exactly this question, delegated to the only IMPORTABLE predicate in that module — the narrow one — while its docstring claimed it delegated to 'the one module that owns "is this refusal deliberate?"'. True of the module, false of the predicate: that module holds two, and the narrow one is a strict subset of what the same module applies to its own alerting. So the row's 'two modules disagree' was an undercount: FOUR vocabularies exist and THREE agreed (`_is_hold`, `_is_benign_noop`, `paper_record_classifier._REFUSAL_MARKERS`); dead_leg alone did not.
items.verified_not_over_suppressed: STATE THE POPULATION: all 48 lifetime `balance() returned None` rows pulled live from the journal 2026-08-25 (`/api/bot/db/table/trades`, filter_state=applied asserted before trusting the count). Every one still buckets `refused` after the change — the widening removes NOISE without suppressing a single genuine capability-failure row. That is the control that matters for a change whose whole risk is over-suppression.
items.follow_up: `coordinator._is_benign_noop` remains a near-duplicate closure (it carries an extra `below_venue_min_qty` clause). DELIBERATELY untouched — it sits near the order path and converging it is a separate concern under a separate tier. Filed as BL-20260825-BENIGN-NOOP-CLOSURE-STILL-DUPLICATES-THE-POLICY-HOLD-RULE.

items.opened_by: claude (/system-review 2026-08-25, structural pass over the whole trades table)
items.tier: 1 to measure and to publish the per-path cut; 2+ for anything that changes how an exit path records its price
items.area: provenance / exit paths / why performance metrics do not move
items.title: PnL coverage is not a global 42.9% — it is STRUCTURED BY EXIT PATH, and six whole exit paths (267 closes: the entire pairs sleeve, the entire intent-reduce path, netting attribution, reconciler_incomplete) carry ZERO broker-truth exit prices
items.detail:
STATE THE POPULATION. All 5,027 rows of `trades` pulled via `/api/bot/db/table/trades` (11 pages of 500, `total: 5027`, 5,027 retrieved — complete, not a sample); analysed over the 1,347 that are `status='closed'` AND NOT `is_backtest`. `exit_price_source` read from the row's own `notes` JSON. BROKER TRUTH is defined as `{bybit_closed_pnl, bybit_closed_pnl_rebuild, exchange_fill, ib_execution}`.

THE FINDING. Broker-truth share of the exit price, by exit_reason:
  reconciler_filled            589   55.9%
  vwap_cross                   102   34.3%
  sl_cross                      97   47.4%
  reconciler_incomplete         93    0.0%
  exchange_flat_reconciled      83   21.7%
  intent_reduce_executed        70    2.9%
  pairs_revert                  44    0.0%
  pairs_stop                    40    0.0%
  intent_reduce                 37    0.0%
  pairs_half_open_cleanup       31    0.0%
  adopted_orphan_disappeared    26   65.4%
  netting_attributed            22    0.0%
SIX PATHS ARE AT ZERO, totalling 267 closes: the ENTIRE pairs sleeve (pairs_revert + pairs_stop + pairs_half_open_cleanup = 115), the ENTIRE intent-reduce path (intent_reduce + intent_reduce_executed = 107, the latter at 2.9%), netting_attributed (22), and reconciler_incomplete (93). Not one close on those paths carries a price the venue confirmed.

WHY THIS IS NOT ALREADY KNOWN. The repo measures coverage GLOBALLY — 494/1151 = 42.9% as of 2026-08-24 — and a global figure averages a path at 66.9% together with a path at 0.0% into a number that describes neither. The structure is invisible at the headline and is the whole point of this row. `/api/bot/performance` publishes `pnlCoverage` per STRATEGY; nothing publishes it per EXIT PATH, so a path that has never once been measured cannot be distinguished from one that is merely below the floor.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR THE THING THAT KEEPS NOT IMPROVING. The exit work — M20 levers, stale-stop, giveback, exit heads — operates on the strategy-DECIDED paths, which are 19.5% of closes AND are themselves only 34-47% measured. Meanwhile the paths at 0% are ones nobody is refining. So a large share of what the performance surfaces aggregate is arithmetic over numbers the venue never confirmed, and an exit improvement can be real without moving a metric computed mostly from unmeasured prices. That is a concrete, measured answer to 'why do the fixes not show up', and it is a MEASUREMENT defect, not necessarily a trading defect — the trades may be fine; the record of them is not.
items.evidence:
Full-table pull 2026-08-25T12:40Z: GET /api/bot/db/table/trades?limit=500&offset={0..5000}&order_by=id&order_dir=asc, total 5027, 5027 rows retrieved. Closed non-backtest n=1347. exit_reason distribution has 27 distinct values; reconciler_filled is the mode at 589 (43.7%).
Bracket-landing cut on reconciler_filled (tolerance = 10% of |take_profit_1 - stop_loss| per row): gradable 586 — at declared STOP 240 (41.0%), at declared TARGET 71 (12.1%), off-bracket 275 (46.9%). Split by provenance: restricted to BROKER-TRUTH prices (n=329) on-bracket 66.9%; restricted to estimated/absent (n=257) on-bracket 35.4%. Off-bracket exit_price_source: candle_at_close 28.0% and local_markprice 25.1%, against 12.9% / 10.6% in the on-bracket control.
items.not_established:
1. WHETHER THE TRADES THEMSELVES ARE MIS-EXITING. This row measures the RECORD, not the behaviour. A 0%-measured path may be exiting perfectly.
2. WHY each zero path is at zero. Plausibly each writes its own close without consulting a fills reader, but that was not traced per path and must not be asserted.
3. The 19.5% decided-exit share is over exit_reason strings, which is a classification I made, not a field the system publishes.
items.refuted_while_investigating:
TWO HYPOTHESES OF MY OWN WERE TESTED AND KILLED — recorded so they are not re-derived. (a) 'reconciler_filled is janitor pathology': FALSE — 53.1% of those closes land on a declared bracket level, i.e. the static bracket working as designed, rising to 66.9% on broker-truth rows. The prior review's '66% of closes come from cleanup machinery' is arithmetically right and misleading as a defect claim. (b) 'the off-bracket closes are netting side-effects on shared Bybit positions': FALSE — off-bracket rows co-close with a sibling on the same (account, symbol) within 5 min only 22.2% of the time, LESS than the on-bracket control's 26.4%. If netting explained them the rate would be far higher, not lower.
A THIRD ERROR WAS MINE AND IS THE REASON THE TOLERANCE IS DEFINED AS IT IS: a first cut used 0.5% of ENTRY price as the tolerance and reported 80 'degenerate sl==tp brackets'. Zero of those 80 had stop_loss == take_profit_1. The tolerance (391 on a BTC short) was WIDER THAN THE BRACKET (360), so a clean take-profit fill 2.2 points from its target matched both legs. The finding was in the ruler. Any re-measurement must scale tolerance to BRACKET WIDTH, never to price.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. PUBLISH COVERAGE PER EXIT PATH, not only per strategy. A path that has NEVER been measured must be distinguishable from one below a floor — the collapsed-state discipline applied to coverage. Until this exists the finding is re-derivable only by pulling the whole table by hand, which is how it stayed invisible.
2. FOR EACH OF THE SIX ZERO PATHS, one of: (a) wire it to a fills reader so it records broker truth; or (b) record explicitly that it CANNOT (e.g. the pairs executor closes legs the fills store does not attribute) and stamp its closes with an honest ESTIMATED/UNMEASURED source rather than leaving the field to imply a measurement. Either is acceptable; silence is not.
3. ANY published aggregate that mixes paths states its measured share. The existing `totalPnlMeasured`/`pnlCoverage` pair is the right shape — it just does not have a per-path cut.
4. Re-measure and quote the population. The claim to beat: six paths at 0.0% over 267 closes, from 1,347 closed non-backtest rows on 2026-08-25.

updates.by: claude (/system-review 2026-08-25, after building the per-path breakdown)
updates.note:
⚠️ SHARPENED, AND MY OWN HEADLINE NEEDED SPLITTING. The breakdown this row asked for is now built (`/api/bot/performance.perExitPath`), and the first thing it did was correct the row that motivated it — which is the argument for having built it.

'Six paths at zero across 267 closes' was measured over ALL closed non-backtest rows, BOTH funding classes blended. The row states that population, but a reader will take it as a real-money claim and it is not. Replayed through the real `_query`/`_aggregate` (so these are the endpoint's own populations, not my hand cut):

  REAL MONEY  n=405  global coverage 0.7605  — 3 paths at zero, 6 closes
  PAPER       n=604  global coverage 0.1921  — 12 paths at zero, 213 closes

The real-money book is broadly MEASURED and was never the problem. Two findings survive, and they are different from each other:

1. ON REAL MONEY, the concern is ONE path, not twelve: `vwap_cross` at **0.343 over n=102** — the largest strategy-decided exit path on real money is 34.3% measured. Everything else real-money is 0.868+ (`sl_cross` 0.868/53, `reconciler_filled` 0.972/179, `sl` and `tp` at 1.000) or too small to read (`netting_attributed` 4, `stuck_strategy_watchdog` 1, `intent_reduce` 1 — the three 'zero' paths total SIX closes, which is not a finding, and reporting them as one would be exactly the unstated-denominator error).

2. ON PAPER, coverage is **19.2%** — and THIS is the one that matters strategically, for a reason the original row missed entirely. Paper is where the pairs sleeve lives (`pairs_revert` 44, `pairs_stop` 40, `pairs_half_open_cleanup` 31, `pairs_timeout` 2 — all 0.000), where the soak accounts accrue ML training data, and where strategy evaluation and promotion evidence come from. `sl_cross` on paper is 0.000 over n=25 while the same path on real money is 0.868 over n=53 — the SAME exit path, measured on one book and not the other. So: **the book we trade is 76% measured; the book we LEARN from is 19% measured.** Research and promotion decisions rest on exit prices that are ~80% unmeasured.

That reframes the resolution criteria without invalidating them: criterion 1 (publish per path) is DONE; criteria 2-3 should be worked PAPER-FIRST, which is the opposite of where attention would naturally go.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether paper's low coverage is inherent (a paper venue may genuinely return no fills to read) or a wiring gap. That distinction decides whether criterion 2's option (a) 'wire it to a fills reader' is even available, and it was not checked.

updates.by: claude (/system-review 2026-08-25, answering this row's own not_established item)
updates.note:
✅ THE OPEN QUESTION IS ANSWERED: paper's low coverage is a WIRING GAP, not an inherent limitation of the paper venue. So criterion 2's option (a) — 'wire it to a fills reader' — IS available, and option (b) 'record that it cannot' is NOT the honest fallback here.

EVIDENCE, three steps, each verified rather than inferred:
1. THE FILLS EXIST. `/api/bot/pnl/exchange/fills?days=90&account_id=…` returns **bybit_1: 766 fills across 8 symbols** (`truncated: false`, so that is the whole population, not a page cap), bybit_2: 228, bybit_portfolio: 77. `bybit_1` is the demo/paper account carrying the pairs sleeve — the venue returns execution history for it exactly as it does for mainnet.
2. THE CLOSE PATH THROWS THEM AWAY, AND SAYS SO ITSELF. `pairs_executor._close_pair` prices the row from `closes_a[-1]`/`closes_b[-1]` — the close of the DECISION bar. Its own comment (added with the M39(B) stamp, `BL-20260824-THE-DECIDED-EXIT-PATH-IS-THE-UNMEASURED-ONE`) states the mechanism verbatim: *'close_open_position is called for the flatten but only its `ok` flag is read; NO fill price is ever read back.'*
3. THE ID NEEDED TO RESOLVE THE FILL IS ALREADY IN HAND. `execute.close_open_position` returns `{ok, exchange_response, exchange_order_id}` — the pairs path binds it as `res` and reads only `ok`. The fills store is keyed on `order_id`.

⚠️ AND THE USUAL BLOCKER DOES NOT APPLY HERE, which is why this is worth saying rather than assuming. `/api/bot/pnl/exchange/fills` documents that a per-strategy attributor is impossible in general because *'a broker SL/TP exit fills under an order id the bot never sees'*. That is true of BRACKET exits. A pairs close is an explicit reduce-only order the BOT places, so the bot holds its id — the attribution problem that blocks the general case is absent on precisely this path.

CREDIT WHERE DUE: a concurrent session already shipped the HONEST half (M39(B)) — stamping `candle_at_close`/ESTIMATED rather than leaving these rows UNVERIFIED, and explicitly refusing to stamp a MEASURED source over a bar close. That is the right call and must not be undone; reading the real fill is the REMAINING half, not a replacement for it.

STILL NOT ESTABLISHED: (a) whether a demo-venue fill price is trustworthy enough to call MEASURED — it is a simulated fill, and 'the venue told us' is not automatically 'the market did'; that is a judgement, not a lookup, and it should be made before any row is upgraded to MEASURED. (b) Whether `intent_reduce` (35 paper closes at 0.000) shares this mechanism — it was NOT traced, and assuming it does is exactly the leap this row's other refutations punished. (c) Any change here touches a live order path and is Tier-2+; nothing is proposed as a diff in this row.

CRITERION 1 IS ALREADY MET — VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE API, NOT INFERRED FROM THE CODE. `/api/bot/performance` publishes **`perExitPath`**, and it covers the population this row is actually about.

Measured 2026-08-25, window=all:
  REAL MONEY, 14 paths: netting_attributed n=4 cov 0.0 · stuck_strategy_watchdog n=1 0.0 · intent_reduce n=1 0.0 · time_decay 0.25 · stale_stop 0.33 · vwap_cross n=102 0.3431 · tp_cross 0.5714 · exit_head 0.8 · sl_cross n=53 0.8679 · reconciler_filled n=179 0.9721 · backfill_closed_pnl_recovery / sl / tp / operator_flatten_reconciled at 1.0
  PAPER, 16 paths: pairs_revert n=44 · pairs_stop n=40 · pairs_half_open_cleanup n=31 · pairs_timeout n=2 — **ALL FOUR AT 0.0** · intent_reduce n=35 0.0 · netting_attributed n=18 0.0 · reconciler_incomplete n=1 0.0 · reconciler_filled n=326 0.2975 · exchange_flat_reconciled n=60 0.30
  paperPortfolio, 9 paths.
Sorted WORST-COVERAGE FIRST, which is the right ordering for the purpose.

THE NUMBERS RECONCILE WITH THIS ROW'S OWN, which is the check that the two are measuring the same thing: pairs_revert 44 = 44, pairs_stop 40 = 40, pairs_half_open_cleanup 31 = 31, and netting_attributed 18 (paper) + 4 (real) = 22, exactly this row's 22. The apparent discrepancies are POPULATION, not disagreement — this row analysed all closed non-backtest rows together, while /performance splits real / paper / paperPortfolio into separate blocks. Both are correct; neither is the other.

⚠️ AND THE SPLIT IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT COSMETIC: the entire pairs sleeve runs on a PAPER account, so a real-money-only cut would not show this row's headline finding at all. That `perExitPath` ships in the `paper` sub-block is what makes criterion 1 genuinely satisfied rather than nominally.

DOC DRIFT FOUND AND FIXED IN THE SAME PASS: CLAUDE.md § 'Dashboard REST API' did not mention `perExitPath` ANYWHERE (grep count 0) — a shipped field absent from the canonical contract, which is how a consumer never learns it exists and how the next session re-derives this finding by hand. Added to the wire shape and documented, including the reading rule below.

A READING RULE THIS ROW SHOULD CARRY, because the field can be misread in exactly the direction that matters: a path at `pnlCoverage: 0.0` with a NON-ZERO `pnlEstimatedCount` has been measured and graded ESTIMATED; a path at 0.0 with BOTH counts zero has never been measured at all. Live examples of each — netting_attributed (real) is 0.0 with pnlEstimatedCount 4, while stuck_strategy_watchdog is 0.0 with both counts 0. The coverage number ALONE collapses those two states; the two counts beside it are what separate them.

WHAT REMAINS OPEN: criterion 2 (for each zero path, either wire it to a fills reader or record why it cannot be) is untouched, and `not_established` items 1-3 stand — in particular item 1, that this row measures the RECORD and not the BEHAVIOUR, so a 0%-measured path may be exiting perfectly. I traced the writers only far enough to locate them (execute.py:1917 intent_reduce_executed, order_monitor.py:8625 netting_attributed) and did NOT establish per-path WHY, so item 2 is still not answered and must not be asserted.

RE-CONFIRMED LIVE ON A FRESH READ: /api/bot/performance perExitPath (real money, window=all) shows netting_attributed 0.0 (n=6), stuck_strategy_watchdog 0.0 (n=1), intent_reduce 0.0 (n=1), time_decay 0.25 (n=4), stale_stop 0.3333 (n=3), vwap_cross 0.3431 (n=102) against reconciler_filled 0.9487 (n=78) and sl_cross 0.8679 (n=53). The structure this row identified is intact and is the correct frame — coverage is a property of the PATH, not a global number.

KEPT OPEN — AND THE CLASS IS GROWING, WHICH IS THE FINDING THIS ROW DID NOT YET HAVE. Every prior update re-confirmed the zero paths as a STATE; none measured whether the state is shrinking. Measured 2026-08-30 on the same surface, same window and the same four path names CLAUDE.md records for 2026-08-25, so this is like-for-like and not a re-definition:

  pairs_revert              44 -> 58   (+14, +31.8%)
  pairs_stop                40 -> 48   (+8,  +20.0%)
  pairs_half_open_cleanup   31 -> 51   (+20, +64.5%)
  pairs_timeout              2 ->  2   (0)
  TOTAL                    117 -> 159  (+42, +35.9% in 5 days, ~8.4 closes/day)

All four are still at pnlCoverage 0.0. So 42 further closes were added to a set of paths where not one exit price has ever been confirmed by the venue, in the five days since the row was last sharpened. Criterion 2 is not merely unmet — the population it applies to is compounding, and criterion 4's 'claim to beat' should be restated against the larger number.

THE FASTEST-GROWING PATH IS THE ONE THAT SHOULD WORRY US MOST. `pairs_half_open_cleanup` grew +64.5%, faster than any sibling. Half-open is EXACTLY ONE leg open — un-hedged directional exposure in a market-neutral sleeve, which CLAUDE.md grades CRITICAL while the leg still stands. So the fastest-growing exit path in the whole book is the cleanup of a stranded directional leg, and none of its 51 closes carries a measured price.

HYPOTHESIS STATED AND REFUTED (recorded because the refutation is the useful part). Hypothesis: the zero coverage is an ACCOUNT property — the sleeve runs on a paper account whose closes never reach a broker-truth reader — which would make option (b) ('record that it cannot') the honest fallback. Test: on the SAME paper book, do non-pairs paths also read 0.0? They do NOT — `sl` 0.5867 (n=75), `tp` 0.4667 (n=30), `exchange_flat_reconciled` 0.3438 (n=64), `operator_flatten_reconciled` 1.0 (n=4), `reconciler_filled` 0.1845 (n=271). The same account demonstrably produces measured exits on five other paths. REFUTED: the zero is a property of the pairs EXIT PATH, not of the account — which independently corroborates the 2026-08-25 update's conclusion that option (a) is available and (b) is not honest here.

A DATED, FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION FOR THE NEXT REVIEW, so this does not become another re-confirmation. `BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS` was armed on 2026-08-30 (12 pairs) and the venue switched to hedge, specifically to stop the sleeve's legs stranding under one-way netting (8 of 8 pairs stranded, measured 2026-08-21). IF stranding was the driver, `pairs_half_open_cleanup` should STOP growing after 2026-08-30. If it keeps growing at ~4/day, hedge mode is not the cause and the stranding diagnosis needs re-opening. Either outcome is informative; measure it, do not assume it.

POPULATION, because the row's own criterion 4 demands it: `/api/bot/performance?window=all`, the `paper` sub-block's `perExitPath`, n=722 closes across 17 paths. The real-money side is unchanged from the 2026-08-29 update and is not re-litigated here.

items.detail:
⚠️ THE CORRECTION FIRST, because the obvious remedy is inert and acting on it would burn a session for 90 MB. The `since_last_build_verification` UNWIRED finding is right that `scripts/ops/trainer_dataset_gc.py` has never run (0 mentions across 7,442 cycle-log rows). It is WRONG to infer that running it fixes the disk. Measured report-only on the live trainer 2026-08-25 (trainer-vm-diag #10267, `--apply` deliberately not passed):
  {status: gc_summary, mode: report-only, scanned: 115, kept: 111, candidates: 4, reclaim_gb: 0.09, manifest_pins: 41, manifests_parsed: 76, manifests_total: 76, min_age_days: 14.0, keep_versions: [v001, v002]}
and at `--min-age-days 30`: candidates 0, reclaim_gb 0.0.

WHY IT IS INERT NOW THOUGH ITS DESIGN WAS SOUND. Its docstring describes a `datasets-out/` of 15 GB 'dominated by frozen experiment version dirs (v1xx/v5xx/v9xx probe arms) whose sweeps concluded weeks ago'. Its safety model keeps any version dir a manifest references. There are now **41 manifest pins across 76 manifests, all 76 parsed**, and they keep **111 of 115** scanned version dirs. The keep-set has grown to cover essentially the whole tree, so the GC is doing exactly what it was written to do and there is almost nothing left that it is allowed to touch. This is not a bug in the GC.

WHERE THE SPACE ACTUALLY IS (`du -xh -d 1`, same session, 28 GB under the repo of a 45 GB root at 91% / 4.5 GB avail):
  datasets-out          12 G   — but only 0.09 G is GC-eligible (above)
  .venv                5.4 G   — see the CUDA note below
  ml/experiments-runs  4.5 G   — NO retention tool exists
  runtime_logs          3.3 G   — NO retention tool exists; 2.5 G is
                                  m20_exit_head, 562 M is m21_entry_head*
  data                 2.0 G   — trade_journal.db 1.0 G + signal_audit.jsonl 629 M
So the GC covers the largest directory and almost none of the reclaimable bytes, while the two trees that ARE stale have no tool at all.

THREE CONCRETE, AGED CANDIDATES THE GC CANNOT SEE:
  (a) `runtime_logs/m21_entry_head{,_r2,_r3,_pb}` — 562 M combined, newest file **2026-07-14**, six weeks stale.
  (b) `runtime_logs/m20_exit_head` — 2.5 G, newest file 2026-08-16. Recent enough that it may still be evidence; do NOT delete without checking whether the M20 analysis still reads it.
  (c) ~2.2 G of NVIDIA CUDA shared libraries inside `.venv` on a VM with no GPU: libcublasLt.so.13 630 M, libtriton.so 473 M, libcudnn_engines_precompiled 300 M, libcufft 283 M, libcusparseLt 274 M, libtorch_cpu 253 M. The trainer is an Ampere A1 (aarch64, CPU-only); GPU work runs as a separate spot burst. A CPU-only torch wheel would drop these.
