items.opened_by: claude (/system-review 2026-08-25, root-caused from the trader journal)
items.tier: 2 (it changes how a live order/market-data path responds to a broker failure)
items.area: IB client / circuit breaker / exit blindness
items.title: The IB circuit breaker treats a PEER-CLOSE identically to a WEDGE and suppresses ALL IB calls for 120s — for the one condition a reconnect clears in milliseconds. 74 episodes in 5.4 days, each blinding every IB leg and short-circuiting the monitor on an OPEN position
items.detail:
THE TWO CONDITIONS ARE OPPOSITES AND GET THE SAME RESPONSE.
  · A WEDGE — the gateway accepts the socket and never answers — MUST be backed off from: every call would block the trader loop, which is the 2026-06 wedge class the breaker was built for.
  · A PEER-CLOSE — the gateway actively drops the socket — is the opposite: the socket is ALREADY GONE, `_is_connected` fails, and the very next `connect()` builds a fresh one. That reconnect IS the recovery. Suppressing IB calls for 120s buys nothing and costs total IB blindness.

MEASURED, from the live trader journal. Episode start 2026-08-24T23:59:09Z (`/api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live.service`), three consecutive lines, verbatim:
  23:59:09,825 ERROR   ib_insync.client | Peer closed connection.
  23:59:09,825 WARNING IBClient: liveness probe error for 10.0.0.251:4002 (account=…5724): ConnectionError: Socket disconnect
  23:59:09,825 WARNING IBClient: circuit breaker tripped for 10.0.0.251:4002 (account=…5724, consecutive failures=1); IB calls suppressed for 120s.
No timeout. No wedge. The peer closed, and the response was a 120s fleet-wide suppression.

WHAT IT COSTS, and this is the part that is not a hygiene issue. During the window EVERY IB leg is blind — measured in one 2-minute window on 2026-08-25: MGC 15m, MES 1d, MES 15m, MES 5m, MHG 1d all returned `candles=None` on the same ticks — and `order_monitor` SHORT-CIRCUITS on an open position: `order_monitor: ict_scalp_mgc_15m — open=1 updated=0 closed=0 no_change=1`. The dynamic exit does not run; the position rides the broker backstop only.

FREQUENCY. 235 `no candle data` failures over 2026-08-20T07:01Z–2026-08-25T09:28Z resolve to **74 distinct episodes** (defined as a failure with no other failure in the preceding 30 min). At the configured `IB_BREAKER_COOLDOWN_S` of 120s that is a LOWER BOUND of ~2.5 hours of IB blindness over 5.4 days. ⚠️ That figure is ARITHMETIC on episode-count × the configured cooldown, NOT a measured sum of blind-time — an episode may trip more than once, and the true total can only be larger. Do not quote it as measured.

THE BREAKER HAS EXACTLY TWO TRIP SITES AND NEITHER BRANCHES ON THE CAUSE: `ib_client.py:601` `_trip_breaker(reason=f"connect_failed: {type(exc).__name__}")` and `:660` `_trip_breaker(reason="liveness_probe_timeout")`. `_probe_liveness` returns a bare `False` for BOTH its timeout branch (:888) and its exception branch (:896), so the caller cannot tell them apart even in principle. That is the collapsed-state shape: the value cannot express which failure happened.
items.evidence:
Journal window 2026-08-24T23:56:40Z–2026-08-25T00:01:00Z via /api/diag/journalctl (1000 lines) — the three quoted lines.
Journal window 2026-08-25T11:39:50Z–11:41:50Z — five IB leg-timeframes returning candles=None on the same ticks with `circuit breaker OPEN for 10.0.0.251:4002`, plus the open=1 monitor short-circuit line.
/api/bot/logs?level=error&limit=1000 — 388 rows spanning 2026-08-20T07:01:48Z–2026-08-25T09:28:26Z (NOT truncated at the cap), 235 of them `no candle data`, clustering into 74 episodes at a 30-min separation.
Code: src/units/accounts/ib_client.py:601, :660, :888, :896; _IB_BREAKER_COOLDOWN_S default 120.0.
items.not_established:
1. WHY the gateway peer-closes. `10.0.0.251:4002` is the socat-relayed gateway VM with its own wedge/reset history; whether this is IBKR's own session recycling, the relay, or the container was NOT traced. The fix proposed below is about the RESPONSE, and does not require knowing the cause — but a cause fix would be strictly better and should be looked for first.
2. The ~2.5h blind-time figure is derived, not measured (see the detail).
3. Whether a peer-close ever co-occurs with a genuine wedge, which would make an immediate-reconnect response wrong. One reconnect attempt is cheap; an unbounded retry loop on a wedged gateway is the 2026-06 cascade, so any fix must keep a bound.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. `_probe_liveness` returns a THREE-STATE result — `ok` / `timed_out` / `disconnected` — instead of a bare bool, so the caller can branch on which failure occurred. Registering it with `collapsed-state-guard` is the natural home.
2. A peer-close does NOT open the breaker for the full cooldown. The minimum honest change: allow ONE immediate reconnect attempt on `disconnected` before tripping, so the common case costs a reconnect rather than 120s of fleet blindness. It MUST stay bounded — an unbounded retry against a wedged gateway is the failure class the breaker exists for.
3. Re-measure the episode count over a comparable window and quote it with its denominator. The claim to beat: 74 episodes / 235 failures over 2026-08-20T07:01Z–2026-08-25T09:28Z.
4. The monitor-blindness consequence is checked, not assumed: confirm an open IB position's dynamic exit runs through a peer-close episode after the change.
items.measurement_trap_introduced_2026_08_25:
⚠️ CRITERION 3'S DENOMINATOR IS ABOUT TO CHANGE, AND I AM THE ONE WHO CHANGED IT. Criterion 3 says to re-measure and names 'the claim to beat: 74 episodes / 235 failures over 2026-08-20T07:01Z-2026-08-25T09:28Z', measured from /api/bot/logs?level=ERROR. That feed is no longer comparable.

BL-20260825-TRANSIENT-CLASSIFIER-MISSES-THE-VARIANT-FAMILIES widened intent_multiplexer's transient token from 'no candle data returned' to 'no candle data', because 2 of 35 builder raise sites omitted the word and the VARIANT families therefore paged at ERROR while every other leg hitting the identical outage was correctly graded WARN. Once that deploys, those rows move ERROR -> WARN and an ERROR-level query returns ~ZERO no-candle rows.

SO A RE-MEASUREMENT ON THE ERROR FEED WILL SHOW THE PROBLEM 'FIXED' WHEN NOTHING ABOUT THE BREAKER HAS CHANGED. Re-measure on WARN+ (/api/bot/logs?level=warn,error) or on the trader journal, and state which. The ERROR-feed figures in this row's evidence block describe a pre-fix population and must be quoted with that qualifier or not at all.

Note this also means the ORIGINAL 74/235 figure was itself an under-count of the condition: it counted only the two mis-graded families, not every IB leg the outage blinded. The row's own detail says every IB leg goes blind, which is the correct description; the number beside it was measured on a filtered surface. Both halves of that are worth keeping.
items.progress_2026_08_25:
CRITERIA 1 AND 2 SHIPPED (Tier-2, operator-selected). 3 and 4 are NOT met and are deliberately left open — they need live data this change has not produced yet.

1. `_probe_liveness` returns one of FOUR states, never a bool: `ok` / `skipped` / `timed_out` / `disconnected`. A test asserts the function body contains no `return True`/`return False` at all, because a caller comparing a bool against a state string would be silently wrong rather than broken. `skipped` is the fourth state and is NOT `ok` — it means we could not probe (stub client, operator opt-out, no usable loop, unknown IB implementation); proceeding is correct, but the caller must not stamp `_mark_probe_ok`, because a cached non-verdict is indistinguishable from a verified one on /api/diag/ib_state.

2. A peer-close no longer opens the breaker within a bounded grace (`IB_PEER_CLOSE_GRACE_ATTEMPTS`, default 1). The socket is already gone, so `connect()` rebuilds it and that reconnect IS the recovery. Bounded because an unbounded reconnect loop against a sick gateway is the exact failure class the breaker exists for: past the grace it trips normally, now under the reason `liveness_probe_disconnected` rather than the factually-wrong `liveness_probe_timeout` — which also closes the sibling row BL-20260825-IB-BREAKER-FAILURE-REASON-IS-MISLABELLED-AS-A-TIMEOUT. A successful connect CLEARS the streak, so the grace covers CONSECUTIVE drops and a slow trickle of unrelated ones can never accumulate into a trip on a healthy gateway.

CLASSIFIER IS NARROW BY DESIGN: type-first (ConnectionError/ConnectionResetError/BrokenPipeError/EOFError) with a message-signature fallback for a library that wraps the drop. Anything unrecognised stays a WEDGE, so the conservative pre-existing response is the default for every case not positively identified.

READ SURFACE: /api/diag/ib_state now carries `last_probe_state`, `peer_close_streak` and `peer_close_grace_attempts`. Without them the change is unobservable — a permanently-broken grace reads exactly like a working one, the `venue_session` lesson. A non-zero streak beside a CLOSED breaker is precisely the state the grace exists to produce.

ROLLBACK is one env flip: `IB_PEER_CLOSE_GRACE_ATTEMPTS=0` restores trip-on-every-probe-failure. An unparseable value falls back to the DEFAULT, not to zero, so a typo cannot silently re-arm the condition.

NOT REGISTERED with collapsed-state-guard, same call and same reason as the two other four-state fields shipped this session: producer and consumer are both in ib_client.py and the guard excludes a producer from its own consumer set, so a contract today would be met by the test file alone or invite a decorative branch. It becomes registrable when another module reads `last_probe_state`.

22 new tests in tests/test_ib_peer_close_vs_wedge.py. tests/test_ib_probe_cache.py's `_count_probes` fake now maps its legacy bool onto the state vocabulary (True→PROBE_OK, False→PROBE_TIMED_OUT, i.e. the wedge those tests actually assert condemns) rather than being widened to accept a bool the production caller no longer understands.
items.still_open: CRITERION 3 (re-measure the episode count) and CRITERION 4 (confirm an open IB position's dynamic exit survives a peer-close episode) both need live post-deploy data and are NOT claimed. See `measurement_trap_introduced_2026_08_25` on this row before re-measuring: the ERROR feed is no longer the right denominator.

updates.note: Re-validated with a live near-instance: /api/diag/ib_state shows client 9102 with last_fail `connect_failed: TimeoutError` at 16:19:02Z that RECOVERED — no breaker open on any of the three clients now. A peer-close and a wedge still resolve to the same 120 s suppression of ALL IB calls, which on the one connection feeding 5 legs is expensive.

items.opened_by: claude (/system-review 2026-08-25, demonstrated live on all three IB clients)
items.tier: 2 (the string is produced inside the live IB client, not in a doc)
items.title: A gateway PEER-CLOSE trips the breaker stamped `liveness_probe_timeout` and raises a message saying the gateway 'did not answer within 5s (likely logged out)' — a cause no code path tested; /api/diag/ib_state reports that wrong reason on ALL THREE clients right now
items.detail:
TEXTBOOK DIAGNOSTIC-PROVENANCE SUB-CLASS A, the variant CLAUDE.md singles out: *'A failure message that names a cause no code path tested is the A-variant that bites hardest (a diag relay blaming "VM down" for a request that never reached the VM) — fix it by branching on the actual failure STAGE, not by rewording the label.'*

THE MECHANISM. `_probe_liveness` has two failure branches and returns a bare `False` from both: the timeout branch (`ib_client.py:888`) and the exception branch (`:896`, which logs *'liveness probe error … ConnectionError: Socket disconnect'*). The caller cannot distinguish them, so it stamps ONE reason for both — `:660 _trip_breaker(reason="liveness_probe_timeout")` — and raises `IBConnectionError` reading *'accepted the socket but did not answer a liveness probe within 5s … (likely logged out)'*.

EVERY CLAUSE OF THAT MESSAGE IS FALSE FOR A PEER-CLOSE. The gateway did not 'accept the socket and not answer' — it CLOSED an established one. Nothing timed out; the failure was immediate. And 'likely logged out' is a diagnosis nothing tested.

⚠️ IT IS NOT COSMETIC, BECAUSE OF WHICH SURFACE CARRIES IT. CLAUDE.md states `/api/diag/ib_state` exists to answer exactly one question: *'is a current failure a TRANSITORY circuit-breaker backoff … or a REAL wedge?'* That surface publishes `last_fail_reason` — and it is this string. So the one read surface built to separate the two conditions reports the wedge cause for the non-wedge failure.

DEMONSTRATED LIVE, not argued. `/api/diag/ib_state` read 2026-08-25T~13:5xZ returns `last_fail_reason: 'liveness_probe_timeout'` for **all three** IB clients (498, 9246, 497) while the journal for the corresponding episode (2026-08-24T23:59:09Z) shows `ib_insync.client | Peer closed connection.` followed by `ConnectionError: Socket disconnect`. A reader triaging from the diag surface would conclude 'the gateway is not answering — likely logged out' and go restart a container that is not the problem.

THIS IS WHY ITS SIBLING WENT UNSEEN. `BL-20260825-IB-BREAKER-CANNOT-TELL-A-PEER-CLOSE-FROM-A-WEDGE` is a policy defect — 120s of fleet-wide IB blindness for a condition a reconnect clears. It survived because the peer-close class is INVISIBLE from every read surface: it is filed under the timeout label. Fix the label and the policy question becomes askable from the outside.
items.evidence:
GET /api/diag/ib_state (2026-08-25): three clients, `last_fail_reason: 'liveness_probe_timeout'` on client_id 498, 9246 and 497.
GET /api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live.service, window 2026-08-24T23:56:40Z–2026-08-25T00:01:00Z: `ERROR | ib_insync.client | Peer closed connection.` then `WARNING | IBClient: liveness probe error for 10.0.0.251:4002 … ConnectionError: Socket disconnect` then `WARNING | IBClient: circuit breaker tripped … suppressed for 120s.`
Code: src/units/accounts/ib_client.py — `_probe_liveness` returns False at :888 (timeout) and :896 (exception); `_trip_breaker(reason="liveness_probe_timeout")` at :660; the raised message at :662-668. Two trip sites total (:601, :660), neither branching on cause.
items.not_established:
1. HOW MANY historical breaker trips stamped `liveness_probe_timeout` were actually peer-closes. The label is the reason that is unanswerable from the stored data — which is the finding, not a gap in it. It becomes measurable only after the fix.
2. Whether the `connect_failed: {type}` site (:601) has the same problem. It at least carries the exception TYPE, so it is better off, but it was not audited.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. The breaker's reason NAMES THE FAILURE THAT HAPPENED. A peer-close is not stamped `liveness_probe_timeout`. The natural fix is the three-state `_probe_liveness` return that its sibling row also needs — one change serves both, which is why they are filed as a pair rather than merged.
2. The raised `IBConnectionError` message does not assert 'accepted the socket but did not answer within Ns' or 'likely logged out' for a failure where neither was observed. Branch on the STAGE; do not reword.
3. `/api/diag/ib_state.last_fail_reason` distinguishes the two on a live read. Verify by correlating one real episode against the journal — the same correlation that produced this row.
4. Consider `diagnostic-provenance-guard` coverage: it scans `scripts/{ml,research,ops,macro,reports}/` and the guard scripts, so `src/units/accounts/` is OUT of its scope and this class can recur there undetected. Widening it is a separate, larger question — noted, not proposed.
items.resolution: Resolved as a side-effect of the four-state probe (BL-20260825-IB-BREAKER-CANNOT-TELL-A-PEER-CLOSE-FROM-A-WEDGE), which is the right shape: the label was wrong because the CODE could not tell the two failures apart, so rewording the literal would have produced a second guess rather than a fact. A peer-close now trips (if it trips at all, past the grace) under `liveness_probe_disconnected`; a genuine double timeout keeps `liveness_probe_timeout`. A test asserts the DISCONNECTED branch cannot contain the timeout literal. `/api/diag/ib_state.last_probe_state` publishes which occurred, so the distinction is checkable from outside rather than only in the journal.

items.opened_by: claude (session_018aKyS3, while extracting is_policy_hold for PR #10281)
items.area: coordinator / execution_diagnostics — the last duplicated policy-hold closure
items.title: coordinator._is_benign_noop remains a near-duplicate of is_policy_hold, so the rule still has two definitions and can drift again
items.detail: PR #10281 lifted the broad policy-hold rule to `execution_diagnostics.is_policy_hold` and pointed `_is_hold` and `dead_leg` at it. `coordinator._is_benign_noop` (src/core/coordinator.py:~2447) was DELIBERATELY left alone: it sits near the order path, and it carries one clause the shared predicate does not (`err.startswith("below_venue_min_qty")`, BL-20260716-BYBIT2-SUBMIN-QTY). Folding it in would have changed `_is_hold`'s behaviour too — the extraction was scoped to be byte-identical for existing callers, and widening the alerting path was not the decision taken.
items.why_it_matters: The mechanical cause of the ORIGINAL defect was that this rule lived in closures nothing could import, so a later caller re-derived a narrower one. One closure remains. The next module needing this question answered can still re-derive rather than import, and the two copies can still drift — with the copy that governs the '🚨 ALL accounts failed to dispatch' roll-up being the one that stayed private.
items.not_proposed: No change proposed here. Converging it means deciding whether `below_venue_min_qty` belongs in the shared rule (which would widen what `_is_hold` and `dead_leg` treat as a hold) or stays a coordinator-local clause layered on top. That is a real question with a live-path consequence, not a refactor.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) `_is_benign_noop` becomes `is_policy_hold(err) or err.startswith('below_venue_min_qty')` — a Tier-2 change with a test asserting the sub-min clause still holds and that `_is_hold`/`dead_leg` behaviour is unchanged; or (b) a recorded decision that the coordinator's rule is deliberately its own, stating what makes it different, with a test pinning the difference so a future edit cannot silently converge them.

updates.note: Re-validated: two definitions of one rule that can drift. Single-owner violation, low blast radius.

items.opened_by: claude (session_018aKyS3, measured while implementing the per-cause floor)
items.area: silent_refusal_alert — the verdict gate, not the row floor
items.title: A rare serious cause on an account that placed even ONE order never alerts, because the verdict gate excludes partially_refused — so the per-cause floor covers 2 of the 3 accounts in the event it was built for
items.detail: `assess` alerts only when `verdict == signalled_never_placed` (placed == 0). PR #10282's per-cause floor makes `balance_unreadable` reachable at one row, but ONLY for an account that placed nothing in the window. An account that placed one order and refused four with `balance() returned None` grades `partially_refused` and is dispositioned `not_a_finding` — the capability defect is real either way.
items.evidence: STATE THE POPULATION: the three accounts carrying `balance_unreadable` on 2026-08-13, read live 2026-08-25 from `/api/bot/db/table/trades` (filter_state=applied asserted), bucketed through the real `dead_leg.bucket_for`/`verdict_for`. Calendar-day bucketing is a PROXY for the rolling SILENT_REFUSAL_WINDOW_HOURS window the detector uses, so the exact counts at check time could differ. ib_paper 0 placed / 5 refused -> signalled_never_placed. alpaca_portfolio 0 placed / 5 refused -> signalled_never_placed. alpaca_paper 1 placed / 4 refused -> partially_refused, NOT covered. Also measured: ib_paper 2026-08-02 (0/1) and 2026-08-11 (0/3) both grade signalled_never_placed, so the floor change does reach those.
items.why_it_matters: This is exactly the reassuring reading the parent row existed to prevent. 'The detector now covers Lane 0 item 0.3' is true of two of the three accounts in the very occurrence the row is about. A future session reading the closed parent row without this one would state coverage it does not have — the same shape as the original defect one level up.
items.not_proposed: Widening the alert to `partially_refused` accounts is NOT proposed. It would change what the detector is FOR — from 'this account places nothing' to 'this account has a serious refusal cause' — a materially larger alerting surface, and lowering the bar on something that pages the operator is how the desensitized-alarm P1 gets manufactured. The measurement above is the evidence such a decision would need.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) a recorded decision to surface a priority cause independently of the verdict gate, with the expected alert-rate change measured over the same lifetime population (48 rows / 11 occurrences) BEFORE it ships; or (b) an explicit recorded decision that a partially-refused account is out of scope for this detector, with Lane 0 item 0.3's criteria updated to name what does cover that case. Closing this by pointing at the per-cause floor is the failure mode this row exists to prevent.

updates.note: Re-validated: the verdict gate excludes partially-refused accounts, so a rare serious cause on an account that placed even one order never alerts. CLAUDE.md records the measured coverage gap (alpaca_paper uncovered while ib_paper and alpaca_portfolio are covered).

items.opened_by: claude (session_018aKyS3, found while preparing the IB_MD_CLIENT_ID provisioning the operator approved)
items.area: system-actions / set-env — which FILE a key is written to
items.title: set-env chose which SERVICE to restart but not which FILE to write, so a key scoped to one service could only be written to a file BOTH services load
items.detail: `scripts/ops/set_env.sh` hardcoded `ENV_FILE="${REPO_DIR}/.env"`. `ict-web-api.service` loads `/etc/ict-trader/web-api.env` AND, deliberately, that same repo `.env` (so operator overrides stay aligned between writer and reader — the 2026-05-11 DATA_DIR incident is in the unit's own comment). `ict-trader-live.service` loads the repo `.env` too. So there was NO way to set a key for one service without setting it for the other, and the action's only scoping knob (`service:`) controls the RESTART, not the WRITE.
items.evidence: Verified exhaustively rather than inferred: `grep -rn IB_MD_CLIENT_ID` over `--include=*.py --include=*.yaml --include=*.service --include=*.sh` returns exactly five non-doc sites, and the ONLY producer into a settings dict is `src/web/api/routers/candles.py::_settings()` (web-api only). `src/runtime/market_data.py::_ib_connection_identity` resolves `settings -> os.environ -> exec_client_id + 1`. So the TRADER, which never passes the key in settings, resolves 498 today. Setting 600 in the shared `.env` would move the trader's market-data socket to 600 while the web-api is already on 600 (its hardcoded literal), i.e. two PROCESSES on one clientId -> IB error 326. `candles.py`'s own docstring already says the override belongs 'on the ict-web-api unit'. `/etc/ict-trader/web-api.env` is root-owned (sudo-read precedent: `scripts/ops/flatten_alpaca_position_action.sh`).
items.why_it_matters: The operator had approved provisioning IB_MD_CLIENT_ID via set-env. Executing that as specified would have STARVED the MES/MGC/MHG candles the reservation exists to protect — strictly worse than the status quo — and it would have reported success. The action would have done exactly what it was asked and broken the thing it was asked to fix.
items.resolution: `env_file:` parameter added — SYMBOLIC targets only (`shared` default = the repo `.env`, byte-identical to prior behaviour; `web-api` = `/etc/ict-trader/web-api.env`). An unknown target is a HARD ERROR, never a fallback to `shared`. A non-shared target reads/writes through `sudo` and writes via `tee` so the existing inode's owner + mode survive; a missing root-owned file is refused rather than created. Threaded through BOTH workflow paths (workflow_dispatch input + issue-body parse). Audit JSON records the target name. `tests/test_set_env_sh.py` (12 tests) pins it and was run against the PRE-CHANGE script as a positive control: 8 of 12 fail there, and the 4 that pass are exactly the unchanged-behaviour cases.
items.resolution_criteria: A set-env dispatch can write a key to a service-scoped env file without touching the shared one, an unrecognised target fails closed rather than silently writing the shared file, and a test demonstrates the difference against the old script. All three met.
items.follow_up: The IB_MD_CLIENT_ID provisioning itself is the NEXT step and is strictly ordered: (1) dispatch set-env env_key=IB_MD_CLIENT_ID env_value=600 env_file=web-api service=ict-web-api.service; (2) verify via get-env AND /api/bot/candles still returning real MES/MGC bars AND whether /api/bot/positions uPnL stops reading 'unavailable' on the ib_paper legs (that last is the Lane 0 item 0.5 test); (3) ONLY THEN a separate PR removing candles.py's hardcoded '600'. Never step 3 before step 1 — the literal is currently the only thing preventing the collision for the candles caller.

items.opened_by: claude (system-review fix round, MHG over-cover apply)
items.title: IB over-cover ROOT CAUSE: place_protective's pre-cancel counts the cancelOrder CALL, never its effect, so IBKR Error 10147 is invisible and every re-arm mints ANOTHER disjoint OCA group
items.detail:
This is the mechanism behind BL-20260816-IB-STOPS-OVER-COVER-IN-DISJOINT-OCA-GROUPS, caught in the trader journal rather than inferred. It was proposed as a fix on 2026-08-17 ('have the re-arm REUSE the existing OCA group') and never made; the row was marked resolved on 2026-08-23 with its own update saying the class was not closed.

MEASURED 2026-08-25T14:52:34Z, ict-trader-live.service journal, one contiguous second:
  1. mhg_pullback_1d produced a trailing verdict {'sl': 6.25507143}.
  2. place_protective logged its own warning: 'no oca_key for MHG - falling back to the symbol-wide pre-cancel'.
  3. It issued cancelOrder on FOUR resting legs: 433, 434 (clientId 597, its own) and 418, 417 (clientId 497).
  4. IBKR answered the foreign two:
       ERROR ib_insync.wrapper | Error 10147, reqId 418: OrderId 418 that needs to be cancelled is not found.
       ERROR ib_insync.wrapper | Error 10147, reqId 417: OrderId 417 that needs to be cancelled is not found.
  5. It placed a FRESH bracket 441/442 in a NEW group oca-protect-440 and reported {'retCode': 0, 'result': {'orderId': '441', 'ocaGroup': 'oca-protect-440', 'legs_placed': 2}, 'retMsg': 'OK'}.

STATE THE POPULATION. /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper at 2026-08-25T14:56:17Z, read_state 'orders_read' (a confirmed clean account-wide read): MHG holds THREE disjoint OCA groups against a 29-lot long -- oca-protect-416 (417 STP 6.231 / 418 LMT 7.1415, client 497), oca-protect-432 (433 STP 6.2515 / 434 LMT 7.1415, client 597), oca-protect-440 (441 STP 6.255 / 442 LMT 7.1415, client 597). 87 lots of resting stop against 29 = 300%, up from the 200% / two-group state the over-cover page fired on at 12:27:44Z the same day. One more group per trailing amend.

WHY IT IS INVISIBLE, three separate defects stacked:
  (a) ib_insync's cancelOrder returns None and never raises; Error 10147 arrives on the wrapper's error callback, which nothing in this repo reads.
  (b) ib_client._cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol does `ib.cancelOrder(trade.order)` then `cancelled += 1` -- it counts the CALL, not the EFFECT. Exactly the distinction CLAUDE.md already spells out for protection_repairs ('counts repairs that REACHED THE VENUE, not ones that succeeded').
  (c) place_protective:1556 DISCARDS that method's return value entirely and arms the fresh bracket unconditionally. The one guard that exists (`account_wide > seen`) cannot fire here, because ib.openTrades() already includes the foreign-client orders once reqAllOpenOrders has populated the local book -- so `seen` counts the very legs that could not be cancelled.

WHY THE CLIENTIDS DIFFER -- THIS ROW AND THE PEER-CLOSE ROW ARE THE SAME BUG. The trader runs on clientId 597 (placeOrder log) having rotated off base 497 (IB_RECONNECT_ROTATE_CLIENTID_AFTER=1, IB_RECONNECT_CLIENTID_STRIDE=100; 597-497=100 exactly). The rotation is driven by reconnect failures, and BL-20260825-IB-BREAKER-CANNOT-TELL-A-PEER-CLOSE-FROM-A-WEDGE measured 74 peer-close episodes over 5.4 days on this gateway. Every bracket placed before a rotation becomes uncancellable by the post-rotation session, and this defect then arms another one on top rather than failing loudly.

THE STRANDED LEGS APPEAR API-UNCANCELLABLE. system-action cancel-ib-order was run in APPLY mode against order 417 with force_client_id (issue #10280), i.e. connecting AS clientId 497: it connected cleanly -- no Error 326, and the trader's own sessions were untouched (/api/diag/ib_state before and after: 498/9246/497 all 'connected', consecutive_failures 0, every last_fail timestamp pre-dating the run) -- and the cancel still did not take effect (verify_state 'still_present', orders_on_account_after 8). So a FRESH session reusing a retired clientId does not inherit cancel rights over that id's orders; clearing group 416 likely needs TWS/the IBKR UI.

NOT ESTABLISHED, and it matters: orders 433/434 were the CURRENT session's OWN (clientId 597), drew NO 10147, received orderStatus callbacks -- and were still resting at 14:56:17Z, 2.5 minutes later. So the same-client cancel also failed to take effect, by a mechanism this row has not traced. If that generalises, group-name determinism alone is not sufficient and the verification in criterion 1 is the load-bearing half.

ALSO NOT ESTABLISHED: how often 10147 fires fleet-wide. /api/diag/journalctl caps at 1000 lines and a 1000-line window on this trader spans about four minutes, so the day's count is not reachable from that surface. The three MHG groups are a lower bound on occurrences for this one symbol.

ib_paper is a PAPER account, so nothing was at risk today. place_protective is the same code on every IB account, and the producer is the ordinary trailing amend.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. _cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol reports its EFFECT, not its calls: after cancelling it re-reads account-wide and returns a per-leg three-state result -- confirmed_gone / refused_not_found (IBKR 10147) / unverified (we could not look) -- never collapsing the last two. Register the contract with collapsed-state-guard.
2. place_protective BRANCHES on that result. The invariant to pin: never place a fresh bracket while legs it attempted to cancel are still resting. Refusing is safe precisely because those legs ARE the protection -- the cost is that the trail does not advance, which is visible and alertable, whereas arming anyway is the accumulation this row describes. The genuinely-naked case (pre-cancel found nothing) must still arm.
3. Thread oca_key through the modify path so the ordinary re-arm is idempotent: order_monitor._apply_update -> execute.modify_open_order -> IBClient.modify_protective -> place_protective. Today exactly ONE of the two place_protective call sites passes it (order_monitor:6950, naked autoprotect); execute.py:2536 passes symbol/direction/qty/sl/tp and nothing else. MIND THE MIGRATION -- order_monitor:7670 already records that a scoped cancel will not match legs resting in legacy oca-protect-<reqId> groups, so switching the modify path to the scoped key WITHOUT criterion 2 in place makes existing positions worse, not better. Criterion 2 lands first.
4. A regression test that plants a resting leg the cancel cannot remove and asserts place_protective refuses to arm a second group -- driven by a simulated 10147, not by a return-value stub, so it pins the wrapper-error path that is the actual defect.
5. Clear the live ib_paper MHG state and re-read to confirm exactly one group. Which leg survives is decided by the journal's declared stop_loss, never guessed -- BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG is what happens otherwise. Trade 4796 declares stop_loss 6.25157143, which matches order 433 (6.2515), NOT the newest group's 441 (6.255) and not 417 (6.231).

evidence.trader_unharmed: ib_state 498/9246/497 connected, consecutive_failures 0, last_fail all pre-run

items.next_action: Criterion 2 SHIPPED as a JOIN, not a refusal (see the 2026-08-25 update — the refuse form was withdrawn on a corrected mechanism). Remaining: criterion 3 (thread oca_key through the modify path, which makes the group deterministic per trade and the join a no-op), criterion 5 (clear the live ib_paper MHG orphan oca-protect-446 at the venue), and confirm on the next trader restart that a re-arm JOINS rather than adding a group.

updates.note:
⚠️ MECHANISM CORRECTED, AND THE FIX CHANGED WITH IT. This row originally said the over-cover grows 'one more group per trailing amend'. THAT IS WRONG, and the correction matters because the first version of the fix was built on it.

MEASURED 2026-08-25T16:13:32Z, ONE monitor pass, from the trader journal — the two outcomes side by side:
  orders 463/464, clientId 497 (the LIVE session's own): PendingCancel -> **Cancelled**
  orders 447/448, clientId 597 (the previous, DEAD session): PendingCancel -> **reverted to PreSubmitted/Submitted**
So a re-arm cancels its OWN previous bracket cleanly and promptly. What cannot be cancelled is a bracket left by a RETIRED clientId — and clientIds turn over on every trader restart and every reconnect rotation (IB_RECONNECT_ROTATE_CLIENTID_AFTER=1; five processes in ~10h measured 2026-08-16). The producer is TURNOVER, not amend volume: one orphan per turnover, on each symbol that re-arms afterwards.

THE '3 GROUPS / 87 LOTS / 300%' READING WAS A TRANSIENT. At 14:56:17Z three groups were resting; by 16:16:50Z the venue read shows the steady state — MES 1 group, MGC 1 group, MHG 2 (one live on 497, one orphan on 597). The 14:56 read caught cancels in flight. The observation was real; the trend I drew from it was not.

WHY THE FIRST FIX WAS WITHDRAWN. Criterion 2 said 'never place a fresh bracket while legs it attempted to cancel are still resting', i.e. REFUSE. Under the corrected mechanism a survivor means 'the previous session died', which happens on every deploy — so refusing would have frozen the trailing stop on EVERY IB symbol after EVERY restart until each orphan was cleared by hand in TWS. A fleet-wide exit-quality regression, to avoid a hazard that has a better remedy.

WHAT SHIPPED INSTEAD (operator-directed 2026-08-25, after the correction was put to them): when the verified pre-cancel leaves survivors, the fresh legs JOIN the survivors' OCA group rather than minting a second one. ocaType=1 then covers every leg on the symbol, so whichever fills first cancels the rest — the reverse-position hazard is removed outright AND the re-arm still takes effect. `place_target_in_group` is the same manoeuvre for a target and makes the same argument; MES's live group already holds legs from clientId 497 AND 9917, which is direct evidence that ADDING across clientIds works even though cancelling does not.

SELECTION + RESIDUE. `_select_join_group` picks by the most resting STOP quantity (a stop firing is what creates the reverse), then leg count, then name for determinism. Survivors spanning several groups still join ONE — strictly better than adding an (N+1)th — and the remainder is ALERTED, not silently absorbed. Survivors with no oca_group cannot be joined at all: the bracket is armed anyway (a protected position beats an unprotected one) and logged as needing a human. The method CANCELS NOTHING, deliberately — choosing which protective leg dies is BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG.

The verification half of criterion 1 is unchanged and shipped: both cancel helpers capture ib.errorEvent, settle a bounded IB_CANCEL_SETTLE_SECONDS, re-read account-wide, and return verify_state ∈ verified/unverified/not_attempted with the venue's own refusal code per leg. `unverified` and `not_attempted` still mint a fresh group: with no confirmed read there may be nothing to join and the position may be naked.

Control verified in both directions: with the join line disabled, exactly the two join-regression tests fail and the multi-group alert still fires.

CRITERION 3 AS WRITTEN WOULD REGRESS THE THING THIS ROW EXISTS TO FIX. Read from the shipped code, not from the criterion's own rationale.

Criterion 3 says: thread oca_key through the modify path so the ordinary re-arm is idempotent, and lands AFTER criterion 2. Criterion 2 has landed — as JOIN, not refuse (previous update). So criterion 3 reads unblocked. It is not.

THE MECHANISM. `_verify_cancel_effect` (ib_client.py:~2688) builds `still_resting` by iterating `attempted.items()` and keeping the ones still present in the post-cancel re-read. A leg that was NEVER ATTEMPTED cannot appear there — it is neither `still_resting` nor `confirmed_gone`. `_select_join_group` consumes `still_resting` alone.

SO, WITH A SCOPED KEY: the pre-cancel attempts only group `oca-protect-t<trade_id>`. Legs resting in a legacy `oca-protect-<reqId>` group are not cancelled AND not observed as survivors, so `still_resting` is empty, `_select_join_group` returns (None, 0), the join does not fire, and place_protective mints a fresh `oca-protect-t<trade_id>` group BESIDE the legacy legs. That is precisely the disjoint-group accumulation this row was opened for — reintroduced by the change meant to prevent it, and this time SILENTLY, because the verified-survivor ERROR log that currently announces it would also stop firing.

This is the same shape as the criterion's own warning ('switching the modify path to the scoped key WITHOUT criterion 2 in place makes existing positions worse') — but it is NOT retired by criterion 2 landing, because the join keys on ATTEMPTED legs and a scoped cancel attempts fewer of them. The criterion's stated precondition is therefore necessary but not sufficient, and acting on it as written is the trap.

WHAT CRITERION 3 SHOULD REQUIRE INSTEAD — three parts, in order:
  3a. Make the post-cancel verification report the symbol's resting PROTECTIVE legs that were       not attempted, not just a count. `account_wide_seen` is already computed but is a bare       integer over ALL of the symbol's open orders (entry parents and working orders included),       so it cannot be used as-is; the legs need the same `_protective_leg_side` classification       the coverage read uses. Until this exists the join is blind outside its own scope.
  3b. Feed those into `_select_join_group` so a scoped re-arm still joins a legacy group rather       than adding to it.
  3c. ONLY THEN thread `oca_key` through order_monitor._apply_update -> execute.modify_open_order       -> IBClient.modify_protective.
Shipping 3c alone is a regression; shipping 3a+3b alone is a strict improvement even if 3c never lands, since it also covers the entry-bracket case (a place() group carries a bare IB-assigned id that a symbol-wide cancel does attempt today, but a scoped one would not).

NOT SHIPPED HERE — 3a/3b touch the live order path (Tier-2) and 3c changes re-arm scoping on every IB symbol. Recorded so the next session does not read criterion 3 as a ready task.

CRITERION 5 UPDATE: the live MHG state is now TWO groups, not three — oca-protect-446 (client 597, the stranded predecessor) and oca-protect-465 (client 497, matching trade 4796's declared stop 6.31207143). Group 416 named in the criterion no longer exists. The join should collapse these to one on the next mhg_pullback_1d trail without any manual TWS clearing; the falsifiable prediction is recorded on BL-20260823-IB-TRAILING-A-STOP-SILENTLY-DROPPED-THE-TARGET.

CRITICAL and it is the ROOT CAUSE of the IB over-cover family. Re-validated: counting the cancelOrder CALL rather than its effect makes Error 10147 invisible. Live evidence the family is still active: 6 `ib_stop_over_cover` ERROR rows (ib_paper/MHG, from 08-25) and 20 `bybit_over_cover` rows. Today's ib_paper MES book is clean, which shows the fix path works when it works, not that the root cause is gone.

items.opened_by: claude (system-review fix round, MHG over-cover apply)
items.title: cancel-ib-order's cancel_response says retCode 0 / 'OK' when IBKR refused the cancel -- the envelope reports that the CALL was made, and only the separate read-back reveals it did nothing
items.detail:
MEASURED on the APPLY run in issue #10280 (2026-08-25T14:51Z). The emitted envelope carried:
  'cancel_response': {'retCode': 0, 'result': {'orderId': '417'}, 'retMsg': 'OK'}
alongside 'action': 'cancel_not_effective', 'verify_state': 'still_present'.

The trader hitting the SAME order one minute later got IBKR's actual answer -- 'Error 10147, reqId 417: OrderId 417 that needs to be cancelled is not found' -- so the venue had refused. The ops envelope had no way to say so: ib_insync's cancelOrder returns None and delivers the refusal on the wrapper error callback, which the script does not subscribe to, so 'OK' means 'we called it'.

THE READ-BACK DID ITS JOB and this row is not about a missed detection -- verify_state 'still_present' plus a non-zero exit is exactly right, and is why the failure was visible at all. The defect is that a reader of the envelope sees a success line and a failure line and cannot tell which is authoritative, or WHY the cancel failed. 'OK' next to 'cancel_not_effective' reads as a race or a slow venue (that is literally what BL-20260817-CANCEL-IB-ORDER-VERIFY-WINDOW-TOO-SHORT concluded about an earlier run, and on that occasion it was right) rather than as a refusal that no wait would fix. Diagnostic-provenance sub-class A: a status naming a result no code path observed.

Cheap to fix and it makes the retry question decidable: a 10147 must never be retried with a longer window, and a genuine race should be.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. The script subscribes to the ib_insync error event for the duration of the cancel and reports any code/message keyed to the reqId it just cancelled.
2. cancel_response stops claiming 'OK' for an unobserved outcome: three states, never collapsed -- accepted_and_confirmed_gone / refused_by_venue (with the IBKR code) / call_made_outcome_unobserved.
3. A refusal must be distinguishable from a too-short verify window, so BL-20260817-CANCEL-IB-ORDER-VERIFY-WINDOW-TOO-SHORT's conclusion stays checkable rather than being re-derived per incident.

evidence.venue_truth: IBKR Error 10147 (order not found for this client)

items.next_action: DONE.

updates.note:
RESOLVED same day. IBClient.cancel now subscribes to ib.errorEvent for the life of the call, waits the bounded IB_CANCEL_SETTLE_SECONDS (0.5s -- the live rejections landed at 156ms and 239ms, so the previous ib.sleep(0) could not have seen one), and returns retCode 1 with a `refusal` block carrying IBKR's own code when the venue refused. An accepted cancel now says 'OK (accepted -- acceptance is not confirmation; verify with a re-read)' rather than a bare 'OK'.

cancel_ib_order.py gains a distinct `refused_by_venue` action, so the four outcomes stay apart: `cancelled` (accepted AND confirmed gone) / `refused_by_venue` (the venue said no -- permanent, a wider verify window cannot help) / `cancelled_unconfirmed` (accepted, the verification read failed) / `cancel_not_effective` (accepted, still resting -- which IS what a wider window is for). That last distinction is the point of criterion 3: BL-20260817-CANCEL-IB-ORDER-VERIFY-WINDOW-TOO-SHORT reached the slow-accept conclusion and was RIGHT for its own run, and nothing in the envelope let a later reader tell that case from this one.

Tests: three added to tests/test_ib_cancel_verification.py, driven by a simulated IBKR error event rather than a return-value stub -- including a control that a refusal for a DIFFERENT order is not attributed to this one (the error event is keyed on reqId, and mis-attributing it would invent a failure).

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, deliberately: it does not make the cancel work. The measured refusal is IBKR 10147, i.e. the submitting clientId no longer holds the order, and no API client can override that -- --perm-id in this script is a SELECTOR only (line 272 still calls client.cancel(str(order_id))), so the wire call is byte-identical either way. Clearing such a leg needs TWS, or reqGlobalCancel, which is account-wide and would strip every position's protection at once.

items.opened_by: claude (system-review fix round, MHG over-cover apply)
items.title: The stop-over-cover CRITICAL page latches on (account, symbol) for 6h, so 200% escalating to 300% on the same symbol pages nobody -- a worsening safety condition is indistinguishable from a held one
items.detail:
Self-reported against the page shipped this morning in PR #10259 (order_monitor._emit_stop_over_cover_alert, durable latch runtime_logs/stop_over_cover_alert_state.json).

MEASURED 2026-08-25. The page fired once, correctly, at 12:27:44Z: 'ib_paper/MHG: position 29.0 but resting STOP qty totals 58.0 (200%) across 2 DISJOINT OCA groups'. By 14:56:17Z the same symbol held THREE groups and 87 lots (300%) and the page did NOT re-fire, because the cooldown key is (account, symbol) and the 6h window had not elapsed. Confirmed against /api/bot/logs?level=error (n=42 rows): exactly one ib_stop_over_cover row in the feed.

The 6h cooldown itself is right and must stay -- it is the direct remedy for BL-20260823-TARGET-NAKED-COOLDOWN-RESETS-ON-EVERY-RESTART, where 202 of 376 CRITICAL rows (53.7% of the entire operator ERROR+ feed) were one un-latched alarm. The defect is the KEY, not the window: 'MHG is over-covered' and 'MHG is over-covered by half again as much, by a mechanism that adds a group per amend' are different facts, and the second is the one that says the condition is being PRODUCED rather than merely standing.

The repo already has the shape that fixes this: silent_refusal_alert latches per (account, cause) precisely so 'an account that stops refusing for zero_balance and starts refusing for a venue cap has a NEW problem' is not swallowed as already-alerting. Same argument, same remedy.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. The over-cover latch key includes the severity of the condition -- the disjoint-group count is the natural discriminator, since it is what makes the naked-reverse hazard worse and it is already in the message. A NEW group on an already-latched (account, symbol) pages once; the unchanged condition stays silent.
2. It must not become a per-sweep alarm: an unchanged group count keeps the existing 6h cooldown, so the total volume on a static condition is unchanged from today.
3. A test that plants 2 groups, asserts one page, plants a 3rd inside the cooldown, and asserts a second page -- and that a 4th sweep with the group count unchanged is silent.
4. Audit the sibling target-naked latch for the same collapse and fix it in the same change if present -- it shares _cooldown_admits and the same (account, symbol) key.
items.next_action: DONE.

updates.note:
RESOLVED same day, and criterion 4's audit changed the shape of the fix.

`_cooldown_admits` gains an optional `severity: int`. A strictly HIGHER severity than any live latch for the same key PAGES; an equal or LOWER one is suppressed as usual. One-directional, and both halves are load-bearing: it pages on worse so a growing condition is never silent, and stays silent on better so an IMPROVING condition cannot generate CRITICALs.

CRITERION 4 FINDING -- the sibling has the same collapse but NOT the same fix, which is why this is a shared primitive rather than two key schemes. The over-cover page's severity is the disjoint-group count: an integer, unable to flap, and monotonically growing under the producing defect, so folding it straight into the latch key would have been correct. `_emit_target_naked_alert`'s severity is the UNCOVERED QUANTITY, which moves in BOTH directions -- a position going from no target to a partial one is a repair, and a key-folding fix would have paged CRITICAL on it. Paging on an improvement is the desensitized-alarm P1 the cooldown exists to prevent, so copying the over-cover remedy across would have introduced the very failure this row is about.

`severity` rides in the stored KEY, not the stored VALUE, so the on-disk shape stays {key: float_timestamp}. Load-bearing: the live trader is holding runtime_logs/target_naked_alert_state.json right now, the TTL prune filters on the value being a number, and the durable-cooldown tests bind that shape -- changing it would orphan a latch that is currently suppressing a CRITICAL. A PRE-SEVERITY entry written by the old build suppresses: it says the condition alerted recently and nothing about how bad it was, and 'we do not know it got worse' must not become 'it got worse'. Tested.

The 6h window is UNCHANGED. On a static condition the volume is identical to today -- one page per window -- so this does not weaken BL-20260823-TARGET-NAKED-COOLDOWN-RESETS-ON-EVERY-RESTART's remedy.

Seven tests across both alert modules. Control verified: with severity passed as None, exactly the two worsening-regression tests fail and the invariant tests still pass.

items.title: A CLASS, not an instance: five alert-latch / cadence state files were written and unreadable, so 'the mechanism stopped firing' and 'it fired and the condition persists' were indistinguishable from every surface
items.detail:
FILED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE. This is a `review_coverage.backlog_classes` finding -- the pattern, not another single row -- reached by sweeping every runtime_logs state file the code writes against the diag `_LOG_FILES` allowlist rather than by hitting one more instance.

THE RECURRENCE IS THE POINT. #8778 shipped `exit_loop_health`'s writer with a docstring that says 'for the diag surface' and NO allowlist entry, and it was found by a session that needed the state and could not get it. Ten days later the same thing had to be caught by hand for `stop_over_cover_alert_state` (2026-08-25, in the PR that shipped the writer). Today's sweep found FIVE more already live. Three occurrences in two weeks is a class, and the class is: a writer lands, the allowlist is a separate file, and nothing links them.

METHOD, so the negative is trustworthy. Regex over `src/**/*.py` for `_STATE_FILENAME = "*.json"` and `runtime_logs_dir() / "*.json"`, compared against the 30 names parsed out of `diag._LOG_FILES`. RULE ONE applies to the probe itself: a FIRST version resolved allowlist entries via their Path constants, matched only 6 of 30, and reported six alert-state files as unreadable that are in fact allowlisted -- false positives. Re-run on the allowlist NAMES (which the route actually keys on) it finds 30 positives, and only then are its negatives worth anything. `package_leg_coverage_state.json` was also a false positive: the allowlist name drops the `_state` suffix.

THE FIVE, all now allowlisted:
  daily_cap_alert_state.json          -- daily-cap alert latch
  exit_loop_health_alert_state.json   -- the LATCH for exit_loop_health, distinct from the state it grades. A breach alerts once per PROCESS (deliberately -- max_interval_ms is a per-process measurement), which is only checkable if the latch can be read.
  prop_status_request.json            -- when each prop account was last asked for a balance
  prop_sl_tp_alert.json               -- which positions were announced as having crossed a bracket
  prop_monitor_pulse.json             -- when the consolidated prop heartbeat last went out

WHY THE PROP THREE ARE THE URGENT ONES, with a live symptom. The prop bridge is MANUAL: there is no broker feed, so these files are the only evidence the bot is still doing its half. Measured 2026-08-25T16:0xZ, /api/bot/prop/status returns status_freshness 'stale' at 47.4 HOURS against a PROP_STATUS_REQUEST_MAX_AGE_HOURS of 24 (snapshot as_of 2026-08-23T16:10:45Z, balance 4764.0). Two readings fit that equally:
  (a) the bot is asking on its 12h cooldown and the operator has not answered -- normal, nothing to fix;
  (b) run_prop_status_request has stopped emitting -- a live defect in the input to BOTH prop_balance's sizing-freshness gate AND the rule-distance panel, i.e. the next prop ticket would be sized against a cushion nobody has measured in two days.
`prop_status_request.json` holds `{account_id: last_request_iso}` and settles it in one read. It was unreachable, and /api/diag/journalctl caps at 1000 lines -- about FOUR MINUTES on this trader -- so the journal cannot answer it either. ⚠️ THIS IS STILL OPEN AS A QUESTION: the read surface ships here, but the file cannot be read until this merges and deploys, so (a) vs (b) is UNRESOLVED as of filing. Do not record the prop cadence as healthy on the strength of this row.

prop_sl_tp_alert.json is a direct INPUT to prop_fills_staleness's crossing detector, whose `unknown` state is defined as 'no entry here' -- so a reader grading that detector could not see its own denominator.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. DONE -- the five names are in diag._LOG_FILES and documented in CLAUDE.md's log_file row (enforced by tests/test_diag_log_file_allowlist_coherence.py, which failed on exactly these five until the doc was updated; that guard already exists and works).
2. STILL OPEN, tracked on this row's next_action: read prop_status_request.json after deploy and settle (a) vs (b) above. If (b), that is a NEW row at Tier-2 -- do not fold it in here.
3. NOT DONE, and the honest gap: nothing PREVENTS the sixth occurrence. The coherence guard checks allowlist-vs-CLAUDE.md, so it only fires once a name is already allowlisted -- it cannot see a writer that never got an entry, which is the actual failure mode all three times. The guard that would is the writer-side one this sweep did by hand: every runtime_logs state file a module writes must have an allowlist entry or an explicit `# read-surface: none - <reason>` marker. Same shape as provenance-consumer-guard ('a signal that is written and never read is worse than a missing one'). Proposed, not built -- and note the new-table-wiring-guard lesson: a presence-only marker is cheaper to lie to than to satisfy, so the marker must name something checkable.
items.next_action: Criterion 2 DONE — the prop cadence is confirmed healthy (last ask 2026-08-25T16:14:58Z, unanswered, not un-emitted). Remaining: criterion 3, the writer-side guard that every runtime_logs state file must have an allowlist entry or an explicit `# read-surface: none - <reason>` marker.

updates.note:
THE OPEN QUESTION IS ANSWERED, minutes after the read surface deployed — which is the cleanest possible demonstration of why it was worth adding.

This row shipped with criterion 2 explicitly UNRESOLVED: /api/bot/prop/status read `stale` at 47.4h against a 24h threshold, and two readings fit equally — (a) the bot is asking on its 12h cooldown and the operator has not answered, or (b) run_prop_status_request has stopped emitting, which would be a defect in the input to prop_balance's sizing-freshness gate AND the rule-distance panel. The row said explicitly: do not record the prop cadence as healthy on the strength of this row.

MEASURED 2026-08-25T17:22Z, first read after the deploy landed (/api/diag/log_file?name=prop_status_request, present:true, path /data/bot-data/runtime_logs/prop_status_request.json):

  {"breakout_1": "2026-08-25T16:14:58.303042+00:00"}

The bot last asked at 16:14:58Z — about 67 minutes before the read, well inside its 12h PROP_STATUS_REQUEST_COOLDOWN_HOURS. **(a) is correct and (b) is REFUTED**: the cadence is running, the ask is going out, and the snapshot is stale because it is UNANSWERED. No defect in the emitter.

That distinction was unreachable from any surface before this change — the two cases render identically on /api/bot/prop/status — and it is precisely the 'the mechanism stopped firing vs it fired and the condition persists' collapse this row is about.

CRITERION 2 CLOSED. Criterion 3 (a writer-side guard so a sixth occurrence cannot ship) remains the open half and is unchanged.

items.title: 74% of prop fills carry NO trade timestamp — the journal records when a trade was REPORTED, not when it happened, so prop hold time and report latency are unmeasurable
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-25T16:3xZ against /api/bot/prop/fills?limit=200 — 35 fills, endpoint count 35, so the whole population and NOT a truncated page.
  carrying opened_at OR closed_at:  9 / 35  = 25.7%
  CLOSED fills carrying closed_at:  4 / 15  = 26.7%
Every row carries `reported_at`. So for three quarters of the prop book the journal can say when the operator told us, and cannot say when the venue traded.

WHY IT MATTERS ON THIS ACCOUNT SPECIFICALLY. On an API account the two are the same instant and the distinction is academic. The prop bridge is MANUAL and the lag is real and large: fill id 33 was REPORTED 2026-08-23T11:04:22Z for a round trip its own reason text dates to 2026-08-22 07:48 -> 08:10 — a 27-hour gap, and that gap is only knowable because a human wrote the times into free text. Consequences:
  * prop hold time cannot be computed, so the prop sleeve is absent from every bars-held / execution-capture measurement the review mandate requires of the other sleeves;
  * report LATENCY — the health metric of a manual bridge, and the thing BL-20260823-PROP-JOURNAL-MISSING-THREE-DAYS-OF-TERMINAL-TRADES was about — cannot be trended, so 'reporting is getting slower' is undetectable until it becomes 'reporting stopped';
  * a reconciliation against the terminal export has to match on price and size alone, because the time axis is missing on 74% of rows.

NOT A DETECTOR REGRESSION, checked rather than assumed. `prop_fills_staleness` is unaffected: its B arm asks 'were any fills REPORTED between these two balance snapshots', for which `reported_at` is the correct field, and its A arm times from `prop_sl_tp_alert`'s crossing record, not from fill rows. So this is a measurement gap, not a broken alarm.

THE COLUMNS EXIST — `opened_at` and `closed_at` are already in the prop_fills schema and are populated on 9 rows, so the writer CAN fill them. This is an ingest gap (the structured report and the screenshot parser do not populate them), not a schema change.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. The report-back ingest populates opened_at/closed_at when the source carries them — the terminal screenshot shows trade-history timestamps and the parser already reads that panel, so the data is present on the image and is being dropped, not absent.
2. THE MISSING VALUE MUST STAY NULL, never backfilled from reported_at. Substituting the report time for the trade time is the FABRICATED bucket exactly — a defensible-looking number with no anchor to the event — and it would silently make every historical latency read as zero. A null here is the honest 'we were not told'.
3. State the population on any prop timing claim until coverage is high: report n_with_trade_time / n_total beside it, the rCoverage/pnlCoverage discipline. Coverage is 25.7% today.
4. Do NOT retro-fill the 26 existing rows from their free-text `reason` by machine. Several DO contain the venue times in prose (fill 33 is one), but a regex over operator prose is a reconstruction presented as a record; if it is done at all it is stamped ESTIMATED with the extraction basis, never as a measured timestamp.

evidence.worked_example: fill 33 reported 2026-08-23T11:04:22Z for a 2026-08-22 07:48->08:10 round trip (27h lag)

items.next_action: Tier-2 — a writer change on the prop ingest path; propose with the operator.

updates.note: Part of the prop cluster. Live: breakout_1 equity $4,755 against its $4,700 static-DD floor ($55.00 of cushion), daily-loss distance null, snapshot 0.9 h fresh, reconcile 84 tickets / 40 fills / 0 unacted. 74% of prop fills carry no trade timestamp, so prop PnL cannot be attributed to a time window — which is why prop window_pnl is reported as NULL in this review rather than as a number.

items.tier: 1 (deploy tooling; the fix predates this row)
items.title: The deploy skipped its restart whenever THIS fetch moved nothing, so an out-of-band `git reset --hard` left the long-running Python processes pinned to stale code with every surface reading clean
items.detail:
FILED RETROACTIVELY 2026-08-25 to close criterion 5 of BL-20260816-DEPLOY-VERSION-ASSERTION-CANNOT-FAIL, which found that scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh cites backlog ids that were never filed. The FIX described below is already in the code and has been for months; what was missing was the row. That gap is not cosmetic: a comment saying 'per BL-X' reads as tracked while being tracked by nobody, and `artifact-validity-guard` cannot catch it because the guard is diff-scoped and grandfathers everything that predates it. The row's own criterion is explicit that the reasoning must NOT simply be deleted — it is the only record of why the gate works as it does — so it is preserved here verbatim in substance.

THE DEFECT. The restart gate skipped whenever PRE_SYNC_HEAD == POST_SYNC_HEAD — 'this fetch pulled nothing new'. But HEAD can advance on disk WITHOUT the long-running Python processes being bounced: a manual `git reset --hard`, or any sync path that moves the worktree without a restart. The processes then hold the OLD in-memory code while HEAD, and this run's PRE==POST comparison, both look clean. The deploy skipped and the change never went live.

Note the shape: it is the same class as BL-20260823-DIAG-VERSION-REPORTS-DISK-SHA-NOT-RUNNING-CODE — a check that asks about the DISK when the question is about the RUNNING PROCESS.

THE FIX (live, scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh). The SHA the services were last (re)started onto is recorded in runtime_logs/deployed_sha.txt and the restart decision is driven off THAT, so drift is caught however HEAD got where it is. The marker sits alongside notify_state.txt and both survive the `git reset --hard` because runtime_logs/ is untracked. FAIL-SAFE: an absent or unresolvable marker falls back to PRE_SYNC_HEAD (the historical behaviour), so a fresh VM never restart-storms on an unknown — only a POSITIVELY-recorded older SHA forces a restart when HEAD did not move. Cited at three sites in that script (the pre-sync capture, the restart-decision gate, and the marker-write band).
items.resolution_criteria: Already met by the deployed_sha.txt gate. This row exists so the three citations resolve; it is not new work.
items.next_action: DONE.

items.title: `systemctl list-units 'ict-*.service'` returned ZERO matches on the Ampere live VM while the units were active, so every code deploy restarted NOTHING and silently pinned the live trader to stale code
items.detail:
FILED RETROACTIVELY 2026-08-25 to close criterion 5 of BL-20260816-DEPLOY-VERSION-ASSERTION-CANNOT-FAIL, which found that scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh cites backlog ids that were never filed. The FIX described below is already in the code and has been for months; what was missing was the row. That gap is not cosmetic: a comment saying 'per BL-X' reads as tracked while being tracked by nobody, and `artifact-validity-guard` cannot catch it because the guard is diff-scoped and grandfathers everything that predates it. The row's own criterion is explicit that the reasoning must NOT simply be deleted — it is the only record of why the gate works as it does — so it is preserved here verbatim in substance.

MEASURED ON THE LIVE VM 2026-06-15. `list-units --all --type=service 'ict-*.service'` returned zero matches even though the units were ACTIVE, so every deploy printed 'enumeration: 0 ict-* unit(s)' and restarted nothing. The live trader stayed on stale code, and the symptom presented as something else entirely — a day of manual restart-bot-service / pull-and-deploy actions that looked like a restart loop.

The stated invariant is the useful part and is worth quoting: **a deploy must NEVER silently restart nothing.** Zero units enumerated is not a clean 'nothing to do'; it is an unasserted denominator, the same sub-class C shape CLAUDE.md names under diagnostic provenance.

THE FIX (live). A three-rung fallback: `list-units`, then the unit-FILE view (independent of runtime load state), then an explicit canonical long-running-unit list (ict-trader-live / ict-web-api / ict-telegram-bot) as a last resort, each rung announcing itself. Cited at two sites in scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh.
items.resolution_criteria: Already met by the three-rung enumeration fallback. This row exists so the two citations resolve; it is not new work.
items.next_action: DONE.

items.title: The trader deploy script ran unmodified on the dedicated IB-Gateway VM, where its pip install and blanket ict-*.service restart could have STARTED the trader on a box never meant to run it
items.detail:
FILED RETROACTIVELY 2026-08-25 to close criterion 5 of BL-20260816-DEPLOY-VERSION-ASSERTION-CANNOT-FAIL, which found that scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh cites backlog ids that were never filed. The FIX described below is already in the code and has been for months; what was missing was the row. That gap is not cosmetic: a comment saying 'per BL-X' reads as tracked while being tracked by nobody, and `artifact-validity-guard` cannot catch it because the guard is diff-scoped and grandfathers everything that predates it. The row's own criterion is explicit that the reasoning must NOT simply be deleted — it is the only record of why the gate works as it does — so it is preserved here verbatim in substance.

THE DEFECT. The gateway VM is a MINIMAL box — the Docker IB-Gateway container plus a couple of stdlib-only systemd units (ict-ib-gateway-{watchdog,reset}), with NO bot venv and NO .env, deliberately. But scripts/deploy_pull_restart.sh is the TRADER deploy: it `pip install -r requirements.txt` (the full bot dependency tree) and restarts every ENUMERATED ict-*.service. Neither belongs there — the pip install would bloat the minimal box, and the enumeration could START the trader/web-api on the gateway, since their unit FILES are copied there even though they are never meant to run.

THE FIX (live). A role short-circuit keyed on /etc/ict-vm-role (written by provision_ib_gateway.sh): on the gateway, refresh the unit FILES (install_systemd_units.sh is idempotent and role-gates its own enables) and bounce the gateway timers so a changed cadence/ExecStart takes effect, then exit BEFORE the pip + trader-restart section.

⚠️ THE `[ -r ]` GUARD IS LOAD-BEARING, not defensive decoration (BL-20260623-VMROLE). The live trader VM correctly has NO role marker, and an input redirection `< file` that fails is reported by the SHELL before the command's own `2>/dev/null` takes effect — so an unguarded read leaked a 'No such file or directory' warning on every single trader deploy. The readability test makes a missing marker a clean empty-role default.

items.title: mcp__github check-run and job reads lag by tens of minutes on this repo, so a COMPLETED check reads as `in_progress` — and a session waiting on CI concludes the job is hung
items.detail:
SELF-REPORTED, three times in one session on PR #10282, each time leading me to a wrong conclusion I stated out loud before catching it.

MEASURED:
  * `guards` completed_at 16:55:23 (a 90-SECOND run). `pull_request_read method=get_check_runs` still returned it as `in_progress` with no completed_at at ~17:14 — I reported it as 'hung 20+ minutes'.
  * `pytest-run` (run 32874604707) completed SUCCESS at 17:05:49, a ~13 minute run. Both `get_check_runs` AND `actions_list method=list_workflow_jobs` kept returning `in_progress` with a frozen step list well past that — I reported '45 minutes on the test step' and opened an investigation into whether my own change had slowed the suite.

WHAT READS CORRECTLY: `actions_get method=get_workflow_run`. Its `status` / `conclusion` / `updated_at` were accurate every time, and `updated_at` is the tell — a run whose `updated_at` is minutes old while `status` says `in_progress` is a STALE READ, not a stalled job.

WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW rather than a shrug: the false reading is systematically in the WRONG DIRECTION. It never shows a running job as finished; it shows a FINISHED job as running. So it does not cause a premature merge — it causes a session to sit blocked on work that is already green, to burn its one sanctioned re-run cancelling a healthy job (I did exactly that, cancelling a run that may well have been about to pass), and to chase a nonexistent performance regression in its own diff. The last of those cost two full local suite runs, ~15 minutes, to refute a hypothesis that only existed because of a stale read.

THE COMPOUNDING ERROR, worth naming because it is the general lesson: a stale read is only dangerous if you do not check whether it is CURRENT. The same session made the same class of mistake on a second axis — comparing a `-k`-filtered local suite (56s) against a full one (427s) and concluding the suite had slowed. Both are RULE ONE failures: a reading trusted without establishing that it was current, or that it was comparable.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. The operating rule, which is the cheap and durable half: when polling CI, read `actions_get method=get_workflow_run` and treat `updated_at` as the freshness signal. Do NOT conclude `in_progress` from `get_check_runs` or `list_workflow_jobs` alone, and NEVER cancel or re-dispatch on that basis. Land it wherever the merge/CI practice is written down so it is reachable by a session that has not read this row.
2. Establish whether the lag is the hosted GitHub MCP's caching or GitHub's own API. Not attempted here — the direct REST API is unreachable from this sandbox (it 403s, per CLAUDE.md), so the two cannot be compared from a web session. A CLI session could settle it in one call.
3. If it is MCP-side caching it is not fixable from this repo, and the rule in (1) is the whole remedy — which is fine, and is why (1) does not depend on (2).

evidence.pytest_run_reported_as: in_progress with a frozen step list
evidence.cost: one healthy run cancelled; two full local suite runs spent refuting a hypothesis that only existed because of the stale read

items.next_action: Tier-1 — write rule (1) into the merge/CI practice doc.

updates.note: RE-CONFIRMED TODAY: mcp__github pull_request_read get_status returned total_count 0 / state pending for my PR at a moment when two check runs had already COMPLETED and reported failures via webhook. So the API read lagged the actual state, exactly as this row says. I relied on the webhook notifications rather than the status read — which is the correct workaround and should be written into the row.

items.title: A concurrent-fetch ref-lock race makes `git fetch` exit non-zero, which aborts deploy_pull_restart.sh BEFORE its restart-decision gate — so the worktree advances and the live processes keep running stale code
items.detail:
OBSERVED LIVE 2026-08-25, on the deploy of this session's own merge.

ict-git-sync.service, 17:15:56:
  >>> Pre-sync HEAD: 530a3cfe...
  >>> Fetching latest from origin...
  error: cannot lock ref 'refs/remotes/origin/main': is at b81458a4... but expected 530a3cfe...
   ! 530a3cfe..b81458a4  main -> origin/main  (unable to update local ref)
  ict-git-sync.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE

TWO CONCURRENT CLAUDE SESSIONS MERGED INSIDE ONE 5-MINUTE TIMER WINDOW (#10282 and #10287), so a second fetch had already advanced refs/remotes/origin/main and this fetch's compare-and-swap failed. `git fetch` returns non-zero on that, the script exits, and — this is the part that matters — the exit happens UPSTREAM of the restart-decision gate.

SO THE PROTECTION THAT EXISTS FOR EXACTLY THIS STATE NEVER RUNS. BL-20260714-DEPLOY-STALE-ON-OOB-SYNC added a deployed_sha.txt marker precisely so 'HEAD advanced without the processes being bounced' is caught however HEAD got there. That gate is correct and it is simply never reached: it lives after the fetch. Measured state during the window — /api/diag/version returned git_sha 530a3cfe (running) against git_sha_on_disk b81458a4, restart_pending true, for 5.5 minutes.

IT SELF-HEALED ON THE NEXT TICK (17:21:30), because the ref was then already at the newer value so the CAS succeeded. State the severity honestly: the observed cost was ONE TICK, about 5.5 minutes of stale code, not an indefinite stall. That is why this is medium and not high.

WHAT MAKES IT WORTH FIXING ANYWAY: the self-heal is not guaranteed, it is a property of the race not recurring. Merge frequency is what drives it, and on a day when concurrent sessions merge repeatedly (today: at least four merges inside forty minutes) back-to-back races are plausible. A deploy that silently no-ops on a transient git error, on a live trading VM, should not depend on the next attempt being luckier.

ALSO WORTH RECORDING: this was only visible BECAUSE `restart_pending` now compares the RUNNING sha to disk. Before BL-20260823-DIAG-VERSION-REPORTS-DISK-SHA-NOT-RUNNING-CODE was fixed on 2026-08-23 the endpoint compared disk to disk, so it would have read `false` throughout this window and the stale-code state would have been invisible on every surface. The fix earned its keep here.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. A fetch failure must not abort the deploy silently. Either retry the fetch once (a ref-lock race is resolved by the next attempt, as this occurrence demonstrates), or let the script CONTINUE to the restart-decision gate — the gate reads deployed_sha.txt against the worktree and does not need the fetch to have succeeded to notice that the running processes are stale.
2. A FAILED deploy must be loud. `ict-git-sync.service` entering `failed` is currently visible only to someone who reads /api/diag/services or the unit journal; nothing alerts. Note this is the same shape as the over-cover detector before 2026-08-25 — correctly detected, reaching no surface a human reads.
3. Do NOT 'fix' this by making the fetch non-fatal without also reaching the gate: swallowing the error and proceeding to a hard-reset against a stale ref would be worse than the abort.
4. Establish whether `git fetch --prune` or a ref-lock retry is the cleaner remedy. Not investigated here.
items.next_action: Tier-1 — retry the fetch once, or fall through to the restart gate on a fetch failure. Plus an alert on ict-git-sync.service entering `failed`.

updates.note: Re-validated and CONDITIONS WERE RIGHT FOR IT TODAY: a concurrent session merged #10412 while I worked, and I separately hit a stale-remote-ref failure needing `git remote prune`. A fetch race aborting the deploy BEFORE its stale-code gate means the gate never runs — fail-open on the wrong side.

items.title: 42 kept_open rows across the three backlogs state NO condition that would ever close them - a permanent-resident class, and 8 of the 11 ml ones are milestone PROGRAMS filed as backlog items
items.detail:
A CLASS PASS, not a row. Per /system-review review_coverage.backlog_classes: read the whole open backlog for PATTERNS before disposing of individual rows.

MEASURED 2026-08-25 over all three backlogs, every kept_open row, checking for an exit condition under ANY field name the corpus actually uses - resolution_criteria, close_condition, trigger_condition, what_to_check, next_action, next_step, action, remaining_work, disposition_when_verified, snoozed_until, proposed_fix, suggested_fix, recommended_fix, recommendation, suggested_next_step. A row is counted only when it has NONE of them.

  health       kept_open 194 -> 26 with no exit condition
  performance  kept_open  29 ->  5
  ml           kept_open  19 -> 11  (57.9%, the worst by far)
  TOTAL 42.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN FIRST TWO READINGS, both made before filing, because each would have made this row wrong in the dangerous direction:

(1) I first read resolution_criteria being a STRING on BL-20260825-PLACE-PROTECTIVE-COUNTS-THE-CANCEL-CALL-NOT-ITS-EFFECT as a schema defect. It is not: measured, string is the DOMINANT convention (health 672 str / 36 list / 203 absent) and spans the full date range including 2026-08-25. There is no list-vs-string defect and no sweep to do.

(2) I then framed this as 'kept_open is excluded from the drain gate, so these rows are invisible'. FALSE - scripts/reports/backlog_counts.py::is_open_status already counts kept_open as OPEN, and its own header records the incident that fixed it (96 genuinely-open items reported as 0). Field beats comment. So these rows ARE counted; what they lack is any stated condition under which they would stop being counted.

WHY IT MATTERS, at its real size. This is not a hidden-work finding - it is a TREADMILL finding. Every /system-review is required to triage every open item; a row with no exit condition is re-read every run and can only ever be re-deferred, because nothing says what would retire it. 42 rows is ~10% of health's 406 open+kept_open total and 58% of the ml backlog's kept_open set, so the ml drain in particular is dominated by items that are structurally undrainable.

A DISTINCT SUB-CLASS with the cleanest fix: 8 of the 11 ml rows are MILESTONE PROGRAMS, not findings - MB-20260717-M24-NET-R, -M23-META-LABEL, -M25-PROMO-CONSOLIDATE, -M24-FUNDING-VISIBILITY, MB-20260720-FCPCV-RETRAIN-NOOP, MB-20260721-MES-15M-HEAD-PARKED, MB-20260726-XSYMYZ-RANGEVOL-DEAD, MB-20260727-CONVICTION-AB-AUC. ROADMAP.md is the canonical record for milestone state (instruction hierarchy #3, ABOVE the backlogs), so a program tracked as a backlog row is tracked in the wrong place and cannot satisfy a backlog exit condition by construction.

evidence.population: every row with status == 'kept_open' in the three backlogs as of 2026-08-25. OPEN rows are NOT in this population and are 100% clean - 212 / 14 / 2 open rows, zero missing resolution_criteria, severity or tier.

items.resolution_criteria:
1. Every one of the 42 listed rows either gains a concrete exit condition (what measurement, deploy or decision retires it) or is re-dispositioned - resolved / wont_fix / superseded / moved to ROADMAP.md. Do NOT bulk-add a boilerplate criterion: a criterion nobody would ever check is the same permanent resident wearing a field.
2. The 8 ml MILESTONE-PROGRAM rows move to ROADMAP.md and are superseded in the backlog with a pointer, so each milestone has exactly one home (two homes is how they drift).
3. A guard or the session-end routine refuses a NEW kept_open row carrying no exit condition - filing is cheap, and this class grew because nothing checked at file time. Scope it diff-wise (the artifact-validity-guard shape) so the 42-row backlog is grandfathered rather than blocking every unrelated PR.
4. Re-measure with the same predicate and report the count; the number, not a claim, closes this row.
refs: scripts/reports/backlog_counts.py (is_open_status - kept_open counts as OPEN; its header records the 96-item under-report incident)

updates.note: CROSS-REFERENCE / PARTIAL SELF-CORRECTION. This row's detail says of the string-vs-list shape: 'There is no list-vs-string defect and no sweep to do.' That is right about the CONVENTION (string is dominant and spans the full date range) and wrong to stop there. BL-20260823-RESOLUTION-CRITERIA-HAS-TWO-TYPES-AND-ITERATING-IT-YIELDS-CHARACTERS had already identified the real hazard, which is not the polymorphism at rest but the SILENT read: `for c in row['resolution_criteria']` is correct on a list and yields one character per line on a string, without raising.
