My reading found the shapes and dismissed them; that row found the accessor. Both are now closed the same way — scripts/ops/_backlog.py::criteria_list, with the string shape declared permanently supported. Recorded here so the two rows do not read as contradicting each other.

DRAINED 17 OF 70. Every open row that carried raw material - an `action`, `next_action`, `resolution` or `proposed_fix` sufficient to derive a falsifiable exit condition - now has a `resolution_criteria` authored FROM THAT MATERIAL. 53 open rows still have none.

THE REMAINING ROWS ARE NOT A BACKLOG OF TYPING. They carry nothing to derive a criterion from, so giving them one would mean inventing an exit condition for a finding whose author did not state one - which is this row's own defect with a criteria field bolted on, and strictly worse than the honest empty state because the row would then LOOK retirable. They need the finding re-established, which is real work per row.

Two of the 17 were worth flagging while authoring, because both look closable and are not: BL-20260808-TRAIL-LEVER-TUNED-ON-NON-LIVE-FAITHFUL-TRAIL carries a full `resolution` dated 2026-08-09 while still kept_open - verified this session that its OTHER half is genuinely outstanding (both src/runtime/trail_decay.py and trail_vol.py still cite scripts/backtest_trend.py, the engine the fidelity pipeline never runs), so the status is correct and the criterion now says which half is load-bearing. And BL-20260731-AUDIT-0731-NEW-FINDINGS is a CONTAINER of 12 undisposed findings; its criterion now forbids closing on 'the plan was worked', which would have silently retired all 12.

⚠️ DIRECTLY ABOUT THIS REVIEW'S OWN OUTPUT, so I am answering it with action rather than agreement. The row says 42 kept_open rows state no closing condition. In this triage I gave every one of the 483 health rows an explicit disposition — resolved / snoozed (with a named trigger) / kept_open (with a named blocker) — precisely so the permanent-resident class does not grow. The 12 snoozed rows each carry a trigger. This row should be re-measured after this PR merges.

RE-MEASURED 2026-09-01 by the operating-layer Phase C migration, on THIS ROW'S OWN criterion (no exit condition under any of the ~16 field names it lists) so the numbers are comparable rather than merely similar.

  health       kept_open 187 -> 24
  ml           kept_open  19 -> 10  (52.6%, still the worst)
  performance  kept_open  32 ->  5
  research     kept_open   0 ->  0
  TOTAL 39, against the 42 measured 2026-08-25.

The class has NOT been fixed; it moved 42 -> 39 in a week, and three rows is well inside what ordinary triage churn explains. Do not read it as a trend.

ONE NEW FACT THAT SHARPENS THE DIAGNOSIS. Widening the scope from kept_open to ALL carried rows (open + kept_open, 576 rows across the four backlogs) leaves the count at 39 -- it adds ZERO. Every `open` row carries an exit condition under some field name; the no-exit class is ENTIRELY confined to kept_open. That is worth knowing because it rules out the broader hypothesis that rows are filed without exits in general: they are not. Something specific to moving a row INTO kept_open is where the exit condition gets lost, which is a much smaller and more tractable target than 'the backlog'.

SEPARATE AND NARROWER, filed here rather than as its own row because it is the same class: on the single field `resolution_criteria` alone, 51 of the 575 carried rows lack one. Those 51 are mostly not in the 39 -- they have an exit under some OTHER field name. It matters because docs/claude/work/ now maps `resolution_criteria` to a work object's `done_condition`, so those 51 objects carry a loud '⚠️ UNKNOWN' done-condition until someone writes one. Population and basis: MEASURED over status in {open, kept_open}, four review backlogs, 2026-09-01; re-run with `python3 scripts/ops/migrate_backlog_to_work_objects.py`.

NOT FIXED BY THIS SESSION -- Phase C's scope was the migration, the WIP ceiling and priority propagation. Recording the measurement so the next pass starts from a number rather than re-deriving one.

ASSESSED BY A DEDICATED DRAIN SESSION AND DELIBERATELY NOT CLOSED — with a judgement on which half is tractable, since this row keeps being re-read and re-deferred. Backlog-drain session #1, 2026-09-01.

I selected this row FIRST, because it is the only genuine CLASS in the health backlog's unresolved set and the drain skill is explicit that a class fix is the only move whose arithmetic beats the filing rate. Having read it in full I am recording why one session cannot close it, so the next one does not re-make the same assessment:

CRITERION 1 (each of the ~39 rows gains a real exit condition or is re-dispositioned) is NOT a bulk operation and this row says so itself — 'Do NOT bulk-add a boilerplate criterion'. The 2026-08-25 population note is the load-bearing measurement: only 15 of 70 carried raw material to promote, and 55 'carry nothing resembling an exit condition anywhere in the row', so the work is re-establishing 55 findings, not typing. That is many sessions of per-row judgement, not one pass.

CRITERION 2 (the 8 ml MILESTONE-PROGRAM rows move to ROADMAP.md) is out of this session's declared scope — I am scoped to health-review-backlog.json and four sibling sessions were live; moving rows into ROADMAP.md while another session edits it is how the 2026-08-14 hand-resolved-merge revert happened.

CRITERION 3 IS THE ONE THAT IS BOTH TRACTABLE AND COMPOUNDING, and is what I would tell the next drain session to build: a diff-scoped guard that REFUSES a new kept_open row carrying no exit condition. It is Tier-1, it is the artifact-validity-guard shape the row already names, and it is the only criterion here that stops the class REGENERATING rather than paying down its stock. The 2026-09-01 Phase C re-measurement gives it a sharper target than the row originally had: widening from kept_open to ALL carried rows (576 across four backlogs) adds ZERO to the count of 39 — every `open` row carries an exit condition under some field name. So the guard does not need to police filing in general; it needs to police the TRANSITION INTO kept_open, which is a much narrower and more checkable thing.

CRITERION 4 (re-measure) — I did not re-measure. The 2026-09-01 Phase C figure (39: health 24 / ml 10 / performance 5 / research 0) is hours old and re-deriving it would produce the same number with a new date, which is activity rather than progress.

NET: nothing about this row changed today. Recording that as a refusal, not as re-validation.

CRITERION 3 IS BUILT AND SHOWN TO FAIL. Criterion 4 is now mechanical. Criteria 1 and 2 are untouched, so this row STAYS OPEN — recording which half moved so the next session does not re-derive the assessment drain session #1 already made.

WHAT SHIPPED. scripts/ops/check_backlog_criteria.py gains a second diff-scoped check that REFUSES a row entering kept_open with no exit condition. It runs under the invocation already registered in scripts/ci/run_guards.py (`--base origin/{base_ref}`, pr_only), so no registry change was needed.

THE HOLE IT CLOSES, precisely. The existing criteria guard grandfathers by ID — `if rid in before: continue` — so an EXISTING row could be flipped to kept_open with nothing said about what would ever retire it, and CI said nothing. That is the mechanism by which this class kept REGENERATING, as distinct from its stock.

IT POLICES THE TRANSITION, NOT FILING, and that is drain #1's sharpening carried into code. This row's own 2026-09-01 Phase C update measured that widening the population from kept_open to ALL carried rows adds ZERO — every `open` row states an exit condition under some field name. Reproduced at 943a7192 this session. So the guard need only police the move INTO kept_open.

THE PREDICATE IS THIS ROW'S OWN, NOT A NEW ONE. EXIT_CONDITION_FIELDS is the 15-field list from this row's `detail`, which until now existed ONLY as prose and was re-derived by hand twice (2026-08-25, 2026-09-01). POSITIVE CONTROL: run over the corpus it reproduces the 2026-09-01 measurement EXACTLY — health 24 / ml 10 / performance 5 / research 0 = 39. A list that merely looked right would not have landed on the same four numbers.

SHOWN TO FAIL, AND SHOWN TO DISCRIMINATE — four runs against origin/main at 943a7192:
  A  unmodified tree                                     -> PASS, exit 0 (0 transitions)
  B  an open row -> kept_open, exit fields stripped       -> FAIL, exit 1
  C  the SAME transition with the exit condition INTACT   -> PASS, exit 0
  D  a new row filed directly as kept_open, no exit       -> FAIL, exit 1
C is the one that matters: without it the guard could be refusing transitions as such rather than the absence of an exit condition, and B alone cannot tell those apart.

IT IS NOT A WALL. Run A reports 0 failures while the census over the same tree counts 24 no-exit kept_open rows in this file (39 across four backlogs). All 24 are grandfathered, which is the condition this row's criterion 3 asked for explicitly ('scope it diff-wise ... so the 42-row backlog is grandfathered rather than blocking every unrelated PR'). A guard that failed on day one would be switched off, which is worse than none.

CRITERION 4 IS NOW MECHANICAL. `--all` prints the per-backlog count through the SAME predicate the guard enforces. Measured 2026-09-02 at 943a7192: health 187 kept_open -> 24 no-exit; performance 31 -> 5; ml 19 -> 10; research 0 -> 0; TOTAL 39. Unchanged from 2026-09-01. A metric and its guard that are two separate hand-derivations are free to disagree and nobody would know which was right; they are now one derivation.

STILL OPEN, and honestly so: criterion 1 (the 39 rows each gain a real exit condition or are re-dispositioned) is per-row judgement — this session authored 3 of them from measurements it actually made, leaving 21 in this file. Criterion 2 (the 8 ml MILESTONE-PROGRAM rows move to ROADMAP.md) is out of scope for a session scoped to one file, for the reason drain #1 gave: siblings are live and ROADMAP.md is contended.

items.population_characterised_2026_08_25:
MEASURED so the next pass starts informed instead of re-deriving it, and so the size of the job is honest.

POPULATION: **70** open rows across all three backlogs carry no `resolution_criteria` at all. (It read 77 an hour earlier; BL-20260825-TWO-DEFINITIONS-OF-OPEN-DISAGREE-ABOUT-SEVEN-ROWS removed 18 terminal rows from the open set and the census fell 109 -> 97 findings. Quote 70 against the canonical predicate, not 77.)

THE JOB DOES NOT DECOMPOSE INTO A TEMPLATE, and that is the load-bearing finding: only **15 of 70** already state a next action or fix under another key (`action` 8, `next_action` 6, `resolution` 2) that could be promoted into a criterion after reading it. The other **55 carry nothing resembling an exit condition anywhere in the row**. So a bulk pass would be inventing 55 closure conditions from titles, which is worse than leaving them: a fabricated criterion makes a row look workable and closes it on the wrong evidence. Author them, or leave them.

OTHER SHAPE: exactly 1 of the 70 is `snoozed_until` (legitimately parked on accrual), so 'they are all waiting on data' is NOT the explanation. Severity splits medium 25 / low 21 / **none 18** / high 5 / `P3` 1 — the 18 unset ones cannot be sorted at all, and the lone `P3` is a foreign vocabulary in a corpus that uses critical|high|medium|low (the same slip this session made once with `P2` and corrected).

SUGGESTED ORDER for whoever takes it: the 5 `high` rows first, then the 15 with raw material (cheapest real progress), then the 18 with no severity (they are invisible to any prioritised read until they have one), then the long tail. Do NOT count a row as drained until its criterion names an OBSERVABLE condition — 'the bug is fixed' is what the criteria guard already rejects.

items.title: gld-compat-matrix printed an IAUM verdict table under prose asserting facts about gld_pullback_1h — the label naming a quantity the code did not compute
items.detail:
FOUND BY RUNNING IT, not by reading it. Dispatched .github/workflows/gld-compat-matrix.yml for strategy=iaum_pullback_1d / symbol=IAUM (run 32884733084) to re-run the survival gate at alpaca_live's new risk_pct. The run succeeded and its TABLE is correctly parameterised — '`iaum_pullback_1d` · IAUM 1d · 9 emitted trades', 11 accounts scored. The NARRATIVE under it read:

    '`gld_pullback_1h` is ALREADY in `alpaca_portfolio`'s roster (config/accounts.yaml, since the 2026-07-16 S-PAPER-PORTFOLIO creation) ... with the confirmed `trending.gld_pullback_1h {short: off}` cell applying globally.'

gld_pullback_1h was not run. Its name, its roster history and its regime cell were printed as conclusions of an IAUM run.

THE CLASS: unprovenanced diagnostic output, sub-class A (semantic substitution) — the label names quantity Q, the code computed something else, and nothing in the output reveals the substitution. A reader trusting the ⭐ section reaches a confident WRONG conclusion, and this output is exactly what a Tier-3 routing decision is meant to rest on.

A SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME SENTENCE: 'is ALREADY in alpaca_portfolio's roster' was ASSERTED, never read. Even for gld_pullback_1h it was a claim the run did not verify; for any other strategy it is simply false-by-default.

FIXED IN THE SAME PASS. The name now comes from the emit payload (falling back to GC_STRAT), and the roster claim is a real read of config/accounts.yaml with THREE states kept apart — `in` / `absent` / `unknown` ('we could not look' is rendered as such, never as 'absent'). The ROUTE prose no longer claims the routing is 'confirmed sound' unconditionally; it says a ROUTE clears that account's own ruleset, which confirms existing routing where the roster carries the strategy and is evidence FOR routing where it does not.

NOT FIXED, AND DELIBERATELY LEFT: the workflow is still NAMED gld-compat-matrix and its header comments still describe the GLD Track-B purpose it was built for. Renaming a workflow breaks every dispatch reference and the issue label; it is a genuinely general per-account compat gate now, and that rename is worth doing on its own rather than inside a fix for the output defect.

evidence.table_was_correct: iaum_pullback_1d · IAUM 1d · pullback harness · feed yahoo · fidelity approximate · fee 0.0 bps · 9 emitted trades
evidence.narrative_was_wrong: asserted gld_pullback_1h roster membership and its trending.gld_pullback_1h {short: off} cell

items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED: the summary's strategy name is read from the emit rather than hardcoded, and the roster membership is READ from config/accounts.yaml with in/absent/unknown kept distinct. Verified by re-reading the render block; a live re-dispatch on a non-GLD strategy should show the strategy's own name throughout the ⭐ section. The residual — the workflow's GLD-specific NAME and header prose — is recorded above as deliberately out of scope.
refs: CLAUDE.md § 'Diagnostic provenance — does the OUTPUT say what it actually computed?' sub-class A

items.title: The trainer's disk fill RATE is structurally unknowable — the figure is recomputed every ~2 minutes into a file that is overwritten, so every reading is discarded
items.detail:
SPLIT OUT OF BL-20260825-TRAINER-DISK-AT-91PCT-AND-ITS-OWN-GC-RECLAIMS-ALMOST-NOTHING, whose `not_established` item 3 reads: 'THE FILL RATE. I have one reading at 91%. The review reported 93% earlier, and /api/bot/ml/status reported 90.1% the same morning — so the trend is unclear and I did not establish GB/day. Without that there is no estimate of how long until it fills, which is the number that decides urgency.'

THAT ITEM CANNOT BE CLOSED BY LOOKING HARDER, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. The measurement is not missing — it is taken constantly and thrown away:
  * scripts/ops/publish_trainer_mirror.sh:416-427 computes shutil.disk_usage on EVERY publish (~2 min) into `trainer_status.json` as {measured,total_gb,used_gb,free_gb,used_pct}. The block is well built — three states, never collapsed, a read failure is `measured:false` with a reason rather than a comfortable 0%.
  * That file is LATEST-ONLY and overwritten each publish. Nothing appends.
  * /api/bot/ml/cycle carries no disk key at all — verified over 400 rows, 33 distinct keys, ZERO containing 'disk'. So the cycle log is not a fallback series either.
So roughly 720 measurements a day are taken and 719 discarded. A reader can answer 'how full is it NOW' and can never answer 'how fast is it filling', which is the question that decides whether this is urgent.

THIS IS A KNOWN CLASS IN THIS REPO, one subsystem over. CLAUDE.md's exposure-soak row records the identical shape: '#8665/#8678 made the measurement emittable then readable without ACCUMULATING it — the first read available was a single Sunday snapshot of a held book', and the remedy there was `exposure_soak.jsonl`, one row per cadence window, with the summary computed over the FILE rather than over a process's lifetime. The same remedy applies here and the same rule about reading a max beside its denominator.

WHAT THE SCATTERED READINGS DO AND DO NOT SUPPORT. Four readings exist for 2026-08-25: 90.1% (ml/status, morning), 93% (the review), 91% / 4.5 GB free (trainer-vm-diag #10267), and 90.2% / 4.73 GB free (ml/status, 19:0xZ, measured by me). ⚠️ DO NOT READ THIS AS A TREND. They come from at least two different instruments, none is timestamped against the others in a way I verified, and n=4 spot readings cannot separate a fill from a build-then-clean cycle. What they DO support, weakly, is that the disk is not monotonically climbing — it was lower at the end of the day than in the middle — which is a reason to doubt an imminent-full story, NOT a reason to stop measuring. The honest state is: rate unknown, and unknowable until something accumulates.
items.resolution_criteria:
1. The trainer's disk reading is APPENDED somewhere durable, one row per publish or per cadence window — the exposure_soak.jsonl shape — carrying the same uncollapsed {measured,reason} the current block already gets right. Cheapest correct option is a `disk` key on the existing training_cycle.jsonl rows or a sibling jsonl in the mirror; both already rsync to the live VM and are already readable via /api/bot/ml/* and the diag log_file allowlist.
2. A reader can compute GB/day over a stated window, and reports it BESIDE the number of samples and the window length — a rate over 3 points is not the claim a rate over 300 is.
3. WITH the rate in hand, the parent row's urgency question is answered one way or the other and recorded: either a projected date the root fills, or a measured statement that it oscillates within a band and does not trend. Either answer closes it; neither may be asserted without the series.
4. NOT a criterion, stated so it is not mistaken for one: nothing here proposes DELETING anything. Retention for the two uncovered trees (ml/experiments-runs, runtime_logs/m2*_head) is the parent row's criterion 2 and is Tier-2 on the trainer.
refs: CLAUDE.md § EXPOSURE_SOAK_SECONDS — the same measure-but-never-accumulate class and its remedy

updates.note: RE-CONFIRMED AND IT IS THE REASON I CANNOT ANSWER THE QUESTION THAT MATTERS. I have three point readings — 93-94% (08-20), 91% (08-25), 91.7% (08-29) — and no rate, because the figure is recomputed into a file that is overwritten. So 'how long until the disk is full' is structurally unanswerable, and that is the number the orderflow-capture risk depends on. Same durable-soak fix as exit_interval_soak. Live re-measurement 2026-08-29: trainer at 91.7% used / 4.03 GB free of 48.28 GB, warning banner firing. ⚠️ This review RAISED the priority of the trainer-disk cluster after reading BL-20260829-ORDERFLOW-CAPTURE-IS-IRREPLACEABLE-AND-UNMONITORED: a full disk stops the ONE data stream that cannot be re-derived.

PARTIAL ANSWER, and it does NOT refute this row — read the two carefully, they are different quantities. This row is correct that the DISK-FREE series is discarded (latest-only trainer_status.json, nothing appends), so the NET fill rate remains unknowable and the row stays open on that. But one CONTRIBUTOR's accrual turns out to be recorded durably in a place nobody looked: `ml/experiments-runs/<model_id>/<run_id>/` run dirs carry a YYYYMMDD prefix IN THE DIRECTORY NAME, so the creation series is on disk and survives every restart. MEASURED 2026-08-29 (trainer-vm-diag #10433). POPULATION: the 23 consecutive days 2026-08-07..2026-08-29 inclusive — 1,562 run dirs, 68/day on 21 days and 67 on two (08-27, 08-29); min 67, max 68, i.e. FLAT, not a trend. Tree size 4,848 MiB over 5,554 run dirs = 0.873 MiB/dir, so 67.9 dirs/day = ~59.3 MiB/day. Against 3.8 GiB free that is ~66 days from this contributor ALONE. TWO THINGS THIS IS NOT. (1) It is NOT the net fill rate: the nightly rebuild rewrites market_features IN PLACE, so within-cycle the disk falls and recovers, and the net figure needs the accumulated free series this row is about. (2) The 0.873 MiB/dir mean is TREE-WIDE over all 5,554 dirs, not measured on the 1,562 recent ones, so the daily figure assumes recent dirs are average-sized — an assumption, not a measurement. TRANSFERABLE: `exposure_soak.jsonl` is the remedy this row cites, and the same trick applies here without building anything — where a producer already stamps a timestamp into a PATH, the series exists and only needs reading.

THE FIRST EVIDENCE FOR CRITERION 3'S SECOND BRANCH — and it points the OPPOSITE way to the class's urgency premise. Criterion 3 asks for "either a projected date the root fills, or a measured statement that it oscillates within a band and does not trend". Measured 2026-08-30 from /api/bot/ml/status::status.disk (path /home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot): **85.7% used, 6.92 GB free of 48.28 GB**.

Against the readings recorded on this class, restricted to those sharing the same 48.28 GB total so they are comparable:
    2026-08-25   91.0% used   4.50 GB free
    2026-08-29   91.7% used   4.03 GB free
    2026-08-30   85.7% used   6.92 GB free   <- +2.89 GB reclaimed in ONE day

So free space went DOWN then sharply UP. Non-monotonic. That is direct evidence for the "oscillates" branch and against the implicit premise running through the whole trainer-disk class — that the root is filling steadily toward zero and needs an urgent GC or retention decision.

⚠️ IT DOES NOT MEET CRITERION 2 AND I AM NOT CLAIMING IT DOES. That criterion says plainly "a rate over 3 points is not the claim a rate over 300 is", and this IS three points, hand-captured by three different sessions rather than sampled. Criterion 1 (durable accumulation) is still unmet, which is exactly why nobody can do better than this. What the reading DOES establish is that the urgency should not be assumed while the accumulation is missing.

⚠️ THE CAUSE OF THE +2.89 GB IS UNKNOWN AND MUST NOT BE GUESSED. Candidates include a GC run, a manual cleanup, log rotation, or a training cycle clearing temp space; none was observed. Recording it as 'the GC finally ran' would be exactly the unprovenanced attribution this repo keeps paying for.

⚠️ ONE EARLIER POINT IS EXCLUDED ON PURPOSE. BL-20260820-TRAINER-DISK-BACK-TO-94PCT records "42 of 45 GB used, 3.2G free" — a 45 GB total, not 48.28. Different denominator, so it is not comparable and is left out rather than silently folded in.

THIS STRENGTHENS THE CASE FOR CRITERION 1 OVER AN EMERGENCY REMEDY. A class of six open rows (BL-20260820-TRAINER-DISK-BACK-TO-94PCT · -THRESHOLDS-UNCALIBRATED · -DATASET-GC-HAS-NO-CALLER · BL-20260825-TRAINER-DISK-AT-91PCT-AND-ITS-OWN-GC-RECLAIMS-ALMOST-NOTHING · this row) all rest on a fill trend that has never been measured, and the one fresh reading available contradicts it. Accumulate first; decide retention second.

items.area: session hand-off / operator-owed work — the missing register
items.title: Operator-owed items are handed forward in PROSE only: no register, no age, no escalation, and no distinction between genuinely-human and defaulted-to-human — so they accumulate silently across sessions
items.detail: Every session ends by listing 'operator-owed' items in a board comment and a sprint log. That is the ONLY mechanism. There is no durable record, so an item has no age, nothing escalates when it rots, and nothing distinguishes an item that GENUINELY needs a human (secret origination, a physical/broker action, a judgement call) from one that merely DEFAULTED to a human because automating it once went wrong. Verified: grep for operator-owed / operator_pending / awaiting_operator across src/, scripts/ and docs/claude/*.md returns ZERO hits — the register does not exist.
items.evidence: STATE THE POPULATION: the three sessions that ran on 2026-08-25, read from their own ✅ DONE comments on board issue #6927. `01X2zMCh` (13:33Z), `qhpxyh` (14:27Z) and `018aKyS3` (16:56Z) each closed by handing forward THE SAME FOUR ITEMS: the live ib_paper MHG 200% stop cover; DIAG_READ_TOKEN rotation; the breakout_1 balance report; a decision on daily_usd: 200. Three sessions, one day, zero state change on any of them. The MHG one is money-at-risk and was described as 'still live, still yours' in all three. BASIS FOR THE 200% CARRIED ABOVE (it is quoted here, so it is stated here rather than only in an unscanned field): n=1 account/symbol, a single point-in-time read of `/api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper` on 2026-08-25 — a 29-lot ib_paper MHG position against two disjoint OCA groups each carrying a 29-lot STP and a 29-lot LMT, so 58 of 29 lots of stop cover = 200%. Not a rate and not a distribution. The hand-forward count is a separate basis: 3 of 3 sessions on 2026-08-25 carried the same four items, against the prior filings of 2026-08-24.
items.why_it_matters: This is the desensitized-alarm P1 in its slowest form. A list that only ever grows and is re-read aloud each session stops being actionable — exactly what `docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md` § 'Backlog governance' says about un-workable rows, applied to the hand-off instead of the backlog. And it puts the operator in the loop by DEFAULT, which the autonomy mandate explicitly forbids: the operator's role is to approve tier-gated actions and set direction, not to be the execution path for work the system could do.
items.the_sharpest_instance: ⚠️ THE MHG OVER-COVER IS NOT A GENUINE HAND-OFF. STATE THE POPULATION for the figure carried in this row: measured 2026-08-25 on ONE account+symbol, `ib_paper` MHG, read from `/api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper` — a 29-lot position against TWO disjoint OCA groups (`oca-protect-416`, `oca-protect-432`), each carrying a 29-lot STP and a 29-lot LMT, i.e. 58 of stop against 29 of position = 200%. n=1 account/symbol, a single point-in-time read, not a rate or a distribution, and calling it one is the bug. `cancel-ib-order` and `attach-ib-target` ALREADY EXIST as documented system-actions (verified in .github/workflows/system-actions.yml and docs/claude/system-actions.md) — so the WIRE is there. It is detect-only because ONE auto-remediation attempt cancelled the leg that MATCHED the journal (BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG). That is a reason to distrust the SELECTION, not the mechanism. The repo already has the pattern for exactly this: `protection_reassert` made its decision a PURE FUNCTION with seven non-collapsed states 'so the policy is arguable in tests rather than against a live position'. Nobody applied that pattern here. 'We automated it once and got it wrong, so a human owns it forever' is how a detect-only design becomes a permanent operator tax.
items.not_proposed: No specific design is proposed here, and deliberately so — the shape (a JSON register vs a labelled-issue queue vs a field on existing backlog rows) is a real choice with different failure modes, and picking it in the row that reports the problem is how a half-considered mechanism gets built. What IS established: the register does not exist, the items measurably do not move, and at least one of them has a sanctioned wire already sitting unused.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) A durable register exists in which every operator-owed item carries an OWNER-CLASS (genuinely-human: secret origination / physical-or-broker / judgement — vs defaulted-to-human: a wire exists or could) and an age; (b) an item aging past a stated threshold ESCALATES rather than being re-listed, and the escalation is measured not asserted; (c) every defaulted-to-human item is either automated or carries a recorded reason it cannot be, with the anti-pattern named — 'one remediation attempt failed' is not sufficient on its own, because the tested-pure-function remedy exists and has a precedent in this repo; (d) ⚠️ THE STANDING PART: a check that FAILS when an item has been carried across N sessions without a state change. Without (d) this closes and silently regresses, which is the same failure the register exists to prevent. Closing on 'a register was created' alone is NOT sufficient — the register must be shown to have MOVED an item at least once.
items.verification_obligation: Operator-directed 2026-08-25: this must be VERIFIED WORKING and then CONTINUE to be verified — it is not done when the mechanism ships, it is done when an item demonstrably moved because of it, and it stays healthy only while the standing check in (d) is green. Treat a green with zero items ever moved as unproven, not as success.

updates.note:
MECHANISM SHIPPED — PR #10291. (a) docs/claude/operator-owed-register.json: every item carries an owner class (genuinely_human split into secret_origination / physical_or_broker / judgement, vs defaulted_to_human) and an age; 'unclassified' is REFUSED, because an unclassified item silently reads as somebody else's problem — which is how the MHG over-cover sat in the human column while its wire had shipped months earlier. (b)+(d) The escalation is a CI failure and it is MEASURED: scripts/ci/check_operator_owed.py counts, from the register's OWN git history, the commits since an item's content last changed — a register commit that leaves an item alone IS one session carrying it unmoved. operator-owed-guard is UNGATED in run_guards.py, because a diff-scoped run is blind to the passage of time. (c) Both defaulted_to_human items were given a wire rather than a reason.

THE SHAPE CHOICE THIS ROW DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN, decided and recorded: a committed JSON file. NOT a field on the backlog rows — the backlogs hold DEFECTS, and most operator-owed items are not defects, so admitting them re-creates the un-workable-row problem § 'Backlog governance' exists to stop. NOT a labelled-issue queue — it cannot be read deterministically by CI and, decisively, it cannot MEASURE carry; a comment thread can only be asserted about. Git history is what turns (d) into a measurement.

⚠️ THE COUNT UNDER-REPORTS AND CAN NEVER OVER-REPORT: a session that never touches the register leaves no commit and is invisible to it. That residual is why age is a SECOND, independent trip path — the silent_refusal_alert.CAUSE_MIN_ROWS shape, where an added path can only ADD escalation, never suppress one.

THE SHARPEST INSTANCE IS RE-CLASSIFIED, and this row's reading of it is confirmed: cancel-ib-order and attach-ib-target had existed all along, so the MHG over-cover was defaulted_to_human. The missing piece was the SELECTION, and it now exists as src/runtime/over_cover_decision.py — a pure function with seven non-collapsed states, the protection_reassert pattern this row named. tests/test_over_cover_decision.py replays the 2026-08-20 failure's own measured inputs (ib_paper MES 15 long, declared stop 7533.69642857, order 338 @ 7516.50 in oca-protect-336 vs order 375 @ 7533.75 in oca-protect-373, MES tick 0.25) and asserts the journal-matching leg is KEPT. It also pins that the selection does not fall out of order id or input order — 375 happens to be BOTH the higher id and the journal match, so an implicit input selection would have passed the anchor test by coincidence.

STATE THE POPULATION for this update's own numbers: n=5 registered items, one register, two commits of register history. Reading at session end — moved=2, carried=3, escalate_carried=0, escalate_aged=0, not_measurable=0, observed_transitions=2 across 2 items. The three carried items sit at 1 of a limit of 2, so the NEXT register commit that leaves them alone fails CI.

⚠️ NOT CLOSED, DELIBERATELY — this row's own verification_obligation is why. Two items moved BECAUSE the register exists (both re-classified on measured evidence, one gaining a wire), which is more than zero and is NOT yet an item leaving the register. The terminal proof is pending on two SEQUENCING facts, not hand-offs: the branch-prune workflow cannot be reached until it is on the default branch, and the MHG cancel is Tier-2 and needs one operator OK. CLOSE THIS ROW ONLY ON (1) an item reaching a terminal status through the register, and (2) the standing check having FAILED at least once on a real carry and been cleared by a real disposition — a green that has never fired is not evidence the escalation works.

CONDITION 1 MET, CONDITION 2 NOT MET. The row stays OPEN, and the split is the point. MET — an item has now travelled the whole register to a terminal status: OO-20260825-STRAY-BRANCH-IB-BREAKER-PEER-CLOSE is `resolved`. It was seeded as a human hand-off by two sessions, re-classified defaulted_to_human on MEASURED evidence (a session credential gets HTTP 403 on `git push --delete` across four attempts while a normal push from the same credential in the same minute succeeds — a boundary for that credential, not for a runner), had its missing wire built, and was then dispatched and confirmed deleted by an independent `git ls-remote` rather than by the workflow's own conclusion. Nobody was asked to do anything. The check reports `observed transitions = 1` and `1 item RESOLVED and out of the open set`. NOT MET — the standing check has still NEVER FAILED on a real carry, so the escalation half remains UNPROVEN BY OBSERVATION. This session expected to observe it: two items sat at carry 1/2 on the feature branch and the next register commit should have escalated one. It did not, and the reason is a defect in the measurement, now filed as BL-20260825-CARRY-COUNT-RESETS-ACROSS-A-SQUASH-MERGE — the PR's three in-branch register commits collapsed to ONE on squash-merge, so `register commits measured` went 3 -> 2 and the carry reset. A session can therefore watch the ratchet approach and never see it fire. ⚠️ DO NOT read the current green as evidence the escalation works. It has fired exactly zero times on a real carry, which is the state this row's own verification_obligation names as unproven rather than successful. Also disposed rather than carried: OO-20260825-IB-PAPER-MHG-STOP-OVER-COVER is now DEFERRED BEHIND A NAMED TRIGGER (an operator OK on the Tier-2 cancel-ib-order dispatch), by the same session that built its wire. Its owner_class was deliberately LEFT as defaulted_to_human: re-labelling it `judgement` now that the only remaining input is an approval would be defensible on its face and is exactly the 'a mislabel buys slack' residual this register documents against itself.

⚠️ RE-CONFIRMED, AND THIS REVIEW IS EVIDENCE OF THE COST. My triage surfaced a large set of Tier-3 items sitting with the operator with no age and no escalation: the prop enforce flip (3rd review), the crypto-pullback demotion (disposition recorded 08-23, unexecuted), 5 shipped levers measured OOS-negative, the alpaca_live go-live cluster (~10 rows), BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS for the pairs sleeve, and the DIAG_READ_TOKEN rotation (100 days exposed). Prose hand-off is how those age silently. A register with an age and an escalation rule is the fix and it is cheap.

items.opened_by: claude (session_017etXEZ) — found by its own CI run
items.title: A whole-file reformat of a backlog silently converts every diff-scoped backlog guard from grandfathered to whole-tree, and the failure names the wrong cause
items.detail:
check_backlog_refs.py and check_backlog_criteria.py are deliberately DIFF-SCOPED: the docstrings say so, and say why — 'a guard that fails everywhere on day one gets switched off or routed around, which is strictly worse than no guard'. Grandfathering the past is what makes them survivable, and it rests entirely on `git diff --base` seeing only the lines a PR actually touched.

A whole-file re-serialization removes that footing. Every row reads as an added line, so the guard grades the ENTIRE backlog as introduced by the PR and fails on the pre-existing debt — 114 of 262 rows lacked resolution_criteria when that population was last measured (2026-08-12), and the standing dangling-reference count is non-zero by design (the --all sweep is registered `allow_fail` for exactly that reason).

MEASURED, on this session's own PR #10291. STATE THE POPULATION: one commit, one guards run (32892050803, head bb0f2c2, 2026-08-25T19:54Z), n=1. Result `PASS 51 · FAIL 1`, the single failure `artifact-validity-guard: python3 scripts/ops/check_backlog_refs.py --base origin/main exited 1`. The same guard passed on the commit before (f0aeab15) and the commit after the reformat was reverted (807e18f). The only difference between them is the serialization of docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json: the file is written at indent=1 and the session re-dumped it at indent=2, producing 23,508 insertions / 23,500 deletions for a 9-line row update.
items.why_it_matters:
The failure is real but it NAMES THE WRONG CAUSE. It points at dangling references — pre-existing ones, in rows the PR never touched — so the obvious readings are 'my row has a bad ref' (it does not) or 'the guard is flaky' (it is not). Both are wrong and both cost a debugging cycle; the second is worse, because concluding a guard is noisy is the first step to routing around it, which is the exact outcome its diff-scoping was designed to prevent.

It also compounds a lapse this repo has now recorded TWICE IN ONE DAY (session 018aKyS3: 'a 46,114-line backlog reformat for a 47-line change — caught reading my own diff'; this session reproduced it hours later). Both were caught by a human reading the diff. Nothing mechanical catches it, and the second-order effect above was not known to either.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) the backlog guards detect a whole-file re-serialization and say so explicitly — e.g. when the added-line count exceeds some large fraction of the file, report 'this looks like a reformat, not N new rows' and grade against the PARSED rows rather than the diff lines, so the message names the real cause; or (b) a guard fails a PR that re-serializes a backlog with different json.dumps options, pointing at scripts/ops/backlog_append.py, which already carries a style-detection candidate list for exactly this and is the tool a session should be reaching for. (a) is the more useful of the two because it fixes the misleading MESSAGE, which is the costly part. Verified by a test that reformats a fixture backlog and asserts the guard's output names the reformat rather than listing rows.

updates.note: ⚠️ THE ROW I MOST HAD TO RESPECT TODAY. A whole-file reformat converts every diff-scoped backlog guard from grandfathered to whole-tree, which would have turned my triage into hundreds of spurious findings. I avoided it by writing through backlog_append.detect_format (byte-exact round-trip) and verifying a no-op write left the file git-clean BEFORE editing. It held across five passes over 483 rows. Still convention, not enforcement.

items.title: operator-owed carry count is not monotonic across a squash merge — N in-branch register commits collapse to 1
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-25 on the register shipped hours earlier by PR #10291. scripts/ci/check_operator_owed.py measures carry from commits touching docs/claude/operator-owed-register.json. On the feature branch it read "register commits measured = 3" and put two items at carry 1/2 with the message "one register commit from escalating". After the PR SQUASH-merged, the same check on main read "register commits measured = 2" and the same items were back at 1/2 — the branch's three register commits had become one. THE DIRECTION IS ARGUABLY CORRECT AND THAT IS WHY THIS IS MEDIUM, NOT HIGH: carry is meant to count SESSIONS that came and went without moving an item, and under squash-merge one PR is roughly one session, so post-merge history counts closer to intent than the in-branch view did. The DEFECT is that the two views disagree and nothing says which is authoritative — an item can read "one commit from escalating" during a PR and then silently reset, so a session can watch the ratchet approach and never see it fire. This is a SECOND under-report mechanism the module header does not account for. It documents only "a session that skips the register leaves no commit"; the squash collapse is larger and applies to every session that DOES use the register. The "under-reports and can never over-report" claim still holds — this makes it under-report more — so the age axis remains the independent trip path, and no escalation is manufactured by it.
items.evidence: Branch claude/operator-owed-register-8lu2w9 head 2e26e33: "register commits measured = 3", OO-20260825-IB-PAPER-MHG-STOP-OVER-COVER(1/2) and OO-20260825-STRAY-BRANCH-IB-BREAKER-PEER-CLOSE(1/2). main at 7603112 (the squash of that branch) plus one new register commit: "register commits measured = 2", MHG back at 1/2.
items.resolution_criteria: Decide and DOCUMENT which history is authoritative, then make the check say so rather than leaving a reader to infer it. Candidates, none yet chosen: count only commits on the default branch (stable, but blind during a PR, which is when the pressure is meant to be felt); count distinct PRs rather than commits; or keep commits and have the check PRINT that an in-branch count is provisional and will collapse on squash. Whatever is chosen, the check must not report a carry number whose meaning changes under the reader without saying so — that is the unstated-population problem this repo already has a rule for.
items.found_by: session_017etXEZ, while resolving the first item through the register

updates.note: Re-validated: N in-branch register commits collapse to 1 under squash, so the carry count is not monotonic. My triage is 5 commits on one branch and will squash to one — the same shape.

items.title: Marking a draft PR ready re-runs the required checks on the UNCHANGED head sha, and the resulting 405 is indistinguishable from a real red
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-25 on PR #10291. All seven checks were success on head 2e26e33, read run-by-run. The PR was then flipped draft -> ready and the squash merge returned 405 '3 of 3 required status checks have not succeeded'. CAUSE: the ready_for_review transition fires a fresh pull_request event on the SAME head sha. Three new guards/pytest-run/pytest-collect runs started at 20:55:02Z, and branch protection evaluates the LATEST check run per NAME — so the identical green set underneath was masked by three in_progress ones. Nothing about the code or the sha changed; the gate was re-armed by the draft flag alone. Cost: one full pytest-run (~14 min) and a 405 whose text reads exactly like a genuine red. PROCEDURE FIX (no code change needed): flip draft -> ready BEFORE the CI you intend to merge on, not after it goes green.
items.evidence: Green set on 2e26e33: pytest-run 32896600141 (event: pull_request), guards 32896600098, pytest-collect 32896600132, repo-inventory 32896600105 — all success. ready_for_review at 20:54:58Z; new runs 32898087986 / 32898087907 / 32898087870 all started 20:55:02Z on the same sha; merge 405 in between; merge succeeded at 21:10Z once they completed.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) record the procedure rule where a session will read it before merging — the session-coordination skill's merge protocol and the merge-guard deny message both enumerate merge preconditions and neither mentions the draft flag; or (b) establish that the required workflows can skip the ready_for_review type so the flip does not re-arm the gate, and say why if they cannot. Closing this needs one of those two, not just this row.
items.found_by: session_017etXEZ, on its own merge

updates.note: Re-validated: a 405 indistinguishable from a real failure. My PR is still draft, so unexercised this session.

items.title: actions_get get_workflow_run is NOT an escape hatch from the check-run read lag — it lagged identically, and its frozen updated_at is not evidence of a stalled job
items.detail: BL-20260825-GITHUB-CHECK-RUN-READS-LAG-AND-READ-AS-STILL-RUNNING recommends actions_get get_workflow_run as the way around a check-run read that says in_progress. MEASURED 2026-08-25 that this workaround can fail the same way. At ~21:03Z, guards and pytest-collect on PR #10291 read in_progress via get_check_runs. Following the row, actions_get was called on run 32898087907 and returned status: in_progress with updated_at frozen at its start time (20:55:03Z) — which was read as positive evidence the jobs were queued for a runner rather than a read artifact. THAT INFERENCE WAS WRONG: guards had completed at 20:56:43Z and pytest-collect at 20:56:28Z, both BEFORE the read that reported them running. So a frozen updated_at means only that the read is stale — it is not a signal about the job. The practical consequence is that neither surface can be trusted to say a run is still going; only a COMPLETED reading is trustworthy, and 'still running' must be treated as 'unknown', which is the collapsed-state problem applied to a CI read.
items.evidence: get_check_runs at ~21:03Z: guards + pytest-collect in_progress. actions_get 32898087907 at ~21:04Z: status in_progress, updated_at 2026-08-25T20:55:03Z. Actual completed_at from the later read: guards 20:56:43Z, pytest-collect 20:56:28Z.
items.resolution_criteria: Amend BL-20260825-GITHUB-CHECK-RUN-READS-LAG-AND-READ-AS-STILL-RUNNING so it no longer presents actions_get as a reliable second opinion, and state the safe reading rule: a 'completed' verdict from either surface is trustworthy; an 'in_progress' verdict from EITHER is 'we could not look', not 'it is running'. Any poller that branches on in_progress needs a wait-and-recheck rather than a conclusion.
items.found_by: session_017etXEZ, correcting its own assertion

updates.note: RE-CONFIRMED TODAY: pull_request_read get_status returned total_count 0 / pending while two check runs had already completed and reported failures by webhook. The webhook was accurate and the API read was not — so the escape hatch is the event stream, not another REST call.

A THIRD SURFACE MEASURED, and it is NOT a fourth 'we could not look' — recorded because this row's safe-reading rule currently enumerates only two surfaces. Backlog-drain session #1, observed end to end on PR #10707's own CI, 2026-09-01T23:27-23:55Z.

THE OBSERVATION. `pull_request_read get_check_runs` and `actions_get get_workflow_run` both reported `pytest-run` as `in_progress`, with the run envelope's `updated_at` FROZEN at 23:27:00Z across every read I made between 23:34Z and 23:44Z. The job genuinely completed at **23:42:52Z** with conclusion `success`. So `updated_at` was stale by **15 m 52 s** and carried no freshness signal whatsoever — which is this row's finding, now with a measured magnitude rather than an assertion.

WHAT THE THIRD SURFACE ADDED. `actions_get get_workflow_job` returns a per-STEP array with its own `started_at`/`completed_at`. Read at 23:34Z it showed steps 1-5 completed with timestamps and step 6 'Run tests' in_progress since **23:27:52Z** — i.e. state 52 seconds LATER than the run envelope's `updated_at` at the same moment, and it was CORRECT: the job really was on step 6, and really did stay there until 23:42:52Z. That let me distinguish 'a long test step is running' from 'the read is lagging', which the two surfaces this row names cannot do.

⚠️ THE NARROW CLAIM ONLY, because the broad one is not supported. This does NOT establish that the job endpoint escapes the caching — the step array did not advance between reads either, and I have ONE observation, on ONE job, of it being fresher than the envelope. What IS supported: (a) the step array was at least as fresh as `updated_at` and strictly more informative, naming WHICH step and when it began; and (b) a step whose `started_at` is recent, plus a plausible duration for that step, is a positive reason to keep waiting rather than a bare `in_progress`. It is a better wait-and-recheck input, not an escape hatch.

THE ROW'S OWN RULE HELD AND WAS WORTH FOLLOWING: I did not conclude, did not cancel, did not re-dispatch, and the job finished green on its own. Recording the magnitude and the third surface so criterion 1's 'safe reading rule' can be written with three surfaces rather than two when someone lands it in the merge/CI practice doc.

A TIMED INSTANCE, on my own PR, because this row's readings so far are qualitative and a duration is what a session needs in order to decide whether to keep polling or to stop.

MEASURED on PR #10724, head sha 78452fc. `pull_request_read` method `get_check_runs` reported `guards` and `pytest-collect` as `in_progress` on FIVE separate reads spanning roughly 02:31Z to 03:04Z. Their true completion times, returned by the SAME endpoint the moment it finally updated, were `pytest-collect` 02:28:25Z and `guards` 02:28:45Z.

So the lag on this read was on the order of THIRTY-FIVE MINUTES, not seconds — and it was SILENT: nothing in the payload distinguished a stale view from a running job. Both jobs had in fact been green the whole time I was polling.

THE POSITIVE CONTROL that makes this a lag rather than slow CI: `repo-inventory` in the same response completed in ELEVEN SECONDS (02:26:54Z -> 02:27:05Z) and was reported `completed` correctly from my first read onward. So the endpoint was serving fresh data for one job and a ~35-minute-stale view for two others in the SAME payload. A reader cannot tell which they are looking at.

AND THE MITIGATION THIS ROW'S SIBLINGS RECOMMEND WAS NOT AVAILABLE TO ME. The standing advice is to prefer `actions_list` / `list_workflow_jobs` per-step reads over `get_check_runs`. `actions_list` is NOT in this session's toolset (ToolSearch returns no match), and `curl https://api.github.com/...` is 403 at the sandbox proxy. So for a session shaped like this one there is no fallback surface at all, and `get_check_runs` is not merely the worse option, it is the only one.

PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE worth carrying: do NOT read a long run of `in_progress` on this endpoint as evidence a job is slow or hung. Frozen `started_at` timestamps across several reads while another job in the same payload updates normally is the signature of the stale view, and waiting it out is correct — I nearly reported CI as unconfirmed on two jobs that had been green for half an hour.

items.title: The disjoint-OCA over-cover page told the operator to cancel a leg the API refuses
items.detail: The CRITICAL stop-over-cover page (shipped 2026-08-25) ends with 'cancel the leg that does NOT match trades.stop_loss'. For the leg it most often names, that instruction is UN-EXECUTABLE: IB binds cancel rights to the SUBMITTING clientId (`cancelOrder` 'can only be used to cancel an order that was placed originally by a client with the same client ID'), and clientIds rotate on reconnect (IB_RECONNECT_ROTATE_CLIENTID_AFTER=1, stride 100), so a group placed by a since-rotated session refuses with Error 10147. The page carried no field from which the operator could tell. MEASURED LIVE, ib_paper MHG, 2026-08-25T20:04Z (/api/diag/ib_open_orders + /api/bot/positions): trade 4796, LONG 29, journal stop_loss 6.31207143 / take_profit_1 7.141302. Two disjoint groups, 58 of resting stop against 29 of position = 200%. `oca-protect-465` = orders 466 STP 6.312 + 467 LMT 7.1415 on clientId 497 (matches the journal). `oca-protect-446` = orders 447 STP 6.2625 + 448 LMT 7.1415 on clientId 597 (6.2625 is the PREVIOUS trail level). THAT PAIR ALSO NAMES THE CAUSE, which no field previously carried: the second group is not a duplicate of unknown origin, it is the trailing amend's own cancel-and-re-place with the CANCEL HALF REFUSED. So groups accrete one per (clientId rotation, trailing amend) pair, and the hazard is ordered rather than theoretical -- the stale stop 6.2625 sits BELOW the live 6.312, so on a fall the live group fires and flattens, then 0.0495 lower the stale group sells 29 more into a naked SHORT. SELF-CORRECTION, recorded because the wrong prediction is the useful part: this session predicted the next trail would collapse 2 groups to 1 (the join picking up 446) and committed to reporting a third group as a non-firing join. The measurement refuted BOTH readings -- the count stayed at 2 but the IDENTITY changed (a fresh 465 appeared, 446 persisted), which neither branch of the prediction covered and which is what exposed the rotation mechanism.
items.resolution_criteria: protection_coverage returns oca_group_client_ids {group: clientId|None} and reader_client_id (the EFFECTIVE, rotation-aware id -- a cancel goes out on that one); _classify_group_owner grades each group this_session/other_session/unknown, never collapsing an unreadable id into 'ours'; the page names each group's clientId, says a foreign group cannot be cancelled from the trader (Error 10147) and must be cleared in TWS, and states the cancel-and-re-place cause; the fields ride structured beside the prose so a consumer need not parse the reason.
items.resolution: Shipped. src/units/accounts/ib_client.py: module-level _readable_client_id (None when unreadable, and a genuine clientId 0 -- TWS's own manual session -- survives rather than being swallowed by a falsy check); _locked_protection_coverage records the first leg's id per group and returns both new keys, INCLUDING on the flat early return so a consumer's branch does not KeyError only when the account is flat. src/runtime/order_monitor.py: _classify_group_owner + the widened page. 'other_session' deliberately does NOT assert 'retired' -- a live sibling in the 496/497/498 exec cluster is indistinguishable from a dead session here and either way this client cannot cancel it, so the weaker true claim is the one made. Call site uses cov.get(), so a coverage dict from a client predating these keys degrades to 'unknown' rather than raising inside a money-at-risk page. Tests: 22 in tests/test_stop_over_cover_alert.py (up from 12) + 11 new in tests/test_ib_coverage_group_client_ids.py. NOT registered with collapsed-state-guard, on the BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS precedent: the guard excludes a producer file from its own consumer set and the only code branching on these states IS the producer, so a row today would be met by the test file alone or invite a decorative branch. Registrable once another module has a real reason to branch on the owner.
follow_ups: The REMEDIATION is still detect-only and correctly so (BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG). But the page now proves the trader CANNOT clear a foreign group, so the stranded oca-protect-446 needs a TWS action or a cancel-as-the-owning-clientId path. Tier-2/3, not opened here.

The producing defect is upstream of the page: modify_protective cancel-and-re-places, and nothing checks whether the cancel half SUCCEEDED before the re-place lands. A re-place after a refused cancel is what accretes the group. Tier-2 (order path).
items.follow_up_2_WITHDRAWN_2026_08_25: MY SECOND FOLLOW-UP ON THIS ROW WAS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN. It said 'modify_protective cancel-and-re-places, and nothing checks whether the cancel half SUCCEEDED before the re-place lands'. That was inferred from the observed two-group state and never checked against the code. Reading it: #10282 (b81458a4, on main 2026-08-25T17:11Z and an ancestor of the deployed sha) already grades the pre-cancel's EFFECT and, when a survivor remains, JOINS its group instead of minting a second one -- BL-20260825-PLACE-PROTECTIVE-COUNTS-THE-CANCEL-CALL-NOT-ITS-EFFECT. Its own comment records the same 447/448-on-clientId-597 measurement I made independently. The REAL remaining gap is different and is filed as BL-20260825-THE-TRAILING-AMEND-NEVER-PASSES-OCA-KEY-SO-IT-STILL-CANCELS-SYMBOL-WIDE. Lesson, same shape as the ERROR-feed one earlier today: I inferred a code behaviour from an observed outcome instead of reading the code.
items.advice_corrected_2026_08_25:
THIRD CORRECTION ON THIS ROW, same root habit as the other two: I asserted a remedy without checking whether the repo already had one. The page's first wording said a foreign group 'must be cancelled in TWS or from the submitting session'. WRONG, and in the expensive direction: `cancel-ib-order` reads the owning clientId account-wide (reqAllOpenOrders) and CONNECTS AS IT, precisely so a stranded protective leg is reachable -- that IS BL-20260816-NO-PER-ORDER-IB-CANCEL, closed 2026-08-17. A CRITICAL page sending the operator to a manual tool when an audited allowlisted action exists is pressure toward the riskier option, which is the same argument that workflow's own docs make. The page now names the action, both required overrides (force_protective + force_client_id), dry-run-first, AND the cost the second override is asking about: an owning id below 9000 is in the trader's execution band and connecting as it EVICTS the trader's live IB session. It also points at scripts/ops/over_cover_proposal.py, which a CONCURRENT session shipped in #10291 and which emits the issue bodies with the group selection already made.

CROSS-SESSION NOTE, since the two halves were built in parallel and are complementary rather than duplicative: #10291's over_cover_decision.py decides WHICH group to cancel (journal-matching, seven non-collapsed states, tested against the 2026-08-20 failure where the remediation cancelled the journal-MATCHING leg); this row's work says WHO submitted each group and therefore what it takes to act. Neither is complete alone: a correct selection whose cancel is refused achieves nothing, and a cancellable group chosen wrongly is the 2026-08-20 incident. Both test suites pass together (72 tests).

items.title: A repeating strategy-builder exception paged every tick and buried every other ERROR
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-25 via /api/bot/logs?level=error&limit=400, which returned 157 rows: 131 of them -- 83.4% of the entire operator ERROR+/CRITICAL feed -- were ONE leg, 'ict_scalp_mgc_15m: no candle data for symbol=MGC', repeating. Sharing that feed and buried by it: 15 Bybit venue rejections (110007 max-contracts), 2 ib_stop_over_cover CRITICALs, 8 target-naked pages, 1 Bybit SL pre-check refusal. This is the desensitized-alarm P1 that CLAUDE.md names as its own bug, and it is the same shape at a WORSE ratio than the ib_target_naked flood the durable-cooldown work was done for (202 of 376 = 53.7%, BL-20260823-TARGET-NAKED-COOLDOWN-RESETS-ON-EVERY-RESTART). STATE THE POPULATION, and note what it excludes: mgc_trend_1h trades the SAME symbol over the same window and is unaffected, so this is NOT an MGC gateway blackout -- it is one leg's timeframe. An earlier framing of this condition as a gateway blackout was refuted by exactly that control, which is why the latch key is per STRATEGY rather than per symbol or per account. The producing fault (why the 15m MGC builder gets no bars) is NOT fixed here and is deliberately still visible -- see resolution. ⚠️ POPULATION CORRECTION, made in the same session that filed this row. The 83.4% above is over a TRUNCATED read: /api/bot/logs?level=error&limit=400 returned only 157 rows. The limit=1000 read returns 401 rows spanning 2026-08-20T08:16Z -> 2026-08-25T20:06Z, over which the same condition is 240 = 59.9%. Both are arithmetically right for what they cover; 83.4% is NOT the feed-wide figure and must not be quoted as one. THE ATTRIBUTION DOES NOT MOVE, and it is the load-bearing half: 240 of 240 no-candle rows are ict_scalp_mgc_15m, and ZERO ERROR rows across the whole 5.5 days mention mgc_trend_1h -- which trades the SAME symbol at the SAME cadence (193 vs 189 evals over an aligned 6h window, so the denominators are measured rather than assumed). A gateway blackout blinding every IB leg would have to hit both; it hits one.
items.resolution_criteria: A repeating builder exception with the same cause pages ERROR once per 6h window and WARN thereafter, so it stops Telegramming while remaining in outcomes.jsonl, /api/bot/logs and the notifications banner; a NEW cause on an already-latched strategy pages immediately; the latch is durable across restarts; and its state file is readable on the diag surface and documented in CLAUDE.md.
items.resolution: Shipped. src/runtime/alert_cooldown.py now OWNS the durable cooldown (lifted from order_monitor, which keeps thin wrappers threading its own _alert_state_path back in so the two suites patching that seam are unaffected). Copying the latch was the thing to avoid: the per-PROCESS time.monotonic() defect target_naked was fixed for on 2026-08-23 is exactly what a copy reintroduces, and living in order_monitor -- a module the trading loop has no business importing -- made copying the path of least resistance. pipeline._report_builder_exception keys the latch on (strategy, digit-normalised cause): digits vary without the condition changing (a bar count, a price, a timestamp), the same normalisation /api/bot/notifications already applies to its operator-warning banner. DOWNGRADED, NOT SUPPRESSED -- Level.WARN still persists and still renders; suppressing outright would make a persisting fault invisible, which is the opposite failure and just as bad. An unreachable latch pages (fails loud), matching alert_cooldown's own unreadable-state behaviour rather than inventing a quieter one. State file allowlisted on /api/diag/log_file and documented in CLAUDE.md in the same commit (the #8778 lesson: a latch that downgrades an ERROR and cannot be inspected leaves 'holding' and 'broken' indistinguishable). 12 new tests; the ownership assertion in test_target_naked_cooldown_is_durable follows the move rather than being weakened, and now also pins that the wrapper DELEGATES.
follow_ups: THE PRODUCING FAULT IS UNTOUCHED: ict_scalp_mgc_15m still cannot fetch bars, at 240/401 = 59.9% of attempts when last measured and higher in the 157-row sample. It is now legible instead of deafening, which is a precondition for diagnosing it, not a substitute. Open separately.

Read strategy_builder_exception_alert_state before concluding a leg has recovered: a WARN-only feed means the latch is HOLDING, not that the fault cleared. Those are opposite facts and the whole reason the state file needed a read surface.
items.population_correction_2026_08_25: The row id embeds '83-PERCENT', which the correction above supersedes. The id is deliberately NOT renamed: a backlog id is an address other artifacts and commits already cite, and silently re-pointing it is worse than one stale word inside it. Read the detail, not the id, for the figure.
items.root_cause_found_2026_08_25: The flood's ROOT CAUSE is BL-20260825-TRANSIENT-CLASSIFIER-MISSES-THE-VARIANT-FAMILIES: the no-candle exception should never have been ERROR at all. The cooldown shipped under this row is now the BACKSTOP, not the fix -- it covers a GENUINE repeating builder bug (a KeyError in an indicator), which neither multiplexer handled and which would otherwise become the whole feed the same way. Both are kept, deliberately: the classifier stops the routine case paging, the cooldown stops the real case flooding.

items.title: The no-candle transient classifier matched 33 of 35 raise sites, and the 2 it missed were whole strategy families
items.detail: ROOT CAUSE of the ERROR-feed flood, found by testing a hypothesis rather than by reading more of the feed. intent_multiplexer._is_transient_market_data_error reclassifies a no-candle builder exception ERROR -> WARN, because a candle fetch returning None is a routine self-recovering outage (usually an IB circuit-breaker backoff). Its token was the substring 'no candle data returned', and its comment asserted 'the phrase is identical across all ~30 builders'. IT WAS NOT: 33 of 35 raise sites in strategy_signal_builders.py use that phrasing and 2 do not -- _ict_scalp_variant_builder (L776) and _trend_donchian_variant_builder (L1727), which raise '<name>: no candle data for symbol=... timeframe=...'. Those are the VARIANT FAMILIES, not two stray legs, so every variant strategy fell through to an ERROR page during exactly the outages the reclassification exists to quieten. MEASURED, full 401-row ERROR+ feed 2026-08-20T08:16Z -> 2026-08-25T20:06Z: 240 rows, 100% ict_scalp_mgc_15m (a variant leg), zero from mgc_trend_1h on the SAME symbol at the SAME cadence (193 vs 189 evals over an aligned 6h window). THE ASYMMETRY IS THE CLASSIFIER, NOT THE LEG. Trader journal at 2026-08-25T20:05:43Z: the circuit breaker trips for 10.0.0.251:4002 and within seconds get_ohlcv fails for MES 1d and MES 15m (x7) with mes_trend_long_1d raising -- all correctly graded WARN and therefore absent from the ERROR feed. The outage was FLEET-WIDE; only the mis-graded family was audible.
items.resolution_criteria: The classifier matches every no-candle raise site in strategy_signal_builders.py, asserted over the CORPUS rather than against a remembered phrasing, with a non-empty-population control so the assertion cannot pass vacuously; it stays gated on RuntimeError so a genuine builder bug still pages; and the legacy pipeline multiplexer grades the same exception the same way by IMPORTING the classifier rather than re-deriving it.
items.resolution: Shipped. Token widened to 'no candle data' -- the part all 35 messages actually share -- still gated on RuntimeError. tests/test_transient_market_data_signature.py asserts it against every raise site parsed out of the builder corpus, with a >= 30-site control test so a broken regex cannot make the suite pass vacuously, and a test pinning that BOTH phrasings are still present (with an instruction to delete that test deliberately if a future sweep normalises them, rather than leave it passing by accident). pipeline._report_builder_exception now imports the same classifier and WARNs a transient outright; a classifier or import failure falls through to the ERROR path (fail loud, never a silent downgrade). The two multiplexers previously disagreed about the same exception -- the legacy path had no transient grading at all.
follow_ups: The 35 messages should be emitted from ONE helper rather than 35 f-strings, so a classifier keyed on prose stops being necessary. Not done here: it touches every builder and the corpus guard makes the current state safe. Tier-1 cleanup.

A phrase-matching classifier is the underlying smell. The durable fix is a typed exception (e.g. TransientMarketDataError) raised by the shared candle-fetch helper, which needs no prose at all. Tier-1, larger.

items.title: The deterministic per-trade OCA group exists, and the trailing-amend path does not use it
items.detail:
#10282 gave place_protective a DETERMINISTIC per-trade OCA group -- 'oca-protect-t<oca_key>' -- so a re-arm cancels only THAT trade's group. The fallback when no oca_key is supplied is the legacy SYMBOL-WIDE cancel, which the code itself flags as the path that 'CAN cancel a sibling trade's protective legs on a netted contract' (BL-20260814-IB-PROTECTION-BOOLEAN-NOT-QUANTITY). MEASURED BY READING EVERY CALL SITE, 2026-08-25. Three IB callers reach place_protective / modify_protective; ONE passes oca_key and TWO do not: (a) order_monitor.py:7042 _attempt_naked_autoprotect -- PASSES it. (b) execute.py:2544 modify_open_order, the IB branch -- DOES NOT. This is the TRAILING-AMEND path, i.e. the one that runs every time a strategy moves a stop, which is the most frequent re-arm in the system. (c) order_monitor.py:7316 _reassert_from_divergence -- DOES NOT (today inert: PROTECTION_REASSERT_MODE defaults to annotate, so it decides but does not call; it would inherit the defect the moment it is flipped to apply). A fourth site, execute.py:2579, is the ALPACA branch with a different client and signature -- not an IB call site, and not part of this finding. Stating that explicitly because a grep for 'modify_protective(' returns four hits and three-of-four would be the wrong denominator.

LIVE CORROBORATION: on ib_paper at 2026-08-25T20:04:54Z the two resting MHG groups are named 'oca-protect-465' and 'oca-protect-446' -- the legacy 'oca-protect-<orderId>' form with NO 't' prefix. If a trailing amend had supplied oca_key the group would read 'oca-protect-t<trade_id>'. The naming is direct evidence the live re-arms take the symbol-wide branch. (The join fix from #10282 IS deployed -- b81458a4 is an ancestor of the running sha 44b50485, confirmed via /api/diag/version with restart_pending false -- so this is not a deploy lag.)
items.resolution_criteria: execute.modify_open_order accepts a trade identifier and forwards it as oca_key on the IB branch, and order_monitor._reassert_from_divergence does the same, so no IB re-arm reaches the symbol-wide pre-cancel while a trade id is in scope; verified by a test that asserts each IB call site passes oca_key, and by the next live re-arm minting a group named 'oca-protect-t<trade_id>' rather than 'oca-protect-<orderId>'.
items.why_it_matters: On a netted IB contract several strategies share ONE broker position while each trade's OCA is sized to its own qty. A symbol-wide pre-cancel from one trade's trailing amend therefore deletes the OTHER trades' resting take-profit legs and replaces them with a bracket covering only the amending trade's qty. That is the documented mechanism behind a take-profit that was reached and never executed. The deterministic group was built precisely to stop it, and the highest-frequency caller does not use it.
items.not_yet_actioned_because: Tier-2: it is the live order path, and modify_open_order has no trade-id parameter today, so the fix threads a new kwarg from order_monitor through execute rather than being a one-line addition. Proposing rather than shipping unilaterally.

updates.note: HIGH and it is the mechanism behind the whole IB over-cover family. Re-validated: the deterministic per-trade OCA group EXISTS and the trailing-amend path does not pass it. Live corroboration: ib_paper MES rests under `oca-protect-408` — the LEGACY <reqId> form, not the keyed oca-protect-t<trade_id> form — which is exactly the un-keyed state PROTECTION_STRAY_GROUP_MODE was written for. Pair with BL-20260826-A-LEGACY-NAMED-STRAY-GROUP-OWNED-BY-THE-TRADER-IS-UNREACHABLE-BY-BOTH-REPAIRS.

items.title: Three Bybit modify tests pass alone and in the full suite, and fail under a -k selection
items.detail:
tests/test_s030_pr4_exchange_modify_close.py::TestModifyOpenOrder {test_bybit_set_trading_stop_called_with_sl_only, ..._with_tp_only, test_bybit_atomic_sl_and_tp} fail when run under `pytest tests/ -k 'modify or protective or rearm or naked or over_cover or execute'`, and PASS both (a) as a whole file in isolation (32/32, twice) and (b) in the full 12,909-test suite. So some other module in that selection leaves state behind that the full suite happens to overwrite before these run.

NOT CAUSED BY THE oca_key CHANGE, established rather than assumed: the same three fail on a clean tree with the source changes stashed, AND with the new tests/test_ib_rearm_scopes_precancel.py excluded from the selection entirely (`and not test_ib_rearm_scopes`). Both controls run, both reproduce.

WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW despite passing in CI: a test that passes or fails on RUN ORDER is a test whose green is not evidence. It passes in CI today by accident of ordering, and the natural developer habit -- run the subset related to what you touched -- is exactly the invocation that fails, so the next person to touch this area will lose time deciding whether they broke it. I did.
items.resolution_criteria: The three tests pass under `pytest tests/ -k 'modify or protective or rearm or naked or over_cover or execute'` as well as in isolation and in the full suite, with the leaking module identified by bisecting the selection and the leak fixed at its source (a fixture that does not restore, or module-level state mutated at import) rather than by reordering or by marking the tests.
items.not_yet_actioned_because: Found while validating an unrelated change; bisecting a 356-test selection to find the leaking module is its own task. Filed with the reproduction and both controls so it can be picked up without re-deriving them.

updates.note: Re-validated: pass alone, pass in full, fail under -k. Same sys.modules-pollution root as BL-20260822 and BL-20260827-TEST-MODULES-STUB-SKLEARN-INTO-SYS-MODULES-AT-IMPORT-TIME — three rows, one cause.

EXAMINED, NOT CHECKABLE FROM THIS SANDBOX — recording so the next session does not spend the same time. Backlog-drain session #1, 2026-09-01.

The criterion names an exact command, which is the right way to write a criterion and is why I reached for this row first: `pytest tests/ -k 'modify or protective or rearm or naked or over_cover or execute'`. I ran it. It does not fail the way the row describes; it does not RUN at all here:
  * first attempt: 345 collection errors, all ModuleNotFoundError — the sandbox ships a bare system python (no yaml, pandas, fastapi).
  * after `pip install pandas numpy fastapi pytest httpx pyyaml pydantic`: 33 collection errors remain, every one a `pyo3_runtime.PanicException: Python API call failed` from pydantic-core — a compiled-ABI mismatch, unrelated to the tests or to the leak this row is about.
  * `pytest` on PATH (/root/.local/bin/pytest) runs under its own uv-managed interpreter, so packages installed into the system python are invisible to it — worth knowing, it wasted a cycle.

I DID NOT run the selection with the 33 modules `--ignore`d, deliberately. This row's subject is cross-module state leakage under a PARTIAL selection; excluding a third of the collected modules changes the selection and would produce a green that answers a different question — the 'green is not evidence' shape. A pass under a mutilated selection is not the criterion.

WHERE IT CAN BE CHECKED: CI (which has the real requirements), or any session with the project venv. The criterion needs no rewriting — it is precise and correct. Related: BL-20260824-SANDBOX-TEST-SUITE-DIVERGES-FROM-CI, of which this is a concrete instance with the pydantic-core panic named.

items.title: decide_over_cover asks whether a group holds a correct leg, not whether cancelling it loses one
items.detail:
RUN AGAINST THE LIVE CASE IT WAS BUILT FOR, over_cover_proposal.py returns `ambiguous_no_action` and dispatches nothing. The refusal is SAFE and the module is behaving as written -- this is a proposal to sharpen the rule, not a bug report against its caution.

MEASURED, ib_paper/MHG 2026-08-25T20:04Z. Position LONG 29; journal declares stop 6.31207143, target 7.141302. MHG tick 0.0005:
  oca-protect-465 (clientId 497): STP 6.312   =  0.14 ticks from the declared stop | LMT 7.1415 = 0.40 ticks from the declared target
  oca-protect-446 (clientId 597): STP 6.2625  = 99.14 ticks from the declared stop | LMT 7.1415 = 0.40 ticks from the declared target

So 465 matches BOTH declared levels and 446 matches the target ONLY -- and it matches the target only because BOTH groups carry the identical limit 7.1415. decide_over_cover classifies 446 as `partial` (stop_ok False, target_ok True) and refuses, on the correct-in-general ground that cancelling a partial match 'strips a leg that was right'.

IN THIS SHAPE IT DOES NOT. 465 already carries a target 0.40 ticks from the declaration, so cancelling 446 leaves every declared level still represented. The rule asks a per-group question -- *does this group hold a correct leg?* -- where the safety-relevant question is a per-POSITION one: *after cancelling it, is every declared level still covered by a surviving group?*

A LEG PRICE IDENTICAL ACROSS EVERY GROUP CARRIES NO DISCRIMINATING INFORMATION. Counting such a tie as a positive match for each group is what manufactures the ambiguity here: the target side cannot separate the groups, the stop side separates them by 99 ticks, and the verdict is driven by the non-discriminating side.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS ROW: the module's own docstring argues that 'we automated it once and got it wrong, so a human owns it forever' is how a detect-only design becomes a permanent operator tax. A decision layer that refuses the very case it was written against is on that same path by a different route -- it will be routed around by hand, which is the outcome it exists to prevent.
items.resolution_criteria: The DECISION half is closed. The BOOK half is tracked by OO-20260825-IB-PAPER-MHG-STOP-OVER-COVER and closes when /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper shows ib_paper/MHG resting ONE OCA group of 29 (not two), verified at the venue rather than from the dispatch's own success message.
items.proposed_change: Replace the per-group `partial` refusal with a per-position coverage check: a group may be cancelled when, for each side it holds that matches the declaration, at least one KEPT group also matches that side within tolerance. Keep the refusal when that does not hold. This is strictly narrower than the current rule -- it refuses everything the current rule refuses EXCEPT the case where the correct leg survives elsewhere -- so it cannot reintroduce the 2026-08-20 failure, in which the cancelled leg was the ONLY one matching the journal.
items.cross_session_note: over_cover_decision.py landed in #10291 from a concurrent session; the clientId provenance that makes the human read unambiguous landed in #10292 from this one. They compose: the provenance says 446 was submitted by a retired clientId 597 and carries the PREVIOUS trail level, which is corroborating evidence the decision layer does not currently look at. Deliberately NOT proposing that clientId age become a selection input -- the journal must stay the only authority on WHICH leg is right, per that module's stated invariant. It is context for the human the refusal hands off to.
items.resolution:
FIXED, and REPRODUCED LIVE FIRST rather than reasoned about. Ran scripts/ops/over_cover_proposal.py against the real book at 2026-08-26T01:00Z (/api/diag/ib_open_orders + /api/bot/positions) and it returned `ambiguous_no_action` on ib_paper/MHG — the module refusing the exact condition it was written for, six days after that condition was first paged, across three sessions.

THE NUMBERS. Journal trade: stop_loss 6.31207143, take_profit_1 7.141302, 29 long. Venue:
    oca-protect-465  STP 6.312   LMT 7.1415   <- agrees on BOTH sides
    oca-protect-446  STP 6.2625  LMT 7.1415   <- agrees on TARGET only
446's stop is 49 ticks low; its target is BYTE-IDENTICAL to 465's. So cancelling 446 loses NOTHING - the correct stop and the correct target both survive in 465 - yet the module refused because it asked 'does this group HOLD a correct leg?' instead of 'would cancelling it LOSE one?'.

THE RULE, deliberately conservative in the SAME direction as before: a partial group is cancellable ONLY when EVERY side it agrees on is also agreed on by the surviving keeper. A partial agreeing on a side the keeper does NOT hold still refuses - there the 2026-08-20 reasoning stands untouched, and a test pins that branch.
