⚠️ REACHING THAT BRANCH TOOK CARE, and the first attempt at its test did not: a keeper with the right stop and a WRONG target is itself graded `partial`, so BOTH groups were partial and the run fell into the no-keeper refusal instead of the branch being tested. The reachable shape is a keeper carrying NO target leg - then it agrees only on `stop` while the stray carries the declared TARGET. A test that passes without reaching its own branch is the vacuous-assertion class.

`partial_groups_covered_by_keep` is published so a cancelled partial can never read as a plain stray in an audit, and the reason string states the two cancel grounds SEPARATELY - folding a covered partial into 'matches nothing declared' would be false on its face, and an operator reads that line before firing a cancel against a live position.

Regression protection intact: all 15 pre-existing tests still pass, including test_reproduces_the_2026_08_20_failure, and the proposal tool's own self-test still selects the stray (338) and keeps the journal-matching leg (375). Break-tested: reverting the resolution fails the live-MHG test.
items.not_done:
THE 200% OVER-COVER ON ib_paper/MHG IS STILL LIVE. This fixed the DECISION, not the book: the tool now emits a concrete proposal (keep oca-protect-465; cancel oca-protect-446 = orders 447 and 448) and dispatches nothing, by design.

THE DISPATCH IS TIER-2 AND CARRIES A REAL HAZARD TO WEIGH. Both issue bodies set `force_client_id: true`, because 446 was submitted by clientId 597 and IB binds cancel rights to the submitter - so the action must CONNECT AS 597. CLAUDE.md warns that an owning id below 9000 is in the trader's execution band and connecting as it EVICTS the trader's live IB session. Measured 2026-08-26T01:00Z (/api/diag/ib_state, age 99.9s) the trader held 497, 498 and 9061 - NOT 597 - so on that reading the eviction risk does not apply. ⚠️ That is a 100-second-old snapshot of a set the trader ROTATES on reconnect failure, so it must be re-read immediately before any apply, not carried forward from this row.

items.title: /v2/account returns the cash-vs-margin discriminator and account_status threw it away
items.detail:
AlpacaClient.account_status() fetched the whole /v2/account payload and kept EIGHT authorization keys via a dict comprehension, discarding the rest. So the one field a gross-exposure CEILING depends on had no read surface anywhere in the system: `multiplier` is the cash-vs-margin discriminator (1 = cash, 2 = Reg-T margin, 4 = PDT day-trading), and on a CASH account a gross-exposure multiple can never exceed 1.0x -- a 2.0x ceiling there is decorative -- while on Reg-T the same value binds. Choosing between them by inference rather than by reading the field is what `field beats comment` forbids, and the data was already on the wire.

WHY IT BLOCKED A REAL DECISION. STEP 1 of BL-20260824-ALPACA-LIVE-GOLIVE-SEQUENCE is 'declare a bound on alpaca_live ... the VALUE needs a basis', citing the gross-exposure soak as the surface that supplies it. MEASURED 2026-08-25 over 2026-08-24T23:08Z -> 2026-08-25T21:47Z (22.7h, n=91 per account, /api/diag/log_file?name=exposure_soak):
  alpaca_live       equity $200.10   gross notional 0.0   multiple 0.0 on ALL 91 rows, zero non-zero
  alpaca_portfolio  equity $98,618.60  notional $197,795.92  max 2.0062 (mean 1.9050, median 1.8569, min 1.8422, p90 2.0056)
  alpaca_paper      equity $83,405.94  notional $166,383.41  max 1.9953

So alpaca_live's OWN soak is uninformative by construction -- it is dry_run and refuses everything, so it holds a permanently flat book and can never produce the distribution the design asks for. The only available basis is the paper mirrors, and alpaca_portfolio is a 14-of-16 roster mirror (BL-20260823-ALPACA-PORTFOLIO-MIRROR-MISSING-TWO-LIVE-LEGS). But their ~2.0x runs on ~$90k MARGIN books, and whether 2.0x is even reachable on a $200 account was unreadable. Hence this row before any ceiling value.

STATE THE POPULATION: 22.7h is NOT a soak. n=91, and only 286 of 1000 rows across the fleet are `rth` (384 extended, 330 closed), so under a third of the window observed a scheduled-open equity venue. The max over a short window is systematically LOW. These figures establish the SHAPE (a continuously ~1.85-2.01x deployed book) and are not a ceiling basis on their own.
items.resolution_criteria: account_status() exposes multiplier plus the buying-power/cash/PDT family in a nested `capacity` block; the eight authorization keys stay top-level and unchanged; an absent key is OMITTED rather than defaulted so an absent multiplier cannot be read as 'cash'; the extraction stays an allowlist rather than becoming a passthrough that ships account ids onto a diag surface; and the block is documented on the /api/diag/broker_account_status row in CLAUDE.md.
items.resolution: Shipped. `capacity` = {multiplier, buying_power, regt_buying_power, daytrading_buying_power, cash, equity, last_equity, pattern_day_trader, daytrade_count}, NESTED so the eight flags keep meaning exactly 'may this account trade at all' -- capacity is a second question and merging it would make `status_flags` a name that lies. No `capacity` key at all omits the block rather than shipping an empty dict, which would read as 'we asked and it is empty'. pattern_day_trader + daytrade_count ride along as the OTHER structural bound nobody models: FINRA caps a non-PDT-flagged margin account at 3 day trades per 5 days, and 16 strategies route to this account. 11 new tests; test_alpaca_wiring's exact-dict assertion was turned into coverage (the eight flags asserted unchanged AND the capacity capture asserted) rather than loosened -- its own comment had said 'extra fields ignored', which is precisely what changed.
follow_ups: READ THE LIVE VALUE NEXT: /api/diag/broker_account_status?account_id=alpaca_live now carries status_flags.capacity.multiplier. That single read decides whether STEP 1's ceiling should be ~2.0 (Reg-T, binds against the measured 12.37x sizer demand) or whether gross exposure is the wrong instrument entirely (cash, where the multiple cannot exceed 1.0 and the real bound is per-trade notional vs a $200 balance under whole-share sizing). This row deliberately does NOT propose the value.

The 22.7h window is not a soak. Before any ceiling ships, take the distribution over a window with meaningful RTH coverage -- BL-20260809-EXPOSURE-SOAK-NOT-YET-TAKEN is the standing row for that and this measurement does not close it.

items.title: The backlog-criteria census had its own definition of 'open' and it disagreed with the canonical one
items.detail:
check_backlog_criteria.py skipped closed rows with a hand-rolled literal `{"resolved", "closed", "wontfix"}` — a SECOND definition of 'is this backlog row open' living beside `scripts/reports/backlog_counts.py::is_open_status`, which is the canonical one and carries its own incident record for why its token sets are shaped as they are.

The two disagreed. The local set missed `superseded`, `invalid`, `duplicate`, `fixed`, `measured_no_action` and the whole `resolved_*` family — and, precisely, it spelled the one closed status it DID try to handle as `wontfix` while the corpus writes `wont_fix`, so the underscore form fell straight through. That is the `WARNING` vs `WARN` shape this repo has already paid for once (BL-20260813-OPERATOR-WARNING-BANNER-CANNOT-MATCH-WARN): a filter that cannot match the value its producer writes, while looking correct.

MEASURED 2026-08-25 by diffing the two predicates row by row across all three backlogs: **18 rows** were counted OPEN by the census and CLOSED by the canonical predicate — 8 `superseded`, 7 `wont_fix`, 3 `invalid`. Every one is a genuinely terminal disposition being asked to carry an exit condition it will never need. The census fell 109 -> 97 findings.

**ZERO rows moved the other way** (skipped -> open), which is the check that matters: the change is strictly a NARROWING and cannot hide a real open row behind the new predicate. That was measured, not reasoned.
items.resolution_criteria: check_backlog_criteria.py resolves open-vs-closed through backlog_counts.is_open_status rather than a local set; the import RAISES rather than falling back to a local approximation; and a row-by-row diff of the two predicates shows rows moving only from open to closed, never the reverse.
items.resolution:
Shipped. The census imports the canonical predicate by file path and RAISES if it cannot be loaded — deliberately, because a guard that quietly degrades to a weaker predicate when its canonical one is missing is the 'cheaper to lie to than to satisfy' failure this file's own header names; it would keep printing a number while measuring something else. Census 109 -> 97 findings over 473 open rows, 18 terminal rows excluded, 0 newly included.

SIDE FIND, corrected in the same change: BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED (severity CRITICAL) carried `wont_fix` while its own criteria begin '1. SHIPPED' and its last update reads 'FULLY REMEDIATED ... verified at the broker'. Set to `resolved`. The other two terminal rows whose text mentioned shipping were CHECKED and left alone: BL-20260629-DEVNULL-OCI-SOURCE-KILL carries `disposition: CLOSE_UNFIXABLE` (the OCI host agent is outside our control; mitigations shipped, the root source cannot be killed) and BL-20260617-ANDROID-56-VISUAL's matches are incidental.
follow_ups: The remaining 97 findings are the real debt: 77 open rows with no resolution_criteria at all, which is exactly BL-20260825-KEPT-OPEN-ROWS-WITH-NO-EXIT-CONDITION-CAN-NEVER-BE-RETIRED. 70 of them are `kept_open`, concentrated in 2026-07 (41) and 2026-08 (22). Not addressed here — writing 77 exit conditions is its own pass and must not be done by template.

items.opened_by: claude (system-review; found in my OWN diff, and caused by my own tool use)
items.title: backlog_union_merge.py hardcoded indent=2 while asserting parity with backlog_append — and reformatted all 4.8 MB of the health backlog on the one PR that used it
items.detail:
BL-20260820-BACKLOG-APPEND-REFORMATS-AND-REATTRIBUTES named the remedy as "a helper both the session-end routine and any tooling append through". backlog_append.py implements it correctly: it round-trips the file's OWN bytes against a candidate list and REFUSES when none reproduces them. backlog_union_merge.py — the conflict-resolution tool — did NOT go through it. It called json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) directly, under a docstring asserting "`ensure_ascii=False` + `indent=2` matches backlog_append.py, so this does not reformat the file and re-attribute unrelated rows to the merging PR".

THAT SENTENCE IS THE DEFECT, and it is field-beats-comment in its purest form: backlog_append.py does not HAVE a fixed format to match. Hardcoding indent=2 matches only files that already are indent=2, and docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json is **indent=1 with a trailing newline** on main. So the tool reformatted it on every conflict it resolved, while its own docstring promised the opposite.

MEASURED, on PR #10292, commit 89dac983 (a merge-conflict resolution): **+23,889 / -23,862 on that one file**. git show --numstat isolates it to that single commit; the other twelve backlog-touching commits on the branch are +2 to +25 each, which is what a normal append looks like. Every diff-scoped guard reads added-vs-origin/main, so the whole 927-row file now reads as added by that PR — which is exactly the re-attribution BL-20260820 exists to prevent, and it is why a diff-scoped impossibility-claim run on the branch reported 9 claims at scattered line numbers that belong to rows nobody in this PR wrote.

TWO THINGS MAKE IT WORSE THAN A COSMETIC CHURN. (1) A conflict resolution is the LIKELIEST moment for this class, because it is the only operation that re-serialises the whole file by construction — so the one door left open is the one most likely to be walked through. (2) The helper CANNOT UNDO IT, only avoid causing it: once a reformat lands, detect_format faithfully reproduces the NEW format on every subsequent write. Every helper-routed append I made after 89dac983 was individually clean (136 insertions / 18 deletions against the branch tip) and all of them silently locked the reformat in.

AND THE SELF-TEST COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT. backlog_union_merge's round-trip check plants an indent=2 fixture and asserts an em-dash survives — a probe that cannot find the positive it is looking for. The indent hazard was invisible to it by construction.
items.fix: SHIPPED in the same session. backlog_union_merge.py now imports detect_format and reproduces the SPINE's serialisation (`theirs`, the branch being merged into, so a merge can never change the target branch's format), REFUSES with FormatNotReproducible rather than reformatting, and prints the detected format before writing so the resolution is a stated decision. The false docstring claim is corrected in place, not deleted. Self-test 18 -> 25: it now plants indent=1 / indent=2 / indent=4 fixtures, asserts each round-trips byte-for-byte AND that the detector does not silently emit indent=2 for the other two, and asserts an unreproducible serialisation is refused.
items.not_done: THE EXISTING REFORMAT IS NOT REVERTED, deliberately. Reverting would be a SECOND 24k-line diff over the same file, and two churns are worse than one; after #10292 merges, main carries indent=2 and detect_format reproduces it from then on, so there is no ongoing breakage — only one permanently polluted diff. Content was verified intact rather than assumed: 919 rows on origin/main -> 927 in the working tree, ZERO ids lost, 8 added and all 8 are this session's new rows.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when a conflict is resolved through backlog_union_merge.py against a file whose on-disk format differs from indent=2, and the resulting diff is confined to the rows that actually changed — verified by git --numstat on that commit, not by reading the tool. Until such a conflict occurs the fix is shipped-but-unexercised and belongs in the review_coverage.unexercised_fixes block, NOT closed on the code landing: this row's own subject is a tool whose docstring asserted a property it did not have, so a code citation is precisely the evidence that should not close it.

updates.note: Re-validated and it is the sharpest irony in the backlog: the merge tool written to protect the file reformatted all 4.8 MB of it. Directly relevant to my triage — I used detect_format rather than a hardcoded indent for exactly this reason.

items.opened_by: claude (system-review; found by cross-checking the route against the trader's own sweep, 9 seconds apart)
items.area: diag read surfaces / exit coverage verification
items.title: /api/diag/bybit_open_orders reports FEWER resting legs than the venue holds for a symbol its settleCoin page DOES return — 3.02 across 7 vs the trader's 9.33 across 9, same position, 9s apart
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-25 on bybit_1/ETHUSDT, position size 5.59 Buy, two independent reads nine seconds apart:

  23:09:13Z  order_monitor._check_broker_naked_bybit_positions (SYMBOL-SCOPED read):
             'resting SL legs total 9.33 (167%) across 9 leg(s)'  -> OVER-covered
  23:09:22Z  /api/diag/bybit_open_orders (settleCoin=USDT account-wide page):
             7 PartialStopLoss legs summing 3.02  -> reads as 54% covered, UNDER-covered

Same account, same symbol, same position size (both report 5.59). The route is missing legs the venue holds.

⚠️ THE ERROR IS IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION. A consumer doing the obvious arithmetic on this route concludes the position is PARTIALLY NAKED with 2.57 ETH unprotected, when the truth is the opposite — it is over-covered at 167%, which is a different defect with a different remedy (cancel-stale-tpsl-legs, not a top-up). I made exactly that error while writing this row and caught it only because the trader's own journal disagreed; a session without that cross-check would have filed a naked-position alarm on a position that has too much protection, not too little.

ROOT CAUSE, read from the code rather than inferred: `account_bybit_open_orders` (src/units/accounts/clients.py, shipped 2026-08-22) reads POSITIONS with a per-symbol cross-check and reads ORDERS with NONE. The positions half carries the BL-20260713-BYBIT2-BTC-SETTLECOIN-BLIND remedy — 'a settleCoin=USDT page can silently OMIT a live symbol', so every CONFIGURED symbol the page missed is re-read symbol-scoped and flagged `settlecoin_blind`. The orders half is a single account-wide `get_open_orders(settleCoin='USDT', orderFilter=...)` page with no equivalent. The reasoning was right and was never carried across.

AND THE EXISTING CROSS-CHECK COULD NOT CATCH THIS ANYWAY, because it is guarded by `if not sym or sym in seen: continue` — it re-reads only symbols the page OMITTED ENTIRELY. Here the page RETURNED ETHUSDT, with fewer legs than exist. 'Present but incomplete' is a third state neither the page nor the cross-check can express, and it is invisible to both.
evidence: trader journal 2026-08-25T23:09:13Z: '_check_broker_naked_bybit_positions: LEG OVER-ACCUMULATION bybit_1/ETHUSDT — position size=5.59 but resting SL legs total 9.33 (167%) across 9 leg(s)'
/api/diag/bybit_open_orders captured_at 2026-08-25T23:09:22.182455+00:00: bybit_1/ETHUSDT 14 legs total, of which 7 PartialStopLoss summing 3.02 and 7 PartialTakeProfit summing 3.02
every returned leg carried a parseable qty (0 nulls), so the 3.02 is not an artifact of null-as-zero — checked explicitly before concluding
order_monitor._SL_LEG_TYPES_MON = {'stoploss','partialstoploss'} — the sweep and this arithmetic classify the same leg types, so the gap is the leg SET, not the classifier
items.impact: Scoped honestly: this is a READ surface, so nothing acts on it automatically and no order path is affected. But it is consumed by analysis sessions that cannot see the query they got, and it was built precisely to be the substrate that CONTRADICTS the reducing verdicts (`_bybit_position_protection` -> a covered quantity). A substrate that under-reports the thing it exists to verify is worse than no substrate, because it is trusted. scripts/ops/exit_path_coverage.py now consumes this route (this session) — its PRESENCE grading (does any stop / any target rest?) survives an incomplete leg set, but any QUANTITY read off it does not.
items.not_done: NOT FIXED IN-SESSION. The fix is to re-read symbol-scoped for every symbol holding an OPEN POSITION and prefer that result, flagging which source served each symbol's legs (`legs_source` ∈ symbol_scoped / settlecoin_page) rather than silently merging — the same never-collapse discipline the rest of the route already follows. Bounded cost: one extra call per open position (9 across 3 accounts at the time of measurement). Left unfixed because the correct shape needs a decision about whether to keep the page read at all, and filing it beats a rushed patch to a surface whose whole value is being trustworthy.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when a read of /api/diag/bybit_open_orders and the trader's own symbol-scoped sweep report the SAME leg count and summed qty for the same position within one sweep interval, demonstrated on a symbol where they currently disagree (bybit_1/ETHUSDT is the recorded instance), AND the payload names which read served each symbol's legs so a future divergence is attributable rather than merely absent. A code citation does not close it: the defect is that the route already LOOKS like it cross-checks.

updates.note: Re-validated and it QUALIFIES a read I made today: I used /api/diag/bybit_open_orders to confirm the surface exists (bybit_2, 2 positions / 4 orders) and this row says the ORDER page can under-report legs for a symbol the position page returns. So my order_count of 4 is a LOWER BOUND, not a census. CLAUDE.md's own note (settleCoin order page returned 7 SL legs where the symbol-scoped read saw 9) is the same finding.

EXAMINED AND DELIBERATELY NOT CLOSED — the mechanism is present and RUNNING, and my read of it was VACUOUS. Recording exactly why, and what a future session must wait for, so nobody closes this on the read I just made.

LIVE READ: /api/diag/bybit_open_orders, 2026-09-02T02:19:56Z, served by https://ict-bot.duckdns.org, against a trader process reporting git_sha 943a7192.

WHAT IS SATISFIED. The second half of the criterion — 'the payload names which read served each symbol's legs so a future divergence is attributable rather than merely absent' — IS met, and observed rather than cited: every bybit account returns `order_symbols_cross_checked` and `order_symbols_unchecked`. On bybit_1, cross_checked = [ADAUSDT, BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT, SOLUSDT] and unchecked = [], i.e. the symbol-scoped re-read ran on all four position-holding symbols including ETHUSDT, the recorded instance.

WHY THAT IS NOT ENOUGH, AND THIS IS THE WHOLE POINT. **Zero rows in the entire response carry `settlecoin_blind`** — 12 orders and 6 positions, all of them absent the flag. That flag is what the implementation sets on a leg the settleCoin page MISSED and the symbol-scoped read RECOVERED. So on this read the cross-check recovered NOTHING and the union was a no-op. I cannot distinguish 'the cross-check works' from 'the cross-check is inert' on evidence in which it never had anything to do. That is the vacuous-probe failure this repo names in RULE ONE: a search returning nothing is not proof of absence, and I have no positive control.

AND THE CRITERION'S OWN DEMONSTRATION IS NOT AVAILABLE. It asks for agreement 'demonstrated on a symbol where they currently disagree (bybit_1/ETHUSDT is the recorded instance)'. They do not currently disagree: ETHUSDT now rests 2 legs against the 7-vs-9 divergence recorded on 2026-08-25, so the over-accumulated book that produced the finding is gone. The condition the criterion requires be reproduced is not reproducible today.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT — and it is cheap once the condition recurs: a read of /api/diag/bybit_open_orders in which at least one row carries `settlecoin_blind: true`. That is the positive control, and it proves the recovery path RAN rather than merely being wired. Until such a read exists, treat `order_count` on this route as a leg count whose completeness is asserted but unproven.

OBSERVED vs INFERRED, stated plainly: the field presence and the cross_checked/unchecked lists are OBSERVED on the live fleet. That the union would recover a missed leg is INFERRED from the code path and is exactly what remains unproven.

items.opened_by: claude (system-review; the third instance of this class in one session, so filed as the CLASS)
items.title: _check_broker_naked_bybit_positions reaches the systemd journal and NOTHING ELSE — 365 lines, 3 logger.error, zero emit(); a live 167% over-covered position alarmed to an audience of nobody
items.detail:
THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT THE IB SIDE HAD, ON THE VENUE WHERE ONE ACCOUNT IS MAINNET. `_emit_stop_over_cover_alert` was added to the IB sweep earlier today for exactly this: `logger.error` reaches the systemd journal and never writes `outcomes.jsonl`, which is what feeds Telegram, the /api/bot/notifications banner and /api/bot/logs?level=error. The Bybit sweep was not given the same treatment and nobody checked whether it needed it.

MEASURED by reading the function: `_check_broker_naked_bybit_positions` is 365 lines and contains 3 `logger.error`, 7 `logger.warning`, and ZERO of `emit(` / `Level.CRITICAL` / `Level.ERROR` / `_cooldown_admits` / any outcomes call. Every condition it detects is journal-only.

CONFIRMED LIVE, with a working control. Over the operator ERROR+ feed (/api/bot/logs?level=error&limit=1000 — 405 rows spanning 2026-08-20T08:16Z -> 2026-08-25T22:48Z, 5.6 days):
    LEG OVER-ACCUMULATION      0
    PARTIALLY NAKED            0
    _check_broker_naked_bybit  0
    CONTROL ib_target_naked  141   <- the feed DOES carry protection alerts
    CONTROL 'bybit' anywhere   18   <- and DOES carry bybit content
The controls are the point: a zero over a feed that carries neither would prove nothing. This feed carries both, so the zero is a real absence.

AND THE CONDITION WAS FIRING INSIDE THAT WINDOW. Trader journal, 2026-08-25T23:09:13Z: 'LEG OVER-ACCUMULATION bybit_1/ETHUSDT — position size=5.59 but resting SL legs total 9.33 (167%) across 9 leg(s). Legs have piled up; a trip would over-close and strand the rest.' That is a live position carrying 167% of stop cover, detected correctly, and invisible on every surface a human reads.

WHY IT MATTERS AT THE SAME SEVERITY AS THE IB CASE: the message names the consequence itself — a trip over-closes and strands the remainder. On a netted one-way book that is the naked-reverse shape. `bybit_1` is demo, but `bybit_2` and `bybit_portfolio` run the same code path and `bybit_2` is MAINNET.

items.opened_by: claude (system-review; root-caused from a live 167% over-cover, then AST-audited every call site)
items.title: The 2026-07-21 close-side leg-cancel fix is passed at 1 of 10 close_open_position call sites — the pairs sleeve was one of the nine, and it leaked 12 legs onto a live position
items.detail:
ROOT CAUSE of BL-20260730-BYBIT1-XRP-LEG-OVERACCUM-WORSENING, which has been open since 2026-07-30 labelled 'worsening' with no cause recorded.

`close_open_position(..., sl_order_id=, tp_order_id=)` cancels the closing trade's own tracked Bybit Partial-tpsl legs after a confirmed close — shipped 2026-07-21 as the structural half of BL-20260721-BYBIT2-XRP-TPSL-LEGCAP and described in CLAUDE.md and ROADMAP.md as done. AST-audited 2026-08-25 across src/ and scripts/: **10 call sites, and exactly ONE passes the ids** (order_monitor.py:1666, which reads them off `matched_trade`). The parameter exists, the cancel logic exists, and nine callers do not use it — the written-and-never-read shape one level up, at the call site rather than the field.

MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, live on bybit_1/ETHUSDT 2026-08-25T23:09Z. Position 5.59 Buy; the trader's own sweep reports resting SL legs totalling 9.33 across 9 legs = **167%**, and logs 'a trip would over-close and strand the rest'. Of 14 resting legs readable, 2 belong to the one OPEN row (4921) and **12 belong to SIX CLOSED rows** — 5003, 4998, 4974, 4937, 4932, 4909, every one closed by `pairs_revert` / `pairs_stop` / `pairs_half_open_cleanup`. **ZERO orphans**: every resting leg maps to a journal row, so the leaked-close path is the WHOLE cause, not a contributing one.

⚠️ THE NINE ARE NOT ONE PROBLEM — dispositioned individually, because a blanket 'pass the ids everywhere' would be wrong at most of them:
  FIXED  src/units/strategies/pairs_executor.py:768 (_close_pair) — the row was ALREADY in scope (`direction`, `position_size`, `entry_price` all read off it three lines up), so this was never a missing-context problem. Two kwargs. Fixed this session.
  EXEMPT src/units/strategies/pairs_executor.py:631 (_unwind_placed_legs) — iterates (symbol, direction, qty) tuples from a partial-placement failure and holds no row.
  EXEMPT scripts/ops/flatten_{ib,alpaca}_position.py — non-Bybit; the kwarg is ignored by every other exchange branch.
  OPEN   src/core/coordinator.py:2074 — the flip_flat close. Works from net signed qty and genuinely has NO trade row; its own comment says the row is closed later by the reconciler's close-on-disappear. A real gap needing a design answer, not a two-line fix.
  OPEN   src/runtime/order_monitor.py:1764, src/units/ui/processor.py:1707, scripts/ops/flatten_bybit_position.py:87 — Bybit-reachable, row availability NOT yet established at each. Do not assume they are all like the pairs one.
  N/A    scripts/sprint047/spot_margin_smoke.py:219 — a smoke script.
items.why_it_matters: On a one-way netted book the legs of a CLOSED trade do not expire — they keep resting against the SURVIVING position. That is over-coverage, and the trader's own message states the consequence: one leg trips, the position flattens, and the remaining legs are still resting to sell qty that no longer exists. bybit_1 is demo; bybit_2 and bybit_portfolio run the same close path and bybit_2 is MAINNET.
items.not_done:
Only the pairs `_close_pair` site is fixed. The four OPEN sites above are untouched — each needs its own row-availability check first, and coordinator.py:2074 needs a design answer rather than a kwarg. The 12 legs ALREADY stranded on bybit_1/ETHUSDT are NOT cleaned up by this fix (it only stops new ones); that backlog is the `cancel-stale-tpsl-legs` system-action, Tier-2, dry-run by default — and this row PREVIOUSLY ended '...which is wired and was genuinely used in July, so it is a remedy that exists rather than one that needs building'. THAT WAS WRONG AND DANGEROUS, twice over. (1) The script existed but its selection was unsafe: it kept the NEWEST leg by Bybit createdTime with zero journal awareness, which on this very position would have kept a CLOSED trade's 0.19 leg and cancelled the live trade's 1.18, taking a 167%-over-covered position to 3.4% covered (BL-20260826-CANCEL-STALE-TPSL-LEGS-WOULD-KEEP-A-CLOSED-TRADES-LEG-AND-CANCEL-THE-LIVE-ONE). (2) 'was used in July' was doing load-bearing work it cannot do: it was used against bybit_2/XRPUSDT, a symbol with ONE open row, which is the only shape its assumption holds for. A remedy that worked on one shape is not evidence about a different shape.

AS OF 2026-08-26 the selector is FIXED — ownership-based, pure, and pinned against the recorded failure (src/runtime/stale_leg_decision.py). The 12 stranded legs are STILL NOT cleaned up: nothing has been dispatched, and the corrected script must be DRY-RUN and its plan checked against the journal first.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when a pairs close on bybit_1 is followed by a read showing that trade's tracked leg ids NO LONGER resting — measured on a real close, not a unit test — AND the four OPEN call sites above each carry a recorded disposition (fixed, or exempt with the reason its row is unavailable). A code citation does not close it: the fix being 'shipped' at one of ten sites is exactly what this row is about.

updates.note:
THE THREE 'OPEN — row availability NOT established' SITES ARE NOW ESTABLISHED, by reading each one. They do NOT share a disposition, and one of them would have been HARMED by the same fix.

1. src/units/ui/processor.py:1707 (close_open_positions) — SAME DEFECT, FIXED. `for row in rows:` and it reads row['id'] / ['account_id'] / ['symbol'] / ['direction'] / ['position_size'] / ['strategy_name']. The row is in scope exactly as in pairs_executor._close_pair, and `qty` IS row['position_size'] — a FULL close — so after a confirmed flat the trade's qty-scoped legs have nothing left to protect. Two kwargs.

2. src/runtime/order_monitor.py:1764 — ROW IN SCOPE, AND MUST NOT BE FIXED THIS WAY. ⚠️ This is the PARTIAL-close path: it is gated on `account_supports_management(cfg, 'partial_close')` and passes a caller-supplied `qty=float(qty)`, NOT the row's position_size. The position is STILL OPEN afterwards, so cancelling its protective legs would strip protection from the remainder — turning a leg-accumulation bug into a NAKED-POSITION bug, which is strictly worse. Under Bybit Partial mode the correct action is an AMEND-DOWN of the leg to the remaining qty, not a cancel and not leaving it: leaving it over-covers the remainder, which is this row's own subject. That is a third disposition category — needs an amend, has neither a fix nor an exemption today — and it is why 'pass the ids everywhere' had to be refused.

3. scripts/ops/flatten_bybit_position.py:87 — EXEMPT BY DESIGN, with a caveat. The script deliberately holds no journal row: its own docstring says 'The journal row is left for the trader's reconciler to close-on-disappear'. It flattens by SYMBOL from the exchange side, so there is no `sl_order_id` to pass without giving an ops script journal access — a design change, not a kwarg. CAVEAT WORTH KEEPING: because it flattens FULLY, the legs it leaves behind are exactly the stale kind, so an operator flatten still seeds the accumulation this row is about. Not proposed here.

RUNNING TALLY: 10 call sites — 2 fixed (pairs _close_pair, processor close_open_positions), 4 exempt with a stated reason (_unwind_placed_legs and flatten_bybit hold no row; flatten_ib/flatten_alpaca are non-Bybit), 1 needs an AMEND not a cancel (order_monitor partial close), 1 open needing a design answer (coordinator flip_flat, no row), 1 n/a (smoke script), 1 already correct (order_monitor:1666, the reference).

⚠️ A TEST-QUALITY NOTE WORTH RECORDING, because it is the failure mode this row is an instance of. My first assertion for the processor fix was `assert "sl_order_id" in captured` against a fake defaulting `sl_order_id=None` — the default populates the key whether or not the caller passes it, so the assertion could not fail. Break-testing caught it: with the fix REVERTED the suite still went green, 16 passed. Replaced with a sentinel default and re-break-tested; it now fails on the revert. A green suite over an assertion that cannot fail is precisely how the original leg leak survived five weeks.

⚠️ CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN `not_done`, AND TO PR #10297's body. Both said the already-stranded legs are handled by `cancel-stale-tpsl-legs` — 'a remedy that already exists and was genuinely used in July'. The first half is true and the implication is WRONG: it exists, and firing it on this position would make things much worse.

Measured before dispatching (which is the only reason this was caught): the script keeps the NEWEST leg per side by Bybit createdTime with zero journal awareness. On bybit_1/ETHUSDT right now the newest SL leg belongs to trade 5003, which is CLOSED, qty 0.19 — so it would KEEP a dead trade's leg and CANCEL open trade 4921's 1.18, leaving a 5.59 position covered at 3.4%. It would turn a 167%-over-covered position into a 96.6%-naked one.

That is BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG reproduced on Bybit — the same class the IB side answered by making its over-cover path detect-only and moving the selection into a pure, separately-tested function.

So the DEPLOYED fix in this row stops NEW leaks and the EXISTING 12 stranded legs remain unresolved, with no safe remedy available today. Filed as BL-20260826-CANCEL-STALE-TPSL-LEGS-WOULD-KEEP-A-CLOSED-TRADES-LEG-AND-CANCEL-THE-LIVE-ONE with the proposed ownership-based selection. Do not read this row's earlier `not_done` as a green light.

HIGH. Re-validated and the pairs sleeve — the one explicitly named as missed — is the sleeve producing 35 half-open cleanups in 9 days. A close-side leg-cancel wired at 1 of 10 sites means 9 close paths leave legs behind, which is a direct contributor to the over-cover and stranded-leg families.

items.opened_by: claude (system-review; caught by reading the remedy's code BEFORE dispatching it)
items.tier: 2 (a live-fireable operator action on the order path)
items.title: cancel-stale-tpsl-legs keeps the NEWEST leg by createdTime with zero journal awareness — on bybit_1/ETHUSDT today that keeps a CLOSED trade's 0.19 leg and cancels the open trade's 1.18, taking a 167%-covered position to 3.4%
items.detail:
THIS IS THE DOCUMENTED REMEDY FOR BL-20260825-CLOSE-SIDE-LEG-CANCEL-IS-WIRED-AT-1-OF-10-CALL-SITES, and firing it on the position that motivated that row would have been catastrophic. Found by reading the script before dispatching, not by running the dry-run — the dry-run would have shown it, but only to a reader who checked the plan against the journal, which is exactly the check the script does not do.

THE RULE (scripts/ops/cancel_stale_tpsl_legs.py::_keep_and_stale, verified in code, not inferred from the docstring): `ordered = sorted(group, key=_created_ms, reverse=True)` then `return ordered[0], ordered[1:]`. It keeps ONE leg per side — the newest by Bybit `createdTime` — and cancels every other. It never reads `trades`, never looks at `sl_order_id`, and has no concept of which leg belongs to which journal row.

ITS ASSUMPTION IS STATED IN ITS OWN DOCSTRING and no longer holds: 'all sharing the qty of the account's SINGLE real position — i.e. duplicate/stale legs stacked on one position'. That was true of the 2026-07-21 bybit_2/XRPUSDT incident it was written for. It is NOT true of a netted symbol carrying SEVERAL open journal rows, where each row legitimately owns its own qty-scoped leg.

MEASURED ON THE LIVE BOOK 2026-08-26T00:10Z — bybit_1/ETHUSDT, position 5.59, TWO open rows (4921 qty 1.18 + 4903 qty 4.41 = 5.59 exactly). Ranking the visible SL legs by createdTime:
    rank 0  qty 0.19  2026-08-25 01:05  owner trade 5003  **CLOSED**   <- would be KEPT
    rank 1  qty 0.47  2026-08-24 23:02  owner trade 4998  closed
    rank 2  qty 0.53  2026-08-24 00:05  owner trade 4974  closed
    rank 3  qty 0.21  2026-08-22 12:05  owner trade 4937  closed
    rank 4  qty 0.26  2026-08-22 11:00  owner trade 4932  closed
    rank 5  qty 1.18  2026-08-22 07:05  owner trade 4921  **OPEN**     <- would be CANCELLED
    rank 6  qty 0.18  2026-08-21 23:01  owner trade 4909  closed

So it would KEEP the leg of a trade that no longer exists and CANCEL the only open row's leg in the visible set, leaving the 5.59 position covered by 0.19 = **3.4%**. It would take a position that is over-covered at 167% to one that is 96.6% NAKED. That is not a partial improvement — it is a strictly worse state than doing nothing.

THIS IS BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG, REPRODUCED ON THE OTHER VENUE. That row is why the IB over-cover path is detect-only and why its selection was moved into a pure, separately-tested function (src/runtime/over_cover_decision.py) checked against the recorded failure. Bybit's stopgap never got that treatment.
items.why_newest_is_wrong: Newest-by-createdTime is a proxy for 'the level the strategy currently intends', which is sound when one row keeps re-adding legs for ONE position (the original incident). On a netted symbol with N open rows it is not a proxy for anything: a leg's age says nothing about whether its owning trade is still open, and a recently-closed trade's leg is newer than an older open trade's. Recency and liveness are different properties and the script conflates them.
items.not_done:
THE 167% OVER-COVER ON bybit_1/ETHUSDT IS STILL UNRESOLVED - this row fixed the SELECTOR, not the book. Nothing has been dispatched. The next step is a DRY-RUN of the corrected script on the live VM, whose plan must then be checked against the journal before any --apply.

AND THE FIGURES IN THIS ROW MUST BE RECOMPUTED FIRST. The leg table above came from /api/diag/bybit_open_orders, which under-reports (7 visible SL legs against the trader's symbol-scoped 9), so the fixture pins the SHAPE, not a complete population. The script's own read IS symbol-scoped (_stop_orders passes symbol=), so its dry-run sees the full set - which is why the dry-run, not this row, is the thing to validate against. Two legs the diag route could not show may be unattributable, in which case the corrected script correctly REFUSES and the cleanup needs those two identified first.
items.proposed_fix: Select by OWNERSHIP, not by age: cancel exactly the legs whose `sl_order_id`/`tp_order_id` belongs to a CLOSED journal row for that (account, symbol), and keep every leg owned by an OPEN row. That is computable today — the join is the one this session used to find the defect, and it produced ZERO unattributable legs (every resting leg mapped to a row). Refuse when any leg is unattributable rather than guessing, and put the decision in a pure function tested against THIS recorded case, mirroring over_cover_decision.py. Keep the existing rule available only behind an explicit flag for the single-row case it was built for, if at all.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when cancel-stale-tpsl-legs, run in DRY-RUN against bybit_1/ETHUSDT in its current state, returns state=cancel_legs with every proposed cancel owned by a closed row and BOTH open rows' legs (4921's and 4903's) in plan.keep - verified against the journal, not against the plan's own wording. A dry-run returning unattributable_legs is NOT a failure of this fix; it is the refusal working, and closes only once those legs are attributed.
items.caveat: The leg table above is from /api/diag/bybit_open_orders, which under-reports legs for a symbol its settleCoin page returns (BL-20260825-...-PAGE-DOES-RETURN): 7 SL legs visible against the trader's symbol-scoped count of 9. The two missing legs do not change the finding — the newest visible leg is already a closed trade's, and trade 4903's leg is absent from the visible set entirely — but the exact post-cancel coverage figure should be recomputed from a symbol-scoped read before any fix is validated.
items.resolution:
FIXED. The selection is now by OWNERSHIP, in a pure separately-tested function: src/runtime/stale_leg_decision.py::decide_stale_legs. A leg is cancelled because the journal row that owns it (trades.sl_order_id / tp_order_id) is CLOSED; every leg owned by an OPEN row is kept; a leg no row claims REFUSES the whole run rather than guessing. Seven states, never collapsed: cancel_legs / no_stale_legs / no_resting_legs / unattributable_legs / would_undercover / not_graded / position_absent.

TWO INDEPENDENT GUARDS, not one. Beyond the ownership rule there is a COVERAGE check: if cancelling the closed-owned legs would leave stop coverage below the position, the run refuses (would_undercover) rather than opening the gap before anything closes it. Verified by break-test - with the ownership predicate deliberately INVERTED, the script does not strand the position naked, it aborts on would_undercover. Defence in depth was the explicit goal: the failure this row records is precisely a single-rule selector being wrong.

PINNED AGAINST THE RECORDED FAILURE. tests/test_stale_leg_decision.py::test_reproduces_the_2026_08_26_failure and tests/ops/test_cancel_stale_tpsl_legs.py::test_does_not_cancel_the_live_trades_leg drive the measured leg table and assert the NEWEST leg (0.19, closed trade 5003) is CANCELLED while trade 4921's older 1.18 and trade 4903's 4.41 are KEPT. Both were break-tested: inverting the predicate fails them (and 5 more), so they are not vacuous. The newest-wins rule cannot return without failing CI.

The script's own docstring was corrected in place - both the rule and the 'all sharing the qty of the account's SINGLE real position' assumption that made the old rule look safe (field beats comment).

items.tier: 2 (new operator alert on the live trader)
items.title: The Bybit sweep detected leg over-accumulation with logger.error only — it reached the systemd journal and NO human surface, for four weeks, while bybit_1/ETHUSDT sat at 167% over-covered
items.detail:
The unpaged-detection class, third recurrence. _check_broker_naked_bybit_positions has counted `over_covered` since 2026-07-30 (BL-20260730-BYBIT1-XRP-LEG-OVERACCUM-WORSENING) and reported it with `logger.error`. logger.error reaches the systemd journal and NOTHING ELSE: it never writes outcomes.jsonl, which is what feeds Telegram, /api/bot/notifications and /api/bot/logs?level=error. Verified in code, not inferred: the 366-line function contains 3 logger.error and ZERO emit( calls.

THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT FIXED FOR IB ONE DAY EARLIER (_emit_stop_over_cover_alert, 2026-08-25), whose own record says the Bybit side was left unchecked.

MEASURED WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL (state the population): the operator ERROR+ feed, /api/bot/logs?level=error&limit=1000, returned 401 rows spanning 2026-08-20T09:42:48Z -> 2026-08-26T00:33:07Z. Bybit over-cover rows: ZERO. ib_stop_over_cover rows: THREE (2026-08-25T12:27Z, 2026-08-25T18:30Z, 2026-08-26T00:33Z, all ib_paper/MHG 200%). The control matters: a quiet feed is not evidence of a quiet condition, and without it 'zero rows' would have been indistinguishable from a broken probe. The IB page fires and is visible; Bybit simply never had a page to find.

AND THE ONLY HUMAN-REACHABLE SURFACE REPORTED THE OPPOSITE SIGN. The enforcing read (_bybit_position_protection) is SYMBOL-SCOPED (client.get_open_orders(symbol=symbol)) and saw 167% OVER-covered on bybit_1/ETHUSDT. /api/diag/bybit_open_orders was settleCoin-PAGED and, read the same session, showed 7 SL legs / 3.02 qty against a 5.59 position = 54% UNDER-covered. So an analysis session reading the diag route would have concluded the position needed MORE protection while the trader had correctly concluded it had far too much. That read gap is fixed in the same change (the orders-half symbol cross-check).
items.resolution:
FIXED. `order_monitor._emit_bybit_over_cover_alert` pages via outcomes.report, wired at the detection site, with `summary['over_cover_alerted']` so the call is assertable.

DELIBERATELY NOT _emit_stop_over_cover_alert(venue='bybit'), even though that function already takes a venue= parameter. Its entire hazard argument is IB-specific and would be FALSE here: it warns that one stop firing leaves a disjoint OCA group resting to sell again into a NAKED SHORT, and routes the operator to cancel-ib-order over IB's clientId cancel-rights rule (Error 10147). Bybit has no OCA groups, and every resting Bybit SL leg is reduceOnly - MEASURED on all four live bybit_1 symbols (XRPUSDT, ADAUSDT, ETHUSDT, BTCUSDT), not assumed - so it cannot flip the position. Reusing it would be a semantic substitution: a confident label over a quantity the code did not compute.

THE BYBIT HAZARD, stated for what it is: (1) the 20-leg cap, at which set_trading_stop refuses (110061) and a GENUINE protective tightening fails SILENTLY - hence leg count and cap headroom on the page; (2) a reduce-only leg owned by a CLOSED row triggering and cutting a live position at a dead trade's level.

LEVEL IS ERROR, NOT CRITICAL. Both reach Telegram (_TELEGRAM_LEVELS = {ERROR, CRITICAL}) so nothing is lost in delivery; CRITICAL is reserved for a position that is UNPROTECTED or REVERSED, and spending it on an over-protected reduce-only book is how the channel gets trained away - 202 of 376 CRITICALs were once one un-latched alarm.

Severity is the LEG COUNT (integer, cannot flap, only grows under the producing defect), so a worsening breaks the 6h window. The cooldown is the SHARED _cooldown_admits, never a copy - copy-pasting a latch is how the per-PROCESS time.monotonic() defect would return in the copy.

THE WIRING IS TESTED SEPARATELY FROM THE PAGER, because it had to be: the 10 unit tests call the pager directly, so deleting the sweep's call to it left all ten GREEN. test_over_accumulation_PAGES_the_operator_not_just_the_journal drives the whole sweep and fails when the call is removed - break-tested. A denominator test (test_a_healthy_symbol_pages_nothing) asserts a correctly-covered position pages nothing, so the page is a signal rather than noise.
items.not_done:
⚠️ THE 'SHIPS UNEXERCISED' CAVEAT IS NOW DISCHARGED — do not re-quote it. The page FIRED on a real position at 2026-08-26T01:16:05Z, three minutes after #10299 merged and deployed (/api/diag/version git_sha 98fec40d, restart_pending false). Observed via /api/bot/logs?level=error, i.e. the operator-facing feed that four weeks of logger.error never reached:

    bybit_over_cover detected: bybit_1/ETHUSDT: position 5.59 but resting SL legs total 9.33 (167%) across 9 leg(s). 9 of Bybit's 20-leg cap are used (11 left); at the cap `set_trading_stop` refuses (ErrCode 110061) and a genuine protective tightening fails SILENTLY...

THE PAGE ALSO INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED THE READ-SURFACE FINDING, which is worth more than the page itself: it reports **9 legs**, from the trader's own symbol-scoped read, against the **7** the settleCoin-paged /api/diag/bybit_open_orders showed. Two producers, one prediction, confirmed - and the orders-half cross-check shipped in the same PR is what closes that gap.

WHAT REMAINS: `journal_qty_divergent`, the other detect-only signal in the same sweep, is still logger.error-only. Its rate must be measured from the trader journal BEFORE adding a page - a condition firing every tick needs a latch design, not a bare emit. Tracked with the other open member of the class on BL-20260826-UNPAGED-DETECTION-CLASS-IS-NEARLY-EXHAUSTED-ONE-MEMBER-LEFT (whose 'nearly exhausted' conclusion is itself withdrawn - see that row).

AND THE BOOK IS STILL OVER-COVERED. The page is the alarm, not the remedy: bybit_1/ETHUSDT still rests 9.33 against 5.59. Clearing it needs a DRY-RUN of the corrected cancel-stale-tpsl-legs whose plan is checked against the journal.
items.resolution_criteria: MET 2026-08-26T01:16:05Z — a real `bybit_over_cover` row on a real position in /api/bot/logs?level=error, three minutes after deploy. The mechanism is EXERCISED, not merely deployed.

items.opened_by: claude (system-review; class sweep, not an instance)
items.tier: 2 (a new operator alert on the live trader)
items.title: The 'detected but paged nobody' class: my sweep said ONE member left and the sweep's own shape was too narrow — a fourth member was found minutes later in the order path, where no counter is incremented
items.detail:
THE CLASS. A live sweep DETECTS a condition, increments a counter, and reports it with `logger.error` — which reaches the systemd journal and NOTHING ELSE, never outcomes.jsonl, so not Telegram, not /api/bot/notifications, not /api/bot/logs?level=error. Three known instances: ib_stop_over_cover (fixed 2026-08-25), bybit over_covered (fixed 2026-08-26), and the member below. Two fixes in two days is what makes it a class rather than a row.

THE SWEEP, and STATE THE POPULATION. AST over all of src/ for the shape all three instances share: an `if` block that increments a `summary[...]` counter AND logs at error level AND contains no paging call. **3 sites matched.** The two just fixed no longer match, which is the check that the detector detects.

⚠️ AND 2 OF THE 3 MATCHES ARE FALSE POSITIVES — verified by reading each, not by trusting the count:
  * order_monitor.py:7835 `stop_price_diverges` — NOT a member. It calls `_reassert_from_divergence`, a real remediation. The heuristic missed it because its paging-token list ('emit(', 'report(', '_emit_', '_alert(', 'notify') does not match '_reassert_'. 'Remediates without paging' is a DIFFERENT state from 'does nothing', and conflating them would have filed a fix for a path that already acts.
  * order_monitor.py:9141 `partially_naked` — NOT a member. It logs and then immediately resolves levels and re-arms/tops up. It self-heals; a page would be noise unless the top-up FAILS, which is a different (and narrower) proposal.
  * order_monitor.py:9005 `journal_qty_divergent` — THE ONE GENUINE MEMBER. Open journal rows summing above the netted exchange size means at least one open row is a PHANTOM, and both analytics and risk sizing read the journal. Nothing remediates it and nothing pages it.

⚠️ MY FIRST PROBE WAS WRONG BY 6x AND I ALMOST FILED ON IT. It counted the literal string 'logger.error' and reported 7 modules repo-wide; a corrected regex covering logger/log/logging/_log/_logger and .error/.critical/.exception found **41 modules / 210 call sites**. The corrected probe was only trusted after a POSITIVE CONTROL (order_monitor.py, a module read this session and known to have them, returned 16). A search returning little is not proof of little.

SO THE CLASS IS NEARLY EXHAUSTED, which is the actionable finding: this does NOT need a guard. A guard built on the heuristic above would carry a measured 2-of-3 false-positive rate, and a guard cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than no guard (the `new-table-wiring-guard` lesson). One remaining member is a row, not a checker.

⚠️ CORRECTED SAME SESSION, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE POINT. Within minutes of filing 'nearly exhausted, one member left' I found a FOURTH member by reading code for an unrelated reason: src/units/accounts/ib_client.py::place_protective logs 'this position is now OVER-COVERED and needs a human at the venue' (line 1835) and 'the position is still over-covered and a human must clear the remainder at the venue' (1821) with logger.error, and that module CANNOT PAGE AT ALL - `grep -c outcomes` returns 1 and the single hit is the English word in a comment (positive control: order_monitor.py returns 18). Filed as BL-20260826-IB-PLACE-PROTECTIVE-KNOWS-IT-JUST-OVER-COVERED-A-POSITION-AND-TELLS-ONLY-THE-JOURNAL.

WHY THE SWEEP MISSED IT: it keyed on an `if` block that increments a `summary[...]` counter AND logs at error level AND has no paging call. That shape was abstracted from the three known instances, which were all SWEEP sites. An ORDER-PATH site increments no counter - it is not tallying a survey, it is reporting what it just did - so it could never match, and the sweep returned a confident '3 sites' over a population that structurally excluded a whole category.

THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON, and it is the same one this session already recorded once for a DERIVED feed: a probe abstracted from known instances inherits their shape, so its denominator is 'sites resembling what we already found', never 'sites where the condition holds'. The 3-site count was accurate about the query and misleading about the class. A denominator needs its own justification, not just a positive control - and I ran the positive control (order_monitor returned 16 error-level logs) and still missed this, because a positive control proves the probe FIRES, not that its shape SPANS the class.

SO 'NEARLY EXHAUSTED' IS WITHDRAWN. Known open members are now TWO: journal_qty_divergent (sweep site) and the place_protective branches (order-path site). The class is NOT enumerated, and the next pass should sweep by 'module has error-level logs AND cannot reach outcomes' (41 modules / 210 call sites by the corrected regex) rather than by the counter shape.
items.not_done:
`journal_qty_divergent` is NOT fixed. It was deliberately left out of the bybit over-cover change rather than swept in on the assumption one page fits both: it is a different condition (a phantom journal row — an analytics/sizing defect, not a live protection one), so it wants its own hazard statement and its own level, and its existing code already shows care about alarm fatigue (it special-cases the pairs-sleeve case so it does not name a remediation that will never come).

⚠️ It was measured at 0 rows in the same 401-row operator ERROR+ feed — but that population CANNOT distinguish 'never fired' from 'fired and is invisible', which is precisely the ambiguity a page removes. Do not read the 0 as evidence the condition is absent. The trader journal (`/api/diag/journalctl`) is where its true rate is readable, and establishing that rate should come BEFORE adding a page — a condition firing every tick needs a latch design, not just an emit.

⚠️ AND THE CONCLUSION 'THIS DOES NOT NEED A GUARD' IS NOW LESS SUPPORTED THAN WHEN WRITTEN. It rested on a measured 2-of-3 false-positive rate over a 3-site population that has since been shown incomplete. The reasoning against a cheap-to-lie-to guard still stands on its own merits; the EVIDENCE for it does not. Re-derive the rate over the wider population before either building a guard or re-asserting that none is needed.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when (a) the true firing RATE of `journal_qty_divergent` has been measured from the trader journal over a stated window — not inferred from its absence in the operator feed — and (b) either it pages through outcomes.report with a hazard statement specific to a phantom journal row and a level justified against the desensitized-alarm P1, or a written finding says it should not page and why. Both outcomes close it; silence does not.

updates.note: Re-validated and my own sweep AGREES the class is nearly exhausted: the operator ERROR feed now carries bybit_over_cover (20), ib_stop_over_cover (6), alpaca_target_naked (16) and ib_target_naked (108) — four detectors that previously reached nobody now page. The row's own caution (its sweep shape was too narrow) is the right posture; do not declare the class closed on a narrow probe.

items.title: place_protective detects that it has just left a position OVER-COVERED across disjoint OCA groups and says so with logger.error only — src/units/accounts/ib_client.py cannot reach outcomes at all, so the one moment with full context reaches no human surface
items.detail:
⚠️ THIS ROW WAS FILED WITH A MUCH LARGER STRUCTURAL CLAIM AND I REFUTED IT MYSELF BEFORE IT LEFT THE SESSION. The original text asserted that the pre-cancel is session-scoped, therefore silently no-ops on a leg owned by a rotated-away clientId, therefore place_protective stacks a second full-size bracket - an 'over-cover generator'. It was a satisfying story built from a partial read, and it is WRONG in its load-bearing step. Recording it because the correction is the useful part.

WHAT IS TRUE (verified by reading each function's enumeration source):
  protection_coverage            -> _req_all_open_orders   ACCOUNT-WIDE
  has_protective_orders          -> reqAllOpenOrders       ACCOUNT-WIDE
  list_open_orders               -> reqAllOpenOrders       ACCOUNT-WIDE
  _cancel_oca_group_for_symbol   -> _open_trades           THIS SESSION
  _cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol -> _open_trades        THIS SESSION
  _verify_cancel_effect          -> _req_all_open_orders   ACCOUNT-WIDE   <-- THE STEP I MISSED

WHAT REFUTES THE CLAIM: the pre-cancel's enumeration is session-scoped, but its VERIFY is account-wide, and place_protective reads that verify's `still_resting` and JOINS the survivors' OCA group instead of minting a second one - its own log line even names the mechanism, 'leg(s) survived the pre-cancel (owned by a retired clientId); JOINING their OCA group'. The loop is closed. A cancel path that cannot SEE a leg is not the same as a code path that cannot HANDLE it, and I conflated the two.

WHAT ACTUALLY SURVIVES, and is the finding: ib_client.py holds FOUR error-level logs and CANNOT PAGE - `grep -c outcomes` returns 1, and that single hit is the English word 'outcomes' in a comment at line 2636, not an import (positive control: order_monitor.py returns 18). Three of the four are in this exact block and each announces a live money-adjacent state at the moment it is created, with full context:
  1812  survivors joined into their group (mitigated, informational)
  1821  'joining %r leaves %d group(s) this session cannot merge or cancel. The position is still over-covered and a human must clear the remainder at the venue.'
  1835  'Arming a fresh bracket anyway ... this position is now OVER-COVERED and needs a human at the venue.'
Rows 1821 and 1835 are the system stating, in its own words, that it has just created the exact condition `_emit_stop_over_cover_alert` pages about - and telling only the systemd journal. The sweep catches it later, from outside, without the context of which call did it or why the join failed.

SO THIS IS A FOURTH MEMBER OF THE UNPAGED-DETECTION CLASS, and it corrects BL-20260826-UNPAGED-DETECTION-CLASS-IS-NEARLY-EXHAUSTED-ONE-MEMBER-LEFT, whose AST sweep keyed on `summary[...] += 1` blocks and therefore could not see an order-path site that increments no counter. The sweep's shape was too narrow, which is a finding about the sweep.

OBSERVED STATE, for whoever picks this up (2026-08-26T01:30Z, /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper vs /api/diag/ib_state trader holding 497/498/9061): MHG rests TWO disjoint groups, oca-protect-465 (clientId 497) and oca-protect-446 (clientId 597) - so on that occasion the JOIN did not happen, and WHY is undetermined from outside: the join code may postdate 446, verify_state may not have been 'verified', or _select_join_group may have declined. That question is exactly what a page at line 1821/1835 would have answered at the time and no later surface can.

⚠️ AND A PREDICTION I MADE IS PROBABLY WRONG - do not act on it. I predicted MGC was 'one re-arm away from 200%' because `place()` sets no ocaGroup (verified: its entry-bracket legs are linked by parentId only, so IBKR auto-assigns the bare numeric group 834864174 seen live) and the scoped pre-cancel matches only `oca-protect-t<key>`. The scoped CANCEL indeed cannot match it - but the account-wide verify would see the survivor and the join path would join it, so the predicted stacking most likely does not occur. MGC is currently CORRECT (51 short; STP 4699.9 / LMT 4602.4 against journal 4699.87285714 / 4602.44071429).
items.not_done:
Nothing is fixed. The proposal is narrow and Tier-2: give ib_client a paging path for the 1821 and 1835 branches - the two that state the position is over-covered - so the operator learns at CREATION time, with the calling context, rather than from a later sweep that can only see the aftermath.

⚠️ DO NOT PAGE 1812. It is the MITIGATED branch (survivors were joined, the legs stay mutually cancelling); paging a successful mitigation is the desensitized-alarm P1 this repo has already paid for twice.

⚠️ AND CHECK THE RATE BEFORE WIRING IT. place_protective runs on every naked re-arm; if 1821/1835 fire often the page needs a latch design (the durable _cooldown_admits shape), not a bare emit. That rate is unmeasured - it is readable from the trader journal via /api/diag/journalctl, and it must be measured first.

SEPARATELY UNRESOLVED: why the join did not happen for MHG's oca-protect-446. Answering it needs the trader journal around when oca-protect-465 was placed, not another venue read.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when the 1821/1835 branches reach outcomes.jsonl and a real firing is OBSERVED in /api/bot/logs?level=error - not when the code merely ships (a fix that is deployed and a fix that works are indistinguishable from every surface we have). Closing on a code change alone does not count.

updates.note: Re-validated: the code KNOWS at the moment it acts and tells only the journal. Detection at the point of causation is strictly better than the after-the-fact sweep, so this is the higher-value half of the over-cover family.

items.title: The bybit_over_cover page I shipped reported '9 of 20 used, 11 left' while the venue held 18 of 20 with TWO left — it divided a COMBINED TP+SL cap by an SL-only count
items.detail:
SELF-INFLICTED, found ~40 minutes after shipping, and only because the cancel-stale-tpsl-legs DRY-RUN was run against the SAME position and listed both collections.

THE SUBSTITUTION: Bybit's cap is 20 COMBINED TP+SL legs per symbol (CLAUDE.md says so in as many words, and the constant I added was even commented "combined TP+SL leg cap"). The page computed `headroom = 20 - leg_count`, and `leg_count` was `len(state['sl_leg_ids'])` — STOP legs only, because `_bybit_position_protection` filters to `_SL_LEG_TYPES_MON`. Right cap, wrong numerator.

MEASURED, both sides, same position, minutes apart:
  the page, 2026-08-26T01:16:05Z : '9 of Bybit's 20-leg cap are used (11 left)'
  the venue, dry-run #10303      : 9 PartialStopLoss + 9 PartialTakeProfit = 18 of 20,
                                   TWO left
A cap-proximity alarm that overstates headroom by 9 legs is worse than no alarm, because it reads as a measurement. This is the diagnostic-provenance sub-class A (semantic substitution) committed in the very change that fixed an unpaged detection - the label named a combined quantity, the code passed a one-sided one.

⚠️ AND IT COST NOTHING TO GET RIGHT: `orderFilter="StopOrder"` already RETURNS the PartialTakeProfit rows - the dry-run's own output proves it, since that is the same call - and they were being discarded by the SL filter before anything counted them. No extra broker call, no new read path.
items.resolution:
FIXED. `_bybit_position_protection` now also returns `protective_leg_count` (SL + TP), counted from rows it already had, and the page uses it for headroom and for severity.

TWO QUANTITIES, NEVER COLLAPSED, and the split is the point: `covered_qty`/`sl_leg_ids` answer a STOP-COVERAGE question and stay SL-only; `protective_leg_count` answers a CAP-PROXIMITY question and is combined. The page prints both ('18 of Bybit's 20-leg COMBINED TP+SL cap are used (2 left; 9 of them are stop legs)') so neither can be mistaken for the other.

AN UNCOUNTABLE TARGET SIDE PUBLISHES NO HEADROOM. `leg_cap_headroom` is None - never `20 - stop_count` - and the prose says 'UNKNOWN (not large)'. Substituting the measurable half for the whole is the defect itself, so the fallback refuses rather than estimates. Severity still falls back to the stop count, so an uncountable target side can never SILENCE a worsening.

BREAK-TESTED IN BOTH HALVES, and the second one was needed: removing the sweep's `protective_leg_count=state.get(...)` argument left all 37 pager+sweep tests GREEN, because the pager's own tests pass the value directly. test_the_page_receives_the_COMBINED_leg_count_not_just_the_stops drives the whole sweep and fails both when the wiring is removed AND when the counter itself is narrowed back to SL-only. That is the SECOND uncovered-wiring gap found in this file today by the same technique.
items.not_done:
✅ EXERCISED AND VERIFIED 2026-08-26T02:19:58Z (deploy 084be99e, restart_pending false). And the corrected page did not merely reproduce the old one — it immediately surfaced a live condition the defect had been CONCEALING. Same position, 14 minutes apart:
    02:06:00 (old) : '10 of Bybit's 20-leg cap are used (10 left)'
    02:19:58 (new) : '20 of Bybit's 20-leg COMBINED TP+SL cap are used
                      (0 left; 10 of them are stop legs)'
bybit_1/ETHUSDT is AT THE CAP. `set_trading_stop` refuses at 20 (110061), so a genuine protective tightening on that position FAILS SILENTLY right now — which is precisely the money-at-risk state the cap warning exists to announce, and the SL-only count reported ten legs of headroom over it.

⚠️ STATE THE POPULATION, because it bounds the urgency: this is `bybit_1`, the DEMO account. Real money was checked in the same pass and is CLEAN — `bybit_2` ETHUSDT 4 legs / XRPUSDT 2 legs, `bybit_portfolio` ETHUSDT 4 / XRPUSDT 2, i.e. 16-18 legs of headroom each (/api/diag/bybit_open_orders, 2026-08-26T02:35Z, read_state orders_read on both). The saturation is confined to demo.

IT IS ALSO STILL ACCUMULATING: SL legs went 9 -> 10 between 01:16 and 02:06 and the combined count reached 20. The cleanup dry-run (#10303) is clean and would take it from 20 legs to 4, but the apply is Tier-2 and awaits an operator decision.

items.title: cancel-ib-order labels IBKR 202 (the cancel CONFIRMATION) as "venue REFUSED", and cites 10147 whatever code arrived
items.detail: Measured live 2026-08-26 on ib_paper/MHG order 447 (issue #10309). IBClient._locked_cancel installs _cancel_error_capture and treats ANY code that lands on the error channel, keyed to the orderId, as a refusal. IBKR delivers informational notices on that same channel, and code 202 is 'Order Canceled' - the cancel CONFIRMATION. The run therefore returned retCode 1 with retMsg 'venue REFUSED the cancel: IBKR error 202' and action 'refused_by_venue' for a cancel that SUCCEEDED. THE OUTCOME IS NOW SETTLED, and it is the opposite of what the tool reported: two later fresh-client account-wide reads (#10310 at 04:36Z, #10313 at 04:43Z) both return orders_on_account 8 with 447 and 448 not_found, against 10 before the cancel - a difference of exactly the two legs of oca-protect-446, with all six other orders identical. Compounding it, the wrapper's note is emitted unconditionally and names a DIFFERENT code: 'Error 10147 specifically means the submitting clientId no longer holds the order' - 10147 was not the code received. Sub-class A unprovenanced diagnostic: a failure message naming a cause no code path tested. RAISED TO HIGH because the direction is the dangerous one for a repair tool: it reports a successful cancel as a venue refusal, which invites an operator to retry a cancel that already worked, or - worse - to conclude a stranded protective order cannot be cleared and reach for flatten-ib-position, which PLACES an order.
evidence: issue #10309 - apply run, cancel_response.refusal {code: 202, message: 'Order Canceled - reason:'}, action 'refused_by_venue', verify_state 'still_present'
issue #10310 - orders_on_account 8, 448 not_found
issue #10313 - read-only dry run with NO force flags (so it never connected as the owning clientId 597), orders_on_account 8, 447 not_found
src/units/accounts/ib_client.py::_locked_cancel - `if refusal:` branch treats any captured code as a refusal
items.resolution_criteria: _cancel_error_capture (or its consumer) distinguishes IBKR INFORMATIONAL codes - 202 at minimum - from genuine rejections, so a 202 renders as a successful cancel rather than retCode 1 / 'venue REFUSED'; and the 10147 note is emitted ONLY when the captured code is 10147. A test asserts both: a captured 202 does not render as a refusal, and a captured non-10147 refusal does not print the 10147 sentence.

updates.note: HIGH. Re-validated: labelling IBKR 202 — the cancel CONFIRMATION — as 'venue REFUSED', and citing 10147 whatever code arrived. Diagnostic-provenance sub-class A on a remediation tool, which means an operator acting on it does the OPPOSITE of what the venue reported.

items.title: /api/diag/ib_open_orders keeps returning orders that were cancelled - the read surface built to CHECK protection claims over-reports them
items.detail: Measured live 2026-08-26 on ib_paper (issues #10309, #10310, #10313). After order 447 was cancelled, /api/diag/ib_open_orders continued to return count 10 including BOTH 447 and 448 - on reads at 04:35Z, 04:36Z, 04:37Z and 04:44Z - while two fresh-client account-wide reads returned 8 with both not_found. The two views differ by EXACTLY the two legs of oca-protect-446 and agree on all six other orders, so this is not a partial or scoped read: the diag side is carrying the cancelled pair forward. MECHANISM (proposed, not yet proven): an IB order-status callback goes to the SUBMITTING client. The web-api process holds a long-lived readonly client (ib_read_client_for) that did not submit these orders, so it never receives their cancel callback; reqAllOpenOrders repopulates ib.trades() but a Trade whose local orderStatus was never updated still filters as active. That predicts a view that only ever GROWS, which is what four reads over 13 minutes show. RULED OUT: client-scoping - #10313 set no force flags, so it never connected as the owning clientId 597 and still saw 8. NOT RULED OUT: that the fresh reads are the wrong ones. WHY IT IS HIGH, and it is not the enforcing path: _check_broker_naked_ib_positions grades with ib_client_for(readonly=False) - the TRADER's own client, which submitted the brackets and does get its own callbacks - so naked-detection and the over-cover page are NOT affected. What IS affected is every human and every session that reasons about live IB order state, because this route is the ONLY surface that does not reduce it to a boolean or a quantity, and it was built precisely so a coverage verdict could be contradicted from outside. A surface that silently accumulates dead orders makes over-cover look worse than it is and can never show a cleanup worked. IT ALREADY CAUSED A WRONG MEASUREMENT IN THIS SESSION: MHG was reported here as THREE resting groups carrying 87 lots of stop against a 29 position. The fresh read shows 8 orders on the account (2 MES + 2 MGC + 4 MHG), i.e. MHG genuinely holds TWO groups - 465 and t4796 - and 58 lots, not 87. The over-cover is real at 200%; the 300% figure was an artifact. Any earlier over-cover measurement taken from this route should be re-checked against a fresh client before being quoted, including BL-20260816-IB-STOPS-OVER-COVER-IN-DISJOINT-OCA-GROUPS.
evidence: /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper - count 10 with 447 + 448 present at 04:35Z, 04:36Z, 04:37Z and 04:44Z
issue #10310 - fresh client, orders_on_account 8, 448 not_found
issue #10313 - fresh client, NO force flags so no connection as clientId 597, orders_on_account 8, 447 not_found
the two views agree on the other six orders (MES 6/410 oca-protect-408, MGC 422/423 group 834864174, MHG 466/467 oca-protect-465, MHG 486/487 oca-protect-t4796)
src/units/accounts/clients.py::account_ib_open_orders - no cache of its own; the staleness is in the long-lived client's ib.trades()
src/runtime/order_monitor.py::_check_broker_naked_ib_positions - uses ib_client_for(readonly=False), the submitting client, so the enforcing path is unaffected
items.resolution_criteria: Prove the mechanism first by reading the same account twice in one run - once through the long-lived readonly client and once through a freshly built one - and diffing the sets; a difference confined to orders cancelled by another client confirms it. Then either the read client refreshes its order book so a cancelled order stops filtering as active, or account_ib_open_orders builds a fresh client per call. Whichever is chosen, the check that ends this row is behavioural: cancel an order via one client and assert /api/diag/ib_open_orders stops returning it, verified on the live fleet.
updates: 2026-08-26 — MECHANISM NOW READ FROM THE CODE, not just inferred from the reads. IBClient._open_trades is `list(ib.openTrades())`, and _req_all_open_orders issues reqAllOpenOrders and then returns exactly that. ib_insync's openTrades() reads its ACCUMULATED Trade cache filtered to active statuses; reqAllOpenOrders delivers openOrder callbacks only for orders that are still OPEN, and nothing prunes a Trade absent from the response. A Trade whose status was never moved to Cancelled - because the orderStatus callback goes to the SUBMITTING client - therefore stays at PreSubmitted in that cache forever and keeps being returned. That is the monotonic-growth prediction, and it is what six reads showed: four stale reads at 10 vs two fresh-client reads at 8, differing by exactly the cancelled pair. PROPOSED FIX, deliberately NOT shipped in this session: have account_ib_open_orders build a FRESH client per call rather than reusing the process's long-lived readonly one, since a fresh ib_insync instance starts with an empty cache and is populated solely by the response. That is not a guess about the library - it is what issues #10310, #10313, #10318 and #10319 measured, each returning the correct 8. WHY IT WAS NOT SHIPPED, stated so the next session does not read this as untouched work: ib_insync is NOT INSTALLED in the web sandbox (verified - `import ib_insync` raises ModuleNotFoundError), and the repo's IB tests are stubs, so they pin this repo's ASSUMPTIONS about the library rather than its behaviour. The change also alters how a live service dials a broker - it adds a connect per call, and a fresh connect always probes - which on a wedged gateway is the failure class IB_PROBE_CACHE_S and the breaker exist for. Read plus connect-behaviour makes it Tier-2 in effect, not a plain Tier-1 read edit, and it should be validated against a real gateway rather than against stubs that cannot fail. A CHEAPER PARTIAL that needs no library contract: the route currently reports read_state 'orders_read', documented as a confirmed clean read, for a view that may carry cancelled orders. That CLAIM is wrong independently of the staleness and could be corrected on its own - but on its own it only relabels the defect, so it is worth doing WITH the fix, not instead of it.

updates.note: ⚠️ RE-CONFIRMED AND I CARRIED THE CAVEAT EXPLICITLY. The route's own envelope now ships `stale_read_caveat` naming this row, and I read it today. It qualifies my clean ib_paper MES finding: the view can show an order already cancelled, so my read is a supersets-not-census. It CANNOT invent a second OCA group that is not there, which is the direction my conclusion depended on — so the conclusion holds while the caveat stands.

items.title: cancel-stale-tpsl-legs reported 'partial_cancel - 7 failed' on a run that fully achieved its goal
items.detail: Measured live 2026-08-26 on bybit_1/ETHUSDT (issue #10308). The run reported action 'partial_cancel', 'cancelled 7/14 stale legs (7 failed)'. All 7 'failures' were TAKE-PROFIT legs and all 7 carried Bybit ErrCode 110001 'order not exists or too late to cancel'. Each shares a createdTime with the stop leg cancelled immediately before it, i.e. Bybit places a Partial SL/TP pair such that cancelling the stop removes its paired target, so the subsequent explicit target cancel is a no-op on an order that is already gone. The OUTCOME was complete and was verified independently of the tool: /api/diag/bybit_open_orders afterwards shows 6 legs (3 SL + 3 TP), exactly the 6 the decision chose to keep, restoring 14 of headroom under Bybit's 20-leg combined cap, with 7.48 of stop resting against the 5.78 position. So the label is a FALSE NEGATIVE on a fully successful run. That direction is less dangerous than the inverse but it is not harmless: it trains an operator to read 'partial_cancel - 7 failed' as routine, which is the desensitized-alarm shape, and it would mask a genuinely partial run.
evidence: issue #10308 - action 'partial_cancel', detail 'cancelled 7/14 stale legs (7 failed)', cancel_results showing all 7 as ErrCode 110001 on PartialTakeProfit legs
the 7 failing TP legs each share createdTime with a stop leg cancelled OK in the same run (e.g. 1787619902658, 1787612573717, 1787529902746)
/api/diag/bybit_open_orders?account_id=bybit_1 post-run - ETHUSDT 3 PartialStopLoss + 3 PartialTakeProfit, combined 6 of 20, stop qty 7.48 vs position 5.78
items.resolution_criteria: A 110001 on a leg the same run already removed via its paired sibling is classified as already_gone rather than failed, so a run that reaches its intended post-state reports success. The states stay separate: already_gone (we removed it via its pair) must not be merged into cancelled (we cancelled it directly) nor into failed (the venue refused). A test asserts a run whose targets all return 110001 after their stops cancelled OK does not report partial_cancel.

updates.note: Re-validated: reporting 'partial_cancel - 7 failed' on a run that fully achieved its goal. Same family as the 202-as-refusal row — remediation tools that misreport their own success.
