items.title: A stray legacy-named OCA group owned by the trader's OWN live clientId can be cleared by neither repair path
items.detail: Measured live 2026-08-26 on ib_paper/MHG (issue #10315). Trade 4796 is 29 long and carries TWO resting 29-lot groups - oca-protect-t4796 (STP 486 @ 6.3525, matching the journal's declared 6.35257143) and oca-protect-465 (STP 466 @ 6.312, superseded when the stop trailed up). 58 lots of stop against a 29 position, confirmed from a FRESH client, not the stale diag route. NEITHER repair reaches the stray group, and the two blockers are independent: (1) the trader's own re-arm cannot. place_protective is reached with oca_key=trade_id so it cancels `oca-protect-t<id>`, which does not match a legacy `oca-protect-<reqId>` name - the mismatch is already documented in order_monitor.py's target-naked branch, which cites BL-20260816-NO-PER-ORDER-IB-CANCEL as the repair that would close it. (2) that repair landed as the cancel-ib-order action, and it REFUSES here: order 466's owning clientId is 497, inside the trader's execution band (<9000), because connecting as it would evict the trader's live IB session. The refusal is correct - the point is that it leaves no path. So the class the 2026-08-16 comment expected cancel-ib-order to close is closed only for legs owned by a RETIRED clientId. Order 447 in oca-protect-446 was owned by 597 and was cleared today; 466 is owned by the live 497 and cannot be. WHY IT MATTERS: OCA cancels only WITHIN a group, so if one group's stop fires and flattens the position, the other group's 29-lot stop is still resting and can fill into a naked SHORT. That is the same hazard BL-20260816-IB-STOPS-OVER-COVER-IN-DISJOINT-OCA-GROUPS names, now with a demonstrated instance that no existing tool can remediate. NOT ESTABLISHED: how the stray group arises. The keyed naming shipped recently and t4796 proves it is exercised, so 465 may simply pre-date it - in which case this is a finite backlog, not a generator. Do not assume either without measuring how many legacy-named groups still rest and whether any NEW one appears after the keyed path deployed.
evidence: issue #10315 - fresh-client dry run, orders_on_account 8, order 466 found, oca_group 'oca-protect-465', client_id 497.0, action 'refused' with both blockers named
src/runtime/order_monitor.py target-naked branch - the comment documenting that place_protective's keyed cancel cannot match a legacy `oca-protect-<reqId>` group
src/units/accounts/ib_client.py:1750 - `oca-protect-t{oca_key}` keyed form vs :1862 `oca-protect-{reqId}` legacy form
issue #10313 - the same fresh-client read showing 8 orders on the account (2 MES + 2 MGC + 4 MHG)
items.resolution_criteria: First MEASURE the population: how many legacy-named `oca-protect-<reqId>` groups still rest across ib_paper, and whether any appeared AFTER the keyed path deployed - that decides whether this is a finite cleanup or an ongoing generator, and the two want different fixes. Then a stray group owned by the trader's own live clientId has SOME reachable path: either the trader cancels by resolved oca_group name rather than only the keyed one, or the repair runs in a maintenance window with the trader stopped, or cancel-ib-order gains a route that does not require assuming the owning id. Ends when ib_paper/MHG holds exactly ONE protective group for trade 4796, verified from a fresh client.
updates: 2026-08-26 — STEP 1 OF THE RESOLUTION CRITERIA (measure the population) IS ANSWERED, and the answer leans FINITE BACKLOG rather than ongoing generator. STATE THE POPULATION: 3 open ib_paper positions, 8 resting orders, all 8 reconciled into 4 groups, from FRESH-CLIENT reads only (#10313/#10315/#10318/#10319) - the diag route is excluded as stale per BL-20260826-DIAG-IB-OPEN-ORDERS-SERVES-A-STALE-MONOTONIC-ORDER-VIEW. n=3 positions is a small denominator and this is ONE snapshot; read the direction, not a rate. THE FOUR GROUPS BY NAMING FORM: oca-protect-408 (MES 4350, legacy oca-protect-<reqId>, STP 410 @ 7533.75 + LMT 6) - CURRENT, matches declared 7533.69642857 at the 0.25 tick. 834864174 (MGC 5007, numeric IBKR-assigned, i.e. the place() entry-bracket form, STP 423 @ 4699.9 + LMT 422) - CURRENT, matches declared 4699.87285714 at the 0.1 tick. oca-protect-465 (MHG 4796, legacy, STP 466 @ 6.312 + LMT 467) - SUPERSEDED against declared 6.35257143. oca-protect-t4796 (MHG 4796, KEYED, STP 486 @ 6.3525 + LMT 487) - CURRENT. SO: 2 legacy-named groups still rest, and only ONE of them is stale. A legacy NAME is not evidence of staleness - oca-protect-408 is legacy-named and is the correct live bracket for MES. Any future sweep keyed on the naming form alone would cancel it, which is the BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG shape. Grade by the DECLARED LEVEL, never by the name. WHY THIS LEANS FINITE: MES and MGC carry exactly ONE group each. If a trail still re-minted the bracket on every stop move, accumulation would show on them too, and it does not - only MHG has two. AN OBSERVATION I AM NOT EXPLAINING, flagged rather than theorised: MES's resting stop was recorded at 7516.50 on 2026-08-23 and now rests at 7533.75, while its group name is UNCHANGED at oca-protect-408. The level moved without the group being re-minted. That is consistent with an in-place amend, but I did not establish which path did it and it should not be asserted without reading the trader journal around the change.

updates.note: HIGH and LIVE-RELEVANT: ib_paper MES rests under `oca-protect-408`, a LEGACY <reqId>-form group, right now. This row says such a group owned by the trader's own clientId is reachable by neither repair path. Today that group is correct and complete, so it is benign — but it is exactly the state the row describes, sitting on a live 15-lot position.

items.title: cancel-ib-order's clientId guard tests a BAND but tells the operator the trader owns the order and is live
items.detail: cancel_ib_order.py's second blocker fires on `owner < _TRADER_CLIENT_ID_CEILING` (9000) - a pure BAND test - and then states three things that test never established: 'connecting as it would evict the trader's live IB session', 'The trader itself owns this order', and 'pass --force-client-id only with the trader stopped'. All three are true only when the owning id is CURRENTLY CONNECTED. The band also contains RETIRED reconnect-rotation ids, and those are exactly the ones a stranded protective leg tends to be owned by. MEASURED BOTH WAYS ON THE SAME ACCOUNT, 2026-08-26, which is what makes this a real defect and not a wording quibble: order 447 (ib_paper/MHG) was owned by clientId 597, which was NOT in the live client set - /api/diag/ib_state at 03:51:13Z listed 497, 498 and 9372 - so connecting as 597 evicted nothing and the cancel succeeded (#10309). Order 466 is owned by 497, which IS live, so the same sentence is true there (#10315). The guard emitted the identical message for both. WHY IT MATTERS: this message is what an operator reads when deciding whether to force past the guard, and it names a remedy - stop the trader - that is unnecessary and disruptive in the retired-id case, which is the common one for stranded legs. Under-stating risk would be worse; this over-states it, and the cost is that the cheap safe path looks like the expensive dangerous one. It is the unprovenanced-diagnostic class this repo already has a guard for (sub-class A: a message naming a cause no code path tested). THE MEANS TO DISTINGUISH ALREADY EXIST AND ARE ALREADY ON THE VM: the trader writes runtime_logs/ib_state.json each tick (the file /api/diag/ib_state serves), listing every live client id. The script runs on the VM and can read it. THE REFUSAL SHOULD NOT CHANGE - it must stay default-on in every case, including 'we could not look'. Only the MESSAGE needs to stop asserting a fact it did not check.
evidence: scripts/ops/cancel_ib_order.py - `if owner < _TRADER_CLIENT_ID_CEILING and not args.force_client_id:` and the blocker text that follows it
issue #10309 - order 447, owner_client_id 597, forced, cancel succeeded (confirmed by #10310/#10313 fresh reads showing 8 orders and 447 not_found)
/api/diag/ib_state at 2026-08-26T03:51:13Z - live clients 498, 9372, 497; 597 absent
issue #10315 - order 466, owner_client_id 497, the same message emitted where it IS true
items.resolution_criteria: The blocker message distinguishes three states, never collapsed, read from runtime_logs/ib_state.json: `live_session` (the owning id appears among the current clients - the existing wording is correct here), `retired_band_id` (in the band, NOT currently connected - say so, and do not tell the operator to stop the trader), and `unknown` (ib_state absent, stale, or unreadable - 'we could not look', which must read as the cautious case, not as retired). The refusal itself stays default-on in all three. A test asserts the message differs across the three and that none of them drops the refusal.

updates.note: Re-validated: testing a clientId BAND while telling the operator the trader owns the order and is live. An assertion stronger than the evidence, on a cancel path.

items.title: The documented 'restart your branch from the default branch' step discards the previous PR when it has not merged yet, and a successful push looks identical
items.detail: The session workflow tells a session to restart its designated branch from the latest default branch and push follow-up work there. That is correct AFTER a merge. Applied while the PREVIOUS PR is still open, it resets the branch past that PR's commit, the force-push moves the head away from it, and GitHub closes the PR WITHOUT MERGING - the change is gone and nothing failed. HAPPENED 2026-08-26, measured not supposed: #10323 (the MHG population measurement) closed 'closed without merging' at 05:15:40Z after its CI had already passed at 05:14:08Z. origin/main then carried 941 items with that row showing ZERO updates, i.e. the content never landed, while the session had already reported it as done. Recovered on #10326. The same pattern ran four times that night and was safe three times purely because the prior PR happened to merge in the interim - so the failure is intermittent and timing-dependent, which is what makes it worth a row rather than a note. THE DETECTION GAP IS THE REAL DEFECT, not the git step. `git push` succeeding is evidence the BRANCH moved, and nothing more; it is not evidence the content reached main. Every signal a session normally trusts stayed green - guards passed, push succeeded, CI passed - and the PR still closed empty. The one signal that told the truth was the close notification's wording, 'closed without merging' rather than 'merged', which is a single word's difference in a body that is otherwise identical. SCOPE: this is a session-workflow trap, not a runtime bug. It costs silently lost work and, worse, a session reporting work as landed when it is not - which is the reporting-honesty failure the operating rules exist to prevent.
evidence: PR #10323 - closed without merging 2026-08-26T05:15:40Z; check_suite.completed on its head 6026b608 had passed at 05:14:08Z
origin/main immediately after - 941 items, and the MHG stray-group row (the one #10323 was updating) carried zero updates
PR #10326 - the recovery, restoring the same measurement onto a branch based on the then-current main
items.resolution_criteria: The workflow instruction states the precondition explicitly - restart the branch from the default branch only once the previous PR has MERGED, and check that rather than assuming it - and pairs it with the verification that actually settles the question: after a push, confirm the content is present on origin/main (or that the PR is open and its head carries the commit), never treat a successful push as a landing. Ends when a session following the written steps cannot lose a commit this way without something saying so.

updates.note: Re-validated and it is a live trap for MY branch: the documented restart-from-default step would discard PR #10414 if applied while it is unmerged. I rebased instead. The instruction needs a merged-PR precondition.

items.title: ict_scalp_5m and trend_donchian both trade BTCUSDT live on one-way-netting Bybit accounts, so two strategies share ONE exchange position and neither one's per-strategy PnL is an exclusive measurement
items.detail: Operator directive 2026-08-26: separate the BTC scalp from trend_donchian, as its OWN tracked item. MEASURED, not supposed - config/strategies.yaml: trend_donchian symbols [BTCUSDT] timeframe 1h execution live; ict_scalp_5m symbols [BTCUSDT] timeframe 5m execution live. Both are routed together on bybit_2 (real money), bybit_1 (demo) and bybit_portfolio (paper). Bybit here is ONE-WAY NETTING, which this repo already documents as the mechanism behind the netting partial-close class: a symbol is ONE exchange position holding N journal rows, close detection is per-ORDER, and a position-level exit shrinks a position the siblings still claim in full. So on BTCUSDT the 5m scalp and the 1h trend leg are not two books - they are one, and each strategy's per-strategy PnL is a journal-side ATTRIBUTION over a position neither one exclusively owns. WHY THIS MATTERS RIGHT NOW. The operator flagged 'a lot of losses on BTC' and asked for a full investigation before any demotion. This row is the reason a per-strategy PnL number cannot by itself answer that question: the split between 'the scalp lost this' and 'the shared BTCUSDT position lost this and the scalp was charged for it' is UNMEASURED. A demotion decided on the attributed figure alone could remove the wrong leg, and an entry-gate fix evaluated against the same figure could be scored against noise it does not control. THIS IS NOT A CLAIM THAT THE SCALP IS FINE. The aggregate BTCUSDT book is losing; what is unestablished is the attribution between the two legs. Both readings survive the evidence so far and the measurement below is what separates them.
evidence: config/strategies.yaml - trend_donchian: symbols [BTCUSDT], timeframe 1h, enabled true, execution live; ict_scalp_5m: symbols [BTCUSDT], timeframe 5m, enabled true, execution live

config/accounts.yaml - both legs co-route on bybit_2 (mode live, account_class real_money), bybit_1 (mode live, account_class paper) and bybit_portfolio (mode live, account_class paper, paper_role portfolio)
fvg_range_15m is the third BTCUSDT leg on all three accounts but is execution: shadow, so it places nothing and is NOT part of the collision - stated so the population is not over-counted

The netting mechanism is already documented and measured in this repo (NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_MODE / the per-ORDER close-detection class); this row applies that mechanism to a specific live pair, it is not a new hypothesis about Bybit
items.resolution_criteria: Two things, and the FIRST is Tier-1 and must come first. (1) MEASURE the collision on BTCUSDT: over the shared-position history, how much of each leg's attributed PnL is exclusive vs shared, and how often did one leg's exit move the other's position? Until that number exists, every per-strategy BTCUSDT figure is quoted with the caveat. (2) DECIDE the separation (Tier-3, operator-gated): route the two legs to accounts that do not net against each other, arm hedge mode for the pair (BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS exists and is deliberately EMPTY - the plumbing is not the switch, and switching a venue's position mode is itself Tier-3), or accept one live BTCUSDT leg per netting account as policy. Closing this by demoting either leg does NOT satisfy it: that removes the collision from one account and leaves it standing on the other two, and leaves the attribution question unanswered for whichever leg remains.
items.notes: Operator-directed 2026-08-26 ('separate it from trend_donchian'), filed as a separate tracked item at the operator's explicit instruction. The operator subsequently directed that NO demotion happen before a full investigation - 'it could be that it just needs better entry gates' - so this row is an input to that investigation, not a consequence of a demotion. No config change was made.

updates.note: MEASURED (resolution criterion 1, the Tier-1 half) — and it REFUTES the reading this row was opened with. Population: bybit_2 / BTCUSDT, closed non-backtest rows whose open AND close timestamps both parse, n=55 (ict_scalp_5m 32, trend_donchian 15, htf_pullback_trend_2h 8), spanning 2026-05-25..2026-08-26. A trade is SHARED if any other-strategy BTCUSDT position on the same account was open at any point in its life, EXCLUSIVE otherwise. Result: 17/55 = 30.9% shared, so 69.1% of real-money BTCUSDT trades are attributable after all. ict_scalp_5m EXCLUSIVE is n=25 / +$1.43 / 14 wins — flat, and that is a clean measurement on trades no sibling could have moved. Its SHARED subset is n=7 / -$0.54. So the collision is REAL and worth fixing (it is why 48 of 81 closes are reconciler-driven rather than bracket-driven) but it is NOT what produces the scalp's results, and the claim in this row's detail that the exclusive-vs-shared split is 'UNMEASURED' is now discharged rather than merely restated. THE ACTUAL STRUCTURAL PROBLEM IS COST, NOT ATTRIBUTION: the Bybit round trip is 0.11% of notional (confirmed against an operator venue screenshot — 711.34 volume, 0.38886+0.39124 = 0.78010, and gross-fees+funding reproduces Bybit's Closed P&L to the cent), while the scalp's declared stop distance has shrunk from a 0.587% median to 0.393% across the two halves of its real-money history. Fee as a fraction of one R: median 0.20 -> 0.32; 6 of the last 16 exceed 0.50R and one (#4076, R=0.068% of price) reached 1.62R, where a FULL 1.5R winner still loses money. CAVEATS: n is small on every cut; overlap is computed from journal timestamps, and a reconciler-closed row's closed_at can lag the venue, which would OVERSTATE overlap; exclusive-vs-shared is not randomly assigned, so the two buckets' PnL is not a controlled comparison; and fee/R uses the DECLARED stop, which most exits never reach (only 14 of 81 closes are bracket exits).

THE MINIMUM-R ENTRY GATE IS REFUTED. Recording it because the proposal was already described to the operator as the likely remedy, and a refuted proposal that is not written down comes back. DERIVATION (exact, not a fit): cost_R = fee_rt * entry / |entry-stop|, so QTY CANCELS and the round-trip cost in R is a function of the stop distance as a fraction of price alone — verified against all 32 real-money rows, max |measured-predicted| = 2.2e-16. With a 1.5R target and 1R stop, expectancy = 2.5p - 1 - c, so at the measured p (0.56 exclusive / 0.607 all-priced) the max tolerable cost is 0.40-0.52R, implying a floor of R >= 0.213-0.275% of price. THEN THE FALSIFYING CHECK: win rate by stop-distance bucket, population ict_scalp_5m / bybit_2 / closed / pnl NOT NULL, n=28. R < 0.220% (cost > 0.50R): n=6, SIX WINS OF SIX, +$22.52. 0.220-0.314%: n=2, 50%, -$1.53. 0.314-0.440%: n=5, 60%, -$3.92. R >= 0.440% (the CHEAPEST trades): n=15, 46.7%, -$16.18. The tightest-stop cohort is the ONLY profitable one and carries the entire account's positive result; win rate falls monotonically as the stop widens. Every gate makes the book worse in-sample: no gate +$0.88, ceiling 0.50R -$21.64, 0.35R -$20.11, 0.25R -$16.18. WHY THE ARITHMETIC MISLED: the breakeven model assumes the payoff is 1.5R win / 1R loss, and the strategy does not close that way — only 14 of 81 closes are bracket exits, 48 are reconciler_filled. The cost calculation is correct; the PAYOFF MODEL it was applied to is not, so a cost-vs-target ratio does not predict this strategy's outcomes. This makes the exit-path problem the primary one rather than a side finding: until the realized payoff matches the declared geometry, ANY gate reasoned from declared geometry is reasoning about a distribution the strategy does not produce. CAVEAT: n=6 with a 100% win rate is far too small to assert those setups are durably good — it is sufficient to refute a gate that would delete them, and nothing more.

HIGH and RE-CONFIRMED STRUCTURALLY: /api/diag/bybit_open_orders reports position_idx 0 on bybit_2, i.e. one-way NETTING confirmed on the real-money account, and ict_scalp_5m traded 14 real-money BTCUSDT closes in 30d. Two strategies sharing one netted position is the same root as the pairs stranding (BL-20260821) and the netting attribution family (BL-20260801).

items.title: The venue's Bybit position mode cannot be read for a symbol that holds no position, which is exactly the state a hedge-mode switch is performed in
items.detail: Arming BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS for a symbol is the sanctioned fix for the netted BTCUSDT strategy collision, and it is Tier-3: it flips a live-order setting. Doing it safely requires reading the venue's CURRENT position mode before the flip and verifying the mode after it. Neither was possible. MEASURED 2026-08-26: `positionIdx` (0 = one-way netting, 1 = hedge-long, 2 = hedge-short) is returned by Bybit on every position row and was DROPPED at extraction in `clients.py::account_bybit_open_orders`, so the only surface that reads Bybit position state published no mode at all - and `/api/diag/bybit_open_orders` duly returned `position_idx: None` for both live bybit_2 positions, which a reader could easily mistake for 'one-way' when it meant 'we did not look'. The claim that bybit_2 is one-way netting was, until this row, sourced from PROSE in CLAUDE.md and never from the venue. THE EXTRACTION IS NOW FIXED and the mode ships on every position row - but that closes only the readable half. BOTH read paths skip `size <= 0`, so a FLAT symbol produces no row at all, and the symbol whose mode actually gates the decision - BTCUSDT, which bybit_2 is flat on - therefore remains unreadable. The gap is structural, not an oversight in the fix: position-list rows describe positions, and the question is about a symbol that has none. Bybit's position mode is per-symbol, so a mode read off XRPUSDT or ETHUSDT is evidence about THOSE symbols and does not transfer to BTCUSDT.
evidence: /api/diag/bybit_open_orders?account_id=bybit_2 (2026-08-26) - read_state=orders_read, 2 positions (XRPUSDT 21.3 Buy, ETHUSDT 0.03 Buy), both with position_idx absent from the payload entirely before the fix

clients.py::account_bybit_open_orders - the position-row extraction listed symbol/side/size/avgPrice/stopLoss/takeProfit/tpSlMode and no positionIdx; two duplicate extraction sites (settleCoin page + per-symbol cross-check) have since been factored onto one _bybit_position_row builder so they cannot drift
Both extraction sites gate on `size <= 0: continue`, so a flat symbol yields no row - verified by reading the code, not inferred
bybit_2 is FLAT on BTCUSDT at the venue (same read), which is what makes this block the decision rather than being academic

src/runtime/bybit_position_mode.py - the resolver exists and apply_position_idx is called from 4 sites in execute.py plus order_monitor.py, so the plumbing is complete and no-ops only because the allowlist is empty; what is missing is the READ, not the write
items.resolution_criteria: A session can determine the position mode for a NAMED SYMBOL on a Bybit account regardless of whether that symbol currently holds a position, and can verify the mode after a switch. The likely shape is a symbol-scoped position-mode read (Bybit returns positionIdx on a zero-size row for an explicitly queried symbol) surfaced on /api/diag/bybit_open_orders beside the existing rows, with the same three-state discipline the rest of that route uses: a mode we could not read must be distinguishable from one-way, never defaulted to it. Reading the mode off a DIFFERENT symbol that happens to hold a position does NOT satisfy this - Bybit's position mode is per-symbol. Until this is closed, arming BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS for BTCUSDT would be a Tier-3 live-order change made blind, and should not be proposed as ready.
items.notes: Found while working the netting collision (BL-20260826-BTC-SCALP-AND-DONCHIAN-SHARE-ONE-NETTED-BTCUSDT-POSITION) at the operator's direction to fix it. This is the concrete blocker on the preferred remedy. The partial fix (surfacing positionIdx on rows that exist) shipped in the same change with tests.

updates.note: RE-CONFIRMED BY CONSTRUCTION IN TODAY'S READ: bybit_2 returned position_idx for its two HELD symbols (XRPUSDT, ETHUSDT) and nothing for any flat symbol — which is exactly the state a hedge-mode switch would need to inspect. This directly gates the BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS decision the pairs sleeve needs.

items.resolution: CRITERION MET, demonstrated six times on live FLAT symbols 2026-08-30. The stated criterion is 'a session can determine the position mode for a NAMED SYMBOL regardless of whether it holds a position, and can verify the mode after a switch'. `switch-bybit-position-mode` does exactly that: it reads `positionIdx` from get_position_info, where one-way returns a single row at idx 0 and hedge returns two at 1/2 — so the SET of indices IS the mode and it stays readable while flat. Evidence: issues 10514/10525/10527/10528 each reported `before: {mode: one_way, position_idxs: [0], flat: true}` then `after: {mode: hedge, position_idxs: [1,2]}` with switch_verified true, on four flat bybit_portfolio symbols; issues 10518/10519 reported `before: {mode: hedge, ...}` + `action: noop_already_in_mode` on two flat bybit_1 symbols. ⚠️ SCOPE CORRECTION the row needs: the title says the mode 'cannot be read for a symbol that holds no position', which is TOO BROAD. It is true of /api/diag/bybit_open_orders (both read paths skip size<=0) and FALSE of the switch action. The residual limitation is that the read arrives via a Tier-2 action rather than a Tier-1 diag route — mitigated because that action defaults to REPORT-ONLY, so the mode can be read without switching anything. Surfacing it on the diag route (the row's suggested shape) remains a nice-to-have, not the criterion.

items.title: exit_reason says reconciler_filled on trades whose exit price sits exactly on the declared SL or TP, so every analysis keyed on the label misattributes fired brackets to the janitor path
items.detail: UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT, sub-class A (the label does not describe what the code observed). `exit_reason` is read across this repo as the exit MECHANISM, and a `reconciler_filled` row is read as 'the strategy did not close this; the janitor noticed it flat'. MEASURED against the PRICE rather than the label — population ict_scalp_5m / bybit_2 / closed / exit_price + stop_loss + take_profit_1 all present, n=28: 11 of 15 `reconciler_filled` rows exited WITHIN 0.05% OF PRICE of a declared bracket level (4 at the stop, 7 at the target), and 22 of 28 rows overall did. The bracket fired; only the attribution went to the reconciler. STABLE ACROSS TOLERANCE, so it is not an artifact of one cutoff: 0.02% -> 20/28, 0.05% -> 22/28, 0.15% -> 24/28, 0.25% -> 26/28, 0.50% -> 28/28, with reconciler rows on a level running 11/15 -> 15/15 over the same sweep. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS STRATEGY: `/api/bot/performance` publishes `perExitPath`, whose whole purpose is to cut coverage BY EXIT PATH and surface structurally unmeasured paths, and CLAUDE.md records six paths at 0.0 coverage read off exactly this field. If a fired bracket is filed under `reconciler_filled`, then the bracket path is under-counted and the reconciler path is inflated with trades it did not decide — in BOTH the numerator and the denominator. The same field also drives the structural-health reading that '64.7% of closes come from cleanup machinery', which is a claim about mechanism sourced from a label this measurement shows can be wrong for the majority of the rows it is applied to. THE MECHANISM IS LARGELY HEALTHY; THE RECORD OF IT IS NOT. That is the opposite of the conclusion a label-only read produces, and it is the direction that matters: it would send a session to fix an exit path that is working.
evidence: Per-row table, ict_scalp_5m/bybit_2, n=28: reconciler_filled AT SL 4, AT TP 7, neither 4; sl AT SL 5; tp AT TP 5; backfill AT TP 1; netting_attributed neither 2

Worked examples: trade 4180 reconciler_filled exit 64100.0 vs declared SL 64110.3 (0.02%); trade 5000 reconciler_filled exit 79493.2 vs declared TP 79505.7 (0.02%); trade 2428 reconciler_filled exit 62647.3 vs declared TP 62658.6 (0.02%)
Tolerance sweep 0.02/0.05/0.10/0.15/0.25/0.50% -> 20/22/22/24/26/28 of 28 overall; the direction of the finding does not depend on the cutoff
Only 6 of 28 rows (4 reconciler_filled + 2 netting_attributed) land near NEITHER declared level at 0.05%, and those are the genuine non-bracket exits
items.resolution_criteria: A consumer can distinguish 'the declared bracket fired and the reconciler was merely the component that noticed' from 'something other than the declared exit closed this trade'. The likely shape is a separate field recording WHICH mechanism the close is attributable to, kept distinct from WHICH component wrote the row, with the usual discipline that 'we could not determine it' is its own state and is never folded into either answer. Comparing exit price to the declared level is the available evidence and is EVIDENCE, NOT PROOF — a trade can close at a level coincidentally, and under one-way netting a sibling's exit can flatten a position at a price that happens to sit near this row's stop. Any fix must not overclaim on that basis. Re-deriving perExitPath's coverage figures on the corrected attribution is part of closing this, since those figures are currently computed over mislabelled buckets.
items.notes: Found while investigating why 48 of 81 ict_scalp_5m closes are reconciler-driven. I had reported to the operator that '83% of this strategy's exits are not the exits it declared', inferred from the exit_reason LABEL; checking the PRICE refutes it — ~79% DO land on a declared level. The error is itself the class this row files: reading a label as though it were the measurement. Related: BL-20260826-BTC-SCALP-AND-DONCHIAN-SHARE-ONE-NETTED-BTCUSDT-POSITION.

updates.note: ⚠️ THIS ROW IS A DUPLICATE AND I FILED IT AS A DISCOVERY. Found while building the 2026-08-26 work plan, by reading the backlog I was about to write a gate item against. The defect was already measured on 2026-08-22, its MECHANISM was already named, and one half was already FIXED: (a) BL-20260822-EXIT-ATTRIBUTION-UNDER-REPORTS-BRACKET-HITS [open] - 'on broker-truth exit prices the declared bracket is reached ~3x more often than the exit_reason records'; (b) BL-20260822-EXIT-REASON-FROZEN-WHEN-PRICE-ARRIVES-LATE [kept_open] - the CAUSE: `_sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit` fills exit_price after the close and never re-runs `_classify_broker_exit`, measured at 91 of 155 broker-truth rows, with 181/181 mislabelled rows carrying no `exit_reason_source` as a 100%% signature; (c) BL-20260823-EXIT-LABEL-FROZEN-ON-THE-ANCHORED-PRICE-PATH [resolved] - the anchored-price sibling, already repaired. And `exit_reason_source` EXISTS and is stamped in order_monitor.py at six sites. WHAT THIS ROW LEGITIMATELY ADDS is a second, independent measurement on a DIFFERENT population - ict_scalp_5m/bybit_2, n=28, comparing exit_price against the DECLARED levels rather than against broker-truth availability, giving 22/28 (78.6%%) on a declared level and 11/15 of the reconciler_filled rows, stable over a 0.02-0.50%% tolerance sweep. That corroborates (a) on a population it did not cover. It is corroboration, not discovery, and the row is re-statused `superseded` accordingly so the backlog does not carry two rows for one defect. THE LESSON IS THIS ROW'S OWN CLASS: I read the journal and the code but not the BACKLOG before concluding the finding was new - the same 'check the primary source' failure, with the backlog as the source. Work the remaining fix under (b), which is kept_open and carries the named mechanism.

Re-validated. Status is `superseded` — carried here for completeness of the triage rather than re-opened. Its live successor is BL-20260822-EXIT-ATTRIBUTION-UNDER-REPORTS-BRACKET-HITS, which is the row that qualifies this review's 8.3% declared-bracket figure as a LOWER BOUND.

items.title: One session produced four wrong conclusions about a live real-money strategy, every one from reading a stored value as though it were the thing it names while its primary source sat available and unconsulted
items.detail: FILED AS A CLASS, NOT AN INSTANCE. Each member below was corrected individually during the 2026-08-26 BTC-scalp investigation; disposing of them one at a time would miss that they are ONE defect with four faces, which is what the backlog_classes pass exists to catch. The shape: a stored field is read as the QUANTITY IT IS NAMED AFTER, a conclusion is drawn, and the primary source that would have settled it was available the whole time and never queried. MEMBERS: (1) `trades.pnl` on bybit_2 read as the account's money -> reported the strategy 'flat, +$0.88, no problem' to the operator; CLAUDE.md documents THAT ACCOUNT as under-recording (wallet-truth -$262.52 vs journal ~-$33) and the operator had to say 'there is definitely a real money problem'. Unconsulted primary source: the account BALANCE ($296.59) and /api/bot/pnl/exchange. (2) bybit_portfolio's -$2,955.74 quoted as 'what the strategy costs unsized-down'; it is the same signals at ~330x the size, and the single worst row in it is the matched pair CLAUDE.md already cites as its canonical fabrication proof. Unconsulted: `position_size`, in the same rows. (3) `exit_reason` read as the exit MECHANISM -> 'the strategy does not close its own trades, 83% of exits are not the declared exits'; 22 of 28 exits land within 0.05% of a declared bracket level. Unconsulted: `exit_price`, in the same rows. (4) 'bybit_2 is one-way netting' asserted from CLAUDE.md PROSE; the venue's `positionIdx` was returned on every position row and dropped at extraction. THE COMMON REMEDY IS CHECKABLE, NOT AN EXHORTATION: in all four the primary source was one field or one endpoint away, and in three of them it was IN THE ROW ALREADY BEING READ. 'Verify before asserting' is already canonical and did not prevent any of these, because the reads FELT like verification - a journal query IS a measurement, of the journal. WHY SEVERITY HIGH DESPITE NO CODE DEFECT: the outputs were a demotion of a live real-money strategy (drafted, reverted only because the operator intervened) and a Tier-3 entry-gate proposal that would have deleted the only profitable cohort (6 of 6 wins, +$22.52). Both were about to be recommended on this reasoning.
evidence: Member 1: reported +$0.88 / 60.7% win over 28 priced bybit_2 rows; operator replied 'There is definitely a real money problem, and the fact that you're not seeing it is also a problem' and supplied venue screenshots
Member 2: matched mirror pairs #4180 (-$4.00, 0.0070 BTC) vs #4181 (-$2,589.78, 2.3420 BTC) - 335x - and CLAUDE.md cites that exact pair as the _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced fabrication proof
Member 3: reconciler_filled rows AT SL 4 / AT TP 7 / neither 4 at a 0.05%-of-price tolerance, stable over a 0.02-0.50% sweep (20/22/22/24/26/28 of 28)
Member 4: /api/diag/bybit_open_orders returned position_idx: None for both live bybit_2 positions because the field was never extracted, not because the venue withheld it

Denominator, so this is a rate and not a list of anecdotes: FOUR of the four substantive conclusions this session reached about the strategy were overturned by a subsequent measurement; none was caught by review, all by re-measurement
items.resolution_criteria: A quantitative claim about money names the SOURCE it was measured from, and a claim sourced from the journal for an account with a known broker-truth discrepancy is either cross-checked against that broker truth or is stated as a journal figure rather than as the account's result. The concrete, testable half: `comms/broker_truth_ledger.json` already records which accounts under-record, and nothing warns a reader who queries those accounts' journal rows - so surfacing that discrepancy ON the per-account read path (a flag on /api/bot/trades/closed or the Data Explorer when the account has a broker-truth record) would have caught member 1 mechanically. Members 2-4 share the narrower rule that a field SITTING IN THE ROW BEING READ (position_size, exit_price) outranks a label in the same row; that one is a review-discipline item and should be written where it will actually be read rather than added as a fifth bullet to a rule that already exists. NOT resolved by restating 'always verify' - that rule was in force and binding for all four.
items.notes: Self-filed. Related rows: BL-20260826-EXIT-REASON-LABELS-A-FIRED-BRACKET-AS-A-RECONCILER-CLOSE, BL-20260826-BYBIT-POSITION-MODE-UNREADABLE-FOR-A-FLAT-SYMBOL, BL-20260826-BTC-SCALP-AND-DONCHIAN-SHARE-ONE-NETTED-BTCUSDT-POSITION. The operator's standing instruction that prompted the investigation - full understanding before demoting anything - is what stopped member 1 from shipping as a config change.

updates.note: ⚠️ THE MOST USEFUL ROW IN THE BACKLOG FOR A REVIEW SESSION, and I want to record that it applied to me. I made THREE wrong readings today and caught each by re-checking: (1) 'every since= returns 0 rows' — actually an HTTP 422 from limit=500 over MAX_LIMIT=200 that my parser rendered as zero; (2) 'the VM clock has drifted 5.1 s' — measured twice at -0.04 s and -0.02 s, so the Bybit 10002 gap is latency or venue-side; (3) 'IB market data is out fleet-wide' — 2026-08-29 is a Saturday and venue_session grades MES `closed`. Same class every time: a stored or returned value read as the measurement.

items.title: Partial-mode leg-id capture is a before/after snapshot diff, so it abstains exactly when several strategies trade one symbol - which is the condition that makes leg accumulation matter
items.detail: BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=partial gives each journal trade its own qty-scoped SL/TP legs, and `trades.sl_order_id` is what lets `modify_open_order` AMEND that specific leg in place instead of ADDING another. A NULL id falls back to the legacy add-a-leg `set_trading_stop`, and added legs accumulate toward Bybit's 20-COMBINED-leg-per-symbol cap, at which a genuine protective tightening is refused (110061) and fails SILENTLY. So leg-id coverage is the whole health of the partial mechanism. THE CAPTURE CANNOT COVER THE HARD CASE BY CONSTRUCTION. `_classify_new_partial_tpsl_legs` reads the resting StopOrder set before and after the entry and takes the difference; its own docstring states it returns None 'unless EXACTLY one new leg of that type appeared - an ambiguous diff (0 ... or >1, e.g. a concurrent same-symbol entry racing this one) leaves that slot None rather than guessing'. Refusing to guess a leg id on a LIVE stop is the right call and must not be softened. The defect is the METHOD: a diff is inherently racy, so it abstains most often on a busy account trading one symbol from several strategies - precisely the account where legs accumulate fastest and the cap is reachable. The mechanism degrades where it is load-bearing and is reliable where it is not needed. MEASURED 2026-08-26 (newest 500 rows per account, non-backtest, opened on/after the 2026-07-21 fix, restricted to rows that actually FILLED): bybit_2 - which routes 6 strategies - is 38/41 = 92.7% tracked. bybit_1 - which routes 26 - is 272/333 = 81.7%, leaving 61 untracked rows, and 39 of those 61 (64%) are the PAIRS SLEEVE (pairs_sol_eth_b 14, pairs_bnb_btc_b 11, pairs_sol_eth_a 10, pairs_bnb_btc_a 4). That fits the mechanism: a pairs open places two legs at once and the sleeve shares its symbols with directional strategies on the same account, so a racing same-symbol entry is the normal case rather than the exception. ETHUSDT is the top untracked symbol (19), and ETHUSDT on bybit_1 is where 20 accumulated legs and a 167% over-cover were measured.
evidence: src/units/accounts/execute.py::_classify_new_partial_tpsl_legs - the docstring names the >1-new-leg race as an abstain condition; the capture is a get_open_orders(orderFilter='StopOrder') read diffed against a pre-entry id set
bybit_2 filled rows since 2026-07-21: 38/41 tracked (92.7%) - 6 strategies routed
bybit_1 filled rows since 2026-07-21: 272/333 tracked (81.7%), 61 untracked - 26 strategies routed
untracked-by-strategy on bybit_1: pairs_* = 39 of 61 (64%); untracked-by-symbol: ETHUSDT 19, SOLUSDT 14, BTCUSDT 13
`orderLinkId` / `order_link_id` appears ZERO times across src/ - the bot never assigns a client-side order id on any Bybit call, so the diff is currently the only identification method available
items.resolution_criteria: A partial-mode leg is identified by CONTENT (its triggerPrice and qty, both of which this entry set and therefore knows) rather than by being the only new leg in a time window, so a concurrent same-symbol entry no longer forces an abstain. Closing this means leg-id coverage on the BUSIEST account (bybit_1, 26 strategies, measured 272/333 = 81.7%) reaching parity with the quietest (bybit_2, 6 strategies, 38/41 = 92.7%), measured the same way — filled rows since the change, per account — rather than an aggregate the quiet account carries. ⚠️ The abstain-rather-than-guess behaviour MUST survive: if two candidate legs match on both attributes, still return None. Mis-attributing a leg id amends a LIVE stop on the wrong trade, which is worse than the accumulation this closes. Tier-2 (live order path); stage on bybit_1, which is both the demo account and the one with the problem. NOT closable by assigning an orderLinkId — see the 2026-08-26T09:40 update for why that is infeasible for legs Bybit creates as a side effect of the entry.
items.notes: Operator-directed 2026-08-26: 'we still need to get the partial mechanism working correctly'. The mechanism is CORRECT where it engages - the live bybit_2 ETHUSDT position holds one netted 0.03 Buy carrying two independent qty-scoped bracket pairs (0.01 + 0.02), which is partial mode doing exactly its job. This row is about the 18.3% of busy-account rows where it silently does not engage.

updates.note: ⚠️ THE FIX THIS ROW PROPOSED IS INFEASIBLE — corrected before any code was written. The resolution criteria said to assign Bybit a client-side `orderLinkId` at placement so a leg is self-identifying. THAT CANNOT APPLY TO THESE LEGS: under partial mode we never place them. `execute.py` sets `stopLoss`/`takeProfit`/`tpslMode=Partial`/`slSize`/`tpSize` ON THE ENTRY ORDER and Bybit creates the legs as a SIDE EFFECT — the code's own comment says 'the place-order response never returns their orderId', which is the entire reason the snapshot diff exists. An `orderLinkId` on the entry would identify the ENTRY, and Bybit documents no parameter that propagates a link id to the auto-created legs. Placing the legs ourselves as separate conditional orders WOULD make them linkable, but that is a much larger order-path change and it forfeits Bybit's atomic attach-at-entry, opening a window in which the position is live and NAKED — strictly worse than the accumulation it would fix. THE FEASIBLE FIX IS IDENTIFICATION BY CONTENT INSTEAD OF BY NOVELTY. We already know, at placement, exactly what the leg will look like: `stopLoss` and `takeProfit` are quantized to the tick by `quantize_price` and `slSize`/`tpSize` are set to the order's own `qty_str`. The resting leg rows carry `triggerPrice` and `qty`. So when the diff returns more than one new leg of a type, it can be disambiguated by matching triggerPrice AND qty against what THIS entry asked for, instead of abstaining because a concurrent entry also appeared. Two entries would have to collide on BOTH price and size to remain ambiguous, which is far rarer than 'any concurrent same-symbol entry'. ⚠️ THE ABSTAIN MUST SURVIVE: if two candidate legs still match on both attributes, return None exactly as today — mis-attributing a leg id amends a LIVE stop on the wrong trade, which is worse than the accumulation this closes. That invariant is the reason to change the DISAMBIGUATION rule and not the abstain rule.

HIGH. Re-validated: a before/after snapshot diff abstains exactly when several strategies trade one symbol concurrently — which is the normal state on netted Bybit accounts (see BL-20260826-BTC-SCALP-AND-DONCHIAN-SHARE-ONE-NETTED-BTCUSDT-POSITION). The mechanism fails under the conditions it exists for.

items.title: Measured: not one signal available at decision time discriminates winners from losers, so every attempt to replace FLIP_POLICY=hold with a smarter arbiter has lost and will keep losing
items.detail: Operator, 2026-08-26: 'flip policy = hold is bullshit - there's no way with all the infra we've built out, that's the best we can do for trade prioritization. We have confidence scoring, geometry, mls - we need to do better than this.' The premise is right and the infrastructure exists; the INPUTS do not. MEASURED — population: closed non-backtest trades joined to their order package, entry+sl+tp present, pnl NOT NULL, n=798 (711 paper / 87 real money), 40.4% wins, split into earlier/later halves by package created_at. AUC against win/loss, where 0.500 is a coin flip: strategy CONFIDENCE 0.496 all / 0.473 earlier / 0.508 later. MAX shadow-model score 0.425 / 0.417 / 0.398 (n=300). MEAN shadow-model score 0.523 / 0.580 / 0.411. Stop distance as %% of price 0.501 / 0.569 / 0.445. Declared reward:risk 0.526 / 0.440 / 0.630. NOTHING CLEARS 0.53 OVERALL AND NOTHING HOLDS ITS SIGN ACROSS THE TWO HALVES — rr swings 0.440 -> 0.630 and ml_mean 0.580 -> 0.411, which is the signature of noise, not of a weak-but-real edge. THIS RETRODICTS BOTH PRIOR FAILURES rather than merely being consistent with them: FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD was exactly 'let a higher-confidence opposing signal override the hold' and lost net-negative across both walk-forward folds (2026-08-11, BL-20260811-FLIP-OVERRIDE-NEVER-WALKFORWARDED); the M18 allocator's EV ranker measured OOS AUC ~= 0.51 and its selection did not beat dumb priority, parking P2/P3 'pending a proven P_win input' (2026-06-30 findings). Confidence at 0.496 over n=798 IS that parked input, measured, and it is not there. A third arbiter built on these same features is predicted to lose for the same reason. FLIP_POLICY=hold is not winning because it is clever - it is winning because it declines to act on a signal nobody has shown carries information.
evidence: confidence AUC 0.496 over n=798 - the single most-quoted decision input in the system, at coin flip

ml_max AUC 0.425 / 0.417 / 0.398 is the ONLY directionally stable column and it points the WRONG way; before reading it as a tradable inverse signal note the documented semantic trap - `score` is max(proba) for a multiclass head and EVERY regime head is multiclass, so ml_max is 'confidence in any class', not P(win) (BL-20260730-PARITY-PROBE-MISLABELS-MAXPROBA)
Real money alone (n=87): confidence 0.545, ml_mean 0.591 - directionally nicer but n=87 against the same features reading flat over n=798, so this is not evidence of an edge the larger sample missed
The two prior attempts and their measured verdicts: FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD net-negative vs plain hold across both folds; M18 allocator ranker OOS AUC ~= 0.51, sizing-normalized edge -$7
items.resolution_criteria: A signal available AT DECISION TIME is shown to discriminate trade outcome out-of-sample - concretely, AUC materially above 0.5 on a holdout, with the SIGN STABLE across time splits, at an n that supports the claim. Only then does replacing hold with a ranked arbiter have an input to rank on, and only then should the parked M18 P2/P3 be revisited. THE LIKELY SHAPE OF THE REAL WORK IS TRAINING, NOT ROUTING: every shadow head in the registry is trained on REGIME, and no head anywhere targets 'will THIS trade win'. The features to try exist and are already persisted - order_packages.confidence / model_scores / signal_logic / meta, the trade's own geometry, and account_context_snapshots (per-signal pre-decision equity, daily PnL, drawdown, open-trade count, keyed by (order_package_id, account_id)). ⚠️ THIS ROW MEASURES SINGLE FEATURES ONLY. It does not rule out a multivariate interaction that no single column shows, and that possibility is exactly what a trained head would test - so read this as 'the obvious inputs are individually dead', not as 'nothing is learnable here'. Closing this by asserting the negative would be over-reading it.
items.notes: Filed in direct answer to an operator directive to do better than hold. The honest answer is that the mechanism to do better already exists (allocator, EV scorer, soak) and has twice been built and twice lost; what is missing is a predictive input, which is a trainer problem. Related: BL-20260826-BTC-SCALP-AND-DONCHIAN-SHARE-ONE-NETTED-BTCUSDT-POSITION.

updates.note: ⚠️ THIS ROW'S HEADLINE IS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE — the title now overstates the finding and should be read against this update, not on its own. The AUCs above were computed over labels that are only 25.6% MEASURED. Provenance of the pnl that DEFINES 'win', same population, n=804: ESTIMATED 251 (31.2%), MEASURED 206 (25.6%), FABRICATED 167 (20.8%), UNVERIFIED-no-stamp 152 (18.9%), netted_duplicate_unattributed 27. AND THE LABEL ITSELF MOVES WITH ITS PROVENANCE: win rate is 48.2% on ESTIMATED rows against 39.3% on MEASURED ones — a 9-point spread, so 'win' is partly a function of how we reconstructed the exit rather than of what the market did. Training or EVALUATING against that mixture teaches/measures our own reconstruction. RE-RUN ON MEASURED-PROVENANCE LABELS ONLY (exit_price_source in exchange_fill / bybit_closed_pnl / ib_execution / bybit_closed_pnl_backfill), n=200, 75 positives, 37.5% wins: CONFIDENCE AUC 0.587 overall, 0.635 earlier half, 0.577 later half — ABOVE 0.5 IN ALL THREE CUTS WITH A STABLE SIGN, against 0.496 on the full label set. The label noise was masking it. Everything else stays unconvincing: rr 0.423 (and it INVERTED from 0.526), R_pct 0.543 but swinging 0.619 -> 0.321, ml_mean 0.495, ml_max 0.424 overall while its two halves read 0.565/0.604 — an incoherence that is itself a reason not to trust that column. SO THE CORRECTED CLAIM IS NARROW AND SPECIFIC: strategy confidence appears to carry real signal (AUC ~0.59) and is invisible unless the evaluation is restricted to broker-confirmed exits; the OTHER inputs remain unsupported. THE CONSEQUENCE IS BIGGER THAN THIS ROW. Both prior attempts that 'proved' prioritization does not work — the FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD walk-forward and the M18 allocator's OOS AUC ~= 0.51 — were verdicts about confidence, and IF either was scored against journal pnl without a provenance restriction, its verdict was measured against the same corrupted labels and is not safe to rely on. I have NOT established which labels those studies used; that is the first thing to check and it is cheap. CAVEATS, because this update must not be over-read the way the original was: n=200 with 75 positives is small, the three cuts are views of ONE dataset rather than a train/test holdout, and a single feature at 0.59 is a lead, not a deployable edge.

⚠️ THE PREVIOUS UPDATE'S BIGGEST CLAIM IS REFUTED — I checked the two prior studies instead of continuing to speculate about them, and NEITHER uses journal pnl, so neither verdict is affected by label provenance. The flip-override walk-forward (docs/research/flip-override-walkforward-2026-08-11.md) is a BACKTEST: BTCUSDT 5m Binance-vision, 2020-06-01 -> 2026-02-28, 604,512 rows, synthetic $10k account at 0.3%/trade, two folds, 34 overrides fired. Its PnL is simulated from candles. The M18 allocator study (docs/research/M18-allocator-backtest-findings-2026-06-29.md) likewise 'simulate[s] every actionable candidate standalone (single-position-per-symbol, no lookahead, fixed notional -> balance-free net-R)' over BTC+ETH+SOL 5m 2022-01->2026-05, 1,545 candidates, expanding walk-forward n_eval=1,236. Both are immune to the corruption I attributed to them. AND THEIR NUMBER IS BETTER THAN MINE. The allocator study measures `confidence` at OOS AUC 0.522 on n_eval=1,236 in an EXPANDING WALK-FORWARD (0.534 on its n=136 first pass). My 0.587 came from n=200 across three views of ONE dataset with no holdout. Those do not conflict: a small in-sample estimate sitting above a large properly-out-of-sample one is what sampling noise looks like, and the larger, OOS, pre-registered-gate measurement is the one to believe. Their gate was 0.55 and 0.522 is below it. SO THE ORIGINAL VERDICT STANDS ON ITS OWN EVIDENCE: confidence carries a small real signal, not enough to rank on. What my provenance work legitimately establishes is narrower and still worth keeping — the LABELS IN THE JOURNAL are only 25.6% measured and their win rate moves 9 points with provenance, so any FUTURE study scored on journal pnl (rather than on simulated candles) must restrict to measured provenance or it will be measuring our own reconstruction. That is a constraint on future work, not a retraction of past work. THE REAL LEAD WAS ALREADY IN THE ALLOCATOR DOC AND IS NOT CONFIDENCE AT ALL: its scorer probe found the strongest single features are ones the scorer does not use — short-horizon MEAN REVERSION (ret_1h / ret_4h corr ~ -0.10: candidates entering after a recent up-move do worse) and TIME OF DAY (hour_utc corr -0.13) — and states that 'a ranker that faded recent momentum + avoided bad hours could plausibly beat priority - the first concrete lead'. That lead is market context, is documented, and is unexplored.

⚠️ THE 'REAL LEAD' IN THE PREVIOUS UPDATE IS ALSO DEAD, and the same document already said so one section further down. I quoted the allocator doc's 'first concrete lead' (fade recent momentum, avoid bad hours) as documented-and-unexplored. It was explored. `allocator_ranker_eval.py:10` defines the market-features-only variant as exactly 'ret_1h/4h/12h, rr, stop/tp dist, vol, hour, dow' — so the 0.5114 OOS AUC at n_eval=1,236 IS that lead, measured. And the doc's own n=136 -> n=1559 table shows it evaporating: ret_1h 0.459 -> 0.487 with corr -0.104 -> +0.031 (THE SIGN FLIPPED), hour_utc 0.443 -> 0.508, ret_4h 0.451 -> 0.475, rr 0.559 -> 0.469, ev_r 0.539 -> 0.484 (below chance). The doc had ALSO pre-flagged it: 'n=136 is too small - a corr of 0.10 at n=136 has a 95%% CI ~= +/-0.17 ... fitting a model on 136 noisy rows would' overfit. I read a lead sentence out of a section the same document retracts two pages later. CLOSING THIS ROW AS RESOLVED WITH THE OPPOSITE HEADLINE TO THE ONE IT WAS FILED UNDER, and the conclusion is now properly evidenced rather than asserted: EVERY candidate selection input has been measured out-of-sample at n_eval~1,236 on an expanding walk-forward and all sit 0.47-0.53 against a pre-registered 0.55 gate — confidence 0.522/0.524, ev_r 0.484, rr 0.469, ret_1h 0.487, ret_4h 0.475, hour_utc 0.508, +regime 0.5110, +cell 0.5077, +regime+cell 0.5140. The only variant that reaches 0.52 needs OWNER IDENTITY, which is a Tier-3 strategy call and not ranking. So FLIP_POLICY=hold is not a placeholder anyone failed to improve on — per-trade SELECTION on this candidate set is not learnable from any input tried, and that is a measured result at real n, not an absence of effort. WHERE THE DOC POINTS INSTEAD, and it agrees with this session's independent findings: 'per-trade timing/selection outcome is [at the wall]' and the live direction is EXIT MANAGEMENT (exit-management-ml-experiment-DESIGN.md §8). That is the same place today's exit-path work landed. The provenance constraint from the 08:55 update SURVIVES as the one durable output of this row and is why the successor row exists: journal labels are 25.6%% measured with a 9-point win-rate spread by provenance, so any future study scored on journal pnl (as opposed to simulated candles) must restrict to measured provenance.

items.tier: 1 — reporting only. `IBClient.cancel` has exactly ONE consumer (scripts/ops/cancel_ib_order.py); the runtime cancel paths branch on `verify_state` + `still_resting` from the venue re-read, never on `refusal`, so no order-path behaviour changes — the same call is sent, only the envelope classification is corrected.
items.title: cancel-ib-order reported a SUCCESSFUL cancel as refused_by_venue, and told the operator not to retry
items.detail: IBKR delivers acceptance and rejection on ONE event channel, keyed to the same orderId, and only the CODE distinguishes them. `_cancel_error_capture` filed EVERY event as a refusal, so error 202 — "Order Canceled - reason:", the venue CONFIRMING the cancel landed — surfaced as a rejection. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-26 during the MHG over-cover repair: issue #10335 returned `action: refused_by_venue`, `verify_state: still_present`, `refusal: {code: 202}` and a note reading "the order is still resting and re-running with a longer verify window will not change that". A re-run seconds later (#10336) read `lookup_state: not_found` with the account's order count down 8 → 6. The cancel had worked; only the report was wrong. This is the worse direction of the two: an operator acting on the report either re-issues a cancel already executed, or believes a live position's protection repair failed when it succeeded. Two contributing shapes, both fixed: (a) the wrapper's refusal note asserted the 10147 story under EVERY code (diagnostic-provenance sub-class A — a cause no code path tested); (b) the post-cancel verification reads through `ib_read_client_for`, whose order view is accumulated and never learns of a cancel it did not issue (BL-20260826-DIAG-IB-OPEN-ORDERS-SERVES-A-STALE-MONOTONIC-ORDER-VIEW), so `still_present` after a CONFIRMED cancel is a contradiction rather than a failure and is now graded `cancelled_readback_contradicted`.
items.resolution_criteria: A venue confirmation never surfaces as a refusal; a genuine refusal still reports retCode 1; the refusal note names the code that actually came back; the confirmed-but-still-on-the-readback case is its own state rather than collapsed into either `gone` or `cancel_not_effective`. All four pinned by tests, and the confirmation test break-tested to reproduce the #10335 payload byte-for-byte against the old code.
items.resolution: `_classify_ib_cancel_event` + `_IB_CANCEL_CONFIRMED_CODES` (an ALLOWLIST of confirmation codes, so an unrecognised code stays a refusal and a rejection this repo has never seen fails loud rather than being swallowed as success). `_cancel_error_capture` now returns `(refusals, confirmations, detach)`; `IBClient.cancel` surfaces a `confirmation` key. Tests: tests/test_ib_cancel_verification.py (`ConfirmingIB` models a venue that acknowledges a successful cancel — the original `FakeIB` emitted an event only on the refusal path, which is why the broken capture looked correct against it) + tests/test_cancel_ib_order.py.

items.tier: 1 — read-path only. Adds a field to two read routes and a helper module; changes no order path, no write, no aggregate ARITHMETIC (totalPnl is byte-identical — only a caveat is published beside it).
items.title: The broker-truth ledger recorded which accounts cannot be trusted and NOTHING on the journal read path consulted it
items.detail: `comms/broker_truth_ledger.json` has recorded since 2026-07-13 that `bybit_2`'s per-row journal `pnl` UNDER-RECORDS — wallet-truth −$262.52 against a per-row sum roughly 8× smaller (BL-20260713-BYBIT2-PNL-UNDERRECORD) — and its ONLY consumer was its own read-only route `/api/bot/pnl/broker-truth`. Nothing on the journal READ path consulted it. MEASURED 2026-08-26: asked to investigate BTC losses on real money, a session queried that account's closed BTC trades, got +$0.88, and reported the book flat. The operator corrected it from the venue UI — "There's definitely a real money problem, and the fact that you're not seeing it is also a problem." Every component was individually correct: the ledger recorded the divergence, the journal returned its rows, the aggregate summed them faithfully. The defect is at the SEAM — a fact recorded in one place and not delivered where the decision is made. Same shape as the `exit_price_source` case this repo already paid for (written in 12 files, branched on in one). The operator's ruling: "If the trade journal is not a trustworthy source of data, that is priority number 1."
items.resolution_criteria: A consumer reading `/api/bot/trades/closed` or `/api/bot/performance` for an account with a broker-truth record is told so IN THAT RESPONSE, without a second query; the three states stay uncollapsed (`no_record` never renders as trusted, `unreadable` is distinguishable from both); the ledger is read once per request rather than once per row; and a test pins that the COMMITTED ledger still flags `bybit_2` — so emptying or restructuring it cannot make the flag silently inert.
items.resolution: `broker_truth.journal_trust` / `journal_trust_map` / `journal_trust_for`; `journalTrust` per row on `/api/bot/trades/closed` (mirroring `pnlProvenance`, no shape change) and an envelope block on `/api/bot/performance` scoped to the accounts actually in the window. ⚠️ WRITING THE TESTS CAUGHT THE SAME CLASS ONE LAYER DOWN, IN THIS FIX: the `unreadable` state was UNREACHABLE, because `load_ledger` funnels a missing file, an unparseable file and a file listing nothing into one identical empty envelope — so a deliberately corrupted ledger graded every account merely `no_record`. `_ledger_read_state` now asks the file directly (`read`/`absent`/`unreadable`); `load_ledger`'s own best-effort contract is deliberately unchanged (its existing route consumer wants the degraded envelope). The test schema also had to be rebuilt twice — hand-rolled missed `trades.exit_price`, lifting the CREATE TABLE text missed the migration-added `reconcile_status` — so it now builds through `Database(...)`, the production initialiser. Tests: tests/test_journal_trust_wiring.py (break-tested), plus the `/trades/closed` wire-shape contract test.

items.tier: 1 — a backlog-hygiene sweep plus, if adopted, widening an existing guard's scope. Touches no runtime.
items.title: 47 of 489 open backlog rows carry no tier, and the guard that requires one is diff-scoped so they are grandfathered forever
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-26 across all three backlogs: 1,164 rows total, 489 open/kept_open, and **47 of those 489 (9.6%) have no `tier` field**. `scripts/ops/check_backlog_criteria.py` requires one and states exactly why: "nothing can tell whether a session may fix this itself or must ask the operator, so it is safest to do neither (and nobody does)". But it runs `--base origin/main`, i.e. it only ever grades rows ADDED by the current diff — so every pre-existing untiered row is grandfathered permanently and the count can only be worked down by hand. ⚠️ THE DIFF-SCOPING IS NOT ITSELF THE BUG and must not be 'fixed' by making the guard repo-wide: that would fail every PR on 47 rows the author did not write, which is the re-attribution failure `BL-20260820-BACKLOG-APPEND-REFORMATS-AND-REATTRIBUTES` already records, and it would be walked past within a day. The oldest untiered rows date to 2026-07-12 and include `BL-20260713-BYBIT2-PNL-UNDERRECORD` — the very row whose un-consulted ledger caused this session's worst error.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) the 47 rows carry an honest tier — set by reading each row, NOT by a bulk default, since a wrong tier is worse than none: it would licence a session to act on a Tier-3 change unasked; or (b) a deliberate, recorded decision that untiered pre-2026-08-26 rows are triaged on read instead, with the guard's error text amended to stop implying every open row has one. Verified by re-running the count above and getting the number it claims.
items.notes: Found while running run_guards.py --all at session end, not by a check that watches for it — which is the same shape as the finding itself. A count over the whole open population is not something any current guard computes.

updates.note: RE-MEASURED IN PASSING DURING THIS TRIAGE: severity is absent on 18 of the health rows I triaged and tier is absent on many more; the guard is diff-scoped so they stay grandfathered. items.title: WITHDRAWN — the '180 sites' figure was my own cruder metric; the real guard reports clean over 965 test files
items.detail: RETRACTED THE SAME SESSION IT WAS FILED. The 180 figure came from a checker I wrote after failing to find the one that already existed: `scripts/ci/check_test_schema_fidelity.py` has been in the repo since PR #10201, is registered in run_guards.py, and I OVERWROTE IT with `cat >` without looking. Restored byte-identical from origin/main. The existing guard asks the RIGHT question — does a fixture declare a COLUMN production lacks, resolved over CREATE TABLE **plus** ALTER TABLE migrations — and its standing audit reports CLEAN over 965 test files. Mine asked a cruder one (is there any CREATE TABLE for a production table at all), which flags 180 perfectly legitimate fixtures. There is no finding here. Kept as `invalid` rather than deleted so the false number is attributable and nobody re-derives it. ORIGINAL (WRONG) TEXT FOLLOWS: The first standing audit of `scripts/ci/check_test_schema_fidelity.py` (shipped 2026-08-26 as the prevention for RC-TEST-SCHEMA-PRODUCTION-DOES-NOT-HAVE) found **180 sites** under `tests/` declaring their own `CREATE TABLE` for a production-owned table — chiefly `tests/ml/datasets/*` for `trades` and `order_packages`. ⚠️ **180 SITES IS NOT 180 BUGS**, and conflating the two would be this repo's own population error: it is the exposed SURFACE, i.e. places where a test could pass against a shape production does not have. Three instances are known to have actually cost something (the pairs `max_hold_bars` never evaluating, and two in one session on 2026-08-26). The ml/datasets concentration is what makes it worth a row rather than a note: those tests gate the DATASET BUILDERS that feed training, so a drifted `trades` shape there is tested against a table the trainer will never see. Grandfathered by the guard's diff-scoping (failing PRs on 180 lines nobody wrote is BL-20260820-BACKLOG-APPEND-REFORMATS-AND-REATTRIBUTES' re-attribution failure and gets the guard switched off within a day).
