items.tier: 3 — any change to stop placement/enforcement is order-path. This row is the MEASUREMENT; the fix is operator-gated.
items.title: HISTORICAL — vwap exited past its decision-time stop on 44.2% of measured closes (65/147), but vwap has been OFF since 2026-06-07 and is routed to no account
items.detail:
⚠️ THIRD CORRECTION, ON THE OPERATOR'S QUESTION 'is vwap still live on bybit 2?' — **NO, AND THIS IS NOT A LIVE BLEED.** Verified three independent ways 2026-08-26: (a) `/api/bot/strategies` reports vwap `execution: shadow`, `enabled: false`, `loaded: false`, `running: false`; (b) `/api/bot/config` shows vwap routed to **no account** — bybit_2 runs trend_donchian, ict_scalp_5m, fvg_range_15m, eth_pullback_2h, xrp_pullback_2h, trend_donchian_eth_4h, trend_donchian_xrp_4h, and vwap is absent from every account's list; (c) vwap's LAST OPEN in the journal is **2026-06-07T20:14:27Z** — 2,180 trades lifetime, none in ~2.5 months, zero open now. The account bybit_2 IS live (`yaml_mode: live`, real_money); the STRATEGY is not. I filed this reading as 'real money, one strategy, the netting account', which implies a current condition, WITHOUT EVER CHECKING WHETHER THE STRATEGY WAS STILL RUNNING. The measurement is correct and its time-bound was never stated — the population is May-June 2026, not now. Priority drops accordingly: this is evidence about a strategy that may one day be re-armed, not money leaking today. It is still worth root-causing BEFORE any re-arm, which is what makes it worth keeping open rather than closing. ORIGINAL TEXT FOLLOWS: CORRECTED THE SAME SESSION, TWICE. (1) The first version quoted COUNTS -- '71 of 72 are bybit_2, 65 of 72 are vwap' -- with no denominator. The clean rows are ALSO bybit_2/vwap (82 of them), so the counts described the population, not a defect. Restated as RATES: bybit_2/vwap **65 of 147 = 44.2%**, bybit_2/ict_scalp_5m 3/15 = 20.0%, eth_pullback_2h 1/8 = 12.5%, trend_donchian 1/10 = 10.0%, and three strategies at 0/5-0/7. vwap survives the denominator check and is the finding. (2) The bybit_2 concentration is NOT a signal at all -- it is a MEASUREMENT-COVERAGE ARTIFACT: bybit is the only exchange in clients.BROKER_PNL_READER_EXCHANGES, so a MEASURED exit price is structurally bybit-only and no other venue can appear in this population. Do not read it as 'the problem is on bybit_2'. (3) THE NETTING HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, in the opposite direction: overlapping same-(account, symbol) trades appear on 4.2% of overshooting rows (3/72) vs 23.3% of clean ones (28/120 sampled) -- a -19.2pp difference, so netted siblings correlate with CLEAN exits, not past-stop ones. Whatever causes it, it is not a sibling leg replacing the resting stop. ORIGINAL TEXT FOLLOWS: Operator asked why trades close at the wrong levels. MEASURED 2026-08-26 over the live journal. POPULATION, because it decides the answer: 5,050 trades pulled; 1,357 closed and non-backtest; **589 joinable to their decision-time `order_packages` bracket**; of those **221 have a MEASURED exit price**. On that n=221: median exit_R −1.005, and **72 (32.6%) land beyond −1.02R**, median overshoot −1.06R, worst −1.86R. Concentration is the finding: **account bybit_2 = 71 of 72; strategy vwap = 65 of 72** — real money, one strategy, the netting account. Top exit_reasons: reconciler_filled 40, sl_cross 13.
⚠️ **THE DENOMINATOR HAD TO BE THE ORDER PACKAGE, NOT `trades.stop_loss`.** A first pass using the trades column produced '22.7% past stop' AND graded 95 correctly-TRAILED rows as inverted brackets, because that column carries the trailed stop (10 writing modules — see `scripts/ops/column_provenance.py trades.stop_loss`). 
⚠️ **THE UNRESTRICTED ARM IS THE KNOWN ARTIFACT, NOT A FINDING.** Across all 589 joinable rows the worst reads −12.54R; `PB-20260807-ICTSCALP-STOP-DID-NOT-CONTAIN-8R` already established that class of figure is substantially an EXIT-PRICE RECONSTRUCTION ARTIFACT. Restricting to measured prices collapses the worst case to −1.86R. Do not quote the unrestricted number.
items.resolution_criteria: ⚠️ **RE-ARM GATE (operator-directed 2026-08-26): vwap does not come back on without an exit-geometry review first.** vwap is `execution: shadow`, routed to no account, and last traded 2026-06-07, so nothing is bleeding today and this row is NOT urgent. But it is also not closable by time passing: if anyone proposes re-arming vwap — or reusing its `entry ± SL_STD_MULT × std_dev` stop construction in another strategy — that proposal must first go through `docs/design/exit-mechanism-construction-PROCESS.md`, and the 44.2% past-stop reading below is the evidence it has to answer. Re-litigating the strategy without that review is what this gate exists to stop. Root-cause why VWAP specifically exits past its declared stop at 44.2% while its same-account peers sit at 0-20%. ⚠️ The netting-sibling hypothesis is ALREADY REFUTED (see detail) — do not re-run it. The strategy-specific rate points at vwap's own stop geometry: `src/units/strategies/vwap.py` computes `stop_loss = entry ± SL_STD_MULT × std_dev`, so a volatility-scaled stop set on a mean-reverting entry may simply be inside normal bar noise, which would make 'past the stop' the expected outcome rather than a failure of enforcement. Distinguish those two before proposing any fix: an enforcement bug and a too-tight stop need opposite changes. Resolved when the mechanism is named with evidence and either fixed or shown to be venue slippage that no change can remove. Re-measure on the same population definition to confirm movement.
items.notes: REFINES PB-20260807-ICTSCALP-STOP-DID-NOT-CONTAIN-8R rather than duplicating it: that row retracts an artifact-driven headline; this one is the corrected measurement on measured-only prices against the decision-time bracket, and reports a concentration that row does not.

updates.note: Re-validated: HISTORICAL by its own label — vwap has been OFF since. But note vwap_cross is still the LARGEST real-money exit path in the live perExitPath cut (102 trades, pnlCoverage 0.3431), so the historical population it describes is substantial and still shapes every aggregate.

items.tier: 1 — the fix is one line in a script's sys.path; RUNNING the tool is the separate Tier-2 half.
items.title: The G1 exit-label backfill shipped INERT: sys.path walked two levels from scripts/ops, so `import src` raised ModuleNotFoundError and it had never once run
items.detail:
`scripts/ops/backfill_exit_labels.py` merged in #10262 on 2026-08-25 with `sys.path.insert(0, dirname(dirname(abspath(__file__))))` — TWO levels from `scripts/ops/`, landing on `scripts/`, not the repo root. `import src.runtime.provenance` therefore raised ModuleNotFoundError and the script could not run from anywhere: not the repo root, and not from `backfill_exit_labels_action.sh`, which invokes it by ABSOLUTE path with no `cd` and no PYTHONPATH. Every one of the eight sibling backfills in that directory uses `parents[2]`; this was the only one that did not.

MEASURED on the live journal 2026-08-26 (via the Caddy diag host; deployed sha da5a7d6d == main, restart_pending false; every query asserted `filter_state: applied`): **0 rows** carry `notes.pre_backfill_exit_reason` and **0** carry `refused_unmeasured_price` — both written ONLY by this tool. Three days after merging it had never executed. Meanwhile the population it exists for was untouched: `trades` with `exit_reason='reconciler_filled'`, n=593 (all `status='closed'`) of 5,056 rows, of which 589 are gradeable and **562 (95.4%) carry no `exit_reason_source` at all**; only 53 rows in the entire table have ever reached the classifier.

FAIL-SAFE, NOT SILENT-WRONG: the wrapper runs `--self-test` as a precondition and aborts on a non-zero exit, so the action could never half-apply. It was inert, and an inert tool is not a capability.

WHY NO TEST CAUGHT IT — the transferable half. The sibling backfill tests load the script via `importlib.util.spec_from_file_location`, and under pytest the repo root is ALREADY on `sys.path`, so a broken insert is harmless and the import succeeds. The test shape and the production shape differed in exactly the dimension that was broken. Only an invocation with a foreign cwd and a scrubbed PYTHONPATH reproduces the wrapper.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED in this PR: path corrected to `parents[2]`, and `tests/ops/test_backfill_exit_labels.py` leads with a subprocess invocation (absolute path, foreign cwd, no inherited PYTHONPATH) that is verified to FAIL on the original line while the importlib-based branch tests pass either way. The REMAINING half is Tier-2 and NOT done: the tool has still never been applied to the live journal. A dry run against a full replica projects 191 rows relabelled (144 sl / 47 tp), 105 refused on a FABRICATED price, 185 honest `unresolved`.
items.notes: Found while working GATE 0 / G1. Same family as the #8778 'writer shipped without a read surface' shape: shipped != working.

items.tier: 1 — one entry in a protected-key tuple; no order path, no schema change.
items.title: `dump_capped` trimmed the `exit_reason_source` provenance marker itself, producing a third value that matches neither the resolved sentinel nor `unresolved`
items.detail:
`src/utils/json_notes.py::_shrink_dict` fits a `trades.notes` blob into 500 chars by repeatedly halving the longest UNPROTECTED string value. `exit_reason_source` was absent from `_DEFAULT_PROTECTED` — which protects its two siblings `pnl_source` and `exit_price_source` — because it was added later (2026-08-23/25) and the tuple is extended by hand.

A provenance marker is a SENTINEL: consumers compare it for equality against a fixed vocabulary, so a trimmed value is not a shorter answer, it is an unreadable third state matching nothing. MEASURED on the live journal 2026-08-26 — population: the 25 `trades` rows whose notes carry a RESOLVED `exit_reason_source` — **2 (8.0%) store `"price_vs_p…"`**: trade 4961 (`bybit_1`/AVAXUSDT, closed 08-23) and trade 4978 (`bybit_portfolio`/BTCUSDT, closed 08-24), both also carrying `_truncated: true`.

BOTH READINGS OF A CORRUPTED MARKER ARE WRONG: a consumer testing `== 'price_vs_pkg_bracket'` counts the row as never-classified; one testing `is None` counts it as classified-but-unknown. Worse, the ABSENCE of this key is load-bearing evidence elsewhere — it is the signature that made the frozen-label class readable (562 of 589 gradeable `reconciler_filled` rows) — so corrupting the key corrupts that denominator too.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED in this PR: `exit_reason_source` added to `_DEFAULT_PROTECTED`, with a test built from row 4961's real stored blob that reproduces `"price_vs_p…"` exactly under the pre-fix set and is verified to FAIL without the change, plus a set-level assertion that every declared provenance marker is protected. NOT repaired retroactively: the 2 existing rows still carry the truncated value — the backfill's `--apply` run would restamp them, since a corrupted marker is not one of the values its idempotency check recognises.
items.notes: Found while measuring the G1 population. The generalisable rule: any field whose value is compared for EQUALITY must never be trimmable.

items.tier: 1 — deleting a never-run script and correcting the doc that pointed at it.
items.title: Two tools existed for the exit-label backfill, and the older one would have relabelled the 105 rows the newer one deliberately REFUSED, stamping them as measured
items.detail:
`scripts/ops/reclassify_frozen_exit_reasons.py` shipped 2026-08-22 (WORKPLAN-2026-08-21 item 1.8, Tier-2 operator-approved) as the historical half of the frozen-exit-label fix, and was left STAGED, NOT RUN. Three days later a different session independently built `scripts/ops/backfill_exit_labels.py` (#10262) for the SAME job, gave it a Tier-2 system-action wrapper, and never referenced the earlier one. Two tools, one job — `RC-BUILT-A-MECHANISM-THAT-ALREADY-EXISTED`. Neither had ever run: measured 2026-08-26, **0 rows carried `exit_reason_prior`** (written only by the older tool) and 0 carried `pre_backfill_exit_reason` (only by the newer).

⚠️ **THE OLDER TOOL WAS NOT MERELY REDUNDANT, IT WAS A LIVE HAZARD, AND THE 08-21 PLAN INSTRUCTED THE NEXT SESSION TO RUN IT** (*"run `--provenance broker_truth` first ... widen only if warranted"* — and "widen" means `--provenance all`). Its apply path writes `notes["exit_reason_source"] = "price_vs_pkg_bracket"` — the MEASURED sentinel — **unconditionally, regardless of the price's provenance**, because `_classify_broker_exit` is provenance-BLIND by design. Its only re-check skips a row whose `exit_reason` is no longer generic.

So after the newer tool's applied run (2026-08-26, 191 relabelled / 105 refused), the 105 rows it REFUSED are still `exit_reason='reconciler_filled'` carrying a FABRICATED price (`local_markprice` — the market read hours after the exit). They would therefore have passed the older tool's re-check, been relabelled `sl`/`tp` off that fabricated price, and had their `refused_unmeasured_price` stamp **overwritten with the measured sentinel** — manufacturing exactly the sl/tp verdicts out of unrelated price action that the provenance gate exists to prevent, and erasing the record that a refusal ever happened.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED 2026-08-26: the script and its test are DELETED (operator decision, asked and answered in-conversation), and the three doc sites that pointed at it are corrected — WORKPLAN-2026-08-21 § "Historical pass" and item 1.8, plus the ROADMAP ledger row — each now naming the tool that actually ran. Verified no code, script, or workflow references remain; the surviving mentions are dated historical records. The surviving tool's gate is strictly better than a `--provenance` flag a caller must remember to pass: it decides PER ROW and stamps the weaker `price_vs_pkg_bracket_est_price` sentinel on an estimated price so it can never read as the stronger verdict.
items.notes: The transferable lesson is about the FLAG, not the duplicate: scoping a destructive write with an opt-in CLI flag whose default is the widest setting puts the safety property in the caller's memory. The surviving tool moves it into the row-level decision, where it cannot be forgotten. Found while re-deriving G5's headline, not by looking for it.

items.tier: 1 — research tooling only (planner + workflow + tests); no order path, no config, no VM mutation.
items.title: The e35 bracket sweep fetched candles into a filename its own resolver never reads, so 4 legs paid a runner and exited GREEN having measured nothing — and the rollup counted the empty report as a measured leg
items.detail:
`.github/workflows/e35-bracket-sweep.yml` derived its output stem INLINE as `data/{symbol}_{tf}.csv`, while `scripts/research/m20_fleet_exit_sweep.py::resolve_data` applies `PROXY_DATA` (`MES->ES_F`, `MGC`/`XAUUSD->GC_F`, `MHG->HG_F`) **unconditionally and with no native fallback**. Two definitions of where a leg's candles live; they disagreed for every `PROXY_DATA` symbol, so the runner wrote `MES_1d.csv` and the sweep looked only for `ES_F_1d.csv`.

⚠️ THE FAILURE WAS GREEN, which is why it survived. Reproduced 2026-08-26 by invoking the sweep exactly as the workflow does, with `MES_1d.csv` on disk: `plan: 0 legs runnable, 1 skipped / SKIP mes_trend_long_1d: data_missing:MES / EXIT CODE = 0`, and the written `report.json` carried `legs: []`. The leg pays the fetch, the job passes, the artifact uploads.

POPULATION: the 25 cells recorded `blocked:no_free_lane_candle_feed` in `docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json` (updated_at 2026-08-24T15:55Z), all in the `bracket_geometry` lever across 25 distinct legs. Running the planner against today's config: **21 schedulable, of which 17 resolved and 4 fetch-then-failed** — `mes_trend_long_1d`, `mgc_pullback_1d`, `mgc_trend_1h`, `xauusd_trend_1h`. The other 4 were correctly out of scope or refused by name.

⚠️ SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT — the rollup could not surface it. `aggregate` counted `report.json` FILES (`{len(reports)} of {planned} leg(s) returned a report`). An empty report is still a returned one, so the count could equal `planned`, the `⚠️ N leg(s) produced no report` warning never fired, and the table — which iterates `legs` — printed no row for them. 4 legs vanished from a summary that read as complete coverage. That is the unasserted-denominator class this same workflow already guards against elsewhere in its own file, which is the point: the guard existed and did not cover the case where the report is real and the measurement is absent.
items.resolution_criteria:
RESOLVED 2026-08-26. (1) `e35_shard_plan.data_basename` is now the ONE definition of the stem, DERIVED from `fleet.PROXY_DATA` rather than restated, and carried in the matrix so the workflow cannot hold a second opinion. (2) `PROXY_DATA` symbols route to **yfinance** (operator-approved 2026-08-26): those stems mean the yfinance full-size contract and `yf_symbols` maps `MES->ES=F`, `MGC`/`XAUUSD->GC=F`, `MHG->HG=F` — exactly that series — whereas dukascopy would write an S&P index CFD and spot XAU under names asserting the futures contract. Cost stated rather than hidden: yfinance caps 1h at ~730 d, so the two 1h legs take a PARTIAL window against the 1830 d request; the fetcher clamps and reports it. (3) `aggregate` counts legs MEASURED, not reports returned, and NAMES each skipped leg's reason. Verified: planner 40 -> 41 jobs and **all 41 resolve after their own fetch (was 37)**. `tests/test_e35_shard_plan_data_basename.py` carries a POSITIVE CONTROL (`test_the_naive_stem_is_what_used_to_break`) so the main assertion cannot go vacuous if `PROXY_DATA` is emptied, and the rollup test lifts its python OUT of the shipping YAML rather than copying it. Each fix confirmed to FAIL against the pre-fix code.

⚠️ STILL OPEN, deliberately NOT closed by this row: the 25 coverage cells remain `blocked:no_free_lane_candle_feed` until the sweep is actually DISPATCHED and returns verdicts. Shipping the fix is not the same as running the work, and flipping the matrix on a code change would assert a measurement nobody took.

items.tier: 1 — reading an observe-only soak; nothing changed.
items.title: Every row the target-extension soak has ever written is a SENTINEL row, so it cannot yet distinguish 'the lever never fires' from 'no real-target trade has approached its target'
items.detail:
WORKPLAN-2026-08-26 item **B3** says to read the `target_extension_soak` (shipped at ANNOTATE 2026-08-23). Read 2026-08-26 via `/api/diag/log_file?name=target_extension_soak`.

**POPULATION: the COMPLETE file, n = 856 rows, 2026-08-23T10:12:20Z → 2026-08-26T12:47:09Z, 19 strategy legs, 22 distinct `order_package_id`.** Completeness is PROVEN, not assumed: a `lines=1000` request returned **856** — a short page, the same proof-of-tail rule the coordination board uses. (A 400-line read returned 400 and would have proven nothing.)

**Every row is the same row:**
- `extension_state`: **856/856** `no_expectation_declared`
- `expectation_state`: **856/856** `sentinel_no_expectation`
- `target_r`: the ONLY value present is **50.0** (the sentinel), `target_source_key` = `tp_r` on all 856
- `extends_so_far` = 0 and `would_move_tp_to` = null on all 856
- **ZERO** rows in ANY informative state — `extend`, `thesis_broken_hold`, `thesis_unknown`, `extension_cap_reached`

**THE COMPOSITION IS STRUCTURAL, NOT INCIDENTAL** — read from the code, not inferred from the data. `src/runtime/target_expectation.py::evaluate_extension` returns `EXT_NO_EXPECTATION` **immediately** when the expectation is sentinel, BEFORE the `approach_frac` gate; and `target_extension_soak._LOGGED_STATES` deliberately EXCLUDES `not_approaching`. So a sentinel leg logs whenever it is evaluated, while a real-target leg logs **nothing at all** until price actually approaches its target. The 24 legs with a real target contributed **zero rows**.

⚠️ **So the soak currently cannot tell two opposite things apart**: (a) the extension lever would never fire, and (b) no real-target trade has come near its target in this window. Those need opposite follow-ups, and `extension_state` alone reads as (a). `CLAUDE.md` already warns *'a soak read on `extension_state` alone would score that as "the lever never fires" when it means "there was never a target"'* — that warning is CORRECT and now has a measurement behind it rather than a prediction.

⚠️ **SECOND, SEPARATE FINDING — ROW COUNT IS NOT EVENT COUNT.** `_ANNOTATED` is an **in-process** set keyed `(order_package_id, extension_state, n_extends)`, so within one process a sentinel package logs exactly ONCE. Yet one package (`pkg-b705f4e472f3488d`) carries **67 rows over 74.6 h**, with gaps min 290 s / median 2576 s / max 30878 s — irregular, and nothing like the 30 s exit-loop cadence. The supported reading is that the dedup resets on every trader restart (the trader redeploys on each merge to `main`), so the count tracks PROCESS LIFETIME rather than trading activity. Not proven from this file alone — correlating `process_started_utc` in `exit_interval_soak` would settle it — but a reader computing 'the lever was evaluated 856 times' is wrong either way. Same family as `BL-20260823-TARGET-NAKED-COOLDOWN-RESETS-ON-EVERY-RESTART`, though here it inflates a log rather than an alarm.
items.resolution_criteria:
This row is a READING, and closing it needs the soak to become able to answer the question it was built for. Either: (1) a real-target leg's trade approaches its target and writes a row in an informative state — at which point re-read and grade the lever on THAT population, not on the sentinel rows; or (2) if none appears over a stated window, establish WHY before concluding anything — 28 of 52 enabled legs declaring `tp_r >= 50` is already recorded, so the denominator of legs that COULD produce a row is 24, and how often any of them approaches is unmeasured.

⚠️ **Do NOT 'fix' this by logging `not_approaching`** — that is the ordinary state of nearly every trade on nearly every tick and the exclusion is deliberate (the desensitized-alarm shape applied to a log). If the denominator is wanted, count it separately rather than emitting a row per tick.

The row-count half is separable and cheaper: make the dedup durable, or stamp the row with the process identity so a reader can divide by it. Until then any count off this file must be quoted as 'rows written', never as 'times evaluated'.

updates.note: Re-validated and CORROBORATED by CLAUDE.md's own figure: 28 of 52 enabled legs declare tp_r >= 50, so more than half the fleet has no target to extend FROM. A soak that is 100% sentinel cannot distinguish 'the lever never fires' from 'there was never a target' — which is the row's exact point.

items.tier: 1 — research evidence recovery + a research-tooling fix; no order path, no config, no VM.
items.title: 1,629 measured e35 cells have sat unmerged on claude/e35-bracket-corpus for two days, and that branch has diverged so far it now REJECTS every new corpus push
items.detail:
Two failures compounding, found 2026-08-26 while running the Lane B / B1 sweep.

**(1) THE ROWS WERE WRITTEN AND THEN NOBODY COLLECTED THEM.** `.github/workflows/e35-bracket-sweep.yml`'s `corpus` job pushes to the ref it ran on, EXCEPT on the default branch, where protection refuses a bare commit (GH006) so it retargets to `claude/e35-bracket-corpus`. That retarget path ends with an explicit notice — *"A HUMAN OR A SESSION must open the PR — this job cannot, and no workflow will fire from its push"* (`BL-20260813-CORPUS-RETARGET-CANNOT-OPEN-ITS-OWN-PR`). **Nobody did.** Measured: the branch carries **3,833** rows against main's **2,219**, and **1,629 measurement keys exist on the branch and nowhere else** — 1,625 `state: measured` plus 4 `inert_equals_base`, across **14 legs** and 14 distinct `sweep_generated_at` stamps from the 2026-08-24 dispatch (run 32783849276): `sol_pullback_2h`, `xrp_pullback_2h`, `avax_pullback_2h`, `htf_pullback_trend_2h`, `squeeze_breakout_4h`, `eth_pullback_2h`, `eth_pullback_prop_2h`, `ada_pullback_2h` (199 cells each) and others. Real bracket-geometry measurements, two days old, invisible to every consumer that reads the committed corpus.

⚠️ **The hand-off warning being CORRECT and LOUD did not make it happen.** The job did everything right and still the evidence went nowhere — which is the point: a notice addressed to nobody in particular is not a mechanism.

**(2) THE BRANCH CAN NO LONGER ACCEPT A PUSH.** Measured the same day: `claude/e35-bracket-corpus` is **53 commits behind main and 163 ahead**, because it was cut from a pre-squash history whose content later reached main as squash commits. The corpus job's retry path (`git rebase origin/$TARGET`) therefore hits a conflict — observed verbatim on run 32974902210: `Could not apply 24431bbf...` then `! [rejected] HEAD -> claude/e35-bracket-corpus (non-fast-forward)` and `could not push the corpus after 3 attempts`. **So every future default-branch dispatch loses its rows the same way**, and a 22-leg matrix would lose 22 legs' worth.

⚠️ Neither side is a superset: main holds **15** keys the branch lacks (the `mes_trend_long_1d` run of 2026-08-26). A `git reset --hard` onto either side drops real measurements — the recovery must be a UNION keyed on `measurement_key`, not a reset.

⚠️ **The sibling already has the tool and it does NOT generalise as-is.** `scripts/research/m20_corpus_union.py` exists for exactly this failure on the M20 lever sweep (its docstring records main 1264 / branch 1004 / 360 stranded) and its merge rule — resolve by `sweep_generated_at`, break ties ONLY by strict key-superset, otherwise REFUSE — is the right one. But it hardcodes `from m20_corpus_extract import measurement_key`, and the e35 corpus has its own key (`leg|cell|tp_cap_pct|split_mode|split_target_oos`). Pointing it at e35 rows unchanged would compute the WRONG identity. Parameterise the key function; do not copy the script (a second copy is the drift its own docstring warns about).
items.resolution_criteria:
Two halves, and the first is the urgent one.

**(a) RECOVER THE 1,629 ROWS.** Union the branch corpus into main's keyed on the e35 `measurement_key`, expected total **3,848** (2,204 shared + 1,629 branch-only + 15 main-only) — assert that arithmetic rather than trusting the row count, and assert no key lost from EITHER side. Land it as a normal PR.

**(b) MAKE THE PATH DURABLE.** Generalise `m20_corpus_union.py` to take its key function per corpus family (M20 vs e35) so there is one union implementation, then decide how `claude/e35-bracket-corpus` is kept mergeable — the current branch cannot rebase and will re-strand rows on the next default-branch dispatch. Until (b) lands, **dispatch the e35 sweep from a working branch, not from `main`**: the corpus job then pushes straight to that branch with no retarget, which is verified working (runs 32972413593 and the 22-leg Lane B matrix).

⚠️ Do NOT close this by resetting either branch onto the other — that is precisely the silent-row-loss the M20 sibling was filed for.
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-08-26 (recovery half). All 1,629 stranded keys are now in `docs/research/e35-bracket-corpus.jsonl` on `main`. Recovered by UNION, never a reset, using `scripts/research/m20_corpus_union.py --corpus e35` — the existing M20 tool PARAMETERISED on which extractor owns `measurement_key`, not copied. **Verified against the produced FILE, not the tool's log: 8,211 rows / 8,211 unique keys / 0 duplicates**, = 6,582 (main) + 1,629 appended. 2,204 keys were shared; 2,152 resolved to the branch row, and every one of those is a 2026-08-23 row superseded by its 2026-08-24 re-measurement — checked, not assumed. **Zero fields were lost** (no replaced row carried a key its winner lacked), which is the `BL-20260816-CORPUS-CONFLICT-REDERIVE-RUNS-THE-STALE-BRANCH-EXTRACTOR` schema-regression check, and **zero 2026-08-26 rows were replaced**. ⚠️ **The BRANCH ITSELF IS STILL DIVERGED AND STILL CANNOT ACCEPT A PUSH** — that half is NOT fixed and is why this row is resolved on the DATA and not on the mechanism. The operative mitigation remains: dispatch the e35 sweep from a WORKING BRANCH, never `main`. A dispatch from `main` will still retarget to the broken branch and still lose its rows.

items.tier: 1 — research gate arithmetic; no order path, no config, no VM.
items.title: The e35 bracket gate compares RAW walk-forward wins against its threshold, so INERT folds count as wins — a recurrence of BL-20260817 in the sweep that consumes the fix
items.detail:
`scripts/research/e35_bracket_geometry_sweep.py:653`:

    passed = usable > 0 and wf["wins"] >= math.ceil(2 * usable / 3)

It reads **`wf["wins"]`** — the RAW count. `m20_fleet_exit_sweep.walkforward` computes **`wins_effective = wins - inert_wins`** (line 2069) for exactly this reason, and `BL-20260817-FLEET-SWEEP-WF-COUNTS-INERT-FOLDS-AS-WINS` is the row that put it there. The e35 gate imports `walkforward` and then ignores the field the fix added. An INERT fold is one where the cell and the base produce the SAME book (`d_net_r == 0.0`), i.e. the cell did nothing that fold — counting it as evidence the cell generalises is the defect.

**POPULATION, stated: every gate-PASSING cell in `docs/research/e35-bracket-corpus.jsonl` — 33 cells (7 from the 2026-08-23 run, 26 from 2026-08-26), and ALL 33 were checkable** (each carries `wf_wins`, `wf_wins_effective` and per-fold `usable`/`inert`), so this is not a sampled figure. **4 of the 33 pass on raw wins and would FAIL on effective**, all from the 2026-08-26 run:

| leg | cell | raw | effective | threshold | inert folds |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `splg_trend_long_1d` | `tp2.5` | 5 | **2** | 4 | 3 |
| `spy_trend_long_1d` | `tp2.5` | 5 | **2** | 4 | 3 |
| `tlt_pullback_1d` | `to48` | 6 | **3** | 4 | 3 |
| `uso_trend_1h` | `tp4` | 5 | **2** | 4 | 3 |

Each has **half its folds inert** — 3 of 6 — so the 'pass' rests on 2–3 folds that actually differed from base.

⚠️ **Blast radius is smaller than the cell count suggests, and the distinction matters.** Three of those four legs have OTHER passing cells that clear the effective threshold cleanly, so their leg-level verdict is unaffected. **Only `splg_trend_long_1d` has its SOLE pass carried by inert folds** — recording that leg as `passed_unshipped` would have asserted 'validated, awaiting implementation' for a cell whose evidence is half-empty. It is recorded `honest_negative` instead, with the arithmetic in its ref.

⚠️ **NOT CHECKED, and deliberately not claimed clean:** the two pre-existing `passed_unshipped` bracket_geometry cells (`eth_pullback_2h`, `eth_pullback_prop_2h`, from the 2026-08-20 run) have **no passing rows in this corpus**, so this measurement says nothing about them either way. They need the same check against that run's own artifacts before anyone treats them as unaffected.
items.resolution_criteria:
Change line 653 to gate on `wins_effective` rather than `wins`, then RE-GATE the existing corpus rather than re-sweeping — every passing row already carries both counts and its per-fold `inert` flags, so the verdicts are recomputable offline at zero runner cost. Expect exactly the 4 cells above to flip, and `splg_trend_long_1d` to be the only leg-level change (its ref already records the reason, so the matrix stays consistent either way).

⚠️ Do NOT 'fix' this by lowering the 2/3 threshold — the threshold is not the defect; counting a fold in which the cell did nothing is.

Also check the 2026-08-20 run's own artifacts for the two `passed_unshipped` cells named above; this row does not cover them and must not be closed as though it did.
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-08-26. `e35_bracket_geometry_sweep` now grades on `wins_effective`, and records `wf_threshold`, `wf_passed_on_raw_wins` and `verdict_basis` beside the verdict so a row where the two tallies disagree is findable rather than inferred. A missing `wins_effective` (a pre-fix `walkforward`) falls back to the RAW tally with `verdict_basis='raw_wins_no_effective_field'` — *we could not look*, never a silent zero, which would have failed every cell as a fleet-wide negative nobody measured. Pinned by `tests/test_e35_gate_inert_folds.py` (7 tests) including a POSITIVE CONTROL that the pre-fix predicate genuinely passes each affected cell, and a property test over usable/wins/inert that the fix can never MANUFACTURE a pass. ⚠️ **RESTATE THE POPULATION — the figure in the 2026-08-26 PR #10345 is SUPERSEDED.** That said *4 of 33 gate-passing cells flip*; that was correct for the corpus as it then stood. After the 1,629-row recovery the population is **51 gate-passing cells (26 from 08-26, 23 from 08-24, 2 from 08-23), all 51 gradeable (0 rows lack the counts), and **9 flip** across 8 legs: `avax_pullback_2h to48`, `sol_pullback_2h tp3`, `splg_trend_long_1d tp2.5`, `spy_trend_long_1d tp2.5`, `tlt_pullback_1d to48`, `trend_donchian_sol_4h to96` + `tp2.5`, `trend_donchian_xrp_4h tp2.5`, `uso_trend_1h tp4`. Two legs lose their SOLE pass (`sol_pullback_2h`, `splg_trend_long_1d`). **The re-gate changes ZERO coverage-matrix statuses**: all 12 matrix-cited cells were re-checked individually against the recovered corpus and every one carries **inert 0** and survives; `sol_pullback_2h` is `blocked:no_dispersion_band` and `splg_trend_long_1d` was already recorded `honest_negative`. ⚠️ **The two 2026-08-20 ETH cells are now ANSWERED and were never at risk** — the open caveat in this row's original text is closed. Their refs already quote `wins_effective` explicitly (`wf 6/6 effective (inert 0)` both). The recovery DID bring 199 rows each for those legs, but their matrix-named cells (`tp2_sm3.5_to48`, `tp4_sm3_to48`) carry `gate_verdict: null` there — **NOT GATED, which is not 'gated and failed'** — so the 08-24 run's zero passing cells says nothing about them either way and must not be read as contradicting the 08-20 result.

items.tier: 1 — a reporting/framing defect in a research statistic; no order path, no config, no VM.
items.title: "the M20 levers fire 1.3%" structurally measures 2 of the 4 lever families, and is cited to a document that does not contain it
items.detail:
Found 2026-08-26 answering workplan item B2.

**(1) THE STATISTIC CAN ONLY EVER SEE HALF THE LEVERS.** M20 has four lever families. `stale_stop` and `giveback_stop` return `{"action":"close","reason":...}` and so land in `trades.exit_reason`. `vol_trail` and `be_touch_arm` do NOT: `src/runtime/trail_vol.py` defines `resolve_vol_trail_mult` and contains no close branch at all — it resolves a trailing MULTIPLIER — and `be_touch_arm` arms break-even so its exit books as `sl`/`sl_cross`. So any "the M20 levers fire X%" read off `exit_reason` measures two of four families. That is a property of where the label is written, not of the sample, so no larger sample fixes it.

**(2) THE CITATION IS WRONG.** `docs/claude/WORKPLAN-2026-08-26.md` item B2 said *"CLAUDE.md records 17 lever firings ever"*. `CLAUDE.md` contains no such figure. The source is `docs/sprint-logs/S-SYSTEM-REVIEW-STRUCTURAL-2026-08-24.md:70` — `| M20 levers | 17 closes ever (1.3%) |` — and it says *17 closes*, not *17 lever firings*. The sprint log is not at fault; the re-citation is.

**(3) THE COUNT DOES NOT REPRODUCE, THOUGH THE RATE DOES.** Re-measured 2026-08-26 after the G1 exit-label backfill. **Population: `/api/bot/performance?window=all` `perExitPath` — real money n=407 closes across 14 paths, paper n=622 across 16 paths; `paperPortfolio` (n=58) is a SUBSET of paper and is not added.** `stale_stop` 3 real + 7 paper = 10; `giveback_stop` 0 real + 3 paper = 3; **13 lever closes of 1,029 = 1.26%** (real money alone 3 of 407 = 0.74%). Cross-checked independently on the Data Explorer (`/api/bot/db/table/trades`, `filter_state: applied` asserted on both queries): `stale_stop` 10, `giveback_stop` 3 — exact agreement across two surfaces. The RATE reproduces (1.26% vs 1.3%); the COUNT does not (13 vs 17) and the denominators differ (1,029 vs 1,324), so these are NOT the same population. The 295-row difference is NOT reconciled — the sprint log's population is not stated in enough detail to reproduce it, and inventing a reconciliation would be worse than recording the gap.

**WHAT IS NOT A DEFECT:** the firing rate itself. **Population: all 52 strategies in `config/strategies.yaml` not marked `enabled: false`** — 3 declare a stale lever (`ict_scalp_eth_15m`, `trend_donchian_eth_prop`, `trend_donchian_xrp_4h`), 1 declares giveback (`uso_trend_1h`), and **zero** declare `vol_trail` or `be_touch_arm`; **4 of 52 (7.7%) declare any M20 lever**. The levers are YAML-declared default-OFF by design. 13 firings from 4 declaring legs is the expected order of magnitude, and there is no declared-but-never-firing leg — which is what a wiring gap would look like. B2 is therefore answered NOT-a-wiring-gap; this row is about the STATISTIC.

⚠️ **AND THE OUTCOME IS STILL UNKNOWN.** `pnlCoverage` on the lever paths: real-money `stale_stop` 0.3333 (1 of 3 measured), paper `stale_stop` 0.0 (0 of 7), paper `giveback_stop` 0.0 (0 of 3) — **1 of the 13 lever closes (7.7%) has a measured PnL**. Whether the levers made or lost money rests on one trade. Do not let "correct-and-rare" about the RATE be read as a verdict on the OUTCOME.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) Every artifact quoting an M20 lever firing rate states that `exit_reason` can only carry `stale_stop` and `giveback_stop`, or quotes a measure that covers all four families (e.g. counting `vol_trail` from the resolved multiplier rather than from a close reason). (b) The B2 row's citation is corrected to the sprint log — DONE 2026-08-26. (c) EITHER the 13-vs-17 difference is reconciled by stating the sprint log's population, OR the 17 is retired in favour of a figure whose population is stated.
items.evidence: src/runtime/trail_vol.py (no close branch); src/runtime/exit_levers.py:181,273 (the two close reasons); config/strategies.yaml (4 of 52 declaring legs); /api/bot/performance?window=all perExitPath; /api/bot/db/table/trades with filter_state=applied; docs/research/m20-lever-firing-rate-2026-08-26.md

updates.note: Re-validated: the '1.3%' figure structurally measures 2 of 4 lever families and is cited to a document that does not support it. A caveat on one of the program's headline numbers — the same shape as my own 8.3% needing its lower-bound caveat.

items.tier: 1 — a local-verification hazard; no order path, no config, no VM, no CI change.
items.title: A full local pytest run carries 32 failures CI does not have, and 5 of them are ORDER-DEPENDENT — so the obvious isolation control mis-attributes them to your branch
items.detail:
Found 2026-08-26 while verifying PR #10346 locally because GitHub Actions had stalled and CI could not be relied on.

**THE NUMBERS. Population: `pytest tests/` in this sandbox with the three ccxt-blocked modules ignored (`test_exit_loop_wiring`, `test_main_loop`, `test_monitor_ohlcv_fetcher`), run twice under identical flags — once on branch `claude/exit-label-reclassification-g1-b9kyip` @ 6a018738 and once in a clean `origin/main` @ 03ee930b worktree.** Branch: **32 failed / 13,141 passed**. Main: **32 failed / 13,115 passed**. The failing node-id SETS are IDENTICAL — `comm` reports zero unique to either side — and the +26 passed delta reconciles exactly to the tests this PR adds (7 + 12 + 7). So all 32 are pre-existing and none is a regression.

**(1) 27 of 32 ARE MISSING-DEPENDENCY FAILURES, sandbox-only.** They cluster in `test_ib_sizing_and_data` (10), `test_alert_drainer_main` (6), `ml/calibration/test_calibration` (5), `test_set_leverage_preflight` (4), `test_vm_health_helper` (1), `test_s067_silent_empty_fixes` (1) — `ccxt`, `pybit`, `psutil`. `requirements.txt` pins all of them, CI installs them, and `pytest-collect`/`pytest-run` passed on `main` at 2026-08-26T14:55Z. Not defects; a sandbox provisioning gap.

**(2) THE DANGEROUS FIVE — ORDER-DEPENDENT, and the obvious control BLAMES YOUR BRANCH FOR THEM.** The `test_send_ping.py::test_claude_bridge_drain_*` family (5 tests) fails in a FULL-suite run and passes in ISOLATION. The natural control — re-run just the failing node-ids against `origin/main` — runs them in isolation, where they PASS, and therefore reports them as failing on your branch and passing on main, i.e. as YOUR regression. Measured exactly that: 27 of the 32 reproduced on main and those 5 'passed', which reads as five regressions in files the PR never touched.
**The comparison is CONFOUNDED: 32 node-ids in isolation is not the same condition as 13,173 with neighbours.** The only sound control is the FULL suite on the base branch under identical flags, which is what settled it here. Three cheaper checks each pointed the right way and none of them was sufficient alone: the 5 pass in isolation on the branch (20/20); running the PR's own new test files immediately before `test_send_ping` passes 60/60; and the PR touches none of the 7 implicated files.
⚠️ The polluting test was NOT identified — this row records the hazard and the sound control, not a root cause for the ordering dependency itself.

**WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS PR:** local verification is the FALLBACK when CI is unavailable, which is exactly when a session is least able to cross-check — and the failure mode is a session either claiming a clean local run it did not have, or 'fixing' five tests that were never broken.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) the sandbox/dev-container installs the pinned test dependencies so a local full run reproduces CI's result, OR (b) the order-dependency in `test_send_ping.py::test_claude_bridge_drain_*` is root-caused and removed so isolation and full-suite agree. Until one holds, a session comparing local failures against a base branch MUST run the FULL suite on that base under identical flags — never just the failing node-ids.
items.evidence: branch full run 32 failed/13,141 passed; origin/main worktree full run 32 failed/13,115 passed under identical flags; comm over the two sorted FAILED node-id lists yields zero unique to either side; tests/test_send_ping.py 20/20 in isolation on the branch; requirements.txt:18 pins ccxt>=4.0.0; CI pytest-collect + pytest-run success on main 2026-08-26T14:55Z

items.title: At the operator's stated $200 funding, alpaca_live cannot size 4 of its 10 priced symbols at all — Alpaca requires whole shares and $10 of risk does not buy one
items.detail:
Found 2026-08-26 while computing the `daily_usd` decision (OO-20260825-ALPACA-LIVE-DAILY-USD-200-DECISION) against the funding level the operator gave: **$200**.

**THE ARITHMETIC.** `config/accounts.yaml::alpaca_live.risk` is `{max_dd_pct: 0.1, daily_loss_pct: 0.1, daily_usd: 200, risk_pct: 0.05}`. At $200 equity that is **$10 of risk per trade**. Alpaca is in `risk.WHOLE_UNIT_QTY_EXCHANGES` (bracket orders reject fractional shares), so the position must round DOWN to whole shares. Notional that risks $10 at a stop of width `s` is `10/s`; shares are `floor((10/s) / price)`.

**Population: the 10 of `alpaca_live`'s 11 declared symbols for which `/api/bot/candles?interval=1d&limit=1` returned a close on 2026-08-26 (SPLG returned none and is EXCLUDED, not assumed).** Prices: SPY 765.50, QQQ 710.65, GLD 421.73, IWM 299.00, USO 127.99, GDX 103.09, IEF 93.25, TLT 83.11, SLV 61.63, IAUM 45.83.

At a **5% stop** ($200 notional): **SPY, QQQ, GLD and IWM all round to ZERO shares** — 4 of 10. At a **2% stop** ($500 notional): SPY and QQQ still round to ZERO — 2 of 10. So the two highest-priced symbols are unsizeable at ANY stop width this risk budget supports, and the set grows as the stop widens.
⚠️ **THE 2%/5% STOPS ARE ILLUSTRATIVE, NOT THE STRATEGIES' OWN.** Each leg derives its stop from `atr_stop_mult × ATR`, so the REAL unreachable set is a function of live ATR per symbol and is not established here. The operator was offered a per-strategy derivation and chose to file the finding as-is. What is established without any stop assumption: a whole share of SPY costs 3.8× the ENTIRE account.

**WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE CAPS.** 16 strategies route to this account, and the unsizeable four (SPY/QQQ/GLD/IWM) carry `spy_trend_long_1d`, `qqq_trend_long_1d`, `gld_pullback_1d`, `gld_pullback_1h`, `iwm_trend_long_1d`, `spy_pullback_1h` and `qqq_pullback_1h`. Funding at $200 therefore does not fund a scaled-down version of the roster — it funds a SUBSET, silently selected by share price rather than by any evaluation of the legs. That selection is invisible in the config, which lists all 16.

⚠️ **INERT TODAY, AND THAT IS NOT A REASON TO IGNORE IT.** `alpaca_live` is `mode: dry_run`, so nothing is being missed right now; this binds the moment the account is switched live at this funding. It is also the honest explanation for the account's zero gross notional across 91 `exposure_soak` rows, which OO-20260825-ALPACA-LIVE-DAILY-USD-200-DECISION's `severity_basis` cites — the execution gate, not a sizing failure.

**CONFIRMED ON THE LIVE ACCOUNT 2026-08-29 — the prediction above is no longer arithmetic, the sizer actually did it.** Population: the 400 most recent `trades` rows via `/api/diag/journal?table=trades&limit=400`, spanning 2026-08-20T08:12Z through 2026-08-29T14:04Z, of which **23 belong to `alpaca_live` and all 23 carry `status='rejected'`** (`pnl` NULL, `closed_at` NULL — no position was ever taken). Five of them carry `risk_refused: sized_qty=0 with balance=200.10`, and they are exactly **GLD (ids 5035, 5128, 5168), SPY (5176), QQQ (5179)** — three of the four symbols this row predicted unsizeable.

⚠️ **THIS DISCHARGES THIS ROW'S OWN STATED CAVEAT FOR THOSE THREE, AND ONLY THOSE THREE.** The row says the 2%/5% stops were illustrative and that the real unreachable set is a function of live ATR per symbol, "not established here". It is established now for GLD/SPY/QQQ: these refusals came from the legs' OWN `atr_stop_mult x ATR` geometry, at the real balance, on the real account — no assumed stop width stands between the finding and the evidence. **IWM produced no row in this window and therefore stays UNCONFIRMED** — an absent row is not evidence the symbol would size; it is evidence we did not observe it.

**The other 18 rows are a different refusal and must not be read as the same finding.** TLT (9) and SLV (3) sized to **qty 2.0** and were then refused by `account_mode_dry_run` — the sizer succeeded and the execution gate stopped them. Six more carry `sized_qty=0 with balance=0.10`, an earlier and different balance state. So the split is: the expensive symbols fail SIZING, the cheap ones failed the MODE gate. Two shares of TLT at 82.93-83.22 is ~$166, i.e. **~83% of the whole account in one trade** — the cash balance, not `risk_pct`, is what clamped it (at `risk_pct` 0.05 the demanded size is ~26.7 shares / ~11x the account; realised risk at the declared stop is therefore ~$0.75, not the $10 the 5% implies).

**WHY THESE REFUSALS WERE SILENT, AND THE CONDITION UNDER WHICH THEY STOP BEING (read from code, not observed firing).** `src/core/coordinator.py:1870` applies the suppression token under `if effective_dry:` — `error_msg = f"dry_run_sizing_skip: {error_msg}"`. All 23 rows predate the 2026-08-29 flip, so the account was effective-dry and the suppression is CORRECT on every one of them. On a genuinely live account the same `sized_qty=0` refusal does **not** get the prefix, so `execution_diagnostics.is_expected_dispatch_skip` returns False and `dead_leg.bucket_for` grades it a real refusal.

⚠️ **BUT THAT DOES NOT MEAN "one page per unsizeable signal", and the narrower statement is the true one.** `silent_refusal_alert` fires only on verdict `signalled_never_placed`, which requires EVERY gradeable row in the window to be refused — an account that placed even one order never alerts, however rare the cause. So the hazard is **not** a leg-level per-signal page; it is a WINDOW-level one: a roster whose legs are all unsizeable, or a 24h window that happens to contain only signals from the unsizeable symbols, reads all-refused and pages. That is live for the FULL 16-leg roster (7 of the 16 legs carry SPY/QQQ/GLD/IWM) and is NOT live for a single sizeable leg such as `tlt_pullback_1h`. Recorded because the broad version of this claim was drafted first and was wrong; the check that corrected it is the `verdict == signalled_never_placed` precondition.

**ONE CLAUSE ABOVE IS NOW STALE.** This row says "INERT TODAY ... `alpaca_live` is `mode: dry_run`". Read from the field 2026-08-29 (`config/accounts.yaml:825`), the account is **`mode: live`**, held flat solely by `strategies: []`. What is inert is the ROUTING, not the mode — and the surrounding comment block at `config/accounts.yaml:813` still reads "mode: dry_run (CI-guarded)", which contradicts line 825 twelve lines below it. Field beats comment; the comment is the thing to fix.

**OPERATOR DECISIONS TAKEN 2026-08-29 AGAINST THIS EVIDENCE** (recorded so the next session does not re-litigate them): plumbing-test leg = **`tlt_pullback_1h`**; per-trade notional cap = **100%, no cap beyond the cash account's own 1.0x limit**; **`risk_pct` stays 0.05**; sequencing = read the cash-settlement soak, flip `ALPACA_CASH_SETTLEMENT_MODE` to `apply` on `alpaca_live` only, and route the leg last. The cap and `risk_pct` answers deliberately leave the cash balance as the sole clamp, which the measured qty-2.0 rows show is what has been happening in practice.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) the per-strategy stop widths are derived so the unreachable set is exact rather than illustrative, and the funding level is chosen with that set in front of the operator; OR (b) `alpaca_live` is funded above the level at which its declared roster is sizeable; OR (c) the roster is narrowed to the symbols a $200 account can actually trade, so the config stops declaring 16 strategies of which several can never place an order. Closing this by noting the account is `mode: dry_run` is NOT sufficient — that makes it dormant, not resolved.
items.evidence: config/accounts.yaml::alpaca_live (risk block + 16 strategies + 11 symbols + mode: dry_run); src/units/accounts/risk.py::WHOLE_UNIT_QTY_EXCHANGES; /api/bot/candles 1d closes for 10 of 11 symbols on 2026-08-26; OO-20260825-ALPACA-LIVE-DAILY-USD-200-DECISION

updates.note: Re-validated: at $200, 4 of 10 priced symbols cannot be sized at all. Part of the alpaca_live cluster — live balance confirmed $200.10 with zero positions and zero gross notional across 1,848 exposure samples.

items.title: IBClient._open_trades swallows the read exception and returns [] -- every caller reads 'we could not look' as 'no orders rest'
items.detail:
`IBClient._open_trades` is four lines: `try: return list(ib.openTrades() or []) except Exception: return []`. That is the exact producer shape `silent-empty-guard` exists to catch -- a broad except returning `[]` -- and it sits under at least three protective-path callers: `_cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol`, `_cancel_oca_group_for_symbol`, and (until this change) the new stray-group sweep.

FOUND BY A TEST, NOT BY INSPECTION. Writing `test_read_failure_is_not_evidence_of_no_strays` for the new sweep, the assertion `read_state == 'could_not_look'` failed with `'legs_read'`: the sweep's own try/except could never fire because the helper had already turned the raised read into an empty list. The sweep now calls `ib.openTrades()` directly so the two states stay distinct; the HELPER is unchanged and every other caller still collapses.

WHY IT IS NOT MERELY COSMETIC FOR THE CANCEL PATHS. On a cancel path an empty read means 'cancel nothing', which is fail-safe in isolation. But `_cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol` then compares `account_wide_seen > seen` to decide whether to warn that legs are resting this session cannot cancel -- with `seen` forced to 0 by a swallowed read, that comparison is being made against a denominator that was never measured, and the method returns `cancelled: 0` which its own docstring says a caller must be able to distinguish from 'could not see a single leg'. The docstring claims that distinction is what the counts provide; the helper removes it one level down.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any live incident traced back to this. It is a latent collapse found while building on top of it, filed rather than fixed because changing a shared helper on the IB order path is Tier-2 and wants its own review of all callers.
evidence: src/units/accounts/ib_client.py::IBClient._open_trades -- `except Exception: return []`
tests/test_ib_stray_group_sweep.py::test_read_failure_is_not_evidence_of_no_strays -- failed 'legs_read' != 'could_not_look' against the helper, passes against a direct ib.openTrades() call

src/units/accounts/ib_client.py::_cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol docstring -- 'cancelled every leg' and 'could not see a single leg' were the same observable outcome ... This now reports counts so a caller can tell them apart
items.resolution_criteria: Make the read three-state at the HELPER (`orders` / `could_not_look` / `empty`) or give it a sibling that raises, then update every caller to branch on it -- `_cancel_resting_orders_for_symbol` and `_cancel_oca_group_for_symbol` at minimum. Ends when a forced `openTrades()` failure makes each of those callers report a read failure rather than a clean zero, asserted by a test per caller. Registering the state with `collapsed-state-guard` is the durable half.

updates.note: Re-validated: _open_trades swallowing the exception and returning [] so every caller reads 'we could not look' as 'no orders'. Textbook collapsed state on the IB protection path, and CLAUDE.md records stray_oca_groups deliberately bypassing it for that reason — so the workaround exists at one call site and the defect remains.

items.title: The MGC over-cover was not merely a hazard -- a stray group's duplicate LIMIT partially FILLED, and the resulting 1-contract journal/exchange divergence is invisible to every IB detector
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-26, ib_paper/MGC, all from FRESH-CLIENT reads (the diag route is excluded as stale per BL-20260826-DIAG-IB-OPEN-ORDERS-SERVES-A-STALE-MONOTONIC-ORDER-VIEW).

WHAT HAPPENED. Trade 5007 (ict_scalp_mgc_15m, short 51 @ 4660.9) carried TWO protective groups: the journal-matching `oca-protect-t5007` (STP BUY 51 @ 4653.9 / LMT BUY 51 @ 4602.4, clientId 497) and the stray `834864174` (STP BUY 50 @ 4699.9 / LMT BUY 51 @ 4602.4, clientId 597). BOTH groups held an identical LMT BUY 51 @ 4602.4, and OCA cancels only WITHIN a group. The cancel-ib-order APPLY run (#10349) read the stray limit as `filled: 1.0, remaining: 50.0` -- so it had ALREADY begun filling. The over-cover class is therefore not purely prospective on this account; it has produced an unintended fill.

THE RESIDUE, AND IT IS THE PART NOTHING WATCHES. `/api/diag/exchange_positions` now reads MGC **short 50** while `trades` row 5007 still reads `position_size 51.0`. The surviving `oca-protect-t5007` therefore rests 51 of stop and 51 of target against a 50 position -- 51/50 = 102% of the position it protects -- so a stop fire over-closes by one contract into a naked LONG 1.

WHY NO DETECTOR SEES IT. (a) The IB over-cover page (`_emit_stop_over_cover_alert`) keys on DISJOINT OCA GROUPS; with the stray group now gone there is exactly ONE group, so it will not fire on a single group at 51/50 = 102%. (b) `journal_qty_divergent` -- the detector that compares summed open journal rows against the netted exchange size -- is implemented in `_check_broker_naked_bybit_positions` and is **Bybit-only**; the IB sweep has no equivalent. So an IB journal/exchange quantity divergence has no detector at all, which is the same shape as the Bybit-only gap `_emit_bybit_over_cover_alert` was added for one day earlier.

STATE THE POPULATION: one account (ib_paper, PAPER -- no real money), one symbol, one contract of divergence. The SIZE is trivial; the CLASS is not, because the same mechanism on a real-money netted account would diverge silently and un-detected.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the reconciler will converge trade 5007 to 50 on its own, and how many other IB rows currently diverge from their exchange size -- nobody has ever measured that, because nothing computes it.

=== MEASURED 2026-08-26T21:05Z, ~1h25m after the fill: THE DIVERGENCE STANDS. The reconciler did NOT converge it. ===
Both sides read in the same minute. Exchange (/api/diag/exchange_positions?account_id=ib_paper): MGC short 50.0. Journal (/api/bot/db/table/trades, status=eq=open, filter_state 'applied' ASSERTED, total 25): trade 5007 position_size 51.0, status open. So the 'NOT ESTABLISHED' above is now ESTABLISHED in the negative -- this does not self-heal on the ~1.4h timescale, and nothing has closed or amended the row.

CONTROL, so this is not read as a broad journal fault: the other two open IB rows agree with the exchange EXACTLY in the same read -- MHG 29.0/29.0 and MES 15.0/15.0. The divergence is specific to the row whose stray leg filled.

AND THE PROTECTION DID NOT RE-ARM DOWN EITHER. /api/diag/ib_open_orders (read_state 'orders_read', 6 orders) shows the surviving journal-matching group oca-protect-t5007 STILL resting STP BUY 51 @ 4653.9 + LMT BUY 51 @ 4602.4 against a 50 position -- 51/50 = 102% of the position it protects. A stop fire therefore over-closes by one contract into a naked LONG 1. Confirmed in the same read: the stray group 834864174 is GONE (no order carries it), so the cancel held.

WHY NOTHING PAGED, restated with the evidence now in hand: the IB over-cover page keys on DISJOINT OCA GROUPS and there is exactly ONE group here, so a single group at 102% is structurally invisible to it; and journal_qty_divergent -- the detector that would compare the summed open journal rows against the netted exchange size -- exists only in _check_broker_naked_bybit_positions. Two detectors, neither covering this.

STATE THE POPULATION: one account (ib_paper, PAPER -- no real money), one symbol, one contract, one point-in-time read at 21:05Z against a fill that landed before 19:38Z. The SIZE is trivial and is not the finding; the finding is that an IB journal/exchange quantity divergence persisted for over an hour with no surface reporting it. STILL NOT ESTABLISHED: how many other IB rows diverge -- that needs the detector this row asks for, because nothing computes it.
evidence: issue #10349 (APPLY) -- order 422 LMT BUY 51 @ 4602.4, oca_group 834864174, filled 1.0, remaining 50.0
issue #10350 / #10351 (fresh-client DRY RUNs) -- orders 422 and 423 both lookup_state not_found, orders_on_account 8 -> 6
/api/diag/exchange_positions?account_id=ib_paper 2026-08-26T19:50Z -- MGC short 50.0
/api/bot/db/table/trades filter_state=applied -- trade 5007 position_size 51.0, status open
src/runtime/order_monitor.py -- journal_qty_divergent lives in _check_broker_naked_bybit_positions only
items.resolution_criteria: Two separable halves. (1) DETECTION: give the IB sweep the journal-vs-exchange quantity comparison its Bybit sibling already has, so a divergence is observable at all; ends when a deliberately divergent IB row is reported on a surface a human reads, asserted by a test. (2) THIS ROW: trade 5007 reads the same size as the exchange, or is closed, verified from a fresh client -- and the decision on how to reconcile it (the fill was real, so the exit price and 1-lot pnl are a MEASURED broker fact that should not be discarded) is recorded rather than silently applied. Do NOT resolve (2) by editing the row to 50 without accounting for the filled contract.

updates.note: ⚠️ HIGH AND IT ELEVATES THE WHOLE OVER-COVER FAMILY FROM HAZARD TO REALISED LOSS: a stray group's duplicate LIMIT partially FILLED and the journal never learned. That is no longer a theoretical 'whichever fires second opens an unintended position' — it happened. This should be read alongside BL-20260825-PLACE-PROTECTIVE-COUNTS-THE-CANCEL-CALL-NOT-ITS-EFFECT (the root cause) as the strongest argument for prioritising that fix.

items.title: config/strategies.yaml told every future session the prop gate is a LOWER bar that licenses strategies which lose real money -- the opposite of the design standard, and the operator caught it being repeated back
items.detail: OPERATOR-FLAGGED 2026-08-27: 'Your statement that the prop account strategies have looser risk management or lower standards is wrong - and if that is how it is framed in our documentation, then we have a serious problem.' It was. The exact string 'this is "+EV to buy accounts and run this", NOT "this is safe"' sat in THREE committed places -- config/strategies.yaml:1194 (trend_donchian_sol_prop execution comment), :1240 (trend_donchian_eth_prop), and docs/sprint-logs/S-M20-EXIT-COVERAGE-MATRIX-2026-08-12.md:1123 -- all traceable to one session on 2026-08-12/13. A session reading the execution: line of a live prop leg (the most-read comment on that leg) was told the prop book is where sub-real-money strategies go. THE DESIGN SAYS THE OPPOSITE: prop-dynamic-exits-faster-banking-DESIGN.md section 6 requires 'higher mean_net_usd/p_profitable AT EQUAL-OR-BETTER SURVIVAL' and 'strict improvement WITHOUT WORSE p_breach'. The intended standard is that the prop RISK MANAGER and the backtest both model the prop rules so the sleeve stays profitable long enough to clear the fee -- not that a worse strategy is acceptable because an account costs $45. THE INFERENCE WAS ALSO UNSOUND ON ITS OWN TERMS: it read a standard-account 'skip' as evidence against the leg, and that skip is ungradeable for three independent reasons (see BL-20260827-STANDARD-ARM-MISMODELS-INTRADAY-MAX-DD-AS-A-TERMINAL-FLOOR). Corroborating evidence that the legs are NOT weak: BL-20260823-PROP-COMPAT-SOL-TWIN-INVERTED measured trend_donchian_sol at EV +$1,162 / P(net>0) 0.9137 and trend_donchian_eth_prop at +$2,074 / 0.9700 on the breakout_1 ruleset, seed-stable. THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON: a comment on an execution: line is not documentation, it is the instruction the next Tier-3 decision reads. A governance doctrine ('prop is where lower-bar strategies go') was created as a byproduct of writing up one gate run, and it survived two weeks and a full-system audit because nothing checks a comment against the design doc it cites.
items.resolution_criteria: All three sites corrected (done 2026-08-27 in this PR for the two strategies.yaml sites; the sprint-log site is a historical record and is annotated rather than rewritten), AND a session that reads either prop leg's execution: comment reports the design standard (strict improvement at equal-or-better survival) rather than the buy-accounts framing. A doc-coherence check that compares a cited design doc's stated gate against the comment citing it would close the class, not just the instance.

updates.note: ⚠️ HIGH AND DOCTRINALLY BACKWARDS — re-validated. A config comment telling every future session the prop gate is a LOWER bar, licensing strategies that lose real money, on the ONE account that can be permanently destroyed and is currently $55 from that. This is a documentation defect with a live-risk consequence and it is cheap to fix.

items.title: account_compat_matrix's STANDARD arm grades a real account's INTRA-DAY, resets-at-midnight, refuses-one-trade max_dd_pct as a PERMANENT account-killing floor off a synthetic $10,000 balance -- so every standard-account verdict on the real-money promotion path is ungraded, not negative
items.detail: Found while answering the operator's question 'why is a SOL strategy on prop but not on bybit_2'. THREE COMPOUNDING ERRORS, each read from the field, not from prose. (1) WRONG RISK SEMANTICS. src/prop/account_rulesets.py::_standard_ruleset feeds the account's max_dd_pct into LimitRules with drawdown_type='static' -- a permanent floor a fixed fraction below the STARTING balance, treated as terminal. src/units/accounts/risk.py line 21 defines that same field as 'max INTRA-DAY equity drawdown from today's high', and the accounts.yaml header says 'intra-day, UTC midnight reset'. Breaching it REFUSES A TRADE; it never disables the account. Two axes inverted at once: intraday->permanent, from-todays-high->from-start. (2) SYNTHETIC BALANCE. account_size_usd falls back to _DEFAULT_STANDARD_SIZE = $10,000 whenever the risk block omits it, which is every standard account today; bybit_2's measured real balance is ~$296.59 (workplan fact 10). (3) THE VERDICT IS THEN GATED HARD ON THOSE NUMBERS: ROUTE requires survival >= 0.90 AND p_breach <= 0.10 against that model. STATE THE POPULATION on the arithmetic: a simplified independent-trial simulation (4,000 paths, 1.5% risk/trade, equity ever <= 0.95*start, no block-bootstrap and no autocorrelation, so NOT the engine's own model) gives p_breach 0.484 at 40% win / 2R over 602 trades and 0.086 at 55% win / 2R. So the gate is NOT arithmetically unreachable -- an excellent strategy can pass -- but a perfectly respectable trend-follower fails it, and it fails on a rule the account does not have. CONSEQUENCE: the standard column of every compat-matrix run to date should be read as UNGRADED. It has been cited at least once (BL-20260803-GLD-ALPACA-PORTFOLIO-SURVIVAL-SKIP quotes survival 0.871 < 0.90 as a routing finding) and once as the basis of a governance doctrine (BL-20260827-PROP-GATE-DOCUMENTED-AS-A-LOWER-BAR-THAN-REAL-MONEY). NOT FIXED IN PLACE, deliberately: correcting the mapping changes gate verdicts on the real-money promotion path, so it is Tier-3 research, not a doc edit. Documented at the call site instead.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) _standard_ruleset models max_dd_pct with the semantics risk.py gives it -- a resetting intraday brake that refuses a trade -- and a re-run shows what the standard column says under the corrected model for the legs already cited from it; or (b) the standard arm is retired and replaced with the net-of-fee performance gate the module docstring already claims it is ('its compatibility test is the ordinary net-of-fee performance backtest'). Either way, every prior standard-column citation is re-graded or withdrawn. A row that merely documents the mismatch does NOT close this.

items.title: aggregate_intents picks ONE winner per SYMBOL globally, before account fan-out -- so a prop-ONLY leg wins the SOLUSDT slot and bybit_1 receives nothing, and trend_donchian_sol has 120 buy signals and ZERO journal rows in seven weeks with no detector covering it
items.detail: MEASURED, not inferred. trend_donchian_sol was routed to bybit_1 on 2026-07-07 with the explicit note that it had 'no paper soak, violating every non-downgraded strategy soaks on a paper account'. Since that date it has produced ZERO rows in trade_journal.db of ANY status -- not one fill, not one rejection. Its only 7 rows are all breakout_1 and all pre-date 07-07. It is not silent: the audit shows 120 buy signals since 2026-08-01 at confidence 1.0, and its entry-identical prop twin trend_donchian_sol_prop shows 137 over the same window at the same ticks. MECHANISM: intent_multiplexer runs aggregate_intents(intents, symbol=...), which collapses to ONE DesiredPosition per SYMBOL across ALL strategies, and intents_to_signal_packages states the scope explicitly -- 'intents are not account-bound at the multiplexer (account fan-out happens downstream in Coordinator.multi_account_execute)'. Six strategies contend for SOLUSDT, all at DEFAULT_PRIORITIES 0. Measured winners on event=pipeline_result, side=buy, 2026-08-01..08-27, n=60: ict_scalp_sol_5m 23, trend_donchian_sol_prop 15, ict_scalp_sol_15m 14, trend_donchian_sol_4h 6, trend_donchian_sol ZERO. On the 15 ticks the PROP-ONLY twin wins, the winner routes to breakout_1 alone and bybit_1 gets nothing -- although nothing on bybit_1 was contending for that slot. So a prop-only variant is consuming the paper account's capacity to accrue the record its own real-money promotion requires. THE CODE COMMENT ASSERTS THE OPPOSITE and is corrected in this PR: intent_multiplexer.py read 'Each is sole on its (symbol, prop-account) so arbitration never fires', which reasons about a (symbol, ACCOUNT) scope the aggregator does not have. NOTHING DETECTS IT, and that is the durable half: silent_refusal_alert grades journal rows and zero rows is its 'we observed nothing -- never graded, never alerts' bucket; the strategy-silence check reads *_eval events, which are present and healthy. A strategy can signal 120 times a month, journal nothing, and leave every green light green.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH: (a) a detector exists for 'strategy emitted actionable intents over a window and produced zero journal rows on an account it is routed to' -- the state between 'evaluating' and 'refused' that no current alert covers; and (b) a Tier-3 decision is recorded on the arbitration scope, either making aggregation account-aware (so a prop-only leg cannot consume a paper account's slot) or explicitly accepting the starvation with the reason stated. Re-adding a strategy to an account's list does NOT close it -- trend_donchian_sol was already added and stayed at zero for seven weeks.

items.title: RECURRENCE (third) of BL-20260813-ENV-VARS-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE: eight governance env vars shipped 2026-08-13..08-26 with no get_env allowlist row, including the one deciding whether a prop ticket that exceeds the account's cushion is capped
items.detail: FILED AS A RECURRENCE, NOT A DISCOVERY -- that the earlier fix did not hold IS the finding. get_env.py's own comment already records the second occurrence as 'self-inflicted on the same day' (PROP_SCREENSHOT_BACKEND, 2026-08-23, allowlisted in the same session that missed it). Measured 2026-08-27 against ALLOWED_KEYS (55 keys at the time): PROP_TICKET_RISK_GATE_MODE, PROTECTION_STRAY_GROUP_MODE, PROTECTION_STRAY_GROUP_ACCOUNTS, BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS, IB_PROBE_CACHE_S, IB_SESSION_CHECK_DISABLED, IB_CLOSE_OUTSIDE_RTH, PROP_STATUS_REQUEST_MAX_AGE_HOURS -- all MISSING, all governing live behaviour, none a secret. The sharpest is PROP_TICKET_RISK_GATE_MODE: on 2026-08-27 breakout_1 sat $64.00 from its $4,700 static-DD floor with an open ticket risking $90.12, so whether that mode is annotate or enforce is the difference between a warning and a permanently disabled account -- and it could not be read from outside. PROTECTION_STRAY_GROUP_ACCOUNTS matters for the same reason its PROTECTION_REASSERT_ sibling was allowlisted on day one: its EMPTY value means NONE, inverted from its other siblings where empty means ALL, so 'unset' and 'armed everywhere' are the same blank. Keys added in this PR (63 now), which fixes the instance. THE CLASS IS NOT FIXED: three occurrences in fourteen days means the allowlist row is not part of shipping a key, and the only thing that would make it so is a check.
items.resolution_criteria: A CI guard that fails when a module reads an env var matching the governance shape (a *_MODE / *_DISABLED / *_ACCOUNTS / *_ENABLED / cadence-or-threshold constant consulted on a live path) and that name is absent from get_env.ALLOWED_KEYS, with an explicit per-key exemption list for anything genuinely secret. Same family as canonical-db-resolver / env-gate-guard / provenance-consumer-guard. Adding the eight keys does NOT close this -- that is the instance, and the instance has now been fixed three times.

items.title: RECURRENCE, generalised: the M20 coverage matrix grades 468 cells at a MEDIAN OOS base of 33 trades, so 70.3% honest_negative is largely 'we could not tell' rather than 'the lever does not help' -- and the identical finding was filed for ONE lever column 13 days ago and never carried across
items.detail: FILED AS A RECURRENCE. BL-20260814-EXIT-HEAD-E1-GATE-IS-90-PERCENT-PREDICTED-BY-OOS-BOOK-SIZE-NOT-SYMBOL (still kept_open) already concluded, for the exit_head_ml column alone, that 'a gate whose outcome is 90% predicted by book size is substantially a POWER TEST' -- book size classified the verdict at 90.0% accuracy, PASS median 600 vs FAIL median 168, and 16 of 36 resolved cells stated no denominator at all. That was filed for 1 of 9 lever columns, kept open, and never generalised. MEASURED FLEET-WIDE 2026-08-27 over docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json (52 legs x 9 levers = 468 cells, arithmetic reconciles exactly). STATUS SPLIT: honest_negative 329 (70.3%), n/a 36, blocked 32, shipped 22, passed_unshipped 22, pending 20, shipped_gate_failed 7. POPULATION FOR THE POWER READ -- the 113 cells whose `ref` PROSE states an IS/OOS base count: median OOS 33 trades, 107/113 = 94.7% under 50, 111/113 = 98.2% under 100, min 4, max 145. ONLY 96 OF THE 329 honest_negative CELLS STATE A COUNT AT ALL (29%) -- the headline is computed over cells most of which carry no denominator anywhere. UNITS WARNING, load-bearing: the 08-14 row's n_oos counts PER-BAR dataset rows (an ML head's input); the 33 here counts OOS TRADES (a hard-lever sweep's base). Different quantities, not one series -- do not merge them. WHY 33 CANNOT ANSWER THE QUESTION: an exit lever moves the TAIL, firing on a minority of trades, while the gate asks for improvement in net_R AND maxDD in BOTH IS and OOS; at 33 OOS the sampling error is the order of any realistic lever effect. THE GATE KNOWS THE SHAPE AND STOPS SHORT: MIN_OOS_TRADES=25 exists with its own insufficient_base verdict, but the floor sits 8 trades BELOW the median of the population it grades (2 cells carry insufficient_base against a median of 33), and exit-refinement/SKILL.md itself records the real gap -- 'the floor is a PROXY for what actually matters, the trades the LEVER fired on ... Per-cell fire counts are not recorded'. THE ERRORS RUN BOTH WAYS, which is why this is not an argument that the levers work: spy_trend_long_1d vt_hot90_t2 PASSED on 3 OOS trades with a 6/6 walk-forward and a delta-maxDD of EXACTLY 0.0 -- a difference of exactly zero is the cell announcing the lever never fired. So neither the 329 negatives nor the 22 passes are trustworthy as they stand. VOCABULARY GAP: the matrix legend defines seven statuses each with a written justification (including shipped_gate_failed, added precisely so a live-but-lapsed lever cannot be absorbed into a neighbour) and is missing exactly one -- honest_negative is defined as 'tested, failed the gate' and there is NO state for 'tested, and the test had no power'. Those call for opposite follow-ups and are today the same cell colour. Same collapsed-state class the repo polices for fields, applied to a verdict.
items.resolution_criteria: ALL of: (a) per-cell LEVER-FIRE count recorded (how many trades the lever actually modified) -- the real denominator, named as an open gap by the skill itself; (b) an effect-vs-noise test in the gate, so a verdict requires the effect to exceed its own sampling error and not merely carry the right sign; (c) an `underpowered` status distinct from `honest_negative`, and THE MATRIX RE-GRADED under it -- a large share of the 329 is expected to move; (d) the base count promoted from prose to a STRUCTURED field, since 71% of negatives state none. Adding the status without re-grading does NOT close this. Until (a)-(d), the 70.3%-negative headline must not be cited as evidence that exits do not matter for these strategies.
