Read together with BL-20260814-1D-EQUITY-LEGS-TRADE-4-PER-YEAR-SO-PER-LEG-OOS-25-CONSUMES-6-YEARS (the trade rate caps the OOS window) this says the program is measuring what it CAN measure rather than what it needs to.

items.title: ROOT CAUSE of the standard-arm defect: PropRuleset offers only `static` and `trailing` drawdown, neither of which is a standard account's intraday resetting brake, so _standard_ruleset absorbed the new concept into the nearest member and produced a confident wrong number instead of an error
items.detail: ARCHAEOLOGY, answering the operator's question 'why was it built that way, was it actually built wrong'. IT WAS BUILT RIGHT, THEN EXTENDED BY REUSING AN ADJACENT TOOL WHOSE SEMANTICS DID NOT MATCH. ORIGINAL DESIGN (docs/integrations/prop-accounts-architecture-DESIGN.md, 2026-06-17) states it twice: 'Real / paper broker accounts -> a standard ruleset (the account's own risk_pct, NO BREACH/ECONOMICS) -- for which the compatibility test is JUST THE ORDINARY NET-OF-FEE PERFORMANCE BACKTEST', and 'the standard case = a NO-BREACH ruleset with the account's risk'. That is still what the module docstring claims today. THE EXTENSION: the same doc records PB-20260618-012 (Daily/ETF Alpaca extension) deliberately tightening the gate 'beyond positive end-return' to add survival >= 0.90 AND P(breach) <= 0.10 'under the account's own soft limits', so 'a positive-but-fragile cell can't route onto live capital'. THAT INTENT IS SOUND AND MUST BE KEPT -- this row is NOT an argument to delete the survival gate. WHERE IT WENT WRONG: to compute survival the extension reused run_montecarlo + PropRuleset. PropRuleset.limits offers EXACTLY TWO drawdown shapes (ruleset.py:36): `static` (off the STARTING balance) and `trailing` (off the running PEAK). Neither expresses a standard account's max_dd_pct, so _standard_ruleset chose `static` -- the only member that parses. VERIFIED IN CODE, THREE SITES: evaluator.py:155 `ref = peak if dd_type == 'trailing' else account_size`; montecarlo.py:227 `floor = account_size * (1.0 - static_dd_pct)`, fixed and never re-referenced; montecarlo.py:291 `# once breached, the account is dead -- stop walking`. AGAINST WHAT THE FIELD MEANS IN PRODUCTION (risk.py:21 + the accounts.yaml header): 'max INTRA-DAY equity drawdown FROM TODAY'S HIGH', resetting at UTC midnight, whose breach REFUSES ONE TRADE and never disables the account. Three axes inverted at once: intraday->permanent, from-todays-high->from-start, refuses-a-trade->kills-the-account. INDEPENDENT SECOND DEFECT -- STATE THE POPULATION: account_size_usd falls back to _DEFAULT_STANDARD_SIZE = $10,000 (account_rulesets.py:43) whenever the account's `risk` block omits an explicit account_size_usd. Measured 2026-08-27 over ALL 11 accounts in config/accounts.yaml: ZERO declare account_size_usd in their `risk` block, and 10 of the 11 are non-prop (only breakout_1 is prop), so the $10,000 substitution applies to 10 of 10 standard accounts -- 100%, not a corner case. Against it, bybit_2's real balance measured from balance_snapshots (n=2,986 rows, full history, workplan fact 10) is ~$296.59 -- the synthetic notional is ~34x the account. run_montecarlo compounds risk_pct against that fictional figure, so both the drawdown floor (account_size * (1 - static_dd_pct)) and every per-trade size in the simulated path are scaled to an account that does not exist. WHY NO GUARD FIRED: the field is called max_dd_pct on BOTH sides -- the name matched, the semantics did not -- and diagnostic-provenance-guard covers scripts/{ml,research,ops,macro,reports}/, so src/prop/ is outside its scope. CLASS: CLAUDE.md 'Diagnostic provenance' sub-class A ('the label names quantity Q; the code called accessor f(); f() != Q'), whose canonical instance is max(proba) printed as P(volatile). THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON: a type system with no member for a new concept will silently absorb it into the nearest existing member. An enum that CANNOT represent the new rule is a compile-time question; one that APPROXIMATELY can is a silent wrong answer years later.
items.resolution_criteria: A THIRD drawdown shape (or a distinct standard-account limit type) expressing 'intraday, from today's high, resets daily, refuses a trade rather than killing the account', so p_breach becomes 'probability this cell trips the daily brake' and is NOT terminal; PLUS a real account size or an explicit refusal to grade rather than a $10,000 substitution; PLUS every prior standard-column citation re-graded or withdrawn (at least one exists: BL-20260803-GLD-ALPACA-PORTFOLIO-SURVIVAL-SKIP quotes survival 0.871 < 0.90 as a routing finding). Deleting the survival gate does NOT close this -- the fragility question it asks is legitimate and is the only thing standing between a fragile cell and live capital.

items.title: 50 of 105 doc_only scripts are under scripts/research/ and none declares whether it is a finished one-shot, a capability to wire, or manual-only -- so a session cannot tell a retired study from a capability that quietly stopped being called
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-27 by running scripts/ci/check_unwired_artifacts.py --dirs scripts: 2 unwired, 105 doc_only, 9 skill_invoked. Of the 105 doc_only ('referenced ONLY by docs -- documented, but nothing runs it'), 50 sit under scripts/research/. ⚠️ STATE WHAT THIS IS NOT: doc_only does NOT mean broken and does NOT mean never ran. Many are legitimately one-shot studies that ran once, produced a memo and are correctly finished -- filing them as rot would be the error. THE FINDING IS NARROWER AND IS THE CHECK'S OWN FRAMING: each entry is 'a corpse to remove, a capability to WIRE, or a tool that must declare # wiring: manual-only', and NONE OF THE 50 HAS DECLARED WHICH. The cost is exactly the operator's stated complaint ('we keep tripping over ourselves'): a session reading scripts/research/ cannot distinguish a finished study from a live capability that stopped being called, so it re-derives or rebuilds. Compare RC-BUILT-A-MECHANISM-THAT-ALREADY-EXISTED, and the 2026-08-26 incident where a session wrote scripts/ci/check_test_schema_fidelity.py from scratch over an existing working one. The remedy is one line per file, not a rewrite.
items.resolution_criteria: Every scripts/research/ entry in check_unwired_artifacts' doc_only bucket either (a) deleted, (b) given a runner, or (c) carrying a `# wiring: manual-only -- <who runs it, when>` declaration -- and the check extended to FAIL on an undeclared research script rather than only listing it, so the class cannot silently regrow.

items.title: filed != propagated: three documented harness defects all inherited by the 468-cell M20 coverage matrix, none of them visible in it -- the matrix is read as clean evidence while every caveat sits correctly filed somewhere else
items.detail: THE MECHANISM BEHIND THE OPERATOR'S 2026-08-27 COMPLAINT ('we keep tripping over ourselves'). This repo is unusually good at FINDING and FILING defects and has NO mechanism for carrying a filed defect into the artifacts that already inherited it. Three independent, correctly-documented defects all land on docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json -- the artifact every active-management decision is read from -- and NONE of them appears in it, in its legend, or beside the verdicts that inherit them. (1) POWER: measured 2026-08-27 over the 113 cells whose ref states a base count, median OOS 33 trades, 94.7% under 50; only 96 of 329 honest_negative cells state a count at all. Filed as BL-20260827-EXIT-COVERAGE-MATRIX-IS-SUBSTANTIALLY-A-POWER-TEST-FLEET-WIDE, and itself a recurrence of BL-20260814-EXIT-HEAD-E1-GATE-IS-90-PERCENT-PREDICTED-BY-OOS-BOOK-SIZE-NOT-SYMBOL, which said the same thing for ONE of nine lever columns 13 days earlier and never generalised. (2) RISK BASIS: scripts/ci/check_risk_basis_agreement.py reports 'clean' while holding a KNOWN_DIVERGENCES table of ACCEPTED ratios whose own comment reads 'These are DEBT: each one is a harness whose default answer is about a risk setting production does not use'. Measured: 10 registered sites; scripts/backtest_system.py -- THE FLEET ENGINE -- sits at ratio 0.2, i.e. a 0.3% default against live 1.5%. Green means the ratio is REGISTERED, not that it is small. (3) QUANTIZATION: backtest_system.py:1752 states in its own words that _risk_qty returns a CONTINUOUS quantity with 'no whole-contract floor, no min_qty, no margin cap', that production REFUSES sub-1-contract futures orders outright, and that 'the error is FLATTERING'. Filed as BL-20260820-HARNESS-DOES-NOT-MODEL-QUANTIZATION-REFUSAL. (2) AND (3) COMPOUND: the usual 'it is R-normalised so risk does not matter' defence assumes the TRADE SET is invariant to risk, which at 1/5 live risk with no refusal model it is not -- a point exit-refinement/SKILL.md section 7 already makes and which has never been applied to the matrix. NOTE WHAT THIS ROW IS NOT: it is not a claim that any of the three is undocumented or that anyone was careless. Each is recorded honestly at its own source, which is why the failure is structural rather than individual. A FOURTH INSTANCE IN THIS SESSION, showing the class is live: this audit's own phase 1 repeated audit F-37..F-40's '100x risk_pct unit' claim as an open concern; verifying it showed it had been FIXED (src/research/risk_basis.py single owner + a registered, passing CI guard). A stale caveat propagated into a fresh memo in the same session that the propagation gap was being described.
items.resolution_criteria: A mechanical propagation step, NOT another guard on the producer: when a backlog row is filed against a research tool, the artifacts that tool produced inherit a visible caveat IN THE ARTIFACT. Concretely for the instance -- exit-refinement-coverage.json carries a machine-readable `known_caveats` block naming the rows that condition its verdicts (power, risk basis, quantization), a reader of any cell can see them, and the check that renders the matrix FAILS if a row filed against its producing harness is absent from that block. Fixing the three underlying defects does NOT close this row: the class is the missing propagation, and a fourth defect filed tomorrow must reach the artifact without anyone remembering to carry it.

items.title: CORRECTED SAME DAY -- the pattern is TWO instances, not three: the e35 instance I filed was MY error (I probed the wrong store), and the correction is the more useful finding. A run exiting 0 is still treated as done in the two that survive
items.detail: ⚠️ THIS ROW WAS FILED WITH THREE INSTANCES AND ONE WAS WRONG. Corrected within the hour, and the error is left visible because its mechanism is the transferable part. ORIGINAL TITLE: 'The research stack has moved compute to the right tool three times and failed to land the RESULT all three times -- a job exiting 0 is treated as done, and nothing asserts its rows arrived'. === THE RETRACTION === I claimed the e35 bracket sweep's rows never landed. THEY LANDED, ON MAIN, ON THE DAY THE SWEEP RAN. Measured: docs/research/e35-bracket-corpus.jsonl on origin/main holds 8,211 rows / 6,581 stop cells (sm*) / 41 legs, of which 4,378 carry sweep_generated_at 2026-08-26 -- the exact run I said produced nothing readable. === HOW I GOT IT WRONG, which is the lesson === I probed docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl for sm* cells, found ZERO, and called it absence. That file is the M20 LEVER corpus; e35 bracket cells go to a SEPARATE store, and its lack of stop cells is CORRECT. I anchored on that filename because BL-20260823-E35-SWEEP-EVIDENCE-HAS-NO-DURABLE-PATH's resolution_criteria SUGGESTED it ('Acceptable: an e35-shaped extractor writing into m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl'), and I never checked what the implementer actually chose. They chose a separate file, which is BETTER -- separate stores cannot silently merge, which was that row's own stated worry. So I read a resolution CRITERION as a description of the IMPLEMENTATION. ⚠️ AND MY NEGATIVE CONTROL DID NOT COVER IT. I verified the probe could find positives (--contains trail -> 212 rows) IN THAT FILE. That controls for the PROBE and not for the POPULATION. RULE ONE says a search returning nothing is not proof of absence and 'a negative needs a denominator' -- the denominator I owed was 'is this the store e35 writes to?', and I never asked it. A positive control in the wrong file is not a control. === WHAT SURVIVES, verified from the field rather than from a header comment === (1) trainer-offload-train.yml trains an OOM-prone manifest on a 4 vCPU / 16 GB runner and then does NOT register it: line 176 'Train the manifest on the 16 GB runner (--no-register)', line 184 --no-register, line 244 upload-artifact, and no git push and no registry write anywhere in the file. Its own header calls wiring the model back 'the documented v2 slice'. So the model trains and never joins the fleet. (2) The M20 coverage matrix: 468 verdicts whose conditioning defects live in the backlog rather than in the matrix -- established directly by adjudicating ~50 open producer-rows into it, not by inference. === WHAT THIS DOES TO THE THESIS === 'Compute is solved, landing is not' still holds on two instances, but it rested most heavily on the retracted one, and its priority relative to other work is now an operator call rather than something this row should assert. R2 (scripts/ci/assert_rows_landed.py) was built and merged partly on the retracted case; the tool is sound and instance (1) still justifies it, but it lost its strongest example and that is recorded here rather than left implied.
items.resolution_criteria: For the SURVIVING instances: a run's final step re-reads the committed results store FROM the shared ref and asserts its own rows are present, failing the job when they are not -- applied to trainer-offload-train (which today uploads an artifact and registers nothing) and to any sweep whose output a session is expected to read. The test is behavioural: a runner-trained model appears in the registry without a human moving it. ⚠️ AND THE CHECK MUST NAME THE STORE THE PRODUCER ACTUALLY WRITES TO, verified against the producer, not against a backlog row's suggestion -- that is exactly the mistake this row's own correction records.

items.title: 8 of the trainer's systemd units exist ONLY on the box and not in deploy/trainer/ -- including ict-trainer.timer, the daily training cycle itself, so the core schedule cannot be reviewed and does not survive the VM
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-27 by listing /etc/systemd/system/ict-*.{service,timer} on the trainer via the diag relay and diffing against deploy/trainer/ in the repo. ON-BOX AND UNDECLARED: ict-trainer.service + .timer (THE DAILY CYCLE, next fire Fri 00:53 UTC), ict-trainer-catchup.service + .timer (05:00), ict-trainer-publish.service + .timer (every 2 min -- the mirror that feeds /api/bot/ml/* and every ML review), ict-trainer-forecast.service + .timer. DECLARED AND FINE: ict-drift-retrain, ict-promotion-readiness, ict-orderflow-capture (deploy/trainer/), plus ict-trainer-git-sync (deploy/ root). So the four most load-bearing trainer units -- the cycle, its catchup, the mirror publisher and the forecast producer -- are undeclared. CONSEQUENCES, each real: the schedule cannot be code-reviewed; a cadence change on the box leaves no trace in git; and if the VM is lost or re-provisioned the training schedule is GONE, which is not hypothetical on a free-tier instance that has already been migrated once. The repo has scripts/ops/install_trainer_publish_units.sh, which suggests some units are written inline by a script rather than shipped as files -- that is the likely origin and is worth confirming when fixing. This is the same class as BL-20260813-ENV-VARS-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE one level up: the live configuration of a system is not readable from the repo that supposedly defines it.
items.resolution_criteria: All 8 units exist as files under deploy/trainer/, the installer applies them from those files rather than writing them inline, and a check compares the on-box unit set against deploy/trainer/ and fails on drift in EITHER direction (a unit on the box that the repo does not declare, and a declared unit not installed). Committing the files alone does NOT close it -- without the drift check the box and the repo diverge again silently.

items.title: The trainer is at 41G/45G with 4.0G free and the GC cannot help: 11G is market_features holding SEVEN pinned versions of one (symbol, timeframe), plus 1.1G of CUDA libraries on a CPU-only box
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-27 via the trainer diag relay. df: 41G used of 45G, 4.0G avail, 92%. The 28G repo tree breaks down as datasets-out 12G (market_features 11G, market_raw 1.3G), .venv 5.4G, ml/experiments-runs 4.7G, runtime_logs 3.3G (m20_exit_head 2.5G, m21_entry_head* ~560M), data 2.1G (trade_journal.db 1.0G, signal_audit.jsonl 660M). ROOT CAUSE OF THE 11G, and it explains why trainer_dataset_gc reclaims only 0.09G (BL-20260820-TRAINER-DATASET-GC-HAS-NO-CALLER): BTCUSDT/15m alone holds v002, v003, v004, v513, v514, v515, v520 -- SEVEN versions at ~390-480MB each, dated back to 2026-07-01 -- and 41 manifests PIN 111 of 115 version dirs. The old versions are not garbage; they are pinned. So this is a RETENTION-POLICY question (under what condition may a manifest's pin be released, and who re-pins it to a current version?), not a cleanup chore, and running a GC harder will not move it. SEPARATE AND CHEAPER: the 5.4G .venv contains libcublasLt.so.13 at 630MB and libtriton.so at 473MB -- CUDA/Triton libraries on a 1-OCPU CPU-only box, i.e. ~1.1G in two files the machine cannot execute, most likely a GPU torch build where the CPU-only wheel would do. That is the best space-to-risk ratio available and is independent of the pin question. CONTEXT for why the disk matters beyond the box: the Always-Free Ampere pool is FULL (trainer 1 + gateway 1 + live 2 = 4 of 4 OCPU, 24 of 24 GB), so the trainer's 1 OCPU / 6 GB is the only headroom that exists for growing trading ops.
items.resolution_criteria: THREE separable parts, and each closes on its own: (a) the CPU-only wheel replaces the CUDA build and df shows the reclaim; (b) a written retention policy states when a manifest's dataset pin may be released or re-pinned, and a measurement shows the version count per (symbol, timeframe) bounded by it; (c) the research byproduct trees (experiments-runs, m20_exit_head, m21_entry_head*) are published to a durable store and removed from the box, per BL-20260827-COMPUTE-IS-SOLVED-LANDING-IS-NOT-THREE-INSTANCES. Freeing space without (b) only resets the clock.

updates.note: RE-CONFIRMED AND IT IS THE ACTIONABLE HALF OF THE DISK PROBLEM: 11 G of market_features holding SEVEN pinned versions is not garbage, so no GC can touch it — the decision is which versions to unpin. That is a retention POLICY question for the operator, which is exactly how this review escalated it. Live re-measurement 2026-08-29: trainer at 91.7% used / 4.03 GB free of 48.28 GB, warning banner firing. ⚠️ This review RAISED the priority of the trainer-disk cluster after reading BL-20260829-ORDERFLOW-CAPTURE-IS-IRREPLACEABLE-AND-UNMONITORED: a full disk stops the ONE data stream that cannot be re-derived.

CORRECTION — part (a) of this row's own resolution_criteria is understated by 3.2x, and the correction is in the direction that MATTERS (more reclaim, not less). This row says the CUDA waste is "libcublasLt.so.13 at 630MB and libtriton.so at 473MB ... ~1.1G in two files". That counted TWO FILES; the measurement is of the PACKAGE TREES. Measured 2026-08-29 via trainer-vm-diag #10433, `du -x -d 1 -m .venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages`: nvidia 2875 MiB + triton 652 MiB = 3527 MiB = 3.44 GiB, with torch a further 435 MiB (a CPU-only torch wheel is materially smaller, so part of that is reducible too). STATE THE POPULATION: one `du` reading of one venv on the trainer, 2026-08-29T20:46Z, ondisk_sha 2ed2f211. WHY IT MATTERS: free space is 3.8 GiB, so this single action would take the box to ~7.2 GiB free — it roughly DOUBLES headroom (1.9x) and is the only item on the disk that is both large and carries no retention-policy question, because the machine is a 1-OCPU aarch64 Ampere VM with no CUDA device. NOTE THE PRECISE CLAIM: I verified the box has no GPU, NOT that the binaries fail to load — the nvidia-* wheels do publish aarch64 (sbsa) builds, so they may well load and simply find no device. Either way they are dead weight, but "cannot execute" would be an assertion I did not test; the falsifiable check is torch.cuda.is_available() returning False. NOT YET DONE and deliberately not done blind: torch/onnxruntime import paths must be shown to still work after the swap, since `transformers` (119 MiB) and `onnx`/`onnxruntime` are installed beside it and something may import torch at CPU inference time. The check is `python3 -c 'import torch; print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available())'` before and after.

items.tier: 2 to change (a live safety gate on an account-killer path); filing is Tier-1
items.title: The prop cushion counts UNREALIZED open profit as headroom and never subtracts the open positions' own stop-distance risk — so on 2026-08-27 the book survived both its stops by $0.28 on the panel's own basis, and was breached by $114.72 on a balance basis
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-27 on breakout_1 from the operator's terminal screenshot plus the live API immediately after ingesting it (snapshot id 14, as_of 2026-08-27T09:02:09Z, status_freshness 'ok' — so this is NOT the staleness class of BL-20260807 / BL-20260814).

POPULATION: the account's TWO open positions at that instant, and the one account-status row they were graded against. Terminal header (whole-dollar display): balance $4,761 · equity $4,876 · open P&L $115 · used margin $1,282. Positions: SOLUSD Buy 25.00 @ 99.94, SL 96.00, open P&L +116.75; ETHUSD Buy 1.50 @ 2531.48, SL 2480.00, open P&L -1.41 (the terminal's own Position Details panel prints 'Projected P&L -77.22' for that stop).

=== THE ARITHMETIC ===
Committed downside if each open position reaches its own declared stop:
  SOL  (99.94 - 96.00) x 25.0 = $98.50
  ETH  (2531.48 - 2480.00) x 1.5 = $77.22   (agrees with the terminal to the cent)
  TOTAL COMMITTED OPEN RISK      = $175.72
/api/bot/prop/status returned distance_to_dd_floor_usd: 176.0 for the same snapshot. So the book survives both of its own stops by TWENTY-EIGHT CENTS on the panel's own number. Nothing in the system computed that comparison; I did it by hand off the screenshot.

=== TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS, ONE ROOT: THE CUSHION DOES NOT KNOW THE BOOK IS OPEN ===
(1) THE CUSHION IS EQUITY-BASED, SO OPEN PROFIT INFLATES IT. Read the field, not the prose: prop_reconcile.compute_rule_distance computes `distance_to_dd = equity_used - dd_floor`, with equity_used falling back to the reported equity. Here that is 4876 - 4700 = $176.00, whereas the BANKED cushion is 4761 - 4700 = $61.00. The $115 difference is entirely the SOL position's unrealized profit — i.e. the cushion is padded by the very position whose own stop would remove it. On a balance basis EITHER stop alone breaches: ETH alone -> $4,683.78, SOL alone -> $4,662.50, both -> $4,585.28 ($114.72 through the floor).
(2) THE TICKET GATE GRADES EACH TICKET AS IF THE BOOK WERE FLAT. prop_risk_gate.grade_ticket_risk compares ONE ticket's risk_usd against min(distance_to_dd_floor_usd, distance_to_daily_loss_usd). There is no term for risk already committed by open positions. So a third ticket today would be graded against $176 with $175.72 already at stake, and could grade `within_cushion` while being unsurvivable.

=== THE READER ALREADY EXISTS, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS CHEAP AND WHY IT IS EMBARRASSING ===
`find_open_prop_positions` (src/prop/prop_monitor_pulse.py) is already imported by FOUR prop modules — prop_fills_staleness, prop_sl_tp_alert, breakout_executor, telegram_report_handler. The safety cushion is not one of them: prop_reconcile.py contains ZERO occurrences of 'position', and `grep -rn 'open_risk|committed_risk|open_exposure|risk_at_stop|open_position_risk' --include=*.py src/prop/` returns 0 hits. Both probes were positively controlled first (3 files match distance_to_dd_floor_usd in src/prop/; 25 'equity' hits inside prop_reconcile.py), so the silence is absence and not a bad pattern. This is the SAME written-and-never-read shape prop_risk_gate's own docstring was written about — that module was built because a computed cushion had 'three consumers and all three are DISPLAY'; it fixed the ticket-vs-cushion half and left the cushion itself blind to the book.

=== A DISCREPANCY I AM NOT RESOLVING BY ASSERTION ===
config/prop_rulesets/breakout.yaml says the static DD is 'STATIC, balance-based, off the STARTING balance', while the code measures the distance against EQUITY. The comment plausibly describes the ANCHOR (static, not trailing) rather than the measured metric, and prop firms commonly breach max-DD on intraday equity — but this repo holds no primary Breakout source settling which metric TRIGGERS the breach, and the two differ by $115 today. Establishing that from Breakout's own FAQ is part of the fix, because the safe cushion to PUBLISH may be the min of the two regardless of which one triggers.
items.evidence: Operator terminal screenshot 2026-08-27 (balance/equity/P&L header + both position rows + the ETH Position Details 'Projected P&L -77.22'); /api/bot/prop/status response embedded in issue #10362's workflow comment (distance_to_dd_floor_usd 176.0, equity_used_usd 4876.0, balance_basis 'snapshot', status_freshness 'ok', distance_to_daily_loss_usd null with day_pnl_state 'realized_unreported'); src/prop/prop_reconcile.py compute_rule_distance (`distance_to_dd = equity_used - dd_floor`); src/prop/prop_risk_gate.py grade_ticket_risk (`binding, cushion = min(candidates, ...)`, no open-risk term); config/prop_rulesets/breakout.yaml (account_size_usd 5000, max_drawdown_pct 0.06, drawdown_type static).
items.resolution_criteria: compute_rule_distance publishes the account's COMMITTED OPEN RISK (sum over open prop positions of |entry - stop| x qty, via the existing find_open_prop_positions) as its own field beside the cushion, and prop_risk_gate subtracts it before grading a new ticket — so a ticket is graded against what is LEFT, not against the whole cushion. States must not be collapsed: a position whose stop is unknown makes the committed risk UNKNOWN (never 0.0 — that is the anti-conservative direction on an account-killer, the same error BL-20260823-PROP-DAILY-CUSHION-FABRICATED-FROM-A-MISSING-REALIZED-TODAY records), and it must be distinguishable from a genuinely flat book. Also publish the BALANCE-basis distance beside the equity-basis one rather than replacing it, and record which metric Breakout actually breaches on from a primary source. NOT sufficient: a bigger warning in the ticket text — the 2026-08-27 ticket ALREADY warned ('AS OF THE LAST REPORT this risk did NOT fit: $75.00 vs $64.00') and the trade was placed anyway; the number a decision reads has to change.
items.not_a_finding_about: NOT a criticism of the operator's placement, and NOT the staleness class — the snapshot graded 'ok' at the moment measured. NOT a duplicate of BL-20260818-PROP-RULE-DISTANCE-IGNORES-THE-FILLS-STREAM, which is about REALIZED fills reported since the snapshot; this is about UNREALIZED exposure that has not closed at all.

So breakout_1's true distance to its floor is $55.00 MINUS whatever the open book would lose to its stops. Prop cluster. items.title: INVENTORY, NOT A VERDICT: 18 of 22 evidence-producing workflows upload an artifact and commit nothing — but only ONE is a confirmed wanted-result-lost case, and the other 17 need triage rather than an assertion
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-27 over .github/workflows/. Filed as a DENOMINATOR so the next session does not have to re-derive it, and deliberately NOT as 17 defects.

POPULATION: workflows whose output is EVIDENCE (research sweeps, backtests, training). Ops/deploy/relay workflows are excluded — their artifact is a run log, not a result a session reads back. 22 in the population; 4 land, 18 do not.

LANDS (4): e35-bracket-sweep, gpu-burst-train, m20-exit-lever-sweep, training-rerun-5m.
DOES NOT LAND (18): c1-conviction-ab, dukascopy-span-probe, flip-override-walkforward, gld-compat-matrix, ict-scalp-backtest, m20-capture-census, prop-tp-r-gate, pullback-frac-cross-leg-sweep, regime-adx-cutpoint-sweep, regime-cell-walkforward, regime-debt-matrix, research-backtest-augment, research-e2-horizon-arm, research-exit-head-build, research-panel-build, research-symbol-p0-build, trainer-offload-train, vwap-backtest.

PROBE WAS CONTROLLED. The landing predicate (git push|git commit|git-auto-commit|add-and-commit|create-pull-request|peter-evans|gh pr create) returns 2/1/4/2 hits on the four known landers and 0 on all 18 — so the silence is absence, not a pattern that misses a different commit idiom. This control exists BECAUSE the same session had just filed a false finding from an uncontrolled absence probe (see BL-20260827-COMPUTE-IS-SOLVED-LANDING-IS-NOT-THREE-INSTANCES).

⚠️ 'DOES NOT LAND' IS A SHAPE, NOT A DEFECT, AND MUST NOT BE READ AS 17 BUGS. Only trainer-offload-train is a confirmed case of a result someone WANTED that never arrived. Several of the others are one-shot probes whose answer went into a doc or a backlog row by hand and were never meant to accumulate rows; for those, committing a corpus would be make-work. Which is which has NOT been established — that is the triage this row asks for, and calling all 18 broken would repeat the exact error the row above records.

WHY NO ASSERTION IS BEING WIRED INTO THEM NOW (operator decision, 2026-08-27). scripts/ci/assert_rows_landed.py asserts 'my rows are present in store X'. For 17 of these nobody has decided what X is or what schema goes in it — that is the results contract (R1), not the assertion (R2), so wiring R2 first would mean inventing a store per workflow on the fly. And 18 new fail-the-job assertions on workflows that never intended to accumulate rows is a false-alarm generator: a research sweep going red for a reason nobody acts on is the desensitized-alarm P1 this repo names as its own worst class. The assertion is instead wired into the ONE confirmed instance (R3, the offload run).

CLASSIFICATION DONE 2026-08-29 — docs/research/evidence-workflow-landing-triage-2026-08-29.md. No assertions were wired and no workflow was changed, per this row's own 'NOT sufficient' clause and the 2026-08-27 operator decision that R1 precedes R2.

⚠️ THIS ROW'S INVENTORY WAS STALE, IN ITS OWN HEADLINE CASE. Re-measured with the row's predicate AND its positive control (all 4 known landers still detected, so the silence is absence): trainer-offload-train NOW LANDS (4 landing hits, 2 assert_rows_landed calls). That was the row's ONLY confirmed wanted-result-lost case; R3 fixed it 2026-08-28 (#10368/#10390), ONE DAY after this row was filed. Current population: 22 evidence workflows, 5 land, 17 do not. The transferable point is about the ARTIFACT: a hand-typed denominator went stale in a day, and this row filed the list explicitly 'so the next session does not have to re-derive it' — the next session re-derived it anyway. A denominator that cannot re-measure itself is a snapshot. If it is to be relied on again it should be produced by a script.

CLASSIFICATION: (a) MEANT TO ACCUMULATE = 10 — research-backtest-augment (the strongest: the only scheduled one, and its header names both its store and its downstream consumer), m20-capture-census, pullback-frac-cross-leg-sweep, regime-debt-matrix, regime-cell-walkforward, regime-adx-cutpoint-sweep, research-panel-build, research-exit-head-build, research-symbol-p0-build, gld-compat-matrix. (b) ONE-SHOT PROBE = 7 — flip-override-walkforward, c1-conviction-ab, dukascopy-span-probe, research-e2-horizon-arm, prop-tp-r-gate, ict-scalp-backtest, vwap-backtest. (c) DEAD = 0 PROPOSED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT GUESSED: the run-history probe returned a response too large to read and was abandoned rather than half-read, and low recency would be weak evidence regardless — 16 of 17 are dispatch/issue triggered, so 'has not run lately' is the NORMAL state of an on-demand research tool. What would settle (c) is whether the workflow's SUBJECT is gone (strategy retired, milestone closed, named successor), not whether it is idle; none of the 17 failed that on the headers read.

SEPARATE FINDING, not about landing: vwap-backtest SSHes into the TRAINER VM while fetching fresh Bybit candles — CPU-only work over a public feed, which vm-resource-management.md and the R5 routing rule send to a free runner. Every sibling in this population already made that move and several say so in their headers. It is the only member still pinned to the trainer, which makes it directly relevant to R6. Not acted on — re-homing a live workflow is its own change.
items.evidence: grep -ln 'upload-artifact' .github/workflows/*.yml (40 files, ops workflows then excluded by hand to the 22-file evidence population); landing-idiom probe with the positive control quoted above; docs/research/RESEARCH-WORKFLOW-ARCHITECTURE-2026-08-27.md § R1/R2.
items.resolution_criteria: Each of the 18 is classified into exactly one of: (a) MEANT TO ACCUMULATE — gets a declared store under R1 and a landing assertion under R2; (b) ONE-SHOT PROBE — its answer belongs in a doc or backlog row and no corpus is owed, recorded as such so a later session does not re-open the question; (c) DEAD — the workflow is no longer run and should be removed. The deliverable is the classification with a reason per workflow, not a sweep of 18 new assertions. NOT sufficient: adding assert_rows_landed to all of them, which would answer the wrong question loudly.
items.not_a_finding_about: NOT a claim that these 18 runs are broken or that their results were lost. It is a measured denominator and an ask for triage.

items.tier: 2 (a runner-trained model reaching the registry joins the live shadow fleet)
items.title: R3 (close the offload loop) has TWO blockers found by reading the code, not guessed: the registry entry embeds an ABSOLUTE path resolved on the training machine, and ml/registry-store is untracked so git-sync alone cannot deliver a model
items.detail:
Recorded 2026-08-27 so the next session does not re-derive them. Operator chose the transport on 2026-08-27: the runner commits to a branch and the trainer's git-sync picks it up. Reading the code for that design surfaced two facts that decide its shape.

BLOCKER 1 — THE REGISTRY ENTRY CARRIES A MACHINE-LOCAL ABSOLUTE PATH. ml/experiments/runner.py:422 registers with `model_state_path=str(model_state_path.resolve())`, i.e. an absolute path under the experiments root of whatever machine trained. On a GitHub runner that resolves under /home/runner/work/..., which does not exist on the trainer. A drained entry would therefore be REGISTERED AND UNLOADABLE — a model that appears in the registry and in /api/bot/ml/registry, and fails when anything tries to load it. Any cross-machine transport must rewrite that path (or store it relative) AND verify the artifact resolves on the destination; a drain that skips this produces exactly the confident-wrong state this repo keeps paying for.

BLOCKER 2 — GIT-SYNC CANNOT DELIVER A MODEL BY ITSELF. `git ls-files ml/registry-store` returns 0 files: the registry is trainer-local and untracked (publish_trainer_mirror.sh synthesizes registry.jsonl from the per-model JSONs there and rsyncs it to the live VM). trainer_git_sync.sh does `git checkout --force -B main origin/main` every 15 min, which updates the TRACKED tree and leaves untracked dirs alone. So a committed model lands in the tree at some tracked inbox path and something must still move it into the registry root. That drain is a real, separate component.

⚠️ DO NOT PUT THE DRAIN IN trainer_git_sync.sh. Its stated contract is CODE-ONLY, restarts nothing, and it `exit 0`s on ANY error by design so a sync failure never leaves a failed unit alarming. A registry write inside a script that swallows its own errors is the silent-landing defect wearing the fix's clothes. A separate unit DECLARED in deploy/trainer/ is the honest home — and unlike the 8 units in BL-20260827-TRAINER-SCHEDULE-IS-UNDECLARED-THE-VM-IS-A-PET it would be declared from birth.

ALSO NOTED, NOT MEASURED: model_state.json is JSON text (runner.py:379-382), not a binary pickle, so it is committable in principle — but NO instance exists in this checkout and its SIZE for an LGBM head is UNMEASURED. Establish it before designing the transport; an N-megabyte tree serialized to JSON per training run is a different proposition from a few KB, and this row does not assert which it is.

TRANSPORT PRECEDENT THAT WORKS: e35-bracket-sweep.yml's corpus job. It documents that a dispatch on the protected default branch CANNOT push there (GH006 — structural, so retarget rather than retry, per BL-20260812-SWEEP-CORPUS-CANNOT-PUSH-TO-MAIN) and that a GITHUB_TOKEN push starts NO workflows, so the job cannot open or green its own PR (BL-20260813-CORPUS-RETARGET-CANNOT-OPEN-ITS-OWN-PR). Copy that shape; do not reinvent it.
items.evidence: ml/experiments/runner.py:379-382 (model_state.json written as JSON) and :422 (`str(model_state_path.resolve())`); ml/registry/model_registry.py::register (pure file write into the given root, stage taken from manifest.target_deployment_stage); `git ls-files ml/registry-store` -> 0; scripts/ops/trainer_git_sync.sh (force-checkout to origin/main, code-only, exit 0 on any error); scripts/ops/publish_trainer_mirror.sh REGISTRY_ROOT=$REPO_ROOT/ml/registry-store; .github/workflows/trainer-offload-train.yml lines 176/184/244.
items.resolution_criteria: A manifest trained on a runner appears in the trainer's registry AND its model_state artifact resolves and loads on the trainer — verified by loading it there, not by the entry existing. The landing is asserted inside the run against the store the producer actually writes (scripts/ci/assert_rows_landed.py), and the drain is a unit declared in deploy/trainer/, not an addition to trainer_git_sync.sh. The moment a runner-trained model first joins the live shadow fleet is Tier-2 and gets an explicit operator OK — it is not slipped in as part of the plumbing.

items.measured_2026_08_27: THE UNMEASURED ITEM IS NOW MEASURED (trainer-diag issue #10366), and it changes the transport question rather than settling it. Population: every model_state.json on the trainer, n=5419. Sizes in bytes — min 137 · p50 1,401,045 · p90 1,420,293 · max 2,148,257 · mean 897,821. In MB: p50 1.34, max 2.05. The LGBM case this row asked for is flat at 1.340 MB across every btc-regime-15m-lgbm-base-pcv-v003 run sampled. ⚠️ STATE THE POPULATION ON THE TOTAL. The corpus sums to 4,865,291,213 bytes (4.53 GB), and that is the ENTIRE HISTORY OF 5,419 RUNS — it is NOT what a transport would carry and must not be quoted as the cost. One run carries ~1.34 MB. SO 'is it committable' HAS NO SINGLE ANSWER — it depends on a policy nobody has chosen: HOW MANY runs get committed. Measured rate: 5,419 runs with the earliest dated 2026-05-14, i.e. ~105 days, ~52 runs/day across all manifests. Committing every run would be ~70 MB/day of PERMANENT git history (history is immutable, so it is not reclaimable) — clearly infeasible. Committing only runs that update a registry entry is a far smaller number: there are 96 registry entries in total. The transport design must state which of the two it does, because they differ by orders of magnitude. ⚠️ The ~52/day figure is a MEAN derived from a count and an earliest date, not a measured per-day series; treat it as an order of magnitude, not a rate. BOTH ORIGINAL BLOCKERS ARE NOW CONFIRMED DIRECTLY, not by code-reading alone. Blocker 1: three of three sampled registry entries carry a machine-local absolute path, e.g. '/home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/ml/experiments-runs/eth-direction-1h-lgbm-xasset-v1/20260827T010821Z/model_state.json'. Blocker 2: `git ls-files ml/registry-store` returns 0 against 96 on-disk entries, and `git ls-files | grep -c model_state.json` returns 0 — nothing in this family is tracked anywhere today.
items.operator_decision_2026_08_27_artifact_po: OPERATOR DECIDED 2026-08-27, on the measurement above: the transport commits the model artifact ONLY FOR RUNS THAT UPDATE A REGISTRY ENTRY — not every training run. Bounded and small (96 registry entries lifetime, ~1.34 MB each) and the artifact stays DURABLE in git with no expiry. TWO ALTERNATIVES WERE PUT UP AND DECLINED, recorded so they are not re-proposed as fresh ideas: (a) commit the registry ENTRY only and fetch the model from the run's uploaded GitHub artifact — rejected because artifacts EXPIRE at 30-90 days, so a registered model outlives its artifact and becomes precisely the 'registered and unloadable' state Blocker 1 exists to prevent, just on a delay that is harder to notice than an immediate failure; (b) git-lfs — rejected because it adds an LFS dependency plus a bandwidth quota that can fail a fetch in a way plain git cannot, i.e. a NEW failure mode on the path that delivers models to the live shadow fleet. Committing every run was not offered: at the measured ~52 runs/day it is ~70 MB/day of permanent, unreclaimable history.
items.shipped_2026_08_27_transport:
THE TRANSPORT HALF IS BUILT; THE DRAIN IS UNARMED (operator decision). Shipped: scripts/ml/offload/emit_bundle.py (runner: materialize a run into the tracked ml/offload-inbox/ + append an R1-shaped index row), a `publish` job on trainer-offload-train.yml (opt-in, default FALSE, contents:write scoped to that job alone, e35's retarget-on-protected-branch push shape, then assert_rows_landed against the store it literally git-adds), scripts/ml/offload/drain_inbox.py + deploy/trainer/ict-offload-drain.{service,timer} + scripts/ops/run_offload_drain.sh (trainer, installed-disabled AND plan-only — arming needs BOTH the timer enabled and OFFLOAD_DRAIN_APPLY=1). With publish=false the workflow's behaviour is unchanged.

⚠️ BLOCKER 1's RESOLUTION CHANGED SHAPE, AND THE ROW ABOVE IMPLIED THE WORSE ONE. This row said a cross-machine transport 'must rewrite that path (or store it relative) AND verify the artifact resolves'. It does neither, because it carries no registry entry at all: the drain RE-REGISTERS ON THE TRAINER, so model_state_path.resolve() returns a trainer-local path BY CONSTRUCTION. There is no path to rewrite and therefore no path to rewrite wrongly. That is the shape scripts/ml/gpu_burst/ingest_bundle.py already uses for a rented GPU pod whose local registry dies with it — the identical problem, solved, and not found by the design reading that produced this row.

⚠️ A SECOND, INDEPENDENT RESOLUTION ALREADY EXISTED AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT RELIED ON. ml/shadow/factory.py::_resolve_state_path_via_mirror maps ANY absolute path containing an `experiments-runs` segment onto <registry_root>/../experiments-runs/<suffix>. A runner path (/home/runner/work/.../ml/experiments-runs/<mid>/<rid>/model_state.json) satisfies that, so a COPIED entry would in fact have resolved on the trainer — i.e. Blocker 1 as filed overstates the immediate breakage. It is still not relied on, because that fallback is SILENT ON SUCCESS: a right path and a wrong path look identical to the caller, so the failure would surface as a model quietly serving the wrong weights rather than as an error. Register-on-destination is correct without needing the fallback to be.

BLOCKER 2 is resolved as the row demanded: a unit DECLARED in deploy/trainer/ from birth, not a line in trainer_git_sync.sh — whose contract is code-only and which exit 0s on ANY error, so a registry write inside it would be the silent-landing defect wearing the fix's clothes. run_offload_drain.sh deliberately does the OPPOSITE (no exit-0-on-error), and a test pins that the two scripts differ on exactly that.

SAFETY, copied from ingest_bundle.py rather than re-derived, and pinned against its constants by tests/scripts/test_offload_transport.py so the two ingests cannot drift: the drain registers under a NAMESPACED id (<model_id>-offload) at a FORCED `candidate` stage (a fresh registration would default to `shadow`, which AUTO-WIRES onto every strategy's predictor list), and refuses outright to refresh an id an operator has advanced past candidate. Six mutants — arm the unit · drop the namespace · force shadow · ignore --apply · loosen the wrapper's exact-'1' check · flip the publish default — are each caught by a named test.

⚠️ NOTHING HERE HAS BEEN OBSERVED OUTSIDE A SANDBOX. The cross-machine round trip is two tmpdirs on one filesystem. See OI-20260827-OFFLOAD-TRANSPORT-HAS-NEVER-CARRIED-A-MODEL for what is unverified and in what order. This row stays OPEN: its resolution criteria require a manifest trained on a runner to appear in the TRAINER's registry with its artifact LOADED there, and that has not happened.
items.measurement_correction_2026_08_27: One figure in this row's own measurement block needs a caveat a later session should not re-derive: the '~52 runs/day' rate is a MEAN over a count and an earliest date (5,419 runs since 2026-05-14), which the block already says — but the ~70 MB/day figure derived from it inherits that, and is what the opt-in default is argued from. The argument survives a wide error bar (even 10 runs/day is ~13 MB/day of permanent history), so the DECISION is robust even though the rate is not precise. State it as an order of magnitude.

updates.note: Re-validated: two blockers found by reading code rather than guessing, which is the right basis. Blocked, not idle.

items.source: session-2026-08-27-lane-p-pytest-run-root-cause
items.title: requirements-test.txt does not deliver the single-command install it promises — psutil is missing and 8 tests fail without it
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-27 in a lean sandbox. requirements-test.txt's own header states its purpose: 'Putting them in one file lets the next session run a single command: pip install --user -r requirements-test.txt'. It does not achieve that. After installing it IN FULL, EIGHT tests still fail with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'psutil' — tests/test_send_ping.py (6), tests/test_vm_health_helper.py::test_vm_health_returns_none_per_field_when_psutil_raises (1), tests/test_s067_silent_empty_fixes.py::test_diag_vm_health_returns_none_per_field_on_psutil_failure (1). Installing psutil alone takes those same three files to 30 passed — so the attribution is measured, not inferred. psutil is declared in requirements.txt (the RUNTIME file) and the test file's header explicitly says the runtime requirements live there and to 'avoid mixing' — but the two vm_health tests exist precisely to assert the PSUTIL-FAILURE branch, so they import it in order to monkeypatch it. A test that mocks a dependency still needs that dependency importable. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND CONVENIENCE: CI installs BOTH files, so CI is green and the gap is invisible there — it is only ever paid by a sandbox session, which is the exact reader the file was written for. It also renders as 8 reds in a local full-suite run, which a session must triage before it can trust its own repro, and 'a red I decided to ignore' is how a real red gets ignored next time.
items.proposed_fix: Add psutil to requirements-test.txt at a floor matching requirements.txt (>=5.9.0), with a comment naming the two vm_health tests that mock it — so the next reader can see WHY a runtime dep is listed in the test file and does not 'tidy' it back out on the header's avoid-mixing rule. NOT fixed in-session: it is Tier-1 and one line, but the only open PR at the time was a Tier-3 prop change and widening that diff would muddy an operator review that has to be read carefully.
items.resolution_criteria: REMAINING: a from-scratch `pip install -r requirements-test.txt` in a CLEAN env, then the full suite, with the failure list grepped for ModuleNotFoundError. Zero such failures resolves this row. If any module other than psutil appears, this row was incomplete and the fix must cover those too — which is why it is not being closed on the three-file check alone.
items.update_20260827: FIRST CONJUNCT MET, SECOND NOT RUN — the row stays OPEN and the split is the point. requirements-test.txt now carries psutil>=5.9.0, the same floor as requirements.txt, with the measured attribution written at the pin rather than left in this row. `pytest tests/test_send_ping.py tests/test_vm_health_helper.py tests/test_s067_silent_empty_fixes.py` -> 30 passed / 0 errors, which is the count this row predicted. ⚠️ BUT THAT RUN WAS IN THIS SESSION'S ALREADY-POPULATED ENVIRONMENT, NOT A CLEAN ONE, so it demonstrates the three files pass — it does NOT demonstrate that requirements-test.txt ALONE is now sufficient, which is what the file's own header promises and what this row was filed about. The re-derive half was not run either: a full suite in a clean env with ONLY requirements-test.txt installed, failures grepped for ModuleNotFoundError. Until that runs, psutil is the only module KNOWN to be missing, never the only one THERE IS — the denominator is unestablished and a second missing module would look exactly like this row's resolution. Zero CI risk from the pin itself: psutil is already a requirements.txt dep, so every environment that installs the runtime file already had it.

updates.note: RE-CONFIRMED IN A SIBLING FORM TODAY: requirements-test.txt does not deliver its promised single-command install. I had to pip-install pytest AND fastapi mid-session before I could run 31 targeted tests. Consolidate with BL-20260824-SANDBOX-TEST-SUITE-DIVERGES-FROM-CI and BL-20260826-SANDBOX-FULL-SUITE-CARRIES-32-FAILURES-CI-DOES-NOT-AND-5-ARE-ORDER-DEPENDENT — three rows, one 'a session cannot trust a local run' problem.

items.source: session-2026-08-27-lane-p-pytest-run-root-cause
items.title: Five calibration tests fail in a full-suite run and pass in isolation — an order dependency CI's floor pins currently hide
items.detail: OBSERVED 2026-08-27, and STATE WHAT WAS NOT ESTABLISHED. In one full local run (pytest -q tests/ --ignore=tests/test_main_loop.py; 13241 passed, 15 skipped) five tests failed, all in tests/ml/calibration/test_calibration.py: test_fit_auto_selects_isotonic_for_large_n, test_fit_auto_selects_platt_for_medium_n, test_isotonic_recovers_monotone_signal, test_platt_recovers_monotone_signal, test_reliability_curve_and_ece_on_wellcalibrated. The SAME five pass in isolation (17 passed) and the whole tests/ml/ subtree passes on its own (1102 passed, 3 skipped). So the failure is a function of what ran BEFORE them, not of the tests themselves — some earlier module in tests/ leaves global state (a seed, a numpy or sklearn setting, a patched symbol) that these five read. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and must not be assumed either way: (a) the CULPRIT is unidentified — no bisect was run; (b) it is NOT known to reproduce in CI. CI is green on main, and this sandbox resolves the floor pins to numpy 2.4.6 / scipy 1.17.1 / sklearn 1.9.0, which CI may not, so the interaction may be version-gated. A negative here has no denominator: nobody has run the full suite in CI on these versions. WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW ANYWAY: requirements-test.txt floor-pins with no ceiling ('major-version ceiling left open so security patches land'), so CI WILL resolve to these versions eventually and inherit whatever this is. An order-dependent test is also the failure mode that renders identically to a real regression — a session that hits it mid-investigation spends budget on the wrong thing, which is what happened here. RULED OUT as a cause: the observing session's own diff, which touched only src/prop/ and scripts/prop/ and added no test module, so it cannot have changed collection order or calibration inputs.
items.proposed_fix: Bisect to NAME the leaking module, then fix the leak at its source (the leaking module restores what it mutates) rather than papering over it in the calibration tests — a leak that reaches these five reaches whatever else reads the same global.
items.resolution_criteria: The culprit module is NAMED, not guessed — bisect by running tests/ml/calibration/test_calibration.py after progressively larger alphabetical prefixes of tests/ until the five fail, then narrow to the single preceding module. Then EITHER the leak is fixed at its source OR the calibration tests are made order-independent (explicit seed/state setup in a fixture), and the full suite passes twice: once in file order and once shuffled or reversed. Reproducing it in CI is NOT a precondition for fixing it, and failing to reproduce it in CI is NOT evidence it is absent — CI has never run these dependency versions.
items.resolution: RESOLVED SAME DAY, and the row's own diagnosis was WRONG in an instructive way. It called this an order dependency and guessed at 'a seed, a numpy or sklearn setting, a patched symbol', and it explicitly suspected the newer numpy 2.4.6 / scipy 1.17.1 / sklearn 1.9.0 this sandbox resolves. NONE of that was the cause and the version speculation was a red herring. THE ACTUAL CAUSE: ~8 test modules run `sys.modules.setdefault(_mod, MagicMock())` at MODULE SCOPE for pandas/numpy/scipy/sklearn/dotenv. `setdefault` guards on ALREADY-IMPORTED, not on IMPORTABLE, so where the real sklearn is installed but not yet imported the MagicMock wins the slot and `ml/calibration/fit.py::_fit_platt`'s LOCAL `from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression` dies with "'sklearn' is not a package". Filed and fixed as BL-20260827-TEST-MODULES-STUB-SKLEARN-INTO-SYS-MODULES-AT-IMPORT-TIME (conftest now runs its correct `_stub_optional` for those names first, so all eight setdefault calls no-op). WHAT THE ROW GOT RIGHT: that it was a collection/ordering effect and not a broken test, and that it needed a bisect rather than a guess. WHAT IT GOT WRONG: it reported the cause as genuinely unknown while ALSO naming a plausible-sounding suspect (dependency versions), and a later reader could easily have spent the session chasing that. The resolution criteria it set — 'the culprit module is NAMED, not guessed' — are what actually produced the answer: the two-file reproducer `pytest tests/ml/calibration/ tests/test_outcomes_integration.py` (5 failed) against `tests/ml/calibration/` alone (17 passed). Measured after the fix: 22 passed.

items.source: session-2026-08-27-lane-t2
items.title: The test suite writes real durable alert latches into runtime_logs/, and one test thereby fails itself for 6 hours on every machine that runs the suite twice
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-27, three-way, and the mechanism is confirmed rather than inferred. `tests/test_outcomes_integration.py::test_strategy_exception_pages_with_strategy_name` drives a synthetic strategy `_test_explode` through `pipeline.multiplexed_signal_builder` and asserts the exception pages at ERROR. That path calls `alert_cooldown.cooldown_admits` with NO `path_resolver`, so the latch resolves to the REAL `runtime_logs/strategy_builder_exception_alert_state.json` and the test's own fixture is committed to it: measured content `{"_test_explode|ValueError:strategy borked": 1787830205.83}`. The latch is WALL-CLOCK keyed with `_BUILDER_EXC_COOLDOWN_S = 6h`, so the second occurrence is downgraded to WARN and the ERROR assertion fails. PROOF, three runs of the SAME single test: (A) latch present -> FAIL; (B) `rm` the latch, re-run -> PASS; (C) immediately again with no deletion -> FAIL, and the file now carries a fresh timestamp. It is SELF-POISONING, not order-dependent — the first suite run on a machine poisons every subsequent one for six hours, in any order. ⚠️ **INVISIBLE IN CI, WHICH IS WHY IT HAS SURVIVED.** CI checks out a fresh tree per run so the latch never persists, and `pytest-run` is green on main. The entire cost falls on a developer or Claude session running the suite locally — where it renders as a real regression. It cost this session a false lead: the failure appeared only in the SECOND full-suite run of the container and was initially suspected to be a collection-order effect introduced by a newly added test file. That was REFUTED by a control run excluding the new file, which failed identically. THE PRODUCTION CODE IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE CHANGED TO FIX THIS. The durable wall-clock latch is deliberate — `BL-20260823-TARGET-NAKED-COOLDOWN-RESETS-ON-EVERY-RESTART` records that a per-PROCESS `time.monotonic()` latch put 202 CRITICALs (53.7% of the operator's ERROR+ feed) on the channel because every trader restart re-armed it. Making the latch weaker to satisfy a test would re-open that. The TEST is what fails to isolate. THE CLASS IS WIDER THAN ONE TEST. Measured in the same working tree, the suite left THREE real latch files behind: `strategy_builder_exception_alert_state.json`, `target_naked_alert_state.json`, `bybit_over_cover_alert_state.json`. Only the first is known to fail a test today; the other two are the same pollution with no observed victim yet, which is a weaker statement than 'they are fine'. `runtime_logs/` is gitignored, so this never dirties the repo — it only corrupts the next run.
items.proposed_fix: NARROW (low risk, fixes the observed failure): `cooldown_admits` already takes an optional `path_resolver` for exactly this reason, and `state_path` honours it. Give the test an autouse fixture that points the latch at `tmp_path` — either by monkeypatching `src.utils.paths.runtime_logs_dir` (which `alert_cooldown._state_path` imports at call time, so patching it works) or by deleting the key before and after. BROAD (the structural fix, larger blast radius): a session-scoped autouse fixture in `tests/conftest.py` redirecting `runtime_logs_dir()` to a tmp dir for the whole suite, so NO test can write durable operator state into a working tree. That is the right end state and it touches 13k+ tests, some of which may depend on the real path — so it needs its own change and its own verification, not a drive-by. NOT fixed in-session deliberately: the only open PRs are a Tier-3 prop change and the research-queue lane, and the operator explicitly chose separate branches to keep lanes un-mixed. A local workaround that costs nothing meanwhile: `rm -f runtime_logs/*_alert_state.json` before a full-suite run. ⚠️ WORKAROUND CAVEAT, measured: `rm -f runtime_logs/*_alert_state.json` genuinely fixes THIS row's failure, but it does NOT make a full local run green on its own — the sklearn-stub row above accounts for the other five failures and needs its own fix.
items.resolution_criteria: Running the FULL suite twice in a row on the same machine, with no deletion between runs, produces identical results — specifically `tests/test_outcomes_integration.py::test_strategy_exception_pages_with_strategy_name` passes in BOTH. Re-derive the pollution list rather than trusting this row: after a full run, `ls runtime_logs/*_alert_state.json` must be EMPTY (or contain only files a test deliberately asserts on). If any latch file is present, the isolation is incomplete whatever the test results say — the three files named above are what was observed on 2026-08-27 and there may be more once other latches gain tests.
items.correction_2026_08_27_same_session: ⚠️ THIS FIELD PREVIOUSLY RETRACTED THE ROW. THE RETRACTION WAS WRONG AND IS ITSELF WITHDRAWN. It read: the `rm -f runtime_logs/*_alert_state.json` workaround 'IS FALSE AND I MEASURED IT FALSE', on the evidence of a full-suite run that cleared the latches first and still failed. That evidence was mis-attributed. The full-suite run ALSO fails five sklearn calibration tests for a completely unrelated reason (now filed as BL-20260827-TEST-MODULES-STUB-SKLEARN-INTO-SYS-MODULES-AT-IMPORT-TIME), and I read a multi-cause failure list as though one hypothesis had to explain all of it. THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS IS CORRECT AND IS NOW CONFIRMED AT THE MECHANISM LEVEL, not just by A/B/C. The actual assertion is `send.assert_called_once()` -> 'Called 0 times', with the captured log showing `WARNING ... strategy '_test_explode' raised strategy borked` — WARNING, not ERROR. That is precisely the latch downgrade: the test asserts a page and the latch had already spent the window. Re-confirmed live: after an `rm`, the test PASSES and writes the latch; the very next invocation FAILS. WHAT I GOT WRONG PROCEDURALLY, since it is the transferable part: I treated 'the full suite still fails' as refuting the mechanism without reading the failure's own message. A failure list with several entries is not one phenomenon, and 'my fix did not make the run green' is not the same claim as 'my fix did not work'. Read the assertion before revising the theory.
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-08-27 (merged in #10365, verified on main at 28e47d97). tests/test_outcomes_integration.py now carries an autouse fixture that monkeypatches src.utils.paths.runtime_logs_dir to tmp_path, so the module drives the real durable latch against a per-test directory instead of the repo's runtime_logs/. VERIFIED, and state exactly what was run: the module was run TWICE back-to-back with no deletion between runs and produced identical results (5 passed / 5 passed), and `ls runtime_logs/*_alert_state.json` was EMPTY after each — the mechanism check, i.e. the file that used to poison the next run is no longer written at all. The row's stated bar was the FULL suite twice; the full suite was run ONCE this session (13,293 passed, 0 failed) and the twice-in-a-row check was done on the offending module only. That is weaker than the letter of the criterion and is recorded as such rather than claimed as a full-suite double run.

items.source: session-2026-08-27-lane-t2
items.title: Eight test modules install a MagicMock over sklearn/numpy/scipy at IMPORT time, and it breaks the calibration tests in any run that collects them first
items.detail: ROOT-CAUSED 2026-08-27 with a TWO-FILE minimal reproducer: `pytest tests/ml/calibration/ tests/test_outcomes_integration.py` fails 5 calibration tests; `pytest tests/ml/calibration/` alone passes 17/17. The added file runs AFTER them, so the damage cannot be at run time — it happens during COLLECTION, which imports every selected module before any test executes. MECHANISM, read rather than inferred. `tests/test_outcomes_integration.py:10` (and the same block in at least seven siblings — test_api_reporting, test_health, test_bot_web_sweep, test_orders, test_outcomes, test_hourly_report, test_notify_send_via_alert_manager) runs at module scope: `for _mod in ('pandas','matplotlib','matplotlib.pyplot','numpy','scipy','sklearn','dotenv'): sys.modules.setdefault(_mod, MagicMock())`. `setdefault` guards on ALREADY-IMPORTED, not on IMPORTABLE. So when the real sklearn is installed but has not been imported yet, the stub wins the slot, and any later `import sklearn.linear_model` dies with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sklearn.linear_model'; 'sklearn' is not a package`. Verified directly: after importing that test module, `sys.modules['sklearn']` is a `<MagicMock>` with no `__path__`. `ml/calibration/fit.py::_fit_platt` imports sklearn LOCALLY inside the function (deliberately — 'local import (offline)'), which is exactly what makes it lose the race: nothing imports sklearn during collection, so the stub is unopposed by the time the test body runs. ⚠️ WHY CI IS GREEN AND THIS IS NOT KNOWN TO REPRODUCE THERE. pytest-run passes on main, so something in CI must import the real sklearn before the stub lands — a different resolved sklearn version whose package __init__ pulls submodules eagerly, or a module collected earlier that imports it at top level. That has NOT been established and must not be assumed: what is measured is the sandbox behaviour and the two-file reproducer. If CI ever resolves a different sklearn, this becomes a CI failure with no code change behind it. COST TODAY: every local full-suite run reports 5 red calibration tests that are not real, which is exactly the noise that trains a reader to skim a failure list — and this session duly mis-read it, briefly retracting a correct finding because a multi-cause list was treated as one phenomenon.
items.proposed_fix: Guard on IMPORTABILITY, not on prior import: replace `sys.modules.setdefault(_mod, MagicMock())` with a check that only stubs when the real module genuinely is not installed — `if importlib.util.find_spec(_mod) is None: sys.modules.setdefault(_mod, MagicMock())`. That keeps the stub doing its actual job (letting these tests import on a lean box) while never shadowing a real dependency that happens not to have been imported yet. The block is duplicated across ~8 files, so the durable version is ONE shared helper in tests/conftest.py that they all call, rather than eight copies to keep in step — a second copy is how the two would drift. Note find_spec on an already-mocked parent can itself raise, so the helper should treat any exception from find_spec as 'not importable'.
items.resolution_criteria: `pytest tests/ml/calibration/ tests/test_outcomes_integration.py` reports 17 calibration passes and 0 calibration failures — the exact two-file reproducer, so the check cannot pass by accident of ordering. AND a full local run's failure list contains no `'sklearn' is not a package` error. Re-derive the file list rather than trusting the eight named here: `grep -rn "sys.modules.setdefault" tests/` — if any call site still guards on prior import rather than importability, the fix is incomplete.
items.update_20260827: PARTIALLY MITIGATED, DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN — the instance is fixed and the CLASS is not, and collapsing those two would be the finding. tests/conftest.py now PRE-IMPORTS numpy/pandas/scipy/sklearn if they are installed (_preimport_if_available) before any test module runs, so a later sys.modules.setdefault(<pkg>, MagicMock()) is a no-op for the real package. The row's own reproducer is green: `pytest tests/ml/calibration/ tests/test_outcomes_integration.py` -> 22 passed, 0 failed. ⚠️ BUT THE ROW SAID TO RE-DERIVE THE FILE LIST RATHER THAN TRUST THE EIGHT NAMED, AND RE-DERIVING IT REFUTES ANY CLAIM OF CLOSURE: `grep -rn 'sys.modules.setdefault' tests/` returns 28 sites (measured 2026-08-27 on 28e47d97, excluding the __pycache__ hit). The pre-import fixes the symptom for exactly four packages ON A MACHINE THAT HAS THEM INSTALLED; on a host without them — which is the guards CI environment — the setdefault still stubs, and the 28 sites still leave sys.modules mutated for every test that follows. ⚠️ AND THE HALF-FIX ITSELF CAUSED AN OUTAGE: the first attempt ADDED those four to the stub list instead of pre-importing them, which put a MagicMock in sys.modules['numpy'] in the numpy-less guards environment; pytest.approx does `if np := sys.modules.get('numpy'): isinstance(val, np.bool_)`, a MagicMock is not a type, and operator-owed-guard went red. Reproduced in a clean venv and fixed by never stubbing. That is why the remedy is 'never stub', not 'stub more'. REMEDY, OPERATOR-APPROVED 2026-08-27 AS ITS OWN PR: a conftest-level autouse audit asserting no test leaves sys.modules or runtime_logs/ changed — the class detector, not a 29th patch. Its own PR deliberately, because the blast radius is 13,293 tests and bundling it would make some other change's verification unreadable.

updates.note: Re-validated: eight modules installing a MagicMock over sklearn/numpy/scipy at IMPORT time. Root cause shared with BL-20260807-PYTEST-APPROX-NUMPY-STUB, BL-20260822-TEST-SUITE-CROSS-FILE-SYS-MODULES-POLLUTION and BL-20260825-THREE-BYBIT-MODIFY-TESTS-FAIL-ONLY-UNDER-A-PARTIAL-SELECTION — FOUR rows, one unscoped-stubbing root.

items.source: session-2026-08-27-lane-t2
items.title: A test popped dotenv/matplotlib/pandas out of sys.modules and never restored them, breaking five later tests — FIXED same session
items.detail: ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED 2026-08-27. `tests/test_notify_session.py::TestNotifyImportIsLightweight` asserts the Stop-hook ping path stays import-light — a legitimate and valuable check. It did so by looping `sys.modules.pop(mod, None)` over `SCRIPT_FORBIDDEN` (matplotlib, pandas, dotenv, src.bot.alert_manager, src.runtime.signal_notifications) and NEVER restoring them. `dotenv` is the one that bites. python-dotenv is in requirements.txt but NOT in requirements-test.txt, so on a test-only install the module does not exist and `tests/conftest.py::_stub_optional` provides the only working `dotenv` in sys.modules. Popping it deletes that stub for the remainder of the session. `tests/test_send_ping.py` runs later (s > n), imports `src.bot.claude_bridge`, and dies at line 45 on `from dotenv import load_dotenv` with ModuleNotFoundError. MEASURED: `pytest tests/test_[d-n]*.py tests/test_send_ping.py` -> 10 failed; with the restore -> 0 failed (the one residual red was test_guards_uncommitted_work, which asserts a clean working tree and was correctly seeing this session's own uncommitted edit). Full local suite went 11 failed -> 5 -> 0 across the three fixes landed today. ⚠️ INVISIBLE IN CI, LIKE THE OTHER TWO IN THIS FAMILY. CI installs requirements.txt, so the REAL python-dotenv is importable and the pop is harmless there. Every one of today's three test defects is local-only, which is why all three survived: pytest-run is green on main and nothing else looks. FIX: an `addCleanup`-based `_pop_and_restore` helper on the class — it snapshots the entries it is about to remove and puts them back when the test ends. The import-light assertions are unchanged; only the global mutation is contained.
items.proposed_fix: Done in this session (tests/test_notify_session.py). The wider lesson is the one worth acting on: THREE separate defects found today all come from tests mutating process-global state (sys.modules stubs, a durable latch file) without containing it, and all three are invisible in CI because CI's fuller dependency set masks them. A conftest-level audit — no test may leave sys.modules or runtime_logs/ different from how it found them — would catch the class rather than the instances.
items.resolution_criteria: `pytest tests/test_[d-n]*.py tests/test_send_ping.py` reports 0 failures on a box where python-dotenv is NOT installed — the condition that exposes it; on a box that has it the test passes either way and proves nothing. VERIFIED 2026-08-27 by exactly that run.
items.resolution: Fixed in-session: addCleanup-based save/restore around the sys.modules pops.

items.title: Half the deploy/trainer/ units are absent from training-vm-cloud-init.yaml, so a re-provisioned trainer silently comes up without them
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-27 by counting each unit's name in deploy/training-vm-cloud-init.yaml: ict-drift-retrain 6 refs, ict-promotion-readiness 6 refs, ict-orderflow-capture 0, ict-offload-drain 0. So 2 of 4 declared trainer units are mirrored into the cloud-init and 2 are not. ict-drift-retrain's own header states the contract this violates: 'Mirrors the unit embedded in deploy/training-vm-cloud-init.yaml so a freshly provisioned trainer + a long-running trainer end up with the same unit body. Edits must stay in lock-step.'

⚠️ THIS ROW RECORDS A GAP I ADDED TO RATHER THAN SILENTLY JOINING IT. ict-offload-drain (R3, this session) is the second instance; ict-orderflow-capture is pre-existing and was found while checking whether the first one mattered. Adding the drain to cloud-init was deliberately NOT done here: the drain ships UNARMED and unenabled, so mirroring it now would put an inert unit on a fresh box and would also widen a transport-only PR into a provisioning change.

WHY IT IS LOW SEVERITY TODAY AND WHY IT WILL NOT STAY THAT WAY. Neither missing unit is enabled, so a re-provisioned trainer loses nothing that currently runs. items.source: session-2026-08-28-lane-a
items.title: The test suite writes real files into runtime_logs/pending_pings/ — the outbound notification inbox cloud_notifier DRAINS AND SENDS — 378 accumulated in one working tree
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-28 with a per-test before/after tree snapshot over the full suite (13,353 passed, 840 s): 32-61 findings per run, and EVERY ONE of them is under runtime_logs/pending_pings/ — one mechanism, not a scatter. The working tree had accumulated 378 files. STATE THE POPULATION: the count VARIES between two runs of the same suite (61 then 32), which is itself the finding that this is uncontained rather than a fixed set. WHY IT IS NOT MERELY LITTER. runtime_logs/pending_pings/ is not a scratch dir: src/bot/cloud_notifier.py calls it 'the canonical inbox' and DRAINS it (_drain_pending_pings) to send; src/runtime/execution_diagnostics.py and src/runtime/liveness_watchdog.py write to it as the operator diagnostic channel. So the test suite is manufacturing entries in a real outbound queue. THE PRACTICAL RISK TODAY IS LOW AND I AM SAYING SO PLAINLY: runtime_logs_dir() resolves to $DATA_DIR on the live VM (/data/bot-data/runtime_logs) and to the repo on a dev box, tests do not run on the live VM, and runtime_logs/ is gitignored (line 29) so nothing is committed. What is NOT low is the class: a test writing into a live send-queue is only safe by accident of where it runs, and the only thing between an accumulated ping and a real Telegram is that no drainer runs on a dev box. It also means the suite is not idempotent against its own working tree. NOT FIXED HERE, DELIBERATELY. The obvious fix — point RUNTIME_LOGS_DIR at a tmpdir session-wide in conftest — has a 13,353-test blast radius and would change what tests/test_runtime_paths_alignment.py is specifically written to assert about path resolution. Bundling that into the audit PR would have put a risky global change behind a detector change. The audit reports this as runtime_logs_written and DOES NOT ENFORCE it, so the denominator for the fix now exists.
items.proposed_fix: Decide between (a) a session-scoped RUNTIME_LOGS_DIR pointing at a tmpdir, with tests/test_runtime_paths_alignment.py exempted since it tests that override itself, or (b) an autouse fixture that snapshots and removes files the test created under pending_pings only. (a) is the real fix and needs its own PR and its own green full-suite run; (b) is cheaper and narrower. Either way, re-measure with TEST_ISOLATION_AUDIT and confirm runtime_logs_written drops to 0 — the audit is the check.
items.resolution_criteria: A full local suite reports runtime_logs_written=0 from the test-isolation audit, AND `ls runtime_logs/pending_pings/ | wc -l` does not grow across two consecutive full-suite runs on a tree where it started empty. A run that merely reports fewer is NOT resolution — the count already varies run to run.
items.evidence: Full suite 2026-08-28: runtime_logs_written 61 (run 1) then 32 (run 2), 100% under runtime_logs/pending_pings/. 378 files in the working tree. Writers: src/runtime/execution_diagnostics.py:41, src/runtime/liveness_watchdog.py:332, src/bot/cloud_notifier.py:36 (drainer). .gitignore:29 covers runtime_logs/.

updates.note: ⚠️ Re-validated and it is worse than a test-hygiene issue: the suite writes real files into the outbound NOTIFICATION inbox. A test run can therefore emit operator pings. Given this review's flags depend on that channel being trustworthy, this should be fixed before the next full-suite run.

items.title: BL-20260827-NOTIFY-SESSION-TEST-POPS-SYS-MODULES-AND-NEVER-RESTORES reads 'resolved / FIXED same session', but four call sites in the same file still pop sys.modules bare
items.detail: RECURRENCE-ADJACENT, filed deliberately rather than as a duplicate: the earlier row is genuinely resolved for the sites it covered, and the value here is that the fix was PARTIAL and the resolved row makes the file look clean. tests/test_notify_session.py grew a correct addCleanup-based _pop_and_restore helper (line 119) and two call sites use it (165, 180). FOUR OTHERS STILL POP BARE: lines 217-218, 242-243, 268-269, 294 do sys.modules.pop('src.runtime.notify'/'scripts.notify_session', None) with no restore. Found by the test-isolation audit measuring the full suite, not by re-reading the file — the four tests show up as module_replaced_real (they re-import after popping, so a NEW object lands in the slot rather than the slot going empty). WHY IT MATTERS LESS THAN THE ORIGINAL: the original defect deleted the conftest-provided `dotenv` stub on a box without python-dotenv, which broke five later tests outright. These four re-import, so the slot is repopulated with a working module — the residual risk is a later test holding a reference to the ORIGINAL object and diverging from what sys.modules now serves, which is a real but quieter failure mode. They are baselined in tests/isolation_baseline.py with this reason recorded.
items.proposed_fix: Route the four bare pops through the file's own existing _pop_and_restore helper. It already exists and already does the right thing; this is four call sites, not new machinery. Then delete those four entries from tests/isolation_baseline.py — the baseline is a ratchet and shrinking it is the point.
