items.source: session-2026-08-28-status-check
items.title: Two concurrent breakout_1 tickets each sized to $75 sum to $150 of open risk against a $142.83 daily-loss limit — prop sizing has no AGGREGATE cap, only a per-ticket one
items.detail: MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-28 off /api/bot/prop/{status,tickets}, not reconstructed. breakout_1 holds TWO filled tickets: ETHUSDT long entry 2527.16 sl 2480.71535714 qty 1.61482564, and SOLUSDT long entry 99.33 sl 96.33535714 qty 25.0447227. Each is sized to EXACTLY $75.00 of declared stop-risk (1.5% of the $5,000 account) — the per-ticket sizing is working precisely. Their SUM is $150.00. The ruleset's daily_loss_pct is 0.03, and the live route reports daily_loss_limit_usd = $142.83. So a same-day double stop-out is $150.00 against a $142.83 limit — a BREACH of the account-killer daily rule, reached by two individually-correct sizings. The static DD floor is the looser constraint here, not the tighter one: distance_to_dd_floor_usd is $176.00 (equity 4876 - floor 4700), so the daily rule binds ~$33 earlier. ⚠️ STATE THE POPULATION AND THE UNKNOWNS. (a) The equity is ONE operator-reported snapshot 31.1h old against a 24h threshold (status_freshness 'stale'), so 4876 can only have moved. (b) distance_to_daily_loss_usd is None and day_pnl_state is 'realized_unreported' — the system CANNOT say how much of today's $142.83 is already spent, so the true headroom may be smaller than $150 vs $142.83 suggests, never larger. (c) These are the tickets' DECLARED stops; the prop bridge has no broker feed, so whether the operator placed them at those levels is unverified by construction. (d) Both stopping out on the same UTC day is a scenario, not a prediction. ROOT: config/prop_rulesets/breakout.yaml sets max_position_pct: null and no aggregate/concurrency risk cap exists in the executor path — grep for daily_loss/max_concurrent/aggregate in src/prop/breakout_executor.py returns nothing. Sizing asks 'is THIS ticket within risk?' and never 'is the BOOK within the daily limit?'. The 4 'suppressed' tickets in the same window show some gate is refusing, but it is not an aggregate-risk gate.
items.proposed_fix: Add an aggregate open-risk pre-flight to the prop emit path: sum declared stop-risk over tickets in a non-terminal state for the account, and refuse (or downsize) a new ticket whose risk would take the total past the ruleset's daily_loss limit. It must read the SAME daily_loss_limit_usd the rule-distance panel computes rather than re-deriving it, or the gate and the panel will drift. ⚠️ It must ALSO be honest when day_pnl is unreported: with day_pnl_state='realized_unreported' the already-spent portion is UNKNOWN, so the cap should be applied against the FULL limit as an upper bound and the refusal must say the basis is unmeasured — never silently assume today's usage is zero.
items.resolution_criteria: A synthetic account holding tickets whose summed declared risk equals the daily-loss limit REFUSES the next ticket, and the refusal reason names the aggregate basis and whether day_pnl was measured. AND the live route can be shown reporting an aggregate figure a reader can check the per-ticket sum against — today no surface publishes the sum at all, which is why this needed hand arithmetic over the ticket list to find.
items.evidence: /api/bot/prop/status?account_id=breakout_1 2026-08-28: balance 4761.0, equity 4876.0, equity_provenance 'measured', status_age_hours 31.13, status_freshness 'stale', daily_loss_limit_usd 142.83, distance_to_daily_loss_usd None, day_pnl_state 'realized_unreported', static_dd_floor_usd 4700.0, distance_to_dd_floor_usd 176.0. /api/bot/prop/tickets: 2 filled, risk $75.00 each, sum $150.00. config/prop_rulesets/breakout.yaml: daily_loss_pct 0.03, max_position_pct null.

updates.note: ⚠️ HIGH AND IT IS THE STRONGEST SINGLE ARGUMENT FOR THE TIER-3 PROP ENFORCE FLIP. Two concurrent tickets each sized to $75 sum to $150 of open risk against a $142.83 daily-loss limit — so the account can be killed by two individually-compliant tickets. The gate I fixed the soak for (prop_risk_gate) grades ONE ticket against the cushion and has no aggregate view, which means even at `enforce` this specific path is not closed. Escalated in this review's report.

items.source: session-2026-08-28-prop-ingest
items.title: prop-report's concurrency group CANCELS a pending report — the exact outcome its own comment says it prevents — and on a manual bridge the report is the only record a close ever happened
items.detail: OBSERVED, not reasoned about. Three prop-report issues were opened ~3s apart on 2026-08-28. Run 33198343845 (SOLUSDT close) succeeded, run 33198356342 (account status) succeeded, and run 33198352180 (ETHUSDT close, -77.22) came back conclusion=CANCELLED having posted nothing. The ETHUSDT close simply did not exist in the journal until it was re-posted by hand as a fourth issue. THE COMMENT ASSERTS THE OPPOSITE OF THE BEHAVIOUR. .github/workflows/prop-report.yml:87-93 reads: 'Serialise so two report-backs never POST concurrently. cancel-in-progress:false so a second request queues + completes in turn rather than being silently dropped'. GitHub's concurrency semantics keep exactly ONE pending run per group: when a third run joins a group that already has one running and one pending, the PENDING one is cancelled. `cancel-in-progress: false` protects the RUNNING job; it says nothing about the queued one. So the setting delivers 'silently dropped' — the precise phrase the comment uses to describe what it avoids. This is the repo's standing defect class (a comment asserting a property the mechanism does not have) sitting on the write path of the ONE integration that has no broker feed to fall back on. WHY IT IS HIGH AND NOT MEDIUM: prop is a manual bridge; the operator's report IS the record. A dropped close leaves a position reading OPEN in the journal forever while it is flat at the venue, which is exactly the state prop_fills_staleness exists to alarm on — so the mechanism can manufacture the condition its sibling alarms about. It is also silent by construction: a cancelled run posts no issue comment, so the requester sees nothing unless they go read the Actions list.
items.proposed_fix: Do not rely on the concurrency group for serialisation of a queue deeper than 2. Either (a) drop the concurrency group and rely on the per-run SSH/curl timeouts plus the fact that ingest_report is a single POST to one chokepoint — concurrent POSTs to a SQLite writer are already serialised server-side; or (b) keep the group but have the workflow FAIL LOUDLY on cancellation by posting the un-ingested payload back to the issue so it is recoverable by hand. ⚠️ Whichever is chosen, the comment must be corrected in the same change: leaving prose that claims queue-and-complete is worse than the current behaviour, because it tells the next reader the payload is safe.
items.resolution_criteria: Three prop-report issues opened within 5 seconds of one another all result in three journalled rows, verified by reading /api/bot/prop/fills — not by the three runs reporting success, since the failure mode here is a run that never starts. AND the workflow comment no longer claims a pending request 'queues + completes in turn' unless that is what the configuration actually does.
items.evidence: Runs 33198343845 (success), 33198352180 (CANCELLED), 33198356342 (success), created 18:13:53 / 18:14:00 / 18:14:03Z. /api/bot/prop/fills showed no ETHUSDT close until issue #10379 re-posted it as fill id 39. .github/workflows/prop-report.yml:87-93.

updates.note: HIGH. Re-validated: the concurrency group CANCELS a pending report — the exact outcome its own comment says it prevents. On a manual bridge a cancelled report is a permanently unrecorded fill, and unrecorded fills are what make the cushion wrong.

items.source: session-2026-08-28-prop-ingest
items.title: The prop rule-distance panel rendered a FALSE static-DD floor BREACH (-19.29) because it applies fills by REPORT time, and the report shape carries no event time to apply them by
items.detail: OBSERVED LIVE on breakout_1 2026-08-28. An account_status of balance/equity 4757.93 was journalled at 18:14:11Z, then an ETHUSDT close of -77.22 (venue event time 07:09Z that same morning) was journalled at 18:17:52Z. prop_reconcile's snapshot_plus_fills reconstruction applies any fill whose reported_at is GREATER than the snapshot's reported_at, so it deducted the -77.22 from a balance that ALREADY INCLUDED it — the operator read 4757.93 off the terminal after both closes. distance_to_dd_floor_usd went to -19.29 (exactly 57.93 - 77.22), i.e. the safety panel showed the account as HAVING BREACHED its static drawdown floor and therefore dead. It had not: the true cushion is +57.93. Re-asserting the snapshot after the fill cleared it (fills_applied_since_snapshot 1 -> 0, balance_basis snapshot_plus_fills -> snapshot). ⚠️ THE RECONSTRUCTION IS A GOOD IDEA AND ITS DOCSTRING IS HONEST ABOUT WHY IT EXISTS — a stale snapshot ignores every close reported since, and it cites a measured 694h case where snapshot+fills reconstructed the balance to within $10. The gap is the KEY, not the concept: on a manual bridge reports arrive out of order BY CONSTRUCTION, because the operator reports when they can rather than when the event happened, and the fill report shape has NO event-time field at all — so the code cannot distinguish 'this close happened after you read your balance' from 'you reported this close late'. It is not choosing the wrong field; the right field does not exist. ⚠️ THE FAILURE IS ASYMMETRIC AND POINTS THE DANGEROUS WAY TWICE: a late-reported LOSS renders a false breach (panic on a live account), and a late-reported WIN inflates the cushion (a trade sized against headroom that is not there). === SECOND LIVE INSTANCE, 2026-08-31 (/system-review), AND IT ERRS THE OPPOSITE WAY. The 08-28 case rendered the cushion too PESSIMISTIC (a false BREACH at -19.29 on a deduction). Today the same mechanism renders it too OPTIMISTIC, which is the more dangerous polarity because nothing alarms. MEASURED: snapshot 18 balance 4754.00 (13:37:39Z) -> snapshot 19 balance 4787.34 (19:33:29Z), delta +33.34. The SOLUSDT close reported at 19:39:00Z carries venue pnl 35.28 GROSS of a -2.08 close commission, i.e. net +33.20 -- matching the observed +33.34 to $0.14. So snapshot 19 ALREADY REFLECTS that close, and `snapshot_plus_fills` adds it a second time because its reported_at (19:39:00Z) is 5.5 minutes AFTER the snapshot's. Live panel: equity_used_usd 4822.62 = 4787.34 + 35.28, distance_to_dd_floor_usd 122.62. TRUE cushion on the snapshot alone is 4787.34 - 4700 = 87.34, so the safety panel OVERSTATES the distance to an account-killer floor by 35.28 -- 40% of the real cushion. TWO THINGS THIS INSTANCE ADDS. (1) The defect is BIDIRECTIONAL, so a fix that only guards against the false-breach direction would leave the optimistic half live; both come from the same 'apply by report time' rule. (2) It ALSO makes the prop_fills_stale banner a FALSE POSITIVE from the same root: prop_fills_staleness counts fills with `start < reported_at <= end` (verified in code, not inferred), so the 19:39:00Z report falls outside the 13:37:39 -> 19:33:29 window and the detector reads fills_in_window: 0 and pages 'balance moved with NO fills reported'. It is latched right now and shows on /api/bot/notifications at severity `alert`. One root cause, two surfaces, one of them an operator page -- which is the desensitized-alarm risk this repo keeps paying for. ⚠️ The residual $0.14 is unexplained and is stated rather than rounded away; the attribution rests on it being small, not on it being zero.
items.proposed_fix: Add an optional event-time field to the fill report shape (e.g. `event_at` / `closed_at`, ISO-8601) and prefer it over `reported_at` when deciding whether a fill post-dates the snapshot; fall back to reported_at when absent, which preserves today's behaviour for every existing row. ⚠️ It must stay THREE-state rather than silently falling back: a fill with no event time is 'we cannot place this in time', which is a different fact from 'it happened after the snapshot' — and the panel should say which basis it used, the way balance_basis already names snapshot vs snapshot_plus_fills. The screenshot parser should populate event_at where the terminal shows it (the History rows carry a timestamp per trade).
items.resolution_criteria: A fill whose event time PRECEDES the latest snapshot but is reported AFTER it does not move distance_to_dd_floor_usd, and the panel names the basis it used. Reproduce with the measured case: snapshot 4757.93 at T, then a -77.22 close with event_at 07:09Z reported at T+4min, must still read +57.93 rather than -19.29.
items.evidence: /api/bot/prop/status?account_id=breakout_1 2026-08-28: distance_to_dd_floor_usd -19.29 with fills_applied_since_snapshot 1 / fills_pnl_since_snapshot_usd -77.22 / balance_basis snapshot_plus_fills; after re-asserting the snapshot at 18:24:08Z, +57.93 with fills_applied 0 / balance_basis snapshot. src/prop/prop_reconcile.py:311-345 (`at <= snap_at` on reported_at).

updates.note: ⚠️ HIGH AND DIRECTLY QUALIFIES THE NUMBER THIS REVIEW LEADS WITH. The panel rendered a FALSE static-DD floor BREACH (-19.29) by applying fills by REPORT time. Today's read shows fills_applied_since_snapshot 0, so the $55.00 cushion I report is not affected by this path right now — but the same mechanism could make the next reading wrong in either direction. Read with BL-20260827-PROP-CUSHION-IGNORES-COMMITTED-OPEN-RISK: one says the cushion is optimistic, this says it can be spuriously pessimistic.

items.source: session-2026-08-28-r3-arm
items.title: ict-offload-drain.service's Description still reads '(UNARMED by default)' on a trainer where it IS armed — every journal line contradicts the next one
items.detail: OBSERVED 2026-08-28 in the trainer journal immediately after arming. systemd logs the unit Description on start and finish, so the journal now reads: 'Starting ICT offload drain — ingest runner-trained models into the registry (UNARMED by default)...' followed one line later by the script's own 'offload-drain: ARMED (OFFLOAD_DRAIN_APPLY=1) — the registry WILL be written.' Both lines are emitted by the same run, one contradicting the other. The Description was accurate when the unit shipped (installed-disabled + Environment=OFFLOAD_DRAIN_APPLY=0) and became wrong the moment a drop-in armed it. ⚠️ THIS IS COSMETIC BUT IT IS THE REPO'S OWN DEFECT CLASS — prose asserting a property the mechanism does not have — sitting on the log surface an operator reads when they want to know whether the drain is writing. The runtime is correct and self-describing (the script prints its real state from the env var), so nothing is mis-behaving; the risk is a reader trusting the Description over the line under it.
items.proposed_fix: Drop '(UNARMED by default)' from the unit Description — the DEFAULT is a property of the shipped Environment line and of the wrapper's own fail-safe, not something the Description should assert, because a drop-in can change it without touching the unit. State what it does, not what it is set to; the script already prints the live state on every run. Note the arming lives in /etc/systemd/system/ict-offload-drain.service.d/armed.conf so `systemctl cat` shows both.
items.resolution_criteria: `journalctl -u ict-offload-drain.service` shows no line claiming UNARMED on a trainer where `systemctl show ict-offload-drain.service -p Environment` returns OFFLOAD_DRAIN_APPLY=1.
items.evidence: Trainer journal 2026-08-28T19:51:11Z: 'Starting ICT offload drain — ... (UNARMED by default)...' immediately followed by 'offload-drain: ARMED (OFFLOAD_DRAIN_APPLY=1)'. deploy/trainer/ict-offload-drain.service Description line.

updates.note: Re-validated: field beats comment, on a systemd Description. Cheap.

items.source: session-2026-08-28-r3-arm
items.title: The armed drain printed [ingested] and exited 0, but a wc -l in the very next shell command still read the OLD registry line count — unexplained, and it makes the obvious post-write check unreliable
items.detail: OBSERVED, and I could not explain it, so it is filed rather than smoothed over. Sequence in ONE trainer command: `wc -l registry.jsonl` -> 95; `OFFLOAD_DRAIN_APPLY=1 bash scripts/ops/run_offload_drain.sh` -> '[ingested] ... registered ... and verified loadable', summary {"ingested": 1}, exit 0; `wc -l registry.jsonl` -> **95 again**. A separate dispatch ~4 minutes later read 96, with `grep -c '^{'` also 96 and the file confirmed to end in a newline, and exactly 1 offload row. So the write DID land and the end state is correct and triple-checked — but the count taken immediately after the drain reported success did not reflect it. ⚠️ WHY IT MATTERS DESPITE BEING BENIGN HERE: 'run the drain, then assert the registry grew' is the natural verification an operator or a future automation writes, and on this evidence that assertion can read stale and be WRONG in the reassuring-then-alarming direction (it looks like the ingest silently did nothing). Candidate causes NOT established: an atomic temp-file+rename whose visibility lagged the process exit; a buffered write flushed at interpreter teardown after the wrapper's `exec`ed python returned; or an NFS/overlay stat cache on the trainer's filesystem. I did not instrument any of them.
items.proposed_fix: Establish the cause before changing anything — re-run the drain on a fresh drop with `stat`/`ls -i` and an `fsync` check around the write, and confirm whether the registry writer uses temp+rename. If it does and the rename is the lag, the fix is for the drain to re-read and REPORT the post-write row count itself (it already knows what it wrote), so callers never need a separate shell-level count that can race it.
items.resolution_criteria: A `wc -l` taken in the same command immediately after an armed drain that reports `ingested` reflects the new row count — OR the drain prints the authoritative post-write count itself and the docs tell callers to read that rather than counting the file.
items.evidence: trainer-vm-diag #10386 (drain reports ingested, wc -l 95 before AND after) vs #10387 four minutes later (wc -l 96, grep -c '^{' 96, trailing newline present, 1 offload row).

updates.note: Re-validated: [ingested] + exit 0 before the row is readable is a write-then-read race that makes the success report premature.

items.source: session-2026-08-29-r6-residency
items.title: The one data stream in the system that cannot be re-derived — the trainer's 24/7 L2 order-flow capture — has NO monitor, and its process staying 'active' is not evidence it is capturing
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-28/29 while answering R6 (diag #10391, #10392). `ict-orderflow-capture.service` on the trainer polls the BTCUSDT order book every 2s and writes 5m microstructure bars (ofi / buy_vol / sell_vol / rel_spread_mean / microprice_dev / n_snapshots). It has run 44 days continuously (since 2026-07-15, PID 728). Its own consuming manifest (ml/configs/btc-regime-5m-lgbm-flow-v1.yaml, echoed in the offload-inbox copy) states: 'The capture is FORWARD-ONLY (no L2 history), so evaluate on the captured window' — L2 depth is not retrievable historically from the public API, so a minute not captured is gone permanently. NOTHING WATCHES IT. Measured: zero references to 'orderflow' anywhere in src/runtime/ or scripts/ops/ alerting code; the unit is absent from the diag canonical-units allowlist; and `trainer_reachability_alert` — the only trainer watchdog — reads the mtime of the trainer_mirror published by the SEPARATE ict-trainer-publish.timer, which would keep advancing normally with this capture dead. WORSE, THE UNIT'S OWN STATE IS NOT THE SIGNAL: the process catches poll errors and continues (its journal carries repeated '[orderflow] order_book error: RequestTimeout' lines while ActiveState stayed 'active'), so 'active (running)' is compatible with writing nothing. That is the silent-failure shape — and the loss it hides is the only loss on this box that no amount of re-running can repair. Related but DISTINCT from BL-20260829-TRAINER-DISK-92-PCT-THREATENS-THE-UNBACKFILLABLE-CAPTURE (that is the likeliest CAUSE of a stall; this is the absence of DETECTION, and would still bite on a crash, a creds change, or an API break).
items.proposed_fix: Watch the DATA's freshness, not the unit's ActiveState — the two came apart in the evidence above. Cheapest correct version: have publish_trainer_mirror.sh stamp the newest microstructure row's `ts` (and its age) into trainer_status.json, which already rsyncs to the live VM every 2 min and is already read by trainer_reachability_alert — so this needs no new transport, no trader->trainer SSH, and no new timer. Then alert when that age exceeds a small multiple of the 300s bar. Grade it with states that do not collapse, per the repo's collapsed-state rule: `fresh` / `stale` / `absent` (no row ever) / `unreadable` (we could not look) — an unreadable stamp must never read as fresh. Consider also surfacing n_snapshots-per-bar, since a degraded ~85% poll rate is a different and milder condition than a stopped capture and the two should not share one alarm.
items.resolution_criteria: A capture-freshness signal exists, is READ by a consumer that can page the operator, and has been observed firing on a real or deliberately-induced stall — verified by seeing the alert, not by reading the code. A passing unit test is NOT the observable (the defect here is precisely that the obvious health check passes while the data stops). The four states must be distinguishable at the consumer.
items.evidence: diag #10391: `ict-orderflow-capture.service` enabled+active, ExecStart poll-seconds 2.0 depth 5. diag #10392: `systemctl status` -> 'active (running) since Wed 2026-07-15 07:13:32 UTC; 1 month 14 days ago', Main PID 728, 87.4M, CPU 3h53m; newest data row ts 2026-08-28T23:50:00Z vs same-command `date -u` 23:58:09; n_snapshots 127-128 per bar; journal shows repeated RequestTimeout while unit stayed active. Repo-side: grep 'orderflow' over src/runtime/ + scripts/ops/ returns zero alerting hits; absent from scripts/check_diag_unit_allowlist.py and diag.py. Full writeup: docs/research/R6-VM-RESIDENCY-VERDICT-2026-08-28.md sections 2 and 6.1.

updates.note: ⚠️ THIS ROW CHANGED HOW I PRIORITISED THE TRAINER DISK, and I want that recorded. The one data stream that cannot be re-derived — 24/7 L2 order-flow capture — has NO monitoring, and it lives on a box at 91.7% disk whose schedule is undeclared (BL-20260827-TRAINER-SCHEDULE-IS-UNDECLARED-THE-VM-IS-A-PET) and whose fill RATE is structurally unknowable (BL-20260825-TRAINER-DISK-IS-MEASURED-EVERY-2-MINUTES-AND-ACCUMULATED-NEVER). Those four rows together are not four medium issues; they are one high-severity risk of permanent, unrecoverable data loss. Escalated to operator_priorities in this review's report.

items.source: session-2026-08-29-r6-residency
items.title: Trainer disk is 92% full (3.9G free) and the largest trees are research byproduct — the thing a full disk stops is the one capture that cannot be re-run
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-28 (diag #10391, #10392): /dev/sda1 45G, 42G used, 3.9G avail, 92%. The 28G repo tree is dominated by byproduct: datasets-out/market_features 11G (32 version dirs across 4 symbols), ml/experiments-runs 4.7G, runtime_logs/m20_exit_head 2.5G, datasets-out/market_raw 1.3G. WHY THIS IS NOT ROUTINE DISK HYGIENE: the same box runs ict-orderflow-capture, whose output is forward-only L2 data that cannot be re-derived from any source (see BL-20260829-ORDERFLOW-CAPTURE-IS-IRREPLACEABLE-AND-UNMONITORED). Every other consumer of this disk loses time to a full disk; that one loses data permanently — and because nothing monitors the capture, a disk-full stall would be SILENT. STATE THE POPULATION: RESEARCH-WORKFLOW-ARCHITECTURE-2026-08-27 section 3 reported 41G used on 08-27 and it reads 42G now, but BOTH are coarse `du -sh`/`df -h` readings, so I am NOT claiming a growth rate or a days-to-full figure from two rounded points — only that the headroom is thin and what it protects is irreplaceable. Note also that section 3 already established the cache cannot be fixed by GC: 41 manifests pin 111 of 115 version dirs, so this is a retention-policy question, not a cleanup chore.

A RATE IS NOW MEASURED (2026-08-29, diag #10394 + #10395), and the earlier refusal to claim one from two rounded readings stands — these are byte-precise:
  2026-08-29T00:18:12Z  free = 4,237,279,232 B
  2026-08-29T00:47:50Z  free = 4,067,926,016 B
  delta -169,353,216 B over 1,778 s  =>  -327.0 MiB/h  =>  ~11.9 HOURS of headroom at that rate.
⚠️ STATE THE POPULATION: n=2 readings 29.6 min apart, and BOTH were taken while ict-trainer.service was ACTIVATING (ExecMainStartTimestamp 00:05:52, ExecMainExitTimestamp n/a — the nightly rebuild had not finished). This is a MID-REBUILD instantaneous rate, NOT a steady-state trend, and must not be extrapolated to a daily figure. The rebuild rewrites market_features in place (1.35 GB BTCUSDT/5m/v002 alone), so the trough within a cycle is the quantity that matters and it has not been observed across a full cycle yet. Notably no file >20 MB was written in the 10 min before reading #2 while free space still fell, so the consumption at that moment was NOT the large frames.
WHY IT IS RECORDED AS A CONCERN RATHER THAN AN ALARM: ~11.9h is long enough that the rebuild completing could reverse it entirely, and short enough that it should not be left unwatched. The capture was verified HEALTHY at reading #2 (unit active, 24,224 rows, newest row 2026-08-29T00:40:00Z against a same-command now of 00:48:08Z), so nothing has been lost. The compounding risk from BL-20260829-ORDERFLOW-CAPTURE-IS-IRREPLACEABLE-AND-UNMONITORED is unchanged: if the disk does fill, the capture stops and NOTHING would report it.

✅ THE ~11.9h FIGURE HAS INFLECTED AND THE CLOCK IS STOOD DOWN (2026-08-29, diag #10396). Do not quote 11.9h as current — it was a MID-REBUILD rate and it behaved exactly as the caveat said it might.
  00:47:50Z free 4,067,926,016 -> 00:55:57Z free 4,057,878,528 = -10,047,488 B / 487 s = -70.8 MiB/h => ~54.6 HOURS of headroom, against -327.0 MiB/h => 11.9h on the previous window. A 4.6x drop.
THE CAUSE IS ESTABLISHED, not inferred: ict-trainer.service logged {'status':'cycle_end','overall_rc':0,'trained':67,'skipped':9,'failed':0} at 00:53:43, INSIDE that window. ⚠️ Note the unit still reads ActiveState=activating / SubState=start / ExecMainExitTimestamp=n/a AFTER logging cycle_end — so the UNIT state is not a usable signal for 'the cycle finished'; the journal is.
THE 'no file >20 MB yet space still fell' PUZZLE IS RESOLVED, and it hands the retention question a number. The consumption is MANY MEDIUM files, not a few large ones: ~1.41 MB of model_state.json per trained model x 67 models = ~94 MB PER NIGHTLY CYCLE into ml/experiments-runs (already 4.7 GB), plus append-only logs — publish.jsonl 18.2 MB, dataset_audit.jsonl 8.7 MB, registry.jsonl 4.5 MB, training_cycle.jsonl 2.0 MB. That is exactly the category RESEARCH-WORKFLOW-ARCHITECTURE section 3 calls 'outputs that should be published, not retained', now with a per-cycle cost attached.
RECOVERABLE SPACE EXISTS AND WAS DELIBERATELY NOT TOUCHED (Tier-2, and the operator was asleep): /tmp 1.2 GB + journald 504 MB + apt cache 132 MB = ~1.8 GB against 4.06 GB free — i.e. the immediate pressure is relievable WITHOUT touching a single pinned dataset version, which matters because unpinning a version changes what a re-run measures (the R1 reproducibility half). Deleted-but-open handles: 0 bytes, so nothing is being held by a live process.
CAPTURE VERIFIED HEALTHY THROUGHOUT all three readings (24,218 -> 24,224 -> 24,226 rows; newest row 2026-08-29T00:50:00Z against a same-command now of 00:56:08Z). Nothing was lost at any point.

✅ STEADY STATE MEASURED (2026-08-29, diag #10397) — AND IT IS ESSENTIALLY FLAT. Do not quote 54.6h either; that window still straddled the cycle boundary. The first post-cycle window is the steady state:
  00:55:57Z free 4,057,878,528 -> 02:12:14Z free 4,057,395,200 = -483,328 B over 76.3 min = -0.36 MiB/h => ~10,673 hours (~445 days).
THE THREE WINDOWS TOGETHER ARE THE POINT, and they are the argument for never quoting an instantaneous rate from a system with a duty cycle:
  00:18->00:47 mid-cycle    -327.0  MiB/h ->    11.9 h
  00:47->00:55 spans end     -70.8  MiB/h ->    54.6 h
  00:55->02:12 post-cycle     -0.36 MiB/h -> ~10,673 h
A ~900x spread across three windows of the same night. The 11.9h reading was real and was ENTIRELY the nightly rebuild; the box is not draining in steady state. The disk pressure is therefore a LEVEL problem (92% full, thin absolute headroom) and NOT a trend problem — which changes the remedy: the retention policy is worth taking on its merits, not as a race against a clock.
⚠️ WHAT STILL STANDS, unchanged by this: 4.06 GB absolute headroom against a nightly cycle that transiently consumes ~170 MB while running, on a box whose irreplaceable capture NOTHING monitors (BL-20260829-ORDERFLOW-CAPTURE-IS-IRREPLACEABLE-AND-UNMONITORED). A flat trend does not make a full disk survivable, it just means it is not imminent.
SHARPENED, and worth knowing before anyone gates on unit state: ict-trainer.service logged cycle_end at 00:53:43 but ExecMainExitTimestamp is 01:24:14 with ActiveState=inactive — the UNIT lagged its own journal by ~31 MINUTES. Reading unit state as 'the cycle finished' would have been wrong by half an hour.
Capture healthy across all four readings (24,218 -> 24,224 -> 24,226 -> 24,241 rows; newest 2026-08-29T02:05:00Z against a same-command now of 02:12:14Z).
items.proposed_fix: Two separable steps, and the first is the urgent one. (1) Protect the capture from its neighbours regardless of the retention decision — the capture needs 87MB RAM and a few MB/day, so the correct guarantee is that byproduct cannot starve it. (2) Take the retention decision section 3 identified and nobody has taken: when may a manifest's dataset-version pin be released? ml/experiments-runs (4.7G) and runtime_logs/m20_exit_head (2.5G) are outputs that should be PUBLISHED and dropped rather than retained — which is the same landing thesis M40 is built on, applied to the trainer's own disk. Do NOT free space by deleting pinned version dirs without that policy: an unpinned rebuild changes what a re-run measures, which is the reproducibility half of R1.
items.resolution_criteria: Either headroom is restored under a WRITTEN retention policy (not an ad-hoc delete), or the capture is relocated off this disk, or a disk-pressure alert exists that names the capture as the thing at risk and has been observed firing. A one-off `rm` that frees space without a policy does NOT resolve this — it resets the clock and the next session re-derives the same finding.
items.evidence: diag #10391 + #10392: `df -h /` -> 45G/42G/3.9G/92%; du breakdown as listed; `find market_features -mindepth 3 -maxdepth 3 -type d | wc -l` -> 32. Writeup: docs/research/R6-VM-RESIDENCY-VERDICT-2026-08-28.md section 6.1.

updates.note: RE-MEASURED 2026-08-29: 91.7% / 4.03 GB free (this row recorded 92% / 3.9 G). Severity is filed `low` and I think that is WRONG given the row's own content — the thing a full disk stops is the unbackfillable capture. Recommend raising to high and consolidating with BL-20260829-ORDERFLOW-CAPTURE-IS-IRREPLACEABLE-AND-UNMONITORED. Live re-measurement 2026-08-29: trainer at 91.7% used / 4.03 GB free of 48.28 GB, warning banner firing. ⚠️ This review RAISED the priority of the trainer-disk cluster after reading BL-20260829-ORDERFLOW-CAPTURE-IS-IRREPLACEABLE-AND-UNMONITORED: a full disk stops the ONE data stream that cannot be re-derived.

items.source: session-2026-08-29-alpaca-golive
items.title: alpaca_live is declared to risk 2.5-3.3x MORE per trade than the paper book that is supposed to be its forward record — the mirror mirrors the roster, not the sizing
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 by reading config/accounts.yaml (field, not prose): alpaca_live risk_pct = 0.05; alpaca_portfolio (its declared paper_role: portfolio mirror) = 0.02; alpaca_paper = 0.015. So the real-money account is declared to risk 2.5x the portfolio mirror and 3.33x the soak book, per trade. WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A TUNING DETAIL: the S-PAPER-PORTFOLIO design makes alpaca_portfolio the 'paper-money mirror of the actual live-traded portfolio' precisely so a live decision can lean on paper evidence, and the alpaca_live go-live sequence (BL-20260824-ALPACA-LIVE-GOLIVE-SEQUENCE) leans on the mirrors for its ONLY available gross-exposure basis (1.8422 min / 1.8569 median / 2.0062 max) because the live account's own soak is a flat book by construction. But position sizing is the term that differs, so a track record accrued at 1.5-2% does not transfer to a book that will trade at 5% — the drawdown and exposure distributions scale with it, which is exactly what the ceiling is being chosen from. DISTINCT FROM BL-20260823-ALPACA-PORTFOLIO-MIRROR-MISSING-TWO-LIVE-LEGS, and filed with similar_ok after reading it: that row is about WHICH LEGS are mirrored (roster coverage, 2 of 16 absent). This is about the SIZING FRACTION on the legs that ARE mirrored. A perfect roster fix would leave this untouched, and the two compound — the mirror is incomplete in membership AND unrepresentative in magnitude on the members it has. NOT ASSERTED: which value is wrong. 0.05 on a $200 account is $10 of risk, which BL-20260826-ALPACA-LIVE-AT-200-USD-CANNOT-SIZE-ITS-LARGEST-SYMBOLS shows cannot buy one whole share of 4 of 10 priced symbols — so lowering it makes that worse and raising the mirrors changes a running soak. That is the trade-off to decide, not a defect to patch.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE EXPOSURE CEILING (derived from code, not assumed) — this is why the row is actionable rather than cosmetic. src/units/accounts/risk.py::_size_unbounded computes risk_usdt = balance_usdt * risk_pct; raw_qty = risk_usdt / (risk_distance * cvu). So notional/equity = risk_pct * entry / risk_distance — EQUITY CANCELS and the gross-exposure multiple is LINEAR in risk_pct. That is exactly the quantity max_gross_exposure_pct governs (RiskManager.gross_exposure returns (open_notional, equity, exposure_multiple)). BL-20260824-ALPACA-LIVE-GOLIVE-SEQUENCE's 2026-08-25 update proposed the mirrors' 1.8422/1.8569/2.0062 multiple as STEP 1's ONLY available basis — but that was measured at risk_pct 0.02 while alpaca_live declares 0.05, so the same signals on live demand ~4.6-5.0x, not 1.85-2.01x. A ~2.0 ceiling taken from the mirror would therefore clamp essentially every live trade, which gross-exposure-governance-DESIGN.md section 6 names as WORSE THAN NO CEILING. The mirror's basis and the live risk_pct cannot both stand. BOUNDS ON THE INFERENCE, stated rather than buried: (i) it scales DEMAND — whole-share flooring is a hard non-linearity at $200 and floors small orders to zero, so filled multiples would be lower and lumpier (consistent with BL-20260826-ALPACA-LIVE-AT-200-USD-CANNOT-SIZE-ITS-LARGEST-SYMBOLS, not contradicting it); the linear argument is the right one for a FUNDED account where flooring stops binding; (ii) the mirror roster differs by 2 of 16 legs so aggregate concurrency is not identical; (iii) the live multiple was NOT re-measured and cannot be while the account is dry_run and flat — the original chicken-and-egg. MEASURED SAME SESSION, and the consequence is worse than the inference that opened this row. Population: all 4178 rows of order_packages paged via the Data Explorer (order_state 'applied' asserted per page; accumulated count 4178 equals the server's own total), of which 369 carry one of the 16 strategies routed to alpaca_live, 369 of 369 gradeable (0 missing entry/sl, 0 zero-distance), window 2026-06-16 through 2026-08-28. Because entry/risk_distance is STRATEGY geometry and account-independent (only risk_pct is an account property), the DEMANDED multiple is measurable without the account ever having traded - which is the basis BL-20260809-EXPOSURE-SOAK-NOT-YET-TAKEN lacks, since alpaca_live's realised soak reads 0.0 on 91 of 91 rows correctly. Result: entry/risk_distance median 79.08, p95 254.25. So the DEMANDED SINGLE-TRADE gross multiple is median 3.95x at risk_pct 0.05 against 1.58x at 0.02 - i.e. the MEDIAN SINGLE TRADE on the live account demands 3.95x the whole account, before any concurrency. Corroborated independently: BL-20260823-ALPACA-RISK-SIZING-EXCEEDS-ACCOUNT-NOTIONAL-AT-EVERY-FUNDING-LEVEL measured 'up to 12.37x' over 6 legs; this run gives p95 12.71x over 369 packages by a different route. THE CEILING IS THE WRONG KNOB. At the mirror-derived 2.0x, 307 of 369 single trades (83.2%) breach it on their own; and to let the largest-sample leg (tlt_pullback_1h, n=74) trade at its MEDIAN the ceiling must be at least 11.06x, which on a $200 account is a rubber stamp rather than a risk control. There is therefore no ceiling value that both permits the book and constrains risk while risk_pct is 0.05, so STEP 1 of the go-live sequence is misframed: the binding parameter is this row's risk_pct mismatch, not the ceiling. Tier-3 - proposed, not changed. Full derivation, per-leg table and the three checks that did NOT become findings: docs/research/ALPACA-LIVE-GOLIVE-STATUS-2026-08-29.md section 7.
items.proposed_fix: Decide and RECORD which of three holds, rather than letting the divergence stand undeclared: (a) the mirrors should match live at 0.05 — then the existing paper track record was accrued under different sizing and should not be quoted for the exposure ceiling without restating; (b) live should come down to the mirrors' 0.015-0.02 — then re-check it against the whole-share floor, since it makes the sizing problem worse; or (c) they are deliberately different, in which case say so in accounts.yaml next to the values and state what the mirror IS evidence for. Whichever is chosen, the gross-exposure basis in the go-live sequence must name the risk_pct it was measured at.
items.resolution_criteria: config/accounts.yaml carries either matched risk_pct across alpaca_live and its portfolio mirror, or an explicit recorded statement of why they differ AND what the mirror's evidence is therefore good for. Additionally the go-live sequence's exposure basis cites the risk_pct it was measured at. NOT sufficient: changing one number quietly — the point is that the mirror's evidential value is currently overstated, and a silent edit leaves the next reader with the same unstated assumption.
items.evidence: config/accounts.yaml read 2026-08-29: alpaca_live.risk.risk_pct=0.05, alpaca_portfolio.risk.risk_pct=0.02, alpaca_paper.risk.risk_pct=0.015 (alpaca_options_paper 0.015). Mirror multiples from the go-live row's 2026-08-25 update. Writeup: docs/research/ALPACA-LIVE-GOLIVE-STATUS-2026-08-29.md section 3.1.

updates.note: Re-validated: alpaca_live declared to risk 2.5-3.3x MORE per trade than the paper book that is supposed to be its forward record. Third independent way the mirrors do not mirror (with the missing-legs row and the symbol-slot-starvation row). A mirror that differs in risk_pct, roster AND symbol allocation is not a forward record at all — and the alpaca_live go-live decision rests on it.

items.tier: 1 (a re-run + a row disposition; the code change it follows from is already merged)
items.source: session-2026-08-29-lane-b-verdict-diff
items.title: Lane P removed the DRAWDOWN contribution to survival/p_breach on standard accounts (correctly), leaving them sensitive ONLY to single-day loss concentration — and the compat gate still consumes both with full authority while never branching on the `dd_model_state` field that says the drawdown was not modelled
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 by isolating Lane P's drawdown half (docs/research/lane-p-compat-verdict-diff-2026-08-29.md section 6). Method: git worktree at f2ea9e44^ vs HEAD, ledger byte-identical, config copied across, and — the step that makes it an isolation rather than a confound — EVERY balance seeded at exactly 10,000, the same figure the BEFORE arm hardcodes, so the size term is numerically identical in both arms and only the drawdown code path differs. Control: 11 of 11 accounts equal size. RESULT on a ledger carrying a sustained -20R drawdown: 10 of 11 accounts move skip -> ROUTE, with `survival` going 0.800-0.857 -> EXACTLY 1.0 and `p_breach` 0.143-0.200 -> EXACTLY 0.0 on every one. breakout_1 (a PROP account on a declared prop ruleset, where a static terminal floor IS correct) does not move — which is the control showing the change is correctly scoped to the standard arm. WHAT IT MEANS: on standard accounts the survival/breach gate is now INERT. A rule that refuses one trade and resets at midnight cannot TERMINATE an account, so there is nothing for a survival simulation to measure and both figures collapse to constants. Two of the gate's three criteria therefore no longer discriminate between books on standard accounts; what gating remains comes from the return metric alone. THE DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE, which is why this is filed rather than noted: BL-20260803-GLD-ALPACA-PORTFOLIO-SURVIVAL-SKIP (kept_open) blocks a routing decision on the grounds that 'gld_pullback_1h ... FAILS that account's survival/breach gate at corrected cost (survival 0.871<0.90, P(breach) 0.132>0.10)'. That is exactly the shape this change eliminates — in the isolated run alpaca_portfolio moves survival 0.8167 -> 1.0 and p_breach 0.1833 -> 0.0. If those are now constants, that row's blocking finding cannot be reproduced, and a routing decision is being held back by a verdict the code no longer produces. DISTINCT FROM the two rows that describe the DEFECT (BL-20260827-STANDARD-ARM-MISMODELS-INTRADAY-MAX-DD-AS-A-TERMINAL-FLOOR and BL-20260827-COMPAT-MATRIX-STANDARD-ARM-BORROWED-A-TYPE-WITH-NO-MEMBER-FOR-ITS-CONCEPT, both still open) — filed with similar_ok after reading them. Those say the old model was WRONG; this says what the FIX did to the gate's discriminating power and to one specific downstream row. Fixing a defect and knowing the blast radius of the fix are different findings, and only the second one unblocks a routing decision. NOT ASSERTED: that BL-20260803 is void. I did not re-run its specific GLD ledger (the emit half needs Yahoo, firewalled in-sandbox). The narrow checkable claim is that the criteria it cites now return constants on standard accounts.

⚠️ 2026-08-29 — MY OWN PREDICTION HERE WAS WRONG ON MECHANISM, corrected by the real-ledger run (issue #10399). I wrote that alpaca_portfolio would show 'survival 0.8167 -> 1.0 and p_breach 0.1833 -> 0.0'. It does NOT. On the real GLD ledger it returns UNGRADED with surv=None / P(breach)=None, as do all ten standard accounts.
WHY THE DIFFERENCE, and it is entirely my synthetic setup: I SEEDED balances into a local balance_snapshots table to run the isolation. The gld-compat-matrix workflow supplies no balance source at all, so account size resolves 'unreadable' -> UNGRADED before survival is ever computed. My constants finding (survival=1.0, p_breach=0.0) is REAL and reproducible — but only on the path where a size RESOLVES. On the runner that path is never reached.
SO THE DIRECTION OF THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES AND THE MECHANISM DOES NOT: BL-20260803's objection is indeed unreproducible on current main, but because the criterion cannot be computed, not because it became a constant. Both statements matter and they are not interchangeable — the second would have implied the gate now passes everything, which is false; it grades nothing.
This is the second time in this lane that a claim of mine held on the population I measured and failed to generalise. The transferable lesson is the same one: state the surface, not just the number.
items.proposed_fix: Two separable steps. (1) Re-run BL-20260803's GLD compat matrix on current main — dispatch gld-compat-matrix.yml, which has Yahoo — and dispose of that row on the result: if the survival/breach objection no longer reproduces, say so explicitly rather than leaving a routing decision blocked by a verdict the code cannot produce. (2) Decide, separately and as an operator call, whether a standard-account compat gate SHOULD retain a survival axis at all. If a non-terminal brake genuinely cannot kill an account then constants are correct and the gate is simply narrower than it looks — in which case say so in the matrix output, because a reader seeing 'survival 1.0' will read it as a measurement rather than as a structural constant. If instead the intended question was 'how often does this book get its trades refused', that is a DIFFERENT quantity and nothing currently computes it.
items.resolution_criteria: TWO things, and the first no longer depends on the second. (1) Re-run BL-20260803's alpaca_portfolio survival check against a DAY-CONCENTRATED loss book and record whether the 0.871 verdict reproduces — that is what settles the held routing decision, and the 'constants' reading must not be used to settle it. (2) Either make `route` branch on `dd_model_state` (a `not_terminal` state means the survival/breach conjuncts are measuring only the daily-loss axis, and the verdict should SAY so rather than read as a full durability gate), or register the field with collapsed-state-guard so the missing consumer is enforced rather than left to a comment. A comment instructing a human to read a field is not a consumer.

updates.note: Re-validated: if survival=1.0 and p_breach=0.0 are CONSTANTS on every standard account, two of the compat gate's three criteria are vacuous. That would void BL-20260803-GLD-ALPACA-PORTFOLIO-SURVIVAL-SKIP's basis — which is why it is filed as 'may void' rather than asserted. Correct posture; needs the measurement.

items.correction_2026_08_31: ⚠️ THIS ROW'S CENTRAL CLAIM WAS TOO STRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN RESTATED IN A NEW ROW. It read: 'Lane P makes survival=1.0 and p_breach=0.0 CONSTANTS on every standard account'. They are NOT constants. MEASURED 2026-08-31 by reading the code rather than re-running the sim: `daily_loss` remains a TERMINAL breach cause in the simulation (src/prop/montecarlo.py sets breach_cause='daily_loss' and terminates the path), and `_standard_ruleset` passes `daily_loss_pct` straight through from the account's risk block. Measured against config/accounts.yaml: 11 of 11 accounts declare `daily_loss_pct` (0.05 on nine, 0.10 on alpaca_live, 0.03 on the prop breakout_1). So the terminal path is ARMED on every account and survival is not structurally constant. WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, and it is narrower and more useful: Lane P removed the DRAWDOWN contribution to p_breach on standard accounts — correctly, because a refusal brake is not an account-killer — so the two figures are now INSENSITIVE TO DRAWDOWN DEPTH and respond only to single-day loss CONCENTRATION. The observed collapse to exactly 1.0/0.0 on the -20R ledger is therefore the expected behaviour of that model on a book whose losses are spread across days and never breach 5% in one, NOT a gate that has stopped working. THE DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE CHANGES WITH IT: BL-20260803's blocking finding (alpaca_portfolio survival 0.871<0.90) is not 'a verdict the code no longer produces'. It is a verdict that now REQUIRES day-concentrated losses to reproduce. That is a re-run against a day-concentrated book, not a write-off — and unblocking that routing decision on the 'constants' reading would have been unblocking it on a false premise, which is why this correction is filed loudly rather than edited away.
items.mechanism_found_2026_08_31: THE SEPARATE, DURABLE FINDING, established the same session and folded in here rather than filed as a near-duplicate (0.64 lexical overlap with this row): `dd_model_state` IS WRITTEN AND NEVER BRANCHED ON. src/prop/montecarlo.py declares it as a deliberate four-state field — `modelled_terminal` / `no_limit_declared` / `not_terminal` / `unmodelled_trailing` — and its own docstring is explicit that on a `not_terminal` ruleset 'the drawdown contributes NOTHING to this figure — so a low p_breach there is not evidence of a durable account, it is evidence that the limit was not part of the simulation'. scripts/prop/account_compat_matrix.py records it into the output row (line 172) with a comment telling a HUMAN to read it beside p_breach — and then computes `route = positive and survives and low_breach`, in which `dd_model_state` does not appear. So the gate emits ROUTE/skip with full authority off two figures whose own producer declares them incomplete for exactly this ruleset shape. Measured consumers of the field across the repo: 3 references, all either its own definition, a docstring, or that one output-row assignment; ZERO branches. This is the `exit_price_source` shape (written in 12 files, branched on in one) that provenance-consumer-guard exists to catch, in a gate that decides whether a strategy routes onto live capital.

items.title: gld-compat-matrix grades EVERY standard account UNGRADED on a runner (no balance source) and then its summary calls that 'does NOT route ... its own ruleset rejects it' — re-introducing the exact conflation Lane P removed, under a Tier-3 de-routing suggestion
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-29 by re-running gld-compat-matrix.yml on current main (issue #10399, defaults gld_pullback_1h/GLD/0bps/730d, 124 emitted trades, fidelity faithful). RESULT: ALL TEN standard accounts returned verdict UNGRADED with 'P(breach)=None, surv=None'. Only breakout_1 (prop, declared ruleset) graded at all — ROUTE, ev_net_usd $1,241, P(net>0)=0.947.

CAUSE, verified rather than inferred: the workflow supplies NO journal DB or balance source (grep over gld-compat-matrix.yml for TRADE_JOURNAL_DB/balance/journal/DATA_DIR returns nothing), so post-Lane-P standard_account_size.load_balance_snapshots() returns None -> size_state 'unreadable' -> UNGRADED. That is the evaluator behaving CORRECTLY; the defect is downstream of it.

DEFECT 1 — THE SUMMARY CONFLATES 'WE COULD NOT MEASURE' WITH 'IT FAILED', AND ATTACHES A TIER-3 SUGGESTION TO IT. The run's own prose reads: '⭐ alpaca_portfolio: UNGRADED (does NOT route) for gld_pullback_1h — FLAG. ... this is a paper book trading a strategy its own ruleset rejects — a genuine Tier-3 flag: consider whether to keep the routing.' UNGRADED does NOT mean the ruleset rejects it. Lane P's own commit message states the rule this violates verbatim: 'AN UNGRADEABLE ACCOUNT RETURNS UNGRADED, NOT skip. Those are different verdicts and conflating them is the defect this whole change exists to remove.' Lane P removed the conflation from the EVALUATOR and the SUMMARY still performs it — and it is the summary a human reads. The concrete risk is a de-routing decision taken because a workflow could not read a balance file.

DEFECT 2 — THE STANDARD ARM IS NOW STRUCTURALLY INERT ON THIS SURFACE. Before Lane P the same workflow produced confident standard verdicts by grading against a SYNTHETIC $10,000; now it correctly refuses, but it refuses EVERYTHING, so the workflow can no longer answer the question it exists to answer for any standard account. Both states are bad in different ways and the second is the honest one — the fix is to give the runner a balance source, not to restore the synthetic default.

CONSEQUENCE FOR BL-20260803-GLD-ALPACA-PORTFOLIO-SURVIVAL-SKIP: its blocking numbers (survival 0.871<0.90, P(breach) 0.132>0.10) were produced by the PRE-Lane-P code path, i.e. computed against the synthetic $10,000 rather than alpaca_portfolio's real ~$95.5k. They are therefore not reproducible on current main AND their original basis was a fabricated account size. That row should be disposed of on this evidence rather than left blocking a routing decision.

DISTINCT FROM the neighbouring rows, and filed with similar_ok after reading them: BL-20260827-STANDARD-ARM-MISMODELS-INTRADAY-MAX-DD-AS-A-TERMINAL-FLOOR and BL-20260827-COMPAT-MATRIX-STANDARD-ARM-BORROWED-A-TYPE-WITH-NO-MEMBER-FOR-ITS-CONCEPT are about the DRAWDOWN MODEL (what Lane P fixed); BL-20260825-COMPAT-MATRIX-SUMMARY-HARDCODES-ONE-STRATEGY-WHILE-ITS-TABLE-IS-PARAMETERISED (resolved) was the summary naming the wrong STRATEGY. This is the summary mis-naming a VERDICT STATE, on a run where the table itself is correct.
items.proposed_fix: Two separable fixes, and the first is the urgent one because it is what a human acts on. (1) The summary must distinguish the three outcomes it currently collapses into 'does NOT route': ROUTE (measured, clears), a genuine FAIL (measured, does not clear), and UNGRADED (we could not establish what to measure against). Only the middle one justifies 'its ruleset rejects it', and only the middle one should carry a de-routing suggestion. An UNGRADED row should say what was missing — here, the account size — and point at the input, not at the routing. (2) Give the runner a balance source so the standard arm can grade at all: the values are already available unauthenticated from /api/bot/accounts/balances (verified this session — 11 accounts, source db), so a fetch-and-seed step needs no secret and no VM. Do NOT restore the synthetic default: that is the fabricated size Lane P removed, and it is what produced BL-20260803's numbers.
items.resolution_criteria: A re-run of gld-compat-matrix shows standard accounts either genuinely graded (real sizes, real verdicts) or UNGRADED with prose that names the missing input and carries NO de-routing suggestion. Verified by reading the run's comment, not the code. NOT sufficient: silencing the star/FLAG line — the flag is worth keeping when a verdict is a real FAIL; what must change is that an unmeasured account stops being reported as a rejected one.
items.evidence: Issue #10399 comment 2026-08-29T04:35:14Z — full 11-row table, 10 standard UNGRADED with surv=None/P(breach)=None, breakout_1 ROUTE $1,241. Cause confirmed by grep over .github/workflows/gld-compat-matrix.yml (no TRADE_JOURNAL_DB/balance/journal/DATA_DIR) plus standard_account_size.load_balance_snapshots returning None on an absent store. Contrast run with balances seeded: docs/research/lane-p-compat-verdict-diff-2026-08-29.md section 2 (same code, real sizes, accounts grade normally).

RUN 33306014754 (workflow_dispatch on main, 2026-08-30T10:15:04Z, conclusion success; defaults gld_pullback_1h / GLD / 0 bps / 730d, 123 emitted trades, fidelity faithful). STATE THE POPULATION: 11 accounts, 10 standard + 1 prop.

DEFECT 2 (arm inert on a runner) — FIXED AND MEASURED. The balance step fetched 11 accounts, `source=db`, `as_of=2026-08-30T10:00:51Z`. NINE of ten standard accounts returned a real verdict where ALL TEN graded UNGRADED on 08-29. `VERDICT_LINE` carries `size=measured` for both alpaca accounts, so the sizes are the venue-derived snapshot and NOT the synthetic $10,000 Lane P removed. The one remaining UNGRADED is `ib_live`, whose balance genuinely came back `balance=None api_ok=False` — so the arm refuses DISCRIMINATINGLY rather than blanket, which is the distinction that makes this fixed rather than merely quiet. DEFECT 1 (summary conflates UNGRADED with rejection) — FIXED. The workflow now has a dedicated UNGRADED branch reading 'this is NOT a rejection ... No routing conclusion follows in either direction', naming the missing input, and carrying NO de-routing suggestion; the 'its own ruleset rejects' sentence moved to the `else` branch, i.e. a MEASURED verdict that did not clear — the one case this row's own proposed_fix says justifies it. EVIDENCE CAVEAT: this row's criteria say 'verified by reading the run's comment'. The comment step is gated on `github.event_name == 'issues'` and this was a workflow_dispatch, so there is no comment — I read the SUMMARY.md content printed in the job log (job 99242607803), which is the same artifact the comment posts verbatim. Stating it so the next reader is not misled about which surface was read.

⚠️ ONE RESIDUAL, FILED SEPARATELY AND NOT SWEPT INTO THIS CLOSE: the criteria's second limb wants an UNGRADED row to carry 'prose that names the missing input'. For `ib_live` it does not — the workflow renders its OWN table with no size/size_state column, and `size_state` reaches prose only in the alpaca_portfolio star section. So `ib_live` reads UNGRADED with no stated reason. See BL-20260830-COMPAT-TABLE-OMITS-THE-SIZE-BASIS-SO-UNGRADED-DOES-NOT-SAY-WHY.

⚠️ NOT A ROUTING CONCLUSION. Every verdict here is at fee_bps=0 on a harness ledger; the row's own standing caveat (revalidate on the account's real venue data before live wiring, Tier-3) is untouched. In particular `alpaca_live` graded ROUTE and that must NOT be read as unblocking the go-live — OI-20260829-ALPACA-GOLIVE-BLOCKED-ON-T1-SETTLEMENT-MODEL is loud and open, and a compat verdict is not a settlement model.

items.title: The Bybit over-cover alert asserts 'Legs have piled up ... strand the rest' as a FIXED literal, so on a ONE-leg position it names a cause its own data refutes and points the responder at the wrong mechanism
items.detail: MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-29T06:18:40Z and 06:20:25Z on the trader journal (/api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live.service, window 06:18:00-06:21:48Z, 1000 lines): '_check_broker_naked_bybit_positions: LEG OVER-ACCUMULATION bybit_1/ETHUSDT - position size=0.22 but resting SL legs total 6.11 (2777%) ACROSS 1 LEG(S). Legs have piled up; a trip would over-close and strand the rest.' The message contradicts itself in one sentence: with ONE leg nothing has piled up, and there is no 'rest' to strand. SOURCE CONFIRMED (field beats comment), src/runtime/order_monitor.py:9160-9170: the two clauses are part of a FIXED format literal emitted whenever `covered > size * _BYBIT_OVERCOVER_FACTOR`, while `len(state['sl_leg_ids'])` is only ever interpolated as a number - it is never branched on. The surrounding comment cites the multi-leg case it was written for (bybit_1 XRPUSDT, 144789.3 across many legs, 444.7%), which is a genuinely different condition. WHY IT MATTERS - THE RATIO IS BEING DRIVEN BY THE WRONG TERM. At 1 leg the percentage is not rising because legs accumulate; it rises because the POSITION SHRANK while one oversized stale leg (6.11) stayed put against a 0.22 position - 27.8x. A responder reading 'legs have piled up' goes looking for accumulation and the 20-leg-cap failure mode, finds one leg, and has been pointed away from the actual mechanism (a leg that was never amended down as the position was reduced). This is the UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT class, sub-class A (semantic substitution: the label names a condition the code did not test) that this repo already documents and guards for in scripts/ - order_monitor is outside diagnostic-provenance-guard's scanned tree, which is why nothing caught it. POPULATION / TREND - STATE IT CAREFULLY. bybit_1/ETHUSDT over-cover reads 167% (recorded in BL-20260826-BYBIT-OVER-COVER-DETECTED-FOR-FOUR-WEEKS-AND-NEVER-PAGED), then 809%, now 2777%. Those are three spot readings, NOT a measured series, and because the denominator is a shrinking position the escalation must NOT be read as 'more legs are piling up' - which is exactly the misreading the alert text invites. NOT A DUPLICATE, and the neighbours were read first: BL-20260826-BYBIT-OVER-COVER-DETECTED-FOR-FOUR-WEEKS-AND-NEVER-PAGED (resolved) is about the alert reaching NO HUMAN SURFACE - it now pages correctly, and that paging is what made this text visible. BL-20260730-BYBIT1-XRP-LEG-OVERACCUM-WORSENING (kept_open) is XRP and is genuine multi-leg accumulation. This row is about the MESSAGE being false on the single-leg branch of the same detector. NOT CLAIMED: I did NOT verify that the named remedy (cancel-stale-tpsl-legs) would strand this position naked. BL-20260826-CANCEL-STALE-TPSL-LEGS-WOULD-KEEP-A-CLOSED-TRADES-LEG-AND-CANCEL-THE-LIVE-ONE says that tool keeps the newest leg, so with one leg it should keep it. That is an inference from another row's text, not a measurement, and it should be measured before anyone runs the remedy here. POPULATION, STATED EXPLICITLY (the guard was right to demand this and the numbers are better for it). The 2777% is ONE observation of ONE (account, symbol) pair, seen n=2 times 105 s apart, in a journal window running 2026-08-29T06:18:00Z through 2026-08-29T06:21:48Z (1000 journal records, the endpoint's page cap - so this is a ~4-minute slice, NOT a day). Its denominator is the position: 6.11 resting SL quantity over 0.22 position quantity = 2777%, across 1 of 1 resting SL legs for that pair. The corroborating IB read covers 2 of 2 resting orders on ib_paper. The 444.7% is not mine - it is the XRPUSDT example quoted in the source comment at order_monitor.py:9152-9154 (144789.3 over 32557.2), carried here only to show which case the wording was written for. The 167% is likewise quoted from BL-20260826-BYBIT-OVER-COVER-DETECTED-FOR-FOUR-WEEKS-AND-NEVER-PAGED, not re-measured by me. So of the three percentages in this row exactly ONE (2777%) is a measurement I took; the other two are citations, and none of the three is a trend - there is no series here, only spot readings on different dates by different sessions.
items.resolution_criteria: The alert branches on `len(state['sl_leg_ids'])`: the multi-leg case keeps the accumulation wording, and the 1-leg case says what is actually true - one leg of N against a position of M, i.e. a leg that was not amended down as the position was reduced - and names a remedy appropriate to THAT condition. Verified by a test that asserts the 1-leg message does not contain 'piled up' or 'the rest', and by observing a real 1-leg alert on the live journal carrying the corrected text. A fix that only edits the wording without branching does not clear this.
evidence: trader journal 2026-08-29T06:18:40Z + 06:20:25Z (two occurrences, ~105s apart)
src/runtime/order_monitor.py:9160-9170 (fixed literal; leg count interpolated, never branched on)
src/runtime/order_monitor.py:9150-9154 (comment citing the multi-leg XRPUSDT case it was written for)

updates.note: Re-validated: a FIXED literal asserting 'legs have piled up' on a one-leg position. Diagnostic-provenance sub-class A in an alert body — and it undermines the credibility of the over-cover pages that only just started reaching operators (20 of them since 08-26).

items.title: A literal-date fixture aged out of a rolling 7-day window and took main red — the THIRD occurrence of a class filed on 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-13, in a file authored 2026-08-26, i.e. AFTER both rows existed
items.detail: RECURRENCE, filed deliberately rather than as a duplicate: that the earlier disposition did not hold IS the finding. Prior rows, both still kept_open: BL-20260813-TESTS-PIN-LITERAL-DATES-AGAINST-ROLLING-WINDOWS ('a test fixture stamped with a LITERAL date, exercised against a ROLLING window, expires and takes the whole repo red') and BL-20260812-WALLCLOCK-TIMEBOMB-TESTS-NO-SOUND-DETECTOR ('no sound detector - one instance reddened main on 2026-08-12'). A third, BL-20260813-PYTEST-RUN-SHORTCIRCUITS-SO-MAIN-MERGES-UNVERIFIED, is resolved and describes the same detonation. THE SHARP PART: tests/test_exit_reason_reclassify_on_late_price.py was ADDED on 2026-08-26 (commit 98fec40, PR #10299) - THIRTEEN DAYS AFTER both rows were filed. The class was known, a detector was recorded as missing, and a new bomb was authored anyway. A lesson logged and not made executable is not a prevention. MECHANISM, measured not inferred. The fixture hard-coded created_at='2026-08-22T00:00:00+00:00', while _sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit's own SELECT filters `datetime(created_at) >= datetime('now', '-7 days')` (Bybit's closed-pnl retention window). Arithmetic on 2026-08-29T06:59:46Z: cutoff '2026-08-22 06:59:46' > fixture '2026-08-22 00:00:00', so the row stopped matching. Fuse length was exactly 7 days; it detonated at 2026-08-29T00:00:00Z. CONFIRMED NOT THE PR'S: the same 5 tests fail identically on origin/main at 76d14af in a clean worktree with no branch changes present. main was red for every open PR in the repo. WHY IT PRESENTED AS A REGRESSION IN UNRELATED CODE: of the 11 tests in the file, the 6 SOURCE-INSPECTION ones (which grep the function's source text) kept PASSING, while the 5 BEHAVIOURAL ones failed as KeyError: 1 / KeyError: 'is_reduce_leg' / 'assert {}'. So the suite simultaneously reported the implementation as correct and appeared to show it broken. A time-bomb fixture does not announce itself as one. FIXED HERE (tier-1, tests only): the fixture now derives created_at as now(utc) - 1 day. src/runtime/order_monitor.py is UNCHANGED - verified clean by git after the fault-injection below. THE FIX WAS VERIFIED BY PLANTED FAULT, NOT BY GREEN: with is_reduce_leg=False hard-coded at the sweep's own call site, test_a_reduce_leg_is_never_graded FAILS; restored, 11 pass. So the repaired fixture restores real coverage rather than passing vacuously. AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THAT CONTROL WAS INVALID, recorded because it is the more instructive half: a regex plant took the FIRST `is_reduce_leg=_is_reduce` in the file (line 4872, a different function) while the sweep's call is at line 9632, so the fault never touched the code under test and all 11 tests 'passed'. That would have supported the confident wrong conclusion 'the test does not bite'. It is the same shape as the retraction recorded in ROADMAP.md M40 - a positive control run inside the wrong location controls for the probe and never for the population. POPULATION FOR THE BLAST RADIUS, stated because the number invites over-reading: 224 test files contain a literal ISO date; 13 of those ALSO exercise a now-relative window in the same file. That 13 is a CO-OCCURRENCE HEURISTIC, not a list of bombs - the probe finds the known positive (this file) which is why it is worth reporting at all, but the other 12 PASS TODAY and I did NOT establish that any of them has a later fuse. Do not read 12 as 12 pending failures.
items.resolution_criteria: An executable prevention exists, which is what the two kept_open rows lack: a check that FAILS when a test fixture supplies a literal date to a code path filtering on a now-relative window. Because a sound general detector is hard (BL-20260812 says so), an acceptable narrower form is a guard over test fixtures that assign a literal ISO date to a field the production SELECT compares against datetime('now', ...). It must be demonstrated on a PLANTED bomb (a fixture dated far enough back to be outside the window) and shown to stay quiet on the relative form now used here — presence of the guard is not evidence; a demonstrated catch is. Filing another instance without building the detector does not clear this row.

updates.note: ⚠️ HIGH, AND IT IS THE CLEANEST RECURRENCE PROOF IN THE BACKLOG: a literal-date fixture aged out of a rolling window and took main red for the THIRD time, 17 days after a detector for exactly this was FILED (BL-20260812-WALLCLOCK-TIMEBOMB-TESTS-NO-SOUND-DETECTOR) and never built. Filing without building is what this review's backlog_classes pass is meant to surface. The detector is cheap; three reddened mains is not.

items.title: account_compat_matrix rescales the R sequence by account_size/base_account_size, so a standard account's verdict is a function of its BALANCE and the MC's scale-invariance is broken
items.detail: scripts/prop/account_compat_matrix.py synthesises the ledger with synth_ledger_from_emit(base_account_size=5000.0, base_risk_pct=0.5) -- pnl on a $5,000 compounding walk. It then calls run_montecarlo(..., account_size=unit.account_size_usd), which calls ledger_to_r_sequence(closed_trades, initial_balance=acct, base_risk_pct=0.5) with acct = THE ACCOUNT'S OWN SIZE. R_k = pnl_k / (balance_before_k * base_risk_pct/100), so recovered R is scaled by roughly base_account_size/account_size. The round-trip is exact ONLY when account_size == base_account_size (5000). The call site's own comment claims the ledger is built 'straight from the emit so it round-trips exactly through montecarlo.ledger_to_r_sequence', which holds only at that one size. MEASURED with an 8-trade ledger of known true net_r [0.8,-1.0,1.5,-1.0,2.0,-0.5,1.1,-1.0]: at 5000 -> identical to truth (1.000x); at 95542.76 (alpaca_portfolio) -> [0.042,-0.053,0.078,...] = 0.052x; at 200.10 (alpaca_live) -> [19.99,-22.81,38.42,...] = 24.99x, diverging as the mis-scaled walk compounds. CONSEQUENCE: the survival / P(breach) arm of the standard gate is dominated by this rescale -- a SMALL account gets ~25x R and breaches at P=1.0, a LARGE one gets ~0.05x and reads survival 1.0 / P(breach) 0.0. That MANUFACTURES the exact pattern a 2026-08-29 session reported as a finding ('every paper book ROUTEs, both real-money books skip, the gate split on account size', 5 legs: tqqq/slv/gld/scha/tlt). RETRACTED in docs/research/alpaca-roster-phase3-compat-gate-2026-08-29.md. NOT a duplicate of BL-20260829-LANE-P-MAY-VOID-THE-GLD-SURVIVAL-SKIP, which claims survival and p_breach are CONSTANTS on standard accounts; the measured survivals here vary (1.0 / 0.4997 / 0.172 / 0.001 / 0.0), so that row does not describe this.
items.resolution_criteria: A test recovers a known net_r sequence UNCHANGED at three different account_size values (200 / 5000 / 95542) through the real synth_ledger_from_emit + ledger_to_r_sequence pair -- it passes at 5000 and fails at the other two today. Reached either by calling ledger_to_r_sequence with initial_balance == the balance the ledger was BUILT at, or by carrying the emit's per-trade net_r through without a balance round-trip. Then the 5 retracted legs are re-graded and the Phase 3 doc carries the corrected verdicts.
items.evidence: Numeric round-trip test run in-session against the real functions (not a reimplementation). Defaults read from the argparse: --base-account-size 5000.0, --base-risk-pct 0.5. items.title: splg_trend_long_1d emits ZERO trades over 730d on its own harness while spy_trend_long_1d emits 8 on the same index, harness, timeframe and window — so it cannot be compat-graded and a real-money candidate slot is held by a leg that never fires
items.detail: FOUND while closing the compat-gate evidence over the 16-leg alpaca_live CANDIDATE roster (recovered from config/accounts.yaml at 624d8841^, before the roster was emptied). 14 of the 16 graded cleanly; this is one of the two that did not. MEASURED (run 33255577584, job 99108556940, head 4f8ec829, 2026-08-29T13:39Z): the workflow's own summary reads `splg_trend_long_1d - SPLG 1d - trend harness - feed yahoo - fidelity FAITHFUL - fee 0.0 bps - 0 emitted trades`, then `COMPAT DID NOT RUN`. The VERDICT_LINE reports state=no_compat_json, which is the 'we could not look' state and NOT 'every account refused' - the three non-read states were kept distinct precisely so this could not be misread as a skip. THE COMPARISON IS THE FINDING, and it is a POSITIVE CONTROL rather than an inference: spy_trend_long_1d emitted n=8 over the SAME 730d window, SAME trend harness, SAME 1d timeframe, SAME yahoo feed, SAME fee (run 33252282572). SPY and SPLG both track the S&P 500, so their price SHAPE is near-identical and a trend-long strategy should fire at comparable rates. 8 vs 0 is therefore structural, not a market difference. NOT ESTABLISHED - do not carry any of these as the cause: (a) yahoo history/coverage for SPLG over the window, (b) a price-LEVEL-dependent filter interacting with SPLG's much lower share price (~$70 vs SPY ~$640) - a min-notional, ATR-absolute or rounding gate would bite SPLG and not SPY, (c) a symbol-mapping problem in the harness. The emit ran 'faithful' and did not error, which argues against a hard data outage but does not rule out thin/partial history. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: SPLG occupies one of 16 real-money candidate slots on alpaca_live. A leg that produces no trades in two years is either broken (fix it) or inert (drop it) - either way it should not be carried into a go-live roster as if it were evidence. It also means the compat gate CANNOT be run for it: there is no ledger to score, so it can never clear the mandatory per-account compatibility step the backtesting/new-strategy skills require. iaum_pullback_1d, the other previously-ungraded candidate, graded fine (n=10, ROUTE on both alpaca_portfolio and alpaca_live, ret 2.9969), so the gap is SPLG-specific and not a property of the two legs that happened to be missing.
items.resolution_criteria: Establish WHY SPLG emits zero: re-run the emit with the candle frame dumped (row count, first/last bar, NaN share) and compare against SPY's over the identical window - that single artifact separates a data problem from a filter problem. THEN either (a) fix the cause and show a non-zero emitted ledger plus a compat verdict for splg_trend_long_1d, or (b) remove it from the alpaca_live candidate roster with the zero-emit measurement recorded as the reason. Explicitly NOT sufficient: re-running the same workflow and getting the same 0, or reasoning about SPLG's liquidity without reading the frame the harness actually received.
items.evidence: Run 33255577584 / job 99108556940 (SPLG, 0 emitted, no_compat_json) vs run 33252282572 (SPY, n=8, ROUTE both accounts) - same harness/timeframe/feed/fee/window, both on head 4f8ec829. items.title: /api/bot/trades/closed?since=<unparseable> returns [] — indistinguishable from 'no trades in the window', with no filter_state to say the filter was dropped
items.source: /system-review 2026-08-29 — found while probing the window
items.why_it_matters: datetime('garbage') is NULL in SQLite, so `close_time >= datetime(?)` is NULL for every row and the route returns []. A caller cannot tell a dropped filter from an empty window. This is precisely the shape the repo already fixed ONE endpoint over: /api/bot/db/table/{name} carries a never-collapsed `filter_state` (applied / not_requested / ignored_unknown_column / ...) because BL-20260813-DB-EXPLORER-SILENTLY-IGNORES-UNKNOWN-FILTER-COLUMN showed a silently-ignored filter returning a confident total. /trades/closed has no equivalent. Its consumers include analysis sessions that cannot see the query they got — the same argument that route's row makes. ⚠️ Population note, because it is how this was found and it cuts both ways: my FIRST probe reported 'every since= value returns 0 rows', which was wrong — I had passed limit=500 over the documented MAX_LIMIT=200, got an HTTP 422, and my own parser rendered the error body as 0 rows. The real defect is narrower than the first reading and was only isolated by adding a no-since control.
items.resolution_criteria: The route distinguishes an APPLIED since-filter from a DROPPED one — either by returning a never-collapsed state alongside the rows (the db_explorer filter_state shape, registered with collapsed-state-guard) or by rejecting an unparseable since with a 400 rather than serving []. A test asserts an unparseable since is not reported the same way as an empty window.
items.next_action: Decide the shape with the operator: the route returns a bare JSON array today, so adding a state field is a wire-shape change for the dashboard + Android clients, whereas a 400 is not. The 400 is probably right (a malformed timestamp is a caller bug), but it is a contract change either way.

updates.note: Filed by THIS review earlier today and carried here so the triage covers every open row without exception. Disposition unchanged: open, Tier-1, and the fix is a wire-shape decision (a never-collapsed filter_state field vs a 400) that touches the dashboard and Android clients, so it wants the operator's call on the contract.
