items.title: the trend and pullback HARNESSES force-close every trade at timeout_bars (default 200) and the LIVE units implement no such exit at all -- a second instance of the class BL-20260810-BACKTEST-DOES-NOT-MODEL-THE-LIVE-CAPPED-TP was marked resolved for
items.detail:
FOUND 2026-08-29 while executing M20 B4 (ship the validated bracket-geometry cells). Six of the 14 passed_unshipped legs won on cells carrying a TIMEOUT component (to24 / to400 / to48) and I could not ship them, so I went looking for the config field. What is there instead is a harness-vs-live divergence.

MEASURED, by reading the code rather than the docs:
  * `scripts/backtest_trend.py:497` -- `exit_idx = min(entry_i + timeout_bars, n - 1)`, plus a bar loop at :502 bounded by `entry_i + timeout_bars + 1`. `--timeout-bars` at :982, DEFAULT 200.
  * `scripts/backtest_pullback.py:496` -- the same construction, and :611 the same bounded loop.
  * `src/units/strategies/trend_donchian.py` -- ZERO occurrences of the string 'timeout'.
  * `src/units/strategies/htf_pullback_trend_2h.py` -- ONE occurrence, at line 49, and it is a DOCSTRING in the Exit section claiming a '``timeout_bars`` backstop'. No code implements it; the module has no bars-held / max-hold / bars-since logic at all (the only `len(candles_df)` hits are data-sufficiency checks at :224/:525/:557/:577).
  * Repo-wide, `timeout_bars` is READ by exactly two units: `fvg_range_15m.py` and `fade_breakout_4h.py`. Neither is the monitor unit for any trend or pullback leg (the wiring tests pin those as `trend_donchian` and `htf_pullback_trend_2h`).

SO: in backtest every trend/pullback trade is force-closed on bar count; live, nothing closes it on bar count. The repo's OWN registry already half-knows this -- `scripts/check_harness_lever_coupling.py` lists `timeout_bars` in BOTH `_TREND_UNMODELLED` and `_PB_UNMODELLED` -- but that registry is scoped to what the HARNESS omits, and here the divergence runs the other way: the harness MODELS it and live does not.

HOW MUCH IT MATTERS, stated honestly and NOT overclaimed. At the default 200 the divergence is close to inert: `docs/research/e35-bracket-is-not-a-decision-2026-08-20.md` records timeout as a near-empty exit bucket (5 of 284 on the E0 leg), and on a 1d leg 200 bars is ~9 months. I did NOT re-measure that bucket across the fleet, so treat 'near-inert at the default' as inherited, not established here. What IS established: the cells that WON the e35 sweep move it to 24 / 48 / 400, and on a 1h leg to24 is about one day -- precisely the region where it would bind hard, and precisely what live cannot honour. So those cells are not 'blocked on wiring', they measure an exit the live system cannot perform.

CONSEQUENCES:
  1. Four to six e35 bracket-geometry cells recorded `passed_unshipped` in `docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json` are UNSHIPPABLE BY CONSTRUCTION, not pending. Legs: mes_trend_long_1d (to24), tlt_pullback_1d (to24), gld_pullback_1h (to24), spy_pullback_1h (to400), eth_pullback_2h (to48), eth_pullback_prop_2h (to48). The matrix does not distinguish 'validated and awaiting approval' from 'validated against a lever production does not have'.
  2. `config/strategies.yaml` declares `timeout_bars` on legs whose units never read it -- mgc_pullback_1d carries `timeout_bars: 200` (and there are further declarations at lines 1540 and 1581). Inert config that reads as a live safety backstop.
  3. `htf_pullback_trend_2h.py`'s docstring asserts an exit the module does not implement. A reader auditing the exit path would conclude a time backstop exists. Field beats comment; the comment is wrong.

RELATIONSHIP TO THE PRIOR ROW, filed with similar_ok after reading it: `BL-20260810-BACKTEST-DOES-NOT-MODEL-THE-LIVE-CAPPED-TP` (status RESOLVED, severity critical) is the SAME CLASS on a different parameter and in the OPPOSITE direction -- there the harness modelled tp at 50R while live placed a capped ~1.3-5R take-profit, so the harness was more permissive than live; here the harness force-closes on bar count while live never does, so the harness is more RESTRICTIVE. That row is marked resolved, and its `detail` is empty. This is therefore not a duplicate and not evidence that its fix failed: it is evidence the fix was PARAMETER-SCOPED when the class is not. Nobody enumerated the other harness parameters against their live counterparts afterwards, which is why this sat until a shipping attempt tripped over it.

NOT ESTABLISHED, deliberately: whether the harness should drop the forced timeout, or the live units should gain one. Both are order-path changes. Also not established: how many NON-e35 trend/pullback backtest verdicts in the coverage matrix were measured under the default 200 and would move without it -- that is the blast-radius question and it needs a measurement, not an assumption.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH: (a) the divergence is closed in one direction -- either the live trend/pullback units honour timeout_bars, or the harnesses stop modelling it and the affected coverage-matrix verdicts are re-graded; and (b) the OTHER harness parameters have been enumerated against their live counterparts, so the class is closed rather than this one instance. A passing test is not enough for (a): it needs a live trade observed closing (or not closing) on bar count as the chosen direction predicts. Fixing the htf_pullback_trend_2h docstring alone does NOT clear this row -- that is the symptom, not the divergence.

updates.note: Arrived on main (#10420) DURING this review's merge and triaged here so the 100%-triage gate covers it rather than stepping over a row that landed mid-run. Read in full; disposition unchanged. It is legitimately blocked: closing the divergence in EITHER direction (live units honour timeout_bars, or the harnesses stop modelling it and the affected coverage verdicts are re-graded) is an order-path change, Tier-2/3, and the row's own criteria correctly refuse a passing test as evidence. Cross-link this review's own reading: it is the same shape as the harness/live gaps I flagged, and its (b) clause — enumerate the OTHER harness parameters against their live counterparts — is the part that closes the CLASS rather than the instance, which is exactly why BL-20260810-BACKTEST-DOES-NOT-MODEL-THE-LIVE-CAPPED-TP was marked resolved and the class was not.

items.title: FIFTH instance of BL-20260813-PYTEST-RUN-SHORTCIRCUITS-SO-MAIN-MERGES-UNVERIFIED: ml/configs/retired/ is read by a contract test AS COMMITTED and is not in the relevance filter — and this one was found by a CHECK, not an incident
items.detail:
tests/test_pytest_run_filter.py's own docstring enumerates four instances of this class (config/, .github/workflows/, scripts/, docs/) and states the thing that matters: "every fix so far added the ONE tree just proven, and the next tree was found by an INCIDENT rather than by a check." This is the fifth tree, and it was found by a check — while verifying why pytest-run reported success in 12 seconds on a manifest-only PR.

MEASURED, not argued. Using the test module's OWN predicate (tests.test_pytest_run_filter._matches, which parses the grep out of .github/workflows/pytest-run.yml), with controls run first so a negative has a denominator:
  positive controls -> scripts/ops/purge_vm_runner.sh True, config/strategies.yaml True, src/main.py True
  negative control  -> README.md False
  ml/configs/mes-regime-1d-lgbm-v2.yaml         False
  ml/configs/retired/btc-regime-15m-tcn-v1.yaml False

AND THE SUITE READS THAT TREE AS COMMITTED. tests/ml/_manifest_paths.py::manifest_path resolves a manifest from ml/configs/ OR ml/configs/retired/, and three tests import it (test_corpus_embedding_market_features, test_reconstruction_evaluator, test_torch_sequence_contract). All three currently resolve into RETIRED: btc-regime-15m-lgbm-corpusemb-pcv-v1, corpus-ssl-encoder-mae-v1, btc-regime-15m-tcn-v1.

REPRODUCED EMPIRICALLY rather than reasoned. Baseline on tests/ml/test_torch_sequence_contract.py: 2 passed, 1 failed (test_predictor_constructs_and_degrades_without_onnxruntime — an environmental ModuleNotFoundError in the sandbox, NOT the manifest; stated so it is not miscounted as signal). Dropping ONE entry from feature_columns in ml/configs/retired/btc-regime-15m-tcn-v1.yaml flips test_manifest_matches_family_and_trainer_contract from PASS to FAIL (AssertionError at test_torch_sequence_contract.py:57). Manifest restored byte-identical from a pre-edit copy; git status clean. So a PR touching only that path short-circuits to a green tick and merges while reddening main — the exact shape of instances 3 and 4.

⚠️ WHAT THIS IS NOT, because my first hypothesis was WRONG and the refutation is the useful half. I initially believed the gap was the ACTIVE ml/configs/ directory — the artifact class that had just stranded mes-regime-1d-lgbm-v2 for 34 days, so it felt obviously right. It is not: NO test globs ml/configs/, and the manifest strings in test_trainer_manifest_health.py ("ml/configs/big.yaml") are FIXTURES, not files, while the ml/configs reference in tests/ml/test_dataset_audit.py:13 is a docstring. Covering the active dir would cost a full ~8-minute suite on every manifest PR for ZERO coverage, which is the CI-minutes cost the short-circuit exists to avoid. The gap is retired/ ONLY, today.

THE SCOPE CALL IS GENUINE AND IS WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN PATCHED BLIND. Three options: (a) add '^ml/configs/retired/' — minimal, precise, zero wasted minutes, but fragile in exactly the way the docstring warns about (the moment a test reads an ACTIVE manifest the gap silently returns); (b) add '^ml/configs/' — durable against that, costs the full suite on every manifest PR; (c) extend test_docs_committed_readers_are_all_covered to DERIVE coverage from what tests demonstrably read, which the docstring already names as the preferred mechanism and as "a bigger change". (c) is the one that retires the CLASS instead of adding the fifth tree by hand — and the docstring is explicit that hand-enumeration is what keeps failing.

ALSO STILL TRUE, and unfixed by any of the three: instance 3's own resolution_criteria required that "pytest-run cannot report a green tick without having executed the suite (or reports a visibly distinct state when it skips)" and was marked RESOLVED without it. A skipped run and a 10,677-test run still render the identical green tick at the merge button. Until that changes, every fix here is mitigation.
items.trigger_condition: Any PR whose diff touches only ml/configs/retired/ (or any future tree the suite reads and the filter does not name).
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (c): test_docs_committed_readers_are_all_covered (or a sibling) DERIVES the covered set from the paths tests actually read, so a newly-read tree fails the guard instead of waiting for an incident — demonstrated by showing it fails on the current filter and passes after the filter is corrected. OR, as an interim, (a)/(b): the filter names the retired tree AND tests/test_pytest_run_filter.py::COVERED gains an entry citing test_torch_sequence_contract as the reader, with the perturbation above as the evidence. Interim closure MUST record that the class is unretired and that instance 3's green-tick ambiguity remains open, so this does not close the way instance 3 did.
items.evidence: tests/test_pytest_run_filter.py (docstring: four prior instances; _filter_regex/_matches); .github/workflows/pytest-run.yml (the grep -Eq relevance pattern); tests/ml/_manifest_paths.py::manifest_path; tests/ml/test_torch_sequence_contract.py:50,57; PR #10435 job 99160852992 log: '##[notice]No code/config/workflow files changed — skipping the pip install + test-run steps (short-circuit, MB-20260706-CI-MINUTES)', 12s green; BL-20260813-PYTEST-RUN-SHORTCIRCUITS-SO-MAIN-MERGES-UNVERIFIED; BL-20260814-COVERAGE-MATRIX-SHORTCIRCUITS-THE-SUITE-THAT-READS-IT

items.title: The Bybit naked re-arm sends positionIdx=0 on `unresolved`, while the resolver's own WARNING says it sends none — inert today, and the two disagree the moment BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS is armed
items.detail:
⚠️ FILED WITH A CORRECTION TO MY OWN FIRST READING, because the overstatement is the more useful half. I first characterised this as a SILENT failed protective re-arm. It is not silent: `bybit_position_mode.position_idx_for` logs at WARNING on `unresolved` ("is declared HEDGE mode but position_side=... is neither long nor short"), and `order_monitor._attempt_naked_autoprotect` logs a second WARNING on a venue refusal and returns False. The observability exists. Do not act on the stronger claim.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, and it is narrower and checkable. The resolver's warning states the consequence as "sending no positionIdx, which Bybit will refuse". That is true of `apply_position_idx`, which leaves the kwargs dict untouched. It is NOT true of this call site: `order_monitor.py:7201` reads `positionIdx=(0 if _pos.idx is None else _pos.idx)` and therefore sends an EXPLICIT 0. So one message describes an absent kwarg while the code sends the one-way value, and a reader reconciling the WARNING against the wire payload finds they disagree.

WHY THE 0 IS NOT SIMPLY A BUG, which is the part that makes this a decision rather than a patch. `unresolved` means hedge is DECLARED in the allowlist and the direction could not be read. During the arming transition the venue may still be one-way, and there 0 is exactly right and the re-arm SUCCEEDS. Once the venue is hedge, 0 is the one-way value and the re-arm fails. So the current fallback is correct in one state and wrong in the other, and refusing early — my first instinct — would be wrong in BOTH, because it would abandon a re-arm that works today. That is why this is filed rather than patched: it is a live protective path and the right behaviour depends on a venue state the call site does not read.

BLAST RADIUS TODAY: ZERO. `BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS` is empty, so `hedge_mode_enabled` is false for every (account, symbol), `unresolved` is unreachable by construction, and every resolution is `one_way` where 0 is correct. This becomes reachable only in the change that first arms the allowlist.
items.trigger_condition: BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS becomes non-empty for any (account, symbol).
items.resolution_criteria: In the change that first arms the allowlist: (a) make the call site branch on `_pos.state` rather than on `idx is None`, so `one_way` and `unresolved` — which the resolver deliberately keeps apart — are not collapsed back together at the point of use; (b) decide and record what `unresolved` should DO, given it is correct-on-one-way and doomed-on-hedge (candidates: send 0 and escalate the failure to the naked-position alert rather than a bare WARNING; or read the venue mode and branch). (c) Fix the resolver's warning text so it does not claim 'no positionIdx' for a caller that sends 0. Closable when a test asserts the wire payload for each of the four resolver states at this call site.

items.title: SIX ops scripts import `src.*` with no sys.path bootstrap, so they die with ModuleNotFoundError when the wrapper invokes them by absolute path — the wrapper's own `cd` does not help, and --help hides it in five of them
items.detail:
FOUND BY SHIPPING INSTANCE #1 OF IT. scripts/ops/bybit_switch_position_mode.py went live in #10445 and its FIRST dispatch (system-action issue #10446) died before reaching a single one of its four guards:
  File "/home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/scripts/ops/bybit_switch_position_mode.py", line 89
    from src.units.ui.data_loaders import list_accounts
  ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'src'
16 unit tests passed on that file and none could catch it, because pytest already puts the repo root on sys.path — so `from src...` resolves in-process and the missing bootstrap is INVISIBLE to any in-process test.

MECHANISM, and it is the part that makes this survive review: the wrappers all `cd "${REPO_DIR}"` first, which LOOKS sufficient and is not. `python3 /abs/path/script.py` seeds sys.path[0] with the SCRIPT's directory (scripts/ops), never the cwd. So the cd is irrelevant and the import fails on the VM while passing everywhere else. flatten_bybit_position.py and flatten_ib_position.py already carry the correct four-line idiom; six scripts do not.

MEASURED, not inferred — run by absolute path from /tmp:
  CONFIRMED BROKEN (reproduced, exact error):
    scripts/ops/dead_leg_audit.py                       (module-level import, line 64)
    scripts/ops/mark_reconciler_incomplete.py           (function-local, line 95)
    scripts/ops/revert_backfill_monitor_closed_pnl.py   (function-local, line 233)
  SAME STRUCTURE, not individually executed (their --apply paths were not run against a live DB):
    scripts/ops/supersede_intent_reduce_phantom_pnl.py    (line 241)
    scripts/ops/supersede_options_adoption_artifacts.py   (line 205)
    scripts/ops/supersede_reset_orphan_artifacts.py       (line 220)

⚠️ `--help` IS NOT A PROBE FOR THIS, and reporting it as one would have produced a false all-clear. On the five function-local scripts `--help` exits inside argparse BEFORE main() reaches the import, so all five printed usage cleanly and read 'ok'. Only dead_leg_audit, whose import is module-level, failed under --help. Running two of the five in their DEFAULT DRY-RUN mode reproduced the error immediately. State what the probe can see: a probe that exits before the code under test is not evidence of absence.

⚠️ ALSO NOT ESTABLISHED: whether these five have EVER been dispatched successfully. If any has, something compensates that I did not find, and that would change the finding. I checked the obvious candidates and ruled them out — no wrapper sets PYTHONPATH, none uses `python -m`, and the import is UNCONDITIONAL (passing --db or TRADE_JOURNAL_DB does not skip it, verified by reading mark_reconciler_incomplete.py:95). I did not check the run history.
items.trigger_condition: Any of the six dispatched as a system-action, or run by absolute path from a cwd other than the repo root.
items.resolution_criteria: Add the existing four-line bootstrap (copy flatten_bybit_position.py:47-54) to each of the six, and prove each fix with a SUBPROCESS test that invokes the script by absolute path from a foreign cwd — an in-process import test cannot fail on this and is therefore vacuous here. Each test must be shown to FAIL with the bootstrap removed before it is trusted (the control run that was done for bybit_switch_position_mode). Closable when all six pass such a test. Better-but-larger alternative, if a reviewer prefers it: have the wrappers export PYTHONPATH="${REPO_DIR}" in _lib.sh so the class cannot recur per-script — that fixes it once at the shared layer rather than six times, and would also cover scripts added later.
items.evidence: system-action issue #10446 (the live traceback); scripts/ops/flatten_bybit_position.py:47-54 (the correct idiom, with its own comment naming this exact hazard); tests/ops/test_bybit_switch_position_mode.py::test_runs_standalone_from_a_foreign_cwd (the regression test + its removed-bootstrap control)

updates.note: FIXED AT THE SHARED LAYER, which this row's own resolution_criteria name as the better-but-larger alternative: scripts/ops/_lib.sh now exports PYTHONPATH="${REPO_DIR}${PYTHONPATH:+:${PYTHONPATH}}", so every one of the 88 wrappers that sources it resolves `from src...` without a per-script bootstrap, and so does any script added later. Appends rather than overwrites, so a caller's own PYTHONPATH survives. === THE POPULATION WAS LARGER THAN THIS ROW RECORDED. The row enumerated SIX scripts, all under scripts/ops/. Measured 2026-08-30 by deriving rather than listing — every scripts/**.py that imports src.* and contains no sys.path.insert/append — the true count is TEN: the six named plus scripts/notify_session.py, scripts/print_runtime_profile.py, scripts/prop/trade_quality_review.py and scripts/send_hourly_now.py. Enumeration undercounted by four, which is the same failure this session hit on the pytest-run filter class an hour earlier: a hand-listed set finds the instances someone happened to look at. === EVIDENCE, and every test is a SUBPROCESS FROM A FOREIGN CWD by design. An in-process test CANNOT fail on this class — pytest already puts the repo root on sys.path, which is why 16 green unit tests sat on the script that then died on its first live dispatch. tests/ops/test_lib_sh_pythonpath.py: _lib.sh exports the repo root; an existing PYTHONPATH survives; an affected module-level importer (dead_leg_audit.py) runs clean when invoked by ABSOLUTE PATH after sourcing _lib.sh; plus a CONTROL asserting the same invocation WITHOUT _lib.sh still fails, so the probe cannot be vacuously green. Non-vacuity proven by removing the export: 3 of 4 fail, the 4th being the control. dead_leg_audit.py was chosen because its import is MODULE-LEVEL — `--help` exits inside argparse before a function-local import runs, which is precisely why `--help` gave a false all-clear on five of these. === ⚠️ SCOPE, stated rather than left to be discovered: this covers WRAPPER-INVOKED scripts. A script run directly, not through a wrapper that sources _lib.sh, still needs its own bootstrap — so the four-line idiom in flatten_bybit_position.py is complementary, not obsolete. Production invokes all ten through wrappers, so the live path is covered. === ⚠️ NOT YET EXERCISED: no wrapper has run since the change. The evidence that settles it is one system-action dispatch of any of the ten completing without ModuleNotFoundError.

items.summary: The full pytest suite produced a failure count that varied run-to-run by one, and the extra failure could not be reproduced or identified. Measured 2026-08-30 in the sandbox (which is missing ccxt/pybit/psutil/sklearn, so it carries a stable 27-failure environment baseline).
items.detail:
SEQUENCE, so the denominator is visible: a run on the Tier-3 geometry branch BEFORE one leg was reverted gave 30 failed / 13382 passed. A run on clean origin/main gave 27 / 13385. A run on the same branch AFTER the revert gave 27 / 13385 with a failure set BYTE-IDENTICAL to the baseline in both directions (comm -23 and comm -13 both empty). The reverted leg reproducibly causes exactly 2 failures, verified by re-applying its config value and re-running every test file that names either that leg or the coverage matrix: 2 failed / 100 passed. So 27 + 2 = 29, and the 30-failure run has ONE failure that is unexplained.

IT DID NOT REPRODUCE and it is NOT identified: the run that saw it did not retain its own FAILED lines (the background capture kept only the tail), so there is no name to chase. A fourth run on the branch mid-way through a `git stash` gave 29 and is discarded as an unreliable measurement — its tree changed underneath it.

SUSPECTED but NOT established: an order-dependent or timing-sensitive test, which is the ordinary cause of a +/-1 spread across otherwise identical suites. Recorded as a suspicion. What IS established is that the current tree carries exactly the baseline failures and nothing more, so nothing is being masked by this.

WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW AT ALL: a suite whose count moves by one without explanation quietly erodes the meaning of green, and the next session comparing counts rather than SETS would reach a wrong conclusion cheaply. The set-diff (comm against a clean-tree baseline) is the technique that made this visible and should be the default for any Tier-3 change, not the count.
items.resolution_criteria: Either the flaky test is identified (e.g. by running the suite with -p no:randomly and with several seeds, or by capturing full FAILED lines across repeated runs) and made deterministic, or three consecutive full-suite runs on an unchanged tree produce identical failure SETS, establishing that the variance is gone. Explicitly NOT sufficient: a single green run, or matching counts without comparing the sets.

items.title: RECURRENCE, 3rd workflow: a concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:false SILENTLY CANCELS the pending run — hit system-actions today and dropped 2 of 4 REAL-MONEY position-mode switches; BL-20260611-002 is marked resolved while its own last update says otherwise and its resolution criteria were never met
items.detail: OBSERVED TODAY, not reasoned about. Four switch-bybit-position-mode issues were opened within 13 seconds (09:47:04/07/14/17Z) to switch bybit_2's four symbols to hedge. Runs 33304889251 (XRPUSDT) and 33304897836 (ADAUSDT) succeeded; 33304891110 (ETHUSDT) and 33304895331 (BTCUSDT) came back conclusion=CANCELLED having made NO venue call. === MECHANISM, verified in the workflow not assumed: .github/workflows/system-actions.yml:229 sets concurrency {group: system-actions, cancel-in-progress: false}. GitHub keeps exactly ONE pending run per group — when a newer run joins, the PENDING one is cancelled. cancel-in-progress protects the RUNNING job and says nothing about the queued one. So one running + one last-queued survive and every run queued between them is dropped. This also explains why the same session's earlier PAIRS of dispatches all succeeded: 1 running + 1 pending is exactly the survivable case, so the batching had been silently on the edge for the whole session. === WHY THIS ONE MATTERS MORE THAN ITS SIBLINGS: it left a REAL-MONEY account (bybit_2, mainnet) in a MIXED position mode — XRPUSDT and ADAUSDT hedge, ETHUSDT and BTCUSDT still one-way — with every completed run reporting 'wrapper exit code: 0' and no error anywhere. Had the operator or a session then armed BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS off the successful issue comments, Bybit would have refused EVERY order on the two symbols that never switched, on an account routing 7 live strategies. The mixed state was detectable only by listing workflow-run conclusions; nothing in the issue comments revealed it. Recovered by re-dispatching the two serially. === THIS IS A CLASS, MEMBERS: (1) BL-20260611-002 vm-diag-snapshot, whose last update on 2026-06-29 reads 'RECURRENCE RECONFIRMED ... a burst of ~6 vm-diag-request issues ... silently CANCELLED ... Still open - the durable fix (per-request concurrency group)'; (2) BL-20260828-PROP-REPORT-CONCURRENCY-SILENTLY-CANCELS-A-QUEUED-REPORT, open/HIGH, where a cancelled run meant a real prop fill (-77.22) was never journalled at all; (3) this instance on system-actions. Three different workflows, one root cause, and the durable fix named in (1) has been applied to NONE of them. === SECONDARY FINDING, and it is why the class survived: BL-20260611-002's status field says 'resolved' while its own newest update carries "status": "open" and describes the bug as still present. Its resolution_criteria ('Filing N diag-request issues back-to-back yields N result comments, or ... all skills instruct spacing') were demonstrably NOT met — this session filed 4 back-to-back and got 2. A row marked resolved that is not resolved is worse than an open row: it is why the duplicate probe surfaced a known, diagnosed, still-live defect as 'resolved' history rather than as a live warning. Reopening it in the same change.
items.evidence: system-actions runs 33304889251 success / 33304891110 CANCELLED / 33304895331 CANCELLED / 33304897836 success, created 09:47:04-09:47:17Z 2026-08-30. .github/workflows/system-actions.yml:229-231 concurrency {group: system-actions, cancel-in-progress: false}. Serial re-dispatch: #10477 (ETHUSDT) and #10478 (BTCUSDT) both switch_verified=true. Sibling rows BL-20260611-002 and BL-20260828-PROP-REPORT-CONCURRENCY-SILENTLY-CANCELS-A-QUEUED-REPORT.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) the three workflows take a PER-REQUEST concurrency group (e.g. group: system-actions-${{ github.event.issue.number }}) so queued dispatches cannot evict one another, verified by opening 4 issues back-to-back and observing 4 result comments — verified by the COMMENTS and the venue/journal effect, never by the runs reporting success, since the failure mode is a run that never starts; or (b) if serialisation is genuinely required, the workflow detects its own cancellation and posts a 'this request was dropped, re-dispatch it' comment, so a silent drop becomes a loud one. Documentation alone does not close this: BL-20260611-002 was closed on a documentation-shaped criterion and the defect recurred twice more.
items.trigger_condition: Any session dispatching more than two issue-triggered workflow requests in the same concurrency group without awaiting each result. Until fixed, dispatch system-actions / vm-diag-snapshot / prop-report requests SERIALLY — one, await its comment, then the next.

items.tier: 1 (tooling + a Tier-2 dispatch to apply it); the live order path is untouched
items.title: An OPERATIONAL flatten leaves no marker on the journal row — the reconciler stamps `reconciler_filled`, so a human-chosen exit is byte-indistinguishable from a strategy exit and lands in the exit-geometry corpus as evidence about the strategy
items.detail:
RAISED BY THE OPERATOR 2026-08-30, immediately after the bybit_2 hedge-mode switch required flattening two live real-money positions to satisfy the flat-symbol guard: 'i want to make sure they are marked correctly as not closed by strategy so we know not to use the exit data in analyses.' They were not marked, and nothing would have marked them.

MECHANISM. scripts/ops/flatten_{bybit,ib,alpaca}_position.py deliberately do not touch the journal — their own docstrings say 'The journal row is left for the trader's reconciler to close-on-disappear.' The reconciler duly observes the position is flat and stamps exit_reason='reconciler_filled' + notes.closed_by='monitor_reconciler'. That is a correct description of HOW the row closed and a misleading one about WHY. No column anywhere records that a human chose the exit time for a reason unrelated to the market.

MEASURED on the two rows (via /api/diag/journal?table=trades&limit=600):
  id=4934 bybit_2 XRPUSDT long  entry 1.4983 exit 1.3866 pnl -2.4509 exit_reason=reconciler_filled exit_price_source=bybit_closed_pnl (MEASURED) exit_reason_source=unresolved
  id=4904 bybit_2 ETHUSDT long  entry 2517.79 exit 2453.43 pnl -1.2872 exit_reason=reconciler_filled exit_price_source=candle_at_close (ESTIMATED) exit_reason_source=unresolved

WHY IT MATTERS. /api/bot/performance's perExitPath buckets on exit_reason, so both rows sit in `reconciler_filled` beside genuine closes; and the exit-refinement corpus reads entry->exit geometry as evidence about the strategy's exit quality. Two rows is nothing on its own — the defect is that the CLASS is unmarkable, and every future operational flatten joins it silently.

A SUSPICION I CHECKED AND HAD TO WITHDRAW, recorded because the withdrawal is the useful part: I first expected backfill-exit-labels to MANUFACTURE a false sl/tp verdict on these rows. It would not. Both exits land mid-bracket (XRP SL 1.28356 / TP 1.64795; ETH SL 2339.08 / TP 2766.83), so the price-vs-bracket classifier correctly returns `unresolved`. The problem is subtler than a false verdict: `unresolved` is documented as 'a genuine non-bracket close', which reads as the STRATEGY's own exit. Honest about the price, silent about the cause.

THE CONVENTION ALREADY EXISTS AND IS UNREACHABLE ON THIS PATH. close_stranded_journal_row.py owns exit_reason='operator_flatten_reconciled' + notes.exit_price_source='operator_flatten_fill' (the latter is in provenance.py's MEASURED set). But it hard-filters `WHERE status = 'open'` — it is the tool for when the reconciler FAILS to close the row. On the normal path, where the reconciler SUCCEEDS, the marker is never applied. So the marker exists precisely for the rarer case and is missing for the common one.

SHIPPED IN THIS CHANGE (the retroactive half): scripts/ops/mark_operator_flattened.py + its Tier-2 action `mark-operator-flattened`. Targets are NAMED, never derived — no column carries 'an operator flattened this', which is the bug, so a filter-based version would invent the signal it exists to record. It writes exit_reason and notes only: no monetary field, and NOT exit_price_source, because the PRICE's provenance and the CLOSE's CAUSE are different questions and stamping operator_flatten_fill over 4934's bybit_closed_pnl would be the exact clobber BL-20260824-RECORDED-EXIT-PRICE-OUTNUMBERS-ALL-BROKER-TRUTH-COMBINED records. 12 planted self-test controls, two non-vacuity controls verified (removing the closed-status guard fails 2 checks; letting it clobber exit_price_source fails 1), plus 4 pytest cases including the wrapper-wiring assertion.

NOT FIXED, AND THIS IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS: the flatten scripts still leave no marker, so the NEXT operational flatten reproduces this and someone has to remember to dispatch the new action afterwards. A remedy that depends on memory is the shape this repo files as a bug everywhere else. The durable fix is for the flatten script to record its intent where the reconciler's close path can read it, so the marking happens without a second dispatch — that touches the live close path and is Tier-2/3, which is why it is proposed here rather than shipped.

ADJACENT, NOT DUPLICATE: BL-20260822-EXIT-REASON-FROZEN-WHEN-PRICE-ARRIVES-LATE (0.70 lexical overlap) is about a label frozen because the CLASSIFIER never re-ran once a price arrived. This is about there being no signal for any classifier to read in the first place. Its fix (backfill-exit-labels) would stamp these rows `unresolved`, which is honest and still does not say 'operator'.
items.resolution_criteria: TWO parts, and the first alone does not close it. (1) RETROACTIVE: trades 4904 and 4934 carry exit_reason='operator_flatten_reconciled' + notes.closed_by_operator, verified by reading the rows back from /api/diag/journal after the mark-operator-flattened dispatch — not by the action reporting success. (2) DURABLE: an operational flatten marks its own journal row WITHOUT a second manual dispatch, so the class cannot recur through forgetfulness; demonstrated by a flatten whose resulting row carries the operator marker with no intervening mark-operator-flattened run. Closable only when (2) is exercised on a real flatten, not when the code merges.
items.what_to_check:
1. Whether any EARLIER operational flatten is sitting in the corpus unmarked. The denominator is UNKNOWN, not zero — I checked only the two rows from today. A sweep for closed rows whose close time is adjacent to a flatten-* system-action audit entry would establish it.
2. Whether ETH 4904's exit price should be recovered. We flattened it ourselves, so a REAL Bybit fill exists, yet the row booked candle_at_close (ESTIMATED). pull-exchange-fills + the Bybit-truth sweep should be able to replace an estimate with the actual fill on a close we ourselves caused.
3. Whether the IB and Alpaca flatten paths need the same treatment — almost certainly yes (identical docstring, identical hand-off to the reconciler), unverified.
items.source: operator question during /system-review 2026-08-30
items.update_2026_08_30: SUBSTANTIAL PROGRESS, NOT CLOSABLE — part (1) met, part (2) partially met, and the blocker on (2) is now named precisely. (1) RETROACTIVE: trades 4904 and 4934 read back from /api/diag/journal both carry exit_reason='operator_flatten_reconciled' + notes.closed_by_operator=true. MET. (2) DURABLE: the flatten scripts now stamp `operator_flatten_intent` on the OPEN row before the broker close, and — after the notes-cap root cause was fixed in PR #10508 — that marker SURVIVES the reconciler close: live trade 4935 (bybit_portfolio/XRPUSDT, flattened 19:06, closed 19:09:57Z) carries `operator_flatten_intent: true` with NO intervening mark-operator-flattened run. So the marker is durable. BUT the row's criterion is that the flatten 'marks its own journal row', and 4935's exit_reason is still 'reconciler_filled' — converting intent into the mark requires `mark_operator_flattened.py --from-intent`, and THAT MODE IS UNREACHABLE FROM THE SYSTEM-ACTION WRAPPER, which requires an explicit trade_id (scripts/ops/mark_operator_flattened_action.sh errors on 'no trade_id'). The derivation half exists in the script and has no operational surface. Closes when --from-intent runs unattended — the approved plan is to wire it into the monitor tick — and a flatten's row reaches exit_reason='operator_flatten_reconciled' with no human dispatch.

updates.note:
PARTIALLY DISPROVEN 2026-09-08 (MI-200, session 01CvFCybCkvrfzaHqNH3tQsb) — THIS ROW'S OWN MEASURED BLOCK IS NOW STALE AND MUST NOT BE RE-QUOTED. It records both exhibits as exit_reason='reconciler_filled'. Read from the live journal today via /api/bot/db/table/trades (filter_state 'applied' asserted), BOTH now read exit_reason='operator_flatten_reconciled':
    id=4934 bybit_2 XRPUSDT pnl -2.4509 exit_reason='operator_flatten_reconciled' (was 'reconciler_filled')
    id=4904 bybit_2 ETHUSDT pnl -1.2872 exit_reason='operator_flatten_reconciled' (was 'reconciler_filled')
So the RETROACTIVE half shipped by this row (scripts/ops/mark_operator_flattened.py + the Tier-2 `mark-operator-flattened` action) is not merely shipped — it has been OBSERVED APPLIED ON THE FLEET, which is a different and stronger fact than the row previously carried. Field beats comment: the column is the truth and this row's prose is what needed fixing.

TWO THINGS THAT DO **NOT** CLEAR, AND THEY ARE DIFFERENT FACTS.
(1) THE STRUCTURAL HALF IS UNTOUCHED — the flatten scripts still leave no marker, so the NEXT operational flatten reproduces this and depends on someone remembering to dispatch the action. That is the half this row itself calls 'the half that matters', and it is why the row stays open.
(2) THE `notes` JSON STILL CARRIES THE MISLEADING VALUE, which nobody has recorded before. Both rows still hold notes.closed_by='monitor_reconciler' and notes.closed_reason='reconciler - Bybit reports order filled and position flat'. So the COLUMN now says operator and the NOTES still say reconciler, and a consumer reading notes (several do — src/utils/json_notes.py exists precisely for this) still sees a human-chosen exit described as a reconciler close. The marker did not clobber notes.exit_price_source, which was DELIBERATE and correct per this row's own reasoning (the PRICE's provenance and the CLOSE's CAUSE are different questions) — but the CAUSE fields in notes were left saying the wrong thing, and that is a genuine residual, not a re-statement of the structural gap.

OPERATIONAL RELEVANCE: both exhibits appear inside the 14-trade real-money losing streak the operator raised on 2026-09-08. Under the corrected label they are correctly excluded from strategy-exit evidence; under the old label they would have counted as two strategy losses. See docs/research/real-money-close-attribution-2026-09-08.md.

items.tier: 1 (research tooling + a workflow assertion; no src/, no config/, no order path)
items.title: e35-bracket-sweep's landing assertion was satisfied by HISTORY, not by the run — it reported `landed` on a run whose rows were all on an unmerged side branch, and could never fail
items.detail: FOUND BY OPERATING THE DISPATCHER, not by reading it. e35-bracket-sweep.yml asserted `--field cell --contains sm --min-rows 1` against docs/research/e35-bracket-corpus.jsonl. That store is CUMULATIVE, so the predicate was satisfied by pre-existing rows and assert_rows_landed's `pending_merge` branch was UNREACHABLE — the check could not fail. MEASURED on run 33306805155 (the first sweep the research-queue dispatcher ever fired): the step reported `landed - 6624 rows with cell containing 'sm' (need >= 1) of 8289 total`, exit 0, while EVERY one of that run's 199 rows sat on the unmerged side branch claude/e35-bracket-corpus-33306805155. POPULATION: all 6,624 matching rows on origin/main predate 2026-08-30; zero came from the run. ONE-WAY FAILURE, in the direction that matters: it can only OVER-report `landed`, and R2 is CREDITED as wired on this workflow (ROADMAP M40 names it as one of the two landing-asserted workflows), so its green read as evidence the rows had arrived. assert_rows_landed.py is NOT at fault and was not changed — its four states are correct and --pushed-ref exists precisely for this case. The INVOCATION was wrong. DISTINCT FROM TWO NEIGHBOURS, deliberately: BL-20260813-CORPUS-RETARGET-CANNOT-OPEN-ITS-OWN-PR explains why no PR opens (a GITHUB_TOKEN push starts no workflows), and BL-20260817-AN-UNMERGED-ARTIFACT-BRANCH-SILENCES-A-GUARD-THAT-READS-MAIN is a guard being SILENCED. Here the guard is not silenced — it actively asserts success. CHRONIC, not a one-off: claude/e35-bracket-corpus (an earlier run's branch) is ALSO still unmerged into main. FIXED in the same session by scoping on `sweep_generated_at`. NOTE FOR ANYONE RE-DERIVING: `run_id` is ABSENT from all 8,294 e35 rows — it exists only in the m20 corpus, where it holds a TIMESTAMP rather than a GitHub run id. I asserted run_id in PR #10486's body and corrected it there; keying on it would be wrong in both corpora for different reasons.
items.resolution_criteria: The assertion must be demonstrably able to FAIL: a planted control in which the run's rows are absent from the shared ref must produce `pending_merge` (non-zero), and the same control must return `landed` once the branch is merged — so it is not merely always-failing. Shipped as tests/test_e35_landing_assertion_run_scoped.py, whose load-bearing case PINS the old vacuous predicate's wrong-but-actual behaviour so a revert fails loudly. NOT closed by the fix alone: the SIBLING SWEEP is unaudited — m20-exit-lever-sweep.yml writes an equally cumulative corpus and may assert the same way. This row closes when the sibling has been READ and either found run-scoped or fixed.
items.what_to_check: python3 scripts/ci/assert_rows_landed.py --store docs/research/e35-bracket-corpus.jsonl --ref origin/main --field cell --contains sm --min-rows 1  -> reports `landed` off history alone. Then grep the landing assertion in .github/workflows/m20-exit-lever-sweep.yml and ask whether its predicate is satisfiable by rows the run did not write.
refs: PR #10486 (landed the stranded rows; body carries the run_id error + its correction)
items.source: research-queue operationalisation 2026-08-30

updates.note: THE SIBLING HAS BEEN READ, and the answer is a THIRD state the criterion did not anticipate — recorded rather than forced into one of the two offered. The criterion says this closes when the sibling 'has been READ and either found run-scoped or fixed'. Read 2026-09-09: .github/workflows/m20-exit-lever-sweep.yml DOES NOT INVOKE assert_rows_landed AT ALL. Measured with a positive control rather than a bare negative: `grep -rn assert_rows_landed .github/workflows/` returns hits in exactly three workflows — trainer-offload-train.yml (L530), gld-compat-matrix.yml (L453) and e35-bracket-sweep.yml (L542, plus its L490 comment) — and none in m20-exit-lever-sweep.yml, so the probe demonstrably finds positives. The sibling writes a cumulative corpus (docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl, its 'Merge this run into the corpus' + 'Commit the corpus' steps at L486-L560) with NO landing assertion over it. So it is neither 'run-scoped' nor 'fixed': it asserts nothing, which is a different and arguably quieter failure than asserting vacuously — there is no green to misread, but also no check that the run's rows arrived. NOT CLOSING ON THIS: the criterion's intent is that the sibling be SAFE, and 'it has no assertion' does not make it safe. What the row now needs is a decision — give m20-exit-lever-sweep.yml a run-scoped assert_rows_landed (matching what e35-bracket-sweep.yml was fixed to do), or record that it deliberately has none. That is a workflow change and is out of a closing session's bounds.

updates.note:
CAUSE ESTABLISHED — it is an ARBITRATION LOSS, not a wiring bug. The row was filed naming two candidate causes with opposite remedies; this settles which, on live evidence.

THE DECISIVE ROW, /api/bot/allocator/soak?symbol=SOLUSDT, logged 2026-08-29T14:55:37Z:
  n_candidates: 2
  candidate A  trend_donchian_sol       entry 105.33  sl 103.82107143  conf 0.9941  score 6.811619
  candidate B  trend_donchian_sol_prop  entry 105.33  sl 103.82107143  conf 0.9941  score 5.906347
  executed_strategy_id: trend_donchian_sol_prop   allocator_choice: trend_donchian_sol
  agree: false   regret_score: 0.905272   score_kind: ev_net_r

IDENTICAL entry, SL and confidence: these are the SAME 1h Donchian strategy on SOLUSDT routed to two accounts (bybit_1 paper / breakout_1 prop). `aggregate_intents` picks ONE winner per SYMBOL GLOBALLY, before account fan-out, so the two collide and the PROP twin wins. The bybit_1 leg therefore never reaches an order package — which is exactly the 0-journal-rows observation.

⚠️ THE ROUTED LEG IS THE LOWER-SCORING ONE, BY THE SYSTEM'S OWN SCORER. 6.811619 vs 5.906347, and the allocator names trend_donchian_sol as its choice. Over the SOLUSDT soak population: total_scanned 47, disagree 42, disagree_pct 89.4, mean_regret 0.778926.

THIS EXPLAINS WORKPLAN LANE R / R2, which observed the OUTCOME without the mechanism: 'The SOL twin is inverted — trend_donchian_sol EV +$1,162 / P 0.9137 vs the routed trend_donchian_sol_prop +$611 / 0.7603.' Three independent measurements now agree on direction — R2's backtest EV, the allocator's live ev_net_r, and the journal (0 rows vs 32 packages). R2 and this row are the same defect seen from two ends.

TWO CANDIDATE CAUSES REFUTED, so they are not re-tested:
 - NOT the loaded-strategy set. /api/bot/strategies runtime shows 52 loaded incl. trend_donchian_sol,    running:true, live on bybit_1, trader ticking (tick_age 1.6s). All six SOL legs resolve an intent    builder and carry symbols=['SOLUSDT'] in _strategy_symbol_scope.
 - NOT a regime OFF-cell. /api/diag/audit_query for event=regime_hard_gate AND regime_shadow_gate on    SOLUSDT over three days returns ZERO rows — consistent with CLAUDE.md's record that no SOL    trend_vol cell is authored and the 2026-07-06 walk-forward says none should be.

A SEPARATE, SMALLER FINDING FOUND WHILE TRACING IT — the audit says the opposite of what happened. At 14:59:03.701891 trend_donchian_sol logged side=buy; at 14:59:03.994185 its prop twin logged side=buy; at 14:59:04.639159 the pipeline_result row for SOLUSDT reads strategy=multiplexed_intents, side=none, status=skipped, reason='no_signal'. Two legs signalled and the audit records 'no_signal'. The information is lost in three stages: intents.py's _flat_position(reason='no_intents_for_symbol') is reached AFTER _hard_regime_gate has already filtered candidates, so it conflates 'nothing signalled' with 'everything was gated'; _desired_to_pipeline_signal carries that reason into meta; and pipeline.py:614 then overwrites it with the generic 'no_signal' on the audit row. Filed separately as BL-20260830-PIPELINE-RESULT-REPORTS-NO-SIGNAL-WHEN-TWO-LEGS-SIGNALLED-AND-LOST-ARBITRATION.

WHY THIS ROW STAYS OPEN AND IS NOT DOWNGRADED: the mechanism is now known but nothing is fixed, and the remedy is TIER-3 — it is Lane P/P3 (decide the arbitration scope: whether a prop leg and a paper/real leg of the SAME strategy on the SAME symbol should compete at all, or fan out per account). That is an order-routing change and belongs to the operator, so it is PROPOSED, not pushed. ⚠️ Do NOT 'fix' this by de-routing either leg on the current evidence: the allocator's score and R2's EV agree the bybit_1 leg is the better one, so the naive fix would remove the wrong twin.

THE MEASUREMENT SHIPPED; THE REMEDY DID NOT, AND THE LEG IS STILL SIGNALLING INTO A VOID. Operator chose 'fan out per account' 2026-08-30. What landed is the Tier-1 half: `src/runtime/arbitration_fanout.py` (a PURE assessment — no I/O, no audit emission, no order path) + `arbitration_fanout_soak.py` at `ARBITRATION_FANOUT_MODE=annotate`, wired observe-only beside the existing M18 allocator soak in `intent_multiplexer`, with its `/api/diag/log_file?name=arbitration_fanout_soak` allowlist entry IN THE SAME COMMIT as the writer.

⚠️ WHAT THE SOAK MEASURES IS NARROWER THAN 'WHAT FAN-OUT WOULD DO', AND THE ROW SAYS SO RATHER THAN LETTING A READER ASSUME. It records STARVATION — which accounts held a candidate and did not get the winner — NOT which candidate each account would elect. Electing a per-account winner means re-running `aggregate_intents` on each account's subset, which re-enters `_hard_regime_gate` and would RE-EMIT a `regime_hard_gate` audit row per account per tick, corrupting the one signal that cleanly partitions 'would have gated' from 'did gate'. Starvation is side-effect-free and sufficient to size the change: an account never starved gains nothing from fanning out. So do NOT read a `starved` row as 'this account would have traded' — whether its candidate then survives its own gate and conflict resolution is UNMEASURED.

VERIFIED to reproduce the live case before wiring: fed the real accounts.yaml roster with candidates [trend_donchian_sol, trend_donchian_sol_prop] and winner trend_donchian_sol_prop, it returns starved=['bybit_1'], breakout_1='routed', accounts_graded=2.

GATE POLARITY, called out because it is deliberately the OPPOSITE of two siblings: `ARBITRATION_FANOUT_ACCOUNTS` EMPTY MEANS **NONE**. `CONVICTION_SIZING_ACCOUNTS` and `NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_ACCOUNTS` read empty as ALL, which CLAUDE.md itself calls 'not a safe default, it is the widest one'; this one would arm a change to WHICH ACCOUNT AN ORDER ROUTES TO, so it copies `PROTECTION_REASSERT_ACCOUNTS` polarity. A test asserts it and says that 'harmonising' it to match the siblings would be the bug, not the fix. The allowlist scopes the BINDING, never the MEASUREMENT — a held-back account is still assessed and annotated, so the rows a reviewer needs before widening exist.

⚠️ `apply` IS NOT IMPLEMENTED and the mode does not pretend otherwise: it is refused back to `annotate` and the row carries `apply_implemented: false` beside the effective `mode` and the requested `global_mode`, so a held-back row can never read as an applied one. Actually fanning arbitration out is a Tier-3 change to `aggregate_intents`' call SCOPE and ships separately, on this soak's evidence.

THIS ROW STAYS OPEN. The detector exists, the cause is known, the blast radius is measured (113/137 = 82.5% fleet-wide), and `trend_donchian_sol` has still never written a row on `bybit_1`. It closes when that leg journals — or when the fan-out ships and the soak shows the starvation gone.

⚠️ MY EARLIER DIAGNOSIS ON THIS ROW WAS INCOMPLETE, AND CORRECTING IT MATTERS BECAUSE IT CHANGES THE FIX. I recorded the cause as the global per-SYMBOL arbitration scope. That scope is a real structural issue and still worth fixing — but it is NOT why this leg loses. It loses to a STRING COMPARISON BUG in the tiebreak: the key ends in `tuple(-ord(c) for c in i.strategy.lower())`, and a shorter tuple that is a PREFIX of a longer one always compares LESS in Python, so `max()` picks the LONGER NAME. `trend_donchian_sol` loses to `trend_donchian_sol_prop` for no reason but the suffix. Every other key is tied: target_qty is the 0.0 sentinel, priority is 0 for all six colliding legs (measured), timestamps differ by milliseconds and favour the loser. Reproduced and it predicts all three live collisions including eth_pullback, which runs the OTHER way because that pair is not a prefix pair. Full root cause + the Tier-3 options: BL-20260830-INTENT-TIEBREAK-PICKS-THE-LONGER-STRATEGY-NAME-SO-SPELLING-DECIDES-WHO-TRADES.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS ROW: the per-account fan-out would fix this leg, but so would the tiebreak, and the tiebreak is a far smaller change than restructuring run_pipeline's dispatch. Do not assume the fan-out is the only route.

AND THE SCOPE IS WIDER THAN THIS LEG. config/accounts.yaml records that on 2026-07-07 (Tier-3, operator-approved) trend_donchian_sol, trend_donchian_eth and eth_pullback_prop_2h were added to bybit_1 precisely because they 'were execution:live but routed ONLY to the prop account breakout_1 — no paper soak, violating "every non-downgraded strategy soaks on a paper account"'. Those three are EXACTLY the three twin collisions. All three lose the tiebreak to their twin, so NONE of them has soaked on paper. An operator-approved fix has been silently inert for ~8 weeks while the config asserts it is in place.

items.title: the pipeline_result audit row says reason='no_signal' for a symbol where two strategies just emitted actionable buy signals — an UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC, sub-class A
items.detail:
MEASURED on the live audit log, 2026-08-29, SOLUSDT:
  14:59:03.701891  trend_donchian_sol_eval        side=buy
  14:59:03.994185  trend_donchian_sol_prop_eval   side=buy
  14:59:04.639159  pipeline_result  strategy=multiplexed_intents  side=none  status=skipped  reason='no_signal'

Two legs signalled and the audit records 'no_signal'. The label is TRUE of the aggregated signal object and FALSE of the situation, which is exactly the semantic substitution CLAUDE.md's 'Diagnostic provenance' section calls sub-class A.

THE INFORMATION IS LOST IN THREE STAGES, and each is individually defensible:
1. src/runtime/intents.py — _hard_regime_gate(candidates) runs BEFORE the `if not candidates` check, so _flat_position(reason='no_intents_for_symbol') is reached both when nothing signalled AND when the gate dropped everything. That is a COLLAPSED STATE in the CLAUDE.md sense: 'we did not look' / 'nothing was there' / 'we looked and removed it' share one string. It is ALSO reached when intents existed and lost arbitration, which the name denies outright.
2. src/runtime/intent_multiplexer.py::_desired_to_pipeline_signal — correctly carries desired.reason into meta['reason'] and the aggregation detail into meta['aggregation']. This stage is FINE; it is the one that preserves the information.
3. src/runtime/pipeline.py:614 — `result = {'status':'skipped','reason':'no_signal','signal':signal}` discards the meta reason and stamps the generic literal onto the audit row.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC: 'no_signal' is precisely the string a reader or a silence check uses to conclude that nothing wanted to trade. It is the audit-side twin of the two-month blind spot in BL-20260830-TREND-DONCHIAN-SOL-SIGNALS-144-TIMES-AND-JOURNALS-NOTHING-ON-BYBIT-1: the journal had no row AND the audit affirmatively said nothing signalled, so both surfaces agreed on a false negative. The true state was recorded only in allocator_soak, which is observe-only and which no health check reads.

⚠️ NOT the same as the regime-gate audit rows. Those fire correctly when the gate acts (regime_hard_gate with enforced:true) — and on SOLUSDT there are ZERO of them over three days, which is how the gate was ruled out as the cause. This row is about the case where NO gate fired and intents simply lost.
items.proposed_fix: Carry the reason that already exists rather than inventing a new mechanism. pipeline.py:614 should prefer the signal's own meta['reason'] when present and fall back to 'no_signal' only when the signal carries none — one line, and it makes 'no_intents_for_symbol' / 'all_intents_flat' visible on the audit surface. SEPARATELY and more importantly, intents.py should stop collapsing: give _flat_position distinct reasons for (a) no intents were built, (b) the regime gate removed them all, and (c) intents existed and none won — today all three read 'no_intents_for_symbol', and (c) is the live case. ⚠️ Do NOT add a decorative branch to satisfy collapsed-state-guard: each new state needs a real consumer, and the natural one is the audit row this same fix unblocks.
items.resolution_criteria: A pipeline_result row is READ BACK from /api/diag/audit_query for a tick on which a strategy signalled and did not route, and its reason distinguishes the arbitration loss from a genuinely quiet symbol. Verified by reading the live row, not by a unit test — a passing test is not an observation of the live mechanism.

items.title: trades.notes is capped at TWO budgets — 15 sites at 500, 7 at 2000 — and NO commit has ever justified either; both are ad-hoc char-slice lengths inherited verbatim by a migration whose stated scope was 'only how the blob is encoded'
items.detail:
TRACED 2026-08-30 through git history, because the split is what shed a provenance key on live rows and the operator asked why 500 exists BEFORE anything was changed.

WHAT HAPPENED. `b355457c` (#4019, 2026-06-19) replaced 12 `json.dumps(payload)[:N]` sites with `dump_capped(payload, N)` to kill the slice-invalid-JSON footgun. Its diff preserves each site's N VERBATIM (`[:2000]` -> `2000`, `[:500]` -> `500`) and its own message states the scope: 'No order/risk logic changed — only how the notes/signal_logic blob is encoded.' So the encoder migration deliberately did not touch the budgets. Tracing further back, the values are per-site slice lengths chosen ad hoc by whoever wrote each call site (the earliest, `a4b40e60`, introduces a bare `[:2000]`).

SO THE ANSWER TO 'why 500?' IS: no reason was ever recorded, at any point. It is not a row-size budget, not a schema limit, and not a measured choice — it is one author's arbitrary slice length propagated mechanically. That is the finding, and it is what makes the split safe to close rather than something to preserve.

MEASURED NOW: 15 call sites use 500, 7 use 2000 (`grep -oE "dump_capped\([^,]*, *[0-9]+\)"` over src/). The 500 group is the one that sheds provenance.

WHAT IT COST, live. Six rows were back-marked as operator flattens on 2026-08-30; trades 5238 and 5239 came back with `exit_reason` set (a COLUMN, so it survived) and BOTH notes keys gone. Their surviving key set was exactly `_DEFAULT_PROTECTED` + `_truncated` — `_shrink_dict`'s minimal envelope. The sequence: the marker wrote uncapped notes, then `order_monitor`'s broker-pnl close path (the 500 site) re-read them, added `exit_price_source`, and wrote back capped, dropping the unprotected keys.

⚠️ AT ~320 CHARS EVEN THE PROTECTED SET OVERFLOWS and `dump_capped` emits the barest marker, so protecting a key is not unconditional safety — it is safety above a budget-dependent floor. Asserted in `tests/test_json_notes_operator_flag_protected.py` rather than left to be discovered. 500 is uncomfortably close to that floor for a blob that already carries seven protected keys.

ADJACENT: BL-20260826-EXIT-REASON-SOURCE-TRUNCATED-BY-THE-NOTES-CAP is the same cap trimming a different provenance marker, fixed by protecting that key. Three markers have now been lost to this cap and each was fixed one key at a time; harmonising the budget would retire the CLASS instead.

What is NOT acceptable is leaving two undocumented budgets and continuing to protect keys one at a time as each is lost.

3. `order_packages.signal_logic` rides the same helper and was not examined.

items.title: aggregate_intents' conflict tiebreak compares a NEGATED-ORD TUPLE, so a shorter strategy name that is a PREFIX of another always loses — which strategy trades is decided by how its name is spelled
items.detail:
ROOT CAUSE of BL-20260830-TREND-DONCHIAN-SOL-SIGNALS-144-TIMES-AND-JOURNALS-NOTHING-ON-BYBIT-1, and it is NOT what that row's first diagnosis said. I recorded the cause as the global per-SYMBOL arbitration scope. That scope IS a real structural issue, but it is not why these legs lose. They lose to a STRING COMPARISON BUG in the tiebreaker.

THE CODE (src/runtime/intents.py, the no-conflict same-side branch):
    winner = max(same_side, key=lambda i: (
        i.target_qty, i.effective_priority(), -i.timestamp,
        tuple(-ord(c) for c in i.strategy.lower()),
    ))
with the comment: 'Alphabetical strategy name negation: max() wants "earlier alphabet" to win, so we negate by sorting descending'.

NEGATING ORDS DOES NOT REVERSE TUPLE-PREFIX ORDERING. In Python a shorter tuple that is a prefix of a longer one always compares LESS, whatever the sign of its elements. So `max()` picks the LONGER NAME whenever one name is a prefix of the other — the negation only affects the first position where the two tuples actually DIFFER, and for a prefix pair there is no such position.

EVERY OTHER KEY IS TIED ON THE LIVE PATH, so the tiebreak is the whole decision:
 - target_qty is the unsized sentinel 0.0 for every candidate (already filed: BL-20260810-INTENT-TARGET-QTY-ALWAYS-ZERO-TWO-CONSEQUENCES, whose note in this very function says the winner is 'decided entirely by the tiebreakers').
 - effective_priority() is 0 for all six colliding legs — MEASURED, not assumed: none sets `priority:` in strategies.yaml and all six resolve 0 from DEFAULT_PRIORITIES.
 - timestamps differ by milliseconds and, where measurable, favour the leg that LOSES.

REPRODUCED, and it predicts all THREE live collisions including the one that runs the other way — which is what rules out coincidence:
   trend_donchian_sol     vs trend_donchian_sol_prop   -> _prop wins   (live: _prop executed)
   trend_donchian_eth     vs trend_donchian_eth_prop   -> _prop wins   (live: _prop executed)
   eth_pullback_2h        vs eth_pullback_prop_2h      -> 2h wins      (live: 2h executed)
The first two are prefix pairs, so the longer name wins. The third is NOT a prefix pair, so it falls through to genuine alphabetical order and '2' (-50) beats 'p' (-112). Three for three against the live allocator_soak.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THESE LEGS. Which strategy trades is currently a function of how its name is SPELLED. Nobody chose that policy, it is not written down anywhere as intent, and it will silently reassign winners the next time a variant is named with a suffix. A `_prop`, `_v2` or `_alt` sibling beats its base name automatically.

IT ALSO EXPLAINS AN OPERATOR-APPROVED FIX THAT SILENTLY NEVER TOOK. config/accounts.yaml, 2026-07-07 (Tier-3, operator-approved, routing-coverage audit): 'added trend_donchian_sol (SOL 1h), trend_donchian_eth (ETH 1h) + eth_pullback_prop_2h ... These three were execution:live but routed ONLY to the prop account breakout_1 — no paper soak, violating "every non-downgraded strategy soaks on a paper account".' Those three legs are EXACTLY the three twin collisions. All three were added to bybit_1 to obtain a paper soak; all three lose this tiebreak to their twin; so none of them has soaked. The violation the change was made to fix has been live ever since while the config asserts it is fixed.
items.proposed_fix:
TIER-3 — this decides which strategy places a live order, so it is proposed, not pushed.

The bug is unambiguous; the REPLACEMENT POLICY is a real decision and should not be picked by whoever fixes the bug. Options, in the order I would argue them:
 (a) Make the intended rule work: compare the NAME STRING directly with a reversed sense (e.g. key on a sentinel-terminated tuple, or sort ascending on the name as the final key) so 'earlier alphabet wins' is what actually happens. Smallest diff, but it keeps a policy whose only merit is determinism — spelling still decides.
 (b) Break the tie on something that MEANS something. `allocator_ev.candidate_ev_score` already ranks candidates by cost-aware EV_R and is already computed on this path for the M18 soak; on the SOL pair it prefers trend_donchian_sol (6.811619 vs 5.906347) — i.e. the leg the current rule starves. ⚠️ But M18's own 2026-06-30 finding is that EV-scorer SELECTION does not beat dumb priority (OOS AUC ~0.51), so this needs its own evidence and must not be waved through on the strength of one pair.
 (c) Stop the collision existing: the per-account fan-out (Lane P/P3). Two legs on disjoint accounts are not competing for the same capital and should never reach a tiebreak at all. This is the structural fix and is orthogonal to (a)/(b) — it removes 113 of 137 measured disagreements; a tiebreak is still needed for the remaining 24 genuine contests.

⚠️ WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, A REGRESSION TEST MUST PIN THE PREFIX CASE. The current comment asserts the opposite of the behaviour, so the next reader will believe the code and not test it.
items.resolution_criteria: A prefix pair (e.g. `x` vs `x_prop`) resolves by the DECLARED policy rather than by name length, pinned by a test that FAILS against the current key — verified by mutation, not by reading the diff. ⚠️ NOT sufficient: the per-account fan-out shipping. That removes the three known collisions but leaves the tiebreak wrong for the 24 genuine cross-strategy contests, where a prefix-named pair would still be decided by spelling.
items.evidence: src/runtime/intents.py conflict-resolution key; DEFAULT_PRIORITIES (all six legs = 0); /api/bot/allocator/soak n=277 (3/3 collisions predicted); config/accounts.yaml 2026-07-07 routing-coverage comment

items.title: A transient red base permanently strands an auto-merge branch, because nothing ever updates it again
items.detail:
PRs #10398 and #10407 sat open for a day, both red on exactly two checks: session-brief-guard ("CLAUDE.md's SESSION-BRIEF block is STALE vs the registers") and 5 pytest failures ALL in tests/test_exit_reason_reclassify_on_late_price.py. Neither relates to what those PRs change (a calendar snapshot; a 9-line append). VERIFIED BY RUNNING EACH CHECK AT EACH COMMIT, not inferred: at their base 76d14af5 the session-brief guard exits 1 and that test file fails 5; on main 15c192bc it exits 0 and 11 pass. The test fix landed in c1f50fc, verified a DESCENDANT of their base. WHY THEY NEVER RECOVER: updated_at was byte-equal to created_at on both. Nothing updates an automation branch after it opens, so checks never re-run and auto-merge waits forever on a frozen snapshot of a base that no longer exists. MY FIRST HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG and is recorded so it is not re-tried: I blamed the documented GITHUB_TOKEN-does-not-trigger-checks trap, which commit-to-main's own description names. Checks DID run. They ran once, on a bad day. PROVEN BY ACTING, not by argument: updating automation/valuation-snapshots-33254438575-1 flipped #10407's guards failure to success and it then AUTO-MERGED unaided at 12:57:19Z. Same content; only the base moved.

⚠️ RECURRENCE 2026-08-31, AND IT IS NO LONGER JUST STRAY BRANCHES — THIS CLASS NOW BREAKS THE AUTONOMOUS RESEARCH LOOP. Severity raised medium -> high on this evidence.

⚠️ THIRD CONFIRMED INSTANCE, 2026-09-09 (session_01DUBXxiaZ3PMERcAfcJce7P) — AND IT IS THE ONE BL-20260901-AUTO-MERGE-DATA-PR-ABANDONED-ON-CONFLICT-AND-NOTHING-ALARMS EXPLICITLY PREDICTED. That row said of strategy-review-packets: it writes to a DATE-STAMPED directory and so is structurally far less prone to this, but it uses the SAME action and inherits the same silent-abandonment failure mode. The prediction was right, and the date-stamped path did NOT save it — this strand is BASE-side, not CONFLICT-side, so the structural protection was against the wrong half. PR #11361 (scheduled run 34207987310, event=schedule, 2026-09-08T09:04:39Z) has been OPEN since 09:05:03Z with updated_at frozen at 09:05:23Z, and comms/strategy_reviews/2026-09-08/ is ABSENT from main. CAUSE ESTABLISHED BY RUNNING THE CHECK, NOT INFERRED — the run error message names two candidates and warns they look identical from the runner: (a) the branch failed on its own content, or (b) never re-run after a transient red base. IT IS (b). #11361 five check runs show guards FAILED at 09:07:13Z while pytest-run, pytest-collect, audit and repo-inventory all PASSED; and check_board_coherence.py --all reports FAILED on a CLEAN worktree of its base a0ec22ce with NONE of #11361 changes applied (R3: check_pr_landing.py:542 hardcodes the retired board 6927). #11361 changes only an INDEX.json plus two landing declarations and cannot touch scripts/ci/. MI-191 fixed that red on main later the same day; nothing re-ran #11361, so it is stranded permanently — this row exact mechanism. ⚠️ WHAT IS NEW AND CARRIES THE SEVERITY: this class now eats a DECISION SURFACE DENOMINATOR, not just a snapshot. The strategy-review series is 7 of 8 days on main, and a reader of comms/strategy_reviews/ cannot tell a missing day from a day the generator did not run. Separately MEASURED on the same workflow: 4 of its 7 scheduled runs concluded failure, EVERY one at commit-to-main 30-minute merge wait rather than in the generator, and THREE of those four landed anyway after the window closed — so on this workflow a red run is USUALLY COSMETIC, which is precisely what makes the one real strand easy to walk past. ⚠️ AND A TEMPTING WRONG READING, CHECKED BEFORE REPORTING: #11361 changes 3 files, which under the selection rule (index always, two files per actionable row) reads as the first actionable strategy ever produced. It is NOT — the two extras are landing declarations and the stranded index reads actionable 0 / by_action hold 52 like every other day. No verdict is lost, only the denominator. NOT FIXED HERE: refreshing another lane automation PR is a merge-queue act and this was a worker session; raised on the board and in docs/claude/work/STRATEGY-REVIEW-WINDOW-FLOOR-2026-09-09.md section 4.

=== FOURTH INSTANCE, SAME DAY, AND IT ESCALATES THIS ROW: THE CLASS NOW REDS EVERY PR IN THE REPO. Measured 2026-09-09T07:50Z. `guards` failed on PR #11513 with PASS 54 / FAIL 1, the single failure being `trainer-capture-watch-guard`. REPRODUCED ON A CLEAN WORKTREE OF origin/main with none of that PR's changes applied, so it is base-side: the receipt docs/claude/work/TRAINER-CAPTURE-WATCH.json read generated_at 2026-09-08T16:44:31Z, i.e. 15.1h old against a 15h window. IT WENT RED ON THE CLOCK, which is the property that makes this instance different from the other three: it is not one stranded artifact nobody reads, it is a guard that fails EVERY PR in the repo until a fresh receipt lands. AND THE FRESH RECEIPT EXISTED AND WAS STRANDED BY THIS EXACT CLASS: PR #11488 (automation/data-commit-34312725937-1) has carried generated_at 2026-09-09T04:53:57Z since 04:54Z and never merged. Its run 34312725937 reads conclusion=failure, and READING THAT AS 'the watcher broke' IS THE UNPROVENANCED-DIAGNOSTIC TRAP THIS REPO HAS A GUARD FAMILY FOR -- checked, not assumed: the receipt was written at 04:53:57Z, 26 SECONDS after the run started, while the failure came at 05:24:29Z, 31 MINUTES in, and the job log's error is verbatim `commit-to-main: PR #11488 did not merge within 30m`. THE MEASUREMENT SUCCEEDED AND ONLY THE LANDING FAILED (event=schedule, run #45, capture_state fresh, controls_ok true, age=236s against a 1800s threshold). SO THE FAILURE MODE COMPOUNDS: a stranded liveness receipt does not merely go unread, it eventually makes the guard that grades it fail closed across the whole repo, and the artifact that would clear it is stranded by the same mechanism. A self-blocking loop. PORTED, NOT WORKED AROUND: the receipt was copied verbatim from #11488's branch into PR #11513 per the drive-to-green rule ('port the same change into this PR now; it no-ops once the base carries it'). It is genuine measured data from a real scheduled run, not a fabricated freshness stamp -- the run was verified to exist and its failure verified to be the landing step before anything was copied. The guard then read 3.0h against the 15h window. ⚠️ THIS PORT IS A WORKAROUND FOR ONE DAY AND NOT A FIX: the next receipt will strand the same way, and 19 of the 20 newest open PRs were automation/* at the time of writing.

The research-queue dispatcher's TWO most recent SCHEDULED runs both failed on exactly this: 33340458710 (2026-08-30T22:56Z) and 33342140520 (23:33Z). Read from the job log, the dispatch itself SUCCEEDED both times — `RQ-20260827-001 dispatched gld-compat-matrix.yml on main`, and its 11 verdict rows are on main 28 seconds later. What failed is the stamp: commit-to-main opened PR #10534, enabled auto-merge, then polled `state=OPEN` for the full 18 minutes and exited 1 with its own error message naming THIS row.

THE COST IS MEASURED, not hypothetical. `last_dispatched_at` for RQ-20260827-001 reached main only via PR #10540 — a MANUAL pull request opened by a session that happened to notice. Had nobody noticed, that job carries no cadence stamp and re-dispatches on EVERY scheduled run. So the loop's own state was rescued by hand, which is precisely what 'runs continuously outside a session' is supposed to stop needing.

NOTE WHAT THIS DOES NOT IMPLY, because the neighbouring diagnosis is tempting and wrong: the stamp branches from these two runs DO carry a destructive diff (27 insertions / 39 deletions on one YAML — the yaml.safe_dump round-trip that deletes comments and reflows block scalars, fixed separately). That is a real defect and it is NOT why these runs failed. They failed on the timeout, before anyone could object to the diff. Attributing the failure to the diff would send the next reader to fix the wrong half.
items.why_it_matters: POPULATION: 7 of 7 automation/* branches were unmerged at discovery, and four had no open PR at all. Three grade-order-packages branches are ~68 days old and 60 commits behind. The failure is silent in both directions - the branch looks like it is waiting for CI, and CI looks like it has already spoken. Every one of these carries data the system generated and then dropped on the floor, which is the same class as the unread-research-corpus finding: work performed, never landed, never noticed.
items.next_action: Run scripts/ops/stuck_automation_branches.py (shipped 2026-08-30 in #10493) and adjudicate the four PR-less branches - 'old' is not 'dead' and nobody has established which they are. Then decide whether a stale automation branch should be refreshed automatically (an empty commit is NOT the mechanism - the repo forbids it; merging the base forward is).
items.resolution_criteria: Do NOT close on the detector alone. stuck_automation_branches.py REPORTS; nothing yet re-runs a stale branch's checks, and the four PR-less branches are unadjudicated. Closes when a stale automation branch is refreshed automatically, or the four are adjudicated AND the class has a standing owner. ⚠️ WIDENED 2026-08-31: closing also requires that a SCHEDULED research-queue dispatch lands its own cadence stamp with no manual rescue — observed on a real run, not asserted. The original criteria are about stray branches; this class is now also the failure mode of the autonomous loop, and a fix that tidies branches without making the stamp land leaves that half open.
