items.summary: Most rows in DEFAULT_PRIORITIES justified a value of 0 with 'this leg runs ALONE on its (symbol, account), so priority is moot -- it never arbitrates against another strategy'. aggregate_intents elects ONE winner per SYMBOL, globally, BEFORE the per-account fan-out in multi_account_execute; it never sees an account. The justification described a scope the aggregator does not use, and it is the reasoning that produced BL-20260830-TREND-DONCHIAN-SOL-SIGNALS-144-TIMES-AND-JOURNALS-NOTHING-ON-BYBIT-1. MEASURED 2026-08-30 against the live config: 12 symbols are contested by more than one enabled leg -- BTCUSDT 7, SOLUSDT 6, ETHUSDT 6, XRPUSDT 4, MGC 3, AVAXUSDT 3, and six more at 2. Every contesting leg sits at priority 0, so the winner is decided entirely by the name tiebreak. Comments corrected + a mutation-verified regression test added (tests/test_priority_arbitration_scope.py); NO priority VALUE was changed, so behaviour is byte-identical.
items.resolution_criteria: Closes when the per-account fan-out ships and a contested symbol is observed routing to more than one account in the same tick, or when the priority values are set deliberately under Tier-3 approval and the test is updated to assert the intended winner rather than the spelling one.
items.notes: Second-order finding: 'execution: shadow' does NOT exclude a leg from this election -- that gate is in multi_account_execute, downstream. 6 of the 12 contested symbols carry at least one shadow leg (BTCUSDT 4 of 7), so a data-only leg can win a symbol and starve every live leg on it for that tick. eth_pullback_prop_2h (shadow) beats trend_donchian_eth (live) head-to-head today. Six comment blocks previously asserting 'never arbitrates a real order' on that basis were corrected.

items.summary: Setting explicit priorities was considered as the remedy for the starved trend_donchian_sol / trend_donchian_eth legs. It cannot work, and shipping it would trade one silent failure for another. VERIFIED 2026-08-30: each base leg and its _prop twin route to DISJOINT account sets (trend_donchian_sol -> {bybit_1}, trend_donchian_sol_prop -> {breakout_1}; same shape for eth), and the twins share entries by design -- the prop variant differs only in exits. So the correct outcome is that BOTH trade. aggregate_intents elects exactly ONE winner per symbol, so any ordering starves one of them; raising the base leg above its twin would starve a Tier-3 operator-approved live prop leg on the account where a breach is TERMINAL. The per-account fan-out is the only remedy that expresses the intended behaviour.
items.resolution_criteria: Closes when the fan-out ships and both twins of at least one pair produce order packages on their own accounts in the same tick, evidenced by the arbitration_fanout soak showing starved_accounts empty for that symbol.
items.notes: State the population: measured against config/strategies.yaml + config/accounts.yaml on 2026-08-30. The base legs also lose to all five of their other rivals in BOTH tiebreak branches, so a two-leg priority fix would not even settle the symbol -- four other legs would still outrank the base leg. The two branches disagree with each other by construction: the same-side branch maximises a negated-ord tuple (a strict PREFIX always loses, so the LONGER name wins) while the opposing-side branch sorts ascending (the SHORTER name wins).

items.opened_by: claude (/system-review 2026-08-30) — found while logging an operator prop-trade update
items.tier: 1 (the reporting path + a backfill); no order path — prop has no broker API
items.title: prop_fills has sl/tp columns and ingest_report accepts them, but 33 of 40 rows leave them NULL and put the bracket in free-text `reason` — so prop_sl_tp_alert's `if not sl and not tp: continue` makes the crossing alert INERT for 11 of 18 open-state fills, including the one live position
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-30 over the FULL prop_fills table (40 rows, 2026-06-22T15:32Z -> 2026-08-29T15:14Z, /api/bot/prop/fills?limit=200):
  rows with a structured sl: 7/40   (tp: 7/40)
  rows in an OPEN state (filled|open): 18, of which with an sl: 7
So ELEVEN open-state prop fills carry no machine-readable stop, and the one live position (id 40, SOLUSDT 49.0 @ 105.04) is one of them.

THE CHAIN. prop_sl_tp_alert reads sl = pos.get('sl') and short-circuits on `if not sl and not tp: continue`. With the column NULL the loop skips the position, so no crossing can ever be announced. prop_fills_staleness's crossing detector then reads crossing_state: unknown — correctly, since 'we did not look' is exactly what happened — which disarms the crossed_unreported half of that alert. The balance-delta half still works.

NOT A MISSING FEATURE — THE PLUMBING IS ALL THERE. prop_fills declares `sl REAL, tp REAL` (prop_journal.py) and prop_report.ingest_report already reads report.get('sl') / report.get('tp') into the insert. The reporter simply does not send them: fill 40's bracket was written into the reason prose as 'PLACED BRACKET DIFFERS FROM THE TICKET: SL 103.00 (ticket 103.82107143), TP 106.18 (ticket 114.38357143)'. That sentence is accurate, human-readable, and unreachable to every consumer.

AND THE PROSE GOES STALE SILENTLY, which is what surfaced it. The operator amended the bracket on the terminal: SL 103.00 -> 105.76 and TP 106.18 -> 114.00 (screenshot 2026-08-30). The journal still carries the original sentence, so it describes a position with 'risk 49.00 x (105.04 - 103.00) = $99.96 against a static-DD cushion of ~$55' — an account-killer shape — when the real stop now sits ABOVE the 105.04 entry and the trade cannot reach the floor at all. ⚠️ It is stale in the SAFE direction here, but the mechanism is symmetric: an operator WIDENING a stop would leave the journal understating risk with nothing to detect it, and there is no ingest path to amend a bracket — ingest_report has exactly two kinds (account_status and fill/close), so a correction would append a SECOND fill row for one position rather than update it.

THREE DIFFERENT STOP VALUES are currently recoverable for this one position and no consumer can tell which is live: the ticket's 103.82107143 (prop_tickets), the prose's 103.00 (fill 40 reason), and the terminal's actual 105.76 (unrecorded anywhere).
items.resolution_criteria: (1) The prop report path POPULATES sl/tp on every fill that has a bracket — the reporter sends them and the screenshot parser extracts them — verified by a new fill landing with non-null columns, not by the prose mentioning a stop. (2) prop_sl_tp_alert is shown to actually evaluate that position (an entry appears in its state file for it), so the short-circuit is no longer taken. (3) A bracket AMENDMENT is expressible without appending a duplicate position row — either a third report kind or an explicit update path. (4) The 11 existing open-state rows are backfilled or explicitly marked unrecoverable; leaving them NULL while new rows are correct would leave the live position uncovered, which is the whole finding.
items.what_to_check:
1. Whether the screenshot parser (src/prop/screenshot_parse.py, PROP_SCREENSHOT_MODEL) extracts Stop loss / Take profit at all — the terminal displays both as columns, so this may be a pure extraction gap rather than a reporter one. UNVERIFIED.
2. Whether the 7 rows that DO carry sl/tp came from a different path, which would name the working producer and make the fix a matter of routing.
3. Whether any past prop position crossed a stop unannounced because of this — the denominator is the 11 uncovered open-state rows, and it is UNKNOWN, not zero.

items.title: RECURRENCE of BL-20260720-GH-ACTIONS-PUSH-EVENTS-DEAD: a session again read `total_count: 0` check runs on its own PR as 'CI has not started' rather than 'merge conflict', re-deriving the diagnosis from scratch — the lesson was recorded verbatim in the backlog and did not reach the point of use
items.detail:
WHAT HAPPENED (2026-08-30, PR #10508). Opened a draft PR; `get_check_runs` returned `total_count: 0` and stayed there across three polls over ~12 minutes. I ran a positive control (`actions_list` repo-wide) which showed another session's branch getting all four workflows within seconds of its push, correctly ruling out an Actions outage — and then went on to read the three workflows' `on:` triggers and grep them for draft gating, before finally calling `pull_request_read` method `get` and seeing `mergeable_state: 'dirty'`. Merging `origin/main` in (one conflict, `docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json`, resolved by `backlog_union_merge.py`: 1020 + 4 theirs + 1 ours = 1025, 0 dupes, 0 deletions) made CI fire within seconds — guards / pytest-collect / repo-inventory all green.

WHY IT IS A RECURRENCE AND NOT A DUPLICATE. `BL-20260720-GH-ACTIONS-PUSH-EVENTS-DEAD` (resolved 2026-07-20) already carries the whole diagnosis in its detail, including the exact control I re-invented: 'before suspecting an Actions outage, check the PR's mergeable_state — dirty means no merge ref, means no pull_request CI; another session's PRs running CI at the same time is the fastest disproof of an outage.' So the KNOWLEDGE was not missing. What failed is RETRIEVAL: it lived only in a 1000-row backlog that CLAUDE.md itself says is too large to read at session start, so it was unreachable at the moment of confusion. That is the failure the operator named on 2026-08-26 ('We aren't using the backlog/lessons learned logs correctly if we still keep running into the same fuck ups'), and filing a third row about it would repeat the same mistake.

DURABLE PREVENTION (this is the fix, not the row). The paragraph is now restated in CLAUDE.md section 'PM-side session capabilities', directly under the existing 'assert a plausible non-zero denominator before believing a nothing-pending answer' rule that this case is an instance of — i.e. at the point of use, in the file that reaches a session before it acts. It names both ids so the chain is followable.

NOTE ON COST. Cheap in absolute terms (~10 minutes, ~6 tool calls) but it is the SECOND time; a third would be a pattern rather than an accident. It also composes with BL-20260821-BACKLOG-JSON-IS-A-SHARED-MUTABLE-ARRAY (open): four conflicts on that one file in a single day is what produced the dirty state here, so the conflict frequency and the mis-read of its symptom are two halves of the same tax.
items.tier: 1 (docs + a backlog row; no runtime path)
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED on landing: `grep -c 'mergeable_state' CLAUDE.md` is non-zero AND the 'PM-side session capabilities' CI-polling paragraph names both BL-20260720-GH-ACTIONS-PUSH-EVENTS-DEAD and this id, so the chain from symptom to cause is followable at the point of use. It REOPENS if a third row of this class is ever filed — that would mean restating it in CLAUDE.md was also not enough, and the next remedy is mechanical (a guard, or a wrapper that reads mergeable_state before reporting check runs) rather than more prose.

items.summary: The arbitration fan-out soak (#10501) grades an account 'starved' on a tick where NO strategy won the symbol at all. Literally the docstring holds -- starved is defined as 'held a candidate and did not get the winner', and with no winner the account did not get one -- but it COLLAPSES two conditions that mean opposite things: (a) another ACCOUNT got the winner and this one was starved of it (the defect the soak exists to measure), and (b) nobody won, so nothing was routed anywhere and no account lost anything. MEASURED on the live soak 2026-08-30, first 9 rows (14:25Z-19:03Z, BTCUSDT 7 / ETHUSDT 2): 13 account-gradings, of which 11 are the NO-WINNER case and only 2 are genuine starvation. So the headline starved_count overstates real starvation by ~5.5x on this sample. This is the sole evidence base for a Tier-3 routing decision, so a naive read of starved_count would materially mislead it.
items.resolution_criteria: Closes when a no-winner tick is graded as its own state (never 'starved') and the soak's summary reports genuine starvation separately from no-winner ticks -- verified by re-reading /api/diag/log_file?name=arbitration_fanout_soak and confirming the two populations are distinguishable without re-deriving them from winning_strategy by hand.
items.notes: The 2 genuine rows are the lane's own thesis confirmed live: bybit_1 starved while breakout_1 routed, winner trend_donchian_eth_prop -- the disjoint-account twin pair from BL-20260830-PRIORITY-CANNOT-RESOLVE-A-DISJOINT-ACCOUNT-TWIN-PAIR. So the soak IS capturing the real signal; the problem is that the real signal is buried under an uninformative one that shares its label. Found by reading the live rows rather than the tests -- the unit tests all pass, because they assert the definition as written rather than whether the two populations are separable. STATE THE POPULATION: n=9 rows over ~4.6h on one process; small, and BTCUSDT-dominated. || FIX SHIPPED 2026-08-30 (next session, PR on branch claude/fanout-starved-state-grading-wy9tk2). `no_winner` and `winner_unattributed` are now their own states; `starved_count`, `no_winner_count` and `winner_unattributed_count` are published side by side; a `no_winner` row is STILL WRITTEN because it is the denominator; `fanout_schema: 2` marks a post-split row so a reader of the accumulated log can tell it from a pre-split one. ⚠️ THE ROW ABOVE SAYS '~5.5x' AND THAT IS THE WRONG RATIO — 5.5 is 11/2 (no-winner gradings per genuine one). The factor by which the HEADLINE `starved_count` overstates the finding is 13/2 = 6.5x, because the old count included the 2 genuine gradings as well. Same 9 rows, same counts, re-derived twice this session: a fixture replay pinned as a test, and a script rebuilding the roster from the rows' own per_account.candidates that asserts each row's accounts_graded reproduces (15 gradings: 13 non-routed + 2 routed). STATUS STAYS OPEN: resolution_criteria requires re-reading /api/diag/log_file?name=arbitration_fanout_soak and confirming the populations are separable THERE, which needs the merge to reach the trader via ict-git-sync first. Tracked to that read by OI-20260830-FANOUT-SOAK-SPLIT-SHIPPED-NOT-YET-READ-LIVE.

updates.note:
RESOLVED — verified by re-reading the route the criterion names, with the population stated.

POPULATION: /api/diag/log_file?name=arbitration_fanout_soak&lines=1000 read 2026-09-01T23:0xZ returned **73 rows** against a requested 1000 (size_bytes 67711), so this is the COMPLETE file, not a truncated tail. Window 2026-08-30T14:25:15.286372Z -> 2026-09-01T22:31:54.627474Z.

(1) A NO-WINNER TICK IS GRADED AS ITS OWN STATE. `no_winner` is emitted as a per-account `state` value in its own right — measured, 19 per-account gradings of `no_winner` beside 19 `starved` and 53 `routed`. Example row, 2026-08-30T21:35:38.205494Z / BTCUSDT: no_winner_accounts ["bybit_1"], no_winner_count 1, starved_count 0, winning_strategy null.

(2) NEVER 'starved'. THE DECISIVE CHECK: over the 60 rows carrying `fanout_schema: 2`, the number with NO winning_strategy that are nonetheless graded starved is **0**. The old conflation is therefore gone on the post-fix schema.

(3) THE SUMMARY REPORTS THE POPULATIONS SEPARATELY, without re-deriving them from winning_strategy by hand — which is the clause the criterion is really about. Three distinct top-level counters ship on every row: starved_count (the finding), no_winner_count and winner_unattributed_count. Over the 60 schema-2 rows: starved_count>0 on **2**, no_winner_count>0 on **15**, winner_unattributed_count>0 on **0**. A reader gets both populations off the row.

⚠️ 13 of the 73 rows carry NO `fanout_schema` key. Those are the pre-fix rows whose `starved_accounts` conflates both populations, and they are correctly RETAINED rather than rewritten — the absent key is the version marker CLAUDE.md tells a reader to check before pooling. Do not pool them: 17 of the 19 raw `starved` per-account gradings sit on those 13 rows, against 2 on the 60 schema-2 rows, which reproduces the ~6.5x overstatement the original finding measured.

items.summary: MEASURED 2026-08-30: 13 workflows call the shared `commit-to-main` action; exactly ONE (gld-compat-matrix.yml) runs `assert_rows_landed.py`, and that one only since today. The other twelve -- cot-positioning-backfill, crypto-signals-backfill, econ-calendar-backfill, econ-calendar-produce, econ-calendar-survey-backfill, econ-event-study, gpu-burst-train, macro-producer-liveness, macro-valuation-backfill, macro-valuation-snapshot, research-queue-dispatch, sysdyn-gas-calibrate -- commit their rows to an AUTO-MERGE PR and never verify the merge happened. `commit-to-main` exits 0 the moment the PR is OPENED, so a green run means 'a PR exists', never 'the rows are on main'. R2 says a run is done when its rows are READABLE on the shared ref; twelve producers assert nothing of the kind. ⚠️ THIS IS THE DETECTION GAP, NOT THE CAUSE, and it is deliberately a separate row from BL-20260830-A-TRANSIENT-RED-BASE-PERMANENTLY-STRANDS-AN-AUTOMERGE-BRANCH (which explains WHY a branch strands) and from BL-20260817-AN-UNMERGED-ARTIFACT-BRANCH-SILENCES-A-GUARD-THAT-READS-MAIN (the consumer side). Fixing the cause would not make a future strand visible; nothing here would still say a word. NOT HYPOTHETICAL -- measured on origin the same day: 5 stranded `automation/*` branches, the oldest 10 weeks. The clean case is `automation/econ-calendar-33232352515-1`: exactly 1 commit off main, dated 2026-08-29T03:49:54Z, carrying 444 rows of comms/macro/econ_calendar_snapshots.jsonl plus a 61,529-line PIT snapshot. Its workflow exited 0. Two days later the data is still not on main and nothing has reported it. ⚠️ STATE THE POPULATION on the other four: `automation/valuation-snapshots` and the three `automation/grade-order-packages-*` are LONG-LIVED reused branches (no run-id suffix, or very old), and `git rev-list --count origin/main..BRANCH` returns 2716/2020 for them -- that number is NOT 2716 stranded data commits and must not be quoted as one; those branches have diverged and the count is unanalysed. The econ-calendar case is the one that is clean enough to be decisive. ⚠️ UPDATED SAME DAY, BEFORE THE ROW EVER SHIPPED: the mechanism this row calls for now EXISTS. `commit-to-main` gained a `verify-merged` input (PR 10524) that blocks until its own PR merges and FAILS if it does not, defaulting OFF so the twelve are byte-for-byte unchanged until each opts in. TWO of the thirteen now verify — gld-compat-matrix.yml and research-queue-dispatch.yml — so the count in the title is the state at filing, not the state now. ELEVEN remain.
items.detail:
HOW IT WAS FOUND: not by audit but by running the thing. gld-compat-matrix run 33331071521 (the first real execution of the landing chain built 2026-08-30) failed its own new assertion with `absent - 0 rows among 0 total rows` on a run that had emitted 124 trades and pushed a good commit. Root cause there was a missing `--pushed-ref` collapsing `pending_merge` into `absent` (fixed in the same PR). But the landing PR #10520 then merged on its own minutes later, and all 11 rows are on main -- which is what prompted asking how many OTHER callers would have noticed either way. Answer: none of them.

WHY IT WAS UNFIXABLE UNTIL TODAY: a caller cannot report `pending_merge` without naming the ref its rows were pushed to, and `commit-to-main` published only `committed` and `pr` -- not the branch. Callers would have had to re-derive `<prefix>-<run_id>-<attempt>`, a second copy of a naming scheme the action owns. The action now publishes `branch` (added 2026-08-30, additive), so the fix is a mechanical per-caller wiring rather than a design problem.

⚠️ THE FIX IS NOT JUST ADDING THE ASSERTION. `commit-to-main` enables AUTO-merge, which waits on required checks (~11 min), so an assertion placed immediately after it reports `pending_merge` on EVERY healthy run -- permanently red, which is the desensitized-alarm P1 and would be worse than the silence it replaces. gld-compat-matrix.yml carries the worked pattern: a bounded wait on `gh pr view --json state` that exits the moment the PR merges and still ASSERTS on timeout. Note this is NOT the trainer-offload-train.yml / e35 shape -- those push a branch and open no PR, so `pending_merge` is their terminal honest state; here it is transient. Copying their shape onto these twelve would produce twelve permanently-red workflows.

SEVERITY: high, not critical -- none of these is an order path, and the data is written and recoverable on its branch rather than lost. What is lost is the KNOWLEDGE that it did not land, which is the same shape as BL-20260827-EIGHTEEN-EVIDENCE-WORKFLOWS-UPLOAD-AND-LAND-NOTHING (those upload and land nothing; these commit and never confirm). Several of the twelve feed macro/econ corpora that later analyses read as complete, so a silent gap is read as an absence of events rather than an absence of data -- 'we did not look' rendered as 'we looked and found nothing'.

UPDATE (same session, ~40 min after filing): resolution option (b) was taken rather than left as a recommendation, because the SECOND caller needing it turned up immediately and writing the wait twice is how two copies drift. The trigger was research-queue-dispatch.yml, and it is the more serious instance: its stamp PR IS the armed cron's only idempotency, so a stranded stamp means `last_dispatched_at` never reaches main and the dispatcher re-fires the SAME job every day indefinitely — burning a runner each time and, for a GPU-routed job, real money against the spend ledger. Its own step comment warned that a fired-but-unstamped job 're-fires forever' while guarding only the FIRE-gate route to that state; this was the other door. Both are now closed and pinned by tests with a positive control (5 pins fail against 8183a387, pass after).

⚠️ DO NOT READ THIS AS THE ROW BEING RESOLVED. Eleven callers still verify nothing, and each is a one-line opt-in PLUS a `timeout-minutes` check — the calling job's budget must exceed the 18-min wait or the job dies mid-wait and reports a timeout for a merge that was about to land (research-queue-dispatch needed 15 -> 35). The five stranded branches are also still stranded; nothing here touched them.
items.resolution_criteria: TEN remaining callers each opt in with `verify-merged: "true"` and a `timeout-minutes` above the wait: cot-positioning-backfill, crypto-signals-backfill, econ-calendar-backfill, econ-calendar-produce, econ-calendar-survey-backfill, econ-event-study, gpu-burst-train, macro-valuation-backfill, macro-valuation-snapshot, sysdyn-gas-calibrate. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-31: this said ELEVEN and named `macro-producer-liveness`, which is NOT a caller — it mentions the string in two COMMENTS and calls only actions/checkout, setup-python and github-script (verified by parsing its steps, not by grepping prose). It is the MONITOR that watches this hop, so demanding it opt in would have left the row uncloseable against a workflow that cannot satisfy it. ⚠️ ALSO: a per-caller opt-in is NOT sufficient, and the row's own framing ("each is a one-line opt-in PLUS a timeout-minutes check") would have shipped the defect again. Widening the shared `verify-timeout-minutes` default 18 -> 30 silently consumed EVERY caller's margin at once, and it had already bitten: gld-compat-matrix sat at `timeout-minutes: 30` against a 30-minute wait — zero margin, killed at exactly the deadline — without anyone editing that file. So closure also requires the GENERIC pin (tests/test_commit_to_main_callers.py) that reads the wait FROM the action and checks it against every caller, so the next widening fails CI instead of eating the margins silently. ⚠️ VERIFY, DO NOT ARGUE: the criterion is a planted unmergeable branch making a caller exit NON-ZERO, not a reading of the YAML — this row exists because twelve workflows LOOKED fine. Row closes when every caller verifies AND one has been shown to fail on a real strand. Separately and NOT by the same change: the 5 stranded `automation/*` branches need dispositioning by hand, ⚠️ not merged blind — `automation/econ-calendar-33232352515-1` touches comms/macro/econ_calendar_snapshots.jsonl, the file behind the #10398 conflict the operator reserved as a domain call.

items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-08-31, on the row's own terms — a planted strand, not a reading of the YAML. (1) EVERY caller verifies: all 13 commit-to-main callers pass verify-merged: "true" (10 added in #10549; gld-compat-matrix, research-queue-dispatch and e35-bracket-sweep already had it), each with a job budget that outlasts the wait. (2) ONE SHOWN TO FAIL ON A REAL STRAND: run 33369708585 (macro-valuation-snapshot, workflow_dispatch on main @ 893a3f23). Its landing PR #10552 was CLOSED without merging while the step waited; the step polled 8 times at 30s and then exited NON-ZERO: 'commit-to-main: .../pull/10552 was CLOSED without merging — the rows on automation/valuation-snapshots-33369708585-1 will never reach main' / 'Process completed with exit code 1'. Job conclusion: failure. Before the change this identical strand exited 0. The PR was reopened and merged immediately after, so no snapshot rows were lost. ⚠️ THE ROW'S OWN PRESCRIPTION WAS UNSAFE AND WAS NOT FOLLOWED LITERALLY. It framed the fix as 'each is a one-line opt-in PLUS a timeout-minutes check'; doing exactly that leaves the hazard, because widening the SHARED verify-timeout-minutes default 18 -> 30 consumed every caller's margin at once — gld-compat-matrix was already sitting at budget 30 vs wait 30, zero margin, in a file nobody had edited. The durable fix is therefore the GENERIC pin tests/test_commit_to_main_callers.py, which reads the wait FROM the action and checks it against every caller. Its positive control named that regression on its own. ⚠️ STILL OPEN AND NOT CLOSED BY THIS: the 5 stranded automation/* branches need dispositioning BY HAND, never merged blind — automation/econ-calendar-33232352515-1 touches comms/macro/econ_calendar_snapshots.jsonl, the file behind the #10398 conflict the operator reserved as a domain call.

items.summary: Bybit HEDGE mode was armed 2026-08-30 (Tier-3, operator-approved) and its OPEN-ITEMS row clears only on 'a pairs `open` event in which both legs are placed and the venue reports position_idx 1 or 2 for each'. MEASURED 2026-08-30T19:30Z against the live /api/diag/log_file?name=pairs_soak (400 rows, 2026-08-27T05:05:26Z->2026-08-30T19:02:33Z): the string 'position_idx' occurs ZERO times in the whole page, as do 'positionIdx', 'position_mode' and 'hedge'. The leg schema on every `open`/`shadow_open` row is exactly {direction, entry_ref, qty, sl, symbol, tp} -- no position/book field of any kind. So the clearing condition names an observable that the surface it names DOES NOT EMIT, and the row cannot be cleared or refuted from it however long the sleeve runs. This is the BL-20260825-ALERT-AND-CADENCE-STATE-FILES-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE class one level in: not a missing FILE, a missing FIELD in the file the criterion points at.
items.resolution_criteria: The pairs executor stamps the RESOLVED position_idx per leg onto the `open` (and `open_failed`/`half_open`) soak row -- the value bybit_position_mode actually passed to the venue, not a re-derivation -- and a row is read back through /api/diag/log_file?name=pairs_soak carrying it. Four states, never collapsed, matching the resolver's own vocabulary: 1 / 2 / null-for-one_way (an absent kwarg is CORRECT there) / null-for-unresolved (we could not read the side, so Bybit REFUSED the order) -- and the last two must be distinguishable, because on a hedge symbol they are opposite outcomes. Closes when OI-20260830-BYBIT-HEDGE-MODE-ARMED-BUT-UNEXERCISED can be graded from the soak rather than by inference.
items.notes: WHY IT IS NOT ACADEMIC: a pair HAS now opened since arming. 2026-08-30T09:05:04Z, SOLUSDT/ETHUSDT on bybit_1, execution_mode 'live', both legs placed with trade_ids (c27731c5.., 9de8c1ef..), and NO half_open followed -- it closed cleanly at 2026-08-30T13:00:53Z. That is the first post-arming open (the OPEN-ITEMS row's own position was 'as of 08:29Z no pair had yet OPENED in hedge mode'), and it is UNGRADEABLE. DO NOT READ IT AS SUCCESS: a clean open with no stranding is equally consistent with (a) hedge mode working and (b) the pair simply never facing a concurrent directional position on either symbol -- which is criterion (3) of the same row, ALSO not recorded in the soak. Before arming, the stranding was plainly visible in this same log: half_open on SOLUSDT/ETHUSDT at 2026-08-29T07:08:26Z, 13:04:24Z and 14:07:14Z, 10 half_open rows in the 400-row page overall. Found while discharging the loud-row reporting duty on a session whose actual task was the arbitration fan-out soak -- i.e. by trying to CHECK the row rather than carry it, which is what that duty is for. STATE THE POPULATION: 400-row tail of one log, ~3.6 days, one process's worth of arming; the zero-occurrence count is over that page, not over the file's lifetime. || ⚠️ SCOPE THE CLAIM TO THIS SURFACE, and read PR #10532 (session 01TXmgt2S1zZjcdCDEpXdxmV) beside it — measured INDEPENDENTLY the same evening and it does NOT contradict this row, it bounds it. At 2026-08-30T18:33:52Z /api/diag/bybit_open_orders showed bybit_1 holding SOLUSDT 15.0 Sell and ETHUSDT 95.01 Sell, BOTH position_idx=2 — so the env->resolver->kwarg->venue half of hedge mode IS observable and IS proven, just not from pairs_soak. What is unobservable is specifically whether a PAIRS LEG carried a positionIdx, because (a) pairs_soak emits no such field and (b) bybit_open_orders is partial-by-construction (it reports only symbols HOLDING a position) and carries no pair or trade id, so it cannot attribute a leg to a pairs open. Do not read this row as 'hedge mode is unproven' — it is 'the PAIRS SLEEVE half is ungradeable from the surface its own criterion names'. ⚠️ ONE CORRECTION TO #10532's READING, offered rather than asserted over it: it says a 40-row tail at 18:34Z showed no `open` at all. True of a 40-row window; a 400-row read the same evening finds the 09:05:04Z SOLUSDT/ETHUSDT open, which simply predates that window. 'No open in the tail I read' and 'the sleeve has not opened' are different statements and only the first is supported — which is the same denominator error this row is about, one level up. || FIX SHIPPED 2026-08-30, same session (PR #10526). `open`/`open_failed` rows now carry `leg_placement`: per leg, `position_idx` + `position_idx_state` (the resolver's own four states, threaded out of execute._submit_order where apply_position_idx's return was being DISCARDED one line after it was computed), `directional_open` (present/absent/unreadable), `placed` and `trade_id`. ⚠️ THE ORDER PATH WAS NEVER BROKEN and this row should not be read as saying it was: _place_pair -> execute_pkg -> _submit_order -> apply_position_idx was already correct, so pairs legs on an armed symbol DID carry a positionIdx all along; the only defect was that nothing recorded it. The execute.py change is additive-only (an optional write-only `observed` out-dict, default None) with zero wire-payload and zero control-flow change — pinned by an AST test that the wire path never BRANCHES on it, because an observability out-param that could alter a live order is the one way this could have been dangerous. ⚠️ THE SECOND HALF MATTERED MORE THAN THE FIRST and was not in this row's original resolution_criteria: criterion (3) of OI-20260830-BYBIT-HEDGE-MODE-ARMED-BUT-UNEXERCISED needs a CONCURRENT DIRECTIONAL position to have existed, and that was equally unrecorded — so a stamped position_idx alone would still not have cleared the row. Hence `directional_open`. STATUS STAYS OPEN: this row closes on READING a post-fix row back through /api/diag/log_file?name=pairs_soak, which needs the merge to reach the trader via ict-git-sync AND a pair to open. 15 tests in tests/test_pairs_leg_placement.py, including the end-to-end wiring test that fails if anyone drops `observed=observed` from the execute_pkg call — a regression that is otherwise SILENT, since the soak keeps writing rows that have simply lost the field.

updates.note:
RESOLVED — the resolved position_idx is stamped per leg and reads back off the route the criterion names.

POPULATION: /api/diag/log_file?name=pairs_soak&lines=1000 read 2026-09-01T23:0xZ returned 1000 rows (size_bytes 1245871 — so this IS a truncated tail, stated rather than glossed), window 2026-08-24T07:03:20.493325Z -> 2026-09-01T23:05:36.691605Z. Events in that window: skip_flat 649, hold 147, skip_concurrency 66, shadow_open 48, **open 46**, half_open 24, close 20.

STAMPED, AND READ BACK: 6 of the 46 `open` rows carry `leg_placement` (the other 40 predate the writer — that absence is the version marker). The most recent, 2026-09-01T05:01:07.916963Z, pair SOLUSDT/ETHUSDT, account bybit_1, execution_mode live:
  leg SOLUSDT long  — placed true, position_idx 1, position_idx_state hedge_long,  directional_open present
  leg ETHUSDT short — placed true, position_idx 2, position_idx_state hedge_short, directional_open absent
This is the value the resolver passed to the venue carried on the row, not a re-derivation.

THE FOUR STATES ARE NOT COLLAPSED, which is the clause that matters: `position_idx_state` ships BESIDE `position_idx`, so null-for-one_way and null-for-unresolved are distinguishable by the state string rather than by a bare null — which is precisely what a null idx alone cannot express, and on a hedge symbol those two are opposite outcomes.

'CLOSES WHEN OI-20260830-BYBIT-HEDGE-MODE-ARMED-BUT-UNEXERCISED CAN BE GRADED FROM THE SOAK RATHER THAN BY INFERENCE' — IT CAN, and all three of that row's criteria are readable off this one soak row: (1) both legs report position_idx 1/2, never 0; (2) both legs placed:true and the last half_open ANYWHERE is 2026-09-01T00:02:52.353773Z, i.e. BEFORE this open, with zero half_open rows for SOLUSDT/ETHUSDT after it; (3) directional_open: present on the SOL leg, so the netting collision that causes stranding WAS actually present — the criterion that row calls 'the whole criterion'.

⚠️ TWO THINGS I DID NOT DO. I observed only two of the four position_idx_state values (hedge_long, hedge_short); one_way and unresolved exist in the producer's vocabulary but were not sampled in this window, so their EMISSION is inferred from code, not observed. And I did NOT clear OI-20260830-BYBIT-HEDGE-MODE-ARMED-BUT-UNEXERCISED — that register row is outside this session's declared scope and four sibling sessions were live; it is flagged to the manager in the PR body instead. This row is about the soak RECORDING the fact, and it does.

items.summary: Every scheduled workflow in this repo now fires 6-12 HOURS after its declared cron, against ~1h before 2026-08-27. MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY 2026-08-30, not taken from prose. POPULATION: purge-artifacts.yml, declared `0 3 * * *`, the 30 consecutive scheduled runs from 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-30 (lag = run_started_at minus the most recent 03:00Z). 08-01..08-26: 0.66-3.42h, median ~1.3h, no outliers. 08-27 onward: 10.88, 12.01, 6.80, 5.98h. The break is sharp and dated. A second control (diag-relay-sweep, `0 6 * * *`) shows the same break on the same date per PR #10487's commit message, and research-queue-dispatch tracks both. ⚠️ THE CAUSE IS NOT ESTABLISHED. Best-effort scheduling under load is the leading explanation and is NOT proven; GitHub documents scheduled workflows as best-effort and does not guarantee a start time. This row records the MEASUREMENT and the operational consequence, and deliberately does not assert a cause. ⚠️ NOTHING IS BEING DROPPED as far as measured — the runs arrive, late. Do not read this as missed executions without checking, because 'late' and 'never' are different facts and only the first is supported here. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-10: the 'NOTHING IS BEING DROPPED' sentence holds only for crons declared WIDER than the lag. An hourly cron measured the same day delivered 27% of its declared slots — below the lag, slots coalesce and simply never run. See the re-measurement in `detail`.
items.detail:
WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS, and it is not the obvious one. The load-bearing consequence is that ANY plan whose correctness depends on a cron firing at roughly its declared time is now wrong, and the plan looks fine right up until it silently does not happen on time.

FOUND BY BEING BITTEN: this session armed the research-queue cron and, to verify the `schedule` branch (unprovable by workflow_dispatch, since `inputs` is populated there and empty on a schedule event), added two throwaway probe crons at 20:50Z/21:20Z on the explicit premise of 'expect ~15 min scheduling lag' — the historical figure, false for four days. Under the current regime those fire around 03:00-09:00Z. The evidence was already in this repo, in PR #10487's own commit message on the very workflow being armed, and was not checked before the approach was chosen.

⚠️ SILVER LINING, STATED SO IT IS NOT MISREAD AS THE PROBE FAILING: probe crons at 20:50/21:20 plus 6-12h still land EARLIER than the daily 06:20 cron plus the same lag, so they remain the faster path to exercising the branch. They were left in place for that reason, not removed.

WIDER EXPOSURE, UNAUDITED AND THE REASON THIS IS NOT `low`: the repo runs many cron'd jobs, including OPERATIONAL ones (diag-relay-sweep, purge-artifacts, and the monitoring/alerting family). A detector that is supposed to look every day and instead looks 6-12h late has a correspondingly wider blind window, and any of them whose value depends on WHEN it ran — a freshness check, a staleness threshold, a daily rollup with a window boundary — may now be grading a different period than its author intended. NOT AUDITED here; that is the work this row asks for, and it should be done by reading each cron'd workflow's purpose rather than by assuming the lag is harmless because the run eventually happened.

⚠️ RE-MEASURED 2026-09-10T16:25Z BY THIS ROW'S OWN METHOD AND ITS OWN CONTROL, WHICH ANSWERS CLAUSE (1): THE LAG DID NOT REVERT, SO CLAUSE (2) IS NOW MANDATORY. POPULATION: purge-artifacts.yml (`0 3 * * *`), the 40 consecutive `event=schedule` runs from 2026-08-02 to 2026-09-10, lag computed per run as run_started_at minus the most recent 03:00Z rather than read from prose. Pre-break 08-02..08-26: 0.66-3.42h, matching what this row records. The 08-27 break reproduces exactly, to the same four figures already here: 10.88, 12.01, 6.80, 5.98h. What is NEW is the eleven days since — 6.43, 5.38, 4.70, 4.85, 4.78, 4.47, 4.70, 5.01, 4.88, 4.93, 4.93h. It has not reverted and it is no longer drifting: it has SETTLED on a ~4.9h plateau. This row's title says 6-12h, which is now wrong in the direction of being scarier than the measurement; ~4.9h is the figure to design against.

⚠️ AND ONE SENTENCE OF THIS ROW IS NOW FALSE FOR PART OF THE POPULATION, WHICH MATTERS BECAUSE IT IS THE SENTENCE THAT TELLS A READER NOT TO WORRY. The summary reads 'NOTHING IS BEING DROPPED as far as measured — the runs arrive, late.' That holds for a DAILY cron and is confirmed here: 40 distinct daily boundaries across 40 spanned days, none missing. It does NOT hold for a cron declared TIGHTER THAN THE LAG. POPULATION: error-feed-digest.yml, declared HOURLY at :35, its last 40 `event=schedule` runs spanning 2026-09-04T11:42Z to 2026-09-10T14:37Z = 146.9h. Forty runs against ~147 declared slots is 27%, median gap 4.04h (min 2.07, max 5.95), and the fire minute is scattered over 31 distinct values, essentially never :35. A constant lag preserves the one-hour SPACING, so four-hour spacing is not lateness, it is COALESCING: a slot whose predecessor is still outstanding produces no run at all. 'Late' and 'never' are different facts, exactly as this row insists — and below the lag, the second is the measured case.

⚠️ THE FIRST TIME THIS BIT A MECHANISM RATHER THAN A PROBE, AND THE MECHANISM SHIPPED TODAY. .github/workflows/stale-automation-sweep.yml (#11519, on main since 2026-09-10T15:09:10Z) declares `17 */2 * * *`, and its own header comment justifies that 2h against the 6h window of check_digest_liveness — the tightest of the four repo-wide receipt guards — on the stated premise that a stranded branch then gets '~3 sweeps' before that clock expires. At a ~4.9h effective cadence it gets about ONE, and since 2h is below the lag the declaration buys nothing a 4h one would not. The premise is now known-wrong IN THE MACHINERY'S OWN COMMENT, which is precisely clause (2)'s target: a threshold tuned against a ~1h lag. NOT FIXED HERE, and stated rather than quietly left: that file is registered LANDING_MACHINERY, so under R12 it cannot self-land and the correction needs a human-read PR. Carried on WO-20260909-EVERY-PR-IN-THE-REPO-IS-RED so it is not left in a commit message.

SEVERITY RAISED medium -> high ON THIS EVIDENCE, and the reason is the row's own: it declined `low` because the exposure was wide but UNAUDITED. It is no longer only potential — one shipped mechanism's stated margin is void, found by reading a single workflow comment against the measurement. Clause (2) is the work; nothing here discharges it.
items.resolution_criteria: Two separable halves, and the second matters more than the first. (1) ESTABLISH whether the lag persists or reverts: re-measure the same purge-artifacts population in ~1 week and state the period. If it reverted, close with the dates; if it persists, it is the new normal and (2) is mandatory. (2) AUDIT the cron'd workflows for time-sensitivity — specifically any that compute a window from `now` rather than from a declared boundary, any freshness/staleness threshold tuned against a ~1h lag, and any whose alert cadence assumes daily coverage. Fix by making the WINDOW explicit rather than by chasing the schedule, since the schedule is not ours to control. ⚠️ DO NOT close this on 'the runs are still arriving' — arrival was never the finding.

items.summary: The research-queue cron was armed 2026-08-30 and DEADLOCKED on its first real fire. `test_dispatcher_is_a_dry_run_unless_fire_is_passed` asserted `"would_dispatch" in outcomes` against QUEUE_DIR = the LIVE `research/queue`, which silently requires the live queue to ALWAYS hold a due job. A fully caught-up queue is the CORRECT steady state and it FAILS that assertion. So: the dispatcher fires and stamps `last_dispatched_at` -> every job grades `not_due` -> the stamp PR's own CI fails on this test -> the stamp never merges -> the job stays due -> it re-fires on the next cron. Indefinitely. THE DISPATCHER WORKING CORRECTLY IS WHAT BREAKS IT. OBSERVED, not theorised: schedule runs 33340458710 (22:56:08Z) and 33342140520 (23:33:46Z), both `event=schedule`, both `conclusion=failure`, the second being the re-fire. Stamp PR #10534 open and unmerged with `pytest-run` red. ⚠️ IT WAS ONLY VISIBLE BECAUSE `commit-to-main` GAINED `verify-merged` HOURS EARLIER (PR #10524). Without it the dispatcher would have exited 0 on an unmerged stamp and this would have re-fired daily, green, forever — which is exactly the failure that row was written about.
items.detail:

The half worth keeping from the old test — that the LIVE queue parses and holds no structurally invalid job — is now a separate test that says NOTHING about how many jobs are due.

VERIFIED against the real failing state rather than by argument: stamping every job (the caught-up `not_due=3` state that deadlocked) now passes 52/52. The 'before' control is not a plant — it is PR #10534's own CI.

THE CLASS: a test whose passing depends on PRODUCTION STATE being in a particular condition. It was not testing the code; it was testing that someone had left work undone. Worth a sweep for siblings — any test reading a live directory/DB and asserting non-emptiness has this shape, and it is invisible until the system catches up.

items.summary: `_stamp` wrote `last_dispatched_at` with `yaml.safe_dump`, a full load/dump round-trip. PyYAML does not model comments, so every `#` line is DELETED and every `>-` block scalar reflowed. MEASURED on the first real stamp (PR #10534, run 33340458710): RQ-20260827-001.yaml went from 2 comments to 0, with `question`, `why_not_inferential`, `basis` and `note` all reflowed — 27 insertions / 39 deletions for what should be ONE added line. ⚠️ THIS ONE SUCCEEDS SILENTLY, which makes it worse than the deadlock filed beside it. The loss rides inside an auto-merged `chore(research-queue): dispatch stamps (auto)` PR that nobody reads, and the blocks destroyed are the job's REASONING — why it is not inferential, why it routes to a runner, what its landing assertion actually proves. A queue whose prose is stripped one fire at a time decays into a set of opaque job names, and nothing would ever report it.
items.detail:
FIXED as a targeted line-level edit: replace an existing top-level `last_dispatched_at:` line in place, else append one; everything else stays byte-for-byte. The file is still PARSED first (a malformed job is an error, not something we append to blindly) and the value is READ BACK and checked, because a text edit can produce a file that still parses and says something else.

Five pins, positive-controlled: restoring the yaml.safe_dump writer fails three of them.

NOT DONE, and it is the generalisation: no guard stops the NEXT tool from round-tripping a human-authored YAML/JSON through a dumper that cannot represent comments. config/ is full of load-bearing comments and several ops scripts write config files. A `yaml.safe_dump` over a committed, hand-authored file is the pattern; whether a guard should refuse it is the open question this row hands on.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED for the dispatcher. The OPEN half: audit for other writers that round-trip a hand-authored committed file through yaml.safe_dump / json.dump and would strip comments or reformat prose — `scripts/ops/` and anything writing `config/` first. Close that half by either converting them to targeted edits or establishing that none exist, ⚠️ with the denominator stated, not by a search that returned nothing.

items.summary: `git fetch` aborts ATOMICALLY on an unknown refspec, so `git fetch origin main "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null || true` updates NEITHER ref when the branch is gone — and `commit-to-main` merges with `--delete-branch`, so on the SUCCESS path the landing branch IS gone by the time the assertion runs. The assertion then read a checkout-time `origin/main` that PREDATES the merge and reported `absent`. MEASURED on gld-compat-matrix run 33340468235: 'Land the corpus on main' SUCCEEDED in 95s (so `verify-merged` observed MERGED, and PR #10535 is in main's history), then 'Assert the rows actually landed' failed INSTANTLY. Mechanism verified directly, not inferred — against a real deleted branch, `git fetch origin main <gone>` prints `fatal: couldn't find remote ref` and leaves origin/main un-updated; against a branch that still exists the same command succeeds and updates it. ⚠️ AN ASSERTION BUILT TO STOP FALSE 'landed' CLAIMS WAS MANUFACTURING FALSE 'absent' ONES, which is the worse direction: it fails correct runs, and a check that is red when the system works is the desensitized-alarm P1. The `|| true` is what hid the fatal.
items.detail:
FIXED as two fetches: the default branch on its own and WITHOUT `|| true` (a swallowed failure there is precisely 'we did not look' rendered as 'the rows are absent'), then the landing branch separately and tolerantly, with `--pushed-ref` passed ONLY when that branch actually resolves — a --pushed-ref naming a deleted ref would make `pending_merge` unreadable again, which is the defect BL-20260830 already covers one layer up. The gone-branch path SAYS SO in the log rather than leaving a reader to infer it from an absent flag.

⚠️ FIXED IN THE SIBLING TOO, WHERE IT IS LATENT RATHER THAN ACTIVE. e35-bracket-sweep.yml carries the identical combined fetch; it pushes its TARGET branch WITHOUT a PR, so nothing deletes it and the fetch succeeds today. It becomes active the moment a merged TARGET is deleted. Fixing only the tree just proven is the recurrence pattern this repo keeps paying for (the pytest-run short-circuit class reached FIVE instances that way).

FOUND BY the armed research-queue cron firing for real. The dispatcher's own failure was a different defect; this one only surfaced because the dispatched gld-compat runs ALSO read as failed while their landing PRs (#10535, #10537) were plainly merged on main — a contradiction that had to be resolved rather than filed as 'both failed'.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED in both workflows, with five pins and a positive control (exactly those five fail against the pre-fix files, the other sixteen unmoved). ⚠️ NOT closed as a CLASS: no guard forbids a combined `git fetch` of a required ref and an optional one, and there are other multi-ref fetches in .github/workflows/. items.title: RQ-20260830-002 declares expected_n=50 against a power floor of 49.06, so 8 of its 9 healthy legs grade underpowered by 0.06-3.06 trades — the monthly re-validation is near-vacuous by construction, not by evidence
items.detail:
MEASURABLE ONLY AS OF 2026-08-31. The e35 corpus carried no achieved OOS count until the extractor was fixed to read base_oos_trades off the gate record (#10543), so this collision existed but could not be seen from any committed artifact.

THE ARITHMETIC. RQ-20260830-002 declares power: alpha=0.05, power=0.8, min_detectable_effect=0.4 sd, design=one_sample. The floor is (z_a/2 + z_b)^2 / d^2 = (1.959964 + 0.841621)^2 / 0.4^2 = 49.06 trades. The sweep's DEFAULT_SPLIT_TARGET_OOS is 50, and the queue unit's own power.basis says n IS that default. So the design targets a sample 0.94 trades above its own floor.

POPULATION: run 33361845836, all 14 shipped legs, the 98 GATED rows (base_oos_trades non-null <=> gate_verdict non-null, 98/98 and 0/2688 -- verified, not assumed). Achieved base_oos_trades per leg:
  9 well-populated legs (>=40): sol_4h 50 | ada_pullback_2h 49, trend_donchian 49, avax_4h 49, xrp_4h 49, uso_trend_1h 49 | ada_4h 48, eth_4h 48 | tlt_pullback_1h 46
  5 thin 1d legs: scha 4, iwm 5, qqq 6, mgc 7, spy 8
ONLY trend_donchian_sol_4h (50) CLEARS 49.06. The other 8 miss by 0.06 to 3.06 trades -- i.e. the powered/underpowered call is decided by where resolve_split's boundary happened to land, not by anything about the leg. A monthly job that grades 8 of its 9 healthy legs 'underpowered' every month is the desensitized-alarm shape: a check that goes red when the system is working.

NOT A DUPLICATE of BL-20260827-EXIT-COVERAGE-MATRIX-IS-SUBSTANTIALLY-A-POWER-TEST-FLEET-WIDE (open), which is the same CLASS in a different place: that row is about the M20 coverage matrix grading 468 cells at a median OOS of 33 with no stated denominator. This one is narrower and sharper -- the denominator IS stated, is achieved as designed, and the DESIGN's own target sits below its own floor. Filed as a recurrence of that class per the backlog tool's guidance, because the 08-27 row was itself filed as a recurrence that had not been carried across.

THE OBVIOUS REMEDY IS THE ONE THIS REPO HAS ALREADY MEASURED AS A CLIFF. Raising split_target_oos is exactly BL-20260814-SPLIT-DERIVATION-FALLBACK-IS-A-CLIFF-SO-ASKING-FOR-MORE-OOS-RETURNS-FAR-FEWER (resolved): going 25 -> 35 CUT achieved OOS from 24 to 4 on three of four legs. The clamp landed by that row's fix makes the cliff far less sharp, but it does not create trades -- the five 1d legs trade ~20x/year and cannot reach 50 at any target, so raising it moves them nowhere and only widens the IS window for the nine that can.

SO THIS IS A DESIGN DECISION, NOT A ONE-LINE FIX, which is why it is filed rather than changed in the session that found it. The options are not equivalent: raise the target with margin (costs runtime, helps only the 9); accept a larger min_detectable_effect so the floor drops below 50 (d=0.45 gives 38.8, d=0.5 gives 31.4 -- honest, and it changes what the job can claim); or keep the floor and read the job as the WATCHLIST its own power.basis already says it is, in which case 'underpowered' is the expected steady state and must be documented as such so nobody reads the red as decay.

DO NOT read the 8 misses as evidence the shipped cells have decayed. This row says the job cannot currently distinguish decay from noise on those legs -- which is the whole point.
items.resolution_criteria: ONE of the three options above is CHOSEN and recorded in RQ-20260830-002's power block with its cost stated, AND the unit's power.basis states the resulting relationship between expected_n and the floor explicitly (target above floor with margin M, or floor lowered to F, or 'underpowered is the expected steady state for legs achieving <49.06 and is not a decay signal'). PLUS: a re-read of a real run's rows confirming the chosen option produces the intended grading -- verified by reading base_oos_trades off landed corpus rows, never by the queue file's prose. Adding a caveat WITHOUT deciding does not close this: the unit already carries a thin-leg caveat and it did not stop the collision.

items.summary: The strategy-confidence score is carried to the arbitration decision point and is read by NEITHER election sort key. Same-side: (target_qty, effective_priority, -timestamp, tuple(-ord(c) for c in name)) via max(). Conflict branch: (-effective_priority, timestamp, name). `confidence` appears in neither, and is used only by the FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD override -- which is DISARMED at 0.0 and hard-returns before reading any confidence. So the ranking signal the system spent months building is present at the decision and never consulted.
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-31, and the tiebreak is worse than arbitrary -- it is DETERMINISTIC AND PERMANENT. `target_qty` is the inert 0.0 sentinel (BL-20260810-INTENT-TARGET-QTY-ALWAYS-ZERO-TWO-CONSEQUENCES) and all six SOLUSDT contenders are DEFAULT_PRIORITIES 0 (verified: trend_donchian_sol, trend_donchian_sol_prop, trend_donchian_eth, trend_donchian_eth_prop, ict_scalp_sol_5m all -> 0), so the key falls to timestamp and then NAME. On a debounced closed-bar tick both donchian twins emit for the same bar, so NAME decides. Verified directly: tuple(-ord(c)) comparison under max() picks `trend_donchian_sol_prop` over `trend_donchian_sol`, because the shorter name is a strict PREFIX of the longer and a prefix tuple compares SMALLER. CONSEQUENCE: a strategy whose name is a prefix of a competitor's can NEVER win the same-side election. That is the mechanism behind the measured 0-of-60 in BL-20260827-PROP-ONLY-TWIN-WINS-THE-GLOBAL-SYMBOL-SLOT-AND-STARVES-ITS-PAPER-SIBLING -- not small-sample bad luck, which is how it had been read. Note the CONFLICT branch sorts ascending and would pick the opposite name, so the two branches disagree about the same pair; only the same-side branch is exercised by the twins (both long). OPERATOR DIRECTION 2026-08-31: prioritisation should use the confidence score, plus active management (re-scoring an open trade to decide whether it should stay live against a better new trade). SCOPE NOTE: this is the decision RULE. The structural half -- WHO decides -- is per-account arbitration, shipped separately in PR #10544 at the annotate default; ranking by confidence GLOBALLY would still starve accounts, so the structural fix lands first and this is built on top of it.
items.resolution_criteria: NOT resolved by adding `confidence` to the sort key and calling it done. Requires: (1) a walk-forward or A/B on scripts/backtest_system.py showing confidence-ranked selection beats the current priority->timestamp->name key on a floor-clearing population, per-symbol and net of cost -- the M18 allocator precedent is the warning here, since its EV ranker measured OOS AUC ~0.51 and did NOT beat dumb priority (docs/research/M18-allocator-backtest-findings-2026-06-29.md); (2) the prefix defect fixed regardless of whether confidence ranking ships, since a name-prefix strategy can never win today and that is a bug on its own; (3) Tier-3 operator approval on the final key. A change that only reorders the tiebreak without evidence is not a fix.
items.found_by: session ec146208 -- found while building the per-account arbitration fan-out (PR #10544), after the operator challenged the alphabetical tiebreak directly. Verified by reading both sort keys and computing the tuple comparison, not inferred.

items.area: strategy confidence (StrategyIntent.confidence, populated from each builder's meta['confidence']) as consumed by src/runtime/intents.py::_election_sort_key
items.summary: The strategy confidence score saturates: `1.0` is 20.5% of per-intent observations, and on 50.1% of live arbitrations EVERY contender's confidence is IDENTICAL, so the score cannot decide the contest it is now the primary key for. Ranking by confidence is correct and shipped; on half the population it is inert.
items.detail: MEASURED on the live `conviction_arbitration` soak — n=371 arbitration records, 2026-06-17T18:16Z -> 2026-08-30T23:34Z, read via /api/diag/log_file?name=conviction_arbitration&lines=1000 (371 of 371 lines parsed, so the page was not truncated). Population: every tick on which >= 2 non-flat intents contended for one symbol; 363 same_direction, 8 priority_conflict. === THE THREE NUMBERS. (1) Conviction-based arbitration would pick a DIFFERENT winner than the pre-2026-08-31 key on 191/371 = 51.5% of contests. (2) Confidence DIFFERENTIATES the contenders on 185/371 = 49.9%. (3) On the remaining 186 = 50.1% every contender's confidence is EXACTLY EQUAL. Across 442 distinct values the single value `1.0` accounts for 154 of 751 per-intent observations = 20.5%. So the signal is genuinely continuous — 442 distinct values is not a boolean — but it is blunt at the top, and the saturation is a large part of why half the contests tie. === WHY THIS IS NOW LOAD-BEARING RATHER THAN COSMETIC. Until 2026-08-31 the election ranked by priority -> timestamp -> NAME and confidence was carried to the decision and never read (BL-20260831-CONFIDENCE-IS-CARRIED-TO-THE-ELECTION-AND-READ-BY-NEITHER-SORT-KEY). Confidence is now the primary discriminator (operator-directed: ranking must be evidence-based), so its resolution directly determines which strategy trades. A score that pins at 1.0 hands the decision to the tier below it on half of all contests. === WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is NOT an argument to revert to name-based ranking, and NOT a claim the confidence score is wrong — only that its DISCRIMINATION is insufficient at the top of its range. The tier below it is now recent 3-day per-strategy PnL (src/runtime/election_track_record.py), so a tie no longer falls to the alphabet; that mitigates the consequence without fixing the cause. === NOT YET ESTABLISHED, and a fix must start here: WHICH builders emit 1.0 and whether it is a clamp, a default, or a genuine saturated reading. The soak carries per_intent[].strategy beside the confidence, so the attribution is computable from the same 371 rows without any new instrumentation — that is the first step, not a redesign.
items.resolution_criteria: (1) ATTRIBUTE IT FIRST: from the existing conviction_arbitration rows, the per-strategy distribution of confidence, naming which builders emit 1.0 and how often. A fix proposed before this is a guess. (2) Establish per builder whether 1.0 is a hard clamp, an unset default, or a real reading — these need different fixes and conflating them is how the wrong one ships. (3) A re-scoring that measurably reduces the exact-tie rate below the measured 50.1% baseline on a comparable population. (4) Tier-3 approval, because the score is now the primary live routing key. ⚠️ RE-MEASURE the 50.1% before and after on the SAME population definition (>= 2 non-flat contenders, one symbol, one tick) — a different denominator would make any improvement unfalsifiable.

items.summary: `research/queue/README.md` documents `blocked` as a supported status, but the dispatcher's validator requires `run.workflow` and `lands.store` REGARDLESS of status — and a blocked job is blocked precisely because those do not exist yet. So the documented status is unrepresentable, and any attempt to use it grades `invalid` on every dispatcher run.
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-31 while filing a genuine piece of blocked research (trade prioritisation, see the related row). The file declared `status: blocked` with a written `blocked_on` naming both missing pieces; `dispatch_queue.py --only ...` still returned: '`run.workflow` is required ... `lands.store` is required'. === WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC. The only two dispositions available are both wrong: leave it queued with a FABRICATED workflow name (the dispatcher fires it, it fails, and the queue has been told a workflow exists when it does not), or leave it invalid — which prints `invalid=1` on EVERY dispatcher run for correct content. This repo treats an alarm that fires on correct behaviour as its own P1 (the desensitized-alarm class), so the second is not a neutral option. The practical effect is that blocked research CANNOT live in the queue and gets pushed out to docs/ + a backlog row, which is exactly the fragmentation the queue was built to end. === NOT YET ESTABLISHED: whether the right fix is to exempt `status: blocked` from the two required fields, or to require a `blocked_on` in their place so a blocked job still declares something actionable. The second is more in keeping with the queue's own design (every state names what moves it), but that is a judgement for whoever fixes it, not a decision this row makes.

items.title: Dispatching system-action issues in rapid succession silently DROPS all but the first and last — a cancelled run leaves its issue OPEN with no comment, which is indistinguishable from queued
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-30. Six switch-bybit-position-mode issues were opened within ~30s (10514-10519). Runs 7412 (first) and 7416/7417 (last two) succeeded; runs 7413, 7414, 7415 came back **cancelled** and their issues 10515/10516/10517 sat OPEN with no comment. All three had to be re-fired one at a time (10525, 10527, 10528), each then succeeding on the first attempt.

CAUSE, read from the workflow rather than inferred: `.github/workflows/system-actions.yml` declares `concurrency: {group: system-actions, cancel-in-progress: false}`. `cancel-in-progress: false` prevents cancelling the RUNNING job but GitHub still keeps at most ONE pending run per group — a third dispatch evicts the second. So a batch of N collapses to the first and the last, deterministically. The same signature is visible earlier the same day (run 7391 cancelled, 7392 succeeded) and was not noticed then.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A PLAIN FAILURE. The issue-driven relay reports outcomes by COMMENTING on the issue and closing it. A cancelled run never reaches that step, so the issue stays open and silent — byte-identical to 'still queued'. A session polling the issue cannot tell a dead dispatch from a slow one and will wait indefinitely; this cost ~5 minutes and a wrong 'still queued' report to the operator before the actions run list was consulted. That is the collapsed-state shape (`we did not run` vs `we have not run YET`) at the ops-relay layer.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND WAITING. The batch here was six VENUE POSITION-MODE SWITCHES. Had the operator not been watching the confirmations, three symbols would have been left one-way at the venue while the env was extended to arm all four — and the two halves disagreeing means Bybit REFUSES EVERY ORDER on the un-switched symbols. A silent drop in a sequence whose whole hazard is 'the two halves must agree' is a live-trading footgun, not a papercut.

RESOLUTION OPTIONS (not chosen here): (a) the dispatcher's contract becomes 'one system-action in flight at a time, confirm before the next' and that is stated in docs/claude/system-actions.md + the git-actions skill, which is the zero-code fix and what this session did by hand; (b) the workflow re-queues rather than drops, e.g. a matrix/queue job or a per-issue concurrency group (`system-actions-${{ github.event.issue.number }}`) so dispatches serialise per issue instead of evicting; (c) at minimum, a cancelled run should comment on its issue so the state is legible — the relay's whole contract is that the issue carries the outcome.
items.resolution_criteria: A batch of >=3 system-action issues opened within one minute either ALL run to completion, or every dropped one carries a comment on its own issue saying it was cancelled and must be re-fired. Checkable by opening 3 no-op actions (e.g. status-check) back-to-back and asserting 3 comments appear. Until then the documented contract must say 'dispatch one at a time and confirm before the next' in BOTH docs/claude/system-actions.md and .claude/skills/git-actions/SKILL.md, greppable for 'one at a time'.

items.title: _shrink_dict's new shed rung drops the LONGEST KEY NAME once the trim loop has emptied every unprotected string — it shed `pre_mark_exit_reason_source` on its first live use while keeping two meaningless empty strings
items.detail:
SELF-INFLICTED, same day, and found by using the thing. PR #10508 added a rung to `_shrink_dict`: when no trimmable string remains, shed the largest unprotected value one at a time before the minimal envelope. That is a real improvement (trade 4935 kept every key but the droppable one). But the ranking is `len(_dumps({k: v}))`, and the trim loop that runs FIRST halves every unprotected string down to `""` — so by the time the shed rung fires, all the candidate values are empty and the ranking degenerates to KEY-NAME LENGTH.

MEASURED on live trades 5238 and 5239 (bybit_1 BNBUSDT/BTCUSDT, marked 2026-08-30T19:48:56Z, notes 494 chars, `_truncated: true`). Surviving unprotected keys: `contract_value_usd: 1.0`, `operator_close_reason: ""`, `operator_marked_at: ""`. Dropped: `pre_mark_exit_reason_source`, whose 27-char NAME made it the largest serialized pair once its value was already `""`. Saving ~32 chars cost the one key that distinguishes a REPAIRED row from a first-time mark.

TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS.
(1) MINE, new: `pre_mark_exit_reason_source` is a provenance sentinel and is not in `_DEFAULT_PROTECTED`, in a change whose own comment says 'EVERY PROVENANCE MARKER BELONGS HERE'. It is small (27-char key, 27-char value) so it satisfies that comment's companion rule that a protected key must be SMALL — the envelope arithmetic needs checking before adding it, which is why this is filed rather than patched in passing.
(2) PRE-EXISTING: trimming a string to `""` and KEEPING it is a collapsed state. `operator_close_reason: ""` reads as 'the operator supplied no reason' when a 58-char reason was given and shredded; absent, empty-because-trimmed, and empty-as-supplied are three different facts sharing one representation. The `_ELLIPSIS` marker is dropped at `new_len == 0`, so even the 'this was cut' signal is lost. Arguably a value trimmed to nothing should be DROPPED rather than kept as a lie.

NOT URGENT: the marking on 5238/5239 is CORRECT — `closed_by_operator: true` and `pre_mark_exit_reason: 'reconciler_filled'` both survived (both protected), and the recovered prior is the right one, verified against `order_packages.close_reason`. What is missing is only the annotation saying WHICH evidence produced it, so a reader cannot tell these two repaired rows from first-time marks.

CANDIDATE FIXES, in order of confidence: (a) add `pre_mark_exit_reason_source` to `_DEFAULT_PROTECTED` after checking the envelope still fits 500 on a representative row; (b) make the shed rung prefer dropping keys whose value is ALREADY empty before touching keys that still carry information, so an emptied `operator_close_reason` goes before a populated sentinel; (c) drop rather than keep a string trimmed to zero length, so `""` never masquerades as a supplied empty value.
items.resolution_criteria: A row marked by mark_operator_flattened through the REPAIR branch (exit_reason already operator_flatten_reconciled, notes flag shed) comes back from the live journal carrying `pre_mark_exit_reason_source == 'order_packages.close_reason'`, on a notes blob that is `_truncated: true` — i.e. the sentinel survives the cap on a row at the budget, not merely on a short one. Re-checkable by re-marking a repaired row and reading /api/diag/journal. Separately, no key in a persisted notes blob is a zero-length string that was non-empty before the cap.

items.title: The strategy-builder exception latch shipped 2026-08-25 and its state file has never been written — the ERROR-feed drop that looks like its win is the MES candle outage ending
items.detail:
FOUND WHILE TRYING TO CREDIT THE LATCH WITH A WIN, which is why it is worth recording — the naive read of the ERROR feed says the fix worked spectacularly, and it is the wrong read.

THE LATCH HAS NEVER BEEN WRITTEN. `/api/diag/log_file?name=strategy_builder_exception_alert_state` returns `present: false` on 2026-08-30, five days after the latch shipped (2026-08-25). Its job is to downgrade a REPEATING strategy-builder exception from ERROR to WARN after the first page in a 6h window, keyed on (strategy, digit-normalised cause).

POSITIVE CONTROL, so the absence is a real absence and not a broken probe: two SIBLING latches read on the SAME surface in the SAME call come back populated — `target_naked_alert_state` (present: true, 793 bytes, 17 keys, newest entry 2026-08-28T16:00:48Z) and `stop_over_cover_alert_state` (present: true, 161 bytes, 4 keys, newest 2026-08-26T15:17:19Z). The diag read demonstrably finds populated latches; this one is genuinely empty.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT NEARLY MISLED ME. Population: `/api/bot/logs?level=error&limit=1000`, 363 rows, span 2026-08-21T04:17Z -> 2026-08-29T14:05Z, NOT at the cap so not truncated. `no candle data` per day: 08-21 25, 08-22 46, 08-23 29, 08-24 62, 08-25 53, then 08-26 ZERO, 08-27 0, 08-28 0, 08-29 0. Pre-fix 35.5/day, post 19.2/day — a headline that reads as a large win.

BUT THE SHAPE REFUTES THE ATTRIBUTION. A latch that downgrades REPEATS leaves a residual of first-per-window pages (up to 4/day per (strategy,cause) at a 6h window), never a hard zero. The series goes 53 -> 0 overnight. That is the signature of the underlying condition ENDING — the MES candle outage clearing — not of a suppressor engaging. And the latch file being absent settles it: nothing was suppressed, because nothing ran.

SO THE VERDICT IS `still_unexercised`, NOT `exercised` and NOT `regressed`. There is no evidence the latch is broken; there is no evidence it has ever run. Those are different states and the ERROR feed alone cannot separate them — which is precisely the collapse the latch's own CLAUDE.md entry warns about ("a WARN-only feed means the latch is holding, not that the fault cleared"). The entry gives the instruction and, until this row, nobody had followed it.

CONTRAST — THE SIBLING FIX IS GENUINELY EXERCISED, which is what a working one looks like. The durable target-naked cooldown (shipped 2026-08-23) moved `ib_target_naked` from 35.0/day (70 rows / 08-21..08-22) to 0.3/day (2 rows / 08-24..08-29), a 99.0% reduction — AND its latch file carries 17 live keys, so the condition is still occurring and still pinging at its declared cadence rather than having gone away. Suppression proven separately from resolution. That is the evidence standard this row says the builder latch has not met.
items.why_it_matters: A shipped-but-never-run suppressor is indistinguishable from a working one on every surface except its own state file, and the volume drop actively invites the wrong credit. If a future flood arrives believing this latch covers it, the operator gets the full flood — the 59.2%-of-feed condition this latch was built for.
items.tier: 1 to verify and to read the writer path; 2 only if the writer turns out to be broken
items.next_action: Wait for or induce the next repeating builder exception and re-read the state file. If it stays absent, read the writer path in the builder-exception classifier for a latch call that is never reached.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) `/api/diag/log_file?name=strategy_builder_exception_alert_state` returns `present: true` with at least one key, captured during or after a real burst of repeating strategy-builder exceptions; AND (b) that same burst shows the expected SHAPE in `/api/bot/logs?level=error` — a small non-zero residual of first-per-window pages rather than either the pre-fix flood or a hard zero, since a hard zero cannot distinguish a working latch from an absent fault; AND (c) if the next burst again leaves no state file, this is re-classified from still_unexercised to a real defect and the writer path is read. Do NOT close this by citing a fall in `no candle data` volume — that fall is already measured and already attributed to the outage ending.
