items.title: The bybit_2 broker-truth ledger stopped at 2026-07-13 — 59 real-money closes over 48 days have never been reconciled, and a consumer cannot tell that window from the measured one
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-30/31. Population, stated because it is the whole point: ALL 1,642 `bybit_2` rows pulled through /api/bot/db/table/trades in four pages (1,642 unique ids == the reported total, and `filter_state: applied` asserted on every page, so `total` is the bybit_2 count and not the whole table). Of those, 456 are closed non-backtest.

THE LEDGER STOPPED ON 2026-07-13 AND TRADING DID NOT. `/api/bot/pnl/broker-truth?account_id=bybit_2` returns `as_of: 2026-07-13`, `window_end: 2026-07-13`, `updated_at: 2026-07-13T19:40:00Z` — 48 days stale. Splitting the journal at that boundary:

    closed non-backtest <= 2026-07-13 : n=397   journal sum   -23.77   <- the reconciled window
    closed non-backtest >  2026-07-13 : n= 59   journal sum    +8.72   <- NEVER RECONCILED
    all closed non-backtest           : n=456   journal sum   -15.05

So 59 REAL-MONEY closes over 48 days have no wallet-truth counterpart. That is UNMEASURED, not clean, and it is exactly the reading CLAUDE.md already forbids for `accountsUnrecorded` ("an absent record means nobody has reconciled that account, never that it reconciles") — the same trap one level down, at the WINDOW rather than the ACCOUNT.

IN THE RECONCILED WINDOW THE UNDER-RECORDING IS 11.0x, NOT THE ~8x THE DOCS QUOTE. Wallet truth -262.52 against a journal sum of -23.77 over those 397 rows — a gap of $238.75. CLAUDE.md and BL-20260713-BYBIT2-PNL-UNDERRECORD say "~-33" and "~8x"; I am recording MY figure and the difference rather than restating theirs, because the populations may differ (mine is closed + non-backtest by `closed_at`) and silently adopting a number I did not reproduce is how a wrong one propagates.

THE CONSUMER CANNOT TELL THE TWO PERIODS APART. `broker_truth.journal_trust_map` grades the ACCOUNT, so every bybit_2 row reads `known_divergent` whether it falls inside the measured window or in the 48 unmeasured days after it. Directionally safe (it over-caveats rather than under-caveats) but it means 'measured and divergent by 11x' and 'never looked at' are the same string to every consumer — the collapsed-state shape, applied to the ledger's own coverage.

WHAT IS **NOT** WRONG HERE, checked so this row does not read as broader than it is. The account's historical mess is over and is not evidence of an ongoing fault: 119 orphaned rows span 2026-05-02 to 2026-07-05 with **zero since 2026-08-01** (112 of them in May); 347 exchange_rejected rows are 325 in May, 5 in all of August, 0 in the last 7 days; and both populations are dominated by `vwap`, which is now `enabled: false` / `execution: shadow` / not loaded. The 16 remaining `unreconciled` orphans ALL carry `reconcile_investigated_at`, so the `orphan_unreconciled` banner being silent is CORRECT behaviour under its own documented predicate, not a missed alert — verified by evaluating that predicate against the rows rather than by assuming.
items.why_it_matters: This is the one real-money account the system already knows it cannot trust per-row, and the authoritative figure that makes it trustworthy is hand-made and 48 days old. Every aggregate quoting bybit_2 since mid-July rests on journal rows that under-recorded by 11x the last time anyone checked. Treating `known_divergent` as a handled state — which is what I did before being corrected — is how a live-money reconciliation gap becomes permanent.
items.tier: 1 to measure and to make coverage legible; the export itself is an operator action (venue UI)
items.next_action: Ask the operator for a Bybit UM export covering 2026-07-13 -> present (the ledger is populated BY HAND from that export — this is one of the narrow genuine operator hand-offs), then re-run the reviewed --emit-ledger path and advance window_end.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) A fresh Bybit UM export covering 2026-07-13 -> present is stitched into `comms/broker_truth_ledger.json` via the reviewed `scripts/ops/reconcile_netting_pnl.py --emit-ledger` path, so `window_end` advances and the 59 (and counting) post-window closes acquire a wallet-truth counterpart; AND (b) the ledger's COVERAGE is legible to a consumer — a row outside the reconciled window must be distinguishable from one inside it, rather than both reading `known_divergent`, so 'never measured' and 'measured and divergent' stop being the same string; AND (c) a recorded cadence or trigger for refreshing the ledger, since a hand-populated authoritative figure with no refresh rule will go stale again by construction — this row IS that recurrence.

updates.note:
RE-MEASURED 2026-09-08 (MI-200, session 01CvFCybCkvrfzaHqNH3tQsb). THE ROW'S HEADLINE NUMBER IS NOW STALE AND THE CLASS HAS GROWN — recording my own figures and the difference rather than restating this row's, because the populations differ and silently adopting a number I did not reproduce is how a wrong one propagates.

POPULATION: all bybit_2 rows returned by /api/bot/trades/closed paged to exhaustion (the LIST population — not_paper + exclude_superseded), pnl NOT NULL, split on closedAt at the ledger boundary. n=427.
    closed, pnl NOT NULL, <= 2026-07-13 (reconciled window) : n=361  journal sum  -39.61
    closed, pnl NOT NULL, >  2026-07-13 (NEVER reconciled)  : n= 66  journal sum  -29.84
    all                                                     : n=427  journal sum  -69.46

SO THE UNRECONCILED WINDOW HAS GROWN FROM 59 CLOSES / 48 DAYS TO 66 CLOSES / 57 DAYS, and the ledger has not moved (as_of still 2026-07-13, comms/broker_truth_ledger.json). My split differs from this row's 2026-08-30 figures (397 / 59, -23.77 / +8.72) because my population is the /trades/closed LIST rather than closed non-backtest by closed_at; both are correct and neither is the other. What is like-for-like is the DIRECTION: the unreconciled window is still growing and is now negative in the journal too.

WHY THIS MATTERS RIGHT NOW, WHICH IS NEW: the operator raised a real-money LOSING STREAK on 2026-09-08, and every close in that streak falls inside the unreconciled window. So there is NO authoritative real-money PnL for the period under investigation — the only figures available are journal figures on the one account 446/447 of whose rows carry journalTrust 'known_divergent'. Any verdict computed on that window is computed on an instrument this repo has already declared divergent, which is exactly what CY-20260906-TRADING-TRUTH says to repair before acting. Full analysis: docs/research/real-money-close-attribution-2026-09-08.md.

items.title: /api/diag/journalctl caps at 1000 lines regardless of `since`, so a 'nothing suspicious since the last review' sweep cannot be made from it
items.detail: The /system-review security_check mandate is a breach-DETECTION sweep over the period since the last review. /api/diag/journalctl accepts `since`/`until` but the line cap is applied INDEPENDENTLY of the window, and it returns the TAIL of the window, so a widened `since` does not widen coverage -- it silently returns the last N lines and reports success. MEASURED 2026-08-31 while running the sweep: ict-web-api walked in five 12h chunks from 2026-08-29T00:00Z, lines=1000 (the max), and FOUR OF FIVE chunks came back at exactly 1000 lines, i.e. truncated; only the final partial-day chunk (921 lines) was swept whole. On ict-trader-live it is far worse -- lines=400 covered 38 SECONDS (06:40:05Z -> 06:40:43Z). So the honest coverage of a 'clean' auth sweep is 'the last 1000 lines of each chunk I happened to request', not the period, and nothing in the envelope says so. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS ONE SWEEP: this is the unasserted-denominator sub-class (CLAUDE.md 'Diagnostic provenance' C) on the surface a review uses to assert a NEGATIVE. An empty result reads as a clean negative and is actually an unstated truncation -- the exact shape of BL-20260807-TRAINER-DIAG-RELAY-SILENT-CMD-TRUNCATION on the trainer relay, now the SECOND instance, on the live-VM surface. THE PROBE ITSELF WAS FINE: positive-controlled against a synthetic 401 line, and the one fully-swept window shows a real status mix (200x768 / 404x18 / 422x2), so a 401/403 would have been seen where it was looked for. The defect is coverage, not detection. RESOLUTION CRITERIA: the envelope declares its own coverage -- return `truncated: true|false` plus the actual first/last timestamps served, so a consumer can never read a capped tail as a swept window; optionally support paging (`until` walk-back) so a period CAN be swept whole. Registering the state with collapsed-state-guard would fit the existing pattern.
items.resolution_criteria: GET /api/diag/journalctl returns a `truncated` boolean plus the actual first/last timestamps SERVED, and a walk of ict-web-api over a >=24h window with lines=1000 shows `truncated:false` on every chunk (or the envelope names the chunks it could not cover) -- verified against the live VM, not in a test.

updates.note:
RE-CHECKED AND STILL OPEN — reproduced live 2026-09-01T23:1xZ, backlog-drain session #1, and it COST ME A CLOSURE, which is worth recording as the concrete impact this row was missing.

THE READ: /api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live&lines=400&since=2026-09-01T22:00:00Z returned exactly 400 lines spanning **2026-09-01T22:00:00Z -> 22:01:44Z** — 1 minute 44 seconds of a 72-minute requested window, i.e. 2.4% of it, with nothing marking the truncation. The trader logs several lines per second, so `lines` binds long before `since` does and the `since` parameter is decorative on a busy unit.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE COSMETIC: I was trying to establish when the trader restarted between 22:01Z and 22:48Z, in order to decide whether BL-20260901-PROP-FILLS-STALENESS-FILTERS-ON-A-MUTABLE-REPORTED-AT-SO-A-CORRECTION-MANUFACTURES-A-FINDING could be closed. The window I needed sat entirely inside the truncated region, and the returned page gives a reader no way to know that — it looks like a complete answer to the question asked. I had to fall back to probing single-line reads at hand-picked timestamps to recover PIDs (3696148 at 22:00, 3719624 at 22:48 and 22:52), which established that a restart happened but not when. That row is left open as a result. A truncation marker, or honouring `since` over `lines`, would have settled it in one call.

items.title: compat-matrix `verdict: ROUTE` conflates 'passes this account's risk rules' with 'can actually be traded here' — 7 of 10 ROUTE rows are venues that cannot list the instrument
items.detail: MEASURED on the latest gld_compat run (2026-08-31T05:20:34Z, strategy gld_pullback_1h__GLD__trades, n_ledger_trades=124, 11 accounts): TEN accounts grade `verdict: ROUTE` and ONE grades `UNGRADED` (ib_live, size_state `unreadable` -- correctly not collapsed). But GLD is a US-listed equity ETF, and the ROUTE set includes `bybit_1`, `bybit_2` and `bybit_portfolio` (crypto perp venues) and `oanda_practice` (FX) -- SEVEN of the ten cannot list the instrument at all. WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY A MISREAD OF A CORRECT DESIGN: evaluating every account IS correct and deliberate -- the matrix's declared job (CLAUDE.md, prop-accounts architecture) is that 'a strategy is never routed to an account it wasn't evaluated against under that account's RULES', so it is a risk-ruleset gate, not a router. The defect is the WORD. `ROUTE` is an imperative that reads as an actionable routing recommendation, and no field in the row distinguishes 'cleared this account's risk rules' from 'is tradable on this venue'. A consumer -- including a future review session reading the corpus rather than the harness -- cannot tell the two apart from the row, which is the unprovenanced-diagnostic sub-class A (the label does not name what was computed). NOT THE FEE. Checked first and REFUTED: `fee_bps_roundtrip: 0.0` on all 44 rows looks like the ~25x fee mis-charge this repo already records for this exact strategy, and it is not -- `.github/workflows/gld-compat-matrix.yml` sets it deliberately ('the CORRECTED commission-free fee (0 bps)', 'GLD is commission-free on Alpaca, so 0'), so the zero is the CORRECTION, not a regression. A separate and milder caveat: commission is the harness's only cost term (no slippage/spread model in account_compat_matrix.py or montecarlo.py), so at exactly 0 the model is frictionless -- but montecarlo.py's own docstring already states that limitation, so it is disclosed, not hidden. RESOLUTION CRITERIA: a compat-matrix row carries an explicit instrument-availability field (e.g. `instrument_tradable` in tradable/not_tradable/unknown, resolved from the account's declared `symbols` in accounts.yaml), and a not_tradable account grades something other than `ROUTE` -- verified by re-running the gld_compat matrix and reading the corpus, with the bybit/oanda rows no longer reading ROUTE for GLD.
items.resolution_criteria: A compat-matrix row carries an instrument-availability field (tradable/not_tradable/unknown, resolved from the account's declared `symbols`), and an account that cannot list the symbol does NOT grade `ROUTE` -- verified by re-running gld-compat-matrix and reading the landed corpus, with the bybit_* and oanda_practice rows for GLD no longer reading ROUTE.

items.title: PROTECTION_STRAY_GROUP_MODE=annotate (the shipped default) computes its verdict and THROWS IT AWAY — no soak row, no diag surface, return value discarded at the call site
items.detail:
`_sweep_stray_oca_groups` is documented as: 'At the shipped default the decision runs in full and cancels nothing, so landing this changes no live behaviour and the flip to `apply` is a separate, REVIEWABLE decision.' The decision is not reviewable, because nothing records it. VERIFIED THREE WAYS: (a) `src/runtime/stray_oca_groups.py` contains ZERO file writes (`grep -cE 'open\(|Path\(|write_text|json.dump'` -> 0); (b) the call site at `src/units/accounts/ib_client.py:1829` invokes it as a BARE STATEMENT — `self._sweep_stray_oca_groups(ib, sym, oca_group, order.get('account_id'))` — so the returned `plan` (carrying mode / global_mode / apply_scope / the five per-group states) is discarded on the same line; (c) no `stray` entry exists in `diag.py`'s `_LOG_FILES` allowlist. The only output is `logger.warning` on two FAILURE paths, and this repo has now recorded three times that `logger.*` reaches the systemd journal and nothing else — never outcomes.jsonl, Telegram, the banner feed, or /api/bot/logs. THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS TWO ROWS ALREADY IN THE RECORD, which is why it is filed as a RECURRENCE rather than a novelty: `prop_risk_gate` promised 'at annotate a soak row is written' while being 318 lines with no file write (the 4th recurrence of BL-20260825-ALERT-AND-CADENCE-STATE-FILES-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE), and the pairs `apply_position_idx` RETURNED the resolved book while 'the call site discarded it one line later, so the only defect was that the answer was thrown away'. Identical defect, third module. IT IS LIVE-RELEVANT RIGHT NOW, not theoretical. Measured 2026-08-31T07:0xZ via /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper (read_state=orders_read, count=6): all three ib_paper positions are correctly two-sided bracketed — MES 15 STP 7533.75 + LMT 8390.5 under the KEYED `oca-protect-408`, but MGC 43 (STP 4408.4 + LMT 4524.5) under `1624576215` and MHG 30 (STP 6.3995 + LMT 7.3215) under `170199976` — BARE-NUMERIC group names, which is exactly the `stray_unkeyed` condition this detector exists to grade and exactly the form CLAUDE.md names ('the bare-numeric form 834864174 measured live on MGC'). So the next keyed re-arm on MGC or MHG is predicted to mint a second, non-mutually-cancelling group beside the existing one — and the detector that would have SEEN it coming records nothing. ⚠️ NOT the same as BL-20260825-PLACE-PROTECTIVE-COUNTS-THE-CANCEL-CALL-NOT-ITS-EFFECT: CLAUDE.md separates them explicitly (that row is the symbol-wide fallback, and its three defects are already fixed in b81458a4, an ancestor of the deployed sha). This row is about the KEYED path's detector being unobservable. ⚠️ The over-cover state is NOT present today — one group per symbol, both legs, qty matching the position — so this is a filed prediction with a stated basis, not an incident.

=== 2026-08-31T20:xx, session ayloee (probe-coverage W3) — INDEPENDENT RE-DERIVATION, and ONE THING THIS ROW DID NOT YET CARRY. I reached the identical finding from the other end while raising probe coverage on OPEN-ITEMS monitoring rows, wrote it up as a fresh row, and `backlog_append`'s similarity check refused it at overlap 0.88 against this one — which is the mechanism working, so my row was DROPPED rather than filed. The independent confirmation is worth one line: same call site, same discarded return, same absent `_LOG_FILES` entry. WHAT IS NEW is the CONSUMER-SIDE consequence, which is why this note is added rather than nothing: `docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json`'s monitoring row OI-20260826-STRAY-OCA-SWEEP-SHIPPED-BUT-UNARMED carried a `probe_absent_reason` asserting the row becomes 'PROBE-ABLE ONCE ARMED', and told a future session to 'attach one against /api/diag/log_file?name=protection_reassert_soak (or the stray-group soak) in the same change that arms PROTECTION_STRAY_GROUP_ACCOUNTS'. BOTH TARGETS ARE WRONG: protection_reassert_soak is a DIFFERENT gate's log and carries no stray-group classification, and 'the stray-group soak' is the file this row says has never been written. So the stated unblock condition was ARMING, when the actual blocker is the WRITER — a session following that instruction would have armed a live-cancel path and still had nothing to read. That reason has been corrected in the same change as this note, and criterion (4) below was added so the fix closes the consumer too.
items.resolution_criteria: `_sweep_stray_oca_groups` writes one row per graded symbol to a soak log (carrying the effective `mode` beside `global_mode` and `apply_scope`, and the per-group state), that log is registered in diag.py's `_LOG_FILES` allowlist IN THE SAME COMMIT as the writer, and `/api/diag/log_file?name=<it>` returns a graded row for ib_paper MGC or MHG — verified on the live VM, not in a test. items.title: docs/research/e35-bracket-gate-corpus.jsonl is 134 rows that NOTHING reads, carry NO date field at all, and duplicate 133 of 134 (leg,cell) pairs already in the live e35 corpus — it looks exactly like gradeable evidence and is not
items.detail:
FOUND while checking which research corpora the disposition reader consumes, after the gld_compat gap (11 rows on disk, 0 units to the reader, read_state 'read') was closed the same day.

MEASURED 2026-08-31 on origin/main:
  - REFERENCED BY ZERO scripts, workflows or tests. Positive-controlled, because silence is not proof of absence: the IDENTICAL grep finds the sibling 'e35-bracket-corpus' in 12 files and this one in 0.
  - NO DATE FIELD OF ANY KIND on any row -- no sweep_generated_at, no run_generated_at, nothing matching at/date/time/stamp. The rows cannot be dated, so the run-scoped assert_rows_landed pattern cannot even scope them.
  - 133 of its 134 (leg, cell) pairs are ALREADY in docs/research/e35-bracket-corpus.jsonl (8,321 rows, 66 dated stamps spanning 2026-08-23 to 2026-08-31).
  - The single pair unique to it is `leg=None cell=None verdict=None` -- a malformed row, not evidence.
  - 133 of 134 carry `base_oos_trades`, so it presents exactly like the achieved-n data a reader looks for.
  - Last touched by an unrelated alpaca-sizing PR (#10347); nothing has deliberately written it since.

WHY IT MATTERS. It sits in docs/research/ beside the live corpus, carries the same field names including an achieved sample size, and has no stamp to distinguish it. A session reading corpora for evidence -- which is the normal thing to do, and what surfaced this -- could read it as current. 'Looks like evidence and is not' is the shape this repo keeps paying for; an UNDATED artifact is the worst version, because the usual defence (scope the claim to a run stamp) is unavailable.

NOT A DUPLICATE of BL-20260817-AN-UNMERGED-ARTIFACT-BRANCH-SILENCES-A-GUARD-THAT-READS-MAIN (that is a committed artifact stranded on an unmerged BRANCH; this one is ON main and the problem is that it should probably not be) nor of BL-20260814-CORPUS-AGREEMENT-COUNTS-141-UNCHECKABLE-CELLS-AS-CHECKED (empty lever columns graded as checked). Related in spirit to both; same subject as neither.

ALSO RECORDED, because I got it wrong on the coordination board first: the OTHER four unregistered corpora are FINE. m20-exit-head-rounds (33 rows), m20-fold-dispersion-arms-consolidated (246), m20-fold-dispersion-arms (60) and paper-book-tracker (9) all have real consumers -- m20_dispersion_rate, m20_exit_head_denominator, m20_consolidate_dispersion_arms, paper_book_tracker, and check_matrix_corpus_agreement which is a CI GUARD. They are intermediates feeding a specific analysis, not standalone units awaiting disposition, so their absence from research_disposition.CORPORA is CORRECT. I had asserted 'unregistered therefore unread' for all five without checking for other consumers, which would have manufactured work on four files including one a guard depends on.
items.resolution_criteria: A DECISION is taken and applied, and the file's status is unambiguous to a reader who has not read this row. Either: (a) DELETED, with the deletion commit stating that 133/134 of its pairs were verified present in the live corpus first and the 134th was the malformed null row -- deleting research data requires showing nothing unique was lost; or (b) KEPT and made unmissable, e.g. renamed out of the corpus namespace or given a header row that states it is superseded and undated, so a reader scanning docs/research/*.jsonl cannot mistake it for current evidence. NOT sufficient: registering it in research_disposition.CORPORA -- that would grade 134 undatable duplicate rows as fresh units and make the problem worse. Verified by re-running the reference grep with its positive control (the sibling corpus must still match, or the probe is broken).
items.found_by: checking which research corpora have consumers, after closing the gld_compat reader gap
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-08-31 by DELETION, operator decision. Option (a) of the two the row offered. The loss check was re-run immediately before the delete and is the evidence: 133 of 134 (leg, cell) pairs verified present in docs/research/e35-bracket-corpus.jsonl, and the 134th is `leg=None cell=None verdict=None` — a malformed row carrying no evidence. The script asserted that shape and would have refused to delete had any genuine row been unique, so 'nothing unique was lost' is a checked claim rather than an assurance.

items.title: The withheld-gain counter was computed on both return paths and forwarded to nothing — written and never read, inside the change whose comment promises it is counted
items.detail:
PR #10532 fixed the prop cushion double-count and added `fills_withheld_unplaceable_gain` so a reader could see the reconstruction is conservative BY CONSTRUCTION rather than that the fill stream was empty. `reconstruct_equity` sets it on BOTH return paths (prop_reconcile.py:383 and :393). `compute_rule_distance` then cherry-picks `fills_applied` and `fills_pnl_usd` into renamed panel keys (:523-524) and never forwards this one — so the value died at the seam and never reached /api/bot/prop/status, the only surface anyone reads.

MEASURED, not inferred: at 2026-08-31T08:40Z, minutes after 0dabfca7 deployed, the panel returned equity_used_usd 4787.34, distance_to_dd_floor_usd 87.34, fills_applied_since_snapshot 0, balance_basis snapshot, equity_provenance measured — the fix itself correctly live — and the key ABSENT. The withheld count should have read 1 (the +35.28 SOLUSDT close, reported_at 2026-08-30T19:39:00.97Z, closed_at None).

WHY THE EXISTING TEST COULD NOT CATCH IT: test_a_gain_reported_after_the_snapshot_is_not_double_counted asserts the key on `reconstruct_equity`'s OWN return value and passed throughout. The defect lived entirely at the seam between two individually-correct functions — the S-PROVENANCE-EXITLEAK shape, where line-by-line audits keep returning clean.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, which is the transferable part: it was NOT found by review. It was found because the deploy-verification plan had nominated this key as the decisive control (it cannot exist pre-deploy, so its appearance proves the new code is running), and the control did not fire. A verification plan that names a field the change ITSELF introduces doubles as a wiring test for that field.

RECURRENCE of the produced-but-never-propagated class: same shape as BL-20260814-TP-GEOMETRY-RECORDED-IN-PROSE-WHILE-THE-CONSUMER-READS-A-FIELD and BL-20260815-EXIT-HEAD-CORPUS-GEOMETRY-NEVER-PROPAGATED-TO-MATRIX, in a new module. Filed as a recurrence, not a duplicate: those fixes were scoped to their own call sites and nothing generalised.
items.resolution_criteria: compute_rule_distance forwards fills_withheld_unplaceable_gain, and a test reads it off compute_rule_distance (the PANEL) rather than off reconstruct_equity, with non-vacuity shown by removing the forward. SATISFIED: test_the_withheld_gain_counter_REACHES_THE_PANEL — fails with the forward removed while the other 10 tests in the file still pass, which is the demonstration that a unit-level assertion could not see it. NOT yet satisfied: live confirmation on /api/bot/prop/status after this lands and deploys — expect the key present and == 1 while snapshot 19 and the +35.28 fill are both still in place.

items.summary: The live wallet-truth path shipped in #10532 WORKS but does NOT yet supersede comms/broker_truth_ledger.json for bybit_2, for TWO independent reasons — and neither was visible until the first live pull. Do not switch journalTrust over on the strength of the pull succeeding.
items.detail:
FIRST LIVE PULL, 2026-08-31T08:43Z: days=60 chunks=9 on all three accounts (bybit_1 1821 rows, bybit_2 618, bybit_portfolio 350, 2789 inserted). The 7-day-range walk is PROVEN — chunks=9 covers 63 days, so the moving-window failure the design warned about did not occur. /api/diag/bybit_wallet_truth returns measured_api for all three.

(1) THE POPULATIONS ARE NEAR-DISJOINT, so the live figure neither confirms nor refutes the ledger. Ledger: -262.52 over 2026-04-15 -> 2026-07-13. Live 60d: +17.04 over 2026-07-02 -> 2026-08-31 (TRADE +17.66, SETTLEMENT -0.62, 618 rows, 0 transfers excluded). They overlap by ~11 days. The default 30d window reads +32.66 over 2026-08-01 -> 2026-08-31, which overlaps the ledger by ZERO days. Reproducing the ledger window needs a ~138-day pull back to 2026-04-15, which was not attempted and whose feasibility depends on Bybit's retention (the 7-day cap is on the QUERYABLE RANGE, not retention — retention depth is UNMEASURED and must be established, not assumed).

(2) THE SUB-ACCOUNT STITCH MAY BE STRUCTURALLY UNREACHABLE, which is the more serious half. The ledger's own note records the -262.52 as 'stitched across two sub-accounts (MAIN -1.52 + SUB -261.01)' with a sub-account switch on 2026-05-10 — so 99.4% of that figure sits in SUB. The puller uses ONE credential pair per configured account id. If that credential addresses one sub-account, the live path CANNOT reproduce the stitched total however far back it pulls, and a switched-over journalTrust would silently report one sub-account's truth as the account's. UNVERIFIED either way: which sub-account the live bybit_2 credential belongs to has not been established. /api/diag/broker_account_status carries a bybit `identity` block with the UID, which is the read that would settle it.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH, and journalTrust must not switch to the live path until both hold: (a) the bybit_2 credential's UID is read from /api/diag/broker_account_status and stated against the MAIN/SUB pair the ledger stitched, so it is KNOWN whether the live path can see SUB at all; and (b) either a pull covering 2026-04-15 -> 2026-07-13 reproduces -262.52 within a stated tolerance, or it is recorded that Bybit retention / the sub-account split makes that window unreachable — in which case the ledger stays authoritative for the historical window and the live path owns only the period after its first pull, with the boundary written down. A pull that merely SUCCEEDS is not evidence for either.

items.summary: collapsed-state-guard's unread-state check could not fire for 19 of its 20 contracts, because a contract's own registry entry counted as a consumer of itself. Turning the check on for the first time surfaced 4 genuine findings at once. Fixed by excluding the registry file; 3 pre-existing findings are grandfathered and reported, not failed.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-31 on main. A contract entry in scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py::CONTRACTS contains (a) its own `consumer_token` regex AS SOURCE TEXT, so the token matches the registry file, and (b) every state literal in its `states` list, so `_states_in` returns ALL of them. The consumer scan excluded only `prod_path`, never the registry itself — so the file that DECLARES a contract automatically satisfied it.

POPULATION: all 20 registered contracts. 19 of 20 are FULLY self-satisfied (token matches the registry AND every state literal appears there); the exception is `pairs_executor.open_state_read`, whose token happens not to match its own entry. So check (3) — 'state(s) X are produced but NO consumer branches on them', the guard's central claim — could not fire however many states were genuinely unread.

WHAT IT WAS HIDING. With the registry excluded, 4 contracts fail immediately:
  research_queue.power_state   — 5 unread (cleared, undeclared, unverifiable, not_applicable, infeasible)
  operator_owed.state          — 5 unread (moved, carried, escalate_aged, not_measurable, snoozed)
  over_cover.state             — 6 unread (cancel_group, no_over_cover, ambiguous_no_action, no_journal_match, no_declared_stop, position_absent)
  netting_attribution.anchor_status — 1 unread (deferred)

This is the guard's OWN named failure mode — 'a guard that is cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than no guard', the new-table-wiring-guard lesson it cites in its docstring — reproduced one level up, on the guard rather than on an annotation. Nothing had to be written wrongly for it to happen: declaring a contract was enough.

SHIPPED IN THIS CHANGE: `_REGISTRY_PATH` is excluded from the consumer scan (the fix), and the 4 findings are routed to a dated GRANDFATHERED_UNREAD set that is PRINTED LOUDLY every run but does not fail CI; `--strict` fails on everything. Failing on all 4 would have made the fix un-landable and the check would have stayed off, which is how a vacuous guard survives. A positive control was run: mutating a real producer (exit_anchor no_anchor -> deferred) makes the guard fire, so it is genuinely live now.

NOT FIXED HERE, and this is the open half: the 3 pre-existing contracts belong to other work (operator_owed, over_cover, netting_attribution) and each needs a real consumer or an honest per-file collapsed-state annotation. A SECOND, separate limitation was found while registering research_queue.power_state: `_states_in` credits only STRING LITERALS, so a consumer that correctly imports the vocabulary (`if v.state == research_queue.INFEASIBLE`) is invisible to the guard, and satisfying it would mean sprinkling literals into modules that do the right thing. The evidence model should credit the constant NAMES too.
items.resolution_criteria: GRANDFATHERED_UNREAD is EMPTY and `python3 scripts/ci/check_collapsed_states.py --strict` exits 0 — each of the 4 contracts having gained a real branching consumer or a per-file collapsed-state annotation naming a declared state. Additionally: `_states_in` credits an imported constant name as evidence, verified by a test that a consumer branching only via constants satisfies its contract. A passing default run is NOT the criterion — that is what the grandfather list buys.

items.summary: scope_overlap's attribution() compares a board START's branch to the PR's branch, so a session that posts ONE START and opens PRs from SEVERAL branches has its own START graded `other` and reported back at it. Same false-positive class as #10594, narrower form: that fix handled a START with no branch, this is a START with a DIFFERENT branch from the same session.
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-08-31T17:26:46Z on PR #10607, read from the posted comment rather than from the code. Comment: `Compared 3 changed file(s) against 66 declared path(s) - 6 attributed to another session, 2 unattributable`. Two of the six are genuine (`claude/research-queue-landing-v4yfq7` at 11:41Z/15:24Z and `claude/research-disposition-resweep-cplgnv` at 15:55Z, both declaring docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json; the latter also ROADMAP.md and docs/sprint-logs/) - THAT HALF IS THE DETECTOR'S FIRST GENUINE CATCH AND IT WORKED. The defect is the third line: `claude/workflows-audit-restructure-fz0sw9` is the SAME session's designated branch, while the PR was opened from `claude/session-wrapup-fz0sw9`. scripts/ci/check_scope_overlap.py::attribution returns 'mine' only when `branch == my_branch` or the START body names `#<my_pr>`; a START posted before any PR exists satisfies neither. THIS IS THE COMMON SHAPE, NOT AN EDGE CASE - a session posts one START at the top and then opens per-task branches, which is what CLAUDE.md's coordination protocol asks for. PROPOSED FIX (small): branches carry a trailing 6-char session suffix shared across one session (`fz0sw9`, `v4yfq7`, `cplgnv`), so match that suffix in addition to the exact branch. ⚠️ IT MUST ONLY EVER ADD TO `mine`, NEVER SUPPRESS AN `other` - under-reporting a real overlap is the worse error, which is exactly why the existing `unattributable` state already resolves toward reporting rather than silence. A suffix that collides between two real sessions would otherwise silence a genuine finding. Add a self-test case with a planted same-suffix-different-branch START, and a negative control with a different suffix that must still grade `other`. NOT A BLOCKER for #10607: the overlap was verified harmless (those sessions' work had already merged as #10602/#10604 and `git merge-tree` against origin/main was CLEAN).
items.resolution_criteria: scripts/ci/check_scope_overlap.py grades a START whose branch shares the PR branch's session suffix as `mine`, proven by (a) a new self-test case with a planted same-suffix-different-branch START AND a negative control with a different suffix that still grades `other`, and (b) a live scope-overlap comment on a real PR in which the posting session's own START no longer appears under another session's attribution.

items.not_a_duplicate_of: BL-20260830-BROKER-TRUTH-LEDGER-STALE-59-REAL-MONEY-CLOSES-UNRECONCILED (0.54 overlap, read before filing). That row is about the hand LEDGER going stale; this is about the LIVE route being unable to report how far its own data reaches. backlog_search returned 8 rows, all lexical; none names this.
items.summary: /api/diag/bybit_wallet_truth reports `window_start_ms` — the bound the CALLER ASKED FOR — and never the earliest row it actually holds. So 'we asked for 200 days' and 'we have 200 days of data' render identically, and the retention question the route exists to inform cannot be answered from it.
items.evidence: Hit 2026-08-31 while answering OI-20260831-LIVE-WALLET-TRUTH-CANNOT-REPRODUCE-THE-LEDGER-WINDOW, whose clears_when required retention be ANSWERED rather than assumed. `src/runtime/bybit_wallet_truth.py` carries `window_start_ms` and no earliest/oldest field; the route echoes it. Measured: days=150 -> 'window 2026-04-03', 631 rows; days=200 -> 'window 2026-02-12', 631 rows; days=400 -> 'window 2025-07-27', 631 rows. The reported window moved back 8 months while the data did not change at all, and a reader taking `window_start_ms` at face value would record 'coverage back to 2025-07-27' — which is false by roughly eight months. THE WORKAROUND THAT WAS ACTUALLY NEEDED: bracket the earliest row by SHRINKING the window until the count falls off its plateau (631 at days>=135 -> 629 at days=130), placing the earliest row between 2026-04-18 and 2026-04-23. That is three extra round-trips and a piece of reasoning, to recover a number the producer already had in hand.
items.why_it_matters: This is the UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC class (sub-class B, implicit input selection) on a money surface: the label names a window and the value is a REQUEST, not a measurement. It nearly produced a wrong conclusion in the session that hit it — 'retention reaches back to 2025-07-27' was the natural read and would have made the sub-account explanation look impossible, since a path with 13 months of coverage 'should' reproduce a 3-month ledger. The real answer (retention is fine; the SCOPE is one sub-account) only became visible after bracketing.
items.resolution_criteria: The envelope carries the data's OWN span for each account — an `earliest_row_ms` / `latest_row_ms` (or an explicit `no_rows` state) sourced from the stored rows, distinct from the requested `window_start_ms`, so 'we asked for N days' and 'we hold N days' can never render the same. ⚠️ Not closed by widening the default window or by documenting the caveat in prose: the field is what a consumer reads. A test should assert the two differ on a store whose earliest row postdates the requested bound.

items.not_a_duplicate_of: BL-20260825-ALERT-AND-CADENCE-STATE-FILES-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE is the same CLASS and this is a RECURRENCE of it, filed deliberately as such: that row's fix added five cadence/latch files to the diag allowlist, and this path shipped afterwards with the same gap, so the earlier fix did not generalise to new writers. Distinct object: this is an ORDER-PATH apply gate, not a cadence/latch state file.
items.summary: PROTECTION_STRAY_GROUP_MODE=apply CANCELS a live position's resting protective legs and writes NO soak file — the verdict reaches `logger` only. So the one thing that would prove the cancel was correct is observable solely through /api/diag/journalctl (rolling, unstructured), and no field-matching probe can be written against it.
items.evidence: Verified 2026-08-31 by reading the producer, not inferred. src/runtime/stray_oca_groups.py is a PURE decision function — grep for soak/jsonl/emit/write returns 0 file writes. ib_client._sweep_stray_oca_groups hands its result to _log_cancel_verdict (ib_client.py:2938), which calls `logger.error`/`logger.warning` only. `stray_oca_soak` is ABSENT from src/web/api/routers/diag.py::_LOG_FILES; the only entry in that family is `protection_reassert_soak`, which belongs to the DIFFERENT re-assert path. Found because scripts/ops/run_probes.py --check refused a new monitoring row for declaring neither `probe` nor `probe_absent_reason` — the guard forced the discovery.
items.why_it_matters: The gate was ARMED on ib_paper on 2026-08-31 (Tier-2, operator-approved; issues #10614/#10615, verified on /proc). Its OPEN-ITEMS row was written with a clears_when asking for a soak row showing `acted: true` — A ROW THAT CANNOT EXIST. So as shipped, an operator-approved order-path capability is running with no structured evidence trail, and its own tracking row was unsatisfiable until corrected. This is precisely the shape CLAUDE.md documents twice over for this subsystem: `logger.error` reaches the systemd journal and NOTHING else — not outcomes.jsonl, not Telegram, not /api/bot/logs — which is why both the IB and Bybit over-cover pages had to be given real emitters. The cancel is the most consequential action in the module and the least observable.
items.resolution_criteria: src/runtime/stray_oca_groups.py (or its ib_client call site) writes runtime_logs/stray_oca_soak.jsonl carrying, per decision: the effective `mode` beside `global_mode` and `apply_scope`, `acted`, the five never-collapsed leg states, the groups cancelled, and the `verify_state`/`still_resting` read-back — AND `stray_oca_soak` is added to diag.py::_LOG_FILES IN THE SAME COMMIT as the writer (a soak that cannot be read is the #8778 lesson). Then OI-20260831-STRAY-OCA-SWEEP-ARMED-ON-IB-PAPER-BUT-HAS-NEVER-CANCELLED gains a real `probe` and drops its probe_absent_reason. NOT closed by: adding the allowlist entry alone (there is no file yet), or by relying on journalctl (rolling and unstructured).

updates.note:
RESOLVED — the apply path's cancel is now PROVABLE, and has been PROVED on a real cancellation, read from the live VM.

WRITER + ALLOWLIST IN THE SAME COMMIT: 2f4600c5 (#10640) adds src/runtime/stray_oca_soak.py (178 lines), the src/units/accounts/ib_client.py call site, tests/test_stray_oca_soak.py, AND the src/web/api/routers/diag.py allowlist entry — verified with `git show --stat`, so the '#8778 lesson' clause (a soak that cannot be read) is met by construction.

LIVE ROW, /api/diag/log_file?name=stray_oca_soak, read 2026-09-01T23:0xZ (present: true, size_bytes 648). The single row, logged 2026-09-01T14:32:35.326605Z, ib_paper / MGC, carries EVERY field the criterion enumerates:
  mode: apply | global_mode: apply | apply_scope: allowlisted   (effective beside global)
  acted: true                                                   (the EFFECT, not the plan)
  legs_by_state: {keep_target 0, sibling_keyed 0, stray_unkeyed 2, ungrouped 0, not_protective 0}   (all FIVE states, explicit zeros, summing to legs_seen 2)
  stray_groups: ["1502161095"] / cancelled_groups: ["1502161095"]  (the groups cancelled)
  verify_state: verified | still_resting: [] | confirmed_gone: ["perm:1502161097", "perm:1502161096"]   (the read-back)
  cancel_calls_made: 2 — deliberately still named for the CALLS, per BL-20260825-PLACE-PROTECTIVE-COUNTS-THE-CANCEL-CALL-NOT-ITS-EFFECT; the OUTCOME is verify_state/still_resting, and here they agree.

So this is not 'the writer shipped' — it is a real apply-mode cancellation of a stray unkeyed group on a live ib_paper position, with a post-cancel read-back confirming both legs gone and nothing left resting. That is the evidence the row said was missing.

⚠️ ONE CLAUSE SATISFIED IN SUBSTANCE UNDER A DIFFERENT ID, stated rather than hidden. The criterion says 'OI-20260831-STRAY-OCA-SWEEP-ARMED-ON-IB-PAPER-BUT-HAS-NEVER-CANCELLED gains a real probe and drops its probe_absent_reason'. NO SUCH OPEN-ITEMS ROW EXISTS (checked all 29 rows in docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json; the only STRAY row is OI-20260826-STRAY-OCA-SWEEP-SHIPPED-BUT-UNARMED). That row carries the probe the criterion describes — scripts/ops/probe_soak.py against /api/diag/log_file?name=stray_oca_soak&lines=1000 with --require decision=stray_unkeyed --require acted=true and a --positive-control over decision~stray_unkeyed,no_strays,could_not_look — and its probe_absent_reason is None. `python3 scripts/ops/run_probes.py --check` passes: 'OK — 19 monitoring row(s), 8 probed, 11 with a declared reason for having none'. The named id was never created; the mechanism it asked for exists on the sibling row.

items.summary: `W<n>` is used as a work-item label by at least THREE unrelated enumerations in this repo, so a bare W-number is ambiguous — and one collision already sent a session's commits, docs and ROADMAP row pointing at a design that was refuted and deliberately not built.
items.why_it_matters: Not cosmetic, because the collision resolves toward a REFUTED artefact. `W3` in the 2026-08-31 operations plan is the MERGE SERIALIZER — measured against 39 merges at a 15.9 min median, found unnecessary, and recorded inline in `.github/workflows/scope-overlap-audit.yml` precisely so no future session re-proposes it. A session doing probe coverage (item 3 of the artifact's FIVE-ITEM work plan, a continuation of W2) stamped `W3` on four modules, a ROADMAP row, a sprint log and four commit messages. A later reader chasing that label lands on the serializer's do-not-build note. The commit messages are immutable, so that ambiguity is now permanent in the history.
items.evidence: Three sequences observed 2026-08-31: (1) the operations plan — W2 = probes/due-list machinery (`.github/workflows/probes.yml:3`), W3 = merge serializer (refuted), W4 = research artifacts (refuted), W5 = CLAUDE.md split (deferred), W6 = local LLM, W7 = backlog schema; (2) the audit artifact's five-item work plan — item 1 = due-list age grading (PR #10600), item 3 = probe coverage; (3) an unrelated `full-system-audit W2` at ROADMAP.md:866. `S-OPERATING-MACHINERY-AUDIT-2026-08-31.md` uses BOTH scheme (1) and scheme (2) within six lines — line 52 'W3 — tell a PR when it touches a file another live session declared' vs line 58 '**work-plan item 1**'. items.not_a_duplicate_of: BL-20260823-ALPACA-CASH-ACCOUNT-SETTLEMENT-UNMODELLED asks for the model to EXIST and is largely answered by PR #10408; this is about the model's BLAST RADIUS once it binds. BL-20260829-ALPACA-MIRROR-DOES-NOT-MIRROR-RISK-PCT is a risk_pct mismatch, not a settlement one. BL-20260826-ALPACA-LIVE-AT-200-USD-CANNOT-SIZE-ITS-LARGEST-SYMBOLS is whole-share affordability on the CASH account. None of the three says the gate applies cash arithmetic to a MARGIN account without checking.
items.summary: ALPACA_CASH_SETTLEMENT_MODE=apply applies cash-account arithmetic to ANY allowlisted account without checking capacity.multiplier, and on a MARGIN account with a negative cash balance it yields basis 0.00 — which halts that account's trading entirely rather than merely constraining it.
items.evidence: src/runtime/cash_settlement.py:253-261 computes basis = max(min(venue_buying_power, venue_cash - unsettled), 0.0). The clamp comment justifies 0.0 as 'you may spend nothing', which is the right reading for a CASH book and a full stop for a margin one. Nothing in settled_basis(), may_apply() or resolve_for_account() consults account type. Measured 2026-08-31 via /api/diag/broker_account_status: alpaca_paper and alpaca_portfolio are BOTH capacity.multiplier=4 with shorting_enabled=true, while alpaca_live is multiplier=1. In the cash_settlement_soak the same day, alpaca_portfolio reported venue_cash NEGATIVE in 2 of 2 rows (-65371.75 and -35712.41) producing basis_usd 0.00 in 2 of 2. STATE THE POPULATION: the whole soak file was 5 rows from one day (2 per mirror), so the FREQUENCY of the negative-cash condition is thin evidence; the MECHANISM is deterministic arithmetic and is not a statistical claim. A negative cash balance is ordinary margin borrowing, not an anomaly.
items.why_it_matters: The allowlist is the only thing standing between this and a halted book, and an allowlist is exactly the kind of thing a later session widens 'for consistency' — this repo has already paid for that shape once in the opposite direction (NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_ACCOUNTS, corrected 2026-08-09, where scoping at the top of the pass made the account being staged TOWARD invisible). The failure here is silent and easy to misread: a halted account emits no orders, so it looks like a signal drought rather than a refusal, and alpaca_portfolio is the account the dashboard's entire 'Paper' view is built on. It nearly happened on 2026-08-31 — the operator asked mid-task to arm the mirrors alongside alpaca_live and the widening was only stopped by reading the arithmetic first.
items.resolution_criteria: settled_basis (or its caller) establishes the account's funding type before applying the cash correction, with the answer NEVER COLLAPSED: a margin account is graded distinctly from 'we could not read the multiplier', and the unreadable case does not silently take the cash branch. A test asserts that an account with multiplier>1 and negative venue_cash does NOT resolve to basis 0.00 via the cash path. Alternatively, may_apply() refuses a non-cash account outright and says so in the soak row's state, so an operator widening the allowlist gets a visible refusal rather than a halt.

items.not_a_duplicate_of: This is not about any individual OPEN-ITEMS row or about probe COVERAGE. It is a defect in the shared probe runner itself, in the exact failure mode its own docstring names as the one it exists to prevent.
items.summary: probe_soak.py raises AttributeError on a bare-LIST diag payload and the unhandled traceback exits 1 — which its own contract defines as EXIT_FAIL, 'the log was READ and NOTHING matched'. A could-not-look is therefore reported as a real negative, and the module's correct `unrecognised envelope` branch is unreachable for this shape.
items.evidence: scripts/ops/probe_soak.py:149 does `if isinstance(payload.get(key), list)` inside a for-loop over ('lines','records','rows'). Its `else:` at :153 correctly returns `None, 'unrecognised envelope'` (= could_not_look, exit 2), but for a payload that is itself a list, `payload.get` raises AttributeError FIRST and the else is never reached. Measured 2026-08-31: `python3 scripts/ops/probe_soak.py --path '/api/diag/journal?table=trades&limit=1000' --require account_id=alpaca_live --require 'status~open,closed,filled'` printed a traceback and exited 1. /api/diag/journal returns a bare JSON array (verified against the live VM — 1000 dict rows, no envelope). The docstring is explicit that this case belongs to code 2: 'Code 2 covers: the fetch failed, no bearer, the payload was not the expected envelope, an unparseable predicate. It is emphatically NOT code 1.' BLAST RADIUS TODAY IS ZERO AND THAT IS WHY IT IS EASY TO MISS: all 3 currently-registered probes read /api/diag/log_file, which returns a `lines` envelope, so none of them hits this path.
items.why_it_matters: The failure is silent precisely where it is most costly. A monitoring row's EXPECTED state is `fail` (the thing being watched has not happened yet), so a crash and the truth render identically — the row looks watched while nothing is looking. That is the same 'curl … || echo {}' shape the docstring says the repo has already paid for twice, reproduced inside the tool built to end it. It blocked a real probe this session: OI-20260831-ALPACA-LIVE-FIRST-REAL-MONEY-LEG-ROUTED-BUT-HAS-NEVER-TRADED is a REAL-MONEY row whose condition is machine-checkable off exactly this endpoint (80 alpaca_live rows in a 1000-row tail spanning a month — a real denominator), and it had to ship with probe_absent_reason instead.
items.resolution_criteria: fetch_rows handles a top-level JSON array as a valid row source (a bare list IS the rows), and any payload shape it cannot interpret returns could_not_look rather than raising — asserted by a test that feeds it a bare list and a garbage scalar and pins exit 0/1 vs 2 respectively. The --self-test grows a case for the bare-list shape and is shown to FAIL against the current code. Then register the probe on the alpaca row and drop its probe_absent_reason.

items.not_a_duplicate_of: Not about any single stale doc row — those were fixed in PR #10639. This is about WHY the session-end mechanism did not prevent them. No existing row covers doc-freshness's own coverage or check_declared_values's denominator; the lexical neighbours backlog_search returned (PR-CI attachment, exit-eval intervals, coverage-matrix short-circuit) are unrelated.
items.summary: The 2026-08-31 alpaca_live go-live left THREE canonical surfaces stale (OPEN-ITEMS risk_pct, CLAUDE.md env row, ROADMAP M15) despite doc-freshness being a binding session-end step. Operator asked why. Measured: it is two DIFFERENT failures, and only one is discipline — the other is that neither the skill nor its CI backstop can see the class at all.
items.evidence: MEASURED 2026-09-01 on origin/main. (1) THE AUTOMATED BACKSTOP HAS A ZERO DENOMINATOR. scripts/ci/check_canonical_doc_coherence.py::check_declared_values iterates a hand-maintained VALUE_CONTRACTS list holding exactly THREE ids — 'branch-protection require-up-to-date', 'POST /api/bot/prop/report write gate', '/api/bot/devices admin-token gate'. None is an env knob. CLAUDE.md's env table documents 67 distinct knobs (regex ^\| `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+` over the file); 0 of 67 are covered. So the guard PASSED on all three stale surfaces, and its PASS was quoted in-session as evidence the docs were coherent — a green that checked nothing, which docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md names as no better than a red that checked nothing. (2) EVEN A REGISTERED CONTRACT WOULD NOT HAVE FIRED. check_declared_values only reports when a doc ASSERTS a value the source contradicts. The CLAUDE.md row asserted NO value — it read 'Tier-2 to flip, and stage it on one account' while the knob had been at apply for hours. SILENCE IS INVISIBLE TO THE CHECK BY CONSTRUCTION, so a knob that is flipped and whose doc simply never mentions it passes forever. (3) THE SKILL'S COVERAGE IS SPLIT. .claude/skills/doc-freshness/SKILL.md (173 lines) has a landing table for ROADMAP.md / sprint log / review backlog and explicitly names ROADMAP as 'the surface that most often gets skipped' — so the ROADMAP staleness is a discipline miss on a KNOWN RECURRING class. But grep for 'live value', 'env var', 'knob', 'set-env' returns nothing in its body: recording a flipped knob's LIVE VALUE in CLAUDE.md's table is not a step the skill asks for at all. (4) THIS SESSION IS ITSELF AN INSTANCE: it did the doc work manually and never invoked the skill, and found the gaps only because the operator asked.
items.why_it_matters: This table is where a session goes to learn what is actually armed on a live money-at-risk system, and CLAUDE.md itself is full of ⚠️ corrections of exactly this shape ('this row said X and it was stale in the DANGEROUS direction'). Those corrections are the symptom; this is the mechanism. The repo's own convention is that a flipped knob carries a LIVE VALUE (BYBIT_TPSL_MODE, FLIP_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD, BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS all do) — the convention exists and is simply unenforced, so compliance is per-session memory. The failure is silent and asymmetric: a doc that says nothing about an ARMED gate reads exactly like a doc about a DISARMED one, and the reader most likely to be misled is a future session deciding whether a Tier-2/3 action is still outstanding. It already cost real confusion this session about whether the T+1 flip had happened.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH halves addressed, and neither alone closes this. (a) COVERAGE: every env knob that CLAUDE.md documents as having a live-flippable value either carries a LIVE VALUE claim or is explicitly marked as at-default, and something MECHANICAL checks it — the natural source is get-env's ALLOWED_KEYS (already the read surface for live values) cross-referenced against the table, so the check has a real denominator instead of a hand-maintained list of 3. Report the denominator in the guard's own output so a future zero-coverage state is visible rather than a green. (b) SILENCE: check_declared_values grows a state for 'the doc asserts NO value for a knob that has one', distinct from 'asserts a wrong one' — the collapsed-state discipline this repo applies everywhere else, applied to its own doc guard. (c) SKILL: doc-freshness's landing table gains a row for 'flipped an env knob / armed a gate this session -> record the LIVE VALUE + how it was verified in CLAUDE.md'. A passing guard on today's docs is NOT evidence for (a) or (b) — the guard passes today on 0/67 coverage.

items.title: GET /api/bot/order-packages?since=<ISO with a raw +00:00 offset> returns ZERO rows and no error - a malformed filter renders as a clean negative
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-01 against the live VM, all three arms in one go on strategy=trend_donchian_xrp_4h, limit=5, include_paper=true:
  no `since`                      -> 5 rows (newest 2026-08-30T23:46:36)
  since=2026-08-30T14:05:00+00:00 -> 0 rows, HTTP 200, no error field
  since=2026-08-30T14:05:00Z      -> 1 row
The `+` in a query string decodes as a SPACE, so the server receives '2026-08-30T14:05:00 00:00'. That value is unparseable, and the route answers 200 with an empty `rows` list rather than rejecting it - so a caller cannot distinguish 'nothing happened since then' from 'your filter was dropped on the floor'. Same class as BL-20260813-DB-EXPLORER-SILENTLY-IGNORES-UNKNOWN-FILTER-COLUMN, which was fixed on /api/bot/db/table/{name} by publishing a never-collapsed `filter_state` (applied / not_requested / ignored_*); this route publishes no such field.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: it cost this session a confident wrong answer. A per-leg sweep over the ten e35 legs returned 0 rows on ALL TEN and would have been reported as 'no order packages on any e35 leg since the deploy' - which is false; the correct answer is 8. It was caught only because RULE ONE's positive control was run (query one leg with no `since`) before trusting the quiet. A reader who skips that control gets a clean, plausible, wrong denominator.

THE ROUTE IS ALSO A PROBE TARGET. docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json carries a probe on OI-20260830-E35-GEOMETRY-SHIPPED-TO-9-LEGS-NOT-YET-LIVE-VERIFIED whose own `checks` field already records the adjacent hazard on /api/bot/trades/closed: `openedAt` is compared lexicographically, which is chronological ONLY because that route serves a +00:00 offset, and 'a switch to a Z suffix would silently break it'. This finding is that same seam from the other side - the offset form the ROUTE serves is the form a QUERY STRING cannot carry unencoded.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER: (a) the route publishes a never-collapsed `since_state` (applied / not_requested / ignored_unparseable) the way /api/bot/db/table/{name} publishes `filter_state`, so a dropped filter is visible in the payload and `count` can be read honestly; OR (b) an unparseable `since` returns 400 rather than an empty 200. Verified by re-running the three-arm measurement above against the live VM and showing the '+00:00' arm no longer renders identically to a genuine empty result. A unit test alone is not sufficient - the defect is in what a LIVE caller cannot distinguish.

items.title: e35's tp_r change is INERT on any trade where the 0.099 venue clamp is tighter than the declared tp_r, and nobody has measured how often that is
items.detail:
The placed target is min(cap_r, tp_r) where cap_r = 0.099 * entry / risk (src/runtime/tp_venue_cap.py, the single owner). So on a trade whose cap_r < tp_r the e35 tp_r value never reaches the wire, and the bracket is byte-identical to what the OLD 50R sentinel would have produced. That makes such a trade unable to verify the tp_r half of e35 however cleanly it closes - the cosmetic-change shape BL-20260730-DONCHIAN-COSMETIC-SHORT-CELLS names, arriving through a different door.

MEASURED LIVE 2026-09-01. Instance: real-money trade 5250 (bybit_2 / trend_donchian_xrp_4h / XRPUSDT short, package pkg-6ee82a43ed3f47df, opened 2026-08-30T23:46:39Z). Declared entry 1.3428, sl 1.38875714, tp 1.2098628 => risk 0.04595714, effective target 2.892634 R. cap_r = 0.099 * 1.3428 / 0.04595714 = 2.892634, reproducing the placed tp to 8 decimal places. The leg's live config carries tp_r: 3, so min(2.892634, 3) = the clamp: the e35 tp_r=3 was INERT on this trade and the same tp would have been placed at tp_r=50.

STATE THE POPULATION, because it is thin and it is the point. Order packages on the ten shipped e35 legs with createdAt >= 2026-08-30T14:05:00Z (the instant e35 half (a) was measured true on the running trader), include_paper=true: n=8, all priced. min(cap_r, tp_r) reproduces the effective target on ALL EIGHT - so the mechanism is behaving exactly as its owner module documents and this is NOT a bug report against that module. The clamp binds on 1 of 8; tp_r binds on 7. But that 7 is NOT reassurance: read against the live /api/bot/config, SEVEN of the ten legs still carry the tp_r: 50 SENTINEL (trend_donchian, trend_donchian_eth_4h, trend_donchian_sol_4h, trend_donchian_ada_4h, trend_donchian_avax_4h, htf_pullback_trend_2h, avax_pullback_2h), so on those the clamp is the ONLY thing setting the target and 'tp_r binds' cannot arise. Only THREE legs carry a changed tp_r (trend_donchian_xrp_4h=3, ada_pullback_2h=4, xrp_pullback_2h=3.0), and exactly ONE of them produced a package in the window - the one where the clamp bound. So the binding rate for the legs the change actually touches is measured over n=1.

cap_r > tp_r requires risk/entry < 0.099/tp_r; at tp_r=3 that is risk below 3.3% of entry. Trade 5250 sat at 3.42%, i.e. the clamp bound by a hair. Whether that is typical for these legs' ATR is exactly what is unmeasured.

=== UPDATE 2026-09-06 (MI-148) — THE BINDING RATE IS NO LONGER UNMEASURED, so this row's own title is now half false; do not re-quote it as an open measurement question. The INERTNESS half stands and this row stays OPEN on it.

Measured with the new instrument scripts/research/bracket_calibration_report.py (+ src/runtime/bracket_calibration.py), which grades a trade's RESTING take-profit in PERCENT-OF-ENTRY -- the basis on which 'is this the clamp?' is directly decidable, since TP_VENUE_CAP_PCT is 9.9% of entry. A target within 2% of the cap is recognised as clamp-bound.

POPULATION: closed, non-backtest, non-pairs `trades` rows, newest 1000 the diag endpoint returns, window 2026-08-09T22:50Z -> 2026-09-06T10:03Z, n=297 directional. Stratified by exit-price provenance and NEVER pooled:
  measured    n=82 graded -> clamp_bound_rate 0.2561
  estimated   n=180       -> clamp_bound_rate 0.3944
  unverified  n=7 (of 33) -> clamp_bound_rate 1.0000

Per leg the rate is bimodal, which is the more useful finding than any pooled figure: the 8 ict_scalp legs (n=162) read 0.0000 on EVERY leg, while the 20 donchian/pullback legs (n=102) read 0.80-1.00 with a median declared target of exactly 0.099. So the clamp does not bind 'sometimes' -- it binds essentially always on one family and never on the other.

AND THE INERTNESS IS WORSE THAN THIS ROW ASSUMED. On 12 donchian/pullback legs the declared target sits at quantile 1.0000 of realised exits (n as per docs/research/bracket-calibration-2026-09-06.md): not one trade in the window ended above it. Independently, over the 102 peak_gradeable position_telemetry rows, only 4 of 102 (3.9%) ever reached the 9.9% level even at the LOWER BOUND of MFE (peak_r_is_lower_bound=True on 168/168).

Full memo: docs/research/bracket-calibration-2026-09-06.md.
items.resolution_criteria: A measurement, over a stated population, of how often min(cap_r, tp_r) selects tp_r rather than cap_r on the THREE legs that carry a changed tp_r (trend_donchian_xrp_4h, ada_pullback_2h, xrp_pullback_2h) - not over all ten, since seven still carry the 50R sentinel and can only ever select the clamp. Reported as a rate with its denominator, over enough packages that n=1 is not the basis. If the clamp binds on most of them, the e35 tp_r change is largely inert on those legs and that conclusion is recorded (a decision either way closes this); if tp_r binds, the change is real and a live trade can verify it. Explicitly NOT sufficient: reading tp_venue_cap.py and reasoning about it - the module is correct and already documents the mechanism; what is missing is the rate.

items.title: probe_actions_log lists runs fine but reads 0 of 20 job logs on a GitHub runner, and its aggregate note collapses every HTTP cause into one count
items.detail:
FIRST REAL RUN OF THE READER, and it does not work. Measured 2026-09-01 in probes.yml run #32 (workflow_dispatch on main, GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest, docs/claude/PROBES.json generated_at 2026-09-01T05:38:50Z). Both probe_actions_log rows returned could_not_run / exit_2:
  gpu-burst-train.yml: '20 run(s) listed but NONE had readable logs (20 unread)'
  guards.yml:          '20 run(s) listed but NONE had readable logs (20 unread)'
So LISTING works - the API is reachable and the token authenticates - and LOG DOWNLOAD fails on 20 of 20, twice, on two unrelated workflows. 0/40.

THE HANDOFF'S HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED, and recording that matters more than the fix. The standing note said 'SUSPECT THE READER - api.github.com is 403 from a web sandbox'. That 403 is real but is NOT the cause here: this ran on a GitHub-hosted runner, not in a sandbox, and the run-listing calls succeeded from the same process with the same bearer. A session acting on the old hypothesis would chase sandbox egress and find nothing.

ALSO REFUTED: a missing permission. probes.yml declares `actions: read` explicitly, with a comment saying it exists for exactly these two probes.

CANDIDATE CAUSES, none asserted, because the note does not carry the evidence to choose between them: (a) GET /actions/jobs/{id}/logs answers 302 to a signed cross-host blob URL, and urllib.request.urlopen follows redirects while RE-SENDING the `Authorization: Bearer` header, which blob hosts reject - the classic trap, and the reader does no header stripping; (b) the `Accept: application/vnd.github+json` header on an endpoint that returns plain text via redirect; (c) log retention, which is ruled out for runs this recent. Corroborating but not decisive: mcp__github__get_job_logs returned HTTP 404 for the probes job itself minutes earlier in the same session, from a different client.

THE READER'S THREE-STATE CONTRACT BEHAVED CORRECTLY and should not be changed - it returned could_not_look rather than a false `fail`, which is the whole design and is why this is diagnosable at all.

CONSEQUENCE: OI-20260831-PROBE-READERS-SHIPPED-BUT-THE-ACTIONS-ONE-HAS-NEVER-RUN-FOR-REAL does NOT clear - its clears_when names a could_not_run as the failure signal, and the signal has now fired. The two rows it feeds (GPU-route/spend-gate and session-brief diff-scoping) remain unprobeable.
items.resolution_criteria: TWO THINGS, and the second is the one that generalises. (1) probe_actions_log returns a GRADED verdict (pass or fail) for at least one of its two rows in a committed docs/claude/PROBES.json, read from the results file rather than a local self-test against the fake server - which is what the reader already passes today and is exactly why this went unnoticed. (2) The aggregate note carries the DISTINCT HTTP causes seen, not just an unread COUNT: '20 unread' cannot distinguish 404 from 403 from 410-expired from a timeout, and those are different findings with different fixes - the collapsed-state defect this repo keeps paying for, occurring inside the reader built to avoid it. The per-job branch already computes the code (it even special-cases 410); it is discarded on the way up.

items.title: The generic DB explorer is unauthenticated and reaches device_tokens.token unredacted, while the dedicated /devices route is gated and returns only a suffix
items.detail: Measured 2026-09-01 from a sandbox session with NO credentials against https://ict-bot.duckdns.org. /api/bot/db/tables returns 200 and exposes 22 tables; /api/bot/db/table/device_tokens?limit=1 returns 200 with columns [id, token, platform, label, subscriptions, created_at, last_seen_at] -- the RAW token column. The dedicated /api/bot/devices route returns 401 AND deliberately emits only token_suffix, which is what establishes that public exposure was never the intent: two paths to one asset, one gated and one not. db_explorer.py's own docstring asserts the premise this violates -- 'No secrets live in either DB (credentials are env/config and redacted elsewhere)' -- the field-beats-comment shape. PROPORTION, stated rather than implied: device_tokens holds 0 rows today so nothing is leaking; it becomes live on first device registration, which is the Android app's only write to the bot; and an FCM registration token is a device identifier rather than a directly usable credential, since sending push additionally requires the FCM server key, which is not exposed here. The operator decided 2026-09-01 to archive the Android app off the live feed, which removes the PRODUCER and so the live risk -- but the ungated any-table path outlives that decision and is the actual defect. Population for the wider surface: /api/bot/{stats,config,positions,trades/closed,accounts/balances,order-packages,prop/fills,logs} all 200 unauthenticated; signals holds 2,273,237 rows, balance_snapshots 29,716, trades 5,288, order_packages 4,254. items.resolution_criteria: THREE things, and the third is the one that is easy to skip. (1) The Android app and the Streamlit dashboard no longer call the live API -- demonstrated by their absence from the consumer set, not by intent. (2) The repos/entry points are archived with a banner saying what replaced them and when, so a future session does not read them as live (the recurring-sessions.md precedent: a doc that called itself binding while nothing ran it). (3) Every CLAUDE.md and architecture reference that names Streamlit or the Android app as a live consumer is corrected -- the bot repo's CLAUDE.md currently opens its dashboard section with 'consumed by two front-ends', and the API table annotates routes with 'Streamlit dashboard' / 'Android app' throughout. items.title: config/strategy_changelog.json records squeeze_breakout_4h DEMOTED live->shadow (Tier-3, operator-approved, 2026-06-01) while config/strategies.yaml sets execution: live EXPLICITLY today
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-01 from CURRENT FILE STATE (see the population caveat below — the history is NOT available in this clone). config/strategy_changelog.json carries, under squeeze_breakout_4h, a 2026-06-01 entry: 'DEMOTED execution: live -> shadow ... Tier-3, operator-approved', citing 60 closed trades at 0% win and net -20R, and saying 'Re-promote only on a fresh net-positive window.' Read through the canonical loader (scripts/ml/strategy_review_packet.load_strategies_yaml, i.e. the `strategies:` wrapper key — reading the raw YAML top level returns nothing and is how this was first misread), config/strategies.yaml today has squeeze_breakout_4h with execution: 'live' PRESENT AND EXPLICIT, and enabled: True. ⚠️ STATE THE POPULATION / BLAST RADIUS: it is routed to exactly ONE account, bybit_1, which is mode: live but account_class: PAPER. So this is NOT real money, and describing it as 'running live' without that qualifier overstates it. ⚠️ WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and must not be asserted: WHEN or WHY the config value changed, and whether a later operator decision re-promoted it and simply was not logged. This session's clone is SHALLOW (git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository = true; 58 reachable commits, earliest 2026-08-31), so `git log -- config/strategies.yaml` returns 1 commit and any history-based claim from here is an artifact of clone depth rather than a fact. An investigating session must `git fetch --unshallow` first. This is a RECURRENCE of a class already twice fixed on other surfaces — BL-20260814-MATRIX-STATUS-CONTRADICTS-LIVE-CONFIG-ON-SIX-LEVER-CELLS (coverage matrix vs config) and BL-20260823-STALE-COMMENT-CLAIMS-PROP-VARIANTS-ARE-SHADOW (a money-path comment vs config), both resolved. That it has now recurred on the CANONICAL DECISION RECORD is the finding: the two earlier fixes were per-surface, and nothing compares the decision record against the config it is supposed to govern. Related: the changelog's most recent ENTRY is dated 2026-07-28 (53 entries, earliest 2026-05-06), so the record has not been written to in over a month while Tier-3 decisions demonstrably continued — which is C4 of the operating-layer build plan.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) the config and the record are reconciled — a session establishes on UNSHALLOWED history whether a re-promotion decision was taken, and then either logs that decision to strategy_changelog.json (if it was operator-approved and merely unrecorded) or restores execution: shadow (if the demotion was never reversed). ⚠️ Both directions are Tier-3 and need explicit operator approval — do NOT flip the execution gate on inference. AND (b) an executable check compares the decision record's latest execution verdict per strategy against config/strategies.yaml and FAILS on a divergence, so this class stops needing a human to notice it on a third surface. A one-off reconciliation without (b) closes the instance and leaves the class, which is what the two prior fixes did.

items.title: work_phase_ping.py pings per-object on `accepted`, so any bulk lifecycle change pages the operator once per row
items.source: Found while choosing the migration's lifecycle mapping; navigated around rather than fixed, because fixing it was outside Phase C's scope.
items.why_it_matters: scripts/ops/work_phase_ping.py sets PING_WORTHY = {in_flight, waiting, done, accepted} and emits one queued notification per transition, with no batching and no cap. Its own docstring states the contract as 'events on STATE CHANGES, never on activity' -- but a BULK edit is activity even though it is made of state changes, and the code cannot tell the two apart. Phase C's migration would have queued 238 pings had `kept_open` been mapped to `accepted` as the design's 'dormant or accepted' wording invites; it was mapped entirely to `dormant` partly for this reason, which is a workaround, not a fix. The next bulk lifecycle edit -- e.g. accepting a batch of triaged rows, which is a normal thing to want to do -- hits this with no warning. Measured control: after migrating 575 objects, `work_phase_ping.py --base origin/main --head HEAD` reported exactly 1 ping-worthy transition (the Phase C object's own ready->in_flight), confirming both the mechanism works and that the storm was avoided by the mapping alone.
items.resolution_criteria: work_phase_ping.py either (a) collapses N transitions in one invocation into a single summary ping above some threshold, or (b) refuses/warns above a threshold so a human decides, or (c) records why per-row paging on a bulk edit is correct. Verified by running it over a ref pair containing >20 transitions into a ping-worthy state and observing the queued row count in docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl.
items.next_action: Add a threshold to work_phase_ping.py::main that summarises rather than enumerates above N transitions.

items.title: econ-calendar-produce's auto-merge PR #10398 has sat mergeable_state=dirty since 2026-08-29 — that day's PIT snapshots never landed and nothing alarmed for 3 days
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-01T12:15Z. PR #10398 'chore(m1): economic-calendar PIT snapshots (auto)', head automation/econ-calendar-33232352515-1, created 2026-08-29T03:49:57Z, updated_at IDENTICAL to created_at (never touched since), state open, mergeable_state 'dirty' (= merge conflict, NOT merely behind), 62,524 additions / 143 deletions across 3 files. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE PR: this is the `.github/actions/commit-to-main` path with verify-merged, which several producers use to land data on main. A conflicted auto-merge PR means (a) that run's data never landed, (b) its verify-merged step failed or timed out, and (c) NOBODY NOTICED FOR THREE DAYS. That is the 'a mechanism that looks armed and is not' class this repo has repeatedly paid for. ⚠️ WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and must not be asserted: whether the SNAPSHOTS themselves were recovered by a later run. econ-calendar-produce regenerates from ALL COMMITTED captures, and this PR *is* the commit of those captures — so if it never merged they were never committed and a later regen could not include them. That is a reasonable inference, NOT a measurement; a later schedule run did succeed (2026-09-01T01:22Z), which is consistent with either outcome. Someone must actually diff the PIT log against the captures. ⚠️ WHY A CONFLICT AT ALL: econ-calendar regenerates a SHARED append-only .jsonl, so two runs touch the same lines — hence the 62k-line diff. The strategy-review-packets workflow added 2026-09-01 writes to a DATE-STAMPED directory (comms/strategy_reviews/<UTC-date>/) and so is structurally far less prone to this, but it uses the SAME action and inherits the same silent-abandonment failure mode.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH: (a) #10398 is resolved or closed with its data reconciled — establish by MEASUREMENT, not inference, whether those captures are present in comms/macro/econ_calendar_snapshots.jsonl today; and (b) an abandoned auto-merge PR becomes VISIBLE rather than silent. A verify-merged timeout already fails the run, and claude-run-failure-alert watches econ-calendar-produce — so establish FIRST why that did not surface it (did the run fail and the alert not fire, or did the run pass because verify-merged was not set on that invocation?). Fixing the alarm without answering that would be treating the symptom.
