items.title: The strategy-review index tests spelled the action vocabulary by hand in UPPERCASE, so 7/7 passed while the live filter matched nothing and opened a 105-file PR
items.detail:
RECURRENCE of the class CLAUDE.md already records for the pairs soak ('the tests that should have caught it declared their own order_packages with a schema production does not have -- so they passed against a fictional table'). Same shape, different surface, two weeks later.

WHAT HAPPENED. .github/workflows/strategy-review-packets.yml selected which review packets to commit with `[r for r in rows if (r.get('proposed_action') or 'HOLD') != 'HOLD']`. scripts/ml/strategy_review_packet.py's Decision.action emits LOWERCASE -- hold/kill/demote_shadow/tune/promote (verified: 23 assignment sites, zero uppercase). The uppercase spelling came from this repo's own PROSE, which renders the vocabulary as KILL/DEMOTE_SHADOW/TUNE/HOLD/PROMOTE in CLAUDE.md's /api/bot/strategies/{name}/review row and in the workflow's own header comment. So the comparison matched nothing, all 52 graded strategies counted as actionable, and the first live run opened a 105-file / 5,932-addition PR against a design whose entire point is committing packets selectively. It merged (#10652).

WHY THE TESTS DID NOT CATCH IT. tests/test_strategy_review_index.py's _rows() fixture was written by hand as [{'proposed_action': 'HOLD'}, {'proposed_action': 'KILL'}, ...] and by_action was asserted as {'HOLD': 2, 'KILL': 1, 'TUNE': 1}. Every assertion was internally consistent and every one described a producer that does not exist. 7/7 green.

A SECOND DEFECT IN THE SAME ARTIFACT, found by the same read. The index row builder read packet.get('n_closed')/win_rate/expectancy/pnl_total; those live under packet['headline'] (Headline.to_dict()), not at the top level. Measured on the merged INDEX.json: 52 of 52 rows null on all four fields. The per-strategy packets were fine -- build_packet was never broken -- so only the index, i.e. the DENOMINATOR artifact, was wrong.

FIX (this PR). The generator owns NO_ACTION_VERDICT + is_actionable(), stamps `actionable` per row, and publishes `no_action_verdict` + an `actionable` count on the envelope, so no consumer spells the value at all; the workflow reads that flag and REFUSES (naming the cause) if the VM's generator predates it. is_actionable(None) is True deliberately -- an ungraded row is 'we did not look', not 'hold'. The fixture now IMPORTS NO_ACTION_VERDICT, and a positive control asserts the constant is a value the decision matrix can actually emit.

TRANSFERABLE LESSON, which is why this is filed rather than just fixed: a test fixture that SPELLS a producer's vocabulary is an assertion about the producer that nothing checks. Derive the fixture from the producer's own constant, or add a positive control that the spelling is reachable. Prose is not a source for an enum value -- field beats comment applies to test data as much as to config.

POSTSCRIPT, ADDED THE SAME HOUR: the CI guard artifact-validity rejected THIS ROW on its first push -- severity 'P2' is not in the accepted vocabulary (critical|high|medium|low). So the row documenting 'do not spell a producer's vocabulary by hand' was itself filed by spelling a consumer's vocabulary by hand, from a severity convention used elsewhere in this repo's prose. Recorded rather than quietly corrected: the class is stickier than a single fix, which is the argument for the executable check named in resolution_criteria rather than for another careful author.
items.resolution_criteria: Resolved by this PR for this surface. The class stays open in the sense that any future hand-spelled fixture reintroduces it; the durable check is the positive control pattern (assert the literal appears in the producer). No CI guard enforces that generally -- if this recurs a third time, that guard is the fix, not another fixture correction.

items.title: RECURRENCE: health-review-backlog.json stopped round-tripping ONE DAY after the same defect was repaired — a row spliced in with ensure_ascii=True + inline separators, which makes append_row REFUSE every future write
items.detail:
⚠️ THIS IS A RECURRENCE AND THAT IS THE FINDING. Phase C's PR body (#10657, 2026-09-01) records repairing this exact class: 'a splice into health-review-backlog.json left a bare comma on its own line, breaking detect_format — the next session to call append_row would have been refused outright'. It recurred within ~24h, same file, different session, different mechanism. The earlier fix repaired the INSTANCE and nothing prevented the CLASS.

WHAT BROKE. main advanced to 05eac09c (#10663, merged by a legacy 'Live trades on Alpaca portfolio account' session). That commit updated row BL-20260823-ALPACA-LIVE-IS-EXEMPT-FROM-BOTH-DETECTORS-THAT-WATCH-IT by hand rather than through append_row, producing a region serialised with ensure_ascii=True (\u26a0\ufe0f where the file uses literal ⚠️) and inline separators where the file uses indent=2. detect_format then reproduced no candidate byte-for-byte and backlog_append raised FormatNotReproducible — which by design REFUSES TO WRITE.

BLAST RADIUS, and it is wider than CI. Any session calling append_row was refused outright, so the repo's own 'file it to the backlog' instruction could not be followed by anyone. It also failed pytest-run on THREE open PRs simultaneously (#10660, #10662, #10664) — including one that does not touch the file at all, which is what proved it was the base and not the branches.

POPULATION, measured: exactly 1 of 1065 items was non-canonical; 10 escaped \uXXXX sequences, all in that one row. So the repair is 2 insertions / 1 deletion, NOT a reformat — content asserted byte-equal as data (json.loads before == after, and the id order unchanged) before writing. A full reformat here would have re-attributed ~21k lines, which is BL-20260820-BACKLOG-APPEND-REFORMATS-AND-REATTRIBUTES.

⚠️ WHY 'resolved' IS ONLY HALF HONEST. The FILE is repaired and append_row works again. The CLASS is not prevented: nothing stops the next hand-edit, and this is now the second occurrence in two days. A CI guard asserting the three live backlogs round-trip WOULD have caught it at the merge that introduced it instead of on three unrelated PRs — tests/test_backlog_append.py::test_the_live_backlogs_all_round_trip exists and DID catch it, but only in pytest-run, which runs after the damage is on main. Filed as its own follow-up rather than claimed here.
items.tier: 1 — tooling/data repair; no order path, no runtime
items.resolution_criteria: OBSERVED, and it is what closed this row: scripts/ops/backlog_append.py::append_row successfully wrote to docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json (item count 1065 -> 1066) and detect_format reproduced the file byte-for-byte afterwards. ⚠️ The criterion is the WRITER WRITING, not a format check passing — a check passing is weaker evidence than the tool the check exists to protect actually doing its job. ⚠️ This criterion covers the FILE only. It does NOT cover the class recurring, which is deliberately a separate row (BL-20260901-NO-PRE-MERGE-GUARD-ON-BACKLOG-ROUND-TRIP) so that closing this one cannot be read as having prevented anything.

items.tier: 1 — a CI guard; no order path
items.title: The backlog round-trip is only checked in pytest-run, i.e. AFTER a breaking merge is on main and failing every open PR
items.detail:
tests/test_backlog_append.py::test_the_live_backlogs_all_round_trip DOES catch a non-canonical backlog — it caught 2026-09-01's — but it lives in pytest-run, the ~15-minute job. So the sequence is: a hand-edit merges to main, main is broken, and the signal arrives on OTHER sessions' unrelated PRs. Measured that day: three open PRs (#10660, #10662, #10664) all went red simultaneously, one of which does not touch the file, and in the meantime append_row REFUSED EVERY WRITE repo-wide — so the standing instruction 'file it to the backlog, never by hand' could not be followed by anyone.

⚠️ THIS IS THE PREVENTION HALF OF A TWICE-SEEN CLASS. Phase C (#10657) repaired the same defect on 2026-09-01 and it recurred within ~24h (BL-20260901-BACKLOG-ROUND-TRIP-BROKEN-AGAIN-BY-A-HAND-WRITTEN-SPLICE). Repairing the instance twice without adding a prevention is the pattern CLAUDE.md's 'we still keep running into the same fuck ups' directive names.

The check is ~10 lines and has no dependencies beyond what backlog_append already imports, so cost is not the obstacle — it simply was never registered in scripts/ci/run_guards.py where it would run in ~1s on every PR.
items.resolution_criteria: A guard registered in scripts/ci/run_guards.py asserts all three live review backlogs round-trip through detect_format, AND it has been SHOWN TO FAIL against a deliberately planted non-canonical row — not merely shown to pass on a clean tree. ⚠️ A guard that has only ever been green is indistinguishable from one that cannot fire; this repo's own guards carry self-tests for exactly that reason, so a passing run on today's clean file does NOT close this.

updates.note:
RESOLVED — and closed on the clause the row said a green run does NOT satisfy.

CLAUSE 1 — a guard registered in scripts/ci/run_guards.py asserts the live backlogs round-trip through detect_format. PRESENT at scripts/ci/run_guards.py:415, `python3 scripts/ops/backlog_append.py --check-live` (landed 065ef2b2, #10665). Run in this session on the clean tree: exit 0, 'backlog round-trip: OK — 3 live backlog(s) reproduce byte-for-byte'.

CLAUSE 2 — SHOWN TO FAIL against a deliberately planted non-canonical row. DONE, not asserted. I copied the three live backlogs into a scratch root, re-serialised health-review-backlog.json with indent=3 + ensure_ascii=True (a combination no entry in _CANDIDATES reproduces), and called check_live_backlogs(<that root>). Result: exit 1 with `::error::a live review backlog does not round-trip:` naming the file and the remedy. So the guard is demonstrably able to fire; it is not a permanently-green check. This is exactly the 'a guard that has only ever been green is indistinguishable from one that cannot fire' bar the row set.

⚠️ ONE GAP FOUND WHILE VERIFYING, and it is NOT covered by this row's criterion — filed rather than folded in: backlog_append.LIVE_BACKLOGS names THREE files (health, performance, ml) while FOUR review backlogs exist on disk — docs/claude/research-review-backlog.json is not checked. The criterion says 'all three live review backlogs' and is literally satisfied; the fourth backlog was created after the criterion was written. See BL-20260901-BACKLOG-ROUND-TRIP-GUARD-COVERS-3-OF-4-LIVE-BACKLOGS.

items.opened_by: claude (GLD close-failure investigation, spawned from the live Telegram page)
items.source: Live alpaca_paper GLD long 39.0 paged '🛑 Position CLOSE failing — won't flatten', streak 12 → 30, 17:28–17:37 ET on 2026-09-01.
items.title: RECURRENCE of BL-20260708-ALPACA-CLOSE-QTY-AVAILABLE: the qty_available-gated flatten was only ever wired into the RTH path, so the extended-hours close still races share release
items.description: MECHANISM. 16:00-20:00 ET is extended hours, so AlpacaClient.close() routes to _close_extended_hours(). That path cancelled the resting bracket, waited for the symbol's OPEN-ORDERS list to clear, then fired a SINGLE POST /v2/orders. Waiting on the open-orders list is the wrong signal, and this repo documents exactly why in _await_qty_available's own docstring: 'Alpaca drops a cancelled order from status=open a beat BEFORE it restores the position's qty_available'. So the POST raced the release and Alpaca rejected it ('insufficient qty available for order (requested: 39, available: 0)') -> retCode 1 -> a REAL close failure -> streak++ -> a page, every 30s tick, all session. WHY IT IS A RECURRENCE AND THAT IS THE FINDING. BL-20260708-ALPACA-CLOSE-QTY-AVAILABLE named this exact remedy ('POLL the position's qty_available ... until it == qty before issuing the DELETE, with a longer bound') and was marked RESOLVED on 2026-08-16. It was resolved for ONE call site: _await_qty_available was invoked from exactly one place, inside the regular-hours loop. The extended-hours sibling was never covered, and nothing checked that the fix reached every path that closes a position. The earlier row even predicted the blast radius -- 'could also strand a REAL alpaca_live position on a slow cancel, not just this paper orphan' -- and alpaca_live has since been routed real money. FIXED IN PR #10666 (draft, Tier-2, awaiting operator OK): _close_extended_hours now awaits the real release, and on an insufficient-qty rejection re-cancels (catching a freshly re-armed protective OCO) and retries within a bounded window, logging the residual open orders on give-up so the failure is self-diagnosing. ALPACA_EXT_PLACE_RETRY_S <= 0 restores the single-shot POST. ⚠️ THE CLASS IS STILL UNPREVENTED. Nothing asserts that every path which flattens a position goes through the same share-release discipline; a third close path added tomorrow would repeat this. That prevention is NOT claimed by #10666 and is the follow-up half of this row.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH halves. (a) INSTANCE: #10666 merges and deploys, and a subsequent extended-hours close on an Alpaca equity position is OBSERVED succeeding -- read from the journal / the close-failure banner, not from a passing test. A test is not an observation of the live path. (b) CLASS: an executable check exists that fails when a position-flattening path does not go through the qty_available gate -- so a third close path cannot silently repeat this a third time. Closing on (a) alone re-creates exactly the state this row is filed about: the 2026-07 row was closed on its instance and the sibling path stayed broken for seven weeks.

items.opened_by: claude (GLD close-failure investigation, spawned from the live Telegram page)
items.source: Same GLD incident: the operator received a continuous stream of 'Position CLOSE failing' CRITICALs rather than a bounded few.
items.title: The close-failure pager repeats on a modulo of the streak, so its rate is set by the exit-loop tick and never widens or caps — ~160 pages per wedged session
items.description: MECHANISM. order_monitor's repeat cadence for the 'Position CLOSE failing — won't flatten' alert was a fixed modulo of the consecutive-failure streak (_streak % _after == 0, _after=3). That ties the PAGE RATE to the TICK RATE: at the EXIT_LOOP_INTERVAL_SECONDS default of 30s it is one page every 90s for as long as the position stays wedged, never widening and never capped -- roughly 160 pages across one extended-hours session. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND NOISE. This is the desensitized-alarm P1 CLAUDE.md names as a bug in itself, on the SAME channel reserved for an unprotected position. The repo has already paid for this exact shape once: 202 of 376 CRITICAL/ERROR rows in one measured window were a single un-latched ib_target_naked alarm (BL-20260823-TARGET-NAKED-COOLDOWN-RESETS-ON-EVERY-RESTART). A second, independent instance of the same failure in a different subsystem is the finding. SECOND-ORDER DEFECT: because the cadence is a modulo of the tick, re-tuning EXIT_LOOP_INTERVAL_SECONDS silently re-tunes the pager. Two knobs, one of them invisible. FIXED IN PR #10666 (draft, Tier-2): paging is now TIME-based with an exponentially widening interval (300s floor, doubling, clamped hourly), decoupled from tick rate. It deliberately NEVER goes silent -- a wedged position keeps pinging at the max interval, because the failure this subsystem exists to end is the SILENT retry loop. Same 4h wedge: 7 pages instead of 160; first page still at the 3rd consecutive failure, unchanged. ⚠️ WHY IT SHIPPED: the pre-existing tests only ever drove the FIRST alert, so the repeat cadence was entirely uncovered. The gap was in the test population, not in anyone's reading of the code.
items.resolution_criteria: #10666 merges and deploys, AND a real wedged-close episode on the live fleet is OBSERVED producing a widening page sequence rather than a fixed-cadence one -- counted from /api/bot/logs?level=error over the episode's own window, with the episode's duration stated so the count has a denominator. A passing unit test is NOT this observation. ⚠️ Do NOT close this on 'the pages stopped': pages stopping is equally consistent with the close path being fixed and the position never wedging again, which would tell you nothing about the pager. The clearing evidence needs a wedge that actually happened.

items.source: Read while working the merge queue; grounded in .github/workflows/claude-run-failure-alert.yml:180 rather than recalled.
items.title: claude-run-failure-alert fires on only 3 of GitHub's ~7 run conclusions, so a workflow that never STARTS (startup_failure) is silent
items.description: The alert's `if:` is `conclusion == 'failure' || 'cancelled' || 'timed_out'`. GitHub's conclusion set also includes `startup_failure`, `action_required`, `stale` and `neutral`. None of those alerts. THE SERIOUS ONE IS `startup_failure`: the workflow never ran at all -- invalid YAML, a bad `uses:` ref, a secret unresolvable at parse time. That is a MORE total failure than `failure` (which at least means steps executed), and it is exactly the state in which a scheduled job silently stops doing its job. `action_required` (waiting on manual approval) and `stale` (abandoned) are the same shape: the run did not do its work and nothing says so. ⚠️ THE COMMENT ABOVE THE FILTER STATES A POPULATION IT DOES NOT HAVE: it reads 'success and skipped never alert', enumerating two exceptions, when the un-covered set is at least six. A reader checking the reasoning would conclude the coverage is complete. That is the unstated-denominator error this repo already has a name for, sitting in the comment rather than the code. WHY IT MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY: this workflow is the thing that notices when OTHER scheduled workflows die, and OI-20260901-SCHEDULED-PROBES-AND-DUE-LIST-HAVE-NEVER-FIRED-ON-CRON already records two workflows that are merged, enabled, and have never once fired. A watcher blind to `startup_failure` is blind to precisely that condition.
items.resolution_criteria: The filter covers every conclusion that means THE RUN DID NOT DO ITS WORK (at minimum `startup_failure` and `action_required`), the comment states the ACTUAL un-covered set rather than an example of it, AND the added coverage is SHOWN to fire -- a run forced to `startup_failure` (e.g. a deliberately invalid workflow on a scratch branch) produces the alert. ⚠️ Do NOT close on the `if:` expression being widened: a filter that has only ever been evaluated against `success` is indistinguishable from one that cannot fire, which is the same standard BL-20260901-NO-PRE-MERGE-GUARD-ON-BACKLOG-ROUND-TRIP was held to.

items.source: scripts/ops/render_session_brief.py:59-68, read directly.
items.title: render_session_brief resolves its three registers CWD-relative and swallows the miss, so a brief rendered from the wrong directory says 'nothing is due'
items.description: `_OPEN_ITEMS`/`_RECURRENCE`/`_CYCLE_PRIORITY` are bare `Path("docs/claude/...")` -- CWD-relative, not anchored to `__file__` or a repo root. `_load()` then catches `OSError` (which includes FileNotFoundError) and returns `{}`. SO THE TWO STATES COLLAPSE: 'we could not find the register' and 'the register is empty' render identically, and the rendered SESSION BRIEF reads as *nothing is due*. That is the dangerous direction, and it lands on the one surface that reaches a session BEFORE it acts -- CLAUDE.md's brief is inlined precisely because hooks do not run on Claude Code on the web and CI guards fire after the wrong work is built. A silently-empty brief does not degrade the mechanism, it inverts it. THE REPO ALREADY FORBIDS THIS CLASS ELSEWHERE: `canonical-db-resolver` exists because a CWD-relative `trade_journal.db` seeded stray duplicate journals under each process's working directory, and `silent-empty-guard` exists for the broad-except-returning-empty half. This site has both defects at once and is covered by neither guard. ⚠️ NOT OBSERVED FAILING -- the renderer is invoked from the repo root today, so this is a latent defect, not a live incident. It is filed at that strength deliberately: what makes it worth fixing is that when it does fire it is SILENT, not that it is firing now.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH halves, because either alone leaves the failure silent. (a) The three paths resolve from an anchor that does not depend on CWD (repo root via `__file__`, or the existing canonical resolver if one fits). (b) A register that CANNOT BE READ is distinguishable from one that is EMPTY -- the brief must say which, rather than rendering a confident 'nothing due'. Verified by rendering from a DIFFERENT working directory and seeing the brief either resolve correctly or announce that it could not look; a passing render from the repo root proves nothing, since that is the path that already works.

items.title: send_ping --kind returned 1 when src.runtime.claude_ping could not be imported, so opting into Format B meant losing the ping outright on a broken tree
items.detail: scripts/notify_on_pull.py states the invariant verbatim: 'No imports from src.runtime.* so a broken trader doesn't break the ping channel.' scripts/send_ping.py's own docstring calls itself 'the canonical producer -- every other process should drop through here'. #10669 added a --kind path to send_ping.py whose ImportError guard did logger.error(...) then return 1, so any producer that opted into Format B lost its ping ENTIRELY on a tree where src/runtime is broken -- exactly the tree an operator most needs to hear about. WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH A ROW rather than a quiet fix: the same change got the identical question RIGHT one layer down. claude_ping's limiter deliberately SENDS when its state file is unreadable, with a test named test_an_unreadable_limiter_SENDS and the reasoning written out ('a broken limiter that suppressed is indistinguishable from a quiet day'). The author applied the rule to the STATE FILE and missed the MODULE IMPORT in the same function. The general form: on a notification path every dependency needs the fail-loud direction, not just the one whose failure you happened to be thinking about. FIXED same day: the guard now warns and sends the body UNFORMATTED (why/unproven appended as plain prefixed lines) rather than dropping it, and the degraded shape is deliberately NOT Format B -- no icon, no indent -- so it cannot be mistaken for the canonical shape and does not become a second renderer. record_sent is gated on whether formatting actually happened, so a degraded ping records no send against the limiter. Three tests pin the direction in tests/test_send_ping.py. CAVEAT ON THE FIX: class gating is unavailable on the degraded path too, so a lifecycle BURST on a broken tree would not be collapsed. Sending is the safe direction there and the condition is rare, but it is a real gap, stated rather than hidden.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED on merge of the fix. Re-opens if a future producer path reintroduces a hard failure on an unavailable formatter, or if the degraded fallback ever grows into a second Format-B-shaped renderer.

items.title: The M7 decision packet grades the whole fleet HOLD by construction: a 7-day window cannot reach the n>=20 evidence floor, so 52/52 legs are ungradeable and the cron will re-emit actionable=0 every day
items.detail: STATE THE POPULATION: the committed 2026-09-01 index (comms/strategy_reviews/2026-09-01/INDEX.json), all 52 enabled strategies, window 7 days as set by .github/workflows/strategy-review-packets.yml (WINDOW_DAYS: '7', wrapper default ACTION_WINDOW_DAYS:-7). Measured: graded 52, actionable 0, by_action {'hold': 52}. n_closed was 0 for 34 legs, 1-4 for 14, 5-19 for 4, and NEVER EXCEEDED 8; the fleet closed 50 trades in total over the window. The generator forces HOLD below MIN_CLOSED_FOR_ACTION = 20 (scripts/ml/strategy_review_packet.py, the PB-20260630-004 floor, which is CORRECT -- a real-money KILL off 1-5 trades is noise). So 52/52 sat under the floor and NO leg could produce a KILL/DEMOTE whatever its PnL. This is not a fleet in good health: 13 of those legs are LOSING money and carry -35446.19 of provenance-trusted pnl_total between them (the packet excludes rows whose pnl provenance is not measured/estimated, so this is not a fabricated-mark figure). ARITHMETIC: at a 7-day window a leg needs ~3 closes/day to be gradeable, against a fleet-wide 50 closes/week -- so the floor is unreachable for every leg, every run, indefinitely. NEITHER COMPONENT IS WRONG ON ITS OWN, which is why this survived review: the floor is deliberate and defended, the window is a reasonable default, and each was chosen without reference to the other. The defect lives at the seam. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE MEASURED CONSTRAINT (DECISION): Phase F/C3 shipped the cron, the committed path and now a reader, and the decision surface still proposes nothing -- so the constraint is not moved by the plumbing alone. WHAT IS ALREADY MITIGATED, so this row is not read as worse than it is: the generator now publishes min_closed_for_action + per-row below_evidence_floor, and GET /api/bot/strategy-reviews reports an `evidence` block with floor_state, so 'nothing needs attention' and 'nothing could be graded' are no longer indistinguishable. That makes the condition VISIBLE; it does not fix it.
items.resolution_criteria: A committed INDEX.json in which at least one strategy is graded at or above MIN_CLOSED_FOR_ACTION -- i.e. evidence.floor_state reads partly_gradeable or all_gradeable rather than none_gradeable -- reached by an operator-approved decision on the window/floor pair rather than by silently widening the window. NOT resolved by a run that merely emits an action; a KILL fired off a window widened far enough to make anything gradeable is the same low-n hazard the floor exists to prevent, one level up. The decision needs to state what evidence a KILL badge should rest on, since window and floor are only meaningful together.

items.title: GET /api/bot/strategy-reviews makes the committed decision record reachable, but nothing renders it -- a route nobody calls is the same written-and-never-read defect one hop out
items.detail: Phase F/C3 closed the grep-verified gap that comms/strategy_reviews/ had ZERO readers by adding GET /api/bot/strategy-reviews. STATED PLAINLY SO IT IS NOT OVERSOLD: a route is not a reader. Today the only consumer is the test suite -- the Svelte SPA and the Streamlit dashboard both render the per-strategy /api/bot/strategies/{name}/review card and neither knows the fleet index exists, so a human still cannot see 'what did the fleet propose today' anywhere. That is the same class the route was built to close (provenance-consumer-guard: a signal written and never read is worse than a missing one), moved one hop rather than eliminated. It is a REAL improvement regardless -- the committed path is now reachable over the Caddy HTTPS host and the record is durable and greppable from the repo by any session -- but the chain evidence -> packet -> DECISION is not complete until something a human looks at shows the badge, which is the whole of C3's purpose. NOTE FOR WHOEVER BUILDS THE PANEL: render evidence.floor_state beside actionable, never actionable alone; a panel showing '0 actions proposed' over an ungradeable fleet reports a clean bill of health for a fleet nobody could grade, which is the defect the evidence block exists to prevent. Also render freshness -- a stale packet beside a confident KILL/PROMOTE badge is indistinguishable from a current one, the defect /api/bot/prop/status grew status_freshness for.
items.resolution_criteria: A consumer a human actually looks at renders the committed fleet index -- the day's proposed actions with graded as the visible denominator -- AND renders evidence.floor_state and freshness beside the action count. A consumer that renders only the action count does NOT resolve this; it reintroduces the unstated-denominator error in the surface built to end it.

items.title: comms/strategy_reviews/2026-09-01/ carries all 52 packets though its own index says actionable=0, because it landed from the run whose selector matched the wrong verdict case
items.detail: The workflow's contract is INDEX always, full packets only where an action is proposed (52 strategies x daily would be ~19,000 files a year). The one committed day does not match it: comms/strategy_reviews/2026-09-01/ holds 105 files -- INDEX.json plus a .json and .md for all 52 strategies -- while its own INDEX reports actionable 0 and by_action {'hold': 52}. Cause is known and already fixed at source, not a live defect: the first run's selector compared Decision.action against uppercase 'HOLD' while the field emits lowercase, so every graded strategy counted as actionable and the run opened a 105-file PR. #10653 fixed the selector and the generator now publishes `actionable` per row so no consumer spells the verdict at all. NOT HARMFUL and deliberately left rather than swept: the extra packets are correct content honestly attributable to the run that made them, and deleting history to make a directory match a contract it predates is the wrong instinct. WHAT IT COSTS: the single committed day is not a representative example of the selective-commit contract, so a reader inferring the contract FROM the artifact would infer the wrong one -- and it inflates the repo by ~104 files per day if the selector ever regresses. The new GET /api/bot/strategy-reviews reports packet_committed per row, so the discrepancy is at least visible rather than needing a directory listing to notice.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) a subsequent committed day demonstrates the contract -- INDEX.json plus packets ONLY for actionable rows -- which makes 2026-09-01 self-evidently the anomaly and closes this without touching history; or (b) an operator decides the pre-fix day should be pruned to its index and it is. (a) is preferred: it is evidence rather than tidying.

items.title: OPEN-ITEMS.json is mixed-serialisation (some rows ensure_ascii-escaped, some literal; indentation differs between rows) so no whole-file write reproduces it -- and unlike the three backlogs it has no append helper
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-01 while adding a row. docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json cannot be reproduced by ANY (indent, ensure_ascii, sort_keys, trailing-newline) combination: json.dumps(indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) differs from the original on 64 lines. Two independent causes, both from past writers disagreeing: (a) ENCODING -- some rows carry literal em-dashes while at least one 'observation' carries an escaped \u2014, so one file mixes ensure_ascii=True and False output; (b) INDENTATION -- earlier item objects put keys at 3 spaces while the LAST item puts them at 6, with a nested list closing at 8. THIS IS EXACTLY THE TRAP scripts/ops/backlog_append.py WAS BUILT FOR, one file over. That helper exists because a naive read-append-write on a backlog produced 21,307 insertions / 21,288 deletions and re-attributed every pre-existing row to the appending PR, turning unrelated diff-scoped guards red for rows the author never wrote. OPEN-ITEMS.json is edited by EVERY session at session end per CLAUDE.md, it is the file the CLAUDE.md SESSION BRIEF is rendered from, and it has NO equivalent helper -- so the same reformat-and-reattribute outcome is available to any session that reaches for the obvious idiom, and nothing warns. THE FILE STAYS VALID JSON AND THE ROW IS CORRECTLY ADDED, which is what makes it silent. WORKED AROUND, NOT FIXED, in this session: the row was inserted surgically as text before the items array's closing bracket, asserting afterwards that the parsed existing items were byte-identical and that only `items` and `updated_at` changed -- diff 20 insertions / 0 deletions. That is a technique a session has to reinvent, which is the gap.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) OPEN-ITEMS.json gains an append helper with the same refusal contract as backlog_append.py -- round-trip the ORIGINAL bytes against candidate serialisations and REFUSE to write when none reproduces them, never silently falling back to a default; or (b) the file is normalised to one serialisation in a single dedicated commit that touches nothing else (so the reformat is attributable to that commit rather than to whoever appends next) AND a guard or the helper keeps it that way. (b) alone is insufficient without something enforcing it, since the file has drifted at least twice already. NOT resolved by documenting 'remember ensure_ascii=False' -- backlog_append.py's own docstring is explicit that documenting it is not sufficient, because the repo already documents plenty that sessions miss.

items.title: docs/api-tier-policy.md pins the coverage NUMBER in CI but leaves the sentence that states the POPULATION unchecked, so the two have drifted apart
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-01 on branch claude/phase-f-c3-decision-prep (PR #10681), while fixing the pytest-run failure the counter drift caused. Source: docs/api-tier-policy.md lines 20-25, and `python3 scripts/check_api_tier_policy.py --list` run in-session on that branch.

THE HEADLINE IS PINNED AND THE PROSE UNDER IT IS NOT. tests/test_check_api_tier_policy.py::TestStatedCoverageIsTrue regex-matches exactly one line -- `**Coverage, computed rather than counted: N of M routes documented**` -- and asserts (N, M) against the enumerator. That worked: adding one route took the code to 103/103 while the banner still said 102/102, and CI caught it. I restated the banner to 103 of 103 (0 undocumented, verified with --list).

BUT THE POPULATION SENTENCE IMMEDIATELY BELOW IT IS UNCHECKED AND IS NOW WRONG TWICE OVER. It reads: 'the enumerator finds exactly those 96 with no false positives, and the only live routes it does not cover are the five defined outside routers/ -- GET /api/health (main.py) and FastAPI's four built-in docs routes.' Against the same run: the enumerator finds 103, not 96; and --list reports FOUR endpoints with no route under routers/ (GET /, GET /api/health, GET /login, GET /static/*), which is neither the number nor the set the sentence names.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND A STALE NUMBER. The banner's own wording is 'computed rather than counted' -- i.e. it advertises that this figure is machine-derived. A reader has no way to tell that the credibility stops at the bold line and the sentence that supplies its POPULATION is hand-written and unverified. That is the repo's own 'always state the population' rule failing at the point where the population is stated: a checked number sitting on an unchecked denominator reads as fully checked. The 96 also cannot be dismissed as a typo -- it is a plausible earlier measurement, so it looks like evidence.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT INTRODUCED BY #10681 -- that PR added one route and moved 102 to 103; the 96 and the 'five' predate it. Deliberately NOT fixed there: the sub-session that found this was scoped to getting CI green without changing the PR's substance, and a drive-by rewrite of an unrelated paragraph is exactly the scope creep that scope forbids. Filing rather than fixing is the disposition, not a punt.

PROPOSED FIX (small): have the same test that pins the number also pin the population sentence -- regex the enumerated total and the outside-routers/ endpoint list out of it and assert both against `enumerate_routes()` / the --list output, so the sentence cannot drift from the banner it explains. Restating the prose alone re-creates the same trap on the next route added.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH: (a) docs/api-tier-policy.md's population sentence states the enumerator's ACTUAL route total and the ACTUAL set of endpoints with no route under src/web/api/routers/, verified against a `scripts/check_api_tier_policy.py --list` run recorded in the closing PR; and (b) a test asserts that sentence's figures against the enumerator, so a future route addition reddens CI the same way the banner already does. (a) ALONE DOES NOT CLOSE THIS -- restating an unchecked sentence leaves it unchecked, and this row exists because it drifted while unchecked. A close that reports only 'the numbers are correct now' is not evidence; name the test.

items.title: The work store's blocked_on edges are 1.0% assessed (6 of 584), so E1 constraint diagnosis refuses to name a stage — the machinery is built and the input is missing
items.detail: STATE THE POPULATION: all 584 docs/claude/work/objects/*.yaml, 0 parse failures, measured 2026-09-01 by scripts/ops/constraint_readout.py. SIX objects carry any blocked_on edge; 578 carry an empty list, 576 of them stating blocked_on_basis: NOT_ASSESSED and 8 carrying no basis key at all. Assessed coverage is therefore 1.0% against the readout's declared 50% floor, so E1 verdicts `insufficient_basis` and NAMES NO STAGE. WHY THIS IS A FINDING AND NOT JUST THE MIGRATION WORKING AS DESIGNED: Phase C was right to migrate without inventing edges (a false blocker is worse than a missing one) and Phase D is right to refuse. But the operating model states that A1 depends on E1 and that E2 capability build is PULLED by a held-up stage, never self-started -- and neither is enforceable while the graph cannot name one. So the redesign's own forcing function is inert until edges are written, and nothing currently schedules that work: 578 dormant rows have no owner and no session is assigned to assess them. THE DANGEROUS READING, which the readout is built to block: a naive walk over these edges reports 'nothing is blocked' across 578 objects with total confidence, because an empty blocked_on renders identically whether it is a claim or an absence. WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS: assessed coverage over 50%, reached by sessions writing TRUE edges on rows they actually understand -- NOT by a bulk pass, which would reproduce the exact defect the migration avoided.
items.resolution_criteria: `python3 scripts/ops/constraint_readout.py` prints verdict `computed` with a named stage, over an assessed coverage above the declared 50% floor (today 6/584 = 1.0%). ⚠️ COVERAGE REACHED BY A BULK PASS DOES NOT COUNT and closes nothing: the edges must be written by sessions that understand the rows, because an invented edge is read by the computation as a true blocker. Read `assessed` beside `population` in docs/claude/CONSTRAINT.json -- never the verdict alone.
items.next_action: Decide (operator or a manager session) how edge assessment gets scheduled: most plausibly, any session touching a row's subject assesses that row's edges before leaving, and Phase G's pull rule is deferred until coverage clears the floor. Re-measure with `python3 scripts/ops/constraint_readout.py` -- it prints the denominator on every run.

scripts/ops/constraint_readout.py

items.title: A blocked_on object edge is graded by the target's lifecycle, but `waiting` covers both 'not delivered' and 'delivered, awaiting an observation' — so a delivered capability keeps propagating a false hold downstream
items.detail: STATE THE POPULATION: the 5 `kind: object` edges in the store on 2026-09-01, of which 3 pointed at a target whose lifecycle is `waiting`. MECHANISM: this repo deliberately holds an object at `waiting` when the thing is BUILT but its done_condition is an observation nobody has made -- WO-20260901-PHASE-A/B/C all sit there on exactly that reasoning, and that reasoning is correct for the object itself. It is wrong for its DEPENDENTS: a dependent needs the CAPABILITY, not the observation. MEASURED INSTANCE: WO-20260901-PHASE-D carried `object -> WO-20260901-PHASE-C` with the note 'E1 walks the typed blocked_on edges, which only exist once the carried rows are migrated'. The migration LANDED; Phase C is `waiting` solely on an unobserved cold-session read of the priority. So the graph reported Phase D blocked by a capability already delivered, which is precisely the false-blocker class the store's README warns about ('on 2026-09-01 three edges written as object: WO-PHASE-A ... made the graph report two phases blocked that were available') -- the SAME class recurring on the SAME day, in a different shape. Two more live edges have it now: PHASE-G -> PHASE-D and PHASE-H -> PHASE-B. INTERIM HANDLING, not a fix: constraint_readout.py publishes `holds_on_waiting_targets` with the caveat rather than resolving it into a state nobody measured. THE STRUCTURAL FIX is a schema question and deliberately not taken here -- either split `waiting` into 'waiting_on_delivery' vs 'waiting_on_observation' (a sixth/seventh lifecycle state, which the design warns against multiplying), or let an object edge name WHAT it needs from the target rather than the target alone.
items.resolution_criteria: A written decision in the operating-layer schema design saying whether a `kind: object` edge names the TARGET or the target's DELIVERABLE, and the store + scripts/ops/constraint_readout.py both reflecting it -- verified by `holds_on_waiting_targets` in docs/claude/CONSTRAINT.json becoming either empty or individually justified, rather than a standing caveat. ⚠️ The caveat disappearing because no object happens to be `waiting` that day does NOT close this: the ambiguity is structural, so it closes on the schema decision, not on a quiet reading.
items.next_action: Design decision on the operating-layer schema: does a `kind: object` edge name the target, or the target's deliverable? Until then, a session writing an object edge should say in its `note` what specifically it needs, so a reader can grade the hold by hand.

items.title: constraint_readout.py's first run filtered operator-owed items on `state` (the field is `status`) and reported all 5 TERMINAL items as decisions waiting on the operator — including one CLAUDE.md forbids raising
items.detail: Caught pre-merge, in the session that wrote it, by reading the register against src/runtime/operator_owed.py rather than trusting the rendered output. THE DEFECT: the readout's item-4 filter did `str(i.get('state','open')).lower() not in ('closed','resolved','done')`. docs/claude/operator-owed-register.json has no `state` key -- the field is `status`, with vocabulary OPEN_STATUSES = ('open','dispatched','snoozed') and TERMINAL_STATUSES = ('resolved','withdrawn') declared in src/runtime/operator_owed.py. So the default fired for every row and all 5 items rendered as OPEN when 4 are `resolved` and 1 is `withdrawn`. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE COUNT: one of the five is OO-20260825-DIAG-READ-TOKEN-ROTATION, which the operator CLOSED and which CLAUDE.md marks with a standing instruction not to raise again ('THE DIAG-TOKEN ROTATION QUESTION IS CLOSED -- DO NOT RAISE IT ... do not file a successor row'). A readout consumed as a work list had therefore manufactured five tasks for a human, one of them explicitly forbidden, and it read as computed. THE GENERAL FORM, which is the transferable part: this is the same class as the WIP ceiling being imported rather than restated -- a second, local copy of another module's vocabulary is free to drift, and here it never even matched. It is also sub-class C of the diagnostic-provenance defect (an unasserted denominator: the filter formed no real predicate and its output was indistinguishable from a filter that matched everything). FIXED by importing OPEN_STATUSES/TERMINAL_STATUSES from the grading module, bucketing an unrecognised status into its own third bucket rather than guessing, refusing to grade at all if the import fails, and a named regression assertion in the module's --self-test.
items.resolution_criteria: ALREADY MET, in the change that filed this row: constraint_readout.py imports OPEN_STATUSES/TERMINAL_STATUSES from src.runtime.operator_owed, refuses to grade at all if that import fails, buckets an unrecognised status separately rather than guessing, and carries a named regression assertion in its --self-test ('a register of terminal items reports ZERO open, not all of them'). Verified by `python3 scripts/ops/constraint_readout.py --self-test` and by section 4 of docs/claude/READOUT.md reading '0 OPEN item(s) ... 5 terminal, not listed'.
items.next_action: None -- fixed in the same change. Kept as a filed row because the lesson is general: any new consumer of a register must import that register's status vocabulary from the module that grades it, never re-derive it.

items.title: board-post.yml — the relay that exists precisely so a 403-scoped session can reach the coordination board — is named in ZERO of the four documents a session consults, so the session it was built for cannot find it
items.detail:
⚠️ THIS ROW WAS FILED WITH A FALSE PREMISE EARLIER IN THE SAME SESSION AND IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN RE-FILED. It originally read 'CLAUDE.md ships a workaround for the PR half of this 403 and NONE for the board half'. That is WRONG: .github/workflows/board-post.yml exists and does exactly that job (BL-20260820-NO-BOARD-POST-RELAY-FOR-READONLY-MCP, already fixed). The correction is kept visible because the mistake IS the finding — I concluded 'no relay exists' from CLAUDE.md, which is what any session in this position would do.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG. MEASURED 2026-09-01 by whole-file grep, with a positive control (the same probe finds 'claude-pr-automerge' in CLAUDE.md 3x): the strings 'board-post' and 'pr-opener' appear ZERO times in ALL FOUR of the documents a session would consult -- CLAUDE.md, docs/claude/coordination-board.md (which CLAUDE.md names as the board's own BODY OF RECORD), .claude/skills/session-coordination/SKILL.md, and docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md. CLAUDE.md's 'Workarounds shipped' list names the diag relay, system-actions, web-api recover, trainer diag, label bootstrap, secret sync and claude-pr-automerge -- and neither of the two relays that cover PR-open and board-post.

WHY THAT IS THE HIGH-SEVERITY HALF. board-post.yml's own header states it was built because 'a read-only session was structurally unable to comply with a binding rule; its only options were to skip the board or to stop'. The relay closed the capability gap and left the DISCOVERY gap wide open, so for a 403-scoped session the outcome is identical to having no relay at all -- and its silence on the board is indistinguishable from no session running. Reproduced live in this session: add_issue_comment on #6927 returned 403 'Resource not accessible by integration' twice minutes apart while issue_read succeeded (so a write-scope boundary, NOT the transient hosted-MCP drop CLAUDE.md documents); create_pull_request 403'd identically; `gh` is not installed and curl to api.github.com 403s from the sandbox proxy. I followed CLAUDE.md, concluded no board path existed, and found both relays only by reading .github/workflows/ directly AFTER the documented paths had failed.

THE GENERAL FORM, which is the transferable part and is a class this repo already names: a capability that is BUILT but unreachable from the surface its user actually reads is the 'shipped and working are different states' distinction applied to DOCUMENTATION -- the same shape as a written-and-never-read provenance field, or a state file shipped without a read surface (BL-20260825-ALERT-AND-CADENCE-STATE-FILES-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE). items.title: prop_fills_staleness detector B filtered fills on `reported_at`, which insert_fill OVERWRITES on every idempotent re-report -- so a corrective re-report pushed an already-reported close out of its own window and latched a false `alert` banner on breakout_1 for 2 days
items.detail:
OBSERVED LIVE on breakout_1. The `prop_fills_stale` banner stood latched at severity `alert` from 2026-08-30T19:33:29Z to at least 2026-09-01T21:2xZ (~2 days) reading 'Prop journal is missing trades: breakout_1 / Balance moved by $33.34 between two reports with no fills reported in between'. THE JOURNAL WAS NOT MISSING THE TRADE. The latch is `balance:18->19`, window (2026-08-30T13:37:39.446290Z, 2026-08-30T19:33:29.584285Z], delta +$33.34, `fills_in_window: 0`. `prop_fills` id 41 -- SOLUSDT long 49 @ 105.04 -> 105.76, pnl 35.28, status `closed` -- carries `created_at` 2026-08-30T19:33:17.466421Z, which is 12.1 SECONDS INSIDE the window, and `reported_at` 2026-08-30T19:39:00.972519Z, 5m31s outside it. `prop_journal.insert_fill` is idempotent and its UPDATE branch OVERWRITES `reported_at` with `now` while preserving `created_at`; the row's own `reason` text carries an explicit 'CORRECTION:'. So a corrective re-report -- routine on a manual bridge -- moved an already-reported close OUT of the window that it explains, and `assess_balance_move` filtered on `reported_at` alone.

THIS IS THE ROW THAT REFUTES A CHECKED CLAIM, WHICH IS WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED QUIETLY. BL-20260825-PROP-FILLS-RECORD-WHEN-THEY-WERE-REPORTED-NOT-WHEN-THEY-TRADED ends: 'NOT A DETECTOR REGRESSION, checked rather than assumed. prop_fills_staleness is unaffected: its B arm asks were any fills REPORTED between these two balance snapshots, for which reported_at is the correct field'. That session did the right check and reached a wrong conclusion, because the missed property is not WHICH question the field answers -- it is that the field is MUTABLE. `reported_at` does not record 'was this reported by then'; it records 'when was this LAST reported', and every correction moves it forward. A membership test over a closed historical window cannot be built on a field that later writes can change.

RECURRENCE OF A NAMED CLASS, THIRD CONSUMER. BL-20260828-RULE-DISTANCE-DOUBLE-COUNTS-A-LATE-REPORTED-EARLIER-FILL (open, high) is the same defect in `prop_reconcile.snapshot_plus_fills` -- it applies fills by REPORT time and rendered a FALSE static-DD floor breach of -19.29. BL-20260825 is the same defect stated as a measurement gap. This is the third prop consumer to key an EVENT-TIME question on a REPORT-TIME field, and the first where the field's mutability (not merely its lag) is the mechanism. The general form: on a manual bridge, report time and event time are different quantities AND the report-time field is not even stable.

IT IS THE DESENSITIZED-ALARM P1 ARRIVING INSIDE THE DETECTOR BUILT TO AVOID IT. This module's own docstring opens by refusing to key on unacted tickets precisely because 'an alert keyed on them would fire constantly on correct behaviour'. It then shipped a different route to the same outcome: an `alert`-severity Telegram + FCM banner standing for days over a correctly-journaled trade. Worse, the design makes it UNCLEARABLE by the operator -- a `balance_moved_unreported` latch is pruned only when a NEWER snapshot supersedes the pair, so on a flat, quiet account with no reason to send a fresh `bal`, a false finding persists indefinitely. That pruning rule is correct and is NOT changed here; the predicate is.

MEASURED, STATING THE POPULATION. All 19 live `prop_account_status` rows for breakout_1 = 18 consecutive snapshot pairs, re-graded through the patched pure function at threshold $25.00. EXACTLY ONE verdict changes: `18->19`, `unreported` -> `explained`, `fills_in_window_bases {'created_at': 1}`. The control holds -- the genuine 2026-08-20 -> 08-23 -$111.86 gap (pair `10->11`) still grades `unreported`, so the basis was widened without blunting the detector. Independent corroboration that nothing is actually missing: whole-history ledger, snapshot id 1 -> id 19, balance move -$427.93 against -$366.87 of reported closed-fill pnl, residual -$61.06 across 14 round trips ~= all-in commissions, several of which the rows' own `reason` text says are excluded from `pnl`; every non-skipped prop position has a closed fill; detector A latched nothing.

NOT A RECURRENCE OF BL-20260823's UNDERLYING CAUSE, checked rather than assumed. That incident was the REPORT PATH breaking (the screenshot reader 404-ing on a wrong model id). Here the report path WORKED: fill id 41 was ingested and then corrected on the same evening, 2026-08-30. What did not hold is the DETECTOR built in response to BL-20260823.

RESIDUAL, AND IT IS THE HALF THIS FIX CANNOT REACH. The trade-time field `closed_at` is what lets a LATE BACKFILL explain the window it repairs, and it is populated on 4 of 41 live fills (4 of the 18 `closed` rows) -- the ingest gap BL-20260825 already names. Measured consequence: the original BL-20260823 -$111.86 gap WAS repaired -- fill id 33, a 2026-08-22 round trip at -111.77, delta $0.09 -- and STILL grades `unreported`, because that row carries its close time only in prose. So a `balance_moved_unreported` finding remains unretireable-by-repair for any fill lacking `closed_at`. Do not read a persistent `unreported` as proof of a missing trade without first checking for a backfill that simply cannot be dated.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) `assess_balance_move` places a fill by EVERY instant it carries, not one mutable field, and publishes which one matched -- SHIPPED in this PR as `fill_evidence_times` (`created_at` immutable-first-report, `reported_at` back-compat, `closed_at` trade time; `opened_at` deliberately EXCLUDED because an open is not evidence that a realized move was reported) plus a `fills_in_window_bases` field that is None before counting and {} after, so 'we did not count' stays distinct from 'we counted and nothing matched'. (b) VERIFIED ON THE FLEET, not in a test: the `prop_fills_stale` banner for breakout_1 is absent from /api/bot/notifications after the trader restarts on the merged sha AND one cadence window (PROP_FILLS_STALENESS_CHECK_SECONDS, default 3600s) has elapsed. No state-file surgery is needed or permitted -- the pair re-grades `explained`, `findings` goes empty, and `stale_fill_accounts()` drops the account, so the latch clears itself; if it does NOT clear, the deploy did not take and that is the finding. (c) the residual is only closed when `closed_at` is populated by the ingest path (BL-20260825), which this row does not claim to fix.

items.title: The M7 review gate runs a 7-day window against an n_closed>=20 KILL/DEMOTE floor, so it can never propose a retirement — 52/52 hold, 0 actionable, best leg n=8
items.source: MEASURED over the FIRST committed packet run, population = ALL 52 enabled strategies: comms/strategy_reviews/2026-09-01/ (generated 12:51:37Z, window 2026-08-25 -> 2026-09-01), parsed per-packet. 52 graded, 52 `hold`, 0 actionable. 35 short-circuited at 'no closed trades in window'; 17 at 'insufficient evidence (n_closed=N < 20)'. The HIGHEST n_closed across all 52 was 8 against a floor of 20 — the gate is 2.5x short of its own floor at its single best leg. .github/workflows/strategy-review-packets.yml sets WINDOW_DAYS: 7.
items.why_it_matters: This is the mechanism that is supposed to RETIRE a strategy, and it is structurally incapable of proposing one at its scheduled cadence. It matters twice over. (1) The operating-layer build plan attributes the same symptom to a DIFFERENT cause — 'Override 5 converts every kill to tune pending artifacts that do not exist' — and that is REFUTED here: Override 5 fired on 0 of 52 and is never reached, because the matrix short-circuits on insufficient evidence long before it can reach demote_shadow/kill. A session acting on the plan's stated cause would fix the wrong thing. (2) The gate cannot distinguish a leg that is YOUNG from a leg that has NEVER CLOSED A TRADE IN ITS LIFE: joined to lifetime closes (/api/bot/performance?window=all, real+paper perStrategy, read 2026-09-01T22:56Z), 12 of the 52 have never closed a trade ever, and only 11 of 52 have a LIFETIME n_closed >= 20 — i.e. would ever be gradeable at the floor over their whole history. Median lifetime n is 6. Both states file as 'hold — insufficient evidence', every day, forever, which is the measured reason 6 strategy retirements have ever occurred against 45 live legs.
items.proposed_fix: TIER-3 — this changes the decision gate itself and is the operator's call, which is why it is filed rather than fixed. Options, not a recommendation: (a) widen ACTION_WINDOW_DAYS so the window can plausibly contain the floor's sample (note BL-20260814-1D-EQUITY-LEGS-TRADE-4-PER-YEAR-SO-PER-LEG-OOS-25-CONSUMES-6-YEARS — for a 1d leg no window short of years reaches n=20, so widening alone does not close it); (b) make the floor timeframe-aware rather than a flat 20; (c) leave the gate alone and let E3's sunset pass own the population it structurally cannot see, which is what shipped in Phase G — scripts/ops/sunset_pass.py grades exactly the legs the gate short-circuits on and stands off (governed_elsewhere) the moment the gate CAN judge one. Do NOT simply lower the floor: n>=20 exists so a kill is not proposed off noise, and lowering it trades a mechanism that cannot fire for one that fires wrongly.
