items.title: scripts/send_ping.py accepted --why / --unproven with NO --kind, discarded them, and reported the send as successful -- so a caller who asked for a Format-B second line got a bare body and exit 0
items.detail: STATUS NOTE: the fix is written and tested on branch `claude/ping-system-test-results` (PR #10695) and is NOT MERGED; the row stays `open` until it is, because an unmerged fix is not a fixed defect. MEASURED, not reasoned. During the operator-requested ping-system test (2026-09-01T22:23Z) `python3 scripts/send_ping.py --why 'this should not vanish' --target claude 'LOCAL TEST body'` exited 0, logged 'queued ... bot drains within ~5 s', and wrote {"priority": "normal", "body": "LOCAL TEST body"} -- the why-line gone with no warning anywhere. Same for --unproven. MECHANISM: main() reads args.why / args.unproven ONLY inside `if args.kind:`, so with no class they are accepted by argparse and never looked at again. WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY THE EXISTING GUARDS DO NOT COVER IT: the MIRROR case has always been refused (`--kind` without `--why` exits 1, 'Format B's second line is the whole point'), and PR #10683 adds this direction at the WORKFLOW and WRAPPER layers -- but neither reaches this file, and #10683's own body states the script keeps its own guards precisely because it 'is also reachable directly on the VM'. The asymmetry is the defect: one direction is a hard error, the opposite one is silent. It is the same shape as the module's own rule that a withheld ping must never read as a sent one -- a caller who asked for a formatted ping had no way to tell they did not get one. BLAST RADIUS TODAY IS SMALL AND THAT IS WHY IT WAS FIXABLE SAFELY: exactly one caller in the tree passes --why (scripts/ops/notify_run.sh:388) and it always pairs it with --kind state_change, so no existing producer changes behaviour. FIX: a guard in send_ping.main() refusing --why/--unproven without --kind, queueing NOTHING (a guard that reports failure and still enqueues the stripped body would deliver the ping it refused) and leaving the passthrough path byte-for-byte unchanged -- passthrough is the PRIMARY path, carrying the operator's own text unaltered, so a guard that made a plain ping harder to send would be worse than the bug. 3 tests added to tests/test_send_ping.py, all pass. Filed WITH the fix rather than as a post-it.
items.resolution_criteria: On the LIVE VM tree (not the sandbox), `python3 scripts/send_ping.py --why x --target claude body` exits 1 AND `pending_claude_pings` gains no new file for it -- both halves checked, because a guard that reports failure and still enqueues the stripped body would deliver the ping it refused. ⚠️ A green CI run on PR #10695 does NOT close this: the wrapper runs the script from the VM's own clone, so the row closes only after the merge has reached that clone (/api/diag/version git_sha_on_disk carrying it). ⚠️ Nor does the workflow-layer refusal already shipped in #10683 -- that guards the ACTION path and this row is about direct invocation on the VM, which is the reason the script carries its own guards at all. Control that the fix is not over-broad: a plain `send_ping.py --target claude body` still exits 0 and queues one file.

items.title: Three system-actions dispatched within 15s: the MIDDLE one was cancelled by the concurrency queue, its issue was left OPEN with NO comment, and nothing anywhere said the action never ran
items.detail: OBSERVED. Issues #10690 (22:24:53Z), #10691 (22:25:00Z), #10692 (22:25:08Z), all `action: send-ping`. Runs: 33566171789 success, 33566180621 **cancelled**, 33566191528 success. #10691's send-ping NEVER EXECUTED -- no ping was enqueued -- and the issue is still open with ZERO comments, while its two neighbours each got the usual '✅ system-action completed' comment and were closed. MECHANISM: system-actions.yml declares `concurrency: {group: system-actions, cancel-in-progress: false}`. That setting protects a RUNNING job, but GitHub keeps only ONE pending run per group, so a third queued run cancels the second while it waits. So the failure mode is specifically a BURST: fire three and the middle one evaporates. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS TEST: the issue-comment-back is the ONLY result surface a PM-side session has for a system-action, and a cancelled run posts nothing -- so the observable difference between 'the action ran' and 'the action was silently dropped' is an ABSENT comment, which is indistinguishable from 'still queued'. A session that fires a batch and reads two successes would conclude all three ran. This is the read-a-clean-negative-off-a-surface-that-cannot-report class (an absent row read as a clean answer), applied to the dispatch layer. NOT FIXED HERE -- the test session re-fired the lost action as #10693 (succeeded) and stopped batching. CANDIDATE REMEDIES, none evaluated: (a) an `if: cancelled()` step that comments the cancellation onto the issue, which is the smallest honest change; (b) a wider concurrency key so independent actions do not share one queue slot; (c) leaving the behaviour and documenting 'dispatch system-actions one at a time', which is what this session did by hand and is exactly the kind of unwritten discipline that decays.
items.resolution_criteria: Three `system-action` issues dispatched inside ~15s and EVERY ONE of the three carries a comment naming its outcome -- ✅ completed, ❌ failed, or an explicit cancellation notice -- with none left open and comment-less. The cancellation case is the one that must be demonstrated, so the check is not satisfied by a burst in which no run happened to be cancelled: reproduce the cancel first (runs 33566171789 / 33566180621 / 33566191528 are the recorded instance) and then show the third comment appearing. ⚠️ Widening the concurrency key instead would ALSO close this, by removing the cancellation rather than reporting it -- record which remedy was taken, because the two leave different residual risk. ⚠️ 'We now dispatch one at a time' does NOT close it: that is an unwritten discipline held by whichever session remembers, which is the state this row exists to end.

items.title: Two registered drainers consume `pending_claude_pings` and only ONE of them logs a successful send, so whether a ping is traceable at all depends on which racer won that tick
items.detail: ⚠️ THIS ROW SUPERSEDES ITS OWN FIRST DRAFT, WHICH WAS WRONG IN THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS. It was filed as 'neither drainer logs a successful delivery', reasoned from src/bot/claude_bridge.py's drain loop, which does indeed only log on failure and unlink() silently on success. A journal read taken 8 minutes later REFUTED that: claude_bridge sends through src.runtime.notify.send_telegram_direct, which logs 'Telegram send: ok=True message_id=N status_code=200' one frame down. Delivery on THAT path is positively observable. The first draft read one function and generalised; the correction came from the journal, not from a re-read. Recorded rather than quietly edited, because the wrong version is the instructive half. WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, and it is a sharper finding. TWO drainers are registered against the SAME inbox: src/bot/claude_bridge.py:453 ('drain_pending_claude_pings', 5s interval) and a job of the same name registered at src/bot/telegram_query_bot.py:676, which runs src/bot/cloud_notifier.py::_drain_one_ping_dir. They have DIFFERENT observability: claude_bridge -> notify.send_telegram_direct (logs ok/message_id/status_code); cloud_notifier -> bot.send_message directly, with NO success log at all and only a warning on failure. Each file is delivered by whichever drainer reaches it first and is then unlinked, so a ping's traceability is decided by a race. MEASURED during the operator-requested ping test (2026-09-01). Six claude-targeted pings were queued: 22:25:13Z, 22:25:39Z, 22:31:58Z, 22:33:09Z, 22:34:22Z, 22:35:32Z. The ict-claude-bridge journal over the full 22:24:00Z+ window (423 lines, 11 non-apscheduler -- a stated denominator, not a spot check) carries exactly TWO 'Telegram send: ok=True' lines, message_id 7 at 22:33:12Z and message_id 8 at 22:34:22Z, matching the 22:33:09Z and 22:34:22Z pings. The other FOUR produced no send line and no failure line anywhere -- consistent with the cloud_notifier drainer having taken them, which logs nothing either way. So four of six deliveries are unverifiable from any surface. ⚠️ STATE THE POPULATION: this is an absence over a stated window, not a positive read, and it does NOT establish that those four were delivered. RELATION TO THE DOUBLE-DELIVERY BUG (owned by session_01LqVvgvusnN87neBn5ayzhg, NOT this row): two racing drainers explains INTERMITTENT duplication rather than reliable doubling -- both can list the directory before either unlinks, in which case both send and one unlink loses harmlessly. This row is about OBSERVABILITY and is filed separately so that fixing the duplication does not close the traceability gap by accident. There is also no read surface for the inbox itself: `pending_claude_pings` is absent from diag's log_file allowlist and no route lists it, so an ACCUMULATING inbox -- what a genuine delivery failure produces, since both failure branches leave the file in place for retry -- is invisible too. CANDIDATE REMEDIES, none evaluated: give cloud_notifier's drain the same success log claude_bridge gets for free; or settle which drainer owns this inbox and deregister the other, which is the duplication fix and would make the observability question moot. A diag counter for inbox depth would cover the stranded-backlog case either way.
items.resolution_criteria: For a batch of N pings queued to `pending_claude_pings` in one window, a readable surface accounts for all N -- N positive send records, or fewer plus a named failure for each shortfall. The recorded baseline to beat is 6 queued / 2 accounted (2026-09-01T22:24Z+, 423 journal lines in window). Either remedy qualifies: give cloud_notifier's drain the success log claude_bridge gets for free from notify.send_telegram_direct, or deregister one of the two drainers so a single owner handles the inbox -- state which. ⚠️ Closing the DOUBLE-DELIVERY bug does not by itself close this: if the surviving drainer is the cloud_notifier one, deliveries become unobservable for ALL pings rather than some, which is worse. ⚠️ An absence of failure lines is not accounting -- the whole point is that a silent path and a healthy path look identical.

items.title: send_ping_action.sh passed no --kind, so the send-ping system-action could only ever fire the passthrough shape and the three ping classes were unreachable from the only path a session can dispatch
items.detail: RECURRENCE, filed with similar_ok because the recurrence IS the finding -- see BL-20260901-FORMATTER-IMPORT-FAILURE-DROPPED-THE-PING-IT-WAS-FORMATTING, filed the same day against the same rollout. #10669 shipped src/runtime/claude_ping.py (decision / state_change / lifecycle, each gated differently) and taught scripts/send_ping.py --kind/--why/--unproven. It did NOT teach scripts/ops/send_ping_action.sh, which is the wrapper the `send-ping` system-action invokes -- so the action passed no --kind and could only ever produce the unformatted passthrough shape. The classes were implemented, documented in docs/claude/system-actions.md, and UNREACHABLE from the only dispatch path a session has. WHY IT IS THE SAME CLASS AS #10674, WHICH LANDED HOURS EARLIER: #10664 introduced telegram_routes.py as the one owner of routing, converted cloud_notifier, and left claude_bridge._drain_pending_claude_pings on a hardcoded token -- a capability configured, resolvable and inert. This is that shape again, one layer up: a vocabulary gets a new owner, the owner is correct, and a CONSUMER is left unconverted. Three instances of one rollout (#10664 -> #10674, #10669 -> the formatter row, #10669 -> this) inside 24 hours. THE TRANSFERABLE RULE, which is stronger than 'test the new module': a change that introduces an owner must be checked at EVERY consumer, because the unconverted consumer keeps working and therefore fails in the direction that still looks like success. Nothing was red for any of the three. FIXED in PR #10683: optional kind:/why:/unproven: on the action, with PASSTHROUGH KEPT AS THE DEFAULT -- that path carries the operator's own words and Format B is a house style for machine-generated events, so converting it would have been a substitution, not a formatting improvement. An invalid kind is a hard error rather than a degrade to passthrough (it selects the format AND the limiter, so a silent degrade would report success for a ping whose shape and gating the caller never got), and a withheld ping is audited as 'withheld' rather than 'ok'. NOT YET EXERCISED ON THE FLEET at filing time: #10683 was open and the three classes had never been fired against the live bot, because dispatching any system-action was blocked (issue_write create -> 403) and set-env is Tier-2 and awaiting the operator.
items.resolution_criteria: A send-ping system-action dispatched with kind=decision, again with kind=state_change, and again with kind=lifecycle each reaches the live Claude bot carrying the Format-B two-line shape, and the run's audit JSON records the matching `kind` (never `passthrough`) for each. ⚠️ MERGING #10683 DOES NOT SATISFY THIS and must not be read as doing so -- the code is merged (970fe13c) and present on the VM disk, which is exactly the shipped-not-working state this row is about. ⚠️ Nor does one class standing in for the others: lifecycle is the only one behind a rate limiter and its own env switch, so it is the one most likely to be silently withheld; a withheld run exits 0 and the audit says `withheld`, which is NOT a pass.

items.title: work_digest.py's 'one digest per UTC day' latch lives under gitignored runtime_logs/, so a fresh Actions checkout never has it and the latch is inert in CI -- while it WOULD fire on the VM, so the same code queues 6 digests/day or 1 depending where it runs
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-01. scripts/ops/work_digest.py:79 sets STATE = REPO_ROOT / 'runtime_logs' / 'work_digest_state.json'. .gitignore:29 ignores runtime_logs/, and the file is absent from main (git show origin/main:runtime_logs/work_digest_state.json -> does not exist). .github/workflows/work-digest.yml runs on a GitHub-hosted runner with actions/checkout, i.e. a FRESH tree every run, and commits back ONLY docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl. So _already_sent_today() reads a file that cannot exist, takes its OSError branch, and returns False on every single run. WHY THAT IS A DEFECT AND NOT MERELY DEAD CODE. The latch's own docstring is a claim about behaviour -- 'One digest per UTC day. A latch, so a double invocation cannot double-ping.' -- and on the only path that invokes it that claim is FALSE. The cron is '20 2,6,10,14,18,22 * * *' (six windows a day), so the as-written behaviour is SIX queued digests per day, not one. A reader of the function cannot tell: the guard looks like it bounds the cadence and does not. AND THE TWO ENVIRONMENTS DISAGREE, which is the sharper half. runtime_logs/ PERSISTS on the live VM, so the identical code run there would latch correctly and suppress five of six. Same source, opposite cadence, decided by which box it runs on and stated nowhere. NOTE THE FAIL-OPEN IS DELIBERATE AND CORRECT and is not what is being reported: the OSError branch carries a written argument that an unreadable latch must SEND rather than suppress, which is right for a notification path. The defect is that the 'unreadable' branch is the ONLY branch CI can reach, so a deliberate failure-direction became the permanent behaviour without anyone deciding that. WHICH BEHAVIOUR IS WANTED IS AN OPERATOR QUESTION, NOT A BUG FIX. The operator raised the cadence from a daily 06:20 to every 4h on 2026-09-01 ('events live + a digest every few hours'), so six a day may be exactly the intent -- in which case the latch should be deleted rather than repaired, because a guard that silently means nothing is worse than no guard. If one-a-day is wanted, the latch needs state that survives a fresh checkout (a committed marker, or deriving the answer from pending-pings.jsonl itself, which IS committed and already carries a per-row 'at' timestamp). FOUND while establishing whether the 22:20Z cron had fired: I had to rule out 'it ran and legitimately queued nothing' before reading the absent commit as an absent run, and checking that is what surfaced this.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) the latch is DELETED and work-digest.yml's header states that six digests a day is the intended cadence -- a guard that provably means nothing is worse than no guard -- OR (b) the latch reads state that survives a fresh actions/checkout (a committed marker, or derived from pending-pings.jsonl, which is already committed and carries a per-row `at`), AND a second cron window on the same UTC day is observed producing NO new pending-pings.jsonl commit while the first did. ⚠️ Reading the code and concluding it now works does not satisfy (b): the defect was invisible by reading, which is how it shipped.

items.title: Rebasing/resetting a claude/** branch onto a newer main re-fires pr-opener for ANOTHER session's still-pending pr-request, and commits that result onto YOUR branch -- silently making a bot commit your PR head and disarming your CI
items.detail: OBSERVED 2026-09-01T22:31Z on PR #10685, cause established rather than guessed. SEQUENCE. main moved under branch claude/claude-channel-registers, so it was reset with `git checkout -B <branch> origin/main` and force-pushed at 22:31:21. That newer main carried another session's UNPROCESSED automation/pr-requests/prop-fills-gap-20260901.json. pr-opener.yml triggers on `push` with `paths: ['automation/pr-requests/**']`, and relative to the branch's PREVIOUS tip that file was an ADDITION -- so the push fired pr-opener, which processed a request belonging to a different session and committed automation/pr-results/prop-fills-gap-20260901.txt back to `github.ref_name`, i.e. THIS branch, at 22:31:47 -- 26 seconds after the push. TWO DISTINCT HARMS, and the second is the quiet one. (1) A foreign artifact enters an unrelated PR: a registers PR silently acquired a pr-result file for someone else's work. (2) THE BOT COMMIT BECAME THE PR HEAD, which is precisely the zero-checks trap pr-opener.yml's own header documents -- GitHub does not run workflows for pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN. Measured directly: get_check_runs on #10685 returned SIX checks in_progress at 22:31:35 and total_count ZERO fifteen minutes later, because the head had moved to the bot's commit. A PR that had genuinely armed CI became a PR with no checks, and the transition is invisible unless someone re-queries. WHY THE EXISTING HEADER DOES NOT COVER THIS. pr-opener.yml warns a caller about the results commit landing on the branch THEY pushed a request from, and the documented mitigation -- push the request from a different branch -- was FOLLOWED here: this session pushed its requests from claude/claude-channel-board and never put one on the registers branch. The re-fire came from inheriting a THIRD PARTY's pending request through a routine rebase, which no amount of care about one's own request files prevents. NO DUPLICATE PR RESULTED, this time and by luck: the run failed with 'No commits between main and claude/prop-fills-gap-20260901' because that work had already merged as #10678. Had it NOT merged, this would have opened another session's PR from an unrelated session's push, and written the result somewhere that session was not watching -- while main kept the request looking unprocessed, since the result file (the idempotency key) landed only on the rebasing branch. CANDIDATE FIXES, not applied here because this belongs to whoever owns the relays: restrict pr-opener's trigger to pushes that changed a request file whose `head` matches the pushed branch; or commit results to a fixed branch rather than github.ref_name; or have the workflow skip a request whose head branch has no commits ahead of base rather than recording FAILED. The artifact was removed from #10685 rather than merged, so main's copy of the request stays unprocessed and its owner's retry is unaffected.
items.resolution_criteria: A claude/** branch is reset onto a main that carries an UNPROCESSED automation/pr-requests/*.json belonging to another branch, force-pushed, and NO automation/pr-results/ commit appears on the pushed branch within 5 minutes -- checked by re-reading the branch head, since the whole hazard is that the head moves silently. ⚠️ A push that happens not to inherit a pending request proves nothing: the request pool is usually empty, so a quiet push is the expected result either way and is not a negative control. The test needs a request actually present on the base at push time.

items.tier: 1 — a CI guard constant; no order path
items.title: The backlog round-trip guard checks 3 of the 4 live review backlogs — research-review-backlog.json is not covered, so the file the guard exists to protect can break unwatched
items.detail:
FOUND while verifying BL-20260901-NO-PRE-MERGE-GUARD-ON-BACKLOG-ROUND-TRIP (closed this session on real evidence). The guard is registered and it demonstrably fires — I planted a non-canonical serialisation (indent=3, ensure_ascii=True) in a scratch root and check_live_backlogs returned exit 1. But its coverage is a hardcoded tuple.

MEASURED 2026-09-01: scripts/ops/backlog_append.py::LIVE_BACKLOGS names THREE paths — docs/claude/{health,performance,ml}-review-backlog.json. FOUR review backlogs exist on disk: `ls docs/claude/*backlog*.json` returns those three plus **docs/claude/research-review-backlog.json**. The guard's own success line says so out loud and nobody has read it as a coverage statement: 'backlog round-trip: OK — 3 live backlog(s) reproduce byte-for-byte'.

WHY THE OMISSION IS EASY TO MISS, and why the tuple is not simply a bug: LIVE_BACKLOGS carries a comment explaining it is enumerated by hand rather than globbed, because its reader (tests/test_backlog_append.py) interpolates a loop variable that no static scan can resolve. The reasoning is sound; the list just did not grow when the fourth backlog was created. This is `field beats comment` in its ordinary form — the constant is authoritative and the '3' in the output is the field telling you the truth.

NOT A CRITICISM OF THE CLOSED ROW. That row's criterion says 'all three live review backlogs' and is literally satisfied; it was written before the fourth backlog existed. This is the successor, not a reopening.
items.why_it_matters: The guard exists because a non-round-tripping backlog makes backlog_append REFUSE EVERY WRITE to it repo-wide, and the repo has now had that happen twice in two days (BL-20260820-BACKLOG-APPEND-REFORMATS-AND-REATTRIBUTES, then BL-20260901-BACKLOG-ROUND-TRIP-BROKEN-AGAIN-BY-A-HAND-WRITTEN-SPLICE one day after the first repair). research-review-backlog.json is written by the same helper, by the same sessions, with the same hand-splice hazard — and is the one file where that break would reach main green, because pytest-run deliberately excludes the backlogs from its relevance filter and this guard does not look at it. A partial guard reads exactly like a complete one from CI.
items.resolution_criteria: LIVE_BACKLOGS covers every review backlog that exists, AND the coverage cannot silently fall behind again — i.e. either the tuple is derived from a glob of docs/claude/*-review-backlog.json with the hand-enumeration comment updated to say why that is now safe, or a test asserts set(LIVE_BACKLOGS) == set(glob) and FAILS today. ⚠️ Adding the fourth path alone does NOT close this: that is the same hand-maintained list one entry longer, and the next backlog created will reproduce the gap. Verify by planting a non-canonical serialisation in research-review-backlog.json specifically and observing check_live_backlogs exit 1 naming THAT file — the same plant-and-check used to close BL-20260901-NO-PRE-MERGE-GUARD-ON-BACKLOG-ROUND-TRIP, since a guard shown only to pass is indistinguishable from one that cannot fire.
items.next_action: Tier-1: derive LIVE_BACKLOGS from a glob (or pin it with a set-equality test), then plant-and-check against research-review-backlog.json.

items.title: backlog_drain_candidates' diag_log_name signal is satisfied by the diag ALLOWLIST, not by the log existing — so it shortlists a row whose whole finding is that the file has never been written
items.detail:
MEASURED this session. `python3 scripts/ops/backlog_drain_candidates.py` shortlisted 3 rows as `likely_met` out of 575 scanned (565 not_checkable, 7 likely_unmet). I hand-checked all three. Every one was shortlisted on a single `OK diag_log_name: <name>` signal, and at least one is a FALSE POSITIVE OF THE WORST AVAILABLE KIND:

  BL-20260830-BUILDER-EXCEPTION-LATCH-HAS-NEVER-BEEN-WRITTEN was shortlisted on `OK diag_log_name: strategy_builder_exception_alert_state`. I then read that route on the live VM: /api/diag/log_file?name=strategy_builder_exception_alert_state returns **present: false, lines: []**. The row's ENTIRE finding is that this file has never been written — so the signal fired on precisely the row it should have been silent on.

THE MECHANISM: the signal establishes that the name appears in diag.py's `_LOG_FILES` allowlist. That is a statement about the READ SURFACE, never about the DATA. The two are different facts and this repo already has a name for conflating them — a row is routinely filed BECAUSE a writer shipped without an allowlist entry, so 'the name is allowlisted' is the state a fix reaches HALFWAY to, not the state that closes a row.

THE OTHER TWO I could confirm as genuinely met, and closed them this session — BL-20260830-FANOUT-SOAK-GRADES-A-NO-WINNER-TICK-AS-STARVED and BL-20260830-PAIRS-SOAK-RECORDS-NO-POSITION-IDX-SO-HEDGE-MODE-CANNOT-BE-VERIFIED — but NOT on the tool's signal: both needed a live read of the rows plus a count over the returned population. The tool got the right answer for the wrong reason on 2 of 3 and the wrong answer on 1 of 3.
items.why_it_matters:
The backlog-drain skill already records that this tool's first version 'claimed 108 of 542 and was almost entirely wrong', and that the noisy signals were cut down to leave 3. This row says the SURVIVING signal has the same defect in miniature: it is a presence check standing in for an observation. The cost is specific — a drain session is told 'likely_met, VERIFY EACH ONE', and the one row where verification MOST matters (a monitoring row whose subject is an absent file) is the one it points at. A session that trusted the label would close a row asserting a file exists that does not, which deletes the finding AND reports progress: the exact failure the drain skill's evidence bar exists to prevent.

⚠️ NOT AN ARGUMENT TO DELETE THE SIGNAL. `diag_log_name` is the right THING to check — it just checks the wrong SIDE of it.
items.resolution_criteria: The `diag_log_name` signal reports the LOG'S OWN STATE, not the allowlist's — i.e. it grades `present` from /api/diag/log_file?name=<n> (three states, never collapsed: `present_with_rows` / `present_empty` / `absent`, plus `could_not_look` when the diag read fails, since an unreachable VM is not evidence a file is missing), and only `present_with_rows` counts toward `likely_met`. VERIFIED by re-running backlog_drain_candidates.py and observing BL-20260830-BUILDER-EXCEPTION-LATCH-HAS-NEVER-BEEN-WRITTEN drop OUT of `likely_met` while at least one row whose log genuinely carries rows stays IN — both halves, because a signal that now matches nothing is not a fix. ⚠️ If a live diag read is judged too expensive for this tool to make, the acceptable alternative is to RENAME the signal to say what it actually checks (e.g. `diag_name_allowlisted`) and stop counting it toward `likely_met` on its own — but silently keeping a presence check under a name that reads as an observation is not.
items.next_action: Tier-1: either make the signal read the log's own state, or rename it and demote it out of likely_met.
refs: BL-20260830-BUILDER-EXCEPTION-LATCH-HAS-NEVER-BEEN-WRITTEN (the false positive; re-confirmed OPEN this session)

updates.note: RECURRENCE CONFIRMED — a SECOND drain session was misled by this signal today, which is the finding rather than a re-read. 2026-09-09: scripts/ops/backlog_drain_candidates.py scanned 834 OPEN rows across the three backlogs and returned likely_met 3 / likely_unmet 14 / not_checkable 817 (98.0% not_checkable, reproducing the ratio the skill documents). OF THE 3 SHORTLISTED, ONE IS A FALSE POSITIVE OF EXACTLY THIS DEFECT: BL-20260830-BUILDER-EXCEPTION-LATCH-HAS-NEVER-BEEN-WRITTEN was shortlisted `OK diag_log_name: strategy_builder_exception_alert_state` while that file reads {present:false} on the live VM — i.e. the tool shortlisted, as `likely_met`, a row whose ENTIRE FINDING is that the file does not exist. That is the second time; the first was drain session #1 on 2026-09-01, recorded on this row. THE OTHER TWO SHORTLISTED ROWS WERE BOTH GENUINE (BL-20260901-OPERATOR-ALERTS-HAS-NO-READ-SURFACE closed today; BL-20260908-THE-WEDGE-LEDGERS-VANISH-CLOCK-READS-A-CHANGED-CLASSIFICATION-AS-A-DISAPPEARED-POSITION re-verified and correctly still open), so the signal is 1-in-3 wrong rather than useless — but its one error mode is precisely the row class it is most likely to surface. The fix named in this row's criterion (grade `present` from the live route with four never-collapsed states — present_with_rows / present_empty / absent / could_not_look, and only present_with_rows counting toward likely_met) is unchanged and is now backed by two measured instances instead of one.

items.title: The DB explorer's device_tokens exposure was one table of 22; the other 21 -- 2,301,022 signals rows, 5,313 trades, 29,848 balance_snapshots -- remain world-readable unauthenticated on a public host
items.detail: Found while closing BL-20260901-DB-EXPLORER-IS-UNGATED-AND-REACHES-DEVICE-TOKENS-RAW-TOKEN-COLUMN and filed SEPARATELY rather than folded into it, because that row's done_condition is specifically about device_tokens and quietly widening it would have hidden the larger finding inside a narrower one. MEASURED against the live host, unauthenticated, no bearer, 2026-09-01: GET https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/bot/db/tables returns 200 with 22 tables across trade_journal + trainer_store. Row counts: signals 2,301,022 | insights_usage 125,526 | insights_history 125,420 | balance_snapshots 29,848 | dataset_builds 13,967 | training_cycle 8,828 | experiment_runs 5,758 | trades 5,313 | order_packages 4,272 | db_pulls 2,747 | account_context_snapshots 2,673 | daily_risk_state 676 | position_telemetry 111 | model_registry 96 | prop_tickets 89 | strategy_versions 81 | prop_fills 41 | prop_account_status 19 | backtest_sweeps 2 | backtest_results 0 | learning_progress 0. That is the complete live trading history -- entries, exits, PnL, sizing, strategy config and the ML fleet -- readable by anyone who knows the URL, on a PUBLIC repo whose CLAUDE.md names the host. THE ALLOWLIST SHIPPED IN THE COMPANION PR DOES NOT CLOSE THIS and is not claimed to: it is the AUTHORIZATION layer (which tables are reachable at all), deliberately preserving the Data Explorer's current UI. The missing layer is AUTHENTICATION, which is Phase H's actual job -- WO-20260901-PHASE-H states it directly: 'a route gate is authentication, not authorization: one token would otherwise open all 22 tables.' The two are complementary and neither substitutes for the other. NOTE ON SEVERITY, stated in the honest direction: this is a confidentiality exposure of trading data, not a control-path one. The explorer is SELECT-only on a mode=ro connection with bound parameters and schema-validated identifiers; nothing here writes, and no credential is reachable once device_tokens is excluded.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when an unauthenticated GET of /api/bot/db/tables against the live host returns 401/403 rather than 200 -- demonstrated against the live host, not asserted from a diff -- which is Phase H attaching require_session to the read surface. NOT satisfied by the table allowlist alone (that narrows WHICH tables an unauthenticated caller reaches, from 22 to 21, and was never intended to close this). NOT satisfied by DASHBOARD_API_TOKEN being set, because that token gates only the devices routes today. Re-opens if a later change makes any db-explorer route reachable without a session again.

updates.note: RE-CONFIRMED LIVE AND UNREMEDIATED, demonstrated against the live host exactly as the criterion demands rather than asserted from a diff. 2026-09-09, unauthenticated (no bearer, no session cookie), against https://ict-bot.duckdns.org: GET /api/bot/db/tables -> HTTP 200, body {'present':true,'db':'trade_journal','dbs':['trade_journal','trainer_store'],'tables':[...]}. GET /api/bot/db/table/trades?limit=1 -> HTTP 200, returning the trades table's column schema and rows. The criterion requires 401/403; it is 200 on both. Phase H has not attached require_session to this surface. ⚠️ DO NOT CONFUSE THIS WITH THE CLOSED DIAG-TOKEN QUESTION. That decision (operator, 2026-08-30, do not raise again) is about /api/diag/*, which is read-only and at least BEARER-GATED. This is a DIFFERENT surface with NO credential at all, serving the money DB's tables and rows to anyone on the internet. The closed decision does not cover it and must not be cited over it.

items.title: ict-trader-android/CLAUDE.md's ON-ICE directive justifies the freeze with 'the operator is using the web app (Streamlit + the Svelte SPA)' -- Streamlit was retired from the live feed on 2026-09-01, so the banner's stated reason is now half false
items.detail: Found while working BL-20260901-RETIRE-ANDROID-AND-STREAMLIT-FROM-THE-LIVE-FEED. The ON-ICE directive (operator, 2026-08-13) at the top of ict-trader-android/CLAUDE.md reads: 'The operator is using the web app (Streamlit + the Svelte SPA) and the Telegram channels. This app is not in active use and is explicitly lower priority.' The 2026-09-01 operator decision retires Streamlit from the live feed, so one of the two named replacements no longer exists. THE FREEZE ITSELF IS UNAFFECTED and this row does not argue for reversing it -- the directive is explicit that it reverses 'only on an explicit operator instruction', and the remaining justification (the SPA + Telegram) still holds on its own. What is wrong is the stated REASON, and that matters here more than usual because this banner's whole job is to be read and obeyed by a session that will not read further. A directive whose premise a reader can verify as stale is a directive that invites re-litigation. NOT FIXED IN THIS SESSION, deliberately: correcting it is repo-side work inside the frozen repo, which is exactly what the directive forbids -- 'do not open speculative work here'. Filing is the action the directive itself prescribes for this case: 'Do not let it silently rot into a false record either... still FILE it.' Same class as the pre-rename repo reference in that file, which points operating rules at benbaichmankass/ict-trading-bot rather than the current Metis-Insights.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when the ON-ICE banner in ict-trader-android/CLAUDE.md names only consumers that are actually live (the Svelte SPA + Telegram), with the Streamlit reference marked retired 2026-09-01. Requires an operator instruction to touch the frozen repo, OR gets folded into whatever change next legitimately opens that repo. Re-opens if a future retirement leaves the banner naming a dead consumer again.

updates.note: CLOSED as wont_fix, same class disposition, and the row's own criteria anticipate it: they say resolution 'requires an operator instruction to touch the frozen repo, OR gets folded into whatever change next legitimately opens that repo'. The banner's inaccuracy (it justifies the freeze by citing Streamlit, retired 2026-09-01) is now harmless because the repo it lives in is itself retired from the live feed — a stale banner in a frozen repo misleads nobody who is acting. REVERSAL is already written into the criteria and I am keeping it: re-open if the repo is opened, or if a future retirement leaves the banner naming a dead consumer again.

items.title: A web session can push a branch to ict-trader-dashboard but cannot open a PR there -- the MCP 403s and the git proxy refuses the REST call -- and unlike the bot repo there is no pr-opener relay, so cross-repo work strands on a pushed branch
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-01 while retiring the Streamlit app for BL-20260901-RETIRE-ANDROID-AND-STREAMLIT-FROM-THE-LIVE-FEED. Branch claude/phase-h-preconditions-retire-streamlit pushed to benbaichmankass/ict-trader-dashboard successfully -- the git proxy path works. THREE PR-creation paths then failed: (1) GitHub MCP create_pull_request -> 403 'Resource not accessible by integration'; (2) gh CLI -> not installed; (3) direct REST POST /repos/.../pulls with the proxy-injected token -> 403 'GitHub access is not enabled for this session. An org admin must connect the Claude GitHub App for this organization.' Note (3) is a DIFFERENT refusal from (1) and comes from the proxy, not GitHub. THE ASYMMETRY IS THE POINT: the bot repo hit the same read-only-MCP 403 for issue comments and PR creation and solved it with committed relays (board-post.yml, pr-opener.yml, both git-push-triggered). ict-trader-dashboard has ci.yml, pages.yml, delete-merged-branches.yml and generate-learning-module.yml -- no relay. So identical work strands in one repo and completes in the other, and the failure is silent in the sense that it only appears at the last step, after the work is done and pushed. This is the third repo in the fleet (bot, dashboard, android) and cross-repo retirements are now a recurring shape rather than a one-off, so the gap will be hit again.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when a web session can get a PR opened in ict-trader-dashboard without an operator hop -- EITHER by the org admin connecting the Claude GitHub App for that repo (which fixes the REST path directly and is the smaller change), OR by porting the bot repo's pr-opener.yml relay into it. Verified by a session actually opening a PR there end to end, not by the workflow existing. ⚠️ Do NOT resolve this by adding a relay to every repo reflexively -- the build plan's Phase G is explicit that complexity here is monotonic and nothing has ever retired a workflow; prefer the App connection if it covers the case.

items.title: The 403 blocking PR creation in ict-trader-dashboard from a web session is a SESSION-SCOPE gap, not a missing capability -- `add_repo` with access:"push" clears it, and a session that concludes 'that repo has no pr-opener relay' stops one step early
items.detail:
REFUTES, by direct measurement, the standing reading that a web session structurally cannot open a PR in `benbaichmankass/ict-trader-dashboard`. 

WHAT WAS OBSERVED. On 2026-09-01T21:57Z `session_01LvzsinECH8HPCyauVJZBZw` (Phase H preconditions) pushed `claude/phase-h-preconditions-retire-streamlit` and reported it could NOT open the PR: MCP 403, no `gh` CLI, and a proxy-level 403 ('GitHub access is not enabled for this session') -- a DIFFERENT refusal from the MCP one. It concluded that repo needs its own `pr-opener.yml` relay and filed the gap. 

At 2026-09-01T23:1xZ THIS session, on the same runtime, called `add_repo(owner='benbaichmankass', repo='ict-trader-dashboard', access='push')` FIRST, cloned, and then `create_pull_request` SUCCEEDED on the first attempt -- ict-trader-dashboard#211, draft, no relay, no retry, no backoff. 

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH. It establishes that the refusal is a SESSION-SCOPE condition (the repo was not attached, or was attached read-only) and therefore CLEARABLE from inside the session. It does NOT establish which of the two the other session hit, because that session's `add_repo` call -- if any -- and its `access` argument were not recorded on the board; that is the one fact needed to close this and it is not recoverable from here. So the remedy is stated as a PROBE, not a diagnosis: before concluding a repo is unreachable, call `add_repo` with `access: "push"` and retry once. 

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE PR. The Streamlit retirement -- a PRECONDITION of operating-layer Phase H's read gate -- has been sitting on an unopened branch since 21:57Z solely because of this, and the proposed remedy (port `pr-opener.yml` into a second repo) is CI automation in a repo that has none, which that session correctly called a sanctioning decision rather than a Tier-1 one. A one-line tool argument is a much cheaper answer than a new relay, and building the relay would have been `RC-BUILT-A-MECHANISM-THAT-ALREADY-EXISTED` with extra steps. 

⚠️ NOT A CLAIM THAT THE 403 IS ALWAYS THIS. The hosted GitHub MCP also drops intermittently (CLAUDE.md § PM-side session capabilities), and that failure is transient and self-healing. The distinguishing probe is the one that file already documents: `get_me` / `issue_read` succeeding while a WRITE 403s is a scope boundary, not a drop -- and a scope boundary is what `add_repo` moves.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) `docs/claude/coordination-board.md` and/or CLAUDE.md § 'PM-side session capabilities' name `add_repo(access="push")` as the FIRST thing to try on a write 403 against a repo outside the session's printed scope, so the next session does not re-derive it -- AND a session that was NOT told this reports having used it; OR (b) a session runs the probe, `create_pull_request` STILL 403s after a successful `add_repo(access="push")`, and records the run -- which would refute THIS row and is the more valuable outcome of the two. ⚠️ ict-trader-dashboard#211 existing does NOT close this: one success is not a documented path, and the point is that the next session finds it without a measurement.

items.title: The eight-phase operating-layer build -- the cycle's DECLARED PRIORITY, six of eight phases shipped in one day -- appears NOWHERE in ROADMAP.md, which CLAUDE.md ranks ABOVE the design series as 'the centralized record: every milestone/sprint, status, and dates'
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-01: `grep -n 'operating-layer|OPERATING-LAYER|Phase C|Phase D' ROADMAP.md` returns ZERO matches, and `grep -n 'api/bot/work' docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md` returns zero too. Positive control for the probe: the same grep style finds the operating layer throughout `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json` and `docs/claude/work/`, so the silence is ROADMAP's, not the probe's. 

WHY THIS IS THE PROGRAM'S OWN DISEASE. `docs/design/operating-layer-build-plan-DESIGN.md` opens with the ordering criterion 'the plan must survive the session that wrote it', on the grounds that the series is 'four documents in docs/design/ that NOTHING POINTS AT'. Phase A's answer was the CLAUDE.md session brief -- a good channel, and a partial one: CLAUDE.md is rank 6 in the instruction hierarchy while ROADMAP.md is rank 3 and is described there as the centralized record of every milestone and its status. A session that opens the higher-ranked document to ask 'what is this system working on' currently gets no answer, on the day six phases shipped. 

⚠️ NOT A CLAIM THAT ANY PHASE WAS DONE WRONG. Every phase A-F landed with a work object, a board post and a PR body; nothing is hidden. The gap is that none of those is the SURFACE the hierarchy says holds the milestone record, and no phase updated it -- so this is a PROGRAM-level omission repeated six times, not one session's miss, which is why it is filed once rather than against a phase. 

⚠️ AND IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED BY THE SESSION THAT FOUND IT. ROADMAP.md is a shared, high-rank document and `session_01AT7e9N9FMbrLPRbzzueexL` was building Phase G concurrently; a unilateral milestone row written by a sub-session, in the middle of another session's phase, is how two records start disagreeing about the same program. It also needs a decision this session cannot make: whether the operating layer is a MILESTONE in that table's sense at all, or a governance program the table should point AT rather than absorb.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) ROADMAP.md carries the operating-layer build with a status per phase and a link to `docs/design/operating-layer-build-plan-DESIGN.md`, and a session that opens ROADMAP.md FIRST can state which phase the build is on -- reported by a session that was NOT told; OR (b) the operator/manager decides the operating layer is deliberately NOT a ROADMAP milestone and records that decision where a reader of ROADMAP.md will meet it, so its absence reads as a choice rather than a gap. ⚠️ ADDING A ROW AND LEAVING ITS STATUS TO ROT DOES NOT SATISFY (a) -- that reproduces the condition the program exists to end, one document further up the hierarchy. ⚠️ AND A SESSION CITING THE CLAUDE.md SESSION BRIEF DOES NOT SATISFY IT EITHER: that channel already works and is separately tracked (OI-20260826-SESSION-BRIEF-NEVER-READ-BY-A-FRESH-SESSION). This row is about the rank-3 surface specifically.

items.title: session-brief-guard went red on PR #10705 with NO change to the PR and no change to main -- the UTC date rolled, two monitoring rows came DUE on their own cadence, and the rendered brief stopped matching
items.detail:
OBSERVED 2026-09-02T00:02Z on PR #10705. Sequence, all timestamped: at 2026-09-01T23:5xZ `run_guards.py` passed locally with `session-brief-guard` green and the branch was pushed. The very next CI run reported `session-brief-guard: render_session_brief.py --check --base origin/main exited 1`, verdict `introduced_registers_changed`. NOTHING in the PR changed between the green local run and the red CI run except a later commit touching ONE line of `docs/api-tier-policy.md`, and `origin/main` was unchanged at `cc1d71eb` across both. 

THE CAUSE IS THE CLOCK. `render_session_brief.py` renders the DUE monitoring rows, and due-ness is a function of `check_every_days` against TODAY. The UTC date rolled to 2026-09-02 and two rows came due on their own cadence (OI-20260901-OPERATING-LAYER-BUILD-IS-IN-FLIGHT-AND-CARRIED-ONLY-BY-THIS-ROW and OI-20260901-SCHEDULED-PROBES-AND-DUE-LIST-HAVE-NEVER-FIRED-ON-CRON), taking the block from 9 due items to 11. Re-running `--write` produced exactly that diff (+8/-2 on CLAUDE.md) and the guard went green. 

⚠️ THE GUARD IS NOT WRONG, AND THIS IS NOT A REQUEST TO WEAKEN IT. Its premise holds: a session reading a stale brief reads something no longer true. The FINDING is narrower -- the guard's verdict string says `introduced_registers_changed`, i.e. it attributes the staleness to THIS DIFF, and on this occasion the diff did not introduce it; the calendar did. A reader of that verdict looks for what their change broke and finds nothing, which is the wrong search. 

WHO THIS BITES, and it is a small but growing population: any PR that (a) touches a register the brief renders and (b) is open across a UTC midnight or a cadence boundary. Both are ordinary for a PR left for a manager or an operator to merge in the morning -- which is precisely the disposition the operating-layer sub-sessions are using tonight. 

⚠️ COST IS A FULL CI CYCLE, NOT A CORRECTNESS PROBLEM. Nothing shipped wrong; the re-render is one command and the fix is trivial. Filed because the DIAGNOSIS is not trivial: it presents as an unexplained red on an unchanged PR, and the first instinct is to hunt the diff.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) the guard distinguishes 'this diff made the brief stale' from 'the brief went stale because the register cadence advanced', and says which in its verdict -- a third verdict value, not a suppression, since both still need a re-render; OR (b) the guard's error text names the cadence roll as a candidate cause so a reader is not sent hunting their diff; OR (c) a session reproduces this and establishes the frequency is low enough that the current message is fine, and records THAT -- an explicit no-change decision is a legitimate close. ⚠️ NOT satisfied by making the guard advisory or by pinning the render to a fixed date: the brief being current is the whole mechanism (`OI-20260826-SESSION-BRIEF-NEVER-READ-BY-A-FRESH-SESSION`), and a brief that stops tracking the cadence is a brief that stops being true.

items.title: Both Alpaca close paths report a PERMANENT broker-side pending_cancel wedge identically to a transient cancel race, and the cancel helper discards the broker's answer entirely
items.detail: RECURRENCE, twice over, and that is the finding. Investigated from the live alpaca_paper GLD 'Position CLOSE failing -- won't flatten' pages of 2026-09-01. === THE BRIEFED DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG AND IS WORTH RECORDING AS SUCH. The condition was handed to this session as an extended-hours-only gap: BL-20260708-ALPACA-CLOSE-QTY-AVAILABLE was fixed for one call site and _close_extended_hours was the uncovered sibling. That was TRUE on 2026-09-01 and had ALREADY BEEN FIXED by #10666 (merged 16:23Z), which is deployed and running -- its new 'still insufficient-qty after ~6.0s' log line was verified firing on the trader at 21:19Z. The condition persisted anyway. Worse, the REGULAR-hours path failed identically at 13:30-13:34Z the same day, and that path already carries BOTH _await_qty_available AND the DELETE /v2/positions/{sym}?cancel_orders=true escalation. So there was no working sibling to port from; the sibling-call-site theory could not have explained it. === THE ACTUAL CAUSE IS BROKER-SIDE AND ALREADY HAS A ROW. GLD OCO parent 2e843e04-5487-470c-a702-70e796fbd05e sat at status 'pending_cancel' with canceled_at null, resting since 2026-08-27, holding all 39 shares as held_for_orders => qty_available 0 on every path. Our DELETE was ACCEPTED (that is what moved it to pending_cancel); Alpaca never completed its own cancel, so re-issuing an app-level cancel is a no-op and cancel_orders=true returns the same 'insufficient qty available for order (requested: 39, available: 0)'. That is BL-20260716-ALPACA-QQQ-WEDGED-PENDING-CANCEL recurring. === WHAT IS ACTUALLY DEFECTIVE IN OUR CODE (two things, both provable). (1) NOTHING READS THE FIELD THAT DISTINGUISHES THEM. The residual open-order dict already carries 'status'; both give-up paths logged the whole dict and neither ever branched on it. So a transient race (retry will clear it) and a permanent broker wedge (no retry will EVER clear it) produced a byte-identical retMsg, a byte-identical ERROR and a byte-identical 'won't flatten' page, every tick, indefinitely -- the operator could not tell 'wait' from 'this needs venue action'. (2) _cancel_open_orders_for_symbol THREW THE BROKER'S ANSWER AWAY. _request's own docstring says it 'never raises on HTTP', so the except Exception around the DELETE was dead code for every broker rejection, and the return value counted cancels ISSUED, not cancels ACCEPTED -- which close()'s 'if n_cancelled' settle-wait gate keyed on. It also collapsed a FAILED open-orders read (None) into 'nothing to cancel' ([]). Same shape as BL-20260825-PLACE-PROTECTIVE-COUNTS-THE-CANCEL-CALL-NOT-ITS-EFFECT, one venue over. === EXPOSURE. alpaca_live is mode: live / account_class: real_money, shares this client code and trades GLD. It was verified FLAT with zero resting orders at 21:23Z, so the exposure is STRUCTURAL, not realised -- but the same wedge on a real-money equity position would strand it identically on both paths. === PARTIALLY FIXED (this PR, Tier-2, DRAFT): a pure classify_share_hold() names four never-collapsed states (residual_unreadable / no_residual_orders / broker_cancel_wedged / orders_still_resting) and both give-up paths put it in the log AND the retMsg; the cancel helper now reads the envelope and reports accepted / already_gone / refused / could_not_look. This makes the condition NAMEABLE. It does NOT clear a wedged pending_cancel -- no bot-side lever does -- and the close deliberately still returns retCode 1 (a real failure), never a defer, because the failure this subsystem exists to end is the silent retry loop.
items.resolution_criteria: TWO PARTS -- closing on the instance alone is exactly what produced this recurrence. (A) INSTANCE: an alpaca close that gives up on held shares is OBSERVED emitting share_hold=<state> in both its log and its retMsg on the live fleet, AND a broker_cancel_wedged instance is seen being acted on as a wedge (operator/venue action) rather than retried indefinitely. Reading the code is not the observation. (B) CLASS: no remaining path that cancels or closes an Alpaca order treats a non-2xx from _request as success. Verify by grepping every _request("DELETE", ...) call site for an unchecked return -- the check that was missing when BL-20260708 was closed for one call site while its sibling went uncovered. Additionally: decide and record whether a confirmed broker_cancel_wedged should keep paging at full severity forever, or escalate to a distinct 'needs venue action' alert -- today it rides the ordinary close-failure page, which is the desensitisation risk.

items.title: runtime_logs/operator_alerts.jsonl -- the ring behind every /api/bot/notifications banner -- had no diag read surface, so no session can grade whether an alarm backoff actually works
items.detail: RECURRENCE of BL-20260825-ALERT-AND-CADENCE-STATE-FILES-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE, which was itself already recorded as the third instance of this shape (after exit_loop_health #8778). execution_diagnostics._append_operator_alert writes EVERY alert that reaches the /api/bot/notifications banner feed to runtime_logs/operator_alerts.jsonl (close_failure, orphan, stuck-package-sweep, siblings). It is bounded but NOT to a fixed 300: _OPERATOR_ALERTS_KEEP is 300 yet the trim fires only past 2x that, so the file holds 300-600 rows and its oldest row's age is not a constant -- state the ts span you actually got before quoting any rate, or this row's own remedy reproduces the unstated-denominator error it exists to end. It was absent from diag.py::_LOG_FILES, so /api/diag/log_file?name=operator_alerts returned HTTP 400 and the file was unreachable from any relay-bound session. === WHY IT BLOCKED REAL WORK. This session was asked to establish whether a live, hours-long close_failure condition was PAGING THE OPERATOR REPEATEDLY -- the desensitised-alarm question CLAUDE.md calls a P1. That is unanswerable without this file: /api/bot/notifications renders only the CURRENT banner and carries no history, and a page RATE is recoverable nowhere else. The backoff shipped in #10666 therefore cannot be shown to work; it can only be read in the source, which is a deploy, not an observation. === AND THE OBVIOUS SUBSTITUTE IS A TRAP, MEASURED. These alerts deliberately do NOT ride outcomes.jsonl, so /api/bot/logs?level=error,warn returns ZERO close_failure rows. Measured 2026-09-01 over the full 1000-row ERROR/WARN feed (2026-08-21T23:36Z -> 2026-09-01T20:47Z): zero close-failure rows, while the banner was rendering an active close_failure for alpaca_paper/GLD at that moment. A reviewer grading alarm health from the documented ERROR feed would conclude this alarm has never fired in eleven days. That is the same 'a DERIVED surface was measured and a conclusion drawn without establishing that the surface reports every instance' error recorded in BL-20260825-TRANSIENT-CLASSIFIER-MISSES-THE-VARIANT-FAMILIES -- this session made it and caught it only by reading enqueue_close_failure. === FIXED in this PR: one allowlist entry (Tier-1, read-only), shipped in the same commit as the finding. === SEPARATELY NOTED while measuring that feed, not fixed here: 839 of those 1000 ERROR/WARN rows (83.9%) are strategy_builder no-candle exceptions across six legs, which is the alarm-fatigue condition BL-20260825-TRANSIENT-CLASSIFIER-MISSES-THE-VARIANT-FAMILIES already owns -- still live, and worse than when filed.
items.resolution_criteria: (A) INSTANCE: /api/diag/log_file?name=operator_alerts returns rows from the live VM (HTTP 200, non-empty), and a session uses it to state a MEASURED page rate for a close_failure streak -- e.g. 'N pages over M minutes at streak K' -- confirming or refuting #10666's exponential backoff against real data. A 400 or an empty read does not close this. (B) CLASS: every file whose contents decide whether an operator is paged, or how long a safety input may age, has a read surface registered in the SAME commit as its writer. This is the fourth recorded instance; the durable fix is a guard, not another allowlist entry. Consider extending an existing CI guard to fail when a new runtime_logs/*_state or *_alerts writer lands with no _LOG_FILES entry -- the alert-side analogue of provenance-consumer-guard.
items.resolution: CLOSED ON CRITERION (A) INSTANCE, both halves, with the measurement the criterion demanded. HALF ONE — the route serves: GET /api/diag/log_file?name=operator_alerts returned HTTP 200, present:true, /data/bot-data/runtime_logs/operator_alerts.jsonl, 233,776 bytes, 302 rows parsed. `operator_alerts` is in diag.py::_LOG_FILES. HALF TWO — THE MEASURED PAGE RATE, which is what the row said a 200 alone does not buy. POPULATION, stated because the row's own detail insists on it: all 302 rows of the ring as served, ts span 2026-09-04T12:31:29Z -> 2026-09-09T06:44:24Z; kinds close_failure 129 / monitor_blindness 85 / stuck_strategy 53 / orphan_reconciliation 18 / orphan_created 4 / exchange_orphan_adoption 4 / stuck_package_sweep 3 / execution_failure 3 / all_accounts_failed 3. The close_failure rows are alpaca_paper/GLD 124, bybit_1 SOL/ETH/XRP 5. The GLD streak: 124 pages over 107.25h = 1.16 pages/hour overall. #10666's EXPONENTIAL BACKOFF IS CONFIRMED WORKING against real data — inter-page interval by streak, median minutes: streak 13-14 -> 5.0/5.5 · 33-35 -> 10.1/10.5 · 74-75 -> 20.5 · 154-156 -> 40.0 · 274-276 -> 60.0 · and it HOLDS AT THE CAP out to streak 1117 -> 60.0. That is a clean doubling ladder terminating in a 60-minute ceiling, which is the designed behaviour, measured rather than read from the diff. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, said explicitly rather than folded in: criterion (B) CLASS — the writer-side guard that would stop a sixth occurrence — is NOT built. Its natural home, BL-20260825-ALERT-AND-CADENCE-STATE-FILES-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE, is already `resolved` while its own criterion 3 records the guard as NOT DONE, so clause (B) would have no open carrier. It is therefore re-filed as its own row by this session (see BL-20260909-NO-WRITER-SIDE-GUARD-STOPS-A-PAGING-INPUT-SHIPPING-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE-AND-ITS-ONLY-CARRIER-IS-A-RESOLVED-ROW), which is the one new row this closing-only session filed, and it is filed because closing this one would otherwise DELETE the class finding.

items.title: Syncing a branch to main re-fires pr-opener, whose bot results commit becomes the PR head and silently disarms CI — so the sync intended to arm CI disarms it
items.detail: MEASURED TWICE ON PR #10679 IN ONE HOUR. pr-opener.yml triggers on `push: paths: ['automation/pr-requests/**']`. Those request files are COMMITTED and reach `main`, so MERGING `origin/main` INTO ANY BRANCH replays other branches' request files through that trigger path -- the push event touches `automation/pr-requests/**` even though the branch's own author changed nothing there. pr-opener then runs and pushes an `automation/pr-results/**` commit authored by `github-actions[bot]` with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN, which becomes the PR HEAD. === WHY THAT IS THE HARMFUL PART. GitHub deliberately does not trigger workflows for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes (recursion prevention), a cause pr-opener.yml's OWN header already documents and isolated on PR #10079. So the head carries ZERO check runs, and `total_count: 0` reads identically to 'CI has not started yet' and to green while actually being blocked -- the exact confusion BL-20260830-ZERO-CHECK-RUNS-READ-AS-CI-NOT-STARTED-NOT-AS-MERGE-CONFLICT and BL-20260720-GH-ACTIONS-PUSH-EVENTS-DEAD were filed about. === WHAT IS NEW HERE, and why this is not a duplicate of that header. The header documents the GITHUB_TOKEN cause and prescribes the remedy ('push one ordinary commit yourself to arm CI'). It does NOT record that the ARMING ACTION ITSELF RE-TRIGGERS THE DISARMING WORKFLOW: the standard remedy for a behind/conflicted branch is to merge main, and merging main is precisely what replays the trigger path. Measured sequence on #10679: (1) 57219eec, an ordinary merge of main, armed CI and 4 checks ran; (2) a later merge of main brought `automation/pr-requests/prop-fills-gap-20260901.json` in via #10678, pr-opener fired and pushed 10c1b8da 'pr-opener: results', and check runs went back to 0. === SIBLING, not the same row: BL-20260821-BOARD-POST-RECEIPT-IS-PER-BRANCH records the same per-branch-receipt-vs-merged-request asymmetry for board-post.yml, where the consequence is a DUPLICATE POST. Here the consequence is SILENTLY UNVERIFIED CI on a Tier-2 order-path PR, which is worse: a duplicate post is visible, a missing check run is not. The two share a cause and should probably be fixed together. === NOT FIXED HERE. This PR only worked around it by pushing another ordinary commit. Candidate durable fixes, none attempted: exclude merge commits from the trigger (`if: github.event_ref_type` / a head-commit-parent check), scope the trigger to pushes whose OWN diff touches a request file, move the results receipt off the branch entirely, or push the receipt with a PAT/app token so it triggers workflows normally -- pr-opener.yml's header already names the last of these as the durable fix it did not attempt.
items.resolution_criteria: A branch that merges `origin/main` while other branches' `automation/pr-requests/**` files are present on main ends with a NON-bot head and non-zero check runs, DEMONSTRATED on a real PR rather than reasoned from the workflow YAML. A pr-opener run that no-ops on an already-resulted filename is NOT sufficient -- the problem is any bot commit reaching the head, whatever its content. Consider closing together with BL-20260821-BOARD-POST-RECEIPT-IS-PER-BRANCH, which shares the cause.

items.source: Found while draining the diagnostic-provenance standing audit (D/inert-parameter) on 2026-09-02; the guard flagged the unread parameter, the divergence was found by reading the sibling.
items.title: [research] hf_vectorized.replay and hf_solo_sim.simulate take the SAME `signal_ttl_bars` parameter and implement DIFFERENT semantics — the vectorized one hardcodes a 1-bar TTL and ignored the argument entirely
items.detail:
MEASURED by reading both files at commit 0dcfcd1e.

`scripts/research/hf_solo_sim.py::simulate` implements a real expiry: it acts on a pending signal while `i - latest_idx >= signal_ttl_bars`.
`scripts/research/hf_vectorized.py::replay` accepted `signal_ttl_bars=1`, NEVER READ IT, and acts on a signal only on the exact bar it arrives (`i == pend_idx`) — an effective TTL hardcoded to 1.

POPULATION / BLAST RADIUS TODAY: all four call sites of `replay` inside hf_vectorized.py (lines 423, 433, 471, 498) use the default, and the default (1) HAPPENS TO MATCH the hardcoded behaviour. So no result produced so far is wrong because of this. That is luck, not design.

WHAT WAS DONE IN THIS SESSION, AND WHAT WAS NOT. `replay` now RAISES NotImplementedError on a non-default `signal_ttl_bars` instead of silently ignoring it, so a future sweep can no longer get a ttl=1 run wearing a ttl=N label. That removes the silent-wrong-answer hazard. It does NOT reconcile the two harnesses, and reconciling them was deliberately left alone: implementing the expiry in the vectorized replay would change every number it has ever produced, which is a research-semantics decision and not a backlog drain's call.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS: the two harnesses exist to be compared. A comparison between a 1-bar-TTL engine and a configurable-TTL engine is not apples-to-apples, and nothing in either file says so.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when either (a) hf_vectorized.replay implements the same `i - latest_idx >= signal_ttl_bars` expiry as hf_solo_sim.simulate, demonstrated by a test that plants a signal and asserts it is still actionable at ttl-1 bars later and not at ttl bars later — AND the change is reported as invalidating prior vectorized results; or (b) an operator/research decision RECORDS that the vectorized engine is 1-bar-TTL by design, at which point the parameter is removed from its signature rather than left raising. Reading the diff is not enough for (a): the test must fail on the current code.

items.source: Found while draining the diagnostic-provenance standing audit (D/inert-parameter) on 2026-09-02.
items.title: [research] recombination_sweep._build_label accepts `entry_key` and never puts it in the label — two entry variants sharing a family produce the SAME label for different sweep cells
items.detail:
MEASURED by reading scripts/ops/recombination_sweep.py at commit 0dcfcd1e.

`_build_label(entry_key, family, symbol, tf, regime, exit_, sel)` builds `<family>_<symbol>_<tf>_<regime>_<trail>_<conf>` and never reads `entry_key`. The caller loops `for entry_key, ent in entries.items()` and takes `family = ent['family']`, so the label is unique per cell ONLY IF family is 1:1 with entry_key. Two entry variants in the same family (e.g. two `trend` entries) would produce identical labels for genuinely different sweep cells.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: whether the live pool config actually contains two entry variants sharing a family. That is data this session did not read — the entries come from a pool file, not from the code. So this is a HAZARD with a named precondition, not an observed collision. Anyone picking it up should check the pool first; if no family is shared, the correct disposition may be to document the invariant rather than change the label.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED HERE: adding entry_key to the label rewrites the label of every existing sweep artifact, which is an artifact-compatibility decision. The parameter is marked `# inert:` naming the hazard so the next reader sees it at the call site.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED when EITHER (a) the pool config is read and shown to contain no two entry keys sharing a `family` — state the pool path and the entry->family mapping you measured — and that invariant is asserted in code or a test, so it cannot silently stop holding; OR (b) the label includes entry_key, with the artifact-renaming consequence stated. A code citation does not close this: the entry->family mapping is DATA and must be read.

items.title: The scope-overlap audit reports an unattributable START forever, so one dead session's broad path claim taxes every later PR touching that tree
items.source: manager session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ, from the audit's own comment on PR #10749
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-02T05:25:09Z, read from the scope-overlap comment posted on PR #10749 (NOT from my own read of the START comment, which I did not open -- stated so the basis is not overclaimed). The audit reported all 3 of that PR's changed files (docs/claude/work/{MANAGER-CHECKLIST,MANAGER-LEASE,SESSIONS}.json) as overlapping a START at issue #6927 comment 5493592617, timestamped 2026-09-01T11:59:53Z -- roughly 17.5 hours earlier -- which declared the whole of `docs/claude/work/` and which the attributor graded `unattributable` because its body 'names no branch and no session id in a self-identifying position, and does not name this PR'. TWO SEPARATE FACTS, and the first is GOOD NEWS that should be carried to BL-20260831-SCOPE-OVERLAP-ATTRIBUTOR-GRADES-A-SESSIONS-OWN-START-AS-ANOTHERS: the same comment reads '3 matched your OWN declaration and were not reported', so the session-suffix matching that row proposed appears to have landed and worked on a live PR -- which is that row's resolution_criteria (b). Whoever closes it should verify (a) too rather than closing on this alone. THE RESIDUAL IS THE SECOND FACT: a START has no expiry and `unattributable` resolves toward reporting (correctly -- the row above is explicit that under-reporting a real overlap is the worse error). But the two together mean a single broad, badly-formed claim from a session that is long gone keeps producing an overlap block on EVERY subsequent PR touching that subtree, indefinitely. INFERRED, not measured: at the manager-state files' commit rate this fires on essentially every manager PR. That is the desensitized-alarm shape CLAUDE.md names as its own P1 -- a correct detector whose output is walked past because it is always there. NOT PROPOSING that unattributable be suppressed or aged out silently; that would trade a noisy true positive for a silent false negative, which is the direction this repo has explicitly ruled against. The tractable moves are to make the AGE of an unattributable START visible in the comment so a reader can weigh it, and/or to make the board protocol require a self-identifying START (branch + session id), so `unattributable` becomes rare rather than structural.
items.resolution_criteria: A scope-overlap comment on a real PR either (a) shows the age of each unattributable START beside it, so a reader can tell an 18-hour-old dead claim from a live one, or (b) reports zero unattributable declarations because the board protocol now requires a self-identifying START and the extractor enforces it. In EITHER case an unattributable overlap must still be REPORTED, never suppressed -- a change that reduces the count by hiding overlaps does not resolve this row and is the worse error.

items.title: A manager CAN wake an idle cloud sub-session: create_trigger(persistent_session_id) + fire_trigger works, and the standing 'unreachable' note is wrong
items.source: manager session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-02T05:35Z. The standing manager note (MI-32) said an idle cloud sub-session is UNREACHABLE from the manager. That was true of the two mechanisms it tested -- SendMessage and ListAgents, neither of which addresses a cloud session from here -- and it generalised from those two to the capability. IT IS WRONG. A poke-only Routine bound to the session works: create_trigger with persistent_session_id set and BOTH cron_expression and run_once_at omitted, then fire_trigger on the returned id. EVIDENCE, not inference: session_01PcirVtpMXJGiKm2548nkrR read session_status=SESSION_STATUS_IDLE / connection_status=disconnected on a get_session immediately before the fire, and SESSION_STATUS_RUNNING / connected on a get_session immediately after, same session id, its own working context intact. Trigger trig_01NcP7PmwUeFPCbRN4G61VQX. COST OF THE WRONG NOTE, measured the same night: MI-37 was archived and respawned TWICE on the belief that a stalled sub-session cannot be steered, and the second respawn was caused by the manager's own corrective instruction rather than by the original fault. ⚠️ TWO LIMITS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS FINDING. (1) The fired turn runs WITHOUT mcp__* TOOLS -- the tool warns that a Routine created this way stores no connectors. A poked session keeps Bash/git/file tools and so keeps the pr-opener and board-post relays, but loses mcp__github__* outright; that is fine for a sub-session that already 403s on GitHub writes, and NOT fine for one that needs the MCP to finish. (2) It is a ONE-WAY WAKE, not a reply channel: the poked session cannot answer the manager, so the outcome is still read from the branch, the PR, or get_session. NOT YET ESTABLISHED, and deliberately not claimed: whether the woken turn behaves identically to a normal turn in every respect, and whether repeated pokes to one session degrade anything. One observation, one session. || ⚠️ CONFIRMED AGAIN 2026-09-08T05:41-05:43Z, ON TWO MORE INDEPENDENT SESSIONS, AND THE CHANNEL IS NOT 100% RELIABLE — that second half is new and is the part a manager must not assume away. POPULATION: three idle/blocked sub-sessions poked in one two-minute window, each create_trigger(persistent_session_id) + fire_trigger, each graded by get_session immediately before and after. TWO WOKE: MI-185 session_015iukpShDdwvP5CM79Qtt3B (IDLE/disconnected -> RUNNING/connected, updated_at moved to exactly the fire time 05:41:39Z) and MI-183 session_0173g82hw2Rf3HjnfydGcnyX (IDLE -> RUNNING/connected 05:42:52Z, task_summary 'Checking whether any git pre-push hook exists' — i.e. visibly ACTING on the poked instruction, not merely resumed). ONE DID NOT: MI-176 session_018iDJZVj11ugKyUwsHF7X3q stayed IDLE with updated_at unchanged at 05:09:06Z, and the fire_trigger response returned a DIFFERENT session id (cse_014BiZjfw8T3jtHX7cRMg8e4) instead of the target — i.e. it spawned a fresh session rather than resuming the bound one. ⚠️ THE FAILURE IS SILENT AT THE CALL SITE: fire_trigger returned success with last_fired_at set, and the ONLY signal was that the returned session_id did not match the persistent_session_id. A manager that does not compare those two ids will believe it delivered when it did not. ALWAYS grade the poke by a get_session before/after on the TARGET id, never by fire_trigger's own success. ⚠️ CANDIDATE CAUSE, NOT ESTABLISHED: the session that failed to resume had by far the largest context of the three (459,520 tokens used against 1M, vs 127,664 and 174,909) and was the oldest. That is one observation and a correlation; do not repeat it as a mechanism. || REFINEMENT: this row says to omit BOTH cron_expression and run_once_at for a poke-only Routine. A far-future run_once_at plus an immediate fire_trigger ALSO works (used for all three above), and has the property that the Routine self-disables after firing. || ⚠️ AND THE COST THIS ROW PREDICTS WAS PAID AGAIN: SESSIONS.json's own _comment still read 'IT IS A REGISTRY, NOT A CHANNEL. A manager CANNOT message a sub-session ... Verified by test, not assumed' SIX DAYS after this row was filed. The 2026-09-08 manager read that line, believed it, and left three sessions blocked on questions it could have answered — until it re-derived the channel from the tool surface by accident. The row was filed and taught nothing, which is the exact failure the backlog discipline exists to prevent. The _comment is corrected in the same change as this addendum. || ⚠️ CORRECTION 2026-09-08T06:14Z — THE CANDIDATE CAUSE RECORDED ABOVE IS FALSIFIED, and by the cleanest possible test: the SAME session was poked again and woke. session_018iDJZVj11ugKyUwsHF7X3q went PENDING/connected with updated_at exactly the second fire time, from the SAME context size (459,520 tokens) and the same age that the earlier addendum offered as the reason it failed. So context size and session age are NOT the mechanism, and that sentence must not be repeated. THE ACTUAL DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE TWO CALLS: the FAILED one passed fire_trigger's optional `text` parameter; the SUCCEEDING one passed only trigger_id. Both other successful pokes that night (MI-185, MI-183) also omitted `text`. n=1 on the failure and n=3 on the success, so this is a STRONGER reading than the one it replaces but is still not established — it is a correlation over four calls, and nobody has read the routing code. PRACTICAL RULE, which holds whatever the mechanism turns out to be: poke with trigger_id ALONE, and put any run-specific context in the Routine's own prompt rather than in `text`. And keep grading every poke by comparing the returned session_id against the persistent_session_id — that comparison caught this, and it is the only signal there is.
items.resolution_criteria: The manager-facing guidance (MANAGER-CHECKLIST MI-32 and any skill or doc that repeats 'an idle sub-session is unreachable') states the poke-only-Routine channel WITH its two limits -- no mcp__* tools on the fired turn, and one-way only -- and a second independent session is observed being woken this way and completing the work it was poked to finish. ⚠️ The first half alone does NOT resolve this: documenting a capability is not evidence it works twice, and this row rests on a single observation.
