items.title: ict_scalp_avax_5m/exit_head_ml is recorded honest_negative, its own cell carries the counter-evidence that the negative did not survive a larger book, and the question has read 'QUEUED for the operator' for 19 days
items.source: Carried out of BL-20260815-SCALP-EXIT-HEAD-MATRIX-DISAGREES-WITH-THE-4-ARM-SCREEN, which is resolved 2026-09-02 on its criterion -- that criterion's text is sol-only while its title also covered this second cell, so the residue is filed rather than closed with it. Read 2026-09-02 out of docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json, row strategy=ict_scalp_avax_5m, cell exit_head_ml.
items.why_it_matters: A recorded verdict that its OWN cell says does not reproduce is worse than an absent one: a reader scanning the matrix column sees `honest_negative` and stops, and the contradiction is four sentences into a ref nobody opens. The cell reads: E1 2026-08-13 n_oos=1000 auc=0.6221 beats_actual=18/20 beats_hard=13/20 -> DOWNGRADED to honest_negative; then COUNTER-EVIDENCE 2026-08-14 (round scalp_5m_20260814T151003Z, relay #9333) re-measured at live parity on a 45% LARGER book -- n_oos 1000 -> 1450, auc 0.6221 -> 0.6175, beats_actual 25/29, beats_hard 24/29 -> CANDIDATE, clearing the gate by 14 points of 58 on the BINDING beats_hard term. Status was left at honest_negative deliberately and correctly (a recorded verdict is not flipped inside the session that produced the re-measurement) and QUEUED for the operator -- and then nothing answered it. ⚠️ NOTE THE ASYMMETRY WITH ITS SIBLING: the sol cell's ship question WAS answered (cancelled, operator 2026-08-23) in the same review; this one was not, so the pair is now half-decided. ⚠️ AND THE DECISION MAY BE MOOT ON A DIFFERENT GROUND, which must not be confused with answering it: ict_scalp has NO exit-head consumer (BL-20260816-EXIT-HEAD-LEVER-HAS-NO-CONSUMER-IN-ICT-SCALP), so even a flip to candidate would be unshippable today. 'It could not ship anyway' is a reason the question is cheap, NOT a reason the recorded status is right.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) the operator answers the status question for ict_scalp_avax_5m -- hold honest_negative, or re-grade on the larger book -- and the answer is written onto the cell with its date, so the 'QUEUED' state is discharged rather than aged; OR (b) the cell is re-graded from ONE agreed parameterization (same fold-mode, same tp_geometry, same book, arm count recorded) and the matrix records that run. ⚠️ Closing this by re-running once and taking whichever verdict comes back does NOT satisfy it -- that is the same single-partition mistake the parent row's 4-arm screen showed to be insufficient, and this cell has never had a 4-arm screen at all. ⚠️ Nor does 'the lever cannot ship on ict_scalp anyway' close it: that answers a different question.
items.next_action: Route the status question to the operator alongside the ict_scalp exit-head-consumer decision (clause (c) of BL-20260816-EXIT-HEAD-LEVER-HAS-NO-CONSUMER-IN-ICT-SCALP) -- they are the same conversation and answering them separately is what left this one behind.

items.title: runtime_logs/pending_claude_pings has TWO live drainers on a 5s tick, so one enqueue was delivered to two conversations — and when the race is won outright the channel is picked by scheduler phase
items.detail:
MEASURED (live journals via /api/diag/journalctl, ict-bot-arm, read 2026-09-01; units ict-claude-bridge.service pid 3708572 and ict-telegram-bot.service pid 3696145). The operator reported first-hand that the test ping dispatched at 22:10:17Z (system-action send-ping, target=claude, file 436339508894-normal.json) arrived in BOTH the new dedicated @ict_cluade_bot channel AND the old trader chat. One enqueue, two deliveries.

CAUSE. The queue has two registered drainers, both live, both on a 5s interval, both resolving the SAME directory via runtime_logs_dir(): (a) claude_bridge._drain_pending_claude_pings (ict-claude-bridge.service) and (b) the _drain_claude_pings job in telegram_query_bot (ict-telegram-bot.service), added 2026-06-22 when the bridge was dead on the Ampere VM and these pings were silently never delivered for weeks. Each does read -> send -> unlink, so the file stays on disk for the whole Telegram POST. Interleaving, from the journals: 22:10:19.934 bridge tick starts; 22:10:21 trader-bot tick reads the SAME file; 22:10:23.212 bridge POST returns, unlinks. The bridge's POST took 3.28s where every other tick that day completed in ~1ms.

The two copies went to different bots because the trader-bot process started 21:37:37Z — BEFORE TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET was set at 22:08:26Z — and logged at 21:37:41Z 'claude pings: no dedicated bot (token_state=fallback ... isolated=False)'. _resolve_claude_bot caches once per process, so that verdict is permanent for its lifetime. NOTE both units share EnvironmentFile=/home/ubuntu/ict-trading-bot/.env, so restarting ict-telegram-bot would make it resolve the dedicated token too and put BOTH copies in the new channel — same bug, less visible. Do not 'fix' it that way.

THE DUPLICATE IS THE VISIBLE HALF AND THE LESS SERIOUS ONE. When the POST is fast the race is won outright and only one copy is sent — but WHICH conversation it lands in is then decided by scheduler phase, so an operator cannot learn where to look. isolated=True on the bridge's route line is true and insufficient: a route isolated at one sender is not isolation while a second sender delivers the same payload.

DENOMINATOR — n=1, and a real rate is NOT OBTAINABLE from the VM today. cloud_notifier's _drain_one_ping_dir logs nothing on a successful send, so the trader-bot copy leaves no trace; only the operator's eyes caught this one. Filed separately as BL-20260901-PING-DRAIN-LOGS-NOTHING-ON-SUCCESS. What the mechanism predicts: a duplicate requires the winning drainer's POST to exceed the ~2s phase gap between the two 5s ticks, so it is intermittent, not every ping.

CLASS SIBLING (not a duplicate): BL-20260816-IB-DUPLICATE-STOPS-IN-SEPARATE-OCA-GROUPS — two independent actors on one resource, neither aware of the other. Different subsystem, same shape.

FIX PREPARED, NOT MERGED, NOT DEPLOYED — draft PR on branch claude/claude-ping-double-delivery-x4mq2p; the manager owns the merge. The bridge becomes the OWNER and the trader-bot drain a declared FAILOVER gated on CLAUDE_PING_FAILOVER_GRACE_S (default 60s): it takes only files the bridge demonstrably has not. Deleting the second drainer was rejected — it would re-open the 2026-06-22 outage. The gate SKIPS, never unlinks, and an unreadable mtime DELIVERS, because the failure this path has actually paid for is LOSS (src/runtime/notify.py, 2026-06-23), not duplication.
items.next_step: After the draft PR merges and ict-telegram-bot restarts on the merged sha, dispatch a send-ping and confirm it arrives in the dedicated channel ONLY. Then check the trader-bot journal for the 'FAILOVER delivering' WARNING — its ABSENCE is the pass (a healthy bridge means the failover takes nothing). A merge is a deploy, not an observation.
items.resolution_criteria: A send-ping dispatched AFTER the fix merges and ict-telegram-bot restarts on the merged sha arrives in the dedicated @ict_cluade_bot channel ONLY — confirmed by the operator, who is the only party who can see both conversations — AND the ict-telegram-bot journal for that window carries NO 'FAILOVER delivering' WARNING (its absence is the pass: a healthy bridge means the failover takes nothing). ⚠️ A MERGE IS NOT AN OBSERVATION and neither is a green test: the trader-bot process caches its route once at start, so the restart is load-bearing. ⚠️ A quiet channel does NOT close this — if nothing arrives at all, delivery broke and THAT is the finding.

items.title: cloud_notifier's ping drain logs nothing on a successful send, so a double delivery has no denominator and is invisible from the VM
items.detail:
MEASURED (src/bot/cloud_notifier.py::_drain_one_ping_dir, read 2026-09-01; live journal of ict-telegram-bot.service 22:09:00Z-22:12:00Z, which returned ONE non-scheduler line and none about a send). The drain logs on malformed JSON, on send failure, on a stale legacy straggler and on a mis-routed legacy ping — and logs NOTHING when a ping is delivered. The bridge's own drain does log ('Telegram send: ok=True message_id=3', 22:10:23Z) because it goes through notify.send_telegram_direct; this path calls bot.send_message directly.

CONSEQUENCE, and it is why this is filed rather than left as a nit: when BL-20260901-CLAUDE-PING-TWO-DRAINERS-ONE-QUEUE double-delivered a ping, the second copy left no trace anywhere on the VM. The duplicate was detectable ONLY because a human happened to be watching two Telegram conversations at once. So the question 'how often does this happen' has no answer from any surface, and 'the drain is quiet' is indistinguishable from 'the drain is not running'. That is the silent-empty shape on the consumer side.

PARTIALLY ADDRESSED, deliberately not closed, by the draft PR on branch claude/claude-ping-double-delivery-x4mq2p: it adds a WARNING on the FAILOVER delivery path only (the case that means the bridge is down). An ordinary successful delivery from either drainer still logs nothing, so there is still no denominator for delivery volume.
items.next_step: Add an INFO line on successful delivery naming the file and the resolved route (telegram_routes.describe(), which names the VARIABLE and never the token value), so delivery volume and destination are countable from the journal. Then re-measure the duplicate rate over a stated window instead of over n=1.
items.resolution_criteria: /api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-telegram-bot over a window containing a known-delivered claude ping returns a line naming that ping file and its resolved route, so delivery is countable from the journal. ⚠️ The line must name the VARIABLE that answered (telegram_routes.describe()), never a token value. ⚠️ Adding the line is a deploy; this closes when a real delivered ping is FOUND in the journal, not when the writer merges.

items.title: Ping-drain tests drive coroutines with asyncio.get_event_loop(), so they pass alone and fail on suite order after a module that uses asyncio.run
items.detail:
OBSERVED while adding tests on 2026-09-01 (sandbox, pytest 3.11). A new test module using asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(...) passed in isolation (9/9) and failed 6/9 when tests/test_claude_ping_routing.py ran first — that module uses asyncio.run, which closes its loop. Switching to a fresh new_event_loop() per call made it order-independent (verified in both orders). tests/test_send_ping.py uses the same get_event_loop() idiom and may be exposed to the same ordering hazard.

⚠️ STATE THE LIMIT: that last part is NOT established. This sandbox lacks PyYAML, so every test in test_send_ping.py that touches the bot modules errors at import (ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml', src/prop/ruleset.py:18) BOTH on this branch and on an unmodified origin/main — 13 identical baseline failures. So its behaviour under a working dependency set was not measured here, and the yaml failures must not be read as an ordering problem. The order-dependence is confirmed only for the idiom, in the new module.
items.next_step: In an environment with the real dependency set, run tests/test_send_ping.py after tests/test_claude_ping_routing.py and see whether it fails on loop state rather than on imports. If it does, replace get_event_loop() with a per-call new_event_loop() there too.
items.resolution_criteria: In an environment holding the real dependency set (PyYAML present, so the modules import), `pytest tests/test_claude_ping_routing.py tests/test_send_ping.py` and the reverse order both pass. ⚠️ If test_send_ping.py still fails on IMPORTS there, that is a different problem and does not close this row. If it passes in both orders as-is, the row closes as NOT-A-DEFECT-THERE — record which, since 'we could not reproduce' and 'it is fine' are different findings.

items.title: A1's constraint readout has no cadence and no staleness guard — it is only as fresh as the last session that typed the command
items.source: Phase-G skills/workflows inventory, session_01YBQQzvgJzSumk1APmjiG7B (docs/audits/operating-layer-skills-workflows-inventory-2026-09-02.md)
items.detail: scripts/ops/constraint_readout.py renders docs/claude/READOUT.md + CONSTRAINT.json, whose headline is inlined into the CLAUDE.md SESSION BRIEF and is what the operator's cycle priority (A2) rests on. The operating model classifies A1 as trigger Cadenced / autonomy Full. MEASURED 2026-09-02: it is NEITHER. (a) No workflow invokes it — `grep -rn constraint_readout .github/workflows/` returns 0 hits over all 129 files. (b) CI runs `--self-test` ONLY; its registration at scripts/ci/run_guards.py:289 carries the note, in the guard's own words, "self-test only; the readout itself is generated on demand, not in CI". (c) CONSTRAINT.json generated_at read 2026-09-01T23:15:16Z at audit time. CONTRAST ITS SIBLING: session-brief-guard runs BOTH `--self-test` AND `--check --base origin/main`, so the session brief cannot go stale without reddening a PR; the readout has no equivalent. This is the work_digest.py defect (shipped with no trigger, appeared in 0 of 125 workflow files) RECURRING WITHIN ONE DAY, in the function with the largest blast radius — work-digest.yml's own header records that precedent as one it exists not to repeat. A readout that ages silently is worse than an absent one: the brief presents it with a date most readers will not diff against today. NOTE THE REMEDY IS A CRON, NOT A GUARD — a staleness --check would red every PR whenever the world moved (BL-20260830-A-TRANSIENT-RED-BASE-PERMANENTLY-STRANDS-AN-AUTOMERGE-BRANCH), which is why session-brief-guard had to be diff-scoped. The working shape exists twice already: work-digest.yml and strategy-review-packets.yml.
items.resolution_criteria: A scheduled workflow regenerates and COMMITS docs/claude/READOUT.md + CONSTRAINT.json, AND a run with event=schedule is observed having done so — verified by the run's EVENT being `schedule`, never by the file existing (a dispatch-driven run writes a byte-identical artifact). Until then, treat READOUT.md's date as the only evidence of its freshness.

items.title: Issue-driven workflows' run counts are dominated by skipped label-filter evaluations, so 87 of 129 workflows are unretireable-by-evidence
items.source: Phase-G skills/workflows inventory, session_01YBQQzvgJzSumk1APmjiG7B (docs/audits/operating-layer-skills-workflows-inventory-2026-09-02.md)
items.detail: Every issue opened in this repo triggers EVERY `issues:`-triggered workflow, each of which then evaluates its label filter and SKIPS. MEASURED 2026-09-02 over all 132 registry workflows: provision-live-vm.yml reads 10,690 lifetime runs with last_conclusion=skipped; claude-run-failure-alert.yml reads 24,445. 87 of the 129 on-disk workflows have their most recent run as a skipped label-filter evaluation dated today. CONSEQUENCE: `runs_total` is not a usage signal for these, and the question a sunset pass must answer — 'has this workflow ever actually done work, and when last?' — has NO cheap surface. This audit could grade dormancy for only 42 of 129 (the push/dispatch/cron-triggered ones), which is why its retire list is 8 and not larger. This is the binding constraint on E3 for workflows: every future sunset pass hits the same wall. Answering it needs a per-workflow scan filtered to non-skipped conclusions.
items.resolution_criteria: A committed artifact exists giving, per workflow, the count and date of its most recent NON-SKIPPED run, refreshed on a cadence — and it is READ by something (sunset-pass.yml is the natural host, since it already reads committed artifacts weekly). A one-off manual scan does not resolve this; the point is that the next sunset pass can answer the question without re-deriving it.

items.title: enabled:true + no cron + next_run_at 0001-01-01 reads identically for a deliberate poke-only Routine and a structurally-dead one
items.source: Phase-G skills/workflows inventory, session_01YBQQzvgJzSumk1APmjiG7B (docs/audits/operating-layer-skills-workflows-inventory-2026-09-02.md)
items.detail: The design series records two Routines (`Health Check Routine`, `Sprint Continue Work`) that sat `enabled: true` with `next_run_at: 0001-01-01` and NO schedule for four months — 'a mechanism that looks armed and is not'. MEASURED 2026-09-02: those two are GONE from the register (list_triggers(enabled=true) returns exactly 2 routines and neither is them; positive control — the call did return two live routines, so the probe finds positives). ⚠️ ATTRIBUTION UNKNOWN: established is that they are absent as this session can read the register, NOT who deleted them or when. BUT THE SHAPE IS BACK: trig_01NcP7PmwUeFPCbRN4G61VQX (created 2026-09-02T05:35Z) is enabled:true, has no cron_expression, and reads next_run_at 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z — byte-identical in register shape to the two dead ones. Here it is DELIBERATE: a poke-only routine the manager fires by hand via fire_trigger. THE FINDING IS THAT THE REGISTER OFFERS NO FIELD SEPARATING THE TWO. This is the collapsed-state class this repo has a CI guard for, sitting in the Claude Code Remote control plane rather than in code, and it is the direct reason the two dead ones survived in plain sight — a reader auditing the register today cannot repeat the 2026-09-01 diagnosis without knowing the creator's intent out of band.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER the control plane gains a field distinguishing poke-only from unscheduled (outside this repo's control, so record it as accepted if so), OR this repo adopts and follows a naming convention that makes the register self-describing — e.g. a `POKE:` prefix on every deliberately-poke-only routine — AND a routine created after that decision is observed carrying it. Deleting the two dead routines does NOT resolve this: they are already gone and the shape recurred anyway.

items.title: The operating layer shipped its object half and not one role pack was updated to know it exists
items.source: Phase-G skills/workflows inventory, session_01YBQQzvgJzSumk1APmjiG7B (docs/audits/operating-layer-skills-workflows-inventory-2026-09-02.md)
items.detail: The operating model's anti-silo mechanism is context = work object + role pack, and the function derivation states plainly that 'Role packs exist as 32 skills.' MEASURED 2026-09-02, case-insensitive across all 32 .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md: docs/claude/work = 0 skills; 'work object' = 0; WIP = 0; blocked_on = 0; CYCLE-PRIORITY = 0; READOUT / 'constraint readout' = 0; MANAGER-LEASE / MANAGER-CHECKLIST = 0; PRODUCE / DISPOSE as session types = 0; sunset-pass / SUNSET-DISPOSITIONS = 0. All 40 hits for 'intent' are the intent MULTIPLEXER (src/runtime/intents.py), not the operating model's intent layer. The single near-hit is full-system-audit:629, 'Philosophy — is the operating model itself sound?', a question the audit asks. `duty` is the only skill wired to newer register machinery and only to OPEN-ITEMS.json and DUE.md, BOTH OF WHICH PREDATE THE WORK STORE. So a session handed a work object still reads a role pack describing the pre-2026-09-01 world — B4's two halves are wired to different systems. ⚠️ THIS IS NOT AN ARGUMENT FOR EDITING 32 FILES: most role packs are domain procedure (how to wire a broker, how to run a sweep) and are correctly indifferent to where work is tracked. The gap is concentrated in the ~6 that govern how a session SITUATES itself: session-coordination, session-handoff, doc-freshness, duty, research-driver, delegate-work.
items.resolution_criteria: At least the six situating role packs name docs/claude/work/, the WIP ceiling and the constraint readout, AND a session is observed reading a work object and its role pack together without having been pointed at the work store by its prompt. Editing the skills is a deploy, not an observation — the second half is what closes this.

items.title: mcp__github__actions_list ignores minimal_output for head_commit.message, so one 20-run page costs thousands of tokens to learn a conclusion string
items.source: session_01NeR2kREiXrXQcYYuRHvzRa (session-invokable-actions sub-session), dispatched to build actions Claude can invoke
items.detail: MEASURED IN-SESSION 2026-09-02, population = ONE call: mcp__github__actions_list(method=list_workflow_runs, workflow_id=pytest-run.yml, perPage=20, minimal_output=true) against benbaichmankass/Metis-Insights. Every one of the 20 rows carried the FULL multi-paragraph head_commit.message -- in this repo those run to 20+ lines because commit messages here are deliberately discursive -- plus the full actor and triggering_actor objects with six URL fields each. The information actually wanted was {name, status, conclusion, created_at, updated_at} per run: about five short fields. The response was on the order of thousands of tokens; the useful payload would have been a few hundred. STATE THE POPULATION: this is ONE observation of ONE call shape. I did not sample other methods or other perPage values, and I did not measure the exact token count -- I have no instrument for that inside a session, which is itself part of why this cost goes unnoticed. What IS established is that minimal_output=true did not strip head_commit.message, because the messages were present in the response I received. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: this is the same class the ci-settled relay was built for -- a session repeatedly buying a fat payload to learn a small fact. It is worse here because minimal_output=true reads as if the caller has already opted out of the bulk, so a session has no reason to suspect it is still paying for it. NOT FIXED IN THIS PR, deliberately: the fix is either upstream in the GitHub MCP server (not this repo's code) or a runs-summary relay alongside ci-settled.yml. The relay is cheap to add -- it is ci-settled.yml's shape with a different query -- and is the right call only if a session actually needs run history often enough to earn a workflow. I did not measure that frequency, so I am not asserting it.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) a re-measurement shows minimal_output=true now omits head_commit.message -- verified by making the call and observing the field ABSENT, not by reading a changelog; OR (b) a runs-summary relay exists (the ci-settled.yml shape: push a request, read one compact result) AND has been used at least once by a session other than the one that built it, with the run recorded here. A relay that merely EXISTS does not close this: this repo has scheduled workflows that were merged, enabled and correct and still did not fire when expected. Nor does 'a session stopped calling actions_list' -- that is as likely to mean the session gave up on the data as that it found a cheaper route.

items.title: issue_read get_comments on the coordination board pages oldest-first, so the mandatory session-start read buys 2026-07 history and misses what is live now
items.source: session_01NeR2kREiXrXQcYYuRHvzRa (session-invokable-actions sub-session), dispatched to build actions Claude can invoke
items.detail: MEASURED IN-SESSION 2026-09-02, population = ONE call: mcp__github__issue_read(method=get_comments, issue_number=6927, perPage=15, page=1). All 15 comments returned were dated 2026-07-19 -- the board's FIRST day, over six weeks stale. The board is #6927 and has been in continuous use since, so page 1 is oldest-first and the live claims sit on the LAST page. WHY THIS IS NOT A NUISANCE. docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md makes reading the board before the first substantive tool call MANDATORY, and the stated PURPOSE is to see 'what every other live session is touching'. The default read returns precisely the comments that cannot answer that question, and it returns them looking exactly like a successful read -- 15 real comments, no error. A session that does the mandated read and proceeds has complied with the letter of the rule while learning nothing about who is live, and has no signal that this happened. That is the collapse this repo names everywhere else: 'we looked and found nothing current' renders identically to 'we looked and found the current state'. I hit this myself: I made the call, got July, and had to reason about the page count rather than get an answer. I did NOT then pay for the last page, so I proceeded without having read the live claims -- stated plainly rather than papered over. WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH: whether the MCP exposes a reverse-order or last-page parameter (I did not enumerate its schema), and how many pages the board now runs to. So I am not asserting the fix; only that the default read is the wrong one.
items.resolution_criteria: The mandated session-start board read reliably surfaces the LIVE claims. Any of: (a) docs/claude/coordination-board.md and the session-coordination skill state the exact call that returns the NEWEST comments -- with the parameter named and a recorded observation of it returning a comment from the current day, not a claim that it should; (b) a board-tail relay (the ci-settled.yml shape) returns the last N comments in one compact payload; or (c) a re-measurement shows the default page 1 now returns recent comments. ⚠️ DOCUMENTING THE PROBLEM DOES NOT CLOSE IT. A warning that the read is oldest-first still leaves every session paying for a second call, and this repo's own record is that a caveat buried in a large doc does not reach the session that needs it. ⚠️ NOR DOES 'no session has complained' -- the whole finding is that the failure is silent.

items.title: DIAG_BASE_URL still points at a VM terminated 2026-06-16, while the Caddy HTTPS path works directly from a sandbox — so sessions keep paying relay round trips for reads they could curl
items.source: session_01NeR2kREiXrXQcYYuRHvzRa (session-invokable-actions sub-session), dispatched to build actions Claude can invoke
items.detail: RE-MEASURED 2026-09-02 from inside a Claude Code sandbox, all four probes in one shell, population = this session: (1) echo $DIAG_BASE_URL -> 'http://141.145.193.91:8001'. That is the Ampere live trader over PLAIN HTTP -- a scheme the platform proxy drops. Note this differs from BL-20260818-DIAG-BASE-URL-POINTS-AT-TERMINATED-VM, which recorded the value as the x86 micro 158.178.210.252; the var has since been half-updated to the right HOST and still carries the wrong SCHEME, so that row's specific value is stale while its conclusion stands. (2) curl https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/health -> HTTP 200. (3) curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $DIAG_READ_TOKEN' https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/diag/version -> HTTP 200 with real JSON ({git_sha: 8d22f8f7, git_sha_on_disk: d8aac5c6, restart_pending: true}). (4) curl https://api.github.com/repos/... -> HTTP 403 (the control: egress is NOT broadly blocked; the GitHub API specifically is). SO THE CREDENTIALED DIAG SURFACE IS DIRECTLY REACHABLE and a diag read costs a Bash call, not a relay round trip (open a labelled issue, wait for a workflow, read a comment back through a fat MCP call). scripts/ops/diag_fetch.sh already self-heals the stale base, which is why this is medium and not high -- but only a session that reaches for that script benefits, and CLAUDE.md's own § 'PM-side session capabilities' still frames the relay as the normal path. SCOPE, stated so this is not read as wider than it is: this covers the LIVE VM's /api/diag/* only. The trainer VM has no HTTP diag surface and is genuinely relay-only, and nothing here changes that. NOT FIXED HERE because the wrong value lives in the cloud ENVIRONMENT's variables, which this session cannot edit, and because correcting the doc without correcting the var would leave the next session reading advice its environment contradicts.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH halves, and neither substitutes for the other: (1) DIAG_BASE_URL in the cloud environment reads an https:// base that answers -- verified by a session ECHOING the var and then curling it successfully in the same shell, never by someone reporting they changed it; and (2) CLAUDE.md § 'PM-side session capabilities' names the direct Caddy path as the FIRST thing to try for live-VM diag reads, with the issue relay as the fallback, and keeps the trainer VM explicitly carved out as relay-only. ⚠️ A PASSING curl FROM ONE SESSION DOES NOT SETTLE (1) ON ITS OWN if that session had to override the var to make it work -- that is the script self-healing, which is already true today and is what has let this sit. The var itself must be right.

items.title: BL-20260821-CHECK-SUITE-EVENT-IS-PER-SUITE-NOT-PER-PR now has a one-command reader (ci-settled), and the merge protocol every session reads still does not name it
items.source: session_01NeR2kREiXrXQcYYuRHvzRa, while building the ci-settled relay after its brief was corrected
items.detail: THIRD INDEPENDENT OBSERVATION of BL-20260821-CHECK-SUITE-EVENT-IS-PER-SUITE-NOT-PER-PR (open, severity high, two prior observations on #10105 and #10106 within one hour). MEASURED 2026-09-02, population = one watch on PR #10757: run 3 of the ci-settled relay recorded guards=passing, pytest-collect=passing, repo-inventory=passing and pytest-run=running, on one head sha. Those are three of the four required contexts, from three different suites. Any check_suite.completed success arriving in that window is a true statement about one suite and a false go-signal for the PR. WHAT IS NEW, and why this is filed rather than folded into the 2026-08-21 row: that row's resolution criteria ask for the rule to be STATED where sessions read it, and until now the only available advice was 'be careful, read get_check_runs and check each required context by name' -- i.e. do several MCP calls, by hand, correctly, under time pressure. There is now a one-command reader that does exactly that and returns a single graded verdict: `scripts/ops/ci_settled.sh <PR> once` (PR #10757). So the rule can change from a caution into an instruction, which is a materially different thing to ask of a session. ⚠️ I DELIBERATELY DID NOT MAKE THAT EDIT MYSELF. It lands in .claude/skills/session-coordination/SKILL.md's merge protocol and in the PreToolUse merge-guard deny message -- the binding path every session takes before merging -- and I am a sub-session whose declared scope on the coordination board did not include it. Unilaterally rewriting the merge protocol from a side branch is the kind of change that should be made by whoever owns the protocol, not smuggled in beside a tooling PR. ⚠️ NOR DOES THE READER EXISTING CLOSE THE 2026-08-21 ROW. A tool nobody is told to run is not a rule anybody follows, which is the whole shape of that row's own complaint.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH, and the second does not follow from the first: (1) .claude/skills/session-coordination/SKILL.md's merge-protocol step names the reader explicitly -- 'run scripts/ops/ci_settled.sh <PR> once and require state==green with mergeable_state not dirty; a check_suite.completed success is NEVER sufficient' -- and the PreToolUse merge-guard deny message carries the same line; AND (2) a session REPORTS having followed it against a live PR where one suite completed green while another required check was still running, naming the PR and quoting the verdict it got. ⚠️ (2) is the half that cannot be satisfied by editing a doc, and it is the half that matters: the 2026-08-21 row records two sessions that avoided the trap by accident rather than by design. ⚠️ AND MERGING PR #10757 DOES NOT COUNT AS EITHER. A relay that is merged and never pointed at is the written-and-never-read defect this repo files under provenance-consumer-guard, one level up.

items.title: subscribe_pr_activity is now the recommended CI trigger and nobody has measured what it misses — its own footer names four exclusions and none has been tested
items.source: session_01NeR2kREiXrXQcYYuRHvzRa; the exclusions are quoted from the event footer relayed by the manager session
items.detail: The check_suite.completed wake delivered by subscribe_pr_activity is the mechanism this repo now leans on instead of polling, and its coverage is UNMEASURED. The event's own footer states four exclusions verbatim: it does not cover cancelled suites, suites with NO RUNS, the App's own suites, or legacy commit statuses. ⚠️ 'SUITES WITH NO RUNS' IS THE DANGEROUS ONE. That is precisely the zero-check-runs state CLAUDE.md records two sessions losing ~10 minutes each to, whose usual causes are a merge conflict (the merge ref cannot be built, so pull_request runs are skipped by construction) or a head pushed by github-actions[bot] (GitHub suppresses workflow triggers for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes). In exactly those cases NO WAKE ARRIVES AT ALL -- and silence from a push mechanism is indistinguishable from 'not finished yet'. A session waiting on a wake for a conflicted PR waits forever and has no signal that this is what is happening. ⚠️ 'CANCELLED SUITES' IS THE SECOND. This repo runs cancel-in-progress: true on its required checks, so a superseded push routinely leaves cancelled suites -- a state that by the footer's own words produces no wake. WHAT I DID NOT MEASURE, stated so this is not read as wider than it is: I did not observe a wake at all this session (the observation is the manager's, relayed), I did not test any of the four exclusions, I did not measure how reliably the wake fires, and I did not test its behaviour on a re-push mid-suite. So this row asserts that the coverage is UNKNOWN, not that it is bad. 'We did not look' is the finding.
items.resolution_criteria: Each exclusion tested against a deliberately constructed condition and the OBSERVATION recorded -- not the footer re-quoted: (a) a PR with a merge conflict (mergeable_state dirty, zero check runs) -- record whether any wake arrives and after how long; (b) a superseded push producing cancelled suites -- same; (c) a re-push mid-suite -- record whether the wake refers to the OLD head sha, which would be a settled verdict for code that is no longer the head; (d) a PR that was never subscribed -- confirm the silence is total. THEN state, in docs/claude/coordination-board.md or the session-coordination skill, which conditions a session must NOT wait on a wake for, and what to run instead (scripts/ops/ci_settled.sh <PR> once covers (a), (b) and (d) by grading the head directly). ⚠️ A PASSING WAKE ON A NORMAL PR CLOSES NOTHING -- that path already works and is not what is in question. The whole row is about the four cases where it is documented NOT to fire. ⚠️ AND 'no session has complained' is not evidence: a wake that never arrives produces silence, which is exactly what waiting looks like.

items.title: check_backlog_refs screens for FU- ids but resolves only against docs/claude/*backlog*.json, so every FU- reference dangles by construction
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 while splitting the API reference out of CLAUDE.md (scripts/ops/check_backlog_refs.py, read at commit d8aac5c6). Population: every tracking id matched by the guard's own REF regex across SEARCH_DIRS = docs/ scripts/ .github/ config/ src/.

REF matches three prefixes -- (?:BL|MB|FU) -- but filed_ids() reads ONLY docs/claude/*backlog*.json items[].id. FU- rows do not live there; they live in comms/follow_ups.json. So an FU- id can never resolve, however correctly it is filed. Measured: 13 distinct FU- ids are cited repo-wide; FU-20260511-001 and FU-20260516-001 are both genuinely filed in comms/follow_ups.json and both are reported dangling.

Latent rather than live: the guard is diff-scoped, so it only fires when a diff introduces an FU- citation. It did fire on this session's PR, which is how it was found. When it fires the finding is FALSE and pushes a session toward 'file the row' for a row that already exists -- i.e. toward a duplicate in the wrong register.

UPDATE 2026-09-02, same session: option (a) IS NOW DONE. filed_ids() reads comms/follow_ups.json via a new EXTRA_REGISTERS table, because the false findings were blocking a PR and the fix is unambiguous -- an id that IS filed should resolve. MEASURED before and after: 12 of the 13 cited FU- ids are genuinely filed there and now resolve; the thirteenth is cited and never filed and STILL dangles, which is the live positive control pinned by tests/test_check_backlog_refs.py::TestFollowUpsRegisterResolves (the id is named THERE and not here -- see the second finding below). So this made the guard MORE accurate, not quieter.

SECOND FINDING, found by tripping it: CITING AN ID *AS AN EXAMPLE OF NON-RESOLUTION* IS A FALSE POSITIVE FOR THIS GUARD. Naming the unfiled control id in this row and in the guard's own docstring made the guard report both files. The guard's premise -- 'a doc saying tracked by BL-X where BL-X was never filed reads as tracked' -- does not hold for a citation whose whole point is that it does NOT resolve. Worked around here by keeping the literal only under tests/, which is outside SEARCH_DIRS; that is a workaround, not a fix. The guard has no override mechanism (unlike collapsed-state-guard's '# collapsed-state:' or diagnostic-provenance-guard's '# inert:'), and if it gains one it must be VERIFIED rather than presence-only, per the new-table-wiring-guard lesson this repo already paid for -- a guard cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than no guard. Low severity: the workaround is cheap and the class is rare.

WHAT REMAINS OPEN, and it is a real question rather than tidy-up: whether the follow-ups register is RETIRED. The newest FU- id anywhere is FU-20260516-001, ~3.5 months old, and nothing canonical says the register is live or dead. If it is retired, FU should come out of REF and the 29 rows in comms/follow_ups.json need a disposition; if it is live, it belongs in the session-end filing instructions alongside the three backlogs, where it currently is not mentioned. Either way somebody has to decide, and 'nobody has filed one lately' is not that decision.
items.resolution_criteria: The RESOLUTION half is done (2026-09-02) and is not what closes this. This closes when the follow-ups register's STATUS is settled and written down: either it is declared live and named in the session-end filing instructions beside the three backlogs, or it is declared retired, FU is removed from REF, and its 29 rows get a disposition. Reporting 'no FU- ids were introduced lately' does NOT close it -- that is the symptom the diff-scoping hides, not the question.

items.title: The mandatory session boot read is ~1.54 MB / ~427k est. tokens; ROADMAP.md alone is 42% and no CLAUDE.md slice can fix it
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-02, wc -c at origin/main d8aac5c6. Population: the five files a session is instructed to read before acting (CLAUDE.md 'Every session' + CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL 'Session-start documentation read'). ROADMAP.md 648,407 (42.1%) | CLAUDE.md 430,453 (28.0%) | OPEN-ITEMS.json 191,955 (12.5%) | ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL 168,495 (10.9%) | CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL 99,222 (6.4%) = 1,538,532 B, ~427k tokens ESTIMATED at ~3.6 B/token (an estimate, not a measurement). The operating-model design measured ~403k on 2026-09-01, so it grew ~24k tokens in one day.

The API-reference split (2026-09-02) took CLAUDE.md 430,453 -> 283,388 B, which is -34.2% of that file but only -8.7% of the boot read. RE-MEASURED after merging main: the boot-read figure FELL from -9.7% while the PR sat UNCHANGED, because OPEN-ITEMS.json grew 191,955 -> 205,121 B in the same few hours. The register outgrew the split, which is this row's whole point. Anyone reporting the boot-read problem as solved on the strength of a CLAUDE.md slice is quoting the wrong denominator.

Inside ROADMAP.md (measured same day): '## Milestone Roadmap' 347,909 B (53.7%), '## Historical Sprint Ledger' 179,606 B (27.7%). The ledger is the cleaner cut -- CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL 'Historical Notes Policy' already says historical material is context-only -- BUT src/web/api/routers/roadmap.py PARSES the ledger's M-mapping column (roadmap.py:196-198, 341) as one of three sprint->milestone resolution paths and serves it at GET /api/bot/roadmap, so a blind move breaks the SPA Roadmap tab.

UNMEASURED, and it is the next thing worth measuring: what fraction of the 347,909 B Milestone Roadmap is CLOSED milestones. Nobody has counted, so 'split the closed ones out' is a guess, not a plan.
items.resolution_criteria: The boot read is measured below 1,000,000 B by the same five-file population and method, AND the reduction is attributed per file. A CLAUDE.md-only reduction does NOT close this -- slice 1 already showed that path tops out around -10%. If the operator decides the current size is acceptable, record THAT as the disposition with the reasoning, closing it as closed_answered rather than leaving it open.

items.title: OPEN-ITEMS.json is not byte-reproducible, so every naive edit silently reformats 1,412 lines and re-attributes the whole register to that PR
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-02, WITH A VALIDATED POSITIVE CONTROL, after the manager session did exactly this and caught it in its own PR diff. scripts/ops/backlog_append.detect_format tries 5 candidate serialisations and REFUSES to write when none reproduces the file byte-for-byte -- the protection added by BL-20260820-BACKLOG-APPEND-REFORMATS-AND-REATTRIBUTES. backlog_append.LIVE_BACKLOGS names FOUR files -- health-review, performance-review, ml-review and research-review -- and ALL FOUR reproduce (indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, no trailing newline), so the probe is known to find a match when one exists. docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json is NOT IN THAT LIST AT ALL, and reproduces under none of the 5 candidates. docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json reproduces under NONE of the 5. CAUSE: its escaping is MIXED. The header's what_this_is carries a literal em-dash while an item written later carries the same character as \u2014, so no single ensure_ascii setting can reproduce the file. It was written by at least two different tools at different times. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: the four protected files are the review backlogs, which the repo's own guidance says nobody reads at session start precisely because they are enormous. OPEN-ITEMS.json is the opposite -- it is THE SHORT LIST EVERY SESSION READS AT START, and its live contents are rendered into CLAUDE.md by render_session_brief.py. So the register with the widest readership is the only one with no append helper and no format guard, and CLAUDE.md's instruction to file 'through scripts/ops/backlog_append.py, never by hand' does not name it. MEASURED BLAST RADIUS, not estimated: a read-append-write with json.dumps(indent=2) produced a diff of 742 insertions / 699 deletions across 1,412 lines for a two-row edit. The correct surgical edit is 21 insertions / 3 deletions. Both pass check_open_items.py, so the guard that exists cannot tell them apart -- it grades CONTENT and says nothing about SERIALISATION. [!] THE REFORMAT IS NOT COSMETIC. It re-attributes every pre-existing row to whoever touched the file, which destroys git blame on the one register used to establish who observed what and when -- the field this repo leans on hardest when separating 'we deployed it' from 'we verified it'.
items.evidence: detect_format over LIVE_BACKLOGS (4 files) plus OPEN-ITEMS.json: 4 reproducible, OPEN-ITEMS not, and OPEN-ITEMS is not a member of LIVE_BACKLOGS so check_live_backlogs never looks at it -- its OK line reads '4 live backlog(s) reproduce byte-for-byte' whether or not OPEN-ITEMS is broken. First byte mismatch at offset 86 under ensure_ascii=True (literal em-dash in the header) and at offset 1450 under ensure_ascii=False (\u2014 escape inside an item added later). Naive rewrite diff --numstat: 742/699 for a two-row edit. Surgical edit: 21/3. Both pass check_open_items.py. [!] CORRECTED IN THE FILING: a first draft of this row said THREE protected files, because three is all it probed. The list has four. The finding survives the correction and the count was wrong.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) OPEN-ITEMS.json is normalised ONCE to a single reproducible serialisation, in a PR that says the 1,412-line diff is a deliberate one-time normalisation, AND an open_items_append helper (or an extension of backlog_append) is added that round-trips it, AND CLAUDE.md's 'file through the helper, never by hand' rule is extended to name this register; OR (b) a CI check FAILS a PR whose OPEN-ITEMS.json diff touches more lines than the rows it changes, so a reformat cannot land silently even without a helper. [!] A HELPER ALONE DOES NOT CLOSE THIS while the file stays unreproducible -- detect_format would refuse and the caller would be pushed straight back to hand-editing, which is the state today. [!] NORMALISING WITHOUT A GUARD DOES NOT CLOSE IT EITHER: the file drifted into mixed escaping once and nothing stopped it, so it will drift again. [!] DO NOT CLOSE THIS BY DOCUMENTING 'edit carefully'. The manager session knew this rule, cited it about backlogs in the same session, and still reformatted the file -- a rule that is known and still broken is evidence for machinery, not for restating the rule.

items.title: Five test modules still MagicMock `numpy` into sys.modules at import time, which breaks pytest.approx for the whole session on any box without numpy -- the exact defect tests/conftest.py documents as fixed
items.detail: RECURRENCE, filed deliberately as its own row rather than as a duplicate: the earlier fix was applied to tests/conftest.py and the copy-pasted stubs it names were LEFT IN PLACE, so the class is closed in one file and open in five. === THE MECHANISM, and it is quoted from the repo's own docstring. tests/conftest.py::_preimport_if_available says: 'An earlier version of this fix routed these four through _stub_optional, which installs a MagicMock when the import fails. That broke pytest.approx outright in any environment WITHOUT numpy -- _pytest.python_api.is_bool does `if np := sys.modules.get("numpy"): return isinstance(val, np.bool_)` so a MagicMock in that slot makes np.bool_ a MagicMock, which is not a type, and isinstance() raises TypeError.' The conftest's own remedy is a PRE-IMPORT: it makes the REAL numpy win the sys.modules slot before any test module runs its own `setdefault`. ⚠️ THAT REMEDY ONLY WORKS WHEN NUMPY IS INSTALLED. Where numpy is ABSENT the pre-import is a documented no-op, and these five modules' import-time `for _mod in ("pandas", "matplotlib", "matplotlib.pyplot", "numpy", "scipy", "sklearn", "dotenv"): sys.modules.setdefault(_mod, MagicMock())` then installs the MagicMock unopposed, poisoning every later pytest.approx in the same process. === THE FIVE (grep-verified 2026-09-02, by parsing the `for _mod in (...)` tuple rather than by a bare `numpy` grep): tests/test_orders.py, tests/test_outcomes_integration.py, tests/test_pipeline_news_veto.py, tests/test_pipeline_result_renderer.py, tests/test_processor_repo_root_resolution.py. Eleven further modules carry the same copy-pasted loop WITHOUT numpy in the tuple and are not implicated. === MEASURED, with a stated population. On a numpy-less sandbox, the 339 test files matching order_monitor|bybit|get_env ran 386 failed / 4610 passed; `pip install numpy` alone took that to 143 failed / 4853 passed. So 243 of those 386 failures (63.0%; denominator = the 386 failures in that run, population = the 339 files above, one sandbox, n = 1 run per arm) were this one stub, and 243 of the 4853 eventual passes were unblocked by installing numpy alone. ⚠️ IT DOES NOT PRESENT AS AN ENVIRONMENT ERROR: the failure surfaces as an ordinary-looking assertion failure on a value that is in fact CORRECT (observed: `assert qty == pytest.approx(0.018)` with qty == 0.018), and the TypeError is four frames down inside _pytest. That is what makes it expensive -- a session reads it as a logic bug in its own diff. === WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A SANDBOX. The conftest docstring records that the ORIGINAL instance was caught by the `guards` CI job, 'which installs only ruff/import-linter/pyyaml/pytest and therefore has no numpy', while `pytest-run` stayed green because it installs the full requirements. That asymmetry is unchanged, so any test collected by a lean job after one of these five is exposed. NOT VERIFIED: whether `guards` currently collects any of the five -- establish that before deciding severity, and do not assume the sandbox reading transfers to CI (the isolation_audit module makes exactly that warning about its own baseline). === REMEDY, and note the repo has already ruled out the obvious one: tests/isolation_audit.py says 'THE REMEDY IS "NEVER STUB", NOT "STUB MORE"'. So drop `numpy` from these five tuples (the tests that genuinely need a numpy stub should stub it locally and restore it), rather than teaching the conftest to stub it earlier. Related: BL-20260827-TEST-MODULES-STUB-SKLEARN-INTO-SYS-MODULES-AT-IMPORT-TIME, BL-20260822-TEST-SUITE-CROSS-FILE-SYS-MODULES-POLLUTION -- same class, different package, and this row exists because fixing them as INSTANCES is what left numpy standing.
items.resolution_criteria: `numpy` no longer appears in the import-time MagicMock tuple of any test module (assert by parsing the `for _mod in (...)` tuples, not by grepping for the word), AND a numpy-less run of a suite that collects at least one of the five followed by a pytest.approx-using test passes. ⚠️ INSTALLING NUMPY IN THE LEAN CI JOB DOES NOT RESOLVE THIS and must not be accepted as a fix: it hides the stub rather than removing it, and the next numpy-less environment re-exposes it -- which is precisely how this recurrence happened. ⚠️ A GREEN `pytest-run` IS NOT EVIDENCE either: that job installs the full requirements, so the real numpy wins the slot and the stub is inert there by construction.

items.title: Following the coordination-board protocol leaves a bot-authored commit at HEAD, so the session's own PR runs no CI and reads as 'waiting'
items.detail: MEASURED: this trap fired THREE TIMES on 2026-09-02 alone -- #10793, #10795 and #10789 -- each time on a PR whose head commit was `github-actions[bot] | board-post: results`. Each read `total_count: 0` check runs and `mergeable_state: blocked`, which is indistinguishable from 'CI has not started yet'. #10793 sat that way for ~35 minutes and #10789 for ~20 before a manager noticed. MECHANISM: `board-post.yml` and `pr-opener.yml` commit a results file back to the PR branch using the workflow's GITHUB_TOKEN. GitHub does not trigger workflows for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes. So if that results commit lands LAST, no workflow fires on the head and the PR is silently un-tested. [!] THE INCENTIVE IS INVERTED, which is what makes this worse than a bug: a session that follows the board protocol is PUNISHED with an invisible PR, and one that skips it is not. That is the MI-28 shape ('following the board protocol makes the audit louder, which inverts the incentive') recurring in a new place. [!] IT IS DOCUMENTED AND THAT HAS NOT WORKED. CLAUDE.md states it verbatim -- 'if such a commit lands last your PR shows ZERO checks and is blocked, not green -- push an ordinary commit after, to arm CI' -- and the manager session that had READ that line hit it three times in one afternoon. A rule that is known and still broken is evidence for machinery, not for restating the rule.
items.evidence: #10789 head 9faec369 authored by github-actions[bot], message 'board-post: results', get_check_runs total_count 0, mergeable_state blocked. #10793 head 069ff90d, same author and message, same symptoms. Both armed by a manager merging origin/main in. No check in scripts/ci/ references check_runs, total_count or a bot-authored head (grep returned nothing; control: 60+ files exist in scripts/ci/).
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) THE CAUSE IS REMOVED -- the relays stop pushing a results commit to the PR branch (write the result to the issue comment, a run artifact, or a side branch), so a bot commit can never be at HEAD; OR (b) the relays push with a credential that DOES trigger workflows (a PAT), which is the documented GitHub behaviour difference; OR (c) the relay itself dispatches the required workflows after its push. [!] AND A DETECTOR EITHER WAY, because the trap is not unique to these two relays -- ANY bot-authored head reproduces it: something that flags an OPEN PR whose head has zero check runs, reaching a surface a manager actually reads. [!] DO NOT CLOSE THIS ON DOCUMENTATION. It is already documented in CLAUDE.md and was hit three times by a session that had read it.

updates.note:
RECURRED ON PR #11140, AND THE DOCUMENTED REMEDY DID NOT WORK — that second half is the new fact and it is the one that matters.

MEASURED. Posting the MANDATORY board DONE left `e3756aef` ('board-post: results', authored by github-actions[bot]) at the PR head. At 14:05:18Z ALL FOUR pull_request workflows were created against that sha and every one concluded `action_required`: Guards #4619, pytest-run #10885, pytest-collect #12006, repo-inventory #10562. Not one workflow — the whole required set.

⚠️ THE REMEDY THIS REPO DOCUMENTS IS 'push one ordinary commit yourself to arm CI' (CLAUDE.md § pr-opener/board-post relays). I PUSHED TWO — fdb26402 and a895a474, both ordinary, both authored by the session's own user, both confirmed on origin — AND NO WORKFLOW RUN WAS CREATED FOR EITHER, for any of the four workflows. `list_workflow_runs` for the branch stayed at total_count 28 with the newest run at 14:05:18Z across repeated polls over ~35 minutes. So the head advanced twice past the bot commit and CI never re-armed.

WHY THAT CHANGES THE DISPOSITION. `action_required` is not 'queued' and not 'failed' — it is AWAITING HUMAN APPROVAL, and no amount of pushing clears it. A session following the remedy will push, see nothing appear, and have no way to tell that from Actions being slow; `get_check_runs` returns `total_count: 0`, which reads exactly like 'CI has not started yet'. The PR's mergeable_state is `blocked`, which is ALSO what a not-yet-run PR looks like. Every surface a session can read says 'wait'; the true state is 'a human must approve'.

⚠️ AND NOTE THE INTERACTION WITH BL-20260903-EMPTY-COMMIT-DOES-ARM-CI-CONTRADICTING-THE-BOARD-RULE-NEVER-AN-EMPTY-ONE: that row measured an EMPTY commit arming CI twice. It was not tried here, deliberately — CLAUDE.md states flatly 'never push an empty commit ... to kick CI', and on this PR it would not have helped anyway, since the block is an approval gate rather than a missing trigger. Recording that it was considered and refused, so the next session does not read the silence as the option being unknown.

REMEDY FOR THE READER, until this row is fixed: if your PR shows total_count 0 AND a bot-authored commit anywhere at or near HEAD, check list_workflow_runs for `action_required` BEFORE concluding CI is slow or re-pushing. A human approving the workflow runs is the only thing that clears it.

items.title: The append-mostly registers are single JSON files, so each merge invalidates every sibling PR's resolve — and the repo already solved this once
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-02: five registers are monolithic JSON and every session appends to them -- health-review-backlog.json 6,236,300 bytes, OPEN-ITEMS.json 220,809, MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json 146,755, SESSIONS.json 83,124, OPEN-PRS.json 21,219. There is NO .gitattributes and NO merge driver, so every append is a textual conflict against every other append. [!] THE REPO HAS ALREADY SOLVED THIS AND DID NOT GENERALISE THE SOLUTION. docs/claude/work/objects/ holds 584 objects as ONE FILE PER OBJECT, and the work store's README states the reason outright: 'One file per object, so two sessions touching different work never conflict.' The registers that keep conflicting are exactly the ones that did not get that treatment. [!] IT IS A MANAGER-AMPLIFIED DEFECT. MI-20 already recorded 'nine merges in three hours left four PRs conflicted on the same append-mostly register', and on 2026-09-02 a manager landed five register-touching PRs in one afternoon (#10790, #10791, #10792, #10795, #10798), re-conflicting every sub-session PR beneath them -- while instructing another session on how to resolve those same conflicts. The manager is the highest-frequency writer and therefore the largest source of the churn.
items.evidence: wc -c on the five files as above. `ls docs/claude/work/objects/*.yaml | wc -l` = 584. `cat .gitattributes` -> file does not exist. MI-20 in MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json records the prior occurrence.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) the registers move to one-file-per-row under a directory, as the work store already did, with the aggregate JSON generated for consumers that need it; OR (b) a git merge driver registered in .gitattributes merges these files BY ROW ID -- union on id, refusing on a genuine same-id divergence -- so two appends never conflict textually. [!] (b) MUST ASSERT BOTH WAYS, not just count: every id present on either side present in the output, AND the counts reconcile. A count can reconcile by luck while a row is lost, which is why the manual resolutions this week asserted per-id membership. [!] DO NOT CLOSE THIS BY ASKING SESSIONS TO MERGE MORE CAREFULLY. Careful manual resolution is what is happening now and it costs a round trip per PR per merge.

items.title: F6 is the condition the autonomy grant rests on, and a manager can merge, spawn, hold and decide all day without any of it touching a notifying path
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-02: docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl was last written at 03:14 and the manager session that ran from ~05:00 to ~13:00 queued NOTHING, while in that window it merged 5 PRs, dispatched 4 sub-sessions, converted a PR to draft to block a deploy, made a judgement call on a fallback design, and corrected itself three times. The operator noticed before the manager did and said so: 'I'm still not getting any pings from you either, which is also a serious lapse here.' MECHANISM, and it is structural rather than forgetfulness: the actions that DO notify are the narrow VM system-actions, which carry a transparency notify (scripts/ops/notify_run.sh). The manager's highest-impact actions do not go through that path at all -- merge_pull_request, update_pull_request (draft/undraft), create_session, create_trigger/fire_trigger and enable_pr_auto_merge are all MCP calls with no notification hop. So the class of action MOST worth telling the operator about is precisely the class that is silent, and the manager must remember to narrate it by hand. [!] F6 IS NOT A NICE-TO-HAVE: the operating-model design names 'autonomous-action notification' as THE CONDITION ON WHICH THE AUTONOMY GRANT WAS MADE. An unnotified autonomous action is not merely undocumented; it is outside the terms the operator agreed to. [!] AND FILING HAS ALREADY FAILED ONCE. MI-54 ('I asked seven decisions today as in-session popups and sent zero pings') was filed EARLIER THE SAME DAY, is still state in_flight, and the manager reproduced the lapse for the following eight hours. A row that records a behaviour does not change it.
items.evidence: pending-pings.jsonl mtime 2026-09-02 03:14, 50 rows, none from this session. send-ping exists as a Tier-1 system-action and was not dispatched until the operator complained (issue #10804). MI-54 in MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json, state in_flight, filed the same day. grep of the system-actions notify path shows it covers the allowlisted VM actions only.
items.resolution_criteria: A manager's autonomous action produces a notification WITHOUT the manager choosing to send one. Acceptable shapes: (a) a repo-side hook on the events that are already observable -- a merge to main authored by a manager session, a new SESSIONS.json row, a PR draft-state flip -- rendering a rolled-up ping on the digest cadence; or (b) the manager preflight of MI-68 REFUSING to proceed when the count of unnotified autonomous actions since the last ping exceeds a stated threshold, in the handoff_check shape that grades `unknown` rather than passing softly. [!] A ROLLED-UP DIGEST IS THE TARGET, NOT A PING PER ACTION. The design is explicit that F6 pings on STATE CHANGES AND DECISIONS and never on ACTIVITY, and this repo has already measured what the other choice costs: 202 of 376 CRITICAL rows in one window were a single un-latched alarm that trained the operator past the one channel reserved for an unprotected position. [!] DO NOT CLOSE THIS BY ADDING A REMINDER TO A PROMPT OR A SKILL. MI-54 is that fix and it did not hold for eight hours.

items.title: The work store's `stage` histogram is a census of SOURCE FILENAMES, not a reading of the work — so QUESTION/DECISION/DEPLOYMENT/OBSERVATION are empty BY CONSTRUCTION and the constraint the design NAMES can never be located, at any edge coverage
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-02 over the whole store (population: every *.yaml in docs/claude/work/objects/, n=584 before this session's additions, 0 parse failures). EVERY stage in the histogram is a deterministic function of one field. 576 of 584 objects carry `source.backlog`, and scripts/ops/migrate_backlog_to_work_objects.py::SOURCES maps the filename to the stage with NO per-row judgement: health-review-backlog.json -> INTEGRITY (498), {ml,performance,research}-review-backlog.json -> EVIDENCE (78). ZERO exceptions. The remaining 8 are the operating-layer build's own phases, all CAPABILITY. So `INTEGRITY 498` is a census of ONE filename, and not one object anywhere in the store had its chain stage chosen by someone reading the work. CONSEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE POINT: QUESTION / DECISION / DEPLOYMENT / OBSERVATION hold zero objects because no producer has ever EMITTED one -- the migration's table names two stages and the build's phases name a third. docs/design/operating-model-DESIGN.md names DECISION as the measured constraint ('evidence is produced far faster than it is converted into choices'), so the store cannot locate the very stage the design says the system is stuck on -- and NO amount of blocked_on edge-writing fixes that. THIS IS NOT BL-20260901-WORK-STORE-EDGES-ARE-1-PERCENT-ASSESSED-SO-THE-CONSTRAINT-CANNOT-BE-COMPUTED, AND CONFLATING THEM IS THE TRAP. That row is about edge COVERAGE (1.0%, below the 50% floor, so constraint_readout.py refuses). This row is about STAGE PROVENANCE. They are independent: a session could take coverage to 100% with perfectly true edges and DECISION would still read zero, so the readout would then name a stage confidently off a histogram that describes four backlog filenames. Fixing coverage WITHOUT fixing this makes the failure worse, because the refusal is currently the only thing stopping the wrong answer being published. THE WORK IS NOT MISSING -- IT IS UNDER A DIFFERENT VOCABULARY, OUTSIDE THE STORE. docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json holds 36 rows whose kinds map onto the empty stages almost exactly: `pending_decision` 3 (= DECISION), `awaiting_verification` 6 and `monitoring` 21 (= OBSERVATION -- 'deployed, awaiting an observation' is that stage's definition). The Phase C migration carried the four review BACKLOGS and never the REGISTER, which is why the chain half is empty and the support half is full. PARTIALLY REMEDIATED IN THE SAME CHANGE, DELIBERATELY NOT IN BULK: constraint_readout.py now grades `stage_basis` (per_object / bulk_by_source_file / unstated, never collapsed, summing to the population checkably) and both READOUT.md and the CLAUDE.md brief now say in terms that the populated stages were assigned from a filename. Three objects were hand-authored from EXISTING OPEN-ITEMS rows (2 DECISION + 1 EVIDENCE), taking DECISION from 0 to 2. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, AND MUST NOT BE DONE AS A TIDY-UP: a bulk re-stage of the 576 migrated rows. Re-staging by filename a second time would reproduce this defect with different numbers, and re-staging by reading 576 prose bodies is 576 individual guesses -- which is exactly the reasoning the migration used to justify the uniform assignment in the first place, and it was right to. The open question is whether OPEN-ITEMS' monitoring/awaiting_verification rows should become OBSERVATION objects, which is a design call, not a cleanup.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) a producer exists that emits QUESTION / DECISION / DEPLOYMENT / OBSERVATION objects from something that genuinely is one -- so the four empty stages become a MEASUREMENT rather than an artifact -- and the store is observed holding objects on at least DECISION and OBSERVATION that no single session hand-wrote; OR (b) it is DECIDED and recorded that the work store covers only the support half of the chain, in which case constraint_readout.py must stop presenting a stage histogram as a diagnosis of the chain at all, and check_capability_pull.py's E2 rule needs a different input than `constraint.named_stage`. A COVERAGE RISE DOES NOT SATISFY THIS. Neither does a bulk re-stage of the migrated rows: a stage assigned by a second uniform rule is the same defect wearing different numbers, and `stage_basis` will still read `bulk_by_source_file` for every one of them.

items.title: callback_handler's wdec branch matches the LITERAL "wdec" while the encoder and the poll claim both resolve CB_PREFIX — a rename moves two of three and silently strands the dispatcher
items.source: session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ, while wiring the decision channel onto the dedicated Claude bot (PR #10789). Noticed rather than hunted: I wrote a comment asserting the claim named the same constant the dispatcher resolves, then checked and it did not.
items.detail: THREE SITES MUST AGREE ON THE CALLBACK PREFIX AND ONLY TWO READ THE SAME SOURCE. `src/runtime/telegram_decisions.CB_PREFIX = "wdec"` is what `encode_callback` writes into `callback_data` and what `answerable_route`/the poll claim ask the registry about; `src/bot/claude_decision_bot.py` registers its handler with `pattern=rf"^{CB_PREFIX}:"` and declares `HANDLED_PREFIXES = (CB_PREFIX,)`. But `src/bot/telegram_query_bot.callback_handler` dispatches on the BARE LITERAL: `elif action == "wdec":`. So renaming CB_PREFIX moves the encoder, the Claude bot's handler AND the poll claim together while leaving the trader bot's branch matching a prefix nothing emits any more. ⚠️ THE FAILURE IS SILENT AND SHAPED EXACTLY LIKE THE ONE THE POLL REGISTRY EXISTS TO CATCH. The trader bot is the FALLBACK destination for decision prompts, so after such a rename its poll claim would still read `polled_with_handler` (the claim is built from CB_PREFIX, which moved) while a real tap fell through `callback_handler`'s if/elif chain to the 'unknown callback data is ignored' tail. The operator taps; the message is not edited; nothing errors; the registry reports the bot as answerable. That is a dead button that reads healthy on every surface, one layer below where PR #10789 fixed it. NOT CURRENTLY BROKEN, and stated as such: `CB_PREFIX` is "wdec" today, so all three agree and every test passes. This is a latent coupling, which is why it is `low` and not higher — it needs a rename to fire. WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN #10789: `src/bot/telegram_query_bot.py` was declared by a concurrent live session (`claude/claude-ping-double-delivery-x4mq2p`), flagged on the coordination board by PR #10778's own DONE comment as the branch most likely to touch the same regions. Edits there were deliberately held to a poll registration plus one log line to avoid racing it. Filed rather than fixed so the observation is not lost — it is a two-line change for whoever owns that file next.
items.resolution_criteria: `src/bot/telegram_query_bot.callback_handler` dispatches the decision callback on the imported `telegram_decisions.CB_PREFIX` rather than the literal "wdec" (e.g. `elif action == CB_PREFIX:` with a module-level import), AND a test pins the agreement so it cannot silently re-diverge — the cheapest honest form is asserting that the prefix the dispatcher branches on equals the prefix `encode_callback` actually emits, rather than asserting both equal the string "wdec" (which would re-hardcode the coupling in the test and pass through the very rename it is meant to catch). ⚠️ Closing this by changing CB_PREFIX's VALUE to match the literal is not a fix — it leaves three sites and two sources.

items.title: claude-pr-automerge fires on a REBASE that touched none of its trigger paths — a push's changed-file set is the pre-push-head→new-head diff, so rebasing onto a moved main drags main's paths in and un-drafts + auto-merges a PR that requested neither
items.source: session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ — observed LIVE on PR #10789 at 2026-09-02T11:34Z, not reasoned about. The PR was opened draft:true and came back draft:false with auto-merge armed.
items.detail: MEASURED, ON A REAL PR. #10789 was opened as a DRAFT (`draft: true`, verified on the API right after `pr-opener` created it) and explicitly must not merge — Tier-2 on a live trading system whose done-condition no CI run can perform. A force-push at 11:34Z rebasing the branch onto a moved `main` (133587f..af9af5e) triggered `.github/workflows/claude-pr-automerge.yml`, which ran `markPullRequestReadyForReview` and `enablePullRequestAutoMerge(SQUASH)`. Re-read immediately after: `draft: false`. **The branch never touched any trigger path.** THE MECHANISM. That workflow is `on: push: branches: [claude/**]` with a `paths:` filter that still includes the LEGACY shared file `.github/pr-automerge-request` — deliberately retained, per its own comment, 'for a transition window so an in-flight branch that already wrote it still fires', with 'Remove it once no open PR carries that file.' That file is present in the TREE (written by an earlier PR and merged to main at 133587f). GitHub computes a push event's changed-file set as the diff from the PRE-PUSH head to the new head — so a REBASE, which replays the branch over everything that landed on main in between, drags every path main changed into that set. If any of those commits touched a trigger path, the filter matches and the workflow fires. ⚠️ SO THE ARMING IS NOT OPT-IN, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE FINDING. The relay's design intent is a per-request file — you ASK for auto-merge by writing one. A rebase asks for nothing, and the repo's own merge protocol actively encourages syncing to main. The condition therefore fires most readily on exactly the branches doing the right thing. ⚠️ IT UN-DRAFTS, WHICH DEFEATS THE ONE SIGNAL A DRAFT EXISTS TO SEND. Every convention in this repo for 'prepared but not approved' — Tier-2 and Tier-3 both — is 'open it as a draft and ping the operator'. A workflow that converts drafts to ready on a push silently removes the marker the tier gate depends on, and the PR then merges on green with no human in the loop. Branch protection does not help: it gates on CHECKS, and the checks were green. ⚠️ RECOVERY WAS NOT AVAILABLE BY THE OBVIOUS ROUTE. Converting the PR back to draft (which also disables auto-merge) needs the GitHub API, and every attempt returned `API rate limit already exceeded for user ID 119055177` while READS kept working — so the session could watch the PR march toward a merge it could not stop. The only lever left was a deliberately failing required check (`tests/test_zz_automerge_hold.py`), which is a workaround, not a fix.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) the legacy `.github/pr-automerge-request` path is removed from the workflow's `paths:` filter — its own comment already says to, once no open PR carries it — AND the file is deleted from the tree, so the only way to arm auto-merge is writing a per-request file; OR (b) the workflow refuses to act on a push whose changed-file set includes a trigger path only incidentally — e.g. it requires the request file to have been ADDED or MODIFIED by a commit authored on this branch, not merely to appear in the push diff. AND, independently of which is chosen: the workflow MUST NOT `markPullRequestReadyForReview` on a PR that is already open as a draft. Opening a PR ready is a legitimate default for one this workflow CREATES; silently un-drafting one somebody else deliberately opened as a draft is not, because the draft flag is what this repo's Tier-2/Tier-3 conventions use to mean 'prepared, not approved'. ⚠️ Closing this by deleting `tests/test_zz_automerge_hold.py` is NOT a fix — that file is the symptom's workaround, and removing it while the trigger stands just re-arms the PR it is holding.

items.title: The CLAUDE.md session brief renders only monitoring rows past their CADENCE, so a `loud: true` row inside its cadence is NOT shown — while the brief's own text, in the same block, orders every loud row to be reported on and never silently carried
items.source: MI-66 (session_019vcX5ZTD8C7wNAEtfPUdFQ), noticed while verifying that two loud rows this session added had reached the brief. They had not, and the guard was right to say the brief matched the registers.
items.detail:
MEASURED, not inferred. scripts/ops/render_session_brief.py::due_items selects on CADENCE ALONE -- `kind == monitoring` and (verified_at absent, or check_every_days <= 0, or elapsed >= cadence). It never reads `loud`. So a loud row observed today with check_every_days 3 is absent from the brief for three days. Verified: two rows added this session with loud:true and verified_at 2026-09-02 produced ZERO occurrences in CLAUDE.md, and session-brief-guard --check passed, so this is the renderer's declared behaviour rather than a stale file.

THE INCONSISTENCY IS WITH TWO OTHER SURFACES, BOTH EXPLICIT.
(1) scripts/ops/render_due_list.py::src_open_items takes the opposite rule, in its own words: 'A `loud` row is listed even when not overdue: CLAUDE.md requires it to be REPORTED ON every session, so it is due by definition.' Two renderers over ONE register disagree about whether loud implies due.
(2) CLAUDE.md's own text -- inside the generated block -- reads: 'A row with `loud: true` must be REPORTED ON in your closing summary -- checked and stated, never silently carried.' So the brief instructs a session to report on rows it does not show it, unless they happen to be overdue.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING PEDANTRY: CLAUDE.md describes itself as 'the only surface that reaches a session before it acts', and hooks do not run on Claude Code on the web, so for a web session the brief is the whole mechanism. A loud row's entire purpose is to be un-skippable; being visible only while overdue makes loudness a function of the cadence, which is the one property loud exists to be independent of.

!! I AM NOT ASSERTING THIS IS A BUG, AND DID NOT CHANGE IT. The one-line fix (`if it.get('loud') or ...`) may be deliberately rejected: priority_lines' docstring says 'The brief must SHRINK as work lands; a priority block that grew into a manifesto would be one more wall to skim past', and permanently rendering every loud row cuts against that. Someone who knows which reading was intended should decide; a session that silently 'fixed' it could make the brief the wall its own design warns about.
items.resolution_criteria: A decision is RECORDED, either way, and the surfaces are made to agree with it. Either (a) loud implies due -- due_items consults `loud`, matching src_open_items' stated rule, and the brief-shrinks concern is addressed (e.g. loud rows render as one compact line rather than the full block); or (b) loud does NOT imply due in the brief -- in which case src_open_items' docstring and the 'must be REPORTED ON in your closing summary' line are corrected to say WHICH surface carries loud rows (DUE.md), so a session is not told to report on something the brief never showed it. !! CLOSING THIS BY EDITING ONLY THE PROSE ON ONE SIDE IS NOT A RESOLUTION -- the defect is that two generators over one register encode different rules, and prose that agrees with neither is how that survived. !! AND A GREEN session-brief-guard DOES NOT RESOLVE IT: the guard checks CLAUDE.md matches what the renderer produces, which is true today and is exactly why this was invisible.

items.title: SESSIONS.json is written at spawn and NEVER updated: 35 of 67 rows name no branch at all, so a cold successor reading them knows a session existed and has no route to its work
items.source: session_01NkekPZw73VYuynYhSdWLWm (MI-70) — measured at main 90437919 while building the Phase E reaper, not reasoned about.
items.detail:
MEASURED, population stated: all 67 rows of docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json at main 90437919, and all 34 branch entries across them. 35 rows carry `branches: []` and `prs: []` — written at spawn, with nothing ever writing back where the work went. Of the 34 branch entries that DO exist: 11 live on origin, 14 landed (a PR they name is in origin/main's history), 7 have no landing evidence, and 2 are PROSE typed into a `branches` array ('(rotating — one PR head at a time)' and 'claude/telegram-ping-mirror (expected; not yet pushed)' — the second being the documented lost-work case from WO-20260901-PHASE-E itself). One row's `prs` entry is a bare int rather than a string.

⚠️ THIS IS A DIFFERENT DEFECT FROM MI-15 / the 26-of-55 census, AND THE EXISTING DETECTORS DO NOT LOOK FOR IT. Those measure sessions ABSENT from the registry. This is sessions PRESENT whose row points at nothing — which reads as coverage while providing none, and is therefore the more dangerous of the two. `session_registry.py::cross_check` compares owner ids and never asks whether a row names a branch, so it passes on all 35.

WHY IT IS NOT 'REMEMBER TO UPDATE THE ROW': the manager CANNOT message a running sub-session, and the constraint is SYMMETRIC — verified again this session, SendMessage from a sub-session to its manager also returns 'No agent named ... is reachable'. The sub-session that would update its own row is exactly the one that may die first. 'Remember to register' has already failed twice; 'remember to update' is the same remedy one step later.

PARTIAL MITIGATION SHIPPED, NOT A FIX: scripts/ops/session_reaper.py recovers the branch from the `Claude-Session:` commit trailer and located 16 of the 35 anyway (live reap: `unreadable` 37 -> 21). It reports recovery on a SEPARATE axis (`branch_source`) precisely so this defect stays visible rather than being masked by a healthy-looking state count. The other 19 rows remain `none_found`.
items.resolution_criteria: `python3 scripts/ops/session_reaper.py --json` reports `by_branch_source.none_found` at 0 over a registry of >=20 rows — i.e. every row either names its own branch or has one recoverable from a commit trailer. ⚠️ A FALLING `none_found` IS NOT ENOUGH ALONE: it also falls when old rows age out, so state the row count beside it. ⚠️ AND THE REAL FIX IS `recovered_from_commit_trailer` FALLING WHILE `registry_declared` RISES (rows record their own branch). The reverse — recovery carrying an ever-larger share — is this defect being MASKED, not resolved, and must be reported as such rather than counted as progress.

items.title: Every commit carries a `Claude-Session:` trailer written as work happens — the durable session→work link the operating model asks for — and until MI-70 nothing in the repo read it
items.source: session_01NkekPZw73VYuynYhSdWLWm (MI-70) — found while looking for the MISSING incremental-progress mechanism and discovering it already existed.
items.detail:
operating-model-DESIGN.md § 'The coordination layer' names three mechanisms, the first being 'state written to the work object AS WORK HAPPENS, not at the end'. That was read as absent. It is not: the attribution footer every session appends puts `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_XXXX` in every commit body — a per-commit, durable, session-authored link from a session to its work, written incrementally and surviving the session's death in git.
