MEASURED at main 90437919: 63 distinct session ids in the last 400 origin/main commit bodies; 118 attributable across the 194 claude/** heads. ZERO consumers — grep over scripts/ and src/ found only the templates that WRITE it.

This is the `provenance-consumer-guard` shape one level up: a signal written and never read, worse than a missing one because a reader sees the field and assumes something acts on it. Here it cost real work — the registry's 35 empty rows were treated as unrecoverable when 16 were recoverable from a signal already on disk.
items.resolution_criteria: ALREADY MET for the CONSUMER gap this row names, verified 2026-09-02: `grep -rn 'Claude-Session' scripts/` returns a reader (scripts/ops/session_reaper.py::attribute_branches_by_trailer), and a live reap attributed 16 registry rows and 98 unregistered branches by it. ⚠️ CLOSED FOR THE CONSUMER GAP ONLY, and the residual is stated rather than claimed fixed: the trailer is a system-prompt CONVENTION, not an enforced format, so a session that omits or rewords it is unattributable and nothing detects that. Closing that residual needs its OWN row.

items.title: claude-pr-automerge's mis-fires were the PER-REQUEST glob, not the legacy shared path — both existing rows mis-attribute the mechanism, and the fix they prescribe would have fixed none of the three observed cases
items.source: session_01XrwTGRY819PCzBnppCTLbi (MI-69), dispatched to remove the legacy path; measured the push diffs before changing anything and found the dispatched diagnosis wrong.
items.detail: A CORRECTION to BL-20260902-A-REBASE-ARMS-AUTOMERGE-BECAUSE-A-PUSH-DIFF-INCLUDES-EVERYTHING-MAIN-CHANGED and to MI-62's sibling row, which is filed on the unmerged branch `claude/mi62/stop-unrequested-automerge` and so does not yet exist on `main` (its id is deliberately not cited here: `artifact-validity-guard` correctly refuses a reference that resolves to nothing, and citing it would read as tracked while being tracked by nobody until that branch lands). Both rows, and the dispatch built on them, name the legacy shared path `.github/pr-automerge-request` as what matched. MEASURED on all three 2026-09-02T13:19Z mis-fires (`9cf89802` mi63-true-blocked-on-edges, `5449ef6c` decision-push-back, `31cff960` openprs-settled-reconciler), taking the push diff as GitHub computes it — parent1..merge, i.e. before-head to after-head: THE LEGACY PATH IS IN ZERO OF THE THREE. It had not been modified on `main` since 2026-08-21 (`fd6c2cab`), so it could not match a 2026-09-02 rebase. What matched in all three is the PER-REQUEST GLOB `.github/pr-automerge-requests/*.txt` — nine such files landed on `main` on 2026-09-02 alone, so any branch merging `main` drags other branches' request files into its own push diff. ⚠️ THE PRESCRIBED FIX WOULD HAVE FIXED NOTHING. Removing the legacy path — which is what both rows' resolution criteria lead with and what MI-69 was dispatched to do — leaves the defect fully intact, because the surviving glob is the one that was matching. Worse, it would have looked like a fix and closed the rows. ⚠️ THE TRANSFERABLE LESSON IS THE ONE THIS REPO KEEPS PAYING FOR: a mechanism was inferred from a plausible reading of the workflow file and never checked against the diff. `git diff --name-only <sha>^1 <sha> -- <paths>` is a one-line check that was available the whole time. Field beats comment; the diff beats the theory about it. THE REAL INVARIANT: a `paths:` filter CANNOT be the gate, because it cannot distinguish 'I asked for auto-merge' from 'I merged somebody else's ask' — the two produce an identical changed-file set. This is the third narrowing of that filter (`**` -> `*.txt` 2026-08-22, then this), and the first two both recurred, because narrowing a filter that cannot express the question is not a fix. FIXED: the load-bearing gate now lives in the job body — the request file must be named for THIS branch and be added-or-modified relative to `main`, so a file inherited by a merge is not an ask. Held by `scripts/ci/check_automerge_trigger.py` (ungated in CI, 6 planted-defect self-tests) and `tests/test_automerge_request_gate.py`, which runs the SHIPPED script under node rather than re-implementing it. Negative control: against the pre-fix workflow the three negative tests FAIL (it calls pulls.create + markReady + enableAutoMerge on a branch that asked nothing); positive control: the two 'a genuine request still arms' tests pass against BOTH workflows, so the trigger is not merely broken.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVED by PR from claude/mi69-automerge-misfire. Re-opens if any of: the `paths:` filter gains an entry; the job body stops comparing the request file against `main`; or `markPullRequestReadyForReview` returns to the executable script. `automerge-trigger-guard` fails CI on all three.

items.title: #10788 and #10764 were un-drafted and armed for auto-merge by the relay; both bodies say they must not merge, and neither branch ever requested it
items.source: session_01XrwTGRY819PCzBnppCTLbi (MI-69) — measured against the live open-PR set while fixing the relay, not reported by anyone.
items.detail: A LIVE, UNRESOLVED STATE at time of filing, and the fix in the same PR does NOT clear it — the relay change stops NEW mis-arming; it cannot retract auto-merge already enabled. #10788 (`claude/decision-push-back`) reads `draft: false`; its own body says 'Draft. Not for merge — it carries an operator decision.' It carries an UNANSWERED operator decision about minting an account-wide `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN`. Armed at 2026-09-02T13:19:04Z, confirmed from the run's own log rather than inferred: run 33634977260 -> `##[notice]auto-merge enabled on #10788 — merges when CI is green`. #10764 (`claude/claude-md-reference-split`) reads `draft: false`; its own body ends 'Left as a DRAFT. The manager owns the merge.' Un-drafted by runs 33609894152 / 33610115896 at 08:39Z / 08:42Z. NEITHER BRANCH ASKED. `git log origin/main..<branch> --name-only` returns no request file for either — checked across all 14 open `claude/**` branches, and the other six non-draft ones each carry their own correctly-named request file, so this is not a measurement artefact. ⚠️ BRANCH PROTECTION IS NOT A BACKSTOP HERE: it gates on CHECKS, and the checks are green or will be. Both will merge with no human in the loop. ⚠️ THE FILING SESSION COULD NOT FIX IT: `update_pull_request` and `disable_pr_auto_merge` are 403 from a read-only session, the same limit that forced #10796 to be CLOSED rather than re-drafted on the same day.
items.resolution_criteria: Someone with PR write access confirms, for EACH of #10788 and #10764, that auto-merge is disabled AND the PR is back to draft (or that the operator has deliberately decided to merge it). Read the state back from the API after acting — the arming was invisible to both PRs' authors, so a claim that it is undone is not the same as observing that it is. ⚠️ If either has already merged by the time this is picked up, record THAT as the outcome rather than closing the row quietly: an unrequested merge of a PR carrying an unanswered operator decision is the harm this class exists to prevent, and it should be recorded as having happened.

items.title: A `git merge origin/main` un-drafted PR #10788 and armed squash auto-merge on it, overruling an explicit operator instruction -- and the repo had no way to turn auto-merge off
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH halves, and neither substitutes for the other. (1) `claude-pr-automerge.yml`'s `on.push.paths` no longer lists `.github/pr-automerge-request`, so a merge of `main` cannot fire it -- checkable by reading the file. (2) The OFF switch EXISTS AND HAS BEEN EXERCISED, not merely deployed: `automation/pr-automerge-disable-results/mi60-10788-keep-draft.txt` on branch `automation/disarm-10788` reads 'auto_merge: disabled' and 'draft: converted', and PR #10788 re-read live returns draft true. BOTH WERE SATISFIED BEFORE THIS ROW WAS FILED, which is why it is filed `resolved` rather than open. [!] WHAT WOULD RE-OPEN IT: any PR armed for auto-merge by a push that requested nothing. [!] AND THIS ROW IS NOT A CLAIM THAT THE STALE FILE IS GONE -- it is deliberately left on disk and inert, so its continued presence is not evidence of this defect and must not be filed as a recurrence.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 on PR #10788, which was opened DRAFT on an explicit operator instruction (*keep it a draft; the operator un-drafts and merges*). A routine `git merge origin/main` was enough to overrule that.

=== MECHANISM. `claude-pr-automerge.yml`'s trigger still listed the LEGACY shared path `.github/pr-automerge-request` alongside the per-request `*.txt` files. Its own header said that path stayed 'for a transition window ... Remove it once no open PR carries that file' -- and the window closed in the worst way: the file was COMMITTED TO `main` (by #10786), so from that moment EVERY branch in the repo carried it and any merge of main 'touched' it. The merge commit fired the workflow on a request nobody made; it ran `markPullRequestReadyForReview` (un-drafting the PR) and `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` (SQUASH).

=== THE HAZARD WAS ALREADY DOCUMENTED AND WAS NOT FIXED, which is the part worth carrying. `docs/github-actions-workflows.md`'s catalog row for this workflow said, in as many words, that it 'triggers on any push that *touches* the request path, so merging `main` can inherit another PR's request' and cited BL-20260821-AUTOMERGE-TRIGGER-IS-A-SINGLE-SHARED-FILE. A warning written in a catalog nobody reads mid-task prevented nothing.

=== EVIDENCE, not inference. Job `open-and-automerge` on run 33628636273 ran 12:12:20Z to 12:12:24Z, FOUR SECONDS. The script returns immediately after enableAutoMerge SUCCEEDS and otherwise falls into an ~8-minute poll loop, so a 4s run is the success path. Independently, the PR flipped `draft: true -> false` while `automation/pr-requests/mi-60-decision-push-back.json` (the request that opened it) records draft true.

=== WHY IT WAS UNRECOVERABLE. Nothing in the repo could turn auto-merge back off. `update_pull_request` returns 403 'Resource not accessible by integration' from the owning session; `pr-close.yml`'s own header says it 'cannot reopen'; and `disablePullRequestAutoMerge` / `convertPullRequestToDraft` appeared NOWHERE in .github/ or scripts/ (grep-verified before the fix). The repo could arm a merge from a runner and could not disarm one -- a one-way door.

=== THE CLASS, which is the transferable part. That file's own trigger had ALREADY been narrowed once for this exact shape: an earlier version used `**` and armed auto-merge on itself by matching a README, and the fix comment says 'A trigger path that a doc edit can fire is a trigger that merges PRs nobody asked to merge.' The residual legacy path is the same defect with a WIDER blast radius, because every branch merges main. A shared, committed file is not a per-caller signal -- it is ambient state, and every branch eventually carries it.

=== FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE (branch claude/decision-push-back). (1) The legacy path is removed from the trigger, so only `.github/pr-automerge-requests/*.txt` fires it. (2) New `.github/workflows/pr-automerge-disable.yml` -- the OFF switch, with `pr-close.yml`'s optimistic-concurrency guard (the request must name the PR's CURRENT head or the run refuses) copied rather than reinvented, and with `disable_state`/`draft_state` graded SEPARATELY so a half-applied disarm cannot read as clean (`already_off` is a real state, distinct from *we could not look*).

=== WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE. The stale `.github/pr-automerge-request` file is LEFT ON DISK. Removing it from the trigger list is what makes it inert (its contents are never read); deleting it would create a merge conflict for every open branch that already modified it -- the exact collision the per-request split was made to end -- and the deleting push would touch that path one last time. Delete it in a quiet window.

items.title: MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json records 0 branches and 2 PR numbers across 72 items — so an item's claim to be `in_flight` cannot be checked against any artifact, and the obvious staleness detector is uncomputable
items.resolution_criteria: OBSERVABLE, and deliberately about the SPAWN PATH rather than the current rows: a NEW checklist item written after this lands carries a `branch` (or a `prs` entry) naming work that exists on origin, populated at spawn time rather than backfilled — verified by reading the item and resolving the branch on origin, not by reading the spawn code. A CENSUS is the second half and is separable: `in_flight` items naming no branch, counted and reported (today 23 of 23), so the residue is visible while it drains. ⚠️ Backfilling the existing 23 does NOT close this — a branch guessed from a title is a false join that reads as a verified one, which is worse than an absent one, the same polarity as an invented `blocked_on` edge being read by the constraint computation as a real blocker. ⚠️ And a CI guard that FAILS on a missing branch must not land until the spawn path populates it, or it fails all 23 rows on day one — the '52 findings for 26 days' condition. Census first, enforce second.
items.source: MI-77 (session_01PbQAQXRY2oB1ep2BFEUZeA), while testing four candidate MCP-free proxies for 'something is waiting on the manager'. Three did not survive contact with the data; this is the one that failed for a reason worth fixing rather than a reason worth accepting.
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-02 over docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json (population: ALL 72 items; state vocabulary is the file's own `states` block). 23 items read `in_flight`. Of those 23, **0 carry a `branch` and 0 carry a `prs` entry**. Across all 72 items: 0 branches, 2 PR entries. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. `in_flight` is defined in the file itself as 'a session is actively working it'. That is a claim about the world, and with no branch and no PR on the row there is NOTHING to check it against — not from CI, not from a successor manager arriving cold, not from a session reading the register. The claim is unfalsifiable by construction. It is not hypothetical that the claim goes wrong: MI-18 reads `in_flight` while its own `owner` field says 'session_01LqVvgvusnN87neBn5ayzhg (archived; its PR #10694 stands)', and #10694's branch has had no push for 18.9h. WHAT IT COST THIS SESSION. The natural detector — 'a checklist item `in_flight` whose owner's branch has had no push for N hours' — is UNCOMPUTABLE against this file, so the watcher that shipped (scripts/ops/pr_queue_latency.py) had to be keyed on the OPEN-PR list instead. That works, and it is strictly weaker in one respect: it can only see work that reached a PR. An `in_flight` item with no PR yet is invisible to it, and the checklist is the only place such an item exists. ⚠️ THE FIX IS NOT 'BACKFILL THE 23 ROWS'. A branch guessed from a title would be worse than an absent one — a false join reads as a verified one, the same polarity as an invented `blocked_on` edge being read by the constraint computation as a real blocker. The durable fix is that the field is populated AT SPAWN, where the manager already knows it: session_registry.py's spawn path records branches on SESSIONS.json rows, and the checklist item is written in the same act. ⚠️ AND SESSIONS.json IS NOT A SUBSTITUTE. It carries branches on some rows, but it is a spawn-time record nothing updates (session_reaper.py measured 35 of 67 rows naming no branch at all), and it has no `state` field to join `in_flight` against. The two registers answer different questions and neither answers this one alone.
items.proposed_fix: Record the branch on the checklist item at the moment the sub-session is spawned — the same act that already writes the SESSIONS.json row — rather than backfilling later or inferring it. Then a cheap offline detector becomes possible: an `in_flight` item whose named branch has had no push for N hours is either finished-and-unrecorded or dead, and both are the manager's to resolve. ⚠️ Do NOT add a guard that FAILS on an item missing a branch until the spawn path populates it, or it fails on all 23 rows the day it lands — the '52 findings for 26 days' condition, where a permanently-red check becomes something everyone walks past. Census first, enforce second.

items.title: pr-queue-watch.yml's concurrency group serialises RUNS but not RECEIPT LANDINGS — a second run can read a main its predecessor's auto-merge receipt has not reached, write a conflicting receipt, strand the branch, and put a FALSE PAGE on the cron-failure channel
items.source: MI-77 (session_01PbQAQXRY2oB1ep2BFEUZeA), found by dispatching the watcher to verify what it had just shipped. The failing run was my own redundant dispatch, not the manager's.
items.resolution_criteria: OBSERVABLE: a run of pr-queue-watch.yml that starts while main does NOT yet carry a receipt at least as fresh as the one it is about to write COMPLETES WITHOUT opening a conflicting commit-to-main PR — verified by dispatching two runs back to back and reading both conclusions plus the open-PR list for `automation/data-commit-*` branches, not by reading the workflow YAML. ⚠️ A single quiet run does NOT close this: the ordinary 6-hourly cadence never reproduces the condition, so a green scheduled run is not evidence. The reproduction is the back-to-back dispatch. ⚠️ DECIDING NOT TO FIX IT ALSO CLOSES THIS and must be RECORDED as a decision — the hazard is unreachable on cadence, so 'accept it; do not double-dispatch' is a legitimate disposition, but it must be written down rather than left looking like an open bug.
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-02. Two workflow_dispatch runs 35s apart: the manager's (33666587546, 18:20:23Z, conclusion success) and mine (33666645309, 18:20:58Z, conclusion FAILURE). The `concurrency: group: pr-queue-watch, cancel-in-progress: false` worked as intended — my run started only after the first FINISHED at 18:23:56Z. But the receipt does not land when the run ends: it lands through .github/actions/commit-to-main as a PAT-authenticated AUTO-MERGE PR, which takes minutes more. So my run checked out a main carrying no receipt, correctly graded `refresh_due: true` (there was nothing to refresh from), wrote one, and opened PR #10835. That PR conflicted the moment the first run's receipt merged, logged `state=OPEN; refresh=failed_conflict` every 30s for the full 30-minute verify-merged budget, and failed the job. ⚠️ THE DEFECT IS NOT IN refresh_due, WHICH BEHAVED CORRECTLY given what it could see. It is that the serialisation boundary is the RUN and the shared resource is the RECEIPT ON MAIN, and those are not the same interval. ⚠️ IT IS UNREACHABLE ON THE DECLARED CADENCE. cron is `41 */6 * * *` and a run takes ~3.5 minutes, so two scheduled runs are six hours apart and cannot overlap. It required two hand dispatches 35 seconds apart, and the second was redundant — the first was already running. TWO COSTS, and the second is the one that matters. (1) A stranded automation branch, the exact shape BL-20260830-A-TRANSIENT-RED-BASE-PERMANENTLY-STRANDS-AN-AUTOMERGE-BRANCH records; #10835 was closed with its cause written on it, and it was SUPERSEDED rather than merely late — main carries the same generated_at WITHOUT the false last_paged_at latch that #10841 cleared, so merging it would have re-introduced that latch. (2) A `failure` conclusion on a workflow watched by claude-run-failure-alert.yml, which reaches the operator as a page that is NOT a queue escalation. Spending the escalation channel on a self-inflicted collision is the desensitised-alarm class this repo has measured at 202 of 376 CRITICALs being one un-latched alarm.
items.proposed_fix: Before landing, re-read the receipt from origin/main and skip the commit-to-main step entirely when main already carries a receipt whose generated_at is at least as new as the one just computed — a no-op landing is correct there, because a fresher receipt is exactly what the liveness guard wants and this run's assessment adds nothing. ⚠️ Do NOT 'fix' this by widening the concurrency group or by dropping verify-merged: the first does not help (the runs were already serialised) and the second re-opens BL-20260830-TWELVE-OF-THIRTEEN-COMMIT-TO-MAIN-CALLERS-NEVER-CHECK-THEIR-ROWS-LANDED, where a green run means only that a PR exists. ⚠️ And weigh whether to fix it at all: the condition is unreachable on the 6-hourly cadence, and this workflow has already taken two corrections in one day. Accepting it with 'do not double-dispatch' written down is a legitimate outcome.

items.title: Heartbeating the manager lease requires a PR through three required checks, so a ~20s liveness signal costs a ~10-18 minute CI cycle against a 90-minute TTL — the recurrence of a class twice marked resolved on lesser mechanisms
items.source: Manager session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ, 18:12Z, hit directly while running its own sweep. RECURRENCE, filed with similar_ok: BL-20260812-SWEEP-CORPUS-CANNOT-PUSH-TO-MAIN and BL-20260706-GPU-BURST-LEDGER-PUSH-RACE are the same class (a mechanism writes to main, branch protection rejects it) and BOTH are marked resolved. Each was fixed for its own writer; the class was not, and it has now landed on the lease.
items.detail:
MEASURED. `git push origin main` carrying only a MANAGER-LEASE.json heartbeat is refused: `GH006: Protected branch update failed` / `3 of 3 required status checks are expected`. So the only path for a heartbeat is a branch + PR + guards + pytest-collect + pytest-run, where pytest-run alone measured 943s and 1103s on two runs today. THE ARITHMETIC IS THE FINDING: the lease TTL is 90 minutes and one heartbeat costs roughly a fifth of it in wall clock and a full CI slot in contention. 

WHY THIS IS NOT MERELY SLOW. The lease exists so that exactly one management session runs at a time, and its takeover is TIME-BASED precisely because a session that dies cannot hand over. That design assumes a heartbeat is cheap enough that a LIVE holder always makes it. Here it is not, so the predictable failure is a manager that is alive, working, and reads as expired — at which point a second manager claims the lease and the one operator requirement the mechanism exists to enforce is violated by the mechanism's own cost. A skipped heartbeat and a dead holder are INDISTINGUISHABLE from outside, which is the collapsed-state shape this repo names elsewhere: the lease can say `held_fresh` or `expired` but cannot say `the holder is alive and could not afford to say so`. 

WHAT I ACTUALLY DID, so the workaround is not mistaken for a fix: I folded the heartbeat into an unrelated manager PR (#10833). That works only when the manager happens to have a PR to make. A quiet management hour — which is exactly the state a supervising manager should be in — produces no PR and therefore no heartbeat. 

NOT PROPOSING THE OBVIOUS FIX. Exempting the lease path from branch protection, or giving it a bot push token, is a protection hole opened for convenience and is not mine to decide. The candidates worth costing are: (a) move the lease off the repo to a surface a session can write cheaply, which loses the property that a COLD session can read it from git — the stated reason it lives in the repo at all; (b) a scheduled workflow that heartbeats on the holder's behalf, which is a check invoked by something other than the actor and therefore the right shape, but must not be able to heartbeat a DEAD holder — that would make the lease immortal, strictly worse than the current cost; (c) accept the cost and shorten nothing, treating the fold-into-a-PR pattern as the contract and saying so in the lease's own docstring, which at least stops the next manager rediscovering this. 

POPULATION NOTE: one manager, one day. I have not measured how often a real management hour produces no PR, and that frequency is what decides whether (c) is survivable.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (1) a manager holding the lease can record a heartbeat without opening a PR, by a path that still lets a COLD session read the holder from git and that CANNOT heartbeat a dead holder; or (2) the fold-into-a-PR pattern is accepted as the contract, written into manager_lease.py's own docstring beside the TTL, AND the frequency of PR-less management hours is measured so the accepted risk has a number behind it. A row that closes on 'it worked today' closes nothing — the failure is a quiet hour, not a busy one.

items.title: `loud: true` is set on 34 of 45 OPEN-ITEMS rows (75.6%), while the register's own rule is that every loud row must be REPORTED in a session's closing summary — a report nobody can actually make, so in practice none are
items.source: Manager session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ, 18:33Z, counted while doing the sweep step that says 'a loud: true row must be REPORTED'. I could not comply, which is the finding.
items.detail:
MEASURED over the WHOLE file at origin/main, not a sample: docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json holds 45 items and 34 carry loud: true = 75.6%. Of those 34, exactly TWO are past their cadence today (OI-20260901-OPERATING-LAYER-BUILD... at 1d/1d, OI-20260829-TRAINER-IS-NOW-A-DECIDED-DEPENDENCY... at 4d/3d) and TWELVE have verified_at null, i.e. never observed at all.

WHY THIS IS THE DESENSITISED-ALARM P1 ONE LEVEL UP. CLAUDE.md's own rule is that a loud row 'must be REPORTED ON in your closing summary -- checked and stated, never silently carried'. At 34 rows that instruction cannot be followed by any session, so what actually happens is that it is followed for none -- the same shape as the 202-of-376 CRITICALs that trained the operator past the one channel reserved for an unprotected position, and as the 62/86 alarming dataset manifests the 'if you see something' rule was written for. A flag that marks three quarters of a register is not a priority signal; it is the register.

THE COMPLEMENT IS ALREADY FILED AND THE PAIR IS THE POINT. BL-20260902-A-LOUD-OPEN-ITEM-IS-ABSENT-FROM-THE-SESSION-BRIEF-THAT-ORDERS-IT-REPORTED records that render_session_brief.py::due_items selects on CADENCE ALONE and never reads `loud`, so a loud row inside its cadence is NOT rendered. Put the two together: the brief UNDER-SHOWS loud rows and the register OVER-MARKS them, so the flag currently changes nothing in either direction. Neither row is worth fixing alone -- making the brief render every loud row would render 34 of them, which is the same failure with more scrolling.

NOT PROPOSING THE OBVIOUS FIX. 'Un-loud some rows' is a judgement about 34 specific items that belongs to whoever understands each, not to a sweep that counted them; and a cap on loud rows would be the bandaid check_open_items.py already reversed for the register itself (MAX_ITEMS = None, with the reasoning that a cap 'bounded the LIST rather than making anything get read or fixed'). The candidates worth costing: (a) loud means SOMETHING IS DUE OR OVERDUE -- derived, not authored, so it cannot saturate by drift; (b) loud stays authored but the brief renders loud-AND-due, making the reportable set the intersection rather than either alone; (c) a severity split, so 'loud' stops being one bucket holding a live money-at-risk row next to a shipped-not-yet-observed one.

POPULATION NOTE: one register, one reading, 2026-09-02T18:33Z. I have not measured how the proportion moved over time, and whether it CREPT to 76% or was always there decides whether this is drift or a design that never discriminated.

=== RE-MEASURED 2026-09-10T01:4xZ BY session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj (manager) -- IT HAS WORSENED, AND THE DIRECTION IS THE FINDING. Same population definition, the WHOLE file at origin/main, not a sample: OPEN-ITEMS.json now holds 72 items and 61 carry loud: true = 84.7%, against 34 of 45 = 75.6% on 2026-09-02. The register grew by 27 rows in eight days and the loud SHARE rose 9.1 points with it, so `loud` is being set close to by-default on new rows. At 61 rows the register's own instruction -- that every loud row 'must be REPORTED ON in your closing summary, checked and stated, never silently carried' -- is further out of reach than when this row was opened, and its diagnosis (a flag marking most of a register is the register, not a priority signal) holds a fortiori. !! HOW THIS INSTANCE WAS FOUND IS ITSELF THE EVIDENCE. The manager went to file a NEW row about the 84.7% figure, ran backlog_search first, and found THIS row at 0.86 overlap. That is the append-vs-duplicate discipline working -- and it is simultaneously a demonstration of the defect: the manager had reported three loud rows BY NAME in four consecutive status updates that night and still did not know this row existed, because 61 loud rows cannot be read and the session brief does not render them (BL-20260902-A-LOUD-OPEN-ITEM-IS-ABSENT-FROM-THE-SESSION-BRIEF-THAT-ORDERS-IT-REPORTED). The flag failed to surface a row ABOUT the flag to the session most actively obeying it. !! NO NEW ROW WAS FILED AND NONE SHOULD BE: this is the same defect getting worse, and a second id would split the evidence and make the trend unreadable. The pair-fix reasoning in this row's own text is unchanged and is not re-litigated here.
items.resolution_criteria: The set of rows a session is actually required to report on is SMALLER than the register and is derivable rather than authored, AND a session is observed reporting on that set in full. ⚠️ Closing this by editing 34 rows' flags without changing what PRODUCES the flag closes nothing -- the proportion will drift back, because every new row is filed by someone who thinks their row is important. ⚠️ And it does NOT close by capping the register: the cap was already tried and reversed for exactly this file.

items.title: SESSIONS.json has a spawn-time writer and NO close-time writer, so every sub-session reads 'working' forever
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-02T20:52Z: all 15 sub-sessions this manager spawned today read state='working' in docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json, while list_sessions reports 14 IDLE and 1 RUNNING. Sessions idle since 12:30Z (MI-05-PHASE-D, 8h) still read 'working'. A cold manager reading this file would believe 15 sessions are live -- and would either not spawn, or wait on work nobody is doing. ROOT CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT FORGETFULNESS: session_registry.py has 'register' and 'confirm', both SPAWN-time, and NOTHING writes a terminal state. MI-15 and the 2026-09-02T05:56Z re-measurement both fixed COMPLETENESS (is the row there?) and neither touched CURRENCY (does the row say what is true now?). The registry therefore went from 'missing rows' to 'present rows that all lie in the same direction', which is WORSE: an absent row is visibly absent, whereas 15 rows reading 'working' looks like a healthy register. Same class as this repo's own landed_unproven-vs-done rule, applied to sessions. 5 of 15 rows also carried checklist_item: null (MI-79..MI-83) so they could not be joined to the checklist at all -- and the offline session-registry-guard cross-checks MANAGER-CHECKLIST owner against the registry, so a null item is invisible to the very guard meant to catch this.
items.evidence: list_sessions(mine=true, limit=60) at 2026-09-02T20:52Z: 60 rows, 15 tagged manager:session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ; 14 SESSION_STATUS_IDLE, 1 SESSION_STATUS_RUNNING (session_018ruZdgEkPZ1XceWzLwuYUU / MI-83). SESSIONS.json at origin/main 24842ead: 15/15 state='working'. Data corrected by hand in this PR; the WRITER is not built.
items.resolution_criteria: A close-time writer exists and is EXERCISED: either (a) session_registry.py gains a 'close' verb a sub-session calls in its own close-out AND a reaper that grades a row against a live list_sessions observation -- a session that dies cannot close itself, so (a) alone is insufficient and the reaper is the load-bearing half; or (b) state is DERIVED at read time from a live observation rather than stored, at which point it cannot go stale. !! CORRECTING THE DATA DOES NOT CLOSE THIS. This PR already did that, and the rows go stale again the next time a session goes idle. The defect is the missing writer. !! A GREEN session-registry-guard DOES NOT CLOSE IT EITHER: that guard checks COMPLETENESS and passed throughout the entire window in which all 15 rows were wrong.

items.title: RECURRENCE of BL-20260830-SCHEDULED-WORKFLOW-LAG-WENT-FROM-1H-TO-6-12H-ON-2026-08-27 — the operator's ping cadence was raised to an hourly GitHub cron on 2026-09-02 while an open row said crons here run 6-12h late; four hours later the operator asked why the pings stopped, and nothing in the repo could tell him a slot had been missed
items.resolution_criteria: TWO PARTS, and they are different facts -- say which you cleared. (1) CARRIER: a work-digest run with event=push is OBSERVED completing and its receipt docs/claude/work/WORK-DIGEST.json appears ON MAIN carrying trigger="push" and a generated_at from that run -- read the run history and that stamp, NEVER the workflow file. A workflow_dispatch run clears NOTHING here, because the failure class being watched is a trigger that does not fire. (2) DETECTOR: check_digest_liveness.py is observed grading `fresh` on a PR OTHER than the one that introduced it, which is what proves it armed itself rather than merely being registered. [!] MERGING THIS CLEARS NEITHER -- a merge is not a deploy and a deploy is not a run. [!] A GREEN SELF-TEST CLEARS NEITHER: 38 assertions already pass in a harness, and a harness is exactly what cannot reach a trigger. [!] AND THE ROW DOES NOT CLEAR ON THE DIGEST ARRIVING WHILE SOMEONE IS WORKING -- the unfixed half is the QUIET window, so clearing it needs either an observed quiet-period heartbeat or a RECORDED operator decision not to buy one (a fresh-session Routine watchdog, ~4 firings/day, measured creator-independent on trig_01TWdAvrwFLe6T9XFoNopTeo). Deciding NOT to is a legitimate outcome and must be recorded as a decision rather than left looking like work in flight.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 by MI-80. work-digest.yml declared `20 * * * *` from 16:22Z and the 17:20Z and 18:20Z slots both did not fire; its COMPLETE life is four runs (run_number 4 -- a census, since a run number cannot exceed the number of runs), three scheduled, ~7h apart against a declared 6x/day, one of them CONCLUDING FAILURE at 07:10Z.

NOT A WORK-DIGEST BUG -- it is repo-wide. Every scheduled producer lands hours late or skips days: probes.yml generated_at 09-01T10:13Z (+4h53m vs `20 5 * * *`, nothing 09-02); due-list.yml landed 09-02T09:57Z (+4h07m); econ-calendar-produce 09-02T00:44Z (+2h14m); macro-valuation-snapshot 09-01T12:52Z (+5h22m, nothing 09-02). Four workflows, four concurrency groups, one shape. Commit-time overstates slip by up to ~30m (the verify-merged wait); probes.yml's generated_at is the clean number. RULED OUT with reasons: the concurrency group (governs execution not run CREATION; a concurrency-cancelled run still appears in history and none do) and the 40-minute budget (a run never created cannot be budget-limited; the 18:34Z dispatch took 2m31s end to end).

WHY THIS IS FILED AS A RECURRENCE AND NOT A DUPLICATE (similar_ok). BL-20260830-SCHEDULED-WORKFLOW-LAG-WENT-FROM-1H-TO-6-12H-ON-2026-08-27 is OPEN and already says 'ANY plan whose correctness depends on a cron firing at roughly its declared time is now wrong', and records that the evidence 'was already in this repo ... and was not checked before the approach was chosen'. Three days later the operator's NOTIFICATION CADENCE -- which F6 makes the CONDITION the autonomy grant rests on -- was put on exactly that carrier. The earlier fix did not hold because it was a row nobody read, not a mechanism. That the same row was un-read twice, the second time on the operator-facing channel, IS the finding.

THE SECOND HALF, AND THE MORE DURABLE ONE: nothing could say a slot had been MISSED. render_due_list.src_red_crons grades the latest scheduled run's CONCLUSION, so a cron that never fires leaves a stale-but-successful latest run and reads clean -- a missed slot and a quiet hour are indistinguishable from it. And it rides due-list.yml, itself a cron, itself measured 4h07m late: a cron watchdog for crons cannot report its own carrier dying.
items.evidence: mcp__github__actions_list run listing 2026-09-02T18:36Z (work-digest run_number 4); git log on each producer's output path; push-event control: merge 8c82be1a at 18:36:23Z triggered five push-event workflows at 18:36:26Z, and main took 34 merges in the 6h to 18:36Z (one every ~10.6 min). Full write-up: docs/research/digest-cadence-carrier-2026-09-02.md
items.proposed_fix: PARTLY SHIPPED by MI-80 (Tier-1): work-digest.yml also fires on push:main, rate-limited to hourly by scripts/ops/digest_due.py over a committed receipt docs/claude/work/WORK-DIGEST.json; scripts/ci/check_digest_liveness.py grades fresh/stale/never_ran/unreadable and runs in run_guards.py on every PR, so a stopped digest reddens CI instead of going silent. NOT FIXED, stated rather than glossed: a push-driven digest cannot produce a heartbeat while main is genuinely quiet -- there is no push to ride, and the cron kept as second carrier is best-effort by measurement. A guaranteed quiet-period heartbeat needs a Claude Routine (reliable on this account -- the :26 manager sweep fired 54s late) at the cost of a session per firing; that is an OPERATOR cost decision and is deliberately not assumed. Also unfixed: the systemic half, that an open correct row did not reach the session that needed it.

items.title: notify_on_pull marks a ping hash DELIVERED on a successful send_ping.enqueue(), which only writes a JSON file to a local inbox dir -- and the bridge that actually calls Telegram logs no outcome, so 'already-delivered' attests a file write and no VM-side log can tell a ping delivered to the wrong chat from one never delivered at all
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 by MI-80, in the code on origin/main and against the live VM.

THE MARKING. notify_on_pull.py:767 calls send_ping.enqueue(body, priority=..., target='claude') and then _record_delivered_hash on its success. enqueue() writes a JSON file into an inbox directory (atomic tmp+rename) and returns the path -- IT MAKES NO NETWORK CALL. Its own comment is honest about this: 'Record the hash after a successful enqueue'. So a hash in runtime_logs/pending_pings_delivered.txt attests A LOCAL FILE WRITE.

THE DEAD CODE THAT MAKES IT LOOK SAFE. _post_telegram (the only function that checks status_code == 200, with retry/backoff and a permanent-failure branch) and _send_priority are DEFINED AND NEVER CALLED in that module -- grep returns their def lines and zero call sites. A reader auditing this file finds correct response-handling code and reasonably concludes delivery is verified. It is not on this path.

AND THE NEXT HOP RECORDS NOTHING EITHER. /api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-claude-bridge.service (60 lines, 20:31-20:33Z) shows drain_pending_claude_pings running every 5s and 'executed successfully' every time, with NO other output -- no count drained, no chat id, no Telegram response. Pure apscheduler start/finish. So reading the journal at exactly the right second would still establish nothing.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. The operator reported at 18:33Z and again ~20:30Z that the work digest is not reaching them, while every upstream signal was green: work-digest run #5 fired on event=schedule 19:47:22Z success; pending-pings.jsonl carries 53 rows with four work_digest entries; the VM is at HEAD; the drain logged '>>> Pings dispatched.' and 11 'skipping already-delivered line' rows. EVERY ONE OF THOSE IS COMPATIBLE WITH THE OPERATOR RECEIVING NOTHING.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. This does NOT establish that the pings were lost. Delivery to the WRONG CHAT is fully live and is well-supported by OI-20260901-CLAUDE-CHANNEL-SEPARATION-SHIPPED-BUT-UNPROVEN, which records exactly this confusion on 2026-09-01 with TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET unset. What IS established is that no VM-side log can DISCRIMINATE the two -- the last hop is observable only on the operator's phone. That is the defect: the system cannot answer its own most important question.
items.evidence: scripts/notify_on_pull.py:767 + :251 (_record_delivered_hash) + :110/:137 (uncalled _post_telegram/_send_priority); scripts/send_ping.py::enqueue/_inbox_for; /api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-claude-bridge.service read 2026-09-02T20:33Z via diag_fetch.sh (served by https://ict-bot.duckdns.org). Write-up: docs/research/digest-cadence-carrier-2026-09-02.md addendum 2.
items.resolution_criteria: A ping's delivery record is derived from the TELEGRAM API RESPONSE rather than from a local file write, and that is OBSERVED end to end: one ping enqueued, the bridge's own log naming the chat_id it sent to and the HTTP status it got back, and the delivered-hash written only after that. [!] A GREEN DRAIN CLEARS NOTHING -- 'executed successfully' every 5s is the current state and is exactly the uninformative signal being reported. [!] NOR DOES SETTING TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET: that would fix the DESTINATION (possibility (a)) and leave the MARKING defect untouched, so the system would still be unable to prove a delivery. Those are two different fixes and closing this on the first would be wrong. [!] AND A PASSING TEST DOES NOT CLEAR IT: the failure is that a real send is unverified on the fleet, which a harness cannot reach.
items.proposed_fix: NOT ATTEMPTED by MI-80 and deliberately so -- it is VM-side, Tier-2, and touches the notification path. Shape: have the bridge's drain record the Telegram response (chat_id + HTTP status) per ping, and move _record_delivered_hash behind that outcome rather than the enqueue. The already-correct _post_telegram is the model; the bug is that nothing calls it. Until then, treat pending_pings_delivered.txt as an ENQUEUE log and rename it to say so, so no future session reads it as delivery evidence.

items.title: The trainer's order-flow capture has ALREADY lost bars, 52 times, and nothing has ever graded the corpus for holes
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-02 (trainer relay #10838, read-only) over the COMPLETE file. POPULATION: all 25,590 consecutive row pairs in datasets-out/market_microstructure/BTCUSDT/5m/v001/data.jsonl -- 25,591 rows parsed, 0 malformed, first_ts 2026-06-04T09:50:00Z, last_ts 2026-09-02T18:35:00Z. 52 transitions are NOT the expected 300s. The 25 largest all fall between 2026-07-02 and 2026-07-15; the worst is 2026-07-05T03:30:00Z -> 06:10:00Z = 9600s, i.e. 31 CONSECUTIVE 5m BARS LOST, with 2026-07-06 carrying two 28-bar gaps. WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE FINDING FROM THE TWO ROWS FILED 2026-08-29 (read as adjacent, not duplicate): BL-20260829-ORDERFLOW-CAPTURE-IS-IRREPLACEABLE-AND-UNMONITORED is about there being no monitor GOING FORWARD, and BL-20260829-TRAINER-DISK-92-PCT-THREATENS-THE-UNBACKFILLABLE-CAPTURE is about the disk. NEITHER says the corpus ALREADY HAS HOLES. It does -- and the holes are the evidence that the failure mode those rows describe is real rather than theoretical: it has happened at least 52 times, silently, and was found only because someone scanned the file by hand. WHY IT MATTERS DOWNSTREAM: these rows are joined as-of by market_features, so a missing bar is not a visible error -- it is a stale or absent microstructure feature on a bar that still trains. Nothing anywhere grades this file for contiguity, so no dataset manifest or model card records which windows are thin. [!] STATE THE LIMIT: only the TOP 25 of the 52 were read, so the dates of the other 27 are UNKNOWN. Do NOT read this as 'no gaps since 2026-07-15' -- that is the unstated-denominator error this repo keeps paying for. What IS separately confirmed is narrower: the 2026-08-29 -> 2026-09-02 window scanned clean, and the 2026-08-31T15:54:39Z VM reboot (kernel 6.8.0-1057-oracl -> -1060, NRestarts=0) cost ZERO bars -- rows run 15:50 -> 15:55 -> 16:00 unbroken. [!] THE FORWARD-LOOKING ALARM SHIPPED IN PR #10843 DOES NOT COVER THIS and must not be read as covering it: it watches FRESHNESS, and says so in its own docstring -- 'a restart that lost an hour leaves a fresh mtime behind it.' Freshness is not contiguity.
items.proposed_fix: A contiguity grader over the capture file (the gap scan in relay #10838 is already the whole algorithm: parse ts, diff consecutive pairs, report every transition != bar_seconds). Run it once to enumerate all 52 with dates, then decide per affected window whether the datasets consuming market_microstructure should exclude or flag it, and record that decision. Whether it then becomes a standing check belongs with the dataset-manifest audit, not with the freshness alarm -- they answer different questions and folding them together would let a fresh-but-holed file read as clean.
items.resolution_criteria: All 52 non-300s transitions are ENUMERATED WITH DATES in a committed artifact (not just the top 25), AND each affected window carries a written disposition -- excluded, flagged, or accepted-as-is with the reason -- in whatever dataset/manifest surface the consumers of market_microstructure actually read. [!] A COUNT IS NOT THE CRITERION: '52 gaps exist' is already established by this row and re-measuring it closes nothing. [!] AND THE FRESHNESS ALARM GOING GREEN CLEARS NOTHING HERE -- it establishes the file is being written, which is a different fact from the file being whole. [!] Deciding the gaps are immaterial to every consumer CLOSES this row too, and must be RECORDED as a decision rather than left looking like an audit still pending.
items.tier: 1 — read-only analysis of a committed/captured artifact; no order path, no live VM mutation, no strategy config.
items.source: MI-81 (OI-20260829 monitoring pass, trainer relay #10838)

items.title: Over-generalising a scoped statement into a standing rule — three instances in one day, one of them an operator's words
items.detail: THE CLASS: a statement true of a SPECIFIC CASE is written into a durable surface as a GENERAL RULE, and then propagates into spawn prompts, checklist rows, work objects and merged PR bodies where the narrowing context is gone. Measured three times on 2026-09-02, by the same session: (1) THE OPERATOR'S OWN WORDS. They refused a session-bound Claude Routine as a Band-Aid for the hourly digest, which needs durable infra (the VM systemd timer, #10859). That was written as 'NO CLAUDE ROUTINE, in any form' into a spawn prompt, MI-86, a work object and #10869's merged body. Operator corrected it at 21:50Z: "that was for that specific thing, not a general rule. I don't want it written into the rules as a general rule." Routines are ALLOWED and are explicitly in scope for manager control over sub-sessions. THE COST IS REAL AND DIRECTIONAL: the prohibition was written into the night manager's prompt, so it was actively barred from the tool most likely to solve its own top item. (2) THE SUB-SESSION 403. A spawn prompt asserted a flat 403 on create_pull_request/add_issue_comment; MEASURED BOTH WAYS THE SAME DAY (MI-75 hit it, MI-77 did not and said so unprompted). An earlier version of the same prompt had asserted the opposite, flatly. Both reached spawn prompts. (3) 'NO SUPERVISE VERB'. True that a RUNNING sub-session cannot be messaged; generalised to 'no inbound channel, control is write-once at spawn' and stated to the operator as measured. An IDLE session CAN be woken via a session-bound Routine (verified: idle/disconnected before the fire, running/connected after, context intact). The real gap is the missing READ, not a missing channel. WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN AN ORDINARY WRONG CLAIM: a general rule is CHEAPER TO OBEY than to re-derive, so it is obeyed without re-checking, and each of the three was written in the SAFE-SOUNDING direction — which is exactly why none of them looked like a risk when written.
items.evidence: (1) grep for 'no Claude Routine' found it in MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json MI-86 and WO-20260902-NIGHT-SHIFT-2026-09-02-03-FINISH.yaml, plus #10869's merged body and the night manager's spawn prompt. Operator correction in-conversation 2026-09-02T21:50Z. (2) MI-75 and MI-77 session records, same day, opposite outcomes on create_pull_request. (3) #10860 body vs the correction in #10866.
items.resolution_criteria: A DURABLE, MECHANICAL CHECK — not a reminder. Candidate shape: any spawn-prompt or register text that states a capability as universally absent ('cannot', 'never works', 'in any form', 'always 403s') must either cite a measurement with a stated population, or be phrased as try-then-fall-back. ⚠️ CORRECTING THE THREE INSTANCES DOES NOT CLOSE THIS — this row's own PR already did that, and the class recurs by construction because the safe-sounding direction always looks free. ⚠️ AND A RULE TELLING CLAUDE 'DON'T OVER-GENERALISE' DOES NOT CLOSE IT EITHER: the operator has ruled that out explicitly — 'no more instructions for Claude, I want actual guards and mechanisms in the repo/vm themselves'. A fourth instance with no detector is the signal that the reminder approach failed again.

items.title: A handoff releases the lease but leaves the outgoing manager's sweep Routines firing, so a stood-down manager keeps being instructed to manage
items.detail: OBSERVED 2026-09-02T22:12:45Z, 35 minutes after a clean handoff. The day manager had spawned a night manager, RELEASED the lease, and stood down. Its hourly sweep Routine then fired anyway and instructed it, verbatim, to 'Heartbeat the lease FIRST', 'merge every green PR', and 'then spawn' — i.e. to resume managing. Two such Routines were bound to that session (cron '26 * * * *' and '10 * * * *'), both enabled, with next_run_at already scheduled. ⚠️ HAD THE SWEEP BEEN FOLLOWED, THE OUTGOING MANAGER WOULD HAVE CLAIMED OR HEARTBEATED THE LEASE BACK OUT FROM UNDER THE INCOMING ONE — producing exactly the two-concurrent-managers state the lease exists to prevent, and which the operator has stated as a requirement ('exactly one management session at a time, never two concurrent'). The lease would not have caught it: the outgoing manager is a LEGITIMATE claimant of a released lease, so the claim would have succeeded. THE GAP IS THAT THE HANDOFF PROCEDURE HAS NO STEP FOR IT. manager_lease.py release does exactly what it says — it releases the lease — and nothing else knows the session has stood down. The sweep Routines are created ad hoc by each manager, live outside the repo (Claude Routines on the account), and are therefore invisible to every in-repo check. A handoff_check.py that graded them would have to make an mcp__* call CI cannot make.
items.evidence: list_triggers filtered to persistent_session_id=session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ returned 2 enabled rows: trig_018Ki4qbWVzsbhG86ecKwBvE (cron '26 * * * *', next_run_at 2026-09-02T22:26:00Z, last_fired 21:26:17Z) and trig_01QoMcM83vtAFcgFdp2WBnEZ (cron '10 * * * *', next_run_at 2026-09-02T23:10:00Z, last_fired 22:12:45Z — the firing that surfaced this). Lease at origin/main read state=released, claimable=True at 22:13Z, i.e. the claim in the sweep's step 1 would have succeeded. Both deleted manually at 22:14Z.
items.resolution_criteria: Standing down is MECHANICAL rather than remembered. Either (a) manager_lease.py release gains a step that disables or deletes the releasing session's own sweep Routines and RECORDS which it found, so the count is auditable; or (b) the sweep prompt's step 1 becomes conditional — read the lease FIRST and STAND DOWN if this session is not the holder and did not release it, rather than heartbeating unconditionally. ⚠️ (b) ALONE IS WEAKER THAN IT LOOKS and must not be treated as sufficient on its own: it is an instruction, and the operator has ruled that shape out ('no more instructions for Claude, I want actual guards and mechanisms'). It also cannot fire if the Routine's prompt is an older version. ⚠️ DELETING THE TWO TRIGGERS DOES NOT CLOSE THIS — that was done on 2026-09-02 and the next manager will create its own. ⚠️ AND 'the Routines die with the session anyway' IS NOT A RESOLUTION: the hazard window is exactly the period when the outgoing session is still ALIVE and handing over, which is when a handoff happens.

items.title: A Tier-1 PR opened through pr-opener and armed for auto-merge never merges: it starts with ZERO checks and auto-merge waits on green forever
items.detail: FILED BY MI-88 as an out-of-scope gap in the route it shipped, not as a defect in that route. MI-88 makes Tier-1 work land itself: declare `.github/pr-landing/{slug}.json` with `landing: "self"`, open the PR not-as-a-draft, and add `.github/pr-automerge-requests/{slug}.txt` so `claude-pr-automerge` enables native auto-merge. Auto-merge merges WHEN THE REQUIRED CHECKS PASS -- which is the safety property, and is also the failure mode here. THE TWO FACTS COMPOSE INTO A SILENT STALL, and neither on its own is new. (a) `pr-opener.yml`'s own header records, MEASURED on PR #10683, that EVERY PR opened through that relay starts with ZERO checks however clean the head is -- the PR is opened by `github-actions[bot]` via `gh pr create` with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub's recursion prevention suppresses the `pull_request` event itself. (b) auto-merge on a PR with zero required-check results never fires. So a session that 403s on `create_pull_request` -- the exact session the relay exists for -- can do everything the landing route asks and still produce a PR that sits forever, looking armed. THAT IS THE SAME OBSERVABLE STATE AS THE PROBLEM MI-88 WAS DISPATCHED TO FIX (a green-looking PR nobody merges), reached by a different mechanism. OBSERVED, NOT MERELY CONSTRUCTED, ON MI-88'S OWN PR #10894 (2026-09-03T06:02Z): opened through the relay after `create_pull_request` returned a write-scope 403, it came back `get_check_runs` total_count 0 with `mergeable_state: blocked` -- NOT `dirty`, so the merge-conflict cause is excluded and this is the relay trap. One ordinary session-credentialed push then attached 4 check runs, confirming the mechanism end to end. n = 1; that PR was a DRAFT and so had not armed auto-merge, meaning the STALL ITSELF (armed + zero checks + never merges) is still inferred from (a)+(b) rather than sighted. Do not report the stall as observed. MITIGATED, NOT FIXED, IN MI-88: `session_registry.py`'s spawn prompt and `.github/pr-landing/README.md` both instruct the caller to push ONE ORDINARY COMMIT AFTER the PR exists to arm CI. That is a human-memory step of exactly the kind this repo keeps recording as insufficient, and it is unenforced -- `pr-landing-guard` cannot see it, because whether checks attached is a GitHub-side fact and CI cannot observe its own absence. THE DURABLE FIX IS NAMED IN `pr-opener.yml`'s OWN HEADER and is deliberately not attempted there or here: a PAT/app token for the PR creation, or a `workflow_run` / `pull_request_target` trigger. Both are larger changes than either PR wanted, and the token half is an operator-originated secret. || [!] 2026-09-06 -- THE STALL IS NOW SIGHTED, and this row explicitly said it was not: it read 'n = 1; that PR was a DRAFT and so had not armed auto-merge, meaning the STALL ITSELF (armed + zero checks + never merges) is still inferred from (a)+(b) rather than sighted. Do not report the stall as observed.' IT IS OBSERVED NOW. PR #11128 (MI-146 follow-up, branch claude/per-merge-ping-reobservation-20260906) was opened 2026-09-06T11:36:12Z by github-actions[bot] through claude-pr-automerge, and read at ~11:38Z as: draft FALSE, auto-merge ENABLED by the relay (its own PR body states it), get_check_runs total_count = 1 -- and that ONE run is `open-and-automerge` ITSELF, so ZERO of the three required contexts (pytest-collect / pytest-run / guards) exist -- with mergeable_state 'blocked', NOT 'dirty', which excludes the merge-conflict cause exactly as the 2026-09-03 reading did. All four conditions of the stall held at once. [!] THE ROW'S SCOPE IS WIDER THAN ITS TITLE: the title and detail name pr-opener, but claude-pr-automerge is a SIBLING RELAY WITH THE SAME ROOT CAUSE -- it also opens the PR as github-actions[bot] with GITHUB_TOKEN, so GitHub's recursion prevention suppresses the `pull_request` `opened` event and guards.yml/pytest never fire. A reader searching for 'pr-opener' will not find this, which is why it is recorded here rather than filed as a fourth near-duplicate row. [!] IT IS WORSE THROUGH THIS RELAY THAN THROUGH pr-opener, because claude-pr-automerge ARMS AUTO-MERGE IN THE SAME ACTION THAT OPENS THE PR -- there is no window in which a caller could notice the PR exists but is unarmed. The PR is born armed and check-less. [!] THE MITIGATION HELD ONLY BECAUSE THE SESSION HAPPENED TO LOOK. This row already calls the 'push one ordinary commit after the PR exists' instruction 'a human-memory step of exactly the kind this repo keeps recording as insufficient', and that is precisely what happened: the CI absence was caught by reading get_check_runs against a KNOWN PRIOR (PR #11124 attached its checks within 43s of creation), not by any alarm. A session that pushed once and stopped would have left an armed, check-less, permanently-unmergeable PR behind it and reported success. guards.yml also deliberately OMITS `ready_for_review` (documented in its own header, 2026-08-31), so un-drafting cannot rescue such a PR either -- the only recovery is a session-credentialed push. NO NEW REMEDY IS PROPOSED HERE: the durable fix named in pr-opener.yml's own header (a PAT/app token for PR creation, or workflow_run / pull_request_target) is unchanged and still operator-gated; what changed is that its motivating failure is no longer hypothetical.
items.resolution_criteria: A PR opened through `pr-opener.yml` is OBSERVED carrying required check runs WITHOUT any subsequent session-credentialed push -- i.e. `pull_request_read method=get_check_runs` returns total_count > 0 on a head commit that was already on the branch when the relay created the PR. Record the PR number and the head sha. [!] READ `get_check_runs`, NEVER `get_status`: `get_status` returns legacy commit statuses and reads total_count 0 on healthy green PRs. [!] A PR whose checks attached AFTER an ordinary push does NOT clear this -- that is the documented workaround working, not the defect being gone, and it is what #10894 already showed. [!] `mergeable_state` must be read alongside: total_count 0 with `dirty` is a merge conflict and is a DIFFERENT fault that must not be counted as either outcome. [!] A green harness clears nothing -- no test can reach GitHub's recursion-prevention behaviour. [!] IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES NOT TO MINT A PAT/app token, this row does NOT clear -- it CHANGES: the relay path is then permanently a two-step (open, then push to arm), which is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one, with the consequence stated -- every Tier-1 PR opened by a 403'd session depends on that second push being remembered, and nothing enforces it.

items.title: AVAXUSDT max_qty=22000 is measured on Bybit's DEMO venue but stored symbol-scoped, so it would silently become a production fallback ceiling if AVAX is ever added to bybit_2
items.detail:
LATENT, NOT LIVE — filed while verifying PR #10780 (MI-90), deliberately not fixed there.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. POPULATION: one venue rejection, bybit_1, AVAXUSDT, 2026-09-02T09:06:11Z, read from the live VM's ict-trader-live.service journal via /api/diag/journalctl: `order_qty:2299510000000 > max_qty:2200000000000 (ErrCode: 10001)`, /1e8 => 22000. The SAME log line names the wire target as api-demo.bybit.com/v5/order/create, and config/accounts.yaml carries `demo: true` on bybit_1. So the 22000 is a real venue-published number, but published by Bybit's DEMO venue.

WHY IT IS NOT A LIVE DEFECT TODAY. POPULATION: all 3 bybit accounts in config/accounts.yaml. AVAXUSDT appears in bybit_1's symbols only. bybit_2 — the sole account with no `demo` flag — lists BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT/XRPUSDT/ADAUSDT; bybit_portfolio (demo: true) likewise. Every AVAX order therefore reaches the same demo venue the ceiling was measured on, so the value is correctly scoped as things stand.

THE TRAP. config/instruments.yaml max_qty is SYMBOL-scoped, not account-scoped. Adding AVAXUSDT to bybit_2 is a one-line config edit that would, with no other change and no warning, promote a demo-measured ceiling into a PRODUCTION fallback ceiling that was never measured on production. It only bites when the live lot-rule lookup misses (prefer_live=True keeps the venue authoritative), which is exactly the rare path the third AVAX recurrence proved is unwatched.

ALSO CORRECTED IN THAT PR, for the record: the recovered diff's own comment claimed a stale ceiling 'can only ever under-size ... never place an illegal order'. That is false — a venue that LOWERS its cap leaves us clamping to a ceiling it no longer honours, and the order is still rejected. A stale ceiling narrows the bug, it does not close it.

RESOLUTION CRITERIA. Either (a) max_qty becomes account/venue-scoped rather than symbol-scoped, or (b) a guard refuses a profile-sourced ceiling whose measuring venue does not match the submitting account's demo/production flag. Documenting the hazard in a YAML comment — which is all MI-90 did — is explicitly NOT sufficient to close this row.
items.source: MI-90 verification of PR #10780 (WO-20260903-AVAX-VENUE-MAX-OWN-THE-ORDER-PATH)
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH observable, in either order: (1) `config/instruments.yaml` AVAXUSDT `max_qty` is no longer reachable as a fallback ceiling for an account whose demo/production flag differs from the venue the value was measured on — demonstrated by a test in which a non-demo bybit account resolving AVAXUSDT on a MISSED live lookup does NOT receive the demo-measured 22000 (it must grade `could_not_look`, or receive a separately-measured production ceiling); and (2) `scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main` is green on the PR carrying that change. Re-reading or re-wording the YAML comment does NOT satisfy this row — the comment already exists and is precisely what this row says is insufficient.

items.opened_by: claude (manager session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ, filing on behalf of a DEAD sub-session — see detail)
items.title: THIRD occurrence: the AVAX venue-max clamp is a silent no-op whenever the live lot-rule lookup misses, because venue_max=None collapses three different answers
items.detail:
⚠️ FILED BY THE MANAGER ON BEHALF OF A SESSION THAT DIED. A sub-session diagnosed this, wrote the fix, cited THIS ID in five files (config/instruments.yaml, src/core/instrument_profile.py, src/units/accounts/{execute,precision,qty_legalize}.py) — and never filed the row. `artifact-validity-guard` caught it: five tracking references resolving to NOTHING, which reads as tracked while being tracked by nobody. The work itself was uncommitted in the manager's container and is preserved, UNREVIEWED, on `claude/mi56-avax-venue-max-recovered` (PR #10780, marked DO NOT MERGE). This row is the RECORD; it is not a claim that that diff is correct.

THE DEFECT, in the dead session's own words from the code it left: `venue_max=None` means three different things and the clamp treated all three as 'no ceiling exists — place it'. `published` — the venue named a ceiling -> CLAMP. `absent` — we read the venue's own lotSizeFilter and it carries no ceiling -> place unmodified. `could_not_look` — nothing that can SPEAK to a ceiling answered (live lookup failed or empty; the static map, which holds step/min only; an InstrumentProfile with no max_qty) -> place, but SAY SO. Only `absent` is evidence that placing unclamped is safe. `could_not_look` is the ABSENCE of evidence, and reading it as `absent` is what made the clamp a silent no-op on the one path already known to reject.

WHY IT IS A RECURRENCE AND NOT A DUPLICATE (filed with similar_ok after reading the candidates): this is the THIRD occurrence of the same live defect. BL-20260810-ICTSCALP-AVAX-QTY-EXCEEDS-VENUE-MAX shipped the clamp and was marked `resolved`; BL-20260821-AVAX-SCALP-SIZES-ABOVE-THE-VENUE-MAXIMUM recorded it rejecting again at ~34,000; on 2026-09-02 `ict_scalp_avax_5m` sent qty 22995.1 against a 22,000 cap EIGHT times. THE CLAMP WAS CORRECT EVERY TIME — that the earlier fix did not hold IS the finding. The mechanism was already filed as BL-20260814-VENUE-MAX-NONE-CANNOT-SAY-WE-COULD-NOT-LOOK (still `kept_open`), which predicted exactly this: a clamp that cannot distinguish those two states will not clamp when the lookup fails. A predicted failure that then happened twice more is worth recording as its own row.

WHY THE TESTS DID NOT CATCH IT: the existing venue-max suite monkeypatches `_resolve_venue_lot_rule` to return `vmax=22_000`, so it exercises the CLAMP and never the RESOLUTION — it passes for the wrong reason, and would keep passing through all three occurrences. The dead session's tests/test_qty_legalize_venue_max_resolution.py is its attempt at that gap and has been reviewed by nobody.

⚠️ THE PROPOSED REMEDY DELIBERATELY DOES NOT REFUSE, and that constraint must survive review: the clamp's whole safety argument is that it cannot alter an order the venue would have accepted. Refusing on an unresolved ceiling would start blocking orders that are legal today (every non-Bybit venue and every static-map symbol resolve to `could_not_look`), which is a far larger blast radius than the bug. It should place — and be LEGIBLE instead of silent, which is what lets a fourth occurrence be seen.
items.resolution_criteria: THE OBSERVABLE CONDITION IS A LOGGED `could_not_look` ON A LIVE ORDER, NOT A MERGE. Specifically, ALL THREE: (1) a real order-path decision on the fleet is observed emitting the resolved venue-max state, with `could_not_look` distinguishable from `absent` on an operator-readable surface — read it off the trader journal or a diag log tail, never off a unit test; (2) a test exists that exercises the RESOLUTION with NO monkeypatch of `_resolve_venue_lot_rule`, and it is shown to FAIL against the pre-fix resolver (a mutation check — a green test proves nothing here, since the current suite is green through all three occurrences); (3) `ict_scalp_avax_5m` places on bybit_1 across a window containing at least one order that previously would have exceeded the cap, with ZERO venue rejections carrying ErrCode 10001 / 'exceeds maximum limit'. ⚠️ MERGING A FIX DOES NOT CLOSE THIS ROW. BL-20260810 was marked `resolved` on exactly that basis and the defect recurred twice; a fourth occurrence closed on a merge would be the same mistake a third time. ⚠️ NOR DOES A QUIET REJECT FEED: zero rejections is only evidence if the leg actually TRADED in the window — an idle strategy and a fixed one produce identical silence, so state the population (orders placed, window, account) alongside the zero.
items.next_action: A live session takes ownership of PR #10780, verifies the three-state resolution against a REAL venue read (not a monkeypatched vmax), confirms could_not_look PLACES rather than refuses, and re-opens it as a normal Tier-2 PR. Do NOT merge #10780 on green CI — its own test suite is the thing under suspicion.

items.summary: scripts/ops/session_registry.py mints registry_key from a SECOND-granular UTC timestamp with no uniqueness check, so two spawns registered inside the same second get the SAME key. Measured 2026-09-03: registering MI-92 and MI-93 back-to-back produced two rows both keyed pending-20260903T070814Z. It is NOT new -- pending-20260902T133456Z is duplicated in the same file from 2026-09-02 and went unnoticed for a day.
items.why_it_matters: A colliding key is not cosmetic. `confirm --registry-key <key> --session-id <id>` matches BY KEY, so with two rows sharing one key it can bind a live session id to the WRONG row -- silently mis-attributing a sub-session to the wrong work object. That is the exact failure SESSIONS.json exists to prevent, arriving through the registry's own key.
items.resolution_criteria: register REFUSES or auto-suffixes on a key that already exists in SESSIONS.json, asserted by a test that registers twice in one second and requires two distinct keys. A finer clock is NOT the fix -- it narrows the window without closing it; the fix is a uniqueness CHECK against the file. Also: confirm must refuse an ambiguous key rather than picking the first match.
items.evidence: docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json @2026-09-03: duplicate registry_key values pending-20260903T070814Z (x2, disambiguated by hand to -b) and pending-20260902T133456Z (x2, left as found).

items.summary: scripts/ops/backlog_append.py is the SANCTIONED appender -- CLAUDE.md tells every session to file through it rather than editing by hand -- and it accepted a row that two REQUIRED CI guards then rejected. Measured 2026-09-03 on BL-20260903-SESSIONS-REGISTRY-KEY-IS-SECOND-GRANULAR-AND-COLLIDES: artifact-validity-guard refused severity 'P2' (not in critical|high|medium|low) and claim-basis-guard refused a missing `status` (not in the declared enum). The append itself reported success.
items.why_it_matters: Filing by the approved route is currently no guarantee of passing CI, so the tool and the guards disagree about what a valid row is. The cost lands at MERGE time on a PR that has already run its full check set -- ~17 minutes of pytest -- when it could be caught at WRITE time for free. It also quietly discourages the sanctioned route: a session that gets reds from backlog_append.py and greens from a hand-edit learns the wrong lesson, which is exactly how the read-append-write reformat defect the appender exists to prevent comes back.
items.resolution_criteria: backlog_append.py REFUSES a row whose `severity` is outside critical|high|medium|low or whose `status` is missing/outside the enum, naming the offending field and the allowed values -- asserted by a test that feeds it a 'P2' severity and a status-less row and requires a non-zero exit. ⚠️ The enum must be IMPORTED from the guards (scripts/ops/check_backlog_criteria.py and scripts/check_claim_basis.py) rather than re-declared, or the two copies drift and this recurs one level down.
items.evidence: CI run 33728581769 (guards, PR #10906): artifact-validity-guard and claim-basis-guard both exited 1 on the single row appended by backlog_append.py minutes earlier, which had reported 'appended ... 1148 item(s)'.
items.found_by: manager session_01Nopk1HcpvWBSEbZxEmALkd, by having its own filed row rejected

items.summary: A sub-session's post_turn_summary.needs_action is written by the session and NEVER cleared by anything. Once the manager satisfies the ask, the session is already idle and cannot rewrite its own summary, so the row reads BLOCKED forever. Measured 2026-09-03: MI-89 (needs_action 'add MI-89 to session_registry.py and update Routine prompt with --write-receipt flag') and MI-90 ('operator decision on Tier-3 merge gate') both still read status_bucket BLOCKED with those exact strings AFTER both asks were fully satisfied -- MI-89's registry row was already on main and the Routine was updated at 07:29Z; MI-90's decision was taken and #10900 was merged at 07:36Z.
items.why_it_matters: This is a desensitized-alarm generator aimed directly at the one mechanism built to catch a manager doing nothing. The Manager Queue Watch (trig_01TWdAvrwFLe6T9XFoNopTeo) was armed at 07:29Z to report every session in BLOCKED with a non-empty needs_action. On its first armed firing it would have reported two sessions as blocked on the manager whose asks were already done -- so the watch cries wolf on day one, and the operator learns to ignore precisely the channel that exists because they had to catch the manager by hand. CLAUDE.md names this class as its own P1: an alarm that fires constantly and is routinely walked past IS the bug.
items.resolution_criteria: The queue watch distinguishes an OPEN ask from a SATISFIED one without the dead session's cooperation, and is shown doing it on a real pair -- one genuinely-blocked session reported, one satisfied-and-archived session NOT reported, in the same run. ⚠️ ARCHIVING IS THE MANAGER'S CURRENT WORKAROUND, NOT THE FIX: it works (archived sessions leave the BLOCKED bucket, verified on all three today) but it requires the manager to remember, which is the same 'remember to do it' remedy that has already failed twice on the sub-session registry. The durable shape is either the manager recording resolution where the watch reads it, or the watch deriving satisfaction from an observable -- the PR merged, the decision answered -- rather than from the session's own stale claim.
items.evidence: Live list_sessions read 2026-09-03T07:47Z: session_01Kyq3Zpgh6DoujFGAMkyJ9o and session_01Q1HYBVoThQdKTWSYQHpm6Y both SESSION_STATUS_IDLE / SESSION_STATUS_BUCKET_BLOCKED carrying satisfied needs_action strings. Both archived by the manager at 07:48Z, after which both read SESSION_STATUS_BUCKET_COMPLETED.

items.title: The board's re-arm rule says 'one ordinary commit, NEVER an empty one' -- measured twice today, an EMPTY commit arms CI fully, and the rule as written pushes sessions to fabricate a filler edit
items.detail: FILED BY MI-92 as an out-of-scope observation, not a defect in the relays. The 2026-09-02 pytest-run retraction posts on #6927 close with a rule repeated in two of them: a github-actions[bot] result commit from pr-opener/board-post re-buries a PR's checks (GITHUB_TOKEN pushes trigger no workflows, so get_check_runs reads total_count 0), and the remedy is 'fix with one ordinary commit, never an empty one'. THE FIRST HALF IS CONFIRMED AND WAS HIT THREE TIMES ON PR #10904 (after the pr-opener results commit, and after each of two board-post results commits). THE SECOND HALF IS CONTRADICTED BY MEASUREMENT. Two `git commit --allow-empty` pushes were used to re-arm, 07769639 and 1709cf85, and both armed CI in full. On the head that followed the empty commit 1709cf85, all five checks ran and completed SUCCESS: repo-inventory (12s), pytest-collect (2.1m), guards (2.3m), audit (6s), and pytest-run started 07:42:46Z / completed 07:59:58Z = 17.2 MINUTES -- inside the 15-17 min band the same board thread established as the genuine full-suite norm (16.7m and 15.6m), and far above the sub-1-minute changed-files short-circuit that thread correctly warns measures nothing. So the empty commit did not merely make checks appear; it produced a real full-suite run that graded the actual PR diff. MECHANISM: an empty commit gets a NEW sha, the push fires pull_request:synchronize, and every guard here grades origin/main...HEAD (three-dot) rather than the head commit's own diff -- so an empty head commit changes nothing about WHAT is graded. WHY THE WORDING MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING PEDANTRY: a session that believes an empty commit will not work must invent a non-empty one, i.e. add a filler edit to a PR that was already validated, which changes the diff under review after its validation run -- the exact shape that cost MI-92 a CI failure today (guards are diff-scoped, and the register/board commits that landed after the guard run made docs-scoped guards newly relevant and caught a stale rendered SESSION-BRIEF). An empty commit is strictly SAFER here because it cannot widen the diff. NOT CLAIMED: that the original author observed an empty commit failing -- no counter-measurement is recorded in those posts, and this row does not assert they were careless, only that the rule as written is not supported by anything on the board and is contradicted by n=2 here.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) someone reproduces an empty commit FAILING to arm checks on a claude/** PR and records the conditions, in which case this row is wrong and the rule should be kept and given its basis; or (b) the guidance is corrected wherever it is repeated -- the 2026-09-02 board posts are immutable history, so the fix is to state it correctly in the durable surface (docs/claude/coordination-board.md or pr-opener.yml's header, which already documents the re-bury trap for itself and not for board-post.yml). NOT sufficient: another session simply using an empty commit successfully without correcting the written rule, since the next session still reads the rule and not the branch history. NOTE the re-bury half of the rule is CONFIRMED and must not be weakened by this correction -- only the 'never an empty one' clause is at issue.

items.summary: MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json has no mechanism forcing it current, so it drifts silently while /status renders it as the manager's authoritative state. Six items created that morning -- MI-88, MI-89, MI-90, MI-92, MI-93, MI-94 -- were ABSENT; the list topped out at MI-91.
