items.title: The work-decision sweep writes its once-only `prompted` marker on a confirmed send but records NO destination, and the only line naming the destination goes to a journal that rolls over in ~30 minutes — so a prompt delivered to the wrong bot is permanently consumed and unattributable
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-03T14:5xZ after the operator said 'I'm still not seeing decisions in the bot'. THE CHANNEL IS NOT DOWN: GET /api/bot/work/decisions returns 8 requests with the new DEC-20260903-SUNSET-DISPOSITION-POLICY present and `not_submitted`, writeGate reads `open`, the sweep runs every 300s and apscheduler logs 'executed successfully', and the ClaudeBot poller heartbeats (pid 440663, prefix wdec). AND THE MARKER SAYS IT WAS SENT: work_decision_prompted carries 'WO-20260903-SUNSET-DISPOSITIONS-OWED::DEC-20260903-SUNSET-DISPOSITION-POLICY' at 2026-09-03T14:05:48.798642Z. Read against the code that is decisive rather than suggestive: run_decision_prompt_sweep writes the marker ONLY after `sent` is truthy (`if not sent: stats['failed'] += 1; continue`), with the comment 'flip only on a confirmed send'. So a send SUCCEEDED and the operator saw nothing. TWO DEFECTS, DIFFERENT FIXES, AND NEITHER IS THE SEND ITSELF. (1) THE MARKER RECORDS NO DESTINATION. Its entry is {prompted_at, object_id, request_id, kind} — there is no field saying WHICH BOT received it. telegram_decisions.answerable_route() can legitimately fall back to the TRADER bot when ClaudeBot is not confirmed polled, and CLAUDE.md documents that fallback as deliberate ('a wrong chat is a noise complaint; holding every decision prompt is an outage'). But the marker is ONCE-ONLY and is pruned only when the request leaves the inbox, so a prompt that went to the wrong chat is PERMANENTLY CONSUMED: the sweep will never re-send it, and nothing on any durable surface says where it went. (2) THE ONE LINE THAT NAMES THE DESTINATION EVAPORATES. The caller DOES log it — telegram_query_bot.py::_sweep_work_decisions emits `logger.info('work-decision prompts: %s', stats)` when anything was prompted, and stats carries `destination` and `poll_state`. But it goes to the systemd journal only. MEASURED: a 1500-line journal pull covers 2026-09-03T14:23:34 -> 14:53:46 — THIRTY MINUTES — so the 14:05:48 send was already unreachable when I looked, 45 minutes later. The evidence needed to diagnose a mis-delivery is gone before anyone can be told there was one.
items.evidence: /api/diag/log_file?name=work_decision_prompted (7 entries, sunset at 14:05:48.798642Z, no destination field on any entry); /api/bot/work/decisions (8 requests, sunset not_submitted, writeGate open); /api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-telegram-bot.service&lines=1500 -> window 14:23:34-14:53:46, ZERO 'work-decision prompts' lines and ZERO telegram_decisions warnings in that window; src/runtime/telegram_decisions.py::run_decision_prompt_sweep marker-write path; src/bot/telegram_query_bot.py::_sweep_work_decisions.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH halves, and say which you fixed. (a) The `prompted` marker entry RECORDS THE DESTINATION (the token variable name and the resolved poll_state, never a token value), so a prompt can be attributed after the fact and a prompt sent to a non-preferred destination can be RE-SENT when routing is fixed rather than being permanently consumed. (b) The sweep's per-run stats land on a DURABLE surface with a diag allowlist entry — the work_digest_receipt.json / prop_fills_staleness_state.json pattern — not only in a journal measured at ~30 minutes of retention. NOT SUFFICIENT: adding more journal logging, which is the surface that already evaporated. NOT SUFFICIENT: making the sweep re-send unconditionally — that would spam a question the operator may already have answered, and the once-only marker exists for a real reason.
items.notes: This is the same family as BL-20260902-PING-DELIVERY-IS-MARKED-ON-A-LOCAL-FILE-WRITE-SO-DELIVERED-IS-NOT-EVIDENCE — a local write standing in for a delivery — but it is NOT a duplicate: that row is about send_ping.enqueue never reading the Telegram response, whereas here the send DOES report success and the gap is that nothing records WHERE it succeeded to. Filed as a recurrence of the class with the distinction stated. ⚠️ The operator's on-demand /decisions command is the working escape hatch and must not be 'fixed' into reading the marker: it deliberately neither reads nor writes it, which is exactly why it could re-surface the questions the sweep had already consumed.
items.resolution: CLOSED ON BOTH HALVES, and BOTH ARE EXERCISED ON THE LIVE FLEET RATHER THAN MERELY DEPLOYED — which is the distinction this repo keeps paying for, so it is the distinction I checked. Read 2026-09-09 via /api/diag/log_file. (a) THE MARKER RECORDS THE DESTINATION. runtime_logs/work_decision_prompted.json, 6,876 bytes, 16 prompted entries, THREE key-shapes: 8 entries carry {destination, poll_state, token_from, chat_from} beside the original four keys; 2 carry those PLUS the full re-delivery block {redelivered_at, redelivered_count, redelivered_from, redelivery_reason}; 6 carry the old four-key shape and are all older than the change (oldest 2026-09-02T10:11:42Z) — i.e. exactly the `unrecorded` state, not a regression. Newest entry, 2026-09-09T01:48:09Z: destination `claude`, poll_state `polled_with_handler`, token_from `TELEGRAM_CLAUDE_BOT_SECRET`, chat_from `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID`. Note the criterion's sharpest requirement is met literally — the field carries the token VARIABLE NAME and never a token value, which matters because this file is on a read surface. AND THE RE-SEND HALF THE CRITERION ASKED FOR IS NOT JUST PRESENT BUT HAS FIRED: two entries carry a completed re-delivery, so 'a prompt sent to a non-preferred destination can be RE-SENT when routing is fixed' is an observed behaviour, not a claim. (b) THE PER-RUN STATS ARE DURABLE. `work_decision_sweep_receipt` is registered in diag.py::_LOG_FILES and reads present:true at 123,480 bytes — so the stats no longer live only in a systemd journal this repo has MEASURED at ~30 minutes retention, which was the whole of the row's (b). WHAT I VERIFIED vs INFERRED: both halves verified by live read. I did NOT verify that a re-delivery reached the operator's phone — that last hop is unobservable from any repo surface and is not what this row asked for (it asked for attribution after the fact, which the destination fields now provide).

items.title: run_guards.py grades a MISSING pytest identically to a failing test, so 'we could not look' is unreadable as anything but 'this is broken'
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-03T17:5xZ on a committed tree during the day manager's wind-down. `scripts/ci/run_guards.py` reported `PASS 46 - FAIL 5 - SKIP 34` and listed five failing guards. TWO were real and were fixed (register-id-guard: 14 new OPEN-PRS rows carried no creation date; stated-population-guard: an added percentage naming no denominator, on a handoff-doc line about how much of that session's context budget had been spent). THE OTHER THREE WERE NOT FAILURES AT ALL -- trainer-capture-watch-guard, artifact-validity-guard and operator-owed-guard each shell out to `python3 -m pytest ...`, and pytest WAS NOT INSTALLED in the session container: every one exited 1 with `No module named pytest`. After `pip install pytest`, the same six test files run `144 passed in 4.05s`. So the guard suite spent three of its five red lines on a condition that says nothing whatever about the code. THIS IS THE REPO'S OWN COLLAPSED-STATES DEFECT, in the tool whose whole job is to tell a session what is wrong: `fail` and `could_not_run` are different facts with opposite remedies (fix the diff vs fix the environment), and folding them makes the suite's headline count uninterpretable -- a session reading `FAIL 5` cannot tell whether it broke five things or zero. IT ALSO POINTS THE WRONG WAY IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: a session that trusts the count wastes a cycle debugging code that is fine, and a session that learns to discount these three stops reading them, which is the desensitized-alarm P1 this repo files against. NOTE THE SIBLING ALREADY ON RECORD, because they are opposite halves of one gap: the day manager's own spawn prompts warn that run_guards can report `FAIL 0` on an INCOMPLETE run -- i.e. silence where it did not look. This row is the same collapse seen from the other side: noise where it did not look.
items.evidence: run_guards.py output (PASS 46 / FAIL 5 / SKIP 34) on branch claude/manager-wind-down-20260903 at commit 52adb643's amended head; `python3 -m pytest <file> -q` -> `/usr/local/bin/python3: No module named pytest` for all three; `pip install pytest` (9.1.1) then the same six files -> 144 passed in 4.05s.
items.resolution_criteria: run_guards.py distinguishes at least three states per guard and reports them separately in its headline: `pass`, `fail` (the command ran and rejected the diff), and `could_not_run` (the command could not execute -- interpreter, module, binary or fixture absent). A `could_not_run` MUST NOT be counted in the FAIL total and MUST NOT be silently folded into SKIP either, because SKIP already means the deliberate, correct 'not relevant to this diff' and conflating the two would hide a broken environment instead of naming it. NOT SUFFICIENT: installing pytest in the container. That fixes today's instance and leaves the grader unable to tell the next one apart. NOT SUFFICIENT EITHER: a green run -- the evidence must be a planted positive, i.e. a guard whose command is made unrunnable on purpose, graded `could_not_run` and excluded from the FAIL count.

items.title: handoff_check's lease check passes ONLY on held_by_me, so the outgoing manager's final act — releasing the lease — makes its own readiness verdict go red
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-03 during the day manager's wind-down, which is the first time this repo has run the protocol end to end. `scripts/ops/handoff_check.py::check_lease` returns PASS only for `held_by_me` and FAIL for every other state, with the message 'A handover of something you do not hold is not a handover.' That reasoning is correct for `expired`, `held_by_other` and `unheld`. IT IS WRONG FOR `released`, AND `released` IS THE STATE A CORRECT HANDOVER ENDS IN. The manager's last act is `manager_lease.py release`, whose own output says 'The next session may claim' and warns that a release nobody can see 'keeps the next manager locked out until the TTL expires' -- so releasing is not merely allowed, it is the thing that makes the successor's claim instant instead of a 90-minute wait. The result is a protocol that can only grade `ready` in a state the manager is supposed to leave, and grades `not_ready` the moment it does the right thing. A MANAGER FOLLOWING THE CHECK LITERALLY WOULD THEREFORE HAND OVER A LEASE IT STILL HOLDS, which is the outcome the check exists to prevent one level up. THIS IS A COLLAPSED STATE IN THE HANDOFF PROTOCOL ITSELF, which is notable because `handoff_check` is otherwise the most careful example of the doctrine in the repo -- its own docstring insists `ready`/`not_ready`/`unknown` are three facts and that `ready` must be unobtainable without a live observation. It simply never separated 'you do not hold it' from 'you held it and handed it back'. ⚠️ AND THE FIX IS NOT `released` -> PASS UNCONDITIONALLY: a lease released by SOMEBODY ELSE says nothing about this manager, so the check must read WHO released it and WHEN, and a release by another session must stay a FAIL.
items.evidence: scripts/ops/handoff_check.py::check_lease -- `if state == 'held_by_me': return PASS` then an unconditional FAIL. Observed live: with the lease held, `handoff-check: [PASS] lease`; after `manager_lease.py release --session-id session_01Nopk1HcpvWBSEbZxEmALkd` the same command grades the same manager FAIL, on a repo where nothing else changed.
items.resolution_criteria: check_lease distinguishes `released_by_me` from the other non-held states and treats it as a PASS for handover readiness, keeping `expired`, `unheld`, `held_by_other` and a release by a DIFFERENT session as FAIL. Evidence must be a planted positive in both directions: a fixture where THIS session released -> PASS, and one where ANOTHER session released -> FAIL. NOT SUFFICIENT: relaxing the check to accept any non-held state, which would let a displaced manager grade itself ready to hand over. NOT SUFFICIENT EITHER: instructing managers to run the check before releasing -- that is a reminder, and this repo has already paid twice for reminders standing in for mechanisms (MI-15).

items.title: check_manager_scope R7 reads the previous heartbeat from `sha~1`, which on a merge commit is the WORKER branch's stale lease blob, so an on-cadence manager grades as silent for hours
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-04 while landing MI-106, on the same PR (#10895) — and it is a SECOND, DIFFERENT blocker on that PR from the authorship defect MI-106 fixes, which is why it is filed rather than folded in. `heartbeat_cadence_gap` does `git show {sha}~1:MANAGER-LEASE.json` to find "this manager's previous heartbeat". `~1` is the FIRST PARENT. On a manager's merge commit into a worker branch the first parent is the WORKER branch's tip, so the "previous heartbeat" it reads is whatever stale lease blob that branch happened to carry — not the manager's previous heartbeat at all. ⚠️ THE GUARD IS NOT WRONG ABOUT ITS INPUTS, IT IS ASKING THE WRONG COMMIT: on 5244dafb (a manager merge of main into #10895, authored 2026-09-03T13:41:06Z) the lease blob says heartbeat_at 09:21:42Z and `5244dafb~1` (= 5504200c, the worker's commit from 06:13Z) says 05:38:03Z, so R7 computes a 223-minute gap against a 90-minute TTL and FAILS. The register says the opposite: reachable from that same merge commit are same-holder heartbeats at 06:35:44Z, 07:46:40Z, 08:09:06Z, 08:32:50Z and 09:21:42Z. The true previous heartbeat is 08:32:50Z — a 49-minute gap, inside the TTL and close to the repo's measured 30-minute median. THE MANAGER WAS ON CADENCE AND THE GUARD SAYS IT WENT SILENT FOR NEARLY FOUR HOURS. ⚠️ THIS IS A FALSE POSITIVE ON THE POSITIVE-DUTY HALF OF THE GUARD, and it fires on exactly the act the manager is supposed to perform — merging. Every manager merge into a branch cut before its recent heartbeats is a candidate. It is adjacent to but NOT the same as MI-105 (R6 going permanently red on a long-lived manager branch via a squash-merged commit that never leaves the range): MI-105 is R6 and range membership, this is R7 and parent traversal.
items.evidence: scripts/ci/check_manager_scope.py::heartbeat_cadence_gap — `rc, prev_blob = _git(root, "show", f"{sha}~1:{LEASE_REL}")`. Reproduced by running main's guard (b95ac61f) over PR #10895's range in a clean worktree: `manager-scope: violation` with `R7 5244dafb (session_01Nopk1HcpvWBSEbZxEmALkd) ... 223 minutes since this manager's previous heartbeat`. Counter-evidence from the register itself: `git log 5244dafb -- docs/claude/work/MANAGER-LEASE.json` yields same-holder heartbeats at 08:32:50Z and 09:21:42Z among others, so the manager heartbeated repeatedly inside the window R7 calls silence. ⚠️ NOT reproducible by checking out the PR head alone: #10895's own tree carries a guard revision that predates R7 (0 occurrences), so the finding appears only under main's guard — which is what CI runs, since actions/checkout resolves a pull_request event to the merge ref.
items.resolution_criteria: R7's "previous heartbeat" is taken from the lease register's history REACHABLE FROM THE COMMIT (all parents), not from `sha~1`: the latest same-holder heartbeat strictly earlier than this commit's own. Evidence must be a plant AND a control in `check_manager_scope.py --self-test`: a manager merge commit whose first parent carries a stale lease blob must grade CLEAN when the register shows on-cadence heartbeats reachable through the second parent, and a genuine >TTL silence must still FAIL — the existing `210min since the previous heartbeat -> violation (R7 only)` case must keep passing unchanged. NOT SUFFICIENT: exempting merge commits from R7 altogether. A manager's merge commit legitimately advances the heartbeat, so exempting it would blind the duty check on the manager's most common commit shape — trading a false positive for a silent false negative, which is the worse of the two.

items.title: three work-digest ceiling tests (and self-test 7) build their control from the LIVE repo, so `pytest-run` — a REQUIRED check — is red on every PR while WIP sits at the ceiling, which is a legal state
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-04 while landing MI-106. ⚠️ THIS IS BLOCKING THE WHOLE QUEUE, NOT ONE PR: `pytest-run` is one of the three required contexts (branch-protection-sync.yml: `["pytest-collect","pytest-run","guards"]`), and it is failing on #10977 (MI-106) AND on #10975 (MI-109, a different session, a completely unrelated diff), both finishing red at 08:38Z. Nothing can self-land while it stays red. ⚠️ THE TESTS ARE WRONG, THE RENDERER IS RIGHT. `tests/test_work_digest.py::test_ceiling_hit_is_loud_and_under_ceiling_is_not` constructs its POSITIVE case (`ceilingHit=True`) but takes its CONTROL straight from `wd.build_digest('HEAD','HEAD')` — the live repo — and asserts 'WIP CEILING HIT' is absent from it. `test_ceiling_is_reported_as_enforced_because_it_is` likewise asserts the under-ceiling string 'IS a gate' appears in the live render. `work_digest.py --self-test` case 7 has the same shape, which is why `test_self_test_passes` fails too (assert 1 == 0). All four assume the repo is UNDER the ceiling. ⚠️ IT IS NOT, AND THAT IS LEGAL: `docs/claude/work/objects/*.yaml` currently holds exactly 8 `in_flight` (WO-20260901-PHASE-E/F/G/H, WO-20260902-MANAGER-PREFLIGHT, WO-20260903-CLOSE-WEDGE-LEDGER-ABSENT, WO-20260903-SUNSET-DISPOSITIONS-OWED, WO-20260904-MANAGER-SCOPE-AUTHORSHIP-SELF-DECLARED) against a ceiling of 8. 8 of 8 is permitted — `check_wip_ceiling.py` refuses the NINTH — so the renderer emitting 'WIP CEILING HIT ... ENFORCED in CI' is correct reporting of a correct state, and the tests break on it. ⚠️ THE TRIGGER IS DATABLE: the 8th object, WO-20260904-MANAGER-SCOPE-AUTHORSHIP-SELF-DECLARED, was added to main by c17b4e7c (#10974) this morning — i.e. the act of spawning the MI-106 session is what reddened the repo's required test check. Confirmed pre-existing and not diff-caused two ways: `python3 scripts/ops/work_digest.py --self-test` prints 'self-test 7 ... FAIL' on an unmodified `origin/main` checkout, and #10975's identical failure shares no files with #10977.
items.evidence: tests/test_work_digest.py:181 `assert "WIP CEILING HIT" not in quiet, "positive control: not-hit stays quiet"` where `quiet = wd.render(wd.build_digest("HEAD", "HEAD"))`; tests/test_work_digest.py:200 `assert "IS a gate" in rendered` over the same live render. Local run on this branch and on unmodified origin/main: 4 failed, 32 passed in tests/test_work_digest.py (3 of the 4 are these; the 4th, test_digest_and_route_publish_the_same_ceiling_facts, additionally needs fastapi and is not separable in this container). CI: #10977 pytest-run failure (run 33852951437), #10975 pytest-run failure (run 33853023636), same window, disjoint diffs.
items.resolution_criteria: Both arms of each ceiling assertion are CONSTRUCTED, so neither can pass or fail for a reason unrelated to the renderer: build the not-hit case the same way the hit case is already built (`inFlight = WIP_CEILING - 1, ceilingHit = False`) instead of reading `build_digest('HEAD','HEAD')`, and do the same in `work_digest.py --self-test` case 7. That is strictly stronger than today's test, not weaker — today's control passes only by accident of repo state. ⚠️ NOT SUFFICIENT: dropping an in_flight object to get under the ceiling. That fixes the symptom by changing the work plan to suit a test, leaves the defect armed for the next time the ceiling is legitimately reached, and the ceiling exists to be reachable. ⚠️ NOT SUFFICIENT EITHER: deleting or xfail-ing the assertions — the ceiling-loudness property is real and worth pinning; it is the CONTROL that is unsound, not the claim.

items.title: a web session's Tier-1 self-land PR is opened as a DRAFT by pr-opener, and claude-pr-automerge refuses to un-draft a PR it did not open — so the PR is green, clean, declared self-land, and cannot land
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-04 on #10993 (claude/decision-answers-guard). All four required checks green (guards, pytest-collect, pytest-run, repo-inventory), `mergeable_state: clean`, `.github/pr-landing/decision-answers-guard.json` declares `tier 1 / landing: self`, and `.github/pr-automerge-requests/` IS armed — and the PR does not land, because `draft: true`.

THE THREE DOORS ARE ALL SHUT AND EACH IS INDIVIDUALLY CORRECT:
(1) `create_pull_request` returns 403 Resource not accessible by integration from a web session, which is why pr-opener exists at all;
(2) pr-opener honours the request file's `draft` field, and CLAUDE.md's harness rule says every Claude PR is opened as a draft — so the natural request carries `draft: true`;
(3) `claude-pr-automerge` refuses to un-draft a PR it did not itself open, BY DESIGN, and pr-opener opened this one. `update_pull_request(draft=false)` also 403s (verified in-session, same boundary as create).

So the intended self-land path assumes claude-pr-automerge OPENED the PR (non-draft). A session that had to use pr-opener — i.e. every web session — lands in a state where the automerge relay will not touch it. This is a TENSION BETWEEN TWO CORRECT RULES, not a broken component: 'Claude PRs are drafts' and 'auto-merge needs a non-draft PR'.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE PR: this is the exact shape `check_pr_landing.py`'s R6 was written for — its own message cites 7 green PRs sitting unmerged on 2026-09-03 — and R6 PASSES here, because the branch IS armed. The guard checks the arming and cannot see the draft flag, so it certifies a PR that still cannot land.

NOT YET ESTABLISHED, and it decides the fix: whether pushing the pr-automerge-request file BEFORE any PR exists would let claude-pr-automerge open it non-draft itself, making pr-opener unnecessary for self-land PRs. That is one ordering experiment, not a code change. Candidate fixes in preference order: (a) a session opening a Tier-1 self-land PR arms the automerge route and does NOT use pr-opener; (b) pr-opener defaults `draft` to false when a matching `landing: "self"` declaration exists; (c) R6 also fails when the PR is a draft, so the guard stops certifying an unlandable PR. (c) is the smallest and closes the certify-what-cannot-land hole regardless of which of (a)/(b) is chosen.

WORKAROUND TODAY: a human clicks 'Ready for review'. One click, but it makes every web-session Tier-1 PR operator-gated, which is precisely what self-land exists to avoid.

FOLLOW-ON, MEASURED 2026-09-04 WHILE APPLYING THE WORKAROUND. Closing and reopening DOES work — #10993 closed via the pr-close relay, and re-arming the route with no open PR made claude-pr-automerge take its create path: #11006 opened `draft: false` with squash auto-merge enabled. So the fix is confirmed, not merely reasoned.

But it carries its own defect: claude-pr-automerge sets the PR TITLE from the HEAD COMMIT SUBJECT at creation time, and never revises it. Any commit pushed afterwards leaves the title describing a commit that is no longer the point of the branch — #11006 is titled `chore(ci): re-arm the automerge route with no open PR`, which is the plumbing commit, while the PR's actual content is a decision guard, a ROADMAP milestone and the demote-and-tune build. ⚠️ THAT TITLE BECOMES THE SQUASH COMMIT ON `main`, so the repo's permanent history mis-labels the change, and `update_pull_request(title=...)` is 403 from a web session like every other PR write. Mitigation that DOES hold: GitHub's squash body is the list of commit messages, so the per-commit detail survives even when the subject line does not. Candidate fix: have claude-pr-automerge refresh the title on a later push, or take the title from the branch's landing declaration rather than from whichever commit happened to be at HEAD when it first ran.
evidence: https://github.com/benbaichmankass/Metis-Insights/pull/10993
.github/workflows/pr-opener.yml
.github/workflows/claude-pr-automerge.yml
scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py
items.resolution_criteria:
TWO OBSERVABLE CONDITIONS, and they are different facts — say which you cleared rather than closing the row on the easier one.

(1) THE DRAFT TRAP. A PR is observed reaching `merged: true` where ALL of: its branch carries a `.github/pr-landing/*.json` with `landing: "self"`; the PR was opened by the `claude-pr-automerge` workflow (NOT pr-opener); and NO human flipped its draft flag — verified by reading the PR's timeline for a `ready_for_review` event and finding none, never by asking whether anyone remembers clicking. Name the PR number. ⚠️ #11006 DOES NOT CLEAR THIS: it only exists because #10993 was closed and reopened by hand, which is the workaround, not the fix. What clears it is the NEXT web session opening a self-land PR and it landing with no rescue.

(2) THE TITLE. A squash commit on `main` from such a PR is observed whose subject describes the CHANGE rather than whichever commit happened to be at HEAD when the relay first ran. Read `git log origin/main` for it. ⚠️ A PR that never received a second push cannot clear this — its title is trivially correct — so the qualifying observation is a PR that was pushed to AFTER the relay opened it.

⚠️ NEITHER IS CLEARED BY A CODE CHANGE ALONE. Editing claude-pr-automerge.yml to refresh the title, or teaching check_pr_landing.py R6 to fail on a draft, is a DEPLOY — this repo's standing distinction — and the row stays open until a real PR is seen going through. ⚠️ AND A DECISION NOT TO FIX IT CLOSES THIS ROW TOO, recorded as a decision with its consequence stated: every web-session Tier-1 PR then needs a human click, which is exactly what self-land exists to avoid.

items.title: an expired manager lease is claimable by anyone and claimed by nobody — nothing reads the expiry and nothing takes over, so a manager that DIES stops management indefinitely
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-04, population = one lease, one expiry: the manager lease expired at 09:38Z and sat expired for 746 minutes, claimable the entire time and claimed by nobody. Nothing restarted management except the operator asking a question at 21:53Z.

THIS IS THE COMPLEMENT OF THE DURABLE WAKE, NOT A DUPLICATE. The wake (WO-20260904-MANAGER-IDLE-IS-UNBOUNDED-AND-NOTHING-WAKES-IT, landed as scripts/ops/manager_wake.py) covers the ALIVE-AND-SILENT manager: it pokes the lease HOLDER, which only works because a session is on the other end to receive it. A manager that has DIED cannot be woken by anything, and manager_wake.py --assess reports that case as `no_manager` and deliberately STOPS THERE. The two mechanisms partition the failure space and neither covers the other's half.

THE LEASE IS NOT A DETECTOR. It EXPIRES correctly -- that half works -- but it is a mutual-exclusion token, not an alarm: nothing READS an expired lease and acts on it. Its own module says takeover is TIME-BASED and deliberately does not require the outgoing manager to do anything, which is right; what is missing is anything that shows up to take the takeover.

THE DESIGN DECISION IS NOT MADE AND MUST NOT BE ASSUMED. Spawning a successor automatically costs duplicated context and the operator has capped concurrent sessions at 3 (MI-64), and it can produce a manager nobody asked for at 04:00Z. Notifying instead is cheaper but puts the operator back in the detection loop. Ask before building.

NOT satisfied by anything that only runs inside a manager session -- that is the same error the wake was built to correct: a dead manager runs nothing. Do NOT build it on a minted credential (operator 2026-09-02: 'no minted tokens, ever') or on a GitHub cron (measured unreliable here: work-digest fired 5x against 24 declared; probes ~4h50m late).

Work object: docs/claude/work/objects/BL-20260904-NOTHING-REAPS-A-DEAD-MANAGER-OR-CLAIMS-AN-EXPIRED-LEASE.yaml
FILED BY THE MI-123 SESSION AS THE ACT OF NOT TAKING THE ITEM -- the wake's own contract requires the reaper be filed separately rather than folded in.
items.resolution_criteria: An expired or released manager lease is OBSERVED being acted on by a mechanism rather than by the operator, within one bounded interval of the expiry, and the observation names WHICH lease expiry and WHAT acted. Either outcome counts: (a) `manager_lease.py status` read from origin/main shows a DIFFERENT holder with a heartbeat inside the TTL, and that successor's session id appears in SESSIONS.json or a commit trailer -- i.e. somebody actually took over; or (b) an operator-facing notification is recorded stating that management has stopped and nothing took over. NOT satisfied by: the lease file merely reading `expired` (that is the condition, not a response to it); a green test or self-test (a harness cannot reach the case); `manager_wake.py --assess` returning `no_manager` (that is this row's evidence, and the wake deliberately does nothing with it); or a manager happening to arrive and claim the lease for unrelated reasons with no mechanism attributable -- record WHICH mechanism acted, or the row stays open.

items.title: check_manager_scope vouches for health-review-backlog only, so a manager routing an item to ml/performance/research backlog can never actually file it
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-04 by the day manager, by being refused. CLAUDE.md states that filing a backlog row is PERMITTED WITH NO CAP -- 'filing is the act of NOT taking the item' -- and check_manager_scope's own docstring agrees, saying health-review-backlog.json is on the surface 'unconditionally' so the manager can file what it notices. But its MANAGER_SURFACE list contains exactly ONE backlog: docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json. The other three (ml-review, performance-review, research-review) are NOT on it, so a manager writing to them fails R2. THE LIVE INSTANCE: MI-108 records an operator direction of 2026-09-03 -- 'we have to continue finding/building a production worthy llm' -- and its own note routes it to the ml-review backlog, correctly, because that file owns AI experiment follow-ups. Measured the same day, ZERO of ml-review-backlog.json's 107 rows carried the subject, so the routing had been recorded and never executed. The manager filed it there and was REFUSED by R2, and backed the write out rather than writing an exception. So the guard's surface and the doc's rule disagree, and the disagreement bites exactly where it is most costly: an item is routed to the right backlog, cannot be filed there by the only session that noticed it, and the alternatives are to file it in the WRONG backlog or not at all. [!] THE GUARD IS NOT OBVIOUSLY WRONG. Its allowlist is DERIVED from what three lease-holding sessions actually committed (263 commits), and an unrecognised path deliberately fails closed -- the same polarity TIER1_SURFACE uses. Widening it to all four backlogs is a judgement about how much authoring a manager should do, which is the very question R6 and the no-cap ruling already argued; it should be decided, not patched. [!] AND THE CHEAP WRONG FIX IS TO FILE EVERYTHING IN health-review. That is how the health backlog reached 1179 rows while ml-review sits at 107, and it defeats the split the three review skills exist to maintain. || SECOND INSTANCE, MEASURED 2026-09-09T23:5xZ by a DIFFERENT manager (session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj), again by being refused, and again not by reading the source first. Five days on, the doc and the guard still disagree and a manager still discovers it the expensive way -- that this row was open the whole time and did not reach the person about to hit it is itself the finding one level up. THE LIVE INSTANCE THIS TIME is not a routing note but an OPERATOR DECISION with nowhere to land: the 2026-09-09 full-system audit put six proposals to the operator, all six were answered, and the carrier row's clears_when requires each disposition to be written INTO THE BACKLOG ROW IT CORRESPONDS TO. Five live in health-review-backlog.json and were annotated; the sixth, F-29's BL-20260909-UNKNOWN-STRATEGY-PRIORITY-NOW-BEATS-45-OF-50-DECLARED-LEGS-AND-THE-CONTENTION-IS-LIVE, lives in performance-review-backlog.json. A one-line append to its notes -- 1 insertion, 1 deletion, no other row touched -- produced 'R2 1710f3aa ... docs/claude/performance-review-backlog.json is not on the manager surface this guard can vouch for'. POSITIVE CONTROL, so this is not an unasserted denominator: the SAME commit appends a row to health-review-backlog.json and R2 does not object. The guard is working exactly as written; the finding is about what was written. THE ANNOTATION WAS DROPPED, NOT FORCED -- no manager-scope-exception was filed, because the cheapest route past this guard must be routing the work to a session, and converting a systematic gap into a per-incident waiver is how the gap survives. The consequence is recorded rather than absorbed: OI-20260909-THE-FULL-SYSTEM-AUDITS-TIER-2-AND-TIER-3-PROPOSALS-ARE-FILED-AND-CARRIED-BY-NOTHING stays open on that one clause. !! WHAT THE SECOND INSTANCE ADDS TO THE CRITERION ABOVE, which was written for a ROUTING note: a disposition is not routable in the same way. A routed item can wait for a session; an operator's recorded answer sitting in the work store while the backlog row still reads as an open proposal is a FALSE RECORD on a money-adjacent surface for as long as it takes. If the surface is widened, the self-test should plant a manager commit touching the PERFORMANCE backlog and assert CLEAN, beside the existing plant asserting a worker path still FAILS -- so the widening cannot quietly become an allow-all.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER check_manager_scope's MANAGER_SURFACE is widened to the other three backlogs with the widening argued in its docstring the way the health-review entry already is, OR CLAUDE.md's 'filing is permitted with no cap' is narrowed in writing to 'the health-review backlog only, and anything else is routed to a session'. What must NOT persist is the current state where the canonical doc says one thing and the guard enforces another, because a manager reading the doc will keep hitting the refusal and the cheapest way out is to mis-file. [!] A row filed in health-review-backlog ABOUT an ml-review subject does not satisfy this and is the failure mode, not the fix. [!] AND SEPARATELY: the MI-108 local-LLM row still needs filing in ml-review-backlog.json by a SESSION -- this row records the blocker, it does not carry the direction.

items.title: send_ping.py and work_digest_now.py queue to a gitignored runtime dir, so a ping queued from a sandbox session never reaches the operator and never satisfies the F6 check
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-04 by the day manager, by running both tools and watching the register NOT move. manager_preflight's f6_digest_owed check reads docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl -- a COMMITTED register -- and graded FAIL at 10 autonomous actions against a threshold of 3, saying 'F6 is the condition on which autonomy was granted'. The manager queued a rolled-up digest with scripts/send_ping.py: the row count of docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl stayed at 79 and git status showed the file unmodified. It had written to runtime_logs/pending_claude_pings/994780836961-normal.json instead. Repeated with scripts/ops/work_digest_now.py --force: same result, row count still 80, queued to runtime_logs/pending_claude_pings/122973854114-normal.json. SPLIT MEASURED ACROSS THE FOUR WRITERS: scripts/ops/work_digest.py (workflow-invoked) and scripts/ops/work_phase_ping.py write to docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl and are therefore committable and visible; scripts/send_ping.py (PENDING_CLAUDE_PINGS_DIR = _RUNTIME_LOGS / 'pending_claude_pings') and work_digest_now.py write to runtime_logs/, which .gitignore line 29 excludes. [!] THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT A FAILED CHECK, IT IS A LOST PING. On the VM that directory is drained by the bot. In a SANDBOX session there is no bot and the container is reclaimed, so the file is written, the tool reports 'queued -- the bot drains within ~5s', and nothing is ever sent. The tool reports success for a delivery that cannot happen. That is the same shape as BL-20260902-PING-DELIVERY-IS-MARKED-ON-A-LOCAL-FILE-WRITE-SO-DELIVERED-IS-NOT-EVIDENCE, one hop earlier: that row is about delivery being marked on a write; this is about the write going somewhere unreachable. [!] AND IT MAKES F6 UNDISCHARGEABLE ON DEMAND. A manager told by its own preflight to 'queue ONE ROLLED-UP DIGEST' has two obvious tools and both are the wrong ones; only work_phase_ping.py (which fires on lifecycle diffs, not on a manager's action count) reaches the graded register. So the check can be red with no available action that turns it green -- which is how a condition-of-autonomy becomes noise.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER the two on-demand tools write to docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl like their siblings (and say, as work_phase_ping.py already does, that an uncommitted row is a ping that never happened), OR they detect that runtime_logs/ is gitignored-and-undrained in this environment and REFUSE with a message naming the tool that does work, rather than reporting 'queued'. [!] Reporting 'queued -- the bot drains within ~5s' when no bot exists is the specific behaviour to remove; a tool may not claim a delivery path it cannot see. [!] NOT SUFFICIENT: documenting which tool to use. Two tools that look right and silently do nothing is the defect, and a doc does not stop the next session reaching for the obvious one.

items.resolution_criteria: CLAUDE.md's citation of the MANAGER-CHECKLIST-GOES-STALE row carries the -AND-STATUS-REPORTS-IT-AS-CURRENT suffix, verified by grepping -o for the id prefix followed by [A-Z-]* in CLAUDE.md and seeing the suffixed form and no bare one. ⚠️ A plain grep -l is NOT sufficient evidence and must not be used to close this: the truncated id is a PREFIX of the correct one, so grep -l matches a corrected file exactly as it matches a broken one — that probe reported 4/4 wrong when the truth was 1/4, and it has no negative control by construction. SECOND, SEPARABLE HALF, and say which you closed: scripts/ops/check_backlog_refs.py runs an UNGATED whole-tree pass in run_guards.py, not only the diff-scoped one — which requires first MEASURING the whole-tree residue and finding it small, since an ungated step over an undrained tree fails every PR on day one (the diagnostic-provenance-guard sequence, 2026-09-02). If the residue turns out to be large, record the count and leave the ungated step unbuilt rather than landing something that must immediately be excepted.
items.title: CLAUDE.md cites the MANAGER-CHECKLIST-GOES-STALE row WITHOUT its -AND-STATUS-REPORTS-IT-AS-CURRENT suffix, so the id it names resolves to nothing
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-04T23:45Z. The filed row is BL-20260903-MANAGER-CHECKLIST-GOES-STALE-SILENTLY-AND-STATUS-REPORTS-IT-AS-CURRENT. CLAUDE.md cites that id minus its -AND-STATUS-REPORTS-IT-AS-CURRENT suffix. (This row deliberately DESCRIBES the truncated form rather than reproducing the token: check_backlog_refs cannot distinguish 'I am citing this dead id AS the defect' from 'I am tracked by this id', so writing it out makes a row about a dead reference itself a dead reference. That limitation is part of the finding.) STATE THE POPULATION: four files carry the string; measured per file by grepping -o for the id prefix followed by [A-Z-]* and comparing whether the match carries the -AND-STATUS-REPORTS-IT-AS-CURRENT suffix (the literal probe string is NOT reproduced here for the reason just given), exactly ONE is truncated (CLAUDE.md) and THREE are correct (scripts/ops/manager_wake.py, scripts/ci/run_guards.py, scripts/ci/check_manager_scope.py). ⚠️ THIS ROW ALMOST WENT OUT CLAIMING ALL FOUR WERE WRONG. A plain `grep -l` for the short id matches every file carrying the LONG id too, because the short id is its prefix — so the obvious probe cannot distinguish the defect from the correct case, and reports 4/4. The finding is 1/4. A prefix-matching probe has no negative control by construction; the -o form is what separated them. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: `artifact-validity-guard` (scripts/ops/check_backlog_refs.py) is DIFF-SCOPED, so it never sees this pre-existing site — it caught the same truncation in a NEW file this session and passed the moment that one was corrected, while CLAUDE.md's copy stayed. CLAUDE.md is the only surface that reaches a session before it acts, so an unresolvable tracking id there reads as tracked while being tracked by nobody — the exact crack the 2026-07-30 operator directive names. RECURRENCE: this is at least the third truncated-BL-id instance in this repo, and the second TONIGHT — the manager hit one earlier in the same session. A one-character-class typo class that keeps recurring is a candidate for an ungated whole-tree `--all` step on check_backlog_refs.py, the way diagnostic-provenance-guard was un-grandfathered on 2026-09-02 once its residue was drained to zero. Measure the whole-tree residue FIRST; an ungated step over an undrained tree fails every PR on day one. || ⚠️ SECOND INSTANCE, AND IT IS EVIDENCE FOR THIS ROW'S SECOND HALF RATHER THAN A NEW ROW (measured 2026-09-09T03:50Z by the manager; a separate row was drafted and DROPPED as a duplicate once this one was read). `scripts/ops/check_backlog_refs.py --all` reports exactly one dangling reference repo-wide: docs/research/POST-VALUE-PIVOT-WORKPLAN-2026-07-27.md line 26 declares an `Anchor` id, described as operator-endorsed, in the MB- namespace dated 2026-07-27 and named for that workplan. THE TOKEN IS DELIBERATELY NOT REPRODUCED HERE, for exactly the reason this row already gives: writing it out would make a row ABOUT a dead reference into a dead reference. That trap fired twice on the manager the same night before this row was found. || ⚠️ IT DIFFERS FROM THE ORIGINAL INSTANCE IN THE REPAIR, WHICH IS WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING: the CLAUDE.md case is a TRUNCATION — the row exists and the citation is short, so the fix is to expand it. This one was NEVER FILED. Measured: MB- is a live prefix (105 rows carry it, 104 in ml-review-backlog.json), and a search across all four backlogs for VALUE / PIVOT / 20260727 returns NO near-match, so it is not a typo for an existing row. An operator-endorsed workplan has therefore read as anchored to a tracking row that has never existed, for six weeks. Which repair is right — file the missing row, or correct the doc's anchor — depends on what that workplan was meant to be tracked BY, and the doc calls the anchor operator-endorsed, so it is not a manager's edit to make. || ⚠️ THIS IS WHAT THE UNGATED WHOLE-TREE PASS BUYS, STATED AS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT: the diff-scoped guard passed on every PR that touched the repo for six weeks and could not see this, because it only grades references a change INTRODUCES. It surfaced the moment `--all` was run by hand. One dangling ref repo-wide is a small number — that is the honest reading, not a crisis — but nobody knew it was one rather than fifty until somebody looked.
items.fix: Correct the citation in CLAUDE.md to the full id. Then measure the whole-tree residue with check_backlog_refs.py over every tracked file (not the diff) and, if it is small, add the ungated `--all` step so a truncated id cannot be reintroduced in a file the diff does not touch.
items.note: Filed rather than fixed BY DESIGN: CLAUDE.md's canonical prose outside the generated SESSION-BRIEF block is NOT the manager surface (check_manager_scope R2), and filing is the act of not taking the item. It is uncapped, deliberately.

items.title: sunset_pass.py collapses 'absent from the performance capture' into 'closed zero', manufacturing retire_candidate verdicts
items.detail: scripts/ops/sunset_pass.py:288 does `life = lifetime.get(name, 0 if lifetime_state == "read" else None)`, defended by a comment asserting '/api/bot/performance lists every strategy with any closed trade, so under `read` an absent leg genuinely closed ZERO -- a real measurement'. THAT ASSERTION IS FALSE. src/web/api/routers/performance.py:324-326 filters `status='closed' AND COALESCE(is_backtest,0)=0 AND pnl IS NOT NULL`, so the capture lists every strategy with a PNL-BEARING close, not with any close. A leg whose every close carries pnl NULL is absent, defaults to 0, and is filed `retire_candidate` / basis `never_closed_lifetime` with the note 'has never closed a single trade in its life'. MEASURED 2026-09-05 against the live capture (/api/bot/performance?window=all): 52 enabled legs, 46 in the capture, 11 ABSENT and silently defaulted to 0. Of the 10 candidates in comms/sunset/2026-09-01, NINE are absent. FIVE of them -- gdx_pullback_1d (2 closes 2026-08-05), gld_pullback_1d (3, 2026-07-07 + 2026-08-05), iaum_pullback_1d (1, 2026-08-05), scha_trend_long_1d (1, 2026-08-24), spy_trend_long_1d (1, 2026-08-18) -- had closed trades in trade_journal.db::trades BEFORE the 2026-09-01T23:13:46Z packet was generated, so the packet's stated basis is false for half its candidates. POSITIVE CONTROL that makes it conclusive: iwm_trend_long_1d, which the packet passed as `watch`, has 7 closed trades of which 4 carry real pnl and 3 carry pnl=None, ALL via the same exchange_flat_reconciled exit path -- so a NULL pnl is not intrinsic to that path, and visibility to the gate turns on whether any one close happened to get pnl stamped. The five candidates are not different in kind from iwm, only in luck. NOTE the upstream cause is already filed and this row does not restate it: BL-20260807-BULK-RECONCILER-CLOSE-NO-EXIT-NO-PNL records 7 rows bulk-closed on 2026-08-05 with null exitPrice and null realizedPnl -- the same date as three of the five. This row is about the SUNSET PASS reading that absence as a measurement, not about why the pnl is null. This is the `docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md` collapsed-states class: sunset_pass.py already implements read/not_read/unreadable correctly at the CAPTURE level; the missing state is PER-LEG.
items.fix: Give the per-leg lifetime read its own three states rather than defaulting: `closed_n` (present in the capture), `no_pnl_bearing_close` (absent from the capture but present in `trades`), and `absent` (in neither). Only the first may ever produce a `never_closed_lifetime` basis. The second is a DIFFERENT finding -- a leg that trades and cannot be graded -- and must not be filed as a retirement candidate. Cheapest correct source for the distinction is a direct COUNT over trades.status='closed' per strategy, which does not depend on pnl at all.
items.resolution_criteria: sunset_pass.py no longer writes a 0 for a leg absent from the lifetime capture: the per-leg read is three-valued and a leg absent from /api/bot/performance but holding at least one row in trades with status='closed' grades as its own basis, NOT `never_closed_lifetime`. Verified by RE-RUNNING the pass against the live capture and confirming that gdx_pullback_1d, gld_pullback_1d, iaum_pullback_1d, scha_trend_long_1d and spy_trend_long_1d no longer carry basis `never_closed_lifetime`, AND that a leg with genuinely zero closed rows still does. NOT SUFFICIENT: a unit test over a synthetic capture -- the defect is a false assumption about a REAL route's filter, and a fixture asserts whatever its author believed. NOT SUFFICIENT: regenerating the packet and observing fewer candidates, which a change in live trading would also produce. NOT SUFFICIENT: fixing the pnl-null writers (BL-20260807) -- that would repopulate the capture and MASK this defect while leaving the collapse in place for the next leg it happens to.
items.note: Found while diagnosing WO-20260905-NEVER-FIRING-LEGS-NEED-A-REPAIR-DIAGNOSIS-NOT-A-RETIREMENT. Full evidence + per-leg table: docs/claude/diagnoses/MI-124-never-firing-legs-diagnosis.md. The operator has twice refused to retire anything; this row is why that refusal was correct -- retiring on this packet's basis would have deleted five legs that were trading.

items.title: The sunset pass files an execution:shadow leg as a retirement candidate for not producing live trades
items.detail: turtle_soup is declared `execution: shadow` in config/strategies.yaml. Per CLAUDE.md's two-execution-gates contract, a `shadow` leg runs and logs order packages everywhere but NEVER sends a live order -- producing no live trades is that gate WORKING EXACTLY AS DECLARED, not evidence against the leg. comms/sunset/2026-09-01 nonetheless files it `retire_candidate`, and its basis (`unrouted`) mentions only that it is routed to no account; nothing in the packet records that it is also shadow. grade_strategies() in scripts/ops/sunset_pass.py reads routing and lifetime closes and never reads the `execution:` field at all, so a deliberately-shadowed research leg is graded on a criterion it is declared exempt from. MEASURED 2026-09-05: turtle_soup is the only `execution: shadow` leg among the 10 candidates, so the current blast radius is one row -- but the gap is structural and any future leg demoted to shadow will be filed the same way. THAT MATTERS NOW BECAUSE docs/design/strategy-demote-and-tune-DESIGN.md makes demote-to-shadow the SANCTIONED remedy: the agreed flow would move a leg to shadow and the sunset pass would then propose retiring it for being shadow, which is the two mechanisms working against each other.
items.fix: grade_strategies() should read `execution:` alongside routing, and a `shadow` leg should grade as its own state (e.g. `not_assessed` / basis `shadow_by_declaration`) rather than `retire_candidate` -- the same shape as the existing `prop_routed` carve-out, which already says 'A zero here is OUR blindness, not the leg's silence'. Shadow is the same kind of blindness and deserves the same carve-out.
items.resolution_criteria: scripts/ops/sunset_pass.py reads config/strategies.yaml::execution and no leg with `execution: shadow` can receive verdict `retire_candidate`; verified by regenerating the pass and confirming turtle_soup grades on a shadow-specific basis that NAMES the shadow declaration, plus a self-check case asserting a shadow leg with zero closes is not a candidate while a LIVE leg with zero closes still is. NOT SUFFICIENT: routing turtle_soup to an account, which changes the leg rather than the grader and leaves the next demoted-to-shadow leg exposed. NOT SUFFICIENT: excluding turtle_soup by name.

items.title: claude-pr-automerge opens the PR before pr-opener can, so a 403'd session's Tier-1 PR keeps a boilerplate description it cannot edit
items.detail: The Tier-1 protocol requires BOTH `.github/pr-landing/<slug>.json` and `.github/pr-automerge-requests/<slug>.txt`. `claude-pr-automerge.yml` fires on any push to a `claude/**` branch touching the automerge-request path and FINDS-OR-OPENS the PR itself. So the moment a session pushes the required Tier-1 pair, that workflow opens the PR with `title = head-commit subject` and a two-line boilerplate body. `pr-opener.yml`, pushed later with the real title and body, then exits with `FAILED: a pull request for branch ... already exists`, and the session cannot repair it: `update_pull_request` 403s for exactly the same reason it needed the relay in the first place. MEASURED 2026-09-05 on PR #11019 (MI-124): title read 'MI-124: file machinery findings, cross-ref existing rows, tier-1 landing' -- an intermediate commit subject, not the change -- and the body carried none of the findings, the population statements, or the guard results. The `board-post.yml` relay cannot substitute because its issue number is hardcoded to #6927 by design. ⚠️ THIS IS NOT THE DRAFT CLUSTER AND MUST NOT BE FOLDED INTO IT. BL-20260903-PR-OPENER-DRAFT-FALSE-IS-UNREACHABLE-SO-TIER-1-CAN-NEVER-SELF-LAND-THROUGH-THE-RELAY and BL-20260904-A-TIER-1-SELF-LAND-PR-OPENED-BY-PR-OPENER-IS-A-DRAFT-AND-CAN-NEVER-SELF-LAND-FROM-A-WEB-SESSION are about pr-opener's `jq '.draft // true'` bug on a PR pr-opener DID open. Here pr-opener opened nothing, and the PR is correctly NOT a draft -- the race happens to dodge that defect while costing the description instead. ⚠️ AND IT IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A SEQUENCING MISTAKE BY ONE SESSION: pushing the landing pair is what the Tier-1 protocol MANDATES, so any session that follows the protocol and also needs pr-opener loses this race. Ordering the two pushes by hand would work, and nothing documents that.
items.fix: Cheapest correct fix: have `claude-pr-automerge.yml`, when it is about to OPEN (not merely find) a PR, first look for an unconsumed `automation/pr-requests/<name>.json` on the branch and use its title/body if present. That keeps one opener while letting the session supply the description. Alternative: teach `pr-opener.yml` to PATCH the title/body of an existing PR for its head branch instead of exiting FAILED -- it holds the GITHUB_TOKEN that can do it, and 'already exists' is currently treated as a terminal error when it is a recoverable one. Interim, documentable today: instruct sessions to push the pr-request file FIRST and the automerge-request file in a LATER push.
items.resolution_criteria: A session that pushes the Tier-1 landing pair and a pr-request file in the SAME push ends with a PR whose title and body are the ones it supplied. Verified by opening one such PR end-to-end from a session whose `update_pull_request` 403s, and reading the PR back with `pull_request_read` method `get` to confirm the title is the supplied title and the body contains the supplied text. NOT SUFFICIENT: a session hand-ordering its two pushes -- that is the documented workaround, not the fix, and it leaves the next session that follows the protocol literally exposed. NOT SUFFICIENT: the PR merging -- this is about the description a reviewer reads, not about landing. NOT SUFFICIENT: fixing pr-opener's draft flag (the two BL-20260903/BL-20260904 rows); that is a different defect on a different code path and closing it changes nothing here.
items.note: Hit while landing MI-124. PR #11019 is the measured instance; its real description is in the PR-body section of docs/claude/diagnoses/MI-124-never-firing-legs-diagnosis.md and in the board START comment on #6927.

items.title: sunset_pass's own --self-test PINNED the MI-126 defect as correct behaviour, which is why it survived review
items.detail: MI-126 repaired `scripts/ops/sunset_pass.py:288`, where `lifetime.get(name, 0 if lifetime_state == 'read' else None)` turned a leg's ABSENCE from the /api/bot/performance capture into a measured zero and thereby into a `retire_candidate`. What is filed here is not that defect (already `BL-20260905-SUNSET-PASS-DEFAULTS-AN-ABSENT-LEG-TO-ZERO-CLOSES-AND-CALLS-IT-NEVER-TRADED`) but the reason it was not caught: the module's OWN `--self-test` asserted it. The check `('a leg with zero lifetime closes is a retire_candidate', r['silent']['verdict'] == 'retire_candidate' and r['silent']['basis'] == 'never_closed_lifetime')` passed its `silent` leg a lifetime map of {'young': 3, 'graded': 44} — so `silent` was ABSENT from the capture, not measured at zero, and the check was green precisely BECAUSE the default manufactured a 0. A reader auditing the default found a passing test named as if it had verified it. The prose comment defending the default and the test asserting it agreed with each other and both were wrong; the field (performance.py's `AND t.pnl IS NOT NULL`) was the only thing that disagreed. This is the 'field beats comment' rule with a test standing in for the comment, and it is a harder case because a green test reads as evidence. Fixed in the same change: `silent` is now IN the capture at 0 (the genuinely measured zero, still a candidate) and an `absent` leg was added beside it asserting the opposite. Population of the mistake: 1 check in 1 module, found by reading the default rather than by any detector.
items.fix: Done for this instance. The open question is the CLASS: nothing detects a self-test whose fixture makes a defended default fire. Cheapest honest next step is a read-through of the other `--self-test` blocks under `scripts/ops/` and `scripts/ci/`, asking of each check whether its fixture exercises the branch the check NAMES.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) a reviewer has read every `--self-test` block under `scripts/ops/` and `scripts/ci/` and RECORDED, per module, whether any check's fixture makes a defaulted/absent value stand in for a measured one — naming the modules read, so the negative has a denominator; or (b) an operator/reviewer decision that this is a one-off and no sweep is warranted, RECORDED as a decision. NOT sufficient: that MI-126's own two checks now pass (that is this instance, already fixed), or that the guard suite is green — no guard looks at this.
items.note: Filed with similar_ok: backlog_search surfaced only lexical overlap (top hit 0.60, BL-20260822-EXIT-REASON-FROZEN-WHEN-PRICE-ARRIVES-LATE) and none of the 8 candidates concerns a test asserting a defect. Deliberately NOT filed as a recurrence of the MI-126 defect row — that row is the false positive; this is why review missed it.

items.title: After MI-126 the sunset pass no longer manufactures a zero — it now has NO lifetime measurement at all for 11 of 52 enabled legs, because /api/bot/performance is not an 'ever closed' oracle
items.detail: MI-126 stopped `scripts/ops/sunset_pass.py` defaulting an absent leg to 0 closes; such a leg is now `leg_lifetime_state: not_observed` with `lifetime_closed_trades: None` and is never proposed for retirement on that absence. That is correct, and it EXPOSES rather than creates the remaining gap: the pass's only lifetime source is `/api/bot/performance?window=all`, whose SQL carries `AND t.pnl IS NOT NULL` (src/web/api/routers/performance.py:324-326), so it lists strategies with a pnl-BEARING close and cannot answer 'did this leg ever close a trade'. Population, measured 2026-09-05 against the live route: 52 enabled legs graded, 46 present, 11 absent — so 11 of 52 (21.2%) now carry no lifetime measurement in either direction. The honest source is a direct count in `trade_journal.db::trades`. Measured there the same day via /api/bot/db/table/trades (filter_state 'applied' asserted on every response; lifetime, non-backtest; positive controls iwm_trend_long_1d 7 closed/4 with pnl, qqq_trend_long_1d 2/2, trend_donchian_sol 1/1 — all non-zero, so the zeros below are a measurement): gdx_pullback_1d 2 closed / 0 with pnl, gld_pullback_1d 3/0, iaum_pullback_1d 1/0, scha_trend_long_1d 1/0, spy_trend_long_1d 1/0, and mes_trend_long_1d, splg_trend_long_1d, tqqq_trend_long_1d, turtle_soup at 0 closes. So FIVE of the eleven demonstrably have closed trades the pass cannot see, and four genuinely have none — two opposite facts that the pass currently renders identically as `not_observed`. NOTE the route's filter is CORRECT for a performance view and must not be changed to suit this consumer; the defect is the absence of a second, count-only source. Same blindness affects the M7 gate: a leg invisible to the performance capture is ungradeable everywhere, not only here (MI-124 section 6.3).
items.fix: Give the sunset pass a count-only lifetime source that does NOT filter on pnl — a direct `SELECT count(*) FROM trades WHERE strategy_name = ? AND status LIKE 'closed%' AND COALESCE(is_backtest,0)=0`, or a small read route exposing it — and let `leg_lifetime_state` distinguish 'measured: never closed' from 'we could not look'. Do NOT touch /api/bot/performance's SQL. Note this is upstream-adjacent to the pnl-stamping defects (BL-20260807-BULK-RECONCILER-CLOSE-NO-EXIT-NO-PNL, BL-20260825-EXIT-PROVENANCE-IS-STRUCTURED-BY-EXIT-PATH-SIX-PATHS-AT-ZERO): fixing those would shrink the absent set but would NOT make the performance route a correct 'ever closed' oracle, so this row does not close on them.
items.resolution_criteria: A sunset pass run whose committed comms/sunset/<date>/INDEX.json shows the count of legs it could not measure lifetime closes for DROP from 11, with the remaining `not_observed` legs distinguishable from legs MEASURED at zero — i.e. a leg with closed trades carrying pnl NULL must grade differently from a leg with no closed trades at all. Read it from the committed artifact, not from a test. EXPLICITLY NOT SUFFICIENT: (a) the pnl-stamping defects being fixed so fewer legs happen to be absent — that shrinks the symptom and leaves the pass still unable to answer the question; (b) `retire_candidate` being low or zero, which is this row's starting state and says nothing about coverage; (c) a green test. ALTERNATIVELY this row closes on a RECORDED decision that the pass should not grade lifetime closes at all and should rely on `persistently_silent` alone — a legitimate answer that must be written down as a decision rather than left looking like work in flight.
items.note: Filed with similar_ok. The nearest existing row is BL-20260905-SUNSET-PASS-DEFAULTS-AN-ABSENT-LEG-TO-ZERO-CLOSES-AND-CALLS-IT-NEVER-TRADED (overlap 0.54) and this is NOT that row: that one is the false-positive defect, fixed by MI-126. This is the COVERAGE gap the fix leaves behind — the pass now declines to guess, and still cannot measure. Filing it separately so the fix is not mistaken for closing the question.

items.title: _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced bounds its scan by created_at (the OPEN) while pricing a CLOSE, so any position held longer than 14 days is never scanned, never anchored and never DECLARED — it lands a silent pnl NULL
items.detail: src/runtime/order_monitor.py:10533 ends the sweep's scan query with `AND datetime(created_at) >= datetime('now', '-14 days')`. created_at is when the position was OPENED; the value the sweep exists to recover is a property of the CLOSE. A position held longer than the window is ALREADY outside it at the moment it closes and stays outside forever, so the row is never selected. It therefore also never reaches the no_anchor branch (order_monitor.py:10637-10655) that stamps `pnl_source: unmeasured` — the honest terminal state INV-2 accepts and INV-2b counts. The result is a SILENT null with no provenance key at all, which src/runtime/provenance.py exists specifically to prevent ('absence of a provenance record is not evidence of measurement'). POPULATION: trade_journal.db::trades, all 5,493 rows fetched complete by pagination, read 2026-09-05 against trader git_sha 5eb59917; non-backtest status='closed', intent_reduce legs excluded, hold computable = 1,373 rows. pnl-NULL share by hold bucket: <1d 22/1103 (2.0%), 1-7d 3/196 (1.5%), 7-14d 12/47 (25.5%), >14d 20/22 (90.9%). Of the 57 pnl-NULL rows in that population the declared/silent split is: held<=14d 15 declared / 22 silent; held>14d 0 declared / 20 silent. ZERO OF 20 — no row held longer than the window has ever been declared. The only two >14d rows carrying a pnl were filled by OTHER paths (pairs_half_open_cleanup wrote its own exit_price; bybit_closed_pnl is broker truth), so this sweep has filled exactly zero long-held rows ever. Blast radius is wider than MI-124's five legs: 14 distinct strategies across 5 accounts (alpaca_paper, alpaca_portfolio, bybit_1, bybit_portfolio, ib_paper) and 5 exit reasons. Every _1d trend/pullback leg is long-horizon by design, so the defect selects for exactly those legs — which is why it read as a property of the legs rather than of the window. It is upstream of the sunset pass and of /api/bot/performance (AND t.pnl IS NOT NULL), so an affected leg is ungradeable everywhere, not just there. NOT A COIN FLIP: MI-124 read these as luck ('not different in kind from iwm, only in luck'). It is deterministic — iwm 2771 (held 0.0d) priced, iwm 2772 (held 15.0d) did not, same leg and same exit path. WHY IT SURVIVED: tests/test_sweep_no_mark_fabrication.py already documents this window as a 'TIME BOMB, DEFUSED 2026-08-13' that reddened main twice by ageing a FIXTURE out of it — read both times as a fixture-clock problem; nobody asked what the same predicate does to a production row that is long-lived by design. REPRODUCTION (landed): tests/test_local_pnl_sweep_window_is_open_keyed.py — two rows identical except hold duration, both closed 2 days ago, with a WORKING anchor monkeypatched in as a positive control; the 38-day row yields scanned==1, pnl NULL, no pnl_source key, declared_unmeasured==0.
items.why_it_matters: A silent NULL is invisible to every consumer of pnl and is indistinguishable from a row nobody looked at — because that is what it is. It is what made five legs look like they had never traded (MI-124) and what manufactured retire_candidate verdicts from an absence (MI-126). It biases the journal specifically against long-horizon legs, i.e. against exactly the strategies whose performance takes longest to establish.
items.next_action: Apply the one-liner: `AND datetime(COALESCE(closed_at, created_at)) >= datetime('now', '-14 days')`. COALESCE is load-bearing — the sweep also selects status='orphaned' rows that may have no closed_at, and those must keep open-keyed behaviour rather than becoming unbounded. ⚠️ ONE EXISTING TEST MUST MOVE WITH IT: tests/test_sweep_no_mark_fabrication.py::test_the_scan_window_check_can_fail ages out only created_at and leaves closed_at recent, so under the fix the row is legitimately in-window and scanned reads 1; the repair is to age out BOTH timestamps, which preserves its intent exactly. Verified to be the only affected test. ⚠️ AND THE DEPLOY ITSELF BACK-FILLS A ROLLING 14-DAY TAIL — every row CLOSED in the last 14 days becomes eligible and is priced from an anchor on the next tick, with no separate approval. Against the 2026-09-05 read that is 5 rows: 4169, 4170 (tlt_pullback_1d), 4422, 4423 (iwm_trend_long_1d), 4484 (gld_pullback_1h). Whoever approves the change is approving those five valuations. Do NOT back-fill anything older; see the diagnosis §2.7.
items.resolution_criteria: The sweep's scan window is keyed on the close (COALESCE(closed_at, created_at)); tests/test_local_pnl_sweep_window_is_open_keyed.py has had its strict-xfail marker and its test_long_hold_row_is_never_even_scanned removed (the xfail XPASSing is the signal); test_the_scan_window_check_can_fail ages out both timestamps and is green; and a re-measurement over the same population shows no closed non-reduce row held >14 days carrying a pnl NULL with NO pnl_source key — i.e. every such row is either priced or explicitly declared unmeasured. Historical rows older than the window are NOT back-filled by this row's resolution; that is a separate decision with its own evidence bar.

items.title: Nothing distinguishes 'leg holding a position by design' from 'leg wedged', so a healthy 33-day trend position escalated as a stuck one
items.detail: mes_trend_long_1d held trade 4350 (MES, ib_paper) open 33 days and was escalated as STUCK with a live position. Established against broker truth 2026-09-05T03:06Z, not the journal: the position is genuinely open on the venue (15 long, entry 7630.872) and rests a COMPLETE quantity-matched OCA bracket — STP 7533.75 + LMT 8390.50, both GTC, one group, 15 against a 15-lot position — matching the journal's declared stop_loss 7533.69642857 and take_profit_1 8390.59025 to the 0.25 MES tick on BOTH legs. It is healthy. The leg's own declared config explains the duration: timeframe 1d, donchian 30, tp_r 50.0, trail_mult 3.0 — a hold-until-trailing-stop configuration that is not designed to close in 33 days. The stop has TRAILED UP 151.5 points from the exit_plan's original 7382.20535714 to 7533.69642857, i.e. the position is being actively managed. The stuck-position watchdog already fired on 2026-08-08 and recorded stuck_position_alive_seen_at — it looked and correctly found the position ALIVE. Every input needed to reach 'this is fine' was present; nothing assembled them, so a human had to.
items.why_it_matters: The cost is misallocated attention and, worse, the risk of an intervention on a healthy live position. A leg holding one position cannot re-enter (the netting guard, working correctly), so 'silent' and 'stuck' and 'holding by design' all present identically on the fleet views.
items.next_action: Add a 'days open vs. expected holding period' column to the open-positions view. The expected period is derivable from what the leg already declares (timeframe, donchian, tp_r, trail_mult) — no new measurement is required. A leg inside its expected band reads as holding; one well outside it reads as a candidate for a look.
items.resolution_criteria: An open-position read surface reports, per open trade, days-open beside an expected-holding-period derived from the leg's declared geometry, and a position inside its band is visibly distinguished from one outside it — demonstrated on trade 4350 (inside) and on at least one genuinely wedged row (outside). No order path changes.

items.title: mes_trend_long_1d minted 7 order packages in 49 minutes from ONE daily signal because sizing returned an empty map, and each was orphaned unexecuted
items.detail: POPULATION: all 8 order_packages for mes_trend_long_1d (filter_state 'applied', total 8), read 2026-09-05. Seven are orphaned, created 2026-06-01 between 09:06:57 and 09:56:04 — roughly every 8 minutes for 49 minutes. All seven carry linked_trade_id: None, orphaned_by: monitor_reconciler, and orphaned_reason 'BUG-049 — no linked_trade_id after 5 min; package was never executed'. All seven share ONE entry_time ('2026-06-01 00:00:00') and one donchian_hi (7611.75): this is a single daily signal re-emitted seven times, not seven signals. All seven carry "sized_qty_by_account": {} — EMPTY. The package that did work (pkg-1d9598b29f38440c, linked to trade 4350) carries {"ib_paper": 15.0}. So sizing resolved to nothing, no order was placed, no trade linked, the reconciler orphaned the package after 5 minutes, and the leg re-emitted on the next tick — seven times until it stopped. ⚠️ THESE ARE NOT TRADE 4350'S DEBRIS and must not be read as such: they predate it by 63 days, are unlinked to it, were never executed, carry no venue state, and are in a terminal status. MI-127 was dispatched on the premise that they were part of 4350's situation; they are a separate, older, self-limited incident.
items.why_it_matters: A 1d leg that re-emits on every tick while sizing returns empty burns order-package ids and reconciler work, and leaves debris that later reads as evidence of a broken leg — which is exactly what happened here. The leg is fine; it traded normally on 2026-08-03. What is unestablished is WHY sizing returned empty that morning, and whether the re-emit loop is bounded by anything other than the condition clearing on its own.
items.next_action: Establish why sized_qty_by_account came back empty on 2026-06-01 (the 7 packages carry the full signal_logic, so the inputs are recoverable), and whether an empty sizing result should suppress re-emission for the rest of the bar on a 1d leg rather than retrying every tick.
items.resolution_criteria: The cause of the empty sizing map on 2026-06-01 is named with evidence, AND either (a) an empty sizing result on a leg whose timeframe exceeds the tick interval no longer re-emits within the same bar — asserted by a test — or (b) it is established with evidence that the existing retry is correctly bounded and the 7-package burst could not recur, in which case this row closes as no-change with that reasoning recorded.

items.title: The pending-pings hash ledger dedupes ACROSS drain passes but not WITHIN one, so two byte-identical rows in the file page the operator twice
items.detail: Found while arming merge=union on docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl (MI-113). notify_on_pull.py::_drain_pending_pings loads the delivered set ONCE from runtime_logs/pending_pings_delivered.txt and never adds to it while iterating; _record_delivered_hash is only called later, per ping, after enqueue succeeds (scripts/notify_on_pull.py:661-691, :842-843, :937). So a hash seen twice inside a single pass is enqueued twice. MEASURED 2026-09-05, population 1 file / 2 byte-identical rows / empty ledger: _drain_pending_pings returned 2 pings carrying 1 distinct line hash. Positive control that the ledger does work as designed: the same row with its hash pre-seeded into `delivered` returns 0 pings. WHY IT MATTERS NOW AND NOT BEFORE: union makes byte-identical duplicates reachable. When a ping row is hand-rescued onto main by value (as #10974 did for five rows) and the PR that carried it later merges, union keeps both copies -- test-merging #10888 into origin/main @5eb59917 yields 91 lines / 90 unique, the 2026-09-03T04:44:40 night_shift_summary row duplicated byte-for-byte. That is one duplicate operator page. This was accepted deliberately rather than overlooked: a duplicate page is noise and recoverable, a dropped ping is loss and is not. NOT FIXED HERE -- scripts/notify_on_pull.py is outside this Tier-1 change's scope (.gitattributes plus one test). NOTE THE CHEAP WRONG FIX: de-duplicating rows in the FILE (a merge driver that drops repeats) is not the same thing and is not safe -- two genuinely distinct events can serialise identically, and dropping one is the ping loss this whole item exists to stop. The fix belongs in the drainer's own bookkeeping.
items.resolution_criteria: _drain_pending_pings adds each line hash to its in-pass `delivered` set as it iterates, so N byte-identical rows in one file yield exactly 1 ping. Proven by a test that feeds a file containing the same row twice with an EMPTY ledger and asserts len(pings) == 1, alongside a positive control asserting that two DISTINCT rows still yield 2 pings (so the dedupe is not swallowing real events). Closing this by editing docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl, or by making a merge driver drop duplicate lines, does NOT satisfy it.

items.title: pr-landing-guard forces a hold on Tier-1 work touching a path outside TIER1_SURFACE, but its closed hold_reason vocabulary has no entry for that, so the declaration cannot be made honestly
items.detail: Hit on the MI-113 branch (claude/mi113-pending-pings-merge-driver), whose whole diff is .gitattributes + one test + backlog rows. R5 refuses `landing: "self"` because .gitattributes is outside TIER1_SURFACE (scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py:162-174) and its message says to set `landing: "hold"` instead. R7 then requires hold_reason from a closed set of five (:221-233), and MEASURED against this diff none of them is true: tier_2_3_needs_approval is false (the canonical doc's Tier-1 examples cover repo hygiene and lint/CI config, and TIER1_SURFACE already carries the sibling root config files .ruff.toml, ruff.toml, pyproject.toml); depends_on_unmerged_pr has no PR to name; awaiting_evidence is false (the measurement is complete and in the PR); operator_asked_to_hold is false (no operator spoke, and the dispatching manager said the opposite -- self-land); changes_landing_machinery is REFUSED by R8, which verifies it against LANDING_MACHINERY (:211-219) and .gitattributes is not in that list. Population: 97 declarations in .github/pr-landing/, of which 10 are holds -- 5 tier-1 operator_asked_to_hold, 4 tier-1 changes_landing_machinery, 4 tier-2 + 1 tier-3 tier_2_3_needs_approval. So no existing declaration has faced this case. The branch shipped operator_asked_to_hold with the imperfection disclosed at the top of hold_text, following the precedent mi102 and mi95 set for a knowingly-approximate token. That is a workaround, not a fix: a closed vocabulary whose nearest entry is false trains authors to pick the nearest label and stop reading, which is the opposite of the 'a hold is a stated KIND of hold, not an adjective' property R7 exists to create. TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME. (a) add a sixth reason such as path_outside_tier1_surface, verified against the diff the way R8 verifies its own -- the hold stays and becomes sayable; (b) add .gitattributes to TIER1_SURFACE -- the hold goes away for this path class. They differ on whether a human should read a merge-policy change at all, which is a judgement for the operator, not for the session that is blocked. ⚠️ NOT FIXED ON THAT BRANCH ON PURPOSE: either fix edits check_pr_landing.py, the guard judging that branch's own PR, which is the 'cheaper to lie to than to satisfy' failure that file's own docstring warns about.
items.resolution_criteria: A Tier-1 diff whose only unvouched path is .gitattributes can produce a pr-landing declaration in which every field is true, and pr-landing-guard passes on it. Proven by a self-test added to check_pr_landing.py's own suite that builds exactly that diff and asserts a pass -- plus a negative control asserting that a diff touching a Tier-2/Tier-3 named path still FAILS, so the fix widened the vocabulary and not the gate. If fix (b) is chosen instead, the same self-test asserts `landing: "self"` passes for that diff while a diff touching config/ or src/ still fails. Closing this by writing a hold_text that explains the mismatch does NOT satisfy it -- that is what was already done.

items.title: test_the_committed_store_declares_at_least_one_real_decision_request asserts the LIVE store currently carries at least one decision request, so answering the last open question turns pytest-run red on a correct production state
items.detail: POPULATION: all 618 work objects in docs/claude/work/objects/*.yaml, scanned 2026-09-05 at 9f2590b2. 9 decision requests found. The test asserts `found` is non-empty, so the margin to red is 9 — the suite goes red when all nine are answered or removed, which is the GOAL state of the decision channel, not a defect. SAME CLASS AS MI-120: a test whose expected value is drawn from live production state asserts that production is currently in a particular condition and reports the violation as a code defect. It is filed rather than fixed under MI-120 because the margin is 9, where MI-120's was 0 (in_flight 8 of 8) and had already blocked the merge queue for ~90 minutes on 2026-09-04. The failure mode is identical: pytest-run is a REQUIRED context, so a legitimate production state blocks every open PR at once, and the block is not attributable to any PR's diff. The docstring makes the coupling deliberate ('Reads the REAL store, not a fixture') and the INTENT is sound — it checks that the mechanism carries real content rather than being deployed and unproven. The objection is to the CHANNEL, not the check: a claim about live production belongs in a monitor that pages, not in a required unit-test context that gates unrelated merges. NOT YET MEASURED: how fast the 9 drain, i.e. how much real time the margin buys.
items.resolution_criteria: The mechanism's coverage is asserted against a CONSTRUCTED store containing a known decision request (proving normalise_requests parses a real object), and passes with the live store carrying both 9 requests and ZERO — demonstrated by running against a fixture store with none, not by waiting for the live store to be convenient. If the 'is the channel actually carrying questions' signal is still wanted, it exists somewhere that does not gate the merge queue. Closing note must state which assertions survive.
