items.title: a sub-session can complete its work and then discover it cannot push, and nothing recovers it — THREE instances on 2026-09-04/05
items.detail: RECURRENCE, measured, three instances in about eighteen hours, each losing a completed unit of work. (1) MI-107 first spawn (session_012p1DoQBRJYyggX8ELT1WEP): reached need_input at 08:00Z with 'push blocked by proxy'; its clone carried the LOWERCASE benbaichmankass/metis-insights, which the sandbox proxy scope denies. ~159k tokens of design work lost; respawned. (2) MI-73 (session_01ThkrPrGUvmomoY8uGEa148, in SESSIONS.json): 'blocked on permission classifier; auto-mode denied add_repo x2 and git push x3'. (3) MI-124 (session_018iMJkpN41FHzNjKj7ShNPS), 2026-09-05T00:34Z: completed a TEN-LEG diagnostic — 57,690 output tokens — and went need_input with 'grant Bash git permissions to push branch + open PR'. MEASURED: `git ls-remote --heads origin` matches NO claude/mi124* branch, so nothing reached origin. ⚠️ THE MANAGER CANNOT RESCUE IT, AND THIS IS NOW VERIFIED TWICE BY TWO DIFFERENT PROBES rather than asserted once: ListAgents returns 'No reachable agents' (cloud sub-sessions are not listed), and a direct SendMessage to the session id returns "No agent named '...' is reachable". The session's own record carries `cross_session_inbound: available`, which is what prompted the re-test — that field describes a capability the SESSION has, NOT an address the manager holds, and reading it as the latter would have been a false correction. ⚠️ THE COMMON SHAPE IS NOT THE CAUSE. The three causes differ — repo-name case, permission-mode denial, permission-mode denial — and treating them as one 'push is flaky' problem is what has let it recur. What is COMMON is the ORDERING: every one of them spent its whole budget FIRST and discovered it could not deliver LAST, when the manager can no longer reach it and a respawn starts from zero. The spawn prompt already carries a `git remote set-url` first action (added after instance 1) and instance 3 still happened, because that fix addresses one cause and not the ordering.
items.resolution_criteria: The spawn-prompt template makes PROVING DELIVERABILITY the first action, before any substantive work: commit an empty or trivial commit on the branch and PUSH it, and on failure STOP and report the exact error rather than proceeding. Verified by a spawned session either (a) pushing that probe commit — visible as a branch on origin within minutes of spawn, before its work exists — or (b) reporting a push failure while its context is still nearly empty, so a respawn costs almost nothing. ⚠️ NOT sufficient: another `git remote set-url` line, or any prose reminder. Instance 3 had the remote-fix line and still stranded, which is the evidence that a per-cause patch does not close the class. ⚠️ AND a spawn that pushes late is NOT evidence either — the criterion is that the push happens BEFORE the budget is spent, so check the branch's first-commit timestamp against the session's created_at, not merely that a branch exists.
items.fix: Add the push-probe as step 0 of the sub-session spawn template (the manager writes it, so it is a prompt change, not code). Consider also whether `session_registry.py register` should emit it, since that is already the surface the manager must pass through to get a spawn prompt.

items.title: backlog_append.py only APPENDS, so the cheapest way to amend a filed row is the hand-edit CLAUDE.md forbids
items.detail: MEASURED on myself, 2026-09-05T00:4xZ. CLAUDE.md says in terms: file through `scripts/ops/backlog_append.py::append_row`, NEVER by hand, because a naive read-append-write reformats every non-ASCII line and re-attributes ~21k lines to the PR. I used the helper correctly to FILE a row. `check_backlog_criteria` then refused that row for missing `resolution_criteria` and `tier` — correctly. To ADD those two fields I hand-spliced JSON, because `append_row` appends and there is no edit entry point, and I broke the file's round-trip; `backlog_append.py --check-live` caught it. ⚠️ THE POINT IS THE INCENTIVE, NOT MY MISTAKE. Two guards in the same suite push in opposite directions: one refuses an incomplete row (so rows WILL need amending), the other refuses a hand-edited file — and the repo ships a supported path for only one of those. The cheapest route to a required edit is therefore the forbidden one, which is the shape CLAUDE.md itself names for a guard cheaper to lie to than to satisfy. Repaired by restoring the file to origin/main's exact serialisation and re-appending all three of the branch's rows through `append_row`; 1186 rows, round-trip clean, guards PASS 52 / FAIL 0.
items.resolution_criteria: `backlog_append.py` exposes an `update_row(path, row_id, **fields)` (or equivalent) that mutates named fields on an existing row and preserves the file's exact serialisation, verified by `--check-live` passing after an update AND by a `git diff` touching only the intended row's lines — a whole-file reformat that happens to still parse is the failure being prevented, not a pass. ⚠️ Prove it by MUTATION: run the update, confirm the diff is line-local, then corrupt the serialisation deliberately and confirm --check-live goes red — otherwise the check may be passing for an unrelated reason.
items.fix: Add an edit/update entry point to backlog_append.py alongside append_row, with the same round-trip guarantee.

items.title: #10398 carries a unique point-in-time capture AND a file that rewinds main by 7 days — merging or closing it whole is wrong either way
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-05T02:3xZ against origin/main. #10398 (automation/econ-calendar-33232352515-1, opened 2026-08-29) touches three files and they need OPPOSITE dispositions: (a) comms/macro/econ_calendar_captures/US-20260829T034952Z.fxstreet.json — 61,529 lines, ABSENT from main (`git cat-file -e` fails). A POINT-IN-TIME capture whose entire value is recording what was known at that instant; it can never be regenerated. Pure addition, nothing to lose by taking it. (b) comms/macro/econ_calendar_upcoming.json — main's is generated_from_observed_at 2026-09-05T00:18:54Z with 429 events; the PR's is 2026-08-29T03:49:52Z with 380. Merging it wholesale REWINDS the current-view file by seven days and drops 49 events. (c) comms/macro/econ_calendar_snapshots.jsonl — +444 lines, append-shaped, needs a row-level check for what main already holds. ⚠️ BOTH WHOLE-PR VERDICTS ARE WRONG. Merging rewinds (b). Closing as superseded destroys (a) permanently — and 'superseded' was the manager's first read, because a LATER run of the same workflow (#11017) merged as 5b6c2b38 and the titles are identical. A same-workflow successor merging does NOT make an earlier PIT capture redundant; that is precisely what point-in-time means. ⚠️ SECOND INSTANCE OF THIS EXACT SHAPE IN THIS QUEUE, which is why it is filed as a class and not just a disposition: #10921 needed the same partial take (a PROBES.json three days NEWER than main's alongside a DUE.json ~20h OLDER), filed as MI-117 and still unrouted. Automation PRs that bundle an append-only artifact with a regenerated current-view file cannot be dispositioned by class, and the queue has now hit that twice.
items.resolution_criteria: #10398 is dispositioned by FILE, not by PR: the capture (a) lands on main — verified by `git cat-file -e origin/main:comms/macro/econ_calendar_captures/US-20260829T034952Z.fxstreet.json` succeeding — while (b) is NOT taken, verified by main's econ_calendar_upcoming.json still reading a generated_from_observed_at no older than 2026-09-05T00:18:54Z. (c) is taken only for rows main does not already hold, verified by a line count that does not duplicate. ⚠️ A PLAIN MERGE THAT HAPPENS TO LEAVE (b) ALONE DOES NOT COUNT — check the stamp, not the merge. ⚠️ AND THE CLASS HALF IS SEPARATE: state whether the econ-calendar workflow should stop bundling an append-only capture with a regenerated view in one PR, since that bundling is what makes every one of these PRs un-dispositionable as a whole. Deciding NOT to change the workflow is a legitimate answer and must be recorded as a decision, with the consequence stated — every future run needs a hand partial-take.
items.fix: Partial-take (a) and the un-held rows of (c) onto main; leave (b). Then rule on the workflow's bundling.
items.note: Filed, not taken: comms/macro/** is not the manager surface, and the take is worker work.

items.title: Rebuilding a branch by copying a directory wholesale rewound five machine-generated registers and silently dropped three filed backlog rows
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-05 on the manager's OWN PR (#11032), and it is the #10398 hazard committed by the session that was holding #10398 in the merge queue precisely because that PR 'carries a file that rewinds main by seven days'. To move hand-edited state from an abandoned branch onto a fresh one cut from main, the session ran `cp -r docs/claude/work`. That directory holds BOTH hand-edited registers (MANAGER-CHECKLIST, MANAGER-LEASE, MERGE-QUEUE, SESSIONS) and MACHINE-GENERATED ones written by scheduled workflows. The copy rewound every generated file in it: WORK-DIGEST.json 2026-09-05T04:43:07Z -> 00:07:41Z (-4.6h); PR-QUEUE-WATCH.json 04:55:44Z -> 2026-09-04T21:02:03Z (-7.9h); REAPER-OBSERVATIONS.json 04:26:43Z -> 2026-09-04T23:02:52Z (-5.4h); TRAINER-CAPTURE-WATCH.json 04:40:40Z -> 2026-09-04T20:51:48Z (-7.8h); OPEN-PRS.json (no stamp, also overwritten). SECOND, SEPARATE LOSS FROM THE SAME ACT: the copy took docs/claude/work/ and NOT docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json, so THREE rows filed earlier that session vanished -- BL-20260905-SUB-SESSIONS-FINISH-WORK-THEY-CANNOT-PUSH-AND-THE-MANAGER-CANNOT-REACH-THEM, BL-20260905-BACKLOG-APPEND-HAS-NO-EDIT-PATH-SO-AMENDING-A-ROW-REQUIRES-THE-FORBIDDEN-HAND-EDIT, and BL-20260905-PR-10398-IS-A-MIXED-TAKE-A-UNIQUE-PIT-CAPTURE-BESIDE-A-SEVEN-DAY-REWIND. Recovered by reading them off the abandoned branch and re-appending via append_row. A straight file take was REFUSED as the fix: measured, it would have dropped 5 rows that reached main after that branch was cut. HOW IT WAS CAUGHT MATTERS MORE THAN THE DEFECT. Nobody read the diff and spotted it. digest-liveness FAILED on the branch and PASSED on a clean origin/main control -- and the session had already written in a commit message that this guard was 'fleet state on a time window, unreachable from a diff that touches only registers'. That assertion was WRONG; the guard was reading a file the diff had rewound. The control cost one worktree and disproved it. THE GENERAL CLASS: a directory that mixes hand-edited and machine-generated state has no safe wholesale copy, and the loss is SILENT in both directions -- a rewind reads as a normal diff, and a file left behind reads as nothing at all.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) docs/claude/work/ distinguishes generated from hand-edited files in a way a copy cannot get wrong -- a manifest, a subdirectory split, or a guard that FAILS when a PR moves a generated register's timestamp BACKWARDS -- demonstrated by constructing a branch that rewinds one and showing the check catches it; OR (b) a recorded decision that no mechanism is warranted and the existing guards (digest-liveness caught one of five here) are accepted as the only net, WITH the consequence stated: the other four rewinds were caught only because they sat in the same directory as the one that alarmed, and nothing would have caught them alone. NOT SUFFICIENT: this instance being repaired (it is), or a note telling sessions to be careful -- 'remember not to copy the directory' is the reminder-instead-of-mechanism non-fix this repo has already paid for twice on MI-15.

items.title: A routed partial-take work object prescribed the rewind it was written to prevent, because it told the worker to re-measure the row set but not which side was newer
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-05 by the worker session for WO-20260905-PROBES-JSON-PARTIAL-TAKE-FROM-10921. The work object routed a Tier-1 partial take: bring docs/claude/PROBES.json from PR #10921 onto main by value, on the stated basis that the PR's file (2026-09-03T09:56:34) was three days newer than main's (2026-09-01T10:13:20). It correctly anticipated ONE axis of staleness -- it warned in bold that the id-population comparison was a day old and MUST be re-run -- but treated the take's DIRECTION as settled fact. Re-measured at execution time: main's docs/claude/PROBES.json is 2026-09-04T09:45:04, i.e. 23.8h NEWER than the PR's, because a later scheduled probe run landed on main after the work object was written. Population, both sides: 34 results rows each, 34 unique ids each; ids on main absent from the PR = 0; ids in the PR absent from main = 0 (set-difference instrument validated by a positive control -- removing 3 ids from the PR side made it report exactly those 3). The whole-file diff is 30 lines and EVERY differing field is a later observation on main: trainer-capture-watch 8 runs vs 3; a matched=2/200 vs 1/200; arbitration_fanout_soak 186/263 vs 162/226; pr-queue-watch 4.7h/14 PRs vs 4.9h/8 PRs. Executing the prescribed take as written would therefore have REWOUND main's probe register by 23.8h -- the same class of harm as BL-20260905-A-WHOLESALE-DIRECTORY-COPY-REWOUND-FIVE-GENERATED-REGISTERS-AND-DROPPED-THREE-FILED-ROWS, arrived at by following the remedy for it. The PR's DUE.json (2026-09-03T09:57:21) is likewise now 43h behind main's (2026-09-05T04:54:34), so all three of the PR's files are stale and nothing in it is takeable. NOT A DUPLICATE of the WHOLESALE row: that one is an operator hazard in a copy command (cp -r over generated files); this one is a hazard in the ROUTING ARTEFACT -- a work object that hard-codes a measured comparison as a premise and scopes its re-measure instruction to only one of the two axes that can go stale. The Done criterion saved it by accident: it read 'stamp 2026-09-03T09:56:34 OR NEWER', which main already satisfied.
items.resolution_criteria: A work object that prescribes taking a file or rows BY VALUE from one ref onto another states the take direction as a re-measurable claim rather than a premise, and its re-measure instruction covers BOTH axes: (a) the row/id population on each side, and (b) which side's artefact is newer at execution time. Concretely: either the work-object template gains a 'verify before acting' block requiring the worker to restate both sides' generated_at stamps and abort if the destination is already at-or-newer, or scripts/ops grows a helper the worker runs that refuses a take whose source stamp is older than the destination's. Demonstrated by a subsequent routed take whose worker report shows both stamps re-measured at execution time.

items.title: MERGE-QUEUE.json's state vocabulary has no term for a PR closed WITHOUT merging, so the only way to record that outcome is to delete the row
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-05. check_manager_scope R8 enforces a CLOSED vocabulary on docs/claude/work/MERGE-QUEUE.json::entries[].state — blocked, green, merged, rebasing, waiting — and the guard's own message explains why that is right: 'a closed vocabulary, so not-my-turn (waiting) and cannot-go (blocked) stay different facts'. The rule is sound and this row is not a request to weaken it. THE GAP: a PR CLOSED WITHOUT MERGING is a real terminal outcome and none of the five terms describes it. `merged` is false. `blocked` and `waiting` both assert the PR is still live. So the only representable action is to DELETE the entry, which is what was done for #10921 — and deleting it removes the reason the PR was closed from the one file a manager reads to run the queue. NOT HYPOTHETICAL and the instance matters: #10921 was closed because a re-measurement REVERSED the premise that had queued it (main's PROBES.json turned out 23.8h NEWER than the PR's, not three days staler), so taking it would have rewound a register. That is precisely the kind of outcome a successor should be able to read off the queue rather than reconstruct. It survives only because it was also written into MANAGER-CHECKLIST MI-117 and as a comment on the PR itself — two places that happened to be available, not a designed home. ⚠️ THE SILENT-LOSS SHAPE: a vocabulary that cannot express an outcome does not produce an error at the moment the outcome happens; it produces a deletion that looks like tidying.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) the vocabulary gains a term for this outcome (e.g. `closed_unmerged`) with R8 updated to accept it and a test asserting an entry carrying it passes while an unknown term still fails — the closed-vocabulary property must survive the addition, or the fix has removed the guard rather than extended it; OR (b) a recorded decision that resolved entries SHOULD be deleted from the queue, with the consequence stated — the reason a PR was closed then lives only in the checklist and on the PR, and a manager reading only MERGE-QUEUE.json cannot tell a PR that was closed on evidence from one that was dropped. NOT SUFFICIENT: deleting entries and considering the matter handled, which is the current behaviour and is what produced this row.

items.title: An EMPTY sized_qty_by_account is an eligibility/resolution failure, never a sizing-arithmetic one — every account was dropped BEFORE position_size ran, and until 2026-09-05 nothing recorded which rule dropped which account
items.detail: FILED RATHER THAN WIDENED INTO, per the operator's Tier-2 scope decision of 2026-09-05: the approved object was the BRAKE (refuse once, log a cause), and the operator was explicitly offered 'investigate WHY sizing returned empty first' and did not take it. This row carries the question the brake deliberately does not answer. POPULATION for the structural claim: all writers of sized_qty_by_account in src/ — there are exactly two, both in Coordinator.multi_account_execute (coordinator.py:1825 sets 0.0 on zero_balance, :1836 sets the sized qty), and both are INSIDE the per-account loop. Positive control that the map is populated on a healthy dispatch: the one mes_trend_long_1d package that worked carries {"ib_paper": 15.0}, and tests/test_s026_g2_position_size.py asserts a two-account map. So an EMPTY map is not 'the sizer answered 0' — that leaves a populated map plus its own rejection rows and engages the existing 300s refusal cooldown. An empty map means the LOOP NEVER RAN FOR ANY ACCOUNT, i.e. every account was excluded by one of six pre-sizing rules: not_configured, symbol->exchange routing (the IB/non-IB gate), strategies declared empty, strategy_not_assigned, outside_account_scope (the arbitration fan-out narrowing), or account_type_mismatch. That is account/instrument/assignment RESOLUTION, and none of it is arithmetic. ⚠️ THE 2026-06-01 CAUSE IS STILL NOT ESTABLISHED AND THIS ROW DOES NOT CLAIM IT IS. What changed on 2026-09-05 is only that the reasons are now RECORDED: the eligibility predicate returned a bare bool, so every dropped account vanished without a recoverable reason and the question was unanswerable from the journal by construction — seven packages each carrying {} and none naming its own cause. mes_trend_long_1d routes to ib_paper and traded normally on 2026-08-03, so a permanent misconfiguration is not the explanation; a transient one (creds unreadable that morning -> configured=False, or an instrument-exchange resolution that returned something other than interactive_brokers for MES) fits the evidence and is unverified.
items.why_it_matters: The parent row BL-20260905-MES-TREND-LONG-1D-RE-EMITTED-ONE-DAILY-SIGNAL-SEVEN-TIMES-IN-49-MINUTES-WHEN-SIZING-RETURNED-EMPTY asks 'why did sizing return empty' as an open question. This row narrows the search from 'the sizer' to 'the eligibility filter' and names the six candidate rules, so whoever picks it up does not re-derive that. It also records that the answer for 2026-06-01 specifically may be permanently unrecoverable — the packages that would have carried the reasons were written before the reasons existed.

For 2026-06-01 retrospectively, the seven packages carry the full signal_logic; check whether ib_paper's configured flag or the MES instrument->exchange resolution could have differed that morning (deploy/restart history, creds), and record either the cause or that it is unrecoverable.

items.tier: 2 — the remedy is in the typed dispatch path, not a doc edit
items.source: src/core/coordinator.py::multi_account_execute_typed
items.title: The empty-sizing brake is wired into multi_account_execute only — multi_account_execute_typed can still re-emit a signal that sized nothing, and arming CENTRALIZED_ALLOCATOR would silently lose the brake
items.detail: SEVERITY IS LOW BECAUSE THE PATH IS NOT LIVE, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE ARGUMENT — say so rather than reading it as 'small'. POPULATION: the two dispatch branches in src/runtime/pipeline.py's actionable-signal block. The typed branch is taken only when _centralized_allocator_enabled(settings) is true; src/runtime/runtime_flags.py:126 defaults CENTRALIZED_ALLOCATOR to 'false' and its own docstring calls the path 'shadow mode only'. ⚠️ I DID NOT ESTABLISH THE LIVE VALUE ON THE VM — this is a code-default reading, not a get-env measurement against /proc/<MainPID>/environ, and this file's own rules say a code default is not the live state. The 2026-09-05 brake (BL-20260905-MES-TREND-LONG-1D-RE-EMITTED-ONE-DAILY-SIGNAL-SEVEN-TIMES-IN-49-MINUTES-WHEN-SIZING-RETURNED-EMPTY) stamps meta.empty_sizing_refusal inside multi_account_execute, and the pipeline gate reads that stamp back. multi_account_execute_typed writes no such stamp, so a typed dispatch that sizes nothing leaves no record for the gate to find and the signal re-emits on the next tick — the exact pre-fix behaviour, preserved behind a default-off flag. This is the 'a required capability sits behind a flag that can be armed without it' shape, one level in: arming the allocator would silently un-arm a brake nobody would think to re-check.
items.why_it_matters: The brake exists because seven phantom order packages per occurrence pollute the order-package data the M7 review packets grade strategies on. Whatever fraction of dispatch moves to the typed path takes that pollution back with it, and nothing would announce the regression — the tests would still pass, because they exercise the legacy path.
items.next_action: Either extend the empty-sizing refusal stamp to multi_account_execute_typed (same helper, same signal_key derivation — signal_key_for_package already takes any package-shaped object), or, if the typed path is being retired rather than armed, record that decision so this row closes as no-change. Read the LIVE CENTRALIZED_ALLOCATOR with get-env before choosing.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) a test drives multi_account_execute_typed to an empty sizing result and asserts exactly one package plus a logged cause, with a positive control that the typed path still emits normally on a real sizing map — mirroring tests/test_bl20260905_empty_sizing_map_refused_once.py; OR (b) the operator decides the typed allocator path is retired and that is recorded here, in which case this closes as no-change. ⚠️ NOT sufficient: observing that CENTRALIZED_ALLOCATOR is currently false. That is the reason the severity is low, not a reason the gap is closed.

items.tier: 1 — the remedy is a state split plus its consumer, in the observability/read path
items.source: src/runtime/strategy_monocle.py::_same_bar_entry_for_strategy
items.title: The bar-close debounce returns None for BOTH 'no debounce applies' and 'we could not resolve this strategy's timeframe', so a config-read failure disarms a live over-trading brake with nothing saying so
items.detail: COLLAPSED STATE, per CLAUDE.md's own design test: can this field say 'we did not look'? It cannot. _same_bar_entry_for_strategy returns None — which the pipeline reads as 'dispatch' — on at least four different facts: the kill-switch is set, no package exists in this bar (the correct permissive answer), a DB read failed (already logged), and _strategy_timeframe_seconds returned None. That last one covers BOTH a strategy with no configured timeframe (NO log at all — the function simply returns None from _timeframe_seconds) and a load_strategy_config() failure (logged, but only as a warning nothing branches on). ⚠️ STATE THE POPULATION, BECAUSE IT IS THE HONEST HALF OF THIS ROW: measured against config/strategies.yaml on 2026-09-05, 0 of 52 enabled strategies (0 of 55 total) lack a timeframe key — POSITIVE CONTROL: the first five enabled legs read turtle_soup 15m, trend_donchian 1h, fade_breakout_4h 4h, squeeze_breakout_4h 4h, ict_scalp_5m 5m, so the probe finds values when they are there. So the per-strategy half of this is LATENT, not live, and this row must not be reported as an active outage. What is NOT measurable from a repo read is the config-read-failure path, which would disarm the debounce for EVERY leg at once, permissively and quietly. Found while reading the three pre-dispatch gates for the 2026-09-05 empty-sizing brake, which deliberately does NOT share this shape: it fires only on a package carrying a NAMED cause and logs that cause on every block.
items.why_it_matters: The debounce is the ceiling on same-bar re-entry (PERF-20260601-001, added after trend_donchian stacked 9 packages in ~1h). A brake whose disarmed state is indistinguishable from its satisfied state cannot be observed to have stopped working — which is how the empty-sizing retry loop went unbounded for 49 minutes without anything naming a cause.
items.next_action: Give _strategy_timeframe_seconds (or the debounce) an explicit three-state result — debounce_applies / no_debounce_needed / timeframe_unresolved — and have the pipeline branch on the third: stay permissive (never block a leg on a config hiccup) but log it distinctly and count it, so a fleet-wide disarm is visible rather than silent. Register the contract with collapsed-state-guard so the states cannot be re-collapsed.
items.resolution_criteria: The three states are produced AND a real consumer branches on each, asserted by a test that drives an unresolvable timeframe and asserts the dispatch still proceeds (fail-permissive is deliberate and must not change) AND that the unresolved state is distinctly recorded. ⚠️ Suppressing the dispatch on an unresolved timeframe is the WRONG fix and must be refused: it would stop a leg trading on a config read hiccup, which is worse than the over-trading it guards against.

items.tier: 1 — dead code removal in the post-dispatch status-hygiene block; changes no execution decision
items.source: src/core/coordinator.py::multi_account_execute — the BUG-049 backstop if/elif chain
items.title: The BUG-049 backstop's 'elif not accounts -> no_eligible_account' arm is now UNREACHABLE, so a reader believes a close_reason value the code can no longer produce
items.detail: MI-129 (the empty-sizing brake, PR #11035) inserted 'if _empty_sizing_cause is not None' AHEAD of the pre-existing 'elif not accounts' arm in the same if/elif chain. _empty_sizing_cause is set whenever sized_qty_by_account is empty; sized_qty_by_account is initialised {} and written ONLY inside the per-account loop (coordinator.py lines 918, 1862, 1873 — verified by grepping every occurrence in the file). So an empty eligible set implies the loop never ran, implies the map is empty, implies _empty_sizing_cause is non-None, implies the 'elif not accounts' arm can NEVER be taken. The value 'no_eligible_account' is therefore no longer producible from this path. ⚠️ STATE THE POPULATION: measured on the LIVE journal 2026-09-05 via /api/diag/journal?table=order_packages&limit=1000 (the most recent 1000 rows, NOT the lifetime), 'no_eligible_account' appears ZERO times — POSITIVE CONTROL: its two siblings from the SAME if/elif chain are the 2nd and 5th commonest values in that window, all_accounts_noop 197 and no_fill_all_accounts 76, so the probe demonstrably sees values minted by this exact code block and its silence on the third is real absence in this window, not a blind read. Found while fixing the two tests MI-129 turned red: tests/test_s030_pr1_order_packages_log.py pinned close_reason == 'no_eligible_account' and can never pass again as written. NOT REMOVED IN #11035, deliberately: that PR is operator-approved on its diff and its scope is the brake; widening it to delete an adjacent arm is the scope creep the dispatch forbade.
items.why_it_matters: This repo's own rule is 'field beats comment' — code that cannot execute is the same trap one level down. A reader (or a future session writing an analytics query, a histogram, or a test) sees three declared close_reason values for the no-trade path and reasonably assumes all three occur. Two do; one is dead. The cost is not an outage — nothing branches on the value — it is a false vocabulary that will be reasoned from, exactly the way the stale prose rows this file is full of were reasoned from.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER the 'elif not accounts' arm is removed and its comment folded into the empty-sizing branch (with a test asserting the empty-eligible-set case still terminalises in-round with a NAMED cause — that contract must not be lost with the dead arm), OR it is proven reachable by an actual path and a test drives it, in which case this row is wrong and should say so. ⚠️ Simply deleting the arm without keeping a test on the empty-eligible-set case is NOT sufficient — that case is the original BUG-049 scenario and losing its coverage would be a worse outcome than the dead code. ⚠️ AND a green test suite is not evidence either way here: the arm being unreachable is precisely why no test covers it.

items.tier: 1 — a CI/test-quality guard plus the one test rewrite (already done in #11035)
items.source: tests/ (whole tree) — instance: tests/test_arbitration_fanout_apply.py::test_account_scope_can_only_subtract
items.title: RECURRENCE of BL-20260818-CAPABILITY-AUDITS-GREP-ONE-FILE-AND-MISS-SHARED-LEVERS, now in a unit test: a check that asserts on SOURCE TEXT converts any rename into a CI failure with no behavioural meaning
items.detail: MI-129 renamed a private nested predicate (_eligible_for_dispatch -> _dispatch_exclusion_reason) and replaced the list comprehension beside it. test_account_scope_can_only_subtract called inspect.getsource(Coordinator.multi_account_execute) and split on the literals 'def _eligible_for_dispatch' and 'accounts = [a for a', so the first split returned a 1-element list and the test died with IndexError — for a change that altered nothing the test is about. ⚠️ STATE THE POPULATION AND HOW IT WAS MEASURED, because the count is small and the surface is not. Denominator: 897 test files / 11373 test functions under tests/. Probe: grep for 'getsource(' across tests/, then a script that reads the 6 lines after each call site and extracts every .split() string literal. Result: 41 files and 71 getsource call sites; of those, 3 files / 7 split literals split the source on a code literal at all; and exactly ONE — tests/test_arbitration_fanout_apply.py:314 — splits on 'def <specific internal name>', the form that cannot survive a rename by construction. The other two are less fragile and were left alone: test_s011_strategy_purity.py:81 splits on the generic 'def ' (survives renames — it iterates function bodies) and test_backtest_system_evidence.py splits on 'return' and ',' (fragile to reformatting, not to a rename). SO THIS IS ONE MEASURED INSTANCE OVER A 71-SITE SURFACE — it is deliberately NOT reported as an epidemic. ⚠️ WHY IT IS FILED AS A CLASS ANYWAY, AND AS A RECURRENCE: BL-20260818-CAPABILITY-AUDITS-GREP-ONE-FILE-AND-MISS-SHARED-LEVERS already filed exactly this shape for the exit-coverage audits ('detect capability by grepping ONE module, so extracting a lever to a shared module reads as losing it'), and BL-20260902-WDEC-DISPATCH-BRANCH-TESTS-A-LITERAL-WHILE-ENCODER-AND-POLL-CLAIM-USE-THE-CONSTANT is its production-code cousin. Filing #3 of the same shape, in a third subsystem, is the recurrence signal — that the earlier row left no detector is the finding. ⚠️ THE SIBLING FAILURE IN THE SAME PR IS EXPLICITLY *NOT* THIS CLASS AND MUST NOT BE COUNTED WITH IT: tests/test_s030_pr1_order_packages_log.py pinned close_reason == 'no_eligible_account', and pinning a short enum-like token IS the correct way to assert a vocabulary contract (measured: 23 such close_reason == literal assertions across 10 test files, 44 for exit_reason — nearly all legitimate). That test broke because the change altered the vocabulary, not because the assertion was brittle. Calling them one class would be the wrong lesson.
items.why_it_matters: A test that reads source text is cheaper to break than to satisfy and carries no behavioural meaning, so it taxes every future refactor of the module it points at while proving nothing about it. Worse, the failure mode is an IndexError rather than an assertion, so it does not even name the property it was defending — a reader has to reconstruct the intent before deciding whether the change was safe. The property here was fully observable: the rewrite drives the real multi_account_execute over five scopes and is mutation-tested in both directions (scope ignored -> fails; scope re-admitting -> fails), which the source read never was.
items.resolution_criteria: A CI check that FAILS a test which splits an inspect.getsource() result on a literal containing 'def <name>' — i.e. the rename-fragile form specifically, NOT all getsource use (asserting a call is present, or iterating on the generic 'def ', is legitimate and must stay allowed, or the check will be disabled the first time it fires on a good test). It must ship with a planted positive control proving it fails closed on a known-bad input, and it must NAME the file and the literal. ⚠️ A count of remaining sites is NOT the criterion: the one live instance is already fixed in #11035, so a check that merely reports zero today proves nothing about whether it would catch the next one. ⚠️ AND documenting 'do not scrape source in tests' is explicitly NOT sufficient — that is the reminder-is-not-a-mechanism non-fix this repo has already paid for, and BL-20260818 is the evidence: it stated the lesson and the shape came back twice.

items.tier: 2 to fix (src/runtime/order_monitor.py, order path) — needs an operator OK
items.source: src/runtime/order_monitor.py:10219 _sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit
items.title: RECURRENCE of MI-128 in the SIBLING sweep: _sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit bounds its scan by datetime(created_at) >= datetime('now','-7 days'), so a Bybit position held longer than 7 days can never have its fee-accurate broker closedPnl recovered
items.detail: FILED, NOT FIXED — out of the MI-128 approval, which scoped to _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced's scan query only. This is the SAME open-vs-close keying defect one function up, and it is filed as a RECURRENCE rather than a duplicate because it shows the class is not confined to the row MI-128 fixed: two sweeps, written at different times, both bound a CLOSE-derived recovery by the OPEN. MECHANISM: the sweep recovers Bybit's own closedPnl, which is BROKER TRUTH (MEASURED) and is retained ~7 days FROM THE CLOSE — hence the 7-day window, which is correct in length and wrong in what it is measured from. Keyed on created_at, a position held longer than 7 days is already outside the window at the moment it closes and stays outside forever, so the fee-accurate number is never fetched. It is the more expensive half of MI-128: MI-128 lost an ESTIMATED value, this loses a MEASURED one, and src/runtime/provenance.py grades that gap explicitly. ORDER BY datetime(created_at) DESC feeds LIMIT 50 and carries the same defect one level down. POPULATION (state it): trade_journal.db::trades, all 5,494 rows fetched complete by pagination via /api/bot/db/table/trades (fetched == total_reported), read 2026-09-05 against live trader git_sha 9337958e. Non-backtest status='closed' Bybit rows (bybit_1/bybit_2/bybit_portfolio) with hold computable = 1,456; excluding intent_reduce legs = 1,204; held > 7 days and therefore unreachable by this sweep = 26; of those, pnl IS NULL = 5 (ids 3316, 3520, 3588, 4135, 4164). POSITIVE CONTROL, so the small count is not read as an empty probe: the same population contains 1,178 rows held <= 7 days that this sweep CAN reach, and MI-128's own measurement found bybit_closed_pnl had successfully filled trade 4163 — so the sweep demonstrably works, on rows inside its window. The 26 is a real denominator, not a silence. NOTE THE INTERACTION WITH MI-128: those 5 rows sit in MI-128's 20-row silent set. Once MI-128 deploys, the LOCAL sweep can reach such a row and will book an ESTIMATED anchored price where a MEASURED broker number was available but never asked for — a provenance DOWNGRADE that MI-128 makes newly reachable, which is why this is filed now rather than left for a later review.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) the scan window and ORDER BY in _sweep_pending_pnl_from_bybit are re-keyed to COALESCE(closed_at, created_at) under a Tier-2 operator OK, with a test that a Bybit row closed recently but held > 7 days is SCANNED — and the same forward-only condition MI-128 carries, stated explicitly, because merging is the deploy here; OR (b) the operator records a decision that broker-truth recovery for long-held Bybit positions is not worth the change, with the consequence stated: those rows are priced by local compute at ESTIMATED, never MEASURED. NOT SUFFICIENT: a green test in a harness (MI-128 shipped one and it says nothing about the fleet); the row count falling on its own (that means the rows aged out, not that they were recovered); or fixing the WHERE and leaving ORDER BY datetime(created_at) DESC in front of LIMIT 50, which reproduces the defect at the limit.

items.tier: 2 to fix (src/runtime/order_monitor.py, order path) — needs an operator OK
items.source: src/runtime/order_monitor.py:10633 _sweep_local_pnl_for_unpriced (broker-reader defer branch)
items.title: The _LOCAL_PNL_BROKER_DEFER_MS grace that stops local compute pre-empting fee-accurate broker truth is measured from created_at, so for any position held longer than the grace it is already spent at the moment of close
items.detail: FILED, NOT FIXED — outside the MI-128 approval, which scoped to the scan query only. THIRD instance of the same open-vs-close keying class in one function's neighbourhood, which is why it is filed rather than carried in a comment. MECHANISM: the branch reads created_ms = _isoformat_to_ms(row['created_at']) and defers a broker-reader account's row while (now - created_ms) < _LOCAL_PNL_BROKER_DEFER_MS (6h). The function's own docstring states the intent: 'This sweep only fills such a row once it is OLDER than that grace — i.e. the broker reader has had its window ... so we never pre-empt the fee-accurate number.' But the broker reader's window opens at the CLOSE — Bybit's closedPnl record does not exist until the position closes — so measuring the grace from the OPEN gives a row held longer than 6h ZERO defer window: it is eligible for local compute on the very first tick after it closes, before the Bybit sweep has had any chance to fetch broker truth. The code does the opposite of what its docstring says it does, in the direction that costs a MEASURED value. This is 'field beats comment' with the field being wrong. POPULATION (state it): same read as the sibling row — trade_journal.db::trades, all 5,494 rows fetched complete by pagination, 2026-09-05, live trader git_sha 9337958e. Closed non-backtest, non-intent_reduce Bybit rows with hold computable = 1,204; of those, 333 (27.7%) were held longer than the 6h grace, so more than a quarter of the Bybit book reaches its close with no defer window left. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and must not be asserted: how often the race is actually LOST is unmeasured. The Bybit sweep runs on the same tick and usually wins, which is why the observed damage is small rather than 333 rows. This row claims the GUARD IS INERT for 27.7% of the book, not that 27.7% of the book was mispriced. Establishing the second needs the sweep-order telemetry nobody has collected. MADE MORE REACHABLE BY MI-128: before it, a long-held row never reached this branch at all because the scan window excluded it first. Re-keying the window to the close is correct and is what exposes this.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) the defer grace is measured from COALESCE(closed_at, created_at) rather than created_at under a Tier-2 operator OK, with a test that a Bybit row held 30 days and closed 1 minute ago IS deferred (currently it is not) and one that a row closed 7 hours ago is NOT; OR (b) the operator records a decision that the grace is intended to be measured from the open, in which case the DOCSTRING must be corrected to say so, because the two currently contradict each other and the comment is the one being believed. NOT SUFFICIENT: reasoning that the Bybit sweep 'usually runs first' — that is an ordering assumption nothing enforces and no test pins; or measuring that few rows were harmed, which grades the outcome of a race rather than the presence of the guard.

items.tier: 3 to change (would write realised pnl onto historical money rows) — operator decision only
items.title: MI-128 is forward-only by operator condition, so 15 long-held closes remain pnl-NULL with NO pnl_source key permanently — recorded so the residual is tracked rather than rediscovered, NOT as a request to back-fill
items.detail: THIS ROW EXISTS TO BE KNOWN, NOT ACTED ON. The operator was put the back-fill question explicitly on 2026-09-05 and did NOT take it; MI-128's approval is approved_with_conditions, condition FORWARD-ONLY. Filing it is the alternative to a future session rediscovering these rows, reading them as a fresh defect, and back-filling them — which would exceed that approval. A session that finds this row should read the condition and leave the rows alone. POPULATION (state it): trade_journal.db::trades, all 5,494 rows fetched complete by pagination via /api/bot/db/table/trades (fetched == total_reported), 2026-09-05, live trader git_sha 9337958e. Non-backtest, status='closed', intent_reduce excluded, hold computable = 1,373. Of these, 20 were held > 14 days and are pnl-NULL carrying no pnl_source key. MI-128's re-keyed 14-day window reaches 5 of them (4169, 4170, 4422, 4423, 4484 — closes inside the window); the other 15 closed more than 14 days ago and are outside ANY 14-day window forever, so no amount of correct forward behaviour will ever reach them. THE CONSEQUENCE, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: each of these 15 is absent from /api/bot/performance, whose SQL carries AND t.pnl IS NOT NULL, so sunset_pass has no lifetime measurement for the legs they belong to. That is the chain MI-128's own diagnosis names: pnl NULL -> absent from performance -> no lifetime measurement -> a retirement basis built on an absence. MI-128 stops the chain being FED; it does not unwind the 15 rows already in it. Do not report MI-128 as having taken the historical silent count to zero — it takes it from 20 to 15, and only if the operator also accepts the 5-row back-fill at merge.
items.resolution_criteria: Closes on a RECORDED OPERATOR DECISION, either way, and on nothing else. EITHER (a) the operator decides these 15 rows are to be left as they are permanently — recorded as a decision, with the /api/bot/performance and sunset_pass consequence stated, so it does not read as work still in flight; OR (b) the operator authorises a bounded one-off pass that DECLARES them (writes pnl_source: unmeasured, unmeasured_reason naming this row) WITHOUT inventing a price — which is a different and much lower-evidence act than pricing them, and is the only variant worth proposing, since pricing a close this old has no anchor and would be FABRICATED by this repo's own definition. NOT SUFFICIENT, and each of these would be the failure this row exists to prevent: a session back-filling the rows on its own judgement; the count dropping because rows were deleted or their status changed; or MI-128 merging (that reaches the other 5 and none of these 15).

items.title: pnl_source and exit_price_source are not columns on trades — a reader that treats them as columns gets None and cannot tell 'no such field' from 'no provenance recorded'
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-05 while verifying #11037 on the fleet, and it very nearly produced a false escalation to the operator. docs/claude/work MI-128's verification read rows via /api/bot/db/table/trades and pulled pnl_source / exit_price_source with dict .get(). BOTH RETURNED None FOR EVERY ROW — not because provenance was absent, but because THEY ARE NOT COLUMNS. The trades table has 41 columns and the only one matching /source|prov/ is cost_source; the two provenance keys live inside the `notes` JSON blob (verified: notes.pnl_source = local_compute, notes.exit_price_source = verdict on row 4169). THE HARM IS PRECISELY THE COLLAPSED-STATE CLASS THIS REPO NAMES: a column read cannot distinguish 'this field does not exist here' from 'we recorded no provenance', and the second is the alarming one. A pre-deploy baseline was taken on that basis and measured NOTHING while reading as a clean observation of five silent-null rows. Then when the sweep wrote pnl=534.66, the same reader reported 'a pnl with no provenance key' — which was the pre-declared FAIL condition for a real-money-adjacent data defect. The escalation was stopped only by checking the column list first: cost_source printed and the other two did not, which is what a MISSING KEY looks like and not what a NULL VALUE looks like. ⚠️ NOTE THE ASYMMETRY THAT MAKES THIS WORTH FIXING RATHER THAN REMEMBERING: the failure is SILENT and biased toward alarm. Every row reads as unprovenanced, so a reader concludes the system is worse than it is, and the more carefully a session pre-declares a FAIL condition on 'no provenance key', the more surely it fires. src/runtime/provenance.py exists to answer this exact question and takes a ROW, so a caller that hand-rolls the field access bypasses the one module that knows where the keys live.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) the read surface exposes the two provenance keys such that a consumer cannot mistake absence for null — e.g. /api/bot/db/table/trades projects them as first-class fields, or the Data Explorer response carries an explicit marker that they are nested — demonstrated by a reader that distinguishes 'no such field' from 'recorded as null' on a real row; OR (b) a recorded decision that callers MUST route provenance questions through src/runtime/provenance.py::classify_pnl rather than reading fields, WITH that stated where a session doing fleet verification will actually see it (this session did not) — a rule that lives only in the module is not reachable by someone querying an HTTP route. NOT SUFFICIENT: this instance being understood, or a note in a checklist row — the next verifier queries the same route and gets the same nulls.

items.title: RECURRENCE: the automerge relay beats pr-opener on every Tier-1 PR — three instances in one night — and the workaround sessions reach for is closing and reopening the PR
items.detail: RECURRENCE of BL-20260905-AUTOMERGE-RELAY-WINS-THE-RACE-WITH-PR-OPENER-SO-EVERY-TIER-1-PR-GETS-A-BOILERPLATE-BODY, filed earlier the SAME NIGHT by MI-127. Filed as a recurrence rather than a duplicate because the earlier row recorded the race; what is new is the FREQUENCY and the WORKAROUND it induces. THREE INSTANCES, 2026-09-05, all within about four hours: (1) MI-127's original on its own PR; (2) the MANAGER's #11036, which the relay opened with the boilerplate body before pr-opener could run — body replaced by hand; (3) MI-125's #11044, opened by the relay with the LAST COMMIT'S SUBJECT as the title ('backlog: file the three MI-125 findings not fixed in this PR'), which understates a PR that also carries the R6 fix. Population: every Tier-1 PR opened by a 403'd session this night; the manager observed no instance where pr-opener won. ⚠️ THE NEW HARM IS THE WORKAROUND, NOT THE TITLE. MI-125's recorded next action was 'closing to reopen with correct title'. Closing and reopening a PR to fix cosmetics burns the PR number, detaches the existing review/CI history, and is one step from the close-and-reopen-to-kick-CI move CLAUDE.md forbids outright — a session that learns the manoeuvre for a title will reach for it under CI pressure. The manager retitled #11044 in place instead, which took one API call, and that is the point: the escape hatch a session reaches for is more expensive AND more dangerous than the fix, because the cheap fix (update_pull_request) is exactly what a 403'd session cannot call. ⚠️ SO THE DEFECT IS ASYMMETRIC BY CONSTRUCTION: the sessions that hit the race are precisely the ones that cannot repair it, and the only actor who can is the manager, who is not watching every PR opening.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) pr-opener wins the race, or the relay does not open a PR when a pr-request file is present for the same branch — demonstrated by a 403'd session opening a Tier-1 PR that lands with ITS OWN title and body, observed on a real PR and not in a test; OR (b) a recorded decision that the relay opening first is acceptable, WITH a stated repair path a 403'd session can actually execute — noting that update_pull_request is the obvious repair and is exactly what such a session cannot call, so 'the session fixes the title' is not a valid answer. ⚠️ EITHER WAY the resolution must say explicitly that closing and reopening a PR is NOT the sanctioned repair, because that is the behaviour currently being induced. NOT SUFFICIENT: retitling instances by hand as they occur, which is what happened twice tonight and is why this is a recurrence.

items.title: econ-calendar-produce opens a PR carrying REGENERATED derived registers, so an unmerged one turns into a 7-day rewind of main
items.detail: PR #10398 (opened 2026-08-29, still open 2026-09-05) changes 3 files: one NEW capture (comms/macro/econ_calendar_captures/US-20260829T034952Z.fxstreet.json, +61529 lines) and the TWO DERIVED registers econ_calendar_snapshots.jsonl and econ_calendar_upcoming.json. scripts/macro/econ_calendar_produce.py is a FULL REGEN over the whole captures dir (its own docstring: 're-running over the same captures reproduces the same log byte-for-byte'), so the two derived files a PR carries are a snapshot of the captures dir AT OPEN TIME. Every later scheduled run adds a capture to main, and the open PR's derived files go progressively staler while its diff still shows them as changes. MEASURED 2026-09-05 on #10398 (population = all 3 files, both sides, at origin/main c6e657f6 and PR head 2726b0f6): merging it whole would have DELETED 2863 (event_id,observed_at) pairs = 2950 rows across the 7 observed_at generations 2026-08-30..2026-09-05 from snapshots.jsonl, and rewound upcoming.json from generated_from_observed_at 2026-09-05T00:18:54Z / 429 events back to 2026-08-29T03:49:52Z / 380 events, losing 49 event_ids and the 5 forward dates 2026-09-14..2026-09-18. The capture itself is a PURE ADD (absent from main, byte-unique against all 39 captures on main) and is the ONLY irreplaceable artifact in the PR. So the automation reliably produces PRs that are unmergeable-as-a-whole after about a day while the one thing worth keeping is trivially takeable. VERIFIED the derived files are fully reconstructible: regenerating from main's 39 captures reproduces main's snapshots.jsonl AND upcoming.json BYTE-FOR-BYTE (blobs d92889ff and 4bb5403f), and a hold-one-out control correctly loses exactly the held generation. NOT FIXED HERE: this session dispositioned #10398 only (took the capture by value, regenerated). The workflow change touches .github/workflows/econ-calendar-produce.yml, out of scope for a Tier-1 data disposition.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) .github/workflows/econ-calendar-produce.yml commits ONLY the new capture and lets a separate regen step rebuild the two derived registers on main, so an econ-calendar PR can never carry a stale derived file -- verified by an econ-calendar PR whose changed-file list contains no econ_calendar_snapshots.jsonl and no econ_calendar_upcoming.json; OR (b) the workflow regenerates its open PR on every run, verified by an econ-calendar PR older than 24h whose upcoming.json generated_from_observed_at equals main's; OR (c) an operator decision to keep the current shape, RECORDED as a decision with the consequence stated -- that each econ-calendar PR must be dispositioned by hand within a day or become a take-by-value. A green CI run clears NONE of these: CI never compared the PR's derived files against main's newer ones, which is why #10398 sat for 7 days looking mergeable.
