items.title: pr-landing-guard's TIER1_SURFACE excludes automation/**, so using the board-post / pr-opener relays blocks self-landing and pushes sessions to delete their own audit trail
items.detail: The three relays CLAUDE.md names for a read-only GitHub MCP (board-post.yml, pr-opener.yml, claude-pr-automerge.yml) all work by committing files under automation/ -- the session writes automation/board-posts/<n>.md or automation/pr-requests/<n>.json, and the runner commits automation/board-results/<n>.txt or automation/pr-results/<n>.txt back to the SAME branch. scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py::TIER1_SURFACE is an allowlist of docs/**, tests/**, comms/**, .github/**, scripts/{ci,ops,research,reports}/**, *.md and the lint configs. automation/** is not in it, and the allowlist is fail-closed BY DESIGN ('a path it does not recognise is not thereby Tier-1'). So R5 refuses self-landing on ANY PR that used a relay -- state=undeclared -- however Tier-1 the rest of the diff is. MEASURED 2026-09-05 on PR #11047, a docs+comms+.github data disposition: guards read PASS 51 / FAIL 0 before the relays ran and PASS 50 / FAIL 1 after, the single failure naming automation/board-results/...txt and automation/pr-requests/...json -- files the session did not choose to add in the first case and had to add to open the PR at all in the second. THE PERVERSE INCENTIVE IS THE POINT: the only ways out are (a) set landing:hold, forfeiting the self-landing this repo built for exactly this population, or (b) git rm the relay's request AND receipt files so the net diff is clean -- which is what this session did, and which DELETES THE IN-REPO EVIDENCE that the MANDATORY coordination-board post happened. A guard whose cheapest satisfaction is erasing an audit trail is the 'cheaper to lie to than to satisfy' shape new-table-wiring-guard's presence-only marker is already recorded here for. The two board comments this session posted (issues/6927#issuecomment-5550557813 and #issuecomment-5550594906) are live on GitHub; only the local receipts were removed, and they survive solely because they are named in a commit message. RELATED BUT DIFFERENT from the automerge-relay race filed the same day (#11045): that is about WHEN the relay commits; this is about WHERE it commits and the guard surface not covering it. NOT FIXED HERE: the remedy is in scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py, outside a Tier-1 DATA disposition's scope, and changing a landing guard while using it to land my own PR is the wrong session for it.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) TIER1_SURFACE gains a NARROW entry for the relay bookkeeping paths only -- automation/board-posts/**, automation/board-results/**, automation/pr-requests/**, automation/pr-results/** -- and NOT automation/** wholesale (the rest of that tree is unexamined and the allowlist's fail-closed polarity is correct); verified by a PR carrying a board post AND a Tier-1 declaration passing check_pr_landing.py with state=declared_self_land, plus a self-test asserting some OTHER automation/ path still fails; OR (b) the relays write their request and result files somewhere already certifiable, or to a branch other than the working one, verified by a relay-using PR whose net diff contains no automation/ path; OR (c) an operator decision that relay-using PRs must always be human-landed, RECORDED as a decision with the consequence stated -- that every read-only-MCP session's PR needs a human, which is the population the relays exist to unblock. NOT SUFFICIENT: a session deleting its own relay files to get green. That is the current workaround and it is the defect, not the fix.
items.source: MI-131 disposition of PR #10398 (session_01J2tRr5LVT1Zer8MkjLVLYV), hit while landing PR #11047

items.title: stop-hook-git-check.sh reports a pushed branch as unpushed, and the cause is the SINGLE-BRANCH refspec, not shallowness — so `git fetch --unshallow` does NOT fix it
items.detail: REPRODUCED 2026-09-05 (MI-123 reported it; this is the independent verification). COMMAND: `echo '{"stop_hook_active":false}' | bash /root/.claude/stop-hook-git-check.sh`. CLONE: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/benbaichmankass/metis-insights`, depth measured at 2 commits reachable (`git rev-list --count HEAD`), `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` = true. STATE: working tree CLEAN and the branch genuinely PUSHED (`git ls-remote --heads origin <branch>` returns exactly the local HEAD sha). RESULT: exit 2, 'Branch <b> has 1 unpushed commit(s) and no remote branch. Please push these changes.' MECHANISM: `--depth 1` implies `--single-branch`, so remote.origin.fetch is '+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main'. `git push -u` therefore never creates refs/remotes/origin/<branch>; line 41's `git rev-parse origin/$current_branch` fails, the hook falls back to upstream=origin/HEAD, and origin/HEAD..HEAD counts the pushed commit as unpushed. || THE REPORTED CAUSE IS WRONG IN THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS. Isolating matrix, population = 4 clone shapes of one origin (main=5 commits), tree clean and feature/x pushed in ALL four: A full clone -> EXIT 0 (positive control, so a silent result here is not vacuous); B --depth 1 -> EXIT 2; C --single-branch at FULL depth, NOT shallow -> EXIT 2; D --depth 1 --no-single-branch, IS shallow -> EXIT 0. So the discriminating variable is the narrow refspec, and shallowness is neither necessary (C) nor sufficient (D). REMEDY MEASURED, both on the same fixture: `git fetch --unshallow` leaves it at EXIT 2 (shallow=false, full history, still firing); setting remote.origin.fetch='+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*' and fetching clears it to EXIT 0. This matters because --unshallow is the remedy a reader of the MI-123 wording would reach for, and it is the one that does not work. || NOT FIXABLE IN THIS REPO: the script is /root/.claude/stop-hook-git-check.sh (also at /home/claude/.claude/), harness-owned container config, NOT scripts/hooks/ — that directory does not exist here. Filed rather than fixed for that reason. || IMPACT: every sub-session container is a --depth 1 clone, so every sub-session that pushes a branch is told at Stop time to push work it has already pushed. The 2026-09-02 manager logged four firings in ~20 minutes and read them as being about a sub-agent's dirty tree; on this evidence the class also fires with a clean tree and nothing to do, which is the desensitised-alarm shape CLAUDE.md names as itself a P1.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER the hook resolves the remote branch without depending on refs/remotes (e.g. `git ls-remote --heads origin $current_branch`, or honouring branch.<name>.merge, which IS set correctly by `git push -u` even under a narrow refspec) and a --depth 1 clone with a pushed branch exits 0 while a genuinely unpushed commit still exits 2 — BOTH halves, since a hook that stops firing entirely is not fixed; OR the container widens remote.origin.fetch after clone and the same two-sided check passes. Escalate to Anthropic/harness owners: it cannot be fixed from this repo. A pass claimed without the second half (a real unpushed commit still caught) does not close this.

items.title: check_manager_scope R6/R7 grade every manager commit in the range, so a TRUE supervision lapse makes its PR unmergeable forever — the only exits are an exception (refused) or a branch rebuild (which has now twice caused collateral defects)
items.detail: NOT A REQUEST TO WEAKEN R6. The finding that motivated this was TRUE and the manager said so publicly. FILED BY MI-125 alongside the R6 wrong-parent fix, because the two are different facts and only the first was fixable inside this session's scope. || INCIDENT 2026-09-05: R6 killed PR #11031, the manager's own 32-commit management record. Commit bfdf2fa3 advanced the lease heartbeat while SESSIONS.json was 154 min stale against a 90-min TTL, because the manager had been idle 143 minutes and the lease had expired. The guard was CORRECT. || THE SHAPE: bfdf2fa3 was an ANCESTOR of the branch tip, so it sat permanently inside the graded range (merge-base..HEAD). The PR could never go green however many later commits fixed the state — there is no 'I have since fixed it' path, because R6 grades the commit that made the claim, not the branch's end state. The available exits were (a) docs/claude/work/manager-scope-exception.yaml, correctly REFUSED — it is for live INCIDENTS, and spending it on a manager's own lapse is the cheaper-to-lie-to-than-to-satisfy failure this repo already names; or (b) rebuild the branch from main, which is what happened, and which SILENTLY DROPPED three filed backlog rows and REWOUND five generated registers, both caught only afterwards. So a true finding cost a rebuild that caused two further defects. || THIS IS NOT THE WRONG-PARENT BUG AND IS NOT FIXED BY MI-125. That fix stops R6 grading a MERGE that advanced no heartbeat (measured: gap=160min on a commit whose heartbeat arrived along the second parent). bfdf2fa3 was an ordinary lease-only commit that really did advance the heartbeat over a stale registry, so it still fails, correctly, after the fix. Verified by keeping self-test case 7 (plain stale heartbeat -> R6 violation) green and adding 8g7, a merge that genuinely advances the heartbeat over a 240-min-stale registry, which must still FAIL. || THE OPEN QUESTION IS POLICY, NOT CODE, WHICH IS WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN DECIDED: is a permanently-unmergeable branch the intended consequence of a recorded lapse? A rule satisfiable only by discarding history is worth examining even when its finding is true. Candidate answers, none of them free: accept it and say so (then the rebuild procedure needs to stop losing filed rows and generated registers — that is the actual recurring harm, twice now); or let a later commit RECORD the lapse rather than erase it, which risks becoming an acknowledgement box that is cheaper to tick than to satisfy; or grade the range's END STATE for R6, which would let a manager launder a lapse behind a later heartbeat and is the weakening this row explicitly does not propose.
items.resolution_criteria: An OPERATOR DECISION recorded in docs/claude/work/** naming which of the three answers holds, WITH the consequence stated in the same place. If the answer is 'the behaviour is correct', the recorded consequence must say plainly that a manager lapse makes its PR permanently unmergeable and that the only remedy is a rebuild — AND a separate row must cover making the rebuild non-lossy, since dropping three backlog rows and rewinding five registers is the measured harm and it has now happened twice. Explicitly NOT sufficient: a code change that makes R6 stop grading historical commits, absent that decision — that is the weakening this row refuses. Explicitly NOT sufficient: this row being read and agreed with; it clears on a WRITTEN decision.

items.title: #10895's R7 face CLEARS when measured against #10895 itself, but the PR is blocked by a merge conflict and carries an unresolved R2 that main's guard now grades `unattributed`
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-05 against PR #10895 ITSELF (head 7a93261f, base main, --base origin/main), because the repo's own rule is that a guard passing elsewhere is not evidence about this PR. Range = 3 commits: 5504200c, 5244dafb (the manager merge of main into the worker branch — the MI-122 shape), 7a93261f. || R7 RESULT: CLEARS. Zero R7 failures AND zero R7 notes under all THREE guard versions — the guard in #10895's own tree (which does NOT contain a0b776fa, verified with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`), the guard on origin/main today (which does), and the MI-125-patched guard. R6 also passes on the merge ('R6 ok: 5244dafb registry 43min before heartbeat, ttl 90'). || BUT THE INFERENCE THAT a0b776fa IS WHAT CLEARED IT IS NOT SUPPORTED: R7 does not grade 5244dafb under the PRE-fix guard either, so the measurement cannot attribute the clearance to a0b776fa. State it as 'R7 does not fire', not as 'the fix cleared it'. || WHAT ACTUALLY BLOCKS IT, and neither is R7: (1) `mergeable_state: dirty` — a MERGE CONFLICT. `get_check_runs` returns total_count 0, which per CLAUDE.md is the conflict signature and not 'CI has not started'; NO CI has ever run on this PR. (2) Under its OWN guard the PR is an R2 VIOLATION: session_011JWFxuYAaEQKCFCmG6gnHJ, a lease holder, committed scripts/notify_on_pull.py and tests/test_notify_merge_pings.py in 5504200c — a manager doing an item. Under main's current guard that same commit instead grades UNATTRIBUTED, because the office-window check places that session out of office (in office 2026-09-01T14:43:23Z..2026-09-02T23:08:05Z; commit authored 2026-09-03T06:13:07Z). The guard says so itself: that is 'NOT a clean bill of health, and NOT an excuse either'. So the R2 question is unresolved, not answered — it moved from a failure to an unestablished attribution.
items.resolution_criteria: The R7-specific blocked edge on #10895 may be CUT, citing the measurement above rather than an inference from a0b776fa. The PR itself closes only when BOTH: (a) the merge conflict is resolved and CI actually RUNS on it (get_check_runs total_count > 0 — a zero count must never be read as green); and (b) the R2 question is dispositioned on its merits — either the manager's authorship of scripts/notify_on_pull.py + tests/ is routed to a worker session and the commits re-authored, or it is argued in docs/claude/work/manager-scope-exception.yaml. Explicitly NOT sufficient: the guard returning rc=0 because the commit grades `unattributed`, which is a coverage gap, not compliance.

items.title: One closed-unmerged PR with no `disposition` makes open_pr_record.py --strict refuse on EVERY reconcile PR, and the reconciler keeps opening more — five were stacked and unmergeable at once
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-05T10:47-11:00Z. POPULATION: all open PRs on benbaichmankass/Metis-Insights, n=9. FIVE of them were `automation/reconcile-open-prs-*` PRs (#11041 07:40Z, #11046 08:20Z, #11051 09:00Z, #11056 09:31Z, #11058 10:37Z), all editing docs/claude/work/OPEN-PRS.json. #11058's guards job read PASS 49 / FAIL 1, the single failure being `session-registry-guard: python3 scripts/ops/open_pr_record.py --strict exited 1`. REPRODUCED locally on that head: `settled=undispositioned` — `#10921: terminal is 'closed_unmerged' and there is no disposition`. || THE LOOP: the reconciler MOVES a no-longer-open PR into settled_prs, and it CANNOT supply a disposition, because a disposition answers WHY a human closed the PR — 'superseded', 'the operator refused it' and 'the author gave up' are opposite next actions and no automated reader can distinguish them. So every run reproduces the identical refusal, and each run ALSO opens a new PR. The stack is unbounded in the number of merges to main, not self-limiting. || WHY IT IS HIGH AND NOT LOW: the guard is correct and must not be weakened — it exists so a successor cannot read a verdict without its condition. The defect is that a manually-supplied field is a hard precondition for an AUTOMATED job's output to be mergeable, with no signal anywhere that the reason is owed until five PRs have already piled up. The blockage was silent for ~3h20m and was found only because the manager read a failing guard log while draining the queue. || WHAT IS NOT THE FIX: back-filling a disposition automatically (that manufactures a reason nobody gave — the absence-is-not-zero class), or relaxing --strict. Candidate fixes: (a) the reconciler REFUSES to move a row it cannot dispositon and says so loudly instead of emitting an unmergeable PR; (b) it closes its own superseded predecessors when it opens a new one; (c) a `disposition_owed` signal surfaced where a manager will see it before five PRs accumulate. || IMMEDIATE STATE: the #10921 disposition was recorded by hand on claude/manager-record-2026-09-05h and the five PRs are being closed as superseded. THAT CLEARS THE INSTANCE AND NOT THE MECHANISM — the next PR closed without merging reproduces it exactly.
items.resolution_criteria: A reconcile run is OBSERVED producing a mergeable PR in a repo state where a PR was closed unmerged and no disposition had yet been written — i.e. the automated job no longer depends on a hand-written field to be mergeable. Explicitly NOT sufficient: the #10921 instance being recorded (that is this row's own workaround), --strict being relaxed, or a disposition being auto-generated.
items.recurrence_20260906: RECURRED 2026-09-06, on a DIFFERENT closed PR — so this is the class repeating, not the 2026-09-05 instance still being unrecorded. MEASURED 19:05Z. The undispositioned row is now **#11105** (closed unmerged 2026-09-06T10:22:01Z, mergeable_state 'blocked'), not #10921. Reproduced by checking out the reconciler's own head ef3ef1ff and running the guard there: `settled=undispositioned — #11105: terminal is 'closed_unmerged' and there is no disposition`, over 46 settled rows. PR #11171's guards job fails on exactly `session-registry-guard: python3 scripts/ops/open_pr_record.py --strict exited 1`, with PASS 49 / FAIL 1 — the same shape and the same single failure as #11058 recorded above. ⚠️ THE STACK IS BACK TO THREE AND STILL GROWING: #11162 (16:56Z), #11170 (17:26Z), #11171 (18:43Z), all open, all editing OPEN-PRS.json, all red on this one guard. ⚠️ AND THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOW OBSERVABLE RATHER THAN THEORETICAL: because none of them can merge, `docs/claude/work/OPEN-PRS.json` on main STILL lists PR #11125 in `open_prs[]` — a PR that merged at 18:43:22Z as 9604b8a5. The register is stale in exactly the way its own `_doc` warns about, and the automation built to prevent that is the thing that cannot land. ⚠️ IT ALSO COSTS A SESSION THAT DEFERS TO THE AUTOMATION. Session_017UnyG4ArXmXKpB8rmEGv1j (MI-139b) hand-moved #11125 to settled_prs, then correctly backed that out on finding the reconciler owns the move by design — and the move then did not happen at all, because the reconciler is deadlocked. Deferring to an automation that cannot land is indistinguishable from doing nothing, and nothing in the register says the automation is stuck. The unblock is unchanged and is still a HUMAN JUDGEMENT: someone must write #11105's disposition. It is knowable — that row's own `blocker` field records manager-scope-guard R2 failing on two manager commits with a CLEAN RE-LAND as the route, and its headline finding (the Bybit close-qty defect) was routed onward and LANDED as #11125 — but writing it means asserting a close reason, which is precisely what this row says no automated reader may do.
items.recurrence_20260907: RECURRED A THIRD TIME, 2026-09-07, and this instance is the largest yet: FOUR undispositioned rows (#11260, #11273, #11277, #11280) blocking FOUR stacked auto-PRs (#11261, #11281, #11287, #11293). Population: measured 23:29Z, open_pr_record.py --strict printed `settled=undispositioned — 4 settled row(s) record an ending nobody accounted for, over 59 row(s)`, and all 4 of 4 auto-PRs open at that moment were red on session-registry-guard for that one reason. So 3 of 3 consecutive days: 09-05 (1 row, 5 stacked), 09-06 (#11105), 09-07 (4 rows, 4 stacked). ⚠️ WHAT MAKES THIS ONE DIAGNOSTIC RATHER THAN JUST ANOTHER TALLY: the manager who caused it had READ this row's own class earlier the same day and still did it, because the omission happens at the moment of CLOSING a PR — where the visible act (a comment on the PR) feels like the record and the durable act (the register field) is invisible and unprompted. The manager wrote a comment on each of the four and recorded nothing. That is the `reminder is not a mechanism` shape this repo has already paid for on MI-15 (twice) and BL-20260903-MANAGER-CHECKLIST-GOES-STALE-SILENTLY-AND-STATUS-REPORTS-IT-AS-CURRENT (⚠️ CLAUDE.md cites this id TRUNCATED, and I copied the truncation — artifact-validity-guard caught it. That mis-citation is itself already filed as BL-20260904-CLAUDE-MD-CITES-A-TRUNCATED-BACKLOG-ID-THAT-RESOLVES-TO-NOTHING, so this is that row recurring too: the canonical doc is still the source a session copies from). ⚠️ AND THE INSTANCE FIX IS NOT THE CLASS FIX: #11295 wrote the four missing dispositions, which unjams today and changes nothing about tomorrow. This row's own resolution_criteria is unchanged and still unmet — the automated job must stop DEPENDING on a hand-written field to be mergeable. Two shapes worth considering and neither is proposed here: have the reconciler write `disposition: "unrecorded — closed by <actor> at <ts>, reason not stated"` (a real fourth state, never a silent pass, so the guard keeps its teeth while the automation stops deadlocking), or refuse the CLOSE rather than the reconcile. NOT FIXED. Recorded by the manager session that caused it.

items.title: open_pr_record.py --strict reads open_prs[] and settled_prs[] independently, so the same PR can sit in BOTH and the guard still passes
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-05T11:02Z, and found by accident rather than by the guard. Rebasing a register fix onto a newer main left PR #11047 in open_prs[] AND settled_prs[] simultaneously: the branch had added it as settled while main still carried it as open, and git's auto-merge kept both. `--strict` then reported `structural=well_formed`, `decisions=graded` (3 rows) and `settled=settled_graded` (43 rows) and EXITED 0. || WHY IT MATTERS: 'open' and 'settled' are contradictory states, and this file is the ONE thing a manager arriving COLD reads to know what is in flight. A duplicated row means the same PR carries two possibly DIFFERENT operator_decision blocks, and nothing says which is current — the half-informed state the file's own _doc warns is worse than a missing row. The concurrent-edit shape that produces it (a branch settling a row while main still lists it open) is the NORMAL shape here, not an exotic one: it is what every reconcile PR does. || The guard already grades three orthogonal properties well. This is a fourth, cheap one: the intersection of the two id sets must be empty. It is the same class as the cross-check the completeness half already performs against a live open-PR list, applied WITHIN the file, where no network is needed.
items.resolution_criteria: open_pr_record.py --strict FAILS a register in which any `pr` appears in both open_prs[] and settled_prs[], demonstrated by a planted-defect case in its own self-test alongside a positive control that stays quiet. Explicitly NOT sufficient: the #11047 duplicate being deduped by hand, which is this row's own workaround.

items.title: A Routine-fired session carries a `cse_` id, not a `session_` id, and archive_session returns not-found for it — so SESSIONS.json and any reaper can neither name it nor reap it
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-05T10:40-10:53Z. A test fire of a manager-wake Routine produced session cse_01Aw2fCJHh6vnVdVRPAddUUB. Two things were then established, not assumed: (1) `archive_session` on that id returned `failed to archive session: the requested resource was not found`, while the same tool works on `session_*` ids from the same account; (2) the id shape differs from every one of the 110 rows in docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json, all of which are `session_*`. || WHY IT MATTERS: the whole registry design rests on a cold manager being able to enumerate and act on what its predecessor spawned, and the operating model's stated next step is a REAPER (a session that dies cannot close itself). A session class that cannot be named in the registry or archived through the tool is invisible to both. It is not hypothetical volume: a Routine at hourly cadence produces 24 such sessions a day, and the one measured here BLOCKED on a permission prompt and sat there — so the accumulating population is specifically the stuck ones. || STATE THE POPULATION HONESTLY: n=1 fired session, one archive attempt. It is not established whether `cse_` ids are unarchivable in general or whether this one was unreachable for another reason; that distinction is what this row owes. The Routine itself was DELETED, so nothing is accumulating right now.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) a Routine-fired session is successfully registered in SESSIONS.json and archived through the tool, naming the id form that worked; or (b) it is established that `cse_` sessions cannot be addressed by these tools at all, and that limitation is written into the reaper's design before the reaper is built. Explicitly NOT sufficient: no Routines currently existing — that is the absence of the trigger, not the absence of the gap.

items.title: The manager-wake Routine CAN be created by a session, and a test fire proved it does neither half: connectors are refused org-wide (no poke) and the fired session blocks on a permission prompt with no human (no receipt)
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-05T10:39-10:53Z by CREATING and TEST-FIRING it, after five sessions in a row asserted without testing that the Routine was 'owed to the operator'. That assertion was HALF WRONG and the testing is the only reason it is now known. || (1) CREATION: `create_trigger` with a `connectors` parameter is refused verbatim — 'the connectors parameter is not available for this organization. Omit the connectors parameter.' WITHOUT it, creation SUCCEEDS (trig_018AkCBVYcWGCXujNQVrZ92h, cron `39 * * * *`, create_new_session_on_fire). So a session CAN create the carrier; what it cannot do is grant it tools. The platform said so at creation: 'this trigger stores no MCP connectors, so the sessions it fires will run without connector (mcp__<server>__*) tools'. The deleted trigger's own record confirms it: `mcp_connections: []` AND `sources: []`. || (2) THE POKE HALF IS IMPOSSIBLE: step 2 of the prompt requires create_trigger + fire_trigger, which are mcp__* tools. Confirmed absent by construction, not guessed. || (3) THE DETECTOR HALF ALSO FAILS, and this is the part nobody predicted: the 10:40:01Z fire DID get a working repo (from the environment, despite `sources: []`) and DID run far enough to stage `.github/pr-automerge-requests/automation-manager-wake.txt` — then BLOCKED on a permission prompt for `git add` at 10:44:44Z and was still blocked, `connection_status: disconnected`, at 10:53Z. A Routine-fired session has no human to answer a prompt. VERIFIED IT LANDED NOTHING: no wake branch on origin (the only match, claude/mi123-manager-durable-wake, is from 2026-09-04T23:17Z), and no receipt on main. || CONSEQUENCE: at hourly cadence this produces 24 permanently-blocked sessions a day that record nothing — worse than no Routine, because a Routine that exists reads as covered. THE TRIGGER WAS THEREFORE DELETED 2026-09-05T10:56Z rather than left firing into nothing. || WHAT IS NOW KNOWN THAT WAS NOT: the blocker is TWO independent things, and only ONE needs the operator. The connector grant is theirs alone. The permission block is a prompt/environment problem a session could investigate.
items.resolution_criteria: A wake fire is OBSERVED completing end to end: its receipt reaches main, AND the run records either a real poke or an explicit `--outcome failed --detail "no poke tool in this session"`. The two halves clear SEPARATELY and must be reported separately: the DETECTOR half clears when a fired session lands a receipt on main without a human answering a prompt; the POKE half clears only when the operator grants the Claude Code Remote connector to the Routine, or records a decision NOT to — which is legitimate and must be recorded as a decision, with the consequence stated, rather than left looking like work in flight. Explicitly NOT sufficient: a Routine existing, or a fire that starts.

items.title: MI-15 recurrence #3: the manager spawned MI-129b and never registered it; the live census found it 3h41m later, and the miss was on a FOLLOW-UP spawn, which is where the soft coupling is weakest
items.detail: RECURRENCE, filed deliberately rather than folded into the existing rows, because the earlier fixes not holding IS the finding. MEASURED 2026-09-05T10:53Z. POPULATION: the 14 most recent sessions from list_sessions(mine=true), graded against the 110 rows of docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json. ONE was absent: session_01CmitsBjXiAJxcuxi3DRoXB (MI-129b), spawned by this manager at 07:12:12Z and unregistered for 3h41m. Backfilled. || PRIOR MEASUREMENTS: 3-of-6 absent on 2026-09-01 (MI-15, remedy recorded as 'remember to register'); 6-of-9 then 26-of-55 on 2026-09-02. This is 1-of-14. The RATE improved; the mechanism did not change. || THE NEW INFORMATION IS *WHICH* SPAWN WAS MISSED, and it sharpens the diagnosis rather than repeating it. The repo's own README concedes the coupling is soft: `register` is placed on the path to THE SPAWN PROMPT, because the repo does not own create_session and has no interposition point. That works when a prompt is being written from scratch. MI-129b was a FOLLOW-UP spawn — a second session on an item whose prompt already existed — so the manager reused prior text and never passed the point where registering happens. Every remaining miss will have this shape, because the from-scratch case is the only one the coupling covers. || The offline detector cannot see it either: session-registry-guard cross-checks MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json owners against the registry, and MI-129b's item (MI-129) was ALREADY owned by the first session, so the checklist showed an owner and the guard stayed quiet. A second session on an already-owned item is invisible to the one enforcement that runs on every PR.
items.resolution_criteria: A follow-up spawn onto an already-owned checklist item is either registered without the manager choosing to, or is DETECTED — by the offline guard learning that one checklist item may map to more than one live session, or by handoff_check grading `unknown` on that specific shape. Explicitly NOT sufficient: the MI-129b backfill (this row's own workaround), a lower miss rate in a later census, or another restatement of 'remember to register' — that remedy has now failed three times and a fourth statement of it is the reminder-is-not-a-mechanism non-fix this repo has already paid for.

items.title: backlog_append's duplicate probe searches the three backlogs and NOT docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json, so a manager can re-diagnose a live checklist item at full cost and the tool stays quiet
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-05T11:00-11:06Z, on myself. I diagnosed the reconcile-open-prs deadlock from scratch — read a failing guards log, reproduced open_pr_record.py --strict on the PR head, traced the loop — and filed BL-20260905-AN-UNDISPOSITIONED-CLOSED-PR-DEADLOCKS-EVERY-RECONCILE-PR-AND-THEY-STACK-UNBOUNDEDLY. append_row accepted it with no similarity warning. It was ALREADY on the checklist as MI-103 ('The reconcile-open-prs generator is jammed on ONE missing fact, and it emits a new PR on every merge'), measured 2026-09-03, same guard, same line, different PR. I found MI-103 only because I read the checklist afterwards to write a status update. || WHY THE PROBE MISSED IT: append_row's token-overlap search covers health-review / performance-review / ml-review backlogs. MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json is not in that set. The checklist is where IN-FLIGHT work lives, so it is precisely the file whose contents a session is most likely to re-derive — the backlogs hold what is NOT being worked, the checklist holds what IS. The probe covers the cold set and not the hot one. || COST HERE: a full re-diagnosis. The recurrence turned out to be genuinely worth filing (MI-103 was `landed_unproven` and this proves it regenerates — instance 1 #10780 2026-09-03 closed 8 stacked PRs, instance 2 #10921 today closed 5, same per-instance workaround both times), so the OUTPUT was not wasted. That is luck, not design: had the row been a plain duplicate it would have entered the backlog as new knowledge and split the record for MI-103 across two files. || ⚠️ STATE THE POPULATION: n=1 observation, mine. It is not established how often this happens — that would need the existing rows graded against the checklist, which nobody has done.
items.resolution_criteria: backlog_append's duplicate probe reads docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json alongside the three backlogs and surfaces a matching checklist item as a candidate, demonstrated by a case where a row restating a live checklist item is flagged AND a positive control that stays quiet. Explicitly NOT sufficient: the MI-103 cross-reference added by hand today, which is this row's own workaround; and NOT a one-off audit of existing rows, which measures the backlog rather than arming the probe.

items.title: The committed registers under docs/claude/ each use a DIFFERENT JSON serialization, and only the three backlogs have a writer that round-trips — so any other register reformats wholesale on a naive read-modify-write
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-05T10:55-11:12Z, by hitting it twice in seventeen minutes. SESSIONS.json and OPEN-PRS.json round-trip at json.dumps(indent=2, ensure_ascii=False). OPEN-ITEMS.json does NOT round-trip at ANY tested setting: indent 1/2/3/4 x ensure_ascii True/False x trailing-newline on/off, plus explicit separators, were all tried and none reproduced the file byte-for-byte — its top level is 1-space indented while item keys are 2-space, i.e. it is not json.dumps output at all and has been hand-edited. || COST, both caught by `git diff --stat` and not by any guard: writing SESSIONS.json at indent=1 produced a 3,518-line diff on a 13-row change; writing OPEN-ITEMS.json at indent=2 produced 2,276 lines on a 1-row change. Both were reverted and redone (the second as a byte-level patch scoped to one item, 3 insertions / 2 deletions). || WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: a whole-file reformat re-attributes every line to the committing PR, buries the actual change, and makes any concurrent edit to the same register a guaranteed conflict — which is the register-serialisation failure already recorded as MI-20-REGISTER-PRS-SERIALIZE-BADLY-UNDER-A-FAST-MERGE-QUEUE. It also defeats the row-aware merge driver, whose whole premise is that unrelated rows are untouched. The backlogs are protected by scripts/ops/backlog_append.py, which exists for exactly this reason; every OTHER register has the same hazard and no such writer. || THE HAZARD IS DIRECTIONAL: the naive write SUCCEEDS and its damage is visible only in the diff size, so it is caught by a human noticing a number, not by CI.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) a shared writer exists that round-trips each committed register under docs/claude/ byte-for-byte on a no-op edit, covering at least OPEN-ITEMS.json / SESSIONS.json / OPEN-PRS.json / MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json / MERGE-QUEUE.json, demonstrated by a test that writes an unchanged file and asserts a zero-byte diff; or (b) the registers are normalised to one serialization AND a CI check fails a PR whose diff to a register exceeds the rows it actually changed. Explicitly NOT sufficient: documenting the per-file indent somewhere, which is the reminder-is-not-a-mechanism non-fix.

items.title: A reconcile-open-prs PR cut BEFORE a disposition lands carries that row with a BLANK disposition, and merging it silently erases the recorded reason — with row counts identical to main, so nothing about the diff looks stale
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-05T11:41Z on PR #11063. This is a SECOND and more dangerous failure mode of MI-103 than the one that item was filed for; the known mode is 'the reconciler emits unmergeable PRs'. POPULATION: #11063's docs/claude/work/OPEN-PRS.json vs origin/main after #11062 landed the #10921 disposition at 11:39Z. BOTH read open_prs [10895, 10398] and settled_prs 43 — IDENTICAL COUNTS — but #11063's #10921 row carries disposition '' while main's carries the recorded reason. #11063 was cut 11:17:47Z, 22 minutes before the fix. || WHY IT IS HIGH: merging it would have overwritten a recorded reason with an empty one, silently undoing the repair and re-jamming open_pr_record.py --strict on the next run — and the ordinary review heuristics do not catch it. Row counts match. The file is a generated register, so a reviewer expects churn. The PR title is the same as every other reconcile PR. The ONLY signal is reading the disposition field of the specific row, which nobody does by hand. || THE GENERAL SHAPE, which is worth more than this instance: any generated register PR cut before a HAND-SUPPLIED field is written will, on merge, revert that field while looking like a no-op. The reconciler is a full recompute from GitHub plus a carry-forward of existing rows; it carries forward what was on main WHEN IT RAN, and a field added after that point is invisible to it. || ⚠️ NOT FIXED BY CLOSING #11063 (done, with the reason posted). The next disposition written by hand has exactly the same exposure to any reconcile PR already open.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) the reconciler refuses to emit, or CI refuses to merge, a register PR whose base has changed a hand-supplied field the PR would blank — demonstrated by a planted case where a PR cut before a disposition lands is caught, alongside a positive control that stays quiet; or (b) the reconciler re-reads the current main at merge time rather than at generation time. Explicitly NOT sufficient: closing #11063, which is this row's own workaround; and NOT a documented instruction to check the field by hand, which is the reminder-is-not-a-mechanism non-fix — the whole finding is that the diff gives a reviewer nothing to notice.

items.title: handoff_check's lease check can never pass after a release, releasing is the correct final act, and the tool's own advice ('fix them, then re-run') reduces to 're-claim a lease to turn a check green'
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-05T12:01Z on myself. handoff_check.py graded readiness=not_ready with SEVEN of eight checks passing and the only FAIL being `lease: you do not hold the lease (state=released)`. I had released at 11:55:16Z, which is the correct final act of a deliberate step-down -- it lets a successor claim immediately instead of waiting out the 90-minute TTL. || THE ORDER IS hold -> check -> release AND NOTHING ENFORCES OR STATES IT. Releasing is naturally the LAST thing a manager does, so the natural sequence produces a red. The failure text then says 'DO NOT hand over yet -- the FAILING checks above name what a successor would lose. Fix them, then re-run.' For this one check, 'fix it' reduces to RE-CLAIM THE LEASE, run the check, and release again -- claiming a lease for the sole purpose of turning a check green. That is the 'cheaper to game than to satisfy' shape this repo names elsewhere (new-table-wiring-guard's presence-only marker), arrived at from the opposite direction: not a guard that is easy to lie to, but advice that recommends the lie. || ⚠️ SEVERITY IS LOW AND DELIBERATELY SO: the check is CORRECT -- a handover of something you do not hold is not a handover -- and the seven checks that measure actual LOSS all passed. Nothing was lost. This is about the incentive and the missing statement of order, not about a wrong verdict. ⚠️ AND THE COMPOSITE VERDICT IS THE PART THAT MISLEADS: `not_ready` reads identically whether a successor would lose live sub-sessions or whether the outgoing manager simply stepped down in the wrong order, and those are opposite situations.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) handoff_check distinguishes 'lease released BY YOU, everything else passes' from 'lease held by someone else / expired' -- a third state, reported as a clean step-down rather than folded into the same not_ready as a real loss; or (b) the tool states the required order (hold -> check -> release) in its own output and docstring so the natural sequence does not produce a red. Explicitly NOT sufficient: removing the lease check (it is correct), or a session re-claiming a lease to pass it, which is the behaviour this row exists to name.

items.title: A sub-session's post_turn_summary freezes at its last turn, so a session whose PR merged afterwards still reads `need_input` / `CI running` — three of three idle sessions were stale this way at close-out
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-05T12:35Z at session close-out. POPULATION: the three sub-sessions still IDLE (not archived) at wrap-up; ALL THREE carried a stale status line, 3 of 3. || MI-113 read status_category `need_input`, status_detail 'PR blocked on human merge + pytest-run stall', and three explicit needs_action items — EIGHT HOURS after #11024 merged and with all three asks resolved (the work object it asked about exists on main; its merge=union driver is in .gitattributes on main). MI-131 read 'PR #11047 CI running (~30 min); auto-merge armed' when #11047 had merged at 08:55:06Z. MI-125 read `completed` and was accurate. || WHY IT MATTERS: post_turn_summary is what a session LAST SAID, and a manager reads it as CURRENT STATE. The failure is directional and expensive both ways — a finished session reads as blocked (so a manager burns a slot re-checking, or worse spawns a replacement), and a session that died mid-work reads as whatever it last claimed, which may be optimistic. I nearly left MI-113 open as a genuine blocker on the strength of its own line; what settled it was checking main. || THE RULE THAT ACTUALLY WORKS, and it cost a separate mistake earlier the same day to learn: JUDGE A SESSION BY ITS MERGED OUTPUT, NEVER BY ITS STATUS LINE. On 2026-09-05 I also judged MI-129 as 'drifting' from a task_summary reading 'refactoring eligibility filters' when that refactor WAS the approved work. Same class, opposite direction. || ⚠️ THIS IS MI-84 SEEN FROM THE SESSION SIDE. MI-84 records 'SESSIONS.json says working for every session forever'; the registry is stale because the SOURCE is stale, so fixing the registry's writer alone does not fix this.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) a session's state is DERIVED at read time from an observation that cannot go stale — its PR states and merged output — rather than from post_turn_summary, so a manager cannot read a frozen claim as current; or (b) handoff_check / manager_view grades a session whose status line contradicts its merged PRs as `stale_status`, a distinct state from both `working` and `done`. Explicitly NOT sufficient: archiving these three (this row's own workaround), or an instruction to 'check main before believing a status line' — that is the reminder-is-not-a-mechanism non-fix, and I followed it correctly here only because I had already been burned by it once today.

items.title: MI-84 measured: 65 of 94 registry rows carried a state the platform contradicts, 58 had never been observed once, and the register claimed 41 sessions working/idle/running while exactly ONE session was running account-wide
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-05T14:35Z against platform truth — list_sessions(mine=true, limit=100) — rather than asserted. POPULATION: the 110 rows of docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json, of which 94 appear in that page; 0 non-terminal rows fell outside it, so coverage of the claim is complete. RESULT: 65 of 94 rows (69.1%) carried a `state` the platform contradicts, and 58 of those had NO `last_observed` block at all — spawned 2026-09-02/03 and never looked at once. || THE HEADLINE NUMBER: the register claimed 41 sessions were `working` / `idle` / `running`. THE PLATFORM REPORTS EXACTLY ONE RUNNING SESSION ACROSS THE ENTIRE ACCOUNT, and it is the manager itself. Every other session is IDLE or ARCHIVED. One register row read `running` (session_018ruZdgEkPZ1XceWzLwuYUU); the platform reports it IDLE. || ROOT CAUSE, which MI-84 names and this quantifies: `working` is what a manager wrote at SPAWN time. Nothing ever revisits it. It was never a measurement, so it cannot decay — it was wrong the moment the session stopped, and it stays wrong forever. That is why 58 rows have never been observed: observing was always a separate, optional act that no mechanism forces. || WHY HIGH: SESSIONS.json is the ONE artefact a manager arriving COLD reads to inherit its predecessor's sub-sessions, and it is the input to the reaper the operating model plans to build. A reaper driven by this file would have believed 41 sessions were live. The register's own README calls a false blocker worse than a missing one; a false LIVE session is the same shape. || ⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH, stated because the clean state column now invites the wrong conclusion: an IDLE session is NOT a finished one. These rows are now honest about LIFECYCLE and say NOTHING about whether each session's deliverable reached main. That audit spans several previous managers' days and was not done. || ⚠️ RE-MEASURED 2026-09-08T03:31Z AND THE PREDICTION IN THIS ROW'S OWN resolution_criteria HELD — that is the finding, not the numbers. The criteria already said the 2026-09-05 re-grade was 'NOT sufficient … and will be stale again within a day'. Three days later, POPULATION: the 17 rows reading `working` on origin/main at 3891f5d8, graded against list_sessions(mine=true, limit=40) (40 returned, 15 of the 17 covered) plus a direct get_session on the 2 outside that window. RESULT: 7 ARCHIVED, 10 IDLE, 0 RUNNING — 17 of 17 wrong, i.e. 100% of `working` rows, against 69.1% of ALL rows on 2026-09-05. The cohort is entirely NEW (the 2026-09-06/08 spawns), so this is not the same rows going unfixed: the defect REPRODUCES on every fresh cohort at the rate this row predicts. A second one-off re-grade was applied on 2026-09-08 (MI-178) and is expected to be stale again on the same schedule; it is recorded as a workaround, NOT as progress on this row. || ONE THING THE 2026-09-05 MEASUREMENT DID NOT SAY, worth adding because it bounds the fix: the grade needs a list_sessions observation, which is an mcp__* tool CI DOES NOT HOLD — the same reason handoff_check.py grades `unknown` rather than `ready` without one. So the 'derive at read time' half of the criteria cannot be met by a CI guard as stated. What CAN be graded offline is STALENESS rather than truth: a `working` row whose spawned_at is older than any plausible session lifetime is a claim nobody has re-checked, and grading THAT `unknown` satisfies this row's second clause without needing platform truth in CI.
items.resolution_criteria: Session state is DERIVED at read time from a live observation rather than stored from spawn time — so a stale value cannot exist — or a mechanism forces the observation and grades a row carrying a state older than a stated window as `unknown`, never as its last written value. Demonstrated by a case where a session that stopped without anyone looking is NOT reported as working. Explicitly NOT sufficient: this one-off re-grade, which is this row's own workaround and will be stale again within a day; and NOT an instruction to re-observe, which is the reminder-is-not-a-mechanism non-fix that MI-15 has already failed three times.

items.title: Operator directive: no session works without ownership. Measured the same day — of 79 idle sessions ZERO have a live owner, 76 are orphaned, 2 are not in the registry at all, and 32 name neither a checklist item nor a work object
items.detail: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-09-05, verbatim: 'no sessions working on their own without ownership. That should not happen in any case.' MEASURED THE SAME DAY against platform truth (list_sessions(mine=true, limit=100)) joined to docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json. POPULATION: the 79 sessions the platform reports IDLE. Every figure is a count: ZERO have an owner session currently RUNNING; 76 ORPHANED (spawned_by is itself idle/archived/dead); 1 records no spawned_by; 2 are absent from the registry entirely; 32 are registered but name NEITHER checklist_item NOR owns_object. The only RUNNING session account-wide was the manager. || WHY HIGH, and it is not tidiness: ownership is what makes work RECOVERABLE. An orphaned session's deliverable either reached main or did not, and with no owner — and for 32 of them no named item — nobody is accountable for finding out. That is precisely the loss the session registry exists to prevent, at a scale nobody had measured. || ⚠️ ENFORCEMENT CANNOT SIT ON TOP OF THE CURRENT REGISTER: before the same-day re-grade, 65 of 94 rows carried a state the platform contradicts and 58 had never been observed once (BL-20260905-THE-SESSION-REGISTRY-WAS-WRONG-ON-69-PERCENT-OF-STATES-AND-58-ROWS-HAD-NEVER-BEEN-OBSERVED-ONCE). Ownership derived from a store 69% wrong about state inherits the lie. Derive it at READ time from a live join — the same fix `state` needs — rather than storing it at spawn. || ⚠️ THE TWO UNREGISTERED SESSIONS ARE THE WORST CASE and are worth separating: a session with no row cannot be owned, cannot be reaped, and cannot even be counted. They were found only because the platform listing was joined against the register; no repo-side check could have seen them.
items.resolution_criteria: All three, and none substitutes for another: (a) a mechanism grades every non-terminal session against a LIVE observation and reports any whose owner is not a running session, demonstrated by a planted orphan caught alongside a positive control that stays quiet; (b) ownership is DERIVED at read time, never stored at spawn, so it cannot go stale as `state` did; (c) the 79 existing orphans are dispositioned — each claimed by a live owner, or closed with its deliverable's fate stated. ⚠️ NOT sufficient: archiving the 79 (resolves lifecycle only — an idle session is not a finished one); a documented rule that managers must check ownership (the reminder-is-not-a-mechanism non-fix MI-15 has failed three times); or a one-off re-grade, which is stale the moment it is written.

items.title: alpaca_live's routed real-money leg cannot place an order: both declared gates read live, yet every signal since the 2026-08-31 routing is journalled 'dry_run_no_order_placed'
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by session_01UaZ9boMDajiCZsjVkr4Fnz during the Phase 1A observation sweep. POPULATION: GET /api/bot/db/table/trades filtered account_id=alpaca_live (filter_state 'applied'), 337 rows spanning 2026-06-25..2026-09-03. Status census: rejected 331, exchange_rejected 5, closed 1. || THE FINDING. Exactly TWO rows exist on or after 2026-08-31, both tlt_pullback_1h (2026-09-01T16:05:36Z, 2026-09-03T13:30:33Z), both status 'rejected', and BOTH carry entry_reason 'REJECTED: dry_run_no_order_placed | tlt_pullback_1h signal'. That token is emitted ONLY under _genuinely_dry (src/units/accounts/execute.py:336 and :457), which per the comment at lines 327-335 means the account mode is dry_run OR the strategy execution is shadow -- and it is deliberately distinct from 'exchange_client_unavailable_no_order_placed', so this is not a wedged-client path. || YET BOTH DECLARED GATES READ LIVE. config/accounts.yaml on origin/main has alpaca_live mode: live, unchanged across the last two commits to touch that file including the routing commit a8a045a ('alpaca_live: route the first real-money leg, with the T+1 gate armed first', #10633, 2026-09-01T01:40:09Z). config/strategies.yaml AND the LIVE /api/bot/config readback both have tlt_pullback_1h execution: live. So at both signal times the RUNNING trader folded dry while every declared surface said live. || TWO CANDIDATE CAUSES, NOT SEPARATED FROM A READ-ONLY SURFACE: (i) the running process held pre-a8a045a config, or (ii) a third term in the effective_dry fold. A declared-vs-running config lag is demonstrably possible on this fleet RIGHT NOW: /api/diag/version at 2026-09-06T08:51:56Z reads git_sha 4ec87e38 against git_sha_on_disk c2e47af5 with restart_pending true, and ict-git-sync.service reads 'inactive' on /api/diag/services. || WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE LEG: OI-20260831-ALPACA-LIVE-FIRST-REAL-MONEY-LEG-ROUTED-BUT-HAS-NEVER-TRADED is waiting for a fill that a dry fold can never produce, so that row cannot clear by the passage of time and the operator's Tier-3 approval to route real money has produced no live capability. Also note the single closed alpaca_live row (id 3119, IEF, 2026-07-02, pnl -0.435) carries pnl_source AND exit_price_source both NULL -- UNVERIFIED provenance.
items.resolution_criteria: Establish WHICH term folded dry: read PROP/effective_dry inputs on the RUNNING process (a get-env read of the account mode against /proc/<MainPID>/environ plus the process's loaded accounts.yaml), not the repo copy. Then EITHER the running config is stale, in which case the fix is the deploy/restart path and the finding is that ict-git-sync left a Tier-3-approved routing unapplied for 5+ days; OR a third dry-fold term exists, in which case name it and cover it with a test. Closed when a tlt_pullback_1h signal on alpaca_live is journalled with a status other than 'rejected', or when the operator records a decision that the account stays dry.

updates.note:
MI-200 (session 01CvFCybCkvrfzaHqNH3tQsb), measured 2026-09-08 12:16-13:10Z. I REPRODUCED THIS ROW INDEPENDENTLY and then ELIMINATED TWO FURTHER CANDIDATES and NARROWED A THIRD. Nothing here contradicts the row; it removes wrong branches so the next session does not re-walk them.

REPRODUCED: the same two rows (5306 @ 2026-09-01T16:05:36Z conf 0.5268; 5415 @ 2026-09-03T13:30:33Z conf 0.7162), both status 'rejected', and I read the `notes` JSON directly rather than entry_reason: both carry {"is_dry": true, "reason": "dry_run_no_order_placed"}. ⚠️ NOTE THE POLARITY FLIP AGAINST THE OLDER ROWS, which is worth having on the record: the four PRE-routing rows (5135/5139/5145/5188, 2026-08-27/28) carry is_dry FALSE with reason 'account_mode_dry_run'. So the two post-routing refusals are not a continuation of the pre-routing state — the recorded shape CHANGED at the routing.

ELIMINATED (1) — THE DOCUMENTED THIRD GATE IS NOT IT. coordinator.py:1322 consults `account_state_dry_run()` (src/runtime/orders.py:34), the M2 belt-and-suspenders override that can force an account dry regardless of accounts.yaml and is NOT surfaced on /api/bot/config. It was my leading hypothesis. It is refuted: config/account_state.yaml on origin/main declares only bybit_1 and bybit_2, so for alpaca_live the accessor returns None (absent account -> None) and the branch is a no-op. Read the file, not the code path.

ELIMINATED (2) — CREDENTIALS / `configured=False` IS NOT IT. load_accounts marks an account configured=False when resolve_credentials() fails (src/units/accounts/__init__.py:97-118), and such an account 'still loads' while refusing live actions. NARROWED (3) — THE STALE-CONFIG BRANCH NOW HAS TO EXPLAIN SOMETHING AWKWARD. This row's candidate (i) is that the running process held pre-a8a045a6 config. But BOTH facts come from the SAME FILE read by the SAME per-call loader: `Coordinator.multi_account_execute` calls `load_accounts(path)` fresh on every invocation and the module states it is 'stateless per-call' (the mechanism OI-20260906's observation established when it found the routing gate binds at DISK SYNC, not at process restart). items.title: /api/diag/log_file is tail-only with a hard 1000-line cap and no offset, which makes every 'N distinct UTC days of soak' criterion unsatisfiable through the instrument those rows point at
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by session_01UaZ9boMDajiCZsjVkr4Fnz during the Phase 1A observation sweep. Read from source: src/web/api/routers/diag.py lines 1779-1811. get_log_file takes only (name, lines); lines is clamped by _clamp(lines, _DEFAULT_LIMIT, _MAX_LIMIT) with _MAX_LIMIT = 1000; the body returns content[-n:]. There is no offset, no since, no cursor, and no head. || CONSEQUENCE, measured on a real row. OI-20260902-BYBIT-COVERAGE-BASIS-MERGED-WITH-ARMING-DELIBERATELY-HELD-FOR-A-SOAK clears only when the soak holds at least 20 graded rows SPANNING AT LEAST 3 DISTINCT UTC DAYS. bybit_coverage_soak.jsonl is 14,015,755 bytes, and its last 1000 lines cover 2026-09-06T05:17:29Z..08:52:12Z -- THREE HOURS AND THIRTY-FIVE MINUTES, one UTC day. At this soak's write rate the readable window can NEVER exceed a single day however long the soak runs, so the multi-day clause cannot be checked through the route the row itself names. The same limit applies to arbitration_fanout_soak (339 rows readable of a 363,337-byte file) and to every other high-rate soak. || THIS IS NOT A REQUEST TO RAISE THE CAP. A bigger tail moves the boundary and does not remove it, and an unbounded read on a 14 MB file from the live web-api is its own hazard. The fix that matches this repo's existing shape is a BOUNDED RECEIPT, as work_digest_receipt.json and PR-QUEUE-WATCH.json already do.
items.resolution_criteria: Have each high-rate soak writer maintain a small rolling summary at its own allowlisted log_file name -- distinct UTC days seen, total graded rows, count of the row-level condition the criterion cares about (e.g. verdicts_differ true), first and last timestamp -- and re-word the affected OPEN-ITEMS criteria to grade off that receipt rather than off a tail the instrument cannot serve. items.title: ict_scalp_mgc_15m 'no candle data' accounts for 87 of 184 operator-visible ERROR+ rows -- the alarm-fatigue shape the repo has already paid for twice

It is the single largest line in the feed by a wide margin -- the next is 16 rows of 'api_call bybit_place_order_failed: The number of contracts exceeds ...'. || WHY THIS IS FILED AS ITS OWN DEFECT rather than as a note. CLAUDE.md's standing rule is explicit that a desensitised alarm is ITSELF a P1 bug, and names the precedent: the trainer dataset audit degenerated to 62/86 manifests alarming and the ETH-xa dead-feature bug soaked for weeks inside that noise. The same shape is present here at 47%. It also directly degrades the rows this sweep depends on: OI-20260826-MHG-OVER-COVER-MECHANISM-UNVERIFIED clears by FINDING a page in this exact feed, and half the feed is one repeating builder exception. || Note the two candidate causes are different and were not separated: either ict_scalp_mgc_15m is requesting a contract/timeframe that has no data (a config or roll problem, in which case the leg is dead and should be shadowed or fixed), or the fetch is failing transiently and being logged at ERROR when it should be a WARNING with a latch. Then either fix/shadow the leg, or downgrade the repeated fetch failure to a latched WARNING so one persistent condition costs one page rather than 87. items.title: board-post.yml's result-file idempotency does not hold across two pushes in quick succession — I duplicated a board comment this way and am filing my own mistake
items.detail: OBSERVED 2026-09-06 by session_01UaZ9boMDajiCZsjVkr4Fnz, and it is MY OWN error, filed because the next session will hit it identically. || WHAT HAPPENED. I pushed automation/board-posts/observation-sweep-1a-start-20260906.md; the relay ran and posted issue #6927 comment 5558305147 at 09:23:06Z. Roughly eight minutes later I pushed a SECOND, different board post (the manager report) in a new commit. That push re-triggered the workflow, which re-processed the FIRST file as well -- because its result file automation/board-results/observation-sweep-1a-start-20260906.txt had not yet been committed back -- and posted comment 5558345078 at 09:31:23Z, byte-identical to 5558305147. The board now carries the same START twice. || WHY THE STATED GUARD DID NOT HOLD. board-post.yml's own header says 'IDEMPOTENCY IS THE RESULT FILE, NOT DELETION OF THE REQUEST', and that is true for a re-run after the result lands. It is NOT true for a re-run that starts BEFORE the result commit lands, which is exactly what a second push a few minutes later produces. The result commit is also deliberately made with [skip ci] and is a separate commit, so there is a real window -- roughly the duration of one relay run -- in which the request file exists with no result file beside it and any new push into automation/board-posts/** re-posts every such request. The workflow's `concurrency` setting did not prevent it: the second run was not cancelled, it queued and then re-processed. || IMPACT IS LOW BUT NOT ZERO. A duplicated board comment is noise on a surface whose whole value is that sessions read it; the board is already 2000+ comments and this repo has a documented alarm-fatigue problem. It is also self-inflicted noise from the mechanism that exists to make coordination cheap. || THE SAME WINDOW EXISTS IN pr-opener.yml, which uses the identical result-file pattern -- there it is masked because GitHub refuses a second PR for an existing head branch (I saw exactly that FAILED-already-exists result), so the duplicate surfaces as an error rather than a duplicate artifact.
items.resolution_criteria: Make the relay skip a request whose comment it has already posted without depending on the result commit having landed -- e.g. write the result file in the SAME commit as nothing else and push it before posting the next request, or have the workflow scan recent board comments for a marker it embeds in each post (a request-name fingerprint) and skip on a match. Closed when two pushes to automation/board-posts/** inside one run's duration are shown to produce exactly one comment per request file. Cheap alternative if that is judged not worth it: RECORD the limitation in the workflow header so a session knows to wait for the result file before pushing again -- but note this repo's own rules say a documented gotcha is not a mechanism, and this is the second relay trap a session has hit today.

items.title: vm-driver's contract -- a .job is CONSUMED on push and must never reach main -- lives only in the workflow's own header comment, and nothing enforces it; a PR carrying one to main was opened today
items.detail: OBSERVED 2026-09-06 by session_01WaQaYCpGb3yZKkkRqk4JfU while re-landing the 1C live-alarms disposition (#11113, superseding #11105). || THE MECHANISM. .github/workflows/vm-driver.yml triggers on `push` to `branches: ['claude/**']` with `paths: ['automation/jobs/**']`, SSHes the file's body to the target VM (live = 141.145.193.91) as `bash -s`, then `git rm`s the job file and commits the result. So a .job is a FIRE-AND-FORGET REQUEST that is consumed, never a durable artifact -- and PUSHING one IS the execution, not merging it. || THE GAP. Nothing enforces that a .job never reaches main. If one lands there, the NEXT `claude/**` branch that merges main and pushes matches `paths: ['automation/jobs/**']` and RE-EXECUTES it on the live money-handling VM -- unrequested, unattributed, potentially weeks later, by a session that has never heard of the work object that wrote it. || MEASURED, and the zero is a validated negative rather than an unexercised probe. Population: the complete automation/jobs/ tree at origin/main (8a16786) plus `git log origin/main -- 'automation/jobs/*'` over the full fetched history -- n = 0 files, 0 commits; automation/results/ on main holds exactly one entry, .gitkeep. Positive control: the same listing against origin/claude/live-alarms-1c-20260906 returns automation/jobs/1c-live-alarms-state-01.job, so the probe finds a .job when one is present. The invariant has held for every job so far because vm-driver ran and removed each one -- i.e. it holds by SIDE EFFECT of the happy path, not by any check. || WHY IT IS LIVE NOW. PR #11105 carried automation/jobs/1c-live-alarms-state-01.job toward main and would have been the first violation. It got that far because vm-driver run 34025596229 FAILED after 21s on c8ccabdf at 2026-09-06T09:46:38Z, so the job was never consumed and simply stayed on the branch. That failure is the only reason the file survived to be merge-able -- which means the invariant is protected by nothing more than vm-driver succeeding. #11113 drops the file deliberately, so nothing has landed. || ALSO WORTH RECORDING: because push is the execution, a `.github/pr-landing/` declaration of `tier: 2 / landing: hold` on a PR adding a .job gates NOTHING -- the bash has already run by the time a human reads the hold. #11105's declaration asserted exactly that protection. || CANDIDATE FIX (not applied): a guard that fails any diff adding a file under automation/jobs/ whose PR base is main, plus a positive-control self-test that the probe fires on a planted .job. Cheap, and it fails closed in the direction that matters.
items.resolution_criteria: CLOSES when a CI guard REFUSES a diff that adds a file under automation/jobs/ on a PR whose base is main, AND that guard carries a positive-control self-test proving it fires on a planted .job -- a guard that reports clean without having been shown to catch a positive is 'we did not look', not a pass. || It does NOT close on the observation that main is currently clean: n = 0 today is the SIDE EFFECT of vm-driver having succeeded every time so far, and vm-driver run 34025596229 already failed once, which is exactly how #11105 came to carry one toward main. || It also does NOT close on dropping the file from #11113 -- that removed one instance and changed nothing about the mechanism. || If the operator decides the risk is acceptable and no guard is wanted, this does not close, it CHANGES: record that as a decision rather than leaving it looking like a check about to be built.

items.title: A sub-session spawned without source_url gets no repo attached, cannot push, and its finished work dies in the container
items.source: manager session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj, 2026-09-06
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-06. The manager spawned three sub-sessions via create_session passing NO source_url. TWO got a repo attached (session_context.sources = benbaichmankass/metis-insights); ONE did not -- session_013r8Joo877hnkYoKRzQsrwW came back with session_context carrying only {model, permission_mode} and NO `sources` key. It completed the whole Phase-1B loss-attribution analysis, committed 7a72a1e, and `git push` was REFUSED by the git proxy: 'repo not in authorized set'. No branch reached origin (verified by git fetch --prune plus a full branch scan). The work is UNRECOVERABLE because the manager cannot message a cloud sub-session: SendMessage returns 'No agent named ... is reachable', ListAgents shows none, and the Claude_Code_Remote MCP exposes create/get/list/interrupt/archive with NO send. Cost: a complete analysis re-run. !! THE FAILURE IS SILENT AND ARRIVES LAST -- the session runs normally throughout and only discovers it at the push, which is when the work is most expensive to lose. !! AND IT IS NON-DETERMINISTIC across identical calls, so 'it worked last time' is not evidence. MITIGATION APPLIED on the retry (session_01XRYfPGr4jAHr4k1rmvTKFi): source_url passed explicitly, plus an instruction to push a skeleton in the first minutes and confirm it reached origin BEFORE investing in the analysis. That is a mitigation, not a fix.

⚠️ RECURRED 2026-09-08, two days after filing, by a manager that had not read this row — TWICE in one minute (MI-188 and MI-189). The recurrence also found a variant this row does not describe: the container can attach a DIFFERENT repo rather than none, which fails QUIETLY and yields plausible findings from the wrong codebase, where the no-repo case fails loudly within seconds. See BL-20260908-SPAWNING-WITHOUT-SOURCE-URL-CAN-ATTACH-THE-WRONG-REPO-NOT-MERELY-NO-REPO-AND-THE-2026-09-06-ROW-DID-NOT-PREVENT-IT. ⚠️ DO NOT CLOSE THIS ROW on a fix that covers only the no-repo case.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER create_session reliably attaches the repo when the parent has it -- measured across >=5 spawns that omit source_url, all carrying `sources` -- OR the spawn path refuses/warns loudly when it does not, OR the manager's spawn helper always passes source_url and a check fails a spawn that omits it. !! ONE session pushing successfully does NOT clear this: the defect is intermittent, so a clear needs a denominator, not an anecdote.

items.title: A sub-session that calls AskUserQuestion blocks indefinitely, and the manager has no channel to answer it
items.source: manager session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj, 2026-09-06
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-06. session_01RHuSYKu1r1ZErc65KLKV8t (Phase 1C) called AskUserQuestion with two questions and went to SESSION_STATUS_REQUIRES_ACTION / status_bucket BLOCKED and stayed there. No human watches a manager-spawned session, so the prompt can never be answered, and the manager cannot answer it either -- SendMessage refuses, ListAgents lists nothing, the CCR MCP has no send tool. That INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMS CLAUDE.md's existing claim that a manager cannot message a running sub-session. !! THE COST WAS NOT THE BLOCK, which was survivable because the session had already pushed its branch. It was that one of its two questions rested on a FALSE PREMISE the manager could have corrected in a sentence: it asked how to reach the live VM having concluded SSH was 'the only route left' after the issue relay 403'd and the vm-driver job was refused by the sandbox classifier. The diag API is reachable from a sandbox container over PLAIN HTTPS, no SSH and no relay -- manager verified at 09:42Z that /api/diag/exchange_positions returned bybit_1's four open positions -- and CLAUDE.md already says to try direct FIRST. So the session marked every live-venue claim NOT VERIFIED and left two of three alarms unsettled over a capability it actually had. !! The session was RIGHT to refuse to work around the classifier blocking its SSH job; that judgement is not the defect.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER a manager gains a real channel to a spawned cloud sub-session (a send path, or a durable inbox it polls), OR every spawn dispatch carries an explicit 'do not call AskUserQuestion -- no human is watching; write the question into your PR body and board post and continue on everything that does not depend on it' AND a session is OBSERVED hitting a real ambiguity and following it. !! The instruction ALONE does not clear this. 'Remember to' has already failed twice on the sub-session registry (MI-15), and a third reminder-as-remedy would be the same non-fix.

items.title: RECURRENCE: a manager commit on a worker branch makes that branch permanently unmergeable, because R2 grades commits in range and a revert adds a second violation
items.source: manager session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj, 2026-09-06
items.detail: RECURRENCE, and that is the finding -- the earlier fix did not hold. Same shape as the R6 instance that killed PR #11031 on 2026-09-05 and is recorded in WO-20260905-MI122-MI123-RESIDUES: 'a lapse becomes UNMERGEABLE FOREVER rather than correctable -- there is no I-have-since-fixed-it path.' That row was filed against R6; this is R2, so the property belongs to the guard's RANGE-GRADING DESIGN and not to any one rule. MEASURED 2026-09-06 on PR #11105 / branch claude/live-alarms-1c-20260906. The manager edited docs/claude/dispositions/2026-09-06-1C-three-live-alarms.md (a worker session's content) to satisfy stated-population-guard -- a two-line fix that was still doing the item. check_manager_scope R2 failed it correctly. The manager then REVERTED the edit, and the revert was graded as a SECOND R2 violation, because R2 grades COMMITS IN THE RANGE rather than the net diff. Verified: `git merge-base --is-ancestor a43ca75d HEAD` succeeds, so the violating commit sits permanently inside the graded range and no later commit can clear it. Guard now reports 2 R2 violations where before there was 1 -- REVERTING MADE THE COUNT WORSE. !! THE THREE EXITS ARE ALL BAD AND THAT IS THE POINT. (1) manager-scope-exception.yaml is for a live INCIDENT, and spending it on a manager's own lapse is the cheaper-to-lie-to-than-to-satisfy failure the guard's own docs name. (2) History rewrite is forbidden on another session's branch. (3) Cherry-picking the author's commits onto a clean branch WOULD work -- the guard reads the self-written Claude-Session trailer, so they would grade as the author's -- but the guard's own text names that as an open, unguarded evasion, so using it knowingly is worse than the red check. What is left is abandoning the branch, which is what the operator chose on 2026-09-05 and which SILENTLY DROPPED three filed backlog rows and REWOUND five generated registers. !! NOTE THE INCENTIVE THIS CREATES, which is the dangerous part: the correct response to noticing your own violation (revert it) makes the branch strictly worse, so the guard currently rewards NOT NOTICING.
items.resolution_criteria: A manager who commits to a worker path has a route back that is neither an exception, nor a history rewrite, nor abandoning the branch. Candidates worth measuring, not a chosen design: R2 grades the NET DIFF at the tip as well as the range and passes when the offending content is no longer present; or a revert that exactly restores the pre-violation blob is recognised and cancels its parent violation; or the range is scoped to commits not already superseded at the tip. !! WHAT DOES NOT CLEAR THIS: another reminder to managers not to touch worker paths. That is the prose that already exists and it did not hold -- the manager who caused this instance had read the rule the same morning and re-stated it in a status update. !! AND ANY FIX MUST NOT WEAKEN THE GUARD: the detection was CORRECT both times and must keep firing. This is about the exit, not the catch.

items.title: /api/bot/trades/closed silently returns [] above limit~200 and for any since= — the route a reviewer grades performance from

items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-06 against the live API by bisection, with a positive control at every step: limit=5 -> 5 rows, limit=100 -> 100, limit=200 -> 200, limit=400 -> 0, limit=800 -> 0, limit=2000 -> 0. Separately ANY `since=<iso8601>` returns 0 rows while the same query without it returns rows: since=2026-07-01T00:00:00Z -> 0, and days=60 -> 0 at limit=2000 but rows at limit=200. NO error, NO status code, NO empty-reason field -- a bare [] that renders identically to 'this window genuinely had no closed trades'. !! THIS IS THE ROUTE A PERFORMANCE REVIEW GRADES FROM, and the dashboard's Trades tab reads it with `since=` (CLAUDE.md documents '/api/bot/trades/closed?limit=200&since=...' as the Performance page's single client-side fetch). A reviewer asking a 90-day question gets a clean empty answer and concludes the book was quiet. The manager hit exactly this three times in a row this session before bisecting. !! IT IS THE silent-empty-guard CLASS ON A READ ROUTE: this repo already has a guard for a producer swallowing an exception into [], and the same shape here reaches a human decision surface instead of a log. It is also the 'unasserted denominator' sub-class C the diagnostic-provenance rule names -- an empty result read as a clean negative. || 2026-09-06, MI-144 (session_01L7dTAuGMdn3CTGeyYV5Mox) -- ADDRESSED, AND THE MEASUREMENT ABOVE IS CORRECTED. RE-MEASURED against the same live endpoint the same day, from a different container: limit=201/400/800/2000 each return HTTP 422 carrying detail[0].type='less_than_equal' and ctx.le=200 -- a REFUSAL NAMING ITS BOUND, not a bare []. And since= WORKS: since=2026-09-01 -> 142 rows; since=2026-07-01T00:00:00Z -> 50 (that is the DEFAULT limit of 50, not a filter failure); limit=200&since=2026-07-01T00:00:00Z -> 78; limit=200&days=60 -> 200. !! ONE ROOT CAUSE EXPLAINS EVERY ORIGINAL OBSERVATION: a probe that coerced a non-200 body into []/0. That also explains this row's own internally-consistent oddity -- 'days=60 -> 0 at limit=2000 but rows at limit=200' -- since days= is not a parameter on this route at all and is ignored, so the ONLY difference between those two calls was the 422. It is the SAME sub-class C the row correctly names, turned on the probe instead of on the route: an unasserted denominator. Recorded rather than quietly dropped, so the next session does not re-derive it. !! THE ROW IS STILL A REAL FINDING AND IS NOT DISMISSED -- the bare [] IS there, in the except handlers: missing DB, locked DB, sqlite3.Error and a blanket Exception each returned [], and the docstring advertised it as a feature. On the route a performance review grades from, an unreadable journal rendering as 'no closed trades yet' is exactly the clean confident wrong negative this row is about. FIXED: 503 + a machine-readable reason (db_file_missing / db_operational / db_read_failed / unexpected_error). The second half of the criteria -- the window above the cap being UNREACHABLE -- is fixed by an `offset` parameter plus X-Total-Count / X-Has-More headers, so a full page is distinguishable from an exhausted one. The cap itself was NOT raised. Two tests that ASSERTED the old bare-[] contract were updated. !! The 'check every OTHER read route' clause is now MEASURED and carried forward as BL-20260906-FOURTEEN-READ-ROUTES-STILL-RETURN-A-BARE-EMPTY-ON-ERROR (28 empty-on-except returns across src/web/api/routers/, 12 justified, 16 bare, 2 of them this route). Evidence: docs/research/trade-record-integrity-2026-09-06.md. || STATUS: the fix is MERGED-PENDING (this branch) and NOT DEPLOYED and NOT OBSERVED on the fleet -- so this row stays `open` deliberately. `fixed_pending_deploy` is not in the status enum, and collapsing 'the code is in' into 'resolved' is the exact conflation CLAUDE.md's manager checklist calls out (`done` means MERGED AND OBSERVED; `landed_unproven` is a different fact). CLOSE IT when a session has OBSERVED the live route return 503 with a `detail.reason` on an unreadable journal, or confirmed the deployed sha carries the change and the X-Total-Count header is present on a real call.
items.resolution_criteria: The route either SERVES the requested window or REFUSES it with a stated reason -- never a bare []. A caller must be able to tell 'no rows matched' from 'your limit exceeded a cap' from 'the query failed'. Verify by the same bisection with a POSITIVE CONTROL: show a limit that returns rows, then the first limit that does not, and show the new response distinguishes them. !! Raising the cap alone does NOT clear this -- the defect is the silence, not the number. !! And check every OTHER read route for the same shape before closing; this was found by accident, so the population of affected routes is UNMEASURED.
