items.title: rCoverage publishes 1.0 while its own rProvenance block on the same payload reads 381 of 424 unverified (89.9%)
items.detail: MEASURED live 2026-09-06 ~11:10Z, https://ict-bot.duckdns.org/api/bot/performance, window=all, n=424: rCoverage 1.0 against rProvenance {confirmedInitial 29, contaminated 14, unverified 381, noBasis 0} — 89.9% unverified. On window=7d it is 9 of 11 unverified (81.8%) and rCoverage STILL reads 1.0. rCoverage answers 'did we compute an R for every row?' while presenting as 'do we know the risk basis for every row?' — different questions with a 90-point gap. This is the repo's own COLLAPSED-STATES class: the field cannot say 'we did not look'. POSITIVE CONTROL that this is a defect and not a limitation: pnlCoverage on the SAME payload does it correctly — 0.7594, with measured 322 / estimated 20 / fabricated 4 / unverified 78, an honest denominator. The correct pattern already exists one field away. WHY IT MATTERS: rCoverage is the instrument that should warn a reader that expectancyR is untrustworthy. On the same endpoint, window=30d publishes expectancyR +0.9818 against profitFactor 0.9507 on a window that LOST money (-$3.63, n=39, contaminated 12 = 30.8%) — a sign contradiction that rCoverage 1.0 actively conceals. R feeds the promotion gates. SECONDARY, same family: on window=24h (n=0) pnlCoverage returns None ('we did not look') while rCoverage returns 0.0 (a real reading) — the same absence encoded two ways on one payload. Found while verifying P1 for the operator-requested measurement-defect list (docs/claude/work/MEASUREMENT-DEFECTS-2026-09-06.md, P2).
items.resolution_criteria: rCoverage either (a) reports the share of rows with a VERIFIED risk basis, so the published number moves with rProvenance rather than contradicting it, or (b) is renamed/rescoped to what it actually measures AND an honest coverage figure is published beside it. Either way it must be able to express 'we did not look' — a zero-trade window must not read 0.0 as if that were a measurement, matching pnlCoverage's None. VERIFY BY RE-READING /api/bot/performance on at least two windows and showing rCoverage and rProvenance now agree; a passing unit test is NOT this observation. Consider registering the field with collapsed-state-guard.

items.title: 33 exit-matrix cells grade a lever `honest_negative`/`shipped` on a leg whose monitor unit has no consumer for it — while the correct status blocked:no_lever_consumer_in_unit exists and is used on 5 sibling cells
items.source: MI-146 audit, session_014jrW67rFyJNnHr7y6dEhec, 2026-09-06
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-06 (docs/research/exit-lever-wiring-audit-2026-09-06.md). POPULATION: the 51 of 52 rows in docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json that resolve to a monitor unit via src.runtime.pipeline.monitor_unit_for (the bundled `shadow fleet` row enumerates no legs and is excluded) x 9 lever columns = 459 cells. Consumer presence was established by grepping each unit's source at origin/main 90575851, with a positive control (giveback_verdict IS found at trend_donchian.py:623 and htf_pullback_trend_2h.py:683, so the probe fires on a positive before being trusted on a negative). 120 of 459 cells (26.1%) carry a TESTED verdict (honest_negative/shipped/passed_unshipped) for a lever with NO runtime consumer in that leg's own unit. !! ~87 OF THOSE ARE DEFENSIBLE AND MUST NOT BE 'FIXED': exit_ladder (45) and regime_flip_exit (42) were replayed offline BEFORE being built, found negative, and the build correctly stopped -- src/runtime/regime_flip_exit.py's own docstring states it has no call sites deliberately. That is the process working. THE GENUINE MISLABEL IS 33 CELLS: 19 exit_head_ml (17 live htf_pullback_* legs whose unit has no exit-head consumer at all, plus ict_scalp_avax_5m and ict_scalp_xrp_15m), 10 giveback_stop (8 ict_scalp legs + squeeze_breakout_4h + fvg_range_15m), 2 stale_stop (squeeze, fvg), 1 vol_trail (squeeze), 1 exit_ladder passed_unshipped (ict_scalp_sol_15m). !! THE CORRECT VOCABULARY ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY USED: 5 ict_scalp exit_head_ml cells carry `blocked:no_lever_consumer_in_unit`, so 19 identically-wired sibling cells reading `honest_negative` is an INTERNAL INCONSISTENCY in one file, not a missing concept. WHY IT MATTERS: 'the backtest says it does not help' and 'there is no code to run it' are OPPOSITE findings and the operator's build decisions hinge on which it is -- operator directive 2026-09-06. REMEDY (Tier-1): re-status the 33; add a `basis` field (live_lever vs harness_only) so the ~87 defensible research-before-build negatives stay honest_negative but are distinguishable from a negative measured on production code; add a CI check that FAILS a cell graded honest_negative/shipped whose lever has no consumer in the leg's monitor_unit_for unit. A reminder is not a mechanism -- this mislabel recurred 33 times inside one committed file. Nearest existing rows checked and are NOT this: BL-20260818-UNGRADED-CELLS-DO-NOT-SURFACE-AT-THE-FLEET-LEVEL (ungraded cells), BL-20260814-NINE-SHIPPED-LEVERS-NEVER-GRADED-AGAINST-THEIR-OWN-ABSENCE (missing lever-OFF arms).
items.resolution_criteria: OBSERVABLE, three parts. (1) The 33 named cells in docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json no longer read honest_negative/shipped/passed_unshipped -- re-run the audit's own cross-tab (resolve each leg with src.runtime.pipeline.monitor_unit_for, grep the unit for the lever's runtime entry point) and it reports 0 cells graded as a tested result with no consumer, DOWN FROM 33. (2) Every cell in the matrix carries a `basis` field valued live_lever or harness_only, so the ~87 defensible research-before-build negatives (exit_ladder 45, regime_flip_exit 42) stay honest_negative and are still distinguishable from a negative measured on production code -- a re-status that collapses those into blocked:no_lever_consumer_in_unit is a REGRESSION, not a fix, and does not close this row. (3) A CI guard registered in scripts/ci/run_guards.py FAILS a planted cell graded honest_negative whose lever has no consumer in the leg's monitor unit -- demonstrated by its own self-test, NOT by the tree merely reading clean, because a guard that has never failed on a known-bad input is not evidence of anything. !! CLAUSE (3) IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: this mislabel recurred 33 times inside a single committed file, so re-statusing without a detector closes the instance and not the class.

items.title: The exit-coverage matrix has no column for target revision, so the capability M20 was RENAMED to require (2026-08-20) is invisible to M20's own done-condition
items.source: MI-146 audit, session_014jrW67rFyJNnHr7y6dEhec, 2026-09-06
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-06 (docs/research/exit-lever-wiring-audit-2026-09-06.md). M20 was renamed from `Exit Refinement` to `Active Trade Management` on 2026-08-20 by operator directive, and docs/design/exit-mechanism-construction-PROCESS.md E3.6 states the requirement: the bracket must carry a predictive expectation at entry and monitoring may revise it in EITHER direction, 'extending a target on an outperforming trade is in scope'. THE MATRIX'S 9 COLUMNS ARE trail_geometry, stale_stop, giveback_stop, exit_ladder, exit_head_ml, trail_decay, regime_flip_exit, vol_trail, bracket_geometry -- the first eight are post-entry overrides that can only TIGHTEN or CLOSE, and bracket_geometry is entry-time only. There is NO column for target extension, none for a stated exit expectation at entry, and none for revision conditioned on the strategy's own thesis. CONSEQUENCE, and it is the dangerous one: M20's done-condition IS the matrix ('no pending/blocked rows on live legs', per .claude/skills/exit-refinement), so M20 CAN BE DECLARED DONE with none of E3.6's three capabilities built -- 320 of 468 cells are already honest_negative. !! THIS IS NOT THE SAME ROW AS BL-20260826-TARGET-EXTENSION-SOAK-IS-100PCT-SENTINEL-AND-CANNOT-YET-OBSERVE-THE-LEVER: that one says the soak cannot yet OBSERVE the lever (re-confirmed 2026-09-06 -- 100 of 100 rows from /api/diag/log_file?name=target_extension_soak read expectation_state=sentinel_no_expectation across 8 live legs, 11 days after it was filed). THIS row says the TRACKER cannot see the capability at all, so its absence never surfaces in the milestone roll-up. Different objects, different remedies. REMEDY (Tier-1, propose-only here): add the missing lever column(s) to the matrix, and replace M20's coverage-only done-condition with the two-part (coverage + outcome) condition proposed in the audit memo. RELATED, and independent confirmation from another direction: BL-20260814-THREE-SIBLING-SWEEPS-STILL-BUILD-NO-TAKE-PROFIT-BOOKS-AND-STAMP-NOTHING records that 42 of 43 regime_flip_exit negatives were graded on no-take-profit books.
items.resolution_criteria: OBSERVABLE, and deliberately does NOT require the lever to work. (1) docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json carries a lever column for target revision, and every live leg has a verdict in it -- so the capability's absence SURFACES in M20's roll-up instead of being invisible to it. (2) ROADMAP.md's M20 row no longer states a coverage-only done-condition: it carries an OUTCOME clause as well, so a fleet of 468 honest_negative cells can no longer satisfy the milestone. The operator sets the threshold values; the row closes on the clause EXISTING and being measurable, not on any particular number. !! DO NOT CLOSE THIS BY BUILDING THE LEVER. Flipping target-extension annotate->act would leave the tracker just as blind as it is today -- the finding is that the tracker cannot SEE the capability, not that the capability is off. !! AND DO NOT CLOSE IT ON THE SOAK: BL-20260826-TARGET-EXTENSION-SOAK-IS-100PCT-SENTINEL-AND-CANNOT-YET-OBSERVE-THE-LEVER owns whether the lever can be observed; this row owns whether the milestone can see it. Different objects, different remedies -- if the operator DECIDES the matrix should not track revision, this row does not close, it CHANGES: record that as a decision rather than leaving it looking like a column about to be added.

items.title: src/runtime/tp_venue_cap.py declares it an OPEN QUESTION whether 0.099 is right off Bybit — measured: it is ~2.9x the p90 of lower-bound MFE, and 0 of 39 non-crypto trades ever reached it
items.detail:
tp_venue_cap.py's own docstring warns that TP_VENUE_CAP_PCT = 0.099 is 'named for a Bybit boundary and is applied to every symbol, including legs that touch no Bybit account' (GLD, QQQ, SCHA, IWM, MES, MGC, ...), and states plainly: 'whether 0.099 is right, too tight, or too loose for a non-Bybit leg is an OPEN QUESTION. Consolidating the declaration does not answer it and must not be read as having answered it.' This row answers it with evidence.

MEASURED 2026-09-06 (MI-148) via the new scripts/research/bracket_calibration_report.py --mfe.
POPULATION: the 102 of 168 /api/diag/position_telemetry rows carrying peak_gradeable=True and a readable peak_r/cap_r. Peak excursion converted to percent-of-entry as (peak_r / cap_r) * TP_VENUE_CAP_PCT.

  crypto (Bybit-traded)     n=63  MFE p50 1.39%  p75 6.15%  p90 9.70%  reached 9.9%: 4/63 = 0.063
  non-crypto (NO Bybit acct) n=39  MFE p50 1.19%  p75 3.00%  p90 3.42%  reached 9.9%: 0/39 = 0.000

So on Bybit-traded crypto the cap is ~1.0x the p90 lower-bound MFE — about right, though by accident, since it is an exchange rejection boundary and never a chosen level. Off Bybit it is ~2.9x the p90 and NOT ONE of 39 trades ever reached it, even at the lower bound.

WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC: on those legs the resting take-profit is not a prediction that is sometimes wrong, it is a level nothing reaches — so 'the trade hit its take-profit' is structurally impossible, the only exit is the ATR trail, and the trail by construction gives back the distance from the high-water mark. The giveback the operator reported is the trail working as designed on legs whose geometry contains no profit-taking prediction. It also means every giveback_stop / regime_flip_exit negative measured on these legs was measured on a book that could not take profit (cf BL-20260814-THREE-SIBLING-SWEEPS-STILL-BUILD-NO-TAKE-PROFIT-BOOKS-AND-STAMP-NOTHING).

STATE THE LIMITS. n=39 on the non-crypto arm and per-leg n runs 1-8, so this supports a DIRECTION and not a per-leg number. peak_provenance is 'estimated' on 168/168 and peak_r_is_lower_bound is True on 168/168, which biases AGAINST the finding on the crypto arm (true p90 may exceed 9.9%) and TOWARD it on the non-crypto arm.

NOT THE SAME ROW as BL-20260823-TP-CLAMP-HAS-NO-SL-REFERENCE (that is R:R < 1 on a high-ATR instrument, a per-trade risk-geometry defect) nor as BL-20260901-E35-TP-R-CAN-BE-INERT-BEHIND-THE-VENUE-CLAMP-AND-THE-BINDING-RATE-IS-UNMEASURED (that is the tp_r change being inert; updated separately with the now-measured binding rate). This row is specifically: the CAP VALUE ITSELF is wrong for the non-Bybit half of the fleet, and that was an explicitly declared open question until now.

REMEDY IS TIER-3 AND IS NOT A LOWERED tp_r. tp_venue_cap.py states no tp_r reproduces the clamp (percent-of-entry vs multiple-of-risk), so an 'equivalent' figure tightens the real target on every trade the clamp was never binding for. The construction must be a per-leg target derived from that leg's own MFE distribution at proper n, conditioned on the family's own thesis per PROCESS doc E3.6(4). The n needed is not available live (1-8 rows/leg) and must come from the offline harness over historical candles, which is not blocked on anything.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) a per-venue split of the TP cap is shipped with each venue's actual published take-profit limit read from that venue (not inferred from Bybit's), or (b) the non-Bybit legs carry a per-leg declared target derived from an MFE distribution at stated n, so the 0.099 stops being the binding level on them. A per-leg target set off the live n=1-8 does NOT close this — that would be the fitted-threshold failure. Closing also requires re-running scripts/research/bracket_calibration_report.py --mfe and recording that the non-crypto 'reached cap' rate is no longer 0/n because the target moved, not because the population did.

items.title: docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json is the one register EVERY session must edit and it has no append helper — a naive read-append-write reformats all 1,148 lines, the exact trap backlog_append.py was built to close one file over
items.detail:
CLAUDE.md § 'Every session' requires every session to READ docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json at start and UPDATE it at end. For the three review backlogs that edit is protected: scripts/ops/backlog_append.py round-trips the file's exact serialisation and REFUSES to write when it cannot reproduce it, because BL-20260820-BACKLOG-APPEND-REFORMATS-AND-REATTRIBUTES measured a ONE-ROW append producing 21,307 insertions / 21,288 deletions.

OPEN-ITEMS.json has no such helper, and it is MORE exposed, not less: it is edited by every session rather than by the ones that happen to file a finding.

MEASURED 2026-09-06 (MI-148), and this is a NEAR-MISS REPORT rather than a theory. Appending one row with json.dumps(indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) — the idiom that IS correct for the review backlogs — produced 1,148 insertions / 1,149 deletions on a 1,197-line file, i.e. a whole-file rewrite. open-items-guard PASSED on it ('OK — 55 items ... every one workable'), so the guard is no protection against this: it validates CONTENT, not the diff. It was caught only by reading git diff --numstat by hand.

ROOT CAUSE: the file's style is not reproducible by json.dumps at any indent. Its list elements sit at the SAME indent level as the enclosing key (item brace at 1 space, keys at 2), whereas json.dumps(indent=1) puts the brace at 2 and keys at 3. Verified by exhaustive round-trip over indent in (1,2,4,None) x ensure_ascii in (False,True) x three separator settings: NO combination reproduces the bytes. So the correct-looking helper call is the wrong one here, and there is nothing in the file or in CLAUDE.md that says so.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS — the same argument backlog_append.py's docstring makes: every diff-scoped guard reads added-vs-origin/main, so a whole-file reformat RE-ATTRIBUTES all 54 pre-existing rows to the appending PR. On a register whose rows carry loud:true and clears_when contracts, that buries the one row the session actually added and turns unrelated sessions' rows red.

WORKAROUND USED THIS SESSION (not a fix): surgical text insertion before the array's closing brace, with the row serialised at indent=1 and every line prefixed one space, then json.loads on the result to refuse writing invalid JSON. 20 insertions, 0 deletions. That works and should not have to be re-derived by the next session.
items.resolution_criteria:
EITHER (a) an append_open_item() helper beside backlog_append.py that round-trips OPEN-ITEMS.json's exact bytes and REFUSES rather than falling back to a default — the refusal is the feature, per backlog_append.py's own docstring — and CLAUDE.md's session-end bullet points at it the way it already points at backlog_append.py; OR (b) OPEN-ITEMS.json is re-serialised ONCE to a json.dumps-reproducible style in a dedicated PR that touches nothing else (so the one unavoidable whole-file diff is isolated and reviewable), after which the ordinary idiom is safe.

Closing requires a demonstration, not an assertion: append a throwaway row through the chosen path and show git diff --numstat reports insertions only. A green open-items-guard does NOT close this — it passed on the 1,148-line reformat.

items.title: RECURRENCE at 35 pairs: the coverage matrix's honest_negative status word cannot say 'the sweep PASSED this and the disposition is withheld', and every aggregate reads the word not the ref prose
items.detail: RECURRENCE of BL-20260814-STALE-CELL-BACKLOG-IS-HALF-ANSWERED-BY-THE-CORPUS-ALREADY, which measured this at 9 rows on 2026-08-14 and was marked RESOLVED. Filed as a recurrence deliberately (similar_ok): that the earlier fix did not hold, and that the number grew ~4x in three weeks, IS the finding. MEASURED 2026-09-06 by MI-145. POPULATION: all 1,376 kind=cell rows of docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl (51 legs, 110 distinct cell names, 218 run ids, sweep dates 2026-08-10..2026-08-17), joined by leg -> exit-refinement-coverage.json rows[].strategy. The sweep has emitted 91 passing verdicts (42 PASS + 49 path_b_wf_pass) = 6.6% of cells, across 50 of 225 distinct (leg,lever) pairs = 22.2%. THIRTY-FIVE of those 50 read honest_negative in the matrix, with best OOS deltas up to +8.326R (gld_pullback_1h trail_decay), +8.316R (tlt_pullback_1d trail_decay), +8.267R (gld_pullback_1h vol_trail). THIS IS NOT A GUARD FAILURE AND NOT DISHONESTY: scripts/ci/check_matrix_corpus_agreement.py run the same session reports OK -- every disagreement is ACKNOWLEDGED in the cell's ref prose, and withholding a live leg's disposition is correctly Tier-3. THE DEFECT IS THAT THE STATUS WORD COLLAPSES TWO STATES: 'the sweep measured this lever on this leg and it lost' and 'the sweep measured it, it WON on at least one cell across a walk-forward, and the disposition is withheld pending an operator decision'. docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md section 'Collapsed states': two distinct states sharing one value, with the dangerous one missing. THE CONSEQUENCE IS CONCRETE, NOT STYLISTIC -- every aggregate over the matrix reads the STATUS COLUMN and never the prose. Two live instances: (a) the 68.4% honest_negative headline in WO-20260906-POSITIVE-CONTROL-ON-THE-EXIT-SWEEP-320's own why: field, which framed all 320 as unfalsifiable; (b) docs/research/exit-lever-wiring-audit-2026-09-06.md (MI-146) concluding 'vol_trail: WIRED, honestly failed everywhere. Nothing to build.' -- the corpus has vol_trail passing a cell on 13 legs. Both are correct reads of the column and wrong about the world. NOTE WHAT THIS DOES NOT SAY: it is NOT a claim any of the 35 should ship. A path_b_wf_pass buys net R by spending drawdown, and m20_fleet_exit_sweep.beats()'s own docstring records path_b_wf_pass at 0-for-3 on the drawdown exchange rate in one measured run. The claim is that the one-word summary is lossy in the direction that CLOSES questions.
items.evidence: docs/research/exit-sweep-positive-control-2026-09-06.md section 3; PR #11136. Reproduce: join docs/research/m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl (verdict in {PASS, path_b_wf_pass}) to docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json on (leg,lever) -> (rows[].strategy, lever column).
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) the matrix gains a status that can express 'measured, a cell passed, disposition withheld' -- e.g. negative_disposition_withheld -- and m20_coverage_rollup.py counts it separately from honest_negative; or (b) the basis field added by MI-145 is extended with corpus_pass: true on each of the 35 and the roll-up reports that count. EITHER WAY the check is that a roll-up run PRINTS the number of honest_negative cells the corpus has passed, so it can never again be invisible to an aggregate. Changing any live leg's DISPOSITION is Tier-3 and is explicitly NOT part of closing this row.

items.title: scripts/ops/exit_mechanism_coverage.MECHANISMS covers 4 of the coverage matrix's 9 lever columns, so any leg-unit wiring guard built on it is partial and must say so
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-06 by MI-145 while verifying MI-146's 33 mislabels. MECHANISMS has exactly four entries -- stale_stop, giveback_stop, exit_head, trail_decay -- against the matrix's nine lever columns (the five with no detector: trail_geometry, exit_ladder, regime_flip_exit, vol_trail, bracket_geometry). CONSEQUENCE, MEASURED: re-deriving MI-146's 33 mislabels with monitor_unit_for + module_implements confirmed 31 and could say NOTHING about the remaining 2 (1 vol_trail, 1 exit_ladder passed_unshipped) -- unchecked, not refuted. 31+2 = 33 reconciles with MI-146 exactly, which is a real cross-check of both readings, but the gap is structural not incidental. WHY IT MATTERS: MI-146 recommendation #1 proposes a CI check that fails an honest_negative or shipped cell whose lever has no consumer in the leg's unit. Built on MECHANISMS -- which is the right base, per BL-20260818-CAPABILITY-AUDITS-GREP-ONE-FILE-AND-MISS-SHARED-LEVERS -- that check would cover 4 of 9 columns while printing OK, which is the 'green while measuring nothing' failure docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md already names. check_matrix_corpus_agreement.py already handles its own version of this correctly and is the model to copy: it prints 'NOT CHECKED (no corpus rows for the lever, declared): 176 live cell(s) across 4 column(s)' as its own line.
items.evidence: docs/research/exit-sweep-positive-control-2026-09-06.md sections 4.1 and 4.4; scripts/ops/exit_mechanism_coverage.py MECHANISMS; PR #11136.
items.resolution_criteria: Either MECHANISMS gains detectors for the five uncovered lever columns, or any guard built on it PRINTS the not-checked columns and their live cell count on every run (the check_matrix_corpus_agreement.py shape) so a reader cannot mistake partial coverage for clean. A guard that covers 4 of 9 and says so is acceptable; one that covers 4 of 9 and prints a bare OK is not.

items.title: The operating-layer registers are guarded but not scaffolded, so every write is discovered wrong by CI ~2 minutes later
items.detail: OPERATOR, 2026-09-06: 'your job is to manage the queue so that we don't lose cycles to these kinds of mistakes ... if you're not doing your job correctly, then it's gonna be very hard for the other sessions to do their job as well'. MEASURED ON THE MANAGER'S OWN PRs IN ONE DAY: SEVEN guard failures, every one a schema/field omission on a REGISTER write, every one found by CI after the PR was open. pr-landing-guard x2 (#11116, and a second branch) - no declaration file; register-id-guard x2 (#11123 recorded a creation date as 'added' where that register wants 'opened_at'; #11137's MI-148 checklist row recorded none at all); probe-guard x1 (a new OPEN-ITEMS monitoring row declared neither probe nor probe_absent_reason); stated-population-guard x2 (#11123, twice, on the very document about stating populations). MI-148's session independently hit register-id-guard on line-wrapped backlog ids the same day, so this is not one session being sloppy. THE GUARDS ARE ALL CORRECT AND SHOULD NOT BE WEAKENED - each names a real failure class the repo has already paid for. What is missing is the OTHER half: scripts/ops/backlog_append.py PROVES the pattern (it round-trips the file's exact serialisation, refuses a restatement, and enforces the schema at WRITE time), and there is NO equivalent for docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json, docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json, or .github/pr-landing/. VERIFIED, not assumed: `ls scripts/ops/ | grep -iE 'append|scaffold'` returns backlog_append.py and nothing else. COMPOUNDING IT: OPEN-ITEMS.json does NOT round-trip through json.dumps at ANY tested indent/ensure_ascii setting, so it can only be patched by string splicing - measured this session, and a splice anchor was wrong on the first attempt. A register that must be hand-spliced by every writer will keep being written wrong. COST SHAPE: each failure is a ~2-minute CI run plus diagnosis, on a queue where the manager's own throughput gates five sub-sessions.
items.resolution_criteria: A writer for each guarded register that CANNOT produce a row the guard rejects, modelled on backlog_append.py: (a) docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json - and it must fix the round-trip problem or own the splice itself, so no caller ever hand-edits it again; (b) docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json; (c) .github/pr-landing/<slug>.json, which can DERIVE the slug from the branch rather than having the author retype it. VERIFY BY PLANTING: for each writer, attempt a row the corresponding guard rejects and show the writer REFUSES it at write time - a passing guard on a well-formed row proves nothing, since that is the case that already works. !! DO NOT WEAKEN ANY GUARD. The guards are the only reason these classes are visible at all; the fix is upstream of them. !! AND DO NOT BUILD A SCAFFOLD THAT ONLY EMITS A TEMPLATE - a template the author edits by hand reintroduces exactly the omissions measured above. The writer must validate what it is about to write. SEPARATELY AND SMALLER: scripts/ops/manager_lease.py has --commit but its help says 'never pushes', while the lease's own canonical rule is 'a claim you did not PUSH protects nothing - another session reads origin, not your working tree'. A tool that stops one step short of its own doc's requirement is a trap; either it pushes, or it says loudly that the lease is not yet protecting anything.

items.title: A finished session prompt sat undispatched 14 days because docs/research/ is not a work register - and the same thesis was re-derived seven times
items.detail: OPERATOR 2026-09-06 on being shown MI-146's audit: 'none of this is news ... the fact that it's not easily accessible as part of this research is problematic in of itself'. MEASURED: docs/research/EXIT-GEOMETRY-REBUILD-SESSION-PROMPT.md was written 2026-08-23, carries the operator's directive verbatim, states its populations, and ends 'Paste this whole file as the opening message of a NEW session.' NOBODY DID, for 14 days. CARRIED BY NOTHING, with a POSITIVE CONTROL: zero work objects named it; zero of the 54 OPEN-ITEMS rows carried it; its only reference in docs/claude/ was an unrelated IB-trailing backlog row. The same probe finds SIX rows carrying the operating-layer design, so the silence is real absence, not a bad probe. COST: the same thesis derived at least SEVEN times across docs/research/ (e35-bracket-is-not-a-decision 08-20, bracket-expectation-construction 08-23 at 34KB, bracket-target-reachability 08-24, bracket-geometry-decision-packet 08-26, e35-matrix-recheck 08-29, e35-passed-unshipped-proposal 08-31, exit-lever-wiring-audit 09-06) and BUILT ZERO TIMES. RECURRENCE: OI-20260901-OPERATING-LAYER-BUILD-IS-IN-FLIGHT-AND-CARRIED-ONLY-BY-THIS-ROW exists for this exact class, the same week - 'four documents under docs/design/ that nothing else points at'. One got a carrier row by hand; this one did not, and the difference was whether a session happened to think of it. GENERAL DEFECT: docs/research/ and docs/design/ are WRITE surfaces with no READ path into planning. Nothing converts a memo that SPECIFIES WORK into a work object, and no session-start surface enumerates un-actioned research - so a perfect, ready-to-paste spec is exactly as invisible as a bad one.
items.resolution_criteria: An artifact that SPECIFIES WORK cannot be created without a register row pointing at it, AND un-actioned specs are visible at session start. Candidates, not a design: (a) a CI check failing a PR that adds docs/research/*SESSION-PROMPT*.md / *-PROPOSAL-*.md / *-DESIGN.md with no matching work object referencing its path; (b) a rendered SESSION-BRIEF section listing specs with no owning object - the surface that demonstrably reaches a session before it acts; (c) a sweep grepping for artifacts whose own text asks for a follow-up ('paste this as', 'next session should', 'not yet built') and filing any with no carrier. VERIFY BY PLANTING a spec with no carrier and showing the mechanism catches it, AND by running it over the existing tree and REPORTING HOW MANY UN-CARRIED SPECS ALREADY EXIST - that count is the finding and is currently UNMEASURED (now owned by WO-20260906-COUNT-THE-UN-CARRIED-SPECS, operator-chosen 2026-09-06). !! A mechanism covering only NEW artifacts leaves the existing pile invisible; say which half you built. !! The 14-day gap was NOT someone forgetting - the artifact was well-written and correctly filed. There was no path from 'filed' to 'planned'. A fix relying on sessions filing better does not address the cause.
items.owner: MI-148 carries the stranded work; the general defect is unowned

items.title: 14 read routes still return a bare [] / {} from an except handler -- the trades/closed class, with its population now MEASURED
items.source: MI-144 session_01L7dTAuGMdn3CTGeyYV5Mox, 2026-09-06
items.detail: BL-20260906-TRADES-CLOSED-SILENTLY-RETURNS-EMPTY-ABOVE-LIMIT-200-AND-FOR-ANY-SINCE closed on /api/bot/trades/closed and its resolution_criteria required checking every OTHER read route for the same shape, because it was found by accident and the affected population was UNMEASURED. It is measured now. MEASURED 2026-09-06 by an AST walk over src/web/api/routers/*.py looking for a Return of an empty List/Dict literal inside an ExceptHandler. POSITIVE CONTROL: the same probe also finds the 12 sites that DO carry an `allow-silent` justification, so its silence elsewhere is evidence rather than an absent probe. Population: 28 such returns, of which 12 are justified and 16 are bare. Two were trades_closed.py and are fixed. THE REMAINING 14, by file: backtests.py:172,174 - bot_config.py:146,178 - dashboard.py:494,510,777 - diag.py:969,1455 - notifications.py:494 - strategies.py:292 - strategy_review.py:163 - training_center.py:137 - work.py:367. !! NOT SWEPT BLIND, DELIBERATELY. Each needs its own consumer-contract judgement: some of these are helper functions where [] is a legitimate value, and turning one into a 503 could break the SPA on a path where degradation is correct. A blind sweep here would be the cosmetic-fix anti-pattern. !! AND `silent-empty-guard` CANNOT SEE THEM: it is DIFF-SCOPED (scripts/check_silent_empty_in_diff.py), so the 14 pre-existing sites are grandfathered and will stay so forever unless drained. That is exactly the residue shape diagnostic-provenance-guard had -- 52 findings frozen for 26 days across five review passes -- and its fix was an ungated whole-tree --all step ADDED AFTER the residue was drained to 0. The same two-step applies here: drain the 14 (each with a judgement), THEN add the ungated step. !! ONE STALE COMMENT TO FIX WHILE HERE: backtests.py:175 justifies its own silence as 'the same contract as trades_closed.py'. That contract changed on 2026-09-06. Field beats comment.
items.resolution_criteria: Each of the 14 sites reaches a WRITTEN disposition: either it refuses with a stated reason (the trades_closed.py shape), or it keeps returning empty WITH an `allow-silent: <reason>` marker naming why an empty value is the correct answer for that consumer. Re-run the AST probe and show the bare count at 0 with the justified count risen correspondingly -- the two must sum to the same 28 (or higher if routes were added), so the partition is checkable by arithmetic. THEN, and only then, add an ungated whole-tree step to silent-empty-guard so the residue cannot silently regrow. !! Adding the ungated step BEFORE draining would fail every PR on day one and would be reverted, which is how a guard gets disabled instead of satisfied.

items.title: All 301 gradeable pairs legs read 0% bracket-reached -- the per-leg sl/tp is probably the wrong yardstick for a spread trade
items.source: MI-144 session_01L7dTAuGMdn3CTGeyYV5Mox, 2026-09-06
items.detail: src/runtime/bracket_outcome.py (MI-144) re-derives 'did this close reach its declared bracket' from the recorded exit price against order_packages.sl/tp. MEASURED 2026-09-06 over the live journal pulled via /api/bot/db/table/{trades,order_packages} (5518 + 4435 rows). Population: closed, non-backtest, pnl NOT NULL, minus orphan_adopt/superseded/exchange_reset_flat, n=1287, of which 1125 gradeable. EVERY pairs leg grades mid_bracket: pairs_sol_eth_a 90/90, pairs_sol_eth_b 89/89, pairs_bnb_btc_a 61/61, pairs_bnb_btc_b 61/61 -- 301 rows, 0 reached, on all four strategies. A 0-for-301 across four independent legs is not a trading result, it is an instrument reading the wrong quantity: the M22 market-neutral sleeve stops on the SPREAD (src.units.strategies.pairs_executor, config/pairs.yaml), not on either leg's own price, and it is an ISOLATED 2-leg order path that never goes through the coordinator fold. !! THIS IS NOT ASSERTED, IT IS THE CANDIDATE EXPLANATION. Nobody has checked what order_packages.sl/tp actually holds for a pairs leg -- it may be a real per-leg protective level, a placeholder, or a spread level written into a price field. Read the field before concluding. !! CONSEQUENCE UNTIL RESOLVED: /api/bot/performance's bracketOutcome all-accounts figures (430/1125 = 38.2% reached) include 301 rows graded on a possibly-inapplicable yardstick. The REAL-MONEY figure is clean by comparison (420 of 424 gradeable, 4 non-gradeable, 228 = 54.3% reached) and is the one to quote.
items.resolution_criteria: Establish from the CODE and the DB -- not from this row -- what order_packages.sl/tp holds for a pairs leg, by reading pairs_executor's package writer and a sample of real pairs rows. Then either (a) the levels ARE per-leg protective levels, in which case 0-for-301 is a real finding about the sleeve and belongs in a performance review, or (b) they are not, in which case bracket_outcome must return a distinct state for a leg whose bracket is not a per-leg price level -- NOT mid_bracket, which currently asserts 'we looked and it ended between the levels'. Either way the all-accounts bracketOutcome numbers get restated with the answer.

items.title: A negative control graded at HEAD was carried by work objects this week's own program created that same day — the control confirmed the remediation instead of testing the condition
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-06 (MI-152, WO-20260906-COUNT-THE-UN-CARRIED-SPECS, PR #11148). The un-carried-spec census needed a KNOWN NEGATIVE to calibrate against: docs/research/EXIT-GEOMETRY-REBUILD-SESSION-PROMPT.md, which BL-20260906-A-RESEARCH-ARTIFACT-THAT-SPECIFIES-WORK-IS-NOT-REGISTERED-AS-WORK records as carried by nothing for 14 days. Graded against HEAD it came back CARRIED -- correctly, because WO-20260906-COUNT-THE-UN-CARRIED-SPECS and WO-20260906-THE-EXIT-GEOMETRY-REBUILD-WAS-SPECIFIED-AND-NEVER-DISPATCHED were created THAT MORNING by the very program diagnosing the stranding. A control measured AFTER the remediation tests the remediation, not the condition, and it fails SILENTLY IN THE REASSURING DIRECTION: the probe looked calibrated and would have under-reported the pile it exists to measure. GENERAL CLASS: whenever a session measures a condition its own cycle has been actively repairing, HEAD is not a valid measurement point for the negative control -- the population moved under it, and it moved because of you. The fix used was to assert the negative control against a PRE-remediation commit (daebbada) in a clean worktree, where it reproduces as `dormant_only`; the same worktree discipline was then needed a SECOND time for the census itself, because the report is an artifact under docs/research/ and running the probe on the branch that adds it puts the report into its own population. TWO instances of the same trap in one session, at two different levels. NOT A DUPLICATE OF RULE ONE: CLAUDE.md already says 'verify your own output too, hardest when it confirms what you expected', which is the disposition; this row names the specific MECHANISM (the measurement point is contaminated by the measurer's own commits, so re-reading the output more carefully cannot catch it -- only re-measuring at a different sha can). backlog_search over all three backlogs returned 8 rows at overlap 0.71, all LEXICAL: none concerns control contamination. Positive control on that probe: the same search finds the genuinely-related rows for other queries, so the silence is absence, not a dead search.
items.resolution_criteria: A session measuring a condition its own cycle has been remediating states WHICH SHA its control was graded at, and why that sha is uncontaminated. Cheap, mechanical form: grade the negative control in a worktree at the last commit before the current cycle's work began, and record that sha beside the result -- scripts/ops/uncarried_specs.py --self-test --strict-negative is a worked example (it REFUSES to pass unless the known-stranded artifact grades un-carried on a pre-remediation tree). !! DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY DROPPING THE CONTROL: the contaminated control still passed, so removing it loses the only thing that caught the under-count. !! AND A PROBE WITH NO NEGATIVE CONTROL AT ALL IS WORSE THAN A CONTAMINATED ONE -- it cannot be wrong in a way anyone notices.

items.title: bracketOutcome joins order_packages on order_package_id only, so it grades 99 of 428 real-money closed non-backtest rows (23.1%) and answers the operator's bracket question over a quarter of the book
items.detail: FOUND 2026-09-06 by checking the DEPLOYED figure against the pre-merge measurement instead of accepting it, minutes after PR #11131 (MI-144) deployed. /api/bot/performance's bracketOutcome resolves a trade's declared bracket by joining order_packages on trades.order_package_id ONLY. MEASURED against the live journal via /api/bot/db/table/*: of 470 real-money closed non-backtest trades only 120 (25.5%) carry an order_package_id, and 325 of the 350 NULL rows ARE reachable through the reverse edge order_packages.linked_trade_id (92.9%); 25 are unreachable by either key. Consequence on the route's own population (n=428): gradeable=99, noBracketRecord=325, published reachedRatio 0.4444. Re-run offline with the SHIPPED classifier, the forward key alone reproduces 44/99 = 44.4% EXACTLY (positive control), while forward-then-fallback grades 420 of 428 (98.1%) and answers 228/420 = 54.3%, sl:tp 187:41. NOTE THE 44.4% IS NOT A WRONG NUMBER -- it is a correct ratio over a denominator the reader cannot see is a quarter of the book, i.e. the same UNPROVENANCED-DENOMINATOR class MI-144 was dispatched to fix, reproduced by the fix itself. noBracketRecord IS published beside it so the state is not collapsed; the hazard is reachedRatio quoted alone. DO NOT CONFLATE WITH R: the same fallback moves rBasis.declaredInitial 103->106 and expectancyR -0.3152 -> -0.3153, because reverse-linked packages carry sl/tp but rarely a meta.risk_per_unit. FIX (Tier-1, read path): pre-aggregated LEFT JOIN on linked_trade_id consulted only where order_package_id is NULL, MIN(order_package_id) for determinism. linked_trade_id is currently UNIQUE across all 4436 packages (1113 over 1113 distinct trades, zero fan-out), so the pre-aggregation is defensive rather than load-bearing today.
items.tier: 1 — read path / analytics only; no writer, no order path
items.resolution_criteria: /api/bot/performance?window=all is OBSERVED on the live fleet with bracketOutcome.gradeable at or above ~420 of 424 and noBracketRecord in the low single digits. CHECK THE COVERAGE, NOT THE RATIO: reachedRatio is not broken and moves only 0.4444 -> ~0.5429, so watching it alone cannot distinguish a fixed instrument from an unfixed one. A merge closes nothing (ict-git-sync must pull it) and a green suite closes nothing (a harness cannot reach the VM). If coverage rises but the ratio does not land near 0.5429, that is the more valuable finding -- record it and keep the row open.
items.observation: MERGED, DEPLOYED and OBSERVED — not merely merged. /api/diag/version read git_sha 92aebf8c == git_sha_on_disk, restart_pending false, at 16:56:45Z; the endpoint still carried the OLD figures at 16:56:24Z, which is the positive control that this is real absence-then-presence and not an unreachable probe. /api/bot/performance?window=all, real money n=424: gradeable 420 (99.1% coverage, from 99 / 23.3%), noBracketRecord 0 (from 321), priceNotMeasurable 4, reachedRatio 0.5429, sl 187 / tp 41 / mid 192. VERIFIED BY ARITHMETIC: states partition to 424 == totalTrades; sl+tp+mid = 420 == gradeable; 228/420 = 0.5429 == the published ratio. rBasis {103,321,0,0} -> {106,318,0,0}, still summing to 424 with declaredInitial+storedStop == rTradeCount; expectancyR -0.3152 -> -0.3153 — the predicted negligible R effect, confirming the two halves stayed separate. NOTE every pre-merge prediction landed exactly; that shows the offline pipeline and the deployed route AGREE, which is what makes them comparable -- it is NOT self-evidence the classifier is correct, which rests on its tests.

items.title: The exit-head in-distribution guard gates on tf+symbols and never reads `family`, while the sibling entry-head guard one file over gates on family FIRST — the exporters are near-identical, so this is an omission, not a design choice
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 (MI-154, session_01S7pASy78QiNViwhSadGdNb) at main 957fc81d.

THE ASYMMETRY. `src/runtime/exit_head_shadow.py::maybe_score_exit_head` builds its candidate list from `artifact.get('tf')` (line 350) and `artifact.get('symbols')` (line 353) and NEVER reads `family`. Its sibling `src/runtime/entry_head_pwin.py::maybe_score_entry_pwin` gates on `artifact.get('family') != family` (line 165) BEFORE the identical `tf` (167) and `symbols` (169) checks, and takes `family` as a required keyword argument. Both artifacts are written by near-identical exporters that both stamp `"family": fam_dir.name` (`scripts/ml/export_exit_head.py:116`, `scripts/ml/export_entry_head.py:67`).

THE SIBLING IS THE POSITIVE CONTROL. A `family` reader DOES exist in this repo, three lines from the identical tf/symbols pair, over an artifact of the same shape — so the exit-head omission is a dropped check, not a deliberate scoping decision. Probe over the whole tree for `.get("family")` / `["family"]` returns 48 hits and exactly ONE of them is an artifact in-distribution guard (entry_head_pwin.py:165); the exit-head guard is absent from that set.

THE GUARD'S OWN DOCSTRING NAMES WHAT IT DOES NOT CHECK. exit_head_shadow.py:342-344 reads 'an out-of-family score would pollute the shadow track record' — it names family as the hazard and then gates on tf and symbols only. tf+symbols cannot separate two strategies trading the SAME symbol on the SAME timeframe, which is precisely ict_scalp vs donchian on SOLUSDT.

⚠️ STATE THE POPULATION, AND THE HAZARD IS LATENT — NOT LIVE — ON TODAY'S CONFIG. This row does NOT claim a scalp artifact would be mis-scored today. Measured by resolving `src.runtime.pipeline.monitor_unit_for` over the FULL population of 55 strategies in config/strategies.yaml: 23 legs resolve to monitor unit `trend_donchian` and therefore reach `maybe_score_exit_head` (the only call site is trend_donchian.py:802). ALL 23 are on 1h, 4h or 1d. On 5m or 15m: NONE. All 8 ict_scalp legs resolve to unit `ict_scalp`, which has no exit-head call site at all. So the tf guard alone currently excludes a 5m/15m scalp artifact, and the family gap costs nothing TODAY.

WHEN IT STOPS BEING LATENT — three ways, and each is a normal next step rather than an exotic one: (a) a scalp exit head is published at 1h/4h/1d; (b) any leg on the donchian monitor moves to 5m/15m; (c) a second family publishes a head at a tf/symbol pair a donchian leg already covers. `exit-head-donchian-1h-v1` is at stage `advisory`, i.e. it CAN influence a live exit, so the collision case is a real-money path, not an observation-only one.

NEW FACT ESTABLISHED HERE — the live artifacts' actual `family` values, read off the trainer. PR #11140 states it deliberately did NOT tighten the donchian side because 'what value its `family` field actually carries has not been read from the mirror (that dir is not on the diag allowlist)'. It has now been read, via the push-triggered `trainer-diag-relay` (run 34047425502, state=ran, remote_exit=0): `runtime_logs/trainer_mirror/exit_head/` holds exactly two files and they declare `exit-head-donchian-1h-v1  family=donchian tf=1h stage=advisory symbols=['BTCUSDT','ETHUSDT','SOLUSDT'] train_rows=34338` and `exit-head-donchian-peak-1h-v1  family=donchian tf=1h stage=shadow symbols=['BTCUSDT','ETHUSDT','SOLUSDT'] train_rows=44244`. Both carry the literal string `donchian`. That is the fact #11140 was missing, and it removes the stated reason for leaving donchian opted out.

IN-FLIGHT FIX — DO NOT DUPLICATE IT. PR #11140 (OPEN, unmerged, tier 3 / landing: hold) already adds caller-opt-in family gating: ict_scalp passes its family, donchian deliberately passes nothing. This row is filed rather than fixed BECAUSE that PR exists and touches the same function — a second implementation would be RC-BUILT-A-MECHANISM-THAT-ALREADY-EXISTED plus a guaranteed merge conflict. The row exists so the gap is tracked if #11140 is closed unmerged, which is a live possibility: it sits under the 2026-08-23 operator SHIP BLOCKED verdict carried by 5 of 52 rows in docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) #11140 merges AND `exit_head_shadow.maybe_score_exit_head` is observed refusing an out-of-family artifact — a real WARNING line naming both family values on a real row, not a unit test; OR (b) #11140 is closed unmerged and the family check is added to the exit-head guard by another change, verified the same way. ⚠️ A PASSING TEST DOES NOT CLOSE THIS. tests/test_exit_head_apply_parity.py already asserts the unit passes family='ict_scalp'; that asserts a caller's argument, not that the guard ever REFUSED anything. ⚠️ AND DO NOT CLOSE IT ON THE HAZARD STAYING LATENT. 'No collision has occurred' is the expected reading while no donchian-monitor leg is on 5m/15m and no scalp head is published — it is the precondition of the row, not evidence against it. Re-measure the 23-leg / 0-on-5m-or-15m population with monitor_unit_for before asserting the gap is still inert; if that count has changed, the row has become urgent rather than resolved. Now that both live artifacts are confirmed to carry family='donchian', the donchian opt-out #11140 left open on an unread field can be closed on evidence.

items.title: An exit_head_ml cell records every re-measurement by APPENDING to one `ref` string, so the FIRST sentence a reader meets is the SUPERSEDED figure set — this produced a false 'two records disagree' finding that blocked PR #11140 for a day.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-06 (MI-153). RECURRENCE of the class named by BL-20260815-EXIT-HEAD-ROUNDS-RUN-IDENTITY-IS-PROSE-NOT-A-FIELD and BL-20260814-TP-GEOMETRY-RECORDED-IN-PROSE-WHILE-THE-CONSUMER-READS-A-FIELD, filed as a recurrence rather than a duplicate because BOTH earlier rows are about a fact recorded in prose that a CONSUMER cannot read, and this one is about a fact recorded in prose that a HUMAN reads WRONG — a different failure with a different remedy, and it has now cost real time.

WHAT HAPPENED. A manager session and this sub-session both recorded, in a work object and a spawn brief, that 'two records report DIFFERENT numbers for the SAME ict_scalp exit-head legs' and that 'all 3 of 3 candidate legs disagree'. They do not. Each of the three exit_head_ml cells carries BOTH figure sets in ONE append-only `ref`, in chronological order, joined by an explicit arrow — ict_scalp_sol_5m literally reads 'n_oos 800 -> 1150, auc 0.6149 -> 0.6184'. The MI-146 audit quoted the SECOND clause; the brief quoted the FIRST clause of the same string. One record read at two points. The operator was then offered 'resolve before arming' vs 'arm now', chose resolve, and PR #11140 was held on an investigation of a contradiction that did not exist.

MECHANISM, and it is structural rather than anyone's carelessness. (a) The cell has NO structured figure field: its complete key set is status/ref/tp_geometry, verified on all three. Every number lives in ~4000 characters of prose. (b) The ref is APPEND-ONLY by convention — each re-measurement, ship-block and operator decision is concatenated with ' || ', which is right for preserving the record and wrong for the reader, because it puts the OLDEST and now-superseded measurement in the opening sentence and the current one several thousand characters in. (c) Nothing joins the cell to the structured evidence: exit_head_ml is a declared exemption in check_matrix_corpus_agreement.CORPUS_EXEMPT_LEVERS because that guard reads only m20-sweep-corpus.jsonl, while the exit-head evidence lives in m20-exit-head-rounds.jsonl. So the one guard that compares a cell against its evidence cannot see this column at all — its own text says so and names the fix.

STATE THE POPULATION. 3 of 3 ict_scalp candidate cells carry two figure sets in one ref with the superseded one first. items.title: qty-legalization-guard forbids BUILDING a second legalizer but never requires USING the one legalizer, so a raw str(float) qty reached the Bybit wire for months while the guard read clean
items.detail: scripts/check_qty_legalization_guard.py exists, by its own docstring, for "the recurring 'a sub-lot qty reached the order path' bug class". What it actually enforces is narrower: it fails a file OUTSIDE src/units/accounts/qty_legalize.py that CALLS get_lot_rule or quantize_qty. src/units/accounts/execute.py::close_open_position called NEITHER -- it built the wire payload as {"qty": str(qty)} straight from the journal -- so it passed the guard cleanly while doing exactly the thing the guard is named for. MEASURED: a bybit_1/SOLUSDT reduce-only close was refused 3 consecutive times at 2026-09-06T03:37:22Z on qty '33.299999999999955' (Bybit 'Qty invalid', ErrCode 10001) and the position could not be flattened by the normal path (WO-20260906-A-BYBIT-REDUCE-ONLY-CLOSE-IS-REJECTED, fixed in PR #11125). POPULATION for the incidence: bybit_* accounts, non-backtest, position_size>0, trades ids 4519-5518 (newest 1000 rows, /api/diag/journal?table=trades&limit=1000, read 2026-09-06 ~11:02Z), n=631 -> 9 off-grid = 1.43%, including id=5342 on bybit_2 (REAL MONEY). The gap is structural, not an oversight in one file: an ABSENCE-of-call guard can never see a site that submits a quantity without consulting anything. The positive form -- 'every code path that puts a qty on an exchange wire routes it through the seam' -- is what would have caught this, AND IT WAS ALREADY DESIGNED: docs/sizing-legalization-DESIGN.md section 3.3 lists TWO bullets and only the first was ever built. The second reads 'fails CI if an order leg / _submit_order call is constructed with a qty that did not pass through legalize_qty'. So this is not a new idea to evaluate -- it is an un-built half of a design the repo already accepted, and the un-built half is the one that catches this class. NOTE the honest difficulty before proposing the obvious version: enumerating 'every path that puts a qty on a wire' by AST is not free (place_order is reached through several client wrappers, and a protective-leg amend sends slSize/tpSize rather than qty), so a naive rule risks either misses or a false-positive rate that gets it silenced -- which per CLAUDE.md is worse than no guard. Scope the first version to the Bybit submission sites this repo already knows about.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) the guard gains a check that FAILS a Bybit order-submission site which builds a qty/slSize/tpSize wire value without routing it through src/units/accounts/qty_legalize.py, with a self-test proving it fails on a planted bad site AND passes on the current tree; or (b) a written decision, with reasoning, that the positive form is not tractable here -- in which case the guard's docstring must stop claiming the broader class. Either settles it; leaving the docstring overclaiming does not.

items.title: modify_open_order's slSize/tpSize and _bybit_top_up_partial_sl's uncovered qty both reach Bybit as a raw str(float), the same shape that made a reduce-only close unflattenable -- and here a rejection fails a PROTECTIVE tightening silently
items.detail: Two Bybit sites share the exact shape fixed for the CLOSE path in PR #11125: a float computed by subtraction is put on the wire as str(...) with no step alignment, so an IEEE-754 residue such as 33.299999999999955 is refused with 'Qty invalid' (ErrCode 10001). SITES: src/units/accounts/execute.py:2578,2580 (modify_open_order's slSize / tpSize) and src/runtime/order_monitor.py:9967 (_bybit_top_up_partial_sl's `uncovered = size - bound_covered`, a subtraction of two venue quantities -- precisely the operation that generates the artifact). STATE THE POPULATION HONESTLY: there is NO observed failure at either site. The 9 off-grid values measured over trades ids 4519-5518 (bybit_*, non-backtest, position_size>0, n=631, read 2026-09-06 ~11:02Z) are all `position_size`, i.e. the close path. Nobody has looked at whether these two paths have ever been rejected, and THAT is part of the finding: the amend path's rejections would be hard to see, because a set_trading_stop refusal fails a protective TIGHTENING and the position simply keeps its old (looser, or absent) stop. WHY THIS WAS DELIBERATELY NOT WIDENED INTO PR #11125: no observed failure, and these are protective order paths where a wrong repair is worse than the bug -- own change, own evidence (operator-approved scope was the close path only). WHEN FIXING, DO NOT REACH FOR legalize_qty: it FLOORS (ROUND_DOWN). Flooring a protective leg UNDER-covers the position, which is the direction that leaves a slice of a live position unprotected. qty_legalize.snap_artifact_qty (added in #11125) snaps to NEAREST and is the shape to reuse -- but establish first whether a protective leg wants NEAREST or a deliberate ROUND-UP (over-cover on a reduce-only leg is bounded by the position), because that is a real question this row does not answer.
items.resolution_criteria: First MEASURE, then decide: search the journal / outcomes feed for a Bybit rejection at either site (ErrCode 10001 on a set_trading_stop or an amend) and state the population and n, including when the answer is zero. Then either wire both sites through the qty_legalize seam with a stated rounding direction and a test per site, or record a dated decision that the paths are unaffected, naming the evidence. A zero-rejection measurement CLOSES this row; not looking does not.

items.title: The register merge driver is BUILT and ships DISARMED — a fresh clone has no merge.* config, and one session hand-resolved eleven conflicts beside it
items.detail: NOT a duplicate of BL-20260902-FIVE-MONOLITHIC-JSON-REGISTERS-RECONFLICT-EVERY-SIBLING-PR-ON-EVERY-MERGE and NOT its resolution — it is the half that row's criterion (b) does not cover. That criterion is now BUILT: scripts/ops/merge_json_register.py exists, .gitattributes maps the five registers to it, and it asserts per-id membership both ways exactly as the row demanded. ⚠️ BUT A GIT MERGE DRIVER IS CLIENT-SIDE AND PER-CLONE. Git runs it only after scripts/ops/install_merge_driver.sh has registered it in THAT clone's config, and .gitattributes says so in its own header ('SHIPPING IT IS NOT ARMING IT, AND FOR THE FIRST DAY NOBODY WAS ARMED'). Nothing in the session-start contract, CLAUDE.md, or any skill tells a session to run the installer, and a remote session's container is a FRESH CLONE every time — so the default state of every new session is DISARMED. MEASURED COST, one session (session_017UnyG4ArXmXKpB8rmEGv1j, MI-139b, PR #11125, 2026-09-06): `git config --get-regexp '^merge\.'` returned NOTHING in a container whose tree contained both the driver and the .gitattributes mapping. That session hand-resolved ELEVEN conflicts between 11:26Z and 18:15Z — nine in health-review-backlog.json, one in OPEN-PRS.json, one in a work-object YAML — none in its order-path diff, and reached five green heads of which four went stale before the merge could be routed. ⚠️ THE HAND RESOLUTIONS WERE NOT WASTED EFFORT AND THIS IS NOT AN ARGUMENT THAT THEY WERE: one round preserved six of main's rows plus two edits, and another preserved an operator's `approved_with_conditions` verdict on PR #10940 that a side-wise resolution would have erased — the exact hazard CLAUDE.md calls worse than a missing row. The point is that a driver written to do precisely that work sat unarmed one directory away.
items.evidence: In-container, on origin/main @9604b8a5: `git config --get-regexp '^merge\.'` -> no output (exit 1); `ls -la scripts/ops/install_merge_driver.sh` -> present, mode 755; `cat .gitattributes` -> present, maps the five registers and carries the 'SHIPPING IT IS NOT ARMING IT' warning in its own header. Conflict count and timestamps: PR #11125 comment 5559817050 (first five, tabulated) plus the merge commits on claude/bybit-close-qty-apply-20260906 for rounds 6-11. Stale green heads: 765d83a2, 76167f7b, 5c290327, 8b37e208; merged on 7c17a2af as 9604b8a5.
items.resolution_criteria: The driver is ARMED BY DEFAULT for a session that did not think to arm it, and that is VERIFIED rather than assumed. Candidates, in rough order of how little they depend on anyone remembering: (a) the session-start contract or a repo bootstrap step runs install_merge_driver.sh, so a fresh container arms itself; (b) a guard or the session brief READS `git config --get-regexp '^merge\.'` and says plainly that the clone is disarmed — cheap, and it converts an invisible default into a visible one; (c) documented in CLAUDE.md § PM-side session capabilities beside the other per-clone facts. ⚠️ DO NOT CLOSE THIS BY ADDING A REMINDER TO A DOC NOBODY READS MID-TASK — that is the 'reminder is not a mechanism' non-fix this repo has already paid for on MI-15 (twice). ⚠️ AND DO NOT CLAIM IT FIXES GITHUB-SIDE MERGEABILITY: .gitattributes already states that GitHub's servers do not run custom merge drivers, so an armed clone removes the HAND-RESOLUTION cost and does NOT make a dirty PR auto-mergeable. A row claiming otherwise would be claiming a fix that is not there. ⚠️ VERIFY BY ARMING A CLONE AND MERGING A REAL DIVERGENT APPEND — not by observing that the file exists, which is what was already true while eleven conflicts were resolved by hand.

items.title: The OPEN-PRS reconciler fires per-merge, so a busy day stacks N simultaneously-open PRs for one derived edit
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-06T16:55Z. SIX reconcile-open-prs PRs were open at once - #11160, #11152, #11145, #11142, #11106, #11099 - spanning 09:10Z to 15:49Z. Population: 6 of 6 inspected with `git diff origin/main...`; 6 of 6 produce an IDENTICAL +30/-20 shape on docs/claude/work/OPEN-PRS.json, and the substantive content of all six is ONE move: the #11105 row from open_prs into settled_prs with terminal closed_unmerged. CAUSE: the reconciler is triggered per merge to main. On a day with roughly 45 merges it therefore cuts a PR per merge, and each is stale the moment the next lands, so they accumulate rather than replace each other. COST is manager attention in exactly the register the merge-queue duty exists to keep readable: six rows of queue noise competing with PRs that carry real work, each needing to be opened and diffed before it can be dismissed. It also multiplies the conflict surface named in BL-20260902-FIVE-MONOLITHIC-JSON-REGISTERS-RECONFLICT-EVERY-SIBLING-PR-ON-EVERY-MERGE, since all six touch the same region of the same monolithic JSON file. NOT A DUPLICATE, and the near neighbours were read before filing. BL-20260905-A-RECONCILE-PR-CUT-BEFORE-A-DISPOSITION-LANDS-WILL-ERASE-IT-ON-MERGE-WITH-IDENTICAL-ROW-COUNTS is about a stale reconcile DESTROYING a disposition on merge - a correctness defect in what one PR contains. BL-20260902-FIVE-MONOLITHIC-JSON-REGISTERS-RECONFLICT-EVERY-SIBLING-PR-ON-EVERY-MERGE is about the file SHAPE making siblings conflict. This row is about the TRIGGER CADENCE producing N of them for one edit, which neither addresses, and which is why closing five and merging one does not stop it recurring tomorrow. Discarding them is SAFE and that is load-bearing to the disposition: this reconcile is DERIVED state, recomputed from GitHub's live open-PR list on every run, so a discarded reconcile costs a recomputation and loses no information. That is why the remedy is safe to make lazier - not why the problem is unimportant.
items.resolution_criteria: The reconciler no longer produces one PR per merge. Either (a) it runs on a SCHEDULE, or is debounced/coalesced, so at most one reconcile PR is open at a time, or (b) a new run UPDATES the existing open reconcile PR's branch instead of cutting a fresh one, or (c) it is shown that a no-op run opens no PR at all AND the six observed here each carried a genuine distinct delta - which the measurement above REFUTES for this instance, so (c) requires new evidence rather than a re-reading of this one. VERIFY BY OBSERVATION, NOT BY READING THE WORKFLOW: count simultaneously-open 'chore(ops): reconcile OPEN-PRS.json' PRs after a day with more than ~10 merges to main. A green workflow edit is not that observation. And a count of 1 on a QUIET day proves nothing - state the merge count alongside the PR count or the denominator is missing.
items.source: manager session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj, while running the merge queue 2026-09-06

items.title: exit-refinement-coverage.json justifies regime_flip_exit:n/a for ict_scalp_5m with a reason that is false — the leg has two OFF cells
items.detail: docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json grades ict_scalp_5m regime_flip_exit as `n/a` with ref: "Fires on an ADX->OFF regime-policy cell; ict_scalp has no regime-policy cell so the flip never fires." FIELD BEATS COMMENT: the cells exist. This is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A (CLAUDE.md): a status reported under a justification naming a condition no code path tested, so a reader who trusts it concludes the leg is ungated when it is gated. The `n/a` VERDICT may still be correct for a different reason (the same ref also calls the mechanism a fleet-wide honest_negative) — the finding is the REASON, not necessarily the grade. The finding is independent of which lever was pulled, so it is carried across here rather than lost with the closed PR — the leg still carries execution: live, so this row's subject is unchanged. Found while establishing whether ict_scalp_5m's exit levers had ever been run (docs/research/ict-scalp-5m-real-money-verdict-2026-09-06.md § 4a).

Whoever fixes it must also decide and RECORD whether n/a is still the right grade given the cells DO exist — if the real basis is the fleet-wide honest_negative the same ref already cites, say that alone and drop the false clause; if the cells make the lever genuinely applicable, the grade changes to pending and the leg joins the sweep queue. items.title: BL-20260730-PR-CI-NOT-ATTACHING's open per-EVENT question has a MECHANISM: a bot-opened PR's checks are not dropped, they are CREATED and land conclusion=action_required (awaiting approval), and get_check_runs cannot see them
items.detail: ANSWERS the standing open question in BL-20260730-PR-CI-NOT-ATTACHING, which after PR #10029 narrowed to 'a per-EVENT delivery drop -- the opened delivery was dropped and the synchronize delivery arrived' and asked for a per-event-type denominator. THE PREMISE IS WRONG IN A USEFUL WAY: nothing is dropped. The runs ARE created; they complete immediately with conclusion=action_required, i.e. HELD AWAITING APPROVAL because the run's triggering_actor is github-actions[bot]. MEASURED 2026-09-06, two PRs, with a positive control. (a) PR #11189 (opened 21:41:50Z by claude-pr-automerge): pull_request_read method=get_check_runs returned total_count=1 (only the opener's own job) and mergeable_state 'blocked' -- NOT 'dirty', so the merge-ref cause this row already documents does NOT apply. actions_list on the same branch showed FOUR runs (Guards, pytest-run, pytest-collect, repo-inventory), all event=pull_request, all head_sha 3aaffef8, all status=completed conclusion=action_required, all triggering_actor github-actions[bot], created 21:41:53-54Z. (b) POSITIVE CONTROL on PR #11188 in the same window: its runs from the AUTHOR's push ran normally (in_progress 21:42:41Z), while its 'pr-opener: results' commit -- pushed by github-actions[bot] -- produced action_required runs at 21:43:03Z. Same repo, same workflows, same minutes; the only variable is the actor. That is exactly the #10029 pattern ('opened' inert, 'synchronize' fine): the bot opens the PR, and the human's next push is what executes. WHY IT READS AS 'CI HAS NOT STARTED': an action_required run is NOT surfaced as a check run, so get_check_runs shows a low or zero total_count. This is a THIRD read-surface trap on the same question, distinct from the two CLAUDE.md documents -- (i) get_status reads the commit-status API and never sees Actions at all, (ii) mergeable_state 'dirty' means no merge ref so nothing runs, and now (iii) runs exist but are gated pending approval, visible ONLY via actions_list. Read mergeable_state to separate (ii) from (iii): 'dirty' is a conflict, 'blocked' with runs held is this. ⚠️ CLAUDE.md's pr-opener/board-post note attributes this to 'GitHub does not trigger workflows for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes'. The REMEDY it gives (push one ordinary commit yourself) is correct and works; the stated MECHANISM is not what is observable -- the workflows ARE triggered. That matters because it changes what else is available: a maintainer can APPROVE the held runs instead of pushing, and a session that believes nothing was triggered will not look for them in actions_list. ⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED, deliberately: WHY the approval gate applies here (repo Actions setting, org policy, or the fork/first-time-contributor rule) is a settings question this session cannot read, and no denominator is claimed -- this is n=2 PRs in one window, not a rate. The narrower claim that IS established is the mechanism and its read surface.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) the approval gate is identified and removed/scoped so bot-opened PRs run CI directly -- needs repo Actions settings, which is operator-side; or (b) the documented remedy is corrected in place: CLAUDE.md's pr-opener/board-post note and BL-20260730-PR-CI-NOT-ATTACHING both say 'delivery dropped' where the observable state is action_required, and both should name actions_list as the surface that reveals it plus mergeable_state as the way to tell a conflict from a held run. ⚠️ Do NOT close this on a single PR whose CI later went green after a push -- that is the remedy working, not the gate being gone.
items.evidence: actions_list method=list_workflow_runs branch=claude/mi143b-closeout-20260906 -> 5 runs, 4 with conclusion=action_required, triggering_actor github-actions[bot]; same call on claude/mi147-backtest-soak-chain-20260906 -> action_required on the 'pr-opener: results' head 0ac6355a while the author-push runs on 71a6c15a executed. pull_request_read get_check_runs on #11189 -> total_count 1; get method=get -> mergeable_state 'blocked' (not 'dirty').

items.title: claude-pr-automerge races pr-opener on a branch's first push and the authored PR title/body is discarded
items.detail: OBSERVED 2026-09-06 on PR #11188 (MI-147). Both relays trigger on a push to claude/**: claude-pr-automerge.yml on .github/pr-automerge-requests/<slug>.txt and pr-opener.yml on automation/pr-requests/<slug>.json. The landing contract requires BOTH files, so a session that pushes the automerge request with its first commit hands claude-pr-automerge the earlier trigger. It find-or-opens the PR with title = head-commit subject and its own GENERIC body ('Opened by the claude-pr-automerge workflow...'). pr-opener then wrote 'FAILED: a pull request for branch ... already exists' to automation/pr-results/<slug>.txt and DISCARDED the authored title and body. MEASURED on #11188: the body was the 4-line generic text; the authored body was 6156 characters. NOT RECOVERABLE IN-SESSION — update_pull_request 403s (write-scope boundary) and so does add_issue_comment, so the session can neither edit the body nor post it as a comment; the PR permanently under-describes its own change on the surface a reviewer reads first. The finding survived only because it was committed as a doc under docs/research/. NOT a duplicate of the documented 'relay results commit buries CI' trap — that one is about check runs, and both happened on this same PR.
items.resolution_criteria: A PR whose branch pushes BOTH .github/pr-automerge-requests/<slug>.txt and automation/pr-requests/<slug>.json in the same push carries the title and body from the pr-request JSON rather than the automerge generic body — OBSERVED on a real PR, not asserted from the workflow diff. Equivalently: automation/pr-results/<slug>.txt no longer reports FAILED-already-exists when the existing PR was opened by the automerge relay for the same branch.

items.title: The exit-head artifact has declared a `family` since export_exit_head.py:116 and the in-distribution guard never read it — tf+symbols cannot separate two strategies on the same symbol and timeframe
items.detail:
FOUND WHILE WIRING, not by audit. `exit_head_shadow.maybe_score_exit_head`'s in-distribution guard is the #6201-class protection: its own comment says it exists because "an out-of-family score would pollute the shadow track record (the 2026-07-12 IWM-1d rows)". It gates on the artifact's `tf` and its `symbols` list. IT NEVER READS THE ARTIFACT'S `family` FIELD, which scripts/ml/export_exit_head.py:116 has written on every artifact it exports (`"family": fam_dir.name`).

WHY tf+symbols IS NOT SUFFICIENT, and why this was harmless until now: those two fields identify a MARKET, not a STRATEGY. Two different strategies trading the SAME symbol on the SAME timeframe are indistinguishable to this guard. That was inert while donchian was the only family with a published head -- measured 2026-09-06 on /api/diag/shadow_stats, the live mirror carries exactly two exit_head artifacts, exit-head-donchian-1h-v1 (advisory) and exit-head-donchian-peak-1h-v1 (shadow), both 1h. It stops being inert the moment a second family publishes one: ict_scalp and trend_donchian both trade SOLUSDT, and a scalp head at 5m/15m would be exactly the collision.

PARTIALLY FIXED IN MI-150, AND THE UNFIXED HALF IS THE POINT OF THIS ROW. The gate is now CALLER-OPT-IN: `maybe_score_exit_head(..., family=...)`, checked against the artifact's own field, with a mismatch logged at WARNING naming both values (a silent refusal is indistinguishable from a trainer naming difference, which would present 'the dir was named differently' as 'this head never fires'). ict_scalp passes `family="ict_scalp"`. **trend_donchian deliberately passes NOTHING and is still ungated.**

THE REASON FOR THAT ASYMMETRY IS AN UNMEASURED VALUE, NOT A JUDGEMENT: WHAT `family` VALUE THE LIVE ADVISORY ARTIFACT ACTUALLY CARRIES HAS NOT BEEN READ. The artifact dir (runtime_logs/trainer_mirror/exit_head/) is not on the diag log_file allowlist, so a PM-side session cannot read it; the token is minted by the trainer as a directory name this repo does not control. exit-head-donchian-1h-v1 is at stage `advisory` and CLOSES REAL POSITIONS on three live legs, so gating it against a string nobody has read is how a working exit gate goes quiet -- the failure would be silent and would look exactly like 'the head is not firing today'.

⚠️ THE FIX IS NOT 'ALSO PASS family FROM DONCHIAN'. That is one line and it is the dangerous line. The order is: (1) read the value off the mirror, (2) confirm it is in _ACCEPTED_FAMILIES['donchian'] = {donchian, trend_donchian}, (3) then gate. Step (1) needs either a trainer-relay read or an addition to the diag allowlist.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH: (a) the `family` value on exit-head-donchian-1h-v1 is READ from the live mirror (trainer-vm-diag relay, or by allowlisting the exit_head artifact dir on /api/diag/log_file) and RECORDED here -- reading it is the whole blocker and is worth doing even if nothing else follows; and (b) either the donchian call site passes its family once that value is confirmed accepted, or a decision is recorded that donchian stays ungated and WHY. ⚠️ Do NOT close this on the ict_scalp half alone: that half is already done and closing on it would leave the live advisory path ungated behind a row that reads resolved.

items.opened_by: claude (MI-150, found by reading the full cell refs the memo summarised)
items.title: MI-146's ship recommendation summarised five matrix cells and dropped the 2026-08-23 SHIP-BLOCKED/ship-CANCELLED operator decision recorded inside those same cells
items.detail:
docs/research/exit-lever-wiring-audit-2026-09-06.md § 'Recommendation 2' presents five ict_scalp exit_head_ml cells as "the ONLY cells in the entire matrix that passed their gate and are blocked on wiring alone", with a table of AUC / beats_actual and a ship/exclude disposition. The dispatch brief built from it repeated that table. BOTH omit two things that are written into the very cells being cited:

1. EVERY ONE OF THE FIVE CARRIES A 2026-08-23 `SHIP BLOCKED` OPERATOR DECISION which re-graded it passed_unshipped -> blocked, and for ict_scalp_sol_5m states outright: "this cell was QUEUED for a Tier-3 ship and the ship is CANCELLED (operator decision 2026-08-23)".
2. FOR ict_scalp_sol_5m THE PASS IS CONTESTED BY A LATER SCREEN: "its pass does not survive re-partitioning -- the 4-arm screen flips it to honest_negative when folds are cut 12 trades later, and its AUC spread across the arms (0.0034) is the SMALLEST of the three legs, so the AUC gave no warning at all" (BL-20260815-SCALP-EXIT-HEAD-MATRIX-DISAGREES-WITH-THE-4-ARM-SCREEN). Its live-parity beats_hard is 16/23 -- clearing by 2 points of 46, so one fold the other way fails it. The memo quotes the passing beats_actual 22/23 and not the marginal binding term.

WHY THIS IS THE DANGEROUS SHAPE AND NOT A TIDINESS COMPLAINT. CLAUDE.md § OPEN-PRS states the principle exactly: a successor knowing NOTHING stalls and re-asks (safe), while one knowing 'approved' WITHOUT the condition can act on it -- "only the half-informed case is dangerous, and a row recording a verdict without its condition is WORSE than a missing row because it reads as complete." A session handed the memo's table and told the operator approved it has everything it needs to ARM a lever over a cancelled ship, on a leg whose pass a later screen reverses. MI-150 came within one unread field of exactly that, and only avoided it by reading the full 2210-3464 character cell refs the memo had summarised into one row each.

NOT THE MEMO'S ACCURACY: the numbers MI-146 quotes are correct as far as they go, and its recommendation (ship the CONSUMER, annotate-first) is the right call and survives the fuller record intact. The defect is that a summary of a cell dropped the cell's OPERATOR DECISION while keeping the cell's METRICS, and metrics without their decision read as a green light.
items.resolution_criteria: A mechanism, not a reminder -- the pattern is already recorded twice (BL-20260903 OPEN-PRS condition-dropping; the CLAUDE.md § OPEN-PRS half-informed-case rule) and prose did not hold. Candidate: a check that any artifact citing a coverage-matrix cell by name must also surface any operator-decision segment in that cell's `ref` (the refs already mark them with recognisable `SHIP BLOCKED (operator decision)` / `operator decision <date>` tokens, so this is greppable). Closing this needs either that check, or a recorded operator decision that memo-level summarisation is accepted as lossy and readers must always open the cell.
