items.title: The ict_scalp exit-head consumer shipped and cannot score any of its 8 legs — the live mirror publishes only 1h artifacts and every scalp leg is 5m/15m
items.detail:
MEASURED, NOT INFERRED. /api/diag/shadow_stats read 2026-09-06 (last_seen 10:00:01Z) returns exactly two exit_head model_ids on the live mirror: exit-head-donchian-1h-v1 (advisory) and exit-head-donchian-peak-1h-v1 (shadow), count 52 each. BOTH ARE 1h. All 8 ict_scalp legs in config/strategies.yaml are 5m or 15m (5m: ict_scalp_5m, _sol_5m, _xrp_5m, _avax_5m; 15m: _xrp_15m, _eth_15m, _sol_15m, _mgc_15m).

exit_head_shadow.maybe_score_exit_head's in-distribution guard skips any artifact whose `tf` does not equal the leg's, so it fail-closes on every scalp leg and returns None. That is the guard working CORRECTLY -- scoring a 5m trade with a 1h head is exactly the out-of-family pollution it exists to prevent (the 2026-07-12 IWM-1d rows).

WHY THIS IS WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A SHRUG. MI-146 identified these five cells as the ONLY passed-gate work in the 468-cell matrix blocked on missing code, and MI-150 wrote that code. The blocker did not clear -- it MOVED, from MISSING CODE to MISSING ARTIFACT, and the second blocker is invisible from the matrix (which grades cells, not the mirror) and from the unit source (which now contains a perfectly good consumer). A future session reading either surface would conclude the lever is ready.

⚠️ AND THE SOAK'S SILENCE IS NOT EVIDENCE. The consumer writes runtime_logs/ict_scalp_exit_head_soak.jsonl on EVERY outcome including `decision_state: not_scored`, deliberately, so a DEAD consumer stays distinguishable from a SILENT one. Once deployed the log will fill immediately with not_scored rows and carry zero firing rows, possibly forever. Read that as *we cannot look*, never as *the head declined to fire*.

NOT A DEFECT IN ANY SHIPPED CODE -- nothing here is broken. It is a gap between what was trained and what was wired, and it is only actionable trainer-side.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) a 5m and/or 15m ict_scalp exit-head artifact is trained and published to runtime_logs/trainer_mirror/exit_head/ AND a soak row is observed with decision_state != not_scored and a non-null model_id (i.e. the in-distribution guard actually admitted a leg); OR (b) a recorded decision that no scalp head will be trained, which is a legitimate outcome and must be written down as a DECISION rather than left looking like a soak about to start. ⚠️ Do NOT close this on the consumer existing -- that is the half MI-150 delivered and is not what this row tracks. ⚠️ And note (a) is necessary but not sufficient for ARMING: arming additionally needs evidence surviving re-partitioning and is blocked by the 2026-08-23 SHIP BLOCKED operator decision.

items.title: scripts/research/backtest_fidelity_calibrate.py calls itself 'the earned-trust linchpin (P0)' and has produced ZERO artifacts in its lifetime -- and even once run it grades OUTCOME agreement (win-rate + realised-R), not exit LOCATION, which is what ML-2's claim is about
items.detail:
TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS, and conflating them would make the second invisible once the first is fixed.

(1) NEVER RUN. The module's docstring names its output convention as comms/research/backtest_fidelity_<strategy>_<symbol>.json. MEASURED 2026-09-06 on origin/main 817a5a5f: no such file exists anywhere in the repo. POSITIVE CONTROL for that negative, because a search returning nothing is not proof of absence -- comms/research/ DOES exist and DOES hold one artifact (crypto_correlation_2026-08-18.json), and a whole-tree `find` for *fidelity* returns only source and test files (scripts/research/backtest_fidelity_{calibrate,cost_ab}.py, tests/test_backtest_fidelity_calibrate.py, plus two unrelated *fidelity* scripts), never an output. So the directory is real and writable and the calibrator has written nothing into it. Its own stated purpose is to end the practice of capping every decision at live-trade accrual: 'we have never MEASURED whether our backtests are right, so we fell back to only trust real live trades -- which caps every decision at reality's clock.' That cap is still in force, and the instrument built to lift it has never been switched on.

(2) IT GRADES THE WRONG QUANTITY FOR THE EXIT-LOCATION QUESTION, so running it does NOT close this row. Its two axes are win-rate agreement and a two-sample KS on the realised-R distribution -- an OUTCOME question. ML-2's claim (PROCESS.md E3.6) is about WHERE a trade exits, in percent-of-entry. Those can diverge: two books can share a win rate and an R distribution while exiting at systematically different distances. And the R axis drags in the contaminated live denominator -- trades.stop_loss is the FINAL trailed stop, which is exactly why MI-148 chose percent-of-entry for the calibration instrument. A fidelity verdict computed in R cannot license a target set in percent-of-entry.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: MI-151 built the ML-2 corpus from the offline harness (166k-184k 15m bars/symbol on the trainer), which is the un-circular source MI-148 gated its clause 1 on. Every number from that corpus is a statement about the HARNESS'S book. Condition 1 of MI-151's proposed gate is precisely this measurement, so until it exists no per-leg target may be set from backtest MFE quantiles.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH, and say which you did. (a) backtest_fidelity_calibrate.py has been RUN on at least one (strategy, symbol) with both a backtest and a live population, and its artifact is committed at a durable path -- an expired CI artifact is not a locator (see BL-20260823-E35-SWEEP-EVIDENCE-HAS-NO-DURABLE-PATH). (b) A separate EXIT-LOCATION fidelity comparison exists on the percent-of-entry basis: the backtest emit's exit_frac distribution against MI-148's live --exits view, per leg, with an abstain floor and the per-leg n stated. Both halves already exist on one basis (scripts/research/ml2_bracket_corpus.py built the backtest half, src/runtime/bracket_calibration.py the live half), so this is constructible and blocked on nothing. Closing on (a) alone leaves ML-2's gate condition 1 unmet and must not be recorded as closing it.

items.tier: 1 — CI/automation tooling (.github/workflows/**); no src/, config/ or order path
items.summary: trainer-diag-relay.yml's commit-back step is `git push origin HEAD:${{ github.ref_name }}` under `set -euo pipefail`, with no rebase and no retry. When a second relay triggered by the SAME push (board-post.yml, pr-opener.yml) commits to the branch first, the relay's push is a non-fast-forward, the step fails, and a result it had ALREADY COMPUTED on the trainer is discarded. Measured 2026-09-07 (MI-154b): request mi154b-scalp-probe-20260907 produced no result after a push that also carried automation/board-posts/; board-post committed 228f2719 first and the relay lost the race. Re-sent ALONE under a fresh name, the identical script returned state=ran remote_exit=0 in ~30s. WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A LOST RUN: the failure presents as an ABSENT result file, byte-identical to 'the relay never fired' and to 'the trainer is unreachable' -- three faults with three different remedies collapsed into one silent state, and the natural first suspicion is the trainer's health, which was fine throughout. It cost ~25 minutes of misdiagnosis. All three push-triggered relays (trainer-diag-relay, board-post, pr-opener) share this commit-back shape, so any two triggered by one push can collide.
items.resolution_criteria: A trainer-diag request and a board-post pushed in ONE commit both produce their result files: `git show origin/<branch>:automation/trainer-diag-results/<name>.txt` returns a result whose header reads state=ran, AND `automation/board-results/<name>.txt` also exists, on the same branch, from that single push. That is the exact sequence that fails today. IF THE PUSH RACE IS INSTEAD MADE LOUD RATHER THAN FIXED, the equivalent observation is that the losing relay's workflow run concludes FAILURE (visible via get_check_runs or the run page) instead of green-with-no-file -- because the defect being closed is the SILENT discard, not the retry itself. A green run with no result file closes nothing. A passing unit test is NOT this observation: the race is between two live workflow runs committing to one ref, which a unit test cannot reproduce.
items.evidence: .github/workflows/trainer-diag-relay.yml 'Commit results back to branch' step; run 34081562219 (state=ran, request sent alone) vs the silent first attempt on the same script; branch claude/mi154b-scalp-artifact-20260907

items.summary: position_telemetry carries ZERO rows for any ict_scalp leg, so the one strategy family the exit-geometry thread calls its existence proof of a calibrated bracket has no MFE record at all — and the absence is invisible because the MFE instruments report per-leg n only for legs that appear
items.evidence: MEASURED 2026-09-07 (MI-155, docs/research/exit-location-fidelity-2026-09-07.md). POPULATION: all 171 rows of /api/diag/position_telemetry?limit=1000 read 2026-09-07 — 0 rows carry a strategy beginning 'ict_scalp', across 35 distinct legs present. POPULATION: config/strategies.yaml at main e4fa09c7 — 8 enabled+live ict_scalp legs (ict_scalp_5m, _sol_5m, _xrp_5m, _avax_5m, _eth_15m, _mgc_15m, _sol_15m, _xrp_15m). The trades exist: MI-148 (docs/research/bracket-calibration-2026-09-06.md) graded 162 ict_scalp trades over 8 legs in its --exits view, which reads `trades`, not position_telemetry. So this is a telemetry-writer gap, not an absence of trading. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND COVERAGE: MI-146, MI-148 and MI-151 all name ict_scalp as the fleet's ONLY family with a calibrated bracket (fixed tp_at_r 1.5, zero clamp-binding, targets at quantile 0.69-0.92 of its own outcomes) and therefore the reference any per-leg target would be constructed against — and the MFE basis on which such a target is set cannot see it. MI-155 grades all 8 ict_scalp legs insufficient_n with n_live=0 for this reason.
items.resolution_criteria: A position_telemetry row carrying an ict_scalp* strategy is OBSERVED on the fleet with a readable peak_r/cap_r — read the table, not the writer diff. If the omission turns out to be DELIBERATE (e.g. the 5m/15m exit loop does not run the telemetry writer by design), that is a valid resolution but must be RECORDED as a decision with its reason, not left looking like a gap about to be filled — and MI-155's memo plus the RESEARCH-CAPABILITY-INDEX row for exit_location_fidelity.py must then say that ict_scalp is out of scope by construction rather than under-sampled.

items.title: tests/test_backtest_ict_cli.py ran the full ICT backtester across four constant-price fixtures and asserted success -- a green that checked nothing
items.resolution_criteria: ALREADY MET on 2026-09-07, and stated so a reader can re-check rather than trust this row. THREE observable conditions, all asserted as tests rather than observed once: (1) `python3 scripts/ci/check_candle_fixture_variance.py` exits 0 over every tracked file AND prints a non-zero graded population -- both halves, because a run that graded nothing also exits 0; (2) the same command exits 1 and NAMES the file when handed a 300-row constant-price CSV (tests/test_candle_fixture_non_degeneracy.py::test_guard_actually_fails_on_a_flat_file) while exiting 0 on data/backtest_candles.csv (::test_guard_passes_the_real_committed_corpus); (3) tests/test_backtest_ict_cli.py::test_ict_validate_manifest_absent_data_fails_loudly passes, i.e. a manifest pair whose candle file is absent produces a NAMED per-pair error instead of a silent zero-trade success. This row REOPENS if `candle-fixture-variance-guard` is removed from scripts/ci/run_guards.py or if any committed candle file grades `degenerate` again.
items.detail: MI-157. FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE THAT FILED THIS -- recorded because the CLASS is what matters, not the instance. test_ict_validate_manifest_runs_all_pairs called backtest_ict_cli.run_all() over all four pairs in data/ict_validate_manifest.csv and asserted `failed == []`. Every one of those four paths pointed at a committed fixture holding 300 rows with EXACTLY ONE DISTINCT CLOSE (btc 95000.0, eth 3200.0, spy 580.0, qqq 490.0; open/high/low constant too). So what the test certified was that the harness does not crash on a flat line -- it could not have failed for any reason connected to trading logic, because a series that does not move cannot produce a trade, a return, or an expectancy. POPULATION: all 4 manifest pairs, i.e. 100% of what the test covered. It is docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md's 'green is not evidence' in its purest form, and it had been passing since the fixtures were added in 29014899. WHY IT SURVIVED: the assertion was true and the data was meaningless, and nothing in the test's own output distinguished those. RESIDUAL WORTH KNOWING: three sibling tests in the same file (test_run_pair_end_to_end_no_trades, test_main_writes_output_file, test_main_config_flag_accepted) used a _make_flat_csv helper for the same convenience; the helper now oscillates the close inside a fixed gapless high/low band, so they still get zero trades for the reason they claim rather than because the market does not exist.
items.checked: Read the test and the five fixtures directly; ran the census over every tracked file; confirmed the 46 pytest collection errors and the 10 mobile-push failures in this container are PRE-EXISTING by re-running them against a stashed origin/main tree (identical counts both ways).

items.title: A sub-session dispatch names a work object path that does not exist, and calls it the contract
items.tier: 1 — the detector is tooling; writing the object is docs
items.resolution_criteria: scripts/ops/session_registry.py::register REFUSES (or loudly warns on) a spawn whose named work_object path does not resolve to a file on origin/main, AND that refusal is OBSERVED firing once against a deliberately bad path (a planted-negative control) as well as passing on a good one. ⚠️ A green registration is NOT the observation: today every registration is green and the check does not exist, so 'register ran and did not complain' is indistinguishable from the current state. ⚠️ AND FIXING THE TWO KNOWN INSTANCES BY HAND CLOSES NOTHING - both were already fixed by hand, by the sessions that hit them, which is precisely why the class survived to recur.
items.found_by: MI-156 (session_0148fMEXBbDgQU3qsrcWujtx), 2026-09-07
items.detail: RECURRENCE, filed as one because the earlier instance was recorded only in a memo and left no detector. MI-156 was dispatched against docs/claude/work/objects/WO-20260907-25-OF-44-ENABLED-LIVE-LEGS-HAVE.yaml with the words 'Read it - it carries your done_condition verbatim and it is the contract'. THE FILE DID NOT EXIST on origin/main 383a4f7. POSITIVE CONTROL for the probe: the same `git ls-tree` over docs/claude/work/objects/ returned 72 other WO-*.yaml files, and the only 2026-09-07 object present was WO-20260907-PER-LEG-BACKTEST-TO-LIVE-EXIT-LOCATION.yaml - so this is a real absence, not a dead probe. MI-148 records the IDENTICAL failure for its own brief ('The work object named in the brief did not exist on origin/main or on disk; this branch creates it'), which makes this at least the second occurrence in the same workstream inside two days. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the work object is what the operating model designates as the durable carrier of a done_condition, precisely so the contract survives the session and the prompt. When it is absent the session must transcribe the contract from its own prompt, which is (a) unverifiable by anyone else, (b) lost when the session ends, and (c) silently weaker than the thing it is presented as. A session that does NOT notice simply reports done against a contract nobody can read. Both known instances were caught only because the session happened to try to open the file. NOT FIXED HERE. MI-156 created the object itself (the MI-148 precedent) and labelled the done_condition as transcribed-from-prose rather than recovered. CANDIDATE REMEDY, not implemented: the spawn path already goes through scripts/ops/session_registry.py register, which is where a work-object path could be checked to exist at registration time - the same shape as check_manager_scope.py's session-registry-guard. A dispatch naming a non-existent object is mechanically detectable and currently is not detected.

items.resolution_criteria: A session that does NOT hold this session's context can post a coordination-board START and READ IT BACK on the board surface -- observed, not asserted. Concretely, ALL THREE: (1) a board post succeeds by one of the two documented paths, i.e. either MCP add_issue_comment returns 2xx or automation/board-results/<name>.txt holds a bare comment URL and the board-post.yml run exits 0 -- a FAILED: line or a non-zero run is NOT this; (2) the comment is visible on the board issue the docs point at, fetched back rather than inferred from the post succeeding; and (3) CLAUDE.md, docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md, docs/claude/coordination-board.md, the session-coordination skill AND .github/workflows/board-post.yml all name the SAME board issue -- verified by grepping each of the five, because the 2026-09-01 finding was precisely that a relay nobody can find from the surface they read is equivalent to no relay. [!] A GREEN board-post.yml RUN IS NOT SUFFICIENT ON ITS OWN and must not be read as closing this: the run that produced this row exited non-zero with the GraphQL ceiling error, so a future green proves the post landed somewhere -- clause (3) is what establishes it landed where every other session is looking. [!] IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES the board should be retired or replaced with a different substrate, this row does NOT close on a workaround -- it CHANGES: record the decision and the new mechanism, and the criteria above re-point at that mechanism. Sessions being unable to coordinate is the condition being tracked, not issue #6927 specifically. [!] AND IT DOES NOT CLOSE ON A SUCCESSOR ISSUE ALONE -- something must WATCH the live comment count and warn before 2500. #6927 was created 2026-07-19 and hit the ceiling 2026-09-07, i.e. it filled in about SEVEN WEEKS, so a successor with no cap watch only resets the timer on this same outage; this repo's own rule is that a finding without a permanent detector recurs. (Added by MI-161, session_01NriFh691pHJFiVc7agPHnC, which hit the identical ceiling independently the same hour and dropped its duplicate row in favour of this one.)
items.title: GitHub issue #6927 has exceeded 2500 comments, so commenting is DISABLED on it -- the coordination-board START post that CLAUDE.md and CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL make MANDATORY before a session's first substantive tool call is now impossible via EVERY documented path.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-07 by this session, both documented paths, in order.

(1) MCP: add_issue_comment on benbaichmankass/metis-insights#6927 -> 403 Resource not accessible by integration. This is the documented write-scope boundary, NOT the transient hosted-MCP drop, so a retry loop does not clear it. CLAUDE.md's remedy for exactly this is the board-post.yml relay.

(2) RELAY: pushed automation/board-posts/mi159-start.md on branch claude/mi159-board-post-only. The workflow ran and wrote automation/board-results/mi159-start.txt containing:
    FAILED:
    GraphQL: Commenting is disabled on issues with more than 2500 comments (addComment)

So the relay behaved CORRECTLY -- it failed loudly and failed the run, which is its documented design ('a session that believes it claimed the board and did not is invisible to every other session AND to itself'). The relay is not the defect. The BOARD is: GitHub hard-disables addComment past 2500 comments and #6927 has crossed it.

WHY THIS IS HIGH AND NOT COSMETIC. The board is not advisory. CLAUDE.md: 'Before your first substantive tool call: check the live coordination board ... and post a START comment naming the files/subsystems/VM you're about to touch.' docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md makes it binding. Every concurrent session is now structurally unable to comply -- the same shape as BL-20260901-COORDINATION-BOARD-WRITES-403-FROM-THIS-SESSION-WHILE-READS-SUCCEED but STRICTLY WORSE, because that one had a working relay as its remedy and this closes the remedy too. A capability that is mandatory and unreachable is, for its user, identical to no capability at all.

SECOND-ORDER RISK, the part that actually costs something: the board is the collision-avoidance mechanism between concurrent sessions. With it dead, nothing warns session B that session A is mid-edit on the same file. The 2026-07-22 incident this rule exists to prevent (a /system-review session colliding unnoticed with a live concurrent session mid-trainer-VM-work) can now recur with no detector.

NOT DIAGNOSED HERE, and stated rather than implied: whether READS on #6927 still work (this session did not need one), and whether any other workflow posts to #6927 and is therefore also failing. Both are worth checking as part of the fix.

CANDIDATE REMEDIES, none applied by this session (all outside a Tier-1 docs scope, and one is an operator call): (a) open a successor board issue and repoint CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md, docs/claude/coordination-board.md, the session-coordination skill AND board-post.yml at it -- the 2026-09-01 finding that a relay nobody can find is equivalent to no relay means the repoint must cover every surface, not just the workflow; (b) roll the board on a cadence, since a successor fills at the same rate; (c) reconsider whether a single append-only GitHub issue is the right substrate for a mechanism that must never stop accepting writes.

=== ADDENDUM 2026-09-08 (MI-83, session_018ruZdgEkPZ1XceWzLwuYUU) — the two items this row left NOT DIAGNOSED, both now measured. The condition is UNCHANGED and still live, so this is a re-confirmation, not a recurrence: issue_read method=get on #6927 returns "comments": 2500, and add_issue_comment still 403s with 'Commenting is disabled on issues with more than 2500 comments'. No successor board issue exists (searched open issues; #6927 is the only match).

(1) READS STILL WORK — AND THAT IS THE DANGEROUS HALF, NOT THE REASSURING ONE. issue_read method=get_comments perPage=1 page=2500 returns comment 5569943168, created 2026-09-07T11:28:17Z: the board's LAST comment, ~14h before this reading. So the mandatory session-start READ succeeds and returns a board FROZEN at that instant, permanently. A successful read of a frozen board is byte-indistinguishable from a read of a live, quiet board — and the documented staleness check (BL-20260817-BOARD-TAIL-READ-CANNOT-ASSERT-IT-REACHED-THE-END: 'a short page is the proof' you reached the end) now succeeds trivially on every attempt and returns the same tail every time, so the one instrument a session has for this cannot fire. Coordination has not degraded to read-only. It has degraded to reading a permanent snapshot that LOOKS live.

(2) TWO OTHER SURFACES TOUCH #6927 THROUGH THE API, AND ONE OF THEM IS A SECOND BROKEN WRITER. Population: every occurrence of '6927' under .github/workflows/ and scripts/ — 13 hits across 7 files — each read to establish whether it READS the board or WRITES to it.
  * .github/workflows/merge-claim-audit.yml — BOTH. Reads at line 83 (listComments) and WRITES at lines 138-140 (createComment with issue_number: board). IT IS BROKEN NOW, on every merge, and nothing has said so. The board's last comment — the very one found in (1) — IS this workflow's merge-slot audit for PR #11226. Its final successful post is the ceiling itself, so every merge since 2026-09-07T11:28Z has produced an audit that could not land. That makes it a second broken writer besides board-post.yml, and unlike board-post.yml (which fails the run deliberately loudly) this one's failure is invisible.
  * .github/workflows/scope-overlap-audit.yml — READS the board (line 147, listComments) and writes to the PR (lines 242, 271), so it still RUNS and still comments. What it emits is now wrong in the QUIET direction: its input is the frozen board, so it can only ever match declarations made before 2026-09-07T11:28Z and will report '0 from a live session' for every PR from here on. Observed on PR #10895 this session: '0 from a live session, 5 from a landed branch'. That verdict READS as 'no collision' when what it MEANS is 'no session can post a claim' — an unasserted denominator, CLAUDE.md's diagnostic-provenance sub-class C, live in production right now. Whatever succeeds #6927 must re-point this workflow too, or it will keep certifying 'no live collision' against an empty universe.
  * .github/workflows/{trainer-diag-relay,trainer-vm-diag}.yml and scripts/ops/session_registry.py name #6927 in PROSE only — no API call. Mechanically unaffected, but each instructs a session to use a board that cannot be posted to, so they belong in the re-point sweep clause (3) of resolution_criteria already requires.

STILL NOT DIAGNOSED, stated rather than implied: whether the VM-lane FIFO claim those two trainer relays describe has any out-of-band substitute; and whether any session has actually collided since the ceiling was hit. The second is unanswerable from here by construction — the mechanism that would have recorded it is the one that is down.

=== ESCALATION 2026-09-08 (MI-83, same session as the addendum above) — THE CEILING ALSO BLOCKS MERGING, AND THE ONLY WAY PAST IS TO LIE TO A GUARD. This is a bigger claim than anything above it and it was found by hitting it, not by reasoning about it.

Calling enable_pr_auto_merge on PR #11306 -- Tier-1, `landing: self`, route armed, all 6 checks green, mergeable_state `clean` -- was REFUSED by the merge-slot guard, verbatim: "Before merging or arming auto-merge on PR #11306, you MUST run the merge-slot protocol ... (2) POST a 🔒 MERGE SLOT CLAIM comment on GitHub issue #6927 naming PR #11306". Step (2) is IMPOSSIBLE: #6927 is at the 2500-comment ceiling and refuses every write by every documented path. So the sanctioned merge route now terminates in a step that cannot be performed.

⚠️ THE GUARD IS RIGHT AND IS NOT THE DEFECT. It states plainly that its own touch-marker is "a hard speed-bump, not the claim itself -- do the real claim". Setting /tmp/.claude-merge-claim-<session>-<pr> without having claimed anything would satisfy the guard while making its premise false -- precisely the "a guard cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than no guard" failure this repo names for `new-table-wiring-guard`'s presence-only marker. This session did NOT set the marker and did NOT merge; #11306 is green, clean and deliberately unlanded. Every other session that reaches this point faces the same two options, and only one of them is honest.

⚠️ SO THE BLAST RADIUS IS NOT "sessions cannot post START claims". It is: (a) no START claim, (b) no DONE, (c) no MERGE SLOT CLAIM -- and therefore (d) NO COMPLIANT MERGE AT ALL by a session that follows the protocol. A repo whose merge path is gated on a write surface that is permanently full has a merge path that is permanently closed. Weigh that when prioritising the successor board.

⚠️ AND A SEPARATE CORRECTION, worth its own line because CLAUDE.md asserts the opposite. CLAUDE.md's session-start contract states the PreToolUse merge guard "is INERT on Claude Code on the web (that runtime loads NO project hooks -- 1,379 consecutive 'Found 0 total hooks in registry' log lines, 2026-08-20)", and therefore that "A MERGE GOING THROUGH IS NOT EVIDENCE THE PROTOCOL RAN". THE GUARD FIRED IN THIS SESSION -- measured, by being blocked by it. Whatever was true of the runtime in 2026-08-20, hooks DO load here now. The dangerous direction is the one the doc points at: a session reading that line concludes the guard cannot stop it and treats the protocol as self-discipline only. Re-measure before re-quoting either claim.

⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED, stated rather than implied: whether the guard is active for EVERY session or only some (n=1 -- this session), and whether any session has already taken the dishonest branch. The second is unanswerable from the repo: setting the marker leaves no artifact, and the audit that would have recorded the claim is merge-claim-audit.yml, which is the workflow the ceiling broke.

items.tier: 1 (the fix is one pathspec in scripts/ops/document_index.py plus a regenerated index)
items.title: document_index population glob 'docs/**/*.md' is a GIT PATHSPEC and excludes every .md directly in docs/ -- 27 documents unregistered, including instruction-hierarchy levels 1 and 2, while the guard reports population=971 registered=971 OK
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-07T14:35Z on origin/main (4ea74fda). STATE THE POPULATION: `git ls-files -- 'docs/*.md'` returns 965 files; `git ls-files -- 'docs/**/*.md'` -- the literal pathspec in document_index.POPULATION_GLOBS -- returns 936 files. The 29-file difference is every .md sitting DIRECTLY in docs/, because in a git pathspec (no `:(glob)` magic) `*` already matches `/`, so `docs/*.md` is recursive while `docs/**/` requires a literal intervening slash. 28 of those 29 are in scope, and 27 of 28 have NO row in docs/DOCUMENT-INDEX.md (only docs/DOCUMENT-INDEX.md itself does).

WHAT IS MISSING IS THE POINT, not the count. docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md (instruction hierarchy LEVEL 1) and docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md (LEVEL 2) are both absent, as are docs/SPRINT-LOG-TEMPLATE-CANONICAL.md, docs/api-tier-policy.md (the CI-enforced single source of truth for route tiers), docs/github-actions-workflows.md, docs/TRADE-PIPELINE.md, docs/strategy-review-gate.md, docs/workplan.md and 19 more. The library built to answer the operator's ask for 'one centralized table where we keep track of everything' cannot see the two documents that outrank CLAUDE.md.

WHY THIS IS HIGH AND NOT COSMETIC: the guard prints `population=971 registered=971` and `document-index: OK`. That is a CLEAN NEGATIVE -- 971 of 971 = 100% coverage of a population that silently excluded the most important members. A reader checking whether the library is complete gets a confident yes. This is sub-class C of UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT as CLAUDE.md defines it (an unasserted denominator), and it is the SECOND instance of the same defect class in the SAME FUNCTION: population()'s own docstring records that `--others --exclude-standard` was missing on the first build, with the note that the guard 'reported OK and the count never moved'. Identical failure, one line over, caught the same way -- by running it against a real file rather than reasoning about it.

REPRO (negative control): on a clean checkout, `echo '# x' > docs/PLANTED.md && git add docs/PLANTED.md && python3 scripts/ci/check_document_index.py` prints population=971 and OK. The same file created at docs/anysubdir/PLANTED.md IS caught -- so R1 works and the POPULATION is what is wrong. NOTE the guard's --self-test passes throughout, correctly: it feeds the rule engine known-bad input, and the rule engine is not the defect.

ALSO NOTE the two governance guards disagree about docs/workplan.md: check_one_live_workplan.py grades it `historical`, so it IS in that guard's population, while the document index cannot see it. Two registers over two different populations is the condition the index exists to end.
items.checked: scripts/ops/document_index.py::population + POPULATION_GLOBS; scripts/ci/check_document_index.py (REPO/parents[2], R1-R5, --self-test); git ls-files with both pathspecs; grep of docs/DOCUMENT-INDEX.md for each excluded path; planted-file negative control at docs/ top level and one directory down.
items.resolution_criteria: The 27 unregistered documents carry index rows AND the guard's own count moves when they are added -- i.e. the population is re-measured, not the index hand-patched. A fix that adds the rows without fixing POPULATION_GLOBS leaves the clean negative in place and does NOT resolve this row. Include a planted-file control at the TOP level of docs/ (the case that escaped) in the guard's self-test, so this cannot regress silently a third time.
items.resolution: FIXED AT THE POPULATION, not the index. POPULATION_GLOBS now uses :(glob)docs/**/*.md (and :(glob).claude/skills/**/*.md), so `/**/` means zero-or-more-directories instead of requiring a literal intervening slash. EVERY CLAUSE CHECKED: (1) the previously-unregistered top-level documents carry index rows — the count is 28, not the 27 this row estimated (git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard: docs/**/*.md -> 936 files/0 top-level; :(glob)docs/**/*.md -> 964/28); (2) the guard's own count MOVED, 971 -> 999 (it reads 1000 on main because concurrent PRs added one document), so the population was re-measured rather than the index hand-patched; (3) the glob itself changed — no rows were hand-added; (4) scripts/ci/check_document_index.py --self-test gained population_control(), which plants REAL files (a top-level docs/*.md — the exact case that escaped — plus a nested one, plus a docs/*.txt that must NOT appear) and grades document_index.population() against the filesystem. THE CONTROL WAS VERIFIED TO CATCH THIS BUG rather than merely added: re-run against the old pathspec, all 13 rule cases PASS and the population control is the ONLY failure, naming the pathspec as the cause. STATUS OF THE 28 NEW ROWS, counted not asserted: 4 carry an established status (3 `live` via ci:canonical-doc-coherence-ACTIVE_DOCS, 1 `historical` via the MI-159 import) and 24 read `unknown` — the honest value for documents nobody has read; repo-wide unknown went 551 -> 574 and no status was manufactured. TWO REGISTERS NOW AGREE: all 13 of MI-159's plan documents are registered (set(mi159) - population() is empty); docs/workplan.md, previously in check_one_live_workplan.py's population but invisible here, now carries a row graded `historical` by the imported MI-159 determination. Verified on main after merge: `document-index: population=1000 registered=1000 headers_read=1000 generated_waived=4 · OK` and the self-test's three planted-file cases PASS.

items.title: Pushing the automerge request and the pr-opener request together lets claude-pr-automerge open the PR first, and the title/body can never be fixed
items.resolution_criteria: A session that pushes BOTH .github/pr-automerge-requests/<slug>.txt and automation/pr-requests/<name>.json ends up with a PR carrying the pr-opener request's TITLE and BODY. Any of: (a) claude-pr-automerge.yml defers to a pending pr-request for the same head branch; (b) pr-opener.yml, on finding the PR already exists, EDITS its title and body instead of writing `FAILED:` and stopping; or (c) the two relays are documented as mutually exclusive with a stated ordering, and CLAUDE.md's relay section says which to use when both would apply. ⚠️ OBSERVE IT: not proven by a green workflow run — it needs one PR opened via this exact double-push whose final title is the requested one, not the head commit's subject.
items.detail: MEASURED on PR #11255. MI-162 pushed .github/pr-automerge-requests/mi-162-document-index-population.txt (required by check_pr_landing.py R6 to declare a Tier-1 self-land) on the same branch it later used automation/pr-requests/*.json to open the PR with a full title and body. claude-pr-automerge.yml triggers on the automerge-request path and FINDS-OR-OPENS the PR, titling it from the HEAD COMMIT SUBJECT — so #11255 opened as 'Waive the header stamp for the two generated matrices the fix revealed', the subject of a minor follow-up commit, which describes neither the PR nor the finding. pr-opener.yml then ran and wrote `FAILED: a pull request for branch ... already exists` to automation/pr-results/, discarding a 6110-character body already written. THE STATE IS UNRECOVERABLE FROM THE SESSION: mcp__github__update_pull_request returns `403 Resource not accessible by integration` (the documented write-scope boundary, distinct from the transient connector drop), so the session that authored the description cannot attach it. CLAUDE.md documents both relays and the zero-checks trap their result commits cause, but does NOT document that they RACE — and the landing rules make the collision the DEFAULT path rather than an edge case, because a Tier-1 self-land REQUIRES the automerge-request file and a 403'd session REQUIRES pr-opener for a real description. A SECOND COST, also measured here: the automation/pr-* files are outside check_pr_landing.py's TIER1_SURFACE, so committing them made the same guard refuse to certify the self-land (R5) until they were removed again. COST: a PR whose title actively misleads a reviewer about what it contains, and whose reasoning survives only in the commit messages. Ordering the pushes (pr-request first, automerge-request second) is the obvious workaround and is NOT a fix — it is a rule nobody is checking.

items.tier: 3 — the fix touches strategy unit files the live VM consumes (observe-only, but Tier-3 by path)
items.title: record_position_telemetry is hooked into only 2 of the live monitor units, so 9 of 44 enabled+live legs emit NO peak-R telemetry at all — and MI-155 grades their n_live=0 identically to legs that genuinely did not trade
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-07 (POPULATION: the 44 legs with enabled: true AND execution: live in config/strategies.yaml at main a55fae75, joined to pipeline.monitor_unit_for). `record_position_telemetry` is called from INSIDE a strategy unit's monitor(). Only `trend_donchian` (:823) and `htf_pullback_trend_2h` (:743) carry the call — `squeeze_breakout_4h`, `ict_scalp`, `turtle_soup` and `vwap` do not. A leg on an unhooked unit therefore emits no telemetry row HOWEVER MUCH IT TRADES, so its n_live=0 is *we did not look*, never *it did not trade*. THE COLLAPSE: MI-155 (docs/research/exit-location-fidelity-2026-09-07.md) grades 13 legs at n_live=0 and calls all 13 `insufficient_n`. That verdict is CORRECT for all 13 and is not what is being challenged — but the REASON differs, and it splits 9 / 4: NINE are structurally invisible (the 8 ict_scalp_* legs + squeeze_breakout_4h) and FOUR are a real absence of positions (splg_trend_long_1d, tqqq_trend_long_1d, trend_donchian_eth_prop, trend_donchian_sol_prop, all on the hooked trend_donchian). That distinction changes what fixes them: the four need trading volume, which is T-9's wall and cannot be moved by effort; the nine need one hook and NO amount of soak will ever produce a row for them. WHY IT IS HIGH AND NOT MEDIUM: the invisible nine include ALL 8 legs running the one-shot break-even mechanism (_base.monitor_breakeven_sl), which is the one mechanism on the fleet that STRUCTURALLY CANNOT bank R — its guard is `sl < entry`, so it fires once and returns None for the rest of the trade's life. So the exit mechanism with the worst theoretical banking behaviour is also the one nothing measures. T-8's fleet-wide banking threshold would be calibrated on a corpus that excludes it by construction. THE FIX IS TWO FILES, not four (verified, not assumed): squeeze_breakout_4h already has `_since_entry` (:249) and binds `window` in monitor() (:336), so the 14-line block from trend_donchian.py:823-833 drops in verbatim; ict_scalp has `_bars_since_entry` (a bar COUNT) but not the DataFrame window, so it needs one extra line importing `since_entry` from src/runtime/exit_levers.py — the ONE canonical definition trend_donchian._since_entry itself delegates to, never a third copy. turtle_soup and vwap are NOT needed: turtle_soup is `execution: shadow` and vwap is `enabled: false`, so neither is in the population, and both would cost more (neither has _since_entry or writes entry_time; vwap writes no risk_per_unit, which peak_r requires). The hook is observe-only by construction — its own comment says it 'reads nothing back and cannot alter the trail' and it is wrapped in `except Exception: pass`. It is Tier-3 only by PATH (a strategy unit file the live VM consumes), so it is PROPOSED, not applied. Instrument: scripts/research/banking_mechanism_audit.py::telemetry_hook_gap re-derives the hooked set FROM SOURCE rather than trusting a constant, and tests/test_banking_mechanism_audit.py fails if that set changes — so this finding cannot rot silently. Full memo: docs/research/banking-half-2026-09-07.md § 3.
items.resolution_criteria: `banking_mechanism_audit.py --telemetry <live pull>` reports n_invisible = 0 over the enabled+live population, AND at least one telemetry row is OBSERVED on the live fleet carrying an ict_scalp_* strategy with a readable peak_r. ⚠️ A PASSING TEST IS NOT THIS OBSERVATION and neither is reading the merged diff — the hook runs inside a live monitor() tick, so only a real row proves it fires. ⚠️ AND DO NOT CLEAR THIS ON n_invisible = 0 ALONE: that grades the CODE (the hook is present), not the FLEET (a row was produced). Those are the two separate gaps this repo keeps conflating — merged is not deployed and deployed is not observed. Say WHICH of the two you established. ⚠️ If the operator declines Proposal A, this row does NOT clear — it CHANGES: the 9 legs are then deliberately unmeasured, which is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one rather than left looking like a fix that is about to happen.

items.title: fetch_backtest_candles.py --source yfinance fails at the COOKIE stage behind the session proxy and reports 'no candles returned', a message naming a fetch that never happened
items.resolution_criteria: MEASURED 2026-09-07 while building the MI-165 be_floor_r corpus: every `--source yfinance` call from a Claude Code web session fails with `Cookie fetch from fc.yahoo.com failed (SSLError)` then `curl: (35) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`, and the lane's final line is `ERROR: no candles returned (source attempted: yfinance)`. The venue is NOT down and the symbol is NOT unmapped: Yahoo's own chart endpoint (query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/<TICKER>) answers HTTP 200 with real bars from the same session using an ordinary User-Agent — verified for GDX (1926 daily bars, 2018-01-02 to 2025-08-29) before it was relied on. It is the yfinance LIBRARY's cookie/crumb handshake that the egress proxy resets, not the data fetch. This is diagnostic-provenance sub-class A (CLAUDE.md): the failure message names a cause — no candles from the venue — that no code path established, and a reader concludes the equity lane is unusable when only the auth dance is. MI-165 worked around it with a direct chart-endpoint reader and said so in its memo rather than silently substituting. RESOLVES WHEN: the yfinance lane either (a) distinguishes the COOKIE stage failure from a real empty-result in its message and exit path — the lane already has a YfFetchFailed/stage vocabulary to hang it on — or (b) falls back to the chart endpoint when the handshake is refused. Either is fine; what must not survive is a stage-1 auth failure rendering as 'the venue returned nothing'.

items.title: check_pr_landing R5 refuses self-land for scripts/backtest_*.py, but no HOLD_REASON names 'Tier-1 work the guard cannot certify', so the declaration must state a reason that is not quite true
items.resolution_criteria: MEASURED 2026-09-07 on branch claude/mi165-be-floor-sweep-20260907. The branch is Tier-1 by the canonical definition (research harnesses + a sweep script + tests + a memo; no src/, no config/, no order path, nothing armed), but three of its paths — scripts/backtest_trend.py, scripts/backtest_pullback.py, scripts/backtest_squeeze.py — are outside TIER1_SURFACE, which covers scripts/ci/**, scripts/ops/**, scripts/research/** and scripts/reports/** but not the backtest harnesses at scripts/ root. R5 therefore refuses `landing: "self"`, correctly and by design ('a path outside TIER1_SURFACE is not thereby dangerous; it is one the guard cannot certify'). THE GAP IS IN HOLD_REASONS, WHICH IS A CLOSED VOCABULARY OF FIVE AND NAMES NONE OF THIS CASE: changes_landing_machinery (verified false by R8), depends_on_unmerged_pr (false), awaiting_evidence (false), operator_asked_to_hold (the CLOSEST available and the one MI-165 used, but not what the hold is actually caused by — the commission explicitly PERMITTED landing the Tier-1 half), tier_2_3_needs_approval (this PR is Tier-1 and arms nothing). So the branch must declare a typed reason that does not name its real cause, and a typed verdict whose basis is stated only in free text is the weaker half of the discipline OPEN-PRS.json::operator_decision exists to enforce. MI-165 therefore put the true cause in hold_text and filed this row rather than leaving the mismatch unrecorded. RESOLVES WHEN either (a) HOLD_REASONS gains a term for it — e.g. `outside_certifiable_surface`, whose R8-style verifier is cheap and exact: the diff must contain a path matched by neither TIER1_SURFACE nor TIER2_PATHS nor TIER3_PATHS — or (b) TIER1_SURFACE is widened to cover the research backtest harnesses (scripts/backtest_*.py), which are tooling by the canonical tier definition and are not consumed by the live VM. (b) is the smaller change; (a) is the more general one and keeps the polarity the guard's docstring argues for. Not fixed here deliberately: both edit scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py, which is LANDING_MACHINERY, so R12 would make this PR unable to land its own fix.

items.title: AlpacaClient.close takes no qty and flattens the WHOLE symbol, so closing one journal trade silently liquidates every sibling trade's shares while their rows stay open with nothing behind them
items.resolution_criteria: MEASURED 2026-09-07 by MI-168 while re-scoping the IB close-confirmation (PR on branch mi-168-trade-scoped-close-confirmation; reasoning in docs/design/close-confirmation-scope-DESIGN.md section 6). execute.close_open_position receives a PER-TRADE qty and, on the alpaca branch, DISCARDS it: AlpacaClient.close(symbol) accepts no quantity at all (pinned by test_alpaca_close_signature_cannot_express_a_trade_scoped_close) and issues DELETE /v2/positions/{sym}, Alpaca's whole-symbol liquidation; _close_extended_hours likewise reads qty from the LIVE POSITION (pos.get('qty')), not from the caller's trade. So with two open journal rows on one symbol, closing trade A removes trade B's shares too and B's row stays open with no venue position behind it. This is the MIRROR of the IB defect MI-167 measured: IB falsely REFUSES a close that succeeded; Alpaca silently OVER-CLOSES. Pinned as current behaviour by test_alpaca_close_of_one_trade_liquidates_its_sibling_too in tests/test_close_confirm_trade_scope.py. !! DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY RE-SCOPING THE CONFIRMATION, which is what MI-167's proposed fix asked for at alpaca_client.py:842 and :1049. The confirmation is symbol-scoped and so is the OPERATION, so the two MATCH and Alpaca is NOT exposed to the false refusal (positive control: test_alpaca_close_is_not_exposed_to_the_false_refusal passes both before and after MI-168). Confirming a trade-sized reduction while the venue liquidated everything would journal one trade closed and leave its sibling's row open — BL-20260707-ALPACA-CLOSE-NOT-CONFIRMED-FLAT's false-SUCCESS re-introduced, on a real-money-capable path. !! REAL-MONEY COUPLING: alpaca_live is mode live / real_money and is immune today ONLY because it cannot place orders at all (MI-140, WO-20260907-ALPACA-LIVE-S-ROUTED-REAL-MONEY-LEG). Remediating MI-140 arms THIS row. The blocked_on edges written by MI-168 name this defect, not the false refusal, so a session acting on the coupling looks for the right thing. RESOLVES WHEN: the operation is made trade-scoped (a qty-sized opposing order rather than DELETE /v2/positions/{sym}, with its share-hold and qty_available interactions worked through) and a close of one row on a multi-row symbol is OBSERVED leaving the sibling's position intact — or the operator rules that whole-symbol close is the intended Alpaca semantics, in which case the DEFECT MOVES to close_open_position silently discarding the qty it was given, and that must be recorded as a decision rather than left looking like a bug nobody fixed. Population note: the precondition (two or more simultaneously-open rows on one (account, symbol)) held for 13 pairs in the 28-day window MI-167 measured; MI-168 did NOT count how many of those were Alpaca, and did NOT count any actual over-close event. We did not look. !! LANDED SEPARATELY FROM ITS OWN PR, DELIBERATELY. This row is MI-168's, verbatim and unedited except for this note; the manager carried it onto main because #11279 is blocked on two operator decisions and a REAL-MONEY finding must not wait on them. The manager did NOT verify the defect — read `opened_by` as the measurer. Carried 2026-09-07T21:45Z by session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj.

items.title: scripts/ops/error_feed_digest.py overwrites docs/claude/ERROR-FEED-DIGEST.md WITHOUT the doc-status header the index guard requires, so every generated digest PR fails a required check and the operator's error feed silently stops landing
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08T00:58Z on PR #11299. document-index-guard is a REQUIRED check and fails the branch with 'R3 UNSTAMPED: docs/claude/ERROR-FEED-DIGEST.md carries no status header'. The same guard on a clean origin/main prints 'document-index: OK — population=1007 registered=1007', so this is not a pre-existing whole-tree failure: main's copy of the file DOES carry the header (line 3, `Doc status: unknown · category unknown · last verified never`), and the generated copy on the branch does NOT. The generator overwrites the file and drops the stamp. 1 of 1 open digest PR is red for this reason; the two older digest PRs (#11261, #11281) were closed as superseded before this cause was isolated, so the population of confirmed instances is 1 and the count of digest PRs that have LANDED since the header requirement took effect is not established here — I did not look. IMPACT: the error-feed digest is the operator's grouped triage view of the trader ERROR/CRITICAL feed. If every regeneration is unmergeable, the committed digest silently freezes at whatever last landed while the workflow keeps running and reporting success — the write-only-log shape this repo already has a guard family for. NOT FIXED BY THE MANAGER, DELIBERATELY: scripts/ is a worker path and check_manager_scope R2 grades COMMITS IN RANGE, so a manager commit here would make the branch permanently unmergeable (it killed #11105 and #11031). Diagnosed and routed instead, per the manager contract.
items.resolution_criteria: RESOLVES WHEN: error_feed_digest.py emits the doc-status header as part of the generated file (matching what docs/DOCUMENT-INDEX.md and check_document_index.py R3 require), AND a NEWLY GENERATED digest PR is OBSERVED passing document-index-guard — not a hand-stamped file, and not a green self-test. A hand-added header on one file fixes one PR and leaves the generator writing an unstamped file on the next run, which is the shape that produced this. ⚠️ CHECK THE SIBLING BEFORE CLOSING: scripts/ops/render_due_list.py writes docs/claude/DUE.md from the same family and appears in the same diff; whether it carries the header was NOT checked here — we did not look. ⚠️ AND ESTABLISH THE DENOMINATOR the filing did not: how many error-feed digest PRs have been opened since the R3 requirement took effect, and how many landed. If the answer is zero landed, the operator's committed error feed has been frozen for that whole window and THAT is the finding, not the guard failure.

items.title: Alpaca protective coverage is graded by SIDE, never by QUANTITY, so alpaca_portfolio/TLT reads FULLY PROTECTED while 56 of its 72 shares hold no protective leg at all
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 by MI-173. LIVE, on a clean read. /api/diag/exchange_positions?account_id=alpaca_portfolio at 01:40:23Z: TLT short 72.0, error null. /api/diag/alpaca_open_orders?account_id=alpaca_portfolio at 01:42:07Z, read_state 'orders_read' (a CONFIRMED clean read, so the absence below is measured, not assumed): TLT holds exactly ONE OCO group, of 16 shares (limit buy 16 @ 74.67 submitted 2026-08-31T13:36:40Z; stop buy 16 @ 82.33 submitted 2026-09-04T17:35:55Z). 72 - 16 = 56 SHARES REST WITH NO PROTECTIVE LEG OF ANY KIND.

IT IS INVISIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT BY ACCIDENT. order_monitor._check_broker_naked_equity_positions calls AlpacaClient.protection_state and grades the two SIDES; its own inline comment records the limit verbatim: `stop_qty=None,  # Alpaca grades sides, not qty`. The sweep asks 'does a stop leg rest? does a target leg rest?' -- on TLT both answer yes -- so a position that is 22% covered grades FULLY PROTECTED and produces no finding.

!! THIS IS NOT BL-20260816-TARGET-NAKEDNESS-UNDETECTABLE-ON-ALPACA-AND-BYBIT AND MUST NOT BE CLOSED AS ITS DUPLICATE. That row is about the SIDE axis (a stop-only book reading protected because has_protective_orders ran one membership test over both sides). The Alpaca half of that axis HAS since been fixed -- the sweep no longer calls has_protective_orders, it calls protection_state and grades sides separately. This row is the QUANTITY axis, which was never done for Alpaca at all. Filed with similar_ok because the overlap is real and the axis is different.

THE PATTERN IS THAT ALPACA KEEPS GETTING HALF THE GENERALISATION. Bybit grades covered_qty (a QUANTITY, PR #8000). IB grades stop_qty/target_qty (QUANTITIES, BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED, whose own headline was 'protection is a QUANTITY and TWO-SIDED'). Alpaca got the two-sided half and never got the quantity half. It is the only one of the three venues where protective coverage is not a quantity.

NO NEW BROKER CALL IS NEEDED. /api/diag/alpaca_open_orders already returns a `qty` on every leg and the sweep already performs the read; this is arithmetic on data in hand.

!! DETECTION ONLY -- DO NOT WIRE A RE-ARM IN THE SAME CHANGE. The one time this class was auto-remediated the repair cancelled the leg that MATCHED the journal (BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG). A partial-coverage re-arm on Alpaca would also have to decide WHICH trade the uncovered shares belong to, which is the attribution problem BL-20260907-ALPACA-CLOSE-OF-ONE-TRADE-LIQUIDATES-ITS-SIBLINGS exists to solve. Grade it, page it, stop.

POPULATION: one account (alpaca_portfolio) read this session. alpaca_paper and alpaca_live were NOT read -- we did not look, and this row must not be read as saying they are clean.

RESOLVES WHEN: the Alpaca sweep compares summed protective-leg qty against position size (the Bybit covered_qty shape) AND a partially-covered Alpaca position is OBSERVED producing a finding on a real read. A passing unit test is not that observation. Evidence: docs/research/alpaca-close-blast-radius-mechanism-2026-09-08.md section 3.3.

items.title: AlpacaClient.modify_protective takes a symbol and no trade identity, so on a multi-row symbol one trade's trailing amend rewrites whichever sibling's protective legs happen to rest there
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 by MI-173 from the code at origin/main 161ee60, while establishing the mechanism for BL-20260907-ALPACA-CLOSE-OF-ONE-TRADE-LIQUIDATES-ITS-SIBLINGS.

execute.modify_open_order's alpaca branch calls `exchange_client.modify_protective(symbol, sl=sl, tp=tp)` -- symbol only, NO trade id, NO qty. AlpacaClient.modify_protective's own docstring is 'Replace the resting SL/TP legs of the open bracket on *symbol*'. On a symbol holding two simultaneously-open journal rows there is no 'the' bracket.

THIS IS THE SAME SCOPE DEFECT AS THE CLOSE, ON A DIFFERENT VERB, AND THE BACKLOG ONLY NAMES THE CLOSE. BL-20260907 names close_open_position discarding its per-trade qty; modify_open_order never had a per-trade identity to discard. A fix that makes only the CLOSE trade-scoped leaves this one live.

THE LIVE VENUE STATE IS WHAT THIS PATH PREDICTS, THOUGH I COULD NOT PROVE CAUSATION. alpaca_portfolio/TLT (read 2026-09-08T01:42:07Z, read_state 'orders_read') holds ONE 16-share OCO whose legs cross-attribute: qty 16 and limit 74.67 match trade 5266 (declared TP 74.670375, size 16); stop 82.33 matches trade 5414 (declared SL 82.32875), NOT 5266 (declared SL 84.61875 -> 84.62). The parent was submitted 2026-08-31T13:36:40Z, six minutes after 5266 opened; the STOP CHILD was submitted 2026-09-04T17:35:55Z, four days later and AFTER 5414 opened on 09-03.

!! TWO EXPLANATIONS FIT AND I COULD NOT DISTINGUISH THEM -- recorded rather than resolved in favour of the more interesting one. (a) CROSS-TRADE CONTAMINATION: 5414's monitor called modify_protective('TLT', sl=82.32875), which patched the only resting stop on the symbol, which was 5266's. (b) JOURNAL/VENUE DIVERGENCE: 5266's own stop trailed to 82.33 at the venue and trades.stop_loss was never updated. (a) is what the code path predicts and explains the 09-04 replacement timestamp; (b) cannot be excluded because both rows are short on the same instrument at nearly the same level and a short's trailing stop legitimately moves down. THE DECIDING EVIDENCE IS GONE: the modify_open_order log line from 2026-09-04 is far past the systemd journal's ~30-minute retention measured by MI-109. Either branch sits in the class CLAUDE.md already names, BL-20260823-MODIFY-IDEMPOTENCE-COMPARES-INTENT-TO-JOURNAL-NEVER-TO-VENUE.

OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE HOLDS UNDER BOTH BRANCHES: the resting stop sits at 82.33 against an implied mark of ~82.26 (derived from venue entry 82.309028 and unrealised_pnl 3.530016 over 72 short) -- about 0.08% away, and by a wide margin the nearest exit trigger on the symbol (5266's declared stop at 84.62 is ~2.9% away). It is 16-qty, so if it fires the blast radius is 16, not 72.

IB HAS THE SIBLING ROW AND ALPACA DID NOT: BL-20260825-THE-TRAILING-AMEND-NEVER-PASSES-OCA-KEY-SO-IT-STILL-CANCELS-SYMBOL-WIDE is the same finding for IB, where a per-trade OCA group EXISTS and the amend path does not use it. On Alpaca there is no per-trade key to not-use: trades.sl_order_id / tp_order_id are BOTH NULL on the two live TLT rows (5266, 5414), so a trade-scoped amend needs a leg-id WRITER before it needs a scoped amender.

RESOLVES WHEN: modify_open_order's alpaca branch identifies the closing/amending trade's OWN legs (trades.sl_order_id / tp_order_id, once written) and patches only those, AND an amend on a multi-row Alpaca symbol is OBSERVED leaving the sibling's legs untouched -- or the operator rules symbol-scoped amend is intended, which must be RECORDED as a decision. Evidence: docs/research/alpaca-close-blast-radius-mechanism-2026-09-08.md sections 1.3 and 3.2.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) execute.modify_open_order's alpaca branch identifies the amending trade's OWN legs (trades.sl_order_id / tp_order_id, which requires the leg-id writer that does not exist yet -- both are NULL on live rows 5266 and 5414) and patches only those, AND an amend on a multi-row Alpaca symbol is OBSERVED leaving the sibling's legs untouched on a real venue read; OR (b) the operator rules that symbol-scoped amend is the intended Alpaca semantics, which must be RECORDED as a decision rather than left looking like a bug nobody fixed. A green harness clears neither -- a harness cannot reach the Alpaca venue.
