items.title: The error-feed digest freeze is SELF-WORSENING, not merely static: because no digest lands, the watermark never advances, so every retry re-reads an ever-widening window and every one of them now hits the bot_logs page cap — rows are being lost, not just delayed
items.detail: SECOND-ORDER CONSEQUENCE of BL-20260908-ERROR-FEED-DIGEST-GENERATOR-STRIPS-THE-DOC-STATUS-HEADER-SO-EVERY-DIGEST-PR-IS-RED, filed separately because it does NOT go away when the generator is fixed and it changes the urgency of landing a digest. MEASURED 2026-09-08T01:5xZ against all three stranded remote branches plus a live local regeneration. Every one of the four carries the IDENTICAL covers_since 2026-09-07T10:41:39.779890+00:00 — main's committed watermark — because the watermark advances only when a digest LANDS, and none has: automation/error-feed-digest-34144211328-1 (generated 16:38:54, next_since 16:32:12), -34160653535-1 (20:46:28, next_since 19:51:46), -34170995331-1 (23:43:56, next_since 23:25:05), and a local --write at 2026-09-08T01:46:14 (all_feeds_read, 122 groups, 1474 rows). They are NOT three distinct windows; they are four successive snapshots of ONE un-advanced window that grows by roughly an hour per scheduled run. THE HARM: all four report truncated_feeds ['bot_logs'] and render the digest's own '⚠️ Page cap hit on bot_logs — older rows exist that this digest did not see' banner. So the window has already outgrown the page cap, and each further hour of freeze pushes more rows off the end of what any single digest can see. This is the difference between a delayed feed and a LOSSY one: the duty pass is not just late, it is being handed a lower bound that gets looser the longer nobody lands anything. ⚠️ THE DIGEST IS HONEST ABOUT THIS AND THAT IS WHY IT IS ONLY MEDIUM — the truncation is stated in the artifact rather than rendering as a quiet feed, which is the design working. The finding is that nothing ACTS on the banner, and the condition is self-reinforcing. ⚠️ NOT ESTABLISHED, AND DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: how many rows have actually fallen off. That needs the bot_logs ring's retention and page cap read against the window width; this row states that truncation IS occurring on every attempt, not how much was lost. WHAT CLEARS IT: one digest LANDS on main and advances covers_since, and the NEXT run is observed reporting truncated_feeds [] over the now-short window. A digest that lands while still truncated clears the freeze but NOT this row. If the window is structurally wider than the cap even at the hourly cadence, the fix is the page limit or a paging read, not the cadence — and that would be a separate change.
items.resolution_criteria: A digest commit lands on main whose covers_since is LATER than 2026-09-07T10:41:39.779890+00:00 (i.e. the watermark actually advanced), AND the NEXT digest generated after it reports truncated_feeds == [] with no 'Page cap hit' banner in docs/claude/ERROR-FEED-DIGEST.md. Read both from the committed ERROR-FEED-DIGEST.json on main, never from a workflow run's conclusion. ⚠️ A digest that LANDS while still reporting truncated_feeds ['bot_logs'] clears the FREEZE but NOT this row — this row is about the window having outgrown the page cap, and a landing that is still truncated is evidence the window is structurally too wide rather than merely backed up. In that case the fix is the page limit or a paging read, and this row should be re-filed against that, not closed.

updates.note: RE-CONFIRMED FROZEN, ALL THREE CLAUSES UNMET, read from the committed artifact on origin/main as the criterion demands (never from a workflow run's conclusion), 2026-09-09. docs/claude/ERROR-FEED-DIGEST.json on origin/main: covers_since = 2026-09-07T10:41:39.779890+00:00 — BYTE-IDENTICAL to the watermark this row names, so it has not advanced at all in the ~46h since the row was filed. generated_at 2026-09-08T05:10:01Z. truncated_feeds = ['bot_logs'], i.e. NOT the empty list the criterion requires. And docs/claude/ERROR-FEED-DIGEST.md on main still carries the 'Page cap hit' banner (1 occurrence). So the self-worsening loop this row describes is confirmed running, not merely predicted.

items.title: Alpaca protection was graded as SIDES only, so a 72-share short carrying a 16-share stop read as covered — 56 shares naked and invisible to every accessor
items.tier: 2 — src/runtime/order_monitor.py + src/units/accounts/alpaca_client.py; detection only, no order placed/cancelled/modified
items.detail: RECURRENCE of BL-20260816-COVERAGE-IS-ONE-SIDED, which is filed RESOLVED. That row was resolved for the SIDES half on all venues and for the QUANTITY half on IB (IBClient.protection_coverage, BL-20260814-IB-PROTECTION-BOOLEAN-NOT-QUANTITY) and on Bybit (order_monitor._bybit_position_protection covered_qty, PR #8000). ALPACA NEVER GOT THE QUANTITY HALF, and the resolved status of the parent row is what hid that for 23 days. AlpacaClient.protection_state returned {stop: bool, target: bool, legs: int} and _check_broker_naked_equity_positions passed stop_qty=None to its page under the literal comment 'Alpaca grades sides, not qty'. Alpaca nets per symbol per account, so N journal trades share ONE broker position sized to their SUM while each trade's bracket is sized to its OWN qty — one surviving bracket made the whole netted position read protected. MEASURED 2026-09-08T02:17:10Z via /api/diag/alpaca_open_orders, read_state=orders_read and positions_state=positions_read on all four declared Alpaca accounts (a confirmed clean read, so the absences below are measured and not a failed look): alpaca_portfolio/TLT held a 72-share SHORT carrying a resting stop for 16 shares. Journal trades 5266 (16 shares, opened 2026-08-31) and 5414 (56 shares, opened 2026-09-03) share the one netted position and only 5266's bracket rests, so trade 5414 is entirely unprotected while declaring stop_loss 82.32875. 56 of 72 shares naked. POSITIVE CONTROL: the same probe over the same read graded the other 14 open positions across alpaca_paper (8) and alpaca_portfolio (6) at exactly 1.00 stop coverage, so the single finding is the probe discriminating and not the probe being blind. REAL MONEY WAS NOT EXPOSED AT THE READ: alpaca_live (mode live, account_class real_money, same client code) read 0 positions and 0 orders on read_state=orders_read, corroborated by 0 open alpaca_live rows in the journal. It was flat, NOT covered — an empty denominator, which is a different fact and must not be reported as 'fully protected'. The defect is structural and applies to alpaca_live identically the moment it holds a position; it trades TLT, the same symbol carrying the paper finding. FIXED AS DETECTION ONLY: AlpacaClient.protection_coverage returns {size, side, stop_qty, target_qty, legs, unknown_qty_legs, source} in the same vocabulary IB and Bybit already use. A leg is counted only if it REDUCES the graded position (Alpaca has no hedge mode, so the reducing side is a function of the position side) — without that filter a resting same-side ENTRY order counts as protection. An unreadable leg qty/type/side, or an unreadable position side, makes coverage UNGRADEABLE (unknown_qty_legs) — never zero and never full, mirroring the IB and Bybit refusals to guess. A non-positive or NaN leg qty is ungradeable rather than abs()-ed, because abs() launders a negative into real coverage and manufactures protection that does not rest (caught by its own test, not by inspection). NOTHING IS RE-ARMED OFF THE NEW GRADE: the re-arm decision still reads protection_state byte-identically. Binding coverage to the repair path is a separate Tier-2 decision needing an operator OK — BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG is what automatic remediation of this class did last time.
items.resolution_criteria: TWO PARTS, different facts — say WHICH you cleared rather than clearing the row on the easier one. (1) DETECTOR OBSERVED: an alpaca_partial_stop_coverage row is found in /api/bot/logs?level=error (or the close_failure/notifications surface), carrying a size and a stop_qty that DIFFER, on a real fleet position — read the log row, never the merged diff and never a passing unit test. The standing alpaca_portfolio/TLT condition (72 vs 16) is the exhibit it should fire on first. ⚠️ A GREEN CI RUN CLEARS NOTHING: 23 assertions pass in tests/test_alpaca_protection_coverage_quantity.py and a harness cannot reach the live monitor tick. ⚠️ AND THE SWEEP REPORTING covered=N CLEARS NOTHING EITHER — grading every position as covered is the detector working while no position is partially naked, which is the healthy case, not an observation of the detector discriminating. (2) THE STANDING TLT CONDITION IS DISPOSITIONED: alpaca_portfolio trade 5414's 56 shares either carry a resting stop (verified on /api/diag/alpaca_open_orders as stop_qty >= size, not from a repair call's return value), or the position is closed, or an operator records a decision to leave it uncovered. ⚠️ IF THE POSITION SIMPLY DISAPPEARS WITH NO ATTRIBUTION, record THAT rather than clearing on it — an unexplained resolution is not evidence the mechanism works, and this repo has already been bitten by crediting an unrelated repair (see the PROTECTION_REASSERT_MODE row in CLAUDE.md, whose one live exhibit vanished with the cause unestablished). ⚠️ IF THE OPERATOR DECLINES to bind the grade to the re-arm path, this row does NOT clear — it CHANGES: a partially-covered Alpaca position is then DETECTED and never repaired, which is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one with that consequence stated, rather than left looking like a repair about to be wired.
items.next_step: Operator decision on whether the quantity grade should BIND the Alpaca re-arm/top-up path as Bybit's does — the Alpaca analogue of BYBIT_GRADED_COVERAGE_MODE, staged per account with an empty allowlist meaning NONE. Until then a partially-covered Alpaca position is DETECTED and pages, and is not repaired.

updates.note: PART (1) DETECTOR OBSERVED IS CLEARED — PART (2) IS NOT, AND THE EXHIBIT HAS WORSENED. Saying which, as the row demands. (1) CLEARED on the exact surface named. GET /api/bot/logs?level=error (125 rows) carries FIVE alpaca_partial_stop_coverage rows, read as log rows and not from a diff or a unit test. The discriminating one, 2026-09-08T11:08:10Z: 'alpaca_portfolio/TLT: position 72.0 carries a resting stop for only 16.0 — 56 unprotected' — size and stop_qty DIFFER, on a real fleet position, and it is the TLT exhibit the row predicted it would fire on first. It is DISCRIMINATING, not blanket: it also fired on two NEW positions at 2026-09-08T13:44Z (alpaca_paper/USO and alpaca_portfolio/USO, both 3.0 vs 0.0). The latch runtime_logs/partial_stop_coverage_alert_state.json corroborates with four keys: alpaca_portfolio|TLT|sev=56, alpaca_portfolio|TLT|sev=75, alpaca_paper|USO|sev=3, alpaca_portfolio|USO|sev=3. (2) NOT CLEARED, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT NEEDS EYES: the TLT condition has DEGRADED, not held. At 2026-09-08T13:37:36Z the feed reads 'alpaca_portfolio/TLT: position 75.0 carries a resting stop for only 0.0 — 75 unprotected'. The 16-share stop that was resting is GONE, so trade 5266's bracket has also vanished and the whole 75-share short is now naked — not the 56-of-72 the standing operator decision was made about. THE DECISION IS NOT RE-OPENED HERE and this session proposes no change; but the operator decided 'the 56 naked TLT shares stay naked' against a 72/16 book, and the book is now 75/0. That is a different state of the world and is recorded so the decision can be re-put on accurate facts if the operator wants it. The severity-keyed latch (sev=56 -> sev=75) is working exactly as designed: a worsening broke the 6h window rather than being swallowed by it.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN UPDATE EARLIER TODAY — the '(2) has WORSENED' half was reported from a DATED SNAPSHOT in the present tense and is wrong as a statement about now. The 'position 75.0 carries a resting stop for only 0.0 — 75 unprotected' row is real but is dated 2026-09-08T13:37:36.743503Z, read from /api/bot/logs?level=error, i.e. a historical alert — not a live position read. THE LIVE READ, /api/diag/alpaca_open_orders at 2026-09-09T08:22Z with read_state=orders_read: alpaca_portfolio holds TLT SHORT 75 against a resting buy-75 STOP @ 82.40 (status `held`, submitted_at 2026-09-08T18:49:44Z) — FULLY COVERED, 75 of 75. The naked window opened at 13:37:36Z and closed about five hours later the same day. Corroborated by partial_stop_coverage_alert_state: sev=56 last fired 2026-09-08T11:08:10Z, sev=75 last fired 2026-09-08T13:37:36Z, nothing since. So relative to the standing operator decision (72 shares, 16-share stop, 22% covered) the position is now 75 with a 75-share stop, 100% covered — the 16-share stop is gone because it was REPLACED, not because protection vanished. [!] WHAT PLACED THAT STOP IS NOT ESTABLISHED. The Alpaca broker-naked sweep re-arming is the obvious candidate and was NOT observed; an unattributed repair is not evidence the mechanism works, which is why part (2) of this row's criterion — an ATTRIBUTED disposition — is still NOT cleared. Part (1) (detector observed on the named surface, size and stop_qty differing, on a real fleet position) stands as cleared on the 72/16 row. [!] ALSO: /api/bot/positions at 2026-09-09T07:44:55Z returned no TLT at all while the diag route showed TLT open on TWO alpaca accounts minutes later. Both reads are honest; that route does not surface these accounts. Recorded as an observation, NOT filed as a defect — whether the scoping is deliberate was not established.

items.title: GET /api/bot/positions — the fleet's only uncapped-looking open-positions read — has a hardcoded LIMIT 50 with no total, no truncation flag and no limit param; measured 29/50 today
items.detail: SECOND CONFIRMED MEMBER of the population BL-20260906-TRADES-CLOSED-SILENTLY-RETURNS-EMPTY-ABOVE-LIMIT-200-AND-FOR-ANY-SINCE explicitly asks to be measured ('check every OTHER read route for the same shape before closing; this was found by accident, so the population of affected routes is UNMEASURED'). That row is about /api/bot/trades/closed; this is the OPEN-positions half and a different route. || MECHANISM, read from source at src/web/api/routers/dashboard.py:770 — _fetch_open_position_rows() builds 'SELECT ... FROM trades WHERE status=\'open\' AND COALESCE(is_backtest,0)=0 [+ paper predicate] ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 50'. The 50 is a LITERAL: get_positions() exposes only include_paper / include_demo, so a caller cannot raise it, cannot ask how many rows exist, and cannot tell a truncated answer from a complete one. The response is a bare JSON array — no envelope, no count, no truncated flag. || MEASURED 2026-09-08T03:24-03:30Z: /api/bot/positions?include_paper=true returned 29 rows, i.e. the fleet runs at 58% of a cap it cannot see. Truncation was therefore NOT exercised and is NOT claimed to have been observed — the cap is read from code, the 29 is measured. || WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE SPA: this is the natural surface for a journal-vs-venue reconciliation, and it is the one MI-177 used, precisely because /api/diag/journal?table=trades caps at 1000 rows ORDER BY id DESC and hid 4 of the 29 open rows (ids 4194, 4195, 4347, 4350 — all opened 2026-07-29..08-03). Those four read as 'venue holds a position the journal does not' and would have been filed as FOUR phantom-position divergences on alpaca_paper (IEF 141, SPY 11), alpaca_portfolio (IEF 152) and ib_paper (MES 15). They are not divergences; they are rows below a read cap. The same failure one level up — /api/bot/positions crossing 50 — would manufacture the identical false finding class with no indicator at all. || HEADROOM IS NOT LARGE: bybit_1 alone declares 26 strategies, alpaca_paper 19, alpaca_portfolio 14. 29 concurrent opens today is not a floor. || MI-177 avoided the trap only by cross-checking against RiskManager._open_gross_notional_from_db (src/units/accounts/risk.py:472), which is an UNCAPPED SQL SUM over all open non-backtest rows and is served per account by /api/diag/exposure. The two agreed to the cent on all 9 accounts where exposure is measurable — that agreement is what proves the 29 rows are the complete set, not the route's own say-so.
items.resolution_criteria: The route either SERVES every open row or SAYS it did not — a caller must be able to distinguish 'these are all of them' from 'this is the first 50'. Minimum: publish a total (rows existing) alongside the returned rows, or a truncated boolean, so a consumer can branch. Verify with a POSITIVE CONTROL, not a code read: stand up >50 open non-backtest rows in a test journal, call the route, and show the response distinguishes the truncated case from the complete one. !! RAISING 50 TO A BIGGER NUMBER DOES NOT CLEAR THIS — the defect is the silence, not the value; a larger silent cap fails identically the day it is crossed. !! AND DO NOT CLEAR ON 'the fleet is only at 29' — that is the condition being relied on, not the fix. Cross-reference BL-20260906-TRADES-CLOSED-SILENTLY-RETURNS-EMPTY-ABOVE-LIMIT-200-AND-FOR-ANY-SINCE: two confirmed members means the remaining population (src/web/api/routers/notifications.py:336 LIMIT 25 and :403 LIMIT 50 are unexamined candidates) should be swept, not sampled.

items.title: /api/diag/exchange_positions returns positions:null for 3 of 11 declared accounts, for THREE different reasons — and breakout_1 (prop, mode:live) has no venue read path in the code at all
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08T03:24:41Z and again at 03:30:39Z, the first fleet-wide journal-vs-venue audit (MI-177, standing pipeline lane pass 4). /api/diag/exchange_positions covered 11 of 11 declared accounts in config/accounts.yaml and returned positions:null — which the route's own docstring defines as 'could-not-read', explicitly NOT flat — for ib_live, oanda_practice and breakout_1. error was null on all three, so nothing on the response distinguishes them; the reasons were established by reading src/units/accounts/clients.py::account_open_positions. || THE THREE REASONS ARE NOT THE SAME AND SHOULD NOT BE REPORTED AS ONE STATE. (1) ib_live — REAL MONEY, mode: dry_run. The IB branch returns None when mode != 'live' ('the live gateway socket stays closed until promotion'). Deliberate and documented. Consequence worth stating anyway: nobody can confirm the fleet's real-money IB account is flat; it is ASSUMED flat because it is dry. (2) oanda_practice — paper, mode: dry_run. Same dry-mode gate in the oanda branch. Deliberate. (3) breakout_1 — PROP, account_class: prop, mode: LIVE, 3 strategies, and the journal carries prop_fills (41 rows) and prop_tickets (91 rows), so it is not dormant. account_open_positions supports exactly four exchanges — bybit, interactive_brokers/ib, alpaca, oanda — and returns None for anything else. exchange: breakout is not among them, so this account's venue position state is UNREADABLE BY CONSTRUCTION and will stay null however the account is configured. (1) and (2) resolve themselves on promotion to live; (3) does not resolve at all. || WHY THIS IS THE FINDING AND NOT A FOOTNOTE: the value of a fleet audit is its denominator. MI-177's verdict is '23 of 24 comparable symbol pairs reconcile exactly, 1 diverges' over EIGHT accounts, not eleven. An audit that reported the other three as clean would be asserting a negative over accounts it never looked at — the unasserted-denominator sub-class the diagnostic-provenance rule names. breakout_1 is the one that cannot be closed by waiting. || ⚠️ NARROWED 2026-09-08 BY MI-189b (lane pass 5) — THE ROUTE-LEVEL CLAIM STANDS, THE ACCOUNT-LEVEL CLAIM IN THIS ROW'S OWN TITLE DOES NOT. 'breakout_1 can never have a venue read' is TRUE of /api/diag/exchange_positions and of account_open_positions, for exactly the reason recorded above, and that half is unchanged. It is FALSE of the ACCOUNT. breakout_1 is a MANUAL BRIDGE with no broker feed BY DESIGN; its venue analogue is the operator's own reported terminal state, journalled in prop_account_status and served by /api/bot/prop/status. Read there on 2026-09-08: the newest snapshot (2026-08-30T19:33:29Z) reports balance 4787.34, equity 4787.34, unrealized 0.00 — equity == balance is the operator's terminal saying the account holds NOTHING. Journal side, over the COMPLETE prop_fills table (41 returned = 41 total), grouped by prop_position_identity.position_key exactly as find_open_prop_positions does: 18 ROWS carry status open/filled but there are only 3 distinct position keys and ZERO open positions. BOTH SIDES SAY FLAT — breakout_1 RECONCILES. It was never unreadable; the audit asked the wrong surface. ⚠️ THE RECONCILIATION IS AS-OF, NOT LIVE: that snapshot is 203.9 hours (8.5 days) old and the system itself grades it status_freshness 'stale' against a 24h threshold, so this is reconciled_as_of_2026-08-30 and never reconciled_now. || ALSO MEASURED MORE PRECISELY: account_open_positions has 17 distinct 'return None' statements (lines 1269-1571; 22 textual matches, 5 of them comments) across at least six semantic classes — bad argument, deliberate dry-mode non-dial, missing creds, gateway unreachable, empty-but-unverifiable snapshot, unsupported exchange — plus a catch-all except. All 17 reach the caller as one null with error:null, so a DESIGNED non-read is indistinguishable on the wire from a gateway OUTAGE. Same shape as the open BL-20260821-IB-OPEN-ORDERS-COULD-NOT-LOOK-CARRIES-NO-REASON on a sibling route. || AND ib_live's disposition in MI-177's audit table ('resolves on its own? yes, on promotion to live') is FALSE — its declared endpoint 127.0.0.1:7496 has no listener and is not this deployment's live port. See BL-20260908-IB-LIVE-ENDPOINT-IS-STALE-AND-PROMOTION-WOULD-NOT-CONNECT. Full record: docs/claude/work/UNREAD-ACCOUNT-VENUE-AUDIT-2026-09-08.md.
items.resolution_criteria: TWO SEPARATE THINGS, and neither substitutes for the other. (a) THE REPORTING HALF: /api/diag/exchange_positions distinguishes WHY a read did not happen — at minimum a reason field separating 'account is dry, socket deliberately not opened' from 'this exchange has no position-read implementation' from 'the read was attempted and failed'. Today all three arrive as positions:null + error:null and a reader cannot tell a deliberate skip from an outage. Verify by reading the live response for ib_live and breakout_1 and showing the two now differ. (b) THE COVERAGE HALF: breakout_1 either gains a venue position read in src/units/accounts/clients.py::account_open_positions, or the repo RECORDS the decision that a live prop account is not venue-reconcilable and says what is relied on instead (prop_fills/prop_tickets, and whether anything compares them to the journal). A recorded decision closes (b) legitimately; silence does not. !! DO NOT CLEAR (b) BY SETTING breakout_1 TO dry_run — that converts an unreadable live account into an unreadable dry one and removes the read for a reason unrelated to the gap. !! DO NOT CLEAR EITHER HALF ON ib_live/oanda_practice being promoted to live — that changes those two accounts' state and leaves the null-vs-null ambiguity and the breakout gap exactly where they are.

items.title: Two binding manager duties collide: the manager MUST run the merge queue, and check_manager_scope R2 fails the merge commit that resolves a register conflict because R2 grades the FIRST-PARENT diff, which drags in every path main touched
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08T05:02Z on PR #11312 (MI-173, operator-approved Tier-3). GitHub refused the merge with 'Pull Request has merge conflicts'. The conflict was in docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json alone — both sides had appended rows — and the register merge driver resolved it correctly (verified independently: base 1281, branch 1284, main 1284, merged 1287 = the exact union, no id missing, none extra, no duplicates). || THE MERGE COMMIT THEN FAILED R2: 'docs/DOCUMENT-INDEX.md is not on the manager surface this guard can vouch for. A manager session that writes this is doing an item instead of managing.' || THE MANAGER AUTHORED NOTHING IN THAT FILE. `git show --cc` on the merge commit lists exactly ONE path — the backlog — because a combined diff shows only what the merge actually RESOLVED. DOCUMENT-INDEX.md auto-merged: main's row came from MI-177 and the branch's row from MI-173. R2 reads the FIRST-PARENT diff, which by construction contains everything main changed since the branch point, so on a merge commit it attributes the whole of main's content to the manager. || WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC: running the merge queue is one of the manager's THREE canonical base duties (CLAUDE.md, operator-directed 2026-09-03), and register conflicts are STRUCTURAL — every manager PR touches SESSIONS.json or MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json, so each dirties the next as it lands (MI-20/MI-76/MI-94). Meanwhile the register merge driver is CLIENT-SIDE ONLY, so GitHub calls every such PR `dirty` and someone must resolve it locally. The manager is therefore required to do a thing it is forbidden to author, and the cheapest way out is the manager-scope-exception file — reserved for a live incident, and used here it would become routine. That is the 'cheaper to lie to than to satisfy' failure this repo already names. || WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD: the manager force-pushed the branch back to its author's commit 525c48a7, removing its own bad commit and restoring the branch exactly as its author left it. No exception was filed and #11312 remains approved and unmerged. || NOT ALWAYS FATAL, WHICH IS WHY IT WILL BE MISSED: the identical merge on #11315 forty minutes earlier PASSED manager-scope, because main happened not to have touched a non-manager path in that window. The guard's verdict therefore depends on what OTHER sessions merged since the branch point, not on anything the manager did — the same commit is clean or a violation depending on unrelated traffic.
items.resolution_criteria: R2 grades a MERGE commit on what it actually resolved (the combined `--cc` diff against both parents) rather than on the first-parent diff, so a manager resolving a register conflict is judged on the resolution and not on every path main carried in — demonstrated by a real manager merge commit that brings a worker-path change in from main and PASSES, alongside a real one that EDITS a worker path and still FAILS. Explicitly NOT sufficient: a manager-scope-exception entry (that is the routine-bypass this row exists to prevent), and NOT a rule that merge commits are skipped entirely — that would let a manager hide a genuine worker-path edit inside a merge. If instead the operator rules that the manager must ROUTE every conflicted PR to a session, this row does not clear — it CHANGES: the merge queue then has a mandatory spawn hop for a mechanical conflict, which is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one with that cost stated.

items.title: There is NO way to add a protective leg on Alpaca without cancelling every resting leg on the symbol: place_protective's pre-cancel is unconditional, and the oca_key its own caller passes to scope it is silently ignored
items.detail:
ESTABLISHED FROM CODE 2026-09-08 while executing WO-20260908-RE-ARM-PROTECTION-FOR-THE-56-NAKED, which is BLOCKED BY THIS ROW and could not be completed because of it. Read against origin/main ed37f5ba.

AlpacaClient.place_protective (src/units/accounts/alpaca_client.py:1361) calls self._cancel_open_orders_for_symbol(sym) UNCONDITIONALLY at line 1405 before placing. That helper delegates to _cancel_open_orders_detailed, which reads _open_orders_for_symbol(symbol) — every open order on the symbol for that account, parents AND nested bracket legs — and issues DELETE /v2/orders/{id} for each. There is no qty scope, no group scope, and no per-trade scope of any kind.

THE CALLER BELIEVES IT IS SCOPING THE CANCEL AND IS NOT. order_monitor._attempt_naked_autoprotect (line 7619) builds the SAME order dict for IB and Alpaca and passes 'oca_key': str(row['id']) under a comment that reads, verbatim: 'Scope the re-arm's pre-cancel to THIS trade's own OCA group. Without it place_protective cancels every resting leg on the symbol root, which on a netted IB contract destroys the OTHER strategies' take-profit legs (BL-20260814-IB-PROTECTION-BOOLEAN-NOT-QUANTITY).' IBClient.place_protective honours that key. AlpacaClient.place_protective READS ONLY symbol, direction, qty, sl, tp — oca_key and account_id are accepted by the signature (it takes a dict) and dropped on the floor. So the exact hazard the comment describes is UNMITIGATED on Alpaca, and the mitigation LOOKS applied at the call site. This is a diagnostic-provenance class-A defect in a comment rather than an output: the annotation names a protection no code path on this venue provides.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS — MEASURED, NOT HYPOTHETICAL. alpaca_portfolio/TLT is a 72-share short held by TWO open journal rows: trade 5266 (tlt_pullback_1d, 16 shares, declares stop_loss 84.61875) and trade 5414 (tlt_pullback_1h, 56 shares, declares stop_loss 82.32875). 16 + 56 = 72, matching the venue position exactly. Read 2026-09-08T04:47:34Z and again 04:50:13Z via /api/diag/alpaca_open_orders, per-account read_state 'orders_read' BOTH times (a confirmed clean read, not a failed look): ONE OCO pair rests on TLT — buy limit 74.67 qty 16 (292b3240) and buy stop 82.33 qty 16 (742c3729). 56 shares carry no protective leg at all and have not since ~2026-09-03. Re-arming those 56 through the only path that exists would DELETE 292b3240 and 742c3729 first, taking the position to 72 naked shares in the window between the cancel and the place, and leaving trade 5266 with no leg of its own afterward — the OCO placed covers only the qty passed. That is precisely the outcome BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG was filed on, one venue over.

AND THERE IS NO OTHER PATH. Measured over the whole tree: place_protective's ONLY caller is _attempt_naked_autoprotect. modify_protective PATCHes existing legs and cannot create coverage for uncovered shares. close(symbol) is whole-symbol with no qty parameter and cancels everything (MI-173). place() is a bracket MARKET ENTRY — on a short, a buy would reduce the position, not protect it. And the system-actions allowlist (.github/workflows/system-actions.yml) carries flatten-alpaca-position, attach-ib-target and cancel-ib-order but NO Alpaca protective-attach action, so there is no sanctioned wire to invoke a repair from a session either. The IB-side sibling of that gap is already filed as BL-20260823-NO-REARM-IB-BRACKET-ACTION; the Alpaca side is worse, because on IB the qty-scoped mechanism at least EXISTS.

THIS IS A RECURRENCE, filed with similar_ok. BL-20260825-THE-TRAILING-AMEND-NEVER-PASSES-OCA-KEY-SO-IT-STILL-CANCELS-SYMBOL-WIDE recorded a caller failing to pass the key on IB. Here the key IS passed and the venue implementation has nowhere to put it, so no amount of fixing call sites reaches this one.

⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-08 AFTER #11315 LANDED ON MAIN MID-SESSION — the DETECTION half of this row's framing is now stale and must not be re-quoted. The reads above were taken against ed37f5ba, where the 56 naked shares were invisible to every accessor. #11315 (MI-176) ships AlpacaClient.protection_coverage and a `partially_naked` counter with an `alpaca_partial_stop_coverage` page, so the condition IS detected now. WHAT IS NOT FIXED, AND IS THIS ROW'S WHOLE SUBJECT: the REPAIR. Read at order_monitor.py:7868, that change's own comment states 'NOTHING IS RE-ARMED OFF THIS GRADE ... The re-arm below still reads protection_state, byte-identically' — and the gate is still `if state.get("stop"): continue`, so trade 5414 is still skipped for re-arm on every pass. Re-verified against the post-#11315 tree: AlpacaClient.place_protective still calls _cancel_open_orders_for_symbol(sym) unconditionally and still reads only symbol/direction/qty/sl/tp, with no oca_key. So 'the position is invisible' is FALSE as of #11315 and 'the position cannot be repaired without cancelling the sibling's legs' is UNCHANGED.
resolution_criteria: Give AlpacaClient.place_protective a scoped pre-cancel: cancel only the legs belonging to the calling trade (Alpaca has no OCA groups, so the scope must be carried explicitly — trades.sl_order_id/tp_order_id already exist as columns and are NULL on both TLT rows, which is its own gap to close first).

Until that exists, place_protective MUST REFUSE rather than silently widen when a caller passes an oca_key it cannot honour. A parameter accepted and ignored is worse than one rejected — the call site currently reads as protected.
Add the Alpaca analogue of attach-ib-target to the system-actions allowlist so a qty-scoped protective leg can be armed on one trade without touching a sibling's. Tier-2, operator-gated.
Verified by a read_state 'orders_read' showing BOTH trade 5266's and trade 5414's legs resting simultaneously on TLT — which no code path in the repo can currently produce.

items.title: AlpacaClient.modify_protective PATCHes EVERY stop leg on the symbol with no per-trade scope, and it has already moved trade 5266's resting stop to trade 5414's declared level — 2.29 away from what 5266 declares
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-08T04:47:34Z and re-confirmed 04:50:13Z, /api/diag/alpaca_open_orders, per-account read_state 'orders_read' both times. Found while executing WO-20260908-RE-ARM-PROTECTION-FOR-THE-56-NAKED; it CORRECTS that work order's stated premise and is the reason the correction matters.

THE WORK ORDER SAID trade 5266's 16-share leg is the one that MATCHES the journal, echoing BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG. IT DOES NOT MATCH. The one OCO pair resting on alpaca_portfolio/TLT is buy limit 74.67 qty 16 (292b3240, submitted 2026-08-31T13:36:40Z) and buy stop 82.33 qty 16 (742c3729, submitted 2026-09-04T17:35:55Z). Attribution: qty 16 and the limit 74.67 both point at trade 5266 (tlt_pullback_1d, 16 shares, take_profit_1 74.670375 -> '74.67'), whose bracket was placed six minutes after it opened. But 5266 declares stop_loss 84.61875 ('84.62'), and the resting stop reads 82.33 — which is trade 5414's declared stop_loss 82.32875 formatted to 2dp exactly as place_protective/modify_protective format it (f'{float(sl):.2f}').

TWO INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATIONS that 84.62 is 5266's real level and 82.33 is foreign to it: (a) the stop leg's submitted_at (2026-09-04T17:35:55Z) differs from its own PARENT's (2026-08-31T13:36:40Z) and postdates trade 5414's open (2026-09-03T13:30:32Z) — the signature of a PATCH leg-replace, which re-submits the leg while the parent keeps its original timestamp; (b) the alpaca_paper mirror of the same strategy carries TLT buy stop 84.62 / buy limit 74.67 (qty 707), so 84.62 is what tlt_pullback_1d declares on the account that was NOT patched. The population for (b) is one mirror account, stated rather than generalised.

MECHANISM, read in the code and not inferred from the timestamps alone. execute.modify_open_order (src/units/accounts/execute.py) has two branches. The IB branch builds an order dict and passes oca_key = trade_id, under a 24-line comment explaining that without it the pre-cancel is SYMBOL-WIDE and strips sibling strategies' legs. The ALPACA branch, forty lines below, calls exchange_client.modify_protective(symbol, sl=sl, tp=tp) — symbol, and two prices. No trade_id, no qty, no leg id. AlpacaClient.modify_protective (alpaca_client.py:1106) then iterates EVERY open order on the symbol and PATCHes stop_price on every leg whose type contains 'stop'. On a symbol two strategies both hold, one trade's routine trailing amend rewrites the other trade's protective level. That is what happened here.

DIRECTION OF THE HARM, stated precisely rather than assumed. Both rows are SHORT, so a BUY stop is the protective side and a LOWER stop fires EARLIER. 5266 now rests at 82.33 against its declared 84.61875 — 2.28875 per share tighter, i.e. it will be stopped out early on 16 shares rather than riding to the level the strategy chose. That is the less dangerous direction and it is NOT the point: the venue level was set by a trade that does not own the leg, the journal and the venue now disagree for 5266, and the same defect with the arguments reversed loosens a stop instead of tightening it. It is also the mirror image of BL-20260820-PROTECTION-COVERAGE-IS-PRICE-BLIND's IB instance, which ran the other way: population n=1 trade (ib_paper MES 4350, 15 contracts), declared stop 7533.69642857 against a resting 7516.5, i.e. 17.196429 points x 15 contracts x the MES $5 multiplier = $1,289.73 of additional loss exposure. MEASURED, and quoted from that row rather than re-derived here. The TLT divergence measured in THIS row is 2.28875 per share on 16 shares = $36.62, and it is in the protective direction; the severity here is the mechanism, not the amount.

PAPER MONEY HERE — alpaca_portfolio is account_class 'paper'. alpaca_live is real money and shares this exact client code; it was verified FLAT (0 positions, 0 orders, read_state 'orders_read') at 04:47:34Z, so it is not exposed TODAY, which is a fact about its book and not about the code path.

RECURRENCE, filed with similar_ok: the class is BL-20260825-THE-TRAILING-AMEND-NEVER-PASSES-OCA-KEY-SO-IT-STILL-CANCELS-SYMBOL-WIDE. That row is about a caller omitting an available key on IB. Here the venue method has no scoping parameter to omit, so fixing every call site would not fix this.
resolution_criteria: Bring trade 5266's resting stop and its declared stop_loss 84.61875 into agreement — and it must READ trades.stop_loss for 5266 rather than take a level from a caller or an operator (the BL-20260820 criterion, which exists because the last repair of this class laundered a venue level into the journal). Tier-2.

Give AlpacaClient.modify_protective a per-trade scope so an amend can only touch the legs of the trade that requested it; a caller that cannot name its trade must keep the old behaviour LOUDLY, as the IB branch already does with its warning, rather than silently.

Establish from the audit trail WHICH amend wrote 82.33 at 2026-09-04T17:35:55Z and confirm it originated from trade 5414 — the timestamps and the price make this the strong reading, but it is a reconstruction and is recorded as one.
Confirmed by a read_state 'orders_read' showing TLT's resting stop legs each within a cent of their OWN trade's declared stop_loss.

updates.note: THE MECHANISM THIS ROW NAMES IS FIXED IN #11337, WHICH IS OPEN AND HELD (Tier-3, landing: hold) — so this row stays OPEN until that merges and is observed. AlpacaClient.modify_protective now takes the named trade's `qty` and PATCHes only legs whose own share count matches it; execute.modify_open_order forwards the leg row's position_size, which it already had. ⚠️ THIS ROW'S LIVE EXHIBIT IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING IN IT AND WAS NOT AVAILABLE TO #11337 WHEN IT WAS WRITTEN: MI-173 (#11312) found the same hybrid OCO on alpaca_portfolio/TLT and could NOT distinguish cross-trade contamination from journal/venue divergence, because the deciding modify_open_order log line was past the journal's ~30-minute retention. This row's read of the leg's submitted_at (four days after its own parent, and after 5414 opened) settles it as CONTAMINATION. So the defect #11337 repairs is EVIDENCED as having fired on a real book, not merely reachable. ⚠️ AND THE FIX IS A REFUSAL, NOT A RESOLUTION, IN ONE CASE: where two open rows on a symbol carry the SAME size, the named trade's leg cannot be identified at all — Alpaca leg ids are never captured at entry and place_protective sets no client_order_id — so #11337 returns retCode 1 rather than guessing. That gap is the subject of the sibling rows BL-20260908-ALPACA-PROTECTION-IS-NOT-TRADE-ATTRIBUTABLE-AT-ALL and BL-20260908-ALPACA-PLACE-PROTECTIVE-IGNORES-OCA-KEY-SO-EVERY-RE-ARM-IS-SYMBOL-WIDE, and closing it is what would turn the refusal into a repair. NOT VERIFIED BY THIS SESSION: the live state this row measured. I am citing MI-179's read, not reproducing it.

items.title: IBClient._locked_close Step 0 clamps close_qty to the SYMBOL's live position (min(requested_qty, live_qty)) — the same symbol-vs-trade scope confusion MI-168 fixed one gate downstream
items.resolution_criteria: NOTICED 2026-09-07 by MI-168 while re-scoping the close-confirmation in the same method; FILED, NOT FIXED, deliberately — MI-168's scope was the confirmation, and changing the clamp changes ORDER SIZING, which is a materially riskier Tier-3 edit than changing what counts as confirmation. src/units/accounts/ib_client.py Step 0 reads live_qty = self._live_position_qty(sym) — the SYMBOL total — and sets close_qty = min(requested_qty, live_qty). That is the same scope confusion as the confirmation gate, one step earlier in the same method. !! IT IS MUCH LESS SEVERE THAN THE CONFIRMATION BUG AND THAT SHOULD NOT BE OVERSTATED: it is a SAFETY clamp and it errs toward UNDER-closing (never transmitting more than the venue holds, which on a one-way futures account would open a reverse position), so it fails in the safe direction. The residual concern is a case nobody has observed: if the symbol total is BELOW this trade's qty because a sibling's lots are gone, the clamp closes the symbol's remainder rather than this trade's lots, which can close another trade's position. NO INSTANCE HAS BEEN MEASURED — this is read from the code, not from a journal, and is filed so the reasoning is not lost rather than because it has bitten. RESOLVES WHEN: either the clamp is re-derived from the trade's own lots with the symbol total kept purely as an upper bound (so it can never exceed the venue AND can never silently retarget another trade's position), or it is established that the current behaviour is correct and the reasoning is written down. Note MI-168's confirmation change consumes this same live_qty as its qty_before baseline, so the two are coupled: a change to the clamp must re-read docs/design/close-confirmation-scope-DESIGN.md section 2 before landing.

items.title: WO-20260906- and WO-20260907-ALPACA-LIVE-S-ROUTED-REAL-MONEY-LEG are two work objects for the same work, so a blocked_on edge written on one is invisible from the other
items.resolution_criteria: MEASURED 2026-09-07 by MI-168 while writing the MI-140 coupling edge. Both files exist under docs/claude/work/objects/, share the same parent_intent (IN-20260903-TRADING-SYSTEM-HEALTH), the same title stem and substantially the same why/done_condition; they differ in opened_at (2026-09-06 vs 2026-09-07) and stage (EVIDENCE vs QUESTION). WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the coupling MI-168 was dispatched to record is an ORDERING CONSTRAINT on real money (MI-140 must not be remediated before MI-168 lands, because alpaca_live's only protection is that it cannot place orders). MI-168 wrote the reciprocal blocked_on edge on the -0907- object the dispatch named. A session that opens the -0906- object instead sees blocked_on: [] with basis NOT_ASSESSED and no sign the constraint exists — and CLAUDE.md is explicit that an empty list is not the claim that nothing blocks it. A duplicated object makes a true edge unreachable from half its own identity. MI-168 did NOT merge them: consolidating two work objects is not this unit's scope and doing it unasked risks discarding whichever fields the other row holds. RESOLVES WHEN: the two are reconciled into one object (or one is explicitly superseded with a pointer), and the MI-140 coupling edge is reachable from whatever survives. Population note: MI-168 found this pair incidentally while looking for ONE named object; it did NOT sweep the 662-object store for other duplicates. We did not look.

items.tier: 2 (entry path — capturing leg ids at order placement)
items.title: Alpaca protective legs carry NO per-trade handle — neither captured leg ids nor a deterministic OCO group — so modify_protective can only identify a trade's own stop by MATCHING ITS QUANTITY, and must refuse when two open rows are the same size
items.detail:
FILED AS A KNOWN SIBLING of BL-20260814-IB-PROTECTION-BOOLEAN-NOT-QUANTITY, deliberately and with similar_ok, because the lexical probe scored it 0.88 and it is NOT a duplicate: that row is IB's and its criterion 2 ('Make protection TRADE-attributable, not symbol-attributable: persist the placed OCA group + leg ids onto the trade row') was MET FOR IB ONLY, via the deterministic per-trade group `oca-protect-t<trade_id>` shipped in PR #9331. Alpaca got neither half. The class is unfixed on a second venue, which is the finding.

MEASURED FROM CODE 2026-09-08 (read at origin/main, not inherited from prose):
  * `trades.sl_order_id` / `tp_order_id` are written on exactly ONE path — `execute.execute_pkg` — and that capture is gated by `str(account_cfg.get('exchange')).lower() == 'bybit'` AND `_bybit_tpsl_mode() == 'partial'` AND category != spot (execute.py, the `_tpsl_pre_leg_ids` block). Nothing else in `src/` or `scripts/` ever writes those columns. So for EVERY Alpaca trade both are NULL by construction, and NULL there is 'nobody captured it', not 'no leg exists'.
  * `AlpacaClient.place_protective` builds a GTC OCO but passes NO client-side identifier that would let a later call find that trade's own legs again — there is no Alpaca analogue of `oca-protect-t<trade_id>`. Alpaca's own `client_order_id` field is available on the order POST and is not used for this.

WHY IT IS LOAD-BEARING RIGHT NOW: it is the reason `AlpacaClient.modify_protective(symbol, sl, tp, qty)` — trade-scoped in this same PR — identifies the named trade's legs by MATCHING THE SHARE COUNT. That is an identification HEURISTIC, not an identity. It is sound whenever the open rows on a symbol differ in size, and it deliberately REFUSES (retCode 1) when two same-side legs carry the same qty, because picking one would be a coin flip on somebody's protection. The refusal is correct behaviour given the missing handle, but it is a capability gap standing in for a fix: a legitimate modify on a symbol holding two equal-sized rows now fails instead of guessing.

NOT ESTABLISHED, stated rather than filled in: how often two simultaneously-open Alpaca rows on one symbol carry the SAME position_size. MI-173 measured exactly one Alpaca multi-row pair in the population it looked at (alpaca_portfolio/TLT, 16 and 56 — different sizes, so the heuristic resolves it), and I did not extend that count. We did not look.

REAL-MONEY COUPLING, unchanged from the rows this one sits beside: alpaca_live is mode live / real_money and shares this client code. It is immune today only because it cannot place orders (MI-140).
items.resolution_criteria: Capture a per-trade handle for Alpaca protective legs at ENTRY, so identification stops depending on quantity. Either (a) persist the OCO parent/child order ids onto the trade row through the columns that already exist (`trades.sl_order_id` / `tp_order_id`) by widening `execute.execute_pkg`'s capture beyond the Bybit-partial gate, or (b) set a deterministic `client_order_id` on the protective legs at placement — the Alpaca analogue of IB's `oca-protect-t<trade_id>` — and look legs up by it. THEN make `AlpacaClient.modify_protective` prefer that handle and fall back to the qty heuristic only when the handle is absent (pre-migration rows). RESOLVED WHEN a modify on a symbol holding TWO simultaneously-open Alpaca rows OF EQUAL SIZE is observed patching only the named trade's leg — which is precisely the case that returns retCode 1 today, so the current refusal is the positive control and must be shown flipping. ⚠️ NOT sufficient: the qty-scoped path passing its unit tests, which is what already ships. ⚠️ NOT sufficient either: a modify succeeding on a symbol whose rows differ in size — the heuristic already handles that and such a pass proves nothing about the gap.

updates.note: CROSS-REFERENCE, added on the same day this row was filed, after MI-179's #11330 landed on main. BL-20260908-ALPACA-PLACE-PROTECTIVE-IGNORES-OCA-KEY-SO-EVERY-RE-ARM-IS-SYMBOL-WIDE is the SAME missing-handle gap seen from the third verb: place_protective's pre-cancel is unconditional and the `oca_key` its caller passes to scope it — the IB mechanism — is silently ignored, because Alpaca has no OCA-group concept for it to bind to. That is why the two rows are not independent findings: honouring an oca_key on Alpaca REQUIRES first creating a per-trade handle, which is exactly what this row asks for. Fixing this one is the precondition for that one. ⚠️ AND THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOW EVIDENCED RATHER THAN REACHABLE: BL-20260908-ALPACA-TRAILING-AMEND-PATCHED-A-SIBLING-TRADES-STOP-TO-THE-WRONG-DECLARED-LEVEL records the defect having FIRED on alpaca_portfolio/TLT — trade 5414's trailing amend rewrote trade 5266's stop to 82.33 against 5266's declared 84.61875.

items.title: The close path's 'strongest programmatic lever left' sends ?cancel_orders=true to DELETE /v2/positions/{symbol}, where Alpaca documents no such parameter — it is documented only on the close-ALL endpoint, so the escalation may be a silent no-op
items.detail:
FOUND WHILE trade-scoping the Alpaca close; NOT fixed here, because settling it needs a live broker probe this session could not make.

WHAT THE CODE DOES. `AlpacaClient.close`'s give-up branch, on an 'insufficient qty available' rejection, issues:
    self._request('DELETE', f'/v2/positions/{sym}?cancel_orders=true')
Its own comment calls this "the exchange's own atomic cancel-then-flatten, the strongest programmatic lever left before an operator paper-console reset" (BL-20260716-ALPACA-QQQ-WEDGED-PENDING-CANCEL).

WHAT THE VENUE DOCUMENTS (read 2026-09-08 from the Alpaca API reference, both endpoints, so the contrast is measured and not inferred from one page):
  * `DELETE /v2/positions` — close ALL positions — DOES document `cancel_orders` (boolean): "If true is specified, cancel all open orders before liquidating all positions."
  * `DELETE /v2/positions/{symbol_or_asset_id}` — close ONE position — documents `qty` and `percentage` and DOES NOT document `cancel_orders`.

So the parameter is being sent to the endpoint it is not defined on. Two readings fit and I could not distinguish them: Alpaca silently IGNORES the unknown query parameter, in which case the escalation is byte-identical to the plain retry that just failed and the comment overstates it by a wide margin; or Alpaca honours it undocumented, in which case the code is right and only the provenance is thin. ⚠️ THE FIRST READING HAS SUPPORTING EVIDENCE ALREADY IN THE REGISTER, which is why this is worth filing rather than shrugging at: OI-20260901-ALPACA-SHARE-HOLD-CLASSIFIER-SHIPPED-NOT-YET-OBSERVED records the alpaca_paper GLD 39-share wedge where "both close paths and Alpaca's own cancel_orders=true liquidation all fail" — i.e. the lever has been exercised against a real wedge and did nothing. That is consistent with a no-op and does not prove one (a genuinely wedged pending_cancel would defeat a working cancel_orders too).

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: if it IS a no-op, then the give-up path's diagnosis is misattributed. The log and the retMsg both say the escalation "also failed", which a reader takes as 'even the atomic cancel-then-flatten could not break this', when the truth would be 'the atomic cancel-then-flatten was never invoked'. That is unprovenanced diagnostic output on the wedge path — the same sub-class as the qty label this PR fixed one function up.

EXPLICITLY NOT ESTABLISHED: which reading is true. No broker call was made. Do not resolve this row by re-reading the docs — they are what produced the question.
items.resolution_criteria: Establish, AGAINST THE BROKER, whether `cancel_orders=true` has any effect on the per-symbol liquidation. The cheap decisive probe: on alpaca_paper, open a position, rest a protective order that holds its shares, then issue DELETE /v2/positions/{sym}?cancel_orders=true and read whether the resting order was cancelled — a response code alone settles nothing, because an ignored query parameter also returns 2xx. THEN either (a) it works → record the observation so the comment stops being a claim, or (b) it is ignored → route the escalation through the endpoint that documents it, or drop the escalation and correct the give-up log and retMsg so they stop reporting a lever that was never pulled. ⚠️ A green unit test resolves NOTHING here: the question is what a remote API does with an undefined parameter, which no fake can answer. ⚠️ AND a close that succeeds on this path does not resolve it either unless the resting order is confirmed cancelled — the flatten may simply have found the shares free.

items.title: MERGE-QUEUE.json entries stay `rebasing` after their PR merges — TWO phantoms de-phantomed by hand in a single manager session, and the phantom holds the one slot R8 exists to protect
items.detail:
MEASURED, n=2 in one session (2026-09-07T20:26Z-2026-09-08T06:58Z, population = every entry in docs/claude/work/MERGE-QUEUE.json over that window). #11306 read `rebasing` while merged as 161ee60a (stale 2h20m). #11318 read `rebasing` while merged as cf04a879 — found only because a de-phantom of a DIFFERENT entry happened to print the queue. Both verified against `git log origin/main --grep='(#N)'`, i.e. the commit on main, NEVER the PR page.

MECHANISM: nothing advances an entry when its PR lands. `check_manager_scope.py` R8 enforces at most one entry `rebasing` — a real invariant, because two concurrent rebases are how the 2026-09-03 dirty-three-times day happened. But the guard checks the COUNT, never whether the holder is still open. So a finished PR silently holds the only rebase slot, and the next manager either blocks on a queue that is actually empty or hand-clears it and learns nothing.

WHY IT IS NOT SELF-CORRECTING: the manager writes this file, and the manager is exactly who is busiest at the moment a PR merges. It is the same shape as MI-15's session-registry misses ('the moment a manager spawns is exactly the moment it is least likely to stop and write a record') and the same shape as the SESSIONS.json `working` rows that MI-178 measured 17-for-17 false. A register whose only writer is the party with the least attention at write time goes false by TIME PASSING, not by anyone being careless.

NOT A DUPLICATE of BL-20260720-MERGE-PROTOCOL-LAPSE (that is about claim-less merges racing `behind`; this is about the queue record outliving the merge). backlog_search returned 8 rows at <=0.56 overlap, all lexical; each was read and none is this.
items.resolution_criteria: A CHECK, not a reminder — a fourth restatement is the non-fix this repo has already paid for on MI-15. Either: (a) check_manager_scope.py R8 additionally FAILS when an entry in a non-terminal state (`rebasing`/`green`/`waiting`/`blocked`) names a PR that is closed or merged on main, so the phantom fails the next manager PR rather than waiting to be noticed; or (b) the merge-queue entry is advanced by the same mechanism that observes the merge. ⚠️ CLEARS ONLY ON AN OBSERVATION: the guard must be seen FAILING a real PR that carries a phantom entry, or seen PASSING a queue whose phantom was auto-advanced. A green self-test clears nothing — a harness is exactly what cannot reach a merge. ⚠️ AND IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES the queue should stay hand-maintained, this row does NOT clear, it CHANGES: the slot is then knowingly unguarded against phantoms and that must be RECORDED as a decision, with the consequence stated.
evidence: MERGE-QUEUE.json entry pr=11306 state=rebasing; git log origin/main --grep='(#11306)' -> 161ee60a (merged)
MERGE-QUEUE.json entry pr=11318 state=rebasing; git log origin/main --grep='(#11318)' -> cf04a879 (merged)
scripts/ci/check_manager_scope.py R8: counts `rebasing` entries; does not resolve any entry's PR state

items.title: exit_lever_soak writes mode='annotate' as a HARDCODED LITERAL on every row, so the file reads as 'every trailing lever is in annotate mode' when it is actually a log of the lever NOT firing — the inverted reading is one step away and I nearly filed it
items.resolution_criteria: MEASURED 2026-09-08 by MI-188b. Population: the last 1000 records of runtime_logs/exit_lever_soak.jsonl (TAIL CAP of a 1,376,985-byte file; spans 2026-08-30T00:53Z -> 2026-09-08T07:25Z; 193 packages, 19 strategies). ALL 1000 read mode='annotate': trail_decay 479, exit_head 183, stale_stop 179, giveback_stop 159. No other value is REACHABLE: record_exit_lever_annotation (src/runtime/exit_lever_soak.py:64) sets "mode": "annotate" unconditionally. THE FIELD IS NOT A MODE. The real gate is `declared_bars is not None` / `declared` (src/runtime/exit_levers.py ~L179 stale_stop, ~L272 giveback_stop; src/runtime/trail_decay.py ~L172 trail_decay): DECLARED in strategy YAML => the lever RETURNS A CLOSE/TIGHTEN AND WRITES NO SOAK ROW; UNDECLARED => it observes and writes one. So the file records only the counterfactual, and '100% annotate' is a fact about the writer, not the fleet. POSITIVE CONTROL that the inverted reading is false: stale_stop closed 14 real trades (2026-07-14 -> 2026-09-02, bybit_1 x11 ict_scalp_eth_15m + bybit_2 x3 trend_donchian_xrp_4h) and giveback_stop closed 5 (2026-08-13 -> 2026-09-02, uso_trend_1h on alpaca_portfolio/alpaca_paper) — inside the same window the soak reports as 100% annotate. This is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A (label does not describe what was computed) in a surface review sessions are told to read. RESOLVED WHEN: a reader of exit_lever_soak.jsonl can tell 'the lever was evaluated and DECLINED to act because undeclared' from 'the lever acted' without reading exit_levers.py — e.g. the field is renamed to something that names the counterfactual (evaluation_scope/observed_only) or the record carries the declared-vs-undeclared determination explicitly — AND a test asserts the two states are distinguishable in the written record. Evidence: re-read the tail and show a row that names its own scope.

items.title: exit_ladder_soak exists to accrue the evidence for graduating the multi-rung ladder to the real exit path, and every record it has written is a ZERO-RUNG ladder identical to the single target already placed — the precondition has been met 3 times in the system's entire history and all 3 were rejected
items.resolution_criteria: MEASURED 2026-09-08 by MI-188b. TWO populations, deliberately separate. (1) TAIL, n=1000 of a 641,866-byte file, spanning 2026-06-19T14:07Z -> 2026-09-08T06:01Z, 51 distinct strategies, venues api 945 / prop 55: ladder.n_rungs == 0 for ALL 1000 and differs_from_single_target == False for ALL 1000. (2) COMPLETE CENSUS of order_packages (n=4467, fetched total==4467) — this is what makes the tail conclusive rather than suggestive: a rung requires meta.tp2 distinct from tp (src/runtime/exit_plan.py L293), and exactly 3 of 4467 packages carry a tp2 EVER — pkg-b133100f432d4f47 (2026-05-10, orphaned), pkg-c5ac7d6ff4034131 (2026-06-02, orphaned), pkg-f6ec69a34e754e1f (2026-07-01, rejected), all turtle_soup, none reaching a managed exit. trades.take_profit_2 is positive on 0 of 5550 rows. So the soak whose stated purpose is the pre-flight evidence for the behaviour-changing P4 graduation has accrued ZERO evidence of a ladder to graduate to, and its own docstring says nothing reads it back — so nothing notices. SAME CLASS as BL-20260826-TARGET-EXTENSION-SOAK-IS-100PCT-SENTINEL-AND-CANNOT-YET-OBSERVE-THE-LEVER on a different soak; filed as a RECURRENCE of that class, not a duplicate of that row. NOT A CLAIM that the ladder is broken — it has never been reachable. RESOLVED WHEN: either (a) the soak records a run with n_rungs > 0 from a real executed order and that record is READ by something, or (b) an operator decision is RECORDED that the ladder is not being graduated, with the consequence stated — that exit_ladder_soak is then accruing a null result indefinitely and should stop being cited as evidence in flight.

items.title: An applied trailing amend leaves no durable record anywhere — both stop fields are overwritten in place, the only log line goes to a journal measured at ~30min retention, and no audit/outcome event is written — so 'how often does the trail fire' cannot be answered at all
items.resolution_criteria: MEASURED 2026-09-08 by MI-188b by tracing order_monitor._apply_update's KIND_MODIFY branch (src/runtime/order_monitor.py ~L1237-1470). An applied amend leaves exactly four traces, none durable: (1) db.update_order_package OVERWRITES order_packages.sl/tp in place, no history row; (2) trades.stop_loss/take_profit_1 likewise overwritten; (3) one logger.info -> systemd journal, whose retention this repo has MEASURED at ~30 minutes (CLAUDE.md, work_decision_sweep_receipt row); (4) enqueue_trade_update, a Telegram ping that is drained. VERIFIED ABSENCE, not assumed: zero log_signal_event/log_outcome calls in L1230-1480 (the only log_signal in the file is L6533, a different path). trades.protection_repairs is documented as DELIBERATELY excluding the ordinary trailing amend, and that exclusion is correct — this row is not asking to reverse it. CONSEQUENCE: the amend RATE is unmeasurable. The best available substitute is a LOWER BOUND on PACKAGES built from order_packages.exit_plan (frozen at entry — verified by grep that no update site exists) vs the current sl: 140 of 2098 gradeable packages (6.7%) show a moved stop, ALL 140 favourable (92 raised on longs, 48 lowered on shorts), the other 2369 of 4467 UNGRADEABLE because they predate the exit_plan migration (created 2026-05-02 -> 2026-07-16). N amends on one package collapse to one observation and a there-and-back move is invisible, so this is a floor on packages and not a count of amends. Same class as BL-20260816-TICK-COST-HAS-NO-DURABLE-HALF-SO-A-BUSY-MERGE-DAY-CANNOT-BE-MEASURED, on the exit path. RESOLVED WHEN: an amend is countable from a surface that outlives the tick — a durable append-only record carrying (package, old_sl, new_sl, lever, ts) — and a query over it reproduces at least the 140-package floor measured here. Evidence: the count, with its population stated.

items.title: RECURRENCE of BL-20260906-A-SUBSESSION-SPAWNED-WITHOUT-SOURCE-URL-GETS-NO-REPO-AND-ITS-WORK-DIES-UNPUSHED, plus a WORSE variant it does not describe: the container can attach a DIFFERENT repo and produce plausible findings from the wrong codebase
items.detail:
RECURRENCE, 2 days after the original was filed, and the recurrence IS the finding: BL-20260906-A-SUBSESSION-SPAWNED-WITHOUT-SOURCE-URL-GETS-NO-REPO-AND-ITS-WORK-DIES-UNPUSHED is OPEN and was not read by the manager that hit it. It is the 'we file lessons and learn none' class the operator named on 2026-08-26.

MEASURED 2026-09-08T07:14-07:19Z, population = the 2 sessions created by `create_session` with `source_url` OMITTED (the tool's own doc says an omitted `environment_id` inherits the caller's environment, which is TRUE and is NOT the same as inheriting its SOURCES):
  * MI-188 session_01PQraBU1dSD52tRyjwcWb8M -> session_context.sources =     [{git_repository: {url: 'https://github.com/the-lizardking/ict-trading-bot'}}]  <- A DIFFERENT REPO
  * MI-189 session_01JjJa5sRhrqQapwx25ebo6Q -> session_context carried NO `sources` key at all
Control: 4 sessions alive at the same moment (MI-180, MI-183b, MI-185b, MI-173) all read benbaichmankass/metis-insights, so this is the omitted parameter and not an environment-wide fault.

THE NEW AND WORSE HALF -- the 2026-09-06 row describes only 'no repo', which FAILS LOUDLY (MI-189 stalled within 90s asking whether to work on an 'ICT notebook'). The wrong-repo case FAILS QUIETLY AND LOOKS LIKE PROGRESS: MI-188 ran for ~4.5 minutes and reported 'analyzing trades journal (1000 newest); zero trailing/partial found yet' -- a confident, quotable, plausible measurement produced against the wrong codebase. Under CY-20260906-TRADING-TRUTH that is precisely the contaminated instrument the cycle exists to prevent, and a manager who did not happen to read `session_context.sources` would have banked it. It was caught only incidentally, while checking whether the push probe had run.

the-lizardking/ict-trading-bot is a REAL repo (the historical pre-rename remote, still referenced in operator preferences), which is why the clone succeeds instead of erroring.
items.resolution_criteria: A CHECK OR A DEFAULT, not a fourth reminder -- the 2026-09-06 row WAS the reminder and it did not hold. Either: (a) every spawn prompt opens with a `git remote -v` assertion naming the expected repo, alongside the push probe, and a session STOPS on mismatch -- cheap, and it converts a silent contamination into a loud refusal; or (b) the repo ships a spawn helper that always passes `source_url` so the manager cannot omit it. ⚠️ CLEARS ONLY ON AN OBSERVATION: a session must be SEEN stopping on a planted wrong remote, or a spawn must be seen carrying the correct `sources` because the helper supplied it. A green self-test clears nothing -- a harness cannot reach `create_session`. ⚠️ AND IT DOES NOT CLEAR by the 2026-09-06 row being closed: that row covers the no-repo case only, and closing it would leave the wrong-repo case -- the quiet one -- unwatched.
