items.title: observe_exposure returns early on an unreadable EQUITY, so open_gross_notional — a pure local SQLite sum needing no venue call — is never computed for exactly the accounts whose venue side is also dark
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08T07:25:30Z via /api/diag/exposure over all 11 declared accounts (count: 11, complete). 9 of 11 report measured:true. TWO report measured:false with unmeasured_reason 'equity_unavailable' and open_gross_notional:null — ib_live (REAL MONEY) and breakout_1 (PROP, mode:live). || THE ORDER OF TWO CHECKS IS THE DEFECT. src/units/accounts/risk.py::observe_exposure (lines 533-541) reads equity FIRST and returns unmeasurable(REASON_NO_EQUITY) at line 536-537, BEFORE line 538 ever calls _open_gross_notional_from_db(). So the notional is NEVER COMPUTED — not computed-and-discarded. That distinction is stated because it changes the fix: the value is not unknown, it was simply never asked for. _open_gross_notional_from_db is a read-only SQLite SUM(ABS(position_size*entry_price)) over trades WHERE account_id=? AND status='open' AND COALESCE(is_backtest,1)=0. It opens no socket, needs no broker and cannot fail for want of equity. || WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDY: an account whose EQUITY cannot be read is very often the same account whose VENUE POSITIONS cannot be read — both of these two are exactly that. So the one surface that could still answer 'what does the JOURNAL think is open here' goes dark at the same moment the venue does, and an auditor is left with no readable side at all. Measured consequence this session: /api/diag/exposure could not serve the journal side for either account and the count had to be obtained from /api/bot/db/table/trades instead. || THE MODULE ALREADY HAS THE VOCABULARY. src/units/accounts/exposure.py declares BOTH REASON_NO_EQUITY and REASON_NO_NOTIONAL (lines 70-71), so 'equity unreadable, notional fine' and 'notional unreadable' are already distinguishable states; the caller just cannot reach the second because it returns before looking. || THE VERDICT SIDE IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE CHANGED. exposure_verdict fail-OPENS on an unmeasurable observation, deliberately, because the alternative is an unreadable journal becoming a self-inflicted trading outage (Prime Directive). This row is about OBSERVABILITY only: an ExposureObservation that carried the notional alongside status:unmeasurable would change no routing decision. Nothing here proposes making an unmeasurable observation bind.
items.resolution_criteria: /api/diag/exposure is OBSERVED reporting a non-null open_gross_notional for an account whose exposure is still graded measured:false — i.e. the journal-side sum survives an unreadable equity. Verified by reading the live route for ib_live or breakout_1 and finding a number where null is today, with status/measured UNCHANGED and unmeasured_reason still naming equity. Explicitly NOT sufficient: a unit test (the two live accounts are what demonstrate it), and NOT sufficient: making the observation measured:true — that would be the collapse this repo's exposure module exists to prevent, and would be a REGRESSION, not a fix.

items.title: The prop balance ask fires correctly every 12h and has gone unanswered for 8.5 days at identical volume — nothing escalates, and the breach cushion is computed off the stale snapshot meanwhile
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08T07:2xZ. /api/bot/prop/status for breakout_1 reports the newest operator snapshot at 2026-08-30T19:33:29Z, status_age_hours 203.91 (8.5 DAYS), status_freshness 'stale' against its own status_max_age_hours of 24.0. On that snapshot rule_distance reports distance_to_dd_floor_usd 87.34 against a static floor of 4700.00 on a 5000 account, and day_pnl_state 'realized_unreported' with daily_loss_used_usd null. breakout_1 is mode:live with 3 strategies routed. || THIS IS NOT A RECURRENCE OF BL-20260814-PROP-BALANCE-REQUEST-ONLY-ASKS-WHILE-A-POSITION-IS-OPEN, AND THAT MATTERS. That row is marked resolved and describes this exact symptom (a breach guard computing off a stale equity), so an 8.5-day-stale balance reads as the fix having failed. IT HAS NOT FAILED. The cadence file runtime_logs/prop_status_request.json (via /api/diag/log_file?name=prop_status_request) reads {"breakout_1": "2026-09-07T19:46:07.298660+00:00"} — approximately 11.6 HOURS before this measurement, against PROP_STATUS_REQUEST_COOLDOWN_HOURS of 12. The ask is firing on schedule. A session filing this as a recurrence would have sent someone to fix working code. || THE ACTUAL GAP: at one ask per 12h over 8.5 days the account has been asked on the order of 17 times and answered zero, and the ask re-fires at IDENTICAL volume forever. There is no escalation ladder — no louder channel, no distinct alarm, no ceiling after which 'the operator is not answering' becomes its own reported condition rather than a quietly repeating request. An alarm that fires constantly and is routinely walked past is the desensitized-alarm failure this repo names as a P1 in its own right. || WHAT IT COSTS RIGHT NOW: MI-189b was able to reconcile breakout_1's journal against its venue (both flat) ONLY as of 2026-08-30. The account cannot be graded on a live basis by anything, because both sides of the comparison descend from operator reports and the newest is 8.5 days old. See docs/claude/work/UNREAD-ACCOUNT-VENUE-AUDIT-2026-09-08.md. || NOT A CODE BUG IN THE ASKER. Filed against the ESCALATION policy, not against src/prop/prop_status_request.py, whose cadence and account-selection are both behaving as designed and as documented in CLAUDE.md. || ⚠️ UPDATED 2026-09-09 BY MI-214 — THE 'IDENTICAL VOLUME FOREVER' PREMISE NO LONGER HOLDS, AND THIS ROW STAYS OPEN FOR ITS OTHER HALF. This row's diagnosis was right and its remedy is now partly delivered from an unexpected direction: the operator said the ping itself was unnecessary ('if there are no prop trades than the account state didn't change'), and src/prop/prop_status_request.py's TRIGGER was changed from the wall-clock age of the snapshot to whether anything has HAPPENED since it. On a genuinely quiescent account the ask no longer fires at all, so the ~17-unanswered-asks-at-identical-volume condition this row measured cannot recur in that shape. THE THRESHOLD WAS NOT TOUCHED (it has four consumers) and the pre-2026-08-14 flat bail was NOT restored. || WHAT REMAINS OPEN, AND IT IS NOW MORE IMPORTANT, NOT LESS: there is still no escalation when an ask that DOES fire goes unanswered — and every remaining ask is now signal-bearing (an open position, a real ticket taken against the cushion, or a read we could not make), which is exactly the precondition an escalation ladder needs. An unanswered ask used to be ambiguous; it no longer is. || AND THE SECOND HALF OF THIS ROW IS UNCHANGED: breakout_1's breach cushion is still computed off the 2026-08-30 snapshot and the account still cannot be graded on a live basis. MI-214 makes that state QUIET rather than NOISY, which is an improvement only because the noise was being ignored — it is not a fix for the staleness itself. A reader must not close this row on the strength of the ping having stopped. || See also BL-20260909-PROP-SIZING-REFUSAL-ON-A-STALE-BALANCE-IS-JOURNALED-BUT-NEVER-PINGED, the OPPOSITE failure in the same subsystem (a condition that produces no ask at all), which MI-214 surfaced while making this change.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) an escalation is OBSERVED firing — a distinct, louder signal (not another copy of the same request) raised after N unanswered asks, seen in outcomes.jsonl / /api/bot/logs?level=error or as a distinct /api/bot/notifications banner, with the unanswered-streak count carried in it; OR (b) an operator decision is RECORDED that an unanswered balance ask needs no escalation, stating the accepted consequence — that breakout_1's breach cushion may be computed off an arbitrarily old snapshot and that the account cannot be reconciled on a live basis. Explicitly NOT sufficient: the operator answering once and status_freshness returning to 'fresh'. That clears the CONDITION and says nothing about what happens the next time an ask goes unanswered, which is what this row is about.

items.title: Filtering prop_fills on status open/filled reports 18 open rows where the code sees 0 open positions — the row status is a report record, not position state, and nothing on the read surface says so
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08T07:2xZ over the COMPLETE prop_fills table (41 rows returned against total 41, so not truncated; /api/bot/db/table/prop_fills, order_state 'applied'). Rows carrying status in {open, filled}: 18. Distinct position keys under src/prop/prop_position_identity.py::position_key — which keys on (account_id, SYMBOL, canonical direction): 3. Open positions under src/prop/prop_monitor_pulse.py::find_open_prop_positions, which takes only the NEWEST fill row per key and admits it only when that row's status is in {open, filled}: ZERO. || SO THE NAIVE READ IS WRONG BY 18 TO 0, AND IT IS THE NATURAL READ. A prop fill row is a REPORT RECORD, not the position's state: an opening report keeps status 'open' in the table permanently, and the position is closed by a LATER row. Concretely, fill id 36 (SOLUSDT long 25.0 @ 99.94, opened 2026-08-26T22:18Z) still reads status 'open' today and always will; fill id 41 (SOLUSDT, status 'closed', created 2026-08-30T19:33:17Z) is the newest row for that key and is what actually closes it. || THIS COST REAL TIME AND NEARLY COST TWO FALSE FINDINGS. MI-189b, reading the status column, drafted (a) 'breakout_1 carries 9 open prop fills, one open 13 days' and (b) 'an open prop position's declared take-profit was crossed on 2026-08-27 and 08-28 and the position is still open'. BOTH ARE FALSE — the position closed on 2026-08-30, the operator reported it, and prop_sl_tp_alert's empty state file and prop_fills_staleness's empty findings are both CORRECT because there is nothing open to watch. Reading either of those as a broken detector would have been the unprovenanced-diagnostic trap this repo has a guard for, aimed at two mechanisms that are working. || NOTHING ON THE READ SURFACE WARNS OF THIS. The status column is exposed verbatim through /api/bot/db/table/prop_fills, which is on the diag allowlist and whose consumers include analysis sessions with no view of the grouping rule. The ONE owner of the contract (find_open_prop_positions / position_key) is correct and is not the problem; the problem is that the raw table is reachable without it and reads as if it answers the same question.
items.resolution_criteria: A reader asking 'what is open on a prop account' can get the answer WITHOUT re-deriving the grouping — EITHER a read surface that reports open POSITIONS (find_open_prop_positions' output exposed on a route, or a documented field on /api/bot/prop/status), OR the prop_fills read surface carrying an explicit caveat naming position_key as the arbiter. Verified by a session obtaining the open-position count from that surface and getting 0 for breakout_1 today where the raw status filter gives 18. Explicitly NOT sufficient: a comment added to prop_fills' table docstring in the code, since the sessions that hit this are reading the HTTP surface, not the module.

items.title: Criteria across this repo state only how to PASS, never how to FAIL — so an item that will never clear is indistinguishable from one whose mechanism is broken, and both sit `waiting` forever
items.detail:
OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-08, on Phase A: "it looks like we've sort of engineered a situation where we can't observe anything without contaminating it, which is inherently contradictory -- so either it's not a good guard to begin with, or we need to design an experiment that will allow us to observe it without contaminating the experiment itself."

THE GENERAL DEFECT, which is worse than the contamination it was spotted through: a criterion that names only satisfying observations and no refuting one CANNOT FAIL. It can only stay open. That is not a measurement -- it is a permanent parking space, and it silently COLLAPSES the two states this repo is most careful about everywhere else: 'the mechanism does not work' and 'nobody has happened to observe it yet' become the same `waiting`.

MEASURED 2026-09-08 (lexical heuristic -- see the caveat, and the population is stated):
  * docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json -- 64 rows carry a `clears_when`. 12 (19%) name an outcome that would close them NEGATIVELY (failed / refuted / unproven, or an explicit 'does NOT clear -- it CHANGES' decision branch). 52 (81%) are PASS-ONLY.
  * docs/claude/work/objects/*.yaml -- 682 objects carry a `done_condition`. FOUR name a negative outcome. 678 (99%) are pass-only.

THE MOTIVATING INSTANCE, and why it is not merely academic: WO-20260901-PHASE-A and PHASE-C require 'a session that arrives COLD, pointed at nothing, cites the CLAUDE.md brief'. Eliciting that requires asking; asking is pointing; pointing is what the criterion excludes. So the only admissible evidence is a coincidence nobody controls, with no expiry and no negative branch -- the phases have sat `waiting` since 2026-09-01 and could sit there indefinitely while the brief is either working or completely dead. Neither state is reachable from the criterion.

⚠️ NOT EVERY PASS-ONLY CRITERION IS WRONG. Some conditions are genuinely one-sided (a fix either is or is not observed on the fleet, and waiting is correct). The defect is specifically a criterion whose satisfying observation is NOT REACHABLE BY ANY ACTION AVAILABLE TO US, with no stated alternative -- that is the subset to find. The 81%/99% figures size the SEARCH SPACE, not the defect count, and must not be quoted as 678 broken rows.

⚠️ CAVEAT ON THE MEASUREMENT: the classifier is a REGEX over prose and therefore UNDERCOUNTS -- a criterion can express refutation in words the pattern misses. Treat the counts as a floor on pass-only-ness and a ceiling on negative-branch coverage. It was not hand-audited.
items.resolution_criteria: A CHECK, not a convention -- prose has already failed here twice (the criterion authors were careful people writing carefully). Wanted: a guard over docs/claude/work/objects/*.yaml and OPEN-ITEMS.json that FAILS a NEW or EDITED criterion which names no refuting observation and no expiry, with an override that must NAME why the condition is legitimately one-sided (verified, not presence-only -- the new-table-wiring-guard lesson). ⚠️ IT MUST BE DIFF-SCOPED FOR NEW/EDITED ROWS ONLY: an ungated pass over 682 legacy objects would red every PR on day one, which is how a guard gets disabled instead of fixed. ⚠️ AND CLEARS ONLY ON AN OBSERVATION: the guard must be SEEN failing a real PR that adds a pass-only criterion, and seen PASSING one that carries a negative branch. A green self-test clears nothing. ⚠️ IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES a negative branch should not be mandatory, this row does NOT clear -- it CHANGES: criteria are then knowingly allowed to be unfalsifiable, which is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one with the consequence stated.
evidence: OPEN-ITEMS.json: 64 rows with clears_when, 12 name a negative outcome, 52 pass-only (regex over prose)
docs/claude/work/objects/*.yaml: 682 done_condition fields, 4 name a negative outcome, 678 pass-only
WO-20260901-PHASE-A done_condition: satisfying observation requires a cold session to volunteer, unprompted, a citation of the brief; asking contaminates; no expiry and no negative branch
WO-20260901-PHASE-C carries the same clause in its first half; its second half ('the ceiling refuses a ninth parent') is sound and testable

items.title: check_board_coherence.py R3 says 'Comments and prose are explicitly ALLOWED and wanted' but grades a PYTHON DOCSTRING as an executable line, so the history it invites cannot be written where it most belongs
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 while fixing the R3 failure on main. `_is_comment` counts a line as a comment ONLY when it starts with `#` or `//`, so every line of a module or function DOCSTRING is graded EXECUTABLE. Reproduced: a docstring sentence reading 'This sentence used to name #6927 as a literal' failed R3 at scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py:315; rewording it to avoid the digits passed. The guard's own module docstring states the opposite contract -- 'Comments and prose are explicitly ALLOWED and wanted -- the history of why #6927 died is the most useful thing in those files' -- so the stated contract and the behaviour disagree, and a docstring is exactly where that history belongs in a Python file.

NOT FILED AS A BUG TO FLIP. The bias is DELIBERATE and documented in `_is_comment` ('deliberately CRUDE and deliberately biased toward calling a line EXECUTABLE: a false executable costs a reviewer one look, while a false comment is a hardcoded board number shipped silently'), and that reasoning is sound -- a docstring-aware parser would be the more complex half of a guard whose whole value is that it is impossible to get wrong. The cost is one reword, which is cheap.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY OWED is the DOC, not the code: R3's contract sentence should say 'a `#` or `//` comment', not 'prose', so the next author is not surprised at CI time by a rule the guard's own description told them did not apply. Workaround recorded at the point of use -- a note in check_pr_landing.py's `_board_claim_sentence` docstring says a retired number may not be named there and points at the `#`-comment block where it may.

POPULATION: one occurrence, found by hitting it. Nothing measures how many other docstrings would trip it, and a search for that would be the useful next step if this is ever picked up.
items.resolution_criteria: check_board_coherence.py's R3 description no longer promises that 'prose' is allowed — it says a `#` or `//` comment specifically — AND a planted self-test case asserts the docstring behaviour, so the contract and the code are pinned to each other rather than merely reworded. Closing by making R3 docstring-aware INSTEAD is also acceptable, but only with a self-test proving a docstring that names a retired number passes while `const board = <retired>;` still fails. ⚠️ Rewording the doc alone with no test clears nothing: the two drifted apart silently once already, which is this row.

items.title: docs/claude/session-board.json's own `_doc` and `schema` prose still name the RETIRED board as the authoritative live merge claim, and no guard can see it because R3 scans only .github/workflows and scripts
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 on main a0ec22ce. `docs/claude/session-board.json` `_doc` reads 'THE AUTHORITATIVE LIVE MERGE CLAIM IS THE MERGE SLOT CLAIM / RELEASE COMMENT ON THE LIVE BOARD (GitHub issue #6927)' and `schema.merge_slot` reads 'DURABLE MIRROR of the authoritative MERGE SLOT CLAIM board comment on #6927 (which is the real live claim)'. That board was retired at GitHub's 2500-comment cap on 2026-09-07T11:28:17Z (docs/claude/board-pointer.json `previous_boards`); the live board is resolved from that pointer.

WHY IT IS NOT MERELY UNTIDY, AND WHY IT IS MEDIUM. This is the file a session opens when it is about to CLAIM THE MERGE SLOT -- i.e. exactly at the moment it needs to know where to post the live claim -- and the instruction it finds there sends it to an issue whose writes 403. The failure mode is the one MI-182 exists to stop: a session concludes the claim is impossible, or posts nowhere, and the merge goes unclaimed.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT: check_board_coherence.py R3 scans only `.github/workflows` and `scripts` ('Prose lives in docs/ and is not scanned for R3 at all'), which is right for a doc recording its own history and wrong for an operational instruction telling a session where to post TODAY. R4 covers four surfaces (CLAUDE.md, coordination-board.md, the session-coordination SKILL, settings.json) and this file is not among them.

NOT FIXED HERE DELIBERATELY. MI-191's diff hinges on this exact file (R13's merge_slot claim and R2's new carve-out), and the carve-out's whole point is that a commit may change `merge_slot` and NOTHING ELSE in it -- so widening this branch's edit to `_doc`/`schema` would be the first thing to contradict the rule it ships. It is a one-key edit for the next session.

REMEDY: reword both to 'the live coordination board, resolved from docs/claude/board-pointer.json', and consider adding this path to R4's MUST_NAME_POINTER so the next rotation cannot leave it behind.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH: (a) `docs/claude/session-board.json`'s `_doc` and `schema.merge_slot` name the live board by POINTER ('resolved from docs/claude/board-pointer.json') and no longer by number, read back from the file on main; and (b) that path is in check_board_coherence.py's R4 MUST_NAME_POINTER, so the next rotation cannot leave it behind — verified by a self-test case in which the file stops naming the pointer and R4 fires. ⚠️ (a) alone clears this only until the next rotation, which is the failure being recorded rather than fixed; say which half you did.

items.title: Three sub-sessions in one morning could push but could NOT `git push --delete` a remote branch, and the failure is reported two different ways — probe branches accumulate on the remote with no cleanup path
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 across three independent sub-session containers, all on benbaichmankass/metis-insights, all of which pushed successfully in the same session:
  - MI-188b: `git push --delete` returns HTTP 403.
  - MI-189b: `send-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet`.
  - MI-191 (this session): IDENTICAL to MI-189b -- 'send-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet' then 'fatal: the remote end hung up unexpectedly'. Ordinary `git push -u origin HEAD` succeeded seconds earlier from the same container and remote.

SO IT IS NOT ONE SESSION'S ACCIDENT, and the two different error texts are the open question: one failure mode reported two ways, or two failure modes. Nobody has established which, and this row does not claim to.

COST, WHICH IS SMALL BUT COMPOUNDING: every session's Step-0 push probe strands a branch on the remote that its author cannot remove. Known stranded as of this filing: probe-push-20260908, probe-push-mi188-1788851739, probe-push-mi188b-1788852063, probe-push-mi189b-1788852087, probe-push-mi191-1788855439, scratch/trainer-relay-probe-0431. They are NOT abandoned work; three board comments now say so, which is itself the sign this needs a row rather than a third comment.

NOT DIAGNOSED. Candidates nobody has tested: a token scope that grants push but not delete (consistent with the 403), a proxy that mishandles a delete refspec's zero-id (consistent with the sideband disconnect), or branch protection. The cheap next step is to capture `GIT_TRACE=1 GIT_CURL_VERBOSE=1` on one delete and read the actual HTTP exchange.

MEANWHILE: a periodic sweep of `probe-push-*` and `scratch/*` from a context that CAN delete would keep the remote clean without solving the cause.
items.resolution_criteria: A `GIT_TRACE=1 GIT_CURL_VERBOSE=1` capture of one failing delete is recorded with its actual HTTP status and response, establishing WHICH of the two reported shapes (403 vs sideband disconnect) is the real one and whether they are one failure or two — and either the delete then works from a sub-session container, or it is RECORDED as a standing limitation with the sweep that cleans up `probe-push-*` named and owned. ⚠️ A successful delete from an interactive or manager session clears NOTHING: the failing population is sub-session containers, and a delete from somewhere else does not sample it. ⚠️ And the stranded branches disappearing is not evidence either — record who removed them.

items.title: check_pr_landing R13 requires EVERY armed branch to write the one `merge_slot` object, so N concurrent lanes each 'hold' a slot only one may hold and every lane after the first hits a hand-resolved conflict on the same 6 lines
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 on the live coordination board #11336. FOUR concurrent sub-sessions posted a START within four minutes of each other, and each declared it would write `merge_slot` in docs/claude/session-board.json for R13: MI-191 (claude/mi191-board-coherence-r13-r2, 08:19:30Z), MI-192 (claude/mi192-system-review, 08:19:59Z, listing 'docs/claude/session-board.json (merge_slot claim for R13)'), MI-193 (claude/mi193-operating-model-measurement, 08:22:06Z), MI-194 (claude/mi194-strategy-decision-record, 08:23:25Z). scope-overlap-audit independently flagged the collision on PR #11357 at 08:40:15Z. So this is four observed declarations, not a projection.

MECHANISM. R13 (added by #11344, merged a0ec22ce 2026-09-08T07:57Z) requires any branch that arms auto-merge to hold `merge_slot`, added-or-modified in ITS OWN diff, with `merge_slot.branch` equal to that branch. `merge_slot` is a SINGLE-VALUED object whose documented meaning is that AT MOST ONE session holds it. Each branch therefore sets the same 6 lines to itself, and each passes R13 on its own branch, so CI never sees the contention. Two consequences: (a) N branches simultaneously assert they hold a one-holder slot, and (b) every lane after the first gets a hand-resolved conflict on those lines, plus a stale claim left on main naming an already-merged branch.

⚠️ THE RESOLUTION RULE IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE BACKLOG'S, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT BL-20260821-BACKLOG-JSON-IS-A-SHARED-MUTABLE-ARRAY. That row is an APPEND-ONLY array where the correct resolution is a UNION and taking one side silently drops rows (BL-20260814-HAND-RESOLVED-BACKLOG-MERGE-SILENTLY-REVERTED-SIX-ITEMS-INCLUDING-A-RESOLUTION). `merge_slot` is a SLOT: a union is meaningless, and the correct resolution is TAKE YOUR OWN BRANCH'S CLAIM, because R13 grades your branch against your branch. A session that carries the class habit across from the backlog and 'unions' here, or that keeps the incoming side to be polite, fails its own R13.

⚠️ NOT A CLAIM THAT R13 IS WRONG. Its own docstring already states it does NOT serialize (BL-20260810-MERGE-SLOT-MIRROR-UNWRITABLE-PRE-MERGE: a committed claim reaches no other session until the branch merges) and that what it buys is an ATTRIBUTABLE, TIMESTAMPED claim on a route the PreToolUse hook is structurally blind to. That is real and worth keeping. What is UNDOCUMENTED is the per-lane conflict tax the rule creates the moment more than one lane arms at once, which is the normal operating mode here — and that the field now records N holders rather than one, so anybody reading `merge_slot` on main to answer 'is the slot free?' gets an answer that means nothing.

NOT FIXED BY MI-191. #11357 is the main-is-red repair and is held for a human merge under R12; widening it to redesign the slot store would delay a fix that every open PR in the repo is blocked on. Warned on the board instead so the four live lanes resolve correctly today.

CANDIDATE REMEDIES, none chosen here: (a) make the claim per-branch rather than a single slot — e.g. `.github/merge-claims/<slug>.json`, which is conflict-free by construction and is the same shape `.github/pr-landing/**` already uses successfully; (b) keep one slot but have R13 accept a claim in a per-branch file; (c) leave it and document the resolution rule. (a) is the option that also fixes the stale-claim-on-main half, and it is the 'slot store not gated on merging' that R13's own docstring says the real-time half needs.

⚠️ COROLLARY, ESTABLISHED 2026-09-08T09:3xZ AFTER #11357 MERGED — THE SLOT IS WRITE-ONLY VIA THE AUTONOMOUS ROUTE, SO IT CAN BE CLAIMED BUT NEVER RELEASED. R13 fires only on an ARMED branch and then requires `merge_slot.branch == this branch`. So a PR whose PURPOSE is to null the slot cannot arm — it would fail the very rule it is tidying up after — and must instead declare `landing: "hold"`, i.e. spend a HUMAN MERGE CLICK on pure housekeeping. The consequence is not hypothetical and is observable on main right now: 417bd6b6 merged #11357 and `docs/claude/session-board.json::merge_slot` on main still reads held_by session_014wizWRD5P388ZL3APK3EGG / branch claude/mi191-board-coherence-r13-r2 — a branch that no longer exists as anything but history. Every autonomous landing claims the slot and none can release it, so main permanently names whichever branch merged last, and the field answers 'is the slot free?' with 'no' forever.

THIS SHARPENS THE REMEDY RATHER THAN ADDING A SECOND ONE. Candidate (a) — a per-branch claim file under .github/merge-claims/<slug>.json — has NO release problem at all: the claim is deleted with the branch, or simply stops being the newest, and two lanes never touch one another's file. Candidates (b) and (c) both leave this corollary standing. Anyone weighing the three should weigh this too.

NOT A REASON TO STOP CLAIMING. The claim's value is the attributable, timestamped record on a route the PreToolUse hook cannot see; a stale claim on main is untidy, not unsafe, and R13 grades each branch against itself so a stale value blocks nobody.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) the merge claim moves to a per-branch artifact so two concurrently-armed branches produce NO conflict in it — verified by actually merging two independently-armed branches in sequence and observing zero conflict in the claim path, not by reading the design; OR (b) it is RECORDED as a decision to keep the single slot, with the take-your-own-side resolution rule written into docs/claude/coordination-board.md and into check_pr_landing.py's R13 failure message, so the next session hitting the conflict is told the rule at the point of use. ⚠️ A quiet week clears NOTHING: the conflict only appears when two lanes arm at once, so absence of conflicts is evidence about lane concurrency, not about this. ⚠️ And a single successful hand-resolution clears nothing either — that is the tax being paid, not removed. ⚠️ AND (b) MUST NOW ALSO STATE HOW THE SLOT IS RELEASED: recording the take-your-own-side rule while leaving the slot unreleasable means main permanently names a merged branch, which is the corollary above and is not a documented state so much as an undocumented one.

updates.note:
CORROBORATED WITH A COUNT, from the displacing side rather than the theory side. In ONE session (12:58Z-13:35Z) I had to displace THREE successive merge_slot claims, and in every case the PR the slot served had ALREADY MERGED — established from the merge commit, never from the age of the claim: session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj / claude/mgr-dispatch-1226-20260908 / #11387 (merged 42913d63); session_011PHmZzVy92M6zjNopAMy51 / claude/mi199-record-correction / #11392 (merged ea20e2c5); session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj / automation/work-digest-34220144791-1 / #11377 (merged 4f8b95bb). n=3 in ~37 minutes.

WHAT THAT ADDS TO THIS ROW: this row argues N lanes all 'hold' a slot only one may hold. The measurement shows the SECOND half — the slot is never RELEASED either, only displaced by the next claimant, so its held_by is a record of who armed most recently and not of who is merging. Both failure modes point the same way: the field cannot answer the question it exists to answer.

⚠️ AND EACH DISPLACEMENT COSTS A CONFLICT. Every one of the three produced an add/add or content conflict on docs/claude/session-board.json that I resolved by hand, which is exactly the register-churn cost MI-102 measured (26 merges in a day, 19 touching a shared register). The slot is not merely uninformative — it is actively generating the conflicts the merge queue exists to prevent.

⚠️ I did NOT file a separate row for this. It is the same class and a fourth id would split the evidence across rows nobody joins.

items.title: RECURRENCE of BL-20260907-DISPATCH-NAMES-A-WORK-OBJECT-THAT-WAS-NEVER-CREATED: the MI-195 dispatch named `operator_answers_2026_09_08` as the CARRIER OF THREE TIER-3 OPERATOR VERDICTS AND THEIR CONDITIONS, said READ THAT BLOCK FIRST, and the block does not exist anywhere in the repo
items.detail:
FILED AS A RECURRENCE, DELIBERATELY, not as a duplicate — backlog_search scored 0.86 against BL-20260907-DISPATCH-NAMES-A-WORK-OBJECT-THAT-WAS-NEVER-CREATED and the whole point is that the earlier row did not hold. That row (2026-09-07) recorded a dispatch naming a work-object PATH that did not exist; MI-148 recorded the same before it. This is the THIRD instance in the same thread, and it is the most dangerous shape yet, because the named surface was not the task description but the OPERATOR'S VERDICTS.

MEASURED 2026-09-08 on origin/main 417bd6b6. The dispatch reads: 'The answers are recorded verbatim under `operator_answers_2026_09_08` in docs/claude/work/objects/WO-20260907-25-OF-44-ENABLED-LIVE-LEGS-HAVE.yaml. READ THAT BLOCK FIRST — it carries the conditions, and a verdict without its condition is worse than no record.' Population: that file, plus every .yaml/.json/.md in the repo. `grep -c operator_answers` on the named file returns 0; `grep -rl operator_answers` across the repo returns nothing. WHY THIS IS HIGH AND NOT MEDIUM. The dispatch's own sentence states the stake correctly — 'a verdict without its condition is worse than no record' — and then points at nothing. A session that trusts the pointer has three Tier-3 verdicts (a live config value on a real-money-adjacent leg, a config vocabulary, and a published state for two live legs) whose CONDITIONS it cannot read. The failure is silent in the dangerous direction: the file EXISTS and is full of relevant prose, so a reader skimming for the block can easily come away believing they read it. The only reason this session did not proceed on a reconstruction is that it grepped rather than skimmed.

WHAT THIS SESSION DID INSTEAD, stated so a later reader knows the provenance is weaker: proceeded on the DISPATCH PROSE, which is one session's transcription rather than a committed record, and said so in the board START and in the PR. The two agree, which is reassurance and NOT verification of the 2026-09-08 answers.

THE REMEDY IS NOT ANOTHER REMINDER — that is what the two prior rows already were. The dispatcher writes the work object; the dispatched session cannot. So the check belongs where the dispatch is composed, or as a guard that fails when a spawn prompt names a `docs/claude/work/**` path-or-anchor that does not resolve on the default branch. Note the anchor half is the new part: BL-20260907 is about a missing FILE and a path-existence check would pass here, because the file exists and only the BLOCK is missing.
items.resolution_criteria: A spawn prompt naming a `docs/claude/work/**` path OR an in-file anchor that does not resolve on the default branch is REFUSED or flagged before the session acts on it — demonstrated by a probe that flags this exact dispatch string (`operator_answers_2026_09_08` in WO-20260907-25-OF-44-ENABLED-LIVE-LEGS-HAVE.yaml) against a positive control that passes for a block which DOES exist in the same file (`decision_requests`). items.title: The tp_intent reader (MI-158) shipped with ZERO tests: nothing asserts that a malformed block degrades to `undeclared`, and nothing asserts the never-summed property the vocabulary exists for
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 on origin/main 417bd6b6: `grep -rln tp_intent tests/` returns NOTHING. Positive control: the same grep over the repo finds 25 occurrences in config/strategies.yaml, 5 in scripts/research/bracket_expectation_census.py and 4 in scripts/research/regime_debt_matrix.py, and `git show --stat 3f88bfff` confirms the MI-158 commit touched exactly four files, none under tests/.

The two properties with nothing behind them are the two the vocabulary was accepted FOR. (1) `resolve_intent`'s docstring promises 'a malformed or non-mapping tp_intent resolves to INTENT_UNDECLARED rather than to a state -- a typo must never be readable as a decision'. That is a claim about the most dangerous input class and no test exercises it. (2) The three states must never be summed; today that is enforced only by a comment and by the shape of one print block, so a later refactor that folds `unexamined` into `none` for a tidier report would turn 'we did not look' into 'we decided' and no test would go red.

This is cheap to close — `resolve_intent` is a pure function with no I/O — which is part of why it is worth closing rather than carrying. Suggested cases: each of the three valid modes round-trips; an unknown mode string, a list, a bare string, None and a missing key ALL land on `undeclared` and are distinguishable from `none`; and a census run over the real config keeps the three bucket counts disjoint and summing to the sentinel total.
items.resolution_criteria: `grep -rl tp_intent tests/` returns at least one file, AND that file asserts BOTH: (a) every malformed input class — unknown mode string, list, bare string, None, missing key — resolves to `undeclared` and is distinguishable from `none`; and (b) the three buckets stay disjoint and sum to the sentinel total when `bracket_expectation_census.py` runs over the real `config/strategies.yaml`. A test that only round-trips the three valid modes does NOT close this row — it misses the typo case the docstring makes a promise about.

items.title: `scripts/ops/document_index.py --write` bumps `last verified` to TODAY on every document in the repo — 436 of them, including all three top-of-hierarchy canonical docs — and `document-index-guard`'s own failure message instructs you to run it
items.resolution_criteria: Running `python3 scripts/ops/document_index.py --write` on a branch that added ONE new document produces a diff touching `docs/DOCUMENT-INDEX.md` and that document ONLY — verified by `git diff --name-only | wc -l` returning 2, against the 439 measured on 2026-09-08. Either the writer stops touching `last verified` on documents whose content it did not change, or it gains an explicit `--restamp` flag that is NOT what the guard's remedy line tells a session to run. ⚠️ NOT sufficient: a warning in the guard message or in the script's docstring — the current failure IS a documented instruction being followed correctly.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 on branch claude/mi195-tp-decisions-and-examine (base origin/main 417bd6b6). This session added exactly ONE new document. `document-index-guard` failed with:

    R1 UNREGISTERED: docs/research/.../SUMMARY.md ... Run: python3 scripts/ops/document_index.py --write

Following that instruction produced a diff of **439 files / 927 insertions / 890 deletions**. Counted precisely: **436 of them had NO change other than a `last verified` date bumped from its real value to `2026-09-08`** (the other three being DOCUMENT-INDEX.md itself, this session's own source edit, and the new document). Among the 436: `docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md` (2026-09-07 -> 2026-09-08), `CLAUDE.md` (2026-09-07 -> 2026-09-08) and `docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md` (2026-09-07 -> 2026-09-08) — i.e. items 1, 2 and 6 of the instruction hierarchy — plus every sprint log back to 2026-05 and every skill SKILL.md.

WHY THIS IS HIGH. `last verified` is the field a session reads to decide whether a doc can be trusted. Stamping it asserts a verification that provably did not happen: no session can verify 436 documents, and this one verified none of them. That is the single failure this repo names most often — RULE ONE's *"'the last session verified it' is not verification"* and the MEASURED / INFERRED / DECIDED rule — committed at scale, in one command, by a session that is doing as it was told. It also destroys the signal permanently in the direction that cannot be recovered: a doc last genuinely verified in May becomes indistinguishable from one verified today, and there is no record of which were which.

AND THE GUARD IS COMPLICIT, which is what makes it a trap rather than a footgun. The blast radius is invisible at the point of decision: the guard reports ONE unregistered file and prescribes a command whose diff is three orders of magnitude larger. A session that runs the documented remedy and does not read `git diff --stat` afterwards ships it. Same family as BL-20260820-BACKLOG-APPEND-REFORMATS-AND-REATTRIBUTES, where the obvious idiom silently rewrote 21k lines — and that one was fixed by making the helper REFUSE rather than by documenting the hazard, which is the precedent this

=== SECOND INSTANCE 2026-09-09, ONE DAY LATER, BY A SESSION THAT HAD READ CLAUDE.md (session_01DUBXxiaZ3PMERcAfcJce7P, PR #11508). THE ROW EXISTED AND DID NOT PREVENT IT — that is the datapoint, and it is the operator's 2026-08-26 complaint exactly: a filed lesson that teaches nothing because nothing enforces it. Same trigger (added ONE document, guard said R1 UNREGISTERED, ran the prescribed remedy), same shape, LARGER blast radius: 452 changed files, of which 448 were a bare `last verified` bump to 2026-09-09 — up from the 436 measured on 2026-09-08, because the population grows. Caught only on the file count (expected ~9), reverted, and the one index row added by hand.

TWO HARMS THIS ROW DOES NOT YET NAME, both measured on that run:

(1) IT MANUFACTURES CROSS-SESSION COLLISIONS, so the damage is not confined to the verification field. `scope-overlap-audit` ran on the pre-revert head and posted to #11508: 'Compared 449 changed file(s) against 116 declared path(s)', naming ~12 `docs/research/*` documents as overlapping a LIVE session's declared paths (session_016KUFTHGYyFDerbnXDSA6Wb). Every one was collateral — that PR's real diff is 10 files and touches no `docs/research/` file at all. So running the documented remedy pollutes the coordination board's own audit with false collisions against sessions doing unrelated work, and a reviewer reading that comment would reasonably conclude the two lanes had collided. An independent confirmation of the blast radius, and a second failure mode.

(2) IT UN-REGISTERS THE VERY DOCUMENT IT WAS RUN TO REGISTER. The new file's own header was rewritten to `Doc status: unknown / last verified: never` — because the index row did not exist yet when the stamper ran — so the next guard invocation failed R3 DISAGREEMENT ('header says unknown but DOCUMENT-INDEX.md says live') on the file the remedy was supposed to fix. The remedy is not merely over-broad; on its own stated purpose it is self-defeating, and a session that runs it twice to 'fix' that is stamping the tree twice.

NOTHING ABOUT THE RESOLUTION CRITERIA CHANGES — they are already precise and this instance satisfies none of them. Adding the recurrence and the two harms rather than filing a fourth row: backlog_search returned this row at 0.77 overlap and per the filing rule a duplicate is dropped and the existing row updated. ⚠️ The workaround that worked, for anyone stuck before the fix lands: revert the collateral and add the single DOCUMENT-INDEX.md row by hand, then restore the new doc's own header to match its siblings. `--census` is report-only and there is no `--register-only`. should follow.

NOT FIXED HERE. This session reverted the mass stamp (`git checkout -- .`, preserving only its own source edit, verified by `git diff --stat` returning one file) and satisfied the guard by DELETING the generated artifact that triggered it rather than registering it, so no canonical doc was touched. That is a workaround for one session, not a fix: the next session to hit R1 will be given the same instruction.

⚠️ CHECK WHETHER THIS HAS ALREADY LANDED. This session did not audit the history for past commits carrying a mass `last verified` bump. If one exists, the dates in those 436 headers are already fiction and the row's remedy should include establishing which. === SECOND OCCURRENCE, 2026-09-09, MI-215 (session_01MrTjuoRpBb7spyQLydXmmT). THE DEFECT BIT AGAIN, ONE DAY AFTER THIS ROW WAS FILED, ON A DIFFERENT SESSION, BY THE SAME ROUTE: check_document_index.py R1 printed 'Run: python3 scripts/ops/document_index.py --write' for ONE new file, and the run modified 430 tracked files (git status --porcelain count) -- every .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md, 200+ sprint logs, docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md, and docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md, whose header went from 'last verified 2026-09-07' to '2026-09-09'. The DOCUMENT-INDEX.md diff alone was 459 insertions / 458 deletions for a one-row addition. [!] I did not find this row before filing a near-duplicate row of my own, since REMOVED and folded into this one, so no second id exists to chase: backlog_append's similarity probe did NOT refuse it, because my wording ('rewrites 430 files', 'asserts a verification nobody made') shares few tokens with this row's ('stamps a false last verified on 436 docs'). That is the documented token-overlap limit -- 'silence is not proof of novelty' -- and the lesson is to run backlog_search.py on the MECHANISM before filing, not only to rely on the append-time refusal. [!] THE COUNT DIFFERS FROM THIS ROW'S HEADLINE AND BOTH ARE RIGHT: 436 was the document POPULATION on 09-08; 430 is the number of tracked files git reported MODIFIED on 09-09. Different denominators, same defect -- do not read the discrepancy as a correction. WORKAROUND THAT WORKED, so the next session need not rediscover it: revert everything (git checkout -- $(git diff --name-only | grep -v <your own files>)) and insert the single index row BY HAND; the checker then passed with a 1-line diff. The same was needed a second time in the same session for a sprint log. [!] TWO OCCURRENCES IN TWO DAYS ARGUE THE PRINTED REMEDY LINE IS THE FIRST THING TO CHANGE: while it names --write, every session that hits R1 is pointed at the blast.

updates.note: IT BIT AGAIN, TWO DAYS LATER, EXACTLY AS DESCRIBED -- and the count has GROWN. NOT re-filed: this row already owns the class, so the recurrence is recorded here. I added one evidence doc, document-index-guard failed R1 with its own remedy line 'Run: python3 scripts/ops/document_index.py --write', I ran it, and it rewrote 455 FILES: 929 lines of docs/DOCUMENT-INDEX.md plus a `last verified` bump to 2026-09-10 on 454 documents I had not read -- among them CLAUDE.md, docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md (2026-09-07 -> 2026-09-10) and docs/ARCHITECTURE-CANONICAL.md, i.e. the top three of the instruction hierarchy. 436 -> 454 since this row was filed. !! IT ALSO MANGLES THE NEW DOC'S OWN HEADER, which this row does not currently mention and which is the part that costs the next session time: my header read 'Doc status: live . category evidence . produced 2026-09-10 by' and --write REPLACED it with 'Doc status: unknown . category unknown . last verified never ... nobody has verified this document's status - do not act on it as current', while also rewriting the relative link depth. So the remedy the guard names DOWNGRADES the very document you ran it to register. WHAT I DID INSTEAD, and it is a viable workaround for the next session: revert everything the script touched (git checkout -- . after stashing the real edits), hand-write the ONE index row next to its alphabetical neighbours, and hand-write the header in the convention a sibling doc uses. check_document_index.py then passes -- 'population=1034 registered=1034 headers_read=1034' -- with a ONE-LINE diff to docs/DOCUMENT-INDEX.md instead of 455 files. The guard's demand is satisfiable without the script; only its remedy LINE says otherwise. !! A --write THAT LANDS IS ALSO A MERGE-CONFLICT GENERATOR against every other open PR touching docs/, which is a second cost this row does not yet state.

items.title: `run_guards.py` reports `PASS n · FAIL 0` while running only three hardcoded pytest invocations and never the suite — so a session that follows the documented pre-push discipline can push a change whose OWN test file was never executed, and the summary does not state that denominator
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) `run_guards.py` runs the test file(s) whose path matches a changed module — for a diff touching `scripts/research/e35_shard_plan.py` it executes `tests/test_e35_shard_plan_data_basename.py` — demonstrated by reverting the MI-195 test fix and seeing the local run go RED where it went green on 2026-09-08; OR (b) its summary block states the denominator explicitly, naming that it does NOT run the repo test suite and which test files it did run, so `PASS n · FAIL 0` can no longer be read as coverage. ⚠️ NOT sufficient: a note in the docstring or in CLAUDE.md — the defect is that the OUTPUT carries a confident label its scope does not support, and the reader is at the terminal, not in the docs.
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-08, and it cost a red CI cycle on PR #11370 in this session.

SEQUENCE. MI-195 changed `scripts/research/e35_shard_plan.py` (added a feed-routing rung) and updated the module's own inline `--selftest` from 63 to 66 assertions, which passed. `python3 scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main` then reported **PASS 73 · FAIL 0 · SKIP 18**. Pushed on that basis. CI's `pytest-run` failed with exactly one test: `tests/test_e35_shard_plan_data_basename.py::test_leveraged_etfs_are_still_refused_by_name — DID NOT RAISE NoFeedSource` (1 failed, 15600 passed).

CAUSE, verified in the guard runner rather than inferred: `grep -n pytest scripts/ci/run_guards.py` finds exactly THREE invocations (lines 728, 1093, 1118), each naming specific files (`tests/test_orderflow_capture_freshness.py`, `tests/test_operator_owed.py`, `tests/test_over_cover_decision.py`). `grep -rn test_e35_shard_plan scripts/ci/run_guards.py` returns NOTHING. So the green was structurally incapable of covering the test file whose NAME matches the module being changed. The suite is covered in CI by the separate `pytest-run` job, so this is purely a PRE-PUSH gap — the loop a session is told to run before pushing.

WHY THIS IS THE 'GREEN IS NOT EVIDENCE' CLASS AND NOT JUST AN INCONVENIENCE. docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md names a green that checked nothing as the same sin as a red that checked nothing. `PASS 73 · FAIL 0` is an UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC (root CLAUDE.md sub-class C, unasserted denominator): the label reads as 'this change is checked' while the scope is 'these 73 named guards ran'. The runner already prints a careful `skipped (not relevant)` list and a `NOT SELECTED because the work is UNCOMMITTED` list — it is meticulous about what it did not run, EXCEPT for the repo's own test suite, which it never mentions at all. A session reading that output has every reason to believe the omission is exhaustive.

⚠️ THE OTHER HALF, worth recording because it is the more general shape: the CONTRACT WAS IN TWO PLACES. `e35_shard_plan.py` carries an inline `--selftest` and `tests/test_e35_shard_plan_data_basename.py` asserts overlapping properties; MI-195 updated the first and did not know the second existed. Neither is wrong to exist, but a session changing the module sees only the one inside the file it has open.

NOT FIXED HERE: this session was mid-drive-to-green on its own PR and widening the guard runner from inside that PR would have been exactly the unrelated-scope creep the merge protocol forbids.

items.title: RECURRENCE + UNIFICATION: the 'container cannot push' class and the 'spawned without source_url' class are ONE defect — 3 of 3 push-denied sessions carried a wrong or absent repo, and a session can predict it in ONE get_session call before spending any budget
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08T08:2xZ. items.resolution_criteria: BOTH, and they are different facts — say which you cleared. (1) PREVENTION: a spawn cannot omit the repo — either create_session is wrapped so source_url is always supplied, or a spawn with no explicit source_url is REFUSED. items.title: SESSIONS.json rows go false BY TIME PASSING, and the decay curve is now measured: median truth-lifetime 61.3 min, 47.9% dead within the hour — the number the existing 'no close writer' rows name the defect without supplying
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08T08:2xZ. POPULATION: all 164 rows of docs/claude/work/SESSIONS.json at origin/main a0ec22c, joined to live records from list_sessions — 164/164 resolved, so the JOIN is COMPLETE (the live listing itself was a 200-row page, but it covered every registry id). CLAIM vs TRUTH: 8 rows claim an active state; 1 is actually RUNNING (12.5%). The other 7 read IDLE. 94 rows now correctly say idle, so the register is better than MI-84's 69%-wrong reading — the wrongness has CONCENTRATED into exactly the rows a manager would act on. THE DECAY CURVE (n=163; 1 excluded as still RUNNING i.e. right-censored): min 1.1m, p10 21.8m, p25 40.4m, MEDIAN 61.3m, p75 121.6m, p90 718.9m, max 7502.3m. Dead within 30m 14.7%; within 42m 27.0%; within 60m 47.9%; within 120m 74.8%. THE '42 MINUTES' ANECDOTE IS THE 27TH PERCENTILE, not an outlier. ESTIMATED, NOT MEASURED: lifetime = live.updated_at - live.created_at. updated_at is the record's last write, which is activity for an idle session but is also bumped by archival/tag edits. DIRECTION OF ERROR: OVER-states life, so the true curve is at or below this one. WHAT IT BOUNDS: any decay/refresh mechanism whose interval exceeds ~60 minutes is by construction wrong about half its active rows. Design against the MEDIAN; the p90 of 12h is a real tail and is NOT the number to build to. THE PER-ROW READING IS SHARPER THAN THE AGGREGATE: MI-188's row was true for 4 MINUTES and MI-189's for 1 MINUTE — both are the wrong-repo spawns of BL-20260908-PUSH-DENIED-AND-WRONG-REPO-ARE-ONE-DEFECT-3-OF-3-AND-A-ONE-CALL-PREDICTOR-EXISTS..., so their rows were false almost from the instant they were written. THE SCHEMA CANNOT SUPPORT A DECAY RULE TODAY: 44 distinct field names across 164 rows; `state` on 156; state_observed_at / state_basis — added TODAY so a claim could be dated — on 6 rows, and on only 2 of the 8 rows currently claiming an active state. EIGHT timestamp fields compete to date a claim (state_observed_at, confirmed_at, observed_at, last_observed_at, last_observed, supervised_at, registered_at, spawned_at). Nothing can decay a row it cannot date under one agreed key. Extends BL-20260902-SESSIONS-REGISTRY-HAS-A-SPAWN-WRITER-AND-NO-CLOSE-WRITER-SO-EVERY-ROW-READS-WORKING and BL-20260905-THE-SESSION-REGISTRY-WAS-WRONG-ON-69-PERCENT-OF-STATES-AND-58-ROWS-HAD-NEVER-BEEN-OBSERVED-ONCE..., which state the defect and carry no lifetime. FILED NOT FIXED (research unit). Evidence: docs/research/operating-model-measurement-2026-09-08.md
items.resolution_criteria: A row claiming an active state either CARRIES a dateable observation under ONE agreed key, or is rendered as STALE rather than as fact. Verified by reading SESSIONS.json at a moment when a session is known to have died and finding its row NOT asserting `working` — i.e. observe the decay happening, not the mechanism existing. THREE STATES MUST STAY APART: observed-active / observed-inactive / NOT-OBSERVED-SINCE-<t>; collapsing the third into the first is the present bug. NOT SUFFICIENT: a reconcile pass run by hand (three have been run and the rows went false again within the hour); the state_observed_at field merely EXISTING (it exists now, on 6 of 164 rows); or a green guard — check_manager_scope R6 already grades the RECORD of supervision and cannot see a row that is simply old.

items.title: Individually-correct guards deadlock in two distinct sub-shapes (path polarity, content polarity) and neither is enumerable today, because a guard declares what it CHECKS and never which actor must write which path or content
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08 by reading the guards (scripts/ci/ READ ONLY — MI-191 owns the live instances; nothing here was changed). Two live instances today decompose into two DIFFERENT shapes, and a fix for one does not touch the other. SUB-SHAPE A, PATH POLARITY: check_pr_landing.py R13 REQUIRES a self-landing branch to write a merge_slot claim into docs/claude/session-board.json. check_manager_scope.py R2 grades a manager commit against MANAGER_SURFACE, which is a strict ALLOWLIST of 9 globs (docs/claude/work/**, OPEN-ITEMS.json, CYCLE-PRIORITY.json, pending-pings.jsonl, health-review-backlog.json, .github/pr-landing/**, .github/pr-automerge-requests/**, automation/**, comms/**); a path on neither the allowlist nor an active exception FAILS with 'not on the manager surface this guard can vouch for'. docs/claude/session-board.json is NOT on MANAGER_SURFACE. So a manager's own self-landing PR must write a file it is forbidden to write. Verified by reading both rule bodies, not inferred from the failure. SUB-SHAPE B, CONTENT POLARITY: check_board_coherence.py R3 forbids the retired board literal on any EXECUTABLE line under .github/workflows/ or scripts/ (comments deliberately exempt); the change required to satisfy R13 contained one. The conflict is over FILE CONTENT, not a path. IS THE CLASS ENUMERABLE? PARTIALLY, AND NOT WITH THE GUARDS AS STRUCTURED. I built the naive static detector for sub-shape A (extract each guard's concrete repo-path constants; report any not covered by MANAGER_SURFACE). RECALL ON THE KNOWN INSTANCE 1/1 — it finds check_pr_landing.py -> docs/claude/session-board.json. PRECISION UNKNOWN AND LOW: 19 candidates returned, 1 adjudicated; THE OTHER 18 ARE NOT-LOOKED-AT, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT STATE FROM FALSE POSITIVE and they are deliberately not reported as findings. RECALL ON SUB-SHAPE B: 0/1 — a path detector cannot see a content conflict. THE REASON PRECISION IS POOR IS THE FINDING: 'guard G names path P' is not the claim 'guard G requires ACTOR A to write P', and NO GUARD DECLARES THE SECOND — the requirement lives in imperative code and prose. Until a guard declares its satisfying set (which actor, which path, which content, required or forbidden) disjointness cannot be COMPUTED, only DISCOVERED BY HITTING IT. Both live instances were found by hitting them, which is the cost this row is about: each costs a red main and a session. AN UNTRIED EMPIRICAL ALTERNATIVE, recorded so it is not re-derived: cross-run every guard's own PASS fixtures against every other guard; a fixture green under its author and red under a sibling is a candidate. Most guards ship self-tests (guard_selftests.py, check_selftest_wiring.py). NOT-LOOKED-AT — I did not run this. FILED NOT FIXED (research unit). Evidence: docs/research/operating-model-measurement-2026-09-08.md
items.resolution_criteria: A guard pair whose satisfying sets are disjoint is detected BEFORE it reds main. Verified by the detector firing on a DELIBERATELY CONSTRUCTED conflicting pair that is not one of the two known instances — a detector validated only against the cases it was written from proves nothing. It must cover BOTH sub-shapes or say explicitly which one it does not cover: a path-only detector that stays silent on a content conflict is the unprovenanced-diagnostic shape (a clean negative that checked one of two conditions). NOT SUFFICIENT: fixing the two live instances (MI-191 is doing that; it removes two points, not the class); a green guard suite (both instances were green ALONE); or an enumeration whose candidates are un-adjudicated — 19 candidates with 1 verified is not a detector, it is a list.

items.title: due-list.yml grants no `actions: read`, so its red-crons source works only because the repo is public
items.detail: Found while wiring the same two sources into constraint-readout.yml. `.github/workflows/due-list.yml` declares `permissions: contents: write / issues: write / pull-requests: write` and passes `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` to the render step. When a `permissions:` block is present GitHub sets every UNLISTED scope to `none`, so `actions` is `none` — and `src_red_crons` calls `/repos/{repo}/actions/runs`, which needs `actions: read`. MEASURED, population = all 46 commits touching docs/claude/DUE.json on this clone: red_crons and unlanded_automation read successfully 12 times, were `no GITHUB_TOKEN` 32 times (local renders), and 403'd twice. So the source DOES work in CI today — but the most likely reason is that this repo is PUBLIC (public-repo Actions runs and PR lists are readable by any token), not that the workflow declared the scope it needs. WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH, stated as plainly as what I did: I did not read a workflow run's own log to confirm which of the two explanations holds, and I did not test a tokenless-but-public call. The alternative reading — that `contents` implies enough — is not ruled out. WHY IT MATTERS: if the repo is ever made private again (it was private as recently as 2026-07-06 per CLAUDE.md), this source starts returning 403 and grades `could_not_read` — honest, but permanently, and a red nightly nobody is waiting on stops surfacing. constraint-readout.yml now declares `actions: read` explicitly and does not have this dependency.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) add `actions: read` to due-list.yml's permissions block and OBSERVE a scheduled run whose committed DUE.json still shows `red_crons: read` — the observation is the point, since adding the scope cannot be distinguished from the public-repo path by reading the file; or (b) establish by reading a real run's log that `contents` already suffices, and record THAT, so a future session does not re-derive the question. NOT sufficient: the source continuing to read while the repo stays public — that is the condition being questioned, not evidence against it.

items.title: `git branch -r --merged` reports every squash-merged branch as UNMERGED, and this repo squash-merges everything
items.detail: I used `git branch -r --merged origin/main | grep -c <branch>` to decide whether a displaced merge_slot claim was STALE, and wrote the answer into a commit message on claude/mi196-due-readout-consolidation (43e2f556). THE ANSWER WAS WRONG AND THE TEST IS UNSOUND. `--merged` asks whether the branch tip is an ANCESTOR of main. A squash merge creates a NEW commit containing the same tree, so the original tip is never an ancestor and the branch reads unmerged FOREVER. This repo squash-merges by default (claude-pr-automerge arms `--squash`), so the test returns 0 for essentially every landed branch. MEASURED, two cases, both false negatives: (1) claude/mi191-r13-slot-release-corollary read 0, and PR #11364 from exactly that head merged 2026-09-08T10:33:27Z (confirmed via search_pull_requests head:<branch>, and #11364 is in main's log); (2) claude/mi193-operating-model-measurement read 0 while #11356 sits in main's log as 4f595f7d. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND MY COMMIT: the failure direction is 'this landed branch looks unmerged'. On the merge_slot that is cosmetic. But the same idiom is the natural way to answer 'is this branch's work already on main?' before reverting, re-landing, or cherry-picking - and there it would justify redoing work that is already in. WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH: I did not grep the repo for other uses of `--merged`, so I do not know whether any script or skill relies on it; that is the survey this row wants. Nor did I check `--no-merged`, which has the mirrored fault.
items.resolution_criteria: (a) Survey `--merged`/`--no-merged` across scripts/, .github/ and .claude/skills/ WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL (show the probe finds a known occurrence) and report the count, zero being a valid and useful answer; and (b) where any is used to decide whether work is on main, replace it with a test that survives squash-merge - the PR state for that head (search_pull_requests head:<branch>), or a content/tree comparison - and record which was chosen. If the survey finds NO uses, close this as documentation only: the value is then the recorded trap, not a code change. NOT sufficient: asserting the idiom is fine because a spot check happened to agree - the two measured cases here both agreed with the WRONG answer until the PR was read.

items.title: Three surfaces render the same due-list collector, and render_daily_brief — one of them — is referenced by no workflow
items.detail: Found while measuring the blast radius of the DUE.md retirement (operator decision consolidate_into_the_readout, 2026-09-08). MEASURED on origin/main at 0e03be9d, with a positive control (the same probe over 'READOUT.md' returns 5 files). THREE renderers now consume the ONE collector in scripts/ops/render_due_list.py: (1) render_due_list itself -> docs/claude/DUE.md + DUE.json, carried by .github/workflows/due-list.yml; (2) scripts/ops/render_daily_brief.py, which at line 150 does `from scripts.ops import render_due_list as _due` and at line 519 calls `_due.build(_due.collect(...))` wholesale; (3) scripts/ops/constraint_readout.py section 5, added by PR #11369 today. Only two of the three import it as a library; the first owns the rendering. THE FINDING IS THE SECOND ONE, which predates today's work and was not named in the operator's decision -- that decision was framed as 'a session had to read TWO surfaces'. There were already three. AND THE PART I COULD NOT EXPLAIN: `grep -rln render_daily_brief .github/workflows/` returns NOTHING, so no workflow appears to carry the daily brief. This repo has a recorded class of generators whose carrier does not fire (OI-20260902-DIGEST-MOVED-OFF-A-CRON-THAT-DOES-NOT-FIRE...; OI-20260902-HOURLY-DIGEST-CARRIER-PREPARED-AND-HELD...), so a generator with no visible carrier is worth establishing rather than assuming. WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH, stated as plainly as what I did: I did not check whether render_daily_brief is invoked from a systemd unit under deploy/, from another script, from a skill, or on demand only -- I only established that no file under .github/workflows/ names it. 'No workflow' is NOT 'no carrier', and I did not run the script or read its output for freshness.
items.resolution_criteria: TWO PARTS, different facts -- say which you settled. (1) CARRIER: establish what actually invokes scripts/ops/render_daily_brief.py -- a systemd unit, another script, a skill step, or nothing -- and record it. If the answer is NOTHING, that is the valuable finding and it becomes its own row about a generator nobody runs; if it is a carrier that exists, record which and whether it has fired, read from run/receipt history rather than from a schedule declaration. (2) DUPLICATION: decide whether three renderings of one collector is intended. It may well be -- they serve different readers (a due queue, a daily brief, a constraint readout) and they share ONE collector, which is the correct shape; this row does not assert it is a defect. What it asserts is that nobody has stated the intent, so a future retirement plans against an undercount. NOT sufficient for (2): deleting a surface to reduce the count without establishing who read it.

items.title: check_manager_scope's merge_slot carve-out requires `merge_slot` to be the ONLY changed key against EVERY parent, so a merge commit whose two parents differ on any other key in session-board.json is refused — the manager cannot merge main into its own armed branch
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 on the real branch claude/mgr-lanes-0819-20260908, twice, at commits 4361873f and c412c92c.

MECHANISM. #11357 (merged 417bd6b6) admits a manager commit touching docs/claude/session-board.json when the ONLY top-level key it changes in that file is `merge_slot`, and that check runs AGAINST EVERY PARENT. R13 separately requires every branch arming auto-merge to hold a `merge_slot` claim naming itself. Both rules are individually right. Together they make a MERGE COMMIT unsatisfiable whenever the two parents disagree on any other key in that file: taking either side's value changes that key against the other parent.

OBSERVED CONCRETELY. Merging origin/main into the armed branch, main's parent (c3486810) carried updated_at 2026-09-08T10:39:53Z and the branch parent (cc8670a9) carried 2026-09-02T06:20:00+00:00. Keeping the branch's value failed with 'it also changes updated_at against parent c3486810'; aligning to main's value then failed with the mirror message 'against parent cc8670a9'. There is no third value that satisfies both. `updated_at` is written by ordinary board activity, so the parents diverging on it is the NORMAL case, not a rare one.

CONSEQUENCE. An armed manager branch cannot take main in at all. The available moves are: (a) never merge main in, which fails once main moves and CI needs a re-run against a newer base; (b) force-push a rebase, which is prohibited; or (c) abandon the branch and re-lay the work as one linear commit off current main, which is what was done here (claude/mgr-lanes-1132-20260908) and which loses the branch's commit history and its open PR.

NOT A PROPOSAL TO WEAKEN THE CARVE-OUT. Admitting a merge commit generally would re-open exactly the hole #11357 closed by deciding admission per commit BY CONTENT rather than by path. A narrower candidate is to compare against the FIRST parent only for merge commits (R2 already reads a merge's first-parent diff elsewhere), or to exempt keys that are byte-identical to one of the parents. Both need the same adversarial treatment #11357 gave the original, and neither is attempted here.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a WORKER branch hits this. Workers are not graded by R2 at all, so the collision is manager-specific by construction — but no worker merge was examined to confirm none of them writes that file.
items.evidence: check_manager_scope.py --base origin/main at 4361873f -> 'docs/claude/session-board.json: it also changes updated_at against parent c3486810'; at c412c92c (updated_at aligned to main) -> the same message naming parent cc8670a9. pr-landing read OK (state=declared_self_land) on both, so the two guards disagreed about the same commit.
items.resolution_criteria: check_manager_scope.py is OBSERVED ADMITTING a merge commit whose two parents differ on a session-board.json key other than merge_slot, while STILL refusing a merge commit that also changes any other top-level key in that file — both halves demonstrated by a deliberate exercise in the guard's own --self-test, since a guard that only learns to say yes has been weakened rather than fixed. AND an armed manager branch is observed taking main in and landing without a re-lay. NOT SUFFICIENT: a green run over a branch that happens not to conflict — that is what every run already does, and it is why this went unnoticed until a merge_slot change landed concurrently. NOT SUFFICIENT: re-laying successfully, which is the WORKAROUND this row exists to remove; it has now been paid twice in one morning and each re-lay must be redone whenever another branch lands a merge_slot change first. IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES the carve-out should stay strict and re-laying is the accepted cost, this row does NOT clear — it CHANGES: manager register branches are then re-laid by policy, which is legitimate and must be RECORDED as a decision, with the consequence stated (every concurrent merge_slot change invalidates an armed manager branch), rather than left looking like a guard fix about to be written.
items.next_step: Decide whether merge commits get a first-parent-only comparison or a parent-identical-key exemption, and adversarially test whichever is chosen against the case #11357 was built to refuse (a merge that ALSO resolves other content is authoring and must stay refused). Until then, a manager branch that goes stale must be re-laid linearly off main rather than merged.

items.title: #11378 left a DUPLICATE `held_by` key inside session-board.json's merge_slot and every guard parsed past it
items.detail: MEASURED on origin/main at 1e1d3718 (2026-09-08T11:52Z): docs/claude/session-board.json's `merge_slot` object carried `"held_by"` TWICE, both reading 'MI-196 (session_01U2ibSa4FNcuV6bSLaPb9GS)'. The diff c3486810..1e1d3718 shows the shape of the mistake: a surgical string replace re-emitted the held_by line instead of replacing it, so the branch/claimed_at lines updated while held_by was appended. IT WAS HARMLESS THIS TIME ONLY BY COINCIDENCE -- the two values were identical. json.loads takes the LAST occurrence silently, so had the sub-session been claiming the slot FROM a different holder, every reader would have seen the new value and no reader would have seen that a prior claim was overwritten rather than released. THE REAL FINDING IS THAT NOTHING CAUGHT IT. The PR merged green: check_board_coherence.py, check_manager_scope.py's merge_slot_claim_only carve-out and check_pr_landing.py all read this file through json.loads, which is duplicate-tolerant by specification, so a structurally malformed claim renders byte-identically to a well-formed one on every surface that grades it. The merge_slot is the file's one load-bearing key -- R13 requires an armed branch to hold it and the carve-out admits a manager commit ONLY when it is the sole top-level key changed -- so it is exactly the wrong place for a defect that parses. REPAIRED opportunistically in the same commit that re-claimed the slot (claude/mgr-lanes-1152-20260908), because that commit rewrites merge_slot wholesale anyway and the carve-out permits precisely that change; the repair is therefore free and adds no new path to the diff. THE DETECTOR IS NOT BUILT and that is what this row is for.
items.resolution_criteria: A guard REFUSES a session-board.json carrying a duplicate key -- i.e. it parses with `object_pairs_hook` and raises on a repeat rather than calling plain json.loads -- and that guard is OBSERVED failing a PR that introduces one (a deliberate exercise counts; a green run over a clean file does NOT, since that is what every run already does). NOT SUFFICIENT: repairing the live file, which is already done -- the file being clean today says nothing about whether the next surgical replace is caught. NOT SUFFICIENT: a unit test over a fixture, for the same reason the rest of this repo does not accept a green harness as evidence a CI path fires. IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES duplicate-key detection is not worth a guard, this row does NOT clear -- it CHANGES: the merge_slot is then structurally unvalidated by decision, which is legitimate and must be RECORDED as one rather than left looking like a check about to be written.
