items.title: ib_paper/MGC: the journal holds 54 lots across two open rows while the broker holds 11 — trade 5531 (43 lots) is a phantom open row, and a live 43-lot protective STOP rests against it
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08 by reconciling every journal open row against venue truth. POPULATION: all 31 non-backtest status='open' rows in trades (via /api/bot/db/table/trades) netted per (account_id, symbol) and compared to /api/diag/exchange_positions captured 2026-09-08T10:29:57Z. 26 of 27 comparable (account, symbol) pairs reconcile EXACTLY to the venue — that is the positive control, and it is why this one divergence is trustworthy rather than a parsing artifact. THE ONE DIVERGENCE: ib_paper/MGC, journal net 54.0 vs venue 11.0, gap 43.0. It is two open rows: id=5353 (mgc_pullback_1d, 11.0 long, opened 2026-09-02T13:41:20Z) and id=5531 (ict_scalp_mgc_15m, 43.0 long, opened 2026-09-07T08:26:33Z). The broker position equals 5353 alone, so 5531's 43 lots do not exist at the venue. BOTH rows carry reconcile_status=NULL — the reconciler has not flagged either, so this is not a known-and-tracked orphan. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND BOOKKEEPING: a 43-lot protective STOP is resting against the phantom. PROTECTION_REASSERT re-armed it at 2026-09-07T11:55:19Z (protection_reassert_soak: trade 5531, decision=reassert, acted=true, applied_state=both_legs_resting, ocaGroup oca-protect-t5531), and trades.protection_repair_last_kind reads 'reassert' / 'both_legs_resting' on row 5531. If that stop fires it SELLS 43 MGC contracts the account does not hold, opening a naked SHORT of 43 lots — exactly the hazard CLAUDE.md names as CRITICAL for disjoint OCA groups. The over-cover page is CORRECT and has been firing since 2026-09-07T12:00:59Z (4 rows through 2026-09-08T06:09:21Z in /api/bot/logs?level=error, population 152 rows spanning 2026-08-25T05:37:42Z-2026-09-08T10:20:49Z, not at the 1000 cap): 'ib_paper/MGC: position 11.0 but resting STOP qty totals 54.0 (491%) across 2 DISJOINT OCA groups oca-protect-t5353, oca-protect-t5531'. The page is a SYMPTOM report; the phantom row is the cause. NOTE THE TIMING BUT DO NOT READ IT AS PROOF OF CAUSATION: the reassert landed 5m40s before the first page. I did not establish which mechanism placed t5353, and the reassert re-arming a bracket for a row the journal says is open is the mechanism behaving as designed on bad input. ROOT CAUSE (verified, not inferred): IB futures NET per contract, so one venue position backs N journal rows and per-order close detection cannot tell that ONE of two open rows has lost its venue backing while the other still has some. This is the same shape as the Bybit netting defect, and the remedy already exists FOR BYBIT ONLY: order_monitor._reconcile_netting_partial_closes selects accounts with `str(a.get('exchange','')).lower() == 'bybit'` (read at src/runtime/order_monitor.py, the bybit_ids set comprehension). There is NO interactive_brokers equivalent, so IB carries the identical netting hazard with no attribution path. ib_paper is a PAPER account so no real money is at risk in this instance — but the code path is account-agnostic and ib_live is real_money (currently mode: dry_run with 0 strategies).
items.remediation: TIER-2/3, PROPOSE ONLY — do NOT cancel the resting legs (standing prohibition; and BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG is what happened the one time this class was auto-remediated). Two separable pieces. (1) IMMEDIATE, operator decision: establish whether trade 5531 should be closed in the journal as an unbacked row, and if so close it and let its bracket be cancelled with it. (2) STRUCTURAL: extend the netting-attribution reconciler to interactive_brokers, or give IB its own equivalent — the Bybit implementation (leg-id-first, FIFO residual, live-leg-picked-last, three-state provenance ladder) is the design to copy, and NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_MODE's annotate-first staging is the safe way to land it. DONE-CONDITION: journal net == venue net for every (account, symbol) pair on a readable account, asserted by a recurring probe rather than by a session happening to look — there is no such probe today, which is why a 43-lot divergence stood ~26h with reconcile_status NULL.
items.resolution_criteria: TWO PARTS, and they are different facts — say which you cleared. (1) THE INSTANCE: trade 5531 is disposed of by an OPERATOR decision (closed as unbacked, or established as genuinely backed), and a fresh read shows journal net == venue net for ib_paper/MGC. ⚠️ The position simply closing does NOT clear this — that makes the divergence unobservable rather than resolved. ⚠️ Nor does the over-cover page going quiet: it keys on DISJOINT OCA GROUPS, so it falls silent the moment one group is cancelled while the journal is still wrong. (2) THE CLASS: order_monitor reconciles journal-vs-venue quantity for interactive_brokers, not only for accounts whose exchange is 'bybit' — verified by finding an IB account in the netting-attribution pass, or an equivalent IB detector, and by a recurring probe that nets every open row per (account, symbol) against the venue and reports an UNREADABLE account as unreadable rather than as agreement.

items.title: backlog_burndown() counts a row as opened only if it carries `opened_at`, but 287 rows carry `opened`/`date` instead and 70 carry no creation date at all — so the burn-down every /system-review steers by is understated
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08 across all three backlog files at working-tree head eafafae4. scripts/ops/system_review_checklist.py::backlog_burndown reads a single creation key, `opened_at`. Census of the health backlog alone: `opened_at` 930 rows, `opened` 283, both 15, `date` 8, and 70 rows with NO creation key under any spelling. Rows carrying only `opened`/`date` are counted as opened in NO month; the 70 keyless rows are invisible to every computation. POSITIVE CONTROL (so this is not a broken probe): the `opened_at` filter finds 930 health rows, so it works — it is PARTIAL, not empty. CONSEQUENCE, and it is the reason this is `high` and not `low`: the operator reframed the backlog metric on 2026-08-31 to NET BURN-DOWN precisely so a review measures CLOSING rather than LOOKING, and this is the function that computes it. Shipped series for 2026-08: opened 536 / closed 331. Recomputed with `opened_at or opened`: opened 677. For 2026-09 (8 days): shipped 91 opened / 15 closed; corrected 232 opened / 15 closed — a file-to-close ratio of ~15:1 against the ~1.64:1 the previous review reported. Cumulative open measured directly from status is 788 (health 721 = 537 open + 184 kept_open; performance 44; ml 23), not the 456 previously carried. This is the cycle priority (CY-20260906-TRADING-TRUTH) in the backlog domain: the instrument under-reports the quantity a review is told to move, so a review can believe it is holding the line while the pile grows ~2.5x faster than the number says.
items.remediation: TIER-1. (1) Make backlog_burndown read the creation date as `opened_at or opened or date`, and COUNT AND PUBLISH the keyless rows as their own state rather than dropping them — `no_creation_date` is 'we cannot place this row in time', which is not the same as 'it was not opened'. (2) Then converge the schema: backlog_append.py should stamp exactly one creation key and be the only writer, which is the structural fix for the whole `register-schema-is-not-one-schema` class (see BL-20260903-THREE-CREATION-DATE-KEYS-IN-ONE-BACKLOG-AND-THE-NEW-GUARD-ACCEPTS-ONLY-ONE, BL-20260905-BACKLOG-APPEND-HAS-NO-EDIT-PATH-SO-AMENDING-A-ROW-REQUIRES-THE-FORBIDDEN-HAND-EDIT). Fixing the reader is the two-line half and must come FIRST; converging the schema is the durable half. DONE-CONDITION: the checklist's burn-down block and a direct status census agree on the open count.
items.resolution_criteria: backlog_burndown() reads the creation date as `opened_at or opened or date`, AND publishes the count of rows carrying no creation key at all as its own state (not silently dropped) — verified by the checklist's burn-down block and a direct status census agreeing on the open count over all three backlogs. A code change alone does not clear it: the two numbers must be shown to agree.

items.title: grade-closed-trades' own `_delta_summary` says `truncated: false` while GitHub renders only the last 50000 bytes of the comment — the reader receives 66 of 165 rows under a banner asserting nothing was truncated
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08 on two real dispatches. Issue #11372 (run 34216722614): NDJSON delta 139808 bytes, comment rendered '(Showing last 50000 of 139808 bytes)'. Issue #11373 (run 34217219506), re-scoped to the review window: the trailing summary line reads {"_delta_summary": true, "emitted": 165, "truncated": false, "more_available": 0, "limit": 400, ...} and the comment STILL rendered only the last 50711 bytes — I recovered 66 of the 165 emitted rows. Both statements are individually true and together they mislead: `truncated: false` is a correct claim about what the ACTION emitted, and a reader takes it as a claim about what they RECEIVED. That is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A as CLAUDE.md defines it — the label names a quantity ('the delta') that is not the quantity the value describes ('the delta the action produced, before a transport the action cannot see'). The action's docstring explicitly says it exists to avoid 'the diag relay's ~55KB comment budget', so the size wall it was built to escape is still there one layer up. IMPACT: the grading-freshness guard requires every closed package in the window to carry a grade. A session that trusted this banner would append 66 rows, believe it had appended 165, and ship a report whose dossiers silently reference ungraded packages. NOT BLOCKING THIS REVIEW: I graded via the documented FALLBACK instead — scripts/ops/grade_closed_trades_from_diag.py fed from a direct /api/bot/db/table/trades pull over HTTPS, which has no comment budget at all. That produced 207 graded closed trades (B 90 / C 67 / D 50) with newest reviewed_at 2026-09-08T10:50:51Z.
items.remediation: TIER-1. Have the wrapper compare its rendered comment length against the emitted byte count and set the summary's `truncated` from what the COMMENT will carry, not from what the action produced — or, better, stop trying to pass bulk data through a comment: write the delta to a run ARTIFACT and put only the summary + artifact URL in the comment. Note the fallback grader's own docstring calls this action its replacement 'avoiding the size wall entirely'; that claim needs correcting in the same change. DONE-CONDITION: a dispatch whose delta exceeds the comment budget reports `truncated: true` with an accurate `more_available`, verified on a real oversized run.
items.resolution_criteria: A dispatch whose NDJSON delta exceeds the issue-comment budget reports `truncated: true` with an accurate `more_available`, OR the delta is delivered as a run artifact with only the summary plus a link in the comment — either settles it. Verified on a REAL oversized run, not a unit test, by comparing the emitted row count against the row count recoverable from the comment. The fallback grader's docstring claim that this action avoids the size wall 'entirely' is corrected in the same change.

items.title: check_unwired_artifacts.py enumerates `rglob('*.py')` only, so shell tools under scripts/ are outside its denominator entirely — its clean report is a SCOPE result, not a COVERAGE result
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08. The guard reports unwired=2 / doc_only=92 / skill_invoked=9 and exits 0. Its file enumeration is `rglob('*.py')`, with no `.sh` suffix test anywhere in the file, so shell tooling cannot appear in any of its three buckets — including the `unwired` one. LIVE INSTANCE: scripts/ops/llm_capacity_benchmark.sh, added 2026-08-31, has zero references anywhere outside docs/ and carries no `# wiring: manual-only` declaration (the repo's sanctioned marker, which 10 other in-window scripts do carry). It is genuinely unwired and the guard cannot see it. WHY THIS IS THE GUARD-IS-VACUOUS SHAPE: the `since_last_build_verification` coverage key instructs a review to 'run check_unwired_artifacts.py and read its diff against the previous run; a newly-appearing entry is a shipped-and-unwired capability'. A reviewer doing exactly that gets a clean answer about a population that silently excludes an entire file type. The guard is not wrong about what it measured; it does not state what it did not measure. Related: BL-20260831-COLLAPSED-STATE-GUARD-SATISFIED-ITSELF-SO-ITS-CENTRAL-CHECK-WAS-VACUOUS and BL-20260906-QTY-LEGALIZATION-GUARD-CANNOT-DETECT-THE-CLASS-ITS-OWN-DOCSTRING-NAMES.
items.remediation: TIER-1. Extend the enumeration to `.sh` (and state the suffix set in the output), and PRINT THE DENOMINATOR — how many files were scanned, by type — so a clean report carries its own scope. A guard that cannot say what it looked at cannot be read as evidence of absence. DONE-CONDITION: the guard's own output names llm_capacity_benchmark.sh as unwired, or that script gains a runner or a `# wiring: manual-only` declaration.
items.resolution_criteria: check_unwired_artifacts.py enumerates shell tools as well as Python AND prints its denominator (how many files it scanned, by suffix) so a clean report carries its own scope — verified by the guard's own output naming scripts/ops/llm_capacity_benchmark.sh as unwired, or by that script gaining a runner or a `# wiring: manual-only` declaration. A pass that merely stays green does not clear this, because green is what it already reports.

items.title: /api/bot/performance never applies exclude_reduce_leg_predicate — its correctness against phantom-PnL reduce legs rests on `pnl IS NOT NULL` plus a historical one-shot cleanup, which is the exact case the predicate's own docstring says that filter does NOT catch
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08. src/web/api/_clean_trades.py::exclude_reduce_leg_predicate exists specifically to keep reduce legs out of per-strategy analytics, and its docstring names two failure modes: count padding, and 'phantom PnL — a reconciler-flipped reduce leg booked reconciler_filled with entry==exit yet a large non-NULL pnl, a fabricated win/loss that the `pnl IS NOT NULL` filter alone does NOT catch'. Its only real consumer is src/web/api/routers/attribution.py (line 33 import, line 125 use). performance.py imports exclude_reconciler_predicate / exclude_reset_flat_predicate / exclude_superseded_predicate and NOT this one; its WHERE clause is status='closed' AND is_backtest=0 AND pnl IS NOT NULL, plus paper/not-paper, _EXCLUDE_RECONCILER and _EXCLUDE_SUPERSEDED. trades_closed.py likewise applies superseded and not-paper but not this predicate. THE LEAK IS ZERO TODAY AND I VERIFIED THAT RATHER THAN ASSUMING IT. Population: all 254 rows with setup_type='intent_reduce' (the table's full count for that filter). 253 are closed; 115 of those carry a non-NULL pnl — i.e. 115 rows `pnl IS NOT NULL` cannot drop — and ALL 115 carry reconcile_status='superseded', so _EXCLUDE_SUPERSEDED removes every one. Rows that would leak: 0. WHY IT IS STILL WORTH A ROW, AND WHY ONLY `low`: the defence is two historical mechanisms, not the predicate. PR #6926 stopped new phantoms at source, and the evidence says it has HELD — the newest phantom-pnl reduce leg closed 2026-07-18, while all 138 closed reduce legs since carry NULL pnl (newest 2026-09-06T03:32:39Z), so ~7 weeks with no recurrence. The superseded flags came from the one-shot `supersede-intent-reduce-phantom-pnl` system-action, which is correctly a manual Tier-2 cleanup and not a recurring job. So today's correctness depends on #6926 continuing to hold; if it ever regresses, the read path has no second line and the phantom lands straight in the headline PnL that promotion and demotion decisions are read from.
items.remediation: TIER-1, defence in depth: apply exclude_reduce_leg_predicate in performance.py (and consider trades_closed.py, where reduce legs currently surface to the SPA as closes with realizedPnl null). It is a pure narrowing of an already-narrowed population and is a no-op against today's data — which is precisely what makes it cheap to land and easy to verify: the endpoint's totals must not move. DONE-CONDITION: performance.py applies the predicate AND /api/bot/performance?window=30d returns byte-identical aggregates before and after.
items.resolution_criteria: src/web/api/routers/performance.py applies exclude_reduce_leg_predicate, AND /api/bot/performance?window=30d returns byte-identical aggregates before and after the change — the no-op result is the proof it is a pure narrowing against today's data rather than a silent restatement of the book. Consider trades_closed.py in the same change, where reduce legs currently surface to the SPA as closes with realizedPnl null.

items.title: session-board.json merge_slot carried held_by TWICE on main and no guard reads the file at all
items.observation: Measured on origin/main at 1e1d3718f while resolving a merge conflict in MI-192b: docs/claude/session-board.json's merge_slot object contains the key held_by TWICE, with identical values (MI-196, session_01U2ibSa4FNcuV6bSLaPb9GS). It is valid-enough JSON that json.load() accepts it and silently keeps the LAST occurrence, so nothing failed and nothing warned. Population: the merge_slot object only; the rest of the file was not audited for duplicate keys, so this is a lower bound, not a count. The MI-192b merge resolution takes its own branch's side per R13 and therefore removes THIS instance as a side effect -- that is not a fix, because the writer is unchanged. No script writes merge_slot: it is hand-edited by each session, which is how a duplicate key gets in. Verified that nothing validates the file: check_board_coherence.py is about the GitHub coordination ISSUE and contains zero references to session-board.json (grep, 0 hits), and run_guards.py registers no session-board guard. So the ONLY reason this was seen is that it happened to land inside a conflict hunk that was being read line by line.
items.why_it_matters: merge_slot is the coordination primitive that is supposed to stop two sessions merging at once. A duplicate key does not break that today -- json.load resolves deterministically to the last value and both copies were identical here -- so the honest severity is low. The hazard is the class, not this instance: if the two copies ever DISAGREE, the file reads as one session's claim to Python and as another's to a human reading the diff, and the slot is exactly the artifact where those two readers must not diverge. Duplicate JSON keys are undefined behaviour per the spec, so the tie-break is a CPython implementation detail, not a contract.
items.remediation: Add a session-board validity check to run_guards.py that parses docs/claude/session-board.json with json.load(object_pairs_hook=...) so duplicate keys RAISE instead of being silently collapsed, and fails the PR naming the offending key and object. Cheap, diff-independent, and it reads the file that today nothing reads. Do NOT fix this by hand-repairing the one instance -- that leaves the writer and the blind spot untouched, which is the post-it-note non-fix this repo already pays for elsewhere.
items.resolution_criteria: A guard registered in run_guards.py is OBSERVED failing a PR that introduces a duplicate key into docs/claude/session-board.json -- demonstrated with a positive control (a deliberately duplicated key makes it red) and a negative control (the current clean file makes it green), because a checker that has never rejected anything has not been shown to work. NOT sufficient: the duplicate key being gone from main (the MI-192b merge already does that, and it says nothing about the next hand-edit). NOT sufficient: a note in the session-coordination skill telling sessions not to duplicate keys -- the file already documents plenty that sessions miss.
items.found_by: MI-192b /system-review (session_012yX7SLyJiqAWG8oVxZSNoq)
items.superseded_note: DUPLICATE of the row named in superseded_by, which is STRICTLY BETTER and is the one to work. Both were filed within ~15 minutes on concurrent branches (this one from MI-192b resolving a merge conflict in #11379, the other from the manager re-laying a register branch onto 1e1d3718), so neither author could see the other and backlog_append's duplicate probe could not fire from either side -- it reads the file on the filing branch, and on each branch the other row did not exist yet. WHY THE OTHER ROW WINS, stated rather than waved at: it identifies the CAUSE (a surgical string replace in #11378 re-emitted the held_by line instead of replacing it, so branch/claimed_at updated while held_by was appended), and it identifies a sharper hazard this row MISSED -- because json.load keeps the LAST occurrence, a claim made FROM a different holder would have every reader see the new value and NO reader see that a prior claim was overwritten rather than released. That is a silent loss of the one mutual-exclusion primitive, which is why `medium` is correct and this row's `low` was wrong: this row argued severity from 'the tie-break is deterministic and both copies were identical today', which is true of the observed instance and not of the class. This row is retained rather than deleted because the two findings were reached INDEPENDENTLY by different routes, which is evidence the class is reachable from ordinary work and not a one-off. NOTHING here needs carrying across -- the other row already states the same structural fix (parse with object_pairs_hook so a duplicate RAISES), the same positive-control requirement, and adds an operator-decision clause this row lacked.

items.resolution_criteria: BOTH, and they are different facts. (1) THE INSTANCE: alpaca_paper GLD is flat or its bracket is gone, AND the resolution is ATTRIBUTED (operator/venue action, or Alpaca finally processing the group) — if the position simply disappears, record THAT rather than closing on it. (2) THE CLASS, which is the part that outlives the instance and does NOT close with it: either a coverage check is observed grading an inert leg as NOT protection — i.e. a real position whose stop has been through the market for a full session is reported uncovered rather than covered — or the operator RECORDS a decision not to model order liveness, with the consequence stated (an inert leg stays indistinguishable from a working one on every venue). ⚠️ NOT sufficient: the GLD position closing. That ends the exhibit and leaves the blind spot exactly where it is. ⚠️ NOT sufficient: a passing unit test — the claim is about what the venue does, which a harness cannot reach.
items.title: alpaca_paper GLD's resting OCO bracket is INERT at the venue -- a sell-stop 13 points in the money has not fired in 12 days, while every protection check grades the position covered
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08T12:21-12:44Z, live, three independent reads. (1) /api/diag/exchange_positions: alpaca_paper GLD long 39 @ 419.508462, unrealised -639.930018 => current price ~403.10. (2) /api/diag/alpaca_open_orders: the position's OCO bracket rests as parent 2e843e04-5487-470c-a702-70e796fbd05e (limit 461.27, status `new`) + child 891ddff0-b24d-4039-9322-8492bcd51e66 (STOP 416.09, status `held`), both submitted 2026-08-27. A sell-stop at 416.09 on a long trading at ~403.10 is ~13 POINTS IN THE MONEY and should have triggered days ago. It has not. (3) The trader journal at 12:20:54Z: our DELETE on the child is refused `rc=422 order pending cancel` while the open-orders listing renders that same order `held`, and our DELETE on the PARENT is ACCEPTED and the parent is still `new` twelve days later. Taken together these say the Alpaca PAPER engine has stopped processing this OCO group entirely: it will not fire it, will not complete a cancel of it, and will not release the shares it reserves. THE FINDING IS NOT THE STUCK CLOSE -- that is MI-199 and is fixed in #11389/#11390. THE FINDING IS THAT THE POSITION IS UNPROTECTED WHILE READING AS PROTECTED. AlpacaClient.has_protective_orders is a BOOLEAN over resting legs, so _check_broker_naked_equity_positions sees a leg, grades GLD covered, and re-arms nothing -- the same shape as BL-20260814-IB-PROTECTION-BOOLEAN-NOT-QUANTITY one venue over, but with a NEW cause: there the leg was real and mis-counted, here the leg EXISTS and the VENUE IS NOT EVALUATING IT. No coverage check anywhere models order LIVENESS, so an inert leg is indistinguishable from a working one. STATE THE POPULATION AND THE EXPOSURE HONESTLY: n=1, on alpaca_paper, which is a PAPER account -- no money is at risk and this must not be reported as if it were. What makes it worth filing at `high` is that alpaca_live is mode: live / real_money, shares this exact client code, and trades GLD; a real-money position under the same venue behaviour would read covered and be naked, and nothing in the repo could tell. I have NOT established whether the live (non-paper) Alpaca engine can produce this state -- that is the open question, not an assumed answer. CHEAPEST DETECTOR IF ONE IS WANTED: a stop whose trigger price has been through the market for longer than a session, on a position that is still open, is a positive observation of an inert leg and needs no new venue call -- both numbers are already on /api/diag/alpaca_open_orders and /api/diag/exchange_positions. Not built here; this row is the record.

items.title: A backed-up merge queue red-lines EVERY PR in the repo via digest-liveness, which makes the queue harder to clear — a self-reinforcing loop, not a one-branch strand
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08T13:05Z. `digest-liveness-guard` (scripts/ci/check_digest_liveness.py) reads docs/claude/work/WORK-DIGEST.json ON MAIN and fails when it is older than 6h. Main carried generated_at 2026-09-08T06:58:52Z, so it graded `stale` at 6.1h and FAILED — on EVERY open PR in the repo simultaneously, including #11389, the operator's twice-asked GLD close fix. THE CARRIER WAS NOT BROKEN. Three fresher receipts existed and every one was sitting in an UNMERGED PR: 11:20:56Z (#11377, trigger=schedule), 09:28:41Z (#11363, trigger=push), 07:58:32Z (#11354, trigger=push). The digest ran; its receipt could not reach main because the queue was backed up. THE LOOP IS THE FINDING, NOT THE STALE FILE. A slow queue makes a time-based liveness guard go stale on main; the stale guard reds every PR; a repo where nothing is green is slower to clear; the queue backs up further. It is self-reinforcing, and it is invisible from any single PR — each one just looks individually red for a reason that is nobody's diff. That is what distinguishes it from BL-20260830-A-TRANSIENT-RED-BASE-PERMANENTLY-STRANDS-AN-AUTOMERGE-BRANCH, which is one branch stranded by a base that was red once; this is a whole-repo condition that GROWS with the backlog. Filed as a sibling, not a duplicate. AND IT COMPOSES WITH THE MERGE SLOT. Only one branch may hold merge_slot (check_pr_landing R13), so clearing the backlog is serialized — while the guard that reds everything is driven by how long the backlog has been unclear. Verified on #11377: PASS 53 / FAIL 1 with the SOLE failure being the R13 slot claim, and PASS 54 / FAIL 0 once claimed. The content was clean the whole time. NOTE WHAT THE GUARD IS FOR AND DO NOT WEAKEN IT: F6 makes operator notification the condition the autonomy grant rests on, so a digest that has genuinely stopped reaching the operator SHOULD red. The defect is not the 6h window; it is that the guard cannot distinguish 'the digest stopped being PRODUCED' (real, alarming) from 'the digest was produced and its receipt is stuck in our own merge queue' (our problem, not the channel's). Those are two different facts and the guard collapses them. ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-09-09 ON A SECOND SIGHTING — THE MECHANISM SENTENCE ABOVE IS WRONG AND IT IS WRONG IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION. This row says the guard 'reads docs/claude/work/WORK-DIGEST.json ON MAIN'. It does not. `read_receipt` does `path.read_text()` on the RECEIPT PATH IN THE CHECKED-OUT TREE, so on a PR it grades THAT PR'S TREE. Read the code, not this sentence. The conclusion this row drew still holds for the 2026-09-08 incident (those branches sat near main, so main's receipt was effectively the one graded), but the stated mechanism would lead a reader to conclude 'main's receipt is fresh, therefore every PR is green' — which is FALSE. MEASURED 2026-09-09T19:5xZ on PR #11519: main carried 18:53:58Z (age 0.94h, PASS) while the branch carried 13:08:15Z (age 6.71h) and the guard FAILED on that PR alone. A long-lived branch goes red on the CALENDAR with a perfectly healthy channel, and the remedy is to merge main in — not to touch the digest. ⚠️ AND THE MESSAGE ASSERTS A CAUSE NO CODE PATH TESTED: it prints 'The channel has worked and has STOPPED' when all it established is that ONE TREE'S receipt is old. On that PR the channel had landed a digest 57 minutes earlier (#11586, opened and merged by commit-to-main itself in 2m17s). That is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A, whose remedy in this repo is to branch on the actual stage rather than reword the label — and there is precedent for the fix: `session-brief-guard` was DIFF-SCOPED for exactly this class (BL-20260902-SESSION-BRIEF-GUARD-CAN-TURN-A-PR-RED-FROM-THE-CLOCK-ALONE-NOT-FROM-ITS-DIFF). This adds a THIRD collapsed case to the two this row already names: 'produced, landed, and the branch reading it is simply old'.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) digest-liveness distinguishes the two states above — e.g. it grades `stale_unmerged` when a fresher receipt exists on an OPEN PR head, which is readable without a broker or VM call, and only grades `stale` when no fresher receipt exists anywhere; or (b) a recorded operator decision that the coupling is acceptable, WITH the consequence stated (every PR reds whenever the queue is slow). Landing #11377 does NOT resolve this — that refreshes the receipt and buys hours, and the loop is structural. Widening the 6h window resolves NOTHING and is the wrong direction: it weakens the only thing watching whether the operator is still being told anything, to work around a queue problem.
items.next_step: Do NOT hand this to the manager as an item — it is a build. Route it to a session with the measurement above; the whole finding is reproducible from PR heads plus docs/claude/work/WORK-DIGEST.json, with no VM access.

items.title: The session brief's SUNSET block never reads SUNSET-DISPOSITIONS.json, so it asks every session to disposition ten legs the operator already decided on 2026-09-04
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08T14:20Z. The CLAUDE.md session brief renders: '🗑️ SUNSET (E3): 10 retirement candidate(s) ... Retiring a leg is Tier-3 — propose, never enact. Disposition them in docs/claude/SUNSET-DISPOSITIONS.json.' ALL TEN ARE ALREADY DISPOSITIONED IN THAT FILE. Read directly: gdx_pullback_1d, gld_pullback_1d, iaum_pullback_1d, mes_trend_long_1d, scha_trend_long_1d, splg_trend_long_1d, spy_trend_long_1d, tqqq_trend_long_1d, trend_donchian_sol, turtle_soup — every one carries disposition 'repair', operator_decision 'refused', decided_at 2026-09-04, under DEC-20260904-DEMOTE-AND-TUNE-FLOW. Ten of ten, not a subset. MECHANISM, established with a positive control rather than inferred: render_session_brief.py delegates to sunset_pass.render_brief_lines(doc), which takes ONLY the sunset PACKET and never opens SUNSET-DISPOSITIONS.json. grep -c 'SUNSET-DISPOSITIONS': sunset_pass.py=1, render_due_list.py=2, render_session_brief.py=0 — and the single hit in sunset_pass.py is INSIDE the string it prints, i.e. the instruction telling the reader to go disposition them. So the verdict is computed from the candidate packet alone and the answer file is write-only for this surface. ⚠️ THIS IS THE DESENSITIZED-ALARM CLASS, AND IT IS THE WORST VARIANT: an instruction that CANNOT BE DISCHARGED BY DOING WHAT IT ASKS. A session that dispositions all ten sees the identical block next session. CLAUDE.md's own rule says a routinely-walked-past alarm is itself a P1. ⚠️ AND IT HAS NOW COST OPERATOR ATTENTION, WHICH IS THE MEASURED CONSTRAINT. On 2026-09-08 the manager surfaced these ten to the operator as an open decision, from the brief, and the operator answered a question that had been settled four days earlier. The brief is the ONE surface that reaches a session before it acts, so a false 'owed' here converts directly into a re-asked decision. ⚠️ WO-20260903-SUNSET-DISPOSITIONS-OWED carries the same stale premise ('Ten strategy legs ... have waited two days') with answer_state unset, so the work store agrees with the brief and disagrees with the register. FIELD BEATS COMMENT: SUNSET-DISPOSITIONS.json is the field.
items.resolution_criteria: render_brief_lines JOINS the candidate packet against SUNSET-DISPOSITIONS.json and reports the UNDISPOSITIONED count, with the dispositioned ones shown as a separate settled figure rather than dropped (dropping them would hide that a decision exists). Verified by rendering the brief against the CURRENT files and seeing the retirement-candidate count read 0-of-10-owed while the ten still appear as decided. ⚠️ NOT sufficient: hand-editing the committed brief text — it regenerates. ⚠️ NOT sufficient: deleting the sunset block — the candidates are real and a future undispositioned one must still surface. ⚠️ A row whose disposition is 'repair'/'refused' is DECIDED, not pending: do not re-open it as owed merely because the leg still exists.

items.title: An answered operator decision is never marked answered in the work store, so any session enumerating 'unanswered decisions' re-asks settled questions — TWO were re-asked to the operator in one message on 2026-09-08
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08T14:30Z. A manager enumerated unanswered decision requests across docs/claude/work/objects/*.yaml by reading each request's answer_state, got 12 rows with state UNSET, and put four of them to the operator as pop-ups. TWO OF THE FOUR WERE ALREADY ANSWERED. (1) The SUNSET TEN — all ten legs carried disposition 'repair' / operator_decision 'refused' in SUNSET-DISPOSITIONS.json, decided 2026-09-04 under DEC-20260904-DEMOTE-AND-TUNE-FLOW. (2) THE M7 REVIEW-PACKET POPULATION — DEC-20260902-REVIEW-PACKET-POPULATION was answered 2026-09-02T13:41:24.542165Z, chosen 'separate_populations', with the tap recorded in /api/diag/log_file?name=work_decision_transit (submission_id e380ea72ed4e4a15af6b16a08e2efb22, submitted_by 'telegram'). The operator's 2026-09-08 answer ('split them') is the SAME answer, given again. THE MECHANISM: answer_state on the object's decision_request is never written back when the answer lands. WO-20260902-DECISION-REVIEW-PACKET-POPULATION still reads lifecycle 'waiting' with an ACTIVE blocked_on{kind: operator_decision, ref: DEC-20260902-REVIEW-PACKET-POPULATION} six days after that ref was answered, and CONSTRAINT.json/READOUT.md faithfully re-render the same stale edge. So every downstream surface agrees with the object and disagrees with the answer. ⚠️ AND THE RECORD IS INTERNALLY CONTRADICTORY ON THE SAME DECISION, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MAKES IT UNSAFE RATHER THAN MERELY NOISY: the transit row says chosen 'separate_populations', while merged PR #10807 is titled 'work: operator answers DEC-20260902-REVIEW-PACKET-POPULATION — both options refused'. Those are different outcomes for one decision id. A session reading either one alone would act confidently and possibly oppositely. Establishing which is correct is part of this row, NOT an assumption to carry: the 2026-09-08 re-answer favours 'separate populations', but that is a THIRD data point rather than a resolution of the first two. ⚠️ THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS BL-20260908-THE-SESSION-BRIEF-ASKS-EVERY-SESSION-TO-DISPOSITION-TEN-LEGS-THAT-WERE-DISPOSITIONED-FOUR-DAYS-AGO AND IS THE WIDER ONE. That row is one renderer failing to read one answer file; this is the write-back itself missing, so it applies to EVERY decision request. Filed as a sibling, not a duplicate. ⚠️ THE COST IS OPERATOR ATTENTION, WHICH IS THE MEASURED CONSTRAINT (DECISION). Re-asking a settled question spends the exact resource the whole operating-model build exists to relieve, and it teaches the operator that the decision queue is untrustworthy — which is worse than the delay.
items.resolution_criteria: A decision request whose ref has been answered can no longer be enumerated as unanswered. Concretely: the object's decision_request carries a terminal answer_state (with the chosen option and the answer's timestamp), the blocked_on{kind: operator_decision} edge is cleared or marked satisfied, and CONSTRAINT.json/READOUT.md stop rendering it as an active hold. items.title: Alpaca ACCEPTS our cancel with a 2xx and the orders do not go away -- they stay at `new`/`held` with canceled_at null, so classify_share_hold grades `orders_still_resting` ("a retry may clear it") on a hold that has stood 12 days, and PAGES the operator every time
items.detail:
MEASURED on the live alpaca_paper GLD hold, 2026-09-08, on trader git_sha bdccf226 (i.e. WITH #11389 deployed). Population for the alert counts: runtime_logs/operator_alerts.jsonl, last 600 lines, span 2026-09-01T18:29:17Z -> 2026-09-08T14:16:09Z, 278 close_failure rows of which 269 are GLD.

=== THE OBSERVATION, from ONE give-up line at 14:12:54Z ===
  cancel: accepted=2 already_gone=0 refused=0
  ... the close path then waits ~6.0s and re-reads ...
  2e843e04-5487-470c-a702-70e796fbd05e  status 'new'   canceled_at: None
  891ddff0-b24d-4039-9322-8492bcd51e66  status 'held'  canceled_at: None
  -> share_hold=orders_still_resting -- "a retry may clear it"
Alpaca returned 2xx for BOTH cancels (there are exactly two GLD orders, so it accepted every one) and then did not perform either. The orders do not even move to pending_cancel -- the broker is not claiming to be cancelling them. Four consecutive attempts across 14:18:20 -> 14:19:50Z are byte-identical, and a direct venue read at 14:19:42Z (/api/diag/alpaca_open_orders) shows both unchanged since their 2026-08-27 submission.

=== WHY THE CLASSIFIER CANNOT SAY THIS ===
classify_share_hold reads STATUSES. `new` and `held` are ordinary cancellable statuses, so the honest reading of the listing alone is `orders_still_resting`, whose text is "the next tick's cancel-then-retry may well clear this on its own. Worth watching before acting." It has said that 181 times over seven days about orders that have not moved in twelve. There is no state for `we asked, the broker said yes, and nothing happened`.

=== THIS IS NOT THE ROW #11389 CLOSED, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE POINT ===
BL-20260901-ALPACA-CANCEL-WEDGE-UNNAMED and BL-20260716-ALPACA-QQQ-WEDGED-PENDING-CANCEL are both about an order sitting at `pending_cancel` -- the shape where the broker DOES say it is cancelling. #11389 (merged bdccf226) handles that and handles the DELETE refusing with `422 order pending cancel`. Neither reaches this: post-deploy the cancel is REFUSED zero times and the listing shows no wedged status, so both of #11389's branches correctly decline and the reading falls through to `orders_still_resting`. #11389 is not wrong; the venue simply stopped producing the evidence it keys on.

=== IT IS A RECURRENCE OF A NAMED CLASS, ONE VENUE OVER, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS FILED RATHER THAN DROPPED ===
BL-20260816-IB-CANCEL-ACCEPTED-BUT-NEVER-COMPLETES-VENUE-CLOSED (open) records IB accepting cancelOrder with retCode 0 'OK' while the order does not go away. Same class: BL-20260825-PLACE-PROTECTIVE-COUNTS-THE-CANCEL-CALL-NOT-ITS-EFFECT, i.e. we count the call the broker ACCEPTED and never whether it WORKED. The IB row's own remedy note asks for a way to say 'accepted, pending at venue' distinctly from 'not effective'; Alpaca needs the same distinction and has even less -- it cannot say either.

=== THE OPERATOR COST, STATED WITH ITS POPULATION ===
GLD close_failure rows 2026-09-04 -> 2026-09-08, n=122: 63 PAGES carrying `orders_still_resting`, against 57 digest + 2 pages carrying `broker_cancel_wedged`. So 63 of the 65 pages in that window come from this reading. close_wedge_standing.UNCLEARABLE_HOLD_STATE is the single string "broker_cancel_wedged", so the MI-34 digest downgrade cannot reach them and neither can #11406's retry suppression. The downgrade itself is working correctly -- 57 digest vs 2 pages when the classification does land -- it is being fed the reassuring reading. This is the desensitised-alarm P1 shape: an alarm that says 'may well clear on its own' 181 times about something that provably will not.

=== THE EVIDENCE FOR A FIX IS ALREADY IN HAND AT THE CLASSIFICATION SITE ===
Both close paths already hold `last_cancel` (a CancelOutcome) and `residual` (the post-wait listing) when they call classify_share_hold. What is missing is only that CancelOutcome.accepted is an int COUNT, not the ids -- so the intersection `we asked to cancel this id AND the broker accepted AND it is still resting AND canceled_at is None` cannot be computed. That intersection is evidence from two broker endpoints inside a SINGLE attempt: it is not 'the failure repeated', which is the thing the MI-199 dispatch explicitly forbids keying on.

NOT YET ESTABLISHED, and deliberately not asserted: WHY Alpaca accepts and does not act. A plausible reading is that an OCO leg cannot be cancelled individually and the parent cancel is silently dropped, but that is a hypothesis and no venue-side confirmation has been obtained. The finding does not depend on it -- the system defect is that no state can express the observation, whatever its cause.

SCOPE: alpaca_paper is PAPER, no money at risk. alpaca_live is REAL MONEY, shares this client code and trades GLD; whether the live engine can reach this state is OPEN and untested.
resolution_criteria: INSTANCE: a give-up on the live fleet is OBSERVED emitting a share_hold that distinguishes 'the broker accepted our cancel and did not perform it' from 'ordinary cancellable orders are resting, a retry may clear it'. Reading the code or a passing unit test is NOT the observation -- the state must be seen in a real retMsg or close_failure body.

CLASS: no Alpaca close/cancel path any longer reports a cancel as effective on the strength of the broker ACCEPTING it. Verify by reading every site that consumes CancelOutcome and confirming each one checks the post-state, not the acceptance -- the same check BL-20260816-IB-CANCEL-ACCEPTED-BUT-NEVER-COMPLETES-VENUE-CLOSED asks for on the IB side.

OPERATOR COST: the GLD page rate is re-measured over a stated post-fix window with its row count and compared against the 63 pages / 122 rows baseline of 2026-09-04 -> 2026-09-08. A page rate that has not fallen means the fix did not reach the dominant cause, and that is the finding, not a rounding error.

The 39 GLD shares are either released or the release is confirmed to need operator/venue action with the reason ESTABLISHED rather than inherited -- and if the position simply disappears, record THAT rather than clearing on it (an unattributed resolution is not evidence the mechanism works).

items.title: _bybit_position_protection grades a symbol off get_positions rows[0], so under hedge mode a zero-size sibling book reads as 'symbol flat' and the netting reconciler closes a LIVE position
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08. src/runtime/order_monitor.py:8821 does `pos = rows[0]` on a SYMBOL-SCOPED client.get_positions(category, symbol=symbol), with no zero-size skip and no hedge-book selection. Since BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS was armed on bybit_1/bybit_2/bybit_portfolio on 2026-08-30 a symbol carries TWO books (positionIdx 1 long / 2 short) and Bybit returns a row for each, including the empty one. When the empty sibling is listed first, size <= 0 and the function returns _flat {size:0.0, side:'', covered_qty:0.0, sl_leg_ids:set()} for a symbol that is NOT flat. _reconcile_netting_partial_closes then computes backed=0.0, excess=journal_qty, and attributes the ENTIRE journal row as closed. LIVE INSTANCE, verified end to end: trade 5568 (bybit_1 ETHUSDT long 26.05, ict_scalp_eth_15m, pkg-5c339e25d5144c32) opened 14:16:47.149Z and was closed `netting_attributed` at 14:24:09Z with netting_attribution_soak recording exchange_qty: 0.0 / excess_qty: 26.05 / attributed_qty: 26.05 / attribution_basis: leg_gone — while the venue held Buy 26.05 @ 2476.6 continuously (read at 14:31:27Z, 14:34:26Z, 14:37:02Z and 14:43:35Z via /api/diag/exchange_positions) and 5568's OWN tracked SL leg 7b5af72f-aa0a-4317-b796-3df599f68030 was still resting Untriggered at qty 26.05 at 14:37:02Z. The close booked a fabricated +$63.8225 (exit_price_source candle_at_close, pnl_source local_compute — ESTIMATED). The reverse reconciler then re-adopted the still-live position as trade 5569 at 14:25:47Z. HOW _flat WAS ESTABLISHED RATHER THAN GUESSED: attribution_basis 'leg_gone' is only emitted when the row's sl_order_id is ABSENT from live_leg_ids, and 5568's leg was demonstrably resting, so live_leg_ids was empty; the only branches returning an empty sl_leg_ids are _flat and full_position_stop, and full_position_stop returns covered_qty == size == 26.05 which produces NO divergence at all. NOT ESTABLISHED: which of _flat's two triggers fired — `not rows` or `rows[0].size <= 0`. No repo surface exposes the raw get_positions payload; saying which would be a guess. Both are the same defect class. ARITHMETIC CROSS-CHECK (population: newest 1000 trades rows, ids 4570-5569, 2026-08-11T10:48Z to 2026-09-08T14:25Z — 19 days before the arming and 10 after): adopted_orphan rows on a BYBIT account = 0 before 2026-08-30 and 13 on/after, while netting_attributed closes ran throughout (30 before, 19 after). So the reconciler's activity is not what changed; its closes started being wrong. That before/after is INFERRED from those two counts, and '0 before' means 0 in those 19 days, not 0 ever. THREE closes are PROVABLY wrong (an adopted_orphan of the same account/symbol/direction and EXACT size followed within 4 minutes): 5515 SOLUSDT short 604.7 -> 5516 at +209s; 5554 SOLUSDT short 545.0 -> 5555 at +223s; 5568 ETHUSDT long 26.05 -> 5569 at +233s. Manufactured ESTIMATED pnl on those three: +$115.8575. THREE IS A LOWER BOUND, not the count — it is only the subset that left a same-size adopt fingerprint; the soak's applied rows show 12 of 21 reading exchange_qty == 0.0 (population: the 1000-line tail of netting_attribution_soak.jsonl, 2026-08-29T07:50Z to 2026-09-08T14:24Z; the file is 3,875,205 bytes so this is a tail, not the whole file), and a flat read is NOT automatically wrong — a genuinely-flat venue with a stale open row is the case this reconciler exists for. I did not establish which of the other nine were correct. NOT DEMO-SCOPED: 7 of the 49 netting_attributed closes in the population are on REAL-MONEY bybit_2 (BTCUSDT x3, ETHUSDT x3, XRPUSDT x1) and one of them — trade 5461, 2026-09-04T12:34:25Z, XRPUSDT long 69.4 — is an exchange_qty: 0.0 flat read on an account where XRP is hedge-armed. THE CYCLE REPEATS: trades 5262 and 5438 are adopted_orphan rows that were THEMSELVES later closed by netting_attributed, so the loop is netting_attributed -> adopt -> netting_attributed -> adopt. Each turn mints a phantom closed trade with an estimated pnl, REWRITES the cost basis (5569 carries the venue's 2476.6 where 5568 declared 2477.54) and drops the tracked leg ids (5569 sl_order_id NULL). This is the BL-20260618-RECONCILE-DUP shape (one MGC position became 18 closed trades, -$20,127) reached through a NEW cause. THE REPO ALREADY GETS THIS RIGHT ONE FILE OVER: account_bybit_open_orders (src/units/accounts/clients.py:1888-1896 and again 1910-1912) skips size <= 0 rows on BOTH the account-wide and the SYMBOL-SCOPED call. That symbol-scoped zero-size `continue` is itself evidence that a symbol-scoped get_positions returns multiple rows, some empty. Full evidence: docs/claude/work/BYBIT-HEDGE-BOOK-FLAT-READ-2026-09-08.md.
items.resolution_criteria: _bybit_position_protection selects the book instead of taking rows[0], AND the two collapses it currently makes are separated: (a) `not rows` on a symbol-scoped call returns None (we could not look — the caller already skips on None) rather than _flat, and (b) more than one LIVE book on a symbol returns None rather than picking one, because guessing which book backs a journal row is the guess that caused this incident. Every-book-empty may still return _flat — that is a real measurement. PROVEN BY: a netting_attribution_soak row on a hedge-armed symbol carrying position_idx and a non-zero exchange_qty where the venue holds a position, plus the absence of any further netting_attributed -> same-size-adopt pair. A PASSING UNIT TEST IS NOT THE OBSERVATION — a fixture cannot reproduce which row Bybit lists first. Explicitly NOT sufficient: widening RECONCILER_READOPT_GUARD_SECONDS (the guard is working as designed and its KEY is what misses — see the sibling row), or re-stamping trade 5569 (it is already correctly `reconciled` against a correctly-named package; the row should never have existed, and re-stamping it would hide the incident).

Tier-2 on the order path, so it needs one operator OK before merge. Ship it WITH the sibling flap-guard row and in that order: this one PREVENTS the incident, the sibling CONTAINS it.

items.title: The re-adopt flap guard's exit_reason allowlist omits netting_attributed, so a strategy row false-closed by the netting reconciler falls straight through with zero flap protection
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08 by reading the predicate, not the prose about it. _recently_closed_adopted_orphan (src/runtime/order_monitor.py:2576-2587) selects "AND (setup_type='adopted_orphan' OR exit_reason IN ('exchange_flat_reconciled', 'exit_coverage_no_strategy'))". `netting_attributed` is NOT in that list, so a STRATEGY-attributed row false-closed by _reconcile_netting_partial_closes carries its original setup_type, matches neither clause, and the BL-20260618-RECONCILE-DUP flap guard cannot see it at all. THIS IS VERBATIM THE GAP THE FUNCTION'S OWN DOCSTRING RECORDS BEING CLOSED FOR THE OTHER TWO REASONS by BL-20260707-ALPACA-CLOSE-NOT-CONFIRMED-FLAT: 'a STRATEGY-ATTRIBUTED row closed by position_snapshot_reconciler ... carries the ORIGINAL strategy's setup_type, never adopted_orphan — so it fell straight through the old guard with ZERO flap protection'. netting_attributed was introduced later (2026-08) and nobody extended the list. So this is a RECURRENCE of an already-diagnosed class in the same function, not a new discovery. AND THE DOCSTRING'S STATED REASON FOR EXCLUDING OTHER CLOSE REASONS DOES NOT DESCRIBE THIS ONE. It says 'a real, broker-confirmed close ... is a genuine flatten and must never suppress a legitimate new position'. netting_attributed is BY CONSTRUCTION not broker-confirmed: its own docstring calls its evidence 'evidence, not proof' and its close is an ESTIMATE anchored to a bar (exit_price_source candle_at_close). So the exclusion rationale that legitimately keeps sl_cross and reconciler_filled out does not apply to it. OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE: trade 5568 (bybit_1 ETHUSDT long 26.05) was closed netting_attributed at 14:21:54Z and the still-live venue position was re-adopted as trade 5569 at 14:25:47Z — 233 seconds later, well inside the 1800s window — with readopt_suppressed NOT incremented. Two prior instances the same way: 5515 -> 5516 (+209s) and 5554 -> 5555 (+223s). RECONCILER_READOPT_GUARD_SECONDS (1800) IS WORKING AS DESIGNED HERE and must not be re-filed as broken: it did not suppress because its KEY does not match, not because its window is short. Widening the window would change nothing. Full evidence: docs/claude/work/BYBIT-HEDGE-BOOK-FLAT-READ-2026-09-08.md.
items.resolution_criteria: 'netting_attributed' is added to the exit_reason IN (...) list in _recently_closed_adopted_orphan, with a test asserting that a strategy-attributed row closed by that reason inside the window SUPPRESSES a re-adopt and alerts detect_only, and that a broker-confirmed close (sl_cross / reconciler_filled) still does NOT suppress. PROVEN ON THE FLEET BY: a readopt_suppressed increment observed on a real netting_attributed -> same-symbol/direction sequence, or the absence of any further netting_attributed -> same-size-adopt pair once the sibling root-cause row is also fixed. NOTE THIS ROW IS CONTAINMENT, NOT THE CURE — it stops the loop and leaves the position adopted-suppressed and alerted; the false close itself is the sibling row BL-20260908-BYBIT-POSITION-PROTECTION-GRADES-A-SYMBOL-OFF-ROWS0-SO-A-HEDGE-BOOK-READS-FLAT-AND-A-LIVE-POSITION-IS-CLOSED. Closing this row alone must not be reported as fixing the incident.

items.title: netting_attribution_soak's exchange_qty: 0.0 collapses three states — venue genuinely flat, we read the wrong hedge book, and the position list came back empty — so a reviewer cannot tell a correct attribution from a catastrophic one
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08 from the soak's own field list. A netting_attribution_soak row carries ts, mode, global_mode, apply_scope, account_id, symbol, direction, trade_id, strategy, row_qty, attributed_qty, attribution_basis, journal_qty, exchange_qty, excess_qty, anchor_status, anchor_price, anchored_at, anchor_basis. It carries NO position_idx and NO source. So exchange_qty: 0.0 cannot distinguish (1) the venue is genuinely flat — the case the reconciler EXISTS for, and a correct attribution; (2) we read the wrong hedge book — the sibling root-cause row, a live position wrongly closed; (3) get_positions returned an empty list — WE DID NOT LOOK. These are not degrees of the same thing; (1) is the mechanism working and (2) is it destroying a live position's journal row. THIS IS WHY THE DEFECT ACCRUED UNEXAMINED. Measured over the 1000-line tail of netting_attribution_soak.jsonl (2026-08-29T07:50Z to 2026-09-08T14:24Z; the file is 3,875,205 bytes so this is a tail, not the whole file): 12 of 21 APPLIED rows read exchange_qty == 0.0, on 6 distinct (account, symbol) pairs including REAL-MONEY bybit_2/XRPUSDT. At least three of the twelve are provably wrong (a same-size adopted_orphan followed within 4 minutes). For the other nine I could not determine from the soak whether the venue was flat or the read was wrong — which is precisely the finding, not a gap in my reading. _bybit_position_protection ALREADY COMPUTES position_idx, and deliberately returns None for it rather than 0 when the venue did not report it ('WE DID NOT LOOK — and must never be read as 0/one-way', its own comment). But it only returns position_idx on the partial_sl_legs branch; the _flat branch, which is the branch that matters here, does not carry it, and _netting_soak_row does not take it. So the careful non-collapse one layer down is discarded before it reaches the surface a reviewer reads. This is docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md § 'Collapsed states' applied to the INSTRUMENT rather than the field, and § 'A soak must carry its own alarm' is the reason it matters: this soak is what the NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_MODE widening decision rests on. Full evidence: docs/claude/work/BYBIT-HEDGE-BOOK-FLAT-READ-2026-09-08.md.
items.resolution_criteria: The soak row carries `source` (the _bybit_position_protection branch that produced the verdict: flat / full_position_stop / partial_sl_legs) and `position_idx` (None when the venue did not report it, NEVER 0), and _bybit_position_protection returns position_idx on the _flat branch too. PROVEN BY: a real soak row on a hedge-armed symbol whose source and position_idx are both populated, read from the live log — not by a test. Then re-grade the 12 flat reads above and record how many were correct; that count is what the NETTING_ATTRIBUTION_MODE widening decision actually needs and nobody has it.

items.title: The adopt path's naked re-arm places a Full-mode bracket over still-resting Partial legs, doubling the cover — and the over-cover trip is structurally blind to it because a Full-mode stop makes the reader return before it ever lists the legs
items.detail: MEASURED LIVE 2026-09-08T14:37:02Z via /api/diag/bybit_open_orders?account_id=bybit_1. bybit_1 ETHUSDT holds ONE position (Buy 26.05 @ 2476.6, positionIdx 1) and FOUR resting protective legs: StopLoss Full 26.05 @ 2465.01 and TakeProfit Full 26.05 @ 2496.32 (created_time 1788877548218 = 14:25:48.218Z), plus PartialStopLoss 26.05 @ 2465.02 and PartialTakeProfit 26.05 @ 2496.33 (created_time 1788877006909 = 14:16:46.909Z). Stop side = 52.10 against a 26.05 position = 200%. PROVENANCE OF EACH PAIR: the Partial legs belong to trade 5568, which is CLOSED; the Full legs were placed 0.3s after trade 5569 was adopted (protection_repair_first_at 14:25:48.303491Z, protection_repair_last_kind naked_rearm, protection_repair_last_verified 'unverified'). So the adopt path's _rearm_broker_protection_after_recovery re-armed WITHOUT asking whether protection already rested, and 5568's close did not cancel its own tracked legs. THE OVER-COVER PAGE CANNOT SEE THIS, and that is the more general half of the finding. The trip at order_monitor.py:9920-9922 requires state['source'] == 'partial_sl_legs'. The position now carries a non-empty position-level stopLoss, so _bybit_position_protection returns via the full_position_stop branch at :8853, which RETURNS BEFORE get_open_orders is called at all — its own comment says so: 'This branch returns BEFORE get_open_orders is called, so we did not read the resting legs at all'. So a Full-mode re-arm laid over Partial legs is invisible to the exact mechanism built to catch leg pile-up, by construction rather than by threshold. SEVERITY IS MEDIUM, DELIBERATELY, AND HERE IS WHY RATHER THAN A BARE LABEL: all four legs are reduce_only and all four are Sell, so they act on the correct book and CANNOT reverse the position — this is not the disjoint-OCA hazard that makes the IB instance CRITICAL. The cost is cap headroom: Bybit refuses at 20 combined TP+SL legs per symbol (110061), at which point a genuine protective tightening fails silently — BL-20260721-BYBIT2-XRP-TPSL-LEGCAP measured 23 stranded legs on real-money bybit_2 XRPUSDT. 4 of 20 used here. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether Bybit cancels the orphaned Partial legs when the position eventually closes. If it does not, they rest against a FUTURE long in the same book. I did not test it and am not asserting it. This instance was CREATED by the flap in BL-20260908-BYBIT-POSITION-PROTECTION-GRADES-A-SYMBOL-OFF-ROWS0-SO-A-HEDGE-BOOK-READS-FLAT-AND-A-LIVE-POSITION-IS-CLOSED, so fixing that root cause removes this instance — but NOT the blind spot, which is independent and stands whatever causes the mixed-mode bracket. Full evidence: docs/claude/work/BYBIT-HEDGE-BOOK-FLAT-READ-2026-09-08.md.
items.resolution_criteria: TWO PARTS, and they are different facts — say which you closed. (1) THE BLIND SPOT: over-cover is detectable when a position carries BOTH a Full-mode position-level stop AND resting Partial legs. That needs the full_position_stop branch to stop returning before it has looked, or a separate leg-count read; note it costs a get_open_orders call the branch currently avoids, so it is a real trade-off and not a free fix. Proven by an observed over-cover page on a mixed-mode bracket, never by a test. (2) THE RE-ARM: the adopt path's naked re-arm consults existing broker coverage before placing, or cancels the closing row's tracked legs. ⚠️ DO NOT RESOLVE (2) BY CANCELLING LEGS ON THE LIVE POSITION AS A ONE-OFF — BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG is what happened the last time that was attempted. The current 200% instance is expected to clear when the root cause lands and this position closes normally; if it clears that way, that is NOT evidence either half is fixed.

items.title: The reverse reconciler's orphan re-attach can name a strategy that did not open the position — it wrote +$612.71 of trend_donchian_eth's PnL onto pairs_sol_eth_b, and the pairs executor then flattened the position 14s later
items.tier: 2 (src/runtime/order_monitor.py adopt path — its output is consumed by pairs_executor's live order path)
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08, MI-204. _reconcile_orphan_exchange_positions' re-attach writes `recovered_strategy` into trades.strategy_name. IT CAN NAME THE WRONG STRATEGY, AND WHEN IT DOES THE WRONGLY-NAMED STRATEGY THEN ACTS ON THE ROW. THE WORKED EXAMPLE IS AIRTIGHT ON ARITHMETIC. Trade 5453: adopted bybit_1 ETHUSDT LONG 17.67 at 2026-09-04T09:02:08.797750Z, attributed to `pairs_sol_eth_b` via pkg-4c085f53442c4345. But 17.67 is an EXACT match for trade 5420, `trend_donchian_eth` long 17.67, closed reconciler_filled 3264s earlier. Population for the scale check: all 80 `pairs_sol_eth_b` ETHUSDT legs in trades ids 4570-5569 — the LARGEST is 2.10 and the typical leg is ~0.37, so 17.67 is 8.4x that strategy's entire observed range; `trend_donchian_eth`'s own ETHUSDT sizes are 17.08-37.76, and 17.67 sits inside them. The row carries strategy_name 'pairs_sol_eth_b' and pnl +612.705681 (exit_price_source candle_at_close — ESTIMATED). FOURTEEN SECONDS AFTER THE ADOPT it closed with exit_reason `pairs_half_open_cleanup` — the PAIRS EXECUTOR acted on it, because the journal now told it this was its leg — and its exit price 2525.85 is byte-identical to pairs leg 5447's. So the pairs sleeve FLATTENED A trend_donchian_eth POSITION and booked another strategy's PnL. For scale, that sleeve's own legs in the same window book -10.455 and -1.3144: a single +612.71 row is ~60x its typical magnitude and dominates any per-strategy aggregate computed for it. RATE, with the population stated: scored each adopt's claimed strategy against THAT strategy's own size distribution on the same symbol, built from non-adopted bybit_1 rows in ids 4570-5569. Of 13 adopted_orphan rows, 6 claimed NO strategy (the honest bare-orphan state) and 2 carried a TRUNCATED recovered_strategy in notes so no reference existed, leaving 5 judgeable: 3 INSIDE (5288 pairs_sol_eth_a 11.90 vs 2-57.5; 5555 ict_scalp_sol_15m 545.0 vs 9.1-2511.7; 5569 ict_scalp_eth_15m 26.05 vs 5.31-114.47) and 2 OUTSIDE — 5448 (SOLUSDT 1236.30 claimed pairs_sol_eth_a, 21.5x its max of 57.5) and 5453 (above, 8.4x). SO 2 OF 5 JUDGEABLE RE-ATTRIBUTIONS NAMED A STRATEGY WHOSE OWN SIZE DISTRIBUTION EXCLUDES THE POSITION, AND BOTH WRONG ONES NAMED A PAIRS STRATEGY. n=5 judgeable is small and the +/-(0.5x, 2x) band is a CHOSEN threshold, not a derived one — but 8.4x and 21.5x are outside any defensible band, so the verdict is robust to the band choice. THREE HARMS, DIFFERENT FACTS: (1) a false strategy attribution written into the journal, contaminating every per-strategy aggregate/grade/expectancy for the named sleeve; (2) cross-strategy PnL contamination; (3) a LIVE ORDER-PATH consequence — pairs_executor closed a position it did not open, on a row a reconciler handed it. (3) is what makes this critical rather than a measurement row. NOT ESTABLISHED AND NOT ASSERTED: the same 17.67 quantity produced TWO closed rows at two different exit prices — 5420 at +315.41 and 5453 at +612.71, +928.12 combined. That is either double-counting (5420's reconciler_filled close was ALSO false) or a genuine off-journal re-entry. reconciler_filled is a broker-confirmed close by this repo's own definition and 5420's close does NOT appear in the netting soak, so I have no evidence it was false. Resolving it needs venue fill history for 2026-09-04T08:07Z, which no repo surface exposes. SIBLINGS, NOT DUPLICATES: BL-20260826-BTC-SCALP-AND-DONCHIAN-SHARE-ONE-NETTED-BTCUSDT-POSITION is attribution being UNCLEAR because two strategies share a netted position; this row is the reconciler ACTIVELY WRITING a wrong one. BL-20260825-EXIT-PROVENANCE-IS-STRUCTURED-BY-EXIT-PATH-SIX-PATHS-AT-ZERO names the pairs sleeve at zero coverage, which is a provenance gap, not a mis-attribution. CONTEXT: the check-in that prompted this asked whether the reverse reconciler EXCLUDES pairs rows. It does NOT — its `known` set is every open non-backtest row on the account with no setup_type or strategy filter, and `_is_pairs_sleeve_row`'s only two call sites are _reconcile_netting_partial_closes:9276 and _check_broker_naked_bybit_positions:9785 (positive control: the helper exists at :9164). So a pairs leg whose row is OPEN cannot be adopted — verified live, row 5571 is open and unadopted. The defect is not which rows are adopted, it is which strategy an adopt is ATTRIBUTED to. Full evidence: docs/claude/work/BYBIT-HEDGE-BOOK-FLAT-READ-2026-09-08.md § ADDENDUM.
items.resolution_criteria: The adopt path refuses to write a strategy_name it cannot support. Concretely: a quantity check against the claimed strategy's own recent size history on that symbol — the cheapest available discriminator, and one that would have refused BOTH wrong attributions here — and on failure the row is left a BARE orphan (recovered_strategy empty, which 6 of 13 correctly already are) rather than attributed to a guess. A bare orphan is the honest state; a wrong attribution is worse than none because it reads as known and is acted on. PROVEN BY: an observed adopt whose re-attach DECLINED on a quantity mismatch and left the row bare, read from the live journal — not by a unit test, which cannot reproduce the venue state that produces a candidate package. ALSO REQUIRED: the two existing OUTSIDE rows (5448, 5453) are dispositioned — either corrected with the reason recorded, or explicitly left with a note that their strategy_name is not trustworthy, so a later aggregate does not silently consume them. NOT SUFFICIENT: fixing the rows[0] root cause (BL-20260908-BYBIT-POSITION-PROTECTION-GRADES-A-SYMBOL-OFF-ROWS0-SO-A-HEDGE-BOOK-READS-FLAT-AND-A-LIVE-POSITION-IS-CLOSED). That reduces how OFTEN adopts happen and does not make the attribution correct when one does; the two defects are independent and 5453's parent chain does not involve a netting false close at all.

Patch shape is in the evidence doc's ADDENDUM. Do NOT bundle it with the rows[0] fix — different function, different failure, and bundling would make one operator decision cover two order-path changes.

items.title: The netting reconciler compares NON-PAIRS journal qty against the WHOLE netted venue position, so every pass with a pairs leg open leaves a phantom residual on a non-pairs row exactly equal to the pairs legs' size
items.tier: 2 (src/runtime/order_monitor.py — decides how much of a live position a journal row still claims)
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08 from the soak row itself, not inferred. _reconcile_netting_partial_closes EXCLUDES pairs-sleeve rows from journal_qty via _is_pairs_sleeve_row (correctly — that executor owns its own state and closing its rows behind its back would desync it), but `backed` is state['size'], the WHOLE netted venue position, which INCLUDES the pairs legs' quantity. So the pass compares NON-PAIRS journal against ALL-VENUE. The two sides of the subtraction cover different populations. LIVE INSTANCE, soak row 2026-09-08T15:26:55.295832Z: trade_id 5569 (bybit_1 ETHUSDT long, the only non-pairs open row on that book) journal_qty 26.05, exchange_qty 0.47, excess_qty 25.58, attributed_qty 25.58, basis fifo -> residual left on the row = 26.05-25.58 = 0.47. AND THE 0.47 IT LEFT IS THE PAIRS LEG'S QUANTITY: trade 5571 (pairs_sol_eth_b, ETHUSDT long 0.47, opened ~15:16Z) is the row that actually owns it. Post-pass state: journal open ETH long on bybit_1 = 5569 (0.47) + 5571 (0.47) = 0.94 against a venue position of 0.47, verified on /api/diag/bybit_open_orders at 15:33Z (ETHUSDT Buy 0.47 position_idx 1). The journal over-claims by exactly the excluded row's size. SYSTEMATIC, NOT A ROUNDING ARTIFACT: the residual always equals the excluded pairs legs' total, so the pass UNDER-attributes by that amount whenever a pairs leg is open on the same book. It SCALES WITH PAIRS LEG SIZE — pairs_sol_eth_a legs reach 57.5 on SOLUSDT (population: all 80 of its SOLUSDT legs in trades ids 4570-5569), so the phantom residual can be 57.5 SOL rather than 0.47 ETH. ⚠️ I CALLED THIS BENIGN 20 MINUTES BEFORE IT FIRED, and the correction is the reason this row exists: on the coordination board at 15:22Z I wrote that two journal rows sharing one hedge book was 'benign in this direction'. It was not. A reader inheriting that sentence would not look. ⚠️ THE EXCLUSION IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE REMOVED — the fix is to make the two sides agree, not to start closing pairs rows. ⚠️ THIS IS INDEPENDENT OF THE rows[0] DEFECT (BL-20260908-BYBIT-POSITION-PROTECTION-GRADES-A-SYMBOL-OFF-ROWS0-SO-A-HEDGE-BOOK-READS-FLAT-AND-A-LIVE-POSITION-IS-CLOSED). That one makes `backed` read 0 when it should read the position; this one makes `backed` too LARGE by the excluded rows' size. They can occur on the same book and push in opposite directions, so fixing either alone leaves the comparison wrong. Full evidence: docs/claude/work/BYBIT-HEDGE-BOOK-FLAT-READ-2026-09-08.md § ADDENDUM 2.
items.resolution_criteria: The two sides of the divergence comparison cover the same population. Two shapes both acceptable: (a) subtract the excluded (pairs) rows' open quantity from `backed` before computing `excess`, so the comparison is non-pairs-journal vs non-pairs-venue; or (b) REFUSE to grade a (account, symbol, direction) book that carries an excluded open row at all, recording the refusal as its own state rather than silently under-attributing — the `we did not look` discipline this repo already applies elsewhere. (a) is more useful and (b) is safer; either is Tier-2. PROVEN BY: a soak row on a book carrying BOTH a pairs and a non-pairs open row where the residual left on the non-pairs row is NOT equal to the pairs legs' size — i.e. the sum of open journal rows on that book reconciles to the venue position. Read it from the live journal plus /api/diag/bybit_open_orders, not from a test: a fixture can assert the arithmetic but cannot show the two populations agreeing on a real netted book. ALSO REQUIRED: trade 5569's standing 0.47 residual is dispositioned — it is currently a phantom that belongs to 5571. ⚠️ NOT by hand-editing the open row's position_size; that is the remediation shape BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG forbids. It should resolve on its own once the comparison is fixed and the book next diverges.
items.next_step: Route with the measurement. Tier-2 — it changes how much of a live position a journal row is deemed to claim. Ship it AFTER the rows[0] fix, since that one is the larger error term, but do NOT bundle them: they are different functions and opposite-signed, and one operator OK should not cover both.

items.title: claude-pr-automerge opens a PR under GITHUB_TOKEN so no CI fires, AND arms auto-merge before CI exists — four sessions hit it on 2026-09-08 and one lost a pushed commit to the resulting race
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08 across four sessions in one day, which is what makes this a mechanism problem rather than four mistakes. TWO defects on one route, and they compound. (1) NO CI FIRES. claude-pr-automerge.yml opens the PR as github-actions[bot] under GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub fires no workflows for GITHUB_TOKEN pushes, so the PR is BORN with no `pull_request` event and carries exactly ONE check run — its own `open-and-automerge`, which is GREEN. It therefore reads as a ready PR whose CI has not started, and because the one run is green it is easy to glance at and call ready. Instances: MI-193 #11356, MI-199 #11392 and #11395, MI-204 #11409 and #11410 and #11411. CLAUDE.md documents this trap for pr-opener.yml and board-post.yml and, as of 2026-09-08, for claude-pr-automerge too — but documenting it has not stopped it recurring, and the remedy is still a manual step every author must remember. (2) THE ARMING RACE DROPS COMMITS, AND THIS IS THE HALF THAT COSTS WORK. Auto-merge is enabled BEFORE any required check exists, so the first commit an author pushes to arm CI becomes the head CI grades — and any commit pushed AFTER that may or may not make the squash, depending on whether CI finishes first. MEASURED ON #11409: auto-merge took head 5590ef5b at 15:05:55Z while commit 527a9b4c was already pushed on the branch; that commit did NOT reach main. Verified rather than assumed — `git show origin/main:CLAUDE.md | grep -c` returned 0 while all nine other files landed. It had to be re-landed on a fresh branch as #11410 (a merged PR is finished and must not be reused). MI-199 recorded the same hazard on #11392 earlier the same day: 'once auto-merge is armed, treat the branch as closed to new content'. THE SEQUENCE THAT WORKS, established empirically over three PRs in this session and offered as the interim workaround: push the arming commit while NO required check is running (it then becomes the head CI grades), verify all four checks are queued, then add NOTHING. #11409 violated the last step and lost a commit; #11410 and #11411 followed it and both landed complete. That is a discipline, not a fix — it depends on the author knowing it, which is precisely what failed four times today. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the workflow can arm auto-merge only after checks attach, or whether opening the PR under a token that triggers workflows is available on this repo's permission set. Both are plausible fixes and I did not verify either.
items.resolution_criteria: A PR opened through claude-pr-automerge carries the four required check runs WITHOUT the author pushing an extra commit, OR auto-merge is not armed until at least one required check has attached (so the arming race cannot silently drop a commit). Either removes the manual step; both together would be better. PROVEN BY: a claude-pr-automerge-opened PR observed with pytest-run / pytest-collect / guards / repo-inventory attached on its FIRST head, read from get_check_runs. ⚠️ NOT sufficient: another line in CLAUDE.md. It is already documented for three workflows and recurred four times in one day anyway — a documented manual step whose omission silently drops committed work is the shape this row is about.
items.next_step: Tier-1 (a workflow file and its own docs; no runtime, order path or config). Route to a session that can verify what token options this repo's permission set actually allows before changing the open path — the arming-order half is the cheaper and more valuable of the two, since it is what loses work.

items.title: R13 forces AUTOMATION PRs to write merge_slot too, and work-digest fires on push:main — so every merge spawns further board-touching merges and a PR needing a full CI cycle cannot converge (17 collisions measured on one PR)
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08 on PR #11370 (MI-195), which took SEVENTEEN merge-conflict cycles over ~6h and had not landed when this was filed. POPULATION: the last 20 commits on origin/main, checked individually with `git show --stat`. ALL TWENTY touch docs/claude/session-board.json. THE PART THAT WAS NOT ANTICIPATED: that set includes AUTOMATION PRs. #11403 'chore(ops): queue the daily work digest (auto)' and #11380 'chore(ops): trainer capture-watch receipt (auto)' both wrote merge_slot; the claim displaced on collision 17 literally read branch: automation/work-digest-34235343785-1, pr: 11403. CAUSE: check_pr_landing.py R6 FAILS landing:self unless the branch is ARMED, and R13 then REQUIRES an armed branch to hold merge_slot added-or-modified in its own diff. Automation PRs self-land, so they arm, so they write the slot. There is NO branch configuration that avoids the file (verified by reading the guard, not assumed): self-land => armed => writes merge_slot. THE FEEDBACK LOOP IS WHY IT NEVER SETTLES: work-digest.yml fires on push:main (#10845/MI-80 moved it off cron deliberately), so every merge opens a work-digest PR which itself auto-merges and touches the board -- alongside reconcile-open-prs and session-reaper, also per-merge. Main therefore cannot stay quiet for the ~15min a CI cycle needs, so a branch whose ONLY conflict is merge_slot can lose indefinitely. 17 consecutive losses is not consistent with a coin-flip race; the arrival rate of board-touching commits simply exceeds the CI window. SIX of the 17 displaced claims named a PR that was ALREADY MERGED and was origin/main's own HEAD at that moment (#11401, #11405, #11407, #11409, #11410, #11414) -- so those collisions were with branches that had finished, contending with nobody. R13's own failure text concedes the claim serializes nothing: 'a committed claim reaches no other session until this branch merges' (BL-20260810-MERGE-SLOT-MIRROR-UNWRITABLE-PRE-MERGE). So the field is mandatory, collides by construction, is written by bots that read no board, and delivers no serialization -- the collision is its whole observable effect. A manager-granted queue slot would NOT have fixed this, which is worth stating because that is what was requested three times: the automation PRs are not reading the coordination board.
items.resolution_criteria: A self-landing PR can satisfy R13 without writing a field that every other self-landing branch also writes in the same commit range. Candidate shapes, none chosen here: (a) per-branch claim FILES under docs/claude/merge-slots/<branch>.json so two claims never touch the same bytes; (b) exempt automation/** from R13, since a bot cannot read or honour a slot anyway; (c) drop R13 and rely on the board comment, which is the only part of the claim any session actually sees. VERIFIED by opening two armed branches concurrently and observing that neither dirties the other, with a POSITIVE CONTROL that a genuine content conflict still conflicts. NOT sufficient: widening any timeout, or telling sessions to merge faster -- the arrival rate is machine-driven. NOT sufficient: removing work-digest's push trigger, which would re-open OI-20260902-DIGEST-MOVED-OFF-A-CRON-THAT-DOES-NOT-FIRE (cron does not fire reliably here); the loop is a symptom, the shared mutable field is the defect.
