items.tier: 1 to FILE and to MEASURE (read-only diag). The FIX is Tier-2: it changes src/runtime/close_wedge_standing.py, which gates whether a live close is re-attempted and whether the operator is paged, on a path shared with real-money Alpaca.
items.title: close_wedge_standing.observe() refreshes `last_seen` ONLY on a `broker_cancel_wedged` reading, so when the classifier flips to any other state while the position stays wedged the entry ages untouched and sweep_vanished retires it as `vanished_unattributed` -- a paged 'the position disappeared and nothing explains it' for a position that never moved
items.detail:
MEASURED on the live alpaca_paper GLD wedge, 2026-09-08, and it carries a DATED PREDICTION rather than a hypothetical.

=== THE OBSERVATION ===
/api/diag/log_file?name=close_wedge_standing read at 16:28:08Z:
  last_sweep_at : 2026-09-08T16:27:10   <- the sweep IS running, every pass
  last_seen     : 2026-09-08T14:05:20   <- 2h22m stale and not advancing
  share_hold    : broker_cancel_wedged
  evidence      : 2e843e04-...:pending_cancel
  first_seen    : 2026-09-03T13:35:04 ; pages_suppressed: 57
The position is NOT gone. A direct venue read at 16:29:06Z (/api/diag/alpaca_open_orders) shows BOTH orders still resting -- parent 2e843e04 `new`, child 891ddff0 `held` -- and the trader is still failing to close it roughly every 30s.

=== THE MECHANISM, read in the code rather than inferred ===
`observe()` opens with `if obs.share_hold != UNCLEARABLE_HOLD_STATE: return Decision(NOT_A_WEDGE, should_page=True, ..., entry=None)` -- it returns BEFORE `_load(path)`, so a non-wedge reading does not touch the ledger at all. `last_seen` is written only on the wedged branch. Around 14:05Z the venue moved 2e843e04 out of `pending_cancel` and the classifier began reading `orders_still_resting`; from that moment nothing refreshes the entry.

`sweep_vanished` then retires any entry whose `last_seen` is older than `vanish_after_hours()` (_DEFAULT_VANISH_AFTER_HOURS = 72.0), stamping `resolution: vanished_unattributed` and PAGING with 'the wedge stopped being observed and no confirmed close was recorded'.

=== THE PREDICTION ===
Unless the classifier returns to `broker_cancel_wedged` first, the entry is retired as `vanished_unattributed` at 2026-09-08T14:05:20Z + 72h = **2026-09-11T14:05:20Z**, for a position that never moved. That is falsifiable: check the ledger and the venue on 09-11.

=== WHY IT IS NOT ALREADY GUARDED, WHICH IS THE INTERESTING PART ===
The module guards this collapse CAREFULLY in one direction and not the other. `sweep_vanished` carries a long comment refusing to retire anything when ITS OWN last run is older than the window, because 'a gap in OUR observation is not a disappearance' -- exactly the right instinct. But it only models the sweep not RUNNING. It has no notion of the sweep running fine while the CLASSIFIER says something else, which is the case here: we were looking the whole time, and the thing we look for changed shape. So `last_seen` conflates 'this wedge was last observed' with 'this wedge was last observed AS A WEDGE', and only the second is true.

=== IT INTERACTS WITH #11406 AND THE INTERACTION IS THE DANGEROUS BIT ===
#11406 (merged a5ba0073) suppresses the futile close retry and re-probes hourly, and its load-bearing property -- asserted structurally by test_suppression_can_never_outlive_the_vanish_sweep -- is that the re-probe keeps `last_seen` alive so the suppression can never manufacture a vanish. THAT GUARANTEE HOLDS ONLY WHILE THE CLASSIFICATION STAYS `broker_cancel_wedged`. The re-probe calls the same observe(), so on any other reading it refreshes nothing, and the test cannot catch this because it compares two CONSTANTS and never exercises a classification change. The PR is not wrong and this is not a regression it introduced -- the defect predates it -- but the safety argument in its description is narrower than it reads.

=== WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED ===
Whether a `vanished_unattributed` page has EVER fired in production. It has not been seen in the operator-alert ring over 2026-09-01 -> 2026-09-08 (checked: no evidence_changed, newly_wedged, cleared_confirmed or vanished_unattributed transition text appears in 278 close_failure rows), so this is a predicted first occurrence, not an observed recurrence.

SCOPE: alpaca_paper is PAPER, no money at risk. The module is venue-agnostic and the page it would emit is an operator-facing false statement about a live position, so the cost is trust in the one channel reserved for unprotected/unclosable positions -- the desensitised-alarm class this repo keeps paying for.

=== CORRECTION 2026-09-08T16:45Z — THE MECHANISM ABOVE IS RIGHT AND INCOMPLETE, AND THE MISSING HALF IS THE BIGGER ONE. I filed the early-return as the cause; it is only one of two gates, and I found the second by measuring rather than by reading further. MEASURED over the post-restart journal window 16:37:07 -> 16:42:15Z (272s, 10 GLD close give-ups at ~30s cadence): ONE of the ten read `broker_cancel_wedged` (16:39:07) and NINE read `orders_still_resting` -- so the classifier is NOT stuck off the wedged reading, it FLAPS at roughly 10%. And yet `last_seen` did not move: still 14:05:20 at last_sweep_at 16:42:21. A wedged reading occurred and the ledger did not record it, which the early-return alone does not explain.
THE REASON: `observe()` is not called per observation. Its only path is order_monitor -> `enqueue_close_failure` -> `route_close_failure` -> `observe`, and that call sits behind `if _should_alert_close_failure(_close_key, _streak)` — an EXPONENTIAL BACKOFF throttle whose own docstring reads 'First page once the streak reaches MONITOR_CLOSE_FAIL_ALERT_AFTER; after that, page only once the interval since the last page has elapsed, DOUBLING that interval each time up to the max.'
SO `last_seen` DOES NOT MEAN 'WHEN THIS WEDGE WAS LAST OBSERVED'. It means 'when a close-failure ALERT last fired AND the classification at that instant read broker_cancel_wedged' — the conjunction of a widening throttle and a flapping classifier. Both must coincide, and each independently gets rarer over time (the throttle by design, the classifier because the venue left `pending_cancel`). That is why 2h37m elapsed across a wedged reading without a refresh.
THIS MAKES THE ROW WORSE, NOT BETTER, IN TWO WAYS. (1) The vanish clock is driven by an ALERTING cadence that is designed to slow down, so the longer a wedge stands the less often its own ledger entry is refreshed — the failure gets more likely the longer the condition persists, which is the opposite of what a staleness detector should do. (2) It is not specific to a classifier flip: even a permanently and correctly `broker_cancel_wedged` position refreshes `last_seen` only at the backoff cadence, so if that interval ever exceeds vanish_after_hours() the retirement fires on a wedge that was never misclassified at all.
⚠️ THE DATED PREDICTION IS THEREFORE LESS CERTAIN THAN THIS ROW FIRST STATED, and I am recording that rather than leaving the sharper claim standing. 2026-09-11T14:05:20Z is when it fires IF no throttle-admitted alert coincides with a wedged reading before then. Given the flap rate is non-zero, that coincidence may well happen first. The DEFECT is not conditional; this INSTANCE firing on that date is.
resolution_criteria: `last_seen` can distinguish 'we last saw this wedge' from 'we last saw it AS A WEDGE'. Concretely: an observation carrying a NON-wedge share_hold for a key already standing in the ledger must record that it was observed (so the vanish clock does not run) while NOT asserting the wedge determination -- a fourth state, not a refresh of the existing one.

sweep_vanished cannot retire an entry whose position is still being observed by the close path. Verify by constructing the case in a test: a standing wedge, a classifier flipped to `orders_still_resting`, the sweep run past the window -- and assert NO `vanished_unattributed` is emitted.

test_suppression_can_never_outlive_the_vanish_sweep is extended past comparing two constants to exercise an actual classification change, since the constant comparison passes today while the guarantee it names does not hold.

THE DATED PREDICTION IS CHECKED: on or after 2026-09-11T14:05:20Z, read /api/diag/log_file?name=close_wedge_standing and /api/diag/alpaca_open_orders together and record what happened -- retired as vanished_unattributed while both orders still rest (prediction confirmed), refreshed because the classifier returned to broker_cancel_wedged (prediction not reached; the defect stands but this instance did not fire), or the position genuinely closed (record the attribution). Do NOT close this row on the third case without establishing the cause.

items.title: constraint-readout.yml has failed every scheduled run it has ever had -- the runner has no PyYAML, so the WIP-ceiling import returns None and the self-test gate aborts
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 over the COMPLETE run history of .github/workflows/constraint-readout.yml: 6 runs exist, ALL SIX carry event=schedule (there has never been a workflow_dispatch run), and ALL SIX concluded `failure` -- runs #1..#6, 2026-09-03T11:05:18Z through 2026-09-08T11:07:32Z, each completing in ~14 seconds. So the A1 constraint readout has NEVER been regenerated by its own cadence since the workflow landed; docs/claude/READOUT.md and docs/claude/CONSTRAINT.json are current only when a session regenerates them by hand.

THIS IS NOT A DELIBERATE EXIT-1 PAGE. CLAUDE.md warns explicitly that pr-queue-watch.yml exits 1 ON PURPOSE to page, so `conclusion: failure` there means the watcher WORKING. That is not this. The job log for run 34219035743 reads, verbatim:
  PASS - an unreadable store verdicts `unreadable`, not `no_objects`
  FAIL - the WIP ceiling is imported from the enforcing guard (got None, want 8)
  1 FAILURE(S)
  ##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.

ROOT CAUSE, established rather than inferred. The workflow runs actions/setup-python@v5 and installs NOTHING, so PyYAML is absent on the runner. scripts/ops/constraint_readout.py guards its own import (`except ImportError: yaml = None`) and survives, but scripts/ci/check_wip_ceiling.py imports yaml at MODULE scope, so the `from check_wip_ceiling import CEILING as WIP_CEILING` at constraint_readout.py:107 raises, the broad `except Exception` sets WIP_CEILING = None, and the self-test's ceiling check fails. REPRODUCED LOCALLY by installing a meta_path finder that makes `import yaml` raise: the identical single FAIL line and `1 FAILURE(S)`. POSITIVE CONTROL: the same command with yaml present prints ALL PASS.

THE GATE IS NOT THE DEFECT AND MUST NOT BE LOOSENED. Without yaml the work store is unreadable, so a run that skipped the self-test would have committed a readout diagnosing nothing -- and this workflow also re-renders the CLAUDE.md session brief, the one surface that reaches a session before it acts. The self-test refusing is the design working.

SECOND, SEPARATE FACT -- LATENESS, WHICH THE FIX DOES NOT TOUCH. Against a declared `5 6 * * *` the six runs started 10:28Z, 10:47Z, 11:05Z, 11:07Z, 11:07Z and 12:18Z: 4.4 to 6.2 hours late, every time. Fixing the dependency addresses the FAILURE, not the CADENCE.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND FRESHNESS: MI-196 ported the due-list's five source classes into the readout as section 5 (#11369, #11378) under the operator decision `consolidate_into_the_readout`, whose second half is retiring docs/claude/DUE.md. That retirement is now HELD on this row. Its carrier due-list.yml has 6 successes in 8 scheduled runs (1 cancelled, 1 failed, 2026-09-01..2026-09-08); constraint-readout.yml has 0 in 6. Retiring DUE.md today would move the only session-facing due list from a carrier that mostly fires onto one that has never once succeeded.

NOT ESTABLISHED, stated as plainly as what is: I have not observed a SCHEDULED run succeed after the fix -- installing a dependency is a deploy, not a run, and this repo's own record (probes.yml ~4h50m late and once rather than daily; session-reaper.yml red five times before its first success) is why a workflow file that parses is not a cadence that fires. items.title: pr-landing-guard R13 makes docs/claude/session-board.json::merge_slot a guaranteed conflict point between any two concurrent self-landing PRs — and R8 passes vacuously on the empty queue that lets it happen
items.detail:
R13 (scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py) requires any ARMED, self-landing branch to hold `merge_slot` in docs/claude/session-board.json ADDED-OR-MODIFIED IN ITS OWN DIFF. `merge_slot` is a single ~5-line object, so EVERY concurrently-open `landing: "self"` PR must rewrite the SAME LINES. Any two of them therefore conflict there BY CONSTRUCTION, and each merge dirties all the others. check_pr_landing.py's own docstring says R13 does NOT serialize anything (each branch carries its own copy, reaching nobody until merge) — so the mechanism manufactures merge conflicts while providing no mutual exclusion.

MEASURED 2026-09-08. PR #11384 (MI-196, Tier-1) was re-resolved through TEN rounds before landing at 17:25:37Z. NATURAL EXPERIMENT with a control: over FOUR consecutive `main` movements (d9c31c05, 4fc54f61, 1b199c72, aa1addad) #11384 was dirtied every time while PR #11418 was dirtied NONE of the four, verified each time with `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only` returning a bare tree oid and zero conflicted paths. The variable is the merge_slot write: #11418 declared `landing: "hold"`, so R13 wanted no claim and it never touched the file. n=4 movements, and all four were themselves self-landing/automation PRs — i.e. exactly the population the mechanism predicts — so this is CONSISTENT WITH the mechanism rather than independent confirmation of it.

THE AUTOMATION IS A PARTICIPANT, NOT A BYSTANDER, which is what makes it unavoidable rather than a scheduling nuisance. From the manager's own commit message on #11403, verbatim: 'The work-digest workflow arms its own landing route ... but cannot claim the merge slot, so pr-landing-guard R13 fails EVERY automation PR that arms auto-merge.' So a session/human claim must be hand-written onto automation branches, and the automation then rewrites merge_slot on its own cadence, dirtying every open self-landing PR each time it lands. The manager independently recorded the same effect in aa1addad's body: 'My own merge_slot write re-dirtied #11384. Recorded as a cost of the slot.'

AND THE GUARD THAT SHOULD CATCH THE CAUSE PASSES VACUOUSLY. check_manager_scope.py R8 enforces 'at most one entry `rebasing`' in docs/claude/work/MERGE-QUEUE.json. That file read `"entries": []` with updated_at 2026-09-08T07:06:00Z. An EMPTY queue satisfies R8 perfectly, so the guard passes cleanly through precisely the state that produces the harm: measured over the 39 merges to main since that timestamp, 33 (84.6%) touched a shared register (OPEN-ITEMS.json / health-review-backlog.json / session-board.json). MERGE-QUEUE.json's own _doc records the incident that created it as 26 merges / 19 (73%) / '#10918 went dirty three times' — so today is WORSE on the count, the rate, and the per-PR round count, with the queue empty throughout. R8 constrains RELATIONSHIPS AMONG ENTRIES THAT EXIST, never WHETHER THE QUEUE IS USED — the same shape CLAUDE.md already concedes for the supervision check ('measures the RECORD of supervision, never supervision itself').

NOT ESTABLISHED, stated rather than papered over: I have NOT established that R13's claim requirement is net-negative overall — it may buy something I have not measured (an audit trail of who intended to merge what), and MERGE-QUEUE.json's _doc argues the queue itself genuinely worked the day it was run. What is established is that the claim is a guaranteed textual conflict point among concurrent self-landing branches, and that nothing currently detects an unused queue. The FIX DIRECTION is therefore not obvious and is deliberately not asserted here: candidates include (a) letting R13 accept a claim file under a per-branch path (.github/pr-landing/** already works this way and does NOT conflict), (b) a third `landing` state for 'queued behind #N', or (c) a detector for a stale/empty MERGE-QUEUE.json while register-touching PRs are open. Whichever is chosen touches landing machinery and wants a deliberate decision, not a drive-by patch from a sub-session.
items.resolution_criteria: TWO PARTS, different facts — say which was resolved. (1) MECHANISM: two concurrently-open self-landing PRs are OBSERVED both passing pr-landing-guard WITHOUT either having to rewrite a line the other also rewrites — proven by `git merge-tree --write-tree --name-only` between the two heads returning ZERO conflicted paths while both PRs' `pr-landing` checks are green. [!] NOT sufficient: one of them declaring `hold` to opt out, which is the workaround this row was found through and leaves the defect intact for every self-landing pair. (2) DETECTION: something FAILS or PAGES on a MERGE-QUEUE.json that is empty or stale while register-touching PRs are open — a guard, a workflow, or a manager check that can tell 'nothing to queue' from 'nobody is queueing'. [!] A green R8 run resolves NOTHING here: R8 passes on an empty queue by construction, which is the finding. [!] And a CLAUDE.md paragraph resolves nothing — the merge-queue duty is already canonised as a manager base function and the measurement above is what happened anyway.
items.next_step: Tier-1 by path (scripts/ci/**, docs/claude/**) but it changes the LANDING ROUTE every PR in the repo goes through, so route it to a session that can hold the whole picture — not a drive-by. Read check_pr_landing.py's R13 docstring and MERGE-QUEUE.json's _doc together before proposing anything; both already reason about this and neither anticipated the conflict-by-construction consequence.

items.title: check_pr_landing.py's `landing: "hold"` collapses 'a human must decide' with 'this must wait its turn' — so a certified Tier-1 PR queued behind another has to rewrite its own declaration to land honestly
items.detail:
`landing: "hold"` is documented as 'a human merges', but HOLD_REASONS mixes two categorically different conditions under that one value:
  A DECISION IS OWED - tier_2_3_needs_approval, operator_asked_to_hold, awaiting_evidence, changes_landing_machinery. A human must CHOOSE something.
  A TURN IS OWED - depends_on_unmerged_pr. Nobody needs to decide anything; the change is already certified Tier-1 and is merely SEQUENCED behind a named PR.

For the second, 'a human merges' is the wrong instruction, and the consequence is concrete rather than cosmetic: PR #11418 was Tier-1 and self-landable by content, declared `hold` / `depends_on_unmerged_pr: #11384` purely to avoid dirtying that PR, and then had to REWRITE ITS OWN DECLARATION to `landing: "self"` once #11384 landed — because merging it while the committed record said 'a human merges' would leave the record contradicting what happened, which is the record-vs-reality divergence this repo keeps paying for. So the honest path costs an extra commit and an extra CI cycle, and the dishonest path is cheaper. That is the wrong way round for a guard.

IT IS ALSO THE ONE HOLD REASON A GUARD COULD VERIFY AND DOESN'T. R9 checks only that hold_text NAMES a PR (`#\d+`) — it never checks whether that PR is still open, so a `depends_on_unmerged_pr` hold naming a PR that merged days ago passes forever and reads as a live blocker. Every other hold reason is a human judgement CI genuinely cannot grade; this one is a single API field.

A third state — e.g. `queued`, meaning 'Tier-1 certified, self-lands once #N is merged' — would express the condition directly, remove the self-rewrite, and be MACHINE-CHECKABLE in both directions (refuse if #N is already merged and the PR has not landed; refuse if #N was never open). This is the 'can this field say what is actually true' shape of docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md § 'Collapsed states', applied to the landing declaration itself.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether a third state is worth the added surface, or whether the cheaper fix is simply to let R9 verify #N's state and document that `hold` covers both senses. I am not asserting which; the collapse is the finding. NOTE the interaction with the R13 row filed alongside this one — a `queued` state that still ARMED auto-merge would inherit R13's merge_slot requirement and reintroduce the conflict-by-construction problem, so the two must be designed together rather than separately.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) a landing declaration can express 'certified, waiting its turn behind #N' WITHOUT claiming a human must decide and WITHOUT the PR having to rewrite its own declaration to land — demonstrated by a real PR that lands under that declaration unchanged; OR (b) an explicit recorded decision that `hold` covers both senses deliberately, AND R9 is extended to verify the named PR's state (refusing a `depends_on_unmerged_pr` hold whose PR is already merged, or was never open). [!] A doc line alone resolves NEITHER: the ambiguity is in the closed vocabulary the guard enforces, not in prose about it. [!] And a passing self-test resolves nothing — check_pr_landing.py's own positive controls already pass on `declared_hold` today, which is why the collapse was invisible until a PR had to live inside it.
items.next_step: Tier-1 (scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py + .github/pr-landing/README.md). Design it TOGETHER with BL-20260908-R13-FORCES-EVERY-SELF-LANDING-BRANCH-TO-REWRITE-ONE-5-LINE-OBJECT-SO-CONCURRENT-PRS-CONFLICT-BY-CONSTRUCTION — same guard, and a naive third state would re-inherit that row's conflict problem. The R9 half (verify the named PR is actually open) is separable, cheap, and worth doing regardless of whether a third state is added.
items.found_by: MI-204, from having to rewrite PR #11418's own hold declaration in order to land it honestly

items.title: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <pr-head> main` reports NOT MERGED for every squash-merged PR in this repo — a confident, silent false negative, and --grep gives the opposite false positive
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 on PR #11384, twice, in OPPOSITE directions. Both probes are ones a session would reasonably reach for to answer 'has this PR landed', and BOTH lied.

FALSE POSITIVE: `git log origin/main --grep='#11384'` returned commit aa1addad while #11384 was still OPEN. `--grep` matches the WHOLE commit message including the body, and aa1addad's body contained the manager's note 'My own merge_slot write re-dirtied #11384' — a commit ABOUT the PR, not one merging it.

FALSE NEGATIVE, and this is the dangerous one: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <pr-head-sha> origin/main` returned NOT-an-ancestor at a moment when main's TIP WAS LITERALLY THE SQUASH COMMIT OF THAT PR (0212b425 'The A1 readout cron has failed 6 of 6 scheduled runs on a missing PyYAML (#11384)'), confirmed independently by `pull_request_read method=get` -> merged: true, merged_at 2026-09-08T17:25:37Z. THIS REPO SQUASH-MERGES, so the squashed commit is a NEW object and a PR's head sha is NEVER an ancestor of main. The probe is not flaky — it is wrong 100% of the time on a merged PR, for every squash-merged PR in the repo's history.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE SESSION: the ancestry test is exactly what one reaches for as the RIGOROUS alternative after being burned by --grep, so the natural correction path leads from a false positive straight to a categorical false negative. It fails silently and confidently — a clean boolean, no error, plausible either way — which is docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md's UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A: the label asks 'is this merged' and the code answers 'is this commit reachable', and under squash-merge those are different questions. A session that trusted it would conclude a MERGED PR IS STILL OPEN — and for anything blocked or queued behind that PR, that means waiting forever on something that already landed. Concretely: had this probe been written into a scheduled check-in, the loop would have re-armed indefinitely against a PR merged an hour earlier. I caught it only because main's visible tip contradicted it.

WHAT ACTUALLY WORKS: `pull_request_read method=get` -> `merged` + `merged_at` (authoritative). On the git side, match the SUBJECT LINE only (`git log origin/main --format='%s' | grep -F '(#N)'`), never the body, since the squash subject carries `(#N)`. [!] Even the subject match is weaker than the API field — a commit could quote '(#N)' in its subject for other reasons — so prefer the API when it is available.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any committed script or workflow in this repo currently uses `--is-ancestor` or `--grep` to decide merge status. I did not sweep for it, and 'I did not look' is not 'there are none'. That sweep is the cheap half of resolving this.
items.resolution_criteria: TWO PARTS. (1) SWEEP: `grep -rn 'is-ancestor\|log.*--grep' scripts/ .github/` is run and every hit that decides MERGE STATUS is either corrected to the API/subject-line form or annotated as not asking that question. A clean sweep resolves this half — but it must be RUN and its result recorded, since this row explicitly does not claim there are no hits. (2) The correct form is written where a session will actually read it at the point of use — CLAUDE.md § PM-side session capabilities already documents the sibling zero-check-runs and 403 traps, which is the precedent for where this belongs. [!] A row in a 1300-row backlog resolves NOTHING on its own: this class recurs precisely because the lesson lives somewhere nobody reads mid-task, which is the reasoning CLAUDE.md gives for restating the mergeable_state trap inline after it cost two sessions ten minutes each.
items.next_step: Tier-1 and cheap. Do the grep sweep FIRST — it is one command and it decides whether this is a documentation row or a code-fix row.
items.found_by: MI-204, checking whether #11384 had merged so it could discharge PR #11418's hold

items.title: RECURRENCE of BL-20260820: /api/bot/trades/closed and /api/bot/strategies publish DIFFERENT exit taxonomies over the same column — 174 of 447 real-money closed rows (38.9%) carry a different label depending on which endpoint you ask, and 53 of them read `sl` on one surface and `other` on the other
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 12:16-12:30Z. POPULATION, because it is the whole point: every real-money closed row returned by GET /api/bot/trades/closed, paged to exhaustion (limit=200, offset 0/200/400) — n=447 unique ids (447 rows, 447 unique, arithmetic cross-check OK), accounts bybit_2 (446) + alpaca_live (1), window 2026-05-09 .. 2026-09-04. Raw exit_reason joined from /api/bot/db/table/trades with filter_state=='applied' asserted on every page (1656 bybit_2 + 337 alpaca_live = 1993 rows, matching both reported totals). Reproduce: scripts/research/real_money_close_attribution.py.

THE TWO NORMALISERS ARE DIFFERENT FUNCTIONS OVER THE SAME `trades.exit_reason` COLUMN, and the newer one is STRICTLY CRUDER. src/web/api/routers/strategies.py::_normalise_exit_reason maps sl/sl_cross->sl, tp/tp_cross->tp, keeps vwap_cross and time_decay as their own buckets, reconciler*->reconciler, rest->other. src/web/api/routers/trades_closed.py::_normalise_close_reason keeps ONLY tp/sl/manual, maps reconciler*-> reconciler, and sends EVERYTHING ELSE to 'other'. Disagreement over the 447:
    vwap_cross  n=102  /strategies 'vwap_cross'  vs  /trades/closed 'other'
    sl_cross    n= 53  /strategies 'sl'          vs  /trades/closed 'other'   <- a STOP-OUT reads as unclassified
    tp_cross    n= 15  /strategies 'tp'          vs  /trades/closed 'other'   <- a TARGET HIT reads as unclassified
    time_decay  n=  4  /strategies 'time_decay'  vs  /trades/closed 'other'
    TOTAL      174 of 447 = 38.9%

WHY IT IS HIGH AND NOT COSMETIC — IT ALREADY CAUSED A WRONG DIAGNOSIS, IN THIS REPO, THIS WEEK. The MI-200 dispatch reasoned from closeReason that 'nine of fifteen closes were not a strategy exit decision at all' and instructed a session to root-cause on that basis. Over the 447-row population that inference is wrong by 174 rows in BOTH directions: 'other' contains 182 rows that ARE strategy exits (vwap_cross 102, sl_cross 53, tp_cross 15, exit_head 5, time_decay 4, stale_stop 3) AND 49 that are not (backfill_closed_pnl_recovery 21, adopted_orphan_disappeared 7, netting_attributed 7, operator_flatten_reconciled 3, manual_closeall 3, netted_misattributed 2, intent_reduce* 5, stuck_strategy_watchdog 1). Fifteen distinct mechanisms in one bucket. This is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A (semantic substitution) per CLAUDE.md, at the reader rather than the producer.

IT IS A RECURRENCE, WHICH IS THE FINDING (filed with similar_ok per the backlog rules). BL-20260820-STRATEGIES-EXIT-REASON-ROLLUP-BUCKETS-LEVERS-AS-OTHER named this exact class on 2026-08-20 and scoped its remedy to strategies.py; trades_closed.py has the same defect in a worse form and was never touched, so fixing one module left the sibling publishing a contradictory answer. The earlier row's proposed class axis (bracket / clock / path / portfolio / infrastructure / unclassified) is the right remedy for BOTH, and applying it to only one is what produced a 38.9% disagreement between two live surfaces.

NOT THE SAME AS BL-20260820-EXIT-REASON-UNCLASSIFIED-IS-THE-MODAL-VALUE, which is about the PRODUCER declaring it could not classify. Here the producer classified fine and two READERS disagree about what it said.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) both endpoints consume ONE shared normaliser with a class axis (the remedy BL-20260820-STRATEGIES-EXIT-REASON-ROLLUP-BUCKETS-LEVERS-AS-OTHER already specifies), so the same trade cannot carry two published labels; OR (b) /api/bot/trades/closed additionally publishes the RAW exit_reason beside closeReason, so a consumer that needs the mechanism can read it without a second join. VERIFIED BY: re-running scripts/research/real_money_close_attribution.py and observing the disagreement count fall to 0 (or, under (b), by asserting the raw field is present and equal to trades.exit_reason on a live pull). A passing unit test is NOT sufficient — the two normalisers each pass their own tests today. NOT sufficient: renaming the 'other' bucket. The remedy is to branch on the actual condition, not reword the label.

items.title: Filtering /api/bot/trades/closed?include_paper=true to accountClass=='real_money' yields a WINDOW, not the real-money population — the default already excludes paper, so the flag NARROWS the real-money row count from 447 to 15, and a session reported the 15 as the population
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-08 12:16-12:30Z against the live API (https://ict-bot.duckdns.org).

THE TRAP. GET /api/bot/trades/closed takes include_paper, DEFAULT False, and the default response is already real-money-only (not_paper_predicate, src/web/api/_clean_trades.py). `limit` is capped at 200. So:
    ?limit=200                     -> 200 rows, ALL real_money,  window 2026-05-19 .. 09-04
    ?limit=200&include_paper=true  -> 200 rows, 185 paper + 15 real_money, window 2026-08-30 .. 09-04
    ?limit=200 paged to exhaustion -> 447 real-money rows,        window 2026-05-09 .. 09-04
Passing include_paper=true and THEN filtering to real_money does not widen the real-money set — it narrows it to whatever fraction of the newest 200 MIXED rows happens to be real money. The 15 are a strict subset of the 447 (verified by id-set containment).

IT IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL AND IT REACHED AN OPERATOR-FACING CONCLUSION. The MI-200 dispatch (2026-09-08 12:16Z) stated its population as 'every accountClass=real_money row on /api/bot/trades/closed?limit=200 - n=15, all bybit_2' and concluded '0 wins, 13 losses'. Both are artifacts of the 5-day slice. Over the real population the book is 117 W / 258 L / 49 flat (n=424 graded on the canonical decision set). It also concluded 'alpaca_live contributed zero closes' — true of the slice, false of the population, which contains an alpaca_live close. A session then reasoned about a losing STREAK from a window that had been selected, unintentionally, to contain one.

WHY IT IS A DEFECT AND NOT JUST A CALLER MISTAKE. The failure is silent and reads as success: the response is 200 OK with a plausible row count, every row genuinely IS real money, and nothing in the payload says the real-money set was truncated by a paper-row quota. This is the 'Green is not evidence' shape — an artifact true relative to its own scope while the scope is wrong — and CLAUDE.md's own 'Always state the population' rule cannot save a caller who cannot SEE that the population moved. Compare the Data Explorer, which had exactly this class fixed by publishing filter_state (BL-20260813-DB-EXPLORER-SILENTLY-IGNORES-UNKNOWN-FILTER-COLUMN): the remedy there was to make the server say what it actually resolved.

NOT A DUPLICATE of BL-20260813-DB-EXPLORER-SILENTLY-IGNORES-UNKNOWN-FILTER-COLUMN: that is a different route and a dropped filter. This is a paging/quota interaction on /trades/closed where the filter WAS applied and the caller's mental model of what include_paper does is inverted.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) /api/bot/trades/closed returns pagination/population metadata a caller can assert on — at minimum the total matching row count for the requested class filter, so `len(rows)` being capped at `limit` is distinguishable from the population being that size; OR (b) the route rejects/warns when include_paper=true is combined with a client-side class filter, OR (c) at minimum, docs/reference/bot-api-reference.md carries an explicit warning on this route stating that include_paper=true NARROWS the real-money set and that the real-money population must be obtained by paging the DEFAULT call. VERIFIED BY: a live pull demonstrating the caller can tell 15-of-a-window from 15-of-a-population without already knowing the answer. NOT sufficient: a docstring in the router (the misreading happened at the API consumer, not in the code).

updates.by: claude (MI-200, session 01CvFCybCkvrfzaHqNH3tQsb) — narrowing my own row
updates.note:
NARROWED BY ITS AUTHOR: MY CRITERION (a) ALREADY SHIPS, so this row must not be read as asking for it. I wrote that the route should 'return pagination/population metadata a caller can assert on — at minimum the total matching row count'. It does, and has since 2026-09-06 (MI-144). MEASURED live 2026-09-08 against the running API:
    GET /api/bot/trades/closed?limit=200                    -> X-Total-Count: 448   X-Has-More: true
    GET /api/bot/trades/closed?limit=200&include_paper=true -> X-Total-Count: 1528  X-Has-More: true
So the DEFAULT call already tells a caller that 200 rows are a truncation of 448 real-money rows — which would have caught the original error outright.

⚠️ THE HEADER DOES NOT FULLY COVER THE include_paper CASE, and that residue is what this row is now for: under include_paper=true, X-Total-Count is 1528 — every CLASS — so it does not give the real-money count, and a caller filtering client-side to real money still has no server-side denominator for the population they are actually building. It is a strong hint (1528 total against 15 real-money rows in hand is obviously a slice) but not an assertion they can make.

SO THE DEFECT IS SMALLER AND DIFFERENT THAN I FILED IT: not 'the metadata is missing' but 'the metadata exists, is not class-scoped, and was not read'. Severity high -> medium. Criterion (a) is SATISFIED; what remains is either a class-scoped count under include_paper, or — cheaper and probably sufficient — a warning at the route's row in docs/reference/bot-api-reference.md that filtering an include_paper response client-side yields a WINDOW, not a population. I have not made that doc edit in this PR: the reference is a level-7 subsystem spec and editing it belongs with whoever settles the criterion, not smuggled into a measurement PR.

⚠️ AND THE PART THAT STILL STANDS UNCHANGED: the incident was real, the wrong population reached an operator-facing conclusion ('0 for 13' over a 5-day slice of a 447-close book), and I found the headers only by reading the reference AFTER the fact — which is itself evidence for the discoverability half.

items.opened_by: claude (MI-200, session 01CvFCybCkvrfzaHqNH3tQsb) — operator-raised: 'if we're not exiting on brackets, then something is still not working'
items.title: WITHDRAWN — `sl_cross` closes that read as profitable are explained by `trades.stop_loss` holding the FINAL TRAILED stop; my R basis was wrong, the label was not
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-08. POPULATION: real-money closed rows on the canonical decision set (/api/bot/trades/closed paged to exhaustion, n=447, minus the KPI exclusions in src/web/api/_clean_trades.py -> n=431), of which 53 carry exit_reason='sl_cross'. Geometry computed per row as R = sign*(exit-entry)/|entry-stop| from the journal's own entry_price/stop_loss/exit_price/direction; 'at_stop' is within 0.10R of -1.0 (a slippage band, CHOSEN not tuned, and stated so the count can be re-derived under a different band). Reproduce: scripts/research/real_money_close_attribution.py plus the geometry block in docs/research/real-money-close-attribution-2026-09-08.md.

THE FINDING. sl_cross closes land: at_stop 27, between 21, beyond_stop 5. So 21 of 53 (39.6%) carry a label asserting price crossed the stop while the recorded exit is not at the stop. NINE of those 21 exited in PROFIT (R > 0), up to R = +1.13 -- e.g. id 1319 (vwap/BTCUSDT, R +1.13, pnl +0.1677, provenance MEASURED), id 4134 (eth_pullback_2h/ETHUSDT, R +1.02, pnl +1.2096), id 3136 (xrp_pullback_2h/XRPUSDT, R +0.90, pnl +0.9640). A position that exited a full R ABOVE its entry did not cross a stop sitting one R BELOW it. The label states a price event that did not occur.

WHY IT MATTERS. exit_reason is the field the exit-refinement corpus, /api/bot/performance's perExitPath and every exit-quality read bucket on. A stop-out and a profitable exit are opposite outcomes; folding the second into the first inflates apparent stop-outs and hides whatever mechanism actually closed those rows. It is the same UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A shape CLAUDE.md already names -- the label names a quantity the code did not compute.

⚠️ STATE THE POPULATION HONESTLY: 6 of the 9 profitable-but-sl_cross rows are `vwap`, a leg OFF since 2026-06-07 and routed to no account, so most of this is HISTORICAL and cannot recur. But 2 are on legs STILL routed to real-money bybit_2 (eth_pullback_2h, xrp_pullback_2h), so it is not purely historical either. Do not report it as either extreme.

⚠️ WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH: the mechanism. I did not read the writer that stamps sl_cross, so I cannot say whether the stop level moved after entry (a trail, which would make 'crossed the stop' true against a LATER stop than the journal's stop_loss column records), whether the classifier ran against a stale price, or whether the label is simply wrong. THE TRAILING HYPOTHESIS IS THE MOST LIKELY AND WOULD MAKE THE LABEL DEFENSIBLE AND THE COLUMN MISLEADING -- if trades.stop_loss holds the ENTRY stop while the exit was against a trailed stop, then every R computed from that column is wrong for every trailed trade, which is a LARGER finding than this row and must be checked before this one is 'fixed'.

ADJACENT, NOT DUPLICATE: BL-20260822-EXIT-ATTRIBUTION-UNDER-REPORTS-BRACKET-HITS is the INVERSE (the bracket is reached more often than exit_reason records); this is over-reporting one specific reason. BL-20260821-GRADER-CALLS-A-RECONCILER-CLOSE-A-TAKE-PROFIT is about the GRADER inferring a mechanism from R; this is about the stored mechanism disagreeing with R.
items.resolution_criteria: FIRST settle the trailing question, because it decides which thing is broken: establish whether trades.stop_loss is the ENTRY stop or the stop in force at close, on a trade known to have trailed. THEN either (a) if stop_loss is the entry stop, the defect is that R-vs-bracket geometry computed from it is invalid for trailed trades -- record that, and this row becomes a symptom of it; or (b) if stop_loss is the stop in force at close, then sl_cross on a row that exited above entry is a genuine mislabel and the writer must be fixed. VERIFIED BY: re-running scripts/research/real_money_close_attribution.py and observing the profitable-sl_cross count fall to 0, or by a recorded finding that the count is explained by trailing with the geometry caveat documented where the corpus reads it. NOT sufficient: renaming the reason, or widening the at_stop band until the rows fall inside it.

updates.note:
WITHDRAWN BY ITS OWN AUTHOR, SAME SESSION, BEFORE MERGE. I filed this hours ago claiming nine `sl_cross` rows 'exited in PROFIT, so the label states a price event that did not happen', and I named the trailed-stop explanation as a HYPOTHESIS that must be settled first. It is not a hypothesis — it is documented, canonical behaviour that I had not read.

`trades.stop_loss` holds the **FINAL TRAILED** stop: `order_monitor._apply_update` mirrors every confirmed amend onto the row (src/runtime/order_monitor.py:1372), correctly, because /api/bot/positions must show where the stop IS. This is stated outright in docs/reference/bot-api-reference.md, and it is the exact contamination MI-144 fixed in expectancyR on 2026-09-06. My R was computed from that column, so a trade whose stop trailed ABOVE entry and then genuinely stopped out reads as exitR > 0 against ENTRY. The label is most likely correct and my denominator was wrong.

⚠️ WHAT I AM *NOT* CLAIMING: I have not proven each of the nine trailed. Establishing that needs the entry-time stop from order_packages.meta::risk_per_unit or the amend history, which I did not pull. So this closes as `closed_answered` — the repo already answers it — NOT as 'verified benign'. If someone wants the nine graded properly, the instrument is `bracketOutcome` on /api/bot/performance (src/runtime/bracket_outcome.py), which grades against order_packages.sl/.tp — the DECISION-TIME bracket — and reads reachedSl 188 / reachedTp 41 / midBracket 192 / reachedRatio 0.5439 over gradeable 421 real-money rows, live 2026-09-08.

RECORDED RATHER THAN DELETED because the mistake is the reusable lesson: I computed a geometry from the most obvious column without checking what that column MEANS, and the answer was one grep away in the canonical reference. Same class as RC-BUILT-A-MECHANISM-THAT-ALREADY-EXISTED, which I also hit in the same session by re-deriving bracketOutcome by hand.

STATUS IS `invalid`, NOT `closed_answered`: check_backlog_criteria enforces the enum ['invalid','kept_open','open','resolved','superseded','wont_fix'] on this file, and CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL's prose disposition name `closed_answered` is not one of them. Field beats comment — the guard's enum is what this file actually admits. `invalid` is also the more accurate of the available values: the row's PREMISE was wrong, which is a different thing from a real finding that got answered.

items.title: check_pr_landing R6 certifies `landing: self` on a branch whose NAME cannot trigger claude-pr-automerge (branches: claude/**), so the PR passes its own guard and then never merges — the exact failure the landing system exists to prevent
items.resolution_criteria: MEASURED 2026-09-08 on a LIVE instance: PR #11347 (branch `mi-168-post-merge-record`) declares tier 1 / landing self, writes .github/pr-automerge-requests/mi-168-post-merge-record.txt, passes `pr-landing: OK - state=declared_self_land`, is GREEN on all 5 checks and `mergeable_state: clean` - and does not merge, because .github/workflows/claude-pr-automerge.yml is `on: push: branches: ["claude/**"]` and the branch is not under `claude/`. The workflow never fires at all. !! THE GUARD STRIPS THE PREFIX BUT NEVER REQUIRES IT. check_pr_landing.py:256 derives the slug as `re.sub(r'^claude/', '', branch).replace('/', '-')` - so a `claude/` prefix is OPTIONAL for slug derivation, and R6 then checks only that the request FILE exists and differs from base. Nothing checks that the branch NAME can reach the workflow. So R6 certifies an arming that is inert by construction. !! IT IS INVISIBLE TO THE GUARD'S OWN SELF-TEST BECAUSE EVERY FIXTURE USES A TRIGGERABLE NAME: check_pr_landing.py:516 creates `claude/demo` and the R6 case at :621 runs against it, so the one branch shape that breaks is the one shape never tested. A positive control passing is what made this survivable to ship. !! DISTINCT FROM BL-20260903-A-PR-OPENED-BY-THE-RELAY-CAN-ARM-AUTOMERGE-AND-THEN-WAIT-ON-GREEN-FOREVER, AND THE TWO MUST NOT BE MERGED: that row is the ZERO-CHECKS cause (a relay-opened PR starts with no checks because the results commit is pushed by github-actions[bot], and auto-merge waits on a green that never arrives) and its remedy is to push one ordinary commit. THIS row is the BRANCH-NAME cause and no push of any kind fixes it. Same symptom - a green Tier-1 PR that sits - opposite remedy. A session that reads only the older row pushes a commit, sees checks go green, and still does not merge. !! AND IT DEFEATS THE STATED PURPOSE OF THE MECHANISM. R6's own failure text says an un-armed declaration is "precisely how 7 green PRs sat unmerged on 2026-09-03". A guard that certifies an arming which cannot fire reproduces that outcome while REPORTING OK, which is worse than not checking: the author now has positive evidence the route is armed. RESOLUTION: either (a) R6 additionally verifies the head branch matches the workflow's own `branches:` filter - read from the workflow file rather than hardcoded, so the two cannot drift - and FAILS a `landing: self` on a branch that cannot trigger it, naming the rename as the fix; or (b) the workflow's branch filter is widened and this row records that decision instead. Add a self-test fixture on a NON-`claude/` branch either way - the absence of one is why this shipped. WORKAROUND for anyone hitting it now: name the branch `claude/<slug>` from the start (the slug derivation already strips the prefix, so no file needs renaming), or have someone with write access merge by hand. Renaming after the PR exists does NOT work: a PR is bound to its head ref, and this session 403s on update_pull_request. POPULATION: n=1 live instance, found incidentally while landing an unrelated Tier-1 correction. NOBODY HAS SWEPT the open-PR list for other self-declared branches outside `claude/**` - we did not look.

items.title: A board `START` declaration has no end, so scope-overlap reports a COMPLETED session as holding paths — 2 of 2 sessions it named on PR #11447 were not running
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-08T20:08Z on the scope-overlap audit comment posted to PR #11447. POPULATION: the 2 distinct sessions the audit named as LIVE across 5 reported path overlaps; BOTH were checked against list_sessions and NEITHER was running. || session_016KUFTHGYyFDerbnXDSA6Wb (MI-204) declared `docs/claude/work/` at 14:35:04Z and its status_bucket is COMPLETED with platform updated_at 18:54:28Z — the declaration outlived the session by ~5.5 hours and was still being reported as live 1.2 hours after that. session_01U2ibSa4FNcuV6bSLaPb9GS (MI-196) declared docs/claude/session-board.json at 12:12:31Z and is IDLE / REVIEW_READY, updated_at 17:39:16Z. The audit's own words are 'nothing says that session has finished', which is literally true and reads to the author as 'that session is still working'. || WHY IT MATTERS, and it is the desensitized-alarm shape this repo has a P1 rule about: the audit fires on EVERY PR touching a commonly-declared path, names sessions that stopped hours ago, and trains the author to skip it — at which point a genuine concurrent-edit collision is reported into a channel nobody reads. The board has no DONE-post requirement that anything enforces (a session that dies cannot post one, which is exactly the case that matters), so a declaration is unbounded by construction. || THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS BL-20260905-A-SESSIONS-OWN-STATUS-LINE-IS-WHAT-IT-LAST-SAID-NOT-WHAT-BECAME-TRUE-SO-FINISHED-WORK-READS-AS-IN-FLIGHT (open) IN A DIFFERENT MECHANISM, and that row's resolution_criteria cannot reach it: it is scoped to post_turn_summary and to handoff_check/manager_view, and this producer is a GitHub comment read by a workflow. Filed with similar_ok after reading it rather than folded in, because a fix for one does not fix the other. || THIRD INSTANCE OF THE CLASS TODAY, IN THREE MECHANISMS, which is why it is worth a row rather than a note: (1) SESSIONS.json rows read `idle` because session_status collapses BLOCKED/FAILED/REVIEW_READY; (2) needs_action froze at each session's last turn — MI-181 asks to review PR #11328 which merged at 05:40:40Z, ELEVEN HOURS before that summary was written, and MI-179 asks to land #11330, merged 06:14:03Z, so 5 of 12 BLOCKED asks were already answered (evidence in MERGE-QUEUE/SESSIONS at PR #11447); (3) this. || ⚠️ PARTIALLY ANSWERED 20:16Z ON THE NEXT PR, AND IT SHARPENS THE ROW RATHER THAN WEAKENING IT. The same audit on PR #11450 rendered a SECOND section — 'Declared by a session whose branch has since landed' — and it distinguishes two staleness signals I had not seen: a declaring BRANCH that merged, and a session that posted a DONE. So the extractor is not staleness-blind; it has two signals and NEITHER is session liveness, which is the one that decides the question. Its own caveat is exact and correct: 'This says the BRANCH landed, not that the session ended.' || THE SAME SESSION APPEARS IN BOTH SECTIONS AT ONCE, which is the cleanest demonstration available that the two are different facts: session_01U2ibSa4FNcuV6bSLaPb9GS (MI-196) is listed as LIVE for its 12:12:31Z declaration while SEVEN of its own earlier declarations are listed under 'branch has since landed' for claude/mi196-due-readout-consolidation. The audit therefore KNOWS that session's branches merged and still reports it as holding paths — and measured against list_sessions it is IDLE / REVIEW_READY. || AND THE LIVE SECTION GREW RATHER THAN SHRANK: on #11450 it named 10 overlaps across 3 sessions where on #11447 it named 5 across 2, so this is not a one-comment artefact. || WHAT I DID NOT ESTABLISH: whether the audit has ever reported a TRUE positive, so I cannot say what its precision is — only that on this sample it was 0 for 2. I have still not read the extractor's source — the two signals above are inferred from its rendered output, not from its code — so I do not know how hard the liveness input would be to add, only that the two signals it has cannot substitute for it.
items.resolution_criteria: The scope-overlap audit distinguishes THREE states rather than two, and says which it means in the comment: `declared_by_a_running_session` / `declared_by_a_session_that_has_since_stopped` / `liveness_unknown` (the session id could not be resolved — WE DID NOT LOOK, never folded into either other state). Explicitly NOT sufficient: (a) requiring a DONE post, since the case that matters is a session that DIED and cannot post one; (b) a wall-clock age cutoff on declarations, which would silence a genuinely long-running session and is a different question from whether it is alive; (c) an instruction to authors to check the session themselves — the reminder-is-not-a-mechanism non-fix. NOTE the liveness read needs list_sessions, an mcp__* tool CI does not hold, so a workflow-side implementation may only be able to reach `liveness_unknown` — in which case the honest outcome is to SAY SO in the comment rather than to keep asserting live.

items.title: A manager read 'no branch on the remote' as 'no work produced', called a working session a STALL, and merged that claim to main 28 seconds before the session opened a 29-file PR
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09. At 23:50Z the manager (session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj) graded MI-205b (session_01ML8uLRrKLMmzR9fFywTWv5) a STALL on this evidence: `list_commits --sha claude/mi205b-ranking-key-harness` returned 404, no PR existed, and its task_summary string had not changed in 32 minutes. It wrote 'alive and unproductive' into SESSIONS.json and MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json and merged it to main as #11472 at 23:53Z. || IT WAS FALSE WHEN IT MERGED. The session's first commit is authored 23:49:59Z, it opened PR #11473 at 23:53:32Z -- 28 seconds before the manager's claim landed -- and that PR is 29 files / 40,979 additions: the N-book portfolio engine, a four-arm ranking-key A/B over 400 days of BTCUSDT 5m, a gate, a workflow, 25 tests, and a written NULL result with the population stated before any number. It also caught two defects in its OWN diff, one a commit-to-main call missing verify-merged. That is not an unproductive session by any reading. || THE DEFECT IS THE INFERENCE, NOT THE READ. The 404 was probably accurate at 23:50Z (the commits were authored locally seconds earlier). What was wrong was treating REMOTE-BRANCH PRESENCE as a proxy for WORK PRODUCED. A session building a large research deliverable reasonably makes its first push at ~90 minutes; the manager never established what a normal first-push latency looks like for this class of task, so it had no denominator and graded against an imagined one. This is RULE ONE's 'a search returning nothing is not proof of absence' applied to a metric never validated as a proxy in the first place. || THE AGGRAVATING FACTOR IS THAT IT WAS PUBLISHED. The manager had explicitly instructed itself -- in a scheduled wake it wrote -- to 'name the stall plainly rather than observe it a fifth time'. That instruction is sound against a genuine stall, and here it converted a weak inference into a durable false record on main, because the pressure it created was to COMMIT to a verdict rather than to improve the evidence. A self-issued instruction to be decisive is not a licence to be decisive on bad evidence. || FILED WITH similar_ok. The 8 lexical neighbours are a DIFFERENT class and must not be folded into this. BL-20260905-SUB-SESSIONS-FINISH-WORK-THEY-CANNOT-PUSH-AND-THE-MANAGER-CANNOT-REACH-THEM and BL-20260906-A-SUBSESSION-SPAWNED-WITHOUT-SOURCE-URL-GETS-NO-REPO-AND-ITS-WORK-DIES-UNPUSHED are about sessions that GENUINELY could not push. BL-20260902-SESSIONS-REGISTRY-IS-A-SPAWN-TIME-RECORD-35-OF-67-ROWS-NAME-NO-BRANCH and BL-20260905-THE-SESSION-REGISTRY-WAS-WRONG-ON-69-PERCENT-OF-STATES-AND-58-ROWS-HAD-NEVER-BEEN-OBSERVED-ONCE are about rows never observed at all. This is the inverse of the first pair and the opposite of the second: the manager DID observe, promptly and repeatedly, and drew a false conclusion from a sound reading.
items.resolution_criteria: A manager pass is observed grading a sub-session's progress WITHOUT using remote-branch presence as the productivity term -- or using it only alongside a stated expectation of first-push latency for that class of task. NOT SUFFICIENT: another backlog row, another line in a wake prompt, or a resolution to be more careful -- this row exists BECAUSE a self-issued instruction to be decisive is what produced the error. What would close it is a cheap POSITIVE probe run before calling a stall: ask the session (create_trigger + fire_trigger, proven to work per BL-20260902-AN-IDLE-CLOUD-SUB-SESSION-IS-RESUMABLE-VIA-A-SESSION-BOUND-ROUTINE-NOT-UNREACHABLE), or read whether its token counters are climbing -- MI-205b's own get_session record showed output_tokens 172,537 and cost_usd 54.03 at the moment it was called unproductive, a directly available counter-signal in a payload the manager had already fetched and did not read.

items.title: `git reset --hard origin/main` run while standing on a feature branch, twice in ~50 minutes by the same session — the second time AFTER writing the reminder against it on main
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09, n=2 in ~50 minutes, same session (the manager). || INSTANCE 1, ~01:25Z: run while standing on `claude/mgr-heartbeat-0100-20260909`. It rewound that branch to main and DISCARDED its two real commits locally (b387dd1e, 24aa0e19). The very next commit was built on main's tree, so a force-push would have wiped the lease heartbeat, the digest-deadlock finding and the MI-208 routing row FROM A PR THAT WAS ALREADY OPEN — and would have reported success. Caught only by noticing that `git log --oneline -1` named MAIN's head on a branch that should have been two commits ahead. Recovered with `git reset --hard origin/<branch>`; the later push was a fast-forward with no force, which independently confirmed the branch was whole. || INSTANCE 2, ~02:17Z: run while standing on `claude/mgr-heartbeat-0155-20260909`. HARMLESS ONLY BY LUCK — that branch's PR (#11480) had already merged, so the reset happened to move it onto the squash commit of its own work. Surfaced by the stop-hook reporting '1 unpushed commit', which was main's commit sitting on a branch that should not have been there. || ⚠️ THE FINDING IS NOT THE MISTAKE, IT IS THAT THE FIX DID NOT HOLD. Between the two instances I wrote '⚠️ `git branch --show-current` before any `reset --hard`' into the MANAGER-LEASE note that MERGED TO MAIN, and into two scheduled wake prompts. It failed on its first test, 50 minutes later. That is this repo's own 'a reminder is not a mechanism' lesson reproduced inside a single session, and it is the reason this row exists rather than a third restatement. || THE MECHANISM-LEVEL CAUSE: `git reset --hard <target>` names ONLY the target. It never names the branch being moved, so it silently operates on whatever HEAD happens to be — the command cannot be made safe by care, because the dangerous argument is the one you do not type. `git checkout main && git pull --ff-only` names the branch it operates on and refuses a non-fast-forward, so it cannot destroy a feature branch even when run from the wrong place. || FILED WITH similar_ok. The 8 lexical neighbours are adjacent and NOT this: BL-20260901-RESETTING-A-CLAUDE-BRANCH-ONTO-NEWER-MAIN-REFIRES-PR-OPENER-FOR-SOMEONE-ELSES-REQUEST is a SIDE-EFFECT of an intentional reset (it re-fires pr-opener), not the reset destroying the branch's own commits; BL-20260816-CORPUS-CONFLICT-REDERIVE-RUNS-THE-STALE-BRANCH-EXTRACTOR is an automated re-derive dropping corpus FIELDS, a different actor and a different loss. Neither covers an interactive session resetting the branch it is standing on.
items.resolution_criteria: The repo's own guidance and prompts stop recommending `git reset --hard origin/main` as the sync idiom and use `git checkout main && git pull --ff-only` instead — checked by grepping the instruction surfaces, not by asserting it. ⚠️ NOT SUFFICIENT: another reminder, in any document or wake prompt, that one should check the current branch first. That is precisely what was tried between instance 1 and instance 2 and it failed within the hour; a row closed on a restatement would be closing on the thing already measured not to work. ⚠️ ALSO NOT SUFFICIENT: 'no further instances observed' — the second instance was harmless by luck, so absence of DAMAGE is not absence of the behaviour, and only the harmful case is visible.

items.title: A routine manager reconcile wrote a bare timestamp over SESSIONS.json's structured `last_observed`, destroying nine `manager_verdict` records — and the loss check passed because it tested KEY PRESENCE, not value shape
items.detail:
WHAT HAPPENED. During the 04:26Z cadence pass I refreshed `last_observed` on 24 SESSIONS.json rows by assigning a timestamp STRING. In 120 of the 176 rows that field is an OBJECT carrying `source`, `session_status`, `status_bucket`, `platform_updated_at`, `needs_action`, `manager_verdict` and `manager_verdict_basis`. The write flattened every one it touched: 158 deletions against 46 insertions.

WHAT WAS ALMOST LOST IS THE POINT. `manager_verdict: answered_already` with a basis like "asks to 'approve PR #11330 to land'. #11330 MERGED 2026-09-08T06:14:03Z" is the mechanism a PREVIOUS manager built against a documented failure — `needs_action` does not decay, it is a session's last-turn claim frozen where it stopped, and five of twelve BLOCKED asks were already answered. That verdict is the ONLY thing stopping a successor re-asking a settled question or, worse, ACTING on a stale ask. Nine of them were in the overwrite.

⚠️ THE REAL FINDING IS THE VERIFICATION, NOT THE WRITE. I did check for loss. I compared `set(old_keys) - set(new_keys)` per row and it returned EMPTY — because the key `last_observed` still existed. A key-presence check cannot see a value replaced by one of a different TYPE, and it returned exactly the reassuring answer I expected. That is RULE ONE's 'verify your own output too, hardest when it confirms what you expected', and the check was mine.

⚠️ AND THE ROUND-TRIP ASSERTION DID NOT COVER IT EITHER. I asserted `json.dumps(d, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + chr(10) == raw` BEFORE editing, which proves the SERIALISATION is faithful and says nothing whatever about whether the edit destroys content. Two checks passed and neither was watching this.

CAUGHT BY the diffstat — 158 deletions for an edit that should have been additive. The line-count shape of a diff is a cheap arithmetic cross-check on a register write, and it is the only thing that fired.

FIXED IN THE SAME PASS by reverting and rewriting the update to merge into the existing dict (`lo = dict(lo); lo.update(...)`), building one where the field was None (56 rows), and asserting at VALUE level that every prior key of every row survived — which reported zero destroyed values, 176 rows, 140 insertions / 49 deletions.

WHY IT IS WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A LESSON. The registers under docs/claude/work/ are append-mostly and are written by hand, by many sessions, with no schema. `check_register_ids` grades ID uniqueness and identity; NOTHING grades whether a write preserved the structure of the rows it touched. A field that is an object in 120 rows and null in 56 is exactly the shape that invites a scalar assignment. The generic remedy is a value-level before/after assertion on any register write, and the mechanical one would be a shape check on `last_observed`.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) a guard that fails a PR whose diff changes the TYPE of an existing value in any docs/claude/work/*.json register row — not just id uniqueness, which check_register_ids already covers — and is observed FAILING on a deliberately-flattened test row, not merely registered; OR (b) `last_observed` is given a declared shape and the 56 null rows are reconciled to it, so a scalar assignment is a type error rather than a silent overwrite. ⚠️ NOT SUFFICIENT: a note in the cadence Routine or in CLAUDE.md telling a manager to be careful — this pass already carried a written warning about registers being append-only and about not taking a side in a merge, and neither covers an in-place field overwrite by the register's own maintainer. ⚠️ ALSO NOT SUFFICIENT: my own value-level assertion, which lives in a throwaway script in one session's context and protects nothing after this turn.

items.title: CORRECTION to BL-20260908-R13-MAKES-EVERY-AUTOMATION-PR-WRITE-THE-MERGE-SLOT-SO-MAIN-CAN-NEVER-BE-QUIET: the action never wrote the slot; a manager hand-wrote it on the two PRs that row cites
items.detail:
CORRECTION, not a recurrence. BL-20260908-R13-MAKES-EVERY-AUTOMATION-PR-WRITE-THE-MERGE-SLOT-SO-MAIN-CAN-NEVER-BE-QUIET states 'Automation PRs self-land, so they arm, so they write the slot' and cites #11403 and #11477 as automation PRs that wrote merge_slot. THE RULE DERIVATION IS RIGHT AND THE OBSERVATION IS NOT: `.github/actions/commit-to-main/action.yml` — the single action all 27 automation producers call — writes the R11 landing declaration and the R6 arming file and DOES NOT write the merge_slot claim. Those PRs carried a claim because a MANAGER hand-pushed it onto their branches to land them.

EVIDENCE, read from the PR's own diff rather than inferred: #11477's docs/claude/session-board.json hunk sets `held_by: "session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj"` — a manager session id, not `github-actions[bot]` — and its `purpose` reads verbatim 'MERGE-QUEUE UNBLOCK. work-digest.yml arms the landing route but never writes a merge_slot claim, so its receipt PR fails R13 and can NEVER merge ... The manager writes the claim this one workflow cannot write for itself.' A squash merge attributes the commit to the merger, so `git log --format=%an` cannot tell these apart; the PR's own file diff can.

WHY THE DIFFERENCE MATTERS AND IS NOT PEDANTRY. A session reading the existing row concludes that automation PRs already satisfy R13 and that the automation lane is merely CONTENDED. It is not — it was DEADLOCKED: measured 2026-09-09, 47 open PRs of which 46 are automation, and PR #11487's guards job reads PASS 53 / FAIL 1 with the 1 being pr-landing-guard on R13 (reproduced locally against automation/session-reaper-34311893227-1). A session acting on the existing row's wording would look for a contention fix and never find the missing write. That is the unprovenanced-diagnostic shape this repo has a guard for, one level up: a claim about a MECHANISM derived from a rule rather than read off the code.

WHAT SURVIVES THE CORRECTION, and it is the more important half: the existing row's MEASUREMENTS are sound and I re-measured its headline independently — 19 of the last 20 commits on origin/main touch docs/claude/session-board.json (population: git show --stat on each of the last 20). Today that churn is driven mostly by manager heartbeats, every one of which writes merge_slot. Fixing the deadlock (PR #11494) ADDS automation PRs to that set, which is a real cost, stated rather than hidden: the conflict-heal shipped with the fix lives inside commit-to-main, so an automation branch re-asserts its claim over main and recovers while a HUMAN branch has no such heal and still loses — which is exactly the 17-consecutive-collision case the existing row measured on #11370.
items.resolution_criteria: The existing row's mechanism sentence is corrected in place (or this row is linked from it), so a future session reading either one cannot conclude that commit-to-main writes the slot. ⚠️ THIS DOES NOT CLEAR BY #11494 MERGING: after that merge the sentence becomes TRUE, and a row corrected by the world moving rather than by anyone reading it teaches nothing — which is the failure mode the operator named on 2026-08-26. ⚠️ AND IT DOES NOT CLEAR THE THREE R13-CONTENTION ROWS, which are about the single shared key being the wrong shape for a repo with dozens of bot landings a day; that is a guard-design decision with operator implications and is deliberately NOT taken here.
items.next_step: A reviewer of #11494 reads this beside BL-20260908-R13-MAKES-EVERY-AUTOMATION-PR-WRITE-THE-MERGE-SLOT-SO-MAIN-CAN-NEVER-BE-QUIET and corrects that row's mechanism sentence. Separately, the human-branch half of the contention has no heal and is the open question for the three R13 rows.

items.title: On 4 closed trades the exit price sits within 5bp of order_packages.sl while trades.stop_loss still carries the ENTRY stop — the row understated the level actually resting at the venue, and /api/bot/positions reads that row
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09 (MI-209), complete census of trades (n=5589) and order_packages (n=4500) via GET /api/bot/db/table/*, evidence docs/research/exit-trailing-banking-broker-truth-2026-09-09.md §3.3. POPULATION: the 194 closed trades on the 146 packages whose stop demonstrably moved (entry-time order_packages.exit_plan.stop.price vs current order_packages.sl). trades.stop_loss DIVERGES from order_packages.sl on 46 of 194 (23.7%), and all 46 sit EXACTLY on the entry-time stop — the leg row never moved at all. MOST OF THAT IS LEGITIMATE AND IS NOT THE FINDING: _apply_update syncs trades.stop_loss only for legs returned by _package_open_legs, so a leg that closed before a later amend correctly keeps its own entry stop; 40 of the 46 closed before their package's updated_at and all 46 belong to 2/3/4-leg packages. THE FINDING IS THE 4 ROWS THAT CONTRADICT THAT EXPLANATION: their exit_price sits within 5bp of order_packages.sl while their own stop_loss reads the entry level — trade 2823 eth_pullback_2h (row 1712.03, pkg 1643.84, exit 1643.99), 3433 trend_donchian (62906.1 / 63971.7 / 63944), 3577 xrp_pullback_2h (1.0655 / 1.1116 / exit 1.1115 — 0.009%, one XRP tick, four minutes before that package row's updated_at), 4469 qqq_pullback_1h (704.327 / 716.115 / 716.04). Three of the four are broker-truth (provenance.is_measured on exit_price_source); the fourth is not. Two independently-set levels agreeing to a tick is not a plausible coincidence, so on those rows the level resting at the venue was the PACKAGE's, not the row's. MECHANISM NOT ESTABLISHED AND NOT CLAIMED — I traced that of the 19 update_order_package( call sites in src/, only order_monitor.py:1460 (the KIND_MODIFY branch) writes sl, and that branch does sync per leg; so this is filed, not diagnosed. THE OTHER 42 DIVERGENT ROWS WERE NOT ADJUDICATED — consistent with legitimate early close is not the same as shown to be it. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the comment at order_monitor.py ~L1397 states the per-leg sync exists precisely so 'a leg whose amend failed must keep showing its real venue level', and on these rows it shows a level the venue did not have; /api/bot/positions reads trades.stop_loss (that is the whole point of the per-leg sync at order_monitor.py ~L1471). SIDE OBSERVATION, deliberately not spelled as an id here because it would resolve to nothing and backlog-refs-guard is right to refuse that: the fix whose rationale that sync rests on is cited by id five times in src/ -- order_monitor.py:77, :1264, :1401, :1471 and database.py:1257 -- and has NO FILED ROW in any of the three backlogs, so a load-bearing order-path decision is documented only in code comments. Pre-existing and outside this unit; recorded here so the next reader of those comments does not go looking for a row that was never written., so an operator surface can understate an active stop. It also changes a research answer: grading trailed stop-outs off trades.stop_loss gives 9 of 14 at the trailed level where order_packages.sl gives 12 of 14, and nothing in either method section forces the field choice.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) the 4 rows are explained by a named code path that moves order_packages.sl or the venue stop without syncing the open leg's trades.stop_loss — naming the path and showing it on one of these four trade ids, after which this closes as closed_answered if the path is correct behaviour; OR (b) if no such path exists, a reproduction showing an open leg's trades.stop_loss left stale after a landed amend, and the sync fixed, with the fix demonstrated to FIRE on that reproduction and to stay silent when the leg legitimately closed before the amend (a guard shown only on the negative case is not shown). Reading the code again without adjudicating one of the four ids does NOT close this. The 42 unadjudicated rows are explicitly out of scope — they are not claimed as defects here.

items.title: provenance.is_measured(row) accepts Any and silently returns False for EVERY row when passed a bucket string instead of a row — the same total-silent-failure its sibling pnl_is_trustworthy has a docstring warning about
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09 (MI-209) in the course of docs/research/exit-trailing-banking-broker-truth-2026-09-09.md §1. is_measured(row: Any, key='exit_price_source') calls classify_row(row, key), which reads row[key]; handed a STRING it raises TypeError internally, catches it, and returns UNVERIFIED. The predicate therefore returns False for 100% of rows with no error, no warning and no log line. POPULATION AND EVIDENCE: over the decision population (closed, non-backtest, pnl NOT NULL, n=1502 on the 2026-09-09 census) the mistaken call returned 'is_measured: 0 of 1502' while a Counter over classify_pnl in the SAME run independently showed 585 measured rows. I made this exact mistake and caught it only because the positive control happened to be printed alongside. THIS IS NOT A NOVEL CLASS — pnl_is_trustworthy's own docstring documents the identical trap one function along ('handed a raw JSON string it reads row[pnl_source] off a str, catches the TypeError, and returns UNVERIFIED for every row. That failure is silent and total, so the decode belongs here, once, and not in each caller'). The decode was moved into that function; is_measured was left with the same footgun and no warning. A provenance filter that fails closed and silently is the dangerous direction for a module whose entire purpose is that UNVERIFIED is never folded into MEASURED: it makes a measured population read as empty, which a caller can easily report as 'no broker-truth rows exist'.
items.resolution_criteria: is_measured (and classify_row) raise TypeError, or return a distinguishable third outcome, when handed a non-mapping — NOT silently UNVERIFIED. Demonstrated by a test asserting BOTH controls: passing a real row with exit_price_source='bybit_closed_pnl' returns True (positive control), and passing the bare string 'measured' does not return False silently. A docstring warning alone does NOT close this — the sibling function already has one and this function is what a caller reaches for first.

items.title: WO-20260908-EXIT-MECHANICS-THE-TRAILING-AND-BANKING-HALF was satisfied and merged on 2026-09-08, its object file stayed lifecycle:dormant/owner:null/closed_at:null, and a fresh session was dispatched onto it the next morning on a 'never been measured' premise
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09 (MI-209). MI-188b measured the object's done_condition and it merged as PR #11351, commit 34b82575, docs/research/exit-trailing-and-banking-measurement-2026-09-08.md, on main. MI-209 was then dispatched on 2026-09-09 with a brief asserting the half 'has never been measured on the same footing' and that the operator has it 'recorded as still owed' — both false, and the brief is a faithful rendering of what the object file says. THE SHAPE IS ALREADY MEASURED IN THIS REPO ONE LEVEL UP: MI-193 (docs/research/operating-model-measurement-2026-09-08.md) measured SESSIONS.json rows at a 61.3-minute median truth-lifetime — a register whose only writer is the act of STARTING, and whose truth ends at an event nothing writes back. This is that class applied to the work store rather than the session registry, and it is worse there because the work store is what dispatch reads.
