items.title: /api/diag/log_file is tail-only and hard-capped at 1000 lines with NO offset, so a soak log is unreadable beyond its last 1000 records from any session — exit_lever_soak's 1000-record tail covers only ~25.7% of its estimated lifetime
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09 (MI-209b), evidence docs/research/exit-banking-tailcap-and-reachability-2026-09-09.md §2. get_log_file does n = _clamp(lines, _DEFAULT_LIMIT, _MAX_LIMIT) with _MAX_LIMIT = 1000 (src/web/api/routers/diag.py:1815 and :876) and reads content[-n:] — tail-only, with NO offset parameter on the route. Its sibling audit_query DOES take limit + offset, added for exactly this reason ('the time/event-filtered reader the line-capped /audit and /log_file tails cannot provide'), so the pattern exists in the same file and was simply never applied here. COVERAGE, MEASURED (size_bytes from the endpoint's own payload) AND ESTIMATED (lifetime record counts extrapolated as size / mean-record-size-of-tail; the tail's mean record size may not represent the whole file, so these are directional): exit_lever_soak 1,415,768 bytes, mean record 363 B, ~3,897 records estimated, 1000-record tail covers ~25.7%; exit_ladder_soak 656,242 bytes, mean record 633 B, ~1,036 records, tail covers ~96.5%. So the two soaks are in completely different positions and must not be spoken of as one cap. WHY IT MATTERS: a session asked to settle whether a soak-derived conclusion is tail-bound cannot do so, and must reason from coverage bounds instead of content. NO OTHER PATH REACHES IT, checked rather than assumed: the vm-diag-snapshot relay issues a path-validated curl at the same route and inherits the cap; system-actions pull-latest-logs runs scripts/ops/pull_logs.sh, which emits a FIXED bundle (status.json, heartbeat, journalctl, signal_audit tail) that contains neither soak and is truncated by the workflow to 50 KB, two orders of magnitude under a 1.4 MB file; and trainer-vm-diag runs arbitrary bash on the TRAINER, which holds a synced journal DB and not the live VM's runtime_logs/. NOT A BLOCKER ON THE BANKING QUESTION, and that must not be misread: the zero-partials result is a COMPLETE census of trades (n=5589) and order_packages (n=4500), never soak-derived, so it is not tail-bound at all.
items.resolution_criteria: GET /api/diag/log_file accepts an offset (or an explicit head/range) so a caller can page a multi-hundred-KB log to its start, mirroring audit_query's existing limit+offset. Demonstrated on exit_lever_soak by BOTH controls: a paged read reaching the file's FIRST record (positive — the record's ts predates the current 1000-record tail window, which begins 2026-08-31T12:03:15Z), and a request beyond the end returning an empty page rather than silently re-serving the tail (negative — an out-of-range page that returns the last 1000 lines is the collapsed state this row exists to prevent, and would be worse than the cap). Raising _MAX_LIMIT alone does NOT close this: it moves the ceiling without making the file pageable, and a 3,897-record file would need it raised again. Tier-2 because it changes a live-VM web-api route; not built by the filing session, which was measurement-only.

items.title: One PR closed unmerged with no recorded disposition makes EVERY reconcile-open-prs PR unmergeable, and the CI failure names `session-registry-guard`, which is not where the defect is
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09T07:20Z. #11390 was closed unmerged on 2026-09-08T14:28:18Z. `reconcile_open_prs.py` correctly MOVES it to `settled_prs[]` verbatim and stamps `terminal: closed_unmerged` -- and it CANNOT know WHY it closed, so it writes no `disposition`. `open_pr_record.py --strict` then correctly REFUSES the file: a settled row that never reached `main` with no reason recorded is lost knowledge, and `superseded` / `the operator refused it` / `the author gave up` are opposite next actions. BOTH COMPONENTS ARE BEHAVING CORRECTLY; the defect is at the seam, which is why a line-by-line read of either one comes back clean. CONSEQUENCE, stated as a population: every `automation/reconcile-open-prs-*` PR opened after that close carries the undispositioned row and fails `guards`. Confirmed on #11499 (open 41 min, guards FAIL) and #11506 (guards FAIL); #11478 is the same family. The job re-fires on every merge to main, so it GENERATES a fresh unmergeable PR per merge -- the queue grows without bound while the register it maintains goes stale. AND THE DIAGNOSTIC POINTS AT THE WRONG PLACE: the failing line reads `session-registry-guard: python3 scripts/ops/open_pr_record.py --strict exited 1`. The registry is not involved; a reader chasing the named guard looks at SESSIONS.json and finds nothing wrong. That is UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT sub-class A (the label names a quantity the code did not compute) under CLAUDE.md's own taxonomy. !! THE MERGE-SLOT DEADLOCK FIX (#11494) DID NOT COVER THIS AND MUST NOT BE READ AS HAVING DONE SO. That fix made automation PRs structurally landable and is PROVEN (#11500 self-landed 06:38:47Z). This is a CONTENT failure in one family on top of it -- a second, independent cause with the same visible symptom, which is exactly how a fixed problem gets re-declared broken or a live one gets declared fixed.
items.evidence: guards job 102366604724 (PR #11499): `PASS 53 / FAIL 1 / SKIP 38`, sole failure `session-registry-guard: scripts/ops/open_pr_record.py --strict exited 1`. Reproduced locally against #11499's OPEN-PRS.json: `settled=undispositioned -- 1 settled row(s) record an ending nobody accounted for, over 80 row(s)`, `::FINDING:: #11390`. Against main's version the same command exits 0 (`settled_graded`, 76 rows) -- the positive control, so the probe can find both answers. reconcile_open_prs.py:218 comments the move as 'every field the session wrote survives verbatim', which is what makes the remedy work at the source row rather than at the output.
items.resolution_criteria: A NEW `automation/reconcile-open-prs-*` PR is OBSERVED with `guards` GREEN, on a run whose input contained at least one closed-unmerged PR. !! A green run over a period where nothing closed unmerged clears NOTHING -- that is the condition being absent, not the defect being fixed, and it is the reading most likely to be mistaken for success. The immediate row is remedied by recording #11390's disposition on its OPEN row so the move carries it (done in this change, and PROVEN by simulating the move and re-running --strict: exit 0, `settled_graded`, 77 rows). What is NOT fixed and is the real ask: (a) nothing prompts anyone to record a disposition when a PR is closed, so the next undispositioned close reproduces this exactly; and (b) the failing line should name `open-pr-record`, not `session-registry-guard`. Both are worker-path changes (`scripts/`), so they are NOT the manager's to make.

items.title: position_telemetry still serves 12 fabricated peak_r = -1e18 rows, and BL-20260818-TELEMETRY-PEAK-R-STORES-COALESCE-SENTINEL is marked `resolved` so nobody will look again
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09T07:41Z against the live journal via GET /api/bot/db/table/position_telemetry?limit=500. POPULATION: the COMPLETE table, n=193 (193 fetched against total=193). 12 rows carry `peak_r = -1e+18` with `peak_state: thin_window`, dated 2026-08-17T15:37Z through 2026-08-24T04:07Z: avax_pullback_2h x6, mgc_trend_1h x2, slv_trend_1h, ada_pullback_2h, trend_donchian_sol_4h. The -1e18 is a SORT KEY -- it exists in the upsert so a NULL loses to any real value -- that gets persisted as though it had been OBSERVED when both sides of the MAX are NULL. THE WRITE-PATH FIX IS IN (the CASE at src/runtime/position_telemetry.py:277 keeps NULL meaning `we did not look`) BUT IT LANDED ONLY ON 2026-09-08 (commit e1d24f6), three weeks after BL-20260818-TELEMETRY-PEAK-R-STORES-COALESCE-SENTINEL was opened, AND THERE IS NO BACKFILL -- grep for a cleanup/migration over the column returns nothing. So the fix stops NEW contamination and leaves the existing 12 rows being served. CONSEQUENCE: any consumer taking MIN(peak_r) or AVG(peak_r) over this column gets a fabricated number. NOT HYPOTHETICAL -- MI-209c hit exactly this on its first pass and computed a `minimum excursion` of -1e+18 before excluding the sentinel. WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH A ROW RATHER THAN A NOTE: the parent row's status reads `resolved` at severity `high` while the contaminated data is still live and still readable through an allowlisted route, so the normal mechanism for someone re-checking it is switched off. A resolved row over unresolved data is worse than an open row, because it converts a known defect into an invisible one.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH, and they are different facts -- say which you did. (1) The 12 rows are cleaned: either peak_r set NULL (the honest value, since peak_state already reads `thin_window` = never measurable) or the rows deleted, VERIFIED by re-running the census probe and finding 0 rows below -1e6, not by reading a migration script. (2) BL-20260818-TELEMETRY-PEAK-R-STORES-COALESCE-SENTINEL is re-opened or its resolution is amended to state that it fixed the WRITE PATH ONLY and left the historical rows -- so the record stops implying the data is clean. NOT sufficient: the write-path CASE being present (that is already true and is what makes this row necessary); a passing unit test (a harness cannot reach the 12 live rows); or the rows ageing out of a tail-limited read.
items.next_step: Re-run `python3 scripts/research/partial_close_reachability.py` -- section [5] prints the sentinel count as its own figure. Then decide NULL-vs-delete for the 12 rows and amend the parent row's resolution.

items.title: position_telemetry.peak_provenance reads `estimated` on 193 of 193 rows and has never once read `measured`, so any excursion claim restricted to broker truth is the empty set
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09T07:41Z via GET /api/bot/db/table/position_telemetry?limit=500. POPULATION: the COMPLETE table, n=193 (193 fetched against total=193). peak_provenance distribution is {'estimated': 193} -- ZERO `measured`, zero `fabricated`, zero `unverified`. THE FIELD EXISTS PRECISELY SO A CONSUMER CAN RESTRICT TO BROKER TRUTH (src/runtime/provenance.py: MEASURED / ESTIMATED / FABRICATED / UNVERIFIED are four different facts and UNVERIFIED is never folded into MEASURED). On this table that restriction yields nothing, so the restriction cannot be applied -- which is the shape MI-209 hit one day earlier on the trades table, where applying the same restriction REVERSED one of MI-188b's headlines. CONSEQUENCE: every excursion-derived statement in the repo -- peak_r, giveback_r, pct_of_cap, and anything downstream that grades active management off them -- rests on ESTIMATED data with no measured control to check it against. THIS IS NOT A BUG IN A LINE OF CODE. It is the instrument having never produced its trusted grade, which is exactly the class CY-20260906-TRADING-TRUTH exists to catch: a verdict computed from an uncalibrated instrument is worse than no verdict because it gets acted on. NOT A CLAIM THAT THE NUMBERS ARE WRONG -- estimated is a legitimate grade and may be the best obtainable for an intra-trade excursion. The claim is that nobody has established WHETHER a measured grade is reachable here, and until someone does, the confidence attached to excursion-based decisions is unbounded.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) at least one row is OBSERVED carrying peak_provenance = `measured`, with the path that produced it named -- read from the live table, not from a test; OR (b) a RECORDED decision that a measured excursion grade is not obtainable for this instrument, stating WHY (e.g. intra-trade excursion needs a tick feed the fleet does not store), so that every downstream consumer can be told once that ESTIMATED is the ceiling rather than each re-deriving it. Deciding (b) is legitimate and must be recorded AS a decision rather than left looking like work in flight. NOT sufficient: the field being populated (it already is, uniformly); a harness that constructs a measured row; or widening the population until a measured row appears from some other table.
items.next_step: Read src/runtime/trail_decay.py (PEAK_MEASURED / PEAK_THIN_WINDOW / unanchored) and establish whether the `measured` branch is reachable at all on the fleet's current candle cadence, or whether it is dead by construction.

items.title: turtle_soup's `execution: shadow` block says it `logs packages for data`, but it is routed to 0 of 11 accounts so it has logged nothing for 70 days -- the stated benefit of the demote is not being realised
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09T07:44Z. FIELD BEATS COMMENT. config/strategies.yaml:52 sets turtle_soup `execution: shadow` (Tier-3, operator-approved 2026-07-07) and its comment states the rationale: `logs packages for data, never sends a live order on ANY account/symbol` -- i.e. the demote deliberately KEEPS the data-collection half. src/core/coordinator.py:1349 implements exactly that: a shadow strategy is forced effective_dry but still logs its order package. BUT THE STRATEGY NEVER RUNS AT ALL, because it is routed to NO ACCOUNT. Read against the LIVE /api/bot/config (as_of 2026-09-09T07:44:46Z, not the YAML): turtle_soup appears in the `strategies` roster of 0 of 11 accounts. POSITIVE CONTROL on the same probe: trend_donchian -> 3 accounts (bybit_1, bybit_2, bybit_portfolio), ict_scalp_5m -> 1, so the zero is real and not a broken roster read. It was de-routed from bybit_1 on 2026-07-01 (config/accounts.yaml:159) and from ib_paper on 2026-07-07 (config/accounts.yaml:600). CONSEQUENCE, as a population: turtle_soup has 3 order_packages in the COMPLETE census of 4500, the most recent dated 2026-07-01T13:39:56Z -- ZERO packages in the 70 days since. The routing change (07-01) and the shadow demote (07-07) were made a week apart and the second one's comment describes a world the first one had already ended. NOTHING IS BROKEN AND NO MONEY IS AT RISK -- both changes were correct and operator-approved. The defect is that the config now DOCUMENTS a data-collection behaviour that cannot occur, so a future session reading it will believe turtle_soup is accruing shadow data and reason from a corpus that does not exist. items.title: The `why has no partial ever banked` question was answered on 2026-09-08 and re-dispatched as open work twice since, because a landed result does not close its own object
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09. MI-188b answered this on 2026-09-08 in docs/research/exit-trailing-and-banking-measurement-2026-09-08.md section 3 -- it names the sole emitter (turtle_soup.py:537), reports turtle_soup's 3 rows, states it never opened a position, and lists four gates including `execution: shadow` and the bybit-only partial_close capability. It LANDED (PR #11351, 34b82575). MI-209 (2026-09-09) re-confirmed the zero and OPENED ITS OWN WRITEUP by reporting that ITS dispatch premise was stale for the same reason -- its object still read `lifecycle: dormant`, `owner: null`, `closed_at: null` after the work had landed. MI-209c (this row) was then dispatched on 2026-09-09 to `establish why it has never fired`, with a brief asserting the question was still standing. IT WAS NOT. Roughly two thirds of MI-209c was re-derivation. THIS IS NOT A COMPLAINT ABOUT A BRIEF -- the mechanism is structural and is already diagnosed in MI-209: the work register's only writer is the act of STARTING, so an object's truth ends at an event nothing writes back. The new fact this row adds is the RECURRENCE and its rate: three units on the same subject in two days, two of them wholly or partly redundant, each one INDEPENDENTLY rediscovering that its own premise was stale. A defect that reproduces on consecutive days at a 2-in-3 rate is a cadence, not an incident. AND THE COST COMPOUNDS IN THE WRONG DIRECTION: each redundant unit lands a further document, so the corpus a future session must read before it can tell whether a question is open grows every time the question is wrongly re-asked. ADDITIONALLY, MI-209c's own dispatched object (WO-20260909-THE-PARTIAL-CLOSE-PRODUCER-IS-BUILT-AND) DID NOT EXIST when the lane was dispatched -- absent from origin/main at ba5fccc -- and landed at e9754ca (PR #11511) only PART-WAY THROUGH the work. CORRECTED IN FLIGHT: the object is real and its done_condition matches what the prompt quoted, so the contract did not move. The defect is the ORDER: a lane was told to read an object as its contract before that object was created, so for most of the unit there was nothing to read and the prompt's paraphrase was the only contract. That is survivable here only because the paraphrase happened to be faithful -- which is luck, not a mechanism.
items.resolution_criteria: A dispatch cannot assert a question is open without a check that could have said otherwise. Concretely, EITHER (a) closing an object is mechanised -- the act of LANDING a PR that references an object writes back its closure, so `dormant`/`owner: null` stops being the resting state of finished work; OR (b) the spawn path verifies the object EXISTS and is not already answered before a lane is dispatched, and a missing object is a refusal rather than something the lane discovers and works around. NOT sufficient: a note in a doc telling sessions to check first -- MI-209 already did check first, correctly, and the question was still re-dispatched the next day, which is the evidence that a prose instruction does not carry this. NOT sufficient either: closing these three objects by hand, which fixes the instances and not the cadence.

items.title: The merge_slot is claimed before every merge and released after none, so the slot a session finds held is almost always a ghost and displacing it is the normal path rather than the exception
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09 between 07:40Z and 08:05Z, by one session that had to take the slot twice in 25 minutes. THREE CONSECUTIVE SPENT CLAIMS were observed, which is the whole population of claims in that window -- not a sample. (1) session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj claimed at 07:40:10Z for claude/mgr-dispatch-lane2-refill-20260909; its PR #11511 MERGED at 07:42:51Z (read via pull_request_read, merged: true) and the slot was never cleared. (2) session_01DUBXxiaZ3PMERcAfcJce7P then claimed for claude/document-index-write-second-instance to land PR #11513, which merged as d9059a0 -- also never cleared. (3) THAT claim's own purpose text records it displacing ITS OWN spent claim from PR #11508 (merged as da6c2b89), and says verbatim `Displace freely; per check_pr_landing.py's own docstring R13 does not serialize.` THE PROTOCOL SAYS `Mirror the claim here before merge, clear after (merged or aborted)`. The before half happens every time because check_pr_landing R13 REFUSES to let a branch arm without it -- a mechanism. The after half is carried by nothing at all: no guard, no workflow, no hook. So the field is monotonically stale by construction, and `held_by` reads as a live holder when it is a merged one. THIS IS NOT A SAFETY DEFECT AND MUST NOT BE FILED AS ONE: concurrent-merge safety rests on branch-protection required status checks, and R13's own docstring is explicit that it records an ATTRIBUTABLE claim and does NOT serialize. The defect is that the surface reads as coordination while providing none, and the cost is per-session friction plus a judgement call every claimant must make alone: a session that respects the stale claim WAITS FOREVER on a merged PR, and one that displaces it cannot tell from the field whether it just cut in front of live work. Both failure modes were live in this window -- this session first WITHDREW its arming pair and queued behind claim (1) before establishing that (1) was spent, which is exactly the wasted wait. AND THE DISPLACEMENT NOTE IS THE ONLY THING CARRYING THE TRUTH: claim (2) is legible only because that session wrote its reasoning into a free-text `purpose`, which nothing requires and nothing reads. ⚠️ ESCALATED 2026-09-09T09:10Z, AND THE ESCALATION CHANGES THE DIAGNOSIS FROM MANNERS TO ARITHMETIC. The count reached SIX, and the sixth displaced claim is NOT A SESSION: it is `github-actions[bot] - work-digest run 34332233675` for automation/work-digest-34332233675-1 (PR #11523, already merged as 884819d), whose own purpose reads `arming auto-merge IS the merge, so R13 takes the slot here`. .github/actions/commit-to-main writes the claim on EVERY automated commit to main and 27 workflows call it, so the slot is rewritten MECHANICALLY at the rate main moves -- no session forgetting is required and none can be asked to stop. MEASURED, over the COMPLETE set of 17 merges to origin/main between 07:04:53Z and 09:05:29Z (16 inter-merge gaps): median gap 7.1 min, MAXIMUM gap 14.1 min. The binding CI check on a human-lane PR here (pytest-run) takes ~19 min, measured at 18.6/18.9/18.8 min across three consecutive runs of PR #11514. So ZERO of 16 gaps were long enough for one CI cycle to complete. A PR holding the slot therefore CANNOT converge by merging main: every cycle is guaranteed to be interrupted by a merge that regenerates the conflict it just resolved. That is not bad luck and it is not a busy afternoon -- it is a self-sustaining loop, and it means this row is BLOCKING rather than cosmetic. Option (a) of the resolution criteria -- clearing the slot from commit-to-main, which already writes it -- is the fix that also ends the loop. Live exhibit: PR #11514 went CI-green three separate times (3acdd20, 950c1c1, ce9aed2) and was re-conflicted on this one line each time.
items.resolution_criteria: The release is carried by a MECHANISM, not by remembering. EITHER (a) the slot is cleared automatically when the claiming branch's PR merges or closes -- the natural home is .github/actions/commit-to-main or the automerge workflow, which already know the branch and already write this file, and the check is that a slot naming a MERGED PR is OBSERVED going to null without a session doing it by hand; OR (b) reads of the slot are made self-dating -- the claim carries its PR number and any consumer resolves that PR's state, so `held_by` set against a merged PR renders as SPENT rather than as held, and a session never has to make the judgement call alone. NOT sufficient: clearing the three claims named above by hand (that fixes the instances, not the cadence); a doc line telling sessions to release after merging (the before-half is enforced by a guard and the after-half by prose, which is precisely the asymmetry that produced this); or arguing it is harmless because branch protection is the real safety net -- that is TRUE and is already stated in the detail, and it is an argument for fixing or RETIRING the field, not for leaving it reading as something it is not. ⚠️ IF THE OPERATOR OR THE MANAGER DECIDES the durable mirror is not worth repairing, this row does NOT clear -- it CHANGES: the mirror is then decoratively stale by decision, which is legitimate and must be RECORDED as one, with the consequence stated (every claimant displaces a ghost and the field must not be read as who is merging).

items.title: The manager held each landing PR until the previous one merged, believing R13 serialised the merge slot -- its own docstring says in bold that it does NOT
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09T08:03Z. check_pr_landing.py's module docstring reads, verbatim and emphasised: 'R13 DOES NOT SERIALIZE, and nothing here should be read as claiming it does. Per BL-20260810-MERGE-SLOT-MIRROR-UNWRITABLE-PRE-MERGE, merge_slot lives in a committed file, so a claim written on a branch reaches no other session until that branch MERGES -- by which point the claim is over. Two branches can each arm, each write a valid claim, and never see one another.' What R13 buys is an ATTRIBUTABLE, TIMESTAMPED claim, and that arming with none (or with someone else's) fails CI. THE MANAGER BELIEVED THE OPPOSITE FOR A FULL SESSION and sequenced on it: each landing PR was held until the previous merged, on the stated reasoning 'R13 serialises the merge slot -- one landing PR at a time'. Cost, stated as a population: five sequential session-board merge-conflict resolutions on 2026-09-09 (#11505, #11509, #11511, #11515 twice), each a full merge-resolve-guard-push cycle, plus lane PRs held behind manager PRs that never needed to wait. WHY THE BELIEF SURVIVED CONTACT WITH EVIDENCE: the file conflicts are REAL -- two branches both editing merge_slot in one committed file DO collide in git -- so every observation was consistent with serialisation and the wrong model was confirmed rather than tested. A git conflict on a shared file is not a mutual-exclusion guarantee, and the two are easy to mistake for each other. It was corrected only because ANOTHER session (lane 3) wrote the disproof into its own slot claim on main -- 'per check_pr_landing.py's own docstring R13 does not serialize' -- where a third party happened to read it. Nothing in the workflow would otherwise have surfaced it.
items.evidence: scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py lines 62-72 (the docstring quoted above) and line 596, whose failure text says the claim 'does NOT serialize -- a committed claim reaches no other session'. The contradicting manager belief is recorded verbatim in this session's own PR bodies and commit messages across #11505, #11509, #11511 and #11515.
items.resolution_criteria: TWO PARTS, and the first alone is the reminder-is-not-a-mechanism non-fix this repo has already paid for. (1) The manager cadence prompt and any manager-facing doc that describes the merge queue state R13's actual property -- attributable claim, NOT mutual exclusion -- so a successor does not re-derive the wrong model from observed file conflicts. (2) The real fix the docstring itself names: a slot store NOT gated on merging, so a claim is visible to other live sessions before its branch lands (that row's option (a), and the same artifact MI-182 needs). Until (2) exists, concurrent-merge safety rests on branch-protection required status checks, where the docstring says it already rested -- so this is a COORDINATION-VISIBILITY gap, not a safety one, and must not be described as the latter. NOT SUFFICIENT: a session asserting it now understands R13. The observable is that two manager PRs are armed concurrently and both land without either being held for the other.

items.title: The manager lease's liveness is coupled to the repo being GREEN: a base-branch red blocks every PR, including the one carrying the heartbeat, so an alive-and-working manager's lease expires
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09T08:05:10Z. `manager_lease.py status` on a freshly pulled main reads heartbeat_at=2026-09-09T07:34:57Z, TTL 90 min, so the lease expires 09:04:57Z. The manager had heartbeated THREE more times since (07:46:27, 07:54:48, 07:56:42) and every one of them is trapped in PR #11515, which cannot merge because `check_trainer_capture_watch` is red on CLEAN MAIN. So the lease of a session that is alive, working and heartbeating on cadence will lapse on the record, and another session reading `origin` would find it claimable. THE COUPLING NOBODY DESIGNED: the lease lives in the repo precisely so it survives its holder's DEATH and is readable by a session arriving COLD -- correct, and the reason it cannot be session state. But that makes its refresh a MERGE, and a merge is gated on the repo being green. Lease liveness therefore depends on CI health, which is a completely unrelated property. ⚠️ THIS IS NOT THE 2026-09-07 CLASS AND MUST NOT BE FILED AS A RECURRENCE OF IT. That one is PACING: a heartbeat is stamped when its PR opens and merges ~60 min later, so it reaches main two-thirds through its own TTL and any slip expires it. The fix there is to merge sooner, and a send_later check-in addresses it. THIS one is not fixable by pacing at all -- when every PR is blocked, no heartbeat can land however promptly it is opened. Conflating them would make the wrong fix look sufficient. ⚠️ AND THE DANGEROUS REMEDY IS THE OBVIOUS ONE. The tempting move is to disable or bypass the failing guard so the heartbeat can land. That is exactly the 'skip a test to get green' failure this repo forbids, made attractive by a deadline. It must not be done, and naming it here is part of the row.
items.evidence: `manager_lease.py status` on main at 08:05:10Z: state=held_fresh, heartbeat_at=2026-09-09T07:34:57Z (landed via #11511), claimable=False, 30 min elapsed of a 90 min TTL. `scripts/ci/check_trainer_capture_watch.py` exits 1 on a clean main checkout ('newest recorded run is 15.1h old, window 15h') -- reproduced against clean main, not inferred from a PR. PR #11515 carries the three later heartbeats and is red on that guard. Root of the red: the refreshed receipt exists in automation PR #11488, itself unmergeable (BL-20260909-A-PR-CLOSED-UNMERGED-WITH-NO-RECORDED-DISPOSITION-BLOCKS-EVERY-RECONCILE-PR-AND-THE-FAILURE-NAMES-THE-WRONG-GUARD is a sibling cause in the same automation-landing family).
items.resolution_criteria: A manager heartbeat can reach `main` while `main` is red on a guard unrelated to the lease -- OBSERVED, not argued. Candidate designs, and the row does not pick one: (a) the lease file lands through a path that is not gated on the full guard set, the way receipts do; (b) the lease TTL is suspended, with the reason recorded, while main is red, so the register says 'could not refresh' rather than silently reading expired -- the three-state discipline this repo uses everywhere else, since `expired` and `could not refresh` are different facts and only one of them means nobody is managing; or (c) a slot/lease store not gated on merging at all, which is the same artifact `check_pr_landing.py`'s R13 docstring says the real-time half needs. ⚠️ NOT ACCEPTABLE AS A FIX: disabling, skipping or bypassing the failing guard to let a heartbeat through, or widening the TTL so the problem is less likely to be hit. Widening hides the coupling rather than removing it and makes the eventual failure rarer and more surprising. ⚠️ A green repo does NOT clear this row -- that is the condition being absent, not the coupling being removed, and it is the reading most likely to be mistaken for a fix.

items.title: Nothing PREVENTS a file that decides whether the operator is paged from shipping with no diag read surface — this is the recurrence half of a FIFTH instance, and its only written carrier is a row already marked `resolved`
items.why_filed_now: FILED DELIBERATELY BY A CLOSING-ONLY SESSION, AND THAT NEEDS ITS JUSTIFICATION STATED. This session's bound was CLOSING ONLY, with one exception: a new row where closing one reveals a genuinely new class. This is that case, and the class is not new — what is new is that it has NO OPEN CARRIER. BL-20260901-OPERATOR-ALERTS-HAS-NO-READ-SURFACE carried two criteria: (A) INSTANCE and (B) CLASS. (A) was satisfied and verified today, so the row closed. (B) — 'the durable fix is a guard, not another allowlist entry' — was NOT satisfied. Its natural home is BL-20260825-ALERT-AND-CADENCE-STATE-FILES-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE, which is ALREADY `resolved` while its own criterion 3 reads, verbatim, 'NOT DONE, and the honest gap: nothing PREVENTS the sixth occurrence.' So closing (A) without filing this would have deleted the only live statement of the class from the open register, leaving it recorded solely inside a resolved row nobody enumerating open work will read. That is the written-and-never-read failure this repo keeps paying for, and it would have been CAUSED by a drain session tidying up.
items.detail: THE CLASS: a module writes a runtime_logs file whose contents decide whether an operator is PAGED (an alert latch) or how long a safety input may AGE (a cadence marker), and that file gets no entry in src/web/api/routers/diag.py::_LOG_FILES. It is then unreachable from any relay-bound session, so 'the mechanism stopped firing' and 'it fired and the condition persists' are indistinguishable from every surface — including from the reviews meant to catch it. RECORDED INSTANCES, five: exit_loop_health (#8778), the five latches swept in BL-20260825 (which was itself already the third instance), operator_alerts (BL-20260901, closed today). WHY THE EXISTING GUARD CANNOT COVER IT, quoting BL-20260825's own criterion 3 rather than re-deriving: tests/test_diag_log_file_allowlist_coherence.py checks allowlist-vs-CLAUDE.md, so it 'only fires once a name is already allowlisted — it cannot see a writer that never got an entry, which is the actual failure mode all three times.' MEASURED TODAY, so the class is sized rather than asserted: the allowlist holds 57 names; I probed 46 of them live and 44 returned present:true. The two absent are strategy_builder_exception_alert_state and daily_cap_alert_state. That is the population the guard would have to reason about, and it shows the allowlist is mostly healthy — the gap is entry, not upkeep.
items.resolution_criteria: A CI guard fails when a module under src/ writes a runtime_logs/*_state.json or *_alerts.jsonl path that has no _LOG_FILES entry, unless the writer carries an explicit `# read-surface: none - <reason>` marker. THREE REQUIREMENTS, each from a mistake this repo has already made and none of them optional: (1) THE MARKER MUST BE VERIFIED, NOT PRESENCE-ONLY — it must name something checkable, because new-table-wiring-guard's presence-only `# data-wiring:` marker made the cheapest way to silence a real finding be to name a table that does not exist, and a guard cheaper to lie to than to satisfy is worse than no guard. (2) IT MUST SHIP WITH A SELF-TEST PROVING IT FAILS on a planted writer with no allowlist entry — a guard whose failure path has never executed is a deploy, not a check. (3) IT MUST STATE ITS DENOMINATOR: how many writer sites it scanned, so a guard that silently stops matching (a renamed path helper, a new write idiom) reads as a shrinking population rather than as continued green. ⚠️ NOT SUFFICIENT: adding another name to _LOG_FILES. That is what was done all five times, and it is why there were five. ⚠️ NOT SUFFICIENT: extending the allowlist-vs-CLAUDE.md coherence test, which by construction cannot see an unlisted writer.
related: BL-20260825-ALERT-AND-CADENCE-STATE-FILES-SHIP-WITHOUT-A-READ-SURFACE (resolved; carries this as its unbuilt criterion 3)
BL-20260901-OPERATOR-ALERTS-HAS-NO-READ-SURFACE (closed 2026-09-09 on criterion (A); this row is its criterion (B))
BL-20260813-NO-GUARD-FOR-ENV-READ-SURFACE (the SAME shape one register over — env vars vs get_env.py ALLOWED_KEYS; a single guard design may serve both, and they should be read together)
