What changed is that the work is now CARRIED by MI-216 and MI-217 rather than by a proposal nothing pointed at.

items.summary: scripts/check_soak_doctrine.py is the CI guard for the 'Promotion evidence - offline edge, live mechanics' rule, and the M7 strategy-review packet contradicted that rule for at least 8 consecutive days without the guard firing once. MEASURED 2026-09-09: the guard file exists (5643 bytes) and contains ZERO textual references to 'strategy_review' or 'MIN_CLOSED' (grep -c = 0). STATE THE LIMIT OF THAT MEASUREMENT HONESTLY: zero textual references establishes that the guard does not NAME the packet; it does not by itself establish that no code path reaches it. Establish which before writing the fix, and report a POSITIVE CONTROL - show the guard firing on a planted violation - because a guard that is silent because it scans nothing is indistinguishable from a guard that is silent because everything passes. That distinction is the whole point. WHY THIS IS THE MORE IMPORTANT OF THE PAIR: the operator has now explained the offline-edge rule to multiple sessions ('I don't know how many more times I can explain this to various cluades'), which is the signal that PROSE HAS FAILED and the prevention must be executable. A rule with a guard that does not cover the surface where the rule is broken is worse than an unguarded rule, because the green guard reads as compliance.
items.resolution_criteria: check_soak_doctrine.py is OBSERVED failing on a PLANTED violation on the strategy-review surface -- a positive control -- and passing once it is removed. ⚠️ A GREEN RUN CLEARS NOTHING HERE: green is the state the guard has been in for the entire eight days the rule was being contradicted, so 'the guard passes' is the symptom, not the evidence. ⚠️ AND FIRST ESTABLISH WHETHER IT REACHES THE SURFACE AT ALL: the measured fact is zero TEXTUAL references to strategy_review or MIN_CLOSED, which is not the same as no code path reaching it. Report which of the two you established.
items.tier: 3 — Tier-3 where it changes what a KILL/DEMOTE verdict rests on; the guard half is Tier-1
items.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-09-09 by MI-215. BOTH clauses met, and the answer to the 'which of the two' question is the STRONGER one: the guard did not merely fail to NAME the packet -- NO CODE PATH REACHED IT. Established by reading all 132 lines of scripts/check_soak_doctrine.py, not by grep: it opens exactly three paths (docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md, .claude/skills/new-strategy/SKILL.md, .claude/skills/backtesting/SKILL.md) and no other path opens any other file. POSITIVE CONTROL OBSERVED against the real scripts/ml/strategy_review_packet.py: an 8th accrual-gated branch was planted using a NEW variable name (`trades_banked = headline.n_closed`, a name in no seed list) -> guard exit 1, 'SOAK-DOCTRINE GUARD FAILED', naming 'line 1137 (decide, reads: trades_banked)' and 8-vs-7 against the ledger; plant removed -> exit 0. The packet file was restored byte-identical (`git diff` empty), so the Tier-3 surface was never changed. That it caught an ALIAS is what proves it is a detector and not a keyword matcher -- the real gate already does `n = headline.n_closed`, so a textual check would have missed six of its seven branches. WHAT SHIPPED: check D in scripts/check_soak_doctrine.py (AST, alias closure to a fixpoint, flags any if/elif whose test reads live/calendar accrual and whose body assigns a verdict), a ratchet ledger at docs/claude/soak-doctrine-exceptions.json (exact count 7; one more fails as a new violation, one fewer as a stale ledger, and the entry's backlog_row is VERIFIED against a real row), and tests/test_soak_doctrine_guard.py (12 tests) so the observation outlives this session. NOT CLEARED BY THIS ROW: the seven live branches themselves -- that repair is Tier-3 and is proposed in docs/design/strategy-leg-offline-edge-basis-PROPOSAL.md, tracked by BL-20260909-STRATEGY-REVIEW-PACKET-GRADES-EDGE-OFF-A-LIVE-WINDOW-WHICH-THE-PROMOTION-EVIDENCE-RULE-FORBIDS, which stays OPEN.

items.summary: check_manager_scope.py R2 admits a manager commit to docs/claude/session-board.json for EXACTLY one thing: a `merge_slot` claim naming the branch being landed. It cannot express a RELEASE (held_by -> null). OBSERVED 2026-09-09: the manager wrote a release after #11524 merged and R2 refused it with 'merge_slot.branch is None, not this branch'. So a manager who has finished landing has only two moves, and both are bad: leave a STALE claim naming a merged branch, or violate R2. THE STALE-CLAIM BRANCH IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL AND IT HAS A MEASURED COST: earlier the same day the slot sat held for claude/mgr-dispatch-lane2-refill-20260909 for ~25 minutes after its PR #11511 had merged, and lane 2 had to announce and DISPLACE it before it could land #11514. That lane handled it correctly, which is the point - the cost landed on someone else. ⚠️ THIS IS A GAP IN THE CARVE-OUT, NOT AN ARGUMENT TO WIDEN R2. Releasing is a LANDING act by exactly the same reasoning that admits the claim, so the narrow fix is to admit a transition to a null/released slot BY THE SESSION THAT HOLDS IT - never a general permission to write session-board.json, which would re-open the hole the carve-out exists to close. ⚠️ AND NOTE THE MITIGATION THAT ALREADY EXISTS, so this is not urgent: R13 does not serialize (its own docstring says so) and slots are displaced freely, so a stale claim delays rather than blocks. Entry point: scripts/ci/check_manager_scope.py R2, the merge_slot carve-out.
items.resolution_criteria: check_manager_scope.py is OBSERVED passing a manager commit that sets merge_slot.held_by to null where the PRIOR value on origin/main named that same session, AND still FAILING a commit that writes any other session-board.json key or another branch's claim - both halves demonstrated, since a fix that only relaxes is a widening. ⚠️ A manager simply stopping writing releases does NOT clear this: that is the stale-claim branch of the same defect, and its cost is paid by the next session rather than by the manager.

items.tier: 1 — process/prose discipline; the fix is how briefs and guards are written
items.summary: OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-09, verbatim: "you keep adding guards in the shape of forbidding questions from being asked - this is incorrect. the problem isn't the question, it's the underlying misunderstanding of infra and processes, and not asking questions isn't what fixes that - it just makes it more likely that you will f****** again in the future because you're not asking the right question. so when I'm upset about isn't that you're asking the same question over and over again. it's that you don't understand how the system works. that's what we need to fix here, not the question". INSTANCE: the manager's MI-215 dispatch brief and checklist note read 'DO NOT RE-ASK THE WINDOW/FLOOR QUESTION IN ANY FORM'. The same session had, hours earlier, put a four-option decision to the operator in which ALL FOUR options rested on a false model of how this system establishes evidence — and then 'prevented' the recurrence by banning the question rather than by conveying the model. WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A NO-OP: a question-ban removes the one signal that a session does not understand something, so the misunderstanding survives and surfaces later as a DIFFERENT wrong action that nobody saw coming. It also trains sessions not to surface the very confusions the operator most wants surfaced. THE CORRECT SHAPES, all of which this repo already uses elsewhere: (a) enforce the RULE the misunderstanding violates (here: a gate producing a STRATEGY verdict must source edge from offline evidence) rather than a phrase; (b) make the SURFACE state the basis of its own output, the diagnostic-provenance discipline; (c) put the MODEL in the brief so a session can reason from it and disagree with it. ⚠️ NOTE THE LEGITIMATE NEIGHBOUR AND DO NOT OVER-CORRECT INTO IT: constraining an ACTION with its reason stated ('propose, never enact'; 'do not restore the pre-2026-08-14 flat bail, because the static DD floor binds while flat') is NOT this defect — it is a tier rule or a stated hazard, and it explains itself. The defect is specifically forbidding an INQUIRY.
items.resolution_criteria: A dispatch brief or checklist note authored AFTER 2026-09-09 is OBSERVED conveying the MODEL a session needs (and inviting it to be challenged) in place of a ban on asking, on a topic where a previous brief used the ban form — cite both, so the change of shape is visible rather than asserted. ⚠️ THIS DOES NOT CLEAR ON A PROMISE OR ON THIS ROW BEING FILED: filing a row about writing better prose is itself the weakest possible response, and the operator's point is that prose reminders have already failed here. ⚠️ NOR does the absence of the phrase 'do not ask' clear it — a brief can forbid an inquiry without those words. ⚠️ AND IF A SESSION IS OBSERVED ASKING A QUESTION THE OLD FORM WOULD HAVE SUPPRESSED, AND THAT QUESTION WAS A GOOD ONE, record it here — that is the positive evidence this row exists to collect.

items.tier: 1 — a measurement; any fix it implies is scoped separately
items.summary: OPERATOR-RAISED 2026-09-09: "our overall operation is clearly not built to suit the system's structure". The system establishes EDGE offline (the backtesting infrastructure) and uses live data for MECHANICS. The operating layer around it repeatedly assumes the opposite — that live outcomes accrue until a verdict becomes possible. The M7 strategy-review packet is ONE confirmed instance (MI-215): it withholds all 52 verdicts for want of live in-window closes. ⚠️ THE POINT OF THIS ROW IS THAT NOBODY HAS COUNTED THE OTHERS, and one instance is not a population. Candidate surfaces to CHECK, not to assume: promotion/demotion gates, the soak framing throughout OPEN-ITEMS.json clears_when texts, `days_to_grade` style horizon reporting, the review skills' own rubrics, `snoozed_until` accrual rows in the backlogs, and any `MIN_*` / `*_MIN_N` constant applied to a LIVE window. For each: does it decide EDGE or MECHANICS, and does it require calendar time to reach a verdict? ⚠️ STATE THE POPULATION AND CARRY A POSITIVE CONTROL — a probe that finds nothing must be shown able to find the known instance (the M7 packet) first, or its silence means nothing. ⚠️ THIS IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A LICENCE TO CHANGE GATES. Report the count and the list; each fix is its own scoped decision, and anything touching what a promotion or KILL rests on is Tier-3. ⚠️ FILING NOTE: an earlier wording of this row's exit condition tripped `accrual-clock guard`, which matches the word 'accrual' and demanded an `accrual_legs` list. That was a FALSE POSITIVE of the narrow kind that module's own comment says it wants to avoid — this row waits on a COUNT, not on trades — and it is a hazard specific to a row whose SUBJECT is calendar-accrual assumptions. Resolved the way the guard itself prescribes, by re-stating the exit condition as the measurement it really is, NOT by adding a fake leg list or weakening the guard. Recorded here so the next author of such a row does not read the failure as their row being wrong.
items.resolution_criteria: A COUNT is reported of operating-layer surfaces that require CALENDAR TIME to pass before an EDGE verdict becomes possible, with the classifier stated, the population defined, and a positive control demonstrating the probe finds the known M7 strategy-review instance. ⚠️ A LIST WITH NO DENOMINATOR DOES NOT CLEAR THIS — 'we found some' is the state it is already in. ⚠️ ZERO IS AN ACCEPTABLE ANSWER ONLY WITH THE POSITIVE CONTROL SHOWN, since the M7 instance is known to exist and a probe that misses it is broken. ⚠️ THIS ROW WAITS ON A MEASUREMENT, NOT ON TRADES — nothing here is gated on live outcomes arriving, and it must not be re-worded into something that is. ⚠️ AND IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES THE MISMATCH IS ACCEPTABLE where it is found, this row does not clear — it CHANGES: that is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one rather than left looking like an audit about to happen.

items.summary: scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py::HOLD_REASONS is a closed set of five, and none of them expresses the case R5 itself produces most often for a Tier-1 PR: work that IS Tier-1 by docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md § Permission Tiers ('Docs, tests, CI, tooling') but touches a path TIER1_SURFACE does not enumerate, so the guard declines to CERTIFY it and directs the author to `landing: "hold"`. Hit 2026-09-09 by MI-215 (PR #11529) on scripts/check_soak_doctrine.py: TIER1_SURFACE lists scripts/ci/**, scripts/ops/**, scripts/research/** and scripts/reports/**, but NOT the scripts/ root, where check_soak_doctrine.py, check_provenance_consumers.py and check_diagnostic_provenance.py all live. The author must then pick `tier_2_3_needs_approval`, whose own description reads 'Tier-2/Tier-3 work' -- so the typed reason contradicts the `tier: 1` field two lines above it. ⚠️ THE HARM IS TO THE TYPED VOCABULARY, NOT TO THIS PR. R7's docstring says the closed set exists so 'a hold is a stated KIND of hold and not an adjective', mirroring the operator_decision discipline in OPEN-PRS.json. A token routinely used to mean something other than what it says is exactly the drift that discipline prevents, and it degrades quietly: every such PR reads afterwards as Tier-2/3 work awaiting approval when it was Tier-1 awaiting a certification the guard could not give.
items.detail: TWO CANDIDATE FIXES, deliberately not applied here -- MI-215 declined to relocate its own guard to clear R5, on the grounds that moving a file so a landing check will certify it is changing code to get green. (a) Add a sixth reason, e.g. `path_outside_tier1_surface`, VERIFIED against the diff the way R8 verifies changes_landing_machinery -- it must fail if no changed path is actually outside TIER1_SURFACE, or it becomes a free excuse, which is the presence-only trap R8's own comment names. (b) Add `scripts/*.py` (the guard scripts at the repo scripts root) to TIER1_SURFACE. ⚠️ (b) IS THE WIDER CHANGE AND SHOULD NOT BE TAKEN AS THE OBVIOUS ONE: the scripts/ root is not exclusively CI guards, and TIER1_SURFACE's whole documented polarity is that an unrecognised path must fail closed rather than arm. Widening it to a directory whose contents are not uniformly Tier-1 trades that property away for convenience. NOT MEASURED: how many PRs have taken this route -- establishing whether this is a recurring shape or a one-off needs a count over the pr-landing declarations on main, with tier:1 + hold_reason:tier_2_3_needs_approval as the probe and a positive control that the probe can find a genuine Tier-2/3 hold.
items.resolution_criteria: A pr-landing declaration is OBSERVED on main whose Tier-1-on-an-uncertifiable-path hold carries a typed reason that MEANS that -- i.e. the `tier` field and the `hold_reason` no longer contradict each other -- read off the committed .github/pr-landing/*.json, not from the guard source. ⚠️ A GREEN pr-landing RUN CLEARS NOTHING: green is the current state, reached precisely BY writing the mismatched token. ⚠️ AND IF A NEW REASON IS ADDED IT MUST BE VERIFIED AGAINST THE DIFF (the R8 pattern) -- an unverified sixth reason is a free excuse and makes this worse, not better; a version that passes with no changed path outside TIER1_SURFACE does not clear this row. ⚠️ IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES the mismatch is acceptable, this row does not clear -- it CHANGES, and must be recorded as a decision that `tier_2_3_needs_approval` is the sanctioned catch-all, so the next reader is not left inferring a tier from a token that does not mean it.

items.tier: 2 — order path adjacent (the fix is a ping, not a sizing change)
items.title: A prop account blocked from trading by a stale balance stops trading with NO operator-facing signal — the refusal is journaled and logged, and the ping that exists for exactly this is on a different branch
items.detail: READ THE CODE, NOT THIS SENTENCE, BEFORE ACTING — the two branches are 800 lines apart and look alike. src/core/coordinator.py::multi_account_execute sizes before it executes. For a prop account the sizing branch (~line 1687) calls src.prop.prop_balance.prop_sizing_balance, which returns state 'stale' once the operator's snapshot is older than PROP_STATUS_REQUEST_MAX_AGE_HOURS, and raises RuntimeError(refusal_message(...)) — a good message that names exactly what the operator should send. The except at ~line 1708 calls log_rejection_to_journal(...) + logger.exception(...) AND NOTHING ELSE. _emit_execution_failure_ping — the operator-facing diagnostic that exists so the operator sees missing-creds / 'exchange rejected' / 'account paused' without grepping journalctl — is on the LATER execute_pkg branch (~line 2494) and is never reached, because sizing raised before execution was attempted. || SO THE REFUSAL MESSAGE IS WRITTEN FOR THE OPERATOR AND DELIVERED TO A LOG FILE. The account silently stops trading. || MEASURED 2026-09-09T09:5xZ, and state the population: /api/diag/journal?table=order_packages&limit=1000 (the endpoint's max), spanning updated_at 2026-08-05T03:14:04Z -> 2026-09-09T09:48:28Z, 77 rows mentioning breakout. Rows carrying 'prop_balance' or 'sizing_failed': 4, all status 'rejected', at 2026-08-11T00:02:24Z and 2026-08-13T07:03:17Z / 17:01:13Z / 22:00:33Z. POSITIVE CONTROL: those 4 are what the probe DID find, so 'none since the 2026-08-30 snapshot' is a real zero and not a broken probe. ⚠️ THE 1000-ROW CAP IS THE LIMIT OF THIS MEASUREMENT — the window starts 2026-08-05 and the table is older, so this is NOT a lifetime count. || WHY IT IS FILED NOW RATHER THAN EARLIER: it was latent while prop_status_request asked on WALL-CLOCK AGE, because that ask reached the operator every 12h whether or not anything needed sizing, and incidentally covered this. MI-214 made the ask fire on ACTIVITY, so a genuinely quiescent account is no longer asked — which is correct, and which makes this the only remaining path by which 'your prop account cannot trade' would reach a human. MI-214 mitigates it deliberately with the ASK_TICKET_SINCE_SNAPSHOT trigger (a real, non-suppressed ticket after the snapshot re-arms the ask) rather than relying on the sizing gate alone — but that fires on the ticket AFTER a refusal, not on the refusal. || NOT A DUPLICATE OF BL-20260908-PROP-BALANCE-ASK-NEVER-ESCALATES-WHEN-UNANSWERED, which is about an ask that FIRES and is IGNORED. This is about a condition that produces NO ask at all. Opposite failure, same subsystem. || DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY MAKING SIZING PERMISSIVE. The refusal is correct and must stay — prop_balance's own docstring is that it can never cause a trade to be sized off a guess. The missing thing is the notification, not the gate. || 🛑 CORRECTED BY ITS OWN AUTHOR, 2026-09-09T11:4xZ, SAME SESSION (MI-214b). THE HEADLINE ABOVE IS OVERSTATED AND THE MEASUREMENT IN THIS ROW IS WRONG. Read this block before acting on anything above it; the id is kept because #11530 links it by name. || (1) THE MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG. This row cites '4 rows carrying prop_balance/sizing_failed, all 2026-08-11/13' as evidence about PROP sizing refusals. Those 4 rows are NOT prop refusals. Re-read 2026-09-09T11:3xZ from /api/diag/journal?table=trades&limit=1000: they are 'balance() returned None' on ib_paper, alpaca_paper and alpaca_portfolio — the NON-prop branch (coordinator.balance_none_refusal_message), a different cause on different accounts. I matched 'prop_balance' OR 'sizing_failed' over a json.dumps of each row and reported the union as if it were the first disjunct. Classic RULE ONE failure, in the direction that flattered my conclusion. || (2) THE ACTUAL POPULATION: breakout_1 has ZERO rows in `trades` in that 1000-row window, and ZERO rows anywhere contain 'prop_balance'. The prop stale-balance refusal has NEVER BEEN OBSERVED FIRING AT ALL. It is not that it fires unnoticed — nothing has reached it, because the prop tickets are suppressed at breakout_executor's reticket check, which runs BEFORE sizing. || (3) 'REACHES NOBODY' IS FALSE. log_rejection_to_journal -> _log_trade_to_journal writes to the `trades` table, which is exactly what silent_refusal_alert._read_window reads. So the refusal DOES reach an operator-facing detector. Verified by running the real code, not by reading it: classify_cause on the genuine string built from prop_balance.refusal_message returns a real bucket, and assess() grades the account signalled_never_placed. The code claim that survives is narrower and still true: the sizing branch does not call _emit_execution_failure_ping (that is on the later execute_pkg branch), so the PING path specifically is not reached — but the ping is not the only operator-facing channel, and this row asserted it was. || (4) WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, now measured rather than assumed — TWO defects, one fixed and one deliberately not. (A) MISLABELLED CAUSE, FIXED in MI-214b: the reason journals as 'REJECTED: sizing_failed: RuntimeError: prop_balance_stale: ...' and matched the generic `sizing_failed` pattern, so the operator was told the size computation failed when the actionable fact is 'send a fresh bal'. UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC sub-class A. A `prop_balance_unreported` pattern now precedes the generic rule, with the ordering pinned by a test because first-match-wins makes a reorder silently re-collapse them. (B) UNREACHABLE FLOOR, NOT FIXED AND DELIBERATELY SO: the cause carries the global SILENT_REFUSAL_MIN_ROWS floor of 5, so one refusal grades `below_min_rows` and does not alert. That is the same shape as BL-20260825-BALANCE-UNREADABLE-CAN-NEVER-REACH-ITS-OWN-ALERT-THRESHOLD, whose remedy was a CAUSE_MIN_ROWS override — but that override was justified by MEASURED run lengths [1,1,1,1,1,1,2,3,6,11,20] over 11 occurrences, and here the event has NEVER OCCURRED, so there is nothing to size it from. Adding an override on precedent alone would be lowering a bar with no evidence. A test asserts the override's ABSENCE and carries this reasoning, so a future session that measures real occurrences deletes it with the measurement in the commit message. || (5) THIS ROW STAYS OPEN, for (B) only. Its resolution_criteria below are superseded by: EITHER a prop-balance refusal is OBSERVED reaching the operator (which now needs 5 in 24h on an account with zero placements), OR the occurrence frequency is MEASURED and the floor decided on it, OR the operator decides a prop account that silently stops trading needs no alert — recorded as a decision with the accepted consequence. ⚠️ AND THE ORIGINAL 'the ping is never reached' CRITERION IS WITHDRAWN as a target: routing the sizing branch to _emit_execution_failure_ping would add a SECOND operator channel for a condition the first already grades, and enqueue_execution_failure has NO rate limiting at all, so it would ping per-signal per-tick. That is the alarm fatigue MI-214 just removed. Do not build it.
items.resolution_criteria: A prop sizing refusal for a stale/absent balance is OBSERVED reaching the operator — a row in outcomes.jsonl / /api/bot/logs?level=error, or a /api/bot/notifications banner, naming the account and carrying prop_balance's own refusal_message text — read off the live surface, not from a test. ⚠️ A GREEN TEST CLEARS NOTHING: the refusal path is already exercised in tests and the gap is which channel the message reaches. ⚠️ AND A JOURNALED order_packages ROW IS NOT SUFFICIENT — that is precisely the current behaviour and the thing being reported as inadequate. ALTERNATIVELY the operator DECIDES that a silently non-trading prop account needs no alert, which clears this row as a RECORDED decision stating the accepted consequence (breakout_1 can stop trading indefinitely with the only evidence being a journalctl line), rather than being left looking like a fix about to happen.

items.title: account_open_positions dedupes Bybit positions by SYMBOL and emits no position_idx, so under hedge mode the second book is silently dropped and _reconcile_open_trades reads a live row as flat and closes it
items.tier: 2 (src/units/accounts/clients.py — its output gates a live close in src/runtime/order_monitor.py)
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09 by reading the code; found while investigating MI-221 (bybit_2 ETHUSDT). src/units/accounts/clients.py:1379-1394, the bybit branch's _emit(), does `if sym in seen: return` — it dedupes by SYMBOL ALONE — and the dict it appends carries NO position_idx. BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS has been armed on bybit_1/bybit_2/bybit_portfolio since 2026-08-30, so one symbol carries TWO books (positionIdx 1 long / 2 short) and Bybit returns a row for each; whichever is listed FIRST wins and the other is dropped with no counter and no log. THIS IS NOT MERELY A READ-FIDELITY BUG — IT SITS ON A LIVE REAL-MONEY CLOSE DECISION. order_monitor._reconcile_open_trades builds positions_cache = _exchange_position_set(account_open_positions(cfg)) at order_monitor.py:4336-4343, and _exchange_position_set (order_monitor.py:2884-2905) keys the set on (symbol, normalised_side). The test at order_monitor.py:4348 is `if (sym, side) in positions_cache: continue`. So when the DROPPED book is the one the journal row is on, the row reads flat and falls through to _close_trade_from_order_status (order_monitor.py:4392) and is CLOSED. Worked example: venue holds ETHUSDT idx2 short and idx1 long 0.04, the short is listed first, _emit emits ('ETHUSDT','short') and drops the long, and the long row's test ('ETHUSDT','long') in positions_cache is False. DISTINCT SITE from BL-20260908-BYBIT-POSITION-PROTECTION-GRADES-A-SYMBOL-OFF-ROWS0-SO-A-HEDGE-BOOK-READS-FLAT-AND-A-LIVE-POSITION-IS-CLOSED, which is _bybit_position_protection at order_monitor.py:8821 taking rows[0] and feeding the NETTING reconciler; this is clients.py::_emit feeding the ORDER-STATUS reconciler. Same class, two independent sites, two different consumers — fixing that row does NOT fix this one, which is why this is filed separately rather than as a comment on it. NOT ESTABLISHED, and deliberately not claimed: that this mechanism closed trade 5471. It requires a second non-zero ETHUSDT book on bybit_2 at 2026-09-08T13:37Z and no read exists from that moment — today's reads (2026-09-09 11:27:53Z and 11:28:38Z via /api/diag/exchange_positions and /api/diag/bybit_open_orders) show NO ETHUSDT book on bybit_2 at all. Evidence: docs/claude/work/BYBIT2-ETH-PHANTOM-CLOSE-2026-09-09.md.
items.resolution_criteria: account_open_positions' bybit branch keys its dedupe on (symbol, positionIdx) rather than symbol alone, emits position_idx on every row, and _exchange_position_set is shown to distinguish the two books — with a test that FAILS on the current code by asserting that a two-book get_positions payload yields both ('SYM','long') and ('SYM','short'). Tier-2: it changes what the reconciler considers open, so it needs an operator OK before merge. Explicitly NOT sufficient: adding position_idx to the emitted dict while leaving the symbol-keyed dedupe in place — the drop happens in the dedupe, not in the shape.

items.title: No repo surface exposes the raw Bybit get_positions payload, so 'venue flat' / 'zero-size hedge sibling' / 'no row returned' are one observation — this blocked root-cause on two real-money P1s one day apart
items.tier: 1 (a read-only diag surface; no order path, no grading)
items.detail: RECURRENCE, and that is the finding — the earlier investigation did not get an instrument and the next one hit the same wall. Every Bybit position reader drops zero-size rows before anyone sees them: clients.py::account_open_positions._emit does `if size <= 0: return` (clients.py:1380-1382) and account_bybit_open_orders does `if size <= 0: continue` (clients.py:1896-1898), both with NO counter and NO log line. So a reader cannot distinguish (i) the venue is genuinely flat on this symbol, (ii) the venue returned a zero-size row — the hedge-mode sibling book, which is the state BYBIT_HEDGE_MODE_SYMBOLS made routine on 2026-08-30, and (iii) the venue returned no row for this symbol at all. Three states, one value, on the read that decides whether a live position exists. MEASURED INSTANCE 1 (2026-09-08): BL-20260908-BYBIT-POSITION-PROTECTION-GRADES-A-SYMBOL-OFF-ROWS0-SO-A-HEDGE-BOOK-READS-FLAT-AND-A-LIVE-POSITION-IS-CLOSED records verbatim 'NOT ESTABLISHED: which of _flat's two triggers fired — `not rows` or `rows[0].size <= 0`. No repo surface exposes the raw get_positions payload; saying which would be a guess.' MEASURED INSTANCE 2 (2026-09-09, MI-221): investigating why bybit_2 ETHUSDT trade 5471 closed while the operator's terminal showed the position live, the manager asked explicitly for the RAW get_positions response because that single observation separates 'the venue is not returning it to this API key' from 'the bot drops it after the read'. It could not be produced. Two symbol-scoped reads at 11:27:53Z and 11:28:38Z established only 'no row with size > 0', which is the collapsed value. This is an INSTRUMENT gap, not a per-site nit: the same missing observation has now stopped two separate real-money investigations at the same step, and will stop the third. Evidence: docs/claude/work/BYBIT2-ETH-PHANTOM-CLOSE-2026-09-09.md § 4c.
items.resolution_criteria: A read-only diag surface returns the raw Bybit position rows for an account/symbol INCLUDING zero-size rows and positionIdx, with a three-state read marker distinguishing 'no rows returned' from 'rows returned, all zero-size' from 'rows returned with a non-zero book' — and a session is OBSERVED using it to say WHICH state a real symbol is in. Explicitly NOT sufficient: adding a log line at the drop site (it is not readable from a session, and the systemd journal retention on this VM was measured at ~30 minutes), or a counter of dropped rows without the positionIdx that says WHICH book was dropped.

items.title: account_bybit_open_orders' symbol cross-check reads account['symbols'] with no accounts.yaml fallback, unlike its position-reading sibling, so a hand-built reduced cfg silently skips protection cross-checking
items.tier: 1 (read-only surface; latent today, no live fault observed)
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09 by reading the code; found while investigating MI-221. The two sibling Bybit readers in src/units/accounts/clients.py resolve the SAME per-symbol cross-check denominator by DIFFERENT means, and only one is defensive. account_open_positions calls _bybit_configured_symbols(account) (clients.py:1221-1244), which prefers account['symbols'] and FALLS BACK to load_accounts_dict() by account_id — and whose own docstring names 'order_monitor._build_account_client' as exactly the kind of caller that hand-builds a reduced cfg. account_bybit_open_orders instead iterates `account.get('symbols') or []` directly (clients.py:1912) with NO fallback. A caller passing a reduced cfg therefore gets a SILENTLY EMPTY cross-check on the PROTECTION surface: no exception, no entry in order_symbols_unchecked (that list records only reads that FAILED, never ones that were never attempted), and a short orders list that reads as complete. That function's own docstring says the settleCoin page under-reports legs and that 'a missing leg reads as missing protection' — which drives a re-arm on a live position. NOT A LIVE FAULT TODAY, and stated as such rather than inflated: the diag route reaches it via list_accounts(), and _load_yaml_accounts explicitly carries 'symbols' through (src/units/ui/data_loaders.py:259), which I verified before filing. It is one refactor or one new caller away from a real protection blind spot, and the asymmetry with its sibling is the defect. Evidence: docs/claude/work/BYBIT2-ETH-PHANTOM-CLOSE-2026-09-09.md § 4b.
items.resolution_criteria: account_bybit_open_orders resolves its cross-check denominator through _bybit_configured_symbols (the same helper its sibling uses) rather than a bare account.get('symbols'), with a test that passes a cfg carrying only account_id and asserts the cross-check still runs. Alternatively: the function records a distinct 'denominator_unresolved' state when it can name no symbols, so an empty cross-check can never read as a complete one — either fix is acceptable, silence is not.

items.tier: 1 — a guard extension; it changes no gate value
items.summary: MI-218 measurement finding, and the LIMIT ON ITS OWN COUNT. check_soak_doctrine.py check D (#11529) detects an accrual-gated verdict as CONTROL FLOW: an `if` whose test reads a live/calendar name and whose body assigns a verdict. It is therefore structurally blind to a gate declared as a DATA FIELD. Measured: ml/promotion/gates.py carries `require_shadow_soak: bool = True` @ `shadow_soak_days: float = 7.0` and `min_trades: int = 200` (LIVE trades) on the DEFAULT GateThresholds profile, and `_gate_shadow_soak` returns `GateResult(..., required=th.require_shadow_soak)` — a constructor argument, no branch. Pass A (check D's algorithm over ALL 8,464 functions in 1,058 files, not its 1-entry GATE_SURFACES map) and Pass B (widened constants AND a widened verdict predicate) BOTH miss it; it was found by READING. ⚠️ THIS IS WHY MI-218's count is reported as `lower_bound` and NOT `measured` — how many more data-shaped gates exist cannot be bounded from inside the instrument. Not a defect in check D's algorithm, which Pass A confirmed has no blind spot of its own shape (7 hits, 1 surface, nothing else across the tree); it is a missing SECOND detector shape. Evidence: docs/research/CALENDAR-TIME-EDGE-SURFACE-CENSUS-2026-09-09.md.
items.resolution_criteria: ⚠️ THIS ROW IS NOT WAITING FOR TRADES AND ITS CLOCK IS NOT A CALENDAR ONE — it waits on a GUARD EXTENSION that can be written today, and it carries no `accrual_legs` because there is no leg to name. (It trips `accrual_clock.py`'s text check only because it is a row ABOUT calendar-time gates rather than one waiting on trades; that is the guard's remedy sentence exactly — re-state the exit condition as the MEASUREMENT it really waits on.) It clears when check D grades DECLARED GATE RECORDS alongside branches — a `required=`/`min_*`/`*_days` field on a thresholds object whose value denotes a live-outcome or wall-clock quantity — AND it is demonstrated on a POSITIVE CONTROL: pointed at ml/promotion/gates.py it must report the default profile's require_shadow_soak and min_trades. ⚠️ A GREEN RUN CLEARS NOTHING: the current guard is already green on that file, which is the finding. ⚠️ AND REPORTING THEM IS NOT CHANGING THEM — both are Tier-3 (see BL-20260909-DEFAULT-PROMOTION-PROFILE-REQUIRES-A-7-DAY-CALENDAR-SOAK-AND-200-LIVE-TRADES); the ledger's per-surface count is where a known instance is declared, exactly as check D already does for M7.

items.tier: 3 — it decides what a model promotion rests on; operator decision, NOT a session's
items.summary: MI-218 CONFIRMED SURFACE S2, and the highest-leverage one found. ml/promotion/gates.py:228 picks `regime_classifier_thresholds()` if `is_regime_classifier(entry)` else a bare `GateThresholds()`. The regime profile sets `require_shadow_soak=False` (WS-1 de-soak, operator-approved 2026-07-26) and `min_trades=5`. EVERY OTHER HEAD lands on the default, where BOTH are REQUIRED: `require_shadow_soak=True` @ `shadow_soak_days=7.0` — a literal 'N days at stage', which CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md § 'Promotion evidence' clause 3 names verbatim as 'a policy artifact, not evidence' — and `min_trades=200` LIVE trades, which at the ~1.2 closes/week the operator cites is ~3.2 YEARS. ⚠️ CANON SAYS THIS IS 'mechanically guarded: tests/ml/test_gates.py asserts that no required gate UNDER THE REGIME-CLASSIFIER PROFILE is a calendar-time edge gate'. That is TRUE and it is SCOPED TO ONE PROFILE. The default profile — used by every non-regime head, including trade-outcome and exit heads — is not covered by that assertion. This is the M7 fact pattern one level up: the rule is binding, the guard is real, and the guard does not reach the surface. Evidence: docs/research/CALENDAR-TIME-EDGE-SURFACE-CENSUS-2026-09-09.md § S2.
items.resolution_criteria: ⚠️ THIS ROW IS NOT WAITING FOR TRADES TO HAPPEN — it waits on an OPERATOR DECISION that can be taken today, and it carries no `accrual_legs` because no leg's trading advances it. (It trips `accrual_clock.py`'s text check only because the GATE it describes is the thing that waits on live trades; the row does not.) The OPERATOR decides, and either answer settles it, but it must be RECORDED as a decision rather than left looking like work about to start: (a) the default profile's calendar-time and live-outcome gates are demoted to advisory the way the regime profile's were — computed + reported, non-blocking — and tests/ml/test_gates.py's assertion is widened past the regime profile so the default cannot silently re-require them; OR (b) the operator decides a trade-outcome head genuinely needs live outcome volume that a regime head does not, which is a legitimate distinction, and the REASON is written into gates.py beside the field so the next session reads a decision instead of a default. ⚠️ NOT SUFFICIENT: reading the values back, or a green tests/ml/test_gates.py — it is green today and that is the finding. ⚠️ A SESSION MUST NOT CHANGE EITHER VALUE ON ITS OWN JUDGEMENT.

items.tier: 2 — it decides whether a leg's backtest is admissible evidence
items.summary: MI-218 CONFIRMED SURFACE S3, and the sharpest instance of the doctrine inverted. scripts/research/backtest_fidelity_calibrate.py::agreement holds `MIN_LIVE_N = 30`; below it the verdict is `insufficient-live` and, in the script's own words, 'backtest is a lead, not a result'. Its OWN docstring states the problem it was built to solve: 'we have never MEASURED whether our backtests are right, so we fell back to only trust real live trades — WHICH CAPS EVERY DECISION AT REALITY'S CLOCK'. The implementation then makes 30 LIVE trades a precondition for a leg's OFFLINE evidence being admissible — ~25 weeks at ~1.2 closes/week. So the instrument built to escape reality's clock is reachable only by waiting on it. ⚠️ STATED FAIRLY, THIS IS NOT A SIMPLE DEFECT: measuring backtest<->live fidelity DOES require live trades, and abstaining is honest rather than a silent pass. The finding is narrower and is the part that contradicts canon: a FIDELITY (mechanics) measurement is used as the ADMISSIBILITY GATE ON AN EDGE CLAIM, so a leg with a clean purged-WF-CV oos_edge and 29 live trades has evidence the system will not look at. Evidence: docs/research/CALENDAR-TIME-EDGE-SURFACE-CENSUS-2026-09-09.md § S3.
items.resolution_criteria: A DESIGN DECISION is taken and recorded on how a leg's offline edge evidence is admitted below MIN_LIVE_N — the candidates being a lower or per-leg floor, or admitting the offline evidence WITH a stated fidelity caveat attached rather than withholding it. ⚠️ LOWERING THE CONSTANT IS NOT THE ANSWER BY ITSELF and must not be done as a quick fix: 30 is a power floor for a two-sample KS, so cutting it buys a calibration nobody should trust — which is a worse failure than the delay. What the row needs is the SEPARATION: fidelity graded on whatever live n exists, and edge admissibility not made downstream of it. ⚠️ AND IF THE DECISION IS THAT NO LEG'S BACKTEST IS TRUSTED UNTIL 30 LIVE CLOSES, that is legitimate and clears this row — but must be RECORDED as a decision, with the ~25-week consequence stated.

items.tier: 1 — a prose fix to a skill rubric
items.summary: MI-218 CONFIRMED SURFACE S4, and the only prose finding that survived reading (19 edge/both candidates -> 1). .claude/skills/exit-refinement/SKILL.md § P7 reads: 'The lever/head soaks LIVE. The next /health-review MUST verify the mechanics of the first real lever-driven exit; /ml-review//performance-review track the realized `future_r_delta` record. Demotion = delete the YAML lines.' ⚠️ THE FIRST HALF IS EXEMPLARY and is why this is a partial rather than a clean finding — 'verify the mechanics of the first real lever-driven exit' is the canonical doctrine stated correctly, and the fix must not damage it. The second half attaches DEMOTION to a REALIZED LIVE R RECORD, which is an edge verdict on live accrual with no stated floor and no offline counterpart. Note this skill is NOT in check_soak_doctrine.py's SOAK_SKILLS list (new-strategy, backtesting), so checks A-C do not read it. Evidence: docs/research/CALENDAR-TIME-EDGE-SURFACE-CENSUS-2026-09-09.md § S4.
items.resolution_criteria: P7 states where the exit lever's EDGE was decided (the offline E3/harness sweep that produced it) and frames the live record as MECHANICS + rolling drift, so demotion rests on the mechanics diverging or the offline basis being withdrawn — not on a live R tally reaching a size. AND exit-refinement is added to check_soak_doctrine.py's SOAK_SKILLS so checks A-C reach it, since a prose fix that nothing guards is the exact drift that guard exists to stop (it was reverted repeatedly in new-strategy before the guard existed). ⚠️ Do NOT delete the 'verify the mechanics of the first real lever-driven exit' sentence — it is the half that is already right.

items.tier: 1 — a reporting field; the floor value is unchanged
items.summary: MI-218 CONDITIONAL SURFACE C1 — deliberately classified neither `edge` nor `mechanics`, because collapsing it either way would assert a fact nobody established. scripts/research/e2_feature_information.py::score_panel gates `verdict = 'unmeasured'` on `min_trades=30` / `min_rows=200`. These are statistical POWER floors and the comment defending them is correct ('An underpowered null is not a negative'). Whether they require CALENDAR TIME depends entirely on which panel is handed in: the intrabar exit panel stamps `source: backtest` and `_COHORT = 'backtest'` (OFFLINE — satisfied by deepening history, i.e. by computing harder), while a journal-sourced panel is LIVE (satisfied only by waiting). `score_panel` does not read the panel manifest's `source` stamp, so the report cannot tell a reader WHICH of the two the floor was enforcing — the same constant, opposite verdicts. This is the general form of the distinction that eliminated 11 of MI-218's 14 automated candidates. Evidence: docs/research/CALENDAR-TIME-EDGE-SURFACE-CENSUS-2026-09-09.md § C1.
items.resolution_criteria: score_panel's report carries the panel's population basis — read from the manifest's existing `source`/cohort stamp, NOT inferred from the row count — and `unmeasured_reason` says whether the floor is satisfiable by deepening history or only by waiting. Three states, not two: `backtest`, `journal`, and `unknown` for a panel whose manifest carries no stamp (we did not look), which must never read as `backtest`. ⚠️ The FLOOR VALUES are not the subject of this row and must not be changed by it.

items.tier: 1 — a doc/tool disagreement; the tool and its test are authoritative
items.summary: MEASURED 2026-09-09 by paying for it: docs/claude/session-board.json's OWN `schema.merge_slot` documents the field as `{ held_by, branch, pr: <int|null>, claimed_at }` — it explicitly declares a `pr` key. scripts/ops/claim_merge_slot.py renders NO `pr` at all (the string does not appear in the file), and tests/test_claim_merge_slot.py::test_real_board_diff_is_small_enough_to_conflict_narrowly FAILS when one is present. ⚠️ THE FAILURE IS OPAQUE AND POINTS AT THE WRONG THING: dropping the extra key shifts every subsequent line, and the test's line-zip then reports `75 lines change; a claim is 4. A whole-file re-serialisation turns every concurrent session edit into a conflict.` So a session that followed the documented schema is told it REFORMATTED THE FILE, which it did not — measured on PR #11538, whose session-board diff was 15 insertions / 4 deletions, nowhere near a reformat. I lost a full CI cycle (~16 min) chasing a reformat that never happened. FIELD BEATS COMMENT: the tool and its test are the truth and the schema string is stale. NOT a defect in the test, whose invariant (keep the diff to the claim) is exactly right and is what makes this file survivable for concurrent sessions.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) the `pr` key is removed from `schema.merge_slot` in docs/claude/session-board.json, so the documented shape matches what claim_merge_slot.py actually writes; OR (b) claim_merge_slot.py renders `pr` and the test's fixture covers it — one or the other, not both surfaces left disagreeing. ⚠️ ALSO WORTH FIXING AND SEPARATE: the test's message asserts a CAUSE (`a whole-file re-serialisation`) that its line-zip cannot distinguish from a one-line insertion or deletion, which is the unprovenanced-diagnostic class CLAUDE.md names — reporting the count alongside `len(a) vs len(b)` would name the real shape. A green run does NOT clear this row: the suite is green whenever nobody has added the documented key.

items.tier: 1 — tooling (the assertion); any widening of a read's scope is Tier-2
items.title: Every venue read is scoped to category=linear and one UID per account, and NOTHING verifies that scope covers all the books the account's capital is actually on
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09T13:12:31Z on live sha d87db750 via the new /api/diag/bybit_raw_positions (MI-221 STEP 1). Population: 5 queries on bybit_2 (settleCoin=USDT page + one symbol-scoped read per configured symbol), repeated across all 3 Bybit accounts; zero query errors, so no could_not_look is hiding in the result. || THE OPERATOR REPORTED an open, UNPROTECTED real-money ETHUSDT position (0.04 ETH, entry 2453.97, TP/SL column reading '+ Add'). Every read this system can make says ETH is FLAT: Bybit returns BOTH hedge books for ETHUSDT on bybit_2 and both carry size_raw '0', avg_price null, side '' -- so this is NOT a row our readers discard (the size<=0 skip), and NOT a missing row. The venue is truthfully reporting flat to this key, and has since 2026-09-08T13:37:13.873Z. No Bybit account the system holds keys for (bybit_1 553832447, bybit_2 553829655, bybit_portfolio 576206494; three distinct UIDs, shared_uid_groups {}) holds any open ETH position. || THE FINDING IS THE GAP THAT LEAVES. Every read in the incident is category:'linear' and one UID per account. An ETH book on a different UID or sub-account, or on inverse / Unified / spot-margin, is invisible to ALL of it -- to exchange_positions, to bybit_open_orders, to _bybit_position_protection, to the naked sweeps, and to BOTH detectors proposed to fix this incident. A position outside that scope is not merely unprotected; it is outside the coverage of every mechanism we have. NOTHING MEASURES THAT SCOPE. || NOT BL-20260908-THREE-OF-ELEVEN-ACCOUNTS-HAVE-NO-VENUE-POSITION-READ-AND-BREAKOUT-1-CAN-NEVER-HAVE-ONE (0.60 lexical overlap, read in full before filing). That row is about reads that return None -- reachability. This is about reads that SUCCEED and return rows whose SCOPE is unverified. The distinction matters because that row's own denominator ('23 of 24 pairs over EIGHT accounts') rests on the assumption this row says is untested: that a readable account is a FULLY read account. || is_sub_account currently reads None on all three Bybit accounts -- 'we could not look', NEVER 'no' -- so the sub-account hypothesis is UNTESTED, not refuted. || REMEDY (proposal, not shipped): a coverage ASSERTION, not a manual check -- for each account, enumerate the categories and UIDs its credentials can reach and compare against what the account DECLARES it trades; grade unknown as unknown, never as covered. Operator directive 2026-09-09 is binding here: the system must not rely on a human checking trades by hand, so the remedy must be an automatic assertion. || WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: where the operator's position actually is (different UID / different category / stale terminal are all live, none tested); and whether the 2026-09-08T13:37:13Z close was CORRECT -- the venue confirms a close occurred, which says nothing about whether exit_reason='sl' describes it truthfully.
items.resolution_criteria: A read surface reports, PER ACCOUNT, the set of venue books its credentials can actually reach -- the product categories queried AND the UID(s) answering -- beside the set the account DECLARES it trades, with a three-state verdict per account that never collapses 'covered' with 'we did not look': observed on the live fleet via a diag read, not from a test fixture. CLEARED when that surface returns a verdict for all 3 Bybit accounts AND at least one account grades something other than 'covered' or the all-covered verdict is confirmed against a positive control (an account deliberately queried on a category it does not trade must grade uncovered, proving the check can fail). NOT SUFFICIENT: a green unit test (a fixture cannot establish which books a real key reaches); the current reads returning rows (that is the assumption under test, not evidence for it); or the operator confirming where their position was (that answers THIS incident and leaves the class unmeasured).

items.title: pr-landing R10 grades the ARMING FILE, but auto-merge GitHub has already enabled SURVIVES the file's removal — so a PR can be declared `hold` and still auto-merge
items.detail: OBSERVED IN THE ACT 2026-09-09 on PR #11555 (MI-221), a Tier-2 diff touching src/units/accounts/clients.py. SEQUENCE: (1) content + .github/pr-automerge-requests/<slug>.txt were pushed in ONE commit; (2) claude-pr-automerge fired on that push, opened/adopted the PR and ENABLED auto-merge (squash) — its open-and-automerge check ran and concluded success; (3) check_pr_landing R5 then REFUSED landing:self because src/** is Tier-2 by path; (4) I removed the arming file and declared landing:hold / hold_reason tier_2_3_needs_approval, and the guard graded `pr-landing: OK — state=declared_needs_approval`. || THE GUARD WAS GREEN AND AUTO-MERGE WAS STILL ARMED. Confirmed by calling disable_pr_auto_merge, which returned 'Auto-merge disabled' — it does not report success on a PR that never had it, so the arm was real, not assumed. Had CI gone green, a Tier-2 change to a live real-money order-path module would have merged with NO human read, while every repo surface said it was correctly held. || ROOT CAUSE: R10 compares the arming FILE against origin/main. Enabling auto-merge is a side effect on GITHUB that outlives the file. Removing the file makes the guard green and changes nothing about the armed state, so the guard's green is evidence about the DIFF and not about whether the PR will merge itself — the exact field-beats-comment inversion this repo keeps paying for, with the guard as the comment. || NOT BL-20260904-A-TIER-1-SELF-LAND-PR-OPENED-BY-PR-OPENER-IS-A-DRAFT-AND-CAN-NEVER-SELF-LAND-FROM-A-WEB-SESSION (0.75 lexical overlap, read in full before filing): that row is a PR that CANNOT land when it should. This is the opposite and more dangerous polarity — a PR that CAN land when it must not. || REACHABLE BY ACCIDENT, not just by the two-push order: any branch that arms, then discovers R5/R4 refuses it, lands in this state. CLAUDE.md already documents opening the PR by hand FIRST and arming SECOND, which makes the one-push order a KNOWN and repeated slip (it hit six PRs on 2026-09-08 and me twice on 2026-09-09), so this is not an exotic path. || WHAT I DID: disabled auto-merge by hand and left the PR held for a human merge. That is a fix for ONE PR, not for the class.
items.resolution_criteria: check_pr_landing (or a sibling CI step) READS the PR's live auto-merge state — not the arming file — and FAILS when auto_merge is enabled while the landing declaration says hold, or while R4/R5 refuse self-landing. Verified by a POSITIVE CONTROL, because the whole defect is a check that passes on a state it cannot see: arm a scratch PR, let the workflow enable auto-merge, remove the arming file and declare hold, and observe the guard FAIL — a guard that stays green there has not been fixed, it has been re-verified as blind. NOT SUFFICIENT: removing the arming file (the observed no-op); a green run on a PR that was never armed (it cannot distinguish the fix from the defect); or documenting the two-push order in prose — that guidance ALREADY exists in CLAUDE.md and was violated six times in two days, which is why this needs a mechanism rather than a reminder.

items.summary: scripts/ops/journal_venue_audit.py was built 2026-09-08 (MI-177) to find journal-vs-venue position divergences fleet-wide, and it reads the venue via _diag("exchange_positions") at line 128 — which serves account_open_positions, the SAME account-wide list that a live real-money position was found missing from on 2026-09-09. bybit_2 held ETHUSDT 0.04 long unprotected for five days while journal trade 5471 recorded it closed on a stop the venue never fired; it is absent from that venue list AND from "trades WHERE status='open'", so it is outside both lists every protective sweep anchors to. HAD THIS AUDIT BEEN ON AN HOURLY CADENCE SINCE THE DAY IT WAS WRITTEN IT WOULD HAVE REPORTED bybit_2 CLEAN ON EVERY RUN. Two separate defects are easy to conflate here and must not be: (a) nothing invokes it — its own header declares manual-only, deliberately not on a cadence — and (b) it is structurally blind, which a schedule does not fix. Fixing only (a) is actively HARMFUL: it converts an unread book into a green light, which is worse than no detector. Its JOURNAL side is correct and hard-won (the /api/diag/journal LIMIT<=1000 cap, the /api/bot/positions hardcoded LIMIT 50 with no truncation flag, and the /api/diag/exposure uncapped-SUM cross-check that makes journal_read_state=complete an assertion) and should be reused, not rebuilt.
items.evidence: order_monitor.py:3128 account_open_positions(cfg) in _reconcile_orphan_exchange_positions; order_monitor.py:9716 _check_broker_naked_bybit_positions enumerates trades WHERE status='open'; scripts/ops/journal_venue_audit.py:128 _diag("exchange_positions"); docs/claude/work/UNREAD-ACCOUNT-VENUE-AUDIT-2026-09-08.md:251 already records "exists and nothing re-runs it"; fleet sweep 2026-09-09T11:36-11:40Z over all 27 journal-open positions across 6 accounts — every one reconciles exactly against its venue read, so the ETH is the sole divergence and the reader is not generally broken.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH, and they are different facts — say which was cleared. (1) A position enumeration exists that depends on NEITHER account_open_positions NOR "trades WHERE status='open'", with its source named and its per-cadence read cost stated as a number. (2) It is OBSERVED reporting a position of this shape — run against a book containing one (or a planted control) and seen to report it. EXPLICITLY DOES NOT CLEAR THIS: putting journal_venue_audit.py on a schedule (that is defect (a) only and makes (b) worse); a green test suite, which cannot reach a venue; a scheduled run reporting clean, which is exactly what the blind version already reports; or repairing the one bybit_2 ETH position, which settles a trade and not the class. IF a session establishes the audit is NOT in fact blind — i.e. the venue surface does return such a position and the miss has another cause — that does not clear this row either; it CORRECTS it, and the correction must be recorded with the read that established it.
items.notes: Operator-directed 2026-09-09: "if this isn't a capability we've already built, then building is the next action item". Filed separately from MI-222 because the audit still exists after MI-222 ships and a future session may reach for it believing it covers this.

items.summary: PR #11514 merged origin/main TWELVE times over ~4h before landing, every round chasing a manager register PR into the same shared files (#11527, #11528, #11531, #11532, #11533 — plus automation PRs #11535, #11539, #11541, which are a SECOND and independent source of the same contention). Each merge voided a CI run of ~16 minutes that had not finished. The lane was doing nothing wrong: it resolved each conflict correctly and promptly, and that promptness is what kept it in the loop. It landed only after the manager FROZE its own register writes for ~20 minutes, which is a workaround held in one session's head and dies with that session. The manager's base duty is to SCHEDULE merges rather than resolve the conflicts that not scheduling them causes; MERGE-QUEUE.json exists and its one enforced invariant is at-most-one rebasing, which does not address a long-running branch being repeatedly dirtied by short manager writes into shared registers.
items.evidence: #11514 head cb70dad9, 18 commits, created 07:55:50Z, merged 11:57:02Z; mergeable_state cycled dirty->blocked repeatedly; contending manager PRs #11527/#11528/#11531/#11532/#11533 and automation #11535/#11539/#11541, all touching docs/claude/work/* or docs/claude/session-board.json. Prior measured harm on the same shape, population stated: over ALL 26 merge commits to main on 2026-09-03 (the full day's merges, not a sample), 19 touched a shared register under docs/claude/ — 19/26 = 73%, two of them bare lease heartbeats. That figure is INHERITED from the MI-102 measurement recorded in CLAUDE.md and was NOT re-measured for this row; today's #11514 count (12 merges of origin/main into one branch over ~4h) is this row's own observation and is independent of it.
items.resolution_criteria: A mechanism — not a remembered practice — that stops a long-running branch being dirtied repeatedly by short writes into shared registers while it waits for CI. Cleared when it is OBSERVED holding: a branch with CI in flight is seen to reach its merge without its base moving under it, and the thing that held the base is a committed rule or a queue state, not a session choosing to wait. EXPLICITLY DOES NOT CLEAR THIS: a manager freezing its writes by hand (that is the workaround, and it is what already happened); a note added to a skill or role pack telling managers to batch (a reminder is not a mechanism — this repo has paid for that non-fix on MI-15 twice); or the count simply being lower on a quiet day, which is a denominator effect and not a change. If the operator decides the churn is an acceptable cost, that CLOSES this row as a recorded decision rather than leaving it looking like work about to start.

items.title: /api/diag/log_file caps at 1000 lines, which on bybit_coverage_soak's volume is ~7 hours — so the soak that is the ONLY declared evidence for the graded-coverage widening decision cannot be read back far enough to evidence anything
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09T16:30Z while trying to answer MI-221's question (B) -- why the per-tick Bybit naked sweep never re-armed trade 5471 across four days (2026-09-04T14:04:14Z..2026-09-08T13:37:13Z). /api/diag/log_file?name=bybit_coverage_soak&lines=1000 returned 1000 rows spanning ONLY 2026-09-09T09:24:47Z..16:29:35Z -- SEVEN HOURS AND FIVE MINUTES. The route's own cap is _MAX_LIMIT = 1000 (src/web/api/routers/diag.py), and _clamp silently reduces any larger request, so 1000 is the hard ceiling for every consumer. At the observed rate (1000 rows / 425 min = 2.35 rows/min) reaching back to the incident's start would need roughly 16,900 rows -- about 17x the ceiling. THE INCIDENT WINDOW IS UNREACHABLE THROUGH THE ONLY SURFACE THAT EXPOSES THIS LOG. || THIS IS A READ-SURFACE LIMIT, NOT DATA LOSS, and the distinction matters for the fix: the file on the VM may hold far more; what is capped is the retrieval. So the remedy is a windowed/paged read, not a change to what is written. || WHY IT IS SEVERE RATHER THAN A NUISANCE: OI-20260902-BYBIT-GRADED-COVERAGE-SOAK-IS-THE-ONLY-EVIDENCE-FOR-WIDENING-AND-NOTHING-WATCHES-IT records that this soak's rows are THE ONLY DECLARED EVIDENCE for the operator's conditional widening of the graded-coverage gate to bybit_portfolio and then bybit_2 (REAL MONEY), and its clears_when requires at least 20 graded rows spanning at least 3 distinct UTC days plus at least one verdicts_differ row. A reader can accumulate that by sampling forward, but CANNOT audit it retrospectively, and cannot check a disagreement reported yesterday. An evidence store that cannot be re-read past 7 hours is weak evidence for a real-money arming decision. || ALSO MEASURED, and it is a separate fact worth keeping: ZERO bybit_2 ETHUSDT rows appear even inside today's 7-hour window -- correctly, because ETH is flat and the sweep grades only symbols carrying a position. So the absence of ETH rows today is NOT evidence about the incident; it is the expected shape for a flat symbol, and must not be read as the sweep having nothing to say.
items.resolution_criteria: /api/diag/log_file (or a sibling) accepts a TIME WINDOW or a cursor, so any allowlisted jsonl can be read back to an arbitrary point rather than only its last 1000 lines. CLEARED when a read of bybit_coverage_soak returns rows from a date at least 3 days before the request, demonstrated on the live fleet -- and verified by a POSITIVE CONTROL that the window bound is real: a request for a window the file does not cover must return an explicit empty-for-that-window state, NEVER the most recent rows, because silently serving the tail for an out-of-range window is the same class of defect as the cap itself. NOT SUFFICIENT: raising _MAX_LIMIT alone (it moves the ceiling without making the bound expressible, and a bigger tail is still a tail); a green unit test over a fixture file; or sampling the tail more often (that accumulates going forward and still cannot audit the past, which is the actual gap).

items.tier: 2 — order path (any change to the coverage basis); the MEASUREMENT is Tier-1
items.title: Under Bybit netting one exchange position backs N journal rows, so a sibling's Partial leg can make a symbol read covered while a row carries no protection of its own — and coverage is graded per SYMBOL, never per ROW
items.detail: OPERATOR HYPOTHESIS, 2026-09-09T16:26Z, verbatim: 'it's possible that there was a partial bracket on the position for one trade - once it closed, another trade, that never had brackets, became visibly naked once it wasn't hiding behind the first trade'. || THE MECHANISM IS REAL ON THIS VENUE. Under one-way netting ONE exchange position backs N journal rows. _bybit_position_protection sums resting SL legs and compares to the POSITION size -- a per-SYMBOL grade -- so a sibling's Partial leg contributes coverage that no reader attributes to a particular row. A row carrying no leg of its own is therefore indistinguishable from a covered one for as long as a sibling's leg rests. || MEASURED ON THIS ACCOUNT AND SYMBOL. Population: every bybit_2 ETHUSDT row in the 1000-row journal window, ids 4611..5610 (~2026-08-11 onward), read 2026-09-09T16:26Z, n=12. TWO rows closed with exit_reason 'netting_attributed' -- the attribution path that exists ONLY because multiple rows share one netted position -- and the timing is striking: 4886 closed 2026-08-21T21:24:02.429Z and its sibling 4808 closed on tp_cross 45.1 SECONDS LATER. Verified from the journal directly, not relayed. || WHAT IS *NOT* DEMONSTRATED, STATED SO THE ROW IS NOT OVER-READ: BOTH netting_attributed rows carry their own sl_order_id (4886 f78cd748..., 4922 5cf9a71f...). The hypothesis is about a row that NEVER HAD BRACKETS hiding behind a sibling, and neither of these is that row. So netting-SHARING is demonstrated; a row with no legs of its own being MASKED is not. The three NULL-leg-id ETH rows in the window (4730, 5355, 5372) are not candidates either -- all three are intent_reduce_executed with created_at == closed_at to the second, i.e. reduce operations rather than opens, so their NULLs are CORRECT. || NOT AN EXPLANATION OF TRADE 5471, and filed separately from it deliberately: 5471 was ALONE on that netted position for its entire life (zero other bybit_2 ETHUSDT rows open at any point 2026-09-04T14:04:14Z..2026-09-08T13:37:13Z; nearest prior close 5403 at 2026-09-03T13:36:27Z, 1d 0:27:47 BEFORE it opened) and carries BOTH leg ids. The hypothesis is refuted FOR THAT TRADE and the class stands on its own evidence. || WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS INCIDENT: the moment the sibling closes, its leg goes, and the uncovered row is what remains -- with no alarm, because nothing ever graded that row as uncovered. The per-tick naked sweep would only notice after the fact, and only if its own symbol-level grade then read short.
items.resolution_criteria: A read surface reports, per OPEN journal row on a netted Bybit symbol, whether THAT ROW's own tracked leg ids (trades.sl_order_id / tp_order_id) are still resting at the venue -- not whether the SYMBOL is covered in aggregate. CLEARED when that surface is observed on the live fleet distinguishing at least two rows on one netted symbol, at least one of which has a resting own-leg and one of which does not, OR when a measurement over the journal establishes the population of rows that have EVER been open without an own-leg while a sibling's leg rested (a count, with the classifier stated and a positive control). NOT SUFFICIENT: the existing symbol-level covered_qty grade (it is the thing under test); a green unit test (a fixture cannot establish venue leg residency); or the observation that 5471 was alone (that refutes the hypothesis for ONE trade and says nothing about the class). ANY CHANGE TO THE COVERAGE BASIS ITSELF IS TIER-2 and must be proposed, not shipped.

items.title: An accessor-level test suite cannot reach a diag route's executor-hop wiring, so a route that raises TypeError on EVERY request shipped green
items.detail: OBSERVED ON THE FIRST LIVE REQUEST 2026-09-09T16:06:02Z. /api/diag/bybit_raw_closed_pnl (shipped in #11560, merged 0ff2afba) returned read_state 'could_not_look' with error 'TypeError: run_account_read() got an unexpected keyword argument symbol'. The route called run_account_read(fn, acc, symbol=..., start_ms=..., end_ms=...); run_account_read(fn, *args) is POSITIONAL-ONLY because it forwards to loop.run_in_executor, which takes no kwargs. So the route raised on EVERY request and could never have returned a record. || WHY IT SHIPPED GREEN, and this is the finding rather than the typo: 7 accessor assertions in tests/test_bybit_raw_closed_pnl_accessor.py all passed, because they call the accessor DIRECTLY. An accessor-level test cannot reach the route's wiring BY CONSTRUCTION -- the seam between the route and the executor hop is exactly what it does not exercise. Nor could import-time checks: the signature mismatch is only raised when the call executes. `guards` was green and `pytest-run` was green. || THE THREE-STATE DESIGN CONTAINED THE BLAST RADIUS AND SHOULD BE CREDITED HONESTLY: because a raised call is recorded as could_not_look and NEVER folded into no_rows/empty records, the broken route reported 'we could not look' instead of 'the venue booked no close'. On this investigation that distinction was load-bearing -- an empty result would have been read as the venue having no record of trade 5471's close, which is the OPPOSITE finding and a P1 of its own. The state design worked; the wiring did not. || REPRODUCED AND FIXED IN-SESSION: a standalone reproduction of run_account_read's contract raises the identical TypeError with kwargs and returns the bound window correctly via functools.partial. Fix binds the keyword-only window with functools.partial BEFORE the hop. || THE GAP IS GENERAL, NOT SPECIFIC TO THIS ROUTE: any diag route whose accessor takes keyword-only arguments has the same seam, and the repo's own test convention splits accessor tests from route tests precisely because route tests need FastAPI's TestClient, 'which does not import in every environment' -- so the sandbox where accessors are validated is structurally the one that cannot validate wiring.
items.resolution_criteria: A route-level test exists for EVERY /api/diag/* route whose accessor takes keyword-only parameters, asserting the accessor receives those parameters through a run_account_read stub that accepts POSITIONAL ARGS ONLY -- i.e. a stub that reproduces loop.run_in_executor's contract, so a kwargs regression raises in the test exactly as it does live. Verified by a POSITIVE CONTROL: revert the functools.partial in one such route and observe the test FAIL; a suite that stays green under that revert has not been fixed, it has been re-verified as blind. NOT SUFFICIENT: accessor-level tests (they cannot reach the seam by construction, which is the finding); a green `guards` or `pytest-run` (both were green while the route raised on every request); or fixing this one route (tests/test_diag_closed_pnl_route_wiring.py covers it, and the class remains open for every other route with a keyword-only accessor).

items.tier: 2 — the row is served by a read surface on the money path; the MEASUREMENT that found it is Tier-1
items.title: Under BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=partial a Bybit position row emits stop_loss/take_profit/tpsl_mode ALL null while fully protected, so the row alone cannot distinguish 'unprotected' from 'protected on the legs'
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09T17:19:49Z on the live real-money account via /api/diag/bybit_open_orders?account_id=bybit_2 (read_state: orders_read, count 1). POPULATION: ONE position, ONE read -- this is a structural claim about the row's SHAPE, not a rate over a fleet. bybit_2 held XRPUSDT Buy 58.5 @ 1.4121 position_idx 1 with TWO resting Partial legs covering it on BOTH sides -- PartialStopLoss trigger 1.3463 qty 58.5 and PartialTakeProfit trigger 1.5535 qty 58.5, both reduce_only, both Untriggered, both carrying tpsl_mode 'Partial'. Leg qty 58.5 against position size 58.5 on each side. The SAME payload's position row read stop_loss: null, take_profit: null, tpsl_mode: null -- all three at once. So on that row 'unprotected' and 'protected on the legs' are the same value, and tpsl_mode, the field that should discriminate, is null too. MECHANISM, corroborated by Bybit's own API docs rather than inferred (bybit-exchange.github.io/docs/v5/position/trading-stop): Full mode 'can be used to MODIFY the parameters of existing TP/SL orders' while Partial mode 'can only ADD partial position TP/SL orders' and 'passing these parameters will create CONDITIONAL ORDERS by the system internally'. Full mode mutates state ON the position; Partial mode creates separate orders, so the position row is empty by construction. src/units/accounts/clients.py::_bybit_position_row maps stopLoss/takeProfit/tpSlMode straight through and inherits that emptiness. [!] NOT A LIVE BUG TODAY, AND THE BOUND IS THE POINT -- CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: both callers of _bybit_position_row are inside account_bybit_open_orders, which ALWAYS ships the resting legs in the same payload, so a consumer of that route CAN tell and no consumer of ours is blind. The row is safe only because of a property of its one current caller, not because it is well-formed. A second caller returning positions WITHOUT the legs would make it a live real-money blindness with no change to the row itself. [!] DO NOT RESTATE THIS AS 'our surfaces are blind too' -- an earlier draft did, and it is wrong in the direction that manufactures alarm.
items.resolution_criteria: A Bybit position row is interpretable ALONE: it carries a leg-derived protection read beside the position-level fields -- covered qty per side and a state that distinguishes protected_on_position / protected_on_legs / unprotected / could_not_look -- verified by reading a LIVE Partial-mode position off /api/diag and seeing a non-null protection state while stopLoss stays null. [!] A test fixture does NOT clear this; the whole finding is about what the venue returns. [!] AND IF THE DECISION IS TO LEAVE THE ROW AS IS because its one caller always ships the legs, that CLEARS this row only as a RECORDED decision naming the invariant a future second caller would have to preserve -- not by the row going quiet.

items.title: RECURRENCE of BL-20260904 through CLAUDE.md's OWN newly-documented remedy: open-the-PR-yourself + create-as-draft leaves auto-merge unarmed, and marking it ready afterwards does not retroactively arm it
items.detail: OBSERVED on PR #11576, 2026-09-09. POPULATION: one PR, one occurrence -- filed as a RECURRENCE of a known class rather than as a rate. CLAUDE.md documents the remedy for the claude-pr-automerge zero-check trap (which hit SIX times on 2026-09-08) as 'OPEN THE PR YOURSELF FIRST, THEN PUSH THE ARMING FILE' -- because the workflow ADOPTS an existing PR rather than opening its own, so CI fires normally. That half worked: #11576 carried 6 real check runs instead of 1. [!] BUT THE STANDING INSTRUCTION IS TO CREATE PULL REQUESTS AS DRAFTS, and GitHub REFUSES to enable auto-merge on a draft PR. Following both instructions produces a PR that is green, adopted, arming-file present, guard passing -- and NOT armed. MEASURED SEQUENCE: open-and-automerge (run 34381990014) completed 17:17:36Z; the PR was marked ready_for_review at 17:17:40Z, FOUR SECONDS LATER. The workflow had already run and exited, and its trigger is a push touching .github/pr-automerge-requests/, so marking ready never re-ran it and nothing ever armed. The PR sat green and unmerged until auto-merge was enabled by hand at 17:22:32Z. [!] RECURRENCE OF BL-20260904-A-TIER-1-SELF-LAND-PR-OPENED-BY-PR-OPENER-IS-A-DRAFT-AND-CAN-NEVER-SELF-LAND-FROM-A-WEB-SESSION, reached by a DIFFERENT route, which is why it is filed rather than folded in: that row is about pr-opener creating the draft, and its remedy IS the open-it-yourself path. The new path reproduces the same end state through the fix for the old one. THE DRAFT STATE, NOT THE OPENER, IS THE INVARIANT CAUSE. [!] THE FAILURE IS SILENT IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION: every visible signal reads healthy -- guard state=declared_self_land, all checks green, arming file in the diff -- so the PR looks ready to land and simply never does. Same 'looks-armed-is-not' class this repo already tracks for env gates. CONFIRMED BY CONTRAST on the very next PR: #11578, identical arming file and guard, opened NON-DRAFT, was armed by the workflow itself at 17:31:03Z.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) claude-pr-automerge FAILS LOUDLY (non-zero, named check) rather than exiting 0 when it cannot arm because the PR is a draft -- verified by a run log on a deliberately drafted PR showing the red; OR (b) it un-drafts a PR it ADOPTED (adoption is consent; it already correctly refuses to un-draft one it did not open), verified on a real PR; OR (c) CLAUDE.md's remedy paragraph states that the PR must be opened NON-DRAFT for the arming file to take, AND a session is observed following it. [!] (c) alone is a prose fix for a class this repo has twice paid for as prose -- prefer (a), which is the board-post.yml posture of refusing to report a post it did not make. [!] A GREEN SELF-TEST CLEARS NOTHING: the failure is that a real workflow exits 0 having armed nothing.

items.summary: The documented rollback MULTI_STRATEGY_INTENT_LAYER=false routes signal generation to a second, parallel builder registry holding 16 of 55 strategies, so exercising it would silently stop 35 of 45 execution:live legs (78%), each logged as an ordinary logger.warning and skipped. No test asserts the two registries agree.
items.evidence: AST parse of src/runtime/pipeline.py: _STRATEGY_BUILDERS n=16. execution:live legs in config/strategies.yaml n=45. Missing from the rollback registry: 35 of 45 (78%) -- ada_pullback_2h, eth_pullback_2h, gdx_pullback_1d, gld_pullback_1d, gld_pullback_1h, iaum_pullback_1d, ict_scalp_avax_5m, ict_scalp_eth_15m and 27 more. pipeline.py:506-509 builder = _STRATEGY_BUILDERS.get(name); if builder is None: logger.warning('Multiplexer: unknown strategy %s -- skipping'); continue. pipeline.py:671 documents the path as 'fall back to it without a code change'. CLAUDE.md calls MULTI_STRATEGY_INTENT_LAYER 'the core intent-aggregation switch, default on'. grep -rn '_STRATEGY_BUILDERS' tests/ for a parity assertion returns NOTHING. The primary registry grew 16->55 across 2026-05..07 and the rollback registry was never followed.
items.resolution_criteria: Clears when EITHER (a) _STRATEGY_BUILDERS is DELETED and multiplexed_signal_builder calls _resolve_builders(), collapsing the two registries into one -- the preferred fix, since syncing two hand-maintained registries recreates the class; OR (b) a test asserts set(_default_intent_builders()) == set(pipeline._STRATEGY_BUILDERS) and is observed FAILING before the fix and passing after. NOT SUFFICIENT: adding the 39 missing entries by hand without the parity test, which leaves the same drift mechanism in place. NOT SUFFICIENT: documenting the gap -- the rollback is advertised in-code as safe, so the doc is not where a session exercising it would look.
items.notes: Found by the MI-225 full-system audit MODULARITY pass and re-verified from AST by the audit lead rather than taken from a sub-agent. The failure mode is the worst available: the rollback appears to work. OPERATOR DISPOSITION RECORDED 2026-09-09 (manager session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj). Answered directly in the Claude Code chat via an AskUserQuestion option picker -- NOT through the transit log, so commit_work_decisions.py has nothing to replay and the answer block on the work object was written by hand. APPROVED, TIER-2 SIGNAL PATH: chosen `collapse_to_one_registry` -- delete pipeline._STRATEGY_BUILDERS and route the rollback through the SAME resolver the primary uses, rather than policing two registries with a parity test. Answer block: docs/claude/work/objects/WO-20260909-DECISION-THE-ROLLBACK-REGISTRY-IS-AN-OUTAGE.yaml. !! DELETING THE SECOND REGISTRY IS THE POINT -- a parity test alone leaves the duplication that caused this, and the operator declined that option explicitly. !! THE ROLLBACK MUST STILL WORK AFTERWARDS: the build is not done until MULTI_STRATEGY_INTENT_LAYER=false is EXERCISED and all 45 execution:live legs still build. A parity assertion stays valuable as the recurrence detector once the second registry is gone. BUILD IN FLIGHT as MI-229 at the time of writing.
