items.title: pr-landing R13 makes docs/claude/session-board.json::merge_slot a guaranteed conflict between any two concurrently-armed PRs, and it cost the full-system audit three ~18-minute CI restarts
items.detail: RECURRENCE, filed with similar_ok because the earlier remedy did not hold and THAT is the finding. pr-landing R13 REFUSES a branch that arms .github/pr-automerge-requests/ without writing docs/claude/session-board.json::merge_slot in its OWN diff -- correctly, because arming IS the merge (claude-pr-automerge enables auto-merge under GITHUB_TOKEN and the PreToolUse slot guard is structurally blind to that route). But merge_slot is a SINGLE-HOLDER key, so any two branches armed at the same time write the same lines and conflict BY CONSTRUCTION. The mechanism intended to SERIALISE merges instead makes every concurrent pair dirty each other. MEASURED 2026-09-09, population = the manager PRs and #11571 across 19:00-20:20Z. #11571 (the MI-225 full-system audit, 2288 additions across 15 files) had its CI restarted THREE times -- 19:11, 19:33 and 19:55 -- and at least two of those were caused by this manager landing register PRs (#11588 at 19:33, #11589 at 19:55). #11571's own diff carries docs/claude/session-board.json +4/-4, which is R13 forcing it. Each restart is a ~18-minute full pytest-run. Earlier the same day the same key forced five rebases on manager branches and one session reported eight forced merge cycles on a single PR. !! THE MANAGER PREDICTED NO CONFLICT AND WAS WRONG, which is why this is filed rather than shrugged at: it listed session-board.json on its own side and still concluded the diffs did not overlap, failing to reason that R13 forces the OTHER branch onto the same key. A collision that is structural should not need to be rediscovered per PR. !! A BOARD POST DID NOT STOP IT. This contention was already posted to the coordination board earlier today for the guard's owning lane, and three more restarts happened afterwards. A post that changes no mechanism is not a mechanism -- that the earlier filing did not hold IS this row's contribution. !! DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY DROPPING THE CLAIM. That was tried and R13 correctly refused it; a branch that arms without claiming is exactly what the rule exists to catch. Nor by declaring landing: hold on a false HOLD_REASONS value -- another session read the closed vocabulary and refused to fabricate a landing record, which was the right call. CANDIDATE DIRECTIONS, none implemented and none endorsed here: (a) make the claim APPEND-ONLY (a list of claims with the newest last) so two branches add different lines and git merges them, with the invariant moved to 'at most one UNRELEASED claim' and checked rather than represented by file position; (b) move the claim off a committed file entirely, onto a surface that has no merge semantics; (c) have R13 accept a claim made in the PR body or a label. Sizing which is right is this row's work, not the manager's. === FOURTH INSTANCE, 2026-09-10T04:4xZ, manager session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj. One manager heartbeat branch (claude/mgr-hb-20260910T0416, PR #11639) had to be REBASED TWICE inside about four minutes, and on both rebases the ONLY conflicting hunk was session-board.json::merge_slot — main moved under it because automation PRs were merging, and each of those merges rewrote the same single-holder key. The rebase route was chosen over merging main in because check_manager_scope R2 reads a merge commit's FIRST-PARENT diff, which would have attributed main's scripts/ml/** and tests/** changes to the manager. !! THIS IS AN ANECDOTE AND IT DOES NOT SATISFY CLAUSE (1) OF THIS ROW'S resolution_criteria, which asks for a RATE over a stated population and window with the CI minutes lost. It is recorded here so the instance is not lost, and deliberately NOT filed as a new row: backlog_search returns EIGHT overlapping rows (two at 0.80/0.70 describing this exact mechanism), every one of them still `open` with no fix attempted, so a fifth row would be near-duplicate accumulation rather than a recurrence finding. !! IT ALSO CONFIRMS THE STRUCTURAL CLAIM RATHER THAN MERELY REPEATING IT: the manager's heartbeat branch conflicts with EVERY automation merge BY CONSTRUCTION, because R13 makes both write the same key, and the manager is the one actor guaranteed to have a branch open across other people's merges.
items.evidence: origin/main 566c0ff4c (#11571 landed 20:19Z). #11571 check-run restarts at 19:11, 19:33:43Z and 19:55:36Z on distinct run ids (34395781952/63/64, 34397953880/84/88/98). #11571 file list read via pull_request_read get_files: docs/claude/session-board.json +4/-4. Manager landings in the same window: #11588 (6295bce38), #11589 (986dc2f1c), both touching docs/claude/session-board.json. scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py R13.
items.resolution_criteria: TWO PARTS, different facts -- say which you delivered. (1) MEASURED: the rate at which concurrently-armed PRs conflict on merge_slot, over a stated population of PRs and a stated window, with the CI minutes lost. Nobody has this number; today's figures are one manager's anecdotes, not a rate. (2) A MECHANISM under which two branches can both satisfy R13 without writing the same lines -- and it must be shown by ARMING TWO BRANCHES CONCURRENTLY and observing no conflict, not by a green unit test. !! A THIRD BOARD POST CLEARS NOTHING; that is what already failed. !! IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES the contention is an acceptable cost, this row does NOT clear -- it CHANGES: that is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one rather than left looking like a fix about to happen.

items.summary: F-61 of the 2026-09-09 full-system audit is REFUTED on its named instances: all four guards it reports as `self-test code present, invoked=0` ARE invoked with --self-test by run_guards.py. The cause is that their argv is wrapped across two source lines, which a single-line grep cannot see.
items.evidence: MEASURED 2026-09-09 on branch claude/mi226-required-guards-failure-path, against origin/main 566c0ff4c. Population: the four guards F-61 names -- check_cost_model_single_owner, check_role_pack_operating_layer, check_tp_venue_cap_single_owner, check_workflow_trigger_reachability. (a) run_guards.py lines 438-440, 465-467, 1620-1622, 1636-1638 each hold ["python3", "scripts/ci/check_X.py",\n "--self-test"] -- a two-line list literal, self-test FIRST, each with a load-bearing comment saying why. (b) EXECUTED, all four: rc=0 with '10/10 passed', 'ALL PASS', '13/13 passed', 'ALL PASS'. (c) THE MECHANISM, with a POSITIVE CONTROL: `grep -c 'check_X.py", "--self-test"'` returns 0 for all four and 1 for check_lever_reachability.py, whose argv fits on one line. So the probe CAN find the pattern and simply cannot see a wrapped one. F-61's UNDERLYING claim stands and is not disputed: check_selftest_wiring.py's denominator is the SELFTESTS registry, not the guard population, and that is what let F-05's four hide. Only the four instance names attributed to the second half are wrong.
items.resolution_criteria: Tier-1. Clears when the audit doc's F-61 row records the refutation with its evidence, so a later session does not 're-fix' four guards that are already wired -- which would be a diff that changes nothing while reading as progress. The general lesson is already MECHANISED and needs no further action: scripts/ci/check_guard_selftest_coverage.py resolves invocations from run_guards.py's AST and compares argv tokens by exact membership, and carries a control ('a `--self-test` argv WRAPPED across two source lines counts as invoked') that fails if it ever regresses to text matching.
items.notes: Filed by the MI-226 sub-session while acting on F-05/F-61. This is the second measured instance in this audit of a probe whose negative was not a negative -- the audit corrected its own 16/79 to 54/79 for a related reason and left the correction visible. Recording it because the repo's standing rule is that a search returning nothing is not proof of absence, and the positive control here PASSED while the probe was still wrong: the control proved the probe could match the ONE-LINE form, which is a different form from the one being looked for.

items.summary: F-04's detector -- 'require each self-test to include at least one assertion on main([...])'s return or a subprocess return code' -- is measured at 17 of 58 wired self-tests, so it ships REPORTED rather than GATED. Gating it on day one would have failed 41 guards and redded every PR.
items.evidence: MEASURED 2026-09-09 by scripts/ci/check_guard_selftest_coverage.py over its own population. Population: the 58 guards whose failure path RESOLVES inside the required `guards` merge context (of 80 guard scripts on disk). 58/58 satisfy the GATED property `asserts_a_verdict` (the self-test exercises something and compares the answer); 17/58 satisfy F-04's stricter `asserts_on_main_or_rc`. The gap is not laziness: the house idiom asserts on the guard's own DECISION FUNCTIONS after planting a violation -- check_role_pack_operating_layer.py's `check(label, got, want)` table and check_one_live_workplan.py's `_expect(root, 1, ...)` are both genuine planted-failure tests that never call main(). That idiom is legitimate evidence.
items.resolution_criteria: Tier-1, and it is a RATCHET not a sprint. Clears when either (a) `asserts_on_main_or_rc` is raised far enough that it can become a second gate, and check_guard_selftest_coverage.py gates it with its own floor; or (b) a session establishes that asserting on a decision function is EQUIVALENT evidence and F-04's wording is narrowed in the audit doc, in which case this row closes as a corrected-detector rather than as work. Do NOT close it by deleting the metric -- the number is printed on every run precisely so it cannot go quiet.
items.notes: Filed by the MI-226 sub-session, which BUILT the instrument that measures this and deliberately did not gate on it. Stated rather than hidden because the repo has paid for the other choice: a guard that fails a large pre-existing population on day one gets DISABLED instead of fixed, which is why check_pr_queue_watch.py passes on `never_ran` and why the diagnostic-provenance residue had to be drained to 0 before its --all step could be made ungated.

items.summary: 21 guards have no failure path in the `guards` context and rest entirely on a pytest file that names them. Statically all 21 appear to plant a violation and assert on it, but that was read, not executed -- they are UNPROVEN, not disproven, and must never be summed into a coverage number.
items.evidence: MEASURED 2026-09-09 by scripts/ci/check_guard_selftest_coverage.py: population 80 guard scripts on disk; 58 covered in the required `guards` context; 21 `pytest_only`; 1 `none` (exempted, see below). STATED LIMIT, and it is the point of this row: pytest is ABSENT from the sub-session container, so none of the 21 was executed here. A first static classifier put 20 of 21 in 'plants a failure and asserts on it' and 2 in 'asserts only that the guard passes'; reading those 2 by hand showed BOTH do plant (tests/test_roadmap_status_glyphs.py::test_guard_flags_offspec_glyph asserts the offender list == ['M99']; tests/test_lever_wiring_guard.py::test_the_guard_can_fail asserts a planted 'GRADEABLE' failure), so the classifier UNDER-counted and the honest static reading is 21 of 21. That is a reading of source, not an observation of a red test. This restates and re-measures the audit's own stated limit about its 21 rows -- it verified only that a file naming the guard exists.
items.resolution_criteria: Tier-1. Clears when a session WITH pytest available mutates each of the 21 guards to break its invariant and OBSERVES the corresponding test go red, then records the count -- a green suite proves nothing here, which is the whole class. ⚠️ It does NOT clear by moving the 21 into the `guards` context: that would raise the coverage number without establishing anything about the tests, and the two populations are kept separate in the instrument precisely so they cannot be traded off. ⚠️ Nor does it clear on the static reading above, which is why that reading is recorded as evidence and not as a pass.
items.notes: Filed by the MI-226 sub-session. The 1 remaining `none` is scripts/ci/check_guard_glob_coverage.py, which is a DIFFERENT and larger finding -- it is not reachable from run_guards.py at all (audit F-02, 'structurally unarmable as written') -- and is exemption-listed in scripts/ci/guard_selftest_exemptions.json with that reasoning, dated, and reported by name under declared_but_never_invoked on every run so it cannot go quiet behind the exemption.

items.title: Four times in one session an identifier was elided or line-wrapped into a reference that resolves to nothing, and prose discipline did not hold
items.summary: MEASURED on session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj, 2026-09-09, n=4 in roughly two hours. (1) textwrap.fill broke BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG across two lines inside a YAML folded scalar, which rejoins with a SPACE, so the parsed value named a row that does not exist -- caught by artifact-validity-guard on #11597. (2) The same wrap split INV-PROTECT-LEG-MATCHES-ROW and INV-PROTECT-OVERCOVER inside the done_condition that defines what an operator's Tier-2 order-path approval requires -- caught by my own sweep, NOT by any guard. (3) Three backlog ids written with a '...' elision in a closed_by_manager block -- caught by artifact-validity-guard on #11598. (4) BL-20260909-MERGE-SLOT-IS-NEVER-RELEASED-AFTER-A-MERGE-SO-EVERY-CLAIMANT-DISPLACES-A-GHOST written without its tail in session-board.json -- caught by artifact-validity-guard on the lease heartbeat PR. !! THE PATTERN IS NOT CARELESSNESS ABOUT ONE ID: long ids are routinely shortened for readability and the shortened form is indistinguishable from a real one at the point of writing. The 2026-07-30 operator directive the guard cites is exactly this -- a doc saying 'tracked by BL-X' where BL-X was never filed reads as TRACKED while being tracked by NOBODY. !! NOT A DUPLICATE OF BL-20260821-BACKLOG-JSON-IS-A-SHARED-MUTABLE-ARRAY, which the appender's similarity probe surfaced at overlap 0.73 and which I read before re-filing: that row is about CONCURRENT SESSIONS COLLIDING on one shared JSON array. This row is about a REFERENCE TO A ROW being written in a form that does not resolve. The overlap is lexical (both say backlog/json/row) and the probe is token overlap with no semantics, exactly as it warns.
items.evidence: artifact-validity-guard failures on PR #11597 and PR #11598 (job 102653641966 named it in the FAILING GUARDS block; the log TAIL does not name the guard, which cost a second log fetch). Case (2) was found only by grepping '[A-Z0-9]-$' over the changed files after case (1) -- no guard reads a folded scalar's REJOINED value, so an identifier split across lines inside one is invisible to check_backlog_refs when neither half is itself an id.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) a check that reads YAML/JSON VALUES rather than raw lines, so an identifier split by a folded scalar and rejoined with a space is caught -- the class case (2) proves is currently undetected; OR (b) an explicit recorded decision that prose discipline is the only control here, with the reasoning. !! DO NOT close this on 'the author will be more careful' -- that is the remedy MI-15 applied twice before it was made machinery, and it failed both times. !! AND NOTE WHAT ALREADY WORKS: check_backlog_refs caught 3 of the 4 and is not the gap. The gap is case (2)'s shape -- an identifier that is not a backlog id, split inside a folded scalar.
notes: Filed by the manager as the act of NOT taking the item: the fix is under scripts/, a worker path the manager may not author (check_manager_scope R2).

items.summary: MI-227 fixed the PARTIALLY consumed half of audit F-36 and deliberately left the FULLY consumed half: when an intent-reduce consumes a parent row entirely, that row closes at size 0 and its own tracked Bybit Partial-tpsl leg is left resting. There is no resize for zero -- clearing such a leg would be a CANCEL, which the operator's 2026-09-09 approval explicitly withholds. The residual is now COUNTED (`legs_left_resting_on_closed_rows` on the reduce audit row's notes) rather than invisible; what is missing is a decision about what should clear it.
items.evidence: REASONED FROM THE VENUE MODEL, NOT MEASURED -- and that distinction is this row's first job. Under BYBIT_TPSL_MODE=partial each trade carries its own qty-scoped reduce-only leg. An intent-reduce that fully consumes parent A shrinks the NETTED position by A's size without taking it to zero, so Bybit does not auto-cancel reduce-only orders, so A's leg should still rest while A's journal row is closed -- leaving the symbol over-covered by A's size. NO LIVE INSTANCE OF THIS SPECIFIC SHAPE WAS OBSERVED. Audit F-36's standing instance (bybit_1/ADAUSDT 2026-09-09T16:47Z) is the PARTIAL case: resting stops totalled 143170.0 = 79227.0 + 63943.0, i.e. exactly TWO legs for TWO open rows, with no third leg belonging to a closed row -- so that reading is evidence about the partial half and says nothing either way about this one. Class incidence for intent-reduce overall is 21 of 1000 journal rows (bybit_1 15, bybit_portfolio 3, bybit_2 3 -- REAL MONEY); how many of those 21 fully consumed a parent has NOT been counted. The counting instrument now exists: src/units/accounts/execute.py::apply_intent_reduce_partial_close returns `legs_left_resting_on_closed_rows` and execute_pkg writes it onto the `intent_reduce_executed` audit row's notes, so the next reduce that hits this shape records it. INV-PROTECT-LEG-MATCHES-ROW (scripts/ops/system_invariants.py) does NOT catch it: its population is OPEN rows, and a closed row's leg has no position_size to match -- stated here rather than left for someone to discover.
items.next_step: TWO STEPS, and the first is not the second. (1) MEASURE: read `/api/diag/log_file?name=...` is not the surface -- query the journal for `exit_reason='intent_reduce_executed'` rows whose notes carry `legs_left_resting_on_closed_rows`, and cross-check the named order ids against `/api/diag/bybit_open_orders` to establish whether such a leg actually rests. A zero count over a window in which fully-consumed reduces DID occur is the negative result and retires this row; a zero count with no fully-consumed reduce in the window establishes nothing. (2) ONLY THEN decide the remedy, and it is Tier-2/3 and the OPERATOR's: cancelling a closed row's own tracked leg is a cancel on a live book, and BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG records that the one prior attempt at remediating an over-covered book by cancelling cancelled the leg that MATCHED the journal. Do not propose a cancel off this row's reasoning alone.
items.not_a_duplicate_of: backlog_search returned 8 lexical overlaps at 0.46-0.55 and NONE is this finding. Read and rejected: the two IB / Full-mode re-arm over-cover rows (BL-20260816-IB-STOPS-OVER-COVER-IN-DISJOINT-OCA-GROUPS, and the 2026-09-08 row about a Full-mode naked re-arm placed over still-resting Partial legs); the two rows about a venue ACCEPTING a cancel it does not perform (the 2026-08-16 IB one and the 2026-09-08 Alpaca one); the two Alpaca symbol-scoping rows from 2026-09-08 (modify_protective taking no trade identity, and place_protective ignoring the oca key); BL-20260816-IB-CLOSE-ABANDONS-ITS-OWN-ORDER; and BL-20260823-MODIFY-IDEMPOTENCE-COMPARES-INTENT-TO-JOURNAL-NEVER-TO-VENUE, which is the trigger-PRICE divergence class and is resolved. This one is the Bybit intent-reduce path specifically, on the CLOSED-row half that MI-227 did not build. Filed with similar_ok after reading all 8. (The sibling ids above are deliberately DESCRIBED rather than quoted: a bare id in this field reads to check_backlog_refs.py as a tracking reference, and an abbreviated one resolves to nothing -- which is exactly the crack that guard exists to close.)
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER of two OPPOSITE outcomes, and they are different findings — say which. (a) IT IS REAL: a `trades` row with exit_reason='intent_reduce_executed' is found whose notes carry a non-empty `legs_left_resting_on_closed_rows`, AND at least one order id named there is still present in /api/diag/bybit_open_orders with a non-zero qty. That is the sighting a Tier-2/3 remedy proposal would rest on, and the manager — not this row — puts it to the operator. (b) IT DOES NOT HAPPEN: over a window containing at least 3 reduces that FULLY consumed a parent (the denominator, and it is not optional — a window with no fully-consumed reduce establishes nothing), no named order id is ever found resting. That RETIRES the remedy question and must be RECORDED as that decision rather than left looking like a measurement still running. !! AN EMPTY notes FIELD ACROSS THE WHOLE WINDOW CLEARS NEITHER and is itself a finding: it means either no reduce fully consumed a parent (check the denominator first) or the writer is not writing, and those are opposite facts. !! A GREEN TEST SUITE CLEARS NOTHING — tests/test_intent_reduce_leg_resize.py asserts the residual is REPORTED, not that it does or does not occur on a venue. !! AND MERGING #MI-227 CLEARS NOTHING: the counting instrument shipping is not an observation.

items.tier: 1 — tooling/cadence; arming a trigger touches .github/ only
items.summary: scripts/ops/build_strategy_evidence.py (MI-216) ships `# wiring: manual-only`, so a per-leg offline edge record in comms/strategy_evidence/ goes STALE SILENTLY the moment that leg's config changes. The record carries a `config_fingerprint` precisely so a moved config is DETECTABLE -- but nothing currently COMPARES it. Detectable and detected are different facts, and only the first shipped. ⚠️ THIS IS THE SAME FAILURE CLASS THE PRODUCER EXISTS TO FIX, ONE LEVEL UP: MI-215 found the M7 gate grading edge off live closes because no offline artifact existed; an offline artifact that quietly describes a configuration the leg no longer has would be worse, because it reads as evidence. ⚠️ AND THE NATURAL TRIGGER IS NOT A CLOCK. An edge record does not decay with time -- the underlying history only grows -- it decays when config/strategies.yaml moves. A nightly cron would refetch a year of candles for 52 legs to keep records nobody had yet asked for, while STILL missing a config change made five minutes after it ran.
items.detail: DEFERRED DELIBERATELY, not overlooked: the consumer that will say how fresh a record must be is MI-217 (the packet emitting `no_offline_evidence` instead of `hold`), and it does not exist yet. Wiring a cadence before its consumer sets a freshness policy nobody has a requirement for. CANDIDATE SHAPES, none applied: (a) a CI check that recomputes config_fingerprint for every committed record and fails a PR that moves a leg's config without refreshing (or explicitly invalidating) its record -- this is the config-change trigger, is free, and needs no candle fetch; (b) a workflow_dispatch + issue-label runner so a session can regenerate on demand on a free runner rather than the trainer VM (docs/claude/vm-resource-management.md); (c) the consumer treats a fingerprint mismatch as `no_offline_evidence` and never as a pass -- which makes staleness fail CLOSED and may make (a) belt-and-braces rather than required. ⚠️ (c) IS THE CHEAPEST AND SHOULD BE COSTED FIRST; do not reach for the cron. NOT MEASURED: how often a leg's config actually moves. Someone should count it over config/strategies.yaml's history before choosing between (a) and (b), because if legs move monthly the answer is different from if they move hourly.
items.resolution_criteria: A record whose leg's config has MOVED is OBSERVED being refused or refreshed rather than read as current -- demonstrated on a real fingerprint mismatch, not asserted from the code. ⚠️ A GREEN CI RUN CLEARS NOTHING: green is the state today, with no comparison happening at all. The evidence is a PLANTED mismatch (edit a leg's config, leave its record) producing a refusal, and passing once the record is refreshed -- the positive-control shape MI-215 and MI-218 both used. ⚠️ AND IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES records may be consumed regardless of fingerprint, this row does NOT clear -- it CHANGES: that is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one, with the consequence stated, rather than left looking like a trigger about to be built.

items.title: ranking-key-ab.yml declares 11 workflow_dispatch inputs against GitHub's hard limit of 10, so it startup-fails on EVERY push to claude/** and its workflow_dispatch is dead — the A/B it exists to run has never been runnable
items.tier: 1 — a .github/workflows/ file; CI/tooling, no runtime or order path
items.filed_by: MI-216 session (session_01MrTjuoRpBb7spyQLydXmmT), incidental to CI verification on PR #11587
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-09T20:35Z. .github/workflows/ranking-key-ab.yml declares ELEVEN workflow_dispatch inputs (symbol, days, roster, clock_tf, signal_ttl_bars, arms, arbitration, books, folds, seed, commit_results). GitHub's documented hard limit is TEN. The file is therefore invalid to GitHub's workflow parser, which has two consequences that are DIFFERENT FACTS and must not be reported as one.

(1) NOISE: it emits a zero-duration `startup_failure` run on every push to `claude/**`. Population: the 10 most recent runs (run_number 417-426), ALL conclusion=failure, ALL with created_at == run_started_at == updated_at, across FIVE branches (claude/mi216-per-leg-offline-edge-record, claude/mgr-hb-2032-20260909, claude/mgr-route-audit-20260909T2020, claude/lane4-stale-automation-landing-20260909, claude/mi225-full-system-audit) and FOUR different sessions. 426 runs exist in total; only the newest 10 were read, so 'every run has always failed' is NOT established — what is established is that the last 10 did, across unrelated authors. Note this fires DESPITE a `paths:` filter naming `.github/ranking-key-ab-request`, a file that DOES NOT EXIST in the tree and which none of these pushes touched: an invalid workflow cannot have its path filter applied, so the filter that should make it near-silent is inert.

(2) THE CAPABILITY IS DEAD, AND THIS IS THE HALF THAT MATTERS. workflow_dispatch on an invalid file cannot be dispatched, so the ranking-key A/B experiment this workflow exists to run CANNOT BE RUN BY ANYONE. It reads as present infrastructure and is entirely inert — the 'looks armed and is not' class. Its own input descriptions carry a careful measured calibration for signal_ttl_bars (ttl 1 -> 1 contested election, 8 -> 20, 16 -> 87, 48 -> 677, 96 -> 1712 on 400d of BTCUSDT) and an explicit refusal to manufacture the population, i.e. real design work sitting behind a door that does not open.

HOW IT WAS FOUND: incidentally, while verifying CI on an unrelated PR (#11587, MI-216). It is invisible in normal use because it is a `push`-event workflow, so it never appears in a PR's required check set and never blocks anything — nobody is paged and no PR turns red. That is exactly why it has survived: the failure is real, continuous, and costs nothing anyone notices.

NOT FIXED HERE, deliberately: this is outside MI-216's declared scope, and the fix is a design choice (which input to drop, or fold two into one CSV) that belongs to whoever owns the ranking-key experiment, not to a session that tripped over it.
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH, and they are different facts — say which you cleared. (a) The input count is brought to <= 10 (drop one, or fold two into a single CSV input — the file already uses CSV inputs for `roster` and `arms`, so the pattern exists) AND a push to a `claude/**` branch is OBSERVED producing NO ranking-key-ab run, or a run that is not a zero-duration failure. Read the run history, never the workflow file. (b) A `workflow_dispatch` run of ranking-key-ab.yml is OBSERVED reaching a non-startup conclusion — i.e. the experiment can actually be run. ⚠️ (a) WITHOUT (b) IS THE TRAP: silencing the push noise while leaving the A/B undispatchable fixes the symptom nobody was paying for and leaves the capability dead. ⚠️ A GREEN YAML LINT CLEARS NOTHING — the file parses fine as YAML today (verified with yaml.safe_load); the violation is a GitHub-specific schema limit no YAML parser knows about. ⚠️ AND IF THE OWNER DECIDES the experiment is retired, this row does NOT clear — it CHANGES: the workflow should then be DELETED rather than left emitting a startup failure on every push, and that must be RECORDED as a decision rather than left looking like a fix about to happen.

items.summary: RECURRENCE of BL-20260816-EXIT-EVAL-INTERVAL-AT-60S-REQUIREMENT, which reads `resolved` (closed 2026-08-22 by #10129 at requirement_state `within`, interval_breaches 0, n=147) -- and the requirement was breached again SIXTEEN DAYS LATER, on 2026-09-07. That the earlier fix did not hold is half the finding. Audit finding F-50, which reached the OPERATOR AS A DECISION AND HAD NO BACKLOG ROW TO LAND IN -- this row is that landing, filed after the fact by the manager, and the filing gap is itself half the point. The M20 60s exit-evaluation promise was BREACHED on 2026-09-07 (recorded fact, not inference) and today's worst observed interval clears the requirement by 48.8 ms. The distribution BODY is unchanged since 2026-08-25 -- only the tail moved -- so the '15.0 s of margin' CLAUDE.md records is gone while every instrument still reads `within` / `interval_breaches: 0`.
items.evidence: TRANSCRIBED from docs/audits/full-system-audit-2026-09-09.md F-50; the manager re-ran no measurement. exit_interval_soak n=989 intervals / 12 processes / 2026-09-09T08:36:14Z->16:54:41Z: mean 29880.6, median 29993.1, p95 34886.9, MAX 59951.2 ms, over_requirement 0 of 1000. MAX ROW: interval_ms 59951.2, pass_ms 31399.1, requirement_s 60.0, over_requirement false. exit_loop_health_alert_state carries {'stale': false, 'requirement_breach_process': '2026-09-07T22:48:54.737905+00:00'}, and exit_loop_health.py:507-519 writes that field ONLY when requirement_state=='breached' fires the alert, so the 09-07 breach is recorded rather than reconstructed. Mechanism by arithmetic from the row's own neighbours: interval = (cadence - prev_pass) + cur_pass, so the requirement breaks whenever a pass is >30 s slower than the one before it; here prev=1448.9 ms, cur=31399.1 ms, delta=29950.2 ms -- it missed by 49.8 ms. One row in the same window (pass_ms 34691.6) WOULD have produced a 63,050 ms interval had it followed a median pass. Against CLAUDE.md's 2026-08-25 reading (n=991 / 10 processes / 8.3 h, same window shape): MAX 45034 ms -> 59951.2 ms, pass 2222 -> 2921.4 ms mean and 19481 -> 34691.6 ms max, while mean 29879 -> 29880.6 and median 29970 -> 29993.1 are unmoved.
items.resolution_criteria: Tier-2, and the operator HAS decided (see notes). Clears when BOTH: (a) exit_loop_health publishes a NEAR-MISS band -- max_interval_ms / requirement_ms >= 0.9 grades WARN, a state DISTINCT from `breached` and from `within`, with a planted-control self-test proving it can reach WARN; and (b) the RESTART GAP (last pass of process N -> first pass of process N+1) is graded against the same 60 s requirement, because it is the one interval the promise covers and the instrument excludes by construction. NOT SUFFICIENT: over_requirement staying 0 -- a binary at a strict threshold cannot see a 48.8 ms miss, which is the entire finding. NOT SUFFICIENT: a green test suite -- a harness cannot produce a process restart on the live trader. NOT SUFFICIENT: merging -- a merge is not a deploy and a deploy is not a graded interval. AND A CONTINUED `within` CLEARS NOTHING: `within` is exactly what the instrument read on 2026-09-07 either side of a breach it recorded in a separate latch. Baseline to compare the restart gap against, measured once in the audit and never since: 11 gaps, 25.3-53.9 s, 0 of 11 over 60 s, 1.3% of wall clock -- clean, but unwatched.
items.notes: WHY THIS ROW EXISTS AT ALL, stated rather than papered over: F-50 was one of SIX audit findings put to the operator as a decision, and it was the only one of the six with no backlog row behind it. The audit filed 19 backlog rows for 68 findings (its own run_record and done_condition_status both say so), so F-50 lacking a row is NOT an anomaly -- it is the normal case for ~49 of the 68. What WAS wrong is a manager claim, written by session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj into the audit work object's closed_by_manager on 2026-09-09, that '67 of 68 are filed in the two review backlogs'. That figure is false, it is mine, and it is corrected in the same change that files this row. A money-at-risk proposal reaching the operator with nothing in the backlog behind it is the real defect the false figure hid. || OPERATOR DISPOSITION RECORDED 2026-09-09 (manager session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj). Answered directly in the Claude Code chat via an AskUserQuestion option picker -- NOT through the transit log, so commit_work_decisions.py has nothing to replay and the answer block on the work object was written by hand. APPROVED, TIER-2 OBSERVABILITY: chosen `near_miss_and_restart_gap` -- the near-miss band AND grading the restart gap, rather than either alone. Answer block: docs/claude/work/objects/WO-20260909-DECISION-M20-EXIT-EVAL-MARGIN-COLLAPSED.yaml. !! THE outcomes.jsonl DELIVERY FIX WAS OFFERED AS A SUPERSET AND WAS NOT CHOSEN, so F-51 (BL-20260909-... is unfiled likewise; the breach page still never reaches the operator feed) stays open and unanswered -- do not read this approval as covering it. !! AN APPROVAL IS NOT A BUILD: the work object is `ready`, never `in_flight`, and no lane has been spawned. || WHAT THE PREDECESSOR ROW STILL SAYS, AND WHY IT IS NOT FLIPPED HERE: BL-20260816-EXIT-EVAL-INTERVAL-AT-60S-REQUIREMENT reads `resolved`, and a reader of that row ALONE would conclude the 60 s requirement holds. It does not, as of 2026-09-07. Its status is deliberately left `resolved` rather than reopened, because #10129 demonstrably DID work on the axis it was closed on -- the distribution BODY is unchanged (mean 29879 -> 29880.6 ms, median 29970 -> 29993.1 ms) and the breach rate fell from 114 of 398 = 28.6% to a single recorded event -- so flipping it to `open` would overstate. What moved is the TAIL alone, which is a different fact and is what this row carries. A reader must hold both, which is exactly why this is filed as a RECURRENCE rather than as an update to that row.

items.summary: check_pr_landing resolves a branch's declaration by BRANCH SLUG (.github/pr-landing/<slug>.json), so a branch RE-CUT from main after its PR merged still carries that merged PR's declaration -- and if the merged PR was a Tier-2 `hold`, R10 refuses any follow-up arming on the same slug. The harness's own guidance says to re-cut the designated branch KEEPING ITS NAME after a merge, so this is reachable from following the documented path, not from doing something unusual. !! THE HAZARD IS THE CHEAPEST FIX, NOT THE REFUSAL: the one-file way past R10 is to rewrite the merged PR's declaration to `tier: 1` / `landing: self`, which satisfies the guard by DESTROYING the record of why that PR was held -- on the one file whose entire job is carrying an attributable landing claim, and which .github/pr-landing/README.md describes as the record a reviewer reads. A guard whose cheapest satisfaction is falsifying the record it protects is the same shape this repo already names for new-table-wiring-guard's presence-only marker ('cheaper to lie to than to satisfy').
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-10 on MI-229. PR #11615 (Tier-2, `landing: hold`, hold_reason tier_2_3_needs_approval) merged as 2ee21f4e5. The close-out was records-only and Tier-1, so it was legitimately self-landable; re-cutting `claude/mi229-collapse-builder-registry` from main and adding `.github/pr-automerge-requests/mi229-collapse-builder-registry.txt` produced, verbatim: `R10 this branch ARMS auto-merge (.github/pr-automerge-requests/mi229-collapse-builder-registry.txt is added/modified) while .github/pr-landing/mi229-collapse-builder-registry.json declares `landing: "hold"` at tier 2. Those are opposite instructions and the arming is the one that would take effect.` The guard is RIGHT on its own terms -- an armed branch beside a hold declaration IS contradictory -- and it has no way to know the hold belonged to an already-merged PR. WORKED AROUND, NOT FIXED, by moving the close-out to a fresh slug (`claude/mi229-closeout-records`) with its own declaration; the deviation from 'keep the same branch name' is stated in that PR's body. POSSIBLE REMEDIES, none applied and none obviously right: (a) let a declaration carry an optional `settled_by_pr` so the guard can tell a spent declaration from a live one, which risks becoming a bypass field; (b) have the guard treat a declaration whose named PR is MERGED as not governing a new arming, which needs a live GitHub read the guards job may not want; (c) accept the fresh-slug workaround and document it in .github/pr-landing/README.md, which is the cheapest and leaves the falsification path open. Choosing between them is a judgement about how much bypass surface to add, so it is filed rather than taken. !! SECOND, SMALLER TRAP HIT THE SAME NIGHT AND WORTH THE SAME ROW: both check_pr_landing.py and scripts/ops/check_backlog_refs.py diff `origin/main...HEAD`, i.e. they grade COMMITTED work. Fixing a finding in the worktree and re-running reports the OLD finding unchanged, which reads exactly like a fix that did not take -- it cost one confused re-run on check_backlog_refs and one on check_pr_landing (the latter graded `declared_needs_approval` while an uncommitted arming file sat on disk, then correctly failed R10 once committed). Neither tool says so in its output.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER of two, and they are different outcomes -- say which. (a) FIXED: check_pr_landing no longer refuses a follow-up arming on a slug whose declaration belongs to an ALREADY-MERGED PR, verified by re-cutting a branch whose PR merged under `landing: hold` and observing `pr-landing: OK` on a Tier-1 arming WITHOUT that merged PR's declaration file having been edited -- that last clause is the whole point, since editing it IS the failure mode this row is about. (b) DOCUMENTED AS INTENDED: .github/pr-landing/README.md states that a follow-up on a settled slug takes a FRESH slug, and says in terms that rewriting a merged PR's declaration is never the remedy. Recording (b) is a legitimate close and must be written down as a decision rather than left looking like a fix in flight. !! NEITHER is cleared by the workaround being used again: MI-229 already routed around it once, and a second session doing the same is evidence the row is REAL, not that it is resolved.
items.source: MI-229 (session_01TM8XjkvVpvMxH4EcLtTsvP) close-out after PR #11615; hit while landing the records-only follow-up.

items.tier: 1 (CI/tooling — the remedy is a wrapper or a guard, not more prose)
items.title: RECURRENCE (third) of BL-20260830-ZERO-CHECK-RUNS-READ-AS-CI-NOT-STARTED-NOT-AS-MERGE-CONFLICT: a manager read three merge-conflicted PRs in one evening as a NEW 'branch wedge' failure class, closed two of them on that false evidence, and came one commit from filing the phantom class as a backlog row — with the corrective paragraph verbatim in its own context window the whole time
items.detail:
WHAT HAPPENED (2026-09-09/10, PRs #11605, #11612, #11619 — all mine). Each showed zero pull_request-event check runs while push-event runs still fired on the same sha. I diagnosed a NEW failure class — a 'branch wedge' — closed #11605 and #11612 on it, re-cut both onto fresh branches, and was one commit from filing the class as its own row on the strength of 'three occurrences in one evening'. 

IT WAS NOT A NEW CLASS. All three read mergeable_state: 'dirty' (measured via pull_request_read method get at 2026-09-10T00:24-00:31Z; bases 2986ce3e / 8f753a34 / 6efbcb2a). GitHub builds pull_request-event runs against the MERGE REF, so when that ref cannot be built the workflows are silently skipped — the documented, expected symptom. 

THE DISPROOF WAS A CONTROL, NOT A RE-READING, and that is the part worth keeping. Re-cutting onto a fresh branch 'worked' every time, which is exactly why the wrong diagnosis kept confirming itself — a re-cut rebuilds the merge ref for the same reason a rebase does. So on #11619 I REBASED instead, changed nothing else, and all five checks fired within ~40s (run ids 102697422375 / 102697422638 / 102697422643 / 102697422695). A wedge does not clear on a rebase; a conflict does. That single substitution falsified the class. 

WHY IT IS A RECURRENCE AND NOT A DUPLICATE, AND WHY IT IS WORSE THAN ITS PREDECESSOR. BL-20260720-GH-ACTIONS-PUSH-EVENTS-DEAD (resolved 2026-07-20) carried the whole diagnosis. BL-20260830-ZERO-CHECK-RUNS-READ-AS-CI-NOT-STARTED-NOT-AS-MERGE-CONFLICT (resolved 2026-08-30) was already the second, and its stated DURABLE PREVENTION was to restate the paragraph in CLAUDE.md 'at the point of use, in the file that reaches a session before it acts'. THAT FIX SHIPPED AND IS PRESENT: the paragraph is in CLAUDE.md § 'PM-side session capabilities', it names both predecessor ids, and it says in terms 'read mergeable_state FIRST … dirty means no merge ref, means no pull_request CI'. It was in my context window, verbatim, for every one of the three misreadings. The 08-30 occurrence cost ~10 minutes and ended in a correct diagnosis; this one produced two PRs closed with false evidence attached and a phantom failure class one commit from being filed. RETRIEVAL was not the failure this time — the text was present and was read past. 

AND ITS PREDECESSOR PREDICTED EXACTLY THIS. BL-20260830's own resolution_criteria closes: 'It REOPENS if a third row of this class is ever filed — that would mean restating it in CLAUDE.md was also not enough, and the next remedy is mechanical (a guard, or a wrapper that reads mergeable_state before reporting check runs) rather than more prose.' This row IS that third filing. The remedy is therefore ALREADY CHOSEN and must not be re-litigated into a fourth prose edit. 

SECOND, INDEPENDENT FINDING IN THE SAME INCIDENT — the merge-slot claimant is now a BOT. What made #11619 dirty was docs/claude/session-board.json: .github/actions/commit-to-main claimed the merge slot for work-digest run 34420408024 at 00:14:55Z and landed as #11618 without releasing it. So BL-20260909-MERGE-SLOT-IS-NEVER-RELEASED-AFTER-A-MERGE-SO-EVERY-CLAIMANT-DISPLACES-A-GHOST is WIDER than sessions: the automation queue is a claimant with no release path, and every manager register write now races it. 

!! THIS ROW WAS ITSELF DELETED BY THE VERY CLASS OF RESOLUTION IT WARNS ABOUT, ~45 MINUTES AFTER IT WAS FILED, AND THAT IS NOW PART OF THE FINDING. It landed on main in #11622 (2832abf10). PR #11627 (MI-229's close-out, 24ad3adf7) resolved a conflict on this file by TAKING A SIDE rather than building a union: it added one row of its own and dropped this one. !! THE LOSS WAS INVISIBLE IN EVERY CHEAP CHECK: the row COUNT was 1419 before and 1419 after, because one row was added as one was removed, so a reviewer comparing totals sees nothing and the git diff shows only 'a changed value at this key'. It was found solely by diffing the ID SETS across the merge, which is the check the union rule actually asks for and which nobody runs by habit. Restored here from 2832abf10 rather than retyped, so the text is the original and not a reconstruction. !! DO NOT READ THIS AS THE LANE MISBEHAVING - the same manager resolved four conflicts on this same file tonight and got a union only because the rule was in front of it each time; the defect is that an append-only register with no merge driver makes taking-a-side the DEFAULT outcome and makes the loss unobservable afterwards. Composes with BL-20260821-BACKLOG-JSON-IS-A-SHARED-MUTABLE-ARRAY.
items.evidence: pull_request_read method=get on #11605 (mergeable_state dirty, base 2986ce3e), #11612 (dirty, base 8f753a34), #11619 (dirty, base 6efbcb2a), all read 2026-09-10T00:24-00:31Z. Rebase control on #11619: head 93083eba8 carried 2 runs, both event=push; head 35d4cc576 after `git rebase origin/main` carried 5, four of them the required pull_request checks, fired 00:28:00-00:28:03Z. Retractions posted as #11612 comment 5610753097 and #11605 comment 5610754676. Positive control that the class already exists: backlog_search on the symptom text returns BL-20260830-ZERO-CHECK-RUNS-READ-AS-CI-NOT-STARTED-NOT-AS-MERGE-CONFLICT at overlap 1.00.
items.resolution_criteria:
A MECHANISM, and its predecessor already named the shape: a session-side wrapper or guard that reads mergeable_state and REPORTS IT BESIDE any check-run count, so a zero/low count can never be presented without the one field that disambiguates it. Cheapest sufficient form: whatever a session calls to poll CI must return `dirty` / `blocked` / `clean` alongside total_count, and a count of 0 or 1 must be UNPRESENTABLE without that state. 

!! WHAT DOES NOT CLEAR THIS, stated because it is what was tried twice: another CLAUDE.md paragraph, another backlog row, or any remedy of the form 'the next session will read more carefully'. The paragraph exists, it is at the point of use, it names both prior ids, and a session holding it verbatim still got it wrong three times in one evening. A fourth restatement is the reminder-is-not-a-mechanism non-fix this repo has already paid for on MI-15 (twice). 

!! NOR does it clear on the three PRs being resolved — they are, and that is the incident ending, not the class. 

!! AND THE DETECTOR MUST BE SHOWN TO TURN RED: plant a dirty PR, confirm the wrapper reports `dirty` rather than a bare zero, then remove it. Per MI-226's finding, a self-test that prints and exits 0 is the presence-only failure this repo has already paid for once. 

WHO: NOT the manager — the remedy lives under scripts/, a worker path check_manager_scope R2 forbids the manager authoring. This row is the act of NOT taking it. 

AND REOPEN BL-20260830 rather than treating it as resolved: its own criterion says a third filing means its fix did not hold.
items.detector: NONE TODAY, and that absence is the finding rather than an omission — CI cannot see a session misreading an API response. The detector this row asks for IS the remedy above; until it exists, the only thing standing between a session and this misreading is prose that has now demonstrably failed three times.

items.title: The manager cadence's own poke-verification check -- compare fire_trigger's returned session_id against persistent_session_id -- returns a MISMATCH on every call including ones that demonstrably delivered, so following it reports 100% of pokes as failed
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-10 over ALL FOUR fire_trigger calls this session made, not a sample. The manager-cadence Routine instructs: 'ALWAYS compare the returned session_id against the persistent_session_id. A mismatch means it spawned a FRESH session and your message went nowhere -- fire_trigger still reports success, so that comparison is the only signal there is.' EVERY CALL RETURNED A MISMATCH: cse_01BJ5uMAbv3j8PCEHAvmy95E, cse_01Qs1vF4TFVu2WwGb5SbBCA1, cse_018bM7rcTwTWtVo2M2dcWjiK, cse_01RFL6CYog4C6uPrXB9APbQ8 -- all `cse_` prefixed, none equal to any `session_` target. AND AT LEAST ONE OF THOSE POKES DEMONSTRABLY DELIVERED. session_01N4QpvcvLWQ5cuKXUcCWJ8E (MI-230) was IDLE and disconnected across two pokes with updated_at frozen at 01:36:02Z; after the third -- a retraction telling it to merge origin/main into its branch -- it pushed exactly that merge at 02:18Z (head 79dac81ae, 'Merge remote-tracking branch origin/main') and its post_turn_summary read 'merged main, 87 tests pass'. So the documented check produced a FALSE NEGATIVE on a delivery that worked. !! CAUSATION IS NOT CLAIMED AND MUST NOT BE READ IN: that lane had independently root-caused the same red, so it may have merged main of its own accord. What IS established is the check's discriminating power -- a signal that reads 'failed' on 4 of 4 calls, one of which coincided exactly with its own instruction, cannot separate a delivered poke from a lost one. THE RETURNED `cse_*` IS A TRIGGER-RUN ID, NOT A SESSION. Reading it as 'it spawned a fresh session' is the UNPROVENANCED-DIAGNOSTIC-OUTPUT class this repo has a guard for, sub-class A: the label names a quantity (the session your message went to) that the accessor does not return. WHY A WRONG CHECK IS WORSE THAN NO CHECK HERE: a manager following it concludes every poke failed, and the documented remedy for a failed poke is to re-poke or archive-and-respawn the lane. BL-20260902-AN-IDLE-CLOUD-SUB-SESSION-IS-RESUMABLE-VIA-A-SESSION-BOUND-ROUTINE-NOT-UNREACHABLE records that exact cost already -- MI-37 archived and respawned TWICE on a wrong belief about reachability, the second respawn caused by the manager's own corrective instruction. This row is how the same cost gets paid again through a different door. !! NOT A DUPLICATE OF THAT ROW AND IT DOES NOT CONTRADICT IT. That row establishes the poke CHANNEL WORKS and carries its two real limits (no mcp__* tools in the fired turn; one-way, no reply). This row is about the VERIFICATION PROCEDURE written around it. That row's own evidence used the RIGHT check -- get_session IDLE->RUNNING across the fire -- which is what the cadence text should say instead. THE HONEST STATE OF THAT RIGHT CHECK IS RECORDED TOO, because it is weaker than it looks: MI-230's updated_at did NOT move at either of the first two fires and it was still IDLE 2 and 4 minutes after them. So IDLE->RUNNING is a POSITIVE signal when seen and is NOT a negative one when absent -- a poked session may simply not be scheduled promptly. Do not read a frozen updated_at as proof of non-delivery either. RESOLUTION CRITERIA: clears when the cadence Routine's text no longer instructs the session_id comparison as the delivery signal AND states the get_session IDLE->RUNNING check together with its limit (absence is not evidence of non-delivery). !! IT DOES NOT CLEAR ON A SINGLE SUCCESSFUL POKE -- that is what already exists and is already filed. And it does not clear by deleting the check with nothing in its place: a manager with no delivery signal at all is the state that produced the double-respawn. DETECTOR: none possible from inside the repo, and that is stated rather than papered over. The cadence Routine's prompt is not a repo file -- it lives in the Routine store and is edited via update_trigger -- so no CI guard can read it. The honest mechanism is that this row is read at the next cadence rewrite.
items.resolution_criteria: The manager-cadence Routine's prompt no longer instructs the fire_trigger session_id comparison as the delivery signal, AND states the get_session IDLE->RUNNING check together with its own limit -- that absence of a transition is NOT evidence of non-delivery. Verified by reading the Routine's prompt back through list_triggers or update_trigger and quoting the new text. !! IT DOES NOT CLEAR ON A SINGLE SUCCESSFUL POKE: that is already filed as BL-20260902-AN-IDLE-CLOUD-SUB-SESSION-IS-RESUMABLE-VIA-A-SESSION-BOUND-ROUTINE-NOT-UNREACHABLE and proves the CHANNEL, never the CHECK. !! IT DOES NOT CLEAR BY DELETING THE CHECK with nothing in its place -- a manager with no delivery signal at all is the state that produced the MI-37 double-respawn. !! AND IT DOES NOT CLEAR ON A CI GUARD: none is possible, because the Routine prompt is not a repo file.

items.title: With merge.jsonregister armed, a local test-merge of a register-touching PR reports a clean merge for a PR GitHub grades `dirty` — the manager's own pre-merge check silently inverts
items.tier: 1 — .gitattributes + scripts/ops/merge_json_register.py; developer/manager tooling, no runtime or order path
items.filed_by: manager session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj, hit while trying to land PR #11626
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-10T02:41Z on PR #11626 (MI-217). The PR was green on all six check runs (pytest-run completed 02:12:03Z) and declared `landing: hold` / `unvouchable_paths`, i.e. it wanted a manager merge click. Before merging I test-merged its head 30e88b06b into origin/main at ac69e16bd in a throwaway worktree — deliberately, because inferring a merge result instead of testing it had already cost this same session an hour earlier the same night. git reported `Auto-merging docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json` / `Automatic merge went well`, rc=0. I then asserted the result was a true union rather than eyeballing it (main 1421 rows + branch 1421 -> 1422 merged, symmetric difference empty, no duplicate ids, neither side's rows dropped) and ran the touched tests on the merged tree (94 passed). On that evidence I called the merge.

THE MERGE API REFUSED: HTTP 405, 'Pull Request has merge conflicts'. Re-reading the PR confirmed `mergeable_state: dirty`, with the SAME base (15318eb4c) and the SAME head I had just merged locally. Main had not moved between the test and the call — origin/main was ac69e16bd before and after.

CAUSE: this clone has `merge.jsonregister` ARMED (`git config --get merge.jsonregister.driver` is set), and `.gitattributes` maps `docs/claude/health-review-backlog.json` to it. The local merge therefore ran `scripts/ops/merge_json_register.py`, which resolved the tail-append-vs-tail-append collision correctly and exited 0. GitHub's servers do not run custom merge drivers, so the server-side 3-way merge conflicted. BOTH RESULTS ARE CORRECT FOR THEIR OWN MERGE; they are answers to different questions, and only one of them predicts whether the merge button works.

THIS IS DOCUMENTED AND I STILL WALKED INTO IT, WHICH IS THE POINT. `.gitattributes` states it in terms: 'A MERGE DRIVER IS CLIENT-SIDE ... GitHub's servers do NOT run custom merge drivers, so this does NOT make a `mergeable_state: dirty` PR auto-mergeable on GitHub.' That sentence answers 'will this PR auto-merge', which is not the question a manager asks. The question a manager asks is 'if I merge this, will it conflict', and for that the armed clone returns a confident CLEAN for a PR that is dirty. Prose one file away did not reach the moment of use.

WHY THE DIRECTION MATTERS. The un-armed failure mode is already filed as BL-20260906-REGISTER-MERGE-DRIVER-SHIPS-UNARMED-AND-A-SESSION-PAID-ELEVEN-HAND-RESOLUTIONS: un-armed, you pay hand-resolutions you did not need to. THIS ROW IS THE INVERSE AND IS NOT A DUPLICATE OF IT: armed, you are told a conflict does not exist. Arming is the recommended state and `scripts/ops/manager_preflight.py` FAILS an un-armed clone, so every manager that follows the preflight is in exactly the configuration that produces this false negative. The remedy for one row is the precondition for the other.

COST HERE WAS SMALL AND THE FAILURE WAS LOUD — the merge API refused, so nothing wrong landed and no work was lost; the cost was one wasted merge attempt and a wrong sentence in a poke I had to correct. THE DANGEROUS SHAPE IS THE ADJACENT ONE, and it is NOT established as having happened: a manager that reads a clean local test-merge as evidence a lane is UNBLOCKED will leave that lane idle believing it is queued, which is the stall class BL-20260903-THE-PR-QUEUE-WATCHER-CANNOT-SEE-A-TEN-MINUTE-STALL is about. #11626's own session was IDLE at the time with post_turn_summary 'PR #11626 green 24min, awaiting merge click; next check ~03:22Z' — it believed it was waiting on me, and would have waited ~40 more minutes had the poke not gone out.

POPULATION: n=1 observed instance. It is a configuration property rather than a statistical one — any PR whose only conflict is inside a `merge=jsonregister` path will merge locally in an armed clone and conflict on GitHub — so the class is certain at n=1. What is NOT established: how many past 'clean test-merge' readings by managers were this false negative. Nobody has surveyed that and this row does not claim a number.

A SIBLING EXISTS AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT NAMED HERE YET. PR #11626's own diff files the same class one level along — a pr-landing rule that reports a confident verdict computed over ZERO paths when run on an uncommitted tree, and whose remedy text then tells the author to declare `landing: "self"` and arm it. Its id is intentionally omitted: it exists only on that unmerged branch, and artifact-validity-guard correctly refuses a tracking reference that resolves to nothing — a row saying 'see BL-X' where BL-X was never filed reads as tracked while tracked by nobody, which is the 2026-07-30 operator directive's exact crack. ⚠️ NAMING IT IN PROSE COUNTS AS A REFERENCE TOO: I tried moving the id out of `related` and into this paragraph, and the guard failed again on the text — correctly, since a reader follows a name wherever it appears. ADD THE REF WHEN #11626 MERGES; it is on that PR and findable by its date. That the two were found within an hour of each other, on the same PR, by two different sessions is the useful part: both are a check grading the wrong INPUT while sounding certain about your change — one over an empty diff, one under a merge driver the grader does not run.
items.resolution_criteria: A manager checking mergeability CANNOT be misled by the armed driver, and it is OBSERVED not being misled. Either (a) the local check itself is made honest — a helper the merge-queue duty actually calls (not prose) that either merges with the drivers DISABLED (`git -c merge.jsonregister.driver=false merge`, or `-c core.attributesFile=/dev/null`) or reports both results side by side and labels which one predicts GitHub; or (b) the duty stops test-merging locally to answer this question at all and reads `mergeable_state` from the API first, with that written into the merge-queue contract rather than left to judgement. VERIFY BY REPRODUCING THE FALSE NEGATIVE AND WATCHING IT NOT HAPPEN: construct two branches that each append a row to the tail of a `merge=jsonregister` register, and confirm the check reports CONFLICT (or 'GitHub will conflict') in an ARMED clone. A test asserting the helper's behaviour on a synthetic repo is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT — the defect only appears when the driver is armed AND .gitattributes maps the path, so the check must exercise that shape. DO NOT 'fix' this by disarming the driver or removing the .gitattributes mapping: that trades this false negative for the eleven hand-resolutions BL-20260906-REGISTER-MERGE-DRIVER-SHIPS-UNARMED-AND-A-SESSION-PAID-ELEVEN-HAND-RESOLUTIONS records, which is a worse trade. The driver is doing its job; what is missing is a way to ask the OTHER question. AND MORE PROSE IN .gitattributes DOES NOT CLEAR THIS — the warning is already there, correctly worded, and was not enough; that is the finding, not the gap.

items.title: RECURRENCE of BL-20260825: the 60s exit-eval requirement did NOT stop being breached -- 1216 breaches / 67444 intervals lifetime (1.803%), max 120189.1ms = 2.0x the requirement, last breach 2026-09-10T00:30:58Z -- and every figure the repo has quoted came from a 1000-row TAIL that reads ZERO
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-10T02:38Z off `GET /api/bot/exit-interval/soak?limit=1`, reading `summary`, which `read_soak_records` computes over EVERY ROW ON DISK rather than the returned page.

POPULATION, because it is the whole finding: 67,444 measured intervals across 442 processes -- the entire soak file, not a window.

  breaches            1216   (1.803% of measured intervals)
  max_interval_ms     120189.1   (2.0x the 60000ms requirement)
  max_interval_at_utc 2026-09-04T04:24:12Z
  mean_interval_ms    31263.1    (the BODY is healthy)
  last_breach_utc     2026-09-10T00:30:58Z

!! THIS IS A RECURRENCE, AND THE ROW IT RECURS AGAINST IS MARKED `resolved`. BL-20260825-EXIT-EVAL-60S-BREACHED-1204-TIMES-CESSATION-UNCONFIRMED recorded 1,204 breaches over 22,670 intervals (5.31%, max 96.1ms->96.1s) and was closed on the claim that the breaches had STOPPED. They did not: 1,204 -> 1,216 (+12), and `max_interval_at_utc` is 2026-09-04, which POSTDATES that closure. The row's own id says CESSATION-UNCONFIRMED and the closure assumed the cessation it had not confirmed.

!! STATE BOTH HALVES -- THE IMPROVEMENT IS REAL AND MUST NOT BE OMITTED. The RATE fell 5.31% -> 1.803%, because the denominator nearly tripled (22,670 -> 67,444) while the breach count barely moved. #10114's IB connector memo and IB_PROBE_CACHE_S did work. What did not happen is CESSATION, and the WORST CASE got worse: 96.1s -> 120.2s. Reporting either half alone misleads in opposite directions -- 'down to 1.8%' hides that it never stopped; 'still breaching, worse max' hides a genuine 3x improvement in rate.

!! WHY NOBODY SAW IT: EVERY PRIOR READING WAS A 1000-ROW TAIL, AND A TAIL READS ZERO. 2026-08-25 recorded `over_requirement 0 of 991 (0.00%)`; audit F-50 on 2026-09-09 recorded `over_requirement 0 of 1000` and built its whole narrative on a 48.8ms margin. Both are CORRECT about their window. CLAUDE.md's EXIT_LOOP_DECOUPLE_DISABLED row predicted this in terms -- 'It is a 1000-row TAIL of a 6.29 MB file ... the max over the whole file may be higher' -- and nobody had checked. It is higher by 2x. The lifetime read is one curl; the surface has existed since the #9627 follow-up (BL-20260816-EXIT-INTERVAL-SOAK-SUMMARY-HAS-NO-READ-SURFACE).

WHAT IS RULED OUT, so the next reader does not re-derive it:
  * NOT a restart artefact. `record_pass` measures completion-to-completion off a PER-PROCESS     monotonic clock, so every one of these is a WITHIN-process gap.
  * NOT first-pass noise. A first pass has `interval_ms: None` and `over_requirement: None`     (deliberately tri-state, not False), and `read_soak_records` counts only rows with a numeric     `interval_ms`.
  * NOT re-graded history. `over_requirement` is stamped at WRITE time against the requirement     as it then stood, so this read did not re-grade anything.

NOT PROPOSED HERE, DELIBERATELY: the CAUSE. Audit F-50 offered the operator `investigate_the_tail` and they chose `near_miss_and_restart_gap` instead, so why one pass runs long is an OPEN and UNCHOSEN question, not a rejected one. MI-230's object was instrumentation; this row is what the instrumentation surfaced. Related and also unanswered: F-51 (the breach page never writes outcomes.jsonl, so the breach history is uncountable from any repo-reachable surface -- which is precisely why 1,216 breaches accrued unread).

WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a decision on whether 1.8% at a 120s worst case is acceptable for a requirement written as an absolute, or whether the tail is now worth root-causing. That is an operator call and is NOT being made here.
items.root_cause: CAUSE ESTABLISHED 2026-09-10 by session_01Ww2pZVK5VUqV8xFFtTs9B1 under WO-20260910-ROOT-CAUSE-THE-EXIT-EVAL-60S-BREACHES. Evidence: docs/claude/work/EXIT-EVAL-60S-ROOTCAUSE-2026-09-10.md. STATE THE POPULATION: GET /api/bot/exit-interval/soak?breached_only=true&limit=2000, read 2026-09-10T06:13Z, returned 1218 of 1218 breaching rows -- a COMPLETE CENSUS, not a sample. (1) MECHANISM: every breach is a slow PASS, and nothing else. 1218 of 1218 have pass_ms > 30s; median pass_ms/interval_ms = 1.000; interval_ms - pass_ms never exceeds 29,351ms and ZERO rows exceed one 30s cadence period. So no scheduler stall, no thread starvation and no sleep overrun survives -- that entire hypothesis class is closed off by the data. (2) !! THIS ROW'S OWN HEADLINE IS CORRECTED: 'did not cease' is true of the COUNT and misleading about the RATE. 1182 of 1218 (97.0%) predate 2026-08-22 and 1157 (95.0%) fall in the four days 2026-08-19..08-22; since 2026-08-23 there are 14 breaches in 18 days, ZERO on 10 of those days. Against a ~2,800 intervals/day denominator the post-fix rate is of order 0.03% versus a lifetime 1.795% -- roughly 60x lower. THE LIFETIME FIGURE IS A POOLED RATE OVER A BIMODAL POPULATION AND MUST NOT BE QUOTED AS CURRENT. BL-20260825-EXIT-EVAL-60S-BREACHED-1204-TIMES-CESSATION-UNCONFIRMED was therefore substantially RIGHT to close on cessation; what it never got was its own clause 2 (a population that could have shown the tail), which this work supplies. Equally the cessation is not total, so closing it outright would also have been wrong. Both halves recorded. (3) THE LIVE RESIDUAL IS THE IBKR NIGHTLY RESET WINDOW, and it is a DIFFERENT cause from the episode: 10 of the 14 post-fix breaches fall in 04:00-05:00Z (71.4%) against 8.6% for the 1204 pre-fix ones, which are flat across all 24 hours -- an ~8x concentration. Direct evidence, not inference: /api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live over 2026-09-10T04:19:25Z..04:22:15Z shows 'Error 1100 Connectivity between IBKR and Trader Workstation has been lost' followed by repeated 'IBMarketData.get_ohlcv timed out waiting for the pinned IB thread (waited 29.0s)' for MES/MHG/MGC while all eleven non-IB packages complete in under a second each. ARITHMETIC RECONCILIATION: 3 x 29.0s + ~4s = 91s against the recorded pass_ms of 91,187ms. The 29.0s is printed by the log line itself and equals _IB_FETCH_QUEUE_TIMEOUT_S = IB_FETCH_TIMEOUT_S * 3.0 + 5.0 (src/exchange/ib_connector.py:113-117). IB fetches are SERIALIZED on one process-wide pinned thread and the pass walks packages one at a time, so a pass costs n_IB_packages x 29s and crosses the 60s requirement at THREE IB packages. !! THIS IS A RECURRENCE AGAINST BL-20260816-IB-QUEUE-TIMEOUT-EXCEEDS-EXIT-BUDGET, which names this mechanism exactly and is marked `resolved` with no resolved_at and no recorded resolution. Its criterion 1 was 'COUNT IT FIRST -- how OFTEN it fires is UNMEASURED'; that denominator is now supplied and the row is re-opened rather than a fourth id being minted. REMEDY: proposed as R2 (a per-pass IB circuit breaker) in the evidence doc and put to the operator as DEC-20260910-EXIT-EVAL-60S-REMEDY. Tier-2, NOT applied.

items.title: The RESTART GAP breaches the 60s exit-eval requirement on 77 of 442 restarts (17.4%), max 210.4s = 3.5x -- ~10x the within-process breach rate, and it was invisible until MI-230 built the grader
items.detail:
FIRST EVER MEASUREMENT of the interval M20's promise covers and every per-process instrument excludes BY CONSTRUCTION. Read 2026-09-10T02:43Z off summary.restart_gap on GET /api/bot/exit-interval/soak, computed over EVERY ROW ON DISK.

POPULATION: 442 process boundaries across 443 processes. ALL gradeable -- ungradeable 0, overlapping 0, unattributed_rows 0 -- so this is a complete read, not a sample.

  restart_gap_state   breached
  breaches            77 / 442  = 17.4%
  near-miss band      37 / 442  = 8.4%   ([54s, 60s])
  max_gap_ms          210409.2  = 210.4s = 3.5068x the requirement
  max gap spanned     2026-08-26T08:14:57Z -> 08:18:27Z
  mean / median       46835 / 44519 ms   (the BODY sits at ~75% of the requirement)

!! THE COMPARISON IS THE FINDING. Within-process intervals over the SAME file breach 1216/67452 = 1.803% at a 120.2s max. So a restart boundary breaches ~10x MORE OFTEN than a within-process interval, and its worst case is 75% longer. The operator's decision (WO-20260909-DECISION-M20-EXIT-EVAL-MARGIN-COLLAPSED, chosen: near_miss_and_restart_gap) called (b) 'the harder half'; measured, it is also the WORSE half.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: exit_loop_health.max_interval_ms is a module global reset on every restart, and record_pass measures completion-to-completion off a PER-PROCESS monotonic clock, so the join between two processes was measured by nobody. The trader restarts on every merge to main -- 443 processes in this file -- and a deploy is exactly when it is least likely to be evaluating exits (old process stopped, new one booting with every cache cold).

!! THE 2026-09-09 AUDIT IS NOT CONTRADICTED, IT WAS OUT-OF-WINDOW. Audit F-50 measured 11 restart gaps at 25.3-53.9s, '0 of 11 over 60s, 1.3% of wall clock -- clean'. That is CORRECT for one day. Over 442 boundaries the rate is 17.4%. This is the tail-vs-lifetime error twice in one night; see the sibling row BL-20260910-EXIT-EVAL-60S-BREACHES-DID-NOT-CEASE-1216-LIFETIME-MAX-120S-AND-EVERY-PRIOR-READ-WAS-A-TAIL

RULED OUT so the next reader need not re-derive it: the grader REFUSES a boundary whose successor's earliest row is not a genuine first pass (a rotated log would otherwise yield an arbitrary within-process interval wearing a restart-gap label, systematically SHORT); an overlapping boundary is named and excluded from the max rather than clamped to 0; and both counts are ZERO here, so neither degrades this reading.

!! A GAP IS NOT PROOF OF A RESTART: if EXIT_LOOP_DECOUPLE_DISABLED were set for a window, nothing writes to the soak and the boundary either side renders as one enormous 'restart gap'. The 210.4s max should be checked against that before it is treated as a single restart -- read its from_utc/to_utc (2026-08-26T08:14:57Z -> 08:18:27Z, 3.5 min) rather than assuming.

NOT PROPOSED HERE: any remedy. Whether 17.4% at a 210s worst case is acceptable for a requirement written as an absolute -- and whether the restart path should evaluate exits before the old process stops, or the requirement should be restated to exclude deploys -- is an OPERATOR decision. MI-230's object was instrumentation and it is discharged; this is what the instrument found on its first read.
items.root_cause: CAUSE ESTABLISHED 2026-09-10 by session_01Ww2pZVK5VUqV8xFFtTs9B1 under WO-20260910-ROOT-CAUSE-THE-EXIT-EVAL-60S-BREACHES. Evidence: docs/claude/work/EXIT-EVAL-60S-ROOTCAUSE-2026-09-10.md. !! IT IS A DIFFERENT CAUSE FROM THE WITHIN-PROCESS BREACHES -- the dispatch flagged the ~10x ratio as a hint the two might differ, and they do. Forcing one story would have produced the wrong remedy for whichever half it did not fit. THE DECOMPOSITION, measured end to end on four consecutive restarts on 2026-09-10 by joining /api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live windows to the soak's own from_utc/to_utc and to the successor's first_pass_of_process pass_ms: A = predecessor's last completed pass -> systemd 'Stopping', i.e. THE UN-SLEPT REMAINDER OF THE LOOP'S OWN 30s CADENCE: 30.3 / 2.1 / 19.0 / 14.1 s -- ~uniform on [0,30s], and the dominant variable term. B = 'Stopping' -> 'Started', i.e. ACTUAL SYSTEMD DOWNTIME: ~0.3s on all four ('Deactivated successfully' in the same second; the process exits cleanly on SIGTERM). C = 'Started' -> 'exit-evaluation loop DECOUPLED': 7.1 / 7.0 / 15.0 / 6.0 s. In the 15s case the boot_reconcile -> DECOUPLED segment was 10.0s and consisted of FIFTEEN set_leverage pre-flight calls across 3 Bybit accounts, EVERY ONE returning retCode=110043 'already set (idempotent)', including a 5s stall on a Bybit recv_window timestamp error. D = thread start -> first pass completes, i.e. THE COLD FIRST PASS: 16.1 / 12.7 / 12.8 / 16.9 s, against a ~2.2s warm pass -- the BL-20260609-001 cold-cache shape. A+B+C+D RECONCILES EXACTLY to the observed gap on all four boundaries (53.5 / 21.8 / 46.8 / 37.0 s). SO THE CAUSE IS ARITHMETIC, NOT A DEFECT: C+D is a fixed floor of ~19-30s and A adds a uniform 0-30s, making the restart gap 19-60s BY CONSTRUCTION against a 60s requirement. The top of the system's own designed range IS the requirement, and at 18.1 restarts/day 6.2% of them land in the overlap. The 20 post-fix breaches are the right tail of that distribution -- 18 of them sit in a narrow 60.0-71.4s band -- and hunting a separate defect per breach would find nothing. !! DEPLOY SPEED IS NOT THE CAUSE AND MUST NOT BE PROPOSED AS THE FIX: term B is ~0.3s. Even a zero-downtime blue/green restart would leave A, which is the loop being correctly IDLE when the deploy lands. !! AND OI-20260910-...'s EXPECTATION IS CONTRADICTED, NOT THE INSTRUMENT: its 11 gaps of 25.3-53.9s with 0 over 60s was an under-powered one-day sample of a distribution whose 94th percentile is the requirement (post-fix p90 56.0s, p95 60.9s). 0 -> non-zero here is the mechanism starting to work. EXPOSURE FIGURE NOBODY HAD: summing every measured boundary, 20,784s of restart gap over the 24.7-day span = 0.973% of wall clock, mean 841 s/day; post-fix 13,584s over 18.0 days = 756 s/day (12.6 min/day, 0.875%). 93.8% of that comes from COMPLIANT restarts, so the breach RATE understates the exposure. REMEDY: proposed as R1 (move _start_exit_loop above _apply_per_account_leverage, after boot_reconcile) in the evidence doc and put to the operator as DEC-20260910-EXIT-EVAL-60S-REMEDY. Tier-2, NOT applied. Shortening EXIT_LOOP_INTERVAL_SECONDS is the single biggest lever on term A and is deliberately NOT proposed -- it doubles the pass rate and hence the broker load, which is the direction both June 2026 wedges came from.

items.title: pr-landing-guard R14 reports 'every changed path IS inside TIER1_SURFACE' over ZERO paths on an uncommitted tree, and its remedy text tells you to declare landing: self and arm it
items.tier: 1 — scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py; CI tooling, no runtime or order path
items.filed_by: MI-217 session (session_01MrTjuoRpBb7spyQLydXmmT), hit while declaring landing on PR #11626
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-10T01:10Z on PR #11626. `check_pr_landing.py::changed_paths` computes `git diff --name-only <merge-base>...HEAD`, i.e. COMMITTED work only. Run against a tree whose changes are staged-or-unstaged but NOT yet committed, the changed set is EMPTY. R14 then evaluates `outside = [p for p in changed if not _match(p, TIER1_SURFACE)]`, gets `[]`, and emits: 'claims `unvouchable_paths`, but every changed path IS inside TIER1_SURFACE. Such a PR can self-land: declare `landing: "self"` and arm it.'

THAT IS A VACUOUS TRUTH OVER AN EMPTY SET, AND THE REMEDY POINTS THE DANGEROUS WAY. The message does not say 'no changed paths were found'; it makes a positive claim about every path, and then instructs the author to REMOVE a hold and arm auto-merge. In this instance the diff (once committed) contained `scripts/ml/_offline_evidence.py` and `scripts/ml/strategy_review_packet.py` — both genuinely OUTSIDE TIER1_SURFACE, and the second is the M7 VERDICT function. Acting on R14 as printed would have self-landed a change to the strategy-review gate on a verdict computed over nothing.

WHAT SAVED IT WAS A CONTRADICTION, NOT THE GUARD: `scripts/ml/**` is plainly absent from the TIER1_SURFACE list, so 'every changed path is inside' could not be true. Committing and re-running produced the correct output — 'R14 verified — paths outside TIER1_SURFACE: scripts/ml/_offline_evidence.py, scripts/ml/strategy_review_packet.py' — and `pr-landing: OK — state=declared_hold`. So the guard is CORRECT on a committed tree; the defect is that it does not distinguish 'I looked and found none outside' from 'I had nothing to look at'.

THIS IS THE SECOND INSTANCE OF THE SAME CLASS IN ONE SESSION and the sibling is worth reading beside it: `check_pr_landing.py --base main` (as opposed to `--base origin/main`) resolves the LOCAL `main` ref, which in this container was 3 days stale, and R5 then reported Tier-3 paths from five other lanes' merges as belonging to this diff. Same shape, opposite direction: one names paths that are not yours, the other names none at all. Both are a guard grading the wrong INPUT while sounding certain about your change. Note the two entry points take OPPOSITE base arguments — `run_guards.py --base main` prefixes `origin/` itself, `check_pr_landing.py` does not.

POPULATION: n=1 observed instance for the empty-diff case (this PR). It is a code-path property rather than a statistical one — `changed == []` yields `outside == []` for any diff — so the class is certain even though the sighting count is one. No survey of how often sessions run the guard pre-commit has been done, and that number is NOT established.
items.resolution_criteria: R14 (and R5, which shares `changed_paths`) DISTINGUISHES an empty changed-set from a surveyed-and-clean one, and is OBSERVED doing so: running `check_pr_landing.py` on a tree with uncommitted changes and an empty committed diff must report something like `no changed paths — nothing to grade (did you forget to commit?)` and must NOT emit the 'every changed path IS inside TIER1_SURFACE … declare landing: self and arm it' remedy. ⚠️ VERIFY BY RUNNING IT ON AN UNCOMMITTED TREE, not by reading the diff — this defect is invisible to a committed-tree run, which is exactly why it survived. ⚠️ A test asserting the new message on a synthetic empty list is NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT: the failure only appears when a real working tree has changes the guard cannot see, so the check must exercise that shape. ⚠️ AND DO NOT 'fix' this by making changed_paths fall back to including uncommitted work — that would make the guard grade something CI never grades, which is a different and worse wrongness; the fix is to report the absence, not to invent a denominator.
