items.title: exit_loop_health's `process_started_utc` is the FIRST PASS'S COMPLETION time, not when the process started - it is late by exactly the boot-plus-cold-pass interval (23.2s measured), and the soak's own docstring dates processes from it
items.detail: UNPROVENANCED DIAGNOSTIC OUTPUT, sub-class A as CLAUDE.md defines it: the label names a quantity the code does not compute. src/runtime/exit_loop_health.py::record_pass sets the module global on its FIRST INVOCATION -- `now_utc = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()` ... `if _started_utc is None: _started_utc = now_utc` -- and record_pass is called AFTER a pass returns. So the field holds the completion time of the exit loop's first pass. It is carried onto every row of exit_interval_soak.jsonl as `process_started_utc` and surfaced on /api/bot/exit-interval/soak and /api/diag/log_file?name=exit_interval_soak. MEASURED over a COMPLETE population, not a sample: all 444 measured restart boundaries returned by summary.restart_gap on GET /api/bot/exit-interval/soak (read 2026-09-10T06:13Z) have `to_utc - to_process` between 0.280ms and 55.121ms, mean 2.026ms. The field equals the first pass's completion to within milliseconds, every time, with no exceptions. HOW LATE, MEASURED: for the process boundary ending 2026-09-10T00:19:11.215Z, /api/diag/journalctl?unit=ict-trader-live shows systemd 'Started ICT Trader Live' at 00:18:48 while `process_started_utc` reads 00:19:11.215 -- 23.2s LATE, i.e. late by exactly the startup-to-thread (7.1s) plus cold-first-pass (16.1s) interval, which is precisely the quantity a reader would want this field to help them measure. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS. (a) exit_interval_soak.py's OWN module docstring dates its five observed processes from these values ('five OBSERVED processes in ~10h (23:06:29 -> 06:24:32 -> ...)') -- every one of those timestamps is late by the boot-plus-cold-pass interval. That docstring is also the place that correctly insists restarts be counted from observed process_started_utc values rather than from merge times, so the field is load-bearing for exactly the reasoning it distorts. (b) A session decomposing a restart gap will naturally compute `first_pass_completion - process_started_utc` as 'how long did startup take' and get ~2ms -- a confident, silent, wrong zero. This session did reach for it and had to fall back to the systemd journal. !! WHAT THIS DOES **NOT** INVALIDATE, stated so nobody over-corrects: the restart-gap measurement itself is CORRECT. exit_restart_gap.grade_restart_gaps joins the predecessor's LAST completion to the successor's FIRST completion using logged_at_utc, and uses process_started_utc only as a GROUPING KEY for process identity -- a role it fills perfectly well, since it is unique per process. The gap numbers stand. It is the field's NAME, and any reader who trusts it as a boot timestamp, that is wrong. Found while root-causing the exit-eval 60s breaches; full context and the four-term restart-gap decomposition in docs/claude/work/EXIT-EVAL-60S-ROOTCAUSE-2026-09-10.md.
items.resolution_criteria: 1. DECIDE RENAME-VS-ADD FIRST, and note this is a SCHEMA CHANGE with existing readers -- exit_restart_gap.py (grouping key), exit_interval_soak.py (builder + summary), src/web/api/routers/exit_interval.py, and any session reading the raw JSONL. A blind rename breaks the grouping; the cheaper fix is to keep the existing key as the process IDENTITY it actually is (consider `process_key` / `first_pass_at_utc`) and, if boot time is genuinely wanted, ADD a real one captured at module import or from /proc/self/stat rather than repurposing this. 2. THE DOCSTRING IS PART OF THE FIX, not an afterthought: exit_interval_soak.py's module docstring dates five processes from these values and must be corrected in the same change, or the stale claim outlives the field. 3. !! DO NOT BACK-FILL EXISTING ROWS. Every row already on disk carries the first-pass-completion value; rewriting them to a reconstructed boot time would assert an observation nobody made. Distinguish by row date. 4. !! A GREEN TEST CLEARS NOTHING HERE -- the field is internally consistent and always has been; the defect is that its NAME describes a different quantity. items.title: RECURRENCE of BL-20260825-UNION-MERGE-HARDCODES-INDENT-AND-REFORMATS-THE-FILE-IT-EXISTS-TO-PROTECT, on the file EVERY session touches: docs/claude/session-board.json was re-serialised indent=1 -> indent=2 on main, so every branch cut before that commit now conflicts on the WHOLE file
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-10 while resolving a real conflict on this file, and the cause was VERIFIED rather than guessed -- my first reading was the opposite one and was wrong. WHAT HAPPENED: commit 2832abf10 (#11622, a manager session) rewrote docs/claude/session-board.json from indent=1 to indent=2. Established by walking every commit that touched the file from merge-base 6295bce38 to origin/main and reading the indentation of line 2 at each: 1 space until 2832abf10, 2 spaces from it onward. WHY IT IS A RECURRENCE AND NOT A DUPLICATE: BL-20260825 is the same CLASS (a hardcoded indent silently re-serialising a shared append-only JSON file) but a different writer and a different file -- backlog_union_merge.py on the health backlog. That row is still OPEN, and the class has now reappeared on the COORDINATION BOARD, which is worse in kind: the backlog is appended by review sessions, while session-board.json is written by EVERY session that claims the merge slot, so the blast radius is the whole fleet rather than one workflow. CLAUDE.md already documents this class in terms for the backlogs ('a naive read-append-write reformats every non-ASCII line and re-attributes ~21k lines to your PR') and routes writers through scripts/ops/backlog_append.py, which REFUSES rather than writing a reformatted file. session-board.json has no such writer and no such refusal -- it is edited ad hoc by whichever session holds the slot. THE COST IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL AND THERE IS A LIVE VICTIM: branch claude/lane4-stale-automation-landing-20260909 (unmerged, last commit a8b68ec80 2026-09-09) still carries the indent=1 form, so its diff against main shows the ENTIRE file rewritten. When it merges it will conflict on every line of a coordination file, and a hand resolution there risks silently reverting the merge slot to a stale holder -- lane4's copy still names claude/mgr-consolidated-20260909T1912 from 2026-09-09T19:12Z. That is the failure mode the file exists to prevent, produced by the file's own formatting. NOT THE FINDING: lane4 did nothing wrong. It is stale relative to a reformat on main, not the author of one -- checked before saying so, because the naive reading (lane4 reformatted it) is the one a session reaches first and it is false. NOR is the indent=2 form itself wrong; the harm is the UNGUARDED TRANSITION, whichever direction it runs. PROPOSED FIX (not applied, and deliberately not chosen for the operator): give session-board.json the same treatment the backlogs already have -- one writer that round-trips the file's EXISTING serialisation and refuses rather than reformatting, the shape backlog_append.py already implements. A cheaper half-measure is a CI guard that fails any PR changing the file's indentation, which catches the transition without requiring every session to route through a helper. WHAT I DID INSTEAD, so this row is not mistaken for an unhandled break: my own edit to this file detected the existing serialisation by round-trip and matched it, changing only the merge_slot block and asserting key-by-key that every other top-level block stayed byte-identical to main's.

items.resolution_criteria: EITHER of two OBSERVABLE outcomes, and they are different -- say which. (a) GUARDED: a planted commit that changes docs/claude/session-board.json's indentation is REFUSED -- either by a CI check that fails on it, or by a single writer that round-trips the file's existing serialisation and raises rather than writing a reformatted file, the shape scripts/ops/backlog_append.py already implements and whose refusal is exercised by a planted control. Verified by RUNNING that control and seeing a non-zero return, never by the guard being registered: a presence-only marker is the failure this repo has already paid for. (b) RETIRED: the operator decides an unguarded shared JSON file is acceptable here, and it is RECORDED as that decision with the consequence stated -- every branch cut before a re-serialisation gets a whole-file conflict on the coordination board, and a hand resolution of that can silently revert the merge slot. !! THE ORIGINATING INSTANCE CLEARING IS NOT SUFFICIENT AND MUST NOT BE READ AS THIS ROW CLOSING: once claude/lane4-stale-automation-landing-20260909 merges or is abandoned, its whole-file conflict disappears while NOTHING prevents the next re-serialisation. That is the trap -- the symptom is self-clearing and the class is not. !! NOR DOES A QUIET PERIOD CLEAR IT: no conflict for a week means nobody re-serialised the file that week, which is a statement about the week and not about the file. !! AND CHECK BL-20260825-UNION-MERGE-HARDCODES-INDENT-AND-REFORMATS-THE-FILE-IT-EXISTS-TO-PROTECT BEFORE CLOSING EITHER: observed once on 2026-09-10, backlog_union_merge.py now reports 'reproducing origin/main's serialisation' rather than hardcoding it, so that sibling row may already be repaired -- but ONE observation of a tool printing the right thing is not a verification, and this row is not evidence for closing that one.

items.title: scripts/ops/backlog_append.py::append_row -- the writer CLAUDE.md MANDATES -- accepts a row with no resolution_criteria, tier or severity, which check_backlog_criteria.py then fails CI for
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-10, both statically and empirically, after it cost this PR a red CI round. STATIC: none of `resolution_criteria`, `tier`, `severity`, `opened_at` appears anywhere in append_row's source. EMPIRICAL (the positive control, because absence in source is not proof of absence in behaviour): append_row on a temp backlog with `{id, title, detail, status}` and nothing else RETURNED NORMALLY, writing 1 row. THE GAP: CLAUDE.md says in terms 'File through scripts/ops/backlog_append.py::append_row, never by hand', and that function does enforce two real things -- it refuses a duplicate id and refuses a row whose text restates an existing one, and it raises FormatNotReproducible rather than writing a reformatted file. It does NOT enforce the three fields scripts/ops/check_backlog_criteria.py fails the required `guards` context for. So the sanctioned path produces a row that lands RED, and the author learns it from CI rather than from the writer. NOT HYPOTHETICAL AND NOT A NEAR MISS: it happened on PR #11640 on this date. The row was filed through append_row, append_row accepted it, and `guards` then failed with 'no resolution_criteria field' -- one guard, one round, attributable entirely to this gap. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ONE WASTED ROUND: a guard is cheapest to satisfy at the moment of writing, when the author still holds the context to say what DONE looks like. Discovered at CI, the pressure is to add the shortest string that turns the check green -- which is how a register fills with resolution_criteria that name no observable condition, the exact failure check_backlog_criteria.py exists to prevent ('the backlog grew +129 net in 30 days with 25% of it >=45 days old and never once advanced'). A SECOND, SMALLER DIVERGENCE, measured over all rows on origin/main at the time: the modern key is `opened_at` (995 rows) but the legacy `opened` is still present (367) and append_row normalises neither, so a session copying an older row's shape silently files on the legacy key. PROPOSED FIX (not applied): have append_row validate the same three fields check_backlog_criteria.py does, IMPORTING that guard's predicate rather than restating it -- a second copy of 'what makes a row workable' is how the writer and the guard would drift apart again, which is the same single-owner argument this repo makes for src/runtime/provenance.py and package_leg_coverage.assess. Raise, do not warn: append_row's existing refusals raise, and a warning printed into a session's scrollback is not a mechanism.
items.resolution_criteria: append_row REFUSES a row missing resolution_criteria / tier / severity, verified by RUNNING the refusal: a planted call omitting them raises, and the same call with them present returns normally. !! A UNIT TEST THAT MERELY IMPORTS THE VALIDATOR DOES NOT CLEAR THIS -- the claim is that the WRITER refuses, so the control must exercise append_row itself, which is the shape of the empirical check that found the gap. !! NOR DOES CI GOING GREEN ON SOME LATER PR: that says the author remembered the fields, not that the writer enforces them, and it is exactly the false assurance this row is about. !! AND IF THE VALIDATION IS DECLINED -- e.g. the fields are judged advisory at write time -- this row does NOT clear, it CHANGES: the mandated writer is then knowingly weaker than the guard, which is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one with that consequence stated, rather than left looking like a fix about to happen.
items.source: MI-231, after PR #11640 went red on artifact-validity-guard for a row filed through the mandated writer

items.title: silent_refusal_alert: an account in SILENT_REFUSAL_SKIP keeps its LAST latch forever, so silent_accounts() hands every review skill a 20-day-old alerting:true verdict -- and BOTH loops that could clear it skip on the same condition
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-10. LATCH: /api/diag/log_file?name=silent_refusal_alert_state shows __last_check__ 2026-09-10T07:58:20Z and 7 of 8 accounts carrying that same updated_at, while alpaca_live alone is frozen at updated_at 2026-08-21T12:38:38Z with alerting:true, cause:risk_refused, verdict:signalled_never_placed, refused 5, placed 0, and NO priority_causes / alerting_basis / alert_disposition keys at all (it predates them). 20 days stale while the detector ran 37 minutes before the read. ENV: get-env on ict-trader-live.service (Actions run 34455224799, issue #11656, 2026-09-10T08:27:26Z) reads SILENT_REFUSAL_SKIP = 'alpaca_live' on BOTH the running process (/proc/<MainPID>/environ, authoritative) and the declared .env; no pending_restart. MECHANISM: run_silent_refusal_check has two loops and BOTH `continue` on `aid in skip` -- the assessment loop, so state[aid] is never rewritten, and the quiet-account RELEASE loop, which was added specifically for this symptom and whose own comment cites THIS account frozen at THIS timestamp on 2026-08-25. So a skipped account's latch is immortal. CONSUMER: silent_accounts() filters on st.get('alerting') with no staleness or skip test, and is what the review skills read to decide whether to flag. IT IS ALSO WRONG ON ITS FACE NOW: the latched cause is risk_refused from a zero-balance era; the account holds 200.22 (broker read 2026-09-10T08:16:55Z) and its 3 refusals since the roster was armed are side_filter suppressions, a different cause. This stale alerting:true is the likely source of the 'alpaca_live cannot place' framing MI-140 and MI-201 both inherited. COLLAPSED STATE: the reader cannot tell 'this account is alerting' from 'this account's alarm is switched OFF and this is what it last said three weeks ago'. NOT A DUPLICATE OF BL-20260823-ALPACA-LIVE-IS-EXEMPT-FROM-BOTH-DETECTORS-THAT-WATCH-IT, which records that the account IS skipped and argues about whether it should be. This row is about what the skip LEAVES BEHIND, and it would apply to any future skipped account. !! THE SKIP ITSELF IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE REMOVED TO FIX THIS -- docs/claude/system-actions.md records it as a deliberate operator silencing (alpaca_live, 127 of 127 orders refused for zero balance). The defect is the immortal latch. PROPOSED FIX (not applied): retire a skipped account's latch on each run -- alerting:false, alert_disposition:'suppressed_env_skip', a fresh updated_at, and the last graded verdict/cause/date preserved under their own keys -- and send NO ping, because silence is the entire point of the skip. It must NOT send the ordinary green [OK], which would assert a recovery nobody measured.
items.resolution_criteria: silent_accounts() no longer returns alpaca_live while it is in SILENT_REFUSAL_SKIP, verified by reading /api/diag/log_file?name=silent_refusal_alert_state on the fleet and seeing that account's row carry a fresh updated_at with alerting:false and an alert_disposition naming the skip -- NOT by a passing test, which cannot reach the live latch file. !! A GREEN SUITE CLEARS NOTHING: the release loop this row is about already has tests and already ships. !! AND THE LATCH SIMPLY VANISHING DOES NOT CLEAR IT EITHER unless the last graded verdict is preserved -- deleting the row loses the record of what was last observed, which is a different fix and a worse one. Alternatively the operator REMOVES alpaca_live from SILENT_REFUSAL_SKIP, in which case the ordinary loops resume and this row closes as closed_answered -- but record that as the decision it is, with the consequence stated (the account starts paging again).

items.title: config/accounts.yaml and the 2026-08-25 affordability sweep both record alpaca_live's reachable set as 'TLT IEF SLV USO IAUM GDX' as though it were a constant -- GDX no longer sizes, and the drift is in the permissive direction
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-10 by running RiskManager.position_size (whole_units=True, available_usd = total_account_usd = balance = 200.22 from /api/diag/broker_account_status, risk_pct 0.02) over EVERY distinct (entry, stop_loss) pair on the buy side of gdx_pullback_1d's gdx_pullback_1d_eval rows since 2026-06-01 (/api/diag/audit_query, n=59 distinct setups, the pull did not hit the 1000-row cap so the population is complete): 0 of 59 size above zero. Median risk/share 7.665 against the round-up ceiling of 1.5 x 0.02 x 200.22 = 6.0066. GDX's current daily close is 99.43 (/api/bot/candles, same day) against the 74.59 the 2026-08-25 sweep used. WHAT THE RECORD SAYS: config/accounts.yaml's alpaca_live risk block states 'reachable : TLT IEF SLV USO IAUM GDX' and explains at length that GDX is reachable at 2% via the round-up-to-one-share relaxation at a 5.28 stop; docs/research/alpaca-200-affordability-sweep-2026-08-25.md carries the same set. Neither is wrong about its own date. WHY IT MATTERS AND WHY IT IS THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION: reachability is a function of PRICE and VOLATILITY, both of which move without a commit, and the record reads as a property of the account. A session proposing a roster from it would propose a leg that cannot place -- which is exactly the class this repo names as 'field beats comment', except here the field is a live price and there is no field to read. The same arithmetic runs the other way too: a symbol can fall back INTO the set and nobody would notice. RELATED BUT DISTINCT: BL-20260826-ALPACA-LIVE-AT-200-USD-CANNOT-SIZE-ITS-LARGEST-SYMBOLS records the constraint; this row records that the recorded ANSWER to the constraint decays. SECOND STALE CLAIM IN THE SAME BLOCK, measured the same day: accounts.yaml states (over order_packages 2026-05-02..2026-08-23) that gld_pullback_1d, gdx_pullback_1d, iaum_pullback_1d and slv_pullback_1d are '100% short' and 'go fully inert' under side_filter: long. Over 2026-06-01..2026-09-10 each of those four produced at least one LONG pipeline_result package (1, 1, 1, 1 respectively). Both readings are correct over their own populations; the record does not say which population it describes, and a session treating those legs as permanently inert would wrongly exclude three real candidates.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) the reachable-set claim is re-derived on demand rather than recorded as a constant -- a script or workflow that runs RiskManager.position_size over the current roster at the current balance and current prices, whose output is the thing sessions read -- or (b) the two prose copies carry an explicit as-of date and a statement that reachability decays with price, so a reader knows to re-measure. !! (b) ALONE IS WEAKER AND MUST BE RECORDED AS THE CHEAPER CHOICE IF TAKEN: a dated claim still goes stale, it merely says so. !! DO NOT close this by editing the GDX line to say 'refused' -- that is the same defect with a different value, and it would be stale again on the next meaningful move in GDX. The claim under repair is that the set is CONSTANT, not the value of any one entry.

items.title: check_pr_landing.py's closed hold_reason vocabulary has no term for the most common real reason a Tier-1 PR gives up self-landing -- that R13's merge_slot claim makes it conflict repeatedly -- so the only way to declare that hold is to assert something false
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-10 on PR #11673 (MI-201). R13 requires a self-landing branch to carry a merge_slot claim in docs/claude/session-board.json. That single object is rewritten by every self-landing PR in the repo, so #11673 went `dirty` THREE TIMES IN TWENTY MINUTES on that one file alone -- 09:13, 09:29, 09:35 -- each time from an unrelated merge, with its own content untouched. This is the loop the coordination board measured on 2026-09-08, where #11384 was re-resolved through TEN rounds and the manager's own comment identified the merge_slot object as the variable ('they write merge_slot, I don't'). MI-204's documented remedy is to declare `landing: hold`, which drops the file from the diff and ends the loop. THE GAP: R7 enforces a closed vocabulary of six hold_reasons -- awaiting_evidence, changes_landing_machinery, depends_on_unmerged_pr, operator_asked_to_hold, tier_2_3_needs_approval, unvouchable_paths -- and NONE describes this. Checked all six against #11673 rather than picking the nearest: the first three and tier_2_3 are plainly false, and unvouchable_paths is false BY THE GUARD'S OWN R14 CHECK, since every path in that diff (ROADMAP.md, docs/research/**, .github/pr-landing/**) is inside TIER1_SURFACE via `*.md`, `docs/**` and `.github/**`. !! SO THE ONLY WAY TO TAKE THE DOCUMENTED REMEDY IS TO ASSERT SOMETHING FALSE. I did exactly that for one commit -- wrote `operator_asked_to_hold` when no operator had asked, with the real reason in hold_text -- then reverted it. That is the mislabelled-verdict failure the guard's OWN message cites: 'a hold is a stated kind of hold and not an adjective -- the operator_decision discipline in docs/claude/work/OPEN-PRS.json'. OPEN-PRS.json's own doctrine is that a row recording a verdict its text does not support is WORSE than a missing row, and burying the truth in hold_text does not repair the typed field a reader greps or a script filters on. !! AND THE INCENTIVE RUNS THE WRONG WAY: the cheapest path is to mislabel, the honest path is to keep re-resolving and keep churning the register for everyone else. A vocabulary that makes the correct action the expensive one is the same shape as a guard cheaper to lie to than to satisfy.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) a new hold_reason exists for this condition -- e.g. `self_land_would_churn_a_shared_register` -- so the remedy MI-204 documented can be declared truthfully, OR (b) R13 stops requiring the claim to live in the DIFF, which removes the conflict source and makes the hold unnecessary. !! (b) IS THE STRUCTURAL FIX AND IS NOT OBVIOUSLY RIGHT: check_pr_landing.py's own docstring says R13 records an ATTRIBUTABLE claim and 'does NOT serialize' (a committed claim reaches no other session until merge, BL-20260810-MERGE-SLOT-MIRROR-UNWRITABLE-PRE-MERGE). If it serializes nothing, what the in-diff requirement buys is attribution alone -- and it is worth measuring whether that is worth this much churn before changing it. Decide, do not just widen. !! DO NOT CLOSE THIS BY ADDING A CATCH-ALL `other`: R7's whole point is a closed vocabulary, and an `other` bucket restores the adjective it was written to forbid. !! AND A GREEN GUARD RUN CLEARS NOTHING -- the guard passes today, on a declaration that is either false or self-landing into the loop. The condition is about which honest options exist.

items.title: RECURRENCE of BL-20260903: the remedy (pip install pytest) is already filed and a session still shipped two real defects past a guard suite it never ran — because the coordination board says to discount those guards
items.detail: THIS IS A RECURRENCE AND THAT IS THE FINDING, so it is filed with similar_ok rather than dropped as a duplicate. BL-20260903-RUN-GUARDS-REPORTS-FAIL-WHERE-THE-TEST-RUNNER-IS-ABSENT-SO-COULD-NOT-LOOK-READS-AS-BROKEN is OPEN, names this exact class, AND ALREADY RECORDS THE ONE-COMMAND REMEDY IN ITS OWN EVIDENCE FIELD (`pip install pytest` (9.1.1) then the same six files -> 144 passed in 4.05s). Seven days later, on 2026-09-10, MI-241 (session_01FyYyybxWC7VD1Rq1doEEdf) hit the identical condition, did NOT install, and reported `PASS 66 - FAIL 4, all four environmental, not the diff` on PR #11652. !! IT WAS NOT A HARMLESS MISREADING. CI then failed on exactly those guards and named TWO REAL DEFECTS that were sitting inside them: (a) the new `reattach-stranded-package-legs` system-action was absent from tests/ops/test_system_actions_workflow.py::EXPECTED_ACTIONS, whose own failure message says every other guard in that module loops over that dict so an unregistered action 'will pass CI and then abort at dispatch before the SSH key step' -- i.e. the wrapper would have MERGED LOOKING CORRECT and failed the operator the first time they ran an approved real-money-adjacent repair; and (b) scripts/ops/notify_run.sh had no priority mapping, so the run would have notified the operator with no routing. Both are load-bearing and NEITHER is reachable by any non-pytest guard. !! THE NEW MECHANISM, WHICH BL-20260903 DOES NOT CONTAIN: THE COUNTERMEASURE LIVES ON A SURFACE NOBODY READS MID-TASK AND THE SURFACE SESSIONS DO READ SAYS THE OPPOSITE. The health-review backlog is 1298 rows and CLAUDE.md itself says the backlogs are 'far too large to read at session start'. Meanwhile the LIVE COORDINATION BOARD -- which every session is required to read before its first substantive change -- carries MI-188b's 2026-09-08 note (#11336, comment 5581292242): 'pytest is not installed in these sub-session containers ... a local run_guards.py here reports FAIL 3 on a clean tree; that is the environment, not the diff.' That note is FACTUALLY TRUE, was written in good faith, and is the most load-bearing sentence a session reads on this subject. It states the diagnosis and omits the remedy, so its practical effect is to license discounting the three guards rather than spending one command on them. A session following the board correctly lands in the failure the backlog already solved. !! SO THE GAP IS NOT KNOWLEDGE, IT IS ROUTING -- which is why 'read the backlog' is not a fix and neither is another restatement. The repo has paid for this shape before (CLAUDE.md: 'a reminder is not a mechanism'; MI-15 twice). Note also that this instance was NOT caught by the guard suite, by the session, or by review -- it was caught by CI, i.e. by the one runner where the tools are actually installed, which is the only reason the two defects did not merge.
items.evidence: MEASURED 2026-09-10 on branch claude/mi241-f39-reattach-dispatch. Before: `python3 scripts/ci/run_guards.py --base main` -> PASS 66 / FAIL 4 / SKIP 23, the four being trainer-capture-watch-guard, artifact-validity-guard, operator-owed-guard (all `python3 -m pytest ...` -> 'No module named pytest', reproduced identically on clean origin/main as a positive control) and layer-guard (`lint-imports` exit 127, binary absent). After `pip install pytest import-linter`: same command -> PASS 70 / FAIL 0 / SKIP 23, every guard executed; `lint-imports --config .importlinter` -> 6 contracts kept, 0 broken. The two defects: PR #11652 head 297814e9e, pytest-run conclusion=failure, run 34454591387 job 102797998910 -- '2 failed, 16074 passed' -- test_no_action_exists_in_the_workflow_that_is_absent_from_EXPECTED_ACTIONS and test_notify_run_handles_every_allowlisted_action. Both fixed in 5383b264b; tests/ops/test_system_actions_workflow.py then 384 passed. Prior row: BL-20260903-RUN-GUARDS-REPORTS-FAIL-WHERE-THE-TEST-RUNNER-IS-ABSENT-SO-COULD-NOT-LOOK-READS-AS-BROKEN (open, severity medium, filed 2026-09-03). Board note: issue #11336 comment 5581292242, 2026-09-08T07:48:21Z.
items.resolution_criteria: The REMEDY reaches a session at the moment it hits the condition, without depending on anyone having read a 1298-row backlog. Sufficient: run_guards.py, on detecting that a guard's runner is absent, PRINTS the install command and grades the guard `could_not_run` distinctly from `fail` (which is BL-20260903's own resolution_criteria -- resolving that row resolves this one, and this row should then be closed as a duplicate of the fix rather than worked separately). Also sufficient and cheaper as an interim: the session-start container provisions pytest + import-linter, making the condition unreachable. !! NOT SUFFICIENT: editing or deleting the board note. It is TRUE, it was correct to post, and a board comment is a per-session artifact that scrolls away -- treating a correct observation as the defect would discourage exactly the reporting this repo wants. The defect is that the tool says nothing at the point of failure. !! NOT SUFFICIENT EITHER: another line in CLAUDE.md. This row's whole content is that the knowledge already existed in writing and did not transfer.

items.title: scripts/ops/stuck_automation_branches.py decides LANDED with `merge-base --is-ancestor`, which is unreachable in a squash-merge repo — so its whole purpose (find genuinely stuck branches) is defeated and its ::warning:: counts merged branches
items.detail:
RECURRENCE / EXTENSION of the OPEN row BL-20260908-MERGE-BASE-IS-ANCESTOR-REPORTS-NOT-MERGED-FOR-EVERY-SQUASH-MERGED-PR-AND-FAILS-SILENTLY. Filed as a separate row deliberately, not as a duplicate, because it ANSWERS THAT ROW'S OWN EXPLICITLY-STATED UNKNOWN. Its closing line reads 'NOT ESTABLISHED: whether any committed script or workflow in this repo currently uses --is-ancestor or --grep to decide me[rged]'. It does. Established 2026-09-10 by MI-247/MI-251 (session_01Ek2KDXDeLAMrN4JH4aEXWf).

THE SITE: scripts/ops/stuck_automation_branches.py::classify, line ~124. It runs `git merge-base --is-ancestor <branch-sha> <shared_ref>` and returns Row(branch, LANDED, ...) on rc 0. On rc 1 it falls through to age-based classification -> STUCK (>= stale_hours) or IN_FLIGHT.

MEASURED, WITH THE POPULATION STATED: over ALL 712 remote-tracking branches in a fresh clone (715 refs less origin/HEAD and 3 scratch refs this session created), EXACTLY ONE grades LANDED by that test, and it is origin/main itself -- trivially an ancestor of itself. So for every real branch LANDED IS DEAD CODE. This repo squash-merges (verified independently the same session: PR #11689 carries merged_at 2026-09-10T11:53:59Z while `--is-ancestor` on its branch head returns not-an-ancestor), and a squash commit is a NEW object sharing no ancestry with the branch it came from.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT MERELY COSMETIC: the tool's stated purpose is to find branches that have NOT landed, and it now cannot distinguish 'merged and not deleted' from 'genuinely stranded'. Line ~223 emits `::warning:: N automation branch(es) have not landed`, so that N is inflated by every merged-but-undeleted branch. It is report-only (a warning, never a failing exit), so the harm is a DESENSITISED ALARM rather than a blocked pipeline -- which is the P1 class CLAUDE.md's 'if you see something, say something' section names explicitly. BL-20260830-A-TRANSIENT-RED-BASE-PERMANENTLY-STRANDS-AN-AUTOMERGE-BRANCH depends on this tool to adjudicate its four PR-less branches; that adjudication is running on a signal that cannot currently be trusted.

WHY ITS SELF-TEST PASSES ANYWAY (so nobody reads green as evidence): the self-test at ~line 163 exercises only state_for_age over (6.0, STUCK) / (48.0, STUCK) pairs plus two tautology guards at ~169/173. It never constructs a squash-merged branch, so the LANDED path is never exercised against the only case that matters. Green here is exactly the vacuous control the file's own docstring warns about one function earlier.

AND THE SAME DEFECT COST A LIVE SESSION TWO ROUNDS THE SAME DAY, which converts the parent row's HYPOTHETICAL harm into a measured one. That row warns: 'had this probe been written into a scheduled check-in, the loop would have re-armed indefinitely against a PR merged an hour earlier.' On 2026-09-10 MI-247 wrote exactly that probe into its own scheduled check-in to test whether the R13 merge_slot holder was TERMINAL, and twice declined to take a slot whose holder had already merged. On a SINGLE-HOLDER resource the failure is worse than waiting: the slot reads permanently occupied, which is a deadlock, and the ancestry test is precisely what a session reaches for as the rigorous alternative after being burned by --grep.

PROPOSED FIX (Tier-1, tooling; NOT applied -- filing is the act of not taking the item): grade LANDED from the squash SUBJECT rather than ancestry, i.e. `git log <shared_ref> --format=%s | grep -F '(#N)'` for the branch's PR number, or from the PR API's merged_at where a token is available; keep a distinct UNKNOWN for 'we could not look' (already present and correct); and add a self-test fixture that plants a SQUASH-merged branch so the LANDED path is exercised against the case that actually occurs. NOTE the parent row's own caveat: even a subject match is weaker than the API field, since a commit could quote '(#N)' for other reasons -- so prefer the API when available and say which was used.

NOT ESTABLISHED, deliberately: the other two committed --is-ancestor sites (.github/actions/commit-to-main/action.yml:400 and .github/workflows/work-digest.yml:167) were NOT audited here. Both may be legitimate -- ancestry is the RIGHT test for asking whether a specific COMMIT is contained, and is only wrong when asking whether a BRANCH has landed. Do not assume they are broken, and do not assume they are fine; they have not been looked at.
items.tier: 1 — tooling / observability (scripts/ops/*.py). No src/, no config/, no order path.
items.resolution_criteria: scripts/ops/stuck_automation_branches.py is OBSERVED placing a genuinely-merged branch into its LANDED bucket — i.e. a real run whose printed output lists, under LANDED, a branch whose PR carries a merged_at timestamp. Read it off the run output, not from the diff. [!] A GREEN SELF-TEST CLEARS NOTHING, and that is the whole point of this row: the self-test exercises only state_for_age plus two tautology guards and never constructs a squash-merged branch, which is the only case that occurs here — so it passed throughout while LANDED was dead code. A fix must therefore ALSO add a fixture that plants a squash-merged branch, or the next regression is equally invisible. [!] AND `stuck=0` DOES NOT CLEAR IT: the STUCK count falling to zero because branches were deleted is byte-identical to the classifier working. The clearing observation is a branch appearing under LANDED, never a count going down. [!] IF THE OPERATOR OR A REVIEW DECIDES THE TOOL SHOULD BE RETIRED instead of fixed, this row does not clear — it CHANGES: automation-branch staleness is then unwatched, which is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one rather than left looking like a fix in flight.

EITHER of three OPPOSITE outcomes, and they are different findings -- say which. (a) MECHANISED: `scripts/ops/claim_merge_slot.py --release` (or equivalent) EXISTS and a real commit to docs/claude/session-board.json is OBSERVED carrying merge_slot cleared to nulls, authored by the session that held it, AFTER its PR merged -- read the committed file on main, not the helper's --help. (b) DERIVED: merge_slot carries the claiming PR number and a reader grades held/finished/unknown from it, so the release is no longer a write anyone must remember. (c) RETIRED: the operator or a manager decides the release is not worth mechanising, the prose step is DELETED from coordination-board.md and session-coordination/SKILL.md, and the decision is RECORDED -- a claim is then SUPERSEDED rather than released, which is legitimate and must not be left looking like a step about to be automated. !! A SINGLE HAND-EDITED RELEASE CLEARS NOTHING: one session doing it by hand is exactly what 25 of 25 did not do, and proves nothing about the next one. !! AND A GREEN R13 CLEARS NOTHING -- R13 grades the CLAIM, which already works; it is blind to whether the slot was ever released.
items.title: The merge-slot RELEASE is prose-only: no helper, no CI rule, and the one splice tool REFUSES to write the released state -- so `merge_slot` collapses `held` and `finished`
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-10 with a POSITIVE CONTROL, not inferred. The CLAIM half is fully mechanised: `scripts/ops/claim_merge_slot.py` exists, `check_pr_landing.py` R13 FAILS an armed branch that does not hold the slot, and the claim is graded in CI on every PR. The RELEASE half exists ONLY as prose, in exactly three places -- docs/claude/coordination-board.md:207 and :499, and .claude/skills/session-coordination/SKILL.md:210, which says to 'clear session-board.json::merge_slot back to nulls immediately after the merge resolves (merged OR aborted). A held-but-abandoned claim blocks everyone.' There is NO helper and NO check. === AND THE ONE SANCTIONED WRITER REFUSES TO PERFORM IT: claim_merge_slot.py raises SpliceError('--branch is empty; R13 grades `merge_slot.branch`') on an empty branch, so the tool built precisely because session-board.json has a bespoke serialisation (a naive re-dump reformats it) CANNOT write the released shape. Releasing correctly means hand-editing the one file the repo went to the trouble of building a splice helper for. === CONSEQUENCE, WHICH IS A COLLAPSED STATE IN THIS REPO'S OWN VOCABULARY: `merge_slot` cannot say 'nobody holds this'. held-by-a-live-session and held-by-a-session-that-finished-hours-ago are ONE value, and a session arriving cold cannot tell them apart without going to GitHub and reading the claiming PR's merge state -- exactly the out-of-band check the durable in-repo slot exists to avoid. === POPULATION: over the LAST 25 commits touching docs/claude/session-board.json, ZERO ever wrote a cleared slot -- every one is a dict naming a session. The documented step has never been performed by anyone, which is the evidence that this is a MECHANISM gap and not a discipline gap. === NOT HYPOTHETICAL, AND IT COST TIME THE SAME DAY: at 13:43Z the slot read held_by session_01HrmZ1RRNM4UnEUaFdrPEjj for branch claude/mgr-hb-20260910T1326, whose own purpose text ended 'Released on merge.' That PR (#11698) had MERGED at 13:34:14Z -- nine minutes earlier -- and the release write never landed. I could establish the claim was stale only by calling pull_request_read on #11698 and reading merged: true. A session that instead waited behind it would have waited on nothing. === AND THE RELEASE IS STRUCTURALLY UNPERFORMABLE FROM AN ARMED PR, which is why this persists rather than being an oversight anyone fixes in passing: R13 requires an ARMED branch to HOLD the slot, so a PR that clears the slot to nulls AND arms itself fails R13 by construction. Clearing it needs an unarmed, hand-merged PR or a direct push to main. This very row is filed from a PR that therefore HOLDS the slot rather than releasing it -- the finding demonstrated, not described.
items.proposed_fix: OPTIONS, none applied -- filed, not fixed, and the choice is arguable. (a) Give claim_merge_slot.py a `--release` flag that splices the nulls shape, and have R13 accept a released slot as a valid terminal state; the armed-PR circularity then still needs R13 to exempt a diff whose ONLY session-board change is a release. (b) DERIVE the slot's liveness instead of asserting it -- carry the claiming PR number and grade held/finished/unknown from GitHub, the shape telegram_poll_registry already uses (a heartbeat expires on its own rather than depending on the holder to write a release). (c) Decide the release is not worth mechanising and DELETE the prose step, recording that a claim is SUPERSEDED rather than released -- legitimate, and better than a documented step nobody has ever performed. !! DO NOT 'fix' this by reminding sessions to release: the measurement above is that 25 of 25 did not, which is the reminder-is-not-a-mechanism non-fix this repo has already paid for on MI-15 (twice).

items.resolution_criteria: A PR opened by claude-pr-automerge under GITHUB_TOKEN is OBSERVED carrying real CI -- i.e. get_check_runs on a bot-opened PR returns the repo's actual required checks (guards, pytest-collect, pytest-run, repo-inventory) and not only `open-and-automerge` -- OR the workflow is observed REFUSING to create a PR at all (adopt-only), so the zero-CI birth is unreachable by construction. Name the PR and paste the check-run census. !! A QUIET WEEK CLEARS NOTHING: the trap fires only when the workflow WINS the race against a session's own create_pull_request, so an absence of occurrences is not evidence the shape is gone -- it went 2026-09-08 (six) to 2026-09-10 (one) with no code change in between. !! RESTATING THE ORDERING RULE ANYWHERE CLEARS NOTHING: that is what already exists at CLAUDE.md line ~1522 and what seven occurrences falsify. !! AND ONE SESSION FOLLOWING THE TWO-PUSH ORDER CORRECTLY (as PR #11700 did) IS NOT A FIX -- it is one session, and the row is about the default.
items.title: RECURRENCE (7th): a PR born under GITHUB_TOKEN carries ONE GREEN check and no real CI -- documented in CLAUDE.md, hit anyway, because the remedy is a two-push ordering rule
items.detail: FILED AS A RECURRENCE DELIBERATELY -- that the documented remedy did not hold IS the finding. CLAUDE.md line ~1522 already describes this exactly ('the PR is *born* with no `pull_request` event and carries exactly ONE check run -- its own `open-and-automerge`') and names SIX occurrences on 2026-09-08 alone (#11356, #11392, #11395, #11407, #11419, #11424). === SEVENTH OCCURRENCE, MEASURED 2026-09-10 ON #11699: I pushed the content and the arming file in ONE push; claude-pr-automerge won the race against my own create_pull_request (which returned 'A pull request already exists'), and the PR was opened by github-actions[bot]. get_check_runs returned total_count 1 -- open-and-automerge, conclusion SUCCESS -- with auto-merge ALREADY ARMED, so that single green check was the entire required-check gate and a PR with ZERO real CI could have squashed on it. I armed real CI with a follow-up commit and the PR then ran guards/pytest-collect/pytest-run/repo-inventory, all green. === WHY THE DOCUMENTED REMEDY DOES NOT HOLD, which is the part worth fixing: the remedy is an ORDERING rule about two SEPARATE pushes (open the PR yourself first, THEN push the arming file), and the ergonomic default -- commit the content and its arming file together, one push, one guard run -- violates it. A rule whose violation is the path of least resistance keeps being violated however well it is written down. Seven occurrences in three days is the evidence. === AND IT IS THE ONLY LOW-CHECK-COUNT CAUSE THAT RENDERS AS A PASS. CLAUDE.md teaches reading mergeable_state to separate `dirty` (merge conflict) from `blocked` (checks pending), both of which show total_count 0. This one shows total_count 1 and GREEN, so neither the count nor the colour flags it. === I ALSO GOT THE DIAGNOSIS WRONG FIRST AND IT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN TIDIED AWAY: my own landing declaration initially asserted CLAUDE.md 'does not yet list' this cause. It does, at line 1522. I claimed a documentation gap without grepping for it, inside a note about being careful, and corrected it in place in the same PR. The false claim shipped in one commit message and is not amendable away.
items.proposed_fix: OPTIONS, none applied. (a) Make claude-pr-automerge ADOPT-ONLY -- refuse to create a PR at all. It already calls pulls.create only when pulls.list returns nothing, so making that branch a hard error converts a silent zero-CI PR into a loud 'open the PR yourself first', and the arming file could then safely ride the same push as the content. That REMOVES the ordering rule rather than restating it. (b) Have the workflow push one trivial arming commit ITSELF after creating the PR, so a PR it opens always carries a pull_request event -- cheaper, but it re-introduces the 'invent a commit' pressure CLAUDE.md warns pads diffs. (c) A guard failing a PR whose only check run is open-and-automerge; note it CANNOT run as a check on that PR (no pull_request event to trigger it), so it must live in the workflow itself or in the merge queue. !! DO NOT fix this by restating the ordering rule -- that is what already exists and what seven occurrences falsify.

items.tier: 1 (test tooling; no runtime, order path or config)
items.title: webapp/tests/api-contract.mjs validates SPA field reads against a RECORDED fixture, which is routinely captured from a locally-patched bot -- so it passes on a field the DEPLOYED bot does not serve, and cannot see the pre-deploy window in which every row reading that field renders as a false negative
items.detail:
RECURRENCE of BL-20260901-TEST-FIXTURE-SPELLED-A-VOCABULARY-THE-PRODUCER-DOES-NOT-EMIT (resolved) in DIFFERENT machinery -- that row was a python test fixture spelling an action vocabulary in the wrong case so 7/7 passed while the live filter matched nothing; this is the same class in the SPA's cross-repo contract checker, which is why it is filed rather than dropped: the first fix was scoped to the instance, not the class.

MEASURED 2026-09-10 while shipping MI-254. The bot half (#11688) adds a per-row `settled` to GET /api/bot/work/decisions; the SPA half read it as `settled === false` / `=== true`. webapp/tests/api-contract.mjs went GREEN (110 field reads / 3 routes) because its fixture webapp/tests/fixtures/work_decisions.json was captured from a bot ALREADY carrying the field -- its own _fixture_note says so honestly ('REAL captured ... AFTER MI-254'). Rendered against the DEPLOYED bot, which does not serve `settled`, ALL 26 DECISIONS VANISHED FROM THE PAGE: neither strict test matched, so every row fell out of both buckets with no trace. Worse, one unanswerable blocked_on edge was present, so the 'Nothing is waiting on you right now' empty-state did not fire either -- the panel read as POPULATED while the inbox was silently empty, on the one surface built to tell the operator what is waiting on them.

THE GAP IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A BAD FIXTURE. The checker asks 'does every field this consumer reads exist in the recorded payload?' -- the mirror of provenance-consumer-guard, and genuinely useful. But the recorded payload is whatever the author captured, and an author shipping a cross-repo pair captures from their own patched bot BY CONSTRUCTION. So the checker validates the POST-deploy contract and is blind to the window between the two merges, which on this system is real: the bot half deploys via ict-git-sync (~5 min after merge) while the SPA deploys via GitHub Pages independently, and a `landing: hold` bot PR waiting on a hand-merge can widen that window to hours. #11688 was exactly that.

!! GREEN HERE IS NOT EVIDENCE THE DEPLOYED BOT SERVES THE FIELD, and nothing says so at the point of use. A reviewer reads 'api-contract: OK -- 110 field read(s) ... all exist in their recorded payloads' and the word RECORDED is doing load-bearing work that the sentence does not flag.

NOT A BLOCKER ON MI-254: that SPA now handles the absent field as a named third state (`ungraded` = we could not tell, surfaced not hidden), so the specific instance is closed and the two PRs no longer have a hard ordering dependency. What is UNFIXED is that the next cross-repo pair has nothing stopping it repeating this -- the fix was mine by hand, prompted by rendering against live, not by any check.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) api-contract.mjs distinguishes a field the consumer reads that is present in the fixture but NOT in a payload captured from the CURRENTLY DEPLOYED bot -- which needs the checker to know a live-capture provenance stamp, so the honest minimum is that a fixture declares whether it was captured from a deployed or a patched bot and the checker REPORTS that rather than passing silently; OR (b) it is recorded as a DECISION that the checker deliberately validates only the post-deploy contract, with the consequence stated -- that every cross-repo field addition must handle its own absence -- and that duty written where an author of such a pair will read it. !! A GREEN RUN CLEARS NOTHING: green is precisely what this row records as uninformative. !! AND FIXING THE ONE FIXTURE CLEARS NOTHING EITHER -- the MI-254 fixture is correct and honest; the gap is that nothing generalises it.
