items.resolution_criteria: `python3 scripts/ops/sweep_stale_automation_prs.py --open-prs <live list>` reports ZERO PRs in state `undated_payload` across two consecutive runs, because each of docs/claude/DUE.md, docs/claude/ERROR-FEED-DIGEST.md, docs/claude/READOUT.md, comms/strategy_reviews/<date>/INDEX.json, comms/macro/valuation_snapshots.jsonl and comms/macro/econ_calendar_captures/*.json now carries a machine-readable generation timestamp its generator wrote. ⚠️ NOT satisfied by widening the sweeper's DATE_FIELDS or defaulting an absent date — that converts 'we could not tell' into 'safe', which is the failure this row exists to prevent.
items.title: 13 of 50 open automation PRs cannot be triaged mechanically because the files they regenerate carry no `generated_at`
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09T08:1xZ, population = the 50 open `automation/*` PRs of 52 open PRs total. `scripts/ops/sweep_stale_automation_prs.py` decides whether a stranded automation PR should be refreshed or is superseded by comparing its payload's own generation timestamp against main's. THIRTEEN PRs grade `undated_payload` — the file differs from main and carries no comparable timestamp, so newer/older CANNOT BE DETERMINED and the sweeper correctly refuses to guess. The undated files are `docs/claude/DUE.md`, `docs/claude/ERROR-FEED-DIGEST.md`, `docs/claude/READOUT.md`, `CLAUDE.md`'s rendered brief block, `comms/strategy_reviews/<date>/INDEX.json`, `comms/macro/valuation_snapshots.jsonl`, `comms/macro/econ_calendar_captures/*.json` and `automation/board-results/*.txt`. Their JSON siblings (TRAINER-CAPTURE-WATCH.json, PR-QUEUE-WATCH.json, OPEN-PRS.json, WORK-DIGEST.json, REAPER-OBSERVATIONS.json) all DO stamp `generated_at` and grade cleanly. REMEDY: have each generator stamp its output — a front-matter or sibling `.meta.json` for the Markdown ones. ⚠️ NOT a sweeper defect: `undated_payload` is the honest reading and must not be softened into a default, which is how a 'we could not tell' becomes a 'safe'. The cost is that those 13 stay a hand triage.

items.resolution_criteria: `python3 scripts/ops/open_pr_record.py --strict --open-prs <live list>` exits 0 with completeness=`recorded`, AND the sweeper's live triage reports zero PRs in `superseded_older` / `superseded_identical` / `superseded_by_open_pr`, because each has been closed with a `closed_unmerged` row carrying a non-empty `disposition`. ⚠️ For the seven carrying a pending-pings row (#11442/#11445/#11452/#11465/#11471/#11493/#11512) the row must additionally name WHERE the rescued ping landed on main and record that it was verified present AFTER that merge — the #10974 pattern. A close without that evidence does not satisfy this row.
items.title: 27 open automation PRs would REWIND main if landed and must be closed with a recorded `disposition`, which nothing does automatically
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09T08:1xZ by `scripts/ops/sweep_stale_automation_prs.py --open-prs`, population = the 50 open `automation/*` PRs. Verdicts: refresh 1 (#11490), superseded_identical 1 (#11488), superseded_older 27, superseded_by_open_pr 1 (#11458), carries_append_only 7, undated_payload 13. The 27 `superseded_older` carry a register OLDER than main's, so landing them would REWIND main — they must be CLOSED, not merged. ⚠️ The sweeper deliberately does NOT close them: a `closed_unmerged` row with no `disposition` grades `undispositioned` in `open_pr_record.py`, which is precisely how the 2026-09-09 06:38→07:36Z window of this same incident happened (fixed by #11509). So each close needs a session to write the row. ⚠️ AND SEVEN MORE ARE NOT SAFE TO CLOSE AT ALL YET: #11442/#11445/#11452/#11465/#11471/#11493/#11512 each carry one `docs/claude/pending-pings.jsonl` row absent from main, and closing drops the operator notification — the hazard `OPEN-PRS.json`'s #10902/#10908/#10914 rows already record. Those need the rescue-by-value that #10974 did. ⚠️ AN EARLIER PASS OF THIS TRIAGE WAS WRONG IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION: classifying by the newest dated register alone called 22 PRs cleanly superseded when the true figure was 15, and would have dropped all seven pings.

items.resolution_criteria: A `stale-automation-sweep` run is OBSERVED refreshing at least one real stranded branch and that PR subsequently MERGES — i.e. the post-run half is proven end to end on a live branch, not only by self-test. Until then the row stays open and the mechanism is DEPLOYED, NOT OBSERVED. ⚠️ Closing this row is NOT a decision to widen `verify-timeout-minutes`: the producer-side bound is a recorded choice, and the row ends when the sweeper is shown to cover it, or when a measurement shows it does not.
items.title: `commit-to-main`'s stale-branch refresh is at most ONE attempt inside one `verify-timeout-minutes` window, so any blocker lasting longer strands the branch permanently
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09. `.github/actions/commit-to-main` refreshes a non-progressing branch by merging main in, but the attempt is bounded twice: at most once per run, and only within `verify-timeout-minutes` (default 30). All 25 of 25 call sites DO set `verify-merged: true` (verified by parsing every workflow that references the action — an earlier grep-based count of 7 was a `-A12` window artefact and is retracted), so the refresh is reachable everywhere and DOES work: #11499's head is a `Merge main so the required checks re-run against the current base` commit. It simply cannot reach a blocker that outlives the run. The R13 blocker of 2026-09-09 lasted from ~2026-09-08 through 06:37:54Z and stranded 47 PRs. `.github/workflows/stale-automation-sweep.yml` now covers the post-run half on a 2h cadence. ⚠️ THE PRODUCER-SIDE BOUND IS UNCHANGED and is left that way deliberately — widening the in-run wait costs a runner-hour per producer per run for a case the sweeper handles for free. Filed so the bound is a recorded choice rather than an oversight.

items.title: A post-#11494 automation PR went GREEN with auto-merge armed and its producer's refresh already spent, then main moved and it conflicted — auto-merge stalls silently and nothing comes back
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-09T09:30Z on PR #11518 (`automation/work-digest-34327540243-1`, opened 08:21:03Z). This is NOT the R13 cause #11494 fixed, and that is the point: #11518 POSTDATES #11494 and carries a valid R13 merge-slot claim in its own diff (verified by diffing its merge-base). The full sequence, each step measured rather than inferred: (1) `commit-to-main`'s stale-branch refresh FIRED AND WORKED — the head commit 9ce35856 is literally `Merge main so the required checks re-run against the current base` with a resolved `docs/claude/session-board.json` conflict; (2) all four required checks went GREEN on that sha at 08:31-08:33Z (Guards, pytest-run, pytest-collect, repo-inventory, all `success`); (3) auto-merge was armed by `gh pr merge --auto --squash` at open time; (4) it is STILL OPEN an hour later, and a trial merge against current main now CONFLICTS in `docs/claude/session-board.json` AND `docs/claude/work/WORK-DIGEST.json`. ⚠️ AUTO-MERGE DOES NOT RESOLVE CONFLICTS — it waits, silently and forever, and reports nothing. The producer's refresh is bounded to ONE attempt inside one `verify-timeout-minutes` window and that attempt is already spent; its run has exited; nothing in the repo comes back. So a PR can be green, armed, correctly claimed and STILL permanently stranded. ⚠️ THE CLASS THEREFORE HAS TWO SUB-CASES AND ONLY ONE IS MECHANICALLY FIXABLE: (i) a stale base whose only conflict is the R13 slot file — `scripts/ops/sweep_stale_automation_prs.py` refreshes it, taking main's board and re-asserting the claim; (ii) a DATA conflict between two generator runs (here WORK-DIGEST.json), which no rule can settle without losing one run's output, so the sweeper correctly REFUSES and reports. For (ii) the newest run supersedes and the older PR must be CLOSED — but #11518 also carries a `pending-pings.jsonl` row absent from main, so closing it drops an operator notification unless the row is rescued by value first (the #10974 pattern). ⚠️ AND THE RATE IS THE REAL PROBLEM: measured over 75 minutes, the open `automation/*` queue went 50 -> 51 (two opened, #11518 and #11525; one closed, #11488, closed BY HAND by a session). The queue grows faster than hand-triage drains it.
items.resolution_criteria: A green, armed automation PR that has gone conflicted is OBSERVED returning to mergeable without a session touching it — i.e. a `stale-automation-sweep` run refreshes it and it merges — for sub-case (i). For sub-case (ii) the row ends when the repo can state, in a mechanism rather than in prose, what happens to the older of two generator runs whose outputs conflict: either the producer regenerates cumulatively so two runs cannot conflict, or the older PR is closed with its append-only rows rescued and a recorded `disposition`. ⚠️ NOT satisfied by widening the sweeper to resolve a WORK-DIGEST conflict by picking a side — that silently discards one run's output, which is the loss this row exists to name.

items.title: commit-to-main's `gh pr create` fails on a shared per-USER GraphQL rate limit, so every automation receipt is pushed to a branch with NO pull request ever opened — sustained repo-wide, and Claude sessions consume the same quota
items.tier: 1 — CI/landing machinery only; no src/, config/, deploy/ or order path
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-09-09T16:56Z. POPULATION: all 164 origin/automation/* branches, compared against main's receipts and against the live open-PR list. SIX branches carry a receipt NEWER than main's and NONE has an open PR — WORK-DIGEST 16:03:36Z / 16:39:51Z / 16:41:36Z, TRAINER-CAPTURE-WATCH 16:46:17Z, PR-QUEUE-WATCH 11:50:12Z and 16:53:15Z. FIVE of the six appeared within the preceding hour. Verified with list_pull_requests(state=all, head=...) returning [] on the ones checked individually: never opened, not closed.

CAUSE, read from the run logs and not inferred. Run 34378237022 (work-digest, 16:41:39Z->16:42:43Z) logs verbatim: `commit-to-main: gh pr create attempt 1/3 failed: GraphQL: API rate limit already exceeded for user ID 119055177`, three times, then `could not open a PR ... THE ROWS ARE NOT LOST -- they are pushed to <branch> and can be opened manually`. BYTE-IDENTICAL to run 34355107317 at 13:08Z on a DIFFERENT workflow, so this is sustained (>=3.5h) and repo-wide across work-digest and data-commit alike -- i.e. every producer of a repo-wide liveness receipt.

WHY IT IS HIGH AND NOT MEDIUM. Four always-run (`when: None`) guards grade a dated receipt that must LAND on main, and each is a REQUIRED check, so a receipt that cannot land eventually reds EVERY OPEN PR in the repository. That is exactly the incident WO-20260909-EVERY-PR-IN-THE-REPO-IS-RED was opened for (main was red on check_trainer_capture_watch 07:44:31Z-07:56:53Z, closed by a HAND PORT from another session). Margins when this was filed: digest +4.17h, trainer-capture +9.65h, pr-queue +18.33h.

⚠️ commit-to-main IS BEHAVING CORRECTLY and must not be 'fixed' by making it quieter: it retries, fails loudly, and states where the rows are. What it cannot do is the 'manually' part, and nothing else does it.

⚠️ THE QUOTA IS SHARED WITH CLAUDE SESSIONS AND THIS IS PLAUSIBLY SELF-INFLICTED AT THE ORG LEVEL. Every Claude session in this repo acts as user id 119055177, so sessions polling CI through the MCP and `gh pr create` inside commit-to-main draw on ONE per-user quota. The session filing this row was itself making MCP calls against this repo throughout the window. That makes it a CAPACITY question about how many sessions run concurrently, not only a workflow bug.

⚠️ THE STALE-AUTOMATION SWEEPER (#11519) CANNOT COVER THIS CLASS. It enumerates the OPEN-PR LIST, so a branch that never got a PR is invisible to it. Its premise -- the branch has no owner once the producing run exits -- is right; its INPUT SET is wrong, and it should iterate branches. Recorded on the WO and deliberately not rushed.

⚠️ AND A HAND-OPENED PR IS NOT AUTO-MERGE-ARMED: commit-to-main dies at `gh pr create`, BEFORE `gh pr merge --auto`, so a rescued PR goes green and then sits unmerged unless someone merges it directly. Observed on #11557.

WORKED AROUND, NOT FIXED, at filing time: #11572 / #11573 / #11574 were opened by hand for the newest receipt of each class, refreshed by the sweeper (slot-file conflicts only) and verified as EFFECT. That is three hand rescues in one afternoon (#11557 was the first) and does not scale.
items.resolution_criteria: TWO PARTS, different facts — say WHICH you cleared. (1) A commit-to-main run is OBSERVED opening a PR successfully after a `gh pr create` rate-limit failure, i.e. the action itself survives an exhausted quota — by falling back to a token whose quota is not shared with interactive sessions (the GITHUB_TOKEN / App installation limit is separate from the per-USER limit), or by a bounded wait-and-retry that outlives the reset window rather than 3 attempts inside 65 seconds. Read the run log, not the workflow file. (2) A stranded branch with NO PR is picked up AUTOMATICALLY — the detector must iterate BRANCHES, since the open-PR list structurally cannot see this class. ⚠️ NEITHER IS CLEARED BY A QUIET DAY: the rate limit resets hourly, so the strand disappearing on its own says the quota recovered, NOT that the mechanism works. Establish it against a run that actually hit the limit. ⚠️ NOR BY HAND-LANDING THE STRANDED RECEIPTS — that is the workaround this row exists to make unnecessary, and it has now been done four times. ⚠️ IF THE OPERATOR DECIDES the remedy is to run fewer concurrent Claude sessions rather than to change the action, this row does NOT clear — it CHANGES: the landing path is then known to degrade under session load, which is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one with that consequence stated.

items.title: R13's merge-slot claim is a GUARANTEED conflict point, not a race lost by chance: every armed self-landing PR must write the same line in session-board.json, and the guard's own docstring concedes it does not serialize
items.source: session_01FyYyybxWC7VD1Rq1doEEdf while landing PR #11717 (Tier-1, tests+docs)
items.detail: RECURRENCE, and the earlier row named only half the mechanism. BL-20260910-THE-MERGE-SLOT-HAS-A-DOCUMENTED-RELEASE-STEP-WITH-NO-MECHANISM-SO-EVERY-CLAIM-READS-HELD-FOREVER says claims are never RELEASED. This row is the other half: the claim is never released AND it is MANDATORY, so the register is a guaranteed contention point for exactly the PRs that use the arming route. READ OFF THE GUARD, NOT INFERRED: scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py R13 fails an armed `landing: self` PR that does not set merge_slot to ITSELF in docs/claude/session-board.json, committed in the same push that arms (R6). There is no path that satisfies R6 without touching that one line. And the module docstring concedes the consequence in terms: 'R13 DOES NOT SERIALIZE, and nothing here should be read as claiming it does ... a committed claim reaches no other session until this branch merges' (BL-20260810-MERGE-SLOT-MIRROR-UNWRITABLE-PRE-MERGE). So two concurrently-armed PRs cannot see each other and both write the same line: they conflict BY CONSTRUCTION. MEASURED, and state the population: all 20 merges to main between 15:02:25Z and 18:33:20Z on 2026-09-10 -- 19 intervals -- mean 11.1 min, median 9.4 min, max 39.7 min, and only 3 of 19 gaps (15.8%) are >= 18 min. One full CI cycle on the affected branch measured 17.6 min (18:20:26Z -> 18:38:00Z). So an armed self-landing PR WHOSE DIFF TRIGGERS THE FULL SUITE has roughly a 1-in-6 chance per attempt of finding a window, and the window must START on the push, so the true figure is worse. !! THAT QUALIFIER IS LOAD-BEARING AND THIS ROW LANDED WITHOUT IT -- an unstated population, in the row whose whole subject is stating populations. THE CI CYCLE IS NOT A CONSTANT: pytest-run is a REQUIRED check so it can carry no `paths:` filter (GitHub would leave it pending forever and block the merge), and it therefore always starts but SKIPS the expensive pip install + test run when nothing python/test-relevant changed -- read off the header comment in .github/workflows/pytest-run.yml, not inferred from timings. MEASURED on the pair that produced this row: #11717 touched tests/ and its pytest-run took ~18 min (18:20:26Z->18:38:00Z); #11728 was docs-only and took 20 SECONDS (20:27:29Z->20:27:49Z). So a docs-only armed PR clears the 9.4 min median gap comfortably while a python/tests PR does not, and the 1-in-6 describes only the latter. !! THE CONFLICT-BY-CONSTRUCTION CLAIM IS UNAFFECTED -- two concurrently-armed PRs write the same line whatever their CI duration; only the odds of losing the race vary. !! AND HOW THIS CORRECTION CAME TO BE A SEPARATE PR IS ITSELF THE THIRD MECHANISM AT WORK, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT READ AS SLOPPINESS: the fix was written and pushed to #11728 at ~20:31Z, and auto-merge had already taken the PR at 20:30:09Z. CLAUDE.md documents exactly this -- 'ONCE AUTO-MERGE IS ARMED, TREAT THE BRANCH AS CLOSED TO NEW CONTENT ... whether a post-arming commit lands is a race with CI duration' (measured on #11392). A 20-second docs-only cycle loses that race almost every time, which is the SAME fast-CI fact this correction is about, biting from the opposite direction: fast CI makes a PR easy to LAND and nearly impossible to AMEND. !! AND THE CORRECTION'S OWN PR THEN HIT THE ORDERING TRAP TOO -- #11730, born under GITHUB_TOKEN with total_count 1 (open-and-automerge, green), i.e. reading as passing while real CI had not run. Cause: content, declaration, arming file and merge_slot were committed together and pushed ONCE, so claude-pr-automerge found no existing PR and opened it itself. CLAUDE.md's remedy is explicit -- open the PR by hand FIRST, push the arming file SECOND -- and this session had followed it correctly on #11717, #11722 and #11728 before forgetting it here. RECORDED BECAUSE THE LESSON IS ABOUT THE DEFAULT, NOT THE AUTHOR: the trap hit six times on 2026-09-08 alone, and it caught a session that had just documented it, on the PR documenting it, three successes later. A rule that must be remembered every time, on every push, against a natural one-commit workflow, is a rule that will keep being missed -- which is the same shape as R13's own defect, one level up. PR #11717 needed TEN resolves over ~3 hours; on the sixth it reached FULL GREEN and still lost, because main moved to 60859ec07 at 18:33:20Z while its own pytest-run finished at 18:38:00Z. It merged at 20:21:10Z only when a quiet window happened to open. !! THE PROPERTY IS BACKWARDS: the busier the repo, the less the arming route works. That is the opposite of what a merge-serialisation mechanism should do under load. !! AND THERE IS A NAMED GENERATOR ON THE OTHER SIDE: .github/actions/commit-to-main claims the slot BY DESIGN -- its own committed purpose text reads 'arming auto-merge IS the merge, so R13 takes the slot here' -- and auto-merge runs no release step, so every automated data commit (work-digest, due-list, error-feed digest, PR-queue receipt) deterministically leaves a stale claim behind it. Ten stale claims were reasoned past in one session, from the manager, from automation, and twice from this session itself. !! THE ESCAPE HATCH IS CORRECTLY SHUT, WHICH IS WHY THIS NEEDS A REAL FIX: disarming (landing: hold) removes the R13 claim and the whole conflict surface, but hold_reason is a closed vocabulary and NONE of its values truthfully describes 'disarming to dodge a race' for a Tier-1 PR nobody asked to hold. Picking one anyway is the 'the only passing move was to lie about why' failure check_pr_landing.py's own source comment records against unvouchable_paths. So the honest options today are: race, or ask a human to merge. !! NOT A RUNNER-BUDGET COMPLAINT -- I twice argued that on the board and it was WRONG: CLAUDE.md:1409 records this repo is public specifically to keep the free unlimited Actions budget, so the ten CI cycles cost nothing. The cost is wall-clock latency on every armed PR and session attention spent adjudicating stale claims.
items.proposed_fix: NOT PROPOSED AS A DECISION -- the merge machinery is the manager's and the operator's, and any change here alters how every PR in the repo lands. Options, with the trade-off each buys: (a) give session-board.json a real merge driver GitHub can run, so the claim line auto-resolves like the jsonregister registers already do -- note .gitattributes maps five registers to jsonregister and GitHub NEVER runs it, so this is a change to what CI/GitHub can do, not just a local arm; (b) move the R13 claim OUT of a shared file into a per-branch path (e.g. .github/merge-slots/<slug>.json), keeping the attributable claim R13 wants while removing the shared line entirely -- this looks cheapest and preserves the guard's stated purpose; (c) have .github/actions/commit-to-main RELEASE the slot after its own merge, which fixes the generator but not the structural conflict; (d) accept it and route armed PRs through the manager's queue by policy rather than by luck. Whichever is chosen, the measurement above is the basis for judging whether it worked: re-measure the inter-merge interval against a full CI cycle.
items.resolution_criteria: An armed self-landing Tier-1 PR is OBSERVED landing on its first CI cycle during a period whose measured inter-merge interval is BELOW one full CI cycle -- i.e. the mechanism works under the load that currently defeats it. !! A quiet-period landing proves NOTHING and must not close this: PR #11717 eventually landed that way on its tenth attempt, which is the observation that OPENED this row. !! A green CI run proves nothing either -- CI was green on the sixth attempt and it still lost. !! If the operator decides the arming route should simply not be used for register-touching PRs, this does NOT close -- it CHANGES: that is a legitimate decision and must be RECORDED as one, with the consequence stated, rather than left looking like a fix that is coming.

items.title: gld-compat landing PRs were closed as superseded on a ROW COUNT, which is not a subset test for an append-only per-run corpus - 22 measured rows discarded, and they were the only alpaca_live verdicts for two legs added to a real-money roster the same day
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-10. PRs #11662 and #11664 were closed unmerged at 13:22Z under the operator's 'rescue the 3, close the 9' batch decision. #11662's closing comment reasons: 'carries 77 rows on main and 66 on this branch - this is an earlier run than the one already reflected on main, so every row it holds is a subset of what landed. There is nothing here main lacks.' THE ROW COUNT WAS CORRECT AND WAS THE WRONG TEST. docs/research/gld-compat-matrix-verdicts.jsonl is append-only PER RUN (writer scripts/research/gld_compat_extract.py:109 is a pure append with no dedup), so a LATER run with MORE rows can still lack a strategy an EARLIER run measured - a superset in count is not a superset in content. Set-compared by (strategy, account_id): #11662 (181c08ee, 66 rows) carried 11 ief_pullback_1d__IEF__trades rows absent from main; #11664 (ef4f9c6f, 77 rows) carried 11 iaum_pullback_1d__IAUM__trades rows absent from main. main held only gld_pullback_1h (55 rows over 5 runs), slv_pullback_1d (11) and tlt_pullback_1d (11). 22 measured rows discarded, none superseded. #11664 was explicitly 'waved through with its sibling' - not row-count-checked at all, and it is the one that carried a full 77, so the check that WAS run was run on the wrong PR of the two. WHY IT MATTERS: ief_pullback_1d and iaum_pullback_1d are two of the four legs commit e88ef612a (MI-247) added to alpaca_live, a REAL-MONEY account, the same day. CLAUDE.md makes the per-account compat matrix mandatory before routing a strategy to an account, and the corpus's own stated done-condition is R2 - 'the run is not done when it exits 0, it is done when its rows are readable on main'. Two of the five live legs had no verdict there. !! THE ROSTER ITSELF IS NOT IN QUESTION AND MUST NOT BE RE-LITIGATED ON THIS ROW: read off the closed branches, all four added legs verdict ROUTE on alpaca_live (survival 1.0, p_breach 0.0, size_state measured; n_ledger_trades 68 IEF / 28 IAUM / 66 TLT / 95 SLV). This is an evidence-READABILITY defect, not a routing error. REPAIRED IN THE SAME PR AS THIS ROW: the 22 non-redundant rows were appended to the corpus, reproducing the writer's own serialisation - verified byte-identical for all 220 lines across both branches and main through json.dumps(r, sort_keys=True), and verified to introduce ZERO duplicate rows keyed on the full (strategy, account_id, run_generated_at) triple (77 -> 99 rows, 99 unique triples). The PRs stay closed; only the non-redundant subset was landed, which serves the batch decision's intent (unjam the queue) rather than reversing it. !! WHAT IS NOT FIXED, AND IS THE ACTUAL CLASS: (1) nothing prevents the next batch closure from using a row count as a subset test - the safe test for this corpus is a set-difference on (strategy, account_id, run_generated_at) and no tooling offers one, so the next person reaches for wc -l again; (2) the reason all twelve were stuck is unchanged - pr-landing R13 forces every armed branch to claim docs/claude/session-board.json in the same push that arms, and that file carries no merge driver in .gitattributes, so it conflicts bare the moment any other armed PR lands (#11662 was 31 commits behind). That class is #11519, itself stuck since 2026-09-09. Closing the PRs is not fixing it, and the closures are how the measurement loss happened. !! AND THE RECOVERY WINDOW IS NOT PERMANENT: the 22 rows were recoverable only because the closed branches still existed when this was checked (fetched by sha on 2026-09-10). A closed PR's branch can be pruned, after which a discarded verdict is unrecoverable and silently so - which is the argument for the set-difference happening BEFORE the close, not after.
items.proposed_fix: Two separable pieces, and the second is the one that matters. (a) Give the corpus a subset check: a --check-subset flag on scripts/research/gld_compat_extract.py answering 'does branch X carry any (strategy, account_id, run_generated_at) triple main lacks?', so a batch closure has something cheaper to reach for than wc -l. (b) Fix #11519 - the R13 same-push session-board claim plus a merge-driverless shared JSON is what jams these landing PRs; either give docs/claude/session-board.json a union merge driver in .gitattributes, or exempt automation landing branches from R13. Do NOT reopen #11662/#11664 - their rows are on main now.
items.evidence: closed branches 181c08ee9a98b3e713d8ea44519a2ffd89baf36d (#11662) and ef4f9c6fe95b86612bcc6635bb9bf4f190459ea2 (#11664); closing comment https://github.com/benbaichmankass/Metis-Insights/pull/11662#issuecomment-5619381118; roster commit e88ef612a; corpus docs/research/gld-compat-matrix-verdicts.jsonl; writer scripts/research/gld_compat_extract.py:109; class row #11519
items.source: MI-201 (verification read after standing down)
items.resolution_criteria: TWO PARTS, and the first is ALREADY MET BY THE PR THAT FILED THIS ROW - say which you cleared. (1) DONE: the 22 rows are readable on main - `git show origin/main:docs/research/gld-compat-matrix-verdicts.jsonl` contains at least one ief_pullback_1d__IEF__trades and one iaum_pullback_1d__IAUM__trades row with account_id 'alpaca_live'. Verify by reading main, never from this row. (2) OPEN, and it is what keeps the row open: the CLASS. Either (a) scripts/research/gld_compat_extract.py grows a --check-subset mode that answers 'does branch X carry any (strategy, account_id, run_generated_at) triple main lacks?' AND is demonstrated on two planted inputs - one genuine superset returning clean, one shaped like #11662 (more rows, missing a strategy) returning the 11 missing triples - because a checker that has only ever seen the clean case is the same unasserted-denominator failure as the row count it replaces; or (b) the operator records a decision that batch closures will not be subset-checked, with the consequence stated, which is legitimate and must be WRITTEN DOWN rather than left looking like tooling about to be built. !! #11519 LANDING DOES NOT CLEAR THIS ROW. Fixing the R13 / merge-driver jam removes the pressure to batch-close and is genuinely the higher-value fix, but a corpus with no subset check is still a corpus whose next supersession call is made on a row count. Clear that on #11519's own row. !! AND A LATER RUN OF THE COMPAT MATRIX THAT HAPPENS TO RE-MEASURE ief/iaum DOES NOT CLEAR PART (1) RETROSPECTIVELY - it would mean the rows are present because someone re-ran a job, not because the discarded measurement was recovered, and it would leave the discard itself unrecorded.

items.title: A jammed merge queue silently staled PROBES.json and CONSTRAINT.json for days, and nothing detects a producer that stops LANDING (as opposed to stops RUNNING)
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-10 while dispositioning the 43 open automation PRs (MI-259, PR #11739). `docs/claude/PROBES.json` last LANDED on main at 2026-09-07T10:36:07 (commit 8d51945aa) and `docs/claude/CONSTRAINT.json` at 2026-09-08T11:47:41 (commit 1e1d3718f) — 3 and 2 days stale respectively. Both producers RAN fine; their PRs (#11366, #11428) simply never merged, because every armed branch claims merge_slot in docs/claude/session-board.json, which carries no merge driver in .gitattributes and so conflicts bare (#11519). ⚠️ THE POINT IS NOT THE STALENESS, IT IS THAT NOBODY COULD HAVE NOTICED. Two sibling producers in the same population DO have landed-freshness detectors — check_pr_queue_watch.py and check_trainer_capture_watch.py grade a dated receipt on every PR, which is exactly why PR-QUEUE-WATCH.json and TRAINER-CAPTURE-WATCH.json were current (2026-09-10T21:11 and 20:58) while these two rotted. PROBES.json and CONSTRAINT.json have no such check, so 'the producer is healthy and its output is 3 days old' is indistinguishable from 'the output is current'. ⚠️ AND THE PROBE STALENESS HAS A CONSEQUENCE, not just an age: main's PROBES.json carried no verdict at all for 3 monitoring rows that are still open in OPEN-ITEMS.json (OI-20260907-CLOSE-CONFIRM-RESCOPE..., OI-20260907-TELEMETRY-HOOK..., OI-20260908-ALPACA-QUANTITY-COVERAGE...), while #11366's 09-08 snapshot did. That snapshot was rescued in #11739, which moves main from 09-07 to 09-08 and does NOT make it current. ⚠️ RELATED BUT DISTINCT, do not merge with it: BL-20260902-CONSTRAINT-READOUT-IS-CADENCED-BY-DESIGN-AND-HAS-NO-CRON-AND-NO-FRESHNESS-CHECK is about the readout having no CADENCE. This row is about a producer that HAS a cadence, RUNS on it, and whose output still never reaches main — a different failure with the same symptom.
items.resolution_criteria: EITHER (a) PROBES.json and CONSTRAINT.json gain a landed-freshness check of the same shape as check_pr_queue_watch.py — grading the committed artifact's own generated_at against a declared window, on every PR — so a producer that stops landing reds a PR instead of going quiet; OR (b) it is RECORDED as a decision that these two are not worth watching, with the consequence stated (their staleness is then unobservable). ⚠️ #11519 being fixed does NOT close this row: that would remove the CURRENT cause of the jam and leave the DETECTION gap exactly where it is, so the next cause produces the same silence. ⚠️ AND RE-RUNNING THE PRODUCERS DOES NOT CLOSE IT EITHER — that refreshes the artifacts and proves nothing about whether anyone would notice next time.
items.source: MI-259 / PR #11739 — docs/claude/work/AUTOMATION-PR-DISPOSITIONS-2026-09-10.json::findings_raised

items.title: Pre-spawn registration is not atomic with the spawn, so a cold session correctly measures its own records as absent and duplicates them
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-10 by session_01M3FPDA7Yp9dmMXFqsYzGi3 (OPS lane, MI-259) ON ITSELF. Its spawn prompt instructed it to confirm registry key `pending-20260910T213243Z`, to read object `WO-20260910-DISPOSITION-THE-34-UNDISPOSITIONED-AUTOMATION-PRS-AND`, and to read a `reason_20260910_ops_lane` block in spawn-priority-exception.yaml. At ~21:40Z all three were absent from EVERY REF — established with `git log --all -S`, not a working-tree grep, with a positive control. The session therefore concluded an MI-15 recurrence, authored its own object via capture_idea.py and its own exception block, and self-registered. ⚠️ ALL THREE THEN LANDED, complete and correct, in #11736 (04151f4dd) at ~21:5xZ — main's pending row already carried this session's id and the right object, and main's exception file already carried a full ops-lane block. THE MANAGER WROTE EVERY RECORD; IT IS NOT AN MI-15 RECURRENCE and must not be filed as one. ⚠️ THE DEFECT IS THE ORDERING, NOT THE MANAGER. The spawn happens before the PR carrying the records merges, so a session that starts reading immediately sees a TRUE negative that is about to become false, and 'the record was never written' is indistinguishable from 'the record has not landed yet'. MEASURED COST here: a duplicate work object briefly existed, a duplicate exception block was written, and the resulting three-way conflict on session-board.json + SESSIONS.json + spawn-priority-exception.yaml made PR #11739 `dirty` with zero checks attached. The duplicates were deleted and main's records adopted wholesale. ⚠️ SECOND INSTANCE THE SAME DAY, INDEPENDENTLY: PR #11738 (MI-240, session_01CTPC91xaHrK6ES33UKjkTY) reports the identical shape for key `pending-20260910T213114Z` and also self-registered. Two of two lanes spawned that hour hit it, so it is not a one-off.
items.resolution_criteria: The spawn prompt NAMES THE PR that carries the pre-spawn records (e.g. 'your registry row and object land in #NNNNN'), so a cold session that finds them absent can check whether that PR is still open and distinguish `not landed yet` from `never written` WITHOUT guessing. A three-state read is the point: `landed` / `pending in #NNNNN` / `absent and no PR names it`. ⚠️ NOT SUFFICIENT: telling sessions to wait or retry — the records may legitimately never land if the manager's PR is closed, and a blind retry loop converts a visible defect into a hang. ⚠️ ALSO NOT SUFFICIENT: making session_registry.py's refusal quieter. The refusal was CORRECT both times and is what caused the records to be authored at all; softening it would trade a duplicate for an orphan.
items.source: MI-259 / PR #11739; second instance PR #11738 (MI-240)

items.title: scope-overlap-audit's declaration markers are a closed 5-substring vocabulary, and the natural heading `Files I will touch:` matches NONE of them -- so such a START declares ZERO paths and the audit then reports `0 from a live session`
items.detail: MEASURED 2026-09-10 by running the real parser (scripts/ci/check_scope_overlap.py) against the real comment, not by reading the code. PR #11738's audit reported 'No LIVE session's declaration matched this PR' and '0 matched your OWN declaration', while the PR's author (session_01CTPC91xaHrK6ES33UKjkTY) HAD posted a START 18 minutes earlier (board #11336 comment 5625762007, 2026-09-10T21:35:35Z) naming src/exchange/ib_connector.py, src/main.py, tests/, .github/pr-landing/ and docs/claude/OPEN-ITEMS.json -- five of the ten files the PR changes. CAUSE, ISOLATED: _DECLARATION_MARKERS = ('touching', 'scope', 'files:', 'editing', 'claiming'), and _classify() opens a declare-section only on a line CONTAINING one of those substrings. The heading used was '**Files I expect to touch:**' -- it contains 'touch' but not 'touching', and 'files' but not 'files:', because the words are separated. Run on the live comment: parse_declared_paths -> (set(), set(), ['IB_FETCH_QUEUE_TIMEOUT_S', 'IB_FETCH_TIMEOUT_S']) -- the ONLY thing it resolved was two env-var names out of the 'Explicitly NOT doing' section, which is why the audit's own lower-bound footnote names exactly those two strings. REPRODUCED over a 6-heading table, each with an identical two-path body: 'Files I expect to touch:' -> NO MARKER, declared=[]; 'Files I will touch:' -> NO MARKER, declared=[]; 'Files I am touching:' -> declare, 2 paths; 'Files:' -> declare, 2 paths; 'Scope I am claiming:' -> declare, 2 paths; 'Scope I am about to touch:' -> declare, 2 paths. So whether a START declares anything at all turns on whether its heading happens to use the gerund, or a colon directly after the word 'files'. 'Files I will touch:' is a phrasing already in use on this board (MI-194's START, 2026-09-08T08:23:25Z). !! IT FAILS IN THE REASSURING DIRECTION, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT WORTH FILING: the audit does not say 'this session's declaration was unreadable', it says '0 from a live session' and '0 matched your OWN declaration'. Those read as 'we looked and there was no live overlap' when the truth is 'we could not parse the claim' -- the collapsed-state defect docs/CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL.md names, sitting inside the mechanism whose entire job is detecting a live collision. The audit is careful about this class elsewhere (it grades board health frozen/unreadable/unprovisioned, and resolves unknown branch staleness toward REPORTING), which is why the gap is worth closing rather than tolerating. !! TWO THINGS I CHECKED AND FOUND INNOCENT, recorded so the next session does not re-hunt them. (1) parse_identity is FINE -- run on the same comment it returns {'sessions': ['session_01CTPC91xaHrK6ES33UKjkTY'], 'branches': ['claude/mi240-arm-ib-per-pass-breaker']}, so both the session id and the '**Branch:**' label line resolve correctly. (2) PAGINATION IS FINE AND I NEARLY FILED THE OPPOSITE. I measured 185 board comments in the audit's 24h lookback against a `per_page: 100` fetch and concluded the newest 85 (10.6h, 9 of 22 STARTs) were invisible -- a clean, plausible, and WRONG diagnosis. The call is github.paginate(...), which walks every page. The count was real and the inference was false; reading the line settled it. PROPOSED FIX (not applied -- this session's scope is R2 ONLY, and one PR is one concern): the marker set is the wrong shape for the job. Either match on a stem ('touch' rather than 'touching', 'file' rather than 'files:') or, better, make an UNRESOLVED START visible: when a comment is classified as a START, carries an identity, and yields ZERO declared paths, report that as its own state -- `declaration_unreadable` -- rather than letting it vanish into a '0 from a live session' headline.
